summary: Sensient Technologies reported quarterly EPS of $0.80, beating Zacks’ estimate by $0.02, with a 9.13% net margin and 16.73% return on equity. Shares opened at $78.53 Tuesday, with a $3.48 billion market cap. The company declared a $0.30 quarterly dividend payable March 1. KeyCorp raised its price target to $84, while Zacks upgraded the stock to “hold.”

XYZprinting invited customers and resellers to see the MfgPro220 xPF ultrafast 3D printer at Rapid + TCT 2018. Priced at $19,950, it offers a 16-liter build volume and is intended for prototyping, tooling, and end-use parts. The printer uses cognitive software, sensors, machine learning, onboard and cloud controls, and Nexa3D’s LSPc technology to deliver high-speed, high-resolution printing. XYZprinting also announced partnerships with BEGO and Nexa3D to develop and manufacture dental and other 3D printers. XYZprinting is backed by New Kinpo Group, while Nexa3D makes ultrafast industrial stereolithography printers.

Collagen is a structural protein that supports skin, tendons, bones, cartilage, muscles, blood vessels and organs, but natural production decreases with age. Supplements commonly contain collagen types I, II and III and may come from marine, bovine, porcine or chicken sources, with hydrolysed collagen described as easily digested and absorbed. Reported potential benefits include supporting skin firmness and hydration, nail strength, bone density, joint health and muscle repair, though research is ongoing. Suggested doses vary by goal, and manufacturers often recommend at least 12 weeks for noticeable results. Experts advise choosing third-party-tested products and supporting collagen production through a balanced diet containing protein, vitamin C and collagen-rich foods such as bone broth.
MedRxiv technical report on phase angle clusters in bioimpedance as an alternative to BMI, posted January 3, 2024.

The Weather Channel is launching an Android app for developing countries that uses IBM mesh networking to send messages phone-to-phone via Bluetooth and Wi-Fi when mobile networks fail during emergencies. The app works over 200 to 500 feet, requires no network setting changes, and adds no extra battery burden. IBM says widespread adoption could create enough nodes to relay alerts and other data, while digital signatures help verify trusted, unmodified information. The 3.2MB app is launching in emerging markets in Asia, Latin America and Africa and is designed for older 2G networks.

The lecture introduces MIT’s Discrete Stochastic Processes course, emphasizing that probability courses often focus on solving well-posed problems, while the harder task is building appropriate models for uncertain real-world situations. The professor distinguishes mathematical probability from real-world modeling, warning that correct mathematics can still fail if the model is poor, especially in areas such as finance, risk, networks, and catastrophe management.

The course will study probability models, discrete stochastic processes, counting processes, Poisson processes, renewal processes, Markov processes, random walks, and martingales. Stochastic processes are described as probability models whose sample points represent functions or sequences over time, often modeled over infinite time spans for mathematical usefulness.

The lecture reviews Kolmogorov’s axioms: a probability model includes a sample space, events as subsets of that space, and probabilities assigned to events. Events must be closed under countable unions and complements, the empty set is an event, the sample space has probability 1, probabilities are nonnegative, and countable disjoint unions have probabilities equal to the sum of their component probabilities. Consequences include complement probabilities, monotonicity, and the union bound.

The professor also discusses independent events and experiments, explaining independence through product probabilities and combined sample spaces such as Cartesian products. Random variables are defined as functions from sample points to real numbers, with distribution functions derived from event probabilities. The lecture ends by stressing the importance of learning to prove statements and to combine intuition with formal reasoning when analyzing complex systems.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2016. The company designs, develops, manufactures and sells fully electric vehicles and Tesla Energy products. It was producing and selling Model S and Model X, had delivered over 122,000 vehicles through March 31, 2016, and unveiled Model 3 during the quarter.

For the quarter, Tesla reported total revenue of $1.15 billion, up from $939.9 million a year earlier, driven primarily by Model S growth and Model X deliveries. Gross profit was $252.5 million, compared with $260.1 million, and gross margin declined to 22.0% from 27.7%. Net loss was $282.3 million, compared with $154.2 million, and basic and diluted net loss per share was $2.13.

As of March 31, 2016, Tesla had $1.44 billion in cash and cash equivalents, total assets of $9.19 billion, total liabilities of $8.18 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $970.4 million. Operating cash used was $249.6 million, investing cash used was $233.8 million, and financing activities provided $715.4 million. The company planned higher production, expanded sales, service and charging infrastructure, continued Gigafactory development, and expected 2016 capital expenditures to be about 50% higher than its prior $1.5 billion estimate.

Bethesda Softworks announced Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus will launch on Nintendo Switch on June 29, digitally and physically, though the cartridge version requires a download. The Switch port follows Bethesda’s releases of Doom and Skyrim and supports Nintendo’s successful hybrid console.

Bell Academy received a Mississippi Alliance for Health, Physical Education, Recreation and Dance grant from Blue Cross Blue Shield of Mississippi in November 2016 to build a new P.E. building. Parent volunteers and community members built the steel structure, which includes sports and exercise equipment. Teacher Joyce Aycock and students said the new indoor space allows for more activities, noise and movement compared with previous classes held outside or in open indoor areas. A horizontal rock-climbing wall is planned before the building’s ribbon cutting Friday.

The President returns a bill donating public lands to states and territories for colleges teaching agriculture and mechanic arts, objecting that it is inexpedient and unconstitutional. The bill would grant 20,000 acres per congressional Senator and Representative, totaling an estimated 6,060,000 acres valued at $7,575,000, with much of it issued as land scrip to states without eligible public lands.

He argues the bill would deprive the Treasury of revenue from public land sales at a time of fiscal difficulty, depress land prices through a flood of scrip, and harm holders of bounty-land warrants. He warns it would blur federal and state responsibilities by encouraging states to rely on the Federal Treasury for education and domestic policy, weakening both governments. He also contends it would injure new states by enabling speculators to acquire large tracts of desirable land, raising costs for actual settlers.

He doubts the bill would effectively advance agriculture or mechanic arts because the Federal Government could not enforce the states’ use of the funds. He says it could damage existing colleges by creating federally endowed rivals and cause disputes within states over distribution.

Constitutionally, he argues Congress lacks power to fund state education through taxation or public lands. He rejects the claim that the power to “dispose of” federal property includes giving land away for state purposes, interpreting it instead as authority to sell or manage lands as a trustee. He distinguishes earlier educational land grants to new states as measures aiding settlement and sale of public lands.

The drive concept is a football passing design using a 10–12 yard basic route and a 3–4 yard shallow crossing route from the same side, creating a triangle read and stressing linebackers. It works well against man and Cover 4 but struggles against Cover 2 and Cover 3 due to underneath defenders. Routes adjust based on man or zone coverage, with receivers staying on the move versus man and sitting in open zones versus zone. The quarterback checks the post pre-snap, then progresses through the go route, shallow cross, basic route, and running back check-down. Variations include bunch formations and backside use in other pass concepts.

The council says it is working to reduce congestion around Southway, Tamerton Foliot and the Derriford Transport Scheme by coordinating planned roadworks, liaising with utility companies, limiting temporary signals to off-peak times where possible, and monitoring traffic flow. Measures include suspending bus lane restrictions on Tavistock Road, carrying out construction in multiple areas to shorten the programme, using weekend and night working, altering George Junction signal timings, and reviewing changes at Budshead Roundabout to improve flow. Further proposals include adjusted lane markings, moving give-way markings, and adding signs to encourage merging. Planned roadworks are listed online, with alerts and advance publicity for disruptive works.

ADT is described as undervalued compared with newly listed peer Verisure, supported by revenue growth, improving profitability, recurring revenue, partnerships with Google and State Farm, debt reduction, and share buybacks. Challenges include customer churn and flat subscriber numbers, while AI, remote assistance, and smart home investments aim to improve retention. Peer valuation implies potential upside of over 33%.

The Department of Higher Education and Training is working to integrate NSFAS systems with colleges and universities amid delays in funding payments that have led to student complaints and protests. Minister Naledi Pandor said unresolved funding for some continuing students was unacceptable and blamed data integration challenges affecting registration confirmation, bursary agreements and funding allocations. The department will assess NSFAS processes, improve integration, and strengthen cooperation with institutional financial aid offices. Government has allocated nearly R7.2bn in additional 2018 funding for poor and working-class students, with R105m to improve NSFAS administration. DA spokesperson Belinda Bozzoli criticized the minister and NSFAS for not explaining how many students are affected, why delays occurred, or when payments will be made.

Allen reported that Kim Ok-kiun, leader of the 1884 revolution and refugee in Japan, was assassinated in Shanghai by Hong Chong-oo, who was later turned over by Chinese authorities to Korea. A related plot in Tokyo involved attempts against another refugee, Pak Yung-ho, and Japanese police forcibly removed a suspect from the Korean legation after Korea refused surrender terms. Kim’s body and Hong were brought to Chemulpo; Kim’s body was taken to Seoul, mutilated, and parts sent around the country despite Japanese efforts to remonstrate. Sill reported unrest in Cholla Do, Chung-ch’ong Do, and Kiong-sang Do caused by oppressive officials, with some officials killed or expelled. He requested naval presence at Chemulpo, recalled American missionaries from the interior, and noted Korean officials wanted more frequent U.S. ship visits.

This document describes AMD Versioned Chip Endorsement Key (VCEK) certificates and the Key Distribution System (KDS) interface for retrieving certificate information used with SEV-SNP. It defines terms, product name determination through CPUID FMS data, and the VCEK trust chain, which uses product-specific AMD Root Key (ARK) and AMD SEV Key (ASK) certificate authorities. VCEK certificates are X.509v3 certificates generated at request time, valid from one day before issuance to seven years after issuance, and include custom extensions describing TCB version elements. Hardware ID length differs by processor family: 64 bytes for Family 19h and 8 bytes for Family 1Ah.

The KDS provides TLS 1.2 HTTP endpoints at https://kdsintf.amd.com to retrieve VCEK certificates for specified product, hardware ID, and SPL values; ARK/ASK certificate chains; and certificate revocation lists. Requests may be rate-limited, and invalid parameters or unsupported values return errors. The service supports pre-fetching certificates for future TCB SPL values within legal ranges to enable smoother firmware upgrades.

Mauricio Pochettino named a 26-player USMNT roster for October friendlies against Ecuador in Austin on Oct. 10 and Australia in Commerce City four days later. Christian Pulisic and Weston McKennie headline the squad, with Antonee Robinson returning after knee surgery and McKennie back for the first time since March. Tanner Tessmann and Aidan Morris were rewarded for strong club form, while Pulisic has six goals and two assists for AC Milan this season. Several players were excluded due to injuries or selection decisions.

UPMSP will declare the UP Board Class 10 and Class 12 results 2018 on April 29 at 12:30 pm on upresults.nic.in and upmspresults.up.nic.in. Class 10 exams were held February 6–22, and Class 12 exams February 6–March 12. Students can check results online or by SMS using their roll numbers.

The speaker describes a tight, defensive game with difficulty establishing possession due to Hasek’s puck-handling. They note frustration, defensive lapses, and Detroit’s adjustments and offense, stressing the need to refocus, tighten play in the defensive zone, correct mistakes, and trust coaching decisions.

The passage describes a vehicle sensing system using radar sensors with two-dimensional arrays of transmitting and receiving antennas. A control processes receiver outputs with two-dimensional MIMO to create an enhanced virtual aperture, improving horizontal and vertical object detection accuracy and resolution. One embodiment uses 12 transmitting antennas and 16 receiving antennas to provide 192 virtual receivers. The system may support driver assistance functions such as autonomous driving, parking assistance, blind spot detection, cross traffic alerts, emergency braking, pedestrian detection, and collision mitigation, and may combine radar data with camera image data or display alerts.

Jennifer Thompson mistakenly identified Ronald Cotton as the man who raped her, leading to his conviction. Eleven years later, post-conviction DNA testing showed Bobby Poole was the attacker; Poole had raped six more women while Cotton was imprisoned. Thompson says trauma and questioning can distort memory unintentionally. After Cotton’s exoneration, she apologized, and he told her he had forgiven her. They became best friends, and Thompson founded Healing Justice, where harmed parties share their stories.

Russia’s central bank cut its key interest rate to 9.25 percent from 9.75 percent, citing falling inflation and forecasting consumer price growth at 4 percent by end-2017 through 2019. It signaled gradual further cuts, while noting inflation risks, global market volatility, and a baseline oil price drop to $40.

Day 1 of the 2025 World Grand Prix of Darts featured first-round action. Rob Cross won a last-leg decider, Krzysztof Ratajski defeated a seed 2-0 with a 95.94 average, Cameron Menzies upset the No. 8 seed, and Joe Cullen beat James Wade 2-0.

A scheduled Oct. 15 paycheck for 1.3 million active-duty U.S. service members could pressure Congress and the White House to end the government shutdown or pass a temporary continuing resolution, according to Goldman Sachs economists. Prediction markets show a high chance the shutdown lasts beyond Oct. 14, but analysts say missed military pay could create political pressure. Other possible pressure points include TSA operations, delayed data releases, mortgage payments for service members, WIC benefits, Obamacare enrollment, and Thanksgiving travel. Some analysts still warn the shutdown could extend into November.

Ghana’s major gold miners, including Newmont, Gold Fields and AngloGold Ashanti, support new government tests to certify export values, the Chamber of Mines said. The measures, added to customs and company checks, aim to improve oversight and taxation. PMMC officials now access gold rooms, take assay samples and join pre-shipment sealing. Ghana earned $5.78 billion from gold exports last year, while the government says about $5 billion in gold export revenue to the UAE is unaccounted for.

The work presents fabrication and characterization of CMOS-compatible hybrid NbN/Si-SiGe superconducting microwave circuits. Devices used 100 nm NbN films sputtered on n-doped Si/Si0.7Ge0.3 wafers and included λ/4 CPW resonators coupled to a common feedline. Fabrication involved oxide removal, NbN deposition, e-beam lithography, CF4/Ar etching, and a deep SF6/C4F8 substrate etch in CPW gaps to shift lossy interfaces and charge-noise sources away from high-field regions. TEM/STEM analysis showed epitaxial SiGe-Si-SiGe quantum well layers, loss of crystallinity and oxygenation in the Si cap layer, and mapped Ge, Si, Nb, and O.

Two scratch-free samples were measured over four cooldowns spanning two years. Resonance frequencies near 5.04–5.60 GHz were observed at 50 mK. Power spectroscopy showed internal quality factors increasing with photon number, with S1 reaching about 860 in the single-photon regime and 1064 at higher power, while S2 ranged from about 500 to 600. Coupling quality factors stayed largely constant. Long-term measurements showed no measurable degradation.

An RLC model was developed using the Si/SiGe dielectric properties and measured resonances. Loss analysis attributed dissipation mainly to power-independent scattering and internal losses, with TLS losses contributing but not dominating; quasiparticle loss was negligible at 50 mK. Temperature-dependent spectroscopy up to 1.7 K showed TLS-related behavior at lower temperatures and quasiparticle-related frequency shifts and losses at higher temperatures. The study concludes that NbN/Si-SiGe resonators provide a stable, manufacturable platform for hybrid superconducting–semiconductor quantum circuits, though further wafer and design optimization is needed to improve coherence.

A report says Edina School District in Minnesota introduces young students to concepts including “white privilege,” with K-2 students at Highlands Elementary participating in a Melanin Project about skin tone. The passage also cites a Michigan State University professor’s co-authored article claiming U.S. yoga practice is linked to white supremacy, colonialism, capitalism, and cultural appropriation.

A diverse workforce helps businesses compete in global markets, but subconscious biases about gender, race, ethnicity, and culture can affect hiring decisions. Studies cited show men favored for math-related roles despite equal performance, resumes with white-sounding names receiving more callbacks than African American-sounding names, and applicants with non-English last names receiving fewer interviews. Employers can reduce bias by using job postings that describe desired behaviors rather than personality types, removing names from resumes before review, reconsidering rejected applications for bias, and using skills-based quizzes or challenges before collecting identifying information. Interview impressions should be examined to ensure they are not rooted in prejudice.

The speaker announces he will soon leave the presidency and return to the role of citizen, thanking Vice President Mondale, his Cabinet, staff, and the American people. He reflects on the Presidency as powerful but constrained by law, custom, Congress, public consent, scrutiny, and debate. He warns that single-issue and special-interest pressures can distort the national interest, making a strong presidency important, and pledges support to the President-elect.

He identifies three major global issues: nuclear destruction, stewardship of the planet’s resources, and human rights. He warns of the growing danger of nuclear weapons while emphasizing the need for both military strength and arms control. He calls for protecting air, water, land, minerals, forests, and food supplies from depletion, pollution, and population pressures. He argues that America must defend human rights at home and abroad, including education, medical care, jobs, equality, and freedom from injustice and intolerance.

He says democracy must be renewed by each generation, linking modern challenges to nuclear survival, human rights, and responsible use of planetary resources. He promises to ensure a smooth presidential transition, continue efforts and prayers for American hostages in Iran, support the new President, and work as a citizen for the nation’s founding values.

China’s foreign exchange regulator said capital outflow pressure eased somewhat in 2016 and the yuan’s exchange rate would become more flexible in 2017. SAFE said reforms would support two-way cross-border capital flows and that authorities would seek to attract inflows. The yuan fell 6.5% against the dollar in 2016 and rose nearly 1% so far in 2017.

The author argues that high-dosage tutoring should be viewed not only as a response to pandemic learning loss but also as a way to build student confidence, support teachers and develop future educators. Teach For America’s Ignite Fellowship has trained more than 5,500 virtual tutors across over 40 communities, with more than 2,000 fellows providing nearly 200,000 hours of customized learning last school year. Reported outcomes include accelerated growth in middle school math and elementary reading. The author says effective tutoring requires structured training, school-based support and technology that expands relationships rather than replaces them. Research cited in the passage found that serving as an Ignite tutor nearly triples the likelihood of applying to Teach For America’s teacher program, with strong effects among men, people of color and non-education majors. Since Ignite began, 550 fellows have joined TFA’s teaching corps, including 280 this year.

Amazon grew from an online bookstore launched by Jeff Bezos in 1995 to the fourth-largest U.S. public company by its 20th IPO anniversary in 2017, despite limited cumulative profitability. Its strategy emphasized long-term market leadership, customer focus, expansion, R&D, and free cash flow over short-term earnings. Amazon broadened through new product categories, acquisitions, Prime, Kindle, devices, and AWS. Prime membership and AWS became major growth drivers, while some initiatives, such as the Fire Phone, failed. From 1997 to 2016, shareholders earned nearly 64,000%, while cumulative net income was $4.9 billion, mostly from 2015–2016. In 2016, Amazon reported $136.0 billion in net sales, $4.2 billion in operating income, $2.4 billion in net income, and $9.7 billion in free cash flow.

The 2025 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine was awarded to Shimon Sakaguchi, Mary Brunkow and Fred Ramsdell for work on regulatory T cells, which prevent the immune system from attacking the body. Sakaguchi identified T-regs in 1995, while Brunkow and Ramsdell linked a mutation to fatal autoimmune disease in mice and later to disease in people. Scientists are studying T-regs for treating autoimmune disorders, cancer and other immune-related conditions.

The passage studies the “free option” problem introduced by Ethereum’s enshrined Proposer–Builder Separation (ePBS) with dual payload and blob deadlines. Unlike MEV-Boost, where relays reveal blocks at slot start, ePBS lets winning builders reveal payloads and blobs later, allowing them to withhold data and make a slot empty if late external information makes included trades unfavorable. This creates a liveness risk without protocol-level penalty.

The authors model how this option affects builder incentives, especially for CEX–DEX arbitrage. They predict that option value and exercise probability rise with volatility, on-chain liquidity, the option window length, and the share of block value from external market signals, while higher atomic MEV lowers exercise probability. The option can cause DEX mispricing and losses for liquidity providers.

Using Ethereum blocks from January 2024 to March 2025, the study finds that with an 8-second option window the average exercise probability is 0.82%, but it rises sharply during high-volatility periods, reaching daily missed block rates of 5.5% and accounting for up to 80% of missed blocks. Blocks with larger CEX–DEX value shares have higher exercise probabilities, and smaller builders more dependent on such flow show higher rates.

The passage evaluates mitigations. Shortening the option window substantially reduces exercise probability but weakens ePBS scalability benefits. Static penalties also reduce exercise probability, while dynamic penalties based on observed exercise can target low missed-block rates with lower average penalties. The paper concludes that the free option affects liveness, market efficiency, liquidity providers, and potentially applications such as prediction markets, requiring protocol-level incentive design.

Microsoft’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2020 identifies Microsoft as a technology company focused on empowering people and organizations through software, services, devices, and solutions. Its offerings include cloud-based services, productivity applications, operating systems, server and business applications, development tools, video games, devices, and online advertising.

Microsoft reports three operating segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. Key products and services include Office, Microsoft 365, Teams, Dynamics, LinkedIn, Azure, SQL Server, Windows Server, GitHub, Windows, Surface, Xbox, and Bing. The company emphasizes growth in cloud computing, artificial intelligence, intelligent edge, remote work tools, gaming, and digital transformation.

The report discusses COVID-19 impacts, including remote work, office closures, virtual events, and uncertainty affecting operations, customers, partners, spending, and accounting estimates. Microsoft also describes sustainability goals, including becoming carbon negative by 2030, racial equity initiatives, and investments in digital skills.

Microsoft had approximately 163,000 full-time employees as of June 30, 2020. Its products are distributed through OEMs, direct sales, distributors, resellers, and cloud solution partners. The company cites risks including intense competition, cloud execution challenges, uncertain returns on investments, acquisition risks, cybersecurity threats, data privacy concerns, and potential impacts from security vulnerabilities.

Geary County authorities arrested Isaac Torgerson of Fort Riley on suspicion of aggravated assault after occupants of another vehicle reported a passenger in his Dodge Ram waved a gun at them during an alleged road rage incident.

The Yankees will start Paul Goldschmidt at first base and bat him sixth in ALDS Game 4 against the Blue Jays, with Ben Rice moving to the bench. Toronto is using opener Louis Varland in a bullpen game, and the Yankees may prefer Goldschmidt for later matchups. Rice had started the first three ALDS games and is 2-for-11. His bench role gives New York catching and pinch-hitting flexibility.

Enron replaced CFO Andrew Fastow with Jeff McMahon after investor concern over Fastow’s role in LJM partnerships that conducted transactions with Enron and were under SEC inquiry. Chairman Kenneth Lay said restoring investor confidence required the change, though Enron denied wrongdoing. Reports cited concerns about conflicts of interest, off-balance-sheet financing, a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity, limited disclosure, possible credit-rating pressure, and shareholder lawsuits. Enron’s stock fell sharply to $16.41, down about half since Oct. 16, prompting analyst downgrades and affecting other energy-trading stocks. McMahon, formerly Enron treasurer and head of industrial markets, was reported to have raised concerns about Fastow’s partnership role.

The author placed a new Temu order after the platform resumed direct shipping from China and received it without extra tariff or duty fees. The article explains that the end of the de minimis exemption created uncertainty for low-cost Chinese e-commerce platforms like Temu and Shein, which had shifted to showing US-shipped products to avoid added fees. The author’s order arrived after a week or two, with mixed product quality, and no tariff bill appeared after a month.

Donnell Gibson, known as “Mr. D,” is a behavior intervention specialist and junior varsity basketball coach at Como Park Senior High in St. Paul. He helps students manage life challenges so they can focus on school, often using basketball to connect lessons to their personal lives. In 2015, Gibson ran into a burning house three times to save a family of 10, earning the St. Paul Fire Department’s highest honor. The experience broadened his goals beyond sports, leading him to start the Gibson Foundation, which mentors young African-American inner-city men through speakers, college tours and basketball. Gibson, who experienced homelessness while growing up, says a high school principal helped him see his own potential.

The passage compiles Oct. 23, 2001 media mentions of Enron. Cauley Geller Bowman & Coates filed a securities class action alleging Enron misrepresented its business and financial condition, failed to timely write down impaired assets, and inflated its stock price during Jan. 18, 2000 to Oct. 17, 2001. Multiple reports said the SEC sought information about Enron transactions with limited partnerships managed by a senior officer, leading to investor concern and a sharp stock decline. Bloomberg reported Enron remained highly rated by many analysts despite investor flight, while also seeking a $750 million Citigroup loan amid concerns about credit access and debt downgrades. TheStreet.com and Forbes reported that Enron’s conference call did not fully resolve questions about off-balance-sheet transactions, equity reductions, and partnerships tied to CFO Andrew Fastow. A Texas Monthly article examined Enron’s rise, internal culture, aggressive trading model, accounting questions, California energy criticism, broadband problems, and Jeff Skilling’s resignation. Separate reports said AES Corp. complained to India’s prime minister about alleged interference by Orissa state authorities, following similar Enron disputes over the Dabhol project.

The speaker described an upbeat meeting about game plan adjustments, emphasizing the team’s need to use speed and skating while staying physical. They praised their goalie for keeping them competitive despite weaker performances and said success depends on mental readiness, individual focus, leadership, and using home-ice energy.

Forwarded Enron email compiles Feb. 23, 2001 news on California’s energy crisis. Articles cover opposition to Enron’s proposed Lake Elsinore hydroelectric project power lines; Gov. Gray Davis’ negotiations to buy utility transmission grids and tentative Edison deal; rising state power-purchase costs; disputes over repayment, rates, and utility debt; lifted power alerts after weeks of emergencies; proposed price cuts from small generators; political criticism from Republicans and commentators; campaign contribution returns; and proposals for discounts near power plants.

The passage presents approaches to study and anticipate drug resistance in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), focusing on microtubule (MT) dynamics, androgen receptor (AR) variants, patient-derived organoids, circulating tumor cells (CTCs), and cytoskeletal regulation. It notes that treatment options for mCRPC remain limited, resistance to systemic therapy is universal, and about one-third of tumors are primarily refractory to taxane-based chemotherapy.

AR signaling is linked to MT dynamics. AR splice variants such as ARv567 and AR-V7 differ in their association with MTs and response to taxanes. In M12 prostate cancer cell lines, AR-wild type expression caused little change in MT growth rates compared with AR-null cells, while ARv7 increased EB1 comet speeds by over 40% and showed predominantly nuclear localization, consistent with taxane-resistant behavior.

The passage describes a computational method for measuring MT dynamics by tracking fluorescent EB1 or EB3 comets in live-cell microscopy. The algorithm detects, tracks, and clusters MT growth tracks to infer growth, pause, and shortening behavior using image filtering, Kalman tracking, and linear assignment methods.

Patient-derived prostate tumor organoids were used to study MT dynamics and drug susceptibility. The passage discusses challenges in culturing primary prostate tumors due to normal tissue overgrowth and describes efforts to adjust organoid culture conditions, including reducing Y-27632 ROCK inhibitor concentration to select for high-grade tumor cells. It also proposes matching individual tumors to tubulin inhibitors based on MT dynamics signatures.

The passage reports that androgen-independent mCRPC CTCs may be much smaller than commonly assumed and can be identified through PSMA expression rather than AR expression. It discusses AR-null and neuroendocrine-like progression, MAPK and FGF signaling, and possible therapeutic relevance of PSMA-targeted therapy, MAPK targeting, ferroptosis, and proteolysis-targeting chimeras.

Multiple mechanisms of MT-related drug resistance are discussed. Op18 upregulation is linked to reduced MT polymerization rates, smaller spindle structures, and possible resilience to therapy. Paclitaxel treatment in breast cancer cells reduced MT growth rates and made MT dynamics more uniform. NAD+ and GPX4 inhibitors are discussed as possible modulators of drug susceptibility and ferroptosis in resistant prostate cancer cells.

The passage emphasizes the roles of pVHL and GSK3β in maintaining MT dynamics. Loss of pVHL, pVHL phosphorylation by GSK3β, or serum starvation altered MT turnover and catastrophe behavior. GSK3β inhibition in serum-starved cells attenuated MT turnover. The passage suggests that pVHL mutation type may relate to differential sensitivity to MT-stabilizing or MT-destabilizing drugs.

Drug resistance evaluation methods include detecting taxane-induced MT bundling with circular Hough transform. In A549 cells treated with paclitaxel, 83% showed rounded MT bundles, while BRCA1 knockdown cells showed reduced response, with 27% forming bundles and lower overall tubulin ring intensity. The passage proposes correlating live-cell MT dynamics in organoids with gene expression signatures and clinical response to identify MT-regulating resistance targets.

The conclusion states that advanced prostate cancer treatment is limited by lack of reliable molecular markers and that ex vivo MT dynamics analysis in patient-derived cells may help anticipate drug resistance, guide therapy, evaluate drug dose effects, and screen compounds that restore abnormal MT homeostasis. It also discusses possible use of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, organoid–immune cell co-cultures, and small-molecule screens to improve immunotherapy responses.

Donchian Channels, invented by Richard Donchian, use upper and lower bands based on the highest high and lowest low of the last N bars. They were designed as a trend-following breakout indicator and are still popular, especially for commodities and currencies. The article argues they work poorly as a trend-following tool for stocks but can work as a mean-reversion indicator when used opposite to their original intent. Backtests on the S&P 500 and SPY showed lower drawdowns and varying returns depending on lookback periods. Curtis Faith’s tests from 1996 to 2007 on currencies, commodities, and Treasuries showed strong annual returns. Donchian Channels resemble Bollinger Bands visually, but may produce different backtest results.

The article reviews Hungary’s general and special education systems, including demographics, government, economy, teacher preparation, laws, and current challenges. Hungary has compulsory education from ages 6 to 16, a school system spanning kindergarten through higher education, and selective admissions processes for secondary and post-secondary pathways. Teacher preparation varies by level, with general education teachers completing university training and practical placements.

Hungary has a long history in special education, beginning with a school for deaf students in 1802 and a special education teacher college in 1906. Students with disabilities are identified by committees of educators, specialists, and physicians, while parents decide placement. Supports include counseling, early development, speech therapy, pedagogical care, conductive care, gifted education, and special physical education. In 2019, more than 88,000 students with special educational needs were enrolled, with about 60% educated inclusively.

Special education teachers complete a four-year university program and specialize in areas such as autism, behavioral disorders, hearing impairment, intellectual disability, learning disability, physical disability, visual disability, or speech therapy. New teachers complete a two-year traineeship, and ongoing professional training is encouraged.

Key issues include difficulties in diagnosis, limited building accessibility, incomplete inclusion, insufficient special education training for general educators, low teacher pay, and teacher attrition. The article recommends improving diagnosis, accessibility, inclusion, teacher preparation, wages, and retention.

The passage analyzes Nvidia, Micron Technology and Western Digital amid a market rebound, warning that not all rallies indicate buying opportunities. Nvidia is described as benefiting from strong earnings and a bounce off its 50-day trendline, which remains upward and supportive. The stock is viewed as technically attractive after last week’s “sell the news” reaction. Micron is presented more cautiously: despite a rally, it remains below its 50-day moving average, which has turned bearish. The passage says Micron’s rebound follows an oversold RSI reading, but resistance near $84 may limit gains and attract sellers.

Canadian lumber producers’ shares fell after BMO Capital Markets downgraded West Fraser, Interfor and Canfor, citing U.S. duties, a stronger Canadian dollar and ongoing litigation. BMO said a near-term lumber dispute resolution was unlikely, with little substantive negotiation. The downgrade came before NAFTA renegotiation talks, while analysts said longer-term stock prospects looked more positive.

President Trump suggested some furloughed federal workers may not receive back pay during the government shutdown, saying it “depends” and blaming Democrats. His remarks followed a draft White House memo arguing back pay is not guaranteed, despite prior administration guidance and a 2019 law stating furloughed employees shall be paid after funding lapses. The administration says Congress must specifically appropriate the funds. The move is viewed as pressure on Senate Democrats to support a Republican stopgap funding bill. Trump also warned of substantial permanent layoffs if the shutdown continues. Federal workers’ union AFGE called the back-pay argument a misinterpretation of the law and said workers should not be used as political bargaining chips.

Select Security acquired Charlotte-based Intelligent Technology Inc. and Carolina Security Group, adding nearly 1,000 customers, staff, and a downtown Charlotte branch. The company will consolidate western North Carolina operations there. Select Security serves nearly 30,000 customers across nine states with security, fire, video, access, and automation systems.

Japan’s economy grew at an annualised 4% in the April-to-June quarter, beating expectations, driven by stronger consumer spending and capital expenditure. Domestic demand offset weaker exports, while Olympic-related investment also boosted growth. Private consumption rose 0.9%, supporting Prime Minister Shinzo Abe’s efforts to revive spending and growth.

Scientists at Newcastle University have 3D printed human corneas for the first time, a proof-of-concept that could help address the global shortage of transplantable corneas. Researchers mixed human corneal stromal stem cells from a healthy donor with alginate and collagen to create a printable bio-ink. Using a low-cost 3D bio-printer, they printed a cornea-shaped structure in under 10 minutes, and the cells were shown to grow afterward. The team also demonstrated that corneas could be printed to match a patient’s eye using scan data. Professor Che Connon said further testing is needed and it will be several years before such corneas could be used for transplants.

Texas Gulf Coast beaches are regularly tested for bacteria associated with feces from humans, pets and wildlife, which can enter ocean water through storm runoff after heavy rain. A warning issued near Galveston Beach’s 57th Street was lifted Friday after water samples came back clear. Officials advise avoiding water during advisories because exposure can cause illness, though conditions usually improve within 48 hours. Galveston County tests 52 sites, and beachgoers can check conditions through TexasBeachWatch.com, GCHD.org or posted advisory signs.

President Reagan addressed the University of Virginia, reflecting on Thomas Jefferson’s influence on American higher education, self-government, religious freedom, and balanced government. He drew parallels between Jefferson’s era and contemporary debates over regulation, taxation, judicial power, and foreign policy.

Reagan argued that democracy and free-market ideas were expanding worldwide, citing developments in the Philippines, Burma, Korea, Chile, Poland, South Africa, China, and the Soviet Union. He highlighted Freedom House statistics showing fewer “not free” countries and more “free” or “partly free” countries. He linked political freedom with economic freedom and described progress in U.S.-Soviet relations, including summits, the INF Treaty, movement toward START, regional conflict negotiations, human rights improvements, and expanded bilateral exchanges.

He cautioned that serious differences with the Soviet Union remained and emphasized skepticism, verification, military strength, and public candor. He rejected the idea that Soviet change was inevitable, crediting Western strength, resolve, and clarity, as well as actions by Gorbachev. Reagan also stressed the need for cooperation between Congress and the President in foreign affairs, criticizing congressional limits he said weakened executive flexibility.

In the question-and-answer session, Reagan said U.S. policy toward the Soviet Union should depend on whether actions match words. On the Middle East, he called PLO acceptance of U.N. Resolutions 242 and 338, Israel’s right to exist, and renunciation of terrorism a step toward dialogue. He defended his anti-terrorism policy, urged young people to vote, cited military rebuilding and economic growth as major accomplishments, and said after leaving office he planned to remain active, speak publicly, possibly write a book, and support causes such as a balanced budget amendment, line-item veto, military defense, and Nancy Reagan’s antidrug work.

The passage lists archival and published sources for documents on foreign policy, including Haig and Regan personal papers, State Department files, the Reagan Library, Library of Congress, NSC, and major newspapers. It then provides source notes for Reagan and Bush campaign statements and speeches from January to October 1980 on defense, peace strategy, China/Taiwan, and foreign policy, with related press coverage.

A 70-mile-wide radar signature over Colorado, initially mistaken by National Weather Service scientists for migrating birds, was identified as swarms of Painted Lady butterflies. Meteorologist Paul Schlatter noted the movement direction was unusual for birds and asked the public for help on Twitter, where responses pointed to butterflies. The species has recently appeared in large numbers around Denver and can glide hundreds of miles daily.

VentureWire’s May 16, 2001 issue reported venture financing, layoffs, acquisitions, product launches, executive changes, and fund news. Top stories included Buzzsaw.com laying off 70 employees, or 30% of staff, while expecting to close a $20 million round; UGO Networks acquiring Bla-Bla.com; EYP Mission Critical Facilities raising $57.5 million led by TA Associates to spin off from Einhorn Yaffee Prescott; and Flatiron Partners moving into J.P. Morgan Chase offices to reduce rent costs.

New funding included KeepSmart raising $5.8 million, VDSL Systems $12.4 million, Creditek $30 million from General Atlantic, LifeClips $12.2 million, Opsys $11.2 million, DigiPlex $48 million in equity and $35 million in debt, and STSN $66.5 million in debt and equity. Viator was closing a $5 million to $10 million Series C round.

Several companies reported financial trouble or cuts: WorkingWoman.com laid off 63% of staff and sought buyers or funding; Metiom filed for Chapter 11; Mybiz.com shut down; OnSite Access laid off about two-thirds of staff; Eyecast cut 50%; and eLedger planned to shut down its ASP service.

M&A items included Motient acquiring Rare Medium, XCare.net buying Confer Software, Escalate acquiring Managize assets, Qiva acquiring Capstan Systems, BrainHeart buying Linq’s mobile Internet division, EMS Technologies acquiring CI Wireless, Parthus buying Chicory, and JAWZ selling its e-business unit.

VC fund news included Invesco closing a $150 million EuroMedia Venture Fund, PSINet Ventures winding down new investments, Schneider Electric launching a $44 million corporate venture arm, Axiomlab raising $17.1 million, CalPERS committing $10 million to SVCV Fund 2, and Friends Ivory & Sime closing 3PC with $61 million.

This study developed a reproducible, data-driven method for prioritising AI-detected chest X-ray abnormalities to support faster lung cancer diagnosis. Conducted across seven Greater Manchester acute trusts, it used a retrospective cohort of 1,282 patients with confirmed lung cancer and abnormal CXR, and a prospective primary care referral cohort of 13,802 CXRs analysed in AI shadow mode. The Annalise CXR AI system assessed 124 possible findings, and prioritisation strategies were based on finding prevalence ratios, initial clinical priority categories, and clinical review.

Three strategies were evaluated. Strategy 1 prioritised 19 high-prevalence-ratio findings, achieving 92.82% sensitivity and 87.21% specificity. Strategy 2 included all high-priority findings, increasing sensitivity to 97.27% but reducing specificity to 62.68%. Strategy 3 combined empirical prevalence with clinical judgement and selected 32 findings, achieving 95.87% sensitivity, 79.11% specificity, 4.43% positive predictive value, and 99.95% negative predictive value.

The authors conclude that the method balances high sensitivity and negative predictive value while accepting lower positive predictive value to reduce missed cancer cases. They note limitations including regional data use, reliance on assumed cancer prevalence in the referral cohort, and lack of external validation. Further multicentre validation and assessment of workflow impact are planned.

The passage explains that the Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) report is a monthly U.S. employment report released by the Department of Labor, typically on the first Friday at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time. It measures changes in non-agricultural jobs and is considered a key indicator of U.S. economic health.

The NFP report affects financial markets because it influences expectations about Federal Reserve interest rate decisions. Strong job growth is generally viewed as positive for the U.S. economy and the dollar, but can pressure bonds due to expectations of higher rates and inflation. Weak job growth is generally seen as negative for the economy and dollar but more favorable for bonds.

The report impacts bonds, equities, forex, and commodities. Bond markets are described as especially sensitive, while forex traders closely watch NFP because it can cause volatility in USD currency pairs. Stocks tend to respond positively when NFP exceeds expectations and negatively when it disappoints. The report can also affect gold, oil, gas, and energy markets.

The passage includes backtests on SPY and TLT around NFP release days. SPY showed an average open-to-close gain of 0.09% on release days, while TLT showed an average return of -0.02%. Subsequent days showed weaker performance. The author concludes that NFP trading strategies are difficult to rely on and that no consistent trading edge has been found in macroeconomic numbers.

ICRC launched the nationwide “Pehlay Zindagi: Give Way to Ambulances—Give Way to Life” campaign in Islamabad to raise public awareness about giving way to ambulances. Supported by over 30 partner organizations, the campaign includes media outreach, a website, pledge application, and the “Friends for Life” virtual platform. It is part of ICRC’s Health Care in Danger project and will run until December 2017. The initiative aims to change public and policymaker behavior, highlight ambulance staff challenges, and assess motorists’ behavior before and after the campaign. It follows the 2016 “Rasta Dein” campaign, which showed a 16% impact.

Mariners vs. Tigers ALDS Game 3 in Detroit was delayed by rain after being scheduled for 4:08 p.m. ET. The series is tied 1-1. The Tigers said first pitch was expected at 7 p.m. ET, while the broadcast reported MLB was aiming for 7:30 p.m., with no team confirmation at that time. Fans waited in the stands and concourse during the delay. Due to overlap with Blue Jays vs. Yankees Game 3, the game was moved to FS2 and will also air on MLB Network and the Fox One App.

Bridgeton National Bank sued Ellas Q. Hepner to recover on a $1,400 promissory note made to Kil-Tone Company and endorsed to the bank. Hepner alleged the note was procured through fraudulent stock-sale representations and an agreement that it would not be negotiated unless the stock was resold at a profit, and claimed the bank had notice through its cashier, Hitchner, who was also Kil-Tone’s treasurer. The trial court excluded testimony about Hitchner’s knowledge and participation, ruling it could not be attributed to the bank, and directed a verdict for the bank. The court upheld that ruling, relying on New Jersey precedent that an agent’s knowledge is chargeable to the principal only when the principal would have received notice if acting directly. The rule to show cause for a new trial was discharged.

The lecture examines pseudorandom graphs through eigenvalues, focusing on \(n,d,\lambda\) graphs: \(d\)-regular graphs on \(n\) vertices whose nontrivial adjacency eigenvalues have absolute value at most \(\lambda\). The expander mixing lemma shows that smaller \(\lambda\) gives stronger discrepancy-type pseudorandomness.

An explicit deterministic example is the Paley graph, a Cayley graph on \(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}\) for primes \(p \equiv 1 \pmod 4\), with edges defined by nonzero quadratic residues. Its eigenvectors are roots-of-unity vectors, and its nontrivial eigenvalues are computed using Gauss sums, showing they are small compared with the degree. The lecture notes that, for Abelian Cayley graphs, eigenvalues correspond to Fourier coefficients; for non-Abelian groups, the analogous framework is representation theory.

The lecture then discusses equivalence between discrepancy and eigenvalue conditions for Cayley graphs. For general non-Cayley graphs, discrepancy need not imply small second eigenvalue, as shown by adding a small disjoint clique to a large random regular graph. For Cayley graphs, a theorem of Conlon and Zhao states that discrepancy with parameter \(\epsilon\) implies an eigenvalue bound with parameter \(8\epsilon\), while the reverse follows from the expander mixing lemma. The proof uses Grothendieck’s inequality, which compares optimization over signs with a semidefinite relaxation over unit vectors.

Finally, the lecture addresses how small \(\lambda\) can be. The Alon-Boppana bound states that for fixed \(d\), the second eigenvalue of an \(n\)-vertex \(d\)-regular graph is at least \(2\sqrt{d-1}-o(1)\). One proof constructs test vectors supported near far-apart vertices and applies the Courant-Fischer characterization. A second, weaker proof uses the trace method by counting closed walks and comparing with walks on the infinite \(d\)-regular tree. The constant \(2\sqrt{d-1}\) is identified as the spectral radius of the infinite \(d\)-regular tree.

Rite-Hite introduced the Uni-Dox Inflatable Shelter for loading docks handling varied truck and trailer configurations. It inflates around secured trailers and deflates before departure using a counterweight retraction system, non-inflatable draft pads, and a blower. Optional controls reduce damage risk, while PitMaster sealing helps block debris and pests.

Apple filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2022. Total net sales were $117.2 billion, down 5% from $123.9 billion a year earlier, mainly due to foreign currency weakness and lower iPhone and Mac sales, partly offset by higher iPad and Services sales. Net income was $30.0 billion, down from $34.6 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $1.88, compared with $2.10.

Product net sales were $96.4 billion and Services net sales were $20.8 billion. By category, iPhone sales were $65.8 billion, Mac $7.7 billion, iPad $9.4 billion, Wearables, Home and Accessories $13.5 billion, and Services $20.8 billion. All geographic segments reported lower net sales year over year.

As of December 31, 2022, Apple had total assets of $346.7 billion, total liabilities of $290.0 billion, and shareholders’ equity of $56.7 billion. Cash generated by operating activities was $34.0 billion. During the quarter, Apple repurchased $19.0 billion of common stock and paid $3.8 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents.

Apple reported COVID-related disruption at its primary iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone 14 Pro Max assembly facility in Zhengzhou, China, which reduced capacity and affected shipments. The company stated there were no material changes to market risk, internal control over financial reporting, critical accounting estimates, or risk factors since its 2022 Form 10-K.

Lower interest rates in the US and globally may support a rebound in housing and related cyclical stocks over the next one to four years. The passage says home improvement and homebuilding stocks have historically outperformed during falling-rate periods, except during the subprime crisis. Tariffs may benefit domestic lumber and wooden-goods manufacturers, though trade deals could alter this. It notes current housing leverage appears lower than in 2007 despite loose lending risks, and contrasts housing headwinds with extended tech valuations.

The speaker discusses his sports preferences and experiences, naming Ron Hextall as his favorite hockey player and describing how he became interested in hockey through teams and people in Birmingham, Philadelphia, Chicago, Arizona, and Nashville. He says NHL playoff hockey, especially overtime, is exciting and nerve-wracking, while the NBA playoffs have not been very competitive. He argues that great players benefit from great teammates, citing Kevin Durant and his own experience in Phoenix. He also emphasizes that winning is difficult and says teams that win multiple championships deserve special respect.

The Appellate Division reviewed Solomon Montlake’s conviction for first-degree grand larceny. Montlake argued that a prior jury discharge barred retrial under former jeopardy. The court held that before submission to a jury, a trial judge may discharge the jury for a substantial reason arising during trial, and any challenge is by plea of former jeopardy at retrial, not habeas corpus. It found the prior discharge proper because the prosecutor repeatedly accused defense counsel of criminal conduct before the jury, and the defense had previously moved to withdraw a juror.

The court also held that cross-examining an alibi witness about unpaid rent was improper because it did not fairly tend to show moral turpitude. More importantly, the trial court committed reversible error by instructing that the alibi had to show the defendants “could not have been” at the crime scene. The court stated the defendant bore no burden to prove alibi; if the alibi evidence, with all other evidence, raised a reasonable doubt about his presence, acquittal was required. The conviction was reversed as to Montlake, and a new trial was granted.

The passage describes AMD AGESA software interfaces, boot-time procedures, parameters, dependencies, status codes, and host-environment call-outs. It covers event log reading, structure allocation and release, processor reset and early initialization, cache-region allocation rules, FCH and GNB configuration, memory initialization, environment setup, graphics/display configuration, late boot table generation, S3 suspend/resume save and restore flows, and AP task dispatching.

These routines generally require a stack established by the host environment, and many require the host to avoid interfering with processor-core communication, MTRRs, or APIC registers.
