Build options can remove support for memory types, ECC, interleaving, training, AMP, processor families, socket types, ACPI tables, WHEA, DMI, S3, Connected Standby, and other features. Build configuration elements describe platform limits and settings such as VRM capability, CPU frequency limits, PCI MMIO base and size, IO APIC count, and ACPI table fields.

Haas School’s Oct. 12, 2000 alumni jobs bulletin lists 20 openings and recruiting opportunities across technology, finance, consulting, business development, healthcare, retail, and education. Roles include CEO/president, product managers, analysts, associates, directors, vice presidents, financial consultants, portfolio managers, and planning managers at companies including Gap Inc., Vividence, ILYTAC, CommerceRoute, BeVocal, Nuance Communications, AXA Advisors, Woodside Asset Management, Office Depot, Merrill Lynch, and others. The email provides locations, degree preferences, expanded job descriptions, qualifications, and application contacts, and invites alumni to submit postings or manage subscriptions.

NVIDIA filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 28, 2018. Third-quarter revenue was $3.181 billion, up from $2.636 billion a year earlier, with net income of $1.230 billion, or $1.97 diluted EPS. For the first nine months of fiscal 2019, revenue was $9.511 billion and net income was $3.575 billion, or $5.71 diluted EPS.

GPU revenue was $2.774 billion for the quarter and $8.195 billion for the first nine months, while Tegra Processor revenue was $407 million for the quarter and $1.316 billion for the first nine months. Revenue by market for the quarter was $1.764 billion from Gaming, $305 million from Professional Visualization, $792 million from Datacenter, $172 million from Automotive, and $148 million from OEM & IP.

Gross margin was 60.4% for the quarter, compared with 59.5% a year earlier. Operating expenses were $863 million, including $605 million for research and development and $258 million for sales, general and administrative expenses. Operating income was $1.058 billion.

As of October 28, 2018, NVIDIA had $13.657 billion in total assets, $4.182 billion in total liabilities, and $9.475 billion in shareholders’ equity. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $7.591 billion. Net cash provided by operating activities for the first nine months was $2.845 billion.

NVIDIA repurchased $855 million of common stock and paid $273 million in dividends during the first nine months of fiscal 2019. In November 2018, the board authorized an additional $7.00 billion for share repurchases and increased the quarterly dividend to $0.16 per share. The company reported ongoing patent-related litigation and stated it had not recorded accruals for the described proceedings.

The passage describes SD Memory Card command behavior and performance-related mechanisms. APP_CMD (CMD55) makes the following command application-specific; defined legal ACMDs set the APP_CMD status bit, undefined legal ACMDs are treated as normal commands, and illegal ACMDs are handled as illegal commands. Certain ACMD numbers are reserved, and ACMD41 has exceptions regarding APP_CMD status.

CMD6 switches or checks card functions in defined groups: Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength, and Power Limit. It is mandatory for Version 1.10 and later cards, valid in Transfer State, and returns R1 plus 512 bits of status. Mode 0 checks supported functions and current/power consumption; Mode 1 switches functions. Function 0 is default, and 0xF preserves the current setting. Power Limit controls total consumable card power and is mandatory in UHS-II mode.

High-Speed mode increases interface speed to 25 MB/sec using a 50 MHz clock and is enabled with CMD6 on Version 1.10 or later cards; support is optional. Command System extensions reserve CMD34-37, CMD50, and CMD57, whose interpretation depends on the selected command system.

CMD8 initializes Version 2.00 or later cards in Idle state by checking host supply voltage and returning R7 with echoed voltage and check pattern if supported. ACMD41’s CCS bit distinguishes SDSC from SDHC/SDXC. SDSC uses byte addressing and CMD16-defined block length, while SDHC/SDXC use 512-byte block addressing and fixed 512-byte memory access blocks.

The host may change or stop the SD bus clock, but must provide required post-transaction clocks and handle ACMD41 and busy-card restrictions. CRC7 protects commands, most responses, CID, and CSD; CRC16 protects data blocks. Commands with CRC errors, unsupported classes, invalid states, or undefined indexes are not executed and set status errors.

Read, write, and erase operations have defined timeout behavior. SDHC and SDXC hosts should use at least 100 ms for reads; write busy periods are generally 250 ms, with some SDXC cases up to 500 ms and UHS-II Data Burst busy up to 1 second.

Commands are 48-bit codewords on CMD, grouped into command classes with mandatory and optional support indicated in CSD/SCR. Responses include R1/R1b, R2, R3, R6, and R7. Card status, SD Status, and task status provide command, feature, and queued-task information.

Speed Class, UHS Speed Grade, and Video Speed Class define optional performance methods for real-time recording. Speed Class uses Allocation Units and Recording Units, with performance based on write, move, read, FAT update, and file-system conditions. SDXC differs by using only entirely free AUs, not supporting move performance, and requiring CMD20 for Speed Class recording control.

Japan’s government upgraded its assessment of business sentiment in April after the BOJ tankan showed improved corporate confidence, while maintaining that the economy is gradually recovering with some weakness. Exports, factory output, employment, and wages support recovery, though overseas economic uncertainty and financial market fluctuations remain concerns.

One police officer and two Barrio 18 gunmen were killed in San Salvador when gang members attacked officers searching for illegal weapons. Eight officers suffered superficial bullet wounds; four were released from hospital. One slain gunman was identified as a Barrio 18 leader suspected in more than a dozen murders.

The study proposes excess deaths and years of potential life lost (YPLL) as metrics for tracking racial mortality inequities in the U.S. Using CDC WONDER death certificate data from 1999 to 2020, the authors compared non-Hispanic Black and non-Hispanic White people under age 85, stratified by sex, age, and cause of death.

From 1999 to 2020, Black females experienced an estimated 658,356 excess deaths and 34.9 million excess YPLL compared with White females; Black males experienced 1,154,108 excess deaths and 47.0 million excess YPLL compared with White males. Excess mortality and YPLL declined from 1999 into the early 2010s, then plateaued through 2019. In 2020, both measures increased sharply, returning near earlier levels and coinciding with the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Heart disease accounted for the highest excess mortality among Black people, while perinatal deaths produced the highest YPLL rates. COVID-19 contributed additional excess mortality and YPLL in 2020. Disparities were especially large among infants, with Black-White mortality and YPLL rate ratios greater than 2.3 for those under 1 year old.

The authors conclude that excess deaths and YPLL among Black people remain substantial, that earlier gains were fragile and reversed by 2020, and that these measures could support public reporting and accountability for health equity.
A 26-year-old Aroland man has been charged with assault with a weapon after a 30-year-old man died from injuries in Aroland First Nation. Police continue to investigate, and a postmortem is planned.

Comcast said it abandoned its bid for most Twenty-First Century Fox assets, leaving Disney as the sole suitor for a potential $40 billion-plus deal. Comcast said it did not receive enough engagement to make a definitive offer. Disney’s talks with Fox continue and could reach a deal this month, sources said.

The passage explains simple moving averages (SMA) as technical indicators that average asset closing prices over a chosen period to identify trends, support, resistance, and potential buy or sell signals. Shorter SMAs react faster and generate more signals, while longer SMAs smooth volatility and are better for long-term trends. Backtests cited suggest short-term SMA strategies work better for mean reversion, while long-term SMAs, especially the 200-day SMA, work better for trend-following with lower drawdowns. SMA is described as lagging because it uses past prices, and it may give false signals in volatile or range-bound markets. The passage also compares SMA with EMA, noting EMA reacts faster by weighting recent prices more, while SMA is simpler and smoother. It concludes that SMA can be useful, especially when backtested and combined with other indicators or strategy parameters.

Colleges are preparing for potential Oct. 7 anniversary disruptions tied to Hamas’s 2023 attack on Israeli civilians. Columbia and the University of Maryland restricted protest planning or campus access due to safety concerns. Student groups, including Students for Justice in Palestine, plan events, and demonstrations are expected at other campuses.

Thirty-seven lawyers, including 10 incoming partners, are moving from Cadwalader, Wickersham & Taft to Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe, joining offices in Charlotte, London, Washington, D.C., and New York. The group focuses on collateralized loan obligations and asset-backed lending. Bloomberg Law and Law360 reported significant partner departures from Cadwalader this year, with Bloomberg counting 33 partners leaving or retiring. Recruiter Sabina Lippman said some partners are moving to firms with broader services and stronger cross-selling platforms. Bloomberg said Cadwalader’s revenue ranking has fallen from No. 39 in 2007 to No. 85 by 2024, partly due to market sensitivity in its core practices, though profits per equity partner averaged $3.7 million in 2024. Cadwalader is adding leadership and lawyers to bolster core practices but has lost nearly a fifth of its partnership this year.

Yahoo is in advanced talks to sell AOL to Italy’s Bending Spoons for about $1.4 billion, though no final deal has been signed. Bending Spoons has more than 300 million monthly users and recently agreed to take Vimeo private.

Music labels may reach AI licensing agreements within weeks with startups and larger firms, focusing on payment for AI-generated tracks and model training. Berkshire Hathaway is buying Occidental Petroleum’s chemical business for $9.7 billion, while Occidental plans to use proceeds mainly to reduce debt.

Tesla delivered a record 497,100 vehicles in Q3, above estimates, as buyers sought the expiring EV tax credit. FICO rose after announcing a licensing model expected to cut mortgage score fees by up to 50%.

Challenger reported September job cuts fell 37% from August, but year-to-date cuts are the highest since 2020, and planned hiring is the lowest since 2009. Caterpillar shares have rallied as investors link its turbines, mining equipment, and construction machinery to AI-related power and infrastructure demand. Wedbush said AI spending could accelerate tech M&A, naming several smaller firms as potential takeover targets.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 3, 2015, reporting that it published a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1. The information was furnished under Items 2.02 and 7.01 and was not deemed filed under the Exchange Act unless specifically incorporated. The report was signed by CFO Deepak Ahuja.

The passage describes example embodiments for operating carrier aggregation and multicarrier communication systems, particularly scheduling in OFDM-based LTE/5G systems. It outlines related patent applications, referenced figures, acronyms, and example physical-layer mechanisms including OFDM subcarriers, frame timing, resource grids, modulation, uplink/downlink processing, base station and wireless device architecture, and configurable interfaces.

It describes 5G network structures involving gNBs, eLTE eNBs, NG core interfaces, carrier aggregation, dual or multi-connectivity, master and secondary cell groups, timing advance groups, random access procedures, PUCCH groups, and time alignment timers. It also covers tight interworking between LTE and 5G RAN, centralized and non-centralized gNB deployment, CU/DU functional split options, and network slicing.

The passage further discusses use of unlicensed spectrum through LAA, listen-before-talk procedures, discontinuous transmission, and coexistence mechanisms. It also describes logical channel configuration, mapping to TTIs, numerologies, cells, logical channel prioritization, MAC multiplexing, grants/DCI, and bearer support for URLLC, eMBB, and mMTC.

Finally, it details bandwidth part configuration and operation, including DL/UL BWP sets, CORESETs, PDCCH monitoring, default and initial active BWPs, BWP activation/deactivation, timers, BWP switching, paired and unpaired spectrum behavior, search spaces, RMSI/OSI monitoring, group-common search space, and contention-based random access via initial active DL and UL BWPs.

The speaker thanks his predecessor and frames the inauguration as a new beginning for government and the nation. He calls for renewed faith in the American dream, unity, trust, competence, compassion, human rights, fair laws, preserved natural beauty, and dignity for all. He emphasizes that national strength abroad depends on strength at home and that U.S. foreign conduct should reflect domestic values. He advocates helping build a just, peaceful, humane world, maintaining quiet strength, fighting poverty, ignorance, and injustice, limiting armaments, and moving toward eliminating nuclear weapons. He closes by expressing hope that the nation will affirm its moral strength and expand the American dream.

This prospective hospital-based follow-up study assessed surgical diagnoses and postoperative outcomes among adults with suspected acute intestinal obstruction at Amana, Mwananyamala, and Temeke regional referral hospitals in Dar es Salaam from December 2021 to July 2022. Adults aged 18 years or older undergoing laparotomy for clinically or radiologically suspected obstruction were included, while referred patients with prior failed laparotomy were excluded.

The study followed 228 patients, totaling 1411 patient-days. Participants were predominantly male (172; 75.4%), with a male-to-female ratio of 3:1. Median age was 34 years, and median hospital stay was 4 days. Patients were recruited from Amana (51; 22%), Mwananyamala (95; 42%), and Temeke (82; 36%).

Adhesions were the most frequent surgical diagnosis, reported in 98 patients, followed by hernia in 48, volvulus in 37, and abdominal tumors in 20. Reported odds ratios were 5.7 for adhesions, 4.2 for volvulus, 2.0 for hernia, and 1.0 for abdominal tumors.

Postoperative outcomes included discharge home in 173 patients (76%), superficial surgical site infection in 20 (9%), wound dehiscence in 2 (0.9%), anastomotic leak in 1 (0.4%), referral to another hospital in 8 (3.5%), death in 12 (5.3%), and unknown outcomes in 12 (5.3%). Surgical outcomes did not significantly differ among the three hospitals. Tests for confounders and interactions were also non-significant at the 5% level.

The authors reported adhesions as the commonest diagnosis associated with intestinal obstruction, noted male predominance, and identified a crude mortality rate of 5.3%. They recommended further studies, including socioeconomic variables, to better explain unknown surgical outcomes.

DAWN-plasma was a prospective multicenter, randomized, open-label phase 2 trial evaluating standard of care plus convalescent plasma versus standard of care alone in hospitalized adult COVID-19 patients. Patients were randomized 2:1. In the full analysis set, 320 patients were in the plasma group and 163 in the control group, with baseline characteristics and concomitant COVID-19 therapies reported as well matched.

The intervention consisted of 4 units of convalescent plasma, totaling about 800–1000 mL, given over 48 hours: 2 units within 12 hours after randomization and 2 units 24–36 hours later. Median administered volume was 884 mL, and 80.7% of plasma units came from donors with neutralizing antibody titers of at least 1/320.

The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive and free of mechanical ventilation on Day 15. Results did not differ between groups: 83.7% in the convalescent plasma group versus 84.1% in the control group. No statistically significant differences were found for secondary endpoints, including mortality, Day 30 outcomes, clinical status, oxygenation, ventilation, hospitalization, laboratory measures, or vital signs.

Adverse events, serious adverse events, severe events, and fatal adverse events were similar between groups. Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 19 of 320 patients in the intervention group, and no TRALI cases were reported. The intervention did not alter the natural course of antibody titers. Higher neutralizing antibody titers at baseline and Day 6 correlated with better outcomes, but the increase in titers between Day 0 and Day 6 did not. The study concluded that early high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not significantly improve clinical outcomes in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

Averaging down is a trading or investing method where an investor buys more of a previously purchased stock after its price falls, lowering the average purchase price and reducing the price increase needed to break even. It can be used as part of a planned scale-in entry strategy, especially for long-term investors who understand the company, but it can also increase losses if the price continues falling. The passage distinguishes averaging down from averaging up and notes that short-term traders often focus on risk management rather than adding to losing positions. Break-even is calculated by dividing total purchase cost by total shares bought, excluding trading fees. A backtest on SPY using RSI signals found that averaging down produced similar capital growth to not averaging down but with smoother performance, improved metrics, reduced drawdowns, and more efficient capital use. The passage states that stocks may be better suited to averaging down because of mean reversion, while other markets may require backtesting and a margin of safety.

San Francisco State University’s Department of Biology will host Personalized Medicine 10.0 on June 2, 2017, reviewing a decade of conference topics, predictions, and future directions in personalized medicine. Since 2008, the conference has featured leaders from biotechnology, pharmaceutical, medical, and academic communities, addressing genomic health, clinical applications, business, regulation, ethics, and cultural impacts. The 2017 meeting will revisit areas including bioinformatics, data management, oncology, epigenetics, rare disease genomics, sequencing technologies, the microbiome, gene therapy, and genome editing. Opening keynote speaker Amylynne Santiago Volker will discuss genetic sequencing through the case of her son, Nicholas Volker. The conference was founded through collaboration between SF State biology chair Michael A. Goldman and SF State alumni Dan Maher, Ken Hitchner, and John Wulf. Registration is open to students, researchers, industry executives, health professionals, and community members.

The passage discusses using Bayesian optimization to improve therapeutic antibody properties, especially in low-data settings with costly wet lab experiments. It highlights uncertainty about how structural information should be incorporated into surrogate models, whether it helps optimize developability or binding properties, and how it compares with sequence-only methods. The work aims to evaluate structural and antibody-specific models, assess whether structure is necessary for strong optimization performance, and introduce a protein language model “soft constraint” as sequence-only prior information. Bayesian optimization is described as an iterative framework using surrogate models and acquisition functions to select new experiments.

Aberdeen Emerging Markets Equity Income Fund, Inc. is the consolidated entity formed from several Aberdeen fund reorganizations into the Aberdeen Chile Fund, renamed effective April 30, 2018, and traded on NYSE American as AEF. It follows a multi-cap emerging markets equity income strategy seeking current income and long-term capital appreciation, normally investing at least 80% of net assets in emerging market equities; leverage is permitted but not currently used. As of May 25, 2018, major holdings included Tencent Holdings, China Mobile, SAIC Motor, Samsung Electronics preferred securities, Vale, and Taiwan Semiconductor, with cash and equivalents at 5.81%. A tender offer and special capital gains distribution totaling about 41% of assets as of April 27, 2018, could further change the portfolio. The figures are unaudited, holdings may change, and no assurance is given that the Fund will meet its objectives.

Joy Lane, ex-girlfriend of Cleveland homicide suspect Steve Stephens, expressed condolences to victim Robert Godwin Sr.’s family and asked for privacy. Police say Stephens randomly shot Godwin, recorded the killing on Facebook Live, referenced Lane in videos, claimed additional killings, and remained under investigation as officials searched for him.

SpaceX’s Falcon 9 is set to launch Hewlett Packard Enterprise’s “Spaceborne Computer” to the International Space Station. The supercomputer can perform one trillion calculations per second and could help process large data sets in space, reducing the need to send massive amounts of raw satellite imagery to Earth. Unlike hardened space computers, it uses commercial hardware with software designed to protect it from hazards such as radiation. HPE will test whether it powers up and functions, then run experiments for a year. If successful, it could lead to more powerful space computers and support future Mars missions where communication delays or outages could make onboard data processing important.

The study compared a chest x-ray-based biological aging model (CXR-Age) with two epigenetic clocks, Horvath Age and DNAm PhenoAge, using data from 2,097 Project Baseline Health Study participants; 1,294 had DNA methylation data and 957 had plasma proteomics. CXR-Age was moderately correlated with chronological age, while both epigenetic clocks were highly correlated with chronological age. CXR-Age acceleration was not significantly associated with DNAm PhenoAge or Horvath age acceleration after adjustment.

Higher CXR-Age acceleration was associated with greater coronary artery calcium, higher ASCVD risk, worse pulmonary function, lower physical function, frailty measures, and disability scores. DNAm PhenoAge acceleration showed similar associations with coronary artery calcium, ASCVD risk, some pulmonary function measures, frailty, and disability, especially in older adults. Horvath age acceleration was not significantly associated with these cardiopulmonary, frailty, or disability measures.

Proteomic analysis found significant associations between CXR-Age acceleration and lower abundance of CDH13 and ApoD, while DNAm PhenoAge acceleration was associated with 13 proteins, including CDH13. No proteins were significantly associated with Horvath age acceleration. Manual review of chest radiographs showed that low CXR-Age acceleration images were often normal with clearer lung fields, while high CXR-Age acceleration images often showed varied lung or thoracic findings, though some had no clear abnormalities.

The authors conclude that CXR-Age is associated with worse cardiopulmonary function and frailty, while DNAm PhenoAge shows related but not identical associations. They note that these clocks may capture different aspects of biological aging and that future work should assess links with incident age-related disease and medical decision-making.

The study addresses automated extraction and normalization of dysmorphic findings from free-text dysmorphology physical examinations in electronic health records using Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms. The authors created a standardized EHR dysmorphology documentation system, collected and de-identified free-text observations, and manually annotated a corpus of 3,826 organ system observations from 1,655 individuals with HPO terms, including positive and negated findings.

They developed PhenoID, a two-step transformer-based pipeline. Its extractor identifies spans referring to abnormal findings while ignoring normal findings, and its normalizer maps each extracted mention to an HPO term ID. The system uses Bio-ClinicalBERT and was trained with both annotated observations and generated examples from HPO preferred terms and synonyms. The authors also evaluated strategies for handling disjoint and overlapping mentions.

PhenoID achieved an F1 score of 0.717 for normalization and outperformed six comparator systems, including PhenoTagger, PhenoBERT, NeuralCR, txt2HPO, and doc2HPO variants. When given gold-standard spans, PhenoID’s normalizer achieved an F1 score of 0.820, near the reported inter-annotator F1 score of 0.844, indicating span extraction as a major performance limitation. Error analysis identified issues including imperfect ontology coverage, descriptive clinical wording, misplaced model attention, and prediction of hyperonyms. The authors conclude that PhenoID achieves state-of-the-art performance for this task, while further improvements in extraction, normalization, and semantic understanding are needed.

London-St. Thomas unemployment rose to 5.5% in September, while the labour force fell by 3,000 and was down 9,300 from a year earlier. Only about 75% of residents aged 25-54 are working, the lowest among 15 major Ontario cities. A King’s University College Poverty Research Centre study found only about half of working-aged Londoners have secure, full-time permanent jobs with benefits; others are in part-time, temporary, contract, casual or self-employed roles. The study linked precarious work to stress, depression, anger and family impacts, with young adults and minorities more likely to face unstable employment. National unemployment stayed at 6.2%, while Ontario added 35,000 jobs and unemployment fell to 5.6%.

New research in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences suggests that harnessing competition among pathogens inside a patient can help existing drugs work despite drug resistance and may prevent resistance from emerging. Researchers at Penn State limited a nutrient used by malaria parasites in infected mice while administering traditional drugs. When the nutrient was available, treatment failed in 40% of mice due to resistant strains; when the nutrient was limited, infections did not rebound. Further tests showed resistant parasites survived nutrient limitation when alone, but failed to grow when competing with drug-sensitive parasites. The researchers describe this as a proof of principle for using ecological manipulation alongside drugs, and suggest future work should identify resources that resistant strains need more than sensitive strains and determine how and when to limit them.

The passage describes a patent-related method, apparatus, system, and computer-readable medium for automatically classifying objects represented by 3D point clouds, including those generated by LIDAR systems. It reviews LIDAR range detection techniques, including chirped, heterodyne, homodyne, and phase-encoded approaches, and explains how point clouds can be produced from measured ranges.

The disclosed classification method obtains a 3D point cloud of an object, extracts surface normals to define translationally and rotationally invariant coordinate systems, and derives feature variables for points in the cloud. It computes a first classification statistic, such as a spin image, and a second classification statistic, such as a covariance matrix, then compares each to trained statistics for a fixed set of object classes using methods such as dimensionality reduction, k-d trees, nearest-neighbor search, clustering, and distance measures. If the two classifiers disagree, a third classifier, such as iterative closest point matching, compares the point cloud only with model point clouds for the two candidate classes to assign the object in near real time. If the object does not match the known classes, it may be treated as unknown.

The passage also describes LIDAR hardware configurations using laser sources, modulators, splitters, optical couplers, detectors, and processors configured to generate or process point clouds and classify objects. Example experiments using a BLACKMORE HRS-3D LIDAR system classified objects such as cones, boxes, pipes, pistols, cubes, and toy guns, with reported class prediction results. The classified object can be used to operate a device, display information, communicate class data, guide a projectile, or control a vehicle.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended April 1, 2017. For the quarter, net sales were $52.9 billion, up from $50.6 billion a year earlier, and net income was $11.0 billion, up from $10.5 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $2.10, compared with $1.90. For the first six months of fiscal 2017, net sales were $131.2 billion and net income was $28.9 billion.

Quarterly net sales increased primarily due to growth in Services, Mac and Other Products, partly offset by foreign currency weakness. iPhone sales were $33.2 billion, iPad sales were $3.9 billion, Mac sales were $5.8 billion, Services sales were $7.0 billion and Other Products sales were $2.9 billion. Net sales increased in the Americas, Europe, Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific, but declined 14% in Greater China.

Gross margin was 38.9%, down from 39.4% a year earlier, primarily due to higher product cost structures and currency effects. Operating expenses rose to $6.5 billion, including $2.8 billion in research and development and $3.7 billion in selling, general and administrative expenses. Other income, net, increased to $587 million.

As of April 1, 2017, total assets were $334.5 billion, including $15.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents, $51.9 billion in short-term marketable securities and $189.7 billion in long-term marketable securities. Total liabilities were $200.5 billion, including $10.0 billion in commercial paper and $84.5 billion in long-term debt. Shareholders’ equity was $134.1 billion.

For the first six months of fiscal 2017, operating activities generated $39.6 billion in cash, investing activities used $33.3 billion and financing activities used $11.6 billion. Apple repurchased $18.0 billion of common stock and paid $6.1 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents during the period.

Apple reported ongoing tax matters, including the European Commission’s State Aid Decision regarding Ireland, which Apple and Ireland appealed. It also described legal proceedings involving Samsung, supply concentration risks, operating lease commitments of $8.2 billion and recent accounting pronouncements.

Children receive their first mobile phones at different ages across countries. In Germany, fewer young children appear to own smartphones than in the United States, where reports show many children get smartphones and service plans by ages 8 to 12. Across parts of Europe, a 2015 study found 46% of children ages 9 to 16 owned smartphones, with school rules and costs affecting use.

Studies cited show varied ownership elsewhere: in South Korea, 72% of children owned smartphones by ages 11 to 12; in Taiwan, cell phone use rose from 45% at age 11 to 71% at age 15; and in Turkey, most surveyed parents favored ages 12 to 17 for a first phone. Reports also found mobile phone access among students in South Africa, lower ownership rates among children in Ghana and Malawi, and a median first-use age of 8 among Australian primary school children studied.

The American Academy of Pediatrics says there is no single “right” age for a child’s first phone, but recommends limits on digital media use, monitoring content and apps, avoiding screens before bedtime, and keeping meals screen-free.

The passage presents the development of a classical EAM potential for the W-H-He system to support radiation damage simulations in fusion reactor materials. Tungsten is considered a plasma-facing material, but irradiation and light gas implantation can cause defects, gas bubbles, swelling, hardening, embrittlement, and tritium retention. Existing W-H-He potentials capture some defect energetics but often neglect relaxation volumes or inaccurately model voids and surfaces. The new potential builds on the Mason W-H potential and adds helium interactions to better reproduce DFT-based binding energies, relaxation volumes, gas behavior, and void-related properties.

The fitting uses a generalized Finnis-Sinclair formulation with spline-based functions and electron densities that may take negative values. A weighted loss function compares defect formation energies, relaxation volumes, binding energies, and gaseous configuration energies against DFT data. Optimization uses an importance-sampling-like global method with Gaussian mixture models, followed by Simplex minimization. DFT data are taken from literature and supplemented with new Vasp calculations for hydrogen-helium defect clusters.

Parameterization uses physics-informed priors, including ZBL short-range behavior. Tungsten-helium interactions are constrained to reflect weak helium-metal bonding. The helium embedding function models repulsion from electron density. Helium-helium interactions are fitted to both virial coefficient data and high-pressure hcp helium DFT data. Hydrogen-helium interactions are fitted to DFT dimer data and refined for defect properties while preserving vacuum behavior. A DFT charge density comparison is introduced to evaluate qualitative electronic interactions involving helium in tungsten.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell/GeForce RTX 50 Series architecture adds FP4 support in fifth-generation Tensor Cores to reduce generative AI model memory use and improve performance. FP4 can require less than half the memory of FP16 with minimal quality loss using NVIDIA TensorRT Model Optimizer. For example, FLUX.dev drops from over 23GB VRAM at FP16 to under 10GB with FP4.

Blackwell improves ray tracing through fourth-generation RT Cores, including doubled ray-triangle intersection throughput over the prior generation, support for Mega Geometry, Triangle Cluster Intersection Engines, Opacity Micromap Engines, and Linear Swept Spheres. Mega Geometry enables ray tracing of full-fidelity geometry in systems such as Unreal Engine 5 Nanite by using cluster-level acceleration structures and partitioned top-level acceleration structures to reduce BVH build costs and CPU overhead. It is supported across NVIDIA ray tracing APIs and RTX GPUs starting with Turing.

Linear Swept Spheres provide hardware ray intersection support for strand-like geometry such as hair, fur, and grass, offering about 2x faster rendering and about 5x less VRAM use than DOTS in common hair-rendering cases. Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 improves GPU thread reordering efficiency and supports better ray tracing and neural shading performance.

The AI Management Processor is a programmable GPU context scheduler using a dedicated RISC-V processor. It offloads scheduling from the CPU, lowers latency, improves workload coordination, and supports smoother gaming and multitasking by managing graphics and AI workloads more predictably.

Blackwell adds hardware encode and decode support for 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC video. Ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR, adds AV1 Ultra High Quality mode, and supports faster exports; the RTX 5090 supports up to three encoders and two decoders. Sixth-generation NVDEC improves H.264 decoding speed and adds 4:2:2 support. DisplayPort 2.1b supports up to 80 Gbps using UHBR 20 for displays such as 8K at 165Hz and 4K at 480Hz with DSC.

Blackwell Max-Q focuses on power efficiency through advanced power gating, separate voltage rails, accelerated frequency switching, and low-latency sleep. Clock adjustments can occur 1000x faster than previous architectures, and deep sleep entry is 10x faster than Ada. In a small language model inference example, power savings of up to 50% are described.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, a transformer-based model for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, and improved frame pacing through enhanced Flip Metering. Multi Frame Generation can generate up to three additional frames per rendered frame, with a frame generation AI model that is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than the prior method. Transformer models improve temporal stability, reduce ghosting, increase motion detail, and improve lighting reconstruction.

Blackwell introduces developer-created neural shaders using Cooperative Vectors APIs for DX12 and Vulkan, allowing Tensor Cores to be accessed through shaders. NVIDIA describes neural texture compression, neural materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces as applications. Neural Texture Compression reduces memory use in one demo from 1110MB to 333MB. RTX Neural Faces uses a real-time generative AI model and 3D pose data to infer more natural-looking faces.

The passage also outlines Blackwell GPU products. GB202 is the flagship GPU with 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT Cores, 768 Tensor Cores, and a 512-bit memory interface, used for the RTX 5090. GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT Cores, 336 Tensor Cores, and a 256-bit interface, used for RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 has 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT Cores, 200 Tensor Cores, and a 192-bit interface, used for RTX 5070. The document ends with NVIDIA’s legal, warranty, liability, trademark, and copyright notices.

Residents from several Southeast Alaska communities are being trained through REAP’s Home Energy Leader Program to conduct affordable household energy assessments. The program aims to help diesel-powered villages reduce high electric bills by identifying low-cost efficiency improvements, such as replacing bulbs with LEDs or changing coffee makers. While the assessments are less detailed than private audits, they cost $25 instead of thousands. Participants from Kake, Angoon, Hoonah, Yakutat and Metlakatla learned to evaluate appliances, windows, lighting and other household energy uses. In one Juneau home, assessors found simple changes could cut the electric bill by nearly 10 percent. The program runs through July 31.

The royal commission exposed widespread misconduct in financial planning at banks and AMP, including false witnessing, conflicted advice, trailing commissions, insurance rorts and fees for no service. The revelations prompted reversals and apologies despite years of whistleblower testimony, media reports and parliamentary inquiries.

Commercial property owners in Southern Nevada have been charged trash fees by Republic Services that were not approved by local lawmakers, despite ordinances requiring approval for fees outside existing agreements. The Las Vegas City Council is set to introduce an ordinance codifying several such fees, including container delivery, removal, exchange and dry run charges. Republic says it reports supplemental service fees annually to municipalities and considers that process approval. Some local officials said they do not recall approving Republic fees, while municipal responses varied. Henderson said the charges may violate its ordinance and will be reviewed; Clark County said commissioner approval is not needed.

Guinness is partnering with former Arsenal footballer Thierry Henry for its Made of Black campaign, marking its first collaboration with a footballer. Henry will work with Guinness in Nigeria and across Africa to highlight people who embody the campaign’s spirit. Guinness Nigeria Marketing Director Adenike Adebola called him an inspirational ambassador. The Made of Black campaign launched in 2014 on MTV Base and celebrates African attitude and identity. Guinness will also engage football fans through Fanzone activations, live football and music experiences, and continued EPL broadcast sponsorship on DStv.

The passage describes patent applications and embodiments for implantable medical devices, particularly cochlear implants, with magnet management features for compatibility with external magnetic fields such as MRI. The devices include an implanted magnet or magnet apparatus within a body, often elastomeric, with structural components such as plates that sandwich the magnet. When an external magnetic field applies torque to the magnet, initial rotation pushes the plates apart, generating resistive forces from elastomeric material, springs, housing structures, or plate geometry to limit further rotation. Embodiments include sliding magnet interfaces, magnet containers allowing revolution, low-friction surfaces, shaped plates, tracks, bumpers, and slits in the elastomeric body for magnet insertion or removal. The teachings are described mainly for cochlear implants but may apply to other hearing prostheses and implanted medical devices with magnets.

This medRxiv preprint examines causal relationships among gut microbiota, plasma metabolites, and fibromyalgia (FM) using Mendelian randomization (MR) with publicly available European GWAS summary data. The study analyzed gut microbiome taxa from MiBioGen, 1,400 plasma metabolites from Chen et al., and FM outcomes from FinnGen.

Bidirectional MR identified six gut microbial taxa causally associated with FM. Family Enterobacteriaceae, genus Butyricicoccus, genus Coprococcus1, and order Enterobacteriales were associated with reduced FM risk, while genus Eggerthella and genus Ruminococcaceae UCG005 were associated with increased susceptibility. No reverse causality was detected.

MR analysis identified 82 plasma metabolites associated with FM, including 44 known metabolites, 24 metabolite ratios, and 14 unknown metabolites. Enrichment analyses implicated caffeine metabolism, α-linolenic acid metabolism, GLP-1 synthesis/secretion/inactivation, and incretin regulation. Key FM-associated metabolites included AFMU, 7-Methylxanthine, 1-Methylxanthine, EPA, SDA, D-Mannose, and Oleoyl-EA.

Further MR analysis linked specific gut taxa to metabolites. Mediation analysis found that 2,3-dihydroxypyridine and palmitoylcholine may mediate the effects of Enterobacteriaceae and Enterobacteriales on FM, with mediation proportions of 14.91% and 12.34%, respectively.

The authors suggest dietary strategies for FM patients, including limiting caffeine, increasing omega-3 fatty acids, adopting a low-glycemic-index diet, and reducing high-oxalate foods. Limitations include lack of demographic subgroup data, restriction mainly to European ancestry datasets, and the need for experimental and clinical validation. The study reports no additional ethical approval requirement, no conflicts of interest, and no specific funding.
TCI Fund Management said Zodiac Aerospace shares were worth 7-10 euros and urged Safran to drop its bid, citing losses and unrealistic margin forecasts.

The article argues that most bullish candlestick patterns have little predictive value, but three showed decent results in quantified backtests on SPY from its 1993 inception to October 2021. The tested patterns were Bearish Engulfing, Three Outside Down, and Bullish Harami, using an exit rule of selling when the close is higher than the previous day’s high. Bearish Engulfing produced 296 trades, 0.53% average gain, 5% CAGR, 71% win rate, 16% max drawdown, and 2.5 profit factor. Three Outside Down produced 112 trades, 0.7% average gain, 2.3% CAGR, 78% win rate, 14% max drawdown, and 2.6 profit factor. Bullish Harami produced 306 trades, 0.33% average gain, 3.1 CAGR, 76% win rate, 25% max drawdown, and 1.65 profit factor. The article notes skepticism toward candlestick patterns because most advice lacks quantified testing and focuses mainly on entries rather than exits.

The agreement sets minimum quantities for Congo products to be purchased for import into the United Kingdom and United States, with prices agreed between Belgium and the purchasing government and payment by usual methods. The UK is to ensure Congo products it purchases are not disadvantaged by customs duties compared with British colonial products. The UK and US agree to try to deliver industrial and other supplies to the Congo within wartime limits. Belgium is to maintain controls in the Congo against transactions aiding enemy powers and establish an export licensing system aligned with British-administered African territories.

In a related airgram, the US Department of State comments on the proposed tripartite agreement, requesting agreed price lists, noting foreign exchange arrangements, opposing guarantees of shipping, questioning payment for unshipped commodities in the Congo, and suggesting the US and UK obtain options on entire outputs of listed products and include provisions for development work in the Congo.

Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell said demand for AI computing power remains “tremendous” and that while too many AI data centers may eventually be built, he sees no signs of that yet. Dell’s server networking business grew 58% last year and 69% last quarter. Shares rose over 3% after the company raised its long-term annual revenue growth target to 7%–9% and its diluted earnings per share growth expectation to 15%. Dell also said it plans to ship $20 billion worth of AI servers in fiscal 2026, double last year’s total.

The passage lists QuantifiedStrategies.com posts on market timing and trading strategies, including Bitcoin market timing, Sy Harding’s Seasonal Timing Strategy, Yale Hirsch’s Best 6 Months Timing Model, Coppock Curve, Fabian Market Timing Model, PENTAD Timing Model, Supertrend Indicator, market regime indicators, and backtested strategy setups. It describes these articles as covering rules, backtests, performance, ETFs, risk analysis, and trading models. The site is managed by Hakan Samuelsson and Oddmund Groette, independent full-time traders and investors with over 20 years of trading experience.
The appeal from New York County Supreme Court orders was unanimously withdrawn under the parties’ January 11, 2010 stipulation.

Turkish prosecutors issued detention warrants for 133 current and former ministry personnel over alleged links to the Gülen movement, mainly based on alleged ByLock use; four were reportedly still on active duty. Separate operations on Thursday led to detentions of women, dismissed teachers, military personnel and other suspects across multiple provinces, including Uşak, Aksaray, Trabzon, Adana and Bitlis-based investigations. The passage states Turkish authorities view ByLock as a Gülen movement communication tool. Since the July 15, 2016 coup attempt, which killed 249 people, the government has blamed the movement, while Fethullah Gülen denied involvement. The Justice Ministry said 50,510 people had been arrested and 169,013 faced legal proceedings on coup charges, with over 150,000 public employees suspended or dismissed.

Leaked benchmarks suggest Nvidia’s Titan V outperforms the Titan Xp and GTX 1080 Ti despite lower boost clocks, scoring 32,774 in Fire Strike versus about 28,000 for the others. Its Volta architecture, HBM2, and 652.8 GB/s memory bandwidth deliver strong gaming performance at 1440p. Priced around $3,000, it targets prosumers and developers, especially for AI workloads.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that on September 20, 2016, its Board amended Section 1.14 of its bylaws regarding proxy access, including clarifications on fund groups, loaned shares, indemnification, and lowering the re-nomination voting support threshold from 25% to 15%. Microsoft also announced its 2016 Annual Shareholders Meeting would be held on November 30, 2016, with shareholders of record as of September 30, 2016 eligible to vote. Exhibit 3.2 contains the bylaws.

David Moyes urged Sunderland’s players to create more chances for Jermain Defoe and improve their own performances as the club fights relegation. Sunderland are bottom of the Premier League, seven points from safety with 10 games remaining, and face Watford, Leicester City and Manchester United in an eight-day span.

Researchers collected enough DNA from beluga whales Qila and Aurora, who died at the Vancouver Aquarium in 2016 from an unidentified toxin, to sequence a complete beluga genome. They say it may help study beluga health, evolution, and conservation in changing environments.

Erie Federal Credit Union reopened the former Glenwood School as its new corporate headquarters and ninth branch after an 18-month renovation. The full-service location includes banking services, a drive-through, ATM, night depository, safe deposit boxes and a community room. The project used local designers and contractors, preserved school history, returned the property to tax rolls, and provides space for future growth.

The passage discusses RSI, ADX, and IBS as short-term trading indicators used in mean-reversion and trend-following strategies. RSI measures price momentum and overbought or oversold conditions, with shorter periods such as two or three days performing best in stock backtests. ADX measures trend strength but not direction, with backtests suggesting 5–10 day periods and thresholds around 30–40. IBS measures the close relative to the bar’s high and low, giving bullish signals at low values and bearish signals at high values.

Backtests are presented for QQQ and SPY. A simple IBS strategy on QQQ produced a 0.78% average gain per trade, 12.1% CAGR, and 38% market exposure. An RSI strategy on SPY produced a 0.98% average gain per trade, 7.5% CAGR, and 41% exposure. An ADX strategy on SPY produced 28 trades, 6.5% CAGR, and 63% exposure. Combining indicators improved results, with one SPY strategy producing 270 trades, a 0.86% average gain, 14% exposure, and a 56% risk-adjusted return; in QQQ it produced a 1.3% average gain and no losing years since 2000. The passage emphasizes simplicity, backtesting, and that no strategy guarantees profits.

Citadel Securities hired Anthony Cronin from Societe Generale to lead Treasuries trading in Europe, expanding its market-making coverage across European hours, parts of Asia, and the Middle East. The firm is aiming to become a top global market maker in dollar rates products and has also hired Michele How for fixed-income sales in London. Citadel Securities has about 100 U.S. Treasuries clients in Asia and Europe and expects that to double this year. Since entering direct Treasuries market-making with investors in 2016, it has nearly tripled counterparties and nearly quadrupled average daily volume. The firm may seek Federal Reserve primary dealer status after adding required products such as TIPS and strips.

The Chaikin Oscillator, developed by Marc Chaikin in the 1980s, measures accumulation/distribution momentum and oscillates around zero. It is calculated using the money flow multiplier, money flow volume, Accumulation/Distribution Line, and the difference between short and long EMAs of the ADL. Positive values indicate accumulation, while negative values suggest distribution; signals may come from zero-line crosses and bullish or bearish divergences. Quantified S&P 500 tests found limited predictive value: one zero-cross strategy produced a 2.4% CAGR over 20 years, while other tested strategies had modest average trade gains, profit factors around 1.6–1.76, and drawdowns of 17%–37%.

The passage argues that Marine Le Pen’s chances in France’s presidential election may be improving despite predictions against her. François Fillon’s scandal has weakened a key rival, while riots in immigrant-heavy suburbs after an alleged police assault could boost Le Pen’s anti-immigration, tough-on-crime campaign. The author notes parallels to past political surprises like Brexit and Trump’s victory.

Dwyane Wade, Gabrielle Union and Wade’s son Zion visited Miami’s Frost Museum of Science, attending a planetarium show, seeing fish, touching stingrays and eating tacos. Wade also responded to a Twitter critic.

University of Kansas researcher Brock Ternes surveyed 864 Kansans and found that well ownership is significantly correlated with increased watering during droughts, with conservation varying by well type. He said well owners may use more water because they are more aware of supplies and rely on groundwater to sustain crops when precipitation is inadequate. The High Plains Aquifer, heavily used for irrigation, may stop supporting some southwestern Kansas irrigation wells within 25 years unless pumping is reduced. Ternes argues well owners should be studied as a distinct group in drought and groundwater conservation research.

Players said frustration has built after missed chances and home losses, but the team has refocused and hopes for its best effort. They believe they have created opportunities and controlled play at times but need to finish, limit turnovers, execute better on entries and power plays, and take more shots. They also said being on the road may help reduce distractions, and they are not concerned about preparation or warmups.

Leon Cooperman said the bull market is in a late stage marked by excessive valuations and crowd-driven momentum, echoing a Warren Buffett warning about market exuberance. He said AI company valuations are “ridiculously high,” while the S&P 500 has risen nearly 40% from April lows. The Buffett Indicator is at 217%, above prior bubble-era peaks. Cooperman said stocks are risky but still less risky than bonds because inflation erodes bond returns.

Several major school districts approved teacher union contracts but later faced funding shortfalls. Philadelphia agreed to 3% annual raises, then sought permission to borrow up to $1.5 billion amid delayed state funding and projected deficits. Fairfax County and Baltimore County renegotiated raises after receiving insufficient funding. Chicago approved a $1.5 billion union contract while facing a $734 million deficit, later balancing its budget through refinancing and other measures. U.S. public school debt rose from $415 billion in 2013 to more than $586 billion in 2023.

The passage describes an autonomous vehicle management system for improving safety in autonomous vehicles and machines. The system receives sensor data, generates and updates an internal map of the vehicle and its environment, and uses goals, safety considerations, localization data, and AI-based techniques to create a safe plan of action. It can control vehicle systems such as braking, steering, propulsion, auxiliary systems, and specialized equipment.

The system may use neural networks for object detection and classification, reinforcement learning for action selection, and “what-if” simulations to evaluate possible future scenarios before choosing actions. It can generate multiple modified internal maps to simulate different object behaviors, parameter values, or focused regions relevant to a goal.

The system can dynamically control sensors by changing what data they capture or transmit, when they transmit it, and how it is communicated. This includes adjusting resolution, field of view, zoom, transmission rate, or turning sensors on or off. Sensor control helps update the internal map with relevant information while reducing unnecessary data.

Additional safety measures include assessing AI model confidence by comparing inference data to training data, overriding low-confidence predictions, using safety indicators for reinforcement learning decisions, and providing users with information about planned future actions and reasons for those actions. The system includes subsystems for sensor interfacing, localization, perception, planning, controls, and information output.

The passage describes methods and apparatus for ACK/NACK feedback in wireless networks with multiple transmission reception points (TRPs), particularly in 5G NR. A base station may send a UE information on PDCCH monitoring occasions for each TRP, whether ACK/NACK feedback bundling across TRPs is allowed, rules for bundling, and downlink assignment index (DAI) definitions. A UE may use this information to determine ACK/NACK codebook size and transmit either joint bundled feedback to multiple TRPs or separate feedback to individual TRPs via PUCCH. The disclosure describes joint DAIs, which count PDCCH grants across TRPs and carriers, and independent DAIs, which count grants per TRP. It also outlines wireless system architecture, NR frame structures, base station and UE processing, and flowcharts for base station and UE operations supporting multi-TRP ACK/NACK feedback.

Big Brothers Big Sisters of Mercer County provided new unassembled bicycles for seven children awaiting mentors. The children built bikes with local law enforcement officers, FBI staff, and other volunteers during an event promoting teamwork, mentoring, and stronger ties with Trenton law enforcement. Each team will also build a second bicycle for another child.
Tippecanoe Middle School in Tipp City released its principal’s list and honor roll students for grades six through eight for the second grading period of the 2017-18 school year.

The SEC phase sets up 32-bit C execution and stack. AGESA provides AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK. AMD initialization uses PEIM modules, including one for processor initialization and AmdCpuEarlyInit PPI publication.

C-BerryTrans is a C++ program licensed under GNU GPL 3.0 for computing Berry curvature–driven anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) and anomalous Nernst conductivity (ANC) within an ab initio framework. It extracts eigenvalues and momentum-matrix elements from WIEN2k calculations and evaluates Berry curvature using a Kubo-like formula, avoiding Wannier interpolation and associated dependence on Wannier-function quality.

The code integrates band-resolved Berry curvature over the full Brillouin zone. AHC is calculated with Fermi–Dirac weighting, while ANC uses an entropy-function weighting. Spin–orbit coupling is required for these transverse responses, and the implemented intrinsic formulas are most appropriate for clean to moderately dirty regimes and low-temperature conditions.

C-BerryTrans supports dense k-mesh calculations, OpenMP parallelization over k-points, binary storage of Berry-curvature data, and post-processing over ranges of temperature and chemical potential. It includes modules for generating full-Brillouin-zone k-lists, controlling memory use by batching k-points, modifying WIEN2k input energy windows, and visualizing weighted Berry-curvature quantities through `berryTrans_plot.py`.

The workflow involves preparing a spin–orbit-coupled, self-consistent WIEN2k calculation; defining parameters in `C-BerryTrans.input`; running `berryTrans` to compute and store Berry curvature; and using `postBerryTrans` to calculate AHC or ANC. The code has been tested on materials including Fe, Pd, Fe3Al, and Co2FeAl, with results compared to literature values.

VentureWire’s Nov. 17, 2000 newsletter reported staff cuts at govWorks, Whitney & Co.’s plan to raise a $2.5 billion global fund, eHitex naming Robert Lewis CEO, and PlanetOut’s planned merger with Gay.com parent Online Partners. The issue also covered executive appointments, new board members, Japan-focused venture fund activity, Kodak venture team hires, and a correction about GreenOrder’s board.

Markets shifted risk-off after a week of earnings, economic data, Fed signals, and policy uncertainty. Earnings were generally stronger than expected, with many S&P 500 companies beating EPS and revenue estimates, but investors sold into good news. GDP beat expectations at 3%, though tariff-related distortions and weak personal spending clouded the reading. Payrolls disappointed at 73,000 jobs, with large downward revisions, while unemployment rose slightly to 4.2%. The Fed remained data-dependent amid inflation, tariff, and labor-force uncertainty, though markets priced in likely rate cuts. Major indexes fell, technical indicators weakened, most sectors declined, and market internals turned negative, suggesting a tactical pullback.

CompareCards presents partner credit cards with 0% introductory APR offers ranging from 12 to 21 months, aimed at consumers carrying balances or planning large purchases. The page highlights cards from Discover, Bank of America, Citi, Capital One, and others, featuring cash back, travel rewards, sign-up bonuses, balance transfer offers, and no-annual-fee options. It notes that low or 0% interest cards can reduce borrowing costs, explains fixed versus variable APRs, and states that introductory rates may revert to regular APRs after the promotional period. The site says compensation from listed companies does not influence its ratings or reviews.

Swiss Economic Affairs Minister Johann Schneider-Ammann said his ministry will consider arms industry requests to ease weapons export rules, including longer licences and lifting a ban on exports to countries in internal armed conflict. The industry cites falling exports, competition and job risks. Critics say exporting to civil war countries would violate neutrality. SRF reported parliament may support further easing.

World stocks and the dollar rose on Monday as fears over a U.S.-North Korea nuclear standoff eased after causing the biggest weekly equity losses of 2017. European and Asia-Pacific shares rebounded, though Tokyo stocks fell despite strong Japanese growth data due to concerns over the yen’s recent surge. The dollar gained against the yen and Swiss franc as safe-haven demand weakened. Analysts cited easing geopolitical tensions and solid corporate earnings and global growth. Japanese growth data and expectations of global recovery pushed bond yields higher, while upcoming Federal Reserve and European Central Bank minutes were seen as possible clues on policy. Softer-than-expected Chinese data had limited market impact but weighed on oil prices.

The passage introduces a hybrid MoM–GSM framework for multiscale electromagnetic problems involving detailed antennas interacting with electrically large environments such as radomes, reflectors, or biological media. Unlike prior MoM–T-matrix approaches, the proposed method models the large surrounding structure with MoM while representing the antenna through a compact generalized scattering matrix, reducing unknowns and enabling modular reuse. The framework can also be extended to GSM–PO and GSM+T-matrix variants for reflectors or structures suited to spherical-wave expansion. The formulation decomposes total fields into incident, structure-scattered, and antenna-radiated components, solves penetrable structures using PMCHWT-based MoM with RWG basis functions, and couples the structure currents to antenna spherical-wave coefficients through GSM relations.

The passage explains defensive approaches to the Single/Double Offense, which uses double and down screens to free shooters. NBA teams generally avoid switching because it can create post mismatches, preferring “Show and Recover,” where defenders step out to force shooters wide, chase under screens, then recover to deny screeners in the post. Defenders also influence shooters away from preferred sides, pressure ballhandlers toward sidelines, deny passes, and pack weakside help toward the ball.

An alternative “All Out SOS Disruption” strategy has the defense initiate contact, switch selectively, and trap the shooter on the wing to disrupt offensive routes. This includes pushing the point guard toward sideline pushpoints, using contact switches, rotating into post fronts and Triangle “I” help positions, denying reversal passes, and trapping post mismatches. The passage stresses timely rotations as the ball leaves the passer’s hands and applying basic SOS rules if further screening or baseline-drive scenarios occur.

Reykjavik has endured an unusually gray, wet summer, with meteorologists looking back to 1914 for worse May and June records. While western Europe, Britain and Scandinavia experience a heat wave, high pressure has shifted the jet stream, sending clouds and rain over Iceland. Reykjavik had only 70 hours of sunshine in June, a cooler-than-average warmest day, and rain every day in May. The poor weather has fueled forecast-watching, boosted demand for last-minute beach holidays and tanning salons, and hurt ice cream vendors, house painters and outdoor pools. Tourism continues, though one campsite reports slightly fewer guests, with many campers adjusting. A historian noted conditions were worse in rainy June 1914 and expressed hope that the rest of the summer may improve.

UBS will continue dividend increases and a USD 2 billion share buyback programme from mid-2025 to 2027 despite Swiss regulatory calls for higher capital buffers. CEO Sergio Ermotti said Credit Suisse integration is progressing, with Swiss systems consolidation expected by early 2026, and that UBS can meet capital expectations without limiting shareholder returns. Analysts view the stance as a sign of strength but note challenges if market conditions worsen.

Russian authorities disputed Captain Scullun’s indemnity claims for the detention of the Cape Horn Pigeon, calling his $45,000 lost-profit estimate exaggerated and suggesting $2,500 as sufficient compensation absent vouchers. Scullun reported the vessel was seized while whaling, taken to Vladivostok, and the crew left without food or shelter. U.S. representatives requested an investigation and aid for the crew. Russian officials later reported the bark’s release and said the allegation about lack of food or shelter was under inquiry, while asserting Scullun had refused offered lodging and food.

Apple Inc.’s 2019 Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended September 28, 2019. Apple designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells related services. Its products include iPhone, Mac, iPad, and Wearables, Home and Accessories, while services include digital content stores, streaming services, AppleCare, iCloud, licensing and other offerings.

Apple reported 2019 total net sales of $260.2 billion, down 2% from $265.6 billion in 2018, and net income of $55.3 billion, down from $59.5 billion. The decline was driven mainly by lower iPhone sales, partly offset by higher Wearables, Home and Accessories and Services sales. Services revenue rose to $46.3 billion, and Wearables, Home and Accessories rose to $24.5 billion. iPhone revenue fell 14% to $142.4 billion.

Apple sells through direct and indirect channels, which accounted for 31% and 69% of 2019 net sales, respectively. No single customer accounted for more than 10% of net sales in 2019, 2018 or 2017. The company had about 137,000 full-time equivalent employees as of September 28, 2019.

Apple identified major risks including global economic conditions, intense competition, product transitions, dependence on resellers, component supply constraints, outsourcing partners, legal and regulatory matters, data security, foreign exchange fluctuations, credit risk and tax changes. The company repurchased $67.1 billion of common stock and paid $14.1 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents during 2019.
A 1932 court opinion by Justice Wolfe lists parties and counsel.

President Trump addressed the United Nations, emphasizing national sovereignty, patriotism, and the responsibility of leaders to prioritize their own citizens. He described U.S. economic growth, military rebuilding, trade reforms, and efforts to renegotiate agreements with Mexico, Canada, Japan, and the United Kingdom. He criticized China’s trade practices, called for changes to the World Trade Organization, and said the U.S. was monitoring Hong Kong.

Trump said the U.S. seeks peace but will defend its interests, condemning Iran’s government, defending sanctions, and calling for Iran to abandon nuclear ambitions and regional aggression. He discussed diplomacy with North Korea, efforts toward peace in Afghanistan, and opposition to illegal immigration and human smuggling. He also criticized conditions in Venezuela, Cuba, and Nicaragua, denounced socialism and communism, and affirmed U.S. support for democracy in Venezuela.

He raised concerns about technology, social media power, bureaucracy, and threats to free speech. He stated support for decriminalizing homosexuality, women’s economic empowerment, religious freedom, opposition to abortion-related international mandates, and the U.S. right to bear arms. He concluded by urging leaders to strengthen their nations, honor their cultures and citizens, and pursue peace and progress beginning at home.

Louisville officials are urging residents not to set off fireworks on Independence Day because the smoke creates particle pollution that can worsen air quality, aggravate respiratory problems, and sometimes exceed federal limits. Airborne and exploding fireworks are illegal in city limits, and officials note neighborhood fireworks can collectively pollute more than the city’s official show.

The lecture restates the Weierstrass M-test and applies it to show uniform convergence of certain function series. It then proves that a power series with radius of convergence \(\rho\) converges uniformly on every closed interval strictly inside \((x_0-\rho, x_0+\rho)\), using the M-test and root test. This uniform convergence justifies term-by-term integration and differentiation within the radius of convergence. The derivative power series is shown to have the same radius of convergence as the original, so higher derivatives may also be computed term by term, implying that a power series is the Taylor series of its associated function.

The lecture then introduces Weierstrass’s approximation theorem: every continuous function on \([0,1]\) is the uniform limit of polynomials. It reduces the proof to functions vanishing at both endpoints, constructs polynomials using kernels \(q_n(x)=c_n(1-x^2)^n\), and proves these kernels are nonnegative, integrate to 1, and converge uniformly to 0 away from 0. Using uniform continuity and boundedness of the continuous function, it shows the constructed polynomial sequence converges uniformly to the function.

In a patent infringement suit over Curtis and Cook patent No. 285,116 for portable elevated railroads, the court found claims 1, 2, and 3 invalid due to prior use shown by uncontradicted testimony. Claim 4, covering an elevated track with branch tracks, a switch, and a traveler, was held valid and infringed by the defendant’s structure. A decree was ordered for the plaintiff on claim 4.

A student-founded Whiteness Group at Kenyon College aims to educate students about whiteness, white privilege, and anti-racist action. Founder Juniper Cruz said the group seeks sustainable activism and was created in response to students whose activism was limited to social media. Meetings include ground rules, including that white participants cannot ask people of color questions and should try to answer their own questions. About 50 students attended the first meeting. Kenyon’s chaplain Rachel Kessler attended a later meeting and wrote that shame or fear among white people can hinder efforts to combat racism and white supremacy.

The Supreme Court appeared largely sympathetic to counselor Kaley Chiles’ challenge to Colorado’s 2019 ban on conversion therapy for minors, with several justices suggesting the law may discriminate based on viewpoint. The law bars licensed mental health professionals from providing treatment intended to change a minor’s sexual orientation or gender identity, while exempting religious ministry.

Chiles argues the ban prevents her from helping clients pursue certain goals related to sexuality or gender. Lower courts declined to block enforcement, finding the law regulates professional conduct and is subject to rational basis review. Chiles and the Trump administration urged the Supreme Court to strike down the law, while Colorado defended it as regulation of a narrow medical treatment associated with harm.

Justices debated Chiles’ standing, whether the law regulates speech or medical treatment, and whether strict scrutiny should apply. Some justices suggested that if stricter review is required, the case may be sent back to lower courts for further consideration.

DDR2/DDR3 memory controller terminal functions describe DDR[0] and DDR[1] signals, including data strobe I/Os for each byte of 32-bit data buses used to synchronize reads and writes.
