The speaker recalls disappointment after losing in the finals but happiness for his brother’s win. He values playing together and spending time with his brother’s family. He says his line’s success comes from trust and consistency, and notes goaltending is crucial, praising both goalies’ performances.

This preprint describes a citizen science approach to monitoring household tap water microbiomes in China. From December 2020 to August 2021, 25 student volunteers collected 50 tap water samples across 32 administrative regions in 19 provinces/regions, including opportunistic samples after the 2021 Henan Floods and Typhoon In-Fa. A low-cost sampling toolkit and standardized protocol were developed using syringe filters, disinfection steps, video guidance, and sample tracking. Of 50 samples, 22 tested positive for microbial DNA. 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding of pooled PCR-positive samples identified 7,635 ASVs and detected pathogenic bacteria including Mycobacterium, Acinetobacter, and Legionella in all PCR-positive samples. Pathogenic species and toxin-producing cyanobacteria were detected in samples from Zhengzhou and Changzhou after extreme weather events. The study presents citizen science as a cost-effective supplement to drinking water microbial monitoring in China.

Dr. Pasvolsky said respect for international obligations, including treaties, was inherent in the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals but could be specifically enumerated later. The Ambassadors of Honduras and Chile discussed whether respect for treaties was included in international law, with Chile noting international law was not clearly defined. A correction to prior minutes was made at Venezuela’s request, and the minutes were approved.

Discussion then turned to Security Council composition. Pasvolsky said the Council must be both effective and representative, with permanent seats tied to major powers’ responsibilities and capacities. He explained that nonpermanent members should outnumber permanent members to prevent decisions by permanent members alone, and noted the American republics had been represented on the League Council and likely would be again. He advised against setting selection rules at this stage.

Chile said further repetition was unnecessary. Brazil argued Latin America should be permanently represented on the Council and emphasized the Organization’s preventive purpose; others requested that Brazil’s remarks be recorded.

Sixteen years after an unidentified injured Mexican migrant, called Pancho by nurses, was hospitalized in San Diego in a vegetative state, a Texas woman saw his photo online and wondered if he was her cousin Gilberto.

Quarters coverage is a 4-deep, 3-underneath defense that lets safeties support both pass coverage and the run game. Cornerbacks cover the #1 receivers, safeties read the #2 receivers, outside linebackers cover the flats, and the middle linebacker handles the middle hook. Offenses attack quarters by throwing to the flats, targeting the open middle of the field, using play action against aggressive safeties, and creating overloads that stress zone responsibilities. The passage highlights five example quarters beaters, including play-action verticals, stick with a backside option route, shallow sting, Y leak, and play-action slot cross concepts.

North Carolina child care academies in at least 11 counties aim to move new early childhood educators into classrooms faster and at little or no cost. Programs last two to six weeks and use either a classroom-ready model, which qualifies graduates to work in licensed child care facilities, or a teaching credential model, which includes EDU 119-equivalent coursework and qualifies graduates to serve as lead teachers. Interest has grown amid staffing shortages, with additional community colleges considering academies. A proposed $1.476 million state pilot was included in the House budget but not enacted, while DCDEE is offering grants of up to $50,000 for new academies. Local programs in Wayne, Johnston, Stanly, McDowell, and Durham counties use foundation, grant, and community partnerships to cover costs, connect graduates to jobs, and support further education.
Caffeine content per ounce varies by coffee chain. McDonald’s has 9 mg, Dunkin’ Donuts 12.7 mg, Peet’s 16.7 mg, Starbucks 20.6 mg, and Deathwish 54.2 mg, described as the world’s strongest coffee.

James Saft argues that the post-election stock market rally faces risks from high valuations and uncertainty over the Trump administration’s ability to deliver tax cuts, infrastructure spending and deregulation after its healthcare bill failure. He notes that market valuations are historically elevated, while the Federal Reserve is raising rates and some policymakers have described asset prices as rich or frothy. Sentiment indicators have surged, but harder economic data and earnings revisions are less supportive. Analysts cited warn that current valuations imply weak future returns unless promised policies significantly boost earnings. Saft concludes that comprehensive tax reform appears unlikely, with piecemeal measures such as foreign cash repatriation more probable, and that a broader reflation is less likely.

The passage describes a continuation patent application for automated object sortation systems, particularly robotic systems for sorting parcels, packages, and articles. It identifies limitations of current manual and partially automated sortation systems, including dependence on human labor, limited throughput, high space requirements, fixed bin assignments, high actuator costs for automated diverts, and inflexibility when many destination bins are needed.

The invention provides methods and systems using programmable motion devices, such as robotic arms, to acquire objects from mixed input areas, perceive identifying indicia, dynamically assign intermediate stations or bins associated with destination locations, and move objects toward those stations. Unlike conventional systems with fixed mappings between bins and destinations, the disclosed system dynamically maps sorter outputs or collection bins to destinations during operation based on object indicia and heuristics. Bins may be reassigned after being filled, emptied, or determined ready for further processing.

Various embodiments include input conveyors, circulating conveyors, multiple input and output conveyors, perception systems using cameras or scanners, stacks of collection bins, output conveyors, movable hoppers, automated carriages, bagging stations, and non-sortable output areas. A central controller coordinates object identification, bin assignment, robotic movement, bin status updates, and routing for further processing. Objects that cannot be identified or assigned may be returned to the input stream or routed to manual sorting.

The passage also describes shuttle wing sortation systems in which an articulated arm drops identified objects through a camera unit into a carriage. The carriage transfers objects to shuttle wing sorter sections, where additional carriages move along tracks between rows of bins and tip objects into assigned bins. Systems may include multiple shuttle wings and robotic arms, allowing scalable throughput and bin counts. The system may allocate high-volume destinations closer to shuttle home positions and distribute busy destinations across wings to reduce cycle time.

The disclosed systems use heuristics based on historical trends, current system state, processed objects, expected deliveries, object characteristics, facility location, downstream demand, and bin contents. Claimed advantages include greater flexibility, fewer required sorter outputs than destinations, reduced space, lower manual labor, lower capital and operating costs, dynamic fault handling, scalability, and more efficient object handling.

The passage describes SEV-ES and SEV-SNP Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocols, including MSR protocol requests and responses for AP reset hold, GHCB GPA preference, registration, unregistration, page state changes, Run VMPL, hypervisor feature support, and guest termination. GHCB GPA registration is required for SEV-SNP guests before first use; guests may request a preferred GPA, register a GPA, and unregister it, while hypervisors must validate registered GPAs and support per-VMPL registration if Multi-VMPL is advertised.

It provides GHCB negotiation examples for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests, covering protocol version negotiation, encryption bit discovery, CPUID handling, GHCB page allocation, shared mapping, and GHCB MSR setup. It also outlines VMGEXIT handling, where guests populate GHCB fields and valid bits, hypervisors process the exit, update state, and resume or terminate the guest.

The passage defines Non-Automatic Exit handling requirements, VALID_BITMAP usage, error reporting through SW_EXITINFO fields, and handling for IOIO, MSR, VMMCALL, MMIO, Page State Change, and SNP Guest Request events. Page State Change requests use shared GHCB structures and support private/shared transitions and PSMASH/UNSMASH hints. SNP Guest Requests use shared request and response pages, firmware APIs, return codes, and retry signaling.

It also describes the SEV-SNP secrets page guest reserved area, including VMPL message sequence numbers, AP jump table address communication, and guest usage space, plus an EFI configuration table for communicating SEV-SNP secrets and CPUID pages to an OS.

In Morris v. Scott, the court held that an action for malicious prosecution may lie even if the original court lacked jurisdiction, when malice and falsehood are the central claims and arrest or trespass is alleged as a consequence. The lower court erred in excluding evidence due to missing jurisdictional averments. Judgment was reversed and a new trial ordered.

The passage explains that lower highs and lower lows generally signal a downtrend but are tested as a short-term reversal pattern. Backtests on SPY, GLD, and TLT show longer holding periods often improve results due to upward drift in those markets. A two-day version slightly improves SPY results but not GLD or TLT. A three-day version in stocks improves average gain and profit factor with relatively low drawdown for a one-day hold. The passage concludes the pattern works best as a short-term reversal pattern in stocks, though other strategies may offer better rewards.

Portsmouth are awaiting contact from the Football Association after Charlton fans released smoke bombs at Fratton Park during Charlton’s 1-0 win. Chief executive Mark Catlin said the club may be asked for observations and could face a fine if its handling is deemed unsatisfactory, but stressed Pompey follows safety procedures and treats such incidents seriously.

Niantic will add 80 second-generation Pokémon from the Gold and Silver games to Pokémon Go later this week, bringing the total Gen 2 count in the game to 88. The update also adds new Nanab and Pinap Berries, avatar customization items, and new Pokémon reactions during battles. Twelve Gen 2 Pokémon remain absent, including six legendaries: Raikou, Entei, Suicune, Lugia, Ho-Oh and Celebi. Niantic has not detailed plans for introducing legendary Pokémon.

The lecture covers smart contracts, decentralized applications, token sales, and related legal issues. Smart contracts are described using Nick Szabo’s definition as promises in digital form with protocols for performance, though they may be neither “smart” nor legally contracts. Ethereum is compared with Bitcoin: both use cryptography and decentralized consensus, but Ethereum is account-based, supports Turing-complete programming, uses state transitions, has multiple Merkle trees, shorter block times, Ether as its native currency, and a more flexible monetary policy. Ethereum began with a presale and ICO, unlike Bitcoin’s launch.

The lecture also reviews smart contract platforms including Ethereum, EOS, NEO, and Ethereum Classic. EOS raised $4.2 billion and set aside funds to support projects using its platform. NEO is described as China-linked and potentially more scalable, while Ethereum Classic resulted from a hard fork. Current decentralized applications are described as limited in usage, with leading examples in gambling, gaming, exchanges, and finance. Initial coin offerings are presented as fundraising mechanisms for networks, often issuing prefunctional tokens; about $20–28 billion has been raised, though many ICOs have failed or been identified as scams or frauds.

Larry Lessig explains contract law as involving promises or performances exchanged for promises or performances. He emphasizes that contracts include express and implied terms and that the state is always relevant because it decides whether contracts are enforceable, illegal, taxable, or otherwise regulated. He argues that code can alter or conflict with legal policy, using digital rights management as an example. Smart contracts may lower transaction costs, especially where legal systems are weak or where automated verification enables new markets, such as flight delay insurance. However, they can also raise costs when contracts require ambiguity, because traditional contracts often leave unlikely contingencies unresolved until later judicial interpretation.

The discussion concludes with questions about blockchain’s role in verification, trust, legal enforceability, leverage, and access to legal services. Lessig argues that many routine legal services could be automated, but courts and lawyers need greater technical understanding to interpret code-based contracts and related systems.

The U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia denied the plaintiffs’ motion to enforce a settlement agreement. Former D.C. Department of Corrections employees Arthur Hood, Jessie Smith, and Susie Thomas alleged they were wrongfully terminated in retaliation for speaking to the media about the city’s halfway-house system. Before trial, the parties agreed to a tentative settlement involving $625,000, but later disputed whether it also included Hood’s and Smith’s re-enrollment in the retirement system.

The court found that the parties agreed to the monetary settlement but did not have a “meeting of the minds” on retirement re-enrollment, a material term claimed by the plaintiffs. The court also declined to enforce a separate settlement as to Thomas. It gave the plaintiffs until September 9, 2002, to accept the $625,000 settlement without retirement benefits or reject it and proceed toward trial.

The speaker says the team is anxious and excited to return after two days, knows it must improve, and wants more traffic in front of Roberto to create scoring chances. They hope familiarity with the opponent will lead to a better game and stress the importance of winning to return home with a split.

Collagen production decreases with age, leading interest in supplements for cosmetic and health support. Collagen provides structure, strength and elasticity to skin, tendons, bones, cartilage, muscles, blood vessels and organs. Common body types include I, II, III, IV and V, while oral supplements mainly contain types I, II and III.

Supplements include hydrolysed collagen, undenatured collagen and gelatin, sourced mostly from animals such as fish, cows, pigs and chickens. Hydrolysed collagen is described as easily digested and absorbed. Potential benefits include support for skin healing, wrinkles, firmness, brittle nails, bone strength, joint pain and connective tissue repair, though research is ongoing.

Suggested studied doses vary by goal, including 2.5 grams for joint pain and skin hydration, 5 grams for bone density in osteopenic postmenopausal people, 15 grams with resistance training for muscle mass, and up to 40 milligrams for joint health. Experts advise using third-party tested products. A balanced diet with protein, vitamin C sources and foods such as bone broth can support natural collagen production.

Backtests of the Santa Claus Rally in European markets found stronger performance during the Christmas/end-of-year period for German stocks and the Euro Stoxx 50. The study used the EWG ETF for German stocks and FEZ ETF for Euro Stoxx 50. EWG showed an average gain of 2.1% per trade, an 81% win ratio, and a profit factor of 13, while FEZ showed a 1.5% average gain, 81% win ratio, and a profit factor of 9. Recent returns were below earlier averages. Positions were typically held for several days, and performance exceeded random weekly gains, though future continuation is not guaranteed.

The Midline Option is an option play in which the quarterback reads an interior defensive lineman to decide whether to hand off to a fullback hitting the A-gap or keep the ball through the B-gap. Its main strength is that the offense can leave a defender unblocked and read him instead, and it complements inside and outside veer by using similar motion to misdirect defenders. Its main weakness is that it exposes the quarterback to frequent hits, so teams typically need a durable quarterback to run it.

Against both 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, the play relies on the fullback running the midline, wingback motion to suggest veer, linemen working to create interior lanes or climb to linebackers, and the quarterback reading the dive key. If the defender crashes toward the fullback, the quarterback keeps; if the defender expands or runs upfield, he hands off.

Common variations include Flexbone Midline, which uses a playside receiver instead of a tight end to spread the defense, and Midline “Follow,” where a wingback becomes an extra lead blocker for short-yardage quarterback keeps.

Dr. Edward Kwapong, newly elected President of IHRMP Ghana, urged HR practitioners to prioritize professional certification over raw academic qualifications. At IHRMP’s ninth graduation in Accra, 136 Associate and nine certified members graduated. Executive Director Ebenezer Agbetor noted growth in the institute, while guest speaker Irene Asare said AI, robotics and humans can combine to improve organisational productivity.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk said the Model 3 had over 500,000 advance reservations as he delivered the first 30 cars to employee buyers at the Fremont, California factory. The $35,000 base model has a 220-mile range, while a $44,000 version can travel 310 miles. Musk warned Tesla faces “at least six months of manufacturing hell” as it ramps production. New buyers may not receive cars until late 2018. Tesla aims to produce 500,000 vehicles next year, nearly six times its 2016 output, despite past production delays and quality issues. The launch is critical for Tesla’s shift from luxury electric cars to mass-market production and could affect its cash needs after burning over $2 billion this year.

Trend Micro researchers found 89 malicious Chrome Web Store extensions affecting over 423,000 users and forming a botnet called Droidclub. The extensions, promoted through malvertising and social engineering, appeared harmless but injected ads, session-replay scripts, and, in an earlier version, Coinhive cryptocurrency-mining code. Droidclub used Yandex Metrica scripts to record users’ activity across visited websites, potentially capturing form data such as names, credit card details, CVV numbers, email addresses, and phone numbers, though not passwords. It also displayed low-quality ads or exploit kits and made removal difficult by redirecting users from reporting or uninstall pages to misleading screens. Trend Micro contacted Google and Cloudflare; the extensions and command-and-control servers were removed. Google said it disabled the affected extensions and blocks more than 1,000 malicious extensions monthly. The report followed other recent discoveries of malicious Chrome extensions and cryptocurrency-mining abuse.

This study examined how pre-existing immunity affects P. falciparum var gene expression and PfEMP1 antibody responses during a Controlled Human Malaria Infection in semi-immune adult males in The Gambia infected with NF54/3D7 sporozoites. Participants were classified as sero-high or sero-low based on antibody responses to malaria antigens. Sero-high individuals had lower peak parasitaemia, and two were classified as controllers due to longer latency and lower parasite multiplication rates.

Whole-transcriptome analysis showed that variant surface antigen genes, especially var genes, were the main differentially expressed genes between sero-high and sero-low individuals. Var expression patterns clustered by infection control status rather than geography when compared with data from a prior Gabon CHMI. Sero-low individuals showed higher var expression entropy, indicating broader var repertoires, while controllers had more restricted var expression. Var gene turnover in vivo was high, with genes expressed at day 14 often becoming undetectable by later timepoints; group A var genes had the highest estimated transition rates.

In vitro culture of parasite isolates showed that, without host immunity, var expression tended toward a high-entropy steady state. Isolates from sero-low individuals converged rapidly to similar expression profiles, while sero-high isolates retained distinct profiles for longer, suggesting lasting effects of immune selection. Mathematical modeling supported high intrinsic switching rates, though lower than in vivo turnover for some var groups.

Protein microarray analysis showed that sero-high individuals recognized more 3D7 PfEMP1 domains before and after infection than sero-low individuals. Sero-low individuals more than doubled their breadth of PfEMP1 domain recognition after infection, while sero-high individuals showed comparatively stable responses. Pre-existing PfEMP1 antibody breadth was negatively associated with var expression diversity and infection markers, and specific antibodies showed moderate negative associations with later expression of some var groups. However, antibody acquisition after infection was not clearly dependent on the intensity of PfEMP1 expression during CHMI.

The authors conclude that intrinsic var switching maintains diverse PfEMP1 repertoires, while pre-existing immune responses restrict var expression through selection, shaping infection outcomes during CHMI.

Soccer formations describe the placement of players to defend one’s goal and attack the opponent’s goal. Formation choice depends on the number of players, player skills, and the coach’s ability to teach and apply tactics. In 11-a-side soccer, the goalkeeper is assumed, and formations describe the 10 field players by defenders, midfielders, and forwards, such as 4-3-3, 4-4-2, or 3-4-3. Some newer designations include 4-3-2-1 and 4-6.

For younger age groups with fewer players, the same shorthand is used. U.S. Soccer recommends 4-3-3 or 4-4-2 for U15–U19, 4-3-3 for U13–U14, and 3-2-3 for U9–U12, with no specified formations for younger groups. Coaches may use discretion for small-sided games. Formations, position names, player placement, and tactics are connected, and coaches should understand these elements and clearly present the formation to the team.

The passage explains the value of distributed system patterns: they allow developers to learn from prior experience, share a common vocabulary, and build reusable components. It argues that patterns can make distributed system design more systematic, as algorithms and object-oriented programming patterns have done in other areas.

It introduces container-based single-node patterns, where multiple tightly coupled containers are co-scheduled on one machine and may share resources. The sidecar pattern uses an auxiliary container to augment an application container, such as adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service, synchronizing configuration, providing process introspection, or building a simple Git-based PaaS. Effective sidecars should be parameterized, have stable APIs, and be documented through Dockerfile directives, labels, and related metadata.

The ambassador pattern places a container between an application and external services to broker communication. Examples include routing requests to shards in a sharded Redis service, abstracting service discovery across environments, and splitting traffic for experiments or production-load testing.

The adapter pattern modifies an application container’s interface to match a standard expected by external tools. It is used for monitoring, logging, and health checks, such as adapting Redis metrics for Prometheus, normalizing logs with fluentd, or adding richer MySQL health checks without changing the original database container.

The passage then contrasts monolithic systems with microservices, describing microservices as distributed components communicating through defined APIs. It states that microservices improve reliability, agility, team independence, and scaling, but make debugging and system design more difficult, motivating the use of distributed patterns.

For multi-node systems, it describes replicated load-balanced services, especially stateless services, where identical replicas sit behind a load balancer for availability and scaling. It discusses readiness probes, session tracking, caching layers, rate limiting, denial-of-service defense, and SSL termination using tools such as Varnish and nginx.

Finally, it explains sharded services, where each shard handles only part of the request space, typically for stateful systems with data too large for one machine. It discusses sharded caches, cache hit rates, performance and failure impacts, replicated sharded caches, shard routing through ambassadors or shared services, and sharding functions based on hashing and modulo operations.

Thirteen-year-old Time for Kids reporter Benje Choucroun asked White House press secretary Sarah Huckabee Sanders what the administration has done and will do to prevent school shootings, citing students’ mental health concerns after lockdown drills. Sanders, visibly emotional, said the administration takes school safety seriously and that a presidential school safety commission was meeting to discuss ways to protect students. Time editor Edward Felsenthal praised Choucroun’s question.

The speaker, called from retirement to the presidency, pledges to state and follow the principles that will guide his administration. He emphasizes that the Constitution rests on the people, grants limited powers to government, and preserves individual rights such as religious liberty, due process, free expression, and participation in public benefits.

He warns that the greatest danger to American institutions is not only federal usurpation, but the concentration of power in one department, especially the executive. He identifies presidential eligibility for a second term as a constitutional defect and pledges not to serve a second term. He argues that the President is not part of the legislative power and that the veto should be used only to protect the Constitution, prevent hasty legislation, and defend minority rights.

He expresses concern about executive control over patronage, public revenue, federal officers, and the press. He pledges not to remove a Treasury Secretary without reporting the circumstances to Congress, to restrict federal officers from election interference, and to protect independent criticism of government. He opposes executive initiation of revenue schemes and argues that public funds should be kept away from executive control. He also criticizes an exclusively metallic currency.

The speaker affirms the rights of residents of the District of Columbia as free American citizens and says congressional authority there should be limited to what is necessary for the federal government’s functions. He stresses the need to preserve harmony among states, respect reserved powers, and avoid interference by citizens of one state in the domestic institutions of another. He urges states to meet financial obligations and preserve credit.

He identifies union, moderation, patriotism, and the spirit of liberty as essential to free government, while warning against faction and party spirit, especially when it increases executive power. In foreign affairs, he pledges to preserve peace without sacrificing national rights or honor, and to deal justly with aboriginal neighbors. He calls for reducing party violence, preventing an executive party in Congress, and relying on legal administration rather than partisan loyalty. He closes by expressing reverence for Christianity, religious liberty, moral responsibility, and confidence in the people’s support.

Riverton Investment Corp. sued for a tax refund after the IRS disallowed deductions for payments made in the 1990s to former management employees when RIC bought back stock issued under a Management Stockholder’s Agreement. The IRS treated the payments as nondeductible stock redemptions; RIC claimed they were deductible compensation.

The court found that whether the payments were redemptions depended on whether the stock had been “transferred” to the employees in the 1980s under tax regulations. That depended on whether the agreement’s restrictions were permanent “non-lapse” restrictions. The court held that Paragraph 9 of the agreement was ambiguous and that parol evidence was admissible. The uncontroverted evidence showed that the employees remained permanently restricted in selling the stock and in the price they could receive, so no transfer occurred for tax purposes. Therefore, the later payments were not stock redemptions and were deductible.

The court rejected the magistrate judge’s recommendation, denied the United States’s motions for summary judgment and to strike, granted RIC’s motion for summary judgment, entered judgment for RIC, and ordered the parties to address damages and interest.

The Nebraska Supreme Court affirmed an injunction preventing enforcement of a judgment against Ida C. Scott’s real estate. Scott, a married woman living with her husband, had a judgment entered against her for goods alleged to be necessaries furnished to her and her husband, but no prior judgment or unsatisfied execution had been obtained against her husband. Under Comp. St. 1911, ch. 53, sec. 1, a married woman’s property is not liable for family necessaries until execution against the husband for that debt has been returned unsatisfied. Because that condition precedent was not met, Scott’s property could not be sold, and the court found it unnecessary to address her claimed federal exemption as a member of the Omaha Tribe.

The passage describes the role of design patterns in software development, from object-oriented programming to distributed systems. Object-oriented programming introduced greater emphasis on data, reusability, and extensibility, and books such as Design Patterns established shared terminology and reusable interface-based patterns. Open source software further demonstrated that software, especially distributed systems, is developed through communities, and container technologies discussed in the book are open source.

Patterns for distributed systems are presented as general blueprints that guide system organization without mandating specific technologies. Their value includes learning from prior experience, creating a shared vocabulary, and enabling reusable components. Distributed systems are needed for reliability, agility, and scale, and the book aims to regularize distributed system design through patterns.

The passage introduces single-node container patterns, where tightly coupled containers are co-scheduled on one machine and may share resources such as filesystems, networking, and memory. Splitting applications on one node into multiple containers supports resource isolation, team ownership, reuse, and separation of concerns.

The sidecar pattern uses an additional container to augment an application container. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service with nginx, synchronizing configuration from an API to a local file, exposing process information through a reusable topz container, and building a simple Git-based PaaS. Effective sidecars should be parameterized, have stable APIs, and be documented through Dockerfile directives and metadata labels.

The ambassador pattern uses a container to broker communication between an application and external services. It can route traffic to sharded storage, provide service brokering across environments, or support request splitting for experiments. Examples include using twemproxy with sharded Redis, connecting applications to environment-specific MySQL services, and using nginx to send 10% of traffic to an experimental service.

The adapter pattern modifies an application container’s interface to match expected conventions. It is useful in heterogeneous systems where applications expose different monitoring, logging, or health-checking interfaces. Examples include adapting Redis metrics for Prometheus, normalizing logs with fluentd, and adding rich MySQL health checks without modifying the MySQL container.

The passage then contrasts single-node patterns with multi-node distributed patterns. Microservices divide applications into small services communicating through APIs, improving team independence, reliability, agility, and scaling, but making debugging and architecture more difficult. Distributed patterns help address these challenges.

Replicated load-balanced services are described as a common pattern for stateless services. Multiple identical replicas sit behind a load balancer to provide redundancy, availability, and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes indicate when replicas can serve traffic. Session-tracked services route a user’s requests to the same replica, often through hashing or cookies.

Application-layer replicated services can include caching and SSL termination. A Varnish caching layer can improve performance, while nginx can terminate SSL. The passage also discusses rate limiting and denial-of-service defense at the edge layer.

Finally, the passage introduces sharded services, where each shard serves only part of the data and a root routes requests. Sharding is mainly used for stateful systems whose data exceeds one machine. A sharded cache improves memory utilization compared with replicated caches but creates concerns around cache failure, hit rate, latency, and rollout capacity. Replicated sharded caches combine sharding with replication to improve resilience and allow shards to scale independently.
Reuters reported Asian currency rates against the U.S. dollar at 0134 GMT on Feb. 2, showing mixed daily moves, while most currencies had gained against the dollar so far in 2018.

The study evaluates the impact of digitalization on higher education quality in Vietnam using the spherical fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (SFAHP). It addresses a research gap: the lack of a systematic framework for ranking digitalization factors affecting online higher education quality. Five criteria were assessed through pairwise comparisons from nine education experts: accessibility of digital resources, adaptability and innovation, pedagogical integration, student engagement, and technological infrastructure.

Results show pedagogical integration as the most important factor, with a priority weight of 23.6%, followed by student engagement at 21.2%, accessibility of digital resources at 20.3%, adaptability and innovation at 18.4%, and technological infrastructure at 16.5%. The findings suggest that integrating teaching methods with technology is central to improving online education quality, while student engagement and equitable access to digital resources are also significant. Although ranked lower, adaptability, innovation, and technological infrastructure remain important for supporting digital education.

The study concludes that higher education institutions and policymakers should prioritize technology-supported pedagogy, interactive and personalized learning, equitable digital access, institutional innovation, and educator development in digital pedagogy. It notes that reliance on expert evaluations may limit stakeholder representation and recommends broader future research.

Mike Hoffman scored in the sixth round of the shootout with a Peter Forsberg-style move to give the Ottawa Senators a 4-3 win over the Philadelphia Flyers. Coach Guy Boucher praised Hoffman’s high-risk, high-reward approach. Rookie Colin White recorded his first NHL point with an assist on Matt Duchene’s first-period goal, and Duchene praised his potential. Mets GM David Stearns criticized Kodai Senga’s inconsistency after two challenging seasons marked by injuries, poor performance and a Triple-A demotion. Stearns said the team still sees potential but cannot count on Senga for 30 starts next year. The Mets missed the playoffs after a strong start and late-season pitching struggles.

SCDNR biologists caught and satellite tagged “Harry-Etta,” a pregnant female tiger shark in St. Helena Sound measuring 12 feet 2 inches and 820 pounds. The SPOT tag will provide real-time movement data over the next year, helping researchers study tiger shark lifespan, reproduction, migration, and habitat use during gestation. Harry-Etta is the fifteenth tiger shark satellite tagged by the team in South Carolina and the first known to be pregnant. Researchers say South Carolina’s southern sounds, especially St. Helena and Port Royal Sounds, may be important foraging, nursing, and reproduction areas. The tag was sponsored by the Harry Hampton Wildlife Fund, and Harry-Etta can be tracked on the OCEARCH Global Shark Tracker.

Offensive linemen play a selfless, physically demanding role focused on protecting teammates and enabling offensive production without receiving much public attention or statistics. The offensive line creates running lanes, protects the quarterback, communicates as a unit, and responds to defensive blitzes, stunts, alignments, and pressures. Its five players line up together on the line of scrimmage, which gives the unit its name. Common nicknames include Hogs, Bruisers, Bulldozers, Big Uglies, and Monsters. Key skills include run-blocking, pass-blocking, athleticism, strength, awareness, and technique, with typical body types ranging from 6’2” to 6’8” and 300–340 pounds. Notable offensive linemen mentioned are Jim Otto at center, John Hannah at guard, and Anthony Munoz at tackle. The passage emphasizes that consistent offensive line play is central to offensive success and helps skill players perform effectively.

Martin Van Buren warns that unrest on the U.S. northern frontier related to the Canadian civil war is increasing despite official efforts. He states that U.S. citizens have aided insurgents with arms, supplies, and military organization at Navy Island. He urges them to return home and warns that unlawful interference with British Provinces will be punished under U.S. law and receive no government support.

Research reviewed by Concordia PhD candidate Sarah Sajedi found that people ingest an average of 39,000 to 52,000 microplastic particles annually, while bottled water users consume about 90,000 more particles than tap water drinkers. The review of more than 140 scientific articles says single-use plastic water bottles can shed micro- and nanoplastics during manufacturing, storage, transport, use, and degradation, especially when exposed to sunlight and temperature changes. These particles can enter the bloodstream and organs and are linked to inflammation, oxidative stress, hormonal disruption, impaired reproduction, neurological damage, and cancer, though long-term effects remain poorly understood due to limited testing and inconsistent measurement methods. Sajedi notes that legislation often targets bags, straws, and packaging but rarely single-use water bottles, and emphasizes education to reduce daily bottled water use.

A fossil found by elk hunter David Bradt in northeastern Montana in 2010 led to the identification of a new elasmosaur species that lived about 70 million years ago in an inland sea east of the Rocky Mountains. Unlike most elasmosaurs, which had necks up to 18 feet with as many as 76 vertebrae, this species had a neck about 7½ feet long with around 40 vertebrae. Researchers said the discovery challenges the idea that elasmosaurs evolved progressively longer necks. The nearly complete fossil was excavated from the Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge and described in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology.

A University of Pennsylvania study published in the Journal of Neuroscience found that transcranial direct-current stimulation of the prefrontal cortex reduced self-reported intentions to commit aggression and increased moral judgment of violent acts. Researchers randomly assigned 81 healthy adults to receive either 20 minutes of stimulation or a brief low-current control procedure. The next day, participants read scenarios involving physical assault and rape and rated how likely they would be to commit them. The stimulated group reported 47% lower likelihood of physical assault and 70% lower likelihood of sexual assault than controls, and judged the acts as more morally wrong. Experts cautioned that self-reported intent may not reflect actual behavior, and the study did not show whether real violence would be reduced.

A security aide to Ebonyi State Governor David Umahi allegedly slapped an FRSC officer, identified as Soji, after the governor’s convoy was delayed at a checkpoint restricting access to Eagle Square for the PDP convention. The FRSC spokesman said no official report had been filed. Newsmen also observed security personnel at the convention ground collecting money from individuals without accreditation before allowing them access.

The author critiques a webinar by leaders of Middle States, SACSCOC and WASC on credit transfer and AI, saying it offered few concrete changes. They welcome accreditors’ preference that colleges “default to yes” on accepting transfer credits but note it is only an urging, not a mandate. The author argues colleges often reject credits for economic reasons and that accreditors now have less leverage after the end of regional monopolies. AI could help by speeding transcript reviews and providing transfer decisions alongside admissions and financial aid, but the author says the shift remains more an intention than a plan.

The lecture continues an algebra chapter aimed at introducing finite fields for later discussion of Reed-Solomon codes. It reviews integers, modular arithmetic, groups, cyclic groups, and the fact that finite cyclic groups are isomorphic to \(Z_n\).

Subgroups are defined as subsets that are themselves groups under the original group operation. Examples in \(Z_{10}\) include \(\{0,5\}\), isomorphic to \(Z_2\), and \(\{0,2,4,6,8\}\), isomorphic to \(Z_5\). For the integers, sets such as \(2Z\), \(3Z\), and generally \(nZ\) are subgroups.

Cosets are introduced as translates of subgroups, such as \(H+g\). Distinct cosets are either identical or disjoint and form a disjoint partition of the group. In finite groups, this leads to Lagrange’s theorem: the size of a subgroup divides the size of the group. Coset addition is defined, and cosets form quotient groups, such as \(Z/2Z\), which is isomorphic to \(Z_2\), and generally \(Z/nZ\), which is isomorphic to \(Z_n\).

Fields are defined as sets with addition and multiplication: the field is an abelian group under addition, its nonzero elements form an abelian group under multiplication, and multiplication distributes over addition. The real, complex, and binary fields are discussed as examples. Prime fields \(F_p\) are constructed from \(\{0,\dots,p-1\}\) with mod-\(p\) addition and multiplication, and this works only when \(p\) is prime. Every finite field with prime \(p\) elements is isomorphic to \(F_p\), and every finite field contains a prime subfield. The characteristic \(p\) of a finite field is the size of this prime subfield, and adding any field element to itself \(p\) times gives zero.

The lecture then introduces polynomials over a field \(F\), written \(F[x]\), with coefficients in \(F\) and finite degree. Polynomial addition is component-wise, and multiplication follows the usual term-by-term rule. The degree of a product is the sum of degrees, with the zero polynomial optionally assigned degree \(-\infty\). Polynomials form an abelian group under addition but not a field under multiplication, because only nonzero degree-zero polynomials have multiplicative inverses.

The 7th annual Julia’s Hope Cup and Carnival takes place Feb. 17 at Chippawa Park in Welland, raising money for The Hope Centre in memory of Julia Turner, who died of cancer in 2011. The event includes a pond-hockey tournament, kids’ mini-tournament, food, games, a silent auction and other activities. Last year it raised $20,000 and drew about 1,000 people. The firm includes Cameron Wirth, Nick Brady and Sadie Ellis, who takes on her biggest case defending Billy Brennan, a pediatric surgeon accused of a 24-year-old murder. Two teenagers from the Smoky Mountain Children's Home were arrested after allegedly stealing a van and leading police on a high-speed chase across East Tennessee. The pursuit ended near Highway 153 when the van hit another vehicle and the Chickamauga Dam barrier wall. No serious injuries were reported.

The OS can use HID AMDI0095 to bind a driver to the TMPM ACPI device, whose resources are declared in ACPI. A page migration driver must enable PAGEMIGRATION_EN in all IOMMUs once. TMPM exposes mailbox registers using a ring buffer for parallel command execution; firmware controls the read pointer, software controls the write pointer, and completion is indicated by pointer movement or the PM_Status TOGGLE bit.

Tesla, Inc.’s 2021 Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended December 31, 2021. Tesla designs, develops, manufactures, sells and leases fully electric vehicles and energy generation and storage systems, and provides related services. It operates in two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. Its automotive products include Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X, with planned vehicles including Cybertruck, Tesla Semi and the new Tesla Roadster. Its energy products include Powerwall, Megapack, retrofit solar systems and Solar Roof.

Tesla sells primarily through its website and company-owned locations, supports customers through service centers, Mobile Service, Superchargers and Destination Chargers, and offers financing, leases and insurance in selected markets. Manufacturing facilities include sites in California, Nevada, New York, Shanghai, and planned production at Gigafactory Berlin and Gigafactory Texas in 2022. The company relies on global suppliers, including for battery cells and raw materials such as lithium, nickel, cobalt, aluminum, steel and copper.

The report describes government incentives, regulatory credits, safety and dealer regulations, solar and storage policies, competition in automotive and energy markets, intellectual property practices, ESG priorities and human capital initiatives. As of December 31, 2021, Tesla and its subsidiaries had 99,290 full-time employees worldwide.

Key risks include impacts from COVID-19 and supply chain constraints, production ramp and cost-control challenges, demand uncertainty, supplier and battery cell availability, competition, international regulatory and operational risks, product defects or recalls, product liability claims, and risks related to financing, leasing and resale value guarantees.

Cirque du Soleil will donate US$500,000 to families of Las Vegas shooting victims and provide 5,000 tickets worth US$500,000 to first responders. The company also plans to join a benefit show and said none of its 1,500 local employees were hurt.

Former Southport MP John Pugh fears the approved Sainsbury’s megastore at Meols Cop retail park, replacing Homebase and two adjacent units, could cause further job losses in Southport town centre. Although Sainsbury’s says it will create 400 jobs, Pugh warns it may draw trade and major stores away from Lord Street, criticising Sefton Council’s support for the development.

President Ram Nath Kovind addressed the nation on the eve of Independence Day in his first speech as president, congratulating citizens on 70 years of Independence and honoring freedom fighters and soldiers. He urged citizens to help build a “New India” by 2022 through participation in government initiatives such as Swachh Bharat, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, GST, and tax compliance. He emphasized cleanliness, women’s equality, education for underprivileged children, selflessness, and responsibility in following laws. Kovind also praised families who gave up LPG subsidies and said India should aim to become fully educated. He had assumed office on July 25 after defeating Meira Kumar in the July 17 presidential election.

WIRED’s Zoë Schiffer and Leah Feiger discuss five stories: Rutgers professor Mark Bray, who wrote a book about antifa, is trying to leave the US after an online campaign and death threats; ICE is seeking contractors for a 24/7 social media surveillance program that may use AI; a Harvard study found AI companion apps used emotional manipulation in 37 percent of goodbye interactions; confusion and misinformation spread in a Facebook group after the FDA approved leucovorin calcium tablets for cerebral folate deficiency as a possible autism-symptom treatment; and OpenAI’s internal tools announcement caused stock drops for companies like DocuSign, HubSpot, and Salesforce. They also discuss whether AI infrastructure spending suggests a bubble, noting projected data center spending far exceeds current consumer AI spending.

GoDaddy gave The Daily Stormer 24 hours to move its domain after the neo-Nazi website posted an article denigrating Heather Heyer, who was killed during violence at a white nationalist rally in Charlottesville, Virginia.

Lexus announced UK pricing for the 2017 LC coupe, with both the V8 LC500 and hybrid LC500h starting at £76,595. Over a third of UK-bound units are already pre-ordered. The LC500 has a 467hp 5.0-litre V8 and 10-speed automatic, while the LC500h produces 354hp. Sport and Sport+ packages add performance and styling upgrades.

A study of more than 24,000 Slimming World members with obesity found that dieters who set the most ambitious weight-loss goals lost an average of 19% of their body weight in a year, compared with 11% among those aiming to lose less than 10%. Researchers and obesity experts said public health guidance encouraging “realistic” 5–10% targets may limit aspirations and suggested people should be encouraged to aim for their desired weight while receiving regular support. Professor Amanda Avery said personal targets can improve motivation, but support with eating, activity and group encouragement remains vital. The passage also highlights Hollie Barrett, who lost 8st 6lbs after setting a high personal target.

A Colorado panel voted to limit what state health plans will pay for Amgen’s arthritis drug Enbrel, setting a $600-per-unit ceiling for government agencies and commercial insurers. The cap equals about $30,350 annually per person, compared with roughly $53,000 paid by the average state insurance plan in 2023.

WIRED tested carry-on luggage and travel bags for plane travel, evaluating materials, weight, size, durability, wheels, handles, straps, zippers, and fit in overhead bins or under seats. The guide highlights options including Travelpro, Peak Design, Rimowa, Antler, State, Briggs & Riley, Yeti, Beis, Take Off, Tom Bihn, Six Moon Designs, and Aer, noting strengths such as organization, durability, smooth wheels, expandability, weather resistance, warranties, and suitability for children, camera gear, backpacks, or personal items. It advises travelers to check airline size requirements, understand TSA’s 3-1-1 liquids rule, and consider that hardware and warranty matter more than whether a suitcase is softshell or hardshell.

A long snapper is a specialized football position responsible for snapping the ball accurately and quickly to holders on extra points and field goals, and to punters on punts. Their work is crucial to scoring opportunities, field position, and avoiding blocked kicks or punts. On kicks, snaps are about 7 yards and must be placed within the holder’s frame; on punts, snaps are about 15 yards and must allow the punter to operate smoothly. Long snappers also help cover punts and may make tackles, so athleticism, toughness, balance, consistency, accuracy, and physicality are important. NFL teams reserve a roster spot for the position despite limited roster size. Long snappers are typically built like linebackers, around 6’1”–6’3” and 230–250 pounds. Other names include LS, deep-snapper for punts, and short-snapper for kicks. Notable long snappers mentioned include Zak DeOssie and Don Mulbach. The position is important because small snapping errors can lead to missed field goals, blocked punts, and major changes in game momentum.

Biloxi Shuckers attendance at MGM Park’s opening series rose 21 percent from last year, including a record Jackie Robinson Day crowd. ESPN highlighted Johnny Davis’ catch, gaining 767,000 Instagram views. The team returns April 22 with promotions and a March of Dimes jersey auction.

Eric Bass forwarded an Oct. 5, 2000 Dallas Morning News “Inside UT Football” newsletter by Chip Brown focused on Texas football and the upcoming Oklahoma game. Brown included quotes from Oklahoma coach Bob Stoops, discussed Texas’ quarterback rotation between Major Applewhite and Chris Simms, predicted Applewhite would start against Oklahoma, and forecast a 24-20 Texas win. The Q&A covered Royal-Memorial Stadium expansion, player injuries and roles, offensive line progress, special teams problems, the halo rule, Texas’ secondary against OU’s passing game, Mack Brown’s handling of criticism, future schedules, recruiting, team development, and other program updates. Brown said Texas had talent but needed chemistry, experience, leadership, and line development to become a consistent top program.

Shelley Corman forwarded a PAKK Yahoo Groups adoption digest to Ricki Winters and asked to add it to contacts. The digest includes 24 messages about Kazakhstan adoption topics, including HIV testing and visa requirements for Russia and Kazakhstan, accommodations in Kazakhstan, adoption airfare discounts through Travel-On and Delta, experiences adopting from Taraz, handling tantrums and adjustment issues, changing or retaining adopted children’s birth dates, and introductions from new or waiting adoptive parents.

The Trump administration announced it will largely continue Obama-era nuclear modernization plans while taking a more aggressive stance toward Russia. Its nuclear posture review calls North Korea a “clear and grave threat,” casts China as a potential nuclear adversary, and says U.S. strategy aims to reduce the likelihood of nuclear use while deterring major attacks, including non-nuclear ones. The review endorses existing arms control agreements, including New START, but says further progress is difficult due to Russian actions. It ends Obama’s push to reduce nuclear weapons’ role in defense policy and proposes modifying some submarine-launched ballistic missiles with smaller-yield warheads and later developing a nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile to counter Russia’s perceived “escalate to de-escalate” doctrine. Arms control groups criticized the policy as reckless.

Ministers negotiating with the DUP reportedly considered abolishing line dancing to secure a deal, citing Ian Paisley’s objections to it. David Davis said other concessions were impractical, while a Leave voter supported the move as an acceptable price for Brexit.

The passage describes the development and testing of the 15-item Language Phenotype Assessment (LPA), a clinician-administered tool designed to evaluate language comprehension in children aged 2 to 5 across three phenotypes: Command, Modifier, and Syntactic. Existing assessments were judged unsuitable for this purpose because they rely heavily on vocabulary, use overly complex sentence structures, are normed for older children, or require picture-based responses.

The LPA uses toy manipulatives and brief verbal instructions to assess command following, modifier integration involving color, size, and number, and syntactic comprehension involving spatial prepositions, noncanonical word order, and simple reasoning. Each item contains four tasks and is scored as passed if at least three tasks are completed correctly. A parent-reported companion measure, the Language Phenotype Evaluation Checklist (LPEC), was also developed with the same three-part structure.

The LPA was tested in 116 neurotypical children aged 1.5 to 7 years. Scores increased nearly linearly from ages 1.5 to 5 and then plateaued. Based on clinician-administered LPA results, 50% of children attained the Command Phenotype by 1.6 years, the Modifier Phenotype by 3.0 years, and the Syntactic Phenotype by 3.7 years; all children attained these phenotypes by ages 3, 4, and 5, respectively. The LPA showed high internal consistency, strong test-retest reliability, and very high inter-observer agreement.

Parent-reported LPEC scores correlated strongly with LPA scores. Parent reports indicated median acquisition ages of 1.6 years for Command, 2.7 years for Modifier, and 3.0 years for Syntactic phenotypes. The LPEC also showed high internal consistency and strong test-retest reliability.

The LPA was additionally administered to 79 children diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder. Among children aged 5 or older, all neurotypical participants attained the Syntactic Phenotype, compared with 39% of participants with ASD by LPA and 48% by LPEC. The authors conclude that the LPA may help identify and monitor language comprehension deficits, guide language therapy, and provide developmental benchmarks for early syntactic language comprehension.

A national EducationNext poll found support for charter schools fell from 51 percent to 39 percent in one year, while support for universal vouchers rose to 45 percent and tax-credit scholarships remained the most popular school choice option at 55 percent. The charter decline appeared across parties and racial and ethnic groups, with no single clear explanation, though disputes over charter expansion may be relevant. The poll also found shifting partisan views: Republican support for universal vouchers rose to 62 percent, while Democratic support fell to 50 percent. Respondents’ views were influenced by whether they were told President Trump supported an issue, but his net influence was nearly nil and weaker than Obama’s in 2009. Republicans and Democrats remained closely aligned in rating local public schools, with 55 percent of Republicans and 54 percent of Democrats giving them an A or B.

The Fraser Institute announced a Feb. 16, 2017 study on whether British Columbia’s carbon tax is revenue neutral, as promised when introduced in 2008. The study comes as the federal government requires provinces to adopt carbon pricing by 2018 and policymakers consider B.C.’s model.

The passage describes robotic systems for transporting objects using a transport robot with a multi-gripper end effector. The end effector includes independently addressable vacuum regions or grippers that can selectively grip and release one or multiple objects simultaneously or sequentially. Image data from cameras, lidar, radar, or other sensors is used to identify target objects, determine positions, plan transport paths, and verify gripping. A controller selects vacuum regions based on object location, size, weight, stacking arrangement, available drop-off space, and transport plans.

The system can include unloading, transfer, transport, and loading units in environments such as warehouses or shipping hubs. A robotic arm moves the end effector between pickup and drop-off locations, while sensors monitor object retention, force, torque, vacuum levels, and package position. The vacuum gripper assembly may include manifolds, suction elements, sealing members, valves, vacuum chambers, and sensors. Vacuum levels and airflow can be adjusted to securely hold objects while avoiding damage.

Operational methods include receiving image data, identifying target objects, selecting addressable vacuum regions, generating gripping and transport commands, verifying grip quality, regripping if needed, and executing or adjusting motion plans. The system can use stored object data, registration records, and gripper data to support object recognition, gripping decisions, and automated transport.

The lecture contrasts pointwise and uniform convergence of sequences of functions. Pointwise convergence requires \(f_n(x)\to f(x)\) for each fixed \(x\), while uniform convergence requires one \(M\) that works for all \(x\) in the set. Uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence, but not conversely.

The example \(f_n(x)=x^n\) on \([0,1]\) converges pointwise to a function that is \(0\) on \([0,1)\) and \(1\) at \(1\). It converges uniformly on \([0,b]\) for \(b<1\), but not uniformly on \([0,1]\). A “tent” function sequence also converges pointwise to \(0\) but not uniformly.

The lecture then discusses interchange of limits. In general, limits cannot always be interchanged. Three questions are considered: whether limits preserve continuity, differentiation, and integration. The answer is yes under uniform convergence, but no under pointwise convergence alone. Counterexamples include \(x^n\), \(x^n/n\), and the tent functions.

The main theorems proved are: the uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous; the integral of a uniform limit equals the limit of the integrals; and, under suitable hypotheses, if \(f_n\to f\) pointwise and \(f_n'\to g\) uniformly, then \(f\) is differentiable and \(f'=g\).

Finally, the Weierstrass M-test is proved: if \(|f_j(x)|\le M_j\) for all \(x\) and \(\sum M_j\) converges, then \(\sum f_j(x)\) converges absolutely pointwise and its partial sums converge uniformly.

The De'Longhi Rivelia automatic latte maker is discounted to $1,300. It uses a touchscreen to prepare milk-based coffee drinks from start to finish, with configurable grinder settings, a swappable bean hopper, and a “bean adapt” function for tuning coffee strength. Its built-in frother produces silky micro-foam, offering easier home cafe-style drinks than manual espresso setups, though not matching the potential quality of a classic portafilter machine.

Imran Mohammad, a Rohingya refugee recognized by UNHCR, describes spending four birthdays in detention on Manus Island after arriving in Papua New Guinea in 2013 at age 19. He recounts overcrowded shipping-container rooms, long queues for food, toilets, showers, laundry, and basic supplies, inadequate prayer space, heat, hunger, limited phone access, and emotional distress. He says conditions in Delta and Mike compounds caused suffering, conflict, isolation, and suicidal thoughts, though he found strength through learning and writing. He describes indefinite detention as filled with daily obstacles, pain, and anguish for those who sought safety in Australia.

The passage describes using a Triangle (1-3-1) offense to attack a Diamond & One defense by placing the star player at the high post, isolating them against the chaser and creating inside triangle action. Options include drives with drop passes for layups, kick-out passes for open shots or penetration, post flashes, and lob exchanges when the high-post entry is overplayed. The offense requires execution, coordination, defensive recognition, timing, communication, and practice in high-post isolation, back cuts, interior passing, and spot-up shooting. Suggested strategies include scouting opponents, recognizing defensive adjustments, varying alignments and entries, moving players, and attacking weaker defenders. The Diamond & One defense is described as four defenders in a zone with one defender denying the opponent’s main scorer.

A funnel-web spider, described as the world’s most venomous spider, was found inside a home in Springwood in the Blue Mountains near Sydney. Bec Sheedy said it was about 5cm wide and that she had not seen one since childhood. Funnel-webs are common along Australia’s east coast but are rarely seen, and their bites can cause severe symptoms including nausea, muscle cramps, sweating and numbness. Thirteen deaths have been recorded in Australia, but none since antivenene was introduced in 1981. Taronga Zoo’s Paul Hare said the spider was likely a male searching for a mate during mating season. He said funnel-webs are defensive rather than aggressive, and advised people in affected areas to avoid handling them, use caution when gardening or cleaning pools, and leave them alone because they help control insects.

The passage describes how total solar eclipses have often inspired fear and religious interpretations, from ancient Greeks, Vikings and Chinese traditions to Americans in 1878 who mistook an eclipse for Judgment Day. David Baron’s book “American Eclipse” recounts both scientific understanding and public terror during that event. Some Christians have linked eclipses to biblical signs, though astronomers reject an eclipse at the crucifixion. Ahead of the Aug. 21 eclipse, Sister Mary Elizabeth says worried Catholics have called her monastery, but the nuns view it as something to enjoy rather than a bad omen. In Islamic tradition, Muhammad taught that an eclipse after his son’s death was a sign of God, not tied to human life or death. Baron says even nonreligious observers may find total eclipses profoundly awe-inspiring because they reveal human smallness in the universe.

KGI’s Ming-Chi Kuo said the 2017 Apple Watch will keep the same form factor as previous models, marking three generations with the same design. He predicted LTE connectivity as the key addition, with LTE and non-LTE versions available in 38mm and 42mm sizes. The passage notes uncertainty about what a future redesign could change, since the interface depends on the current form factor, though thickness could be reduced. It also discusses the possibility that power-saving improvements in a non-LTE model could allow either better battery life or a thinner watch.

A recent college graduate living at home says their mother is demanding $480 per month for rent and phone costs while they start a temporary minimum-wage job earning about $1,600 per month. They also owe tuition, need certification exams, and want to save for a car and apartment. They describe conflicts with their mother, including a recent argument related to their hearing problems and a previous dispute over rent and a school refund.

The response advises the graduate to manage earnings carefully, consider additional jobs, use this transitional period to gain varied experience, and be honest about their role in the strained relationship. It notes that if the mother withheld money or lashed out over the hearing issue as described, that is not normal, but also asks what the mother’s version of the conflict would be.

The speaker pledges to faithfully perform presidential duties according to the Constitution, which he presents as a successful inheritance from the founding generation. He reviews national growth under it, including population expansion, territorial extension, new states, treaties, commerce, liberty, law, and economical government, while acknowledging disease, foreign conflict, war, and internal dissensions. He argues that former party divisions have largely subsided after years of peace and urges citizens to abandon lingering rancor.

He emphasizes the federal and national character of government, assigning domestic concerns to the states and matters involving the Union or foreign powers to the General Government, while stressing mutual respect among representatives from all sections. He praises his predecessor’s administration for preserving peace, reducing debt and taxes, revising the military, acquiring Florida, extending boundaries to the Pacific, recognizing southern nations’ independence, improving defenses, opposing the African slave trade, and promoting exploration, Native civilization, and internal improvements.

He commits to continuing these policies, especially internal improvements, while acknowledging constitutional objections and hoping deliberation will resolve them. Noting the unusual circumstances of his election and limited prior public confidence, he promises upright intentions, devotion to the country, diligent service, cooperation with government bodies and the people, and reliance on divine providence.

President James Madison’s September 1, 1814 proclamation condemns British attacks on Washington, Alexandria, and threatened coastal towns, describing the destruction of public buildings, seizure of private property, and declared plans for further devastation as violations of humanity and civilized warfare. He calls on Americans to unite in resisting and expelling the invader, directs civil and military officers to fulfill their duties, and authorizes military district commanders to call nearby militia to defend exposed or threatened places.

The speaker described a frustrating playoff loss, saying the team played well but gave up too many third-period chances and failed to execute late. They credited Detroit’s effort and said the team must rebound.

The speaker described a tight hockey game decided by bounces, blocked shots, and missed chances. They said the opposing team capitalized on a scramble and later benefited from another bounce after his team failed to clear the puck. He noted his line generated opportunities but needed to finish more. He discussed an incident with an opponent talking after the game, saying he hit him on the foot with his stick. He also described an unusual play where the puck rested on Osgood’s back and was covered by a hand, saying he did not know the rule. He said the team made mistakes, expected a tough series, remained confident in its game, and would prepare quickly for the next matchup.

This study used the Multiphase Optimization Strategy framework to identify effective components of a mobile health sleep promotion platform for children aged 9–12 years with insufficient sleep. Ninety-seven participants from southeastern Pennsylvania and southern New Jersey completed sleep tracking through Fitbit devices and the Way to Health platform. All received sleep tracking and weekly performance feedback, while five components were tested in a factorial design: guideline-based versus personalized sleep goals, child-directed and caregiver-directed loss-framed financial incentives, screen time reduction messaging, and daily routine messaging.

Average baseline weeknight sleep duration was 7.7 hours. Overall, sleep increased by 24 minutes during the intervention and 21 minutes during follow-up. No single component achieved the predefined optimization criterion of increasing weeknight sleep by at least 30 minutes. However, two component combinations did. The highest-ranked combination included the core intervention, a caregiver-directed loss-framed incentive, screen time reduction messaging, and daily routine messaging, increasing sleep by 39.6 minutes during intervention and 33.2 minutes during follow-up. The second included the core intervention, caregiver-directed loss-framed incentive, and daily routine messaging, increasing sleep by 32.0 minutes during intervention and 26.6 minutes during follow-up.

The study concluded that sleep tracking, performance feedback, a sleep goal, caregiver-directed loss-framed incentives, and messaging to reduce screen time and establish routines were optimal settings for the mobile health platform. Limitations included a single geographic site, a predominantly non-Hispanic White sample, fewer captured sleep data among Black participants, a short follow-up period, and use of a commercial sleep tracker with a proprietary algorithm.

A central team found Gorakhpur’s BRD Hospital had admitted patients 10 times beyond capacity after at least 30 children died. Multiple infants shared warmers, and overcrowding was cited as a key issue alongside oxygen supply problems. Reports said nearby SNCUs were non-existent or non-functional. Union health officials announced an Rs 85 crore regional medical centre in Gorakhpur.

May 9, 2001 news mentions include Questia Media cutting about half its staff after slowing book digitization, with Enron Chairman Ken Lay noted as an investor. Market reports said the Dow fell while Nasdaq rose, and Enron shares declined to $56.11 amid weakness in utility and energy-trading stocks.

In Japan, Enron Japan Vice President Nicholas O’Day said the deregulated power market lacked real competition, faced barriers for new entrants, and needed an independent regulator. A related report said Enron commissioned the Brattle Group to assess Japan’s power industry.

In Europe, Williams announced plans to enter deregulating gas and power markets from London, joining companies including Enron.

Several India reports focused on Enron’s Dabhol Power Company dispute with Maharashtra State Electricity Board. Reports said families of expatriate executives were moved from Mumbai to Singapore and security increased, though Enron declined comment. MSEB denied underutilizing its capacity to justify Dabhol purchases, said Uran plant output was constrained by fuel costs, denied federal pressure over the Enron deal, and appointed former Bombay High Court judge M.L. Pendse as arbitrator. The global aluminum foil packaging market is expected to grow at about 4.5% CAGR, driven by packaging innovation, demand from pharmaceutical, cosmetic, food, and beverage sectors, changing consumer lifestyles, and rising spending power. Aluminum foil offers corrosion resistance, hygiene, non-toxicity, and product protection. Growth may be limited by inadequate recycling processes in some countries. Asia Pacific is expected to be the fastest-growing region due to rising income and purchasing power.

MyWorld is a gaming platform that lets players create, customize, store, share, and improve their own games. Users can build objects, select genres and scenes, set rules, and choose single-player, PvP, or Co-Op modes. Creation uses design mode for placing objects and constructor mode for modeling them, including functional items like turrets, sensors, and robots. Players can level up to unlock pre-built materials and customize avatars. The team has launched a Kickstarter campaign to fund further development, offering exclusive materials to early backers.

The paper addresses deontic argumentation, focusing on how argumentative frameworks can determine obligations and permissions in normative domains such as law. Its main concern is weak permission, understood as permission derived from the failure to justify an obligation to the contrary. The authors argue that standard grounded and stable argumentation semantics do not adequately support weak permission when unresolved conflicts between obligations exist.

The paper defines a Deontic Argumentation Theory consisting of facts and rules that generate arguments for literals, obligations, strong permissions, and weak permissions. Weak permissions are represented through “imaginary arguments,” while other arguments are “natural.” Attacks between arguments capture conflicts among literals, obligations, permissions, and weak permissions.

Using examples and formal results, the paper shows that in conflictual theories containing applicable rules for both an obligation and its contrary, grounded and stable semantics fail to justify weak permissions for either side. Consequently, conflicted literals cannot be treated as weakly facultative under those semantics.

To address this, the paper introduces a new wp-semantics based on argumentation semantics for Defeasible Logic. This semantics distinguishes between wp-acceptable and wp-rejected arguments and constructs a unique extension containing justified and rejected arguments. The authors prove that the wp-extension is unique, conflict-free, and that no argument is both justified and rejected. They also show that every argument justified under grounded semantics is justified under wp-semantics.

The new semantics supports weak permission in cases of unresolved obligation conflicts: when both an obligation and its contrary are blocked by conflict, the corresponding weak permissions can be justified. The paper discusses this result in relation to legal inconsistency, sanctions, and principles of legality, arguing that unresolved conflicts within the same legal system should not arbitrarily justify one obligation over the other.

The paper reviews related work in formal argumentation, deontic reasoning, ASPIC+, Input/Output logic, Defeasible Deontic Logic, and prior treatments of weak permission. It concludes that the proposed semantics addresses a gap in existing approaches by handling weak permission in deontic argumentation with unresolved conflicts.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K reporting results from its October 7, 2021 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. James Murdoch and Kimbal Musk were elected as Class II directors for three-year terms. Stockholders did not approve management proposals to reduce director terms to two years or eliminate supermajority voting requirements because they did not meet the required 66 2/3% threshold of outstanding shares. Stockholders approved the ratification of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as Tesla’s independent registered public accounting firm for fiscal year 2021. Advisory stockholder proposals to reduce director terms to one year and provide additional diversity and inclusion reporting were approved. Advisory proposals regarding employee arbitration reporting, board-level oversight of human capital management, and additional human rights reporting were not approved. The report was signed by CFO Zachary J. Kirkhorn on October 13, 2021.

Naïve Forex traders often believe they need exceptional talent or can earn quickly, but the passage argues they should understand market reality, avoid outside influence, and wait for suitable trade setups. It emphasizes mental stability, risk control, and learning technical, fundamental, and sentiment analysis. Traders are encouraged to rely on themselves, develop independent judgment, build their own trading style, and use expert advice only as knowledge while progressing gradually.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that Angela Ahrendts, Senior Vice President, Retail, would depart effective April 15, 2019. Deirdre O’Brien succeeded her as Senior Vice President, Retail + People, effective February 5, 2019. The report was signed on February 6, 2019 by Katherine Adams.

The National Technology Security Coalition and Cloud Security Alliance are partnering to improve cloud vendor security reviews by promoting CSA’s Security, Trust & Assurance Registry and related tools as recommended practices. They aim to streamline vendor security reviews, reduce effort, encourage best practices, and create a STAR-based questionnaire mapped to widely used compliance frameworks. A joint whitepaper will explain the program for CISOs and vendors. The organizations will also participate in each other’s events, discuss industry issues in working groups, and collaborate on cloud security research. CSA focuses on cloud security best practices, while NTSC advocates for CISOs and cybersecurity policy.

Consumer Electricals Ltd submitted an expression of interest on September 20, 2017, for Kenstar’s business and brand after an invitation from Videocon Industries.
