The bid price was not disclosed, results are pending, and no binding documents or negotiations have occurred. Videocon group is selling assets to reduce debt exceeding Rs 40,000 crore.

Daniella Teutsch and Sara Wolf founded HydroChic in 2007 to create attractive modest swimwear, inspired by their own difficulty finding concealing bathing suits as religious Jewish women. Customer feedback revealed demand from women with mastectomies, bariatric surgeries, skin cancer, and psoriasis, leading the company to design supportive, concealing, compression, and skin-protective athletic wear. Serving women with special health needs became a key part of the business and brought both financial success and personal impact.

Legal experts expect higher education to be a frequent subject for the Supreme Court, though only two college-related transgender rights cases are on the main docket. Much attention is on the shadow docket, which allows rapid rulings without full briefings, arguments or explanations and has created uncertainty for colleges. Experts say likely issues include transgender rights, international student and scholar visa policies, First Amendment rights, academic freedom and federal funding. Cases involving transgender athletes, including West Virginia v. B.P.J. and Little v. Hecox, could affect Title IX interpretations beyond sports. Other shadow docket matters involve immigration policy, agency staffing, funding threats and identification documents for transgender or nonbinary people. Experts warn emergency rulings may allow policy changes before full review, creating consequences that may be difficult to reverse.

Oklahoma City Taco Bell employees called police after 52-year-old Zette Madden allegedly threatened them, demanded money, and damaged registers, doors, a drive-thru window, and a menu with a tire iron. Police say she ignored orders to drop it and was tased. She was hospitalized for cuts and jailed on robbery and property destruction charges.

Riley Oil Company in Paoli, Indiana, is a family-run full-service gas station that has operated since 1971. Employees pump gas, wash windshields and check oil for free. Owners Jo Ann and Jeff Riley say the business values customer service, conversation and family involvement, with multiple Riley family members working there and future generations expected to continue the tradition.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K dated June 2, 2022, reporting that it updated guidance for the quarter ending June 30, 2022, due to unfavorable foreign exchange rate movement through May. A slide deck with revised guidance was furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing includes standard forward-looking statement cautions and lists Microsoft’s registered securities on NASDAQ. The report was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

Falkland Islands Senior Fisheries Scientist Alexander Arkhipkin warned that largely unregulated high seas fishing, including in the Southwest Atlantic, limits data on vessels, catches, species and sizes, complicating stock assessments and raising overfishing risks. He contributed to a September 2017 IMARPE workshop in Lima on jumbo squid stock assessment, prompted by rising foreign jigger activity in the Eastern Pacific. The workshop produced recommendations on surveys, stock structure analysis and assessment techniques to improve knowledge and international collaboration.

Nintendo confirmed Labo will include Toy Con Garage, a tool for creating custom cardboard accessories using basic inputs, actions, and if-then statements. Demonstrations included a cardboard electric guitar and electronic tennis. It is unclear whether buying a Labo set is required to access it.

The study uses molecular dynamics nanoindentation simulations combined with orientation-resolved Schmid factor mapping to examine temperature-dependent slip activation in single-crystalline α-titanium. Simulations were performed in LAMMPS using an EAM potential for [0001], [10̅10], and [2̅110] orientations at 10, 300, and 600 K. Dislocation structures, shear strain, strain tensor components, surface morphology, and dislocation density were analyzed.

Load–displacement curves showed Hertzian elastic behavior followed by plasticity onset. Pop-in events were strongest for [0001], while [10̅10] and [2̅110] showed smoother dislocation nucleation. Contact pressure decreased with increasing temperature after deeper indentation, reflecting enhanced atomic mobility and reduced indentation resistance.

For [0001], basal a-type dislocations dominated, with c-type, prismatic, and pyramidal ⟨c+a⟩ dislocations also present. Low temperature promoted localized deformation and stress-induced HCP-to-BCC transformation, while higher temperature produced more diffuse deformation. Surface morphology evolved from localized imprints at 10 K to stronger pile-up at 300 K and more relaxed features at 600 K.

For [10̅10], plasticity involved prismatic and basal slip, with pyramidal slip activated at higher stress and temperature. A lasso mechanism produced prismatic loops, especially at 300 K, and surface morphology showed a characteristic two-lobe pile-up pattern. For [2̅110], dislocation loops formed beneath the indenter and expanded across multiple slip planes, producing asymmetric pile-up and temperature-dependent recovery.

Dislocation density was highest for [0001] at all temperatures, increasing from 0.86 to 1.52 × 10¹⁶ m⁻² between 10 and 600 K. Prismatic orientations showed lower densities that decreased with temperature, indicating enhanced recovery and annihilation. Overall, temperature and crystallographic orientation strongly controlled slip activation, defect retention, and nanoindentation-induced surface morphology in α-titanium.

The disclosure relates to physical layer preambles and signaling for wireless communication, including WLAN systems using APs and STAs. It describes packet structures for PPDUs that include a preamble and data portion, with legacy fields followed by a universal signal field (U-SIG) and, in some formats, version-specific signal fields such as EHT-SIG.

The U-SIG may include version-independent fields, such as a version identifier, uplink/downlink indication, TXOP duration, BSS color, and frequency occupation information, as well as version-dependent fields such as packet format information. The packet format may identify trigger-based, single-user, multi-user, or unified single-user/multi-user PPDUs. The U-SIG may indicate bandwidth, punctured channel information, EHT-SIG format, modulation and coding, compression mode, and other signaling needed to decode later fields.

The EHT-SIG may provide additional signaling, including resource unit allocation, per-user information, spatial stream configuration, and scheduling information for OFDMA or MU-MIMO transmissions. The disclosure describes designs for transmitting EHT-SIG content across subchannels or content channels, including duplicated or different signaling per subchannel, punctured transmissions, and parallelized signaling.

The disclosure also describes wireless devices, APs, and STAs that include radios, modems, processors, memory, and antennas for generating, transmitting, receiving, and decoding such packets. It discusses use in IEEE 802.11 protocols, including 802.11be and later versions, and includes example fields, bit allocations, bandwidth and puncturing options, compression modes, and spatial reuse signaling.

Darren Till won a close, controversial unanimous decision over Stephen Thompson at UFC Fight Night 130 in Liverpool. Critics argued the location may have influenced the result, and Till said he would rematch Thompson in America as soon as possible if Thompson is not injured. The fight featured little action aside from Till’s final-round knockdown.

The Justice Department asked the Education Department to investigate the University of Nevada at Reno’s UndocuPack program, questioning whether taxpayer funds support services for undocumented students. UNR president Brian Sandoval said the program serves all students regardless of citizenship, uses no federal funds, and complies with state and federal law. Advocates say the move is part of broader Trump administration efforts targeting higher education benefits and supports for undocumented students, including lawsuits over in-state tuition and investigations of scholarships. They warn colleges may scale back lawful support programs out of fear, while UNR plans to respond through legal channels.

The passage describes a system, method, and computer program product for processing mobile payments when user devices or merchant payment systems are disconnected from payment servers. A user device associated with an e-wallet can be enabled for an offline payment mode, but only one device per e-wallet may have this mode enabled at a time to prevent multiple offline transactions from overdrawing accounts or exceeding reserved offline balances.

Offline transactions are conducted through local communications between a user device and a merchant payment system, such as NFC, Bluetooth, ZigBee, Z-Wave, LAN, USB, or QR/barcode scanning. The merchant payment system sends an offline payment request, and the user device checks whether the offline balance is sufficient, obtains user approval, updates the remaining offline balance, and returns a payment approval message. Both the user device and merchant payment system may store offline transaction information and send it to a payment server when network connectivity is restored.

The payment server maintains e-wallet configuration data, offline mode status, reserved offline amounts, and processed transaction identifiers. When it receives offline transaction information, it checks whether the transaction ID was previously processed to prevent duplicate processing, then debits the payer account, updates the pre-authorized offline amount, and credits the merchant account. The passage also describes enabling offline mode, reserving funds for offline use, transferring offline mode between user devices through local communications, and possible implementation in cloud computing environments.

The passage describes the High Post Split Offense as a simple but effective basketball offense using a 2-3 high alignment, high post splits, down screens, back cuts, post isolations, post-ups, and variations to create scoring opportunities for all five players. It emphasizes execution, spacing, timing, defensive recognition, and non-verbal coordination. Key options include guards splitting the high post, counters to defensive pressure such as fake splits, direct basket cuts, handoffs, and two-same-side cuts, plus down-screen reads including curls, fades, back cuts, screen-and-rolls, and slips. The high post can shoot, drive, pass, or counter overplay with lobs, wing feeds, exchanges, and player interchange. Variations include wing back-cut entries, wing pass entries, double-away action, and single/double screen continuity. The passage also stresses strong post-ups, offensive rebounding through anticipation and effort, and regular individual skill development in practice.

The passage describes a tonneau cover for pickup truck beds with multiple movable panel sections and a base panel. The cover includes latching assemblies with pinch latch handles on opposite sides of each panel, connected so actuating one handle can release latches on both sides. Springs bias the latches toward the latched condition and return them when force is removed. The design may include integrated lights near the latch handles, flush-mounted latch assemblies, adjustable rail clips, and side rails with seals to reduce water entry. Additional features include a vertical gusset assembly to hold folded panels upright, hinge assemblies with hinge seals, spacers and seal rods, and a buckle securement system with a channel bracket to hold folded panels in open or folded positions.

A Bank of England regulator said British banks should not expect major further capital or liquidity rule changes after Basel III implementation, with future focus on new risks, unintended regulatory effects, cyber resilience, and impacts on derivatives clearing.

Aaron Judge will have his injured elbow evaluated after the Yankees’ season ended. The injury sidelined him briefly in late July and limited him mostly to DH before he returned to the outfield with reduced arm strength. Judge said he will “do some work” on it but does not know if surgery is needed.

The passage describes semiconductor packaging methods and structures for forming large or super-large multi-die integrated fan-out (InFO) packages. Interconnect structures or a universal interconnect structure are bonded to a carrier substrate, embedded in a first encapsulant, thinned to expose contacts, and used to form a reconstructed wafer. Tested packaged semiconductor devices or discrete semiconductor components, such as processors and memory cubes, are bonded to the interconnect structures or redistribution layers using solder bonding or low-temperature copper-to-copper bonding. Underfill may be applied, and the devices are encased in a second encapsulant, thinned, de-bonded from the carrier, and provided with external contacts for connection to external devices such as printed circuit boards.

Embodiments include semiconductor dies arranged over individual interconnect structures, bridging adjacent interconnect structures, or sharing a universal interconnect structure. Other embodiments form multiple universal redistribution layers over an embedded interconnect structure before bonding semiconductor components. The disclosed processes use tested known-good components, wafer-level integration, encapsulation, redistribution layers, through-substrate vias, passivation layers, and external contacts to improve component and board-level reliability. The packages can support sizes greater than 70 mm by 70 mm for high-performance computing applications requiring high data rates, large bandwidths, and low latency.

Microsoft’s Form 10-K for fiscal year ended June 30, 2021 identifies Microsoft as a technology company focused on empowering people and organizations through software, services, devices, and solutions. Its offerings include cloud-based services, productivity applications, operating systems, server applications, business solutions, software development tools, video games, PCs, tablets, gaming consoles, accessories, online advertising, support, and consulting.

Microsoft’s strategy centers on three ambitions: reinventing productivity and business processes; building the intelligent cloud and intelligent edge platform; and creating more personal computing. Key products and services discussed include Microsoft 365, Teams, Viva, Dynamics 365, Power Platform, Azure, Azure Stack, Azure Arc, GitHub, Visual Studio, Windows 10, Windows 11, Edge, Surface, Xbox Game Pass, and Xbox Cloud Gaming. The report also notes the March 2021 acquisition of ZeniMax Media and an April 2021 agreement to acquire Nuance Communications.

Microsoft reports three operating segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. These include Office, LinkedIn, Dynamics, Azure, server products, enterprise services, Windows, Devices, Gaming, and Search advertising. The company describes competition across these areas from firms including Apple, Google, Amazon, IBM, Oracle, Salesforce, SAP, Slack, Zoom, Sony, Nintendo, Facebook, and others.

The filing includes discussion of COVID-19 impacts, sustainability commitments, racial equity initiatives, digital skills programs, and human capital resources. As of June 30, 2021, Microsoft employed about 181,000 full-time people, including 103,000 in the U.S. and 78,000 internationally. The report also lists executive officers, including Satya Nadella as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer.

Microsoft’s common stock trades on Nasdaq under MSFT. As of December 31, 2020, the aggregate market value of common stock held by non-affiliates was $1.7 trillion, and as of July 26, 2021, there were 7,514,891,248 shares outstanding. The report identifies strategic and competitive risks, including intense competition, platform-based ecosystem competition, evolving business models, and execution risks related to cloud-based services.

On Nov. 26, 2001, multiple news reports described worsening investor concern over Enron’s finances and the pending Dynegy acquisition. Enron shares fell to around $4, reaching lows near $3.76, far below the implied Dynegy offer and less than one-third of reported book value. Analysts and investors questioned whether Dynegy would complete, renegotiate, or abandon the deal amid Enron’s financial disclosures, weakened trading business, debt pressures, and possible “material adverse change” clauses.

Enron and its banks formalized an extension of a $690 million loan deadline to Dec. 14, while discussions continued on broader debt restructuring and potential new financing. Enron bonds traded at distressed levels, and rating concerns persisted. Reports said Citigroup had reduced exposure to Enron through credit default swap transactions tied to synthetic Enron debt.

Enron also faced employee class-action lawsuits over 401(k) retirement plan losses, with one suit seeking $850 million and alleging employees were sold inflated Enron stock and restricted from selling during a plan lockdown. Other reports covered possible sales of Enron assets in Brazil and India, and broader concerns about energy trading companies following Enron’s collapse.

Martin Colin Hodder, 45, of Macclesfield, was jailed for 18 weeks after admitting two assault charges at Stockport magistrates’ court. The court heard he attacked his ex-partner and her daughter with a butter knife in January after drinking a bottle and a half of vodka. Prosecutors said he first held the knife to his own throat, then cut his ex-partner’s arms and slashed her daughter’s wrist after threatening them. Magistrates described it as a sustained weapon attack in a domestic setting while drunk and imposed a year-long restraining order. His ex-partner criticised the sentence as too lenient.

Coach Julien said there was no update on an injured player, who was being evaluated, and declined to speculate on availability. He said a skilled but inexperienced player was used because the team needed him, and he was not disappointed with his performance. Julien said the team improved in the third period after sitting back too much earlier. He emphasized the series was “do or die,” with the goal of winning at home to force another game, and said there was no panic. He discussed the importance of depth, secondary scoring, awareness around the net, face-offs, lineup tinkering, and avoiding “passengers.” Julien defended Zdeno Chara, calling him one of the league’s best defensemen and a strong captain. He said both teams have created tight, close, exciting games, with coaches making adjustments to gain an edge.

Enerfax Daily for February 20, 2002 reported North American natural gas and power prices, futures, volumes, and market news. NYMEX March natural gas futures rose $0.191 to $2.397/MMBtu, driven by fund buying, below-normal weather forecasts, and expectations of a 110–120 Bcf storage withdrawal. Henry Hub next-day gas rose $0.13 to $2.32/MMBtu.

Major news items included a shareholder lawsuit against JP Morgan Chase over Enron exposure disclosures; El Paso Corp’s planned $750 million sale of Texas pipelines, gathering systems, and related assets to El Paso Energy Partners; AES’s plan to sell $1 billion–$1.5 billion in assets after a sharp stock decline and liquidity concerns; and debate over a proposed derivatives oversight bill criticized by the National Energy Marketers Association. Other articles covered Enron accounting disclosure issues, data center power demand forecasts, and MISO, PJM, and SPP’s upcoming Single Market Design Forum meeting. The issue also listed power and gas bulletins, financial market declines, and multiple energy industry advertisements and event notices.

The passage describes MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 device subsystems, interfaces, application guidance, support resources, revision history, and packaging information. The LFSS_B subsystem uses the 32kHz LFCLK for low-power peripherals and includes RTC_B and an independent watchdog timer. RTC_B provides real-time clock/calendar functions, alarms, periodic wake interrupts, calibration, temperature drift compensation, and clock output for calibration. IWDT_B monitors code execution using an independent LFOSC-based clock and can generate a POR reset if not serviced. WWDT can generate a reset or interrupt within a specified timing window and supports sleep-mode stopping and interval timer mode.

The devices include TIMGx general-purpose timers and TIMAx advanced timers with counters, prescalers, synchronization, triggers, DMA/interrupt support, PWM, fault handling, and capture/compare features. Analog and I/O sections describe internal analog connections, DAC_OUT use on PA15, IOMUX-controlled digital I/O, wake-up logic, and open-drain 5V-tolerant I/O behavior. Debug and programming support include a two-wire SWD interface and a boot strap loader over UART or I2C, protected by a 256-bit password and optionally disabled.

Factory constants provide read-only device capability, trim, revision, and identification data. Application guidance recommends VDD decoupling capacitors, NRST pullup and pulldown components, an optional ROSC resistor for SYSOSC frequency correction, a VCORE tank capacitor, and pullups for open-drain outputs. Support sections list TI development tools, SDKs, IDEs, documentation resources, trademarks, ESD caution, revision updates, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

The speaker says the team’s win was essential to keep the series alive and that improved skating, physical play, faceoffs, and offensive pressure helped. He emphasizes sticking to their style, managing the puck better, staying poised in an emotional environment, and focusing on preparation inside the dressing room rather than media criticism. He praises individual contributions and leadership, notes New Jersey’s team strength, and says success depends on resilience, execution, and earning breaks through hard play.

Ben Bishop said he feels better and that rest helped. He reflected on his path through multiple organizations, saying time in the minors taught him how to be a pro and prepared him for his chance in Tampa. He emphasized approaching every game the same way, including do-or-die situations, and said the team has been consistent all year. He noted players are angry after losses but expects them to bounce back, and described the season as enjoyable with a great locker room.

University of Michigan researchers developed a clear, durable “omniphobic” coating that can repel nearly every known liquid and prevent grime buildup on surfaces such as tables, floors, walls, and phone screens. Inspired by Anish Tuteja’s desire to make cleaning up after his child easier, the coating combines fluorinated polyurethane and F-POSS. Researchers say it could help keep homes and daycares cleaner and may have industrial uses. The team is now studying whether the material is toxic.

Plug Power Inc. (NASDAQ: PLUG) shares fell 1.54% in the most recent session, closing at $1.92. Analysts have a 52-week average price target of $3.22 based on 7 opinions, with targets ranging from $1.30 to $5. The stock’s average brokerage recommendation is 1.86, with 1 Buy, 4 Outperform, 1 Hold, 1 Underperform, and 0 Sell ratings. Its ATR-14 is 0.08, weekly volatility is 3.54%, monthly volatility is 4.50%, and RSI is 51.76. Plug Power has a market capitalization of $445.8 million, 232.19 million shares outstanding, and traded 2.29 million shares versus an average of 3.79 million.

Paula Norrell sued Waste Away Group, Inc. alleging gender discrimination under Title VII after the company promoted Terry White instead of her to district sales manager for the combined Montgomery-Opelika district. The court found Norrell established a prima facie failure-to-promote case, but Waste Away articulated legitimate, nondiscriminatory reasons for selecting White, including his prior experience in the same combined-district role, outside sales and management experience, and leadership skills. The court concluded Norrell failed to show these reasons were pretext for gender discrimination; alleged remarks by supervisors were stray or unrelated to the decision. Norrell abandoned her disparate impact claim. The court granted Waste Away’s motion for summary judgment on all claims, entered judgment for Waste Away, and taxed costs against Norrell.

Queen Elizabeth visited Royal Manchester Children’s Hospital, meeting young victims of the Manchester bombing and emergency responders. She spoke with 14-year-old Evie Mills, called the attack “wicked,” and noted that “everyone’s united here.”

The Triangle Post Offense, created and refined by Tex Winter, is a basketball system based on defensive recognition, precise spacing, player movement, and fundamental execution rather than set plays. It uses a sideline triangle on one side and a weakside two-person game on the other, involving all players and emphasizing low-post play, passing, cuts, screens, reversals, and one-on-one opportunities. Players maintain 15–20 feet of spacing to spread the defense, discourage help or double teams, and create passing and driving lanes.

The offense can begin through many entries, including outside and inside cuts, dribble clears, off-guard cuts, post pops, base screens, reversals, weaves, exchanges, and post reversals. Its options include post ups, post splits, corner actions, screen-and-rolls, solo post cuts, and weakside two-game pass or dribble series. It also includes automatic counters to defensive overplays such as fronting the post, sagging wing defenders, double teams, denied reversals, and denied backdoor passes.

Successful use requires players to understand every position, read defensive deployment, execute fundamentals, and practice through breakdown drills and scrimmaging. The passage also emphasizes scouting opponents, varying entries, and understanding the offense even for defensive preparation.

Bollinger Bands are a technical indicator developed by John Bollinger in the 1980s to analyze asset volatility and potential trend changes. They consist of a central moving average with upper and lower bands based on standard deviations. In TradingView, the default setting uses a 20-period moving average, but the period, standard deviation multiplier, and price source can be adjusted. The passage notes that Bollinger Bands can support breakout, mean reversion, or squeeze strategies, but they do not create a profitable system on their own. Disadvantages include false signals, reduced effectiveness in range-bound markets, signal delays, and sensitivity to settings. TradingView and Pine Script can be used to calculate and test Bollinger Bands strategies, but proper rule definition, parameter optimization, risk management, and backtesting are necessary.

FTB Advisors Inc. increased its stake in Vanguard Total International Stock ETF by 3.6% in the second quarter to 13,149 shares worth $706,000. Other institutional investors, including Wells Fargo, Eaton Vance, Allen Investment Management, and Private Advisor Group, also raised holdings. VXUS traded at $54.8501 on Friday, with a 1-year range of $44.68 to $55.28, and recently paid a quarterly dividend of $0.298 per share.

The speaker accepts the presidency as a solemn public trust and pledges to serve the welfare of all citizens. He emphasizes the strength of democratic self-government, urges an end to partisan and sectional animosity, and calls for renewed devotion to the Constitution, administered in a spirit of amity, mutual concession, and respect for the division of federal, state, and executive powers.

He states that citizens as well as public officials share responsibility for preserving constitutional government through vigilance and fair judgment. Public expenditures should be limited to necessary needs, and officials should model simplicity and economy. Foreign policy should remain independent, peaceful, neutral, and free of entangling alliances.

The speaker calls for sound finances, reduced unnecessary taxation, protection of the public domain, fair treatment and advancement of Indians toward citizenship, repression of polygamy in the Territories, enforcement of laws against certain servile immigration, and civil-service reform based on merit rather than partisan reward. He affirms that freedmen are entitled to all constitutional rights and bear the duties of citizenship. He concludes by urging practical, united effort in public service and invoking God’s aid and blessing.

Jane Goodall, who died October 1 at 91, studied chimpanzees in Tanzania’s Gombe National Park for decades and also built a unique collection of chimp skeletons from individuals with known life histories. Her team preserved bones from chimps after death, allowing researchers to examine how age, sex, weight and experiences shaped skeletal features. Goodall declined to speculate about what the collection might reveal for understanding ancient hominids, saying, “We just don’t know.” She explained her motivation simply: field researchers “shouldn’t waste anything.” The skeleton of Flo, a prominent Gombe matriarch, showed how the collection yielded insights into body size, weight estimation and bone loss. The author argues that Goodall’s preservation efforts continued to provide scientific value beyond her fieldwork.

The TPS7H500x-SP series is a family of radiation-hardness-assured, peak current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, with a 0.613-V reference accuracy of +0.7%/-1%, configurable 100-kHz to 2-MHz switching frequency, and external synchronization support. The family includes TPS7H5001-SP, TPS7H5002-SP, TPS7H5003-SP, and TPS7H5004-SP.

TPS7H5001-SP is a full-featured dual-output controller for Si and GaN converters, supporting synchronous rectifier outputs, programmable dead time, and configurable maximum duty cycle. TPS7H5002-SP is a single-output controller for buck and single-ended isolated topologies with synchronous rectification, configurable dead time and leading-edge blanking, and 75% or 100% maximum duty cycle. TPS7H5003-SP is similar but has fixed 50-ns dead time and leading-edge blanking. TPS7H5004-SP is a dual-output controller for non-synchronous push-pull and full-bridge topologies, with configurable leading-edge blanking and a fixed 50% maximum duty cycle.

The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require VIN bypass capacitance. Start-up requires VLDO above UVLO, reference availability, EN above threshold, FAULT below threshold, and junction temperature below shutdown. Features include soft start, programmable UVLO, internal oscillator, external synchronization, primary-secondary synchronization, current sensing, cycle-by-cycle current limit, hiccup-mode restart, external fault shutdown, slope compensation, thermal shutdown, and frequency compensation support.

The document also provides design guidance for a synchronous push-pull GaN converter using TPS7H5001-SP, including component-selection methods for switching frequency, feedback resistors, dead time, leading-edge blanking, soft start, transformer, FETs, clamp, output filter, current sensing, hiccup timing, compensation, and slope compensation. It includes power-supply and PCB layout recommendations, related documentation, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

The author describes the second week of motherhood as especially difficult, marked by severe sleep deprivation, painful breastfeeding, concerns about babies not gaining weight, loneliness after support decreased, and difficulty understanding or soothing a crying newborn. These challenges affected the author’s mental health, confidence, and relationship with her husband, leading to emotional distress and conflict. The author says the experience eventually improved.

Amazon.com filed an 8-K reporting that on June 15, 2017 it entered into a merger agreement with Whole Foods Market, Inc. and Walnut Merger Sub, Inc. Under the agreement, Merger Sub will merge into Whole Foods Market, which will survive as an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Amazon. Whole Foods shareholders will receive $42.00 per share in cash, subject to specified exclusions. The merger requires Whole Foods shareholder approval, regulatory clearances, and other customary conditions, and is not conditioned on Amazon obtaining financing. Either party may terminate the agreement under certain circumstances, including if the merger is not completed by February 15, 2018, subject to a possible 90-day extension. Whole Foods may owe Amazon a $400 million termination fee in specified circumstances. Amazon expects to finance the transaction with debt financing and cash on hand and entered into a commitment letter for a 364-day senior unsecured bridge term loan facility of up to $13.7 billion. Amazon and Whole Foods issued a joint press release on June 16, 2017 announcing the agreement.

A follow-through day is a market-timing concept developed by William J. O’Neil to identify a potential shift from a correction or downtrend to a new uptrend. It occurs on Day 4 or later of a valid rally attempt when a major index closes significantly higher than the previous day on higher volume. A rally attempt begins with a higher close, and remains valid if the index does not fall below the initial low during the next days.

The passage says follow-through days can signal renewed momentum and help investors re-enter the market, but they are not perfect and may fail if the index makes a new low. Backtesting on the S&P 500 using SPY showed poor short-term results, attributed to mean reversion in indices, though results improved slightly with an RSI filter. The article concludes that follow-through days may be less useful for short-term index traders, while O’Neil’s focus was on individual growth stocks.

The double top chart pattern is a bearish reversal formation made of two swing highs at roughly the same level with a swing low between them. It appears at the end of an uptrend or prolonged pullback in a downtrend and suggests the price may decline after breaking below the neckline, which acts as support. Traders may use it to close long positions or enter short positions after a neckline break or retest. Profit targets are estimated by projecting the pattern’s height downward from the neckline, while stop losses may be placed in the middle or above the pattern. The passage notes that coding and backtesting the pattern is difficult. It cites Thomas Bulkowski’s research, which found only 39% of double top formations reached their target, and argues that shorting stocks is difficult due to the stock market’s upward bias. Suggested rules include confirming an uptrend, ensuring the two highs are within 3% of each other, and waiting for a significant volume break below the neckline.

Retired Metro Police homicide detective Phil Ramos reviewed newly released 1 October body camera footage and said officers appeared tense and anxious outside Stephen Paddock’s hotel room. He said forgetting to activate a body camera and an accidental gun discharge were understandable given the expectation of a possible firefight. Ramos noted surprise over the lack of timestamps and cautioned that conclusions cannot be drawn from the videos alone.

A heat wave in the northeastern United States is expected to move west after the Fourth of July, bringing dangerous temperatures to the central U.S. and southern California, the National Weather Service said. New York City faced heat index values up to 106°F and an air quality alert. At least one heat-related death was reported in Pennsylvania. A storm front is expected to cool the eastern seaboard later in the week.

News reports from Oct. 29, 2001 focused on worsening corporate credit quality and Enron’s financial troubles. Moody’s reported far more U.S. companies under review for downgrade than upgrade, while S&P projected about $100 billion in corporate debt defaults for 2001 amid recession and effects from Sept. 11.

Enron’s shares fell to near seven-year lows after Moody’s cut its senior unsecured debt rating to Baa2, two levels above junk, and placed ratings on review for further downgrade. Reports cited Enron’s $638 million third-quarter loss, $1.01 billion in charges, a $1.2 billion equity reduction, off-balance-sheet partnership concerns involving former CFO Andrew Fastow, and an SEC inquiry. Enron drew down about $3 billion in credit lines, used about $2 billion to repay commercial paper, and sought an additional $1 billion to $2 billion in bank credit to restore investor and market confidence.

U.S. energy traders including Mirant, Duke, El Paso and American Electric Power said dealings with Enron remained normal, though they were monitoring credit exposure. European energy firms were reportedly restricting or freezing trades with Enron pending new credit arrangements. Analysts and investors expressed concern that deteriorating confidence and credit access could affect Enron’s trading business, while some said a junk rating was not likely. Other items discussed possible harsher lending terms, asset sales, a rumored Royal Dutch/Shell interest in Enron, insider buying at independent power producers excluding Enron, and commentary on Enron’s broader market and Houston civic significance.

Microsoft’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2021 reported total revenue of $45.3 billion, up from $37.2 billion a year earlier, and net income of $20.5 billion, up from $13.9 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $2.71, compared with $1.82. Operating income rose to $20.2 billion. Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 36% to $20.7 billion. Segment revenue was $15.0 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $17.0 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $13.3 billion for More Personal Computing. Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $130.6 billion, and total assets were $335.4 billion. Microsoft also reported a $3.3 billion net income tax benefit related to the transfer of intangible properties.

The passage argues that education policy has become more politically polarized since COVID-19 and the 2020 racial reckoning, with increased scrutiny of schools, distrust in institutions, and intensified activism around curriculum, staffing, school choice, and student well-being. Despite this climate, it states that cross-partisan education policy progress is occurring in states, even as federal gridlock persists.

The paper uses “cross-partisan” to describe support across political divides, noting that traditional bipartisanship is often viewed negatively in the current political environment. It identifies five factors associated with successful cross-partisan education initiatives: clear and broadly appealing communication, responsiveness to local context, political cover for stakeholders, opportunities for both sides to claim a win, and strategic use of media.

Examples include state action on the science of reading after the Sold a Story podcast, teacher apprenticeship programs supported by federal funds in Republican-led states, the Interstate Teacher Mobility Compact, locally tailored career and technical education programs in Idaho and North Carolina, Virginia’s revised history standards, teacher pay increases paired with conservative priorities, and expanded civics education requirements.

The passage also advises advocates to understand the political landscape, define success realistically, identify shared problems, assess urgency, consider effects on frontline educators, frame policies as expanding opportunity, avoid mission creep, prioritize core goals, and understand opponents’ values. It concludes that meaningful cross-partisan education policy change is achievable when advocates focus on students’ needs, local support, clear communication, and practical collaboration.

The passage previews the Indianapolis Colts’ options for the No. 6 pick in the 2018 NFL Draft, highlighting Bradley Chubb, Quenton Nelson, and Saquon Barkley as top prospects. It notes the Colts’ need to improve their pass rush, protect Andrew Luck, and add foundational talent during Chris Ballard’s rebuild.

This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed Chikungunya seroprevalence in Ethiopia using studies published in English from 2016 to November 2023. Following PRISMA guidelines, 40 records were identified and five eligible studies were included. The pooled seroprevalence was 12.35%, with the highest regional prevalence in SNNPR and the highest district prevalence in Debub Ari, while Lare district had the lowest. Seroprevalence varied by geography, occupation, age, sex, education, and diagnostic method. Farmers and adults generally had higher prevalence, while sex-related findings were inconsistent. Subgroup analyses showed significant heterogeneity, especially among ELISA-based studies. Begg’s and Egger’s tests found no significant publication bias. The review concludes that Chikungunya remains a public health concern in Ethiopia and recommends improved preparedness, collaboration, public awareness, and consideration of diagnostic methods and population factors in control strategies.

The Piotroski F-Score strategy, developed by Joseph Piotroski, is a stock selection method that evaluates companies using nine financial criteria related to profitability, liquidity, and efficiency. Stocks scoring 8 or 9 are considered financially strong, while scores of 0 to 4 indicate weak financials. The strategy is commonly used by value investors to identify undervalued stocks with strong fundamentals and may also help with growth stock selection, but it is not a guarantee of success and should be used with other research.

The passage discusses using the F-Score for portfolio construction, financial ratio analysis, risk-return evaluation, identifying value stocks, and backtesting. Alpha Architect tested the strategy on NYSE stocks from 1974 to 2014 and found annual returns of 13.3% for its modified F-score, 12.6% for the original Piotroski score, and 11.2% for the S&P 500, with similar standard deviations. On the cheapest 20% of stocks with F-Scores above 6, returns were 15.9% for Alpha Architect’s method, 15.2% for the Piotroski score, and 11.2% for the S&P 500. The passage also cites tests on European, Norwegian, and Swedish stocks.

Patrick McCaffery, a 6-foot-8 four-star 2019 recruit and son of Iowa coach Fran McCaffery, committed to Iowa after realizing he wanted to play for his father, alongside his brother Connor, and in front of his family. He announced the decision after telling his mother, Connor, and his AAU coach.

McCaffery is Iowa’s first 2019 recruit and is highly ranked nationally, with Rivals placing him 30th, Scout 42nd, and the 247Sports Composite 36th. He said Iowa faced little serious competition for his commitment and cited the program’s playing style, fastbreak offense, and freedom to play through mistakes as reasons for choosing the Hawkeyes.

He hopes to recruit other 2019 prospects, including D.J. Carton, Trace Jackson-Davis, and Tyrell Terry. McCaffery averaged 13.8 points on 60.6 percent shooting as a sophomore while helping Iowa City West win a Class 4A state title. He has focused on gaining strength, increasing his weight from about 165 to 175 pounds, and preparing for the physicality of Big Ten basketball.

At oral argument, several Supreme Court justices appeared open to allowing trial judges to restrict overnight discussions between defense lawyers and clients who are still testifying, particularly discussions directly about testimony, while permitting talk about trial strategy or related collateral matters. The case involves David Villarreal, convicted of murder after a Texas trial judge barred his lawyer from discussing his testimony overnight. Villarreal argued this denied effective assistance of counsel, but Texas courts upheld the conviction.

Villarreal’s lawyer, Stuart Banner, argued that any line between trial strategy and testimony is unclear and would chill defense counsel. Justices Ketanji Brown Jackson, Elena Kagan, and Neil Gorsuch questioned whether courts could prohibit a narrow category of testimony preparation or coaching. Texas argued lawyers should not discuss the content or manner of testimony, including advice such as speaking clearly or making eye contact. The United States proposed a brighter rule barring any discussion of the client’s testimony, while allowing matters such as plea discussions.

The passage presents material from *Designing Distributed Systems*, including online resources, permissions for using example code, O’Reilly Safari information, publisher contact details, and acknowledgments.

It explains that modern applications often require distributed systems to meet expectations for availability, reliability, agility, and rapid scaling. Containers and container orchestrators are described as foundational tools that make distributed systems easier to build through reusable components and patterns. The passage reviews the evolution from purpose-built machines to client-server systems and then to internet-era distributed systems. It compares distributed systems patterns to earlier advances in algorithms, object-oriented programming, design patterns, and open source software.

Patterns are defined as general blueprints for organizing distributed systems without requiring specific technologies. Their value includes learning from others’ experience, establishing a shared vocabulary, and enabling reusable components.

The passage introduces single-node container patterns, where multiple tightly coupled containers are colocated on one machine and may share resources such as filesystems, network namespaces, and memory. It explains motivations for splitting single-node applications into multiple containers: resource isolation, team ownership, reuse, and separation of concerns.

The sidecar pattern uses an auxiliary container to augment an application container. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service, synchronizing configuration from an API, providing process introspection, and building a simple Git-based platform as a service. Effective sidecars should be parameterized, have stable APIs, and be documented through Dockerfile directives, environment variables, and labels.

The ambassador pattern uses a container to broker communication between an application and external services. Examples include routing requests to shards in a sharded Redis deployment, brokering service connections across environments, and splitting traffic for experiments or production-load testing.

The adapter pattern modifies an application container’s interface to match a standard expected interface. It is applied to monitoring, logging, and health checks. Examples include adapting Redis metrics for Prometheus, normalizing logs with fluentd, and adding rich MySQL health checks without modifying the MySQL container.

The passage then contrasts single-node patterns with multi-node distributed patterns and introduces microservices as systems composed of separate services communicating through APIs. Microservices can improve reliability, agility, team independence, and scaling, but they also make debugging and architecture more difficult.

It describes replicated load-balanced services, especially stateless services, where identical replicas serve traffic behind a load balancer for availability and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes indicate when replicas can serve requests. Session-tracked services route a user’s requests to the same replica when needed. Additional layers such as caching with Varnish and SSL termination with nginx can be added as replicated tiers. The passage also discusses rate limiting and denial-of-service defense at the caching layer.

Finally, the passage introduces sharded services, where each shard serves only part of the request space and a root or load-balancing node routes requests to the appropriate shard. Sharded services are generally used for stateful systems when the stored state is too large for one machine.

The report and appendix cover events up to the January 17, 1893 revolution, continuing from a later report tied to the February 14, 1893 treaty with Hawaii’s Provisional Government. The passage lists chronological papers, an index, bibliography, congressional documents, and early U.S.-Hawaiian diplomatic records. It includes the 1826 Treaty of Friendship, Commerce, and Navigation between the United States and the Sandwich Islands, related agreements signed at Honolulu, and notes on protecting foreigners, seamen, American claims, and maintaining friendly relations while gathering information on U.S. commercial interests.

Rudy Gestede said Middlesbrough must stay positive to end their winless run and avoid relegation. The 19th-placed side face Arsenal, who are sixth and coming off a 3-0 loss to Crystal Palace. Gestede said Middlesbrough must stay focused against Arsenal’s quality.

The passage explains motivations and patterns for organizing containerized applications. Containers create boundaries for resources, ownership, and separation of concerns, which can justify splitting even single-machine applications into multiple containers. Separate containers allow different resource priorities, clearer team ownership, reusable modules, and simpler testing, updating, deployment, rollout, and rollback.

Single-node container groups assume tightly coupled containers that can be coscheduled on one machine and may share filesystems, volumes, network namespaces, process namespaces, and memory. Kubernetes calls this grouping a pod. The sidecar pattern uses an auxiliary container to augment an application container. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service with an nginx sidecar, synchronizing configuration from an API into a shared filesystem, providing a reusable process-inspection interface, and building a simple Git-based PaaS using a Node.js server plus a Git synchronization sidecar. Effective sidecars should be modular and reusable through clear parameterization, stable APIs, and documentation using Dockerfile directives such as EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL.

The ambassador pattern uses a companion container to broker communication between an application and external systems. It separates application logic from connection, routing, or discovery logic. Examples include routing client requests to sharded Redis or memcached backends using twemproxy, brokering service discovery for different environments such as public cloud or private cloud MySQL deployments, and splitting traffic for experiments using nginx, such as sending 90% of traffic to production and 10% to an experimental service.

The adapter pattern uses a companion container to modify an application’s interface so it conforms to expected operational standards. This is useful because real systems combine custom, vendor, open source, and binary components with different conventions. Adapters can normalize monitoring, logging, and health-check interfaces. Examples include adding a Prometheus Redis exporter, using fluentd plugins to normalize Redis slow logs or Apache Storm logs, and adding a MySQL health-check adapter that runs diagnostic queries without modifying the MySQL image.

The passage then contrasts single-node patterns with multi-node distributed patterns. Microservices divide systems into independently deployed components communicating through defined APIs, improving reliability, agility, team independence, and scaling flexibility, but making debugging and system design harder. Distributed patterns help make such systems easier to design and debug.

Replicated load-balanced services use identical service replicas behind a load balancer for redundancy and scale. Stateless services should use multiple replicas for high availability and can scale horizontally by adding replicas. Readiness probes tell load balancers when containers are ready to receive traffic. Session-tracked services route a user’s requests to the same replica, often through IP hashing or application-level tracking such as cookies. Application-layer replicated services may add caching layers such as Varnish, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination using nginx.

Sharded services differ from replicated services because each shard handles only a subset of requests, with a routing layer directing requests to the correct shard. Sharding is generally used for stateful services when state exceeds one machine’s capacity. A sharded cache can improve memory utilization by ensuring different cache replicas store different data, but failures or rollouts can reduce cache hit rate and performance. Replicated shards can improve resilience and allow scaling of hot shards. Sharding functions map requests to shards, commonly using hashing and modulo operations; effective functions require deterministic and uniform hashes and carefully chosen keys. Consistent hashing reduces remapping when shard counts change.

The lecture concludes the unit on the predecessor problem by presenting lower bounds that nearly match known upper bounds from van Emde Boas structures and fusion tries. The main lower bound discussed is for static predecessor data structures with polynomial space, showing an expected query lower bound of roughly the minimum of a van Emde Boas-type term and a fusion-trie-type term, up to logarithmic factors.

The lecture first surveys prior work: Ajtai gave an early lower bound; Miltersen introduced a communication complexity perspective; later work developed round elimination; Beame and Fich, and independently Xiao, proved near-optimal pure bounds in terms of word size or problem size; Sen gave a cleaner round elimination proof; and Pătraşcu and Thorup later established tight trade-offs among universe size, word size, and space.

The proof focuses on the easier colored predecessor problem, where each stored element is red or blue and a query returns only the color of the predecessor. A lower bound for this problem also applies to ordinary predecessor. The model used is the cell-probe model, where only memory word reads are counted.

The data structure problem is reformulated as a communication problem between Alice, who knows the query, and Bob, who knows the stored data. Alice sends an address using about log space bits, and Bob returns a word of w bits; each memory probe corresponds to a communication round. The round elimination lemma says that for a derived problem where one party does not know which of many inputs matters, the first message can be removed at the cost of a small increase in error.

The proof alternately eliminates Alice-to-Bob and Bob-to-Alice messages. Eliminating Alice-to-Bob messages corresponds to a van Emde Boas-like reduction in the word size; eliminating Bob-to-Alice messages corresponds to a fusion-tree-like reduction in the number of stored elements. Repeating these reductions until either the universe size or number of elements becomes too small yields a contradiction if too few probes were used, since a zero-message protocol cannot answer the colored predecessor problem with probability better than one half.

This gives a lower bound of the form  
\(\Omega(\min(\log_a w,\log_b n))\),  
where \(a\) is the number of bits Alice sends and \(b\) is the number of bits Bob sends. For polynomial-space data structures, this implies a lower bound close to the known upper bounds, differing by a log-log factor.

This study examined SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccine responses in 40 participants: 13 healthy controls and 27 rheumatoid arthritis patients treated with methotrexate, abatacept, or rituximab. Rituximab-treated patients had nearly absent anti-spike antibody responses. Abatacept-treated patients had significantly reduced spike-specific and neutralizing antibodies, impaired IgG class switching, altered memory B cell differentiation, and reduced production of IL-2, IFNγ, and IL-21 by spike-specific CD4+ T cells. Methotrexate-treated patients showed reduced spike-specific CD4+ T cell responses but no significant reduction in antibody levels in this cohort. The findings suggest abatacept limits vaccine efficacy by disrupting T cell help needed for effective B cell activation and class-switched neutralizing antibody production, supporting temporary cessation of abatacept around vaccination when clinically manageable.

Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund Danantara plans to launch at least eight waste-to-power projects by the end of October, starting in Jakarta before expanding across Java and Bali to cover 33 municipalities. Each plant is expected to process 1,000 tonnes of waste daily and generate about 15 MW of electricity, with costs of 2–3 trillion rupiah per facility. Danantara will finance and oversee the projects, PLN will buy the electricity, and local governments will provide land. The initiative supports Indonesia’s 2025–2034 electricity plan and aims to reduce waste, emissions, and landfill reliance while expanding renewable energy.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Ampere GA10x GPU architecture, focusing on GA102 and GA104. GA10x builds on Turing and is designed for graphics, ray tracing, AI, compute, and professional workloads. Compared with Turing, Ampere is up to 1.7x faster in raster graphics, up to 2x faster in ray tracing, and up to 1.9x more power efficient at the same performance level.

GA102 powers the GeForce RTX 3090, RTX 3080, RTX A6000, and NVIDIA A40, while GA104 powers the RTX 3070. GA102 is fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm 8N NVIDIA custom process, includes 28.3 billion transistors, and contains up to 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores. GA10x doubles FP32 processing throughput per SM compared with Turing, improves RT Core throughput, and adds Tensor Core support for sparsity and new data types, including TF32.

The GeForce RTX 3090 targets 8K HDR gaming with 10,496 CUDA Cores and 24GB of GDDR6X memory. The RTX 3080 delivers up to twice the performance of the RTX 2080, while the RTX 3070 rivals the RTX 2080 Ti. GA10x also adds HDMI 2.1 and AV1 decode support.

For professional and data center use, the RTX A6000 and A40 include 48GB of GDDR6 memory, with NVLink support for 96GB combined memory across two GPUs. GA102 also supports third-generation NVLink and PCIe Gen 4. Architectural updates include larger L1/shared memory, increased shared memory bandwidth, optimized ROP placement within GPCs, and concurrent RT, graphics, and compute processing.

MTN and four banks are seeking to raise a combined GH¢4.67 billion on the Ghana Stock Exchange within six months, marking a major test for the market. MTN plans to raise GH¢3.48 billion through an IPO, while Access Bank, Agricultural Development Bank, Republic Bank and Societe Generale seek GH¢1.19 billion through rights issues to meet the Bank of Ghana’s GH¢400 million capital requirement by December 2018.

Former GSE Council Chairman Dr Sam Mensah said failure to meet the targets would show the offers exceed the market’s capacity. He warned that the timing is risky, as MTN’s IPO could absorb much available liquidity, and advised banks to have alternative recapitalisation plans.

Pension assets exceeding GH¢21 billion may support the transactions, but Axis Pensions CEO Afriyie Oware said strong foreign participation would be needed. Analysts said the market could handle the offers, though future profit repatriation by foreign investors could pressure the cedi. Retail investor participation is expected to depend on the value and pricing of the offers.

The Supreme Court will consider whether the Constitution’s ex post facto clause applies to restitution under the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act. Holsey Ellingburg argues restitution is criminal because it is imposed during sentencing, governed by criminal procedures, enforced through incarceration, and described as punitive. The government agrees MVRA restitution is criminal, while a court-appointed amicus defends the sentence. The passage suggests the court is unlikely to uphold an enhanced restitution obligation the government declines to defend.
Delta Air Lines intends to acquire up to an additional 32% of Grupo Aeroméxico at MXP$43.59 per share, pending regulatory approvals in Mexico and the United States.

This study translated and psychometrically evaluated an Arabic version of the Orthognathic Quality of Life Questionnaire (OQLQ) for Saudi Arabian adults with malocclusions and dentofacial deformities undergoing orthognathic treatment. The OQLQ was translated, back-translated, reviewed by an expert committee, and pilot tested. Seventy-four patients completed the questionnaire before or after surgery, 12 completed it both before and after surgery, and 15 separate patients completed it twice for test-retest assessment.

The Arabic OQLQ showed excellent internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.92). Test-retest reliability was excellent overall and for most domains, with “awareness of dentofacial deformity” showing good reliability. Construct validity was supported by associations between OQLQ scores, perceived postoperative appearance, and satisfaction with surgery. Responsiveness was supported by lower overall OQLQ scores after surgery, indicating better quality of life; paired data also showed significant improvement in facial esthetics.

The authors conclude that the Arabic OQLQ is conceptually similar to the English version, comprehensible, reliable, valid, and responsive for assessing quality of life in Arabic-speaking orthognathic patients. Limitations included small test-retest and paired cohorts, lack of comparison with other validated instruments, and recruitment from one private practice in Saudi Arabia.
The appeal was docketed and dismissed by motion and consent, without costs.

Tradeshift raised $250 million in Series E funding led by Goldman Sachs and PSP Investments, bringing total funding above $400 million and valuation past $1.1 billion. Participants included HSBC, H14, GP Bullhound and Gray Swan. Co-founder Mikkel Hippe Brun will join the board.

Stephen Pearse discusses startup funding, pitching, and execution. He says startups need an exit path through IPO or acquisition, and investors seek high returns despite high failure rates. Effective pitches should be simple, compelling, tailored to the audience, and built around a strong hook, customer pain points, market opportunity, business model, competition, team, financials, timeline, and a clear funding offer. He emphasizes practicing presentations, avoiding technical jargon, managing questions, raising money before it is urgently needed, approaching investors in parallel, and using introductions to stand out. Pearse also stresses cash-flow management, flexibility to pivot, speed over patents, a clear mission, strong team chemistry, focus, leadership, confidence, passion, and investor networks.

The speaker says the team is now more comfortable in the Stanley Cup Finals, has improved by playing its own game, and remains confident on the road. They emphasize the team’s depth, strong goaltending, ownership support, and successful additions during the season. The speaker praises an injured teammate’s hard work and playoff performance, says the next game in Anaheim will be intense, and stresses focusing only on winning the next game.

This systematic review examined evidence on how student personality traits influence satisfaction and success in online learning in higher education, with relevance to occupational therapy education. Searches of multiple databases identified 23 peer-reviewed studies from 2000 to June 2024, all level IV evidence; none focused specifically on occupational therapy. Studies used Big Five or Myers-Briggs-type personality assessments and measured outcomes such as GPA, grades, satisfaction, engagement, and assignment preferences.

Findings showed conscientiousness was consistently associated with higher grades, satisfaction, engagement, and success across online or blended formats. Agreeableness and openness were often positively related to satisfaction, engagement, GPA, or willingness to adopt online education. Neuroticism was generally negatively associated with satisfaction, engagement, and success, though one study found higher neuroticism linked to better online course performance. Extraversion showed mixed results: extraverts often preferred face-to-face or interactive online activities, while some studies found no effect on GPA or satisfaction.

The review found low strength of evidence due to study design limitations and varied measures, especially satisfaction surveys. It highlights a need for stronger research, particularly in occupational therapy education, and suggests educators consider personality-informed course design, self-regulated learning support, and Universal Design for Learning to improve online learning outcomes.

Leeds hosted the UK’s first Reclaim the Night march in November 1977, amid fear caused by Peter Sutcliffe’s murders and advice that women should not walk alone after dark. Organised by the Leeds Revolutionary Feminist Group, the marches protested harassment, violence and curfews on women, with events held in 12 towns and cities. The movement continued for over a decade, faded in the early 1990s, and was revived in 2004. Forty years later, Leeds theatre company RashDash created The Darkest Corners, a performance in a Holbeck car park inspired by the marches, women’s experiences of feeling unsafe at night, and global female activists.

Southwestern College adjuncts held a poorly attended rally seeking better wages and protections equal to full-time instructors. Adjuncts teach nearly 75 percent of classes but lack the same benefits, job security, paid office hours and disability leave. Speakers described long commutes between multiple colleges, financial strain and concerns that stress and travel reduce education quality. Some said part-time status leaves them vulnerable to losing work and without adequate medical coverage. College President Dr. Kindred Murillo and Trustee Roberto Alcantar spoke in support, praising adjuncts’ value and sacrifices. Organizers urged students and faculty to help advocate for adjuncts.

Pika, founded in 2023 by Demi Guo and Chenlin Meng, has raised about $135 million at a $470 million valuation and has 16.4 million users. Its TikTok-like AI video app targets Gen Z and Gen Alpha with short, playful videos generated from selfies and simple prompts through its Predictive Video feature. The newsletter also notes rising San Francisco rents tied to AI startups, TSMC’s record profit growth driven by AI chip demand, Spotify’s partnerships with major music companies to develop responsible AI products, and low U.S. public trust in AI mental health tools.

Mark Cuban said TrumpRx.gov, a planned federal direct-to-consumer prescription drug discount platform, could be impactful if it forces pharmacy benefit managers to change. The site, expected in early 2026, will begin with Pfizer drugs at average savings of 50%, with other drugmakers expected to join. Cuban gave the platform a “B,” citing strong personnel but noting PBM stocks rose after the announcement, suggesting limited market concern. He said PBMs still benefit from the current system, and pricing impact will be difficult without fundamental changes. KFF’s Drew Altman said such platforms may mainly help uninsured people because most Americans buy drugs through insurance.

NVIDIA Turing GPUs add hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink, enabling VR headsets to receive power, display, and data through one USB-C connector and reducing cable complexity. Turing also replaces prior SLI MIO/PCIe transfers with NVLink on TU102 and TU104 GPUs, supporting two-way SLI with higher bandwidth but not 3-way or 4-way SLI.

Turing introduces real-time ray tracing using RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs combined with NVIDIA RTX software. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, offloading shader multiprocessors. NVIDIA describes hybrid rendering as the preferred approach for games, combining rasterization with ray tracing for effects such as reflections, refractions, shadows, and ambient occlusion. Denoising reduces the number of rays required per pixel. Turing ray tracing is stated to be about 10 times faster than Pascal’s software ray tracing.

NVIDIA NGX is a Turing-only AI graphics stack using Tensor Cores and pretrained DNN models for features such as DLSS, DLSS 2X, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS renders with fewer input samples and infers higher-quality output, while DLSS 2X targets image quality close to 64x supersampling.

Turing adds new graphics pipeline capabilities including Mesh Shading, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering. Mesh Shading introduces task and mesh shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and improve rendering of many complex objects. VRS lets developers vary shading rate in 16x16 screen regions for content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. TSS decouples visibility sampling from shading by storing shading results in texture space for reuse. MVR renders up to four hardware views per pass and expands Pascal’s simultaneous multi-projection functionality.

For VR, Turing combines VirtualLink, MVR, VRS-based foveated rendering, and RT Core acceleration for VRWorks Audio. The passage also describes Turing support for DX12 Tier 3 bindless Constant Buffer Views and Unordered Access Views, and Tier 2 resource heaps.

The TU104 GPU includes up to 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 13.6 billion transistors, and one x8 second-generation NVLink link. It is used in products including GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. Tesla T4 uses a TU104 configuration with 40 SMs, 2560 CUDA cores, 320 Tensor Cores, a 256-bit memory interface, and 320 GB/s bandwidth. TU106, used in GeForce RTX 2070, includes 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, 10.8 billion transistors, and no NVLink or SLI support.

The passage defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering, weighting Tensor, CUDA, RT Core, and INT32 operations according to estimated frame-time usage. It also explains ray tracing basics, BVH acceleration, denoising, and examples of ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections in games and demos. NVIDIA states that hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH algorithms, and RT Cores together enable real-time ray tracing on Turing.

The article examines Colombian higher education students’ perceptions and preferences regarding online learning (OL) and emergency remote education (ERE) during the COVID-19 pandemic. OL is described as a planned, technology-mediated modality with flexible time, space, and learning styles, while ERE is presented as a temporary response to crisis conditions, often involving rapid adaptation of in-person courses to remote formats.

The study used a case study approach at a medium-sized private university in Colombia’s Caribbean region. Eighty-eight undergraduate students completed an online survey comparing OL and ERE across 14 dimensions, including content quality, interaction, assessment, feedback, time requirements, resources, platforms, and technical support. The researchers used descriptive statistics, the add-on preferential groups model, permutation tests, and content analysis of open-ended responses.

Results showed that students generally had positive perceptions of both modalities, but OL was rated higher in most assessed dimensions. Statistically significant differences favored OL in areas such as content quality, active and collaborative activities, respect for diverse learning styles, time for asynchronous and synchronous activities, resource availability, assessment strategies, educational platforms, and technical support. Students especially preferred OL for independent and asynchronous activities, assessment strategies, and content quality. Interaction among students was the only dimension where preferences between OL and ERE were nearly equal.

Open-ended responses indicated that students valued ERE for allowing academic continuity during the pandemic, offering flexibility, supporting instructor contact, enabling peer interaction, and promoting the use of ICT tools. Reported weaknesses of ERE included lack of organization, excessive content, limited instructor preparation, and insufficiently dynamic technological resources. Students valued OL for its flexibility, structure, planning, learning effectiveness, interaction, and use of ICT tools. Suggested improvements for OL included stronger instructor-student interaction, more dynamic activities, reduced workload, better assessment logistics, and more synchronous spaces.

The article concludes that both OL and ERE were positively perceived, but students preferred OL overall because of its stronger planning, structure, and support for learning. It emphasizes the need for continued instructor training in pedagogy, digital tools, course design, interaction, and assessment, as well as the importance of designing learning environments that promote meaningful interaction, manageable workloads, and effective assessment in post-COVID-19 higher education.

The Russell 2000 Index tracks about 2,000 U.S. small-cap stocks and is a market-weighted subset of the Russell 3000. It is rebalanced annually, typically on the fourth Friday of June, to keep the index aligned with its small-cap methodology by adding or removing companies and adjusting constituent weights. This process can create buying and selling imbalances.

The passage describes a Russell 2000 rebalancing trading strategy based on reported abnormal outperformance near the end of June. The strategy buys the Russell 2000 at the close of the first trading day after June 23 and sells at the close of the first trading day of July. A backtest using ^RUT data from 1988 found an average gain of 1.34% over an average six trading days, compared with 0.85% for the S&P 500 over the same period. A hedged version, long Russell 2000 and short S&P 500, averaged 0.23% and performed weakly in recent years.

Motley Fool Money reviews the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card, highlighting unlimited 2% cash rewards, a $200 bonus after $500 in purchases in the first 3 months, 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, no annual fee, Visa Signature Concierge, and up to $600 cell phone protection. Approval is most likely for applicants with good credit, typically 670 or higher. The passage also lists offers for Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards and Citi Double Cash cards, and includes disclosures that Motley Fool Money receives partner compensation, which may affect product placement but not ratings.

Digital leaders use transparent, data-driven objectives aligned with strategy to coordinate teams around shared goals and connect individual work to company outcomes. Effective goal-setting combines top-down direction with bottom-up buy-in, while excessive reliance on quantitative analysis can slow decisions and weaken intuition. Digital laggards often fail to connect goals clearly to strategy, causing misalignment and poorly understood priorities.

A strong data culture supports vertical alignment through metrics tied to company goals and horizontal alignment through common data models and transparent access. Digital leaders emphasize learning, transparency, measurement, and aligned values, while laggards often struggle with entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient leadership focus. Cultural transformation requires compelling reasons understood across the organization.

Organizations commonly fall into four patterns: data novices, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant. Each has different strengths and gaps, and can target actions to build a stronger data culture.

The President returns without approval a bill appropriating $1,378,450 for more than forty harbor and river improvements. He argues that the Constitution does not grant Congress power to fund or construct internal improvements within states, except for limited navigation safeguards such as lighthouses, beacons, buoys, and piers connected to foreign commerce or naval protection. He says many projects in the bill are local, not tied to foreign commerce, and would create an unchecked federal system of internal improvements. He warns this would consolidate federal power, undermine state authority, encourage sectional competition for public funds, produce wasteful spending, and unfairly burden states opposed to such expenditures. He also objects that the appropriations are unwise during a foreign war, when loans or Treasury notes may be needed, and says the bill would lead to growing demands, debt, or taxation.

Coach DeBoer said his team made mistakes, started tentatively, and did not deserve to win, though it improved in spurts. He expects the group to self-analyze and respond as it did after early deficits in previous rounds. He emphasized the need for traffic, bodies, and shots against strong goaltending, while avoiding frustration. DeBoer said the team would maintain its routine rather than change its approach, noted excitement in New Jersey around the Stanley Cup Final, and highlighted the organization’s experience from management, coaches, and players.

The speaker says the players were ready and gave their best effort, but Boston played strongly, had excellent goaltending, protected rebounds well, scored tough goals, and deserved to win. He refuses to blame injuries and says both teams competed hard, but Boston was better in the deciding game. He also discusses preparing for a seventh Stanley Cup Final game, managing nerves, focusing on the team’s process, confidence in a hard effort, and feeling excited and privileged to coach in the NHL and have a chance to play for the Cup.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated May 1, 2018, reporting that it issued a press release and related data sheet on its financial results for the second fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2018. The filing includes Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2 and was signed by CFO Luca Maestri.

This statistical analysis plan describes analyses for Zealand Pharma protocol ZP4207-17086, a phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled parallel-arm trial evaluating efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of a single 0.6 mg dose of dasiglucagon in children with type 1 diabetes and hypoglycemia. The primary objective is to show superiority of dasiglucagon versus placebo; secondary objectives include comparison with GlucaGen, safety assessment, and PK profiling.

The study includes screening, treatment with single dosing on Day 0/1, and follow-up at Day 28. Planned sample size is 20 patients on dasiglucagon, 10 on placebo, and 10 on GlucaGen. The primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery, defined as a ≥20 mg/dL increase from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose. Primary analysis will use the full analysis set, with supportive per-protocol analyses; safety analyses will use all randomized patients who received trial product.

Analyses will be performed using SAS and Phoenix WinNonlin. Statistical tests are generally two-sided at the 0.05 significance level.
