Continuous variables will be summarized descriptively, categorical variables by counts and percentages, and PK parameters with additional geometric summaries where applicable. Missing data will not be imputed.

Primary efficacy will be analyzed with Kaplan-Meier methods and stratified log-rank testing by age group and injection site, with sensitivity and supportive analyses including Wilcoxon tests, Cox proportional hazards models, and linear interpolation of recovery times. Secondary efficacy endpoints include glucose recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes and plasma glucose changes from baseline at those time points, analyzed using stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests or ANOVA as appropriate.

Safety analyses include exposure, insulin use, hypoglycemia induction, rescue glucose infusion, local tolerability, adverse events, laboratory results, vital signs, ECGs, physical examination listings, and immunogenicity. Adverse events will be coded with MedDRA and summarized mainly as treatment-emergent events by treatment group, severity, causality, seriousness, and special categories. Concomitant medications will be coded using WHODrug.

The plan also defines analysis populations, treatment notation, baseline handling, protocol deviations, demographic and baseline summaries, PK/PD sampling and presentation, quality control requirements for SAS programming, and planned tables, listings, and figures. Changes from the protocol include rewording the primary efficacy analysis and adding sensitivity and supportive analyses.

Reports say Queen Elizabeth II is considering stepping aside when she turns 95 to allow Prince Charles to reign, with sources saying she wants a seamless transition. Clarence House has not commented on “Plan Regency,” which would use the Regency Act to give Charles full power while the Queen is still alive. The Queen, who ascended the throne in 1952 and is Britain’s longest-reigning monarch, remains popular. If she abdicated, Charles would become King; if he abdicated, the throne would pass to Prince William, followed by Prince George.

The passage describes NVIDIA GA10x Ampere GPUs, emphasizing GDDR6X memory, RTX IO, data center GPUs, display/video features, and professional GPU capabilities. Developed with Micron, GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling to move two bits per clock edge, reaching up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth on GA10x GPUs. It also introduces MTA encoding, new training and equalization schemes, and Error Detection and Replay to detect and retry memory transmission errors during overclocking.

NVIDIA RTX IO is presented as a solution to storage and decompression bottlenecks in modern games and creative workloads. Used with Microsoft DirectStorage, it enables GPU-based asset loading and lossless decompression, reducing CPU workload, improving I/O performance, supporting faster game loading, reducing stutter, and enabling large open-world games and professional datasets.

The passage outlines the NVIDIA A40 data center GPU, based on GA10x Ampere architecture, with higher FP32, ray-tracing, AI, and PCIe Gen4 performance than prior Turing-based GPUs. It supports 48GB memory, up to 96GB with NVLink, vGPU software, Quadro Sync, and NVIDIA EGX Platform compatibility.

Ampere display support includes DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, DSC 1.2a, 4K at 120Hz, and 8K at 60Hz. GA10x GPUs include fifth-generation NVDEC with hardware decode for codecs including AV1, and seventh-generation NVENC for hardware video encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

The passage also summarizes Ampere architecture improvements, including up to 2x gains in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI, second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores with sparsity, and support for DLSS and 8K HDR rendering. It describes GeForce RTX 3090, RTX 3070, NVIDIA RTX A6000, and related performance claims, memory configurations, and professional rendering, HPC, and deep learning use cases. The document ends with NVIDIA legal notices, warranty disclaimers, usage limitations, and trademark information.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K dated April 12, 2021, reporting that it entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Nuance Communications for $56.00 per share in an all-cash transaction valued at $19.7 billion, including Nuance’s net debt. Microsoft issued a press release and planned investor presentations about the transaction, included as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. The report was signed by Assistant Secretary Keith R. Dolliver.

The Office of Management and Budget has identified 4,132 to 4,232 federal workers for layoffs during the government shutdown. A filing cited cuts at Commerce, Health and Human Services, Housing and Urban Development, Homeland Security, and Treasury. The layoffs follow an OMB memo telling agencies to consider terminations for programs not aligned with the president’s priorities. Federal employee unions have sued, arguing the shutdown is being improperly used to justify layoffs. Some agencies confirmed reductions, while many federal workers remain furloughed or working without pay and are worried about job security and finances.

Punith Kumar, 19, from Choolai, secured first place in India and third internationally in the ACCA Chartered Accountant final P2 exam. He completed much of the course in two years and three months while interning at IRIS Techsolve. He credits his mentor, coaching, and rigorous study schedule, and plans to finish the course by September.

The passage discusses damages for wrongful arrest or detention of vessels, emphasizing loss of use measured by probable earnings or catch. It cites international arbitration examples, including the Hope On, Col. Lloyd Aspinwall, and Bering Sea claims, where awards included estimated lost catches. It argues the Bering Sea Commission consistently applied this rule. The passage also states that a government agent may not forcibly board a friendly nation’s ship and compel its crew into public service, citing Hall’s view that aliens may not be enrolled without consent.

The passage argues that SPY shows short-term mean reversion: it tends to rise after a red day and fall after a green day, despite momentum working over longer timeframes. It explains mean reversion as prices returning toward long-run averages after fluctuations. A backtested strategy using SPY, adjusted for dividends and splits, buys after a red day and sells after a green day. The passage states this strategy produced strong returns, spent less time in the market, achieved better risk-adjusted results, and had significantly lower drawdown than the comparison strategies mentioned.

Ofcom has proposed automatic compensation for landline and broadband customers when services are not repaired quickly, new services are not activated on the promised day, or engineers miss appointments. Compensation would be paid as cash or bill credit, set by Ofcom, and apply only to fixed broadband and landline services. Ofcom estimates up to 2.6 million more customers could receive up to £185m annually. The passage supports the proposal, citing broadband as an essential service and describing a customer’s prolonged unresolved outage. A consultation is open until 5 June, with a decision expected around year-end.

Forwarded Enron email contains the January 21, 1999 Option Investor Newsletter. The newsletter reports broad market weakness: the Dow fell 71.83 to 9264.08, Nasdaq fell 70.77 to 2344.72, and S&P 500 fell 21.46 to 1235.16. It attributes selling pressure to Internet stock declines, profit-taking, global currency concerns involving Brazil and rumors about China or Hong Kong, and cautious comments from Alan Greenspan. The newsletter warns against holding positions over earnings, citing post-earnings sell-offs despite positive results.

Market posture shifted to neutral for technology and bearish for insurance, with sentiment indicators showing bearish near-term overtones and advice to protect long positions. It highlights Internet sector weakness but says AOL remained comparatively favored ahead of earnings.

The newsletter reviews call and put option plays, including updates on PRIA, NOKA, DELL, CSCO, AOL, WCOM, AT&T, MSFT, TLAB, MYG, SUNW, LXK, XIRC, COF, and ETH, and put plays such as AVT, BAC, BDX, CPB, DD, EK, ERTS, HSY, LLY, MCHP, MRK, PKN, RMBS, and WLA. Dropped call picks include QCOM, DIS, YHOO, CHKPF, LU, and ATI.

New call plays are Vodafone, following its AirTouch merger agreement, and Qwest Communications, based on telecom sector strength and recent business relationships. New combo plays include Citrix, Read-Rite, Level 3 Communications, and Sepracor. The combo section says Wednesday’s spreads were mostly available near recommended prices and Thursday’s portfolio positions generally withstood the sell-off.

Sonora High School’s 2017 Wildcats Athletic Hall of Fame class includes 12 former athletes and coaches spanning graduates from 1950 to 2008. Inductees are Howard “Socky” Keefe, Dennis Jackson, Don Moore, Cam Fray, Jon Wagner, Mark McCollough, Becky Fray Aguilar, Jodi Gardella Richey, Lloyd Gaspar, Jessica Peterson McCornack, Gary Smith and Lexi Kopf Scoles. Their achievements include league, section and state-level honors across football, basketball, baseball, wrestling, volleyball, softball, tennis, soccer, golf, water polo and coaching. The Hall of Fame banquet will be held Nov. 4 at the Sonora Elks Lodge, with a no-host bar at 5 p.m., dinner at 6 p.m. and awards at 7 p.m.

The passage argues that book banning and censorship are expanding from K–12 schools into higher education. It cites PEN America’s report of 22,810 book-banning instances in U.S. public schools from 2021 to 2025 and describes growing fear among librarians. It highlights cases involving Franciscan University, New College of Florida, military academies, West Point, Princeton, Texas A&M, syllabus-publication proposals, and the Trump administration’s proposed higher education compact. The passage says these efforts target library books, curricula, course assignments, diversity, gender, and political ideas. It concludes that opposition to book banning has broad public support and calls for a united defense of free expression across educational institutions.

The passage describes Carter administration use of MONs for higher-risk, higher-cost, or geographically specific covert operations and later for significant changes to findings, while new covert actions required presidential findings. It explains congressional notification requirements under Hughes-Ryan and the 1980 Intelligence Oversight Act, including reduced briefing requirements and the “Gang of Eight” provision. It then lists source notes for January 1983 U.S.-Soviet documents, including Shultz’s four-part agenda of human rights, arms control, regional issues, and bilateral relations.

A federal judge in Brooklyn ruled that the Freedom of Access to Clinic Entrances Act, which bars harassment of women seeking abortion services, also applies to Falun Gong practitioners. U.S. District Judge Jack Weinstein upheld the law’s religion section as constitutional, rejecting a challenge by the Chinese Anti-Cult World Alliance, which is accused of harassing Falun Gong members. Weinstein said religion is tied to interstate commerce and that “place of religious worship” should be interpreted broadly, not limited to formal buildings. He certified the ruling for appeal before a trial that he said would be difficult and require interpreters.

The Arkansas Supreme Court affirmed a $10,000 judgment for Fannie M. Conarty, administratrix and widow of W. G. Conarty, against the St. Louis & San Francisco Railroad Company under the Federal Employers’ Liability Act and Safety Appliance Act.

The court held that removal to federal court based on diversity of citizenship was barred by the valid nonremoval provision of the federal act. It also held that the amended Employers’ Liability Act permits one action by the personal representative for both pecuniary loss to the widow and next of kin and the deceased’s pain and suffering.

The court found that the defective coal car, though sent for heavy repairs and temporarily moved within the Fort Smith yard, remained in use in interstate commerce. Because the missing drawbar and coupler caused Conarty’s fatal injury, the railroad was liable under the Safety Appliance Act. The court also held that the widow could testify about the deceased’s contributions to her, as that evidence concerned damages rather than the transaction creating liability.

The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe said the official US dollar to bond note exchange rate remains 1:1 and urged the public to use licensed bureaux de change, money transfer agencies and financial institutions. Governor Dr John Mangudya said 45 institutions had been licensed and warned that exchanges with other currencies should not exceed a 10 percent fee spread. He welcomed arrests of illegal money changers under new exchange control regulations and said retailers refusing non-cash payments would face corrective action. The Government introduced the law after inflated black-market rates caused panic, social media claims about bond note devaluation, panic buying and artificial shortages.

The dollar reached three-week highs against a currency basket after New York Fed President William Dudley signaled continued commitment to rate hikes, supporting U.S. Treasury yields. The dollar index rose 0.1 percent to 101.260, while the dollar gained 0.3 percent to 111.43 yen. Markets also watched geopolitical risks after U.S. strikes in Syria and the deployment of a Navy strike group toward the Korean peninsula. U.S. March job growth missed forecasts, but unemployment fell to 4.5 percent. Speculators cut bullish dollar bets to a five-week low. The euro weakened to $1.0580 amid uncertainty over France’s presidential election as polls showed the race tightening.

This study evaluated the prognostic value of PNI, NLR, and PLR in patients with chronic hepatitis C-associated cirrhosis complicated by type 2 diabetes. It included 56 such patients, 85 patients with hepatitis C-associated cirrhosis, and 85 patients with type 2 diabetes from Fu yang Second People's Hospital between January 2018 and December 2021. Patients with both conditions were classified by 6-month prognosis into poor and good prognosis groups. Laboratory measures included albumin, AST, ALT, and blood cell counts, used to calculate NLR, PNI, and PLR from admission data.

The passage describes limits for continuous-wave optical interferometry using squeezed-state inputs. For time-dependent phase estimation with pure squeezed states and no loss, the spectral quantum Cramer-Rao bound gives precision scaling as \(1/[\Delta\Omega\, n(n+2)]\), yielding Heisenberg scaling for large photon flux per frequency mode. Precision improves with squeezing bandwidth and photon occupancy per mode. The bound can be attained using two homodyne detectors and a nonlinear estimator based on filtered, squared homodyne records.

The Rubber Band trading strategy is a contrarian, mean-reversion approach mainly for stocks, seeking overbought or oversold conditions where price may return toward its mean. Traders may use indicators such as Keltner Channels, Bollinger Bands, or momentum oscillators. With Keltner Channels, prices above the upper band may indicate a potential decline, while prices below the lower band may indicate a potential rise; reversal candlestick patterns may be used for confirmation. Profit targets are often set near the middle band or opposite band. A backtested XLP example reported 328 trades, 0.45% average gain per trade, 6.1% CAGR, 20% market exposure, profit factor of 2, and 16% maximum drawdown. The passage states the strategy works mainly on stocks and is harder to apply to assets like gold and commodities.

UK university staff are in their fourth week of strikes over pension changes, with unsuccessful talks prompting UCU to announce 14 further strike days likely during exam periods between April and June if no agreement is reached. The University of Edinburgh was criticised by UCU Scotland for asking law lecturers to provide recordings of past lectures missed due to industrial action.

A National Academy of Sciences and National Academy of Medicine report says heritable human DNA editing should be allowed only to prevent serious, strongly heritable diseases, not to enhance traits such as strength, intelligence or beauty. Germline editing is illegal in the U.S. and has raised ethical concerns, though CRISPR-Cas9 has made gene editing more feasible and widespread. The report says clinical trials should proceed only when no reasonable alternatives exist, target genes linked to serious disease, assess risks and benefits, undergo public scrutiny, and include long-term follow-up across generations. The panel urged continued public debate, international oversight and regulation, and alignment with societal values.

Singapore police arrested eight women and 15 men during a week-long joint enforcement operation from May 21 to 27. About 700 people at over 70 units were checked. Arrests involved alleged online sexual services, illegal gambling and drink-driving. Cash and handphones were seized.

This study used ADNI data to evaluate whether plasma biomarkers combined with other non-invasive measures can predict cognitive decline and progression to MCI or dementia in non-demented individuals. Two cohorts were analyzed: one with plasma NfL and p-tau181, and a subset also including Aβ42/40. Predictors included demographics, APOE4, baseline composite cognitive scores, plasma biomarkers, and MRI-derived measures. A two-stage machine learning framework used ridge regression to derive an MRI score and random forest regression to predict decline in memory, executive function, language, and visuospatial domains.

Adding plasma biomarkers or MRI improved prediction of memory decline, and combining both produced the strongest performance. In Cohort 1, memory decline prediction improved from a correlation of 0.38 in the basic model to 0.45 with plasma biomarkers, 0.46 with MRI, and 0.50 in the combined model. Improvements for other cognitive domains were limited, except for language in the combined model. MRI score, baseline cognitive scores, NfL, and p-tau181 were important predictors, while Aβ42/40 had the lowest importance among plasma biomarkers. Prediction was stronger in MCI participants than cognitively unimpaired participants.

Predicted memory decline was associated with progression to MCI or dementia. In Cohort 2, the combined model achieved the highest C-index for progression prediction: 0.76 in cognitively unimpaired individuals and 0.79 in MCI individuals. Individuals in the highest tertile of predicted memory decline had substantially higher progression risk than those in the lowest tertile. The study concludes that plasma biomarkers, especially when combined with MRI and cognitive measures, can help predict domain-specific cognitive decline and dementia progression, though prediction remains challenging in cognitively unimpaired individuals and in non-memory domains.

Aiden Markram said he is honoured to captain South Africa after Faf du Plessis was ruled out with a finger injury. Markram acknowledged the added pressure and responsibility but said support from senior players and advice from du Plessis would help. The Proteas trail India 1-0 in the six-match series after losing in Durban, and Markram said they need an improved all-round performance in the second ODI.

Google expanded speech recognition to 30 additional languages and locales, bringing total support to 119. The update includes eight Indian languages, plus Swahili and Amharic, and is initially available in Gboard for Android, Voice Search, and the Cloud Speech API. U.S. English users can also dictate emojis by voice. Google plans to add the languages to other products, including Google Translate. The expansion targets emerging markets, especially India, where mobile internet use is large. Google developed the capabilities by collecting speech samples from native speakers and using them to train machine learning models.

Saints begin their 2017/18 Anglo-Welsh Cup campaign away to Exeter Chiefs on November 4, then host Dragons on November 11. They visit Sale Sharks in late January and host Harlequins in early February. Saints are pooled with Saracens, Scarlets and Worcester Warriors.

CoreLogic reported national home prices rose 7.1% from May 2017 to May 2018 and 1.1% from April. Low housing supply, especially entry-level homes, is driving higher prices. In May 2018, 40% of the 100 largest metro markets were overvalued. Utah, Washington, Nevada and Idaho saw double-digit annual gains. CoreLogic forecast a 5.1% national increase by May 2019 amid strong renter demand to buy.

The passage proposes a model-based geostatistical (MBG) approach to design and analyze soil-transmitted helminth impact assessment surveys more efficiently. It uses baseline prevalence data, environmental risk factors, preventive chemotherapy history, and potential sampling locations to predict baseline prevalence, project prevalence at impact using a multi-state Markov model and local thinning, and compare candidate survey designs.

The method was applied to data from Kenya, Sierra Leone, and Zimbabwe. Kenya data were used to estimate transition probabilities because the same schools were surveyed in 2012, 2015, and 2017. Projected impact prevalence was similar to actual impact prevalence in Kenya, but discrepancies were larger in Sierra Leone and Zimbabwe, likely because their endemicity levels differed from Kenya’s.

Simulation results showed that the MBG approach achieved the same accuracy as the classical survey approach with substantially smaller sample sizes. Estimated survey cost reductions averaged 80%, with reductions of 91% in Zimbabwe, 86% in Kenya, and 62% in Sierra Leone. The authors conclude that MBG can provide impact assessments with higher accuracy at lower cost, produce detailed impact prevalence maps, and potentially support STH control and surveillance.

TeraAgent is a distributed simulation engine designed to overcome BioDynaMo’s single-server scaling limits for agent-based simulations. Agent-based models use locally interacting agents that can produce emergent behavior and are applied in domains including biology, medicine, epidemiology, finance, and policy. Existing BioDynaMo simulations are limited by shared-memory OpenMP execution, restricting simulation size, integration with MPI-based tools, and hardware flexibility.

TeraAgent scales simulations across multiple servers by spatially partitioning the simulation space. It handles aura updates for boundary interactions, agent migration between ranks, and load balancing. To reduce communication overhead, it introduces a tailored serialization mechanism that avoids pointer deduplication, deserialization overhead, endian conversions, and schema evolution, while allowing received objects to remain mutable. It also applies delta encoding to reduce repeated data transfers between iterations, exploiting gradual changes in agent attributes.

The engine supports MPI hybrid and MPI-only execution, distributed initialization, global and diffusive load balancing, incremental neighbor search grid updates, and improved modularity. It aims to let users move simulations from laptops to workstations, servers, clouds, and supercomputers with little or no model-code modification.

Evaluation uses benchmark simulations in cell clustering, cell proliferation, epidemiology, and oncology. TeraAgent reproduces BioDynaMo results and, in MPI hybrid mode, performs close to BioDynaMo on one node while enabling distributed execution. It improves ParaView in-situ visualization performance by 39×, simulates 250× more agents than BioDynaMo, and achieves an 8× higher agent update rate per CPU core than Biocellion. Its serialization provides median speedups of 110× for serialization and 37× for deserialization, while delta encoding reduces transferred data by up to 3.5×. TeraAgent demonstrates extreme-scale simulations of 501.51 billion agents on 84,096 CPU cores, an 84× improvement over the reported state of the art.

Alere said certain financial statements from 2012-2015 should not be relied upon due to misstatements, mainly involving revenue recognition in South Korea and one Japan transaction. It expects no impact on total revenue by transaction but noted material weaknesses in controls and may miss its May 15, 2017 quarterly filing deadline.

The passage describes a vehicle vision and driver monitoring system using one or more exterior and interior cameras, vehicle sensors, and an electronic control unit to capture and process image and vehicle data. The system estimates driver attention by determining driving workload, distraction workload, and optionally a maximum driver workload. Inputs may include driver identity, driving behavior, posture, emotions, health biometrics, gaze, drowsiness, environmental conditions, vehicle controls, media use, and passenger activity. Weighted driving and distraction workloads may be subtracted from a maximum workload to express driver attention as a percentage.

The system may use in-cabin cameras, exterior cameras, radar, lidar, GPS, microphones, ADAS data, weather information, and vehicle communication systems. It can detect objects, vehicles, pedestrians, hazardous conditions, and whether the driver is aware of them. If awareness is lacking and risk exceeds a threshold, the system may autonomously brake or steer. The system may also apply to autonomous vehicles where an occupant may need to take control. Calibration values, confidence levels, and machine learning may adjust module inputs and outputs during testing or operation.

Shonda Rhimes’ Shondaland production company has signed a deal to create new shows for Netflix, while “Grey’s Anatomy,” “Scandal” and “How to Get Away With Murder” will remain on ABC. Financial terms and the deal’s length were not disclosed. Rhimes said Netflix offered “limitless possibilities” for her next career phase.

The American Academy of Pediatrics says five tests commonly ordered for children who are short, overweight or showing early puberty signs are not always necessary if the child is otherwise healthy. These include hormone, endocrine, vitamin D, thyroid or insulin tests, and thyroid ultrasounds. The group advises weighing risks and benefits and using evidence-based criteria. Testing may be appropriate for children with specific concerns, such as significantly short stature based on parents’ height, disorders linked to low bone mass, abnormal growth rates, signs of thyroid disease, or certain thyroid gland abnormalities.

Letters posted by Grassroots Leadership describe migrant women’s accounts of detention and family separation after crossing the US-Mexico border. One anonymous Guatemalan woman said she was held for eight days in a chain-link holding area she called “la perrera,” without bathing or brushing her teeth, and slept on the floor under aluminum blankets. She said she did not know her children’s whereabouts for 21 days after they were taken from her. Her lawyer said the woman was captured near Hidalgo, Texas, transferred to Laredo and then to the T. Don Hutto Residential Center, and was released June 26.

Other letters described emotional distress from separation, including mothers writing to their children and asking to be reunited. ICE said it could not address specific claims because names and facility details were redacted or unclear. Grassroots Leadership said the letters were written to publicly seek help for release from detention and reunification with children.

The passage describes a patent application for displaying marker elements in a virtual scene. A terminal renders a virtual scene, obtains marker indication information for a user-marked target virtual item, retrieves graphic data for a marker element, renders the marker, and displays it near the target item for user accounts in the same team. The marker may be shared through a server, which receives a marking request, checks whether the marked item is within a visible distance of teammates’ virtual objects, and sends marker indication information to eligible terminals. The marker can include selectable types, different graphics based on the marking user, distance information, and an icon on a thumbnail map. Markers may be removed after a preset duration by server cancellation information or a local timer. The application also describes corresponding apparatus modules, terminal/server interactions, computer devices, and non-transitory computer-readable storage media for implementing the method.

A Hays County judge ordered Texas State to reinstate history professor Thomas Alter after his firing over alleged incitement during a virtual socialism conference speech. Alter sued, alleging violations of free speech, due process and contract rights. He will be reinstated without pay and not teach while his case is reviewed.

Pairs trading is a market-neutral strategy that buys one asset and sells another historically correlated asset to profit from temporary divergence or convergence in their price spread. It can be applied to stocks, ETFs, futures, currencies, options, and other instruments, and is described as a subset of statistical arbitrage. Pair selection often uses correlation, cointegration, fundamentals, volatility, beta, and risk management.

The passage says pairs trading originated at Morgan Stanley in the 1980s and has been used by proprietary traders and hedge funds. Its main advantage is reduced dependence on overall market direction, with potential uncorrelated returns. Studies cited report average annualized excess returns for top-pairs portfolios of about 11% to 15.92%, though transaction costs and institutional factors matter.

The passage emphasizes several risks and drawbacks: pairs can stop moving together, spreads can reset after sudden moves, positions are not truly market-neutral, leverage is often needed, shorting costs may apply, and four transactions per trade increase slippage and commissions. It also warns that many traders lose large profits quickly due to leverage, doubling down, and black swan events.

Backtests on KO/PEP and GS/MS showed some returns but less than buying and holding the S&P 500. The passage concludes that pairs trading can still work but is less profitable than before, with easier opportunities largely arbitraged away, making diversification and understanding fundamentals important.

Tesla Motors filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2016. As of that date, Tesla had $12.59 billion in total assets, $9.90 billion in total liabilities, and $2.68 billion in stockholders’ equity. Cash and cash equivalents were $3.08 billion, up from $1.20 billion at December 31, 2015. Customer deposits rose to $690.4 million, primarily due to Model 3 deposits.

For the third quarter of 2016, Tesla reported total revenue of $2.30 billion, compared with $936.8 million in the third quarter of 2015, and net income of $21.9 million, compared with a net loss of $229.9 million a year earlier. For the nine months ended September 30, 2016, revenue was $4.72 billion and net loss was $553.6 million. Operating cash flow for the nine-month period was $324.4 million, while investing activities used $821.7 million and financing activities provided $2.37 billion.

Tesla designs, manufactures and sells fully electric vehicles and energy products. It was producing and selling Model S and Model X, had unveiled Model 3, and sold Powerwall and Powerpack energy products. The company produced about 25,180 vehicles in the third quarter of 2016 and planned approximately 50,000 deliveries in the second half of 2016. It targeted overall vehicle production of 500,000 vehicles in 2018.

In May 2016, Tesla completed a public offering of common stock, raising about $1.7 billion net. In July 2016, it entered into a definitive agreement to acquire SolarCity Corporation, subject to stockholder approvals and other closing conditions. Tesla also reported ongoing investments in the Gigafactory, manufacturing capacity, retail and service locations, and charging infrastructure.

Researchers at La Jolla Institute for Immunology found that ALS patients showed stronger T cell responses to C9orf72, a neuron-related protein linked to ALS, than people without the disease. Patients whose immune cells produced more anti-inflammatory IL-10 in response to C9orf72 were predicted to survive longer than those with more inflammatory responses. The findings suggest an autoimmune component may be involved in ALS and could inform future treatments or disease monitoring, but researchers cautioned they do not prove ALS is an autoimmune disease or that self-reactive T cells drive progression. Larger studies and animal models are planned.

Henrik Lundqvist said the late first-period goal was difficult, but his team created chances and believes it can turn the series around. He felt he has played well despite allowing goals, citing deflections and a two-on-one play, but said he must raise his level. He emphasized focusing on the next game, getting a strong start, working hard, making good decisions, creating traffic at the net, and earning a first win against a strong opponent.

Cryptocurrency-related crime is rising in Japan despite an overall decline in reported crime. The theft of 523 million NEM coins worth ¥58 billion from Coincheck highlighted security concerns, which the Financial Services Agency had previously warned the company about. Japan has played a major role in cryptocurrency, recognizing bitcoin as legal tender and registering 16 exchanges, though Coincheck was not among them. Other issues include alleged fraud involving Ripple, ransomware scams, and risks tied to initial coin offerings. The FSA has warned that ICO tokens may rapidly lose value and carry fraud risks, but regulation remains unclear in Japan. Facebook has banned ICO ads, and U.S. regulators have halted an allegedly fraudulent ICO, while Japanese consumers are currently warned to proceed at their own risk.

Investing.com reports that market momentum remains intact but charts show early warnings. The S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July and 7.8% year-to-date, though it slipped 1.6% on the first day of August. Volatility and credit spreads are seeing a seasonal upturn, investors are increasing exposure to tech stocks, and U.S. electricity demand reached a new all-time high. Short-term technicals appear tenuous as breadth rolls over from overbought levels, while medium- and long-term trend indicators remain healthy. The passage also includes promotional investment content, market headlines, and risk disclosures about trading losses, data accuracy, and website use.

The passage criticizes an Ontario Liberal-commissioned report proposing major changes to student assessment, including scrapping Grade 3 and Grade 9 EQAO tests, removing the mandatory high school literacy test, and reducing other provincewide testing. It says Education Minister Indira Naidoo-Harris supports the report but delayed implementation until after further consultation and the provincial election. The author argues the changes would weaken accountability, reduce independent data on student performance, and shift too much assessment responsibility to teachers. The passage notes teachers’ longstanding opposition to EQAO testing, says the EQAO was not consulted, and cites EQAO concerns that eliminating primary-division testing would reduce data for improving elementary schools. It also says the report supports more classroom assessment, accessibility improvements, and discourages using results to rank schools.

Auswide Bank originated from building society mergers in Queensland’s Wide Bay Burnett region, later expanded to Sydney and Melbourne, listed on the Australian Stock Exchange in 1994, and became a bank in 2015. Its mission emphasizes customer focus and the “power of small” in competition with Australia’s major banks. For fiscal year ended June 30, 2020, Auswide reported AUD3.789 billion in assets, AUD3.206 billion in net loans and advances, AUD3.019 billion in deposits and short-term borrowings, AUD70.5 million in net interest revenue, AUD18.5 million in net profit after tax, and AUD13.6 million in dividends.

The case presents representative fiscal 2021 transactions, including a share issue, additional Reserve Bank borrowing, purchases of supplies and office furniture, customer deposits and withdrawals, loan originations and repayments, interest revenue and expense, employee benefits, broker commissions, a loan sale gain, dividends, depreciation, loan impairment expense, and no goodwill impairment. The assignment asks students to record the transactions, prepare a June 30, 2021 balance sheet, and calculate fiscal 2021 net income and cash flow, ignoring taxes. Exhibits provide Auswide’s fiscal 2020 income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement.

Motivate introduced 250 Ford GoBike Plus electric pedal-assist bikes at stations in western San Francisco as part of the Bay Area Ford GoBike bike-share program. Officials and cyclists tested them on steep Page Street, where the electric assist made climbing easier. Motivate CEO Jay Walder said the bikes are intended to help riders handle San Francisco’s hills, attract new users and encourage longer trips. Ford GoBike currently has 287 stations and 3,600 bikes across five Bay Area cities, but the e-bikes are only in San Francisco for now. Walder said the program is coordinated with cities, contrasting it with the recent arrival of electric scooters.

Special education teacher shortages are widespread, especially in high-poverty urban and rural districts, and Washington reports more than 20% of special education teachers working under conditional certificates. The article presents an exploratory case study of the Washington Education Association Teacher Residency Program, a union-led, non-IHE-affiliated alternative certification program piloted in 2023–24 to prepare special education teachers.

The program was created to address special education teacher shortages and improve workforce diversity. Sixteen residents participated across three Washington districts, with many coming from diverse racial, linguistic, paraprofessional, or emergency substitute backgrounds. The 18-month program combined coursework, four nine-week field placements, mentoring, coaching, competency-based assessment, and a curriculum focused on cultural competency, equity, family and community engagement, and learning partnerships. Instruction used a Hyflex model and was aligned with Washington special education teaching standards.

Emerging technologies were incorporated through tools such as Mursion simulations, AI-related professional development, Jamboard, mobile speech-generation devices, and assistive and instructional technology evaluations during placements. Residents received a living wage, health insurance, mentoring, coaching, and placement support, while committing to work in their residency district for three years after licensure.

The study found the program integrated comprehensive evidence-based preparation components, technology, and financial incentives. The article concludes that the WEA Teacher Residency Program offers an innovative model for addressing special education teacher shortages and diversifying the educator workforce, while noting limitations related to scale, sustainability, short study duration, and small sample size.

The speaker emphasizes defensive responsibility, simple play, and avoiding turnovers. Winning the next two games matters more than personal records. Prior experience helps with pressure and media attention, which can be enjoyable but sometimes excessive.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Health Secretary Abid Majeed directed the formation of provincial, district and union council committees led by paediatricians to oversee the upcoming measles campaign. He emphasized communication, social mobilization, staff training, logistics, vaccines and referral systems for adverse events. The province-wide campaign, starting in October, aims to vaccinate 4.3 million children aged nine to 59 months. Officials said it was planned due to rising measles cases across almost all districts.

In *Lykins v. Aluminum Workers International Union*, plaintiff Toy Lykins challenged the unions’ alleged use of mandatory dues for purposes beyond collective bargaining, contract administration, and grievance adjustment, claiming violation of his First Amendment rights. He had refused to rejoin the union but paid required fees under a union security clause in the collective bargaining agreement.

The court denied defendants’ motion for summary judgment. It held that a justiciable controversy existed because defendants had plaintiff’s money and allegedly spent it contrary to his objections. The court also rejected defendants’ argument that plaintiff failed to exhaust statutory remedies, finding he had requested an accounting and had no duty to attend union meetings.

The court found sufficient governmental action because union shop clauses are authorized by the National Labor Relations Act. It held that the NLRA should not be interpreted to authorize unions to spend dissenting employees’ mandatory dues on political or ideological purposes unrelated to collective bargaining. The court declined to decide which specific expenditures would require refund pending factual development. An amended order later struck the jurisdiction discussion concerning the amount-in-controversy requirement, noting jurisdiction existed under 28 U.S.C. § 1337(a).

A Gallup-Walton Family Foundation survey found that more than 1 in 4 U.S. public school teachers lack basic materials or staffing support needed to work effectively, affecting job satisfaction. Teachers most often reported shortages of staff, with about two-thirds lacking teaching assistants, aides, paraprofessionals or behavior specialists, and 62% lacking mental health resources or special educators. Teachers with adequate resources were more likely to be satisfied at work, 77% versus 44%.

The survey, conducted during the 2024-25 school year with teachers from the RAND American Teacher Panel, also found gaps in classroom supplies: 24% lacked enough furniture, 25% lacked laptops or classroom computers and 35% lacked printing supplies. One-third said ordering materials was difficult. Technology shortages were more common in low-income schools, while furniture and staffing shortages appeared across income levels. About half of teachers said professional development was not grounded in student needs, and many valued collaborative planning and observing other teachers, though only one-third had that opportunity.

Alan Oppenheim discusses implementing causal linear shift-invariant systems described by linear constant coefficient difference equations. Such systems can be represented using digital networks built from three operations: delay, multiplication, and addition. Block diagrams use delay elements labeled \(z^{-1}\), multiplier branches, and adders.

He introduces signal flow graphs as an alternative graphical notation, consisting of directed branches connected at nodes, with node variables defined as sums of incoming branch outputs. For linear signal flow graphs, branch outputs are linear functions of branch inputs, often scalar gains or functions of \(z\). A first-order difference equation is shown in both block diagram and signal flow graph form.

The lecture then connects signal flow graphs to matrix representations of digital networks. Node variables can be expressed as linear equations involving branch transmittances, source inputs, and output equations. Separating coefficient branches from delay branches yields time-domain equations equivalent to coupled first-order difference equations.

An example illustrates computability of node orderings. A network is computable if nodes can be ordered so the coefficient matrix has no nonzero entries on or above the main diagonal. Delay-free loops lead to non-computable networks, though their equations may still be solvable or rearranged. The next lectures will cover common structures for recursive and non-recursive digital filters.

The passage reports on the Japan Society of Technology Education’s development of “The New Framework for Technology and Engineering Education for Creating a Next Generation Learning” (NGTE). It explains that STEAM education is gaining attention in Japan, but technology and engineering education needs a clearer role within it, especially because Japan’s curriculum reform process must connect new concepts with prior educational reforms.

Japan’s current junior high school “Technology” curriculum covers material processing, biological cultivation, energy conversion, and information technology, aiming to develop technological understanding, problem-solving abilities, and attitudes toward sustainable society. A survey of 1,656 students in Hyogo Prefecture found that students generally viewed Technology classes positively and engaged in collaborative and problem-solving activities, but had weaker experiences in linking learning to social issues and in exploratory activities such as inquiry, experimentation, and observation. Regression analysis suggested that current learning activities had weak influence on abilities for technological innovation and governance.

In response, JSTE revised its earlier framework and created NGTE. NGTE focuses on technology and engineering literacy for all citizens, defining its goals as developing abilities for technological innovation and governance. It strengthens links to engineering science, adds “Technological Systems” such as AI, IoT, robotics, and Big Data processing, and emphasizes integration of cyber and physical technologies in relation to Society 5.0.

NGTE proposes a Triple-Loop Model of the engineering design process, consisting of Needs Exploration, Seeds Exploration, and Creation loops. It also presents a STEAM learning model centered on engineering design and the creation of technological artefacts through transdisciplinary learning. Evaluation by JSTE members generally supported the framework, though the definition of “engineering” was revised for clarity.

The passage argues that academic societies can contribute to curriculum reform by surveying learners, interpreting findings in relation to social change, developing curriculum proposals, and participating in national curriculum revision. Future tasks include testing NGTE through classroom practice and reforming teacher education and training to support implementation.

The lecture discusses capabilities as a model for privilege separation and sandboxing, contrasting them with Unix-style ambient authority. It begins with the confused deputy problem, where a Fortran compiler with extra privileges to write in `/sysx` could be tricked by a user into overwriting protected files such as statistics or billing files through normal compiler options. The problem arose because the compiler implicitly used all available privileges rather than explicitly choosing which authority to exercise for each operation.

Ambient authority is described as permission derived implicitly from context, such as a process UID or network location behind a firewall. The lecture explains that this can cause software to unintentionally use privileges on behalf of an untrusted caller. Capabilities address this by tying access directly to unforgeable references, such as Unix file descriptors. If a process has a capability, it can access the object subject to restrictions; if it does not, it cannot. File descriptors are unforgeable because user programs can only supply integers that the kernel interprets through the process’s file descriptor table.

The lecture then discusses Capsicum, a FreeBSD capability-based sandboxing system. Capsicum is intended for developers who restructure applications so risky components run with fewer privileges. It is useful for programs such as `tcpdump`, gzip, browsers, and other code that parses attacker-controlled input. Unlike virtual machines, Capsicum allows fine-grained sharing through file descriptors, though it requires application changes.

Capsicum’s `cap_enter` places a process in capability mode, blocking access to global namespaces such as the filesystem, network addresses, and process IDs except through existing capabilities. It introduces mechanisms such as `openat` for directory-relative access and process descriptors for managing child processes through file descriptors. The system restricts operations on file descriptors using capability rights masks. It also uses `libcapsicum`, including `lch_start`, to start sandboxes with explicit arguments, memory state, and file descriptors, avoiding inherited sensitive state.

Examples include modifying `tcpdump` to restrict terminal access and gzip to isolate compression or decompression logic. Capsicum could simplify aspects of OKWS by replacing chroot-style isolation, reducing root requirements, and providing append-only log capabilities, though network connections and service configuration remain awkward. A helper daemon called Casper can provide controlled access to services such as DNS from sandboxed processes.

The lecture concludes by noting that Capsicum’s guarantees depend on correct developer use, accurate rights assignment, proper kernel enforcement, and bug-free handling of system calls. It briefly contrasts Capsicum with Linux mechanisms that filter system calls but are less fine-grained.

Alan Oppenheim presents an example of designing a digital low-pass infinite impulse response filter using impulse invariance and the bilinear transformation. The design begins with analog Butterworth filters, defined by cutoff frequency and filter order, with monotonic frequency response and poles on the Butterworth circle. A digital low-pass specification is set with passband edge 0.2π, stopband edge 0.3π, passband deviation within 1 dB, and stopband attenuation at least 15 dB.

For impulse invariance, the digital specifications are converted to analog specifications using frequency scaling while initially neglecting aliasing. Solving the Butterworth design equations gives a noninteger order, so the order is rounded up to 6. The passband specification is met exactly and the stopband specification is exceeded to compensate for aliasing. The sampling period parameter cancels out and is shown to be irrelevant.

For the bilinear transformation, the critical digital frequencies are pre-warped to analog frequencies. The resulting Butterworth equations again give a noninteger order, so order 6 is chosen. The stopband specification is met exactly and the passband specification is exceeded. Compared with impulse invariance, the bilinear design gives stronger attenuation at higher frequencies due to frequency warping and avoids aliasing.

The lecture concludes that these methods generalize beyond low-pass filters using frequency transformations, and the next lecture will address finite impulse response filter design.

Defensive ends are a highly valued defensive position in football because they help disrupt passing attacks and stop the run. They typically line up on the edge of the defensive line, across from or outside offensive tackles, and are responsible for maintaining gap discipline, pressuring quarterbacks, forcing ball carriers, batting passes, creating sacks, and causing fumbles. Their role is especially important as offenses rely more on passing, since elite pass rushers can pressure quarterbacks without frequent blitzing and allow defenses to use more players in coverage.

The position is called defensive end because players line up on the end of the formation. Common abbreviation: DE. Key skills include strength, quickness, recognition, and consistent technique. Typical body traits include a 6’3”–6’7”, 270–290-pound, lengthy, big, athletic build.

Notable defensive ends mentioned include Reggie White, Bruce Smith, and Dwight Freeney. Elite defensive ends can affect every play by combining size, strength, and athleticism to pressure the passer, disrupt throwing lanes, handle run responsibilities, penetrate the backfield, and absorb double teams.

Utah County hired former federal public defender Kathryn N. Nester to represent Tyler James Robinson, 22, who is accused of fatally shooting Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10 and could face the death penalty if convicted. After two poor opening games, the team won twice at home with contributions from lower lines. They are improving puck movement, speed, and defensive patience, aiming to create more chances without taking risks while drawing confidence from road success.

TLV321x devices include an internal Power-On Reset circuit that holds the output low during startup for up to 32 µs after VPOR of 1.65 V is crossed. Once the supply reaches at least the minimum voltage and the delay ends, the comparator output reflects the differential input state.

The comparator compares VIN to VREF: output is low when VIN is below VREF and high when VIN is above VREF; output logic can be inverted by swapping input pins. Propagation delay occurs between input threshold crossing and output response, and overdrive voltage affects delay, with smaller overdrive causing longer delays. Rise and fall times are measured between 20% and 80% of the output waveform.

Because TLV321x devices have only 1.8 mV internal hysteresis, external hysteresis can be added using positive feedback to reduce chatter when slow or noisy inputs are near the switching threshold. The passage describes inverting and non-inverting hysteresis configurations, their resistor networks, trip thresholds, and total hysteresis equations.

A typical application is low-side current sensing, where an amplifier boosts the shunt-resistor voltage and a comparator changes state when the amplified voltage exceeds an over-current threshold, such as 1.1 V. The passage emphasizes close low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic supply bypassing, stable low-noise supplies, careful grounding, minimizing input-output coupling, and optional series resistance or controlled-impedance routing to reduce ringing and oscillations.

The document also lists application references, support resources, ESD handling cautions, revision and packaging information, and TI disclaimers stating that design resources are provided “as is” and customers are responsible for selecting, designing, validating, and testing their applications.

The passage describes the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) specification, which standardizes communication between SEV-ES or SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors. SEV-ES and SEV-SNP encrypt guest register state during world switches, so Non-Automatic Exits require the guest to selectively share state through the GHCB.

The GHCB is a 4 KB decrypted page whose layout mirrors parts of the SEV-ES VMCB save state area while limiting exposed guest state. Version 2 adds SEV-SNP support, hypervisor feature advertisement through a FEATURES bitmap, CPUID-related enhancements, restricted APIC emulation support, GHCB GPA registration for SEV-SNP guests, and other protocol functions.

The passage outlines revision updates, including expanded guest request sequence numbers, VLEK GUID documentation, APIC ID list retrieval, multi-VMPL support, SEV-TIO support, Secure AVIC support, GHCB unregister support, and EFI protocols for SEV-SNP secrets and CPUID pages.

It also describes GHCB MSR protocol usage, protocol negotiation examples for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests, supported Non-Automatic Exit handling, error reporting through SW_EXITINFO fields, VALID_BITMAP requirements, GHCB usage during VMGEXIT, and specific handling for I/O, MSR, VMMCALL, MMIO, and Page State Change events.

The Zipper offense is a basketball set designed to free shooters, create point-guard penetration, generate strong post-ups, enable quick ball reversal, and attack the weak side. It begins with a dribble-clear entry to the wing while shooters start low and come high off ball-side and weakside down screens. The point guard may drive, pass to a shooter, or feed the screener posting low.

The offense includes reads and counters for defensive reactions such as baseline denial, weakside help, double teams, overplayed passing lanes, switches, mismatches, and show-and-recover coverage. Options include baseline or middle drives, drop passes, kick-outs, back cuts, post feeds, flash actions, back screens, mid screens, and screen-and-roll sequences.

The system emphasizes proper down-screen execution, post skills, weakside action, ball reversal, offensive rebounding, and continuity into motion, single/double, flex, triangle post, side screen, or power passing game actions. Variations include Zipper Curl, Zipper Blocks, Zipper Back, and sideline out-of-bounds entries.

Successful use requires scouting, player movement, attacking weak defenders, timing, footwork, non-verbal communication, and coordinated execution among the ballhandler, screener, and receiver. The passage also stresses individual skill development and preparation to defend the Zipper offense.

Amazon introduced Chime, a unified communications service combining voice, video, chat and online meetings. It enters a crowded market against major technology, telecom and pure-play vendors. Chime supports peer-to-peer and group conferences for up to 100 people, screen sharing, recording, scheduling integrations, cross-platform apps and switching devices without dropping meetings.

The paper studies “transportation” of theorems about LF specifications: lifting properties proved under one regularly structured typing context to contexts with different schematic structures. LF is used to encode rule-based relational specifications, with dependent types representing relations and terms representing derivations; higher-order abstract syntax often produces non-empty, regularly patterned typing contexts.

The work addresses when one LF context can replace another without affecting formula validity. It builds on the subordination relation between types, which helps identify context variables irrelevant to a typing judgement, and extends this idea from individual judgements to properties involving multiple judgements and schematically defined context families.

The problem is formalized in the logic L𝐿𝐹, whose atomic formulas are LF typing judgements and whose quantifiers range over LF terms and contexts governed by context schemas. The paper develops context schema subsumption to characterize when formulas universally quantified over one context schema remain valid under another. It presents a sound proof rule for theorem transportation, discusses its integration into the Adelfa proof assistant, and illustrates its use with examples.

Researchers developed MeTro, a highly elastic surgical glue that can seal wounds within 60 seconds when treated with UV light. Created by scientists from the University of Sydney and the United States, it uses a natural elastic protein and may replace stitches or staples, especially for tissues that expand and contract, such as lungs, arteries and the heart. It has been tested on rodents and pigs, can degrade in line with healing, and is now ready for clinical testing.

A memorandum for President Roosevelt outlined topics for informal discussions with British Colonial Secretary Oliver Stanley during his January 15–18 visit to Washington, primarily concerning the Anglo-American Caribbean Commission. It compared British and U.S. views on dependent territories, including distinctions between trust territories and colonies, independence or self-government, international accountability, standards for administration, regional advisory commissions, and their relation to a general international organization.

Coaches should teach the context of soccer tackling before specific techniques, including safety, legal and illegal contact, Law 12, and referee interpretation. A legal tackle attempts to dispossess an opponent without violating rules on careless, reckless, or excessive-force challenges. Poor tackles can cause fouls, cards, injuries, direct free kicks, or penalty kicks.

Defenders should tackle based on player positions, ball location, field location, and game circumstances. A successful tackle may win the ball, kick it away, or put it out of bounds. Proper defensive play includes marking, staying goal-side, delaying, containing, communicating, maintaining a cushion, and choosing the right time to tackle.

Legal contact is generally fair shoulder-to-shoulder contact within playing distance of the ball, without excessive force, arms, or elbows. Illegal contact includes improper charges, jumps, kicks, pushes, strikes, tackles, trips, and other actions judged careless, reckless, or excessive. Reckless play requires a caution, and excessive force or serious foul play requires a red card.

Referees assess the defender’s proximity, intent to play the ball, force used, tackle angle, contact point, and whether the challenge endangers the opponent. Winning or touching the ball first does not excuse illegal contact. Tackles from behind, late tackles, two-footed lunges, studs-up challenges, high contact, and wild kicking motions are especially risky.

Players should tackle skillfully, keep one foot grounded, avoid unnecessary or dangerous challenges, recover quickly, and practice varied tackling techniques safely. Coaches should also teach what not to do, account for fatigue and skill mismatches, and remind attackers how to protect themselves from poor tackles.

Twelve-year-old Charlotte Olson of Voorhees, New Jersey, collected more than 1,300 books for Cooper University Health System’s Read and Reach Out program, exceeding her original goal of 1,000. She gathered donations through family, neighbors, local businesses, social media, and donation boxes, ultimately receiving over 2,000 books and raising $250 for new books. The hospital’s program, established in 1998, gives books to children to encourage reading and serves over 75,000 children annually statewide. Charlotte is pursuing a community service award through National American Miss Pre-teen New Jersey and hopes to become an emergency room doctor.

Apple Inc.’s 2020 Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended September 26, 2020. Apple, a California corporation established in 1977 and headquartered in Cupertino, designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells related services. Its products include iPhone, Mac, iPad, and Wearables, Home and Accessories; services include advertising, AppleCare, cloud services, digital content, and payment services.

Apple reported 2020 total net sales of $274.5 billion, net income of $57.4 billion, and diluted earnings per share of $3.28. Net sales increased 6% from 2019, mainly due to higher Services and Wearables, Home and Accessories sales. Direct and indirect distribution channels accounted for 34% and 66% of total net sales, respectively. Apple had approximately 147,000 full-time equivalent employees.

The filing states that COVID-19 affected Apple’s business through temporary retail and channel closures, remote work, supply chain disruptions, and uncertainty around future operational and financial impacts. Apple identified risks including competition, supply constraints, outsourcing dependence, legal and regulatory matters, cybersecurity, economic conditions, foreign exchange, tax changes, and reliance on third-party developers and content.

Apple’s common stock trades on Nasdaq under AAPL. In August 2020, Apple completed a four-for-one stock split. During 2020, Apple repurchased $72.5 billion of common stock and paid $14.1 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents.

Bruce Bochy will not return as Texas Rangers manager after a three-year tenure that included the franchise’s first World Series title in 2023, followed by two non-winning, non-playoff seasons. The Rangers and Bochy mutually agreed to end his managerial role after an 81-81 season, and the team offered him an advisory front office position. Bochy went 249-237 with Texas and remains sixth all-time in managerial wins with a 2,252-2,266 career record and four World Series titles. Rangers president Chris Young praised Bochy’s impact. Former Marlins manager Skip Schumaker, currently a Rangers senior adviser, is a potential replacement. Bob Melvin was also fired by the Giants, and Rocco Baldelli was fired by the Twins.

U.S. Treasury yields fell sharply after President Donald Trump said he wanted interest rates to stay low and that the dollar was “getting too strong.” The 10-year Treasury yield hit a five-month low of 2.22 percent, with its largest weekly drop since October 2015. The dollar initially slumped but later recovered. A flatter yield curve weighed on bank stocks, contributing to declines in European equities, while U.S. futures pointed lower. Trump also said China was not manipulating its currency and did not rule out re-nominating Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen. Strong Chinese trade data and Trump’s China comments supported Asian stocks, though Japan’s Nikkei fell as the yen strengthened. European markets were also affected by concerns over the French presidential election. Oil prices recovered modestly, while gold stayed near a five-month high.

Cover 3 remains widely used because it limits deep plays, supports run defense, and allows pre-snap disguise. It uses four underneath defenders and three deep-zone defenders, with the free safety closing the middle of the field. Its structure can force long throws to the flats and timely throws over the middle while adding a defender to the box.

Offenses attack Cover 3 by targeting the seams and flats through quick-game concepts, RPOs, four verticals, and flood concepts. Quarterbacks can take access throws like outs and hitches against bailing corners, read flat defenders on slant-flat or dig-whip combinations, and use RPOs based on whether the flat defender plays the run or pass. Four verticals attacks seam vulnerabilities, often with quarterbacks looking off the free safety. Flood concepts such as sail overload one side and stress zone defenders at multiple levels.

The passage also highlights play examples including Dagger, sprint-out flat/out concepts, square out-seam, Y-Cross, and post-wheel designs, showing different ways offenses try to stress Cover 3 defenders.

The NR7 trading strategy is a narrow-range volatility strategy attributed to Tony Crabel, entering when the daily trading range is low. The article backtests the strategy on SPY since 1993 using custom entry and exit rules. The original version produced a 7.8% CAGR, 0.27% average gain per trade, 899 trades, 35% time invested, and 25% maximum drawdown, which the authors consider reasonable but not worth trading. Optimization of lookback periods did not improve average gain by holding longer. Adding one undisclosed parameter improved results to a 0.46% average gain per trade, 13% drawdown, and fewer trades. The authors note NR7 may diversify mean-reversion portfolios because it enters on low volatility rather than weakness, and caution that faulty high-low data can affect results.

The President reports that the Union is internally prosperous, with growth in wealth, population, agriculture, manufactures, navigation, commerce, and public well-being. He says the recent election affirmed the equality of the States and citizens, attachment to the Constitution and Union, and rejection of sectional political parties.

He denounces political agitation against slavery and argues that Northern interference with Southern domestic institutions, resistance to fugitive-service laws, and disputes over territorial organization have threatened constitutional order. He defends the repeal of the territorial restriction line in the Kansas-Nebraska Act, arguing that Congress lacked authority to impose such restrictions and that settlers should determine institutions under popular sovereignty. He states that disorder in Kansas resulted from outside interference from both North and South, not from the organic law, and reports that insurrectionary movements and armed incursions have been suppressed, tranquillity restored, and no blood shed by U.S. forces. He says the Executive lacks authority to supervise territorial elections, but expects Kansas or Congress to remove unconstitutional or improper laws.

Federal receipts for the last fiscal year totaled $73,918,141, with total resources of $92,850,117. Expenditures excluding public debt payments were $60,172,401, and including them $72,948,792. The public debt has been reduced to $30,963,909. The President urges reduction of customs revenue to about $48 million to $50 million and renews recommendations for Treasury-related legislation.

The Army has been heavily employed against hostile Indians, especially in Washington and Oregon Territories, and the President recommends organizational improvements, changes in troop distribution, and faster armament increases. He reports that the Navy has improved in efficiency, discipline, ordnance, training, and ships, and supports further naval expansion. Public land sales totaled 9,227,878 acres, with additional land located under warrants and other purposes. The Post Office spent $10,407,868 and received $7,620,801, leaving a deficit of $2,787,046; he highlights increased mail facilities, railroad service costs, and recommendations on franking and mail steamship lines.

Foreign relations remain generally amicable. Issues with Great Britain over foreign enlistment and Central America are being resolved, and a supplemental treaty concerning Central American transit routes will be submitted to the Senate. The 1854 treaty with Great Britain improved fisheries access and trade with British North American provinces. Negotiations continue with Denmark over Sound dues and with Spain over Cuban commerce.

The President discusses maritime law proposals from the Paris conference, accepting effective-blockade rules but opposing abolition of privateering unless private property at sea is also protected from seizure by public armed vessels, except contraband. Russia approves this modification, and France is favorably disposed.

He reports unresolved claims against Mexico, uncertainty in Nicaragua, and serious disputes with New Granada over tonnage duties, mail taxes across the Isthmus, and the Panama riot that killed U.S. citizens and damaged railroad property. He has demanded punishment and indemnity, stationed naval forces at Panama and Aspinwall, and opened negotiations for compensation and security.

The message closes by noting peace at home and abroad, prosperity, westward settlement, and restored constitutional order, while expressing gratitude as the President prepares to leave office.

The speaker argues that the United States entered the war to defend its national rights, honor, freedom, and security, and must recognize that the nation’s and world’s fate will be decided in Europe. The address calls for sacrifice to prove popular government can defend itself, support human freedom and justice, and oppose nations that violate international agreements. Even if allies fail, America should continue fighting, using the conflict to strengthen citizenship, loyalty, and national unity.

The passage examines the 2008 global financial crisis, emphasizing the collapse of the U.S. housing market, excessive borrowing, deregulation, complex derivatives, and close ties between Wall Street and Washington. Housing prices rose rapidly while incomes stayed flat, supported by loosened lending standards and high-risk mortgages. When defaults increased and housing prices fell, mortgage-backed securities and credit default swaps spread losses through the financial system, freezing credit markets and threatening major banks.

Andrew Lo argued that greed, fear, complacency during prosperity, poor risk management, and lack of transparency contributed to the crisis. Simon Johnson argued that a powerful banking “oligarchy” took excessive risks with implicit government backing and became too big to fail. The passage also identifies blame across banks, regulators, politicians, credit-rating agencies, government-sponsored enterprises, investors, and homeowners.

The U.S. government responded with TARP funds, the Public Private Investment Program, and stress tests for major banks. Johnson criticized the response as inconsistent and advocated temporary government-managed receivership, breaking up large banks, separating toxic assets, and re-privatizing healthy parts. Lo proposed more effective regulation, better systemic-risk data, a Capital Markets Safety Board, risk-sensitive accounting, improved corporate governance, stronger risk-management roles, limits on political influence, and better finance education. The passage concludes that the crisis’s full effects and the success of government responses remained uncertain, while future financial crises were considered likely.

Britain’s SIG named Ernst & Young as external auditor after the FRC began investigating Deloitte’s audits of SIG’s 2015 and 2016 financial statements. SIG is reviewing historic accounts following whistleblowing allegations of profit overstatement. The company maintained full-year profit expectations as first-half revenues rose 0.6 percent.

North Wales Police have made 55 drink-drive and 40 drug-drive arrests in just over two weeks during the All Wales Summer Anti Drink and Drug Driving campaign, launched on 14 June. Inspector Dave Cust said officers are using increased patrols, intelligence and technology to target offenders, warning convictions could lead to disqualification, fines and job losses. Police urged the public to report suspected impaired drivers.

Canada’s S&P/TSX composite rose for a seventh straight day to a record 15,801.06, led by financials after strong Canadian and U.S. economic data. U.S. stocks opened little changed after recent record highs, as data and Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen’s comments increased focus on possible interest rate hikes. Yellen said delaying a hike would be unwise but gave no timing and noted uncertainty over Trump administration policy. Retail sales and consumer prices rose more than expected. Oil prices fell below $56 as a large reported rise in U.S. crude inventories raised supply concerns despite strong OPEC compliance with output cuts. Brent fell to $55.62 and U.S. crude to $52.84.

Alexei Ponikarovsky said tomorrow’s game is a must-win, the team remains positive despite being down in the series, and they need to keep generating shots, traffic, and rebounds. He noted they faced similar struggles against the Rangers but stayed with their game and won.

CMB BC won the Ivan Henson Memorial Trophy final against March Town 3–2, with overall shots of 66–62. In the annual ladies versus men game after the AGM, the ladies won 20–16, with shots of 163–157, after a close six-round triples match.

The speaker says his longtime coach, who shares his French background, has been important to his development, communication, confidence, and success. He describes John as an experienced backup goalie and positive addition to the team. He emphasizes staying focused after early pressure, using video to adjust, and the importance of penalty killing and special teams in playoff success.

Doug Ford held his first major rally as Ontario Progressive Conservative leader in Toronto, telling nearly 2,000 supporters he aims to defeat Kathleen Wynne’s Liberals and form a majority government. He criticized the province’s finances, the throne speech, taxes, hydro rates and regulations, while promising to make Ontario more business-friendly, revive manufacturing and pursue Ring of Fire mining projects. Former leadership rivals Christine Elliott, Caroline Mulroney and Tanya Granic Allen joined him onstage. Supporters cited Ford’s personality, tax-cut promises, opposition to a carbon tax, fiscal responsibility and possible review of the sex education curriculum as reasons for backing him.

The paper presents a new Nd i/Nd ii model atom for 1D NLTE abundance analysis in FGK stars, motivated by the need for accurate r-process abundance measurements in metal-poor stars. The model includes 268 Nd i levels, 556 Nd ii levels, one Nd iii ground state, 1558 bound-bound transitions, and bound-free and collisional transitions. Atomic data were drawn from VALD, NIST, linemake, and prior NIR line work, with radiative transfer performed using MULTI2.3, MARCS atmospheres, and TS-NLTE synthetic spectra.

Solar and HD222925 tests show NLTE Nd ii abundances are higher than LTE values. The authors adopt a hydrogen collision scaling factor of SH = 0.1, finding good agreement with meteoritic solar Nd abundance and previously studied benchmark stars. Tests adding theoretical Nd ii levels and hyperfine/isotopic splitting show negligible effects on the derived NLTE corrections.

NLTE abundances were derived for several metal-poor and r-process-enhanced stars. Optical Nd ii lines generally show positive NLTE corrections, increasing as effective temperature, surface gravity, and metallicity decrease, while H-band lines can show negative corrections. A grid of NLTE corrections was computed for 122 Nd ii lines over FGK metal-poor stellar parameters, and interpolation within the grid was shown to be accurate.

The corrections range from about −0.3 to +0.5 dex depending on stellar parameters and line properties. The largest positive corrections occur for blue lines in cool, low-gravity, metal-poor stars, while negative corrections occur mainly for NIR H-band lines in low-gravity, higher-temperature models. Corrections also vary with excitation potential and Nd abundance. The authors conclude that NLTE modeling is necessary for reliable Nd ii abundance analysis, especially in metal-poor giants, and recommend using higher-excitation optical and NIR Nd lines when possible.

Curtis Granderson hit his 300th homer to open a five-run eighth inning, helping the New York Mets rally from a 4-1 deficit to beat the Chicago Cubs 9-4. Lucas Duda added a three-run homer, and T.J. Rivera had three hits. Matt Harvey allowed three homers in four innings, said his arm was not working, and planned to see a doctor. Neil Walker left with a left leg injury and will have an MRI. The Mets took two of three from the Cubs and have won five of six. Chicago got early homers from Anthony Rizzo, Ian Happ and Kyle Schwarber but lost for the sixth time in eight games.

The release of “Fifty Shades Darker” has driven lingerie stores and erotic websites to capitalize on rising interest in bondage-related products. Coco de Mer launched an official collection with E.L. James, while Ann Summers released an S&M-inspired Valentine’s campaign. Online sales remain dominant, with bondage and related product sales rising significantly since the first film and overall online sex toy, bondage, and lingerie sales up 62 percent year on year since 2014.

The speaker marks the peaceful transfer of power, thanks President Clinton and Vice President Gore, and describes America as a nation united by ideals of freedom, equality, and opportunity. He pledges to build a nation of justice and opportunity through civility, courage, compassion, and character.
