The United States sued Hale County, Alabama officials under the Voting Rights Act of 1965, alleging that changes from district-based to at-large elections for county commissioners were implemented without Section 5 preclearance. The parties stipulated that Alabama had been designated under the Act in 1965, that Hale County previously elected commissioners by district, and that 1965, 1971, and 1973 Alabama enactments changed or governed at-large elections but were never precleared by the Attorney General or the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia.

The court held that the Voting Rights Act applies to Hale County because Alabama’s designation covered its political subdivisions. It found that the county’s shift to at-large commissioner elections was a voting change subject to Section 5 and that the unprecleared 1965, 1971, and 1973 enactments were legally unenforceable. Elections held under those acts were unlawful, but actions already taken or to be taken by officials elected under them remained valid until lawful successors were elected. Unless preclearance was obtained, Hale County was required to return to district elections under the 1959 Alabama act.

The court allowed the November 2, 1976 election to proceed, with elected commissioners serving provisionally. It ordered defendants to submit the relevant enactments and requested information to the Attorney General within fifteen days, directed expedited review, and required further action in the District Court for the District of Columbia if the Attorney General objected. If defendants failed to pursue such action or did not obtain approval, a prompt district-based election was to be held. The court retained jurisdiction.

In a supplemental opinion, the court rejected defendants’ argument that Hale County was not covered because it was not separately listed in the Federal Register. Citing legislative history and cases interpreting the Act, the court concluded that designation of an entire state includes all political subdivisions within that state.

Anna Gasser won gold in the Olympic debut of women’s Big Air snowboarding in Pyeongchang, edging Jamie Anderson with a final-jump double cork 1080 that scored 96 and gave her 185.00 total points. Anderson, who led entering the last round after scores of 90 and 87.25, fell on her final landing and took silver. Zoi Sadowski Synnott earned bronze with 157.50, giving New Zealand its first Winter Olympic medal in 26 years. The event was moved up a day due to wind concerns after difficult slopestyle conditions earlier in the Games.

The passage describes flexible cable interconnect technologies for quantum computing and cryogenic systems. The cables include electrically insulating flexible strips with metal striplines, grounding planes, vias for electromagnetic shielding, and rigid boards or stiffeners at one or both ends. They can route DC, low-frequency, and high-frequency signals through dilution refrigerator isothermal plates to quantum processing units, while addressing scaling challenges related to I/O density, thermal load, assembly, and serviceability.

The described systems may integrate filters, attenuators, amplifiers, circulators, isolators, connectors, absorptive materials, and signal conditioning modules into flex cables or rigid boards. Flex cables may use superconducting or non-superconducting metals, multilayer stripline structures, fanout regions, solder bumps, indium sheets, blind-mate connectors, compliant joints, and thermal clamping to isothermal plates. Absorptive materials may be incorporated into cable or board regions near ground-plane windows for high-frequency attenuation.

The passage also lists embodiments and clauses covering flexible cables, cryogenic systems, cable systems combining superconducting and non-superconducting sections, compliant-joint connections, stiffened cable ends, quantum processor interfaces, and systems configured to carry signals to quantum processing units with superconducting circuits.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPU architecture improves graphics, compute, ray tracing, AI, memory, I/O, and display capabilities over Turing. Its SM supports FP32 processing on both primary datapaths, doubling peak FP32 throughput; the GeForce RTX 3090 delivers over 35 FP32 TFLOPS, and RTX A6000/A40 benefit in 3D design, CAD/CAE simulation, and professional workflows. GA10x SMs include 128 CUDA cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation RT Core, 128 KB L1/shared memory, and larger cache/shared-memory bandwidth than Turing.

Second-generation RT Cores provide up to 2x ray tracing performance, concurrent RT with graphics or compute, and hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur through a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit. This benefits games, photorealistic rendering, architectural design, virtual prototyping, and applications using APIs such as NVIDIA OptiX, Microsoft DXR, and Vulkan ray tracing.

Third-generation Tensor Cores add support for TF32, BF16, and structured sparsity. Sparsity can double Tensor Core throughput, while TF32 can improve AI training throughput without code changes. Tensor Cores accelerate DLSS, AI denoising, NVIDIA Broadcast, NVIDIA Canvas, and other AI-based graphics and inference features, including DLSS support up to 8K.

GA10x uses GDDR6X memory on GeForce RTX 3090 and RTX 3080, reaching up to 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth through PAM4 signaling. RTX A6000 and A40 use 48 GB GDDR6, expandable to 96 GB with two GPUs via third-generation NVLink. NVLink provides 112.5 GB/sec total bandwidth between two GPUs, and PCIe Gen 4 doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth.

The full GA102 GPU contains seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, twelve 32-bit memory controllers, 6144 KB L2 cache, and 112 ROPs. Moving ROPs into the GPC improves raster operations, multisample anti-aliasing, pixel fillrate, and blending. Ampere GPUs are described as up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing at the same performance level.

RTX IO, used with Microsoft DirectStorage, enables GPU-based loading and decompression of game and creative assets, reducing CPU work and improving I/O performance. GA10x also supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, HDCP 2.3, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode up to 8K60 HDR, and seventh-generation NVENC for hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

The NVIDIA A40 targets data center visual computing with 48 GB memory, PCIe Gen 4, NVLink scaling, vGPU support, and EGX compatibility. The RTX A6000 targets desktop workstations with GA102, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, 48 GB GDDR6, NVLink memory scaling, and professional certifications. The GeForce RTX 3090 includes 24 GB GDDR6X and targets creators, data scientists, AI developers, and extreme gamers.

A Teagasc survey of 314 male farmers in south-east Ireland found 20% had never consulted a doctor and 57% had visited one in the past year, below the national male average. Farmers had higher mortality from cardiovascular disease and cancers than other occupational groups. Reported ill health included lower back pain, arthritis and anxiety. Smoking was lower than the national average, weekly binge drinking was similar, and rheumatoid arthritis was three times higher than the national male average.

The speaker calls the upcoming final the biggest game, says the team is calm but nervous, values an injured teammate’s presence and advice, and notes strong fan and city support throughout the playoffs.

Former New York Judge Louis L. Nock joined Anderson Kill after resigning from the bench under an agreement with New York judicial ethics regulators, who dropped misconduct charges in exchange for his resignation and promise not to seek judicial office again. Complaints alleged rude and unprofessional behavior toward court staff and retaliatory threats against commission staff and witnesses. Nock denied misconduct, and no findings of wrongdoing were made. Anderson Kill said he disclosed the allegations before hiring and that they did not call his conduct or character into question. His lawyer said Nock had already planned to leave the bench and was pleased to return to private practice.

The LIVE-AIR phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated lenzilumab, a GM-CSF neutralizing monoclonal antibody, in hospitalized adults with COVID-19 pneumonia. The study analyzed C-reactive protein (CRP) as a biomarker for predicting progression to invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) or death and for identifying patients most likely to benefit from lenzilumab.

In the overall modified intent-to-treat population, lenzilumab improved survival without ventilation (SWOV) compared with placebo. Multivariate analysis found baseline CRP to be the strongest predictor of progression to IMV or death. Participants with baseline CRP <150 mg/L, representing most of the study population, had the greatest benefit from lenzilumab, including improved SWOV, lower incidence of IMV, ECMO, or death, more ventilator-free days, fewer ICU days, and faster recovery. Participants with baseline CRP ≥150 mg/L showed similar SWOV outcomes with lenzilumab and placebo.

CRP levels were higher in patients with greater COVID-19 severity and remained elevated in participants who required IMV or died. Lenzilumab reduced CRP levels more rapidly than placebo. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher were less frequent with lenzilumab than placebo among participants with baseline CRP <150 mg/L, and no serious adverse events attributable to lenzilumab were reported.

The analysis suggests baseline CRP may help predict COVID-19 progression and identify hospitalized patients more likely to respond to lenzilumab, particularly those with CRP <150 mg/L.

The White House confirmed plans to withdraw Kathleen Hartnett White’s nomination to chair the Council on Environmental Quality. White, a climate change skeptic with fossil fuel industry ties, had served on a Texas environmental oversight commission and was a senior fellow at the Texas Public Policy Foundation. Her nomination stalled in the Senate after being returned at the end of 2017 and resubmitted in January. Critics cited her statements questioning climate science, opposing stricter pollution limits and praising fossil fuels. The Washington Post first reported the planned withdrawal, later confirmed by a White House official. Senator Tom Carper said withdrawing the nomination was the right decision.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced to life in prison plus 30 years for conspiracy and solicitation in the 2014 murder of Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, her former son-in-law. She maintained her innocence and denied prior knowledge of the murder-for-hire plot. Judge Stephen Everett cited her “utter lack of remorse.” Prosecutors said the motive involved the Adelson family’s desire for Markel’s ex-wife, Wendi Adelson, to move to South Florida with their children.

Ray tracing realistically simulates lighting but is computationally intensive. Earlier GPUs could not perform high-quality real-time ray tracing on a single GPU, so games relied on rasterization. NVIDIA’s Turing GPUs enable real-time ray tracing through new hardware acceleration engines called RT Cores.

Christopher K. Merker studied public pension fund governance after observing that boards and investment committees often lacked consistency, engagement, or investment expertise. Because governance data was limited, he and colleagues at Marquette University developed a research protocol to collect it. Their analysis of 35 public pension plans from 2008 to 2012 found wide performance variation, with annualized returns ranging from 15% to -4.2%. They linked these differences to governance-related behavioral factors, including organizational stability, professionalism, board composition, engagement, staff involvement, and diligence. Monthly meetings, more retired board members, and greater delegation to reliable staff were associated with better results. Investment expenses and required contribution rates were not statistically significant in their model. Plans with the highest Fiduciary Effectiveness Quotient scores outperformed the lowest quintile by nearly two to one, and each unit improvement in the score corresponded to a 0.36% increase in five-year performance. The study concludes that governance influences investment performance and can be measured.

A cross-sectional study assessed knowledge, attitudes and practices of contraception among 217 female students at NTA TV College, Nigeria. The mean age was 22 years, and the response rate was 96%. Good knowledge, attitude and practice levels were 55.3%, 47.5% and 50.7%, respectively. About 73.7% had ever had sex. Friends and the internet were the main sources of contraceptive information, while condoms and oral contraceptive pills were the most commonly used methods. Fear of side effects or health risks was the most common reason for non-use.

Multivariable analysis found that being older than 19 years predicted good contraceptive knowledge. Being a diploma student, living off-campus and having good knowledge predicted good attitude. Being from Plateau State’s indigenous population and having ever had sex predicted good contraceptive practice.

The study concluded that knowledge, attitude and practice of contraception were relatively low among the students and called for improved advocacy, policies and youth-friendly sexual and reproductive health services.

Hui Ying Financial Holdings reported 2017 revenues of $46.50 million, up 88.4% from 2016, and net income of $15.27 million, up 343.9%. Diluted EPS rose to $0.21 from $0.05. Total loans facilitated increased 59.9% to $1.31 billion, with 23,263 loans, 8,047 borrowers, and 69,232 investors. Revenue growth was driven by higher loan volume and the entrusted loan business launched in June 2017. Operating income rose 301.6% to $17.95 million, while operating expenses increased 41.2% to $28.55 million. As of December 31, 2017, the company had $12.68 million in cash and cash equivalents, $55.27 million in current assets, $17.47 million in current liabilities, and a current ratio of 3.16.

Chrissy Teigen discussed her stretch marks and pregnancy skincare routine with Refinery29. She said she has had stretch marks for years, especially on her thighs, and comes from a family prone to them. Though she has no stretch marks on her belly, she focuses on prevention during pregnancy, spending 10–15 minutes nightly applying products with help from John Legend and Luna. She uses Aquaphor, coconut oil, and Lumière de Vie products, which she said she receives for free after working with the brand. Teigen also said she has never seen a woman without stretch marks and that every model she has worked with has had at least one.

Research from the University of Essex and University College London found that girls who used social media for an hour or more by age 10 reported lower well-being by age 15. The study of 9,859 UK adolescents found girls used social media more than boys, and well-being declined more sharply for girls during adolescence. By age 15, 59% of girls used social media for at least an hour daily, compared with 46% of boys. Researchers noted the link may be underestimated due to self-reported data and school-day-only measures.

The email compiles January 26, 2001 media mentions of Enron. Articles discuss California’s power crisis and deregulation problems, Wall Street activity where Enron shares rose after profit projections, criticism of Enron’s gains and political ties amid California shortages, U.S. concern over Maharashtra’s contract dispute with Enron’s Dabhol project, possible missed Maharashtra State Electricity Board payment to Dabhol Power, Enron’s wind-power projects, and employee concerns over Enron’s new forced ranking performance-review system.

The coach said Chris Pronger’s absence requires the whole group to absorb extra minutes, with Joe DiPenta entering the lineup and players such as Jackman, Beauchemin, Niedermayer, O’Donnell, and Huskins taking larger roles. He said the next game would be the toughest and preparation had to begin immediately.

The President returns House bill No. 6242, a rivers and harbors appropriations bill, without signature despite acknowledging that many provisions serve valuable national purposes, including Potomac marsh reclamation, harbor lines, and Mississippi River improvement. His main objection is that the bill includes appropriations for purely local improvements, which he considers beyond constitutional powers and unrelated to common defense, general welfare, or interstate commerce. He argues such local spending encourages escalating demands for similar appropriations and notes that river and harbor appropriations have risen sharply, reaching $18,743,875 in the current bill. He also objects that the amount exceeds present needs and cannot be spent economically within the fiscal year. He suggests Congress appropriate only half the total for the year, with spending limited to projects selected by the Secretary of War under presidential direction and within the bill’s project limits.

A free domestic violence support group for women survivors meets Tuesdays at noon; call 541-400-0186 for details. AARP Tax Aide offers free walk-in tax help in Hood River and The Dalles with required documents. Chess for Success registration is open for a Feb. 24 Region 20 tournament at The Dalles Middle School. HRVHS Girl Up is collecting cleaned bras and sports bras in February for local women and homeless shelters.

PVF Chairman Chaudhry Mohammad Yaqoob urged the federal government to build a well-equipped sports complex in Abbottabad, citing its moderate summer weather as suitable for national camps and possible international events. He said Pakistan currently relies on the Pakistan Sports Complex in Islamabad, where hot weather and lack of air-conditioning at Liaquat Gymnasium affect athletes. He criticized spending Rs1200 million on the Narowal Sports Complex, saying it is too far for practical use. Yaqoob also called for expanded boarding facilities in Islamabad. Regarding Asian Games preparations, he said the volleyball federation requested an early camp, as two and a half months were insufficient, and noted financial issues had delayed camps. Iranian coach Hamid Movahedi was expected to join camps in Peshawar.

Chicago’s former Johnson Publishing Company headquarters, longtime home of Ebony and Jet, has been granted landmark status and sold to 3L Real Estate for $10 million. The developer plans a $20 million conversion into 150 luxury apartments with amenities, while preserving elements such as the Ebony and Jet façade signs. Construction is expected to begin in 2018 and finish the following year.

The Federal Government has announced developmental projects for the South-East, beginning with the foundation laying of the Assumpta Science Centre in Owerri, Imo State. Science and Technology Minister Ogbonnaya Onu said the project follows an MoU with the Pontifical Council for Culture of the Vatican City and reflects the Buhari administration’s focus on science, technology and innovation for economic diversification and sustainable development. He thanked Ofekata community for donating land and urged stakeholders to sustain the project. Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha, represented by Chris Nwike, pledged support for its speedy completion.

The passage describes TPS7H500x-SP radiation-hardness-assured peak current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. Slope compensation is used to mitigate subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle, with recommended compensation equal to the inductor falling current slope and set using a resistor from RSC to AVSS. The controllers support Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation using components connected between COMP and AVSS.

The devices stop switching during thermal shutdown above a typical 175°C junction temperature and restart when temperature falls below 160°C. They operate with fixed-frequency peak current mode control, sensing switch current through an external resistor and turning off the power switch when sensed current reaches the internally scaled COMP voltage.

An example synchronous push-pull converter design using TPS7H5001-SP and GaN devices is provided, including selections for switching frequency, feedback resistors, dead time, leading-edge blanking, soft-start, transformer ratio and inductance, GaN FET ratings, RCD clamp, output inductor and capacitance, overcurrent sensing, hiccup capacitor, frequency compensation, and slope compensation resistor. The example uses a 500-kHz switching frequency, 5-V output, about 25-ns dead time, 33-nF soft-start capacitor, 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 0.47-µH output inductor, about 2.3 mF output capacitance, 7.5-Ω current sense resistor, and 102-kΩ RSC resistor.

Power supply guidance specifies a 4-V to 14-V input range, proper regulation, and at least a 0.1-µF VIN-to-AVSS bypass capacitor placed close to the controller. Layout guidelines emphasize minimizing noisy switch-node and high-current loops, separating analog and power grounds with a single connection point, placing bypass and compensation components close to the device, routing sensitive traces away from high dv/dt signals, filtering CS_ILIM as needed, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS with multiple vias.

The passage also lists documentation resources, update notification methods, support forums, trademark and ESD cautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, orderable, and disclaimer information.

CJ Affiliate, formerly Commission Junction, is a long-running affiliate network that connects advertisers and publishers, tracks sales or leads, handles payments, and provides tracking, management, reporting, and promotional tools. Joining is free and requires a website or social media profile with relevant content and traffic, with approval needed before applying to advertiser programs. Publishers can search programs by niche, apply, use affiliate links, and monitor clicks, sales, and commissions through the dashboard. CJ offers programs across many niches, tools such as banners and product feeds, and payments by direct deposit, check, or Payoneer, with minimum payout requirements. The passage describes CJ as useful for beginners and advanced affiliates, though it notes a learning curve and potentially strict approvals.

The Eagles held training camp Monday ahead of Thursday’s preseason game against the Bills. Newly acquired cornerback Ronald Darby practiced Sunday with the first-team defense after being traded for Jordan Matthews and a third-round pick. Defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz said Darby was still learning calls. Questions remain about Alshon Jeffery and Carson Wentz’s playing time.

The first lecture introduces MIT 2.830J, Control of Manufacturing Processes, taught by Duane Boning and David Hardt, with Hayden Taylor as TA. Lectures are video-linked between Cambridge and Singapore, with recorded materials available when holidays affect one location. Course materials, lecture slides, readings, assignments, and problem sets are distributed through the Stellar website.

The course assumes experience with at least one manufacturing process and some background in probability and statistics, though key statistical tools will be reviewed. Semiconductor processes will be used frequently as examples, alongside broader manufacturing processes such as forming, bending, assembly, injection molding, and aerospace manufacturing.

Two required textbooks are assigned: May and Spanos’s book on semiconductor process control and Montgomery’s Introduction to Statistical Quality Control. Grades are based on weekly problem sets, two quizzes, and a team project; there is no final exam. Problem sets require individual write-ups explaining reasoning, while the team project involves collaborative analysis, an oral presentation, and a written report.

The team projects will focus on topics such as process diagnosis, process improvement, statistical process control, process optimization, robustness, design of experiments, yield modeling, and defect modeling. Projects should ideally use existing or newly generated process data from research or prior experience.

The main theme of the course is manufacturing variation and its effect on quality. The class will emphasize understanding, modeling, detecting, reducing, and controlling variation. It will cover physical and empirical process models, statistical process control, design of experiments, response surface modeling, optimization, and feedback control.

Manufacturing process goals discussed include minimizing cost, time, rework, energy use, setup effects, and equipment problems while improving quality, throughput, flexibility, and conformance to specifications. The lecture also introduces a general process model involving workpieces, equipment, process environments, controllable settings, disturbances, sensors, outputs, and product characteristics. The course will use this framework to study how process inputs and disturbances affect output variation and how control methods can reduce it.

CoreWeave shares rose as much as 8% after announcing new tools for developers to train, monitor and build AI agents, including a serverless reinforcement learning service. The company says the service can train models faster at 40% lower cost than local Nvidia H100 GPUs without affecting model quality. The launch follows CoreWeave’s $1 billion acquisition of Weights and Biases and complements its GPU rental business. CoreWeave also plans to buy Core Scientific for $9 billion, despite shareholder opposition.

This study translated and culturally adapted the Waterloo Footedness Questionnaire-Revised into Arabic and evaluated its validity and reliability among Arabic-speaking adults in Saudi Arabia. Following established cross-cultural adaptation guidelines, the questionnaire underwent forward translation, synthesis, back translation, expert review, pilot testing with 30 participants, and larger-scale testing with 290 participants.

Only minor wording and response-format changes were needed. Participants and experts found the Arabic version clear, relevant, and appropriate. Factor analysis supported a single-factor structure, with all 10 items loading above 0.5 and explaining 55.79% of variance after extraction. The questionnaire showed excellent internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.93), excellent test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.94), acceptable agreement between test and retest scores, and a standard error of measurement of 4.5 points. It also correlated significantly with a common single-item foot-dominance question (r = 0.48, p < 0.001).

The study concludes that the Arabic WFQ-R is a valid and reliable tool for assessing footedness in Arabic-speaking adults, though further testing is recommended in other Arabic-speaking contexts and populations.

The passage is an excerpt from a Texas Instruments DaVinci digital media processor datasheet covering terminal functions, device configuration, operating conditions, power/reset/clock management, and peripheral timing. It describes analog TV output pins, supply voltage requirements, reserved pins, boot mode sampling via BTMODE[15:0], XIP/NAND/MMC/SPI/EMAC/PCIe/UART boot configurations, pin multiplexing through PINCNTL registers, and guidance for unused pins and pullup/pulldown resistors.

It also summarizes interconnect architecture, absolute maximum and recommended operating conditions, electrical characteristics, PRCM functions, voltage and power domains, SmartReflex/DVFS, SRAM shutdown, I/O voltage options, standby mode, supply sequencing, decoupling, reset types and behavior, reset isolation for PCIe and EMAC, clock sources, oscillators, PLLs, SYSCLK/module clock limits, interrupt controllers, timing measurement conventions, and peripheral details for DCAN, EDMA, advanced emulation/trace/JTAG, and the Ethernet MAC switch.

President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo is expected to deliver the 2018 State of the Nation Address in Parliament on February 8. Parliament will adjourn early the previous day to prepare the chamber, and members were urged to arrive by 9:15 a.m. and not bring guests.

Lasting peace must rest on equality of rights among nations, not differences in power, territory, or resources. Governments must derive authority from the consent of the governed, and peoples should not be transferred between sovereignties as property. A united, independent, autonomous Poland is cited as an example, along with guarantees of security, worship, and development for affected peoples. Stability requires justice, freedom, and acceptance by populations. Nations should have access to sea routes, and the seas must be free in law and fact to enable peace, equality, cooperation, and commerce. Achieving this may require changes to international practice, limits on naval armaments, and broader limits on military preparations. Peace requires concession, sacrifice, accommodation, and planning by statesmen. The speaker says he speaks openly to express the world’s desire for peace and believes he represents the views of the United States, liberals, friends of humanity, and silent masses suffering from war.

The passage explains seasonal trading in silver, focusing on months with historically stronger performance. Seasonality refers to recurring price patterns tied to times of the year, business cycles, news, or holidays. Silver has typically performed best in January and July, with positive returns 69.5% and 63.6% of the time, while June and September are weaker months. The passage suggests silver seasonality may be driven by industrial users placing orders early in the year. A backtested strategy since 2001 holds silver during December–February and July–August. It holds silver 5 months per year, reportedly outperforming buy and hold by about 3.9% annually, with a risk-adjusted return of 26.93% versus 7.33% and maximum drawdown reduced from -71.65% to -23.34%.

The ADS868xW supports internal or external 4.096V references selected through INTREF_DIS, with required decoupling on REFIO and REFCAP and limits on driving external loads. The internal reference is factory trimmed, temperature compensated, and can shift after solder reflow due to thermal stress. The ADC supports single-ended and differential bipolar or unipolar ranges with straight-binary output.

The device provides configurable alarm functions for input thresholds and AVDD limits, with active and tripped flags available through the alarm pin, registers, or appended output data. Its multiSPI interface supports standard SPI, dual SDO, source-synchronous protocols, daisy-chain operation, and 32-bit data transfer frames for reads and writes. Operational states include RESET, ACQ, and CONV, with NAP and power-down modes for lower power.

Nine configuration registers control device ID, reset and power, SDI/SDO protocols, output data, input range and reference, and alarm thresholds. Application guidance describes using ADS868xW in industrial analog input modules, including alarm hysteresis for thermistor sensing, power-supply decoupling, PCB layout practices, and related documentation.

India’s selectors face a difficult task choosing the T20I squad for the England series due to injuries, possible rest for key players, and limited fitness checks after a conditioning camp was cancelled. Miyung Buster circulated a list of March 29–30, 2001 articles on California and U.S. energy issues. The articles report that Gov. Gray Davis sought another $500 million for state power purchases, bringing total purchases for PG&E and Southern California Edison to $4.7 billion, while the utilities began reimbursing the state. A Northern California judge temporarily halted Trump administration layoffs of federal workers during the government shutdown. Unions sued, alleging the administration unlawfully used the shutdown to justify staff cuts. An OMB filing indicated 4,132 to 4,232 workers were marked for layoffs across several departments, while OMB head Russell Vought said layoffs could total about 10,000. Union leaders praised the ruling. Federal workers remain affected by furloughs, missed pay, and uncertainty, with some agencies and support programs reporting financial strain among employees. The administration can appeal the decision.

The disclosure describes video encoding and decoding methods that allow a single bitstream derived from an HDR source to be used by both SDR and HDR systems. An encoder receives an HDR master and a reference SDR master of the same video, and may also receive target SDR display properties. It finds a color volume transform that converts HDR values into SDR values that, after SDR display operations, substantially match the reference SDR values. The encoder generates metadata identifying the transform and encodes values into a bitstream.

In one embodiment, the encoder converts HDR values to SDR values, optionally performs color conversion, quantization, and chroma subsampling, and encodes the SDR values. SDR systems decode and display the SDR values, while HDR systems use metadata to apply an inverse color volume transform and reconstruct HDR values for display.

In another embodiment, the encoder encodes HDR values into the bitstream and provides metadata describing how SDR systems can convert decoded HDR values into SDR values that substantially match the reference SDR master. HDR systems decode and display the HDR values, while SDR systems use the metadata-defined color volume transform before display.

The color volume transform may be represented by a tone mapping function, scaling factor, three-dimensional lookup table, or one-dimensional lookup tables. The encoder may determine the transform by testing candidate transforms against the reference SDR master using emulated SDR display operations, or by using formulas that minimize distortion. Metadata can also describe related color conversion, quantization, chroma subsampling, and display operations.

Sprint and The Sprint Foundation announced the 1Million Project, a five-year initiative to connect 1 million low-income high school students lacking home internet access. Starting Aug. 15, Sprint will provide free devices and wireless service to 180,000 students this school year across more than 1,300 schools in 32 states. Selected students receive a smartphone, tablet, or hotspot plus 3GB of high-speed LTE data monthly for up to four years. Sprint said the program addresses homework and school-related access needs. A January pilot with 3,750 students found 86% reported improved attitudes toward learning and help completing homework.

Ella Ravenscroft, a 20-year-old model from Salford and Miss Teen Galaxy England 2016, is warning about sunbed risks after having moles removed from her stomach when they changed size, shape and colour following two years of using sunbeds once or twice a week. She said she was upset about possible scarring but realised removal was necessary to avoid skin cancer risk, and now plans to use only fake tan.

She shared photos online to raise awareness and urged people to get itchy or growing moles checked. The passage states sunbed use can increase melanoma risk by 16 to 20 per cent, with almost 500 people diagnosed each year in Greater Manchester and around a fifth dying.

Most moles are benign, but changes in colour, size, shape, texture, uneven edges, bleeding, oozing, crusting, inflammation, itching, or a mole that looks different from others can be warning signs. Cancer awareness nurse Jessica Turner advised people to know their skin and show unusual changes, growths or sores that do not heal to a doctor, as early treatment can make a big difference.

Gulf stock markets mostly fell on Wednesday, led by Qatar, whose index dropped 2.3% as QNB, Qatar Islamic Bank, Qatar Electricity and Water, and Industries Qatar declined on profit-taking after earlier gains linked to MSCI weighting increases. Josie Goodenow, California Garden Clubs Inc. Bee Chairman, will speak on “All About Bees” at the Laguna Beach Garden Club on Oct. 13. The free public meeting begins with a 9:30 a.m. social and 10 a.m. general meeting at Laguna Presbyterian Church. Her program covers native bees, European honeybees, and ways to support bee populations and yard health.

Hexane is a hydrocarbon solvent derived from crude oil and found in volatile fractions of some plants. It is used in industrial manufacturing, seed oil extraction, cleaning agents, and consumer products such as glues, gasoline, rubber, and cement. Pure hexane is mainly used in laboratories, while solvent-based hexane is widely applied in industry. Hexane can be hazardous, with excessive inhalation causing weakness, numbness, blurred vision, headache, and fatigue; OSHA has set a 500 ppm exposure limit. Demand is expected to grow due to its use in edible oil production and refined cooking oils. Asia Pacific, especially China, dominates production and consumption, while North America and Europe are expected to grow due to automotive rubber demand.

Nicole Sciortino and Vincent Licciardello, both 30, were charged in Dunmore, Pennsylvania, with endangering the welfare of their two children after police found the 10- and 11-year-old home alone in poor conditions. Investigators said Sciortino was in Florida while Licciardello occasionally dropped off food. Both received $10,000 unsecured bail, and the children are staying with family friends.

Jon Klemm is described as underrated, Greg de Vries as a solid physical NHL defenseman after a strong year, and Skoula as an up-and-coming defenseman with speed, strength, size, poise, and a great shot. An unnamed forward is described as one of the league’s best in recent years.

This study evaluated cerebrospinal fluid tumor-derived DNA (CSF-tDNA) analysis using CAPP-Seq in 81 CSF, blood, and tissue samples from 24 patients with advanced lung cancer undergoing lumbar puncture for suspected leptomeningeal disease (LMD). CSF-tDNA variant allele fractions were significantly higher than plasma circulating tumor DNA levels and were positively correlated with plasma levels. For definitive LMD, CSF-tDNA showed 91.7% sensitivity, compared with 81.8% for cytology and 80.0% for MRI. CSF-tDNA detection was associated with worse overall survival.

In patients progressing after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy, resistance mutations were frequently detected in plasma but were less common in matched CSF, suggesting spatial differences in resistance mechanisms. In a prospective osimertinib cohort, increased CSF-tDNA after treatment was associated with CNS progression, and post-osimertinib CSF-tDNA variant allele fraction was prognostic for CNS progression.

The authors conclude that CSF-tDNA detection is feasible in lung cancer patients with suspected LMD and may improve diagnosis, prognostication, response monitoring, and treatment strategies that account for compartment-specific resistance.

NHS Digital figures provided to Devon Live show 719 people were admitted to hospitals in Devon, Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly with eating disorders in 2016-17, including two children under 10. Admissions also included 13 children aged 10-12, 91 aged 13-15 and 117 aged 16-18. Women and girls made up 94% of cases. Anorexia accounted for 45% of admissions and bulimia 24%. Admissions have more than doubled since 2010-11, when 298 people were admitted, reaching the highest recorded level. Charities Young Minds and Beat described the figures as concerning, stressing early intervention and warning that hospital admissions represent only the most severe cases and may not reflect overall prevalence.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K reporting that on June 14, 2021 it entered an underwriting agreement with Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, as representative of the underwriters, to issue and sell $5.0 billion of unsecured senior notes: $1.25 billion of 0.309% notes due 2023, $1.25 billion of 0.584% notes due 2024, $1.25 billion of 1.550% notes due 2028, and $1.25 billion of 2.000% notes due 2031. Net proceeds were approximately $4.98 billion and are intended for general corporate purposes, including possible repayment of indebtedness. The notes are governed by a 2016 indenture with Wells Fargo Bank, supplemented by a June 16, 2021 officers’ certificate. The filing describes interest payment dates, redemption terms, covenants, default provisions, and a change-of-control repurchase requirement. The report also lists related exhibits and was signed by CFO Colette M. Kress.

Poor medication adherence is common among patients undergoing hemodialysis, who often take 10–20 tablets daily, with reported non-adherence rates above 50% and up to 98.6%. Non-adherence is linked to poor management of CKD-related complications and increased mortality. Person-centered care (PCC), including shared decision-making, care continuity, needs-driven practice, coordination, and improved physician-patient communication, has been proposed to improve adherence, but empirical evidence is limited. Trust in physicians may mediate the relationship between PCC and medication adherence.

This multicenter cross-sectional study examined Japanese patients undergoing hemodialysis to explore relationships among PCC, trust in physicians, and medication adherence, and to assess whether trust mediates the PCC-adherence relationship. It was conducted at six outpatient hemodialysis facilities, approved by Fukushima Medical University, and followed the Declaration of Helsinki. Eligible participants were adult dialysis patients regularly attending participating facilities and able to complete questionnaires; exclusions included no regular prescriptions, severe dementia, or complete blindness. Data were collected from April 2022 to February 2023 using paper questionnaires. Medication adherence was assessed with the Japanese ASK-12 scale.

Archive360 announced it is a finalist in two 2017 DBTA Readers’ Choice Awards categories: Archive2Azure for Best Cloud Storage Solution and FastCollect for PSTs for Best Data Storage Solution. Archive2Azure is a managed compliance storage solution for Microsoft Azure designed to migrate and manage legacy email archives and other low-touch data while supporting compliance and eDiscovery readiness. FastCollect for PSTs automates PST discovery, rehydration, migration, deletion, storage and auditing to support legal and regulatory compliance. Winners will be featured on the DBTA website and in the August 2017 issue of Database Trends and Applications.

The Supreme Court is considering Victor Tony Jones’s request to block his scheduled execution for a 1990 double murder conviction. The court has not granted any execution postponement requests this year despite receiving more than 30 emergency applications. If Jones is executed, he would be the 34th person executed in 2025 and Florida’s 13th, contributing to the highest national execution total in about a decade. Executions had declined for years, reaching 11 in 2021, amid debates over lethal injection drugs and moratoriums during the Biden administration. President Trump ended the federal moratorium after returning to office. The court has recently ruled for death row inmates in several merits cases, but its emergency docket has shown an unbroken streak of stay denials this year. Upcoming cases include one on intellectual disability standards in capital cases, while the 2025 execution total could reach 43.

The passage compiles July 2001 media mentions of Enron. Fortune ranked Enron No. 16 on its Global 500 list. BusinessWeek reported shrinking corporate profits, noting Enron’s 196% revenue gain drove much of surveyed sales growth. Dow Jones reported western U.S. electricity price declines and FERC price caps led Portland General Electric to halt a 45-megawatt peaking turbine project, while other developers canceled projects. Reuters discussed post-Kyoto emissions trading and noted gas and power traders like Enron could use existing trading skills. Another Reuters item said Kobe Steel was raising funds for a wholesale power business in Japan, where Enron had expressed interest. The South Florida Sun-Sentinel reported Enron canceled a Miami-Dade power plant plan and focused on Deerfield Beach, where construction faced a county moratorium. The Washington Post reported Karl Rove met with representatives of companies, including Enron, while holding stock later divested. TheStreet.com reported Ken Lay and Jeffrey Skilling sold Enron shares while publicly describing the stock as undervalued, and separately said Enron’s broadband business had lost value after earlier boosting expectations.

Tesla’s 2016 launch of the $35,000 Model 3 drew major preorders, but by 2018 the company faced “production hell,” large losses, cash concerns, and delays in reaching 5,000 cars per week. Elon Musk attributed part of the difficulty to excessive automation.

The U.S. auto industry was large but slow-growing, with entrenched automakers, low margins, high barriers to entry, fragmented suppliers, and declining customer loyalty. Industry change was driven by electric vehicles, autonomous driving, connected cars, and alternatives to private ownership such as ride-hailing, car-sharing, bikes, and scooters. Automakers and suppliers were investing heavily in EVs, batteries, software, and mobility services, while dealerships faced pressure from online buying and EVs’ lower service needs.

Tesla entered the market in 2003, went public in 2010, and pursued Musk’s strategy of starting with premium EVs before moving toward mass-market cars. The Roadster, Model S, and Model X established Tesla in luxury EVs but suffered delays, glitches, and missed projections. The Model 3 was Tesla’s first mass-production effort. Tesla pursued unusually high vertical integration, including battery production at its Nevada Gigafactory and extensive in-house component manufacturing, while relying on a highly automated Fremont factory.

Tesla also differed from traditional automakers by selling through company-owned stores, building its own Supercharger network, and using software updates to improve vehicles. Musk’s later plan envisioned fully autonomous Teslas participating in a shared fleet when not in use. By 2018, observers were divided between those who saw Tesla as a disruptive force accelerating sustainable transportation and those who questioned whether it could survive and thrive in the auto industry.

Coach Sutter said his team is not changing its approach and must continue doing the same things that brought success. He described the opponent as skilled, hardworking, bigger and quicker up front, and said both teams are close enough that bounces, calls, or changes can decide games. He emphasized smart forechecking, staying within structure, managing physical play without penalties, and not over-chasing matchups. He noted ice conditions, shift lengths, faceoffs, and home-ice last change affect line usage and puck movement.
Jaguar is testing the 2018 F-Pace SVR at the Nürburgring, likely with a 5.0-liter supercharged V8 from the F-Type SVR or F-Type R producing 500–575 hp.

DLSS 4 transitions from CNNs to transformer-based AI models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving temporal stability, reducing ghosting, enhancing lighting detail, and increasing image detail in motion. Transformer models use self-attention, handle larger pixel windows, scale more effectively, and use more Tensor Core processing power.

Blackwell introduces developer-created neural shaders, enabling AI models to approximate complex shader calculations. NVIDIA’s Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan, developed with Microsoft, allows Tensor Cores to be accessed through shaders, supporting neural texture compression, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces.

RTX Neural Materials use neural approximations to render complex layered materials in real time. RTX Neural Texture Compression reduces memory use and supports stochastic texture filtering. Neural Radiance Cache approximates indirect lighting from path-traced rays to improve performance and lighting quality. RTX Skin brings ray-traced subsurface scattering to games, while RTX Neural Faces uses generative AI to infer more natural real-time faces.

The passage also outlines GPU shader evolution and describes Blackwell GPUs including GB202, GB203, and GB205, with GeForce RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, and 5070 products based on them. It concludes with NVIDIA specification disclaimers, liability limits, and trademark notices.

MKM Partners raised its price target for Tutor Perini Corporation from $31 to $34 and maintained a buy rating. Other analysts have issued mixed ratings, with four hold and four buy ratings, giving the stock a consensus buy rating and $27.29 target. The North Carolina Court of Appeals affirmed the dismissal of Lewis Williamson’s appeal challenging Surf City’s closure of a 20-foot portion of North Shore Drive adjacent to both Williamson’s and the town’s properties. Surf City had followed the procedural requirements of N.C.G.S. § 160A-299, including adopting a resolution of intent, providing notice, holding a public hearing, and approving the closure by majority vote. Williamson argued the closure was improper because the town intended to use its vested portion of the closed street to construct public facilities. The court held that the statute does not limit a town’s authority to close a street based on its intent, so long as statutory procedures are followed. Because Surf City owned adjacent property, it obtained a vested interest in part of the closed street and could use it for any lawful purpose. The court also rejected Williamson’s argument that the statute permits only closure of an entire street, concluding that a town may close all or part of a street upon compliance with statutory procedure.

The passage introduces a study on forecasting daily COVID-19 confirmed and death cases for five heavily affected countries: the USA, India, Brazil, Russia, and the UK. It argues that COVID-19’s dynamic and robust datasets make single models such as ARIMA, SVM, or ARNN insufficient, motivating hybrid approaches that combine linear and nonlinear modeling. The study proposes hybrid ARNNS and SVMAR models for short-term and long-term out-of-sample forecasts, aiming to support health, policy, and scientific decision-making. Data consist of daily confirmed and death cases from Global Change Data Lab, with country-specific start dates and a common end date of January 15, 2021. Preliminary analysis indicates the datasets are not normally distributed.

Investing.com content discusses seasonal market weakness over the past 35 years, noting thin liquidity, reduced volume, tax-loss selling, institutional rebalancing, and fading earnings momentum in August. The analysis highlights TLT’s technical setup, suggesting yields may drop further if resistance is cleared, while noting risk-on behavior and a bullish divergence. A weaker dollar below 98 is described as supportive for commodities, with gold and energy-related materials also discussed. The passage says weakening dollar, lower yields, and rising gold are generally risk-off signals, while market direction should be assessed using July calendar ranges. It also includes promotional stock-market content, headlines, and risk disclosures about trading financial instruments and cryptocurrencies.

The passage describes a patent application for a rotating shaft mechanism and a mobile terminal with a flexible foldable display. The mechanism is intended to improve the folding effect of foldable devices by reducing folded hinge thickness and providing space for the flexible display during bending.

The rotating shaft mechanism includes a main shaft assembly, swing arm assemblies, and a support assembly. Swing arms connect to two housings of the mobile terminal and rotate relative to the main shaft assembly. Connecting rods link the swing arms and main shaft assembly, with rotation axes different from but parallel to those of the swing arms. Support plates on both sides of the main shaft assembly rotate or slide with the swing arms or connecting rods to form a folding space that accommodates the flexible display when folded.

The mechanism may include arc-shaped sliding slots and arms, staggered swing arm structures, engaging gears for synchronized housing movement, and limiting mechanisms using cams, protrusions, notches, and elastic parts to stabilize folded and unfolded states and provide damping. Support plates can be connected by pin shafts or arc-shaped sliding structures, and may support the display flush with the main shaft surface when unfolded.

A flexible blocking layer, such as an elastic steel or plastic plate, may cover exposed notches and improve appearance during folding. The mobile terminal includes two housings, the rotating shaft mechanism, and a flexible display, which may be adhesively connected to the housings and optionally to support plates. In folded states, non-adhesive display areas may form droplet-shaped or semi-arc-shaped bends within the space formed by the support plates and main shaft assembly.

A Kuwaiti court sentenced Salem Buhan and Amira Hussein to death for torturing and killing their three-year-old daughter, whose body was kept in a freezer. The verdict is not final and must be reviewed by appeals and supreme courts.

Royalty North Partners Ltd. granted 35,000 incentive stock options exercisable at C$1.47 per share until October 6, 2022, and awarded 37,500 Restricted Share Rights vesting over two years to certain directors and senior officers. The company focuses on royalty financing for private mid-market businesses.

The passage describes the United States’ policy against using armed force to collect ordinary contract debts owed to its citizens by foreign governments, arguing that such force undermines sovereignty and can lead to oppression and unjustified war. At the Rio conference, delegates supported asking the Second Hague Peace Conference to examine compulsory collection of public debts and ways to reduce conflicts of pecuniary origin, while noting that Rio itself should not set rules because many American nations were debtors and European nations creditors. The passage also recounts U.S. and Mexican mediation in the war among Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras, which led to peace talks aboard a U.S. warship and helped prevent loss of life and property. The Rio Conference praised this mediation and presented it as an example of cooperative American action promoting peace and stronger international standards.

Dr. Ian K. Smith’s The Clean 20 is a clean eating guide featuring 20 accessible foods, daily meal plans, 60 recipes, substitutions, and 20-minute workouts, aiming to reduce processed foods while including varied food groups.

The railway line between Lincoln and Grimsby was opened in 1848 by the Manchester, Sheffield and Lincolnshire Railway to transport goods, including fish, to and from Grimsby’s port. Its route included the River Witham Bridge at Stamp End in Lincoln, recently replaced by Network Rail in a £7m project.

Designed by MS&LR engineer John Fowler, the bridge used wrought iron box/tubular girder technology and may have been the oldest surviving railway bridge of its type still carrying trains in Britain. Fowler adopted William Fairbairn’s tubular girder design after initially considering timber cased with boiler plate, in the context of concerns following the 1847 Dee Bridge disaster.

The bridge originally carried double track over three spans, with a central iron tubular girder span and likely timber side spans. It was altered and reinforced in 1903, 1948 and 1968 to handle heavier trains, with timber spans replaced by metal decks, additional girders and plates added, and a new steel deck installed.

Scientists used kirigami-inspired concentric slits in thin Mylar disks to create parachutes that automatically unfurl into lattice shapes as cargo falls. In tests, they fell straighter and closer to targets than traditional parachutes or uncut disks, though they produce less drag because of their holes. A 0.5-meter kirigami parachute slowed a 1-kilogram water bottle dropped from 60 meters to about 14 meters per second. Potential uses include humanitarian aid drops and drone package delivery, with future designs possibly using biodegradable materials or adaptations for space missions.

Intraday trading involves buying and selling financial instruments within the same trading day, including stocks, futures, or forex. It may involve scalping or day trading, aiming to profit from intraday price movements while avoiding overnight risk. The passage says intraday trading is difficult, risky, and often unprofitable for most traders, especially without a backtested, quantified trading plan. In the US, pattern day traders must meet FINRA requirements, including maintaining at least $25,000 in a margin account. Suggested rules include learning the market, setting realistic goals, avoiding herd behavior, choosing a reputable broker, trading liquid stocks, understanding company fundamentals, using automated quantified systems, and reviewing results periodically. The passage emphasizes backtesting, notes that intraday strategies can be harder to test than daily strategies, and provides an example using WTI crude oil futures with mixed results. It also discusses common strategies, markets, indicators, capital needs, and trading times, while arguing that stocks offer better opportunities than forex and that most traders lose money.

This multicenter cross-sectional study assessed SARS-CoV-2 humoral immunity in 1,411 emergency department patients at five university hospitals in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, between August and September 2022. Researchers measured Spike IgG, Nucleocapsid IgG, and serum neutralization against Wu01, BA.4/5, and BQ.1.1, and analyzed associations with vaccination, infection history, medical conditions, immunosuppression, age, and other factors.

Participants had a median age of 53 years; 64.2% reported preconditions, 13.6% reported drug immunosuppression, 94.4% had received at least one EU-approved COVID-19 vaccine, and 45.7% reported prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. Spike IgG was detected in 95.6% of participants, while 67.7% were vaccinated according to German recommendations. Spike IgG levels increased with the number of prior Spike-antigen contacts and were lower in participants with drug immunosuppression. Nucleocapsid IgG was detected in 24.0% and was strongly associated with reported prior infection.

Neutralizing activity was detected against Wu01 in 94.4% and against BA.4/5 in 84.9% of participants, with BA.4/5 neutralization 5.92-fold lower than Wu01. Spike IgG correlated with neutralizing activity, but prediction was less accurate for immune-evasive variants. In a representative subsample of 423 participants, neutralizing activity was detected against BQ.1.1 in 73.8%, with a 23.6-fold reduction compared with Wu01 and 4.2-fold reduction compared with BA.4/5. Among individuals with Spike IgG below 1,000 BAU/ml, 59.6% had no detectable neutralization against BQ.1.1.

Regression and Bayesian analyses identified Spike IgG, prior infections, vaccination history, Nucleocapsid IgG, and time since infection as key predictors of neutralizing activity, with age and other factors contributing in some models. The authors conclude that high Spike IgG seroprevalence coexisted with moderate vaccination-recommendation adherence and reduced neutralization against BQ.1.1, supporting improved vaccine uptake to reduce COVID-19 risk.
The Ohio Supreme Court reversed the court of appeals’ judgment based on State v. Szefcyk; Justice Cook did not participate.

Netflix shares fell 0.68% in premarket trading despite announcing that Shonda Rhimes will move future shows to the platform while continuing existing ABC series. The deal follows Netflix’s Millarworld acquisition and Disney’s plan to pull movies for its own streaming service. Barron’s suggested Netflix shares could fall due to content losses and rising debt.

The North Carolina Court of Appeals reversed the trial court’s dismissal of controlled substances charges against Ryan Jeffery Adams. After Adams’s arrest, cocaine and marijuana were seized, and the Department of Revenue docketed a $456,574.26 tax judgment under the North Carolina Controlled Substance Tax Act, of which Adams paid a portion. The trial court dismissed the criminal charges on double jeopardy grounds. The Court of Appeals held that the dismissal conflicted with binding North Carolina appellate precedent in State v. Ballenger and State v. Creason, which upheld the drug tax against similar constitutional challenges. The court rejected reliance on the Fourth Circuit’s Lynn v. West decision because lower federal appellate decisions are not binding on North Carolina courts. It stated that only the North Carolina Supreme Court or General Assembly could alter the controlling law.

The Buck Sweep, popularized by Tubby Raymond and the University of Delaware, is a signature Wing-T play. It is a misdirection off-tackle run using two pulling blockers and can hit either inside a vertical crease or outside, depending on defensive reaction. Its strengths include disguising the ball, stressing multiple gaps through the Buck Series, creating defensive indecision, and using blocking angles that help smaller offensive linemen move defenders horizontally. Its weaknesses are reliance on precise timing, spacing, puller ability, and significant practice for handoffs, pull paths, and tailback reads.

The passage outlines blocking rules for the Buck Sweep against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, detailing responsibilities for linemen, backs, quarterback, tight end, wingback, and receiver. It also describes two variations: the Shotgun Wing-T Buck Sweep, which changes backfield action and can include a quarterback keep read, and the I-Wing Buck Sweep, which mainly changes the formation presentation while keeping the blocking scheme similar.

The passage discusses concerns that Google may discontinue Inbox, its alternative Gmail interface, especially amid a confirmed Gmail redesign adopting Inbox features like email snoozing and Smart Reply, slower visible updates, and Google’s history of ending services. Google states that the upcoming Gmail announcement brings “no changes to Inbox by Gmail” and says Inbox remains a product for specific workflows and testing email innovations.

The author notes that Inbox has continued receiving unannounced features, including AI-powered Highlights, unsubscribe suggestions, and follow-up prompts. Inbox also retains distinct functions such as bundled message organization, trip-related summaries, key detail extraction, integrated Google reminders, and attaching reminders to emails. Past Google comments described Inbox as a long-term experiment that might eventually replace Gmail, though current usage figures are unclear. A former product manager said in 2016 that Inbox had a “non-trivial” and growing user base, and the Android app shows 10 million installs. The passage concludes that Inbox does not appear abandoned or likely to be shut down soon.

The shiitake mushroom market is projected to grow at a 15.31% CAGR, reaching USD 26.7 billion by 2022 and USD 35.4 billion by 2023. Asia Pacific held 82.54% market share in 2017, with China accounting for 97% of the regional market. Growth is driven by nutritional, medicinal, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic applications. Key players include Bonduelle SA, Mitoku, Agro Dutch Industries, and The Mushroom Company.

Freelance writer Oobah Butler created a fake TripAdvisor listing for “The Shed at Dulwich,” a supposed appointment-only restaurant in his London garden shed, to test how easily the platform could be manipulated. Using a website, burner phone, fake menu, staged food photos, and reviews from friends and family, the nonexistent restaurant rose from last place to TripAdvisor’s No. 1 restaurant in London. The listing attracted reservation requests, media attention, offers, and inquiries, despite having no address or actual service. TripAdvisor said it had reviewed and penalized the listing before Butler exposed the hoax, adding that its fraud systems focus mainly on fake reviews for real businesses. The incident drew wider comparisons to online misinformation and platform vulnerabilities. Butler later opened the “restaurant” for one night with actors, foodies, and inexpensive instant food.

The passage describes container design patterns for building modular distributed systems. It recommends documenting container images through Dockerfiles using directives such as EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL, including metadata based on shared label schemas.

It reviews the sidecar pattern, where a container extends an application container, then introduces the ambassador pattern, where a companion container brokers communication between an application and external services. Ambassador examples include routing requests to sharded Redis or memcached backends with twemproxy, brokering environment-specific services such as MySQL, and splitting traffic for experiments using nginx, including weighted routing and IP hashing for consistent user experience.

The adapter pattern is presented as a way to modify an application container’s interface without changing the application itself. Adapters can normalize monitoring, logging, and health-check interfaces. Examples include using a Prometheus Redis exporter, fluentd plugins for Redis slow logs and Apache Storm logs, and a MySQL health-check adapter that exposes an HTTP health interface while leaving the MySQL container unchanged.

The passage then contrasts single-node patterns with multi-node distributed patterns and introduces microservices as systems composed of separate processes communicating through defined APIs. It describes benefits such as reliability, agility, independent scaling, and clearer team boundaries, while noting drawbacks including harder debugging and more complex design.

Several distributed patterns are covered. Replicated load-balanced services use identical stateless replicas behind a load balancer for availability and scaling, supported by readiness probes. Session-tracked services route a user’s requests to the same replica, often using IP hashing, cookies, or consistent hashing. Application-layer replicated services can add caching with Varnish, rate limiting for denial-of-service defense, and SSL termination with nginx.

Sharded services divide state across shards, with routing logic directing requests to the appropriate shard. Sharded caches improve memory utilization compared with replicated caches but introduce concerns around shard failure, cache hit rate, latency, rollouts, and capacity. Replicated sharded caches improve resilience and allow hot shards to be scaled. The passage also explains sharding functions, key selection, and consistent hashing to reduce remapping during resharding.

The scatter/gather pattern distributes parts of a request to multiple leaf nodes, gathers partial results, and combines them at a root node. It is useful for parallel computation such as document search, but excessive parallelism can introduce overhead, straggler latency, and availability risks. Replicating each shard improves reliability and supports upgrades under load.

Finally, the passage introduces function-as-a-service and event-driven computing. FaaS simplifies deployment from source code, automatically scales and restarts functions, and encourages modular stateless design, but its forced decoupling requires network communication between functions and external storage for state, which can complicate operations.

Port Gregory experienced repeated power outages from Thursday to Monday, affecting residents’ medical equipment and food supplies. Resident Betty Sawers reported losing about $500 of frozen food, while a neighbour could not use a CPAP machine. Western Power cited storm-related resource pressures and said eligible customers could claim an outage payment capped at $80.

This study examines motor coordination after stroke using a high-density EMG wearable sleeve across functional hand, wrist, and forearm movements. It compares able-bodied participants with individuals with chronic stroke, focusing on co-contraction, muscle coupling, and muscle synergies as potential markers of altered motor control. Seven stroke participants and seven able-bodied participants completed cued movement tasks while EMG was recorded from the forearm. Stroke participants also completed clinical assessments including Fugl-Meyer, Box and Blocks, and Modified Ashworth Scale tests. EMG data were filtered, artifact-corrected, mapped across sleeve sizes and arms, and analyzed using muscle group masks, co-contraction indices, correlation metrics, and muscle synergy decomposition. The work aims to demonstrate that an easy-to-use HD-EMG sleeve can extract motor-related features that may support stroke rehabilitation research and clinical assessment.

The passage argues that the Allied war effort suffers from uncoordinated strategy caused by conflicting nationalist aims within the coalition. It claims that emphasis on national ambitions weakened cooperation, contributing to misunderstandings with Russia and disasters for Italy and Rumania. The author says unity requires simplifying and pooling war aims, shifting political power toward middle parties, and placating the moderate left rather than the irreconcilable right. Sustained success, especially on the Western Front, depends on broad popular consent, efficient administration, and diplomacy that counters German liberal appeals. Without this, Allied morale and military strength may weaken. The passage predicts Germany may seek winter peace talks to divide Allied morale, while the Allies will suppress peace discussion until possible 1918 gains reduce German prestige and allow negotiation.

The company will provide more detailed capital allocation plans with its second-quarter results. The passage describes 4D-STEM measurements of cryogenic SrTiO3 to visualize nanoscale polarization. SrTiO3 is cubic and non-polar at room temperature, undergoes an antiferrodistortive transition near 105 K, and enters a quantum paraelectric regime below about 40 K without long-range ferroelectric order. Polarization is extracted from inversion-related Kikuchi band asymmetries in electron diffraction, supported by multislice simulations.

Experiments show that below the antiferrodistortive transition, SrTiO3 contains local polar nanodomains despite the centrosymmetric structural distortion. At 69 K, polar domains about 20 nm in size appear and show periodic spatial correlations with a length scale near 25 nm. Cooling below about 40 K fragments these nanodomains into smaller, more disordered clusters, with correlation length decreasing to about 14 nm and periodic ordering suppressed. Temperature-dependent maps show polar nanodomains nucleate near 111 K, grow and self-organize down to about 69 K, then lose order and fragment on further cooling.

The authors conclude that quantum paraelectric SrTiO3 is not characterized by an absence of polarization, but by re-entrant disordering of preexisting polar nanodomains. The observed polar textures may relate to SrTiO3’s anomalous low-temperature properties and motivate studies of how external tuning or doping affects these nanoscale polar states.

The dollar hit multi-week highs against the yen and euro after September U.S. wage growth exceeded expectations despite hurricane-distorted payroll losses. Analysts said rising earnings supported the case for Federal Reserve tightening, with futures pricing a 93% chance of a December rate hike.

Fior Markets released “Cooking Oil Market 2017 Global Analysis and Forecast to 2022,” covering industry trends, statistics, segmentation, growth, market share, revenue, leading players, regions, types, and applications. PIMS employees continued their protest for a fifth day demanding separation of PIMS from SZABMU, sealing Vice Chancellor Prof. Dr. Javed Akram’s office and forcing him out. Protest leaders rejected assurances, saying they would continue until their demand is met. Political and CDA representatives also expressed solidarity with the protesters.

The speaker says the team is used to starting series on the road and playing in loud arenas, though the media attention is different. They emphasize sticking to their plan, handling adversity, and improving after a poor, passive effort against New Jersey. They say the team must work harder, skate better, make things tougher for the Devils’ defense, get more shots on Brodeur, and respond in the next game.

Dinbych were tested by Wrexham after three high-scoring wins, but held on in a competitive Division Two (North) match. Wrexham led 12-10 at half-time through tries from James Price and James Weston, while Tom Seddon scored for Dinbych and Dan O’Sullivan added a penalty. Second-half tries from Aidyn Jones and Owain Davies put Dinbych ahead before Jack Ratcliff’s late converted try earned Wrexham a losing bonus point. Singapore Airlines will restart nonstop Singapore-Newark flights on Oct. 12, making it the world’s longest flight by distance at about 9,000 nautical miles, or 9,537 statute miles. The route, last flown in 2013, will surpass Qatar Airways’ Doha-Auckland service. Scheduled flight times are 18 hours, 45 minutes to Singapore and 18 hours, 25 minutes to Newark. The airline will use the new Airbus A350-900ULR, configured with 67 business-class and 94 premium economy seats, with no standard coach. Service will begin three times weekly and is expected to become daily after another aircraft enters service. Newark will be Singapore Airlines’ fifth U.S. airport.

Peruvian police are considering expelling U.S. citizen John Dougherty and Canadian citizen Jennifer Moore for allegedly inciting rural protests against Hudbay Minerals’ Constancia copper mine. Authorities said they entered as tourists but violated that status. Hudbay had suspended operations in November amid protests demanding promised development projects.

Archaeologists in Egypt discovered a 4,400-year-old tomb near the pyramids outside Cairo, likely belonging to Hetpet, a high-ranking 5th Dynasty official. The tomb contains wall paintings of hunting, fishing, and monkeys. Officials believe Hetpet may have another tomb in Giza’s western necropolis, where excavation is underway.

This article reports a mapping review of U.S.-based occupational therapy fieldwork education literature from 1989 to October 2020. The review was conducted by an AOTA Academic Fieldwork Coordinators Academic Leadership Council ad hoc committee to update understanding of the fieldwork literature and identify gaps using the AOTA Occupational Therapy Education Research Agenda–Revised (2018), education level, and fieldwork level.

Searches of four databases and the Journal of Occupational Therapy Education identified 1,619 records after duplicates were removed. After abstract screening, retrieval, and full-text review, 67 articles met inclusion criteria. Most articles focused on occupational therapy rather than occupational therapy assistant education, and most addressed Level II fieldwork. Of the 67 included articles, 55 focused exclusively on occupational therapy fieldwork, one exclusively on OTA fieldwork, and five on both. Forty-six focused on Level II fieldwork, 16 on Level I, and five on both.

The literature mapped primarily to two Education Research Agenda categories: learner characteristics and competencies (31 articles) and instructional methods (23 articles). Fewer articles addressed socialization to the profession or faculty development and resources. No articles mapped to theory building, signature pedagogies, or promotion of diversity, inclusion, and equity.

The review found that fieldwork research remains disproportionately focused on Level II occupational therapy fieldwork, especially instructional methods and learner competencies. Level I fieldwork, OTA fieldwork, theory building, signature pedagogies, faculty development, socialization to the profession, and diversity, inclusion, and equity remain underrepresented. The authors recommend collaborative research involving fieldwork stakeholders and suggest that future revisions of the AOTA Education Research Agenda more explicitly include fieldwork education.

A federal judge denied the US government’s request to delay an order allowing transgender people to enlist in the military starting January 1, 2018. The Pentagon said it is preparing to comply, while the Justice Department reviews legal options.

The lecture reviews collective Thomson scattering spectra and how the spectral density function encodes frequency-resolved plasma information through electron density fluctuations. Using a test-particle formalism, the spectrum is separated into electron and ion components, though scattering is always from electrons: some electrons respond to other electrons, while others follow ions. For Maxwellian electron and ion distributions, susceptibilities depend on the collective scattering parameter α = 1/(kλ_De) and a function of the ratio between wave phase velocity and thermal velocity.

In the limit α² → 0, susceptibilities vanish, permittivity approaches 1, no plasma-wave resonances appear, and the spectrum reduces to the electron distribution function, corresponding to incoherent scattering from individual electrons within the Debye length. For arbitrary α, high-frequency limits recover electron plasma waves, with resonances whose positions depend on density and temperature and whose widths relate to electron temperature through damping. Low-frequency limits recover ion acoustic waves, which appear or are damped depending on zT_e/T_i. When this ratio is large, strong ion acoustic resonances appear; when small, the spectrum resembles the ion distribution function.

The total scattered cross-section can be split into electron and ion features. At small α, the electron feature dominates; at large α, the ion feature dominates. Because electron plasma waves and ion acoustic waves occur at very different frequencies, they are usually difficult to measure with the same spectrometer.

Electron-ion drift produces asymmetry in ion acoustic peaks because the waves experience different electron damping. Fitting the full spectral density function can yield the drift velocity along the scattering wave vector and therefore the local current component, provided density is known. Ion acoustic spectra can also provide electron temperature, ion temperature, ion flow velocity, and electron-ion drift, but not electron density directly.

Magnetic fields can in principle modulate ion and electron features at cyclotron frequencies, but the measurement is difficult. Collisions generally damp coherent features and modify incoherent spectra, so neglecting them can lead to incorrect interpretation. Finite collection volume, finite measurement time, velocity gradients, turbulence, and finite collection angle can broaden or distort spectra, causing incorrect inferred plasma parameters unless accounted for. Smaller collection volumes or angles reduce these effects but lower signal. Current research includes non-Maxwellian distribution functions, faster evaluation methods, machine learning, and multi-angle Thomson scattering measurements.
