Texas educators, parents and policy experts worry that a new law replacing STAAR with three shorter tests may increase testing time and student stress rather than reduce it. The system, launching in 2027-28, will include tests at the beginning, middle and end of the year, ban some practice tests and provide faster results to help teachers adjust instruction. Critics say school accountability ratings may still rely heavily on the end-of-year exam, keeping pressure high while adding more testing. TEA will determine testing protocols, raising concerns that all three exams could resemble STAAR’s restrictive conditions. Supporters say the law will reduce over-testing, while some educators and parents want more teacher input and more relaxed assessments like MAP tests.

The study examines Turkey’s highly centralized education administration system and proposes a local education boards model as an alternative. It argues that Turkey’s current directorate-based structure limits participation, transparency, accountability, democracy, flexibility, and sustainability, while OECD countries with more localized and board-based education governance generally show higher PISA results and GDP per capita than Turkey.

Using a mixed-method exploratory sequential design, the study analyzed education administration systems in 16 OECD countries whose PISA and GDP averages exceed OECD averages. It also surveyed teachers and administrators in Seyhan district of Adana province. The questionnaire was tested for validity and reliability through test-retest analysis and correlation measures.

Qualitative findings show that many OECD countries use education boards, councils, commissions, or committees at national, regional, local, vocational, and school levels. These structures often include teachers, parents, local governments, unions, universities, civil society, professional bodies, and other stakeholders. Quantitative findings show that most surveyed participants preferred local administration over central administration, wanted education managed by elected boards or commissions, and supported broad stakeholder participation in provincial, district, vocational, school, and inspection boards. Many participants also favored transferring several operational duties from the central ministry to local education units.

The study concludes that Turkey should replace its centralized directorate-based education administration with a participatory local education boards model. The proposed model includes central bodies for national policy, monitoring, and evaluation, and local boards for provincial, district, vocational, school, and inspection functions. The authors recommend piloting the model, conducting further research on board structure and operation, and considering it as an alternative for education policy reform.

A bug in Atlassian Jira and Confluence can expose AWS secret access keys through a vulnerable proxy enabling XSS and SSRF attacks, potentially allowing instance takeover, data theft, or destruction. NIST rated the flaw 6.1, and Atlassian has fixed affected products, but some companies still run exposed legacy deployments. Researcher Robert Wiggins found over a dozen major vulnerable deployments. EE, Insider, Easy Metrics, the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, IEEE, Ronin, and A&E Networks took action after being contacted. Three unnamed organizations did not respond and remain vulnerable. Updating Atlassian software is described as the best solution.

NVIDIA RTX IO integrates with Microsoft DirectStorage to reduce IO overhead on NVMe SSD gaming PCs by keeping data compressed until GPU-based lossless decompression, offloading CPU work and improving I/O performance. GA10x Ampere GPUs provide up to 2x improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI, with second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, GDDR6X support, RTX IO, advanced display support, fifth-generation NVDEC decoding, and seventh-generation NVENC encoding.

The NVIDIA A40 is a GA10x Ampere data center GPU for visual computing, offering up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput, up to 5x AI and data science throughput, PCIe Gen4, 48GB memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink, vGPU support, Quadro Sync, and EGX Platform compatibility. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU includes 10,752 CUDA cores, 48GB GDDR6, ray-tracing and AI features, and NVLink support for 96GB combined memory.

Ampere GPUs support DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 8K60 and 4K120 displays, HDCP 2.3, and hardware decode for codecs including MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, HEVC, VP8, VP9, and AV1. GA10x GPUs are described as the first to support AV1 hardware decode, enabling up to 8K60 HDR playback with low CPU use. NVENC enables hardware video encoding for streaming and high-resolution encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 24GB GDDR6X and is positioned for creators, data scientists, AI developers, and extreme gamers. The RTX 3070 uses GA104, is faster than the RTX 2080 Ti, and uses GDDR6. GA10x also introduces Error Detection and Replay for GDDR6X memory overclocking, detecting transmission errors and replaying failed transactions until successful.

England qualified for the 2018 World Cup but were poor in a 1-0 win over Slovenia. The passage argues Gareth Southgate’s cautious 4-2-3-1 system limits attacking players such as Harry Kane, Marcus Rashford and Raheem Sterling, and that Dele Alli is England’s only viable No. 10, with Sterling better used on the wing. It says upcoming friendlies against Brazil and Germany should be used to try a bolder approach, including three centre backs, advanced wing-backs, and attacking roles for Alli, Rashford and Kane, to avoid another early tournament exit.

Spotify, Comcast, and Oracle recently announced co-CEO structures, reflecting renewed interest in a model still used by only about 1.2% of Russell 3000 companies. Experts say co-CEOs can help divide responsibilities, support succession planning, and potentially improve performance; a Harvard Business Review study found companies with two CEOs had higher average annual shareholder returns than comparable single-CEO firms from 1996 to 2020. However, the structure can create ambiguity, power struggles, and governance challenges if roles and decision-making authority are unclear. Examples include Netflix, Salesforce, Sony Interactive Entertainment, Chipotle, Lennar, Warby Parker, and Revolve. Experts emphasized that success depends on alignment, clear responsibilities, collaboration, and both leaders accepting shared accountability.

This passage is from a 2018 ebook edition of a 1902 Foreign Relations of the United States volume concerning whaling and sealing claims against Russia over the arrest and seizure of four American vessels. It includes publication notes from the Office of the Historian and documents transmitting Herbert H. D. Peirce’s memorandum supporting U.S. claims for indemnity before arbitrator T. M. C. Asser.

NVIDIA filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 25, 2015. Third-quarter revenue was $1.305 billion, up from $1.225 billion a year earlier, with net income of $246 million versus $173 million. For the first nine months of fiscal 2016, revenue was $3.609 billion versus $3.431 billion, while net income declined to $406 million from $437 million. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled about $4.7 billion, and total assets were $7.174 billion.

GPU segment revenue rose to $1.110 billion in the quarter, driven mainly by high-end GeForce gaming products, while Tegra Processor revenue fell to $129 million due to lower OEM smartphone and tablet sales, partly offset by automotive, development services and SHIELD revenue. NVIDIA recorded $97 million in restructuring and other charges for the first nine months related to winding down Icera modem operations and expected additional charges of $25 million to $35 million in the fourth quarter. The company repurchased shares, paid dividends, disclosed ongoing patent litigation involving Samsung and Qualcomm, and announced a subsequent $135 million accelerated share repurchase agreement.

Embodiments describe a display device including a substrate, pixel and opposing electrodes, a thin-film encapsulation portion with alternating organic and inorganic layers, and a planarization layer on the encapsulation portion. The planarization layer covers an edge portion of the encapsulation portion whose height gradually decreases, and its edge side surface forms a larger angle with the substrate than the encapsulation edge, for example about 70 degrees or more. This structure maximizes a flat upper surface for forming patterns such as on-cell touch electrodes or touch wiring.

The encapsulation portion blocks moisture and oxygen from reaching the light-emitting device layer, while inorganic layers cover organic encapsulation layers to reduce moisture penetration. The planarization layer may be formed across the entire encapsulation portion or only near its edge, may include organic material, and may have a flat or curved edge surface. Patterns formed on the planarization layer can include capacitive touch sensors with touch electrodes and wiring arranged in display and peripheral areas. The planarization layer helps reduce touch dead space and parasitic capacitance between the touch sensor pattern and underlying opposing electrode.

The passage outlines defensive requirements for stopping the UCLA offense, especially high post rub cuts, down screens, and low post action. It presents two main strategies: Basic NBA Show & Recover and All Out SOS Disruption. In Show & Recover, defenders avoid switching, force the cutter behind the high post screen, have the big defender show and bump the cutter, then recover to denial positions while weakside defenders pack the lane. In the final matchup, defenders pressure the ball, deny passes, and push post players off the block. In SOS Disruption, the defense initiates pressure by trapping the wing on the first pass, exploiting the point guard’s cut to the low post. Defenders rotate into denial and help positions, close out on cross-court passes, and match up using SOS principles, with rotations occurring as the ball leaves the passer’s hands.

The Court of Claims awarded compensation for New York State’s appropriation of parts of claimant’s approximately 365-acre property near Massena for the St. Lawrence River project. The property was partly zoned agricultural and partly industrial, with no improvements and prior easements.

The State appropriated: about 183 acres north of Middle Road in 1955; a 0.15-acre flooding easement in 1956; 25.34 acres in fee in 1957; and a 55.38-acre transmission-line easement in 1957. Claimant sought $309,000, while the State valued damages between $28,000 and $40,000.

The court considered whether project-related increases in value could be included, discussing United States v. Miller and related cases. It found no sufficient evidence that the first appropriated parcel was probably within the project area, so project-enhanced value was excluded. For later appropriations south of Middle Road, the court found the land was adjacent property not originally probably to be taken, so enhanced market value from proximity could be considered.

The court awarded: $32,000 for Parcels 185 and 148; $100 for Parcel 2202; $39,750 for Parcel 2159, including direct and consequential damages; and $27,700 for Parcel 2169. Interest was granted for specified periods. The total principal award was $99,550.

A Supreme Court majority appeared inclined to reverse lower court rulings that Rep. Michael Bost lacked standing to challenge an Illinois law allowing mail-in ballots postmarked by Election Day to be counted up to 14 days later. The central issue was what standing test should apply in election-law cases. Paul Clement argued candidates should be able to challenge material election changes, but Justice Elena Kagan suggested a narrower standard requiring a showing that the rule creates an electoral disadvantage, without proving likely defeat. Justices Sotomayor and Jackson questioned Bost’s standing because the rule could not cause him to lose his safe seat. Illinois Solicitor General Jane Notz initially said Kagan’s test was acceptable but later clarified that reduced victory margin alone should not suffice. Justice Kavanaugh raised concerns that denying pre-election standing would force challenges into post-election litigation, where remedies could be difficult.

The study investigates how microstructural components affect electrical resistivity in Al-Mg-Si alloys using microscale four-point probe measurements inside an SEM, alongside XRD, SEM/EDS, EBSD, and bulk Van der Pauw resistivity measurements. Three main alloy compositions were prepared and heat treated under different annealing conditions to stabilize non-coherent precipitates.

XRD and microscopy showed Al solid solution with Si and Mg2Si precipitates, whose volume fraction increased with Mg and Si content. Bulk resistivity generally increased as Al content decreased, while heat treatment affected resistivity similarly across compositions, with 350°C for 72 h giving the lowest values.

Microscale measurements showed that grain interior resistivity, including Al solid solution and nano-precipitates, depended on heat treatment rather than overall alloy composition. Measurements across individual Si and Mg2Si precipitates found that both phases contributed similarly to resistivity, regardless of precipitate type or shape. The study concludes that Al-Mg-Si alloy resistivity scales linearly with total Mg and Si solute content, with coefficients dependent on heat treatment, and that precipitate volume fraction is more important than precipitate identity.

Y-Cross is a drop-back Air Raid concept used across football from varied formations, with or without play action, and against many coverages. It functions as a weak-side flood concept built around a post, deep crosser, and running back flat/check-down, with backside route tags such as smash, curl-flat, or dig. The crossing route can be run by a tight end or slot receiver depending on personnel.

The concept is effective against man coverage because the post and crosser run away from defenders, and against Cover 4 because the boundary safety may be involved in the run fit, creating space for the post. It is less favorable against Cover 3 because the post safety occupies the middle of the field. Quarterback progression is typically post, deep crosser, then running back check-down or backside dig, with high-low reads on safeties and linebackers. Variations include post-wheel combinations and curl-flat tags, allowing offenses to tailor the concept to personnel and quarterback ability.

Bitcoin rose to a six-week high Tuesday, gaining 4.4 percent to $9,340.88, as reports of major financial institutions exploring cryptocurrency boosted sentiment. Gains lifted other cryptocurrencies, raising total digital currency market capitalization to $427 billion, the highest since early March. Reports cited Goldman Sachs hiring a head of digital asset markets, Barclays gauging client interest in a crypto trading desk, and a Thomson Reuters survey showing one in five financial institutions considering cryptocurrency trading within 12 months. Trading volume reached $28 billion over 24 hours, though participants noted ongoing regulatory challenges.

DWI arrests in Wichita Falls have decreased, with 25 arrests from Jan. 1 to March 19 this year compared with 39 in 2016 and 38 in 2017. Sgt. Harold McClure said people may better understand the need for sober drivers. Ridesharing services like Uber and Lyft, which arrived last summer, may also be contributing to the decline.

The passage outlines EUR/USD trading concepts, strategies, risks, and tools. It describes EUR/USD as the world’s most traded and highly liquid currency pair, influenced by Eurozone and U.S. economic conditions, interest rates, inflation, central bank policies, employment data, GDP, geopolitical events, news releases, and market sentiment.

It emphasizes building a trading strategy using technical analysis, fundamental analysis, sentiment analysis, strict rules, and backtesting. Mentioned tools include moving averages, Fibonacci retracements, support and resistance, candlestick patterns, volatility indicators, trend indicators, and correlation analysis. The passage repeatedly recommends backtesting strategies and using demo accounts before live trading.

Trading styles discussed include position trading, swing trading, day trading, scalping, breakout trading, carry trades, hedging, CFD trading, and diversified forex pair trading. It notes that scalping and day trading are difficult, many traders lose money, and forex trading is largely described as highly competitive and difficult.

Risk management themes include proper position sizing, limiting leverage, using or testing stop-loss orders, managing volatility, trading uncorrelated strategies, and avoiding excessive risk per trade. Broker selection considerations include regulation, security, platform quality, fees, account minimums, and customer support.

The passage identifies the European and U.S. session overlap as a key period for EUR/USD trading, especially around 12:00–16:00 GMT in summer or 13:00–17:00 GMT in winter. It also explains that EUR/USD quotes the euro as the base currency and U.S. dollar as the quote currency, while USD/EUR reverses this relationship. Common mistakes include lack of discipline, poor risk management, excessive leverage, no backtested plan, inadequate diversification, and not practicing with a demo account.

The Trump administration’s proposed $100,000 fee for new H-1B visas could affect colleges and universities, which employed more than 16,000 approved H-1B workers as of June 30. The program helps institutions hire academic staff, researchers and doctors, often tied to medical centers. At least 930 institutions had H-1B employees, with nearly half of approvals concentrated at 50 institutions. The proposal does not apply to current visa holders, and it remains unclear whether universities will be subject to the fee. Higher education advocates argue research and medical hires serve the national interest, while experts warn the fee could hinder colleges’ ability to fill key roles.

The study presents a bibliometric analysis of artificial intelligence in STEM education from 2020 to 2024 using citation analysis. Data were collected from the Dimensions database with the keywords “artificial intelligence” and “STEM education,” yielding 101 documents, of which 35 journal articles were analyzed using Microsoft Excel and VOSviewer.

The passage describes AI’s role in education and STEM education, including personalized learning, adaptive systems, analytics, assessment, instructional automation, teacher support, and administrative assistance. It also notes challenges such as ethical concerns, data privacy, learner autonomy, AI literacy, and potential issues when AI dominates monitoring and control of learning.

Results show that publications and citations increased notably in 2024, with 15 publications receiving 234 citations, averaging 15.62 citations per publication. The United States led in documents and citations, with 9 documents and 103 citations, followed by China with 5 documents and no citations. The most cited authors were Nesra Yannier, Kenneth R. Koedinger, and Scott E. Hudson, each with one article cited 55 times. The most cited journal was the International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education, with 55 citations. The most cited article was “Active Learning is About More Than Hands-On: A Mixed-Reality AI System to Support STEM Education,” also with 55 citations. Carnegie Mellon University was the most cited institution.

The study concludes that AI in STEM education is a growing research area with potential to improve learning outcomes, engagement, and teaching support, while requiring attention to ethical implementation, AI literacy, and ongoing evaluation.

Natural disasters cannot be prevented, but their health impacts can be reduced through stronger preparation and infrastructure. Hurricanes Maria, Harvey and Irma caused widespread hazards, including power loss, contaminated floodwaters, toxic chemical releases, mold, mosquito-borne disease risks, unstable structures, downed power lines, heat-related dangers for elderly residents, mental stress, housing loss and economic damage. The passage argues that better prevention, public education, hardened infrastructure, secured industrial sites, stronger seawalls, tree trimming and storm-resistant electrical grids could reduce harm before, during and after disasters. Florida had made some utility improvements before Irma, but the storm still cut power to half the state’s customers.

Investing.com highlights market pressures from seasonal weakness, thin liquidity, tax-loss selling, institutional rebalancing, and fading earnings optimism. The passage discusses technical views on TLT, yields, the dollar, commodities, gold, and market risk indicators, while noting divergence between growth and value. It also includes market headlines, promotional content, and trading risk disclosures.

At the California Democrats’ convention in San Diego, no gubernatorial or U.S. Senate candidate reached the 60% threshold for endorsement, but two Democrats in targeted Orange County House races won state party backing. Dave Min received the endorsement in the race against Rep. Mimi Walters after opponents forced a floor challenge, but party Chairman Eric Bauman ruled the endorsement stood. Hans Keirstead was endorsed in the race against Rep. Dana Rohrabacher despite efforts by five Democratic rivals to block him. Endorsements allow candidates to appear as party-backed choices on sample ballots and aid campaign messaging. In other targeted Southern California GOP districts, Mike Levin, Bryan Caforio and Jay Chen led local endorsement votes but fell short of thresholds. Delegates favored Kevin de León over Sen. Dianne Feinstein, while Gavin Newsom led the governor endorsement vote but also fell short.

A Tennessee mother’s Facebook video of her son Keaton describing bullying at school drew widespread support after gaining over 18 million views. Keaton said classmates insulted him and mistreated him. A fundraising page for his education raised over $29,000, and athletes and entertainers, including Delanie Walker, Tyler Byrd, Kelsea Ballerini, Dale Earnhardt Jr. and Snoop Dogg, offered support.

Gunmen kidnapped 52 farmers, mostly Uzbeks, from three villages in Darz Ab district, Jowzjan province, Afghanistan, while they worked on their land. Provincial police blamed Taliban fighters controlling much of the district and said elders and the police chief were seeking their release, with an operation possible if talks fail. The Taliban said it could not confirm the report. The motive was unclear.

European scientists are promoting October 10 as International Coccolithophore Day to raise awareness of coccolithophores, microscopic ocean algae that regulate carbon, produce oxygen, support marine food webs, and leave climate records through calcium carbonate plates that become deep-sea sediments, chalk, and limestone. Five institutions are leading the effort, highlighting research on their role in carbon storage, ocean chemistry, ecosystems, viruses, bacteria, aerosols, and fossil records. Scientists warn that climate change is altering seawater conditions and threatening these organisms, with potential consequences for marine ecosystems and climate stability.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K dated June 28, 2021, reporting that it completed a simplification of its corporate structure by repatriating economic rights of certain non-U.S. intellectual property to the United States through domestication of a foreign subsidiary. The company updated its second-quarter fiscal 2022 tax outlook, expecting GAAP and non-GAAP tax rates of 13%, plus or minus 1%, excluding discrete items, up from 10%. The domestication is expected to produce a discrete tax benefit of approximately $250 million to $300 million in the quarter. NVIDIA stated the move aligns its corporate structure with its operating structure and related tax law developments.

This study compared prodromal symptoms and drug prescriptions before diagnoses of Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, and dementia with Lewy bodies using UK THIN primary care data, with selected replication in UK Biobank. The THIN cohort included 20,214 Alzheimer’s patients, 28,222 Parkinson’s patients, 4,682 dementia with Lewy bodies patients, and 20,214 controls.

All three disorders showed higher rates of multiple health conditions than controls in the five years before diagnosis. Memory problems were more frequent before Alzheimer’s disease, tremor before Parkinson’s disease, and hallucinations, confusion, falls, depression, autonomic dysfunction, constipation, urinary disorders, and hypotension were especially associated with dementia with Lewy bodies. Constipation and autonomic dysfunction were stronger before Parkinson’s disease and dementia with Lewy bodies than before Alzheimer’s disease.

Treatments for depression, anxiety, and constipation were more often prescribed before all three diagnoses, while several antihypertensive and antidiabetic medications were less often prescribed. Statins were less often prescribed before Parkinson’s disease than before Alzheimer’s disease, a finding replicated in UK Biobank. Among Parkinson’s patients, prior prescriptions for hypercholesterolemia, constipation, depression, and psychosis were associated with a dementia diagnosis within five years after Parkinson’s diagnosis.

The authors conclude that neurodegenerative diseases have long prodromal phases visible in primary care records, and that lipid-lowering therapies may have differing associations across these disorders, requiring further study.

Tesla Motors filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2015. The company designs, manufactures and sells fully electric vehicles, powertrain components and Tesla Energy products. It had delivered over 78,000 Model S vehicles through June 30, 2015, planned Model X customer deliveries late in Q3 2015, and aimed to begin Model 3 deliveries in late 2017.

For Q2 2015, total revenue was $955.0 million, up from $769.3 million in Q2 2014, driven mainly by increased Model S deliveries. Gross profit was $213.4 million, while gross margin declined to 22.3% from 27.7%. Net loss was $184.2 million, compared with $61.9 million a year earlier. For the first six months of 2015, revenue was $1.89 billion and net loss was $338.4 million.

As of June 30, 2015, Tesla had $6.47 billion in total assets, $5.70 billion in total liabilities, and $715.9 million in stockholders’ equity. Cash and cash equivalents were $1.15 billion, down from $1.91 billion at December 31, 2014. Inventory rose to $1.21 billion, and property, plant and equipment increased to $2.65 billion. Operating cash flow for the first six months of 2015 was negative $291.3 million, investing cash flow was negative $855.2 million, and financing cash flow was positive $404.5 million.

Tesla expected 2015 deliveries of 50,000 to 55,000 Model S and Model X vehicles and planned about $1.5 billion in 2015 capital expenditures. It continued expanding production capacity, stores, service centers, the Supercharger network and the Gigafactory in Nevada. The company also reported legal proceedings, including a securities class action lawsuit dismissed with prejudice in 2014, with plaintiffs’ appeal pending.

Gold trading involves speculating on gold prices for profit through futures, options, spot markets, stocks, CFDs, and ETFs, usually with cash settlement rather than physical delivery. Gold is also used as a store of value, status symbol, hedge, and “safe haven” asset. Its price can fluctuate due to supply, demand, and political, social, and economic unrest.

The passage outlines gold’s historical use, from ancient Egypt to gold-backed currencies, the Bretton Woods system, and later futures and online trading. It states that gold is difficult to trade because it depends heavily on macro news, but some strategies have worked over time.

The article focuses on a gold weekend swing trading strategy using GLD from late 2004 to September 2021. Basic Thursday-to-Friday and Thursday-close-to-Monday-open tests showed limited tradability, but adding one simple parameter improved results enough for a small position. The passage concludes that commodities and gold swing trading are difficult, though the weekend gold strategy shows promise.

Investing.com page featuring market headlines and an article arguing that gold’s recent rally has not been matched by silver, platinum, or mining stocks, which the author views as bearish. The article says GDXJ remained below its April closing high, the USD Index is verifying a bullish inverse head-and-shoulders breakout, and stocks show bearish signals despite a short-term pause. It compares current conditions to 2008 and includes promotional stock-screening content, reader comments, related headlines, and trading risk disclosures.

Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones was fined $250,000 by the NFL for an “inadvertent” obscene gesture toward fans at MetLife Stadium during Dallas’ 37-22 win. Jones said he meant to give a thumbs-up to Cowboys fans after a touchdown. The Cowboys are likely to appeal and have until Friday to decide.

A review of the latest Voluntary National Reviews from 18 Eastern Mediterranean Region countries assessed reporting on health-related SDG targets and indicators. All reviewed VNRs described mechanisms for monitoring SDG progress, and 11 reported on all 17 SDGs, with higher-income countries tending to report more comprehensively. Seventeen VNRs said targets and indicators were prioritized or adapted nationally, but only eight explicitly mentioned 2030 country targets.

Data availability was a major challenge. Nine VNRs discussed data availability, and 14 cited limited data as a challenge to monitoring and reporting, often linked to limited human resource capacity, low data quality, lack of statistical tools, limited transparency, and insufficient disaggregation. Reporting on health indicators varied by indicator type and income level. Maternal mortality, neonatal mortality, and under-5 mortality were the most commonly reported SDG3 indicators, while trend reporting was limited; Qatar was the only country reporting trends across all SDG3 indicators.

The study found that reporting was higher for indicators derived from disease surveillance and civil registration and vital statistics systems than for routine health information systems and national surveys. It concludes that while countries showed commitment to the SDGs, weak health information systems, limited data availability, and analytical capacity constrain monitoring. Strengthening regulatory frameworks, civil registration and vital statistics systems, population-based surveys, and data collection capacity is needed to improve access to quality data for health-related SDGs.

A rare white moose filmed in Värmland, Sweden, drew global attention. The BBC reported Sweden has about 100 such moose, whose white fur comes from a genetic mutation rather than albinism. Social media users compared it to mythical creatures and fantasy characters. The status of twin white calves as albino or piebald is unknown.

The speaker says tomorrow’s game is important, but the series is long. Their team must regroup, improve the power play, and avoid letups after controlling early play but allowing the opponent to battle back in the third period.

Princeton researchers and collaborators developed Diag2Diag, an AI tool that uses data from existing fusion diagnostics to generate detailed synthetic readings for sensors that are missing, limited, or unable to measure certain plasma regions. Tested with DIII-D data, it could improve plasma monitoring and control, reduce hardware needs, and make future fusion reactors more compact, reliable, and less costly. The tool is especially useful for studying the plasma edge, or pedestal, where stability affects performance. Diag2Diag also provided evidence supporting the magnetic island theory for suppressing edge-localized modes using resonant magnetic perturbations. Researchers plan to expand its use to other fusion diagnostics and fields with limited sensor data.

The passage lists AI content generator and writing tools for 2022, describing their uses, features, limitations, and pricing. Tools covered include Jasper, Copy.ai, Frase, Article Forge, Rytr, CopySmith, Hypotenuse, Kafkai, and Peppertype. Features discussed include SEO optimization, plagiarism checks, templates, multilingual support, long-form writing, product descriptions, content briefs, and integrations. The article concludes that AI writers can help create content more efficiently and recommends choosing a tool based on requirements and budget, while favoring Jasper.

The ADS868xW ADC integrates a high-bandwidth, low-noise, stable ADC input driver and supports internal or external 4.096V references selected through the INTREF_DIS bit in RANGE_SEL_REG. The internal reference is enabled by default, requires at least 4.7µF decoupling on REFIO, and should not drive external loads without a buffer. Reference accuracy can shift after solder reflow due to thermal stress; placing the device in the second reflow pass can reduce exposure. External reference mode uses REFIO as an input and the internal buffer drives REFCAP, which requires at least 10µF plus a nearby 1µF capacitor.

The device supports single-ended and differential bipolar or unipolar ranges with straight-binary output. It provides input and AVDD alarms on a configurable multifunction pin. Input alarm thresholds and hysteresis are programmable; AVDD alarms use fixed typical thresholds of 4.7V and 5.3V. Alarm flags are available through the pin, ALARM_REG, or appended output data.

The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI, dual-SDO, source-synchronous read modes, and daisy-chain operation. Devices appear to the host as 32-bit input-output shift registers. Functional states are RESET, ACQ, and CONV, controlled by RST and CONVST/CS. Reset can be application reset or power-on reset. Data frames begin on CONVST/CS falling edge and end on its rising edge; 32 clocks form an optimal frame, fewer clocks create a short read-only frame, and more clocks create a long frame using the last 32 input bits as the command.

The device has nine configuration registers for device ID, reset and power control, input and output protocol control, output data formatting, range and reference selection, alarm status, and alarm thresholds. Output data can include conversion results, register data, fixed patterns, device address, range flags, alarm flags, and parity.

Application guidance describes using ADS868xW in industrial analog input modules with external multiplexing, programmable voltage and current inputs, alarm-based temperature monitoring, supply decoupling, and PCB layout separation of analog and digital sections. The device supports NAP and power-down modes for reduced power consumption. AVDD and DVDD supplies require proper decoupling, and reference pins require specified capacitors for stable performance.

Origin PC announced a new Eon15-S gaming laptop starting at $999, using Nvidia’s GeForce 1050Ti graphics card. The base model includes an Intel Core i3 processor and 120GB SSD, with upgrades available for a Core i5 and more storage. It also features an IPS display and 24/7 US-based lifetime support.

The Supreme Court declined to hear Ghislaine Maxwell’s appeal challenging charges tied to a 2007 non-prosecution agreement with Jeffrey Epstein. Maxwell argued the agreement’s protection for “potential co-conspirators” bound all U.S. attorney’s offices, but the 2nd Circuit held it applied only to the district that made the deal unless stated otherwise. The solicitor general argued the agreement was unusual and not worthy of Supreme Court review.

The 5-Day Low of The Range Strategy goes long when IBS is below 0.25 and the close is below the lowest low of the previous five days, then exits after five days. From January 1993 to today, it produced 517 trades, 309 winners, a 60% win ratio, and an average return of 0.46% per trade, above the 0.11% average return for any five-day period. Profitability peaks over 3–7 days, with a 10.76% annualized return when exiting after five days, though recent performance has weakened. The strategy can be adapted for short selling using range criteria such as 0.75 or 0.9, but short results are less profitable.

The study evaluated the MicroGEM Sal6830™ SARS-CoV-2 Saliva Test, a point-of-care RT-PCR platform using patient self-collected saliva in a sealed cartridge, intended to reduce turnaround time, sample handling, operator exposure, and reliance on nasopharyngeal swabs. Clinical performance and usability studies were conducted at two U.S. health clinics with non-laboratory trained healthcare workers.

Blinded sample testing used 48 saliva samples, including verified negative saliva and positives spiked at 1.9 × the Sal6830™ limit of detection. All negative and positive results matched expectations except one positive sample that returned an invalid result. In a prospective clinical comparison, 119 participants provided both saliva for Sal6830™ testing and nasopharyngeal swabs for Cepheid Xpert Xpress CoV-2/Flu/RSV testing. Sal6830™ showed 87.2% positive percent agreement, 97.2% negative percent agreement, and 93.3% overall agreement with the comparator.

Nine healthcare workers completed usability questionnaires and reported that the Sal6830™ was easy to use, results were easy to interpret, and technical support was not needed. The study concluded that non-laboratory trained healthcare workers could use the Sal6830™ accurately and confidently in point-of-care settings.
Division Three reversed and remanded State v. Nelson on July 3, 2014.

Neural Radiance Cache is a neural shader that trains tiny neural networks on live game data to cache and approximate radiance. It uses path-traced rays after one bounce to infer many-bounce lighting, reducing GPU workload while improving global illumination, dynamic lighting, indirect light quality, scalability, and adaptability in challenging scenarios.

A voice-directed inspection system supports multiple inspectors inspecting business assets. A host computer or site computer provides an inspection plan divided into sections. Inspection assistance devices, including portable computers and headsets, request assignments, receive unfinished sections, provide audible commands, collect spoken updates, and send completion updates to a site computer. The site computer determines whether multiple unfinished sections are available, assigns sections to different devices, and forwards updates to the host computer. Inspection plans may be edited, converted between text and speech, prioritized, and divided by asset parts, systems, or noninterfering work areas.

The speaker is thrilled to have won the Stanley Cup, praises Buffalo’s strong young team, and reflects on the grueling playoff run after missing the previous year. They emphasize the team’s perseverance through adversity and injuries, noting contributions from players like Hull and Mike, and credit the veteran group’s experience and determination.

The passage discusses criticism of Bruen’s two-step Second Amendment test, which requires courts to assess constitutional text and historical firearm regulation. Critics argue judges lack historians’ expertise, but the author says judges are lawyers who routinely answer historical legal questions. The author argues Bruen’s text inquiry is often manageable, while historical-tradition disputes may require more work but rely on durable legal sources. When history is uncertain, legal burdens of proof help courts decide cases. The passage contrasts this with Justice Breyer’s proposed means-ends scrutiny, which Bruen rejected as improper lawmaking.

In the UK, many ovarian cancer cases are diagnosed late, with nearly half of recently diagnosed women first presenting as emergency cases and fewer than one third diagnosed at stage 1 or 2. Jo Stanford of Ovarian Cancer Action says delays can stem from limited symptom awareness, difficulty accessing appointments, and symptoms being dismissed. There is no routine screening test for ovarian cancer, and a smear test does not detect it.

The four main symptoms highlighted are persistent bloating, difficulty eating or feeling full quickly, needing to urinate more often or urgently, and persistent tummy or pelvic pain. Other possible signs include lower back aches, digestive discomfort, unexpected bleeding after menopause, and unusual tiredness. Stanford advises people to seek medical advice if symptoms are regular or unusual for them.

Ovarian Cancer Action offers a free online symptom checker and downloadable symptoms diary to help people track symptoms and discuss them with a doctor. Early detection is associated with a 95% survival chance, compared with 16% for stage four disease. Stanford stresses that symptom awareness can support earlier diagnosis and that family, friends, and others can encourage women to seek medical help.

DryShips reported in an April 17 6-K that it raised $14.5 million through the issuance of 7,912,449 shares at an average price of $1.79, below the $30 million requested through Kalani Investors. The issuance increased shares outstanding to 54.92 million and caused 16.8% dilution. The article says market demand for the stock remains weak, with $173.4 million still to be issued under the current prospectus supplement versus a $106 million equity market capitalization at the April 17 close. At the recent issuance pace of about $3.2 million per day, completing the remaining offering would take about 54 trading days and require issuing an estimated 105.7 million additional shares, causing substantial dilution. The author argues DryShips may need debt financing to support acquisitions but could continue equity issuance after any stock price rebound. The author discloses no current position but may initiate a long position and actively trade the stock.

The lecture introduces a “decision mentality” for poker: evaluate decisions by expected value rather than outcomes, because luck can make bad decisions win and good decisions lose in the short term. The professor illustrates this with credit card roulette and a story about accidentally finding money after making a mistake.

Three levels of poker reasoning are described. Level one is putting an opponent on a specific hand, which is criticized as unreliable. Level two, or exploitative play, compares one’s hand against an opponent’s range and tendencies, using pot odds and equity calculations. Level three, or optimal play, compares one’s range against an opponent’s range and aims to prevent exploitation, similar to Nash equilibrium reasoning. Rock-paper-scissors is used to contrast exploitative and optimal strategies.

The lecture explains why blinds are necessary: without forced money in the pot, players would rarely enter hands, similar to a “Who’s Taller?” game where only the tallest should participate. Stack size should be measured in big blinds, and effective stack size depends on the stacks of opponents still able to contest the hand.

Position is defined relative to the blinds and dealer button. Later positions can play more hands because fewer players remain to contest the blinds. Equity is introduced as the probability or share of the pot a hand has, calculated from remaining cards, opponent hand ranges, or tools such as PokerStove.

For tournament play, the professor recommends raising rather than calling when no one has entered the pot, usually to about 2.25 big blinds, and going all in when effective stacks are small. Antes make stealing blinds more valuable and widen playable ranges. Beginner mistakes include calling instead of raising unopened pots and being too afraid to go all in pre-flop.

Suggested opening ranges are tight in early position and widen substantially toward the button and small blind. The professor notes these ranges are conservative and may be predictable, but useful for beginners. The lecture concludes with example all-in equity and calling calculations using Nash-style ranges and a live demonstration of how equities change across flop, turn, and river.

Hurricane Maria struck Puerto Rico on September 20, 2017, causing severe wind, flooding, infrastructure damage, power loss for 3.4 million people, over $82 billion in damages, and major agricultural losses. The passage discusses excess mortality after emergencies and notes limitations in prior Hurricane Maria mortality studies, including short follow-up, limited causes of death, and lack of adjustment for population displacement.

The research proposes a semiparametric Poisson regression model to estimate deaths associated with the emergency by cause and post-emergency period. The model incorporates population size, displacement, annual trends, within-year mortality variation, causes of death, and interactions between cause and emergency period. It uses penalized likelihood and restricted maximum likelihood to estimate parameters and allows estimation of excess deaths by comparing predicted deaths under post-emergency and pre-emergency conditions.
NASA is considering using the HAMMER spacecraft to deflect or destroy hazardous asteroids like Bennu, which has a 1 in 2,700 chance of hitting Earth in 2135. Bennu has been monitored since 1999.

Dylan Drysdale, Tim Loughran and Garry Cullum won class titles at the final round of the 2017 Molecule ProKart Series at KartSport Hamilton’s Agrisea Raceway. In Wifiplus KZ2, Aaron Wilson won the Final and round, but Drysdale secured the series title by four points over Wilson, with Mat Kinsman third. Kinsman had earlier won all three heats and the Pre-Final before contact ended his Final. In Aarque Group KZ2 Masters, Tim Loughran won the round and series after Enrico van der Griend crashed in heat three; Brett Hollander finished second overall and van der Griend third. In KZ2 Restricted, Garry Cullum won all races after qualifying to claim the round and his fourth series title, ahead of Regan Hall and Aaron Wooley.

Hendrik Bessembinder’s 2017 study found that most U.S. stocks from 1926 to 2015 did not outperform one-month Treasury Bills; only 43% did, and a small number of stocks generated much of the market’s gains. The passage argues that while stock market averages have been strong, the median stock has performed poorly, making individual stock selection difficult. A similar study of the Oslo Stock Exchange from 1985 to 2017 found that only 18 large companies accounted for all value creation. The passage concludes that most stocks do not outperform Treasury Bills and recommends passive funds or strong diversification for individual stock investors.

At higher levels of soccer, if a player may be injured and the referee allows play to continue, players may show sportsmanship by kicking the ball out of bounds to stop play when there is no immediate threat on goal. After treatment, play restarts with a throw-in for the opposing team, which is expected to return the ball to the team that kicked it out, usually backward toward a defender. Neither team should exploit this courtesy, and play should resume only after the receiving defender has possession. Similar etiquette applies to dropped balls after injury stoppages, with possession restored fairly before normal play continues.

The passage discusses e-Maintenance as a key component of e-Manufacturing and e-Business, enabling predictive maintenance, near-zero downtime, real-time monitoring, performance assessment, and integration with tools such as ERP, CRM, and e-commerce systems. It identifies research needs including predictive intelligence, degradation detection, data mining, secure informatics platforms, web-based optimization, training, and enterprise culture development.

It also presents a reconfigurable maintenance concept for enterprises, linking product quality, system configuration, tolerance assignment, maintenance policy, reliability, and production costs. Shared diagnostic knowledge and service activities among companies can improve reconfiguration efficiency and support reliability, sustainability, serviceability, and lifecycle safeguarding.

The modular reconfigurable maintenance system uses distributed communication, monitoring modules, sensors, historical data, and expert systems to detect adverse conditions, identify faults, support preventive and corrective actions, and expand a knowledge base. The conclusion states that competitive pressures and mass customization require companies to respond quickly and cost-effectively, making integrated reconfigurable maintenance necessary for maintaining production quality and reliability.

Teachers’ Union of Ireland general secretary John MacGabhann warned teachers against becoming Facebook friends with students, saying it can undermine professional distance and create risks through photos or comments taken out of context. He urged teachers to be cautious on social media, avoid hasty or angry posts, and stay out of online disputes. He also criticised employers who use technology and social media to expect constant staff availability, advising members not to respond to unreasonable contact outside obligations.

The author argues that bearish views on U.S. equities may be premature, noting that market breadth is showing underlying strength despite concerns about low VIX levels and complacency. The article presents 21 charts to challenge pessimistic forecasts. The author discloses long positions in U.S. equities and VIX and states the content is not investment advice.

The speaker expresses gratitude for the people’s confidence and acknowledges the responsibilities of executing federal laws, managing foreign and state relations, revenue, military forces, and communications with the legislature. He pledges to respect constitutional limits, preserve peace and friendship with foreign nations, respect state powers, practice strict economy, reduce the national debt, and ensure accountability in public spending. He supports equitable revenue measures favoring agriculture, commerce, and manufacturing, along with constitutionally permitted internal improvements and education. He opposes enlarging the standing army, supports naval and military improvements, and emphasizes the national militia as the chief defense. He promises a just and humane policy toward Indian tribes, reform of abuses in federal patronage and appointments, selection of diligent and capable public officers, cooperation with other branches of government, and reliance on divine guidance.

VentureWire’s May 17, 2001 newsletter reports that Tahoe Networks launched with a $38 million first round led by Redpoint Ventures with Accel Partners, while Startups.com became Startups Inc., shifted from an accelerator to market intelligence, and cut 11 of 35 employees. Hermes Pensions Management said BTPS allocated $965 million for private company and fund investments, and OffRoad Capital split into OffRoad Technologies and OffRoad Capital while cutting half its staff.

New financing items include investments in Algorx, Alphamosaic, Comlase, Xora, e.Intelligence, Foundstone, Yube, White Amber, Beyond Genomics, Cpocket, Embark, and 3G Infrastructure. Bad-news items include Eazel ceasing operations after failing to secure funding and RoundArch cutting 12% of North American staff.

Product and company updates include launches or changes by Compete, Wireless Intellect Labs, Sightward, and Impart Technology. M&A activity includes acquisitions involving All Bases Covered, Princeton eCom, printCafe, Lost Boys, Pitman, Bignose.com, and eKit.com. Executive and personnel changes include appointments at Clarity, SmartBargains, Creative Planet, CyLex, Zone Labs, PrivateExpress, EVLogix, Encompass Ventures, and Atlas Venture. Bezeq and Discount Capital Markets are establishing a $50 million communications-focused venture fund.

The passage examines how education policies in the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus have been shaped by historical developments, Council decisions, and the discourses of TRNC Presidents. It states that education has served not only academic purposes but also the construction and preservation of Turkish Cypriot identity, particularly through history, language, and cultural curricula.

The Turkish Cypriot education system evolved through the Ottoman, British colonial, Republic of Cyprus, and post-1974 periods. After 1974 and the 1983 declaration of the TRNC, education was restructured in close cooperation with Turkey, with emphasis on national identity. Council decisions influenced reforms in teacher training, curricula, school infrastructure, textbook revision, higher education, and educational quality.

The passage highlights the role of history textbooks in shaping collective identity. For many years, textbooks emphasized Turkish Cypriot victimization and Turkish-Greek conflict, contributing to polarization. Since the early 2000s, EU harmonization efforts and bicommunal projects encouraged more pluralistic and reconciliatory approaches, though reforms faced political and social resistance.

Presidential discourses are presented as central to education policy. Rauf Denktaş emphasized national identity and integration with Turkey; Mehmet Ali Talat focused on European harmonization and modernization; Derviş Eroğlu stressed cooperation with Turkey and technical education; Mustafa Akıncı emphasized multiculturalism and dialogue; and Ersin Tatar prioritized national identity and integration with Turkey.

The passage concludes that TRNC education policies should be based on political independence, scientific neutrality, long-term strategy, multi-perspective history curricula, cooperation with Turkey, local needs, and educational autonomy.

A letter attributed to fired assistant U.S. attorney Michael Ben’Ary said his termination followed a false social media post while he was prosecuting a terrorism case tied to the 2021 Afghanistan airport bombing. The letter criticized Justice Department leadership, saying it was prioritizing punishment of President Trump’s perceived enemies over national security. Ben’Ary was reportedly fired after commentator Julie Kelly suggested he was an ally of former Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco and part of internal resistance to the indictment of James Comey.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said India’s accession to the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation has raised the grouping’s political profile and capacity to stabilise Central and South Asia, including Afghanistan. He praised India’s foreign policy, called for India-Russia trade to reach $30 billion by 2025, and said deeper defence cooperation would increase technology transfer. Lavrov criticised the US strategy in Afghanistan focused on force, saying NATO had failed to curb extremism, terrorism, or drug trade. He denied Russia supported the Taliban, saying contacts were limited to protecting citizens and urging negotiations under UN criteria. He said resolving Afghanistan requires the government, Taliban, neighbours, and influential countries, and supported a smaller group than the Kabul Process.

The speaker says the team must be prepared for an opponent playing to extend the series and force another game. Their focus is on starting well, competing with urgency, and taking the opportunity to end the series, especially given the opponent’s home success.

Malcolm Mitchell, a New England Patriots wide receiver and Super Bowl XVI contributor, will receive the Promise Hero Award from America’s Promise Alliance for his literacy advocacy. Mitchell struggled with reading in college at the University of Georgia and taught himself by starting with children’s books. His experience led him to create Read with Malcolm, a youth literacy initiative that promotes book ownership and reading among students in underserved communities. The organization aims to address low literacy and limited access to age-appropriate books in low-income households. Mitchell, who graduated in communications, was drafted by the Patriots, and wrote The Magician’s Hat, said his goal is to inspire children to read, overcome adversity, and recognize the opportunities literacy can provide.

Yandex will report its financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2018, on July 26, 2018. Management will hold a conference call and webcast that day to discuss second-quarter results. The release includes dial-in, replay, and webcast details, along with company background and investor and media contacts.

DA leader Mmusi Maimane accused President Jacob Zuma and the ANC of using “Radical Economic Transformation” to enrich political elites while neglecting ordinary South Africans, especially unemployed youth. He cited the Esidimeni deaths, Marikana, alleged corruption, security at SONA, land reform, BEE, mining policy and the nuclear deal as examples of government failure and self-enrichment. Maimane described young unemployed and excluded South Africans as a “Lost Generation” and outlined a DA “Rescue Plan” focused on education reform, student funding, apprenticeships, private-sector job creation, support for small businesses, infrastructure, land ownership, policing, healthcare, anti-corruption measures and a leaner state.

The passage argues that the Supreme Court is likely to uphold President Trump’s firing of FTC Commissioner Rebecca Kelly Slaughter but may not overturn Humphrey’s Executor outright. It explains that Humphrey’s Executor upheld FTC independence in 1936 by characterizing the FTC as primarily quasi-legislative and quasi-judicial, not executive. Recent cases, especially Seila Law, have treated that precedent narrowly by examining an agency’s actual powers and structure. The passage notes that the modern FTC has expanded rulemaking and enforcement authority, has become more politically driven, and may now resemble an executive law-enforcement agency more than the FTC described in 1936. It suggests the Court may preserve Humphrey’s Executor in modified form to distinguish agencies exercising executive power from those, such as the Federal Reserve, with different structures and functions.

The passage discusses digital accessibility as an essential requirement for inclusive digital technologies and notes that, despite legal mandates and WCAG guidelines, global compliance remains low. It identifies a major accessibility skills gap among developers, educators, and organizations, linked partly to limited integration of accessibility in computer science curricula, especially in India.

To address this gap, the authors designed and delivered a one-day digital accessibility workshop for software professionals, computer science educators, and UX designers in India. The workshop aimed to build foundational knowledge, introduce legal and technical frameworks such as WCAG, promote disability etiquette and inclusive communication, and encourage accessibility as a shared responsibility. It included five modules: accessibility basics, accessibility design, accessible software engineering, accessibility testing and reporting, and teaching accessibility. Activities included hands-on exploration of assistive technologies, disability simulations, case studies, accessibility tool demonstrations, and lightning talks.

The workshop had 73 participants: 33 software engineers, 28 educators, and 12 UX designers. Most had no prior formal accessibility experience. Feedback was highly positive, with participants rating the workshop as engaging, effective, and practically relevant. Accessibility tools demonstrations received the highest number of exceptional ratings. All participants said they would recommend the workshop, and many reported increased confidence and changed perceptions about accessibility and personal responsibility.

Open-ended feedback identified interest in advanced inclusive design and development, AI and emerging technologies for accessibility, accessibility for diverse users, organizational and policy strategies, and more real-world, practice-based learning. The authors note that some technical sessions were challenging for participants with less technical experience and that simulations should be supplemented or replaced with lived-experience perspectives. They recommend pre-workshop materials, role-specific content, case studies, peer learning, and continued engagement.

The passage concludes that informal, hands-on accessibility workshops can help bridge accessibility knowledge gaps in India’s computing education and professional sectors, but sustained follow-up is needed to assess workplace application.

Alexa can help with cleaning by using the Cleaning Buddy skill to schedule tasks, enabling voice purchasing to order supplies from Amazon, controlling compatible robot vacuums like Roomba or Neato with voice commands, and assisting with laundry through Laundrapp pickup or stain-removal advice from skills like Good Housekeeping or Stains Be Gone.

MIT researchers developed a refined prime editing system that reduces unintended DNA errors by modifying Cas9 proteins and stabilizing the RNA template. The final editor, called vPE, produced error rates about 1/60th of the original, ranging from one in 101 to one in 543 edits in mouse and human cells. The approach does not add delivery complexity or extra steps and could make gene therapy safer and more practical for genetic diseases. The team is also working to improve editor efficiency and tissue-specific delivery.

British police declared a major incident after a man and woman in their 40s were found unconscious in Amesbury and hospitalized in critical condition from exposure to an unknown substance. Counterterrorism officers are working with Wiltshire Police. Amesbury is near Salisbury, where Sergei and Yulia Skripal were poisoned. Police cordoned off sites, said wider risk was not believed, and are investigating whether a crime occurred.

The study investigates surface defects introduced by electropolishing bulk niobium for superconducting radio frequency cavities. Starting from highly mechanically polished Nb samples, the authors used white light interferometry and atomic force microscopy to characterize topographic changes after varying electropolishing removals.

Electropolishing produced intergranular sloped steps at grain boundaries, with step heights up to about 70 nm and local slope angles up to about 50°. Surface roughness generally increased with electropolishing removal, though the results depended strongly on local microstructure and grain orientation. Sequential electropolishing showed that previous steps were smoothed while new steps formed at shifted grain-boundary locations, indicating that the defects arise primarily during the electropolishing process rather than from subsequent electrolyte exposure.

Using London-theory calculations, the authors found that these sloped grain-boundary steps can cause magnetic field enhancement and suppression of the superheating field, reducing the high-field stability of the Meissner state. The defects may therefore limit achievable peak magnetic fields in electropolished bulk Nb more than previously expected. The analysis also showed that such topography can alter shallow impurity diffusion profiles, reducing impurity concentration near regions where vortex penetration is favored.

The study concludes that microscopic surface defects from electropolishing are important limitations for high-gradient SRF cavity performance, and that smoother surfaces and improved polishing processes are needed for fields near or beyond the niobium superheating field and for next-generation SRF materials.

D.A.N. Joint Venture III, L.P. sought to deny Chapter 7 discharge to debtor Ambrozy Jerry Fasolak under Bankruptcy Code § 727(a)(2), (a)(3), (a)(4), and (a)(5). Fasolak, a retired former owner of A & F Corporation, had filed Chapter 13 in Pennsylvania before filing Chapter 7 in Florida. The plaintiff alleged fraudulent transfers or concealment of assets, inadequate records, false oaths, and failure to explain loss of assets.

The court found that although Fasolak made transfers to his wife and had inaccuracies in his bankruptcy filings, the evidence did not prove fraudulent intent. It also found that the plaintiff did not identify missing financial records, did not show that false statements were knowingly and fraudulently made, and did not establish an unexplained loss of specific assets. The court concluded that the plaintiff failed to meet its burden under all asserted grounds.

Final judgment was ordered in favor of Fasolak, and a Chapter 7 discharge was to be entered.

Polo originated in Persia more than 20 centuries ago, later spreading through the Middle East, Central Asia and the Far East. The modern version came from India, where British travelers encountered it and brought it to England before it reached the U.S. Today, about 250 polo clubs operate in 43 states.

The Milwaukee Polo Club, located in Hartland, traces local polo to 1923 and has been at its current site for more than 20 years. Club representative Thomas Esser says MPC aims to counter polo’s elite image by presenting itself as accessible “blue collar” polo, with members including nurses, students, bartenders, retirees, teenagers and seniors. Matches cost $5 to attend, with children admitted free.

Games usually consist of six seven-minute chukkers and last about two hours, including a halftime divot stomp where fans can meet horses and players. Teams include players from Des Moines, the Twin Cities, Chicago, St. Louis and beyond. Outdoor play depends on safe weather and field conditions; if matches are canceled, members may still hold demonstrations and answer questions.

Esser emphasizes horse care, saying players understand their horses’ needs, limit their work, provide rest after hard play and view them as teammates. The club is located at N75 W30311 County Highway VV in Hartland, with more information available by phone or at milwaukeepoloclub.com.

After recent ICE arrests in the Austin area, Austin ISD lawyers instructed staff not to share unvetted resources or discuss political or controversial issues on district property, citing heightened scrutiny from state lawmakers. The memo followed detentions of at least 51 people and reports of student anxiety. School Board Vice President Paul Saldana criticized the memo, saying the board was not briefed and that it contradicted district commitments. Superintendent Paul Cruz posted general immigrant and refugee resources, while Education Austin distributed Know Your Rights materials and lawyer contacts. The union planned a news conference, and board members were set to discuss the memo.

The speaker emphasizes preparation, focus, execution, and living in the present over momentum or carryover. He says losing would be devastating because opportunities to reach this stage are rare in a salary-cap league, especially with injuries and closely matched teams. He stresses the importance of depth, player development, and contributions from younger players, saying teams cannot rely on only one or two players. He discusses seeking favorable matchups, starting well in Pittsburgh, limiting turnovers, and handling the puck better against the forecheck. He says both goalies and teams have been stronger at home, praises Ozzie’s response and professionalism, and notes Hossa appears satisfied with his decision and played well. He describes team building as sacrifice, winning together, and playing for one another, while urging players and families to enjoy the opportunity because it may not come again.

A 13-year-old girl was seriously but stably injured after being shot in the thigh in Guildford, Sydney, on Tuesday night. Police believe the shooting was not random and plan to speak with her when possible.

Sen. Mark Warner said Republicans are trying to undermine Robert Mueller’s investigation and the FBI, citing the Nunes memo as part of a partisan campaign. He said he and Sen. Richard Burr were denied access to the memo before release and criticized the use of classified information. Warner also said the Senate Russia investigation is vital to preventing future cyber threats and argued that President Trump’s failure to acknowledge the threat leaves the country less safe.

Penny stocks are low-priced stocks, often defined by the SEC as stocks below $5, and many trade over the counter or on the Pink Sheets rather than major exchanges. The passage argues that penny stocks are risky because many involve unproven or failing businesses, limited financial disclosure, low liquidity, high volatility, and exposure to scams. OTC and Pink Sheets markets have fewer listing and reporting requirements than exchanges such as NYSE or Nasdaq, making research harder and trading more expensive due to wide bid-ask spreads and commissions.

The passage warns that penny stocks attract traders hoping for quick wealth, but most ultimately fail or become worthless. It identifies common scams, including “know-it-all” gurus selling formulas, pump-and-dump schemes, and company-led dilution schemes. While some traders may accept the risks or allocate a small portion of assets, the passage recommends avoiding penny stocks unless the risks and pitfalls are clearly understood.

The passage studies many-to-one two-sided matching between participants and teams, motivated by applications such as residents–hospitals, students–colleges, and workers–firms. It argues that standard participant-side justified envy-freeness can be unfair to teams, especially when participants are indifferent among teams but teams value participants differently. Existing team-side envy-freeness notions from fair division, such as EF1, may conflict with participant-justified envy-freeness in many-to-one matching.

The authors introduce team-justified EF1, which treats a team’s envy as justified only with respect to participants in another team who do not strictly prefer that other team. Under ordinal preferences with ties, they define stochastic-dominance versions, including team-justified SD-EF1, which imply corresponding additive-valuation notions consistent with the rankings.

Two preliminary approaches are discussed. A restricted round-robin algorithm assigning participants only to top-ranked teams satisfies team-justified SD-EF1 and participant-EF, but may be highly unbalanced. An auxiliary one-to-one matching approach using team slots satisfies team-justified SD-EF1, participant-justified EF, and balancedness, but may fail swap stability.

The main contribution is a polynomial-time algorithm that creates team slots, maintains eligibility sets for participants, repeatedly computes a lexicographically optimal eligible matching, and expands eligibility for unmatched participants. The returned allocation satisfies team-justified SD-EF1, participant-justified EF, balancedness, and Pareto optimality, and therefore swap stability. When all participants are indifferent among teams, the algorithm reduces to round-robin; when all preferences are strict, it reduces to the participant-proposing Gale–Shapley algorithm.

The passage further proves that, with augmented tie-breaking, the main algorithm is group-strategyproof for participants: no group of participants can misreport preferences so that all strictly benefit. The proof uses blocking paths and properties of the algorithm’s lexicographic matching choices.

Finally, the authors extend the framework to teams with quotas and cases where participants or teams may prefer being unassigned. By adding dummy participants and a dummy team, the algorithm yields allocations satisfying stability, extended team-justified SD-EF1, Pareto optimality, and group-strategyproofness for participants.

Digital laggards prioritize short-term needs, optimize existing initiatives, discourage risk-taking, and provide transactional training focused on current roles. Digital leaders, while also facing challenges, deliberately build learning mindsets over time and may create controlled environments for safe experimentation, as shown by a pharmaceutical company that automated compliance checks and expanded the tool after a successful launch.

Digital leaders emphasize transparent data access and shared decision-making, supported by governance controls that protect data and build trust. They believe data helps good ideas emerge from anywhere in the organization. Digital laggards tend to restrict access, store data in silos, rely on tenure or business judgment, and use data mainly to justify decisions already made. Research cited in the passage found that 88% of digital leaders have standardized APIs enabling easy data flow between departments, compared with 27% of digital laggards.

Digital leaders use measurement to learn, set realistic but ambitious goals, track progress with data-driven metrics, and combine formal evaluation with broader feedback. Clear metrics can give teams flexibility to innovate. A retail company case study showed how real-time sales reporting enabled faster data-driven decisions across business areas. Digital laggards often set aspirational goals not grounded in data, causing employees to avoid measurement and focus instead on process adherence, which can stifle innovation.

Digital leaders use data-driven objectives to align teams with company strategy through transparent, often combined top-down and bottom-up goal-setting. However, some can overuse analysis and slow simple decisions. Digital laggards often fail to connect goals clearly to strategy, resulting in misalignment.

The passage argues that strong data culture depends on learning, risk-taking, transparency, measurement, and alignment between leadership beliefs, company values, and daily behavior. Digital laggards may recognize the importance of data culture but struggle due to entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient leadership focus. Organizations may begin transformation as data novices, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant, and can build on existing strengths to improve their data culture.

The speaker reviews the nation’s first century under written constitutions, praising the founders’ creation of a stronger Union and noting the Constitution’s expansion, preservation through civil war, and supremacy over states and citizens. He urges the country to move beyond settled controversies, affirming that slavery’s abolition and equal citizenship for Black Americans fulfilled the promise of liberty. He condemns denial of equal suffrage as a threat to government, while identifying voter ignorance and illiteracy as dangers requiring universal education.

He calls for national reconciliation, continued prosperity, sound public credit, specie payments, careful handling of silver coinage, redemption of paper notes, and debt refunding without disrupting national-bank notes. He advocates greater attention to agriculture, manufacturing, transportation, waterways, ocean tonnage, and protection of American interests in any interoceanic canal.

The speaker defends religious freedom but urges Congress to prohibit criminal practices such as polygamy in the Territories and prevent ecclesiastical power from usurping government authority. He supports civil service reform through laws fixing tenure and removal grounds for minor offices. He pledges to uphold the Constitution, enforce federal law, maintain economy, require honest public service, and seek the support of citizens, Congress, officials, and God.

ATR trailing stop is a technical indicator introduced by J. Welles Wilder that helps traders set dynamic stop-loss levels based on average true range, a measure of price volatility. It is used to determine exit points, protect profits, minimize losses, and adapt stop levels to changing market conditions across instruments such as stocks and futures. ATR trailing stop values are calculated by multiplying ATR by a multiplier, typically 3.5, then subtracting the result from the previous close for long positions or adding it for short positions. It can also support entry signals by identifying breakouts or reversals. ATR bands help identify potential breakouts and gauge volatility. A potential trend reversal is signaled when price consistently breaches trailing stop levels, while the cross point marks the intersection of price and the trailing stop. Limitations include that ATR trailing stop may not fully account for past performance or price movements, so traders should consider other analyses and the inherent risk of losses.

Drew Faust announced she will step down as Harvard University president on June 30, 2018, after 11 years in the role and as Harvard’s fundraising campaign concludes. Faust, Harvard’s first female president, plans to take a sabbatical and return to scholarship. University leaders credited her with restoring trust after prior campus conflict, fostering collaboration, expanding financial aid, supporting the arts and sciences, and overseeing a campaign that raised $8 billion. Her tenure also included controversy over social clubs, diversity concerns, the men’s soccer team suspension, and endowment losses. In her final year, she said she will focus on research funding, recruitment, and inclusion. A search committee will be formed to find her replacement.

Texas A&M’s streak of having at least one first-round NFL draft pick every year since 2011 depends largely on receiver Christian Kirk, who bypassed his senior season and is projected as a fringe first-round selection. USA Today ranked Kirk as the fourth-best receiver, outside its first-round projection. Safety Armani Watts is expected to be a mid-round pick, while receiver Damion Ratley could be selected late. Defensive tackle Zaycoven Henderson’s draft prospects have declined after a December arrest and pending criminal case. The Aggies have had nine first-round picks since 2011, including Myles Garrett, Von Miller, Ryan Tannehill, Luke Joeckel, Jake Matthews, Mike Evans, Johnny Manziel, Cedric Ogbuehi and Germain Ifedi.

Alphabet will pay $24.5 million to settle Donald Trump’s lawsuit over YouTube’s suspension of his account after the January 6, 2021, Capitol riot, with $22 million going to Trump and $2.5 million to co-plaintiffs. Trump directed his share to the Trust for the National Mall and the construction of a White House ballroom. YouTube suspended Trump six days after the riot and reinstated him in March 2023. Trump had sued YouTube, X, and Meta in 2021 over platform bans; he previously settled with Meta for $25 million and X for $10 million. Alphabet admitted no liability or fault.

Michigan State Superintendent Michael Rice is retiring after leading since 2019. In a Chalkbeat interview, he said Michigan students need the full 180 instructional days and criticized laws allowing professional development and virtual days to count toward that total. Rice cited persistent challenges including flat national test performance, weak early literacy, chronic absenteeism, mental health concerns, and slow academic recovery, though he noted gains in preschool enrollment, school funding equity, and graduation rates.
