He said Michigan should learn from Mississippi’s reading improvements by emphasizing science of reading training, literacy coaches, strong materials, smaller early-grade classes in high-poverty schools, and protected instructional time. Rice also said teacher shortages are improving due to state investments, but are not over.

Peter Lynch is a retired money manager who led Fidelity’s Magellan Fund from 1977 to 1990, achieving 29.2% average annual returns and growing the fund from $20 million to $14 billion. His strategy emphasized “invest in what you understand,” fundamental analysis, and finding undervalued companies with clear business models rather than predicting markets or reacting to short-term price moves. He categorized companies as slow-growing, moderately growing, fast-growing, cyclical, turnarounds, and undervalued-asset firms, with a strong focus on growth stocks. Lynch reviewed holdings quarterly, stayed invested rather than holding cash, and sold or reduced positions when prices rose without supporting fundamentals or when business prospects weakened.
Scientists urge listing cheetahs as Endangered after assessments found low southern African populations and disappearance from 91% of their historic range.

Ghana Football Association Vice President George Afriyie was relieved of his duties after an Executive Committee meeting, following earlier signs of a rift with GFA President Kwesi Nyantakyi. Afriyie had announced plans to contest the 2019 GFA elections, while Nyantakyi reportedly distrusted him over financial disagreements and alleged ties to critic Nii Lante Vanderpuije. Afriyie had already been removed as head of the Black Stars Management Committee, a role now taken by Winfred Osei. The article says Afriyie’s dismissal clarifies divisions within the Executive Committee and may intensify his bid for the GFA presidency. It also raises questions about whether Nyantakyi, who has led the GFA since 2005 and had said he would not seek re-election, may run again amid internal opposition.

June 8, 2001 news clips focus on the Dabhol Power Company crisis involving Enron, MSEB, lenders, regulators and the government. Indian and foreign lenders appointed Stone & Webster to assess the cost and implications of suspending or mothballing Phase II of the 2,184 MW project, which was 92% complete, amid unresolved disputes over the power purchase agreement and power offtake. Enron suggested temporary suspension and indicated willingness to reduce its rate of return from 16% to 11%, while lenders sought a negotiated solution and stronger government commitments.

Reports said MSEB had stopped buying Dabhol power, disputed its high tariff, and rescinded the PPA, while DPC challenged MERC’s jurisdiction and sought Bombay High Court intervention against MERC orders restraining arbitration and escrow activation. The Godbole panel said DPC’s return on equity should not exceed 16% and accused DPC of adopting different positions in negotiations and elsewhere. Other articles said states were unlikely to buy Dabhol power at existing costs, private power producers welcomed Prime Minister Vajpayee’s interest, and activists called for a judicial inquiry into the Enron deal.

The speaker says the series has been tightly contested, with momentum swings and strong play from both teams. He praises his team’s effort, resilience through injuries, and excitement for the upcoming decisive game at home. He emphasizes the importance of Red Wings history, learning from great players, staying poised, focusing on execution rather than the prize, and appreciating the opportunity to compete for the Stanley Cup. He also notes Detroit fans’ passion for hockey amid difficult economic conditions and says players like Hossa should focus on doing their part for the team.

HPBOSE declared the Himachal Pradesh Class 12 Result 2018 on April 24 at 14:07 on hpbose.org. Students can check results online, via other result websites, or by SMS using HP12ROLLNUMBER sent to 56263.

Eight years after graduating, the author reflects fondly on college while recognizing missed opportunities and things they would do differently. They emphasize that college experiences vary, but recall meeting exceptional people, taking interesting classes, and loving campus life before focusing on their regrets.

The study examines forecasting Aedes invasive mosquito abundance in the Basque Country, a non-endemic region in northern Spain where no autochthonous Aedes-borne disease cases have been recorded, despite increasing imported dengue, chikungunya, and Zika cases and expanding Aedes albopictus and Aedes japonicus populations.

Mosquito egg-count data from ovitraps were collected across the Basque Country from 2013 to 2023, while meteorological data from 2016 to 2023 included temperature, relative humidity, and precipitation. Ovitraps were distributed across 63 municipalities, with sampling generally conducted every 14 days from June to November. The analysis focused on Gipuzkoa and Bizkaia because Araba had insufficient positive egg-count data for reliable modeling.

Egg counts were averaged using the 20 highest provincial counts per 14-day interval to reduce inconsistencies and zero-count skewness. Meteorological variables were aggregated over matching 14-day periods. Missing entomological values were imputed as zero, outliers in egg counts were smoothed using a central moving average, and training/testing splits used the final year as test data.

Exploratory analysis found skewed, over-dispersed, non-normal variables. Temperature showed the strongest association with egg counts, with Spearman correlations of 0.72 in Gipuzkoa and 0.80 in Bizkaia. Lagged temperature showed the highest correlation at a two-week lag, while precipitation showed weak negative correlations at longer lags. Humidity had weaker positive associations.

The study compared several models, including Generalized Linear Models, SARIMAX, Random Forest, and Conditional Inference Trees, using MAE, RMSE, and R². Incorporating lagged versions of independent variables and egg counts generally improved performance. Random Forest performed best on training data, explaining 98% of variance in both Gipuzkoa and Bizkaia, but showed weaker test performance, suggesting possible overfitting. GLM performed best on the test datasets, explaining 85% of variance in Gipuzkoa and 81% in Bizkaia, with SARIMAX close behind. Conditional Inference Trees performed worst overall.

After adding 2023 data to the training set, the best-performing models were used to forecast 2024 mosquito abundance. The study estimated lower mosquito abundance in 2024 than in the previous year in both provinces. The authors conclude that temperature and mosquito egg abundance are key predictors, continuous localized surveillance is essential, and predictive modeling can help guide public health and vector-control strategies in non-endemic regions.

Seven more candidates qualified for the special election to replace U.S. Rep. Tom Price in Georgia’s 6th Congressional District, bringing the field to 15. The election is April 18, with a likely runoff scheduled for June 20.

Liverpool open the 2017/18 Premier League season away at Watford on August 12 and finish at home to Brighton on May 13. Key fixtures include Everton, Manchester United, Swansea on Boxing Day, and Chelsea away. Dates may change.

The Geminid meteor shower peaks Wednesday night, with best viewing between midnight and 4 a.m. Thursday. Up to 50 meteors may be visible, especially in rural areas. A smaller crescent moon should improve viewing, though some late clouds are possible.

A UK study published in Thorax found that CT lung cancer screening may encourage high-risk smokers to quit. Researchers identified eligible smokers from questionnaires sent to British residents ages 50 to 75 and compared those invited for CT screening with those not invited. After two weeks, 10 percent of screened participants had quit smoking, rising to 15 percent after two years, compared with 5 percent in the non-screened group. The authors noted participants were self-selected and may already have been considering quitting, but concluded CT screening can provide a “teachable moment” for smoking cessation, especially when integrated with other anti-smoking interventions.

Caltech and six other institutions received $4.9 million from the U.S. Geological Survey to develop the West Coast ShakeAlert earthquake-warning system. The USGS also bought about $1 million in sensors. The system, under development since 2006, would provide seconds of warning before earthquakes.

Valmet Oyj’s Board of Directors approved a new long-term share-based incentive plan for key employees covering discretionary periods in 2018, 2019 and 2020. The plan aims to align shareholder and employee objectives, support long-term company value, and retain key employees. For 2018, rewards are based on Comparable EBITA margin and stable business orders received growth, paid in shares and cash in 2019. Shares are subject to a two-year restriction period. The plan covers about 120 participants, including management and management talents, with total rewards capped at approximately 586,000 Valmet shares before taxes and related costs.

Northwestern is drawing national attention as it nears its first NCAA bid after a 66-59 upset over Wisconsin. Coach Chris Collins and players Bryant McIntosh and Vic Law emphasized staying focused despite expectations. The Wildcats next face Maryland and will again be without Scottie Lindsey, who is out with mono.

American Airlines sent Theresa Staab a Net SAAver Weekend Getaway Fares email for travel the next weekend. Domestic departures are November 30–December 1, 2001, and international departures are November 29–30, 2001, with returns December 3 or 4 and tickets required by November 23, 2001. The email lists numerous roundtrip domestic and international fares, notes some American Eagle service, and directs customers to book at AA.com using an AAdvantage number and PIN. It also promotes AAdvantage Net SAAver Awards, AA Vacations, Fairmont, Starwood, and Hertz offers, and includes fare restrictions, taxes, fees, change rules, and unsubscribe instructions.

A U.S. study of 202 Illinois daycare and Head Start staff found sun safety was a lower health education priority than nutrition, exercise and brushing teeth. Fewer than one in five respondents listed sun protection, bike helmets or vaccinations as top priorities. About half of programs provided sunscreen, but most did not let children apply it themselves; some may have been influenced by school rules treating sunscreen as medication. Many programs used spray sunscreen, especially Head Start programs, though some applied it incorrectly to children’s faces. Most programs reported no sunburns and followed heat-index guidelines. Researchers and experts said early childhood programs need more sun protection education, and parents can help by applying sunscreen, providing protective clothing and modeling sun-safe behavior.

A federal jury in Denver found that former radio host David Mueller assaulted and battered Taylor Swift by groping her during a 2013 preconcert photo session. Swift had countersued after Mueller claimed her accusation was false and led to his firing from KYGO. Jurors awarded Swift the symbolic $1 she sought and also found that her mother and manager did not improperly interfere with Mueller’s contract. Swift said she would donate to organizations helping sexual assault victims defend themselves.

Angela B. Ryan describes how becoming pregnant changed her view of pregnant professionals and exposed her to unwanted attention and touching in legal workplaces, including an opposing counsel stroking her stomach in court. She argues that such “belly touching,” often minimized as a rub or pat, is an invasion of autonomy and should be recognized as harassment or assault, not treated as harmless or affectionate. Ryan notes that pregnancy discrimination and pregnancy-based harassment are already addressed under federal law and EEOC guidance, but unwanted physical contact is rarely confronted in practice. She calls on the legal profession to prohibit touching pregnant people without explicit consent through training, HR policies, judicial education and workplace culture changes.
Pete Hegseth addressed top military leaders, arguing for changes to a force he described as soft and “woke.”

The speaker says the team has improved puck management and positioning, feels confident after two wins, and is focused only on Thursday’s game. They expect a strong home opponent but see no road issue. They credit their goalie’s outstanding play, say the layoff affected timing, and note both teams are defensively strong and capable of comebacks.

On Christmas Eve 2012, Commander Chris Hadfield marked the holiday aboard the International Space Station, hiding cards from crew members’ families for them to find. Orbiting Earth every 92 minutes complicated the idea of “Christmas morning,” but Hadfield emphasized the importance of maintaining traditions in space for psychological well-being. The crew celebrated with space-safe foods, including fruitcake, ready-to-eat turkey, reconstituted potatoes and processed vegetables, along with a small Velcroed Christmas tree and stockings filled with chocolate and nuts. Hadfield said holidays, birthdays and family losses were treated seriously because mental health was essential to mission success. His American and Russian crew members also planned ways to celebrate holidays from their cultures.

NVIDIA A100 provides larger L1/shared memory per SM than V100, 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache nearly 7x larger than V100, 2.3x L2 read bandwidth, L2 residency controls, and Compute Data Compression for up to 4x additional DRAM bandwidth and L2 improvement.

Polling began for 69 of Uttarakhand’s 70 assembly seats amid tight security, with over 74 lakh voters deciding the fate of 628 candidates. Nearly 30,000 security personnel and 60,000 polling officials were deployed across 10,685 booths. Polling in Karnaprayag was rescheduled to March 9 after a candidate’s death.

The passage describes SD Memory Card physical-layer operations and command behavior. ACMD23 can pre-erase a specified number of blocks before CMD25 to speed multiple block writes; unused remaining blocks become undefined if writing stops early, and the count resets after the write. Erase operations use CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38, with sequence errors reported in status bits; protected sectors are skipped, and erased data value depends on the card.

DISCARD and Full User Area Logical Erase (FULE) are CMD38-based operations for SDHC/SDXC cards, not SPI. Hosts must check SD_STATUS support bits before issuing them. DISCARD treats contents as “don’t care,” while FULE logically erases the full user area. Both indicate busy by holding DAT0 low and have specified busy timeouts.

Write protection includes a mechanical switch, optional internal protection, and password-based locking. CMD42 manages passwords, lock/unlock, Force Erase, and Card Ownership Protection (COP). Locked cards accept only limited commands and block data access. COP adds Force Erase Password (FEP), COP Unlock, protected force erase, and restrictions on clearing passwords when FEP is set.

APP_CMD (CMD55) makes the next command an application-specific ACMD, with defined behavior for legal, illegal, and undefined ACMDs. CMD6 switches or checks card functions across groups including access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. Mode 0 queries support and current/power; Mode 1 switches functions. High-Speed mode is selected through CMD6 and requires one-to-one host-card signaling.

CMD8 checks interface voltage for version 2.00 or later cards before ACMD41. SDSC uses byte addressing and CMD16 block length, while SDHC/SDXC use 512-byte block addressing and fixed 512-byte memory access blocks. Hosts may change or stop the bus clock with restrictions, including providing clocks after transactions and during ACMD41 handling.

CRC7 protects commands and most responses; CRC16 protects data blocks. Commands with CRC errors or illegal commands are not executed and set status errors. Read, write, discard, FULE, and erase operations have defined timeout behavior. The passage also outlines SD command types, fixed 48-bit command format, command classes, application-specific and switch-function command tables, UHS-II command differences, state transitions, and response formats including R1, R1b, R2, and R3.

In a tort action for personal injuries, the plaintiff was injured while bowling at alleys owned by the defendant when a splinter from the sliding approach floor entered his finger as he delivered a ball with his hand close to, but not touching, the floor. Evidence showed the floor was old, uneven, warped, dirty, and splintered, and that the approach flooring had been reused from other alleys. The plaintiff later underwent three operations to remove splinters.

The defendant moved for a directed verdict and requested jury instructions asserting that the approach was only for walking and sliding, not for hand contact, and that the plaintiff’s conduct was negligent. The trial judge denied the motion and refused the instructions. The jury returned a $750 verdict for the plaintiff, and the case was reported.

The court held that the evidence warranted a finding that the defendant failed to exercise reasonable care to keep the premises safe and did not require a ruling that the plaintiff was contributorily negligent. The plaintiff’s due care was a question for the jury. Judgment was ordered for the plaintiff on the verdict.

Samsung announced three cheaper, water- and dust-resistant Galaxy A smartphones, its first product unveiling since the Galaxy Note 7 launch. The A3, A5 and A7 will debut in Russia before expanding elsewhere. They feature varying screen sizes, 16-megapixel cameras, fingerprint sensors, metal frames and 3D glass backs, but less processing power and storage than Galaxy S phones.

The 1902 passport rules state that only the Secretary of State may issue U.S. passports, with applications abroad handled through U.S. diplomatic or consular officers and applications in insular possessions through the chief executive. Passports may be granted only to persons owing allegiance to the United States, not merely those who declared intent to become citizens. Applicants must submit a sworn written application with identifying details, a physical description, oath of allegiance, purpose of temporary travel, intent to return, and witness certification. Additional evidence is required for persons born abroad to U.S. citizen fathers, naturalized citizens, women, children claiming citizenship through a naturalized parent, and residents of U.S. insular possessions owing allegiance to the United States.

The passage references TMS320DM814x technical manual sections on system MMU, L3/L4 interconnects, and L4 peripheral memory maps. It describes DDR DMM TILER extended addressing, which adds a 4-GB range via a 33rd address bit for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views, fully accessible only to HDVPSS and ISS. It also explains package pin assignment figures, terminal function table fields, multiplexed pin control, and boot configuration pins shared with GPMC functions after reset.

China launched a new talent visa to attract young professionals and science and technology graduates from top universities, as the US imposed a $100,000 H-1B fee. The move sparked xenophobic backlash.

After the July 4 Kerr County floods killed 25 Camp Mystic campers, two counselors, including 18-year-old Chloe Childress, and the camp director, grieving parents organized to push for stronger Texas camp safety laws. Matthew and Wendie Childress, along with parents including Blake Bonner, whose 9-year-old daughter Lila died, worked with lobbyists and lawmakers to advocate for reforms. Gov. Greg Abbott signed bills requiring youth camps to move overnight cabins out of floodplains, monitor weather warnings with radios, install alert systems, and train staff on emergency plans and evacuation routes to higher ground. Parents said the advocacy honored their daughters, but did not ease the loss.

A federal judge rejected a challenge to the Biden administration’s gainful-employment rule, siding with the Education Department. The rule requires for-profit and nondegree programs to show graduates can afford loan payments and earn more than high school graduates, or risk losing federal aid after repeated failures. Industry and advocacy groups responded differently, with future rule-making expected.

AI, especially LLMs, may transform social science research by improving access to large-scale data, automating analysis, synthesizing research data, and supporting hypothesis or theory generation. Benefits include scalable role-playing simulations, zero-shot and in-context learning for tasks such as sentiment analysis and response coding, and potential human-AI collaboration in theory development. Key challenges include dataset access, model costs, bias, oversimplified stereotypes, uncertain validity of synthetic responses, misinformation risks, and the need for human oversight.

Responsible AI governance must address misinformation, deepfakes, bias, discrimination, safety, transparency, accountability, and regulatory uncertainty. Existing efforts by governments and technology companies aim to mitigate risks, but gaps remain between industry and policymakers, across countries, and in identifying emerging LLM risks such as jailbreaks. The passage calls for forward-looking, human-centered governance involving industry, academia, policymakers, developers, users, and communities, with both top-down regulation and bottom-up reporting mechanisms.

An international cross-sectional analysis of the COVID-PCD participatory cohort examined diagnostic testing among 747 people with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) from 49 countries. Participants reported use and recall of nasal nitric oxide (nNO), biopsy-based analyses, and genetic testing, along with demographic and clinical information.

Most participants (92%) reported diagnostic testing, but use varied substantially by country. Among participants older than 5 years, 49% reported nNO measurement. Overall, 75% reported biopsy samples for electron or video microscopy, and 58% reported genetic testing. Biopsy was the most common test in most countries, while genetic testing was most common in North America and France. Only one-third of participants older than 5 years reported receiving all three tests: nNO, biopsy, and genetic testing.

Recall differed by test and country. Participants least often forgot whether biopsy had been performed, while recall was poorest for nNO. Many participants who remembered biopsy did not know whether samples were analysed by high-speed video microscopy or electron microscopy. Recall was lowest in Switzerland.

More recent diagnosis was associated with higher reported use of nNO, biopsy, and genetic testing. Participants with situs abnormalities reported fewer diagnostic tests than those with normal situs. Age at diagnosis was not associated with testing.

The study found marked international variation and incomplete diagnostic work-up among many people with PCD. The authors conclude that clinicians should review prior tests and results with patients and consider supplementary testing, especially for people diagnosed long ago or those with situs abnormalities, to improve diagnostic characterization for personalized medicine.

Halliburton reported first-quarter net income of $46 million, or 5 cents per share, versus a year-earlier loss. Adjusted earnings of 41 cents per share met expectations, while revenue of $5.74 billion missed forecasts. Shares are up over 6% this year and 10% over 12 months.

The Third Circuit reviewed Prava Chatterjee’s appeal from the district court’s denial of her petition to vacate a settlement and release of an admiralty death claim arising from the 1975 collision between the S.S. EDGAR M. QUEENY and the S.S. CORINTHOS, which killed her son. Chatterjee alleged that she never authorized her son-in-law, Anil Ghosal, to act for her, never signed the power of attorney, never retained U.S. counsel, and never received settlement proceeds.

The court held that Indian law governs the validity of the special power of attorney, while federal maritime law governs the validity of the release. It further held that the Garrett standard requiring careful scrutiny of seamen’s releases applies to settlements made by survivors of deceased seamen, placing the burden on the shipowners to prove the release was valid.

The court found no abuse of discretion in excluding prior Calcutta Commission testimony, but held that the district court’s refusal to authorize a new commission in India denied Chatterjee a fair opportunity to prove her allegations of fraud and forgery. The Third Circuit vacated the district court’s order and remanded with directions to invoke a commission to take testimony in India.

U.S. arrivals data show 19 percent fewer international students entered in August than in the same month in 2024, aligning with enrollment decline predictions but conflicting with Department of Homeland Security data showing a 0.8 percent increase. Experts say arrivals data is incomplete but useful, while SEVIS data may be inaccurate or affected by reporting gaps and OPT counts. Declines were steepest among students from Africa, Asia and the Middle East, with major drops from Iran, Syria, Haiti, Ghana, Nigeria and India. Visa interview freezes, delays and new reviews are cited as key factors. Experts warn the final enrollment decline could exceed 20 percent and may worsen in 2026, with fuller data expected in November.

The passage argues that NAFTA has been highly beneficial for Canada, especially manufacturing, and that modernizing it should be a federal priority. It says Canada remains too dependent on North American markets and that other free-trade agreements have not significantly increased exports. The author argues Canada needs a broader trade plan with five elements: improve domestic business competitiveness through tax and regulatory reform; ensure trade agreements address non-tariff barriers; choose trade partners based on realistic business ties; leverage existing supply chains and industrial strengths; and better support small and medium-sized enterprises in expanding globally. The passage concludes that Canada must modernize its business environment and export supports without waiting for NAFTA renegotiation outcomes.

A New Delhi court deferred to July 6 the hearing on the ED chargesheet against Karti Chidambaram and two companies in the Aircel-Maxis money laundering case. The ED charged Karti, ASCPL and CMSPL under PMLA, alleging irregular FIPB clearance in 2006 when P. Chidambaram was Finance Minister. It claimed Maxis’s actual FDI was Rs 3,565.91 crore, above the Finance Minister’s approval limit, but was projected as Rs 180 crore. The ED also alleged payments to CMSPL and ASCPL. Karti has interim protection from arrest till July 10 and is also accused in the INX Media case.

The speaker says a player probably will not play but refuses to confirm his status. They deny fatigue is a factor, express pride in the team, accept an inconclusive replay ruling, and say venue has not greatly affected performance despite possible home distractions. Recent games were decided in overtime.

Pokémon GO’s Solstice Event features fire- and ice-themed spawns and increased catch-related XP ahead of an anniversary update expected to add collaborative gym gameplay. The event gives triple XP for catching Pokémon and for throw bonuses, which can become six times XP with discounted Lucky Eggs. The author says this makes accurate throws more rewarding and encourages active play rather than evolving Pokémon for XP, since evolution receives no special bonus. The bonuses may help casual and midcore players level up before gym changes, though they are less useful for high-level players.

Roosevelt reports to Congress on the Crimea Conference at Yalta, saying its lasting success depends on congressional and public support. He states that the conference had two main purposes: to hasten Germany’s defeat with minimal Allied losses and to build foundations for postwar international order and lasting peace.

He says the Allies agreed on closer military coordination, including daily information exchange among forces on the western, eastern, and Italian fronts, and arrangements for effective distribution of materials and transportation. He emphasizes that Germany must surrender unconditionally, while clarifying that this does not mean destruction or enslavement of the German people. It means Allied occupation and control, the end of Nazism and militarism, punishment of war criminals, disarmament, reparations in kind, and prevention of future German aggression.

Roosevelt describes agreements on an international security organization, including resolution of voting procedures for the Security Council, with a United Nations conference scheduled in San Francisco on April 25, 1945. He stresses that world peace requires bipartisan American support and cooperation among all peace-loving nations.

He says the major Allies agreed to joint responsibility for liberated areas and former Axis satellites, including support for representative interim governments, democratic processes, and free elections. On Poland, he describes agreement on a reorganized provisional government, future free elections, and boundary compromises involving the Curzon Line and territorial compensation in the north and west. France was invited to take a German occupation zone, join the Allied Control Council, sponsor the San Francisco conference, serve on the Security Council, and share responsibility for liberated Europe.

Roosevelt notes that the conference focused on Europe, while British and American staffs planned increased operations against Japan. He warns that victory over Germany will not end the war and that Japan’s unconditional surrender remains essential. He concludes that Yalta was a turning point and that the United States must choose world collaboration to avoid another world conflict.

Theresa May faces pressure from Conservative Brexiteers ahead of a Chequers cabinet meeting, with Andrea Jenkyns warning that failing to deliver Brexit or pursuing a “half in, half out” approach would be catastrophic for the party. Jacob Rees-Mogg also urged May to uphold promises to leave the EU single market and customs union. Brexiteers fear a “soft Brexit” would keep the UK aligned with EU rules and limit trade freedom, while Remain-supporting MPs argue pragmatism is needed to avoid disruption. Michael Gove said May has a clear plan to leave the EU, maintain market access, and regain control of laws and borders, and predicted cabinet unity.

The passage argues that after nearly a decade of strong post-crisis gains, the U.S. stock market may be entering a more difficult environment. The S&P 500 had gone more than 60 trading days without a new high, while the Federal Reserve was raising rates and shrinking its balance sheet rather than supporting markets as in earlier volatility episodes. The author highlights elevated volatility in 2018 after unusually calm trading in 2017, noting frequent 1% and 2% daily moves and comparing the pattern to prior periods preceding difficult markets. The passage suggests continued or rising volatility could signal a bull market top, warns that distorted markets may face painful price discovery, and urges investors to look for risks not yet widely recognized despite strong earnings forecasts.

The passage explains Bogleheads 3 and 4 Fund Portfolios, low-cost index fund strategies based on Jack Bogle’s philosophy of broad diversification and long-term investing. The 3 Fund Portfolio includes U.S. stocks, international stocks, and U.S. bonds; the 4 Fund Portfolio adds international bonds. Suggested funds include VTI, VEU, BND, and IXUS. Example allocations are 50% U.S. stocks, 30% international stocks, and 20% bonds for the 3 Fund Portfolio, and 50%, 30%, 10%, and 10% respectively for the 4 Fund Portfolio. The 4 Fund Portfolio may offer broader global diversification. Market conditions affect stocks and bonds, but the portfolios are intended for disciplined long-term investing. Backtests showed annual returns of 7.6% with a 28% max drawdown for the 3 Fund Portfolio, and 7.8% with a 31% max drawdown for the 4 Fund Portfolio.

Guyana will host the CWWA’s 26th Annual Conference and Exhibition from October 16 to 20 at the Guyana Marriott Hotel. The forum will address water, wastewater and waste management, feature technical papers and exhibitors, review a regional waste management action plan, and prepare Caribbean positions for international forums.

The speaker announces a nationwide mobilization to provide winter relief for unemployed citizens and their families during the depression. A national organization led by Walter Gifford will coordinate with state and local agencies, relief committees, community chests, businesses, labor, churches, and civic groups to raise funds and administer aid. The effort aims to provide work where possible, direct assistance where necessary, and support health and character-building services.

The Federal Government is expanding public works, supporting nearly 700,000 families, stopping immigration, and adopting credit measures to stimulate employment. States and municipalities are also expanding public works and tax-supported relief, but voluntary local action is still needed to prevent hunger and cold. The speaker appeals to citizens’ responsibility, generosity, and community self-help, urging full support before Thanksgiving so that distressed families may face winter without fear.

LG introduced the V35 ThinQ, a premium smartphone with a Snapdragon 845 processor, 6GB RAM, a 6-inch 2880 x 1440 OLED display, no notch, and a headphone jack. It has IP68 resistance, MIL-STD 810G testing, dual 16MP rear cameras, an 8MP front camera, AI camera features, Google Lens, far-field Google Assistant support, Hi-Fi audio, a 3,300 mAh battery, Quick Charge 3.0, face and fingerprint recognition, 64GB or 128GB storage, and microSD support. Pricing and release details were not announced.

Drug repurposing identifies new uses for existing drugs and is especially relevant for rare diseases, where treatments are limited. The study uses the Elsevier Biology Knowledge Graph (EBKG), built with AI NLP from open access (OA) and controlled access (CA) biomedical literature, to compare OA and CA contributions to knowledge relevant to rare disease drug repurposing.

EBKG contains biomedical concepts and relations extracted from abstracts, full-text articles, clinical trials, and databases. The analysis focused on rare disease relations and drug-target relations. OA and CA publications contributed similar numbers of knowledge graph relations, though CA had more NLP-asserted statements. OA contribution increased after 2006, and more than half of relations needed for rare disease drug repurposing are now in OA. Rare diseases with more than 100 relations tended to have more than 50% of their relations in OA, while drug-target relations showed no similar pattern.

Most relations in both OA and CA are supported by a single reference. Nearly all relations supported by four or more references are in OA, but CA-only facts continue to increase annually, though more slowly than OA facts. The study found no meaningful difference between OA and CA in citation rate or time to first citation.

Single-reference, uncited relations have accumulated rapidly in rare disease literature and across EBKG. Most uncited relations were extracted from peer-reviewed literature, and many appear to come from original research articles not followed up by later studies. The authors conclude that citation rate does not differ between OA and CA, about half of graph relations have only one reference, and additional confidence scores are needed to evaluate knowledge graph relations.

Lawmakers planned to use President Trump’s first State of the Union address to highlight several issues. Many female Democratic lawmakers intended to wear black in solidarity with the #MeToo movement, while some invited sexual assault survivors as guests. Democratic leaders and lawmakers invited young immigrants protected under DACA to emphasize the immigration debate, while Rep. Kevin Cramer invited a border wall prototype contractor. At least eight Democratic lawmakers announced they would boycott the speech. Bill Nye attended as the guest of Rep. Jim Bridenstine, Trump’s NASA nominee, amid criticism of the nomination. Rep. Joe Kennedy of Massachusetts was set to deliver the Democratic response.

Managed by Q was a 15-month-old on-demand office cleaning and maintenance startup founded by Dan Teran and Saman Rahmanian. By July 2015, it had raised $15 million in Series A funding, expanded from New York to Chicago and San Francisco, and maintained high customer satisfaction. Q used technology, including customer iPads and operator apps, to provide transparency, task tracking, communication, and ordering for cleaning, maintenance, and office supplies.

Unlike many on-demand startups, Q moved away from subcontractors and hired its field operators as employees to improve quality, professionalism, and commitment. It paid above industry averages, offered benefits to eligible workers, provided training, used standardized procedures, and promoted from within. Its culture emphasized transparency, community, equal respect for all operators, and continuous feedback.

Q targeted companies in Class B and C commercial buildings and earned most customer spending from cleaning, with additional revenue from maintenance and supplies. By July 2015, it served 228 accounts in New York, 25 in Chicago, and 28 in San Francisco. The company faced a growth decision: expand into new cities such as Boston, Atlanta, and Washington, DC, or deepen existing markets by adding customers and broadening services, including third-party vendor referrals. Teran wanted growth without compromising Q’s employment model, service quality, or culture.

The lecture previews course logistics: a short problem set, a quiz covering statistical basics through SPC and control charting, closed book with one page of notes and provided statistical tables, and a later shift to yield modeling.

The main topic is the relationship between control charts and hypothesis testing. Control charts are described as repeated hypothesis tests where control limits are set by the false alarm probability alpha. Beta is the missed-alarm probability when the process has shifted, and sample size affects beta while control limits are adjusted to maintain alpha. Average run length is introduced as the inverse of alpha for an in-control process and as the inverse of one minus beta for detecting an actual shift.

The lecture distinguishes control limits from specification limits. Control limits are statistical thresholds for detecting unusual process behavior, while specification limits define acceptable product performance. False alarms cannot be identified from a control chart alone; alarms require investigation, including checking measurement equipment, reviewing historical trends, and examining process changes.

Process capability is introduced using CP and CPK. CP compares specification width to six standard deviations of process spread, while CPK also accounts for mean offset from specification limits. Examples show how centering and variance affect capability and nonconforming part probabilities. Quality loss functions are presented as another way to penalize deviation from target, incorporating both variance and mistargeting.

The lecture closes by previewing alternative control charts for faster or more sensitive detection, including moving average, exponentially weighted moving average, and cumulative sum charts.

Iraq has begun aerial bombardment of Islamic State-held Tal Afar, west of Mosul, with a ground attack expected after the air campaign. Authorities identified Tal Afar as the next target following the recapture of Mosul. The town had about 200,000 residents before Islamic State took control.

A chronological list of diplomatic records and telegrams dated January 8 to September 3, 1942, with file numbers, origins including Washington, Helsinki, Kuibyshev/Moscow, Stockholm, London, and Ankara, and related receipt times. Many entries reference “European War 1939” and Finland-related file categories.

Sarahah is a free Android and iOS app that lets users receive anonymous messages through a profile anyone can visit. Messages appear in an inbox where users can flag, delete, reply to, or favourite them. The app has recently become popular, though it was already used in regions such as Egypt and Saudi Arabia. Reviews are sharply divided, with many praising it while others warn about hateful comments and bullying risks. Developers describe it as a tool for constructive anonymous feedback and offer privacy controls, including hiding profiles from search, limiting comments to logged-in users, and blocking senders. The app is simple and focused on private messaging rather than public social interaction, but its long-term popularity remains uncertain.

Detective Mike Wissbaum in Washington, Missouri, was exposed to heroin mixed with fentanyl while giving rescue breaths to an overdose victim after administering Narcan. Both were hospitalized and recovered. Police warn the drug combination is increasingly common and dangerous to first responders.

The PGA848 is a monolithic high-voltage, high-bandwidth precision programmable-gain instrumentation amplifier with a single-ended output and eight binary gain settings from 0.5V/V to 100V/V selected by A0, A1, and A2 pins. It is intended for factory automation, analog input modules, data acquisition, test and measurement, and semiconductor test. Its input circuitry operates linearly within 3V maximum of either supply, with common-mode range depending on common-mode voltage, differential input voltage, gain, and reference voltage.

A typical application drives a 16-bit, 1MSPS ADS8860 SAR ADC using ±15V input-stage supplies and a 5.3V output-stage/ADC supply. The REF6250 provides a 5V ADC reference, divided to 2.5V and buffered by an OPA192 to set the PGA848 REF pin at ADC midscale. The design uses input EMI/RFI filtering, a feedback capacitor filter, and an ADC charge-reservoir RC filter; the nominal front-end bandwidth is 318kHz and maintains –0.1dB flatness to 41kHz.

Recommended operation is specified with ±15V input and output supplies, while supply voltages above 40V permanently damage the device. Layout guidance includes symmetrical matched inputs, close low-ESR bypass capacitors, separation of input traces from supply/output traces, minimized leakage and parasitic capacitance, fewer thermal junctions, and distance from heat sources. The document also references TI simulation tools, related documentation, support resources, ESD precautions, revision history, packaging information, and TI disclaimers.

The study examines tungsten oxidation in dry air and tungsten trioxide sublimation, focusing on conditions relevant to fusion reactor accident, maintenance, waste handling and detritiation scenarios. Pure tungsten was oxidised between 400°C and 1050°C using thermogravimetric analysis, while WO3 sublimation was measured between 750°C and 1100°C. Oxide phases and microstructures were characterised using XRD, Raman spectroscopy, optical microscopy, SEM and EBSD.

Tungsten oxidation showed a transition from parabolic to linear kinetics, with activation energies of 180.4 ± 3.8 kJ/mol and 117.5 ± 3.3 kJ/mol for the two regimes, respectively. WO3 sublimation followed an Arrhenius trend with an activation energy of 335.8 ± 17 kJ/mol. Oxidation was more pronounced at specimen edges, and higher perimeter-to-area ratios increased measured oxidation rates in the linear regime. Oxide spalling from edges was observed during handling.

XRD and Raman spectroscopy showed that WO2.9 and WO3 form at the oxide surface, while Raman cross-section mapping identified a layered oxide scale consisting of an inner WO2 layer about 30–50 nm thick, a WO2.72 layer about 10–20 µm thick, and an outer WO2.9/WO3 layer. SEM revealed voids, cracks, delamination and cavities in oxide scales formed at elevated temperatures. Crack formation was associated with volume expansion, thermal expansion mismatch, oxide phase differences and grain-orientation-dependent oxidation.

The results indicate that tungsten forms non-protective oxide scales with linear growth at all investigated temperatures, and that voids, cracks, dust formation and oxide spalling above 600°C may affect fusion reactor component handling. The observed WO2 layer may help explain low detritiation efficiency reported for JET tungsten tiles.

Joseph Nicholson, convicted in 2007 of first-degree murder for fatally stabbing 16-year-old Joey Tanner and attempting to murder Jeremy Rodgers, will be resentenced for second-degree murder after the Ontario Court of Appeal found the trial judge inadequately instructed the jury. Second-degree murder carries life in prison with parole eligibility after 10 to 25 years; the Crown is seeking 16 years. Court heard Nicholson rushed from a Barrie apartment with a knife during a confrontation and inflicted fatal and severe wounds. The Crown cited his violent record and prison misconduct, while court also heard about his troubled childhood. Tanner’s parents expressed continuing grief and anger. Nicholson apologized in court and said he wanted to rehabilitate himself. Justice Guy Di Tomaso will impose sentence Aug. 11.

Katie Albert, a Waterloo resident and SIUE psychology student studying abroad in Florence, describes the second half of her semester. Her Italian class is advancing, and she continues to enjoy painting and drawing, creating works inspired by Florence’s gardens, churches, bridges, sculptures and street views. She also participated in cultural activities, including a cooking class, and took school-sponsored trips to Siena, Pisa and Lucca.

During spring break, she visited seven countries in 10 days: Denmark, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, France, Germany and Switzerland. Highlights included museums in Copenhagen and Amsterdam, Belgian waffles in Brussels, historical and art sites in Luxembourg and France, visiting friends in Germany, and traveling to Becherbach, where her fourth-great-grandfather was born. She also returned to Adelboden, Switzerland, and went tandem paragliding near Geneva.

Back in Florence, she noticed tourist season had begun and resumed classes and daily routines. She later traveled to Split, Croatia, for rafting, cliff diving, beach time on Braĉ and a visit to Krka National Park, reaching 20 countries visited by age 20. With three weeks left, she reflects on finals, packing, souvenirs, leaving friends and feeling both reluctant to leave Florence and ready to return home.

Australia’s childcare subsidies will be replaced on July 2 by a single means- and activity-tested payment, but eligible families must update their Centrelink details through myGov or risk missing payments. About 489,000 of 1.2 million eligible families had not registered under the new system. Families must provide estimated 2018/19 income, activity hours and childcare type.

Under the system, both parents generally need to work, study, volunteer or seek work at least eight hours a fortnight. Subsidy rates range from 85 per cent of fees for families earning $66,958 or less to no subsidy for families earning more than $351,248. Families earning under $186,958 will have no annual rebate cap, while higher-income families will have a cap of just over $10,000 per child.

Activity levels determine subsidised care hours, from 36 to 100 hours per fortnight. Exemptions and additional subsidies apply for vulnerable families, grandparents, financial hardship and transitions from income support to work. Children must meet immunisation requirements unless exempt.

Jeffing is a run-walk-run fitness method created by Olympian Jeff Galloway in the 1970s. Dr John Gallucci Jr says it involves planned walking breaks during runs, making exercise less intimidating, reducing fatigue, supporting muscle recovery, and helping lower injury risk compared with running continuously. Beginners can start with 1–2 minutes of running followed by 1–2 minutes of walking, then adjust gradually. Experienced runners may use Jeffing for long runs or recovery weeks. Gallucci warns that progressing too quickly or using poor running mechanics can still cause injuries such as knee pain, shin splints, or plantar fasciitis.

The passage states that the last trading day of the month has historically been weak for the S&P 500. Investing in SPY from the close of the second-to-last trading day to the close of the last trading day produced an average loss of 0.06% per trade and a negative 0.8% CAGR since 1993. Overnight performance from the prior close to the last day’s open averaged 0.04%, while intraday performance from open to close averaged -0.11% with a 42% win rate. The passage suggests the weakness may be structural or due to profit-taking and notes that there is no positive end-of-month effect on the last trading day.

Sharon Haliwell, 48, died by suicide at her Wigan home after addiction to sleeping pills and abuse by her husband. Her inquest raised concerns about poor communication between North West Boroughs NHS Foundation Trust teams after two assessments identified suicide risk, but she was not referred for counselling due to an error. The trust said it was improving training, alerts and procedures to share risk information. Coroner Prof Jennifer Leeming issued a prevention of death notice while noting some improvements.

The passage surveys algebraic and combinatorial invariants of matroids and hyperplane arrangements, focusing on Orlik–Solomon algebras, holonomy Lie algebras, Chen Lie algebras, resonance varieties, Koszul modules, and multinets. It explains that realizable matroids correspond to hyperplane arrangements whose intersection lattices connect matroid combinatorics with arrangement complement topology and fundamental groups. The survey highlights open questions about resonance linearity, torsion in holonomy Lie algebras, and Chen ranks expressed through multinets.

Matroids are introduced as finite structures generalizing linear independence, with independent sets, circuits, bases, ranks, flats, lattices of flats, modularity, supersolvability, localization, and direct sums. Examples include uniform matroids and graphic matroids, with realizations by generic, Boolean, graphic, and braid arrangements.

Multinets are defined as partitions of a matroid ground set with multiplicities satisfying balance, rank-2 flat, and base-locus conditions, with an added connectivity condition for multinets. Reduced multinets, nets, base loci, line-closed parts, and numerical identities are discussed. For realizable matroids, a Riemann–Hurwitz type inequality is stated, and the passage asks whether it holds for non-realizable matroids.

The text connects 3-nets with Latin squares and k-nets with tuples of orthogonal Latin squares. It notes results on which finite groups can be realized by 3-nets in the complex projective plane, including examples from cyclic, abelian, dihedral, quaternion, and certain projective linear groups. It also presents Yuzvinsky’s question asking whether all 3-nets in CP² are algebraic.

The Orlik–Solomon algebra of a matroid is then defined as a quotient of an exterior algebra by circuit relations. Its graded ranks are determined by the Möbius function of the lattice of flats, and its Poincaré polynomial is introduced. The projective Orlik–Solomon algebra is defined via the kernel of the induced derivation, and quadratic and Gröbner-basis properties are related to supersolvability.

The speaker says fatigue is not a factor in the Stanley Cup final because adrenaline takes over and the series is a race to four wins. They emphasize their team’s experience, resilience after losses, and key players. They praise the chemistry of Sykora, Elias, and Arnott, but believe physical play can shut them down. They also express confidence in Joe, saying he is playing well despite not scoring much, creating chances and contributing offensively.

Tiffany Gholston, born with a heart murmur, received a pacemaker at 20 and now supports the American Heart Association’s Go Red For Women campaign. She maintains her health through activity, diet, and meditation, and helps raise awareness and funds for heart health research.

Hackers released more unaired HBO episodes, including “Curb Your Enthusiasm,” “Insecure,” “Ballers” and “The Deuce,” but no new “Game of Thrones” material. HBO said it would not engage with the hackers, who have sought a multi-million-dollar ransom.

Anna Ryder Richardson is leaving Manor House Wildlife Park in Pembrokeshire for a dilapidated farmhouse near Bordeaux and is divorcing her husband, Colin MacDougall. She says the stress, workload and expense of running the zoo destroyed their 16-year relationship. The couple bought the rundown park in 2008 for £1 million and invested another £1 million renovating it, while living for years in basic accommodation. Their life at the zoo was filmed for television, but Anna says the lack of privacy and constant pressures affected the family. A 2010 accident involving a falling tree also brought serious consequences and, she believes, changed their marriage. Colin will continue managing the zoo, while Anna plans to live in France with their daughters and rebuild her television career.

The passage lists The 74 headlines and links on education, youth, school integration, policy, STEM, and current events, including that a west Texas all-girls camp where 27 children and counselors died in July floods plans to reopen next summer.

Motley Fool Money reviews the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card as a no-annual-fee cash back card offering unlimited 2% cash rewards on purchases, a $200 bonus after spending $500 in the first 3 months, and 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a variable APR of 18.99%, 23.99%, or 28.99%. The card also includes up to $600 in cell phone protection with a $25 deductible and Visa Signature® Concierge access. Approval is most likely for applicants with good credit, typically 670 or higher. The passage also lists offers for Capital One Quicksilver and Citi Double Cash cards and includes disclosures about advertising partnerships, compensation, and editorial policies.

Albert Einstein College of Medicine researchers reported in PLOS Biology that intense exercise may temporarily suppress appetite through heat-sensitive receptors in POMC neurons in the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus. In mouse studies, capsaicin or heat activated TRPV1-like receptors on about two-thirds of these neurons. Infusing capsaicin into the arcuate nucleus reduced food intake for 12 hours, but blocking or silencing the receptors prevented this effect. Treadmill exercise raised body and arcuate nucleus temperatures and reduced food intake by about 50 percent compared with non-exercising mice. Exercise did not reduce food intake in mice whose POMC neurons lacked the receptors. The researchers said body temperature can act as a biological signal regulating feeding behavior.

The Texas Department of Labor and Standards sued to enforce obligations under the Health Spa Act against American Savings Bank, surety on a letter of credit secured by Anna Black. The trial court ruled for the Department, and the court of appeals affirmed, finding good cause to admit documentary evidence not timely identified. The Supreme Court of Texas denied writ of error but stated it did not approve the appellate court’s distinction between witnesses and documents or relieve parties of showing good cause in the record under Rule 215.5.

Researchers from the Harvard-Smithsonian Centre for Astrophysics and Tel Aviv University propose using a global network of mobile phones and low-cost radio receivers to detect fast radio bursts from within the Milky Way. Phones could monitor relevant radio frequencies, upload candidate signals to a central system, and allow simultaneous detections to identify real events. GPS timing could help triangulate a burst’s sky position, while frequency data could estimate its distance within the Galaxy. FRBs are brief radio signals from unknown sources; only FRB 121102 has been observed repeating and traced to a galaxy three billion light years away. Researchers estimate a Milky Way FRB may occur every 30 to 1,500 years, though a repeating source could be active now.

McLaren says it has addressed the reliability problems that disrupted pre-season testing, including wheel nut, battery, exhaust and overheating issues. Eric Boullier said factory work has focused on maximizing performance for the Australian Grand Prix. Fernando Alonso said the Renault-powered MCL33 showed potential but still needs development, while Boullier noted McLaren’s midfield position remains difficult to judge.

Early forecasts suggest cloudy or unsettled weather could affect viewing of Monday’s partial solar eclipse in Philadelphia, though predictions remain uncertain. Philadelphia is outside the path of totality, with South Carolina the nearest state in it. The total eclipse will occur in Charleston at 2:48 p.m. ET.

The passage describes systems and methods for adapting, updating, and evaluating radiotherapy treatment plans using real-time imaging data acquired before or during treatment. Biological, physiological, and anatomical data may be extracted from modalities such as PET, MRI, SPECT, MPI, CT, X-ray, and ultrasound. Data may include tracer uptake values, PET tracer kinetics, tissue metabolism, hypoxia, osteogenic activity, HER2 expression, blood flow, vascularity, tumor morphology, lymphatic activity, and anatomical changes.

Treatment plans may be modified based on these data by changing dose objectives, target or dose-shaping geometry, dose distributions, treatment duration, fractionation, or number of sessions. The passage also describes evaluating treatment suitability using clinical parameters, plan quality index values, and dose-volume histograms, including bounded DVH curves. Notifications may indicate whether treatment should proceed, proceed with review, require adaptation, or stop.

The systems include imaging components, radiation treatment components, controllers, communication interfaces, displays, PET detectors, therapeutic radiation sources, dynamic multi-leaf collimators, and gantries. Adaptive radiotherapy may be online, real-time, or offline, with treatment plans updated before, during, or after a session based on newly acquired data.

A hockey player reflects on finally winning the Stanley Cup after eight difficult years, thanking teammates, leaders, Larry Murphy, Scotty, and his family for their support. He says he stayed motivated despite doubts, feels healthy enough to keep playing, and hopes bringing the Cup to Moscow could boost interest and investment in Russian hockey.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated October 26, 2017, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2017. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Exchange Act unless specifically incorporated by reference. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer.

Huddersfield Giants aim to build on strong early results after beating Warrington in pre-season and Widnes in their Super League opener, with coach Rick Stone urging continued improvement ahead of their home clash with Salford.

This compilation bridges the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals and the United Nations Charter, focusing on the United States role in establishing the UN legal framework. It presents the American Delegation’s positions, policy development, negotiations, debates, drafting, and informal agreements among major powers during the San Francisco Conference. It traces U.S. policy recommendations through May 1945 and Conference work through the Charter’s signing on June 26. Documentation includes minutes of U.S. Delegation, “Big Four,” “Big Five,” and informal meetings, coordinated with published Conference records. It also contains records involving Secretary of State Stettinius, correspondence, memoranda, diplomatic notes, policy statements, and Presidential correspondence, drawn from State Department files, libraries, government offices, and published sources.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K reporting that on March 22, 2016, it entered into an accelerated share repurchase agreement with Barclays Bank PLC. NVIDIA will pay $500 million and receive 12,108,715 shares of its common stock as part of its previously announced plan to return $1 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases in the current fiscal year. Settlement may involve additional share delivery by Barclays or share/cash delivery by NVIDIA based on volume-weighted average prices during the agreement term.

Intel shares rose 7% after a report said the company is in early talks with AMD to manufacture chips through Intel Foundry. Such a deal would be significant for Intel’s foundry business and could signal AMD’s confidence in using its competitor for manufacturing. AMD’s potential manufacturing volume is unclear. Intel declined to comment, and AMD said it does not comment on rumor or speculation.

The coach said the team shortens shifts in the third period so players do not return tired and can perform on their next shift. Lineup decisions remain unsettled, with Hrkac, Plante, Hogue, Sydor and Keane among the options. Hull is considered doubtful, and the team is preparing as if he will not play, while Hogue may progress through warmup and could be available soon. The coach avoids disclosing exact injury details to protect players and the team but aims to be clear about availability.

The team’s shutdown pair is assigned to whichever opposing line is most dangerous, with attention on players such as Brown, Peca and others. Keane and Carbonneau were given rest options after heavy minutes. The coach described managing Hull through compromise: freedom with the puck, but adherence to team structure without it. He said the team wants more sacrifice than in a previous overtime loss, including blocking shots. He also emphasized keeping Peca from controlling tempo and away from the net.

The passage compiles May 18, 2001 news items mentioning Enron. A Dow Jones column says California’s long-term power contracts had declined in value as western forward power prices fell, while Enron was described by traders as having sold aggressively during the prior two months. An options report says an institutional investor made a bullish Enron options trade, buying June 55 calls and selling June 50 puts as Enron stock rose to about $54.24.

Several reports cover Saudi Arabia’s selection of international oil companies for three major natural-gas projects requiring about $25 billion in investment. Exxon Mobil, Shell, BP, Phillips, TotalFinaElf, Conoco, Occidental, and Enron were selected. Enron and Occidental received stakes in the Red Sea project, led by Exxon Mobil. Leaders for the South Ghawar and Shaybah projects were expected to be announced by June 5.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated July 18, 2019, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2019. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act unless specifically incorporated by reference. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer.

Steven Kean discussed Enron’s role in defending Ex-Im Bank funding, saying it appeared smaller than reported by The Wall Street Journal and aligned with Enron’s current interest level. He noted budget cuts, reduced headcount, and John Hardy’s move into Linda Robertson’s DC organization, while saying Hardy still had project finance work tied to existing projects, ongoing pursuits, and asset-sale transfer issues. Hardy said Enron should support Ex-Im and OPIC programs but was not leading the lobbying effort or participating in Capitol Hill meetings, though Enron needed agency support for Electrobolt and problem projects.

The forwarded news mentions reported that major exporters, including Enron, Boeing, Caterpillar, and Halliburton, were lobbying against proposed Ex-Im Bank budget cuts. Other articles mentioned Houston office development involving Enron, Dutch gas market liberalization and Enron Europe trading, California utility and power-contract issues involving Enron, doubts about Sierra Pacific’s acquisition of Enron’s Portland General Electric, and falling U.S. natural gas prices.

The Stack Offense compacts players into two stacks near the free throw line, using three ballhandlers while two post players serve mainly as stationary screeners. Ballhandlers dribble penetrate to the wing, while same-side teammates pop off post screens for passes and rotate into stack positions. If defenders overplay passing lanes, players back cut rather than fight pressure. Options include basket rolls by overplayed receivers or posts, baseline drives when defenders fail to protect the basket, and drop passes to posts when help defense sags. Posts can step out as pressure releases to reset continuity.

Horace Maynard Middle School Principal Greg Clay said he was not aware of repeated bullying of sixth-grader Keaton Jones and that the lunch incident described in Jones’ viral video had been resolved, with action taken involving other children. The video, posted by Jones’ mother, drew widespread attention and support online. Clay said the school planned an assembly on bullying and already had an anti-bullying talk scheduled for January. Other district parents said bullying occurs at times but did not view it as worse in Union County than elsewhere.

The passage describes a hardware-aware machine learning model scaling/swapping system (MLMS) for selecting and interchanging AI/ML models efficiently under changing hardware, system, network, and environmental conditions. The system uses a supernet containing multiple subnets, monitors performance and context information, and triggers subnet searches when constraints or metrics change. A subnet selector chooses replacement subnets that satisfy performance and hardware constraints while minimizing data-transfer and memory-write costs by selecting models with maximum overlap in pretrained parameters. The MLMS framework includes interfaces for user-provided configurations, performance auditing, subnet pools, and support for various NAS or search algorithms. It is intended for resource-constrained and dynamic platforms such as IoT devices, drones, edge nodes, autonomous systems, and cloud or federated learning environments. The passage also outlines relevant ML concepts, neural network structures, performance metrics, context types, and example hardware/software architectures for implementing the system.

A cross-sectional secret shopper study assessed access to electronically prescribed nameless expedited partner therapy (EPT) at 335 New York City pharmacies and examined associations with neighborhood socioeconomic vulnerability using the CDC Social Vulnerability Index. Pseudopatients called pharmacies asking whether an EPT prescription for chlamydia could be sent electronically under “Expedited Partner,” without personally identifiable information.

Among surveyed pharmacies, 40% of pharmacists reported awareness of EPT, and awareness was associated with greater willingness to dispense nameless EPT prescriptions. Overall willingness remained low at 30%. Pharmacists willing to dispense used varied approaches: 28% used “Expedited Partner,” 34% used double prescriptions or refills under the index patient’s name, and 6% required the partner’s name. Thirty-one percent refused or ended the call, most often citing unfamiliarity with EPT or belief that a patient name was legally required. Less than half of fillable prescriptions followed New York State guidelines.

National chain pharmacies were more likely than non-chain pharmacies to report EPT awareness. Higher neighborhood socioeconomic vulnerability was associated with greater EPT awareness, but not with willingness to fill EPT prescriptions. Neighborhood chlamydia rates and borough-level location were not significantly associated with EPT awareness or dispensing willingness.

The study concludes that pharmacy-level barriers to EPT implementation include limited awareness, low willingness to dispense nameless prescriptions, and poor guideline adherence. The authors identify a need for pharmacist education, policy interventions, electronic prescribing improvements, and further research on geographic and structural disparities in EPT access.

The passage argues that globalization affects education policy, language hierarchies, curricula, textbooks, and classroom practice, making global education important in English language learning. It presents English as a lingua franca for international communication and suggests that EFL curricula should include global issues such as health, climate change, war, energy, environmental protection, culture, trade, poverty, human rights, and technological cooperation.

The study involved 372 non-English-major university students at three Taiwanese universities over 18 weeks. Students discussed global topics through group work, presentations, films, online resources, Facebook interaction, and survey reflections. Topics included global warming, tourism, music, festivals, food, cultures, technology, sports, endangered animals, Middle East conflicts, alternative energy, therapies, architecture, and environmental protection.

Survey results showed strong student support for integrating globalization into English education. Most students viewed global issues as important, interesting, and relevant to formal curricula. They identified global warming, energy, and environmental protection as especially significant, said online media supported learning, and reported that global topics increased motivation to learn English and confidence in international communication. The passage concludes that English curricula can help university students connect professional knowledge with global issues and prepare them for participation in an interconnected world.

This single case study examined whether smartphone touchscreen interactions could track behavioural changes related to anti-seizure medication changes and seizures in a man in his late twenties with refractory right temporal lobe epilepsy. Over 185 days, 718,357 touchscreen interactions were recorded alongside seizure diary data; during a five-day epilepsy monitoring unit admission, video-EEG documented multiple seizures, including one focal to bilateral tonic-clonic convulsion. The subject’s lamotrigine and perampanel were tapered before admission and withdrawn during admission.

Touchscreen interaction patterns were analysed using daily inter-touch interval distributions. Medication tapering was associated with an increased probability of fast next-interval dynamics, which reversed after medication restart. The day of the convulsion showed an increased probability of slow next-interval dynamics compared with the three preceding days. The authors conclude that smartphone touchscreen data may unobtrusively capture medication- and seizure-related behavioural fluctuations in epilepsy, but cohort studies are needed to assess generalisability.

Skinimalism is a skincare approach that simplifies routines by focusing on a few high-quality, targeted products that support the skin barrier and avoid overwhelming the skin. Dr Hazel Parkinson says it can reduce irritation, sensitivity, waste, packaging, cost, and stress from complex routines. It may benefit sensitive, ageing, acne-prone, eczema-prone, rosacea-prone, hyperpigmented, or menopausal skin when tailored carefully, often using gentle cleansers, moisturisers, SPF, and selected actives. People transitioning from multi-step routines should remove products gradually and allow 2–4 weeks for skin to adapt.

Microsoft filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2018. Revenue was $29.1 billion, up from $24.5 billion a year earlier; net income was $8.8 billion, up from $6.6 billion; diluted EPS was $1.14, up from $0.84. Operating income rose to $10.0 billion from $7.7 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $135.9 billion, and total assets were $257.6 billion.

Revenue grew across all segments: Productivity and Business Processes revenue was $9.8 billion, Intelligent Cloud was $8.6 billion, and More Personal Computing was $10.7 billion. Commercial cloud revenue increased 47% to $8.5 billion. Growth was driven by Office 365, LinkedIn, Dynamics 365, Azure, Windows Commercial, Gaming, Search advertising, and Surface. Azure revenue grew 76%, Gaming revenue grew 44%, and LinkedIn revenue grew 33%.

Cost of revenue increased 20%, research and development expenses increased 11%, and sales and marketing expenses increased 8%. The effective tax rate decreased to 14% from 18%, primarily due to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. Microsoft recorded a provisional net charge of $13.7 billion related to the TCJA in fiscal 2018 and had not completed its accounting for the tax effects as of September 30, 2018.

Microsoft had $76.2 billion in long-term debt including the current portion. It repurchased $2.6 billion of common stock during the quarter and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.46 per share. The company expected to close its $7.5 billion stock transaction to acquire GitHub by the end of October 2018. Deloitte & Touche LLP reviewed the interim financial information and was not aware of material modifications needed for GAAP conformity.

Wide receivers are increasingly valued in football as offenses rely more on passing, highlighted by six receivers being selected in the first 20 picks of the 2022 NFL draft. Their main role is to complete the passing game by running routes, getting open, making catches, and creating difficult one-on-one matchups for defenses. They also need toughness, football IQ, chemistry with quarterbacks, and the ability to handle limited touches or physical contact. A secondary but important responsibility is run blocking, which can help turn short runs into big plays.

The name “wide receiver” comes from lining up wide near the sideline and receiving passes from the quarterback. Other names include WR, wideout, split-end, and flanker. Key skills include route-running, run-blocking, body control, speed, strong hands, coordination, and agility. Wide receivers vary in size but are generally lean, often ranging from 5’10” to 6’4” and 180 to 220 pounds.

Notable wide receivers include Jerry Rice, Randy Moss, and Steve Largent. Elite receivers are important because they force defenses to adjust coverage, influence safety alignment, and create strategic advantages for offenses.

Market Basket, a New England supermarket chain founded by the Demoulas family, developed a high-volume, low-price business model supported by experienced employees, internal promotion, generous profit sharing, strong supplier relationships, and close attention to customers. By 2014 it had 25,000 non-unionized employees, 71 stores, $4.6 billion in revenue, no debt, and operating margins above several competitors. Its stores emphasized uniform low pricing, daytime stocking so employees could assist customers, local product customization, and a service culture.

The company was shaped by a long family dispute between descendants of brothers Mike and George Demoulas. After litigation in the 1990s, George’s side, led by Arthur S. Demoulas, gained a 50.5% stake. Mike’s son, Arthur T. Demoulas, became CEO in 2008 and continued the company’s model, prioritizing employees, low prices, low costs, and no debt. Some shareholders opposed his management style, spending decisions, and resistance to board oversight.

In 2013, a shift in board control gave Arthur S.’s side power. The board limited Arthur T.’s authority, approved a $300 million shareholder dividend, and in June 2014 fired him along with senior executives. Employees, vendors, and customers feared the company’s model would change. In July 2014, headquarters workers, warehouse employees, and truck drivers walked out, demanding Arthur T.’s reinstatement. Store employees, customers, vendors, politicians, and outside observers joined or supported protests and boycotts. Sales fell more than 90%, deliveries stopped, part-time employees were let go, and vendors and nearby businesses were hurt.

On August 27, 2014, shareholders agreed that Arthur T. and his family would buy Arthur S.’s side’s 50.5% stake for $1.6 billion. Arthur T. and his management team were reinstated with full operational authority during the transition. Employees, vendors, and customers returned, and operations recovered within weeks. The company then faced the challenge of maintaining low prices, employee benefits, growth, and its business model while carrying the debt from the buyout.

A University of Connecticut study found that vaping nicotine-based e-cigarette liquid can cause DNA damage approximately equivalent to smoking unfiltered tobacco cigarettes. Researchers used a low-cost 3D-printed electro-optical screening device acting as a “fake lung” with human enzymes and DNA. DNA damage increased with the number of puffs tested at 20, 60, and 100. The findings were published in ACS Sensors, and researchers are continuing work on related 3D-printed toxicity screening and cancer diagnostic platforms.

The passage explains how to backtest a momentum trading strategy in Python using yfinance, pandas, numpy, and matplotlib. The strategy uses Select Sector SPDR ETFs, adjusted close prices, monthly rebalancing, and a momentum factor defined as each ETF’s rolling past 9-month performance. It selects the top three ETFs each month, builds an equally weighted portfolio, calculates monthly returns, and plots performance against SPY. The strategy produced a 9.89% CAGR compared with SPY’s 9.46%, showing performance nearly identical to the benchmark. The passage also notes that the ETF list and assets can be customized.

PerovSegNet is a YOLOv8-seg-based deep learning framework for automated SEM image segmentation of perovskite and lead iodide films. It addresses challenges such as low contrast, complex backgrounds, fine grain boundaries, small defects, and limited annotated data. The authors created PerovData, a public dataset of 10,994 augmented annotated SEM images derived from 40 manually labeled samples, with classes for perovskite, lead iodide, and defects.

The model incorporates two modules: ASDCB, which improves multi-scale feature extraction and boundary localization using dilated convolutions, attention, channel shuffle, and lightweight convolution; and SAD, which preserves fine-scale textures and large-scale structures through depthwise separable convolutions and adaptive pooling.
