Lowered targets included Ascena Retail to $2.50 and Rite Aid to $2.25. Other targets included Costco at $185, Inovio at $13, Eli Lilly at $86, and Mallinckrodt at $70.

The speaker expresses gratitude for reelection and attributes national accord to the strength and stability of the Union. He reviews the prior term, noting the recent war’s costs and the subsequent effort to improve defense through coastal fortifications and naval expansion, which he presents as measures for peace, economy, and protection.

He states that the United States has maintained impartial neutrality in the conflict between Spain and its South American colonies, while suppressing piracy and illegal expeditions. He highlights the ratified treaty with Spain, especially the acquisition of Florida, and reviews agreements with Britain, ongoing commercial negotiations with France, and naval measures related to the Barbary Powers, the Pacific, piracy, and the slave trade.

He describes national finances as prosperous, citing debt reduction and defense improvements, but notes reduced revenue from depressed prices and discusses loans, internal taxes, and excises as possible responses. He calls for reforms in policy toward Indian tribes, including securing individual land rights, education, civil government, and support.

He warns that Europe is unsettled, says the United States should remain neutral while defending maritime rights, and emphasizes preparedness during peace. Domestically, he praises the representative system, popular sovereignty, national expansion from St. Croix to the Sabine, the admission of new states, population growth, and the country’s increasing strength. He closes by pledging faithful execution of his duties with confidence in his advisers, citizens, and God.

This review protocol aims to evaluate published studies using viral culture to assess potential SARS-CoV-2 infectivity in immunosuppressed solid organ or hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients. It will examine relationships between serial rt-PCR Ct values or other viral burden measures and the presence or duration of replication-competent virus, as well as possible influences of age, sex, underlying conditions, immunosuppression, vaccination status, symptoms, and disease course.

Searches will cover LitCovid, medRxiv, Google Scholar, and the WHO COVID-19 database from November 2019 to December 31, 2021, without language restrictions. Eligible studies must report serial PCR or other respiratory viral burden measures alongside viral culture data from transplant patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection. Reviews, abstracts, posters, post-mortem-only studies, non-respiratory-only studies, and studies without viral culture will be excluded.

Screening, data extraction, and quality assessment will be conducted by multiple reviewers. Data will be reported according to PRISMA standards and summarized narratively rather than pooled, due to expected differences in laboratory methods and assays. The work is funded by the National Institute of Health Research Evidence Synthesis Working Group and the University of Calgary.

The speaker mourns the murdered President and emphasizes the stability of constitutional succession. He pledges to honor his predecessor’s aims of reform, economy, prosperity, security, and honorable foreign relations. Noting national prosperity, settled fiscal policy, peaceful foreign affairs, and no need for an unusual congressional session, he assumes the executive trust with reliance on divine guidance and the American people.

Lincolnshire County Council has approved a new care leavers strategy to support young people leaving care. Support includes guidance up to age 25, council tax discounts, help with university costs and driving licences, and contact for care leavers in custody. The leaving care services budget is about £1.2 million, supporting 300 young people.

A fossil from southwestern China shows a pregnant Dinocephalosaurus, a fish-eating marine reptile from about 245 million years ago, with an embryo inside, indicating it gave birth to live young. Scientists said this changes understanding of vertebrate reproductive evolution and makes Dinocephalosaurus the first known archosauromorph to be viviparous. The 13-foot reptile had a very long neck, flippers, a small head and fish-catching teeth. Researchers said live birth suggests it was fully marine. The embryo’s curled position and forward orientation showed it was offspring, not prey. Scientists also said Dinocephalosaurus likely determined offspring sex genetically.

PenFed Credit Union President and CEO James Schenck accepted the Large Business Philanthropist of the Year award at Volunteer Alexandria’s 20th annual Business Philanthropy Summit. The summit promotes collaboration among businesses, nonprofits, government entities and Alexandria residents to improve community wellbeing. PenFed and the PenFed Foundation support military members, veterans and local communities through donations including $300,000 to Serve Our Willing Warriors, $125,000 to the Kennedy Center, $100,000 to DC Habitat for Humanity, $75,000 to the Military Officers Association of America and $15,000 to Bunker Labs. PenFed also supports accessible housing for wounded warriors and launched the Veteran Entrepreneur Investment Program. The PenFed Foundation, based in Alexandria, has provided more than $30 million since 2001 to veterans, active duty service members, families and caregivers. Schenck volunteers as CEO of the foundation without compensation and serves on several boards. PenFed, founded in 1935, serves over 1.6 million members worldwide and holds $23 billion in assets.

WIRED reports that Amazon Prime Day returns October 7–8, with early deals already available on WIRED-tested products. Updated September 30, 2025, the list adds deals on Amazon devices, a cheap laptop, a fitness tracker, a smart bird feeder, and other gadgets. Featured discounts include the Apple iPad (2025), MacBook Air (M4, 2025), Arlo Pro 5S Security Camera, Kindle Scribe (2024), Anker MagGo Power Bank, and Ultrahuman Ring Air.

The Nebraska Supreme Court affirmed a Burt County district court judgment in favor of Farmers State Bank of Craig against Samuel J. Lydick on a $3,000 promissory note, and in favor of Everett J. Martin on Lydick’s fraud claims. Lydick alleged the note stemmed from earlier notes given for stock in the Missouri Valley Cattle Loan Company, which he claimed he was fraudulently induced to buy, and asserted Martin acted for himself and the bank in the alleged fraud.

The trial court directed a verdict against Lydick on his affirmative claim against the bank, submitted to the jury whether the bank was a purchaser for value in good faith before maturity without notice of defects, and the jury found for the bank. The jury also found for Martin on the fraud allegations. The court properly withdrew a second stock-purchase issue due to lack of competent evidence.

The Supreme Court held the evidence supported the verdicts, the jury instructions were proper, and refused instructions were either covered, unsupported by evidence, or contrary to Nebraska law. Relying on Bank of Commerce & Savings v. Randell, the court held a payee may be a holder in due course when it receives a negotiable instrument in good faith, for value, before maturity, and without notice of infirmity, from a holder to whom it was negotiated as a completed instrument. The judgment was affirmed.

China has spent two decades modernising the PLA to match its rising global influence, defend regional interests, protect trade routes, support initiatives like AIIB and OBOR, and counter US military presence in the Indo-Pacific. The PLA has transformed significantly since the late 1990s, contributing to a more assertive China, though its future use remains uncertain.

Latin American stocks rebounded Monday as appetite for risky assets improved after U.S. officials downplayed the prospect of imminent war with North Korea. Mexico’s S&P/BVM IPC rose 1.1% after its biggest weekly decline in eight months, while Brazil’s Bovespa reached its highest level since May, led by gains in Cia Paranaense de Energia. Currency moves were subdued, with the Mexican peso firming as traders awaited NAFTA talks and the Brazilian real seesawing ahead of an expected fiscal goal revision.

North Korea’s rarely traded defaulted debt is likely to become even less accessible after new sanctions imposed over its missile tests. The debt, tied to loans in default since the 1980s, was repackaged in 1997 into transferable securities by BNP, with syndicated loans of about $1 billion face value and total obligations estimated at about $3 billion in 2013. Trading had occurred since around 2000, and prices rose after Kim Jong-il’s death on hopes of economic opening, but the market effectively froze in early 2013 after sanctions. Exotix Capital said it has not seen trades in three to four years. New U.N. sanctions could cut North Korea’s $3 billion annual export revenue by a third. Franklin Emerging Markets Debt Opportunities Fund held $15.5 million principal in NK Debt Corporation zero-coupon bonds in 2016 but assigned no value. Experts said resolution is unlikely for a long time, comparing North Korea’s debt situation to Cuba’s.

Court documents say Jennifer Bartell was shot several times by Joshua Bowen on March 14 after a Facebook argument involving Bartell’s daughter escalated into a planned meeting and then a confrontation at Bartell’s home. Bowen, Albany Pierce, Shaunicka Cooley, and Shyrayno Jackson were arrested. Neighbors said they were shocked but relieved the shooting was not random.

The passage presents a modular framework for AI-driven, multi-modal synchrotron experiments at NSLS-II, designed to coordinate XRD and XAFS measurements across multiple beamlines while keeping humans in control through adjudicators and configurable AI agents. The framework uses Bluesky, queue servers, Tiled, JupyterHub, secure data streaming, and virtualized agents for data processing, analysis, Bayesian optimization-based decision-making, and measurement suggestions.

The authors demonstrate synchronous XRD and XAFS mapping of Al-Ni-Pt combinatorial thin-film libraries at the PDF and BMM beamlines. AI agents processed data in real time, communicated between beamlines, and supported autonomous and grid-based acquisition strategies. Post-experiment analysis showed spatial composition gradients from EXAFS and identified FCC and FCT structural trends from XRD, though detailed phase quantification was limited by overlapping peaks, texturing, anisotropic broadening, and uncertainty in phase models.

A digital twin was developed for testing and benchmarking autonomous diffraction workflows without using beamtime. Simulated Al-Li-Fe oxide mapping campaigns showed that AI-driven measurement selection outperformed geometric grid and random sampling strategies in resolving phase boundaries and localized features. The passage concludes that the framework supports extensible, FAIR-aligned, human-AI collaborative experiments and can serve as a foundation for routine multi-modal, multi-beamline AI-assisted studies at user facilities.

Let’s Grow Kids, a Vermont child care advocacy organization founded by Rick Davis in 2015, was designed to operate for 10 years and sunset in 2025. Led by Aly Richards, it raised more than $70 million, grew to 40 staff, and helped build support for Act 76, Vermont’s 2023 law creating a near-universal child care program. Since then, over 100 child care programs have opened, adding more than 1,000 spaces, 230 early educator jobs, and tuition assistance eligibility for 4,000 more children.

Leaders said the planned sunset created urgency, accountability, philanthropic support, and a focus on building lasting infrastructure. The organization spent years preparing permanent partners to continue work on financing, workforce, data, advocacy, and implementation. Former staff have moved into key roles across Vermont’s child care system, while remaining staff are transitioning to the Let’s Grow Kids Action Network to help protect Act 76 funding.

Vermont’s system is not fully universal; an estimated 80% to 90% of families with children in child care qualify for subsidies. Richards said other states have sought guidance on Vermont’s approach, and she argues the sunset strategy was central to the campaign’s effectiveness.

A federal judge ruled that Nirvana’s 1991 album cover showing Spencer Elden as a naked baby underwater was not child pornography and dismissed his 2021 lawsuit. Judge Fernando Olguin said the image was not lascivious and was most analogous to a family photo of a nude child bathing.

A Florida Museum study found that lice parasitizing primates and humans have continuously hosted vitamin-producing bacterial endosymbionts for at least 20 to 25 million years, matching the period when great apes and old world monkeys shared a common ancestor. Lice rely on these bacteria for essential vitamins missing from blood, while the bacteria cannot live outside their hosts. Researchers sequenced endosymbiont genomes from lice on humans, chimpanzees, gorillas and red colobus monkeys, finding very small genomes of 530,000 to 570,000 base pairs. The genomes show extensive remodeling over 25 million years, with key symbiosis genes clustered together and much of the genome devoted to B-vitamin synthesis. The findings help illuminate lice, bacterial genome evolution and primate evolutionary history.

A University of Bern-led study used deep learning to identify dust devils in more than 50,000 satellite images from ESA’s CaSSIS and HRSC cameras, then analyzed stereo images of about 300 dust devils to measure their movement. Researchers found Martian dust devils and surrounding near-surface winds can reach up to 44 m/s, or about 160 km/h, faster than previous surface measurements suggested. These winds may lift much more dust into the Martian atmosphere than previously assumed, affecting weather, climate, dunes, and surface features. The findings provide global-scale data over about two decades and may improve atmospheric models and planning for future Mars missions.

A Utah audit found the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control mispriced seven items after a markup change, overcharging business customers $1,161 and losing $186 on other sales. The department plans refunds and added software checks. Auditors also found a delayed $4.6 million revenue transfer to school lunch and public safety programs, later corrected.

The study examined whether resting-state functional connectivity (FC) of the nucleus accumbens (NAc) predicts the course of ADHD symptoms in adults newly diagnosed with ADHD. Fifty-four physically healthy adult patients were assessed at diagnosis (t1) using the Wender-Reimherr Interview (WRI), underwent baseline fMRI, and were followed up about three years later (t2). All patients were prescribed methylphenidate after diagnosis; at follow-up, 34 were still taking stimulants and 20 had discontinued medication after non-response.

ADHD symptom severity decreased overall from t1 to t2. Higher baseline WRI scores were associated with lower FC between the NAc and the right paracingulate gyrus. Greater symptom improvement over time was associated with lower FC between the NAc and the right anterior insular cortex. Medication status influenced connectivity-outcome relationships: among patients continuing stimulant treatment, higher FC between the NAc and right posterior insular cortex predicted better long-term outcome, while among those no longer receiving medication, higher FC predicted worse outcome. Motion-related effects did not differ significantly between treated and non-responder groups.

The authors conclude that FC patterns between the reward system, default mode network, and salience network correlate with ADHD symptom course and medication response. They suggest NAc connectivity may have potential as a biological marker for stimulant response and clinical prognosis, while noting limitations including small sample size, resting-state fMRI constraints, and the need for larger and more comprehensive future studies.

The passage describes the 1793 yellow fever epidemic in Philadelphia, linked to Aedes aegypti mosquitoes and Caribbean refugees during a hot, dry summer. More than 5,000 people, over 10 percent of the city’s population, died before the outbreak ended. Doctors including Benjamin Rush and Philip Syng Physick tried ineffective measures such as bloodletting, smoke purification, and quarantine before later research identified mosquitoes as the vector.

The passage connects this history to modern concerns, noting Brazil’s severe yellow fever outbreak beginning in December 2016, with hundreds of confirmed and suspected cases and fears of spread near major cities. Pablo Tebas notes that mosquito control advice remains similar to past guidance, but vaccines are essential where outbreak conditions are difficult to avoid. The yellow fever vaccine, widely used since 1939, is described as 99 percent effective and generally requiring one dose. Brazil has requested millions of doses, and WHO recommends vaccination for travelers to Brazil and nearby areas. The passage also mentions Penn research into Zika vaccines using DNA and mRNA technologies.

Rachael Caplan, 29, has severe Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS), leaving her bedridden in her parents’ Thornhill home and in constant pain. Once athletic and pursuing family law, she developed symptoms during law school and was diagnosed in 2013 after about 18 months. Doctors describe CRPS as a rare neurological pain disorder that can spread, disable patients, and is much more treatable if caught early. Caplan’s treatments, including physiotherapy and opioids, have largely failed or worsened symptoms, though green light therapy has recently helped her sleep and reduced head pain. Her friends and family launched the #AceThisFire ice-water challenge to raise awareness. Caplan hopes sharing her story will lead to faster diagnoses, better treatments, and possibly remission.

Gulf Island Fabrication trades at a significant discount to book value after a sharp share-price decline following a difficult fourth quarter. The company operates fabrication, shipyards, and services divisions, but its offshore platform and offshore support vessel markets remain highly pressured, with oversupply in the Gulf of Mexico and muted demand for new offshore platforms. Operational issues also hurt results: two support vessels for Hornbeck Offshore had technical problems, delaying delivery to 2019 and causing a $23.9 million loss.

Despite weak margins and bleak near-term results, the author highlights positives: Gulf Island has little debt, its backlog is now more concentrated in shipyards, and it has potential growth opportunities including the SeaOne Caribbean Fuels Supply Project and a memorandum of understanding related to an East Coast offshore wind project. The company is also selling non-core Texas facilities, including a South Yard under a $55 million purchase option, with total book value for related assets around $100 million. The author argues that if sales occur near book value, the remaining business is being valued very cheaply relative to market capitalization, making the stock attractive on valuation, with potential contracts as an added upside.

QoCGM is an open-source MATLAB tool for analyzing preprocessed continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) data from CSV files. It removes duplicate timestamps, identifies missing periods using sampling frequency and tolerance settings, and handles missing data through PCHIP interpolation or removal. The tool outputs derived CGM metrics to CSV, including descriptive statistics, time-in-range measures, glycemic risk indicators, variability metrics, glycemic control indicators, hypoglycemia events, and multiscale entropy. Some metrics are calculated for whole-day, daytime, nighttime, and day-to-day variation.

An example analysis used seven days of CGM data from 324 participants with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes in the DiaMonT trial. Median glucose was 162 mg/dL, median time-in-range was 65%, and median coefficient of variation was 24%. Coefficient of determination analysis showed overlap among many metrics, while day-to-day standard deviation of TIR and mean, MCI, Mobility, and DTpM had low R² values with other metrics, suggesting distinct information. Diurnal and nocturnal TIR metrics also differed, supporting separate analysis. The authors conclude QoCGM may support CGM research and clinical analysis, while further research is needed on clinical implications.

European statesmen at the conference will likely focus on securing means of recuperation, as demobilization may cause revolutionary discontent or economic crisis without raw materials, transport, markets, and credit. Control over allocating these resources will be a major negotiating instrument. The passage argues that Germany’s influence in the Near East and eastern Europe remains central, but its reconstruction depends on access to overseas supplies and markets because Middle Europe cannot function as a closed economic system. Two German imperialist schools are described: the Kühlmann-Helfferich group seeks accommodation with western nations to gain overseas supplies while maintaining dominance in the Near East, while the Fatherland Party seeks access through military and naval power. Belgium is presented as the pivot of German policy, with its control offering commercial advantages, limiting England’s ability to land forces in France, and potentially extending German influence through an administrative division involving Flanders.

Dunkin' Donuts will launch its fall menu on Aug. 28, bringing back pumpkin spice and adding maple pecan coffees and lattes, pumpkin cream cheese, and a maple sugar bacon breakfast sandwich for a limited time. The company expects maple to appeal to customers similarly to pumpkin. McDonald's and Starbucks have not announced this year's fall drink releases. Dunkin' has reported better-than-expected earnings for seven straight quarters, helped by new and limited-time products, including breakfast sandwiches, cold brew, and fruited iced tea.

The speaker says a player was given a day off and remains day to day. They note second-period struggles in Boston and emphasize making every shift count. They say key players are performing better than their points show despite strong opposing defense and goaltending. The team remains focused on one game at a time and believes it is ready for the challenge.

Sarasota County petitioned for certiorari to review a Department of Administration declaratory statement that a proposed crude oil splitter in Manatee County was not subject to development of regional impact procedures under Chapter 380 unless covered by listed administrative rules. The court denied the petition, holding Sarasota County lacked standing to invoke judicial review because it was not a developer, regional planning agency, appropriate local government, or state planning agency authorized to initiate the DRI process. The court stated that an unfavorable declaratory statement alone does not create standing and suggested the county seek action through entities designated by statute.

Chief Judge Boardman concurred, noting Sarasota County could proceed through its regional planning agency or under the Florida Environmental Protection Act. Judge Scheb dissented, arguing the court should review the declaratory statement as final agency action and that the Department wrongly limited DRI determinations to developments listed in administrative regulations.

ICICI Bank said its mortgage loan portfolio crossed Rs 1.5 trillion, making it the largest private player in the segment, and aims to grow it to Rs 2 trillion by FY20 at 15% annually. The mortgage book is half of its Rs 3 trillion retail loan portfolio. Growth is expected from tier II and III towns and supported by PM Awas Yojna. The bank is expanding digitisation, online project approvals, approved project repositories, and loan processing centres.

Research by Tweak Mattress found the average Brit wakes three times a night, while one in 10 wakes seven to 10 times. Common causes include needing the toilet, discomfort, snoring, partners taking bed space, tossing and turning, sleep talking, phone use, reading or TV, nightmares, and anxiety. Psychologist Robert Stewart said sleep quality is affected by sleep hygiene, such as routines and avoiding food, drink, and screens before bed, and by sleep cycles. He noted people are most likely to wake during REM sleep, and disturbances like noise, snoring, or discomfort can prevent them returning to sleep.

The passage reviews Larry Connors’ R3 mean-reversion strategy from “High Probability ETF Trading,” tested on ETFs using rules based on price above the 200-day moving average and 2-day RSI declines, entering below RSI 10 and exiting above RSI 70. The author could not fully replicate Connors’ original results and found about half the strategies performed worse over the following 12 years. A 25-ETF portfolio test from 2000 to December 2020 produced 992 trades, a 75% win rate, 0.68% average gain, 2.08 profit factor, -16% maximum drawdown, and 6.47% CAGR. For SPY and QQQ, profit factor was 3.37 but CAGR was 2.69%. The passage concludes the R3 strategy still works, especially in equity markets, but may be improved.

The passage presents a modelling study estimating COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness over time using national vaccine effectiveness data from England for Delta and Omicron BA.1/BA.2. The authors model waning and boosting of immunity for AZD1222, BNT162b2, and mRNA-1273 against mild disease, hospitalisation, and death, using an inferred immune level and a logistic relationship to protection.

The model estimates a 6.5-fold reduction in vaccine-induced immune level against Omicron relative to Delta. It finds that mRNA-1273 generated the highest inferred immune levels, followed by BNT162b2 and AZD1222. Protection waned rapidly at first, with an estimated initial half-life of 33 days, followed by slower decline with a half-life of 580 days. One year after boosting, predicted protection against Omicron hospitalisation was moderate and protection against infection or mild disease was low.

Using immunogenicity data for Moderna’s bivalent mRNA-1273.214 vaccine, the authors estimate a 1.61-fold higher neutralising antibody titre against BA.1 compared with the original mRNA-1273 vaccine. They predict that bivalent boosting gives similar short-term protection against severe outcomes to the original booster but more sustained protection over one year, with hospitalisation effectiveness estimated at 77.9% after one year versus 60.0% for the original vaccine.

The authors conclude that modelling clinical effectiveness with immunogenicity data may help guide booster strategies, especially as variants evolve and clinical comparator groups become harder to identify. Limitations include inability to separate infection- and vaccine-induced immunity, lack of direct immunological measurements, and uncertainty in distinguishing COVID-19 hospitalisations and deaths from incidental positive tests.
The Eighth Circuit denied Earl Ringo’s petitions for rehearing en banc and by the panel. Judge Bye would have granted en banc rehearing, and Judge Benton did not participate.

N62.4 billion in 91-day and 182-day Treasury bills and N168.1 billion in OMO maturities were expected to enter the market, though the bills would be rolled over. Afrinvest said CBN liquidity mop-ups would keep OBB and overnight rates in check. System liquidity was negative last week due to primary market issuances, Retail SMIS forex auction, and N28.6 billion in OMO sales. OBB and overnight rates spiked midweek before easing after a N113.05 billion OMO maturity, but closed higher week-on-week.

The treasury bills market was bearish, with average yields rising to 18.5% due to tight liquidity. The Federal Executive Council approved dollar-backed treasury instruments to restructure debt, reduce borrowing costs, and extend maturities, subject to National Assembly approval. The government also approved the 2018–2020 MTEF/FSP, targeting growth of 3.5% in 2018, 4.5% in 2019, and 7% in 2020.

In forex, the CBN continued interventions, including a $100 million SMIS auction. The official naira rate stayed at N305.55/$, NAFEX appreciated to N365.91/$, NIFEX depreciated to N365.20/$, and the parallel rate remained N367/$. Afrinvest expected short- to medium-term forex stability.

The domestic bond market was bearish, with average yields at 16.8%. The importers’ and exporters’ forex window attracted $4 billion from foreign investors since April, and the Bankers’ Committee said exchange rates were nearing convergence.

Six Texas public university systems have ordered reviews of curricula, syllabi and course descriptions amid conservative political scrutiny of faculty teaching gender identity. Texas A&M began an audit after backlash over a children’s literature lesson, and systems including University of North Texas, University of Texas, University of Houston and Texas Woman’s University initiated reviews citing compliance with laws, executive orders or state guidance. The passage notes no current federal or state law prohibits public university professors from teaching about transgender identity, and it remains unclear whether courses will be censored or removed.

Faculty advocates warned that political control over teaching harms education. Conservative critics have used publicly posted syllabi and course information to identify faculty. Platforms such as Simple Syllabus, used by many universities, can make syllabi searchable; some Texas institutions allow public access, partly due to a state law requiring public syllabi. A University of Houston lecturer said a conservative news site targeted him using information from Simple Syllabus. The company said it offers privacy controls, while faculty face conflicting pressures to limit public details but also provide detailed syllabi to avoid complaints.

Love in the Time of Chasmosaurs is an educational dinosaur website focused on paleoart, scientific discoveries, reviews, museum visits, and dinosaur news. Active since 2009, it features factual reports, links to scientific articles, humorous critiques of books, toys, films, and TV shows, and monthly news round-ups.

Olivia Munn had no breast cancer symptoms and negative mammogram, ultrasound, and genetic tests, but a two-minute lifetime risk assessment showed a 37% risk. She pursued an MRI and was diagnosed with stage 1 breast cancer at 43. The same assessment later led to her mother’s stage 1 diagnosis. Munn said the assessment should be standard care.

Hugh Jackman revealed he is undergoing treatment again for basal cell carcinoma, a common and rarely fatal skin cancer. He credited frequent checks and doctors, urged sunscreen use, and has previously been treated several times since his first diagnosis in 2013.

The passage describes a study examining COVID-19 mRNA vaccination effects on glucose control in people with healthy, pre-diabetic, and diabetic status and in mice. Vaccination increased SARS-CoV-2 spike-related immune markers similarly across human groups, but booster vaccination was associated with worsened insulin resistance indicators in pre-diabetic and diabetic subjects, including higher HbA1c, HOMA-IR, triglycerides, and TyG index, without significant fasting glucose or insulin changes. In mice, repeated BNT162b2 vaccination impaired glucose tolerance, insulin tolerance, and insulin signaling, while increasing triglycerides. Metformin improved vaccine-associated insulin resistance and insulin signaling in mice without reducing vaccine-related immune markers. The authors recommend further surveillance and long-term studies in pre-diabetic and diabetic individuals after booster vaccination.

Doug Ford launched his Progressive Conservative election campaign at the Toronto Congress Centre after becoming party leader. The rally drew an enthusiastic crowd and included support from former leadership rivals Christine Elliott, Caroline Mulroney and Tanya Granic Allen. Ford framed Premier Kathleen Wynne and the Liberals as his opponents, criticized government debt and spending, and promised prosperity for all Ontarians. Kory Teneycke is expected to manage Ford’s campaign, with Jeff Silverstein as communications manager. Party candidates and supporters expressed optimism while acknowledging the election would be difficult.

Stan Lee was hospitalized at Cedar-Sinai after experiencing shortness of breath and an irregular heartbeat, but his condition remained stable and he has since been released. His representative said he is doing well, though he will return for monitoring. Lee recently appeared at the Hollywood premiere of “Black Panther,” which he created with Jack Kirby in 1966.

Valeant, J. Michael Pearson, Pershing Square Capital Management and William Ackman entered a litigation management agreement related to a California putative class action and Allergan litigation. The agreement includes fee-sharing, forbearance by Pershing Square parties, mutual claims releases, and terminates Nov. 1, 2017, absent a settlement stipulation.

Severe storms spawned tornadoes across the Southeast on Monday night, damaging homes, downing trees and causing power outages in northern Alabama. The National Weather Service in Huntsville reported at least three confirmed tornadoes, and Limestone County officials reported roof damage, displaced outbuildings and road closures but no injuries. Jacksonville State University reported significant campus damage, including major roof damage at Pete Mathews Coliseum. Tornado warnings remained in parts of northern Alabama and southern Tennessee, with a tornado watch issued for much of northern Georgia. Forecasters warned of possible intense tornadoes, damaging winds, and hail up to 3 inches. Alabama officials increased emergency staffing, schools dismissed early, and the University of Alabama suspended operations and opened shelters.

This prospective study examined inflammatory and oxidative stress markers in 101 cardiomyopathy patients and 101 healthy controls. Patients included 43 with dilated cardiomyopathy and 58 with other cardiomyopathies. Blood samples were analyzed for CRP, TNF-α, IL-6, NT-proBNP, malondialdehyde, and glutathione peroxidase activity. Cardiomyopathy patients had significantly higher CRP, TNF-α, malondialdehyde, glutathione peroxidase, and NT-proBNP levels than controls. TNF-α correlated positively with glutathione peroxidase and malondialdehyde, while NT-proBNP correlated with malondialdehyde and glutathione peroxidase. The authors conclude that inflammatory and oxidative stress markers are correlated in cardiomyopathy patients, suggesting interaction between these processes in late-stage cardiomyopathy.

The speaker says big-game experience, preparation, habits, and team play matter most, while routines such as game-day skates help maintain focus. He emphasizes not taking on too much personally and says the team understands what it must do. After winning, he describes it as a dream come true made possible by sacrifices, shot blocking, goaltending, and contributions from many players. He explains a painful knee injury that limited his ability to skate and led him to sit out rather than hurt the team. He also reflects on veteran teammates finally winning, support from traveling Pittsburgh fans, and the loyalty of fans after difficult years and the previous season’s disappointment.

Premier Li Keqiang said China will further open its economy, expand access to services and manufacturing, lower import tariffs, and allow foreign and domestic firms to compete fairly. He also said China will not force technology transfers and will better protect intellectual property, amid rising global trade war concerns.

Amadeus FiRe AG issued a correction to a 10 February 2017 major holding notification. BNP Paribas Investment Partners S.A., Paris, crossed a voting rights threshold on 9 February 2017 due to acquisition/disposal of shares. Its resulting position was 259,295 voting rights, or 4.99% of Amadeus FiRe AG’s total 5,198,237 voting rights, down from 5.003%. No voting rights through instruments were reported. BNP Paribas Investment Partners Belgium S.A. was listed as a shareholder holding directly 3% or more.
Ajman’s ruler Sheikh Humaid bin Rashid Al Nuaimi issued a decree reducing the tourism tax on hotels and tourism companies from 10% to 7% until December 31 to boost tourism and investment.

Huntington University Hospital’s cardiac surgery patients received blood transfusions at rates well above national and peer averages, with about 71% of AVR and CABG patients transfused from 2011 to 2013. Research cited in the case linked transfusions after cardiac surgery to lower survival, and bleeding-related complications cost HUH nearly $8 million in 2013. Dr. Frank Young was asked to lead a blood conservation project aiming to cut blood product use by two-thirds within a year, reduce costs by $2.5 million annually, and improve long-term survival.

Young faced challenges from HUH’s complex structure, where cardiac surgical teams included many specialists who did not report to surgeons, and transfusion decisions could be made without surgeon notification. He also had to persuade veteran surgeons accustomed to existing routines. Supporters included anesthesiologist Anil Gupta, administrators, nurses, perfusionists, cardiologists, and some surgeons. Proposed techniques included autologous blood harvest and retrograde autologous priming. Young needed to determine how to begin, involve stakeholders, address skeptics, and make changes sustainable.

Meb Faber’s Three-Way Momentum/Trend-Following Model invests equally in stocks, bonds, and gold when each asset’s monthly 3-bar moving average is above its 10-bar moving average. The article describes it as more momentum than trend-following and says it returned 13% annually from 1971 to 2015. A backtest using GLD, SPY, and TLT from 2006 turned $100,000 into $422,000, with an 8.9% CAGR, 57% win rate, 1.6 profit factor, and 18% maximum drawdown. Since 2015, performance was weaker at 5.3% annually, but drawdowns remained low. With 1.5 leverage, returns rose to 13.1% with a 26% maximum drawdown. Optimization showed similar results across nearby settings, suggesting the strategy was not curve-fitted.

The passage defines soccer passing direction terminology based on the ball’s expected path from a player in possession, generally assuming the player faces the attacking goal. Main directions include forward, angled right, right, back and right, back, back and left, left, and angled left. It explains related terms such as deep, downfield, down the line, long, short, square, lateral, wide, diagonal, reverse, centering, and back passes. It also defines broader concepts including angle of a pass, back heel, center, far post, near post, outlet, possession pass, reverse field, switch fields, horizontal axis, vertical axis, and straight-line runs or passes.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 31, 2017, reporting that it issued a press release and data sheet on its financial results for the first fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2016. The filing lists the press release and data sheet as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2 and was signed by CFO Luca Maestri.

Mark Haedicke emailed the State Bar of Michigan e-Journal list asking to be removed. The statistical analysis plan compares dasiglucagon 0.6 mg primarily with placebo, with GlucaGen included as a marketed reference. Based on assumed median recovery times of 10 minutes for dasiglucagon and over 50 minutes for placebo, 20 dasiglucagon and 10 placebo patients provide 90% power using a 2-sided log-rank test at 5% significance with 45 minutes follow-up; 10 GlucaGen patients are expected to suffice.

Analyses will use tables, listings, and figures following ICH conventions. Testing is generally 2-sided at the 0.05 level. Continuous variables will be summarized descriptively; categorical variables by counts and percentages. SAS 9.4 or higher will be used, with PK/PD analyses in Phoenix WinNonlin 6.4 or higher. Analyses defined before unblinding are a priori; later analyses are post hoc and exploratory.

Analysis sets include the safety analysis set, full analysis set (FAS), and per protocol set (PPS). The primary endpoint will be analyzed on the FAS, with supportive PPS analysis; safety analyses will use the safety set. Protocol deviations affecting PPS inclusion will be determined before unblinding.

The primary efficacy endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery, defined as the first ≥20 mg/dL increase from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose. Secondary endpoints include plasma glucose recovery within 30, 20, 15, and 10 minutes, and plasma glucose changes from baseline at those times or at rescue. The primary model adjusts for age group and injection site. Missing data will not be imputed.

Multiplicity will be controlled hierarchically across the primary endpoint and secondary endpoints for dasiglucagon versus placebo. GlucaGen comparisons are not part of the inferential hierarchy. Time to recovery will be summarized using Kaplan-Meier methods and analyzed with a stratified log-rank test; sensitivity and supportive analyses include alternate censoring approaches, Wilcoxon testing, Cox proportional hazards models, and linear interpolation of recovery time.

Secondary recovery rates will be analyzed using Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests stratified by age group and injection site, with Fisher’s exact test if needed. Plasma glucose changes will be analyzed by ANOVA with treatment, age group, and injection site.

PK analyses will summarize plasma dasiglucagon and glucagon concentrations and non-compartmental PK metrics. PD analysis includes plasma glucose response as area under the effect curve above baseline from 0 to 30 minutes. Concentration and glucose results will be listed, summarized, and plotted.

Safety analyses include exposure, insulin administration, hypoglycemia induction, trial medication, rescue glucose infusion, local tolerability, adverse events, laboratory data, vital signs, physical examination, ECG, and immunogenicity. TEAEs are defined as post-dose events or worsening pre-existing events. Adverse events will be coded with MedDRA and summarized by treatment, system organ class, preferred term, relationship, severity, and special categories. Concomitant medications will be coded using WHODrug and summarized by ATC class and preferred name.

The appendices specify table, listing, figure formatting, handling of missing or incomplete dates, calculation formulas, SAS programming quality control requirements, and a planned list of outputs.

Phlogopite, a layered dark mica mineral, is susceptible to ionizing radiation and is relevant to geological dating, radionuclide waste storage studies, and 2D optoelectronic applications. The study models its response to irradiation using the XTANT-3 code, which combines tight-binding molecular dynamics, transport Monte Carlo, and Boltzmann collision methods to capture electronic and atomic nonequilibrium, nonthermal, and nonadiabatic effects.

The calculated electronic density of states agrees qualitatively with prior DFT results. The ideal crystal band gap is 7.5 eV and decreases to about 6.5 eV at room temperature. Under a 92 eV, 10 fs photon pulse, simulations predict first damage at about 0.17 eV/atom, where hydrogen detaches and migrates while other sublattices remain stable. This agrees with experimental β- and γ-irradiation damage near 1000 kGy, equivalent to about 0.2 eV/atom.

Electron-phonon coupling cools the electronic system and suppresses some nonthermal damage, raising the damage threshold compared with Born-Oppenheimer simulations. At about 0.4 eV/atom, Mg atoms begin liquid-like diffusion while other sublattices remain stable, forming a superionic state. At about 0.5 eV/atom, the whole lattice disorders, with H and Mg disordering fastest and Al and K slowest. Around 0.9 eV/atom, the band gap collapses and the material becomes metallic. At about 2 eV/atom, nonthermal atomic heating occurs on femtosecond timescales, most strongly affecting oxygen and potassium.

The results indicate multiple transient irradiation-induced states in phlogopite, including hydrogen-migrating, superionic, disordered, semi-metallic, and metallic states. Threshold fluences were also estimated to guide future X-ray irradiation experiments.

The lecture evaluates Winthrop Center and 425 Park Avenue from stakeholder, market, cost, and risk perspectives. Discussion focused on uncertainty around tenant willingness to pay, evidence from cognitive and productivity studies, and the need to target tenants who value health benefits. The project secured Citadel as an anchor tenant at record-high rents, but later faced financial distress due to construction delays from retaining the existing structure, wiping out equity before Blackstone salvaged the project.

The lecture reviews utility from beliefs, focusing on anticipatory utility, information avoidance, overoptimism, and learning biases. People may avoid negative information, such as health risks, when beliefs themselves provide utility, but incorrect beliefs can distort decisions when actions like treatment, saving, travel, or family planning depend on accurate information. Overoptimism may increase current utility, but it can also lead to disappointment or poor choices.

Evidence discussed includes studies showing people are optimistic about future life outcomes, risks, abilities, and traits. However, MIT students in survey data appear under-confident academically, especially female students, possibly due to frequent feedback, social comparison, or motivational effects. Ego utility is introduced as the value people get from feeling good about themselves, distinct from but related to anticipatory utility. Positive illusions may support psychological well-being, while “depressive realism” suggests realistic expectations may harm mental health.

The lecture then discusses empirical evidence on motivated beliefs. Experiments by Eil and Rao show people update more from favorable information about IQ or attractiveness than from unfavorable information, and are more willing to pay for information expected to be positive. Other work suggests motivated memory, where people later remember positive signals more than negative ones. Real-world evidence includes overconfident investors trading more and earning less, and overconfident managers making value-destroying mergers.

The lecture shifts to Bayesian learning, noting that people often know the direction in which evidence should move beliefs but struggle with how much to update. Because Bayes’ rule is cognitively demanding, people use heuristics, which are useful but can produce systematic errors. Three deviations are discussed: gambler’s fallacy, hot-hand fallacy, and base-rate neglect. The gambler’s fallacy is the belief that an outcome becomes more likely after not occurring for a while in independent draws. The hot-hand fallacy is the belief that recent success predicts continued success. Both can arise from belief in the “law of small numbers.” Base-rate neglect occurs when people overweight new information and underweight prior probabilities.

The lecture also covers heuristics and biases, including representativeness, illustrated by the Linda problem, and availability, where people judge probabilities by how easily examples come to mind. It concludes that understanding why people are misinformed matters for policy: salience and information provision may help when people miss information or hold wrong theories, but may be less effective or even harmful when people intentionally avoid information because beliefs provide utility.

Topological insulator lasers aim to address common laser problems such as sensitivity to defects, loss of efficiency, unstable output power, unwanted colors, and distorted beam profiles at higher power. In topological insulators, the bulk resists electron flow while surface states can conduct with reduced scattering because reversing direction requires a spin flip that is difficult in an insulator. The article explains that an analogous protected state can be created for light using a lattice of optical waveguide rings.

In the described laser, rings on the edge are excited so light travels around the perimeter while the interior absorbs it. Carefully placed intermediary rings control how light leaks between rings, creating a protected state in which unwanted light is scattered out and the protected light is amplified. Researchers modeled and fabricated such structures, comparing protected and unprotected edge-state lasers. The protected laser continued operating even with missing rings, was more efficient, and did not produce new colors as power increased, unlike the unprotected version. The article notes possible relevance for applications requiring stable, sharply defined wavelengths, including 5G networks and space-based interferometers.

Researchers recorded medical problems in participants who received at least one study vaccine dose. In Phase 1, some participants had temporary drops in lymphocyte counts 1 to 3 days after Dose 1 of BNT162b1 or BNT162b2, which returned to normal by 6 to 8 days after Dose 1; none had low lymphocytes 6 to 8 days after Dose 2. Injection site reactions and systemic events within 7 days were generally well tolerated, short-lived, and mostly mild or moderate. Pain at the injection site was the most common injection site reaction, while tiredness and headache were the most common systemic events.

In Phase 1, BNT162b1 and BNT162b2 doses of 10, 20, and 30 µg were well tolerated, but BNT162b1 100 µg was stopped after Dose 1 because of injection site reactions or systemic events. BNT162b2 30 µg was selected for Phase 2/3. No Phase 1 participants left because of medical problems. In Phase 2/3, 30 µg BNT162b2 was well tolerated, with safety results similar to earlier phases; fewer than 1% left due to medical problems in both BNT162b2 and placebo groups.

Serious medical problems were uncommon. In Phase 1, 2 BNT162b2 participants had serious medical problems, and researchers did not consider them vaccine-related. In Phase 2/3 and Phase 3 booster groups, few participants had serious medical problems, with no single serious problem occurring in at least 1% of participants; most were not considered vaccine-related. No participants died in Phase 1. In Phase 2/3, deaths occurred in BNT162b2 and placebo/BNT162b2 groups, but researchers did not believe they were caused by BNT162b2. No BNT162b2SA-naive Phase 3 participants died after receiving BNT162b2SA.

The lecture discusses neutral particle diagnostics for measuring ion distribution functions in plasma cores, where ions are well confined and fully ionized. Other diagnostics such as electron cyclotron emission, laser-induced fluorescence, and Thomson scattering are limited because they mainly measure electron properties or require bound electrons. Neutral diagnostics rely on core ions becoming neutrals, which can escape confinement and carry information about the ion distribution.

Neutral production can occur through charge exchange with edge neutrals or neutral beam injection. Neutral transport is limited by re-ionization processes, including electron impact ionization, ion impact ionization, and charge exchange with ions. Charge exchange is especially important because it has a large cross-section. For dense, hot plasmas, the neutral mean free path may be only about 10 cm, so useful core neutral escape requires relatively low line-integrated density, around less than \(10^{19}\,\text{m}^{-2}\).

Edge fueling can produce detectable core neutrals because many edge neutrals enter the plasma, while radiative recombination in the core is negligible because ionization rapidly removes neutrals. Passive charge exchange diagnostics use escaping neutrals, pass them through a stripping cell to turn them into ions, and separate them by velocity with a magnetic field to infer an energy distribution. This can reveal Maxwellian slopes, ion temperature, and fast-ion tails, but the measurement is line-integrated and difficult to localize.

Active diagnostics use neutral beams to localize charge exchange to the intersection of the beam and detector view. Neutral beams are also used for heating and current drive, but are limited in high-density machines. Charge exchange recombination spectroscopy uses neutral beams to give electrons to fully stripped impurity ions, causing them to emit characteristic photons. These emissions can measure impurity density, ion temperature, and flow velocity, though background emission and edge charge exchange can complicate interpretation; beam modulation can help isolate the signal.

Beam emission spectroscopy observes light from excited neutral beam atoms caused by collisions in the plasma. Since line intensity depends on electron density, it can measure localized density fluctuations important for turbulent transport, though accurate interpretation requires modeling relevant processes and beam attenuation.

The motional Stark effect uses the electric field seen by fast neutral beam particles moving through a magnetic field, proportional to \(V \times B\), which splits atomic energy levels. Measuring the splitting and polarization of emitted lines can provide magnetic field information, especially the poloidal field component, supporting magnetic reconstruction and current profile inference.

In late 2004, Toyota’s TMMGA operation faced serious quality and production problems with rear suspension cradles supplied by ChassisCo’s Athens, Georgia plant for the 2003 Suprima crossover. ChassisCo’s output was about 60% of target, parts were often nonconforming, defect tracking was weak, and Toyota feared the vehicle program and quality could be at risk.

Toyota’s Production System emphasized jidoka, just-in-time production, continuous improvement, problem solving, respect for people, close supplier collaboration, and rapid communication of problems. Toyota had previously built a strong relationship with ChassisCo during the 1997 Suprima launch, when Toyota supplied and tuned stamped parts, helped design the plant and equipment, and placed experienced support on site. ChassisCo later succeeded with Toyota’s Responsa program, leading Toyota to give it greater responsibility for the 2003 Suprima, including sourcing, logistics, inventory management, and project management for 85 parts.

The 2003 Suprima program proved far more complex. Automation increased sharply, weld content doubled, riveting was added, and ChassisCo assumed responsibility for second-tier suppliers. ChassisCo lacked sufficient project management, supplier management, quality systems, tool-and-die resources, and experience with Toyota’s technical requirements and tuning processes. Its organization had been decentralized, experienced launch knowledge was dispersed, and engineering resources were stretched across many global launches. Cost pressure also led ChassisCo to use tight plant space and low-cost suppliers, some of whom lacked relevant capability.

Toyota also underestimated the capability gap and did not discover second-tier supplier problems until late. Despite failing Toyota’s high-volume production trials, the Suprima launched in September 2003. During 2004, Athens suffered high scrap, downtime, overtime, poor parts quality, weak standardized work, and inadequate defect flowout control. Toyota audits found serious weld conformance issues, and an arc welding process audit scored Athens at 13%.

By fall 2004, both companies were strained. ChassisCo argued it lacked resources and was losing money, while Toyota stressed that the underlying quality problems had to be fixed immediately. Bernstein concluded that TMMGA’s resources were also taxed and that the situation required urgent next steps beyond the support already provided.

Radiotheranostics enables personalized cancer imaging and therapy, but current radiopharmaceutical therapy often uses standardized dosing that does not account for patient variability. Computational nuclear oncology and theranostic digital twins use physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models to estimate absorbed doses and treatment responses in tumors and normal tissues.

PBPK models in radiopharmaceutical therapy integrate computational, anatomical-physiological, radiopharmaceutical, and treatment protocol components. They can be developed using bottom-up, top-down, or middle-out approaches, with middle-out modeling combining mechanistic knowledge and patient-specific data. These models support dose optimization, imaging schedules, treatment intervals, and response simulation, but must be validated for their intended use.

Verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification are essential for clinical translation. Verification checks model structure, equations, parameters, units, simulations, and biological plausibility. Validation assesses goodness-of-fit, model selection, sensitivity analysis, and predictive performance using internal and external data. Uncertainty quantification characterizes variability in parameters and outputs using statistical distributions, sampling methods, confidence intervals, and accuracy metrics such as relative deviation, RMSE, and MAPE.

Extending PBPK models into dynamic theranostic digital twins introduces additional challenges because these systems require continuous integration of imaging, laboratory, and clinical data. Their verification and validation must be iterative and responsive to changing patient physiology, treatment response, and data variability.

The passage concludes that rigorous, fit-for-purpose VVUQ frameworks are needed to improve confidence in PBPK models, support regulatory acceptance, and enable their integration into clinical radiopharmaceutical therapy workflows.

McGill University researchers developed DOLPHIN, an AI tool that detects subtle disease markers inside single cells by analyzing exon and junction reads rather than collapsing data into gene-level counts. In pancreatic cancer data, DOLPHIN identified more than 800 previously missed markers and distinguished high-risk aggressive cancers from less severe cases, which could help guide treatment choices. Researchers say DOLPHIN may also support future digital models of human cells to simulate disease behavior and drug responses. Their next step is expanding the tool to analyze millions of cells.

The passage introduces a theory-driven framework for evaluating and improving LLM persuasion using Bayesian persuasion. It argues that existing evaluations of LLM persuasiveness are inconsistent, subjective, and hard to generalize. The proposed approach models persuasion as strategic information disclosure by a Sender that shifts a Receiver’s beliefs toward the Sender’s objective. It uses persuasion gains and conditional mutual information as measures of persuasive capability and strategic signaling. The paper constructs LLM-based persuasion environments from human persuasion datasets, validates the design with a 45-person human study, and benchmarks opinion-change tasks. Experiments indicate that frontier models such as DeepSeek-R1 achieve higher persuasion gains and more adaptive disclosure, while reinforcement learning can train small models like Llama3.2-3B-Instruct to reach persuasive capabilities comparable to larger models and transfer strategies across Receiver architectures.

The Clock Zone Offense is a simple 1-3-1 freelance passing offense with basic clockwise and counterclockwise rotations. It can be used against person-to-person defenses and zones, relying on sharp ball movement to create outside shots, basket cuts, post rolls, and weakside attacks. When a wing passes to the corner, the wing cuts to the basket and outside players rotate; if help defense collapses, the corner can feed the post. Ball reversal attacks the weak side when the defense matches the overload. A dribble-clear option lets the wing dribble toward the corner while the corner back cuts and roles are exchanged.

The offense includes continuity rules for corner passes, dribble clears, and reversal passes. It targets baseline weaknesses in a 1-3-1 zone and middle/corner vulnerabilities in a 1-2-2 zone. Against traps or double teams, the “Cat” 2-1-2 alignment uses quick passing, middle flashes, kick-outs, and trap escape passes. Additional rules include post rolls on baseline-corner passes and baseline back cuts when the ball enters the middle. Crunch-time specials include “Vegas,” a double screen away for a shot or post option, and “Back,” a weakside lob play.

The passage describes systems, methods, and computer-readable media for using a variable multiplexer to make an external vehicle device compatible with different vehicle communication bus pinout configurations. Vehicles may use standardized data link connectors, such as OBD ports, but manufacturers can assign different functions to pins, requiring different cables. The disclosed external device uses a configurable multiplexer to electronically map connector pins to the correct functions, enabling use with multiple vehicles through a single standardized cable.

The device may determine the correct pinout configuration by sending a vehicle identifier, such as a VIN, to a remote computing system with a vehicle data index, or by entering a listening mode to monitor bus data and compare received signals against known pinout configurations. It may also use checksum comparisons to identify the configuration that validates received data. The passage also describes related components, including a network gateway, connection detection, pinout determination and modification components, example methods for configuring the multiplexer, and general software and machine architectures for implementing the system.

DLSS 4 Multi Frame Generation on Blackwell generates up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame using faster, lower-VRAM AI models and AI-based optical flow. Enhanced Flip Metering moves frame pacing to the display engine for smoother timing, supported by fifth-generation Tensor Cores and the AI Management Processor.

DLSS 4 introduces transformer-based AI models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, replacing CNN-based models to improve temporal stability, reduce ghosting, enhance lighting detail, and improve detail in motion. Super Resolution reconstructs higher-resolution frames from lower-resolution inputs, Ray Reconstruction improves ray-traced image quality, and DLAA provides AI-based anti-aliasing at native resolution.

Blackwell introduces developer-created neural shaders, enabled through Cooperative Vectors APIs for DX12 and Vulkan, allowing Tensor Cores to be accessed through graphics shaders. Neural shader technologies include RTX Neural Materials, RTX Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. These techniques use neural networks for approximating materials, compressing textures, improving global illumination, rendering subsurface scattering, and generating more natural faces in real time.

The passage also describes Blackwell GPU products. GB202 targets the ultra-enthusiast segment and includes 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, and 768 Tensor Cores, with GeForce RTX 5090 as its first RTX 50 series product. GB203 targets the high-end segment with 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, and 336 Tensor Cores, powering RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 targets the performance segment with 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA Cores, 50 RT Cores, and 200 Tensor Cores, powering RTX 5070. NVIDIA states the specification is provided “as is” and may change without notice.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture centers on the TU102 GPU, with TU104 and TU106 using scaled-down versions of the same design. TU102 includes six GPCs, 36 TPCs, 72 SMs, 4608 CUDA Cores, 576 Tensor Cores, 72 RT Cores, 96 ROPs, 6 MB of L2 cache, and a 384-bit GDDR6 interface. Each SM includes CUDA Cores, Tensor Cores, an RT Core, texture units, register files, and configurable L1/shared memory.

Turing revises the SM architecture with concurrent FP32 and INT32 execution, independent thread scheduling, unified L1/shared memory/texture caching, and larger, faster caches. NVIDIA states these changes improve delivered performance per CUDA core by 50% compared with Pascal. Turing also introduces GDDR6 memory, improved compression, and higher effective bandwidth, with TU102-based RTX 2080 Ti delivering about 50% higher effective bandwidth than Pascal GP102-based GTX 1080 Ti.

Turing Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, and INT4 precision modes for deep learning training, inferencing, and neural graphics features. NVIDIA NGX uses Tensor Cores for AI-based features such as DLSS, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS is trained using high-quality reference images and aims to improve performance while maintaining image quality.

Turing adds RT Cores in each SM to accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time ray tracing with NVIDIA RTX, Microsoft DXR, OptiX, and related APIs. The architecture supports hybrid rendering, combining rasterization and ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, and ambient occlusion. NVIDIA states Turing can perform ray tracing about 10 times faster than Pascal using RT Cores.

The architecture includes second-generation NVLink on TU102 and TU104 for multi-GPU communication and SLI. TU102 provides two x8 NVLink links for 100 GB/s bidirectional bandwidth, while TU104 provides one x8 link. Turing also includes a new display engine supporting DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, HDR processing, enhanced NVENC and NVDEC video capabilities, USB Type-C, and VirtualLink for VR headset connectivity.

Additional graphics features include Mesh Shading, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, Multi-View Rendering, improved resource management, and VR-focused enhancements. VRS supports content adaptive shading, motion adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. MVR extends Pascal’s SMP capabilities and supports up to four hardware views per pass.

TU104 includes six GPCs, 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, and is used in products such as GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. Tesla T4 uses a TU104 configuration with 2560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores for inferencing workloads. TU106, used in GeForce RTX 2070, includes three GPCs, 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but does not support NVLink or SLI.

The passage also defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric combining Tensor, FP32, RT Core, and INT32 operations according to estimated hybrid-rendering usage. It concludes with a ray tracing overview covering ray casting, BVH acceleration, denoising, and examples of ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections. NVIDIA also includes standard legal notices disclaiming warranties, limiting liability, and reserving the right to change specifications.

The passage discusses equality, equality of opportunity, education, and equal opportunity in education. Equality is presented as a moral and social ideal shaped by economic, legal, political, and sociological debates, including equality of opportunity and political, racial, social, economic, and gender equality. Equality of opportunity is described as access to existing resources and advantageous positions based on knowledge and talent rather than origin.

Education is defined as a social process that develops individuals’ skills, attitudes, culture, and desired behaviors. Equal opportunity in education is described as enabling individuals to benefit from educational services without discrimination and according to their abilities and needs. Factors affecting it include economic, geographical, political, individual, and social conditions.

In Turkey, education policy is shaped mainly by the Ministry of National Education, with National Education Councils contributing to reforms. Equal opportunity issues in Turkey are linked to inadequate schools, economic difficulties, insufficient learning environments, and cultural and social factors affecting student motivation.

The passage concludes that equal opportunity in education is interpreted differently, but educational conditions should consider each child’s abilities and needs. It recommends measuring children’s abilities early, improving access and quality, reducing regional and school-type achievement differences, strengthening infrastructure, improving teacher quality, making all schools qualified, updating teacher education, and expanding high-standard preschool education.

Patterns help identify reusable components, improving development speed, consistency, and quality. The passage introduces container-based patterns for distributed systems, beginning with single-node container groups that share resources and are coscheduled, such as Kubernetes pods.

Single-node patterns include sidecar, ambassador, and adapter. Sidecars augment an application container, often to add HTTPS, synchronize configuration, provide process introspection, or build a simple Git-based PaaS. Effective sidecars should be modular, parameterized, have stable APIs, and be documented. Ambassadors broker communication between an application and external services, such as routing to sharded Redis, handling service discovery, or splitting requests for experiments. Adapters modify an application’s interface to match expected conventions, such as monitoring, logging, or health checking, without changing the original container.

The passage then describes multi-node distributed patterns and microservices. Microservices divide systems into smaller services with defined APIs, improving team autonomy, scaling, and release agility, but making debugging and design harder. Replicated load-balanced services use identical stateless replicas behind a load balancer for availability and horizontal scaling, with readiness probes indicating when replicas can serve traffic. Variants include session-tracked services, caching layers, rate limiting, and SSL termination.

Sharded services divide state across shards, with routing logic directing requests to the correct shard. Sharding is useful when state is too large for one machine and can improve cache memory utilization. Sharded caches require careful consideration of hit rate, performance impact, rollout behavior, and failure handling. Shards may also be replicated for resiliency and scaling. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform, and selecting the correct shard key is critical to grouping equivalent requests while avoiding incorrect cache results.

The Reverse Action Offense, introduced by Hall of Fame coach Pete Newell in the late 1950s, is a guard-around continuity offense built on precise execution, footwork, timing, spacing, and off-ball post screens. Its main options include weakside rub cuts to the basket, post-up play, guard-around isolation, sideline triangle action, and quick counters to defensive overplays.

The basic continuity begins with an entry pass to a wing, followed by a guard-around cut to the corner. If no shot is available, the weakside wing cuts off a post screen, while the ball can be reversed to continue the same action on the opposite side. Entries can begin through weakside or strongside passes, dribble clears, back cuts, or backdoor actions.

The offense relies on reading defensive positioning. Against different screen coverages, players use over-the-top cuts, baseline cuts, screener pops, dives, drives, pull-up jumpers, slips, rolls, and drive-and-kick passes. Post play includes counters to defenders playing high side, baseline side, behind, fronting, or double-teaming, with options such as power layups, baby hooks, lob passes, triple-threat moves, ball reversals, and pressure releases.

Reverse Action also uses back cuts against pass denial, corner give-and-go actions, screen-and-roll counters, and special late-game plays such as weakside screen-and-rolls, double screens, and back-screen lob options.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s RTX Blackwell neural rendering architecture and related GeForce RTX 50 Series features. Blackwell GB20x GPUs unify INT32 and FP32 cores, doubling possible integer operations for many instructions compared with Ada, though unified cores can operate as either FP32 or INT32 in a given cycle. Texture units increase from 512 in GeForce RTX 4090 to 680 in RTX 5090, raising bilinear-filtered texel rates and doubling point-sampling texture performance per cycle versus Ada.

Blackwell introduces GDDR7 memory using PAM3 signaling, higher channel density, improved SNR, advanced equalization, reengineered clocking, enhanced I/O training, Enhanced CRC, built-in always-on single-bit ECC, and Error Detection and Replay. RTX 5090 ships with 28 Gbps GDDR7 and 1.792 TB/s peak bandwidth, while RTX 5080 ships with 30 Gbps GDDR7 and 960 GB/s.

Fifth-generation Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, INT8, FP8, new FP4 and FP6 operations, and a second-generation FP8 Transformer Engine. FP4 reduces AI model memory needs and can improve performance; for example, FLUX.dev requires over 23 GB in FP16 but under 10 GB in FP4, and RTX 5090 with FP4 can generate images faster than RTX 4090 with FP16.

Blackwell’s fourth-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput versus the prior generation and add hardware for Mega Geometry and Linear Swept Spheres. Mega Geometry enables full-fidelity ray tracing for high-detail level-of-detail systems such as Nanite through cluster-level acceleration structures, partitioned top-level acceleration structures, batched GPU-driven APIs, and faster BVH construction. It is supported across NVIDIA ray tracing APIs and RTX GPUs starting with Turing. Linear Swept Spheres accelerate ray tracing of strand-like geometry such as hair, offering about 2x speed and 5x lower VRAM use versus DOTS in common hair-rendering cases.

Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 improves Blackwell’s ray tracing and neural shading efficiency with more efficient reorder logic and better coherence extraction. The AI Management Processor is a programmable RISC-V GPU context scheduler that reduces CPU scheduling dependency, lowers latency, and helps coordinate AI and graphics workloads.

Blackwell adds hardware encode and decode support for 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC video. Its ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality, adds AV1 Ultra High Quality mode, and supports up to three encoders and two decoders on RTX 5090. The sixth-generation NVDEC improves H.264 decoding and adds 4:2:2 support. DisplayPort 2.1b enables up to 80 Gbps bandwidth with UHBR 20.

Max-Q improvements include advanced power gating, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, memory clock tree gating, accelerated frequency switching up to 1000x faster than previous architectures, and faster low-latency sleep. Blackwell can enter its deepest sleep state 10x faster than Ada, enabling power savings in workloads such as small language model inference.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three additional frames per rendered frame. Its new frame generation model is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and runs once per rendered frame. Enhanced Flip Metering moves frame pacing to the display engine. DLSS 4 also adopts transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving temporal stability, motion detail, lighting detail, and reducing artifacts.

The reverse play is a high-risk, high-reward football trick play that deceives the defense by moving the ball one direction before giving it to another player going the opposite way. In a traditional reverse, the quarterback hands or tosses the ball to a running back or receiver, who then gives it to a receiver crossing back the other way. Success depends on timing, disguise, momentum, and blockers sealing off defenders.

Examples include a 2018 Carolina Panthers play where DJ Moore took the initial toss and Curtis Samuel received the reverse for a big gain that became a touchdown. The Arizona Cardinals used a fake reverse with Kyler Murray, who faked handoffs to create space for himself to run. Purdue ran a reverse screen against Michigan State, using multiple exchanges before setting up blockers downfield for a touchdown. A reverse pass variation had a receiver take the reverse and throw to the quarterback, who had released into space for a touchdown.

Building a soccer defensive wall places defenders shoulder-to-shoulder about 10 yards from the ball to block part of the goal during nearby free kicks. Walls become important as youth players gain the ability to shoot accurately and powerfully, often around age 12 on full-sized fields. A wall reduces the shooting angle, usually covering the near side while the goalkeeper covers the far side.

Defenders must react quickly, anticipate wall situations, mark attackers, and prepare for counterattacks. Under Law 13, defenders must be 10 yards from the ball unless on their own goal line, but referees are not required to wait for a wall to be built. Attackers may take a quick free kick if conditions allow. If they request the wall be moved back for a ceremonial free kick, they must wait for the referee’s whistle. Defenders who delay the restart by blocking the ball may be cautioned.

The goalkeeper decides whether to build a wall, usually based on the ball’s location and the goalkeeper’s experience and confidence. The closer the ball is to goal and the center of the field, the more defenders are needed. Walls may range from two players near the sides to five or more directly in front of goal.

In traditional wall building, an Anchor or Post-man moves to a point 10 yards from the ball on the line between the near post and the ball. The goalkeeper positions the Anchor with verbal and visual commands, and other players join shoulder-to-shoulder. The wall must avoid gaps, remain firm, and react after the kick. Players may protect body parts if arms remain tight to the body and do not move toward the ball.

A non-traditional method uses a designated Wall Setter beyond the ball to position the Anchor, allowing the goalkeeper to keep sight of the ball and prepare for a quick kick. Rarely, an indirect free kick less than 10 yards from goal requires defenders to build a wall on the goal line. Coaches should train wall angles, proper wall size, goalkeeper positioning, and responses to set pieces while warning players against delaying tactics.
