The paper argues that the reproduction number is limited because it does not account for time-varying testing, even though detected cases depend on diagnostic effort. The authors compare it with their acceleration index, an elasticity measuring the proportional change in cases relative to the proportional change in tests, interpretable as current viral speed relative to average viral speed.

They derive a formal relationship showing that the reproduction number is a special case of the acceleration index. The reproduction number tracks case growth, while the acceleration index adjusts case growth by test growth. When test intensity differs from infectivity intensity, the reproduction number can overestimate or underestimate viral acceleration. The authors state that accurate tracking requires either using the acceleration index alone or combining the reproduction number with test and infectivity intensities.

Using French COVID-19 data from May 13, 2020, to October 26, 2022, the paper finds substantial differences between the two indicators. The reproduction number often underestimated viral spread compared with the test-controlled acceleration index, especially during the Omicron period in autumn 2022. Analysis of France’s second lockdown also shows that ignoring changes in testing can give misleading signals about epidemic deceleration. Similar patterns in five other countries suggest the issue is not specific to France.

The authors conclude that the acceleration index is a more parsimonious and context-dependent measure for tracking epidemic dynamics because it incorporates diagnostic effort. They also note limitations, including unaccounted cases when testing is not compulsory, symptomatic and asymptomatic infections, and the dependence of the index’s accuracy on testing volume.

Simone Askew, a 20-year-old international history major from Fairfax, Va., became the first black woman to serve as first captain of West Point’s Corps of Cadets, the academy’s highest cadet leadership role. Askew emphasized mentorship for aspiring young women, while others praised her leadership.

A May 8, 2001 Enron media roundup covers California power-market criticism, Enron’s possible purchase of U.K. power plants to reduce trading risk, Scottish Power’s restructuring and possible interest in Enron’s Portland General unit, and multiple reports on Enron’s Dabhol Power Company dispute in India. Articles report that Dabhol lenders may cut interest rates or sue if disputes with Maharashtra and MSEB continue, customs blocked Rs 300 crore of Dabhol equipment over duty issues, and Dabhol agreed to meet a Maharashtra negotiating committee without offering to renegotiate its contract. Other items note Northern Border Partners’ $100 million purchase of Midwestern Gas Transmission, BP’s consideration of a Tampa liquefied natural gas terminal, and a U.S. appeals ruling allowing Enron to source power for California universities from utilities rather than the spot market.

Microsoft’s fiscal 2017 Form 10-K covers the year ended June 30, 2017. Microsoft is a Washington corporation headquartered in Redmond, Washington, with common stock listed on NASDAQ. As of December 31, 2016, its non-affiliate market value was $466.5 billion, and as of July 31, 2017, it had 7.70 billion shares outstanding.

Microsoft describes its mission as empowering every person and organization to achieve more. Its strategy centers on platforms and productivity services for an intelligent cloud and intelligent edge infused with AI. It operates worldwide in over 190 countries and develops, licenses, supports, and sells software, services, devices, cloud solutions, consulting, advertising, gaming, and related offerings.

The company’s three ambitions are to reinvent productivity and business processes, build the intelligent cloud platform, and create more personal computing. It completed its acquisition of LinkedIn on December 8, 2016. Microsoft reports three operating segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. These include offerings such as Office, Dynamics, LinkedIn, Azure, Windows Server, SQL Server, Windows, Surface, Xbox, Bing, and search advertising.

Research and development expense was $13.0 billion in fiscal 2017, representing 14% of revenue. Microsoft develops most products internally through engineering groups including Office, Artificial Intelligence and Research, Cloud and Enterprise, Windows and Devices, and LinkedIn. It held over 66,000 issued patents and over 35,000 pending patents.

Microsoft markets and distributes products and services through OEMs, direct sales, distributors, and resellers. Licensing options include Enterprise Agreements, Microsoft Product and Services Agreements, Open Licensing, Select Plus, Microsoft Online Subscription Agreements, and partner programs. Customers include consumers, businesses, enterprises, public-sector institutions, developers, internet service providers, and OEMs; no single customer accounted for more than 10% of revenue in fiscal 2017, 2016, or 2015.

As of June 30, 2017, Microsoft employed about 124,000 full-time people, including 73,000 in the U.S. and 51,000 internationally. LinkedIn added approximately 11,000 employees in fiscal 2017.

Key risks include intense competition, execution risks in cloud services, uncertain returns on investments and acquisitions, impairment of goodwill or intangible assets, intellectual property protection and infringement claims, cyberattacks, data breaches, service outages, regulatory and antitrust scrutiny, anti-corruption and trade compliance issues, privacy and data-transfer rules, talent retention challenges, litigation, tax liabilities, and quality or supply problems in hardware and software products.

Syrian rebels in Daraa faced a Russian deadline to accept surrender terms or renewed military action by Assad’s forces, backed by Moscow. Russia rejected rebel demands for a ceasefire, army withdrawal, and safe passage, instead proposing regime restoration, local police control, and Russian military police coordination. More than 30 towns had agreed to return to regime control, expanding government control of Daraa to about 60 percent. The offensive displaced 270,000 to 330,000 people, with Jordan and Israel keeping borders closed. Human Rights Watch urged both countries to admit asylum seekers. The UN Security Council planned an emergency meeting, while Jordan’s foreign minister met Russia’s Sergei Lavrov, who said Moscow sought rebel disarmament and reconciliation.

The speaker says the NHL long viewed Las Vegas as a promising market despite challenges with an arena, ownership, and economics, and this season confirmed its potential. They note no fixed timetable or Seattle-related impact. Early fan enthusiasm showed strong support. The expansion team’s Stanley Cup Finals run is described as positive for hockey, not a judgment on other teams. The speaker also says the league follows scientific conclusions on disputed links and praises franchises’ community outreach.

This study examined Ethiopian education policy intentions and secondary school principals’ and teachers’ conceptualizations of curriculum differentiation. It analyzed national policy documents and interview data from two principals and 17 teachers in regular and special day secondary schools. Policy documents conceptualize curriculum differentiation through tracks, fields of study, streams, school types, and differentiated curriculum components in inclusive classrooms. Principals’ and teachers’ views varied, including lack of awareness, divergent interpretations, and alignment with policy intentions. The study found incoherence among policy documents and gaps between policy intentions and school-level understandings. It concludes that clearer policy guidance and more explicit curriculum structures are needed to address students’ diverse needs.

NVIDIA filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 28, 2019. Second-quarter revenue was $2.579 billion, down from $3.123 billion a year earlier; net income was $552 million, down from $1.101 billion; diluted EPS was $0.90, down from $1.76. For the first half of fiscal 2020, revenue was $4.799 billion and net income was $947 million.

GPU revenue was $2.104 billion for the quarter, while Tegra Processor revenue was $475 million. Gaming revenue was $1.313 billion, Data Center $655 million, Professional Visualization $291 million, Automotive $209 million, and OEM and Other $111 million. Gross margin was 59.8%, compared with 63.3% a year earlier. Operating expenses rose to $970 million.

As of July 28, 2019, NVIDIA had $8.475 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, total assets of $14.775 billion, and long-term debt of $1.989 billion. The company paid $195 million in cash dividends during the first half of fiscal 2020 and had authorization to repurchase up to $7.24 billion of common stock through December 2022.

NVIDIA agreed to acquire Mellanox Technologies for $125 per share in cash, representing approximately $6.9 billion in enterprise value, subject to regulatory approvals. The company reported ongoing securities, derivative, and Mellanox merger-related litigation but recorded no accrual for contingent liabilities.

Former FBI Deputy Director Andrew McCabe was fired on March 16, two days before his planned early retirement at age 50, putting his Federal Employees Retirement System pension and health benefits at risk. McCabe, a 21-year FBI veteran, was dismissed amid an internal investigation into unauthorized media disclosures related to the Hillary Clinton email probe. He had been expected to receive about $60,000 annually under an enhanced law enforcement pension rate, but may now have to wait until age 57 and eight months to access benefits, potentially losing monthly payments and family health coverage in the interim. The passage explains that pensions are defined benefit plans based on service length and salary, and that FERS includes a Basic Benefit Plan, Social Security, and the Thrift Savings Plan. Some lawmakers reportedly offered McCabe short-term federal work to help preserve his pension, though a former law enforcement official said such work would need to be in a primary law enforcement role or require another 10 years of service. McCabe may also appeal.

The St. Louis Blues have much of their core signed for at least three seasons, with nine key players costing $47.425 million against the cap. Vladimir Tarasenko, Jake Allen, Alex Pietrangelo and Colton Parayko are presented as potentially strong-value contracts, while Alexander Steen, Vladimir Sobotka and Patrik Berglund carry some concerns. The team faces upcoming decisions on defensemen such as Jay Bouwmeester, Carl Gunnarsson, Robert Bortuzzo, Nate Prosser and RFA Joel Edmundson, with prospects Vince Dunn and Jordan Schmaltz possibly affecting those choices. The CBI told the Supreme Court it has begun a preliminary inquiry into the alleged SSC CGL Tier II 2017 paper leak. The court declined a monitored probe but allowed petitioners to return if dissatisfied.

Central Illinois officials are setting mosquito traps at 19 locations to rapidly test for West Nile virus after Illinois reported an unusually early human case in mid-May. A Decatur lab allows mosquitoes to be captured, tested and treated in less than 24 hours, helping officials decide quickly whether to spray. No human cases have been reported in Macon County this year, though a mosquito batch tested positive in June. Illinois reported 90 human cases and eight deaths last year.

ISDA’s June 4, 2001 press report compiles articles on Basel II, credit derivatives, energy, Argentina’s debt swap, and structured options. Reports say Basel II is nearing agreement for 2004 implementation but faces criticism over complexity, operational risk, costs, competitive effects, and readiness, especially from Asian central bankers, smaller banks, and Australian regulators concerned about mortgage risk weightings. Derivatives industry participants expect some Basel II concerns may be addressed, but uncertainty remains over the proposed “W” charge on credit derivatives.

Credit derivatives articles note ISDA work on standardized documentation for swaps based on convertible and zero-coupon convertible bonds, and efforts to resolve successor issues when companies split or restructure, highlighted by AT&T and National Power cases.

Other reports cover Deutsche Bank and ABN-Amro withdrawing from Argentina’s debt exchange management over possible U.S. securities-rule concerns; a dispute between California’s grid operator and federal regulators over independence from state control during the energy crisis; and the use of structured options products, including capital-protected notes, with potential application in India.

The bark Cape Horn Pigeon sailed on a whaling voyage on December 7, 1891. On September 10, 1892, while whaling in the Okhotsk Sea, it was seized on the open sea by an armed Imperial Russian naval vessel and taken by force to Vladivostok. The captain had previously visited Vladivostok, stated his intention to whale in the Okhotsk Sea, and requested permission to enter certain bays considered within Russian jurisdiction, but no permission was granted and no broader Russian claim over the sea was communicated. The captain protested the seizure, and the crew was compelled to help navigate the Russian vessel. The bark was detained until October 1, 1892. The arresting officer claimed the Okhotsk Sea was a closed sea, but the cited Russian foreign ministry note did not support that claim. After arrival at Vladivostok, the captain telegraphed the U.S. legation in St. Petersburg, which contacted the Russian foreign ministry and was informed that the bark had been released.

Canyon Barry scored a season-high 30 points as No. 15 Florida beat Auburn 114-95 for its seventh straight win. The Gators broke their previous scoring high, shot 56 percent, made 11 of 19 3-pointers and 37 of 42 free throws, and pulled away after a 50-50 halftime tie. KeVaughn Allen added 17 points, all in the second half, while Kasey Hill had 11 points and 12 assists. Anfernee McLemore led Auburn with 19 points. Florida improved to 21-5 and 11-2 in the SEC; Auburn fell to 16-10 and 5-8. Barry’s school-record free throw streak ended at 42.

An Islamic State car bomb killed 24 people and wounded 67 in Baghdad’s Sadr City district, targeting a Shi’ite gathering, according to an Amaq statement. Other recent attacks in Baghdad and near Najaf killed dozens, while a separate central Baghdad blast killed one civilian and wounded nine. Iraqi forces, backed by the U.S.-led coalition, continued fighting to retake Mosul, with counter-terrorism forces clearing districts and destroying car bombs. Islamic State also attacked positions north of Baghdad, killing pro-government fighters, cutting a strategic road to Mosul, seizing checkpoints near Shirqat, and executing nine Sunni tribal fighters near Udhaim.

Using CEPS data from 13,981 students, this study examines how parental education level relates to child cognitive ability through descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression. Parental education is measured by parents’ years of schooling, while child cognitive ability is measured by standardized 3PL test scores. Control variables include child, family, and school characteristics, with educational expectations and parent-child interaction tested as mediators.

Findings show a significant positive correlation: each additional year in the maximum education of either parent is associated with a 0.019-point increase in child cognitive ability. Parental education affects cognition partly through educational expectations, children’s own educational expectations, and parent-child companionship. The effect is stronger for girls than boys, stronger among urban than rural families, and greater among children with lower cognitive ability.

The passage describes stackless native assembler procedures using register passing to initialize and later remove a pre-memory stack region. The initialization routine runs on all processor cores, sets up processor/cache state before main memory is available, divides stack space among cores, maps it globally, sets x86-64 MTRRs, and creates a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instance. It handles protected and real mode differently for SS:ESP setup, destroys specified registers, and returns AGESA_SUCCESS, WARNING for stack reentry, or FATAL for unknown processor family. AARCH64 APUs with PSP do not use these stack macros because PSP initializes DRAM.

The removal routine disables Cache-as-RAM after main memory is available, must run on all cores, flushes cache lines, preserves EBX, and should be invoked only by the BSP. It returns AGESA_SUCCESS when stack space is disabled.

The passage also describes AmdCreateStruct, which allocates and initializes AGESA parameter structures using PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, or ByHost allocation. ByHost requires the host to provide sufficient storage and may overlay the CREATE_STRUCT_PARAMS structure on success.

The lecture covers portfolio-level financing for sustainable real estate, focusing on public-market vehicles such as REITs and green bonds, followed by benchmarking and disclosure tools. REITs are publicly traded companies that invest mainly in income-generating real estate, receive tax advantages if they meet rules such as holding most assets and income in real estate and distributing most income, and allow investors liquidity, diversification, lower capital requirements, and shared risk, though with less control than direct ownership.

The discussion compares REIT development across countries, including Colombia, Mexico, South Korea, Thailand, and China. China’s REITs are described as a newer, infrastructure-focused tool used by local governments and quasi-government companies to raise capital, with possible expansion into commercial real estate.

The lecture then examines “green REITs,” noting that many REITs now set net-zero or ESG targets, often influenced by institutional investors such as pension funds and asset managers, especially from Europe, Canada, Australia, and Germany. Research cited suggests REITs with larger shares of green buildings have higher returns and lower risk, though questions of causality remain. Ongoing research aims to compare REITs’ “green talking” through public commitments with “green doing” through actual investments.

Green bonds are introduced as fixed-income instruments issued by governments, companies, or REITs to raise capital for green investments such as renewable energy, clean energy, resilient infrastructure, or green buildings. They may lower capital costs when investors value their green credentials, but issuers need standards and validation to avoid greenwashing.

The final section emphasizes measurement, data, benchmarking, and disclosure. Tools and firms discussed include EPA Portfolio Manager, Measurabl, DNV, CRREM, and GRESB, which acts as a portfolio-level sustainability benchmark similar to LEED at the building level. Studies using GRESB data find associations between higher ESG scores, better fund or REIT performance, and lower borrowing costs. The lecture also notes concerns about inconsistent ESG ratings and describes MIT Sloan research on “ESG Confusion” and efforts to derive more reliable ESG measures.

The passage summarizes NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPU architecture, focusing on GA102 and GA104 GPUs used in products such as GeForce RTX 3090, RTX 3080, RTX 3070, RTX A6000, and NVIDIA A40. GA10x builds on Turing with higher efficiency and performance, offering up to 1.7x faster raster graphics and up to 2x faster ray tracing. GA102 includes up to 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, 336 third-generation Tensor Cores, 28.3 billion transistors, and a Samsung 8nm custom process.

Key architectural improvements include doubled FP32 throughput per SM, larger and faster L1/shared memory, ROP optimizations, PCIe Gen 4 support, third-generation NVLink, and GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling delivering up to 936 GB/sec bandwidth. Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection performance, support concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute, and add hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 support, structured sparsity, and higher throughput for AI workloads including DLSS, AI denoising, NVIDIA Broadcast, and NVIDIA Canvas.

The passage also describes DLSS support for up to 8K gaming, RTX IO for GPU-based asset loading and decompression with Microsoft DirectStorage, and fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode. Seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware video encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC. NVIDIA A40 is positioned for data center visual computing and virtual workstations, while RTX A6000 targets professional desktop workflows with 48 GB GDDR6 and NVLink scalability to 96 GB. The document also notes Error Detection and Replay technology for GDDR6X memory overclocking and includes product comparisons and legal disclaimers.

Tristan Walker founded Walker & Co. after struggling to find shaving products suited to his hair and skin. The company, designed for people of color, sells men’s shaving products under Bevel and launched a women’s line called Form. Walker aims to make the beauty industry more inclusive and eliminate segregated “ethnic” beauty aisles. Before founding the company, he worked at Andreessen Horowitz and Foursquare and founded Code2040 to expand tech opportunities for young people of color. He says his biggest fear is failing to fulfill the company’s long-term vision. Walker hopes his work helps people of color be treated as first-class consumers and encourages aspiring entrepreneurs to focus on problems they are uniquely positioned to solve.

The lecture introduces an MIT general relativity course, its materials, grading, structure, and initial concepts. Sean Carroll’s general relativity textbook is the main semi-required text, with Schutz, Misner-Thorne-Wheeler, and Wald suggested as supplements for different purposes. Grades are based entirely on 11 problem sets, with no final exam.

The course’s first half covers the mathematical foundations needed to derive the Einstein field equations, while the second half applies them to topics such as Newtonian limits, classic tests of general relativity, cosmology, black holes, gravitational waves, and neutron stars. The lecturer begins with special relativity using geometric language to prepare for more complex general relativity.

Spacetime is defined as a manifold of events endowed with a metric. A manifold is described as a connected set of points; an event is when and where something happens; and a metric provides a notion of distance between events. The metric will later be connected to gravity.

The lecture introduces inertial reference frames as lattices of clocks and measuring rods moving freely, non-rotating, orthogonal, uniformly spaced, and uniformly ticking. Clocks are synchronized using Einstein’s procedure, based on the invariant speed of light: a light pulse sent from one clock to another and reflected back sets the second clock’s time to the midpoint between emission and reception times.

The lecturer sets units so the speed of light equals 1, making velocities dimensionless fractions of light speed. He then introduces spacetime displacement vectors between events, emphasizing that events and vectors are geometric objects independent of coordinate labels. Different inertial observers assign different components to the same vector, related by Lorentz transformations. The lecture also introduces index notation, Einstein summation convention, dummy and free indices, and defines a spacetime vector as a quartet of components that transforms between inertial reference frames like a displacement vector and obeys vector-space linearity rules.

Dividend aristocrats are US companies that have increased dividend payments for at least 25 consecutive years. Investors can access them through the ProShares S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats ETF (NOBL), which contains 52 companies. Examples with indicative gross yields include AT&T (4.61%), Chevron (3.66%), Consolidated Edison (3.67%), AbbVie (4.11%), Exxon Mobil (3.32%), Procter & Gamble (3.19%), Walmart (2.89%), Coca-Cola (3.38%), and McDonald’s (3.06%). These companies operate across communications, energy, pharmaceuticals, consumer goods, retail, beverages, and restaurants. The article states it is for educational and informational purposes only and not investment, tax, or legal advice.

The speaker credits Patty’s big saves during early penalty trouble for giving the team momentum, says they improved by staying out of the penalty box and playing their style, and looks forward to the next home game. They aim to learn from past mistakes, play patiently, and wait for opportunities.

Tecomaria capensis (Cape Honeysuckle) is a Bignoniaceae shrub or small tree up to 6 m, used as a garden and hedging plant. It has opposite compound leaves, trumpet-shaped flowers in orange-red, pale orange, or yellow forms, and slender flattened fruit. It is listed as Least Concern by SANBI. It occurs in thicket and forest margins in southern, eastern and tropical Africa, including Eastern Cape, KwaZulu-Natal, Limpopo, Mpumalanga and Western Cape. It is browsed by game and stock and visited by sunbirds, butterflies and bees. It is used in traditional medicine and in Xhosa protective necklets called isixhoxho. It grows best in well-drained, composted soil with regular watering and winter pruning.

The study investigates how well deep learning models estimate mammographic density from low dose mammograms, using paired standard and approximately 10% dose images from the ALDRAM dataset and training data from PROCAS. Models were trained separately on standard dose PROCAS images and simulated low dose images, then evaluated on ALDRAM.

Low dose and standard dose predictions were highly similar, especially when averaging across RCC and RMLO views and combining predictions from multiple models. Variation between CC and MLO views was comparable to variation between standard and low dose images. Averaging across views and models reduced prediction differences.

The study found no evidence that age or dose ratio affected low dose prediction performance. Performance was poorer for higher breast density, smaller breast area, and smaller image size, with image size effects likely related to breast area. Larger differences between CC and MLO low dose predictions, or between separately trained low dose models, were associated with larger differences between low and standard dose predictions. No notable outliers were found.

The results support the feasibility of using low dose mammography with deep learning for density estimation, while indicating that systematic differences, particularly related to breast density and breast area, require further investigation and possible correction.

The passage presents GroceryDB, an open-source database of over 50,000 foods and beverages from Walmart, Target, and Whole Foods, analyzed using the machine-learning Food Processing Score (FPro). FPro estimates processing levels from nutrition facts, producing a continuous score from unprocessed to ultra-processed.

The study finds that grocery inventories are dominated by higher-processing products, though Whole Foods offers more minimally processed items than Walmart and Target. Processing levels vary by category: some, such as chips, bread, and mac & cheese, offer limited lower-processing choices, while cereals, milk and substitutes, pasta-noodles, and snack bars show wider variation. GroceryDB’s FPro distribution resembles USDA food databases, but many products are absent from other branded-product datasets.

Higher processing is generally associated with cheaper calories, though the relationship differs by food category. Ingredient-tree analysis shows that more complex ingredient lists tend to accompany higher processing. The authors introduce an Ingredient Processing Score to rank ingredients by their contribution to processing, identifying variation among additives and oils.

The passage argues that GroceryDB and FPro can support consumer decision-making, public health initiatives, and product reformulation, while noting limitations from incomplete food-label data and the need for richer chemical and ingredient information.
Figures show headphone views; broken lines are environmental, not claimed.

The passage describes a short-selling strategy bundle containing three backtested strategies with entries and exits at the close or next open. It includes plain-English rules and code for Amibroker and TradeStation/EasyLanguage, with TradingView/Pine Script available without guarantees. Backtests are referenced for SPY, XLP, and SMH. Short Strategy 1 had 125 trades, 0.72% average gain per trade, 2.9% CAGR, and 11% maximum drawdown. Combined-strategy performance metrics are also referenced.

MSPM0Gx51x MCUs are ultra-low-power 32-bit Arm Cortex-M0+ devices operating up to 80MHz, offering 256KB to 512KB flash, up to 128KB SRAM, dual CAN-FD, cybersecurity features, and integrated analog modules. They support secure boot, firmware updates, IP protection, AES acceleration, and TRNG. The devices include ADCs, DAC, comparators, and are supported by TI development kits, SDK, documentation, training, and forums.

Google announced Google Cloud Partner Interconnect, enabling direct connections between on-premises data centers and Google Cloud through 23 global partners for hybrid cloud deployments. Unlike Dedicated Interconnect, which offers only 10Gbps full circuits, Partner Interconnect supports partial circuits from 50Mbps to 10Gbps. Google says partners have already certified infrastructure, making setup easier. The service lets businesses use Google Cloud without routing data over the public internet, improving control and reducing latency, though traffic is not encrypted by default. The announcement follows other Google hybrid cloud efforts with Cisco and Nutanix. General availability is expected in the coming weeks.

CTP N.V. published an Analyst/Investor Day slide deck. The passage also includes Seeking Alpha transcript team information, related article headlines, and chart metadata showing a single data point on 2025-09-24 at 19.87.

VirtualLink simplifies VR headset setup by carrying power, display, and data through a single USB-C connector, enabling VR on small form factor devices. Turing TU102 and TU104 GPUs replace prior SLI MIO/PCIe transfers with second-generation NVLink; TU102 has two x8 links and TU104 has one, each providing 25 GB/sec per direction. Turing supports two-way SLI with NVLink, but not 3-way or 4-way SLI.

Turing introduces real-time ray tracing through RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs combined with NVIDIA RTX software. The architecture supports hybrid rendering, using rasterization where effective and ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, offloading SMs and enabling far higher ray tracing performance than Pascal. NVIDIA also uses denoising to reduce the number of rays required per pixel.

NVIDIA NGX is a Turing-only AI graphics technology stack using Tensor Cores and pretrained neural networks. Its features include DLSS, DLSS 2X, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS uses training from 64x supersampled images to produce image quality similar to TAA with improved performance, while DLSS 2X targets quality close to 64x supersampling.

Turing adds Mesh Shading with Task Shaders and Mesh Shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and improve handling of complex geometry. Variable Rate Shading lets developers vary shading rate by 16x16 screen regions or primitives, enabling Content Adaptive Shading, Motion Adaptive Shading, and Foveated Rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and appearance sampling by storing shading in texture space for reuse across pixels, frames, or stereo views. Multi-View Rendering expands Pascal’s SMP by supporting up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 at the API level.

For VR, Turing combines VirtualLink, MVR, VRS-based foveated rendering, and RT Core acceleration for NVIDIA VRWorks Audio. Turing also extends DX12 resource support with bindless Constant Buffer Views and Unordered Access Views and supports Tier 2 resource heaps.

The TU104 GPU includes up to six GPCs, 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 13.6 billion transistors, and one x8 NVLink link. It is used in products including GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. Tesla T4 uses a TU104 configuration with five GPCs, 40 SMs, 2560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, and 320 GB/s memory bandwidth. TU106, used in GeForce RTX 2070, includes three GPCs, 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, and 10.8 billion transistors, but does not support NVLink or SLI.

The passage defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering that weights Tensor, FP32, RT Core, and INT32 operations by estimated frame-time usage. It also explains ray tracing mechanics, BVH acceleration, denoising, and examples of ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections. It concludes with NVIDIA legal notices, warranty disclaimers, trademark information, and copyright statements.

From 1961 to 1962, the Special Group (Augmented) oversaw Operation Mongoose, a covert program against Castro’s regime, coordinated by Edward Lansdale and implemented mainly by CIA units. Kennedy also created the Special Group (Counter-Insurgency) in 1962 for broad counterinsurgency policy. In 1964, NSAM No. 303 renamed Special Group 5412 the 303 Committee without changing its role. The Special Group and 303 Committee approved 163 covert actions under Kennedy and 142 under Johnson through February 1967, though the Church Committee later found only 14 percent of CIA projects since 1961 received case-by-case review. In 1970, Nixon’s NSDM 40 replaced the 303 Committee with the 40 Committee, added the Attorney General, and required approval and annual review of major or sensitive covert operations. The 40 Committee focused on major projects and considered about 25 percent of CIA covert actions. The 1974 Hughes-Ryan amendment required presidential findings for covert actions and expanded congressional oversight.

A self-driving Uber SUV struck and killed 49-year-old Elaine Herzberg in Tempe, Arizona, while operating in autonomous mode with a human backup driver. Police said she was walking a bicycle outside a crosswalk and the vehicle was traveling about 40 mph. Uber suspended autonomous road testing in Phoenix, Pittsburgh, San Francisco and Toronto and said it was cooperating with investigators. The NTSB and NHTSA sent investigators, while local police said no conclusions had been reached about fault.

Experts said the crash, the first death involving a fully autonomous test vehicle, could damage public perception of self-driving technology and increase pressure for regulation. Autonomous vehicles have been promoted as a way to reduce traffic deaths, though oversight varies by state. Arizona has taken a light regulatory approach and has no reporting requirements, unlike California. The article also notes earlier crashes involving Uber and Tesla vehicles with autonomous or semi-autonomous features, and discusses pending federal guidelines and congressional proposals on autonomous vehicle regulation.

The lecture examines security attacks through economic incentives, focusing on spam. Some attacks, such as ideological or state-sponsored ones, may not be economically deterred, but attacks involving profit can potentially be reduced by increasing attacker costs or disrupting revenue chains.

Spam remains common because it is cheap to send and even very low response rates can be profitable. Examples include Chinese “text message cars,” which can collect phone numbers and send up to 200,000 messages daily; their equipment costs about $1,600 and can generate roughly the same amount in daily profit, while fines are low and enforcement is rare. Some Chinese carriers also profit from spam traffic, including bulk messaging through 106-prefix numbers.

The lecture describes markets for cyberattack resources, including compromised systems, websites, email accounts, botnet services, malware kits, zero-day exploits, and stolen user data. Companies such as Endgame are cited as selling information on unpatched machines and exploit subscriptions. Customers may include governments and companies, with some firms conducting “hackbacks” against attackers.

The spam ecosystem is divided into advertising, click support, and realization. Advertising involves getting users to click links, often through email, texts, or social networks. Sending spam is inexpensive, about $60 per million messages, but conversion rates are extremely low; one study of 350 million spam messages found about 10,000 clicks and 28 purchase attempts. Defenses such as IP blacklists, email charges, computational puzzles, and CAPTCHAs can raise costs but have deployment and usability problems. Attackers evade them using botnets, compromised webmail accounts, BGP hijacking, and low-cost CAPTCHA-solving services, often involving human labor.

Click support requires domain registration, DNS, and web servers. Spammers use DNS, redirection services, compromised sites, botnets, and fast-flux techniques to create indirection and avoid takedowns. Affiliate programs often handle backend operations, including payment processing, and are decentralized, making direct enforcement difficult.

The realization phase involves payments and delivery. Credit card transactions pass through merchants, payment processors, acquiring banks, card networks, and issuing banks. Spammers often properly classify transactions and ship goods to avoid fines and chargebacks. Since only a limited number of acquiring banks work with spammers, payment networks may be a useful choke point. After research exposed these payment flows, Visa changed policies by labeling pharmaceutical sales high-risk and strengthening rules against illegal drug and trademark-infringing sales.

The lecture also discusses ethical issues in security research, including researchers making test purchases from spam links, and notes that legal oversight varies. It concludes with hackbacks, where companies such as Microsoft and partners have taken action against botnets using legal arguments such as trademark infringement.

One year after Hurricane Helene caused severe flooding at four western North Carolina school buildings, districts reported varied recovery progress. Atkinson Elementary in Henderson County returned in December 2024 after floor replacement and continued support from the Boys & Girls Club. Old Fort Elementary in McDowell County reopened for the 2025-26 school year after extensive repairs and flood mitigation. Valle Crucis School in Watauga County remains displaced while a new building’s opening is delayed, with students housed at community institutions. In Yancey County, Micaville Elementary closed permanently, with students moved to other schools and expansions underway. District leaders emphasized community partnerships, communication challenges, infrastructure concerns, and ongoing FEMA and facility planning work.

The district court denied Willie Tyler’s motions to dismiss the indictment before retrial on obstruction-of-justice counts related to the 1992 murder of witness Doreen Proctor. Tyler argued retrial was barred by the Confrontation Clause, Double Jeopardy Clause, and Due Process Clause.

The court held that testimony from Detective David Fones about Proctor’s statements would not violate the Confrontation Clause because it would be offered to show she made communications relevant to a potential federal investigation, not for the truth of the statements. The court rejected Tyler’s double jeopardy arguments, finding that retrial was permitted because his convictions were vacated due to legal error, not insufficient evidence. It also rejected his due process claim, finding no outrageous government conduct or established Brady violation warranting dismissal.

The court concluded that retrial could proceed on Counts II and III under the investigation-related communications theory.

The passage compares children’s mobile phone ownership across countries, beginning with Sara Zaske’s observation that her daughter did not want a phone in Germany but felt pressure to have a smartphone after moving to California. Studies cited show wide variation: about 46% of European children ages 9 to 16 owned smartphones in 2013-14, while 45% of U.S. children ages 10 to 12 had smartphones with service plans. Ownership often begins later outside the U.S. and Europe, with notable rates in South Korea, Taiwan, South Africa, Ghana, Malawi, and Australia. The speaker says the team’s coaching staff believed they had the right playoff matchups but did not win them in the first two games. Chongqing’s online tax payment system has streamlined property and business tax procedures, allowing users to upload documents, get approvals, make appointments and complete payments online. Since its launch, nearly 90 percent of businesses in the city’s nine central districts use it, reducing average wait times from 83 minutes to 15 minutes. The platform, launched under “internet plus taxation” guidelines, combines local and state tax services. Mobile services are also available, with over 1.2 million people using phones to pay taxes this year. Officials say about 95 percent of transactions can now be completed online.

U.S. stocks posted modest gains despite a prolonged federal government shutdown delaying key economic data. Investors relied on private indicators, with technology and growth shares leading advances. Analysts said markets remain cautious and selective, warning volatility could rise if shutdown uncertainty persists. Pan Finance describes itself as a global financial intelligence source.

Kinder Morgan plans to resume dividend increases funded by internally generated cash flow while continuing to fund growth without new debt or equity. The company operates a large North American midstream network, including 70,000 miles of natural gas pipelines, oil transport capacity, and terminal assets. After financial pressure during the oil crash and a 75% dividend cut, Kinder Morgan has shifted back toward expansion spending, reduced debt, and lowered interest expenses. Its 2017 budget projects $4.46 billion in distributable cash flow, $3.2 billion in growth capital, and further debt reduction through Kinder Morgan Canada. The company expects dividend increases through 2020 and has a $12 billion growth backlog, mostly fee-based, which is expected to increase adjusted EBITDA and support future cash flow.

President Donald Trump said the U.S. will impose an additional 100% tariff on China and export controls on critical software starting Nov. 1, 2025, or sooner depending on China’s actions. The move follows China’s new rare earth export restrictions and would raise U.S. tariffs on China to 130%, near the 145% level imposed in April. Stocks and bond yields fell, with the S&P 500 dropping 2.7%. China dominates processed rare earths and rare earth magnets, giving it leverage over the U.S. Trump also suggested he may not meet Xi Jinping at a South Korea summit, weakening hopes for a trade deal involving U.S. soybean purchases.

Hong introduces quantum field theory as the study of quantum dynamics of fields, with quantum electrodynamics as a central goal of the course. He explains that QFT describes three fundamental interactions completely, is useful in quantum gravity, and has applications across theoretical physics, including condensed matter and statistical physics. The course is the first in a three-semester sequence, focused mainly on fundamental concepts.

He advises students that QFT is conceptually difficult but can be approached as quantum mechanics with infinitely many degrees of freedom. He emphasizes understanding quantum mechanics, especially the Heisenberg picture, connecting formalisms to concrete physical problems, and building intuition through examples and problem sets. He notes that most learning in the graduate course will occur outside class and that lecture notation may differ from recommended textbooks.

The lecture begins with classical field theory and the principle of locality, attributed to Faraday: physical effects propagate from point to neighboring point rather than through action at a distance. Fields assign dynamical variables to each point in space, with examples including electric and magnetic fields, scalar fields, vector fields, tensor fields, and spinor fields. Maxwell’s equations and Einstein gravity are presented as local theories because their equations involve fields and derivatives at the same point.

Hong then formulates the action principle for classical fields. Locality constrains the Lagrangian to be a spatial integral of a Lagrangian density depending on fields and their derivatives at a single point. The canonical momentum density, Hamiltonian density, and Euler-Lagrange equations for fields are derived. The discussion is restricted mainly to translation-invariant and Lorentz-invariant field theories.

Examples include Maxwell theory, Einstein gravity, and scalar field theory. For a real scalar field, the action contains derivative terms and a potential \(V(\phi)\). Translation symmetry requires parameters in \(V(\phi)\) to be constant. A linear potential gives an external force, while a quadratic potential leads to the Klein-Gordon equation, described as the simplest scalar field theory.

The passage presents a quantum algorithmic framework for sparsifying generalized linear models (GLMs) to accelerate regression and empirical risk minimization problems. It considers objectives of the form \(F(x)=\sum_i f_i(\langle a_i,x\rangle-b_i)\), focusing on loss functions satisfying \((L,\theta,c)\)-properness, including \(\ell_p\), Huber, and \(\gamma_p\) losses. The framework constructs small weighted subsets that preserve the objective within a multiplicative error over a specified range.

The main result is a quantum algorithm that, with high probability, builds an \(\tilde O(\log(s_{\max}/s_{\min})\, n/\varepsilon^2)\)-sparse \(\varepsilon\)-approximate sparsifier in time \(\tilde O((n^\omega+nr^2+r\sqrt{mn}/\varepsilon)\log(s_{\max}/s_{\min}))\), where \(m\) is the number of samples, \(n\) the dimension, and \(r\) row sparsity. For homogeneous losses the scale-ratio dependence can be removed.

The approach uses multiscale leverage score overestimates as importance scores, quantum leverage score approximation, quantum weight initialization, quantum importance sampling, and quantum sum estimation. Applications include quantum speedups for linear, multiple, ridge, lasso, Huber, \(\ell_p\), and \(\gamma_p\) regression, often improving the dependence on \(m\) compared with classical algorithms and prior quantum results.

The passage explains the Flex offense “Pick the Picker,” a continuity basketball offense built on baseline screens, down screens, back cuts, ball reversal, and weakside rebounding. It describes basic sequences in which players pass, screen, cut, pop out, or isolate in the post, with options for shots, feeds, and continued continuity. It also covers responses to defensive overplay, including back cuts, weakside lobs, and back door plays. Various entries include high post rub, weakside shuffle cut, and dribble clear action. A “Pop” variation adds a weakside double screen, giving receivers options to cut low, cut high, or pop out for a shot. The passage emphasizes offensive rebounding through anticipation, determination, hustle, inside position, and repeated efforts.

Digital Foundry’s analysis of Monster Hunter World found strong monster and character models, detailed textures, good shadows, and attractive water surfaces, but also weak contrast, washed-out lighting, minimal HDR impact, clipping, collision issues, and poor motion blur.

On base consoles, PS4 runs at 1080p while Xbox One runs at 864p, with both having uncapped and uneven frame rates; Xbox One performs worse. On PS4 Pro and Xbox One X, Resolution mode gives Pro 1800p checkerboard rendering and One X 1728p native rendering, with smoother edges on One X but sharper detail on Pro. Some distant visual assets are missing on One X, and Pro often performs slightly better.

In Frame-rate mode, both enhanced consoles run at 1080p with uncapped performance between 30 and 60 fps; One X is generally faster, though inconsistently, while still missing some assets. In Graphics mode, both remain at 1080p with improved detail distance; missing One X assets reappear, and One X performs notably better than Pro.

Overall, the passage describes Monster Hunter World as enjoyable to play but technically disappointing, with visuals and performance falling short across all consoles, especially on Xbox One X.

Snowy plover nests have been spotted at Clatsop Spit on Oregon’s northern coast for the first time in decades, three years after Fort Stevens State Park created a special management area for the threatened species. Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X2 lineup includes the X2 Elite and X2 Elite Extreme, with early benchmarks run on a reference laptop using the top-tier X2 Elite Extreme. In Cinebench 2024, the 18-core chip scored 1,974 in multi-core performance, 62 percent faster than Apple’s base M4 and 15 percent faster than the M4 Pro, though still behind the M4 Max. Its single-core score of 161 reflects Qualcomm’s claimed 39 percent improvement over the prior generation, but remains behind Apple’s M4.

Graphics performance showed major gains. In 3DMark Steel Nomad Light, the X2 Elite Extreme scored 5,628, 53 percent ahead of Intel Lunar Lake integrated graphics, and in 3DMark Solar Bay it was 30 percent faster than Apple’s M4. Qualcomm also claimed improvements over the Snapdragon X Elite in Photoshop, Lightroom, and Premiere Pro, though those were not independently tested.

The results come with caveats: testing used only the X2 Elite Extreme in a 16-inch reference laptop, not final retail systems or smaller designs. The X2 lineup includes three SKUs: the top X2 Elite Extreme with 18 cores, dual-core 5-GHz boost, and 12-channel memory up to 228 GB/s; plus two X2 Elite chips with either 18 or 12 cores and 8-channel memory. All include an 80 TOPS NPU. Real-world performance remains unconfirmed until laptops with these chips launch.

Chris selected a cohesive team of consultants who knew one another and worked well together. The team identified a need among small districts for an affordable integrated planning and budgeting system and developed specifications with generally positive outside feedback. Suzanne Nimocks forwarded a McKinsey memorandum dated December 6, 2000, providing a periodic update on international electric power sector privatization and restructuring from June to November 2000.

The memo states that privatization and restructuring were continuing globally as governments sought foreign investment to meet rising power demand. State-owned utilities were increasingly being unbundled, and wholesale and retail competition was being introduced. Some international players were reducing risk by shifting investments toward the U.S. and Europe.

In Europe, EU directives were driving liberalization, market opening, unbundling, mergers, alliances, and cross-border investment. Several countries had introduced or planned retail access, independent transmission arrangements, privatizations, power pools, or trading platforms, though barriers remained in countries such as France, Germany, Greece, and Austria.

In Central and Eastern Europe, privatization and restructuring were advancing, often linked to IMF conditions or EU accession goals. Countries including Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Romania, Slovakia, Turkey, Ukraine, and Russia were pursuing varying degrees of unbundling, privatization, and market opening.

In Asia-Pacific, recovering economies were restarting power reforms, but IPPs faced issues involving power purchase agreements, guarantees, and state utility finances. Australia, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, New Zealand, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, the Philippines, Taiwan, China, and Vietnam were at different stages of market opening, restructuring, privatization, or regulatory reform.

In Latin America, currency fluctuations, inflation, droughts, ownership limits, and hydro dependence slowed some privatizations, though generation, distribution, and transmission reforms continued. Many countries had privatized major assets, while Venezuela and Mexico were noted as exceptions among major economies.

In Africa and the Middle East, governments were increasingly opening power sectors to foreign investment, mostly through IPPs. Some countries were considering broader privatization, unbundling, or concessions, while regional transmission projects were developing in Africa, the Middle East, and the Gulf.

This study used SEER Research Plus data from 2000–2018 to examine mortality and overall survival among U.S. patients with soft-tissue sarcomas, including heart cancer, and to develop nomogram-based survival predictions by sarcoma type and treatment. From 7.75 million cancer cases, 55,261 soft tissue cancers were identified, with 24,849 patients meeting inclusion criteria. The selected sarcoma types were liposarcoma, leiomyosarcoma, synovial sarcoma, spindle cell sarcoma, giant cell sarcoma, and myxofibrosarcoma.

Patients had a mean diagnosis age of 59 years; 56% were male and 82% were white. Liposarcoma was the most common subtype, while spindle cell sarcoma was the least common. At diagnosis, 67% had localized disease, 21% regional disease, and 12% distant disease. Surgery was received by 82% of patients, radiotherapy by 42%, chemotherapy by 19%, and primary systemic therapy by 14%.

Survival differed significantly by sarcoma type. Myxofibrosarcoma had the highest overall survival rate at 75%, while spindle cell sarcoma had the lowest at 37%. Increasing age, male sex, non-white race, higher tumor grade, and advanced cancer stage were associated with poorer survival. Distant-stage disease had substantially higher mortality than localized-stage disease. Surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy were associated with reduced mortality, while primary systemic therapy showed conflicting results. Surgery showed the strongest mortality reduction across sarcoma subtypes.

Nomograms were developed to estimate 5- and 10-year survival probabilities using age, sex, race, cancer stage, grade, sarcoma type, and treatment. The study reported close agreement between predicted and observed outcomes. Limitations included unavailable SEER variables such as surgical margins, recurrence, radiotherapy details, and some histological and clinical factors, as well as the need for external validation.

Queensland’s cyclone season remains active, with models showing possible low-pressure systems near the coast before Easter.
