The lecture discusses efficient mechanical designs in nature, focusing on sandwich structures and density gradients. Many monocot leaves, such as iris leaves, have sandwich-like construction: stiff sclerenchyma fibers on the top and bottom with parenchyma cells forming a foam-like core. This structure helps leaves stand upright at low material cost. Cat tails and grasses show related designs, with stiff outer layers separated by internal webs or low-density tissue.

The lecturer describes experiments on iris leaves treated as sandwich beams. Rectangular leaf samples were loaded as cantilevers, and measured deflections were compared with sandwich beam equations using estimated face modulus and core shear modulus. The calculated stiffnesses were not exact but were of the same order as measurements, supporting the idea that iris leaves behave mechanically like sandwich beams.

Other natural sandwich structures include New Zealand seakelp, whose honeycomb-like core contains gas pockets for buoyancy; bird skulls, where trabecular bone separates thin inner and outer plates to reduce weight; cuttlefish “bone,” a calcium carbonate shell with air pockets used for buoyancy control; and horseshoe crab and Galapagos tortoise shells.

The lecture then examines palm stems, which reduce weight through radial density gradients rather than sandwich construction. Unlike trees, some palms grow taller without increasing stem diameter. They resist increasing bending loads by adding layers to cell walls as they age, making tissue denser, especially near the outer surface where bending stresses are greatest. Data from Paul Rich showed palm density increasing outward, with stiffness and strength varying as powers of density. Calculations indicated that this density gradient can make the stem about 2.5 times stiffer than a uniform-density stem of the same mass. The strength distribution also closely matches the bending stress distribution, making the structure mechanically efficient. Bamboo is mentioned as another plant with a similar radial density gradient.

Glenn Ellison introduces MIT 14.271 as a basic industrial organization course focused on IO theory and empirical work, especially for students writing IO theses. The course will generally pair theory lectures with empirical lectures. He emphasizes that IO relies heavily on theory because many policy questions, such as breaking up firms or regulating default agreements, cannot be tested through natural experiments. Empirical IO is also central because it evaluates model assumptions and magnitudes.

The lecture begins with monopoly pricing. A single-product monopolist sets marginal revenue equal to marginal cost, yielding the Lerner index formula: markup as a share of price equals the negative inverse of demand elasticity. Ellison stresses that firms with market power price based on demand elasticities, not demand levels. Monopoly creates profit, consumer surplus, and deadweight loss because mutually beneficial trades are not made. Other possible costs of monopoly include productive inefficiency, quality distortions, rent seeking, and equity concerns, though IO models typically use quasi-linear preferences and set aside income effects.

For multiproduct monopolists, pricing must account for how changing one product’s price affects sales of other products. Diversion ratios matter: with substitutes, markups may exceed the single-product Lerner formula; with complements, firms may price one good below cost to increase profitable sales of another. Examples include printers and ink, newspapers and advertisements, and Google paying Apple to make Google the default search engine.

The lecture then discusses product quality. A monopolist chooses quality based on the marginal consumer’s willingness to pay for quality improvements, while a social planner would consider the average consumer among those served. Monopoly quality may therefore be too high or too low relative to the social optimum. In homogeneous-consumer models, the monopolist’s quality choice is socially optimal because marginal and average consumers coincide.

Ellison next covers durable goods. With commitment power, a durable-goods monopolist should set the monopoly price initially and not later lower price to move down the demand curve, because consumers are forward-looking. Price declines may arise from preferences for early ownership, falling production costs, learning, capacity constraints, or lack of commitment. Without commitment, firms may lower prices later, reducing profits. The Coase conjecture states that with continuous repricing and no commitment, monopoly profits can go to zero, though Ellison notes several reasons it may not apply, including price-adjustment frictions, reputations, new high-value consumers, non-forward-looking consumers, rentals, best-price guarantees, and capacity choices.

The final topic is information design in monopoly pricing. Firms vary in how much product information they provide, as illustrated by laptops, mattresses, and wholesale used cars. Information intermediaries such as Yelp or Amazon may also shape information to affect consumer surplus and seller pricing. Using an example of a new Clover sandwich, Ellison shows that full information, no information, and partial information can produce different profits and consumer surplus. Concealing information can make consumers more homogeneous and increase monopoly profit, while carefully designed partial information can raise consumer surplus and, in the example, also raise profit. The next class will continue information design and discuss empirical papers on monopoly pricing by Chevalier-Goolsbee and Gentzkow-Shapiro.

The passage presents a study on Temperature Scaling (TS) for calibrating CNN-based brain tumor classification from MRI scans under noisy conditions. A lightweight CNN was trained on a composite dataset from Figshare, SARTAJ, and Br35H, with images resized and preprocessed. The model was evaluated before and after TS using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL), and Expected Calibration Error (ECE). Synthetic Gaussian, Poisson, Salt & Pepper, Speckle, and Uniform noise were added to test robustness.

Baseline results showed high accuracy, with TS slightly reducing some classification metrics while minimally affecting NLL and ECE. Under noisy conditions, TS generally reduced NLL and ECE while maintaining or slightly improving prediction metrics. Optimal temperature values varied by noise type and intensity. Additional experiments with ResNet50 showed TS reduced false positives, false negatives, NLL, and ECE without affecting overall accuracy. The study concludes that TS improves calibration reliability under multiple noise scenarios without sacrificing prediction quality, and proposes future comparisons with other calibration methods on larger datasets and modern architectures.

Australia’s business investment rose 0.4% in the first quarter, below expectations. Buildings and structures fell 1.3%, led by a 16% drop in new factories, while equipment, plant and machinery rose 2.5%. Future capex estimates were also weaker than forecast.

George Herbert and two friends chased a suspected bike thief in Bristol, causing him to abandon a stolen white mountain bike. Herbert reported the theft to police, who told him to keep the bike while they try to identify the owner. He is appealing for the rightful owner to provide a matching description or photo, as he does not know where the bike was stolen from.

The passage examines translanguaging in middle grades education, focusing on how teacher candidates understand and use it with multilingual young adolescents. It argues that schools often maintain monolingual norms, while translanguaging can support multilingual students’ linguistic repertoires, identities, belonging, and academic learning. The study addresses gaps in educators’ preparation and implementation of translanguaging practices.

Using a case study approach, the authors studied two middle grades teacher candidates in a year-long Professional Development School experience who were pursuing ESL endorsements. Data came from coursework impressions, interviews, field notes, classroom visits, and supervision notes. The candidates, Patricia and Ruby, worked in different middle schools with transitional ESL and bilingual program contexts.

Findings showed that both candidates held positive, asset-based views of translanguaging and believed their coursework had provided useful strategies. However, both struggled to apply translanguaging in classroom practice. Patricia attempted supports such as online translation tools, peer support, and translated materials, but felt limited in implementation. Ruby valued translanguaging but felt unprepared, especially because she did not speak Spanish, and used few language-inclusive practices. Both candidates also saw limited modeling of translanguaging by cooperating teachers.

The authors conclude that coursework and clinical hours alone were insufficient to close the gap between theory and practice. They argue that middle grades teacher preparation should also build cooperating teachers’ capacity to create linguistically inclusive classrooms. The passage calls for professional development on translanguaging for middle level educators and more research focused specifically on translanguaging with young adolescents.

The lecture finishes Cantor’s theorem: for any set \(A\), \(|A|<|\mathcal P(A)|\). An injection sends \(x\in A\) to \(\{x\}\), and equality of cardinalities is contradicted by assuming a surjection \(g:A\to\mathcal P(A)\) and defining \(B=\{x\in A:x\notin g(x)\}\), leading to \(b\in g(b)\) iff \(b\notin g(b)\). This shows infinitely many infinite cardinalities.

The lecture then begins describing the real numbers via the statement that there exists a unique ordered field containing \(\mathbb Q\) with the least upper bound property, denoted \(\mathbb R\). It defines ordered sets as sets with a relation allowing comparison of any two elements and satisfying transitivity. Examples include the usual orders on \(\mathbb Z\) and \(\mathbb Q\), and dictionary order on \(\mathbb Q\times\mathbb Q\); subset inclusion on \(\mathcal P(\mathbb N)\) is not an order because not all elements are comparable.

Upper bounds, lower bounds, supremum, and infimum are defined for subsets of ordered sets, with examples in \(\mathbb Z\) and \(\mathbb Q\). The least upper bound property means every nonempty bounded-above subset has a supremum in the set. Some simple ordered sets and certain integer subsets have this property, but \(\mathbb Q\) does not. The lecture begins proving this using \(E=\{q\in\mathbb Q:q>0,\ q^2<2\}\), showing that if \(x=\sup E\) in \(\mathbb Q\), then \(x\ge1\) and starting the proof that \(x^2=2\).

The speaker said this year felt different, with an extra day for family and a good practice. They noted regular-season focus issues at game starts but said the team improved and that focus is no longer an issue in the playoffs.

RDRAND and RDSEED read values from a cryptographic co-processor via relatively slow MMIO access. For latency-sensitive applications, a hybrid approach can seed a PRNG with hardware-generated random values to improve performance and security. AMD Zen processors include a hardware random number generator, and the AMD Secure RNG library abstracts low-level access into an API for uses such as cryptographic key generation.

Ford’s CFO John Lawler prepared for an investor call after the February 6, 2024 release of Ford’s 2023 results, the first full-year results under a new reporting structure that separately disclosed Ford Model e, its EV business. Ford Model e reported a $4.7 billion loss before interest and taxes in 2023, up from losses of $0.9 billion in 2021 and $2.1 billion in 2022, contrasting with profits from Ford’s conventional vehicles.

Ford had explored EVs since Henry Ford’s early work on electric car prototypes, but repeatedly halted projects. Its Focus Electric launched in 2009 and was discontinued in 2018 with the broader Focus lineup. Ford later increased EV investment plans from $4.5 billion for 2016–2020 to $50 billion through 2026, aiming for EVs to reach 50% of global production by 2030. In 2021 it introduced the Mustang Mach-E, F-150 Lightning, and E-Transit, received 275,000 orders or reservations by year-end, and became the No. 2 U.S. EV seller. Momentum weakened in 2023, and Ford delayed $12 billion of planned EV investment amid softer demand and pricing pressure.

The passage also contrasts R&D accounting under U.S. GAAP and IFRS. U.S. GAAP expenses R&D as incurred, while IFRS allows qualifying development costs to be capitalized after feasibility is established. Lawler noted Ford’s 2023 R&D expense was $8.2 billion, exceeding its $5.5 billion consolidated profit before interest and taxes, while some international competitors capitalized portions of development costs.

NVIDIA filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 25, 2020. Third-quarter revenue was $4.726 billion, up from $3.014 billion a year earlier, with net income of $1.336 billion and diluted EPS of $2.12. For the first nine months of fiscal 2021, revenue was $11.672 billion, net income was $2.875 billion, and diluted EPS was $4.59. As of October 25, 2020, NVIDIA had total assets of $26.881 billion, total liabilities of $11.547 billion, and shareholders’ equity of $15.334 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $10.139 billion.

NVIDIA completed its $7.134 billion acquisition of Mellanox on April 27, 2020, adding goodwill and intangible assets, and entered into a $40 billion agreement to acquire Arm Limited on September 13, 2020, subject to regulatory approvals and other closing conditions. The company reported two segments: Graphics and Compute & Networking. Third-quarter Graphics revenue was $2.787 billion, while Compute & Networking revenue was $1.939 billion. By market platform, Gaming revenue was $2.271 billion, Data Center was $1.900 billion, Professional Visualization was $236 million, Automotive was $125 million, and OEM and Other was $194 million.

NVIDIA stated that COVID-19 affected operations and demand patterns, with Gaming and Data Center benefiting from work-, learn-, and play-from-home trends, while Professional Visualization and Automotive experienced mixed impacts.

HCPEA named Dr. Terry Woodward as its next President and will hold its inaugural HCPEA Healthcare Forum in June in Park City, Utah. Woodward co-founded Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan’s healthcare private equity practice in 2009 and has been an HCPEA director since 2014. HCPEA is a nonprofit trade association supporting the healthcare private equity community, whose member firms collectively have over $1 trillion in AUM and have started 1,500+ healthcare businesses.

Cboe Global Markets began offering bitcoin futures, marking the first bitcoin-backed security trading on a government-regulated exchange. Early trading suggested many investors expected bitcoin’s price to rise, and Cboe reported heavy website traffic while trading systems operated normally. Bitcoin rose about 8% shortly after futures trading began, later trading above $16,000, while next-month futures contracts traded above $18,000. The cryptocurrency had surged about 1,500% since the start of the year and remained highly volatile on unregulated exchanges. Critics called bitcoin a bubble or fraud, while industry insiders expected broader acceptance. Futures allow investors to speculate on bitcoin’s price without owning it and also make it easier to bet against the currency.

North American cannabis stocks fell sharply, with the North American Marijuana Index down 27.2 percent and the U.S. Marijuana Index down 18.1 percent. Alan Brochstein attributed the Canadian decline to over $1.2 billion in deal offerings and investor concerns over Aphria’s Nuuvera purchase, while speculative U.S. names also sold off. The Horizons Marijuana Life Sciences Index ETF lost 29.61 percent and ETFMG Alternative Harvest ETF fell 19.2 percent. Major stock declines included Aurora Cannabis, Cronos Group, Canopy Growth, THC Biomed, Aphria, MedReleaf and CannTrust. Industry news included MassRoots raising $4.75 million, DOJA Cannabis and Tokyo Smoke merging into Hiku Brands, Jane West launching equity crowdfunding, new cannabis stock indexes from New Cannabis Ventures and Green Market Report, a CNVest pitch contest, Canopy launching a $50 million venture fund, iAnthus acquiring Citiva, and ABCANN announcing a $70 million bought deal.

Billionaire real estate investor Jeff Greene told CNBC that higher interest rates and fiscal policy could threaten the long-running stock market rally. He argued that years of Washington inaction left the Federal Reserve as the main driver of markets through near-zero rates and a $4.5 trillion balance sheet, fueling strong investor sentiment. Greene said low borrowing costs have been more stimulative than tax cuts would be, and warned that Trump administration policy efforts could push rates higher and slow the economy. He noted that stocks have roughly tripled during the bull market, supported partly by low yields, but said weak economic growth does not justify a sharply higher rate environment and expects rates to rise slowly.

The UAE said its first Barakah nuclear reactor will come online in late 2019 or early 2020, after earlier delays. The $20 billion plant’s four reactors are at varying completion stages and are expected to produce 5,600 megawatts, about 25 percent of UAE electricity needs, when fully operational.

Divergence trading compares price swings with oscillator or indicator movements to identify potential momentum shifts or reversals. Divergence occurs when price and indicators such as RSI, MACD, Stochastic Oscillator, or CCI move out of phase. Classical divergence may signal reversals or pullbacks, while hidden divergence often appears during trend pullbacks and may indicate trend continuation. Bullish divergence involves weakening downward price action relative to indicators, while bearish divergence involves weakening upward price action.

The passage emphasizes that divergence strategies are difficult to quantify and should be backtested, optimized, and combined with confirmation signals, market context, volume analysis, and risk management. A simple S&P 500 ETF backtest showed favorable profit factors and Sharpe ratios for some settings, though with relatively few trades and possible curve fitting. Examples include bullish and bearish divergence signals on Nasdaq 100, TSLA, and S&P 500 charts around 2018 and 2020. Common mistakes include misunderstanding divergence, relying only on divergence signals, overtrading, poor risk management, and emotional decision-making.

Power traces should be short, direct, and thick, with a minimum of 15 mils per ampere on standard PCBs. Inductors, output capacitors, and output diodes should be placed close together to reduce EMI, inductance, resistance, noise spikes, ringing, and voltage errors. IC, capacitor, and diode grounds should connect close to a ground plane; ground planes on both PCB sides and multilayer separation of power and signal planes can improve noise and EMI performance. Use one standard via per 200 mA for significant interplane current, and arrange switching current loops to flow in the same direction to reduce radiated EMI.

For UC1825B-SP devices, each output driver can deliver 2-A peak currents, requiring careful layout and a ground plane. A power-ground section should handle high di/dt output-stage currents and connect to PGND. VCC should be bypassed to power ground, while VREF and analog circuitry should be bypassed to signal ground using high-frequency capacitors; TI recommends low ESR/ESL ceramic 1-mF capacitors for VCC and VREF. MOSFET sources, input power return, and the bulk input capacitor must connect to power ground, and outputs should be clamped to VCC and PGND with high-current Schottky diodes.

The document also provides information on receiving documentation updates, TI E2E support forums, trademarks, ESD precautions, and mechanical, packaging, and ordering data, with notices that information and resources are subject to change and provided under TI disclaimers and terms.

The Tenth Circuit affirmed dismissal of Charles A. Meeker’s § 1983 civil rights complaint arising from a New Mexico child abuse investigation that led to custody of his four daughters being transferred to the Human Services Department. The court held Meeker could not represent his minor daughters because he was not an attorney. It adopted the district court’s reasoning that claims against most defendants were barred by res judicata and that some defendants had not been properly served. The court also held that guardian ad litem Deborah Grout was not acting under color of state law for § 1983 purposes because her duty was independent loyalty to the minors, not the state. All defendants’ motions to affirm were granted.

President Andrew Johnson, citing constitutional duties to guarantee republican government and enforce federal law, declared that rebellion had left North Carolina without civil government. He appointed William W. Holden provisional governor to organize a convention of loyal voters to amend the state constitution and restore North Carolina’s constitutional relations with the federal government. Convention voters and delegates had to take the May 29, 1865 amnesty oath and meet pre-secession voter qualifications. Johnson directed military, State, Treasury, Post Office, judicial, Navy, and Interior officials to assist restoration of federal authority, laws, courts, revenue collection, postal service, naval property control, and other federal functions in North Carolina.

The Missouri Court of Appeals affirmed summary judgment for the Bank of St. Louis and its employees in Harvey F. Euge’s malicious prosecution suit. Euge sought damages after his bogus-check conviction was reversed by the Missouri Supreme Court. The court held that reversal of the conviction did not establish lack of probable cause, especially because the original conviction created a presumption of probable cause unless obtained by improper means. Since the underlying facts were undisputed and supported probable cause as a matter of law, the issue was for the court rather than a jury. The court found no error in granting defendants’ motion for summary judgment.

Britain’s FTSE 100 rose 0.6 percent to 7,353.89, recovering from a three-month low as financials and miners rebounded after last week’s sell-off linked to U.S.-North Korea tensions. Banks gained 0.8 percent and miners 1.7 percent, with Standard Chartered, Glencore and BHP Billiton among top gainers. Energy stocks limited gains as oil fell. TUI rose 4.8 percent to a record high after a Credit Suisse upgrade, while Experian and G4S fell after Morgan Stanley downgrades. Mid caps gained 0.8 percent.

The passage introduces video object segmentation-aware audio generation, a task for generating audio for a specific segmented object in a video rather than an entire scene. The authors propose SAGANet, which extends MMAudio with a segmentation-aware control module using global and localized visual features, segmentation masks, and gated cross-attention while training only a fraction of parameters. The model is conditioned on text, video, and object masks, and can generalize from single-source training videos to multi-source test scenes.

The authors also present Segmented Music Solos, a dataset of 5-second musical performance clips with sounding-object segmentation masks, built from MUSIC21, AVSBench, Solos, and URMP. Experiments show SAGANet outperforms MMAudio on distribution matching, audio quality, semantic alignment, and temporal synchronization, with LoRA fine-tuning further improving performance. Ablations indicate that combining global context, focal crops, and masks yields the strongest temporal and semantic results.

Tom Petty’s cause of death was deferred pending further tests after an autopsy. He died at 66 after cardiac arrest and being taken off life support when no brain activity was found. Tributes followed from musicians and fans. Petty rose to fame with the Heartbreakers and later joined The Traveling Wilburys.

A senior Iranian Revolutionary Guards commander said the Guards were ready to prevent regional oil exports if the United States banned Iranian oil sales, backing President Hassan Rouhani’s warning about disrupting shipments. Rouhani’s comments came as Washington demanded countries halt Iranian oil imports by Nov. 4 or face financial measures after leaving the 2015 nuclear deal. Iranian Opec governor Hossein Kazempour Ardebili said US pressure would raise global oil prices and hurt American consumers. The EU is trying to keep the nuclear deal alive despite sanctions challenges. Rouhani said Iran would remain in the accord if remaining signatories guaranteed its benefits. Foreign ministers from China, France, Germany, Britain and Russia will meet Iranian officials in Vienna.

The Gretna Trust & Savings Bank, as dative testamentary executor of Priscilla Lewis’s succession, sued David Lewis to recover $505.58 withdrawn from her bank account after her death and also claimed rent. David admitted withdrawing the funds but argued they belonged to him because he had loaned money to his mother and she intended the bank funds to repay him. The court found the money was deposited in Priscilla Lewis’s name and withdrawn after her death, making David only a creditor of the estate who could not satisfy his claim by taking succession assets. The rent claim was not proven. The appellate court reversed the dismissal and awarded the executor $505.58 plus legal interest and costs.

The work addresses how robots can compare competing valid plans, infer which is better, and explain the differences to humans. It proposes an ontological model extending OCRA with plan qualities such as cost, expected makespan, and number of tasks, along with relations for comparing qualities and plans. Logical rules use these qualities to infer whether one plan is better, worse, or equivalent to another.

The approach is implemented with OWL 2 DL, KnowRob, Prolog rules, ROSPlan, and a framework called know-plan. It is demonstrated through a drink-delivery scenario and validated by answering competency questions about plan characteristics, relations between characteristics, and relations between plans.

The paper also introduces ACXON, an algorithm for generating contrastive ontology-based explanatory narratives. ACXON retrieves divergent knowledge about pairs of entities, filters non-divergent information, and constructs textual explanations at different specificity levels. Compared with the AXON baseline across several temporal planning domains, ACXON uses fewer knowledge tuples and reduces explanation communication time, especially at higher specificity levels. The paper also discusses a refinement to make knowledge selection more restrictive and potentially support shorter, personalized explanations. Future work includes improving narrative accessibility and conducting user studies.

The RSPCA investigated 2,902 animal cruelty complaints in Nottinghamshire in 2017, averaging eight per day and down from 3,157 in 2016. Cases included two kittens beaten to death by owner Aaron Barker, who was jailed for 20 weeks, and 40 animals found in stacked cages without food, water, blankets or toys. Five dogs were put down and one puppy died. Most county complaints involved dogs, followed by cats and horses. Nationally, the RSPCA investigated 141,760 animal welfare complaints in 2017.

The report examines links between Treasury liquidity, fiscal flows, and the saying “Sell in May and come back in November.” It cites recurring Treasury cash balance peaks around January, May, and November. The author argues May is the most consistent stock market liquidity boost because tax refunds enter private hands, with some funds invested in stocks, bonds, and real estate. November spikes are attributed to Fed Treasury buybacks, which may also add investable funds. The author suggests 2018 and 2019 could see stronger May effects due to tax law changes and notes that February and November patterns need further research.

The Directorate General of Goods and Services Tax Intelligence has reportedly issued notices to banks demanding over Rs 6,000 crore in taxes on free or bundled services for customers maintaining minimum balances, calculated retrospectively over five years. The demand values these services using charges imposed on customers who fail to maintain minimum balances. Banks are likely to challenge it, and if upheld, may pass the costs to customers.

A Karolinska Institutet study of 27,500 UK Biobank participants found that poor self-reported sleep was associated with brains appearing older than participants’ chronological age, based on MRI scans and machine learning. Sleep health was scored using chronotype, sleep duration, insomnia, snoring, and daytime sleepiness. Each 1-point decrease in healthy sleep score was linked to about six months greater brain-age gap, and people with poor sleep had brains appearing about one year older on average. Low-grade inflammation explained just over 10% of the association. Researchers said healthier sleep may help prevent accelerated brain aging, though findings may be limited by the UK Biobank’s healthier-than-average participants and reliance on self-reported sleep.

Recent cosmic shear measurements from KiDS, DES, and HSC have made weak gravitational lensing a competitive cosmological probe, achieving percent-level measurements of S8, though Ωm and σ8 remain highly degenerate in lensing-only analyses. Current precision is mainly limited by intrinsic alignments (IA) of galaxies and baryonic feedback, with this paper focusing on IA, which can significantly bias cosmological parameters if unmodelled or inaccurately modelled.

The passage reviews IA models including NLA, extended-NLA, tidal torque, TATT, halo-model, and effective-field-theory approaches. Observations suggest strong colour dependence: red bright galaxies tend to be strongly aligned, while blue galaxies are consistent with no alignment, though survey selection effects limit generalisation.

The paper presents a pipeline that injects NLA, extended-NLA, tidal torque, and extended tidal torque IA models into a large N-body simulation to produce cosmic shear catalogues. It also couples tidal fields to halo-occupation-distribution galaxies to study non-linear galaxy bias and source clustering effects on weak lensing probes. The simulations are based on SkySim5000, an upgrade from cosmoDC2.

The passage also outlines cosmic shear statistics used in the analysis. It describes shear two-point correlation functions predicted from the matter power spectrum under the Limber approximation and measured from simulated galaxy ellipticities. It then introduces non-Gaussian lensing statistics, noting their potential to capture information beyond two-point functions, and describes generating galaxy shear catalogues, aperture mass maps, and convergence maps using Kaiser–Squires inversion.

The speaker welcomes leaders and guests to the signing of a declaration of principles on interim Palestinian self-government between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization. He recalls previous peace efforts, including the Camp David accords, the Egypt-Israel peace, the Madrid negotiations, and the roles of Presidents Carter and Bush. He praises Prime Minister Rabin, Foreign Minister Peres, Chairman Arafat, Mr. Abbas, and Norway for helping advance the agreement. The speaker emphasizes that the accord aims to reconcile Israeli security with Palestinian hopes, acknowledges the difficult work ahead, and pledges active U.S. support for implementation. He urges continued mutual recognition, resistance to extremism, and dedication to a peaceful future for the region’s children.

A 14-year-old girl was arrested in Kingston after allegedly damaging her grandmother’s home during an outburst over a non-working phone. Police said she smashed dishes and a window, fled officers, was later apprehended after a foot chase, and was charged with mischief before being released to her mother with conditions and a court date.

Tesla, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2019. The company, headquartered in Palo Alto, California, reported 180,244,858 common shares outstanding as of October 21, 2019. Tesla operates in two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage.

As of September 30, 2019, total assets were $32.795 billion, total liabilities were $25.313 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $6.040 billion. Cash and cash equivalents were $5.338 billion. For Q3 2019, total revenue was $6.303 billion, gross profit was $1.191 billion, income from operations was $261 million, and net income attributable to common stockholders was $143 million, or $0.80 basic EPS. For the nine months ended September 30, 2019, revenue was $17.194 billion and net loss attributable to common stockholders was $967 million.

Operating cash flow for the nine-month period was $980 million, investing activities used $1.033 billion, and financing activities provided $1.608 billion. Tesla adopted ASC 842 lease accounting on January 1, 2019, completed its acquisition of Maxwell Technologies on May 16, 2019, and reported inventory of $3.581 billion, property and equipment of $10.190 billion, solar energy systems of $6.168 billion, accrued warranty of $983 million, and customer deposits of $665 million.

Oil fell below US$56 a barrel after the American Petroleum Institute reported a larger-than-expected 9.9 million-barrel rise in U.S. crude inventories, raising doubts about whether OPEC-led cuts are tightening supply. Brent crude dropped to US$55.62 and U.S. crude to US$52.84. OPEC and partners, including Russia, are cutting output by nearly 1.8 million barrels per day in early 2017, with OPEC achieving over 90% compliance in January. However, rising U.S. stocks, revived U.S. output, a stronger dollar, mixed OPEC adherence, and smaller non-OPEC cutbacks pressured prices.

Restoration Affiliates (RA) was founded in 2011 by Rich Piltch of ARS, Damon Gersh of Maxons Restoration, Ras Fenger of Disaster One, and Andy Goldberg of RestoreCore as a collaborative partnership of independent regional restoration and reconstruction firms. Inspired by a “Go-Giver” philosophy of giving without expecting immediate return, RA aimed to help smaller firms compete with national providers such as Belfor by offering national coverage, local expertise, and shared capacity for large losses and catastrophes.

By fall 2013, RA had 21 member organizations with combined revenue of $300 million. Members were privately owned, commercially focused, full-service restoration contractors meeting specific revenue, insurance, licensing, service, communication, and training standards. RA was structured as an LLC with equal shareholders, a nine-person board, committees, dues, marketing contributions, and referral fees for work passed between affiliates.

The restoration industry was fragmented, but large insurance and property management companies increasingly wanted fewer providers with national reach. ARS had shifted its business from reliance on insurance companies toward property management companies, emphasizing relationships, priority service agreements, training, disaster planning, live 24/7 phone response, daily communication, and detailed reporting.

RA’s early success included winning a three-year national contract with Forest City Enterprises after presenting its national coverage and disaster planning software capabilities. However, RA still faced unresolved strategic questions: how much authority an outside administrator should have; how to create transparent communication and job-tracking systems; how to establish and enforce consistent service standards; how to handle overlapping territories and internal competition; whether referral fees supported or undermined collaboration; how to price referred work; which disaster planning software to market; and how to define and promote RA’s value proposition. Piltch believed RA offered ARS and its peers a low-risk growth strategy, but wanted these issues resolved so other members could assume more responsibility.

The paper develops a general method for proving codensity presentations of monads using the principle “Codensity Monads = Density + Duality.” Its central notion is a codensity setting: a functor decomposes through a dual equivalence, the opposite of a dense functor, and a contravariant right adjoint that induces a monad. The main theorem states that in every such setting, the induced monad is isomorphic to the codensity monad of the original functor.

The framework reduces codensity proofs to density results, which are often standard in algebraic categories, and separates domain-specific work from categorical structure. It recovers known codensity presentations, including the ultrafilter monad on sets and topological spaces, the Vietoris monad on Stone spaces, the Giry monad, Radon and Kantorovich monads, double dualization monads, and the monad arising from Isbell duality. It also provides new presentations for the filter monads on sets and topological spaces, the lower Vietoris monad on topological spaces, the expectation monad, and a double dualization monad on abelian groups.

The paper applies the theorem uniformly across several settings: ultrafilter and filter monads via Boolean algebras and semilattices; Vietoris-type monads via join-semilattices, complete semilattices, and frames; probability monads via effect algebras, effect modules, and representation theorems; and semiring-valued measure monads via modules over finite semirings. It concludes by suggesting future work on formalizing the theorem in the theory of monads, extending it to monad extensions, relating it to prior general ultrafilter-monad results, and applying it to further Vietoris and probabilistic powerdomain variants.

Henry Clay was born on April 12, 1777, in Hanover County, Virginia, during the American Revolution, and died in Washington after a long public career. His father died when Clay was young, and his formal education was limited, though he continued learning throughout life. Licensed to practice law in his twenty-third year, he moved to Lexington, Kentucky, practiced law, and entered public office in 1803.

Clay served in the Kentucky Legislature, the United States Senate, and the United States House of Representatives, where he was repeatedly chosen Speaker. He helped negotiate the treaty ending the War of 1812, later served as Secretary of State under John Quincy Adams, returned to law, and again served in the Senate until shortly before his death. His official career lasted from 1803 to 1852, with fewer than ten years outside public office.

The passage presents Clay as a nationally significant statesman known for eloquence, judgment, will, devotion to the Union, and concern for human liberty. It emphasizes his role in major crises, including the War of 1812, the Missouri question, Nullification, and later compromise measures involving slavery and newly acquired territory. Though repeatedly defeated for the presidency in 1824, 1832, and 1844, he retained a large following.

The passage describes Clay as opposed in principle to slavery while also noting that he owned slaves and favored gradual emancipation in Kentucky. It portrays him as rejecting extremes on slavery, supporting the American Colonization Society, and hoping colonization might help end slavery while benefiting Africa. It concludes by mourning Clay’s death and presenting him as a providential figure in national emergencies.

The passage compiles quotes criticizing taxation, debt, banking, corporate tax breaks, patriotism, and education, emphasizing themes of middle-class burden, financial control, profit-driven corporations, learning from mistakes, and control of perception.

Jacob Hackin became the first person in Cambridge prosecuted for failing to clear up dog mess after ignoring a fixed penalty notice issued at Midsummer Common. He pleaded guilty and was ordered to pay a £75 fine, £125 costs and a £30 victim surcharge. Cambridge council said dog owners must clean up after pets and warned fouling will not be tolerated.

A visiting Harvard Law School professor, Carlos Portugal Gouvêa, was arrested Oct. 1 for firing a pellet gun near a Jewish temple during Yom Kippur services. He told police he was hunting rats. The temple was locked down after security heard shots. Gouvêa was charged with illegally discharging a pellet gun, disturbing the peace, disorderly conduct and property damage for allegedly breaking a nearby car window. Harvard placed him on administrative leave. Police and synagogue officials said they did not believe antisemitism was involved. His lawyer called the matter a misunderstanding.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that on January 30, 2017 it entered into an underwriting agreement for the issuance and sale of $17 billion in senior unsecured notes. The offering includes notes due 2020, 2022, 2024, 2027, 2037, 2047, and 2057 with interest rates ranging from 1.850% to 4.500%. The notes will be issued under a May 18, 2009 indenture, as supplemented by a Twelfth Supplemental Indenture dated February 6, 2017, with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A. as trustee. Interest is payable semiannually on February 6 and August 6, beginning August 6, 2017. The filing also lists related exhibits, including the underwriting agreement, supplemental indenture, note forms, and legal opinions.

Kelly Keefe will become president of Highland Heights-based ERC on Jan. 1, making her the first woman to lead the organization in its 97-year history. She succeeds Pat Perry, who will remain as chairman during the transition and focus on NorthCoast 99, ERChealth, and client relations. Keefe has worked at ERC for nearly 13 years, currently as vice president of training, consulting, and coaching services, and previously spent eight years at Deloitte.

Former CIA case officer Kevin Mallory, 60, is on trial in Virginia on charges that he gave a Chinese spy top-secret information, including details about human assets, for $25,000. Prosecutors say Mallory’s actions were exposed after customs agents found $16,500 in undeclared cash when he returned from Shanghai in 2017, leading to further investigation of a Samsung phone and computer discs containing classified documents. Defense lawyers argue Mallory was loyal to the U.S. and was trying to draw out Chinese intelligence contacts by providing phony materials, saying he had already contacted CIA associates about a suspicious Chinese think tank offer. Mallory faces up to life in prison under an espionage statute rarely tried in court.

The passage describes a virtual object machine learning system integrated with a messaging system. The system generates synthetic training data from 3D models, such as hands or dogs, by programmatically varying poses, textures, lighting, camera positions, and environment backgrounds. Markers or metadata identify key points such as joints, edges, and other regions of interest, enabling labeled training images to be produced without manual labeling.

The training data is used by machine learning schemes, including support vector machines, logistic regression, K-nearest neighbor methods, convolutional neural networks, supervised neural networks, and unsupervised schemes, to classify objects, poses, gestures, and key points in images or videos. Classification results may support features such as applying annotations or overlays in a messaging application, for example adding text based on a detected hand gesture or dog pose.

The passage also describes the messaging system architecture, including client applications, server systems, APIs, databases, image processing, social networking, ephemeral message timers, content collections such as stories, annotation systems, message structures, and supporting software and hardware architectures.

Upgrade is a near-future sci-fi, horror, and action film starring Logan Marshall-Green as Grey Trace, a technology-averse mechanic who becomes paralyzed after a savage attack. A secret processor called STEM restores his movement and gives him machine-like precision, leading him to seek revenge and uncover the truth. The review praises the film’s violent but purposeful action, believable futuristic setting, exploration of artificial intelligence, and strong visual execution. It notes that the mystery is predictable and could have used more exposition, but says the film remains gripping, entertaining, and successful across multiple genres.

Sen. John McCain criticized President Trump for approving release of the GOP-Nunes memo, calling it a partisan attack on the FBI and Justice Department that undermines the rule of law. He urged officials to stop politicizing Robert Mueller’s Russia investigation, warning such actions serve Putin’s interests. The memo alleges FBI surveillance abuses involving Carter Page, while Democrats sought release of their response memo.

The message transmits correspondence between Hawaiian agents and the Secretary of State and discusses U.S. interests in Hawaii and China. It notes that the Hawaiian Islands are progressing in civilization, are strategically located in the Pacific, and serve as a major stopping place for American and European vessels, especially U.S. whaling ships. Although Hawaii’s government is described as new and weak, it is portrayed as peaceful and interested in education, religion, morals, and the arts of civilized life. The United States seeks no exclusive control over Hawaii but supports its independence, security, and prosperity, and would oppose attempts by another power to seize or colonize the islands. Congress is asked to fund a moderate allowance for the U.S. consul there to protect American citizens and address complaints involving them.

The message also reviews developments in China following Britain’s treaty opening Amoy, Foo-Choo-Foo, Ningpo, and Chinghai to British commerce. It questions whether U.S. trade will also gain access and notes substantial American imports from China and growing exports to China. In Freeman v. Polstein, a real estate broker sued a purchaser for commission after failing to secure acceptable purchase terms. Another broker procured the accepted offer. The court held there was no proof of a special contract making the purchaser liable and no evidence plaintiff brought about the sale. Judgment for plaintiff was reversed and a new trial granted.

Thabane Sigadla, 24, from KwaDabeka, was sentenced to 38 years’ imprisonment for carjacking, possessing an unlicensed firearm and ammunition, after being linked to hijackings in KwaDabeka in 2016 and New Germany in 2017.

Azerbaijan’s Health Ministry spokesperson Safaya Ahmadova said the US State Department’s travel health recommendations for Azerbaijan do not reflect the country’s healthcare situation. She said Azerbaijan’s medical standards are recognized internationally, foreigners receive treatment there, and US claims about tuberculosis are untrue, with cases decreasing yearly.

Nanyang Polytechnic scientists led by Dr Henry Leung have developed a more sustainable method to convert coffee waste into biodegradable plastic. Their process adds water and Cupriavidus necator bacteria to “Nanyang coffee” waste, allowing bacteria to produce PHA, a biopolymer used for biodegradable plastics. After initial low purity and waste-producing extraction methods, the team switched to cheaper, eco-friendlier solvents and genetically modified the bacteria, achieving over 50 per cent purity and about 1g to 3g of pure PHA from 100g of coffee waste. The team has completed laboratory experiments and is seeking industrial partners to commercialise the process within three to five years.

The passage introduces AI-Noether, a formal abductive reasoning system for scientific discovery. It addresses cases where a discovered polynomial formula fits data but is not derivable from existing scientific theory. Given background axioms and a target hypothesis expressed as polynomial equations, AI-Noether generates candidate missing or modified axioms that allow the hypothesis to be derived.

The method has three steps: Encode, which represents axioms and hypotheses as ideals and varieties; Decompose, which uses primary decomposition to identify irreducible components introduced by the hypothesis; and Reason, which tests candidate generators via Gröbner-basis elimination to determine whether adding them makes the hypothesis derivable.

The paper positions AI-Noether as distinct from systems such as AI-Feynman, AI-Descartes, and AI-Hilbert, which focus on discovering formulae or checking consistency with background theory rather than identifying missing axioms. It reviews related work in abductive reasoning, explainable machine learning, and AI-driven scientific discovery.

Experiments test the system on scientific-law axiom systems including Kepler’s Third Law, Compton scattering, Einstein relations, escape velocity, light damping, Hagen–Poiseuille, neutrino decay, Hall effect, and carrier-resolved photo-Hall effect. In single-axiom removal tests, AI-Noether recovered nearly all missing axioms reported, including all axioms in most listed systems. For multiple missing axioms, recovery was more limited, with success rates varying by benchmark and failures more common when three axioms were missing.

The paper also gives a sufficient algebraic criterion for recoverability based on ideals having the same height and a common minimal associated prime. It concludes that AI-Noether can help reconcile polynomial scientific discoveries with existing theory and suggests future extensions to non-polynomial laws such as ODEs and PDEs.

The Iowa Supreme Court reviewed whether Gary Kehde was entitled to unemployment benefits after being discharged by Dubuque Packing Company for possessing a lit marijuana cigarette on company premises. The Department of Job Service had disqualified him for misconduct, but the district court reversed, finding the Department improperly refused to give effect to the employer’s withdrawal of its protest.

The Supreme Court held that Kehde was not required to apply for rehearing before seeking judicial review, so the district court had jurisdiction. However, it ruled that withdrawal of an employer’s protest does not automatically entitle a claimant to benefits because eligibility depends on the facts found by the agency. The court found substantial evidence that Kehde’s possession of marijuana on company premises constituted misconduct, even without proof he knew of the company rule, because it violated standards the employer had a right to expect. The court reversed and remanded.

STAT’s biotech newsletter previews fourth-quarter biotech events and highlights news including calls for a U.K. antitrust probe into drugmakers, the government shutdown’s impact on HHS, Trump administration pharma tariff and Pfizer pricing developments, women’s health companies, autism treatment expectations, drug trials in pregnant women, and updates involving UnitedHealth, FDA, MoonLake, Lilly, Amgen, and Tylenol.

A regulation American football field is 120 yards long and 53.3 yards wide, or 360 by 160 feet, covering about 1.32 acres. The main playing area between the end zones is 100 yards long, while each end zone is 10 yards deep and 53.3 yards wide. Goal lines are 100 yards apart, and a ball must break the plane of the goal line to score a touchdown.

Field markings help officials spot the ball and track progress. Yard lines appear every yard, with full-width lines every five yards and numbers generally every ten yards. Hash marks determine ball placement and vary by level: 18 feet 6 inches apart in the NFL, 40 feet in college, and 53 feet 4 inches in high school. Field numbers also vary, positioned 12 yards from the sideline in the NFL, typically 9 yards in college, and usually 6 yards in high school. Sidelines are 6 feet wide and help define boundaries while keeping sideline personnel away from play.

The IMF said Ghana’s “Ghana beyond Aid” vision and first-year economic performance under President Akufo-Addo are an inspiration to Africa. Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta outlined the agenda at the IMF/World Bank Spring Meetings, highlighting domestic resource mobilisation, investment in job-creating sectors, and plans to sustain growth.

MoviePass announced data showing its ticket purchases made up significant portions of opening weekend domestic box office grosses, including 13.21% for Roman J. Israel, Esq. and 10% for Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri, with usage increasing in later weeks for some films. The company also signed a marketing and performance-based revenue agreement with an unnamed independent movie distributor, meaning it will promote certain films to subscribers and earn revenue based on increased ticket sales. The passage notes that MoviePass ads align with the company’s stated plan to grow its user base, collect viewing data, and target marketing to subscribers.

A March 27, 2018 test by Stagno found that 20 of 124 VPN and proxy providers leaked users’ real IP addresses via WebRTC, while 101 hid IPs. The passage lists leaking providers and links to a Google document with results and logging policies. It recommends testing VPNs with IP leak tools and disabling WebRTC or using browser add-ons if leaks occur. It also lists VPN services said to protect privacy with WebRTC, including ExpressVPN, NordVPN, StrongVPN, Private Internet Access, VyprVPN, and others.

Industry-sponsored clinical trials have become increasingly complex, raising participant and staff burden, costs, and trial duration. The passage describes Merck’s “Lean Design” project, which aimed to simplify schedules of assessment by rebuilding them from “Ground Zero,” retaining essential elements such as primary endpoints and adverse event collection while challenging other assessments based on biological plausibility, timing, frequency, sample size, and relevance.

Merck applied Lean Design workshops to six protocols across therapeutic areas including cardiovascular disease, psychiatry, cancer, and other medical conditions. The Faro Smart Design Tool quantified participant time, staff time, activity costs, blood volumes, resource needs, and operational complexity for original, workshop-recommended, and adopted versions of schedules of assessment.

Workshops commonly recommended reducing laboratory tests, physical examinations, repeated assessments, and full-participant assessments where subsets were sufficient. Recommended reductions varied by trial, with participant time reduced by 4 to 47 hours per participant. In a large cardiovascular trial, recommended savings of about $9,000 per participant could have saved nearly $120 million overall. Study teams adopted some but not all recommendations, often because protocols were already in late development or due to concerns about uncertainty, regulatory expectations, quality-of-life measures, or pharmacology assessments.

The authors conclude that rebuilding protocols using Lean Design principles and real-time quantitative feedback can substantially reduce inessential schedule elements, participant and staff burden, complexity, and costs. Merck subsequently launched a company-wide effort to implement Lean Design principles across therapeutic areas, though the authors note that results should be tested in other companies.

The passage describes an improved non-occluding intravascular blood pump designed to reduce hemolysis and blood clotting by minimizing shear forces. The pump includes a cylindrical shroud with inlet and outlet, an impeller, a centrally disposed motor, and pillars coupling the motor to the shroud. Design features include a trumpeted inlet, extended shroud length, raked-back impeller blade leading edges, optimized bare hub length, matched impeller and stator flare angles, selected impeller-shroud clearance, blade wrap angle, and pillar alignment with outlet flow. Computational fluid dynamics and experimental testing identified shear stress hotspots at the impeller, shroud, and pillars. Iterative prototype development, especially prototype P_31, reduced maximum and mean shear stress, improved flow guidance and efficiency, maintained hydraulic output, and showed substantially improved normalized hemolysis results compared with earlier designs.

MRC Vaudreuil-Soulanges officials sought to reassure residents that local recyclables are being processed despite a global recycling crisis caused by China’s stricter standards for imported materials. The MRC, a member of Tricentris since 2017, generates about 17,000 tonnes of recyclable materials annually. Tricentris manages nearly 33 per cent of Quebec’s recyclables and says it is coping by investing in research, quality improvements, and market diversification. Officials urged citizens to continue recycling and improve sorting quality, directing them to online tools and Tricentris updates.

In Mason Brothers & Tarlin v. United States, the court considered the dutiable value of Christmas tree ornaments exported from Germany in August 1938 and entered at Boston. Based on stipulated similarity to F. W. Woolworth Co. v. United States and comparable market conditions, the court found the ornaments were freely offered in the Sonneberg-Lauscha district for domestic consumption and export. The proper foreign and export values were held to be invoice unit prices plus 3% social assessments and applicable packing, container, and shipment-preparation costs. The appeal was dismissed as to other merchandise.

Asteroid 2025 TF, a 1–3 meter near-Earth object, passed 428 ± 7 km above Antarctica on October 1, near the altitude of the International Space Station. It was detected by the Catalina Sky Survey hours after its flyby and posed no danger. ESA astronomers used the Las Cumbres Observatory telescope in Australia to refine its trajectory and closest-approach timing with high precision. The event demonstrated the ability of planetary defense networks to track small, fast-moving objects and improve detection and prediction systems.

The speaker says winning the first game provides confidence and forces the opponent to adjust. The break between games is acceptable and allowed time to enjoy the win. A key player remains day to day but helps with faceoffs and penalty kills. The upcoming matchup is tough, requiring the team to reach its potential.

Molecular dynamics simulations were used to study radiation damage in pure niobium at 300 K for PKA energies of 1–75 keV, comparing SNAP, EAM, FS-1, and FS-2 interatomic potentials. All potentials showed rapid Frenkel pair production, recombination, and stabilization, with subcascade formation beginning around 20 keV and defect production following two energy-dependent power-law regimes. Vacancy clustering was consistently stronger than interstitial clustering, while maximum cluster sizes increased with PKA energy.

The potentials differed substantially in predicted defect production, clustering, and morphology. EAM produced the highest surviving defect counts and large vacancy clusters, with a balanced mix of loop- and ring-like structures and occasional ⟨100⟩ clusters. FS-1 generated more compact or disordered clusters, including ⟨110⟩ dumbbells, crowdions, small C15 rings, and hybrid structures. FS-2 favored extended 1/2⟨111⟩ dumbbells, crowdions, and dislocation loops, matching dominant experimental defect types. SNAP produced compact cascades, disordered clusters, ⟨111⟩ dumbbells, and many C15-like rings up to nine atoms, which may evolve into 1/2⟨111⟩ or ⟨100⟩ loops. The study shows that interatomic potential choice strongly affects predicted radiation damage in niobium.

Live Nation is celebrating National Concert Week with $20 all-in tickets to over 2,000 summer concerts and events from April 30 to May 8. The promotion includes more than 1.5 million tickets across multiple genres, available on its website.
Horsell Lodge near Woking, Surrey offers specialised residential and dementia care, including respite and long-term options, with bespoke support based on residents’ personal histories and needs.

A Federal High Court in Katsina ordered former Governor Ibrahim Shema remanded in EFCC custody until April 27 over alleged N5.7 billion SURE-P money laundering charges. Shema pleaded not guilty to 26 counts. The court deferred hearing his written bail application after prosecution objected to both written and oral bail requests.

The article reviews Google’s Pixel Watch 4 as a $399 outdoor smartwatch with multi-day battery life, satellite emergency communication, offline Google Maps, Fitbit health tracking, and a slimmer design. Compared with the Apple Watch Ultra 3, it is less rugged, has more limited satellite messaging, weaker water resistance, and fewer adventure features, but costs about half as much. The Apple Watch Ultra 3 offers broader satellite texting, international availability, stronger durability, dive-computer use, and better water-lock behavior. However, the Pixel Watch 4’s Fitbit-based sleep and health tracking, fast charging, comfort, and integration with Google Maps make it a strong sub-$500 option for outdoor use.

The passage examines limitations of machine learning-assisted genome-wide association studies (ML-assisted GWAS), where missing phenotypes are imputed and then used for genetic association testing. The authors argue that conventional approaches treat imputed phenotypes as observed and can produce pervasive false-positive associations because they do not account for imputation uncertainty or SNP-level differences between observed and imputed phenotypes.

Using UK Biobank type 2 diabetes data, the authors trained a phenotype imputation model and performed GWAS on imputed diabetes status. Despite reasonable imputation quality and high genetic correlation with the ground-truth GWAS, the imputed GWAS had high replication failure rates. Many false positives were linked to variants associated with HbA1c through erythrocytic rather than glycemic pathways, making them associated with imputed diabetes but not true diabetes risk.

The authors introduce Post-prediction GWAS (POP-GWAS), a summary-statistics-based framework that combines GWAS of observed phenotypes in labeled samples, imputed phenotypes in labeled samples, and imputed phenotypes in unlabeled samples. POP-GWAS uses SNP-level differences between observed and imputed phenotype associations in labeled data to debias imputed GWAS results. The authors state that POP-GWAS provides unbiased estimates, valid p-values, improved power over GWAS using only observed phenotypes, and requires minimal assumptions about imputation methods, variables, or quality.

Simulations showed that conventional imputed GWAS can be biased and have inflated type-I error, while POP-GWAS remained valid and more powerful than observed-only GWAS. In the type 2 diabetes benchmark, POP-GWAS replicated all identified loci in the ground-truth GWAS and avoided the erythrocyte-related false positives.

The authors also applied POP-GWAS to dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-derived bone mineral density across 14 skeletal sites in UK Biobank. POP-GWAS increased effective sample size, identified 188 independent loci compared with 135 from conventional GWAS, and, after meta-analysis, identified 303 genome-wide significant loci including 89 novel loci. The results highlighted site-specific genetic architecture, genetic correlations with fracture and osteoarthritis traits, and candidate genes including COL4A2, WWOX, and LGR5.

The authors conclude that current ML-assisted GWAS methods can be invalid, while POP-GWAS offers a valid, powerful, computationally efficient framework for future genetic studies using imputed phenotypes.

The passage presents a framework for designing dilute viscoelastic Boger fluids with targeted rheological properties. The authors use polyisobutylene dissolved in polybutene/light mineral oil mixtures and characterize the fluids using rheometry and gel permeation chromatography. They apply the Zimm model to extract shear modulus, relaxation time, polymer-solvent interaction parameter, and first normal stress difference coefficient, while noting that the Zimm estimate for the latter overpredicts measurements by a constant factor. Experiments identify power-law relationships between rheological properties and design parameters: polymer concentration, molecular weight, and solvent viscosity. These empirical relationships form an invertible design matrix that maps target values of modulus, relaxation time, and normal stress coefficient to fluid composition. The method is experimentally validated by fabricating fluids with controlled modulus, relaxation time, or normal stress behavior, and is proposed as useful for designing Boger fluids, interpreting viscoelastic flow experiments, and estimating material properties that are difficult to measure directly.

Jason Day will face Louis Oosthuizen, Jason Dufner and James Hahn in the WGC-Match Play group stage in Texas. Fellow Australians Marc Leishman and Cameron Smith are also in the field, with Smith needing a strong result to secure a Masters invitation. Day and Leishman are on opposite sides of the draw, while Smith could meet Day in the semi-finals.

The passage introduces a paper on logical approaches to nondeterministic polynomial time over semirings. It situates semirings as algebraic structures used in computer science for Boolean decision problems, counting, real-valued computation, weighted automata, database provenance, and semiring semantics for logics. The paper extends prior work on first-order semiring semantics to existential second-order logic, aiming to prove semiring analogues of Fagin’s and Cook’s theorems and to generalize connections between nondeterministic computation over the reals and existential theories to positive commutative semirings.

The preliminaries define semirings, ordered semirings, positive semirings, and the natural order, with examples including the Boolean semiring, non-negative reals, natural numbers, tropical semiring, polynomial semirings, and Łukasiewicz semiring. The paper assumes semirings are commutative, positive, and non-trivial.

The passage defines propositional, first-order, and existential second-order logics over semirings with constants and formula comparisons. Formula evaluation maps to semiring values, with conjunction interpreted as multiplication, disjunction as addition, existential quantification as summation, and universal quantification as product. Satisfiability is defined as evaluation to a non-zero value. Existential second-order quantification is given Boolean-style semantics over extensions of interpretations.

The passage also defines BSS machines over semirings, including input, output, computation, branch, and shift nodes, and introduces nondeterministic computation by allowing guessed semiring-valued inputs. This yields the complexity class NPK and corresponding polynomial-time reductions and completeness.

Finally, the passage states a semiring version of Fagin’s theorem. It shows that existential second-order semiring logic is contained in NPK and begins proving the converse by encoding polynomial-time BSSK computations as existential second-order formulas over ordered K-interpretations.

Week 7 Idaho high school football rankings saw the top 15 remain largely stable, with Bishop Kelly staying No. 1 after a 22-20 win over Columbia and No. 4 Eagle remaining unbeaten after a 21-14 win over Mountain View. Rocky Mountain, Rigby, Hillcrest, Timberline, Kendrick, Lakeland and others also remained strong with decisive wins. The biggest movement came near the bottom, where Minico entered the rankings at 4-1 and Ririe joined at 6-0. Middleton and Capital dropped out after losses. Several undefeated teams continued notable starts, including Owyhee, North Fremont, West Side and Ririe.

The Supreme Court returns from its summer break for its annual “long conference,” where justices will review petitions that accumulated over recess and are expected to grant five to 15 cases. The 2025-26 term begins Oct. 6.

Recent coverage highlighted Justice Clarence Thomas questioning rigid reliance on precedent, former Justice Anthony Kennedy warning about increasing partisanship and antagonism in public discourse and court opinions, and Louisiana Solicitor General J. Benjamin Aguiñaga’s role in major Voting Rights Act and Ten Commandments cases. Other commentary discussed former Justice Lewis Powell’s influence on Joel Klein and Justice Amy Coney Barrett’s approach to originalism.

The court recently allowed the Trump administration to withhold nearly $4 billion in foreign-aid funding and was asked to review Trump’s executive order on birthright citizenship. A response is due in a case involving the administration’s effort to end protected status for Venezuelan citizens. The passage also explains Supreme Court order lists and notes research suggesting emergency docket timing varies and may correlate with ideological outcomes.

Euro zone stocks began 2017 at their highest in over a year after factory PMI rose to 54.9, its fastest expansion in more than five years. Thin holiday trading affected markets, while the euro fell below US$1.05 as the dollar resumed gains on expectations of U.S. rate hikes and fiscal expansion under Donald Trump. Italy’s FTSE MIB, Germany’s DAX and France’s CAC all reached multi-month highs, and lower-rated euro zone bond yields fell.

Islamic State attacks in Istanbul and Baghdad had limited immediate market impact, though the Turkish lira slipped near record lows amid concerns over instability and tourism. China’s manufacturing expanded for a fifth month, though growth slowed, while the yuan ended 2016 as Asia’s worst-performing currency. Bitcoin rose above US$1,000 for the first time since late 2013.

The passage is a Texas Monthly article examining Enron’s rise and troubles in 2001. It describes Enron’s transformation from a debt-burdened pipeline company into a dominant energy trading firm under Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling, whose Gas Bank model and trading strategies helped Enron control major natural gas and electricity markets. The company built an aggressive culture focused on intellectual talent, rapid dealmaking, high compensation, internal competition, and harsh employee ranking.

The article argues that Enron’s culture contributed to its problems. Its pursuit of quick profits, use of mark-to-market accounting, willingness to abandon projects, and treatment of clients as “counterparties” drew criticism. Enron expanded into new markets including electricity, paper, steel, weather, broadband, and online trading, while moving away from asset-heavy businesses. Rebecca Mark’s international and water ventures, including Dabhol and Azurix, are presented as examples of troubled asset-based projects.

By 2001, Enron faced falling stock prices, criticism over California’s energy crisis, costly problems in India, the collapse of telecommunications, failed broadband ambitions, scrutiny of accounting practices, and negative press. Skilling resigned after six months as CEO, citing personal reasons, while Lay returned and promised a more focused and less harsh Enron culture.

The NBA released its full 2017-18 season schedule, including the national TV schedule on TNT, ESPN, ABC and NBA TV. The season opens Oct. 17 with Boston at Cleveland and Houston at Golden State on TNT. Christmas Day features Philadelphia at New York, Cleveland at Golden State, Washington at Boston, Houston at Oklahoma City and Minnesota at the L.A. Lakers. The listed national TV schedule runs through April 11.

The passage lists Bengali transliteration mappings for digits, punctuation, currency and special signs, including ways to type reserved symbols using “~”. It explains that common English symbols remain unchanged, gives “namaskaar” for নমস্কার, and describes ZWJ/ZWNJ use for alternate ligature rendering, half-formed or dead consonants, and separating paired vowels like ai or au.

The passage argues that the retail apparel sector is under pressure from e-commerce, overexpanded store chains, mall overcapacity, and trade policy uncertainty. It presents Francesca’s Holdings Corp. as a financially strong company in the sector, with $488 million in sales, a $320 million market capitalization, $48 million in cash, no debt, and about $57.6 million in free cash flow. Francesca’s operates more than 670 stores in 48 states and targets women aged 18–35 with apparel, jewelry, and accessories, with plans to reach 900 stores.

For 1Q17, sales rose 1% to $107.7 million due to new boutiques, while comparable store sales fell 5% and net income declined to $4.3 million from $7.1 million. FY18 guidance projects net sales of $518 million to $537 million and diluted EPS of $1.07 to $1.17. The passage notes that Francesca’s has strong liquidity, mixed valuation metrics, solid profitability, and is repurchasing shares. It concludes that despite competition and uncertainty, the company’s cash flow and balance sheet may support future share price growth.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 26, 2015. Apple is a California corporation headquartered in Cupertino, established in 1977. It designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, personal computers, portable digital music players, and related software, services, accessories, networking solutions, and third-party digital content and applications.

Apple’s products and services include iPhone, iPad, Mac, iPod, Apple Watch, Apple TV, iOS, OS X, watchOS, iCloud, Apple Pay, Internet Services, software applications, accessories, and support offerings. In September 2015, Apple introduced iPhone 6s and 6s Plus, announced iPad Pro, released iOS 9, OS X El Capitan, and watchOS 2, and announced a new Apple TV, tvOS, and Apple TV App Store.

Apple sells products worldwide through retail stores, online stores, direct sales, cellular network carriers, wholesalers, retailers, and value-added resellers. Its customers include consumers, small and mid-sized businesses, education, enterprise, and government markets. In 2015, direct and indirect distribution channels accounted for 26% and 74% of net sales, respectively; no single customer accounted for more than 10% of net sales in 2015, 2014, or 2013.

In 2015, Apple changed its reportable segments to geographic segments: Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific. Domestic and international net sales accounted for 35% and 65% of total net sales, respectively. Substantially all hardware products are manufactured by outsourcing partners primarily in Asia, while some Mac computers are manufactured in the U.S. and Ireland.

Apple’s strategy focuses on providing a high-quality user experience through integrated hardware, software, and services; expanding digital content and application delivery; supporting third-party developers; and investing in retail, online, distribution, research and development, marketing, and advertising. R&D expense was $8.1 billion in 2015, $6.0 billion in 2014, and $4.5 billion in 2013.

The company identifies major risks including global economic conditions, intense competition, rapid technological change, product transitions, reliance on distributors and carriers, inventory and supply risks, dependence on outsourcing partners, product quality issues, access to third-party content and intellectual property, legal proceedings, regulation, international operations, retail store risks, system failures, data protection obligations, retention of key personnel, business interruptions, quarterly fluctuations, stock price volatility, currency exchange rates, credit risk, and tax changes.

As of September 26, 2015, Apple had approximately 110,000 full-time equivalent employees. It owned or leased 25.6 million square feet of building space and owned 1,757 acres of land. Its common stock trades on NASDAQ under AAPL. Apple paid $11.4 billion in dividends in 2015 and expected quarterly dividends of $0.52 per common share, subject to Board approval.

Oil prices dipped after Israel and Hamas agreed to pause fighting in Gaza, easing regional risks. U.S. stocks were little changed near record highs, with the S&P 500 up 0.1%, while gold stayed near its record and Treasury yields rose slightly. PepsiCo beat adjusted profit forecasts despite weaker North American demand, Delta raised optimism with stronger earnings, and Novo Nordisk announced a $4.7 billion Akero Therapeutics acquisition. European markets were mixed, while most Asian stocks rose.

Callinex Mines filed an independent technical report on SEDAR for a maiden 2018 Preliminary Economic Assessment of its 100%-owned Nash Creek and Superjack Projects in New Brunswick. The PEA outlines a 10-year, 3,900 tpd open-pit operation at Nash Creek with dense media separation and flotation facilities. It estimates a pre-tax IRR of 34.1%, post-tax IRR of 25.2%, pre-tax NPV8% of C$230 million and post-tax NPV8% of C$128 million, with C$168 million in pre-production capital costs and zinc priced at US$1.25/lb. The projects are near highway, power, smelter, port, rail and power infrastructure. Callinex plans drilling to identify nearby satellite deposits and notes further exploration potential across its 150 km² land package.

Pay for private college presidents rose in 2015, with 58 earning over $1 million, up from 39 in 2014, according to Chronicle of Higher Education data cited by The New York Times. Average compensation increased 9% to $570,000. Ohio presidents in the top 100 included Daniel Curran, Barbara Snyder, Grant H. Cornwell and Marvin Krislov.

The African Union Commission’s Department of Trade and Industry organized the First African Union Start Up Fest to discuss youth entrepreneurship, start-up development, capacity needs, policy-private sector engagement, and foundations for an African Association of Start-ups. Participants included tech hubs, youth entrepreneurs, officials, RECs, business leaders, development partners, academia, and civil society. Speakers emphasized SMEs’ role in competitiveness, the need for infrastructure, education, capacity building, labour market efficiency, youth entrepreneurship, digital economy opportunities, inclusion, and expanded access to education, skills, finance, technology, infrastructure, and training. A key outcome was agreement to hold a follow-up side event at the 2018 Transform Africa Summit in Kigali on creating an African Association of Community Innovation Hub.

This study used the multi-ancestry transcriptome-wide association method METRO with European American and African American gene expression and genotype data from GENOA, plus GWAS summary statistics, to identify genes associated with general cognitive function, white matter hyperintensity, and Alzheimer’s disease. After FOCUS fine-mapping, the authors identified 266 genes for general cognitive function, 23 for white matter hyperintensity, 69 for Alzheimer’s disease using a European ancestry GWAS, and 2 for Alzheimer’s disease using an African ancestry GWAS. Several identified genes had not been reported in the original GWAS analyses.
