Enrichment analyses implicated pathways related to innate immunity, vascular dysfunction, neuroinflammation, amyloid processes, and protein regulation. ICA1L overlapped between white matter hyperintensity and Alzheimer’s disease analyses, suggesting a possible shared transcriptomic mechanism between Alzheimer’s disease and vascular dementia pathology. The authors note limitations including use of transformed B-lymphocyte expression data and reliance mainly on European ancestry GWAS, but conclude that multi-ancestry TWAS may help identify gene targets for dementia prevention or treatment.

Offsites may focus on alignment, communication, coordination or celebration, but breakthrough-oriented events should disrupt routines, build connections, center on a meaningful shared purpose, align people and programming with that purpose, and drive practical follow-through. Yarrow Kraner’s HATCH experiences apply these principles through unfamiliar settings, communal living, limited connectivity, inclusive collaboration, and careful curation of diverse participants. Programs combine preparation, talks, exercises, activities, prototype work, music, meals and free time to spark creativity, deepen relationships and support impactful action.

Enron was mentioned in multiple June 7, 2001 reports, including a Chicago power supply agreement with Exelon’s Commonwealth Edison to provide electricity to Chicago and 47 suburbs, with Enron supplying 60% of 400 megawatts annually. Several reports focused on Enron’s Dabhol Power project in India, where lenders met in Singapore over disputes with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board involving unpaid bills, high tariffs, possible termination, and the future of the project’s second phase. Indian officials, including Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, expressed confidence the dispute could be resolved. Other mentions included Enron Broadband’s participation in a $30 million investment in AP Engines, Enron Power Operations leasing additional London office space, Enron’s role among energy companies criticized in California, and lobbying related to California direct-access electricity rules.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2022. The company designs, manufactures and sells fully electric vehicles and solar energy generation and storage products, reporting through automotive and energy generation and storage segments.

For Q1 2022, total revenue was $18.76 billion, up from $10.39 billion in Q1 2021. Automotive revenue was $16.86 billion, energy generation and storage revenue was $616 million, and services and other revenue was $1.28 billion. Gross profit was $5.46 billion, income from operations was $3.60 billion, and net income attributable to common stockholders was $3.32 billion, or $2.86 diluted earnings per share.

As of March 31, 2022, Tesla had total assets of $66.04 billion, total liabilities of $30.63 billion, and total stockholders’ equity of $34.09 billion. Cash and cash equivalents were $17.51 billion, while total current assets were $29.05 billion. Net cash provided by operating activities was $4.00 billion, net cash used in investing activities was $2.17 billion, and net cash used in financing activities was $1.91 billion.

Tesla reported continued effects from COVID-19, including logistics and supply chain challenges, semiconductor shortages, temporary manufacturing closures, inflation, and increased shipping, raw material and labor costs. The company stated these factors contributed to product pricing adjustments.

The filing also discusses digital assets, debt, inventory, property and equipment, stock-based compensation, lease arrangements in New York and Shanghai, and multiple legal proceedings, including matters related to the SolarCity acquisition, the 2018 CEO Performance Award, directors’ compensation, a potential going-private transaction, and alleged race discrimination. As of April 19, 2022, Tesla had 1,036,009,925 shares of common stock outstanding.

Chiefs defensive lineman Chris Jones said he stopped pursuing Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence on the game-winning touchdown because he thought Lawrence was down. Jones called it a learning lesson, said it won’t happen again, and denied deactivating social media to avoid criticism, saying the accounts were already inactive before the game. He said he is focused on the Chiefs’ upcoming Sunday night game against the Lions.

This study examined how the interval between SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and natural infection affects hybrid immunity. Researchers analyzed two cohorts: a longitudinal group of 10 previously infected individuals and 20 infection-naïve vaccinated controls, and a cross-sectional group of 66 participants including vaccine-only individuals, people infected before vaccination, and people with breakthrough infections. Serum samples were tested using ELISA and live-virus neutralization assays against original SARS-CoV-2 and variants including Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, Omicron BA.1, and Omicron BA.2.

Previously infected vaccinees showed significantly higher neutralizing titers than vaccine-only participants. In the larger cohort, hybrid immunity produced higher spike-specific antibody levels and stronger neutralization against all tested variants, with the largest fold increases against Beta and Omicron variants. Hybrid immune sera also showed improved antibody potency and broader variant cross-neutralization compared with vaccination alone.

The interval between infection and vaccination was the strongest factor associated with antibody levels and neutralizing titers. Longer intervals, ranging up to 404 days, were associated with progressively higher neutralization, especially against more vaccine-resistant variants. Variant cross-neutralization also improved with longer exposure intervals, while neutralizing potency index did not significantly change over time. These patterns were observed both in individuals infected before vaccination and in those with breakthrough infections.

The authors conclude that hybrid immunity provides stronger and broader serum antibody responses than vaccination alone, and that immune responses continue to improve for at least 400 days between antigen exposures. They state that delayed vaccination after infection may still provide substantial benefits, particularly against emerging vaccine-resistant variants, while noting that intentional infection is not a reasonable public health strategy due to the risks of COVID-19.

DPI (UK), a Castle Donington company making aluminium frames and lightboxes, has received more than £12,200 from the Collaborate scheme to buy a new automated saw. The equipment will allow the firm to cut larger aluminium panels, produce bigger structures in-house, reduce contract completion times, increase output and potentially create jobs. The company, launched three years ago by Sandra Wiggins and Paul Tomlinson, has grown rapidly, moved to larger premises and reported 37% growth last year. Collaborate, funded by the ERDF and partners and overseen by Leicester City Council, offers £5,000 to £25,000 grants to eligible businesses, alongside workshops and business advice.

President Trump’s description of the House-passed health care bill as “mean” upset some conservatives who said he had pressured them to support it. Rep. Dave Brat said the comment left Republicans “scratching our heads,” noting Trump had praised the bill after its passage. Senate Republicans remained divided on changes involving Medicaid expansion, coverage requirements and subsidies. Sen. John Cornyn said passage by July 4 was a goal but suggested the process could take until late July.

ARDD issued a report commending Jordanian government agencies and UNHCR for rapid legal support to Syrian refugees. The report highlighted internationally recognised legal services in camps, coordination mechanisms, free protection services, documentation support, legal awareness programmes, and capacity-building for legal providers. It noted challenges including evolving refugee needs, labour market access procedures, limited evaluation of legal aid, financial constraints, and pressure on Jordan. A recent UNHCR registration campaign has registered 25,000 refugees.

Andrew W. Lo introduces MIT Sloan’s 15.401 Finance Theory, an introductory course for first-year MBA students. He argues that finance is central to business because it provides a rigorous and practical framework for valuation and management decisions. He defines finance as “mathematics plus money” and illustrates its relevance through James Simons, Warren Buffett, and Jack Welch, who used different skills but all understood financial logic.

Lo outlines the course’s focus on four parts of the financial system: households, financial intermediaries, non-financial corporations, and capital markets. He identifies two fundamental challenges in finance: valuing assets and managing assets. Using an auction of an unopened package containing an iPod Nano, he demonstrates price discovery under limited information and explains that lack of transparency can reduce value.

The course framework begins with accounting concepts, especially stocks and flows, represented by balance sheets and income statements. Corporate finance decisions are described in terms of cash flows involving investors, real assets, operations, reinvestment, and payouts. Lo also applies the same framework to household financial decisions, including education, labor income, consumption, saving, borrowing, and risk management.

He emphasizes that time and risk are what make finance distinct and challenging. The course will first cover valuation and net present value, then risk, and finally applications to corporate finance. Lo also introduces basic principles of finance, including no systematic free lunch, preference for more money, money sooner, and less risk, and self-interested behavior.

Course requirements include readings, participation, one case study, a midterm, and a cumulative final. Optional problem sets with solutions will be provided, and many exam questions will come from them. Lo advises students to review notes, attend lectures prepared, work both individually and in groups, ask questions, and engage personally with the material.

Moody’s said India may meet its 3.3% fiscal deficit target for the year ending March 2019 by cutting planned capital spending, despite risks to revenue and spending targets. Poll respondents in Singapore and Mumbai mostly expected fiscal slippage. Rising crude oil prices were seen as a major economic risk, while the PSB recapitalisation package was viewed as insufficient.
Sensors show greater noctule bats catch birds midair.

A differentially private database security system receives client queries for private databases and returns differentially private responses based on specified privacy parameters and privacy budgets. The system identifies requested data and operations, modifies the operations according to a differential privacy level, executes them on the data, and provides the resulting private output to the client.

The system includes a user interface, library, account management system, query handling engine, database integrator, and privacy system. It supports differentially private count, median, mean, variance, interquartile range, batch and stochastic gradient, random forest, histogram, model testing, synthetic database, and validation queries. Techniques include adding Laplacian, Gaussian, or Cauchy noise; perturbing model training or outputs; creating perturbed histograms and confusion matrices; and projecting data into a differentially private synthetic database while preserving spatial relationships.

The disclosure also defines differential privacy, privacy parameters, global sensitivity, local sensitivity, and smooth sensitivity, and describes example computer hardware capable of executing the described methods.

Texas Instruments warns that the MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 integrated circuits can be damaged by ESD, potentially causing performance degradation or failure. Revision A, updated September 30, 2025, revised power modes, package options, device tables, specifications, CPU features, ADC ENOB, DEBUGSS, DEVICEID, and USERID information, and removed DGS32 package content. The document includes mechanical, packaging, soldering, stencil, thermal pad, via, tape, ordering, RoHS, MSL, and part-marking information, with drawings and data subject to change. TI provides resources “as is,” disclaims warranties, and states users are responsible for product selection, design, validation, testing, and compliance.

TyreWatch predictive tyre management launched on 16 May at Harwell Innovation and Science Campus. Designed for fleets, it monitors tyre pressure and temperature via rim-mounted sensors and sends real-time data to a central server using cellular and satellite communications. Fleet managers receive web portal updates and push notifications, while drivers see only a dashboard warning light. The system analyses vehicle-specific baselines and issues maintenance or critical alerts depending on pressure loss or temperature trends. It can continue monitoring after vehicles stop, helping detect punctures before the next workday. TyreWatch supports integration with existing vehicle technologies and third-party telematics, and is offered as software-as-a-service or a retrofit solution. Testing reportedly prevented 95% of tyre-related breakdowns. It was developed by the Pathway to Autonomous Commercial Vehicles consortium with £1.2 million Innovate UK funding.

The passage describes using a “horns” or double mid-screen alignment to attack a Box & One defense when the star player is a ballhandler. The alignment lets the star go left or right, drive, pass to a rolling screener, or kick out to corner shooters. Counters include drop passes when help defense steps up, screen-and-pop variations, and single/double continuity if no shot is available. Successful execution requires proper screening, post play, offensive rebounding, recognition, communication, timing, and experience. Implementation includes breakdown drills, scrimmaging, scouting opponents’ defensive reads, adjusting during games, varying alignments, and attacking weaker defenders. The Box & One defense uses four zone defenders and one “Chaser” denying the star the ball.

Japanese government bonds firmed after a strong two-year auction, with the 10-year yield steady at 0.015% and futures up 0.04 at 151.02. The 2.2 trillion yen sale drew bids 5.51 times the amount offered, above the previous 3.82 ratio, pushing short and superlong yields lower. Investors awaited details of the Bank of Japan’s May bond-purchase plans after April reductions in shorter-dated buying. BOJ officials remain divided over guidance on annual purchases, while Governor Haruhiko Kuroda said yield targets can be achieved with less buying. The BOJ kept policy unchanged Thursday and gave its most optimistic economic assessment in nine years. Japan’s core consumer prices rose for a third month in March, but less than expected.

Jammu and Kashmir Deputy Chief Minister Nirmal Singh said the government is considering introducing skill development courses and an optional skill development paper in educational institutions. He interacted with students of GCW Gandhi Nagar and GDC Nawakadal, praised their vocational initiatives, and urged colleges to improve students’ technical skills and product quality to promote entrepreneurship.

A fired Tacoma Walmart employee allegedly tried to retrieve a safe he had attempted to steal, which contained heroin and Xanax. He admitted the safe and drugs were his, and deputies booked the 24-year-old into Pierce County Jail for unlawful possession of a controlled substance.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced to life in prison plus 30 years for her role in the 2014 murder of Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, her former son-in-law. Adelson denied involvement and claimed she was convicted without evidence, prompting Judge Stephen Everett to cite her “utter lack of remorse.” Prosecutors said the murder stemmed from the Adelson family’s desire to move Markel’s ex-wife, Wendi Adelson, and their children to South Florida. Her husband, Harvey Adelson, also said she was innocent.

The address expresses gratitude for peace, health, liberty, and abundant harvests, then reviews foreign relations, finances, domestic policy, and public administration. Relations with most nations remain peaceful. The Russia-Ottoman war is discussed with hope for moderation and relief for Greeks. Relations with France are stable, though U.S. indemnity claims remain unresolved. The northeastern boundary dispute with Great Britain has been referred to the King of the Netherlands as umpire. Commercial tensions with Great Britain continue, especially over colonial trade restrictions. A treaty with Austria has been prepared, and the United States continues to promote reciprocal commercial treaties.

The address reports favorable revenue conditions, with receipts exceeding expectations and substantial payments made toward the public debt. Revenue for 1829 is expected to equal or exceed 1828, aided by increased grain and flour exports due to poor European harvests. The tariff is defended as a response to foreign commercial restrictions and as protection for domestic industry, though revision is recommended if it burdens any section unfairly. The address also warns against state resistance to federal laws on claims of unconstitutionality.

Reports from the War Department describe the Army as generally disciplined and call attention to relations with Indian tribes, including land acquisition, subsistence obligations, and conflicts over sovereignty. Public works, fortifications, surveys, canals, harbors, and the Military Academy at West Point are described as important national undertakings. Naval reports note suppression of piracy, protection of neutral commerce, planned exploration in the Pacific and South Seas, and continued improvements to ships, dry docks, timber supplies, and navy yards.

The Post Office has greatly expanded since 1792, though recent expenditures slightly exceeded receipts. A new penitentiary in the District of Columbia has been completed, requiring legislation for its use. Claims under the Treaty of Ghent have been distributed. Public land revenues remain significant, and Congress is asked to consider extending payment deadlines for land purchasers. The address also urges timely legislation for the fifth census, with improvements in manufacturing returns, age categories, and compensation for census workers.

The study reviewed adrenalectomy specimens from 2018 to September 2022 and found that normal adult adrenal veins have asymmetrical longitudinal smooth muscle bundles resembling fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) lesions. Adrenal cortical adenomas and pheochromocytomas commonly showed vascular changes consistent with segmental arterial mediolysis (SAM), including hyalinization, intimal fibroplasia, myxoid or fibrinoid degeneration, and reduced arterial wall thickness. No FMD-like lesions were found outside adrenal tissue, and fetal adrenal vessels lacked these changes. The authors suggest that adrenal tissue milieu, hormones, or hormone receptors may contribute to vascular wall changes and the pathogenesis of FMD/SAM-like lesions.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated October 26, 2021, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2021. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Exchange Act unless specifically incorporated by reference. The filing was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

Two pieces of ammunition were found in a Litchfield High School bathroom, prompting a soft lockdown at the high school and middle school. Police responded, and students were dismissed to parents around 10 a.m.

HPC in manufacturing is evolving from traditional customized and prebuilt systems toward public cloud, hybrid cloud, and HPCaaS models. IDC says public cloud is expected to become the most important HPC architecture, while hybrid models can combine in-house handling of sensitive data with cloud scalability for peaks or non-critical workloads. Public cloud and HPCaaS can improve performance, agility, flexibility, cost management, access to modern hardware and methods, collaboration, and support for new data-based products, services, and business models. However, cloud-based HPC still requires skilled personnel to configure clusters, run calculations, and analyze results.

IDC recommends that manufacturers evaluate whether to build in-house HPC or buy services based on utilization, budget, performance, flexibility, security, energy efficiency, and skills. It also recommends developing virtual product and manufacturing processes, creating a holistic data strategy and single source of truth, choosing scalable and secure HPC solutions, and using external expertise where needed. The findings are based on a December 2021 survey of 200 decision makers at industrial enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

The passage argues that the Yankees reflect MLB’s shift away from emphasizing starting pitching and toward stronger bullpens, highlighted by Aroldis Chapman’s closer contract and the team’s continued focus on relievers like Dellin Betances. It notes this trend dates back to the Joe Torre era with Wettland, Nelson, and Rivera. The author questions whether highly paid starters are worth it when managers often remove them after about five innings, citing 2015’s average of 87 pitches per start and declining quality starts. John Smoltz is presented as favoring starters pitching more innings. The passage also says heavy bullpen use lengthens games and notes the commissioner has considered limits on reliever usage.

A study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences found that airplane passengers who want to avoid colds or flu may reduce contact by choosing a window seat and staying there. Researchers observed 10 U.S. flights, tested surfaces and air for viruses, and modeled exposure to a hypothetical infectious passenger, concluding that about one person on a 150-passenger flight would be infected on average. The study found no tested cold or flu viruses and observed only one coughing passenger, limiting broader conclusions. It was funded by Boeing, which also had input in the results. Researchers found that aisle-seat passengers moved most often and that the 11 people closest to an infected passenger faced the highest risk. Experts called the study novel but too small for general conclusions.

The passage explains the SuperTrend indicator, a trend-following technical analysis tool created by Oliver Seban to identify trend direction, continuation, and reversals. It appears as a line on price charts, turning green below rising prices and red above falling prices, and reverses when price closes across the prior SuperTrend value. The indicator is based on median price and Average True Range (ATR), using bands calculated with an ATR period and multiplier; Seban’s default settings are 10 periods and a multiplier of 3.

A backtest on the S&P 500 over 60 years using weekly data, long-only trades, reinvested capital, and no commissions, slippage, or dividends produced a win rate of about 67%, with a maximum drawdown of 24.6% versus 56.24% for buy-and-hold. The article states the indicator works best on instruments that sustain trends and identifies weekly charts as the best tested timeframe, though it can be used intraday, daily, or weekly.

The passage describes SuperTrend as a lagging indicator that can provide clear entry and exit signals, filter market noise, assist with stop-loss placement, and adapt to volatility by widening or tightening its trend line. It can be combined with RSI, moving averages, and Bollinger Bands for confirmation. Limitations include false signals and whipsaws, especially in volatile or choppy markets, so backtesting, parameter adjustment, and risk management are recommended.

Nathan Calvin, general counsel of the AI policy nonprofit Encode, accused OpenAI of using intimidation tactics against critics while California’s SB 53 AI safety law was under debate. Calvin said OpenAI subpoenaed him and Encode as part of its litigation involving Elon Musk, seeking private communications about SB 53 and implying critics were secretly funded by Musk, which Calvin denied. He alleged OpenAI used the lawsuit as a pretext to intimidate opponents and weaken the bill’s transparency and safety requirements.

OpenAI chief strategy officer Jason Kwon said Encode’s support for Musk in the lawsuit and its funding disclosures raised legitimate questions, and that subpoenas are standard in litigation. Other AI safety figures, former OpenAI employees, and nonprofit leaders expressed concern about the alleged tactics. Calvin said Encode refused to provide documents because it is not funded by Musk. He praised some OpenAI safety work but said the company’s actions were inconsistent with its nonprofit mission.

The message reports that the country is at peace, national defense remains effective, public health has improved, and private, state, local, and federal relief efforts are addressing distress during the depression. It states that emergency economic measures, including actions by the Federal Reserve and Reconstruction Finance Corporation, helped prevent disaster and contributed to signs of recovery, though the worldwide depression continued.

The President identifies three priorities for recovery: reducing government expenditures and balancing the federal budget, reorganizing the banking system, and cooperating economically with other nations. He proposes major budget reductions, continued furloughs and salary cuts for federal employees, limits on federal public works, veterans’ payment reforms, broader excise taxes, and consolidation of federal agencies. He argues that banking failures and hoarding have worsened the crisis and calls for immediate banking reform, including changes to farm loan systems, while rejecting currency inflation or government banking.

The message urges international cooperation on disarmament, economic recovery, monetary stability, trade barriers, and war debts, while opposing suspension of December 15 debt payments. It also notes pending legislative issues including transportation, power regulation, antitrust law, conservation, child health, the World Court, the St. Lawrence Seaway Treaty, bankruptcy, and court procedure. The conclusion emphasizes limited emergency federal action, individual responsibility, local and state roles, voluntary cooperation, and preservation of liberty and individualism.

A Case Western Reserve University study published in The Journal of Family Violence estimates that childhood exposure to domestic violence costs the U.S. economy more than $55 billion annually through higher health-care costs, increased violent crime, and productivity losses linked to lower educational attainment. The CDC estimates 15.5 million U.S. children are exposed to intimate partner violence each year, and more than 25% experience such exposure during childhood. The study estimates that by age 64, each exposed child costs the economy nearly $50,000 on average, including $11,042 in medical costs, $13,922 in violent-crime-related costs, and $25,531 in lost productivity. Researchers said the findings quantify the long-term public health and economic burden of childhood exposure to domestic violence and may help policymakers support prevention and treatment efforts.

The passage criticizes We Energies as a regulated monopoly with high rates and highly paid executives, arguing that utilities face little competition and should prioritize residents and businesses over profit. It says Milwaukee-area electric rates were once among the lowest under former CEO Charlie McNeer, but rose sharply after the Public Service Commission became more compliant with utility rate requests. The author attributes increases to power plant overbuilding and high shareholder returns. Groups including the Citizens Utility Board and the new Initiative for Competitive Energy are challenging rates before the PSC, with some calling for a rollback rather than We Energies’ proposed rate freeze through 2019.

Canadian Blood Services is opening Canada’s largest blood donation clinic at Eau Claire Market in Calgary on July 10, replacing the 18-bed 13th Avenue S.W. clinic with a 20-bed site. The organization is seeking 150,000 donations by July 1 for Canada’s 150th birthday but needs 50,000 more by the end of June. O negative blood supply is critically low. Calgary will also get a new operations facility off Barlow Trail in 2020.

Plaintiffs, Cromwell and four employees, sought to enjoin NASD Regulation from compelling testimony in its investigation of Pallet trading, punishing assertions of Fifth Amendment privilege, and allegedly using grand jury materials. They argued NASD Regulation was acting as an agent of federal prosecutors and that grand jury secrecy had been violated.

The court found NASD Regulation’s Division of Enforcement conducted an independent private regulatory investigation, despite contacts with prosecutors and CPAG, a separate NASD unit assisting criminal investigations. The court credited testimony denying that the Rule 8210 interview demands resulted from government coercion or suggestion, and held the Fifth Amendment did not apply because the relevant conduct was not attributable to the government.

The court also found no credible evidence that grand jury materials were improperly disclosed to or used by unauthorized Regulation personnel. Plaintiffs failed to show that documents used in NASD questioning were protected “matters occurring before the grand jury.”

The court denied relief, while noting that NASD Regulation’s physical and administrative separation between CPAG and enforcement staff was inadequate enough to create concerns and warrant careful review.

F2 Logistics seeks a fourth straight win and the No. 2 seed when it faces Generika-Ayala in the 2018 PSL Grand Prix at The Arena. Generika-Ayala recently earned its first win after four losses. Coach Arnold Laniog urged focus, noting all teams can surprise. Sta. Lucia meets winless Smart in the opener, while several teams continue battling for positions Nos. 3 to 7.

Prince’s music becoming available on Spotify sparked mixed reactions because he opposed the platform while alive. The passage lists other artists resisting or limiting Spotify access: Taylor Swift objected to music being perceived as having no value; Garth Brooks avoids Spotify and iTunes, favoring his own website; Thom Yorke criticized Spotify despite Radiohead’s music being available there; Beyoncé’s Lemonade is absent due to Tidal; and Joanna Newsom called Spotify “a villainous cabal of major labels.”

Market Research Future reports that the global blowout preventer market is expected to grow significantly by 2021, driven by rising oil and gas demand, increased unconventional drilling, offshore exploration, and higher safety standards. The report segments the market by type, well type, and region, and analyzes pricing, supply chains, Porter’s five forces, revenues, country-level trends, key players, and competitive developments. The Middle East is expected to dominate due to onshore drilling, while Asia-Pacific is also projected to grow strongly due to hydrocarbon potential. Key players include Aker Solutions, Weatherford International, FMC Technologies, Cameron International, National Oil Well Verco, Proserve, and Uztel.

The passage is from the SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 and includes licensing, disclaimer, terminology, table-of-contents, figure/table listings, and technical excerpts. It states that implementing portions of SD Specifications versions 1.0 or 1.01 may require licenses from SD-3C, LLC, and that the Simplified Specification/Addendum is provided “AS-IS” without warranties or implied licenses.

The specification defines SD Memory Cards, SDIO compatibility, physical interfaces, command protocols, registers, electrical parameters, and related addenda. SD cards are described by read/write or ROM capability, supply voltage, capacity classes, speed classes, bus protocols, form factors, security features, write protection, and content protection. Capacity classes are SDSC up to 2 GB, SDHC over 2 GB through 32 GB, and SDXC over 32 GB through 2 TB.

The passage describes SD bus, SPI bus, UHS-I, UHS-II, low-voltage interface, application performance class, cache, self-maintenance, and command queue features. UHS-I supports up to 104 MB/s on a 4-bit SD bus, while UHS-II includes modes up to FD624 at 624 MB/s. Communication is host-controlled using broadcast or addressed commands, with card identification mode and data transfer mode. Initialization uses commands such as CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, CMD3, and voltage-switch procedures for UHS-I.

The specification also outlines command/response/data token structure, CRC protection, block read/write operations, card registers, ROM card command restrictions, card reset behavior, and data transfer rules including use of CMD12 to stop read or write operations.

Lake Lugano, in Switzerland’s Italian-speaking canton of Ticino, is presented as a quieter alternative to crowded Lake Como. The glacial lake offers palm-lined promenades, cobbled streets, alpine scenery, mild sunny weather, and fewer tourists. Experts recommend visiting lakeside villages such as Gandria, Morcote, and Bré by ferry, along with attractions including Monte San Salvatore, Monte Generoso, Parco Ciano, Parco San Grato, Parco Scherrer, and the Olive Grove Trail. Visitors can enjoy hiking, art museums, local cuisine, Ticino merlot, lakefront cafés, boat-access restaurants, and historic stays such as Grand Hotel Villa Castagnola.

Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and Public Safety Minister Ralph Goodale expressed condolences after a van attack in Toronto killed 10 people and injured 15. Trudeau said there was no apparent terrorism or national security link and praised first responders for their bravery. Goodale said Toronto police are leading a large homicide investigation with support from all levels of government. Police arrested 25-year-old Alek Minassian, who was due in court on April 24, 2018.

European stocks opened slightly higher Tuesday, led by energy shares as Brent crude hit a more than two-year high after the Forties pipeline shutdown. London’s FTSE 100 rose 0.2%, while Paris’s CAC 40 and Frankfurt’s DAX each gained 0.1%. Investors are awaiting interest rate decisions from the US Federal Reserve, Bank of England and European Central Bank.

Outgoing Fed chair Janet Yellen said recent Wall Street gains were not necessarily a “bubble,” though asset valuations were elevated and investors should diversify. She described the US economy and job market as strong, with wages rising faster. Yellen said she was disappointed Trump did not renew her term. Jerome Powell will replace her as Fed chair.

Dunas Capital Asset Management, founded in Spain in 2016, manages around €4.5 billion and focuses on capital preservation, risk management, transparency, innovation, and sustainable growth. The firm offers traditional and alternative investment strategies across financial and real estate markets, serving local and international clients. Its investment philosophy applies value investing across asset classes with strict volatility-based risk controls. Dunas Capital manages four mutual funds with different return and risk targets, plus alternative investments in areas including infrastructure, renewable energy, transportation assets, and agriculture.

In Hogg’s Estate, the court dismissed exceptions and confirmed the account. The majority held that the will’s gift to “grandchildren” included all grandchildren, including the children of afterborn children, because the term was unambiguous and no heir may be disinherited except by express words or necessary implication. The court rejected arguments that only grandchildren of the four children named in the will should inherit, reasoning that “per stirpes” determined shares but did not limit the class.

Judge Stearne dissented, joined by Judge Sinkler. The dissent argued that the will, read as a whole and as of its execution date, showed the testator intended to benefit only his four named children and their issue. It viewed the inclusion of grandchildren of afterborn children, whose parent had already received an intestate share, as contrary to the testator’s intent and an unjust distribution.

The tax department is likely to use the net asset value method to determine FMV of unlisted shares for capital gains tax, targeting undervalued property sales through company structures. The budget proposal deems FMV as consideration if higher than sale price, worrying unlisted companies, start-ups, promoters, PE investors and venture funds.

AMD’s SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block specification defines legal terms for using the specification and standardizes how SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests communicate with hypervisors while protecting guest register state. It describes the 4 KB decrypted GHCB page, GHCB MSR protocol, protocol negotiation, feature advertisement, GHCB GPA registration, VMGEXIT handling, automatic and non-automatic exits, and required guest state exposure.

The specification covers support for SEV-SNP features including secrets and CPUID pages, EFI confidential computing blob protocol, page state changes, guest requests, extended guest requests, AP creation, APIC ID lists, multi-VMPL execution, restricted injection, hypervisor doorbells, IPI and timer requests, SEV-TIO guest requests, and Secure AVIC. It also documents SMP booting, NMI handling, debug register support, termination requests, unsupported exits, and guest identification of SEV-ES support.

The document states that SMM is not supported in this version and nested virtualization is not supported under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP.

Former Katsina State Governor Ibrahim Shehu Shema was remanded in EFCC custody by a Federal High Court in Katsina over alleged N5.7 billion SURE-P money laundering. He pleaded not guilty to 26 charges. Justice Babagana Ashigar set April 27, 2018, to hear his written bail application after rejecting an oral request.

Dogs of the Dow is a stock-picking strategy that invests equal amounts in the 10 highest dividend-yielding stocks among the 30 Dow Jones Industrial Average components, rebalancing annually at the start of each year. It aims to outperform the DJIA by focusing on high-yield blue-chip stocks. The strategy was popularized by Michael B. O’Higgins in 1991, though related concepts appeared earlier.

Investors can implement it by buying individual stocks, ETFs, or mutual funds that follow the approach. Backtests in the passage show underperformance versus the S&P 500 over recent decades: from 1998, $10,000 grew to $32,000 under Dogs of the Dow versus $60,000 in the S&P 500, with CAGRs of 5% and 7.7%. A 2014 comparison also found related ETFs underperformed the S&P 500. The passage concludes the strategy is simple but poorly diversified and should only be a small part of assets.

FULE logically erases the entire user area using CMD32 with argument 0, CMD33 with the end of user area, and CMD38 with argument 00000002h. Hosts must check FULE_SUPPORT before issuing it. Unsupported or improperly addressed FULE results in ERASE. Out-of-sequence commands set status errors and reset the sequence. FULE is supported only for SDHC and SDXC cards, not SPI, and progress is indicated by DAT0 low.

June 26, 2001 news coverage focused on California’s energy crisis. FERC began closed settlement talks among California officials, utilities, power suppliers, and other Western interests over refund claims, with California seeking about $8.9 billion for alleged electricity overcharges and generators disputing the figure while citing unpaid bills. Judge Curtis Wagner urged compromise and warned he could recommend a settlement if talks failed. Gov. Gray Davis met with new FERC commissioners Pat Wood and Nora Brownell, discussing refunds, natural gas prices, plant inspections, and allegations by former Duke Energy workers that Duke reduced output and manipulated operations during shortages; Duke denied wrongdoing. Other articles covered state efforts to suspend direct access to protect repayment of power purchases, concerns about whether proposed new power plants would lower prices, and growing interest in solar-powered housing developments.

The S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price NSA Index rose 6.3% year over year in February 2018, up from 6.1% in January. The 10-City Composite increased 6.5%, and the 20-City Composite rose 6.8%. Seattle, Las Vegas, and San Francisco posted the largest annual gains at 12.7%, 11.6%, and 10.1%, respectively. Before seasonal adjustment, the National Index rose 0.4% month over month, while both composites gained 0.7%; after adjustment, the National Index rose 0.5% and both composites gained 0.8%. All 20 cities reported monthly increases. David Blitzer said home prices have risen continuously for 70 months and are likely to keep rising amid economic and employment growth.

The passage describes COVIDFast, a rapid, high-throughput, RNA extraction-free RT-qPCR assay for detecting SARS-CoV-2 in anterior nares swab samples (SwabFAST) or saliva samples (SalivaFAST). The assay uses proprietary buffers, standardized 2 mL barcoded cryovials, compatible collection devices, and automated lab workflows to reduce bottlenecks associated with conventional RNA extraction.

Buffer optimization showed that Tris-Borate-EDTA supported SwabFAST testing and Tris (2-carboxyethyl) phosphine supported SalivaFAST. The SwabFAST viral transport buffer remained stable across tested storage temperatures and durations. Analytical validation found that extraction-free testing produced qualitative results comparable to extraction-based RT-qPCR, with a limit of detection of 4 copies/µL for both swab and saliva.

Clinical validation showed 100% positive and negative percent agreement for swab samples compared with extraction-based CDC protocol testing, and 98.8% positive and 99.4% negative agreement for saliva samples. Compared with SalivaDirect, SwabFAST showed 83.3% positive and 99.4% negative agreement, while SalivaFAST showed 95% positive and 100% negative agreement. By December 23, 2021, COVIDFast had been used for 409,883 tests, mostly SwabFAST, with an overall positivity rate of 8.10%. The authors state that eliminating RNA extraction improves speed, cost, throughput, and reduces contamination and human error.

Coach Quenneville said the team has experience in big games but must stay focused, prepare properly, and improve on its last performance. He described the playoff journey as difficult, citing division battles and tough series, and praised the team’s resilience. He highlighted the leadership of the core players, Hossa’s complete and consistent game, Kimmo’s reliability, and the importance of depth. He said the team will not change its preparation, must avoid looking ahead, start strong, and rely on quickness, pace, consistency, and players rising to challenges.

In Betteys v. Ætna Life Insurance Co., the court considered claims under Dr. William H. Betteys’ accident policy after his death, alleged to have resulted from an infected hand injury. The insurer denied liability for death benefits, recalled death-proof forms, but offered to consider weekly disability indemnity upon proof. The court held that letters from the insurer and agents were admissible on waiver of proof, and that denial of liability excused proof of death. However, waiver of proof requirements did not waive the policy’s time limit for bringing suit. Because the beneficiary failed to sue for death benefits within the contractual period, that claim was barred. The judgment for plaintiff was reversed, with a new trial granted only on the weekly disability indemnity claim.

Austria's Financial Market Authority raised its forecast for proceeds from Heta Asset Resolution's asset sales to 8.6 billion euros from 6.0 billion, citing better-than-expected results. The increase benefits Austria and Carinthia, now Heta's largest creditor. The FMA expects an initial payment of around 4 billion euros to creditors over the summer.

Three police ranks and a former corporal testified in the preliminary inquiry into the alleged robbery-murders of Phyllis Caesar and Constance Fraser, found bound and gagged in their South Road home in October 2017. Imran Khan, Steven Andrews, and Phillip Suffrien are charged. The inquiry continues Monday before Principal Magistrate Judy Latchman.

The passage proposes a DNN-Transformer-Autoencoder hybrid deep learning framework for corporate tax risk supervision and risk level assessment. The model addresses limitations of manual and rule-based tax supervision by combining static enterprise attributes, temporal financial and taxation records, and anomaly detection signals. Its DNN module models static features such as firm size, industry, registration information, capital, and ownership; the Transformer captures temporal dependencies in financial and tax time-series data; and the Autoencoder detects anomalous patterns through reconstruction error. Fused representations are used to classify enterprises into low-, medium-, or high-risk levels.

Experiments use real corporate tax declarations and financial records from about 12,000 enterprises across industries including manufacturing, retail, and internet services. Features include static attributes, quarterly financial indicators, tax behavior, and expert-assigned risk labels. Compared with logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and DNN-LSTM, the proposed model achieves the best test performance, with 0.91 accuracy, 0.86 recall, and 0.88 F1-score. Training and validation losses converge around 40 epochs, indicating stable convergence and generalization.

The study concludes that the hybrid framework improves detection of complex and hidden tax risk patterns, supports risk stratification and regulatory resource allocation, but is limited by feature scope and computational complexity.

The passage presents a theoretical study of orbital degrees of freedom in magnon–phonon coupled systems, focusing on magnon-polarons. It argues that bosonic quasiparticle orbital angular moment can arise from global lattice rotation and from the quantum geometry of Bloch wavefunctions, with the latter remaining finite even when lattice orbital motion vanishes. Using a two-dimensional honeycomb antiferromagnet with Néel order as an example, the study shows that magnetoelastic coupling breaks relevant symmetries, enables intra-band and inter-band orbital angular moment transfer between magnons and phonons, and allows out-of-plane phonon modes to acquire finite out-of-plane orbital angular moment through hybridization.

The work proposes that magnon-polaron orbital angular moment can be detected through electric polarization and a transverse voltage generated under a temperature or strain gradient. In the modeled MnPS3-based system, magnon–phonon coupling strongly enhances electric activity, making the orbital contribution dominant at low magnetic fields and increasing the response with temperature and coupling strength. The authors conclude that quantum geometry provides a universal origin for orbital degrees of freedom in periodic bosonic and fermionic systems, and that magnon–phonon coupling offers a platform for electrical control of magnetization and phononic transport.

The passage describes SD Memory Card physical layer procedures and command behavior. CMD19 sends a fixed tuning block in 1.8V signaling transfer state to tune host sampling timing, with up to 40 executions completed by the card within 150 ms excluding host processing. During identification the host remains at fOD, then may switch to fPP in data transfer mode. CMD9 reads CSD, CMD4 optionally sets DSR, and CMD7 selects or deselects cards; only one card may be in Transfer State.

Data transfers are point-to-point with the selected card. Read and write commands can be aborted with CMD12. Write operations may enter Programming State and indicate busy by holding DAT0 low; some operations allow buffering, but CSD write, write protection, and erase do not. CMD0 or CMD15 can terminate programming and may destroy data. ACMD6 changes bus width only when the card is unlocked.

The passage defines read and write behavior, including block-oriented transfer, CRC protection, block length limits, partial and misaligned access handling, and error reporting such as BLOCK_LEN_ERROR, ADDRESS_ERROR, WP_VIOLATION, and CRC failure. Multiple block write is preferred for faster operation, and ACMD23 may set a pre-erased block count before CMD25. ACMD22 reports the number of well-written blocks after some multiple-write errors.

Erase operations use CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38. DISCARD and Full User Area Logical Erase (FULE) are CMD38 variants supported only for SDHC and SDXC, not SPI; hosts must check support bits before issuing them. DISCARD treats contents as “don’t care,” while FULE logically erases the full user area. Busy indication uses DAT0, with specified timeouts.

Three write-protection methods are described: mechanical switch, optional internal write protection, and password-based card lock. CMD42 manages password lock/unlock, password setting and clearing, Force Erase, and Card Ownership Protection (COP). COP adds Force Erase Password (FEP), COP Unlock, FEP management, and FEP Force Erase. Locked cards accept only specified basic and lock-related commands; ACMD6 is rejected while locked.

APP_CMD (CMD55) causes the next command to be interpreted as an application-specific command if defined and legal. CMD6 switches or queries functions including access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. It returns a 512-bit status block and supports Mode 0 checking and Mode 1 switching. High-Speed mode is optional and entered via CMD6. CMD8 checks interface voltage during initialization for version 2.00 or later cards.

The passage also covers capacity-type differences: SDSC uses byte addressing and CMD16 block lengths, while SDHC and SDXC use 512-byte block addressing and fixed 512-byte memory access blocks. Hosts may change or stop the bus clock under restrictions and must provide eight clock cycles after transactions before shutdown. CRC7 protects commands, responses, CID, and CSD; CRC16 protects data blocks. Commands with CRC errors or illegal commands are not executed and set status errors. Read and write timeout behavior is defined, including 100 ms read timeout guidance and 250 ms write busy limits for high-capacity cards.

The IMF advised Saudi Arabia to implement reforms and price hikes gradually to avoid harming growth, despite praising its efforts to boost non-oil revenue and cut spending after the oil price crash. Saudi Arabia has recorded large deficits and expects a 2017 deficit of nine percent of GDP, down from 17.2 percent in 2016. Its economy contracted in the first two quarters, with IMF projecting 0.1 percent growth this year. Under Vision 2030 and the Fiscal Balance Programme, Riyadh seeks budget balance by 2019, but the IMF recommended targeting 2022. Measures include higher excise taxes, energy and water prices, expatriate labour fees, planned fuel and electricity hikes, and a five-percent VAT next year.

Value area trading uses volume profile to identify the price range where 70% of trading volume occurred during a given period. Traders use these areas as potential support, resistance, buying, selling, stop-loss, and profit target levels. It is common in futures but can be applied to stocks and forex, across intraday, daily, weekly, or monthly charts. Signals may come from breakouts, reversals, pullbacks, candlestick patterns, or momentum divergences. Risks include false signals, changing value areas, outdated information, and relying on value area alone. Risk management includes stop-loss orders, position sizing, diversification, and discipline. The passage states that backtesting this strategy is difficult and no backtest is provided.

Astronomers and citizen scientists plan extensive observations during next Monday’s U.S. solar eclipse, using ground instruments, the International Space Station, 11 satellites, three planes and more than 70 high-altitude balloons. The moon’s shadow will cross from Oregon to South Carolina, while NASA and the National Science Foundation spend about $7.7 million on eclipse projects. Researchers will study the sun’s corona, space weather, Earth’s weather, and animal and plant behavior. Citizen projects include balloon footage, the Citizen CATE telescope network, iNaturalist observations, zoo monitoring and Berkeley’s Eclipse Megamovie. Scientists say eclipses uniquely reveal the sun’s corona, whose extreme heat and magnetic activity remain key mysteries. Past eclipses aided discoveries including helium’s spectrum and evidence supporting Einstein’s general theory of relativity.

The study investigates equilibrium vacancy concentrations in a nine-component refractory multi-principal element alloy containing group 4, 5, and 6 elements. It develops a canonical-ensemble thermodynamic formalism, extending prior coarse-graining methods, to compute dilute vacancy concentrations and local elemental environments around vacancies from Monte Carlo simulations.

First-principles density functional theory calculations are used to train an embedded cluster expansion model for ordering energetics of refractory elements and vacancies on the body-centered cubic lattice. The model achieves about 8 meV/site accuracy and reproduces binary alloy convex hulls and solute-vacancy energetics.

Finite-temperature Monte Carlo simulations show that alloys containing group 4 elements have vacancy concentrations 10–100 times higher than alloys composed only of group 5 and 6 elements. In HfMoNbTiZr, vacancies are enriched in Zr and Hf in the first-neighbor shell and Mo in the second-neighbor shell. The results also show that short-range order and bonding energetics strongly influence vacancy formation: strong favorable bonds reduce vacancy concentrations, while unfavorable bonding increases them.

The study finds that increasing group 4 element content lowers vacancy formation free energies and can raise vacancy concentrations to levels relevant for mass transport, though excessive group 4 content may affect phase stability. Comparisons with special quasi-random structure-based vacancy formation density-of-states methods show that single-configuration approximations can underestimate vacancy concentrations when short-range order is significant.

The work provides a first-principles statistical-mechanics framework for identifying multicomponent alloy chemistries with targeted vacancy concentrations.

The passage lists The 74 headlines, led by a report that the superintendent of Iowa’s largest school district was arrested by ICE, alongside education and youth-related stories on school integration, supplies, COVID vaccines, college access, STEM, and student achievements.

In Waterhouse v. Gibson, the court held that a conveyance by execution levy is construed like a conveyance by deed. When land is set off under execution without any written exception, buildings standing on it pass with the land, whether or not they have foundations sunk into the ground. Parol evidence was inadmissible to show that the buildings were excluded from the appraisal or reserved for the debtor. The court affirmed judgment for the plaintiff for the value of the removed barn and blacksmith’s shop.

A Danish study found children born to mothers with rheumatoid arthritis had higher risks of developing rheumatoid arthritis, thyroid disease and epilepsy. Researchers analyzed 25 years of data and said doctors should pay special attention to these conditions in children exposed to rheumatoid arthritis in utero.

A University of Maryland study of 1,099 young adults found that those who consumed energy drinks from ages 21 to 24, especially persistently, were more likely to later use cocaine or prescription stimulants non-medically. Researchers said the link requires further investigation.

Microsoft filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2020. For the three months ended March 31, 2020, revenue was $35.0 billion, up from $30.6 billion in 2019; operating income was $13.0 billion; net income was $10.8 billion; and diluted earnings per share were $1.40. For the nine months ended March 31, 2020, revenue was $105.0 billion, operating income was $39.6 billion, net income was $33.1 billion, and diluted EPS was $4.30.

As of March 31, 2020, Microsoft had $137.6 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments; total assets of $285.4 billion; total liabilities of $170.9 billion; and stockholders’ equity of $114.5 billion. Net cash from operations was $17.5 billion for the quarter and $42.0 billion for the nine-month period.

Segment revenue for the quarter was $11.7 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $12.3 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $11.0 billion for More Personal Computing. Commercial cloud revenue was $13.3 billion for the quarter and $37.4 billion for the nine months.

Microsoft stated that COVID-19 had minimal net impact on third-quarter revenue, increasing cloud usage and demand for remote work and learning products while reducing transactional licensing, LinkedIn advertising spend, and search advertising. The company reported ongoing legal matters, $304 million in accrued legal liabilities, and a $40.0 billion share repurchase program with $36.8 billion remaining as of March 31, 2020.

The passage describes video encoding and decoding techniques involving intra prediction and non-separable transforms. It explains video compression concepts, intra and inter prediction, directional intra modes, non-directional smooth modes, recursive filtering modes, chroma-from-luma prediction, multi-line intra prediction, and encoder/decoder architectures.

The disclosed methods encode or decode coding information for a block, determine a directional intra prediction mode using a nominal mode and angular offset, select a non-separable transform based on the nominal mode, and reconstruct the block using the directional mode and transform. The non-separable transform may be a secondary transform such as LFNST, selected from a transform set using a transform index, and may be limited to specific coefficients or disabled for certain modes.

The disclosure also covers applying non-separable transforms to non-directional modes, including DC, PAETH, SMOOTH, SMOOTH_V, SMOOTH_H, recursive filtering modes, and CfL, with transform sets associated among these modes or nominal directional modes. It further describes related systems, communication environments, encoder and decoder components, transform coding processes, line graph transforms, and computer-readable media storing instructions for performing the methods.

The speaker recalls Detroit as his first team, with strong memories including two semifinal runs and being treated well by the city. He describes his trade to Washington as initially exciting but difficult, says the team improved after changes, and expects returning to Detroit to feel special.

Azerbaijan aims to increase exports of honey and beekeeping products, Agriculture Minister Heydar Asadov said. He noted growing global demand, Azerbaijan’s organic honey advantage, and interest from markets such as China and Japan. The ministry has developed proposals to boost state support for beekeeping, to be submitted to the president and government.

The study examines Hungarian higher education lecturers’ characteristics, employment patterns, regulations, career structures, earnings, and future supply through doctoral students, using Hungarian and international statistical databases and documentary analysis of legislation.

After 1990, Hungary inherited a fragmented, low-capacity higher education system. Student numbers expanded strongly until the mid-2000s, supported by policy goals to approach developed democratic societies’ participation rates. Later, demographic decline, admissions policies, tuition and cost-reimbursement rules, the Bologna two-cycle system, and post-2010 restrictions shaped enrolment. Since 2010, reduced state support, higher tuition for paying students, and stricter entry requirements contributed to lower participation and increased inequalities in access. Hungary’s share of young graduates remained below the EU 2020 target.

The employment environment changed through pluralism in institutional maintenance and later privatization. By 2023, most lecturers worked in foundation higher education, while public-sector employment declined sharply. The number of lecturers rose with student numbers until 2004, later diverged from enrolment trends, and increased again after 2015. The student-teacher ratio peaked in 2006 and fell by 2022. Hungarian lecturers are older than the OECD average but remain in the international middle range by age composition. The share of women lecturers has increased, though it remains below leading countries.

Academic qualification rules still reflect elements of the post-war Soviet-style system, especially the continued role of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences. Since 1993, universities have had the right to provide doctoral education and award PhDs. Legislation defines requirements for university professors, associate professors, assistant professors, and assistant lecturers, including doctoral degrees, habilitation, teaching and research performance, and later stronger international recognition and foreign-language publication expectations. Post-2010 reforms reduced institutional autonomy through the chancellor system, changes to accreditation, and the transfer of most state universities to public foundations governed by boards of trustees.

The structure of academic staff changed substantially. Since 2005, the total number of lecturers has broadly stagnated, while the number of university and college professors fell significantly. Possible contributing factors include retirement, reduced funding, and stricter appointment requirements. Public-sector academic salaries remained low, while privatized “model-changing” universities increased salaries but tied them to detailed performance evaluation systems.

Hungarian doctoral graduates entering higher education teaching and research face lower lifetime earnings than graduates working in the business sector. Earnings losses during doctoral study, modest starting salaries, and low early-career academic wages reduce the financial attractiveness of academic careers. International comparisons also show Hungary in a weak position regarding doctoral students per population, raising concerns about the future supply of educators and researchers.

The passage concludes that low incomes, career abandonment, emigration, institutional rigidity, lack of transparency, disadvantages for women and families, limited international access, infrastructure problems, and weak advocacy hinder Hungarian higher education and research. It argues that policymakers should reconsider educators’ position and address barriers to progress.

The Texas Education Agency is investigating hundreds of teachers’ social media comments about Charlie Kirk’s killing, after Commissioner Mike Morath called some posts “reprehensible and inappropriate” and said they could be referred for possible license suspension. Gov. Greg Abbott supported the move, accusing some teachers of calling for or inciting violence.

Legal experts and public education advocates say the investigations may violate teachers’ free speech rights, especially when educators speak in a personal capacity on matters of public concern. They argue disciplinary action would require showing that comments caused significant workplace disruption or impaired job performance. Advocates also warned that political pressure could chill public employees’ speech.

The agency did not answer questions about how it would account for First Amendment protections. Texas AFT President Zeph Capo described the response as a politically driven “witch hunt” and said firing teachers over disagreeable comments should not be the response.

Marc Ó Sé said an injury-free James O'Donoghue could be a huge boost for Kerry after scoring nine points against Clare. He believes O'Donoghue will improve with games, regain confidence, and form a dangerous attacking threat alongside Paul Geaney if he stays fit.

The passage explains that bond trading strategies can diversify a portfolio because bonds often have low correlation with stocks. It focuses on Treasury bonds, defining bonds as loans from investors to issuers in exchange for scheduled interest and principal repayment at maturity. Bond strategies vary by time horizon, risk tolerance, market conditions, and objectives such as income, preservation, or appreciation. Common risks and mistakes include interest rate risk, credit and liquidity risks, poor diversification, overreliance on historical data, weak risk management, and emotional decision-making.

The article presents several backtested TLT Treasury bond strategies, including seasonal, swing trade, and intermarket approaches, and argues that combining bond strategies with S&P 500 strategies improved returns and reduced drawdowns. It emphasizes that bond prices generally fall when interest rates rise and rise when rates fall. Day trading bonds is described as more challenging than stocks due to lower volatility and sensitivity to interest rates, economic data, and central bank policy. Bond strategies can be automated using predefined algorithmic criteria, though human oversight remains important. For beginners, dollar-cost averaging is suggested.

Enron was reported to be in advanced talks to sell Portland General Electric to Northwest Natural Gas for about $1.8 billion in cash and stock, with Northwest assuming roughly $1 billion in debt; NW Natural confirmed discussions but said no agreement was assured. Reports also covered Enron’s planned European job cuts of up to 500 positions, BG Group’s potentially jeopardized $388 million purchase of Enron’s Indian upstream assets over operatorship issues, and Tata Power’s possible bid for Enron’s stake in Dabhol Power, while BSES said it would not buy the stake.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that Frank H. Brod will retire as Chief Accounting Officer, stepping down July 31, 2020 and remaining through September 30, 2020 for transition. Alice L. Jolla, 54, Microsoft’s Corporate Controller since 2014, will become Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer effective July 31, 2020. She will receive a $1.5 million stock award under the 2017 Stock Plan, vesting quarterly.

Bitcoin fell below US$8,000 for the first time since November before recovering, continuing a steep decline from its December record. Concerns include global regulatory threats, the Coincheck heist, manipulation fears and Facebook’s crypto ad ban. Rival cryptocurrencies also dropped, while analysts cited weakening investor appetite and potential crackdowns.

The Business Insider Scottish Accountancy & Finance Awards recognise accountants’ contributions to private and public sector organisations. The 2018 event includes a reception, dinner, entertainment by DNA, and an awards ceremony presented by Sarah Heaney. Categories include accountancy firms, finance directors, young accountant, tax team, and corporate finance team. Tickets are available for tables or individuals, including reception, dinner, wine, programme, and entertainment.

Best Hope Services plans to launch Nigeria’s first online trade exhibition in May to showcase local innovations and products without physical venues. CEO Olu Adenodi said the platform will help exhibitors and visitors participate remotely. Prof. Joseph Mba said the e-fair will support national development and cover expo, connect, trade and events sections.

President Trump criticized ABC for not apologizing to him for “HORRIBLE statements” after the network canceled Roseanne Barr’s show over her racist tweet about Valerie Jarrett. ABC CEO Bob Iger called Jarrett to apologize and said the network had zero tolerance for such comments. Democratic lawmakers criticized Trump’s response, while Jarrett said the incident should be a teaching moment and that “the tone does start at the top.”

Microsoft is reportedly developing Polaris, a stripped-down version of Windows 10 built on the modular Windows Core OS. Designed for desktops, laptops and 2-in-1 devices, Polaris would run UWP apps from the Microsoft Store instead of traditional desktop applications. It is expected to use CShell, a new interface intended to make Windows lighter, faster and more adaptable across devices while removing legacy components. Unlike Windows 10 S, users would not be able to upgrade Polaris to Windows 10 Pro. Microsoft is reportedly exploring remote virtualization to support legacy applications. Windows Central suggests Polaris could arrive in 2019.

Researchers studied how polypropylene’s molecular regularity, or isotacticity, and cooling history affect its mechanical properties. Polypropylene chains with more isotactic segments form more crystallites, making the material harder and stronger. The team tested films with varying isotacticity, prepared by rapid quenching or slow cooling, and measured their behavior under stretching. They found that mechanical properties depend on both isotacticity and thermal treatment, with crystallinity and crystallite form influencing elastic modulus. The findings could help synthesize polypropylene with predetermined properties such as elasticity or hardness.

The passage states that China and the United States share interests in peace, trade, modernization, and concern over Soviet military buildup, though they disagree on Taiwan. It outlines five principles for a Reagan-Bush Administration: maintaining important strategic relations with China; promoting peace, stability, and economic growth in the Western Pacific with regional partners; cooperating against aggression or hegemony; and developing U.S. relations with Taiwan under the Taiwan Relations Act. The speaker criticizes Jimmy Carter’s normalization concessions to China and argues that Congress strengthened safeguards for Taiwan. The Taiwan Relations Act is described as the legal basis for U.S.-Taiwan relations, supporting peaceful resolution of Taiwan’s future, defensive arms sales, and U.S. capacity to resist coercion threatening Taiwan’s security or system. It also establishes procedures for conducting relations through the American Institute in Taiwan with congressional funding and oversight.

The JACL Kakehashi Program will select up to 200 Japanese American or Asian American students and young professionals ages 18–25 for nine-day trips to Japan to promote U.S.-Japan relations. Trips run Dec. 13–20 and March 12–20, 2018, with application deadlines Oct. 9 and Jan. 2. Japanese nationals/passport holders are ineligible.

Wal-Mart’s reported bid for online clothing retailer Bonobos is part of its effort to expand in online fashion, attract younger customers, and compete with Amazon. The deal would be its fourth small online clothing-and-accessories acquisition in 2017, following ShoeBuy, Moosejaw, and ModCloth. The strategy is led by Marc Lore, who took over Wal-Mart’s e-commerce after the $3.3 billion Jet.com acquisition. Although Wal-Mart is the largest brick-and-mortar clothing retailer, its online sales remain about 3 percent of total sales, and it has struggled to attract affluent online shoppers and apparel brands. Analysts said the acquisitions could help build fashion brands, but some questioned their impact and past success. Wal-Mart continues to lag Amazon, which leads the U.S. online clothing and footwear market.

Intel released Coffee Lake 14nm desktop processors and Z370 chipsets, with motherboard vendors launching Z370 boards globally. More Coffee Lake CPUs and chipsets are planned through 2018, alongside Gemini Lake, Coffee Lake notebook and vPro processors. Cannon Lake 10nm processors are expected in mid-2018, while Ice Lake is slated for 2019.

The passage introduces molecular augmented dynamics (MAD), an O(N) modified molecular dynamics method for generating low-energy, ab-initio accurate atomistic structures of disordered materials that match experimental data. Existing Monte Carlo, molecular dynamics, reverse Monte Carlo, and hybrid reverse Monte Carlo approaches can struggle with experimental agreement, computational efficiency, scaling, physical accuracy, or the need for material-specific constraints. Prior MD-based attempts to incorporate experimental potentials suffered from poor scaling, inaccurate gradients, and inadequate treatment of thermal effects.

MAD uses a Hamiltonian combining kinetic energy, an interatomic potential, and an experimental potential that measures disagreement between predicted and experimental observables. This enables multi-objective optimization of physical plausibility and experimental agreement. The article derives general MAD equations and analytic, linearly scaling experimental forces for XRD, ND, PDF, and XPS observables, including thermal broadening. It also notes that descriptor-based observables with local, position-differentiable descriptors can be incorporated with linear scaling, and reports implementation and scaling details in TurboGAP.

This “Tips of the Week” entry shares several maker tips: adding rare earth magnets to tester wires for easier hookups, using an old motor as a rotating display turntable, attaching a hobby knife to a compass for circle cutting, marking untrue material edges with a squiggly line, turning a drill press into a makeshift drum sander, and using an inexpensive Ikea flexi-neck LED lamp for directed workbench lighting.

The “Drive & Kick” offense is a three-player weave from a 3-2 spread, using dribble penetration for layups or kick-out passes when defenders stop the drive. Players pass outside, replace receivers, and continue the action. Options include corner kick-outs against zone help and drop passes to back-cutting corner players.

On May 30, 1976, Kent Howerton won the AMA 500cc National Motocross opener at Moto-Masters, with Bob Hannah second and Tony DiStefano third. In 1982, Ricky Johnson won the High Point 250 National, while Darrell Shultz won the 500 Class. The passage also notes Toronto Supercross results, Yamaha budget cuts, rider concerns over the Trans-USA Championship, and Ross Pederson’s 1987 Montreal Supercross win.

The Housing Authority of the City of Santa Barbara received a Gold Nugget Award for Best Affordable Project for Bradley Studios, a 54-unit development built in 2012 for low- and extremely low-income residents with special needs. Developed with McGillivray Construction and Peikert Group Architects, the infill project replaced blighted buildings and features California Craftsman-style design, connected structures, community spaces, and social service offices offering mental health, addiction, job training, and life skills support.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture, as an 8th-generation data center GPU for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads. A100 builds on Tesla V100 with third-generation Tensor Cores, support for TF32, BF16, FP64, FP16, INT8, INT4, and binary formats, and fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity that can double Tensor Core throughput. It provides 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, larger L1/shared memory, Compute Data Compression, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, and CUDA 11 support.

A100 includes Multi-Instance GPU capability, allowing one GPU to be partitioned into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory bandwidth, and fault isolation, benefiting multi-tenant cloud and virtualized environments. It also supports Compute Instances for simultaneous context execution and Volta-style MPS.

The GPU uses third-generation NVLink, offering 12 links and 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, plus PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV. It adds improved error and fault detection, NVJPG decode, optical flow acceleration, stronger atomic performance, and five NVDEC units.

The passage also describes DGX A100, a system with eight A100 GPUs connected through NVLink and NVSwitch, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and up to 56 isolated GPU instances through MIG. DGX A100 supports large-scale AI infrastructure using Mellanox InfiniBand, Magnum IO, NGC software, Slurm, Kubernetes, and DeepOps.

Acting CDC director Jim O’Neill called for replacing the combined MMR vaccine with separate measles, mumps, and rubella shots, echoing President Trump, though the passage says no evidence supports safety or effectiveness benefits. Experts say separating the shots could reduce vaccine completion, leave children more vulnerable, and is currently infeasible because monovalent vaccines are unavailable in the U.S. The article notes the MMR vaccine has been used for over half a century, is highly effective, and has minimal side-effect risks, while rhetoric from officials could lower vaccination rates.

The study used spatial transcriptomics, single-cell spatial imaging, and quantitative immunohistochemistry to characterize IDO1- and PD-L1-expressing myeloid cell niches in lesion biopsies from Sri Lankan cutaneous leishmaniasis patients and other dermal leishmaniasis cases from Brazil and India. In Sri Lankan lesions, CD274 and IDO1 localized to myeloid-rich regions in the papillary dermis and deeper T cell-rich areas. Mature dendritic cells and CCL18+ macrophages were major IDO1/PD-L1-expressing populations.

Neighbourhood analysis showed that IDO1+ and CD274+ myeloid cells were commonly near CD8+ memory T cells, regulatory T cells, and CCL18+ macrophages. IL32 was highly expressed by CD8+ memory T cells and Tregs, while CXCL9 and CCL18 were mainly expressed by myeloid cells. IL32 and CXCL9 were also associated with IDO1/CD274-rich spots in Brazilian L. braziliensis CL and Indian L. donovani PKDL lesions. Across disease forms, five genes—IL32, LYZ, GBP1, IFI30, and FTH1—were common correlates of IDO1 and CD274 expression.

In Sri Lankan patients treated with sodium stibogluconate, high dermal IL-32 abundance was associated with slower cure. Patients with low CD8+IL-32+ cell abundance were significantly more likely to cure earlier, while FoxP3+IL-32+ abundance did not show a significant association. The authors identify IL-32+ CD8+ T cells as a prognostic marker for rate of cure and propose that IL-32 contributes to IDO1/PD-L1 immunoregulatory niches in dermal leishmaniasis.

MSPM0C1105/6 MCUs are ultra-low-power 32-bit Arm Cortex-M0+ devices operating up to 32MHz, with supply voltage from 1.62V to 3.6V and temperature range from -40°C to 125°C. They include up to 64KB flash, 8KB SRAM, a high-speed on-chip oscillator, DMA, CRC-16, ADC, comparator, temperature sensor, timers, watchdogs, UART, SPI, and I2C peripherals supporting protocols such as LIN, IrDA, DALI, SMBus, and PMBus.

The devices support RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN operating modes across two power domains.
