The findings may support calls for tighter neonicotinoid restrictions in the EU, while pesticide companies and some farmers argue restrictions have reduced canola yields and increased use of other pesticides.

The passage describes NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture features and related DGX A100 system capabilities. A100 includes 40 GB HBM2 memory using five active stacks and delivers 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, more than 1.7x Tesla V100. Its memory subsystem, L2 cache, L1 caches, and register files support SECDED ECC. The GPU has a 40 MB L2 cache, 6.7x larger than V100, with two partitions, 2.3x higher L2 bandwidth, residency controls, and Compute Data Compression that can improve DRAM and L2 bandwidth and L2 capacity.

A100 uses NVIDIA Ampere architecture with more SMs than V100 and third-generation Tensor Cores. It improves Tensor Core utilization through wider thread data sharing, fewer instructions and register accesses, asynchronous copy from global memory to shared memory, asynchronous barriers, larger shared memory allocation, higher HBM2 and L2 bandwidth, and improved cache management. CUDA 11 supports features including Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, L2 cache residency controls, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, and Cooperative Groups enhancements.

The Multi-Instance GPU feature can partition one A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances, each with isolated compute and memory resources including SMs, L2 cache slices, memory controllers, and DRAM paths. MIG is intended to improve utilization, quality of service, fault isolation, and multi-tenant or multi-user operation. GPU Instances are built from GPU slices, and Compute Instances allow further partitioning and simultaneous context execution.

A100 includes third-generation NVLink with twelve links and 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 with 31.5 GB/sec per direction for x16 connections, and SR-IOV support. The architecture adds fault detection, attribution, isolation, containment, and recovery features. Other features include hardware JPEG decode through NVJPG, optical flow and stereo disparity acceleration, improved atomic throughput, and five NVDEC units.

DGX A100 uses eight A100 GPUs connected through third-generation NVLink and NVSwitch, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and up to 56 isolated GPU Instances using MIG. Its software stack includes CUDA, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC Private Registry, and GPU-accelerated containers for deep learning, inference, data analytics, and HPC. The passage also explains sparse neural networks, pruning, fine-grained and coarse-grained sparsity, and A100’s fine-grained structured sparsity support.

The passage argues that Swarthmore students often take academics, internships, and self-presentation very seriously, but should accept mistakes and laugh at themselves. It emphasizes that errors such as poor grades, embarrassment, or being wrong are not life-altering and can be learning experiences. The author describes Swarthmore as intense and unusual, encouraging students to step back, find humor, and give themselves breaks. The passage also urges students to extend this forgiveness to others, assume good intent when peers misspeak, and seek clarification before reacting. Laughter is presented as an imperfect but helpful way to handle discomfort.

San Diego County confirmed its first West Nile virus case of the year in a Spring Valley woman. Officials warned symptoms can appear two to 14 days after mosquito bites. California has reported 231 illnesses and 12 deaths this year. Residents are urged to prevent mosquito bites and remove standing water.

Asian equities were cautious after the US Federal Reserve raised rates by 25 basis points and detailed plans to unwind its balance sheet. The Nikkei, Kospi, ASX 200 and Hang Seng fell, while mainland China indexes edged higher. Markets viewed the move as dovish and doubted the Fed’s projection of three hikes this year. Toshiba shares declined amid Western Digital legal action and reports it may miss its financial statement deadline. Oil prices hovered near seven-month lows after a build in US gasoline stocks. The dollar index stayed below 97, while the Australian dollar rose on stronger jobs data and the New Zealand dollar fell after weaker GDP figures. Upcoming events included data from Australia and China, the Bank of Japan meeting, and the Bank of England rate decision. Wall Street closed mixed after the Fed announcement.

The lecture discusses updates to problem set 8, noting that problem 8.2 may require more background and problem 8.3 should be deferred unless the BCJR algorithm is covered. It then completes Chapter 11 by presenting Hadamard transform realizations of Reed-Muller codes over F2. The Hadamard transform is defined using the universal matrix Um, an m-fold tensor product of a 2 by 2 self-inverse matrix, so the transform is its own inverse.

Reed-Muller codes are described as generated by selected rows of Um according to row weight, with examples including the 8,1,8 repetition code, the 8,4,4 code, and the 8,7,2 single parity-check code. The lecture explains how graphical realizations of Hadamard transforms can be built recursively from simple binary constraint nodes resembling controlled NOT gates. These realizations use binary internal variables and simple equality and zero-sum constraints but contain cycles.

For the 8,4,4 code, fixing some input variables to zero and leaving others free gives a reduced Hadamard transform realization. This graph is simple but cyclic. By agglomerating parts of the graph, a cycle-free realization equivalent to a two-section trellis is obtained, though with higher state and branch complexity. The lecture emphasizes the trade-off between simple cyclic graphs and more complex cycle-free graphs, and briefly relates this to general Reed-Muller and Golay code realizations.

The lecture then closes Chapter 11 and notes related graphical model styles, including factor graphs, Markov graphs, and Bayesian networks. Chapter 12 begins with the sum-product algorithm for decoding codes on graphs. The algorithm is introduced as a method for a posteriori probability decoding, first on cycle-free graphs, where it gives exact results in finite time, including the BCJR algorithm for trellises. On graphs with cycles it becomes iterative and approximate.

A posteriori probability decoding is defined as computing probability vectors for each external and internal variable given the received sequence. The lecture derives that these probabilities can be expressed as sums of products using Bayes’ law and memoryless channel assumptions, separating intrinsic information from extrinsic information. It introduces the past-future decomposition for cycle-free graphs, where cutting an internal edge separates the graph into independent past and future parts conditioned on the state variable. The lecture ends before completing the sum-product algorithm.

The passage introduces the Situation Calculus as a logical framework for modeling dynamic systems and discusses Reiter’s successor state axioms as a solution to the frame problem under the Markov property. It then describes extensions to non-Markovian domains, where action preconditions and effects may depend on past situations, and highlights applications such as database transactions, planning, and smart contracts. The paper’s aim is to use a Situation Calculus account of obligations to formalize a taxonomy of obligation types using non-Markovian theories. It outlines the sequential and temporal Situation Calculus, basic action theories, non-Markovian control, and a running door-opening example with actions, fluents, precondition axioms, and successor state axioms. It also summarizes an embedding of deontic obligation into Situation Calculus using a fluent O(s′, s), where Oblg(ϕ, s) means that ϕ holds in all deontically accessible situations from s.

This medRxiv preprint investigates brain ageing and multiple sclerosis-specific neurodegeneration using MRI and deep learning. The authors proposed a brain-predicted disease duration gap (DD gap) as a quantitative biomarker of multiple sclerosis-related brain structural damage, comparing it with the established brain-age gap (BAG) and an alternative multiple sclerosis-specific age model (MS-age gap).

The retrospective multicentre study included 4,392 patients for age and disease-duration modelling, plus an external longitudinal early multiple sclerosis cohort of 252 patients with 749 sessions and a mean follow-up of 4.5 years. Models used 3D T1-weighted MRI scans, with FLAIR scans used for lesion segmentation. BAG was estimated using the DeepBrainNet model, while disease duration and MS-age were modelled using an in-house deep learning architecture.

Patients with multiple sclerosis showed older-appearing brains, with a mean BAG of 7.81 years. The DD prediction model performed above chance level, with mean absolute error of 5.63 years and R² of 0.34, outperforming associations between disease duration and total lesion or thalamic volumes. DD gap and BAG were largely independent, while MS-age gap correlated more strongly with BAG. Interpretability analyses indicated that predictions were influenced by distributed brain volume changes and, for disease-specific models, by lesions.

Both BAG and DD gap were positively associated with physical disability measured by EDSS, and DD gap added explanatory value beyond BAG. In longitudinal analysis, annualised EDSS worsening correlated with increases in both BAG and DD gap, and DD gap again added explanatory value beyond BAG. MS-age gap did not significantly improve models of disability or progression.

The authors conclude that DD gap is a clinically meaningful MRI-derived measure of multiple sclerosis-specific brain damage and progression that complements healthy brain-age models. They note limitations including noise in estimating disease duration, potential treatment-related biases, and the need for further validation in broader clinical populations.

Five years after archaeologists confirmed that remains found beneath a Leicester car park were Richard III’s, the discovery had lasting effects on several people. Dominic Smee, who has the same type of scoliosis as Richard III, helped research how the king may have fought in armour and gained confidence through a documentary. Michael Ibsen, a descendant of Richard III’s sister, provided DNA that helped confirm the remains and briefly experienced public attention. Car park attendant Mike Mistry witnessed the dig, had painted the “R” marking the reserved space above the grave, and later missed meeting visitors after being made redundant. Musician Ian Churchward was inspired by the discovery to create several Richard III-themed folk-rock albums with his band, The Legendary Ten Seconds.

Fox News Halftime Report discusses California’s declining party affiliation, arguing that weaker parties and nonpartisan primaries may increase factionalism rather than reduce extremism. It cites polling showing Ted Cruz leading Beto O’Rourke in Texas, Democrats ahead in House preference, and Trump’s approval underwater. Other items cover Trump continuing claims about FBI spying despite Trey Gowdy’s comments, reports that Trump pressured Jeff Sessions over recusal, campaign ad trends on immigration and health care, donor fundraising, and Phoenix Mayor Greg Stanton resigning to run for Congress. The newsletter also includes commentary on political correctness, historical notes on Andrew Jackson’s duel, and a story about Long Island Rail Road passengers singing “Piano Man.”

Junior County, a top-five shooting guard in the 2026 class, committed to UConn after visiting campus and meeting with coach Dan Hurley. The 6-foot-4 Wasatch Academy guard is ranked No. 43 overall in the SC Next 100 and No. 4 at his position. He averaged 13.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.4 assists on the Nike EYBL circuit. County is UConn’s first 2026 commitment.

Beijing ordered 15 online real estate portals to remove misleading information, false advertising, feng shui content, financing advice, and claims of rising returns as part of efforts to cool the housing market. The move follows tighter mortgage rules, higher down payments for second homes, and a ban on buying third properties.

The TPS7H500x-SP family includes radiation-hardness-assured peak current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies such as buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. TPS7H5001-SP, TPS7H5002-SP, and TPS7H5003-SP support configurable maximum duty cycle through the DCL pin, while TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50% duty cycle with DCL tied to AVSS. A 100% duty cycle requires DCL connected to VLDO on compatible devices; 75% is selected by leaving DCL floating.

The CS_ILIM pin senses transformer primary-side current for PWM operation and overcurrent protection. The COMP voltage sets the peak current reference, and outputs turn off when sensed current reaches COMP/2. When CS_ILIM reaches 1.05 V nominal, the controller enters cycle-by-cycle current limiting and then hiccup mode if the overcurrent persists. The HICC capacitor sets both the delay before switching stops and the non-switching restart interval; a minimum 3.3 nF is recommended.

The FAULT pin enables external protections such as overcurrent or overvoltage protection. If FAULT exceeds 0.6 V for the specified minimum pulse width, switching stops and SS discharges. Once FAULT falls below 0.5 V, restart occurs after a delay of about 15 switching cycles plus internal logic delay.

Slope compensation is used to prevent subharmonic oscillation when duty cycle exceeds 50%. It is set with a resistor from RSC to AVSS, with the recommended slope compensation equal to the inductor falling current slope. The controllers use a transconductance error amplifier and support Type 2A or Type 2B compensation, with Type 2A adding a high-frequency capacitor for noise attenuation.

Thermal shutdown stops switching when junction temperature exceeds 175°C typical and restarts power-up when it falls below 160°C typical. The devices operate from a 4 V to 14 V input supply and require proper bypassing, including at least 0.1 µF from VIN to AVSS.

An example synchronous push-pull converter using TPS7H5001-SP and GaN devices targets 500 kHz switching, 5 V output, approximately 25 ns dead time, about 50 ns leading-edge blanking, a 33 nF soft-start capacitor, 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 0.47 µH output inductor, about 2.3 mF output capacitance, 7.5 Ω current-sense resistor, 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation, and 102 kΩ slope compensation resistor.

Layout guidance includes separating feedback and noise-sensitive traces from switching nodes and magnetics, minimizing high-current and high-dv/dt loop areas, separating analog and power grounds with a single connection point, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, filtering CS_ILIM if needed, routing SYNC away from sensitive pins, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS with multiple vias.

VentureWire’s November 14, 2000 issue reports venture financings, layoffs, acquisitions, executive changes, and fund news. Top stories include Apax merging its European and Israeli units and pledging $600 million for Israeli telecom, IT, and healthcare companies; New Edge Networks cutting 135 jobs; KSolutions raising a $50 million first round from Great Hill Equity Partners; and Cisco acquiring wireless chip firm Radiata for $295 million in stock.

New funding announcements include SmartEnergy raising $15 million, Cablesoft $11.5 million, Nitronex $9.5 million, E4X $6 million, PhotonEx $80 million, StorageApps $50 million, Blaze Network Products $40 million, Telespree $19 million, Circline $13.2 million, SupplyEdge $11 million, Equator over $40 million, Datasweep $30 million, ThinkFree $16 million, and Digital Creations $12 million.

Bad news items include several top executives leaving Divine InterVentures subsidiary Buzz MSP, eSociety shutting down, and iExplore cutting staff during a restructuring. Product and branding updates include Venture Studio launching EstimatesOnline, Wapmagic renaming itself AtoBe, Radix Wireless becoming BeamReach Networks, and NetEx becoming Certia.

M&A news includes Coventus’ acquisition agreement with easi Solutions lapsing, iKnowMed buying CancerSource.com, Streampipe.com acquiring 4ward Logic, and USBX acquiring BizQuest. The issue also reports new board appointments, CEO changes at several companies, Murphree Venture Partners’ first close of a new fund, personnel additions at Horizon Ventures and St. Paul Venture Capital, and corrections involving Patricof & Co. Ventures and TenantDirect.com.

Researchers led by OIST used fossil evidence and 17 rare horizontal gene transfers to refine the evolutionary timeline of fungi. Their analysis suggests living fungi share a common ancestor dating to about 1.4–0.9 billion years ago, hundreds of millions of years before land plants. The findings indicate fungi likely interacted with algae, recycled nutrients, broke down rock, and helped form primitive soils, preparing terrestrial environments for later plant colonization.

The passage argues that U.S. strategic superiority during the Cuban missile crisis helped prevent war, but that later policymakers underestimated Soviet ambitions and allowed the Soviet Union to gain military advantages. It criticizes the Carter Administration as weak and inconsistent in responding to Soviet actions in Cuba and Afghanistan, and contends that weakness encourages aggression. The passage calls for restoring U.S. military strength, maintaining a strong strategic deterrent, combating terrorism, consulting allies, strengthening alliances, and reaffirming American principles as the path to peace.

United Airlines highlighted its premium strategy, including keeping lounges from becoming overcrowded and expanding seatback entertainment to more than 146,000 seats across 765 planes. The remarks indirectly targeted Delta, which has faced Sky Club crowding, and American, which largely avoids seatback screens on domestic aircraft. United reported a 6% year-over-year rise in premium cabin revenue, while its stock fell after revenue missed analyst expectations despite stronger earnings.

An “Enron Mentions” email compiles news items from Oct. 19–20, 2001. The Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg report that Enron CFO Andrew Fastow’s LJM2 partnership made millions from transactions with Enron, raising conflict-of-interest concerns amid Enron’s $618 million quarterly loss, $1.01 billion write-off, and $1.2 billion shareholder equity reduction. TheStreet.com criticizes Enron’s complex accounting and LJM-related share repurchase. NewPower says it amended a netting agreement with Enron subsidiaries to reduce cash collateral requirements while seeking asset-backed financing. Other items note Enron’s lobbying payments to Quinn Gillespie, Ken Lay’s role in a Houston arena campaign, Enron Metals staff cuts in Europe, and a Bombay High Court hearing on Dabhol Power Company’s dispute with Maharashtra regulators.

China’s top official in Hong Kong, Zhang Xiaoming, warned that Beijing would not tolerate activities in the city that harm national sovereignty, challenge central authority or the Basic Law, or subvert mainland stability. His comments come amid tensions over pro-independence lawmakers, concerns about eroding freedoms, the bookseller disappearances, and fears of tighter Beijing control as Hong Kong prepares for a leadership change.

MusConv is an online software program for transferring playlists from Spotify to Amazon Music. Users select Spotify as the source, choose a playlist, set Amazon Music as the destination, and click “Transfer.” MusConv offers Basic, Professional, and Ultimate subscriptions with varying features including CSV export, updates, batch importing, and priority support.

The speaker said the team raised its level of play and did what was needed to win, while focusing on preparing for the next game Monday night. He described using a hoodie and headphones to clear his head and avoid distractions. He emphasized learning from past experiences, including the Chicago series, and said his motivation comes from himself, teammates, family, friends, love of the game, and the goal of winning the Stanley Cup. He praised teammates for key penalty kills, shot blocking, and limiting second and third chances.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated July 23, 2015, announcing its second quarter 2015 financial results. The filing includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and information on non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. The report was signed by CFO Brian T. Olsavsky.

The Competition and Markets Authority said some care homes may be breaking consumer law by charging vulnerable self-funding residents unfair fees, including billing after death, charging before admission, threatening eviction, failing to advertise prices, and making complaints difficult. The watchdog is considering new legislation and is bringing a test case on current protections. It said residents often struggle to understand care options and funding, while Citizens’ Advice warned of distress and financial pressure from gaps in consumer protection.

Caring Health Center in Springfield is participating in National Health Center Week alongside other state and national community health centers. The center serves more than 20,000 people, and CEO Tania Barber hopes to raise awareness of its services. Monday’s Elected Officials Day included representatives, community leaders, and healthcare honors.

In his farewell Oval Office address, the President thanks Americans and his administration, reviews achievements in the economy, education, welfare, crime, health insurance, poverty reduction, environmental protection, and global leadership. He urges continued fiscal responsibility, active U.S. leadership in an interconnected world, and national unity amid diversity. He wishes President-elect George W. Bush well and expresses hope and pride in continuing service as a citizen.

Ohio education regulators are reviewing a whistleblower’s claim that the now-closed Electronic Classroom of Tomorrow manipulated student attendance data using ActivTrak software to increase state funding. The former technology employee said school officials ordered staff to adjust data after the state sought repayment of $60 million for 2015-2016 overpayments. The Education Department had challenged ECOT’s use of the software, saying it duplicated learning hours, and will consider the claims in a new attendance review. ECOT representatives disputed or said they were unaware of the allegations. State auditors also reviewed the claims for an unreleased financial audit, while some officials and critics called for a criminal investigation.

Seven-year-old Joseph Nyberg started “Heart Cents” after his grandfather died of heart disease, collecting pennies and dollars to help St. Joseph’s heart patients. He placed collection buckets in Savannah and Richmond Hill and raised over $200. A heart patient’s family matched the donation, bringing it to $422, and another anonymous donation later raised the total to $672.14. The money will help patients with costs such as transportation and co-pays.

A valid device write requires at least 32 SCLKs within a data transfer frame. Device read protocols include legacy SPI-compatible single SDO-x, legacy SPI-compatible dual SDO-x, and source-synchronous protocols. After power-up or asynchronous reset, the device uses SPI-00-S for reads and writes. Other SPI-compatible protocols are selected by programming SDI_MODE[1:0], with read operation using SDO_MODE[1:0] = 00b. In SPI-compatible modes, RVS stays low during the frame. Dual SDO mode is enabled by setting SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] to 11b, making the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin function as SDO-1. Dual SDO launches two bits per SCLK edge and uses the same timing specifications as single SDO.

The paper examines blockchain education in U.S. AACSB-accredited universities, motivated by enterprise knowledge gaps in implementing and operating blockchain solutions. It argues that blockchain integration affects multiple enterprise functions, including management, finance, supply chain, IT, law, procurement, and sales, and requires technical, social, methodological, and personal competencies.

In March 2024, the authors reviewed 533 AACSB-accredited U.S. universities and found that 151, about 28%, offered at least one blockchain-related course, totaling 361 courses. Most blockchain courses were offered by Computer Science, Information Systems, Finance, Business and Strategy, and Law departments, though some appeared in fields such as Biology, Literature, and Political Science. Most courses were undergraduate-level. Public universities offered more blockchain courses in total, but a higher percentage of private universities offered at least one course. Larger universities were more likely to offer blockchain courses.

Course topics were categorized into fundamentals and overview, digital assets and cryptocurrencies, technical development, business implications, law and compliance, supply chain and governance, interplay with other technologies, and other topics. Fundamentals and overview was the largest category, followed by digital assets and cryptocurrencies and technical development. Courses also addressed emerging technologies connected to blockchain, especially AI and machine learning, the Internet of Things, and non-fungible tokens.

The study concludes that blockchain education is interdisciplinary and increasingly connected with other emerging technologies. It recommends future research on course topics, industry competency needs, alignment between disciplines and competencies, job-level requirements, and replication of the study in five years.

The disclosure describes noninvasive physiological monitoring devices and methods that combine optical sensor data from multiple patient measurement sites to generate a single measurement of physiological parameters. Sensors may be placed at sites such as the nose, earlobe, finger, hand, foot, or other cephalic or peripheral locations. Raw or minimally processed signals from the sensors are combined by one or more signal processors, optionally using a single algorithm, to measure parameters such as oxygen saturation, pulse rate, plethysmograph waveform, perfusion index, pleth variability index, methemoglobin, carboxyhemoglobin, total hemoglobin, glucose, and other patient characteristics.

The disclosure also describes optical sensors with multiple light emitters and multiple photodetectors arranged across a sensor area, including three-dimensional configurations conforming to patient anatomy. These configurations can provide varied light path lengths, topology information, sensor-position validation, and improved measurement robustness. The systems may independently process individual sensor signals, combine signals from multiple sites, compare measurements, or generate final measurements based on combined or weighted data.
In 2023, Katalin Karikó won the Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine.

The passage describes a surgical robotic component with an articulated terminal wrist portion for positioning a surgical instrument or end effector and sensing applied forces. The wrist includes distal, intermediate, and basal segments with roll and transverse articulations, including a universal or spherical joint arrangement. Torque sensors associated with wrist joints measure torque about multiple axes, allowing forces applied to the instrument or end effector from different directions to be resolved by a control processor and optionally used for haptic force feedback. The described robot arm uses sequences of revolute roll and pitch joints to provide mobility while remaining relatively slim and lightweight, supporting surgical access in constrained spaces and reducing kinematic singularities. The wrist may be located at the end of a robot arm or at the distal end of a surgical instrument, and may attach to instruments or end effectors such as grippers, shears, cameras, lasers, or knives. Torque sensors may use strain gauges, piezoelectric gauges, or magnetostrictive sensing, with wired or wireless communication to the control unit.

CoreLogic reported May year-over-year home price increases of 8.3% in Los Angeles County, 8.2% in Riverside and San Bernardino counties, and 6.2% in Orange County, with gains near multi-year highs despite slower sales. National prices rose 7.1% and California prices 8.9%. CoreLogic attributed rising prices to limited supply, especially entry-level homes, as many homeowners keep low-rate mortgages rather than sell.

Kesha tweeted support for Taylor Swift after former DJ David Mueller sued Swift, alleging she fabricated a groping claim that led to his firing. A judge dismissed Mueller’s lawsuit, while Swift’s $1 countersuit for assault and battery remained pending. Swift previously supported Kesha in 2016 by donating $250,000 during Kesha’s legal battle with Dr. Luke. Other stars, including Lena Dunham and Nelly Furtado, also supported Swift.

The passage explains that distributed systems rely on containers as foundational building blocks and argues for splitting even single-node applications into multiple containers. Containerization creates boundaries for resources, team ownership, and separation of concerns. Separate containers allow different resource priorities, prevent lower-priority components from affecting user-facing services, support reusable modules owned by small teams, and make applications easier to understand, test, update, deploy, and roll back. The book’s following chapters present patterns for modular groups of tightly dependent containers that can be co-scheduled on one machine and may share volumes, filesystems, network namespaces, or memory.

Mikel Obi said the Super Eagles will give their best in their June 2, 2018 friendly against England at Wembley, ahead of the World Cup. Nigeria will also play the Czech Republic before facing Croatia, Iceland and Argentina in Group D. England will face Tunisia, Panama and Belgium in Group G.

The Combo defense uses three aggressive outside pass denials and two inside zone defenders to counter spread offenses relying on dribble penetration. X1 protects the middle and forces sideline, while X2 and X3 deny passes. After passes or penetration, defenders rotate to deny returns, trap, support backside, and force difficult passes. If O4 and O5 are strong handlers and shooters, use a quarter-court 1-3-1 trap.

United Distributors sued Aireo Appliance & Hardware, Henry R. Burke, and Alfred R. Willis in solido on a note, relying on a credit guarantee Willis signed when he was considering becoming a 50% shareholder in Aireo. Willis denied liability, arguing the guarantee’s sole consideration was his anticipated ownership interest, which never materialized, and that plaintiff knew he would not be associated with the corporation. After Willis withdrew, plaintiff’s salesman returned related papers and knew Willis would not join Aireo, though the guarantee remained in plaintiff’s files. The debt arose from purchases made about a year later under Burke’s operation. The court found Willis signed only because he intended to become a shareholder, and once that plan failed and plaintiff was informed, the motive for the guarantee failed and the contract became ineffective. The judgment dismissing the suit against Willis was affirmed.

Johnson & Johnson reported a mixed first-quarter update, with sales slightly below consensus while adjusted earnings per share met expectations. Its shares traded around $125, implying a forward P/E of 19x and EV/EBITDA of 11.9x, levels described as not prohibitively priced but offering little implied upside after a rally from late January to mid-March. The company raised 2017 guidance, including Actelion’s estimated impact, to sales of $75.4 billion-$76.1 billion and adjusted EPS of $7.00-$7.15. Remicade sales fell 6% year over year to $1.67 billion, and baby care, oral care and wound care sales also declined. EPS rose despite a higher tax rate, though buybacks lifted reported EPS from $1.57 to $1.61. The author argues JNJ’s fundamentals remain solid but sees more downside risk for the equity, finds long-term debt relatively attractive, and prefers to seek value elsewhere.

The passage documents AGESA procedures and host-environment interfaces for AMD platform initialization, memory setup, boot, suspend, resume, and required call-outs.

A stackless assembler procedure initializes processors and cache-as-RAM to create a pre-memory stack region for all cores, maps it to global address space, sets MTRRs on x86-64, and creates a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instance. A companion procedure removes the pre-memory stack after main memory is available, flushes cache lines, disables CAR mode, and preserves EBX.

AmdCreateStruct allocates and initializes AGESA parameter structures using pre-memory heap, post-memory DRAM, or host-provided storage; AmdReleaseStruct frees them. Other service procedures retrieve DIMM data-eye results, APIC addresses, execution-cache size, processor die PCI addresses, current core identity, memory FRU location for an address, MMIO mappings, and event log entries.

Entry procedures are ordered by boot phase. AmdInitReset performs minimal processor initialization and execution-cache setup after reset. AmdInitEarly performs full pre-memory processor initialization, HyperTransport setup, power-management configuration, PCIe/GNB customization, and may request warm reset. AmdInitPost initializes main memory, transfers artifacts from cache storage, prepares processors for host control, and disables the pre-memory stack. AmdInitEnv moves HOB/artifact data into permanent host-controlled memory. Later procedures configure graphics, generate ACPI/DMI/IVRS/PState/WHEA/CRAT/CDIT tables, prepare for OS boot, and save state for S3 suspend.

Resume procedures restore silicon and memory state using saved nonvolatile and volatile context data, reinitialize memory from self-refresh, restore registers after PCI configuration is re-established, and complete final restoration before OS handoff.

Required host call-outs include allocating, locating, and deallocating buffers; initiating cold or warm reset; reading DIMM SPD data before memory initialization; and dispatching functions to APs after AGESA releases AP control. Additional entry points support AP task execution, PCIe port reset, AP status checking, AP idle mode, and platform-specific hooks.

Optional or conditionally required hooks allow IDS nonvolatile data access, heap-base selection, memory timing and voltage adjustments before DRAM initialization or training, external Vref control, resume self-refresh handling, video BIOS repost, expert FCH customization, memory-test voltage changes, and platform-specific device controls. The passage also describes build-configuration and platform-configuration structures for CPU, memory, graphics, PCIe, FCH, power, VRM, UMA, ECC, interleaving, display, SATA, USB, audio, IOMMU, and related features.

ConocoPhillips agreed to sell its San Juan Basin assets to an affiliate of Hilcorp Energy for $2.7 billion in cash, with up to $300 million in additional payments tied to Henry Hub natural gas prices over six years. The assets include 0.6 billion boe of proved reserves, 78% of which are natural gas, and cover 1.3 million acres. The sale follows a larger Canadian asset sale to Cenovus for $13.3 billion.

The transaction will reduce ConocoPhillips’ production by about 115,000 barrels per day and, combined with the Canadian sale, lower projected 2017 production by 25.4%. Operating cash flow is expected to decline by $0.2 billion to $0.3 billion. The company may also record a non-cash impairment, as the assets are on its books for $5.9 billion.

Management said proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, without specifying debt reduction, buybacks, capital spending, or acquisitions. The author views the sale as reasonable given the natural-gas-heavy reserve mix, but says value creation depends on how management uses the cash.
Figures show embodiments of a graphical user interface on a display screen; broken lines indicate unclaimed display screen or device elements.

The passage outlines tasks for a peace conference, including assessing doubtful states, arranging economic settlements, and safeguarding minorities in various regions. It describes how the Inquiry can assist through indexed data, maps, graphs, reports, problem evaluations, and trained staff, while noting tasks outside its scope, such as prisoner repatriation, reconstruction, armaments, aircraft law, raw materials, treaties, current commitments, and record drafting. It also includes correspondence in which S. E. Mezes requests a confidential proposed agreement on mutual guarantees of sovereignty and territorial integrity among American republics, and Secretary of State Robert Lansing sends him a proposed “Pan American Treaty.” The treaty draft states aims to maintain territorial integrity, political independence, republican government, defined boundaries, peaceful dispute settlement, international justice, and peace within member states.

Brayan Rocchio hit an eighth-inning home run off Troy Melton to spark a five-run rally as the Guardians beat the Tigers and forced a decisive Game 3 in the AL Wild Card Series. Detroit stranded a team playoff-record 15 baserunners. Rocchio, who earlier spent six weeks in Triple-A, said Cleveland plays without pressure and keeps battling until the final out.

VIX futures, introduced in 2004, are Cboe Futures Exchange contracts based on the VIX Index, which measures expected 30-day implied volatility in the U.S. equity market. Traders use VIX futures to speculate on volatility, hedge equity market risk, diversify portfolios, and pursue arbitrage or alpha strategies. A VIX futures strategy may use technical or fundamental indicators for entries and exits, along with risk management and position sizing.

VIX futures do not precisely track spot VIX. The S&P 500 VIX Short-Term Futures Index captures only about half of spot VIX movement, and rolling contracts can create long-term performance drag, making VIX futures costly as a long-term hedge. The article reports that prior backtests of VIX futures did not find a valuable tradable strategy, but a spot VIX-based stock strategy showed low market exposure, a 23% maximum drawdown, and strong results in 2008 and 2022.

VIX prices are mainly affected by the stock market cycle and contango or backwardation. VIX typically declines during bullish S&P 500 phases and rises during bearish phases. VIX seasonality is described as stronger in summer and fall, stagnant in winter, and declining in spring.

VIX futures trade Monday to Friday on CFE, with regular hours from 8:30 a.m. to 3:15 p.m. CT and extended sessions. The futures symbol is VX; the index symbol is VIX. Full contracts equal the index value times $1,000, while mini contracts equal one-tenth of that. The tick size is $50 for the full contract, with a minimum price fluctuation of 0.05. Contracts are financially settled, with a block minimum of 200 contracts.

The all-time high cited for VIX futures is 80.850 in March 2020. The VIX Index’s cited high is 89.53 in October 2008, and its low is 8.56 in November 2017. Traders can access VIX futures through a funded futures broker account, and charts are available through platforms such as TradingView and Yahoo Finance.

The study developed simultaneous ADF-EDS-EELS tomography to map structure, chemical composition, and transition metal valence states in 3D at the nanoscale with reduced electron dose and precise multimodal alignment. The method was applied to LiNi1/3Co1/3Mn1/3O2 cathode particles in pristine, 50-cycle, 100-cycle, and 200-cycle states.

Electrochemical testing showed capacity loss of 34.3% after 50 cycles, 52.2% after 100 cycles, and complete capacity failure after 200 cycles. Atomic-resolution imaging showed structural evolution from layered to spinel-like and then rock-salt structures. Chemical composition remained largely uniform through particle depth, with oxygen nearly constant up to 100 cycles and sharply reduced at 200 cycles; transition metal-rich regions increased during cycling, especially near surfaces.

Valence state maps showed strong depth dependence unlike chemical composition. Mn4+ and Co3+ dominated pristine particles and remained relatively stable up to 100 cycles, but decreased sharply by 200 cycles, with corresponding increases in Mn2+ and Co2+. Transition metal inhomogeneity was surface-localized and coupled to valence state shifts. The results indicate that degradation arises from interacting structural phase transitions, transition metal migration, and dissolution-driven segregation, rather than structural change alone.

The Elliott Wave theory, developed by Ralph Nelson Elliott after studying 75 years of stock data, is a technical analysis principle stating that asset prices move in recognizable wave patterns. It classifies waves into impulse waves, which move with the trend, and corrective waves, which move against it. Impulse waves contain five sub-waves, while corrective waves contain three. Traders use the theory in stocks, forex, and commodities to identify potential buying and selling opportunities, often alongside indicators such as moving averages, trend lines, RSI, or stochastic oscillators. The theory is subjective, difficult to backtest, lacks clear entry and exit rules, and is criticized for loose interpretation and potential curve fitting. There is no best timeframe; it depends on trading style.

The justices considered whether restitution under the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act is criminal punishment subject to the ex post facto clause. Ellingburg and the government both argued the MVRA cannot be applied retroactively to increase his punishment, while an appointed attorney defended the sentence. Alito highlighted civil, victim-compensation features, while Kagan and Jackson emphasized restitution’s role in criminal sentencing. The author predicts the Court will reject applying the statute to Ellingburg.

The Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed the trial court’s decision that Mumma Brothers Drilling Co. owed sales or use tax on drilling equipment purchases. The taxpayer drilled water wells and installed or repaired related equipment for residences, farms, and commercial users. The court held Mumma was a contractor under Indiana tax law because it bought tangible personal property and incorporated it into facilities becoming part of the land. The taxpayer claimed an exemption for machinery used in extracting tangible personal property, arguing that water was being extracted. The court rejected the exemption because the ultimate users generally used the water personally or in their own operations, with no evidence of resale. The court concluded the exemption was intended for manufacturing-related extraction involving resale and prevention of tax pyramiding, not extraction of water for personal use.

Verizon Communications saw $56.85 million in net inflows Friday despite closing down $0.37 at $48.81, ranking 11th among tracked companies for daily net inflow. Analysts currently average a “Hold” rating with a $52.86 target price. The company reported quarterly EPS of $0.96 on revenue of $30.55 billion, and analysts expect $3.76 EPS for the fiscal year. Verizon raised its quarterly dividend to $0.59, payable Nov. 1. Recent activity also included unusually high call option volume, insider stock sales, and several hedge fund position changes.

The Eleventh Circuit affirmed Alexis Perez’s 51-month sentence after his guilty plea to conspiracy to commit mail fraud. The court held that Perez was not entitled to a three-level reduction for an incomplete conspiracy because he and his co-conspirators had taken crucial steps toward completing the offense, had a detailed plan, had the means to execute it, and were on the verge of doing so. The court also upheld denial of a minor-role reduction, finding that Perez was importantly involved in planning and preparation, understood the fraudulent scheme, was paid for his services, and failed to show he was less culpable than most co-conspirators.

The passage describes NVIDIA RTX IO, which uses Microsoft DirectStorage and GPU-based lossless decompression to reduce CPU storage bottlenecks, improve I/O performance, speed game loading, support asset streaming, and benefit professional workloads involving large datasets. It also outlines NVIDIA GA10x Ampere architecture features, including improved shading, ray tracing, AI performance, GDDR6X support, advanced display capabilities, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4a, AV1 hardware decode, fifth-generation NVDEC, and seventh-generation NVENC.

The NVIDIA A40 is presented as a GA10x Ampere-based data center GPU for visual computing, AI, data science, virtualization, and rendering, with up to 48GB memory per GPU and NVLink scaling to 96GB. The RTX A6000 is described as a professional workstation GPU with 48GB GDDR6, NVLink support, ray tracing, AI denoising, and large-scene rendering capabilities. The passage also covers GeForce RTX 3090 and RTX 3070 specifications, GDDR6X Error Detection and Replay for memory overclocking, and NVIDIA’s warranty, liability, and licensing disclaimers.

To reduce debt, limit credit card use, create a spending plan, build an emergency fund, and put extra money toward monthly payments. Cut unnecessary expenses, prioritize debts with the highest interest rates, and redirect payments from paid-off balances to remaining debts. Gradual lifestyle changes can help make debt repayment more manageable.

The passage discusses metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), emphasizing limited treatment options, frequent resistance to androgen signaling inhibitors and taxanes, and the need for ex vivo methods to predict drug response. It focuses on microtubule (MT) dynamics as a functional marker of drug susceptibility and resistance.

The authors describe computational tracking of EB1/EB3-labeled MT plus-end comets in live-cell imaging to quantify MT growth, pausing, shortening, and spatial organization. In M12 prostate cancer cells, AR-wt expression caused little change in MT growth compared with AR-null cells, while ARv7 expression increased EB1 speeds by over 40% and showed distinct MT organization, consistent with taxane resistance. Patient-derived prostate organoids from primary, lymph node, and metastatic tissues are proposed as models to match tumors to tubulin inhibitors based on MT dynamics signatures.

The passage reports efforts to optimize prostate organoid culture, including reduced Y-27632 ROCK inhibitor to select for high-grade tumor cells. It notes that benign tissue is more dependent on Y-27632, while high-grade tumor cells are more apoptosis-resilient. The text also discusses small circulating tumor cells in androgen-independent mCRPC, detectable by PSMA, and suggests that size-based CTC methods may miss these cells.

Multiple regulators of MT dynamics and drug resistance are reviewed, including AR variants, Op18/STMN1, ERG, BRCA1, pVHL, GSK3β, CLIP170, CLASPs, NAD+, HIF1α, and MAPK-related pathways. The authors report that paclitaxel attenuates MT growth in MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells and that BRCA1 knockdown in A549 cells reduces paclitaxel-induced MT bundling. Circular Hough transform is used to quantify drug-induced circular MT bundles as a marker of taxane activity.

The passage proposes correlating live-cell MT dynamics, gene expression signatures, organoid drug response, and patient outcomes to anticipate resistance. It also suggests validating MT-regulating targets through knockdown organoids, patient-derived xenografts, tissue slice assays, transcriptomics, and co-culture immune screens. The conclusion argues that quantitative imaging of MT dynamics in patient-derived cells may help select drug regimens, identify sensitizing compounds, and guide treatment strategies in localized and metastatic prostate cancer.

A day trading price action strategy uses patterns in an asset’s intraday price movements to determine trade entries and exits. Price action trading is a form of technical analysis focused mainly on historical price behavior rather than fundamentals or indicators. Traders study swing highs and lows, candlestick behavior, chart structure, trends, ranges, support and resistance, and patterns that may indicate continuation or reversal.

Common price action patterns include reversal chart patterns, continuation chart patterns, harmonic patterns, and candlestick patterns. Some traders use pure price action with tools such as trend lines and support/resistance levels, while others combine it with indicators such as moving averages, VIX, or RSI.

The passage emphasizes that there is no universally best price action strategy and that effectiveness depends on the market and strategy rules. Backtesting is presented as essential, though difficult because price action patterns can be hard to code and manual testing may be affected by bias. An example WTI crude oil futures backtest showed weak historical performance, while later out-of-sample results showed limited positive performance. The passage concludes that day trading price action strategies should be quantified and tested before use.

Spanish police dismantled a prostitution network exploiting transsexuals recruited through fake “Miss Trans” contests in Venezuela. Over 20 victims were freed, and 14 suspects arrested. Police said victims faced document confiscation, forced debt, prostitution, drug dealing, and inhumane conditions.

Google honored Max Born’s 135th birthday with a Doodle recognizing his contributions to quantum mechanics. Born was born in Breslau, Germany, in 1882 and later taught theoretical physics at the University of Göttingen, where notable scientists studied or worked. He was a longtime friend of Albert Einstein despite differing views on quantum theory. After Hitler rose to power, Born, who was Jewish, emigrated to England after being expelled from his post. He received the 1954 Nobel Prize for the Born Rule, a probability-based principle central to quantum mechanics. Born died on Jan. 5, 1970, at age 87.

The Regulatory Sandbox in Education bill allows district and charter schools to create innovation plans and seek state board rule waivers. LEAs may use certain restricted funds and accept private support for innovative programs. The Utah State Board of Education must report annually on approved plans, waivers, denials, terminations, statutory barriers, and legislative recommendations. Since no LEA applications or approved plans are known, the recommendation is for the board to increase awareness, provide website information, develop optional application forms, and promote the program through existing channels.

UK employment rose by 109,000 in the three months to April, taking the employment rate to a joint-record 74.8%, with surveys showing continued strong hiring. However, regular earnings growth slowed to 1.7%, while consumer price inflation reached 2.9%, meaning real pay is falling. The squeeze on households is expected to weigh on consumer spending, leaving growth dependent on exports, corporate services and business investment. Election-related uncertainty may weaken business confidence and domestic growth. Input cost inflation has moderated, suggesting consumer inflation may cool later in the year, though wage growth shows little sign of improving. The passage says Bank of England policymakers are increasingly likely to keep interest rates on hold amid weak wages, inflation and Brexit uncertainty.

Minister Schoenfeld told Finnish Foreign Minister Witting that reports of favorable American public and press attitudes toward Finland did not match his understanding and reiterated the U.S. position. Witting said Procopé had qualified his report and remained pessimistic long term. Witting defended Finnish strategic aims, including control of the Karelian and Onega Isthmuses, citing threats from the Murmansk railroad area. Schoenfeld questioned reliance on strategic lines and emphasized political foundations for security. Witting argued Finnish “realism” came from long experience with Russia and said Finland was trying to preserve itself. Schoenfeld reported that Witting seemed aware Finland was increasingly subject to forces beyond its control.

In a separate note, the Secretary of State informed Finnish Minister Procopé that U.S. citizens serving in Finnish diplomatic or consular posts were subject to Finnish jurisdiction in their official capacities and could be required to comply with U.S. requests or lose their official connections. Finnish consular personnel were also required to make inquiries before leaving their city limits.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on December 21, 2015, its Board of Directors amended its Amended and Restated Bylaws to implement proxy access. The new provision allows a shareholder or group of up to twenty shareholders owning at least 3% of Apple’s common stock continuously for at least three years to include director nominees in annual meeting proxy materials, up to 20% of the Board, subject to bylaw requirements. Related amendments were also made to shareholder notice and other bylaw provisions.

The passage describes AGESA software integration with a host BIOS through a binary image interface. The host BIOS uses bridge code to call the AGESA dispatcher, while AGESA uses a call-out port and router to request host services. The host environment must establish a valid stack, create standard headers, locate binary image entry points, implement required call-outs, and provide a call-out router.

It outlines UEFI execution phases, AGESA library and build targets, required build tools, platform option files, environment variables, and integration steps such as copying option files, enabling Cache-As-RAM, and avoiding changes to stack or cache controls during the pre-memory period. It also describes stack-related macros and procedures for early initialization, enabling a UEFI stack, and disabling the pre-memory stack.

The passage documents AGESA service procedures including structure creation and release, data eye retrieval, APIC and PCI address lookup, processor-core identification, memory address-to-DIMM mapping, MMIO range updates, and event log reading. It lists main initialization entry points such as AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, AmdInitMid, AmdInitLate, AmdInitRtb, and resume-related procedures, with their purposes, dependencies, configuration structures, and status results.

It also covers UEFI PEIM and DXE drivers, published PPIs and protocols, memory initialization outputs, graphics and FCH configuration options, ACPI/DMI table generation, S3 suspend and resume context handling, and required host call-out functions such as buffer allocation.

DBS says Indian government bonds remain under upward yield pressure from supply and rising developed-market yields, though most of the sell-off may be over and future increases may be modest. It favors shorter-term bonds, is neutral-to-negative on longer-term bonds, and sees better entry points ahead. The rupee and Sensex have weakened year-to-date, with the rupee vulnerable due to India’s current account deficit, widening savings-investment gap, bond pressure, and rising US rates. DBS expects the rupee to depreciate toward 67 this year.

NEMA’s South East coordinator, Walson Ibarakumo, warned of impending floods in parts of Enugu, Anambra and Ebonyi, citing NIHSA and NiMET forecasts and climate change. He urged early preparation and attitude changes on energy use. High-risk areas include Enugu South and East; Aguata, Idemili North and Ogbaru; and several flood-prone areas in Ebonyi.

Al-Qaida-linked militants in Syria downed a Russian Su-25 fighter jet in Idlib province and killed the pilot after he ejected and resisted capture, according to militants, monitors and Russia’s Defense Ministry. The plane was reportedly shot down near Saraqeb, where Syrian forces, backed by Russian airstrikes, have been advancing. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reported heavy airstrikes in the area and said many residents were fleeing. Syrian state media said government forces captured nearby positions, while the U.N. said more than 270,000 people had been displaced in Idlib since Dec. 15.

Separately, fighting continued in Afrin between Turkish forces with allied Syrian opposition fighters and the Syrian Kurdish YPG militia. Turkey said three soldiers were killed, bringing its losses in the Afrin offensive to eight soldiers and at least 24 allied fighters. Turkey said it aims to clear the YPG from Afrin and called on the United States to disengage from the group.

NVIDIA’s fiscal 2015 Form 10-K covers the year ended January 25, 2015. The company, headquartered in Santa Clara, California, develops visual computing products and operates through GPU and Tegra Processor segments, addressing Gaming, Enterprise, High Performance Computing & Cloud, and Automotive markets. Its brands include GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, GRID, Tegra, DRIVE, and SHIELD.

For fiscal 2015, NVIDIA reported revenue of $4.68 billion, operating income of $759.0 million, net income of $630.6 million, and diluted earnings per share of $1.12. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $4.62 billion at year-end. The company spent $1.36 billion on research and development and had 9,228 employees, including 6,658 in research and development.

NVIDIA uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on third parties for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging. It identified major risks including competition, dependence on design wins, licensing uncertainty, product defects, cybersecurity threats, reliance on suppliers, demand forecasting, international operations, intellectual property disputes, operating-result fluctuations, and indebtedness.

During fiscal 2015, NVIDIA introduced Maxwell-based GeForce and Quadro products, expanded Tesla and GRID initiatives, launched SHIELD tablet and GRID streaming, announced Tegra X1 and DRIVE automotive computers, and returned $1.00 billion to shareholders through repurchases and dividends. Its common stock trades on NASDAQ under NVDA.

Mentoring relationships with adults and peers, including school-based, afterschool, community-based, and naturally formed relationships with teachers and other adults, can support students’ academic achievement, engagement, attendance, behavior, and educational attainment. The passage emphasizes heightened need after COVID-19 disruptions, which affected learning, connection to adults, and student well-being, especially among low-income students, students of color, students with disabilities, and marginalized youth.

Multiple meta-analyses and research syntheses found positive effects of mentoring programs on academic outcomes such as attendance, grades, test scores, classroom behavior, school connectedness, engagement, and educational confidence. Studies of specific programs—including Big Brothers Big Sisters School-Based Mentoring, Gear Up, AMPED, Project Arrive, Success Mentors, Check and Connect, Quantum Opportunities, Village Model of Care, and Pathways to Education—reported gains in areas such as grades, attendance, credits earned, graduation, and college enrollment.

Research also shows that mentoring relationships formed naturally with teachers, counselors, coaches, school staff, and other caring adults are associated with stronger school attachment, motivation, GPAs, educational attainment, and positive outcomes for students of color. However, access to mentoring is uneven, with youth of color, low-income youth, and youth whose parents have limited education reporting fewer mentoring relationships. The passage argues that expanding mentoring quantity and quality requires public and private investment at local, state, and federal levels.

Xiaomi Redmi 5 goes on sale in India at 12 pm on Amazon India, Mi.com and Mi Home stores, with over 4 lakh units claimed to be available. Prices are Rs 7,999 for 2GB RAM/16GB storage, Rs 8,999 for 3GB/32GB, and Rs 10,999 for 4GB/64GB, all supporting microSD expansion up to 128GB via a hybrid dual-SIM slot. The phone features a 5.7-inch HD+ 18:9 display, metal unibody design, rear fingerprint scanner, Qualcomm Snapdragon 450 processor, 3300mAh battery, 12MP rear camera, 5MP front camera with selfie flash, Android Nougat 7.1.2 with MIUI 9, and four colour options: Black, Gold, Lake Blue and Rose Gold.

The Colts blew another lead in a 13-7 overtime loss after a late penalty negated a go-ahead conversion and Adam Vinatieri tied it in blizzard conditions. Coach Chuck Pagano said the weather left players with “dead legs” ahead of a Thursday game against Denver. Indianapolis has lost four straight, been eliminated from playoff contention and faces questions about Pagano’s future. Players said they remain focused on finishing the season. Ryan Kelly and Rashaan Melvin practiced Monday, while Donte Moncrief is week to week with an ankle injury.

The President transmits State Department correspondence and explains why he will not submit the proposed 1853 convention with Mexico on a Tehuantepec transit way for Senate ratification. He objects that it would bind the United States for many years to guarantee a private company’s foreign contract, protect its people, property, and capital, and limit withdrawal of protection. He also states it would conflict with obligations under the 1850 convention with Great Britain.

A longitudinal evaluation in a 149-bed Georgia nursing home assessed SARS-CoV-2 antibody responses after infection and Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccination from October 2020 to April 2021. Eleven residents were analyzed; median age was 74 years, 64% were male, all had cardiovascular disease, 91% had at least three underlying conditions, four had severe COVID-19 requiring hospitalization, and one died. Ten participants received two vaccine doses; one declined vaccination.

Among 10 participants with post-infection serology, nine developed detectable Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA antibodies, eight developed IgM, and one did not develop detectable binding antibodies during early testing. Median time to detection within 30 days was 13 days for Pan-Ig and IgG, 16 days for IgA, and 15 days for IgM. At first antibody detection, some participants remained RT-PCR positive, but none had culturable virus. Pan-Ig and IgG remained elevated after infection, while IgM and IgA began declining around 31–60 days.

After vaccination, all 10 vaccinated participants had detectable Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA antibodies, and six had detectable IgM. Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA titers increased after the second vaccine dose compared with pre-vaccination levels; IgG geometric mean titers were 10–200 times higher post-vaccination than post-infection. The unvaccinated participant maintained Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA through 150 days post-diagnosis but had lower Pan-Ig and IgG after 90 days than vaccinated participants.

The authors conclude that nursing home residents in this cohort mounted durable and diverse humoral immune responses after infection, and vaccination augmented Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA responses.

Lever Brothers appealed a Patent Office decision dismissing its opposition to Thrift-D-Lux Cleaners’ application to register a service mark for dry cleaning and pressing services. Lever relied on its prior use and registration of “Lux” for soap flakes, toilet soap, and liquid detergents, as well as its “Lux Laundry Plan” involving laundries that used the “Lux Laundry” name.

Thrift-D-Lux’s mark featured “Thrift-D-Lux” with “Cleaners” and slogans suggesting “thrifty in price” and “de luxe in quality.” Lever argued the mark was confusingly similar to “Lux,” with “Lux” as the dominant element. The court found “Thrift-D-Lux” conveyed thrift combined with “de luxe,” a common descriptive term, rather than “Thrifty Lux.”

The court distinguished prior cases cited by Lever and found the relationship between Lever’s goods and Thrift-D-Lux’s services too tenuous. Because Lever provided no evidence of likely confusion or damage, the Commissioner’s decision was affirmed.

An outside day, or outside bar, is a two-bar pattern where the current bar has a higher high and lower low than the previous bar and consumes its full range. It may indicate rising volatility and can act as a continuation or reversal signal depending on context. Bullish and bearish outside days depend on the direction of the second bar, while outside reversals occur when the bars move in opposite directions within a price swing. The passage states that outside day strategies are subjective and should be combined with technical analysis and backtesting. Backtests on SPY found average performance after outside days to be zero, negative after higher closes, and slightly positive after lower closes, but not tradable.

Oclaro reported a 47% revenue increase, margin expansion to 39%, and EPS growth to $0.79, while trading at about 11 times fiscal 2017 earnings. Analysts expect EPS of $0.74 in 2018 and $0.82 in 2019. Demand is strongest in 100G products, which now make up 81% of Oclaro’s revenue, with QSFP28 sales doubling sequentially, while legacy CFP and 40G-and-below products declined. China revenue fell sequentially and is expected to decline further near term, though management expects future demand for QSFP28, 25G, and 100G transceivers, including for 5G front-haul deployments. The article argues Oclaro is well positioned in high-growth optical networking areas, including 100G and emerging 400G products, with less exposure to legacy products than peers. The company has no debt, $258 million in cash and short-term investments, generated $46 million in operating cash flow, and expects Q1 2018 revenue of $151 million to $159 million. The author concludes Oclaro appears cheaply valued and better insulated from industry cyclicality due to its focus on newer, higher-margin products.

Aziz Ansari said on “Good Hang with Amy Poehler” that he uses a flip phone, has not had email for about 10 years, and avoids apps like Uber. He said living with less technology gives him space to think and helps his writing, while acknowledging this lifestyle is not realistic for everyone. Ansari criticized ChatGPT as “outsourcing critical thinking” and said he prefers human conversation. The article also notes other celebrities and some non-celebrities who have reduced smartphone or internet use.

The Pennsylvania Supreme Court affirmed judgment for the assignees of a Pennsylvania judgment. The Thompson Oil Company had assigned its judgment in good faith to Pennsylvania residents before New York attachment proceedings were brought against the company’s alleged debtors. The court held that the valid Pennsylvania assignment transferred all interest to the assignees, leaving the company with no attachable interest. The New York attachment judgment and garnishees’ payment did not bar the assignees’ recovery because the assignees and the assigned judgment were not within New York jurisdiction, the assignees were not parties or privies, and full faith and credit does not prevent inquiry into jurisdiction. Any error in ordering oyer of the New York record was waived.

President George H. W. Bush thanks President Reagan, invokes George Washington and the continuity of American democracy, and opens with a prayer that power be used to serve people. He says the nation is peaceful and prosperous, freedom is advancing globally, and free markets, speech, elections, and will are the basis of a just life. He urges Americans to value service, duty, sacrifice, and community over material success, and calls for addressing homelessness, neglected children, addiction, crime, welfare dependency, and young mothers through both government action and citizen involvement. He promotes “a Thousand Points of Light” and asks for renewed cooperation between the Executive and Congress, especially on the budget and bipartisanship after Vietnam-era divisions. Internationally, he pledges strength for peace, fidelity to alliances and agreements, continued engagement with the Soviet Union, and concern for Americans held or missing abroad. He calls for tolerance while declaring drugs a scourge that must be stopped, and closes by expressing confidence in the future and a commitment to unity, diversity, and generosity.

Nassau County jurors acquitted 18-year-old Jasmine Copeland of manslaughter, gang assault and other charges in the 2014 stabbing death of 17-year-old Abbigale Thomas during a brawl in Freeport. Prosecutors alleged Copeland stabbed Thomas after social media insults escalated into a confrontation, but jurors rejected that theory after about three hours of deliberation. Copeland’s attorney said her client was innocent and argued that although Copeland carried a knife, she did not use it.

Northern Ireland’s health service is the only one in the UK not led by a minister and faces pressures including ageing population, complex care needs, GP staffing issues, drug costs and long hospital waiting lists. Additional funding was allocated, but over 83,000 people waited more than a year for a first hospital appointment. Recent crises included neurology patient recalls and serious care home failings. Rafael Bengoa’s 2016 reform recommendations had cross-party support, but Stormont’s collapse left no health minister to lead implementation.

James Horne, a plastic surgeon, sued the New York State Department of Health under Executive Law § 296, alleging that revocation of his medical license discriminated against him based on adult Attention Deficit Disorder. Supreme Court granted the Department’s summary judgment motion, finding the action was essentially a challenge to the license revocation that had to be brought as a CPLR article 78 proceeding and was time barred. The appellate court affirmed, holding that the complaint and requested relief depended on reversing the Administrative Review Board’s determination. It rejected Horne’s argument that article 78 review was not exclusive under Public Health Law § 230-c (5), and found it unnecessary to address res judicata or collateral estoppel.

Zeta Global is acquiring Marigold’s enterprise software business for $325 million, its largest acquisition and 17th since its 2007 founding. Marian Gaborik and Dwight King discussed needing better starts after three straight two-goal deficits, while expressing confidence the team will find energy despite heavy overtime minutes. Gaborik said returning to Madison Square Garden after being traded will be special, citing the building’s history, renovations and fans. William Green’s final lecture reviews stochastic methods, emphasizing multidimensional integrals with weighting factors, including Boltzmann distributions and Bayesian likelihood-prior formulations. He explains that Metropolis Monte Carlo can evaluate such integrals but requires careful step-size selection: too large causes repeated rejected states, too small limits sampling. Adaptive step sizing, multiple initial states, and reasonableness checks are recommended. Monte Carlo gives rough estimates quickly but improves only as one over the square root of sample count, making high accuracy costly.

He discusses Kinetic Monte Carlo for systems with huge discrete state spaces, such as catalytic surfaces with many sites and possible adsorbates. Because full probability vectors and transition matrices are impossible to store, Gillespie trajectories are used. Sampling issues include many low-probability states, computational cost from frequent events, and the need to compute averages on the fly. Initial conditions should be sampled, often using Poisson distributions. Simplifications may include treating fast diffusion as equilibrated, slowing unimportant fast processes, or removing very slow events outside the timescale of interest.

Green also reviews molecular dynamics, which solves atomic equations of motion, often with force fields and the velocity Verlet algorithm, sometimes using thermostats. It is useful for time-dependent processes on picosecond to nanosecond scales but limited by very small time steps and may not sample slow conformational changes or equilibria well.

He concludes that Metropolis Monte Carlo, Kinetic Monte Carlo, and molecular dynamics are suited to different problems, and researchers must choose methods appropriate to the question rather than using familiar tools indiscriminately.

A new analysis led by Darren McKnight of LeoLabs identifies the 50 low-Earth orbit objects most likely to generate future space debris through collisions. Most are decades-old rocket bodies: 76 percent were deposited before 2000, and 88 percent are rocket bodies. Removing all 50 would reduce debris-generating potential in low-Earth orbit by 50 percent; removing the top 10 would cut risk by 30 percent.

Russia and the Soviet Union account for 34 of the top 50 objects, followed by China with 10. However, China has recently become the main source of new long-lived rocket debris, leaving 21 of 26 hazardous rocket bodies abandoned in orbit since January 2024. Many are linked to launches for China’s Guowang and Thousand Sails megaconstellations, and McKnight warned this trend could add more than 100 rocket bodies that violate the 25-year orbital-debris guideline.

The passage notes that deorbiting upper stages can reduce payload capacity and that some rockets lack restart capability, though McKnight said China has demonstrated sustainable practices on some missions. China says it is researching debris removal, while agencies in Europe and Japan have funded limited active-debris-removal efforts. McKnight argues removing even 10 to 20 high-risk objects could meaningfully reduce the chance of cascading collisions known as Kessler Syndrome.

Buchanan sought a writ of error after his New York murder conviction and death sentence were affirmed, claiming denial of due process and an impartial jury because juror Paradise allegedly became physically and mentally incapacitated during deliberations. The New York Court of Appeals found the issues concerning the juror’s illness, separation of jurors, and competency were factual matters resolved against Buchanan after conflicting evidence. The Supreme Court held that a juror’s physical and mental condition and competency to return a verdict are questions of fact not reviewable on writ of error to a state court in an action at law. The application was denied.

The passage describes patent-related technology for detecting gastric neoplasia, particularly premalignant and malignant gastric cancer, using DNA methylation markers. It states that gastric cancer remains difficult to cure because many patients present with advanced disease, creating a need for improved early detection methods.

The technology identifies differentially methylated regions (DMRs) as biomarkers by comparing methylation states in gastric cancer samples with controls such as normal stomach tissue, normal colon tissue, plasma, and white blood cell DNA. Reduced Representation Bisulfite Sequencing and validation studies identified 123 novel methylation markers, including optimized marker panels for stomach cancer detection. Reported marker sets include a 10-marker panel, a 30-marker panel, and a 12-marker plasma panel. A 3-marker plasma panel comprising ELMO1, ZNF569, and C13orf18 detected gastric cancer with 86% sensitivity at 100% specificity.

The passage describes methods for assaying methylation states of one or more markers in samples such as gastric tissue, plasma, stool, blood, urine, or other biological samples. Detection methods may include bisulfite treatment, methylation-specific PCR, sequencing, QuARTS assays, methylation-sensitive restriction enzymes, mass spectrometry, target capture, and next-generation sequencing.

The technology also includes compositions, oligonucleotides, primers, probes, reaction mixtures, kits, and systems for detecting methylated DMRs. Systems may include analysis components, software for comparing sample methylation to control or reference data, databases, and alert components for reporting gastric cancer-associated methylation states or risk-related values. The passage further provides definitions of relevant terms and describes figures showing marker performance, ROC curves, plasma marker levels by cancer stage, and assay results for gastric cancer markers.

The passage describes AGESA software interface rules, error handling, build models, UEFI integration, stack setup, and initialization procedures. Host code must call only published interface functions, establish a valid stack before AGESA calls, avoid enabling execution caching before memory initialization except through provided AGESA functions, and avoid modifying cache controls during Cache-As-RAM operation.

AGESA calls return status codes that guide host action: success, unsupported, bounds check, alert, warning, error, critical, and fatal. The host environment is responsible for responding appropriately, including logging, notifying users, stopping POST, or preventing OS boot where required. Events are stored in a circular log buffer and retrieved with `AmdReadEventLog`.

The binary module model uses a host BIOS bridge to call the AGESA dispatcher, while AGESA uses a call-out port and host router to invoke host services. The host must implement call-out routing, fill standard headers, and provide required services. UEFI support spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases, with PEIMs and DXE drivers handling processor, memory, reset coordination, late initialization, table generation, VGA control, and protocol publication.

Build guidance covers binary module and source integration methods, platform option files, UEFI control files, required environment variables, toolchains, and platform-specific build configuration. Reference files in the Addendum directory show implementation examples and default platform options.

Provided AGESA routines include stack enable/disable macros, structure creation and release, processor and memory query services, MMIO range updates, event log reads, and initialization entry points such as `AmdInitReset`, `AmdInitEarly`, `AmdInitPost`, `AmdInitEnv`, `AmdInitLate`, `AmdInitRtb`, and `AmdInitResume`. These procedures initialize processors, memory, chipset interfaces, graphics, ACPI/DMI tables, S3 suspend context, and resume state, with specific ordering, dependencies, and host responsibilities.
