In Lewis v. Bayer AG, plaintiffs sought class certification over claims arising from ingestion of Baycol, a cholesterol-lowering statin withdrawn from the market in August 2001 after reports of rhabdomyolysis. Plaintiffs alleged Baycol caused increased risks of rhabdomyolysis, kidney disease, CoQ10 depletion, and other injuries, and proposed four classes covering Pennsylvania and nationwide medical monitoring and personal injury claims.

The court found numerosity satisfied but held that nationwide and personal injury classes lacked commonality because individual factual and legal issues predominated, including differing medical histories, dosages, warnings, causation, and state laws. It also rejected UTPCPL claims for class treatment because reliance and causation required individualized proof. The court found common issues only for Pennsylvania residents seeking medical monitoring and found the named representatives typical and adequate for that claim.

The court granted certification only for Class I: Pennsylvania persons prescribed and ingesting Baycol who had not been diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis or congestive heart disease, seeking medical monitoring including CoQ10 testing, CK testing, chest x-rays, a court-supervised monitoring program, and related equitable relief. Arthur Conner, Milton Angert, and Lisa Frost were appointed class representatives, plaintiffs’ counsel was appointed class counsel, and certification was denied for all other classes.

The passage describes patent embodiments for improving wireless downlink communication reliability through downlink assignments for downlink control channels. A user equipment monitors multiple PDCCH candidates in different control resource sets, receives downlink assignments, determines PDSCH resource allocations and DMRS symbol locations based on the assignments and CORESET symbol sets, and decodes the corresponding downlink data channels. It addresses TCI state handling, QCL relationships, PDSCH repetition windows, DMRS placement when CORESETs overlap or differ in duration, and PUCCH resource determination when multiple CORESETs or PDCCHs are used. A defensive switch in soccer occurs when the first defender is beaten and the second, or support, defender takes over the ball carrier while the first defender moves to cover the second defender’s original mark or position. The support defender should be goalside, behind and inside the first defender, positioned to block the direct path to goal and guide the attacker toward the sideline. The support defender must communicate arrival and instructions, using calls such as “support,” “jockey,” “tackle,” or “switch.”

Training begins with players understanding one-on-one defending, goalside positioning, defensive stance, individual defending, and support responsibilities. Coaches demonstrate positioning, then add movement, communication, half-speed practice, and full-speed game conditions. Scenarios include switches down the sideline, switches inside from the sideline, midfield switches with or without the ball, and switching back after play is no longer active.

The second defender initiates the switch, and the first defender must recover efficiently to the new role. If the support defender had no marking assignment, the beaten defender should retreat into a proper support position.

The passage outlines a study on how the COVID-19 pandemic influenced special education due process hearing decisions involving Pennsylvania city Local Education Agencies (LEAs). Under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA), students with disabilities are entitled to a free appropriate public education (FAPE), and families may pursue due process hearings when they believe rights have been violated. Pennsylvania has historically been highly active in IDEA disputes, and city LEAs such as Philadelphia and Pittsburgh faced documented compliance issues during the pandemic.

The study addresses limited scholarship on pandemic effects at the local level by comparing published Pennsylvania hearing officer decisions involving city LEAs from two years before and two years after March 16, 2020. It asks whether city LEAs were involved in more hearings after the pandemic, whether hearing officer outcomes were significantly related to the pandemic period, and what remedies city LEAs were ordered to provide.

Using an ex-post facto design, the study reviews publicly available Office for Dispute Resolution decisions from March 16, 2018, to March 15, 2022. After removing duplicates, 323 hearings remain for review, with non-city LEA cases excluded. Decisions are categorized by pre- or post-COVID period, ruling outcomes, and owed remedies, including independent educational evaluations, compensatory education, and reimbursements.

WHO data on 1,622 urban locations in 92 countries shows PM 2.5 pollution is highest in Pakistan’s urban areas, followed by Qatar and Afghanistan. The rankings cover cities only, not entire countries, and are weighted by city population. Delhi’s average PM 2.5 concentration is 150 micrograms per cubic metre, compared with London’s 16. Europe’s most polluted cities are in Turkey, Bulgaria and Serbia. Australia has the least polluted urban areas, followed by Brunei and New Zealand; the UK ranks 21st for air quality.

Russ Tedrake compares model-free policy gradient methods with value-function methods. Policy gradients can scale to high-dimensional systems, exploit smoothness, are simple local searches in policy space, and have strong convergence properties, but they can have high variance, require many trials, and depend on choices such as parameterization. Value-function methods can be more data-efficient because they learn compact scalar estimates and reuse prior estimates, but their convergence guarantees are weaker; small value-function changes can cause large policy changes and instability.

The lecture introduces actor-critic methods as a way to combine both approaches. The actor represents the policy, while the critic estimates value. Using a value estimate to compare expected and observed rewards can reduce the variance of policy-gradient updates without breaking convergence if it is uncorrelated with the added noise. Tedrake cites work by Konda and Tsitsiklis, Sutton, and Jan Peters, and briefly describes the policy gradient theorem and online actor-critic updates using estimated Q functions.

Tedrake then presents his thesis work on the Toddler walking robot as a case study. Toddler was designed as a passive-dynamic-inspired, underactuated robot with actuated ankles and a passive hip. It used a policy-gradient/actor-critic approach with a low-dimensional value approximation and updates once per footstep, aiming to stabilize a desired return map. The robot learned to walk on flat ground within minutes, adapted to disturbances and terrain changes, and converged much faster when reusing a previously learned value function. Tedrake emphasizes that the method worked without an accurate model and that the value estimate was essential for fast learning.

The Georgia Court of Appeals affirmed a Chatham County Superior Court order granting Ricky G. Rau’s petition to modify custody and child support, awarding him sole legal and physical custody of his three minor children with Kathrine Clark. The prior order had granted joint legal custody, with varying physical custody arrangements among the children. Rau sought modification, alleging material changes affecting the children’s welfare, including Clark’s failure to follow custody arrangements and provide a suitable furnished residence.

The majority held that Clark’s pro se appellate brief failed to comply with court rules because it lacked a statement of facts, record citations, clear enumerations of error, and supporting legal argument. The court also noted that no transcript of the bench trial was included, despite the hearing having been reported. Because Clark, as appellant, bore the burden of showing error, the court presumed the regularity of the trial proceedings and that sufficient evidence supported the trial court’s ruling. The majority rejected the dissent’s view that the custody order was facially deficient for not expressly reciting the “best interest of the child” standard, concluding that the trial court’s finding of a material substantial change affecting the children’s welfare was sufficient absent a request for specific findings.

The dissent argued that the custody order should be vacated and remanded because it failed to state that the custody change was in the children’s best interest, a required legal standard for custody modification. The dissent maintained that Clark’s notice of appeal and brief sufficiently identified the challenged custody order and her argument that the trial court failed to consider statutory best-interest factors. It concluded that appellate review was warranted despite deficiencies in Clark’s brief and absence of a transcript.

Under a May trade deal, the United States allowed China to export cooked poultry meat in exchange for China accepting U.S. beef and liquefied natural gas. The U.S. has no poultry shortage; it is the world’s largest poultry producer. Imports are limited to cooked poultry likely because raw poultry could transmit avian influenza, including viruses that can infect birds and humans.

Properly cooked poultry poses no food safety risk from viruses or bacteria, but undercooking or cross-contamination can spread salmonella or campylobacter. Additional concerns include antibiotic residues and heavy metals, which may be greater risks in China due to weaker enforcement, limited farmer awareness, coal-related contamination, and lack of transparent public food safety data. China has announced plans to improve monitoring of residues by 2020.

The USDA’s Food Safety Inspection Service determines whether foreign safeguards are equivalent to U.S. standards, relies on approved countries to certify and inspect eligible plants, and conducts annual on-site audits. Cooked poultry is excluded from country-of-origin labeling, so U.S. consumers may not know if they are eating poultry grown and processed in China, including in restaurants. China’s ability to compete in the U.S. market depends on price, but its poultry industry is less integrated and technologically advanced than the U.S. industry.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s RTX Blackwell neural rendering architecture and related GeForce RTX 50 Series features. FP4 support reduces FLUX.dev VRAM needs from over 23GB at FP16 to under 10GB and improves image generation speed on RTX 5090. Blackwell adds fifth-generation Tensor Cores, fourth-generation RT Cores, doubled ray-triangle intersection throughput, Mega Geometry support, Linear Swept Spheres for hair and strand rendering, and Shader Execution Reordering 2.0.

It is supported across NVIDIA ray tracing APIs and RTX GPUs starting with Turing. Linear Swept Spheres provide faster, lower-VRAM rendering for hair-like geometry than DOTS.

Blackwell includes an AI Management Processor for GPU context scheduling, new video and display capabilities including 4:2:2 encode/decode, ninth-generation NVENC, improved NVDEC, and DisplayPort 2.1b. Max-Q improvements include advanced power gating, accelerated frequency switching, and faster low-latency sleep.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving performance, stability, and image quality. The passage also describes neural shaders, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces.

The document outlines GB202, GB203, and GB205 GPU configurations and associated GeForce RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, and 5070 products, followed by NVIDIA legal, warranty, trademark, and copyright notices.

The passage argues that traders can make money in a bear market by sticking to a prepared trading plan, backtesting strategies across bull and bear markets, and trading both long and short positions. It defines a bear market as when the market is below its 200-day moving average, stating that since 1960 the S&P 500 has spent about 30% of its time in bear markets, which average 25 trading days and occur about twice a year by this mechanical measure.

The article emphasizes that investors often make cognitive mistakes, such as buying after strong gains and selling after declines. It recommends disciplined, rule-based trading and warns against reacting to fear or pessimistic news. For long-term investors, it advises continuing to invest during bear markets because lower prices can create buying opportunities.

The passage says short strategies often work better in volatile and falling markets, while some long strategies may also perform well during bear markets due to strong rallies. It presents backtested examples involving SPY and QQQ to support the view that robust strategies can outperform during bear markets and benefit from compounding by limiting losses.

For crypto, the passage notes that trend-following strategies have held up in some cases. Overall, it presents bear markets as opportunities rather than events to fear, provided traders use valid, backtested strategies and remain disciplined.

The passage criticizes celebrities who declined to perform at Donald Trump’s inauguration, calling their actions disrespectful and politically biased. Strength training can build muscle mass, strength and endurance, but poor technique, inadequate warm-up or cool-down, and progressing too quickly can increase injury risk. Common injuries include rotator cuff injuries, hamstring strains or tears, herniated discs, tendonitis, and tennis or golfer’s elbow. These may result from repetitive movements, sudden forceful motions, poor form, or lifting weights beyond current ability.

Prevention includes using correct technique, maintaining good posture, warming up properly, stretching gently, limiting forceful repetitions, working within personal limits, and increasing workout intensity gradually. Warm-ups raise heart rate and blood flow to prepare muscles, while cool-downs help regulate blood flow after exercise. Dynamic movements are recommended before strength training, while static stretches are more useful after a workout.

Pain should not be ignored or pushed through. Rest, hydration, good nutrition, ice, compression and elevation may help recovery. Persistent pain or suspected injury should be discussed with a doctor, and beginners may benefit from guidance from a qualified fitness instructor or personal trainer.

The passage describes UC1825B-SP converter design considerations and layout guidance. Output diode voltage stress is calculated as Vout + VinMAX, and the selected diode should be rated well above that value; a 60-V diode was chosen. In push-pull topology, primary MOSFETs can see about twice the input voltage plus ringing, so MOSFET voltage ratings should be about 2.5 to 3 times the input voltage. The output filter design used about 1145 µF capacitance, six ceramic capacitors before the filter, bulk tantalum capacitors with small ceramics, a 500-nH filter inductor, and a 0.5-Ω damping resistor. Type IIB compensation was selected with a 5-kHz crossover target, with compensation pole and zero placement adjusted during testing. The sense resistor monitors transformer ripple current and shuts down switching when peak current exceeds the limit, with the CS pin threshold around 1 V.

Test figures show MOSFET voltage stress, output voltage ripple, and full output voltage transient at 48-V input and 10-A load, including a 0-A to 10-A load step. The UC1825B-SP operates from a regulated 10-V to 30-V input supply, with added bulk capacitance recommended if the supply is more than a few inches away.

Layout guidance emphasizes low-EMI inductors, short and thick power traces, careful grounding, close placement of input/output capacitors and compensation components, separation of feedback traces from noisy power paths, and use of ground planes. VCC and VREF should be bypassed with high-frequency capacitors, and high di/dt power ground paths should be isolated from analog signal grounding. The passage also includes documentation, support, trademark, ESD, packaging, mechanical, and TI disclaimer information.

Human Rights Watch says Syrian refugees fleeing increased violence in north-west Syria are being shot at, beaten, detained, denied medical care and forced back by Turkish border guards. Witnesses reported children being shot and a woman sent back after giving birth. Turkey’s border is closed except for critical medical cases. The reports come amid escalating bombing in Idlib, Hama and Aleppo, with dozens of civilians killed, and continued attacks on Eastern Ghouta, where the UN has warned of severe malnutrition.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K dated May 13, 2019, reporting that it issued a press release announcing the final offer consideration for its exchange offer for all outstanding shares of Maxwell Technologies common stock. The filing also includes tax opinions from Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati and DLA Piper LLP related to the offer and subsequent merger, incorporated into Tesla’s Form S-4 registration statement. Exhibits include the two tax opinions and the press release.

New research published in Value in Health found that testing women at risk of hereditary breast cancer for variants in 7 cancer-associated genes, rather than only BRCA1/2, followed by risk-reduction management, could cost-effectively improve life expectancy. A decision-analytic model compared BRCA1/2 testing with a 7-gene strategy including TP53, PTEN, CDH1, STK11, and PALB2. For 50- and 40-year-old women, the 7-gene strategy met World Health Organization cost-effectiveness guidelines. Lead author Yonghong Li said expanded gene panels may identify additional inherited breast cancer risk beyond BRCA1/2.

Eric Robinson, 46, was arrested in Plantation and charged with first-degree murder for allegedly killing his roommate and attempting to hide the body in a dumpster near Nob Hill Road and Cleary Boulevard. Police have not released the victim’s name pending family notification. Neighbors said Robinson had a history of conflict with a woman living at the duplex, and police had been called there before. Robinson had recent arrests for domestic violence, strangulation, and cocaine possession.

Switching is central to the SOS Pressure Defense system, using automatic contact switching to reduce hesitation, deny passing lanes, disrupt screening offenses, force turnovers or rushed shots, and reduce fouls. The basic switching call is “Screen-Over-Switch”: the defender alerts the screen, hedges over to block the cutter’s path, and switches assignments with the teammate.

Off-ball switching attacks passing lanes and denies catches and quick shots. Down screens and back screens use contact switches followed by SNUGGLE pass-denial positioning, with emphasis on leaving no space between defenders and offensive players. Baseline screens use a Hi-Lo rule: defenders switch if the cutter goes baseline low, but do not switch if the cutter goes high over the screen.

On-ball switching differs by location. Above the free throw line extended, defenders aggressively contact switch to deny quick jump shots and middle penetration, then use SMOTHER and SNUGGLE positioning. Below the free throw line extended, defenders trap near the baseline or corner, rotate into Triangle I positioning, and close out to the nearest offensive players on a pass out of the trap.

Shop & Save Market signed a letter of intent to open a grocery store in the former Dominick’s at Jeffery Plaza in South Shore, the last vacant former Dominick’s in Chicago. Owner Cezary Jakubowski said the deal is not final, but the store could open in 18 to 24 months. Mayor Rahm Emanuel said more than $10 million in tax increment financing would support the project. Shop & Save hopes to buy the entire plaza, retain tenants and attract new ones, though remodeling the deteriorated space will require major construction.

The passage describes patent-related embodiments for storage systems and artificial intelligence infrastructure. It covers storage arrays, storage controllers, storage clusters, non-volatile solid-state storage, NVRAM buffering, direct-mapped flash storage, fast-write storage, erasure coding, mirroring, garbage collection, failover, authority-based data ownership, and distributed control across storage nodes.

The described systems include client devices connected to storage arrays via SAN or LAN, controllers that manage storage tasks, persistent storage resources made up of storage drives and NVRAM, and clustered storage nodes housed in chassis. Storage nodes may distribute data and metadata across multiple devices using erasure coding and redundant copies, allowing continued operation after failures and supporting proactive rebuilds.

The passage also describes storage cluster architecture with blades, authorities, control planes, compute planes, and storage planes. Authorities manage partitions of flash and NVRAM, handle client requests, migrate between blades, and support rebalancing when blades are added, removed, or fail. The system supports protocols and services such as NFS, CIFS/SMB, SCSI, HTTP, LDAP, IPv4, IPv6, audit logs, access controls, encryption key rotation, and multi-tenancy.

The passage further describes coupling storage systems to cloud service providers through data communication links. Cloud services may include infrastructure, platform, software, authentication, and storage services, and may be implemented as private, public, or hybrid cloud environments.

The passage describes power, reset, clocking, interrupt, timing, and peripheral features of a Texas Instruments device. SmartReflex modules reduce Core Logic Voltage Domain power consumption using DVFS and AVS concepts, though AVS is marked not supported. Each voltage domain supports selectable OPPs with defined frequency and voltage ranges, but not all OPP combinations are supported. SRAM blocks can enter shutdown mode to reduce leakage, and I/O groups support independently selectable 1.8 V or 3.3 V supplies, while DDR I/O supports 1.5 V or 1.8 V.

The device supports low-power standby, defined by switchable power domains off, ARM Cortex-A8 idle at lowest frequency, and unused blocks clock-gated. It requires defined power-up and power-down supply sequencing, PLL and analog supply filtering, and recommended decoupling capacitors. Multiple reset types are described, including POR, external warm reset, emulation warm reset, watchdog reset, software global cold/warm resets, test reset, local resets, PCIe reset isolation, and EMAC switch reset isolation. Reset behavior includes Hi-Z I/O states, RSTOUT_WD_OUT behavior, boot-mode latching, and ARM execution from Boot ROM after reset.

Clocking is generated from reference clocks, PLLs, dividers, and PRCM SYSCLKs. DEV and AUX clocks may come from crystals or 1.8 V LVCMOS inputs; SERDES requires a low-jitter differential clock for PCIe. The device includes top-level and embedded PLLs, bypass mode after reset, PLL supply filtering requirements, frequency limits, SYSCLK limits, and module clock limits. Interrupt handling is provided through the ARM Cortex-A8 AINTC and C674x DSP interrupt controller, with default and multiplexed event sources.

Peripheral sections cover timing and features for DCAN, EDMA, debug and trace, JTAG, EMAC switch, MDIO, GPIO, GPMC/ELM, NAND/NOR interfaces, and HDMI. EMAC supports two external Ethernet ports with MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII modes, plus MDIO management. GPIO provides up to 128 configurable pins with interrupt support. GPMC supports NOR, NAND, SRAM, pseudo-SRAM, and error handling through ELM. HDMI includes an HDMI 1.3a-compliant transmitter, TMDS routing guidelines, DDC I2C connections, optional CEC, and ESD/layout considerations.

Mediclinic’s shares rose after improved Middle East outlook. Its Swiss, southern African and Dubai operations met expectations, while Abu Dhabi faced regulatory challenges. Middle East revenue fell 8%, but improvement is expected.

Whitworth University will lower its annual tuition from $54,000 to $26,900 next fall and make merit-based discounts publicly tied to GPA. Officials say the change is meant to reduce sticker shock and provide clearer cost information, not address enrollment declines. The move reflects broader criticism of opaque tuition-discount models at private colleges. Researchers say tuition resets have mixed enrollment results but may increase interest among Pell-eligible students. Experts note that high prices can still signal quality, creating incentives for colleges to maintain inflated sticker prices despite widespread discounts. Whitworth leaders report positive feedback from families.

A study led by University of Guelph professor Nigel Raine found that exposure to the neonicotinoid pesticide thiamethoxam made bumblebee queens 26 per cent less likely to lay eggs and start new colonies. The research, published in Nature Ecology & Evolution, suggests this could increase the risk of population extinction. Raine’s lab tested queens exposed to a parasite, artificial hibernation, and pesticide-laden pollen at field-realistic levels; the parasite had little effect, but pesticide exposure significantly reduced egg laying. Raine said the findings may be conservative because the study examined only one pesticide and one parasite, while wild bees face additional pressures such as disease and habitat destruction.

Five English clubs—Manchester City, Manchester United, Liverpool, Tottenham and Chelsea—qualified for the Champions League last 16, the first time one country has had five teams at that stage. Chelsea, who finished second in their group, can face only PSG, Barcelona or Besiktas. The other English group winners could draw major opponents including Bayern Munich, Juventus or Real Madrid, though Tottenham cannot face Real after finishing above them. Basel, Sevilla, Shakhtar Donetsk and Porto are seen as kinder draws. PSG are bookmakers’ favourites. In the Europa League draw, seeded Arsenal could face Celtic but will avoid several group winners and top Champions League dropouts.

Tyler Denton was stabbed to death at her Rhyl home, Mold Crown Court heard. Prosecutor John Philpotts said her housemate, Redvers Bickley, attacked her after becoming enraged during a birthday gathering for Tyler’s partner, Hayley Barnett. He allegedly wounded Tyler’s sisters, Cody and Shannen, and their father, Paul, when they tried to escape or help. Shannen may have survived by pretending to be dead, while Cody helped hide Tyler in a bush. Paul Denton was also stabbed before he and Cody overpowered Bickley. Tyler died after a neck artery was cut, causing massive internal blood loss. Her father and sisters recovered from serious injuries. Bickley admits killing Tyler but denies murder and attempted murder. The trial continues.

STAT’s biotech roundup notes TCGX closing a $1.3 billion fund, upcoming FDA-supported studies of a Covid-19 antibody treatment, Datroway data in advanced triple-negative breast cancer, obefazimod data for ulcerative colitis, and Europe’s effort to finalize a major pharmaceutical policy overhaul aimed at improving medicine access while retaining drugmaker investment.

Tony Robinson has become patron of the John Cracknell Youth Enterprise Bank, which gives grants of up to £1,000 to young people in parts of Yorkshire. The bank has supported more than 400 young people and is linked to the Hull Youth Enterprise Partnership.

Texas Monthly’s article describes Enron’s rise from a troubled pipeline company into a dominant energy-trading firm under Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling, driven by deregulation, the Gas Bank model, aggressive recruiting, merit-based pay, and a high-pressure culture focused on rapid profits and innovation. It says Enron expanded into electricity, commodities, broadband, and international projects while relying heavily on mark-to-market accounting and hard-nosed dealmaking. By 2001, the company faced falling stock, criticism over California’s energy crisis, problems with its India power plant and broadband ventures, scrutiny of accounting practices, and internal morale issues. Skilling resigned after six months as CEO, citing personal reasons, while Lay returned and promised a renewed focus closer to Enron’s core business.

Coach DeBoer said his team improved defensively, maintained belief despite close losses, and understands momentum can shift quickly. He emphasized staying with the current lineup, praised Pavelski’s leadership and impact, noted confidence on the road, and said the team is prepared for a difficult effort to extend the series.

An engineering graduate, Ankit of Dhakoli village, allegedly killed Sheelu, 23, and her cousin Shivani at their home in Bahpur village after Sheelu rejected his marriage proposal. Police said he strangled Sheelu, killed Shivani with a motorcycle clutch wire after she witnessed it, burned the bodies, and later admitted to the killings.

The passage describes the David Swensen Portfolio, or Yale Model, developed by David Swensen and Dean Takahashi for the Yale endowment. It emphasizes broad diversification across stocks, bonds, and alternative investments such as private equity, real estate, hedge funds, and natural resources, along with low-cost index funds, passive strategies, and risk management. Swensen transformed Yale’s endowment from a traditional 60/40 portfolio into a highly successful fund, with annualized returns of 12.5% from 1985 to 2020 versus 9.7% for the S&P 500.

The passage notes that the portfolio’s allocation can be implemented with ETFs and adjusted to investor goals and risk tolerance. A backtest using selected ETFs produced annual returns of 6.23%, underperforming the S&P 500 due to bond exposure and weak emerging markets, though with lower drawdowns. It concludes that the Yale Model is not suitable for everyone and investors should consider their goals, risk tolerance, and possibly consult a financial advisor.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture and its improvements over Tesla V100. A100 has 108 SMs and 432 Tensor Cores, delivering up to 312 TFLOPS dense mixed-precision FP16/FP32 performance, 2.5x V100 mixed-precision Tensor Core performance, and 20x V100 standard FP32 throughput. Its Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, INT4, binary, TF32, BF16, and FP64. TF32 is used by default for AI training without script changes, while FP16 or BF16 mixed precision offers higher throughput.

A100 accelerates HPC workloads with FP64 Tensor Core support, reaching 19.5 TFLOPS peak FP64 throughput, 2.5x Tesla V100. In mixed-precision iterative refinement using cuSOLVER TCAIRS, TF32 showed the strongest convergence and geomean speedup among tested Tensor Core modes. The architecture introduces 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity, which compresses weights, reduces bandwidth, and doubles Tensor Core throughput for supported sparse operations with minimal reported inference accuracy loss after pruning and fine-tuning.

The GPU includes a combined L1/shared memory subsystem of 192 KB per SM, separate FP32 and INT32 cores for simultaneous execution, 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/s bandwidth, SECDED ECC protection, and a 40 MB L2 cache, 6.7x larger than V100. L2 improvements include higher bandwidth, residency controls, and compute data compression.

A100 adds Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), allowing one GPU to be partitioned into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory bandwidth, and fault isolation. It supports cloud, multi-tenant, single-user, and multi-user use cases, and can combine with MPS. The architecture also includes third-generation NVLink with 600 GB/s total GPU bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, improved error handling, NVJPG JPEG decode, optical flow acceleration, improved atomics, and five NVDEC units.

CUDA 11 supports A100 features including Tensor Cores, sparsity, MIG, CUDA Graphs, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency control, and Cooperative Groups enhancements. DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs, NVLink, NVSwitch, Mellanox networking, MIG, and NVIDIA software containers to support scalable AI, HPC, analytics, and inference workloads.

The study develops TOPIC (TOpology-constrained Prediction of Inorganic Crystals), a crystal structure prediction algorithm for lithium oxide solid-state electrolytes with fully connected oxygen corner-sharing frameworks. The method reduces the configurational search space by enforcing corner-sharing bond topology constraints, using machine-learning interatomic potentials for structure optimization and DFT for final energy validation.

TOPIC is validated by reproducing known oxide structures, including systems with up to 192 atoms per unit cell such as cubic Li7La3Zr2O12, as well as LiTi2(PO4)3, LiGa(SeO3)2, LiTa2PO8, LiAlSiO4 polymorphs, and others. It also identifies low-energy or metastable structures not previously reported, including a LiTaSiO5 structure lower in energy than the reported phase and a metastable LiTa2PO8 polymorph with higher predicted conductivity.

The study screens quaternary lithium oxide compositions built from octahedral and tetrahedral units. It finds that the lithium ratio, defined as the number of Li atoms divided by the number of non-Li metal atoms, correlates with the stability of corner-sharing frameworks: lower Li ratios generally favor corner-sharing structures, while higher Li contents tend to favor non-corner-sharing frameworks. Corner-sharing structures also show much higher predicted ionic conductivity than non-corner-sharing structures.

A comprehensive screening identifies 92 candidate materials with predicted room-temperature ionic conductivity above 0.1 mS cm−1. DFT-based molecular dynamics further validates 15 low-energy candidates, many containing Si and several containing Hf. Notable candidates include Li4Hf2Si3O12, predicted to have an ionic conductivity of 14.09 mS cm−1 and a 6.5 eV band gap. Several candidates share known framework types such as NASICON, while others exhibit novel structural prototypes.

The analysis shows that increasing Li content can reduce activation barriers in several shared frameworks, though some structures deviate from this trend due to changes in conduction pathways. Hf doping in Li2Ta2SiO8 is shown to reduce activation energy and convert quasi-one-dimensional Li conduction into a three-dimensional network. The study concludes that TOPIC enables efficient exploration of complex oxide electrolyte chemical spaces and provides design guidance for next-generation solid-state electrolytes.

A prospective single-center study of 157 patients hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure evaluated bioimpedance spectroscopy (BIS) for assessing fluid overload and predicting outcomes. BIS measured overhydration (OH) and OH/extracellular water (OH/ECW) at admission and discharge, with analyses stratified by chronic kidney disease (CKD) and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). CKD patients had higher fluid overload measures, and HFrEF patients showed greater OH/ECW reduction during hospitalization. During 10.7 ± 7.1 months of follow-up, OH, OH/ECW, and their changes did not significantly predict major adverse cardiovascular events or heart failure hospitalization in any subgroup. The study concluded that BIS can monitor fluid status in ADHF, especially in HFrEF, but its prognostic value in CKD and HFpEF remains limited and requires further study.

NVIDIA filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 30, 2017. Second-quarter revenue was $2.23 billion, up from $1.43 billion a year earlier, with net income of $583 million versus $261 million. Diluted earnings per share were $0.92, compared with $0.41. For the first half of fiscal 2018, revenue was $4.17 billion and net income was $1.09 billion.

GPU segment revenue was $1.90 billion in the quarter, driven by gaming, datacenter, professional visualization, and PC OEM sales, including cryptocurrency mining demand. Tegra Processor revenue was $333 million, supported by gaming platforms, services, and automotive products. The Intel patent license agreement ended in the first quarter of fiscal 2018.

Gross margin was 58.4% for the quarter. Operating expenses rose to $614 million, mainly due to higher headcount, compensation, and growth initiatives in gaming, artificial intelligence, and autonomous driving. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $5.88 billion at July 30, 2017. During the first half of fiscal 2018, NVIDIA repurchased $758 million of common stock and paid $166 million in dividends.

After Ontario recognized an 18th-century treaty in 2013 affirming Haudenosaunee hunting rights, Six Nations hunters began a regulated six-day annual deer harvest in Short Hills Provincial Park with government support. The harvest is viewed by participants as cultural renewal, reconciliation, a source of traditional food, and an ecological measure in an overpopulated deer area. Protesters, including Animal Alliance of Canada, oppose hunting in the park and have confronted hunters, prompting accusations that the protests target Indigenous culture, especially because other regional hunts are not similarly opposed. Hunters and supporters say the harvest provides venison for ceremonies, elders, families and longhouses, supports nutrition amid high diabetes and obesity rates, and helps pass on traditions to younger generations. Ministry staff monitor deer, while police have investigated vandalism and other incidents around the park.

The lecture contrasts wireline channels, modeled mainly as additive white Gaussian noise, with wireless channels, where fading arises from physical propagation effects. In free space, far-field electric and magnetic fields decay as \(1/r\), include propagation delay \(r/c\), and are affected by transmitting and receiving antenna patterns. With fixed antennas and free space, the channel behaves like a linear time-invariant system similar to wireline communication.

When a receiving antenna moves, the received signal experiences Doppler shift because propagation delay changes over time. A single Doppler shift is usually not a serious communication problem because receiver frequency recovery can track it. The more difficult problem is multipath fading, where multiple paths have different Doppler shifts and delays. In an example with a reflecting wall, direct and reflected paths create beats, causing periodic fast fading at the Doppler-related frequency. This can produce intervals with little received energy.

Other propagation situations, such as reflections from roads or partially absorbing walls, create different attenuation laws and delays. Because real wireless environments involve many complex paths, exact electromagnetic modeling is impractical for detection, though it can help with base-station placement and understanding general phenomena.

The lecture introduces a ray-tracing channel model in which each path has a time-varying attenuation and propagation delay. The channel system function is a sum of these path contributions. Since the wireless channel is linear but time-varying, standard linear time-invariant Fourier methods do not directly apply; a sinusoidal input can produce multiple shifted frequency components. Instead, the output can be represented through time-varying convolution, where the impulse response changes slowly with time.

For narrowband communication and baseband modeling, the passband channel is shifted down to baseband. Doppler effects appear as time-varying phase terms. With frequency recovery, the receiver tracks an average Doppler shift, leaving residual variations determined by the spread among path Doppler shifts. This Doppler spread determines how long the channel appears approximately time-invariant and how often channel measurements must be updated.

BrainWorking Recursive Therapy has arrived in Dunstable to help Bedfordshire residents with anxiety-related conditions. The treatment uses neuroscience techniques to change reactions to triggers. Advanced practitioner Keith Tunstall offers free initial consultations, confidential appointments, and sessions via Skype or FaceTime from High Street South.

The speaker said the game was more defensive and realistic than the previous one, but two quick goals hurt their momentum. They felt the team played well in the third period, remains confident, and looks forward to returning home, where they have played well. The speaker also mentioned learning from their first professional goalie coach.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2020. Net sales increased to $75.45 billion from $59.70 billion in Q1 2019, while net income decreased to $2.54 billion from $3.56 billion. Operating income decreased to $3.99 billion from $4.42 billion. North America net sales were $46.13 billion, International net sales were $19.11 billion, and AWS net sales were $10.22 billion. AWS operating income rose to $3.08 billion, while North America operating income fell to $1.31 billion and International operating loss increased to $398 million. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $49.29 billion at March 31, 2020. The company reported COVID-19 impacts including increased demand for essential products, reduced demand for discretionary products, supply chain interruptions, higher fulfillment and shipping costs, and increased allowances for doubtful accounts. Amazon had 498,776,032 common shares outstanding as of April 22, 2020.

Sterling Bank Plc increased loans and advances by 27% to N598.1 billion in 2017, despite many banks reducing exposure due to rising defaults. Gross earnings rose 19.8% to N133.5 billion, driven by growth in interest and non-interest income. Non-interest income increased 87.8% to N23.2 billion, profit before tax rose to N8.606 billion, and profit after tax grew to N8.521 billion. Customer deposits rose 17.1% to N684.8 billion, shareholders’ funds increased 20.2% to N102.9 billion, and total assets reached N1.1 trillion.

The bank’s non-performing loan ratio improved to 6.2% from 9.9%, while capital adequacy rose to 12.2%. The oil and gas sector received the largest share of loans at N251.59 billion, followed by real estate and agriculture.

Managing Director Abubakar Suleiman attributed the results to institutional strength, growth in non-interest banking, prudent loan management, retail expansion, and digital transformation, including the launch of the Specta online lending platform. He said the bank would focus on agility, digitisation, and business specialisation, with emphasis on health, education, agriculture, renewable energy, and transportation.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on December 1, 2022, it closed the sale of five series of notes totaling $8.25 billion in principal amount, due from 2024 through 2032. The aggregate public offering price was $8.246 billion, with estimated net proceeds of approximately $8.235 billion before offering expenses. The notes were issued under a prior indenture and related supplemental documents. The filing also lists related exhibits, including the underwriting agreement, officers’ certificate, note forms, and legal opinion.

The author evaluated Neo Performance Materials as a potential investment because the growth of electric vehicles could increase demand for rare earths, especially neodymium used in permanent magnet motors. Neo’s Magnequench business, which produces rare earth magnetic powders, accounted for 46.7% of 2017 revenue and 72.8% of EBITDA, aligning with this thesis. The company also appeared cheaply valued at 6.1x EV/EBITDA.

However, due diligence found a major risk: Magnequench’s dominant position depends on intellectual property, and two patents covering the majority of its products expired in December 2017. This could allow competitors to produce similar products without compensation, potentially affecting revenues and earnings as early as 2018. Although Neo may have other protections or new products, the author considers the risk too significant to take a position.

European spot electricity prices for Monday delivery rose on forecasts of slower wind speeds reducing renewable generation, while demand in Germany and France stayed broadly flat. French and German baseload power both reached 36 euros/MWh. German wind output was expected to fall sharply, while French nuclear availability remained stable. Forward prices were mixed, with German year-ahead flat and French higher. Coal prices rose, while oil, gas and carbon weakened. Czech day-ahead power also rose to 36 euros/MWh.

NASA is requiring employees working on Artemis missions with SpaceX and Blue Origin to continue during the U.S. government shutdown, unpaid until funding resumes. NASA plans to furlough about 15,000 workers while keeping about 3,000 working. Shutdown-supported work includes Artemis operations, the International Space Station and operational satellite missions. SpaceX and Blue Origin have Artemis lunar lander contracts, though neither has finalized its design.

Staff at the Prestwick Budgens face uncertainty after owner Food Retail Operations Ltd entered administration, affecting nearly 900 employees nationwide. Administrators PwC said all 34 stores will continue trading while buyers are sought. Around 27 Prestwick staff are affected, with Co-Op offering possible support if no buyer is found.
A player is praised for his skating, size, skill, work ethic, leadership, and increased goal scoring, with opponents noting he is difficult to play against and requires careful, physical defending.

U.S. gasoline demand reached a March record of 9.6 million b/d, contributing to lower inventories and a national average gas price of $2.55, up two cents from last week and month and 26 cents from last year. Michigan, Ohio and Illinois saw the largest monthly increases, while Hawaii and California had the highest prices. South and Southeast prices rose but remained among the nation’s cheapest. Inventories fell but stayed above 85 million bbl.

The passage argues that civil liberties and academic freedom on Canadian campuses have declined, citing demands for safe zones, trigger warnings, and opposition to controversial speakers. It discusses Lindsay Shepherd’s case at Wilfrid Laurier University, where she was criticized for showing a video of Jordan Peterson and later received an apology after public backlash. The author connects campus political correctness to workplaces and HR practices, claiming harassment investigations often exceed legal requirements. The passage states that not every negative workplace encounter is harassment, performance management and appropriate discipline are not harassment, and stress leave is only required when stress becomes a medically recognized disabling condition.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2015 reports revenue of $23.8 billion, down from $26.5 billion a year earlier, net income of $5.0 billion, down from $5.9 billion, and diluted earnings per share of $0.62, down from $0.71. For the six months ended December 31, 2015, revenue was $44.2 billion, net income was $9.6 billion, and diluted EPS was $1.20.

Total assets were $180.1 billion as of December 31, 2015, compared with $176.2 billion as of June 30, 2015. Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $102.6 billion. Total liabilities were $103.3 billion, including $40.7 billion in long-term debt, and stockholders’ equity was $76.8 billion.

Revenue declined primarily due to Windows 10 revenue deferrals and unfavorable foreign currency effects. Microsoft reported three segments beginning fiscal 2016: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. For the quarter, segment revenue was $6.7 billion, $6.3 billion, and $12.7 billion, respectively, while Corporate and Other reduced revenue by $1.9 billion, mainly due to Windows 10 and Halo 5 revenue deferrals.

Operating income was $6.0 billion for the quarter, down from $7.8 billion. Gross margin declined to $13.9 billion. Cost of revenue, sales and marketing, and general and administrative expenses decreased, while research and development was largely unchanged. The effective tax rate was 15%, down from 25% a year earlier.

Net cash from operations was $5.6 billion for the quarter and $14.2 billion for the six-month period. Microsoft repurchased $3.6 billion of common stock during the quarter and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.36 per share. The company also issued $13.0 billion of debt securities in November 2015.

Microsoft disclosed ongoing legal matters involving patents, intellectual property, antitrust and unfair competition claims, copyright levies, and product-related litigation. As of December 31, 2015, it had accrued $560 million in aggregate legal liabilities and stated that additional adverse outcomes of about $1.5 billion beyond recorded amounts were reasonably possible.

The speaker said their team ran out of energy as the series continued and was beaten by a great Tampa team. They cited injuries to Donovan’s MCL and Robyn’s ankle, praised the officiating, congratulated Tampa, and expressed pride in their players.

Aftab, a Kashmiri student, said 15-20 people assaulted him and a friend after they left a mosque in Mahenderhgarh. Haryana Police lodged an FIR, while Jammu and Kashmir Police said an officer was in contact with the students. Mehbooba Mufti urged action and a probe.

The speaker said the team’s defense fell short of its playoff standard, with mistakes and penalties allowing skilled opponents to capitalize. They noted some early chances were missed, while the goalie played well despite limited recent action and received insufficient support.

The Nigerian Immigration Service told a Federal High Court in Abuja that suspended Supreme Court justice Sylvester Ngwuta used two similar standard international passports interchangeably, which it said violated immigration law. Witness Tanko Kutana said the service issued a replacement after Ngwuta submitted an affidavit claiming the first was missing, but he failed to return the recovered passport. Kutana said four diplomatic and two standard passports were found with Ngwuta, and forensic analysis found no evidence of forgery. Justice John Tsoho adjourned the trial until October 20.

The Tri State Psychology Conference, founded by Marshall University students and faculty in 1993, will mark its 25th anniversary on April 20 at West Liberty University. Created to give psychology students professional conference experience, it has grown from a local event to a regional conference hosted by multiple schools.

The lecture continues the study of folding polygons into convex polyhedra using boundary gluings and gluing trees. A cube folded from a cross is used to illustrate an Alexandroff gluing and its corresponding gluing tree.

The main topics are combinatorial bounds and algorithms for general gluings, edge-to-edge gluings, and polygons of bounded sharpness. General and edge-to-edge gluings can have exponentially many combinatorial types, with upper and lower bounds of \(2^{\Theta(n)}\). For bounded sharpness polygons, where reflex angles are bounded away from 360 degrees by a constant, the number of gluings is polynomial. The decision problem for general gluings remains open for polynomial time; the best known algorithm is exponential.

To make the number of gluings finite, the lecture defines combinatorial types of gluings: an abstract gluing tree plus labels indicating which polygon vertices or edges occur at junctions. An exponential upper bound is proved by bounding the number of leaves and nodes in such trees. An exponential lower bound is shown using a spiky star polygon with many possible edge-to-edge gluings.

For bounded sharpness polygons, each leaf of the gluing tree has at least constant curvature, so the number of leaves is bounded by a constant. This leads to polynomial bounds on the number of combinatorially distinct gluings.

The lecture then presents dynamic programming algorithms. For edge-to-edge gluings, subproblems are boundary chains between two vertices. Enumerating all gluings takes exponential time, while deciding whether any valid edge-to-edge gluing exists can be done in polynomial time by storing only a gluing that minimizes the angle glued at each subproblem endpoint. The resulting decision algorithm runs in cubic time.

For arbitrary gluings, the algorithm is generalized using subproblems involving vertices glued to vertices or edges, with cases called “zip” and “tug.” This gives an exponential-time enumeration algorithm, and for bounded sharpness polygons it becomes polynomial because only polynomially many gluings must be considered.

The lecture concludes with examples produced by implemented algorithms, including all gluings of the Latin cross. The cross has 85 gluings but only 23 distinct polyhedra. Other examples include gluings of an equilateral triangle and a square, including rolling belts and polyhedra such as tetrahedra, octahedra, and flat doubly covered polygons.

NES Global Talent seeks a Performance Specialist for a six-month onshore contract in Aberdeen with a global operator. The role covers PSCM Functional Performance Management, Risk & Assurance, planning, performance reporting, compliance, and insights for leadership. Candidates need finance, accounting, procurement knowledge, strong analytical and communication skills, Excel expertise, and relevant qualifications.

Guests should execute HLT with interrupts disabled and, after resuming, examine interrupt state as if receiving #HV. Doorbell pages are configured through GHCB VMGEXIT requests, including preferred address, set, and query actions. Hosts should emulate APIC interrupt presentation semantics, write pending vectors or non-maskable events into the doorbell page, manage #HV signaling, track acknowledgements, and handle EOI through NoEoiRequired or APIC writes. Guests receiving #HV must atomically exchange pending event fields before acting, validate vectors, handle non-maskable events even when interrupts are disabled, and complete EOI using NoEoiRequired or an APIC register write. Non-cooperative host or guest behavior may cause lost notifications or denial of service but should not compromise host integrity.

The Texas Rangers’ manager search is centered on internal candidate Skip Schumaker, a special adviser under contract through October. President Chris Young said the team has begun a formal process but has not pursued external candidates. Schumaker was the 2023 NL Manager of the Year with Miami. Bruce Bochy and Texas agreed to end his managerial stint after an 81-81 season, and he has been offered an advisory role.

BCHL Today’s March 19, 2018 edition recaps playoff action. Vernon beat Wenatchee 3-1 to take a 2-0 series lead, with Ty Taylor improving to a 1.65 goals-against average and .942 save percentage. Penticton defeated Trail 7-2, also going up 2-0, powered by five power-play goals. Powell River edged Victoria 3-2 for a 2-0 lead, with Matteo Paler-Chow making 40 saves. Surrey rebounded from a game-one loss to beat Prince George 3-2 and tie their series 1-1 behind Mario Cavaliere’s 46-save performance. Surrey’s Jackson Ross committed to NCAA Division I Colorado College, becoming the sixth Eagles player this season to earn a scholarship.

Martin Braithwaite left Middlesbrough for Bordeaux in January, seemingly to improve his chances of playing regularly and securing a place in Denmark’s World Cup squad. The article argues the decision is understandable but disappointing, suggesting he might have earned a place under Tony Pulis and helped Boro push for promotion. It notes Viktor Fischer as a rival for Braithwaite’s Denmark spot and says the move will be judged by whether he reaches and performs at Russia 2018. Meanwhile, Middlesbrough must try to build momentum, reach the play-offs and potentially return to the Premier League without him.

Russia’s foreign ministry said U.S. missile defense deployments in Romania and planned systems in Poland violate the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Force Treaty, calling them a “gross violation” of obligations.

The passage discusses whether LLMs can help social scientists generate novel hypotheses or theories, noting concerns about originality, validity, falsifiability, oversimplification, and the need for human-AI collaboration. It then addresses AI governance, arguing that rapid generative AI development creates legal and ethical risks including misinformation, deepfakes, bias, discrimination, and regulatory uncertainty. Existing efforts by governments and companies aim to align AI with rights, inclusiveness, safety, transparency, and accountability, but gaps remain between industry and government, across national regulations, and in identifying risks during real-world use. The passage calls for forward-looking, human-centered governance through partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers, combined with bottom-up reporting by developers, users, and communities, transparent handling of issues, and mechanisms to update regulations promptly. It also includes references and acknowledgments for contributors to the whitepaper.

ASTROCO is a conformer-style encoder for astronomical time series that combines global self-attention, local depthwise convolutions, and gating to improve masked-reconstruction learning of stellar light curves. It addresses limitations of prior Astromer transformer models, which treat time steps equally and lack mechanisms to control noisy or distant measurements. Inputs combine magnitudes, uncertainties, and sinusoidal time embeddings through learned projection, and pretraining uses BERT-style masked reconstruction over 50% of positions. Each encoder block includes multi-head self-attention, a GLU-based convolutional sublayer, and a gated feed-forward network with residuals and normalization. Sequence embeddings are formed by trainable softmax mixing of features from all layers followed by masked mean pooling. On the MACHO R-band dataset, ASTROCO-S and ASTROCO-L achieve lower reconstruction error and higher macro-F1 classification scores than Astromer v1/v2, with the smaller model using fewer resources and the larger model setting the strongest benchmark.

Las Vegas Valley residents filing last-minute 2016 tax returns had until 10 p.m. Tuesday to get them postmarked. The Postal Service advised using sufficient postage, clear addresses, sealed envelopes and saving mailing or delivery receipts.

The Carlsberg UK Northamptonshire Food and Drink Awards 2017/18 announced its winners at Northampton’s Royal & Derngate on November 15, celebrating local produce, drink, dining venues and culinary workers. The event opened with a toast to Antonio Carluccio OBE, who had died the previous week, led by William Sitwell. Eat Out Eat Well gold venues were also recognised. The Hopping Hare in Northampton won Booker Food Pub of the Year, while its chef Arturs Dzerins was runner-up for Booker Young Chef of the Year. Other winners included Workbridge Coffee Shop, The Exotic Dining, The Folly, Richard Walker, Victoria Austin, The Dukes Arms, Steve Reid of Friars Farm, Tom Warner and Christina Warner-Keogh, and Alaric Neville.

The speaker said the team played a solid game but had brief breakdowns that led to quick goals. They felt confident despite the loss, noting they had chances but couldn’t finish, and emphasized needing a full effort against a strong defensive team that capitalizes on mistakes.

The speaker said his team played poorly against Anaheim, with turnovers, weak puck movement, defensive coverage breakdowns, and trouble handling Anaheim’s physical forecheck. He said the game was still winnable until late and expects the team to improve, making the series competitive. He cited the winning goal as an example of lost coverage and said Jason Spezza’s play must improve after a difficult game.

He said Anaheim’s physical play came from strong dump-ins, aggressive forechecking, and net-front pressure, and that his team must adjust by holding up forecheckers better and supporting defensemen more effectively. He expressed uncertainty about how obstruction and extra contact were being officiated and planned to speak with the series supervisor.

The speaker discussed Anaheim players Ryan Getzlaf, Corey Perry, Chris Kunitz, and Miller, recalling how his organization valued them in the draft and acquisitions. He praised their competitiveness and long-term value.

He said he chose not to break up his forward lines during the game despite struggles, wanting to give them time against Anaheim’s strong checking line and defense pairings. He also mentioned advice from Scotty Bowman about line combinations. The team needs its best players to find success, draw penalties, and compete better.

He criticized the team’s failed five-on-three power play, saying they did not shoot enough and wasted time. He also said the team must be more responsible in its own end, with centers offering better support. He compared Anaheim’s forecheck to Buffalo’s but said Anaheim finishes checks much harder.

Girlfriends’ Kenna McNeil said the shop is preparing flowers, corsages, tux orders and accessories for Liberal High School’s April 22 prom and other area proms. Staff began around March 1 to allow time for flower shipments and custom selections. The shop has received close to 100 orders, with a recent rush of 20 to 30 tux and corsage orders. McNeil said staff help students choose flowers, ribbons, stones and other details, aiming to make each order unique and beautiful.

The passage outlines defensive approaches to counter the Triangle Offense. Basic NBA defense emphasizes packing the lane, denying inside options, forcing perimeter shots, and using show-and-recover tactics against cuts, post feeds, screens, and weakside actions. Defenders pressure the ball, deny passes, collapse into help positions, contest post play, and close out on shooters.

SOS disruption is a more aggressive strategy designed to interrupt the offense’s initial flow by extending pressure, lengthening passing lanes, forcing the offense away from preferred areas, denying cuts, fronting the post, switching, and disrupting weakside actions.

All Out SOS Disruption initiates pressure on the first pass by trapping the wing before the offense can run its cuts or passes, forcing players into freelance play. Rotations then cover skip passes, corner passes, baseline drives, and post feeds, with defenders moving into help, denial, trap, and fronting positions according to SOS rules.

Scores of fishermen clashed with police in central Vietnam while attempting to file lawsuits seeking compensation from Taiwanese firm Formosa after a toxic waste dump killed tonnes of fish in 2016. Activists and witnesses said some protesters were beaten, hospitalized, or briefly detained. Formosa paid Vietnam’s government $500 million, but the fishermen said they had not received compensation. Previous lawsuits by fishermen were dismissed.

The paper overviews twelve shared tasks organized within NFDI4DS, a German consortium supporting FAIR, transparent, and reproducible research data infrastructure for data science and AI. Shared tasks are presented as community mechanisms for benchmarking methods, producing reusable resources, and fostering interdisciplinary collaboration.

Seven completed tasks are described: SOMD 2025 on software mention and attribute extraction from scholarly articles; SciVQA on visual question answering over scientific figures; ClimateCheck on linking climate-related social media claims to scholarly evidence and classifying support relations; FoRC2025 on field-of-research classification for ACL Anthology papers; LLMs4Subjects@SemEval-2025 on bilingual subject tagging for technical library records; LLMs4OL-2024 on ontology learning with large language models; and Scholarly QALD on question answering over scholarly knowledge graphs.

One ongoing task, CheckThat!Lab Task 4, addresses scientific web discourse by detecting science-related claims and references in tweets and retrieving source papers for implicit scientific claims.

Four tasks under development are outlined: detecting dataset and machine-learning model mentions in scholarly articles; ReadMe2KG, extracting and linking entities from GitHub README files to the NFDI4DS knowledge graph; CURED, evaluating clinical prognosis models with calibrated uncertainty estimates; and Algorithm2Domain, supporting benchmarking of algorithm generalisability and domain adaptation.

The paper concludes that these shared tasks contribute to NFDI4DS and the broader NFDI mission by advancing methods and infrastructure for sustainable, interoperable research data practices.

Digital leaders use relevant data and detailed metrics to set ambitious goals, track progress, and evaluate performance. Data-driven measurement supports objective feedback, adaptability, autonomy, experimentation, innovation, and risk-taking rather than rigid control.

Hollywood’s summer movie season opens early with “Avengers: Infinity War,” as the industry seeks to recover from a box office decline and a weak previous summer. Major franchise releases include “Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom,” “Deadpool 2,” “Solo,” “The Incredibles 2,” “Ant-Man and the Wasp” and “Mission: Impossible — Fallout.” Analysts note that while tent-pole films remain top earners, oversaturation can increase competition for the same audience dollars. Studios are also emphasizing varied slates, including comedies, action films, documentaries, female-led reboots and independent releases. Executives say year-round scheduling and diverse offerings are increasingly important as audiences become more selective and competition from services like Netflix grows. The season also includes unconventional films such as “Hereditary,” “Eighth Grade,” “Blindspotting,” “Sorry to Bother You,” “The Happytime Murders” and “Hotel Artemis,” whose director said audiences want films with more personality and less formula.

The Colchester-Milton Rotary Club volunteered May 17 to plant saplings at Pine Island Farm along the Winooski River as part of an Intervale Center restoration project building on a 2014 planting. Volunteers from Dealer.com and Vermont Gas also participated, with guidance from the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and Intervale staff. The saplings are intended to reduce greenhouse gases and erosion. The effort responds to Rotary International president Ian H.S. Riseley’s challenge to plant one tree per Rotary member during the Rotary year. The local club, with 45 members, had also planted five larger trees earlier in 2018 at Porters Point School and hopes to continue similar projects in Milton.

Motley Fool Money reviews the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card, highlighting unlimited 2% cash rewards on purchases, a $200 bonus after spending $500 in the first 3 months, 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, no annual fee, and up to $600 cell phone protection. Recommended credit is Good/Excellent (670–850), though approval is not guaranteed. The passage also lists alternative cards, including Capital One Quicksilver and Citi Double Cash, and notes Motley Fool’s compensation and advertising relationships.
