Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer.

Wall Street stocks gave up early gains Thursday as rising bond yields and a technology pullback weighed on markets ahead of major earnings. The Fed held rates steady but signaled concern about inflation, while labor market and factory price data added to inflation worries. The Dow rose 0.14%, the S&P 500 slipped 0.06%, and the Nasdaq fell 0.35%. Financials gained as banks benefited from higher rates. eBay jumped after earnings and a payments shift away from PayPal, whose shares fell, while UPS dropped after higher shipping costs hurt profit. S&P 500 earnings growth estimates rose to 14.9%, with most reporting companies beating expectations. Amazon rose after hours, while Alphabet and Apple declined after results.

This study examines global ranking trends of higher education institutions (HEIs) in selected Asian countries using Times Higher Education World University Rankings data from 2015 to 2025. The literature shows extensive research on ranking systems and selected Asian HEIs, but limited longitudinal research comparing ranking positions across Asian regions.

Using a qualitative multiple case study design and document analysis, the study reviewed the top five HEIs from ten populous Asian countries: Bangladesh, China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Pakistan, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, and the Russian Federation. Data were collected from publicly available THE rankings, and external evaluators reviewed the analyses to support validity.

Findings show that Chinese and Japanese HEIs performed most strongly. Chinese universities, especially Tsinghua University and Peking University, showed consistent improvement and ranked among the global top 100. Japanese HEIs also maintained strong positions, with the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University consistently ranking highly. Russian HEIs generally showed stable and positive performance, with Lomonosov Moscow State University remaining among the top 200.

Indian HEIs showed improvement, though they remained below the top global rankings. Indonesian, Pakistani, Philippine, Thai, Vietnamese, and Bangladeshi HEIs generally showed inconsistent, neutral, or declining ranking patterns. Bangladesh HEIs appeared only in recent rankings, limiting trend analysis. Vietnamese HEIs showed a clearer downward trend after entering the rankings.

The study concludes that, except for China, Japan, and Russia, most selected Asian HEIs lag behind international competitors and lack stable positive ranking patterns. It recommends stronger globalization efforts, improved marketing, expanded funding, international offices, and supportive government policies to increase the global visibility and competitiveness of Asian HEIs.

NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture targets HPC, AI, and data center workloads with major improvements over Tesla V100. A100 Tensor Cores accelerate IEEE-compliant FP64 computations, delivering up to 19.5 TFLOPS peak FP64 throughput, 2.5x V100. Mixed-precision Tensor Cores support HPC iterative refinement solvers through cuSOLVER, with TF32 showing the most robust results among tested Tensor Core modes and up to 4x speedups for large matrices.

A100 introduces fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity, allowing trained neural network weights to be pruned and compressed for a 2x reduction in data footprint and bandwidth while Sparse Tensor Cores skip zero values to double math throughput. NVIDIA describes a dense-training, structured-pruning, and fine-tuning workflow that showed virtually no inference accuracy loss across evaluated networks.

The architecture improves memory and execution resources with 192 KB/SM combined L1 cache and shared memory, simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, 40 GB HBM2 memory delivering 1555 GB/s bandwidth, SECDED ECC protection, and a 40 MB L2 cache that is 6.7x larger than V100’s. A100 also adds L2 residency controls and Compute Data Compression, which can improve DRAM bandwidth, L2 bandwidth, and L2 capacity.

For deep learning, A100 includes third-generation Tensor Cores, more SMs than V100, larger Tensor operations, improved data sharing, asynchronous copy instructions, asynchronous barriers, expanded shared memory allocation, and higher L2 and DRAM bandwidth. CUDA 11 supports these features along with Tensor Core formats, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, L2 cache controls, cooperative groups, and related programming advances.

A100’s Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can partition one GPU into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory resources, enabling predictable throughput, latency, fault isolation, and quality of service for multiple users, VMs, containers, or processes. MIG supports configurations with GPU slices, Compute Instances, Sys Pipes, isolated L2 slices, frame buffer memory, and migration of vGPU state between compatible instances.

Connectivity and system features include third-generation NVLink with 12 links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth per A100, NVSwitch support, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, improved error and fault detection, NVJPG hardware JPEG decode, Optical Flow Accelerator support, higher atomic operation throughput, and five NVDEC units. DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with NVLink, NVSwitch, Mellanox HDR InfiniBand, MIG, and NVIDIA software to support scalable AI, HPC, analytics, and inference workloads.

Odell Beckham Jr. accepted a six-game NFL suspension for violating the league’s performance-enhancing drugs policy, delaying his comeback attempt. The free-agent receiver said he failed a PED test last season but denied knowingly taking banned substances, saying the league cited high testosterone levels. The suspension began Tuesday, making him eligible to play in Week 12. Beckham, who was released by the Dolphins last December after nine catches for 55 yards in nine games, said he still wants to return this season.

Giuriato and Lovecchio (2025) examined whether increasing physical education hours with cognitively engaging activities improves attention in middle school students. The study included 75 students from classes 6 and 7, assigned to experimental and control groups. Class 6 had four hours of physical education per week, while Class 7 had two. Activities included agility drills, coordination circuits, volleyball, and badminton. Attention was assessed in October and December using the Bells Test, measuring bells identified within 30 seconds and 120 seconds.

Results showed significant improvements in 30-second attention speed for experimental groups in both classes, with stronger gains in Class 6. Sustained attention over 120 seconds improved significantly only in the Class 6 experimental group. Control groups showed no significant changes. The authors conclude that increased physical education, particularly with structured cognitively demanding activities, may improve short-term attention, while effects on sustained attention are less consistent and require further research.

The UK Competition and Markets Authority has designated Google Search with Strategic Market Status after a 10-month investigation, giving the regulator power to impose targeted competition measures under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act. Potential interventions include choice screens for rival search engines, fair ranking principles, increased data portability, and requiring permission to use publishers’ content in AI Overviews without affecting search visibility. The CMA says Google handles over 90 percent of UK general search queries and that UK firms spent more than £10 billion on Google search ads in 2024. Google warned that proposed measures could slow innovation and harm businesses. The rules may affect Google Search, News, Top Stories, and Discover, but not Google News or Gemini.

The lecture discusses renormalization and logarithm summation in Soft-Collinear Effective Theory (SCET), using the heavy-to-light current in \(b \to s\gamma\) as a starting example. After including zero-bin contributions, the effective theory result separates into terms matching QCD infrared divergences, ultraviolet divergences canceled by operator counterterms, and finite matching pieces. The counterterm contains a \(1/\epsilon^2\) divergence and logarithms involving the collinear label momentum \(\omega\), which is fixed to \(m_b\) by external kinematics in this process.

The anomalous dimension is derived from the Wilson coefficient renormalization. It contains a regular term and a logarithmic “cusp” term. The cusp anomalous dimension controls leading logarithms, while the regular anomalous dimension contributes at next-to-leading logarithmic order. Solving the renormalization group equation gives Sudakov double logarithms. In QED with fixed coupling this produces a Sudakov exponential; in QCD the running coupling modifies the exponent through ratios of \(\alpha_s\). Logarithmic counting is organized in \(\log C\), with leading logs of the form \(\alpha_s^k \log^{k+1}\), followed by next-to-leading and next-to-next-to-leading terms. Higher logarithmic accuracy requires higher-loop cusp and non-cusp anomalous dimensions and matching coefficients.

The “cusp” arises from Wilson lines meeting at a sharp angle, such as an ultrasoft Wilson line along the heavy-quark velocity joined to a lightlike collinear Wilson line. Similar cusp-like structures also appear in collinear graphs involving Wilson lines ending on quark fields. When an operator has only one building block in each collinear direction, label momenta are fixed by external kinematics and renormalization is multiplicative. When multiple fields share the same collinear direction, loop momenta can enter label combinations, producing convolution-type anomalous dimension equations such as those appearing in DGLAP and related evolution equations.

The lecture then begins applying SCET to deep inelastic scattering. In the inclusive region, where \(P_X^2\sim Q^2\), the Breit frame is used: the incoming proton is collinear and the final hadronic state is hard. The hadronic tensor is written through the optical theorem as a current-current correlator. Matching onto SCET gives leading-power quark and gluon operators built from collinear building blocks. The quark operator is related to the parton distribution function through a forward proton matrix element, with momentum conservation imposing equality of two label momenta and leaving one momentum fraction variable.

The passage explains the role of design patterns in distributed systems, emphasizing that open source communities helped show software development as a community effort and that container technologies underlying the discussed patterns are open source. Patterns are defined as general blueprints for organizing distributed systems without mandating specific technologies. Their value lies in helping developers learn from prior experience, providing a shared vocabulary, and enabling reusable components.

The passage focuses first on single-node container patterns. Containers can be split on one machine to provide resource isolation, clarify team ownership, enable separation of concerns, and support modular reuse. Kubernetes pods are presented as a way to tightly group containers that share resources such as volumes, filesystems, network namespaces, and memory.

The sidecar pattern uses a secondary container to augment an application container. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service through an nginx proxy, synchronizing configuration from an API to a filesystem, providing a reusable process-inspection interface, and building a simple Git-based platform-as-a-service. Effective sidecars should be parameterized, expose stable APIs, and be documented through Dockerfile directives and labels.

The ambassador pattern uses a container to broker communication between an application and external services. It can route requests to sharded storage, act as a service broker across different environments, or split traffic for experiments. Examples include using twemproxy with sharded Redis and nginx for sending 10% of traffic to an experimental service.

The adapter pattern modifies an application’s interface to match a common expected interface. It is useful for heterogeneous systems requiring consistent monitoring, logging, or health checks. Examples include adapting Redis metrics for Prometheus, normalizing logs with fluentd, and adding richer MySQL health checks without modifying the database container.

The passage then introduces multi-node patterns and microservices. Microservices divide functionality into separate services with defined APIs, improving team independence, release agility, and scaling, but making debugging and architecture more difficult. Distributed patterns help address these challenges.

Replicated load-balanced services are described as a basic distributed pattern for stateless applications. Replication improves availability, supports rolling updates, and enables horizontal scaling. Readiness probes tell load balancers when instances can serve traffic. Variations include session-tracked services, caching layers using tools such as Varnish, rate limiting, denial-of-service defense, and SSL termination using nginx.

Finally, the passage describes sharded services, where each shard handles only part of the data and a routing layer directs requests. Sharding is mainly used for stateful systems whose data is too large for one machine. A sharded cache can improve memory utilization, request capacity, and latency, but failures can reduce performance. Replicating shards improves resilience and allows scaling of individual hot shards. Examples include sharded memcache using Kubernetes StatefulSets, Services, twemproxy, and either an ambassador container or a shared shard-routing service.

A Science study found 75% of 198 honey samples from nearly 200 global sites contained neonicotinoid pesticides. North America had the highest contamination rate at 86%, followed by Asia at 80% and Europe at 79%.

Rockwood School District in Missouri teaches early reading through grade-level classroom cohorts rather than grouping students across grades by ability. All students receive whole-class phonics and comprehension instruction, followed by flexible small-group reteaching or enrichment based on current needs. The district also uses independent and partner reading, targeted interventions, movement-based learning tools, and supports such as visual cues and pre-teaching. The author argues that ability grouping can limit lower-track students’ exposure to grade-level content and make it harder to catch up. Rockwood reports that in 2024–25, its kindergarteners exceeded national proficiency averages in every skill group, while first and second graders outpaced national averages across nearly every domain.

The disclosure describes methods and hardware for configuring Deep Neural Network activation modules that use programmable lookup tables to approximate activation functions. Calibration data is provided to a representation of the hardware, inputs to activation modules are monitored to determine expected input ranges, and lookup data is generated and loaded so the lookup table represents the activation function over those ranges rather than the full possible input range.

The hardware may implement CNNs or other DNNs and includes components such as convolution engines, accumulators, activation modules, normalization and pooling modules, buffers, and memory interfaces. Activation functions may be represented by stored data points, gradients and offsets, or curves, with output values calculated by interpolation, including linear or quadratic interpolation. Lookup tables may use separate odd and even data stores to read adjacent points simultaneously and may store multiple data sets so one can be updated while another is used.

The method may be repeated for multiple activation functions, activation modules, or hardware passes. Inputs outside the determined range may be clamped to boundary values or approximated by extrapolation. Offsets may be applied to center input ranges before lookup. A simple ReLU path may be used instead of the lookup table for ReLU functions, allowing unused logic to be turned off.

The disclosure also covers data processing systems, software, computer-readable storage media, integrated circuit datasets, and manufacturing systems for producing hardware implementing these methods.

China announced it will shut down its domestic ivory market by the end of 2017, targeting the world’s largest demand source for ivory. Elephant populations in Africa have fallen sharply, largely due to poaching for tusks, despite a 1989 international ivory trade ban that did not cover older ivory. Conservationists say closing China’s legal trade could significantly reduce demand and help protect elephants. China’s plan includes redirecting ivory carvers to museum or other projects and educating the public about ivory trade’s impact. The U.S. has already restricted most ivory trade, and the move may influence other countries to follow.

The passage reviews literature on new models and quality in higher education, with emphasis on online learning, quality assurance, leadership, technology, rankings, and institutional change. Several studies address the COVID-19 shift to online and e-learning, identifying technological infrastructure, digital literacy, instructional design, student support, social interaction, gender differences, and institutional backing as key factors affecting teaching quality and student experience. Other works examine leadership spirituality, resistance to change, stakeholder expectations, service quality, student loyalty, and higher education leaders’ views on pandemic-related challenges and opportunities.

The review also discusses quality assurance and management frameworks, including accreditation, peer review, ISO 21001, recognition of non-formal and informal learning, faculty development, curriculum reform, and online teaching support. Multiple entries focus on university rankings, covering their relationship to academic quality, importance, use in accreditation, role in combating diploma mills, and critiques regarding methodology and unintended effects. Additional topics include internationalization, virtual universities, ICT-based governance, entrepreneurship, AI, big data, high technology, academic freedom, equity and inclusion indicators, sustainable development goals, and career development.

The conclusion states that higher education publications are changing through innovative models and technologies, including open access and collaborative digital platforms, creating both challenges and opportunities for scholars, institutions, and publishers.

Platinum futures provide exposure to the platinum market for speculation, diversification, or hedging. Platinum is a rare, heavy, silver-white metal used in jewelry, catalytic converters, and many industrial applications. Futures contracts are standardized agreements to exchange platinum at a set price on a future date and trade on CME Globex under the symbol PL, with physical delivery settlement.

A platinum futures strategy uses technical and fundamental analysis, entry and exit signals, position sizing, and risk management. The passage presents two backtested strategies: one long/short strategy with 473 combined trades, a 64% win rate, 0.57% average gain, and 1.7 profit factor; and one seasonal strategy with 60 trades, a 75% win rate, 0.66% average gain, and 2.3 profit factor. Platinum tends to perform better in winter and spring than in summer and fall.

Platinum prices are affected by supply and demand, political and economic events, production costs, automotive and jewelry demand, industrial uses, substitutes such as palladium, and instability in major producing regions. South Africa and Russia supply a large share of platinum, with South Africa accounting for most global supply and proven reserves.

CME platinum futures represent 50 troy ounces, are quoted in U.S. dollars and cents per ounce, have a minimum fluctuation of $0.10 per ounce, and a tick size of $5 per contract. Trading involves leverage, which can magnify gains and losses. Alternatives include platinum CFDs, ETFs, stocks, options, and physical platinum. The passage states that platinum trading may offer diversification benefits but is difficult due to volatility, macroeconomic sensitivity, erratic news, and lack of a natural commodity trading edge.

The passage argues that high-dosage tutoring should be viewed not only as a response to pandemic learning loss but also as a way to build student confidence, support teachers and develop future educators. Teach For America’s Ignite Fellowship has trained more than 5,500 virtual tutors across over 40 communities, with fellows delivering nearly 200,000 hours of customized learning last school year. The program reports faster-than-expected growth in math and reading scores. The author emphasizes that tutoring requires structured training, ongoing coaching and integration with school instruction; that technology should expand access to relationships rather than replace them; and that tutoring can serve as a teacher pipeline. Research cited in the passage finds Ignite tutoring nearly triples the likelihood of applying to TFA’s teacher program, with especially large effects among men, people of color and non-education majors. Since launch, 550 Ignite fellows have joined TFA’s teaching corps.

The President returns House bill No. 7864 without approval. The bill would exclude immigrants over 16 who cannot read and write English or another language, with limited family exceptions, and would require applicants to read and write a passage from the U.S. Constitution. The President argues this literacy test is a radical departure from U.S. immigration policy, which has historically admitted immigrants who were physically and morally sound and willing to work. He says illiteracy is not a reliable measure of desirable citizenship or public safety, and that disorder is more likely caused by educated agitators than illiterate laborers.

He also criticizes the bill’s family exceptions as indefinite and inadequate, noting omissions and practical uncertainties. The bill would also restrict certain male aliens from working on U.S. public works or regularly entering the country for private labor, and would criminalize their employment. The President argues these provisions are illiberal, especially along the northern border, could harm citizens who benefit from cross-border labor, invite retaliation, and are too uncertain to define a crime. He concludes the bill is unnecessarily harsh, oppressive, and harmful.

At Dumbarton Oaks on October 7, 1944, representatives of the United States, Great Britain, and China informally discussed dissolving the League of Nations and transitioning to the United Nations, agreeing to exchange papers, though none were received. The League’s Supervisory Committee later appointed a three-member committee to select a Conciliation Committee to confer with a United Nations group on dissolution and transfer of functions. U.S. officials made no commitments and recommended taking no initiative, leaving the matter to the United Nations Conference unless League members Britain or China acted.

At a January 31, 1945 meeting with representatives of certain American republics, Acting Secretary Grew emphasized the importance of the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals and invited continued discussion. Biosecurity screening software checks DNA manufacturing orders for potentially harmful proteins, but researchers found AI-made tweaks to toxins or viral proteins can bypass filters. In computer simulations, Eric Horvitz and colleagues generated about 76,000 blueprints for 72 harmful proteins. Screens flagged nearly all original proteins, but many AI-adjusted versions slipped through. Software patches improved detection, including for fragmented genes, though about 3 percent of variants were still missed. The team did not create physical proteins, and it is unclear whether the variants retained their function. James Diggans of Twist Bioscience said attempts to produce malicious proteins are “close to zero,” though screening remains an important safeguard.

The passage presents GeoSQL-Eval, an end-to-end automated framework for evaluating large language models on PostGIS GeoSQL generation, and GeoSQL-Bench, a benchmark of 14,178 tasks. The benchmark includes 2,380 multiple-choice and true/false questions, 7,488 syntax-level SQL generation questions, and 4,310 table schema retrieval questions, covering conceptual understanding, syntax generation, semantic alignment, execution accuracy, and robustness. Tasks were built from the PostGIS 3.5 manual, UN-GGIM themes, and ISO 19115-1 categories, using GPT-4o-assisted Self-Instruct generation followed by expert review.

GeoSQL-Eval evaluates generated queries through answer matching, PostgreSQL AST parsing, execution in PostGIS, schema and function alignment, result comparison for geometric and non-geometric outputs, pass@n, coefficient of variation, stability-adjusted accuracy, entropy-weighted ranking, resource consumption, and error logging. The study evaluates 24 models across six categories: general non-reasoning models, reasoning-enhanced models, code generation models, geospatial code models, SQL generation models, and GeoSQL generation strategies.

Results show that general non-reasoning and reasoning-enhanced models perform best overall, with GPT-5, o4-mini, and DeepSeek-R1-0528 ranking highly across multiple dimensions. Conceptual questions achieve relatively high accuracy, while table schema retrieval remains the main bottleneck. Syntax accuracy is often high but does not guarantee successful execution. Function invocation and parameter matching are major weaknesses, and underspecified prompts significantly reduce performance. The dominant error types are PostGIS function errors and SQL syntax errors. General non-reasoning models are generally more efficient, while o4-mini provides a strong balance of accuracy and resource use. The study also releases a GeoSQL-Eval leaderboard platform for model submission and comparison.

The authors conclude that GeoSQL-Eval provides a systematic, reproducible way to assess LLM capability in GeoSQL generation and identify model weaknesses. Limitations include incomplete coverage of all PostGIS functions, focus on PostGIS rather than other spatial databases or extensions, and limited model coverage. Future work may expand functions, systems, models, and continuous evaluation mechanisms.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated May 10, 2018, announcing results for the quarter ended April 29, 2018. The filing includes a press release and CFO commentary by Colette M. Kress as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2, furnished but not deemed filed under the Securities Exchange Act.

New Orleans, especially the Lower Ninth Ward, still bears scars from Hurricane Katrina, with many poor, predominantly black residents unable to return amid rebuilding costs, development and gentrification. The cup and handle pattern, also called the cup with handle pattern, is a bullish continuation chart pattern resembling a rounded cup followed by a smaller handle. It forms after a price rally, marks consolidation, and is completed when price breaks above the handle’s resistance, often with increased volume. The inverted version forms in a downtrend and signals bearish continuation. Traders use the pattern to identify long opportunities, set targets by measuring cup depth, and place stop-losses below the handle or cup bottom. Confirmation often involves volume, price action, broader market context, and other indicators. Backtests cited show mixed results: one S&P 500 test underperformed the index, while Bulkowski reported a 26% failure rate that dropped to 10% after upside breakout, but no clear statistical expectancy. Common mistakes include entering before confirmation, ignoring volume, poor stop-loss or target placement, neglecting market conditions, and relying solely on the pattern.

Boston is described as the world’s leading life sciences hub, with unmatched lab space and major venture capital and federal research funding, but its edge is threatened by federal funding cuts and challenges to higher education.

Higher-order Feynman diagrams can include loop corrections, such as a self-energy correction to a propagator. Calculating such a loop leads to an integral that behaves logarithmically and diverges to infinity at high momentum, creating problems because physical quantities like cross-sections and lifetimes should not be infinite or zero.

A cutoff scale can be introduced so the integral is evaluated only up to a finite scale, preserving sensible behavior such as Lorentz invariance, though an infinite contribution remains beyond the cutoff. Renormalization addresses this by redefining physical quantities so masses and coupling constants appear as bare values plus corrections.

Although corrections may diverge at infinite scale, experiments occur at specific scales, so theoretical predictions can still be compared with measurements. Couplings for electromagnetic, weak, and strong interactions depend on energy scale and “run” with it, though they do not all converge at very high mass scales. Introducing new particles could change this running and potentially allow the couplings to unify at a specific scale, suggesting possible new physics. Physical masses and couplings are therefore scale-dependent and must be evaluated at the scale of an experiment.

The lecture revisits the graph removal lemma and introduces the induced graph removal lemma, where graphs with few induced copies of a fixed graph H can be made induced H-free by adding or deleting few edges. Unlike the usual removal lemma, the induced version must handle both edges and non-edges, making irregular pairs in regularity partitions a major obstacle.

To address this, the lecture presents the strong regularity lemma, which produces two equitable partitions P and Q, with Q refining P, Q being very regular, and the energy difference between P and Q small. This is proved by repeatedly applying Szemerédi’s regularity lemma and using bounded energy increments. The resulting bounds are extremely large, involving iterated tower-type “wowzer” functions.

A corollary of strong regularity gives a partition into parts Vi with subsets Wi such that all pairs Wi, Wj are regular, the Wi are large, and most densities between Vi, Vj are close to those between Wi, Wj. This removes the irregular-pair problem.

Using this corollary, the induced removal lemma is proved by partitioning, cleaning low- and high-density pairs through edge deletion or addition, and applying a counting lemma to show that any remaining induced copy of H would imply many original induced copies, contradicting the hypothesis.

The lecture also states an infinite removal lemma for possibly infinite families of forbidden induced subgraphs, requiring stronger dependence in the regularity parameters. Finally, it connects removal lemmas to property testing: triangle removal implies a randomized tester for triangle-freeness, and the infinite removal lemma implies that every hereditary graph property is testable with one-sided error using an oblivious tester.

The passage compares dollar-cost averaging and lump sum investing. Dollar-cost averaging invests fixed amounts at regular intervals to reduce concern over short-term volatility, while lump sum investing puts a large amount into the market at once. The article backtests a lump sum buy-and-hold strategy using a diversified equal-weight portfolio of five asset classes via liquid ETFs with long histories. It concludes that, historically, lump sum investing has offered a higher probability of success over long-term horizons, preferably at least ten years, because markets tend to rise over time and earlier investment allows more time for growth. The passage states that long-term effects of financial crises become relatively insignificant.

NeoWorld is a framework for interactive world generation that constructs an infinitely expandable virtual world from a single image. It begins with lightweight object-centric 2D/2.5D Gaussian layers and progressively converts interaction-relevant or user-specified objects into full 3D representations. This hybrid structure keeps background regions efficient while enabling foreground objects to support 3D-consistent exploration, object manipulation, and physics-based animation.

The method uses panoptic segmentation to create object-centric Gaussian layers, binds compact instance-aware attributes through a codebook, and maintains cross-view object consistency through label matching. Objects are unfolded from 2.5D to 3D based on proximity to the camera or user prompts, using image-to-3D reconstruction followed by coarse and fine alignment. A fallback strategy reverts unreliable reconstructions to 2.5D when rendered-object similarity is low. Large language models interpret user commands, identify target objects, and generate manipulation or animation attributes.

Experiments compare NeoWorld with unbounded world generation, video diffusion, object-centric representation, and interactive manipulation baselines. NeoWorld improves 3D consistency, scene quality, and long-term consistency over prior 3D world generation methods while maintaining reasonable efficiency. Its object-centric representation achieves higher segmentation IoU than OmniSeg3DGS and GaussianGrouping, and user-interaction evaluations show stronger text-motion alignment than video diffusion baselines. Ablations show that the codebook representation balances quality and efficiency, the alignment pipeline improves plausibility and coherence, and selected hyperparameters provide a trade-off between robustness and computational cost.

The paper concludes that NeoWorld enables object-level semantic interaction and 3D physical consistency in expanding virtual worlds, but its cascaded design depends on external pretrained modules and can fail due to alignment errors, prompt ambiguity, reconstruction failures, or segmentation mistakes.

The passage describes ADS9803 features, configuration, and application guidance. The device has eight analog input channels with internal clamp protection allowing input swings up to ±18V; above this threshold, input current must remain within ±10mA, commonly limited with series resistors that can also form antialiasing low-pass filters. Each channel includes a programmable gain amplifier supporting single-ended and differential bipolar inputs, programmable input ranges, and selectable low-pass filter bandwidths. A wide common-mode rejection circuit supports common-mode voltages up to ±12V, with configurable settings for differential and single-ended inputs.

The ADS9803 outputs 20-bit conversion data in straight-binary or two’s-complement format and supports differential or single-ended free-running sampling clocks. Multiple devices can be synchronized using SMPL_SYNC. The device includes an internal precision low-drift reference, with optional external reference through REFIO. Its data interface supports 2-lane or 4-lane SDR and DDR modes, source-synchronous output, data randomization using XOR, simple and moving data averaging, and digital test patterns including fixed, ramp, and alternating patterns.

Reset, power-down, initialization, speed-boost mode, SPI register access, and daisy-chain SPI operation are described. Speed-boost mode supports up to 8MSPS for a selected channel pair while other channels remain idle. Registers are organized into banks and control data format, averaging, test patterns, speed boost, bandwidth, power-down, reference, output lanes, input ranges, and common-mode configuration.

Application guidance presents the ADS9803 as an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS DAQ system for ATE applications, with post-calibration TUE of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C for a ±5V range. It supports PMU measurement directly or through multiplexers, with wide-bandwidth mode settling to 99.95% full scale in 7.5µs. Layout recommendations include separating analog and digital paths, placing bypass and reference capacitors close to pins, and using appropriate grounding and ESD precautions.

The study developed a whole-body physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model to predict tissue concentrations of the four first-line tuberculosis drugs—rifampicin, ethambutol, isoniazid, and pyrazinamide—at extrapulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB) sites, especially pleura and lymph nodes. The model extends a previous PBPK framework by adding pleural fluid and lymph node compartments and uses physiological parameters, tissue:plasma partition coefficients, and calibrated pharmacokinetic parameters. Plasma and lung concentration data were used for calibration and validation.

The model reasonably reproduced reported plasma concentrations and some lung and pleural concentration data. In pleural fluid, predicted pyrazinamide and ethambutol concentrations were below critical concentrations, while rifampicin and isoniazid were above them, though rifampicin was over-predicted. In lung tissue, rifampicin and isoniazid stayed above critical concentrations for much of the time, while ethambutol was often below and pyrazinamide remained below. Across extrapulmonary sites, rifampicin generally exceeded its critical concentration, ethambutol failed to do so in several compartments, isoniazid exceeded thresholds in both slow and fast acetylators but varied by acetylator status, and pyrazinamide did not reach its MIC or critical concentration in any compartment.

The authors note limitations including lack of tissue validation data, assumptions of drug-susceptible TB, no significant drug-drug interactions, no rifampicin autoinduction, no age-dependent pharmacokinetics, and use of a single consolidated lymph node compartment. They conclude that PBPK modelling may help evaluate and optimize EPTB treatment regimens, but more in vivo pharmacokinetic data at EPTB sites are needed.

Researchers harmonized Korea’s CRCS-K and Taiwan’s TREAT-AIS stroke registries into the K-T collaborative EVT registry, comprising 9,941 endovascular thrombectomy-treated acute ischemic stroke patients and about 200 common data fields. Taiwanese patients were older, had more vascular risk factors, more severe strokes, lower pre-stroke functional independence, lower IV thrombolysis use, and lower 90-day functional independence than Korean patients. Successful recanalization and symptomatic hemorrhagic transformation rates were broadly similar between cohorts, while 90-day mortality was higher in the Korean cohort.

Age strongly influenced EVT outcomes. Patients aged ≥80 had lower favorable functional outcomes, higher mortality, and lower successful recanalization rates than younger patients, but symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage did not differ significantly by age. The age-outcome relationship was most pronounced between 75 and 85 years. In elderly patients, favorable recovery was associated with younger age within the subgroup, female sex, pre-stroke independence, lower baseline NIHSS, and bridging thrombolysis. The study concludes that harmonized multinational registries can clarify regional EVT differences in East Asia and that advanced age is linked to poorer outcomes, though selected elderly patients may still benefit.

This study examined how mydriasis affects retinal image gradability and AI performance for diabetic retinopathy screening using a portable fundus camera. It included 327 patients imaged before and after Tropicamide 0.5% dilation. Images were labeled by masked ophthalmologists, and a CNN model trained on the mBRSET dataset was evaluated on paired mydriatic and non-mydriatic images.

Mydriatic imaging produced significantly more gradable images than non-mydriatic imaging: 1056 images (82.1%) versus 699 images (55.6%), P < 0.001. In non-mydriatic images, lower gradability was associated with systemic hypertension, older age, longer diabetes duration, male gender, and Indigenous race.

After quality screening, 597 paired images were analyzed by the AI model. For detecting diabetic retinopathy, performance was higher with mydriatic images than non-mydriatic images: accuracy was 82.91% versus 79.23%, F1 score 0.83 versus 0.79, and AUC 0.94 versus 0.93. Mydriatic images had fewer false positives but slightly more false negatives. The difference between groups was not statistically significant by Chi-square test (P = 0.3279).

The study concludes that mydriasis improves image gradability and may enhance AI-based diabetic retinopathy screening with portable cameras, though non-mydriatic imaging remains relevant in resource-limited settings. Limitations included use of a single dataset and camera model, possible selection bias from paired-image analysis, and variability in image acquisition by non-specialized personnel.

The lecture introduces probabilistically checkable proofs (PCPs) and explains how to construct them from the GKR protocol, before moving later toward cryptographic arguments with computational soundness. A PCP converts a classical proof or NP witness into a possibly larger polynomial-size proof that a verifier can check by reading only a few randomly chosen locations. The verifier normally reads the full instance, though PCPs of proximity relax this.

The PCP complexity class is defined with completeness, soundness, randomness, and query parameters. For inputs in the language, there must be a PCP accepted with probability at least the completeness parameter; for inputs outside the language, every alleged PCP is accepted with probability at most the soundness parameter. The verifier is described as a probabilistic polynomial-time oracle machine, typically nonadaptive: it chooses all queried proof locations before reading them. Nonadaptivity is useful for later applications.

The lecture states a theorem that all NP languages have PCPs with completeness 1, soundness 1/2, and polylogarithmic randomness and query complexity. Known results can reduce randomness to logarithmic and queries to 3, but the lecture focuses on the polylogarithmic construction.

The construction is shown for 3SAT, using the fact that NP languages can be reduced to 3SAT and that the verification circuit has small depth and suitable uniformity. The GKR protocol is recalled: for each layer of a circuit, the prover considers low-degree extensions of wire values over a field and uses sumcheck protocols to reduce claims about one layer to claims about the previous layer.

To build the PCP, the prover writes into the proof the low-degree extensions of the witness and every circuit layer, as well as all possible prover messages for the sumcheck protocols for every relevant layer, point, and verifier randomness. The verifier then simulates the GKR verifier by reading the corresponding entries from the PCP rather than interacting with a prover. At the end, it checks needed values in the low-degree extension of the witness.

Soundness follows from the soundness of the sumcheck protocols and a union bound over the 2d sumchecks. The field size is chosen large enough, but still polylogarithmic, so that the PCP remains polynomial size. The query and randomness complexities are polylogarithmic. The construction relies on GKR’s structure, which allows the proof tree to be opened efficiently because previous randomness can be forgotten between subprotocols. A low-degree test is still needed for the input-layer low-degree extension, since the verifier does not possess the witness.

The paper addresses the scalability limits of biomedical image registration, where high-resolution images can require billions of transform parameters and exceed current GPU memory capacities. It identifies major memory and compute bottlenecks in deformable registration: grid sampling and warp composition, localized normalized cross-correlation, and mutual information. The authors propose fused CUDA kernels, including a composite implicit grid sampler, implicit Parzen windowing for mutual information, and fused cross-correlation, reducing intermediate high-bandwidth memory use.

They introduce Flash Fused Distributed Primitives (FFDP), a distributed framework using Grid Parallel sharding with boundary synchronization and a ring sampler for distributed interpolation without allgathering the moving image. FFDP supports distributed MSE, LNCC, and MI losses. Experiments show speed and memory improvements for existing optimization and deep learning pipelines, including up to 7.48× acceleration for traditional registration and 6.14× for deep learning methods. The framework registers a 250µm in-vivo MRI to a 100µm ex-vivo human brain FLASH volume with over 11.8B transform parameters in about one minute on 8 A6000 GPUs. On a simulated 250µm ex-vivo brain MRI dataset, the method outperforms baselines in accuracy and efficiency, while ablations show reduced memory and runtime for key operations and the importance of boundary synchronization.

The Georgia Court of Appeals affirmed Robert Pearl Bryson’s convictions for aggravated sodomy, aggravated child molestation, child molestation, and failure to register as a sex offender. The court held that testimony and recorded interviews from the child victims provided sufficient evidence for the aggravated sodomy and child molestation convictions, and that Bryson’s departure from Georgia for over a year without notifying Stephens County authorities supported his failure-to-register conviction.

The court found no reversible error in the denial of Bryson’s motions to quash the indictment, including challenges involving the sheriff’s wife serving on the grand jury and the timing of Count 8. It also upheld the denial of trial counsel’s motion to withdraw shortly before trial, finding no abuse of discretion because withdrawal would have delayed trial.

The court ruled that severance of the failure-to-register counts was not required because the charges were connected to the molestation allegations and Bryson’s flight, and the jury could distinguish the evidence. It also held that admission of Bryson’s North Carolina no-contest plea was not error because it was admissible for sex-offender registration purposes, and the jury was instructed not to treat it as an admission of guilt.

Finally, the court concluded that Bryson waived his ineffective-assistance claim by refusing to pursue it at the motion-for-new-trial hearing despite being warned by the trial court. The judgment was affirmed.

The paper examines the relationship between Artificial Intelligence, Big Data, and Advanced Analytics in digital business transformation. It develops a multidimensional data-driven AI innovation taxonomy and maturity framework using literature review, expert interviews, and taxonomy-development methods. The study defines an AI/BD/AA micro-level value chain covering data acquisition, curation, storage, and usage for decision-making. It also links AI maturity to advanced analytics maturity across five levels: Human Led/Initial Analytics; Human Led, Machine Supported/Advanced Analytics I; Machine Led, Human Supported/Advanced Analytics II; Machine Led, Human Governed/Advanced Analytics III; and Machine Controlled/Advanced Analytics IV. The framework is intended to help organizations evaluate AI-based automation, human-machine relationships, enterprise platforms, and data-driven innovation strategies across industries.

The Mississippi Supreme Court affirmed Ulysses S. Gandy’s second manslaughter conviction and ten-year sentence arising from a fatal two-car collision that killed three people. Gandy argued the verdict was against the weight of the evidence, a jury instruction was wrongly refused, certain exhibit sketches were improperly admitted, and the jury should have received a recess during deliberations. The Court held that conflicting evidence about vehicle positions and Gandy’s intoxication was for the jury to resolve and was sufficient to support culpable negligence. It found no reversible error in refusing the proposed intoxication instruction, admitting sketches used only to show witnesses’ observations after the crash, or failing to recess the jury absent a request or supporting authority.

The passage lists AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 errata and workarounds. Reported issues include unreliable SSMI signaling when IRQ and SSMI occur simultaneously; UDMA failure if IDE bus mastering is enabled before sending a PIO command packet; most GPIO wake inputs not working from ACPI S3; incorrect RTC CMOS reads after specific extended-port writes; LPC I/O failures during block or demand legacy DMA; USB controller register read failures when clock gating is enabled; IDE bus master reset after unexpected ATAPI interrupt; AuxOutputFull being cleared by Port 60h reads; fixed tACK timing that still meets requirements; possible ATAC hangs with WORD-aligned PRDs; LPC aborts with certain sync timing; SMB NEGACK bit misbehavior; GLPCI retry counter counting other PCI retries; GPIO high bank atomic writes clearing unselected bits after suspend; SMBus data hold time below specification; missing LOWBAT_FLAG after abnormal standby; and Sleep_X/Sleep_Y not deasserting if certain delays exceed PM_SED. Recommended actions include using normal UDMA order, PWRBTN# or external circuitry for S3 wake, single-transfer DMA, disabling USB clock gating, interrupts for USB PS/2 emulation, DWORD alignment for ATAC PRDs, PLD workaround for LPC-to-ISA bridge cases, adjusted SMB status clearing, increasing or disabling retry limit, read-modify-write after suspend, and programming sleep delay counters below PM_SED.

The study developed a model linking Google Community Mobility Reports (GCMR) to SARS-CoV-2 transmission dynamics, using hospitalization data from Norwegian and Swedish regions from February 2020 to July 2021 and two German regions from February to December 2020. The model treated four GCMR settings—workplaces, transit stations, groceries and pharmacies, and retail and recreation—as additive contributors to transmissibility, while temperature and variants of concern were modeled as multiplicative effects.

The model fit hospitalization trends well and estimated that GCMR-captured settings accounted for 60.0% of infections in Sweden and 38.7% in Norway, with unexplained transmission attributed to other settings through weekly regional parameters. Transit stations and workplaces were the most important GCMR settings in Norway and Sweden, while retail and recreation contributed most in the German regions. A 20°C temperature increase was associated with about a 40% reduction in transmissibility in Norway and Sweden, with a similar effect in Germany. Delta was associated with roughly doubled transmissibility, while Alpha showed limited or inconsistent increases.

The authors conclude that GCMR data were clearly associated with SARS-CoV-2 dynamics and may support real-time assessment of population activity during epidemics, but their use requires strong assumptions, complex modeling, and many parameters. Limitations include assumed linear relationships between mobility and infectious contacts, potential measurement error in GCMRs, simplified vaccination modeling, and fixed assumptions about disease parameters.

He calls for a balanced budget amendment, line-item veto, tax simplification, school prayer, anticrime legislation, tuition tax credits, enterprise zones, and reduced nuclear arms through negotiations with the Soviet Union. Reagan emphasizes individual liberty, limited government, opposition to bigotry, national strength, support for allies including Israel, and the belief that America has regained confidence and is entering a “springtime of hope.”

Grief is a personal emotional reaction to losing someone or something important, or to major life changes such as becoming a carer, declining health, retirement or moving home. It can occur before an expected loss, such as terminal illness, and may affect both the person who is ill and their loved ones. Moving from a long-term home can also cause grief, especially after bereavement or when support networks are lost.

Grief does not follow fixed stages and may involve shifting emotions, including numbness, denial, relief, yearning, repeated thoughts about the death, restlessness, sleep problems, loss of confidence, guilt, anger, sadness and depression. There is no right way to grieve and no set duration. Over time, many people find good days become more frequent, though the loss remains. Support from family, friends, a GP, specialist organisations or bereavement services may help.

The ADS9803 supports simple and moving data averaging to improve SNR, digital test patterns for debugging, reset and power-down controls, initialization by register writes, and speed-boost mode up to 8MSPS for a selected analog input channel pair. Test patterns include fixed, digital ramp, and alternating outputs for channel groups CH[4:1] and CH[8:5]. The device uses three register banks accessed through SPI, with procedures for register read/write operations and daisy-chain configurations for multiple ADCs.

Register sections describe controls for SPI mode, daisy-chain length, bank selection, averaging, XOR operation, test patterns, speed-boost mode, gain correction, power-down, analog bandwidth, reference selection, output lanes, and common-mode range. Application guidance describes use in ATE systems, where the eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS ADS9803 provides calibrated TUE of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C and supports multiplexed PMU signal measurement with wide-bandwidth settling to 99.95% FS in 7.5µs. Layout recommendations include separate decoupling, short ground connections, and keeping analog and reference signals away from noise sources.

Enron mentions from July 9–10, 2001, focus on California’s energy crisis and Enron’s Dabhol project in India. California records showed many public and private electricity suppliers charged high prices, with some charging more than firms criticized by Gov. Gray Davis, including Enron. A Senate probe accused Duke Energy of limiting public release of bidding data, while Enron and Mirant were cited over document compliance. Federal talks failed to settle California refund claims; a judge planned to recommend refunds far below California’s $8.9 billion demand.

In India, Dabhol Power CEO Neil McGregor resigned after his contract expired. Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay met Indian officials about the disputed $2.9 billion Dabhol project, saying no conclusions were reached but Enron remained committed to finding a solution. Reports also noted possible new engineering consultants for Dabhol, lenders’ concerns, and Enron seeking industry help.

Other mentions included Enron Broadband Services as an investor in Tropic Networks, analysts rating Enron a “buy” despite controversies, and expectations that power producers, including Enron, would meet second-quarter earnings targets.

The Patriots struggled offensively against the Dolphins on Monday night but remained within seven points in the final minute. Stephen Gostkowski’s onside kick attempt was widely criticized, with Jon Gruden calling it “the most bizarre onside kick” he had seen. Miami recovered and won the game.

Scientists found that periwinkle sea snails exposed to predicted 2100 ocean acidification conditions adapted by altering shell formation. Though their metabolism declined, they produced less-dense inner shells and less-soluble shells, suggesting periwinkles and potentially other calcifying organisms may adapt to acidifying oceans.

To beat the offside trap, attackers must recognize when defenders are moving up, stay onside when the ball is passed, avoid interfering if caught offside, and exploit the space behind the defense. Tactics include dribbling through without passing, timed through passes, horizontal or bending runs, checking runs toward the ball, short or back passes to buy time, deep-lying midfield runs, delayed runs, possession play, and using a designated non-runner on free kicks. Attackers should also watch for defenders who fail to move up, leaving players onside. Successfully beating the trap can create a one-on-one chance with the goalkeeper and may discourage the defense from using the trap again.

Researchers led by Vanderbilt’s Joshua Caldwell reported in Nature Materials an advance in hyperlensing using isotopically purified hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). By making hBN crystals with 99 percent isotopically pure boron, they reduced infrared optical losses, tripled polariton lifetime and travel distance, and improved potential imaging capability by about tenfold over previous hBN results. The team calculates that lenses made from the purified crystal could in principle image objects as small as 30 nanometers, potentially enabling observation of viruses and cellular processes in living cells without harmful preparation or radiation. Hyperlenses using infrared light may also provide spectroscopic “fingerprints” and have applications in biological and medical science, communications, and nanoscale optical components. Researchers from several U.S. institutions contributed, with funding from multiple federal agencies.
In People v. Roldán, the court found the case nearly identical to case No. 2037, differing only in loan amount. For the same reasons, the judgment was reversed and the defendant acquitted.

China blacklisted Canadian technology research firm TechInsights and nine subsidiaries, accusing them of endangering national security after a report on Huawei’s advanced AI chips. The restrictions bar Chinese organisations from working with or sharing data with TechInsights. Analysts say the move reflects tighter control over tech information and rising semiconductor tensions.

Barron’s argued Netflix shares could lose more than half their value, citing Disney’s planned content withdrawal, Facebook’s video service, Amazon Prime competition, cash burn, and accounting concerns. The passage counters that competition fears are overstated, noting Netflix has grown from 23.6 million subscribers to 104 million despite Amazon and YouTube. It also says Netflix has successfully raised prices in the U.S., Australia, and Canada, showing pricing flexibility. The passage argues Netflix’s large subscriber base gives it scale advantages, spending control, and appeal to content creators, while acknowledging the stock is not cheap and may correct.

Ryan Kerr, 26, of Evercreech, was remanded in custody by Taunton Crown Court after admitting multiple assaults, including attacks on a rival, the rival’s mother, and a man at The George Hotel. The court heard he had previous convictions and showed no remorse. Sentencing was adjourned for the judge to consider his decision.

A Pediatrics study found that from 1990 to 2015, nearly 17,000 U.S. children under 6 were treated in emergency rooms for window blind-related injuries, with about one death per month and two injuries per day. Most injuries were minor, but cord entanglement accounted for 11.9% of cases, nearly 80% of hospitalizations, and more than 94% of 271 deaths. Nearly all entanglements involved blind cords, usually at home and often when children were briefly unsupervised.

Researchers and safety advocates say voluntary standards have not been enough and support mandatory rules requiring blinds with cordless, unexposed, or inaccessible cords. The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission began mandatory rulemaking in 2014, while manufacturers proposed revising voluntary standards to require most stock products to be cordless or have inaccessible cords. Experts recommend cordless or inaccessible cord window coverings in homes where children live or visit.

Peterborough City Council leader John Holdich highlighted council efforts to address housing, including £4 million for new homes and bringing 179 long-term empty private properties back into use last year through the Empty Homes strategy. Over five years, 663 empty homes have been returned to use, generating over £3 million from the New Homes Bonus scheme. He also noted the publication of Phase Two budget proposals and said government grants to the council have fallen from £55 million to £10 million over eight years, arguing Peterborough is unfairly funded due to outdated population figures. Holdich said Public Space Protection Orders introduced six months ago have led to fewer littering fines and less unauthorised cycling. He also announced the launch of CHUMS, a service supporting children and young people with mild to moderate mental health issues.

Chef and cookbook author Shannon Bard announced that Zapoteca, the Portland restaurant she owned with her husband, Tom, has closed permanently. Bard cited changing family priorities as their children grow older. The couple still operates Toroso, Salud, a cooking school and catering company. Zapoteca opened six years ago and inspired Bard’s 2015 cookbook.

The study was approved by Independent Ethics Committees at participating centers and conducted according to the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines. The study examined whether best supportive care plus high-volume, high-neutralizing-antibody convalescent plasma improved efficacy and safety outcomes versus supportive care alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients, with focus on clinical severity, oxygenation, ventilation, hospitalization, and need for mechanical ventilation.

The NAAIM Exposure Index, compiled weekly by the National Association of Active Investment Managers, measures the average reported exposure of its members to U.S. equity markets using a two-week moving average of survey responses. It is used to gauge investor sentiment, with high readings suggesting bullishness and low readings suggesting bearishness, and is sometimes viewed as a contrarian indicator. However, the passage states the index is not predictive and mainly reflects recent portfolio adjustments by active managers. Backtests found limited value in using the index for contrarian trading strategies, with low readings producing better returns than high readings but overall performance described as poor compared with other indicators such as the VIX.

Lubrizol Corp. will invest US$80 million to expand capacity and technology for its engineered polymers TPU business in North America, Europe, and Asia. The expansion includes new production capabilities, storage, logistics, and lines in Songjiang, China. Further investments are planned in Asia and Europe in 2019. The company reported 2016 revenues of US$6.5 billion.

Manchester City hosts Burnley at the Etihad Stadium on Jan. 2, needing a win to keep pace in the title race, while Burnley seeks points to avoid relegation. Sergio Aguero returns for City, with Kevin de Bruyne and David Silva key to breaking down Burnley. Burnley’s threats include Andre Gray and Sam Vokes, but they have struggled away from home.

Jeff Horn will defend his WBO welterweight title against Gary Corcoran in Brisbane, seeking to validate his disputed win over Manny Pacquiao and potentially set up major 2018 fights, including against Terence Crawford or Pacquiao. Promoter Bob Arum said a Horn win could lead to significant welterweight bouts. Horn remains focused on Corcoran, who is 17-1, ranked 10th by the WBO and fighting for his first world title outside Britain and Ireland. The buildup included accusations from Corcoran’s camp that Horn head-butted opponents, while Horn’s team dismissed the complaints. Both sides expect an aggressive fight.

President Trump announced Pfizer agreed to lower drug prices for Medicaid and patients and launch new medicines at parity with prices in other countries. In return, Pfizer may avoid certain tariffs if it continues investing in U.S. manufacturing. Policy experts said the deal’s impact on affordability and Medicaid budgets remains unclear, since Medicaid already receives low prices and rebates.

This preprint investigated neural noise in Tourette syndrome (TS) using EEG responses to single-pulse median nerve stimulation in 19 adults with TS and matched healthy controls. Neural noise was defined as trial-by-trial variability in response magnitude or timing. Early and mid-latency somatosensory evoked potential timing, temporal variability, and spatial topography were largely similar between groups, but the P2/P100 component was significantly larger in the TS group and associated with tic impairment. Trial-by-trial SEP amplitude variability was substantially higher in TS across the epoch, while coefficient-of-variation measures decreased after stimulation in both groups. Power spectral density analyses showed increased high-beta and gamma activity and flatter 1/f slopes in TS. Inter-trial phase coherence increased after stimulation in both groups, with some reduced or altered coherence patterns in TS. The authors conclude that sensorimotor population recruitment may be less stable at rest in TS but can normalize following somatosensory stimulation.

Facebook released a detailed public rule book outlining what posts are allowed on its platform, covering issues such as drug use, sex work, bullying, hate speech and violence. The company said the move is intended to clarify its policies and increase transparency amid criticism over both inadequate moderation and excessive removals. Users will now be able to appeal decisions on individual content takedowns, and Facebook will provide more specific removal reasons in more cases. The company uses automated tools and 7,500 moderators, and updates policies through regular internal reviews informed by outside experts. The new standards detail prohibited content, including certain drug-use admissions, harassment of minors, hacked material in most cases, and some graphic imagery. The rules do not cover government legal removal requests, false information, or personal data issues.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on June 20, 2017, it completed the issuance and sale of $1.0 billion aggregate principal amount of 3.000% Notes due June 20, 2027. A federal jury cleared retired Little Rock police lieutenant David Hudson of excessive-force claims over a 2011 incident in which he was recorded punching Jon “Chris” Erwin seven times outside Ferneau restaurant. After two days of testimony, jurors found Hudson’s use of force reasonable from his perspective. Erwin alleged the punches and takedown were unreasonable and caused injuries, while Hudson argued Erwin was intoxicated, resisted arrest and posed a potential threat. Charges against Erwin and a friend were later dropped for procedural reasons, but jurors did not hear that. The city of Little Rock and Ferneau’s owner settled Erwin’s claims before trial. The passage is an email sharing a Texas Monthly article titled “How Enron Blew It,” which examines Enron’s rise and troubles in 2001. The article describes Enron’s transformation from a pipeline company into a major energy trading firm under Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling, driven by deregulation, the Gas Bank concept, aggressive trading, and expansion into electricity, commodities, broadband, and online markets. It portrays Enron’s culture as focused on intelligence, risk-taking, speed, high compensation, intense competition, and harsh performance reviews.

The article says Enron’s success brought rapid revenue and stock growth, but also customer hard-nosedness, subjective mark-to-market accounting, internal pressure, secrecy, and weak loyalty. It details conflicts between Skilling’s asset-light trading vision and Rebecca Mark’s asset-heavy international projects, including problems with Dabhol in India and Azurix.

By 2001, Enron faced falling stock prices, criticism over California’s energy crisis, costly international projects, a failed broadband strategy, questions about accounting, negative press, and analyst concerns. Skilling resigned after six months as CEO, citing personal reasons, and Lay returned, promising a more focused and gentler Enron. The article concludes with Skilling expressing continued belief in new technologies, commodity trading, and Enron’s future.

U.S. statements on the war received little attention in the Finnish press. Finnish irritation toward German troops was increasing, though Finland remained dependent on Germany for military supplies and food. German influence was evident in pressure on the Finnish press and Nazi-style editing. War weariness and Social Democratic restiveness were growing, including a trade union petition warning that continued war would worsen conditions, especially food distribution. Discontent also appeared among ordinary Finns and soldiers, who questioned holding distant Soviet Karelia. The passage suggests Finnish resistance could weaken if the Soviet front stayed active.

Vyshinski told Thurston he had not heard rumors of Soviet-Finnish conversations. In Washington, Higgs warned Finnish representative Toivola that censorship of U.S. Legation calls and Finnish press attacks on the United States were damaging Finland’s position with its friends. Toivola agreed, said he would urge Helsinki to be more careful, and acknowledged that the press could not criticize Germany because of Finland’s dependence on it.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2018. Net sales rose to $51.0 billion from $35.7 billion in Q1 2017, with product sales of $31.6 billion and service sales of $19.4 billion. Net income increased to $1.6 billion from $724 million, and diluted earnings per share rose to $3.27 from $1.48. Operating income increased to $1.9 billion from $1.0 billion.
