Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash totaled $17.6 billion at March 31, 2018. Cash used in operating activities was $1.8 billion for the quarter, cash used in investing activities was $533 million, and cash used in financing activities was $2.2 billion. Total assets were $126.4 billion, total liabilities were $94.9 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $31.5 billion.

Amazon adopted new revenue recognition guidance on January 1, 2018, increasing retained earnings by about $650 million. The company reported $24.3 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding and no repurchases of common stock in Q1 2018. It acquired Ring Inc. on April 12, 2018 for approximately $900 million, net of cash acquired. The filing also describes tax matters, legal proceedings, contractual commitments, and risks affecting future results.

The coach said both teams face the same officiating standard, though tighter calls and frequent penalties have made it hard for either team to establish its style or for coaches to assess momentum and flow. He said his team must move the puck quicker, make technical adjustments through the neutral zone, and rely on simpler plays toward the net. He praised Detroit’s penalty killing intelligence and said his team’s power play is unlikely to improve through one or two simple fixes. He credited defensive restructuring after personnel changes with improving balance and allowing players to fit better by strength. He discussed challenges coaching in loud arenas, managing matchups, distributing ice time, and using the fourth line more. He said Arturs Irbe’s workload and mindset do not concern him and that he avoids overcoaching goaltenders. He described his coaching approach as adaptable, reliant on staff delegation, and rooted in his enjoyment of hockey. He also confirmed Sami Kapanen would play the point on the power play.

The paper addresses process modeling in Materials Science and Engineering (MSE), focusing on the extraction and reuse of ontology design patterns (ODPs) for scientific workflows. It identifies three domain-specific requirements: representing process structure, data and resources, and project goals with participant roles. The study analyzes relevant ontologies, including PMDcore, the General Process Ontology, WILD, P-PLAN, Metadata4Ing, and OPMW, and maps their support for Process, Resource, and Project ODPs.

A baseline automated extraction method is proposed using semantic similarity between natural-language requirements and ontology annotations. Ontology terms are embedded with sentence transformer models, ranked by cosine similarity, and evaluated against manually curated ground truth using precision, recall, and F1-score. ROBOT-based modular extraction is used to generate reusable ontology modules, with the STAR method and no intermediate classes selected as the default configuration.

Results show that P-PLAN performs best for Process and Resource ODPs, while PMDcore supports all three categories and has strong recall for Project ODPs. Metadata4Ing supports Resource and Project ODPs, OPMW supports Process and Resource ODPs, WILD supports Process ODPs, and GPO supports Process and Resource ODPs. The authors note limitations including dependence on annotation quality, sensitivity to requirement wording, independent processing of ontologies, and reliance on modularization. Future work will expand coverage to more MSE subdomains, incorporate ontology mappings, improve evaluation methods, and develop a platform for publishing extracted patterns and collecting community feedback.

Florida State linebacker Ethan Pritchard was released from Tallahassee Memorial Hospital nearly six weeks after being shot in the back of the head and moved to Brooks Rehabilitation in Jacksonville. FSU said he is alert, responsive and able to communicate. Authorities described the Aug. 31 shooting as mistaken identity, and four people were arrested. Pritchard’s father thanked supporters, medical staff, law enforcement and coach Mike Norvell, saying Ethan has “a long journey ahead.”

Old Forge High School students Christian Killino, Iain Kerrigan and Kole Barbetti organized a Math-a-thon for their senior project, raising $3,864 for St. Jude’s Research Hospital. Rosemarie Corigliano was installed as president of the Wayne Memorial Hospital Auxiliary, with other officers named for two-year terms; the group has upcoming fundraisers in July and September. Hannah Perry Burgess, owner of the Beekeeper’s Daughter and a fifth-generation beekeeper, presented a program on honey bees and conservation at a Scranton City DAR meeting.

GoDaddy gave neo-Nazi site The Daily Stormer 24 hours to move its domain after publisher Andrew Anglin posted an article mocking Heather Heyer, who was killed at the Charlottesville rally. GoDaddy said the post could incite further violence and violated its terms. The site later claimed it had been hacked, but contributor Andrew Auernheimer said that was a prank and that the site had alternate domain options. GoDaddy said it only managed the domain, not hosting. The passage also describes The Daily Stormer’s Nazi-inspired name, harassment campaigns, a lawsuit by Tanya Gersh, crowdfunding for Anglin’s legal expenses, and previous bans by PayPal and an advertising company.

In July 2021, Public Health Wales investigated a Salmonella Typhimurium outbreak after two gastroenteritis cases reported attending an Eid al-Adha barbecue in Cardiff. Case finding identified 22 symptomatic cases within a social network of 43 people, with most cases occurring after the barbecue and some later cases suggesting person-to-person transmission.

Investigators conducted cohort and nested case-control studies among attendees of the barbecue and associated lunch events, collected food histories, and performed microbiological and whole genome sequencing analyses. Consumption of the traditional raw liver dish “marrara” at the barbecue was identified as the most likely vehicle of infection. Firth regression found raw liver consumption was significantly associated with illness, while lamb and spicy sauce were not significant in the multivariable model. Severe illness was common: 12 cases sought emergency care, six were admitted, and one required intensive care.

Human isolates and raw lamb samples from leftovers, local butchers, and the supplying abattoir had genetically indistinguishable Salmonella Typhimurium sequences. Raw sheep’s liver samples were unavailable. The investigation suggested widespread contamination of sheep meat and possible cross-contamination during preparation and serving.

Public Health Wales developed culturally sensitive food safety messaging with community input, including multilingual materials and communications around World Food Safety Day and Eid al-Adha. The authors conclude that outbreak investigations linked to cultural events should consider community-specific foods beyond routine questionnaires, and that proactive messaging on raw or undercooked meat and offal may reduce public health risk.

A D.C. appeals court ruled the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service lacks authority under the Lacey Act to restrict interstate trade of Burmese pythons and other giant exotic snakes within the continental U.S., though import bans and state laws remain unaffected. The United States Association of Reptile Keepers sued in 2013 to challenge federal bans imposed in 2012 and expanded in 2015 to prevent invasive snakes from spreading, especially in Florida. The court said the law allows restrictions between the continental U.S. and territories such as Hawaii, not among the contiguous states. The wildlife service is reviewing the ruling and considering next steps. Reptile keepers called the ban unnecessary and overbroad, while environmental advocates warned the decision could affect efforts to control invasive species.

Fad diets, cleanses, and restrictive eating may cause temporary weight loss but are not sustainable. Bonnie Taub-Dix says healthy weight loss should focus on reconnecting with food, building a positive body relationship, moderation, and maintaining habits that support looking and feeling your best.

The speaker said their team began playing better after Holik’s chance, as the pace slowed and they started holding the puck, gaining confidence and making plays. They felt faceoffs were one of few advantages but said more areas must improve to beat New Jersey, which still controls much of the series. The team used three centers with four winger sets and plans lineup changes. The speaker emphasized emotion, past experience in long games, and the need to outplay New Jersey in more areas, while noting New Jersey still needs one win and remains in a strong position.

The passage argues that weakening family life and declining birth rates threaten the nation. It urges Congress to act on two issues: developing American shipping and reforming currency laws. The author supports legislation to encourage shipping, especially improved direct communication and fast mail lines with South America, arguing that lack of steamship connections disadvantages American business compared with Europe. On currency, the passage says the national bank act aided growth but current laws are defective, especially during crop seasons, causing severe call-money interest fluctuations, higher commercial rates, and credit uncertainty. It calls for revision while rejecting overly complicated plans or any measure impairing pledged United States 2 percent bonds. One proposed plan would let national banks issue a limited amount of taxed notes to meet emergencies during financial stringency, not to increase bank profits.

Gold Coast signed veteran Michael Gordon to a two-year NRL deal after his release from the Sydney Roosters, filling the Titans’ fullback vacancy following Jarryd Hayne’s departure. Gordon, 34, is also expected to take on goal kicking duties and said he was excited to return to his home region.

The passage describes the Coppock Curve Strategy, created by economist E.S.C. Coppock in 1965 as a long-term investment indicator. It is a smoothed momentum indicator mainly used for stock market swings, calculated as a 10-month weighted moving average of the sum of 11-month and 14-month rates of change. The strategy enters long when the curve crosses above zero and exits when it crosses below zero. Applied to monthly S&P 500 data, it produced few trades, including two six-year trades with gains of about 80% and 65%. Since 1960, the backtest showed 12 trades, reduced drawdowns, less market exposure, and higher risk-adjusted return than buy-and-hold. The passage concludes the strategy remains valid for exploiting market bullish bias while filtering corrections.

Morgan “Dr. Noc” McSweeney, a biotech scientist and social media influencer, discusses using “edutainment” to communicate public health and science topics online. He says effective science content should be engaging, nuanced, and aimed especially at people who are confused rather than strongly opposed. His videos include reactions to misinformation, explanations of health research, and nonpolarizing science topics that can bring broader audiences to evidence-based content.

McSweeney says public audiences often want detailed explanations rather than simplified dismissals, citing acetaminophen and autism as an example. He argues that institutions like the WHO, CDC, NIH, and FDA have not invested enough in influencer-style communication and face resource, review, and format challenges. He also says science communicators should show some personal humanity because trust depends not only on credentials and data but also on the messenger. He keeps his biotech job separate from his content, avoids engaging hostile comments, and believes more diverse experts should create evidence-based health content.

Nick Foles, the Eagles’ backup quarterback, entered Super Bowl LII with a chance to lead Philadelphia to its first Super Bowl win after Carson Wentz’s knee injury ended his MVP-caliber season. Even if Foles wins, the passage says Wentz remains the Eagles’ long-term starter, assuming his recovery stays on track for 2018. Foles’ future is less certain: Philadelphia could keep him as a valuable backup or trade him while his value is high, especially with potential interest from quarterback-needy teams and Howie Roseman’s history of making trades. Foles is unlikely to force a move, having embraced a supporting role behind Wentz. The passage concludes that Foles’ career could take more unexpected turns regardless of the Super Bowl outcome.

The speaker congratulates the 100th Congress during the Constitution’s bicentennial, honors new congressional leadership, and calls for cooperation. He cites economic progress, including lower inflation, interest rates, unemployment, and job growth, while accepting responsibility for mistakes in the Iran initiative. He urges support for defense spending, security assistance, opposition to Soviet expansion, aid to Afghan and Nicaraguan anti-communist forces, and continued pursuit of arms reductions without weakening SDI.

Domestically, he calls for a balanced budget amendment, a line-item veto, adherence to deficit-reduction targets, no tax increases, welfare reform, protection against catastrophic illness for the elderly, competitiveness initiatives, fair trade, education improvements, anti-drug efforts, voluntary school prayer, worker retraining, and agricultural support. He frames the Constitution’s principle of “We the people” as the foundation of American government and concludes by affirming optimism about America’s future.

The passage references TMS320DM814x device documentation on L4 peripheral memory maps, interconnect details, and DDR DMM TILER extended addressing. The TILER provides an additional 4-GB address range via a 33rd address bit for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views, fully accessible only to HDVPSS and ISS, while other masters can access one view through the 512-MB base map region. It also describes package pin assignment figures and terminal function tables covering signal names, pin multiplexing, pin types, pullup/pulldown states, supply voltages, and functions. Boot configuration pins are multiplexed with GPMC functions, sampled at reset for ARM Cortex-A8 boot settings, and then used as GPMC data/address pins.

The speaker says the team must not be outworked and needs to play for each other. They felt not everyone contributed in the Stanley Cup Final, and the only game they fully came to play was the one they won. They said the team has shifted from defensive focus to trying to score, is out of sync offensively, and must get more shots to the net.

The author wrote the book to address repeated reimplementation in distributed system development. Containers and orchestrators enable reusable components and shared patterns, making reliable distributed systems more approachable, efficient, and standardized for developers.

UND Campus Senate Chair Dana Harsell said the executive committee will discuss an NDSU Faculty Senate draft resolution on concerns within the North Dakota University System. The draft cites a “crisis of confidence” tied to budget cuts, consolidation efforts and perceived lack of support, and calls for stronger collaboration with the State Board of Higher Education, Chancellor Mark Hagerott and state leaders, including a Higher Education Summit. Harsell said UND will consider whether the wider senate supports it, though circumstances may change.

Energy Central’s February 20, 2002 Research Report Watch is a bi-weekly HTML email listing newly published power industry research, reports newly posted to Energy Central, and new white papers. National Weather Service Lubbock issued updated zone forecasts for the South Plains area on March 18, 2018. A wind advisory was in effect until 7 a.m. Monday across listed Texas zones. Conditions were mostly clear and windy overnight with areas or patches of blowing dust. Monday was forecast to be sunny and windy, with colder mostly clear conditions Monday night. The week was expected to be mostly sunny and dry, warming from highs in the 60s Tuesday to the 80s and lower 90s by Thursday and Friday. A 20 percent chance of thunderstorms was forecast Saturday night for King, Garza, Kent, and Stonewall counties.

Patrick Kane discussed possible Blackhawks lineup changes, comparing Zdeno Chara’s reach to Ryan Suter’s and emphasizing using speed rather than overthinking the matchup. He said playing overseas was beneficial, reflected on the difficulty of seeing another team win the Cup after Chicago, and noted the excitement and attention surrounding another Stanley Cup Final. Kane praised Boston’s defense and Tuukka Rask while saying Chicago’s depth will be needed. He also said he and teammates have improved since their previous Cup run, especially defensively, and highlighted backchecking, fan enthusiasm in Chicago, and his focus on wanting the puck and making plays.

The lecture covers sustainable finance for real estate at the asset level, focusing on how capital supports green, healthy, and climate-resilient buildings. Sustainable real estate value begins with tenants and users: if they value lower operating costs, better indoor air quality, or resilience, they may pay rent premiums, which can translate into higher owner income and developer sale prices.

The lecture frames sustainable finance as an emerging field influenced by Larry Fink’s 2020 statement that climate risk is financial risk. Real estate fits into this framework through both space markets and capital markets. Individuals act as tenants and investors, directing demand and capital toward sustainable assets. Investors compare an asset’s expected return with their weighted average cost of capital; investments proceed when returns exceed capital costs or net present value is positive.

Portfolio theory is used to explain why green buildings may attract capital. Compared with conventional or “brown” buildings, true green buildings may have higher net operating income due to regulation and tenant preferences, and lower discount rates due to reduced risk. Brown buildings may face penalties, lower demand, higher risk premiums, and declining value. Green buildings can shift efficient frontiers outward, attracting capital, though increased demand may later reduce expected returns.

The debt side focuses on mortgages and climate risk. Properties exposed to flooding, wildfire, hurricanes, or other risks may lose value, increasing delinquency and default risk. Research cited on California wildfires found higher default rates in fire zones. The lecture also discusses challenges for Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, flood insurance, and climate-risk appraisal, noting tensions between accurate risk pricing and social equity for lower-income households in risky locations.

Green mortgages are presented as a positive financing tool. Banks may lend more or charge lower rates for energy-efficient homes because such homes may have higher values, lower utility bills, and lower default risk. Studies cited find energy-efficient homes and commercial buildings have lower default risk, with stronger effects for low-income households. The lecture also describes financing renovation by lending more upfront based on expected post-renovation value increases.

A blitz in football is a defensive play where five or more defenders rush into the offensive backfield to pressure the quarterback or disrupt the ball carrier. Teams normally rush four players, but blitzes send extra defenders to create quicker pressure, sacks, bad throws, or disrupted runs. Blitzing carries risk because fewer defenders remain in coverage, and mobile quarterbacks can evade pressure.

Defensive coordinators call blitzes as part of broader defensive strategy to stop the run, defend the pass, and get the offense off the field. Common types include zone blitzes, where a linebacker rushes and another defender drops into coverage; safety and cornerback blitzes, which use defensive backs to create surprise pressure; zero blitzes, which leave no deep safety; and run blitzes, designed to stop rushing plays quickly.

Offenses can beat blitzes with quick passes, mobile quarterbacks, or max protection schemes that keep extra blockers near the quarterback. Effective quarterbacks identify blitzes and find the weak point in the defense.

Romania’s rapidly changing technological, informational and social context makes lifelong learning essential for Library and Information Science professionals. The Romanian library system includes the National Library, public, educational and specialised libraries, under different ministries and local authorities, with two main professional associations. LIS higher education developed after 1999, with four universities still offering programmes.

Romanian librarian training includes three routes: a bachelor’s degree in LIS; a bachelor’s degree in another field plus postgraduate LIS training; or competences acquired outside formal education and assessed through occupational standards. LIS programmes have low appeal due to low professional prestige, salaries and educational investment. Postgraduate LIS programmes attract graduates from diverse fields but function as initial rather than advanced education. Non-formal training includes library visits, professional events, tutoring and mentoring, though institutions rarely provide required financial support for staff training.

The 2012 national Occupational Standard for Librarian (higher education), developed by the National Library of Romania and recognised by the National Authority for Qualifications, defines required competences and activities. These include communication, digital, social, civic, entrepreneurial and cultural competences; work organisation; legal, safety and environmental compliance; and management of library documents. It also details professional activities such as collection development, cataloguing, conservation, user services, automation, digitisation, promotion, research, methodological work and management planning.

The passage concludes that the standard is important for professional assessment and promotion, but should better address internationalisation, multicultural adaptation, information literacy, reading promotion and psycho-pedagogical skills for librarians working with children. Lifelong learning is hindered by outdated stereotypes of librarianship, so LIS institutions and methodological libraries should adapt programmes to new professional competences.

The passage introduces a model of information design that integrates behavioral framing effects with Bayesian persuasion. It argues that traditional models focus on correlations between signals and states, while evidence from behavioral economics shows that wording, context, and other framing cues affect decisions. The authors propose a framework where a sender can influence a receiver through both recommendation schemes and framings that induce beliefs.

The work studies three variants: recommendation-only, framing-only, and joint framing-and-recommendation optimization. Using an LLM-inspired belief oracle that maps framings to receiver beliefs, the authors find that framing-only optimization is discontinuous and computationally hard, while joint optimization is more tractable, continuous, and admits a quasi-polynomial-time approximation scheme. Empirically, they implement a hill-climbing method using LLMs for framing optimization and belief estimation, combined with analytical recommendation optimization. Case studies involving real estate and clothing advertising show strong LLM-measured effectiveness, with human-subject results directionally supporting the predictions but showing more variance.

The passage also situates the work among related research on algorithmic information design, LLM-based persuasion, framing effects, and using LLMs as proxies for human behavior.

The passage describes several container and distributed system patterns. The adapter pattern uses a separate container to make heterogeneous application interfaces conform to expected standards, such as monitoring, logging, or health checks. Examples include adapting Redis metrics for Prometheus, normalizing logs with Fluentd, and adding rich MySQL health checks without modifying the database container.

It then introduces microservices as multi-node systems composed of independently deployed components communicating through defined APIs. Microservices improve reliability, agility, team independence, and scaling, but make debugging and architecture more difficult.

Replicated load-balanced services are presented for stateless applications. Multiple identical replicas sit behind a load balancer to improve availability and horizontal scale. Readiness probes indicate when replicas can serve traffic. Variations include session-tracked services, caching layers using tools such as Varnish, rate limiting, denial-of-service defense, and SSL termination with nginx.

Sharded services divide requests or data among shards, usually for stateful systems whose data exceeds one machine’s capacity. Sharded caches improve memory utilization compared with replicated caches but require careful planning for failures, upgrades, hot shards, and sharding functions. Consistent hashing reduces remapping when shard counts change.

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing by sending work to multiple leaf nodes and combining partial results at a root. It is useful for independent computation such as document search, but overhead, stragglers, and availability risks increase with the number of leaves. Replicating shards improves reliability and scalability.

The passage also discusses function-as-a-service and event-driven processing. FaaS simplifies deployment, scaling, and modularity, but complicates observability, dependency tracking, background processing, memory-heavy workloads, and sustained high-volume cost models. Suitable patterns include request/response decorators, event handlers, two-factor authentication workflows, and event-based pipelines.

The lecture introduces the second-order wave equation \(u_{tt}=c^2u_{xx}\) and its equivalent first-order system form, whose symmetric matrix has eigenvalues \(c\) and \(-c\), representing waves traveling in opposite directions. The professor notes that real wave problems may involve variable coefficients, forcing terms, high frequencies, boundaries, and higher dimensions, making numerical treatment harder.

The continuous wave equation is analyzed using exponential solutions, showing two characteristic directions and a general solution as a sum of functions of \(x-ct\) and \(x+ct\). Initial displacement and velocity determine the solution, with waves propagating along characteristic lines.

The lecture then studies semidiscrete methods, where space is discretized but time remains continuous, also called the method of lines. Substituting exponential modes into the second-difference spatial approximation reveals dispersion: different frequencies behave differently because the discrete factor involves trigonometric terms rather than simply \(k^2\). For small \(\Delta x\), the approximation is consistent and second-order accurate.

Finally, the fully discrete leapfrog scheme is introduced, using centered second differences in both time and space. Stability is examined through a growth factor \(g\), leading to a quadratic equation. Stability requires both roots to have magnitude at most 1, which corresponds to the Courant condition \(r=c\Delta t/\Delta x \leq 1\). The next lecture will discuss staggered grids.

The study investigates high-energy (1 MeV) electron beam irradiation as a controllable method for defect engineering in CVD-grown monolayer MoS2. Samples were irradiated for 30, 60, and 120 seconds at constant beam energy and flux, then analyzed using Raman spectroscopy, photoluminescence, XPS, KPFM, circular polarization-resolved PL, and first-principles calculations.

Raman and PL results show irradiation-induced disorder, increased defect density, exciton blueshifts, and PL quenching. XPS reveals Mo-O bonding and increasing Mo6+ signals with longer irradiation, indicating oxidation at sulfur vacancy sites, while KPFM shows an increased work function consistent with p-type doping. Low-temperature PL identifies defect-bound emissions 200–300 meV below the A exciton, which intensify with irradiation time and are linked to oxygen-related sulfur vacancy states. Power-dependent PL confirms increased optically active defect states after irradiation.

Circular polarization-resolved PL shows that valley polarization decreases from 62% in the as-grown sample to 38% after 120 seconds of irradiation, attributed to defect-mediated intervalley transitions and carrier trapping. First-principles calculations support the experimental findings by showing that oxygen interactions at sulfur vacancies create acceptor-like defect states near the valence band, explaining the defect emission and p-type behavior. The work demonstrates that high-energy electron irradiation can tune defect states and excitonic behavior in monolayer MoS2, with potential applicability to other TMDs.

The Wing-T offense uses misdirection, unusual formations, and a varied run game to exploit aggressive or undisciplined defenses by making different plays look similar. Developed by Harold “Tubby” Raymond at the University of Delaware, it is often called the Delaware Wing-T. It typically requires at least two capable running backs, including a strong fullback, an athletic quarterback with good footwork, and quick offensive linemen who can pull and trap.

Its strengths include slowing defenses through deception, play action, motion, and uncommon formations, while experienced coaches can adjust to defensive looks. Its main weakness is the lack of a traditional dropback passing game, though teams can add shotgun spread formations.

Common formations include the Wing, Wing-Slot, and unbalanced sets. Common runs include Buck Sweep, Down/Belly G, and Trap. Common passes include Waggle, single-receiver option routes, and play-action vertical passes. The traditional Wing-T is rare in major college football but remains common in high school, and its principles have influenced spread offenses, including those used by Gus Malzahn.

The ADS868xW enters ACQ state on power-up, after asynchronous reset, or after each conversion to acquire the analog input signal. RST falling edge moves it to RESET, and CONVST/CS rising edge starts CONV state. In CONV state, conversion uses an internal clock, ignores further CONVST/CS transitions during tconv, then returns to ACQ. The host monitors RVS or waits tconv_max before starting another operation.

The device has nine configuration registers and supports data write and read operations. A data transfer frame begins on the CONVST/CS falling edge and ends on the next rising edge, which starts conversion. During a frame, SCLK shifts data into SDI and out through SDO-x. A 32-SCLK frame is optimal and treated as a valid command; fewer clocks create a short frame treated as NOP for writes but valid for reading MSBs; more clocks create a long frame using the last 32 input bits as the command.

Programming uses 32-bit commands, including byte and half-word read/write, set, and clear operations. HWORD commands ignore the LSB of the 9-bit address. Output data in the next frame depends on DATA_VAL settings and the prior command: fixed patterns, register data after READ or READ_HWORD, or the latest 16-bit conversion result. Optional flags include device address, input range, AVDD alarms, input alarms, and parity.

The multiSPI interface supports legacy SPI-compatible protocols for writes and reads, single or dual SDO output, and source-synchronous read protocols using RVS as an output clock. On power-up or reset, SPI-00-S is used until SDI_MODE is programmed. Dual SDO mode halves the clock cycles needed to output the same number of bits.

The register map includes DEVICE_ID_REG, RST_PWRCTL_REG, SDI_CTL_REG, SDO_CTL_REG, DATAOUT_CTL_REG, RANGE_SEL_REG, ALARM_REG, ALARM_H_TH_REG, and ALARM_L_TH_REG. These configure device ID, reset and power modes, serial protocols, output data, input range and reference, alarms, and alarm thresholds.

The ADS868xW is a 16-bit SAR ADC data acquisition device with integrated analog front end, programmable gain amplifier, ADC driver, precision reference, buffer, overvoltage protection, input alarm, and AVDD alarm. An example industrial module combines ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 for voltage, current, or temperature sensing. The input alarm supports programmable high and low thresholds and hysteresis.

The device uses AVDD and DVDD supplies with recommended decoupling. It supports NAP and power-down modes to reduce power consumption. NAP is enabled through RST_PWRCTL_REG and entered when CONVST/CS remains high after conversion; power-down disables analog blocks while retaining interface activity and registers. Layout guidance includes separating analog and digital sections, using close bypass capacitors, and decoupling REFCAP and REFIO.

Co-defendants Richard Gregory Williams III and Kipling Deshawn Colbert received 143 and 109 years, respectively, including sentences for unrelated charges.

Corning Incorporated, founded in 1851, built its identity around science-based innovation in specialty glass, ceramics, and materials. Its history included major products and businesses such as railroad signal glass, Edison light bulbs, Pyrex, television glass, fiberglass, silicones, optical fiber, catalytic converter substrates, medical services, LCD glass, diesel filters, and life sciences products.

After rapid growth in telecommunications during the late 1990s, Corning was hit hard by the 2001–2002 telecom crash: revenues fell from $6.3 billion in 2001 to $3.1 billion in 2002, the stock dropped from $100 to $1.50, the company took a $5.4 billion loss, and more than 12,000 employees were laid off. By 2008, Corning had recovered, with 24,800 employees, renewed telecom sales, leadership in LCD glass, a stock price near $23, and about 70% of laid-off employees back at the company.

Corning managed innovation through centralized governance, especially the Growth and Strategy Council (GSC), led by CEO Wendell Weeks, COO Peter Volanakis, and CTO Joe Miller. The GSC met regularly to advise businesses, allocate resources, review portfolios, and guide high-potential innovation programs, especially later-stage projects. It worked alongside the Corning Technology Council, which reviewed earlier-stage technologies. Corning also created a centralized new business development function in 2005.

Corning’s innovation model emphasized deep technology expertise, customer systems problems, protected intellectual property, world-class manufacturing, disciplined stage-gate reviews, and “patient money” for long-term opportunities. The company spent about 10% of revenue on research, development, and engineering, with corporate funding supporting research for both current businesses and future opportunities.

The GSC helped balance resources across businesses, challenge assumptions, and support major decisions such as investment in diesel filters and fiber-to-the-home technologies. Managers credited it with encouraging frank dialogue and reducing siloed decision-making, though some criticized large meeting sizes and presentation pressure. Future challenges included maintaining honest discussion, prioritizing programs, scaling the process as Corning sought faster new-business creation, and understanding unfamiliar markets and business models.

The passage describes the S&P 500 Financial Services sector as companies classified under GICS Financial Services, including banks, investment firms, insurers, and fintech companies serving individuals, SMEs, and corporations. The sector is tracked by ETFs such as Vanguard Financials ETF (VFH) and Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLF). It lists major financial stocks by market capitalization as of July 2022, including Berkshire Hathaway, JP Morgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup, and Goldman Sachs. The passage notes that the financial sector fell 85% from its 2007 peak during the 2008/09 crisis, leading many investors to avoid it, though it says the sector has since changed and consolidated. It presents a backtested XLF trading strategy with 198 trades, 1.05% average gain, 73% win rate, 21% max drawdown, and 2.25 profit factor, emphasizing the sector’s high volatility and correlation with the broader market.

San Miguel Pure Foods is delaying its planned P100-150 billion follow-on offering to the third or fourth quarter due to market volatility and other stock rights offerings. The sale aims to raise public float after its merger with Ginebra San Miguel and San Miguel Brewery into San Miguel Food and Beverage. SMPFC reported 2017 net income of P6.9 billion, up 16%, on revenues of P117 billion.

The passage presents a scalable fabrication method for visible-range Fabry–Perot microcavities using buckled dielectric membrane mirrors. The approach starts with double-sided polished silicon wafers, applies repeated wet thermal oxidation and HF removal to reduce surface roughness to about 50–33 pm, deposits SiO₂/Ta₂O₅ dielectric stacks, and releases circular mirrors by backside etching. Built-in compressive strain causes the suspended mirrors to buckle into concave shapes with reproducible, rotationally symmetric profiles and radii of curvature from 0.9 mm to 21 mm.

The resulting microcavities achieve high performance at 780.24 nm. Ring-down measurements show a maximum finesse of 0.89 × 10⁶ with linewidth κ = (2π) 233 ± 1 kHz, and a maximum quality factor of 2.3 × 10⁹ with κ = (2π) 124 ± 0.5 kHz. Loss analysis bounds absorption plus scattering at ≤2.20 ppm and implies an upper surface-roughness bound of ≤90 pm, with performance comparable to state-of-the-art visible dielectric coating loss. Finesse decreases with increasing cavity length due to diffractive loss, while Q initially rises and then falls at longer lengths.

The method also supports compact assembled cavities. Manually glued mirror-chip assemblies produced 45 µm and 1 mm cavities, with the 45 µm device showing a linewidth of (2π) 5.16 ± 0.14 MHz and an FSR of 3.18 THz. The authors conclude that these micromirrors and microcavities combine high finesse, small size, standard silicon fabrication, small mode volume, and flexible integration, making them relevant for visible lasers, sensing, quantum networking, filters, transfer cavities, and external resonators.

Amazon is developing a top-secret domestic robot project codenamed “Vesta,” overseen by Gregg Zehr at its Lab126 hardware division. The company has increased hiring for robotics roles and may test robots in employees’ homes by the end of the year, with possible consumer release as early as 2019, though plans could change. The robot’s functions are unclear, but sources speculate it may act as a mobile Alexa. Prototypes reportedly use advanced cameras and computer vision to navigate homes. The project is separate from Amazon Robotics’ warehouse robots. The passage notes past challenges in domestic robotics, with iRobot’s Roomba as a major success, and says advances in AI, vision, cameras and voice activation could support Amazon’s effort. Research and Markets estimates the consumer robot market could reach $15 billion annually by 2023.

Nigeria is seeing growth in shopping malls, especially in Lagos, driven by demand for convenient one-stop shopping, brand-conscious consumers and after-work shopping needs. Emmanuel Efuntayo of Ibukun Efuntayo & Co said the trend reflects investor confidence and economic development. Major retailers such as Shoprite and Spar have expanded in the country. The malls are described as beneficial for creating jobs, improving shopping experiences and increasing government tax revenues.

The passage describes computer-implemented methods, systems, and program products for creating and simulating digital twin models of physical assets. Real-time data from sensors, IoT devices, and recording systems is used to create and update digital twin models that reflect asset components, configurations, performance, maintenance, repairs, and other changes over time. Multiple timestamped versions of a digital twin may be stored, managed, and compared.

The disclosed simulation system allows users to select a current, previous, base, or hybrid digital twin model for simulation. Hybrid models may combine components from multiple digital twin versions. Users may configure simulations to bypass selected components, substitute alternative components, provide overriding intermediate values for non-simulated portions, and focus analysis on selected components. Simulation results may include intermediate and final outputs, which can be reported, archived, reviewed, rerun, or used to revise simulation parameters.

The system may operate in networked, cloud, distributed, or containerized computing environments. It includes modules for digital twin creation, data collection, version management, simulation, and reporting. The passage also describes supporting data processing, storage, communication, cloud service, and containerization infrastructure.

Paul Tisdale said Exeter City could be proud of their performance despite a 1-0 defeat at league leaders Luton Town. Exeter were missing six defenders and gave 20-year-old Jordan Storey his first league start, but lost only to Harry Cornick’s deflected strike. Tisdale said Luton deserved to win on the balance of play, though Exeter defended well and nearly equalised late on. Liam McAlinden had a goal ruled out for a foul by Robbie Simpson on goalkeeper Marek Stech, a decision Tisdale disagreed with but said was consistent with the referee’s approach. He praised Matt Taylor and Andy Tillson for preparing Storey to step up from seventh-choice centre-back. Tisdale added that Exeter’s form remained strong despite the result, ahead of their match against Wycombe Wanderers.

At reset de-assertion, BTMODE[15:0] pins are sampled and latched into CONTROL_STATUS. BTMODE[15:11] configure GPMC CS0 settings, BTMODE[4:0] determine boot order, BTMODE[7:5] are reserved, BTMODE[9:8] select Ethernet PHY mode for EMAC boot, and BTMODE[10] selects GPMC muxing for XIP modes.

WhatsApp, India’s dominant messaging app, is gradually expanding beyond chat into services such as calls and payments, similar to WeChat’s ecosystem. The passage argues that mobile internet competition centers on user engagement through content, payments, gaming, and integrated services. Hike, backed by Airtel, could compete by bundling payments with Airtel TV and Wynk content. Gaming initiatives like Paytm’s Gamepind show another engagement route. The broader Indian internet market is becoming an oligopoly backed by major global conglomerates.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting results from its March 10, 2015 Annual Meeting of Shareholders. Shareholders elected Tim Cook, Al Gore, Bob Iger, Andrea Jung, Art Levinson, Ron Sugar, and Sue Wagner as directors. They approved ratifying Ernst & Young LLP as the independent registered public accounting firm for 2015, approved executive compensation on an advisory basis, and approved amending the Employee Stock Purchase Plan to add 50,000,000 authorized shares. Shareholder proposals titled “Risk Report” and “Proxy Access for Shareholders” were not approved. The amended and restated Employee Stock Purchase Plan was filed as Exhibit 10.1.

Environment and Climate Change Canada found that more than a dozen studied phthalates posed no human health risk, with one needing further environmental study. Environmental Defence criticized the decision, citing EU findings and urging Canada to modernize chemical laws. Minister Catherine McKenna said the government is considering recommended reforms and will present a plan by June 2018.

A security appliance is described that provides network security functions such as packet inspection, filtering, blocking, forwarding, modification, and rule management. Unlike appliances managed only through a network connection, it may include a local input/output interface, such as a multi-touch display, allowing administrators to control configuration and mitigation actions during denial-of-service attacks or other conditions that impair remote access. Commands from the local interface may receive priority access to memory and processing resources, enabling actions such as shutting down ports, blacklisting sources, changing filter rules, or reordering rule priorities without rebooting or disconnecting the device.

The passage also describes using geoprocessing-based analysis for packet filtering, mapping packet parameters such as IP addresses, ports, protocols, payload sizes, and other fields to spatial regions and searching them with R-tree indexes to improve rule-matching speed. It further describes distributing security rules from a management server to appliances, with mandatory rules sent to all devices and potential rules distributed according to likelihood or weight, reducing memory, bandwidth, and processing requirements while allowing detection of emerging attacks.

The appliance may buffer or block packets from unrecognized devices until a local user authorizes them through the interface. It may display notifications, log events, reserve resources for the interface during attacks, and discard packets if no authorization or interaction occurs within a specified time. The described systems may be implemented using computing devices with processors, memory, network interfaces, storage, and input/output components.

The passage argues that narrow standardized testing options constrain school choice by influencing curriculum and teaching methods. It cites studies showing educators adjust instruction in response to high-stakes tests and gives examples of states requiring private school choice participants or public students to take specific exams such as the Wisconsin Forward Exam, ACT, or SAT. It criticizes reliance on the College Board and ACT, claiming some exams have lowered rigor or narrowed academic expectations. Rather than banning standardized tests, the passage supports testing choice, including alternatives such as the Classic Learning Test. It recommends that states offer multiple assessment options for school choice programs, public college admissions, scholarships, and graduation requirements, citing Arkansas and Florida as examples.

The Supreme Court will hear a challenge to Colorado’s 2019 Minor Conversion Therapy Law, which bars licensed mental health professionals from providing conversion therapy to minors but exempts religious ministry. Therapist Kaley Chiles argues the law violates her free speech rights because her counseling uses only speech and the ban discriminates based on viewpoint, requiring strict scrutiny. Lower courts refused to block enforcement, finding the law regulates professional conduct that incidentally involves speech and survives rational basis review. The federal government supports sending the case back for strict scrutiny.

Colorado argues the law regulates unsafe and ineffective healthcare treatment, not speech, and was enacted to protect minors amid evidence linking conversion therapy to depression, anxiety, suicidal thoughts, and suicide attempts. The state says the ban is narrow, targets only treatment aimed at changing a minor’s sexual orientation or gender identity, and would survive even strict scrutiny. Both sides warn of broader consequences for regulation of professional-client conversations and healthcare standards.

A Canadian Society of Palliative Care Physicians report concludes that expanding palliative and hospice care across Canada would improve care while reducing costs. Based on published economic studies, it says hospital-based palliative care saves about $7,000 to $8,000 per patient, outpatient services can reduce direct health care costs by about 30%, and home-based care can reduce use of more expensive services. An Ontario projection estimated expanded in-home palliative care could cost $76 million to $108 million annually while avoiding $191 million to $385 million in health costs. The report also says shifting patients from acute care to residential hospices can save about $600 per day. The CSPCP recommends federal, provincial, and territorial action to improve, monitor, and evaluate access and quality.

David Murray criticised ASX corporate governance principles, arguing they have become overly prescriptive and contributed to weaker governance and a trust deficit in the financial sector. He called for institutions to reassess internal failures and develop new mechanisms to strengthen governance practices.

The seventh Johnston Press South Business Awards were held at Brighton’s Grand Hotel and presented by Nick Wallis. Chichester’s Guardian Angel Carers won Overall Business of the Year and Large Business of the Year. Olive and Vine in Midhurst won Place to Eat or Drink, while Brandon Relph of Go Creative in Eastbourne won Young Achiever. Southsea Bathing Hut in Portsmouth was named Retailer of the Year, and Talks at Six in Chichester won Outstanding Contribution to the Community after raising over £7,500 for charity. Other winners included Gardiner and Scardifield for Customer Service, Ricardo Plc for Innovation, Nature Shop for Green Business, Digi Tool Box Ltd for Employer of the Year, and Dawn Lawrence for Business Personality of the Year.

The court affirmed judgment for the defendants in a collision damage case. It held that the trial court properly instructed the jury on the plaintiff’s negligence allegations, including failure to sound a horn, and was not required without request to charge on right-of-way or speed reduction where those issues were not pleaded. Charges on lawful highway use, statutory and ordinance violations, comparative negligence, and damages were not reversible error. The evidence was conflicting, and the verdict for defendants was authorized.

Gardaí in Louth appealed for information on the murder of 18-year-old Cameron Reilly, whose body was found in Dunleer with neck injuries. They are seeking his iPhone, believed key to the investigation, and urged the community to come forward. Separately, gardaí in west Dublin seized a semi-automatic shotgun, arrested two people, and recovered drugs worth about €1m during an organised crime operation.
The Central Bank of Nigeria introduced FORM X to ease forex access for SMEs and retail businesses needing $10,000 or less, requiring basic documentation for genuine transactions.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K reporting that on June 16, 2019, its Board appointed Donald F. Robertson Jr. as Vice President, Chief Accounting Officer and Principal Accounting Officer, effective June 17, 2019. He will report to CFO Colette Kress. Robertson previously held accounting and finance leadership roles at Western Digital and SanDisk and is a certified public accountant. He replaces Michael Byron, who will become Vice President, Finance, Merger & Acquisition Integration and Financial Systems.

Robertson’s at-will offer includes a $650,000 annual salary, a $600,000 sign-on bonus subject to repayment if employment ends before one year, 15,000 restricted stock units vesting over about four years, eligibility for NVIDIA’s employee stock purchase plan and benefits, and a standard indemnity agreement.

The passage describes techniques for enhanced trick-play playback, such as fast-forward and rewind, for streamed video. The system uses metadata, including frame address information or indexes, to identify specific frames such as key frames within one or more video streams. A client maintains a normal playback buffer with continuous video content and a separate trick-play window that stores only selected frames from portions outside the normal buffer, avoiding download of intervening frames. During trick-play, the player displays the selected buffered frames to provide faster-than-real-time playback with frequent updates and lower latency.

The system may select frames based on playback rate, anticipated trick-play behavior, streaming performance metrics, frame size, bitrate, and available streams. It may adaptively choose frames from different bitrate streams and later expand the normal buffer by downloading missing intervening frames without re-requesting frames already stored. Multiple trick-play windows may support different speeds or quality levels. Trick-play buffering may begin in response to user input, predicted movement beyond the normal buffer, or proximity to metadata-defined jump points.

The architecture includes video repositories, streaming servers, optional proxy servers, streaming clients, video players, performance monitors, and trick-play optimizers. Proxy servers may generate metadata, indexes, proxy streams, or jump points when origin servers lack support. The techniques may be used with protocols such as HLS and may support adaptive bitrate streaming, live or stored content, key-frame indexing, audio or trick-play indexes, and buffer management for smoother playback.

Breast cancer is the most common cancer in the UK, with around 56,000 new cases each year. Breast lumps can vary in size and texture, sometimes feeling pea-like, hard, irregular, or larger, and may occur in the breast or armpit. People are advised to regularly check their breasts and armpits, looking for unfamiliar lumps, swelling, dimpling, changes in breast shape or size, nipple changes, discharge, rashes, redness, dryness, or unexplained pain.

Self-checking can be done in front of a mirror, lying down, sitting up, or in the bath or shower, using circular motions across the breast and armpit. Checking every two weeks to once a month, ideally at the same time each month, helps identify what is normal and spot changes.

A doctor should assess any concerning lump or change. They may ask about medical and family history, medicines, smoking, alcohol, and how the lump was noticed, then examine and refer if needed.

Risk factors include some hormone treatments, genetic mutations, early periods, later menopause, age at childbirth, and not having children. Risk may be reduced through an active lifestyle, maintaining a healthy weight, and breastfeeding. Men can also develop breast cancer, usually as a lump or nipple change. Early diagnosis improves treatment effectiveness and survival.

Travis Haydon, 20, was jailed for 18 months after stabbing Liam Brown in the stomach with a flick knife during an argument over a spilt drink at Plymouth’s Newmarket Tavern. Haydon admitted assault causing actual bodily harm, possessing a knife in public, cannabis possession, and breaching a suspended sentence for affray. Plymouth Crown Court heard Brown suffered a two-centimetre puncture wound, was kept in hospital overnight, and was not thought to have lasting damage. Recorder Paul Grumbar cited Haydon’s record for violence and weapons, saying knife offences usually lead to prison. Haydon’s defence said he feared being punched, had complied with parts of his previous order, and had an ill father.

SPYR, Inc. announced it will issue shareholders of record as of May 19, 2017, a 1-for-1 dividend of shares in a new spin-off company created to divest its restaurant division. The new company is expected to file a registration statement with the SEC to become a separate publicly traded entity with its own ticker symbol. SPYR said the spin-off will focus on licensing or franchising the Eat at Joe’s name and concept, manufacturing and distributing branded foods, and potentially acquiring companies with food concepts. Stock Market Media Group disclosed it publishes SPYR-related content under a paid agreement with SPYR, including a $5,000 monthly fee and 250,000 restricted common shares.

Researchers described Breugnathair elgolensis, a 167-million-year-old Jurassic lizard fossil found on Scotland’s Isle of Skye in 2016. The animal had snake-like jaws and curved, hook-like teeth resembling those of modern pythons, but also a short body and fully formed limbs like a lizard. Detailed study using CT scans and high-powered x-rays showed it combined snake-like and gecko-like features in one animal, leading researchers to place it in a newly defined extinct predatory squamate group, Parviraptoridae. The fossil may indicate that snake ancestors differed from expectations, or that snake-like predatory traits evolved independently in another early squamate lineage. Researchers said its exact relationship to snake origins remains unresolved.

The A100 GPU has 40 MB of L2 cache, 6.7x larger than V100, improving HPC and AI workload performance by caching more data and reducing HBM2 access. Its shared, two-partition L2 design provides 2.3x higher bandwidth than V100, with 5120 Bytes/clk read bandwidth versus 2048 Bytes/clk. It includes cache residency controls and adds Compute Data Compression for improved DRAM and L2 bandwidth.

Chicago faces a major security challenge as large crowds gather for the Chicago Marathon, a Cubs playoff game and a Bears Monday night game shortly after the Las Vegas mass shooting. Officials said security plans have been rechecked, with 1,000 additional police officers and more undercover officers deployed for the marathon. Security experts emphasized vigilance around high-rises, crowd awareness and layered defenses such as bag checks and metal detectors. City officials said they have coordinated with building security personnel and have a robust plan in place. Mayor Rahm Emanuel said he is fully confident the events are secure. Some marathon runners said the Las Vegas attack raised concerns but did not stop them from participating.

The passage describes MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 device features and support information. The RTC_B provides real-time clock/calendar functions, alarms, periodic wake-up interrupts, calibration, temperature drift compensation, and clock output. IWDT_B supervises code execution using an independent LFOSC clock and can reset the device, while WWDT can generate resets or interrupts within a time window and supports sleep stopping and interval timer mode. TIMGx and TIMAx timers provide counting, prescaling, synchronization, triggers, PWM, fault handling, DMA/interrupt support, and capture/compare functions.

The passage also covers analog connections, IOMUX-managed digital I/O, SWD debugging, BSL programming through UART or I2C with password protection, and factory constants containing read-only device and trim data. Application guidance recommends VDD decoupling capacitors, NRST pullup circuitry, optional SYSOSC FCL resistor, a VCORE capacitor, and pullups for 5V-tolerant open-drain I/O. Device support information includes TI development tools, software, documentation, support forums, trademarks, ESD cautions, revision history updates, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.
Evo 1 and Evo 2 generated bacteriophage genomes; some outperformed a known strain.

Saudi Aramco plans to change its long-term crude pricing formula for Asian sales from October, using a 50:50 average of DME Oman crude futures and Platts-assessed Dubai cash prices instead of Platts Oman and Dubai assessments, trade sources said. The move, its first benchmark change since the mid-1980s, could boost DME Oman futures liquidity and hedging. Aramco, DME and Platts did not comment, and it is unclear whether other Middle East producers will follow.

The speaker welcomes visiting chiefs, affirms friendship and peace, and promises that established boundaries and laws will protect their lands, property, and persons from encroachment. In response to their request to sell land to pay merchant debts, he says the United States is willing to buy land on the Mississippi for river establishments, but will appoint agents to negotiate boundaries and value on site. He rejects any claim for repayment on lands formerly sold to the English, saying custom and testimony indicate payment was made, and that any unpaid debt would belong to the English. He encourages the chiefs to adopt farming, stock raising, spinning, and weaving, offering aid. He clarifies that prior goods were gifts and that a store on their land did not transfer ownership. Other concerns will be handled by the Secretary at War. He also arranges for their travel and safe return home.

Genel Altimeaux appealed the denial of unemployment benefits after the UAC found he voluntarily quit Ocean Construction. Altimeaux, a Haitian worker with limited English, was dismissed after a workplace pay dispute involving Haitian employees. An initial hearing occurred without him, and a supervisor testified that Altimeaux quit. After remand, it was determined Altimeaux had not received notice, and a second hearing was held. At that hearing, Altimeaux denied quitting, and another supervisor admitted he did not personally hear Altimeaux quit. The court held that the referee improperly relied on uncross-examined testimony from the first hearing and that the finding was not supported by competent, substantial evidence. The court reversed and directed reinstatement of Altimeaux’s unemployment award.

DoorDash unveiled Dot, a nearly five-foot-tall autonomous delivery robot developed by DoorDash Labs as part of a planned hybrid delivery model involving humans, drones, and autonomous vehicles. Dot has cameras, sensors, a red design, pixelated eyes, and is intended to operate on sidewalks, roads, and bike lanes, raising technical, regulatory, transportation, and labor questions. DoorDash also partners with Coco Robotics, whose smaller robots operate in parts of Los Angeles and still use teleoperators when needed.

The discussion notes that delivery robot enthusiasm peaked around the early pandemic, then cooled as companies such as Amazon and FedEx pulled back due to technical challenges. Sidewalks are especially difficult because of unpredictable pedestrians, accessibility needs, and infrastructure obstacles. Companies like Starship Technologies have found more success on controlled environments such as college campuses.

Participants discuss concerns about robots using bike lanes, possible lobbying for regulatory changes, and whether robots could replace delivery workers. They conclude that robots are unlikely to outnumber humans soon because customers often need deliveries brought directly to doors, through gates, or up stairs. Examples from China show robots handling limited parts of deliveries, such as hotel elevator trips, while human workers still perform much of the labor.

Pin and Pull is a perimeter run play that uses favorable down block angles and pullers as lead blockers in space. Its strengths are getting extra blockers to the point of attack, offering blocking flexibility based on defensive fronts, and allowing the tailback to run from the C-gap to the sideline. Its main weakness is personnel dependence: offenses need guards who can pull and run, and the concept works best with a speed back who can stretch the defense horizontally and cut vertically.

Pin and Pull differs from Buck Sweep because Buck Sweep traditionally includes a simultaneous inside run threat, while Pin and Pull is a true perimeter run. The passage outlines assignments against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts for linemen, receivers, quarterback, and tailback. It also describes two toss variations, including one using receiver motion and another using a tight end-wing surface to create better blocking angles.

Researchers used biologgers with sensors and microphones to track greater noctule bats hunting at night. The data show the bats ascend above migrating songbirds, dive toward prey using feeding buzzes, and can capture and eat birds in flight. In one recorded case, a bird was caught and consumed during a 23-minute flight. DNA evidence from severed wings and netted bats with feathers and blood further supports that greater noctules prey on songbirds.

Some parents are questioning Township High School District 113’s process for hiring a new Highland Park High School principal, citing limited parent representation and concerns about transparency. Superintendent Christopher Dignam said the process mirrors last year’s Deerfield High School principal search. A search firm is screening candidates, after which administrators will narrow the field to finalists for an 18-member stakeholder committee to interview. Principal Tom Koulentes is leaving June 30 for Libertyville High School. Board member Julie Gordon said parents at a PTO meeting were unclear why some applicants were not selected for the committee.

Investing.com content discusses market headlines and an analysis arguing that gold’s recent rally was not matched by silver, platinum, or mining stocks, especially the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF. The author views miners’ weak response, a potential USD Index rally, and stock market weakness as bearish signals resembling 2008 conditions. The passage also includes promotional stock-screening content, user comments, market headlines, and risk disclosures about trading financial instruments and cryptocurrencies.

Verizon and AST SpaceMobile announced a commercial agreement to provide space-based cellular broadband across the continental US. The author rates Verizon a “strong buy” due to improved long-term prospects, valuation, and analyst sentiment, while rating AST SpaceMobile a “sell” because of dilution, minimal revenue, and high valuation.

Former Nepali prime minister K.P. Oli appeared set to return to power after winning his parliamentary seat, with his Communist UML party and Maoist allies on course for a majority. He has pledged a full five-year government and infrastructure development. Analysts cited prospects for stability, investment and the need to balance relations with China and India.

Plans for a 32-mile smart motorway on the M4 between London and Theale will go on show before work starts in September. The £862.4m project will widen the road to four lanes, rebuild or widen bridges, and use technology to manage speeds and congestion. Completion is expected by March 2022.

Brock University researchers found that rosemary extract reduced growth and survival of A549 human lung cancer cells in lab tests. Led by Evangelina Tsiani, the team studied how rosemary polyphenols affect the Akt signalling pathway, which is linked to cancer cell proliferation. The extract inhibited cancer cell survival and spread, promoted apoptosis, blocked Akt pathway activity, and prevented activation of certain proteins. Tsiani said the findings suggest rosemary extract may have anti-tumour and chemoprevention properties, but cautioned it is too early to recommend eating rosemary to prevent or treat lung cancer. Further research will examine which rosemary compounds, possibly carnosic acid and rosmarinic acid, produce the effects.

A January 17, 2002 Enron news roundup covers investigations and fallout from the company’s collapse. Reports focus on Enron’s failed Blockbuster video-on-demand venture and the related Project Braveheart partnership, through which Enron booked $110.9 million in profits despite the venture being only a pilot. Other articles examine Enron’s use of off-balance-sheet partnerships, Arthur Andersen’s approval of structures and destruction of documents, and concerns that Andersen knew of accounting issues months earlier.

The roundup also details scrutiny of PricewaterhouseCoopers, KPMG, McKinsey, Enron’s board, SEC Chairman Harvey Pitt, and political contacts involving the Bush administration, Vice President Cheney’s energy task force, and members of Congress. Congressional, Justice Department, SEC, FBI, and state inquiries are described, including questioning of Andersen partner David Duncan and memos from whistleblower Sherron Watkins.

Additional items cover proposed reviews of retirement-plan protections after Enron employees lost 401(k) savings, the impact of Enron’s collapse on European energy trading, increased activity at IntercontinentalExchange, and American Electric Power’s acquisition of Enron Nordic Energy.

GA10x Ampere GPUs introduce GDDR6X memory with up to 19.5 Gbps data rates and 936 GB/s peak bandwidth, plus pseudo-independent channels and Error Detection and Replay for memory overclocking. NVIDIA RTX IO, used with Microsoft DirectStorage, shifts game asset loading and lossless decompression from CPU to RTX GPUs, reducing I/O bottlenecks, improving load times, streaming, frame rates, and CPU utilization.

The NVIDIA A40 targets data center visual computing, AI, data science, virtual workstations, and remote workloads, offering improved FP32, ray tracing, AI throughput, PCIe Gen4 bandwidth, 48 GB memory expandable to 96 GB via NVLink, vGPU support, and EGX compatibility. Ampere GPUs support high-resolution displays including 4K120 and 8K60, DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, DSC, and HDCP.

GA10x includes fifth-generation NVDEC with hardware decoding for codecs including AV1 up to 8K60 HDR, and seventh-generation NVENC for hardware video encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC. The architecture provides up to 2x improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI, with second-generation RT Cores and third-generation Tensor Cores. The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 24 GB GDDR6X, while the RTX 3070 uses GA104 with GDDR6. The RTX A6000 provides GA102, 48 GB GDDR6 memory, NVLink support up to 96 GB, and professional rendering, AI, HPC, and visualization performance improvements.

COTUTOR is presented as a generative AI-assisted education model that combines knowledge tracing, signal processing, and convex optimization to personalize learning. It uses real-time student interaction data, including submissions, participation logs, queries, and feedback, to estimate knowledge states and recommend resources or interventions. The system is implemented with online programming education platforms and AI chatbot interfaces that provide reminders, question handling, and resource recommendations. Its knowledge tracing builds on Bayesian Knowledge Tracing, updated from Online Judge submission outcomes and contextual features. The paper also formulates educational resource allocation as a convex optimization problem, using constraints on resource budgets and prerequisite relationships to optimize student sentiment or learning strategies across sessions.

BioNTech SE published a slide deck for an InstaDeep Ltd special call. Seeking Alpha’s transcripts team noted its role in transcript-related projects and ongoing coverage expansion. The passage also lists related stock articles and chart data spanning Sept. 26 to Oct. 1, 2025, with values from 96.98 to 102.72.

Jamie Dimon said AI is real and businesses should use it, but warned that some asset prices are high and in “bubble territory.” He compared AI enthusiasm to the early internet, arguing that while some investments may fail, the technology will likely pay off overall. Dimon cautioned that AI will eliminate jobs and urged governments and businesses to plan for retraining, income support, or other safety nets. JPMorgan has invested billions in AI since 2012, with more than 2,000 staff and hundreds of applications in areas like fraud, risk, marketing, customer service, and legal analysis. Dimon distinguished proven AI uses from generative AI, whose efficiency gains he said are harder to measure.

Jane Goodall, who died October 1 at 91, studied chimpanzees in Tanzania’s Gombe National Park for decades and also assembled a unique collection of chimp skeletons from known individuals. Her team preserved bones from chimps with recorded sex, age, weight and life histories, allowing researchers to study how development and experience shaped skeletal features. In a 1990 interview, Goodall emphasized that field researchers “shouldn’t waste anything” and was cautious about drawing conclusions for ancient hominid fossils. One notable case was Flo, a dominant matriarch whose skeleton revealed unusual size, weight and bone-loss patterns. The collection continued to provide scientific insights after Goodall moved from fieldwork into activism and writing.

The email forwards “Enron Mentions - 11/26/01,” a collection of news items largely focused on Enron’s financial crisis and Dynegy’s proposed acquisition.

Reports say Dynegy and Enron publicly intended to proceed with the merger, but Dynegy was reviewing Enron’s finances and had contractual protections, including material-adverse-change provisions and rights tied to litigation liabilities. Enron’s stock had fallen sharply, trading far below Dynegy’s offer value, prompting speculation that Dynegy could renegotiate or abandon the deal. Enron was seeking $500 million to $1 billion from outside investors, with potential support from JP Morgan Chase, Citigroup, and private equity firms, while credit ratings agencies had not downgraded Enron’s debt as the deal remained pending.

Several articles discuss Enron’s accounting problems, including restated earnings, off-balance-sheet partnerships, SEC investigation, and broader concerns about pro forma earnings, operating earnings, GAAP reporting, and corporate write-offs. BusinessWeek argues that inconsistent earnings measures have created confusion for investors and calls for clearer accounting standards.

Other items cover ChevronTexaco’s stake in Dynegy, Dynegy’s potential gains from Enron’s trading assets, antitrust concerns in California, options trading in Enron calls, Rebecca Mark’s post-Enron activities, and Indian reports involving Enron’s stake in Dabhol Power Co., including denials from Aditya Birla Group and comments from Indian officials.

Gold prices could rise to $1,400 an ounce by year-end, driven by U.S.-North Korea tensions, political risks, and stronger demand from China and India, according to VTB Capital’s Evgeny Ananiev. Gold traded at $1,281.86 Monday and has gained 12 percent this year. Metals Focus analyst Chirag Sheth also expects prices to reach $1,400 within six to nine months, citing haven demand and a softer Federal Reserve stance on interest rates. Ray Dalio recommended investors hold 5 to 10 percent of assets in gold and warned of risks including war and a U.S. debt-ceiling default. Indian jewelry demand and imports are expected to rise, while China’s gold consumption increased nearly 10 percent in the first half.

A Business Insider reporter stayed one night at Villa Casa Casuarina, the former Versace Mansion in Miami’s South Beach, booking the least expensive room, the Aurora Suite, for about $864. The hotel, originally built in the 1930s and later transformed by Gianni Versace, has hosted celebrities and now includes suites, Gianni’s restaurant, and the Thousand Mosaic Pool. The reporter found the hotel mostly empty beyond the restaurant, with attentive staff making her feel like the only guest. She described a spacious, ornate suite with a four-poster king bed, robes, window seating, detailed artwork, and a luxurious shower. She also enjoyed the gold-tiled pool, rooftop deck, observatory, ocean views, and complimentary breakfast, saying the stay made her feel glamorous.

Asian shares were mostly lower Wednesday after a late U.S. stock sell-off ended a three-day winning streak. Major indexes in Japan, China, Hong Kong, South Korea and Australia fell, while some Southeast Asian and Taiwan shares rose. Investors watched escalating U.S.-China tariff plans, China’s yuan movements, and central bank reassurances. Oil prices rose, while the dollar weakened against the yen and euro.

The Student Finance Board denied additional funding for the Association of Students for Africa’s Akwaaba Banquet and denied the Unified Greek Council’s Stroll for a Cure, citing high cost per student and other concerns. It tabled A Taste of South America over possible charitable-event policy issues and food costs, and tabled Swing Dance Club’s dance floor rental request due to cost. The board funded Inter-Greek Council’s AirBand for $6,672.50, Asian American Association’s Mystique of the East 2017 for $54.06, Swing Dance Club’s Once Upon A Rock Step for $1,094.84 and SFB’s Summer Training Retreat for $1,139.

The passage describes multi-camera imaging systems for detecting and imaging faint objects in space or other low-light environments using arrays of economical or lower-performance cameras. The systems improve image signal-to-noise ratio by co-registering and combining images from multiple cameras viewing a common field, with potential SNR improvement of about √N, where N is the number of combined images.

Three configurations are described: a common field array, where multiple cameras share a common field of view; a hybrid field array, where multiple common-field camera arrays produce combined images that are stitched into a wider composite image; and an adaptive field array, where cameras first cover a broader field to detect a target and then reorient toward a common field containing the target for higher-SNR imaging.

The systems may use co-located or geographically dispersed cameras, computing devices for image registration and processing, and calibration steps including dark frame, flat frame, bias frame, barrel distortion, and field calibration. Benefits described include lower cost, scalability, flexibility, increased effective bit depth, improved deconvolution capability, and reduction of cosmic-ray artifacts.

The passage also describes a process for identifying uncorrelated space targets: images are calibrated, registered, combined, and processed to detect streaks from moving objects; streak data is used for orbit determination; and derived orbit parameters are compared with a space object catalog to determine whether the object is already cataloged or is an uncorrelated target.

Researchers from the University of Washington and small companies conducted the first large-scale field trial using poplar trees fortified with a probiotic microbe to clean groundwater contaminated with trichloroethylene (TCE) at a Superfund site. The selected microbe, isolated from poplars growing in TCE-contaminated soil, broke down nearly all TCE in lab tests. At NASA Ames, inoculated trees grew larger and healthier than untreated trees, showed greatly reduced TCE levels after three years, and were linked to lower downstream groundwater contamination and increased chloride, a byproduct of TCE degradation. The authors say the method could improve phytoremediation, reduce cleanup costs, and help address polluted sites where traditional cleanup is expensive.

Iraqi Shi'ite cleric Moqtada al-Sadr said his followers would hand over weapons used against Islamic State if fighters receive jobs or are incorporated into official forces, and if families of those killed are supported. His Peace Brigades are part of the Popular Mobilisation Forces.

Reports citing anonymous U.S. officials say Russian intelligence officials repeatedly contacted members of President Trump’s campaign, though agencies have not found proof of collusion. The communications were intercepted during intelligence collection amid investigations into Russian election interference, and officials are still examining the reasons for the contacts. Trump dismissed the reports as “conspiracy theories,” while the Kremlin also criticized them and the use of anonymous sources. The FBI and Senate Intelligence Committee are investigating Russia-related allegations, though some Republicans oppose an independent inquiry. Rep. Mike Johnson said existing committees should handle the matter and raised concerns about leaks of classified surveillance information.
