The reports follow the departures of Michael Flynn, Paul Manafort and Carter Page amid Russia-related allegations. Manafort denied improper ties to Putin’s government.

The passage describes deploying a sharded Redis cache on Kubernetes using a StatefulSet to create three Redis pods and a Service to provide DNS names for each shard. These DNS entries are used to configure twemproxy, which proxies Redis traffic on localhost:6379, with configuration deployed via a Kubernetes ConfigMap.

A security guard at Padmanava College of Engineering died on duty, a week after Assistant Professor Jharna Dalei’s suicide. Police said the deaths are unrelated and registered an abetment case against an absconding faculty member.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2020. The company designs, manufactures and sells fully electric vehicles and solar energy generation and storage products, reporting automotive and energy generation and storage segments. As of October 20, 2020, 947,900,733 common shares were outstanding.

For Q3 2020, Tesla reported $8.77 billion in revenue, $2.06 billion in gross profit, $809 million in income from operations, and $331 million in net income attributable to common stockholders. For the nine months ended September 30, 2020, revenue was $20.79 billion and net income attributable to common stockholders was $451 million. Cash and cash equivalents were $14.53 billion at September 30, 2020, up from $6.27 billion at December 31, 2019. Total assets were $45.69 billion, total liabilities were $28.14 billion, and total stockholders’ equity was $16.03 billion.

Tesla noted COVID-19 impacts, including temporary manufacturing suspensions, supplier disruptions, employee furloughs and compensation reductions, and challenges in vehicle deliveries and energy product deployments. The company resumed operations at all manufacturing facilities by the end of the first half of 2020. In 2020, Tesla completed a public stock offering, a five-for-one stock split, and a $5.00 billion at-the-market common stock offering.

Natural zircon single-crystal plates were shock-compressed in laboratory experiments to 13.6 and 51.3 GPa to study trace-element behavior during zircon–reidite transformation. X-ray diffraction showed that the 13.6 GPa sample remained zircon, while the 51.3 GPa sample transformed mainly to textured reidite with weak residual zircon. Both samples were fractured; the higher-pressure sample showed numerous thin fractures and density-related back-scattered electron contrast indicating variable residual zircon.

Spectroscopic analyses found that loading to 13.6 GPa caused defects and cathodoluminescence changes without clear polymorphic transformation. Loading to 51.3 GPa reduced cathodoluminescence intensity, shifted emission toward shorter wavelengths, and produced strong REE-related luminescence features. Bright micrometer-scale yellow speckles in the reidite sample were attributed to enhanced REE³⁺ luminescence, likely associated with segregation of trace cations on planar defects formed during transformation.

The study concludes that zircon transformation to reidite can cause rapid trace-cation segregation under shock conditions without prolonged annealing, possibly linked to the reconstructive mechanism of the phase transition and local charge imbalance. Shock fracturing may increase surface area and influence later release of segregated trace elements during interaction with fluid or melt.
The White House blocked congressionally approved funds for the Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency, prompting Senate Republican condemnation and calls to reverse the move.

The email circulates June 4–5, 2001 news articles on California’s energy crisis. Topics include debate over wholesale electricity price controls, Rep. Doug Ose’s price mitigation bill, criticism of FERC oversight, planned power plants returning from maintenance, continued blackout risks, conservation gains, utility rate hikes, PG&E bankruptcy issues, Edison lobbying, subpoenas for energy companies, Chevron’s warning about refinery blackouts, natural gas pipeline and pricing concerns, and new long-term power contracts with the state. Several articles discuss political blame between state and federal officials, allegations of market manipulation, and efforts to expand supply while managing high costs.

The passage describes a patent application related to ladar transmitters, including priority claims to earlier U.S. patent applications. It identifies needs for improved computer vision and ladar systems, noting limitations of conventional ladar such as high cost, size, weight, power use, bandwidth demands, short range, and limited adaptability.

The disclosed embodiments include scanning ladar transmitters using movable mirrors, pre-scan compression, shot lists, and beam scanner controllers. A field splitter/inverter is described for splitting and inverting scan fields so slower scan portions can be directed toward desired regions, such as the center of a scan area. Variations include W-shaped reflectors, triangular prism arrangements, overlapping field inversion, adjustable mirror pitch angles, and paired scanning mirrors.

The passage also describes Lissajous scan patterns with induced periodic phase drift to reduce scan gaps and improve gaze in selected regions. A process using system parameters, gap detection, and total least squares optimization is presented for generating phase drift controls.

Another disclosed embodiment is a compact beam scanner assembly using an ellipsoidal conjugate reflector positioned between two scan mirrors. This ellipsoidal reimaging mirror can reduce required mirror size, support compact packaging, maintain collimation, and reduce scan field distortion when configured according to described geometric constraints.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated April 27, 2021, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2021. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

Market guidance lists Nifty and Bank Nifty levels with stops, possible moves, and option strategy. Stock calls: short Tata Steel and Ambuja Cements with targets of Rs 567 and Rs 226, respectively; go long PowerGrid with target Rs 196. Targets are for the next session unless stated otherwise.

The passage describes the Citi Simplicity® Card as offering 0% intro APR for 21 months on balance transfers and 12 months on purchases, with no annual fee, late fees, or penalty APR. After the intro period, the variable APR is 17.99%–28.74%. Balance transfers must be completed within four months, with a 3% intro transfer fee, then 5%. The recommended credit score is Good/Excellent (670–850), though approval is not guaranteed. The passage also discloses that Motley Fool Money receives partner commissions and that Citi is an advertising partner.

Scientists say asteroid Bennu has a small chance of hitting Earth in 2135, though the odds are about 1 in 2700 and it is not large enough to cause dinosaur-level extinction. NASA researchers have proposed the theoretical HAMMER mission, using a heavy impactor or nuclear device to deflect a threatening asteroid. NASA studies such plans to improve planetary defense, as past impacts in Tunguska and Russia caused major damage and injuries. NASA detects about 1000 near-Earth objects yearly, with many possibly still undiscovered. Bennu is useful for testing deflection calculations because it is well studied, and OSIRIS-REx is mapping it, analyzing its composition, and returning a sample to Earth.

Party-list Rep. Lito Atienza filed House Bill 4758 to create a Metropolitan Manila Government headed by an elected governor, replacing the MMDA, whose chairman is appointed by the President. Atienza said the MMDA has been ineffective and lacks accountability in addressing traffic, flooding, garbage, and other concerns. He argued that an elected governor would be answerable to residents and better able to work with mayors and implement a development master plan. The proposed government would include a governor, vice governor, and Metro Manila Council elected across Metro Manila, with council members elected from each congressional district.

Manchester City beat Burnley to move up to third despite Fernandinho’s first-half red card for a two-footed challenge, which triggers a four-match ban. Gael Clichy and substitute Sergio Aguero scored after the break before Ben Mee replied for Burnley, who could not find an equaliser. Aguero, left on the bench initially, made the decisive impact after replacing Kelechi Iheanacho at half-time.

A Dec. 31, 2001 Enron news digest includes articles on the company’s collapse and related market issues. The New York Times reported that Enron’s bankruptcy left no successor in broadband bandwidth commodity trading, a market weakened by excess fiber capacity, falling prices, dot-com failures and limited telecom participation. The Wall Street Journal argued that overvalued stock and unrealistic growth expectations pushed Enron into unfamiliar markets and misleading disclosures, while another article said large write-offs can signal business distress, citing Enron, Bethlehem Steel, At Home, Lucent and Providian.

Other Wall Street Journal coverage said SEC Chairman Harvey Pitt’s handling of Enron would test his leadership and enforcement approach, and listed warning signs of corporate distress, including credit-default swaps, falling bond prices, bank credit drawdowns, debt ratios, debt-payment dates and restructuring advisers. Los Angeles Times articles covered unrealistic long-term 401(k) return expectations, anger over Polaroid executive retention bonuses during bankruptcy, concerns that post-Enron spending cuts by power producers could slow plant construction, and criticism of University of California fund managers for holding Enron stock during its decline.

Dow Jones reported that American Electric Power bought Enron Wind’s 160-megawatt Indian Mesa Wind Power Project for $175 million, and that Credit Suisse First Boston resigned from Enron’s unsecured creditors committee. Bloomberg quoted California regulator Loretta Lynch criticizing the state’s deregulation plan and Enron’s role in the power market. A Bloomberg commentary gave Enron a “Stocky” award for its 99% share decline, shareholder-equity losses tied to partnerships, earnings restatements, failed Dynegy deal and Chapter 11 filing.

Eric Fung, 37, left California for Tokyo to start Colega AI after finding Silicon Valley too expensive and less appealing. Born in Brooklyn to Hong Kong immigrant parents, he worked in advertising, startups, and restaurants before founding companies. His US-registered AI startup is based in Tokyo and targets Japan’s many small businesses. Fung is adjusting to language barriers, Japanese work culture, and life in Tokyo with his wife, while noting lower housing and everyday costs than California.

The Consumer Mortgage Coalition urged the Treasury Department to let mortgage lenders and servicers use the National Directory of New Hires as an alternative to the IRS income verification system, citing concerns that IVES problems could delay mortgage closings. The group said NDNH could quickly verify current and prior-year income with consumer consent and help expand access to credit. It also asked Treasury to seek congressional funding to upgrade IVES.

CompareCards presents partner credit cards with 0% introductory APR offers ranging from 12 to 21 months, aimed at balance transfers and large purchases. The page highlights cards from Discover, Bank of America, Citi, Capital One, and others, listing cash back, travel rewards, bonus offers, fees, APR ranges after promotions, and no-annual-fee options. It explains that low or 0% interest cards can reduce borrowing costs, distinguishes fixed and variable APRs, and notes that promotional rates may revert after the introductory period. CompareCards says compensation from listed companies does not influence its ratings or reviews.
ESPN highlights include 2025 MLB ballpark food, the 2026 Savannah Bananas selection show, Stephen A. Smith reacting to a Yankees win, and ESPN BET wagering information.

Sirius XM is presented as a low-growth, cash-generating business with low-cost fixed-rate debt around 4.3%, strong cash flow coverage, expected satellite spending cuts that could raise free cash flow by 2026, share repurchases, ROIC of 11–12% versus a 6% WACC, and valuation upside based on EV/EBITDA and DCF analysis. The author discloses a long position in SIRI.

A new analysis of the West African Ebola epidemic found that 3 percent of patients caused more than 60 percent of infections, highlighting the role of “superspreaders.” The 2014-2016 outbreak in Guinea, Sierra Leone and Liberia infected more than 28,000 people and killed at least 11,000. Researchers found each Ebola patient infected 2.39 others on average, but many infected no one while some infected many. Transmission was lower in hospitals and care centers, while people staying home and traditional funeral practices helped drive spread. The study suggested age was a key predictor, with very young and very old patients likely to attract close caregiving. Similar superspreading occurred in SARS and MERS outbreaks. Ebola was eventually controlled through public health measures including safe burials and rapid hospitalization.

The automated fare collection (AFC) system market was valued at $4.81 billion in 2016 and is projected to reach $12.81 billion by 2024, growing at a CAGR of 13.3% from 2017 to 2024. AFC automates public transport ticketing through components such as automatic gate machines, ticket vending machines, and ticket checking machines. It improves fare collection efficiency, transaction speed, security, and reduces queues and manual errors. Market growth is driven by adoption of new technologies and government investments, while lack of awareness and limited smart card use may restrain growth. The market is segmented by component, application, technology platform, and geography. Key players include Advanced Card Systems, Atos, Cubic Transportation Systems, LG CNS, NXP Semiconductors, Omron, Samsung SDS, Scheidt & Bachmann, Thales, and LECIP.

Bayhorse Silver Inc. is increasing the equity portion of its non-brokered private placement to 3,000,000 units at $0.10 per unit for gross proceeds of $300,000, subject to TSX-V approval. Proceeds will fund equipment acquisition, working capital for the Bayhorse Silver Mine, and general administrative costs.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture introduces second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, higher FP32 throughput, larger caches, GDDR6X memory, PCIe Gen 4, and third-generation NVLink. The new RT Cores can deliver up to 2x ray tracing performance over Turing, support concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute workloads, and add hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur. The GA10x SM doubles FP32 throughput versus Turing by enabling FP32 processing on both datapaths and includes 128 CUDA Cores, four Tensor Cores, one RT Core, and 128 KB of configurable L1/shared memory.

Third-generation Tensor Cores support new data types including TF32 and BF16, improve efficiency, and add structured sparsity that can double Tensor Core throughput for supported workloads. They accelerate AI training, inference, DLSS, AI denoising, NVIDIA Broadcast, and NVIDIA Canvas. DLSS on Ampere supports up to 8K and a 9x super-resolution scaling factor.

GDDR6X memory, developed with Micron, uses PAM4 signaling and supports up to 19.5 Gbps, enabling up to 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth. RTX A6000 and A40 use 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, expandable to 96 GB with NVLink. Third-generation NVLink provides 112.5 GB/sec total bandwidth between two GPUs, while PCIe Gen 4 doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth.

GA102 contains up to seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, 112 ROPs, twelve 32-bit memory controllers, and 6144 KB of L2 cache. ROPs are moved into the GPC to improve raster operations. Ampere GPUs are described as up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing at the same performance level.

NVIDIA RTX IO enables GPU-based loading and decompression of assets with Microsoft DirectStorage, reducing CPU workload and improving I/O performance. GA10x also supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 8K displays, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-generation NVENC for hardware video encoding.

The NVIDIA A40 targets data center visual computing, virtualization, rendering, AI, and large datasets, while the RTX A6000 targets professional desktop workstations. GeForce RTX 3090, 3080, and 3070 use GA10x architecture features, with RTX 3090 positioned for creators, data scientists, AI developers, and extreme gamers. GDDR6X Error Detection and Replay helps detect memory transmission errors during overclocking by retrying failed transactions.

The Massachusetts House and Senate passed supplemental budget bills including $15 million for districts educating more than 2,300 students who arrived from Puerto Rico after Hurricane Maria. Funds would be distributed through the existing education aid formula based on added students. Springfield accepted the most students. Minor bill differences must be negotiated before reaching Gov. Baker.

The author describes taking and passing the online test for “Jeopardy!” despite not considering himself a trivia expert, using the experience to reflect on how memory works. He notes that neuroscience still lacks consensus on the physiological, cellular or molecular basis of learning and memory, once called the search for the “engram.” Experiments by Karl Lashley suggested memories may be distributed across the brain, while Wilder Penfield’s work indicated specific memories could be triggered in localized areas. Recent UCLA snail experiments suggesting memory transfer by RNA recall James McConnell’s 1960s flatworm studies, which the author unsuccessfully tried to replicate. He emphasizes that science is often messy and unresolved, especially in memory research.

The passage describes methods, systems, and devices for Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) transmissions and small data transmission in New Radio (NR), particularly when user equipment (UE) is in RRC-IDLE or RRC-INACTIVE states. It identifies inefficiencies in LTE small data transmission, where RRC connection setup and release create signaling overhead, and reviews control-plane and user-plane approaches for reducing that overhead.

The described solution configures contention-based radio resources for a configured grant physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH), broadcast to UEs through system information. A UE may transmit small data over the configured grant PUSCH while remaining idle or inactive, using NOMA parameters such as demodulation reference signal ports, multiple access signatures, interleavers, and spreading sequences. The system may support random access preamble multiplexing, front-loaded DMRS, guard bands, extended cyclic prefixes, and multiple configured grant resources for different message sizes or transmission periods.

The passage also describes NOMA transmission techniques that mitigate or eliminate sequence collision by using UE-specific reference bits and data bits. Reference bits may be generated from UE-specific identities and multiple access identities, jointly encoded with information bits using systematic LDPC or Polar coding, and used as a preamble or DMRS for activity detection, channel estimation, and multiple access signature indication. Additional mechanisms include UE-specific interleaving, rate matching, modulation, symbol spreading, and sparse resource element mapping.

For UEs in RRC-IDLE, small data may be sent using NAS security context and configured grant resources, with reception responses monitored through PDCCH. For UEs in RRC-INACTIVE, stored access stratum context may allow configured grant small data transmission without full RRC connection establishment, unless retransmission or larger data transfer requires connected state transition. The passage also describes applying NOMA to random access PUSCH transmissions to reduce collision probability and latency.

The Tax Court reviewed an IRS Appeals determination allowing levy collection of Robert Eugene Poindexter’s unpaid 1994 and 1996 income taxes. Poindexter had reported the taxes on his returns but did not pay them, later claiming the returns were inaccurate due to a royalty dispute with record companies and other alleged errors. The Court rejected the IRS argument that self-reported liabilities cannot be challenged in a section 6330 hearing, citing Montgomery. However, it held that Poindexter failed to allege specific facts showing the assessments were wrong, such as incorrect income, deductions, credits, or computations. He also failed to substantiate claims of procedural errors or improper levies. The Court granted summary judgment for the Commissioner and sustained the proposed collection action.

Acting CDC Director Jim O’Neill approved recommendations allowing anyone over 6 months to receive updated Covid-19 shots after discussing risks and benefits with a provider, preserving insurance coverage but leaving prescription requirements unclear. The approval enables states to order doses for low-income children through the Vaccines for Children program. O’Neill also approved separate MMR and chickenpox shots for children under 4 instead of a combined vaccine.

Police are appealing for witnesses after a father was allegedly spat at, punched and kicked in Coed Bach Park, Pontarddulais, Swansea, on 29 June while walking with his children. The attack followed his confrontation of a group over a black and white moped being ridden erratically near children. Police described the assault as “particularly nasty and unprovoked” and released descriptions of two male attackers and a woman with a young child.

Agents Mutual, owner of OnTheMarket.com, plans to float on London’s AIM and raise £50 million to challenge Rightmove and Zoopla. The UK’s third-largest property portal will use the funds for marketing, sales, customer relations and technology, including a major national TV, digital and print campaign. Chief executive Ian Springett said demutualisation had strong member support and new long-term listing deals had been signed. Hargreaves Lansdown analyst George Salmon said OnTheMarket still faces a significant challenge in competing with the two leading portals. The company launched in 2015 and recently won a competition case over its rule limiting agents to one other rival portal.

The plaintiff sued on burglary insurance policies after a safe burglary involving a check-cashing fund of cash and payroll checks. The policies excluded coverage unless the insured kept records enabling the insurers to accurately determine the loss. The plaintiff recorded only a total amount, $2,922, on a scratch pad and did not separately list cash and checks or record details identifying the checks. He later recovered $182 by recalling two checks, and the jury awarded $2,740.

The court held that substantial compliance with record-keeping clauses requires records sufficient to determine liability with reasonable accuracy. Because the stolen fund included checks, the plaintiff needed records listing each check and enough information to make claims against the drawers. His scratch-pad total was insufficient, and the insurers could not accurately determine the loss from his records. The judgment was reversed and the case remanded with directions to dismiss the complaint.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed a Tax Court judgment holding Pacific Basin Manufacturing & Trade Company liable for income tax deficiencies for tax years ending June 30, 1975 and 1976. The taxpayer, a Delaware corporation operating in American Samoa, excluded sales revenue from its Hawaiian parent under 26 U.S.C. § 931(a), which exempts certain possession-source income. The IRS agreed the taxpayer met § 931(a) conditions but found the proceeds taxable under § 931(b), which includes amounts “received” within the United States. Because Sultan deposited checks into the taxpayer’s Honolulu bank account, the court held the funds were received in the United States. The court rejected the taxpayer’s argument that receipt should depend on the corporation’s primary physical presence, finding that interpretation would make § 931(b) largely meaningless.

The National Endowment for the Humanities and First Nations Development Institute will each contribute about $2 million to fund Native language education programs in tribal communities. The effort aims to revitalize endangered Native American languages through competitive grants, with about 15 programs funded annually. Eligible efforts may include immersion, retention, and restoration programs, with tribes invited to submit proposals after an advisory committee is formed.

The passage examines variance reduction techniques (VRTs) and population control techniques (PCTs) for time-dependent Monte Carlo neutron transport simulations. It focuses on implicit capture, weight windows, CADIS, FW-CADIS, and Cooper-Larsen methods, alongside uniform combing and weight-based combing. Two codes were used: Shift, with limited time-dependent capabilities and DENOVO coupling for adjoint methods, and MC/DC, which supports broader time-dependent features and both combing methods.

Results from a pulsed slab problem in Shift showed FW-CADIS modestly improved efficiency over analog simulation, while CADIS performed poorly for global tallies. In MC/DC’s AZURV1 benchmark, Cooper-Larsen weight windows with uniform combing greatly improved figures of merit, especially at low-flux wavefront regions, and time-dependent weight windows outperformed static ones. Weight-based combing failed with Cooper-Larsen weight windows due to excessive splitting and memory exhaustion. Implicit capture performed poorly with uniform combing. In a 1D SCRAM problem, population control improved efficiency, Cooper-Larsen with uniform combing performed best, and weight-based combing again conflicted with weight windows.

The work concludes that selecting compatible VRT and PCT combinations is essential. Cooper-Larsen weight windows with uniform combing are effective for global variance reduction in time-dependent problems, while weight windows with weight-based combing and implicit capture with uniform combing can reduce efficiency or fail. Time-dependent adaptations of steady-state variance reduction methods show promise for improving dynamic Monte Carlo simulations.

The article argues that language education in the United States faces low enrollment and program cuts despite the vital role languages play in human connection. It centers on ACTFL’s idea that “language connects” and proposes fostering “imagined communities” in K–16 classrooms to help students feel connected to target languages, cultures, and speakers.

Imagined communities are formed through imagination with people or groups not immediately accessible. The approach asks instructors to design plausible, authentic scenarios in which students imagine using the target language in real-world cultural contexts. It is best implemented through task-based instruction, with tasks made meaningful to students and supported by authentic materials, websites, realia, and just-in-time instruction.

Example scenarios include students planning a move or study abroad experience in a target-language city, finding apartments, shopping for furniture or food, using transit systems, researching courses or jobs, writing emails, résumés, or cover letters, and planning outings using authentic resources. These tasks aim to help students see similarities with target-language communities and imagine themselves participating in everyday life there.

The approach requires planning, creativity, scaffolding, student autonomy, authentic assessments, and adaptation to student needs. Reported outcomes include deeper cultural and language learning, new ways of examining cultures, increased feelings of connection with target-language speakers, and greater feelings of membership in target-language communities. The article concludes that centering language learning on connection can support student engagement, retention, and the future of language education.

U.S. Rep. Garret Graves said the shooting of Rep. Steve Scalise and three others reflects a divisive political climate where rhetoric has consequences. Scalise was critically injured by James T. Hodgkinson, who had anti-Republican views and had volunteered for Bernie Sanders, though police had not stated a motive. Sanders condemned the shooting and all violence. Some Republicans said threats against them have intensified amid backlash to President Trump. Trump called for unity, saying Americans are strongest when unified.

The disclosure describes methods, polypeptides, nucleic acids, vectors, and genetically modified host cells for producing cannabinoids, cannabinoid precursors, derivatives, and precursor derivatives. It identifies GOT polypeptides, including CsPT4 and truncated CsPT4t, that catalyze cannabigerolic acid production from GPP and olivetolic acid at least ten times more than CsPT1. Engineered host cells may express GOT with TKS, OAC, cannabinoid synthases, and enzymes for GPP, malonyl-CoA, acyl-CoA, mevalonate-pathway, and acetyl-CoA production. The methods include culturing modified cells, optionally with carboxylic acids or olivetolic acid derivatives, and recovering cannabinoids such as CBGA, THCA, THC, CBDA, CBD, and related compounds. The disclosure also covers in vivo and cell-free production, broad substrate specificity for generating non-naturally occurring derivatives, and use of microbial fermentation as an alternative to plant extraction or chemical synthesis.

A May 3, 2001 Enron news digest lists articles on Enron-related energy, finance, and corporate developments. Topics include a Pompano Beach hearing on an Enron power plant proposal; debate over whether California should refuse high-priced electricity purchases; Indian lenders seeking government help in Enron’s Dabhol Power dispute; and Dabhol’s planned meeting with a Maharashtra renegotiation panel, later postponed to May 11.

Other items cover DNC criticism of Bush energy policy and energy industry influence; Innogy beginning wholesale power trading in mainland Europe, where Enron is among active traders; Mosaic Group’s strong first-quarter results and work for Enron-created New Power; Enron’s role in bankruptcy swaps and credit derivatives; and expanding corporate use of credit derivatives through Enron Credit.

The digest also reports Allegheny Energy’s purchase of 1,710 MW of Midwest gas-fired generation capacity from Enron North America; Salomon Smith Barney’s reduced forecasts for power generation profitability; Fitch affirming Northern Border ratings and changing its outlook to stable; EnergieKontor’s wind turbine agreement with Enron Wind; and Scottish Power’s restructuring, including reports involving Enron’s Portland General unit.

An Ilorin Magistrates’ Court remanded herdsmen Shehu Abubakar and Abdulkareem Maikudi at Okekura Prisons for allegedly killing Musa Kareem after a dispute over a cell phone. They face charges of criminal conspiracy and culpable homicide. The prosecutor said investigation was ongoing and opposed bail. The case was adjourned until July 12.

The speaker felt energized despite many power plays and penalty kills, citing the team’s depth across four lines as a strength. They said both teams defended well, blocked shots, and handled penalties aggressively. The team focused on staying composed, continuing its approach, and eventually found an opening that led to a successful shot.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2019. As of October 16, 2019, it had 495,797,220 common shares outstanding. For Q3 2019, total net sales were $69.981 billion, up from $56.576 billion in Q3 2018. Net income was $2.134 billion, down from $2.883 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $4.23, down from $5.75. For the nine months ended September 30, 2019, net sales were $193.086 billion, net income was $8.320 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $16.53.

Segment net sales for Q3 2019 were $42.638 billion for North America, $18.348 billion for International, and $8.995 billion for AWS. Segment operating income was $1.282 billion for North America, a $386 million loss for International, and $2.261 billion for AWS. Consolidated operating income was $3.157 billion in Q3 2019.

As of September 30, 2019, Amazon reported total assets of $199.099 billion, total liabilities including current liabilities, lease liabilities, debt, and other long-term liabilities, and stockholders’ equity of $56.508 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash ended the period at $23.554 billion. For the nine months ended September 30, 2019, operating activities provided $18.855 billion, investing activities used $20.745 billion, and financing activities used $6.495 billion.

The filing discusses accounting policies, adoption of new lease and film-cost accounting guidance, lease obligations, debt, tax matters, legal proceedings, commitments, and risks. Amazon had $24.3 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding and no borrowings under its commercial paper program or unsecured revolving credit agreement as of September 30, 2019.

A New York Times survey found many responding federal judges dissatisfied with the Supreme Court’s emergency docket decisions in Trump-related cases. Of 65 judges, 47 said the Court had not used the docket appropriately, and 48 said lower courts lacked sufficient guidance. Most said the docket harmed public perception of the judiciary. Some judges anonymously criticized the orders, while a Trump appointee defended them. The Times noted respondents may not represent the judiciary overall, and a Volokh Conspiracy critique argued unhappy judges may have been more likely to respond.

Energy Central Direct’s Jan. 15, 2002 daily edition lists power industry news including Enron-related investigations, political fallout, bankruptcy issues, UBS’s purchase of Enron’s trading unit, and Andersen document destruction scrutiny. Other topics include National Grid’s pending Niagara Mohawk takeover approval, California utility and procurement issues, Texas customer switching, Ohio deregulation concerns, energy mergers, FERC and regulatory actions, renewable energy projects, nuclear security and waste developments, international power sector updates, utility stock gainers, and gas industry headlines.
The court affirmed the denial of Michael Moss’s unemployment benefits, finding substantial evidence that he was discharged for misconduct after pulling a box cutter on his supervisor.

Nigeria launched its National Cancer Control Plan 2018-2022 in Abuja to improve cancer diagnosis, treatment, drug access, and healthcare quality. At the event, Health Minister Professor Isaac Adewole highlighted BVGH’s African Access Initiative (AAI), which is working with Nigerian hospitals to deliver cancer medicines, technologies, and training. AAI, led by BVGH with partners including AORTIC, IFPMA/Access Accelerated, Pfizer, and Takeda, aims to expand access to cancer care, strengthen infrastructure, and build clinical and research capacity in Nigeria and four other African countries. BVGH has completed needs assessments at eight Nigerian hospitals, with eight more underway, to guide sustainable cancer treatment access efforts.

JPMorgan downgraded Valero Energy from Overweight to Neutral while raising its price target from $75 to $78. Analysts said the stock has already benefited from stable returns and improved capital discipline under CEO Joe Gorder, but further multiple expansion may take time due to industry cyclicality. The firm estimates Valero’s total return potential, including dividend, at 6 percent versus 7 percent for the group.

The passage examines President Trump’s pardon power amid Robert Mueller’s Russia investigation, focusing on Trump’s pardon of Scooter Libby shortly after FBI raids on Michael Cohen’s home and office. Critics argued the Libby pardon could signal protection for Trump associates, while the White House said it corrected an injustice and denied any implied message. Legal experts disagree on whether pardons issued for corrupt purposes, or self-pardons, would be valid, though pardons do not protect a president from impeachment. Historical examples include George H.W. Bush’s Iran-Contra pardons, Nixon’s consideration of a self-pardon, and Bill Clinton’s pardon of Marc Rich.

The article notes reports that Trump’s lawyer discussed possible pardons for Michael Flynn and Paul Manafort, which John Dowd denied. Flynn later pleaded guilty and cooperated; Manafort pleaded not guilty. Democrats, including Rep. Adam Schiff, proposed legislation requiring disclosure of evidence when pardons involve investigations tied to the president or his family. New York Attorney General Eric Schneiderman sought changes to state law to prevent presidential pardons from blocking state prosecutions. Legal analysts said pardons may not end investigations because recipients can lose Fifth Amendment protections and be compelled to testify truthfully.

Texas Instruments provides current mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for TLV3211, TLV3212, TLV3214, TLV3221, and TLV3222 devices, subject to change without notice. Dimensions follow specified standards, with notes on tolerances, tape orientation, solder mask, stencil design, and alternate IPC recommendations. TI resources are provided “as is” for skilled developers, who are responsible for product selection, design, validation, testing, compliance, and indemnification. TI disclaims warranties and liability, restricts resource use to applications involving the described TI products, and rejects additional terms.

This retrospective study used MIMIC-IV data to examine the association between resting heart rate (RHR) and all-cause mortality (ACM) in ICU patients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). The cohort included 1,918 adult patients admitted from 2011 to 2019, grouped into RHR quartiles. Outcomes were ACM at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year after ICU admission. Higher RHR quartiles were associated with more intraventricular hemorrhage, mild liver disease, diabetes, mechanical ventilation, and higher mortality. Kaplan-Meier and multivariate Cox analyses showed that RHR above 78.5 bpm was associated with increased ACM risk. Restricted cubic splines identified a nonlinear relationship, with 90.3 bpm as a cutoff: RHR below this level may be protective, while RHR above it was independently associated with higher ACM risk. Subgroup analyses suggested an interaction with age, though mediation effects were limited. The authors conclude that RHR stratification may help risk assessment and management in ICU patients with ICH.

The passage presents a study of Large Language Model (LLM)-driven agent-based social simulation focused on whether LLM agents exhibit egoistic or altruistic behavior when individual and collective interests conflict. The authors argue that prior LLM social simulations often emphasize human-like personas or small game-theoretic settings, but do not sufficiently examine LLMs’ intrinsic social tendencies in large-scale group environments.

The study proposes a Schelling-variant urban migration model with over 200 agents distributed across residential blocks. Agents decide whether to stay or move based on individual utility and system utility, with optional social communication through a public message board. The model evaluates outcomes using macro-level measures such as Price of Anarchy and Residential Gini Index, and micro-level behavioral categories such as selfish gain, altruistic sacrifice, win-win actions, and lose-lose actions. A qualitative LLM-as-judge analysis is also used to interpret agent reasoning and message-board content.

Experiments compare several LLMs, including o1-mini, o3-mini, Qwen2.5-7B, Deepseek-V3.1, Deepseek-R1, and Gemini-2.5-pro, under different guidance and message-board conditions. Results identify two behavioral archetypes. “Adaptive Egoists,” including o1-mini, o3-mini, and Qwen2.5-7B, tend toward self-interest and suboptimal collective outcomes without social communication, but some become more altruistic when exposed to message-board norms. “Altruistic Optimizers,” including Gemini-2.5-pro and Deepseek models, consistently achieve optimal collective outcomes and display high altruistic action rates even without social interaction.

The authors conclude that choosing an LLM for social simulation is also a theoretical choice about the type of social actor being modeled. Adaptive Egoists may better represent bounded, socially influenced human-like dynamics, while Altruistic Optimizers may be more suitable for modeling idealized pro-social or collective-welfare-oriented actors. The passage notes limitations including simplified migration dynamics and homogeneous agents, and suggests future work involving human validation and real-world heterogeneous agent profiles.

Purdue University ended its GEAR UP program after the U.S. Department of Education canceled a $34.9 million grant, citing policy and civil rights concerns tied to DEI and culturally responsive teaching. The program served over 13,000 low-income Indiana students. Purdue did not appeal. At least nine GEAR UP grants were canceled.

Edinburgh has seen increased haar this spring due to weaker Atlantic temperature contrasts reducing the jet stream’s influence. This has led to more persistent easterly winds instead of Scotland’s usual westerlies, making the east more prone to haar while creating sharp east-west weather differences.

Volkswagen’s ID Buzz may reach production because it shares underpinnings with other ID models, though it may not arrive until around 2025. The ID targets Golf buyers, while the Crozz could suit the American EV market.

DWH Deutsche Werte Holding AG moved to the Vienna Stock Exchange’s mid market segment on 23 April 2018, increasing transparency and publicity obligations for investors. The company is supported by Capital Lounge GmbH, while ICF BANK AG provides liquidity. The exchange also highlighted planned legal changes to allow Austrian bearer shares back on the Third Market.

The lecture explains how to quantitatively measure premiums for green buildings and urban amenities using hedonic pricing models. It distinguishes stated preference, based on surveys, from revealed preference, based on observed market behavior such as rents and sale prices. Housing is presented as a bundle of attributes—physical features, location, transit access, parks, green certification, and unobserved residual factors—whose values can be estimated through regression.

The instructor explains that coefficients in log-price regressions indicate percentage changes in price, such as a LEED dummy variable showing a green building premium. Examples include studies estimating rent and sale premiums for LEED or Energy Star buildings, and a hypothetical Winthrop Center analysis comparing willingness to pay for views, health, and green features in office and condo markets.

A major focus is causal inference. The lecture discusses the problem of comparing “apples to oranges” when green buildings differ from non-green buildings in age, class, location, developer quality, or other unobserved factors. It introduces counterfactuals, treatment and control groups, bias, endogeneity, omitted variables, reverse causality, and selection bias. Methods to improve comparisons include adding controls, randomized controlled trials, geographic matching, propensity score matching, regression discontinuity, instrumental variables, and difference-in-differences.

The lecture also extends hedonic methods to urban amenities such as schools, subway access, parks, walkability, and air pollution. Examples include estimating school district premiums in China, subway-related land value increases for transit-oriented development, and park-related property appreciation. Bryant Park is discussed as a public-private partnership where nearby stakeholders helped fund restoration in expectation of property value gains. The High Line is used to illustrate how environmental improvements can raise willingness to pay nearby, while also contributing to environmental gentrification and displacement.

The Supreme Court issued orders from its Sept. 29 private conference and added no new cases to its docket. It denied review in several cases, including challenges involving Ghislaine Maxwell’s prosecution, Missouri gun law enforcement limits, a police dog drug sniff, claims by Laura Loomer against social media platforms, and Native Americans’ challenge to an Arizona land transfer involving a sacred site. The court also asked the U.S. solicitor general for views in three cases involving federal nuclear safety regulations, trademark law, and arbitration under the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act.

Turtle Trading is a trend-following strategy developed by Richard Dennis and William Eckhardt in the 1980s to test whether trading could be taught. Dennis trained novice traders, called the Turtles, funded their accounts, and many became successful, supporting his view that trading skills can be learned.

The original rules focused on mechanical breakout entries, volatility-based position sizing using ATR, pyramiding winning trades, and predefined exits and stop-losses. The strategy sought to identify new trends early, trade in their direction, add positions as trends progressed, and exit when an opposing trend appeared.

The Turtles traded many futures markets, including bonds, commodities, stock index futures, metals, energy products, and currencies. Some participants later founded trading firms, though not all were successful. Dennis later suffered major losses and stopped trading, while Eckhardt admitted the experiment proved him wrong and later founded a successful CTA.

The passage states that Turtle Trading can still work today, especially in markets with clear trends, though performance may be weaker than in the 1980s. Modern traders often modify the rules with technical indicators. Backtests and indices such as the Barclay CTA Index and Mt. Lucas Management Index suggest trend-following strategies can provide returns and low correlation to stocks, but they also involve whipsaws, low win rates, long drawdowns, and difficulty in real-money execution.

Preliminary BC Coroners Service data show 1,422 suspected illicit drug overdose deaths in British Columbia in 2017, a 43% increase from 993 in 2016. Deaths declined in the last four months of 2017, averaging 96.5 per month versus 129.5 in the first eight months. Fentanyl was detected in about 81% of 2017 deaths, usually with other illicit drugs; carfentanil was detected in 64 deaths from June to December. Most deaths occurred indoors, especially in private residences, and none occurred at supervised consumption or overdose prevention sites. Key trends included more deaths in the five days after income assistance payments, the highest death rate in Vancouver Coastal Health, and the highest numbers in Vancouver, Surrey and Victoria. Most people who died were aged 19 to 59, and about four in five were male. Officials emphasized the continuing public-health crisis and the need for prevention strategies such as naloxone distribution, drug checking, outreach and treatment connections.
A Harvard Business School study found several AI companions use tactics to prevent conversations from ending.

Luca Speight, 18, received the Outstanding Achievement Award and Isle of Wight College Student of the Year 2018. He was praised for catching up after three months’ illness, volunteering at college events, excelling in work placement, and showing determination. After a life-threatening illness and major operation, he returned to his Level 2 Catering and Hospitality course to pursue becoming a chef.

The ADS868xW includes a second-order antialiasing low-pass filter at the PGA output to reduce front-end amplifier and resistor noise, typically with a 500kHz –3dB cutoff. An integrated high-bandwidth, low-noise ADC driver supports charging and discharging ADC sample-and-hold capacitors at maximum sampling rate.

The device supports internal or external 4.096V references through the REFIO pin, selected with the INTREF_DIS bit in RANGE_SEL_REG. The internal reference is enabled by default, factory-trimmed, temperature-compensated over –40°C to +125°C, and requires at least a 4.7µF capacitor between REFIO and REFGND. Mechanical or thermal stress, especially solder reflow, can shift the internal reference value. External reference mode disables the internal reference and applies a 4.096V source to REFIO; the internal buffer drives REFCAP, which requires at least 10µF plus a nearby 1µF decoupling capacitor.

The ADC supports single-ended and differential inputs with bipolar and unipolar ranges. Output data are in straight-binary format, with LSB size equal to full-scale range divided by 2¹⁶. The device provides input and AVDD alarms through the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin when configured. Input alarms use programmable high and low thresholds with hysteresis, while AVDD alarms use fixed thresholds of 4.7V and 5.3V. Alarm flags include active and tripped indicators, readable through ALARM_REG, the ALARM pin, or appended output data.

The multiSPI digital interface supports data and command exchange with a host through shift registers, configuration registers, and protocol logic. It supports single-device SPI, full multiSPI configurations, and daisy-chain operation for multiple devices. In daisy-chain mode, devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK, and an optimal frame contains 32 × N SCLK capture edges for N devices.

The device has RESET, ACQ, and CONV states. RESET is controlled by the active-low RST pin and can perform an application reset or power-on reset. ACQ acquires the analog input signal and can use NAP mode for lower power. CONV begins on the rising edge of CONVST/CS, uses an internal clock, and returns to ACQ after conversion.

Programming uses nine configuration registers and two operations: data write and data read. A data transfer frame begins on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and ends on the next rising edge. Frames with 32 SCLKs are optimal; shorter frames are treated as invalid for writes but can read MSBs, while longer frames use the last 32 shifted-in bits as the command. Output data can include conversion results, register data, fixed patterns, device address, range flags, alarm flags, and parity.

The interface supports standard SPI-compatible protocols for configuration and readback, single or dual SDO output, and source-synchronous read protocols using RVS as the output clock. Registers configure device ID, reset and power control, SDI and SDO modes, output data formatting, input range and reference selection, alarm flags, and alarm thresholds.

Application guidance describes using ADS868xW in industrial analog input modules for PLC, DCS, or DAS systems, including voltage and current ranges such as ±2.5V, ±5V, ±10V, 0V to 5V, 0V to 10V, 4mA to 20mA, and 0mA to 20mA. An example combines ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 differential multiplexer. The device includes programmable gain, ADC driver, reference, overvoltage protection, input alarm, and AVDD alarm.

Power recommendations specify separate AVDD and DVDD supplies with decoupling. AVDD requires minimum 10µF and 1µF capacitors, DVDD requires a nearby minimum 10µF capacitor, and proper decoupling improves PSRR. Low-power NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput rates. Layout guidance recommends separating analog and digital sections, using clean bypassed supplies, placing decoupling capacitors close to pins, and properly decoupling REFCAP and REFIO.

This study investigated dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) using natural dyes extracted from mangosteen peel (MP), rich in anthocyanins, and grass jelly leaves (GJL), rich in chlorophyll. MP and GJL extracts were mixed at ratios of 3:1, 2:1, 1:1, 1:2, and 1:3 and applied to TiO2-coated ITO substrates, with iodide electrolyte and graphite counter electrodes.

UV-Vis analysis showed that mixed dyes combined the absorption characteristics of both extracts, broadening visible-light absorption. Microscopy and FESEM revealed that MP-rich films showed cracking, while mixed-dye films, especially balanced compositions, had more uniform morphology and better TiO2 coverage. DSSC testing showed efficiencies from 2.12% to 3.50%, with the highest power conversion efficiency at the 1:3 MP:GJL ratio. Single-dye controls were lower, with MP at 2.75% and GJL at 2.12%. Stability testing over 10 cycles showed GJL-rich mixtures retained performance better than some other ratios, while the 1:1 mixture declined rapidly.

The study concludes that blending MP and GJL dyes improves DSSC performance through complementary light absorption and improved charge collection, with the 1:3 ratio giving the best result. Future work should address long-term stability.

Depoe Bay, Oregon, is preparing for the Aug. 21 total solar eclipse with disaster-style planning as large crowds are expected near the first landfall point of totality. Officials have planned for years and recently added portable restrooms, garbage cans, protective glasses, and resident advisories to stock supplies and expect traffic gridlock. With Highway 101 as the only main access route, emergency officials fear congestion could block ambulances or fire engines, so three fire stations will be staffed and lanes kept clear. The small harbor is also preparing for heavy boat traffic, with the Coast Guard monitoring vessels.

Figma shares rose 7% Monday after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman demonstrated Figma’s integration with ChatGPT at OpenAI’s DevDay conference. The integration will let ChatGPT users ask Figma to perform tasks, such as turning a sketch into a workable diagram. Altman said developers can submit apps for review later in 2025 and that monetization options for third-party integrations will come over time.

Benjamin David Sherwood of Wisconsin was sentenced in Houston to 11 years in prison and lifetime supervision after pleading guilty to traveling across state lines for illicit contact with a child and enticing a minor. Authorities said he responded to an undercover ad involving a fictional child, traveled to Houston, and was arrested in a hotel room. He must register as a sex offender.

NVIDIA RTX IO uses GPU-based loading and lossless decompression with Microsoft DirectStorage to reduce CPU storage overhead, improve I/O performance, accelerate game loading, reduce stutter and object pop-in, and support large open worlds and professional workloads involving large datasets.

The NVIDIA A40, based on GA10x Ampere architecture, targets data center visual computing, AI, rendering, simulation, and virtualized workloads. It offers up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput versus Quadro RTX 6000, up to 5x AI throughput or 10x with sparsity, PCIe Gen4 bandwidth, 48GB memory expandable to 96GB via NVLink, vGPU support, Quadro Sync, and EGX Platform compatibility.

GA10x Ampere GPUs support DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 4K 120Hz, 8K 60Hz, HDCP 2.3, fifth-generation NVDEC decoding, AV1 hardware decode up to 8K60 HDR, and seventh-generation NVENC encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC. Ampere improves programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI performance by up to 2x, adds second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores with sparsity, GDDR6X support, and RTX IO.

The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 24GB GDDR6X and targets creators, data scientists, AI developers, and extreme gamers. The RTX 3070 uses GA104 and is described as faster than the GeForce RTX 2080 Ti. GA10x GDDR6X includes Error Detection and Replay to retry memory transmission errors during overclocking. The RTX A6000 uses GA102 with 48GB GDDR6, supports NVLink to 96GB, and targets professional rendering, AI, HPC, and large 3D datasets.

Microsoft’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2018 reported quarterly revenue of $26.8 billion, up from $23.2 billion a year earlier, and net income of $7.4 billion, up from $5.5 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $0.95 versus $0.70. For the nine months ended March 31, 2018, revenue was $80.3 billion, up from $71.0 billion, while net income fell to $7.7 billion from $17.4 billion, primarily reflecting a higher tax provision related to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act.

As of March 31, 2018, Microsoft had total assets of $245.5 billion, total liabilities of $166.3 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $79.2 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $132.3 billion. Long-term debt, including the current portion, had a carrying value of $76.9 billion.

Net cash from operations was $12.2 billion for the quarter and $32.5 billion for the nine-month period. Microsoft paid $3.2 billion in quarterly dividends and repurchased $3.8 billion of common stock during the quarter.

The company recorded a provisional $13.8 billion net charge related to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. Unearned revenue was $24.0 billion, and contracted revenue not yet recognized was $61 billion. Microsoft also disclosed pending legal matters, including patent, antitrust, product-related, and employment-related claims, with accrued legal liabilities of $371 million.

BMW launched the 1 Series sedan in China with Brilliance Automotive in July 2016 and may consider bringing it to India. The compact sedan, based on the UKL1 platform, could compete with Mercedes-Benz CLA and Audi A3. It features BMW design elements, front-wheel drive, petrol engines in China, and would likely get diesel options in India.

The Portland Thorns enter the NWSL playoffs aiming to improve on last season’s home semifinal loss after finishing second at 14-5-5. They host the Orlando Pride, led by Alex Morgan and Marta, in one semifinal, while Supporters’ Shield winner North Carolina Courage hosts the Chicago Red Stars in the other. Portland, unbeaten against Orlando, set a league record with 10 home wins, while Orlando will be without injured midfielder Camila. North Carolina finished first at 16-7-1 behind Lynn Williams but is 0-3 against Chicago, which features Christen Press and Julie Ertz. The winners meet Oct. 14 in Orlando for the championship. The NWSL is completing its fifth season, with Sam Kerr winning the Golden Boot after scoring a league-record 17 goals. Lifetime will televise both semifinals as part of the league’s first national broadcast deal.

Forecasts suggest Oroville Dam’s spillways may face less strain than feared over the next 10 days. The Feather River basin is expected to receive 7.5 inches of rain, compared with 13.6 inches during the earlier storm that damaged the main spillway and threatened the emergency spillway. Rain is expected to be more spread out and colder, with lower snow levels reducing short-term runoff. Meteorologist Jan Null said inflows should be far lower than during the prior storm, while upstream dams are holding back water. State officials have been lowering the reservoir by about 4 inches per hour; by Tuesday afternoon it was 15 feet below the emergency spillway lip and could drop further before Friday’s rain. Null warned that warm spring weather melting record snowpack remains a concern.

Phuket Governor Norraphat Plodthong ordered lifeguards to return to patrol Phuket beaches by April 1 during a March 21 meeting. The NNT reported that local administrative offices must handle beaches in Muang Phuket and Kathu districts, while a procured company would cover Thalang district beaches. Offices lacking six-month budgets from April may request support from the PPAO, though this contrasts with the governor’s Dec 12 order that the PPAO no longer be involved. The NNT gave no explanation for the apparent change. The Phuket News said its questions to the governor about the lifeguard shortage remained unanswered.

The lecture reviews the LSZ theorem, which relates scattering amplitudes to momentum-space time-ordered correlation functions by taking external momenta on shell and stripping off external propagators. Initial and final states are distinguished by the sign of the on-shell energy in the Fourier-transformed correlation function. For scattering amplitudes, only connected truncated diagrams are used; diagrams that only correct external legs are absorbed into a constant wavefunction factor \(Z\), which is process-independent for a given particle type and equals 1 at leading order.

The lecture then concludes the discussion of interacting scalar theories and begins the topic of fermions. It introduces the historical motivation for the Dirac equation: attempts to construct a relativistic first-order wave equation addressing issues with the Klein-Gordon equation, such as lack of positive definite probability and negative energy states. Dirac proposed using matrices \(\alpha_i\) and \(\beta\) in a first-order Hamiltonian equation. Requiring the squared equation to reduce to the Klein-Gordon equation imposes anticommutation relations and Hermiticity conditions on these matrices, requiring at least \(4\times4\) matrices for massive particles.

The four-component object \(\psi\) is introduced as a spinor. By defining gamma matrices, the Dirac equation is written compactly as \((\gamma^\mu \partial_\mu - m)\psi=0\), with gamma matrices satisfying the Clifford algebra \(\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}\). Different gamma-matrix representations are related by similarity transformations and are physically equivalent, though different choices are convenient in different limits. For massless particles, a two-component description using Pauli matrices is possible. The lecture ends by preparing to show that the Dirac equation is Lorentz covariant, after recalling how Lorentz covariance works for the Klein-Gordon equation.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2017. Q1 2017 net sales were $35.7 billion, up from $29.1 billion in Q1 2016. Net income was $724 million, compared with $513 million, while operating income declined to $1.0 billion from $1.1 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.48, compared with $1.07.

Net cash used in operating activities was $1.6 billion for Q1 2017, compared with $2.0 billion in Q1 2016. For the trailing twelve months ended March 31, 2017, operating cash flow was $17.6 billion and free cash flow was $10.2 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $21.5 billion at March 31, 2017.

Segment net sales were $21.0 billion for North America, $11.1 billion for International, and $3.7 billion for AWS. Operating income was $596 million for North America and $890 million for AWS, while International reported an operating loss of $481 million. AWS sales grew 43% year over year.

Total assets were $81.0 billion at March 31, 2017, and stockholders’ equity was $21.7 billion. Long-term debt had a face value of $7.8 billion, excluding the current portion. Amazon reported principal contractual commitments of $45.9 billion and signed an agreement to acquire Souq Group Ltd. for $580 million in cash, subject to adjustments.

The filing describes accounting policy updates, tax matters, legal proceedings, market risks, and operating risks. Amazon’s Q2 2017 guidance projected net sales of $35.25 billion to $37.75 billion and operating income of $425 million to $1.075 billion.

Schmidt Sciences, founded by Eric and Wendy Schmidt, will spend $45 million over five years on global carbon cycle research, including a project deploying four uncrewed surface vessels in the Southern Ocean around Antarctica. The drones will collect public data, including winter measurements of CO2 in the water, to help scientists understand why the Southern Ocean absorbs a large share of ocean-based carbon dioxide despite limited existing data from the remote, rough, cloudy region. The vessels will operate beyond commercial shipping routes, use machine learning to optimize routes, and be run through a public-private partnership involving USV companies and NOAA. Scientists say such outside funding is increasingly important amid proposed federal cuts to NOAA, NSF, and climate research programs.

Lab experiments suggest tiny bubbles of air and methane in water can create faint electrical sparks, or microlightning, that might ignite methane gas associated with will-o’-the-wisps. Researchers used 3-D printed nozzles, photon counters and high-speed cameras to study bubbles mimicking swamp gas seepage, eventually capturing tiny lightning zaps when smaller, crowded bubbles formed. Some chemists say the findings show microbubbles can discharge electricity but do not fully explain will-o’-the-wisps, since swamps differ from the lab setup and the observed sparks occurred underwater while the lights appear in air. Researchers also say the work may advance triboelectricity and could help trigger chemical reactions, study atmospheric pollutant behavior or break down pollutant gases.

The passage describes AGESA host-environment procedures for early processor, cache, and memory initialization. A stackless native assembler procedure creates a pre-memory stack region using register passing, divides it among cores, maps it to global address space, sets x86-64 MTRRs, and must run on all cores. It handles protected and real mode differently, creates a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instance, and returns success, warning, or fatal status codes. A related procedure removes the pre-memory stack once main memory is available, disables CAR mode without modifying MTRRs, flushes cache lines, preserves EBX, and should be invoked only by the BSP.

AmdCreateStruct allocates and initializes AGESA parameter structures using PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, or ByHost allocation methods, requires an established stack, and returns success, error, or fatal status. Other services obtain DIMM data eye bitmaps, APIC addresses for x86-64 cores, available pre-memory execution cache size, PCI addresses for processor dies, current processor socket/die/core identity, and memory FRU/error-location details for a specified address. Many services require coherent HyperTransport links and a stack established through provided service functions. AARCH64 APUs with PSP do not use the stack and very early macros because the PSP initializes DRAM.

In a daisy-chain topology, all devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK from the host. Device 1 receives host SDO, each device’s SDO-0 connects to the next SDI, and the last device returns data to the host SDI. Devices use identical configurations, single SDO-0 output, external clock, and SDO_CTL_REG bits 7-0 set to 00h. Data shifts MSB-first; the host receives device N first. Optimal frames require 32 × N SCLK capture edges.

Solawave’s 4-in-1 Renewal Wand is on sale during Prime Day for a little over $100. WIRED says it targets specific areas, uses vibration and warmth, requires three minutes of manual use, and some staffers saw skin-tightening results around the eyes. Solawave’s red light face mask is also discounted to $227.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated February 10, 2016. The Board elected Wendell P. Weeks as a director and appointed him to the Audit Committee, effective February 10, 2016. Weeks is CEO, President, and Chairman of Corning Incorporated and a director of Merck & Co., Inc. He received a restricted stock unit award for 1,365 Amazon shares vesting over three years, subject to continued service, and entered into an indemnification agreement.

The Board approved a two-year leave of absence for Diego Piacentini, Senior Vice President, International Consumer Business, beginning August 2016, and suspended forfeiture of his restricted stock units during the leave. Russ Grandinetti will assume responsibility for international consumer business, reporting to Jeffrey A. Wilke.

The Board also authorized up to $5 billion in common stock repurchases with no fixed expiration, replacing a 2010 $2 billion authorization.

EUR/USD remains in a bearish channel but momentum may be slowing; resistance breaks could invalidate the bearish wave count. GBP/USD is testing triangle resistance, with potential bullish breakout or bearish continuation toward 1.05. USD/JPY shows a bull flag, though a support break may signal a larger retracement.

The message urges Congress to enact comprehensive conservation legislation for public lands and natural resources. It describes the reduction and past misuse of the public domain, including fraud and outdated land laws, and calls for land classification, validation of prior withdrawals, and clear authority for the Interior Department to withdraw lands pending legislation. It recommends separating surface agricultural rights from mineral rights, leasing coal, oil, gas, phosphate, and similar resources on terms preventing monopoly, including in Alaska.

The message emphasizes conserving water-power sites through limited-term private use under federal conditions to prevent monopolies, and highlights soil conservation as central to national welfare. It supports reclamation and irrigation projects but notes that too many were begun with inadequate funds, recommending up to $30 million in bonds to complete existing projects and aid settlers.

It calls for repeal of existing timber-land disposal laws, sale of timber separately, continued management and expansion of national forests, and moderate federal spending for reforestation near navigable streams. It also recommends inland waterway improvements, especially dams on the Ohio River and improvements to the Mississippi and Missouri Rivers, where costs and benefits have been studied. The message urges prompt congressional action without waiting for ongoing investigations of the Interior Department and Forest Service.

The passage describes the AMD SEV-ES and SEV-SNP Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) specification, which standardizes how encrypted guests communicate selected state to a hypervisor during Non-Automatic Exits. The GHCB is a 4 KB decrypted shared page whose layout mirrors parts of the SEV-ES VMCB save state area while limiting exposed guest state. Version 2 adds SEV-SNP support, hypervisor feature advertisement, restricted APIC emulation support, GHCB protocol enhancements, and later revisions add features such as APIC ID retrieval, multi-VMPL support, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, and updated guest request handling.

The document defines GHCB MSR protocol functions, protocol negotiation, GHCB GPA registration for SEV-SNP guests, hypervisor feature bitmap handling, termination requests, CPUID requests before GHCB setup, page state changes, SNP guest requests, extended guest requests for certificates, AP creation, restricted injection doorbell pages, IPI and timer requests, APIC ID lists, VMPL switching, SEV-TIO requests, and Secure AVIC backing page registration.

It also specifies guest and hypervisor behavior for VMGEXIT processing, VALID_BITMAP use, supported Non-Automatic Exit handling, error reporting, MMIO and I/O emulation, AP booting and reset hold behavior, NMI handling, hardware debug register virtualization, and unsupported features such as SMM and nested virtualization. The final sections describe restricted injection host notification using a shared #HV doorbell page, including pending event fields, EOI optimization, interrupt shadow handling, and host behavior for interrupt and non-maskable event delivery.

NVIDIA RTX IO helps artists, designers, and games handle large datasets by speeding movement of textures, meshes, and other assets from storage to GPU memory. It works with Microsoft DirectStorage and adds GPU-based lossless decompression, reducing CPU load and improving I/O performance. RTX IO targets faster loading, streaming, and better GPU memory use for rendering, VR, and next-generation games.

The NVIDIA A40, based on GA10x Ampere architecture, is positioned as a data center GPU for visual computing, AI, data science, simulation, and virtual workstations. Compared with Quadro RTX 6000, it offers up to 2X FP32 throughput, up to 2X ray-tracing throughput, and up to 5X AI/data science throughput, or 10X with sparsity. It includes 48GB of GPU memory, scalable to 96GB using NVLink, supports vGPU software, Quadro Sync, and is compatible with the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

GA10x Ampere GPUs support high-resolution displays, including 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz, with DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, DSC 1.2a, and HDCP support. Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for codecs including MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, HEVC, VP8, VP9, and AV1. GA10x is described as the first GPU family with AV1 hardware decode, enabling up to 8K60 HDR playback with low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware video encoding for streaming, archiving, and high-resolution encoding up to 4K on H.264 and 8K on HEVC.

The GA10x Ampere architecture improves programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI performance by up to 2X. It includes second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores with sparsity, GDDR6X memory support, and RTX IO. The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102, has 24GB of GDDR6X memory, 82 SMs, and 10,496 CUDA cores. The RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6, and is described as faster than the GeForce RTX 2080 Ti.

Error Detection and Replay technology on GDDR6X detects transmission errors and replays failed memory transactions, helping overclockers identify memory limits through performance plateauing. The RTX A6000 includes GA102, 10,752 CUDA cores, 48GB GDDR6 memory, ray-tracing and AI features, NVLink support up to 96GB, and professional certifications. The passage ends with NVIDIA warranty, liability, licensing, and trademark disclaimers.

Natalie Grabow, 80, of New Jersey, set the world record as the oldest woman to finish the Kona Ironman World Championship, completing it in 16:45:26. She began running in her 40s, learned to swim at 59, and started triathlons at 60. She trains for months, works out about two hours daily, eats a varied diet, and plans to keep competing as long as she can.

The passage explains consumer confidence indices, focusing on the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index and the Conference Board’s Consumer Confidence Index. These indices measure consumer optimism or pessimism about the economy, based on surveys about current conditions, expectations, personal finances, and spending outlooks. Changes under 5% are described as usually insignificant, while larger shifts may indicate changes in economic momentum.

Using OECD U.S. consumer confidence data from 1993, the article backtests S&P 500 performance. A strategy invested only when consumer confidence was above its 12-month moving average grew $10,000 to $99,000 over 28 years, with an 8.4% CAGR and 23% maximum drawdown, compared with buy-and-hold ending at $159,000, 10.4% CAGR, and 55% drawdown. The opposite strategy, investing only when confidence was below its 12-month average, grew to $15,000, or 1.58% annually. The passage concludes that stocks perform better when consumer confidence is above its 12-month moving average and poorly when it is below.

Lenovo officially unveiled the limited edition ThinkPad 25 at Yamato Labs in Japan. Based on the T470 and inspired by the 1992 ThinkPad 700C, it includes retro design elements alongside modern hardware such as a 14-inch Full HD touchscreen, Core i7, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD, and starts at $1,899.

NVIDIA GA10x Ampere architecture GPUs target data center, professional visualization, gaming, AI, and compute workloads with second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, improved FP32 throughput, PCIe Gen4, and support for advanced display, video, and memory technologies.

The NVIDIA A40 is presented as a data center GPU for visual computing, delivering up to 2X FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 5X AI training and data science throughput versus Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB memory expandable to 96GB via NVLink. It supports vGPU software, Quadro Sync, DisplayPort outputs, and the NVIDIA EGX Platform.

GA10x GPUs support DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, DSC 1.2a, HDCP 2.3/1.x, 4K120 and 8K60 displays, fifth-generation NVDEC decoding, AV1 hardware decode up to 8K60 HDR, and seventh-generation NVENC encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC. The architecture also supports GDDR6X memory, RTX IO, and Error Detection and Replay for GDDR6X memory overclocking.

The passage also describes GeForce RTX 3090 and RTX 3070 specifications, RTX A6000 workstation capabilities with 48GB GDDR6 expandable to 96GB via NVLink, and NVIDIA disclaimers about specifications, warranties, liability, and product use.

COPD is a leading cause of death in the United States and is caused almost exclusively by smoking. Symptoms include chronic coughing and shortness of breath. Diagnosis involves smoking history and pulmonary function tests. Treatments such as inhalers, oxygen, and pulmonary rehabilitation can reduce symptoms, but damage cannot be reversed. Quitting smoking is key to prevention and slowing progression.

The passage discusses molecular dynamics methods for calculating thermal conductivity, focusing on Green-Kubo and non-equilibrium MD approaches and the central role of heat flux. It notes that LAMMPS has used heat-flux formulations that are exact for pair potentials but can be incorrect for many-body potentials, despite exact formulas by Torii et al. Existing corrections apply only to limited systems. The work extends and implements Torii et al.’s formulas in LAMMPS for heat flux in a control volume, heat current through a control surface, and spectral decomposition for arbitrary many-body potentials. The article then outlines theoretical background, comparative tests using Tersoff and Stillinger-Weber potentials, and spectral decomposition results for graphene and MoS₂.

The study evaluated distance education practices implemented during the COVID-19 pandemic in Turkish higher education institutions providing sports education and aimed to offer suggestions for improvement. Using a qualitative case study model and descriptive analysis, data were collected through semi-structured online interviews with 14 lecturers in sports-related departments at Turkish universities between December 2020 and November 2021.

Distance education was described as beneficial for removing time and place limitations, enabling lesson repetition, improving access to resources, supporting use of information technologies, reducing costs, and helping limit pandemic spread. Reported negative aspects included communication problems, low participation, motivation issues, unequal opportunities, access and equipment problems, ineffective applied lessons, social isolation, and assessment concerns. Major challenges involved internet and infrastructure problems, difficulties in assessment and evaluation, ineffective communication, lesson intensity, and limited student interest.

Participants stated that distance education was necessary during the pandemic but that the process was not managed effectively enough. Concerns included delayed decision-making, insufficient institutional infrastructure, inadequate in-service training, problems with education platforms, and excessive administrative monitoring.
