The study concluded that distance education can serve as an alternative when formal education is disrupted, but in sports sciences it requires field-specific planning, especially for applied courses. It also emphasized the need for improved infrastructure, accessibility, assessment systems, lecturer training, and data security measures.

The paper studies tunnel magnetoresistance in Mn3Sn(01̄10)/MgO(110)/Mn3Sn magnetic tunnel junctions using first-principles calculations. Mn3Sn is a kagome noncollinear antiferromagnet with an inverse 120° magnetic structure that breaks time-reversal symmetry and produces momentum-dependent spin splitting. The selected Mn3Sn(01̄10) geometry is relevant for electrical switching via spin-orbit torque.

The authors construct Mn3Sn/MgO/Mn3Sn junctions with MgO barriers and calculate tunneling conductance using density functional theory, the Landauer–Büttiker formula, and scattering-theory methods. They analyze the spin polarization of bulk Mn3Sn, the complex band structure of MgO, and momentum-resolved transmission through the junctions.

The calculations show tunneling transport through sufficiently thick MgO barriers and a tunnel magnetoresistance ratio exceeding 1000% for thicker barriers. The TMR effect is mainly attributed to the x-component of Mn3Sn’s momentum-dependent spin polarization and to electron filtering by the MgO barrier, especially near small in-plane momentum. The study concludes that Mn3Sn can serve as a promising electrode material for antiferromagnetic magnetic tunnel junction devices.

A Journal of Neuroscience study tested whether barn owls can process moving visual elements similarly to primates. Researchers showed owls moving black dots on grey backgrounds and tracked how quickly they turned toward a target dot moving differently from the others. The owls detected the target more easily when surrounding dots moved uniformly rather than in scattered directions. Brain recordings from the ocular tectum, involved in basic visual processing, varied with dot movement, suggesting this area helps owls group moving elements and distinguish objects from backgrounds despite their simpler brains.

The passage lists repeated global finance and technology headlines, then focuses on Jeff Bezos’s suggestion that future data centres could be built in orbit to meet rising cloud and AI computing demand while easing land, energy and cooling constraints. It notes possible benefits such as solar power and resilience, but highlights challenges including radiation shielding, power storage, cooling in a vacuum, low-latency communication, and launch and maintenance costs. It also describes other firms exploring orbital or lunar infrastructure and includes a brief profile of Pan Finance’s global financial news operations.
Strong US jobs and wage data raised expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes, boosting the dollar and Treasury yields while stocks fell. Ten-year Treasury yields reached 2.84 percent.

Gold edged lower as the dollar rose against the euro ahead of U.S. nonfarm payrolls data, which investors expected to offer clues on future U.S. interest rate hikes. Spot gold fell 0.3% to $1,345.22 an ounce, while June U.S. gold futures were flat. Stronger jobs data could support expectations of further Federal Reserve rate increases, pressuring non-yielding bullion. The Fed recently left rates unchanged but raised its inflation outlook. Gold was set to end the week little changed after recent gains. Silver and platinum fell, while palladium rose slightly but remained on track for its biggest weekly drop since September.

Lifeline Fiji program director Jeremiah Merekula said suicide remains a taboo issue in Fiji despite high rates. NSAAC statistics recorded 124 suicides and 107 attempts in 2015, and 102 suicides and 104 attempts in 2016. From 2011 to March this year, Fiji recorded 627 suicides and 694 attempts, including 56 suicides and 97 attempts among children. Lifeline Fiji is promoting help-seeking behaviour, awareness of emotional distress, and parent programs, and offers a 24/7 helpline.

Clark County Schools Superintendent Pat Skorkowsky ended his tenure after five years as superintendent and 30 years in the district. He said he was proud of raising the graduation rate from 60% to 83% and expanding magnet schools by over 10,000 seats. He noted challenges including a $60 million budget shortfall, education funding, teacher pay, school safety and mental health support. Skorkowsky urged incoming superintendent Dr. Jesus Jara and the school board to prepare for the 2019 legislative session and said marijuana tax revenue should benefit counties where it is generated. He advised Jara to listen to the community and said they will work together for a few weeks.

At RSA Conference 2017, Intel Security’s Chris Young warned that attackers can manipulate “small data” used in decision-making models, creating “data landmines” that lead to faulty outcomes, losses and missed opportunities. He also highlighted insecure home networks and IoT devices as risks to corporate networks, citing the Mirai botnet. Microsoft President Brad Smith urged the tech community to act as a “digital Switzerland,” focusing on defense, protecting customers, refusing attacks on civilians and cooperating against threats. He called for digital Geneva Conventions, limits on government stockpiling of vulnerabilities, an international cyber agency to attribute nation-state attacks, and greater private-sector leadership in protecting civilian cyber assets.

The passage describes a patent application for a location-sharing system with a map-based graphical user interface used with a social media application. The system receives authorized location information from a user’s client device, determines the user’s current trajectory, accesses historical location data, and predicts a presumed destination by correlating current movement with habitual places or recurring trajectory patterns. The predicted destination, and optionally an estimated time of arrival, may be displayed on friends’ client devices through a map interface using avatars and destination icons.

The system includes client applications, a location sharing server system, API and application servers, databases, messaging functions, and a social network system maintaining entity graphs and location tables. Users may control whether and with whom their locations are shared, including friend groups or custom lists. The map GUI can show friends’ avatars, allow selection of friends, center the map on a selected user, and support actions such as chat.

The prediction process may identify habitual places such as home, work, or school from historical data, compute probabilities for candidate destinations, and update or stop displaying a presumed destination if later data lowers confidence. Historical trajectories may be clustered and averaged into recurring trajectory patterns, which can help infer destinations, transport modes, predicted locations during communication loss, and arrival times using factors such as average duration, speed, weather, traffic, and public transport schedules.

Vale of Glamorgan Brewery has applied to open a micropub, the Radyr Tap, in an empty Station Road unit in Radyr, Cardiff. The suburb has been without a pub since the Radyr Arms closed in 2003. The proposal follows a Twitter campaign by resident Jamie Grundy. The brewery says the venue would provide a social space and celebrate local beer, serving its own beers, local ales, craft beers, wines, spirits, takeaway drinks, meats, cheeses and snacks. A consultation runs until June 19 before Cardiff council decides.

The passage describes MSPM0G MCU features, operation, peripherals, support resources, and packaging information. The CPU subsystem uses an ARM Cortex-M0+ running from 32 kHz to 80 MHz, with prefetch/cache, SysTick, MPU, NVIC, and interrupt grouping. The devices support RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN power modes, with PD1 for CPU, memory, and high-performance peripherals and PD0 for low-power peripherals.

The PMU provides regulated core supplies, VDD supervision, BOR monitoring, and trim protection. The clock module includes LFOSC, SYSOSC, LFXT/LFCKIN, HFXT/HFCKIN, and SYSPLL, distributing clocks such as MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, LFCLK, ADC clock, CAN clock, and others. DMA supports multiple channels, repeated and single transfers, configurable triggers, interrupts, cascading, ping-pong buffers, and stride mode. The event manager routes static, DMA, and generic peripheral events.

Memory features include dual-bank flash up to 256 kB/512 kB plus 16 kB data flash, ECC, 1 kB sectors, endurance options, and bank address swap for OTA updates. SRAM is up to 128 kB across two 64 kB banks, with Bank 0 ECC or parity protected and Bank 1 optionally enabled. GPIO supports up to 93 pins, wake functions, and fast wake from STOP and STANDBY. IOMUX controls pad configuration and peripheral pin routing.

Analog and mixed-signal features include two 12-bit ADCs, a temperature sensor, configurable internal or external voltage reference, comparators, and a 12-bit DAC. Security features include AES-128/256 acceleration, firewalls, secure key storage, CRC, TRNG, AESADV, and a keystore for up to four keys. Communication interfaces include UART, I2C, SPI, CAN-FD, and serial wire debug. Low-frequency features include LFSS_B, RTC_B, IWDT_B, WWDT, and general-purpose and advanced timers.

The passage also covers device analog connections, input/output diagrams, boot strap loader operation over UART or I2C with password protection, factory constants, recommended application schematic practices, development tools and software, documentation support, trademarks, ESD caution, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

Komar Uddin, 68, denies charges including sexual assault, assault by penetration, causing a female to engage in sexual activity and two counts of rape. Leicester Crown Court heard he allegedly raped a 19-year-old woman during a candlelit spiritual ritual at her family home in 2015, after being invited by her father to drive out an evil spirit. The complainant said Uddin used holy oil, sexually touched her, raped her twice, told her not to tell anyone, and claimed she was pregnant. Prosecutors said he exploited the family’s beliefs and trust while relatives were downstairs. An internal swab reportedly contained Uddin’s DNA. The defence suggested the woman was lying and had initiated sexual contact, which she denied. Uddin was arrested, bailed, left the country, and was later extradited from Germany. The trial continues.

MIT has publicly rejected the Trump administration’s proposed “Compact for Academic Excellence in Higher Education,” becoming the first of nine invited universities to do so. The compact would require broad campus changes in exchange for preferential federal funding treatment. MIT president Sally Kornbluth said the proposal conflicted with MIT’s values, institutional independence and belief that federal funding should be based on merit. She argued that U.S. scientific leadership depends on independent thinking and open competition.

Other invited universities are still reviewing the proposal, though University of Texas officials expressed interest, while Dartmouth emphasized its commitment to academic freedom without formally rejecting it. Some state officials in California, Virginia and Pennsylvania have opposed the compact and warned of financial consequences for institutions that sign it. MIT’s decision drew praise from academics and Democratic lawmakers, while some Trump-aligned figures suggested possible retaliation.

Prosecutors released three cellphone videos found on Nikolas Cruz’s phone after the Feb. 14 shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School, where 17 people were killed and 17 injured. In the videos, Cruz said he intended to become a school shooter, kill at least 20 people with an AR-15, and attack the Parkland school. He described arriving by Uber and opening fire, closely matching surveillance footage. He also spoke about loneliness, anger, hatred, and a former girlfriend. Cruz faces 17 murder and 17 attempted murder charges. His lawyers said he would plead guilty for life without parole, but prosecutors have not waived the death penalty. The videos were released under Florida public records law.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its 2020 Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2020. The company is incorporated in Delaware, headquartered in Seattle, Washington, and its common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under AMZN. As of January 20, 2021, it had 503,564,743 common shares outstanding, and its non-affiliate voting stock market value was $1.174 trillion as of June 30, 2020.

Amazon organizes operations into North America, International, and Amazon Web Services segments. It serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators through online and physical stores, third-party seller programs, AWS technology services, advertising, publishing, and digital content offerings. Amazon Prime includes shipping, streaming, and other benefits. The company employed approximately 1,298,000 full-time and part-time employees as of December 31, 2020.

Amazon reported net sales of $386.1 billion in 2020, up from $280.5 billion in 2019. Operating income was $22.9 billion, net income was $21.3 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $41.83. Net cash provided by operating activities was $66.1 billion. Total assets were $321.2 billion and total long-term obligations were $101.4 billion as of December 31, 2020.

The filing identifies risks including intense competition, international operations, expansion into new products and regions, inventory and fulfillment challenges, cybersecurity, system interruptions, supplier dependence, acquisitions, payments, regulation, litigation, tax liabilities, government contracts, and COVID-19-related disruptions. Amazon incurred more than $11.5 billion in COVID-19-related costs during 2020.

The passage calls for 1,000 additional naval officers, enlarged Annapolis classes, easier retirement for impaired senior officers, and improved promotion to maintain efficiency amid heavy strain on junior officers and recruits. It argues that a strong navy is necessary to avoid trouble and disaster. It reports record Post-Office receipts of $121,848,047.26, with rural free delivery now a fixed policy showing strong revenue growth, 11,650 routes operating, and 10,748 more requested. The service is described as beneficial to farmers, rural property, education, and reducing isolation. The passage also supports continued national irrigation in the West, stronger forest protection, and legislation to protect game on forest reserves.

Researchers found that blocking the protein Ant2 reprograms T cells’ energy metabolism, making them more active, resilient, faster-replicating, and more effective at targeting tumors. The study, involving Hebrew University, Philipps University of Marburg, and MD Anderson researchers, showed this rewiring can be triggered genetically or with drugs, suggesting potential for future cancer immunotherapies, though further studies and clinical trials are needed.

Facebook took over two hours to remove live videos posted by shooting suspect Steve Stephens showing Robert Godwin’s death. Separately, activist Hugo Castro went missing in Mexico after seeking help on Facebook Live. In Georgia, Democrats hope Jon Ossoff can win a long-held Republican House seat amid anti-Trump energy.

Michael T. Klare argues that Donald Trump’s foreign policy seeks not only to disrupt the existing liberal world order but to build a new alignment based on fossil-fuel interests. The passage says Trump has supported fossil fuels domestically, opposed renewable-energy policies, withdrawn from the Paris climate accord, and sought closer ties with Saudi Arabia and Russia while alienating NATO and green-leaning European allies. It describes his Saudi visit as a revival of the U.S.-Saudi alliance, including a $110 billion arms deal and energy cooperation, and his Europe trip as weakening NATO ties and rejecting European appeals to remain in the Paris agreement. The article frames a potential U.S.-Russia-Saudi “trilateral” fossil-fuel bloc as economically powerful because of its large share of global oil and gas production, while noting obstacles such as Russia-Saudi disagreements over Syria and Iran.

This study surveyed 304 medical students from four Belgian universities to assess knowledge, attitudes, and exposure regarding global surgery. Only 24.7% reported prior exposure, most often through social media, while 75.3% wanted more exposure, preferably through optional teaching, events, clinical internships, and required teaching. Students were less familiar with global surgery than global health, and global surgery was rarely or never incorporated into required curricula. Nearly all respondents considered global surgery relevant, and most supported more compulsory teaching. Knowledge was poor: 23.9% knew that five billion people lack access to timely, safe, affordable surgical care, and 21.7% knew that about 150 million additional procedures are needed annually. About one-third were interested in global surgery or global health careers, but reported barriers included personal responsibilities, language barriers, lack of established career paths, financial constraints, and limited mentorship. The authors conclude that Belgian medical students show strong interest but limited knowledge and exposure, supporting development of global surgery curricula, pre-clinical seminars, and equitable international clinical internships.

A March 27, 2018 test by Stagno of 124 VPN and proxy providers found that 20 leaked users’ real IPs via WebRTC, while 101 kept IPs hidden. The passage lists leaking services including Astrill, BlackVPN, Hola!VPN, Hoxx VPN, psiphon3, TOR as proxy, Windscribe add-ons, and others. It says users can test VPNs with tools from ExpressVPN, VoidSec, and ipleak.net. If a VPN leaks IPs, users can disable WebRTC manually or install an add-on. The passage also lists VPNs described as protecting privacy with WebRTC, including ExpressVPN, NordVPN, StrongVPN, Private Internet Access, VyprVPN, HideMyAss, CyberGhost, and others.

The passage critiques Paul Ehrlich’s 1968 portrayal of overpopulation in Delhi, noting Jack Caldwell’s argument that similar crowding existed in Western cities and questioning whether fears about developing-world megacities reflect bias. It argues that cities are not driving population growth but help reduce it, as urban residents tend to have fewer children than rural populations, with examples from Kenya and India. Urban growth is attributed to migration from rural areas, after which smaller families become common. However, the passage says cities also intensify consumption, using disproportionate amounts of materials, food, water and other resources, while producing large volumes of waste and sewage.

This section provides current mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for ADS8681W, ADS8685W, and ADS8689W devices, subject to change without notice. It defines notes on product status, preproduction material, RoHS values, lead finish, MSL/reflow ratings, and part markings. TI states the information is based partly on third parties, may be limited by proprietary data, and is provided “as is” without warranties. Users are responsible for product selection, application design, validation, testing, and compliance. TI limits liability and rejects additional terms.

Global equities declined Monday as U.S. 10-year Treasury yields neared 3 percent, raising concerns about government debt supply, inflation and competition with stocks. Commodities fell after the United States suggested it could ease sanctions on Russia’s Rusal, sending aluminum sharply lower and pressuring materials shares, including Alcoa. The dollar rose to a seven-week high as the euro and yen weakened. Oil recovered from earlier losses, with U.S. crude and Brent settling higher amid mixed views on OPEC production limits and potential U.S. sanctions on Iran. U.S. stocks were little changed ahead of major earnings reports, with investors watching companies including Alphabet, Facebook, Boeing and Chevron.

Caterpillar’s board kept its quarterly dividend unchanged at $0.77 per share, payable May 20 to shareholders of record on April 24. The stock yields 3.25% and has raised dividends for 23 consecutive years, but this marks its seventh straight quarter of flat payouts. Goldman Sachs added Caterpillar to its conviction buy list, citing improving mining capital spending and setting a $120 price target, while the stock has already risen nearly 20% in nine months.

Optimism is tied to potential benefits from Trump administration energy, coal, infrastructure, and U.S. manufacturing policies, along with stronger U.S. economic conditions, higher oil prices, and reduced concerns about China. However, the stock trades near its 52-week high and at high earnings multiples, while the company faces a federal tax investigation and uncertainty around any infrastructure bill.

Caterpillar’s revenue and EBITDA fell in 2016 for a fourth year, cash flow has weakened, and management remains “prudently cautious.” The company expects 2017 revenue and adjusted earnings per share to decline, making dividend growth difficult. The author advises investors to exercise caution.

EchoingECG is a probabilistic student-teacher framework for ECG modeling that integrates PCME++ with ECHO-CLIP to learn ECG representations aligned with ECHO and text data. It addresses ECG signal complexity through probabilistic contrastive learning, enabling many-to-many mappings with uncertainty-aware embeddings, and reduces reliance on large annotated ECG-ECHO datasets by using ECHO-CLIP as a teacher. The approach aims to capture structural and functional cardiac insights from ECHO and support downstream uncertainty-aware evaluation.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on April 20, 2022, reporting that it released financial results for the quarter ended March 31, 2022 by posting its First Quarter 2022 Update on its website. The update is attached as Exhibit 99.1, with an Inline XBRL cover page file as Exhibit 104. The report was signed by CFO Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

Chris King, 57, attended his first Leeds Rhinos match at Headingley Carnegie Stadium after becoming the first person in the UK to receive a double hand transplant. He lost his hands in a work accident and was applauded at half-time while drawing the golden gamble ticket. He praised the atmosphere and the Rhinos’ 42-22 win over Widnes Vikings.

Henry L. Stimson argued that raising territorial adjustments or trusteeships while excluding Pacific areas of U.S. interest would create distrust, highlight U.S. aims, and harm discussions. The passage describes a study evaluating a workflow for optical genome mapping (OGM) analysis and reporting in hematologic malignancies using Bionano Access and Variant Intelligence Applications (VIA). Current cytogenetic methods such as karyotyping, FISH, and chromosomal microarray have limitations in resolution, subjectivity, labor requirements, and ability to detect both copy number and balanced structural variants in a single test. OGM is presented as a cytogenomic method capable of detecting structural rearrangements and copy number variants from 5 kbp to large-scale chromosomal abnormalities.

The study extended prior implementation guidance from the International Consortium for Optical Genome Mapping in Hematologic Malignancies by developing a VIA-based workflow focused on myeloid neoplasms. Ten retrospective cases, including nine acute myeloid leukemia cases and one myelodysplastic syndrome/neoplasm case, were analyzed repeatedly by independent technologist-director teams. Samples were processed for OGM, analyzed with Bionano Solve, imported into VIA, and reviewed using customized views, classifications, filters, guideline annotations, and report templates.

After comparison with standard-of-care testing, OGM identified all variants reported by karyotype and/or FISH. Four cases were negative by both standard-of-care testing and OGM. In five of six positive cases, standard-of-care sentinel variants were unanimously reported and classified as Tier 1A in OGM reviews. One case with trisomy 21 showed variability in reporting and classification. OGM also detected additional variants not reported by standard-of-care testing in five of six positive cases, including large copy number losses, trisomy 8, small deletions, and complex rearrangements.

Technologist review times averaged 25.2 minutes for negative cases, 28.5 minutes for simple cases, and 47.3 minutes for complex cases. The VIA workflow reduced review time compared with prior Bionano Access-only analysis and supported structured variant curation, classification, and report generation.

The authors conclude that OGM analysis using Bionano Access and VIA provides a streamlined and efficient approach for interpreting and reporting cytogenomic variants in hematologic disorders, with potential to standardize variant analysis and clinical interpretation.

The passage presents a bibliometric study of academic research on digital accessibility in education from 2013 to 2024 using Web of Science, Scopus, and ERIC, with VOSviewer for analysis. Publications specifically on “digital accessibility” and education totaled 924, rising from 4 in 2013 to 339 in 2024, with notable growth after 2019. Scopus contained the largest share of records.

Journal articles were the most common publication type, followed by conference papers and book chapters. The main research areas were digital accessibility and inclusion, education and social sciences, and computer science and engineering. English dominated publication language, with 873 of 924 publications.

Most education-level studies focused on higher education, with 469 publications. The leading contributing countries were the United States, the United Kingdom, and Spain. Citation analysis in Web of Science showed that the most cited documents included Gorriz (2023), Kuc-Czarnecka (2020), and Bong (2024). Chen Weiqin was the most cited author, while the United States and England led country-level citations.

The study concludes that academic interest in digital accessibility in education has grown substantially, especially after the COVID-19 pandemic, but education-focused studies, international collaboration, and stronger legal and research frameworks remain limited.

The paper examines the normative assumption that educational disparities should be corrected, arguing that this assumption is grounded in fairness and can be clarified through luck egalitarianism. Luck egalitarianism holds that disadvantages caused by factors beyond individual control, such as socioeconomic status, gender, ethnicity, disability, or region of origin, are unfair and should be reduced. Applied to education, it supports removing the influence of social background on children’s educational opportunities, resources, and attainment.

The paper also identifies problems with pursuing fairness alone, using Elizabeth Anderson’s critiques of luck egalitarianism: the harshness objection and the humiliation objection. The harshness objection argues that luck egalitarianism can leave individuals without support when their disadvantages result from their own choices, as in the example of a former aspiring musician who dropped out of high school and later lives in poverty. The humiliation objection argues that compensatory policies can stigmatize and demean those they aim to help, such as low-achieving or poor students receiving targeted support.

To address these problems, the paper proposes adding three values to fairness: fresh start, sufficiency, and respect. Fresh start supports opportunities for individuals to recover from past choices and try again. Sufficiency emphasizes guaranteeing everyone a minimum threshold of welfare or educational attainment, though questions remain about where to set that threshold. Respect requires attention to whether educational practices intended to reduce disparities may cause shame or humiliation.

The paper concludes that empirical research on educational disparities should examine not only fairness but also whether students have chances for fresh starts, whether all students meet sufficient educational thresholds, and what forms of humiliation children experience in classrooms. It argues that collaboration between empirical social science and normative theory can generate better research questions about educational disparities.

In Hardin v. White, the court held that an injunction bond need not be double the judgment amount when the injunction seeks only to prevent sale of specific property under a general execution, rather than to restrain collection of the judgment itself.

The case involved an attempt to enjoin sale of real estate in Keokuk. White had obtained foreclosure decrees involving the same indebtedness, caused the real estate to be sold under execution for part of the decree, and later sought to levy on the debtor’s statutory right of redemption for the remaining balance. The court held that, after selling the property under execution for part of the debt when one execution could and should have covered the whole, White exhausted his remedy against that property. Allowing a creditor to reserve part of a judgment for a later execution would undermine the statutory right of redemption.

On rehearing, the court acknowledged factual clarifications but found them immaterial. Although the second execution was formally issued under a different decree from a chattel mortgage foreclosure, both decrees covered the same indebtedness, which could be collected only once. The court distinguished Barnes v. Cavanagh and affirmed the injunction.

Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a genetic group of disorders that causes abnormal hemoglobin, producing sickle-shaped red blood cells. These cells do not last as long as normal cells and can stick in blood vessels, reducing healthy red blood cells and blocking blood flow. SCD can affect people of any background, but the gene is most common among people of sub-Saharan African descent and is also more common in parts of South and Central America, Saudi Arabia, India, Turkey, Greece, and Italy. About 100,000 people in the United States are affected.

Key symptoms include sickle cell crisis, acute chest syndrome, swollen hands and feet, anemia, jaundice, kidney, spleen, gallbladder, lung, heart, eye, bone, joint, and infection problems, leg sores, strokes, and painful prolonged erections in men. Smoking increases the risk of pain episodes and acute chest syndrome, which is a major cause of hospitalization and death in SCD.

SCD is diagnosed with a blood test and is often detected at birth through newborn screening in the U.S. Prenatal testing is also available. Management includes education, regular checkups and screening, vaccinations, antibiotics for children up to age 5, blood and urine tests, oxygen tests, eye exams, ultrasounds, and cognitive tests. Treatments may include pain medication, hospital care, medicines to increase fetal hemoglobin, blood transfusions, and, in severe cases, hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Lifestyle measures include avoiding tobacco smoke, eating a balanced diet, limiting alcohol, getting enough rest, and exercising to support heart health.

Heikin Ashi is a Japanese candlestick-based charting method that smooths price movements to highlight trends and consolidation phases. Unlike traditional candlesticks, it does not show real prices; its open, high, low, and close values are derived from formulas, so trades cannot be executed directly at Heikin Ashi prices. The passage describes Heikin Ashi as a technical indicator rather than a replacement for candlesticks, noting that it is lagging because it reflects past price action.

The article explains the calculation of Heikin Ashi values, discusses simplified formulas, and states that haOpen is an exponential moving average of prior haClose values. It also presents Amibroker code concepts and suggests customizing the open calculation parameter to adjust noise filtering.

The passage tests Heikin Ashi strategies, including a monthly S&P 500 trend-following system that buys when haClose crosses above haOpen and sells when haOpen crosses above haClose. It reports that the strategy has a 49.4% win ratio and favorable performance metrics. Another tested strategy uses ADX and two red Heikin Ashi candles, with an exit when the close exceeds the previous day’s high; on the S&P 500 it produced a 5.27% CAGR with 5% market exposure. The passage concludes that Heikin Ashi can work, especially on longer time frames.

The Side Screen is a motion offense built around continuous on-ball side screens, quick ball reversal, and constant player movement. It can begin through a dribble clear, pass and clear, or high post rub entry. The main action has the wing drive off a post screen, with options to attack the basket, pull up, pass to the screener rolling or popping out, or kick out to shooters. Continuity includes back cuts, screen-and-roll action, dribble handoffs, and ball reversal. Defensive counters include slipping the screen against show-and-recover coverage, exploiting mismatches when defenses switch, and using spacing with a high post and corner cuts when defenses trap.

A three-year study of 195 Ugandan health facilities found that smaller, rural and for-profit providers struggle to sustain HIV treatment services despite support such as free ARVs, equipment and training. The lecture introduces a three-part MIT series on nuclear arms control and nonproliferation, emphasizing India and Pakistan as a possible nuclear flash point. The opening remarks note the catastrophic human and climatic effects of nuclear exchanges, the decline of public attention to nuclear risks after the Cold War, and the need for technically trained people in arms control, verification, and policy work.

Vipin Narang then presents an overview of nuclear proliferation and deterrence in South Asia. He explains deterrence theory, distinguishing deterrence by punishment from deterrence by denial, and identifies capability, credibility, and communication as core requirements. He also reviews nuclear weapons types, delivery systems, command arrangements, and the strategic choices states face in managing arsenals.

Narang describes India’s nuclear program as initially motivated by China, especially the 1962 war and China’s 1964 nuclear test. India conducted a “peaceful nuclear explosion” in 1974, but its program then remained largely dormant until Pakistan’s nuclear progress prompted weaponization efforts in the late 1980s. India tested nuclear weapons in 1998 and adopted a posture of assured retaliation, no first use, civilian control, and primarily strategic weapons.

Pakistan’s nuclear program, Narang argues, was driven mainly by India’s conventional military superiority and the trauma of the 1971 war that led to Bangladesh’s independence. Pakistan pursued nuclear weapons through uranium enrichment and later plutonium production, received assistance from China, and developed delivery systems with Chinese and North Korean links. Its doctrine emphasizes first use and battlefield nuclear weapons to deter Indian conventional attacks.

The lecture contrasts South Asia with the Cold War, noting shorter missile flight times, less mature command systems, geographic proximity, and the presence of militant proxy attacks. Narang reviews crises including Kargil in 1999, the 2001 Indian Parliament attack, and the 2008 Mumbai attacks, arguing that Pakistan’s nuclear posture has constrained India’s conventional retaliation. He describes India as frustrated by militant attacks but cautious because retaliation could risk nuclear escalation.

In discussion, Narang addresses Pakistan’s strategic motivations, militant groups, U.S. policy toward Pakistan, A.Q. Khan’s proliferation network, and the difficulty of using sanctions after Pakistan became nuclear. He concludes that South Asia remains unstable because future mass-casualty attacks in India could create pressure for military retaliation, while Pakistan’s tactical and strategic nuclear capabilities increase escalation risks.
AIRSS generates chemically informed random structures using MINSEP and TARGVOL constraints, then optimizes overlaps and lattice/ionic degrees of freedom at fixed volume.

The Supreme Court will hear a case on whether state “affidavit of merit” requirements for medical malpractice suits apply in federal court. Delaware’s statute requires either obvious negligence or an affidavit from a medical professional supporting the claim. Harold Berk, a Florida resident, sued a Delaware doctor and hospital in federal court without such an affidavit; lower courts dismissed the case, treating the requirement as substantive under the Erie doctrine.

Berk argues federal procedural rules govern pleading requirements and do not require an affidavit. The doctor and hospital argue Delaware’s statute does not conflict with federal rules and serves as a substantive limit on malpractice litigation. Supporting professors argue applying such state procedures in federal court would disrupt federal judicial administration. The case could affect whether plaintiffs who can access federal court face fewer barriers than those in state court.

The speaker said the opponent’s power play was effective, creating chances and scoring key goals, while their own team needed better positioning in lanes and stronger special teams. They felt their team had good stretches, especially late in the second period, but momentum shifted after the opponent’s early push and power-play success. The speaker noted surprise at some calls, emphasized being more careful with sticks and interference, and said the team must regroup for Thursday.

The President informs Congress that South Carolina’s ordinance nullifying federal tariff and revenue laws has created the emergency anticipated in his annual message. The ordinance declares certain acts of Congress void within South Carolina, forbids enforcement of duties, blocks appeals to the U.S. Supreme Court, requires state officers and jurors to swear support for the ordinance, and threatens separation from the Union if the federal government uses force or otherwise coerces the State.

He reports that South Carolina’s legislature and governors have taken further measures to enforce the ordinance, obstruct federal revenue collection, protect those resisting federal law, organize militia and volunteers, and authorize resistance to federal authority. He argues these actions would overthrow the federal revenue system in South Carolina, give its ports an unlawful preference, and challenge the supremacy of the Constitution and laws of the United States.

The President maintains that South Carolina has not used constitutional remedies such as the courts, elections, or amendment, but has instead set its own authority above federal law. He rejects the claimed right of a single State to nullify federal laws or withdraw from the Union at will, calling such purposes revolutionary and inconsistent with the obligations of the federal compact.

He states that existing laws and ordinary judicial processes may be inadequate because South Carolina’s measures would use state courts, sheriffs, penalties, and armed force to prevent customs officers and federal courts from acting. He has already directed Treasury officials and collectors to perform their duties and moved the Charleston custom-house to Castle Pinckney as a precaution.

He recommends that Congress authorize measures to secure customs collection, including allowing the President to alter ports and districts, place custom-houses in secure locations, protect vessels and cargoes in federal custody with land and naval forces or militia when necessary, permit removal of certain state suits against federal officers to federal courts, provide protection and redress for those obeying federal law, and adapt existing militia laws to meet organized resistance. He closes by urging Congress to preserve public order, enforce the laws, and affirm the supremacy of the Constitution and the indissolubility of the Union.

This study reviewed plasma microbial cell-free DNA sequencing results from the Karius Test in a large commercial cohort to assess performance metrics, positivity rates, and microbial diversity. The Karius Test detects and quantifies mcfDNA from more than 1,500 bacteria, DNA viruses, fungi, and parasites in plasma.

From April 2018 to September 2021, 19,739 samples from 16,172 hospitalized patients across 39 states and Washington, D.C., were tested. The median time from sample receipt to result was 26 hours, and 96% of samples produced valid results. Among 18,690 analyzed reports from 15,165 patients, 58% identified at least one microbe, while 42% were negative. Positive reports included 22,792 detections representing 701 unique taxa: 526 bacteria, 103 fungi, 47 viruses, and 24 parasites.

The 50 most frequently reported taxa accounted for 69% of all detections and included 36 bacteria, 9 viruses, and 5 fungi. Common detections included cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, Candida species, Pneumocystis jirovecii, Aspergillus fumigatus, and multiple bacterial taxa. The test also detected diagnostically challenging organisms, including Legionella, Nocardia, Mycobacterium, zoonotic and vector-borne bacteria, systemic dimorphic fungi, Mucorales, dematiaceous fungi, microsporidia, protozoa, and helminths.

The authors state that test performance in this large cohort was consistent with prior validation data and that unbiased plasma mcfDNA sequencing can detect a broad range of common and uncommon pathogens within a clinically relevant timeframe. They also note that positivity was lower than in studies focused on defined clinical uses, supporting the need for diagnostic stewardship and further studies to clarify optimal indications, interpretation, clinical impact, and cost effectiveness. Limitations included lack of orthogonal testing data, limited clinical context, absence of treatment and outcome data, and constraints in analyzing repeated testing.

Coach Julien said the team did not play its best game, citing poor decision-making, weak puck movement, coverage issues, and an “average” overall performance that was not good enough. He credited the players for battling back, tying the game, and giving themselves a chance, but said the opponent was better and capitalized on mistakes. He emphasized refocusing after frustration with calls, improving for the next game, and treating the series as tight and competitive.

Julien praised Patrice Bergeron’s consistent two-way play and playoff success, Jagr’s playmaking and work habits, and Johnny’s reliable defense and scoring. He said players need open communication with coaches and noted Tyler wanted to know how he could help. He also discussed lineup and role flexibility, penalty killing, faceoffs, and the importance of players embracing assigned roles. Julien said the focus remains on winning the current game, making smart decisions, and not looking ahead.

This passage presents a pilot study on using a convolutional neural network to classify thyroid ultrasound images as benign or malignant. Thyroid nodules can be difficult to detect early, and existing diagnostic methods such as fine needle aspiration are invasive, while ultrasound interpretation requires expert radiologists. The study used the public Thyroid Digital Image Database, labeling TI-RADS TR2 and TR3 images as benign and TR4 and TR5 as malignant. Images were normalized, augmented through rotation, shifting, and flipping, and class weights were applied to address an imbalance favoring malignant cases. The model combined pre-trained VGG-16 and Inception v3 networks, used binary cross-entropy, and was trained with early stopping and learning-rate adjustments. It was trained for 10 epochs with a batch size of 8. The hybrid model achieved 87.5% accuracy and an AUROC of 0.929. The authors state that results were limited by the small, skewed dataset and suggest that larger clinical datasets and normal images could improve the model.

India’s opposition Congress party elected Rahul Gandhi unopposed as president, succeeding his mother Sonia Gandhi, as it prepares to challenge Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the 2019 national elections. Gandhi has faced doubts over his leadership since Congress’s heavy 2014 defeat, while Modi remains highly popular. Congress hopes upcoming state elections, including in Gujarat, can help revive the party amid criticism of slowing growth and tax implementation.

NVIDIA filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended April 28, 2019. Revenue was $2.22 billion, down 31% from $3.21 billion a year earlier. Net income was $394 million, or $0.64 diluted EPS, down from $1.24 billion, or $1.98 diluted EPS. Gross margin was 58.4%, compared with 64.5% a year earlier. Operating expenses rose 21% to $938 million, driven by employee-related costs, infrastructure, stock-based compensation, and Mellanox acquisition costs.

GPU segment revenue was $2.02 billion, down 27%, reflecting declines in gaming and data center revenue and the absence of cryptocurrency mining processor revenue. Tegra Processor revenue was $198 million, down 55%, mainly due to lower shipments of SOC modules for gaming platforms. By market, Gaming revenue was $1.06 billion, Data Center $634 million, Professional Visualization $266 million, Automotive $166 million, and OEM and Other $99 million.

Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $7.80 billion, up from $7.42 billion at January 27, 2019. Operating cash flow was $720 million. NVIDIA paid $97 million in dividends during the quarter and intended to return $3.00 billion to shareholders by the end of fiscal 2020, including prior repurchases.

On March 10, 2019, NVIDIA agreed to acquire Mellanox for $125 per share in cash, representing an enterprise value of approximately $6.9 billion, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. A $350 million termination fee could apply under certain circumstances.

NVIDIA adopted a new lease accounting standard, recognizing $470 million of operating lease assets and $500 million of operating lease liabilities. The company reported no borrowings under its $575 million credit agreement and no commercial paper issued. Legal matters included settled patent litigation, securities and derivative lawsuits related to channel inventory and cryptocurrency mining demand, and litigation concerning the Mellanox merger. Management concluded disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of April 28, 2019.

The passage examines the relationship between interest rates and the S&P 500 using backtests based on the 10-year yield and a simple moving average rule. It notes that while finance theory often assumes stocks and interest rates have an inverse relationship, correlations have become more positive since the 2000s. A strategy buying the S&P 500 when rates were rising produced poor compounded returns. A strategy buying when rates were falling performed much better, with higher CAGR, slightly less market exposure, and similar drawdowns, though it worked better before the 1990s than during the 2000s and 2010s.

President Barack Obama will deliver a farewell address on Jan. 10 in Chicago to reflect on his presidency and thank supporters. In an email, he cited George Washington’s farewell address and emphasized national challenges, change, and unity. Donald Trump, who pledged to reverse key Obama policies, will be sworn in on Jan. 20.

Technology, market access, and economic conditions have made entrepreneurship increasingly accessible. Hiscox’s 2016 DNA of Entrepreneur report surveyed over 4,000 small and medium-sized businesses in six countries, including more than 1,000 in the U.S. Among U.S. respondents, 50 percent said they always wanted to be their own boss, while flexibility, control, and remote work were stronger motivators than making more money.

U.S. entrepreneurs reported strong performance, with 70 percent seeing revenue growth, 68 percent profit growth, and 73 percent more new customers. U.S. businesses also showed the highest optimism among surveyed countries, with 23 percent planning to hire. However, 61 percent lacked succession plans.

Funding remains a challenge: 17 percent said bank funding was harder to obtain, 23 percent used personal credit cards, and others used venture capital or peer-to-peer funding. Oregon offers several state-backed financing programs for small businesses. Government support was viewed less favorably, with 34 percent saying policies support entrepreneurs and 31 percent reporting negative effects from political instability.

The passage describes American entrepreneurship as cautiously optimistic, with Oregon experiencing strong job and wage growth and continued opportunities for small business ownership.

The Apple Watch Series 3 with LTE is expanding slowly despite Apple’s dominance in wearables. After limited launches and carrier support issues, LTE pre-orders will open May 4 in Denmark, Sweden, and India, with deliveries a week later. Three will support it in Denmark and Sweden; Reliance Jio and Airtel in India.

IFC Films promoted Mark Boxer to executive vice president of sales and distribution and Lauren Schwartz to senior vice president of publicity and promotions. Boxer oversees distribution across IFC Films, Sundance Selects, and IFC Midnight, while Schwartz has led promotional campaigns for notable films. Company co-presidents praised their contributions to IFC Films’ reputation in independent cinema.

The MMA Manifesto’s middleweight rankings list Michael Bisping as No. 1 and UFC Middleweight Champion, followed by Luke Rockhold, Yoel Romero, Chris Weidman and Ronaldo “Jacare” Souza tied at No. 4, Gegard Mousasi, Robert Whittaker, Anderson Silva, Vitor Belfort, and Kelvin Gastelum. Suspended fighters and those inactive for at least 12 months without a scheduled fight are excluded. Belfort is scheduled to face Gastelum at UFC Fight Night: Belfort vs Gastelum on March 11. Derek Brunson dropped out of the top 10, while Brunson, David Branch, Mamed Khalidov, and Krzysztof Jotko are listed as bubbling under.

Marquez Charter Elementary reopened a temporary campus nearly nine months after the Palisades fire destroyed much of the school, making its roughly 130 students the first public school students to return to a campus destroyed by the January Palisades and Eaton fires. The temporary site includes 19 classrooms, a kitchen, library and play areas. Its rebuild is estimated at $202.6 million and expected by 2028, while rebuilding three damaged campuses may cost about $600 million. Enrollment at Marquez has fallen about 58%, and most students no longer live in the Palisades. Some parents welcomed the return as a milestone, while others raised concerns about transportation, environmental risks and lack of consensus. Other affected schools in Los Angeles and Pasadena are using temporary structures or awaiting rebuild plans and funding.

The study examines open education through bibliometric analysis to identify trends, emerging areas, and implications for policy and practice. It addresses gaps in prior research, which often focuses narrowly on OER or MOOCs rather than the broader open education ecosystem, including open textbooks, open-access journals, pedagogy, assessment, and knowledge creation.

Using the Web of Science database, the authors analyzed 402 English-language publications on open education up to September 2023 with VOSviewer. The dataset received 3,041 citations, with an average of 7.56 citations per article and an H-index of 27. Publications began appearing significantly in 2016, peaked at 82 in 2020, and declined to 56 in 2021.

Co-citation analysis identified five research clusters: evolving open education, OER’s role in education, adoption of open education, educational paradigms of MOOCs, and implementation of open educational practices. Co-word analysis identified five emerging themes: blended learning in open education, openness in the COVID-19 era, challenges of OER adoption, inclusive digital pedagogy, and collaborative online academia.

The findings show that open education is dynamic and shaped by pedagogy, technology, equity, access, and institutional practices. OER can reduce costs, expand access, and support flexible learning, but adoption faces barriers including faculty resistance, limited institutional support, infrastructure gaps, sustainability concerns, and regional inequalities. The study recommends further research using additional databases, qualitative methods, and attention to regional and institutional differences.

The OHL trading strategy is an intraday stock trading approach using the open, high, and low prices in the first few minutes of a session to determine entries. A buy signal occurs when the open equals the day’s low, suggesting bullish sentiment; a sell signal occurs when the open equals the day’s high, suggesting bearish sentiment. It is typically applied on 1-, 5-, or 15-minute charts, especially near the market open.

Some traders combine OHL with central pivot range levels, going long only when an OHL buy signal occurs above CPR levels and short only when an OHL sell signal occurs below them. Backtests on the S&P 500/ES futures showed 1,401 trades with an average gain of 0.04%, improving to 0.06% when today’s open was above yesterday’s close and falling to 0.01% when below. WTI crude oil showed a 0.12% average gain under similar bullish conditions. Reversed rules produced 0.00% average gains for SPY and WTI. The article concludes that early trading direction has some predictive value, though the simple backtests require further development.

The passage presents a neural solver intended to apply physics-informed neural networks to complex multi-patch CAD geometries. It addresses three PINN limitations: enforcing solution continuity across patch interfaces, strongly imposing Dirichlet boundary conditions, and handling geometry parts with large variations in size and shape. The method combines PINNs with isogeometric analysis, using NURBS parametrizations to map neural-network ansatz functions from reference domains to physical domains. Patch-specific neural networks approximate interior solutions, while interface-specific terms enforce continuity across neighboring patches. Dirichlet conditions are imposed through modified ansatz/output constructions rather than weak loss penalties. Training uses a variational PINN formulation in which the discretized energy functional serves as the loss. The work relates this approach to prior PINN–IGA, domain decomposition, boundary-condition enforcement, and normalization methods, and states that its efficacy is demonstrated on 2D magnetostatics and 3D nonlinear solid mechanics applications.

Owen Sound Foodland is among 87 Ontario stores approved by the LCBO to sell beer and cider starting in April, bringing the provincial total to 370. Owner Bill Graham said the move supports one-stop shopping. The store, located in Georgian Bluffs, will sell alcohol from its new 34,000-square-foot location, tentatively opening March 22, with expanded departments, services, seating, and staffing increasing from 100 to about 160 employees.

A Merrion Capital review found 88% of 33 Irish publicly quoted companies recently met or beat earnings expectations, with average EPS growth of 8% despite sterling weakness after Brexit. Aryzta, Ryanair, Tullow Oil and IFG missed forecasts, while 16 companies including CRH, Kerry, Grafton, Greencore, Cairn Homes and FBD beat them. The Iseq reached a 15-month high, though it lagged other European markets amid Brexit concerns. Irish Continental Group led Iseq 10 gains, while Aryzta was the worst performer, down 27.2%.

First-principles calculations are accurate but computationally costly, while machine learning force fields offer faster alternatives. The passage introduces ADAPT, a coordinate-based Transformer for predicting per-atom forces and energies from Cartesian coordinates and atomic descriptors, targeting defect computations in silicon. Unlike graph neural network approaches, ADAPT avoids graph-based inductive biases and uses attention over all atom interactions. It is trained on a DFT defect database and reportedly outperforms pretrained and retrained MACE and MatterSim models while requiring much lower training cost. ADAPT represents each atom as a token with 12 coordinate and atomic-feature inputs, embedded into a higher-dimensional space for force prediction.

The Detroit Tigers are linked to free-agent closer Robert Suarez, who is expected to opt out this offseason. The team used a closer-by-committee approach and lacks a true closer. Suarez posted a 2.97 ERA, 75 strikeouts, 0.904 WHIP and 40 saves in 70 appearances this season, making him a suggested fit for Detroit.

Haas School’s Nov. 2, 2000 alumni jobs bulletin lists 17 opportunities from companies including Plumtree Software, Sanrise, ViroLogic, Atomz.com, Kaiser Permanente, Copper Mountain Networks, Loudcloud, Terrace Consulting, Rhapsody Networks, PG&E, McKinsey, Amerix, The Nature Conservancy/PBS, Zhanra Infostructure, and Morgan Stanley Dean Witter. Roles span marketing, program management, finance, business development, product management, operations, consulting, analysis, and technical positions across California, Chicago, Virginia, and Shenzhen. The bulletin also includes expanded job descriptions, application contacts, Haas alumni career resources, subscription instructions, and announcements for the UC Berkeley Business Plan Competition, Big Game BBQ, and Women in Leadership Conference.

This research examines parents’ experiences, opinions, criticisms, and suggestions regarding compulsory emergency distance education in Turkey during the COVID-19 pandemic. After face-to-face education was suspended in March 2020, Turkey used platforms and services such as EBA, EBA TV, ADES, technical support, and psychological support to continue education.

The study used a descriptive survey model and included 2,371 parents of K-12 students from regions across Turkey. Data were collected through a 16-question questionnaire and analyzed with descriptive statistics, frequency analysis, and content analysis.

Findings show that 57.7% of parents expressed positive views about distance education, mainly because it maintained educational continuity, protected health, and allowed learning independent of time and place. However, 42.3% expressed negative views, citing inefficiency, inadequacy, adaptation difficulties, learning problems, technical issues, unequal opportunities, and insufficient content. Most parents did not arrange private lessons for their children during this period. Communication with teachers was mostly conducted through WhatsApp, followed by Zoom/Skype, phone calls, and SMS.

Parents most strongly agreed that students should not be charged internet connection fees for EBA use, that students had difficulty adapting to distance education, that distance education exams did not measure real success, and that students struggled to maintain study discipline. They most strongly rejected the idea that distance education should fully replace face-to-face education. Major criticisms focused on inadequacy, difficulty, limited lesson time, lack of similarity to face-to-face education, and technical problems. Positive views emphasized process management, opportunity for repetition, and health protection. Suggestions included conducting exams, continuing distance education as support after face-to-face education resumes, improving content and materials, and increasing lesson duration.

The study concludes that parents generally saw distance education as preferable to no education, but not as a substitute for face-to-face education. They reported problems related to student adaptation, motivation, self-discipline, technical access, internet quality, device availability, content adequacy, and inequality of opportunity. The study recommends improving technological infrastructure, reducing internet access costs, supporting families lacking digital devices, strengthening open educational resources, enriching content, and developing digital literacy skills for learners, teachers, parents, and society.

The Mongolian and Tibetan Affairs Commission is to be merged with the Ministry of Culture and the Mainland Affairs Council by year’s end, after nearly a century of operation. The Executive Yuan has not budgeted for it next fiscal year and plans to transfer six of its 49 employees to the council, with others continuing related work under the ministry. The commission, founded in 1928, has faced abolition calls because Taiwan does not control Mongolia or Tibet, though the Constitution still lists them as traditional territories. The Executive Yuan plans to propose scrapping the law authorizing the commission. Reactions were mixed: some lawmakers supported abolition, while others raised concerns about Mongolia’s status, cross-strait implications, or urged abolishing other agencies.

The speaker reflects on growth despite losing, emphasizing that second place is not rewarded in pro sports. They praise the opponents’ disciplined, team-first play and note missed chances in a game decided by small margins.

Jose Mourinho urged Marouane Fellaini to sign a new Manchester United contract amid a stand-off over a new deal. Fellaini faces further tests on a knee injury after being substituted against Tottenham and could be out for up to two months. He will miss the Huddersfield match and may miss United’s Champions League games against Sevilla, having already missed 20 games through injury this season.

Merger arbitrage seeks to profit from the spread between a target company’s market price and the acquisition offer price after a merger or acquisition is announced. It requires assessing deal completion likelihood, regulatory risks, deal terms, liquidity, market conditions, and ongoing developments, as failed deals can cause large losses. Backtests of available funds showed lower returns but much lower volatility than the S&P 500: the IQ Merger Arbitrage ETF had a 2.73% CAGR versus 18.52% for the S&P 500, while The Merger Fund had a 4.46% CAGR versus 17.37% for SPY. A Verdad Research study of 835 deals from 2000 to 2020 found an 89% closure rate, with successful deals averaging 2.0% returns, canceled deals losing 2.8%, and a blended average return of 1.5% on long exposure. The passage concludes that merger arbitrage can provide uncorrelated returns but is difficult to execute qualitatively because it requires deep deal-specific analysis.

Renewable energy output fluctuates because resources like wind and sunlight vary, creating challenges for grids without storage and requiring backup power plants to remain available. Prof. Mahesh Bandi of OIST used turbulence theory and wind plant data to explain wind power fluctuations in a paper in Physical Review Letters. He showed that wind power fluctuation spectra match wind speed fluctuation spectra not simply because power depends on wind speed cubed, but because of how turbulence affects measurements over time at fixed turbine locations.

Bandi found that turbines within the same turbulent wind eddies can produce correlated power fluctuations, making a wind plant behave like one large turbine. Even geographically dispersed wind plants can show correlated low-frequency fluctuations if they fall within the same long time-scale eddy, though high-frequency fluctuations may average out. This demonstrates a natural limit to “geographic smoothing,” the idea that dispersed wind farms can average out each other’s variability. Using data from wind plants in Texas and Ireland, Bandi showed this limit exists in practice.

The findings may improve estimates of reserve power needs and inform energy and environmental policy by helping determine better regional mixes of renewable energy sources.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 26, 2022, reporting that it released financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended December 31, 2021 by posting its Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2021 Update on its website. The update is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The filing also includes a Cover Page Interactive Data File as Exhibit 104 and was signed by CFO Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

Oxygen-containing rare-earth hydrides show color-neutral photochromism under ambient conditions and are promising for smart windows. This study examines yttrium oxyhydride (YHO) films, whose optical transmittance under blue-light illumination exhibits rapid initial photodarkening followed by slower decay, with slower bleaching afterward. Simple zero-, first-, and second-order kinetic models do not describe the behavior. Because REHO films are multiphase, the authors propose a two-phase exponential model incorporating a non-photoactive fraction and hydrogen transfer. EELS spectra show different plasmon peaks for photochromic and opaque YHO films, suggesting more free or mobile hydrogen in photochromic films. The fitted model identifies a fast process occurring in the first 2–3 minutes, likely linked to local structural changes or loosely bound hydrogen loss, and a slower process attributed to hydrogen migration or diffusion with lattice contraction. The model fits the experimental transmittance data well and may aid comparison and optimization of photochromic films.

The federal government shut down after Congress failed to pass a short-term funding bill, creating uncertainty for education programs already affected by grants cancellations and funding freezes. Most schools should see minimal short-term disruption, with Title I and special education funds expected to be available, but districts relying on impact aid could face cash flow problems. A longer shutdown could affect Head Start, school nutrition programs, and other supports for low-income families.

The Trump administration may use the shutdown to pursue further downsizing, after the Office of Management and Budget directed agencies to consider additional mass layoffs. Federal employee unions have sued over the plan.

Head Start grantees serving about 6,500 children expect funding soon and do not plan immediate closures, though longer delays could change that. WIC may require states to use their own funds, while school meal reimbursements for September and October are expected to continue. SNAP benefits should continue if the shutdown lasts no more than a week.

At the Education Department, most employees would stop working, civil rights investigations and regulatory work would pause, and states and districts may be unable to get grant support. Ongoing work, including education statistics restructuring and some charter school funding timelines, could be delayed.

Chicago wheat rose 0.9% to $4.54-3/4 a bushel, recovering slightly after its largest three-day decline since 2013, as rain and snow benefited drought-hit U.S. winter wheat areas in the southern Plains. Corn edged up 0.1% to $3.75-1/2 after four losses, while soybeans rose 0.2% to $10.25 following Monday’s decline. USDA ratings showed Kansas winter wheat good-to-excellent conditions slipped to 11%, with Texas also lower. Ukraine’s winter grains were mostly good or satisfactory. Analysts cited Argentine rains pressuring corn. Oil and Asian shares fell amid crude supply concerns and U.S. technology stock weakness.

William Asa Hutchinson III, son of Arkansas Gov. Asa Hutchinson, was arrested in West Fork on charges including DWI, speeding and implied consent violation. He was released on bond and has upcoming court dates. The arrest follows a dismissed prior DWI case and a 2016 Alabama drug-related arrest.

U.S. investor Paul Kazarian, owner of Japonica Partners and a major holder of Greek debt, has opened his first European office in Lisbon and said Portugal’s corporate sector offers investment opportunities. He praised Socialist governments in Portugal and Greece for improving public finances after the euro zone debt crisis. Kazarian said Japonica remains a long-term holder of Greek debt after buying bonds when investors avoided Athens. In Portugal, he is considering areas such as real estate and technology, noting the property boom and growing tech sector. He said Portuguese firms often focus on former colonies such as Angola and Mozambique, but Japonica could add value by helping attractive businesses become globally competitive. The Lisbon office will also examine opportunities across Europe.

The Education Department said it will rewrite Obama-era Borrower Defense to Repayment and Gainful Employment rules on student loan forgiveness and college accountability. Betsy DeVos called the regulations burdensome, confusing and unfair, while saying nearly 16,000 pending claims will still be processed. Eight states and Washington, D.C., moved in federal court to preserve the rules, arguing they protect borrowers from misleading and predatory institutions. Critics said revising the rules could leave students with unaffordable debt and taxpayers responsible for costs, while an industry group said the move would protect students from fraud and schools from unfair attacks.

Nigeria’s T-bills market was slightly bullish amid strong liquidity from a N300bn bond maturity. CBN’s N49.60bn PMA was moderately oversubscribed. OBB and OVN rates fell to 1.75% and 2.50%. FX rates weakened in several segments, while sovereign bonds lost ground, especially the 2047s.

This study investigated degradation in commercial Ni-rich NMC/graphite 3032 coin cells cycled at high C-rates using XRD, SEM, EDS, and lithium Nuclear Reaction Analysis (Li-NRA). Cells were cycled at 1C, 2C, and 3C between 2.7 and 4.3 V at 25 °C for 278 total cycles. Capacity remained stable at 1C, declined to 132.84 mAh after 67 cycles at 2C, and fell to 42.67 mAh after 200 cycles at 3C, with internal resistance rising to about 0.34 Ω.

XRD showed contraction of the NMC cathode c-lattice parameter after cycling, indicating structural degradation and reduced lithium transport, while graphite showed slight c-axis expansion linked to lithium trapping, SEI growth, or disorder. SEM revealed surface decomposition and micro-cavities in cycled cathodes and roughness, cracks, and exfoliation in cycled graphite. EDS indicated cathode density decreased after cycling, while anode density increased, consistent with lithium accumulation and surface-layer changes.

Li-NRA quantified lithium redistribution: the degraded NMC cathode lost 1.86 × 10²² Li atoms/cm³, while the graphite anode gained 1.38 × 10²² Li atoms/cm³. The study concludes that high C-rate cycling accelerates capacity fade through cathode lithium loss, structural degradation, SEI growth, lithium trapping, and lithium plating, and that Li-NRA is effective for spatially resolved lithium profiling in battery electrodes.

The University of Calgary Chess Club will host the annual Battle of Alberta chess tournament Feb. 18–19 in That Empty Space. About 30–40 players are expected, including U of C students, independent players and non-students. The tournament follows World Chess Federation rules, and registration costs $10 for students and $15 for non-students.

The Panthers signed Kawann “KK” Short to a five-year, $80 million deal, ending lengthy negotiations and avoiding the franchise tag. The move reinforces GM Dave Gettleman’s focus on defensive linemen and Carolina’s win-now approach. The team also added veterans Julius Peppers, Mike Adams and Captain Munnerlyn to a defense led by Luke Kuechly and Thomas Davis.

Offensively, concerns remain about Cam Newton’s recovery from shoulder surgery and recent injuries, prompting talk of evolving the offense toward fewer zone reads and more short passing. Carolina replaced departing receivers Ted Ginn Jr. and Philly Brown with Russell Shepard and Charles Johnson, and invested heavily in left tackle Matt Kalil while hoping Michael Oher returns healthy.

With Short secured, the Panthers’ next major move is the draft, where they hold the No. 8 pick. The passage identifies Leonard Fournette, Christian McCaffrey and O.J. Howard as potential offensive playmakers to help Newton.

Prime Day discounts make some MacBooks more attractive than others. The M4 MacBook Air, especially the 13-inch model at $800 with 16 GB RAM and 256 GB storage, is described as the best deal and suitable for most people. Rumored M5 MacBook Air upgrades are not expected to be major. The M1 MacBook Air at $600 remains a budget option, though a new entry-level MacBook may replace it. MacBook Pro discounts are smaller, and potential M5 and later redesigned M6 models make waiting more appealing for buyers seeking maximum performance.

Sugar futures are derivative contracts to buy or sell a specified quantity of sugar at a future date for a pre-agreed price. They trade on ICE Futures US under symbol SB and on CME Globex under symbol YO. ICE contracts are physically settled, while CME contracts are financially settled. Each contract represents 112,000 pounds of sugar, with a minimum price fluctuation of 0.0001 per pound and a tick size of $11.20.

Sugar futures can be used for speculation, portfolio diversification, hedging, or arbitrage. A sugar futures trading strategy may use technical and fundamental analysis, entry and exit rules, position sizing, and risk management. The passage notes that sugar is difficult to trade and that the author does not currently trade a sugar strategy. A tested ATR channel breakout trend-following strategy showed only limited promise, with a low win ratio, many small winners, and a few large winners.

Sugar prices are affected by supply, inventories, crops, weather, government subsidies and tariffs, ethanol demand, oil prices, Brazil’s currency value, geopolitics, and regulations. Sugar futures have historically performed better in February, June, July, November, and December. Based on TradingView data cited, SB sugar futures reached an all-time high of 66.00 US cents in November 1974 and an all-time low of 2.63 US cents in June 1985. Futures trading risks include adverse price movement and leverage-related losses.

The passage describes systems and methods using a cache coherent switch on chip connected through Compute Express Link (CXL) to enable low-latency memory access, coherent caching, component disaggregation, and composable server resource sharing. The switch may connect processors, accelerators, memories, storage, ASICs, NICs, persistent memory, GPUs, FPGAs, and other devices, allowing component-to-component traffic and resource pooling without requiring the CPU to control all transfers.

The cache coherent switch on chip may include upstream and downstream PCI/CXL ports, switched fabric circuitry, processing cores, virtual hierarchies, bridges for legacy devices, fabric managers, and accelerators for compression, security, erasure coding, and computational storage services. It may allocate, deallocate, hot-insert, and hot-remove resources, assign devices to virtual hierarchies, and manage cache hierarchies and cache buffer operations.

The described systems support memory expansion, pooled memory and accelerator resources across servers, racks, data centers, Ethernet, the Internet, or other networks, including CXL-over-Ethernet bridging. They may use local memory as a cache buffer for remote persistent memory, support AI/ML prefetching, maintain cache coherency between accelerators and processors, and reduce CPU bottlenecks in data movement.

Additional embodiments describe Ethernet-connected memory, CXL-to-Ethernet bridges, packet and frame formats for read/write requests and responses, modified Layer 2 formats with configurable interframe gaps, IP security headers, CXL over MPLS/IP/TCP/UDP/ROCE software stacks, and defined command codes for memory, prefetch, hot-add, hot-remove, discovery, and error messages.

President Thomas Jefferson issued a proclamation on November 27, 1806, warning that people in the United States were organizing an unlawful military expedition against Spanish territories. He ordered participants to withdraw, commanded officials to prevent the enterprise, seize related vessels and supplies, and bring offenders to justice.

The Supreme Court appeared likely to give police more leeway to enter homes without warrants during emergencies in William Case’s challenge to a Montana incident in which officers entered his home after suicide-related threats and shot him. Case argued evidence should be excluded because officers lacked a warrant and probable cause, while Montana argued the Fourth Amendment bars unreasonable searches, not all warrantless entries. Several justices questioned applying probable cause outside criminal investigations and discussed an “objectively reasonable” emergency standard. The court also debated whether to apply that standard itself or send the case back to Montana courts. A decision is expected by late June or early July.

Kano Pillars drew 1-1 with Niger Tornadoes in a rescheduled week 12 NPFL match at Sani Abacha Stadium. Andrew Ikefe scored for Tornadoes in the 19th minute, while Junior Lokosa equalised from a penalty in the 81st, taking his season tally to 11 goals. Coach Ibrahim Musa praised his players’ fighting spirit and said the team would prepare for Kwara United.

Microsoft’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2019 reported revenue of $33.1 billion, up from $29.1 billion a year earlier, and net income of $10.7 billion, up from $8.8 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.38 versus $1.14. Operating income rose to $12.7 billion from $10.0 billion, while gross margin increased to $22.6 billion.

Revenue grew across all segments: Productivity and Business Processes reached $11.1 billion, Intelligent Cloud $10.8 billion, and More Personal Computing $11.1 billion. Commercial cloud revenue increased 36% to $11.6 billion, driven by growth in Office 365 Commercial, Azure, LinkedIn, Dynamics 365, and other cloud services. Azure revenue grew 59%, LinkedIn revenue grew 25%, and Windows Commercial revenue grew 26%.

As of September 30, 2019, Microsoft had total assets of $279.0 billion, total liabilities of $172.9 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $106.1 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $136.6 billion. Net cash from operations was $13.8 billion, while financing activities used $10.2 billion, including debt repayments, share repurchases, and dividends.

Microsoft repurchased $4.0 billion of common stock during the quarter and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.51 per share. The company also had $7.4 billion remaining under its 2016 share repurchase authorization and approved a new $40.0 billion repurchase program in September 2019.

The company reported an effective tax rate of 16%, compared with 14% in the prior year. It remained under IRS audit for tax years 2004 to 2013, with primary unresolved issues related to transfer pricing. Microsoft also disclosed ongoing legal and regulatory matters, including patent claims, Canadian antitrust class actions, a China antitrust investigation, cell phone litigation, and employment-related litigation.
