The passage describes patent-related methods, apparatuses, and systems for multi-user wireless transmissions in WLAN and related wireless systems. It identifies limitations in IEEE 802.11ac group ID mechanisms, including limited support for large numbers of clusters, multiple MU transmission schemes, combined OFDMA and OFDM MU-MIMO grouping, flexible per-transmission scheduling, and MAC efficiency due to MU control frame overhead.

The disclosed embodiments include wireless transmit/receive units configured to receive and decode null data packet multi-user MAC PLCP protocol data units, determine whether a received frame is an NDP MU MAC PPDU based on an NDP condition, process an NDP SIG field containing MU control information, determine an NDP MAC frame type, generate a response, and transmit the response.

The passage describes example communications systems, WTRUs, RANs, base stations, access points, STAs, core network components, and wireless technologies that may support the disclosed embodiments. It also describes WLAN infrastructure and independent BSS operation, wideband channel aggregation, and MU transmission mechanisms.

Several MU clustering and scheduling mechanisms are disclosed. An AP may transmit clustering management frames containing membership and position bit-fields, define clusters for DL and UL OFDM MU-MIMO and OFDMA schemes, assign cluster ID ranges by fixed specification or signaling, and update user positions per transmission through PLCP SIG fields or MU control frames. Other embodiments assign cluster IDs using NDP MAC frames or omit cluster IDs by signaling MU clustering directly in MU data transmissions or immediately preceding MU control frames.

The passage further describes using NDP MAC PPDUs to reduce MU control overhead. Two HE NDP MAC PPDU examples are provided: one with a single HE-NDP-SIG field and another with HE-NDP-SIG-A and HE-NDP-SIG-B fields. These fields may carry common, user-specific, or resource-specific control or management information, including NDP indications, MAC frame bodies, CRCs, tail bits, frame lengths, and dedicated signaling.

Examples of HE NDP MU control frames include MU-RTS, MU-CTS, MU-Poll, ULR, MU schedule, and MU ACK frames. MU-RTS frames may reserve MU transmission opportunities and schedule downlink MU transmissions, while MU-CTS frames may confirm readiness and provide sub-channel or synchronization information. The described frame bodies may include fields such as NDP MAC frame type, MU mode, AP address or transmitter address, group ID, duration, response protocol, bandwidth, synchronization information, NDP-SIG-B presence, PAID, and sub-channel information. STAs may use these fields to determine whether they are intended receivers, prepare responses, transmit response frames using time, frequency, code, or spatial division, or set NAV values if not involved.

During a family road trip to Badlands, Glacier, Yellowstone, and Devil’s Tower, the author reflects on weather and climate communication. Watching Old Faithful’s predicted eruption window prompts thoughts on better conveying uncertainty in forecasts, citing examples such as hurricane cones, Capital Weather Gang graphics, and meteorologists advocating probability ranges. A Yellowstone bison encounter leads to observations that people often ignore warnings and misjudge risks, including floods, heat, climate change, and hurricane evacuations. The author cites views that climate change is a major economic risk and notes psychological factors such as prioritizing familiar goals, optimism bias, and poor risk assessment. At Glacier National Park, the author expresses concern about shrinking glaciers, referencing National Park Service figures showing a decline from more than 100 glaciers in 1910 to 26 active glaciers in 2015. A conversation with a woman who called climate change “fake news” because of cold camping weather highlights the challenge of distinguishing daily weather from global climate trends.

The draw play is a run designed to briefly resemble a pass before a late handoff, aiming to exploit defenses expecting a throw. It is most effective in pass-heavy offenses or obvious passing situations, especially against spread-out defenses. Its main weakness is interior blitz pressure, which can leave an unblocked defender able to stop the tailback in the backfield; offenses may attach an RPO to address this.

Against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, linemen take pass sets to invite defenders upfield, then create inside running lanes, while receivers release vertically to sell pass routes before blocking. The quarterback shows pass before handing off, and the tailback initially mimics pass protection before taking the ball.

Variations include QB Draw, using an athletic quarterback with the same blocking and receiver rules, often with a perimeter RPO, and Lead Draw from 12-personnel Strong-I, which changes tight end, double-team, and fullback assignments.

Kingwood High School in Texas reopened for the first time since Hurricane Harvey caused millions of dollars in flood damage. Its 2,782 students had been relocated during repairs. Renovations included replacing flooring, walls and doors, adding security enhancements, and building a new gym, theater and pool. An open house is planned.

Finnish confidence in German success against Russia had strengthened after Allied reverses, though concern remained about German exhaustion and future Soviet pressure on Finland. Westman said Finland had miscalculated in expecting a short, victorious war ignored by Britain, and future Finnish offensives remained uncertain. In a conversation with Berle, the Finnish Minister discussed deteriorating Finnish-American relations and acknowledged U.S. objections that Finland’s war could not be separated from the broader conflict because Finland was fighting alongside Germany. He reported that continued Finnish policy might lead to a U.S.-Finnish break but said Finland could not fight both Russia and Germany. Schoenfeld reported no Finnish press mention of Stalin’s stated Soviet aims regarding the Baltic States and Karelia, and later said Finnish authorities were suppressing or distorting Roosevelt’s war statements while reporting Churchill more fully. Finland’s increased bread ration, based on promised German grain, was undermined by Baltic ice blocking shipments, forcing requisition of seed and reserve cereals and underscoring dependence on Germany for essential food supplies.

The study examines Moroccan teachers’ perspectives on education leaders’ role in sustaining ICT use in compulsory education after COVID-19. A questionnaire was completed by 130 primary and secondary teachers who stopped using technology after returning to face-to-face classes. Findings show that ICT use was hindered by limited devices, internet access, digital resources, training, techno-pedagogical knowledge, and institutional support. Although Morocco expanded digital platforms, televised lessons, and teacher training during the pandemic, these gains were not sustained. The study concludes that barriers are mainly linked to leadership and system-level issues, and recommends stronger technology leadership, unified platforms, improved training, better infrastructure, digital content quality standards, and greater support for students and teachers.

Ian Murray, 74, was fined after pleading guilty to driving without due care and attention for a collision with a cyclist in Hathersage on May 14. The cyclist suffered bruises, grazes, a facial laceration and pins-and-needles sensations but is expected to recover. Murray said he had not seen the cyclist while turning right into a garage. He was fined £185, ordered to pay £85 costs and a £30 victim surcharge, and received six penalty points.

Strategies for defending a superstar include full pass denial with help defense, trapping mismatches, taking charges, boxing out, influencing the ball away, preventing return passes, and forcing the player to expend energy by defending, running, fighting through screens, and boxing out. Combination defenses may also be used.

A Hylian Shield New Nintendo 2DS XL launches exclusively at GameStop on July 2 for $159.99, pre-loaded with “The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds.” Nintendo’s 3DS family has sold 72 million units globally, while the Switch sold nearly 18 million last fiscal year.

The study investigates how stacking geometry controls magnetic, electronic, and magnetoelectric properties in CrI2 bilayers using first-principles DFT, DFT+U, spin-orbit coupling calculations, and exchange-parameter extraction with TB2J. Monolayer CrI2 is found to have a stripe antiferromagnetic AFx ground state, lying below zigzag AFM, AFy, and ferromagnetic states, with a band gap of about 1.12 eV.

For bilayers, direct and indirect stacking families are examined. The indirect BA′ registry with antiparallel AFx interlayer alignment is identified as the global ground state, with AB′ configurations close in energy and direct or high-symmetry stackings less favorable. Bilayer formation slightly reduces the band gap to about 0.99–1.07 eV due to interlayer hybridization, while gap trends depend on registry, orbital character, and magnetic alignment rather than interlayer distance alone.

Controlled sliding maps show moderate energy barriers of about 25–50 meV per formula unit between registries, suggesting feasible mechanical switching. The nearest-neighbor in-plane exchanges dominate the magnetic energy scale: bilayer formation strengthens antiferromagnetic A–B and ferromagnetic A–A/B–B in-plane couplings by about 6–10% relative to the monolayer. Interlayer exchange is much weaker but changes sign with stacking and magnetic texture, providing secondary tunability.

Symmetry breaking in indirect stackings activates Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions and magnetoelectric coupling, while centrosymmetric configurations forbid them. The symmetric in-plane exchange anisotropy remains nearly registry-independent. Projected band-center analysis indicates spin-selective superexchange through Cr-d and I-p states as the electronic origin of the robust antiferromagnetic order. Berry-phase calculations predict registry-dependent in-plane polarization, linking inversion breaking to anisotropic exchange and magnetoelectric effects.

The work concludes that bilayer CrI2 is a promising platform for stacking-controlled magnetism, mechanically reconfigurable spintronics, and multifunctional van der Waals devices.

Marsha Jackson, newly promoted Head of Internal Audit at NYSE-listed RiseEngineer Corporation, is responsible for financial controls and FCPA compliance, including oversight of its Elysium subsidiary. Elysium ranks low on Transparency International’s Corruption Perceptions Index. After RiseEngineer wins a $1.2 billion Elysium government contract, a whistleblower alleges misconduct.

Marsha’s team finds that RiseEngineer managers had dinners and exchanged gifts with Elysium officials, invited officials and their families to Boston, transferred contract payments from Elysium to headquarters, paid $3 million to TGH Consulting, and withdrew $5 million in cash, only $1 million of which had documentation. An email thread showed one salesperson suggesting legal review and another responding, “Call me.” RiseEngineer Elysium was its auditor’s only client, and two employees suggested the tip may have come from a disgruntled former employee.

The compliance team reports weak controls at RiseEngineer Elysium. Subsidiary head Sarah Smith prioritizes profitability, gives salespeople broad autonomy, and usually defers to sales. Sales staff have uncapped commissions and received $100,000 each from the contract. The finance manager handles accounting and most banking transactions, permits cash withdrawals and transfers with incomplete or no documentation, requires no independent approval, and estimates accounting classifications when uncertain.

The passage also outlines internal control concepts under COSO and FCPA requirements prohibiting bribery of foreign officials and requiring transparent records and accounting controls.

Monitoring distributed applications is complicated by varied interfaces and protocols across custom and third-party components. Monitoring systems often use plugins to adapt these formats to a common interface. Using the adapter pattern, a separate monitoring container transforms an application container’s monitoring output for the general monitoring system, improving maintainability, reuse, independent updates, and resource isolation.

Soccer players specialize by position within formations and systems of play, but all players, especially young players, should learn all skills and experience every position. Coaches should choose a formation, define position names, and use them consistently.

The four general soccer positions are goalkeeper, defenders, midfielders, and forwards. The goalkeeper is the only position named in the Laws of the Game, wears a contrasting jersey, and may handle the ball only inside the team’s penalty area. Defenders play in front of the goalkeeper and focus on covering opponents, winning the ball, blocking shots, and starting counterattacks. Midfielders connect defense and attack, defend after turnovers, support forwards, and need strong all-around skills and fitness. Forwards are the main attackers, expected to create chances, pass, shoot, score, and play under pressure.

Specific position names vary by formation and include center backs, fullbacks, sweepers, outside backs, attacking and defensive midfielders, wing backs, wide midfielders, center forwards, strikers, wings, withdrawn forwards, and supporting strikers. Many soccer positions have synonyms and acronyms, so consistent terminology helps avoid confusing the team.

Skoltech researchers developed a mathematical model of memory based on engrams, sparse neuron groups representing concepts through features tied to sensory input. Their analysis suggests memory capacity is maximized in a seven-dimensional conceptual space, leading to the speculative claim that seven senses may be optimal. The findings may inform robotics, AI, and theoretical models of human memory.

Larry Williams introduced the Williams Vix Fix in 2007 as a synthetic VIX for securities beyond the S&P 500, Nasdaq, and Dow Jones 30. The VIX reflects implied volatility and market fear, with high readings often associated with short-term market lows and low readings with market peaks. The Williams Vix Fix is calculated as `(Highest Close over 22 days – Low) / Highest Close over 22 days * 100`, measuring recent price volatility over about one trading month. The passage says it resembles the real VIX in levels, swings, magnitude, and timing, and may be used in other markets. Tested strategies on stock indices produced positive results, including one improved QQQ strategy with frequent trades, a 75% win rate, and returns exceeding buy-and-hold while invested 20% of the time. The indicator is described as mean-reverting and working reasonably well on stock indices, including on the short side.

The passage explains how to backtest a Bollinger Band trading strategy in Python using historical Microsoft data from yfinance, along with pandas, numpy, and matplotlib. It calculates 20-day simple moving averages and standard deviations, then creates upper and lower Bollinger Bands at two standard deviations from the SMA. The strategy assigns a buy position when adjusted close is below the lower band and a sell signal when it is above the upper band, using numpy’s np.where(). Daily strategy returns are calculated from price changes and lagged positions, then compounded with cumprod() to plot an equity curve. The example strategy compounded at 2.65% per year while invested 10.6% of the time, and is presented for informational and Python demonstration purposes.

Melania Trump is hosting executives from Amazon, Snap, Facebook, Google, Twitter and other internet groups to discuss cyberbullying and internet safety, marking her first public event on the issue since naming it a priority as first lady. Major tech companies have anti-harassment policies but largely depend on users to report abuse, and their efforts have been criticized as insufficient. Twitter has introduced policies against hateful content and nonconsensual sharing of nude images, while Yik Yak shut down partly after bullying complaints. Online harassment includes posting embarrassing photos, cruel remarks and sharing private screenshots, and a Pew poll found 41 percent of US adults believed they had been harassed online. Companies face challenges policing huge volumes of content while balancing abuse prevention with free expression. There is no federal bullying law, and state laws vary. Sameer Hinduja said the federal government could help schools with tools and funding. Mrs. Trump has also focused on child well-being, opioid impacts on children, online time limits and promoting kindness.

Opera launched Neon, an AI-powered browser designed for proactive, task-oriented browsing, including form filling, site comparisons and code writing. It can navigate pages autonomously while operating locally on users’ devices, with tools for AI-managed workspaces and reusable prompts. Opera plans Neon as a subscription product for power users, entering the agentic browsing market alongside competitors, while facing reliability, safety, transparency and regulatory challenges.

Karuna Nundy, a Supreme Court advocate, works on anti-rape and sexual harassment laws, constitutional law, Bhopal gas tragedy victims and rape survivor representation. Educated at St. Stephen’s, Cambridge and Columbia, she specialises in corporate, property, media and tech law. She helped draft Womanifesto, a women’s rights bill addressing laws on crimes against women.

Warby Parker is presented as an attractive investment due to retail expansion, customer growth, rising average selling prices, new product lines, and high gross margins despite tariffs. The company raised FY25 guidance to 14%-15% revenue growth and nearly two points of margin expansion, with double-digit growth expected in FY26. The author reiterates a “Buy” rating despite premium valuation and discloses a long position in WRBY.

A video of Tennessee middle school student Keaton Jones tearfully describing being bullied at school went viral after his mother posted it on Facebook. Keaton described being insulted, called names, and having milk poured on him, while urging others who are bullied to stay strong. His sister Lakyn Jones said he attends Horace Maynard Middle School near Knoxville and later thanked supporters online.

The video drew widespread support from athletes, celebrities, and public figures, including University of Tennessee quarterback Jarrett Guarantano, LeBron James, Gal Gadot, Chris Evans, Mark Ruffalo, Millie Bobby Brown, Bernice King, and Tennessee senators Lamar Alexander and Bob Corker. Several people invited Keaton to events or encouraged anti-bullying awareness.

Attention also turned to Keaton’s family after reports that his mother, Kimberly Jones, had posted images of Confederate flags on Facebook. Lakyn defended her family, and ESPN’s Jemele Hill said her invitation for Keaton to visit ESPN still stood while calling the situation a “teachable moment.” A GoFundMe campaign in Keaton’s name raised more than $58,000 before donations were paused, with organizer Joseph Lam saying the focus should remain on Keaton rather than his mother.

The passage describes a footwear sole structure with an outsole incorporating traction elements. The outsole includes an annular cleat set arranged around a central axis on the plantar surface and radial cleat sets aligned along axes intersecting that central axis, with some radial sets including peripheral cleats on the outsole’s peripheral surface. The annular cleat set may be located on the medial forefoot ball portion and include major and minor cleats in concentric rings. Radial cleat sets may include major cleats, progressively smaller minor cleats, and obliquely oriented peripheral cleats, while a heel cleat set may include major and minor cleats on a heel plate. The sole structure may also include a composite midsole, forefoot and heel outsole plates with shells, skeletons, and inserts, plus a shank and cradle for support. The configuration is described as providing traction in multiple directions, rotational movement about the central axis, and improved lateral traction.

The Motz Corporation, founded in 1977, serves natural and synthetic turf markets and is parent company to The Motz Group and USGreentech. The company has transitioned to an employee stock ownership plan, giving employees beneficial ownership while aiming to support employee engagement, customer satisfaction and talent attraction. Founder and CEO Joe Motz said the move recognizes employees’ role in building the company. Management will remain unchanged, with Joe Motz continuing as CEO and executive leaders Zach Burns, Valerie Webster and Kevin McDonnell remaining in their roles. The Motz Group specializes in sports field design, construction, replacement, maintenance and management. USGreentech focuses on synthetic turf infill products for sports fields, putting greens and lawns.

Coach Julien said his team has played well in the playoffs but wants a more complete effort in the finals. He emphasized improved confidence and puck movement on the power play, a calm approach under pressure, and confidence on the road. He discussed scoring chances, balancing respect and authority as a coach, adapting to modern players, trusting multiple forward lines in matchups, and praised Dennis Seidenberg’s size, strength, battle, and ability to elevate his game.

This edition publishes documents mainly from Department of State files and the American Commission to Negotiate Peace, with related materials from personal papers and institutional collections. It covers chiefly the period of active American participation in the Paris Peace Conference through December 9, 1919, following established Foreign Relations selection principles while omitting some secondary material. The project was compiled and edited within the Division of Research and Publication, with assistance from government officers and archival institutions. The passage also lists principal treaties and conference topics, including termination of hostilities, American preparations, country representation, Allied policies, League of Nations proposals, and other agenda items.

The State Bar of Michigan e-Journal for May 18, 2001, includes case summaries in administrative law, criminal law, family law, insurance, litigation, municipal law, negligence and intentional tort, real property, tax, and worker’s compensation. It reports Michigan Supreme Court orders and Michigan Court of Appeals opinions, including rulings on PSC carrier charges, drug profile testimony, sentencing, custody mediation, termination of parental rights, uninsured motorist coverage, dismissal and pleading issues, zoning-related consent judgments, employer intentional tort claims, and rain tax refunds. The issue also contains fields of practice listings, classified advertisements, positions available, archived e-Journal links, and contact information.

Cleary’s boxer Lewis Williams will compete for the Elite Three Nations 91kg title in Rotherham, aiming to emulate Morgan Ansell’s youth title win. Josh Finch will face Cameron Hatton on Cleary’s Gym’s June 8 home show.

Weybridge Orthodontics offers Invisalign for mild-to-moderate dental misalignment using custom transparent aligners created from 3D images. Patients wear each aligner pair for 7–10 days, with treatment typically taking 12–18 months. The removable appliances avoid wire-and-bracket braces, fit around eating and brushing, and may improve dental function, aesthetics, hygiene, and reduce jaw strain. The practice provides consultations and can show a simulation of expected results before treatment begins.

Researchers have generated muon beams using small laser-driven particle accelerators, reducing the need for massive facilities. Muons can penetrate dense materials and may enable faster scanning of shipping containers for contraband such as plutonium or uranium. Experiments at Berkeley Lab, ELI-NP in Romania, and Shanghai produced muons by using lasers to accelerate electrons into dense targets. Researchers say advances in laser accelerators could eventually make portable muon sources possible, though current systems are not yet compact enough.

South32 abandoned its US$200 million plan to buy Peabody Energy’s Metropolitan coal mine in Australia due to competition concerns over coal supply to local steelmakers. CEO Graham Kerr said required concessions would undermine the deal’s merits. Peabody, recently out of bankruptcy, said it was surprised by the impasse and will keep operating the mine and its Port Kembla coal terminal stake.

President Donald Trump met with Jared Isaacman to discuss another nomination to lead NASA after withdrawing his earlier nomination over Isaacman’s political contributions and close ties to Elon Musk. Isaacman, who declined to comment, has led two private SpaceX flights and founded Shift4.

This study examined whether vitamin B12 metabolism or levels have a genetic role in Parkinson’s disease (PD). Researchers analyzed common and rare variants in B12-related genes, pathway-specific polygenic risk scores, Mendelian randomization, and genetic correlations using European-ancestry datasets. No robust association was found between common or rare B12 metabolism variants and PD risk. Mendelian randomization showed no causal association between B12 levels and PD risk, age at onset, motor or cognitive progression, and genetic correlation analyses were also negative. The authors conclude that B12 levels or metabolism may not play a prominent genetic role in PD development or progression, while non-genetic factors such as gastrointestinal dysfunction and microbiota changes may contribute to lower B12 levels observed in PD patients.

The paper develops simple pseudospin models for two phenyltetrazole-family organic crystals with long-range ordering: APHTZ and MPHTZ. These lead-free systems exhibit ordering driven by proton tautomerism, where proton relocation along hydrogen bonds switches associated dipoles through changes in tetrazole π-bonds.

APHTZ is modeled as a canted ferroelectric with two sublattices: ferroelectric order along the a axis and antiferroelectric order along the b axis in its FE-I ground configuration. The model predicts a second-order transition to the paraelectric phase, Curie-Weiss behavior of dielectric permittivity, and polarization switching under transverse field Eb from FE-I to FE-II, corresponding to a 90° rotation of net polarization. It predicts a single ferroelectric hysteresis loop for field along a and a double antiferroelectric-type loop for field along b. Because of limited experimental data, APHTZ parameter choices are described as preliminary.

MPHTZ is modeled as a uniaxial antiferroelectric with chains along the a axis and checkerboard antiferroelectric ordering between chains. Its four-sublattice model reduces to a two-sublattice antiferroelectric Ising model. The model reproduces available experimental polarization-field data at 300 K and predicts classical field-induced antiferroelectric-to-ferroelectric switching with double hysteresis loops, finite dielectric permittivity at the transition, and a tricritical point in the temperature-field phase diagram.

For both crystals, the switching field is linked to the spontaneous order parameter and intersublattice coupling. The authors conclude that additional measurements of spontaneous polarization, dielectric permittivity, switching behavior, and phase-transition temperatures are needed to validate and refine the models.

Niantic announced that Pokémon GO will add “over 80” Johto Pokémon from Pokémon Gold and Silver later this week, all discoverable in the wild once the update goes live. The update will also add evolution items from PokéStops, Nanab and Pinap berries, new avatar clothing, and unspecified new encounter gameplay. A trailer shows interface changes including a berry shortcut and adjusted camera/backpack elements. The update does not mention improved tracking, trading, or player-versus-player battles. Some Generation II Pokémon remain unaccounted for, likely including existing baby Pokémon, evolutions requiring items, and Legendary Pokémon. Screenshots suggest Pokémon genders, purchasable berries, and evolution previews may be included.

Charleston City Council will again consider carriage horse heat regulations, including revised conditions for resuming tours. Separately, one carriage company equipped drivers with body cameras to address heckling and possible abuse.

Lorna Gibson continues a lecture on energy absorption in foams. Energy absorption diagrams are constructed from compressive stress-strain curves by plotting normalized absorbed energy against normalized peak stress, usually on log-log scales. Tests are performed at constant strain rate and temperature for foams of different relative densities. The most efficient operating point is the “shoulder” of each curve, just before densification, where energy absorption is maximized without a large increase in peak stress. Connecting shoulder points gives optimum design lines; repeating this for different strain rates or temperatures incorporates rate or thermal sensitivity.

For elastomeric foams, normalizing by the solid modulus allows different flexible elastomeric foams to be represented on one diagram because both modulus and plateau stress depend on the solid modulus. For foams made from materials with a yield point, diagrams are valid for foams with the same ratio of solid yield strength to solid modulus.

Gibson explains how diagrams can be generated from experiments or from foam models. For open-cell elastomeric foams, equations describe the linear elastic region, the stress plateau, densification strain, and the optimum shoulder line. Similar approaches apply to closed-cell foams and plastic foams, though plastic foam diagrams are less general because they depend on the yield-strength-to-modulus ratio. The model curves show how deformation and failure mechanisms contribute to energy absorption and indicate that foams can absorb a given energy at much lower peak stress than fully dense solids.

She then gives design examples for impact protection. In one packaging example, known mass, contact area, drop height, maximum deceleration, and polyurethane modulus are used to calculate allowable peak stress, absorbed energy, foam thickness, strain rate, and optimum relative density through an iterative process. In another example, foam thickness is specified but material is not; the diagram is used to estimate the required solid modulus and foam density. A bicycle helmet example uses a material selection chart to identify 5% dense expanded polystyrene as a good foam choice for absorbing impact energy under specified head mass, deceleration, contact area, and liner thickness assumptions.

The lecture ends with a discussion of woodpeckers as an energy absorption example. Gibson describes why woodpeckers peck and notes that acorn woodpeckers store acorns in granaries. High-speed video studies from the late 1970s measured bill speeds around 15 miles per hour and decelerations up to 1,500g. A scaling argument suggests woodpeckers tolerate high decelerations because of their smaller brain size, brain orientation, and shorter impact duration. She also notes woodpecker adaptations such as stiff tail feathers and zygodactyl feet. The next lecture will begin sandwich panels, including engineered and natural examples.

The passage outlines German peace policy as immediate recuperation through supplies and organization of the Near East, and notes the President’s determination to oppose it. It then reports the Inquiry’s organization as of December 15, 1917: an Executive Committee, division chiefs, assistants, collaborators, and a filing and digesting staff led by Dr. Mezes, with material edited, catalogued, indexed, and made readily accessible. The Inquiry draws personnel from numerous universities, libraries, and organizations, with operations centered at the American Geographical Society. Its research plan aims to assemble reliable material by February 15 on urgent issues, including the Baltic-to-Persian Gulf region, Central Africa, Central Powers’ economic needs, and freedom of the seas. Current work includes compiling official government declarations on war settlement and international policy, and examining Western press and periodicals for policy statements by opposition figures, minority parties, and social groups.

Nutritional High International secured a 12-month extension to April 18, 2018, of its US$800,000 secured note on its Pueblo, Colorado property with Veterans Capital Fund. The company will continue paying 13% annual interest, pay renewal and extension fees of 1% each, extend 3,333,334 warrants to October 18, 2018, and issue 1,000,000 new warrants at CAD$0.15, subject to regulatory approval.

The company also entered a term sheet for a loan secured by its La Pine, Oregon property. The Oregon loan principal will be the lesser of 85% of the appraised value or US$400,000, carry 13% annual interest for 18 months, and include up to 1,125,515 warrants at CAD$0.165, subject to approval. The loan remains subject to lender due diligence expected in May 2017.

Eric Bass forwarded an Oct. 5, 2000 “Inside UT Football” newsletter by Chip Brown. The newsletter focuses on the Texas-Oklahoma rivalry, quotes Oklahoma coach Bob Stoops, and answers reader questions about UT football. Topics include Royal-Memorial Stadium expansion, player status and development, punt coverage, offensive line progress, Shaun Rogers’ ankle injury, UT’s secondary against OU’s passing game, the Major Applewhite-Chris Simms quarterback rotation, special teams problems, recruiting and future expectations, scheduling, Mack Brown’s handling of criticism, and the Colorado game time. Brown predicts Texas will beat Oklahoma 24-20 and says Applewhite is expected to start and play most or all of the game.

NVIDIA Tensor Cores, introduced in Volta, accelerate matrix multiplication for neural network training and inferencing. The Ampere-based A100 GPU has more SMs than Tesla V100 and third-generation Tensor Cores delivering 16x higher peak mixed-precision performance than FP32 FMA. Ampere adds optimizations to improve Tensor Core utilization, programmability, memory bandwidth, latency, and strong scaling for fixed deep learning workloads.

The speaker says every game is different and expects power-play chances, noting Buff remains useful physically and around the net though he is not playing tonight. Laddy skated lightly. The team wants to make Pronger defend, be physical on him, and spend more time in the opponent’s end. They viewed the first goal as important, praised Benny’s quick response goal and deceptive shot, and credited Antti’s calm attitude, preparation, and goaltending. The speaker says the team spent too much time in its own zone but improved its team game, while the energy line contributed with forechecking, hitting, and useful minutes. Looking ahead to the road game, the team expects a loud building and a tough challenge, aiming to play its best and rely on the effective road approach used in earlier playoff series.

The speaker said the team was frustrated after the loss but returned to practice to regroup and work on key areas. They identified problems with not getting the puck deep, poor neutral-zone play, lack of execution, and insufficient speed. The opponent was credited as a strong team that capitalized on mistakes, including a bad line change and screened shot. The speaker said Ron was not the main reason for the loss, noting many players were not sharp. They emphasized keeping the game simple, getting to the forecheck, avoiding overthinking matchups, and winning the next game to even the series.

The federal judiciary will use funding not tied to new congressional appropriations, including court fee balances, to keep paid operations running during the government shutdown. Courts expect to pay staff through Oct. 17, while federal judges will continue receiving constitutionally protected salaries. Most proceedings and deadlines will continue, though some cases involving unavailable executive-branch attorneys may be delayed. The Supreme Court also plans to use non-annual funds during short-term funding lapses. Some district courts have delayed civil cases involving the federal government, while some judges are refusing to pause such cases. If funds run out, courts will operate under the Antideficiency Act, with some staff working without pay to support constitutional functions and others potentially furloughed.

The U.S. Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to withhold $4 billion in foreign aid while Congress considers a rescission request under the Impoundment Control Act. The court said the government had made a sufficient early showing that plaintiffs may lack standing and mandamus relief, and that foreign affairs harms may outweigh plaintiffs’ harms, but said the ruling was not final. The ABA, a plaintiff, said tens of millions in funding for foreign rule-of-law and human-rights programs were frozen. Justice Elena Kagan dissented, joined by Justices Sonia Sotomayor and Ketanji Brown Jackson, arguing the emergency application involved high-stakes, uncharted issues. The dispute stems from a district court order requiring $10.5 billion in foreign aid spending, with $4 billion still at issue.

More than 200 schools in North Wales closed after snow and ice caused hazardous conditions, with temperatures falling to -8C and a yellow ice warning in place until 11am. Closures included 78 schools in Flintshire, 48 in Wrexham, 47 in Denbighshire, 11 in Conwy, and several in Gwynedd. Some schools had partial openings, while Anglesey reported no closures.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K reporting actions from its June 3, 2021 Annual Meeting. Stockholders approved an amendment to increase authorized common shares from 2 billion to 4 billion, filed in Delaware on June 4, 2021. They also elected 13 directors for one-year terms, approved executive compensation on an advisory basis, and ratified PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as independent auditor for the fiscal year ending January 30, 2022.

Boston University Summer Term offers open-enrollment undergraduate, graduate, and pre-college programs with over 700 courses in more than 75 subjects, available days, evenings, or online in six-week sessions. Summer 1 runs May 23–June 30; Summer 2 runs July 3–August 11.

Andrew Lo discusses Lehman Brothers’ 2007 financial position, noting $19 billion in net revenues, $4 billion in net income, $145 billion in long-term capital, $282 billion in assets under management, 28,500 employees, and a 16-to-1 net leverage ratio. He explains leverage using home mortgages: with 20% down on a $500,000 house, a 10% price decline cuts the homeowner’s equity in half; with 5% down, the same decline wipes out equity and creates further loss. He argues that high leverage is dangerous when asset volatility rises, as happened in housing markets.

Lo connects subprime mortgage defaults to adjustable-rate mortgages, low teaser rates, rising payments, falling home values, and non-recourse loans that allow borrowers to walk away from homes while damaging their credit. He says the Fed was expected to cut rates to reduce pressure and defaults, though low rates may also contribute to inflation and bubbles.

He explains that Lehman filed for Chapter 11 after the Fed declined to provide support and potential buyers such as Barclays and Bank of America withdrew without a government backstop. Bankruptcy means courts supervise asset disposition to repay creditors, with shareholders last in line. He compares Lehman’s collapse to Bear Stearns, emphasizing loss of confidence, exposure to mortgage-related securities, and the destruction of business value.

Lo then discusses inflation as a change in purchasing power distinct from the time value of money. Nominal returns measure dollar growth, while real returns adjust for price changes. He states that real return is approximately nominal return minus inflation and that nominal cash flows should be discounted with nominal rates, while real cash flows should be discounted with real rates.

The lecture then introduces fixed income securities, including Treasury, agency, corporate, municipal, mortgage-backed, asset-backed, and other debt instruments. Lo describes the large size and growth of bond markets, especially mortgage-related and asset-backed securities, and distinguishes issuers, investors, and intermediaries. He explains that bonds generally trade less frequently than equities and may be less liquid.

Finally, Lo outlines bond valuation. Fixed income securities have known cash flows, so valuation depends on timing, discount rates, and present value. A coupon bond pays periodic coupons plus principal at maturity, while a pure discount bond pays only at maturity and sells below face value. He notes that STRIPS separate coupon and principal payments into individual securities and that bond prices can imply interest rates and market expectations, including expectations about Fed rate cuts.

A Jan. 25, 2002 Enron news roundup reported expanding scrutiny of the company’s collapse, including claims that Enron disclosed confidential partnership information to select LJM2 investors, allegations that Enron Energy Services inflated profits, and congressional investigations into Arthur Andersen’s destruction of Enron-related documents. Reports covered Kenneth Lay’s resignation, possible restructuring leadership by Stephen Cooper, debates over appointing a bankruptcy trustee, and mixed reactions from former employees. Other articles examined 401(k) reform proposals, Enron’s history and political ties, potential liquidation of Enron Australia, effects on charities, aid efforts for laid-off workers, and book deals related to the scandal.

President Trump welcomed French President Emmanuel Macron to the White House for the first state visit of his presidency, praising the U.S.-France alliance and thanking Macron for support in the Syria missile strike. The leaders planned talks on Syria, security, trade and the Iran nuclear deal, which Trump criticized while Macron called imperfect but worth preserving without a “Plan B.” The visit included a South Lawn ceremony, a tree planting, a helicopter tour, dinner at Mount Vernon, an Oval Office meeting, a joint news conference and a state dinner for about 150 guests. Melania Trump oversaw dinner details, including rack of lamb, nectarine tart and floral decorations. Expected attendees included Christine Lagarde, Paul Ryan, Steven Mnuchin, Jim Mattis, Bill Cassidy and Mike Pompeo; no congressional Democrats or journalists were invited, though Louisiana Gov. John Bel Edwards was expected to attend.

Tesla Motors filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2015. The company reported $939.9 million in revenue, up from $620.5 million a year earlier, driven primarily by increased Model S deliveries. Net loss was $154.2 million, compared with $49.8 million in the prior-year quarter, and loss per share was $1.22. Gross margin rose to 27.7% from 25.0%.

As of March 31, 2015, Tesla had $6.12 billion in total assets, $5.24 billion in total liabilities, $826.0 million in stockholders’ equity, and $1.51 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Operating cash flow was negative $131.8 million, investing cash outflow was $432.3 million, and financing cash inflow was $186.2 million.

Tesla stated it had delivered over 66,000 Model S vehicles through March 31, 2015, planned to begin Model X deliveries late in the third quarter of 2015, and aimed to introduce Model 3 in 2017. The company expected to deliver about 55,000 Model S and Model X vehicles in 2015 and planned about $1.5 billion in capital expenditures, including investments in production capacity, Model X, Model 3, the Gigafactory, stores, service centers, and Superchargers.

The filing discusses accounting policies, customer financing and leasing programs, convertible debt, warranty reserves, stock-based compensation, market risks, controls and procedures, legal proceedings, and risk factors, including possible delays in Model X and future vehicle development, production ramp, supply chain, and regulatory approvals.

Particle released an LTE-enabled module for connected device developers, targeting products dependent on retiring 2G and 3G networks. The module includes cloud and SIM support and is aimed at industrial uses such as dispersed sensors in factories or agriculture. It is part of Particle’s broader suite including a device cloud, operating system and developer toolkit. The lineup includes two certified LTE CAT-M1 models powered by Qualcomm and u-blox components. An LTE hardware evaluation kit costs $89, while individual modules cost $69. Particle says it has 8,500 customers and more than 140,000 developers.

OpenChart-SE is a citizen science project addressing limited access to Swedish EHR text for clinical NLP research by collecting artificial Swedish emergency care EHRs. Swedish physicians and medical students wrote plausible records for imagined emergency department patients using a mock Swedish EHR form. In the pilot phase, 50 artificial EHRs were collected, reviewed by an emergency care physician, deemed realistic, and released publicly as OpenChart-SE corpus version 1 on Zenodo. The records cover varied adult emergency scenarios, include 12% priority-one patients, describe patients aged 18–94, and range from 954 to 2738 characters. The corpus is not suitable for clinical insight because it contains no real EHRs, but is intended as training and validation data for Swedish clinical NLP tools. The project is open for further submissions, with quality-controlled updates planned periodically.

The passage describes ADS9803 initialization, configuration, SPI access, daisy-chain operation, register functions, and application guidance. After power-up or reset, the ADS9803 requires a register-write initialization sequence with a free-running sampling clock connected. Users can then configure analog input range, bandwidth, common-mode range, data interface lanes, internal reference, averaging, digital test patterns, gain correction, and speed-boost mode. Speed-boost mode converts one selected analog input channel pair at up to 8MSPS while the other six channels remain idle.

Register writes use 24-bit SPI frames, with register bank selection through address 0x03. Register reads require enabling SPI read mode and using SPI_MODE, then reading selected register addresses. Multiple devices can be connected in an SPI daisy-chain with shared CS and SCLK; DAISY_CHAIN_LEN defines the number of devices after the first ADC, and register operations require N × 24 SCLKs.

The register descriptions include controls for SPI mode, daisy-chain length, register bank selection, initialization settings, data format, averaging, XOR operation, test patterns, user-defined appended bits, speed-boost configuration, analog bandwidth, channel power-down, reference selection, output lane mode, common-mode range, and gain correction.

The ADS9803 is presented as an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS DAQ device for ATE applications. It supports calibrated TUE performance, external switches or multiplexers, low-noise and wide-bandwidth modes, and 99.95% full-scale settling in 7.5µs in wide-bandwidth mode. Power supplies include AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD, with no required power-up sequence. Layout guidance recommends close bypass and reference capacitors, avoiding vias between pins and capacitors, separating analog paths from digital lines, and keeping analog and reference signals away from noise sources.

Panthers kicker Graham Gano missed three of four field goals in a loss to the Buccaneers and criticized Tampa Bay’s video board for showing live footage behind the goal posts during his kicks while using a solid red background for Roberto Aguayo’s attempts. A league official said using a video board to distract a kicker violates rules. Gano also cited PA feedback and a horn but said he was still responsible. Coach Ron Rivera called it “bush-league” that the stadium showed slow-motion replays of Thomas Davis knocking Russell Shepard down, saying it could incite fans.

The speaker says playing forward allows more creativity, but they plan to keep things simple, work hard, and create room for Mike and Jere. They expect a tough, energetic opponent in a key game and emphasize matching that energy. They credit the team’s closeness, depth, willingness to block shots, and focus on taking the series one period at a time.

The passage argues that teacher education must be reformed to prepare educators for 21st-century classrooms shaped by technology, diversity, social change, and global challenges. Key priorities include integrating technology through frameworks such as TPACK, fostering critical thinking and problem-solving through constructivist and inquiry-based methods, preparing teachers for diverse learners through inclusive and culturally responsive practices, promoting collaboration and lifelong professional development, and equipping teachers to address global issues such as climate change, inequality, and social justice. The paper uses TPACK and constructivism as its main conceptual frameworks and cites literature emphasizing content knowledge, pedagogy, equity, differentiated instruction, cultural competence, collaboration, and professional learning. Light-field imaging captures spatial and angular information from a 3D scene in a single snapshot, avoiding the sequential scanning used in confocal, multiphoton, and light-sheet microscopy. This enables computational refocusing, synthetic aperture imaging, multi-view rendering, and volumetric reconstruction, while reducing trade-offs involving speed, signal-to-noise ratio, and photodamage. Its foundations include the plenoptic function, 4D light-field parameterizations, geometric optics models, and wave-optics models needed for high-NA and high-resolution microscopy.

In biomedicine, light-field microscopy enables high-speed volumetric fluorescence imaging for dynamic biological processes, including neuronal activity, whole-brain imaging in model organisms, single-cell imaging, and subcellular dynamics. Fourier or extended light-field microscopy improves sampling and has been applied in neuroscience, cell biology, organoids, flow cytometry, fluorescence lifetime imaging, and other platforms. Light-field mesoscopy extends the approach to millimeter-to-centimeter imaging with cellular resolution, including mouse cortex calcium imaging and miniature systems for wide-field 3D fluorescence imaging. Light-field endoscopy aims to provide real-time 3D imaging, digital refocusing, and depth measurement using microlens arrays, tunable lenses, GRIN lens arrays, fiber bundles, and related designs, though flexible endoscopic integration remains challenging.

Key limitations include large data volumes, sensor speed constraints, resolution trade-offs, limited depth accuracy, scattering, aberrations, and the redistribution of space-bandwidth product from lateral resolution into 3D sampling. Proposed solutions include compressive sensing, event-based cameras, squeezed light-field microscopy, scanning and virtual-scanning methods, adaptive optics, meta-optics, and AI-based reconstruction. Deep learning methods can improve speed, resolution, and artifact reduction, but depend on training data and raise concerns about generalization, interpretability, and reliability.

The City of Bisbee sought mandamus against Cochise County, its treasurer, and supervisors to recover penalties, fees, costs, and interest collected on delinquent city taxes from 1918 to 1931 but retained in the county general fund. The trial court sustained demurrers and dismissed the action.

The Arizona Supreme Court held that mandamus was a proper remedy against the county treasurer because funds collected for the city were held in trust and could be compelled to be paid over, even if diverted to another fund. However, mandamus did not lie against Cochise County or its board of supervisors because the funds, if belonging to Bisbee, were never legally county funds and no supervisor approval or county claim was required.

The court found that under the 1917 law, the county treasurer was required to remit to municipalities delinquent taxes and related interest, costs, and fees collected before June 13, 1931. These amounts belonged to Bisbee, not the county. The statute of limitations did not bar the action because trust funds held by a public officer are not subject to limitation until repudiation or refusal, and Bisbee sued within one year of the treasurer’s refusal.

For amounts collected after June 12, 1931, a new statute required interest, penalties, charges, and fees connected with tax collection to be credited to the county general fund, so Bisbee had no claim to them.

The judgment was reversed as to Treasurer Kitchel and remanded with instructions to overrule the demurrer against him; dismissal as to the county and supervisors was proper.

The study presents a field-deployable metagenomic next-generation sequencing protocol using Oxford Nanopore Technology to improve untargeted detection of viral nucleic acids from clinical swab samples. It evaluated pretreatments for SARS-CoV-2-positive oropharyngeal swabs, comparing no treatment, DNase I treatment, filtration, and DNase I followed by filtration.

Pretreatment increased SARS-CoV-2 detection compared with no treatment. DNase I followed by filtration produced the strongest effect, increasing SARS-CoV-2 BLAST hits to 99.9%, achieving 99.3% reference genome coverage after 20 hours, and producing a 525-fold increase in viral reads per 100,000 reads. This combination also reached over 50% genome coverage after 10 minutes. DNase I alone and filtration alone improved detection but were less effective.

Testing individual samples showed that all samples with CT values at or below 30 achieved 85.8–100% SARS-CoV-2 genome coverage after 20 hours, while samples with CT values at or above 33 had lower coverage. All 14 positive samples were identified as clade 21J (Delta), and Pangolin assigned Delta sub-lineages for samples with CT values below 33.

The authors conclude that a 15-minute DNase I and filtration pretreatment substantially improves SARS-CoV-2 detection by Nanopore-based mNGS and may support simpler laboratory or field-based detection of viral pathogens in animal and human swab samples.
