Some pins may lack analog functions, wake-up logic, drive strength control, or pull resistors; 5V-tolerant open-drain I/O lacks output-high PMOS, pullup resistor, and clamping diode.

The device includes a two-wire ARM-compatible SWD interface and a boot strap loader for UART or I2C programming and configuration, protected by a 256-bit user-defined password and disable option. The BSL can be invoked by a hardware invoke pin during boot, by blank reset vector and stack pointer, or by application software command.

A memory-mapped FACTORY region stores read-only device capability, identification, hardware revision, and trim data. Typical application guidance recommends VDD/VSS decoupling capacitors, an NRST pullup with pulldown capacitor, an optional SYSOSC FCL resistor, a required VCORE tank capacitor, and pullup resistors for 5V-tolerant open-drain I/O.

Device support includes TI development tools, LaunchPad ecosystem resources, SDKs, SysConfig, IDEs, compilers, documentation updates, E2E forums, trademark notices, and ESD handling cautions. The revision history lists many April 2025 updates to specifications, features, operating modes, electrical characteristics, peripherals, security, and documentation. Mechanical, packaging, orderable, and disclaimer information is also provided.

Facebook released a public version of its Community Guidelines, detailing what content it may remove when reported. The document is based on principles of “safety,” “voice,” and “equity,” and serves as a moderation manual for judging posts, comments, images, and videos. Expert moderator Rochelle LaPlante said the guidelines are not unusual but praised their transparency and detail. The passage notes that some rules are broad while others are highly specific, likely reflecting past controversies and difficult cases. Facebook develops such policies in regular internal meetings described by Monika Bickert as “mini legislative sessions.”

Point72 Europe London LLP bought 10,000 shares of Hershey Company worth about $1.07 million in the second quarter. Other hedge funds also adjusted positions, and institutional investors own 51.39% of the stock. Analysts’ ratings include three sell, eight hold and five buy, with a consensus “Hold” rating and $111.55 target price. Recent insider sales included transactions by Michele Buck and D. Michael Wege; insiders sold 4,504,500 shares worth $477.5 million over 90 days. Hershey traded at $108.83 on Friday, with a $23.12 billion market cap. The company reported quarterly EPS of $1.09 on revenue of $1.66 billion, beating estimates, and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.656 per share payable December 15.

Arizona police arrested 92-year-old Anna Mae Blessing on suspicion of murdering her 72-year-old son after allegedly shooting him over plans to place her in assisted living. Authorities said she hid two handguns, confronted him, and later tried to aim at his girlfriend, who disarmed her. Blessing was held on US$500,000 bail.

YbCu1.14Se2 was studied as an exchange-disordered triangular magnet related to triangular-lattice QSL candidates. Single-crystal x-ray diffraction shows a P-3m1 structure with Yb ions forming a well-ordered triangular lattice, while Cu sites are partially occupied at about 56.6%, with no ordered Cu-vacancy pattern. Magnetic susceptibility indicates a Yb3+ local moment, a Kramer’s doublet ground state, and antiferromagnetic exchange at low temperatures. Specific heat shows no magnetic ordering transition between 100 mK and 10 K, has sublinear low-temperature behavior, and recovers about 85% of R ln(2) entropy by 10 K after subtracting a low-temperature Schottky anomaly. Ultra-low-temperature ac susceptibility shows a frequency-dependent peak near 0.1 K, characteristic of spin-glass freezing, while field-dependent susceptibility lacks the 1/3 magnetization plateau seen in several related triangular-lattice compounds. The results indicate a spin-disordered ground state similar to YbMgGaO4 and consistent with behavior expected in disordered frustrated triangular magnets.

Mark Messier and Bridgestone announced the Bridgestone Youth Leadership Award in its fourth year, honoring Robert “Knobby” Knudsen for his community work with children, including the Kids Skate for Kids program in Windsor. His son Robert Knudsen Jr. accepted the award and shared a quote reflecting his father’s belief in improving the world through helping children.

Messier also announced Dustin Brown, Shane Doan, and Ryan Callahan as finalists for the Mark Messier Leadership Award, recognizing their on-ice leadership and community work. In later comments, Messier praised Brown’s maturity and charity efforts, discussed the difficulty of Stanley Cup playoff runs, reflected on past Rangers-Devils playoff storylines, highlighted improved NHL skill and young talent, and said the Rangers’ season represented major progress despite the need for more depth.

The speaker thanks citizens for entrusting him with the nation’s highest executive office, acknowledges the difficulty of the task, and seeks guidance from other constitutional authorities. He urges unity after political conflict, emphasizing majority rule tempered by protection of minority rights and rejection of political intolerance. He affirms commitment to union, republican and federal principles, representative government, and confidence in the strength of self-government.

He defines good government as wise and frugal, preventing injury while leaving people free in their pursuits. He lists essential principles: equal justice, peace and commerce with all nations without entangling alliances, support for state governments, preservation of the constitutional authority of the general government, protection of elections, majority rule, a disciplined militia, civilian supremacy, economy, payment of debts, encouragement of agriculture and commerce, public information, and freedoms of religion, press, person, habeas corpus, and jury trial. He asks indulgence for unintentional errors, pledges to promote happiness and freedom, and invokes divine guidance for peace and prosperity.

Christian Bushman says CPR saved her life after an object fell from a closet, hit her chest, and caused cardiac arrest in 2014. Her sister-in-law Cathy Carson, a CPR instructor, found her unresponsive, called for 911, and performed CPR until help arrived. Bushman later learned and taught CPR, urging others to do the same. The passage notes many out-of-hospital cardiac arrests happen at home and women receive bystander CPR less often than men.

Torsten Sløk said the U.S. economy is strengthening despite repeated forecasts of a slowdown, arguing economists should reassess their predictions. He cited resilient growth and warned that further Fed rate cuts could raise inflation risks. Mike Wilson’s “rolling recession” thesis suggests the economy is shifting into recovery, though ADP data shows labor market weakness.

National Literacy Month highlights both the value of literacy programs and persistent inequities in reading access. The passage argues that culturally responsive books, small classes, enrichment, and civic action projects can help Black youth build literacy and leadership. It cites Partnership for Growth LA’s Read Lead Freedom Schools and Anastacia Nwosu’s path from student to “Kid Mayor,” mentor, college graduate, and California Assemblymember field deputy. A 2023–24 pilot reported higher English Language Arts proficiency, lower chronic absenteeism, and family-reported gains in confidence and motivation. The authors call for sustained support for local literacy programs, family reading tools, and evidence-based literacy instruction.

Congress has assembled at the permanent seat of government after the removal of public offices, records, and property from Philadelphia. The President congratulates Congress and the people, notes temporary accommodation issues, and urges consideration of whether Congress should exercise its constitutional authority over the District of Columbia.

He reports that the temporary army has been discharged, recommends further attention to the federal judiciary system, and announces that a treaty of amity and commerce with Prussia has been ratified and promulgated. Negotiations with Great Britain over the 6th article of the treaty remain unresolved, while negotiations with France are ongoing after the envoys were respectfully received.

The President urges continued efforts for peace but warns against abandoning self-protection. He recommends systematic naval defense, completion of fortifications at principal ports and harbors, and continued encouragement of domestic arms manufacturing. He notes that the Navy has protected commerce and met expectations.

He will provide estimates for the next year and revenue and expenditure accounts, observing that revenue has exceeded any previous equal period. He concludes by urging preservation of national institutions, resistance to dangerous innovations, and pledging cooperation with Congress in promoting public happiness.

Nobel Peace Prize winner Beatrice Fihn, executive director of the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons, warned that panic, carelessness, misconstrued comments or bruised egos could lead to nuclear destruction and mass civilian deaths. Her remarks referenced escalating rhetoric and insults between Donald Trump and Kim Jong Un, including Trump’s threat at the UN to destroy North Korea. Fihn said nuclear risks are greater than at the end of the Cold War due to more nuclear-armed states, terrorism and cyber warfare. ICAN is a coalition of NGOs working toward a nuclear weapons ban treaty.

The passage develops bivariate zero-inflated Poisson models for multivariate count data, motivated by applications such as insurance claims and environmental disasters where excess zeros and dependence between count variables are common. The proposed model represents counts as \(X=WT\), where \(W\) is a common Bernoulli inflation factor and \(T=(T_1,T_2)\) is a dependent Poisson pair. Marginally, each component follows a zero-inflated Poisson distribution with common inflation parameter \(\phi\) and rates \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\).

Dependence is modeled by allowing \(T\) to follow either the comonotonic-shock or counter-monotonic-shock bivariate Poisson model of Genest et al. (2018), producing respectively the BZIP+ and BZIP− classes. The passage derives joint probability mass functions, distribution functions, and probability generating functions for both positive and negative dependence cases. Dependence is governed by both the zero-inflation parameter \(\phi\) and the latent dependence parameter \(\theta\). The covariance and correlation formulas show that \(\theta\) increases dependence in BZIP+ and decreases it in BZIP−, while \(\phi\) affects both marginal behavior and association through shared zeros. The BZIP+ model can attain the upper Fréchet-Hoeffding bound when \(\theta=1\), while the BZIP− model only attains the lower bound when \(\phi=0\).

The passage presents estimation methods including method of moments, maximum likelihood, and an EM algorithm. Method of moments uses marginal moments to estimate \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\phi\), and covariance to estimate \(\theta\), with asymptotic consistency and normality stated. Maximum likelihood estimation is derived from the joint likelihood, with a closed-form expression for \(\hat{\phi}\) conditional on \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\theta\), and both one-step and two-step implementations are discussed. The EM algorithm treats the Bernoulli inflation factor as latent and updates \(\phi\), marginal rates, and \(\theta\) iteratively.

Simulation studies across varying sample sizes, Poisson rates, inflation levels, and dependence strengths assess estimation performance for BZIP+ and BZIP−. Results show that likelihood-based methods generally outperform method of moments in root mean squared error, while all methods improve with larger samples. Estimation becomes more variable as zero inflation increases because fewer nonzero observations inform the Poisson parameters. Numerical difficulties arise mainly in small samples, especially with high zero inflation and low rates.

An application to Australian catastrophic-event data models monthly counts of floods, storms, and bushfires. The BZIP+ model is fitted to flood and storm counts, while BZIP− is fitted to flood and bushfire counts. Both applications indicate significant zero inflation and dependence, supporting the need for models that accommodate both features. The passage also notes that multivariate extensions are possible, especially for positive dependence using multivariate comonotonic-shock Poisson models.

The ADS7828 supports an internal 2.5V or external reference. A +5V supply requires an external +5V reference for full dynamic range, while +2.7V can use the internal reference. Lower reference voltages reduce LSB size and increase apparent offset, gain, and noise errors.

The passage gives a bearish view on US$INR January futures, recommending selling at 68.20–68.30 with targets of 67.95/67.75 and stop loss at 68.40. It cites falling Indian bond yields, rupee weakness, dollar index profit booking, and expectations of supply pressure at higher dollar levels.

Gas prices rose in Montgomery to $2.18, while the national average reached $2.40, its highest level since 2015, according to GasBuddy. Analysts cited declining oil inventories, geopolitical tensions, rising summer demand, and possible OPEC production cuts as factors. Alabama’s average remained among the lowest nationally. GasBuddy suggested prices may peak soon, while AAA predicted increases through September.

Zimbabwe’s Health Ministry estimates there are 44,586 female sex workers aged 15 to 49, excluding transactional sex and male sex workers, with about 6,800 in Bulawayo and 12,800 in Harare. HIV prevalence among sex workers averages 55 percent, compared with the 13 percent national average, with rates above 54 percent in surveyed sites. The HIV and Aids Estimates Report says 25,900 people died of Aids-related causes in 2016, down from 278 deaths per day in 2005 to 71. Officials said the report helps guide HIV funding and programming, while concerns were raised about neglecting key populations.

GoSun introduced the Fusion, a solar-electric oven designed to steam, bake, or roast without fuel in varied conditions, including indoors, at night, through clouds, and in freezing cold. The oven combines GoSun’s vacuum-insulated solar cooking technology with a 12-volt, 150-watt electric heating element that can be powered by a compact lithium-ion battery and is described as five times more efficient than a typical oven. The Fusion cooks at 350°F, has a 3.2-liter capacity to feed five people, weighs 10 pounds, and is built to be portable, durable, weatherproof, and cool to the touch. GoSun launched a Kickstarter campaign offering early-backer deals. The company says it has sold more than 25,000 solar stoves in over 80 countries.

The passage outlines a treaty in which the contracting parties mutually guarantee territorial integrity and political independence under republican governments, agree to settle boundary disputes amicably or through arbitration, and submit unresolved disputes to investigation before hostilities. They also agree to prevent hostile military expeditions and arms exports supporting insurrections against established governments, unless belligerency has been recognized. The treaty’s ratification, deposit, duration, denunciation procedures, and archival arrangements are specified. It then includes a confidential note from S. E. Mezes to the Secretary of State about drafting general principles from an enclosure, and a letter from Secretary of War Baker to Walter Lippmann supporting efforts to make postwar Germany livable for its people and the world, while requiring reliable assurances about the use of resources.

The United States District Court for the District of Nevada granted AAA Nevada Insurance Company’s motion for summary judgment in its declaratory relief action against insured Vinh Chau and others. Chau was insured by AAA when he was involved in an accident that caused Benjamin Buenaventura’s death. The policy provided bodily injury liability limits of $100,000 per person and $300,000 per accident.

Counsel for the Buenaventuras demanded settlement for policy limits within two weeks and proof that no other policy limits were available, but did not identify all heirs or lienholders or provide a release. AAA attempted to contact counsel, including visiting the office and preparing a check, but was unable to obtain the necessary information. Counsel later withdrew the policy-limits settlement offer and alleged AAA failed to respond. The Buenaventuras then filed a wrongful death action seeking $999,997.

The Court held that AAA’s contractual liability under the policy was limited to $100,000. It also found that AAA did not act in bad faith by failing to settle within the two-week deadline because it had a reasonable basis for not complying: AAA could not verify all potential claimants, and counsel did not respond to its inquiries. The Court rejected the Interveners’ arguments that factual disputes, additional discovery, or jurisdictional objections precluded summary judgment.

The passage discusses challenges students may face when writing academic essays and suggests choosing interesting topics, brainstorming, forming a thesis, editing, maintaining a formal tone, and using tools such as mind-mapping software. It also promotes online essay-writing services, claiming they provide expert writers, custom papers, coursework help, and support for students seeking better grades.

Russ Tedrake reviews temporal difference (TD) learning for policy evaluation and notes that Markov chain methods with discretized state/action spaces become impractical for systems like the acrobot because dimensionality grows quickly. The lecture introduces function approximation as a way to apply TD learning to continuous or higher-dimensional systems.

He presents least squares function approximation: given input/output samples, choose parameters to minimize squared prediction error. Neural networks are described as one possible function class, but Tedrake emphasizes linear function approximators, where outputs are linear combinations of potentially nonlinear basis functions. These allow explicit least squares solutions for parameters rather than gradient descent. Examples include radial basis functions, barycentric interpolators, Fourier bases, and polynomial bases.

Tedrake then discusses nonlinear system identification as a least squares problem. For many robot manipulators, rigid body dynamics are nonlinear in state variables but linear in grouped parameters. A pendulum example shows how parameters such as inertia, damping, and gravity-related terms can be estimated from sampled motion data using linear least squares. He notes limitations, including motor saturation, insufficient excitation, hidden state, and choosing appropriate basis functions.

The lecture extends TD(lambda) from tabular Markov chains to linear function approximation. Instead of maintaining eligibility traces for discrete states, the algorithm maintains eligibility traces for parameters. The trace decays over time and is incremented according to the gradient of the value estimate with respect to the parameters; for linear approximators this gradient is the basis-function vector. Tedrake states that for lambda = 1 the update corresponds to gradient descent on Monte Carlo error, while for other lambda values convergence proofs for linear function approximators were developed by Tsitsiklis and Van Roy.

He also discusses the inefficiency of online TD methods, which use each data point once for a small incremental update. Least squares temporal difference learning (LSTD) is introduced as a batch-style method that accumulates information from data and computes parameter estimates directly from stored matrices. Tedrake describes LSTD as more data-efficient, avoiding learning-rate tuning and dependence on initial parameter guesses.

The lecture concludes by emphasizing function approximation as essential for scaling reinforcement learning beyond tabular methods. Linear function approximation has the strongest theoretical support, and future lectures will cover policy function approximation and actor-critic methods combining policy and value-function approximation.

Most Southeast Asian stock markets edged lower as investors awaited the U.S. Federal Reserve policy meeting, with attention on whether projections would signal four rate hikes this year. Thai shares fell the most, led by energy weakness, while Singapore declined for a fourth session and Indonesia slipped. Philippine shares recovered from early losses to close slightly lower, with improved valuations cited after recent declines. Malaysia closed marginally higher on financial and telecom gains. Vietnam rose for a sixth straight session, reaching its highest close since March 2007.

The passage explains the football Trap play, a quick downhill run scheme that kicks out an interior defensive lineman and works well against aggressive pass rushers. Its strengths include speed, deception, and reliance on angle blocks, making it useful for smaller offensive linemen. Its weakness is against defenses that squeeze interior gaps. The passage details blocking assignments against 3-4 and 4-3 fronts and describes shotgun RPO and Wing-T variations.

Hillview Middle School will host an outdoor family movie night featuring “Sing” on April 27 at 7:30 p.m. Attendees should bring money for food and drinks. Proceeds benefit the Leukemia and Lymphoma Society and the Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation.

The passage discusses Gary Kleck and Marc Gertz’s 1990s National Self-Defense Survey, which estimated over 2.2 million defensive gun uses annually in the United States. It states that later CDC surveys from 1996–1998 produced similar estimates of about 2.46–2.5 million annual defensive gun uses but were not published or acknowledged by the CDC. The passage argues that the unpublished findings challenged gun-control narratives during the Clinton administration and says this raises concerns about government transparency. It further contends that the findings support private gun ownership and emphasizes public education on gun control and related political issues.

The speaker reviews U.S. foreign policy, emphasizing national unity, cooperation between Congress and the President, and the need to sustain American credibility abroad. He describes U.S. alliances with Europe, Japan, and other democracies as strong, notes progress with the Soviet Union and China, and cites American efforts in the Middle East, Latin America, Africa, energy, food, environment, and law of the sea.

A major focus is the crisis in Vietnam and Cambodia. The speaker says North Vietnam violated the Paris accords, while U.S. legal restrictions and reduced aid weakened South Vietnam’s position. He asks Congress to provide $722 million in emergency military assistance and $250 million in economic and humanitarian aid to South Vietnam, and to clarify authority for evacuating Americans and endangered Vietnamese. He also urges support for Cambodia, citing its need for food, ammunition, and time to seek a peaceful solution.

The speaker calls for maintaining U.S. commitments while avoiding disunity. He reaffirms security ties with Japan and South Korea, announces planned consultations with Asian leaders, and stresses strong relations with Europe and NATO. He urges Congress to lift the arms embargo on Turkey, saying it has hindered efforts to resolve the Cyprus dispute, and says assistance to Greece is being discussed.

He also urges changes to trade restrictions affecting certain OPEC countries and to sanctions tied to Soviet emigration, arguing that these measures have harmed U.S. interests. He pledges continued efforts toward Middle East peace, strategic arms control with the Soviet Union, and improved relations with China.

The speaker highlights global challenges including hunger, energy, oceans, technology, environment, and relations between developed and developing nations. He calls for domestic energy action, protection of effective intelligence services under responsible oversight, and preservation of a strong defense budget. He concludes by urging one coherent foreign policy marked by courage, constancy, compassion, and cooperation.

Biodegradable plastic bags are being questioned as an environmental solution. A University of Edinburgh study led by Jesse Harrison found that research on their full life cycle and degradation rates is inconsistent, poorly defined, and not useful enough to inform policy or regulation.

Stocks moving heavily Tuesday included Kinder Morgan rising after Canada agreed to buy its pipeline project, while Bank of America and Petrobras fell. ZTO Express, Booz Allen Hamilton, American Woodmark, KB Home, and American Water Works gained on company or market developments.

Mitsui & Co said April-December net profit rose 64% to a record 376.8 billion yen and raised its full-year forecast to 440 billion yen, citing higher iron ore and coking coal prices and strength in metals, energy, steel products, machinery and infrastructure. Itochu reported record profit of 357.1 billion yen but kept its forecast unchanged. Sojitz raised its annual profit forecast to 56 billion yen on stronger coal prices.

The passage describes AGESA™ software porting and interface requirements for a host BIOS. Errors other than SUCCESS and BOUNDS_CHK imply an event was logged; the event log retains the 16 most recent events and can be read with AmdReadEventLog.

Support for 16-bit Real Mode is deprecated. The binary module remains viable in 32-bit protected mode with flat addressing. The host BIOS interfaces with AGESA through a bridge that calls the dispatcher, while AGESA calls back into the host through a CallOut port and host CallOut router. The host must establish a valid stack, create and fill standard headers, implement required call-outs, and use published entry points rather than internal procedure names.

For UEFI, execution spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases. AGESA core files are organized into libraries and build targets for these stages. Required build tools include MASM and Microsoft assembler/C compilers for 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit development. UEFI-specific porting includes StdHeader redefinition, environment-specific libraries, and SEC stack setup using AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK.

The PEI implementation includes processor initialization, memory initialization, and reset coordination PEIMs. These publish PPIs after reset, early initialization, post initialization, and memory initialization, and may generate HOBs containing memory information. The DXE driver performs late initialization, creates AMD component information tables, and publishes AgesaDxeProtocol. A GPU VGA control DXE driver manages VGA resource decoding for the iGPU.

Reference files in the Addendum directory provide examples and platform option templates. UEFI build control files and environment variables such as AGESA_ROOT, AGESA_OptsDir, and the AMD platform solution name must be integrated into the host build system. Initial integration steps include copying platform option files, setting environment variables, generating documentation, enabling Cache-as-RAM before AmdInitReset, and avoiding modification of SS, ESP, cache controls, or MTRRs during the Cache-as-RAM period.

The passage defines stack and early POST macros, including AMD_RESET_ENABLEMENT, AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK, and procedures to disable the pre-memory stack. These are stackless native assembly routines and must be used by the host environment. AArch64 APUs with PSP do not use these stack and early macros because PSP initializes DRAM.

Several service procedures are described, including AmdCreateStruct and AmdReleaseStruct for parameter block storage, routines to obtain DIMM data eye results, APIC addresses, execution cache size, PCI addresses, current core identity, memory FRU location, MMIO range allocation, and event log entries. Most require a stack and may depend on operational coherent HyperTransport links.

Published AGESA entry points are described in boot-time order. AmdInitReset performs minimal processor initialization after reset and configures execution cache regions and certain FCH settings. AmdInitEarly establishes the boot environment, performs full HyperTransport initialization, configures power management, and may request warm reset. AmdInitPost initializes system memory, transitions from pre-memory to post-memory, prepares processors for host control, and disables the pre-memory stack. AmdInitEnv transfers artifact data/HOBs to host-controlled memory and configures GNB/FCH settings before PCI enumeration.

Later functions include graphics display configuration after PCI resource allocation, AmdInitLate for generating ACPI, DMI, P-state, WHEA, ALIB, IVRS, CRAT, and CDIT tables, and AmdInitRtb for saving context before suspend. Resume procedures restore silicon and memory state using saved nonvolatile and volatile context data, restore processor registers after PCI structures are re-established, and perform final preparation before OS handoff.

A writer describes a long emergency room wait at Norfolk General Hospital, arguing doctors should have authority to call in help when wait times exceed two hours and blaming administrators rather than medical staff. Another writer criticizes seniors in long-term care having to pay medication fees and questions why provincial funding for new long-term care beds was announced shortly before the June 7 election.

Peter DeBoer said the team gained energy from returning veteran players and momentum from finally winning after struggling to establish it in the series. He praised a rookie’s ability to perform in key moments and said the team would not be there without him. DeBoer said the players remain motivated, enjoy being together, and are focused on staying alive in the Stanley Cup playoffs. He credited a veteran player’s composure and legacy, called for more scoring, expressed confidence in the power play despite strong opposing goaltending and penalty killing, and said the team must end its losing streak or its season will end.

KDKA-TV and WPXI-TV faced criticism after reporting false information that Antwon Rose II was seen on video firing a gun before the June 19 North Braddock shooting and that gunshot residue was found on his hands. Allegheny County Police Superintendent Coleman McDonough stated the video did not show Rose firing a gun and that the residue claim was false, cautioning media against unverified sources. WTAE-TV did not report the claims. KDKA later retracted the report and expressed regret. WPXI initially defended its reporting, then issued a written apology on June 28 for pain caused to Rose’s family and the community. The passage argues the stations failed by airing unverified information.

The passage describes systems and methods for dynamically providing video overlays. A client device receives video from an intermediate device such as a set-top box, identifies the set-top box, detects video content using fingerprints or template matching, and selects replacement video content based on the identified content. The client device uses templates associated with the set-top box to determine how original video, menus, notifications, informational bars, picture-in-picture regions, or semi-transparent overlays are arranged.

Reference fingerprints are generated from known video content, and query fingerprints are generated from video received by the client device. A video identification system compares query fingerprints to reference fingerprints using indexed patch values and distance measurements to identify video content, channels, broadcasters, or playback positions. Replacement content may then be retrieved from a replacement content server.

Templates define regions, masks, coordinates, bitmap comparisons, blending parameters, and overlay types. They may be generated manually or programmatically by analyzing known and unknown regions of received video, static and changing regions, or blended areas. The client device can resize, crop, reposition, blend, or partially replace video so that replacement content mimics how the set-top box presented the original content while preserving relevant overlays. Semi-transparent overlays may be transferred, reconstructed, filtered, or regenerated over replacement content.

The system can handle changes in video input, such as channel changes, by stopping replacement playback and resuming it when the original content returns. It can also detect modified playback states such as pause, fast-forward, rewind, or altered speed, and apply corresponding changes to replacement video. Data structures store picture-in-picture, menu overlay, menu blend, and template information by device and template identifiers. The described components may be implemented in hardware, software, or networked machines using machine-readable instructions.

YouTube announced four new YouTube Red Original series for family audiences, created with the YouTube Kids app in mind and debuting in spring. The series feature L2M, DanTDM, TheAtlanticCraft’s Joe and Cody, and Fruit Ninja. Additional shows will premiere in 2017, and YouTube Kids will soon be available on select LG and Samsung Smart TVs.

The lecture discusses multi-stakeholder engagement in sustainable supply chains, using palm oil and Golden Agri-Resources as a case. Participants identify stakeholders including growers, mills, corporations, consumers, governments, certifiers, investors, NGOs, and local and international communities. They debate strategies involving Greenpeace, RSPO and ISPO standards, certification costs, transparency, farmer incentives, productivity, communication, and whether GAR should pursue higher sustainability standards or broader market competitiveness. The instructor explains how NGOs often pressure public brands to drive supply chain changes and gives examples involving Nestle, Mitsubishi, Chiquita, Dell, Walmart, Starbucks, and industry collaborations such as the Sustainability Consortium, EICC, and Sustainable Apparel Coalition. The lecture also addresses challenges with sustainability labels, certification rigor, greenwashing, and NGO-company partnerships.

Costa has become the world’s second-largest coffee chain behind Starbucks, helping drive Britain’s growing coffee market. Its UK presence exceeds 2,000 shops, while sales reached £3.4 billion in 2016 and are forecast to keep rising.

Costa opened a new roastery in Basildon, Essex, chosen for its proximity to Tilbury Docks and London links. The site quadruples annual roasting capacity from 11,000 to 45,000 tonnes, enough for 2.1 billion cups a year, and uses automated packing expected to improve productivity by 25 percent. The facility emphasizes sustainability, with solar panels, rainwater heating, LED lighting, and Rainforest Alliance Certified coffee.

The article describes Costa’s roasting and quality-control process, including cleaning green coffee beans, roasting them, testing samples for colour and moisture, and lab-checking beans from every bag for defects and taste. About 8 percent of beans are rejected annually. Costa’s blend uses arabica and robusta beans, including robusta from Vietnam, the world’s second-biggest coffee producer after Brazil.

Costa also highlights staff development, including barista training and internal promotion. Master of Coffee Gennaro Pellicia, whose tongue is insured for £10 million, oversees tasting standards. The Basildon site can train 3,000 baristas a year and has space for future expansion, with a planned lifespan of at least 30 years.

MSPM0C1105/6 MCUs are ultra-low-power 32-bit Arm Cortex-M0+ devices operating up to 32MHz, with 1.62V to 3.6V supply and -40°C to 125°C range. They include up to 64KB flash, 8KB SRAM, on-chip oscillator, DMA, CRC, ADC, comparator, timers, watchdog, and UART, SPI, and I2C interfaces.

The Kiss of Death trading strategy is a sell signal for the S&P 500 that occurs when the index falls from an all-time high below its monthly 21-EMA, rebounds above it, then drops below its recent low. Since 1960, it triggered in 1969, 1973, 1978, 2001, and 2008, preceding major bear markets, but a September 2022 signal was followed by a market rise. The tested strategy sells on the signal and re-enters when the S&P 500 closes above its 10-month EMA. A backtest from 1967 found it improved buy-and-hold performance by raising CAGR and nearly halving maximum drawdown.

Fair Isaac shares rose more than 20% after the FICO score creator announced a pricing model allowing mortgage lenders to obtain credit scores through mortgage resellers rather than credit bureaus. The company said the change gives lenders pricing and distribution choices and removes unnecessary markups. Shares of Experian, TransUnion and Equifax fell 4% to 10% as investors viewed the move as potentially reducing credit bureaus’ role. Raymond James analyst Patrick O’Shaughnessy said the model could improve Fair Isaac’s economics and disintermediate bureaus from their markup on FICO scores. Federal Housing Finance Agency director Bill Pulte praised the move as a creative solution for consumers.

Tesla Motors filed a Form 8-K dated March 11, 2016, reporting an immaterial error in its 2015 Form 10-K that overstated the cost and net book value of the Supercharger network. The correct net book value as of December 31, 2015 was $166.6 million. The error was limited to one section and did not affect consolidated financial statements or notes.

Pekkala told Schoenfeld that most Finns sympathized with the democracies and increasingly believed Finland should make a separate peace with the Soviet Union, views he said were shared by Mannerheim, many army members, Social Democrats, and smaller parties, though not the Agrarians. Schoenfeld later told Foreign Minister Witting the U.S. position; Witting replied that Finland depended on German goodwill for 93% of imports, compared Finland’s situation with German troops to Iceland’s with Allied troops, and described Finland as “like a mouse in a trap,” showing little willingness to break from Germany. From Sweden, Johnson reported that Finland’s military situation was deteriorating and warned that a Soviet offensive and Finnish collapse could provoke Swedish calls to aid Finland, benefiting pro-German forces and risking a political crisis. Soviet Minister Kollontay was reportedly concerned about these effects and favored a simple cessation of fighting.

Scientists developed a molecular sensor that releases a thyme-like thymol flavor when it encounters influenza virus neuraminidase, potentially enabling taste-based flu detection through gum or lozenges. Current PCR tests are accurate but slow and expensive, while at-home lateral flow tests may miss pre-symptomatic infections. In lab tests, the sensor released thymol within 30 minutes in saliva from people diagnosed with flu and did not alter human or mouse cell function. Researchers hope to begin human clinical trials in about two years to test detection in pre- and post-symptomatic people. The technology has been patented with the European Patent Office.

Four Baltimore County executive candidates—Vicki Almond, Jim Brochin, Johnny Olszewski Jr. and Al Redmer Jr.—addressed real estate and development professionals at a forum, pledging to support smart growth and improve development approvals. None backed impact fees, and all described the approval process as cumbersome or in need of reform. They also discussed rezoning, with several calling for decisions to align with the county master plan and be more predictable. Brochin criticized “pay-to-play politics,” while others emphasized development’s role in economic growth and tax revenue. The forum was one of several scheduled before the June 26 primary.

The 12th Harrogate Advertiser Business Awards will be held as a black-tie dinner and entertainment event at Harrogate’s Royal Hall on Thursday, April 27, marking the first time the restored Edwardian theatre has hosted the ceremony. Entries are open until noon on Monday, March 13, and businesses may enter multiple categories. The awards recognise companies across the Harrogate Advertiser’s coverage area, with 10 categories including rural business, tourism, family-run business, employer, company size awards, website, business personality and lifetime achievement. The main sponsor is Verity Frearson, with individual sponsors for each award.

The passage argues that academic freedom is neither an inherent virtue nor a practical reality, citing Robert Oscar Lopez’s experience at California State University, Northridge and his later criticism of tenure and higher education. It claims tenure protects only select faculty while adjuncts remain vulnerable, and that ideological standards determine whose speech is tolerated. The author contends that higher education has become politically biased, morally and intellectually corrupt, and harmful to students through high tuition, debt, and weak job prospects. The passage endorses Lopez’s call to reduce funding for colleges, promote associate degrees, trade schools, and apprenticeships, and replace appeals to academic freedom with a focus on whether teachings are true or false.

The passage examines the first trading day of the month effect in the S&P 500 using SPY data since 1993. It defines the effect as the first trading day, not the first calendar day, of each month. The S&P 500’s average daily gain is 0.04%, while buying at the close of the last trading day of the month and selling at the close of the first trading day averages 0.24%. However, the passage says this basic approach is unstable and not viable as a standalone strategy, with much of its performance occurring before the 2008/09 financial crisis. February and July are identified as the strongest first trading days by month. The article presents improved versions using filters or criteria, including one with a 0.35% average gain, 67% win rate, 2.5 profit factor, and 5% maximum drawdown. It suggests the effect may be linked to capital inflows from savers, pension funds, and automatic savings.
The passage describes multiple views of a cooling fan design and states that broken lines show unclaimed portions.

The passage studies profit maximization in repeated bilateral trade by a broker under dominant-strategy incentive compatibility and individual rationality. Unlike prior work focused on welfare or gains-from-trade, it aims to minimize regret against the best mechanism in hindsight, including complex non-fixed-price mechanisms. In the stochastic i.i.d. setting with possibly correlated valuations, the authors give a polynomial-time algorithm with nearly tight \(\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T})\) regret and prove a matching \(\Omega(\sqrt{T})\) lower bound up to logarithmic factors, also implying sample complexity of about \(1/\varepsilon^2\). In the adversarial setting, they show no algorithm can achieve sublinear regret even against a \(2/3+\varepsilon\) fraction of optimal profit. They also apply a correspondence with non-excludable mechanism design to improve the regret bound for the joint ads problem from \(O(T^{3/4})\) to \(\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T})\). The passage highlights challenges from the non-parametric mechanism space and irregular profit functions.

The passage introduces RAPSEM, a Rank-Preserving Structural Equation Model for mediation analysis with latent variables. It explains that mediators help identify how interventions affect outcomes, but valid causal mediation requires addressing confounding. Standard SEM handles measurement error and latent constructs but depends on sequential ignorability, which is often unrealistic because relevant mediator–outcome confounders may be unmeasured. Rank-preserving models based on g-estimation relax this requirement by allowing omitted covariates if they do not modify treatment or mediator effects, but they have not previously been extended to latent variable models. RAPSEM integrates rank-preserving models with factor score regression and interaction corrections to estimate controlled direct and mediation effects while accounting for measurement error and omitted confounders under a no-effect-modifier assumption. The passage defines these effects in a randomized trial using potential outcomes and begins specifying the model’s measurement structure.

The speaker says the team has balanced hard work with fun, helping their success. They praise a fearless player’s shot-blocking and daily presence, note excitement building after rest days and media attention, and commend an underrated, smooth defenseman nominated for top defenseman.

The speaker said the team felt comfortable, played well, and trusted it would capitalize on chances. He praised the goalie for performing well after a difficult year for the team’s goalies, saying the team has confidence in him. He said the team has created another opportunity to even the series and compared the feeling to the San Jose series. He discussed the team’s growth together and praised key players for leadership, skill, work ethic, and scoring important goals. He said opponents are pressuring the power play effectively, but the team remains confident its personnel will produce. He credited Ryan Smyth’s effort, competitiveness, and ability to score around the net. The speaker emphasized that coaching, structure, adjustments, and game plans have been crucial throughout the playoffs. He said the team handled adversity and maintained focus after a frustrating incident. He added that the team has not yet played its best and believes improving slightly could help take over the series. He also said the organization’s tradition makes the experience more special.

Plymouth gift and gadget shop Hawkin's Bazaar will close its New George Street store on February 4. The shop, which has operated there for four years after six years in the West End, is holding a closing down sale with discounts of 50 to 75 per cent.

The study investigates whether transformers can learn transitive reasoning, framed as directed graph connectivity, from individual training examples rather than in-context prompts. It compares low-dimensional grid graphs with disconnected chain graphs, hypothesizing that connectivity is easier to learn when nodes can be embedded so path existence is inferable from node representations.

Experiments train transformers on node-pair connectivity labels while varying model size, graph size, grid dimensionality, and number of chains. Results show transformers learn connectivity more successfully on grid graphs than disconnected chain graphs. Increasing model size improves performance on grid graphs but not comparably on disconnected chain graphs. Increasing graph size keeps grid-graph performance consistent and improves disconnected-chain performance when it lengthens chains. Higher grid dimensionality and more disconnected chains make connectivity harder to learn, with graph-size scaling helping more than model-size scaling in these harder settings. The study concludes that transformers benefit from low-dimensional embedding structure when learning transitive relations and suggests evaluating real-world graphs in future work.

Visceral leishmaniasis (VL) is endemic in Ethiopia, including Somali Regional State, but its epidemiology and risk factors there are inadequately studied. This cross-sectional study in Denan district, south-eastern Ethiopia, assessed VL sero-prevalence, knowledge, attitudes and practices, associated factors, and sand fly species abundance from April to August 2021.

Among 187 participants from six kebeles, DAT testing found an overall VL sero-prevalence of 9.63%. Significant associated factors included age group, housing type, wall characteristics, floor condition, outdoor sleeping, and sleeping near animal shelters. Multivariable analysis identified age 19–36, damp floors, outdoor sleeping, and sleeping outdoors near animal shelters as associated with VL infection.

Knowledge and attitudes were limited: 53.48% had heard of VL, 42% identified sand fly bites as the transmission route, 89% knew at least one symptom, 78% considered VL treatable, 36% believed it was preventable, and 44% believed untreated VL could be fatal. Preventive practices included bed net use, insecticide spraying, smoking plant materials, and environmental cleaning.

Entomological surveys collected 823 sand flies representing 12 species from indoor, peri-domestic, forest, and termite mound habitats. Sergentomyia clydie was the most abundant species, while Phlebotomus orientalis was the dominant Phlebotomus species and was mainly collected from termite mounds and forest habitats. The study concludes that VL sero-prevalence is relatively high in this new focus, community awareness is inadequate, and P. orientalis may contribute to VL transmission in the area.

Cincinnati beat No. 14 Iowa State, handing the Cyclones their first loss. The Bearcats led 31-7 before Iowa State rallied within eight late, but Cincinnati recovered an onside kick to secure the win. Cincinnati improved to 4-1 and 2-0 in the Big 12, while Iowa State fell to 5-1 and 2-1.

MADSEN Cycles offers customized bucket bikes with large rear buckets that can carry up to four kids and cargo. The bikes include removable bench seats and seat belts, and the company provides accessories to improve comfort, security, style, and function. Accessories include rain covers, frame-mounted front racks, and a middle bucket seat for pets, diaper changes, or carrying drinks.

The North Carolina court held that the defendant was not given reasonable time to prepare for trial after withdrawing his guilty plea and entering a not guilty plea. The defendant had requested time to obtain witnesses from Florida and West Virginia, and his appointed counsel also requested a continuance until the following week. Both requests were denied, and the case was tried the next day, resulting in a misdemeanor conviction and two-year sentence. The court found this was error, noting potential prejudice from jurors hearing the withdrawn guilty plea and counsel’s need for time to investigate. A new trial was ordered.

Jerome “Jay” Powell, President Donald Trump’s pick to lead the US Federal Reserve, succeeds Janet Yellen as chair at a time of strong growth, low unemployment, quiet inflation and rising wages. Yellen leaves after one term, having ended bond-buying, begun reducing Fed holdings and overseen gradual rate increases. Powell, a rare non-economist in the role, may soon face difficult decisions over how quickly to raise interest rates as the US economy grows, tax cuts take effect and global economies expand simultaneously. The Fed raised rates three times last year and signaled three more likely this year, with the first expected in March. Policymakers remain divided over inflation and the effects of fiscal stimulus, while faster rate hikes could unsettle markets.

The Supreme Court will consider whether federal firearm statutes Sections 924(c) and 924(j) allow separate convictions and sentences for the same conduct. The case involves Barrett, convicted after armed robberies that led to a fatal shooting. Section 924(c) covers firearm use tied to certain crimes, while Section 924(j) adds liability when death results. The issue turns on double jeopardy principles and the Blockburger test for determining whether Congress intended multiple punishments. Barrett and the government argue separate sentences are not permitted; court-appointed amicus Nicole McCloud defends the lower court’s ruling allowing them.

Vocational education assessment requires both formative and summative approaches that address theoretical knowledge, technical skills, and workplace competence. Formative assessment involves immediate feedback, self-assessment, peer review, multiple attempts, and teacher judgment, but it can be difficult because teachable moments may be unplanned and teachers need time and preparation to use it effectively.

Competence-based education connects classroom learning to workplace performance by assessing students against industry standards rather than only academic outcomes. It emphasizes observable performance, workplace quality standards, clear expectations, and authentic vocational tasks. Workplace practicum evaluations can provide effective evidence of competence and may improve student motivation and engagement.

Authentic assessment in VET should reflect real workplace conditions, including the social context of performance and feedback from supervisors. While authenticity can reduce reliability because vocational competence is difficult to standardize, clear procedures, rubrics, professional development, and calibration with other teachers and experts can improve consistency.

A comprehensive VET assessment program should include written tests, technical skills assessments, workplace evaluations, process and product assessments, and both formative and summative methods. Because vocational competence includes knowledge, technical skills, and workplace skills, assessment should cover levels ranging from knowing information to performing authentic tasks in workplace settings.

The Second Circuit affirmed summary judgment for Reisdorf Brothers on Patrick and Linda George’s federal Clean Water Act and Resource Conservation and Recovery Act claims. The court held that the plaintiffs failed to raise a genuine issue of material fact showing continuous or intermittent pollutant discharges under the CWA; evidence of a 2009 chemical spill showed only a discrete past incident, and claims involving fertilizer, pesticide, molasses, oil, water discharge, and storm water were speculative, waived, or improperly raised. The court also affirmed summary judgment on the RCRA claim because the plaintiffs did not allege or show violation of the relevant federal open-dumping regulations. It upheld the district court’s refusal to exercise supplemental jurisdiction over the plaintiffs’ state adverse possession claim after dismissing the federal claims. The court further affirmed the denial of attorney’s fees to Reisdorf, finding no abuse of discretion because the plaintiffs’ claims were not frivolous or brought in bad faith.

Phil Kessel scored twice with an assist and Evgeni Malkin had two goals and two assists as the Pittsburgh Penguins beat the Washington Capitals 7-4. Bryan Rust, Carl Hagelin and Patric Hornqvist also scored for Pittsburgh, which won its fourth straight and seventh consecutive home game. Sidney Crosby extended his scoring streak to 11 games, and Matt Murray made 29 saves. Alex Ovechkin scored twice for Washington, raising his NHL-leading season total to 32, while Dmitry Orlov and Evgeny Kuznetsov also scored. Pittsburgh broke open the game with three goals early in the third period, chasing Braden Holtby. The Penguins went 3 for 4 on the power play, while Washington went 0 for 3.

This study used longitudinal PREVEND cohort data from Groningen, Netherlands, to model transitions between KDIGO kidney disease risk stages and their association with new-onset heart failure. Participants were categorized by eGFR and urinary albumin excretion into low, intermediate, and high/very high risk stages. A multi-state model estimated age- and sex-specific transition rates while accounting for misclassification and interval-censored measurements.

At baseline, 8,569 participants were included; 79.8% were low risk, 14.9% intermediate risk, and 3.5% high/very high risk. Over a median 12.6 years, 373 developed new-onset heart failure and 710 died before heart failure. Forward transitions across KDIGO stages increased with age and were generally higher in men, while younger participants and women were more likely to transition backward from intermediate to low risk. Progression to intermediate risk occurred mainly between ages 60 and 70, and progression to high/very high risk mainly after age 70.

More advanced KDIGO stages were associated with higher risk of new-onset heart failure. Relative risks were stronger in younger participants, while absolute rate differences were larger in older participants. Women had lower transition rates to heart failure than men. Misclassification was notable, especially from intermediate to low risk and from high/very high to intermediate risk, and was lower when cystatin C-based eGFR was used. The model showed excellent calibration. The authors conclude that slowing progression of KDIGO risk stages may reduce new-onset heart failure in middle-aged populations.

The passage presents a study developing a scale to measure prospective teachers’ attitudes toward values education through distance education. It reviews literature on values education, distance education, and related studies, noting that no existing scale specifically measures attitudes toward values education through distance education.

The study used a descriptive survey model and followed DeVellis’s scale development steps. Participants were 341 prospective teachers from Gazi University’s Faculty of Education, mostly female and from different grade levels. An initial 43-item pool was created through literature review and prospective teachers’ written opinions. After expert review, language review, and a pilot study, a 40-item Likert-type scale was administered.

Exploratory factor analysis showed a two-factor structure after removing four items. The final scale includes 36 items: 21 positive and 15 negative. The two factors were named “Necessity and Usefulness” and “Feasibility.” The scale explained 63.286% of total variance. Reliability was high, with Cronbach’s alpha values of .969 and .961 for the two factors. Item analyses showed that all items were distinctive and had adequate item-total correlations.

The study concludes that the scale provides valid and reliable measurements for identifying prospective teachers’ attitudes toward values education through distance education. It notes limitations including gender imbalance, data from only one university, and lack of an external comparable scale. Future studies are recommended to conduct confirmatory factor analysis with participants from different universities and examine additional validity and reliability evidence.

The passage discusses ways to access and trade Australian financial markets, including ETFs, ADRs, direct stock trading through international brokers such as Interactive Brokers, and stock CFDs through Australian CFD brokers. It uses the US-traded iShares MSCI-Australia ETF (EWA) as a proxy for the Australian stock market in backtests.

The passage states that Australia’s equity market has significant exposure to commodities, making it different from markets such as the US. It says mean reversion and classical strategies, including the 200-day moving average and Golden Cross, were less effective for EWA, while seasonal strategies performed better. A Santa Claus effect strategy for Australian stocks reportedly had only two negative years since 1996, with a 92% win rate, an average gain of 2.4% per trade, and 1.87% annual returns while invested 2.3% of the year.

US investors can trade Australian equity ETFs and the Invesco CurrencyShares Australian Dollar Trust (FXA), which tracks the Australian dollar versus the US dollar. The passage also notes that the ASX lists over 2,000 companies and offers stocks, ETFs, bonds, and other securities. Australia’s main exchange is the Australian Securities Exchange, with the Sydney Stock Exchange also mentioned.

Australian markets are open Monday to Friday, excluding national holidays, from 10:00 am to 4:00 pm Australian Eastern Daylight Time, or 11:00 pm to 5:00 am GMT. The Australian dollar can be traded against major currencies, including AUD/USD, EUR/AUD, GBP/AUD, AUD/JPY, AUD/NZD, AUD/CAD, and AUD/CHF.

Indian press reports from April 27, 2001 said the Dabhol Power Company board authorised its management, including Neil McGregor and K Wade Cline, to issue a notice terminating its power purchase agreement with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board. The decision was approved six to one, with IDBI opposing and MSEB barred from voting as an interested party.

Reports said the move did not necessarily mean immediate termination, as procedures, lender consent, and a possible suspension or consultation period could apply. International and domestic lenders were divided, with some foreign lenders supporting a pull-out or halting further disbursements, while Indian lenders including IDBI favoured renegotiation.

MSEB paid Rs 134 crore toward DPC’s March bill “under protest,” while disputing part of the amount and maintaining claims including a Rs 401 crore penalty against DPC. Maharashtra and central government officials said they preferred renegotiation and an amicable settlement. Several reports cited possible central liabilities if the project were terminated, including one year’s electricity bill and a $300 million termination fee.

Defending a talented tall or wide post player requires team adjustments, including pressure on passers, helpside support, traps, and strong individual fundamentals before the catch. Strategies include beating the post to the block, pushing them away from the basket, fronting, denying passing lanes, forcing play to their weaker side, pressing full court, and using adjusted 2-3 zone or Diamond & One defenses.

Stephen Paddock bought 1,000 tracer rounds before the Las Vegas shooting, though it was unclear whether he used them. Authorities said his preparations included stockpiling 23 guns, modifying some for continuous fire, setting up cameras, and booking rooms overlooking other festivals. Investigators were still seeking a motive and examining whether he planned additional attacks, including a possible car bombing. Paddock had ammunition, fertilizer, and Tannerite in his car. His girlfriend, Marilou Danley, said she was unaware of his plans and had seen no signs he might become violent.

Justice Babatunde Quadri of the Federal High Court, Abuja admitted EFCC documents as evidence against Chinese national Li Ya Ping, charged with allegedly concealing $300,000 while attempting to fly to Dubai. EFCC witness Hassan Mohammed Misau testified that Customs intercepted the defendant at Abuja airport and handed him, documents, devices, and the money to EFCC.

Aledo leads Ryan 2-0 in a Friday night Texas high school football matchup in Denton after Ryan was called for intentional grounding in its own end zone, resulting in a safety. Aledo is ranked in The Sporting News Top 25 and No. 16 in the Massey Ratings, while Ryan is unranked.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2017. Net sales were $37.96 billion for Q2 2017, up from $30.40 billion in Q2 2016, while net income fell to $197 million from $857 million. For the first six months of 2017, net sales were $73.67 billion and net income was $921 million, compared with $59.53 billion and $1.37 billion in the prior-year period.

Operating income declined to $628 million in Q2 2017 from $1.29 billion in Q2 2016. North America operating income was $436 million, International operating loss was $724 million, and AWS operating income was $916 million. AWS net sales rose to $4.10 billion in Q2 2017 from $2.89 billion in Q2 2016.

Cash and cash equivalents were $13.20 billion at June 30, 2017, down from $19.33 billion at December 31, 2016. Total assets were $87.78 billion, total liabilities were $64.57 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $23.21 billion. Operating cash flow was $3.83 billion in Q2 2017 and $17.89 billion for the trailing twelve months ended June 30, 2017.

Amazon entered into an agreement in June 2017 to acquire Whole Foods Market, Inc. for approximately $13.7 billion, including net debt, expected to be funded with debt financing and cash on hand. In May 2017, Amazon acquired Souq Group Ltd. for approximately $586 million net of cash acquired. The company also disclosed tax matters, legal proceedings, contractual commitments of $49.18 billion, and ongoing risks related to operations, taxes, litigation, and market conditions.

The passage identifies key archival sources for Foreign Relations, 1981–1988, Volume IV, including Reagan Library White House, NSC, State Department, and related files on Soviet policy. It also notes online resources and introduces documentation on U.S. covert actions. During the Truman administration, NSC 4–A authorized peacetime covert psychological operations under the CIA, while NSC 10/2 later expanded this to broader covert operations with plausible deniability.

VentureWire’s October 19, 2000 issue reports major venture financing and company developments. St. Paul Venture Capital closed a $1.3 billion sixth fund, idealab! postponed its IPO citing market volatility, Constellation Ventures closed a $350 million fund, and New Edge Networks raised $139.9 million in cash and debt financing. Numerous companies announced funding rounds, including Alopa, MMS, Egenera, Widevine, Propel, EZchip, Revit, GivingCapital, Clairvoyant, Ajunto, LockStream, and others. New product and company launches included Ipingpong, Capital IQ, Stonepath Europe, First World E-Commerce Group, Vation, and Practice.com. Other news included EMI taking an equity stake in Soundbuzz, NetObjects acquiring MyComputer.com for about $51 million, several board appointments, BeyondMedia.com naming Ilknur Sancak president, new venture fund activity by Hudson Venture Partners and RiverVest, Discovery Capital acquiring ExFund Technologies, and Onset Ventures promoting Susan Mason to general partner.

The passage provides SanDisk MP3 player FAQ, support, warranty, licensing, and disposal information. Playback issues may result from missing rights; firmware should be updated for correct function and features. CDs must be ripped before transfer, unsupported files must be converted, and MTP transfers depend on file type and folder. Podcasts are supported if MP3 at 32–320 kbps, and unknown artist/album entries usually indicate missing ID3 tags. Technical support is available through SanDisk by phone or online. The 1-year limited warranty covers the original purchaser, excludes third-party software/content and misuse, and may provide repair, replacement, or refund. SanDisk disclaims liability for lost data and certain damages. The passage also describes Microsoft WM-DRM notices, SanDisk software license terms and restrictions, warranty disclaimers, liability limits, termination, export rules, and instructions not to dispose of the device with unsorted household waste.

Children born to obese women are twice as likely to be obese by age two, and childhood obesity is also linked to fathers’ obesity. Research suggests eggs and sperm carry molecules influenced by parents’ nutrition that can affect a child’s obesity risk. Maternal BMI at conception is closely associated with young children’s obesity, while paternal BMI and fatness are linked to children’s birthweight and body fat. When both parents are obese, the child’s risk of becoming overweight doubles compared with having one overweight parent.

Sperm carry non-coding RNAs that may influence development, and these differ in obese males. Eggs are also affected by maternal nutrition; higher fat intake and obesity can alter egg fat content, metabolism, and mitochondria, potentially increasing offspring susceptibility to obesity and diabetes. Embryos can also respond to positive signals. In mice, anti-diabetes drugs, exercise, diet, and exercise interventions have improved egg or sperm quality and reduced transmission of obesity risk. Limited human data show children conceived after maternal gastric banding were less obese than siblings conceived before it. The passage argues that pre-conception health planning should include both mothers and fathers, and that preventing obesity in adolescents and young adults may influence community obesity rates.

Ozzie played well and made key saves, but the team allowed more scoring chances than expected. After taking the lead, they struggled, while the opponent gained confidence in the second period during a first-game feeling-out process.

STAT’s biotech roundup reports that Novo Nordisk plans to buy Akero Therapeutics, developer of a MASH liver disease drug, for up to $5.2 billion. The passage also lists other health and biotech headlines, including potential U.K. drug spending changes, infectious disease research concerns, rare disease CRISPR questions, cannabis use among people with psychosis, Amgen drug developments, and drug pricing issues.

Football has become increasingly focused on passing, making cornerbacks crucial defensive players. A cornerback’s primary job is to cover opposing wide receivers in man or zone coverage, often in difficult one-on-one situations where mistakes can lead to big gains or touchdowns. The position is named for its responsibility to protect the outside thirds of the field near the boundary and is part of the defensive backs unit.

Cornerbacks are typically fast, agile, and skilled at backpedaling, changing direction, and sprinting to stay with receivers. They also help defend runs to the outside by tackling or forcing runners back inside. Great cornerbacks are sometimes called “lockdown corners” because they can neutralize top receivers.

Notable cornerbacks mentioned include Deion Sanders, Charles Woodson, Mel Blount, Champ Bailey, Ty Law, Darrell Revis, Dick Lane, Mike Haynes, Lem Barney, and Dick LeBeau. The position is important because strong cornerback play can limit passing attacks, force quarterbacks to hesitate, and help the pass rush. Revis’s nickname, “Revis Island,” reflected his ability to cover receivers without safety help.

David Jones has not renewed Jesinta Franklin’s contract after two years, saying it is “taking another direction” and thanking her for her work. The retailer announced Victoria Lee as its newest ambassador. The future of fellow ambassador Jessica Gomes is reportedly unclear.

CeeDee Lamb, who has missed two games with a high ankle sprain suffered in Week 3, was seen doing rehab work on a side field Wednesday, his first outdoor activity since the injury. His Week 6 status remains doubtful, but Stephen Jones said Lamb and several teammates could return within the next two weeks.

The passage explains goal kick rules and tactics for defending them. A goal kick is taken when the attacking team last touches the ball over the defenders’ goal line, and the ball is in play once it is kicked and visibly moves. Opponents should be outside the penalty area until the kick is taken, with retakes required in certain cases if they interfere before the ball is in play.

Defending goal kicks aims to win the ball immediately in a dangerous area or prevent easy buildup and long successful kicks. Key tactics include marking likely receivers with a mix of man-to-man and zone coverage, moving aggressively to win the ball, transitioning quickly to attack if possession is gained, and pressing high if it is not. Suggested positioning places strikers near the kicker and short options, midfielders ready for lofted balls, and backs supporting wide defensive areas.

For young players, build-out lines are used to help teams play out from the back by requiring opponents to retreat. Coaches should teach wide, upfield play, avoid passing across their own goal, and use simple target and secondary receiver options. Older youth players progress to wider and deeper targets, with added midfield options and defensive pressure in training. Adult teams can use all goal kick options, including short passes, deep targets, and planned runs.

Coaching tips emphasize quick reactions, awareness that goal kicks are direct, effects of wind and field conditions, constant sight of the ball, scouting opponents’ kicking range and tendencies, and drilling goal kick defense seriously.

Leicester pharmacist Zameer Ghumra, 38, was jailed for six years after being convicted at Nottingham Crown Court of disseminating terrorist propaganda. He showed a beheading video to a child, posted pro-ISIS content, and tried to radicalise primary school-age children, causing lasting distress to two boys.

The passage reviews a backtest of Larry Connors’ 3-day high/low ETF trading strategy from “High Probability ETF Trading” (2009). The strategy buys an ETF after three consecutive days of lower highs and lower lows, with criteria including price above the 200-day moving average and below the 5-day moving average. Connors emphasized fully testable strategies, high win ratios of at least 65%, and trading ETFs rather than stocks. Original tests covered 20 popular ETFs through 2008. Updated testing suggests 13 of 20 ETFs performed worse since the original test, though the strategy still shows some promise. A portfolio test using 25 ETFs, maximum five positions, and 20% allocation per position was also discussed, with the worst drawdown occurring in July 2011 during the EU debt crisis.

NewMarket is a major producer of additives for petroleum-based fuels and lubricants through its Afton Chemical business, with strong margins, cash flow, and returns on capital. However, growth has been weak, with sales declining between 2014 and 2016 due to longer oil-change intervals, fuel-efficiency improvements, and engine design changes. The company is more focused on gasoline additives than faster-growing diesel additives.

NewMarket is expanding in emerging markets through its acquisition of Aditivos Mexicanos and a new Singapore plant, which could help it benefit from vehicle growth in Asia and other developing regions. The company also invests significantly in R&D for fuel-efficiency additives, new lubricant specifications, hydraulic fluids, and industrial lubricants.

The author expects about 3% long-term revenue growth and improved free cash flow after the Singapore plant is completed, but does not view the shares as undervalued. The stock price appears to already reflect substantial future cash flow growth, and stronger growth may require greater diversification or further acquisitions.

Nippon Express said an employee falsified inspection stamps on government-stockpiled rice stored for Mitsubishi Corp., which received a farm ministry business improvement order in May. Misconduct affected 251 container bags whose original bags were damaged or wet. Fifteen 30-kilogram bags were shipped for livestock feed, with no reported health damage; the rest will be incinerated, and none went for human consumption.
EON Resources published a slide deck; the passage also describes Seeking Alpha’s transcripts team and chart data ranges.

The passage outlines contract terms for officers and seamen on the vessel “Cape Horn Pigeon.” Expenses arising from misconduct, desertion, disobedience, or mutiny are charged to responsible individuals. The master may displace an incompetent or unwilling officer or seaman after trial, adjust his lay, and increase the lay of any replacement promoted. If sickness or death prevents completion of the voyage, representatives receive a proportional share. Crew are accountable for vessel property and cargo handling entrusted to them. Those who complete the voyage properly are to be paid in San Francisco based on specified rates for whale oil, sperm oil, and whalebone, with whalebone rates depending on the Arctic fleet’s total catch. Signatories affirm voluntary agreement, pledge to report aboard when ordered, and agree not to bring distilled spirits except for medical use, with violation forfeiting their share. The document is certified as a true copy by San Francisco’s Deputy Collector on February 28, 1893, and by Secretary of State John Hay on September 1, 1900.

The passage lists repeated global finance and technology headlines, then details the Bifrost subsea cable, a 20,000-kilometre, $760 million system connecting Singapore and the U.S. West Coast. The paper examines how 147 second-year engineering and technical management students at a Hungarian university evaluate skills needed for future employability within Education 4.0. It reviews Industry 4.0, digital transformation, Education 4.0, and job skills identified by the World Economic Forum, emphasizing problem-solving, self-management, teamwork, technology use, digital competence, lifelong learning, and international experience.

Using survey data collected in 2019 and 2021, the study analyzed students’ priorities for skill development, the perceived value of international study, career success factors, and higher education’s contribution to employability. Quantitative analysis was conducted with SPSS using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and CHAID decision tree analysis.

Students overall ranked problem-solving, specialization-related knowledge, communication skills, and technical/IT preparedness as important. Engineering students placed more emphasis on specialization-related knowledge and technical and mathematical knowledge, while technical management students emphasized decision-making and analytical skills. Both groups valued international study mainly for improving foreign language skills, though business students prioritized networking and adaptation to international norms more than engineering students. Students viewed individual talents, professional devotion, and networks as key factors in graduate labor market success.

The study found partial differences between the two student groups in expectations from higher education, especially regarding job-related knowledge, quantitative analysis, teamwork, and self-understanding. It concludes that universities should adapt curricula to Education 4.0 by integrating technical, digital, and soft skill development, supporting international experience, and promoting multidisciplinary and practice-oriented learning.

Thirty-seven lawyers, including 10 incoming partners, are leaving Cadwalader, Wickersham & Taft for Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe, joining offices in Charlotte, London, Washington, D.C., and New York. Reports say Cadwalader has seen significant partner departures this year, with Bloomberg Law counting 33 partner exits including retirements.
