In Hill v. Levine, the plaintiff sought specific performance of a written agreement to sell Boston lots with good title free of encumbrances. The defendant refused, arguing that a deed provision requiring any redivided lot to have at least fifty feet of frontage created a continuing restriction or at least a reasonable doubt about title. The Superior Court dismissed the bill.

The Supreme Judicial Court held that the frontage provision was not part of a general scheme benefiting other lots, was a personal agreement between grantor and grantee, and was subject to the deed’s twenty-year restriction period. Its omission from later deeds and a Land Court decree supported that conclusion. The provision did not create an equitable easement appurtenant to remaining land. Because the issue was only the construction of a written deed and there was no reasonable doubt about its meaning, the possibility of future litigation did not justify refusing specific performance. The decree was reversed, and specific performance was ordered.

Manchester United are reportedly cleared to make a £50m bid for Fulham teenager Ryan Sessegnon, with Fulham preparing for his possible January departure amid interest from United and Tottenham. Jose Mourinho has also reportedly held talks with Marouane Fellaini about extending his contract, which expires at the end of the season.

Maldives President Yameen Abdul Gayoom said he was open to holding an early presidential election after the Supreme Court ordered the release and retrial of political prisoners, including exiled former President Mohammed Nasheed, and reinstated 12 opposition lawmakers. Their return would cost Yameen’s party its parliamentary majority, and parliament’s opening was indefinitely postponed. Yameen said authorities were working on how to implement the ruling without causing difficulties. He also dismissed two police chiefs after the order, with no reason given for the latest removal. Opposition protests demanding the prisoners’ release were dispersed by police using force, and journalists were kept away from some events. U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged the government to respect the court order and supported all-party talks. Nasheed said he would run again for president after his conviction was overturned.

Microsoft announced upcoming Windows 10 accessibility updates for users with visual impairment, including redesigned Ease of Access settings, new display options, improved Narrator responsiveness and voice-based text styling, and enhanced eye control. Some features are available in Insider preview builds, with more accessibility updates promised later this year.

Marine heatwaves are prolonged periods of unusually warm ocean water that can occur in any season and last weeks or months, harming marine ecosystems, fisheries and aquaculture. Scientists recently developed a definition to study their global patterns. Analysis of more than 100 years of sea surface temperature data found marine heatwaves have become longer and more frequent, with marine heatwave days increasing 54% from 1925 to 2016. Between 1925–1954 and 1987–2016, their frequency rose 34% and duration 17%, trends linked to rising ocean temperatures.

Recent events caused major impacts, including kelp forest loss in western Australia, seagrass decline in Shark Bay, disruption of the Gulf of Maine lobster fishery, and effects from the North Pacific “Blob,” such as fishery closures, marine mammal strandings, harmful algal blooms and weather changes. Human-caused climate change has made some marine heatwaves far more likely, including events affecting the Great Barrier Reef and Tasmanian fisheries. Scientists aim to improve forecasts to help managers and industries respond, while reducing greenhouse gas emissions is identified as necessary to limit worsening impacts.

Scientists have used stored sperm from Sudan, the last male northern white rhino, to fertilize southern white rhino eggs, creating two hybrid embryos that have been frozen for possible future implantation. Researchers hope to obtain eggs from the two remaining northern white rhino females, Fatu and Najin, to create pure northern white rhino embryos and aim for a calf within three years. Other options include hybrid breeding or deriving sperm and eggs from cells, though major uncertainties remain. Some conservationists warn that reliance on reproductive technology could reduce focus on existing conservation efforts.

The Carolina Panthers ended their 2016 season with a 17-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, finishing 6-10. Carolina opened with a strong touchdown drive but struggled offensively afterward, while the defense allowed repeated Tampa Bay drives despite giving up only 300 total yards. Cam Newton completed 56% of his passes and threw three interceptions, and Graham Gano missed three field goals while playing with a broken bone in his plant foot. The Panthers scored late but failed on a two-point conversion after Greg Olsen slipped. Positives included performances from David Mayo, Shaq Thompson, James Bradberry, and Damiere Byrd. Carolina will pick eighth in the next NFL draft.

An MIT study found Manhattan could meet 98% of ride demand with 3,000 four-person shared taxis, or 2,000 10-passenger vans, if riders accepted pooling, longer trips, and average waits of 2.8 minutes. Researchers analyzed three million taxi rides from March 2013. The shift could reduce congestion and pollution but may be unpopular with riders and drivers, and could leave many taxi and for-hire drivers without work.

The lecture explains Kerberos as a cryptographic protocol for authenticating users, clients, and services over an untrusted network. Kerberos was designed for distributed systems with many workstations and servers, replacing weaker approaches such as IP-address-based authentication. It remains used at MIT and forms a basis for Microsoft Active Directory.

Kerberos relies on a trusted Key Distribution Center (KDC), which stores shared keys for users and services and maps them to principal names. Users must also trust their own workstations, since a compromised workstation can capture passwords or tickets. Kerberos provides authentication, while individual services handle authorization through mechanisms such as access control lists.

The protocol uses tickets and authenticators. A user first obtains a ticket from the Kerberos service using a key derived from the user’s password. This usually grants access to the Ticket Granting Service (TGS), allowing the user to discard the password-derived key and later request service tickets without retyping the password. Service tickets contain a session key shared between the client and service, encrypted so that only the intended service can read it. Authenticators help prevent replay attacks by including client identity, address, and timestamp data.

The lecture discusses several Kerberos 4 weaknesses. It assumed encryption also provided message integrity, enabled offline password guessing, used DES with fixed 56-bit keys, relied partly on IP addresses, reused the same key for traffic in both directions, and had flaws in password-changing that could reveal newer passwords if older ones were later disclosed. Kerberos 5 addresses many issues by authenticating messages, supporting stronger encryption algorithms, using separate keys, and improving password-change protocols with mechanisms such as Diffie-Hellman key exchange.

The KDC is highly trusted and must be protected, because compromising it allows attackers to issue tickets for any user or service. Kerberos supports read-only replicas so users can continue logging in and obtaining tickets if the master KDC is unavailable. If a service key is compromised, it must be replaced, since attackers with that key can decrypt tickets, observe traffic, or forge tickets for that service.

The passage describes a patent disclosure for methods and systems that detect, process, and respond to speech commands across multiple networked data modules, such as media devices or loudspeakers. Devices in a group detect an activation command, compute a “Hot Word” score based on factors such as signal power, recognizer confidence, source location, and audio processing quality, and use these scores to determine which devices captured the best audio. A group leader may collect scores, mute playback, activate microphones on selected devices, combine their recorded speech data, send a request to an external server, receive a requested action, and distribute the response to the group. Alternatively, devices may broadcast scores and confidence levels to one another in a decentralized approach.

The system supports partial processing of speech commands by selecting the best audio segments from different devices, including situations where a user moves while speaking. It also describes a content management system with data modules assigned dynamic roles such as Player, Follower, and Renderer for receiving, distributing, and playing media content. A computing device implementation includes processors, memory, applications, and stored data for speech processing, network statistics, Hot Words, and module characteristics. The disclosure also notes possible implementations in hardware, software, firmware, storage media, and networked computing devices.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated August 15, 2017, reporting that it issued a press release announcing the pricing of a previously announced private placement offering of $16.0 billion in aggregate principal amount of senior unsecured notes. The passage describes SD Memory Card Physical Layer Specification details on lock/unlock behavior, commands, switching functions, timing, status, capacity differences, CRC, and speed classes.

Force erase does not erase the secure area; during execution the card remains locked and retains temporary/group write protection, then unlocks and clears those protections after all user area erase completes. ACMD6 is rejected while locked, and bus width changes only when unlocked. Locked cards accept only specified commands; other commands, including security commands, are illegal. Lock/unlock support differs among Type 1, Type 2, and Type 3 cards.

APP_CMD (CMD55) makes the following command application-specific; defined, undefined, legal, and illegal ACMD handling is described, with ACMD41 having exceptions for APP_CMD status. CMD6 switches or checks card functions, including access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. Mode 0 queries support and current/power consumption; Mode 1 switches functions. CMD6 returns R1 plus a 512-bit status block. Function 0 is default, 0xF keeps current function, and busy status indicates functions that should not be changed. Power Limit controls total card power and is mandatory in UHS-II.

High-Speed mode provides 25 MB/sec interface speed using 50 MHz clock and is enabled by CMD6 on Version 1.10 or later cards if supported. Command system extensions reserve CMD34-37, CMD50, and CMD57. CMD8 is used in Idle state for Version 2.00 or later cards to check host supply voltage and returns R7 if accepted.

SDSC uses byte addressing and CMD16-defined block length, while SDHC/SDXC use 512-byte block addressing for memory access commands and disable partial or misaligned access. SDHC/SDXC do not support write-protected groups. Hosts may change or stop the bus clock with restrictions, must provide eight clocks after transactions, and must manage ACMD41 and busy-card conditions correctly.

Commands, responses, data, CSD, and CID are protected by CRC7 or CRC16 as applicable. CRC failures and illegal commands prevent execution and set status bits. Read, write, and erase timeout rules are defined, including different limits for SDHC, SDXC, multiple-block writes, and UHS-II data bursts.

The passage defines command types, 48-bit command format, command classes, supported command requirements, application-specific commands, UHS-II command differences, response formats R1, R1b, R2, R3, R6, and R7, and card, SD, and task status fields.

Speed Class methods classify card performance for real-time recording. Speed Class, UHS Speed Grade, and Video Speed Class are optional in this version. Allocation Units and Recording Units define write management. Speed Class performance covers write, move, read, FAT update, and host-buffer considerations. SDXC Speed Class differs by using larger AU/RU sizes, requiring sequential writes to entirely free AUs, not supporting move performance, and adding exFAT-related FAT, bitmap, directory entry, CI update, and CMD20 behavior.

The passage outlines documentation for the 1945 United Nations Conference on International Organization in San Francisco, held April 25–June 26 to draft a world security organization charter. Fifty governments unanimously approved the UN Charter, the Statute of the International Court of Justice, and interim arrangements for a Preparatory Commission on June 25; the Charter was signed June 26 by 153 delegates, with space left for Poland. The U.S. Senate consented to ratification on July 28, President Truman ratified on August 8, and the Charter entered into force October 24, 1945. The Conference used the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals as its agenda, operated through commissions and technical committees, and produced extensive mimeographed documentation later published in a 22-volume series.

He defended “America First” as compatible with international cooperation, called for fair and reciprocal trade, and criticized unfair economic practices. He also discussed energy production, military investment, allied defense contributions, efforts against North Korea, Iran, ISIS, and terrorism, and proposed a merit-based immigration system. In questions from Klaus Schwab, Trump said tax reform was a major priority because it encouraged investment, worker bonuses, and economic confidence. He cited his business background, deregulation efforts, and role as a “cheerleader” for the United States as important to his presidency.

A year after Loper Bright overruled Chevron, courts are shifting agency-review doctrine toward independent textualist statutory interpretation, relying on dictionaries, ordinary meaning, grammar, and statutory structure rather than agency expertise or broader policy considerations. Skidmore deference has not disappeared but appears mostly in indirect “shadow” form, with courts noting consistent agency interpretations as support after reaching their own readings. Lower courts are divided and inconsistent in applying it. The major questions doctrine remains important after Loper Bright, and Justice Kavanaugh has suggested it may not apply in national security and foreign policy contexts involving presidential authority. The coming term may clarify how textualism, Skidmore, and the major questions doctrine will operate in the post-Chevron administrative state.

Danica Patrick said she “had a moment” after confronting fans who booed her at Pocono Raceway when she did not sign an autograph for a man restrained by security. She said her job is to drive and communicate with her crew chief, not sign autographs, and that the boos hurt her feelings. The incident sparked debate among NASCAR drivers. Kevin Harvick said signing autographs is fully part of a driver’s job and responsibility. Ryan Blaney said it is not part of the job but is something drivers should do, especially for kids. Dale Earnhardt Jr. said the incident reflected poorly on Patrick and that interacting with fans can provide encouragement after disappointing performances.

Alabama leads Vanderbilt in the third quarter of a Week 6 SEC matchup featuring multiple scoring plays, turnovers, sacks, penalties, punts and field goals. Ty Simpson threw touchdown passes to Germie Bernard and Ryan Williams but also had his first interception of the season. Diego Pavia led Vanderbilt drives, including a touchdown pass to Sedrick Alexander, while Alexander also scored on a 65-yard run. The preview frames the game as important for playoff positioning, highlighting Vanderbilt’s 5-0 start, Alabama’s rebound after a Florida State loss, and the quarterback matchup between Pavia and Simpson.

Scale-in trading is a planned strategy of gradually building a position as more entry opportunities appear, aiming to improve average entry price or manage execution. Retail investors may use it to buy as prices fall, often through dollar-cost averaging, while day and swing traders may add to winning positions. Institutional traders use scaling in to fill large orders without causing major price impact or attracting front-running.

The strategy requires discipline and differs from double-down or Martingale methods, which add to losing trades in attempts to recover losses. Scaling out is the opposite approach, gradually exiting a position to lock in profits while leaving room for further gains.

Benefits include lower average entry prices, reduced slippage, and more efficient risk use. Risks include incomplete position building before a reversal or losses if the market reverses after adding to a winning trade. The passage states that a backtest showed lower CAGR but improved risk-adjusted performance when using a scale-in approach.

This multicenter prospective registry study evaluated whether the German 17-item Speech, Spatial and Qualities of Hearing Scale (SSQ17) can assess hearing loss-related quality of life in unilateral Menière’s disease. Ninety-seven patients meeting definite, probable, or Menière’s characteristics criteria underwent vestibular assessment, MRI exclusion of retrocochlear causes, pure-tone and speech audiometry, and SSQ17 testing.

Hearing loss was asymmetric and worse in affected ears, with mean 4PTA of 51.9 dB HL versus 19.3 dB HL in unaffected ears, and monosyllabic speech recognition of 33.9% versus 86.6%. The SSQ17 mean total score was 6.0, with subscale means of 5.3 for speech hearing, 5.1 for spatial hearing, and 7.2 for qualities of hearing. Internal consistency was excellent, with Cronbach’s alpha of 0.960 for the total score and 0.904–0.956 across subscales. SSQ17 scores correlated negatively with affected-ear pure-tone thresholds and positively with speech recognition scores. The study concluded that SSQ17 is a viable patient-reported tool for assessing hearing-related burden in advanced listening conditions in patients with Menière’s disease.

This retrospective single-center cohort study evaluated predictors of rebleeding in adults admitted to Rennes University Hospital for aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage between 2020 and 2022. Among 226 included patients, 33 (15%) experienced rebleeding. Previously reported risk factors such as systolic blood pressure, aneurysm size, aneurysm location, WFNS and Fisher grades, and intracerebral or intraventricular hematoma did not significantly differ between patients with and without rebleeding in baseline comparisons.

In univariate analysis, only time since first symptoms was associated with rebleeding risk; each additional hour increased the odds by 0.7%. This association remained significant in multivariate analysis, where WFNS score was also an independent predictor. Rebleeding patients had longer mean time to event than non-rebleeding patients, and two-thirds of rebleeding events occurred more than 24 hours after symptom onset. Patients secured within 24 hours had fewer rebleeding events than those treated later. Prognosis at 1 and 6 months did not significantly differ between groups, though more patients without rebleeding had GOS 5 scores at 6 months.

The study concludes that elapsed time since headache onset is a significant risk factor for rebleeding and supports prompt aneurysm securing in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage.

The passage examines calendar effects in long-term Treasuries using the TLT ETF, which tracks 20-year Treasury bonds, over a test period from 2004 to August 2021. It states that TLT prices move inversely to interest rates. The article identifies two main effects: weak performance during the first seven trading days of the month and stronger returns during the rest of the month. A combined strategy using long positions around the end/rest of the month and short positions during the first seven trading days produced higher annual returns and lower drawdowns than buy and hold in the backtest. The passage also mentions that full Python code and related trading strategy rules are provided.

This scoping review examines inflammation and anti-inflammatory strategies in depression, focusing on randomized controlled trials and related animal studies. The passage describes evidence linking depression with elevated inflammatory markers and neuroinflammatory pathways, including NLRP3, NF-κB, and P2X7R, and reviews pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions that may modulate these pathways.

The literature review identified 31 animal studies on neuroinflammatory target-based treatments. Pharmacological interventions included Empagliflozin, calcitriol, brexpiprazole with fluoxetine, antiretroviral approaches, progesterone, nutritional supplements, and natural extracts. Non-pharmacological interventions included acupuncture, exercise, and photobiomodulation. These studies generally reported improvements in depressive-like behaviours and neuroinflammation, but most were short-term, small-scale, and not yet clinically transferable.

The scoping review searched PubMed and included randomized controlled trials involving anti-inflammatory strategies for depression. Eleven studies published between 2008 and 2024 were included, covering 907 patients, mostly with major depressive disorder. Treatments included fluoxetine, infliximab, ketamine, minocycline, vortioxetine plus celecoxib, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, glycopyrrolate, and lacquer tree. Treatment durations ranged from 2 to 18 weeks. Inflammatory markers assessed included CRP, hs-CRP, sTNFR1, sTNFR2, IL-2, IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β, IFN-γ, and others.

The review found that anti-inflammatory strategies may improve depressive symptoms in some patients, particularly those with elevated inflammatory markers. However, responses varied substantially between patients, and drug safety, unclear biomarker selection, high testing costs, and limited generalisability were major challenges. The passage notes that current studies often rely on traditional depression rating scales and lack clear definitions or standardized approaches to measuring inflammation.

The authors conclude that pharmacological anti-inflammatory strategies for depression currently have limited research value and poor feasibility. They suggest future work should focus more on non-pharmacological anti-inflammatory approaches, such as exercise and positive thinking, and on low-cost, generalisable research designs. The passage also discusses potential future roles for artificial intelligence and micro-robots in monitoring inflammation and supporting personalized depression treatment.

On Nov. 29, 2001, multiple reports described Enron nearing what could become the largest bankruptcy reorganization after Dynegy abandoned its takeover and credit agencies cut Enron to junk status. Senate Majority Leader Tom Daschle called for Congress to investigate Enron’s collapse and its broader energy-sector implications. Enron’s European operations entered administration, trading platforms and exchanges restricted or suspended Enron activity, and EnronOnline reopened only to help counterparties unwind positions. Energy, metals, derivatives, bond, bank, office real estate, foreign exchange, and international asset markets reacted to Enron’s troubles, though some U.S. power and gas markets remained orderly. Companies and banks disclosed exposures ranging from tens of millions to hundreds of millions of dollars, while analysts anticipated complex bankruptcy issues involving derivatives, creditors, overseas assets, and possible asset sales, including Enron Metals.

Digital laggards often struggle to connect goals to strategy, leading employees to deprioritize unclear objectives and causing misalignment. A data-driven culture can improve vertical alignment by linking metrics and objectives to company goals, and horizontal alignment through common data models and transparent access that support collaboration.

Digital leaders emphasize data culture as central, using learning mindsets, transparent data access, clear metrics, and organizational alignment. In these firms, culture aligns leadership beliefs, company values, and employee behavior. Digital laggards may recognize the importance of data culture but face entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient leadership focus.

Transformation is possible, as some digital leaders have successfully changed or are changing their cultures, though even mature organizations continue to face tensions. Strong data cultures depend on beliefs in learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement being reflected in values and daily practices.

Organizations often fall into four patterns: data novices, which lack cultural and system support; insight ready firms, which accept risk but lack advanced capabilities; tech enabled firms, which have technology but lack experimentation; and data reliant firms, which may overuse data in ways that discourage critical thinking.

A Seattle Public Utilities study found that extreme, long-lasting rainstorms have become more common and more intense in Seattle over the past 15 years, though typical drizzle and short showers have not changed much. SPU uses rainfall data from 17 gauges across the city to plan drainage and sewage infrastructure. The study found that rainfall amounts once considered once-in-a-century events can now be expected more often, such as 4 inches in 24 hours now projected once every 25 years, while the new once-in-a-century 24-hour standard exceeds 5 inches.

Residents and workers described noticing more persistent heavy rain, including impacts on construction. SPU officials said the findings matter for flood prevention and environmental protection, especially because Seattle’s drainage and wastewater systems were designed for a less intense rainfall pattern. Future infrastructure projects will use the updated rainfall data. Officials also linked the findings to climate change and said the region should better prepare for flooding.

NVIDIA’s RTX Blackwell architecture introduces Mega Geometry, which uses triangle clusters, CLAS, GPU-driven batched APIs, and PTLAS to reduce BVH construction and management overhead, support high object counts, and accelerate techniques such as subdivision surfaces. Blackwell RT Cores add hardware cluster engines, compression, up to 2x ray-triangle intersection rate versus third-generation RT Cores, and reduced VRAM use.

Blackwell adds hardware support for Linear Swept Spheres for strands such as hair and fur, offering about 2x faster rendering and about 5x lower VRAM use than DOTS in common hair rendering cases. SER 2.0 improves shader execution reordering efficiency and precision, while the AI Management Processor offloads GPU context scheduling from the CPU to reduce latency and improve workload coordination.

Video and display updates include hardware 4:2:2 encode/decode support, ninth-generation NVENC with improved AV1 and HEVC quality, AV1 Ultra High Quality mode, improved NVDEC, and DisplayPort 2.1b with up to 80 Gbps bandwidth. Blackwell Max-Q improvements include advanced power gating, accelerated frequency switching, faster low-latency sleep, and potential power savings such as up to 50% in a small language model inference example.

DLSS 4 adds Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three additional frames per rendered frame, with a faster, lower-VRAM AI model and enhanced Flip Metering. It also introduces transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving temporal stability, detail in motion, lighting detail, and artifact reduction.

Blackwell supports neural shaders through Cooperative Vectors APIs for DX12 and Vulkan, enabling Tensor Core access from graphics shaders. Described neural techniques include RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. The passage also outlines GB202, GB203, and GB205 GPU configurations and associated GeForce RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, and 5070 products, followed by NVIDIA warranty, liability, and trademark notices.

The passage outlines the 1942 Foreign Relations volume arrangement and lists Belgium-related materials, including U.S.-Belgian mutual aid and military service agreements. The passage describes a vehicle driving assistance system using cameras and/or sensors such as radar, lidar, LADAR, and ultrasonic sensors to detect surrounding vehicles, objects, lanes, and available space. It can operate in driver assistance or autonomous modes, use decision logic or algorithms to select maneuvers, integrate adaptive cruise control limits, and communicate via vehicle-to-vehicle or vehicle-to-infrastructure systems.

Mapbox, which provides mapping data for apps rather than making its own mapping app, announced partnerships with Microsoft, ARM and Intel’s Mobileye to expand into self-driving car technology. Its tools help car computers identify road features such as lanes, speed limits, pedestrians and signs. Microsoft Azure will process camera data to improve navigation algorithms, ARM will optimize detection speed on its chips, and Mobileye data will be delivered to cars efficiently to provide a 200-meter map ahead as sensor backup.

NVIDIA filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2015. Quarterly revenue was $1.153 billion, up from $1.103 billion a year earlier, while net income fell to $26 million from $128 million. Six-month revenue was $2.304 billion, up from $2.206 billion, and net income was $160 million, down from $265 million. Gross margin was 55.0% for the quarter and 55.8% for the six months.

The GPU segment generated $959 million in quarterly revenue, up 9%, driven mainly by high-end GeForce gaming GPUs. Tegra Processor revenue declined 19% to $128 million, reflecting lower OEM smartphone and tablet sales, partly offset by automotive growth, development services, and SHIELD devices. Licensing and other revenue was $66 million.

Operating expenses rose to $558 million for the quarter, including $89 million in restructuring and other charges related to winding down Icera modem operations after no viable buyer was found. NVIDIA expects an additional $15 million to $25 million in restructuring charges during the rest of fiscal 2016, affecting about 5% of its workforce. Income tax expense included a $27 million deferred tax asset write-down related to Icera, partly offset by a $13 million tax benefit.

NVIDIA announced a voluntary recall of SHIELD 8-inch tablets sold between July 2014 and July 2015 due to battery overheating risk and recorded a $21 million warranty-related charge. The company began construction of a new Santa Clara headquarters under an off-balance-sheet operating lease arrangement, with banks committed to fund up to $380 million.

As of July 26, 2015, NVIDIA had $435 million in cash and cash equivalents, $4.070 billion in marketable securities, total assets of $6.979 billion, long-term debt of $1.399 billion, and shareholders’ equity of $4.185 billion. Operating activities provided $409 million in cash during the six months. NVIDIA returned $452 million to shareholders in the quarter through dividends and an accelerated share repurchase agreement.

The filing also describes ongoing patent litigation involving NVIDIA, Samsung, and Qualcomm, while a prior securities class action was concluded after the Supreme Court denied plaintiffs’ petition.

The Seventh Circuit reversed the district court’s dismissal of a putative class action challenging Illinois counties’ bail fee practices and remanded for further proceedings. Six former arrestees from Kane and DuPage Counties alleged they were required to pay bond fees as a condition of release, in violation of the Eighth and Fourteenth Amendments under § 1983. The court held that the named plaintiffs had standing to pursue individual claims against Kane and DuPage because they alleged monetary injury traceable to county policy and redressable by suit.

The court also held that the putative class claims against Kane and DuPage should not have been dismissed without a Rule 23 analysis. As to the other 17 counties, the court found that plaintiffs might be able to proceed if class certification requirements are met, because the counties’ practices arose under the same state statute and may be “juridically linked.” The court left Rule 23 issues, related litigation effects, and the scope of any class action for the district court on remand.

The Marin Nail Trail 6 is a £1100 29in trail hardtail with a 6061 hydroformed aluminium frame, 120mm RockShox Recon fork, SRAM GX 1x11 drivetrain with Sunrace 11-42 cassette, Shimano Deore hydraulic brakes, Formula hubs, Marin 30mm rims, and Schwalbe tyres. It uses mixed internal and external cable routing, includes dropper post routing and twin bottle mounts, and has size-specific wheel options.

The review describes the XL 29in model as roomy, comfortable for an aluminium hardtail, and stable, with predictable handling and a solid riding position. The frame is praised for compliance, traction, mud clearance, and upgrade potential. The reviewer found it enjoyable for daily riding, local trails, singletrack, and casual riding, concluding that it is a fun, capable bike with smart components and a ride that encourages frequent use.

The passage presents a solid-state near-infrared-to-visible photon upconversion system based on triplet-triplet annihilation in an organic bulk-heterojunction architecture. The system uses DIB-SQ as an electron donor and PCBM as a fullerene acceptor to form a NIR-sensitive sensitizer layer, combined with rubrene or DBP-doped rubrene as the annihilator/photoemitter layer. The work treats triplet charge-transfer states in DIB-SQ:PCBM, usually considered loss channels in photovoltaics, as useful intermediates for generating rubrene triplets.

By varying the DIB-SQ:PCBM ratio, the authors found that a 1:3 blend optimized triplet sensitization and upconverted emission. The DIB-SQ:PCBM/rubrene system emitted in the 550–650 nm range under 690 nm excitation, while neat DIB-SQ or PCBM sensitizer layers performed poorly. DBP doping shifted emission to about 605 nm and improved performance through singlet energy harvesting from rubrene. The DIB-SQ:PCBM (1:3)/rubrene:DBP device achieved an upconversion quantum yield of 1.36% at irradiation intensities above 69.7 mW/cm², with a threshold intensity of 60.5 mW/cm².

Time-resolved photoluminescence and transient absorption measurements showed that charge-transfer states, molecular triplets in PCBM, and rubrene triplet states participate in the upconversion mechanism. The proposed pathway involves singlet exciton formation in the sensitizer, charge separation, formation of singlet and triplet charge-transfer states, triplet energy transfer to rubrene either directly or via PCBM triplets, and subsequent triplet-triplet annihilation producing visible emission. Magnetic-field-dependent photoluminescence supported the role of triplet-triplet annihilation in the upconverted emission.

The study concludes that fullerene-based bulk heterojunctions can be engineered to use charge-transfer-state recombination for sensitized triplet generation, enabling solid-state NIR photon upconversion with potential relevance to optoelectronic devices and photon imaging.

In Vredenburg et al. v. Behan et al., the plaintiff-appellee moved to dismiss a devolutive appeal, arguing that the transcript and clerk’s certificate were incomplete, not all parties or heirs of a deceased defendant were cited, and some appellants had acquiesced in the judgment. The Court held that three partial transcripts filed under the same docket number, with the clerk certifying that together they contained all proceedings, evidence, and documents, substantially complied with the law. It also held that appellants need not name every appellee in the appeal petition if they request citation of appellees, since citation is the clerk’s duty. The alleged acquiescence of some appellants did not defeat the appeal rights of those who had not acquiesced, and any issue regarding the deceased defendant’s heirs did not warrant dismissal. The motion to dismiss was denied, with costs.

San Diego Unified School District rescinded a resolution inviting Education Secretary Betsy DeVos to visit after objections from the San Diego Education Association, parents, and community partners. The union criticized DeVos’s support for vouchers and charter management organizations. Board president Richard Barrera, who had co-sponsored the resolution, withdrew support and said public education supporters should oppose DeVos’s ideology.

The passage also notes protests against DeVos at a Washington, D.C. school, which American Federation of Teachers president Randi Weingarten said she did not condone while still urging DeVos to visit public schools. DeVos’s confirmation drew opposition from multiple groups and required Vice President Mike Pence to break a Senate tie. At a White House listening session with parents and teachers from various school settings, President Trump praised DeVos and promoted school choice, while DeVos said she wanted to listen and learn how to ensure equal access to quality education.

The Woodland Trust’s Nature’s Calendar has recorded 42 spring indicators at over 1,000 UK locations in 2017, including snowdrops, hazel catkins and song thrush singing. Fewer sightings than 2016 are linked to colder January temperatures, though records remain valuable for monitoring climate change impacts on wildlife.

Victor Wembanyama used the offseason to recover and transform physically and mentally after a serious right shoulder diagnosis. He trained at a Shaolin temple in China, played soccer abroad, hosted events in France, visited NASA, worked with Kevin Garnett, and held fan supporter tryouts in San Antonio. He also trained with Hakeem Olajuwon, developing new post moves and a variation of the “Dream Shake.” Wembanyama said the traumatic medical experience shaped his summer and that he is now ready to return to basketball.

Kimberly Kirkwood forwarded a chain email on Dec. 12, 2000, wishing recipients a happy holiday and saying it was a fun message to pass around. The forwarded message claims wishes will come true after scrolling and forwarding it, includes anecdotal examples, and warns of bad luck if not sent onward.

U.S. chargé Denby reported the Korea situation as critical, with hostilities imminent, while China sought peaceful diplomatic action and requested great-power support to urge Japan to withdraw troops from Korea. Denby relayed requests from British minister O’Conor and Viceroy Li but declined to act without proper Chinese request. Sill reported Admiral’s departure left him in a perilous position after promising the Korean King asylum; Gresham replied that the U.S. could not intervene forcibly and had not advised Korea to protest. Denby later noted little change, possible Japanese troop transport preparations, a Japanese audience with China’s Emperor, and Li’s request for a military loan. Sill reported no fighting because no new Chinese troops had arrived, while Japan had about 15,000 troops and 3,000 coolies in Korea, using merchant vessels as transports. He noted generally orderly Japanese conduct, one incident involving British representatives, and Otori’s reform demands as the chief development.

Tesla’s 2017 Form 10-K describes the company as a vertically integrated sustainable energy business that designs, manufactures, sells, installs and services fully electric vehicles, energy storage products and solar energy systems. Its vehicle products include Model S, Model X and Model 3, with future plans for commercial EVs, Tesla Semi and a new Roadster. Energy products include Powerwall 2, Powerpack 2, solar systems and Solar Roof.

Tesla sells vehicles through company-owned stores, galleries, service centers and online channels, and operates Supercharger and Destination Charging networks. It manufactures vehicles and components mainly in Fremont, Lathrop, Tilburg and Gigafactory 1 near Reno, while energy storage products are made at Gigafactory 1 and solar products at Fremont and Gigafactory 2 in Buffalo. The company reported 37,543 full-time employees as of December 31, 2017.

The filing outlines Tesla’s technologies in battery packs, power electronics, dual-motor powertrains, vehicle software, autopilot and self-driving development, energy storage integration and solar system design. It also describes financing, warranty and service programs for vehicles, solar systems and energy storage products.

Tesla identifies major risks including production and launch delays, especially for Model 3, dependence on single-source suppliers, challenges scaling manufacturing and deliveries, consumer adoption of electric vehicles, Gigafactory 1 ramp risks, product defects, battery safety concerns, material cost volatility, product liability claims, regulatory limits, and intense competition in vehicles, energy storage and solar energy.

IGP Ibrahim Idris warned Ekiti police officers not to aid politicians in manipulating results during the July 14, 2018 governorship election, saying their duty is to protect voters, observers and election materials. Represented by ACP Abayomi Shogunle, he urged the public to report officers involved in rigging and warned that misconduct could lead to dismissal and legal action. Idris reminded officers that some policemen accused of misbehaving in the 2014 Ekiti election had been punished. The passage also notes that protesting policemen in Maiduguri accused Idris of corruption, inhumane treatment and selling promotions.

Nearly 600 SUNY Oneonta students and staff attended a memorial service for Daniel William Michaels, 18, who died Dec. 3. The service included readings, shared condolences for his family, and noted more than $17,000 raised for a scholarship in his name.

State Bar of Michigan e-Journal for May 23, 2001 listed case summaries in bankruptcy, civil rights, constitutional law, criminal law, employment, family law, insurance, litigation, municipal law, negligence, and real property, plus classifieds, fields-of-practice listings, news, archived journals, contacts, and bar events.

Key decisions included: In re Hood held TSAC was not immune in a bankruptcy dischargeability action; Thakur affirmed summary disposition in a racial discrimination claim; several criminal cases affirmed convictions or addressed discovery, suppression, lost evidence, and counsel claims; Slawick affirmed a defamation verdict for a former employee; three family law cases affirmed termination of parental rights; Van Reken reversed insurance recovery for land contract vendors; Moton affirmed striking a supplemental witness list; Domine reinstated a zoning board’s variance denial; Berry applied the fireman’s rule; Garrison affirmed dismissal of negligence claims against a hospital; and Girard applied the open and obvious doctrine.

The issue also included fields-of-practice attorney listings, classified ads for services and positions, and bar events on Social Security disability and probate planning.

The Fresh Market Inc. named Yvonne Cowser Yancy senior vice president and chief human resources officer. Yancy brings over 20 years of HR experience in public and private sectors, including roles at Fortune 500 companies and as Atlanta’s HR commissioner. She will oversee HR and benefits functions, including talent acquisition, organizational development, training, compensation, and wellness. Yancy holds degrees from Georgia State and Northwestern and serves on civic and nonprofit boards.

Insurance Australia Group shares continued falling after a drop of over 4%, reaching $8.07 in morning trade. The decline is linked to concerns from the Royal Commission into financial services misconduct, which has highlighted scandals in the insurance sector, though no findings specifically involve IAG. An AFR report noted possible malpractice and the unexplained leave of general counsel Chris Bertuch. Despite volatility, IAG recently made a $525 million sale agreement and reported a positive half-year result with a 7.7% dividend increase.

The passage describes power, reset, clocking, interrupt, debug, and peripheral features for TI DM8127/DM814x DaVinci digital media processors. Core logic voltage domains support independently selectable operating performance points with dynamic voltage frequency scaling; adaptive voltage scaling is described but not supported. SRAM blocks can enter shutdown to reduce leakage, losing stored data. The device supports selectable I/O voltages, PHY power-down modes, low-power standby, required supply sequencing, decoupling and filtering recommendations, and reset behaviors including power-on, warm, watchdog, software, test, local, PCIe isolation, and EMAC switch isolation resets.

Clocking is generated from reference clocks, PLLs, dividers, SYSCLKs, and module clocks. DEV and AUX clocks may use crystals or 1.8-V LVCMOS inputs; SERDES requires a low-jitter differential clock; optional audio and 32768-Hz clocks are supported. The device includes multiple PLLs with bypass mode after reset and specified frequency constraints.

The passage also outlines interrupt handling by the ARM Cortex-A8 AINTC and C674x DSP interrupt controller, timing measurement assumptions, transition-level guidance, and board-routing considerations. Peripheral sections summarize DCAN, EDMA, advanced event triggering, trace, JTAG, EMAC switch and MDIO, GPIO, GPMC/ELM, NAND/NOR timing, and HDMI transmitter capabilities and PCB layout guidelines.
Japanese government bond prices fell as U.S. Treasuries retreated and markets awaited the Bank of Japan’s April bond-buying plans, with some expecting reduced purchases of shorter-dated JGBs.

Ángel Bracero sued S. Ramírez & Co. for injuries caused when bags of rice fell on him in a Ponce shop. The defendant argued it did not own or control the shop and that Bracero was a workman limited to a compensation claim. The court found Bracero was an independent contractor and that evidence supported the defendant’s control of a Ponce branch. However, the Supreme Court reversed the judgment, holding that res ipsa loquitur did not apply because others, including the plaintiff and workmen, had handled the pile, and that the record showed no negligence attributable to the defendant at the time of the accident. Chief Justice Del Toro dissented, concluding the trial court’s findings were supported by evidence that the pile was defectively built, the defendant had been warned, and its negligence caused the injury.

The passage reports that the S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July and 7.8% year to date, though it fell 1.6% on the first day of August. Market momentum is described as intact, with medium- and long-term trend indicators healthy, but short-term technicals, volatility, credit spreads, and seasonal headwinds show early warning signs. WiseGuyReports announced the “Gonorrhea - Pipeline Review, H2 2017” report, covering therapeutics under development for gonorrhea, an infection caused by a sexually transmitted bacterium affecting males and females. The speaker clarifies that they meant the team likes its chances if it plays its best. They express confidence, pride in reaching a Stanley Cup Finals game with home-ice advantage, and say every shift matters. They emphasize preparation, leadership by example, and focusing on playing their game.

In 2011, Akamai, the world’s largest content delivery network, faced a localization challenge as local competitors gained share in non-U.S. markets and some major customers developed competing capabilities. Akamai operated a decentralized server network across 78 countries, serving major clients such as Apple, Amazon, Microsoft, Samsung, Netflix, and government agencies. Although 29% of revenue came from outside the United States, its market share declined in markets such as South Korea, China, and India.

Akamai’s globally set products, pricing, and sales targets often did not fit local market conditions. Local teams reported mismatches in customer needs, pricing pressure from lower-cost competitors, weak brand recognition, and operational issues such as ISP relationships. Examples included Japan rejecting a newly acquired mobile technology already available locally and South Korea showing Akamai’s weaker local competitiveness against CDNetworks.

In 2011, Akamai reorganized into business units and geographic theaters to improve coordination, clarify customer ownership, and address gaps between headquarters and local markets. Charley Dublin was tasked with helping determine where and how much Akamai needed to localize while preserving global processes needed to serve multinational customers.

Gold prices have risen more than 50% over the past year to record highs, driven by recession fears, macroeconomic and political uncertainty, lower-rate expectations, dollar weakness and central bank buying. Analysts expect prices to keep rising, pressuring jewelry companies that sell lower-priced gold products. Brands including Mejuri, Signet, BaubleBar, Alexis Bittar and Rowan are responding with price increases, gold-plated or demi-fine alternatives, supply-chain changes and other product adjustments. Executives said consumers remain price-sensitive, especially outside luxury markets, and some view the gold surge as a broader economic warning sign.

The passage presents an evolutionary hypergame framework for modeling situations where individuals have heterogeneous access to strategies. It extends the prisoner’s dilemma with voluntary participation to three strategies: cooperation, defection, and loner. Players may possess different subsets of these strategies, producing asymmetric strategic contexts despite a symmetric payoff structure.

The model uses two timescales. On the fast timescale, players interact repeatedly and update strategies through introspection dynamics, where higher introspection strength means payoffs more strongly guide decisions. This process is formulated as a Markov chain with a stationary distribution used to compute average payoffs between strategy sets. On the slow timescale, strategy sets evolve through payoff-based competition, modeled in well-mixed and spatially structured populations.

Tournament analyses show that under weak introspection, strategy sets involving defection or loner behavior often perform best. As introspection strength and benefit-to-cost ratios increase, the strategy set {C, L} becomes increasingly competitive. Theoretical analysis explains this by showing that {C, L} supports self-reciprocal cooperation in self-play and helps players avoid exploitation by defectors through switching to loner behavior.

Evolutionary simulations confirm these patterns. In well-mixed populations with three strategy sets, weak introspection favors {D, L}, while strong introspection leads to dominance by {C, L}. With all seven possible strategy sets, weak introspection favors {L}, but stronger introspection shifts dominance toward {C, L}. In spatial populations, similar transitions occur, though intermediate regimes may include coexistence or temporary dominance by {C}.

The study concludes that heterogeneous strategy access and introspection dynamics substantially reshape evolutionary outcomes. Higher introspection promotes cooperation, while weak introspection favors defection or abstention. The framework allows strategies and strategy sets to co-evolve and is proposed as a general approach for studying cooperation in heterogeneous populations.

The study assessed ex vivo susceptibility of Ugandan Plasmodium falciparum isolates to nine antimalarial drugs from July 2019 to June 2024, with genotyping of candidate resistance genes. Of 1,297 isolates collected in eastern and northern Uganda, 1,114 were successfully evaluated. Most commonly used antimalarials remained potent at low nanomolar concentrations, while pyrimethamine activity was poor. From 2016 to 2024, susceptibility increased for chloroquine but decreased for dihydroartemisinin, lumefantrine, and mefloquine, with stronger changes in eastern Uganda. PfCRT K76T and PfMDR1 N86Y resistance mutations were rare, while SP-resistance mutations remained common. PfK13 C469Y and A675V mutations were prevalent in northern Uganda and increasing in eastern Uganda, and were associated with decreased susceptibility to dihydroartemisinin and lumefantrine. The clinical implications of these modest susceptibility decreases are uncertain, but continued parasitological and genomic surveillance and policy measures to limit resistance and treatment failure are prioritized.

InVirtuoGen is proposed as a continuous-time discrete flow model operating directly on fragmented SMILES for fragment-based drug discovery. It aims to address limitations of autoregressive and masked diffusion approaches by refining all sequence positions simultaneously rather than completing tokens in a fixed or masked order. The method extends SAFE-style fragmented SMILES with explicit attachment points, BRICS-based decomposition, random fragment shuffling, and atomic-level tokenization.

The model uses a discrete flow framework with a diffusion transformer backbone and a time-weighted training loss. It is evaluated on de novo generation, fragment-constrained generation, PMO target property optimization, and lead optimization, using pretraining datasets comparable to GenMol and SAFE-GPT.

For de novo generation, InVirtuoGen achieves a stronger quality-diversity Pareto frontier than GenMol and SAFE-GPT, with performance improving at finer simulation time steps. In fragment-constrained tasks, it shows competitive average quality and diversity and higher uniqueness, but lower validity than GenMol. The paper also introduces a hybrid optimization framework combining a genetic algorithm with PPO adapted to discrete flows, using full-sequence inputs to support recombination and refinement.

Blackwell adds SER 2.0 with more efficient reordering logic, an AI Management Processor to schedule GPU contexts and reduce CPU dependency, and new video features including hardware 4:2:2 encode/decode support. The lecture reviews Wald’s equality, stopping trials, and generalized stopping trials, emphasizing that stopping decisions must depend only on observed past variables. Wald’s equality applies to IID variables and relates the expected stopped sum to the mean increment times the expected stopping trial.

The professor applies Wald’s equality to renewal theory by defining \(J=N(t)+1\), the first arrival after time \(t\), since \(N(t)\) itself is not a stopping trial. This yields bounds used in the elementary renewal theorem, which states that \(\lim_{t\to\infty} E[N(t)]/t = 1/\bar X\). The proof requires truncation arguments because the residual life can be poorly behaved.

Generalized stopping trials are introduced for paired variables such as interarrival and service times. This framework is used for G/G/1 queues, where arrivals to an empty system begin new busy periods and form embedded renewal points, provided the system empties with probability 1.

Little’s theorem is then derived as an accounting identity: the time integral of the number in the system equals the sum of customer waiting times. In the limit, the time-average number in the system equals the arrival rate times the average waiting time.

Finally, the Pollaczek-Khinchin formula for M/G/1 queues is discussed. For Poisson arrivals and IID service times, the expected waiting time in queue is \(\lambda \overline{V^2}/[2(1-\rho)]\), where \(\rho=\lambda\bar V\). The lecture explains how service-time variability and traffic intensity affect queueing delay.

The passage presents a study claiming generation and detection of magnetic monopoles on the surface of 3D topological insulators using STM/STS. It explains that topological magnetoelectric effects can induce magnetic responses from electric fields in topological insulators, but direct detection has been difficult due to field-generation and characterization challenges.

The authors propose using image potential states (IPS), Rydberg-like energy levels formed near surfaces under STM field-emission conditions, to probe monopole-induced magnetic fields. A radially distributed electric field from the STM tip is argued to generate circulating Hall currents at interfaces where the topological parameter changes, producing effective magnetic monopoles in 3D topological insulators. These monopoles interact with IPS orbital magnetic moments, causing Zeeman-like splitting of IPS energy levels.

Experiments were performed on Bi phases grown on Si(111): topologically trivial √3-Bi, 2D topological Bi(110), and 3D higher-order topological Bi(111). IPS peaks on √3-Bi and Bi(110) followed Gaussian profiles and showed decreasing linewidth with increasing principal quantum number. On Bi(111), IPS peaks with n > 1 broadened and split, especially the n = 2 peak. The authors rule out alternative explanations including symmetric/antisymmetric IPS series, quantum well states, and quantum-dot confinement.

The observed IPS splitting on Bi(111) was fitted with a model in which orbital angular momentum levels split under a monopole-generated magnetic field. The splitting energy’s dependence on quantum number and tunneling current was consistent with the proposed theoretical relationships. Increasing tunneling current, interpreted as increasing tip electric field, continuously modulated the IPS splitting.

The authors conclude that the STM-induced electric field generated and manipulated magnetic monopole singularity fields on a 3D topological insulator surface, and that IPS splitting provides evidence for their detection.

Blackwell adds hardware encode/decode support for 4:2:2 chroma-sampled H.264 and HEVC video, complementing prior 4:4:4 and 4:2:0 support. YUV 4:2:2 retains full luminance and half chrominance information, requiring two-thirds the data of 4:4:4 while offering twice the color resolution of 4:2:0, benefiting HDR, text, fine lines, and color grading workflows.

Blackwell’s ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR, adds 4:2:2 H.264/HEVC encoding, and introduces AV1 Ultra High Quality mode for an additional 5% improvement. The RTX 5090 supports up to three encoders and two decoders, increasing export speeds by over 50% versus the prior generation and 4x versus RTX 3090. Its sixth-generation NVDEC provides 2x faster H.264 decoding and 4:2:2 H.264/HEVC decode support. Blackwell also supports DisplayPort 2.1b with up to 80 Gbps bandwidth, enabling 8K at 165Hz and 4K at 480Hz with DSC.

Blackwell Max-Q improves power efficiency through advanced power gating, faster clock gating, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, accelerated frequency switching, and low-latency sleep. Clocks can adjust 1000x faster than previous architectures, and the deepest sleep state is entered 10x faster than Ada, enabling up to 50% power savings in a small language model inference example.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three additional frames per rendered frame. Its new frame generation model is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and runs once per rendered frame. Blackwell also uses enhanced Flip Metering in the display engine for frame pacing. DLSS 4 adopts transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving temporal stability, reducing ghosting, enhancing lighting detail, and increasing detail in motion.

Blackwell introduces developer-created neural shaders, enabled by Cooperative Vectors APIs for DX12 and Vulkan and differentiable shading features in Slang. Neural shader applications include neural texture compression, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. These techniques use AI to approximate complex rendering, compress textures, infer indirect lighting, model subsurface scattering, and generate more natural-looking faces in real time.

The Blackwell GPU family includes GB202, GB203, and GB205. GB202 contains 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, and 768 Tensor cores. GB203 contains 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, and 336 Tensor cores. An inside day occurs when today’s high is lower than yesterday’s high and today’s low is higher than yesterday’s low, meaning all price action falls within the prior day’s range. It can appear on different time frames but is most common on daily bars and varies by market, with frequent occurrences in markets such as oil and gold. The opposite is an outside day, which has both a higher high and lower low than the previous day.

The passage states that backtests show inside days alone are poor trading signals and do not reliably predict future movement. In the S&P 500 ETF SPY, inside days occurred about 10% of the time since 1993. Adding filters such as a five-day RSI below 50 improved average gain but still did not create a strongly tradable strategy. A swing trading variation produced 89 trades since 1993 with an average gain of 0.45% and a profit factor of 2.1, but it worked only in equity markets and not in gold. The conclusion is that inside days require additional variables to be useful in a trading strategy.

Heating oil is a low-viscosity crude oil product used mainly for heating buildings and is a highly seasonal commodity because demand rises in winter. Heating oil futures are contracts to buy or sell a specified quantity at a future date and trade on ICE Futures Europe and CME. ICE contracts use symbol UHO and are cash-settled; CME contracts use symbol HO and are physically delivered.

A heating oil futures strategy uses technical and fundamental analysis, position sizing, and risk management to trade price movements. A backtest cited in the passage produced 168 trades, an average profit of $370 per trade, a 2.02 profit factor, and a 59% win rate. The passage also notes heating oil has historically performed better from February to August than during winter months.

Each contract represents 42,000 gallons, or 1,000 barrels. The minimum price fluctuation is $0.0001 per gallon, equal to $4.20 per contract. CME trading runs Sunday to Friday from 5 p.m. to 4 p.m. CT, while ICE trading runs from 1 a.m. to 11 p.m. London time. Trading terminates on the last business day of the month before the contract month.

Heating oil prices are affected by weather, crude oil prices, refinery capacity, and alternative heating fuel costs. Major risks include adverse leveraged price movements. The passage states the all-time high was $5.2215 per gallon in April 2022 and the all-time low was $0.2920 in February 1999. An ETF mentioned for heating oil exposure is WisdomTree’s HEAT ETF.

The passage argues that damages for the unlawful seizure and detention of the whaling ship Cape Horn Pigeon are direct losses, not speculative profits. Strength training can build muscle mass, strength and endurance, but poor technique, inadequate warm-ups or cool-downs, and increasing workout intensity too quickly can cause injuries. Common injuries include rotator cuff injuries, hamstring strains or tears, herniated discs, tendonitis, and tennis or golfer’s elbow. Prevention includes warming up, cooling down, using correct form, maintaining good posture, stretching, avoiding excessive repetitions or unsuitable weights, progressing gradually, and stopping if pain persists. Recovery may involve rest, hydration, diet, ice, compression, elevation, painkillers, physiotherapy, injections or surgery depending on the injury. A doctor should be consulted if pain or discomfort continues, and a qualified trainer can help create a safe strength-training programme.

The passage presents an extension of an ab initio approach for calculating spin diffusion length and spin lifetime to include electric-field-driven spin drift along periodic directions. The method uses a linearized density-matrix master equation with a covariant derivative formalism and Wannier-based finite differences to treat drift, scattering, diffusion, and coherent terms. It aims to accurately simulate electric-field effects on spin diffusion length beyond conventional drift-diffusion models, which may fail in systems with spatial spin precession. The paper outlines derivations of the steady-state transport equation, eigenvalue-based calculations of spin diffusion length, a new Rayleigh-Ritz-based model formula, and applications to monolayer WSe₂, bulk GaAs, bulk GaN, and graphene-h-BN.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPUs, including GA102 and GA104, build on Turing with higher performance and efficiency for graphics, ray tracing, AI, compute, and professional workloads. GA102 is used in the GeForce RTX 3090, RTX 3080, NVIDIA RTX A6000, and NVIDIA A40, while GA104 is used in the GeForce RTX 3070. A full GA102 GPU includes 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, 336 third-generation Tensor Cores, 28.3 billion transistors, and is fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm 8N NVIDIA Custom Process.

The GeForce RTX 3090 targets 8K HDR gaming and high-end creator workloads, the RTX 3080 delivers up to 2x GeForce RTX 2080 performance, and the RTX 3070 rivals the prior-generation RTX 2080 Ti. The RTX A6000 targets desktop visual computing, while the A40 targets data center visual computing, virtualization, rendering, simulation, AI, and compute workloads.

Appellant pled guilty to theft by receiving and financial transaction card theft and was sentenced to ten years’ probation with restitution. The court found no abuse of discretion in continuing the restitution hearing to secure victims. However, because appellant was not charged with the burglaries from which additional stolen items came, restitution could only cover damages from her charged offenses. The judgment was reversed and remanded for resentencing; remaining error was moot.

A Middlebury Public Safety officer falsely identified former student Addis Fouche-Channer ’17 as a participant in the March protest of Charles Murray’s lecture, leading to police and college inquiries and a disciplinary charge. Fouche-Channer denied being there and provided Wi-Fi logs, witness statements, class work, emails and phone activity data supporting her account; the college then dropped the hearing. She later filed a racial profiling complaint against the officer, prompting an internal investigation that remained unresolved as of publication. Fouche-Channer criticized the process as treating her as guilty despite evidence she was not at the protest. Officials and the officer did not respond to requests for comment, and the college said the decision was delayed.

The passage presents a framework for Vehicular Cloud Computing in 5G urban environments, aiming to assess feasibility, energy impact, CO2 savings, and incentive mechanisms. It proposes centralized task offloading using vehicles, a network operator, a controller, and cloud backup resources. The system collects vehicle beacons, ranks execution nodes by dwell time, energy, and capacity, and assigns tasks under deadline and capacity constraints. It defines delay, energy, and cost models for the network operator and executors, accounting for stochastic conditions such as mobility, network quality, and workload. Task allocation maximizes utility based on payments, costs, and deadline satisfaction using nominal estimates, while actual values are later reported. Revenue sharing is modeled through coalitional game theory, with stable payoff allocation among the network operator and selected executors under uncertainty.

Chamomile refers to plants long used as herbal remedies, with German chamomile (Matricaria recutita) and Roman chamomile widely grown. Matricaria recutita has been used in teas for fevers, flu, digestive disorders, and skin ailments. Its flower extract, chamomile or blue oil, contains medicinal compounds including coumarins, sesquiterpenes, polyacetylenes, and flavonoids, and is known for anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and spasmolytic properties. The oil is commonly obtained by steam distillation, though yields are low. It is used for relaxation, insomnia, mood enhancement, anxiety, aching joints and muscles, skin products, digestive issues, conjunctivitis symptoms, and commercial products such as soaps, perfumes, cosmetics, foods, and beverages.

America’s science education faces declining proficiency and interest despite growing STEM job opportunities. The passage argues that improving science teaching requires high-quality instructional materials and sustained curriculum-based professional learning, similar to the science of reading movement. It emphasizes inquiry-based, phenomenon-driven instruction in which students investigate, analyze data, construct explanations and solve relevant problems. Districts should adopt strong materials, support teachers in using them, provide planning time and ongoing training, and help school leaders prioritize effective implementation over immediate test results.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that on May 25, 2016 it announced plans to streamline its smartphone hardware business, reducing up to 1,850 positions, including 1,350 at Microsoft Mobile Oy in Finland. For the quarter ending June 30, 2016, Microsoft expects to record an impairment and restructuring charge of about $950 million, including about $200 million for severance. The actions are expected to be substantially complete by the end of calendar 2016 and fully complete by July 2017. The filing includes a related press release as Exhibit 99.1 and forward-looking statement disclaimers.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC dated November 7, 2018. The report states that Tesla published a blog post on its website, attached as Exhibit 99.1 and incorporated by reference. The filing was signed by Todd A. Maron, General Counsel, on November 7, 2018.

Exxon Mobil reported December-quarter earnings of 88 cents per share, below analyst expectations of $1.04, causing shares to fall 3% pre-market and reducing market cap by $10 billion. Annual earnings were $19.7 billion on $244.36 billion in revenue, including an estimated $5.9 billion tax-cut gain. CEO Darren Woods said Exxon would invest $50 billion in the U.S. over five years, while the dividend remained 77 cents. The article notes Exxon’s 2017 gains came largely from crude oil despite lower production, and future investment targets tripling Permian Basin output to 600,000 barrels per day. Risks include rising U.S. shale output and lower futures prices, though refining and chemical earnings rose. Goldman Sachs raised its oil price outlook, citing strong demand, Venezuela losses, and OPEC compliance.

This preprint presents a protocol for the Canadian Social Determinants Urban Laboratory (CSDUL), a multilevel, longitudinal virtual data environment designed to study how social determinants contribute to income-related health inequalities in urban Canada. The project is led through the Urban Public Health Network Research Group and is guided by the WHO Social Determinants of Health framework.

CSDUL will combine linked survey, administrative, registry, tax, environmental, socioeconomic, and government spending data within Statistics Canada Research Data Centres. Its initial observation window will be 2011–2017, with plans to expand as new data become available. The study will focus on Canadian cities and towns defined as census agglomerations or census metropolitan areas.

The project uses a hub-and-node structure. The central hub will assemble data and coordinate development, while five nodes will create and validate area-based indicators related to political and economic context, environmental context, socioeconomic context, material circumstances, and health systems. Individual-level variables will include demographics, income, health behaviours, comorbidities, health system access, and health history.

After developing CSDUL, the team will replicate WHO/Europe’s decomposition analysis of income-related inequalities in self-reported health for urban Canada. Self-reported health will be the primary outcome, with mental health and life satisfaction also examined. The analysis will estimate the relative contributions of different social determinants and levels of influence to health inequalities, using pooled multilevel logistic regression and Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition methods.

The authors state that CSDUL will support comparative, multilevel health equity research, reduce barriers to using complex linked data, and help identify determinants most strongly associated with health outcomes in Canadian urban populations.

A meta-analysis of studies involving 333,247 adults found moderate alcohol drinkers were less likely than abstainers or heavy drinkers to die of any cause, especially older adults, women and non-Latino white people. Moderate drinking did not reduce cancer mortality but was linked to about a quarter lower risk of death from heart disease or stroke. Heavy drinking and weekly binge drinking increased mortality, largely through higher cancer risk. Moderate drinking was defined as up to 14 servings weekly for men and up to seven for women. The study also found benefits varied by age, gender and ethnicity, with no mortality reduction among adults 18 to 39.

IWM is the iShares Russell 2000 ETF, tracking the Russell 2000 index and providing exposure to small-cap U.S. stocks. The Russell 2000 measures the 2,000 smallest companies in the Russell 3000 and is rebalanced annually in June. The passage describes a Russell 2000 rebalancing trading strategy, noting solid performance, possible hedging against the S&P 500, and diversification benefits because IWM can trend differently from the broader market.

Marcus Lemonis, CEO of Good Sam Club and Camping World, bought bankrupt Gander Mountain and is reopening 69 stores as Gander Outdoors. The passage criticizes his involvement with Good Sam and notes the Good Sam mascot has been repurposed for Gander Outdoors.

In January 1917, U.S. diplomats reported on wartime diplomacy and reactions to peace initiatives. Ambassador Page in Italy protested anti-American press activity and coal price controls; the Italian foreign minister defended fixed prices as necessary to continue the war and suggested the President might ask Germany to define its aims. Page also reported Vatican criticism of the Balfour note and concerns about alleged Allied plans expanding Russian influence in Europe and the Orient. The U.S. minister in Greece reported that a settlement was progressing satisfactorily and that the British minister hoped the blockade would soon be lifted. Minister Van Dyke in the Netherlands forwarded material concerning President Wilson’s December 18 peace note. Wilson’s January 1917 Senate address stated that the Central Powers had offered only a conference, while the Entente had given more definite peace conditions, bringing discussion closer to both ending the war and establishing an international concert to prevent future catastrophes.

Apple has reportedly stopped developing a cheaper, lighter Vision Pro headset and is shifting focus to lightweight AI smart glasses similar to Meta’s Ray-Bans. The Vision Pro, launched in 2024 at $3,500, has struggled due to its price, bulk, limited developer support, and unclear use case. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports Apple may still release an updated Vision Pro with a better chip, but executives privately view the device as overengineered. The article notes Meta and Google are pursuing smart glasses, but says there is still little evidence that many consumers want face-worn computers. While enterprise uses may exist, widespread consumer adoption remains unproven.

Cory Stillman said Doug Weight’s absence would be felt, but the team is resilient and has other centermen available. He emphasized creating more net traffic, pressuring the opposing goalie, refocusing after the last game, using the extra rest, playing physically, and preparing to win Saturday and close out the series.

Taylor Swift is credited as the sole songwriter on more than 60 songs, meaning she wrote the lyrics and melodies alone. Business Insider lists 67 such tracks across her career, including “Our Song,” “Love Story,” “Dear John,” “Red,” “Lover,” “My Tears Ricochet,” “Vigilante Shit,” “The Black Dog,” “Peter,” and “The Manuscript.”

The speaker says winning the Stanley Cup is the biggest accomplishment of his career but that he must continue proving himself. He reflects on being happy playing in Finland, though returning was a tough decision that paid off. During the final, he tried to stay level after a crucial goal because there was still work left. He admits feeling nervous early in the game and “faking” confidence through to the win. He calls the Conn Smythe Trophy an honor, while emphasizing the Stanley Cup as the main goal.

Public universities in Texas have directed faculty to review syllabi and course content for compliance with state and federal laws and executive orders, creating confusion over what content is prohibited. San Jacinto College said faculty were asked to ensure course materials align with state course manuals, and said it does not plan a formal ban on teaching transgender identity, though a faculty member later said faculty were verbally told not to teach about gender beyond the male-female binary. At Texas Tech’s Angelo State University, faculty received verbal and written directives amid confusion over whether pride flags, preferred names, pronouns or transgender identity topics were banned. Texas Tech’s chancellor told university leaders to comply with laws recognizing only male and female sexes. Texas A&M is also reviewing course content after actions related to a gender identity lecture. FIRE attorney Adam Steinbaugh said no state or federal law bars professors from teaching about transgender identity and called the directives voluntary censorship conflicting with the First Amendment.

Joe Hadzima introduces MIT’s “Nuts and Bolts of New Ventures and Business Plans,” a six-session course focused on planning and executing new ventures rather than producing a fixed business plan. He explains that the approach applies to businesses, nonprofits, social entrepreneurship, and government ventures. The course began 25 years earlier after students requested practical entrepreneurship instruction, and Hadzima frames its creation as an entrepreneurial example: identifying customers, defining a task, recruiting capable people, and executing.

Hadzima emphasizes two core venture principles: creating value and capturing enough value to make the effort sustainable. Ventures require people, resources, skills, and luck. He introduces the diverse class audience, teaching team, and Virtual Ink case study, noting that its business plan is useful but not a model to copy.

The lecture outlines why planning matters, even if written plans may not always be necessary. A plan helps entrepreneurs understand the business, assess whether the opportunity is worth their time, attract partners or financing, and communicate a shared vision. Key questions include who the customers or users are, whether they will buy or use the offering, how value will be captured, how the product or service will be delivered, and what resources are needed.
