Missed interrupts can prevent the clock from restarting, potentially causing system hangs or unexpected behavior.

The passage describes traditional Russian remedies for sunburn, including sour cream, yogurt, and kefir to soften red skin; egg whites, nettle decoction, and watermelon juice to reduce pain; sea buckthorn oil for peeling and chafing; potatoes, carrots, and pumpkins for itching; and sauerkraut for swelling. It also lists soda-water compresses, oatmeal paste, and a sour cream and lemon juice mask as additional treatments, and suggests eating vitamin-rich fruits.

The Supreme Court denied Google’s request to pause an order requiring changes to Google Play policies after antitrust litigation with Epic Games. A jury found Google unlawfully maintained a monopoly, and lower courts upheld an injunction requiring Google to allow developers to use independent payment systems and, later, permit more competing app stores. Google cited security risks, while Epic argued those claims had been rejected.

Brown’s Academic Code committee reported continued high numbers of academic code violations, with over half occurring in computer science. In 2015-16, 49 undergraduates and seven graduate students were charged, receiving sanctions ranging from no violation to suspension or dismissal. The committee seeks to expand faculty membership due to case volume. Prevention efforts include a required online tutorial, syllabus integrity standards, and computer science collaboration policies reinforced through skits, quizzes and reminders. Computer science uses MOSS to detect programming plagiarism, though some cases involve improper collaboration or furnishing answers. Officials noted slight overrepresentation of international students and first-years, attributing some issues to differing educational systems and expectations. Brown revised international student orientation to address academic integrity and is considering panels, an academic integrity week and possibly an honor code.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K reporting that on April 16, 2020, Mellanox Technologies and NVIDIA International Holdings received Chinese antitrust approval for NVIDIA Holdings’ proposed acquisition of Mellanox. The companies had also received approvals from the European Commission and Mexico, and the U.S. Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired on May 23, 2019. The transaction was expected to close on or about April 27, 2020, subject to remaining customary closing conditions.

The Rancho Bernardo Kiwanis Club celebrated 50 years of service at StoneRidge Country Club. Founded in 1967 as the Kiwanis Club of Los Rancheros, it was organized largely by Franklin Lenfesty, whose $160,000 donation started its foundation. The club supports youth groups, scouts, local projects, Rady Children’s Hospital, Ronald McDonald House, and transitional homes in Romania. Its annual Labor Day pancake breakfast raises about $20,000. In 2016, it helped raise $120,000 for a Rancho Bernardo Community Park tot lot. The 40-member club is led by President John O’Rourke.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its fiscal 2019 Form 10-K for the year ended January 27, 2019. The company is incorporated in Delaware, headquartered in Santa Clara, California, and its common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol NVDA. As of July 27, 2018, the aggregate market value of voting stock held by non-affiliates was approximately $146.66 billion, and as of February 15, 2019, 606 million shares were outstanding.

NVIDIA describes itself as a GPU-focused computing company that has expanded from PC graphics into artificial intelligence, high performance computing, virtual reality, and autonomous vehicles. Its business has two reportable segments: GPU and Tegra Processor. GPU brands include GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, GRID, and DGX. Tegra products support platforms including DRIVE, SHIELD, Clara AGX, and Jetson AGX.

The company serves four main markets: Gaming, Professional Visualization, Datacenter, and Automotive. Gaming products include GeForce GPUs, SHIELD devices, GeForce NOW, and console-related platforms. Professional Visualization products include Quadro and RTX technologies for design, rendering, and creative applications. Datacenter offerings include GPUs, CUDA, libraries, DGX systems, NVIDIA GPU Cloud, Tesla accelerators, and GRID virtualization. Automotive offerings include DRIVE hardware and software for autonomous driving and in-vehicle AI.

NVIDIA’s strategy focuses on advancing GPU computing, extending leadership in AI and visual computing, developing autonomous vehicle platforms, and leveraging intellectual property through licensing and development agreements. The company uses a partner-based sales model involving OEMs, ODMs, system builders, cloud providers, automotive companies, distributors, and developers.

NVIDIA uses a fabless manufacturing model and relies on third parties for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging. Key suppliers include Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, Samsung Electronics, Advanced Semiconductor Engineering, Amkor, BYD, Hon Hai, Quanta, Wistron, Micron, Samsung Semiconductor, and SK Hynix. The company manages inventory based on demand forecasts and reported $7.42 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities at fiscal year-end 2019.

The company faces intense competition from suppliers of GPUs, SOCs, AI computing processors, and related technologies, including AMD, Intel, Xilinx, Qualcomm, Broadcom, Samsung, Texas Instruments, Renesas, and others. NVIDIA relies on patents, trademarks, trade secrets, nondisclosure agreements, and licensing arrangements to protect intellectual property.

As of January 27, 2019, NVIDIA had 13,277 employees, including 9,486 in research and development. Its executive officers included Jen-Hsun Huang, Colette Kress, Ajay Puri, Debora Shoquist, and Timothy Teter.

The risk factors discussed include market changes, competition, cybersecurity threats, product defects, reliance on third-party manufacturers, failure to achieve design wins, business disruptions, demand forecasting errors, international operations, employee retention, acquisitions, intellectual property disputes, operating result fluctuations, privacy regulation, tax exposure, litigation, and anti-takeover provisions.

NVIDIA’s headquarters include leased and owned facilities in Santa Clara, California, with additional leased and owned facilities in the United States, India, Asia, and Europe. The company stated it had sufficient facilities for the next twelve months. Since 2004, NVIDIA has repurchased 260 million shares for $7.08 billion, and in November 2018 its board authorized an additional $7.00 billion in repurchases through December 2022.

The President reports that, when he took office, federal authority had largely ceased in several Southern states, where forts, arsenals, custom-houses, revenue, and arms had been seized, officers had resigned, and an illegal Confederate organization was seeking foreign recognition. His initial policy was to exhaust peaceful measures, hold remaining federal property, collect revenue, continue mail service, and avoid disturbing citizens’ rights.

Fort Sumter became central after Major Anderson and military advisers concluded it could not be reinforced in time by available forces. The administration sought to reinforce Fort Pickens and prepared an expedition only to provision Sumter, notifying South Carolina that no men, arms, or ammunition would be sent unless resisted or attacked. South Carolina forces attacked and reduced the fort before the expedition arrived, which the President characterizes as aggression intended to force immediate dissolution of the Union.

He states that this conflict raises whether a constitutional republic can preserve itself against internal enemies. The government therefore called out military power to resist force with force. A call for 75,000 militia, a blockade of insurrectionary ports, volunteer enlistments, military expansion, and limited suspension of habeas corpus followed. He asks Congress to authorize at least 400,000 men and $400,000,000 to make the contest short and decisive.

The President rejects the legality of secession, arguing that states exist only within the Union, possess only constitutional powers, and cannot lawfully destroy the government. He criticizes “armed neutrality” in border states as effectively aiding disunion. He describes Virginia’s shift after Fort Sumter, its military actions, alliance with the Confederacy, and the relocation of the insurrectionary government to Richmond.

He presents the struggle as a people’s contest to preserve a government dedicated to liberty, equal opportunity, constitutional elections, and republican government. He praises loyal officers and especially common soldiers and sailors who remained faithful. He says the government’s aim is preservation, not conquest or subjugation, and that after rebellion is suppressed it will act under the Constitution and laws. He concludes that compromise cannot reward an armed effort to overturn an election and urges Congress to perform its duty.

This retrospective CMR study evaluated 15 adults with excessive left ventricular trabeculation to assess how trabecular anatomy affects measurements of LV volumes and ejection fraction. The authors separately labeled compact wall, central cavity, trabeculations, and intertrabecular recesses in end-diastole and end-systole. Intertrabecular recesses showed significantly greater ejection fraction than the central cavity. Including trabeculations in the blood pool increased EDV and ESV and reduced EF, while excluding recesses reduced LV volumes and EF. Contouring trabeculations reclassified EF categories, halving the number of patients with severely reduced EF. The study concludes that trabecular contouring may provide more accurate LV volume and EF assessment in excessive trabeculation.

Amazon’s Early Easter Sales offer the Netgear Arlo three-camera home security system for £249.99, down from £409.99, on 19 March only. The system includes smartphone/browser control, motion alerts, night vision, waterproof battery-powered cameras, free week-long online storage, expandability, and Alexa support.

Lois Riess, 56, is in custody in Texas after a manhunt following allegations that she killed her husband, David Riess, in Minnesota, stole $11,000 from his account, then traveled to Florida and killed Pamela Hutchinson, whom authorities said she targeted because they looked alike. Riess faces Florida charges including second-degree murder, grand theft, vehicle theft and criminal use of identification; in Minnesota she is charged with felony theft, with a murder charge pending. A Texas judge ruled she may be extradited to either state. Florida prosecutors could seek a first-degree murder indictment, which could make the death penalty possible, while Minnesota has no death penalty. Officials may consider which state tries her first. Authorities also cited Riess’s history of gambling and alleged theft from her disabled sister’s guardianship account.

President Biden said the United States had made progress against COVID-19 through vaccination, reduced deaths, and economic recovery, but warned that the Delta variant and nearly 80 million unvaccinated Americans were driving hospitalizations and deaths. He announced a six-part plan: require vaccination or weekly testing for employers with 100 or more workers, expand vaccination mandates for healthcare workers, federal employees, contractors, and Head Start educators, and require paid time off for vaccination; protect vaccinated people through booster readiness; keep schools open with vaccination, masking, testing, ventilation, and legal support for local school protections; expand rapid and free testing and increase mask enforcement on transportation; support small businesses through expanded disaster loans; and improve COVID-19 care through more federal medical teams and increased monoclonal antibody shipments. He also emphasized equity, international vaccine donations, and pandemic preparedness, urging Americans to get vaccinated.

Harvey Ulfers of Cedar Falls was sentenced to 2 years, 9 months for wire fraud and money laundering involving undervalued scrap metal from Deere’s Waterloo foundry. He was fined and ordered to pay restitution. Co-conspirator Patrick Williams also was sentenced.

The paper examines how blockchain companies create and capture value through digital business models. It frames blockchain as a distributed, cryptographically secured ledger that enables immutable, transparent, and trustless transactions, while noting debate over whether blockchain is disruptive or foundational. Using digital business model and value configuration theories, the study focuses on value creation logic and value capturing mechanisms.

The authors conducted an exploratory multiple case study of five permissioned consortium blockchain companies in mainland China, using interviews and archival data. The analysis identifies five blockchain-inspired business models: platformer, disintermediator, mediator, transformer, and co-innovator. These models create value respectively through blockchain architecture innovation, displacing incumbents in value chains, resolving value-chain inefficiencies, transforming business practices, and codeveloping blockchain alternatives to existing practices.

Each model has a distinct value capture mechanism and challenge. Platformers seek to become standards for future innovation but face compatibility issues. Disintermediators act as market equalizers but encounter resistance from existing players. Mediators offer firm-specific benefits across value chains but need incumbent buy-in. Transformers transfer lessons from tailored blockchain solutions across industries but face limited transferability. Co-innovators capture value through licensing but face high costs and limited profitability in small-scale implementations. The study contributes a typology of blockchain business models and notes limits from its five-company China-based sample.

Only four members remain on the 26-person National Council on the Humanities after the Trump administration fired a majority of its members. The council advises the NEH on grants, policy and funding. Fired member Karen Stout said she was disappointed by the dismissals.

Halimat Oniru, founder of Haleem Group, is portrayed as a successful Nigerian entrepreneur whose company operates in several states, creates many jobs, and is prominent in dredging and road construction, while she is described as private, humble, and philanthropic.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2021. The company reported Q2 2021 net sales of $113.1 billion, up from $88.9 billion in Q2 2020, and net income of $7.8 billion, up from $5.2 billion. For the first six months of 2021, net sales were $221.6 billion and net income was $15.9 billion.

Operating income was $7.7 billion in Q2 2021 and $16.6 billion for the first six months. Segment net sales for Q2 2021 were $67.6 billion for North America, $30.7 billion for International, and $14.8 billion for AWS. Segment operating income was $3.1 billion, $362 million, and $4.2 billion, respectively.

Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash totaled $40.7 billion at June 30, 2021. Total assets were $360.3 billion, total liabilities were $245.5 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $114.8 billion. Long-term debt was $50.3 billion, including $18.5 billion of senior notes issued in May 2021.

Amazon reported Q2 2021 operating cash flow of $12.7 billion, investing cash outflow of $22.1 billion, and financing cash inflow of $15.6 billion. The company entered an agreement to acquire MGM Holdings Inc. for approximately $8.5 billion, including debt. It also disclosed legal and tax matters, including a €746 million Luxembourg data protection fine that it intends to contest.

This cohort study extended follow-up of COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness in England to up to 50 weeks after second dose or 31 March 2022, estimating effectiveness of BNT162b2 and ChAdOx1 across 12 consecutive 4-week periods in risk-based subgroups.

Among 1,990,562 BNT162b2 recipients, 3,281,054 ChAdOx1 recipients, and 1,227,170 unvaccinated individuals, third-dose uptake became very high in older and clinically vulnerable groups, reaching at least 90% in the 65+, 18–64 clinically vulnerable, and 40–64 subgroups. In these groups, individuals who remained with only two doses appeared highly selected and had higher non-COVID-19 mortality than unvaccinated individuals, suggesting selection bias. The authors therefore did not interpret two-dose vaccine effectiveness beyond 26 weeks for COVID-19 outcomes in these groups.

In the 18–39 subgroup, third-dose uptake was lower, reaching 73%, and there was no evidence of increased non-COVID-19 mortality among those remaining with two doses. Hazard ratios for COVID-19 hospitalisation waned approximately log-linearly, with vaccine effectiveness negligible by weeks 35–38. Hazard ratios for positive SARS-CoV-2 tests waned until weeks 23–26, with apparent effectiveness negligible by weeks 15–18, though this may reflect differences in testing behaviour between vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals. Waning in this subgroup did not appear affected by the emergence of omicron.

The study concludes that estimating long-term effectiveness of two vaccine doses is difficult when third-dose uptake is high, and that future studies should consider selection bias, testing behaviour, and non-COVID-19 outcomes when interpreting vaccine effectiveness.

Two Oceans Restaurant in Table Mountain National Park, a voluntary WWF SASSI member, has stopped selling West Coast Rock Lobster after it was red-listed as unsustainable. SASSI reports less than 2% of the WCRL population remains, and SANParks TMNP supports the conservation initiative.

The passage describes a patent application related to real-time weather analysis and forecasting systems, incorporating prior U.S. patent applications and patents. The technology concerns systems, software, and methods for determining current weather phenomena and rapidly generating accurate weather and precipitation forecasts using real-time, high-frequency, and historical sensor data.

The background identifies limitations in existing fog detection and weather forecasting systems, including reliance on direct observation, difficulty distinguishing fog-related RF attenuation from other atmospheric causes, inability to process satellite microwave link attenuation efficiently, and insufficient handling of high-frequency data from sources such as vehicles. Existing systems are described as too slow or limited for rapidly changing weather phenomena affecting transportation, especially aviation.

The described system collects data from diverse sources, including terrestrial and satellite microwave links, weather radar, numerical weather prediction models, stationary and vehicle-mounted weather sensors, map data, and other sources. It preprocesses and normalizes this data, estimates precipitation, atmospheric water vapor, liquid water content, and fog, and generates forecasts and derived visibility measures such as runway visual range (RVR). The system uses parallel processing, asynchronous data collection, blending of multiple weather data sources, machine learning models, and cadence-based forecast cycles to support near real-time updates, with forecast cycles potentially as short as one minute.

The architecture includes four main server components: an information collection and normalization server, an offline/background processing server, a modeling and prediction server, and an information distribution and alerting server. These servers interact through system databases and external databases to collect, process, model, forecast, and distribute weather information and alerts.

A central concept is cadence-based processing, in which repeated cadence cycles create cadence instances that organize collected, processed, generated, forecast, and post-processed data into tile layers and tile stacks. The system can reuse, compare, propagate, or partially recalculate tile layers to reduce computation when data changes are limited. A cadence manager controls timing, processing stages, resource use, and decisions between full recalculation and incremental updates.

The system supports blending of precipitation and wind data, classification of storm conditions, use of forecast and collected data across cadence instances, and selective updating of dependent forecast layers. It is presented as improving processing throughput, forecast timeliness, and accuracy for applications including precipitation forecasting, fog inference, and aviation runway visibility forecasting.

Linda Ronstadt, whose singing career was sidelined by Parkinson’s disease, continues public appearances through “A Conversation With Linda,” featuring archival material from her career and audience Q&A sessions. She discussed living with Parkinson’s, including difficulty singing, talking, brushing her teeth, traveling, and the need to be selective with plans while continuing daily exercise. Upcoming events were scheduled in San Rafael, Folsom, and Saratoga, California.

The passage also notes Ronstadt’s 2014 Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction and details the 40th anniversary expanded edition of her 1977 album Simple Dreams. The album reached Number One, produced several Top 40 hits, earned Grammy recognition, became a major platinum seller, and included songs by artists such as Roy Orbison, Buddy Holly, Warren Zevon, and The Rolling Stones.

The passage describes a patent application for managing digital certificates in blockchain systems. It addresses the risk that a centralized certificate authority (CA), if hacked or malicious, can improperly issue, modify, or revoke digital certificate permissions and compromise blockchain security.

The proposed methods require blockchain consensus verification before a CA-issued digital certificate, certificate revocation list, revocation record, or revocation-list update is written to the blockchain. Nodes participating in consensus verify the submitted data, broadcast verification results, and determine success based on thresholds such as the number or proportion of successful verifications. If consensus succeeds, the blockchain writes the data; if it fails, the request is rejected.

The system can store certificate revocation lists or construct them from revocation records in local ledgers, allowing nodes to verify transaction participants’ certificates locally rather than relying on remote CA verification. Transactions can be accepted or rejected based on whether certificates appear in the revocation list and on applicable transaction rules.

The passage also describes related apparatuses, electronic devices, computer-readable storage media, and systems implementing these methods. The stated benefit is that CA-issued certificates are invalid until confirmed by blockchain consensus, reducing security risks from faulty, hacked, or malicious CAs and improving certificate verification efficiency.

The passage describes MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 device features and support information. The LFSS independent watchdog timer uses its own 32kHz LFOSC-based clock source, offers eight timer periods from 2ms to 2hr, and generates a POR reset if not reset in time. The windowed watchdog timer supervises code execution, can generate a reset or interrupt within a defined time window, supports eight periods, sleep-mode stopping, and interval timer mode.

The devices include TIMGx general-purpose timers and TIMAx advanced timers. TIMGx supports 16-/32-bit counting, prescaling, shadow registers on selected instances, quadrature encoder and Hall sensor input on selected instances, synchronization, cross triggering, and interrupt/DMA or peripheral triggers. TIMAx supports 16-bit counting, prescaling, repeat counting, shadow registers, complementary PWM with dead-band insertion, configurable fault handling, synchronization, triggers, and additional capture/compare channels.

The passage also covers internal analog connections, noting DAC_OUT connects to PA15; IOMUX digital I/O selection and control; SWD debug access; and the boot strap loader, which supports UART or I2C programming, password protection, optional disabling, and multiple invocation methods. Factory constants provide read-only device capability, trim, revision, and identification data.

Application guidance recommends VDD/VSS decoupling capacitors, NRST pullup and capacitor values, an optional SYSOSC FCL resistor, a VCORE tank capacitor, and pullups for 5V-tolerant open-drain I/O. Support sections list development tools, SDKs, IDEs, documentation resources, trademarks, ESD cautions, revision-history changes, and mechanical, packaging, orderable, and legal disclaimer information.

Kyle Busch of Joe Gibbs Racing won the Overton’s 400 in the No. 18 Skittles America Mix Toyota, earning his 48th Monster Energy NASCAR Cup Series victory, fifth win of the season and second at Chicago. Aric Almirola won Stage 1, and Kevin Harvick won Stage 2. Busch struggled with tight handling early, finishing 12th in Stage 1 and 11th in Stage 2 after multiple adjustments. In Stage 3, fast pit stops helped move him forward, and he took the lead after a lap 207 caution. Busch led 59 laps and held off Kyle Larson on the final lap, winning by 1.162 seconds. He tied Buck Baker for 14th on the all-time Cup wins list and reached 190 wins across NASCAR’s top three divisions. The next race is the Coke Zero Sugar 400 at Daytona.

This study further validated the COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale–Modified (C19-YRSm), a 17-item patient-reported outcome measure for Long Covid, using data from 1,314 patients in the UK LOCOMOTION study. The instrument assesses symptom severity, functional disability, overall health, and other symptoms. Participants were mostly Caucasian females with a mean age of 48; 10% had been hospitalised for COVID-19 and just over 2% admitted to ICU.

Results showed good item and scale characteristics, negligible missing data, good internal and test-retest reliability, and expected correlations with the FACIT-Fatigue scale. C19-YRSm subscales distinguished between symptom burden levels and between patients with and without hospitalisation or ICU admission. Over 30 days, the scale detected symptom changes and was more responsive than the EQ-5D-5L. Initial minimally important differences were estimated as 2 for symptom severity, 2 for functional disability, and 1 for overall health; minimal clinically important differences were estimated as 4 for symptom severity and functional disability. Confirmatory factor analysis provided reasonable support for a two-factor structure reflecting symptom severity and functional disability.

The study concludes that C19-YRSm is a valid, reliable, responsive, brief, and easy-to-administer condition-specific measure for monitoring Long Covid in clinical and research settings.

President Trump said Monday’s explosion near Manhattan’s Port Authority Bus Terminal showed the need for Congress to enact immigration reforms, including ending “chain migration” and increasing immigration security. Police said suspect Akayed Ullah, a Bangladeshi-descended permanent resident living in Brooklyn, detonated a crude device in a tunnel near Times Square. Homeland Security said Ullah entered the U.S. in 2011 on a family immigrant visa. Trump also called for more ICE officers, expanded immigration arrest and detention powers, and stronger penalties for convicted terrorists, including the death penalty in appropriate cases.

The passage describes design guidance for TPS7H500x-SP push-pull converter applications, including transformer turns ratio, primary inductance, FET selection, synchronous rectifiers, RCD clamp, output inductor, output capacitance and filtering, current sensing, hiccup timing, compensation, and slope compensation. Example design values include a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40 µH primary inductance, 170 V primary GaN FETs, 80 V synchronous rectifier GaN FETs, 0.47 µH output inductor, about 2.3 mF output capacitance, 7.5 Ω current sense resistor, 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, 40.2 kΩ/15 nF/47 pF compensation components, and 102 kΩ slope compensation resistor. The controller operates from 4 V to 14 V and requires proper bypassing, with at least 0.1 µF from VIN to AVSS. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switch-node and high-current loop areas, routing noise-sensitive traces away from switching signals, placing bypass and compensation components near the controller, and using appropriate CFP backside metallization connections. The passage also lists related documentation, update notification resources, support forums, trademark and ESD cautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, orderable, and disclaimer information.

Department of Transport briefing material says some commercial State company boards believe 2011 salary rates for chief executives are too low to attract or retain suitable candidates. It also notes discontent over Government policy ending performance-related bonuses and benefits such as car allowances for new or renewed CEO contracts. Some chief executives with bonus clauses in their contracts are threatening legal action, including claims for back payments, and the CEO of Dún Laoghaire Harbour Company has referred unpaid bonuses to the High Court. The companies under the department include CIÉ transport firms, the DAA, Irish Aviation Authority, and port and harbour companies.

Edmonton police seized $3.2 million worth of carfentanil from a vacant basement suite in southwest Edmonton after firefighters responding to a Jan. 28 fire call found suspicious powder. Police said it was the department’s largest carfentanil seizure. Investigators found 16 kilograms of blue powder containing carfentanil, additional pink powder containing the drug, and 12 kilograms of white powder believed to be caffeine used to cut it. Police said the drugs were likely intended for street distribution and could amount to about 161,000 doses. No arrests have been made. Alberta Health Services condemned the building, citing suspected clandestine drug production. Police are seeking the basement tenant, considered a person of interest, and continue to investigate.

The San Diego County Fair’s “Where the West is Fun” exhibit includes interactive Western-themed activities and educational displays, including a Kumeyaay Nation presence. Tribal members perform songs in their native language on Wednesdays and plan Kids’ Day crafts. The exhibit features a map of current Kumeyaay communities, photos, and cultural information. Organizers say the display helps correct misconceptions that Kumeyaay people no longer exist. Other exhibit elements address myths about the Wild West and include daily live entertainment.

Ruth Negga told AnOther magazine she was impatient for school to end because she resented how teachers spoke to her. She compared acting’s structure to school but found acting freeing. Negga said luck has played an important role in her career. She received her first Oscar nomination for Loving, which tells the story of Richard and Mildred Loving and the Supreme Court case that overturned bans on interracial marriage. The Academy Awards take place February 26.

VentureWire People’s May 30, 2001 newsletter reports executive changes across technology and venture-backed companies. Joe Bryant’s Nov. 9, 2000 cheatsheets.net email provides Week 11 fantasy football matchup analysis for passing and rushing games, grouping teams into favorable, even, downside, and defense-favored matchups. NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 31, 2016. The company is incorporated in Delaware, headquartered in Santa Clara, California, and its common stock trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the symbol NVDA. As of March 11, 2016, 542 million shares of common stock were outstanding.

NVIDIA describes itself as a leader in visual computing that has evolved from a PC graphics chip company into a specialized platform company serving Gaming, Professional Visualization, Datacenter and Automotive markets. Its two reportable segments are GPU and Tegra Processor. GPU brands include GeForce for gaming, Quadro for design professionals, Tesla for deep learning and accelerated computing, and GRID for cloud-based visual computing. Tegra processors support platforms including DRIVE for automotive computing and SHIELD for gaming devices.

The company reported revenue of $5.01 billion, income from operations of $747 million and net income of $614 million for fiscal 2016. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $5.04 billion at year-end. NVIDIA incurred $1.33 billion in research and development expense and had 9,227 employees, including 6,566 in research and development. During fiscal 2016, the company began winding down its Icera modem operations, recording restructuring and other charges.

NVIDIA uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on third parties for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing and packaging. It identified Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited and Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. among its wafer suppliers, and several subcontractors for assembly and testing. The company said one customer, ASUSTeK Computer Inc., accounted for 11% of fiscal 2016 revenue.

The filing identifies risks including intense competition, execution of new business models, replacement of Intel licensing revenue, manufacturing yield issues, product defects, cybersecurity incidents, reliance on third-party manufacturers and tools, failure to secure design wins, business disruptions, customer concentration, gross margin pressures, demand forecasting errors, international operations, acquisitions, intellectual property disputes, stock price volatility, privacy issues, headquarters construction risks, indebtedness, warrant dilution and anti-takeover provisions.

NVIDIA paid $213 million in cash dividends in fiscal 2016 and had repurchased an aggregate of 231 million shares for $3.85 billion through January 31, 2016. As of that date, it was authorized to repurchase up to an additional $1.47 billion of common stock through December 2018 and intended to return approximately $1.00 billion to shareholders in fiscal 2017 through repurchases and dividends.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated July 26, 2022, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2022. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1, along with an Inline XBRL cover page file. The filing was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

A Regina father urged drivers to avoid splashing pedestrians after a car drenched his wife and infant son with slush. Regina and Saskatoon bylaws prohibit splashing pedestrians, but police say enforcement is difficult without driver, vehicle and licence plate details.

Eisenhower accepts the Republican nomination for president, thanks the convention, and expresses satisfaction that Richard Nixon remains on the ticket. He argues that the Republican Party is “the Party of the Future” because its policies are based on long-range principle rather than expediency, address current and future issues, unite Americans rather than divide them, promote action through free individuals rather than paternalistic government, and are dedicated to peace.

He cites farm policy, labor relations, and limiting federal centralization as examples of principle-based government. He urges Republicans, independents, and supportive Democrats to spread the party’s message, register voters, and ensure turnout. He notes young people’s support for the administration and expresses hope that states will lower the voting age.

Eisenhower says the country must focus on emerging needs such as water, highways, health, housing, power, atomic energy, urban redevelopment, and education. He emphasizes social justice, citing progress against discrimination in the armed services, the District of Columbia, and among government contractors, while naming groups still needing fair treatment, including older workers, people with disabilities, migratory laborers, American Indians, women, small businesses, and distressed areas.

On peace, he highlights Atoms for Peace, disarmament efforts, national strength, collective security, and cautious engagement with peoples under communist rule. He argues that lasting peace requires moral, economic, and military strength; cooperation among free nations; and efforts to reduce mistrust through exchanges of people, ideas, and culture. He closes by invoking Lincoln’s hope for a divided house to cease being divided and accepts the nomination with confidence in Republican principles.

The paper examines statistical independence (SI) in Bell’s theorem and argues that SI is best understood as the claim that random sampling procedures yield representative samples. It defines superdeterministic theories as those that violate SI by implying systematic failure of random sampling to produce representative samples.

The authors challenge the view that superdeterminism must involve deterministic theories with fine-tuned initial conditions. They identify three forms: deterministic theories with fine-tuned initial conditions, theories involving statistical flukes, and “nomic exclusion” theories, where laws prevent certain combinations of measurement settings and hidden variables. They discuss examples including Leibnizian Quantum Mechanics, branching theories, and toy “goblin” models.

The paper also argues that retrocausal theories and invariant set theory need not violate SI and are not necessarily superdeterministic. It then considers philosophical consequences, claiming that some forms of superdeterminism may restrict free will, that all superdeterministic theories contain a conspiratorial element, and that although superdeterminism does not necessarily undermine the scientific method, it remains in a pre-scientific state.

The World Bank raised China’s 2025 GDP growth forecast from 4.5% to 4.8%, citing government stimulus, stronger domestic investment, industrial output, infrastructure spending, manufacturing support, and improved consumer sentiment. It warned growth may slow in 2026 due to fiscal constraints, global trade uncertainty, property weakness, local government debt, demographic pressures, and declining productivity.

Researchers led by Dr. Davide Tanasi of the University of South Florida analyzed residue from pottery fragments found in the 1990s at Castelluccio, Sicily, and identified it as olive oil. Using Nuclear Magnetic Resonance, Gas Chromatography and Mass Spectrometry, they detected oleic and linoleic acids in a reconstructed 3.5-foot storage container. The find is described as the oldest chemical evidence of olive oil in Italian prehistory, pushing back evidence for systematic olive oil production by at least 700 years. The study was published in Analytical Methods.

Will Ma explains independent chip model (ICM) theory for poker tournaments, where chip value is nonlinear because players aim to survive and move up payout levels rather than simply maximize chips. He contrasts chip EV with money EV, gives a three-player example showing how ICM calculates tournament equity, and notes that ICM is irrelevant in cash games, winner-take-all events, heads-up play, and early tournament stages, but highly relevant on payout bubbles, final tables, and satellites.

He then reviews a tournament final table, explaining how ICM affects strategy: big stacks can pressure opponents by moving all in first, while players should call all-ins more tightly to avoid busting before shorter stacks. He analyzes several hands, including spots where large shoves, folds, and bluffs are justified or questionable because of ICM. He also discusses satellite strategy, “traffic intersection” dynamics, rare cases where folding aces can be correct, cooperative play concerns, and later heads-up play where ICM no longer applies. The lecture ends with Ma winning the reviewed tournament and previewing upcoming classes on cash games, deep-stack play, postflop raising, and a guest lecture by Bill Chen.

Jim Cramer has become more cautious on Snap after previously comparing it to early Facebook following strong fourth-quarter results. He now cites Snapchat’s unpopular redesign, concerns about declining user engagement, negative celebrity reactions, and potential advertiser pullback as risks. Snap shares lost their post-earnings gains, and Cramer said the stock remains too expensive and risky for now, though he may consider buying at a lower price. Snap reports first-quarter results on May 1.

Children’s self-concept develops during puberty and early adolescence, when peers become more important and physical and emotional changes can create insecurity. Feelings of rejection may affect academics or contribute to depression. Parents are advised to respond with patience, reassurance, and nonjudgmental listening rather than telling children what to think. If signs of depression appear, such as falling grades or withdrawal, professional help from a school counselor or counselor may support both the child and parents.

The passage explains that running backs are key offensive football players whose main job is to run the ball efficiently, protect possession, and gain yardage. They line up in the backfield and may also be responsible for pass blocking and catching passes. Running backs are also called tailbacks or halfbacks, while fullbacks are sometimes grouped with them but usually have distinct traits.

Typical running backs are athletic, physically built, and often shorter than teammates, with estimated sizes of 5’9”–6’2” and 190–235 pounds. Important skills include speed, agility, vision, toughness, strength, quickness, and pass-catching ability. Different roles include short-yardage backs, who gain tough yards, and all-purpose backs, who contribute as receivers.

The passage lists Barry Sanders, Emmitt Smith, Walter Payton, Jim Brown, and LaDainian Tomlinson as notable running backs. It emphasizes that elite running backs help offenses by breaking tackles, making defenders miss, creating big plays, and contributing as runners, blockers, and receivers.

David Luiz is holidaying in Dubai after a difficult season at Chelsea marked by injuries, limited appearances, and being dropped from Brazil’s World Cup squad. He shared photos flyboarding and at the Burj Khalifa while his Chelsea future and Antonio Conte’s remain unclear.

The passage offers advice on making money from unwanted holiday gifts by selling, trading or regifting them. Kijiji, eBay, auction houses, garage sales, Bunz and gift card resale services are suggested depending on the item. Electronics, heavy items, collectibles, furniture, clothing, perfume, makeup, home decor and gift cards may perform well on different platforms. Sellers are advised to use clear photos, strong descriptions, relevant tags and realistic pricing based on sold listings and item condition. Timing can help, with January, weekends and Sundays noted as active periods, while furniture and home decor may sell well before the school year. Gift cards can be sold or exchanged, though often for less than face value. Regifting is described as acceptable only for new, appropriate items in original packaging, and not for handmade, personalized or carefully chosen gifts.

Antonio Conte says he is facing harsher media scrutiny than other Premier League managers, with repeated questions about his Chelsea future despite his desire to see out the remaining 18 months of his contract. Chelsea, league champions and FA Cup finalists in Conte’s first season, are 18 points behind Manchester City and battling for a top-four finish. Conte compared his treatment with that of rival managers and said criticism of Arsene Wenger came only after many years. Ahead of Chelsea’s match at Watford, he said his ambition is to have another season in England and respect his contract.

NASA launched Voyager 1 and 2 in 1977 to study Jupiter and Saturn. Voyager 2 launched first but arrived at Jupiter after Voyager 1, and was sent on a trajectory allowing flybys of Uranus and Neptune. Together they collected data on four planets and 48 moons. Both probes later began the Voyager Interstellar Mission; Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012. Each carries a Golden Record with information about Earth and humanity, intended to last millions of years.

The passage introduces inverse problems in science and engineering, emphasizing their ill-posed nature and added difficulty on irregular geometries. It argues that classical PDE-constrained optimization is costly at scale, while most operator learning and diffusion-based methods remain focused on regular domains or forward tasks. The work proposes GeoFunFlow, a geometry-aware diffusion framework for reconstructing PDE-governed physical fields from sparse, noisy sensor data on complex geometries. Its components include a geometric function autoencoder using a Perceiver module for variable-size unstructured meshes, coupling with a latent diffusion model for posterior sampling, theoretical posterior approximation guarantees, and benchmark results showing improved accuracy and inference efficiency over baselines.

The related work reviews neural operator methods, including DeepONet, FNO, transformer-based variants, and approaches for irregular meshes, as well as diffusion-based models for PDEs and physical simulations. It notes that most diffusion-operator methods remain limited to uniform grids. The preliminaries define operator learning for PDE solution maps and rectified flow, a deterministic ODE-based generative method used for conditional posterior sampling without explicit likelihood evaluation or MCMC. The problem setup focuses on reconstructing fields on bounded irregular domains from noisy pointwise measurements across varying geometries.

Chicago hotels must provide panic buttons for workers who are alone in guest rooms, following reports of widespread sexual harassment. The buttons alert supervisors, managers and human resources with the employee’s name and location.

Researchers at Karolinska Institutet and Finnish collaborators developed the CORE model, a tool that predicts 10-year risk of severe liver disease using age, sex, and three routine liver enzyme blood tests: AST, ALT, and GGT. Designed for primary care, it aims to enable earlier detection of cirrhosis, liver cancer, and need for liver transplant. In data from over 480,000 Stockholm health-check participants followed for up to 30 years, about 1.5% developed severe liver disease. CORE distinguished those who did or did not develop disease in 88% of cases, outperforming the FIB-4 method. It also showed high accuracy in Finnish and UK groups. Researchers say further testing is needed in high-risk groups and integration into medical record systems would support clinical use.

Mark Taylor forwarded parts of the Jan. 19 Option Investor Newsletter to Yao Apasu and Sara Shackleton. Numerous call and put positions were updated, Ford was added as a new call play, and no new put plays were added. DeBeers’s 2008 case examines whether synthetic diamonds threatened the natural diamond industry and how DeBeers should respond. Synthetic diamonds were chemically identical to mined diamonds, could be produced in laboratories within days, cost 15%–40% less, and were marketed as environmentally friendlier and free from conflict-diamond concerns. Producers such as Gemesis, Apollo, Chatham, and others were expanding sales, though jewelry-grade synthetic diamonds were generally limited to smaller sizes and often colored stones.

The diamond industry produced about $13 billion in rough stones and $62 billion in jewelry annually. Major producing countries included Botswana, Russia, South Africa, Angola, Canada, Australia, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Processing was dominated by India, while the United States accounted for 46% of diamond demand. Demand was also growing in India and China.

DeBeers had long dominated the industry by controlling supply through its Central Selling Organization, but its position weakened in the 1990s due to Russian, Australian, and Canadian production outside its control, antitrust pressure, and criticism over blood diamonds. In response, DeBeers shifted from supply control to a demand-driven, brand-focused strategy, reduced stockpiling, emphasized conflict-free diamonds, introduced the Supplier of Choice program, developed branding efforts such as Forevermark, and expanded into retail through a venture with LVMH.

Synthetic diamonds raised questions over terminology, certification, consumer perception, and potential substitution. The industry supported detection and disclosure, while the Gemological Institute of America began grading lab-grown diamonds using the same 4-Cs system. Synthetic diamonds also had growing industrial applications in semiconductors, optics, data storage, and biological uses.

DeBeers publicly downplayed synthetics, emphasizing natural diamonds as ancient and unique, while investing in detection technology, consumer education, and new natural diamond supplies. The case ends by contrasting consumer concerns about ethics and value with traditional jewelry-industry arguments about romance, rarity, and authenticity.

President Biden addressed the U.N. General Assembly for the final time as president, reflecting on decades of public service and arguing that global challenges can be overcome through cooperation. He cited past progress on the Cold War, Vietnam, apartheid, war crimes accountability, 9/11, Iraq, and Afghanistan, while acknowledging current crises including Ukraine, Gaza, Sudan, climate change, disease, hunger, displacement, threats to democracy, and risks from artificial intelligence.

He urged continued support for Ukraine against Russia, responsible management of competition with China, and cooperation on issues such as synthetic narcotics. He called for a ceasefire and hostage deal in Gaza, efforts to prevent wider war involving Hezbollah and Lebanon, progress toward a two-state solution, and measures to ensure Iran never obtains a nuclear weapon. He also called for ending the war in Sudan and improving humanitarian access.

Biden highlighted U.S. investments in development, food security, global health, climate action, clean energy, COVID vaccine donations, and support for African countries responding to mpox. He advocated U.N. reform, including expanding the Security Council, and emphasized the need for global rules on AI. He closed by defending democracy, explaining his decision not to seek a second term, and urging leaders to serve their people and work together for peace.

IEP News for May 10, 2001 compiled articles on California’s energy crisis. PUC President Loretta Lynch proposed a tiered rate plan sparing about half of residential customers while raising bills sharply for heavier users and businesses.

Gov. Amanda Nunes defeated Ronda Rousey at UFC 207 to retain her title, then criticized Rousey’s coach Edmond Tarverdyan, saying he made Rousey believe she was a boxer despite her strong judo background. The passage notes Tarverdyan had previously faced criticism from Rousey’s mother, fans, and pundits. Rousey suffered her second consecutive loss after being overwhelmed by Nunes’ striking. Dana White said Nunes’ popularity would grow, while Rousey said she needed time to reflect on her future amid speculation about retirement.

Bernstorff reported that House, on Wilson’s behalf, offered confidential peace mediation based on Wilson’s Senate message and requested Germany disclose peace terms publicly. Wilson believed Germany had a moral obligation to state its conditions, hoped to convene peace conferences soon, and viewed the Entente note as a bluff. Bernstorff urged delaying unrestricted U-boat warfare, warning it would make war with the United States unavoidable and strengthen the American war party, while cooperation with Wilson could improve Germany’s diplomatic position.

Sharp reported from France that Socialist deputies approved Wilson’s Senate address, urging the French Government and belligerent representatives to support his peace initiative. He noted the group’s influence and said its action could build support for Wilson’s message. The study addresses Medicare overutilization and fraud detection in ophthalmology using machine learning. Existing approaches often rely on the LEIE dataset, which has severe class imbalance and focuses on overt fraud, potentially missing subtler overutilization patterns. The authors created a labeled dataset of 663 ophthalmologists using 2015 Medicare billing data, with labels assigned by experienced physicians and medical billers. Features were derived from CMS Medicare Provider Utilization and Payment Data, including procedure-level billing measures and payment ratios.

Several supervised models were evaluated, including K-nearest neighbor, logistic regression, support vector machines, multilayer perceptron, extreme gradient boosting, and a stacking ensemble. The stacking ensemble performed best, with an AUROC of 0.907 and the lowest Brier score. Applied to 2021 Medicare data, the model predicted that 1,457 of 17,013 ophthalmologists were likely overutilizers, yielding an estimated nationwide overutilization rate of 8.6%. Estimated annual Medicare losses from ophthalmology overutilization were $437.1 million.

Feature importance analysis found that Medicare payment per patient was strongly associated with predicted overutilization, along with certain HCPCS code utilization patterns. The study also reported regional variation in predicted overutilization rates and monetary losses across Medicare jurisdictions. Limitations include the small labeled dataset, reliance on model-based estimates, difficulty distinguishing overutilization from intentional fraud, and the need for specialty-specific labeled datasets to apply the approach elsewhere.

BSEB has declared the BETET/BSITET 2011 Special Examination 2016 results for Paper I and II on biharboard.ac.in. Candidates can check results using their 10-digit roll number, and official answer keys have also been released.

The passage outlines statistical analysis plans for a clinical study comparing dasiglucagon 0.6 mg, placebo, and GlucaGen®. Demographic and baseline characteristics, diabetes history, medical history, BMI, concomitant medications, and current diabetes treatment will be summarized by treatment group, with coding using MedDRA and WHODrug.

Primary efficacy analysis will use the full analysis set, with supportive analyses in the per-protocol set. The primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery, defined as a ≥20 mg/dL increase from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose. Analyses include Kaplan-Meier summaries, stratified log-rank tests by age group and injection site, sensitivity analyses, Wilcoxon testing, Cox proportional hazards modeling when appropriate, and linear interpolation as supportive analysis. Secondary endpoints include plasma glucose recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes and plasma glucose changes from baseline at those times. Multiplicity will be controlled using a hierarchical testing procedure for dasiglucagon versus placebo.

Pharmacokinetic analyses will summarize plasma dasiglucagon and glucagon concentrations and PK metrics using non-compartmental methods. Pharmacodynamic analyses will summarize plasma glucose response, including AUE0-30min.

Safety analyses will use the safety set and include exposure, insulin use, hypoglycemia induction, rescue glucose infusion, local tolerability, adverse events, laboratory tests, pregnancy and alcohol tests, vital signs, physical examination, ECG, and immunogenicity. TEAEs will be coded using MedDRA and summarized by treatment group. ADA incidence will be analyzed descriptively.

The passage also describes handling of missing or incomplete dates, programming and presentation standards for tables, figures, and listings, SAS quality-control requirements, and planned outputs for tables, figures, and listings.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2019. The company designs, develops, manufactures and sells fully electric vehicles, solar energy generation products, and energy storage products, and reports two segments: automotive and energy generation and storage.

For the quarter, Tesla reported total revenues of $4.54 billion, up from $3.41 billion in the same period of 2018. Automotive revenues were $3.72 billion, energy generation and storage revenues were $324.7 million, and services and other revenues were $492.9 million. Gross profit was $565.7 million. Loss from operations was $521.8 million, and net loss attributable to common stockholders was $702.1 million, or $4.10 per basic and diluted share.

As of March 31, 2019, Tesla had total assets of $28.91 billion, total liabilities of $22.87 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $4.61 billion. Cash and cash equivalents were $2.20 billion, down from $3.69 billion at December 31, 2018. Total debt was $10.33 billion, including $6.78 billion of recourse debt and $3.54 billion of non-recourse debt. Net cash used in operating activities was $639.6 million.

Tesla adopted the new lease accounting standard on January 1, 2019, recognizing operating lease right-of-use assets and liabilities and derecognizing build-to-suit lease assets and liabilities. North Carolina child care academies in at least 11 counties help prepare early childhood educators for classrooms in two to six weeks at little to no cost. The lecture discusses SCET for dijet production in \(e^+e^-\) collisions, where a virtual photon or \(Z\) produces two back-to-back collinear jets plus ultra-soft radiation. The relevant scales are the hard scale \(Q\), jet scale \(m\), ultra-soft scale \(m^2/Q\), and \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}\). Hemisphere invariant masses \(m^2\) and \(\bar m^2\) restrict events to dijet configurations when both are much smaller than \(Q^2\).

Two regions are distinguished: the peak region, where \(m^2/Q \sim \Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}\) and nonperturbative effects must be treated as order one, and the tail region, where \(m^2/Q \gg \Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}\) and the leading cross section is perturbative with nonperturbative power corrections. The dominant nonperturbative corrections scale as powers of \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}/\mu_s\).

The QCD current is matched onto SCET operators containing collinear fields and Wilson lines. After field redefinitions, the SCET Lagrangian and Hilbert space factor into \(n\)-collinear, \(\bar n\)-collinear, and ultra-soft sectors. This enables a factorization theorem for hemisphere masses: a hard function multiplies convolutions of two jet functions and a soft function. The soft function contains ultra-soft dynamics and may include nonperturbative effects.

The thrust observable is introduced as a one-variable projection of the hemisphere mass measurement. In the dijet limit, \(\tau=1-T\) is proportional to the sum of the two hemisphere invariant masses over \(Q^2\). Its cross section has a peak region dominated by nonperturbative soft effects, a tail region where perturbative soft functions and power corrections apply, and a large-\(\tau\) region where the dijet description no longer applies.

Perturbatively, the hard function comes from matching the quark form factor, while jet and soft functions are computed from corresponding collinear and Wilson-line matrix elements. Their renormalization involves anomalous dimensions and convolutions, requiring renormalization group evolution to resum logarithms such as powers of \(\alpha_s \log^2 \tau\).

The LST-1 and MAGIC Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescope systems at La Palma use On-Site Analysis pipelines to provide rapid, reliable analysis products for alerts, scheduling, and data quality checks while reducing reliance on fast off-site raw data transfer. MAGIC’s OSA has operated since 2012 and processes data through high-level products such as significance estimates, spectra, light curves, and sky maps. LST-1’s OSA has operated since 2021 and currently processes raw data to reconstructed events, with higher-level analysis being added.

MAGIC records up to 2 TB of raw data per day, while LST-1 records up to 30 TB. Both systems perform next-day analysis using standard processing chains, typically delivering results before 14:00 local time. Their workflows convert DL0 raw data through calibration, reconstruction, event selection, and instrument response production. Jobs are launched automatically, parallelized through batch systems, monitored via web pages, and supported by error handling and notifications.

The LST-1 OSA evolved from MAGIC’s system but uses different software. MAGIC includes automatic high-level physics products, while LST-1 integrates daily data-check summaries. Processed data are later transferred off-site for user access and dedicated rapid analyses.

Key lessons are that next-day analysis is necessary for VHE observatories, pipelines must coordinate with databases and simulation tools, and automation should include human intervention options plus robust error detection and recovery. These systems are considered useful prototypes for future CTAO onsite pipelines.

The HHLL trading strategy is a price action reversal strategy that seeks buying opportunities in downtrends and selling opportunities in uptrends. It looks for breaks in trend structure: in an uptrend, a higher high followed by a lower low may signal a bearish reversal; in a downtrend, a lower low followed by a higher high may signal a bullish reversal. Trades are entered on pullbacks to prior highs or lows after the reversal signal.

The passage notes that the ZigZag indicator can illustrate HHLL patterns but is unsuitable for backtesting or trading because it uses forward-looking elements. Backtesting the strategy is difficult due to discretion in identifying tops and bottoms. A simplified backtest on Philip Morris produced 118 trades, a 9.8% CAGR, 1.26% average gain per trade, and a 2.2 profit factor.

The passage describes the evolution of U.S. covert action oversight from 1948 to 1963. NSC 10/2 defined covert activities, excluding military conflict, espionage, counter-espionage, and military deception. The CIA’s Office of Policy Coordination, created in 1948, managed covert actions and initially received guidance directly from State in peacetime and the military in wartime, with the DCI informed. In 1950 guidance was routed through the DCI. During the Korean conflict, covert action expanded rapidly, prompting requests for clearer policy direction. Truman created the Psychological Strategy Board in 1951, and NSC 10/5 reaffirmed and expanded CIA covert authority.

Under Eisenhower, NSC directives narrowed CIA latitude. NSC 5412 and later versions clarified DCI responsibility, required coordination with State and Defense, and led to the NSC 5412/2 Special Group, which reviewed and approved CIA covert action programs. Meetings became weekly in 1959, though criteria for review remained informal and initiative stayed largely with the CIA. After the Bay of Pigs, the Taylor Report recommended stronger high-level direction. The Special Group gained greater responsibility, and in 1963 adopted informal criteria for submitting projects, including risk, success prospects, exposure, political sensitivity, and cost.

Fullbacks are physical offensive players used mainly in two-back sets as blockers in run and pass schemes. They often line up near or behind the quarterback and rarely receive the ball, though they may run short-yardage plays or catch short passes. Their main job is to block defenders, especially linebackers at the second level, to help create running lanes. Fullbacks are typically tough, thick-built players around 5’11”–6’1” and 235–250 pounds, with skills in run blocking, pass blocking, toughness, agility, and pass catching. The position is more common in pro-style offenses and less used in spread offenses. Other names include power back and blocking back. Notable fullbacks include Mike Alstott and Larry Csonka. The passage emphasizes that fullbacks are important but under-recognized contributors to traditional running offenses.

The author recalls organizing for a 2012 May Day general strike in New York that drew thousands nationally but failed to disrupt business as usual. New strike calls have emerged in response to the Trump administration, including a Feb. 17 action promoted by Francine Prose and David Simon and a March 8 women’s strike led by women authors and activists, including Angela Davis, focused on “a feminism for the 99 percent.”

It highlights Poland’s 2016 women’s strike against a proposed anti-abortion bill as a model: it did not shut down all commerce but used boycotts, marches, and solidarity closures to help defeat the measure.

March 8 organizers avoid calling their action a traditional general strike, citing anti-strike laws, low union density, and risks to vulnerable women of color. Instead, they propose a “mass strike” including demonstrations, walkouts, boycotts, and other locally adapted actions. Potential supporters include the National Organization for Women, the Chicago Teachers Union, Black Lives Matter-affiliated leaders, and Palestinian rights groups. While critics argue traditional general strikes are unrealistic in the United States, the author suggests these actions could teach activists new forms of collective resistance.

The passage describes SD Memory Card physical-layer command behavior, data transfer states, and related operations. SET_DSR (CMD4) configures driver stages and may switch clock rate, while CMD7 selects one card into Transfer State; only one card can be selected at a time, and deselection returns cards to Stand-by State. Data communication in Data Transfer Mode is point-to-point with the selected card. Read and write transfers can be aborted by CMD12, and programming or erase operations may continue when another card is selected unless the card is reset.

Read operations use block-oriented transfers with CRC protection, with CMD17 for single-block reads and CMD18 for multiple-block reads. Write operations use CMD24, CMD25, CMD27, CMD42, and CMD56 in write mode, with CRC checking before programming. Cards may buffer block writes, indicate busy on DAT0, and reject some commands while programming. Multiple block write can be accelerated with ACMD23 pre-erase. Erase uses CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38; DISCARD and Full User Area Logical Erase (FULE) are CMD38 variants supported for SDHC and SDXC cards, not SPI, with specific arguments and busy indications.

The passage covers write protection mechanisms: mechanical write-protect switch, optional internal write protection, and password-based card lock. CMD42 manages password setting, clearing, locking, unlocking, force erase, and Card Ownership Protection (COP). COP introduces Force Erase Password (FEP), COP Unlock, FEP management, FEP Force Erase, and restrictions on clearing passwords when FEP is set. Locked cards accept only defined basic and lock-related commands; ACMD6 is rejected while locked.

APP_CMD (CMD55) marks the following command as application-specific, with rules for defined, undefined, legal, and illegal ACMD handling. CMD6 switches or checks card functions across function groups including bus speed, command system, driver strength, and power limit. Version 1.10 and later cards must support CMD6. High-Speed mode raises interface speed to 25 MB/sec via CMD6 and requires one-to-one host-card signaling. CMD8 checks interface voltage and enables command expansion for Version 2.00 and later cards.

The passage also distinguishes SDSC from SDHC/SDXC addressing: SDSC uses byte addressing and CMD16 block length, while SDHC/SDXC use fixed 512-byte block addressing and disable partial or misaligned memory access. Hosts may change or stop the bus clock under restrictions and must provide required clock cycles after transactions. CRC7 protects commands and responses, while CRC16 protects data blocks. Command errors, illegal commands, and CRC failures set status bits and prevent execution. Read, write, erase, DISCARD, FULE, and UHS-II operations have specified timeout and busy behavior.

Microsoft’s Form 10-K for fiscal year ended June 30, 2018 describes the company as a technology provider focused on empowering people and organizations through software, services, devices, and cloud-based solutions. Its products include operating systems, productivity applications, server applications, business solutions, development tools, video games, PCs, tablets, gaming consoles, and related services.

Microsoft organizes its business into three reportable segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. Productivity and Business Processes includes Office, Office 365, LinkedIn, and Dynamics. Intelligent Cloud includes server products, Azure, and enterprise services. More Personal Computing includes Windows, devices such as Surface, gaming products and services, and search advertising.

The company emphasizes three strategic ambitions: reinventing productivity and business processes, building the intelligent cloud platform, and creating more personal computing. It highlights continued investment in Microsoft 365, Azure, artificial intelligence, Windows 10, gaming, and cloud services. Microsoft announced plans to acquire GitHub in June 2018.

Research and development expenses were $14.7 billion in fiscal 2018, representing 13% of revenue. Microsoft employed approximately 131,000 full-time employees as of June 30, 2018, including 78,000 in the United States and 53,000 internationally.

The passage outlines claims arising from the seizure of the Cape Horn Pigeon. It seeks $45,000 for an established item, $31,000 for the impressment of 31 American crew members into Russian naval service at $1,000 each, and compensation for enforced crew labor in navigating a Russian schooner to Vladivostok. It also claims $200 for provisions consumed by Russian personnel, $210 for crew board at Vladivostok, and $3,040 for general expenses, including documented costs and anticipated expenses in proving the claim. A Seattle Uber driver returned a woman’s purse after Officer Eric Michl texted that he could be arrested and sent a selfie proving he was police. The driver had previously demanded more money.

The speaker praised the Philadelphia Flyers for their resilience, competitiveness, and growth through adversity, while acknowledging the pain of losing. He congratulated the Chicago Blackhawks, crediting their speed, offense, defense, playoff run, and Stanley Cup championship. He said the Flyers had chances late in regulation and overtime but could not capitalize. He discussed lineup adjustments, praised Chicago’s goaltending, and highlighted strong playoff performances from Scott Hartnell and the Briere-Hartnell-Leino line. In pregame remarks, he emphasized managing energy rather than nerves, focusing only on winning one elimination game at home, and relying on experienced leaders to handle pressure.

The October 2025 Supreme Court term is expected to feature major cases on presidential power, voting rights, civil rights, social issues and criminal procedure. The court recently used its emergency docket to allow several Trump administration actions, often in 6-3 rulings reversing lower courts.

Upcoming cases include challenges to President Trump’s authority to impose tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and questions about Congress’ power to limit presidential removal of agency heads. The administration has also asked the court to review Trump’s executive order restricting birthright citizenship, which lower federal courts have found unconstitutional.

The court will rehear a Louisiana redistricting case involving Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act and whether creating a second majority-Black district violates the 14th or 15th Amendments. The case could affect disparate impact liability under civil rights laws.

Other cases involve Colorado’s ban on conversion therapy, state laws barring transgender athletes from teams matching their gender identities, and whether police need probable cause under the emergency aid exception to enter a home without a warrant. The term is expected to produce significant rulings affecting law and society.

Centers lead the offensive line by communicating calls, identifying defensive looks, directing pass protections and run blocking assignments, and snapping the ball every play. Though often smaller or less athletic than other offensive linemen, they rely on football IQ, leadership, toughness, agility, strength, blocking ability, and snapping skills. Positioned in the middle of the offensive line, centers are sometimes called the quarterbacks of the offensive line. They must study defenses, make quick decisions, block defensive linemen and linebackers, pick up blitzes, and maintain strong trust with the quarterback. The passage cites Jim Otto and Mike Webster as notable centers.

The passage describes embodiments of waveguide devices for near-eye displays, head-mounted displays, head-up displays, and related optical systems that provide more uniform output illumination by mitigating banding artifacts. The devices include an optical substrate, light source, light coupler, light extractor, and a debanding optic that shifts or modifies the pupil so extracted light has a substantially flat illumination profile, with spatial non-uniformity preferably below 10% or 20%.

Banding is described as gaps or overlaps in light extracted from a total internal reflection waveguide, influenced by field angle, waveguide thickness, and aperture thickness. Proposed debanding approaches include effective input aperture control, multiple or switchable gratings, grating arrays, rolled K-vectors, passive grating layers, refractive index layers, GRIN media, partially reflecting or polarization-modifying layers, variable numerical aperture microdisplays, tilted microdisplays, coupling prisms, and light-absorbing films.

The passage also describes color waveguide embodiments using stacked optical substrates and input stops with dichroic portions to reduce color banding, along with methods for producing, coupling, guiding, extracting, and debanding light in waveguide devices. Various grating technologies, including Bragg gratings, switchable Bragg gratings, holographic polymer dispersed liquid crystal gratings, fold gratings, and multiplexed gratings, are discussed as input couplers, output extractors, or pupil-shifting elements.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated October 27, 2016, reporting the announcement of its third quarter 2016 financial results. The filing incorporates a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Palestine police arrested two people after about 30 unlocked cars were burglarized Tuesday morning and are still seeking more suspects. Police urged residents to report rummaged vehicles and lock car doors. One victim captured a burglary on surveillance; only small pocket change was stolen.

The Burr Ridge Village Board approved fiscal policies requiring a 20% minimum unreserved general fund balance, balanced general fund spending, and limits on total expenses. The passage describes clocking, timing, and peripheral interface requirements for a Texas Instruments TMS320DM814x/DM8127 device. The PCIE PHY requires a high-quality, low-jitter differential SERDES clock with AC coupling capacitors placed close to the processor. External clock inputs include AUD_CLKIN0/1/2, CLKIN32, DEVOSC, AUXOSC, and selectable CLKOUT0/1 outputs. The device includes multiple top-level and embedded PLLs, which reset in bypass mode and must be configured within specified frequency and power-supply limits.

It outlines interrupt architecture for ARM Cortex-A8, Media Controller, and C674x DSP events; EDMA channel synchronization; Advanced Event Triggering; trace support; and IEEE 1149.1 JTAG operation. It also gives AC timing measurement assumptions, board-routing considerations, and use of IBIS models.

Peripheral sections cover DCAN, EMAC switch, MDIO, GPIO, GPMC/ELM, HDMI, HDVPSS, video DAC, I2C, ISS camera interfaces, and DDR2/DDR3 memory controllers. The EMAC supports MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII with MDIO PHY management. The GPMC supports NOR, NAND, SRAM, and related timing modes, while the ELM supports BCH error location. HDMI includes TMDS, DDC, and CEC guidance with impedance, ESD, and PCB layout requirements. DDR2/DDR3 sections specify supported memory widths, routing rules, termination, bypassing, keepout regions, and compatible JEDEC devices.

High-performance computing (HPC) helps manufacturing and process industries perform complex calculations through parallel processing on connected systems.
