DLAA uses AI-based anti-aliasing and DLSS Super Resolution technology to improve native-resolution image quality, temporal stability, and motion detail. NVIDIA’s Blackwell architecture is designed to accelerate neural shaders, which use AI models to approximate complex shader calculations and are presented as the next stage in GPU shader evolution. The passage reviews shader milestones from fixed-function pipelines through vertex, pixel, geometry, compute, mesh, ray tracing, and Blackwell neural shaders.

Blackwell enables Tensor Cores to be accessed through shaders via the Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan, developed with Microsoft. Combined with Slang features, this supports neural techniques such as neural texture compression, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. These technologies aim to improve real-time rendering of materials, compressed textures, indirect lighting, subsurface scattering, and faces using neural networks or generative AI.

The passage also outlines Blackwell GPU products. GB202 is the flagship GPU with 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, and 768 Tensor Cores, used for the GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA Cores, and 336 Tensor Cores, used for RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 has 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA Cores, and 200 Tensor Cores, used for RTX 5070. The passage ends with NVIDIA legal disclaimers, warranty limitations, trademark notices, and copyright information.

Carson High School’s 2018 Winterfest began Thursday with a Johnny Depp film-themed week of activities. Events include contests, entertainment, a dance, and court crownings, culminating with the Senior Winterfest King and Queen announced Feb. 9 during the boys basketball game against Douglas.

Larry Connors’ %b strategy, from High Probability Trading, is a mean-reversion ETF strategy based on Bollinger Bands. It buys when the close is above the 200-day moving average and %b is below 0.2 for three consecutive days, and exits when %b closes above 0.8. The article tests the strategy from ETF inception to today using a 5-day Bollinger Band lookback and two standard deviations, noting Connors’ original parameters were not specified. Results were strong for QQQ and SPY but had few trades. A 25-ETF portfolio test from 2000 to December 2020 produced 677 trades, a 75% win rate, 0.76% average gain, 1.9 profit factor, 4.84% CAGR, 16% max drawdown, and 17% market exposure. Using a 10-day lookback improved CAGR to 8.2% but raised drawdown to 24%.

The Yankees host the Red Sox in Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium on Tuesday, Sept. 30, at 6:08 p.m. ET. Boston enters as the No. 5 seed after finishing 89-73, while New York is the top Wild Card at 94-68 and on an eight-game winning streak. The winner advances to face Toronto in the ALDS. The game airs on SiriusXM, with the Yankees broadcast on channel 89 and Red Sox broadcast on channel 178.

The study introduces a coarse-grained rod-sphere particle model to represent silica nanoparticles with grafted polymer bundles such as crystallized PiPrOx. The model consists of a repulsive sphere tethered to a rigid five-bead rod, with three rod interaction types: lock-and-key, symmetric, and unspecific. Molecular dynamics simulations varied sphere radius, temperature, and rod interaction type to examine self-assembly.

The simulations produced mesostructures including bulk assemblies, bilayers, monolayers, ribbons, fibers, worms, stars, spheres, gels, liquids, and disperse states. Structures were classified using a dimensionality parameter based on the gyration tensor and a degree-of-order parameter based on rod alignment. Increasing sphere size generally reduced assembly dimensionality because the sphere created geometric frustration that limited growth directions. Rod interaction specificity influenced whether structures formed as bilayers or monolayers, ribbons or fibers, stars or spheres, and ordered or disordered assemblies.

Self-assembly typically proceeded through aggregation, growth, and consolidation. For certain lock-and-key systems, ribbons spontaneously twisted into double helices, with pitch decreasing as sphere radius increased. The model reproduced experimentally observed fibers and spherical clusters of PiPrOx-grafted silica nanoparticles and predicts additional mesostructures controlled by geometric hindrance and interaction type.

This study examined transcriptome-wide gene expression differences in whole blood from 194 virally non-detectable people living with HIV (PLWH) on antiretroviral therapy (ART) and 361 HIV-1 seronegative individuals. Among 20,211 genes tested, 566 were differentially expressed by HIV status, with 274 up-regulated and 292 down-regulated in PLWH. These genes were enriched for immune-related biological processes including cell migration, adhesion, T cell biology, lymphocyte immune response, calcium signaling, and PI3K signaling, as well as KEGG pathways related to immune function and cancer, including pathways in cancer, chronic myeloid leukemia, and non-small cell lung cancer.

Cell-type deconvolution found higher estimated proportions of CD8+ T cells and follicular helper T cells in HIV-positive samples, and lower proportions of naïve CD4+ T cells, resting CD4+ memory T cells, and resting mast cells. Cell-type expression analyses indicated that dysregulated genes were expressed across multiple innate and adaptive immune cell types.

Using prior ART-related gene expression data, 234 HIV-associated differentially expressed genes were classified as ART-affected and 332 as ART-unaffected. Most ART-affected genes showed expression shifts opposite to pre/post-ART comparisons, suggesting ART and viral suppression move expression toward, but do not fully restore, the HIV-negative state. ART-affected genes were enriched for immune, viral process, nucleic acid metabolism, natural killer cell-related, and cancer-related pathways, while ART-unaffected genes were more narrowly linked to T cell biology.

Genetic analyses identified 22,475 eQTLs for 258 differentially expressed genes. Heritability enrichment was significant for blood cell counts and several inflammatory diseases, but not for cancer traits or HIV acquisition. Colocalization was observed for selected genes with immune-related traits and limited cancer traits. Drug target analysis found 111 differentially expressed genes targeted by clinical trial or approved compounds, including 42 targeted by approved drugs.

The study concludes that virally suppressed PLWH on ART show widespread gene dysregulation linked to immune function, cancer-related pathways, and potential pharmacological targets for co-occurring health conditions.

Tesla’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2017 reports total assets of $28.1 billion, total liabilities of $21.9 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $4.7 billion. Cash and cash equivalents were $3.5 billion. For the three months ended September 30, 2017, total revenues were $3.0 billion, gross profit was $449.1 million, and net loss attributable to common stockholders was $619.4 million, or $3.70 per share. For the nine months ended September 30, 2017, total revenues were $8.5 billion and net loss attributable to common stockholders was $1.3 billion.

Tesla operates in automotive and energy generation and storage segments. It acquired Grohmann Engineering in January 2017 for $109.5 million in cash and had completed its SolarCity acquisition in November 2016. During the nine months ended September 30, 2017, Tesla used $570.5 million in operating activities, $3.5 billion in investing activities, and generated $4.1 billion from financing activities. The filing also discusses resale value guarantees, warranties, debt issuances and repayments, accounting standards, equity compensation, lease commitments, and several legal proceedings.

This study examined serum lipid profiles in Thai university students with simple dysmood disorder (SDMD) and first-episode SDMD (FE-SDMD), excluding participants with metabolic syndrome. The authors focused on lecithin-cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT), free cholesterol, ApoE, reverse cholesterol transport (RCT), and atherogenicity indices.

Participants were depressed and healthy control students matched by age, sex, education, and BMI. Depression severity, suicidal behaviors, brooding, and lipid biomarkers were assessed using clinical scales and laboratory assays. Statistical analyses included generalized linear models, regression, and partial least squares analysis.

Compared with controls, SDMD and FE-SDMD participants showed decreased LCAT activity and increased free cholesterol and ApoE. HDLc, ApoA1, RCT, ApoB, and triglycerides did not show substantial changes in SDMD or FE-SDMD. Free cholesterol was positively associated with depression severity, suicidal behaviors, brooding, and the depression phenome, while LCAT was inversely associated with these outcomes. LCAT’s effects on the depression phenome were mediated by free cholesterol and brooding.

Subclinical metabolic syndrome affected lipid profiles, including lower HDLc and RCT and higher triglycerides, ApoE, ApoB/ApoA, and Athero/RCT indices. However, decreased LCAT and elevated free cholesterol were also present in SDMD and FE-SDMD participants without subclinical metabolic syndrome. Interactions between SDMD and subclinical metabolic syndrome were linked to reduced HDLc and RCT and increased ApoB/ApoA.

The authors conclude that SDMD and FE-SDMD are associated with decreased LCAT and elevated free cholesterol and ApoE, suggesting a pre-proatherogenic state distinct from major dysmood disorder and influenced by interactions with subclinical metabolic syndrome. They recommend lipid screening for free cholesterol, LCAT, and ApoE in FE-SDMD.

More than 250 small earthquakes struck near the California-Mexico border since New Year’s Eve, with the strongest a magnitude 3.9 beneath Brawley. The swarm occurred in the southern Brawley Seismic Zone, which connects the San Andreas and Imperial faults and is closely monitored because both can produce damaging earthquakes. Caltech seismologist Egill Hauksson said there was concern the swarm could trigger a magnitude 5 or larger quake, though that possibility had largely receded by Sunday night. The nearby Imperial fault produced major earthquakes in 1940 and 1979, causing deaths, injuries, and infrastructure damage. Previous swarms in the northern Brawley Seismic Zone have raised concerns about larger San Andreas events. Brawley’s mayor said the earthquakes, rain, and New Year’s fireworks unsettled residents and pets.

The speaker expresses humility in assuming the presidency, honors his predecessors and the founding generation, and pledges reliance on fellow officials, the people, and Providence. He describes the United States as prosperous, respected abroad, and successful under institutions built on compromise, limited federal power, and the reserved authority of states and the people. He argues that past fears about taxation, faction, self-government, war, territorial expansion, federal-state conflict, and slavery have largely failed to undermine the Union. He pledges strict adherence to the Constitution, opposition to congressional abolition of slavery in the District of Columbia against slaveholding states’ wishes or interference with slavery in the states, and devotion to national concerns and foreign relations. He endorses friendship with all nations, equal commerce, avoidance of alliances, neutrality in foreign disputes, and defense of national rights. He closes by promising faithful service and invoking divine protection and peace for the country.

Real Madrid drew 2-2 with 17th-placed Levante after Giampaolo Pazzini scored an 89th-minute equaliser on his debut. Isco had put Real ahead after Emmanuel Boateng cancelled out Sergio Ramos’ opener. The result leaves Real fourth in La Liga, 18 points behind Barcelona and two points above Villarreal.

Enron disclosed an informal SEC request for information about related-party transactions involving partnerships formerly run by CFO Andrew Fastow, including LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment. The inquiry followed Enron’s third-quarter announcement of a $1.01 billion charge, a $618 million loss, and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity tied to unwinding partnership arrangements. Enron shares fell about 21% to $20.65, with analysts and investors citing concerns over disclosure, conflicts of interest, off-balance-sheet financing vehicles, possible shareholder dilution, and the company’s credibility. Kenneth Lay said Enron would cooperate fully and sought to address investor concerns through a conference call. Shareholder lawsuits and a class action were filed alleging misrepresentations and failures to disclose financial problems.

The passage says market momentum remains intact but early warnings are emerging. The S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July and 7.8% year to date, though it slipped at the start of August. Volatility and credit spreads are showing seasonal increases, portfolios are increasingly weighted toward tech, and US electricity demand hit a new high. Short-term technicals appear weaker, while medium- and longer-term trend indicators remain healthy.

The lecture demonstrates standard experimental games used to study social preferences. Students play dictator games with candy, apples, and money, varying stakes, communication, and privacy. The professor then introduces the ultimatum game, where responders can accept or reject offers, and discusses public, communication, and strategy-method versions. Finally, students play a trust game, where an investor’s transfer is multiplied before the responder decides how much to return. The professor notes that the classroom demonstrations are less rigorous than formal experiments and says future classes will examine what carefully run studies show and whether lab-game behavior predicts real-world behavior.

The flea flicker is a football trick play designed to look like a run before the ball is returned to the quarterback for a downfield pass. It works by drawing defenders, including defensive backs and safeties, toward the line of scrimmage, creating openings for receivers who initially appear to block before running routes. The play tests defensive discipline and can produce big gains if defenders react to the run fake.

The play is credited to Illinois coach Bob Zuppke, who used it against Penn in 1925 and later said he first called it in 1910 at Oak Park High School. Zuppke said the name came from the “quick flicking action of a dog getting rid of fleas.”

A quarterback can be penalized for intentional grounding on a flea flicker because he has relinquished possession during the play and must throw toward an eligible receiver. The passage gives examples including Michigan’s 2022 flea flicker against TCU, a reverse flea flicker involving Baker Mayfield and Dimitri Flowers, and a fake flea flicker in which the running back fakes a toss back before continuing upfield.

The Ordnance Factories Board said it successfully upgraded 130-mm field guns to 155-mm capability at its Nalanda facility and expects an Army order for 300 guns. The upgrade costs Rs 1 crore per gun versus Rs 15 crore for a new gun, increasing range from 27 km to 36 km.

The lecture discusses sparse matrix elimination for solving Ax = b, focusing on fill-in, where zeros become nonzeros during elimination. The professor explains fill-in through matrix entries and graph representations, where nodes represent rows and edges represent nonzero entries. Reordering unknowns can greatly affect fill-in; matrix-wise this corresponds to permutation matrices, and graph-wise to renumbering nodes.

Several ordering strategies are described, including red-black ordering, approximate minimum degree, and graph separators leading to nested dissection. Minimum degree chooses the next pivot node with the fewest connections to reduce fill-in, while graph separators divide a graph into parts connected through a smaller separator that is ordered last. The lecture also notes that fill-in can be measured by counting nonzeros in the L and U factors, and mentions MATLAB tools such as `spye`, `chol`, and `nnz`.

The ADS868xW includes internal overvoltage protection on each analog input, with external surge, ESD, and EFT protection recommended. When AVDD is 5V and the device is properly powered, the input protection withstands up to ±20V; when AVDD is floating, protection is limited to ±15V. Input resistors, PGA gain-setting resistors, and antiparallel diodes limit current and protect internal circuitry.

The analog front end includes a programmable gain amplifier that supports multiple single-ended and differential input ranges selected through RANGE_SEL[3:0], a second-order antialiasing low-pass filter with a typical 500kHz cutoff, and an integrated ADC driver for charging and discharging SAR ADC sample-and-hold capacitors.

The device supports internal or external 4.096V reference operation. The internal reference is enabled by default and requires a minimum 4.7µF capacitor on REFIO. External reference mode is selected by disabling the internal reference and applying 4.096V to REFIO; REFCAP requires at least 10µF plus a nearby 1µF capacitor. The internal reference can shift from solder reflow stress, and the reference buffer has typical 0.5ppm/°C drift and maximum 2ppm/°C drift.

The ADC supports bipolar and unipolar single-ended or differential inputs and outputs straight-binary data. Alarm features include programmable input high and low thresholds with hysteresis and fixed AVDD alarms at typical 4.7V and 5.3V. Alarm flags can be read through the alarm pin, registers, or appended to output data.

Communication uses a multiSPI interface with standard SPI, dual-SDO, source-synchronous, and daisy-chain options. The device has RESET, ACQ, and CONV states controlled by RST and CONVST/CS. Data frames begin on CONVST/CS falling edge and end on the rising edge; 32 SCLKs form an optimal frame. The device includes nine configuration registers controlling device ID, reset and power, SDI/SDO protocols, data output, input range and reference, and alarms.

Application information describes use in industrial analog input modules with an ADS8681W and MUX36D08 for eight differential channels. The device provides programmable low-power NAP and power-down modes. Layout guidance recommends separating analog and digital routing, using close decoupling capacitors on AVDD, DVDD, REFIO, and REFCAP, and maintaining short low-impedance ground connections.

Contractor’s Sand and Gravel petitioned for review after the Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission vacated an ALJ’s award of attorneys’ fees and expenses under the Equal Access to Justice Act. The fees arose from CSG’s successful defense against MSHA citations alleging that its crusher grounding system violated 30 C.F.R. § 56.12025. The citation claimed frame grounding was prohibited, though the regulation required only that electrical circuits be grounded and did not forbid frame grounding or require fourth-wire grounding. CSG presented undisputed evidence that its equipment was grounded; the Secretary offered no contrary testing or evidence.

The court held that the Commission had jurisdiction to review the ALJ’s fee award, rejecting CSG’s argument that the ALJ’s substantial-justification finding was final. However, the court ruled that the Secretary’s position in the underlying Mine Act proceedings was not substantially justified. It found that enforcing a prohibition not contained in the regulation was unreasonable, that prior administrative decisions had rejected similar theories, and that any safety concerns should have been addressed through rulemaking. The court reversed the Commission, restored the ALJ’s award, and remanded for determination of additional costs for CSG’s petition for review.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated September 11, 2015, reporting that Bradford L. Smith was appointed President and Chief Legal Officer effective that date. Smith, age 56, previously served as General Counsel and Executive Vice President, Legal and Corporate Affairs. He joined Microsoft in 1993 and had served as General Counsel since 2002.

September jobs data differed sharply between surveys: the establishment survey showed job losses, while the household survey reported 906,000 more people working, record employment of 154.3 million, falling unemployment, a larger labor force, higher participation, and a 4.2 percent unemployment rate. Wages rose 2.9 percent. Beth Ann Bovino said the labor market appeared stronger than the establishment report suggested, possibly because hurricane-affected businesses could not respond to the BLS survey. Markets were largely unfazed, and prior hurricane periods showed payroll rebounds after weak initial reports.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2020. Net sales rose to $88.9 billion in Q2 2020 from $63.4 billion in Q2 2019, and to $164.4 billion for the first six months of 2020 from $123.1 billion a year earlier. Q2 net income increased to $5.2 billion from $2.6 billion, while diluted EPS rose to $10.30 from $5.22. Operating income increased to $5.8 billion in Q2 2020 from $3.1 billion in Q2 2019.

Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash were $37.8 billion at June 30, 2020. Total assets increased to $258.3 billion from $225.2 billion at December 31, 2019, and stockholders’ equity rose to $73.7 billion from $62.1 billion. Long-term debt increased to $33.1 billion, including $10.0 billion of senior unsecured notes issued in June 2020.

Amazon reported three segments: North America, International, and AWS. Q2 2020 sales were $55.4 billion for North America, $22.7 billion for International, and $10.8 billion for AWS. AWS operating income was $3.4 billion, North America operating income was $2.1 billion, and International operating income was $345 million.

The company stated that COVID-19 affected operations, demand, fulfillment, supply chains, and costs. It incurred more than $4 billion in COVID-19-related costs in Q2 2020 and hired 175,000 additional employees to increase fulfillment capacity. Amazon also changed the estimated useful life of servers from three to four years, reducing depreciation and amortization expense and increasing net income.

The passage advises starting saving and investing early, emphasizing that time, frequent contributions, and compounding can significantly increase wealth. It gives an example where saving €50 monthly from age 20 at 5% annual return reaches €75,000 by age 60, while starting at 40 requires €185 monthly. It recommends separating savings from spending, investing regularly, reinvesting interest or dividends, and reviewing personal spending habits to redirect money into investments. The article is presented for educational and informational purposes only and is not investment, tax, or legal advice.

Malik Nabers’ season-ending torn ACL and meniscus at MetLife Stadium has renewed concerns about its FieldTurf surface. An opposing team executive said players are “petrified” of playing there, and NFLPA interim director David White raised the issue during a Giants visit. At least 15 players have suffered knee ligament or Achilles tears at MetLife since 2020. Although players overwhelmingly prefer grass, the NFL says injury rates have not shown a current turf disadvantage and has no plans to change MetLife’s surface.

The speaker discussed Soviet concerns about trusteeship arrangements for detached territories, including Italian colonies and territories detached from Japan, and agreed to share relevant documents with the Russians. Both sides agreed League of Nations members should initiate its liquidation. The Soviet representative reiterated support for including Soviet Republics as initial members while excluding associated nations and neutrals. They briefly discussed possible seats for the organization, including Pays de Gex, but no decision followed. Reviewing Latin American suggestions, he accepted that ideas such as political independence, territorial integrity, peaceful change, treaty revision, and international law could be included, possibly in the preamble. He opposed proposals strengthening the Assembly and Court at the Council’s expense and criticized objections to permanent-member voting in disputes involving them. The speaker said acceptance of the proposed voting formula might weaken such objections and agreed to provide an analysis of Council functions under that formula. The meeting ended amicably.

Researchers found that cancer cells can transfer mitochondria into neighboring fibroblasts through thin nanotube-like structures, reprogramming the fibroblasts to grow faster and increase activity of cancer-linked genes. When injected with cancer cells in mouse ears, these altered fibroblasts promoted tumor growth. Sabine Werner’s team identified MIRO2 as a key protein that moves mitochondria to the cell edge where transfer tubes form; without MIRO2, cancer cells could not send mitochondria to fibroblasts. Other researchers note that cancer cells may also transfer mitochondria to immune cells, weakening their cancer-fighting abilities, and that the field of mitochondrial transfer is still developing.

The speaker says there is little carryover or added rivalry from last year and that a potential player return does not change their approach. They respect him but are focused on their own play. They acknowledge home-crowd advantage, believe they played well despite early losses, and remain confident they can win a road game.

The passage argues that philosophy of education is often treated as peripheral to mainstream educational research, which is typically framed around quantitative and qualitative empirical methods. Major research methods texts rarely present philosophy of education as a form of research, instead separating ethical, theoretical, and normative issues from the core of scholarship. As a result, students and colleagues may view philosophy of education as lacking the features of “real” research, such as data gathering and analysis.

The author connects this marginalization to academic precarity. Doctoral students, facing uncertain job markets, often avoid areas perceived as nonessential or professionally risky. Philosophy of education can appear impractical compared with fields more aligned with grant funding, high-impact journals, and empirical research expectations. Research assessment systems that emphasize external funding, citation counts, and journal impact factors further disadvantage philosophers of education, whose work often does not fit those measures.

The passage also critiques a “scientistic” orientation in educational research, especially the privileging of randomized controlled trials, large-scale quantitative studies, systematic reviews, and claims of generalizability. The author argues that such approaches can oversimplify educational phenomena, neglect contextual differences, and ignore ethical questions about what it means for an intervention to “work.” Philosophical inquiry is presented as important for examining assumptions about evidence, impact, effectiveness, and educational aims.

The author reviews how philosophers of education have responded by defending the field, encouraging students to resist narrow performance measures, and emphasizing intellectual development, identity, collaboration, and value-driven inquiry. However, the field itself has long been internally contested over its purpose, methods, history, rigor, and relevance. Its sense of precarity is not new; historical examples show recurring concerns about marginalization, applied research pressures, and the field’s legitimacy.

The passage challenges nostalgic ideas of past “golden years” in philosophy of education, suggesting they may be partial, self-serving, and historically limited. Rather than seeking a lost unity, the author proposes recognizing the field’s pluralism, internal contestation, reflexivity, and criticality as strengths. A starting point for renewal is to question the dominant assumption that educational research must be empirical.

Penn State’s White Building renovations, underway since summer 2016, are expected to finish by late March, with additional improvements continuing through the semester. Updates include a renovated lobby, new registration desks, stairwell, elevator, and entrance changes to improve traffic flow, monitoring, safety, policy compliance, and future usage tracking.

The speaker presents the presidential oath as a public covenant between the President and the people to uphold the Constitution, enforce laws equally, and protect civil and political rights. He reflects on the nation’s first century under the Constitution, noting growth in population, territory, wealth, education, religion, charity, temperance, and opportunity, while acknowledging remaining hardship and lawlessness.

He supports protective tariffs, domestic manufacturing, mining, and economic diversification, especially in formerly agricultural Southern states, and rejects sectional executive policy. He emphasizes uniform enforcement of all laws, condemns nullification, mob action, corporate lawbreaking, and denial of legal rights.

The address calls for stricter naturalization standards while maintaining hospitality to immigration, a foreign policy of noninterference in Europe, resistance to European control in the Americas, protection of citizens abroad, peaceful diplomacy, and fair acquisition of naval and commercial privileges. It urges civil-service reform, efficient appointments, economy in public spending, reduction of surplus revenue without harming protective tariffs, naval modernization, American steamship lines, better pensions for Union veterans and families, admission of new western states, secure land titles, election-law reform, ballot protection, education as a remedy for electoral ignorance, and moderation of party conflict. The speaker closes by expressing confidence in the nation’s future if justice, mercy, education, virtue, and patriotism are upheld.

The global visceral pain market is expected to reach USD 14.22 billion by 2024, driven by a growing geriatric population, rising prevalence, and increased awareness. North America led the market in 2016, while Asia Pacific is projected to grow fastest at a 6.2% CAGR. Analgesics dominated therapeutics with 60.4% share, and Crohn’s disease was the largest indication segment with 41.4%. Key players include Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson, AbbVie, Takeda, Allergan, and AstraZeneca, with growth supported by R&D, collaborations, healthcare spending, and government initiatives.

Superannuation tax changes coming into force in July are expected to increase self-managed super funds, with over two million Australians projected to have them within 15 years. Key changes include a $1.6 million transfer balance cap, reduced concessional and non-concessional contribution caps, changes to transition-to-retirement pensions, spouse tax offset thresholds, tax-deductible contributions, and removal of some provisions. The passage says more professionals, self-employed people, younger Australians, and women are setting up SMSFs, while older male business owners remain the largest sector by fund value but are declining in number.

The Finance Ministry amended Rule 80 of the Compendium of Rules on Advances, retaining provisions for advances to families of government servants who die in service. The advance under Rule 79 must not exceed Rs 25,000, applies from the memorandum date, and already sanctioned cases will not be reopened.

Players discussed injuries, the physical toll of a long playoff run, and the team’s confidence. Jason Garrison described a broken play leading to a chance for Fil and said the next game is a must-win. J.T. Brown said the team stays focused, avoids outside noise, and aims to rebound after losses.

The passage proposes a global, regulator-reported database for significant AI incidents in financial markets. It argues that AI adoption in finance is increasing rapidly, while existing public AI incident databases miss many financial-sector events because key reports are confidential, market-sensitive, or require finance-specific metrics. Current regulations and fragmented reporting systems do not adequately address AI-specific risks such as opaque trading strategies, market manipulation, systemic risk propagation, and disinformation-driven volatility.

Drawing lessons from healthcare and aviation incident reporting, the paper recommends a semi-public framework that supports learning while protecting confidential business information. The proposed database adapts post-trade reporting structures and includes 15 mandatory fields covering market context, volume metrics, price impact, and AI-specific information. It deliberately omits temporal data and uses percentage-based metrics to reduce the risk of identifying firms or exposing proprietary strategies. Significant incidents are defined as AI-driven trades causing more than 5% price deviation or more than 20% volume anomaly versus the 30-day average.

Using 2,999 synthetic records generated from 20 identified algorithmic trading incidents, the paper demonstrates two use cases: systemic risk monitoring and market manipulation detection. The analysis suggests AI system type affects trading behaviour more than geography and that risks may propagate similarly across regions, supporting coordinated global oversight. Clustering analysis identifies trading zones linked to stable activity, anomalous patterns, transition states, irregular behaviour, and strategic trading.

The paper concludes that a global AI incident reporting framework could improve transparency, accountability, cross-border coordination, and regulatory capacity while preserving sensitive market information.

Sweden’s unemployment stayed at 7.3 percent in July 2017, unchanged from a year earlier, but unemployment was 3.9 percent among Swedish-born people and 21.8 percent among foreign-born people. A record 76,561 foreigners were registered in Arbetsförmedlingen’s Introduction Programme, up from 59,362. Long-term unemployment also rose slightly, partly due to programme participants, while Arbetsförmedlingen warned it needs more government funding.

Version 2 of the SEV-ES GHCB specification adds enhanced SEV-ES support, initial SEV-SNP support, and hypervisor feature advertisement through a FEATURES bitmap. Later revisions add updates for 64-bit SEV-SNP guest request sequence numbers, VMGEXIT error reporting, VLEK GUID definition, APIC ID list retrieval, multi-VMPL support, SEV-ES page state change notification, EFI protocols for SEV-SNP secrets and CPUID pages, SEV trusted IO, Secure AVIC, GHCB unregister support, and hardware debug behavior changes.

The GHCB enables guest-hypervisor communication through a shared, 4K-aligned page and MSR 0xc001_0130. The GHCB MSR protocol supports negotiation, CPUID requests, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration and unregistration, page state changes, VMPL switching, feature bitmap requests, and guest termination. SEV-SNP guests must register a GHCB GPA before first use, and hypervisors must validate registered GHCB use.

The document describes GHCB negotiation examples for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests, VMGEXIT handling, valid non-automatic exit events, required GHCB state fields, error reporting via SW_EXITINFO fields, and specific NAE handling for IO, MSR, MMIO, page state changes, SNP guest requests, extended guest requests, AP creation, restricted injection doorbell pages, IPI, timers, APIC ID lists, VMPL switching, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, and termination.

SEV-SNP support includes secrets page reserved-area fields for VMPL message sequence numbers, AP jump table address, and guest usage; an EFI Confidential Computing Blob protocol for secrets and CPUID pages; and extended request formats for certificates and trusted IO data. SEV-TIO guest requests communicate device measurements, certificates, and SPDM attestation reports.

The specification covers SMP booting challenges under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, AP reset hold behavior, AP jump table transfer between firmware and OS, SNP AP creation using VMSA pages, and vCPU hotplug support when SNP AP creation is used. It also defines NMI completion signaling, hardware debug register virtualization behavior, lack of SMM and nested virtualization support, and restricted injection using a shared #HV doorbell page with PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields for interrupt and non-maskable event notification.

Derivatives are financial contracts whose value depends on an underlying asset such as a commodity, stock, currency, index, or interest rate. Common types include futures, options, forwards, swaps, and CFDs. They are used for hedging, speculation, and accessing difficult-to-trade markets, and may trade on exchanges or OTC markets, with OTC instruments generally carrying greater risk.

Futures and forwards obligate parties to trade an asset at a future date, while options give buyers the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell at a strike price before expiration. CFDs exchange the price difference between opening and closing a trade.

The passage emphasizes that derivatives trading is risky, often due to leverage, uncertainty, poor product structure, and cognitive biases. It recommends trading only for hedging or with a specific backtested plan, warning that derivatives can damage capital if misunderstood or misused. It also discusses hedging equity portfolios with put options and cites backtested put-selling research showing slightly higher compound returns than the S&P 500 with lower volatility over one studied period.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated July 21, 2015, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2015. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and was not deemed “filed” under Section 18 of the Exchange Act.

The paper compares pretrained large language models and small proprietary Transformer models for financial transaction understanding, specifically mapping messy POS transaction text to merchant IDs. Existing regex and Enhanced String Distance methods covered about 80% of transactions but were unscalable and left Rawcleansed transactions unmanaged. The study evaluated Encoder-Only, Decoder-Only, and Encoder-Decoder approaches using open-source models and proprietary versions trained on transaction data.

Results showed that fine-tuned LLMs improved over out-of-the-box models, but small proprietary models achieved comparable or better accuracy with far fewer parameters, faster training, lower cost, and lower latency. The Proprietary Decoder-Only model reached 72.07% weighted accuracy with 1.7M parameters, close to Llama3’s 72.89% with 8B parameters, while meeting the inference requirement. Experiments found that larger models were not always better; tokenizer choice, vocabulary size, embedding size, and model depth affected performance differently by architecture.

For deployment, the Proprietary Decoder-Only model was applied to Rawcleansed transactions while retaining existing Rulebased and ESD systems. It correctly predicted 72% of Rawcleansed transactions, increasing overall transaction coverage from 80% to 94% and producing an estimated annual cost reduction of $13.2 million.

IHE editors discuss federal policy developments affecting higher education, including cuts to minority-serving institution funding, restrictions on international students, student borrowing rule making, and the administration’s “Compact for Academic Excellence.”

Sunderland manager David Moyes named an injury-hit team to face Liverpool, with Lamine Kone and Victor Anichebe ruled out and Donald Love replacing suspended Billy Jones. GOG’s 2017 Piñata Madness event lets users buy $3 “piñatas” containing random games valued between $6 and $45, excluding expansions, soundtracks, and other non-game items. The U.S. Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter-point to 1%–1.25%, its third increase in six months, and signaled one more possible hike this year. It also plans to gradually reduce its US$4.5 trillion bond portfolio, which could raise long-term rates. The Fed acted despite sluggish growth, citing solid hiring and a 4.3% unemployment rate, while inflation remains below its 2% target. Political uncertainty and low inflation could slow future hikes. President Trump is expected to fill three Fed board vacancies, potentially shifting policy toward a more hawkish stance. Fed Chair Janet Yellen’s term ends in February, and Trump has not indicated whether he will renominate her.

The Horns offense uses a 1-4 high alignment with two high post screeners to create mid screen/roll options in either direction, reduce baseline help, and generate drives, post rolls, pull-up jumpers, kick-out shots, and low-post opportunities. It is effective against pressure defenses and difficult to disrupt by forcing the ballhandler away from one screen. Success depends on coordinated execution, timing, footwork, nonverbal communication, and proper reads by the ballhandler and screeners.

The passage outlines counters to defensive reactions such as trailing, sagging, going under, switching, showing and recovering, cheating over screens, overplaying posts, and trapping. It also describes Horns variations used to fit personnel, including High Post Rub, Twin Side Screens, Loop Entry, Weakside Split, Picket Fence, and Hand Back Lob. Installation emphasizes breakdown drills, scrimmaging, individual skill work, and scouting opponents to anticipate defensive techniques and adjust alignments, entries, and matchups.

The passage describes Blackwell GPUs GB202, GB203, and GB205 for different graphics segments. Chess originated in India about 1,500 years ago and is described as a complex strategy game involving tactics, decision-making, planning, logic, memory, concentration, and creativity. The passage presents chess as more than a game, describing it as a science, art, and educational activity with potential cognitive, personal, and social benefits.

Research cited in the passage links chess with improved planning, critical thinking, concentration, problem-solving, self-confidence, self-control, observation, social interaction, and academic skills. Chess may support learning by requiring players to evaluate alternatives, anticipate consequences, receive immediate feedback, and adapt strategies. Studies discussed report possible benefits for mathematics, reading, spatial ability, logical thinking, IQ, and general cognitive development, though some findings are described as speculative or limited.

The passage emphasizes a possible relationship between chess and mathematics because both involve strategy, pattern recognition, prediction, analysis, and problem-solving. Some studies found chess training improved mathematics achievement, including among special education students, while others caution that chess should not be credited with improving basic mathematical skills directly. Reading improvements are also discussed, possibly through visualization and comprehension, but claims remain uncertain.

Chess-playing students are described as more adaptable to school, more academically successful, more confident, and more optimistic, according to some studies and teacher reports. Chess may also help students develop patience, perseverance, sportsmanship, emotional control, and friendships. Children may learn chess more easily than adults because they adapt schemas faster, simplify learning, and tolerate mistakes better.

The passage also notes limitations in chess research. Positive outcomes may be influenced by the Pygmalion effect, teacher effort, special learning environments, student motivation, prior intelligence, or practice rather than chess alone. Studies often lack ideal experimental design, active control groups, random assignment, or sufficient measurement of abstract traits such as motivation and attitude. The relationship between chess, intelligence, expertise, academic achievement, and cognitive development remains complex and requires further detailed, longitudinal, qualitative, quantitative, and mixed-method research.

California’s 2016 Gun Violence Restraining Order law led to 190 court orders in 2016-17 allowing temporary firearm removal from people deemed dangerous. AMD Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) enables secure, non-persistent runtime updates to selected AMD-provided binary firmware components and settings without requiring a BIOS reflash or system reset. It is intended for high-priority runtime issues and security mitigations, not for x86 BIOS code such as SMM, AGESA, UEFI, or run-once boot code like ABL. SFS updates do not persist across reboots and are interim steps between BIOS releases.

SFS packages target specific PI releases, base patch levels, firmware versions, and system states. Customers are responsible for validating patches and providing an SFS Deployment Agent to initiate and track updates through the PSP/ASP driver. Packages may patch registers, replace microprocessor firmware images, or update parts of firmware packages.

SFS uses version tracking through the SFS Patch Level (SFSPL), individual firmware and Security Patch Level (SPL) values, and System Patch Level (SYSPL) for run-once code effects. AMD cryptographically signs all SFS packages; customers may optionally co-sign packages to require customer approval before deployment. BIOS support for SFS and co-signing is opt-in and configured through BIOS tokens.

The AMD Security Processor verifies signatures before applying packages and acts as the root of trust for detection for AMD-signed firmware. If co-signing is enabled, the customer BIOS provides a public key during early boot, and updates must authenticate against both customer and AMD signatures.

SFS packages must be applied at runtime, sequentially, and in numerical order. The ASP protects package memory, verifies signatures, executes the patch, updates patch-level information, and returns status. Version information can be queried through SFS commands. Packages are named by family, AGESA release, and increasing SFS number, and must match the firmware combination on the target system.

Hollywood Bowl Group’s full-year results were well received, with shares rising nearly 8%. The paper evaluates reasoning in voice-interactive AI systems and identifies a consistent “Voice Reasoning Gap” (VRG): voice models perform much worse than text models on reasoning tasks, especially complex multi-step problems. In one example, GPT-realtime scores 6.1% on math problems, while GPT-5 scores 74.8%. The authors argue the gap is not mainly due to acoustic understanding, since current voice models can transcribe and analyze audio well, but instead reflects a tension between low-latency streaming speech and the iterative, revisable computation used in text-based reasoning.

To study this, the authors introduce VERA, a benchmark of 2,931 voice-optimized episodes across five tracks: Math, Web, Science, Context, and Factual recall. Items are adapted from established datasets through filtering, TTS-aware rewriting, quality validation, and speech generation. VERA enables comparison across commercial voice APIs, open voice models, end-to-end voice systems, text-only models, and a cascade baseline called LiveAnswer.

Results show an average 40.4-point accuracy drop for voice models relative to text baselines. The gap is moderate on factual retrieval but severe on complex reasoning, with voice models generally plateauing below 10–11% accuracy. Increasing thinking time does not resolve the issue: Audio Flamingo 3’s thinking mode greatly increases latency but does not improve accuracy. LiveAnswer, which separates reasoning from narration using GPT-5, improves performance but still falls short of text-only GPT-5 and fails badly on context tasks. Speech clarity also does not explain the gap.

The authors find architecture-specific failure patterns. Native streaming models tend to produce fluent but incorrect answers, while cascade systems more often introduce unsupported facts, off-target responses, and logical contradictions. End-to-end systems show other failure modes, including disengagement or off-target outputs.

The paper concludes that the VRG is a systemic architectural challenge rather than a simple engineering issue. It suggests future voice assistants may need architectures that decouple reasoning from real-time narration through editable internal states, asynchronous processing, chunked reasoning, and better coordination between reasoning and speech generation.

Reuters interviewed Rohingya fighters and refugees in Bangladesh who described ARSA as a poorly equipped insurgent group that recruited many villagers shortly before its Aug. 25 attacks on Myanmar police posts. Fighters said they were promised firearms but often attacked with knives, sticks, homemade explosives and limited training, with coordination through WhatsApp. ARSA says it fights for Rohingya rights, while Myanmar calls it an Islamist extremist group and says it coerces support. Analysts warned that desperation in refugee camps could strengthen militancy or attract transnational Islamist groups. Several fighters said they remained willing to fight despite heavy losses and the Myanmar military counteroffensive that drove more than half a million Rohingya into Bangladesh.

NVIDIA’s GA102 and GA104 are GA10x-class Ampere architecture GPUs that build on Turing and target gaming, professional visualization, AI, compute, and data center workloads. GA102 is used in the GeForce RTX 3090, RTX 3080, RTX A6000, and A40, while GA104 is used in the RTX 3070. GA10x GPUs are up to 1.7x faster than Turing in raster graphics and up to 2x faster in ray tracing, with up to 1.9x better power efficiency at the same performance level.

GA102 is fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm 8N NVIDIA Custom Process, contains 28.3 billion transistors, and includes CUDA Cores, second-generation RT Cores, and third-generation Tensor Cores. A full GA102 has 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, 336 Tensor Cores, seven GPCs, 84 SMs, 112 ROPs, a 384-bit memory subsystem, and 6,144 KB of L2 cache. GA10x SMs double FP32 throughput compared with Turing, increase L1/shared memory capacity and bandwidth, and support concurrent RT, graphics, and compute workloads.

The second-generation RT Core doubles ray/triangle intersection testing throughput over Turing and adds hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores support new data types including TF32 and BF16, provide sparsity support, and accelerate AI features such as DLSS, AI denoising, NVIDIA Broadcast, and NVIDIA Canvas. GA10x also supports GDDR6X memory, PCIe Gen 4, third-generation NVLink on select GPUs, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4a, AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-generation NVENC encoding.

The GeForce RTX 3090 targets 8K HDR gaming with 10,496 CUDA Cores and 24 GB of GDDR6X memory, while the RTX 3080 offers up to 2x the performance of the RTX 2080 and the RTX 3070 rivals the RTX 2080 Ti. The RTX A6000 combines 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, 336 Tensor Cores, and 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, expandable to 96 GB with NVLink. The A40 is designed for data center visual computing, virtual workstations, rendering, simulation, AI, and compute workloads, with similar core counts and memory size to the RTX A6000.

Additional GA10x technologies include RTX IO, which uses GPU-based loading and decompression with Microsoft DirectStorage to reduce CPU workload and improve asset streaming, and Error Detection and Replay for GDDR6X memory transmission errors. NVIDIA states that GA10x Ampere GPUs provide up to 2x improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI, enabling higher-frame-rate ray-traced gaming, professional rendering, and accelerated workstation and data center workloads.

Randall Margraves, father of three daughters abused by Larry Nassar, tried to attack the former sports doctor in a Michigan courtroom after Judge Janice Cunningham denied his request for time alone with Nassar in a locked room. The TLV32xx input range extends from 200 mV below V– to 200 mV above V+, with no output phase inversion within this range. Inputs include ESD clamps, must not exceed supply rails by more than 200 mV, and should be current-limited to 10 mA or less, often using series resistance. Unused inputs should not be tied together; they must be held within the valid input range with at least 50 mV differential voltage.

The TLV32xx family includes 1.8 mV internal hysteresis. Comparator trip behavior depends on threshold voltage, offset voltage, and hysteresis. TLV321x devices use push-pull outputs capable of sourcing and sinking current, while TLV322x devices use open-drain outputs that can be pulled up to 0 V to 5.5 V. Push-pull outputs must not be connected to other outputs or supply rails, and unused push-pull outputs should float. Open-drain outputs support wired-OR and logic translation; TI recommends 100 µA to 1 mA pull-up current, and unused outputs may float or connect to V–.

The devices include ESD protection to V+ and V– and a power-on-reset circuit. During startup, after V+ crosses 1.65 V, POR holds the output low for up to 32 µs before the output reflects the differential input state.

Comparator operation compares VIN to VREF; output logic can be inverted by swapping inputs. Propagation delay depends on transition direction and overdrive voltage, with smaller overdrive increasing delay. External hysteresis can reduce chatter when inputs move slowly near the switching threshold and may be implemented with resistor networks in inverting or non-inverting configurations.

A typical low-side current-sensing application uses an amplifier and comparator to signal when the amplified shunt voltage exceeds 1.1 V. Proper bypassing with a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor near each supply pin is critical due to fast output edges. Layout should minimize input-output coupling, use solid grounding, place input series resistors near the device, and may use output series resistance or controlled-impedance routing for long traces. TI notes that application information is not part of the component specification and must be validated by customers.

The Supreme Court considered whether it has jurisdiction to review Michael Bowe’s challenge to the dismissal of his request to file a successive Section 2255 habeas motion attacking a federal firearm conviction. Bowe argues that Section 2244(b)(3)(E), which bars appeals or certiorari from grants or denials of authorization for successive applications, does not block review because the court of appeals dismissed his request under Section 2244(b)(1) rather than denying authorization under Section 2244(b)(3)(C). He also argues, with the federal government, that Section 2244(b)(1) applies only to state inmates because it refers to Section 2254. Justices questioned both Bowe’s jurisdictional theory and the government’s contrary position. An appointed friend of the court defended applying Section 2244(b)(1) to federal prisoners. The questioning focused mainly on jurisdiction, but there did not appear to be five votes to hold that Section 2244(b)(1) applies to federal inmates if the court reaches that issue.

The speaker is pleased with the team’s series-opening win but says the next game is crucial and could shape the series. Python is an open-source, high-level programming language widely used in algorithmic trading, data analysis, quantitative research, risk management, and backtesting. Traders use Python to build trading algorithms, analyze large datasets, create execution and risk management systems, and test strategies on historical data. Its popularity comes from readability, free commercial-use packages, extensive libraries such as Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn, and Zipline, and a large developer community.

Backtesting evaluates a trading strategy by applying coded rules to historical price data, but it does not guarantee future success and should account for trading costs. Common Python backtesting frameworks include PyAlgoTrade, Bt, Backtrader, Fastquant, LEAN/QuantConnect, and Zipline. The passage highlights QuantConnect and Backtrader as popular options, while noting that the best framework depends on the trader’s needs.

Python can support automated and live trading, but the passage argues that beginners may benefit from existing trading software such as Amibroker or Tradestation because trading success depends more on strategy quality and market interpretation than coding ability. It also describes Quantified Strategies as a source of backtested trading strategies, Python code, and plain-English trading rules.

The Kentucky Supreme Court reviewed how KRS 342.120(4) applied to workers’ compensation liability for prior occupational disability after a subsequent injury. David Eugene Bunch had serious prior back injuries and surgeries before a 1977 work-related fall left him totally and permanently disabled. The Workers’ Compensation Board found the employer liable for 15%, the Special Fund liable for 30%, and excluded 55% as preexisting occupational disability. The circuit court affirmed, but the Court of Appeals ordered the 55% apportioned to the Special Fund.

The Supreme Court reversed the Court of Appeals and affirmed the circuit court. It held that the proper test is the degree of occupational disability existing immediately before the later injury, not merely whether the employee was working. Prior occupational disability, categorized as active disability, is not compensable, and any contrary language in prior cases was overruled.

The lecture introduces data structures for memory hierarchies, where computers have multiple cache and memory levels with increasing size and latency. It defines the external memory model, which considers two levels: a fast cache of size M and an infinite slow disk, both divided into blocks of size B. The cost measured is the number of block transfers; computation and cache access are free. Scanning N items costs ceiling(N/B) transfers, and B-trees support searches in log base B+1 of N transfers, which is optimal in the comparison model.

The lecture surveys external memory results: optimal sorting costs (N/B) log base M/B of (N/B), permuting costs the minimum of sorting time and N in the indivisible model, and buffer trees provide amortized dynamic operations related to sorting, with delayed queries and batch updates. Buffer trees also support priority queue operations such as insert and delete-min in the sorting-bound-per-operation time.

The cache-oblivious model is then introduced. Algorithms do not know B or M and look like RAM algorithms, while cache replacement is assumed optimal for analysis. LRU or FIFO replacement can approximate optimal behavior within constant factors using a larger cache. Cache-oblivious algorithms are good for all B and M simultaneously, which helps with multilevel hierarchies and changing cache parameters. In this model, scanning remains efficient, search trees can achieve order log base B+1 of N for search, insert, and delete, sorting achieves the same external-memory bound, but optimal permuting with the external-memory minimum bound is impossible. Priority queues achieve the optimal bound under a tall-cache assumption.

The lecture focuses on cache-oblivious search trees. For static search, it uses a balanced binary search tree laid out in van Emde Boas order: recursively split the tree at the middle level, lay out the top subtree, then the bottom subtrees. For any B, a root-to-leaf path visits order log base B of N blocks because subtrees of size less than B occupy at most two blocks and have height theta(log B).

For dynamic cache-oblivious B-trees, the lecture builds on order file maintenance, which stores ordered elements in a linear-size array with gaps and supports insertions and deletions by moving elements in intervals of amortized log² N size using scans. Keys are stored in this ordered file, with a van Emde Boas-layout tree above it storing subtree maxima. Searches use the tree and take log base B of N transfers. Updates modify the ordered file and propagate changes upward in postorder, yielding amortized update cost log base B of N plus log² N/B.

Finally, indirection improves update time. The previous structure stores only one representative, such as the minimum, from each bottom group of theta(log N) items. Searches scan the relevant bottom group, adding only log N/B cost. Splitting and merging bottom groups slow top-level updates by a factor of log N, reducing the extra update term. This yields cache-oblivious B-tree performance matching B-trees for searches and updates, aside from the ordered file maintenance component deferred to the next lecture.

Electronic Arts will go private in a $55 billion all-cash deal backed by Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners, the largest leveraged buyout in history. CEO Andrew Wilson will remain in charge. The deal offers shareholders a roughly 25% premium and removes Wall Street pressure after EA’s stock was hit by outlook cuts tied to “EA Sports FC.” Analysts said private ownership may still bring demands, while EA faces challenges including reliance on older franchises, mobile gaming struggles, and competition for “Battlefield 6.” Wilson may focus on innovation through generative AI and esports expansion.

The SNB and ECB are assessing a possible link between Switzerland’s SIC network and the Eurosystem’s TIPS platform to enable faster cross-border transfers. The exploratory phase runs through 2026 and will examine technical, economic, legal, compliance, operational, settlement risk, cybersecurity, liquidity, and regulatory issues. If implemented, it could reduce reliance on correspondent banking and improve payment speed, cost, transparency, and interoperability.

Commissioner.COM sent a Nov. 17, 2001 fantasy football report for “Get Bad with Yourself,” including SportsLine promotions, the “Luccis Losers” roster, injury notes, and NFL player updates. Luccis Losers had 8 active and 7 reserve players, with injuries to Cameron Cleeland, Rob Johnson, and Kurt Warner. Colorado Boy Scout Troop 1532, formed in 2014, is made up almost entirely of refugees from places including Burma, Rwanda and Nepal. Leaders say the troop helps children adjust to American culture while giving them a safe place to be themselves. Founded by Dr. P.J. Parmar with a Denver-area refugee clinic, the troop often meets only for camping trips because families face transportation, work and financial challenges. Leaders also cite difficulties maintaining membership, finding adult leaders, and focusing on merit badges and rank advancement. Despite discipline issues, parents and scouts say the troop teaches respect, leadership and confidence.

The speaker says the team can play better in the upcoming games against Boston and is excited to compete for the Stanley Cup with home-ice advantage. He emphasizes reliance on top players, team accountability, and handling adversity against a strong Bruins opponent. He says offensive struggles are a team issue, not a goaltending issue, and confirms Roberto is starting. ChatGPT is an AI system developed by OpenAI and launched in November 2022, with ChatGPT 4 released in March 2023 as a paid upgrade. The passage explains that ChatGPT can support trading by analyzing market data, generating trading ideas, brainstorming strategies, and producing code for backtesting, but it is not a trading platform, does not provide financial advice, and cannot be expected to generate reliably profitable strategies on request.

The article describes using ChatGPT by first clarifying the intended trading use, then asking it for strategy ideas and deeper explanations. The lecture introduces batch arguments (BARGs), also called SNARGs for Batch NP, which allow a prover to convince a verifier that multiple NP instances are all true using a single proof. A BARG consists of generator, prover, and verifier algorithms with a CRS. It is succinct when the proof is shorter than the total witness length. Completeness requires honest proofs to verify, and soundness requires cheating proofs for false batches to be accepted only with negligible probability.

BARGs are motivated by batching in proof systems, analogous to aggregation in signatures, and are used as building blocks for SNARGs for all of P. The lecture notes that Gentry-Wichs impossibility results make general SNARGs for NP difficult under falsifiable assumptions, but BARGs avoid contradiction because a proof of size near the witness length can still be succinct relative to k witnesses.

The main theorem states that BARGs can be constructed from Learning With Errors, with proof size depending polynomially on the relation circuit size, log k, and the security parameter, and with verification decomposable into preprocessing over all instances and a short online phase.

The construction begins from a simplified Kilian-style protocol: the prover creates PCPs for each instance-witness pair, arranges them as rows of a matrix, hashes each column, receives a PCP query, and opens queried columns. The verifier checks hash consistency and runs PCP verification for each instance. To make the protocol non-interactive, the verifier’s random query is replaced by a correlation-intractable hash of the first-round message.

A difficulty arises because the relation needed for correlation intractability may not be sparse when ordinary compressing hashes have many PCP preimages. The lecture introduces somewhere statistical binding (SSB) hashes, whose keys hide a chosen index but statistically bind the input at that index. SSB hashes can be built from FHE by encrypting the index and homomorphically selecting the indexed input, with an extractor using a trapdoor to recover the bound value.

Using SSB hashes to hash PCP columns binds one row of the PCP matrix. In the soundness proof, if some batch instance is false, the CRS is hybrid-switched to bind that false row. Extraction fixes its PCP row, and any accepted proof implies a PCP query accepting that false instance, yielding a relation violation handled by correlation intractability.

These controls initialize the electron–nuclear system, generate all four Bell states, and reconstruct their density matrices using quantum state tomography.

The lecture reviews covariant derivatives, Lie derivatives, Killing vectors, and tensor densities, then introduces geodesics. Naive derivatives on curved manifolds are not tensorial, motivating transport laws such as the covariant derivative. Lie derivatives are tensorial despite being expressible with partial derivatives, and Killing vectors describe metric symmetries through Killing’s equation.

The Levi-Civita symbol and the determinant of the metric are tensor densities, with the metric determinant having weight -2. Multiplying tensor densities by suitable powers of the metric determinant converts them into proper tensors, commonly used to construct covariant volume elements. The determinant also provides a shortcut for computing contracted Christoffel symbols, leading to a simplified expression for the covariant divergence of a vector and a curved-space form related to Gauss’s theorem. This shortcut generally does not extend to arbitrary tensor divergences, except in special cases such as antisymmetric tensors. Stress-energy conservation in general relativity is local, and cannot generally be promoted to a global conservation law because vectors at different tangent spaces cannot be directly compared without path-dependent transport.

The lecture then derives the geodesic equation as the motion of a freely falling test body with only mass and no charge, spin, or spatial extent. Such a body parallel transports its tangent vector, producing the geodesic equation. Geodesics describe leading-order gravitational motion, while forces, charge, spin, or finite size add correction terms. A non-affine parameterization can be reparameterized into an affine one, for which the geodesic equation has zero on the right-hand side; proper time is a natural affine parameter for timelike paths.

A second route to geodesics uses an action principle based on extremizing accumulated proper time between two events. For timelike paths, the freefall trajectory is the one of extremal, specifically maximal, aging. The lecture closes by noting that null trajectories for light require modifications because proper time is not defined along them, and that Killing vectors combined with geodesic motion lead to conserved quantities such as energy in time-independent spacetimes.

The passage specifies SD Memory Card behavior across identification, data transfer, command handling, read/write/erase operations, bus modes, protection, and function switching.

During Card Identification Mode, the host remains at fOD frequency; in Data Transfer Mode it may use fPP. CMD9 reads CSD data, CMD4 may configure DSR, and CMD7 selects one card into Transfer State or deselects cards using RCA 0. Only one card may be in Transfer State at a time. Data communication in Data Transfer Mode is point-to-point with the selected card. Read and write commands can be aborted with CMD12; write commands must be stopped before deselection. Programming and erase operations may continue after deselection, and DAT0 indicates busy.

ACMD6 selects 1-bit or 4-bit bus width, with 1-bit as default after power-up or CMD0. Read and write transfers use CRC protection. Block reads use CMD17 or CMD18, and multiple reads continue until CMD12. Block writes use CMD24, CMD25 and related commands; multiple block write is preferred for speed. ACMD23 can set a pre-erase count before CMD25. CMD13 may poll card status.

Erase uses CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38 in sequence. DISCARD and Full User Area Logical Erase use CMD38 arguments 00000001h and 00000002h respectively, are supported only for SDHC and SDXC cards, and are not supported through SPI. Unsupported DISCARD or FULE results in ERASE execution. Busy is indicated by DAT0 low.

Write protection includes a mechanical switch, optional internal write protection, and password-based card locking. CMD42 manages password setting, clearing, locking, unlocking, Force Erase, and Card Ownership Protection. Locked cards accept only specified basic and lock-related commands and reject ACMD6. COP cards add FEP handling, COP Unlock, protected force erase, and restrictions on clearing passwords when FEP is set.

APP_CMD (CMD55) causes the next command to be interpreted as an application-specific command when defined and legal. CMD6 switches or checks card functions, including bus speed, command system, driver strength, and power limit. CMD6 is valid in Transfer State and returns a 512-bit status block. Mode 0 checks supported functions and current or power consumption; Mode 1 switches functions. High-Speed mode uses CMD6 and raises interface speed to 25 MB/sec when supported.

CMD8 initializes cards compliant with Version 2.00 or later by checking host supply voltage and echoing a check pattern. SDSC uses byte addressing and CMD16 block length, while SDHC and SDXC use 512-byte block addressing for memory access commands and disable partial and misaligned access.

The host may change or stop the bus clock, with restrictions, and must provide eight clocks after transactions before stopping the clock. Commands, responses, and data are protected by CRC7 or CRC16. CRC or illegal command errors prevent execution and set status bits. Read, write, erase, DISCARD, and FULE operations have defined timeout and busy behavior, including special SDXC and UHS-II busy timing rules.

The Biorepository and Integrative Genomics (BIG) Initiative in Tennessee links genomic data, electronic health records, and environmental information from a diverse Mid-South population to support inclusive genomics and precision medicine. The study analyzed 13,152 genomes from BIG, a cohort that has consented over 42,000 participants and collected more than 15,000 biosamples, with 87% of participants under age 18.

The cohort showed substantial genetic diversity: 50% of analyzed participants were inferred to have non-European or admixed ancestry, including 20% similar to African reference populations and 30% with admixed origins. Ancestry was geographically stratified, with African ancestry more common in urban areas and European ancestry more common in suburban regions, indicating that geography may confound association analyses.

The study identified 6.8 million high-confidence variable sites and 771,717 novel single nucleotide variants absent from major reference databases. Novel variants were mostly rare and ancestry-specific, with some predicted to have functional or clinical relevance. Individuals with African or admixed African ancestry had more variable sites relative to the reference genome, supporting the authors’ call for pangenomic approaches.

Disease analyses using electronic health records examined obesity, hypertension, diabetes, and asthma. Pediatric participants had high numbers of diabetes and asthma cases, and minority groups showed higher odds ratios for obesity and asthma. Zip-code analyses suggested environmental components for obesity and asthma, especially in selected suburban areas around Memphis.

The study also found discrepancies between self-reported race and inferred genetic ancestry. Some genetically related individuals self-identified in different racial categories, and some individuals with the same self-reported race had differing inferred ancestries. The authors state that these findings highlight limitations of using race as a biomedical variable.

BIG includes community engagement through genomics education programs and advisory boards, including MEMGEN and local community groups. Future priorities include expanding the cohort, increasing adult participation, continuing community education, and adopting pangenomic analyses to improve representation and equitable health outcomes.

The passage argues that Andropov may have personal, military, economic, and political incentives to pursue an arms control agreement rather than endless negotiation. The Soviet military might accept arms control if it constrains U.S. defense programs, and economic pressures may favor slowing military spending increases. Politically, Andropov may face competition from Chernenko and could benefit from outflanking détente supporters with an agreement. The author recommends focusing on arms control, especially INF talks, where timing creates leverage, while START can wait. A private channel is preferred because Andropov values secrecy, bureaucratic management would be easier, and leaks or resistance within the U.S. government could undermine negotiations. The proposed first step is a short letter expressing concern about renewed confrontation, acknowledging differences, and inviting serious progress on reducing nuclear arms.

A commodity trading advisor (CTA) is an individual, organization, or fund that provides advice or management for trading futures, commodity options, forex contracts, swaps, and related managed futures strategies. CTAs may manage individual accounts or run CTA funds structured like hedge funds, but they are generally limited to derivatives, unlike broader hedge funds. They are typically registered with the CFTC and members of the NFA.

CTA strategies may be discretionary or systematic, with many using algorithmic models based on trend following, momentum, technical analysis, or fundamental data. Trend following is described as the predominant CTA strategy, aiming to identify medium- to long-term trends through signal generation and exposure sizing. Momentum strategies may trade multiple asset classes, including equity, bond, currency, and commodity futures.

The passage emphasizes that successful CTA investing depends heavily on portfolio construction, risk management, and low correlation among strategies or funds, not simply on maximizing returns. CTA strategies may reduce portfolio risk when uncorrelated with other investments, but they also involve risks such as losses, volatility, unreliable data, capital requirements, and the need for market knowledge.

This systematic review examines empirically documented uses and risks of large language models (LLMs) in education. It focuses on four questions: which applications are most studied, how they are assessed, what risks arise, and what mitigation strategies are proposed. Using a PRISMA-guided process across five databases, the authors included 70 studies from 2023–2025 and grouped them into three application areas: operational effectiveness, personalized applications, and interactive learning tools.

For operational effectiveness, studies examine LLMs in feedback generation, data processing, domain knowledge tasks, and teaching-related functions. Reported risks include superficial understanding, limited robustness, hallucinations, anthropomorphic characteristics, bias, privacy concerns, and knowledge limitations. LLM feedback often lacks contextual sensitivity, indirect guidance, and pedagogical depth compared with teacher feedback.

For personalized applications, studies investigate grading, student progress monitoring, content generation, predictions, and recommendations. The dominant risk is bias, including demographic, cultural, linguistic, gender, disability, income, and racial disparities. LLMs may generate stereotyped content, produce culturally misaligned materials, or offer unequal recommendations across student groups.

For interactive learning tools, studies assess student engagement, cognitive impact, and academic performance. Key risks include reduced critical engagement, over-reliance, weakened metacognition, lower creativity, reduced agency, privacy concerns, and inconsistent outputs. Some studies report improved efficiency or writing accuracy, but also reduced motivation, shallow revision, weaker independent learning, and poorer outcomes in tasks requiring creativity or deep understanding.

The review proposes mitigation strategies for educators, developers, students, and governments. These include human oversight, teacher training, privacy safeguards, transparent LLM-use policies, bias audits, inclusive model design, explainability, verification of outputs, responsible student use, data governance, and stakeholder collaboration.

The authors introduce the LLM-Risk Adapted Learning Model, based on interaction, monitoring, and outcome stages. It describes how risks emerge and compound across learner–LLM interactions, affecting engagement, interpretation, memory, performance, motivation, and future learning behaviour. The review concludes that responsible LLM integration requires attention to technical limitations, cognitive processes, pedagogy, equity, transparency, and learner wellbeing.

The passage urges soccer coaches to create documented contingency plans with input from coaches, players, and parents rather than reacting in emergencies. It outlines “what if” planning areas including communications, backups, player health and eligibility, practice issues, pre-game procedures, equipment, field conditions, injuries, weather, referee problems, player conduct, transportation, post-game pickup, and coach absence or succession.
