It recommends checklists, delegation, backup personnel, preparedness among assistants, players, and parents, and recognition that not all problems can be anticipated or controlled.

The passage proposes using Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs) to improve 4D-Var data assimilation by learning an approximation of the inverse Hessian operator across a distribution of problems. In the 4D-Var framework, the optimal initial state is obtained from a Hessian-based linear system, but solving it directly or iteratively can be expensive, especially for ill-conditioned cases. The proposed method uses an FNO to map the adjoint-derived vector \(f\) to an initial-state estimate, either as a standalone solver or as an initializer for conjugate gradient (CG), forming FNO-CG.

Experiments use a linear advection equation on a periodic domain, with training and testing data generated from varied background states, covariance length scales, and sparse observation configurations. Results show that standalone FNO is generally less accurate than CG, but it captures enough structure to improve CG initialization. Compared with standard CG, FNO-CG reduces average relative error from \(4.26 \times 10^{-2}\) to \(1.61 \times 10^{-2}\) and average iterations from 127 to 105, corresponding to 62% lower error and 17% fewer iterations. Gains are strongest for ill-conditioned Hessian problems. The authors conclude that FNOs can approximate operators beyond PDE solvers and plan to extend the approach to nonlinear and chaotic PDEs.

Media reports on Oct. 25, 2001, focused on Enron’s financial and credibility problems. BusinessWeek reported Enron took a $1.01 billion charge tied to broadband, water trading, and limited partnerships, contributing to a $618 million third-quarter loss. Standard & Poor’s affirmed Enron’s ratings but changed its outlook to negative, citing reduced market capitalization, weakened investor confidence, and challenges in selling assets to reduce debt. Fitch and Moody’s also reviewed Enron debt for possible downgrade.

Energy trading firms said they were concerned but mostly continued doing business with Enron, which handled about a quarter of U.S. power and gas trading. Reports noted worries about EnronOnline and counterparty risk, though trading volumes remained high. Enron said it had access to about $3.35 billion to $3.4 billion in credit lines.

Enron replaced CFO Andrew Fastow with Jeff McMahon amid scrutiny of Fastow-linked partnerships and an SEC inquiry. Analysts criticized Enron’s transparency and questioned potential liabilities, including $3.2 billion to $3.3 billion tied to affiliated entities. Enron shares closed at $16.35, down sharply for the year. Kenneth Lay also resigned from i2 Technologies’ board to focus on Enron.

Nova Scotia Community College professors and support staff ratified new six-year agreements running from Sept. 1, 2014, to Aug. 31, 2020. The agreements include a seven-per-cent wage increase and options for collecting retirement service awards.

Darren McGregor said Hibs’ 3-2 comeback win over Rangers at Ibrox was “character-building” after they conceded early in an intense atmosphere. Alfredo Morelos put Rangers ahead, but Simon Murray equalised before Ryan Jack was sent off, James Tavernier scored an own goal and Vykintas Slivka added Hibs’ third. McGregor praised Hibs’ determination and said Jack was rightly dismissed for pressing his head against Anthony Stokes. He also highlighted Murray’s strong start at Hibs, noting his ten goals in seven competitive matches and praising his work rate and improvement.

VentureWire’s September 14, 2000 issue reports major private-company financing, acquisitions, launches, and executive changes. Top stories include Inktomi’s agreement to acquire webcast software firm FastForward Networks for about $1.3 billion; Bertelsmann’s launch of a $1 billion eBertelsmann venture fund; Algorithmics’ $60 million second round and acquisition of Sentry Financial Systems; Artisan Entertainment’s creation of a $50 million digital media investment unit; Privista’s $17 million first round; and Technologic Partners’ naming of ten Investors’ Choice winners at Internet Outlook.

New funding items include rounds or investments for Optranet, SiteBurst, CraniaMania, SecureOps, Pax Clearing, OnePage, Allrecipes.com, Everypath, Epoch Internet, FoodMarketplace.com, MontaVista Software, Circadence, b4bpartner, Prefer Network, Lost Wax, Replicon, iMedica, Linbox, Chevin Software Engineering, Industry to Industry, CyberCrop.com, and Primitive Root, among others.

New product and company launches include wireless technology firm mDiversity, Cinema Entertainment Group’s planned interactive digital television channel, and Daedalus Venture Group. M&A activity includes 724 Solutions buying Spyonit.com, PCsupport.com acquiring MyHelpDesk.com, Covad Communications acquiring a 70% stake in Loop Holdings Europe, and Quicknet Technologies purchasing Equivalence. Board and executive changes were announced at Fenix Enterprises, Definity Health, Troika Networks, eRIDE, I-Impact, MediaPrise, and PetroWEB.com. Vestar Capital Partners also opened its first European office in Paris.

Low volatility stock strategy involves investing in stocks with lower price fluctuation than the overall market, often measured by a beta below 1. These stocks are commonly found in sectors such as utilities, consumer staples, and healthcare, and may appeal to investors seeking lower risk and more consistent returns, especially those with lower risk tolerance or nearing retirement.

The strategy focuses on companies with stable earnings, consistent dividends, predictable business models, and lower debt. It can be implemented through low volatility ETFs or mutual funds, such as SPLV, or by selecting individual low volatility stocks using historical volatility, technical analysis, and fundamental analysis. Diversification across sectors and periodic rebalancing are recommended.

Low volatility investing may require a long time horizon, potentially years or decades. Although it can reduce portfolio volatility, it has risks and limitations, including long periods of underperformance and potentially lower returns over some periods. Backtesting can estimate past performance but does not reliably predict future results.

The passage cites research indicating that low volatility stocks have historically outperformed high volatility stocks in many markets. Kenneth French’s data from 1964 to 2015 showed poor returns from the 10% most volatile stocks, especially in major market downturns. Other research found the low volatility effect across developed and emerging markets. Berkshire Hathaway’s performance is presented as consistent with the low volatility hypothesis, emphasizing cheap, safe, quality stocks.

The ADS9803 supports configurable 2-lane or 4-lane SDR/DDR source-synchronous data interfaces, outputting 20-bit ADC results MSB-first in 24-bit packets with zero padding. It provides DCLKOUT and FCLKOUT clocks, configurable via SPI registers, with data clock frequency dependent on sampling clock, lane count, and SDR/DDR mode. The device includes data randomization using XOR with either a PRBS bit or ADC LSB to reduce ground-bounce correlation, plus simple and moving average modes to improve SNR.

The ADS9803 supports fixed, ramp, and alternating digital test patterns for channel groups CH[4:1] and CH[8:5]. Reset and power-down can be controlled by pins or registers, and initialization requires a defined sequence of register writes with a free-running sampling clock. Speed-boost mode allows up to 8MSPS sampling for one selected analog input channel pair while other channels remain idle.

SPI configuration uses three register banks, with bank selection through register 0x03; register reads require enabling SPI read mode. Multiple devices can be configured in a daisy-chain topology, with shared CS/SCLK and chained SDI/SDO connections, requiring N × 24 SCLK frames. The register map defines controls for data format, averaging, randomization, test patterns, gain correction, speed-boost mode, analog bandwidth, power-down, reference selection, lane mode, and common-mode range.

Application information describes the ADS9803 as an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS DAQ device for ATE use, with post-calibration TUE of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C for ±5V range. It supports direct or multiplexed PMU measurement, low-noise and wide-bandwidth modes, and wide-bandwidth settling to 99.95% full scale in 7.5µs. Layout guidance recommends close bypass and reference capacitors, avoiding vias between supply/reference pins and capacitors, separating analog paths from digital lines, and using short ground connections.

A TeamLease survey across nine Tier I cities found job loss risk highest in Delhi, followed by Bengaluru and Hyderabad, while Pune had the lowest risk. Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Chandigarh, Chennai and Kolkata showed moderate risk. By sector, industrial manufacturing had the highest risk, followed by construction and real estate, and BPO/IT-enabled services. Healthcare and telecom had the lowest risk.

Several Swedish hockey figures react to the retirement of a highly regarded Swedish player, calling him an icon, role model, and one of the best Swedish or European players. They praise his professionalism, low-key personality, consistency, two decades in the NHL, four Stanley Cups, seven Norris Trophies, and influence on young Swedish players. Some compare his legacy with players like Forsberg, Sundin, and Jagr, while emphasizing his long-term importance to his franchise.

David Wybron, headteacher of Lord Williams’s School in Thame, is urging the Government to reform GCSEs, teacher recruitment policy and school funding. He says state school pupils face tougher, more exam-heavy GCSEs than independent school pupils, while schools risk league table penalties if they use IGCSEs. He argues the new GCSE content is excessive and not educationally justified. Wybron also highlights a teacher recruitment crisis, saying immigration rules make it difficult to hire overseas teachers, and supports adding all teaching subjects to the shortage occupation list. He says funding remains a serious problem, with Lord Williams’s pupils set to receive over £1,000 less per head than pupils in better-funded authorities.
Naughty Dog highlighted Uncharted: The Lost Legacy at Sony E3 2017, showing Chloe Frazer and Nadine Ross in a full Uncharted adventure developed soon after Uncharted 4 was completed.

The Triple RSI trading strategy is a modified RSI-based mean reversion strategy with four key variables, three based on RSI. Its rules use RSI readings, the 200-day moving average, and buy/sell signals, inspired by Larry Connors’ R3 strategy. A backtest on SPY since 1993 produced 83 trades, an average gain of 1.4% per trade, a win rate of about 90–91%, and a profit factor of 5. The passage notes that the strategy has strong historical metrics but few trades, and suggests traders may adjust rules to increase activity or use it cautiously alongside a long-term buy-and-hold portfolio with limited leverage.

The passage is a specification update listing unresolved issues for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3. Reported problems affect PIT behavior, GLIU debug and error features, PIC interrupt handling, DMA priority rotation, thermal alarm recovery, PMC sleep clock control, UART access during DMA, LPC transactions, USB over-voltage protection and clock gating, illegal I/O address handling, ACPI/PMC register access sizes, KEL emulation and snoop modes, PCI back-to-back reads, SSMI reliability, IDE/ATAC UDMA and PRD handling, RTC CMOS RAM access, SMB controller NEGACK behavior, GPIO high bank writes after suspend, SMBus hold time, LOWBAT_FLAG reporting, and Sleep_X/Sleep_Y deassertion.

Many issues are described as having no or limited operational impact, while others may cause hangs, missed interrupts, invalid reads, discarded writes, failed DMA or UDMA transfers, corrupted register writes, unreliable wake events, or nonfunctional clock-gated domains. Resolutions generally require software or configuration workarounds, such as avoiding unsupported sequences, disabling automatic clock gating for affected domains, using DWORD-aligned PRDs, avoiding byte or word accesses to certain registers, using single-transfer DMA instead of block or demand modes, using normal UDMA command ordering, writing SMB status twice, using external circuitry or protection components, or programming sleep delay counters below the PM_SED delay. Some issues have no resolution.

Defensive tackles play a central role in football defenses by stopping the run, pressuring quarterbacks, occupying double teams, and creating opportunities for linebackers, defensive backs, and edge rushers. They line up on the interior of the defensive line and may also be called defensive tackles, nose tackles, or nose guards, especially when aligned over the center. Their work often does not produce flashy statistics but is important in short-yardage situations, backfield penetration, and disrupting offensive rhythm.

In the run game, defensive tackles defeat blocks, penetrate the backfield, tackle ball carriers, and absorb double teams to free other defenders. In the pass game, they operate in tight spaces against centers and guards, often facing help from other blockers, but can still earn sacks or disrupt quarterbacks.

Typical defensive tackles are strong, agile, tough, and able to recognize plays, with a general body type of 6’2” to 6’4”, 300 to 335 pounds, and a thick, sturdy build. Aaron Donald and “Mean” Joe Greene are cited as notable examples. Their ability to create pressure without blitzing and help defend the run allows defenses to use more players in coverage and simplifies defensive play-calling.

The passage introduces PRDNet, a crystal property prediction framework that combines graph-based crystal representations with reciprocal-space, diffraction-based information. It argues that existing real-space encoders, including multi-edge graph models, angular embedding methods, and periodic vector-based systems, can map distinct crystal structures to identical representations because they rely on local encodings and finite receptive fields. Diffraction-space representations are presented as a way to capture complete long-range periodic information. PRDNet uses learned pseudo-particles as probes to generate synthetic diffraction patterns that better distinguish atoms and local structural environments than conventional probes such as X-rays, electrons, or neutrons. The model is designed to be invariant to rotations, reflections, translations, and crystallographic symmetries. Evaluations on Materials Project, JARVIS-DFT, and MatBench reportedly show state-of-the-art performance across crystal property prediction tasks.

China’s official manufacturing PMI rose to 51.9 in May from 51.4 in April, the fastest growth in eight months and above expectations, with production and new orders strengthening and export orders improving. Economists warned the strength may be temporary, citing eased pollution controls, weak end-demand, deleveraging, trade tensions with the United States, and funding pressures. Small firms contracted while large and medium firms expanded, and 40.1 percent of surveyed firms cited tighter funding concerns. Hi-tech manufacturing rose to 54.8 despite U.S. tariff and investment restriction risks. China’s first-quarter growth was 6.8 percent, but investment and retail sales showed stress, and economists expect annual growth to slow to 6.5 percent from 6.9 percent in 2017. The non-manufacturing PMI edged up to 54.9, construction slipped to 60.1, and the composite PMI rose to 54.6.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture introduces higher performance for ray tracing, AI, shading, memory, storage I/O, display, and video workloads. DLSS uses Tensor Cores and neural networks to reconstruct high-quality images from multiple frames, with Ampere adding third-generation Tensor Cores and 9x scaling to make 8K ray-traced gaming at 60 fps feasible in some titles.

GA10x GPUs use GDDR6X memory developed with Micron, using PAM4 signaling and MTA encoding to deliver up to 19.5 Gbps data rates and 936 GB/sec bandwidth. RTX IO, working with Microsoft DirectStorage, enables GPU-based loading and lossless decompression of assets, reducing CPU load and improving storage throughput for games and professional workloads.

The NVIDIA A40 targets data center visual computing, offering higher FP32, ray tracing, and AI throughput than Quadro RTX 6000, PCIe Gen4 bandwidth, 48GB memory expandable to 96GB via NVLink, vGPU support, and EGX compatibility. Ampere also supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 8K60 and 4K120 displays, HDCP 2.3, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-generation NVENC encoding.

GeForce RTX 30-series GPUs provide up to 2x gains in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. The RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 24GB GDDR6X, while RTX 3070 uses GA104 with GDDR6 and performance above RTX 2080 Ti. Error Detection and Replay helps identify GDDR6X memory overclocking limits. The RTX A6000 provides 48GB GDDR6, NVLink expansion to 96GB, hardware ray tracing, AI denoising, and professional workstation performance improvements.

Intel shares rose 3% Thursday, bringing their monthly gain to over 50% and lifting the stock above $37. The rally raised the U.S. government’s Intel stake to roughly $16 billion, following the Trump administration’s $8.9 billion August investment for 433.3 million shares at $20.47 each.

The passage defines SD Memory Card command legality, command states, and several command functions in the Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00. Defined and undefined commands may be legal or illegal depending on card state. ACMD41 has exceptions: its response lacks APP_CMD status, APP_CMD may appear in later CMD11 or CMD3 responses, and hosts should ignore it there.

CMD6 switches or queries card functions in Transfer State. Function groups include Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength, and Power Limit; CMD6 supports six groups with sixteen functions each. Mode 0 checks supported functions and maximum current/power, while Mode 1 switches functions. Function 0 is default, and 0xF keeps the current function. CMD6 returns R1 plus a 512-bit status block. Hosts should verify support through SD_SPEC or CCC bit 10; CMD6 is mandatory for Version 1.10 and later cards.

Power Limit replaces Current Limit for UHS-II and applies to total VDD1 and VDD2 power. Its default is 0.72W, while higher performance may require selecting higher limits. UHS-II requires Function Group 4 support; Function Groups 1 and 3 are unused. The switch status includes maximum current/power, supported functions, selected functions, and busy status. Busy functions should not be switched, and Mode 0 should be used to check busy status.

High-Speed mode provides 25 MB/sec interface speed using 50 MHz clock and is selected through CMD6 on Version 1.10 and later cards. Command System switching changes behavior of reserved commands CMD34-37, CMD50, and CMD57; support is optional. CMD8 initializes Version 2.00 or later cards, checks host voltage compatibility in Idle state, and returns R7 if accepted.

Card capacity affects memory access commands: SDSC uses byte addressing and CMD16 block length, while SDHC and SDXC use 512-byte block addressing and fixed 512-byte access blocks. SDHC and SDXC disable partial and misaligned access and do not support write-protected groups.

Hosts may change or stop the SD bus clock, but must provide required clocks after transactions. CRC7 protects commands and most responses; CRC16 protects data blocks. CRC errors and illegal commands prevent execution and set status bits. Read, write, and erase timeout rules are defined, including longer SDXC busy cases and UHS-II Data Burst busy timing.

Commands are categorized by type and class, use a 48-bit format, and are reported through CCC and SCR fields. Responses include R1, R1b, R2, R3, R6, and R7. Card status, SD Status, and Task Status report error, feature, and queued-task information.

The passage also describes SD Status fields for protected area, Speed Class, AU size, erase timeout, UHS Speed Grade, Video Speed Class, suspension address, Application Performance Class, and Command Queue support. Speed Class, UHS Speed Grade, and Video Speed Class methods classify card performance for real-time recording. Speed Class defines Allocation Units, Recording Units, write/read performance, FAT update behavior, and measurement requirements for SDSC, SDHC, and SDXC. SDXC differs by requiring free AUs, not supporting move performance, using exFAT-related FAT/Bitmap/directory updates, and mandating CMD20 for Speed Class recording. UHS Speed Grades define 0, 1, and 3 for performance below 10 MB/sec, at least 10 MB/sec, and at least 30 MB/sec.

Truman bids farewell before Eisenhower’s inauguration, praising the peaceful democratic transfer of power and urging citizens to support the new President. He reflects on taking office after Roosevelt’s death, early decisions during the end of World War II, use of the atomic bomb, and the demands of the presidency. He describes his administration’s response to the Cold War, including support for Iran, Greece, Turkey, the Marshall Plan, Berlin airlift, alliances, and Korea, arguing these actions resisted aggression and helped prevent world war. He rejects starting atomic war, expresses faith that free societies will prevail over communism, and envisions peaceful scientific development. He also cites domestic prosperity, bank stability, fairer income distribution, and progress on civil rights. He thanks Americans for their support and says he and Mrs. Truman leave without regret.

Lilly Nguyen and Phil De Carlos married at Texas Children’s Hospital so their premature son, Lucas, could be part of the day. Lucas was born at 24 weeks by emergency C-section and has grown from 1 lb., 12 oz. to 4 lbs., 4 oz. De Carlos proposed in Lucas’s NICU room, and the family visited Lucas after the ceremony.

The passage introduces Truthful Text Summarization (TTS), a framework for making LLM-based multi-source summaries robust to strategic manipulation by content sources. It argues that current retrieval-augmented generation work often focuses on summary quality given fixed sources, while neglecting how AI summaries change incentives for sources whose visibility depends on inclusion in generated answers. LLM weaknesses such as hallucination, prompt injection vulnerability, and difficulty resolving conflicting claims can make manipulation profitable.

TTS filters sources before final summarization. It decomposes retrieved documents into atomic claims, uses a leave-one-out process so a source cannot shape the claims used to judge it, extracts each source’s stance on those claims, and scores sources using a multi-task peer-prediction rule. The score rewards informative agreement with peers while discounting generic or chance agreement. Low-scoring sources are filtered or downweighted before generating the final summary.

The theoretical analysis shows that, under stated assumptions, truthful reporting maximizes expected score. The framework provides informed truthfulness, strong truthfulness under certain conditions, and finite-sample guarantees that improve as the number of claims increases. Source utility is modeled through inclusion in the final summary rather than monetary payment.

Experiments on 300-sample subsets of Natural Questions and ClashEval compare TTS with standard LLM summaries, majority-prompting, and majority-claim baselines. TTS achieves higher precision, F1, and answer accuracy, including 70.7% answer accuracy on NQ and 74.3% on ClashEval. It also separates reliable from unreliable sources without ground-truth labels and resists coordinated uninformative behavior better than majority-based scoring. The passage concludes that TTS aligns source incentives by making truthful, informative reporting the best strategy for inclusion.

The Opportunity Project (TOP), a nonprofit early education program serving children ages 1 to 5 in high-poverty areas of Wichita and Derby, has shown long-term benefits for students. A study found TOP graduates outperformed similar peers in academics, social skills and attendance through eighth grade, including higher rates of reading at grade level. TOP uses a Reggio Emilia-inspired approach and supports families through scholarships, community resources, education partnerships and Parent Cafe workshops. William Eckels, a single father whose son Elijah attends TOP, said the program helped both his child’s learning and his own parenting, and inspired him to consider pursuing a degree in education.

MIT and the Carnegie Institution for Science released a public dataset of nearby stars to help expand the search for exoplanets. Gathered over 20 years by the W.M. Keck Observatory, it includes nearly 61,000 measurements of more than 1,600 stars, along with open-source software and a tutorial. Researchers have already identified more than 100 potential exoplanets. The dataset, collected with the HIRES instrument, will be periodically updated and is open to academics and the public.

The Trump administration began permanent layoffs of federal workers on the 10th day of the U.S. government shutdown, with OMB Director Russell Vought saying “The RIFs have begun” and later confirming the cuts were “substantial.” Trump said the number of layoffs would “be a lot” and “Democrat-oriented.” Notices went to employees at agencies including Treasury, HHS, Commerce, Education, Energy, EPA, Homeland Security, HUD and Interior.

Unions representing federal workers vowed legal action, with AFGE saying a lawsuit had been filed and AFL-CIO saying it would see the administration in court. Democrats, including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, accused Trump and Vought of choosing to harm workers, while Republican Sen. Susan Collins also opposed the layoffs, calling them arbitrary and harmful.

The administration and Republicans blamed Democrats for the shutdown, while Democrats have refused to back a Republican stopgap funding bill without extending enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits. Competing funding measures failed again in the Senate, and the shutdown was expected to continue at least until the following week.

NVIDIA Turing GPUs add enhanced video, VR, multi-GPU, rendering, AI, and shading capabilities. NVENC supports H.265 8K encode at 30 fps with bitrate savings for HEVC and H.264, while NVDEC supports HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. Turing improves encoder quality versus Pascal and fast x264 while lowering CPU use and enabling 4K streaming.

Turing supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink, which combines power, display, and data for VR headsets through one USB-C connector. Turing TU102 and TU104 use second-generation NVLink for SLI data transfer, enabling higher bandwidth than prior SLI bridges; two-way SLI is supported, but 3-way and 4-way are not.

Turing introduces RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs to accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing. Combined with NVIDIA RTX, DXR, OptiX, denoising, and hybrid rendering, this enables real-time ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, ambient occlusion, and indirect lighting on a single GPU. Turing can deliver 10+ Giga Rays/sec using RT Cores, compared with Pascal performing ray tracing in software.

NVIDIA NGX uses Turing Tensor Cores and deep neural networks for AI graphics features. DLSS improves performance and image quality compared with TAA by training on 64x supersampled reference images; DLSS 2X targets image quality close to 64xSS. NGX also includes InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

Turing adds Mesh Shading with Task and Mesh Shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and enable efficient rendering of many complex objects. Variable Rate Shading lets developers vary shading rate per 16x16-pixel region for content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and shading, allowing shaded texels to be reused across frames or stereo views. Multi-View Rendering supports up to four hardware views per pass and expands Pascal’s SMP for VR and other multi-view workloads.

Turing improves VR through VirtualLink, MVR, VRS-based foveated rendering, and RT Core acceleration for VRWorks Audio. TU104 includes up to 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and one x8 NVLink link, and is used in products including GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. Tesla T4 uses TU104 with 2560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores. TU106, used in GeForce RTX 2070, includes 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but lacks NVLink and SLI support.

The passage defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering, combining weighted Tensor, FP32, RT Core, and INT32 operations. It also explains ray tracing basics, BVH acceleration, denoising, and how ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections can improve realism over rasterization-based techniques.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2018. Total net sales were $52.9 billion for Q2 2018, up from $38.0 billion in Q2 2017, and $103.9 billion for the first six months of 2018, up from $73.7 billion. Net income was $2.5 billion in Q2 2018, compared with $197 million in Q2 2017, and $4.2 billion for the first six months of 2018, compared with $921 million. Diluted earnings per share were $5.07 for Q2 2018 and $8.34 for the first six months.

Operating income rose to $3.0 billion in Q2 2018 from $628 million in Q2 2017. By segment, Q2 2018 operating income was $1.8 billion for North America, a $494 million loss for International, and $1.6 billion for AWS. AWS net sales increased to $6.1 billion in Q2 2018 from $4.1 billion in Q2 2017.

Net cash provided by operating activities was $7.4 billion in Q2 2018 and $5.7 billion for the first six months. Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash totaled $20.5 billion at June 30, 2018. Total assets were $134.1 billion, total liabilities were $99.1 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $35.0 billion.

Amazon adopted new revenue recognition guidance in 2018, increasing retained earnings by about $650 million and changing the classification of Prime memberships and certain advertising and digital content revenue. The company acquired Ring Inc. on April 12, 2018, for approximately $853 million net of cash acquired.

Amazon reported $24.3 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding and established a $7.0 billion commercial paper program and a $7.0 billion unsecured revolving credit facility in April 2018, with no borrowings outstanding under either at June 30, 2018. The company disclosed ongoing tax matters, sanctions-related reporting, indirect tax claims, and patent infringement litigation, while stating it disputes certain allegations and intends to defend itself vigorously.

Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is a Toronto Blue Jays star born in Montreal in 1999 while his father, Hall of Famer Vladimir Guerrero Sr., played for the Expos. He later moved to the Dominican Republic with his mother, Riquelma Ramos, and spent summers in the U.S. with his father.

Guerrero Jr. is married to Nathalie Guerrero, and they have two daughters, Vlaimel and Vlaishel. His father, Vladimir Sr., played in MLB from 1996 to 2011, won the 2004 AL MVP, earned nine All-Star selections, and was inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame in 2018.

Several relatives are also connected to baseball. His brother Pablo Guerrero is in the Texas Rangers system, and half-brother Vladi Miguel Guerrero signed with the Mets. His uncle Wilton Guerrero played in MLB from 1996 to 2004 and helped teach Guerrero Jr. baseball, while uncle Julio Guerrero played in the Red Sox minor league system. His godfather is Hall of Fame pitcher Pedro Martinez. Cousins Gabriel Guerrero and Gregory Guerrero also played professional baseball.

Seattle’s 103-year-old Smith Tower is modernizing its manually operated elevators to improve safety, reliability, accessibility and service times while preserving their historic appearance. Owner Unico Properties, which bought the building in 2015, began the work in June after landmark approval. Elevator operators will no longer be required by mid-2018, though Unico says at least one will remain as a historical nod. Longtime operator Hamilton Beale plans to leave Seattle and return to Virginia. The 1914 tower, once the tallest west of the Mississippi, remains an office building and tourist attraction.

The court affirmed judgment for Catharine Heilmann in a dispute over savings bank deposits made by Diedrick Grafing in his name “in trust for” her. It held that the deposits created a valid trust, not a gift, despite Grafing retaining the bank books and drawing interest during his life. Payment of part of the fund to Heilmann was treated as recognition of her title, not evidence of a loan. The court also held that even if the money was intended to pass to Heilmann only at Grafing’s death, the arrangement was not testamentary because her interest vested when the deposits were made. Any promises by Heilmann to distribute money to others would have to be enforced by those parties, not by Grafing’s executrices.

A fake Michael Flynn Twitter account misled House Democrats Nancy Pelosi and Elijah Cummings, who cited a false tweet calling Flynn a “scapegoat” while criticizing Republicans’ investigation of his resignation. Flynn Jr. said the tweet was fake, and both lawmakers’ offices later acknowledged the mistake. The New York Times also cited the unverified account, then removed the references and corrected its story.

The 123 reversal pattern is a three-swing chart formation that may indicate a trend reversal. In an uptrend, a bearish 123 pattern forms when price fails to make a higher high and then breaks below the prior swing low. In a downtrend, a bullish 123 pattern, or 123 bottom, forms when price fails to make a lower low and then breaks above the prior swing high. The pattern resembles double tops and double bottoms but differs because the second swing does not reach the prior high or low.

Trading rules include entering after price breaks point 2, placing a stop loss beyond point 3 or point 1 in volatile markets, and estimating a profit target by measuring the pattern. The pattern can be used across markets such as stocks, forex, commodities, and Bitcoin, though the passage suggests focusing on bullish setups for stocks. Backtests on GLD showed more promising results for bullish reversals than bearish reversals, with the author noting the strategy may be improved by adding parameters.

Hajime, a rival to the Mirai IoT malware, has infected an estimated 100,000 devices worldwide and is considered more resilient because it uses a decentralized peer-to-peer network rather than command-and-control servers. Like Mirai, it targets poorly secured IoT devices such as cameras, DVRs and routers by trying username and password combinations. Researchers have not observed Hajime launching DDoS attacks and do not know who controls it or its purpose, though it could potentially be used for cybercrime, research, or to disrupt Mirai. Hajime appears more widespread than Mirai but infects a smaller range of device architectures, while Mirai variants affect more platforms. Researchers say both malware families may persist because many vulnerable IoT devices remain unpatched or cannot be fixed.

OpenAI reached a $500 billion valuation after current and former employees sold about $6.6 billion in stock through a secondary share sale, with investors including SoftBank, Thrive Capital, Dragoneer, MGX, and T. Rowe Price. Its valuation rose from around $300 billion earlier in 2025, supported by $4.3 billion in first-half revenue. The milestone strengthens OpenAI’s position among major private technology firms but raises questions about sustained growth, profitability, governance, competition, and regulation.

The passage describes techniques for cooperative monitoring networks that combine multiple existing monitoring systems to monitor and respond to events across homes, businesses, neighborhoods, or mobile users. A monitoring application server and/or central alarm station server may detect events from a particular monitoring system, evaluate them against rules, and activate nearby or otherwise selected monitoring systems to share alerts, sensor data, camera feeds, and device controls.

The systems may include control units, sensors, cameras, lighting or household device modules, user devices, application servers, and alarm station servers connected through wired or wireless networks. Cooperative networks may be formed based on proximity, user preferences, consent, vacancy state, event type, or predefined rules, and may be modified over time by adding or removing monitoring systems.

Examples include tracking an intruder across neighboring properties using cameras and lights, sending cascading alerts during medical emergencies, assisting a mobile device user who presses a panic button, and distinguishing local malfunctions from neighborhood-wide issues such as power failures, communication failures, radio-frequency jamming, or solar panel abnormalities. The system may treat events as property-specific or cooperative depending on data from one or more monitoring systems and may respond differently based on that classification.

Rules and user interfaces may define event criteria, cooperative responses, adaptation schemes, and potential participants. Cooperative monitoring networks may also incorporate public monitoring systems or devices, such as traffic cameras or street lamps, and may be managed by servers or coordinated by monitoring control units within participating systems.

The passage discusses Investing.com market headlines and an analysis arguing that gold’s recent rally, weak mining stock performance, a potentially bullish USD Index pattern, and weakening stocks suggest bearish conditions reminiscent of 2008. It also includes promotional content for AI stock portfolios, reader comments, related headlines on tariffs and markets, and standard trading risk disclosures.

The speaker assumes the Presidency under extraordinary circumstances, acknowledging he was not elected by ballot and asking Americans to confirm him with their prayers. He pledges to be President of all the people, act with openness and honesty, work with Congress, and move the nation forward together. He promises a sincere search for peace, affirms that the Constitution works, and calls for healing after Watergate. He asks prayers for Richard Nixon and his family, reaffirms his commitment to uphold the Constitution and do what is right, and vows not to let the American people down.

The passage explains the UCLA High Post Rub Offense, a high post attack associated with John Wooden’s UCLA teams and used at many basketball levels. It emphasizes spacing, execution, inside-outside options, ball reversal, down screens, and defensive reads. The offense is often run from a 1–4 set and can suit teams without a dominant low post player by using a skilled passing and shooting post and a point guard who can cut or post up.

The basic action begins with the point guard passing to the wing and rubbing off the high post screen, then cutting to the basket or posting up. If no shot is available, the ball is reversed to the high post and the offense flows into down-screen actions. The passage details counters to defensive tactics such as trailing, denying cuts, going behind screens, showing and recovering, switching, fronting, double-teaming, and overplaying passing lanes.

It also covers post isolation reads, low post moves, post splits, weakside options, automatic counters, and strategies for teaching the offense through breakdown drills and scrimmaging. Success depends on precise timing, footwork, communication, player coordination, scouting opponents, recognizing defensive adjustments, and moving players to attack weak defenders.

The passage emphasizes reservation-based education and vocational development for Indians, including English instruction, diversified industries, and support for native crafts, while calling for high standards and fair pay for officials handling Indian affairs. It highlights successful federal scientific assistance to farmers through pest control, new crops, rice expansion, range restoration, forage crops, and fruit storage and export. It recommends support for Smithsonian plans to improve the national museum and preserve records and specimens of endangered peoples and animals. It also urges the District of Columbia to serve as a national model in sanitation, housing, charitable and correctional systems, labor legislation, employer liability, railroad safety, and improvements to the 1893 safety-appliance law.

Andrew Lo’s lecture continues capital budgeting by comparing net present value (NPV) with alternatives used in practice: payback period, discounted payback, profitability index, and internal rate of return (IRR). He emphasizes that NPV, and in more advanced settings adjusted present value (APV), should be the primary decision rule because it measures value in dollars and accounts for scale. Payback is simple and may reflect concerns such as career risk, uncertainty, or liquidity, but it ignores timing, scale, risk, and cash flows after payback. Profitability index is closely related to NPV for accept/reject decisions but can misrank mutually exclusive projects because it ignores scale.

Lo explains that IRR is widely used, especially in bonds and private equity, but can fail when cash flows include multiple sign changes or future outflows. IRR may not exist, may have multiple values, can misrank loans, and also ignores scale. It agrees with NPV only under restrictive conditions, including a single initial outflow, one project, constant opportunity cost of capital, and a hurdle rate equal to that cost.

The lecture also discusses practical capital budgeting issues such as scale, capital rationing, competitive response, changing project risk over time, after-tax cash flows, and using CAPM for discount rates. Lo notes that business decisions also involve political, social, cultural, and implementation considerations beyond financial analysis.

The lecture then begins the topic of efficient markets. Lo explains that much of finance relies on market prices, rational behavior, and supply equaling demand, but he plans to discuss both why markets can be trusted and why they can fail. He introduces market efficiency through the stock market reaction to the 1986 Challenger explosion, where Morton Thiokol’s stock fell sharply within hours, months before an official report identified its O-ring as the cause.

The speaker says losing was a missed opportunity but the team must stay balanced, correct mistakes, and return to its game. They emphasize getting the puck deep, doing the “dirty work,” winning battles, finishing checks, and managing the neutral zone against Dallas, a strong transition team with big defensemen. The team played better in the first game by wearing Dallas down but played into their hands in the second. Road play has been a strength, and consistency in simple details is seen as key.

Troll Cakes, a New York City bakery/detective agency, makes chocolate chip brownie cakes decorated with internet insults and anonymously sends them to trolls. Cakes cost $35 to make and ship, with an extra $25 to track down an address. The company also offers a $30 option to send a Trump tweet cake to the White House.

A forwarded email chain titled “cancer: don't u dare delete” was sent to Enron recipients on Nov. 27, 2000 after being repeatedly forwarded through many addresses. The underlying message claims that a 7-year-old named Amy Bruce has severe lung cancer, a brain tumor, and medical bills, and says the Make A Wish Foundation will donate 7 cents for every name on the list, urging recipients to forward it.

This study examined associations between maternal, infant, and child gut microbiomes and child neurodevelopment in 116 mother-child pairs from the VDAART cohort. Stool metagenomic, metabolomic, and short-chain fatty acid data were collected from mothers during pregnancy and from children at 3–6 months, year one, and year three. Neurodevelopment was assessed at years one, two, and three using ASQ-3 across five domains.

The maternal gut microbiome showed stronger predictive relevance for children’s year-one neurodevelopment than the infant or year-one child gut microbiome. Predictive power from maternal and infant microbiomes decreased for year-two neurodevelopment, and neither maternal nor child microbiomes predicted year-three neurodevelopment. Infant gut microbiota became more similar to maternal microbiota with age, but this similarity did not explain ASQ associations. Some taxa overlapped between maternal and infant microbiomes but showed different associations with ASQ outcomes, including divergent patterns for Fusobacteriia/Fusobacteriota.

The authors conclude that the prenatal period may be an important window for gut microbiome associations with early neurodevelopment. Limitations include small sample size, limited pregnancy time points, and the need for validation and mechanistic studies.

Travis Zajac said the opposing goalie is quick, plays low, handles pucks well, and requires more traffic and shots. He said the team lacked a bounce but can draw confidence from past series and focus on winning tomorrow.

A player described entering late in a Stanley Cup Final as a learning process, said preparation and confidence are important, acknowledged a puck-handling mistake, and expressed belief he can help the team by staying ready.

Observations of dwarf galaxies orbiting Centaurus A, 13 million light-years away, show that 14 of its 16 satellites move in the same plane, contrary to the random, spherical distribution expected under the lambda cold dark matter model. Similar planar satellite orbits are known around the Milky Way and Andromeda, but this is the first such observation outside the Local Group. Study author Marcel Pawlowski said the findings may indicate missing elements or flaws in existing dark matter simulations or models. Other astrophysicists, including Mike Boylan-Kolchin, argue the standard model should not be abandoned without stronger evidence and suggest the pattern could be a statistical fluke or linked to large-scale dark matter filaments. Scientists say more observations of distant galaxies are needed.

The study developed and validated a Fluorescent Immuno-Lectin Assay (FILA) to measure lubricin glycoforms in synovial fluid and plasma in relation to osteoarthritis (OA). FILA showed acceptable validation performance and correlated with mass spectrometry measurements of lubricin glycans in synovial fluid. Lubricin levels and glycosylation differed markedly between synovial fluid and plasma, with higher levels in synovial fluid and relatively higher sialylation in plasma. In plasma from OA patients and controls, most lubricin glycoforms did not differ significantly, but SNA-detected glycoforms were decreased in OA. Lubricin glycoforms in plasma also correlated with BMI and age: BMI was positively associated with several glycoforms, while age was associated with reduced sialylation and increased Tn-antigen detection. The findings suggest plasma and synovial lubricin have different glycosylation profiles, and plasma lubricin glycosylation may be influenced by OA, BMI, and age.

The passage explains offensive soccer corner kick options, emphasizing that planned restarts should include a set play, a target area or receiver, and a proper service by a designated kicker. Common types include far post corners, near post corners, medium corners, top-of-the-arc corners, short corners, skip header corners, direct score corners, and floated-ball corners. Each option differs by target location, service style, receiver movement, and tactical purpose, such as exploiting weak defenders, drawing defenders away, testing the goalkeeper, or creating heading opportunities.

Coaches should select corner kick plays based on player abilities, including kicking distance, height, accuracy, aggressiveness, and heading skill. Players should learn all roles and movements, beginning without defenders and progressing to full game-like practice. Coaches may modify plays for tactical advantage and should prepare teams for clearances, counterattacks, rebounds, deflections, and other unpredictable outcomes.

Additional tips include accounting for wind, keeping the ball away from the goalkeeper unless deliberately testing them, ensuring the kicker does not touch the ball again until another player does, waiting for referee readiness, using signals or numbers for plays, timing runs properly, avoiding offside after loose balls, and quickly transitioning to defense when needed.

Tesla Motors filed a Form 8-K reporting that on June 10, 2015, it and Tesla Motors Netherlands B.V. entered into an ABL Credit Agreement with several lenders for a senior secured asset-based revolving credit facility of up to $500 million, with potential to increase to $750 million. The facility includes a $100 million letter of credit subfacility and a $40 million swingline loan subfacility, may be used for working capital and general corporate purposes, and matures on June 10, 2020. No amounts were outstanding at closing. Borrowings are secured by certain assets and subject to customary covenants and default provisions. The filing was signed by CFO Deepak Ahuja on June 12, 2015.

Michael Barnard argues that politicians who deny climate change will be held accountable as hurricanes, wildfires, migration, and worsening climate impacts shift voter priorities. He predicts these events will reduce Republican support and increase Democratic votes unless Republicans change their stance on climate change.

This longitudinal household study evaluated pneumococcal carriage and potential adult-to-adult transmission among community-dwelling adults aged 60 or older. From 2020 to 2022, 121 individuals from 61 households provided saliva samples every two weeks over 10 weeks; 62 participated in both study seasons. Pneumococcus was detected by qPCR using piaB, with serotyping attempted through multiplex qPCR and culture when possible.

Overall, 52 of 1,088 tested samples were pneumococcus-positive, and 27 of 121 participants were colonized at least once. Carriage prevalence was similar across the two study seasons. Both household members carried pneumococcus in a small number of households, but the study found no clear evidence of adult-to-adult transmission. Pneumococcal carriage was higher among participants reporting contact with children, especially children under 10 years old, and acquisition risk increased with frequent child contact. The estimated average time to acquire pneumococcus was 358 days, and mean detectable colonization duration was 17.7 days.

The authors concluded that pneumococcal carriage among older adults was most associated with contact with young children rather than clear household adult-to-adult transmission, and that adult pneumococcal conjugate vaccination may mainly provide direct protection for adults exposed to children.

Europe will launch Sentinel-3B, the seventh satellite in the Copernicus Earth-monitoring constellation, to track ocean and coastal conditions including sea level, temperature, pollution, sea ice and vegetation. Working with Sentinel-3A, it will provide data within three hours around the clock and also monitor rivers, lakes and wildfires. Copernicus, funded by the EU and ESA, provides free environmental data and supports disaster response. The programme’s 2008–2020 budget is about 7.5 billion euros, with uncertainty over Britain’s role after Brexit.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated April 24, 2019, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2019. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Exchange Act unless specifically incorporated by reference. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer.

Workers in Gainesville, Florida, removed the “Old Joe” Confederate statue from outside the Alachua County Administration Building after months of protests and failed relocation attempts. It will be returned to the local United Daughters of the Confederacy chapter. In Tampa, a Confederate memorial park on private property was vandalized with red paint and derogatory comments, officials said. Other local Confederate monuments have also been targeted amid renewed debate following violence in Charlottesville, Virginia.

The passage describes a “Double Stack” offense for attacking a Triangle & Two defense, which is designed to deny touches to strong shooters. The offense positions posts at the mid-post with shooters behind them, giving shooters space and a timing advantage to pop out, curl, fade, back cut, or exploit defensive switches. It includes stack screen reads, cross and fake-cross entries, single/double screen actions, base screen options, and side screen two-player actions. Successful execution requires coordination, screening, post play, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. Recommended teaching methods include breakdown drills, shell drills, and scrimmaging. Game strategy emphasizes scouting defensive techniques and matchups, recognizing adjustments, varying alignments and entries, and attacking weak defenders. The passage also defines the Triangle & Two defense as three players in a triangle zone and two chasers denying specific opponents the ball.

In the AEGEAN study, 1162 subjects were randomized to Primary SOC or Additional Educational Program groups; 1160 received study drug. At 24 weeks, 1054 completed the visit and 108 discontinued. In Part 2, 524 subjects were randomized to Secondary SOC or Continued Additional Educational Program groups; 1003 completed the 48-week visit and 50 discontinued after 24 weeks. Baseline characteristics were comparable across groups.

Apixaban compliance was high and similar across groups, exceeding 95% through 24 weeks and 94% at 48 weeks. Mean adherence at 24 weeks was 91.64% with Primary SOC and 91.88% with the Additional Educational Program, with no significant difference. From weeks 24 to 48, adherence was also similar across Primary SOC, Secondary SOC, and Continued Additional Educational Program groups. Persistence at 24 and 48 weeks showed no significant group differences. Fully adherent subject percentages were also similar.

Safety endpoints were comparable across study groups. Before 24 weeks, adverse events occurred in 51.2% of Primary SOC subjects and 52.0% of Additional Educational Program subjects. Between 24 and 48 weeks, adverse events occurred in 33.8%, 40.8%, and 38.6% of Primary SOC, Secondary SOC, and Continued Additional Educational Program subjects, respectively. Overall, 24 deaths were reported, no pregnancies occurred, and laboratory review showed no clinically concerning hepatic or renal signal. The study concluded that adherence and persistence were high and sustained, and the educational program did not provide additional benefit.
Stoke City defender Geoff Cameron said Saturday’s match against Hull City is a must-win as Stoke sit 13th, eight points above relegation, after a five-game winless run. Hull are 17th.

A phase 2 trial presented by Seattle Children's Research Institute found that adding abatacept (Orencia) to standard graft-versus-host disease prevention therapy reduced severe acute GvHD from 32% to 3% in pediatric and adult patients receiving mismatched unrelated donor stem cell transplants. Patients receiving abatacept showed improved disease-free and overall survival, lower transplantation-related mortality, intact immune reconstitution, no major uncontrolled infection, and no increase in relapse. At one year, overall survival was 85% with abatacept, compared with 57% and 68% in two control groups; disease-free survival was 79%, compared with 50% and 63%. The study included 43 mismatched donor transplant patients across 18 sites, with controls drawn from a national database. A second randomized double-blind cohort of 140 matched unrelated donor transplant patients completed enrollment, with data expected within six months.

The passage describes portions of the SEV-ES/SEV-SNP Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol and related NAE event handling.

A GHCB/VMGEXIT example shows a guest handling a #VC exception by disabling preemption and interrupts, ensuring the GHCB physical address is set in MSR 0xc001_0130, clearing old invocation data, setting required GHCB fields, executing VMGEXIT, and later copying returned save-state information back to guest register state. The hypervisor receives VMEXIT_VMGEXIT, locates and maps the GHCB, processes the request based on SW_EXITCODE, updates state, and resumes the guest. Before long mode or 32-bit PAE, SEV-ES guests should avoid unplanned NAE events because encrypted memory prevents GHCB communication unless encryption bit position is known.

For SEV-SNP, the hypervisor should provide a secrets page and CPUID page. The secrets page includes a reserved guest area for communicating message sequence numbers, AP jump table address, and guest-defined data across operating environments. EFI platforms may communicate SEV-SNP confidential computing blob information through an EFI configuration table.

NAE events cause #VC exceptions in SEV-ES guests. Guests inspect the #VC error code, populate GHCB fields, invoke VMGEXIT, then process returned hypervisor results. The protocol defines required NAE events, guest and hypervisor state, VALID_BITMAP usage, and error reporting through SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2. Guests should clear VALID_BITMAP before each NAE event, and hypervisors should do likewise before returning results. VMGEXIT processing should be protected by disabling interrupts and preemption; NMI contexts may require a separate GHCB or saved GHCB state.

The passage details handling for IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO #NPF, page state changes, SNP guest requests, SNP extended guest requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell pages, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID lists, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO guest requests, Secure AVIC, termination requests, and unsupported NAE events. These mechanisms use GHCB fields, shared buffers, decrypted pages, and hypervisor validation to perform I/O, MMIO, firmware requests, page ownership transitions, AP boot support, restricted injection, interrupt delivery, timer emulation, APIC discovery, VMPL switching, trusted I/O operations, and guest termination.

SMP booting under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP is constrained because hypervisors cannot modify measured and encrypted vCPU register state after launch. The passage describes AP reset-hold mechanisms, AP jump tables, and SEV-SNP AP Creation using VMGEXIT SW_EXITCODE 0x8000_0013. With AP Creation, a guest can provide VMSA pages using RMPADJUST, create or update AP state, and support vCPU hotplug.

For NMIs, the hypervisor must not intercept IRET, must intercept #DB, and must rely on an “NMI Complete” message from the guest before injecting another NMI. Debug register virtualization may be supported through DebugVirtualization; otherwise, DR7 accesses are intercepted and cached. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

The passage also defines SNP Restricted Injection doorbell behavior. A shared host-owned #HV doorbell page contains PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields used to notify guests of interrupts, NMIs, or virtual #MC events. The host presents pending interrupts by writing vectors into PendingEvent and may deliver #HV depending on state. Guests acknowledge events with atomic exchanges, validate observed vectors, and use NoEoiRequired to optimize end-of-interrupt handling without always exiting the VM.

President Obama addressed Syria’s civil war and the Assad regime’s alleged August 21 chemical weapons attack, which he said killed over a thousand people, including children. He argued that chemical weapons violate international law and threaten U.S. and global security by weakening norms against weapons of mass destruction and encouraging dictators or terrorists. Obama said he had considered a targeted military strike to deter and degrade Assad’s chemical weapons capability, while ruling out U.S. ground troops, open-ended war, regime change by force, or a prolonged air campaign. He defended seeking congressional authorization but asked Congress to postpone a vote while pursuing a diplomatic initiative involving Russia, the U.N. Security Council, and allies to require Syria to surrender and destroy its chemical weapons under international control. He said the U.S. military would remain positioned to respond if diplomacy failed and argued that limited action may be necessary to uphold international norms and protect civilians.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2015. Net sales were $25.4 billion for Q3 2015, up from $20.6 billion in Q3 2014, and $71.3 billion for the first nine months of 2015, up from $59.7 billion. Net income was $79 million in Q3 2015 compared with a $437 million loss in Q3 2014; nine-month net income was $114 million compared with a $455 million loss.

Operating income was $406 million in Q3 2015 versus a $544 million operating loss in Q3 2014. For the first nine months, operating income was $1.1 billion versus a $412 million operating loss. Cash provided by operating activities was $2.6 billion for Q3 2015 and $3.1 billion for the first nine months. Cash and cash equivalents were $10.7 billion at September 30, 2015, compared with $14.6 billion at December 31, 2014.

Amazon reported three segments: North America, International, and AWS. Q3 2015 net sales were $15.0 billion for North America, $8.3 billion for International, and $2.1 billion for AWS. Segment operating income was $528 million for North America, a $56 million loss for International, and $521 million for AWS.

Total assets were $56.2 billion at September 30, 2015. Long-term debt was $8.2 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $12.4 billion. Amazon had $33.9 billion in principal contractual commitments, including debt, lease obligations, operating leases, purchase obligations, and other commitments.

The company disclosed ongoing legal and tax matters, including copyright tariff claims in Europe, several patent infringement cases, IRS transfer pricing disputes, French tax assessments, and a European Commission investigation involving Luxembourg tax decisions. Amazon stated it disputes the allegations or assessments in these matters and intends to defend itself vigorously.

A Milwaukee woman said suspects kicked in her front door around 11 p.m. on New Year’s Eve while she was home. Her alarm scared them away, and police said similar incidents were reported on her street. The door was badly damaged and possibly had blood left on it. The passage also promotes a Snowcast app.

Biogen fell after its CFO departed, while H&R Block rose on stronger-than-expected results. Utilities gained as bond yields fell, but banks declined. GameStop slipped on weak retail sales, Brookdale rose on sale talks, Synchronoss fell on restatements, and Anadarko dropped with oil prices.

The speaker thanked Secretary Hegseth, General Caine, the Joint Chiefs, and U.S. military leaders, praising the armed forces and describing service as Commander-in-Chief as an honor. He discussed renaming the Department of Defense as the Department of War, saying it reflected purpose, identity, and strength.

He claimed his administration rebuilt the military, strengthened borders, restored merit-based standards, increased recruitment and retention, and committed over $1 trillion to military spending in 2026. He highlighted investments in nuclear deterrence, the F-47 fighter jet, the Golden Dome missile defense shield, naval expansion, submarines, B-2 bombers, and a 3.8% pay raise for service members.

The speaker said he had helped settle multiple wars, including conflicts involving India and Pakistan, Congo and Rwanda, Azerbaijan, Kosovo and Serbia, and was working on Gaza and Ukraine. He described a proposed “Board of Peace” for Gaza and said NATO allies had increased defense commitments while buying U.S. weapons.

He criticized the previous administration’s handling of Afghanistan, immigration, military recruitment, and Ukraine aid. He also criticized the press, political correctness, and Democratic-run cities, saying domestic unrest, crime, cartels, and illegal immigration were threats “from within.” He praised the National Guard’s role in Washington, D.C., and said military and law enforcement would be used to address crime and civil disturbances.

The speech ended by emphasizing military strength, readiness, deterrence, and the goal of winning while avoiding unnecessary wars.

Childs Farm Baby Moisturiser, sold for £3.99 in shops including Boots and Asda, has been praised online by people reporting improvements in eczema and psoriasis. Laura Gray said on Facebook that her psoriasis cleared within 24 hours after using it. Paige Sweeney said it helped her three-year-old daughter Evie-Rae’s eczema after other treatments and dermatologist appointments had not resolved it. Joanne, whose one-year-old daughter Kelisha had severe eczema, said regular use left her child’s skin clear after four weeks. Childs Farm dermatologist Dr Jennifer Crawley said regular moisturising is important for eczema because it hydrates and soothes irritated skin.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 28, 2021, reporting that it issued a press release on financial results for its second fiscal quarter ended March 27, 2021. The filing lists Apple’s registered securities on Nasdaq and includes Exhibit 99.1, the press release, and Exhibit 104, Inline XBRL cover page data. The report was signed by CFO Luca Maestri.

This study examined whether the 2021 CKD-EPI creatinine equation, which removed race from estimated GFR calculation, changed CKD diagnosis timing and staging compared with the 2009 race-based equation. Using Truveta electronic health record data, researchers analyzed 8,080,889 adults with serum creatinine results from 2016–2023; 15.5% were Black or African American. Patients needed at least three creatinine values over more than 90 days and were excluded for pregnancy, polycystic kidney disease, or acute kidney injury.

Overall, 1,239,185 patients met criteria for CKD stages 3a–5 using either equation. The 2021 equation identified CKD earlier for 24% of Black patients and 0.7% of non-Black patients. Staging discordance was significant, especially among Black patients and in earlier CKD stages. Nearly half of Black patients classified as stage 3a by the 2021 equation did not meet CKD criteria under the 2009 equation, and half classified as stage 3b by the 2021 equation were classified as stage 3a by the 2009 equation. In multivariate analysis, Black patients were 126 times more likely than non-Black patients to have an increased CKD stage using the 2021 equation.

The authors conclude that removing race from GFR estimation led to earlier CKD identification and higher staging for many Black patients, potentially reducing disparities in diagnosis and care. Social determinants included in the study were not significantly associated with increased staging. Limitations included reliance on EHR data and use of a comorbidity index not validated for this population.
Clinical trials show oral GLP-1 drugs may aid weight loss without needles or refrigeration.

Legal experts Shane Kilcommins and Eimear Spain criticised the proposed Communications (Retention of Data) Bill 2017, saying it omits key Murray Report recommendations. While the bill would require district court authorisation for communication data requests, it lacks specific protections for journalists’ data, including High Court approval and limits on identifying sources. Kilcommins said journalistic sources are a recognised privileged category and important for press freedom. The bill also omits a recommendation for an independent, resourced supervisory body to oversee service providers’ data security. Spain criticised the continued use of retrospective High Court reviews, noting earlier reviews were brief and described by the Irish Human Rights and Equality Commission as “light touch” and not human rights compliant, though she said the bill expands prior judicial authorisation.

The speaker says the season comes down to one final game and that home-ice advantage is not a major factor. He emphasizes that the team has bounced back all year, earned its place, and must focus on the next game rather than past series. He describes the situation as mentally draining and says rest is important. He expresses surprise at the team’s penalties, attributing them to emotion, frustration, and opponents’ provocations. He says some player-status questions may be answered after rest and a morning skate. He also says hatred between teams is normal in a long series and can intensify competition.

Deanna Conley, 77, suffered chronic back pain for nearly 40 years despite scans, injections, pain psychology treatment, and five spinal fusion surgeries. Dr. Michael Bottros at Washington University Pain Management Center recommended a spinal cord stimulator implant, which uses pulsing electrodes in the epidural space to block pain signals. After a successful trial, Conley received a permanent implant with a rechargeable battery and wireless controller. She no longer needed a walker or wheelchair and described the result as a “Christmas miracle.” Bottros said data show many patients still do well after five years, though longer-term outcomes are still being studied. He has implanted 40 to 50 patients in the past year, with nearly all seeing remarkable results.

Donald Trump faced criticism for a tweet defending his writing abilities that contained misspellings and grammatical errors, including using “poured” instead of “pored.” Tony Schwartz, ghostwriter of The Art of the Deal and a longtime Trump critic, responded that Trump is incapable of reading a book, much less writing one. J.K. Rowling also mocked the tweet. The passage also notes separate criticism of Trump for initially denying a request to lower flags after a deadly Annapolis newsroom shooting, before later ordering them lowered.

Rory McKelvie, a 19-year-old from Biggar, Lanarkshire, was found dead at an address in his hometown last weekend. His death is not being treated as suspicious. His mother Sharryn said he “passed away in his sleep.” In social media posts before his death, Rory said he had struggled with mental health issues, claimed he received little support from doctors, and said he was told he was not “bad enough yet” and should return closer to “breaking point.” He also said someone had stopped him from taking his own life in November and urged others who were struggling to talk to friends, family, or him. Tributes were shared online, including from his girlfriend Caitlin Brigham.

Clinton County was recognized by Site Selection magazine as one of the “Top 100 Micropolitans” in the U.S., with the Wilmington–Clinton County micropolitan tied for 64th. Ohio had 16 Top 100 micropolitans in 2017, the most of any state. Clinton County submitted four qualifying projects, representing $70 million in new investment, 150 new job opportunities, and 400 retained jobs. Projects were submitted by the Clinton County Port Authority and vetted by JobsOhio and Site Selection. The Bright Farms facility under construction on Davids Drive was cited as bringing capital investment and jobs to Wilmington.

Arsene Wenger said he wants to fit Arsenal’s attacking players, including Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, Henrikh Mkhitaryan, Mesut Ozil and Alexandre Lacazette, into the team while improving defensive balance. Wenger said Arsenal’s attacking approach is part of the club’s “DNA,” but acknowledged the need to reduce goals conceded. He defended Ozil’s new £350,000-a-week contract as cheaper than signing a replacement and said Arsenal must only pay what it can afford. Wenger also said Aubameyang’s availability against Everton depended on his fitness after illness, and that Lacazette would receive no guarantees because players must compete for places.

A Nov. 30, 2001 media roundup reported widening fallout from Enron’s collapse. Enron Australia was barred from trading Australian power futures after credit downgrades raised funding concerns. Nord Pool cleared all Enron trades without losses, while Enron was suspended from trading on several European exchanges, including EEX; Dutch APX and grid operator Tennet said Enron still met access requirements. Enron failed to deliver gas to German utilities, and European energy markets saw volatility as utilities worked to replace Enron’s role.

Reports said Enron’s European business entered administration, with job losses expected, while assets such as Wessex Water, Teesside power station, Enron Direct, metals trading, and other European operations drew potential buyer interest. Enron’s overseas assets in Brazil, India, Japan, and Europe remained uncertain. The Teesside power station was reported to be operating normally.

Dynegy, after abandoning its Enron merger, said it retained rights to acquire Enron’s Northern Natural Gas pipeline and that the unit could not file for bankruptcy without Dynegy’s consent; Enron disputed Dynegy’s claim. Fitch kept Dynegy on negative watch amid expected legal challenges.

Regulatory and legal scrutiny increased, with the SEC promising a swift investigation, federal prosecutors seeking to monitor the SEC probe, and U.S. congressional committees planning hearings. Analysts warned Enron could cost insurers more than $3 billion, and reports highlighted potential litigation and bankruptcy issues involving Enron’s derivatives and off-balance-sheet obligations. Enron employees described halted trading and uncertainty as the company neared bankruptcy.

Edmonton blogger Barry Kent Winters, 62, was charged June 1 with wilfully promoting hatred against an identifiable group, a rare Criminal Code charge. Police said his blogs contained racist, homophobic, transphobic and other hateful attacks against many groups and public figures, as well as violent fantasies and claims about individuals. After years of complaints and a 13-month investigation, police laid the charge with approval from Alberta’s deputy attorney general, and courts ordered the blogs taken down as a release condition. The passage supports denouncing the blogs and credits complainants, but raises concerns that prosecuting offensive speech may affect free-speech rights, give Winters notoriety, and fail to address broader hatred.

The Strategic National Stockpile is a $7 billion federal repository of medicines and supplies for bioterrorism, nuclear attacks, infectious disease outbreaks, natural disasters and other public health emergencies. Managed mostly by the CDC since 1999, it includes antibiotics, vaccines, antivirals, antitoxins, nerve-agent antidotes and emergency supply packages stored in secret warehouses and other locations nationwide.

The Trump administration plans to shift oversight of the $575 million program to HHS’s assistant secretary for preparedness and response. Supporters say the move will streamline decisions, improve coordination and align purchasing responsibility with stockpile planning. Critics, including public health officials and bipartisan lawmakers, worry it could disrupt CDC relationships with state and local agencies, weaken “last mile” delivery, and increase industry influence over what products are purchased.

Officials say the change is not due to CDC performance and may raise the program’s visibility and funding. Congress has urged HHS to maintain a strong CDC role. The current CDC director said emergency response procedures will not change.

Paula and John Larison appealed summary judgment for Public Water Supply District #1 of Andrew County in a personal injury case after Mrs. Larison fell when a water meter lid in their yard slid off, causing her leg to enter the meter well and resulting in serious injuries. The Larisons claimed the Water District was negligent, knew or should have known of a dangerous condition, and was alternatively liable under res ipsa loquitur.

The Missouri Court of Appeals held that sovereign immunity could be waived under the dangerous condition exception if the statutory elements were met. It found a genuine issue of material fact on whether the Water District’s operator negligently replaced the lid after reading the meter nine days before the accident, because circumstantial evidence could support competing inferences about whether the operator or someone else caused the lid to be unsecured. The court reversed summary judgment on the operator negligence claim and related loss of consortium claim.

The court affirmed summary judgment on the claim that the Water District knew or should have known of the dangerous condition, finding insufficient evidence that any known risk caused the injury. It also affirmed summary judgment on the res ipsa loquitur claim because the Water District did not have exclusive control over the meter lid, which was accessible in the Larisons’ yard.

This study assessed possible associations between COVID-19 vaccination and audiovestibular conditions in Australia using spontaneous adverse event reports from SAEFVIC and a self-controlled case series analysis of general practice data from the POLAR platform. It examined adults with hearing loss, vertigo, or tinnitus within 42 days after vaccination between January 2021 and March 2023.

Among eligible records, vertigo was the most frequent condition, followed by tinnitus and hearing loss. Spontaneous reporting rates for audiovestibular events were higher after adenovirus vector vaccines than mRNA vaccines, particularly after dose 1. The SCCS analysis found increased relative incidence of audiovestibular conditions after both adenovirus vector and mRNA vaccines. Subgroup analysis found increased vertigo presentations after mRNA vaccines and increased tinnitus presentations after both adenovirus vector and mRNA vaccines. No increased incidence of hearing loss was observed after any COVID-19 vaccine.

The authors note that COVID-19 infection and reporting biases may confound findings. They conclude that healthcare providers should be aware of potential vertigo and tinnitus following COVID-19 vaccination and counsel patients accordingly.

The lecture explains the Higgs mechanism, proposed in the 1960s to give masses to gauge bosons while preserving gauge theory structure. Direct mass terms for spin-one gauge fields break local gauge invariance, so mass is generated through spontaneous symmetry breaking. In a toy U(1) model, a complex scalar field with a nonzero vacuum expectation value produces a massive gauge boson and one massive scalar field, while the Goldstone boson is absorbed as the longitudinal component of the gauge field.

For the Standard Model, the mechanism is generalized to the SU(2) × U(1) gauge group using a complex scalar doublet with four components. Choosing a potential with negative mass-squared allows spontaneous symmetry breaking.
