Coupling this Higgs field to the gauge fields gives masses to the W and Z bosons, while the photon remains massless. The W and Z masses depend on the vacuum expectation value and the gauge couplings, and are related through the weak mixing angle. Three Goldstone bosons are absorbed into the W+, W−, and Z bosons, leaving one physical scalar Higgs boson, discovered in 2012.

BCom (Hons) third-semester students in Indore were mistakenly given Corporate Accounts question papers during a scheduled Corporate Law exam, delaying the exam by about 30 minutes while Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya sent correct papers. The Corporate Accounts exam was scheduled for December 18, prompting allegations of a leak, but university officials denied that the papers were served and said the set could be changed if needed. Separately, DAVV said BCom (Hons) will continue under the annual exam system, citing no instructions from the higher education department to restore the semester system.

Gold steadied below $1,250 an ounce after its biggest weekly drop since May, as markets awaited an expected U.S. Federal Reserve rate hike and guidance on future policy. Analysts said dovish language could support gold by weakening the dollar and lowering Treasury yields. Money managers sharply cut net long positions in COMEX gold and silver, with silver seeing a record drop in net positions. Silver, platinum and palladium prices were slightly lower.

Fire departments statewide are holding October Fire Prevention Month education sessions under the theme “Every Second counts—know two ways out.” Officials urge families to keep exits clear, ensure windows can open, teach children how to respond to alarms, stay outside during fires, discuss fire dangers, and rehearse home fire drills.

Education groups in China are formed to reduce disparities in basic education caused by the movement of students and teachers toward areas and schools with stronger resources. Typically organized around a prestigious core school, they connect member schools through administrator and teacher exchanges, training, shared resources, curriculum research, evaluation systems, and teacher rotation.

The passage states that education groups can improve member schools’ overall quality, raise teacher satisfaction and professional competence, support students’ broader development, and reduce public anxiety over school choice. Examples include Shanghai’s policy support and curriculum coordination, teacher survey results in Jing’an District, inter-school student activities in Zhengzhou, and improved access to prestigious schools in Hangzhou’s Xiacheng District.

However, education groups face problems. Core school culture may be imposed on ordinary schools, weakening their individuality. Ordinary schools may struggle to apply prestigious schools’ educational philosophies because of differences in teacher capacity and student learning ability. Core schools may also lack sustained motivation because expansion requires financial and human resources and adds management pressure.

The passage suggests establishing equal and democratic relationships among member schools, creating a standing committee, improving communication, strengthening teacher team building and rotation, using online resource-sharing platforms, and securing government policy and financial support. It concludes that education groups are a tool for educational equity in China, but further study is needed on sustaining cooperation while preserving each school’s distinctive characteristics.

Amazon Prime Big Deal Days includes discounts across nearly the entire Kindle lineup. WIRED highlights the Kindle Colorsoft and Signature Edition, Kindle Scribe, Kindle Paperwhite and Signature Edition, base Kindle, Colorsoft Kids, and Paperwhite Kids as worthwhile options. The article recommends the Paperwhite as the best all-around Kindle, the base Kindle for budget buyers, the Scribe for readers who also want a digital notebook, and Kids models for included covers and Kids+ content.
John Whitfield’s coram nobis application alleging ineffective appellate counsel was denied by the court.

Adidas and Refinery29 created Boost the Nation, a limited-edition series of UltraBOOST X running shoes with one custom pair for each U.S. state, all designed by female artists and auctioned to benefit Women Win. Georgia’s pair, designed by Lizzie Darden, features a peach theme with pink-orange coloring and a leaf on green shoelaces. The article notes mixed symbolism among state designs and says Georgia’s bid was $350 at publication, while Ohio’s reached $1000.

The passage describes GHCB negotiation, VMGEXIT handling, NAE events, and related SEV-ES/SEV-SNP mechanisms. In GHCB negotiation, the hypervisor sets VMCB offset 0x00a0 before first vCPU launch to provide GHCB protocol and encryption-bit information, while the guest uses CPUID, MSR protocols, and #VC handling to determine protocol compatibility, configure encrypted page tables, allocate a shared GHCB page, and register its GPA before VMGEXIT use. SEV-SNP guests may also use validated CPUID page information and register GHCB GPA through MSR protocol.

VMGEXIT processing requires the guest #VC handler to disable preemption and interrupts, prepare GHCB fields and validity bits, set the GHCB MSR, execute VMGEXIT, and copy returned state back after the hypervisor processes the exit. The hypervisor obtains the GHCB GPA from VMCB offset 0x00a0, translates it, handles the SW_EXITCODE, updates GHCB state, and resumes the guest. Guests should avoid unplanned NAE events before long mode or 32-bit PAE because GHCB communication would otherwise use encrypted memory inaccessible to the hypervisor.

The passage defines GHCB data structures and protocols including the SEV-SNP secrets page reserved area, EFI SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob configuration table, NAE event behavior, VALID_BITMAP handling, and standard VMGEXIT error reporting through SW_EXITINFO fields. It outlines special handling for IOIO, MSR, VMMCALL, MMIO, page state changes, SNP guest requests, extended guest requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell pages, #HV IPIs and timers, APIC ID lists, VMPL switching, SEV-TIO guest requests, Secure AVIC backing pages, termination requests, and unsupported NAE exits.

The document also covers guest identification of SEV-ES through CPUID properties, SMP boot challenges under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, AP reset hold and AP jump table mechanisms, SNP AP creation using VMSA pages, and the limitation that vCPU hotplug is unsupported except through SNP AP creation support. It specifies NMI handling requirements, hardware debug register virtualization behavior, and states that SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

For SNP Restricted Injection, the passage defines #HV doorbell page communication, including PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields, host and guest behavior for interrupt presentation, acknowledgment, EOI handling, non-maskable events, and HLT interaction. The host writes pending interrupt or event information into the shared doorbell page and signals #HV when appropriate, while the guest atomically reads and clears fields, validates vectors, handles interrupts or non-maskable events, and performs EOI either through NoEoiRequired or VMGEXIT.

Britain’s FTSE 100 closed 0.4 percent higher after a volatile session following the formal triggering of Brexit, helped by sterling weakness and gains in export-heavy firms. The mid-cap index rose 0.1 percent. 3I Group jumped after a Morgan Stanley upgrade, and London Stock Exchange shares rose after EU regulators blocked its Deutsche Boerse merger. Mining stocks BHP Billiton and Antofagasta gained with copper prices, while gold miners, AA, and Acacia Mining fell.

The court unanimously affirmed Vu Ngo’s conviction after a jury trial for three counts of first-degree robbery. His claim of discriminatory use of a peremptory challenge was unpreserved and not reviewed in the interest of justice. The court also upheld denial of suppression, finding his hospital interaction with police was not initially an unlawful detention, that any brief request to remain available did not amount to a seizure, and that later police had reasonable suspicion to detain him for identification and questioning.

A mail delivery notice reports that Jeff Dasovich’s email to hgovenar@mail.acom2.com failed due to “Relaying denied” and “User unknown.”

The original email circulated a confidential message intended for Senator Brulte regarding Enron’s proposed California electricity crisis legislation. Dasovich said Enron planned to deliver proposed legislation and possibly circulate it broadly, develop a one-page summary, build a supporting coalition, and activate PR efforts. The materials addressed distributed generation barriers, DWR credit risks under AB1X and possible fixes, California’s projected summer 2001 supply shortfall and blackout risk, and proposed legislation to increase supply, reduce demand, establish a competitive retail market, and restore investor-owned utility solvency.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K reporting that David M. Shannon, Executive Vice President, Chief Administrative Officer and Secretary, informed the company on June 16, 2016 that he will retire at year-end. Upon his retirement, Senior Vice President and General Counsel Brian E. Cabrera will lead the legal team, and NVIDIA will recruit a human resources leader.

This study examined enlarged perivascular spaces (PVS), a component of the glymphatic system, in people with epilepsy. Researchers recruited 467 epilepsy patients from Hospital das Clínicas, Unicamp, Brazil, including temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis, MRI-negative temporal lobe epilepsy, extratemporal focal epilepsy, and idiopathic generalized epilepsy, and compared them with 473 healthy controls. Participants underwent 3T T1-weighted MRI, and PVS were segmented using the PINGU deep-learning algorithm. PVS volume fractions were analyzed in white matter and basal ganglia with age and sex as covariates.

All epilepsy subtypes showed significantly higher PVS volume fraction and number in the basal ganglia than controls, with increases of about 101–140% and large effect sizes. No significant white matter PVS enlargement remained after correcting for age and sex. The TLE-HS group showed contralateral PVS asymmetry, but focal epilepsy did not show consistent ipsilateral temporal-lobe PVS enlargement. PVS measures were not associated with duration of illness.

The authors conclude that basal ganglia PVS are enlarged across epilepsy subtypes. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether seizures impair glymphatic function or whether impaired glymphatics contribute to epilepsy development.

Dr. Thomas Wilson Ikubese, a 2019 presidential aspirant and convener of the YesWeFit Revolution, joined the Alliance for New Nigeria after consultations and the Nigerian Intervention Movement’s adoption of ANN. A statement by Ayobami Ogedengbe said Ikubese would run for president under ANN and was urging other young aspirants to unite under the NIM arrangement. The move came two weeks after he left the National Conscience Party, accusing its leadership of over-taxation.

Doctors warned that eye cancer in India is often detected late, making treatment complex and risking blindness or death. Ocular oncology expert Bikramjit Pal said awareness, early detection, and protocol adherence are crucial, while specialised facilities and trained doctors are scarce. Retinoblastoma, common in children under five, can be treated early but may become fatal if diagnosis is delayed.

The passage presents a correct-by-construction design and Rocq implementation of a fault-tolerant voter unit for synchronous N-modular redundant measurement systems used in avionics control applications. The voter selects a reliable measured value from redundant input units, handles transient and permanent faults, avoids unnecessary switching of the prime unit, and provides reliability indicators to the controller.

The system assumes input units may report self-identified health status and may also have deviation faults when measurements differ from the ground truth beyond a threshold. Byzantine faults are excluded. Faults persisting beyond a configured persistence limit are treated as permanent, and permanently faulty units are isolated. The voter operates under assumptions about the maximum number of simultaneous faults and the minimum number of non-permanently faulty units required for reliable operation.

The work formulates requirements for fault identification, isolation, output generation, validity status, and output age. It defines soundness and completeness limits for deviation fault identification and shows that the proposed requirements match theoretical limits. When complete identification is impossible, the algorithm can still identify subsets of faulty and non-faulty units to extend reliable operation. It may temporarily enter an unidentifiable state while retaining previous output, with bounded output age.

The voter is modeled as a state transition system with five abstract states covering normal operation, transient prime-unit faults, isolated units with valid output, unidentifiable operation, and invalid operation. Fault identification follows formal rules based on miscomparisons, risky counts, and isolation status.

The implementation in Rocq embeds proofs of requirements as invariants in the voter state and transition functions. Properties R1–R16 are verified in about 23 seconds on the stated machine. The verified code can be extracted to OCaml, Haskell, or Scheme; the extracted OCaml code has 362 lines and takes about 3 milliseconds for a single-cycle transition. Future directions include hierarchical redundancy management and verified fault handling for asynchronous redundant systems.

AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) guide describes optional SEV/SNP extensions and a TMPM engine for offloading page migration between system physical addresses while preserving guest physical addresses. TMPM supports tiered memory optimization, migration of pages targeted by concurrent DMA, and migration of SNP guest pages inaccessible to the HV/OS. Availability is checked via the ENGINE_READY bit, and IOMMU enablement is required.

TMPM provides PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO for migrating hypervisor/default pages, including pages used by DMA, by coordinating with IOMMU host page table entries, and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST for migrating SNP guest pages. Guest migration requires source pages in Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid state and destination pages in Pre-Migration state; after migration, destinations inherit source state and sources become Pre-Migration. Commands can migrate up to 128 pages using page migration lists, with per-page status and partial-success reporting.

The guide defines driver operation through a separate page migration ring buffer, mailbox registers, initialization and shutdown flows, pause/resume behavior, interrupts, and SPA encoding. The ring buffer uses DEFAULT or HV_FIXED pages, supports parallel command execution, and reports completion through command status, read pointers, and optional interrupts. Performance improves with larger batches, especially 16 or more pages and up to 128 pages per command.

Restrictions include 4KB-aligned page movement only, non-migration of IOMMU structures, ring buffers, argument pages, vIOMMU private page tables, and pinned backing buffers. TMPM firmware can be reloaded only when no operations are in flight and the ring buffer is torn down; reload capability and procedure depend on EPYC family and firmware version. The document also specifies command formats, capabilities queries, status and error codes, and error-handling behavior, including ring buffer errors, migration list errors, hardware errors, and possible unrecoverable page states.

The study developed and evaluated a model for integrating environmental education into expanded educational opportunity schools in Nakhon Pathom Primary Educational Service Area 2, based on the theory of multiple intelligences. The research involved 364 lower secondary students, 44 teachers, and three school directors, using questionnaires, interviews, SWOT analysis, and model effectiveness testing.

Findings showed community environmental problems linked mainly to agriculture and urbanization, including soil chemical residues, wastewater odor, air pollution from agricultural chemicals, indiscriminate waste disposal, and cultural effects from technological advancement. Students had moderate environmental education learning overall, with the lowest scores in awareness and participation, while teachers showed a high level of environmental learning.

The developed integration model met the efficiency criterion, with E1/E2 scores of 81.51/82.11. Expert evaluation found high content and construct validity. After using the model, students’ achievement scores increased from 5.90 to 24.63, and satisfaction was high overall. The study concluded that integrating environmental education through multiple intelligences can improve students’ environmental knowledge, awareness, skills, participation, and evaluation ability in expanded opportunity schools. Future work should focus on sustainable environmental education standards, curricula, and teaching innovations.

A seven-judge Supreme Court Constitution Bench held that re-promulgation of ordinances is a fraud on the Constitution and subverts democratic legislative processes. It ruled that the President’s and Governor’s satisfaction in issuing ordinances under Articles 123 and 213 is subject to judicial review. The case concerned successive Bihar ordinances appointing school teachers who were not regularised after the ordinances lapsed. The majority held that ordinances must be laid before the legislature and failure to do so is a serious constitutional infraction. It also held that ordinances have legislative force but cease after prescribed constitutional limits. Salaries already paid to teachers will not be recovered.

The passage examines how online informal education contributes to personalized learning in design education, particularly through digitalization and computational design. It distinguishes formal, non-formal, informal, and random learning, and contrasts conventional education with online education, noting that digital tools, internet access, virtual environments, and multimedia resources have enabled more active, collaborative, global, lifelong, and personalized learning.

The study focuses on design education, where digital technologies have accelerated production, expanded access to tools, and supported learning through workshops, courses, online platforms, algorithms, software, and artificial intelligence. It asks how diversified informal online learning platforms contribute to formal design education. Using literature review and case study analysis, the study evaluates two synchronous online informal programs: “Introduction to Computational Design” by Driven by Volumes and “Sustainability through Computational Design” by Rethinking the Future.

The findings indicate that online workshops and courses support applied learning, discussion, multidisciplinary exchange, collaboration, rapid access to design tools, and the development of computational and parametric design skills. They help participants learn software such as Rhino and Grasshopper, engage with environmental data, and apply design methods through assignments, demonstrations, discussions, and presentations. These programs can strengthen self-confidence, professional skills, and awareness of current design and environmental issues.

The passage also identifies limitations. Online informal education may require personal access to computers, software, and reliable internet; may be limited by participant quotas, cost, and trainer-specific approaches; and may lack physical interaction. Certificates and outcomes from informal programs are often not included in formal transcripts, limiting their integration with compulsory education. Differences in methods, materials, assessment, and access raise concerns about inclusiveness and universal educational accessibility.

The conclusion states that online informal education provides frameworks for personalized learning, reinforces formal design education, encourages collaboration and discussion, and improves access to information, while also increasing competition and individualization in education and professional life.
A non-inverting comparator with hysteresis uses a two-resistor network and VREF. Output switches high when VIN rises above VIN1 and low when VIN drops below VIN2; hysteresis equals VIN1 minus VIN2.

A University of Surrey study says solar energy is now the cheapest large-scale power source, costing as little as £0.02 per unit in the sunniest countries and outcompeting coal, gas and wind. Global solar capacity exceeded 1.5 terawatts in 2024, double 2020 levels. Lithium-ion battery prices have fallen 89% since 2010, making solar-plus-storage systems more cost-effective and reliable. Key challenges include grid congestion and wasted energy in regions with high solar output. Researchers say smart grids, AI forecasting, stronger regional connections, energy storage, material innovations and sustained policy support are needed to accelerate the clean energy transition.

The passage contains denunciations of foreign religious doctrines as false, disorderly, and opposed to traditional principles, ancestral rites, loyalty, and proper conduct. It accuses religious leaders and converts of insincerity, greed, neglect of parents, improper marriage practices, misusing schools, and using preaching trips for personal gain. One notice orders religious leaders to gather their possessions and leave, threatening an attack if they do not depart by a stated date.

A dispatch from Mr. Heard to Mr. Gresham reports that Confucian followers in Seoul petitioned the King, claiming the Tong Hâk taught false doctrines that corrupted the people and asking that its followers be forced back to the right path or exterminated. Although there was concern that Western religion might also be denounced, this did not occur. The King replied that the government would handle the matter and urged the petitioners to study their own principles.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated January 26, 2015, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2014. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Exchange Act.

The passage describes a bull market signal strategy based on the S&P 500 closing above its 200-day SMA for 18 consecutive days during a bear market. The strategy sells when the S&P 500 falls 20% from its all-time high and buys after the signal appears. A backtest from 1927 to the present generated 12 signals, with average gains of 9.54% after six months and 21.84% after one year. Reported metrics include a 7.24% CAGR, 15.26 standard deviation, 0.24 Sharpe ratio, 60% maximum drawdown, and 87.38% time in the market. Excluding the 1929 crash, maximum drawdown falls to about 25%. Compared with the Golden Cross, the strategy produced fewer signals and no false signals, while spending more time invested. The last signal occurred on February 15, 2023.

St. George welcomed an 11-member delegation from its sister city Ibigawa, Japan, during the week of the 41st annual St. George Marathon. The group included Vice Mayor Sunao Isaji, city officials, race representatives and four runners, including elite entrants Kenji Miyazaki and Mitsue Tomita. The delegates were hosted by local families, recognized at city events and attended an international luncheon where ceremonial gifts were exchanged. Mayor Jon Pike said St. George will send officials and top runners to Japan for the 30th Ibigawa Marathon in November. The delegation’s five-day visit includes local attractions, Zion National Park and participation in marathon-related activities.

Rain Bird’s 9v WPX battery-operated irrigation controller is designed for areas without mains power. It is waterproof, submersible, suitable for valve boxes, supports 1–6 zones, includes LCD programming, and runs up to two years with two batteries.
A player described scoring after a line change and pass from Teemu, then said the team stayed disciplined after a strong period and finished the game with the decisive goal.

A study in Nature Ecology & Evolution found that birds and mammals adapt to temperature changes about two to three times faster than reptiles and amphibians over geological timescales. Researchers analyzed data on nearly 11,500 living and fossil species to reconstruct habitats and temperature shifts over 270 million years. Lead author Jonathan Rolland said traits such as internal temperature regulation and body heat for developing offspring may have helped birds and mammals expand into colder regions. However, the study’s findings may not predict survival under current climate change, which is occurring much faster than past shifts. Rolland also noted that pollution, hunting, habitat loss, and invasive species are major drivers of extinction. The research may help scientists understand how animal groups respond to environmental pressures.

The passage describes SEV-ES and SEV-SNP GHCB mechanisms for VMPL switching, trusted I/O guest requests, Secure AVIC backing pages, termination requests, unsupported exits, SEV-ES identification, AP boot and creation, NMI handling, debug register virtualization, and unsupported SMM and nested virtualization. It specifies hypervisor and guest responsibilities for VMSA/GHCB handling, TIO data pages and returned measurements/certificates/reports, Secure AVIC page registration, termination reason reporting, AP reset hold and jump table use, SNP AP creation with guest-supplied VMSA pages, and NMI completion signaling.

The passage also defines #HV doorbell page behavior for SNP Restricted Injection. The doorbell page contains PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields, must be host-owned and accessed unencrypted, and is configured through VMGEXIT requests. Kuwait expects to finish cleaning a crude oil spill in its southern Gulf waters this week, Oil Minister Essam al-Marzouq said. No new oil patches were found, and authorities are clearing areas near shore while investigating the cause. Khafji Joint Operations said its facilities were safe and activated an emergency response plan.

Ola and Uber drivers in Delhi-NCR threatened a one-day strike on Tuesday over low fares and company commissions, potentially affecting commuters. The Delhi High Court restrained two taxi-driver unions from disrupting cab services. Sarvodaya Drivers' Association, claiming to represent 1.25 lakh app-based taxis, demanded fares rise from Rs 6 to Rs 20 per km and abolition of a 25% commission. The group planned a protest march to the Delhi chief minister’s residence and warned of an indefinite strike if demands are ignored. Some auto and taxi unions denied joining the strike.

Investors who had overlooked geopolitical and economic risks are now concerned after stocks fell more than 2 percent, marking the worst week in two years. A strong jobs report suggesting rising wages raised fears of inflation and earlier withdrawal of cheap central bank money. Treasury yields have surged as stocks sold off. The market’s long rise since 2009 was supported by low global interest rates intended to spur investment, hiring and economic recovery.

The passage argues that market corrections are routine and usually do not become bear markets. It states that fewer than one in five corrections escalate into bear markets, corrections have occurred on average every year since 1900, and the average correction has been a 13.5% decline lasting 54 days. It defines a correction as a 10%–20% drop and a bear market as a drop of more than 20%.

The passage notes that bear markets are more severe, with the S&P 500 historically falling an average of 33%, and more than a third involving drops over 40%. It says the 14 U.S. bear markets over the past 70 years lasted from 45 to 694 days, averaging about a year. From 1980 through 2015, the S&P 500 had an average intra-year decline of 14.2%, yet ended positive in 27 of 36 years.

The author emphasizes staying calm, maintaining communication with advisers, understanding market behavior, and taking responsibility for investment decisions rather than reacting emotionally to downturns.

The passage describes an augmented reality tracking system for image-guided surgery using head-mounted displays. A healthcare professional wears a head-mounted device that displays a computer-generated image, such as virtual patient anatomy and a virtual surgical tool, aligned with the patient’s body. The system tracks a patient marker and a tool marker to determine the position and orientation of the head-mounted device, patient anatomy, and tool. A single tracking device, typically a camera mounted on the head-mounted device, may determine position without triangulation by imaging a patient marker whose appearance uniquely corresponds to viewing location and orientation.

The system may incorporate additional tracking data when the first tracking device loses line of sight to the patient marker, tool marker, or portions of them. Additional data may come from a tracking device on another head-mounted device worn by a second healthcare professional, or from a stationary tracking device in the operating room. When the first tracking device has line of sight to both the patient marker and tool, the augmented reality image may be generated using only its data. When it does not, the image may be generated at least partly from the additional tracking device.

Different display responses are described, including showing the second healthcare professional’s augmented view on the first display, showing a full virtual view from the second line of sight, or continuing to show the virtual anatomy and tool from a previous first-person view while updating the tool position using additional tracking data. The system may also use an inertial-measurement unit to track head-mounted device movement when the patient marker is obscured. The passage further describes related apparatus, methods, cameras, light sources, reflective markers, processors, and computer-readable media for implementing these functions.

The passage advocates moderate, practical reform through government supervision rather than government ownership or unchecked business. It argues that combinations of capital and labor are necessary in modern industry and should not all be prohibited; instead, harmful combinations should be rigorously controlled. Current laws banning all combinations are described as ineffective and damaging, especially when they technically criminalize railroad agreements needed for fair operations. The passage recommends allowing railroad agreements if approved by the Interstate Commerce Commission and made public, and urges Congress to amend laws that cannot be enforced without disrupting business.

It also discusses taxation under the federal system, distinguishing local taxes, such as real estate and state-granted franchises, from taxes better handled by the national government. It supports continued federal revenue from tariffs and excise taxes, and recommends considering graduated inheritance and income taxes. The passage argues that wealthy individuals owe special obligations because they benefit from government protection, but stresses that taxation must be just, moderate, and equal in spirit toward rich and poor.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2018 reported net sales of $61.1 billion for the quarter, up from $52.9 billion a year earlier, and net income of $13.8 billion, up from $11.0 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $2.73 versus $2.10. For the first six months of fiscal 2018, net sales were $149.4 billion and net income was $33.9 billion.

Quarterly sales increased across all geographic segments, led by Japan, Greater China and the Americas. iPhone net sales rose 14% to $38.0 billion, Services rose 31% to $9.2 billion, iPad rose 6% to $4.1 billion, Mac sales were flat at $5.8 billion, and Other Products rose 38% to $4.0 billion. Gross margin was 38.3%, compared with 38.9% a year earlier.

Apple reported $367.5 billion in total assets, $240.6 billion in total liabilities and $126.9 billion in shareholders’ equity as of March 31, 2018. Cash and cash equivalents were $45.1 billion. Operating cash flow for the first six months was $43.4 billion.

The company spent $23.5 billion on open-market share repurchases and paid $3.2 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents during the quarter. As of March 31, 2018, $199.6 billion of its $210 billion repurchase authorization had been used, and on May 1, 2018 the board authorized a new $100 billion repurchase program.

Apple discussed the impact of the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, including a lower federal tax rate, deemed repatriation tax, and provisional tax estimates. It also described ongoing legal matters, including VirnetX litigation, and supply, market, foreign exchange, tax and operational risks.

The TPS7H500x-SP series includes radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies such as buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. Devices provide primary switching outputs OUTA and, on some versions, OUTB; each has roughly 150-mA peak current capability, so external gate drivers are recommended. OUTB is active only when the duty-cycle limit is set to 50% by connecting DCL to AVSS, valid for TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP. Synchronous rectifier outputs SRA and, only on TPS7H5001-SP, SRB are also available; SR outputs remain off during soft-start until SS exceeds 1 V.

TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP allow programmable dead times using PS and SP resistors, while TPS7H5003-SP has a fixed 50-ns typical dead time. Leading-edge blank time is programmable on all devices except TPS7H5003-SP, where it is fixed at 50 ns typical. Pulse skipping is implemented to address minimum on-time issues, especially at high switching frequency, and occurs when COMP is below 0.3 V at the system clock rising edge and the previous duty cycle was below 25%.

TPS7H5001-SP, TPS7H5002-SP, and TPS7H5003-SP support configurable maximum duty cycle through DCL, while TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50%. DCL to VLDO selects 100% duty cycle on compatible devices, DCL floating selects 75%, and DCL to AVSS selects 50% where supported. The CS_ILIM pin senses current for PWM control and overcurrent protection; when CS_ILIM reaches 1.05 V nominal, hiccup-mode current limiting begins. The HICC capacitor controls cycle-by-cycle limiting delay and restart timing. The FAULT pin enables external protection functions and shuts down switching if its voltage exceeds 0.6 V typical for the required minimum pulse width.

Slope compensation is supported through the RSC pin to mitigate subharmonic oscillation in peak-current-mode control. The device supports Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation using components connected to COMP and AVSS. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C typical and restarts power-up below 160°C typical.

The passage provides a synchronous push-pull converter design example using TPS7H5001-SP and GaN devices at 500 kHz, including selected values for timing, feedback, transformer, FETs, clamp, output inductor, output capacitance, current sensing, hiccup capacitor, frequency compensation, and slope compensation. Power-supply guidance specifies a 4-V to 14-V input range, regulated and bypassed with at least 0.1 µF from VIN to AVSS. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing noisy switching loops and switch-node area, careful routing of feedback and sensitive signals, close placement of bypass and compensation components, filtering CS_ILIM if needed, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS with vias. The document also includes related documentation references, support resources, revision history, package information, and TI disclaimers.

Two teens were arrested and a third person remains at large after a police pursuit in Frankston. Police pursued a black Subaru with stolen plates after road workers reported it speeding through roadworks. The car was dumped in Bayswater, where a 17-year-old girl and 18-year-old man were arrested.

Penn State University will no longer allow the student-led Outing Club, founded in 1920, to organize outdoor trips, citing safety risks in remote areas with poor cell service and distance from emergency services. The Nittany Grotto Caving Club and Nittany Divers SCUBA Club were also directed to end trips after a risk review students say did not include club leaders. University officials said student safety is the priority and a university-run outdoor trip program will continue, though students criticized the decision and its cost.

The passage compiles May 18, 2001 news mentioning Enron. Articles report that California’s long-term power contracts may be jeopardized after failed bond support, while falling western power prices reduced contract values and affected generators and traders including Enron. An options report notes bullish Enron options trading as its stock rose to $54.24. Multiple reports say Saudi Arabia selected international firms for three major natural gas projects totaling about $25 billion; ExxonMobil will lead Core Venture 2 on the Red Sea, with Enron and Occidental receiving stakes, while Shell, ExxonMobil, BP, Phillips, TotalFinaElf and Conoco were selected for other ventures. Leaders for Core Ventures 1 and 3 and memoranda of understanding were expected by June 5.

Android 8.0 Oreo introduced refinements including Picture-in-Picture Mode, Notification Dots, Smart Text Selection, Notification Snoozing and Autofill Framework. Picture-in-Picture lets supported apps play video or show content in a floating window at the OS level, extending Android Nougat’s split-screen multitasking. Supported apps mentioned include Chrome, Duo, Play Movies & TV, Play Services, Maps, WhatsApp, YouTube and VLC, though YouTube requires YouTube Red.

To use PiP with YouTube in Chrome, open YouTube in desktop mode, play a video, enter full screen, swipe up to show navigation buttons and tap Home. The video becomes a movable floating window, allowing use of other apps. Tapping the window shows controls to pause, close, or return to full screen; dragging it to the bottom dismisses it. If PiP does not work, enable it in Settings under Apps & notifications, Advanced, Special app access, Picture-in-picture.

FTX, founded by Sam Bankman-Fried and Gary Wang in 2019, grew into the world’s second-largest crypto exchange, valued at $32 billion in early 2022. Its affiliated trading firm, Alameda Research, was founded by Bankman-Fried and Tara Mac Aulay and later led by Caroline Ellison. Nishad Singh, an engineer with a 5% FTX stake, worked for both Alameda and FTX.

FTX specialized in crypto derivatives and leveraged products and issued its own token, FTT. Alameda held large amounts of FTT and used it as collateral for loans. In November 2022, CoinDesk leaked Alameda’s balance sheet, showing heavy reliance on FTT. Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao then announced he would sell Binance’s FTT holdings, triggering a sharp drop in FTT’s price and a run on FTX. Customers withdrew more than $6 billion in 72 hours, and FTX paused withdrawals on November 8.

FTX and related entities, including Alameda and FTX.US, filed for bankruptcy on November 11, 2022. John Ray, appointed CEO and restructuring officer, described a severe failure of corporate controls and trustworthy financial information. FTX lacked an independent board, accounting department, and CFO.

U.S. authorities charged Bankman-Fried with fraud, money laundering, and campaign finance offenses, alleging that billions in FTX customer funds were diverted to Alameda for investments, real estate, political donations, and personal spending. Bankman-Fried pled not guilty. Wang, Ellison, and Singh pled guilty. Singh admitted writing code that enabled customer funds to be diverted to Alameda, making illegal political contributions with Alameda money, and inflating FTX’s 2021 revenue by about $50 million at Bankman-Fried’s request.

The SEC alleged that FTX secretly diverted customer funds to Alameda, gave Alameda special privileges including a large line of credit and exemption from liquidation controls, concealed risks from illiquid assets such as FTT, and misrepresented the security and segregation of customer assets. The collapse raised questions about the roles of investors, auditors, regulators, celebrity endorsers, customers, and FTX executives.

In Thomas Henderson v. Alex. Beaton et al., Henderson sued in trespass to try title and for partition of an undivided half interest in the M. Latham league in Navarro County. The central issue was whether a 1839 instrument from Mastin Latham to William F. Henderson was an executory contract or a deed. The court held it was an absolute, unconditional conveyance of an undivided half interest, not an executory contract, and that its partition clause did not create a forfeitable condition.

Because the deed was executed, the defense of stale demand was inapplicable. The limitation defenses also failed: ten years’ possession had not accrued, no tax payments supported five-year limitation, and the possession shown did not constitute title or color of title for three-year limitation. The court reversed the judgment for defendants and remanded the case.

Ukraine partnered with Bitfury Group to place a broad range of government electronic data on a blockchain platform, in what Bitfury CEO Valery Vavilov described as the largest government blockchain deal to date. The initiative aims to improve transparency, accountability, efficiency, and asset security. Ukraine and Bitfury signed a memorandum of understanding, with a pilot planned for late this year covering areas such as state registers, public services, social security, public health, and energy. After the pilot, the program is expected to expand to all areas, including cybersecurity. Bitfury previously worked with Georgia on a blockchain land-titling registry pilot.
Annual Fund gifts support rule of law, independent courts, access to justice, fair representation, and donor thank-you gifts.

The president reports that efforts to persuade Britain and France to revoke measures violating neutral rights and restricting U.S. commerce have failed: France has not responded, and Britain rejected the proposed arrangement. As no authorized basis exists to suspend the embargo, it remains in force, though it is credited with protecting mariners and property and allowing defensive preparations.

Congress is asked to decide the proper course amid continued dangers to neutral commerce. Documents on foreign edicts, ministerial instructions, and the unresolved British attack on the Chesapeake are submitted. Relations with other European powers are largely unchanged; negotiations with Spain are paused. Relations with the Barbary powers remain generally harmonious except for an incident involving Algiers.

Peace with Indian nations has been maintained, with several tribes cooperating in prosecuting offenders and showing interest in agriculture, manufacturing, and closer relations with the United States. Harbor defenses, gunboats, recruiting, militia readiness, arms production, and enforcement of the embargo are reviewed, with emphasis on strengthening the militia and domestic arms supply.

The embargo and loss of foreign commerce have encouraged internal manufactures and improvements. Treasury receipts are near eighteen million dollars, debt payments continue, and Congress is asked to consider future uses of revenue surpluses, including possible reductions or public improvements.

In closing, the president expresses gratitude to Congress and citizens, acknowledges possible errors of judgment, and voices confidence in the republic’s future prosperity and stability.

Investors will focus on five themes next week: the Bank of England’s “Super Thursday,” with rates expected unchanged but attention on inflation, growth, sterling, oil and global growth; Australian and New Zealand central bank meetings amid cooling housing markets, low inflation and stronger currencies, alongside key China data; U.S. trade deficit data, expected to widen, plus retail sales trends and the risk of another government shutdown; diverging U.S. and European earnings expectations, with European firms pressured by the weak dollar while U.S. earnings benefit from tax changes; and emerging market central bank decisions, including possible Russian rate cuts, expected Mexican hikes, potential Romanian tightening and India holding rates while possibly adopting a tougher tone.

Joseph McGreal, a former Orland Park police officer, sued the Village of Orland Park and police officials, alleging he was fired in retaliation for protected speech at a November 2009 village board meeting and asserting intentional infliction of emotional distress. The district court granted summary judgment for the defendants. The Seventh Circuit affirmed, holding that McGreal provided no admissible evidence that the defendants knew of his alleged protected speech, that the speech motivated his firing, or that the defendants’ stated reasons for termination were pretextual. The court also found no evidence of extreme and outrageous conduct or severe emotional distress.

HoopTactics presents baseline, sideline, and full-court out-of-bounds plays designed to create high-percentage shots with multiple options and flow into predetermined continuity if no shot is available. For late-game full-court situations, teams should practice inbounding under pressure, use their best inbounder, shooters, and primary player, and consider advancing the ball before calling timeout. When simply needing to inbound safely, a baseline out-of-bounds play and strong free throw shooters are recommended.

Kyle Freeland pitched 5 1/3 innings and doubled during a three-run fourth as the Colorado Rockies beat the San Francisco Giants 11-4. Every Rockies starter had a hit, with David Dahl hitting his first career pinch-hit homer. Evan Longoria homered twice and Buster Posey also homered for San Francisco. Giants starter Jeff Samardzija left after one inning with shoulder tightness, and rookie Dereck Rodriguez exited after being hit in the shin by a line drive in his major league debut. The Giants committed multiple errors, helping Colorado score three unearned runs in the fourth.

Maddie Sabourin, an 18-year-old high school senior in Georgia, has spent years helping her grandfather, Sam Senseney, find a kidney donor. Senseney, 63, has been on the transplant list for six years and undergoes dialysis three days a week. After family and friends failed to match, Maddie raised awareness for organ donation and $7,500 for the American Kidney Fund. After turning 18, she learned she was a match, persuaded doctors to allow the donation despite her age, and told her grandfather with a card. They will meet doctors next week to set a surgery date, hoped to be within a month.

James Webb Space Telescope observations of the nearby rogue planet SIMP-0136 revealed strong auroral activity, storms, temperature variations under 5 °C, and constant silicate, sand-like cloud coverage. Astronomers from Trinity College Dublin used brightness changes as the planet rotated to track atmospheric temperature, chemistry, and clouds. The planet’s atmosphere exceeds 1,500 °C, and chemical changes suggest storms similar to Jupiter’s Great Red Spot. The study, led by Dr. Evert Nasedkin and the Exo-Aimsir group, represents the first direct measurement of changing atmospheric properties in an extra-solar object and shows how advanced models applied to JWST data can help study weather beyond the solar system.

The passage describes patent embodiments for enhanced 5G network slicing, particularly selecting an Access and Mobility Management Function (AMF) for isolated network slices. It outlines 5G system components and functions, including UE, RAN, AMF, SMF, UPF, PCF, NEF, NRF, UDM, NSSF, and related registration, connection management, QoS, PDU session, and network slice procedures.

The disclosure identifies limitations in existing network slice implementations for supporting isolated slices and proposes mechanisms using network slice isolation information during UE registration. Isolation types include fully isolated network slices, partly isolated slices with shared RAN, and partly isolated slices with shared RAN and AMF; isolation may also be logical or physical.

In example procedures, a UE sends a registration request containing requested NSSAI, identifiers, DNN, PDU session information, and network slice isolation information. Depending on the isolation type, the RAN may send AMF selection requests to an NRF, NSSF, or UDM. These functions may use requested NSSAI, subscribed NSSAI, allowed NSSAI, DNN, UE identity, subscription data, local policies, and isolation information to select an AMF. The selected AMF’s IP address or FQDN is returned to the RAN, which continues registration and may provide allowed NSSAI and slice isolation information to the UE.

E. F. Joy, as assignee of W. W. Montague & Co., sought to set aside Louis Helbing’s 1893 gift deed conveying San Francisco property to his wife, Louise. The deeds were not recorded until 1895, after Helbing obtained credit from Montague while appearing to own the property. The trial court found the conveyance was not made to defraud creditors, and the appellate court affirmed. It held that nonrecordation was suspicious but insufficient alone to prove fraudulent intent, that the burden was on the plaintiff, and that excluded evidence about later concealment of goods did not justify reversal.

The passage tests a pair trading strategy involving SPY and TLT after large opposite moves, such as on June 18–21, 2021, when SPY rose 1.43% and TLT fell 1.67%. The strategy goes long SPY and short TLT when SPY falls more than 1.25 times its 50-day average high-low range and TLT rises more than 1.25 times its equivalent range on the same day. Backtests from 2003 to June 2021 showed erratic results, weak recent performance, a CAGR of 1.93%, a 60% win rate, and an average gain of 0.18% per round trip. Changing holding periods or movement criteria did not materially improve results, and the strategy was deemed not tradeable.

Tropical Storm Nate, the 15th Atlantic system this season, moved toward Mexico’s Yucatan Peninsula and was expected to strengthen before possible landfall in southeast Louisiana as a Category 1 hurricane. Louisiana declared a state of emergency, mobilized 1,300 National Guard troops and ordered evacuations in some coastal areas. Nate has killed at least 22 people in Latin America, including 15 in Nicaragua and seven in Costa Rica, where flooding forced 5,000 into shelters. Officials warned of flooding, storm surge and severe winds but said Nate was expected to move quickly. The storm comes during a highly active Atlantic hurricane season, with September setting a record for Accumulated Cyclone Energy.

This retrospective cross-sectional study examined factors causing delayed discharge from a 23-bed subacute Complex Discharge Unit at St James’s Hospital, Dublin, during March 2020–February 2021. Data from electronic patient records included adult CDU patients with hospital length of stay over 15 days, assessed by age, gender, multimorbidity, diagnoses, and discharge-delay causes.

Among 390 admissions, 83.6% were over 65, median age was 79 years, 59.7% were women, and 48.2% had more than four comorbidities. Median CDU length of stay was 19.4 days, and 237 patients had stays over 15 days. Infection or sepsis was the most common admission diagnosis. Delays were associated with complications from primary diagnoses or multimorbidity, frailty or falls requiring rehabilitation, community service issues, patient-centred needs, and healthcare-associated infection. Patient-centred needs and complications from primary diagnoses were statistically significant factors in stratified Cox regression. The study concluded that primary-diagnosis complexity and patient-centred needs, including cognition, psychosocial needs, and carer needs, were the most common discharge-delay factors during the pandemic.
OpenAI is preparing a stand-alone social app for AI-generated videos powered by Sora 2, featuring a TikTok-like vertical feed, recommendations, and options to like, comment, or remix videos.

Bank of England research says a central bank digital currency could strengthen the impact of monetary policy by acting as a close substitute for bank deposits while offering interest and payment services. The Bank is not currently planning to issue one but has studied its design and risks. Researchers said a CBDC could make commercial banks adjust interest rates faster in line with central bank rates and improve quantitative easing by allowing the central bank to buy assets from non-banks directly with central bank money, bypassing banks.

The Warren Buffett ETF Portfolio (90/10) is based on Buffett’s 2013 letter instructing that 90% of his wife’s inheritance be invested in a very low-fee stock index fund and 10% in short-term government bonds. The strategy uses low-cost, passively managed S&P 500 ETFs for growth and government bond ETFs to reduce volatility and risk. It emphasizes long-term passive investing, low fees, diversification, and avoiding market timing or overactive trading.

The portfolio is presented as simple, cost-effective, and suitable for beginners, with implementation through either lump-sum investing or dollar-cost averaging. Asset allocation may depend on goals, risk tolerance, and time horizon. The passage notes risks, tax implications from capital gains and dividends, and recommends consulting financial or tax professionals for individual advice.

Backtests compare 90% SPY with 10% in SHY, IEI, or TLT. SPY/SHY and SPY/IEI slightly underperform SPY alone, while SPY/TLT performs better than the other bond mixes and nearly matches SPY, with 2022 bond market weakness cited as a cause of underperformance. Longer bond maturities are described as riskier but historically offering compensation for that added risk.

Official reports state that 600 to 800 American citizens in Cuba are destitute and lack food, medicine, work, or funds. The President recommends at least $50,000 for relief and possible transportation back to the United States.

In People v Schaub, the Michigan Court of Appeals considered whether sufficient evidence supported binding over Lawrence B. Schaub on a child abandonment charge after he allegedly transferred his ten-month-old daughter to an undercover police officer for financial gain. The district court dismissed the charge, finding the child was never left without care. The circuit court reversed and reinstated the charge.

The Court of Appeals reversed the circuit court and remanded. It held that child abandonment under MCL 750.135 requires both exposure of a child under six and intent to wholly abandon the child. The court found sufficient evidence that Schaub intended to wholly abandon his daughter because he agreed to sell her, relinquish parental rights, and allow others to raise her. However, relying on Shannon v People, the court held that the prosecution failed to establish “exposure” because the child was handed directly to another person to care for her and was not left unattended or placed at risk of personal injury from abandonment. The court noted that Schaub’s actions were “repugnant” but did not satisfy the statutory element of exposure.

The court also noted that a later statute prohibiting the sale or purchase of people could not be applied retroactively, and that reversal was without prejudice to possible common-law felony charges if applicable.

Judge O’Connell dissented, arguing that selling an infant to total strangers without adequate investigation could expose the child to injury and should be decided by a jury.

Walmart says drone delivery is ready to become a key part of its operations and plans to expand it to “most areas” where it operates, though no timeline was given. The company is scaling partnerships, especially with Alphabet’s Wing, expanding beyond 100 planned stores and adding locations in Northwest Arkansas. Regulatory changes, infrastructure needs, and customer adoption remain hurdles. Walmart says it has surpassed 300,000 drone deliveries.

The editor acknowledges assistance from staff at the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library, Library of Congress, CIA, and Office of the Historian, as well as permissions from the Haig and Jeane Kirkpatrick estates. The volume was researched, selected, annotated, reviewed, declassified, and edited by Office of the Historian staff under named supervisors. Sources for Foreign Relations, 1981–1988, Volume I included public materials such as presidential papers, State Department publications, congressional records, disarmament documents, Reagan Library files, transition papers, White House speechwriting and records files, classified Reagan Library presidential and staff records, George Shultz’s donated papers, State Department Policy Planning Staff files, Haig memoranda of conversation, and the Department of State Central Foreign Policy File.

The passage explains the Golden Cross Trading Strategy, which uses a short and long moving average, specifically the 50-day and 200-day averages. A Golden Cross occurs when the 50-day moving average crosses above the 200-day moving average, signaling a buy, while a cross below signals a sell. The strategy aims to stay invested during bullish markets and reduce losses during bear markets, though it can produce whipsaw signals.

The article backtests the strategy on the S&P 500 using daily bars from 1960. It produced 33 trades, with each trade lasting about 350 days on average. Starting with $100,000, the strategy ended with $7.2 million over 66 years, excluding reinvested dividends. It had a 79% win rate, an average trade gain of 15.8%, and an annual return of 6.8%, compared with 7.2% for buy-and-hold. However, it was invested only 70% of the time, giving a risk-adjusted return of 9.6%. Its maximum drawdown was 33%, compared with 56% for buy-and-hold.

Richard A. Milan, an Indiana State Prison inmate, brought a pro se § 1983 claim over the denial of a July 10, 1988 visit with Judy Ballard, alleging violations of due process and the Eighth Amendment. The court reviewed summary judgment standards and relevant cases on prison visitation liberty interests. It found that prison regulations did not create a protected liberty interest in visitation and that the failure to provide written notice of the denial, though contrary to procedure, did not establish a substantive constitutional violation. The court denied Milan’s summary judgment motion and granted summary judgment for the defendants.

This cross-sectional quantitative study assessed antiretroviral therapy (ART) non-adherence among HIV patients in the catchment area of Kibungo Referral Hospital, Rwanda. Among 424 respondents selected from 13 health centers and one referral hospital, 13% were non-adherent and 87% were adherent to ART. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed with Fisher’s exact tests and logistic regression.

Bivariate analyses found ART non-adherence was associated with age, education, household size, multiple sexual partners, travel time to ART services, waiting time, smoking, disclosure to friends, stigma, side effects, forgetfulness, and integration of ART into daily routines. Multivariate analysis identified younger age, lack of tertiary education, stigma, perceived ineffectiveness of ART, and failure to integrate ART into daily activities as significant factors associated with non-adherence. Setting an alarm reminder was not significantly associated with adherence.

The study concluded that ART non-adherence at Kibungo Referral Hospital was slightly high and influenced by demographic, psychosocial, and behavioral factors.

A storage appliance operates as a cache between data sources and cloud storage for snapshots. The system supports snapshot reclamation by marking snapshots for deletion, identifying valid metadata and data ranges, and implicitly transferring ownership to succeeding valid snapshots while deleting or adjusting overwritten records and data ranges.

To reduce eviction of stable data in forever-incremental snapshot configurations, the appliance creates synthetic baseline snapshots and refreshes eviction state data for stable cached data blocks. It may expand ownership of valid metadata to a recent snapshot or maintain a reverse-incremental synthetic baseline by moving overwritten data to pre-baseline snapshots and updating metadata, fingerprint data, and eviction state.

The passage studies time-delayed full feedback in learning in normal-form games, focusing on optimistic Follow the Regularized Leader (OFTRL). Optimistic algorithms such as OFTRL and optimistic Mirror Descent can achieve O(1) regret and convergence to Nash equilibria in certain games without delay, but real-world feedback may arrive late, making future reward prediction harder.

The study shows that even a small fixed delay can significantly worsen OFTRL. In unconstrained Matching Pennies with a Euclidean regularizer, OFTRL with any delay m ≥ 1 suffers Ω(√T) regret and diverges from equilibrium. The analysis explains this through a radius-growth rate α = m − n + 1/2, where delay expands trajectories, optimism contracts them, and discretization errors add expansion.

To address this, the paper proposes Weighted Optimistic FTRL (WOFTRL), which multiplies the optimistic reward term by n. A Taylor-expansion interpretation shows that the optimistic weight n can cancel the time delay m. When n = m + 1, WOFTRL satisfies an RVU property and achieves O(1) total regret with an appropriate learning rate, though delay worsens constants through λ = (m + 1)(m + 2)/2.

Experiments on Matching Pennies and Sato’s game show small O(1) regret when n > m, larger O(√T) regret when n ≤ m, and some exceptional O(√T) behavior for large delays with finite learning rates. For poly-matrix zero-sum games, WOFTRL with n = m + 1 and sufficiently small learning rate achieves best-iterate convergence to Nash equilibrium. Simulations on weighted Rock-Paper-Scissors show convergence when n > m and non-convergence when n ≤ m.

The study concludes that time delay can undermine optimistic learning, but sufficiently weighted optimism can restore O(1) regret and convergence properties. Future directions include proving last-iterate convergence and studying stochastic or adversarial delays.

The passage describes NVIDIA GA10x Ampere architecture GPUs and related products, emphasizing performance, efficiency, memory, ray tracing, AI, I/O, and professional workloads.

GA10x GPUs include third-generation Tensor Cores supporting new data types such as TF32 and BF16, plus Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity that can double Tensor Core throughput for sparse matrix operations. TF32 can provide up to 5x training throughput over the prior generation without code changes. Tensor Cores accelerate DLSS, AI denoising, NVIDIA Broadcast, NVIDIA Canvas, and other AI-based graphics and inference features.

GA10x uses second-generation RT Cores with dedicated BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection hardware. These RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection testing rates over Turing and add hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur through an Interpolate Triangle Position unit. GA10x also supports concurrent RT Core and graphics or compute workloads, including simultaneous compute-compute workloads.

The GA102 GPU contains seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, twelve 32-bit memory controllers, and 6144 KB of L2 cache. Each GA10x SM includes 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation RT Core, four texture units, a 256 KB register file, and 128 KB of L1/shared memory. GA10x doubles peak FP32 throughput compared with Turing by adding FP32 capability to both datapaths in each SM partition.

GA10x GPUs support GDDR6X memory, PCIe Gen 4, and third-generation NVLink. GDDR6X reaches up to 19.5 Gbps and uses PAM4 signaling to increase memory bandwidth, with the GeForce RTX 3090 reaching up to 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth. PCIe Gen 4 doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth, while NVLink can connect two RTX A6000 or A40 GPUs to scale memory from 48 GB to 96 GB. RTX 3090 supports two-GPU SLI through NVLink, but 3-way and 4-way SLI are not supported.

The architecture improves raster operations by moving ROPs into the GPC. A full GA102 GPU has 112 ROPs, improving multisample anti-aliasing, pixel fillrate, and blending performance. GA10x also increases L1 cache capacity and shared memory bandwidth compared with Turing.

The paper proposes a research agenda for integrating AI into society in ways described as harmonious, synergistic, and resilient. The paper highlights risks from advanced AI systems, including bias, misinformation, privacy violations, harmful outputs, malicious use, over-reliance, deskilling, social inequality, and challenges in regulation. Several research directions and projects are described, including value evaluation methods for LLMs, CulturePark for improving cross-cultural understanding, jailbreaking defenses, DyVal for dynamic evaluation, concept activation vector methods for interpretable control, and AI-assisted approaches to social science research. The paper emphasizes that AI governance should combine top-down regulation with bottom-up reporting and community participation, supported by cooperation among industry, academia, policymakers, and users.

The white paper is presented as the result of workshops, collaborations, and joint research involving Microsoft Research Asia and researchers from multiple disciplines and institutions, with the aim of building a shared research community around responsible and beneficial Societal AI.

The Stack Zone Offense is a zone offense based on overload principles, using stack alignment to create matchup and adjustment problems for defenses. It emphasizes spacing, movement, defined player roles, weakside attacks, multiple entries, late-clock specials, and offensive rebounding. Players have specific responsibilities: the point guard directs the offense, the shooting guard is the primary three-point shooter, the small forward works the baseline and rebounds, and the power forward and post operate from low and high post areas while rebounding.

The offense progresses through overload reads, pass-and-cut action, high post rolls, and ball reversals. It includes counters for defensive matchups, switches, pass denial, and overplays, using skip passes, baseline cuts, post feeds, screens, and weakside overloads. Optional entries include flop, exchange, triple stack, dribble, and weakside flop attacks. Crunch-time specials include “Vegas,” a double-away screen action; “Back,” a weakside lob option; and “Cat,” a 2-1-2 alignment used against traps and double teams. Key rules include post rolls on baseline-corner passes and baseline-corner back cuts when the ball enters the middle.

The passage distinguishes ceremonial free kicks from quick free kicks, noting that quick restarts can exploit defensive lapses. It also describes rare indirect free kicks near goal, where defenders may stand on the goal line. Practice should progress from rehearsing without defenders to using mannequins, stationary defenders, active defenders, and scrimmage situations while enforcing rules and correcting problems. Coaches are advised to keep set pieces simple, prepare contingencies, scout opponents, and avoid wasted kicks into walls or over the goal.

In Hunter and Others v. Bales, Bales, as assignee of Thompson, sought specific performance of a real estate sale contract against Matthew R. Hunter, Moses Hunter, and Moore. The trial court found for Bales, and the Supreme Court affirmed. The court held that where evidence supports two conflicting theories, the appellate court will adopt the theory sustaining the lower court’s finding.

Moore first authorized an agent to sell land to Thompson, and Thompson made a verbal agreement with the agent. Moore later orally agreed to sell the land to Matthew R. Hunter, but then executed a title bond to Thompson. Moore subsequently deeded the land to Hunter, who knew of Thompson’s prior written agreement. The court held Thompson had the prior equity and could enforce specific performance.

The court also held that in equity a valid land sale contract makes the vendee the equitable owner, with the vendor holding title in trust subject to a lien for purchase money. A parol contract may be treated as void when the vendor makes a valid inconsistent sale. In a specific performance suit, the plaintiff need not bring purchase money into court before decree; an offer in the complaint is sufficient. After Thompson tendered the purchase money and accrued interest and demanded a deed, no further interest was owed absent proof he used the money. The judgment was affirmed with costs.

In excerpts from a foreign affairs speech, Reagan says America must be strong, reliable, and predictable to preserve peace and freedom. He calls for a coherent national strategy, rebuilding military strength, maintaining stronger and less vulnerable nuclear deterrent forces, achieving naval superiority, and restoring the ability to project power in regions such as the Persian Gulf.

Cars.com’s 2018 American-Made Index ranks vehicles by U.S. assembly, American-made parts, engine and transmission origin, and factory job support. The Jeep Cherokee topped the list, followed by the Honda Odyssey, Honda Ridgeline, Ford Taurus, Chevrolet Volt, Honda Pilot, Acura MDX, Ford Explorer, Ford F-150, and Chevrolet Corvette. The list shows some foreign automakers use more American-made components than domestic automakers.

Florida officials presented plans to connect the Sawgrass Expressway to I-95 via Southwest 10th Street in Deerfield Beach, a project previously stopped by local opposition in the 1980s. Two options were shown, both preserving a local Southwest 10th Street. FDOT says the project aims to ease rush-hour congestion, but residents and Mayor Bill Ganz expressed concern over impacts including construction, property values, and proximity to a major highway.

This study compared a syndromic PCR respiratory panel with a targeted hybridization capture-based metagenomic next-generation sequencing workflow using 29 nasopharyngeal samples from individuals suspected of acute upper respiratory infection. PCR detected 15 microorganisms in 28 positive samples, while mNGS identified 44 microorganisms, including 29 additional organisms not detected by PCR. Concordance for shared targets was high, with 98.33% positive percent agreement and 100% negative percent agreement. The mNGS workflow detected bacteria, viruses, and fungi and enabled phenotypic grouping by pathogenic potential using the IDbyDNA Explify platform. The authors conclude that targeted hybridization capture-based mNGS may supplement current respiratory diagnostics by identifying broader respiratory coinfections and supporting phenotypic interpretation, but further studies are needed to establish clinical relevance.

Nigeria faces a worsening doctor shortage as many physicians migrate, mainly to the UK and US. NOIPolls says 88% of Nigerian doctors plan to leave, while the physician-patient ratio has declined to 1:5,000 against WHO’s 1:600 recommendation. Causes include high taxes, low satisfaction, poor pay, and overseas knowledge gaps.

The paper proposes an architecture for digitally structured information exchange between enterprises in industrial ecosystems, focusing on technical information in plant lifecycle management. Current practices rely on manual, error-prone tools such as spreadsheets and email, while existing standards and integrations lack sufficient scope, scalability, or support for technical information. The proposed solution uses an open consortium to define common business practices and information formats, and a network of mediators to route information between business partners through single integrations and adapters. The architecture aims to support scalable communication despite heterogeneous back-end systems. A prototype demonstrated delivery of equipment information between suppliers and plant operators in maintenance and renewal project cases. The paper concludes that the main challenge is organising ecosystem-wide collaboration, since the required ICT technologies already exist.

The case concerned whether Buffalo could impose a second assessment on benefited property owners to pay additional costs for constructing a sewer. The city had first assessed $1,058.63 and contracted with Randolph to build the sewer for that amount. During construction, Randolph encountered unforeseen quicksand, making completion impossible for the contract price or twice that amount. He stopped work and petitioned for additional compensation; the common council allowed $588.13 more and ordered a further assessment.

The plaintiffs argued the second assessment was illegal because the city had already fixed the cost, contracted for the work, and taken security for performance. The court held that Buffalo’s charter authorized further assessments when an original assessment proved insufficient. It also held that a municipal corporation empowered to make public improvements may modify or increase a contract price when equitably justified, unless prohibited by its charter. Because the quicksand was unforeseen, the added compensation was not a gratuity, and the second assessment was valid. The order was affirmed, with judgment against the plaintiffs.

The study investigated physical education teacher education (PETE) students’ experiences in gaining 21st-century skills through peer mentoring in a 14-week first-year movement education course at a university in Türkiye. Designed as a qualitative case study, it involved 3 peer mentors, 25 first-year peer learners, and a course lecturer. The course used storytelling, gamification, social media communication, group tasks, peer feedback, and student-designed teaching activities.

Data were collected through field notes, reflection notes, meetings, audio recordings, social media messages, short films, peer feedback, and online reflections, then analyzed through inductive continuous comparison. Three themes emerged: peer learners excluded group members who did not contribute but supported those who made effort; peer mentors and learners developed teaching content, increasing responsibility, productivity, and teacher awareness; and storytelling connected course content with daily life, making learning more memorable.

The study concluded that peer mentoring and interactive, nontraditional learning environments helped PETE students experience 21st-century skills such as communication, cooperation, responsibility, leadership, adaptability, creativity, problem-solving, and technology use. Storytelling supported active participation, lasting learning, and connections between movement skills and real-life experiences. The study recommended integrating peer mentoring and storytelling-based designs more sustainably into undergraduate teacher education programs.

The Korean diet, or K-diet, is based on traditional Korean eating habits and emphasizes whole, unprocessed foods, fresh vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, fermented foods, seasonings, and smaller portions. Common foods include rice, barley, vegetables, kimchi, fermented soybean products, soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and broth-based dishes. It minimizes processed foods, sugary drinks, unhealthy fats, and dairy.

Potential benefits include support for overall wellbeing, weight loss when combined with physical activity, improved digestion from probiotic foods, and gut health benefits from fermented foods. It is high in fibre and low in calories and saturated fats. Drawbacks may include high sodium from fermented foods and condiments, low calcium due to limited dairy, spicy ingredients that may irritate digestive issues, and high carbohydrate content requiring portion control for some people.

Google is launching three experimental mobile photography apps for Android and iOS, inspired by Motion Stills and built on technologies such as object recognition, person segmentation, stylization, and image encoding. Storyboard for Android turns videos into single-page comic layouts with selected frames and visual styles. Selfissimo! for iOS and Android automatically captures black-and-white selfies when users stop moving. Scrubbies for iOS lets users manipulate video playback speed and direction to create loops. Google says the apps use technology under active research and public feedback will guide future development.

Motley Fool Money promotes the Citi Simplicity® Card as a balance transfer option for people with credit card debt. The card offers 0% intro APR for 21 months on balance transfers and 12 months on purchases, followed by a variable APR of 17.99%–28.74%. Balance transfers must be completed within four months to receive the introductory 3% fee, with a $5 minimum; afterward the fee is 5%. The card has no annual fee, late fees, or penalty rate. Recommended credit is good to excellent, though approval is not guaranteed. The passage states that transferring $5,000 in debt at 24% APR could result in paying a $150 transfer fee instead of $2,428 in interest. Motley Fool Money discloses that it receives compensation from partners, including Citi/Citigroup, which may affect product placement but not ratings.

The passage argues that Russian officials violated the rights of American crew members from the Cape Horn Pigeon by forcibly compelling them to navigate a Russian vessel, leaving Russia liable for damages beyond labor value. It says their later acceptance of payment should not bar claims for impressment, loss of liberty, and poor treatment after being left without suitable food or shelter in Vladivostok. It also states that interest on indemnity awards is widely accepted, citing multiple arbitration precedents. The damages claim for loss of vessel use is based on an estimated average catch of eight whales, supported by affidavits, with calculations using whale bone and oil yields and market prices for bone and oil.

ESPN’s Week 6 college football Power Rankings focus on offensive strengths and areas needing improvement as the season nears its midpoint. Penn State and preseason No. 1 Texas dropped out of the Top 25, while the rankings were reshuffled after upsets and close calls.

Ohio State’s defense has excelled, but its run game needs more explosive plays. Miami is 5-0 and can both run physically and hit passing plays, though it has had late-game offensive lulls. Oregon’s offense has been led by Dante Moore’s efficient passing and breakout freshman running backs. Ole Miss has scored well since its quarterback change but needs more big runs.

Texas A&M moved into the top five after a 31-9 win, supported by a strong defense and improving offense. Oklahoma still needs a reliable run game beyond its injured quarterback.
