Indiana’s offense ranks highly nationally but struggled in a recent road win and faces Oregon next. Texas Tech stayed unbeaten with a dominant win despite red zone issues.

Alabama’s offense showed balance in a win over Vanderbilt, though Ty Simpson noted he must avoid sacks. Georgia beat Kentucky but needs offensive line continuity amid injuries. Tennessee’s deep passing has improved, while Georgia Tech wants more consistency through the air. LSU and Missouri have productive elements but need better rushing support and pass protection, respectively.

Other notes include Memphis remaining unbeaten behind a strong rushing attack, Cincinnati producing balanced offense in Big 12 play, and Texas struggling badly on offense in a loss to Florida.

Pumpkin is a nutrient-rich fruit in the Cucurbitaceae family and can be used in many foods beyond pie, including soups, salads, desserts, preserves, muffins, quick breads, and baked dishes. One cup of cooked pumpkin is low in calories and provides fibre, iron, potassium, carbohydrates, vitamin E, and carotenoids including alpha-carotene, beta-carotene, lutein, and zeaxanthin. Its potassium content is higher than that of a large banana and is linked in the passage to healthy blood pressure and reduced cardiovascular risk. The passage describes pumpkin’s plant nutrients as beneficial for cardiovascular health, immunity, eye health, cognition, and blood pressure, highlighting the roles of potassium, phytonutrients, and carotenoids.

Version 2 of the GHCB specification adds hypervisor feature advertisement through a 52-bit FEATURES bitmap that guests can request before a GHCB is established. The GHCB is a guest-specified, shared, 4K-aligned page whose GPA is communicated through MSR 0xc001_0130 and VMCB offset 0x00a0; the hypervisor must not intercept access to this MSR. The lower 12 bits of the GHCB MSR support an MSR protocol for requests such as SEV information, CPUID values, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration and unregistration, page state changes, VMPL switching, hypervisor feature support, and guest termination.

GHCB GPA registration is supported and required for SEV-SNP guests. A guest may request a preferred GHCB GPA, must register a GHCB GPA before first use, and may unregister it later. Registration replaces any previous registration, and a hypervisor must terminate a guest that supplies a GHCB GPA not matching the registered value. If SEV-SNP Multi-VMPL is advertised, each VMPL level must be allowed to register a GHCB GPA.

The passage describes example GHCB negotiation for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests, including use of CPUID, SEV information, encryption-bit discovery, shared GHCB page setup, and GHCB GPA registration for SEV-SNP. VMGEXIT processing uses GHCB fields, VALID_BITMAP, SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2. Non-automatic exits cause #VC exceptions for SEV-ES guests; guests provide required state in the GHCB, issue VMGEXIT, and process hypervisor results. Hypervisors can report VMGEXIT errors through SW_EXITINFO fields.

Supported NAE-related mechanisms include IOIO, MSR, VMMCALL, MMIO, page state change, SNP guest requests, SNP extended guest requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell page setup, #HV IPI, #HV timer, APIC ID list retrieval, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO guest requests, Secure AVIC backing page registration, termination requests, and unsupported-event handling. Several SEV-SNP features require shared pages, GPA-to-SPA translation, RMP table updates, and specific retry or error reporting behavior.

The passage also covers SEV-SNP secrets page guest-reserved fields, EFI configuration table support for secrets and CPUID pages, SEV-ES guest identification through CPUID properties, AP boot challenges under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, AP jump table use, vCPU hotplug limitations without SNP AP Creation, NMI completion signaling, debug register virtualization behavior, and states that SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

Restricted Injection uses a shared #HV doorbell page with PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields to communicate host notifications. The host presents interrupts, NMIs, and machine checks through this page and may signal #HV; the guest atomically acknowledges events and handles EOI either by clearing NoEoiRequired or by VMGEXIT to write the x2APIC EOI MSR. The doorbell protocol defines host and guest behavior for interrupt presentation, acknowledgement, non-maskable events, halt handling, and non-cooperative behavior.

Lincoln County defeated Laughlin in its Homecoming volleyball game after winning the first two sets, dropping later sets, and taking the final set to 15 while holding Laughlin under 10 points. Coach Chantel Holt said the team played well early but struggled mentally when trying to finish in four sets. She also used many substitutions, saying it built team camaraderie and showed the team had options. The Lady Lynx next play Calvary at home.

The passage presents a systematic review and computational taxonomy of social-scientific research on large language models (LLMs). It argues that LLMs should be studied as social artifacts whose significance emerges from both technical design and social embedding. The review addresses three questions: what themes organize the social science of LLMs, whether unsupervised clustering can recover a stable taxonomy, and how machine-derived categories align with expert classifications.

Using a PRISMA-compliant search across major databases, the study screened 64,717 records and included 270 studies. Most were journal articles, with substantial preprint and conference representation, and publications increased sharply from 2023 onward. Study 1 embedded titles and abstracts with Sentence-BERT, applied K-means clustering, validated the solution with internal and stability metrics, and used LDA topic modeling to interpret clusters. A robust three-cluster structure emerged: LLM as Social Minds, LLM Societies, and LLM–Human Interactions.

The LLM as Social Minds cluster covers work on theory of mind, moral and social reasoning, bias, self-regulation, preferences, ideological profiles, deception, trust, and epistemic risk. The LLM Societies cluster covers multi-agent simulations, generative agents, cooperation, game settings, collective epistemics, institutional design, norms, and committee-like decision processes. The LLM–Human Interactions cluster covers perception, anthropomorphism, trust, affective communication, collaboration, creativity, education, productivity, inequality, social engineering, and governance risks.

Study 2 compared the machine taxonomy with expert coding. Expert labels were highly predictable from text embeddings, with Macro-F1 of 0.954 ± 0.018. Alignment between unsupervised clusters and expert categories was strong, with NMI of 0.811 and ARI of 0.867. Boundary cases mainly occurred where individual cognition, multi-agent collectives, and human interaction overlapped.

The discussion frames the three categories as levels of analysis rather than competing schools. It argues that claims about LLM cognition, multi-agent behavior, and human-facing effects require different evidentiary standards, and that the taxonomy can support cumulative research, measurement validation, robustness testing, and cross-level hypotheses. The passage concludes that the key question is not whether LLMs resemble persons, but how their predictions become embedded in institutions, interfaces, governance arrangements, and human practices.

Wiseguyreports added a 2017 Global Smart Service Robots Market report covering demand, growth, opportunities, key players, and forecasts to 2022. The report uses SWOT analysis and examines production, consumption, revenue, market share, price, capacity, and growth by manufacturer, region, product type, and application. Regions include North America, Europe, China, Japan, Southeast Asia, and India. Product segments are personal and professional service robots, with commercial and home uses. Key manufacturers include SoftBank, Kawada, Honda, Hajime Research Institute, PROTRYLY VISION GROUP, Ubtech Robotics, Suzhou Pangolin Robot, SIASUN Robot, ROBOTIS, Hanson Robotics, Dongbu Robot, Engineered Arts, Willow Garage, and QIHAN Technology/Sanbot.

The 49ers ruled out Brock Purdy, Ricky Pearsall and Jauan Jennings for Thursday night’s game against the Rams. Purdy cited the short turnaround as a challenge for recovery from toe soreness, and Mac Jones will make his third start of the season after returning to full strength from a sprained knee. Pearsall and Jennings worsened existing injuries against Jacksonville, leaving San Francisco short-handed against a Rams defense ranked highly in yards allowed, defensive EPA and sacks. The 49ers will have extra rest after the game before visiting Tampa Bay in Week 6.

The passage describes AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, an optional extension to SEV and SNP for offloading page migration between system physical addresses while preserving guest physical addresses. TMPM support is detected through the ENGINE_READY bit and requires IOMMU enablement.

TMPM helps tiered memory systems move frequently accessed data to faster memory and less frequently accessed data to slower memory. It can safely migrate pages involved in concurrent DMA by pausing DMA traffic and updating IOMMU mappings, and it can migrate SNP-protected guest pages as a trusted agent. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO supports migration of pages targeted by DMA and hypervisor state pages, while PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST supports migration of SNP guest pages using the Pre-Migration RMP state.

TMPM commands can migrate up to 128 pages using Page Migration Lists. Per-page statuses indicate success, retryable conditions such as PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE, or failures. Commands with 16 or more pages provide better bandwidth, with maximum performance at 128 pages. Ring buffer performance improves when kept filled, and interrupts should generally be requested at sequence ends or low-water marks.

Certain structures must not be migrated, including IOMMU SPA-based structures, vIOMMU private page tables, pinned backing storage buffers, the ring buffer, and argument pages. Source pages for PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO must be DMA-mapped through one IOMMU host page table. Host software must avoid concurrent modifications to referenced IOMMU host page table entries during TMPM operations.

TMPM firmware can be reloaded only when no operations are in flight, after pausing operations and tearing down the ring buffer. Reload requires compatible firmware versioning and checking ENGINE_READY before communication. TMPM hardware only moves data between 4KB-aligned pages, so all system physical addresses must be 4KB aligned.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2016. As of October 19, 2016, it had 475,166,527 common shares outstanding.

For Q3 2016, Amazon reported net sales of $32.7 billion, up from $25.4 billion in Q3 2015, and net income of $252 million, up from $79 million. Operating income rose to $575 million from $406 million. For the nine months ended September 30, 2016, net sales were $92.2 billion, net income was $1.6 billion, and operating income was $2.9 billion.

Q3 2016 segment sales were $18.9 billion for North America, $10.6 billion for International, and $3.2 billion for AWS. Segment operating income was $255 million for North America and $861 million for AWS, while International recorded an operating loss of $541 million. AWS sales increased 55% year over year in Q3 2016.

Operating cash flow was $4.5 billion in Q3 2016 and $5.8 billion for the first nine months of 2016. Cash and cash equivalents were $13.7 billion as of September 30, 2016, compared with $15.9 billion at December 31, 2015. Total assets were $70.9 billion, total liabilities were $53.1 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $17.8 billion.

Amazon reported $8.3 billion in long-term debt face value and no borrowings outstanding under its $3.0 billion unsecured revolving credit facility as of September 30, 2016. The company also disclosed commitments totaling $39.9 billion, including debt, leases, purchase obligations, and other commitments.

The filing discusses accounting policies, recent accounting pronouncements, tax matters, legal proceedings, and contingencies. Amazon reported ongoing tax examinations, including disputes with the IRS and French Tax Administration, and noted a European Commission investigation involving Luxembourg tax decisions. The company also disclosed a patent infringement complaint filed by Broadcom Corporation and Avago Technologies General IP against Amazon entities, which Amazon disputes.

King Salman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan held talks in Riyadh on bilateral cooperation and regional and international developments. Erdogan received an official reception, and Crown Prince Muhammad Bin Naif separately discussed regional peace, security, and combating terrorism with him.

The passage describes a year-long knowledge exchange project in England between UCL Institute of Education’s Citizenship PGCE programme and Diversity Role Models to support student teachers in developing trans-inclusive citizenship education. Set against rising hostility, media debate, and draft Department for Education guidance on gender-questioning children and Relationships, Sex and Health Education, the project examined how teachers can use rights-based approaches, equality law, and human rights frameworks to support transgender students.

Student teachers attended workshops, applied learning during placements, and presented examples of practice. They commonly used “actualising” to connect LGBTQ+ identities to real-life contexts, though most examples focused on sexual orientation rather than trans identities. Participants linked this gap to uncertainty and fear caused by public debate and proposed policy changes.

The project found that Citizenship education can support trans inclusion by teaching equality and human rights law, using personal stories to build empathy, addressing bullying through clear policies and restorative approaches, and promoting visibility through school displays, Pride groups, and allyship. International frameworks such as the UNCRC, Yogyakarta Principles+10, and UNESCO guidance were presented as supporting inclusive education and teacher training. The authors conclude that effective trans inclusion requires whole-school approaches, confident specialist teaching, and partnerships with civil society organisations.

The passage describes medical problems reported after BNT162b2 booster doses in Phase 2/3 and Phase 3 studies. Serious medical problems were defined as life-threatening, requiring hospital care, or causing lasting problems. In Phase 1, between Dose 1 and 6 months after Dose 2, 2 participants had serious medical problems: inflamed appendix in the BNT162b2 20-µg group and inflamed nerves in the BNT162b2 30-µg group. Researchers did not believe these were related.

The message urges Congress to approve substantial tariff reductions on Cuban imports to the United States through a reciprocal commercial arrangement. It cites prior recommendations and President McKinley’s statements that Cuba should have close, friendly, and reciprocal relations with the United States and that its prosperity should be restored. The author notes an urgent appeal from Cuba’s president warning of financial ruin without legislative relief.

The message argues that reciprocity with Cuba is unique, compatible with the U.S. protective tariff system, and authorized under existing tariff law for reductions up to 20 percent for a particular country. It rejects objections that benefits would go mainly to American sugar refiners, saying safeguards can be provided. It states the issue is not broader tariff revision but a special arrangement covering Cuban products.

The author contends that fears of harm to American industries are unfounded, comparing them to earlier concerns about Hawaii, and says many U.S. industries would benefit from access to the Cuban market. The message links the proposal to U.S. interests in the West Indies, Central America, and related regions after the Spanish-American War and the expected Isthmian Canal.

It emphasizes that Cuba is independent but has accepted special international obligations at U.S. request, and therefore should receive special economic concessions. The message concludes that the United States, having helped secure and administer Cuba’s freedom, should continue that policy by giving Cuba economic assistance that supports its self-government and future prosperity.

Taiwan health authorities urge residents to avoid raw or undercooked eggs amid rising avian flu risk, cook eggs and poultry thoroughly, wash hands after handling eggshells, and seek medical care for fever.

Malaysia’s central bank will allow all resident entities to short-sell Malaysian government securities from May 2 to boost bond market liquidity and risk management. It will also expand hedging options for non-bank entities and residents, consider short selling of shariah-compliant MGII bonds, and introduce a new financial markets code of conduct. The measures aim to improve liquidity and encourage more onshore ringgit trade.

Kinlochleven has received three new defibrillators through local fundraising, donations, and Lucky 2B Here support. Residents have completed emergency life support training, with devices planned for the Co-op and GP surgery. The first responders group has raised £2,900 of £3,500.

In an action against the executor of James McKechnie, Charles Jones claimed McKechnie had promised to indemnify him for endorsing notes made for Sherman Kingsbury, Jones’s son-in-law, and to save him harmless from resulting losses. Jones alleged he relied on these promises when endorsing notes and giving mortgages as collateral, which were later foreclosed after Kingsbury and McKechnie failed to pay.

The defendant denied the alleged agreements. The court noted that the main surviving witness to the agreements was Kingsbury, whose testimony was subject to suspicion because of his relationship to Jones. The trial court admitted evidence that McKechnie, Denbow, and Kingsbury had speculated in hops, and that McKechnie refused an offer to sell the hops at a profit large enough to pay Kingsbury’s debts.

The appellate court held this evidence was irrelevant to the indemnity issue, likely to create sympathy for Jones and Kingsbury and prejudice against McKechnie, and prejudicial to the defendant. The judgment and order denying a new trial were reversed, and a new trial was granted.

Magda Enriquez secretly joined the Sandinistas in 1976, later becoming a founding member of their women’s association and a representative of AMNLAE on Nicaragua’s Council of State. Educated in the United States, she returned to Nicaragua, founded a school for mentally disabled children, and became involved in slum organizing after linking children’s disabilities to malnutrition. Influenced by Roman Catholic liberation theology, she entered revolutionary work and requested military training after witnessing police repression and a crop-poisoning attack during a peasant land sit-in in 1978 that led to children’s deaths.

Enriquez describes balancing revolutionary work with motherhood, relying on community, party support, and solidarity to care for her children during absences. She says the revolution has not immediately solved women’s problems but has created opportunities to address them. She has also participated in delegations preparing for Nicaragua’s elections, calling democracy a new experience for Nicaraguans.

Harry Kane led England to the World Cup quarter-finals with a penalty in a 4-3 shootout win over Colombia after Yerry Mina’s late equaliser. Kane said England were fully focused on facing Sweden and remained the tournament’s top scorer with six goals. Kieran Trippier praised the team’s spirit after scoring in the shootout. Colombia’s Radamel Falcao accused the referee of favouring England, while Diego Maradona called the result a “monumental theft.”

Hinsdale South High School seniors were named Illinois State Scholars, a recognition for top academic achievement based on ACT/SAT scores, unweighted GPA and class size, awarded to students in the top 10 percent of Illinois graduating seniors.

Between 24 and 48 weeks, adverse events occurred in 33.8% of Primary SOC, 40.8% of Secondary SOC, and 38.6% of Continued Additional Educational Program subjects. Serious AEs occurred in 11.8%, 13.5%, and 14.0%, respectively. Overall, 24 deaths and no pregnancies were reported. AEGEAN found high apixaban adherence/persistence, with no added benefit from education.

The article argues that retirees and FIRE individuals face a significant risk of running out of money if they lack a large margin of safety, withdraw too much, experience poor early investment returns, or are poorly diversified. It explains FIRE as “Financial Independent Retire Early” and uses a hypothetical couple retiring in January 2000 with $1 million and annual withdrawals to show how bad market timing and continued withdrawals can deplete a portfolio. The passage emphasizes sequence risk, withdrawal rates, and diversification as key factors. It discusses the 4% rule, notes that lower withdrawal rates such as 3% may improve outcomes, and cites Edward Thorp’s view that very low spending may be needed for long-term sustainability. The article concludes that survival in retirement depends on conservative planning, frugality, diversification, and a low withdrawal rate.

Appleton couple Andrea and Luke Benrud are sharing their story nationally to encourage CPR training after Luke used CPR learned in a Red Cross class to save Andrea when she collapsed from an undetected heart defect. Their family is now CPR trained.

Analysts expect the European Central Bank to temper expectations for a quick exit from eurozone stimulus, keeping interest rates at historic lows and maintaining the September expiry for its €30 billion monthly bond-buying scheme. Risks include sluggish inflation, a stronger euro, potential US trade tensions, and slower momentum in business indicators. Inflation was 1.3% in March, below the ECB’s target of just under 2%, while forecasts see it reaching 1.7% by 2020. Despite signs of weaker momentum, eurozone growth forecasts for 2018 have been raised to 2.4%. Analysts expect ECB normalisation away from QE and low rates to remain gradual and cautious.

Body camera footage from an Aug. 19 Grand Rapids police incident shows Officer Kevin Penn pressing the muzzle of his AR-15 against a suspect’s head during an arrest connected to an alleged armed robbery, apparently involving mistaken identity. The suspect, who was drunk and allegedly noncompliant, had been tased and brought to the ground before the incident. An Internal Affairs report said the suspect complained of pain and another officer pushed the rifle away. Kent County Prosecutor Chris Becker said the conduct was not trained or condoned but declined to file criminal charges. The suspect was arrested for resisting arrest and later released. Penn was allowed to resign, and other officers reported his actions.

Manheim Township police charged Jonathan Erick Miles, 33, after allegedly finding two marijuana plants, controlled substances and smoking devices during an April 9 search of his home. He also faces child endangerment charges for allegedly being under the influence while caring for his daughter. He was released on $20,000 unsecured bail. Police also reported recent charges against Glen VanDerSchaaf, Tyran Gregory Ellis and Gilberto Isaac-Suarez in separate cases.

Companies use exhibitions and events to improve brand image and gather customer feedback, often requiring experienced hosts, promoters, models, hostesses, and moderators. Traditional recruitment agencies can be costly and limited, while Professionate offers an online event staffing platform connecting companies, recruitment agencies, and temporary job candidates worldwide. Employers can register, view candidate profiles, images, ratings, and reviews, while candidates can upload profiles and apply for vacancies. The passage also promotes Professionate’s event staffing and hostess services in Dubai.

The U.N. warned that Yemen’s war and unpaid teacher salaries could leave up to 4.5 million children unable to finish the school year, increasing risks of child recruitment and early marriage. UNICEF said 166,000 teachers have not been paid since October, amid a banking dispute between the government and Houthi authorities.

Channel 4’s documentary *The Super Orgasm* follows five women who say they can have many orgasms in one sexual encounter, with one reporting more than 60. The program includes experiments measuring arousal, brain waves, and brain blood flow, but experts note the research was not scientific because it involved few participants and no control group. Cynthia Graham and Nan Wise say the term “super orgasm” is misleading and differs little from multiple orgasms. They emphasize that orgasm experiences vary widely, that the women featured are uncommon, and that having many orgasms should not be treated as a standard or goal for all women.

This study examined whether sex differences affect the relationship between the self-reported PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5) and the clinician-administered Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 (CAPS-5). The sample included 100 adults, 56 males and 44 females, who completed both assessments. Veteran status and trauma type, military or civilian, were recorded.

CAPS-5 scores did not significantly differ by sex or trauma type, indicating similar clinician-assessed PTSD symptom severity across groups. Overall, PCL-5 and CAPS-5 scores were significantly correlated, but the correlation was stronger in females than males. Females also showed a higher odds ratio for PCL-5 predicting CAPS-5 classification. Male participants showed significant deviation from the ideal PCL-5/CAPS-5 regression line, while female participants did not.

Using PCL-5 alone led to more PTSD misclassification among males than females. Fifteen males were misclassified compared with five females, with most misclassifications involving PCL-5 scores meeting PTSD criteria when CAPS-5 did not.

Trauma type also affected alignment between measures. Participants with civilian trauma showed stronger PCL-5/CAPS-5 correlations than those with military trauma, a pattern observed in both sexes, though the female military trauma subgroup was very small.

The authors conclude that PCL-5 and CAPS-5 are correlated, but alignment is stronger in females and civilian trauma cases. They suggest clinicians should consider sex and trauma type when interpreting PCL-5 results, especially for male and military trauma populations. Limitations include the modest sample size, few females with military trauma, and recruitment from one geographic region.

The lecture develops continuity and its relationship to limits and sequences. It proves that if a point is not a cluster point of a set, every function is continuous there, while if it is a cluster point, continuity at that point is equivalent to the function’s limit equaling its value. It also proves the sequential characterization: a function is continuous at c iff every sequence in the domain converging to c has function values converging to f(c).

Using this characterization, the lecture shows sine is continuous via an epsilon-delta proof and derives continuity of cosine from sine. It gives an example of a function discontinuous everywhere: the function equal to 1 on rationals and 0 on irrationals, using sequences of rationals or irrationals converging to any point.

The lecture then proves that sums, products, quotients with nonzero denominator, and compositions of continuous functions are continuous. Consequences include continuity of powers, polynomials, and functions such as 1/(3 + sin⁴x). It concludes by previewing the minimum-maximum theorem and intermediate value theorem for continuous functions on intervals.

STAT’s biotech update highlights FDA approval of a second generic mifepristone, Amgen’s Repatha trial showing reduced risk of major heart events, and coverage of NIH efforts to reduce reliance on animal testing.

Cover 3 is a 4-under, 3-deep zone defense with two cornerbacks and a free safety covering deep thirds while four underneath defenders cover hook, curl, and flat zones. It is used to limit deep passes, balance run and pass defense, and allow a safety to play near the line of scrimmage. Its strengths include balanced coverage and added run support, making it common at high school and college levels. Weaknesses include vulnerability in the flats, seams, perimeter runs, and four-vertical concepts. Common variations include flipping safety responsibilities, Cover 3 fire zone blitzes, Cover 3 Buzz, and pattern-reading techniques such as Rip/Liz coverage.

The Times reported that officials said Trump campaign advisers, including Paul Manafort, were intercepted on calls with Russian intelligence officials, which Manafort denied. U.S. intelligence officials have linked Russia to election-related cyberattacks and efforts to help Trump win, while Russia denies involvement. Rep. Elijah Cummings called the report alarming. The report followed Michael Flynn’s resignation over calls with Russia’s ambassador about sanctions. Sean Spicer said nothing had changed regarding Trump’s denial of campaign contacts with Russians.

An involuntary bankruptcy petition was filed against John Jacob Beechwood, who denied insolvency and acts of bankruptcy and claimed immunity as a farmer under the Bankruptcy Act. A jury found he was insolvent and had committed acts of bankruptcy, including conveying his farm to his wife on September 20, 1940. The court considered whether he was a farmer at the time of the acts.

Beechwood lived on and operated a farm, but he had been a full-time employee of Fidelity and Casualty Company of New York, earning $7,200 annually, with additional legal income. His farm activities were part-time before his resignation, and his principal income came from non-farming work. The court held that he was not personally engaged in farming as his principal livelihood at the relevant times and therefore was not immune from involuntary bankruptcy. An order adjudicating him bankrupt was to be entered.

The President transmits to the House documents and correspondence concerning the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo and the Senate’s amendments, including instructions to U.S. commissioners sent to Mexico. He explains that although he had previously withheld the instructions as potentially prejudicial to public interests, he now provides them because the House requested them and they are necessary to understand the related documents.

The commissioners were instructed only to obtain Mexico’s ratification of the treaty as amended by the Senate, not to negotiate or modify it. The Mexican Congress approved the amended treaty before the commissioners were officially received or held conferences, relying only on explanations sent by the U.S. Secretary of State. Ratifications were exchanged afterward, and the treaty was proclaimed in the United States.

The President states that the later “protocol” summarizing conversations between the commissioners and Mexican officials was not part of the treaty and did not alter it. He argues that both governments understood the treaty to be ratified as amended. He reviews the protocol’s three explanations—on rights of inhabitants of ceded territories, land grants, and Mexico’s ability to transfer the $12 million payment obligation—and concludes they were consistent with the treaty and created no new obligations or modifications. Therefore, he took no further action regarding the protocol.

S. E. Mezes reports progress from a Thursday meeting and circulates a memorandum on topics for The Inquiry, including peace conference techniques, war-breeding areas, national data and aspirations, international governmental arrangements, world organization, laws of war, reparations, internationalized trade routes, and business and diplomacy. A preliminary survey lists practical conference tasks where The Inquiry can assist: establishing boundaries and governments, assessing doubtful states, economic arrangements, minority protections, equality of economic opportunity, international law, and diplomatic history. It identifies regions where these tasks may or must apply, including Russia, Poland, Slesvig, Belgium, Luxemburg, Alsace-Lorraine, Trentino, Triest, Austria-Hungary, the Balkans, Turkey, Africa, the Far East, Pacific Islands, Latin America, Persia and Afghanistan, and Spitsbergen. Boundaries are required for several European and Ottoman regions, while government arrangements are required for Poland and Austria-Hungary and may be needed elsewhere.

Amazon is preparing a new round of layoffs that could cut up to 15% of its human resources division, known internally as PXT, with additional cuts likely in other parts of its core consumer business, according to sources. The total number of affected employees and timing are unclear, and Amazon declined to comment. The cuts come as Amazon seeks to reduce employee costs while investing heavily in AI products, infrastructure, and datacenters, with planned capital expenditures exceeding $100 billion this year. CEO Andy Jassy has said AI-related efficiency gains are expected to reduce Amazon’s corporate workforce. Amazon previously cut at least 27,000 corporate jobs from late 2022 into 2023. While planning corporate layoffs, Amazon also announced plans to hire 250,000 seasonal warehouse and logistics workers in the U.S.

The address affirms the Constitution, democracy, and the founding creed that all are created equal with rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. It argues that each generation must adapt founding principles to new challenges through collective action while preserving individual initiative, hard work, and responsibility.

The speech says America has advanced through struggles over slavery, economic modernization, fair markets, and protections for the vulnerable. It notes that war is ending, economic recovery has begun, and the nation’s future depends on unity, a rising middle class, opportunity, education, government reform, and rewarding effort.

It supports security and dignity through Medicare, Medicaid, and Social Security while calling for lower health care costs and deficit reduction. It calls for action on climate change, leadership in sustainable energy, and protection of natural resources. It advocates national security through military strength, rule of law, peaceful engagement, alliances, democracy, human dignity, and justice.

The address emphasizes equality as an unfinished task, citing women’s equal pay, equal treatment for gay Americans, voting rights, immigration reform, and children’s safety. It says citizens must act despite disagreement and imperfection, reject absolutism and political spectacle, and use their votes and voices to shape national debates. The speech concludes by urging common effort, purpose, and dedication to carry forward freedom.

CarsDirect found December incentives on fuel-efficient vehicles, including leases from $159/month and discounts up to $18,100. Kia offers $5,000 off the 2017 Optima Hybrid in Western states or $4,000 elsewhere, with a 0-percent 60-month financing option that reduces bonus cash. The Optima Plug-In leases for $249/month for 36 months with $1,999 down, while the 2017 Hyundai Sonata Plug-In Hybrid is $289/month with $1,699 due in California for conquest buyers. Chevrolet offers the 2017 Volt at $273/month for 39 months with $500 due.

In California, the 2017 Kia Soul EV can get $18,100 off the EV+ model or lease from $159/month for 36 months with $1,999 due. Chevrolet Bolt EV leases start at $303/month for 36 months in some regions, or $329/month elsewhere with higher mileage. The 2018 Chevrolet Equinox diesel has a nationwide $4,000 discount. The Toyota Yaris iA has $2,000 off in Southern California, bringing its price to about $15,000.

A GreenMedInfo article reports on a Journal of Hematology & Thromboembolic Diseases study examining Bt/Cry toxins used in genetically modified crops. The study, by researchers at the University of Brasilia, tested effects on non-target mammalian organisms and found that Cry toxins caused hematological changes in mice, including damage to red blood cell lineage, hypochromic anemia, suppressed bone marrow proliferation, and abnormal lymphocyte patterns described as consistent with some leukemias. The article says the findings challenge claims that Bt toxins are selectively toxic to insects and inactive in mammals. The authors concluded that genetically modified Bt spore-crystals expressing Cry1Aa, Cry1Ab, Cry1Ac, or Cry2A may pose hematological risks to vertebrates, with toxic effects increasing over longer exposure, and called for further studies before deeming them safe for mammals. The article also criticizes biotech industry safety claims, raises concerns about combined exposure to Bt toxins and glyphosate-based herbicides, and advocates GMO labeling, bans, and participation in anti-Monsanto activism.

H H Martyn & Co, founded by Herbert Henry Martyn in Cheltenham in 1888, became a major craftsmanship and engineering firm. It expanded to Sunningend, employed over 1,000 people by 1910, and produced work in iron, stone, plaster, stained glass, furniture, ship interiors, aircraft and vehicles. Its commissions included gates for Marble Arch, work for Buckingham Palace and Windsor Castle, Selfridges’ frontage, the House of Commons Speaker’s Chair and Dispatch Boxes, the Cenotaph, and projects for overseas royalty and buildings.

The firm fitted out more than 100 ocean liners, including the Titanic, Lusitania, Queen Mary, Queen Elizabeth and QE2. During the First World War it made military aircraft, leading to the Gloster Aircraft Company, and later contributed to the Golden Arrow land-speed record car. It also made Wolseley cars and designed the Unibus scooter.

Martyn’s continued major art-metal and sculpture work into the 1960s. Bought by Maples in the 1930s, it received wartime contracts but suffered after 1945. Maples sold its assets and closed the company in 1971.

The passage describes a Global Meat Starter Culture Market research report covering historical, current, and projected revenues, market status, growth rate, trends, drivers, constraints, risks, opportunities, PEST and Porter’s Five Forces analysis, competitive landscape, and regional markets. It profiles manufacturers including Chr. Hansen, Danisco, Kerry, SOYUZSNAB, FRUTAROM, Galactic, PROQUIGA, Sacco System, Lallemand, and others. The report segments the market by product type into maturation starters and surface starters, and by application into meat, poultry, seafood, and others. Regions covered include the United States, China, Europe, Japan, Southeast Asia, India, and Rest of World. It also includes SWOT, investment feasibility, production, supply, demand, pricing, and forecast analyses.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated September 9, 2020. The Board elected General (Ret.) Keith B. Alexander as a director and appointed him to the Audit Committee. Alexander is Co-CEO, President, and Chairman of IronNet Cybersecurity, Inc., and previously served as Commander of U.S. Cyber Command and Director of the NSA. He received a restricted stock unit award for 288 Amazon shares vesting over three years and entered into the company’s standard director indemnification agreement.

In 1826, Capt. Thomas ap Catesby Jones visited Honolulu to address deserters from American vessels and claims by resident Americans, successfully negotiating an unratified treaty of friendship, commerce, and navigation. Subsequent U.S. naval visits included Capt. Finch’s 1829 mission carrying presidential presents and a letter urging peace, justice, and respect for Hawaiian laws. U.S. officers also intervened informally, including Commodore Downs’s efforts after the 1831 deportation of Roman Catholic priests. In 1839, French commander Laplace demanded protections for Catholics and a treaty, threatening hostilities; the treaty was signed and violence avoided. British pressures followed, including a treaty forced in 1836 and Lord George Paulet’s 1843 seizure of the islands, compelling Kamehameha III to cede authority. A British commission governed until Commodore Kearney protested in July 1843. Rear-Admiral Thomas then reached an agreement with the King, restored the Hawaiian flag on July 31, and disavowed Paulet’s seizure.

Progress Software held its Q3 fiscal 2025 earnings call on September 29, 2025, with investor relations executive Michael Micciche introducing CEO Yogesh Gupta and CFO Anthony Folger. The company noted the call would include forward-looking statements on performance, strategy, products, cost initiatives and ShareFile integration, subject to risks in SEC filings. Financial figures discussed were identified as non-GAAP unless otherwise stated.

A new study suggests the hot Jupiter WASP-121b, about 880 light-years from Earth, has a stratosphere where temperatures rise with altitude, similar to a common atmospheric feature in the solar system. Led by Thomas Evans of the University of Exeter, researchers used NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope to detect glowing water molecule signatures in the planet’s atmosphere during transits. WASP-121b orbits its star every 1.3 days, is nearly twice Jupiter’s size, and has upper-atmosphere temperatures around 4,500–4,600 degrees Fahrenheit. Researchers said the finding is the strongest evidence yet for a stratosphere on an exoplanet and an important step toward detailed atmospheric studies of smaller, cooler planets in the future.

The passage introduces a Bayesian recursive bipartitioning framework for community detection in networks that avoids pre-specifying the number of communities. It addresses limitations of existing methods, where different model selection criteria can yield different community counts and where hierarchical network structure may be meaningful. The proposed method recursively divides a network into two subnetworks using a model-based partitioning algorithm and stops based on a Bayes factor comparing models with and without community structure.

The framework can use any likelihood-based community detection model and is demonstrated for stochastic block models, edge exchangeable models, and latent space models. The passage defines these models, including their assumptions, likelihood structures, and community representations. For stochastic block models, it discusses consistency of recursive bipartitioning under Erdős-Rényi modularity, giving conditions for strong and weak consistency based on expected degree and subnetwork size.

The inference approach uses Gibbs sampling for partitioning and the Bayes factor as the stopping rule. The passage provides sampling details for stochastic block models and begins presenting the Gibbs sampling procedure for edge exchangeable models, including block assignment updates and parameter updates.

Winthrop University will receive $1.1 million as part of a $20 million National Science Foundation Research Infrastructure and Improvement award supporting 10 South Carolina institutions over five years. The funding, announced Sept. 19, will support research on complex materials through the MADE in SC initiative, managed by EPSCoR. Winthrop’s share will fund 36 summer student research experiences, equipment, upgrades, student conference travel and faculty research. Researchers include Maria Gelabert, Fatima Amir, Clifton Harris, Jason Hurlbert, Robin Lammi and Pat Owens. Projects will examine electronic, optical and biomaterials, including nanoparticles, supercapacitors and photocatalysis. The research focuses on materials such as optical crystals and proteins, with potential applications in lasers, water treatment, regenerative medicine and clean energy. Winthrop will also develop two-week summer teacher workshops for regional high schools.

Coach Sutter said the previous seven-game series against Chicago, including multiple overtimes and a disrupted schedule, was emotionally and physically demanding. He noted roster changes since earlier meetings and that several players were in their first Stanley Cup Final, which may have affected the start. He said the team can play better and should avoid chasing leads. Sutter praised Kyle’s energy, discussed Mike Richards’ winning role, Jonathan’s focus, player development, Madison Square Garden’s atmosphere, defensive changes, and in-game line adjustments to manage players’ performance.

The Patient Charter, based on the NHS Constitution, sets out patients’ legal rights, NHS pledges, and patient responsibilities. It states that NHS care should be free at the point of use, with some exceptions, and based on need rather than ability to pay. Patients have rights to fair access, safe and high-quality care, NICE-recommended treatments where clinically appropriate, informed consent, privacy, choice, involvement in decisions, openness when things go wrong, and proper complaint handling.

The Charter also covers NHS duties to plan services for communities, maintain safety and quality standards, explain treatment funding decisions, and support accountability through complaints, the Ombudsman, judicial review, and compensation for negligence. Patients are expected to look after their health where possible, respect staff and other patients, follow or discuss treatment plans, attend appointments, and take part in vaccination and screening programmes.

The passage presents the Charter as a framework for safe, fair, respectful care and a reminder that the NHS depends on shared responsibility between patients, staff, and society.

The passage explains the Average True Range (ATR), a volatility indicator developed by J. Welles Wilder Jr., commonly used for stop-loss placement, position sizing, and identifying potential breakouts. It describes calculating ATR in Python with pandas_ta using SPY data from Yahoo Finance and backtesting a simple ATR-based strategy on SPY. The strategy holds the asset during high volatility and sells when volatility is low. Results were not very promising, though risk-adjusted performance improved, and combining ATR with other indicators may improve outcomes.

A University of Bristol-led study found that the chloroplast lineage split from its closest cyanobacterial ancestor more than 2.1 billion years ago in low-salinity environments. About 200 million years later, chloroplasts and eukaryotic hosts formed a symbiotic relationship. The study also found that marine algae diversified much later, around 800–750 million years ago, suggesting early algae evolved in freshwater environments before colonising marine habitats.

NASA will broadcast a six-hour ISS spacewalk on August 17 starting at 10:00am EDT. Russian Expedition 52 cosmonauts Fyodor Yurchikhin and Sergey Ryazanskiy will exit the Pirs airlock around 10:45am to deploy five nanosatellites, collect residue samples from the station exterior, and install handrails and struts. The satellites include one testing a 3D-printed casing in orbit and another commemorating Russian space anniversaries. This is the only planned Expedition 52 spacewalk and one of the longest of 2017.

The neo-Nazi website the Daily Stormer was dropped by GoDaddy after publishing an article mocking Heather Heyer, who was killed during the Charlottesville counterprotest, and praising her alleged killer. GoDaddy said the article could incite further violence and violated its terms of service. The site then moved its domain registration to Google, which soon announced it also would cancel the registration for violating its terms. The site’s hosting remained obscured through Cloudflare, which said it found some content on sites using its network repugnant but did not comment on specific users.

The Daily Stormer, founded by Andrew Anglin in 2013, is described as influential in the online white supremacist ecosystem. It also recently criticized Google for firing engineer James Damore. Separately, the site claimed it had been hacked by Anonymous, though Anglin later said he regained control. Anglin is also facing a Southern Poverty Law Center lawsuit over an alleged harassment campaign against Tanya Gersh’s family, and his whereabouts remain unknown.

Anne-Marie D'Amico, an Invesco employee, was identified as one of 10 people killed in the Toronto van attack on Yonge Street. Fifteen others were injured. Suspect Alex Minassian, 25, was arrested after a confrontation with police and was due in court. Police said the attack appeared deliberate but the motive remained unclear, and they continued seeking witnesses and information to identify victims.

A retrospective cohort study reviewed records of children admitted with clinical measles at Mulago National Referral Hospital, Uganda, from January to December 2018 to describe outcomes and estimate direct health system costs. Of 570 admissions, 553 charts were retrieved; after exclusions and sampling, 267 charts were analyzed. Patients had a median age of 1 year, 63% were under 1 year, and median hospital stay was 4 days. Thirty patients (11.3%) died, and 185 (69.3%) developed multiple complications, most commonly severe pneumonia, gastroenteritis, conjunctivitis, malnutrition, and encephalitis.

The average direct health care cost per patient was USD 33.13, including blood tests, radiology, and treatment. Average overhead costs were USD 81.37, mainly human resources, giving an estimated total direct cost of USD 114.50 per measles case. Costs were higher among males, patients with comorbidities, those hospitalized longer than 15 days, and those who died. The study concluded that measles mortality and complications were high and that treatment costs were substantial, supporting efforts to promote measles immunization.

The disclosure relates to big data recommendation systems and describes a recommendation model training method, apparatus, recommendation method, storage medium, and computer program product. The method selects positive samples from sample sets into a training set, calculates sampling probabilities for negative samples, selects negative samples based on those probabilities, and trains a recommendation model using the resulting training set.

Negative-sample sampling probabilities are calculated using one or more rules: the probability is negatively correlated with the score difference between a positive sample and a negative sample, negatively correlated with the vector distance between their feature vectors, and positively correlated with the variation of a ranking indicator after their rankings are exchanged. The goal is to assign higher sampling probabilities to negative samples that have greater impact on model training and ranking performance.

Samples may include user features, object features, and labels indicating positive or negative samples. The trained recommendation model may recommend one or more objects to a target user based on user and object features, and may also generate estimated scores used in later training iterations. The disclosure also describes correcting sampling probabilities by dividing by a maximum reference value and comparing corrected probabilities with random numbers to select negative samples.

The system architecture includes a data collection device, training device, execution device, storage system, and client device. The training device trains the recommendation model from sampled data, while the execution device uses the model to score and rank to-be-recommended objects and recommend the top M objects. Experimental comparisons on a HUAWEI APPGALLERY data set report improved ranking indicators compared with no sampling, random sampling, dynamic negative sampling, and optimized logistic regression sampling.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture, and its features for AI, HPC, data analytics, and data center workloads. A100 is built on TSMC 7nm N7, includes up to 108 SMs, 6912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, 40 GB HBM2 memory, 40 MB L2 cache, and supports PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, third-generation NVLink, MIG, and CUDA 11 capabilities.

A100’s third-generation Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary operations. They provide higher throughput than V100, including up to 312 TFLOPS dense mixed-precision FP16/FP32 performance, 19.5 TFLOPS peak FP64 throughput, and additional acceleration through fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity. TF32 enables tensor core acceleration for FP32 inputs by default, while FP16 and BF16 mixed precision offer higher training throughput.

The architecture adds asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, Compute Data Compression, improved atomic operations, hardware JPEG decode, optical flow acceleration, and multiple NVDEC units. Its 40 GB HBM2 subsystem delivers 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, and its 40 MB L2 cache provides higher bandwidth and capacity than V100. ECC protects HBM2, L2, L1 caches, and register files.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can partition one A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory bandwidth, and fault isolation. MIG supports multi-tenant, single-tenant, VM, container, and process use cases while maintaining CUDA programming compatibility. Compute Instances and Volta-style MPS enable multiple contexts and processes to run simultaneously.

Third-generation NVLink doubles the number of links compared with V100, providing 600 GB/sec total A100 bandwidth and improved error detection and recovery. PCIe Gen 4 provides 31.5 GB/sec per direction for x16 connections, and SR-IOV allows a single PCIe-connected GPU to be shared or virtualized across processes or VMs.

CUDA 11 supports A100 features including Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Task Graph acceleration, MIG, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, Cooperative Groups enhancements, and L2 cache controls. CUDA Task Graphs reduce CPU launch overhead and improve execution of repeated workflows.

The passage also describes NVIDIA DGX A100, which uses eight A100 GPUs connected by third-generation NVLink and NVSwitch, delivers up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, supports up to 56 MIG instances, and is designed for scalable AI infrastructure with NGC software, CUDA, containers, deep learning frameworks, inference, data analytics, and HPC tools.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K reporting that on February 8, 2022, NVIDIA, SoftBank Group Capital Limited, and SVF Holdco (UK) Limited mutually terminated their September 13, 2020 Share Purchase Agreement involving Arm Limited due to significant regulatory challenges preventing completion of the transaction. Under the agreement’s terms, the sellers will retain NVIDIA’s $1.25 billion prepayment, and NVIDIA will retain its 20-year Arm license. NVIDIA expects to record a $1.36 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal 2023 related to the termination.

The High/Low zone offense combines a three-player outside passing attack with an inside high/low rotation. It can start from many alignments, is relatively simple to learn, and uses constant interior movement to create matchup problems, inside scoring chances, weakside attacks, and open outside shots when the defense collapses. Sharp passing, ball movement, shooting, rebounding, and zone reads are key fundamentals.

The basic continuity begins with a point-to-wing entry, followed by a post roll to the basket or short corner and a weakside post flash into the middle. If no pass is available, the ball is reversed to continue the action. Post options include shots, baseline cuts, skip passes, kick-outs, and feeds to spot-up shooters or low-post players.

Common entries include Dribble Clear, 1-4 Slice, Mid Screen, and Horns, each designed to initiate the same high/low continuity through cuts, rolls, flashes, screens, and ball reversal. The offense can also flow into quick-hitting set plays late in the clock or after timeouts, including Pin Down, Weakside Double, and Vegas, which use down screens, double screens, skip passes, lobs, and post rolls to create scoring opportunities.

The passage describes parts of the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol and related SEV-SNP mechanisms. It covers MSR protocol requests for CPUID register values, AP reset hold, preferred and registered GHCB GPA handling, page state changes, Run VMPL, GHCB unregistration, hypervisor feature support, and guest termination. CPUID requests return one register at a time and do not support non-zero sub-leafs or function 0x0000_000d.

GHCB GPA registration is required for SEV-SNP guests before first GHCB use. A guest may request a hypervisor-preferred GHCB GPA, register a GHCB GPA, or unregister the current GPA. The hypervisor must reject mismatched GHCB GPAs and may support separate registrations per VMPL level when Multi-VMPL is advertised.

The passage provides SEV-ES and SEV-SNP GHCB negotiation examples. Guests use CPUID and MSR protocols to determine GHCB protocol versions and encryption bit positions, establish long mode, configure encrypted page tables, allocate a shared GHCB page, and register it when required. A VMGEXIT example shows a guest handling a #VC exception, populating GHCB fields, and the hypervisor processing the exit through the GHCB.

Non-automatic exits (NAEs) are handled through #VC exceptions and VMGEXIT. Guests and hypervisors must set valid GHCB bitmap bits for fields used, especially SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2. Standard VMGEXIT error handling uses SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2 to request exceptions or report malformed input.

Several NAE events are described, including IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, AP Creation, #HV doorbell page, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC, Termination Request, and Unsupported Event. Page State Change requests use shared GHCB buffer structures and support private/shared page transitions and PSMASH/UNSMASH hints. SNP Guest Request and Extended Guest Request use shared request, response, and data pages to communicate with SEV-SNP firmware and may return certificates. SNP TIO Guest Request supports trusted device interactions and returned measurements, certificates, and attestation data.

The passage also describes SEV-SNP secrets page reserved fields for VMPL guest request sequence numbers, an AP jump table address, and guest usage data. It defines an EFI SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob configuration table used to communicate secrets and CPUID pages to the OS.

SMP booting under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP is discussed, including AP reset hold, AP jump table use, and SNP AP Creation. Traditional INIT-SIPI-SIPI booting is constrained because the hypervisor cannot update measured and encrypted vCPU registers. SNP AP Creation allows a guest to provide VMSA pages for AP state and can support vCPU hotplug.

The passage states that NMI handling requires the hypervisor to avoid intercepting IRET, intercept #DB, and rely on a guest “NMI Complete” VMGEXIT message. Debug register virtualization is supported when DebugVirtualization is enabled; otherwise DR7 reads and writes must be intercepted and handled by the #VC handler. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

Restricted Injection uses a shared #HV doorbell page for host notifications. The page includes PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields to represent interrupts, NMIs, machine checks, and EOI assistance. Guests configure the doorbell page through GHCB VMGEXIT requests. Host and guest behavior is specified for presenting interrupts, acknowledging events, handling EOIs, and avoiding missed notifications or improper #HV recursion.

Aqua Terra filed a preliminary long form prospectus with securities commissions in Canadian provinces except Québec for a proposed initial public offering of common shares. The offering will be underwritten by a syndicate co-led by TD Securities, Canaccord Genuity, and RBC Capital Markets, with share number and price still undetermined and no assurance of completion. The prospectus remains subject to completion or amendment and is available on SEDAR. The release is not an offer to sell and is not for distribution in the United States. Aqua Terra provides water disposal services to Canadian and U.S. onshore oil and natural gas producers.

Charlie Tillett discusses how startups should build and use business plan financials. He argues that financial projections are important even though they will not be exact, because they identify key assumptions, business drivers, cash needs, and milestones. He emphasizes that the CEO’s primary responsibility is maintaining cash, since running out of cash can quickly threaten the company.

Tillett explains that investors evaluate teams, market opportunities, business models, and potential returns. Venture capitalists typically seek significant ownership, meaningful investment amounts, and 3x to 5x returns over five to seven years. He illustrates how pre-money valuation, investment size, angel rounds, venture rounds, employee option pools, and later financings dilute founders’ ownership. He also notes that investors often receive preferred shares, special rights, and board representation.

The lecture defines key financial statement elements: revenue, cost of goods sold, gross margin, sales and marketing, R&D, G&A, and operating profit/EBITDA. Tillett recommends analyzing whether projected revenue is realistic, whether margins and expenses resemble comparable companies, and how much cash is required before profitability. He compares business models across retail, restaurants, hardware, software, and internet companies, showing differences in gross margins, R&D spending, operating profit, and revenue per employee.

He advises building projections from the bottom up rather than assuming a percentage of a large market. Sales forecasts should connect to salespeople, territories, conversion rates, units sold, and pricing. He discourages using automated business planning software because creating the model helps founders understand the business. He recommends quarterly projections, formulas where possible, clear staffing plans, salary and benefit assumptions, cost of goods sold detail, non-salary expenses, and simple cash flow proxies based on operating losses and capital expenses.

Tillett discusses compensation, saying founders should earn a living wage but remain motivated to increase shareholder value. He also covers equity allocation, recommending vesting for founders and employees because future work is more important than past work. Typical equity ranges are presented for CEOs, VPs, senior managers, and key contributors, with larger grants for founding team members. He concludes by noting that early CFO expertise can help during fundraising and reduce dilution.

The paper presents a proof-of-concept system for supporting criminal investigations through semantic integration and analysis of Instant Messaging App data, such as WhatsApp chats extracted from seized smartphones. The approach builds a Neo4j knowledge graph from chat metadata and messages, enriches audio messages using Whisper speech-to-text transcription, extracts and links entities through a Named Entity Recognition and Linking pipeline, and supports exploration through graph queries and a faceted semantic search interface called DAVE.

The work was developed within an Italian research project in collaboration with investigators and tested on data from two real investigations involving fraud and corruption. Investigators reported that existing tools provide limited support for large-scale chat analysis, especially for audio messages. The proposed system aims to improve search, evidence exploration, and integration across heterogeneous investigative data without replacing human decision-making.

Experiments showed that graph-based modeling, transcription, and entity-based search can help explore large volumes of chat data and filter results by participants, entities, and annotations. Investigators found the graph visualizations, text-plus-relation queries, and audio transcription useful. The current system has limitations, especially in entity extraction quality on instant messaging data, and future work includes in-domain fine-tuning, improved interfaces, and enrichment of images and videos. Ethical safeguards include local data storage, restricted access, avoidance of external APIs, and support for verification against original data.

STAT’s Pharmalittle reports that BlinkRx is hosting a pharmaceutical summit with Donald Trump Jr. and Trump administration officials, raising concerns among drug-company representatives because BlinkRx could benefit from direct-to-consumer drug sales policies. It also says Pfizer’s drug-pricing agreement with the administration has prompted other major drugmakers to seek similar deals, though whether these efforts will lower prescription prices remains unclear.

The lecture reviews coding for bandwidth-limited AWGN channels, emphasizing Euclidean-space constellations, lattice constellations, shaping gain, and coding gain. The professor explains that shaping can be optimized with an n-sphere, yielding a maximum asymptotic gain of πe/6, or 1.53 dB, though practical schemes such as shell mapping and trellis shaping can obtain about 1 dB.

The lecture then discusses dense lattices, including the hexagonal lattice, D4, E8, Barnes-Wall lattices, and the Leech lattice. Although higher-dimensional lattices can have large nominal coding gains, their many nearest neighbors reduce effective coding gain, limiting practical performance.

Trellis-coded modulation is presented as a major advance for bandwidth-limited channels. Ungerboeck’s approach expands the constellation, uses set partitioning, and applies convolutional codes to improve Euclidean distance. Simple trellis codes can provide 3–4.5 dB gain, while larger trellis codes with shaping can reach roughly 6–7.5 dB total effective gain, still a few dB from the Shannon limit.

The lecture briefly covers higher-performance methods, including multilevel coding, turbo and LDPC codes, Reed-Solomon codes at higher reliability levels, and bit-interleaved coded modulation. It concludes that coding for traditional AWGN channels is mature and close to the Shannon limit, with current research shifting toward multi-user, network, and other channel models.

UNC Chapel Hill reinstated professor Dwayne Dixon after a threat assessment found no basis that he posed a threat or violated university policy. Dixon, a teaching associate professor, has participated in counterprotests to alt-right rallies and was criticized by a Turning Point USA spokesperson over his political affiliations.

The passage explains that the gold-silver ratio measures how many ounces of silver equal the value of one ounce of gold, calculated by dividing the gold price by the silver price using the same currency and weight. Traders use it to assess whether gold or silver is relatively overpriced or underpriced, often through contrarian or mean-reversion strategies involving futures, options, or ETFs. Historically, the ratio was fixed by governments, such as 12:1 in Rome and 15:1 under the U.S. Coinage Act of 1792, but it has floated since the end of fixed monetary standards. The passage states that backtests of gold, silver, and a GLD/SLV pair trade using the ratio showed poor, erratic, or flat results, and concludes that the ratio did not produce robust profitable strategies in the tested cases.

Hetzner now peers directly at NAP Africa in Isando via a 10Gbps circuit, expanding its presence at South African Internet exchange points alongside NAP Africa Cape Town and JINX. The company says over 65% of its local traffic now routes through exchange points instead of transit links, contributing more than 4Gbps and growing. Hetzner supports settlement-free peering to reduce connectivity costs, lower latency and improve resilience, and peers with major South African and global network operators. Its Samrand carrier-neutral data centre connects to major fibre routes, redundant transit links, 10Gbps interfaces and four international cable systems. Hetzner invites network operators to peer via exchange points or directly.

The lecture presents ongoing thesis research on manufacturing polymer microfluidic devices using hot embossing. Polymers are attractive because they are inexpensive, often transparent, and mechanically tough. Hot embossing involves heating a thermoplastic above its glass transition temperature, applying and holding a load so the polymer fills stamp cavities, cooling under load, and removing the stamp. Key process parameters include temperature, load, loading time, and hold time.

The speaker contrasts micro hot embossing with thermal nanoimprint lithography, which patterns very thin polymer layers on hard substrates and may support submicron lithography. Stamp fabrication methods include deep reactive ion etching of silicon, electroplating nickel, and using tougher materials such as metallic glasses.

The research focuses on efficient modeling and characterization tools for predicting embossed topography without relying solely on empirical testing or full nonlinear finite element simulations. Effects are considered at substrate, device-pattern, and individual-feature length scales. A simplified linear elastic “rubbery” model for PMMA, using a point-load response and one fitted Young’s modulus, matched experimental topography well for short hold times. Carefully designed periodic test patterns enabled rapid extraction of material behavior as a function of temperature, pressure, feature pitch, and density.

Experiments on PMMA, ZEONOR, and TOPAS showed dependencies on temperature, force, hold time, feature size, pitch, density, and material anisotropy. A fractional factorial experiment on TOPAS found temperature, force, and hold time significant, while loading time was less clearly significant. Some materials showed strong orientation-dependent behavior.

The lecture also addresses de-molding challenges, including stamp breakage, ridges, sheared polymer, thermal contraction, sidewall distortion, friction, and mechanical locking. Controlling de-molding temperature near the glass transition may reduce defects, but requires accurate temperature control. The class ends with administrative discussion about project presentations and questions on paper length and optimization methods.

Deborah Jones of Cougar Creek Streamkeepers argues that the proposed development at Scott Road and 75A Avenue conflicts with the North Delta Area Plan and Cougar Creek ISMP, particularly because it proposes 35 storeys where six are specified and fails to preserve trees, provide permeable ground, support rainwater infiltration, or include meaningful green amenities. She says the project should not qualify for Scott Road Revitalization incentives because its environmental impact would be high, reducing tree cover and groundwater recharge while increasing flood, drought and wildfire vulnerability. Jones also argues that approving the project could encourage further upzoning, speculation and higher housing prices, and questions whether highrise condos address housing supply. She says Delta should only consider the proposal with major environmental mitigation, including a reduced underground footprint and at least 15 per cent fully permeable open space for large trees and infiltration. She urges similar permeable-land requirements for all multi-family developments.

The SFS specification describes attestation, resiliency, command handling, update packaging, and runtime behavior for firmware servicing. Attestation data should be requested through appropriate interfaces such as SPDM or DPE, and SFS provides measurements to attestation data managers. Some attestation schemes prevent updates to certain AMD-provided firmware, which AMD will not modify.

Update packages must verify required firmware versions before applying and should not apply if any portion cannot complete. Packages are non-persistent across reboots, so customers may apply patches during OS boot, after boot, or during operation. SFS commands require specific 2MB and 4KB memory alignment rules, use a TEE extended command buffer, and are submitted through the ASP mailbox interface.

For customer co-signed packages, software may append a co-signing header, the AMD update package, and an optional co-signing signature. The ASP checks memory protection, verifies customer and AMD signatures, loads and runs the patch, updates patch-level information, and returns status. Version commands report current firmware, patch levels, supported firmware versions, and related security patch levels.

SFS packages are binary objects aligned to AGESA releases and use names such as `fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg`. Packages apply only to specific firmware and system patch-level combinations. Updates run in parallel with x86 and DMA traffic and are designed to minimize performance impact, with few cases requiring OS quiescence.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended June 30, 2018. For the quarter, net sales were $53.3 billion, up from $45.4 billion a year earlier, and net income was $11.5 billion, up from $8.7 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $2.34, compared with $1.67. For the first nine months of fiscal 2018, net sales were $202.7 billion and net income was $45.4 billion.

Apple reported total assets of $349.2 billion as of June 30, 2018, down from $375.3 billion at September 30, 2017. Cash and cash equivalents were $32.0 billion, short-term marketable securities were $39.0 billion, and long-term marketable securities were $172.8 billion. Total liabilities were $234.2 billion, including $97.1 billion of long-term debt.

Quarterly net sales increased across all geographic segments: Americas rose 20% to $24.5 billion, Europe rose 14% to $12.1 billion, Greater China rose 19% to $9.6 billion, Japan rose 7% to $3.9 billion, and Rest of Asia Pacific rose 16% to $3.2 billion. By product, iPhone net sales increased 20% to $29.9 billion, Services rose 31% to $9.5 billion, and Other Products rose 37% to $3.7 billion. iPad and Mac net sales each declined 5%.

Gross margin for the quarter was $20.4 billion, or 38.3% of net sales. Operating expenses were $7.8 billion, including $3.7 billion for research and development and $4.1 billion for selling, general and administrative expenses. Operating income was $12.6 billion.

During the quarter, Apple repurchased $20.0 billion of common stock and paid $3.7 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents. The company completed its prior $210 billion share repurchase program and began a new program authorized for up to $100 billion.

Apple recorded tax-related impacts from the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, including a revised provisional estimate of $900 million. It also began funding escrow related to the European Commission State Aid Decision, with €4.5 billion deposited by June 30, 2018 and an additional €4.5 billion funded afterward. The company disclosed ongoing legal matters involving VirnetX and Qualcomm.

The passage introduces CBCT-to-CT synthetic CT generation for image-guided and adaptive radiotherapy, noting CBCT’s daily imaging advantages but limitations in artifacts and HU consistency, while CT provides better HU calibration and dose calculation. It reviews registration-based, GAN, CNN, hybrid, transformer, and diffusion approaches, highlighting limitations such as anatomical dependence, instability, hallucinations, interpretability issues, and computational cost.

The work proposes EqDiff-CT, a conditional DDPM framework for CBCT-to-CT synthesis using 2D axial slices. It employs a time-conditioned, group-equivariant U-Net denoiser via e2cnn with C4 rotational equivariance, self-attention, CBCT conditioning at each timestep, and a non-adversarial MSE/SSIM objective on predicted noise. Evaluated on the SynthRAD2025 Head & Neck dataset with an 80/20 patient-wise split, the attention-enhanced diffusion model outperformed a baseline diffusion model and CycleGAN across SSIM, PSNR, MSE, and MAE, while preserving structures such as the mandible, airway, and cervical spine.

The speaker says their team must prepare for Dallas at its best, noting Dallas often responds strongly after a first-game loss with more aggression, forechecking and physical play. They emphasize limiting time and space for players like Modano, Hull and Nieuwendyk, treating each game separately, and not dwelling on past series. The team is mostly healthy, with Madden’s injury less serious than feared. The speaker says Dallas played more aggressively, their own team made poor puck decisions, failed to follow the game plan, and played one of its worst recent games while still staying close. They note a missed offside before Hull’s goal but say it was not why they lost. With the series tied 1-1, they say there is no reason to panic and the team must play better in Dallas.
The Weston Public Library will mark the Aug. 21 solar eclipse with free solar viewers, a pinhole projector workshop, and a NASA livestream. Weston is expected to see about 70% coverage.

CDC reports illnesses from mosquito, tick and flea bites have tripled in the U.S. since 2004. In Venice, still water in the canals, wetlands and yards can breed mosquitoes, and West Nile Virus is present in the surrounding area. The virus spreads from infected birds to mosquitoes and then to humans and animals. Most infected people show no symptoms, while some experience illness and fewer than one percent develop severe neuroinvasive disease. Los Angeles County West Vector & Vector-Borne Disease Control District manages local mosquito control. Officials advise using repellents, especially between dusk and dawn, and eliminating standing water that can serve as breeding sites.

The study developed a model to interpret detections of influenza A H5 RNA in wastewater by estimating potential inputs from humans, cow milk, poultry feces, and wildfowl feces. It was motivated by H5N1 outbreaks in birds beginning in 2022 and dairy cattle in 2024, alongside H5 RNA detections in U.S. wastewater starting in March 2024. The authors retrospectively tested 110 wastewater solids samples collected from September 2023 to May 2024 at a California publicly owned treatment works serving 750,000 people with combined stormwater and sanitary sewers. Samples were analyzed for total influenza A, H1, H3, and H5 RNA using droplet digital RT-PCR. The model estimates H5 RNA inputs needed to produce measured wastewater concentrations, accounting for RNA in both wastewater solids and liquids and using plant flow and suspended solids data.

The SteelSeries Arctis GameBuds, rated 9/10 by WIRED, are discounted to $128 on Amazon in Xbox and PlayStation versions. They support Switch, PC, and smartphones, include a USB-C dongle for low-latency 2.4GHz audio, offer Bluetooth, and provide about 10 hours of battery life or 40 hours with the case. The author highlights their portability, comfort, sound isolation, mobile app with game-specific EQ settings, active noise-canceling controls, and physical buttons.

The study develops metal inorganic-organic complex (MIOC) glasses using a ligand-tuning approach.
