Two Zn-based MIOC crystals, ZnCl2HIm2 (MIOC-4) and ZnCl2HbIm2 (MIOC-7), were synthesized by slow evaporation through chloride introduction into ZIF-type systems. MIOC-4 has a monoclinic stacked hydrogen-bonded structure, while MIOC-7 has a triclinic interdigitated structure with additional π-π interactions.

Both crystals form transparent glasses by melt-quenching. MIOC-4 and MIOC-7 have melting points of 440 K and 508 K and glass-transition temperatures of 282 K and 359 K, respectively. In situ XRD showed that melting begins with slippage and distortion of hydrogen-bonded structures, followed by hydrogen-bond breaking and disordering. MIOC-7’s interdigitated structure gives higher thermal stability than MIOC-4.

Mixed-ligand synthesis produced binary MIOC mixed-crystals with reduced melting points and tunable glass-transition temperatures. Increasing HbIm content raised Tg from 282 to 360 K, attributed to increased steric hindrance in the glass network. The lowest melting point was 415 K for ZnCl2HbIm0.498HIm1.502 mixed crystals.

Spectroscopic and diffraction analyses showed that vitrification preserves short-range Zn-N, Zn-Cl, and Zn-C correlations while eliminating medium- and long-range intermolecular Zn-Zn and Cl-Cl correlations. C-H···Cl hydrogen bonds weaken or disappear, while disordered N-H···Cl hydrogen-bond networks dominate the glass structure. NMR and synchrotron XRD confirmed short-range disorder in MIOC-7 glass.

The ligand-tuning strategy was extended to other metal nodes (Co, Cu) and anions (SCN-), yielding additional MIOC crystals and glasses. MIOC-7 glass exhibited enhanced visible photoluminescence under 365 nm excitation, with an internal photoluminescence quantum yield of 3.4%, compared with 1.2% for the crystal. Its excitation-dependent emission was linked to frozen tetrahedral conformations in the hydrogen-bonded glass network, suggesting potential anti-counterfeiting applications.

James Harden became the first NBA player to score 60 points in a triple-double, adding 10 rebounds and 11 assists as the short-handed Houston Rockets beat the Orlando Magic 114-107. Harden broke Calvin Murphy’s 1978 Houston single-game scoring record of 57 points and scored 18 in the fourth quarter, including a late four-point play that brought him to 60. He shot 19 of 30 from the field, made five 3-pointers and hit 17 of 18 free throws while playing a season-high 46:26. The Rockets were without Chris Paul and Trevor Ariza, and Eric Gordon left with lower back stiffness. Mario Hezonja and Marreese Speights led Orlando with 17 points each.

The passage describes a networked exercise system, exemplified by a treadmill, that provides live-streamed and archived instructor-led exercise classes, social interaction, performance tracking, competition, and gamification features. The system includes exercise machines connected to digital hardware, backend servers, recording locations, displays, cameras, microphones, speakers, sensors, software, and communications networks, enabling instructors and users to interact through video, audio, data, chat, and performance metrics.

Example treadmill embodiments include a deck with a continuous belt or track formed with slats, motors for controlling belt speed and deck incline, posts, arms, crossbars, a movable display, sensors, emergency stop features, trays, and user controls. Separate rotary controls may be mounted on opposite arms and configured to control different treadmill functions, such as speed and incline. Rotary controls may include rotatable outer portions, inner input devices, indicators, detents, encoders, printed circuit boards, LEDs, tactile or audible feedback, and sensors for detecting rotation and user input. Alternative substantially linear or capacitive controls are also described.

The system can measure and display exercise machine and user performance metrics, including speed, incline, distance, work, power, heart rate, respiration, hydration, calorie burn, and trends over time. User interfaces displayed on the machine allow users to access live and archived classes, class schedules, featured classes, class libraries, just-run options, performance data, leaderboards, and class-related information. During classes, video content may be shown with overlaid performance metrics, timelines, scorecards, and other interactive information.

The passage outlines how to teach and implement an early offense and press break through precise execution, spacing, timing, footwork, and the Whole-Part-Whole method. Coaches should prepare players before games, teach roles and reads, use progressive breakdown drills, and practice live against strong defense. Objectives include building poise against presses, advancing the ball quickly with controlled passes, attacking double teams and outnumbered situations, flowing into early offense, and anticipating missed shots. Press break work should be part of every practice. Game strategies include playing tough defense, breaking on every possession, scouting defensive tactics, and staying alert to adjustments. Defensive pressure can disrupt fast breaks and early offense while creating steals and easy baskets.

The passage specifies Socket 940 mechanical, material, marking, contact, solder, actuation, durability, inspection, and electrical requirements. The socket cover supports the 940-pin ceramic µPGA package without pin damage, with seating-plane flatness under 0.25 mm and height of 4.00 ± 0.20 mm from the PCB mounting plane. Base and cover are LCP rated UL 94 V-0; base is black and cover is natural or ivory. Cover thickness must not exceed 1.17 mm, and flatness must remain under 0.25 mm after reflow and testing. A removable overlay supports vacuum pick-and-place and must not outgas or leave residue.

Required markings include “SOCKET 940,” lock/unlock indicators, an A01 orientation triangle, supplier UL symbol, and lot traceability marking. Contacts use high-strength copper alloy, nickel plating of at least 1.27 µm, and gold plating of at least 0.76 µm on mating areas. SMT solder balls are 63/37 ± 5% tin-lead, 0.76 mm diameter, used with 0.64 mm PCB pads, and must meet 0.20 mm coplanarity.

A stainless steel actuation lever provides toolless operation. Open-position insertion/extraction forces must not exceed 2 kgf; closed-position extraction force must be at least 0.013 kgf per pin. Lever actuation force must be under 3.6 kgf, and pin displacement under 1.0 mm. The socket must maintain integrity after 50 cycles.

Visual requirements prohibit missing, malformed, damaged, or misaligned solder balls; damaged contacts; missing gold; cracks; flashing; cover/base gaps; damaged latches; or lever defects. Electrical requirements include 1.5 A per contact with under 30°C rise, LLCR not exceeding 25 mΩ initially or finally, inductance under specified limits, capacitance under 1 pF, differential impedance of 100 Ω ± 10%, propagation delay skew under 10 ps plus measurement error, dielectric withstand of at least 650 Vac, and insulation resistance of at least 1000 MΩ.

The speaker says the goalie showed mental strength after losing a game, responding with an outstanding performance and remaining calm after mistakes. He compares Bergeron and Ryan O’Reilly as strong faceoff players who work hard and play well on both sides of the puck. He sees similarities between the teams, including strong defense, forechecking, physical play, hard work, and mobile defensemen. He emphasizes playing physically but cleanly, staying disciplined after whistles, and focusing on getting the puck rather than just hitting. He says the team identity is built on a team-first approach where no player is bigger than the team. He also notes that the schedule and travel require using two good goalies.

Kentucky high school valedictorian Christian Bales and student council president Katherine Frantz delivered their graduation speeches by bullhorn outside Holy Cross High School’s commencement after the Diocese of Covington barred them from speaking. The diocese said the speeches were submitted late and, upon review, were political and inconsistent with Catholic teaching. Bales, who is gay, said he thought officials may have feared he would go off script, though he did not mention his sexual orientation in the speech. His remarks praised youth activism, including students advocating for gun-law changes after the Marjory Stoneman Douglas shooting, and urged young people to speak out despite opposition. Bales and his mother said the decision to silence him amplified his message, which has since received widespread media attention.

The Justice Department’s hiring of assistant US attorneys has slowed sharply under the Trump administration, with LinkedIn data showing about 42 new hires from January through August, less than half the number in the same periods of the prior four years. Current and former prosecutors cite budget pressures, hiring freezes, higher pay costs, morale problems, political turmoil, and departures as contributing factors. Some offices are now trying to hire more prosecutors, and the DOJ does not appear to be lowering standards, with many new hires coming from prominent firms, prosecutors’ offices, or top law schools. Former DOJ officials are divided: some still encourage young lawyers to seek federal prosecutor jobs, while others warn of possible political interference and ethical risks.

The article examines whether the ADX indicator can support profitable trading strategies through historical backtests. Developed by Welles Wilder in 1978, ADX measures trend strength using DI+, DI-, and ADX components, with high readings indicating trending markets and low readings indicating non-trending markets. The author notes ADX is lagging and often stays below high levels on longer time frames.

Backtests show ADX performs reasonably but not strongly as a standalone tool. A DI+ and DI- crossover strategy on the S&P 500 produced a 5.4% CAGR, 0.42% average trade, 55% market exposure, and 1.71 profit factor. An ADX breakout strategy had a small drawdown of 13.76% but only a 3.03% CAGR versus 9.9% for buy and hold.

The article finds ADX more useful when combined with another indicator. Adding an ADX filter reduced market exposure, improved profit factor, and worked better on Nasdaq than on the S&P 500 in the tested example. The conclusion is that ADX is versatile, somewhat useful alone, and more effective as a supplement to other indicators, with proper backtesting recommended.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPUs expand concurrent processing by allowing RT Core work to run alongside graphics or compute workloads and enabling two compute workloads simultaneously within an SM. Dedicated RT Cores reduce shader load, while second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection performance over Turing and add hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur through an Interpolate Triangle Position unit. This enables more accurate motion blur for moving and deforming geometry, with support through OptiX 7 and applications such as Blender, V-Ray, Arnold, and Redshift.

Ampere improves RTX performance through 2x FP32 processing, L1 cache improvements, second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, GDDR6X memory, and new concurrency features. In the Wolfenstein: Youngblood example, RTX 3080 renders a frame in 6.7 ms compared with longer frame times on Turing configurations.

GA10x third-generation Tensor Cores support additional data types including TF32 and BF16, improve efficiency, and add Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity for up to 2x throughput on supported matrix operations. These Tensor Cores accelerate AI-based graphics features such as DLSS, denoising, RTX Voice, RTX Broadcast effects, AI Super Rez, and AI Slow-Mo. DLSS on Ampere supports a 9x Super Resolution scaling factor, enabling 8K gaming at 60 fps in many titles on GeForce RTX 3090.

GA10x GPUs introduce GDDR6X memory developed with Micron, using PAM4 signaling and MTA encoding to increase bandwidth. GDDR6X supports up to 19.5 Gbps data rates and up to 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth, improving performance for workloads such as ray tracing, AI inference, and 8K rendering. Error Detection and Replay helps detect and retry GDDR6X transmission errors during overclocking.

NVIDIA RTX IO works with Microsoft DirectStorage to enable GPU-based loading and lossless decompression of assets, reducing CPU workload and improving I/O performance compared with hard drives and traditional storage APIs. It is intended to improve load times, streaming, frame rates, and handling of large game and creative datasets.

GA10x also includes updated display, decode, and encode capabilities. It supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, DSC 1.2a, HDCP 2.3, 8K displays, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-generation NVENC for hardware video encoding.

The NVIDIA A40 is a GA10x-based data center GPU for visual computing, offering higher FP32, ray tracing, AI, PCIe Gen4, and memory capabilities than prior Turing-based products. The RTX A6000 is a professional workstation GPU with 48GB of GDDR6 memory, NVLink support for 96GB combined memory, hardware-accelerated ray tracing, motion blur, and AI denoising. The passage also describes GeForce RTX 3090 and RTX 3070 specifications and states that GA10x provides up to 2x improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI for GeForce RTX 30-Series GPUs.

The speaker described supporting a developing play in overtime, capitalizing on a delayed penalty, and setting up a teammate for the deciding goal. They emphasized competing, support, and attention to detail, especially on special teams. They said penalties hurt momentum and give the opponent’s skilled power play too many chances, so staying out of the box is important. They also expressed excitement about returning home, praised the town’s support, and said the team has confidence in its depth despite injuries.

A study by Stanford, Harvard and the Census Bureau found that in 99 percent of U.S. neighborhoods, black boys earn less as adults than white boys from similar socioeconomic backgrounds. Using de-identified data from 20 million children and parents, researchers found black and Native American children have the lowest upward mobility, while white and Asian children have the highest. The gap persists even among wealthy families. Children raised in the bottom fifth of income have a 7 percent overall chance of reaching the top fifth, compared with 11 percent for white children and 2.5 percent for black children. The black-white income gap is driven largely by differences between men; black women slightly out-earn white women when parental income is controlled. Neighborhoods still affect outcomes, but affluent areas often show larger black-white gaps. Some areas, including suburbs near Washington, D.C., showed greater parity, associated with lower racial bias and higher percentages of present black fathers in the community.

Future Electronics and NXP are hosting a free seminar on the i.MX RT Series Crossover Processor in San Sebastian, Spain, on July 4, 2018. The workshop will introduce the processor’s Arm Cortex-M core, real-time functionality, MCU usability and hands-on exercises. The passage also describes Future Electronics’ global distribution business, engineering services, and company background.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K reporting that on October 7, 2016, it entered into a Credit Agreement with Wells Fargo Bank, Goldman Sachs Bank USA, Morgan Stanley MUFG Loan Partners, LLC, and other lenders. The agreement allows NVIDIA to borrow, repay, and re-borrow up to $575 million for working capital and general corporate purposes through October 7, 2021, when outstanding obligations become due. It also permits up to $425 million in additional revolving loan commitments and/or letter of credit commitments, subject to conditions. Loans bear interest based on either the Adjusted LIBO Rate or Alternate Base Rate plus an applicable rate. The agreement includes customary representations, covenants, default provisions, and restrictions, and the obligations are unsecured senior obligations ranking equally with NVIDIA’s existing and future unsecured unsubordinated debt. The filing includes the Credit Agreement as Exhibit 1.1 and was signed by CFO Colette M. Kress on October 13, 2016.

The speaker thanks Berliners and celebrates the reunification of Berlin and Germany, honoring the courage shown during the city’s division, including resistance in 1953, family separation, and the peaceful movement that helped bring down the Wall. He pledges that a new American Embassy will stand in Berlin and calls for a new “civil courage” to build a democratic, prosperous, and peaceful Europe based on freedom, open markets, cooperation, and vigilance against division by race, ethnicity, or religion. He urges young people to believe in peace and their future, cites democratic and economic progress and NATO’s Partnership for Peace, and affirms that America will stand with Berlin and Europe. He concludes by describing the Brandenburg Gate as a gateway to a united Europe and declaring Berlin free.

President Donald Trump announced a deal with Pfizer to lower U.S. drug prices, including offering Medicaid patients existing drugs at the lowest prices available in other developed nations and providing “most-favored-nation” pricing for new drugs to Medicare, Medicaid and commercial payers. Pfizer will receive a three-year exemption from pharmaceutical-specific tariffs if it invests further in U.S. manufacturing, with plans for $70 billion in domestic manufacturing and research. The company will offer some drugs through TrumpRx.gov at discounts averaging 50% and up to 85%. Trump said similar deals are being pursued with other drugmakers, including Eli Lilly, and warned tariffs could apply if agreements are not reached.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K reporting that on January 18, 2017, its Board appointed Tim Teter as senior vice president, general counsel and secretary, contingent on his expected employment start date of January 23, 2017. Teter, 50, was most recently a Cooley LLP partner focused on patent and technology litigation and previously worked as an engineer at Lockheed Missiles and Space Company. He will assume legal department leadership from David M. Shannon, who previously announced his planned retirement but will continue leading human resources and assist on legal matters until retirement. Teter’s offer includes at-will employment, an $850,000 annual salary, target annual incentive compensation of $250,000 beginning fiscal 2018, a $450,000 anniversary bonus subject to conditions, RSUs valued at $5.8 million vesting over about four years, eligibility for NVIDIA’s employee stock purchase plan and benefits programs, and an expected standard indemnity agreement.

The author’s dividend growth portfolio gained 15% in 2016, outperforming the S&P 500’s 11.66% total return and beating it every month. The portfolio’s goal is 6–8% annual returns, and its 2015 return was 5.39%.

Of the 27 positions held all year, five declined: Gilead Sciences, CVS Health, Starbucks, Coca-Cola, and Target. Gilead was the worst performer, down nearly 30%, followed by CVS Health, down almost 20%. The top performers were Chevron, JPMorgan, AT&T, 3M, and Aflac.

The author made one sale, trading Baxalta for Visa, and added several companies during the year, including Visa, Cisco, Pepsi, Cummins, Honeywell, Qualcomm, Disney, and V.F. Corp. Purchases averaged more than a 6% return, with Boeing, Cisco, and Microsoft performing especially well, while CVS Health purchases declined.

By year-end, the portfolio held 35 companies across IRAs and share builder accounts. The author plans to continue buying dividend-paying companies believed to be below fair value.

The paper studies satisficing paths in game theory and multi-agent reinforcement learning from a topological perspective. It introduces the grouped satisficing path, extending the classical “win-stay, lose-shift” principle from individual players to groups. The main question is when, from any initial joint strategy, there exists a finite-length grouped satisficing path leading to an equilibrium.

The paper establishes topological properties of local minima of the best response group count and proves a reduction principle: under convex compact strategy sets and continuous partially analytic payoff functions, a local minimum occurs exactly when groups already achieving best responses continue to do so after admissible updates. The main existence theorem states that if, additionally, every sub-game has an equilibrium, then every initial joint strategy has a finite-length grouped satisficing path to an equilibrium.

The results imply the existence of finite-length satisficing paths in continuous games satisfying quasi-convexity conditions, N-player mixed games with finite strategy sets, stationary finite-state stochastic games, and k-step finite-state stochastic games. The paper discusses connections to convergence results and stochastic update methods, and identifies open problems concerning necessary conditions, approximate equilibria, and restrictions on non-best-responding players.

Virtual education can provide flexibility, individualized learning, credit recovery, accommodations for some students with special needs, increased parental engagement, and preparation for post-secondary virtual collaboration. Challenges include internet access, motivation, delayed feedback, isolation, difficulty providing accommodations, technology needs, parental burden, student engagement, and monitoring learning.

The study surveyed Indiana public school superintendents and virtual program administrators and conducted follow-up interviews to examine virtual education during the COVID-19 pandemic. Responses came from 96 superintendents and 36 program administrators; interviews included six superintendents and five program administrators. Most respondents were from rural districts and had served in their roles for five or fewer years.

Findings showed that COVID-19 concerns were the leading factor in implementing or maintaining virtual programs, followed by credit recovery. The most cited benefits were maintaining enrollment during the pandemic, credit recovery, and learner convenience and flexibility. The most cited challenges were student engagement, ensuring curriculum and instructional quality, and staffing virtual classes.

Interview themes centered on the pandemic’s impact on districts, teachers, and students. Districts faced enrollment and financial concerns and accelerated technology plans. Teachers experienced stress, limited professional development, and rapid adjustments to virtual platforms, though some improved technology skills. Students faced social-emotional concerns, engagement and attendance problems, time-management difficulties, and varying levels of parental support.

The study concludes that COVID-19 spurred growth in Indiana virtual education and prompted school leaders to respond, while many benefits and challenges reflected issues historically associated with virtual programs. It recommends further research on post-pandemic program changes, effective virtual program characteristics, student needs, and successful virtual educators.

The lecture covers theoretical models of protein folding and interlocked chains. For protein folding, it focuses on the HP model, which represents amino acids as hydrophobic or hydrophilic nodes folded on a lattice, with scores based on adjacent hydrophobic pairs. Finding an optimal HP folding is NP-hard in both 3D and 2D lattices. A known 1/3-approximation algorithm uses parity on the square grid to align hydrophobic nodes and form many H-H bonds. The lecture also discusses unique optimal foldings, known constructions for certain open and closed chain lengths, and open questions about extending uniqueness to other grids and designing HP sequences that fold into target shapes.

The second part discusses interlocked 3D chains. It introduces Lubiw’s problem: how many cuts are needed to unlock a 3D chain, with known bounds between about n/4 and n/2. The lecture surveys when short open and closed chains can separate or interlock, including results that multiple hairpins always separate, two 3-chains separate, but certain 3- and 4-chain combinations can interlock. It presents geometric scaling arguments for separability and topological arguments for interlocking. The lecture concludes by noting that interlocked chains are used in PSPACE-completeness proofs for motion between 3D chain configurations, while the complexity of unfolding a chain from a given configuration remains open.

E-minis are electronically traded futures contracts that are smaller than standard futures contracts, first created by the CME and traded mainly on Globex. They cover indexes, commodities, currencies, and some stocks, with the S&P 500 E-mini remaining highly active. E-minis allow speculation, hedging, leverage, and lower capital access, but can be volatile and risky.

Trading requires a futures broker, understanding of margin, order types, expiration, settlement, and risk management. For the S&P 500 E-mini, the passage gives an example value of $200,000 at 4,000 index points and a CME maintenance margin of $10,000, recommending about $13,000–$15,000 or more to trade safely. Costs vary by broker, commonly including commissions, exchange, broker, and clearing fees.

The passage presents a backtested S&P 500 E-mini strategy from 2000–2021 with 163 trades, 0.89% average gain, 79% win rate, and profit factor of 2; in 2022, it made 13 trades averaging 0.18%. It stresses that traders need a written, backtested plan, discipline, and records. Scalping is described as highly competitive and generally discouraged due to commissions, slippage, and better-capitalized participants.

WIRED lists Amazon Prime Big Deal Days deals under $100, available to Prime members October 7 and 8. Tested picks include streaming devices, earbuds, speakers, wireless chargers, desks, gaming accessories, security cameras, smart pet products, kitchen appliances, cleaning tools, bedding, personal care items, toys, and games, with discounts on brands such as Roku, Ninja, Belkin, Anker, Eufy, Petlibro, Instant Pot, Bissell, Philips, Razer, and Melissa & Doug.

The passage examines competencies needed for leaders of digital education transformation through bibliometric analysis, focusing on digital transformation, digital disruption, Education 4.0, and Thailand’s Digital Thailand 4.0 strategy. It argues that educators must adapt to irreversible digital changes accelerated by COVID-19, including online learning, hybrid learning, remote supervision, data-driven decision-making, and new educational technologies.

The research identifies five key areas for digital transformation leadership in education: digital literacy or competency, digital readiness, digital culture, digital mindset, and digital leadership. Digital literacy includes access to and use of computers, the internet, cybersecurity, digital media, and online collaboration. Digital readiness involves preparing individuals and organizations with strategies, infrastructure, new processes, and acceptance of change. Digital culture requires organizations to integrate technology, support collaboration, ensure data security, use digital ecosystems, and adopt innovation. Digital mindset involves changing traditional thinking, embracing innovation, and accepting that older educational methods may no longer fit modern contexts. Digital leadership requires vision, communication, collaboration, technological competence, adaptability, professional growth, and the ability to guide institutions through transformation.

The passage emphasizes that digital transformation in education affects teaching methods, student engagement, assessment, infrastructure, organizational culture, and leadership roles. It concludes that educators should become digitally ready, build digital teams, reshape work cultures, and guide institutions, administrators, teachers, and students into the digital era, while maintaining that technology cannot replace good teachers. The bibliometric analysis provides directions for further research on preparing future leaders of digital education transformation.

TI lists support resources through TI E2E forums, trademark ownership, and an ESD caution stating improper handling can damage integrated circuits. The April 2025 revision for MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 updates features, device variants, comparison tables, electrical specifications, thermal data, supply current, oscillator, ADC, temperature sensor, VREF, comparator, SPI, operating modes, DMA, flash, SRAM, security, UART, LFSS, and timer information. Mechanical, packaging, and orderable information is provided as current but subject to change. Notes cover package dimensions, thermal pad soldering, vias, stencil recommendations, part status, preproduction material limitations, RoHS values, lead finish, MSL rating, part markings, and qualified automotive versions. TI states technical and design resources are provided “AS IS,” may change without notice, and are intended for skilled developers responsible for product selection, design, validation, testing, and compliance.

The study examines Songyang Academy within Songshan culture and its relationship to general education. It uses documentary research, field studies, interviews, observations, local chronicles, historical texts, media materials, and recorded field data to analyze the academy’s historical development, educational philosophy, and relevance to modern general education.

Songyang Academy, with a history of more than 1,500 years, developed from Songyang Temple and became one of China’s four major academies. It rose during the Song Dynasty, attracting scholars such as Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, and Sima Guang, but declined during periods of war and political change in later dynasties. It revived in the early Qing Dynasty before losing prominence after the abolition of the imperial examination system.

The academy’s educational philosophy centered on moral cultivation, personality development, practical learning, and the unity of knowledge and action. It emphasized Confucian teachings, non-discriminatory access to education, autonomous learning, questioning, debate, and teacher guidance. Its management structure was simple and hierarchical, led by respected scholars.

The passage argues that Songyang Academy’s focus on morality, broad learning, independent thinking, practice, and comprehensive human development aligns closely with modern general education. It concludes that adapting aspects of the academy model can support modern education reform and contribute to cultivating well-rounded talents.

Kobe University researchers found that germinating orchids depend on wood-decaying fungi for carbon from rotting logs. In field tests with four orchid species, germination occurred only near decaying logs, and seedlings were almost exclusively associated with these fungi. The fungal partnerships closely matched those found in adult orchids with coral-shaped rhizomes. Researchers suggest orchids without these structures may shift to other fungi as they grow and deadwood carbon declines. The findings reveal a carbon pathway from deadwood to green plants, clarify orchid seedling ecology, and may help explain the evolution of fully fungus-dependent orchids. The study also emphasizes the importance of protecting deadwood and its fungi for orchid conservation.

Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School reopened for classes for the first time since 17 students and teachers were killed, with heavy police security, grief counselors, therapy animals, volunteers and memorials on campus. Some students said the armed presence was unsettling, while others described nervousness, trauma and determination to return. Students continued activism against gun violence, including preparations for a national school walkout.

Dick’s Sporting Goods announced it would stop selling assault-style rifles and guns to anyone under 21. In Florida, victims’ relatives urged lawmakers to act on school-safety and gun legislation. A House committee advanced a bill to raise the age for buying long guns to 21 and allow trained, deputized teachers to carry concealed weapons if districts permit it. Broward’s superintendent and student activist David Hogg opposed arming teachers. Gov. Rick Scott supported passing a bill but had not said whether he would veto one including that provision.

The study examined elementary teachers’ attitudes toward inclusive education for learners with special education needs in Liloan District, Cebu Province, Philippines. It was grounded in the Theory of Planned Behavior, Ecological Systems Theory, Social Learning Theory, and Philippine inclusive education laws and policies. Using a descriptive correlational design, the study surveyed 30 purposively selected inclusion teachers from four public schools through a demographic questionnaire and the Modified STATIC instrument.

Most respondents were female, married, aged 34–43, and had graduate-level units. Most had only 1–5 years of experience handling learners with special education needs and had attended only 1–2 inclusive education trainings. Many teachers had limited numbers of learners with special needs in their classes, with learning disabilities being the most common learner difficulty.

Teachers generally showed positive attitudes toward inclusive education, especially regarding its social benefits, philosophical principles, professional importance, and the need for training and support. They strongly valued equal access, differentiated instruction, inclusive culture, professional development, and collaboration with special education teachers. However, they expressed concerns about academic impacts, large class sizes, limited resources, insufficient assistive technology, scheduling constraints, access to specialists, and logistical readiness.

Statistical tests found no significant relationship between teacher demographic profiles and attitudes toward inclusive education. The study concluded that teachers shared generally consistent and positive views regardless of background, but effective implementation requires sustained professional development, stronger support systems, adequate resources, smaller class sizes, assistive technologies, qualified personnel, and school-based intervention planning. The study proposed an evidence-based Teacher Inclusion Support Plan and emphasized continuous monitoring and refinement to support inclusive education practices.

The speaker says an honor came after initial disappointment at not being nominated for the rookie trophy. They focused on winning, preparation, and readiness, explaining they stayed in Europe an extra year to become mentally and physically prepared before joining the Flyers. They credit hard work, motivation from veteran teammates, and growing confidence after a slow start for their progress.

The author refers to his 21-year-old college senior daughter as “The Girl” to protect her privacy. Though he believes she would excel as a literature professor, he discourages that path because full-time humanities faculty jobs are extremely scarce and worsening amid cost pressures, demographics, AI and politics. He notes adjacent fields like journalism, publishing and web media are also struggling. His daughter is interested in librarianship, which he supports because information science skills may be more flexible. He asks readers for advice for talented young people suited to academia but facing limited opportunities.

A paper examining a hypothetical 40 percent reduction in NIH funding found that more than half of 21st-century FDA-approved drugs were linked to research that might not have been funded under a smaller NIH budget. Researchers analyzed NIH grants from 1980 to 2007 and drugs with new active ingredients approved from 2000 to 2023. Of 557 approved drugs, 40 had patents directly acknowledging NIH extramural funding, and 14 cited at-risk grants. Fifty-nine percent had patents citing NIH-supported research publications, with 65 drugs classified as highly linked to such research. Drugs connected to at-risk research were not found to be less important: 60 percent received FDA priority review versus 41 percent of unlinked drugs, and they had higher average market value. The paper argues that past large NIH cuts would likely have reduced medical innovation, while noting its estimates are conservative because they focus only on direct links to specific grants.

The Appellate Division affirmed dismissal of Brian O’Loughlin’s defamation action against the Patrolmen’s Benevolent Association and its president, Phil Caruso. Caruso had published a letter criticizing O’Loughlin and eight other officers for requesting refunds of a $20 contribution toward a police memorial, saying they had “no feelings” and were “a disgrace.” The court held that, although harsh and insensitive, the statements were vague, subjective expressions of opinion rather than actionable statements of fact or mixed opinion. An average reader of the PBA magazine would understand them as Caruso’s personal view about the officers’ refusal to support the memorial contribution.

MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 MCUs include up to 128KB SRAM split into two 64KB banks, with Bank 0 ECC or parity protected and available in run, sleep, stop, and standby modes, while Bank 1 can be selectively enabled and lacks ECC or parity. SRAM supports write-execute partitioning for read-write and read-execute regions.

The devices provide GPIO through Ports A, B, and C with up to 93 GPIO pins, IOMUX for pin configuration and digital muxing, two 12-bit ADC modules, a temperature sensor connected to an ADC channel, configurable internal or external VREF, comparators, and a 12-bit buffered DAC. Device analog connections note that DAC_OUT connects to PA15 and external circuitry on PA15 should be avoided when using DAC_OUT.

Security and acceleration features include AES-128/256 support, firewalls, secure key storage for up to four AES keys, CRC-16 and CRC-32, a TRNG generating 32-bit random numbers, an AESADV accelerator, a keystore controller, and a math accelerator. Communication peripherals include UART, I2C with SMBus support, SPI up to 32Mbits/s under specified conditions, and CAN-FD compliant with ISO 11898-1:2015 up to 5Mbit/s.

The Low-Frequency Sub System includes RTC_B and an independent watchdog timer. RTC_B provides calendar, alarm, periodic wakeup, calibration, and clock output features, while IWDT_B can generate a POR reset if not serviced. The WWDT supports reset or interrupt generation and interval timer mode. TIMGx and TIMAx timer peripherals provide counting, prescaling, synchronization, triggers, PWM, fault handling, and DMA or interrupt support.

The passage also describes SWD debug access, a UART or I2C boot strap loader protected by a 256-bit password, factory constants for device identification and trim data, typical application layout recommendations for decoupling, NRST, SYSOSC FCL, VCORE, and ODIO pullups, development tools and documentation resources, trademarks, ESD cautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

Vertical farming grows crops in controlled, layered environments using methods such as hydroponics and aeroponics. Market growth is driven by food demand, population growth, reduced reliance on water and soil, better food quality, new technologies, pesticide-free production, and artificial lighting. High urban setup costs, energy use, and focus on high-value crops hinder growth. The global market is expected to reach about USD 6 billion by 2022 at a 21% CAGR. North America leads the market, while Asia-Pacific is expected to grow rapidly due to urbanization, limited fertile land, and investment.

Global population growth is increasing pressure to boost cereal production, driving pesticide use in grain and cereal crops, especially herbicides. Agricultural advances include crop protection, irrigation, soil management, farming techniques, GM technology, fungicides, and pesticides. Crop rotation helps maintain soil nutrients, improve fertility and yield, reduce erosion, and mitigate pest attacks, while excessive crop protection chemicals can harm the environment, human health, and soil productivity. The grain and cereal crop protection market includes insecticides, herbicides, and fungicides, with herbicides dominant due to low cost, R&D investment, and new active ingredients. North America leads the market, followed by Asia Pacific and Europe, with Asia Pacific expected to expand rapidly.

Kayleigh Gray, whose daughter Emilia was born prematurely at 27 weeks and treated at Royal Preston Hospital’s Neo Natal Unit, donated 25 pairs of acrylic turtle doves with support from her employer, Sign Build. Designed by Kayleigh, the paired doves are for parents and babies to keep one each during a baby’s hospital stay.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2022. The company reported total assets of $74.43 billion, total liabilities of $33.30 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $39.85 billion. Cash and cash equivalents were $19.53 billion, up from $17.58 billion at December 31, 2021.

For the three months ended September 30, 2022, Tesla reported revenue of $21.45 billion, gross profit of $5.38 billion, income from operations of $3.69 billion, and net income attributable to common stockholders of $3.29 billion. For the nine months ended September 30, 2022, revenue was $57.14 billion and net income attributable to common stockholders was $8.87 billion. Net cash provided by operating activities for the nine-month period was $11.45 billion.

Tesla operates in two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. The company noted continuing impacts from COVID-19, including logistics and supply chain challenges, semiconductor supply shortfalls, inflationary pressures, and increased raw material, shipping, transportation, and labor costs.

In August 2022, Tesla completed a three-for-one stock split in the form of a stock dividend and increased authorized common shares by 4.0 billion. As of October 18, 2022, 3,157,752,449 common shares were outstanding.

The filing also discusses digital assets, debt, stock-based compensation including the 2018 CEO Performance Award, operating lease arrangements in New York and Shanghai, and ongoing legal proceedings related to the SolarCity acquisition, the 2018 CEO Performance Award, and director compensation.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K on August 15, 2019, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the quarter ended July 28, 2019. The filing includes Exhibit 99.1, the press release titled “NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Second Quarter Fiscal 2020,” and Exhibit 99.2, CFO commentary by Colette M. Kress. The materials are furnished, not filed, under securities law provisions.

The speaker emphasizes maintaining the same focused mentality throughout the series and concentrating only on taking the final step in the next game. He praises teammates for their contributions on and off the ice, including an old-school player whose value is now being recognized, Marian’s leadership and motivation after past losses, and depth players who have stepped into pressure situations. He says the team expects opponents to respond and will continue pressuring their top players. Reflecting on the Stanley Cup as a lifelong dream, he describes the playoffs as an emotional ride requiring discipline and energy management. He credits the locker room’s shared awareness, leadership, and contributions throughout the lineup, says winning matters more than location, and notes how fortunate he and another young player have been to reach this point so early in their careers.

Only 18% of American workers are very confident they are on track for a secure retirement. The passage recommends three steps: estimate projected retirement income based on current savings and Social Security rather than relying on saving 10%; monitor investment fees, which can significantly reduce retirement balances; and maintain an appropriate asset allocation based on age and risk tolerance. It says low fees, adequate savings, and suitable investment risk can help build a substantial retirement nest egg.

A shorthanded goal was described as decisive, with a strong second effort. The speaker said the team expected to need road wins as the lower seed and had to kill penalties. They noted both teams had stretches of not being sharp, praised key saves, said four lines were needed after five days off, and emphasized the team must improve its first period.

An analysis by Notre Dame law professor Derek Muller found that 92.45% of 2023-2024 campaign contributions from lawyers and staff at top BigLaw and large plaintiffs-side firms went to Democrats, up from a 6-1 Democratic-to-Republican ratio in 2017-2020. The group gave about $52 million to Democratic-affiliated groups and $4 million to Republican-affiliated groups. Among top-grossing firms, Cleary Gottlieb had the highest Democratic share at 99.7%, while Nelson Mullins had the lowest at 66.4%.

WiseGuyReports published a report on the US data center UPS market, forecasting a 4.01% CAGR during 2016-2020. UPS systems provide temporary power during outages, protect infrastructure from sags and surges, and include rectifiers, inverters, and batteries or flywheels. The report covers market prospects for 2015-2020, segmented by centralized, zone/floor-level, and rackmount UPS systems, and by topology including standby, line-interactive, and double-conversion online UPS. Key vendors include ABB, Eaton, Emerson Network Power, GE Industrial Solutions, Schneider Electric, and Tripp Lite. Other vendors include Active Power, Controlled Power Company, Gamatronic, IntelliPower, Power Innovations International, and Toshiba. The report identifies increased data center power outages as a market driver, UPS battery failure as a challenge, and advances in data center infrastructure management as a trend.

New York’s Board of Regents voted unanimously to let special-education students earn local high-school diplomas through occupational assessments instead of minimum English and math Regents exam scores. Adopted on an emergency basis, the plan may apply to students graduating as early as January. Students must meet CDOS requirements and be deemed proficient by district superintendents, with temporary flexibility for 2017-18 and 2018-19 graduates. Parents welcomed the change, arguing the CDOS certificate alone is not recognized like a diploma. Critics warned the change could revive separate academic tracks and objected to the measure’s rapid approval with little notice.

E-mini Russell 2000 Index futures are CME-traded derivative contracts based on the Russell 2000 Index, a market-cap-weighted index of 2,000 small-cap U.S. companies. The E-mini contract equals $50 times the index value and trades on CME Globex from Sunday to Friday, generally 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET, with quarterly contracts in March, June, September, and December. Contracts are cash settled, with trading ending at 9:30 a.m. ET on the third Friday of the contract month.

A trading strategy for these futures may use technical and fundamental analysis, entry and exit rules, position sizing, and risk management for speculation, hedging, arbitrage, or spread trading. The passage gives a Russell 2000 rebalance strategy tied to the fourth Friday of June, reporting a 1.34% average unleveraged gain per trade and a 76% win rate. Seasonality is described as stronger in spring, with August and December also relatively better months.

The passage lists contract details including ticker RTY, tick sizes of $5.00 for outright Globex trading and $2.50 for BTIC, TACO, and calendar spreads, and minimum price fluctuations of 0.10 and 0.05 index points respectively. It states the all-time high was 2460.8 in November 2021. Key risks include leveraged losses from adverse price movement. Factors affecting prices include component stock movements, interest rates, economic news, and the U.S. dollar.

Turkey secured a €974 million loan from international lenders for a central Anatolia highway project aimed at improving regional connectivity, trade access, logistics, and economic development. The financing includes sustainability standards and reflects confidence in Turkey’s infrastructure plans, though terrain, land acquisition issues, borrowing costs, and lira volatility may pose challenges.

Jawed Zia, former Novartis India managing director, resigned 15 days after taking charge and may move to Abbott India, sources told ET. Novartis has not named a replacement. Novartis and Abbott compete in areas including cardiovascular and diabetes, and both face investigation over alleged Galvus price collusion.

The passage describes the emergence of SARS-CoV-2 and COVID-19, noting the lack of approved coronavirus therapies. The DAWN protocol investigates potential treatments, including convalescent plasma, which may help clear infection but has uncertain efficacy and safety risks, requiring randomized controlled study in hospitalized adult SARS-CoV-2 patients.

Riverwood Nursing Center, d/b/a Glenwood Nursing Center, appealed AHCA’s dismissal of its administrative hearing request as untimely. AHCA had filed an administrative complaint seeking license revocation and penalties, with a 21-day deadline for Glenwood to request a hearing by June 14, 2010. Glenwood filed on June 15 after AHCA counsel allegedly agreed to accept the late filing.

The court held equitable tolling did not apply because Glenwood knew the deadline and did not allege it was misled before the deadline, prevented from filing, or timely filed in the wrong forum. The court also rejected Glenwood’s claim that its April 16, 2010 letter to CMS challenging federal deficiencies and mentioning “state tags” served as an earlier AHCA hearing request. The letter was addressed to CMS, not AHCA, and was not filed with AHCA’s agency clerk as required. The court affirmed AHCA’s dismissal with prejudice, license revocation, and $25,000 fine.

The passage presents 10 backtested swing trading strategies, including S&P 500 reversal and overnight strategies, Nasdaq Monday/Tuesday trades, rotation strategies using SPY, TLT and GLD, XLP mean reversion, MACD-Histogram, turn-of-the-month trading, and 200-day/12-month moving average trend-following. It defines swing trading as holding positions longer than day trades but generally not more than a few months. The author argues that backtesting, mechanical trading, diversification, small position sizing, and independent verification are important because swing trading is difficult and risky. The passage states that buy-and-hold investing should remain a savings cornerstone, while systematic swing trading may improve risk-adjusted returns. It says most swing traders are unsuccessful, realistic annual returns are 5% to 20%, and successful swing traders typically quantify and test their strategies.

Mattermost is an open source, self-hosted instant messaging platform written in Golang and React, using MySQL or PostgreSQL and offering features such as file sharing, messaging, emojis, and video calls. The tutorial explains how to deploy Mattermost on CentOS 7 with MariaDB/MySQL, create a database and system user, download and install Mattermost, configure its database settings, test the server, create a systemd service, and enable it at boot. It also shows how to configure Nginx as an SSL reverse proxy, reload Nginx, create the first administrator account and team, set the site URL, configure email notifications, and restart Mattermost.

The disclosure describes wood-type golf club heads, particularly drivers, with raised sole portions that increase sole curvature, stiffen the structure, reduce mass, alter acoustics, and create discretionary mass. Raised sole regions may be bounded by cantilevered ledges, sit pads, channels, and weight tracks, and may include thinner areas, ribs, grooves, or composite sole inserts. Crown inserts and sole inserts may be made from lighter materials than the body to reduce mass and allow mass redistribution.

Several embodiments include bi-level soles, large raised sole areas, toe-side and heel-side raised sole portions, front channels, rear or front-to-rear weight tracks, and adjustable sliding or threaded weights. These features are described as enabling adjustment of center of gravity, moment of inertia, launch, spin, forgiveness, acoustics, appearance, durability, and customizability.

The disclosure also provides dimensional ranges, curvature comparisons, volume and mass ranges, CG and MOI measurement definitions, exemplary performance tables, forgiveness ratios, and manufacturing methods. Bodies may be made from titanium, aluminum, steel, alloys, or other materials, while inserts may use composite or polymeric materials including carbon fiber and thermoplastic or thermoset matrices.

Federal regulators fined Altaba, formerly Yahoo, $35 million for failing to disclose a 2014 data breach that compromised hundreds of millions of accounts. The SEC said Yahoo did not properly investigate or inform investors before the breach became public during Verizon’s acquisition. Sen. Mark Warner welcomed the decision.

U.S. Treasury yields rose Monday as easing U.S.-North Korea tensions reduced demand for safe-haven government debt and encouraged investors toward riskier assets. The 10-year Treasury yield rose over 3 basis points to 2.222% after hitting a six-week low Friday, while the two-year yield rose 2 basis points to 1.314% after softer July inflation data had lowered Fed rate-hike expectations.

This withdrawn medRxiv preprint evaluates six machine learning models for pancreatic cancer diagnosis using a synthetic dataset containing demographic, clinical, and symptom predictors. Models tested included Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM, Neural Network, Decision Tree, and SuperLearner. The dataset was split 80/20 for training and testing, with preprocessing for missing values, scaling, and categorical encoding, but no resampling.

All models achieved similar accuracy, ranging from 76.05% to 76.35%, but sensitivity was very low. Random Forest and Decision Tree detected no true positive cases. SVM had the highest sensitivity at 1.90%, while SuperLearner had the highest precision at 66.67% but sensitivity of only 0.42%. Logistic Regression and Neural Network showed sensitivities of 1.47% and precision of 58.33%.

The study identifies class imbalance as a major limitation and suggests resampling, cost-sensitive learning, threshold tuning, feature engineering, explainable AI, and real-world clinical validation to improve clinical usefulness.

The passage describes TPS7H500x-SP controller features, operation, application guidance, and documentation updates. In hiccup mode, when CS_ILIM exceeds 1.05 V, cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins and CHICC charges with an 80-µA pulsed current until reaching 0.6 V, after which SS discharges and switching stops. HICC is pulled to 1 V, then discharged by a 1-µA restart current; switching restarts when HICC falls to 0.3 V. CHICC sets both the current-limit delay and restart-disable time, with 3.3 nF recommended minimum.

The FAULT pin allows external protections such as input overcurrent or overvoltage protection. If FAULT exceeds 0.6 V for the specified minimum pulse width, SS discharges and outputs stop switching until FAULT falls below 0.5 V, followed by a delay of about 15 switching cycles plus internal logic delay before soft-start restarts. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C typical and restarts power-up below 160°C typical.

Slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation in peak current mode control when duty cycle exceeds 50%. TPS7H500x-SP implements slope compensation as a voltage ramp set by a resistor from RSC to AVSS; the recommended value equals the falling current slope. Type 2A or Type 2B compensation can be used with the transconductance error amplifier, with Type 2A adding CHF for high-frequency noise attenuation.

The TPS7H500x-SP series uses fixed-frequency peak current mode control for space-grade DC-DC converters and requires external gate drivers. It supports up to 2 MHz switching and topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. An example synchronous push-pull GaN converter uses TPS7H5001-SP at 500 kHz, 5-V output, selected timing, soft-start, transformer, FET, clamp, output inductor, capacitance, current-sense, hiccup, compensation, and slope-compensation components.

Power supply guidance specifies a 4-V to 14-V input range, a well-regulated and bypassed input, at least 0.1 µF from VIN to AVSS, ceramic X5R or better capacitors placed close to the controller, and bulk capacitance if the supply is more than a few inches away. Layout guidance emphasizes separating noisy switching paths from sensitive signals, minimizing switch-node copper and high-current loop areas, separating analog and power grounds with a single connection point, placing bypass and compensation components close to pins, filtering CS_ILIM if needed, routing SYNC and output-drive traces away from sensitive nodes, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS with vias.

The passage also lists related TI documentation, notification and support resources, trademarks, ESD cautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information. Revision F released QMLP options for TPS7H5002-SP, TPS7H5003-SP, and TPS7H5004-SP and added an orderable mechanical no-die package; Revision E released the TPS7H5001-SP QMLP option and updated related sections.

RTX Neural Faces uses a real-time generative AI model to improve facial rendering by inferring natural-looking faces from rasterized input and 3D pose data, trained on images under varied angles, lighting, emotions, and occlusions.

Salesforce said it will invest more than $2.2 billion in its French business over five years, coinciding with President Emmanuel Macron’s state visit to Washington. The company cited rapid growth in France and plans to expand staffing, real estate and data center capacity.

A Feb. 9 11Alive study found the CDC cut more than $700,000 in 2016, largely from HIV prevention, while Atlanta continued ranking high in HIV levels. Public health experts cited lack of prevention awareness, limited access to care and expensive PrEP medication as major issues, especially in underserved communities. Stigma and Georgia laws criminalizing certain activities by people who know they have HIV may discourage disclosure and testing. Experts said many people delay testing until HIV has progressed toward AIDS. A Georgia State campaign aims to increase student testing. Georgia ranks fifth nationally for new HIV diagnoses, with two-thirds of Georgians living with HIV residing in Atlanta. A proposed bill, HB 65, would add HIV/AIDS to conditions covered by medical marijuana.

Churchill, a remote community of 900, has been shrinking since its rail line washed out in spring 2017. Officials say 30 families have left amid job losses and rising food and fuel costs. The local school is down about 40 students, affecting activities and possibly staffing. The full impact remains unclear, and there is no timeline for rail repairs.

Research by the Cinnamon Network found that more than 3,500 churches and 200,000 volunteers are supporting health and social care initiatives amid NHS funding and resource pressures. Its report studied 32 church-led projects addressing issues such as mental health, obesity and social isolation, arguing they are cost-effective and help NHS staff focus on clinical work. One highlighted initiative is parish nursing, where registered nurses are recruited by churches to support local patients. A Cambridgeshire GP described a parish nurse as an invaluable addition who can spend time with patients and advocate for them. Parish nursing began in the UK in 2005 and now involves more than 100 nurses working with 85 churches, with another 100 expected within 18 months. Parish Nursing chief executive Ros Moore said the work supports preventative care and monitoring rather than replacing NHS nurses.

Microsoft’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2017 reported total revenue of $22.1 billion, up from $20.5 billion in the prior-year quarter. Net income was $4.8 billion, compared with $3.8 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $0.61, compared with $0.47. For the nine months ended March 31, 2017, revenue was $66.6 billion, net income was $14.7 billion, and diluted EPS was $1.87.

As of March 31, 2017, Microsoft had total assets of $225.0 billion, total liabilities of $155.3 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $69.7 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $126.0 billion. Long-term debt, including the current portion, had a carrying value of $76.8 billion.

Microsoft completed its acquisition of LinkedIn on December 8, 2016 for a preliminary purchase price of $27.0 billion. LinkedIn contributed $975 million in revenue and an operating loss of $386 million in the quarter. The acquisition resulted in $16.7 billion of goodwill and $7.9 billion of intangible assets.

Segment revenue for the quarter was $8.0 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $6.8 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $8.8 billion for More Personal Computing, offset by a $1.5 billion Corporate and Other adjustment related to Windows 10 revenue deferral. Management highlighted growth in commercial cloud annualized revenue run rate, Office 365, Dynamics 365, Azure, Windows OEM, Windows Commercial, search advertising, and gaming, while Surface revenue declined.

Microsoft repurchased $8.7 billion of common stock during the first nine months of fiscal 2017 and declared quarterly dividends of $0.39 per share. The company reported aggregate accrued legal liabilities of $443 million and stated that adverse outcomes beyond recorded amounts could reasonably reach approximately $1.5 billion. Deloitte & Touche LLP reviewed the interim financial statements and stated it was not aware of material modifications needed for conformity with U.S. GAAP.

IDC’s white paper examines how IT-based simulation, modeling, data analysis, and high-performance computing support manufacturing innovation. Based on a December 2021 survey of 200 decision makers in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, it finds that manufacturers use these tools to improve product development, production planning, quality, costs, and decision-making. Deployment is growing across value creation stages, but data silos and lack of unified information bases limit benefits. Technologies such as digital twins, virtual prototyping, high-performance data analytics, visualization, AR/VR, and cloud-based workstations enable new scenarios and collaboration. Demand for high-performance calculations is expected to rise sharply as existing simulations are often slow, outdated, or inaccurate. Four out of five surveyed decision makers view HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation because it enables faster, more complex, and higher-quality calculations and supports new usage scenarios.

Columbiana defeated Lisbon 49-47 after scoring twice in the final 23 seconds, improving to 5-0 overall and 3-0 in EOAC play while Lisbon fell to 3-2 and 2-1. Alexis Cross tied the game with a baseline drive, and Kayla Muslovski’s steal and layup provided the winning points. Muslovski and Cross each scored 14 for the Clippers, while Izzy Perez led Lisbon with 17 points and Maddie Liberati added 12. Kennedy Fullum and Cross each had six rebounds for Columbiana, and Autumn Oehlstrom led Lisbon with seven. Columbiana also won the junior varsity game 33-23.

Reddit surpassed Facebook as the third most visited US platform, according to Alexa, behind Google and YouTube. Users spend more daily time on Reddit than Facebook. The ranking shift comes amid Facebook’s Cambridge Analytica scandal and GDPR-related changes.

Suspected jihadists killed at least 18 people and wounded several in an overnight attack on the Aziz Istanbul restaurant in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. Security forces killed both attackers and freed people trapped inside. Officials called it a terrorist attack and said the toll was provisional. Burkina Faso has faced sporadic jihadist violence, mostly near its northern border with Mali. The attack followed previous Islamist militant attacks in the region, including a deadly 2016 assault in Ouagadougou.

The BCCI is expected to oppose any ICC move to replace the 2021 Champions Trophy in India with a World T20, with treasurer Anirudh Chaudhry saying it could cost the board and stakeholders about $30 million. The issue may be discussed at ICC Board meetings in Kolkata under “Formats and ICC Competition Architecture.” The 2019-2023 FTP had allotted the 2020 World T20 to Australia, the 2021 Champions Trophy and 2023 World Cup to India. The ICC also adjusted the 2019 World Cup schedule after the BCCI advanced the IPL to March 29-May 19, ensuring a 15-day gap before the World Cup. India will begin against South Africa on June 5 and play Pakistan on June 16.

Severe storms threatened 29 million people across the Southeast, with risks of damaging hail, high winds and tornadoes in parts of Alabama, Georgia, Tennessee and northeast Mississippi. Forecasters warned of possible strong tornadoes, especially in northern Alabama. Hail fell in northern Mississippi, and schools and Birmingham city offices closed early due to the threat.

The passage introduces iMOOE, a physics-guided invariant learning framework for zero-shot out-of-distribution PDE dynamics forecasting. It argues that existing meta-learning, parameter-conditioning, and pretraining approaches often require test-time samples or fine-tuning and do not explicitly capture invariant PDE structure. The authors define two PDE invariance principles: invariant elementary operators and invariant composition relationships among operators, parameters, and forcing terms.

iMOOE uses a mixture of operator experts to approximate distinct physical processes and a fusion network to combine expert outputs with exogenous inputs. It is trained with a prediction loss, risk equality loss across environments, frequency-enrichment loss to address spectral bias, and mask diversity loss for operator specialization. Experiments on simulated PDE systems and real-world sea surface temperature data show improved zero-shot OOD performance over several baselines. The framework is also shown to be compatible with multiple neural operator backbones. Limitations include validation on a limited range of dynamical systems, with future work planned for irregular grids and broader real-world applications.

Indian markets erased early weekly gains, with the Nifty ending down 0.3 percent, while mid- and small-cap indexes rose about 1.5 percent each. Sentiment was hurt by U.S. tariff concerns, possible global rate hikes, political uncertainty after TDP quit the BJP alliance, RBI restrictions on LoUs and LCs, and tensions over bank fraud oversight. The rupee strengthened to 64.93 per dollar, while crude oil was largely flat. Crude sulfate turpentine is a flammable, water-insoluble derivative of turpentine obtained as a Kraft process byproduct. It contains terpene hydrocarbons and sulfur compounds, mainly alpha-pinene and beta-pinene, with smaller amounts of limonene, camphene, carene, and terpinene. It is primarily used in fragrances and flavors, with major end uses in cosmetics and food and beverages, and also serves as a solvent for oil-based paints, varnishes, and chemical synthesis. Market growth may be restrained by high distillation investment requirements and limited black liquor retrieval. Alpha-pinene is used as an anti-inflammatory agent, beta-pinene in perfumery, and carene provides pine-like, woody, cedar, sweet, and pungent fragrances.

The lecture covers interacting Bose gases, focusing on how unsolvable many-body Hamiltonians are reduced to solvable approximations. It reviews the Bogoliubov approximation for homogeneous Bose-Einstein condensates, where condensate operators are replaced by numbers, yielding noninteracting quasiparticles with linear low-momentum and quadratic high-momentum dispersion. Interactions cause quantum depletion, which is small in alkali gas condensates but large in liquid helium.

Experiments discussed include observing sound propagation in a condensate using a repulsive laser beam and measuring quasiparticle dispersion through stimulated light scattering, or Bragg spectroscopy. The lecture then treats inhomogeneous condensates using position-space field operators and the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, a nonlinear Schrödinger equation for the macroscopic wave function. The interaction term tends to flatten density, leading to concepts such as the healing length and the Thomas-Fermi approximation, where density follows the inverted trapping potential when kinetic energy is neglected.

The Gross-Pitaevskii equation is used to explain condensate expansion, vortices, and vortex lattices. Vortices arise because rotating quantum fluids cannot undergo rigid-body rotation; angular momentum is carried by singular points where density vanishes. Multiply charged vortices are unstable and split into singly charged vortices, which repel and can form regular lattices.

The lecture then introduces Bose-Einstein condensates in optical lattices. Periodic potentials lead to Bloch waves, band structure, Wannier functions, tunneling matrix element \(J\), and onsite interaction energy \(U\). In the tight-binding limit, the Bose-Hubbard model describes tunneling and onsite interactions. When \(U \gg J\), tunneling is suppressed and the system forms a Mott insulator with fixed particle number per site. When \(J \gg U\), the system is superfluid. A mean-field approximation is used to derive the superfluid–Mott insulator transition and its phase diagram. The transition can be observed through time-of-flight interference patterns or quantum gas microscopy showing site-resolved atom occupation.
The speaker emphasizes focusing on each shift and period, executing well, seizing the rare opportunity, and sharing a strong desire to win the Cup.

The passage describes a Learning Health System framework and Pragmatic Trial Operations playbook for implementing and evaluating Ambient AI, a generative AI tool embedded in Epic EHR to support clinical documentation at UW Health. The playbook included governance, user experience, technical integration, documentation sustainment, and analytics components. An alpha phase tested safety, usability, workflows, compliance, and monitoring, while a beta phase used a 24-week multisite stepped-wedge pragmatic randomized clinical trial of 66 providers to assess effects on provider well-being using the Professional Fulfillment Index.

Ambient AI was integrated through Epic APIs and FHIR, with provider and patient consent processes, training, technical onboarding, and real-time dashboards tracking utilization, documentation efficiency, consent compliance, and provider feedback. Governance included executive sponsors, implementation teams, and specialized workgroups.

In the alpha phase, 20 providers across five specialties and 8,527 encounters were evaluated. Weighted median Ambient AI utilization was 65.4%. Interviews identified barriers involving organizational context, provider and patient readiness, documentation preferences, technical issues, and task suitability. Rapid Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles led to workflow, training, and support changes. Manual review found documentation coding accuracy decreased from 79% to 35% after implementation because visit diagnoses were no longer pulled into notes; a revised template restored accuracy to pre-intervention levels. Manual coding review required 598.33 hours, prompting development of an LLM-based ICD-10 review system, which achieved a mean Jaccard score of 0.54 in validation.

The study concludes that aligning research and operations within a Learning Health System can support rigorous, scalable evaluation of evolving GenAI tools while maintaining operational efficiency, governance, monitoring, and readiness for broader implementation if effective.

A newlywed Northamptonshire couple had to walk home after police stopped their BMW wedding car for speeding at 46mph in a 30mph zone and found the driver had no insurance. Police said the vehicle could not continue, but the couple remained in high spirits and took a selfie with the officer before walking two minutes home.

Kari L. Baumann appealed the district court’s summary judgment in favor of The Kroger Company and Dr. Gregory P. Tayler in a healthcare malpractice case. Baumann had failed to disclose expert witnesses by the stipulated deadline under Utah Rule of Civil Procedure 26. Defendants moved for summary judgment, arguing she could not prove standard of care, breach, or causation without expert testimony. Baumann later submitted an expert report only as to Kroger, after the court’s filing cutoff, and submitted none as to Dr. Tayler.

The Utah Court of Appeals held that Baumann’s argument regarding an expert report for Dr. Tayler was unpreserved because she never requested such relief in the district court. As to Kroger, the court held that Rule 26(d)(4), not Rule 16(d), controlled because the issue was failure to disclose an expert witness. Under Rule 26, undisclosed witnesses or materials may not be used unless the failure was harmless or supported by good cause. The district court found no good cause, and Baumann did not challenge the need for expert testimony. The Court of Appeals concluded the district court did not abuse its discretion in excluding the expert evidence and affirmed summary judgment.

The President returns to the House a bill to facilitate refunding the national debt, citing objections to section 5. He supports prompt passage of a suitable refunding measure to reduce annual interest payments, but argues that section 5 is not essential to refunding and would seriously impair the national banking system. The section would make 3 percent bonds the only bonds acceptable as security for national-bank circulation or public deposits after July 1, 1881, limiting new bank formation and capital expansion. He contends this would deprive banks and noteholders of stronger securities, create a monopoly for existing banks able to acquire higher-interest bonds before July, threaten the banking system, disturb confidence, and harm national prosperity. Therefore, he vetoes the bill and returns it for reconsideration.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Ampere GA10x GPU architecture, focusing on GA102 and GA104 GPUs used in GeForce RTX 30-series, RTX A6000, and A40 products. GA10x builds on Turing with up to 1.7x faster raster graphics and up to 2x faster ray tracing, using 2x FP32 processing, second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, larger L1/shared memory, improved ROP placement, PCIe Gen 4, and third-generation NVLink.

GA102 includes up to 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, and 336 Tensor Cores, fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm process with 28.3 billion transistors. The architecture doubles FP32 throughput per SM, improves ray/triangle intersection performance, supports concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute, and adds hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur through an Interpolate Triangle Position unit.

Third-generation Tensor Cores support sparsity, TF32, BF16, FP16, INT8, INT4, and 1-bit modes, accelerating AI workloads such as DLSS, denoising, NVIDIA Broadcast, and Canvas. DLSS improvements enable up to 8K gaming on supported hardware. GA10x also introduces GDDR6X memory with PAM4 signaling, reaching up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec bandwidth, plus Error Detection and Replay for memory overclocking feedback.

Additional features include RTX IO for GPU-based asset loading and decompression with Microsoft DirectStorage, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4a, AV1 hardware decode through fifth-generation NVDEC, and seventh-generation NVENC for hardware video encoding. The A40 targets data center visual computing and virtualization, while the RTX A6000 targets professional workstation rendering, AI, visualization, and compute workloads with 48 GB GDDR6 and NVLink scalability to 96 GB.
