A study in Psychological Medicine found that lonely millennials had twice the risk of mental health problems such as depression and anxiety compared with those connected to others. Researchers from King’s College London analysed 2,066 millennial twins in England and Wales, with the latest data collected at age 18. Seven percent often felt lonely, while 23–31% felt left out or lacked companionship. Loneliness was also linked to a 38% higher risk of unemployment and more risky behaviours such as smoking and not exercising. Other research suggests teenagers and young adults are lonelier than older people. The passage notes social media’s role may depend on how it is used, and cites research suggesting loneliness can be contagious. Researchers said early intervention may help prevent young adults from remaining lonely as they age.

The paper investigates whether large language models can detect and fix API misuses in Python data science libraries, where correct API behavior often depends on both documentation directives and runtime data characteristics. It proposes DSCHECKER, an LLM-based approach that prompts models with code, relevant API directives, and dynamic variable information extracted by running the code.

The study evaluates DSCHECKER on DSMISUSES, an updated dataset derived from prior work containing 38 reproducible API misuses and 38 corrected snippets across NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, scikit-learn, and seaborn. Experiments compare prompt variants with no added context, data information only, API directives only, and both types of context. Results show that adding API directives and variable information generally improves performance, with llama using the full prompt achieving the best zero-shot detection F1-score of 61.18% and fix rate of 51.28%.

Few-shot prompting produced mixed results: it significantly improved detection and fixing for GPT-4o but slightly reduced detection performance for llama and did not improve its fixing rate. DSCHECKER was also tested on 15 reproduced deep learning API misuses from a separate dataset, achieving a 48% detection F1-score and 26.67% fix rate, with better performance when API directives were available.

Compared with LLMAPIDET, an existing LLM-based tool for deep learning API misuse detection, DSCHECKER performed better on DSMISUSES. LLMAPIDET detected no misuses using its original deep learning rules and achieved 11.19% average recall under cross-validation, while DSCHECKER with GPT-4o-mini achieved 46.15% recall and did not require prior misuse-fix examples.

The paper also introduces DSCHECKERagent, which lets the LLM request API documentation and variable information through function calls. With GPT-4o, it achieved a 48.65% detection F1-score and 39.47% fix rate, lower than DSCHECKER but indicating potential for practical settings where relevant context is not predefined. The authors identify challenges including hallucinated documentation requests, difficulty using full API documentation, and the need for more LLM-friendly API documentation formats.

Rams Coach Sean McVay said Todd Gurley will receive increasing preseason work, including through the third game against the Chargers, to prepare for the Sept. 10 opener against the Colts. Gurley had four carries for two yards and a 10-yard catch in a 13-10 win over the Cowboys. McVay said Gurley’s workload requires a careful balance because he works hard and wants to compete, but the team wants him ready and at his best for the regular season.

Researchers found that island flying foxes in Malaysia help pollinate durian trees rather than damage them. Camera traps in a Tioman Island durian orchard showed the bats feeding on nectar without harming flowers and contributing to durian reproductive success. The study highlights the ecological and agricultural value of bats, which often have a negative public image. Island flying fox populations are declining due to hunting and habitat loss, and the species is endangered in Malaysia.

Rice University and the Houston Museum of Natural Science have collaborated on space science outreach since 1988, beginning with an NSF-funded Teacher Research Program and later developing multiple educational technology projects. For the 2023–2024 Heliophysics Big Year and the 2024 total solar eclipse, they expanded outreach through eclipse animations, teacher training, websites, media, public events, planetarium programming, safety materials, eclipse viewers, and participation in Citizen CATE 2024.

Updated eclipse animations were distributed to 186 educators in 33 countries and 33 U.S. states, with more than 19,000 YouTube views. The fulldome planetarium show “Totality,” produced with HMNS, Rice, and ePlanetarium, covered eclipse science, history, safety, and future eclipses. It was distributed to 147 planetariums, with a Texas version sent to 53 Texas sites; reported views exceeded 180,000 when including HMNS, FullDomeOnDemand rentals, and YouTube.

Teacher outreach included Rice courses and workshops emphasizing eclipse science and safety. Documented teacher participation totaled 5,104, excluding broader public and student events. The eclipse website provided animations, activities, graphics, FAQs, training, safety guidance, and resources, supported by email lists and newsletters. Survey responses indicated wide redistribution of materials, averaging more than 500 people reached per respondent.

The project distributed more than 35,000 eclipse glasses, 30,000 viewing cards, and, through a Buc-ee’s-funded HMNS effort, more than one million eclipse viewers to Texas schools. Public events for the 2023 annular and 2024 total eclipses included observing activities at HMNS, Corpus Christi, Bandera, and Citizen CATE-related sites.

Citizen CATE 2024 used 35 community-led sites and additional professional or outreach sites to observe the April 8, 2024 eclipse with identical telescopes, cameras, and procedures. More than 250 participants were involved, over 80% of teams observed some or all of totality, and analysis of the coronal data was ongoing.

The outreach also included media appearances, an eclipse expedition with more than 300 Rice participants, and space weather alerts during the May 2024 geomagnetic storm. Overall documented reach exceeded 250,000 in leveraged venues, with total reach estimated at more than 1.5 million people.

A University of Eastern Finland study of 2,480 men aged 42 to 60 found that higher blood levels of linoleic acid, an omega-6 fatty acid found in vegetable oils, nuts, and seeds, were linked to a 43% lower risk of premature death over 22 years. Higher levels were also associated with reduced cardiovascular death risk, but not cancer death. A weaker link was found for arachidonic acid. The findings were published in The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition.

Gray Davis’ plan to buy utility transmission lines, rescue financially distressed utilities, secure federal support, and manage the state’s energy crisis.

The Public Utilities Commission planned to review residential electricity baseline levels and whether temporary rate hikes should continue. PUC President Loretta Lynch defended the agency’s actions, blamed failed deregulation, and said the commission should have recognized problems sooner.

Several reports said the California Independent System Operator alleged suppliers overcharged utilities by about $562 million in December and January and asked federal regulators to seek refunds. Generators denied wrongdoing and resisted calls to forgive utility debts. PG&E announced it would pay only a fraction of recent power bills, angering smaller suppliers and raising bankruptcy concerns.

Other articles described long-term power contracts between California and Calpine, emergency gas purchasing arrangements for PG&E, calls for temporary federal price caps, and criticism that state control of transmission and generation could be costly, politically driven, and slow to implement.

The passage describes a study of whole-body mu-opioid receptor imaging using [11C]carfentanil PET on the PennPET Explorer. It reviews opioid misuse, MOR agonists and antagonists, prior [11C]CFN-PET brain studies, sex and age differences in MOR availability, and the potential of long axial field-of-view PET for dynamic whole-body imaging and extra-CNS reference regions. Healthy adults aged 18–45 without psychiatric or substance use disorders were enrolled. Participants underwent MRI and 90-minute dynamic [11C]CFN PET/CT imaging. Images were analyzed with PMOD, using brain volumes of interest including amygdala, caudate, putamen, thalamus, and ventral tegmentum, with the visual cortex as reference tissue to calculate distribution volume ratios.

Mitch Larkin may add the individual medley to his Commonwealth Games trials program after winning the 400m IM at the Queensland titles in 4:20.45. The dual backstroke world champion said he is open to attempting the event but will keep his main focus on returning his backstroke to world-class level. Larkin won 100m and 200m backstroke gold at the 2015 world championships but left the Rio Olympics with 200m silver and no 100m medal. After changing coaches since Rio, he said a difficult year has renewed his hunger and attention to training details.

The lecture revisits weak duality in least squares, showing that optimality occurs when \(b = Ax + w\), linking primal and dual problems. A related geometry identity is posed: for any point connected to the four corners of a rectangle, the sums of squares of opposite distances are equal.

The main topic is inverse and ill-posed problems. Examples include estimating velocity from noisy position data, finding Earth density from seismic travel times or gravitational fields, medical imaging, scattering problems, identifying coefficients in PDEs, and reconstructing matrices from inputs and outputs. Ill-posedness arises because small measurement noise can cause large errors, especially when derivatives or high frequencies are involved.

Integral equations of the first kind are introduced as common models for inverse problems, with second-kind equations obtained by adding a regularizing identity term. GPS is discussed as an example where position can be measured from satellite signals, while velocity estimation is more sensitive to noise; Doppler frequency methods may help.

The lecture then describes Tikhonov regularization, minimizing \(\|Ax-b\|^2+\alpha\|x\|^2\), leading to \((A^TA+\alpha I)u=b\). The parameter \(\alpha\) balances instability from too little regularization against oversmoothing from too much. With noise size \(\delta\), a useful choice is \(\alpha=\delta^{2/3}\). A final example from genomics notes that estimating gene importance through derivatives from limited high-dimensional samples is also ill-posed and requires regularization.
Ventura police will review procedures after Anthony Mele was fatally stabbed in a steakhouse by Jamal Jackson, who had earlier been reported for disruptive behavior but deemed not a threat.

Canon’s EOS M6 replaces the M3 as an entry-level mirrorless camera aimed at users wanting DSLR-like photo quality. It is similar to the M5 but lacks a built-in viewfinder, has body/control changes, and a lower-resolution flip-up touchscreen. Shipping was planned for April 2017 from $780. The passage notes cheaper Sony A5100 and A6000 alternatives with similar or better features.

A total solar eclipse on Aug. 21 will cross the U.S. from Oregon to South Carolina, the first coast-to-coast total eclipse in 99 years and the first in the Lower 48 in 38 years. NASA, scientists, schools, businesses and communities along the path of totality are preparing events, research and broadcasts. The total eclipse will last about 1.5 hours as the moon’s shadow moves across the country, with darkness lasting up to 2 minutes and 44 seconds in southern Illinois. Researchers will study the sun, the moon’s shadow, and animal and plant reactions, while balloons, satellites, telescopes, astronauts, ships and planes observe the event. Eye protection is required except during totality, and large crowds are expected because about 200 million people live within a day’s drive of the path. A partial eclipse will be visible across parts of Canada, Central America and South America.

IDC’s white paper examines the use of IT-based simulation, modeling, data analysis, and high-performance computing in manufacturing. Based on a December 2021 survey of 200 decision makers in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, it finds that enterprises use these technologies to increase innovation, improve quality, reduce costs, speed development, and support decision-making. HPC is presented as enabling faster, more complex calculations, new usage scenarios, and greater agility, with 81% of respondents viewing it as a game changer. Douglas Haig, 55, of Arizona, was charged with conspiracy to manufacture and sell armor-piercing ammunition without a license, allegedly selling ammunition to Las Vegas gunman Stephen Paddock before the October 1, 2017 shooting that killed 58 people and wounded hundreds. Haig was released on bail pending a February 15 hearing and faces up to five years in prison and a possible $250,000 fine. Investigators said ammunition found in Paddock’s hotel rooms bore Haig’s fingerprints or tool marks consistent with his equipment.

The lecture discusses additive energy as a measure of additive structure in subsets of an Abelian group. For sets \(A\) and \(B\), the additive energy \(E(A,B)\) counts quadruples satisfying \(a_1+b_1=a_2+b_2\), equivalently \(\sum_x r_{A,B}(x)^2\), where \(r_{A,B}(x)\) counts representations of \(x\) as \(a+b\). For one set \(A\), the trivial bounds are roughly \(|A|^2 \le E(A) \le |A|^3\).

Small doubling implies large additive energy: if \(|A+A|\le k|A|\), then by Cauchy-Schwarz \(E(A)\ge |A|^3/k\). The converse is false in general, since a set may contain a highly structured subset plus unstructured elements, giving high energy but large doubling.

The Balog-Szemerédi-Gowers theorem addresses this by showing that if a set has large additive energy, then it contains a large subset with small doubling. A two-set version states that if \(A\) and \(B\) have size at most \(n\) and large energy, then there are large subsets \(A'\subseteq A\), \(B'\subseteq B\) with \(|A'+B'|\) bounded polynomially in the parameter times \(n\). This implies the one-set version using Ruzsa-type inequalities.

The proof is reduced to a graphical version: for a dense bipartite graph \(G\) between \(A\) and \(B\), if the restricted sumset along edges is small, then large subsets \(A'\) and \(B'\) have small complete sumset. Popular sums are used to construct such a graph from large additive energy.

The graphical theorem is proved using graph-theoretic lemmas. A dependent random choice argument gives a path-of-length-2 lemma: in a dense bipartite graph, there is a large subset of one side where most pairs have many common neighbors. This is upgraded to a path-of-length-3 lemma by trimming low-degree vertices and selecting large subsets so that every pair across them is joined by many length-3 paths.

Finally, each length-3 path allows \(a+b\) to be expressed as \(x-y+z\), with \(x,y,z\) from the restricted sumset. Since the restricted sumset is small and there are many such paths, the complete sumset \(A'+B'\) is small. This proves the graphical Balog-Szemerédi-Gowers theorem and hence the additive version.

Colorado coach Deion Sanders was scheduled for a medical procedure Tuesday for blood clot issues and said he hoped to return to practice the next day and coach Saturday against No. 22 Iowa State. Sanders said the condition is hereditary and unrelated to his workload. He experienced significant leg pain during Colorado’s 35-21 loss at TCU. Sanders has previously dealt with blood clots, including toe amputations in 2021 and procedures in 2023. He also spent time away from the team over the summer after treatment for aggressive bladder cancer.

Rockefeller University researchers led by A. James Hudspeth kept a tiny slice of mammalian cochlea alive and functional outside the body for the first time. Using a custom chamber that replicated the cochlea’s living environment, they observed gerbil cochlear tissue responding to sound in real time. The experiment showed how hair-cell ion channels and outer hair-cell electromotility amplify vibrations, and provided direct evidence that a Hopf bifurcation underlies mammalian hearing amplification, as previously documented in other animals. Researchers say the ex vivo cochlea could enable targeted studies of hearing mechanisms and support future efforts to develop treatments for sensorineural hearing loss.

NVIDIA Ampere adds BF16, TF32, and FP64 to Tensor Cores. BF16 and FP16 support mixed-precision neural network training and provide 16x FP32 throughput on A100 GPUs. TF32 enables default Tensor Core acceleration for AI training using FP32 inputs and outputs with reduced internal precision.

The passage describes embodiments of memory arrays with vertically alternating tiers of insulative material and memory cells. Each memory cell includes a transistor with first and second source/drain regions, a horizontally oriented channel region, and one or more gates, plus a capacitor with first and second electrodes separated by capacitor insulator. The first capacitor electrode is coupled to the first source/drain region. Second capacitor electrodes across multiple tiers may be electrically coupled through an elevationally extending capacitor-electrode structure, while second source/drain regions across tiers may be coupled to an elevationally extending sense-line structure. Variations include different gate arrangements, stacked memory cells within a tier, annular regions, shared capacitor electrodes, and staircase contacts. The passage also outlines an example fabrication process involving stacked materials, etching, deposition, formation of source/drain regions, gates, capacitors, sense-line structures, capacitor-electrode structures, and conductive vias.

Each digital I/O maps to a PINCMx register for configuring pin functions. IOMUX supports one managed digital function per pin, and PINCM.PF/PC should be 0 for non-IOMUX functions unless concurrent use has no contention.

The XPIC delays clearing IRR during interrupt acknowledge, causing duplicate CPU interrupts when master PIC AEOI is enabled. AEOI auto-issues non-specific EOI and is unsuitable for nested multilevel interrupts.

President Biden spoke in Pittsburgh about rebuilding the middle class and U.S. infrastructure through the American Jobs Plan, which he described as part of a broader agenda with the American Families Plan. He said the American Rescue Plan addressed immediate crises from COVID-19, jobs, and the economy, and argued that the next step is a major investment in long-term growth.

Biden said the American Jobs Plan would modernize roads, bridges, airports, ports, rail, transit, water systems, broadband, the electric grid, housing, and commercial buildings. He said it would replace lead pipes, expand high-speed Internet, build electric vehicle charging stations, support clean energy, improve care for seniors and people with disabilities, and increase federal non-defense research and development. He said the plan would create millions of good-paying jobs, strengthen unions, support domestic manufacturing, address climate risks, and improve U.S. competitiveness, including with China.

He described the proposal as a roughly $2 trillion one-time capital investment over about eight years. To pay for it, he proposed raising the corporate tax rate to 28 percent, establishing a 21 percent global minimum tax for U.S. corporations, ending incentives for offshoring, and increasing IRS enforcement against corporations. He said no one making under $400,000 would see federal taxes rise.

Biden called for bipartisan cooperation, saying infrastructure has historically had support from both parties and that the United States must show democracies can deliver results.

The passage describes a patent continuation for automated storage, retrieval, and processing systems. The invention provides systems using storage bins, destination bins, gantry retrieval conveyance systems, and programmable motion devices to move bins and transfer objects between them. A processing programmable motion device, such as a robotic arm with an end effector, grasps selected objects from storage bins and deposits them into destination bins according to a manifest.

The system may include separate or combined storage and destination sections, with programmable motion devices moving bins to and from processing locations. Perception systems provide image or scanning data to identify objects and determine grasp locations. Grasp selection may consider object visibility, surface flatness, center of mass, surface normals, and features such as barcodes. The system may learn good and bad grasp locations from prior grasp attempts.

Several embodiments are described, including systems with separate storage and destination gantries, a shared gantry for intermixed storage and destination bins, processing stations between multiple bin arrays, and multi-floor systems with many storage, destination, and processing sections. Computer systems track bin identities and locations, direct bin movement, and control object distribution to destination bins.

The coach said the team generated traffic, shots, rebounds, energy, territory, and scoring chances but could not find a third goal. He felt the team settled after a poor start and handled the elimination-game pressure with controlled emotion. He praised the defensive effort against plays below the goal line, acknowledged Burns’ offensive threat, and expressed trust in the team’s leadership and routines. He said Crosby remains a force, Sergei has been invaluable to the defense, Malkin’s game is improving, and Matt brings important on-ice impact, experience, composure, and leadership.

The President stated that 653 troops, excluding marines at the navy-yard, were assembled in Washington to support civil authority and preserve order before or during the President-elect’s inauguration. He said no proven conspiracy had been found, but public alarm, rumors, threats, and concern for public property, government archives, city peace, and the inauguration justified precautionary defensive measures.

Bear markets are described as longer and steeper than corrections, often associated with declines of 20% or more, though there is no official rule. They feature higher volatility, sharp rallies, and sudden equity drops, while recoveries can take much longer. The S&P 500 spent 70% of its time above the 200-day moving average since 1960 and 85% since 2010. During 2000–2003, the dividend-adjusted S&P 500 fell 45%, while Nasdaq fell more than 80% and took 15 years to recover. The passage argues that investors may benefit from lower prices, while traders may benefit from increased volatility and opportunities for long and short strategies.

The Louisiana Supreme Court did not consider Arthur Rhodes’s writ as untimely. It stated he has exhausted state post-conviction relief unless a narrow exception permits a successive application, and ordered the district court to record a consistent minute entry.

Hong Kong stocks ended slightly higher as property weakness offset gains in shipping firms and Tencent. The Hang Seng rose 0.2%, while the China Enterprises Index gained 0.1%. Tencent, banking stocks, and Fosun rose, but real estate dipped amid tighter property curbs and Moody’s warnings on China property risks.

The study investigates thermal transport in β-Ga₂O₃ under uniform strain and strain gradients using first-principles-based neuroevolution machine-learning potentials combined with the phonon Boltzmann transport equation. β-Ga₂O₃ is promising for high-power, UV, and flexible devices, but its low thermal conductivity and strain sensitivity create thermal management challenges.

The model accurately reproduces DFT energies, forces, virials, phonon dispersions, lattice parameters, and experimental thermal conductivities. Uniform strain substantially modulates thermal conductivity anisotropically, mainly by changing intrinsic phonon lifetimes rather than heat capacity or group velocity. Strains involving the b-axis produce the strongest effects.

Strain gradients suppress thermal conductivity more strongly than corresponding uniform tensile strains, especially in nanoscale films. In 10 nm films, uniaxial gradients of 0.6%/nm reduce thermal conductivity by about 32–37%, while biaxial gradients reduce it by about 42–43%, roughly 1.5 times stronger than equivalent uniform biaxial strain. Similar suppression occurs in nanowires. The mechanism is attributed to gradient-induced symmetry breaking, phonon spectral broadening, activation of previously forbidden scattering channels, localized vibrational modes, and expanded phonon scattering phase space, especially affecting acoustic and low-lying optical phonons.

Unlike uniform strain, strain gradients strongly reduce thermal conductivity without substantially changing thermal anisotropy ratios. The authors conclude that strain gradients must be explicitly considered in β-Ga₂O₃ thermal modeling and may provide opportunities for thermal engineering in ultra-wide bandgap and flexible electronic devices.

The passage advises startup owners on attracting investors during initial fundraising. It emphasizes making the business stand out by focusing on return on investment, including equity expectations and possible mentoring arrangements. It highlights the importance of founders presenting themselves confidently while accepting advice, and of having an experienced, proactive team. Evidence of market traction, such as revenue or customer satisfaction, can strengthen credibility. The passage also notes that investors may seek opportunities in specific industries, emerging markets, or businesses addressing gaps or disrupting saturated sectors. A detailed business plan with accurate projections, market research, and awareness of risks, competition, and financial implications is described as crucial. The article concludes that preparation, confidence, and business awareness can improve a startup owner’s chances of securing funding.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K dated July 20, 2017, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2017. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Exchange Act.

UCLA researchers led by Heather Christofk and William Lowry found a way to activate hair follicle stem cells by altering their metabolism, potentially promoting hair growth for baldness or alopecia. The study, published in Nature Cell Biology, showed that lactate production affects hair follicle stem cell activation in mice: blocking lactate prevented activation, while increasing lactate accelerated activation and the hair cycle. The team identified two skin-applied drugs in mice, RCGD423 and UK5099, that promote lactate production and quicker hair growth through different mechanisms. Both uses are covered by provisional patent applications. The drugs were tested only preclinically and have not been tested in humans or approved by the FDA.

Colgate-Palmolive’s stock outlook has improved as analysts expect renewed revenue and profit growth, with Argus setting a $72 price target and the stock trading below 20 times forward earnings. The company remains a dividend aristocrat, having raised its dividend annually since 1964 and currently yielding about 2.6%. However, the passage argues investors should remain cautious because Colgate lacks a strong moat. Its products are highly commoditized, and e-commerce has weakened large consumer brands’ historical shelf-space advantage by giving smaller and niche competitors more visibility. Despite loyal customers, stable dividends, and improving earnings, the author believes the stock remains vulnerable and too expensive at around 20 times earnings.

European Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker said India’s 5.7% GDP growth is not viewed abroad as a slowdown and compares favorably with Europe’s 2%. His remarks came amid domestic criticism over growth slowing after demonetisation and GST implementation, including comments by Jim Yong Kim and Yashwant Sinha.

Officials raised the AJC Peachtree Road Race alert to Code Red, advising runners to slow down, follow instructions and consider stopping. Weather was expected to be dry and hot, with a $70,000 prize purse for American athletes.

The passage describes DEBUGSS for MSPM0 devices, which connects the ARM SWD two-wire interface to device debug functions, supports processor and device-state debugging, mailbox communication, configurable peripheral behavior during debug halt, PMCU reset and mode requests, SWD lockout, and password-authenticated debugging. It also describes the read-only FACTORY region containing device capabilities, trim, hardware revision, DEVICEID, and USERID values.

Application guidance recommends 10µF and 0.1µF low-ESR ceramic decoupling capacitors near VDD/VSS, a 47kΩ pullup and 1000pF pulldown on NRST, crystal oscillator bypass capacitors where applicable, and pullup resistors for 5V-tolerant open-drain IOs used for I2C or UART. TI provides development resources, documentation, support forums, trademarks, ESD handling cautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, soldering, orderable, and disclaimer information for MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 devices.

The shallow cross concept pairs a basic route and shallow drag from opposite directions to stress linebacker-level defenders and provide answers against man and zone coverage. It can serve as a quick option versus blitz, a middle-field attack, or a secondary progression after downfield reads. It works well against man, Tampa 2, and Cover 4, but is less effective against Cover 3 due to the defense’s numbers in flat and hook areas.

Route coaching points include a 10–12 yard basic route by the TE, a 3–4 yard shallow drag by the slot, go and post routes by outside receivers, and a flare/checkdown by the back. The quarterback reads downfield first, then progresses to post, drag, basic, and running back checkdown, adjusting quickly to the shallow combination under pressure.

Variations include Bunch X Shallow Cross, which uses bunch alignment and high-to-low reads, and Empty Shallow Cross Post-Wheel, which gives quick answers against pressure and stresses one-high defenses.

The lecture reviews digital communication as communication with a binary interface between source and destination, emphasizing standardization, layering, and Shannon’s result that such an interface loses no performance. The course plan is to study source coding first, then channel coding, beginning with discrete source coding under an assumed reliable binary channel.

Source coding is divided into sampling or expansion of analog inputs, quantization into a finite alphabet with distortion, and discrete coding into binary sequences. Discrete source coding maps symbol sequences into binary sequences with unique decodability, meaning the decoder can recover the original symbols when the bits are correct.

Fixed-length coding maps each source symbol to a binary string of length \(l\), requiring \(2^l \ge m\) for alphabet size \(m\), so \(l=\lceil \log_2 m\rceil\). Generalized fixed-length coding groups source symbols into blocks of length \(n\), reducing bits per source symbol toward \(\log_2 m\) as \(n\) grows. The specific names or meanings of symbols do not matter for coding; only the number of distinguishable symbols matters.

Variable-length codes use shorter code words for more probable symbols and longer ones for rare symbols. Code words are concatenated without separators, so unique decodability is required. Prefix-free codes are introduced as codes in which no code word is a prefix of another. They can be represented by binary trees and are instantaneously decodable because the decoder recognizes a code word as soon as its final bit arrives.

The Kraft inequality states that any prefix-free code with code word lengths \(l(x)\) satisfies \(\sum_x 2^{-l(x)} \le 1\), and conversely, if this inequality holds, a prefix-free code with those lengths can be constructed. A full prefix-free code satisfies the inequality with equality. The proof is described using intervals from base-2 expansions.

Unique decodability is then defined more generally: no concatenation of code words for one source string may equal the concatenation for any different source string. Some uniquely decodable codes are not prefix-free, though prefix-free codes are simpler and useful.

The next topic is discrete memoryless sources, whose outputs are infinite sequences of independent, identically distributed letters from a finite alphabet under a common probability measure. This model will be used to introduce probabilities, entropy, and optimal coding.

WIS News 10 will air a special on preparing for Total Eclipse Columbia, covering safety and science. On Aug. 21, Columbia and the Midlands will be in the path of totality, where the moon will fully cover the sun and create daytime darkness.

Brea Police is using a Polaris Gem Global Electric Motorcar to patrol The Tracks at Brea trail, downtown entertainment district, and park trails. The all-electric vehicle travels up to 25 mph, has a 98-mile battery range, seats two, and cost about $21,000 funded by Air Quality Management District money.

The lecture introduces the economics of green buildings, focusing on how to make a business case that aligns environmental and social goals with profit. Since most urban buildings are supplied by the private sector, the instructor emphasizes the need to incentivize developers and investors through market mechanisms.

Using Millennium Partners as an example, the lecture shows that developers’ priorities shift with market and policy contexts. Earlier projects emphasized luxury, job creation, downtown revitalization, or wellness, while the current Winthrop Center emphasizes sustainability and certifications such as Passive House and LEED. The instructor argues that students should critically examine whether sustainability claims reflect long-standing values or changing business incentives.

The lecture explains green building economics through three stakeholders: tenants, owners, and developers. Tenants may value green buildings because of lower operating costs, better health, higher productivity, employee recruitment and retention, and ESG or reputation benefits. These benefits can increase tenants’ willingness to pay rent. Owners may benefit from higher rents, lower vacancy, reduced operating costs, lower depreciation, higher resale values, and lower risk. Developers may benefit if owners are willing to pay more for green buildings, though this must be weighed against higher construction costs.

A pro forma cash-flow example shows how green building features may affect potential income, vacancy, operating expenses, capital expenditures, resale price, cap rates, and discount rates, producing a higher net present value in favorable cases. Empirical studies cited in the lecture find average rent and sale-price premiums for green buildings, but with wide variation; some cases show little or no premium, and operating cost effects are inconclusive. The instructor stresses that green building economics vary by project, market, skill, technology, supply chain, and building type.

The lecture then discusses market failures. Information asymmetry can prevent buyers or tenants from recognizing green building benefits, reducing willingness to pay and discouraging developers from supplying greener buildings. A study in China found that residents of green buildings had higher willingness to pay, while residents of non-green buildings increased their willingness to pay after receiving information. The instructor also discusses greenwashing, where developers market buildings as green without credible performance or certification. Certification systems such as LEED are presented as a way to reduce information asymmetry and support market trust.

The passage argues that learning assessment is well established in credit-bearing higher education but remains limited in noncredit continuing education, despite the prevalence and demand for such programs. Noncredit continuing education includes licensure-related professional education, career skill development, and personal enrichment, and often serves learners with varied motivations and backgrounds.

The authors recommend using assessment to improve curriculum, pedagogy, and learning outcomes. They emphasize creating clear, measurable, realistic learning outcomes based on program duration, learner background, instructor collaboration, and SMART criteria. They suggest that surveys, commonly used for satisfaction and marketing feedback, can also include learning outcome-focused questions, including retrospective pre-post items, while noting that these reflect learner perceptions rather than direct evidence.

For direct assessment, the authors propose practical methods suited to short and medium-length programs, such as adding quiz-type questions to end-of-course surveys, using simple two-point scoring, observing learner performance, and evaluating learner-created products. They stress the importance of validity, fairness, transparency, and designing assessments that produce useful work for learners. The passage concludes that well-crafted outcomes, learning-focused surveys, and direct assessments are feasible in noncredit education and can support course improvement, credentialing, personnel decisions, and resource requests.

BG Group agreed to buy Enron’s offshore Indian oil and gas assets for $388 million, including 30% stakes in the Tapti gas field and Panna/Mukta oil and gas fields and a 62.64% interest in the CB-OS/1 exploration block. The assets have more than 170 million barrels of oil equivalent in reserves and produce about 20,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. Analysts described the price as favorable, though the deal requires Indian government approval and agreement from partners on BG taking over operatorship.

The sale is part of Enron’s retreat from physical assets in India, while it continues trying to exit the Dabhol Power Project, where it holds a 65% stake. Dabhol has faced payment disputes with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board, shutdowns, and a reported $24 million interest-payment default to Indian lenders for phase II.

Other Enron mentions include a stock-market rally in which Enron shares rose 9.4%, Southern California Edison owing nearly $4 billion to power companies including Enron, and former Enron Energy Services vice chairman Thomas White being named the Defense Department’s liaison for homeland security.

The lecture concludes Markov chains and introduces dynamic programming. It reviews eigenvalues and eigenvectors for Markov chains with transient and recurrent states, showing that for block upper diagonal transition matrices, the eigenvalues are the combined eigenvalues of the transient and recurrent submatrices, while transition terms from transient to recurrent states do not affect them. The result extends to multiple recurrent classes, and left eigenvectors for recurrent classes can be embedded with zeros.

The lecture then introduces rewards or costs associated with Markov chain states, focusing on expected rewards and aggregate rewards over time. For ergodic unit chains, long-run expected reward per step converges to a steady-state gain independent of the starting state, while transient effects depend on the initial state.

A first-passage-time problem is formulated as a reward problem by assigning unit reward until a chosen state is reached, then modifying that state into a trapping state with zero reward. This allows expected first passage times to be found by solving linear equations.

Dynamic programming is presented as an algorithm for decision-based Markov processes where each action determines both an immediate reward and transition probabilities. Unlike stationary policies, dynamic programming optimizes finite-horizon decisions by working backward from the final reward. The optimal expected reward for each state and horizon is computed recursively by maximizing immediate reward plus expected future reward. The lecture ends by noting that renewal processes will be covered next.

The application describes information sending and reception methods, apparatuses, communication nodes, and a storage medium for communication systems, particularly high-frequency or millimeter-wave systems where maximum power exposure (MPE) affects uplink transmission. A first communication node sends report information to a second communication node; the report includes first type power parameter information and/or uplink channel state information. The second communication node receives the report and schedules the first communication node, enabling determination of maximum power reduction and reducing exposure impact on the human body.

The power parameter information may include maximum power reduction, remaining energy, accumulated energy, uplink duty cycle information, alert identification, power backoff, or power headroom. Uplink channel state information may include reference signal information, antenna group information, uplink path loss, quasi co-location information, quasi co-location beam information, or an uplink corrected value. Antenna group information may refer to a beam group, antenna port group, antenna panel, panel, or reference signal resource group.

The methods support associating or determining power parameters based on antenna groups, reference signals, or transmission parameters. Reports may be periodic, semi-persistent, or aperiodic, and may be triggered by thresholds, parameter variations, timers, signaling, or configuration information. Power headroom may include real or virtual power headroom and may be associated with uplink power control parameters, spatial relations, antenna groups, uplink reference signals, or downlink reference signals.

The second communication node may configure report information, windows for energy calculation, and enabling information for maximum power reduction or uplink reporting. The application also provides corresponding sending and reception apparatuses, first and second communication nodes with processors and storage, and a storage medium storing programs for implementing the methods.

The power play is a gap run scheme featuring a backside guard pull, a kick-out block, and back blocks to create angles at the point of attack. It is widely used across personnel groups and formations because it creates double teams, leverage, and numbers near the running back’s path. Vertical double teams suit stronger offensive lines, while horizontal combinations can help undersized lines.

Its main weakness is backside pursuit and penetration, especially through the gap vacated by the pulling guard. Against even fronts, the backside edge defender can disrupt the play if not slowed by the tackle. Against odd fronts, an incorrect center point call can leave a backside rusher unblocked.

The passage outlines common blocking assignments for power against 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, including the pulling guard targeting the playside inside linebacker, the fullback kicking out the end man, and the tailback staying on the pulling guard’s inside hip. Variations include Diamond Fullhouse power, with adjusted F and U responsibilities, and gun same-side Power RPO, which pairs the run with quarterback throw options based on defensive alignment.

Dairylea Cooperative appealed an order denying its application to quash a subpoena duces tecum issued by the New York Attorney-General for a grand jury investigation. Dairylea argued the Attorney-General lacked authority and that the subpoena was overly burdensome. The lower court accepted only the burden argument, after the subpoena’s scope was limited, and denied relief. The appellate court held the appeal was permissible and found that a sufficient request had been made by the Commissioner of Agriculture and Markets under Executive Law § 63(3). The order was affirmed without costs.

Bill Purswell was convicted in Liberty County of unlawfully transporting intoxicating liquor and sentenced to one year in the penitentiary. Officers hiding in a field near McElvain’s home during a social gathering saw Purswell carrying a jug that contained whiskey and arrested him without a warrant. Purswell objected that the arrest and evidence were illegal because the officers had no arrest or search warrant.

The court held that any complaint about an illegal search of McElvain’s premises was personal to the owner or possessor of those premises and unavailable to Purswell. It also held that officers may arrest without a warrant when a felony is committed in their presence, and that the evidence supported admission of the officers’ testimony and the jug. A general objection to the jury charge was insufficient because exceptions must be specific. The conviction was affirmed.

On rehearing, Purswell claimed the jury considered his failure to testify, but his own affidavit was unsupported by juror affidavits or other evidence. Because the record stated evidence was heard on the motion for new trial but that evidence was not brought forward, the court presumed the trial court’s ruling was justified. Rehearing was denied.

South Dakota’s Board of Regents directed staff and university officials to prepare a plan for closing Pierre’s Capital University Center, with the proposal due at the Oct. 3-5 meeting at Dakota State University.

Firefly Aerospace shares fell nearly 21% after its Alpha Flight 7 rocket exploded during a first-stage test at its Briggs, Texas, facility. The company said safety protocols were followed, personnel were safe, and no other facilities were impacted. Firefly went public last month, raising $868 million at a $6.3 billion valuation, but its stock has since fallen more than 50%.

An email chain forwards a Texas Monthly article titled “How Enron Blew It,” about Enron’s rise, culture, and troubles in 2001. The article describes Enron’s transformation from a pipeline company into a major energy trading firm under Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling, driven by deregulation, the Gas Bank concept, aggressive trading, and expansion into electricity, broadband, commodities, and online trading.

It portrays Enron’s culture as intensely competitive, youth-oriented, risk-taking, and focused on rapid profits, with lavish recruiting, high bonuses, and a harsh performance review system known as “rank and yank.” The article argues that this culture helped fuel growth but also encouraged internal competition, short-term thinking, secrecy, and weak loyalty.

The article details tensions between Skilling’s asset-light trading model and older asset-heavy businesses, including Rebecca Mark’s international projects and Azurix, which struggled after its IPO. It also describes Enron’s problems in 2001: criticism during California’s energy crisis, the troubled Dabhol project in India, the collapse of telecommunications and broadband hopes, scrutiny of accounting practices, negative press, falling stock prices, and analyst concerns.

Skilling resigned after six months as CEO, citing personal reasons and dissatisfaction with the job’s demands, while Lay returned as CEO and promised a more focused and gentler Enron.

Enron-related news on Oct. 29, 2001 focused on falling shares, credit concerns, and scrutiny of its partnerships. Moody’s downgraded Enron’s senior unsecured debt to Baa2, two notches above junk, and kept ratings under review, citing reduced financial flexibility after write-downs and equity charges tied to previously undisclosed partnerships. Enron said it was seeking additional bank credit after drawing about $3 billion to $3.3 billion from credit lines and buying back commercial paper. Analysts said lenders may demand harsher terms, collateral, higher interest rates, or asset-sale proceeds for debt repayment.

Enron shares fell to multi-year lows after losing more than half their value in roughly two weeks, amid SEC scrutiny of related-party transactions involving former CFO Andrew Fastow. European energy firms reportedly became wary of trading with Enron or restricted dealings due to credit concerns. Dow Jones articles questioned Enron’s asset-light strategy, disclosure practices, talent retention, and broadband-related transactions, while noting multiple shareholder lawsuits over partnerships and alleged conflicts of interest. A separate Moody’s report said U.S. corporate credit quality was worsening broadly, with downgrades expected to outnumber upgrades.

The passage describes LTE, LTE-Advanced carrier aggregation, MAC/RRC/physical-layer functions, uplink scheduling, semi-persistent scheduling, and ProSe/D2D sidelink communication as background for vehicular V2X services. It explains that V2X communication may use sidelink resources for V2V, V2P, V2I, and V2N services, including periodic Cooperative Awareness Messages and event-triggered notifications. For UE-autonomous sidelink resource allocation, sensing and resource reservation are used so devices can avoid resources reserved by others.

The disclosure proposes an improved autonomous radio resource allocation procedure for sidelink data transmission. A transmitting device continuously performs resource sensing before data arrives, including monitoring scheduling assignments from other devices and optionally measuring received signal energy. Because a device cannot sense while transmitting, some sensing opportunities may be missed. When data becomes available, the device selects resources within a transmission window using sensing results from a prior sensing window. Subframes in the transmission window are classified as primary if all corresponding sensing information was obtained, and secondary if sensing information is incomplete due to prior transmissions. The device preferably selects resources in primary subframes over secondary subframes.

Resource candidates may be ranked separately for primary and secondary subframes using factors such as transmission delay and predicted energy, with shorter delay and lower predicted energy preferred. If no suitable resources are available, preemption of reserved resources may be considered. The disclosure also applies similar sensing, ranking, reservation, and primary/secondary subframe selection principles to scheduling assignment transmissions, including scheduling assignments that indicate resources reserved for later scheduling assignments or data.

The passage argues that Arctic security should be understood as a complex, interconnected system shaped by environmental, geopolitical, economic, and sociocultural factors. Climate change, shifting political interests, resource development, shipping, Indigenous governance, and military activity interact in ways that can create cascading effects, as illustrated by the Nome port expansion. Because decisions in one domain may affect others, Arctic security education should move beyond siloed, linear approaches.

Systems thinking is presented as an educational framework for identifying system components, understanding interactions, recognizing feedback loops, and anticipating second- and third-order consequences. It emphasizes holistic analysis, pattern recognition, leverage points, interdisciplinary learning, and long-term, adaptive decision-making. Compared with traditional methods, systems thinking uses integrated learning, nonlinear problem-solving, broad stakeholder inclusion, scenario-based application, and attention to indirect consequences.

The passage proposes integrating systems thinking into Arctic security curricula through interdisciplinary content, scenario-based learning, simulations, wargaming, role-playing, stakeholder exercises, concept mapping, and interactive case studies. Assessment should emphasize applied competencies such as strategic foresight, adaptability, interdisciplinary analysis, reflective reasoning, and scenario-based problem-solving rather than only theoretical knowledge.

A Systems Thinking Education Model is described with three components: core principles, leverage points, and learning and assessment strategies. Leverage points include shifting mental models, improving information flows, adapting governance structures, encouraging behavioral and operational shifts, and using technology responsibly. The model is presented as especially suitable for online graduate education through asynchronous learning, simulations, multimedia case studies, discussion forums, concept mapping, reflective exercises, and collaborative interdisciplinary projects.

The passage concludes that systems thinking can help Arctic security professionals anticipate unintended consequences, address interdependencies, and develop sustainable, adaptive strategies for a rapidly changing and contested region.

The passage identifies “special” five-minute periods in soccer matches when goals are reportedly scored more often, including the start of each half, after goals or penalty events, after dangerous fouls, before halftime, near the end of matches, and around extra time. It urges coaches to prepare players to exploit or defend during these moments. Suggested causes are psychological, such as excitement, lack of readiness, complacency, anger, urgency, or defensive caution. The passage emphasizes avoiding emotional letdowns after goals, whether from overconfidence after scoring or discouragement after conceding, and recommends reminders such as “No letdown!”

Q3 2025 commentary says anticipated municipal credit challenges have arrived, highlighted by the government shutdown, though munis remain a very safe, flight-to-quality asset class. The Fed lowered short-term rates in September amid slowing job growth and mixed inflation. Many municipalities received upgrades due to better-funded reserves. The passage also includes David Kotok’s biography and lists related investment articles and municipal bond ETFs.

Newcomers to Canada can improve their job search by building networks early, searching online before arriving, using free career workshops, pursuing internships or volunteer roles, checking whether credentials need updating, and improving English or French proficiency through language courses or associations. Preparation can help candidates navigate an unfamiliar labour market more effectively.

Treetops is a Keynsham care home for elderly people with dementia, offering family-sized units, communal areas, individual support, care planning with families, a support group, named carers, and organised activities inside and outside the home.

Lorna Gibson introduces a course on cellular materials: porous materials with typically less than 30% solid volume. The course will cover honeycombs, foams, medical materials such as trabecular bone and tissue engineering scaffolds, and natural cellular materials including wood, cork, bamboo, plant tissues, shells, skulls, and quills. It will examine processing, structure, modeling, deformation, failure, stiffness, strength, fracture toughness, energy absorption, thermal insulation, sandwich panels, and material selection.

The course begins with honeycombs because their repeating unit cells are easier to analyze, then moves to foams and applications of mechanical models to bone, scaffolds, energy absorption, and lightweight panels. Students will complete open-ended projects in pairs on cellular materials; past examples include negative Poisson’s ratio honeycombs, osteoporosis, elephant skull sound transmission, tissue engineering scaffolds, and food foams.

Examples of engineering cellular solids include aluminum, paper resin, ceramic, polymer, metal, glass, carbon, and food foams. Honeycombs may be used in sandwich panels and catalytic converters, while foams are useful for low weight, energy absorption, thermal insulation, and catalyst support. Open-cell and closed-cell structures, anisotropic cell shapes, and 3-D lattice materials will also be discussed.

Medical examples include trabecular bone, osteoporosis-related density loss, micro-CT imaging of bone deformation, porous coatings for orthopedic implants, and tissue engineering scaffolds designed to mimic extracellular matrix. The lecture also describes studies of cell contraction, attachment, and migration on scaffolds.

Natural cellular materials include wood, cork, parenchyma in plants, sponge structures, leaf and skull sandwich structures, bamboo and palm density gradients, and plant stems or animal quills with cellular cores that resist buckling. Cork’s corrugated cells are linked to its zero Poisson’s ratio in one direction.

The lecture then begins processing methods. Honeycombs can be made by expansion, corrugation, extrusion, 3-D printing, selective laser curing, casting, or bio-carbon templating from wood. Polymer foams are made by introducing gas bubbles through mechanical stirring or blowing agents and stabilizing them by crosslinking or cooling; syntactic and structural foams are also described. Metal foams can be made by stirring gas into molten aluminum with silicon carbide, using titanium hydride powders, replicating polymer foams, vapor deposition, entrapped gas expansion, hollow spheres, or fugitive phases. Gibson concludes with a brief account of her education and career path from civil engineering to cellular materials research.

Trump’s meeting with Trudeau eased concerns about US-Canada trade, with Trump saying issues were less severe than with Mexico and suggesting tweaks rather than an overhaul. USD/CAD fell to 1.3060 despite lower crude prices. Markets awaited Yellen’s testimony, China CPI and PPI data, and a Kuroda speech amid speculation on yield curve control.

An American Soccer Player’s Creed outlines conduct for players: maintain awareness of the ball, communicate with teammates and coaches, play intelligently and aggressively without fouling, support the team, respect opponents and referees, learn from mistakes, know the Laws of the Game, and demonstrate fair play and sportsmanship.

Supreme Court justices debated whether Delaware procedures limiting medical malpractice lawsuits should apply in federal court. Justices Elena Kagan, Ketanji Brown Jackson, and Sonia Sotomayor questioned the rules, arguing they conflict with the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure by requiring plaintiffs to meet additional steps before a case proceeds. Frederick Yarger, representing the defendants, argued federal courts need not disregard an entire state statute if only parts conflict with federal rules. Justice Neil Gorsuch questioned whether courts could selectively apply parts of Delaware law without effectively rewriting it. The passage notes that Chief Justice John Roberts and Justices Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito said little, making the likely outcome unclear. Several justices appeared ready to reject Delaware’s procedures, but the court’s overall position remained uncertain.

Blair school district voters narrowly rejected a $250,000 transportation bond for three buses, with 58.76% approval, short of the required 60%. Area elections also decided municipal and school board races, including wins by John Womack and Jon Kidwell in Altus, Roberta Ellis in Walters, and several school board candidates across Southwest Oklahoma.

The DAWN-PLASMA study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 multicenter trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of convalescent plasma plus standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. The study followed Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines, with protocol and consent approval by Independent Ethics Committees.

The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary endpoints included clinical status at Days 15 and 30, time to sustained clinical improvement or discharge, mechanical ventilation or death at 30 and 90 days, thromboembolism, transfusion-related effects, antibody titer correlations, safety, quality of life, adverse events, laboratory data, and vital signs.

Eligible participants were adults with informed consent, confirmed or clinically supported SARS-CoV-2 infection, illness with radiographic or clinical respiratory involvement, and known ABO D typing. Exclusions included mechanical ventilation before or at randomization, unacceptable safety risks, severe allergic reaction to plasma, treatment restrictions excluding ventilation or intubation, and recent anti-CD20 therapy.

Participants were randomized 2:1 to convalescent plasma plus standard care or standard care alone. Plasma recipients received 800–1000 mL in four doses, with the first two units administered within 12 hours after randomization and the second two units 24–36 hours later. Plasma with neutralizing antibody titers below 1/160 was not allowed.

Five patients withdrew before intervention and one was a screen failure; all six were substituted. No patients were lost to follow-up after intervention. Data were collected in RedCap, monitored by the sponsor, and analyzed according to a statistical analysis plan finalized on 27 October 2020.

Bank of Canada senior deputy governor Carolyn Wilkins said Canada’s high household debt relative to disposable income should gradually stabilize as credit growth slows and labour income rises. The household debt ratio was 170.4 per cent in late 2017, slightly below its peak. Wilkins noted debt accumulation took years and will take time to unwind, while asset purchases have raised net worth. Governor Stephen Poloz said high debt has made households more sensitive to interest rate changes.

The paper examines website usability for e-business portals in Saudi Arabia, an emerging online market with growing e-commerce activity. It focuses on whether Saudi e-business websites support positive customer experiences and identifies design issues affecting users. A cross-sectional evaluation was conducted with two student groups trained in user interface evaluation: 26 participants assessed retail websites, and 39 assessed reservation websites. Eight websites were evaluated, and participants completed a questionnaire covering navigation, design, and content.

Findings showed generally positive ratings but also recurring usability weaknesses. Navigation issues included weak internal navigation, sitemap problems, orphan pages, and links affecting menu visibility. Design issues included inconsistent language interfaces, font-size consistency, layout simplicity, icon labeling, and menu highlighting. Content-related weaknesses included missing contact information, lack of sitemap, weak ordering, and absence of last update dates. Reliability testing showed Cronbach Alpha values of 0.66 for group 1 and 0.79 for group 2, with converging results across both groups.

The study concludes that Saudi e-business portals should improve navigation, interface language consistency, layout, icon labeling, contact information, and update details to enhance user satisfaction, engagement, acquisition, and retention. It notes limitations in sample size and website coverage and recommends further qualitative and long-term quantitative studies.
The speaker says their team must battle to the net, get pucks in scoring areas, shoot high on a big goalie, and regroup after a disappointing loss to start strong and score first.

The passage outlines basketball strategies for attacking defensive pressure and breaking presses. Teams should anticipate presses, spread the floor, use short crisp passes, work the ball through the middle, attack outnumbered situations, and maintain defensive balance. Players should avoid careless dribbling, one-handed or lob passes, sideline traps, telegraphed passes, and rushed decisions. Effective press breaks rely on teamwork, defined roles, precise execution, spacing, timing, and regular practice. Coaches should teach press breaks using the Whole-Part-Whole method, progressive drills, live defensive practice, and scouting. Objectives include building poise, advancing the ball under control, attacking double teams, flowing into early offense, and preparing for defensive pressure on every possession.

In a May 1980 interview, Ronald Reagan questioned President Carter’s response to the failed Iran hostage rescue mission and discussed concerns about Soviet influence in Iran, calling any Iranian move toward the Soviet camp a serious threat to the Middle East, U.S. security, and allies. On July 17, 1980, Reagan accepted the Republican presidential nomination in Detroit, emphasizing peace through strength, national security, readiness to negotiate, and resistance to threats against freedom. In another address, he told veterans that those who had experienced war understood that peace was preserved not by weakness but by maintaining adequate defense capability.

The study investigates coherent control of three nearest-neighbor 15N nuclear spins adjacent to negatively charged boron vacancy (V−B) centers in isotopically enriched h10B15N. Using pulsed electron-nuclear double resonance, the authors selectively address four nuclear spin states arising from the three spin-1/2 nitrogen nuclei. Hyperfine-mediated electron-nuclear mixing lifts transition degeneracies, creates distinct nuclear resonance transitions, and enhances the effective nuclear g-factor by about 116 compared with isolated 15N spins.

Experiments show narrow nuclear resonance linewidths, magnetic-field-dependent transition energies, coherent nuclear Rabi oscillations, and Rabi coherence times exceeding 10 µs, longer than the V−B electron spin coherence time. Optical pumping unexpectedly causes rapid nuclear spin depolarization within about 1 µs, tentatively attributed to relaxation through the optically excited triplet state.

The results show that strongly coupled 15N nuclear spins near V−B centers in hBN can serve as controllable quantum resources for nuclear-assisted dynamics, quantum memories, and quantum sensing in integrated two-dimensional platforms.

The Pennsylvania Supreme Court affirmed the Commonwealth Court, holding that Act 109 is constitutional and enforceable as applied to nonsectarian nonpublic schools. The court concluded that Lemon v. Kurtzman invalidated Act 109 only as applied to sectarian schools, that the Act is severable, that later legislation did not impliedly repeal it, and that determining whether a school is sectarian or nonsectarian does not create excessive entanglement with religion under the First Amendment.

Amid Jake Browning’s inconsistent play for the Bengals in place of Joe Burrow, former Cincinnati starter Andy Dalton has been mentioned as a speculative trade option. Dalton, now with the Panthers, previously played under Zac Taylor in 2019 and is signed through 2026. Browning has 506 passing yards, three touchdowns and five interceptions through three games, raising concerns about Cincinnati’s quarterback stability.

Tesla, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2018. The company reported total revenue of $3.41 billion, up from $2.70 billion in the same period of 2017, and a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $709.6 million, compared with $330.3 million in 2017. Total assets were $27.27 billion, total liabilities were $21.55 billion, and cash and cash equivalents were $2.67 billion. Net cash used in operating activities was $398.4 million, and net cash used in investing activities was $728.6 million.

Tesla adopted the new ASC 606 revenue standard on January 1, 2018, resulting in a $623.2 million decrease to beginning accumulated deficit and changes to revenue recognition for certain vehicle sales with resale value guarantees. The company operates in two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. It reported customer deposits of $984.8 million, inventory of $2.57 billion, property, plant and equipment of $10.52 billion, and total debt of $10.47 billion. Tesla stated it was in compliance with all financial debt covenants as of March 31, 2018.

Socket 940 uses LCP base and cover rated UL 94 V-0, with black base and natural or ivory cover. Cover thickness must not exceed 1.17 mm and flatness must remain under 0.25 mm before and after reflow, environmental, and mechanical testing. A removable overlay supports vacuum pick-and-place and must not outgas or leave residue. Required markings include “SOCKET 940,” lock/unlock indicators, pin A01 orientation symbol, UL symbol, and lot traceability.

Contacts use high-strength copper alloy with nickel plating and gold on mating areas; no lubricants are allowed on mating areas. SMT solder balls are 63/37 ±5% tin-lead, 0.76 mm diameter, used with 0.64 mm PCB pads, and must meet 0.20 mm co-planarity. A solder barrier must prevent wicking.

A stainless steel lever actuates the socket. Open-position insertion/extraction forces must not exceed 2 kgf; closed-position extraction must be at least 0.013 kgf per pin. Lever actuation/de-actuation force must be under 3.6 kgf, and pin displacement under 1.0 mm. The socket must survive 50 actuation cycles.

Visual requirements prohibit defective solder balls, contacts, cover/base cracks or flashing, damaged tabs or latch, gaps, and damaged or missing levers. Electrical requirements include 1.5 A per contact with under 30°C rise, LLCR not exceeding 25 mΩ initially or after testing, inductance and capacitance limits, 100 Ω ±10% differential impedance, propagation delay skew under 10 ps plus measurement error, 650 Vac dielectric withstand voltage, and 1000 MΩ minimum insulation resistance.

The passage describes the 2018 ebook edition of the 1906 Foreign Relations of the United States volume, noting its searchable, portable format and citation guidance. It then presents part of the President’s annual message, citing unprecedented prosperity, urging Congress to ban corporate campaign contributions, and advocating a government right of appeal in criminal cases involving legal questions.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2016. The company designs, develops, manufactures and sells fully electric vehicles and energy products, with subsidiaries in North America, Europe and Asia. As of July 29, 2016, it had 148,692,605 common shares outstanding.

For the quarter ended June 30, 2016, Tesla reported total revenue of $1.27 billion, up from $955.0 million a year earlier, driven mainly by higher vehicle deliveries and Model X introduction. Automotive revenue was $1.18 billion, while services and other revenue was $88.2 million. Gross profit was $274.8 million, and gross margin declined to 21.6% from 22.3%. Net loss was $293.2 million, compared with $184.2 million in the prior-year quarter. For the six months ended June 30, 2016, total revenue was $2.42 billion and net loss was $575.5 million.

As of June 30, 2016, Tesla had $11.87 billion in total assets, including $3.25 billion in cash and cash equivalents, and $9.31 billion in total liabilities. Inventory was $1.61 billion. Stockholders’ equity was $2.52 billion. Net cash used in operating activities for the first six months of 2016 was $99.3 million, while financing activities provided $2.69 billion, including $1.7 billion from a May 2016 common stock offering.

Tesla was producing and selling Model S and Model X, had unveiled Model 3 in the first quarter of 2016, and continued selling Powerwall and Powerpack energy products. In the second quarter, it produced 18,345 vehicles, including about 6,200 Model X vehicles, and planned approximately 50,000 deliveries in the second half of 2016. It targeted overall vehicle production of 500,000 vehicles in 2018.

Tesla planned approximately $2.25 billion in 2016 capital expenditures, including Model 3 production lines, Gigafactory equipment, retail and service locations, and Supercharger expansion. As of June 30, 2016, it had incurred $430.7 million of Gigafactory costs and operated 661 Supercharger locations globally.

On July 31, 2016, Tesla entered into an agreement to acquire SolarCity Corporation, subject to stockholder and regulatory approvals. Subsequent to June 30, 2016, it received conversion notices for about $411 million principal value of 2018 convertible notes, expected to be paid in the third quarter of 2016.

Bill Belichick accepted responsibility after North Carolina’s 38–10 loss to Clemson, citing early defensive breakdowns, penalties, poor third-down execution and offensive struggles. He declined to assess the rebuild but said the team would keep working and praised its effort despite the defeat.

The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, with AVDD powering internal circuits and DVDD supporting the digital interface. AVDD should be decoupled to AGND with at least 10µF and 1µF capacitors per supply, with the 1µF capacitor placed close to the pins; DVDD should have a nearby minimum 10µF decoupling capacitor to support digital switching current and improve PSRR.

The device supports NAP and power-down modes to reduce power consumption at lower throughput. NAP mode is enabled by unlocking RST_PWRCTL_REG and setting NAP_EN, with wakeup triggered by a CONVST/CS falling edge after tNAP_WKUP. Power-down mode is enabled by setting PWRDN; analog blocks power down while the interface and registers remain active, and wakeup requires clearing PWRDN and waiting tPWRUP.

PCB layout guidance includes separating analog and digital sections, keeping analog and reference signals away from digital noise, using clean and well-bypassed supplies, minimizing vias between supply pins and capacitors, and connecting grounds with short, low-impedance paths. REFCAP requires 1µF and 10µF capacitors close to the pins, and REFIO requires at least 4.7µF if the internal reference is used. The passage also lists related TI documentation, update and support resources, trademark and ESD cautions, revision history, packaging information, and TI disclaimers.

The passage argues that Russia denies responsibility for the poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal, despite British claims that Russia continued producing and stockpiling Novichok. It cites Russian officials’ denials and suggestions of alternative blame, then calls for stronger Western sanctions targeting assets held by Vladimir Putin’s associates and closing loopholes that enable Russian money-laundering.

The article investigates symmetry-protected braiding of topological edge-state pairs in coupled SSH chains. A double-coupled SSH system is used to show twisted edge-state spectra, Abelian braiding, and adiabatic transport protected by inversion symmetry and time-dependent interchain symmetry. This enables a particle initially localized at one chain end to transfer to two ends of another chain with a tunable ratio set by an accumulated dynamical phase.

The study then extends the model to triple-coupled SSH chains, where three edge-state pairs exhibit non-Abelian braiding. Different braiding sequences produce different final chains, demonstrating operation-order-dependent topological transport. For two identical bosons, the system realizes non-Abelian Hong-Ou-Mandel interference and generates spatial NOON states whose output chain depends on the braiding sequence. The authors also discuss possible implementation in adiabatically modulated photonic waveguide arrays.

Clark County schools are deciding individually how to spend new Nevada weighted funding for students learning English or living in poverty who score in the bottom 25 percent on state tests and do not attend schools receiving Zoom or Victory funds. Garside Junior High in Las Vegas will receive more than $450,000 for 378 eligible students. Teacher Kimberly Ivanick said the money could expand after-school tutoring and provide more technology to support English learners. The state allocated $36 million, with more than $34 million going to Clark County schools, and spending will be tracked to assess effects on student achievement.

Since becoming Speedy chief executive in 2015 after a profit warning, Russell Down has refocused the company on customers, cost control, product availability and asset utilisation. Speedy had faced unreliable asset data after an IT upgrade, declining revenue from reduced attention to smaller customers, and equipment backlogs caused by moving testing and repairs to regional super stores. Recent half-year results showed profits rising 58.8% to £10.8m, lower net debt and improved ROCE. Down has worked to rebuild stakeholder confidence, improve staff engagement, introduce customer surveys, and revive the “Speedy spirit.” The company is now pursuing organic growth and acquisitions, including Prolift Access and Platform Sales & Hire, to expand its powered access offering and support more customer demand through its own fleet.

Mastitis is the dairy industry’s costliest disease, with clinical cases costing farmers over $400 and reducing cow comfort and future milk production. It is usually treated with antibiotics, but antibiotics do not repair mammary tissue damaged by bacterial inflammation. Cornell researchers Gerlinde Van de Walle and Daryl Nydam studied secretions from bovine mammary stem cells as a possible alternative therapy. Their Scientific Reports paper found these secreted factors may support tissue healing, blood vessel formation and cell migration, protect epithelial cells from bacterial toxins, and provide antimicrobial effects. The factors were especially effective against toxins from gram-negative bacteria, which are often harder to treat and less responsive to current FDA-approved intramammary antimicrobials than gram-positive bacteria. The researchers plan to test whether the stem cell secretome works in cows with mastitis.

Hyundai Motor and Kia Motors installed a V2X vehicle-road communication system on a 14-kilometer road section with seven intersections in Hwaseong to support autonomous driving research. The system enables real-time information exchange among vehicles, roads, signals and pedestrians using relay stations and CCTVs. The companies will collect data through year-end to improve the system for a 2020 government infrastructure project.

The message transmits to the Senate a treaty for the annexation of the Hawaiian Islands, concluded on February 14, 1893, between U.S. and Hawaiian provisional government representatives. It states that the treaty leaves detailed annexation questions for future adjustment by the United States. The Administration says it had supported Hawaiian independence while stable, denies promoting the monarchy’s overthrow, and attributes events to Queen Liliuokalani’s policies and the weakness of her government. It argues that restoring the Queen would be undesirable and disruptive, and that the United States must increase its influence. The message presents annexation, rather than a protectorate, as best for Hawaiians and necessary for U.S. interests, urging prompt Senate action and future legislation protecting residents’ rights.

Caitlin Bassett says the build-up to Sunshine Coast Lightning’s Super Netball grand final against Greater Western Sydney is unlike anything in her career. The fortnight wait brought nerves but let her absorb the occasion. Teammates Geva Mentor and Laura Langman have helped prepare her, while Mentor has trained against tall men’s player Junior Levi to prepare for the Giants’ attack.
