The passage explains the Relative Strength Index (RSI), an oscillator developed by Welles Wilder in 1978 to measure gains and losses over a chosen period and identify overbought or oversold market conditions. RSI ranges from 0 to 100, with low readings treated as more bullish and high readings as more bearish in mean-reverting strategies.

The article states that RSI works best on stocks and stock indices, especially mean-reverting securities, and performs worse on other assets such as forex and some commodity-related stocks. It emphasizes that RSI should be backtested and combined with filters, variables, or other indicators rather than used alone.

Backtests discussed include a 2-day RSI strategy on SPY buying below 15 and selling above 85, which performed slightly worse than buy-and-hold but with less market exposure and lower drawdown. A 10-day RSI strategy performed worse. The passage states that shorter RSI settings, often below five days, have worked best in the authors’ tests. A QQQ backtest produced about 300 trades, a 0.82% average gain per trade, a 71% win rate, and a 23% maximum drawdown.

The passage also discusses RSI divergences, multiple time-frame RSI strategies, RSI 14 versus RSI 21, Connors RSI, Cutler’s RSI, and the use of RSI in day trading. It concludes that RSI is most useful on daily bars, with short lookback periods, stocks, and additional confirmation tools.

The passage explains how coaches can introduce offensive corner kicks to young soccer players. A corner kick is awarded when the defending team sends the ball completely over its own end line, and it gives the attacking team a set-play opportunity near goal. Coaches should teach the basic elements of Law 17, including ball placement in the nearest corner arc, defenders staying 10 yards away, the kicker not touching the ball again until another player does, and not removing the corner flag.

The recommended progression includes demonstrating proper corner-kick technique, practicing right- and left-footed kicks from both corners, introducing a simple play with a corner taker, receiver, and cover man, rotating players through all positions, then assigning specific players and adding defenders. The sample play has the corner taker pass to a receiver, who turns toward goal while the corner taker and cover man move into supporting positions. Coaches are advised to practice different options, add realism with defenders, introduce more passing choices as players improve, and remind players to wait for the referee’s signal before taking kicks in games.

The passage argues that Landor v. Louisiana Department of Corrections and Public Safety, though a technical RLUIPA remedies case, is an important religious-freedom dispute. Damon Landor, a Rastafarian prisoner, alleges officials violated his rights by shaving his dreadlocks despite precedent protecting his religious exercise. The author contends RLUIPA should allow money damages and predicts Landor will win. The passage also criticizes common narratives that Supreme Court religious-freedom cases are mainly partisan, majority-serving, or culture-war driven, emphasizing unanimous rulings and protections for diverse religious minorities.

San Diego police pursued a wanted shooting suspect in City Heights after he fled a traffic stop attempt. The chase ended when he crashed into fences at Central Elementary School and a fire station. Police said he fled armed with a gun and was arrested nearby.

The passage lists 1945 presidential and State Department documents and summarizes postwar changes in U.S. foreign policy administration. It notes leadership changes including Stettinius’s resignation, Byrnes becoming Secretary of State, Grew’s resignation, Acheson becoming Under Secretary, Hurley’s resignation, and Marshall’s appointment as envoy to China. It also records Hull receiving the Nobel Peace Prize. Additional duties assigned to the State Department included international information functions from wartime agencies and research/intelligence functions from the abolished Office of Strategic Services, with Truman directing State to lead development of a coordinated foreign intelligence program.

A retrospective analytical study examined traumatic brain injury (TBI) risk factors in 671 patients treated at a republic hospital from 07/01/2017 to 17/12/2018. The sample included 459 men and 212 women, with a mean age of 46.016 years. Most patients lived in the city, while 21.90% lived in villages. Domestic accidents were the most frequent cause of TBI overall and in both sexes, affecting 294 patients, including 172 men and 122 women. Other causes included alcohol-related injury, motor vehicle injury, criminal injury, work injury, convulsive syndrome, postoperative haematoma, sports injury, and unknown causes.

Men were affected at a younger mean age than women and had longer hospitalization than women. Patients living in villages were reported to have increased TBI risk, and older age was directly correlated with longer hospitalization. Conservative therapy was required in most cases, while 198 patients required surgical treatment, most commonly surgical debridement of wounds.

The study concluded that domestic accidents were the most frequently reported cause of TBI in both men and women, men were affected earlier in life than women, village residents had increased TBI risk, and gender played an important role in TBI severity, incidence, outcomes, and complications.

Sodium cumenesulfonate is a hydrotrope available in powder and liquid forms that improves solubility, lowers cloud point, promotes ingredient compatibility, and moderates viscosity in aqueous products. It is used in detergents, cleaners, drilling fluids, oilfield applications, metal processing, anti-caking agents, coupling agents, and hydrogen sulfide scavengers. Market demand is expected to be driven by industrialization and household detergent use in emerging economies, while raw material price volatility, health hazards from heavy exposure, and reduced R&D may hinder growth. Liquid form and household applications held major market shares in 2015 and are expected to remain dominant.

U.S. stocks fell about 2% on Monday, led by a technology selloff after reports that Facebook user data was misused by a political consultancy tied to Donald Trump’s campaign. Facebook dropped 7.1%, while other FAANG stocks also declined. The Nasdaq fell 2.09% and the S&P technology index dropped 2.5%. All 11 major S&P sectors were lower, with the S&P 500 down 1.44% and the Dow down 1.23%. Investors also weighed trade-war concerns ahead of a G20 meeting, rising market volatility, political uncertainty and an upcoming Federal Reserve decision, with markets focused on the outlook for interest rate hikes.

Blackwell introduces advanced power management with reduced entry and exit latencies for deep power states, finer-grain clock, power, and rail gating, full memory clock-tree gating, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, and faster low-latency sleep. Its accelerated frequency switching adjusts clocks to dynamic workloads 1000x faster than previous GPU architectures, improving performance and power efficiency. In one small language model inference example, combined performance and power-state improvements produced up to 50% power savings.

DLSS 4 adds Multi Frame Generation, which can generate up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame. Its new frame generation AI model is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and runs once per rendered frame. Blackwell also uses enhanced Flip Metering in the display engine for more precise frame pacing. DLSS 4 transitions from CNN-based models to transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving temporal stability, lighting detail, detail in motion, and reducing artifacts.

Blackwell is designed to support neural shaders, with Tensor Cores accessible through shaders via Cooperative Vectors APIs for DX12 and Vulkan. Neural shader applications include neural texture compression, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. These techniques use neural networks to approximate complex rendering tasks, compress textures, infer lighting, simulate subsurface scattering, and improve real-time facial rendering.

The passage also outlines Blackwell GPU products. GB202 is the flagship GPU with 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores, and a 512-bit memory interface, used for the GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 targets the high-end segment with 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA cores, and a 256-bit memory interface, used for the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 targets the performance segment with 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA cores, and a 192-bit memory interface, used for the RTX 5070. The passage ends with NVIDIA warranty, liability, licensing, trademark, and copyright notices.

Frost Brown Todd and Gibbons plan to merge in January, forming FBT Gibbons with 800 lawyers in 25 offices. The merger expands Frost Brown Todd into the Northeast, including New York and New Jersey. Leaders said the initial focus will be integration, though further growth is possible. Robert Sartin will chair the merged firm, while Adam Hall and Peter Torcicollo will serve as co-managing partners. Frost Brown Todd reported $336.5 million in gross revenue, and Gibbons reported $115 million.

Stephen Hawking, the renowned theoretical physicist, has died, his family said. Known for his work on space, time, black holes and the search for a unified theory of physics, Hawking became internationally famous through his best-selling book “A Brief History of Time.” Diagnosed with ALS at 21, he lived with the disease for more than 50 years and later communicated through an electronic voice synthesizer. He held the Lucasian Professorship of Mathematics at Cambridge, appeared in popular television shows, and inspired renewed interest in science. His life was portrayed in the 2014 film “The Theory of Everything,” for which Eddie Redmayne won an Academy Award.

A treaty providing larger annuities and Hawaiian statehood failed after Kamehameha III died in 1855 and his successor opposed the project. A reciprocity treaty negotiated in 1855 also failed ratification. Subsequent correspondence focused mainly on claims and routine matters, while the Civil War delayed renewed treaty efforts. In 1867, U.S. and Hawaiian representatives concluded another reciprocity treaty, approved by the President but not ratified by the Senate. U.S. officials also discussed possible annexation, with Seward advising that annexation should be preferred if it conflicted with reciprocity. The presence of the U.S.S. Lackawanna in Hawaiian waters caused concern for the King and delayed Hawaiian ratification. Hawaii ratified the treaty on July 30, 1867, but the U.S. Senate rejected it on June 1, 1870.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on February 16, 2016, it entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs, Deutsche Bank Securities, J.P. Morgan Securities, and Merrill Lynch for the issuance and sale of multiple floating and fixed rate notes totaling $12 billion, with maturities from 2018 through 2046. The notes are issued under Apple’s April 29, 2013 indenture and Form S-3 registration statement. Floating rate interest is payable quarterly beginning May 23, 2016, and fixed rate interest is payable semiannually beginning August 23, 2016. The notes are senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. The filing includes related exhibits, including the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, forms of notes, legal opinion, earnings-to-fixed-charges computation, and consent. The report was signed February 23, 2016, by CFO Luca Maestri.

The speaker takes the presidential oath, invokes divine guidance, and pledges to preserve the Constitution and Union while not seeking reelection. He emphasizes majority rule, popular sovereignty in the territories, and submission to the Supreme Court on slavery-related questions. He urges an end to slavery agitation, warning it has endangered harmony and the Union. He condemns calculations favoring disunion and stresses the economic and political value of national unity.

He calls for public integrity, warns that treasury surpluses and public land distribution can foster corruption, and supports using surplus revenue for constitutional national purposes such as debt reduction and naval improvement. He favors limited revenue, tariff fairness, settlement of public lands by actual settlers, equality for naturalized citizens, and strict constitutional construction. He argues Congress may fund a military road to protect California and Pacific possessions from invasion.

In foreign affairs, he advocates peace, commerce, friendship, frank diplomacy, respect for national independence, noninterference except for self-preservation, and avoidance of entangling alliances. He states that U.S. territorial acquisitions have been by purchase or voluntary union and should continue only under justice and honor.

Synaptics announced plans to mass produce “Clear ID,” an optical in-display fingerprint sensor embedded under a smartphone screen. The company says it is aimed at bezel-less designs, is twice as fast as 3D facial recognition, requires one touch, and can unlock phones from various angles. Synaptics said consumers prefer front-facing fingerprint authentication, though it remains unclear when the technology will appear in smartphones.

Bemidji defeated Thief River Falls 77-45, improving to 14-6. Caden Rolfes scored 18 points and Linaes Whiting added 17, while Caleb Carlson had 14 and Jeremy Beberg 10. Coach Travis Peterson praised the team’s sustained effort and execution ahead of the section tournament.

Florida State University President John Thrasher appointed a 15-member advisory panel to review campus policies on names, markers, statues and other recognitions amid national debates over Confederate symbols. The committee will be chaired by Renisha Gibbs, associate vice president for human resources and chief diversity officer. Thrasher said the panel should seek input from the FSU community and recommend criteria for naming policies. The review follows calls from Students for a Democratic Society to remove the Francis Eppes statue near the Westcott Building, citing his history as a slave owner and Confederate supporter. The committee will meet next week, with meetings open to the public, and a website will be launched.

The passage describes container design patterns and distributed system patterns. Reusable containers should have clearly defined APIs, including parameters, service calls, and exposed interfaces; even subtle changes to parameter semantics can be breaking changes. Containers should also be documented through Dockerfile directives such as EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL, using shared label schemas where possible.

The sidecar pattern augments an application container with additional functionality, supporting legacy updates and reusable utility containers. The ambassador pattern brokers communication between an application and external services. Examples include routing to sharded Redis or memcached backends with twemproxy, service brokering across environments, and request splitting for experiments using nginx. The adapter pattern modifies an application’s interface to meet expected conventions, such as Prometheus monitoring, normalized logging with fluentd, or richer MySQL health checks without changing the original container.

The passage then introduces multi-node distributed patterns and microservices. Microservices split systems into independently managed services with defined APIs, improving reliability, agility, and scaling, but making debugging and architecture more complex. Replicated load-balanced services use identical stateless replicas behind a load balancer for availability and horizontal scale, supported by readiness probes. Variations include session tracking, caching layers such as Varnish, rate limiting, and SSL termination with nginx.

Sharded services split state across shards when data exceeds a single machine’s capacity. Sharded caches improve memory utilization but require careful planning around cache failure, hit rates, rollout impact, shard replication, shard routing, and sharding functions. Consistent hashing reduces remapping during resharding, and shard keys must be chosen based on request semantics.

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing by sending work to multiple leaf nodes and combining partial results at a root. It can support document search and sharded document search, but excessive parallelism introduces overhead and straggler latency. Replicating each shard improves reliability, upgrades, and scale. The passage ends by introducing function-as-a-service as an event- or request-driven style often used as part of broader architectures.

The government shutdown has left essential aviation safety workers, including air traffic controllers and TSA agents, working without pay while some FAA employees are furloughed. Workers say air travel remains safe, but the shutdown is increasing stress, reducing support, slowing projects, and could delay repairs. Some fear more furloughs, mass firings, or consequences for taking needed absences.

Experts and employees warn that delays and cancellations may grow if the shutdown continues, especially given existing air traffic controller shortages. The FAA says it will slow traffic at affected airports when staffing constraints arise to maintain safety, and the Transportation Department says safety-critical positions are exempt from reductions in force. TSA and DOT officials blamed political opponents for the shutdown, while workers and union representatives said employees feel used as political pawns and are worried about pay, commuting costs, and bargaining rights.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture, as a data center GPU for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads. It builds on Tesla V100 with third-generation Tensor Cores, support for TF32, BF16, FP64, FP16, INT8, INT4, and binary operations, and fine-grained structured sparsity that can double Tensor Core throughput. A100 provides major performance gains over V100, including 10x faster TF32 Tensor Core operations than V100 FP32 FMA, 2.5x FP16/FP32 mixed-precision performance, 2.5x FP64 performance, and up to 20x sparse INT8 performance.

A100 includes 108 SMs, 432 Tensor Cores, 6912 FP32 CUDA cores, 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/s bandwidth, and a 40 MB L2 cache nearly 7x larger than V100. It adds Multi-Instance GPU technology, allowing one GPU to be partitioned into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory bandwidth, and fault isolation. This is aimed at improving utilization, QoS, and multi-tenant support for cloud providers and enterprises.

The GPU supports third-generation NVLink with 12 links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, NVIDIA Magnum IO, Mellanox InfiniBand and Ethernet, and NVSwitch-based scaling. CUDA 11 adds support for A100 features including Tensor Cores, sparsity, task graphs, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, MIG management, and cooperative groups. Additional A100 features include improved atomics, NVJPG JPEG decode, five NVDEC units, optical flow acceleration, and improved error and fault handling.

The passage also describes DGX A100, which uses eight A100 GPUs connected through NVLink and NVSwitch, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and up to 56 GPU Instances through MIG. DGX A100 is presented as a scalable AI infrastructure platform supported by CUDA, NGC containers, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, Magnum IO, and software for deep learning, inference, data analytics, and HPC.

Close to 3,000 participants are expected in Kelowna for the 23rd BMO Okanagan Marathon, featuring marathon, half marathon, 10 km, timed 5 km, kids, and recreational events from City Park. Walk-up registration and package pickup are available at the Sports Expo. The Boston-qualifying course runs along Okanagan Lake. New additions include timing for the 5 km and an adult beverage garden. Events include Saturday’s Friendship Run, 5 km, and kids run, followed Sunday by the marathon, half marathon, and 10 km. The event supports The Sunshine Foundation of Canada and relies on more than 300 volunteers.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 27, 2022, reporting that it issued a press release on its financial results for the first fiscal quarter ended December 25, 2021. The release is attached as Exhibit 99.1, with Inline XBRL cover page data as Exhibit 104. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The passage describes a patent disclosure for devices, systems, and methods used in robotic-assisted and/or navigation-assisted spinal surgery, particularly implant placement in a vertebral pedicle. It identifies limitations of K-wire techniques, current robotic systems, tool interchangeability, and navigation errors caused by vertebral movement during procedures such as discectomy and cage placement.

The disclosure includes methods using a manipulator, end effector, screw, coaxial sleeve, navigation system, and controllers to position and advance the screw and sleeve along a planned insertion trajectory through soft tissue, then advance the screw into the vertebral body while disengaging it from the sleeve. Variants include a sleeve with a flexible movable distal feature that remains closed during soft-tissue advancement and opens when the screw passes through, and a tracking device with markers and a ratcheting mechanism coupled to the screw.

The detailed description presents a robotic surgical system, modular drive couplers, interchangeable working tools, elongate sleeves for tissue retraction and working channels, and workflows for incision, dilation, drilling, tapping, tap marker placement, and relocalization. Tracking devices, navigation features, and tap markers are used to verify or update vertebral position during surgery.

A New York panel unanimously recommended that the state Medicaid program pause coverage of Sarepta Therapeutics’ Duchenne muscular dystrophy treatment Elevidys until the FDA adds safety and clinical trial data to its label and the state evaluates Sarepta’s planned regimen to reduce liver failure risk. Some Medicaid coverage may continue case by case for patients under 21 based on medical necessity.

Anjuna police registered two unnatural death cases involving tourists from Tamil Nadu and Kerala. Pravin Sundaram, 28, collapsed after returning from Vagator and was declared dead at a private hospital; sources said he had attended a rave party. Another youth, Abdul, reportedly from Kerala, died after being brought to a hospital by an unknown person. Both bodies were sent to GMC for autopsy, with viscera to be preserved. Police are investigating and awaiting reports. A minister called for stopping outdoor music parties and drug-related activities.

Mums and children with Down’s syndrome from the “DesignerGenes” Facebook group gained global praise for a Carpool Karaoke-style video made for World Down’s Syndrome Day. Inspired by SingingHands and featuring Christina Perri’s “A Thousand Years,” the video exceeded 600,000 views, moved James Corden, and aims to change perceptions of Down’s syndrome.

The St. John’s Edge defeated the London Lightning 123-110 in Game 4 in St. John’s, tying the best-of-seven NBL Canada Central Division final 2-2. Game 5 is Thursday in St. John’s, with Game 6 set for Sunday in London. London started strong but struggled afterward, while St. John’s played with more energy, won the paint scoring 50-38, and benefited from 13 missed Lightning free throws. Charles Hinkle and Coron Williams led the Edge with 28 points each, and Ryan Reid added 22. Royce White scored 32 for London, and Ryan Anderson had 21. Edge coach Jeff Dunlap adjusted by starting Alex Johnson and using Reid against smaller defenders. Lightning coach Keith Vassell said he needed to have the team better prepared and would revisit his short bench usage. White and Anderson had a brief confrontation near officials at the end of the third quarter, which Vassell described as competitive frustration. NBL deputy commissioner Audley Stephenson also confirmed an investigation into a fan complaint alleging White used a homophobic slur during Game 3, though reports differed on what was said.

The speaker reflects on playing hockey in different settings and says the team is focused on Wednesday’s decisive game after putting the previous result behind them. They express confidence because the team has played well on the road and emphasize sticking to a simple, hard-to-play-against style: forechecking, getting pucks deep, closing gaps, defending hard, and putting pucks toward the net. They felt the previous game was generally strong despite quick goals against in the third period, crediting both goaltenders for key saves. The speaker also notes the value of rest before travel, the importance of relaxing and preparing together, and looks forward to having an important physical, scoring player back in the lineup.

Topshop recalled till display barrier units nationwide after 10-year-old Kaden Reddick died from serious head injuries involving a store display at its Reading branch. Police are investigating and supporting the family, while Reading Borough Council will work with them on health and safety matters. Topshop and the Oracle shopping centre expressed sadness, and the store remained closed.

The study examined Turkish teachers’ views on Turkish lessons and technological tools used during distance education in Turkey during the COVID-19 pandemic. A qualitative case study model was used. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 20 Turkish teachers in Hazro district of Diyarbakır, and the data were analyzed descriptively.

Teachers stated that distance education was implemented under difficult and unprepared conditions, but that the process was managed within available means. While 45% said education progressed, 25% found the progress insufficient, 20% said it did not progress, and 10% remained neutral. Most teachers viewed EBA and EBA TV as useful, though some noted infrastructure problems and insufficiencies.

No participant found distance education fully efficient; 70% found it insufficiently efficient and 30% found it inefficient. Teachers reported that target behaviors and achievements were only partially met, mainly because many students lacked internet access, devices, or regular attendance. Major problems included lack of tablets, phones or computers, weak internet infrastructure, multiple school-age children sharing devices at home, parental difficulties, and reduced lesson time.

For Turkish lessons, teachers said students mainly needed reading books, dictionaries, technological materials, and more practice-based activities for reading, writing, listening and speaking skills. The phone was the most used communication tool, and WhatsApp was the most used application, followed by Zoom and EBA.

Teachers said Turkish teachers in distance education should know their subject, plan lessons, use visuals and digital content, communicate effectively, consider individual differences, use technology well, and follow current developments. Recommendations included improving internet infrastructure, eliminating device shortages, strengthening EBA, supporting face-to-face education with distance education, increasing teacher technology training, continuing reading activities, and rearranging post-pandemic target behaviors and achievements according to student needs.

The FDA announced a crackdown on illegal sales of Juul e-cigarettes to minors, including nationwide undercover checks at stores and online retailers. Juul products, popular among teens, contain high nicotine levels and are difficult to detect. Since March, FDA checks found 40 violations, leading to warning letters. The agency also worked with eBay to remove Juul listings, requested documents from Juul’s maker to understand youth appeal, and plans similar requests to other manufacturers. FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb said further enforcement actions and education efforts are planned. The Truth Initiative urged faster regulation and removal of youth-attracting flavors.

The speaker marks the orderly transfer of power as a moment of unity and potential beginning, arguing that rapid change, space exploration, and global fear of war create a rare opportunity for peace. He calls on America to seek the honor of peacemaker and to help lead the world toward lasting peace.

He praises recent American achievements in science, industry, agriculture, economic growth, broader prosperity, and expanding freedom, while acknowledging a crisis of spirit marked by war, division, discord, and unfulfilled lives. He urges Americans to lower their voices, listen to one another, include those left out, and help those left behind.

The speaker says government must continue work on employment, housing, education, cities, rural areas, the environment, and quality of life, while recognizing that government alone cannot meet the nation’s needs. He calls for joint action by government and citizens, emphasizing service, shared destiny, racial unity, and equal dignity.

Internationally, he declares an era of negotiation, open communication, peaceful competition, cooperation on arms reduction and poverty, and strength against threats. He commits his office to peace among nations, seeking not victory over others but healing, compassion, understanding, and self-determination. Referring to Apollo astronauts’ view of Earth, he concludes that humanity’s destiny is shared and lies in people’s own hands and hearts.

Diana Beresford-Kroeger lives on a 160-acre property near Merrickville with her husband, Christian, where they created an arboretum and organic garden called Carrigliath. Born in Ireland, she lost her family at age 11 and was later taught old Irish teachings about nature, trees, and life. She studied botany, medical biochemistry, nuclear radiation, organic chemistry, and later pursued research in Canada.

After receiving trees as a wedding gift, Diana began gardening and became concerned about local deforestation and rare plants being destroyed. She and Christian worked to classify and save plants in the area. Her environmental work grew into writing books, speaking internationally, and creating the film “Call of the Forest: The Forgotten Wisdom of Trees,” which explores deforestation, climate change, and the importance of trees. She also developed a “Bioplan,” encouraging each person to plant one tree per year for six years to reduce atmospheric carbon dioxide. The Canadian-made film has drawn large audiences, earned award nominations, and is based on her book “The Global Forest.” Diana hopes her work helps future generations live decent lives.

The speaker describes a former teammate as honest, tough, hardworking, and capable of becoming a head coach. He says the opponent has strong defense and depth, making the series challenging but familiar. He expresses excitement about the opportunity, confidence in his team, and appreciation for passionate Canadian hockey crowds. He notes modern goalies are athletic and difficult to beat, praises his team’s forward depth, jokes about age, and says Giguere would receive more recognition in a larger market.

Cases of Hindu girls in Pakistan’s Sindh province converting to Islam and marrying Muslim men have alarmed the Hindu minority, with families and activists alleging abduction, coercion, and organized forced conversions, while the girls often testify in court that they converted and married voluntarily. Ravita Meghwar’s case reflects this pattern: her family says she was kidnapped and forcibly converted, while she says she eloped by choice.

Sindh, home to many Pakistani Hindus, has seen reported forced conversions linked to powerful shrines, seminaries, clerics, and local politicians. Lower-caste and low-income Hindus are described as especially vulnerable due to social discrimination and feudal power structures. Courts often accept the girls’ testimony, leaving families and activists frustrated.

A 2016 Sindh bill banning forced conversions and conversions before age 18 passed the legislature but was blocked after opposition from hardline religious groups. Activists now rely on Sindh’s law against marriage under 18, though judges have still allowed some girls to live with their husbands.

The issue has contributed to anxiety among Hindus about their future in Pakistan. Some are relocating from villages to cities, while others are migrating to India. Mass conversions of Hindu families are also reported in Sindh, with seminaries and clerics offering support to new converts.

A Las Vegas high school senior argues that youth employment can help disconnected young people reengage with school and community. After nearly dropping out, he began working and says the job helped him improve academically, build skills, gain confidence, and connect classroom learning to real life. The passage cites research linking youth jobs, internships, and apprenticeships to better attendance, academic performance, social development, work readiness, and reduced justice-system involvement. It notes that many youth, especially African American peers, struggle to find opportunities, and calls for governments to incentivize businesses and address barriers such as transportation and scheduling.
