Saturday night remains a key ratings battleground for BBC1 and ITV, but launching successful new entertainment shows in the slot is difficult. As a result, schedules rely heavily on long-running hits such as Strictly, The X Factor and Casualty, while many new formats fail. Few Saturday night entertainment shows have endured over the decades, and recent successes are rare, with The Voice UK cited as a moderate exception. Past concerns about the decline of Saturday entertainment were eased by Strictly and The X Factor replacing Blind Date, but both will eventually fade. TV controllers and producers continue seeking new formats, though success is unpredictable and often depends on instinct, producer track record and hope.

The speaker says Dallas played two strong periods but hurt itself in the third with correctable mistakes, especially puck support errors and odd-man rushes. He says the team’s focus is not winning three games, but winning the next game and bringing the series back home. He credits New Jersey’s speed, size, commitment to defending, and ability to win loose pucks, saying their defensive passion has been stronger by small margins. He says Dallas must stay within its system, avoid “home run” plays, eliminate easy chances, and raise its defensive level when the game intensifies.

He praises several New Jersey players, including Gomez, Rafalski, White, Madden, Malakhov, and the influence of Fetisov and coach Larry Robinson. He says Dallas’s leadership and dressing room emotion must drive the response, with coaches focusing more on tactical information. He discusses Modano trying to do too much, Carbonneau needing a defined role, and the difficulty of repeating as champions under constant pressure. He remains confident Dallas will respond with a strong game.

Combination defenses are used to limit touches by top offensive players or as surprise tactics, with timing and surprise key to success. Common types include Box and One, Diamond and One, and Triangle and Two, each designed to target one or more scorers while using zone alignments.

A study of 10.3 million insurance claims found that pre-existing psychiatric or behavioural conditions and psychoactive medication use were associated with later prescription opioid claims, especially long-term use. About 1.7% of patients became long-term opioid users, with higher risks among those with mental health conditions, substance use disorders, prior opioid use disorders, or ADHD medication use.

AfD’s rising support in Bavaria has pressured Germany’s governing coalition and Interior Minister Horst Seehofer to demand a harsher immigration stance. Angela Merkel agreed to create asylum transit centers along the German-Austrian border, where some migrants who previously applied in other EU countries may be held before possible return. The deal was intended to preserve Merkel’s coalition with the CSU and SPD, but the SPD questioned it because transit centers were not in the coalition agreement. Austria has not agreed to accept rejected asylum seekers and warned it may respond similarly, raising concerns about the EU’s open-border system. The dispute reflects broader European divisions, with several countries refusing to accept migrants from other EU states.

The NPD Group identified five trends expected to shape Britain’s £57 billion foodservice industry in 2018: wider use of smartphone click & collect, greater investment in staff training and retention, more personalized and tiered loyalty schemes, stronger alignment between brand promises and customer experience, and increased use of recommendations from staff, data and technology. The report says click & collect can reduce wait times, improve efficiency, increase sales and provide better customer data, but may require layout changes and staff training. It emphasizes that well-trained staff can improve loyalty, satisfaction and profits. Loyalty schemes are expected to move beyond discounts toward VIP and exclusive offers. Operators are urged to avoid over-promising, as poor service or quality can damage repeat business and trigger social media complaints. Personalized recommendations may help customers feel valued and encourage return visits.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture, as a data center accelerator for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads. It highlights major improvements over Tesla V100, including third-generation Tensor Cores, support for TF32, BF16, FP64, FP16, INT8, INT4, and binary data types, fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity, and significantly higher throughput for training, inference, and HPC applications.

A100 includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, larger L1/shared memory, Compute Data Compression, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, improved atomics, NVJPG decode, NVDEC units, and an Optical Flow Accelerator. CUDA 11 adds support for these features, including CUDA Graph acceleration, sparsity, Multi-Instance GPU, and improved programming capabilities.

The passage emphasizes A100’s Multi-Instance GPU feature, which can partition one GPU into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory bandwidth, and fault isolation. This is presented as especially useful for cloud service providers, multi-tenant environments, virtual machines, containers, and mixed workloads.

A100 also introduces third-generation NVLink, providing up to 600 GB/sec total GPU bandwidth, improved error detection and recovery, PCIe Gen 4 support, SR-IOV, and compatibility with NVIDIA Magnum IO and Mellanox InfiniBand and Ethernet solutions for scaling multi-GPU and multi-node systems.

The DGX A100 system uses eight A100 GPUs connected through NVLink and NVSwitch, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance in a 6U system. It supports scaling to large AI clusters and can provide up to 56 isolated GPU instances through MIG, with software support from NVIDIA GPU Cloud, Magnum IO, Slurm, Kubernetes, and NVIDIA DeepOps.

The lecture reviews binary detection by simplifying communication to a one-bit problem: a transmitted 0 or 1 becomes a one-dimensional observation \(v\), and the detector guesses the input hypothesis \(H\). The professor emphasizes solving simple “toy” problems first, arguing that understanding the simplest theoretical model helps address practical systems.

A detector is assumed to use a known probability model and to maximize the probability of a correct guess, called MAP detection. For binary hypotheses, MAP compares posterior probabilities. Using Bayes’ rule, this becomes a likelihood-ratio test: choose 0 if the likelihood ratio is at least the threshold \(p_1/p_0\), otherwise choose 1. The likelihood ratio is a sufficient statistic because it contains all information needed for the decision.

For binary antipodal signaling in Gaussian noise, 0 maps to \(+a\), 1 maps to \(-a\), and the received value is the signal plus Gaussian noise with variance \(N_0/2\). The log-likelihood ratio simplifies to \(4av/N_0\), so the decision is a threshold test on \(v\). With equal prior probabilities, the threshold is zero and the error probability is \(Q(\sqrt{2E_b/N_0})\), where \(E_b=a^2\). Non-antipodal binary signals have the same error probability determined by their separation, but shifting the signal midpoint adds energy without improving error performance.

The lecture extends the same idea to real antipodal vectors in white Gaussian noise. The log-likelihood ratio depends on the inner product of the received vector with the signal vector, making that inner product the sufficient statistic. This corresponds to projecting the received vector onto the signal direction, or for waveforms, using a matched filter before applying the same one-dimensional binary decision rule.

The Nobel Committee for Chemistry awarded three chemists from UC Berkeley, Kyoto University and the University of Melbourne for developing metal-organic frameworks, structures combining metal ions and carbon-based molecules. These frameworks can store substances, harvest water or toxic gases, and over 100,000 have been created.

The plaintiffs sued to recover the price of a horse sold to the defendant. The defendant returned the horse after using it, disputed the sale terms, claimed a 30-day trial agreement, invoked the statute of frauds, and alleged breach of warranty. The court found delivery and acceptance, rejected the defenses, and affirmed judgment for the plaintiffs with costs.
The Fourth Circuit affirmed the district court’s denial of Paul Nagy’s Rule 60(b) motion, finding no reversible error and dispensing with oral argument.

The passage describes systems and methods for plasma processing substrates using shaped-pulse bias to create arbitrarily shaped ion energy distribution functions (IEDFs). In reactive ion etch chambers, RF bias creates a self-bias voltage that affects ion energy, ion directionality, feature profile, and selectivity. Conventional RF bias often produces two-peak IEDFs, while a special shaped-pulse bias can maintain a nearly constant sheath and substrate voltage for most of each cycle, producing a mono-energetic IEDF.

The disclosed methods modify shaped-pulse bias waveforms to control IEDF shape. One method modulates the amplitude of the negative voltage jump so that the relative number of pulses at each amplitude determines the fraction of ions at corresponding energies. Bursts of pulses may be arranged to create single-, two-, or multi-peak IEDFs, including wider profiles useful for certain etch applications. Other methods alter the voltage ramp during ion current compensation: overcompensation uses a more negative slope, increasing substrate voltage magnitude during the compensation phase and producing a wider, double-peaked IEDF; undercompensation uses a less negative slope, decreasing substrate voltage magnitude and producing a wider, single-peaked IEDF.

The described substrate processing system includes a substrate support assembly, power electrode, ceramic layer, bias supply, and optional controller with memory and processor to execute control programs for applying these waveform modifications.

A Kazakh man died and another was hospitalized after debris from a Russian Soyuz 2.1a rocket launched from Baikonur sparked a steppe fire in Kazakhstan. The fire, in the planned fallout zone near Zhezkazgan, was worsened by high temperatures and wind. The men were clearing debris for NPO Mashinostroyeniya, according to emergency services and Roscosmos.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2020, reporting 501,751,183 common shares outstanding as of October 21, 2020. Q3 2020 net sales were $96.1 billion, up from $70.0 billion in Q3 2019; operating income was $6.2 billion, up from $3.2 billion; and net income was $6.3 billion, up from $2.1 billion. For the nine months ended September 30, 2020, net sales were $260.5 billion, operating income was $16.0 billion, and net income was $14.1 billion.

Operating cash flow for the nine months ended September 30, 2020 was $35.6 billion, while investing activities used $42.6 billion and financing activities provided $712 million. As of September 30, 2020, Amazon had $29.9 billion in cash and cash equivalents, $38.5 billion in marketable securities, total assets of $282.2 billion, long-term debt of $32.9 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $82.8 billion.

Segment net sales for Q3 2020 were $59.4 billion for North America, $25.2 billion for International, and $11.6 billion for AWS. Segment operating income was $2.3 billion for North America, $407 million for International, and $3.5 billion for AWS. Amazon reported more than $2.5 billion in COVID-19 related costs in Q3 2020 and more than $7.5 billion for the first three quarters of 2020.

The speaker says the win is a huge boost but only a first step, with more wins needed. They credit a key shorthanded goal, strong first-period play, four-line effort, skating, neutral-zone defense, and good road hockey. They hope to bring the series back to Edmonton, win at home, and force another game.

The Princeton offense is an unstructured, team-oriented style based on constant motion, spacing, ball control, passing, defensive reads, and back-door cuts. Popularized by Pete Carril, it involves all five players and requires outside shooting, two-handed passing and driving, court awareness, conditioning, patience, and unselfishness.

Coaches must fully commit to the system because it gives players freedom to create rather than relying on set plays. Its benefits include teamwork, daily skill development, defensive practice against movement, unpredictability, no need to reset plays, and difficulty for defenses to block out or scout.

The offense is adaptable against pressure, sagging man-to-man, and zone defenses. Proper spacing of 12 to 15 feet spreads the defense, limits help and double teams, improves passing, and opens the basket area for cuts, drives, post play, and splits. It commonly begins in a 2-3 high-post alignment and flows through entries, exchanges, post action, and repeated continuity.

Key elements include wing and guard entries, high-post actions, dribble clears, zipper and mid-screen entries, exchanges, down screens, back cuts, post flashes, kick-out passes, dribble penetration, weave actions, and quick-hitting specials. Post-ups are often used to collapse the defense and create outside shots rather than as primary scoring options.

The offense controls tempo through patience and frequent passing, sometimes using 15 to 20 passes per possession, while still taking quick-break opportunities. Back cuts are central counters to defensive pressure and overplays. Dribbling is used selectively for spacing, exchanges, penetration, and counters.

The passage also notes press-break preparation and describes psychological effects on opponents, including pressure from low-possession games, frustration, fatigue, rushed shots, and vulnerability to back cuts, outside shooting, and transition baskets.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s Ampere GA10x/GA102 GPU architecture, fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm 8N NVIDIA Custom Process. GA102 contains 28.3 billion transistors and includes CUDA Cores for programmable shading, RT Cores for ray tracing, and Tensor Cores for AI workloads. A full GA102 GPU has 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores.

Compared with Turing, GA10x doubles FP32 shader throughput by enabling FP32 processing on both SM datapaths, improves ray/triangle intersection throughput with second-generation RT Cores, and increases Tensor Core performance through third-generation Tensor Cores with sparsity, TF32, BF16, FP16, INT8, INT4, and other supported data types. The RTX 3080 is cited as delivering 30 shader TFLOPS, 58 RT TFLOPS, and 238 sparse Tensor TFLOPS. Ampere GPUs are described as up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing at the same performance level.

GA102 includes seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, 112 ROPs, twelve 32-bit memory controllers, and 6 MB of L2 cache. Each GA10x SM includes 128 CUDA Cores, four Tensor Cores, one RT Core, texture units, registers, and configurable L1/shared memory. ROPs are moved into the GPC to improve raster performance.

The architecture adds GDDR6X memory support, reaching up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/s bandwidth, using PAM4 signaling and related coding and signal integrity techniques. RTX A6000 and A40 use 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, expandable to 96 GB with NVLink. Third-generation NVLink provides 112.5 GB/s total bandwidth between two GPUs, while PCIe Gen 4 doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth.

Second-generation RT Cores support concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute, and add hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur through an Interpolate Triangle Position unit. Third-generation Tensor Cores accelerate AI denoising, DLSS, NVIDIA Broadcast, Canvas, and AI training and inference. DLSS is described as enabling higher-performance rendering, including 8K gaming scenarios.

The passage also covers RTX IO, which uses GPU-based loading and decompression with Microsoft DirectStorage to reduce CPU workload and improve asset streaming. Display and media features include DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, HDCP support, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-generation NVENC for hardware video encoding.

The NVIDIA A40 is presented as a data center GPU for visual computing, supporting vGPU, EGX, PCIe Gen4, 48 GB memory, and NVLink scaling. The RTX A6000 is described as a professional workstation GPU with GA102, 48 GB of GDDR6, ray tracing, AI acceleration, and NVLink support. Appendices summarize GeForce RTX 3090 and RTX 3070 specifications, GDDR6X Error Detection and Replay for memory overclocking, RTX A6000 performance comparisons, and NVIDIA legal disclaimers.

The coach said the team was outmuscled early in the second period but improved late in the period and played well in the third, continuing its strong third-period scoring trend. He praised a key player for contributing five-on-five, on the power play and penalty kill. He was pleased with Manny’s return, citing his faceoffs, defensive play and scoring chance, and said he should improve. He declined to share injury details, calling lineup choices game-time decisions and saying secrecy protects players. He discussed taking years to tell the twins apart and described Daniel as quieter and Henrik as more outspoken. He said a returning player would be eased in and used for faceoffs and defensive situations, while he would not break up the Torres-Lapierre-Hansen line. He also said the team must avoid offensive-zone penalties and hopes the power play improves.

Volunteers in southern NSW and the ACT are surveying local waterways in late winter to help monitor the elusive, near-threatened platypus. In the Cooma region, Waterwatch has conducted four years of surveys on the Upper Murrumbidgee River, the only formal platypus monitoring there. Although no platypus were seen during one recent survey, a native water rat was spotted. Waterwatch says four years of data suggest platypus numbers are stable at the site. The surveys provide baseline data for biologists as platypus numbers have declined across eastern Australia and Tasmania due to habitat change, reduced river flows, introduced fish and discarded waste. People are encouraged to report sightings year-round and look for platypus in August and September during early mornings or late evenings.

The Iowa Supreme Court affirmed dismissal of an action by Secor’s administrator to collect a foreign deficiency judgment and to enjoin alleged fraudulent conveyances by James E. and Elizabeth Siver to their sons. The Sivers counterclaimed that Secor had induced a prior land exchange through false representations about the quality, condition, and value of a mountain farm, causing damages exceeding the judgment.

The court held that objections to witness competency must specifically state the facts causing incompetency; a general objection that a witness is “incompetent and unqualified” is insufficient. It also held that interested witnesses in a fraud action against an administrator may testify about property description, quality, value, reliance on representations, and the condition of property received, and that an objection to testimony about a personal transaction with a deceased person does not necessarily include personal communications.

The court found sufficient admissible evidence to support the Sivers’ counterclaim and upheld the trial court’s ruling that the equities favored the appellees. It also refused to retax costs against the administratrix individually, finding no error in taxing them against her in her official capacity.

Justices Ladd, Salinger, and Stevens dissented, arguing that the objections were sufficient and that the Sivers’ testimony about communications and transactions with Secor should have been excluded.

The lecture reviews Wald’s identity and equality for random walks with stopping times at two thresholds, emphasizing their use in threshold-crossing and sequential hypothesis testing. It explains likelihood ratios, log-likelihood ratios, MAP and Neyman-Pearson tests, sufficient statistics, and how sequential tests control error probabilities by stopping when thresholds are crossed. The professor contrasts fixed-sample tests with sequential testing and discusses tradeoffs between thresholds, error probabilities, and expected numbers of observations.

The lecture then derives Wald’s equality from Wald’s identity and uses a second derivative case for zero-mean random walks, including the expected stopping time for a simple random walk between two thresholds. It introduces martingales as sequences whose conditional expected next value equals the current value, connects them to fair gambling games, proves a basic conditioning lemma, and gives examples including zero-mean random walks, dependent zero-mean increments, signed products, and product-form martingales. A double-or-nothing example shows that limits and expectations cannot always be interchanged. The lecture also defines submartingales and supermartingales, notes their sign relationship, and introduces Jensen’s inequality for convex functions.

The passage lists 10 AI tools for content creation in 2025: ChatGPT for writing and content optimization; Canva Magic Studio for visual design and social media content; RunwayML for AI video creation and editing effects; Midjourney V6 for professional-quality image generation; Synthesia for AI avatar videos and multilingual presentations; Descript for podcast and video editing with transcription; ElevenLabs for voice synthesis and multilingual voiceovers; Tribescaler for viral content and headline optimization; Clickable for automated ad creation; and CopyAI for marketing copywriting. It says these tools help creators, marketers, businesses, educators, podcasters, and social media managers produce content faster, maintain brand voice, improve quality, and scale production. The passage concludes that AI amplifies creativity rather than replacing it and notes that features and pricing may change and that the article contains affiliate links.

Socket 940 requires molded markings for socket ID, lock/unlock direction, pin A01 orientation, supplier UL symbol, and lot traceability, all positioned to remain visible where specified. Contacts use high-strength copper alloy with nickel plating and gold on mating areas; no lubricants may be present on shipped contact mating areas. SMT solder balls are 63/37 tin-lead, 0.76 mm diameter, used with 0.64 mm PCB pads, require solder barriers, and must meet 0.20 mm coplanarity.

The socket uses a stainless steel actuation lever with latch support. Open-position insertion/extraction forces must not exceed 2 kgf; closed-position extraction must be at least 0.013 kgf per pin. Lever actuation/de-actuation force must be under 3.6 kgf, pin displacement under 1.0 mm, and the socket must withstand 50 cycles.

Visual inspection requirements prohibit missing, damaged, malformed, or misaligned solder balls, contacts, cover/base features, latch, or lever; gold plating must be present on contact mating surfaces. Electrical requirements include 1.5 A per contact with under 30°C rise, LLCR not exceeding 25 mΩ initially or finally, inductance and capacitance limits, 100 Ω ±10% differential impedance, propagation delay skew under 10 ps plus measurement error, crosstalk evaluation, 650 Vac dielectric withstand voltage, and 1000 MΩ minimum insulation resistance.

Smartphone makers are trying to achieve full-screen displays while accommodating selfie cameras and sensors, often using bezels or notches. Vivo’s Apex concept uses an under-screen fingerprint sensor and pop-up camera but adds complexity, cost, and bulk. The passage proposes transparent OLED panels as a better solution, allowing cameras behind the display with per-pixel transparency when needed. Transparent OLED has already been shown by companies including Samsung, LG, Panasonic, and Sharp, mainly in TVs and smart windows, and could eventually be adapted for smartphones.

A study found that a traditional Bulgarian and Turkish yogurt-making method uses four live ants added to warmed cow’s milk and buried in an ant mound overnight. Bacteria on the ants, along with formic acid and milk-digesting enzymes from ants and microbes, acidify and thicken the milk. Live ants worked better than frozen or dehydrated ants, though they may carry rare disease-causing parasites.

The speaker describes being unexpectedly placed in the Stanley Cup Finals, crediting Coach Burns, the veterans’ calming leadership, and team depth for helping him contribute. He says he felt calm, wanted to help in any way, and was grateful to score, though contributing did not need to be on the scoresheet. He emphasizes that different players stepped up throughout the playoffs, which he views as a mark of a championship team. He also praises Marty and an injured leader’s locker-room presence and guidance. The speaker recalls the final moments as intense, emotional, and unforgettable.

The Clark County School District Board of Trustees voted on May 2, 2018, to select Dr. Jesus Jara as its new superintendent. Jara had served as deputy superintendent for Orange County Public Schools in Orlando since 2012 and previously led Monroe County Public Schools in Florida. His selection followed a divided board process and public support from many speakers for Dr. Mike Barton, CCSD’s chief student achievement officer, whose nomination failed 4-3. Trustees debated for about two hours before voting on Jara. Vice President Carolyn Edwards urged the community to give him a fair chance and focus on student achievement. The district hoped Jara would start before the end of June to work with retiring superintendent Pat Skorkowsky. Six finalists were considered, including three internal and three external candidates.

The command migrates one or more SNP guest pages within system physical address space and may replace PAGE_MOVE for faster operation. It supports 4K pages and physically contiguous, 2M-aligned 2M pages, but not non-contiguous 2M pages. DMA and CPU access to migrating pages are not supported; CPU access is generally blocked by marking pages non-present.

Source pages must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, destination pages Pre-Migration. After migration, destination pages inherit source state and sources return to Pre-Migration. Firmware validates platform state, page states, guest context, exclusive RMP access, and matching page sizes, then invalidates and syncs CPU TLBs, copies data, and updates destination and source RMPs.

An end command marks completion of migration command strings and may interrupt on completion; most input fields are ignored. Errors may occur in command format, migration entries, ring buffer management, or hardware operation. Status is reported through command fields, list entries, PM_STATUS, or MCA. Hardware errors may make affected command pages unrecoverable, though software may attempt state preservation before reboot.

Action on Smoking and Health argues that the goal for preventable tobacco deaths must be zero, framing smokers as victims of an addictive, deadly product engineered and marketed by the tobacco industry. The passage cites the Danish Institute for Human Rights and the Cape Town Declaration in stating that tobacco production and marketing conflict with the human right to health. ASH, founded in 1967, supports bold measures toward a tobacco-free world and aims to eliminate tobacco-related deaths.
The court dismissed the appeal because an order sustaining a demurrer to an amended petition without further disposition is not a final, appealable order.

The passage discusses gamification as an innovative approach in academic education, emphasizing its potential to increase motivation, engagement, cooperation, competition, and practical learning. It presents four projects conducted at the Institute of Pedagogy at the University of Wrocław in 2014–2015.

The Kulturalny Wrocław project used location-based games to teach cultural education and information technology. Students solved riddles connected with cultural sites in Wrocław. Participants valued outdoor learning, independence, group integration, and memorable experiences, though some questioned whether traditional classes might cover more content.

The Gamification in career management project was a five-day seminar for students in Lower Silesia. It combined expert meetings with a gamified science-fiction plot, missions, points, badges, and prizes. Students and instructors assessed it as effective, noting high engagement, group integration, strong exam results, and self-diagnosis of skills. Instructors stressed that preparing such courses required substantial effort and was most practical when repeated or externally funded.

The Entrepreneurship in Lower Silesian educational practice project used a location-based game to diagnose and develop entrepreneurship competences. Participants completed tasks, earned game money, and solved problems. They praised its socialising character, movement, teamwork, attractiveness, and development of soft skills, but noted possible limits related to weather, unfamiliar locations, organisation, competition, and access to information.

The Learning through games project used a LARP game to develop soft skills. Students played fantasy roles, completed tasks, and worked toward a group goal. Educational aims were achieved, especially in negotiation, communication, creativity, and group management, but students without prior RPG or LARP experience had lower satisfaction and more difficulty with the rules and roles.

The passage concludes that educational games can successfully support academic education when matched to students’ experience, subject matter, time, and resources. Simple games with clear rules and strategic choice are easier to integrate into curricula, while complex games require greater preparation, tutorials, socialising activities, and often external funding.

Sydney maths teacher Eddie Woo has risen to prominence through his popular YouTube channel, WooTube, awards and a new role as a master teacher with the NSW Department of Education. Named Australia’s Local Hero for 2018 and a finalist in the $US1 million Global Teacher Prize, Woo continues teaching at Cherrybrook Technology High School while travelling NSW to mentor teachers and students. WooTube began in 2012 when he filmed lessons for an ill student and now has more than 200,000 subscribers and over 12 million views. His regional maths forums draw large crowds, with students and educators praising his engaging approach to mathematics. Officials describe him as an exceptional teacher, though his growing fame has made his schedule busier and affected time with his family.

The IRS announced inflation-adjusted 2026 tax brackets and deductions under the One Big Beautiful Bill to address rising living costs and bracket creep. The standard deduction will rise to $32,200 for joint filers, $16,100 for single filers, and $24,150 for heads of household. The 37% top rate will apply above $640,600 for individuals and $768,700 for couples. The estate tax exemption will increase to $15 million, with changes to EITC and child tax credit thresholds and a new $6,000 deduction for taxpayers aged 65 and older beginning in 2025. Analysts say the changes offer limited household relief while preserving federal revenue.

The passage is from a Sansa Fuze MP3 player manual. It describes the player’s features, including a 1.9-inch color screen, FM radio where available, built-in microphone, microSD/SDHC expansion, support for music, audiobook, photo, and video playback, voice recording, internal data storage, and rechargeable battery life of up to 24 hours for audio or 5 hours for video. It explains charging, power, reset, hold switch, thumbwheel navigation, computer connection, firmware updates, formatting, and safe disconnection. It also provides instructions for transferring music, playlists, photos, and videos using drag-and-drop, Windows Media Player, Audible Manager, and Sansa Media Converter. Additional sections cover playing music, audiobooks, videos, photos, and slideshows; using repeat, shuffle, bookmarks, ratings, and Go Lists; listening to and presetting FM radio stations; recording FM radio; setting FM region and mode; and making voice recordings. The manual notes that copyrighted material must be used in compliance with applicable laws.

The New Jersey Supreme Court affirmed Chancery Division orders denying costs and counsel fees to union defendants in two related cases brought by United States Pipe and Foundry Co. In the arbitration case, the court held the suit to determine arbitrability of a discharged worker’s grievance was not within the Anti-Injunction Act, so counsel fees were unavailable. In the strike case, although the Act applied and an injunction had been reversed on appeal, the reversal was for procedural deficiencies, not because the company lacked a substantive basis for injunctive relief. The court held costs and counsel fees under N.J.S. 2A:15-53 are mandatory only when injunctive relief is denied or reversed on the merits. The judgments were affirmed, with costs to respondent only in the arbitration case.

Huron County Acting CAO, Director of Cultural Services and County Librarian Meighan Wark presented to Central Huron Council about proposed renovations to bring Clinton Library up to accreditation standards and improve accessibility, services and facilities. While Huron County Library and 11 branches received accreditation in 2015, Clinton did not, largely due to accessibility and space issues.

Wark explained that the county provides staff, materials, furniture, equipment and services, while the municipality is responsible for the building, maintenance and utilities. Renovation planning would use Ontario Public Library Guidelines and other resources to determine required space and components such as circulation desks, technology areas, flexible space and storage. Wider aisles, lower shelves and other accessibility standards affect square footage needs.

Next steps would involve agreeing on required service components and space needs, then working with an architect on draft drawings for council and community review. Wark said provincial funding may be possible, especially if the project is “shovel-ready.” Council will continue discussions, and Wark said the Huron County Library could invest in the interior if the municipality commits to building changes.

Charlie Alliston is on trial at the Old Bailey over the death of Kim Briggs, 44, who was hit while crossing Old Street in east London on February 12, 2016, and died a week later from severe head injuries. Prosecutors said Alliston, then 18, was riding a fixed-wheel track bike without a front brake at nearly 20mph, which made it unlawful for road use and dangerous in a busy area. The court heard reconstructions showed he could have stopped in time if the bike had a front brake. Prosecutors also cited online posts in which Alliston blamed Briggs for the collision. Alliston denies manslaughter and causing bodily harm by wanton or furious driving.

Elijah Brown scored 27 points, including 17 of New Mexico’s final 19, as the Lobos beat Boise State 78-73. New Mexico used an 11-0 first-half run and held off a late Boise State rally. Obij Ajet and Damien Jefferson each scored 14 for the Lobos, while Chandler Hutchison had a career-high 31 for Boise State. The win tightened the Mountain West standings, with New Mexico one game back in the loss column. Tim Williams missed his fourth straight game for New Mexico with a foot injury.

A Harvard Institute of Politics poll found 65% of millennials favored Democrats over Republicans for 2018. Key findings included low optimism about the country’s direction, 25% approval of President Trump, concern over internal threats, and 61% support for stricter gun laws.

Preempt announced new integrations for its Preempt Behavioral Firewall at RSA 2017. Data integrations include Okta, Azure Active Directory and VPN gateways, while enforcement integrations include SecureAuth, RSA SecurID, Duo, Google Authenticator and HP Aruba ClearPass. The company said these additions provide deeper context for internal network threat detection and more options to automatically block, notify, redirect or challenge users. The firewall combines User and Entity Behavioral Analytics with adaptive response to detect and respond to suspicious activity, malicious insiders and risky behavior in real time.

This retrospective cohort study used 2017–2019 HCUP-NIS data to examine whether perinatal mood disorders were associated with peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) and cardiac events during pregnancy and postpartum. Among over 2.2 million hospitalizations, 168,729 patients (7.4%) had an ICD-10-coded mood disorder. Patients with mood disorders had higher rates of PPCM (0.12% vs 0.05%) and composite adverse cardiac events (0.36% vs 0.14%) than those without mood disorders. After adjustment for demographic, clinical, and hospital factors, mood disorders remained independently associated with PPCM (aOR 1.36), composite adverse cardiac events (aOR 1.57), and pulmonary edema (aOR 1.62), but not maternal death. The study concludes that perinatal mood disorders are associated with increased PPCM and cardiac event rates, warranting further investigation into mental health care and cardiac risk prevention in pregnancy and postpartum.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture introduces a redesigned SM with two SMs per TPC, 64 FP32 Cores and 64 INT32 Cores per SM, concurrent FP32/INT32 execution, independent thread scheduling, eight Tensor Cores, and one RT Core. Each SM is divided into four processing blocks and includes configurable shared memory/L1 cache. These changes, along with a unified cache design, larger L2 cache, and improved datapaths, are stated to deliver a 50% improvement in performance per CUDA core over Pascal.

Turing Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, and INT4 precision for deep learning training, inference, and neural graphics. They accelerate NVIDIA NGX features including DLSS, AI InPainting, AI Super Rez, and AI Slow-Mo. Tesla T4, based on Turing, targets data center inference with 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, up to 130 TOPS INT8 and 260 TOPS INT4 performance, 16 GB memory, and 320 GB/s bandwidth.

Turing adds GDDR6 memory with 14 Gbps signaling and improved power efficiency, enhanced compression, larger and faster L2 caches, and about 50% higher effective bandwidth compared with Pascal in cited examples. Its display and video engines support DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, HDR processing, HEVC 8K encode, improved NVENC quality, enhanced NVDEC formats, USB-C, and VirtualLink for single-cable VR headset connectivity. TU102 and TU104 use NVLink for SLI data transfers.

Turing enables hybrid rendering by combining rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, offloading SMs and enabling real-time ray tracing effects such as reflections, shadows, ambient occlusion, refractions, and indirect lighting. The passage states Turing can achieve over 10 Giga Rays/sec and run ray tracing about 10 times faster than Pascal.

Additional graphics features include Mesh Shading, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering. These aim to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks, vary shading rate by region or object motion, reuse shading work in texture space, and render multiple views or instances more efficiently. Turing also expands VR-related capabilities through VirtualLink, MVR, foveated rendering via VRS, and RT Core acceleration for VRWorks Audio.

The passage describes TU104 and TU106 GPUs. TU104 includes up to 48 SMs, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and second-generation NVLink, and is used in products such as GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. TU106 includes 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but does not support NVLink or SLI. The passage also defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric combining Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations for hybrid rendering workloads.

In card identification mode, the host resets cards, validates voltage, identifies cards, and requests an RCA using CMD lines only. CMD0 resets cards to Idle State except inactive cards, while power-on places all cards in Idle State. Cards default to RCA 0x0000, input CMD lines, and 400KHz clock frequency, with driver strength depending on signaling. CMD8 verifies interface operating voltage by exchanging VHS, CRC, and check pattern; unsupported voltage yields no response and idle state. CMD8 is mandatory before the first ACMD41 for SDHC or SDXC initialization.

The speaker says losing was difficult after the team worked hard to reach that point, but credits the opposing team for playing well and deserving the win. He praises his teammates, discusses the importance of preparation and effort in the playoffs, and notes home-ice advantage in the series. He says an individual award was not the one he wanted, as his goal was the Stanley Cup, especially for his ill mother. He congratulates the opposing goalie and says the team will move forward next season one game at a time.

Washington police will announce charges against 12 Turkish security agents over violence during Turkey’s president’s visit, with seven facing felonies and five misdemeanors. Two men, Sinan Narin and Eyup Yildirim, were arrested on assault charges related to the May 16 altercation outside the Turkish ambassador’s residence.

TI documentation update notifications are available through product folders on ti.com via weekly digests, with revision histories providing change details. TI E2E forums offer design support, with linked content provided “AS IS.” multiSPI and TI E2E are Texas Instruments trademarks. The passage warns that ESD can damage integrated circuits and recommends proper handling. Revision A changed ADS8685W and ADS8689W status from Advance Information to Production Data. Mechanical, packaging, and orderable information is current but subject to change. Additional notes define status, material type, RoHS values, lead finish, MSL rating, and part marking. TI provides resources “AS IS,” disclaims warranties, limits liability, and states users are responsible for product selection, design, validation, testing, and compliance.

Mary Meeker’s Internet Trends report highlights rapid growth in China’s short-form video market. Time spent watching videos under five minutes rose 360 percent in 2017, while 76 percent of consumers used only one short-video app. Douyin and Kuaishou each report about 100 million daily active users and average viewing of 52 minutes per day. As short-form viewing approaches long-form levels, content providers seeking ad revenue are urged to pay attention.

Apple’s iOS 11.4 update adds AirPlay 2, enabling multi-room audio, stereo HomePod pairing, improved buffering, and continued streaming during calls or other media use. HomePod gains Siri calendar support, though personal requests still lack individual voice recognition. AirPlay 2 support is planned by several third-party speaker makers, but streaming still relies on an iOS device as the hub. The update also introduces Messages in iCloud, syncing message history and deletions across devices while moving photos and attachments to iCloud, which may affect users on the free 5GB plan. The update is available now.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K reporting results from its May 16, 2018 Annual Meeting. Stockholders approved amendments to the 2007 Equity Incentive Plan, increasing its share reserve by 23,000,000 shares, and the 2012 Employee Stock Purchase Plan, increasing its share reserve by 13,500,000 shares. Stockholders elected eleven directors for one-year terms, approved executive compensation on an advisory basis, ratified PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as independent registered accounting firm for the fiscal year ending January 27, 2019, and approved both amended plans. The filing included the amended plans as exhibits and was signed May 21, 2018.

U.S. stocks rebounded Wednesday as investors hoped Italy could avoid new elections, with banks, energy companies, and small companies leading gains. The S&P 500 rose 1.3%, the Dow gained 1.3%, and the Nasdaq added 0.9%, while the Russell 2000 closed at a record high. Italy’s FTSE MIB rose 2.1% after Carlo Cottarelli cited “new possibilities” to form a government. Bond yields increased in the U.S., helping bank stocks, while U.S. crude rose 2.2% to $68.21 a barrel, boosting energy shares. Trade concerns persisted amid U.S.-China tariff tensions and U.S.-EU talks. European markets were mixed, the euro rose, and gold, silver, and copper posted modest gains.

The appellate court modified the order, holding that summary judgment was improperly granted on Hartford’s bad-faith settlement negotiation claims because evidence could support findings that General Accident delayed offering policy limits and caused damages. Issues of witness credibility and damages were for a jury. The court affirmed dismissal of Hartford’s fourth cause of action alleging Insurance Law § 2601 violations.

A University of Rochester Medical Centre study in mice found that low doses of alcohol improved glymphatic system activity, the brain’s waste-clearing process, and reduced brain inflammation without impairing cognitive or motor performance. High alcohol exposure increased inflammation, particularly in astrocytes, and impaired cognitive and motor skills. Intermediate and very high doses reduced glymphatic function, though suppression after chronic moderate exposure was restored 24 hours after stopping. Lead author Dr Maiken Nedergaard said the findings suggest low alcohol doses may aid brain waste removal, including proteins associated with Alzheimer’s disease and dementia, while excessive intake is harmful. The study was published in Scientific Reports.

The passage explains defensive run fit “spacing” terminology and how coaches translate concepts into executable schemes. Run fits are influenced by front spacing—odd or even, based on where the open gap or “bubble” is—and by coverage, described as 7-, 8-, or 9-man spacing. In 7-man spacing, defenses are light in the box, often use middle-of-field-open coverage, and rely on tools such as two-gapping, tite fronts, stunts, stack-track-fallback versus zone, and spill-overlap versus gap schemes. In 8-man spacing, defenses are “gapped out,” usually play middle-of-field-closed coverage, and use one-gap fits, indicator fitting, and lever-spill-lever concepts. In 9-man spacing, defenses are “maxed out,” often tied to cover 0 or blitz fits, with extra defenders in the run fit. The passage also applies these concepts to 3-4 defenses, noting that odd and even spacing can appear in any man-spacing structure depending on overhang responsibilities and defensive philosophy.

The passage describes TPS7H500x-SP controller operating modes, protection features, design guidance, and application considerations. External synchronization requires RT floating and a SYNC clock at twice the desired switching frequency, from 200 kHz to 4 MHz with 40%–60% duty cycle. Two controllers can operate in primary-secondary mode for synchronized independent converters or interleaved parallel operation, with the secondary inverting the received clock and creating a 90° or 270° phase shift.

The controllers support configurable primary and synchronous rectifier outputs depending on device variant, with about 150-mA peak output capability and recommended external gate drivers. Dead time, leading-edge blanking, duty-cycle limits, current sensing, hiccup-mode overcurrent response, external fault shutdown, slope compensation, frequency compensation, and thermal shutdown are described. Pulse skipping prevents minimum-on-time issues under certain COMP voltage and duty-cycle conditions.

The application section presents a synchronous push-pull converter design using TPS7H5001-SP and GaN devices, including component selection for switching frequency, feedback resistors, dead time, blanking time, soft start, transformer, FETs, clamp, output inductor and capacitance, current limit, hiccup capacitor, compensation, and slope compensation. Power supply and layout recommendations emphasize regulated input, proper bypassing, short high-current paths, separation of analog and power grounds, careful routing of noise-sensitive traces, and close placement of filtering and compensation components. The document also lists related resources, revision history, packaging information, and TI disclaimers.

Andrew Lo discusses market fear during the financial crisis, noting the Fed’s efforts to maintain liquidity and arguing that suspending mark-to-market accounting would be harmful because market prices require actual transactions. He suggests that transparency tools, such as a marketplace for CDO pricing, could create opportunities.

The lecture introduces hedging with derivatives, especially forwards and futures, to reduce risks such as currency or commodity price fluctuations. Lo explains differing views on corporate hedging: some argue shareholders can hedge themselves, while others say firms should hedge to reduce cash-flow uncertainty and financial distress. Examples include mining companies with different hedging policies and evidence that many large firms use derivatives.

A forward contract is defined as a customized, over-the-counter agreement between two parties to buy or sell an asset at a future date for a price set today. It may involve physical delivery, has no initial value when fairly priced, and carries illiquidity and counterparty risk. Lo uses soybeans and oil examples to show how forward prices reflect market expectations and how large price movements can create incentives to default.

A futures contract is presented as a standardized version of a forward contract traded on an exchange, marked to market daily, and supported by a clearing corporation. Daily settlement reduces counterparty risk by limiting losses to short intervals. Futures contracts require margin deposits, maintenance margins, and margin calls; positions can be closed if required funds are not provided. Lo also notes that many futures are cash settled, though some allow physical delivery.

Kentucky sophomore forward Wenyen Gabriel announced he will keep his name in the 2018 NBA draft and begin his professional career rather than return for his junior season. Gabriel declared without hiring an agent and sought feedback from NBA teams, though he was not invited to the NBA scouting combine and was not listed among ESPN’s top 100 prospects. He averaged 6.8 points and 5.4 rebounds as a sophomore, shot 39.6% from 3-point range, and led Kentucky with 40 blocks. Coach John Calipari praised Gabriel’s versatility and improvement but said he would need to work hard to find a role. Kentucky has also lost several players to the draft or transfers, while PJ Washington is returning and Stanford graduate transfer Reid Travis was reportedly a possible addition.

The lecture reviews the dressed atom picture and applies it to stimulated light forces. In this framework, atom–laser coupling is diagonalized first, producing dressed states split by the generalized Rabi frequency, while spontaneous emission couples dressed-state manifolds. In the strong Rabi-frequency secular limit, dressed-state populations and coherences decouple, giving rate equations, steady-state populations, relaxation times, and an interpretation of Mollow triplet intensities and linewidths.

The professor contrasts bare-state and dressed-state descriptions of spontaneous emission: the bare basis explains photon antibunching, while the dressed basis explains alternating red- and blue-detuned sideband emission. For dipole forces, atoms in the two dressed states experience equal and opposite forces; population imbalance gives the net force, attractive for red detuning and repulsive for blue detuning. On resonance, average dipole force vanishes, but force fluctuations cause heating.

A finite time lag in dressed-state population adjustment for moving atoms produces a nonadiabatic force. In a blue-detuned standing wave this yields friction and cooling, called blue molasses. Heating is described by a momentum diffusion coefficient derived from force correlations; in strong fields, fluctuations from transitions between dressed levels dominate over recoil heating.

The lecture then explains Sisyphus cooling for a two-level atom in a blue-detuned standing wave: atoms tend to climb potential hills and make spontaneous transitions near the top, losing kinetic energy. A perturbative large-detuning treatment gives simple expressions for dressed states, transition rates, cooling rate, friction coefficient, diffusion, and the result that the limiting temperature is comparable to the optical lattice depth, so two-level laser cooling cannot localize atoms within a lattice.

Finally, the professor summarizes several equivalent pictures of dipole potentials, including Optical Bloch equations, dressed atoms, induced dipoles, and refraction by dielectric objects, relating the latter to optical tweezers.

Russ Tedrake introduces trajectory optimization as policy search over parameterized controllers, focusing on open-loop control trajectories. He explains shooting methods, where simulations are repeatedly run while updating parameters using gradients computed by adjoint/backpropagation-through-time methods or forward sensitivity methods such as real-time recurrent learning. He compares these approaches, noting trade-offs in memory, computation, and handling constraints.

He demonstrates using SNOPT and sequential quadratic programming for pendulum, cart-pole, and acrobot examples, emphasizing faster convergence, no learning-rate tuning, and easier incorporation of constraints compared with simple gradient descent. He then presents direct collocation, which optimizes both controls and states while enforcing dynamics as explicit constraints, often improving initialization and constraint handling. He notes limitations such as local minima and fixed-step discretization, but argues these methods are practical for many trajectory problems. The lecture ends by previewing trajectory stabilization with LQR and iterative LQR methods.

North Carolina child care academies in at least 11 counties are offering low- or no-cost fast-track training to address early childhood educator shortages. Programs last two to six weeks and use either a classroom-ready model, which qualifies graduates to work in licensed child care facilities, or a teaching credential model, which includes EDU 119-equivalent training and qualifies graduates to be lead teachers.

A $1.476 million state pilot to expand academies passed the House but was not included in the final budget measure signed in August. The state Division of Child Development and Early Education is offering grants of up to $50,000 for up to 10 colleges or universities to run academies from October 2025 to July 2026.

Programs are typically collaborations among Smart Start partnerships, community colleges, and Child Care Resource and Referral organizations. Examples in Wayne, Johnston, Stanly, McDowell, and Durham counties show varying costs, funding sources, schedules, and graduate outcomes, with some graduates entering child care jobs and others pursuing further education.

A Norwalk, Iowa family says a DOT highway expansion project affected their 68-year-old well, leaving them without clean water for two months. Erin and Mark Paschell said they were told construction would avoid the well, but they now must bring in water for cooking and cannot bathe their children or do laundry at home. The DOT said it is investigating what happened and working to resolve the issue. Connecting to Warren County’s rural water system could take 30 to 60 days, so Mark and a contractor dug a trench and laid a water line themselves. The DOT has offered to put the family in a hotel and reimburse cleaning supplies for damage caused by dirty water.

Panthers coach Bob Boughner said injured goaltenders Roberto Luongo and James Reimer could become more active next week and may be ready to rejoin the lineup. Luongo has missed 23 games with a lower-body injury, while Reimer is nearing the two-week mark after pulling his groin. Boughner hopes both can practice Monday, pending input from goaltending coach Robb Tallas.

In their absence, Harri Sateri has started and posted a .937 save percentage, delaying Samuel Montembeault’s NHL debut. If Luongo or Reimer returns, Montembeault would likely be sent back to AHL Springfield. Forward Jamie McGinn will return Saturday against Detroit after missing two games with an upper-body injury and will play on the third line with Jared McCann and Maxim Mamin.

Backtests using Yahoo Finance Bitcoin data from 2014 indicate a positive end-of-month, or turn-of-the-month, effect that may support a trading strategy. The tested approach optimized entry days before month-end and exit days after the new month, with results showing higher average gains than random periods of similar length. One version produced a 3.3% average gain per trade, 41.8% CAGR, 16% time in the market, and 25% maximum drawdown. The strategy is acknowledged as somewhat curve-fitted, and an improved version reduced drawdowns but also lowered CAGR due to fewer trades. The article concludes that Bitcoin’s end-of-month effect can potentially be used as a turn-of-the-month strategy.

A retrospective review examined 377 intubated, mechanically ventilated COVID-19 ICU patients who underwent bedside percutaneous tracheostomy at Jaber Al Ahmad Al Sabah Hospital in Kuwait between March 2020 and March 2022. The hospital adopted percutaneous tracheostomy, generally after at least 7 days of intubation, to reduce transfers, staffing needs, and contamination risk.

Patients had a mean age of 56.2 years and mean BMI of 31.3; 59% were male. Common comorbidities included diabetes (50%) and hypertension (48%). The mean time from intubation to tracheostomy was 17.4 days. At the time of procedure, 29% were on ECMO and 23% on dialysis.

Complications occurred in 85 cases (23%): 6% intra-operative, 9% early, and 7% late. Minor bleeding was the most common complication, occurring in 54 cases (14%). Other complications included peristomal wound infection, pneumothorax, loss of airway, tracheo-esophageal fistula, tracheo-innominate fistula, and one conversion to open tracheostomy. No deaths were attributed to the procedure.

After tracheostomy, 54% of patients were weaned from sedation after a mean of 7.5 days, and 41% were weaned from mechanical ventilation after a mean of 12.9 days. Overall mortality was 63%, with all deaths related to COVID-19 complications. Among discharged patients, 38% were decannulated before discharge. The authors concluded that percutaneous tracheostomy can be safely performed in COVID-19 patients and may facilitate weaning, while optimal timing remains uncertain.

The ADS9803 can be reset through the RESET pin or register field, and powered down through the PWDN pin or PD_CH field. After reset or power-up, registers return to default values and the device requires an initialization sequence with a free-running sampling clock. User configuration includes analog input range, bandwidth, common-mode range, data interface lanes, and reference settings.

The device converts analog inputs after initialization and supports speed-boost mode up to 8MSPS for one selected analog input channel pair while the other six channels remain idle. Register access uses 16-bit configuration registers in three banks with 8-bit addresses. SPI write and read operations require bank selection through register 0x03, and read access uses SPI_RD_EN and SPI_MODE settings. Multiple ADS9803 devices can be configured in SPI daisy-chain mode by setting DAISY_CHAIN_LEN; daisy-chain writes require N × 24 SCLKs.

The register section describes fields for SPI mode, daisy-chain length, bank selection, data format, averaging, XOR operation, digital test patterns, speed-boost mode, gain error correction, power-down, input bandwidth, output lanes, common-mode range, and initialization-related settings. Reserved fields should remain at default values.

In application information, the ADS9803 is described as an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS DAQ system for ATE applications. With calibration, it has 0.0015% TUE at 25°C ±5°C. It supports multiplexed PMU signals, low-noise and wide-bandwidth modes, and wide-bandwidth settling to 99.95% full scale in 7.5µs. Layout guidance includes separate decoupling, short reference connections, and keeping analog and reference signals away from noise sources.

Yale-New Haven Hospital sued Clifford Mitchell and Laureen and Vincent Wilczynski to collect unpaid medical bills. Mitchell and Laureen Wilczynski raised special defenses alleging the hospital violated the Hill-Burton Act and Connecticut’s hospital bed funds statute by failing to provide required free-care notices, and they filed CUTPA counterclaims based on those alleged violations.

The hospital moved for summary judgment, arguing the services were rendered, charges were reasonable, the defendants owed payment, and the defenses and counterclaims were legally invalid because no private cause of action existed under the cited statutes. The court rejected these arguments, finding persuasive authority that indigent patients may enforce Hill-Burton obligations and may assert noncompliance as a defense to hospital collection actions. The court also held that similar reasoning applied to the hospital bed funds statute and that alleged violations of either statute could support CUTPA claims. It further found that CUTPA claims could proceed even if the underlying statutes lacked private remedies, and rejected the hospital’s federal preemption argument.

The court denied the hospital’s motions for summary judgment in all three cases.

Cancer screening can detect early signs of cancer before symptoms appear, improving the chance of successful treatment. The NHS offers three main screening programmes: cervical screening every five years for women and people with a cervix aged 25 to 64, breast screening every three years for women and people aged 50 to 71, and bowel screening every two years for people aged 50 to 74.

Cervical screening tests for high-risk HPV using a sample from the cervix. A negative result means a low chance of cervical cancer; a positive result may lead to further testing or colposcopy. Breast screening uses mammograms to detect breast cancer, and people over 71 can arrange continued screening. Bowel screening uses a home FIT kit to detect tiny amounts of blood in stool; a positive result leads to urgent colonoscopy.

Screening can also identify pre-cancerous changes, particularly in cervical and bowel screening, and may reduce deaths from breast, bowel, and cervical cancers. Eligible people are usually invited by post, but missed or overdue appointments can be checked through a GP surgery or relevant screening service. People with symptoms should contact a doctor rather than wait for routine screening.

Some screening, such as prostate cancer checks, is handled case by case with a doctor. People with higher risk, including women with neurofibromatosis type 1, may need earlier screening. Private screening may be an option for those outside NHS eligibility or with concerns such as family history or unusual symptoms.

The lecture introduces computation of the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and the fast Fourier transform (FFT), a class of algorithms that computes the DFT far more efficiently than direct computation. Direct DFT computation requires about \(N^2\) complex multiplications and additions, making large transforms costly. FFT algorithms exploit DFT properties, especially periodicity and decomposition, to reduce computation. For \(N\) expressed as a product of factors, the FFT complexity is proportional to \(N\) times the sum of those factors; when \(N\) is a power of 2, it becomes proportional to \(N \log_2 N\).

The lecture develops a decimation-in-time FFT for \(N\) a power of 2. The input sequence is split into even- and odd-indexed subsequences, whose \(N/2\)-point DFTs are computed as \(G(k)\) and \(H(k)\). The full DFT is then formed as \(X(k)=G(k)+W_N^kH(k)\), using the periodicity of the smaller DFTs. This decomposition is applied recursively until two-point DFTs remain.

The resulting flow graph consists of repeated “butterfly” computations. A simplification uses the fact that powers of \(W_N\) separated by \(N/2\) differ by a factor of \(-1\), so each butterfly can be implemented with one multiplication followed by an addition and subtraction. The lecture notes that the input order becomes rearranged, later identified as bit-reversed order, and concludes by previewing further FFT forms and memory/storage considerations.

The passage introduces indexed containers as representations of indexed datatypes and relates them to generalized polynomials and polynomial functors. It explains that monads on such functors require choices of unit and multiplication, motivating a characterization of monoid structures on indexed containers.

The work extends Uustalu’s characterization of monoid structures from non-indexed to indexed containers, defines the corresponding monoidal structure, proves that these structures precisely match monad structures on indexed container functors, and provides examples including products of indexed container monads, indexed state and writer monads, and a free monad yielding well-scoped λ-terms. The development is formalized in Cubical Agda.

The passage also reviews related work on polynomial monads, container formalizations, and distributive laws, then begins defining indexed containers, their extents as endofunctors on Set-indexed families, their morphisms, their category ICI, and the full and faithful extent functor into endofunctors on SetI.

The lecture introduces Szemerédi’s graph regularity lemma, a tool stating that every graph has a vertex partition into a bounded number of parts such that most pairs of parts behave “random-like.” For vertex sets \(X,Y\), the edge density is the number of edges between them divided by \(|X||Y|\). A pair \((X,Y)\) is \(\epsilon\)-regular if every sufficiently large \(A\subseteq X\) and \(B\subseteq Y\) has edge density within \(\epsilon\) of the density between \(X\) and \(Y\). A partition is \(\epsilon\)-regular if only an \(\epsilon\)-weighted fraction of vertex pairs lie between non-\(\epsilon\)-regular parts.

Szemerédi’s regularity lemma states that for every \(\epsilon\), there is an \(M\), depending only on \(\epsilon\), such that every graph has an \(\epsilon\)-regular partition into at most \(M\) parts. Variants can require equitable partitions and a minimum number of parts.

The proof uses an energy increment argument. The energy of a partition is a weighted mean of squared edge densities between its parts. Refining a partition never decreases energy, and refining along subsets witnessing irregularity increases energy by at least a fixed amount depending on \(\epsilon\). If a partition is not \(\epsilon\)-regular, one refines all irregular pairs simultaneously, increasing energy by at least \(\epsilon^5\). Since energy lies between 0 and 1, this process stops after boundedly many steps, yielding an \(\epsilon\)-regular partition.

The proof gives a very large bound on the number of parts, a tower-type function in \(1/\epsilon\). Gowers proved that such tower-type bounds are essentially unavoidable. The lecture also notes that equitable versions require modifying the iterative proof rather than adjusting the final partition, because regularity is not necessarily preserved under refinement.

Digital piracy emerged with mass Internet connectivity and digital content, beginning prominently with Napster in 1999, and has remained resilient despite legal, technical, educational, and policy countermeasures. It reduces revenues by enabling consumers to substitute licensed purchases with unlicensed copies, though piracy loss estimates are imprecise because not every pirated copy equals a lost sale.

The study asks how firms can design business models to reduce the negative impact of digital piracy. It analyzes Netflix and Spotify as case studies using archival sources, industry reports, media materials, company information, academic literature, and interviews with executives from media firms and the two platforms.

The passage argues that piracy attracts users through low perceived cost, broad content access, release-window and geographic bypassing, DRM-free use, and convenience, while also having drawbacks such as inconsistent quality, technical effort, slower access, legal risk, and limited discovery or community features. Piracy is more attractive for audio and film than for written and interactive works because copies are easier to create, share, and consume.

Spotify and Netflix respond through business model innovation: streaming access, subscription or freemium pricing, broad device compatibility, large catalogs, consistent quality, social features, recommendations, and wider geographic availability. Their models compete less by eradicating piracy and more by improving the consumption experience, especially convenience, discovery, personalization, and social interaction.

The passage concludes that digital distribution business models can offer effective responses to piracy, especially when enabled by digital technologies. It suggests these lessons may apply to other content categories, while noting that industry differences and boundary conditions require further research.

The Chargers’ future in San Diego is being determined largely by the NFL and team ownership, with Chairman Dean Spanos reportedly close to choosing a move to Los Angeles but still seeking league help to stay. The NFL previously pledged an additional $100 million, bringing its total commitment to $300 million, while the Chargers’ Measure C plan included a $350 million team contribution. The projected $1.025 billion total remains up to $175 million short of estimated Mission Valley stadium costs. Spanos has until Jan. 15 to accept the option to join the Rams in Los Angeles. Any downtown stadium plan involving public money would require a public vote in 2018 or 2020.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 27, 2015. For the quarter, net sales were $49.6 billion, up from $37.4 billion a year earlier, and net income was $10.7 billion, up from $7.7 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.85, compared with $1.28. For the first nine months of fiscal 2015, net sales were $182.2 billion and net income was $42.3 billion.

Growth was driven mainly by iPhone sales following the launch of iPhone 6 and 6 Plus. Quarterly iPhone net sales rose 59% to $31.4 billion, while unit sales rose 35% to 47.5 million. iPad net sales declined 23% to $4.5 billion, and unit sales declined 18%. Mac net sales rose 9% to $6.0 billion. Services net sales rose 12% to $5.0 billion. Greater China net sales increased 112% to $13.2 billion.

Apple reported total assets of $273.2 billion, total liabilities of $147.5 billion and shareholders’ equity of $125.7 billion. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $202.8 billion. Long-term debt was $47.4 billion, with $2.5 billion classified as current. Operating cash flow for the first nine months was $67.8 billion.

During the quarter, Apple repurchased shares, paid dividends, issued additional debt, began shipping Apple Watch and the new MacBook, and announced Apple Music, iOS 9, OS X El Capitan and watchOS 2. The company also described ongoing tax matters, legal proceedings involving Smartflash and Samsung, supply-chain risks, and accounting policies related to financial instruments, derivatives, debt, equity compensation and segment reporting.

Mariano Del Cid-Mendez appealed his illegal reentry conviction and sentence, challenging 8 U.S.C. § 1326(b)(1), (2) and the use of mandatory Sentencing Guidelines. The Fifth Circuit held his constitutional challenge was foreclosed by Almendarez-Torres and circuit precedent. The Government conceded he preserved his Booker claim, and the record did not show the district court would have imposed the same sentence under advisory Guidelines. The court vacated the sentence and remanded for further proceedings.

Southern Illinois defeated Evansville 73-61 at the Ford Center after a late push. Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull said China has the strongest obligation to use its leverage to curb North Korea’s nuclear and missile threats. His comments followed a failed North Korean missile test and came ahead of US Vice President Mike Pence’s visit to Australia. Beijing faces pressure, especially from the US, to take tougher action against Pyongyang.

The study examined the relative role of age groups in four Omicron epidemic waves in France from March 1 to Dec. 29, 2022, using publicly available ICU admission data and a relative risk statistic comparing age-group proportions before and after epidemic peaks. Four waves were analyzed: Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Autumn-Winter.

Results indicated that children aged 10–19 had the highest relative risk in the Spring wave and Autumn wave, while children aged 0–9 had the highest estimate in the Summer wave. In the Autumn-Winter wave, the highest estimate was among adults aged 30–39, followed by adults aged 40–49 and persons over 80. The authors concluded that leading relative roles in propagating Omicron waves shifted over time from children and younger adults to adults aged 30–49 and those over 80.

The study suggests that increasing booster vaccination coverage among adults, and possibly children, may help mitigate Omicron transmission, and that additional efforts may be needed to limit spread among elderly persons, including in Long-Term Care facilities. Limitations include possible effects of inconsistent infection detection and uncertainty about the relationship between the relative risk statistic and transmission roles.

Randall Margraves, father of three Larry Nassar victims, lunged at Nassar in a Michigan courtroom after the judge denied his request for time alone with him. Deputies restrained Margraves, who later apologized; Judge Janice Cunningham declined to punish him but said assault was unacceptable. The incident occurred during Nassar’s third sentencing hearing on assault charges related to Twistars gymnastics club. More than 30 victims had given statements in the hearing, following a prior hearing where over 150 women and girls said Nassar abused them. Nassar had already received sentences of up to 175 years for abuse and 60 years for child pornography.

An international team led by Harald Ebeling of the University of Hawaiʻi discovered a distant quiescent galaxy, eMACSJ1341-QG-1, magnified 30 times by gravitational lensing from the massive galaxy cluster eMACSJ1341.9-2441. Observed with the Hubble Space Telescope, the extreme magnification allows astronomers to study a rare galaxy that has stopped forming stars. Follow-up observations are underway in Chile and on Maunakea, and the discovery was published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

Indian equity markets rose for the fourth consecutive week ended Friday, supported by a normal monsoon forecast, strong IT earnings, positive global cues and expectations of healthy corporate results. The Sensex gained 222.93 points, or 0.65%, to close at 34,415.58, while the Nifty50 rose 83.45 points, or 0.80%, to 10,564.05. Gains were partly limited by higher crude oil prices, a weaker rupee and selling in banking stocks amid expectations of a more hawkish RBI stance. WPI inflation eased to 2.47% in March. The rupee fell 92 paise to 66.13 against the dollar. Foreign institutional investors sold shares worth Rs 2,821.24 crore, while domestic institutional investors bought Rs 2,124.16 crore. IT, metal, FMCG and realty indices gained, while PSU banks, energy and Bank Nifty declined. TCS led weekly Sensex gainers after strong earnings, while Axis Bank was the top loser.

Around 400 Brentwood high and middle school students were sent home after a 70-pound boa constrictor escaped from a biology classroom enclosure. The snake was later found beneath the floor wrapped around pipes.

Larry Connors’ Multiple Days Up and Multiple Days Down strategy, from “High Probability Trading,” is a mean-reversion ETF strategy that buys when an ETF is above its 200-day moving average, below its 5-day moving average, and has declined at least 4 of the last 5 trading days. It sells when the ETF closes above its 5-day moving average, with no stop-loss. Tests through December 2020 found mixed ETF results and the lowest profit factor among Connors’ compared mean-reversion strategies. A SPY and QQQ version had 287 trades, a 1.82 profit factor, 12% maximum drawdown, 2.4% CAGR, and 7.7% market exposure. Short-side results were generally difficult, though SPY and QQQ shorts showed a 65% win rate and 0.68% average gain.

Freeport High School recognized students in grades 9-12 for second-quarter academic excellence with High Honors and Honors. Aston Villa beat Burton Albion 3-2 at Villa Park, with goals from Scott Hogan, Albert Adomah and Jack Grealish. Burton scored through an Ahmed Elmohamady own goal and Liam Boyce. Villa’s sixth straight win left them third, one point behind Derby County.

Virginia Chestnuts is a family-owned orchard in Nelson County, Virginia, operated by David and Kim Bryant. After purchasing land in 2003, they tested chestnut viability, then planted more than 1,600 blight-resistant Dunstan trees. Despite weather and cicada challenges, the orchard produced strong harvests, including at least 3,000 pounds in 2017, drawing interest from local bakers, brewers, distillers, and food hubs.

The orchard harvests from mid-September to late October, processing and storing chestnuts on-site before delivery or shipping. The Bryants sell raw chestnuts in the shell or peeled, and promote them through tastings, roasting events, and recipe sharing. Their chestnuts have been used in breads, stuffing, beer, restaurant dishes, and desserts. Virginia Chestnuts also participated in Richmond’s Fire, Flour & Fork event, where they roasted chestnuts and highlighted their role in reviving a seasonal American tradition.

A near-complete skull of a new early mammal relative, Cifelliodon wahkarmoosuch, was discovered in eastern Utah. The small, hair-covered, egg-laying animal had a snout, buck teeth and plant-crushing molars. Published in Nature, the study suggests Pangea split about 15 million years later than previously thought and that early mammal relatives were more diverse and globally dispersed during the dinosaur era than scientists had believed. The fossil was found on Bureau of Land Management land and is displayed at the Natural History Museum of Utah.
