Michigan State University scientists studied adaptive multi-paddock (AMP) grass-fed cattle operations and grain-fed feedlots, finding that AMP grazing can potentially offset greenhouse gas emissions and make the finishing phase of beef production a net carbon sink. At MSU research sites, they compared cattle productivity and emissions from digestion, manure, feed production, energy use and soil erosion. AMP systems showed environmental benefits, while feedlot emissions were higher, largely due to fertilizer-related nitrogen emissions from feed production. However, feedlots produced the same amount of beef on half the land, leaving more land for other uses. Researchers noted that carbon sequestration may decline over time and that AMP is less productive than feedlots but more productive than continuous grazing. Rowntree emphasized that both grass- and grain-fed systems have areas for improvement, including reduced fertilizer use, cover crops and grazing practices that allow plant recovery, improve root systems and build soil organic matter.

Maria Sharapova lost in the first round of Wimbledon to qualifier Vitalia Diatchenko 6-7 (3), 7-6 (3), 6-4 after repeatedly giving up leads, including serving for the match. The defeat was especially unexpected given Sharapova’s strong Grand Slam opener record and Diatchenko’s limited tour-level success. The result was part of a record wave of first-round exits by seven top-10 men’s and women’s seeds, including Petra Kvitova, Caroline Garcia, Sloane Stephens, Elina Svitolina, Dominic Thiem, David Goffin and Grigor Dimitrov. Players cited grass-court unpredictability, pressure and the quick transition from clay to grass as possible factors. Sharapova said she failed to play correctly in crucial moments.

At Leander High School’s 2017 prom, senior Keilany Solano was named prom queen but gave her tiara and sash to fellow nominee Abby Cano, a classmate with Down syndrome. Solano said the gesture was unplanned and that she believed Cano would be happier and deserved it more. Cano’s mother said she was surprised and touched, noting her daughter has long been treated kindly at school.

The TPS7H500x-SP devices are radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. They generate an internal 1.23-V bandgap reference, divided to 0.613 V for the error amplifier, and require a 470-nF REFCAP capacitor. The transconductance error amplifier compares VSENSE to the lower of SS or the 0.613-V reference, with compensation connected at COMP.

Output voltage is programmed with a resistor divider to VSENSE. Soft start is set by a capacitor on SS; synchronous rectifier outputs activate after SS exceeds 1 V. Switching frequency can be set by an internal oscillator, external synchronization, or primary-secondary synchronization. Internal oscillator mode uses an RT resistor and supports 100 kHz to 2 MHz switching; SYNC outputs twice the switching frequency. External synchronization leaves RT floating and applies a 200-kHz to 4-MHz clock at SYNC. Primary-secondary mode uses one controller’s SYNC output to clock another controller, with possible 90° or 270° phase shift.

The devices provide different combinations of primary outputs OUTA/OUTB and synchronous rectifier outputs SRA/SRB. External gate drivers are recommended because output peak current capability is about 150 mA. Dead time and leading-edge blanking are programmable on some devices, while TPS7H5003-SP has fixed 50-ns typical values. Pulse skipping addresses minimum-on-time limits, including during high-frequency operation.

Duty-cycle limits are configured with DCL on supported devices for 50%, 75%, or 100% operation; TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50%. CS_ILIM senses current for PWM operation and overcurrent protection. When CS_ILIM reaches 1.05 V, cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins and hiccup-mode timing is controlled by a capacitor on HICC. FAULT enables external protection functions and shuts down switching when its threshold is exceeded. Slope compensation is programmed with RSC to mitigate subharmonic oscillation. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C typical and restarts below 160°C typical.

The application section describes use in buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge converters, including a TPS7H5001-SP synchronous push-pull GaN design example. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing high-current and switching loops, careful routing of feedback and noise-sensitive traces, close placement of bypass and compensation components, and appropriate filtering of current-sense signals. Power supply recommendations specify a 4-V to 14-V input range and at least 0.1 µF VIN bypass capacitance.

SFS is disabled by default and requires customer BIOS opt-in, with optional customer co-signing of update packages. During early boot, BIOS may provide a customer RSA public key to ASP for package verification; if co-signing is enabled, packages authenticate first against the customer key and then the AMD SFS key. Update packages can modify registers, replace firmware images, or update firmware components, and they validate applicable firmware and patch levels before applying. SEV updates are automatically committed to prevent rollback, and SNP systems require update pages to be HV-FIXED. SFS update packages are non-persistent across reboots and may be applied during OS boot, after boot, or during operation. Issuing SFS commands requires aligned memory buffers and communication through the ASP TEE mailbox. ASP verifies memory protection, customer and AMD signatures, executes the patch, updates patch level information, and returns status. Commands also support retrieving firmware and patch version information. Packages are named by family, AGESA release, and sequence number, and released packages must match the firmware and system patch levels on the target system. Updates generally run alongside x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact; some SEV updates may require virtual machines to stop and restart.

Samsung Electronics is expected to beat fourth-quarter 2016 earnings forecasts despite the Note 7 fallout, driven by strong chip sales. FnGuide put operating income consensus at about $6.5 billion, while some firms projected over $6.63 billion. IBK Securities forecast $7.21 billion. Samsung will announce earnings guidance on Friday.

Episode three of Marvel’s Inhumans, titled “Divide and Conquer,” airs on ABC at 9:00 p.m. ET and follows the Royal Family after Maximus’s coup forces them to Earth. Viewers without cable can stream ABC through Sling TV or DirecTV Now where available. Sling TV offers ABC in eight markets through its $20 basic package plus a $5 Broadcast Extra add-on, with a 7-day free trial. DirecTV Now’s “Live a Little” package costs $35, includes ABC in 39 markets, and also offers a 7-day free trial. Both services allow viewing online or through their apps on compatible devices.

The Second Circuit affirmed the district court’s denial of Rodney Nicholson’s habeas petition challenging his New York second-degree murder conviction. Nicholson argued that state courts violated due process by excluding Darnell Phelps’s hearsay confession and denying a new trial under Chambers v. Mississippi. The court assumed without deciding that Chambers could apply to retrial motions but held that Nicholson failed to show the state courts improperly rejected reliable exculpatory hearsay. Phelps’s confession conflicted with his prior denial, could not apparently be tested by cross-examination, and may have been tailored to public forensic evidence. The court also noted eyewitness testimony identifying Nicholson and that Phelps’s confession did not necessarily exonerate him. Because the confession was suspect, denial of a new trial did not violate due process.

Helping Hands Hawaii’s Ready to Learn program is holding its annual school supply drive from June 1 to July 31, 2017, to provide free basic educational supplies to low-income and homeless students. American Savings Bank branches will serve as collection sites from June 14 to July 14, with donations staying on each island to benefit local students. RTL prepares school supply kits for all grade levels, valued at about $10 each, using donated and bulk-purchased supplies. High-demand items include notebooks, crayons, portfolios, glue, scissors, pens, calculators, composition books, erasers, folder paper, rulers and backpacks. As of April 2017, the program had raised more than $12,000 and collected enough supplies for 3,115 kits, benefiting more than 6,000 students. Supporters can donate supplies or money, organize drives, volunteer to pack kits, or contribute online, by mail or in person. Students in grades K-12 must be referred by a participating social service organization by June 23, 2017.

Members of Congress continue to be paid during a government shutdown because the Constitution requires compensation and the 27th Amendment limits changes to that pay. Since 1981, lawmakers’ salaries have been funded through mandatory spending, which shutdowns do not affect. Federal workers may miss paychecks if the shutdown lasts, though furloughed workers are guaranteed retroactive pay under a 2019 law. Some lawmakers have proposed withholding or docking congressional pay during shutdowns, but constitutional limits complicate such efforts. Funding is set to run out Tuesday amid disputes over a short-term funding bill, Medicaid cuts, and Affordable Care Act tax credits.

A man identified as 27-year-old Akayed Ullah set off a crude pipe bomb strapped to his body in a subway passage near Times Square during Monday morning rush hour, injuring himself and three others with non-life-threatening injuries. Mayor Bill de Blasio and Police Commissioner James O’Neill called it an attempted terror attack. Officials said Ullah, who lives in Brooklyn and may be of Bangladeshi descent, was inspired by the Islamic State group but apparently had no direct contact with it. The low-tech device was attached with Velcro and plastic ties. The blast caused smoke, a large emergency response, and major transit disruptions around the Port Authority terminal. President Donald Trump was briefed on the explosion.

Coach Sutter discussed player comparisons, his transition into coaching after he could no longer play, and his path through minor-league and organizational coaching roles. He said Dustin Brown was central to the team’s identity and wanted to make an impact in the playoffs after a disappointing regular season. Sutter emphasized how difficult it is to win, citing sacrifice, opportunity, and team commitment. He said his family rarely discussed his brothers’ championships but he was proud of them. He reflected on past playoff lessons, the team’s resilience, special plays by Nash and Doughty, roster differences from the previous Stanley Cup team, and the challenge of understanding winning and losing at that level. He said lineup decisions are based on the best chance to win each game.

STAT’s Morning Rounds newsletter notes that if Congress does not fund the government by tomorrow, Medicare patients receiving hospital-level care at home through the Acute Hospital Care at Home initiative must be discharged or returned to hospitals by September 30, 2025. The passage also lists recent health-related headlines on FDA actions, drug trials, hospital reporting, food insecurity, autism-related claims, and biotech developments.

The coach expressed confidence in the coaching staff but emphasized that players determine results on the ice. He praised the team for playing within its strengths, keeping the game simple, defending hard, blocking shots, and improving through effort and execution. He said the group respects Cully and understands the opportunity ahead, but must earn success through performance. The team’s focus is on staying in the moment, controlling what it can, following its process and routines, and being at its best in the next game.

The speaker praises a player’s defensive ability, speed, reach, and penalty-killing skills, noting he can create chances when opportunities arise. They also say Evgeni looks healthy, energetic, and urgent in the series, and describe Zetterberg as consistent, smart, and dangerous across the ice.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 29, 2021, reporting its first quarter 2021 financial results under Item 2.02. The filing incorporates a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and information on non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Tesla reported record Q3 2025 deliveries of 497,099 vehicles, up 7.4% year over year and above forecasts, driven by U.S. buyers rushing before the $7,500 federal EV tax credit expired on 30 September. Incentives helped lift sales, but analysts questioned whether demand was pulled forward and whether Tesla can meet its 1.61 million full-year delivery goal. U.S. sales surged, while Europe and UK performance weakened amid stronger competition. Investor reaction was muted, with attention shifting to pricing, new models, and Tesla’s energy division, which delivered a record 12.5 GWh of storage capacity. The passage also lists other global finance and business headlines and describes Pan Finance as a global financial intelligence publication.

Around 200 people gathered in Nottingham’s market square for a vigil for 18-year-old Mariam Moustafa, who died after an attack outside the intu Victoria Centre. Her father, Mohamed Moustafa, thanked attendees and called for justice, saying the turnout sent a strong message of unity. Speakers included Mariam’s sister, a former teacher and an Egyptian Coptic priest, who called for answers and an end to violence. Attendees expressed support for the family and solidarity against violence. The event, organised by Yousuf Farooq of Nottingham Stand Up To Racism and the Nottingham People’s Assembly, drew widespread online interest and was described as a moment for the city to come together.

The National Beer Wholesalers Association launched DeliveringLocalJobs.com to highlight 135,000 beer distribution employees across all 50 states. The campaign says these workers earn $11.2 billion in wages and help generate $70 billion in U.S. GDP, nearly $180 million in community economic impacts and nearly $13 billion in tax revenue. The website features videos, employee stories, state-by-state economic data, and information on distributors’ work with more than 5,000 brewers and importers.

The UC1825B-SP oscillator uses a sawtooth waveform, with the rising edge controlled by RT and CT and the falling edge setting output dead time. RT should be selected first based on maximum duty cycle, then CT based on frequency and DMAX; recommended RT values are 1 kΩ to 100 kΩ, and DMAX below 70% is not recommended.

The device is a dual-output controller with integrated push-pull drivers and can support half-bridge and full-bridge applications using external high-side drivers. It supports voltage-mode topologies and, with minimal external components, current-mode topologies using RAMP for current sense and ILIM for current limit, with external slope compensation.

A 215-kHz switching frequency was selected as a tradeoff between bandwidth and efficiency, using RT = 10 kΩ and CT = 680 pF. The design targeted 30% duty cycle, used a transformer turns ratio of 2.2, auxiliary winding ratio of 1.5, primary inductance of 120 µH, and output inductor of 2.2 µH. A 10% starting value is generally used for ΔVclamp in the RCD clamp, and Kclamp of 1.5 is recommended. The output diode was selected with a 60-V rating, and push-pull MOSFETs should be rated about 2.5 to 3 times the input voltage.

The output filter used about 1145 µF capacitance and a 500-nH inductor to reduce ripple, with 0.5 Ω damping. Type IIB compensation was used with a 5-kHz crossover target. The sense resistor detects transformer ripple current and shuts down switching if peak current exceeds the set limit.

The device operates from a well-regulated 10-V to 30-V input supply. Layout guidance emphasizes low-EMI inductors, short and thick power traces, close placement of capacitors and compensation parts, separated signal and power grounding, ground planes, and careful handling of high di/dt output currents. TI also provides documentation update, support, ESD caution, packaging, and warranty disclaimer information.

The passage highlights azcentral Cardinals video coverage and discusses quarterback Carson Palmer’s career and outlook. Palmer joined Arizona in 2013, had a strong 2015 season after a 2014 ACL injury, but declined in 2016. He said he feels healthy, evaluates his future yearly, still enjoys football, and prefers the Cardinals’ underdog role after their 7-8-1 season.

Microsoft filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2022. For the three months ended December 31, 2022, revenue was $52.7 billion, up from $51.7 billion a year earlier; net income was $16.4 billion, down from $18.8 billion; and diluted earnings per share were $2.20, down from $2.48. For the six months ended December 31, 2022, revenue was $102.9 billion, net income was $34.0 billion, and diluted EPS was $4.54.

As of December 31, 2022, Microsoft had total assets of $364.6 billion, total liabilities of $181.4 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $183.1 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $99.5 billion. Net cash from operations was $34.4 billion for the six-month period.

Segment revenue for the quarter was $17.0 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $21.5 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $14.2 billion for More Personal Computing. Microsoft Cloud revenue was $27.1 billion for the quarter and $52.8 billion for the six months ended December 31, 2022.

Microsoft recorded $800 million in employee severance expenses related to a January 18, 2023 announcement to reduce its workforce by approximately 10,000 jobs through the third quarter of fiscal 2023. The company also noted its pending $68.7 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.

Bollinger Bands measure an asset’s volatility using a moving average and upper and lower bands based on standard deviations. Wider bands indicate higher volatility, while contracting bands indicate low volatility. The Bollinger Band Squeeze strategy looks for periods of low volatility followed by a breakout, then trades in the breakout direction.

The passage describes a backtest using the difference between the upper and lower bands as a squeeze indicator. The tested strategy performed poorly across many assets, with consumer staples as a possible exception. On Pepsi, it returned 12.5% versus 14.8% for buy and hold while being invested 61% of the time. The authors state that multiple versions and variations were tested without success and caution against relying on anecdotal evidence.

John A. Bollinger, born in 1950, developed Bollinger Bands in the 1980s and authored *Bollinger on Bollinger Bands*. He also published the *Capital Growth Letter* newsletter in 1987.

The passage notes that the squeeze is a breakout strategy, unlike mean reversion strategies, and may have lower win rates and whipsaws. It emphasizes backtesting, positive expectancy, disciplined execution, and mechanical trading. It also states that strategies may work differently across assets, since stocks tend toward mean reversion while commodities do not.

The passage reports concern in Korea over possible unrest linked to the Tong Hâk movement and speculation about Tai Wen-kun retaliation. Augustine Heard notes interrupted communications, the King’s alarm, Admiral Harmony’s inquiry, and the arrival of the U.S.S. Petrel at Chemulpo, where Chinese and Japanese warships were also present. Heard asked Commander Dayton to remain temporarily and requested ammunition for rifles. The latter part contains an official order responding to Confucian scholars’ petition, directing authorities to arrest movement leaders, suppress “heterodoxy,” issue proclamations, enforce obedience to the law, and uphold loyalty and filial duty.

Butterfield reported a strong Q1 2018, with core return on average tangible common equity rising to 24.3% from 22.3% in Q4 2017 and net interest margin increasing to 3.05% from 2.87%. Net interest income grew $3.8 million to $79.9 million, while non-interest income declined 6.1% sequentially due to seasonal factors. Core non-interest expense was $76 million, and the core efficiency ratio was 62.3%, trending toward the 60% target. Total assets reached about $11 billion, deposits averaged $9.8 billion, and loans rose to $4.0 billion, driven by sovereign lending and U.K. residential mortgage growth. Non-accrual loans declined to $42.4 million, and credit conditions remained benign. The bank closed Deutsche Bank’s Global Trust Solutions acquisition, opened operations in Singapore, and continued working toward acquiring Deutsche Bank’s banking operations in Cayman and the Channel Islands, which could increase deposits by up to 20%. Management said Butterfield remains positioned for rising rates, is pursuing further acquisitions, and raised the quarterly dividend to $0.38 per share.

Pedro Russell, after a nontraditional academic path and roles in consulting, education publishing, and education finance, earned an MBA at MIT Sloan and co-founded GPS Partners with Garrison Jones and Stephen McGarvey. GPS focused on acquiring for-profit medical technical schools and identified MedPro Institute, a Boston-area vocational school founded in 1998 by Dr. Samantha Hill.

MedPro offered certificate programs in medical assisting, phlebotomy, medical billing and coding, and dental assisting, combining classroom and hands-on training with small class sizes, high graduation rates, and strong job placement outcomes. Hill was open to selling, and GPS began due diligence after signing a letter of intent.

Russell found MedPro relied mostly on word of mouth and saw growth potential through advertising, but was uncertain how higher enrollment would affect costs. He reviewed major expenses, including rent, cleaning, instructor pay, career services salaries, accreditation fees, supplies, liability insurance, internet, and electricity. He recognized that GPS needed to understand cost behavior and resource usage as enrollment changed before deciding whether to proceed with the acquisition.

The speaker says Andy has overcome injuries, become a key player, and contributed physically in the playoffs. They expect an emotional game in Vancouver, with loud Canucks fans, but stress staying composed and playing their style. They also say Newfoundland’s passionate hockey fans should support another team and benefit the local economy.

Hammerson confirmed it received and rejected a “highly preliminary and non-binding” £4.88bn cash-and-share proposal from Klépierre, valuing it at 615p per share, a 41% premium to its March 16 closing price. Hammerson said the offer was unsolicited, opportunistic, and significantly undervalued the company. Its shares rose to around 545p, about 25% above Friday’s close. Hammerson remains committed to acquiring Intu Properties, citing portfolio quality, leasing opportunities, and expected annual synergies of about £25m. Chairman David Tyler criticized Klépierre’s offer as below book value and partly in shares of a company he described as having a lower-quality portfolio and lower growth prospects.

The speaker says Roli’s injury is unfortunate but creates an opportunity for whoever plays. He emphasizes confidence, moving past a bad play, and focusing on the Stanley Cup Finals. He says teammates trust each other, Roli will help with shooter tendencies, and the goal is to stay prepared, regain rhythm, and play well.

Sen. Cory Booker campaigned in Alabama for Democratic Senate nominee Doug Jones, with attention also on Booker’s possible 2020 presidential ambitions. Alabama is not competitive in presidential general elections but can be important in Democratic primaries because of African-American voters’ influence. Jones’ campaign generally kept national Democrats away to avoid attacks tying him to outsiders, but members of the Congressional Black Caucus campaigned because Jones needed strong black voter turnout. Booker and former Massachusetts Gov. Deval Patrick appeared for Jones, while Sen. Kamala Harris supported him through fundraising and donations. The passage notes that Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama relied heavily on African-American support in Southern primaries, and that Booker’s visit could help introduce him to Alabama voters.

The Second Circuit reviewed a Board of Tax Appeals decision upholding a 1931 income tax deficiency against Pfeiffer based on a preferred stock dividend received on common stock. The court held that section 115(f) of the Revenue Act of 1928 exempted stock dividends without qualification, including preferred stock dividends on common stock, relying on statutory language, legislative history, Treasury practice, and related case law. It also declined to consider the Commissioner’s arguments about taxation of redeemed 1928 preferred shares because those issues were not properly before the court and no cross-appeal had been filed. The deficiency determination was reversed. Judge Learned Hand dissented, arguing that Congress intended to exempt only stock dividends constitutionally protected under Eisner v. Macomber and that preferred shares issued on common stock were taxable income.

Dan Le Batard said people in the Miami Heat organization believed LeBron James had “checked out” during the 2014 NBA Finals and knew he was leaving. The passage connects this claim to James’ current Cavaliers situation, noting expectations he may opt out and questioning whether a similar issue could arise if Cleveland reaches the 2018 Finals.

Bitcoin rose about 2% Friday to $123,874, within 1% of its mid-August all-time high, as the U.S. government shutdown entered its third day. It is up 12% for the week. Standard Chartered’s Geoff Kendrick said bitcoin is trading with “US government risks” and expects a new high soon, with a target of $135,000. Gold, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq also gained Friday.

The California Supreme Court held that a creditor’s failure to present a claim against a deceased debtor’s estate within the statutory period does not extinguish the debt, but only bars the remedy against the estate. Because the debt secured by a deed of trust remained unpaid, the executors could not obtain equitable relief compelling surrender of the security or enjoining a trustee’s sale without paying the debt. The judgment enjoining the sale was reversed, with directions to sustain the demurrer. Justice Crockett, joined by Justice McKinstry, dissented, arguing that failure to present the claim should defeat the lien and allow the estate to recover the property for administration.

Investigators found red-stained bedding and an empty box of Coricidin Cold & Cough medicine at the North Carolina home where Matthew James Phelps said he woke from a medicated stupor to find his wife, Lauren, fatally stabbed. Phelps called 911 on September 1, saying he had taken more cough medicine than he should have and believed it made him kill her. Lauren was still alive when police arrived but later died at a hospital. Phelps, who has no criminal record, is being held without bail on first-degree murder charges.

Google canceled the Daily Stormer’s website registration, saying the neo-Nazi site violated policies against inciting violence, shortly after GoDaddy gave it 24 hours to find a new host. The actions followed a Daily Stormer article ridiculing Heather Heyer, who was killed while protesting a white nationalist rally in Charlottesville. YouTube terminated the site’s channel for hate-speech violations, and Facebook said it removes Daily Stormer links unless posts clearly condemn the content. Other web-service companies, including Tucows and Cloudflare, distanced themselves from hosting the site. The moves came amid broader pressure on tech companies to address extremist content online while balancing free-speech concerns.

Transport CS James Macharia blamed the boda boda sector’s disorder on poor enforcement of existing regulations, saying NTSA and other bodies have failed to implement the laws. He told MPs the ministry is working with county transport committees and the traffic department to improve enforcement. Ruiru MP Simon King’ara called for a separate motorbike safety authority, saying NTSA is overwhelmed, and urged action against those delaying reforms. He noted the sector’s revenue contribution amid disputes with counties, including Nairobi’s CBD ban.

The IRS is furloughing about 34,000 workers, nearly half its workforce, due to the ongoing government shutdown. About 39,870 employees, or 53.6%, will remain on the job. The agency said most operations are closed after a lapse in appropriations.

The passage describes bonded optical devices for wearable electronics and display applications such as AR smart glasses, HUDs, projection systems, smart watches, and phones. It addresses the need for small, high-resolution, bright displays, particularly where pixel pitch must be very small for near-eye viewing. The disclosed devices use monochromatic optical elements, such as red, green, and blue microLED arrays, bonded to carrier or processor elements with active circuitry that controls individual emitters.

The optical elements may be directly or hybrid bonded to silicon, CMOS, glass, TFT, or other backplanes without adhesive, using dielectric-to-dielectric and conductor-to-conductor bonding. These bonding methods can support fine pixel pitches, including below 10 microns and in some cases below 5 microns or 1 micron. The devices may be formed through die-to-wafer, die-to-die, or wafer-to-wafer processes.

Multiple monochromatic bonded optical devices can be combined so their emitted light is superimposed into a multicolor image. Optical pathways may include waveguides, lenses, mirrors, beamsplitters, prisms, input couplings, and output couplings to direct image data to a user. Red, green, and blue LED chips may be bonded to separate carriers or a common carrier and arranged parallel, laterally offset, or angled relative to one another.

The passage also describes optical isolation structures, such as trenches, to limit crosstalk between pixels or groups of pixels. Pixels may be individually controlled or grouped into matrices, allowing brightness control and redundancy. The disclosed bonded optical devices can include arrays of independently controllable LEDs, processor circuitry, optical pathways for superimposed light, and optional adhesive or adhesive-free coupling to waveguides.

The study reviews public financing instruments for innovative cleantech start-ups and SMEs in Europe, many under Horizon 2020. Funding commonly includes loans, equity, grants, and guarantees for areas such as energy efficiency, smart cities, ICT, renewable energy, and healthcare. Key managing bodies include the EIB, EIF, EBRD, EUREKA, and the European Commission. The report benchmarks instruments by metrics including portfolio size, investment size, success rates, TRL, consortium needs, financing share, monitoring frequency, and support services. Many instruments also offer coaching, advisory, commercialization, IP, R&D, and business acceleration support.

The speaker addresses a Washington meeting convened to aid victims of the Johnstown-area calamity in Pennsylvania, emphasizing national sympathy and charity. He reports that Jacksonville, Florida, has pledged $2,000 for relief. Citing a dispatch from Pennsylvania’s governor, he says Williamsport also suffered severe losses, with thousands hungry, homeless, and penniless, and urges immediate food shipments there. He recommends forming committees to collect food, clothing and bedclothing, and money for later rebuilding and refurnishing homes. He expresses hope that the national capital will respond generously and notes that he has personally subscribed to the relief effort.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPU architecture and its improvements over Turing. The GA10x SM has four partitions, a 128 KB shared L1 data cache/shared memory subsystem, third-generation Tensor Cores, and doubled FP32 throughput by enabling FP32 processing on both datapaths. It supports concurrent FP32 and INT32 execution, double-speed FP16, larger L1 cache capacity, and doubled shared memory bandwidth versus Turing. Ampere GPUs are stated to be up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing at the same performance level.

GA10x includes second-generation RT Cores with dedicated BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection hardware, doubling ray/triangle intersection testing rate over Turing. It also adds concurrent RT and graphics or compute processing, and hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur through a new Interpolate Triangle Position unit, enabling faster rendering of moving and deforming geometry.

Third-generation Tensor Cores support additional data types including TF32 and BF16, improve efficiency, and add Fine-Grained Structured Sparsity, which can double effective matrix throughput by skipping zero-valued elements. These Tensor Cores accelerate AI features such as DLSS, denoising, RTX Voice, and NGX services. DLSS on Ampere supports a 9x Super Resolution scaling factor for 8K gaming.

The architecture introduces GDDR6X memory developed with Micron, using PAM4 signaling and MTA encoding to reach up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth. NVIDIA RTX IO uses GPU-based loading and decompression with Microsoft DirectStorage to reduce CPU workload, improve I/O performance, and support faster asset streaming.

The passage also covers NVIDIA A40 and RTX A6000 professional GPUs, highlighting improved FP32, ray tracing, AI, PCIe Gen4, large memory configurations, NVLink support, virtualization, and data center or workstation use cases. GA10x supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, HDCP, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode up to 8K60 HDR, and seventh-generation NVENC for hardware video encoding. Appendices describe GeForce RTX 3090 and RTX 3070 specifications, GDDR6X Error Detection and Replay for overclocking feedback, RTX A6000 performance comparisons, and standard NVIDIA legal notices.

Tennessee National Wildlife Refuge headquarters and Visitor Center will close August 21 for the solar eclipse. Visitors are directed to Cross Creeks National Wildlife Refuge in Dover to view totality, with staff assisting and solar glasses available for $3. Parking rules apply, no lunches will be sold, and event proceeds support Friends of Cross Creeks NWR.

William Brock was convicted of molestation of a juvenile and sentenced to ten years at hard labor. On appeal, he argued that the evidence was insufficient and that the sentence was excessive. The court found that medical testimony, the child’s statements to her mother, testimony about Brock’s access to and control over the child, and the child’s behavior around him supported the jury’s verdict beyond a reasonable doubt. The court also found that the trial judge properly considered sentencing factors and did not abuse discretion. Brock’s conviction and sentence were affirmed.

Centrica’s share price has fallen 35% over the past year, giving it an 8.6% dividend yield. Despite regulatory uncertainty, business model changes, and limited dividend growth prospects, it trades at a P/E ratio of about 10 and is expected to grow earnings 7% this year. Volution reported interim revenue growth of 11.6% and adjusted operating profit growth of 6.7% to £18.3m, while margins fell due to acquisitions. It also acquired New Zealand ventilation supplier Simx Limited. Volution’s dividend yield is 2.2%, with payouts covered 3.3 times by profit, suggesting scope for faster dividend growth.

The study examined education faculty students’ attitudes and opinions toward the Research Methods in Education (RME) course after changes in its name and content. It aimed to determine attitude levels, whether attitudes differed by department and class level, and students’ views on the course and its implementation.

A mixed-method sequential explanatory design was used. The quantitative sample included 190 students from Turkish Teaching, English Teaching, and Pre-School Teaching departments at Bayburt University Faculty of Education. Data were collected with a researcher-developed 21-item attitude scale with three dimensions: contribution to the profession, confidence, and contribution to daily life. Quantitative data were analyzed using Kruskal Wallis H and Mann Whitney U tests because scores were not normally distributed. The qualitative sample consisted of 10 pre-service teachers selected through purposive sampling, and data were gathered through focus group interviews analyzed by content analysis.

Findings showed that students’ attitudes toward the RME course did not differ significantly by department. However, attitudes differed significantly by class level, with a difference between first- and fourth-year students. Among attitude dimensions, contribution to daily life had the highest mean scores. In focus group findings, 90% of participants stated that the course was necessary, especially for understanding scientific research processes and supporting other education courses. Half reported personal gains, 30% reported gains related to scientific research, and 20% reported profession-oriented gains. Regarding teaching processes, 60% said the course duration was insufficient, while others noted the importance of the lecturer’s teaching style and issues with tools and materials.

The study recommends providing prerequisite knowledge before the RME course, offering it in later years, ensuring related courses such as measurement and evaluation are taken beforehand, and considering making RME compulsory, extending its duration or credits, or structuring it as RME 1 and RME 2.

President Bush thanked the press corps at his final press conference and answered questions on the financial bailout, Gaza, national security, the Republican Party, his record, and the transition to President-elect Obama. He said he would request the remaining $350 billion in bailout funds only if Obama asked him to, defended actions taken to stabilize credit markets, and said Obama would face major challenges from the economy and potential attacks on the homeland.

On Gaza, Bush supported a sustainable cease-fire requiring Hamas to stop firing rockets and said Israel had a right to defend itself while being mindful of civilians and humanitarian aid. He defended his two-state peace efforts and said extremist violence had complicated progress.

Bush said North Korea and Iran remained dangerous and emphasized the need for verification in talks with North Korea. He argued the Republican Party should become more inclusive, compassionate, and broad-minded, particularly on immigration. Responding to criticism of his presidency, he defended the Iraq troop surge, tax cuts, and crisis-era economic interventions, while acknowledging mistakes and disappointments including the “Mission Accomplished” banner, some rhetoric, the timing of Social Security reform, Abu Ghraib, and the absence of weapons of mass destruction in Iraq.

He rejected claims that America’s moral standing had been damaged, defended counterterrorism policies, and said most people abroad still viewed the United States as strong and compassionate. On Hurricane Katrina, he said reconstruction was incomplete but improving, defended the speed of some federal rescue efforts, and noted large federal spending for recovery. He called Obama’s election an historic sign of racial progress while saying more work remained. Bush said he hoped Obama would be treated respectfully and wished him success.

This study examined culturally sensitive mentorship needs among entry-level occupational therapy students, particularly those from historically underrepresented groups. Using a cross-sectional electronic survey at a large urban private university, researchers collected responses from 133 students, including 59 who identified as BIPOC, Hispanic/Latinx, or biracial and not white.

Findings showed that current mentorship was insufficient for many students from historically underrepresented groups. While 89.5% had experienced formal or informal mentorship in the past, only 34% currently had a mentor. Students valued mentors with strong interpersonal qualities, relevant professional expertise, availability, shared interests, and, for some, similar cultural or ethnic backgrounds. Many students, especially BIPOC students, considered it important for mentors to recognize their own biases and prejudices. Hispanic/Latinx students were more likely to report lower agreement that mentors worked effectively across background differences or helped integrate personal life with school responsibilities.

Students expressed a need for mentors who demonstrate cultural humility, empathy, anti-racism allyship, and support in navigating discrimination, microaggressions, cultural isolation, and workplace challenges. They also wanted guidance on clinical reasoning, networking, certification preparation, job searching, work-life balance, and transitioning from school to professional practice.

The study concludes that occupational therapy programs should develop culturally sensitive mentorship models combining formal and informal support, mentor training, diverse mentor representation, and institutional commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, justice, and accessibility. Limitations include the single-institution urban sample, cross-sectional design, and limited attention to intersecting identities beyond race and ethnicity.

The Colorado Supreme Court considered an original proceeding seeking prohibition against the Denver district court after it denied defendants’ motion to quash service of process made in California. The underlying case involved fraud and rescission or damages related to the sale of a Denver home. Defendants argued they were California residents, not Colorado residents, so service under Colorado Rule 4(f)(1), which permits out-of-state personal service on Colorado residents, was invalid.

The court held it had authority to entertain prohibition where an inferior court was proceeding without personal jurisdiction. The uncontroverted evidence showed defendants had left Colorado, had no Colorado residence or abode, intended to establish residence at low altitude for health reasons, lived and worked in Ventura, obtained California licenses, registered to vote there, bought lots for a home, and had not returned to Colorado. Plaintiffs failed to prove defendants remained Colorado residents after defendants made a prima facie showing otherwise.

The court concluded the California service was invalid, the trial court lacked personal jurisdiction over defendants, and the trial court erred in denying the motion to quash. The rule to show cause was made absolute.

The Sensex closed 12.31 points lower at 28,339.31, while the Nifty fell 0.14% to 8,792. Five stocks hit new 52-week highs: AIA Engineering, after reporting 17.6% profit growth and declaring an interim dividend; Alkem Laboratories, after posting 24.9% profit growth and higher US sales; KEC International, which touched Rs 170 before closing lower; Exide Industries, which hit Rs 218 and received a buy rating from Anand Rathi; and Kalpataru Power Transmission, which reached Rs 299.85 amid unusually high trading volumes before closing slightly lower.

European markets reached record highs, with the STOXX 600 up about 0.5%, driven by gains in steel and banking stocks. Steelmakers rose after the European Commission proposed reducing tariff-free steel import quotas, while banks benefited from stable bond yields and improved credit margins. Auto stocks weakened, led by BMW after it cut its 2025 profit forecast. Royal Rumble 2017 is set for the Alamodome, with WWE aiming to sell over 60,000 tickets. Confirmed or expected names include Goldberg, Brock Lesnar, John Cena, The Undertaker, and possibly Shawn Michaels in a non-wrestling role. Confirmed matches include AJ Styles defending the WWE Championship against John Cena, Kevin Owens defending the WWE Universal Championship against Roman Reigns with Chris Jericho suspended in a shark cage, and the 30-Man Royal Rumble featuring Goldberg and Lesnar.

Bath Rugby fans faced major travel disruption after their team’s 24-20 Champions Cup loss to Toulon, with snow, ice, wind, rain and cancellations affecting flights from Marseille, Nice and Amsterdam to the UK. Some supporters were stranded for days, forced to reroute via cities including Paris, Munich, Brussels and Madrid, or take delayed trains. Several fans missed work, arranged extra pet care, or risked missing the funeral of fellow supporter Mike Grice. Others experienced airport confusion, overbooking, diversions to Bournemouth and Cardiff, and long runway delays. Bath’s team returned to Bristol on a chartered flight, while many supporters remained in France, though some tried to make the best of the enforced stay.

U.S. rare earth and critical mineral stocks surged after China tightened export restrictions ahead of an expected Xi-Trump meeting. The rules require licenses for certain rare earth-containing products and use of Chinese related technologies. The White House is assessing the impact, while investors speculate the Trump administration may expand investments in domestic supply chains.

The passage presents HCAR, a three-phase hybrid Constraint Acquisition framework designed to reduce over-fitting when learning constraint programming models with global constraints from limited examples. It begins with passive learning to generate candidate global constraints and prune fixed-arity constraints, then uses a Query-Driven Interactive Refinement phase to evaluate global candidates through oracle queries, machine learning-based confidence priors, Bayesian updates, budget management, and subset exploration for rejected constraints. A final active learning phase learns remaining fixed-arity constraints. The work targets over-fitted global constraints such as AllDifferent, Sum, and Count, aiming to preserve valid structures while eliminating spurious ones. Empirical validation is reported to show high accuracy and model coverage with manageable query complexity.

The speaker describes being out of action for about seven months during contract negotiations, wanting to return to competitive hockey. Selection for the Russian Olympic team helped him regain focus. After an offer from North Carolina, Detroit matched it, allowing him to stay with the Red Wings, which he wanted because Detroit felt like a second hometown. He returned quickly, played despite exhaustion, and felt the importance of staying with his teammates. He also recalls Vladimir “Vladi” being present during the Stanley Cup celebration, saying his appearance and reaction inspired the team.

Two Boeing 737 MAX 8 crashes killed 346 people: Lion Air Flight 610 in October 2018 and Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 in March 2019. Both involved sudden loss of control shortly after takeoff. Boeing initially emphasized maintenance and pilot factors but later issued guidance on erroneous angle-of-attack data and uncommanded nose-down movement linked to the Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System (MCAS).

The 737 MAX was developed quickly after Airbus’s A320neo threatened Boeing’s market position. Boeing chose to update the 737 rather than design a new aircraft, adding larger engines that changed the plane’s aerodynamics. MCAS was created to counter a pitch-up tendency, but later design changes made it more powerful, allowed repeated activation, removed a G-force trigger, and left it dependent on a single angle-of-attack sensor. Alerts that could warn pilots of sensor disagreement were optional or not operable unless airlines bought related equipment.

Boeing sought FAA certification by presenting MCAS as a minor modification and worked to avoid simulator training for pilots transitioning from earlier 737 models. Investigations found that key FAA personnel were not fully informed about MCAS changes and that FAA certification and delegation processes had communication, oversight, and independence weaknesses. Many pilots later said they had not been told about MCAS.

The passage also describes Boeing’s historical engineering-centered culture, later changes after the McDonnell Douglas merger, increased focus on shareholder value, layoffs, outsourcing, and employee concerns about quality and management pressure. Internal communications showed Boeing employees had concerns about the 737 MAX program before the crashes.

After the Ethiopian crash, the United States grounded all 737 MAX aircraft in March 2019. The plane remained grounded for 21 months, during which Boeing lost orders and faced major financial, legal, regulatory, and reputational damage. The FAA allowed the aircraft to return to service in November 2020 with new training requirements, including simulator training. Boeing replaced senior leaders, created safety-related oversight changes, and continued to face questions about design, management, regulation, and accountability.

The study examines orbital and spin Edelstein effects in doped monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides under an out-of-plane gate field, focusing on how broken mirror symmetry enables in-plane chiral orbital and spin textures. A five-orbital metal d-state Hamiltonian, fitted to density-functional band structures, is used to model several TMDs and compute Edelstein susceptibilities for electron- and hole-doped systems.

The gate field breaks σh symmetry, producing Rashba-type textures that drive orbital and spin moment accumulation under an in-plane charge current. For electron doping, the orbital Edelstein effect is much larger than the spin Edelstein effect and increases with electron concentration. For hole doping, both effects are dominated by the Γ valley once it is occupied; otherwise the response from K/K′ valleys is weaker.

The results show that compressive strain can raise the Γ valence band relative to K/K′, allowing holes to occupy the Γ pocket at lower doping and strongly enhancing both orbital and spin Edelstein responses. The calculated orbital Edelstein susceptibilities in TMDs are typically larger than values reported for other material systems, suggesting doped gated TMDs as promising platforms for studying orbital Edelstein physics.

Keltner Channels, also called Keltner Bands, are a technical analysis tool developed by Chester W. Keltner in the 1960s to assess volatility, trends, overbought and oversold conditions, and potential entry and exit points. They consist of a middle moving average line, often an EMA, plus upper and lower bands based on a multiple of Average True Range (ATR). The bands expand and contract with volatility.

Keltner Channels differ from Bollinger Bands because Bollinger Bands use standard deviation, while Keltner Channels use ATR. Bollinger Bands are described as more responsive and more variable in expansion and contraction. A common Keltner setting is a 20-period EMA with a 2 ATR multiplier, though optimal settings vary by asset, market conditions, and trading style.

Traders may use Keltner Channels for trend following, breakout trading, mean reversion, swing trading, and scalping. Entry signals often occur when price breaks above or below the bands, while exits may occur near the opposite band. Price moving outside the channel can suggest overbought or oversold conditions, trend continuation, or possible reversal. The passage states that Keltner Channels do not repaint once plotted.

A backtest on SPY using one Keltner strategy produced 288 trades, a 77% win rate, 6.3% CAGR, 15% market exposure, and a profit factor of 2. A momentum version using around 30 days and 1.3 ATR produced 143 trades and a 3.6% CAGR. The passage notes that profitability depends on market conditions, risk management, discipline, and trader skill, and that Keltner Channels should not be used in isolation.

The passage reviews literature and reports a study on research expectations for U.S. mathematics education faculty. Prior research suggests expectations vary by institution type, department type, and assigned research time, and often emphasize publication quantity and value of scholarly activities.

The study surveyed U.S. mathematics education faculty with research expectations. A sample was built from authors publishing in mathematics education journals, edited volumes, and practitioner journals from 2015–2017. Of 1,593 survey recipients, 821 responded; after exclusions, 404 respondents were in the target population. The survey asked about demographics, expected number of publications, and how different scholarly products and activities count toward tenure and promotion. Analyses examined institution type, department type, and research commitment.

Overall, respondents were evenly split between education and mathematics departments. Expected research time was typically 20–40%, ranging from 0–70%. Faculty were expected to publish about 1.64 papers per year on average. Research journal articles were the most valued publication type. Books, book chapters, practitioner articles, and conference proceedings usually counted some, while textbook value lacked consensus. Presentations were often expected but usually counted some. External funding was often expected or valued, especially when obtained. Professional development was generally neither required nor highly valued. First authorship was considered important.

Expectations varied by Carnegie classification. R1 faculty typically had 40% research time and were expected to publish about 2.25 papers yearly; non-journal publications were less valued, and pursuing or obtaining external funding and giving presentations were more often required. R2 faculty averaged about 1.5 papers yearly and were more likely to have publication expectations stated in written documents. Faculty at other institutions typically had about 20% research time and averaged about one paper yearly; external funding was less often expected, while presentations and professional development were more valued.

Higher research commitment was associated with more expected papers, greater emphasis on external funding and authorship position, and lower value placed on books, book chapters, practitioner articles, and professional development. Department differences were limited: mathematics departments reported slightly fewer expected papers, valued conference proceedings and funding more, and were less likely to require presentations or professional development than education departments.

The authors conclude that research expectations vary by institution type, department, and research commitment, and recommend clearer departmental communication and written expectations regarding publication numbers, publication types, scholarly activities, funding, and authorship.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K reporting that on December 12, 2016, it entered into a Termination Agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co. to terminate 63,259,180.62 outstanding warrants to purchase NVIDIA common stock issued under two 2013 warrant transactions. Government shutdowns have historically had limited economic and market impact, but this one could differ if President Donald Trump makes some federal furloughs permanent. Analysts say that would depart from past practice and add uncertainty, especially for an already fragile labor market. Shutdowns typically reduce GDP by about 0.1 percentage point per week, with losses usually recovered later. A prolonged shutdown could also delay key economic data because the Labor Department and Bureau of Labor Statistics would largely close, potentially affecting jobs reports, inflation data, Social Security cost-of-living adjustments, and Federal Reserve decision-making. Analysts generally expect the overall economic impact to be mild, though furloughed workers and contractors could face significant financial strain.

A column discusses Netflix’s “Unknown Number: The High School Catfish,” a documentary about Beal City, Michigan, student Lauryn Licari receiving months of hateful, graphic and threatening texts that appeared to come from someone close to her and her boyfriend, Owen McKenny. The author says the documentary highlights technology’s harms and missed a chance to explain cellphone forensics in depth. The Fabian Market Timing Model is a quantitative long-term trend-following strategy for the S&P 500, developed by Richard Fabian in the 1960s. The passage emphasizes mechanical trading rules, discipline, and giving the model time to work. Lorna Gibson discusses modeling osteoporosis in trabecular bone using Voronoi honeycombs, motivated by the irregular foam-like structure of bone. She describes obtaining a whale vertebra for student testing because its trabecular bone is relatively uniform, and suggests preparing specimens using water-jet cutting and coring.

The lecture reviews finite element models of 2D Voronoi honeycombs. Their elastic moduli agree closely with earlier analytical models, but their strengths are lower than regular hexagonal honeycombs because random strut lengths and orientations create broader stress and strain distributions. Models with elastic-perfectly plastic cell walls show a transition between elastic buckling and plastic yielding at about 3.5% relative density, with minimum strength near 5% due to interaction between failure modes.

Gibson then explains osteoporosis models comparing uniform thinning of struts with removal of struts. Removing struts causes much larger reductions in modulus and strength than thinning, and properties drop to zero at the percolation threshold, where the structure separates into disconnected pieces. More bone-like 2D models are made by perturbing square Voronoi arrays to match vertebral trabecular orientation, and 3D Voronoi models show that more material must be removed to reach comparable stiffness loss; the 3D percolation threshold is about 50%.

The lecture also covers metal foams as possible bone substitute materials or porous implant coatings that allow bone ingrowth. Examples include titanium and tantalum foams made by replica processes, fugitive phase methods, foaming agents, argon gas expansion, freeze casting, selective laser sintering, and powder ignition. Their stress-strain behavior resembles other foams, though published modulus and strength data show substantial scatter due to structural variation.

Finally, Gibson discusses bone in evolutionary studies. Early mineralized organisms used calcium carbonate or silica, while true bone with collagen and calcium phosphate appeared in vertebrates around 450 million years ago. Because bone structure reflects loading, trabecular architecture can help infer locomotion in fossil species. A study of fossil ilium fragments from Oreopithecus bambolii compared trabecular density and architecture with humans and non-human primates, finding features more similar to humans, suggesting the species was bipedal or partly bipedal.

The article explores how dialogic pedagogy can connect educational values with classroom practice in music and mathematics education. It is framed by concerns about democratic dialogue, citizenship, Bildung, and the need for education that supports critical, participatory, and inquisitive students.

The study is an interdisciplinary qualitative project using two cases: a choir project in pre-service music teacher education and a classroom talk in upper-primary mathematics. The researchers analyze the cases through concepts including epistemological dialogue, ontological dialogue, Bildung, musicking, mathematizing, and didactic contract.

The theoretical framework distinguishes epistemological dialogue, focused on subject knowledge, from ontological dialogue, focused on students’ self-understanding and existential engagement. Bildung is presented as formation involving critical independence, human development, and democratic participation.

In the choir case, a teacher includes a student-suggested song from Rent and shares a personal story connected to HIV/AIDS. The analysis describes how music-making involved subject learning, personal meaning, shared participation, and existential dimensions. In the mathematics case, a teacher leads students in exploring patterns between fractions. The analysis highlights student participation, questioning, hypothesis-making, and shared uncertainty as features of dialogic mathematics education.

The discussion identifies common features across the cases: teachers listened to students, allowed student contributions to influence classroom activity, took risks, and participated as whole persons. The article argues that dialogic classroom practices can support participation, Bildung, and democratic capacities, while also noting tensions around teacher authority, student voice, and the difficulty of planning or controlling ontological dialogue.

British Transport Police are appealing for information after a 19-year-old woman was sexually assaulted on a train to Taunton on April 8. The incident occurred near Highbridge and Burnham, and passengers intervened before the suspect left at Bridgwater with his group.

The speaker argues that the United States must help shape and guarantee a lasting postwar peace, but only under conditions consistent with its principles and acceptable to mankind. The war’s settlement must create a peace worth preserving, not merely serve immediate national interests or establish a new balance of power. Lasting peace requires a universal covenant backed by the organized force of mankind, including the peoples of the New World. The speaker emphasizes that the war must end in a “peace without victory,” because imposed terms would create humiliation, resentment, and instability. Only a peace among equals, based on shared benefit and just settlement of disputes, can endure.

Whangarei District Council advises drivers that winter brings parking congestion around Kensington Park, with no immediate plans to add parking. It warns against illegal parking that blocks access, damages verges or obstructs footpaths. Council first issues warning fliers, then tickets, and suggests planning ahead, carpooling, drop-offs, and walking from available parking.

Scientists reported in The FASEB Journal that TRPM8 and TRPP3 receptors on brown adipose tissue cells may be therapeutic targets for increasing metabolism-boosting brown fat. Using human bone marrow stem cells and subcutaneous belly fat cells, researchers found both receptors highly expressed in differentiated brown fat. Activating TRPM8 supported browning, while inhibiting it impeded the process; eliminating TRPP3 prevented brown fat formation. The findings may inform treatments for obesity, diabetes, and related metabolic disorders.

The Jammu and Kashmir Public Service Commission kept in abeyance the result of the Combined Competitive (Preliminary) Examination, 2016, declared on April 23, 2017, and withdrew notifications for the Main Examination after discrepancies were reported in question papers and answer keys. The Commission decided to refer all 23 subjects’ question papers and answer keys to independent third-party experts for review. The move followed candidate representations and RTI applications alleging inaccuracies, ambiguity, wrong options, mistakes and printing errors, despite earlier review by subject experts. Further action and the next Main Examination date will be decided after expert reports are received. A total of 36,681 candidates appeared in both preliminary papers, and 6,925 had been declared successful for the Main Examination.

Lyminster Primary School in Littlehampton was told to improve after a May Ofsted inspection. Inspector Marcia Goodwin said new headteacher Steven McGinley and senior leaders had made positive changes and the school was well placed to improve, but their work had not yet had enough impact. The report cited weak past teaching, under-achievement in last year’s Year 6 SATs and teaching that was not consistently good. McGinley said the school had a clear improvement plan and was confident it could return to “good.”

The lecture continues the study of linearized Einstein equations, focusing on the transverse-traceless metric perturbation \(h_{ij}^{TT}\), the gauge-invariant radiative part of spacetime perturbations. Previous results showed that the ten perturbation degrees of freedom split into six gauge-invariant functions and four gauge degrees of freedom, with \(h_{ij}^{TT}\) obeying a wave equation and containing two independent degrees of freedom corresponding to gravitational wave polarizations.

The lecture first examines a gravitational wave propagating in the \(z\)-direction, with only spatial transverse-traceless components nonzero. Symmetry and tracelessness leave two independent components, \(h_{xx}\) and \(h_{xy}\). A direct geodesic calculation shows that freely falling particles remain fixed in the chosen coordinates, illustrating that coordinate-dependent motion can obscure physical effects. The observable impact instead appears in relative measurements between separated bodies.

Two methods are used to describe this effect. First, the round-trip travel time of light between two nearby freely falling bodies depends on \(h_{xx}^{TT}\), suggesting how timing variations can reveal gravitational waves. Second, geodesic deviation shows that gravitational waves produce tidal accelerations between nearby bodies. For \(h_{xx}\), a ring of particles is alternately stretched along one axis and squeezed along the perpendicular axis, defining the plus polarization. For \(h_{xy}\), the same effect occurs along axes rotated by 45 degrees, defining the cross polarization. LIGO detects such tidal stretches and squeezes by measuring laser light travel times and interference in its arms.

The lecture then explains how to compute \(h_{ij}^{TT}\) from a source. In Lorentz gauge, the linearized Einstein equation has a retarded integral solution involving the stress-energy tensor. For distant sources, the source-detector distance is approximated as constant across the source, yielding the leading multipole term. Using the tensor virial theorem, the spatial stress integral is related to the second time derivative of the source quadrupole moment. The transverse and traceless parts are extracted using projection tensors orthogonal to the wave propagation direction. This produces the quadrupole formula for gravitational waves: the radiative field is proportional to the second time derivative of the source quadrupole moment, projected into transverse-traceless form, scaled by \(2G/r\). The next lecture will address the related quadrupole formula for gravitational-wave energy.

Bluehole launched PUBG’s Xbox One community event, Snipe City, challenging players to collectively get 400,000 kills with M24 and Kar98 rifles by July 10. Eligible players receive rewards if successful, with results on July 11.

Zacks Investment Research upgraded State Bank Financial Corporation (NASDAQ: STBZ) from “sell” to “buy” with a $30 price target, implying 11.69% upside. Hovde Group previously downgraded the stock to “market perform” and lowered its target to $24.50. Analysts average a “Hold” rating and $25.25 target. Shares opened at $26.86, with a $963.28 million market cap. The company reported quarterly EPS of $0.34, above the $0.31 estimate, and analysts expect $1.33 EPS for the fiscal year. State Bank declared a $0.14 quarterly dividend. Directors Robert H. Mcmahon and John D. Houser recently sold shares. Institutional investors own 81.81% of the stock.

Apple filed its Q2 2023 Form 10-Q for the quarter ended April 1, 2023. Total net sales were $94.8 billion, down 3% from $97.3 billion a year earlier, with net income of $24.2 billion versus $25.0 billion. Diluted EPS was $1.52, unchanged from the prior-year quarter. Products net sales were $73.9 billion and Services net sales were $20.9 billion. Mac sales declined 31%, iPad sales declined 13%, Services rose 5%, and iPhone sales were relatively flat.

For the first six months of 2023, net sales were $212.0 billion, down 4%, and net income was $54.2 billion, down from $59.6 billion. Cash generated by operating activities was $62.6 billion. As of April 1, 2023, Apple had $332.2 billion in total assets, $270.0 billion in total liabilities, and $62.2 billion in shareholders’ equity. Apple repurchased $19.1 billion of common stock and paid $3.7 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents during the quarter. On May 4, 2023, the board authorized an additional $90 billion share repurchase program and raised the quarterly dividend to $0.24 per share.

The Texas Court of Civil Appeals affirmed the divorce granted to John and Mary Lee Geesbreght and the award of custody of their minor children to John, holding that the Tarrant County court had jurisdiction and that no reversible error occurred in the jury proceedings on custody. The court found Mary Lee had waived jurisdictional complaints and that Texas remained the children’s legal domicile.

The court reversed and remanded the property division. It held that the trial court erred by valuing John’s stock in Emergency Medicine Consultants only at book value and failing to consider any corporate goodwill separate from John’s personal professional goodwill. Because relevant property interests were not fully considered, a new trial was ordered solely on property division. Appeal costs were split equally between the parties.

Asian shares fell as investors sold U.S. technology stocks amid regulatory concerns over Facebook’s improper user data access controversy, while awaiting Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s first policy meeting and watching U.S. trade measures. MSCI Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan dropped 0.2%, and Japan’s Nikkei fell 1.0%. Wall Street also declined, with Facebook down 6.8%. Concerns over possible U.S.-China trade tensions followed Trump’s steel and aluminum tariffs and potential tariffs on Chinese goods. U.S. short-term Treasury yields rose ahead of an expected Fed rate hike, while the dollar gained little. The euro rose after reports on ECB rate discussions, the pound hit a one-month high after a Brexit transition agreement, and oil prices were little changed.

NVIDIA filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 29, 2018. Second-quarter revenue was $3.123 billion, up from $2.230 billion a year earlier; net income was $1.101 billion, up from $583 million; and diluted EPS was $1.76, up from $0.92. For the first half of fiscal 2019, revenue was $6.330 billion, net income was $2.345 billion, and diluted EPS was $3.74.

Second-quarter GPU revenue was $2.656 billion, up 40% year over year, driven by gaming, professional visualization, and datacenter growth, partly offset by lower cryptocurrency-related GPU demand. Tegra Processor revenue was $467 million, also up 40%, supported by gaming platform SOC modules, automotive revenue, and development agreements. Gaming revenue was $1.805 billion, datacenter revenue was $760 million, professional visualization revenue was $281 million, automotive revenue was $161 million, and OEM & IP revenue was $116 million.

Gross margin was 63.3% for the quarter, compared with 58.4% a year earlier. Operating expenses rose to $818 million from $614 million, mainly due to higher employee-related costs. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $7.943 billion as of July 29, 2018. During the first half of fiscal 2019, NVIDIA repurchased $655 million of common stock and paid $182 million in dividends. The company reported no material changes to market risks, risk factors, internal controls, or off-balance-sheet arrangements.

Lagos and Ogun health workers are on high alert for Lassa fever. Ogun confirmed one case involving a 20-year-old man now isolated and responding to treatment, with 66 contacts under surveillance. LUTH said its confirmed cases are responding to treatment.

The study externally validated a longitudinal Grade of Membership (L-GoM) model of Alzheimer’s disease progression in the Predictors 3 cohort, a community-based, multiethnic sample from northern Manhattan that included participants with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) dementia. The model, previously developed using Predictors 2 and validated using Predictors 1, uses fixed covariates and time-varying clinical signs and symptoms across 11 domains to estimate four latent disease subtype scores and predict outcomes.

Predictors 3 included 273 participants with follow-up data: 123 with MCI and 150 with AD dementia at the initial visit. Among MCI participants, 40 later converted to AD dementia; among AD participants, 32 later reverted to a non-dementia diagnosis. Compared with Predictors 2, Predictors 3 participants were older, more often female and Hispanic, had lower educational attainment, and had a lower frequency of the ApoE e4 allele.

The model’s predictions were evaluated against observed survival and need for full-time care over up to 7.5 years. Survival predictions fit well for AD nonreverters and MCI participants, but not for AD reverters, who had substantially higher survival than predicted. Predictions for need for full-time care generally supported model validity, especially after excluding AD reverters, though some deviations occurred for MCI participants and early follow-up points.

The authors concluded that the L-GoM model can predict mortality and need for full-time care in community-dwelling older adults with AD across different ethnic, linguistic, and socioeconomic backgrounds, except in likely misdiagnosed AD cases identified by later reversion. They also found that the model extends to individuals with MCI.

The Dallas Stars and Vegas Golden Knights held pregame tributes for Las Vegas shooting victims, a Stars staff member, and announcer Dave Strader before Vegas’ major pro sports debut.

Fibonacci trading uses tools such as retracements, expansions, fans, and channels to identify potential support, resistance, entry, exit, stop-loss, and profit-target levels. Common retracement levels include 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, and 78.6%. The best timeframe and levels depend on trading style, market volatility, and backtesting results.

The passage states that Fibonacci tools are popular because they mark potential levels before price reaches them, but it emphasizes that evidence for their effectiveness is limited. It argues that many Fibonacci strategies rely on anecdotal claims rather than backtested proof. A cited dissertation by Clarissa Gunawan found passive buy-and-hold strategies outperformed active Fibonacci retracement strategies, though Fibonacci may still help mark support, resistance, and profit targets. The passage recommends using Fibonacci cautiously, preferably with other indicators, and avoiding strategies that have not been backtested.

Day trading involves buying and selling financial instruments within the same trading day to profit from short-term price movements. The passage describes many strategies, including momentum, range trading, scalping, breakout, pullback, reversal, gap, news, pattern, seasonal, dark pool, statistical arbitrage, pairs, order flow, market making, short squeeze, volatility-based, market profile, regime switching, volatility targeting, and phase analysis trading. It emphasizes that strategies require clear rules, discipline, risk management, emotional control, and adaptation to market conditions.

Day trading differs from swing trading because positions are closed the same day rather than held for days or weeks. Risks include market volatility, leverage, emotional decision-making, and potential financial losses. Technical analysis, backtesting, and predefined entry and exit rules are presented as important tools, though backtesting does not guarantee future results. The passage states that day trading can be profitable, but most traders do not make money, with statistics suggesting as little as 10% do. It also notes that expecting a consistent 1% daily return is unrealistic.

A Yale-Brookings study says AI has not yet caused broad disruption in the U.S. labor market, despite concerns about entry-level jobs and Gen Z hiring struggles. Gimbel and co-author Molly Kinder emphasize that AI exposure does not necessarily mean job loss, and systemic displacement would likely take years, emerging only if companies redesign workflows around AI.
