Ukrainian startup Dropla is developing Blue Eyes, an AI system designed to help detect Russian ambush drones and landmines along Ukrainian supply routes. Russia has increasingly used explosive-laden quadcopters hidden behind the front line to attack logistics vehicles, creating what is described as a “smart minefield.”

Blue Eyes analyzes real-time video from cheap quadcopters flying ahead of or alongside convoys, identifies threats, and sends coordinates to Ukraine’s battle management system. Founder V’yacheslav Shvaydak said the AI has been trained to detect more than 170 types of explosive threats and is now being adapted to find idle quadcopters. Multiple frontline units have tested it since early summer, and Dropla hopes to expand deployments fivefold near the zero line.

The passage presents Education Savings Accounts (ESAs) as a major school-choice turning point comparable to the spread of charter schools in 1993, but with different political alignment and accountability structures. It states that recent universal or near-universal ESA programs have largely emerged in Republican-led states and provide public funds to parents for private school tuition, pods, homeschooling, and related goods and services, with fewer regulatory requirements than charter schools.

The passage traces ESAs and conventional vouchers to Milton Friedman’s writings, arguing that their central purpose is to reduce government’s role in education and save taxpayer money rather than fund high-quality schooling. It notes that ESA allocations are typically far below per-pupil public school spending and contrasts this with some European voucher systems where funding is closer to public-school spending levels.

The passage identifies several concerns: weak oversight of ESA spending, limited accountability for teacher qualifications, testing, curriculum, and graduation data, rising private school tuition after ESA adoption, and rapidly increasing state costs as programs subsidize families already using private schools. It also argues that ESAs may harm public school budgets, particularly in rural areas where schools serve as civic centers, and may increase discrimination against students, faculty, and staff based on disability, religion, sexual orientation, or other factors.

The passage reviews support and criticism of vouchers and ESAs from various scholars and organizations. It notes that while some advocates supported targeted vouchers for low-income families, ESAs are chiefly promoted by Friedman-aligned and conservative organizations, though some school-choice supporters have raised concerns about windfalls for wealthier families, inequity, and spending oversight.

The passage concludes with recommendations to repeal ESA programs where possible, oppose expansion where repeal is not feasible, impose spending limits and stronger oversight, require public reporting on participating schools, mandate certified teachers and academic assessments, enforce civil rights and anti-discrimination protections, and document ESA effects on students, families, public schools, and rural communities.

The Side Screen Offense is a two-player screen-and-roll isolation widely used in the NBA. It can be initiated quickly through a post setting an on-ball screen, making it useful when plays break down or late in the shot clock. It is typically run to allow the ballhandler to drive middle with the strong hand.

The ballhandler’s main options are driving to the basket, pulling up if the defender goes under, passing to the screener rolling or popping, or kicking out to shooters when help defense commits. Success depends on coordination between ballhandler and screener, including timing, footwork, nonverbal communication, and experience.

The passage outlines defensive reads and counters: drive when chased over the screen; drop pass when baseline help appears; kick out when weakside help sags; pull up when the defender goes under; drive opposite when the defender cheats early; cross over when the defender fights through; pass to a popping screener against show-and-recover; feed the rolling or posting screener on switches; isolate mismatches; slip the screen against anticipated switches; throw a lob if the screen is denied; and spread the floor into a 2-1-2 alignment against traps.

Common entries include High Post Rub, Power/Motion, Horns, and a Boston option. If the side screen does not produce a shot, teams may flow into continuities such as Flex, Triangle Game, Single/Double Motion, weakside double screens, or baseline down screens.

Teaching the offense requires players to understand its components and basic offensive skills. Recommended methods include breakdown drills, scrimmaging, and ongoing individual skill development. Game strategy emphasizes scouting defensive tendencies, preparing counters, varying entries and alignments, attacking weak defenders, and using side screens late in the clock. The passage also notes that teams should understand the offense defensively because it is widely used.

The passage describes patent continuations and incorporated provisional applications relating to a fluid end for hydraulic fracturing. It explains that traditional fluid ends operate under high pressure with abrasive fluids, often developing fatigue cracks and leakage at high-stress areas such as intersecting bores and flange necks, creating a need for designs that delay wear and failure.

The described fluid end uses multiple side-by-side fluid end sections instead of a single housing, allowing individual replacement. Each section has a generally cylindrical housing with one horizontal bore, eliminating intersecting bore stress points and reducing manufacturing complexity. The design includes connect plates, intake and discharge manifolds, a fluid routing plug, suction and discharge valves, stuffing box, retainers, seals, and shaped passages and bevels intended to route fluid, reduce stress, manage proppant wear, and simplify maintenance.

The disclosure describes methods and user equipment (UE) configurations for applying scheduling offsets to support power saving in next-generation wireless networks. A UE may receive a power saving signal from a base station that includes a minimum applicable scheduling offset, such as K0min, between a PDCCH and a PDSCH. The UE determines an application delay, applies existing scheduling behavior during that delay, and applies the minimum scheduling offset restriction afterward. The base station may ensure scheduling values meet the minimum offset, allowing the UE to enter a power saving state such as micro sleep.

The disclosure also addresses HARQ feedback for power saving indicators. A UE may send HARQ-ACK-only or HARQ-ACK/NACK feedback after receiving a power saving signal, with timing determined by DCI, RRC signaling, predefined values, or scheduled PUSCH resources. HARQ feedback for power saving indicators may be included in an existing HARQ codebook, placed at the MSB or LSB, generated independently using dedicated PUCCH resources, or multiplexed with HARQ feedback for PDSCH receptions.

The disclosure further describes default beam operation in a power saving state. When antenna panels or SRS resource sets are deactivated, the UE may use only valid spatial domain or QCL information associated with active panels. For PUSCH or PUCCH transmission, the UE may select beams based on valid PUCCH resources, CORESET spatial information, SRS resource indicators, or configured power saving parameters. Example base station, UE, and wireless node architectures are also described.

A woolly rhino horn found with a skull in Siberian permafrost is the longest yet discovered and dates to about 19,600 years ago. Used across the front seven by defensive coordinator Matt Patricia, Reese combines prototypical size, elite athleticism, play strength, burst, and tackling ability. He is especially effective as a downhill run defender and quarterback spy, with enough movement skills to suggest coverage upside, though his coverage sample and zone-processing evaluation remain limited. The lecture explains static fusion trees, a word RAM data structure for predecessor and successor queries in \(O(\log_w n)\) time using linear space and polynomial preprocessing. Fusion trees use B-tree-like branching of \(w^{1/5}\), requiring each node to answer predecessor queries in constant time.

A fusion node stores sorted keys and uses “sketching” to keep only important bit positions, defined by branching levels in the binary trie of the keys. These bits preserve the order of stored keys. Since a query’s sketch may not preserve its true position, the search is corrected by finding where the query diverges from the stored-key trie, constructing a modified query, and searching again in sketch space.

The lecture describes approximate sketching with masks and integer multiplication, showing how to pack important bits into \(O(w^{4/5})\) bits while avoiding collisions. It then explains parallel comparison: concatenate sketches of stored keys, replicate the query sketch, subtract in parallel, and use bit operations to find the rank. Finally, it presents a constant-time method for finding the most significant set bit by splitting a word into clusters, identifying nonempty clusters, using perfect sketching, and applying parallel comparison. These techniques together implement static fusion trees on the word RAM.

The Supreme Court relisted 17 long-conference cert petitions for further consideration, covering issues including parental rights and school gender-identity policies, religious accommodations to New York’s former COVID-19 vaccine mandate, Section 230 immunity for Grindr, jury-trial rights in state administrative enforcement, prison-condition relief under the Prison Litigation Reform Act, arbitration exemptions for local delivery workers, plea-agreement appeal waivers, child-witness confrontation rights, public-trial rights during COVID-era jury selection, and a Jan. 6 defendant affected by a presidential pardon.

Sevilla midfielder Pablo Sarabia welcomed drawing Manchester United in the Champions League last 16, saying Sevilla only wanted to avoid Manchester City and PSG. A Children’s Rights Alliance report says homelessness is harming children’s education in the greater Dublin area, with nearly 4,000 affected. Based on research with teachers, principals and homeless parents, it found children going to school hungry, tired or in dirty clothes, facing long journeys, absences, poor homework conditions, and mental health and behavioural impacts. Parents sometimes choose between food and school travel costs. The report recommends free school travel, ring-fenced school funding for meals and supports, and suitable accommodation near schools, with families not kept in emergency housing beyond six months.

The lecture explains life cycle assessment (LCA) as a method for evaluating environmental impacts of products or services from raw materials through end of life. It contrasts product-level LCA with corporate carbon footprinting and uses a hand-drying study commissioned by Dyson as the main example.

LCA is described as having four stages: goal and scope definition, inventory analysis, impact assessment, and interpretation. In the hand-drying study, the functional unit was a pair of dried hands, allowing comparison among Dyson Airblade models, the Xlerator dryer, paper towels, recycled paper towels, standard dryers, and cotton roll towels. The study aimed both to inform Dyson engineers about impact drivers and to compare products for possible external claims.

The lecture emphasizes that LCA depends heavily on assumptions, boundaries, data access, and uncertainty. In the hand-drying study, assumptions included manufacturing location, product lifetime, drying time, electricity grid mix, paper towel use, recycling allocation, cut-off rules, and excluded capital goods. Data came from company information, prior studies, public sources, and databases such as ecoinvent, requiring proxy data when exact materials were unavailable.

The inventory phase identifies inputs and outputs such as raw materials, energy, emissions, water, and waste. The impact phase classifies and characterizes these outputs into measures such as global warming potential, cumulative energy demand, water use, and broader indicators like IMPACT 2002+. The interpretation phase evaluates sensitivity and uncertainty through one-factor sensitivity tests, scenario analysis, and simulations.

The study found the Dyson Airblade generally had the lowest environmental impact, though some scenarios could favor alternatives such as the Xlerator. The lecture stresses that comparative LCAs require careful review because assumptions and data limitations can strongly influence results.

The report analyzes the global Angelica Seed oil market, covering historical, current, and projected revenues by sector, segment, end user, and region. It examines market status, growth rate, trends, drivers, constraints, risks, opportunities, PEST and Porter’s Five Forces, applications, regions, and competitive landscape. Covered companies include Albert Vieille, Berje, Elixens, Ernesto Ventos, Robertet Group, Treatt Plc, and others. Regions include the United States, China, Europe, Japan, Southeast Asia, India, and Rest of World. The report also includes SWOT, investment feasibility, return analysis, production, demand, pricing, and forecast data.

This study analyzed secondary data from a cross-sectional baseline survey and a randomized controlled open-label trial in Muheza district, Tanzania, to assess malnutrition risk factors and the impact of intermittent preventive therapy for malaria on nutritional status among school-age children. Among 1,566 children aged 5–15 years, baseline malaria prevalence was 27%; 23% of children aged 5–10 were underweight, 21% of all children were stunted, and 28% were thin or severely thin. Malaria was associated with higher odds of stunting, low socioeconomic status with underweight, and recent malaria history with thinness. Children were randomized to dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine, artesunate-amodiaquine, or standard care and followed for 20 months. Preventive antimalarial treatment did not significantly improve weight, height, or BMI compared with standard care. The study concludes that malaria and malnutrition are both substantial burdens in the setting and recommends integrated malaria control and nutrition programs, including school food availability and community nutrition education.

NVIDIA Tesla T4 is a Turing-based GPU for inferencing in data centers, enterprises, and edge devices. It has 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, 16 GB GPU memory, 320 GB/s memory bandwidth, and delivers up to 130 TOPS INT8 and 260 TOPS INT4 inferencing performance. NVIDIA states it provides up to 40X higher inference performance and more than 50X higher energy efficiency than CPU-based inferencing, and up to twice the energy efficiency of Tesla P4.

The Turing architecture adds Tensor Cores, RT Cores, improved Multi-Process Service, enhanced video decode/encode, GDDR6 memory, larger and faster L2 caches, improved lossless memory compression, and higher effective bandwidth. Its display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, HDR processing, tone mapping, and Display Stream Compression. Turing also supports USB-C and VirtualLink for single-cable VR headset connectivity, and uses NVLink for SLI GPU-to-GPU data transfers on TU102 and TU104.

Turing introduces hybrid rendering, combining rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, ambient occlusion, and other effects. NVIDIA describes Turing ray tracing as significantly faster than Pascal software ray tracing, with RT Cores enabling about 10x faster ray tracing.

NVIDIA NGX uses Turing Tensor Cores and deep neural networks for AI-based graphics features, including DLSS, DLSS 2X, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS is trained using high-quality supersampled reference images and is described as improving performance while maintaining image quality compared with TAA.

Other Turing graphics features include Mesh Shading with Task and Mesh Shaders, Variable Rate Shading for content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering, Texture Space Shading for decoupling visibility and appearance sampling, and Multi-View Rendering for rendering multiple viewpoints in one pass. Turing also expands DX12 resource binding support.

The passage describes TU104 and TU106 GPUs. TU104 includes up to 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and second-generation NVLink, and is used in products including GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. TU106 includes 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, and is used in GeForce RTX 2070 without NVLink or SLI support.

The document also explains RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering, basic ray tracing mechanics, BVH acceleration structures, denoising, and the use of ray tracing for shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections. It concludes with NVIDIA legal, warranty, trademark, and copyright notices.

Colleges and universities were expected to award over a million bachelor’s degrees in 2016–17, including many to nontraditional students such as working adults, parents and experienced professionals. Students over 24 made up nearly two-fifths of postsecondary enrollment in 2016. University of Phoenix president Timothy P. Slottow advises working adults returning to school to build a support system, research programs and costs, seek credit for prior learning or military experience, and choose flexible, structured programs aligned with career goals.

The speaker describes the Stanley Cup Finals as exciting but says overexcitement can lead to trying too much instead of playing their regular game. They expect the series to become more intense and physical. They discuss creating traffic against opposing goaltenders, moving them side to side, and breaking down the defense. They also emphasize puck possession, making tired defensemen chase, wearing them down with physical play, and doing more to earn power plays after going a full game without one.

The Yankee concept is a pro-style shot play built around a post-dig combination designed to attack the middle of the field and create explosive plays. It is often run from heavier personnel to encourage one-high safety looks, allowing the quarterback to high-low the free safety: throw the post if the safety plays low or the dig if the safety drops deep. It works best against Cover 1 and Cover 3, but is less effective against Cover 2 and Cover 4, where the quarterback should move quickly to underneath routes.

Primary routes include a deep post by the Z receiver, a 15-yard dig by the X receiver, a 5–6 yard crossing route by the tight end, a flare by the tailback, and a 3–4 yard arrow by the fullback. The quarterback’s progression is post, dig, crosser, then check-down. Variations include a 2x2 version with shallow crossers and a version using whip routes underneath to affect linebacker coverage and create space for the dig.

A study in Science Advances found that in parts of Antarctica with notable ice loss, including the Amundsen Sea and Sabrina Coast, rapid glacier melt is disrupting a cooling process that normally helps keep water beneath ice shelves cold. Instead, meltwater is helping warm water pool under the ice, increasing melting from below and creating a feedback loop that could accelerate sea-level rise. Researchers warn this may raise the risk of ice shelf collapse, which in a worst-case “pulse” scenario could lead to much faster sea-level rise than current projections for vulnerable cities such as Miami. The study also notes that reduced Antarctic bottom water could slow ocean currents, potentially contributing to more atmospheric warming and superstorms.

A longitudinal study compared immune responses to Covishield and Covaxin in 691 vaccine-naïve adults aged 18–45 across four sites in Bengaluru and Pune, India; 506 participants formed the per-protocol population. Participants received two doses of Covaxin 28 days apart or Covishield 12 weeks apart and were classified by baseline serostatus using anti-spike antibody titers.

Covishield generally elicited stronger immune responses than Covaxin. In baseline seronegative participants, seroconversion after two doses was 98.3% with Covishield and 74.4% with Covaxin. In baseline seropositive participants, antibody titers rose at least twofold after vaccination in 91.7% of Covishield recipients and 66.9% of Covaxin recipients. Covishield also produced higher anti-spike antibody titers after each dose in both serostatus groups and significant neutralizing antibody increases in a tested subset, while Covaxin did not show statistically significant neutralizing titer increases.

T cell analyses in a subset showed Covishield significantly increased spike-specific CD4 T cells and induced detectable CD8 T cell responses in seronegative participants, while Covaxin mainly elicited CD4 T cell responses and did not significantly expand nucleocapsid/matrix-specific CD4 T cells. In seropositive participants, neither vaccine significantly increased spike-specific CD4 or CD8 T cell frequencies.

The Omicron wave affected sampling and prevented clear assessment of durability. Cohorts vaccinated or sampled during the Omicron wave showed higher Covaxin responses and more comparable antibody levels between vaccines. Covishield produced broader and more potent surrogate neutralization against SARS-CoV-2 variants than Covaxin, especially in seropositive participants. Neither vaccine elicited Omicron-specific antibodies in seronegative individuals after vaccination alone, while one Covishield dose elicited measurable Omicron-specific responses in seropositive individuals.

The study notes limitations including lack of measurement of non-neutralizing antibody functions, inability to assess durability due to Omicron exposure, reliance on antibody patterns rather than RT-PCR to infer asymptomatic Omicron infection, sparse sampling during the Omicron wave, and absence of correlates of protection for Covaxin.

The speaker says he is overwhelmed by recent events and feels unprepared for his unexpected responsibilities. He offers no specific policy, saying his actions will define his administration, but points to his past commitment to free government and popular rights. He asks for support in guiding the Government through its current perils.

Zebronics launched the Buddy Speakers in India for Rs. 1699. The lightweight 630g portable wireless speaker features an LED display, RGB LED light, 5W RMS output, Bluetooth with 10-meter range, FM, USB, MicroSD, and AUX connectivity. It has a built-in rechargeable battery offering up to 3 hours of playback.

The author argues that expanding apprenticeships requires stronger pre-apprenticeship pathways, especially in construction, where current programs can be selective and inaccessible to motivated learners needing support. Pre-apprenticeships can provide career exposure, skills, mentoring, assessment preparation and credentials. The passage says these programs are limited by insufficient funding, lack of outcome tracking and costly barriers such as transportation, childcare and lost wages. It recommends creative financing for wraparound supports, better data collection and strategic investment from employers, unions, government and philanthropy to expand access and strengthen workforce pipelines.

An AI tool called Waldo scanned more than 430,000 Reddit posts about cannabis use and flagged over 28,000 as potentially describing harmful or unexpected side effects. Researchers verified 250 flagged posts and found 86 percent represented problematic cannabis experiences. Waldo was trained on manually reviewed Reddit posts and outperformed ChatGPT by producing fewer false positives, though not surpassing human reviewers. Researchers say such tools could help public health workers detect side effects shared online, especially where official reporting systems are limited, but caution that effectiveness on other products remains uncertain and privacy protections would be needed.

Enterprises surveyed largely prefer outsourcing HPC workloads, with 87% using or planning external HPC infrastructure. Colocation is also common, with 74% operating or planning their own HPC systems in external datacenters. Innovation partners are used or planned by 43%, though suitability is limited for time-sensitive commercial use. Only 6% currently run on-premises HPC, while 28% plan to do so within two years.

The paper presents Robodoc, a prototype medical chatbot that integrates OpenAI APIs with specialized models for medical conversations. It uses Teachable Machine transfer-learning models for X-ray and OCT image analysis, detecting viral and bacterial pneumonia, Drusen, Choroidal Neovascularization, and Diabetic Macular Edema, and a TensorFlow.js model for diabetes detection from numerical features. Built with Angular/TypeScript, the system uses OpenAI function calling to select the appropriate model based on user text or uploaded images and generate user-friendly responses. A stub appointment function was tested for urgent OCT cases. Results showed generally good integration, with some deviations such as confusion between DME and Drusen, viral pneumonia being marked urgent, and normal X-rays sometimes classified as pneumonia. The paper argues that public APIs and tools like Teachable Machine can enable low-cost chatbot interfaces for bioinformatics models, while noting that such systems should assist rather than replace medical professionals.

NASA ambassador Theo Wellington told the Wilson County Commission that the upcoming total solar eclipse could be the largest one-day public event in U.S. history, with areas in the 70-mile path, including Wilson County, expected to see major visitor increases. She said Wilson County is near the center of the path and the fairgrounds will experience totality just two seconds short of the maximum 2 minutes, 40 seconds. The commission also voted to allow eligible retiring sheriff’s officers to keep their service weapons and approved funding to train and certify a school resource officer for Springdale Elementary School, opening in August.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture adds enhanced Tensor Cores with FP16, INT8, and INT4 precision modes, enabling faster deep learning training and especially inference. In GeForce GPUs, Tensor Cores support NVIDIA NGX features such as DLSS, AI InPainting, AI Super Rez, and AI Slow-Mo. Tesla T4, based on Turing, targets data center, enterprise, and edge inference, with 2,560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, up to 130 TOPS INT8 and 260 TOPS INT4 performance, plus higher inference performance and energy efficiency than CPU-based systems.

Turing improves memory, display, and video capabilities with GDDR6 memory, larger and faster L2 caches, improved memory compression, DisplayPort 1.4a with 8K support, HDR processing, enhanced NVENC and NVDEC video units, USB-C and VirtualLink support for VR headsets, and NVLink-based two-way SLI on supported GPUs. It also introduces features such as mesh shading, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, Multi-View Rendering, and improved resource management.

Turing introduces RT Cores for real-time ray tracing, accelerating BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing. Combined with hybrid rendering, denoising, RTX software, and APIs such as Microsoft DXR, Turing enables real-time ray-traced reflections, shadows, ambient occlusion, and other effects on a single GPU. RT Cores provide much faster ray tracing than Pascal software-based approaches.

The architecture supports a hybrid rendering model combining rasterization, ray tracing, AI, and simulation. NVIDIA describes RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric that accounts for Tensor, CUDA, RT Core, and INT32 operations. Turing GPUs include TU102, TU104, and TU106 variants used across GeForce RTX, Quadro RTX, and Tesla products, with TU104 used in products such as GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000, and TU106 used in GeForce RTX 2070.

The passage defines swing trading as holding positions from about one day to a few weeks, usually no longer than a month. It evaluates six swing trading indicators on SPY: RSI, Internal Bar Strength, Stochastics, Bollinger Bands, WilliamsVixFix, and Williams %R. The article emphasizes risk-adjusted return, comparing annual return to exposure and maximum drawdown. It states that the best time frame for swing trading indicators is generally 1–15 days. Based on backtests, Williams %R is considered the best swing trading indicator because it produced stable results across variables and had the lowest average maximum drawdown, supporting better risk-adjusted returns.

National greatness depends on organized patriotism that places loyalty to the whole country above local, sectional, or class interests. Industrial and agricultural classes, capitalists, and wageworkers must cooperate. Efficient education, especially technical, industrial, scientific, and commercial training, is essential, though federalism limits national control outside the District of Columbia. Public schools should avoid purely literary training that discourages industrial work and should develop manual skill and industrial intelligence. The passage argues for advanced labor-related legislation where possible and emphasizes improving the efficiency, dignity, and rewards of wageworkers. It also stresses the national importance of farmers, who need practical scientific and technical education, better cultivation methods, stronger organization, and full opportunities for moral, mental, physical, and economic development.

The passage describes a patent application for video signal encoding and decoding methods and apparatuses. It addresses improving intra- and inter-prediction efficiency, including weighted inter-prediction, motion vector precision adjustment using reconstructed neighboring pixels, intra-prediction result correction, efficient intra-prediction mode encoding, and prediction by dividing a current block into sub-blocks.

For inter-prediction, motion information and weight prediction parameters may be merged from neighboring blocks or decoded from a bitstream. Prediction blocks are generated by applying multiplication and/or addition weight parameters to reference blocks. Weight parameters may be encoded directly, as differences from prediction values or neighboring parameters, or derived using reconstructed pixel areas near the current and reference blocks, including regression-based methods.

For intra-prediction, the method may decode or encode intra-prediction modes using candidate modes based on neighboring blocks, mode differences from previous blocks, or reconstructed pixel areas. Prediction samples may be corrected based on reconstructed neighboring pixels and correction coefficients. Correction coefficients may be derived using blocks with similar reconstructed pixel areas, standard deviations, or other similarity measures.

The passage also outlines general video encoder and decoder structures, including prediction, transform, quantization, entropy coding/decoding, filtering, and memory components, and describes related flowcharts and figures for weighted prediction, correction, motion vector improvement, and sub-block prediction.

Microsoft filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2015. Revenue was $20.4 billion, down from $23.2 billion a year earlier; gross margin was $13.2 billion; operating income was $5.8 billion; net income was $4.6 billion; and diluted earnings per share were $0.57. Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $99.4 billion, and total assets were $172.9 billion. Net cash from operations was $8.6 billion.

Microsoft reorganized its reporting segments into Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. Segment revenue was $6.3 billion, $5.9 billion, and $9.4 billion, respectively, with Corporate and Other reflecting a $1.2 billion reduction, mainly from Windows 10 revenue deferrals. Windows 10 revenue is recognized over the estimated device life of two to four years; Microsoft deferred a net $1.3 billion related to Windows 10 during the quarter.

Revenue declined primarily due to lower More Personal Computing revenue and Windows 10 deferrals, partly offset by Intelligent Cloud growth. Operating income was nearly flat as lower gross margin was offset by lower restructuring and sales and marketing expenses. Microsoft repurchased $4.0 billion of common stock and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.36 per share. Legal matters included patent, antitrust, product-related, and other claims, with accrued aggregate legal liabilities of $568 million and reasonably possible additional losses of approximately $1.5 billion.

The Romanian leu was steady ahead of the central bank’s rate decision, with markets split on whether it would deliver a fourth hike this year to 2.75 percent. Some Central European currencies firmed after China’s central bank acted to support the yuan. The forint and Czech crown rose 0.2 percent, while the leu traded flat. Romania’s central bank has tightened monetary conditions by allowing the 3-month ROBOR rate to rise above its benchmark. Hungarian short-term rates remain low despite higher bond yields and inflation concerns; the forint rebounded after the yuan’s recovery and speculation about central bank policy credibility.

The Straits Times Index rose 29 points, or 0.9 per cent, to 3,308.69, tracking gains in most major Asian markets as investors reacted to weak US inflation data and easing US-North Korea tensions. Hong Kong, South Korea and Shanghai advanced, while Japan’s Nikkei fell nearly 1 per cent despite stronger-than-expected economic growth. Analysts said geopolitical risks may persist, especially around North Korea’s Liberation Day, and market sentiment is likely to remain cautious, with upcoming economic data also in focus. In Singapore, gainers slightly outnumbered losers. OCBC and DBS led banking gains, while UOB declined. Property stocks CapitaLand and City Developments rose. Olam gained after reporting higher quarterly profit and revenue, while Asian Pay Television Trust rose despite a drop in quarterly net profit.

Two TPS7H500x-SP controllers can operate in primary-secondary mode using the SYNC pin. The primary uses RT to set switching frequency and outputs a clock at twice that frequency; the secondary leaves RT floating and uses the primary SYNC output for external synchronization. This supports either two independent synchronized converters sharing only SYNC, or a single interleaved parallel converter requiring shared VSENSE, COMP, SS, HICC, and SYNC connections. The secondary inverts the received clock, creating a 90° or 270° phase shift between corresponding primary and secondary switching outputs. OUTB waveforms apply only to TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP.

U.S. stocks opened higher Monday after the Easter weekend, led by gains in technology, industrial and consumer-focused companies, as China reported first-quarter economic growth of 6.9 percent. The S&P 500, Dow, Nasdaq and Russell 2000 all rose about 0.5 to 0.6 percent.

Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon and Netflix gained, with Netflix set to report results after the close. Alere surged after accepting a reduced $5.3 billion buyout offer from Abbott Laboratories. Eli Lilly and Incyte fell after the FDA declined to approve their rheumatoid arthritis pill, citing the need for more data. Snyder’s-Lance dropped after issuing a weak forecast and announcing CEO Carl Lee Jr.’s retirement. Arconic rose after CEO Klaus Kleinfeld stepped down, and Straight Path Communications climbed on the possibility of a competing buyout offer.

Oil prices slipped, bond yields edged lower, the dollar fell against the yen, and the euro rose. Major European and Hong Kong markets were closed for Easter, while Japanese and South Korean markets gained slightly.

The passage explains how to backtest a MACD trading strategy in Python using Apple historical data from Yahoo Finance via yfinance, with pandas for calculations and matplotlib for plotting. It defines MACD as the 12-period closing price EMA minus the 26-period closing price EMA, with a 9-period EMA signal line and histogram. The strategy assigns a long regime when the histogram is nonnegative, applied from the next row because returns start after the signal day. The example reports a 15.04% CAGR for the MACD strategy versus 19.07% for buy and hold, with the strategy invested 51.13% of the time.

Former prime minister Jean Chrétien addressed about 1,000 Liberals at Steven Del Duca’s Vaughan-Woodbridge nomination meeting, reflecting on unity after the Yonge St. van attack. Del Duca urged blood donations and called for campaign support despite polls favoring Doug Ford. He and Chrétien praised Premier Kathleen Wynne’s record. Outside, LiUNA Local 183 members protested budget labour changes affecting work sites.

Christian Brothers defensive lineman Bill Norton, a four-star 2019 prospect, committed to Georgia. The 6-foot-6, 270-pound Norton chose the Bulldogs over several major offers shortly after visiting Tennessee. Coach Thomas McDaniel praised his athleticism and said Georgia consistently viewed him as a defensive lineman.

The passage presents 3DPCNet, a pose-only, estimator-agnostic module for canonicalizing monocular 3D human poses into a fixed body-centered frame to reduce viewpoint-dependent variability in kinematic analysis. The network uses parallel GCN and Transformer branches fused with cross-attention and adaptive gating to predict a 6D global rotation mapped to SO(3), with an optional residual correction for joint refinement. It is trained with synthetically rotated 3D poses and a composite loss including pose reconstruction, rotation geodesic loss, cycle consistency, perceptual constraints, and regularization.

Experiments use MM-Fi for canonicalization and TotalCapture for kinematic signal evaluation. On MM-Fi, 3DPCNet reduces MPJPE from about 63–65 mm to 46–49 mm and rotation error from 20–22° to 3–4°, showing stability across cross-subject and cross-environment protocols. Compared with a deterministic geometric baseline, 3DPCNet better aligns canonical poses and produces more faithful wrist trajectories. On TotalCapture, canonicalized accelerations derived from pose estimators visually correspond more closely to synchronized IMU signals than the geometric baseline, including under challenging lateral views.

The work concludes that pose-only canonicalization can reduce viewpoint-induced variability and improve downstream kinematic trajectories for applications such as rehabilitation, sports analysis, and VR training. Limitations include possible non-rigid deviations from the residual head, no absolute scale recovery, dependence on input pose quality, and reliance on pose-space augmentation rather than real multi-view imagery.

Under new federal tax law withholding tables, about 90% of workers should see more take-home pay starting in February, though amounts vary by income, family status, pay frequency and W-4 allowances. Examples from H&R Block estimate a married couple earning $90,000 with two children could receive about $61 more per semi-monthly paycheck, while a single person earning $35,000 with no children could receive nearly $32 more.

Families with children may see larger gains because the child tax credit doubled to $2,000 per qualifying child and income phaseouts changed. Employers must use the new withholding tables by Feb. 15, using W-4 information already on file. A revised W-4 and IRS withholding calculator are expected, and taxpayers are advised to review withholding to avoid owing taxes in 2019.

The law also raises the standard deduction, limits some itemized deductions, ends deductibility of home equity loan interest, and caps certain state and local tax deductions at $10,000. Bonus withholding falls from 25% to 22%, meaning larger bonus checks after withholding.

Dick Tuck, a Democratic Party operative known for political pranks targeting Richard Nixon, died in Tucson, Arizona, at 94, according to longtime friend Lorraine Glicksman. Tuck’s stunts included arranging a poorly attended Nixon campus event in 1950, planting bogus fortune cookies at a Republican fundraiser, posing as a fire marshal to understate Nixon crowds, and using a Chinese sign referencing a Howard Hughes loan during Nixon’s 1962 governor campaign. He also worked in traditional roles, including Robert F. Kennedy’s 1968 presidential campaign, and unsuccessfully ran for the California Senate in 1966. Tuck remained critical of Nixon late in life, saying Nixon’s resignation date should become a holiday called “Nixmas.”

The passage examines wartime and online education in African higher education through a bibliometric study. It states that ICT has supported the growth of online education in African universities since the 1990s, but challenges remain, including weak ICT infrastructure, limited rural internet access, poor affordability, insufficient digital skills, weak policies, and educator resistance. Wars in Africa have caused displacement, civilian casualties, destruction of infrastructure, brain drain, disrupted academic programmes, and insecurity, all of which hinder education and ICT deployment. Online education is presented as a way to sustain learning during conflict, though it requires training, technology adaptation, and institutional preparedness.

The study used bibliometric analysis of Scopus publications from 2000 to 2024, narrowing results from 90 documents on wartime and online education to 53 suitable items. The United States had the most publications, followed by Ukraine; no African country appeared among the represented countries. Further screening for wartime, education, and online learning found only five publications from Ukraine, Austria, and the United States. Publications increased notably in 2023. Most documents were articles, and social sciences was the dominant subject area. Keyword analysis identified themes around e-learning, online teaching, students, teachers, Ukraine, and war.

The passage concludes that there is a major research gap on wartime and online learning in African higher education. It calls for more research on online learning during conflict, organisational sustainability, brain drain, trauma among students and faculty, and inclusive online education for people with disabilities.

Mathieu Henderson ended his four-year OHL career with a breakout final season, finishing ninth among OHL defencemen in scoring with 10 goals and 44 assists in 68 games for the Flint Firebirds. The Brantford native said he exceeded expectations and was happy with his junior career. His OHL years included Plymouth’s relocation to Flint and a turbulent 2015-16 season, but he continued improving, especially defensively, raising his plus/minus from minus-45 to minus-seven. Flint’s season ended with a first-round playoff loss to Sault Ste. Marie, during which Henderson scored the team’s first postseason goal. Afterward, he played three games with the ECHL’s South Carolina Stingrays. Henderson said he is considering pro hockey in North America or Europe or going to school, and credited hockey, his coaches, teammates and parents for his opportunities.

The civil aviation ministry has asked the finance ministry to defer GST implementation by two months, saying airlines need more time to update systems and address compliance concerns. Airlines have cited issues with global ticket distribution systems, unclear rules, possible taxation of aircraft parts movement, and higher costs. The finance ministry has maintained GST will roll out on July 1.

The IRS announced higher federal income tax brackets and standard deductions for 2026 to adjust for inflation. The standard deduction will rise to $32,200 for married couples filing jointly and $16,100 for single filers. The top 37% rate will apply to individuals with taxable income above $640,600 and joint filers at $768,700 or more. Other changes include long-term capital gains brackets, estate and gift tax exemptions, child tax credit eligibility and earned income tax credit eligibility. The announcement followed the IRS saying it would furlough nearly half its workforce during the government shutdown.

The lecture introduces online markets, focusing mainly on Google, with brief discussion of Amazon-related platform models. It begins with a review of Vickrey-Clarke-Groves mechanisms for private-value social choice problems. VCG mechanisms ask agents to report types, choose the utilitarian allocation based on reports, and charge each agent the negative externality they impose on others. They implement utilitarian outcomes in dominant strategies but are not budget balanced and can be impractical when the space of alternatives is very large.

The lecture then discusses Google’s dominance in search, high profitability, and role in funding other Google products. It notes antitrust suits alleging monopolization of search and online advertising practices. Google runs an auction for ads on every search query, with the number and placement of ads depending on how commercial the query is. Unlike earlier Yahoo! first-price ad auctions, which produced unstable bidding cycles and poor ad relevance, Google uses standing per-click bids, quality scores, ranking by bid times quality, and generalized second-price payments.

Edelman, Ostrovsky, and Schwarz model Google’s ad auction as a generalized second-price position auction. The mechanism is not VCG and truthful bidding is not generally an equilibrium, but bidders shade bids in equilibrium. A key result is that equilibrium payments reproduce VCG payments, making the mechanism efficient and an ex post equilibrium. This helps explain stable bidding and why Google’s ad pages can perform well. The lecture emphasizes that quality scores and reserve prices are important in practice, though not fully captured by the basic model.

Athey and Ellison’s model adds consumer search. Consumers incur costs when clicking ads, advertisers differ privately in quality, and sponsored search can guide consumers by ordering firms by likely relevance. Reserve prices can improve welfare by signaling that displayed ads are likely worth considering. Under uniform search costs, consumer surplus and social welfare are maximized at the same reserve price, while departures from the consumer-optimal reserve price benefit Google at the expense of consumers and advertisers.

The lecture briefly covers Anderson and Renault’s model with endogenous pricing, where firms set prices after learning screen position and multiple search equilibria can arise. It also discusses Armstrong and Zhou’s platform design model, where platforms choose what information consumers receive about products. Consumer-optimal outcomes are generally unattainable because information that helps consumers choose also gives firms pricing power, while different information structures mainly shift surplus between consumers and producers.

Embodiments concern managing indexed data in computing environments, particularly optimizing index file size based on storage conditions for indexed data. The passage describes data intake and query systems, including SPLUNK® ENTERPRISE, that collect machine-generated data from sources such as servers, networks, applications, mobile devices, sensors, and IoT devices. The system stores minimally processed raw data as timestamped events, supports late-binding schemas, and applies extraction rules at search time to derive field values.

The architecture includes host devices, client devices, forwarders, indexers, search heads, and data stores. Forwarders receive raw data, segment it into blocks, add metadata, and forward it for processing. Indexers parse data into events, assign timestamps and metadata, optionally transform events, generate keyword indexes, and store events in time-based buckets. Search heads receive queries, delegate parts to indexers, combine partial results, and return events, calculated values, reports, or visualizations.

The system supports field extraction across heterogeneous data sources, allowing common field names to correlate semantically equivalent values from differently formatted events. User interfaces include search screens, time range pickers, data source selectors, event lists, timelines, field sidebars, report editors, and visualization tools. Data models provide hierarchical, search-time mappings of semantic knowledge, enabling users to generate reports without directly writing query language.

Several acceleration techniques are described: distributing search operations across multiple indexers, using keyword indexes, maintaining high-performance analytics stores or summarization tables for field-value combinations, and generating intermediate summaries to speed periodic report updates. The passage also discusses security and data center monitoring applications, including SPLUNK® APP FOR ENTERPRISE SECURITY and SPLUNK® APP FOR VMWARE®, which use stored event data, schemas, dashboards, alerts, notable events, performance metrics, and visualizations to support investigation and monitoring.

The system may be deployed on premises or as a cloud-based service, where subscribers access configurable system instances over a network.

Egyptian archaeologists unveiled a Fifth Dynasty Old Kingdom tomb on the Giza plateau built for Hetpet, a priestess of Hathor. Discovered in Giza’s western cemetery, the tomb features an L-shaped shrine, a purification basin inscribed with Hetpet’s name and titles, and well-preserved wall paintings showing hunting, fishing, offerings, music, dancing, and rare monkey scenes. Officials said similar monkey imagery had previously been found only in the tomb of Ka-Iber in Saqqara. Archaeologists plan to continue excavations at the site.

SOS full court pressure scenarios are designed to make offenses react to backcourt pressure, alter tempo, create fatigue, force turnovers, and generate transition opportunities. Primary “shadow” presses include Back shadow, Up shadow, and Face shadow, differing by initial alignment, while secondary “Blitz” pressures are more aggressive and deny first passing lanes with deep backcourt trapping. Effective execution depends on SOS fundamentals: forcing the ball away from the middle, denying penetration and passing lanes, and transitioning to Base Go Red unless pressure is broken.

The UK and Ukraine discussed maintaining and strengthening trade and investment links after Brexit, including continuity of the EU-Ukraine Association Agreement and DCFTA, to avoid disruption and preserve preferential trade terms during the UK-EU Implementation Period.

Amber Enterprises received Sebi approval to raise about Rs 555 crore through an IPO, including a Rs 450 crore fresh issue and Rs 105 crore promoter share sale. Proceeds will be used for loan repayment, advance payments, and general corporate purposes.

GHCBData is used to communicate GHCB addresses, supported protocol versions, and the SEV page table encryption bit. The hypervisor supplies protocol version ranges and the encryption bit before the GHCB address is established; the guest selects a supported version or terminates if none is compatible. CPUID information needed before GHCB setup can be requested through the MSR protocol, though only one register value is returned per VMGEXIT and functions requiring non-zero sub-leafs are unsupported.

GHCB GPA registration is required for SEV-SNP guests before first GHCB use. A guest may request a hypervisor-preferred GHCB GPA, register a selected GPA, or unregister the current GPA. Registration replaces any previous registration, and the hypervisor must terminate the guest if a supplied GHCB GPA does not match the registered value. Multi-VMPL support requires separate GHCB GPA registration per VMPL.

GHCB negotiation examples describe how the hypervisor initializes VMCB offset 0x00a0, how the guest obtains the encryption bit and protocol range, enters long mode, marks the GHCB shared, registers it when required, and writes the GHCB GPA to MSR 0xc001_0130 before VMGEXIT use. VMGEXIT handling requires the guest to populate GHCB fields and valid bits, while the hypervisor reads the GHCB GPA, processes the exit, updates response state, and resumes the guest.

Non-Automatic Exit events cause #VC exceptions for SEV-ES guests. The guest inspects the error code, supplies required state in the GHCB, invokes VMGEXIT, and later copies returned state back. Guests and hypervisors must reset and set VALID_BITMAP bits for provided fields. SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2 are used for errors, including requested exceptions, malformed input, unregistered GHCB addresses, invalid scratch fields, missing valid bits, or invalid NAE input.

The passage defines handling for IOIO, MSR, VMMCALL, MMIO, page state change, SNP guest request, SNP extended guest request, AP creation, #HV doorbell page, #HV send IPI, #HV timer, APIC ID list, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO guest request, Secure AVIC, termination request, and unsupported NAE events. Page state changes use shared buffer structures and update progress fields so interrupted requests can resume. SNP guest requests use shared request and response pages and return firmware status in SW_EXITINFO2. Extended requests can return certificate data in GUID-indexed tables.

SEV-SNP guests receive a secrets page, including a guest reserved area for VMPL message sequence numbers, AP jump table address, and guest usage. EFI platforms may communicate secrets and CPUID pages through an SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob configuration table.

SMP boot under SEV-ES and some SEV-SNP configurations cannot rely on the hypervisor modifying measured register state. AP reset hold protocols allow APs to halt until INIT-SIPI-SIPI, while the SNP AP Creation NAE event allows guests to provide VMSA pages and can support vCPU hotplug. Restricted Injection requires SNP AP Creation instead of AP Reset Hold.

For NMIs, the hypervisor must not intercept IRET, must intercept #DB, and must wait for an “NMI Complete” VMGEXIT message before injecting another NMI. Hardware debug register virtualization is supported when DebugVirtualization is enabled; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and cached. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

Restricted Injection uses a shared #HV doorbell page with PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. The host presents interrupts and non-maskable events through this page and may signal #HV. This study examined extracellular matrix changes in the hippocampus in substance use disorder (SUD), major depressive disorder (MDD), comorbid SUD/MDD, and controls, with a focus on perineuronal nets (PNNs), WFA-labeled glia, and related gene expression. Human postmortem hippocampal samples were analyzed using microscopy and qPCR, and hippocampal samples from rhesus macaques with chronic alcohol self-administration were used to assess alcohol-related effects.

Subjects with SUD showed increased PNN density in CA1 stratum oriens and several other hippocampal regions, increased WFA-labeled glia in CA4 and dentate gyrus, increased Pvb and Vamp2 expression, increased Chsy1 expression, and decreased Mmp9 and Ctss expression. Rhesus macaques with chronic alcohol self-administration also showed increased hippocampal PNN density and increased WFA-labeled glia in the dentate gyrus. Subjects with MDD generally showed decreased PNN density in CA1, increased WFA-glia in several regions, increased Pvb and Vamp2 expression, and increased Ctss expression. Subjects with comorbid SUD/MDD showed altered PNN and WFA-glia densities, increased Pvb, Acan, and Chsy1 expression, and decreased Gfap expression.

The authors conclude that increased hippocampal PNNs in SUD, along with reduced ECM proteolytic gene expression and altered synaptic markers, supports preclinical evidence that PNNs may stabilize reward memories and could be relevant to cue-induced relapse. Opposing or altered findings in MDD and comorbid SUD/MDD highlight the importance of considering psychiatric comorbidities in SUD pathology and treatment research.

The passage describes systems and methods for localizing, classifying, and detecting abnormalities in medical images using deep learning. One approach uses a jointly trained localization network and classification network to generate lesion localization maps and classify lesions, including multi-modality fusion for mpMRI images and regression-based scoring such as PI-RADS. The networks may use encoder-decoder architectures, classification networks, localization heat maps, preprocessing, anatomical masks, and post-processing features.

Another approach detects abnormalities by deleting portions of an input medical image, generating synthesized images with a trained generative adversarial network, selecting a synthesized normal image, and detecting abnormal regions by comparing the input image with the normal image. Deleted regions may be selected randomly, by pattern, by target location, or with stencils.

The passage also describes training deep learning models using multi-site datasets. A model is trained on data from multiple clinical sites, then optimized for a deployment site using annotated deployment data. Sub-datasets may be reordered by similarity, deployment samples by uncertainty, and models selectively updated based on performance comparisons. The described methods may be implemented on computer systems, cloud systems, apparatuses, or non-transitory computer-readable media.

UVA Health System’s thoracic Enhanced Recovery After Surgery program, launched in 2016, helped thoracic surgery patients leave the hospital sooner while reducing costs and opioid use. In its first year, the program enrolled 139 patients and was compared with more than 220 prior patients. It reduced morphine equivalent use by 74% in one group and 59% in another without worsening reported pain, cut median hospital stays for thoracotomy patients by two days, saved more than $1.3 million, and freed beds for an estimated 28 additional patients. The review found no increase in surgical complications or readmissions. The program emphasizes patient education, standardized care, nutritional optimization, reduced intravenous fluids, early mobility, and pain control with less opioid use. Researchers plan continued evaluation, including patient outcomes and outpatient opioid use. The findings were published in the Annals of Thoracic Surgery.

The passage explains offensive goal kicks in soccer, emphasizing that the main objective is to retain possession and build an attack. A goal kick is awarded when the attacking team last touches the ball over the defenders’ goal line and may be taken by any player from within the goal area. The ball is in play once kicked and visibly moves, and opponents may then enter the penalty area.

For young players, smaller fields and build-out lines help prevent opponents from immediately pressuring goal kicks. Suggested youth tactics include short kicks to nearby teammates, dribbling wide and upfield, using secondary receivers, and avoiding passes across one’s own goal. Players must be positioned and ready, and one player should be prepared to defend if possession is lost.

For older youth, goal-kick options expand to multiple targets based on defensive coverage, including wider and farther upfield receivers and supporting midfielders. Coaches should train setups on both sides of the field, add defenders in practice, and teach targets to move strongly toward the ball.

For adults, all goal-kick options are available, including short passes, pre-arranged targets, and deeper kicks. Goalkeepers usually take the kick. The passage also notes that goal kicks are direct restarts and that wind or field conditions can significantly affect outcomes.

A prospective descriptive cross-sectional study at Tesseney Community Hospital, Eritrea, examined clinical features and outcomes of scorpion sting admissions from 1 June 2019 to 31 May 2020. Among 165 patients, sex distribution was nearly equal, 61.8% were aged 15 years or older, 57% were from urban areas, and shepherds, farmers, and students were the most common occupational groups. Most stings occurred on the foot, at night, and indoors; black scorpions were most often identified. Eight patients died, giving a case fatality rate of 4.8%.

The most common manifestations were localized pain, sweating, vomiting, paraesthesia, relative bradycardia, restlessness, fever, and shock. By Abroug’s classification, 20.6% were class I, 35.8% class II, and 43.6% class III. Children had more severe envenomation, with those under five presenting with class III stings in 75% of cases. Patients younger than 15 years and those with no formal education were reported as possible predisposing factors for symptom severity. Most cases occurred during summer, especially September and October.

Treatment included local anesthesia, oral analgesics, diazepam, IV fluids, antibiotics, and, for moderate to severe cases, nifedipine and/or scorpion antivenom. The study concluded that localized pain, sweating, and vomiting were the main clinical features; adults had a higher sting burden, while children had greater severity and related fatality. Recommendations included prevention education, improved care-seeking, availability of essential drugs such as prazosin, updated treatment guidelines, and surveys on scorpion habitats, seasonality, and species.

The passage explains that a random walk trading strategy is based on the idea that stock prices move unpredictably, making technical, fundamental, and sentiment analysis unreliable. It emphasizes diversification, often through broad market index funds or diversified stock portfolios, rather than market timing.

The random walk theory, popularized by Burton Malkiel’s *A Random Walk Down Wall Street* and traced to Louise Bachelier, assumes stock prices have an equal chance of rising or falling. It is compared with the efficient market hypothesis, which argues prices reflect available information; both suggest it is difficult to consistently outperform the market, though the passage notes contradictions and limitations in both theories.

The article discusses the Wall Street Journal Dartboard Contest, where experts beat dart-selected stocks more often but did not significantly outperform the Dow Jones Industrial Average. Backtests showed a random-entry strategy performed positively on SPY, helped by the stock market’s upward drift, but performed poorly on GLD. The passage concludes that short-term price action is mostly random, but systematic rules, backtesting, and the stock market’s long-term upward drift may offer trading opportunities.

Anthurium, a South American plant with red, pink, or white flowers, can filter ammonia and xylene indoors. It needs indirect light, humidity, 18°C–21°C temperatures, winter leaf spraying, and regular repotting. Its sap and leaves may cause allergies.

The paper studies finitely generated Gorenstein-projective modules over the dual integers Z[ε], noting that classifying all Z[ε]-modules is infeasible. It relates G-proj Z[ε] to torsionless modules, perfect differential structures, and orbits of bounded complexes of free abelian groups, while noting failure of the Krull-Remak-Schmidt property. Its main theorem states equivalences among the stable category of Gorenstein-projective Z[ε]-modules, submodules of free Z[ε]-modules modulo projectives, Db(Z)/[1], and categories of perfect differential structures. The paper also describes a chain of dense functors from bounded complexes of free abelian groups to finite abelian groups, and a commutative cube formed by functors modulo shifts, projectives, and stalk objects.

The passage presents a Bayesian hierarchical multinomial model for estimating viral variant dynamics using genomic sequencing data pooled across countries. It addresses challenges caused by sparse and geographically uneven sequencing, noting that as of July 1, 2022, the United States and United Kingdom contributed 54.9% of SARS-CoV-2 sequences in GISAID, and 10% of submitting countries contributed 90.3% of sequences.

The model estimates country-specific variant prevalence, country-specific growth rates, and global relative fitness while accounting for geographic heterogeneity and limited data. It partially pools information across countries and variants, shrinking uncertain country-specific estimates toward broader global patterns unless data strongly support deviation. The framework is intended to improve estimates in regions with limited sequencing capacity and for newly emerging variants with few sequences.

Applied to SARS-CoV-2 variants from April to July 2022, the model found that BA.4 and BA.5 rapidly replaced BA.2, with heterogeneous invasion patterns across countries. BA.5 had the highest estimated global fitness advantage relative to BA.2, followed by BA.4 and BA.2.12.1, while BA.1 was estimated to be less fit than BA.2. Country-specific fitness advantages varied substantially.

Retrospective validation using BA.5 emergence in Portugal showed that the multicountry model produced more stable early estimates and lower Brier scores than single-country multinomial regression, especially when local data were sparse. Unlike the single-country model, it could generate country-specific estimates before a variant was observed in sufficient quantities locally.

The authors state that the method can support real-time genomic surveillance, nowcasting, and early risk assessment, including in low- and middle-income countries. They note assumptions including random sampling within geographic units, unbiased sequencing across variants, correct lineage assignment, constant relative fitness during the modeled period, and equal generation intervals across variants.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis won the 2025 Nobel Prize in physics for demonstrating quantum tunneling and energy quantization in an electric circuit in the 1980s. Their Josephson junction experiments showed quantum effects at a macroscopic scale and helped form the basis for superconducting qubits used in quantum computers.

IT-based simulation, modeling, virtual prototyping, digital twins, IoT data, and high-performance data analytics are expanding industrial product development and manufacturing scenarios by accelerating development, reducing physical testing, improving feedback loops, and supporting optimization. IDC’s survey of 200 industrial decision makers in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland found broad current use and growing demand for high-performance calculations, though many enterprises face outdated simulations, slow iterations, limited computing capacity, and infrastructure constraints.

HPC is presented as a key enabler for complex calculations, higher-quality simulations, more iterations, new use cases, and faster innovation. Most surveyed decision makers view HPC as a game changer, while adoption is growing through professional infrastructures, pilots, and planned deployments. Enterprises use or plan external HPC infrastructures, colocation, research partners, on-premises systems, public cloud, hybrid cloud, and HPC as a Service. Cloud-based HPC and HPCaaS are highlighted for scalability, flexibility, cost optimization, access to modern hardware and methods, collaboration, and support for new HPC-based business models. IDC concludes that simulations, modeling, analytics, digital twins, and HPC are becoming central to manufacturing digital transformation, requiring integrated data strategies, a single source of truth, suitable HPC operating models, scalable and secure solutions, energy efficiency, and external expertise where needed.

The passage provides design guidance for TPS7H500x-SP push-pull converter applications. It recommends an 80-V GaN FET for synchronous rectification despite an expected 20-V maximum stress, with optional parallel Schottky diodes to reduce soft-start current and reverse conduction losses. An RCD clamp can limit switch-node voltage and should be optimized through testing. The example design uses a 0.47-µH output inductor, at least 1.3 mF output capacitance for ripple and transient requirements, and about 2.3 mF total capacitance for radiation-induced SET mitigation. Optional output filtering can reduce ripple, with damping added if high-frequency peaking occurs.

The design sets cycle-by-cycle current limiting near 35 A, selects a 7.5-Ω current-sense resistor, uses a 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, and applies Type 2A compensation with 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF components. A 102-kΩ slope compensation resistor is connected between RSC and AVSS.

Power supply guidance specifies a 4-V to 14-V controller input, proper bypassing, at least 0.1 µF from VIN to AVSS, ceramic capacitors near the controller, and bulk capacitance when the input supply is distant. Layout guidance emphasizes separating noisy power paths from sensitive signals, minimizing switch-node area and high-current loops, separating analog and power grounds with a single connection point, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, filtering CS_ILIM if needed, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS with vias. The passage also lists related documentation, update notification information, support resources, ESD cautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, orderable, and disclaimer information.

The Open Source Definition emerged in early February 1998, after Netscape’s source code release prompted interest in a business-friendly alternative to “free software.” Christine Peterson proposed “open source,” while Bruce Perens published the OSD, adapted from the Debian Free Software Guidelines. Both open source and free software center on available source code and licenses favoring user freedom, though open source was framed as more commercially palatable. The approach gained broad industry adoption, with major tech companies and platforms relying on open source components. Microsoft, once hostile to Linux, later embraced open source. Red Hat’s Tim Burke said open source has shifted from cloning proprietary software to leading innovation.

The passage describes MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 device modules, features, support resources, and documentation updates. The PMU provides regulated core supplies, VDD supervision, BOR thresholds, operating-mode regulator support, and parity-protected trim. The clock module supplies internal and external oscillators, SYSPLL, and distributed clocks for CPU, peripherals, ADC, CAN, and external output. DMA supports memory transfers without CPU intervention, multiple full-feature and basic channels, configurable triggers, interrupts, cascading, and stride mode.

The event manager routes peripheral events to the CPU, DMA, or other peripherals. Memory-related sections describe flash with ECC, in-circuit program/erase, 1kB sectors, endurance options, and bank address swap; SRAM up to 128KB in two banks with protection and partitioning; and factory constants for device data and trim information. GPIO supports up to 93 pins, wake features, and bit set/clear/toggle operations, while IOMUX configures IO pads, muxing, and pin functions.

Analog and mixed-signal peripherals include two 12-bit ADCs with fast conversion, averaging, internal channels, and references; a temperature sensor connected to ADC input with factory calibration; VREF with selectable 1.4V and 2.5V internal references or external reference; comparators with wakeup and timer fault connections; and a 12-bit buffered DAC with calibration, FIFO, DMA, and hardware trigger support.

Security features include AES-128/256 acceleration, firewalls, secure key storage, CRC, TRNG, AESADV modes, keystore storage for up to four keys, and CRC-16/CRC-32. Communication peripherals include UART, I2C, SPI, and CAN-FD with DMA/FIFO support and protocol-specific features. LFSS includes RTC_B and IWDT; RTC_B provides calendar, alarms, periodic interrupts, calibration, and clock output, while IWDT and WWDT supervise code execution. TIMGx and TIMAx timers provide counting, PWM, synchronization, triggers, fault handling, and DMA/interrupt generation.

The passage also covers analog connections, IO diagrams, SWD debug, BSL programming over UART or I2C with password protection, typical application connection guidance, development tools, documentation support, trademarks, ESD caution, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.
