Energy storage is promoted as a way to integrate more renewable energy and reduce reliance on fossil fuels, but its economic value depends on whether bill savings exceed capital and running costs. Storage technologies vary: lithium ion batteries suit small-scale use but remain costly; pumped hydro is cheap at large scale; flywheels support short bursts and grid stability; and compressed air, liquid air, flow batteries and hydrogen have different roles.

Lithium ion battery costs have fallen significantly, but for a household with rooftop solar and variable electricity rates, a 7kWh battery must cost under about A$7,000 installed, or A$1,000 per kWh, to break even. Current battery costs are about A$1,000–3,000 per kWh. If electricity tariffs flatten, batteries may need to fall to around A$300 per kWh to be cost-effective. Network savings from batteries are limited if electricity demand is flat or falling.

Pumped hydro costs about A$100 per kWh and already provides 1,500MW in the National Electricity Market, making it a cheaper and more controllable option where geography allows. However, lithium ion batteries may still become popular due to consumer behaviour rather than economics.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on August 3, 2020, it amended its Restated Articles of Incorporation to increase authorized common shares from 12.6 billion to 50.4 billion and provide for a four-for-one stock split effective at 5 p.m. Pacific daylight time on August 28, 2020. The filing includes the Restated Articles as Exhibit 3.1 and was signed by Katherine Adams on August 7, 2020.

Bitcoin futures were set to begin trading on Cboe Global Markets’ Cboe Futures Exchange, adding momentum to bitcoin’s rapid and volatile price rise. The cash-settled contracts are based on Gemini Exchange’s bitcoin auction price. Supporters say regulated futures could broaden access, allow hedging, and improve price discovery, while avoiding digital wallets and unregulated spot exchanges. However, major banks and brokerages responded cautiously, with some delaying access or clearing, and others imposing restrictions. Analysts said futures may eventually reduce volatility, but risks remain, including uncertain pricing, clearinghouse exposure, margin failures, and potential manipulation of the underlying spot market.

The Korean diet is based on traditional Korean eating habits, emphasizing whole, unprocessed foods, vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, fermented foods, smaller portions, and broth-based dishes. Common foods include rice, barley, vegetables, kimchi, fermented soybean products, soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and spices. It limits processed foods, sugary drinks, unhealthy fats, and dairy. Potential benefits include weight loss, improved digestion, gut health, and overall wellbeing due to fibre, plant-based foods, fermented foods, and antioxidants. Drawbacks include high sodium, low calcium, spicy ingredients that may irritate digestion, and high carbohydrate content requiring portion control.
CoachingAmericanSoccer.com provides general on-field tactical guidance for new soccer players and coaches.
The speaker expresses support for Horton’s recovery, notes the team must move on after a tough loss, and says they will focus on improving and responding strongly in the next game.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated October 28, 2021, reporting that it issued a press release on its financial results for the fourth fiscal quarter ended September 25, 2021. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1, with Inline XBRL cover page data as Exhibit 104. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The passage provides Sansa Fuze instructions for transferring, playing, managing, and deleting media. Music can be transferred by drag-and-drop, Windows Media Player playlists and sync, or Audible Manager for Audible files. Photos and videos require Sansa Media Converter, which can convert, crop, rotate, resize, and transfer files to the player or microSD card.

The Sansa Fuze supports playback of MP3, WMA, secure WMA, Audible, audiobooks, podcasts, WAV, and voice recordings in supported formats. It includes controls for playback, skipping, fast-forwarding, rewinding, volume, repeat, shuffle, MusicEQ, ratings, Go Lists, deletion, audiobook chapter mode, and playback speed. Videos can be played from the Video menu with options for bookmarks, ratings, brightness, and deletion. Photos can be viewed individually or as slideshows with shuffle, loop, slide duration, music, Photo Go List, and deletion options.

The player may include FM radio, with tuning, preset programming, automatic preset scanning, preset deletion, radio recording, FM region, and mono/stereo mode options. It also has a built-in microphone for voice recordings.

Content can be deleted directly from the player or through Windows Explorer on a computer. System settings include wallpaper color, display art in lists, backlight, power saver, language, date and time, brightness, volume, factory reset, device information, USB mode, formatting, and press-and-hold behavior.

Troubleshooting covers supported bit rates, formatting, firmware updates, photo and video transfer, unsupported playback due to rights, podcasts, unknown artist or album metadata, microSD and microSDHC compatibility, and power reset. The support section provides SanDisk contact information, support links, warranty terms, and software license restrictions, disclaimers, liability limits, transfer rules, termination terms, high-risk-use exclusions, and governing law.

The ADS9803 supports a speed-boost mode up to 8MSPS for one user-selected analog input channel pair, with the remaining six channels idle and conversion on every sampling clock. Register access uses 16-bit configuration registers across three banks selected through REG_BANK_SEL; SPI writes and reads require specified frame sequences, with read mode enabled through SPI_RD_EN and SPI_MODE. Multiple ADCs can be configured in a daisy-chain topology using shared CS and SCLK, chained SDI/SDO connections, and DAISY_CHAIN_LEN to define the number of downstream devices; register writes require N × 24 SCLKs.

The passage lists register fields for bank selection, daisy-chain length, test patterns, averaging, XOR operation, gain error correction, speed-boost configuration, analog input bandwidth, power-down control, reference selection, output lane mode, common-mode range, and initialization settings. Application information describes ADS9803 use in ATE systems as an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS DAQ with built-in analog front end, post-calibration TUE of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C, and wide-bandwidth settling to 99.95% full scale in 7.5µs. Power, decoupling, and layout guidance recommends separate decoupling for supply pins, close bypass capacitors, and keeping analog and reference signals away from noise sources. The document also includes TI support, documentation update, ESD, packaging, orderable information, and disclaimer sections.

This retrospective study aimed to develop a predictive model for shunt-dependent hydrocephalus (SDHC) after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). Medical records of 109 patients treated with surgical clipping or endovascular coiling from 2013 to 2021 were analyzed. All patients received external ventricular drainage, and ventriculoperitoneal shunt surgery was performed after failed drainage challenge or recurrent hydrocephalus. Multivariate analysis identified age ≥65 years, Hunt and Hess scale ≥3, and clipping rather than coiling as significant predictors of SDHC. A nomogram based on these factors was developed, with an area under the curve of 0.753. The authors noted the study was limited by its retrospective design and small sample size.

Nike reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $11.72 billion, up 1% from a year earlier and above Wall Street expectations, despite previously forecasting a mid-single-digit decline. Net income fell to $727 million, or 49 cents per share, from $1.05 billion, or 70 cents per share, while gross margin dropped to 42.2%. CEO Elliott Hill said Nike is making progress in wholesale, running and North America, but other sports, geographies and channels remain challenged. Wholesale revenue rose, North America sales increased 4%, Nike direct sales fell 4%, and China revenue declined 9%. Nike continues its turnaround strategy, including clearing old inventory through discounts, reorganizing teams by sport, and expanding its focus on female customers through NikeSKIMS.

Dolphins receiver Tyreek Hill dislocated his knee during Monday night’s win over the Jets and remained hospitalized overnight for further tests. The injury occurred early in the third quarter after a 10-yard catch when his left leg twisted as he was tackled out of bounds. Hill had six catches for 67 yards before exiting. Coach Mike McDaniel said Hill was in good spirits and wanted the team to secure its first win of the season.

An international team found live giant shipworms, Kuphus polythalamia, in a lagoon on an abandoned log farm in the Philippines, enabling study of a species long known from shells but rarely seen alive. The mud-dwelling mollusk lives in a tusk-like shell up to 5 feet long and feeds on hydrogen sulfide through microbes in its gill rather than eating wood. Researchers hope studying these microbes may reveal new antimicrobial substances. The findings were published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Scientists said many aspects of the animal’s life cycle, age and populations remain unknown.

The passage discusses a seasonal trading strategy for the German stock market using the iShares MSCI Germany ETF (EWG), which tracks large and mid-size German companies. The DAX 40 is Germany’s main stock index, comprising 40 blue-chip companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, and has returned 5.36% annually since inception. EWG’s historical monthly returns since 1996 suggest its strongest performance occurs in the final quarter, while the rest of the year is mostly sideways. The proposed strategy invests only during the last three months of each year. A backtest using dividend- and split-adjusted EWG data found that this approach performed well over recent decades.

Earlier, warmer, and drier springs in the northern Rockies are affecting native cutthroat trout, which thrive in cold streams. As climate change warms and lowers stream flows, rainbow trout are moving into cutthroat habitat and breeding with them. Ecologist Clint Muhlfeld says the resulting hybrids are less fit and cannot revert to pure cutthroat genetics. A study in Global Change Biology found widespread hybridization, especially where rainbow trout were introduced by fish and game departments. Some states are trying to remove rainbow trout to protect cutthroat trout, whose native genomes and adaptive traits could otherwise be permanently lost.

A nationwide study of Medicare-aged adults found that long-term outdoor exposure to trichloroethylene (TCE), an industrial solvent used in metal degreasing and dry cleaning, was associated with a modestly higher risk of Parkinson’s disease. Researchers compared 221,789 people with Parkinson’s to over 1.1 million without it and estimated exposure using ZIP+4 locations and EPA air pollution data. Those in areas with the highest TCE levels had a 10% higher risk than those in the lowest exposure areas, after adjusting for factors such as age, smoking history and fine particulate pollution. The study shows an association, not causation, and may not apply to younger people or reflect lifetime or indoor exposure.

Former INEC official Christian Nwosu told a Lagos Federal High Court that EFCC operatives coerced him into admitting he received N30 million from former Petroleum Minister Dieziani Alison-Madueke. He alleged that operative Usman Zakari threatened detention unless he wrote a dictated statement, and that he was escorted to a bank to make drafts totaling N5 million to the EFCC. Nwosu also claimed he was pressured to surrender property worth N30 million and that EFCC prosecutor Rotimi Oyedepo advised him to cooperate, allegedly warning he could be convicted and jailed if he refused.
John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis won the 2025 Nobel Prize in physics for demonstrating quantum effects in an electric circuit.

State Street Corporation agreed to pay $5 million to settle Department of Labor claims that it paid 305 senior female employees and 15 black vice presidents less than colleagues in the same positions, while denying the allegations. The firm commissioned the “Fearless Girl” statue, installed in New York’s financial district to promote women in leadership and State Street Global Advisors’ gender diversity index. The passage highlights criticism and irony surrounding the settlement and the statue’s message.

Sir John Deane’s sixth form college held its fourth Evening of Jazz and Soul at the Macdonald Portal Hotel, Golf and Spa in Tarporley. A 35-strong jazz collective directed by Timothy Murphy performed 60s soul and classic swing. Head of performing arts Alison Richards praised the students and audience support. The college’s next event is a classical music evening at Arley Hall on February 9.

The passage highlights 2016 Evening Sun stories: Norwich children Evan and Brynn Meek handed out 220 lunches to homeless people in Manhattan; Norwich Police Officer Thomas Miller left after eight years to join Syracuse Police, with recognition of his community work with K9 Nitro; and Tracy A. Price of Norwich was arrested for allegedly torturing, injuring, and neglecting a dog.

A swimming advisory was issued for Little Beach in Port Stanley due to high bacteria levels, warning of possible gastrointestinal illness and infection. The beach remains open, as the threshold for closure has not been reached. Some visitors continued swimming, with one parent saying she had not noticed the advisory signs. Advisories are posted on the Elgin St. Thomas Health Unit website.

A 36-year-old New York man, Reinaldo De Jesus Henao, was arrested at Coachella after concertgoers used “Find my iPhone” to track stolen phones. Police said he had more than 100 cellphones in his backpack and faces grand theft and possession of stolen property charges.

Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology used machine learning and advanced simulations to clarify the low-temperature structure of formamidinium lead iodide, a promising halide perovskite for efficient, flexible solar cells. Their models enabled much longer simulations with millions of atoms and were compared with experiments at the University of Birmingham. The findings address a longstanding question about the material’s phase and may help researchers better design and control perovskite materials and mixtures for future solar technologies.

Syrian grandmother Wafa Yahia, whose case is central to Hawaii’s lawsuit challenging President Trump’s travel ban, arrived in Honolulu after receiving U.S. approval. Her son-in-law, imam Ismail Elshikh, is a plaintiff arguing the ban prevented her visit. Legal challenges continue, with appeals pending and Supreme Court review expected. Hawaii Attorney General Doug Chin said her visa approval does not affect the lawsuit, while Elshikh said the challenge enabled his children to reunite with their grandmother.

Cuba honored Fidel Castro with a military parade in Havana marking the 58th anniversary of the revolution that brought him to power. Tens of thousands marched, some carrying “We are Fidel” banners and photos, despite his request against a personality cult. The event came as Cuba faces economic strain, Raul Castro’s planned departure, and uncertainty over US ties under President-elect Donald Trump.

A study in the Journal of Experimental Psychology suggests general distraction can boost mood after a breakup in the short term but should be used sparingly. Distractions include hobbies, school, or exercise. Focusing on negative aspects of an ex or past relationship may also help people move on faster.

The author describes difficulty sleeping during pregnancy due to discomfort and advice to avoid sleeping on the back, stomach, or right side. As a stomach-sleeper, she worried about rest and researched pregnancy pillows. After seeing a recommendation for the U-shaped Leachco pillow, she bought it and found it greatly improved comfort, allowing side sleeping, easier turning, and better support. She also used it while relaxing on the couch. Downsides include its large size, scratchy original cover, and tendency to disrupt blankets, though replacement covers are available. She considers the pillow worthwhile and plans to keep using it after pregnancy.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated July 27, 2021, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2021. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The filing lists Microsoft’s registered securities on NASDAQ and was signed by Alice L. Jolla, Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer.

Vale SA said its stock conversion plan received support from 84.4 percent of preferred shares, exceeding the required threshold. Executives said the success could accelerate listing common shares on São Paulo’s Novo Mercado, possibly this year, and no cash incentives are planned for remaining preferred shareholders. The restructuring merges share classes, aims to broaden the investor base, improve governance, and reduce political influence, though Brazil’s government retains a golden share. Vale also planned to absorb Valepar as part of its move toward dispersed ownership.

The study analyzed the Omicron BA.1 wave in England from November 2021 to January 2022 using 48,615 English BA.1 genomes, global genomic data, mobility data, and epidemiological data. It identified at least 6,455 independent introductions into England, most of which were singletons. A small number of early introductions, many occurring before or during travel restrictions on southern African countries, accounted for a large share of reported BA.1 infections. Importations continued to rise through mid-December, with estimated importation intensity from the United States exceeding that from South Africa during the restriction period.

Omicron BA.1 initially expanded around Greater London and surrounding areas, then spread to other regions through human mobility. Greater London acted as a major source during the early expansion, while later spread involved more mid- and long-range movements from other regions. Mobility reductions from mid-December to early January and behavioral responses to rising case numbers likely contributed to spatial and temporal differences in epidemic peaks. The authors conclude that targeted travel restrictions were largely ineffective once local transmission and alternative importation routes existed, and that future responses require integrated genomic, epidemiological, and mobility analyses.

The paper adopts the UN definition of youth as ages 15–24 and defines skills development as both hard and soft skills. It frames cooperative education (co-op) as a form of experiential learning integrated into curricula to improve school-to-work transitions and align education with Nigeria’s labor market needs.

Nigeria’s youth unemployment has risen in recent years and is higher than total unemployment, while youth employment-to-population ratios remain lower than those of the overall working population. Labor market challenges include informality, high NEET rates, gender disparities, regional differences, and higher unemployment among some educated youth.

Co-op originated in industrialized countries and is used in some African post-secondary institutions. Its core elements are integrated curriculum, learning through work experience, and coordinated administration. Models include alternating school and work terms, parallel school-work schedules, and sandwich-style placements. Reported benefits include improved employability, earnings, career clarity, employer recruitment, curriculum development, and labor productivity, though research quality varies and evidence is mainly from developed countries.

Existing Nigerian responses to youth unemployment include SIWES, SURE-P, and N-SIP. SIWES provides work experience for tertiary students but is described as less integrated with academic curricula and employer collaboration than co-op. The paper argues that co-op could complement or be integrated into existing government programs, especially SIWES and N-Power, using government support, employer participation, and institutional coordination. It recommends the alternating co-op model and suggests pilot testing before wider rollout.

The paper concludes that co-op could strengthen collaboration among universities, employers, and government to better prepare Nigerian youth for work, but broader labor demand and supply policies are also needed. Further research is recommended on governance, suitable co-op models, institutional adaptation, and applicability beyond tertiary education.

This qualitative phenomenological study examined primary school teachers’ views on the participation of students with disabilities in inclusive settings in virtual education during the COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 10 general education primary school teachers in the Marmara region and analyzed using content analysis.

Findings showed that teachers used EBA, Zoom, WhatsApp, parent communication, support activities, and varied instructional practices to conduct virtual education. Some students with disabilities participated regularly, especially with family support and adequate technology, while others had limited or no participation due to internet or device problems, parents’ low literacy or technology skills, lack of family follow-up, or preference for rehabilitation center education.

Teachers reported challenges including difficulty individualizing instruction, limited student interaction, problems tracking assignments, students keeping cameras off, low motivation, behavioral issues, crowded classes, insufficient communication with parents, and inadequate support for social development. Some teachers reported fewer problems when families were economically stable, cooperative, and actively monitored students.

Suggested solutions included strengthening teacher-parent cooperation, providing device and internet support, improving EBA support points, keeping schools accessible for students with disabilities, supporting both academic and social development, coordinating with rehabilitation centers, and preparing virtual education materials suitable for students with disabilities and their families.

The TLV321/2x comparators consume 40 µA per channel with 40 ns propagation delay. TLV321x devices have push-pull outputs, while TLV322x devices have open-drain outputs that can be pulled up to voltages up to 5.5 V independent of comparator supply voltage.

Inputs operate from 200 mV below V− to 200 mV above V+, with no phase inversion within this range. Input voltages must not exceed supply rails by more than 200 mV, and input current should be limited to 10 mA or less, with series resistance recommended for transients or faults. Unused inputs should not be tied together; they must be biased within the valid range with at least 50 mV differential voltage.

The devices include 1.8 mV internal hysteresis. External hysteresis can be added using feedback networks for inverting or non-inverting comparator configurations to reduce chatter near the switching threshold. Smaller overdrive voltage increases propagation delay, especially below 100 mV.

Push-pull outputs can sink and source current but must not be connected to other outputs or shorted to supply rails; unused push-pull outputs should float. Open-drain outputs support wired-OR logic and level translation; TI recommends pull-up currents from 100 µA to 1 mA. Unused open-drain outputs may float or connect to V−.

Inputs and outputs include ESD protection to V+ and V−. The devices also include power-on reset, holding the output low for up to 32 µs after the 1.65 V threshold is crossed. Applications include basic comparison and low-side current sensing. Proper bypassing, grounding, high-speed PCB layout, and minimized input-output coupling are recommended.

The filing includes Exhibit 99.1, the press release on second quarter fiscal 2019 results, and Exhibit 99.2, CFO commentary by Colette M. Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPU architecture, including GA102, GeForce RTX 30-series, RTX A6000, and A40 features. GA10x SMs include 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, a second-generation RT Core, larger L1/shared memory, and doubled FP32 throughput compared with Turing. GA102 uses a 384-bit memory subsystem with twelve 32-bit controllers, 6144 KB L2 cache, and reorganized ROPs within GPCs, increasing full-chip ROP count to 112.

GA10x improves raster, shader, ray tracing, AI, and memory performance. Its second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection testing over Turing, support concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute, and add hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur through an Interpolate Triangle Position unit. Third-generation Tensor Cores support more data types, including TF32 and BF16, and structured sparsity that can double effective throughput for certain matrix operations. DLSS benefits from these Tensor Core improvements, including support for 8K gaming scenarios.

The architecture introduces GDDR6X memory, developed with Micron, using PAM4 signaling to reach data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth up to 936 GB/sec. Error Detection and Replay helps detect and retry GDDR6X transmission errors during memory overclocking. NVIDIA RTX IO, used with Microsoft DirectStorage, enables GPU-based loading and decompression of assets to reduce CPU workload and improve I/O performance.

The passage also covers display, video, and workstation/data center capabilities. Ampere supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, DSC, HDCP, 8K display output, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-generation NVENC encoding. The NVIDIA A40 targets data center visual computing with improved FP32, ray tracing, AI, PCIe Gen4, 48 GB memory, NVLink scalability, vGPU support, and EGX compatibility. The RTX A6000 provides workstation performance with 48 GB GDDR6, NVLink support, hardware-accelerated ray tracing, motion blur, AI denoising, and professional certifications. The passage concludes with NVIDIA’s standard legal disclaimers and trademark notices.

The United States reached the Davis Cup quarterfinals by defeating Serbia 3-0 in Nis, with Ryan Harrison and Steve Johnson winning the doubles after singles victories by Sam Querrey and John Isner. Kazakhstan also advanced 3-0, eliminating Switzerland in Astana. Belgium failed to clinch against Hungary, while defending champion France took a 2-1 lead over the Netherlands. Croatia, Spain, Germany and Italy also moved ahead 2-1 in their ties after doubles victories.

The passage discusses Justice Barrett’s defense of originalism and applies it to a Supreme Court case involving Louisiana’s creation of a second majority-Black congressional district to avoid a Voting Rights Act violation. The author argues that the constitutional doctrine limiting race-conscious districting, which began with a 1993 case and now invalidates districts where race “predominates” unless strict scrutiny is met, lacks support in the original public meaning of either the 14th or 15th Amendments.

The author contends that the 14th Amendment was not originally understood to regulate voting rights, as shown by the later adoption of the 15th and 19th Amendments and by the 14th Amendment’s own provisions on reduced representation. The passage also argues that the 15th Amendment addresses denial or abridgment of voting rights, not claims based solely on race-conscious district placement without vote dilution.

The passage acknowledges that precedent and stare decisis complicate an originalist approach, but argues that the race-predominance doctrine is unworkable and conflicts with Voting Rights Act vote-dilution jurisprudence. It concludes that an originalist should reconsider and reject that doctrine rather than weaken Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, while leaving Congress free to outlaw such districting by statute.

Euclid police will review a cellphone video showing a white officer repeatedly punching a 25-year-old Black man during a traffic-stop arrest. The officer is on paid leave, and the NAACP seeks a federal investigation.

The Investors Intelligence Sentiment Index, also called Advisor Sentiment, surveys over 100 independent market newsletters to classify advisors as bullish, bearish, or expecting a correction. Created by AW Cohen in 1963 and published by Chartcraft, it is widely used as a contrarian indicator, especially at extreme readings. Bullish readings above 55% suggest excessive optimism and may be negative for the market, while readings below 35% suggest excessive pessimism and may be positive. Weekly figures also track stocks above 10-week and 30-week moving averages, with the former used for short-to-intermediate turns and the latter for major turns. Readings above 70% may indicate an overbought market, and below 30% an oversold market. Investor sentiment refers to the overall mood of investors about the market. Unlike AAII, which surveys individual investors about the next six months, Investors Intelligence focuses on investment advisors and commentators. The index can be found through Chartcraft’s website by subscription.

Authorities said a male suspect wearing a homemade pipe bomb attempted to detonate it, but it malfunctioned or did not go off as planned. Multiple sources said some employees changed the replies back, only for them to be altered again. Similar partisan suggested language was also reportedly sent at the Department of Labor. Experts said the partisan language could raise Hatch Act concerns, and public policy professor Don Moynihan called it coercive and invasive. The court affirmed Ronald Haynes’s conviction and sentence, granted assigned counsel’s request to withdraw, found no nonfrivolous appeal issues, and held his pro se claims were barred by a valid appeal waiver.

The policy brief argues that the out-of-school children (OOSC) indicator is too narrow because it measures only formal school enrollment and overlooks informal, non-formal, community-based, religious, and technology-based education pathways. Using Afghanistan as a case study, it proposes replacing OOSC with an out-of-education children (OOEC) indicator that treats education as an activity within a broader ecosystem.

Afghanistan illustrates the limitations of OOSC. Formal schooling has long been shaped by conflict, ideology, geography, culture, poverty, and political instability. Although school enrollment rose significantly after 2002, millions of children remained excluded, and the Taliban’s 2021 ban on girls’ secondary education worsened the crisis. OOSC data also misses children learning through madrasas, community-based education, online platforms, radio, television, apprenticeships, or work-related learning.

The brief identifies several barriers to formal school attendance in Afghanistan: geographic isolation, insecurity, unequal resource distribution, nomadic lifestyles, child labor, disability, poverty, gender norms, lack of female teachers, distance to schools, and weak infrastructure. It also notes problems with enrollment data, including chronic absenteeism, ghost schools, and ghost students.

The proposed OOEC indicator would broaden measurement to include all learning pathways, support education system transformation, and encourage policymakers to view education as an interconnected ecosystem rather than a single institution. Implementing OOEC would require new data systems, revised credentialing, collaboration among education actors, and different approaches to resource allocation. The brief concludes that shifting to OOEC could help address systemic barriers, recognize diverse educational pathways, and support inclusive, equitable, high-quality education.

SFS is an AMD firmware feature for applying selected high-priority firmware fixes at runtime without rebooting, though patches are non-persistent and must be reapplied after reset. AMD distributes fixes as Seamless Firmware Servicing update packages, which are cryptographically signed; customers may optionally co-sign packages to enforce their own approval before deployment.

SFS tracks changes using SFS Patch Level (SFSPL), firmware component versions and Security Patch Levels (SPL), and System Patch Level (SYSPL) for run-once code effects. These values help ensure updates apply only to compatible firmware and operational states and can be queried by the host OS.

The AMD Security Processor (ASP) verifies AMD signatures before applying SFS packages and, if configured during early boot, verifies customer co-signatures. OEM/ODM firmware remains responsible for the firmware root of trust for update unless other protections apply. BIOS must explicitly enable SFS and optional co-signing using configuration tokens, both disabled by default.

SFS packages apply sequentially, in numerical order, at runtime. In multi-socket systems, the first socket’s ASP receives the patch and the package handles local and additional sockets as needed. Packages may modify registers or SRAM, replace firmware images, or update firmware components. SEV updates are automatically committed to prevent rollback, and reverting an SFS-updated SEV image requires reboot.

SFS commands require specific memory alignment and buffer layout. A deployment agent builds the command buffer, optional co-signing header and signature, and AMD update package, then sends the request through the ASP TEE mailbox interface. The ASP protects the memory region, verifies signatures, runs the patch, updates patch-level information, and returns status.

SFS supports commands to get firmware version information and to load, verify, and execute update packages. Packages are binary objects aligned to AGESA releases and named with family, AGESA release, and a monotonically increasing SFS number. Updates are designed to minimize performance impact and generally avoid OS quiescing or restart, though some cases such as SEV firmware updates may require affected virtual machines to stop and restart.

The passage outlines passport application rules for U.S. citizens and others owing allegiance to the United States. Applicants must swear allegiance, provide identifying physical details, and include witness certification. Additional documentation is required for persons born abroad to U.S. citizen fathers, naturalized citizens, women, children claiming citizenship through a naturalized parent, and residents of U.S. insular possessions. Passports expire after two years and require a new application. A passport may include an applicant’s wife, minor children, or eligible servant, but others need separate passports. Professional titles are excluded. Insular executive officers may refuse passports for improper purposes or noncompliance. Fees are listed for passports, applications, and oaths.
Lab tests suggest jostling air and methane microbubbles can create tiny lightning zaps that may ignite swamp will-o’-the-wisps.

Archaeologists in Mexico plan to excavate a sealed tunnel at Chichen Itza that may lead beneath the El Castillo pyramid to a hidden cenote, a water-filled cavern central to Mayan spirituality. Cenotes supplied fresh water in Yucatan and were viewed by the Maya as entrances to the underworld, where offerings, including human sacrifices, were made to maintain balance with deities.

Mexican scientist Rene Chavez Segura identified a hidden cenote under El Castillo two years ago. Divers later explored passageways from the nearby Ossuary pyramid but found them intentionally blocked. Guillermo de Anda, leading the Great Mayan Aquifer Project team, expects the excavation to take about three months.

El Castillo, a temple to Kukulcan, is aligned with cardinal directions and has 365 steps. De Anda says known cenotes to the north, east, south and west suggest the hidden cenote may represent a fifth direction, or “axis mundi.” He also says more research is needed to understand Mayan sacrifice, including findings that many victims in Chichen Itza’s Sacred Cenote were children in poor health.
New York court affirmed Enix Bussey’s conviction without opinion.

Patriarch Theophilos III of Jerusalem said his Church will appeal an Israeli court ruling approving the sale of church property in East Jerusalem to companies representing Israeli settlers. The Church argues the deal was illegal and politically motivated. The properties near Jaffa Gate would be leased to Ateret Cohanim for 99 years. Theophilos also warned of efforts to restrict Christian churches’ control over real estate and called for international intervention.

The European Union announced a €545 million ($636 million) investment package for renewable energy and electrification projects in Africa, including transmission lines, rural electrification, wind and hydro projects, and mini-grids. The effort is part of the EU’s Global Gateway initiative, which seeks to expand electricity access, support Africa’s clean energy transition, create green jobs, and rival China’s Belt and Road Initiative. China has invested heavily in global infrastructure and clean energy in Africa, including major energy contracts and solar panel exports. The EU and Western partners are also pursuing African infrastructure and resource projects, including the Lobito Corridor, as Africa’s minerals and energy choices become central to global climate and geopolitical goals.

A take a knee chart helps football coaches determine when the offense can safely kneel to run time off the clock while protecting a late-game lead. The offense uses victory formation, and the quarterback kneels after the snap, allowing the clock to continue if the opponent has no timeouts. The passage emphasizes that effective clock management is important for coaches, especially in end-of-game situations. It notes that high school timing rules often resemble college rules, with a 40-second play clock and no two-minute warning, and warns that incomplete passes can stop the clock and give opponents more time.

S&P Global Ratings downgraded Bridgeview, Illinois, four notches to BB-minus, citing debt pressures tied to $135 million in bonds issued for Toyota Park stadium. The junk rating is on watch for possible further downgrade. S&P noted weak liquidity, an underperforming stadium, and about $256 million in general obligation debt.

AP photos show pronouncer Brian Sietsema and contestants in the 3rd Round of the Scripps National Spelling Bee in Oxon Hill, Maryland, on May 30, 2018, with spellers from various locations correctly or incorrectly spelling words and reacting onstage.

The study examines kindergarten teachers’ views on distance education in preschool education after its mandatory use during COVID-19 school closures in Greece. It focuses on teachers in the Region of Epirus and investigates their prior familiarity with distance education, links between ICT literacy and experience, attitudes toward future use, and factors supporting or limiting integration.

The research used a quantitative approach with an anonymous online questionnaire completed by 82 kindergarten teachers between May and June 2021. Most participants were women, had bachelor’s degrees, and had 15 or more years of service. About half held basic ICT certification and 35.4% held advanced ICT certification.

Findings show that most teachers had little or no familiarity with distance education before the pandemic, and over 90% had not used it in kindergarten beforehand. Synchronous tools were used more than asynchronous ones, with Webex used by almost 89% of participants and email by about 60%. Teachers generally viewed distance education negatively for preschool education. They reported problems including limited school digital infrastructure, inadequate access to internet and devices, young children’s difficulty using technology independently, reduced psychomotor activities, weaker development of social skills, and the need for an adult supervisor at home.

Statistical analysis found that teachers with advanced ICT certification reported greater prior familiarity with distance education than those without certification. No statistically significant relationship was found between years of service and ICT familiarity.

The study concludes that kindergarten teachers in Epirus were largely unprepared for distance education and hesitant about its integration in kindergarten, except mainly as an emergency solution when face-to-face attendance is impossible. It highlights the need for teacher training, improved digital infrastructure, better technological access, interactive resources, and support for families if distance education is to be used in preschool settings.

The passage consists mostly of spam-like comments advertising hacking services, including database tampering, spying on communications, credit score changes, grade changes, and financial fraud, alongside one comment offering a marble-topped coffee table for sale.

ML²B is introduced as a multilingual benchmark for evaluating LLMs on generating complete machine learning pipelines from natural-language task descriptions. It extends 30 Kaggle competitions, including 24 public and 6 private tasks, into 13 languages, producing 390 evaluation instances across tabular, text, and image modalities and 12 domains. The benchmark includes structured metadata, human-reviewed task descriptions, standardized data cards, leakage controls, Docker-based execution, and a code grader that evaluates submitted code through reproducible function-based formats.

The benchmark addresses limitations of existing ML code generation benchmarks, which focus on English-only tasks, snippet-level code, or lack multilingual end-to-end ML workflows. ML²B also incorporates private competitions to reduce benchmark data leakage risks and uses modular submission formats to reduce preprocessing leakage.

Translations of task descriptions, domains, and data cards were produced with GPT-4o and manually reviewed by native speakers with technical backgrounds. Evaluation uses percentile ranks on Kaggle leaderboards to normalize performance across heterogeneous competition metrics.

Experiments evaluated five LLM configurations across AIDE and ML-Master frameworks. Results show consistent performance degradation on non-English tasks, with English generally producing stronger rankings. Low-resource languages such as Kazakh, Belarusian, and Romanian showed higher failure rates and worse percentiles. Performance varied by domain and metric: image categorization and text classification were more stable, while tabular classification and regression showed greater cross-lingual instability. Hybrid models sometimes improved results in harder non-English settings, but no model was universally best.

Common failure patterns included missing training execution, invalid data loading, inconsistent preprocessing, modified function signatures, global dependencies, deprecated or nonexistent APIs, and non-functional code. Static leakage analysis found potential leakage in 61 of 554 modular submissions, with 33 remaining as possible leakage cases after further inspection.

The 9 EMA trading strategy uses the 9-period exponential moving average to identify short-term market trends and generate buy or sell signals. A buy signal occurs when price moves above the 9 EMA, and a sell signal occurs when price moves below it. The strategy can be applied to markets such as stocks, forex, commodities, crypto, options, and futures, but the passage states it works better in trending assets like Bitcoin than in mean-reverting markets like stocks.

Backtesting showed a Bitcoin 9 EMA crossover system produced 284 trades with an average gain of 2.65% per trade, while the same approach performed poorly on the S&P 500/SPY. Adding a 200-day moving average trend filter reduced Bitcoin trades to 153 and increased average gain per trade to 4%, but only modestly improved the S&P 500/SPY result. The strategy can be combined with indicators such as RSI, Bollinger Bands, MACD, volume, candlestick patterns, and longer-term moving averages. Risk management methods include stop-loss orders, position sizing, diversification, defined exits, avoiding over-leverage, and avoiding emotional trading.

Mark Palmer forwarded to Enron colleagues a class action complaint filed in San Diego County Superior Court against Reliant, Southern Company, NRG, Dynegy, AES, Williams Energy, Duke Energy, and unnamed defendants, noting a reporter said Enron’s suit would look similar. The complaint, brought by Pamela R. Gordon on behalf of California electricity customers, alleges defendants manipulated California wholesale electricity markets beginning around May 22, 2000 by using confidential real-time generation and transmission data, withholding capacity, exporting or parking power, timing outages, and creating congestion to raise prices. It cites FERC, CPUC, CAISO, media reports, and market analyses alleging unjust and unreasonable prices, market power, and billions of dollars in overcharges during summer 2000. The claims include violations of California antitrust and unfair competition laws, consumer remedies law, and unconscionability, seeking class certification, damages, treble damages where applicable, restitution, disgorgement, injunctive relief, interest, fees, and costs.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2018. The company is incorporated in Delaware, headquartered in Seattle, and its common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under “AMZN.” As of June 30, 2018, voting stock held by non-affiliates had an aggregate market value of about $693.9 billion, and 491.2 million shares were outstanding as of January 23, 2019.

Amazon describes its goal as being “Earth’s most customer-centric company” and operates through three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services. It serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators, and provides services including advertising. Consumer offerings include online and physical stores, electronic devices, media content, and Amazon Prime. Seller programs allow third parties to sell through Amazon’s stores and use fulfillment services. AWS provides compute, storage, database, and other services. Kindle Direct Publishing and related programs serve authors, publishers, musicians, filmmakers, and developers.

Amazon reported significant competition across retail, media, search, e-commerce services, logistics, cloud services, and consumer electronics. Key competitive factors include selection, price, convenience, fulfillment speed and reliability, service quality, and customer willingness to change business practices. The company relies on intellectual property protections and noted seasonality, with 31% of 2018 annual revenue recognized in the fourth quarter. It employed about 647,500 full-time and part-time employees as of December 31, 2018.

Major risks identified include intense competition, rapid expansion, entry into new products and regions, operating-result fluctuations, international regulatory and business risks, fulfillment and data center challenges, seasonality, dependence on commercial relationships and acquisitions, foreign exchange exposure, reliance on senior and technical personnel, data breaches, system interruptions, inventory risk, intellectual property disputes, stock-price volatility, evolving regulation, tax liabilities, supplier risks, government contract risks, product liability, payments risks, and potential liability for seller misconduct.

GOLDWOOD PLY is a plywood manufacturer in Yamunanagar, Haryana, offering products such as block board, flush doors, and plywood across India. The company emphasizes quality manufacturing, timely delivery, mutual trust, transparency, sustainable development, people growth, and environmental safety.

The Missouri Student Union held its annual Veterans Day wreath laying ceremony Friday in Columbia, participating in the National Remembrance Day Roll Call by reading names of MU student veterans who were killed. Speakers included MU student and military leaders, and Robert Ross, director of the MU Veterans Center, which serves more than 400 student veterans. The Konektadong Pinoy Act, enacted on August 24, 2025, aims to reduce barriers to competition in the Philippine telecom market. The passage argues it could enable Virtual Network Operators and other entrants to challenge PLDT, potentially worsening profitability and growth pressures in a mature, highly penetrated industry. Despite PLDT’s valuation, the author prefers to stay on the sidelines due to entrant risk.

The passage argues that effective law enforcement often depends on less-publicized legislation whose importance is understood by interested opponents. It says the Government has begun using criminal law in trust and interstate commerce cases where success is reasonably possible, after initially relying on civil proceedings, and that fines and imprisonment have had deterrent effects. Quoting Judge Holt, it describes a railroad rebate case as clear, flagrant, deliberate, and harmful because discriminatory rates could disadvantage competitors. Holt emphasized the offenders’ education, the railroad’s public obligations, the secrecy and difficulty of proving rebate violations, and the rarity of such prosecutions. He concluded that penalties should match the gravity of the offense, with the main penalty imposed on the corporation rather than the traffic manager.

Joy Williams, BSN, RN, a Louisiana registered nurse with over seven years of experience, will be featured in Worldwide Leaders In Healthcare by the International Nurses Association. She began nursing in 2009, earned her BSN from Dillard University in 2016, and is a member of nursing associations.

Passports expire two years after issuance, and new passports require a new application. Existing passports may substitute for naturalization certificates if they contain sufficient naturalization information. One passport may include an applicant’s wife, minor children, or eligible servant under stated conditions; others require separate passports. Professional titles are excluded. A one-dollar fee must accompany citizen applications by currency or postal money order. The Department of State will not obtain foreign visés, provides application blanks, and requires communications to include a return address. The Secretary of State may refuse passports for unlawful or improper purposes or noncompliance. Under amended Section 4075, rules are prescribed for issuing passports in the United States and insular possessions. In insular possessions, applications are made to the chief executive; temporarily abroad applicants use U.S. diplomatic or consular officers. Passports may be issued only to persons owing allegiance to the United States, not merely those declaring intent to become citizens. Applications must be written affidavits with required authentication and personal, residence, travel, return, and citizenship-duty declarations.

The passage presents the Atlas of Human-AI Interaction, an open-source framework that uses large language models to synthesize empirical findings from human-AI interaction research. The system analyzes over 1,000 papers from major HCI-related sources, extracts findings as structured cause-relationship-effect triplets, and organizes them into a knowledge graph with 1,310 nodes and 3,908 edges.

The Atlas pipeline includes abstract collection, empirical finding extraction, triplet normalization, semantic clustering, and graph construction. It provides three interactive views: a 3D Graph View for exploring research themes and gaps, a Cause-Effect View for tracing relationships, and a Paper View for examining extracted findings from individual papers.

Analysis of the graph identified major research clusters involving human stakeholders, AI technologies, and conceptual objects. Common themes included AI in education, explanation and trust, design processes, decision support, and recursive human-AI effects. Network analysis also found integration opportunities around large language models, generative AI, trust, chatbots, and autonomous agents, suggesting the need for cross-domain frameworks.

A user study with 20 human-AI interaction researchers found that the Atlas supported landscape exploration, relationship discovery, and research gap identification. Participants valued the visual and spatial representations but noted limitations in paper detail, coverage, temporal analysis, and applicability to highly technical research.

The authors argue that AI-assisted literature synthesis can help researchers and practitioners navigate the rapidly expanding human-AI interaction field, support evidence-based design, and identify gaps and patterns that traditional reviews may miss. Future work includes continuous updates, richer relationship types, improved extraction methods, and more advanced connectivity analysis.

The 4-3 defense uses four defensive linemen, three linebackers, and four defensive backs, with smaller, athletic front-seven players. Its traditional under front includes two 5-technique defensive ends, a 1-technique nose guard, and a 3-technique defensive tackle, often considered the key position. The defense is strong against the run because it places seven defenders in the box and assigns each defender a specific gap. It also supports multiple coverages and can generate interior pass rush through the 3-technique tackle.

Its weaknesses include difficulty against modern spread offenses, which pull linebackers out of the box and create coverage challenges, especially for the Sam linebacker. Many teams respond by replacing the Sam with nickel personnel. Offenses attack the 4-3 by spreading the field or running outside zone schemes to outflank the edge.

Common blitzes include a Will edge blitz and a zone blitz with a defensive end dropping into coverage. Common coverages include Tampa 2, where the Mike linebacker drops into the deep middle, and Cover 3, with three deep defenders and linebackers in hook-to-curl zones.

The defense was brought to the NFL by Tom Landry, modernized by Jimmy Johnson, and popularized again by the early-2000s Tampa Bay Buccaneers through the Tampa 2. The Buccaneers, 2006 Chicago Bears, and Montini Catholic High School are cited as notable users of the 4-3 defense.

Small group differentiation is presented as a strategy to improve learning outcomes and inclusivity in elementary and higher education, especially for diverse learners, English language learners, students with disabilities, and students from varied cultural, linguistic, and socioeconomic backgrounds. The passage cites demographic shifts in U.S. public schools and rising language diversity as reasons educators must address varied learning needs through differentiated instruction rather than one-size-fits-all teaching.

The study used a systematic literature search of Ebsco, Embase, Google Scholar, Microsoft Academic Search, and ProQuest, reviewing works from 2000 to 2023 focused on differentiation, student diversity, and learning outcomes. Constructivism and Sociocultural Theory guide the research, emphasizing active knowledge construction, social interaction, collaboration, scaffolding, and the teacher’s role in supporting learning.

Differentiation involves adapting content, process, products, and learning environment based on student readiness, interests, learning profiles, linguistic needs, skills, and cultural backgrounds. In elementary education, teachers often guide less independent learners and adjust foundational instruction within stable classroom groups. In higher education, students are more independent, content is more specialized, and student groupings vary by courses and program structures.

Small group instruction can increase engagement, provide modeling and repeated practice, support struggling students, challenge higher achievers, and foster discussion, relationships, autonomy, and participation. Effective differentiation depends on ongoing assessment, appropriate instructional-level materials, verbal scaffolding, clear expectations, flexible grouping, student choice, and adjustment of instruction based on progress. Inclusive and culturally responsive environments, relevant materials, reflection exercises, and real-world connections are described as supporting engagement and learning.

Challenges include the time required for planning, preparation, grouping, lesson design, and assessment; large class sizes; limited teacher support; and the need to understand students’ backgrounds, strengths, interests, and struggles. Student disability data under IDEA is discussed as another dimension of classroom diversity affecting instructional planning. Administrative support is described as important for effective implementation.

The passage notes limitations, including limited data on differentiated and small group pedagogy across settings, insufficient comparative analysis, and a lack of studies connecting small group instruction with learning outcomes, benchmarks, or test scores. It concludes that differentiation in elementary and higher education shares the goal of accommodating diverse student needs but differs in implementation. Future research should include longitudinal studies from elementary through higher education and studies comparing outcomes by learning style.

Google launched Gemini Enterprise, an AI platform for business customers that provides access to Gemini Ultra models and tools for data governance, security, compliance, explainability, and access controls. Built on Google Cloud, it lets firms customise models with proprietary data and integrates with Google Workspace and third-party software. Google aims to compete in enterprise AI by emphasizing transparency, accountability, and regulated-sector needs, though it must prove reliability and returns for customers.

Ray Dalio’s All Weather Portfolio, developed by Bridgewater Associates, is a diversified defensive strategy designed to perform across inflation, deflation, and stagflation. It uses stocks, bonds, and commodities to reduce drawdowns through diversification and low correlation rather than maximize returns. The article says the portfolio has historically had lower returns than stocks but smoother performance and smaller drawdowns, including during 2008/09, Covid-19 in 2020, and 2022. Backtests from 2007 show modest CAGR, lower volatility, and better downside protection than the S&P 500, though it underperforms in strong equity bull markets. The portfolio may suit risk-averse investors, retirees, or FIRE investors, with suggested rebalancing once or twice per year, preferably in a tax-deferred account. Leverage or changed allocations can raise returns but increase drawdowns. Future performance is not guaranteed.

Mother appealed a dissolution judgment awarding $31 per month in child support for each of two children and abating support during father’s visitation. The children spend about half their time with father under a visitation arrangement resembling joint custody. Father earned $16,930 in 1985, with income likely to increase; mother’s income figure was disputed because it included a $6,000 settlement. The court agreed father’s visitation expenses should factor into support but found the trial court’s amount insufficient. Because standard formulas were difficult to apply, the judgment was modified to require father to pay $65 per month for each child, effective from the decision date, and otherwise affirmed.

Please, Continue (Hamlet), playing at Melbourne Festival, stages Hamlet’s trial for Polonius’s murder in a real courtroom with real judges, lawyers and legal teams, while actors play Hamlet, Ophelia and Gertrude. Created by Yan Duyvendak and Roger Bernat, the participatory work has been performed in 12 countries since its 2011 Swiss premiere, adapting to each jurisdiction’s legal system and using an audience-selected jury of 12.

The project grew from the creators’ interest in trials, including Guantanamo transcripts, and aims to show how the justice system works by placing a fictional case in a real legal setting. It also draws on a real case involving a young man accused of killing his girlfriend’s father. Duyvendak says the show reveals the complexity of justice, as audience members often shift their views during the trial, especially after hearing closing arguments. Jury participants have reported that the experience changed their views on sentencing.
Order affirmed; Thomas, J., dissented because the ex parte order deprived plaintiff of a statutory reply right.

This study systematically reviews and bibliometrically analyzes research on the metaverse in education using Scopus data from January 2015 to July 2024. After applying PRISMA procedures and inclusion criteria, 270 English-language journal articles were analyzed with VOSviewer.

The study found no publications on the metaverse in education before 2020. Publications increased from four articles in both 2020 and 2021 to 36 in 2022, peaked at 131 in 2023, and reached 91 by July 2024. South Korea, China, and the United States produced the most publications, while South Korea, the United Kingdom, and China received the most citations.

The most influential journals included IEEE Transactions on Learning Technologies, which had the highest number of articles, and Sustainability (Switzerland), which had the highest citation count. The most cited article was Dwivedi et al.’s 2022 article, “Metaverse beyond the hype,” with 890 citations.

Keyword co-occurrence analysis identified “metaverse,” “virtual reality,” “education,” “augmented reality,” and “artificial intelligence” as the most frequent terms. Prominent research topics included the use of the metaverse to create virtual educational environments and studies of students’ and teachers’ perceptions and attitudes toward metaverse-based education. The review also identified extended reality, blockchain, sustainability, and gamification as possible areas for future exploration.

The study concludes that research on the metaverse in education has grown rapidly since 2020, especially from 2022 onward. It identifies gaps including the need for longitudinal studies on long-term educational outcomes and comparative studies across different cultural and educational systems.

Michigan State Police, Emergency Management and Homeland Security are encouraging Michigan residents, businesses and organizations to join a voluntary statewide tornado drill at 1 p.m. Wednesday during Severe Weather Awareness Week. Officials urge residents to identify shelter areas, practice drills, monitor weather reports, understand tornado watches and warnings, recognize warning signs, and prepare 72-hour emergency kits. Nearly all state facilities will participate. If severe weather occurs April 19, the drill will move to 1 p.m. Thursday.

The passage outlines basketball transition defense principles, emphasizing that strong transition defense begins with good offense: ball security, good shot selection, offensive rebounding, and defensive balance. Players should sprint back, maintain vision of the ball, seek the level of the ball, avoid running beside opponents, and force extra passes to allow defenders to recover.

It stresses preparation for outnumbered situations, including breakaways, 2-on-1, and 3-on-2 scenarios, with goals of delaying the ball, preventing layups, pressuring the ball handler, taking charges, rebounding, and counterattacking. Defensive balance requires assigned rebounding and safety roles, with bigs sprinting back to protect the basket and support the on-ball defender.

After missed shots, missed free throws, turnovers, and blocked shots, defenders should jam the rebounder, deny or disrupt outlet passes—especially to the primary ball handler—slow penetration, match up, and protect the basket. Made field goals and free throws provide opportunities to set full- or half-court pressure.

Game strategies include scouting opponents, disrupting outlet passes, demanding full sprint recovery, and substituting players who fail to hustle back. Teaching transition defense should focus on awareness, decision-making, offensive rebounding, defensive balance, sprinting back, defending outnumbered situations, and making stops after turnovers, using the Whole-Part-Whole method and transition breakdown drills.

The Navy’s free Pier Pressure mobile app supports responsible drinking during Alcohol Awareness Month and year-round. Part of the Keep What You’ve Earned campaign, it uses interactive tools including a calorie counter and Uber/Lyft integration. The app has been played over 30,000 times and is available on iTunes and Google Play.

The Dow Jones fell 424.56 points Tuesday amid concerns over rising interest rates and Caterpillar’s outlook. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq also declined. Caterpillar dropped after warning its first quarter may be the year’s peak, while 3M and Alphabet fell. The 10-year Treasury yield rose above 3 percent, raising borrowing-cost concerns.

Florence O. Summers sued Clennon C. Hemsell and Columbian Fuel Corporation for the death of her husband, J. W. Summers, in an automobile collision, alleging Hemsell’s negligence and corporate liability because he was acting as an employee. A jury awarded appellees $30,890.

The appellate court held that several jury instructions were erroneous. The trial court improperly assumed life expectancies based on mortality tables, including 34½ years for J. W. Summers and approximately twenty years for his mother, instead of leaving those fact questions to the jury. It also erred by instructing the jury to consider support in the manner Mrs. Summers expected, loss of love and fatherly advice, and possible higher education expenses without proper basis. The court further stated that the jury should have been instructed not to consider grief or sorrow as damages. It rejected appellants’ complaints about refusal to submit certain sole proximate cause and new independent cause issues. The court also found improper appellees’ counsel’s argument criticizing appellants for introducing admissible divorce records.

The judgment was reversed and the cause remanded.

The passage defines SEV-ES/SEV-SNP Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) handling for non-automatic exits (NAEs), VMGEXIT processing, and related guest-hypervisor protocols. Guests and hypervisors must mark valid GHCB fields in VALID_BITMAP, reset it before each event, and minimally use SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2. VMGEXIT invocations should be protected by disabling interrupts and preemption, and separate or saved GHCB state is recommended for NMI contexts. Hypervisors report VMGEXIT errors through SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2.

The text describes handling for IOIO, MSR, VMMCALL, MMIO, page state changes, SNP guest requests, extended guest requests, TIO guest requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell pages, #HV IPI, #HV timers, APIC ID lists, VMPL switching, Secure AVIC backing pages, termination requests, and unsupported exits. Several events require shared buffers or shared pages, validation of guest-provided pages, and specific register or GHCB field usage. Page state change requests support private/shared transitions and SNP RMP updates, with resumable progress tracking and reason codes. SNP guest request events allow guests to communicate with SEV-SNP firmware through the hypervisor; extended variants can return certificate data, while TIO variants can return measurements, certificates, and attestation reports.

The passage also covers guest identification of SEV-ES support through CPUID, SMP boot challenges under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, AP reset hold behavior, AP jump table requirements, and SNP AP creation using VMSA pages. vCPU hotplug is unsupported under traditional SEV-ES constraints but can be supported through SNP AP creation. NMI handling requires the hypervisor to use the guest’s “NMI Complete” message before injecting another NMI. Debug register virtualization is supported when DebugVirtualization is enabled; otherwise DR7 access must be intercepted and emulated. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

For SNP Restricted Injection, the passage defines #HV doorbell page behavior. The doorbell page contains PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields used to deliver interrupts and non-maskable events while preserving APIC-like semantics. It specifies host and guest responsibilities for mapping the page, presenting vectors, acknowledging interrupts, handling EOI optimization, managing non-maskable events, and avoiding missed interrupts around HLT.

A security researcher found a disabled-by-default keylogger in Synaptics touchpad drivers on hundreds of HP notebooks, tablets and other devices. HP confirmed the issue, said neither HP nor Synaptics accessed customer data, and released patches for more than 450 affected products. Researcher Michael Myng said the keylogger was debug trace code and could be enabled through a registry change by someone with administrative privileges. HP urged affected users to install updates. The issue follows a similar May discovery involving keylogging code in Conexant audio drivers on HP laptops, also attributed to debugging code left in shipped software.

Police in Xinjiang’s Pishan County shot dead three knife-wielding assailants who killed five people and injured 10. Authorities called the attackers “thugs,” said order was restored, and launched an investigation. The passage also cites previous violent incidents in Xinjiang-linked cases and Beijing’s accusations against Uighur separatist groups.

Johnny Juzang is making a case for a Timberwolves roster spot on a non-guaranteed contract after Minnesota lost Nickeil Alexander-Walker. He scored 20 points in 14 minutes in a preseason game and has made 9 of 15 three-pointers this preseason. The article notes his shooting could fit Minnesota’s bench needs.

Philadelphia extended its unbeaten run to four matches and remained in the Eastern Conference playoff race, led by Borek Dockal’s goal, two assists, and strong playmaking against Chicago. Ilsinho also scored after beating Bastian Schweinsteiger with a quick move. Johns Hopkins and Mayo Clinic researchers published a JAMA Internal Medicine implementation guide urging hospitals to eliminate CK-MB blood testing for suspected heart attacks, citing American College of Cardiology guidance and five peer-reviewed studies showing it adds no diagnostic value and can be safely discontinued. Cardiac troponin is identified as the preferred biomarker because of its sensitivity and prognostic value. Despite guidelines, a 2013 survey found 77% of nearly 2,000 U.S. labs still used CK-MB. Researchers note financial implications, estimating heart attack blood tests add $416 million annually to care costs. The guide recommends hospitalwide education, removing CK-MB from standard order sets, adding electronic ordering alerts, and measuring test use and patient outcomes. It is the first in a planned HVPAA series targeting low-value practices.

Indian-origin surgeon Dr Sachiendra Amaragiri was struck off the UK medical register after a tribunal found he abused his position by sending a love letter to a female patient. The patient contacted police, saying she was distressed. Amaragiri apologized and plans to appeal.

The passage investigates how well observational molecular-line diagnostics recover infall velocities in collapsing prestellar cores. The authors combine smoothed-particle hydrodynamic simulations of a collapsing 5 solar-mass prestellar core with time-dependent chemistry and radiative transfer to generate synthetic line observations. They model molecular abundances and line emission for species including C18O, N2H+, HCO+, H13CO+, CS, and C34S, then apply the Myers et al. (1996) method to estimate infall velocities from self-absorbed line profiles.

The simulations show that density and velocity profiles evolve significantly between 0.81 and 0.87 Myr, while molecular abundance profiles remain similar. Synthetic line profiles vary more strongly with aperture size than with timestep. Calculated infall velocities from line-pair tracers are consistently below the true mass-weighted velocities of the simulation. CS-based estimates are closest but reach only about half the true value, while HCO+ can underestimate it by an order of magnitude. The discrepancy arises from chemical and radiative transfer effects and from applying constant-velocity slab models to realistic radial velocity profiles.

The authors conclude that commonly used line-profile techniques systematically underestimate prestellar core infall velocities and therefore mass accretion rates, potentially by an order of magnitude. They suggest optically thin non-thermal velocity dispersions may better trace infall speed in isolated collapsing cores, though this may not apply in more complex turbulent environments.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K reporting that, effective March 11, 2021, Jerome Guillen transitioned from President, Automotive to President, Tesla Heavy Trucking. He will lead all aspects of the Tesla Semi program, including related charging and servicing networks.

Sony launched a U.S. instant rebate and trade-in offer through September 30, 2017, with up to $300 off select cameras, up to $500 extra for trading in an interchangeable lens camera, up to $200 off A7 cameras, and up to $100 off select full-frame lenses and accessories, including free U.S. shipping.

Compass Minerals International is rated “Buy” due to attractive valuation and operational improvement. Revenue and volumes are rising in salt and plant nutrition, while cost cuts are improving cash flow and EBITDA. The company has higher net debt and leverage than peers but trades at lower multiples, suggesting upside potential. Management expects further top-line growth in 2025, though leverage risk prevents a “Strong Buy” rating.

The passage describes the CANSLIM method, developed by William O’Neill of Investor’s Business Daily, as a stock-selection approach based on seven criteria intended to identify strong-performing stocks. The author says backtests show CANSLIM has beaten the S&P 500 since 2003, but with higher volatility and larger drawdowns, possibly due to its small-cap exposure. The IBD 50 list ranks stocks using CANSLIM criteria and is available to subscribers. The method is mainly for long-term investing, is difficult to backtest, and involves risks including volatility, capital loss, and underperformance in recent years.

The speaker says the team needed and earned a win, with Rucchin scoring twice, Jiggy playing well, and the group controlling much of the game. He says preparation and maintaining their approach are key, and he leads by example rather than speaking much. He views the first two games in New Jersey as uncharacteristic, says Anaheim regained its play at home, and believes they must improve on the road and tighten defensively. He says being close to the Stanley Cup means a lot but the team remains focused on preparing for the next game. He also discusses a past hit, saying he felt fine after being checked by doctors, and describes the series as highly competitive with growing animosity.

Peter Crouch made a widely shared joke on Twitter after the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge appeared with their third child outside St Mary’s Hospital. His wife Abbey Clancy responded with a blunt reply that drew laughter online. Crystal Palace also joked on Twitter after AFP reported Kate had given birth to a son, pretending “palace” was the baby’s name.

The passage discusses the Golden State Warriors’ habit of falling behind before rallying, especially in the second half. Mark Jackson says coach Steve Kerr would likely be concerned about relying on urgency after halftime, though the team has shown an ability to adjust and recover. The Warriors led the NBA in third-quarter scoring and overcame large deficits against the Rockets in Games 6 and 7, but failed to do so in Games 2, 4 and 5. The passage compares their comeback style to examples from horse racing, Olympic running and the Oakland A’s. Jeff Van Gundy and Jackson both warn that repeatedly digging early holes can eventually be costly.

Investors are buying closed-end equity mutual fund schemes on stock exchanges because existing holders are selling them at discounts to NAV due to poor liquidity. Since these schemes can be redeemed at NAV only at maturity, buyers may gain from the discount plus any upside. Examples include Reliance Close Ended Mutual Fund Series A Growth trading about 10% below NAV, HDFC Equity Opportunities Fund and Series 2 at 6% discounts, and Reliance Close End Equity Fund Series II Dividend at 9%. Discounts depend on time to maturity and tax considerations, with shorter remaining periods potentially attracting higher discounts. Experts say opportunities are hard to find due to low trading activity and suggest focusing on schemes with assets above Rs 250 crore.

Airbus is developing Project Vahana, an autonomous flying taxi intended to help commuters avoid congested roads. The company says it is using clean technology and expects lower infrastructure costs compared with roads and bridges. Airbus hopes to offer short-haul trips by 2021, with a prototype targeted for 2017. Other companies are also pursuing flying vehicles, including Uber with VTOL aircraft, Urban Aeronautics with the Cormorant passenger drone, and AeroMobil with a land-and-air vehicle. Investors such as Skype’s co-founder and Google co-founder Larry Page have also backed flying car efforts.

A letter attributed to fired assistant U.S. attorney Michael Ben’Ary said his termination during a terrorism prosecution was apparently prompted by a false social media post. The letter criticized DOJ leadership, saying it prioritized punishing President Trump’s perceived enemies over national security and public safety.

The passage describes a light emitting diode device and manufacturing method aimed at improving connection reliability between micro light emitting diodes and electrodes. The device includes a thin film transistor substrate, first and second diode electrodes, a first passivation pattern, micro light emitting diodes, and first and second bridge patterns electrically connecting the electrodes to the diodes. Each micro light emitting diode may include a cylindrical inorganic light emitting material surrounded by a protective layer, with exposed semiconductor sidewalls connected to bridge patterns. The first passivation pattern sidewalls and diode sidewalls form the same plane to reduce steps and minimize bridge pattern breakage. The manufacturing method forms passivation patterns and micro light emitting diodes using a single mask process with two etching steps, including anisotropic first etching and more isotropic second etching, followed by formation of bridge and passivation layers.
