Aspen is replacing its Fourth of July fireworks with a 15-minute drone show due to wildfire risk in drought-hit Colorado, where strict fire restrictions are in place. Officials say 50 drones will light the sky in patriotic colours and music at Wagner Park, organised by the Aspen Chamber Resort Association.

ESPN’s MLB wild-card coverage highlights three winner-take-all Game 3s, the second time baseball has hosted three such playoff games in one day. The Dodgers advanced to the NLDS, with Yamamoto helping clinch and Ohtani set to start Game 1. Detroit’s struggles with runners in scoring position are emphasized after stranding 15 in Game 2. Padres-Cubs is framed as a likely bullpen battle between Yu Darvish and Jameson Taillon. Red Sox-Yankees may hinge on Boston getting length from its pitchers after heavy bullpen use in Game 2.

Jio announced Galaxy Club offers for Samsung Galaxy J2 2018 and Galaxy J7 Duo buyers, including Rs 2,750 instant cashback as 55 vouchers of Rs 50 each. Galaxy J2 2018 buyers using Jio get 100GB additional data on Rs 198 and Rs 299 plans, while Galaxy J7 Duo buyers get double data on those plans. The offers are valid until September 30 and apply to online and offline purchases.

The passage states that U.S. national debt surpassed $21 trillion, growing by $73 billion in one day, $215 billion in February, and more than $1 trillion in six months. It argues that debt growth is outpacing GDP growth, noting the debt rose 6% last year compared with 4.4% nominal GDP growth, and increased 123% over a decade while the economy grew 36%. The author rejects claims that the debt does not matter because it is owed domestically, warning that defaulting on obligations to institutions such as Social Security, banks, or the Federal Reserve would be catastrophic. The passage concludes by describing public responses to the debt as ignoring it, dismissing it, or preparing for possible consequences.

The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau finalized rules requiring payday and auto title lenders to assess whether borrowers can repay loans within 30 days and limiting repeated account debits without reauthorization. Supporters say the rules address loan rollovers, high fees, overdrafts, and debt cycles; a CFPB study found more than 80 percent of payday loans are rolled over or followed by another loan within two weeks. Industry representatives say the rules could cut off credit access for 30 million to 40 million customers and push borrowers toward unregulated lenders. The CFPB estimates loan volume could fall by half and many payday stores could close. The rules would take effect in 2019 but face opposition from Republicans and could be rolled back by Congress. A Pew poll found 70 percent of surveyed adults support more regulation of payday lenders.

Seattle Children’s offers a writing program through its Pediatric Advanced Care Team to help parents express emotions through journaling. Meagan Holt uses it to cope with her daughter Madeline’s likely fatal Zellweger Syndrome, saying writing provides an outlet for feelings she once bottled up. Staff say the program can bring empowerment, calm, relief and acceptance, and it relies on donations.

This study examined pretreatment sarcoma biopsies to identify biomarkers associated with response to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapy. RNA sequencing from 67 patients across three ICI trials identified two tumor immune states: immune-hot and immune-cold. Immune-hot tumors had higher immune infiltrates, higher expression of checkpoint-related genes including CD274/PD-L1 and CTLA4, higher response rates to ICI therapy, and longer progression-free survival than immune-cold tumors.

The analysis found that expression of specific transposable elements (TEs) and the chromatin-interacting transcription factor IKZF1 predicted immune type. Higher TE score and IKZF1 expression were associated with immune-hot tumors, immune and inflammatory pathway activation, antigen-processing machinery, interferon signaling, CD8+ T cell effector pathways, higher PD-L1 expression, improved progression-free survival, and higher overall response rates for IKZF1-high tumors. Conditional independence analysis suggested that IKZF1 may regulate TE expression, which may influence immune type, though functional studies are needed.

Findings were validated in 190 TCGA sarcoma samples, where immune-hot tumors, high TE score, and high IKZF1 expression were associated with improved overall survival and immune pathway activation. The authors propose IKZF1 expression and TE score as potential predictive biomarkers for ICI outcomes in sarcoma and suggest that pharmacologic derepression of TEs through epigenetic targeting could be explored to enhance immune responsiveness. Limitations include the small original cohort, sarcoma subtype heterogeneity, different ICI regimens, and differences between the treatment and validation cohorts.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on October 27, 2022, reporting its third quarter 2022 financial results. The filing incorporates a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and information on non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Happy Home Furnishers is closing its Neath store after 33 years, citing anti-social behaviour, lack of free parking and rising business rates. Managing director Mike Semmens said street works disrupted businesses, a bench installed near the store attracted drinkers, and staff dealt with fights, mess, broken bottles and needles. Some local traders said anti-social behaviour is worse in summer, while others said it has limited impact on them.

Neath Council said town centre improvements were for overall benefit, benches were installed for mobility reasons and later removed, and it is working with police and partners to tackle anti-social behaviour. On parking, Semmens argued more short-stay free spaces are needed, while the council pointed to a 600-space multi-storey car park and some free parking after 3pm. Semmens said business rates have risen substantially, though Neath is no worse than other towns. The Welsh Government said relief schemes support small businesses. The company will continue trading elsewhere and may seek another Neath site.

The Ravens traded pass rusher Odafe Oweh and a 2026 fifth-round pick to the Chargers for safety Alohi Gilman, sources told ESPN. Oweh has no sacks through five games after a 10-sack season and reduced playing time, while Baltimore frees about $8 million in cap space. The 1-4 Ravens are struggling defensively, allowing an NFL-worst 35.4 points per game and ranking 31st in pass defense. Baltimore also added safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson to its practice squad. Gilman helps address safety depth, while the Chargers add an edge rusher amid injuries and a greater need at that position.

This study explores physics teachers’ attitudes and scepticism toward physics education research, especially its practical value for teaching. It addresses a research gap linked to the theory-practice divide and evidence-based teaching. Using a mixed-methods design, the authors first interviewed 13 German physics teachers, then surveyed 174 physics teachers from Germany and Austria.

Interview results identified seven attitudes, including both positive views, such as seeing physics education research as relevant to teaching, and sceptical views, such as prioritizing personal teaching experience, doubting classroom applicability, and criticizing cooperation between research and school practice. Survey analysis identified four factors of scepticism: relevance for the individual teacher, feasibility for classroom practice, relevance for teaching in general, and cooperation between research and schools.

Latent profile analysis found four teacher profiles: “The Sceptical Ones” (14%), who questioned the value and applicability of research; “The Uncertain Ones” (27%), who showed mostly neutral attitudes; “The Undersupplied Ones” (41%), who valued research but saw it as insufficiently applicable and poorly connected to practice; and “The Research Advocates” (18%), who held the least sceptical views. Multinomial logistic regression showed that more frequent reading of instructional journals was associated with membership in less sceptical profiles, while teaching experience, teacher education, school type, and doctoral degree were not significant predictors.

The study concludes that physics teachers are not generally sceptical of physics education research, but notable scepticism exists, especially regarding cooperation between research and practice. The authors suggest stronger integration of research into teacher education, better communication of findings, and closer collaboration between researchers and teachers. Limitations include small and convenience samples, possible participation bias, and constraints of the statistical methods.

African countries were urged to use modern technology to address tax non-compliance at the 18th VADA Forum in Lilongwe. Malawi’s Treasury Secretary Ben Botolo highlighted electronic fiscal devices and cashless transactions as ways to improve VAT collection. VADA Chairperson Henry Saka called for stronger regulatory strategies and African solutions to tax evasion. The forum gathers VAT officials from 10 member countries to improve domestic revenue mobilization.

The President clarifies that his earlier message to the Senate did not deny Congress’s constitutional authority to regulate the custody, safekeeping, and disposition of public money and property. He states that the Executive claims no control over such property except as granted by law, and requests that this clarification be entered with the prior message in the Senate journal.

The lecture reviews propagators in free scalar field theory, including heuristic interpretations as transition amplitudes and correlation functions. The Feynman propagator is described as a time-ordered correlation function, while retarded, advanced, and Feynman Green functions differ by how integration contours avoid poles at \(\omega=\pm\omega_k\). These contour choices can be equivalently implemented using infinitesimal \(i\epsilon\) prescriptions that shift pole locations.

Free theory correlation functions are discussed: vacuum \(n\)-point functions factorize into sums of products of two-point functions because creation and annihilation operators must pair. Composite operators such as \(\phi^2\), \(\phi^3\), Hamiltonian density, and stress tensor can be singular when fields are multiplied at the same point, illustrating divergences and the need for renormalization.

The lecture then introduces interactions by adding nonlinear terms such as \(\lambda \phi^4\) to the free scalar Lagrangian. The resulting equation of motion is nonlinear and not exactly solvable, so perturbation theory in small \(\lambda\) is proposed. Scattering is presented as the main experimental way to probe interactions. The S-matrix is defined as the transition amplitude between free initial states at \(t=-\infty\) and free final states at \(t=+\infty\). For weak interactions, \(S=1+iT\), with the identity corresponding to no interaction. Momentum conservation allows extracting a delta function from \(T\), leaving the scattering amplitude \(M_{\alpha\beta}\). The S-matrix is unitary, and symmetries of the Hamiltonian constrain its matrix elements. The LSZ theorem is cited as relating scattering amplitudes to time-ordered correlation functions in the interacting vacuum. The lecture ends by preparing to introduce the path integral approach.

The speaker emphasizes that Detroit must stay focused at home despite well-wishers and distractions, noting the team has played well on the road and must be prepared for a complete game. They discuss the importance of avoiding penalties, not retaliating, and handling momentum swings. Mike is described as confident, resilient, and experienced in goal. The speaker says home ice is not automatic, past history is not a focus, and previous playoff experiences have helped the team. They also review defensive pairings, player roles, roster moves, ice conditions, and preparation routines before the next game.

The application describes sidelink positioning methods, apparatuses, processors, storage media, and communication systems for improving terminal device positioning accuracy. Existing positioning technologies rely on measurements between terminal devices and network devices, are controlled by a core network, and may have increasing errors as the distance from the network device grows.

The proposed methods use sidelink positioning reference signals between terminal devices. A network device sends sidelink positioning configurations to a first terminal device and a second terminal device. The first terminal device may send a first sidelink positioning reference signal to the second terminal device, and the second terminal device measures it to obtain a first measurement value. The second terminal device may also send a second sidelink positioning reference signal to the first terminal device, and the first terminal device measures it to obtain a second measurement value. Measurement values may include Rx−Tx time differences and angle-of-arrival measurements.

The position of the first terminal device is determined based on the first measurement value, optionally the second measurement value, and the position of the second terminal device. This determination may be performed by the first terminal device or by the network device. Measurement values may be reported over Uu or PC5 interfaces. The sidelink positioning configurations may include time-frequency resources, sequence information, terminal information, and measurement reporting configurations.

The methods may reduce positioning latency because measurement values do not need to be transmitted through a core network, and they may improve accuracy by using another terminal device as a reference object. The solution also supports cases where the first terminal device does not support sidelink reference signal measurement, allowing the second terminal device to perform measurement instead. The application further describes related apparatus structures, processors, computer program products, computer-readable storage media, and a communication system including network and terminal devices.
The passage lists views of two embodiments of an analytical instrument design and states that broken-line features are not part of the claimed design.

Retired civil litigator Marcel Strigberger describes decluttering his home by discarding law school books he bought more than 50 years ago. He reflects humorously on remembered cases and concepts from contract, property and other legal texts, questioning their relevance after decades of practice. He recycles most of the books, regrets possibly tossing one valuable volume, and keeps one thick book to use as a reading stand.

A 2014 Wall Street Journal article reported that Hertz Global Holdings would restate and correct three years of results due to accounting problems, causing its stock to fall about 9%. Analyst Abby Devins examined whether the issues related to Hertz’s large rental fleet and future vehicle acquisitions.

In 2013, the U.S. car rental industry generated about $36 billion in revenue and was dominated by Enterprise, Avis Budget, and Hertz, which together held 71% market share. Hertz operated nearly 12,000 locations in 145 countries, employed over 30,000 people, and managed a fleet of more than 700,000 cars. After going public in 2006, Hertz expanded from a mainly on-airport business brand into multiple segments, including Dollar Thrifty, Firefly, China Auto Rental, Donlen fleet leasing, and equipment rental.

Hertz reported record revenue and EBITDA in 2013, with total revenue rising from $8.3 billion in 2011 to $10.8 billion in 2013 and net income attributable to Hertz increasing from $164.2 million to $346.2 million. Depreciation was significant, averaging about 25% of expenses, and revenue earning equipment represented over half of total assets in 2012 and 2013.

Hertz depreciated revenue earning equipment on a straight-line basis using estimated holding periods and residual values, reviewed quarterly. Rental cars included program cars, with manufacturer repurchase or depreciation guarantees, and non-program cars, which carried residual price risk. U.S. program car purchases fell from 61% of total purchases in 2006 to 18% in 2013, while international program purchases remained higher. Devins collected Hertz and Avis data on revenue earning equipment, depreciation, gains or losses on sales, and income before taxes to assess depreciation’s possible role in Hertz’s accounting issues.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated October 25, 2018, announcing its third quarter 2018 financial results. The filing incorporates a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and information on non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. It was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

AI may augment human cognition, learning, creativity, and skill development, but its effects depend on design, deployment, and use. Key risks include over-reliance on AI, which may weaken learning and critical thinking, and limited internalization of skills, which may reduce independent knowledge retention. Mitigations include avoiding passive use, delegating only non-essential tasks, encouraging critical problem-solving, and designing AI as a thought partner rather than a replacement.

AI may also reshape labor and collaboration. LLMs can reduce knowledge scarcity, blur job boundaries, and enable complex tasks without specialized skills, potentially challenging traditional social roles and the middle class. The passage identifies possible growth of the gig economy, supported by AI-enabled algorithmic management, with benefits such as flexibility and efficiency but risks including weak labor protections and instability. It also describes more dynamic global collaboration, including inter-organizational and individual-to-organization partnerships. Recommended responses include equitable AI access, new industries, employment opportunities, social safety nets, institutional reforms, updated welfare systems, and coordinated efforts among academia, industry, and government.

In social science research, AI and LLMs may improve access to data, automate analysis, and support hypothesis generation. LLMs can synthesize research data, simulate demographic preferences and behaviors, and assist in tasks such as stance detection, sentiment analysis, and response coding. However, concerns include bias, underrepresentation of minority views, oversimplified stereotypes, misinformation, and uncertainty about whether LLM-generated responses accurately reflect real participants. Human-AI collaboration is presented as necessary to balance automation with oversight, AI search with human intuition, and innovation with rigor.

AI regulation must evolve to address misinformation, deepfakes, bias, discrimination, safety, transparency, accountability, and the difficulty of regulating fast-changing complex models. Existing efforts by governments and technology companies aim to mitigate risks, but gaps remain between industry and policymakers and among countries’ regulatory approaches. The passage calls for top-down partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers, forward-looking regulation, and bottom-up reporting from developers, researchers, users, and communities. Effective governance should include transparent issue handling, timely updates to regulations and guidelines, and monitoring of community-specific regulatory needs.

Rivers State Governor Nyesom Wike urged the United States to establish a visa office in Port Harcourt for the South-South and South-East. During a visit by US Ambassador William Symington, Wike accused the NDDC of serving as a fundraising body for politicians, alleging corruption, election funding, and failure to support agreed projects, including the Mother and Child Hospital. He also called for the cleanup of Ogoni land and sought US partnerships in agriculture, oil and gas, industrialization, and investment.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated March 19, 2020, reporting publication of a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1 under Item 7.01 Regulation FD Disclosure. The information is furnished, not deemed filed, unless specifically incorporated by reference. The report lists Tesla common stock trading as TSLA on Nasdaq and was signed by CFO Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

Unused TLV32xx inputs should not be tied together; they must be connected within the specified input voltage range with at least 50 mV differential voltage. The family has 1.8 mV internal hysteresis, with trip behavior determined by threshold voltage, input offset voltage, and hysteresis. TLV321x devices use push-pull outputs that can source and sink current, must not be connected to other outputs or shorted to rails, and unused outputs should float. TLV322x devices use open-drain outputs that support pullups from 0 V to 5.5 V, wired-OR operation, and level translation; TI recommends 100 µA to 1 mA pullup current, and unused outputs may float or connect to V–.

Inputs and outputs include ESD protection to V+ and V–, and input currents should be limited to 10 mA or less when clamp conduction is possible. TLV321x devices include a power-on reset that holds the output low for up to 32 µs after the 1.65 V POR threshold is crossed. Comparator output depends on whether VIN is above or below VREF, with propagation delay affected by overdrive voltage. External hysteresis can reduce chatter when inputs transition slowly near the threshold, using inverting or non-inverting resistor networks.

A typical low-side current-sensing application uses an amplifier and comparator to signal when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1 V. Proper bypassing, stable supplies, grounding, and high-speed PCB layout are required to avoid ringing, false triggers, oscillation, and input-output coupling. The document also provides references, support resources, ESD handling cautions, revision history, mechanical and packaging information, and TI warranty and use disclaimers.

Coach Vigneault said the team must “bring its A game” to beat a very strong, structured, skilled and physical opponent that does not deviate from its game plan. He felt the first period was good but the third was not, and said the team needs better compete level, execution and commitment to the plan. He noted Henrik Lundqvist kept them in the game, while some others played well, but a “B game” will not be enough. Vigneault said adjustments will be made, the team must turn the page, and speed is one strength they need to use. He praised Johnny as a consistent defenseman, Rick for strong all-around play and positive scoring-chance results, and said one defenseman’s stamina and overall play have improved throughout the playoffs.

The passage urges creating a Cabinet-level secretary of commerce to address issues involving labor, capital, corporations, and international business, with broad powers over interstate corporations. It supports reciprocity with Cuba, citing the United States’ political relationship with Cuba after vacating the island and its interest in closer economic ties. It also notes a trade convention with Great Britain regarding Newfoundland. The passage favors arbitration over war where possible, praises The Hague tribunal, and cites its use by the United States and Mexico. It recommends consideration of Hawaiian fire claims and supports building an isthmian canal, preferably at Panama, noting title negotiations and the need for a continuing national policy.

The professor discusses possible pathways to nuclear war, comparing nuclear risk with climate change and emphasizing that nuclear war has a low daily probability but potentially catastrophic consequences. He identifies fear and distrust as central drivers of nuclear escalation, especially between the United States and Russia, and highlights risks from hair-trigger alert systems, early warning failures, cyberattack, and short decision times.

He reviews debates over the use and utility of nuclear weapons, the postwar arms race, deterrence, nuclear taboo, and the possibility that luck has helped prevent nuclear war since 1945. He argues that current arsenals remain excessive and that inspections under arms control agreements may be more important than numerical limits.

The talk examines proliferation and the Non-Proliferation Treaty, noting tensions between non-nuclear states’ obligations not to acquire weapons and nuclear states’ obligation to disarm. The professor discusses India-Pakistan tensions as a major pathway to escalation, citing Pakistan’s aggressive deployment posture and India’s focus on China. He also addresses North Korea, Iran negotiations, nuclear inspections, and concerns about enrichment capabilities.

He describes Obama’s nuclear record as mixed: raising hopes for abolition, achieving New START, and improving nuclear security, while retaining hair-trigger alert, lacking engagement with North Korea, and supporting modernization. He argues abolition should be assessed by comparative risk reduction, not the elimination of all risk, and says diplomacy, inspections, and long-term thinking remain essential.

CPRE Bedfordshire criticised Central Bedfordshire Council’s claim that 44,000 to 55,000 new homes are needed over 20 years, saying a Freedom of Information response shows about 60% would be for people moving into the area. It said the plans risk loss of countryside and strain already pressured road and rail infrastructure. The housing assessment identified 32,000 homes needed from 2015 to 2035, with CBC adding 7,400 for Luton residents and up to 20% contingency. CBC said it must plan for projected population needs under national policy, including migration, natural change and affordability.

Woodstock grief specialists Vicki Travnicek and Nicole Bruder advise grieving people to plan for holiday events, limit attendance if needed, have an exit plan, acknowledge emotions, share memories, be patient, and consider new traditions while keeping meaningful old ones. The Surviving Suicide Grief Support Group, facilitated by trained peer volunteers, meets twice monthly at Smith-Leroy Funeral Home starting again in January. Additional grief programs include “Understanding Your Grief” in Woodstock beginning April 4 and an eight-week “Healing Journey Through Grief” in Ingersoll from Feb. 1 to March 22.

President Andrew Johnson sent the House further correspondence with General U. S. Grant about Grant’s departure from the War Office. Johnson’s February 10, 1868 letter disputed Grant’s account, accused him of having intended to thwart Johnson regarding Edwin M. Stanton’s suspension, and alleged insubordination over orders issued through the War Department. Johnson included statements from five Cabinet members about the January 14 Cabinet conversation, generally supporting Johnson’s recollection that Grant had agreed either to remain as Secretary of War ad interim pending judicial proceedings or to notify Johnson in time to make another appointment. Grant’s February 11 reply denied any intent to disobey a lawful presidential order, said he had interpreted an ambiguous instruction regarding Stanton’s authority, and cited communications showing other departments continued to recognize Stanton as Secretary of War.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated October 20, 2016, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2016. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Exchange Act unless specifically incorporated by reference. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer.

North Carolina fell to 2-3 after a 38-10 loss to Clemson, trailing 28-3 after the first quarter and dropping to 0-3 against Power 4 teams. Bill Belichick said UNC does not need structural changes, blaming poor execution, concentration and coaching while saying the team must improve what it is already doing. GM Mike Lombardi described the season as a rebuild, but players pushed back, saying they are focused on winning. Belichick said playing time will go to those who perform best, regardless of age.

The article argues that advocacy is a core responsibility in special education and should be integrated throughout pre-service teacher preparation rather than taught as a single lesson. It presents an undergraduate inclusive special education course, “All Means All,” as a model. The course embeds advocacy through learning goals, recurring reflections, TED Talk analyses, policy and law activities, debate, and a final persuasive TED-style presentation and paper.

Course activities include studying special education court cases through a jigsaw activity, analyzing arguments about inclusion, debating full inclusion, examining disability advocacy history and the ADA, and writing from the perspective of stakeholders. These assignments are scaffolded to build students’ skills in argumentation, policy analysis, critical reflection, communication, and persuasive advocacy.

The article emphasizes that special educators need preparation to advocate across classrooms, schools, communities, states, and federal contexts. It concludes that advocacy-focused coursework can help pre-service teachers develop agency, navigate systemic barriers, use evidence-based practices, and advocate effectively for students with disabilities.

The authors argue that community-based organizations and out-of-school programs should be part of the youth mental health safety net. They say camps, mentoring, sports, and after-school programs already provide trusted relationships and belonging, making staff well positioned to recognize distress, respond, and refer youth to professionals. They call for investment in training, protocols, partnerships with mental health providers, referral systems, and support for frontline workers to complement school-based efforts.

Medical students face substantial stressors, including demanding curricula, clinical pressures, sleep deprivation, financial concerns, and work-life imbalance, increasing their risk of psychological distress and burnout. The COVID-19 pandemic intensified concerns about anxiety, depression, and disrupted academic routines, highlighting the need for resilience skills in medical education. While resilience-building programs exist in North America, few medical programs in the MENA region proactively support students in sustaining mental health.

This qualitative phenomenological study explored Year 4 medical students’ perceptions of resilience and their experiences with a curriculum-based resilience skills building course at Mohammed Bin Rashid University of Medicine and Health Sciences in Dubai, UAE. The six-hour course, delivered during the first clinical year of the MBBS program, aimed to raise awareness of stress and burnout and introduce tools such as mindfulness, meditation, cognitive behavioural therapy basics, emotional intelligence, coping strategies, gratitude, and mental toughness. It was grounded in constructivist experiential learning and included reflection, feedback, journaling, OSCE assessment, attendance, and a reflective essay.

Data came from reflective essays submitted by 37 students. Thematic analysis produced a conceptual framework called the “3As of Building Resilience”: Awareness, Application, and Appraisal. Under Awareness, students described resilience as an active, ongoing process involving coping, adaptation, self-awareness, and internal and external resources. They associated resilience with mindfulness, meditation, reflection, emotional intelligence, and social support, and viewed it as relevant to academic demands, clinical transitions, future medical practice, wellbeing, and patient care. They also recognized that resilience requires conscious practice and effort.

Under Application, students described practical strategies such as mindfulness, meditation, breathing exercises, reflection, yoga, exercise, prayer, journaling, gratitude, time management, reframing thoughts, rest, social support, and self-care. Reported challenges included skepticism, lack of time, difficulty prioritizing practice, resistance to changing habits, and the perceived effort required.

Under Appraisal, students generally valued resilience building and reported perceived benefits including reduced stress and anxiety, improved emotional regulation, self-awareness, confidence, coping, sleep, concentration, gratitude, and academic and clinical functioning. Many students positively appraised the course, stating that it introduced useful lifelong skills, encouraged reflection, fostered shared experience, and helped them integrate resilience practices into daily life.

The study concluded that integrating a constructivist, self-directed resilience skills course into medical curricula is likely to be positively received by students and may increase awareness and application of resilience-related practices.

Avoyelles Parish is projected to spend $8,123 per student in state and local revenues in 2017-18, ranking 68th of 69 Louisiana public school districts. Its local contribution, $2,102 per student, also ranks 68th. The state average is $9,015, down from $10,888 in 2015. Louisiana’s Minimum Foundation Program starts at $3,961 per student and adjusts funding based on local tax capacity and student needs. Avoyelles receives about 74.15 percent of its funding from the state. A Senate resolution requested a study on the actual cost of education and funding mechanisms by Feb. 1, 2018.

Executive Order 11905, issued by President Ford in 1976, replaced the 40 Committee with the Operations Advisory Group to review covert actions, retained the DCI’s implementation role, required formal recommendations and reviews, and banned U.S. Government involvement in political assassinations and domestic intelligence activities. Under Carter, Hughes-Ryan requirements remained while the OAG was replaced by the NSC Special Coordination Committee, later known as SCC-Intelligence, with membership expanded in EO 12036 to include the Attorney General and OMB Director as full members. The SCC-I created the Special Activities Working Group to review covert action proposals, but it gradually fell out of use and was replaced by other interagency groups. The Carter administration also used “world-wide” or “generic” presidential findings for lower-risk covert operations, supported by CIA- and State-cleared “Perspectives” documents that gave specific guidance; riskier operations required separate findings or memoranda.

The lecture discusses modern industrial organization issues involving platforms, focusing on dominant digital platforms, access, contestability, and fairness. The professor contrasts traditional antitrust and regulation with newer concerns such as intellectual property sharing, R&D joint ventures, standard setting, data pools, collective negotiations, common ownership, and algorithmic collusion.

The lecture centers on two-sided platforms connecting consumers with merchants or apps, including both in-house and third-party providers. Key concerns include behavioral manipulation, self-preferencing, contestability of core platform markets, and whether third-party apps or merchants receive fair access and compensation. European regulation, including the Digital Markets Act, Digital Services Act, Artificial Intelligence Act, and platform-to-business rules, is described as more advanced than U.S. efforts.

The professor critiques the Chicago School argument that platforms have incentives to maintain rich ecosystems because they can charge consumers more. Three limitations are presented: consumer prices may be regulated or constrained; digital platforms often face a zero lower bound because optimal consumer prices may be negative but cannot be set below zero due to arbitrage; and apps or merchants may also face zero lower bounds that generate supranormal profits.

Platforms are compared to public utilities because they have network effects and low marginal costs, but the professor argues they cannot be regulated like traditional utilities because they are global firms, change rapidly, and have difficult-to-measure investment histories and product boundaries. Breakups are also described as challenging because digital business segments evolve quickly.

The Digital Markets Act is described as targeting dominant platforms through designation thresholds and obligations such as fair treatment of merchants. Enforcement may rely heavily on self-execution because regulators have limited resources. The lecture also discusses mixed ecosystems, where platforms combine in-house and third-party offerings, and notes policy debates over whether platforms should be forced into pure broker roles.

Contestability is discussed through multihoming, interoperability, portability, and disintermediation. The professor explains that interoperability can help entrants compete with incumbents, but implementation is difficult because incumbents lack incentives to assist rivals. Entry for buyout, including examples involving Facebook’s acquisitions of Instagram and WhatsApp and similar patterns in pharmaceuticals, is presented as a concern because it may deter competition without benefiting consumers.

The lecture reviews traditional access pricing, including the efficient component pricing rule, which caps access charges based on the incumbent’s lost downstream profit when a rival serves a customer. The professor then extends access pricing to two-sided platforms. In a model with consumers, a core platform, an in-house app, and a superior third-party app, access charges, ancillary benefits, and zero lower bounds determine incentives for foreclosure or squeezing. Too-low access charges can induce non-price foreclosure, while too-high charges can squeeze third-party apps. The optimal access charge is described as equal to the ancillary benefit, though estimating that benefit is difficult for regulators.

The lecture concludes by noting the need for simple, usable regulatory rules for digital platforms and previews a later discussion on the morality of markets and how antitrust authorities may consider responsibilities such as environmental concerns.

The passage welcomes readers to Super Bowl LII weekend, noting the Patriots will play the Eagles in Minneapolis and inviting participation in a Sunday game thread. It presents five Friday night questions about 2018 playoff teams, Kirk Cousins’ next team, Nick Foles completions, the coin flip, and Rob Gronkowski receiving yards, plus bonus questions about combined game totals and Alan Faneca’s Hall of Fame chances. It also recaps prior Senior Bowl Week answers, including opinions on Le’Veon Bell’s contract, preferred Senior Bowl prospects for the Steelers, XFL interest, and Pro Bowl prediction results. The passage closes by noting upcoming NFL award and Hall of Fame announcements and lists the contest leaderboard, led by Alan Tman with 48.5 points.

The lecture introduces 18.100A Real Analysis, whose goals are to build proof-writing and proof-reading skills while proving statements about real numbers, functions, and limits. It defines sets, the empty set, element notation, quantifiers, implication, subsets, equality of sets, and proper subsets. It reviews set descriptions and examples including natural numbers, integers, rationals, reals, and odd numbers, noting inclusions among number systems and stating that defining the real numbers is an early goal of the course.

The lecture defines union, intersection, set difference, complement, and disjoint sets, then proves the first of DeMorgan’s Laws by showing both set inclusions. It explains the structure of proofs as using hypotheses, definitions, logic, and calculations to reach a conclusion.

It then introduces the well-ordering property of the natural numbers and uses it to prove the principle of mathematical induction by contradiction. Finally, it demonstrates induction with two examples: the finite geometric sum formula for \(c \ne 1\), and the inequality \((1+c)^n \ge 1+nc\) for \(c \ge -1\).

Top stories include continued debate over investigations into Trump administration ties to Russia after Flynn’s exit, a possible U.S. shift on Israeli-Palestinian peace policy, an arrest in Kim Jong Nam’s death, NATO talks on spending, terrorism and Russia, and concerns over cracks in California’s Oroville Dam. Other items cover risky driving, a Boeing union vote in South Carolina, laser labeling of produce in Sweden, Kate Upton’s third Sports Illustrated swimsuit cover, and Rumor winning Westminster best in show.

New NASA-supported research suggests Uranus emits about 15% more energy than it receives from the Sun, challenging decades of belief based on Voyager 2 data that the planet had no internal heat. Using advanced computer modeling and decades of telescope observations, researchers reassessed how much sunlight Uranus reflects and how much heat it releases. The findings indicate Uranus has some internal warmth, though far less than Neptune, and may offer clues about the planet’s formation, unusual sideways rotation, possible violent past, and similar-sized exoplanets.

Oclaro Inc. (NASDAQ: OCLR) shares fell 0.99% in the most recent session, closing at $9.04. Analysts have a 52-week mean price target of $9.27 based on 13 opinions, with targets ranging from $6.50 to $11.25. The stock’s average brokerage recommendation is 2.38, with 2 Buy ratings, 3 Outperform ratings, 9 Hold ratings, and no Underperform or Sell ratings. Oclaro’s ATR-14 is 0.29, weekly volatility is 2.50%, and monthly volatility is 3.07%. Its RSI is 55.48. The company has a market capitalization of $1.53 billion and 169.6 million outstanding shares. In the previous trade, 1.62 million shares changed hands, compared with an average volume of 5.58 million.

The study developed and externally validated machine learning models to predict pulmonary restriction from spirometric, demographic, and anthropometric data, comparing them with the forced vital capacity lower limit of normal (FVC LLN) used in ERS/ATS guidelines. Development used 42,462 pulmonary function tests from one academic health system; validation used 24,524 tests from another.

Logistic regression, random forest, and boosted tree models were trained, with the random forest model showing the best overall performance. In the validation dataset, the random forest model had a negative predictive value of 88.3%, compared with 72.7% for the FVC LLN. It had higher sensitivity but lower specificity than the FVC LLN and excluded the need for static lung volume measurement in fewer tests. Model performance was less equitable among non-Hispanic Black than non-Hispanic White patients, but disparities were smaller with the random forest model than with the FVC LLN.

Decision curve analysis favored the random forest model over the FVC LLN across most thresholds. The authors concluded that machine learning models improved both accuracy and equity in excluding restriction from spirometry, while noting limitations including poor calibration in external validation, possible ascertainment bias, limited racial and ethnic diversity, and residual inequity.

The Iowa Supreme Court dismissed certiorari proceedings brought by G. M. Cox against District Judge George W. Burnham. Cox argued that the court lacked jurisdiction to grant pharmacist P. H. Bell a permit to sell intoxicating liquors because Bell’s application was heard at a later term than the one to which it was originally brought.

The court held that statutes governing liquor permits are construed like statutes generally, except that they must be interpreted to prevent evasion of liquor laws. Code section 2389, requiring prompt hearing of permit applications and trial at the first term if court business allows, is not mandatory in a way that removes the court’s general discretion over its docket. If a permit application is not heard during the first term and no vacation hearing is set, adjournment does not automatically dismiss the application or deprive the court of jurisdiction. Undisposed matters stand continued under the general statute. In the absence of contrary evidence, the court presumed there was cause for postponing Bell’s application.

Because the later hearing was held in open court, appeared regular, and was not evasive, the court found no jurisdictional defect. The proceedings were dismissed.

Asian stocks were unsettled and the yuan stayed near 11-month lows ahead of a July 6 deadline for U.S. tariffs on $34 billion of Chinese goods, which Beijing has vowed to match. MSCI’s Asia-Pacific index outside Japan edged up 0.1% after a nine-month low, while Japan’s Nikkei fell 0.5%. Wall Street declined, led by pressure on technology shares, including Facebook, Tesla and Micron. A Chinese sales injunction against Micron weighed on other chipmakers and related Japanese shares. China’s central bank said it was monitoring foreign exchange moves and aimed to keep the yuan stable. The Mexican peso posted its biggest one-day gain in over two years after comments from the president-elect. Major currencies were little changed. Oil rose on a larger-than-expected drop in U.S. stockpiles, while copper remained near nine-month lows on trade concerns.

Tesla, Inc. filed its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2018. The company designs, develops, manufactures and sells fully electric vehicles, energy generation and storage systems, installs and maintains energy systems, and sells solar electricity. Its reportable segments are automotive and energy generation and storage. As of December 31, 2018, Tesla had 48,817 full-time employees.

Tesla produced and sold Model S, Model X and Model 3, and planned future vehicles including Model Y, Tesla Semi, a pickup truck and a new Tesla Roadster. It also offered Powerwall 2, Powerpack 2, solar energy systems and Solar Roof. Tesla sold vehicles through company-owned stores, galleries, service centers and online, supported by Supercharger and Destination Charging networks.

Tesla manufactured vehicles and components primarily in Fremont and Lathrop, California; Tilburg, Netherlands; and Gigafactory 1 near Reno, Nevada. It manufactured energy storage products at Gigafactory 1 and solar products at U.S. facilities including Gigafactory 2 in Buffalo, New York. In January 2019, Tesla began construction of Gigafactory Shanghai, where it intended to produce certain Model 3 trims for the local China market by the end of 2019.

The filing describes risks including delays in product development, manufacturing, delivery and service ramp; challenges scaling Model 3 production and international operations; dependence on suppliers, many of which are single-source; uncertainty in consumer adoption of electric vehicles; potential product defects or restrictions on features; manufacturing cost targets; and possible increases, shortages or disruptions in materials such as lithium-ion cells, aluminum, steel, lithium, nickel, copper and cobalt.

The passage describes a January 2017 stock selection process for Dividend Champions, Contenders, and Challengers, excluding REITs and MLPs. The author first selects companies in the top half of the Dugan Stock Scoring System, then applies filters for yield, market cap, Graham number, payout ratio, dividend increase, EPS growth, debt/equity ratio, and minimum Dugan Score. The Dugan system evaluates CCC stocks using risk, value, past performance, and future performance expectations, emphasizing current conditions and expected future results rather than past stock performance. Sector weighting recommendations from brokers add small bonuses or penalties. Applying the 2017 formula and filters produced 21 high-scoring CCC companies. The passage includes investment disclaimers and discloses long positions in several stocks.

East of England Ambulance Service NHS Trust was rated Requires Improvement overall by the CQC after a March inspection, though its caring services were rated Outstanding. Inspectors noted progress in safeguarding, Mental Capacity Act understanding and incident reporting, but found issues with response standards, winter delays, staff morale, leadership engagement and consistency of processes. The CQC said improvements are needed in emergency response times, risk registers, staff support and mentoring. Chief Executive Robert Morton welcomed recognition of improvements and praised staff, saying the trust faces challenges across a large area but is working to strengthen local leadership, communication and services, supported by £11.5 million in additional funding.

Coach DeBoer said the team has been in difficult series situations before and must get one win to build momentum. He said lineup changes would be considered through tape review but not made out of panic. He credited Los Angeles and its goaltender for stopping quality chances, said the team needs more goals and a first goal, and defended his players’ effort. He also discussed travel and schedule adjustments, praised the officiating overall, and questioned one momentum-changing call involving a lost puck.

Temple Grandin will present “Livestock Handling and Animal Behavior” at a breakfast event from 7-9 a.m. Friday, Feb. 23, at the Tehama District Fairground in Red Bluff. The $15 event is sponsored by Shasta College Ag Leadership Club and UC Cooperative Extension.

Israel and Canada signed a modernized Canada-Israel Free Trade Agreement in Montreal, replacing their 1997 deal. The revised agreement removes duties on thousands of additional products, including fresh fruit and canned goods, and adds chapters on labor, the environment, trade and gender, small and medium-sized enterprises, corporate social responsibility, and improved dispute settlement. Canadian Minister Francois-Phillippe Champagne said it would improve market access and support growth in both countries, while Israeli Minister Eli Cohen said it would create new opportunities for Israeli exports, increase competition, and reduce living costs. The agreement aims to double bilateral trade and will take effect after ratification by both parliaments.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture enables real-time ray tracing on single-GPU systems using new RT Cores, RTX software, and filtering algorithms. Alongside Microsoft’s DirectML and DXR APIs, it supports real-time AI and ray tracing for games. Turing also adds advanced shading features, inherits CUDA enhancements from Volta, and powers products including GeForce RTX 2080 Ti and Quadro RTX 6000.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended March 30, 2019. For the quarter, total net sales were $58.0 billion, down from $61.1 billion a year earlier, driven by lower iPhone sales and partly offset by higher Services and Wearables, Home and Accessories sales. Net income was $11.6 billion, compared with $13.8 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $2.46, compared with $2.73. For the six months ended March 30, 2019, net sales were $142.3 billion and net income was $31.5 billion.

As of March 30, 2019, Apple reported total assets of $342.0 billion, total liabilities of $236.1 billion and shareholders’ equity of $105.9 billion. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $225.4 billion. The company had $11.9 billion in commercial paper and $101.2 billion in term debt outstanding.

Apple adopted new accounting standards related to revenue recognition, financial instruments, income taxes and restricted cash. The company reported ongoing legal and tax matters, including the European Commission state aid decision, VirnetX litigation, a Qualcomm settlement reached April 16, 2019, and iOS performance management cases.

During the quarter, Apple released new iPad Air, iPad mini, iMac and AirPods products, and announced Apple News+, Apple Card, Apple Arcade, a new Apple TV app and Apple TV+. Apple repurchased $24.0 billion of common stock and paid $3.4 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents during the quarter.

The passage explains that diet can support recovery from infections such as colds and flu by providing nutrients, energy, and immune support. It highlights the importance of varied fruit and vegetables, vitamin C, vitamin A, protein, herbs and spices, probiotics, and nuts and seeds. These foods may support immune function, gut health, cell repair, and overall recovery.

A Danish study found that children of older mothers had fewer behavioural, social and emotional problems at ages seven and 11, but not by age 15. Researchers linked this to older mothers’ greater psychological maturity, including being more tolerant, emotionally stable, positive about parenting, and less likely to scold or physically discipline children. The study used data from 4,741 mothers in the Danish Longitudinal Survey of Children, with findings significant beyond demographic and socioeconomic factors. Researchers also noted that later motherhood carries health risks, including miscarriage, premature birth and deformities.

This study conducted a PRISMA-guided meta-analysis of 13 empirical studies from eight countries examining AI-related technologies in education, including chatbots, generative AI, online learning, virtual reality, learning management systems, and AI platforms. Literature was searched in Google Scholar, ERIC, and Scopus for English peer-reviewed studies published from January 2015 to July 2024.

The overall effect of AI-related technologies in education was positive and statistically significant, with an effect size of 0.86, p < 0.0001, and 95% CI [0.45, 1.27], though heterogeneity was high (I² = 86.15%) and publication bias was reported. Chatbots and generative AI showed the largest effect size, 1.02, p < 0.0001, 95% CI [0.45, 1.59]. Online learning and virtual reality showed a positive effect size of 0.79, p < 0.07, 95% CI [-0.04, 1.62]. Learning management systems and AI platforms showed a significant positive effect size of 0.62, p < 0.05, 95% CI [0.03, 1.21].

The study also tested novel Naive Bayes, TF-IDF, BERT-based, and hybrid fixed/random-effects approaches, which produced similarly positive overall results. The authors conclude that AI technologies can significantly improve educational outcomes, while noting substantial heterogeneity, publication bias, and the need for careful implementation and further research.
Scientists coaxed human skin cells fused with empty eggs to undergo meiosis, creating functional eggs that formed early embryos.

Niu Technologies’ stock has posted large gains in 2025, supported by strong recent growth, but the author argues this growth may not continue fast enough to justify current valuations. Potential disruptions could challenge expectations, leading the author to maintain a neutral view and hold rating on NIU stock.

Fredrik went for X-rays, with a report expected by the end of the day, after missing a few shifts but returning to finish the game. The speaker said the team had a poor start and especially struggled with passing, causing turnovers that stalled the offense. He defended a playoff line as productive, defensively strong, and cohesive.

He said the power play failed partly because the team did not take good shots and needed to adjust. He emphasized focusing on evening the series rather than relying on history, though he recalled a past Montreal playoff comeback. He was unsure whether ice conditions contributed but said turnovers and bad passes were clear on review.

The speaker said one player did not have his best game but avoided blaming individuals. He noted Carolina’s speed, faceoff strength, and quick puck movement, and said penalties created ice-time imbalances for Detroit’s top players while limiting effective players with under ten minutes. He said adjustments may be needed to balance minutes, improve entries, get the puck deeper, and change the forecheck.

Russian math after-school programs are growing across the U.S., led by the Russian School of Mathematics, which has 22,000 students and 40 branches. Parents cite dissatisfaction with U.S. math instruction, desire for rigor, and hopes that stronger math skills will help children. Programs emphasize reasoning, early algebra and geometry, understanding why procedures work, and challenging homework, often costing about $2,000 a year.

The approach traces to Soviet math traditions and immigration by Russian Jews, including co-founder Inessa Rifkin, who started the Russian School of Mathematics in Newton in 1997 after finding her son’s math education lacking. Other programs, such as the Studio of Engaging Math in Brighton, adapt Russian materials with small groups, puzzles, manipulatives, and ability-based instruction.

Educators note possible benefits, including greater student confidence and more participation in honors math, but also challenges: uneven preparation within public school classrooms, possible overconfidence, pressure on families, and widening gaps between students who can afford enrichment and those who cannot. Researchers say Russian math has not been extensively studied in the U.S., and its broader impact remains unclear.

The passage describes a patent application for CAR T cell therapies with enhanced efficacy through reducing or eliminating the expression or function of Tet methylcytosine dioxygenase genes, particularly Tet2, in engineered immune effector cells such as T cells or NK cells. The invention provides CAR-expressing cells targeting tumor antigens, including CD19, with Tet1, Tet2, and/or Tet3 inhibition or disruption to decrease 5-hydroxymethylcytosine levels and improve CAR T cell proliferation, function, cytokine production, degranulation, and therapeutic efficacy.

Tet inhibition may be achieved using gene editing systems such as CRISPR/Cas9, zinc finger nucleases, TALENs, or meganucleases; siRNA or shRNA; small molecules; dominant-negative proteins; or nucleic acids encoding these inhibitors. The passage also describes methods for manufacturing CAR-expressing cells by integrating CAR-encoding nucleic acid into Tet genes or contacting CAR cells ex vivo with Tet inhibitors, as well as vectors encoding both a CAR and a Tet inhibitor.

The compositions and methods are proposed for treating diseases associated with tumor antigen expression, including hematologic cancers, solid tumors, proliferative diseases, precancerous conditions, and some non-cancer indications. The passage reports data from a CLL patient treated with CD19 CAR T cells, where CAR19 insertion into the Tet2 gene was associated with clonal expansion, disrupted Tet2 transcripts, reduced demethylation markers, and expansion of CAR T cells. Additional experiments show that Tet2 knockdown or editing in human T cells reduced 5-hydroxymethylcytosine, promoted T stem cell memory-like populations, and affected CAR T cell expansion, cytokine production, and proliferation.

This Mendelian randomization study assessed whether genetically determined pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) causally affects cardiovascular disease risks and whether hypertension mediates these associations. Using 11 independent PAT-associated SNPs from GWAS data as instrumental variables, the study analyzed associations with multiple cardiovascular outcomes, including CVD, heart failure, hypertension, coronary heart disease, ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, and venous thromboembolism.

Genetically determined PAT was significantly associated with higher risks of CVD, heart failure, hypertension, coronary heart disease, ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, and venous thromboembolism. No clear association was found with cardiac arrhythmias, atrial fibrillation, aortic aneurysm, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, myocardial infarction, cardioembolic stroke, small vessel stroke, large artery stroke, or subarachnoid hemorrhage. Sensitivity analyses supported the main findings and did not identify notable heterogeneity, horizontal pleiotropy, or outlying SNPs.

Two-step mediation analysis indicated that hypertension partly mediated the associations between PAT and CVD-related outcomes, including heart failure, coronary heart disease, ischemic heart disease, and ischemic stroke. The authors suggest PAT may be a potential therapeutic target for some cardiovascular diseases and that antihypertensive strategies may provide related cardiovascular benefits. Limitations included unavailable original PAT GWAS data, European-only participants, some sample overlap, possible residual bias, and small case numbers for several outcomes.

Enron disclosed that the SEC requested information about related-party transactions involving partnerships formerly run by CFO Andrew Fastow, including LJM Cayman and LJM2 Co-Investment. The company described the request as an informal inquiry and said it would cooperate fully. The disclosure followed Enron’s announcement of a $1.01 billion third-quarter write-off, a $618 million loss, and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity tied to unwinding partnership-related arrangements.

Enron shares fell more than 20% to $20.65 on heavy volume, extending a sharp decline amid investor concerns over unclear disclosures, potential conflicts of interest, off-balance-sheet financing vehicles, possible dilution from trusts such as Whitewing and Marlin, and the risk of debt downgrades. Analysts cited concerns about Enron’s transparency, valuation of assets, and possible further write-offs.

Shareholder lawsuits were filed alleging misrepresentations, delayed write-downs, and breaches of fiduciary duty related to Fastow’s partnerships and Enron’s financial reporting. Enron said its board, auditors, attorneys, and SEC filings had addressed the arrangements, while Kenneth Lay scheduled a conference call to respond to investor concerns.

Three youths were killed during an Indian troop siege and search operation in Awneera, Shopian, sparking protests in which civilians were injured. A mosque and four homes were reportedly blasted, and locals alleged house ransacking. Two Indian soldiers were killed in an attack, with others injured in Shopian and Bandipora. Train services remained suspended. Kashmiri resistance leaders opposed efforts to alter Jammu and Kashmir’s disputed status or demographics.

The passage discusses sexual harassment in universities and workplaces, citing Richard Akindele’s dismissal by OAU after being found guilty of soliciting sex from a student. It commends OAU’s swift action and urges higher institutions to expose and punish offending lecturers, protect female students, and encourage students to focus on their studies.

Tom Evans said his terminally ill 23-month-old son Alfie was breathing unassisted nine hours after life support was withdrawn at Alder Hey Children’s Hospital. He claimed doctors initially left Alfie without food, water or oxygen but later provided oxygen and water after a lengthy discussion. Evans said Alfie’s mother, Kate James, was lying beside him and felt comfortable. He argued Alfie was not suffering and said he believed his son would need some form of life support soon. Kate later posted that Alfie had been allowed oxygen and water.

The speaker says the team must set its own tone on the road, expect an inspired and desperate opponent, and be ready for the crowd’s energy. They view the extra day as useful for rest, practice, preparation, and adjustments. The speaker emphasizes execution, winning more faceoffs, staying patient under pressure, and playing more aggressively to create chances. They note that injuries are common at this stage and everyone must be ready to contribute. The speaker praises a versatile teammate for doing whatever role is needed and getting rewarded offensively. They also credits an intense former-player coach for helping forwards with subtle details.

The passage is an Enron media roundup for June 4, 2001. Articles report that Bush adviser Karl Rove held stock in major companies including Enron while awaiting ethics approval to divest; Saudi Arabia signed energy investment agreements with nine oil firms, including Enron, for natural gas and related projects worth at least $25 billion; and commentators criticized energy companies during the California energy crisis while discussing boom-bust energy cycles.

Several reports focus on India. Fitch lowered India’s sovereign rating outlook to negative, citing fiscal policy, privatization and foreign investment concerns, while analysts debated whether the Enron-Dabhol dispute influenced the move. The rupee ended steady despite ratings concerns. Lenders to Enron’s Dabhol Power Company planned talks in Singapore over support for the $2.9 billion project amid disputes with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board over payments, power costs and contract termination. Indian Power Minister Suresh Prabhu said power reforms were entering a new phase focused on distribution, private sales, utility finances and honoring international contracts.

Other items note Spectron brokered a UK gas-electricity spark spread deal between Powergen and Enron; Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo accused Enron of poor performance and bad faith on a Lagos power project; an opinion piece warned the Bush administration might pressure India over Enron’s interests; and Enron Japan’s Joseph Hirl said Japan’s electricity market had opened but lacked genuine competition.

The study developed and validated an unbiased metagenomic next-generation sequencing workflow for infectious disease detection using HostEL for human background depletion and AmpRE for single-tube DNA/RNA library preparation. HostEL uses selective lysis and magnetic bead-immobilized nucleases to enrich pathogen nucleic acids, while AmpRE prepares libraries from both DNA and RNA with reduced processing steps.

Analytical validation used human plasma spiked with ZymoBIOMICS microbial standards at concentrations down to 70,000 cells/mL. Low-depth sequencing on iSeq 100 detected all 10 bacterial and fungal species at all dilutions with HostEL treatment, while untreated samples lost signal at lower concentrations. HostEL achieved 96% sensitivity and 96% specificity, compared with 82% sensitivity and 97% specificity without treatment.

Clinical validation used 42 banked plasma samples previously classified by molecular testing. After excluding low-quality samples with Ct≥33 or undetectable qPCR results, the workflow showed 93% agreement with clinical results. It detected DNA viruses, RNA viruses, and bacteria, and showed no false positives in eight clinically negative control samples. Sequencing reads correlated linearly with qPCR Ct values, with confident detection reported up to Ct 30 and below.

The workflow was tested on iSeq 100, simulated shorter iSeq reads, and MiniSeq, with comparable detection performance. The authors conclude that HostEL and AmpRE can reduce time, cost, and effort for metagenomic sequencing while enabling detection of bacteria, fungi, DNA viruses, and RNA viruses in plasma.

Cruzin’ for Life’s free transport van for Mission Hope Cancer Center in Santa Maria has served more than 2,600 cancer patients and logged over 34,000 miles in its first year, helping patients from several nearby communities get to treatments. The nonprofit raised funds to retrofit the wheelchair-accessible van, aided by a $36,000 donation from Santa Maria Energy, and continues funding operations through events such as its Valentine’s Day crab feed and annual car show. Mission Hope officials said the service helps prevent missed treatments, and Cruzin’ for Life may consider a second van if need and funding continue.

A woman declared dead by paramedics after a fatal car crash near Carletonville, South Africa, was later found alive in a mortuary refrigerator. She was taken to hospital, and ambulance service Distress Alert said procedures were followed and launched an investigation. Two other occupants of the vehicle died.

San Juan Mayor Carmen Yulín Cruz called new Hurricane Maria death toll estimates “a day of collective mourning” and criticized the Puerto Rican government and Trump administration. Harvard researchers estimated 4,645 excess deaths in Puerto Rico from Sept. 20 to Dec. 31, far above the official toll of 64, though the report’s margin of error ranged from 793 to 8,498. Cruz said the figure confirmed the official count was wrong and expressed frustration that President Trump had not apologized for the lives lost. She also said Puerto Rico was not prepared for another hurricane season, despite learning from past shortcomings.

Jim Montgomery enters his first full season as St. Louis Blues head coach in 2025–26 after taking over midseason and leading the team to the first playoff round. The Blues open Oct. 9 at Enterprise Center, with seven of their first 11 games at home. Key schedule points include early rivalry games, 26 division matchups, an Olympic break from Feb. 5–25, and a late stretch featuring Central Division opponents before the season finale in Utah on April 16. Major storylines include defensive improvement, young forwards’ development, and how quickly Montgomery’s system produces results.

Celtic’s 2-1 win over Rangers at Ibrox left them 19 points ahead with a game in hand, their biggest potential gap over Rangers since 1925-26. That season Celtic finished 20 points ahead of Rangers under today’s points system. The current margin could surpass that record if Celtic win their game in hand.

Backtests using Yahoo Finance data from 2007 suggest NIFTY 50 has a positive end-of-month, or turn-of-the-month, effect similar to that documented in the US market. The tested strategy enters long at the close of the fifth-last trading day of the month and exits at the close of the second trading day of the new month, using trading days rather than calendar days. An initial 100,000 investment compounded through the test period produced a 10.5% CAGR, outperforming buy and hold while being exposed to the market 30% of the time, with a 26% maximum drawdown. The authors note some curve fitting but say results remain reasonably robust when entry and exit days are varied.

The study reviews links between drama-based pedagogy and STEAM education and presents a pilot case study using two drama activities with 19 first-year female university students at ELTE University in Budapest. The research examined how students view dramatic activities in science or history classes and what they can achieve in STEAM classrooms through drama.

Using qualitative participant observation, detailed field notes, and student reflections, researchers observed activities on the life cycle of a butterfly and the Indian caste system. Findings showed that students demonstrated creativity, collaboration, problem-solving, motivation, and engagement. Students reported that the activities helped them express ideas, work together, interpret content in varied ways, and enjoy learning more than through teacher-led explanation.

The study concludes that drama can support STEAM learning by making teaching enjoyable, encouraging artistic interpretation, strengthening confidence and concentration, and helping students understand topics through group work and imaginative expression. It also notes challenges, including uneven participation, time constraints, lack of experience, and limited confidence. The authors acknowledge limitations due to the small, demographically narrow sample and participants’ limited experience with STEAM and drama-based pedagogy.

TrackR announced updates to its Bluetooth tracking devices ahead of CES. The new TrackR pixel is a cheaper, colorful alternative to the TrackR bravo, while the updated TrackR wallet 2.0 is credit card-like and thin. Both use app-based Bluetooth tracking and crowd GPS, with replaceable batteries. TrackR also introduced the atlas smart plug for room-level tracking and Alexa support. Prices range from $24.99 to $39.99, with spring launches expected.

Lightning is not attracted to metal or water; height, pointy shape and isolation are the main factors in where it strikes. A metal-roofed vehicle can offer protection because lightning travels through the metal to the ground, not because of rubber tires. Lightning can strike up to 10 miles from a storm, can hit the same place repeatedly, and trees are unsafe shelters because they are likely strike targets. Most leisure-related lightning deaths occur on or near water, not among golfers.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K reporting that on May 2, 2016, it announced a settlement with Samsung resolving all pending intellectual property litigation between the companies in U.S. district courts, the U.S. International Trade Commission, and the U.S. Patent Office. The settlement includes limited patent licensing by each company, with no broad cross-licensing or other compensation.

The passage describes an autonomous vehicle system with a primary autonomous vehicle control sub-system and multiple independent auxiliary control units. The primary system uses sensors and processing resources to determine vehicle actions, trajectories, and control parameters for interfaces such as braking, steering, propulsion, shifting, and lighting.

The auxiliary control units operate independently of the primary control system and may use separate sensors, logic, communication buses, power sources, and vehicle interfaces. They can detect predefined safety-related events or conditions, such as imminent collisions, lane hazards, roadway obstructions, traffic signals, internal malfunctions, or failure of the primary control system. Upon detection, they can generate predefined vehicle response outputs, including braking, steering, lane keeping, pulling over, stopping, activating lights, or combinations of actions. These outputs may override or bypass primary control commands.

The auxiliary units may also operate in a trajectory verification mode. In this mode, the primary control system sends current or planned future vehicle location data to the auxiliary units, which evaluate whether planned trajectories are safe and return alerts, warnings, instructions, or response outputs. The primary system can use this information to verify, select, or recalculate trajectories.

The described method includes operating the vehicle with the primary autonomous control system while auxiliary control units continuously monitor for predefined events or conditions. When triggered, the auxiliary units either communicate vehicle response outputs directly to vehicle interfaces or send them to the primary control system for trajectory verification or action planning.

Thinking Machines Lab, cofounded and led by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, has launched its first product, Tinker, an API tool for fine-tuning frontier AI models. Tinker automates much of the infrastructure work involved in custom model training and currently supports Meta’s Llama and Alibaba’s Qwen using supervised learning and reinforcement learning. The company says the tool is intended to make advanced model tuning more accessible to researchers, developers, businesses, and hobbyists.

Thinking Machines Lab includes several former OpenAI researchers and raised $2 billion in seed funding at a $12 billion valuation. Beta testers said Tinker is simpler than building reinforcement learning systems from scratch and offers a strong balance of abstraction and user control. The company is currently vetting API users, plans automated safeguards against misuse, and expects to charge for access eventually. Murati said Tinker reflects a broader effort to make frontier AI research more open.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2021. The company is incorporated in Delaware, headquartered in Seattle, and its common stock trades on Nasdaq under AMZN. As of January 26, 2022, it had 508,844,410 common shares outstanding, and the aggregate market value of voting stock held by non-affiliates as of June 30, 2021 was about $1.51 trillion.

Amazon organizes operations into North America, International, and AWS segments. It serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, content creators, advertisers, and employees through online and physical stores, devices, media content, seller programs, AWS technology services, publishing tools, and advertising services. The company employed approximately 1,608,000 full-time and part-time employees as of December 31, 2021.

Amazon identifies intense competition, expansion into new products and geographies, international regulatory risks, demand variability, seller fraud, intellectual property issues, foreign exchange exposure, operational scale, fulfillment and data center risks, cybersecurity, system interruptions, personnel retention, supplier relationships, acquisitions, inventory, payments, stock volatility, government regulation, litigation, product liability, tax obligations, and government contract requirements as significant risk factors.

For 2021, cash provided by operating activities was $46.3 billion, cash used in investing activities was $58.2 billion, and cash provided by financing activities was $6.3 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $96.0 billion as of December 31, 2021. Amazon operated leased and owned facilities for offices, physical stores, fulfillment, data centers, and other uses across North America and international locations.

This study developed and externally validated deep learning MRI biomarkers to identify extra-prostatic extension (EPE) and seminal vesicle invasion (SVI) in localized prostate cancer and assess their prognostic value for biochemical recurrence (BCR). The primary Yale cohort included 820 biopsy-proven prostate cancer patients treated with surgery or radiation; 612 were used for training and 208 for internal testing. External validation used community hospital patients and the public Prostate-Dx dataset.

EPE and SVI ground-truth labels were associated with increased BCR and remained significant after adjustment for clinical covariates. The EPE model achieved AUCs of 0.719 on the Yale test set, 0.743 on the community hospital set, and 0.611 on Prostate-Dx. The SVI model achieved AUCs of 0.724, 0.678, and 0.775, respectively. Patients classified as biomarker-positive for EPE or SVI had lower 5-year BCR-free survival than biomarker-negative patients across training, test, surgery, and radiation groups.

Combining EPE and SVI biomarkers improved prognostic performance compared with either biomarker alone. Patients with two negative biomarkers had a 5-year BCR-free survival of 79.3%, compared with 65.6% for one positive biomarker and 60.0% for two positive biomarkers. The combined biomarker also stratified risk within Gleason score groups and among patients without pathologic EPE or SVI.

Model interpretability analyses using Grad-CAM, hierarchical clustering, and dimensionality reduction supported that model features were associated with EPE and SVI status. Integrating the imaging biomarkers into NCCN and UCSF-CAPRA risk systems reclassified 26.4% of patients and improved C-indexes for BCR prediction. The authors conclude that deep learning MRI biomarkers for EPE and SVI can improve localized prostate cancer risk stratification and may support treatment personalization.
