Microsoft Corporation filed its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2015. The company is incorporated in Washington, headquartered in Redmond, and listed on NASDAQ. Its mission is to empower every person and organization to achieve more, with a strategy focused on best-in-class platforms and productivity services for a mobile-first, cloud-first world.

Microsoft develops, licenses, and supports software, services, devices, cloud-based solutions, online advertising, consulting, support, and training. Its research and development priorities are reinventing productivity and business processes, building the intelligent cloud platform, and creating more personal computing, with Windows 10 described as central to its personal computing strategy.

The company operates six segments: Devices and Consumer Licensing, Computing and Gaming Hardware, Phone Hardware, Devices and Consumer Other, Commercial Licensing, and Commercial Other. Products and services include Windows, Office, Windows Phone, Xbox, Surface, Lumia and other phones, Bing, MSN, Office 365, Azure, Dynamics, Skype, server products, and enterprise services. Microsoft acquired substantially all of Nokia’s Devices and Services Business in April 2014 and reports it in Phone Hardware.

Microsoft operates worldwide with offices in more than 100 countries, regional operations centers, global data centers, and phone manufacturing primarily in Vietnam. Hardware including Xbox, Surface, games, PC accessories, and other devices is mainly produced by third-party manufacturers. Research and development expense was $12.0 billion in fiscal 2015, representing 13% of revenue.

The company distributes products and services through OEMs, distributors, resellers, online channels, Microsoft retail stores, carriers, and partner programs. Customers include consumers, small and medium-sized organizations, large enterprises, public sector institutions, internet service providers, developers, and OEMs. No individual customer accounted for more than 10% of revenue in fiscal 2015, 2014, or 2013.

As of June 30, 2015, Microsoft employed about 118,000 full-time people. In June 2015, management approved a restructuring plan to eliminate up to 7,800 positions in fiscal 2016, primarily in Phone Hardware.

Key risks include intense competition, execution risks in cloud services, uncertain returns from new investments, acquisition and integration risks, goodwill or intangible asset impairments, intellectual property challenges, cyberattacks, privacy and data security issues, service outages, regulatory scrutiny, anti-corruption and trade compliance risks, talent retention, litigation, tax liabilities, product quality or supply problems, global operational risks, and catastrophic or geopolitical disruptions.

Michael Flynn resigned after reports that he discussed U.S. sanctions with Russia’s ambassador before Trump took office. Officials, including acting Attorney General Sally Yates, warned White House counsel Donald McGahn that Flynn could be vulnerable to Russian blackmail, and reports said Trump knew weeks before Vice President Pence. Trump responded by criticizing leaks and dismissing Russia-related allegations. Pundits and some political figures called for investigations into possible Trump administration ties to Moscow, suggesting Flynn and McGahn could become key witnesses if hearings examine what Trump knew and when.

The passage describes reset, clocking, interrupt, timing, and peripheral features of Texas Instruments TMS320DM814x DaVinci Digital Media Processors. Software Global Warm Reset is initiated through the PRM_RSTCTRL register and mostly behaves like External Warm Reset, with specific RSTOUT_WD_OUT behavior. Local resets affect only associated modules, while simultaneous reset sources are handled by priority and recorded in PRM_RSTST. The device supports PCIe and EMAC Switch reset isolation, with software procedures for Root Complex and Endpoint PCIe modes. Reset behavior includes RSTOUT_WD_OUT signaling, emulation reset effects, power-domain warm and cold resets, and I/O pin Hi-Z behavior with exceptions for emulation, EMAC, DDR, and RSTOUT_WD_OUT pins.

Clocking is generated from DEV and AUX clocks using internal oscillators with external crystals or 1.8-V LVCMOS-compatible inputs. DEV is normally 20 MHz but may range from 20–30 MHz under specified conditions; AUX is optional at 20–30 MHz. The document covers SERDES, audio, RTC, CLKOUT, PLL, SYSCLK, and module clock requirements, including PLL bypass after reset and PLL supply filtering.

Interrupt sections describe ARM Cortex-A8 AINTC support for up to 128 requests and C674x DSP interrupt mapping with default and multiplexed events. Timing and board-design guidance covers AC timing measurement, transition levels, routing delays, monotonic signal transitions, and IBIS model use.

Peripheral summaries include DCAN, EDMA, AET debug, Trace, IEEE 1149.1 JTAG, EMAC Switch, MDIO, GPIO, GPMC/ELM, HDMI, HDVPSS, video DAC, I2C, Imaging Subsystem, and DDR2/DDR3 memory controller. These sections list supported features, register areas, interface modes, timing requirements, electrical characteristics, PCB layout guidance, and references to detailed technical reference manual chapters.

The Power Offense is a basketball set used to free shooters through baseline crosses, down screens, and continuous movement while attacking both sides of the defense. Its basic action has wings cross under the basket, curl off post down screens, and receive passes for shots or create post opportunities if defenders switch. Players must read defensive reactions such as trailing, cheating over screens, switching, showing, or overplaying, and counter with curls, fades, back cuts, screen-and-rolls, slips, post isolations, or drives.

The offense emphasizes offensive rebounding, with inside positioning and weakside rebounders. It includes automatic counters such as fake cross entries, misdirection, back cuts, direct post entries, and dribble drives. If initial actions fail, continuity can flow into motion, side screens, drive-and-kick, or triangle post action. A single/double variation gives a top shooter options off different baseline screens.

Successful implementation depends on execution, timing, screening, post play, defensive recognition, and coordinated communication among ballhandler, screener, and receiver. Coaches should use breakdown drills, individual skill work, scouting, varied entries, and late-clock side screens while preparing players to recognize and attack defensive adjustments.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on June 3, 2015, it entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs International and Mitsubishi UFJ Securities International plc to issue and sell ¥250,000,000,000 of 0.350% Notes due 2020. The notes will be issued under an April 29, 2013 indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A., and related officer’s certificate dated June 10, 2015. Interest is payable semi-annually on June 10 and December 10 beginning December 10, 2015, and the notes mature June 10, 2020. The notes are senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt. Exhibits include the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, form of global note, and Shearman & Sterling LLP opinion and consent.

The message reports Britain’s refusal to submit the Venezuela–British Guiana boundary dispute to arbitration and responds to Britain’s objections to applying the Monroe Doctrine. It argues that the doctrine remains valid, essential to U.S. peace, safety, institutions, and interests, and applies when a European power extends control over territory claimed by an American republic against that republic’s will. The message rejects the claim that the doctrine lacks standing because it is not formally part of international law, asserting that U.S. rights and claims under it deserve recognition.

The United States had proposed arbitration to determine whether Britain was improperly extending its possessions or merely claiming territory within its rightful boundaries. Britain declined, which the message calls disappointing and unsatisfactory. Since Venezuela has not accepted Britain’s current proposal, the message states that the United States must determine the true boundary itself through a careful, evidence-based inquiry.

The President asks Congress to appropriate funds for a commission appointed by the Executive to investigate and report promptly. If the United States determines that territory belongs to Venezuela, the message says it will be the duty of the United States to resist, by every means in its power, British appropriation or jurisdiction over that territory. The message acknowledges the gravity of this course but argues that submission to wrong and injustice would endanger national honor, self-respect, safety, and greatness.

Ruston (La.) traveled to Stephenville (Texas) for a midseason high school football matchup between ranked teams. Ruston entered 4-0 and No. 2 in the Sporting News Louisiana Top 25, while Stephenville entered 5-0 and No. 25 in the Sporting News Texas Top 25. Ruston beat Stephenville 63-17 last year. After both teams opened with three-and-outs, Ruston’s Dalen Powell fumbled at the Bearcats’ 19, and Stephenville quarterback Trot Jordan threw a 19-yard touchdown to Jhett Banuelos for a 7-0 lead.

The October 2025 Supreme Court term begins Oct. 6 with major cases involving presidential power, voting rights, social issues and criminal procedure. Over the summer, the court issued several 6-3 emergency docket rulings allowing Trump administration actions, including removals from federal commissions, termination of NIH grants and ICE stops in Los Angeles, over liberal dissents.

The court will hear challenges to President Trump’s authority to impose tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and to Congress’ ability to limit presidential removal of agency heads. The administration has also asked the court to review Trump’s executive order restricting birthright citizenship, which lower federal courts have found unconstitutional.

The court will rehear a Louisiana redistricting case involving Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act and whether the creation of a second majority-Black congressional district violates the 14th or 15th Amendments. The case could affect disparate impact liability under civil rights laws.

Other cases involve Colorado’s ban on conversion therapy, laws in Idaho and West Virginia barring transgender athletes from teams matching their gender identities, and a Fourth Amendment question about whether police need probable cause to enter a home under the emergency aid exception. The term is expected to produce rulings with significant effects on law and American society.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2015. The company reported Q2 2015 net sales of $23.2 billion, up from $19.3 billion in Q2 2014, with net income of $92 million versus a net loss of $126 million. For the six months ended June 30, 2015, net sales were $45.9 billion, up from $39.1 billion, and net income was $35 million versus a net loss of $18 million.

Q2 2015 operating income was $464 million, compared with an operating loss of $15 million in Q2 2014. Segment results showed North America net sales of $13.8 billion and operating income of $703 million; International net sales of $7.6 billion and operating loss of $19 million; and AWS net sales of $1.8 billion and operating income of $391 million. AWS sales increased 81% year over year in Q2 2015.

Cash and cash equivalents were $10.3 billion at June 30, 2015, compared with $14.6 billion at December 31, 2014. Total assets were $52.4 billion, total liabilities were $40.7 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $11.8 billion. Net cash provided by operating activities was $2.0 billion in Q2 2015 and $498 million for the first six months of 2015. Free cash flow for the trailing twelve months ended June 30, 2015 was $4.4 billion.

The company reported $9.6 billion in total debt face value and no borrowings outstanding under its $2.0 billion revolving credit facility. It completed acquisitions totaling $349 million during the first half of 2015. Amazon also disclosed ongoing legal and tax matters, including patent litigation, a European Commission competition investigation, IRS transfer pricing disputes, French tax assessments, and a European Commission investigation involving Luxembourg tax decisions.

Northeast Mississippi saw several positive developments last week. Karmel Davis, a Parkway Elementary parent and frequent volunteer, was named Tupelo Public School District’s 2017 Parent of the Year. Corey Crayton and her family received a new Habitat for Humanity home funded by HomeStretch Furniture after completing sweat equity requirements. Belden native Noah Barbieri, a Millsaps College junior, was named a Truman Scholar, receiving $30,000 for graduate school and public service leadership development.

After a difficult overtime loss in the finals, the speaker says the team must regroup, stay ready, and play better. They note both goalies performed well, scoring was limited, and future success depends on adjusting without dwelling on missed opportunities.

DHS proposed replacing “duration of status,” which lets international students remain in the U.S. until completing their studies, with a four-year stay limit requiring extensions through USCIS. The rule would also restrict changes of major and institutional transfers. DHS said the change aims to reduce F and J visa overstays, but NAFSA and others argued overstay rates are overestimated and existing systems already monitor students.

More than 15,700 comments were submitted before the Sept. 29 deadline. Many commenters said four years is insufficient for many undergraduate programs, Ph.D.s, architecture degrees, internships, research, and students facing emergencies. They also warned extensions would be costly, slow, uncertain, and burdensome for USCIS and universities.

Higher education leaders, researchers, hospitals, and business commenters said the rule could reduce international enrollment, harm research, disrupt medical training for about 17,000 J-1 physicians, and affect health-care access, especially in underserved areas. Some commenters supported the proposal, saying international students displace Americans. The Council for Christian Colleges and Universities suggested limiting the rule to colleges with admission rates under 30 percent.

AI is raising unresolved questions in drug patent law, including whether AI can be an inventor and how predictive technology affects what inventions are considered obvious to a skilled person. Patent lawyer DeAnn Smith expects these issues to be addressed in future litigation.

This study examined the views of bilingual early childhood teachers in private preschools offering foreign-language education and monolingual teachers in state preschools in Ankara on bilingualism and bilingual education. Using a qualitative phenomenological design, researchers interviewed 16 teachers, 8 bilingual and 8 monolingual, and analyzed the data through content analysis. Five themes emerged: benefits of bilingual education, bilingual children attending monolingual schools, bilingual education programs, issues in bilingual education, and the impact of bilingualism on children’s development.

Teachers generally viewed bilingualism as an advantage, citing benefits for career prospects, self-confidence, communication skills, cultural awareness, and cognitive development. Many believed bilingual children in monolingual schools risk losing one language, though some monolingual teachers saw monolingual schooling as helpful for strengthening the dominant community language. Teachers showed limited knowledge of bilingual education program models but emphasized the need for staff proficient in both languages, appropriate bilingual materials, and supportive environments. Reported challenges included insufficient qualified personnel, limited resources, children’s language gaps, family-related issues, and program implementation problems. The study concludes that bilingual education should be expanded in Türkiye, with stronger teacher training, better resources, parental support, and clearer program standards.

This review examined lung cancer screening methods, focusing on biomarkers for early detection. A PubMed search for “biomarkers for early diagnosis of lung cancer” was filtered to clinical research from the past 10 years, with final included articles assessed for screening method, lung cancer type, biomarkers, demographics, sensitivity, specificity, and related findings.

The review found several potential biomarkers and screening approaches. Volatile organic compounds had 80% sensitivity and 80% specificity. Circulating tumor DNA had 80% sensitivity and 96% specificity. Four miRNA molecules showed high sensitivities of 93–96% but low specificities of 23–33%. Methylation markers in sputum and serum varied widely in sensitivity and specificity. Ga-Alfatide II PET/CT scans had about 86% sensitivity and 85% specificity. Combined score analysis and WT-IDH showed limitations as screening methods.

The authors identified circulating tumor DNA and Ga-Alfatide II PET/CT scans as the most promising screening tools due to their higher sensitivity and specificity. They conclude that improved screening, along with further study of immunotherapy, chemotherapy, therapeutic response rates, and combination treatments, may help increase early detection and reduce lung cancer mortality.

The study compared three surveys on primary care physicians’ electronic health record (EHR) use and interoperability: the 2021 National Electronic Health Records Survey, the 2022 American Board of Family Medicine Continuous Certification Questionnaire, and the 2022 UCSF Physician Health IT Survey. The surveys used different sampling and response strategies, with response rates of 18.2%, 100%, and 3.6%, respectively.

Respondent characteristics differed substantially across surveys by age, practice setting, practice size, geography, and EHR vendor. Despite these differences, all surveys showed limited physician satisfaction with EHRs, substantial after-hours documentation, and ongoing interoperability problems. About one quarter of physicians were very satisfied with their EHRs, about three-quarters reported at least one hour of after-work documentation daily, and only about 20% reported often having outside clinical information available. Epic users generally reported better experiences, while private practice physicians reported less availability of external information.

Many survey responses differed statistically, suggesting that findings may vary depending on the data source used. The authors conclude that while the surveys support similar broad conclusions, differences in respondent composition and response methods affect detailed results. They suggest supplementing NEHRS with data from mandatory certification surveys, while noting limitations including question differences and the CCQ’s focus on family physicians.

A multicentre randomised controlled trial evaluated PrAISED, a 12-month dementia-specific exercise and functional activity rehabilitation programme for people over 65 with mild dementia or mild cognitive impairment. The intervention was tailored, home-based, involved carers, and focused on strength, balance, daily activities, risk enablement and community participation. It was compared with falls prevention assessment and advice.

A total of 365 patient-carer pairs were randomised. Despite reasonable adherence and positive reception by participants, carers and therapists, PrAISED did not improve activities of daily living, physical activity, quality of life, balance, functional mobility, cognition or other main health outcomes at 12 months. Falls rates may have been slightly lower, but this was statistically uncertain and did not translate into functional benefit. Some underpowered cognitive measures suggested possible benefits in specific domains.

The trial was disrupted by COVID-19, requiring remote delivery and assessment for some participants, but sensitivity analyses did not suggest different results. The authors conclude that exercise or functionally oriented rehabilitation is unlikely to change the rate of ability loss in dementia and that future support should focus more on living well, practical problem-solving, supported functioning, personhood, inclusion, emotional support and carers.

On August 17, ISS Expedition 52 Commander Fyodor Yurchikhin and Flight Engineer Sergey Ryazanskiy will conduct a spacewalk from the Pirs airlock, broadcast on NASA TV. Tasks include deploying five nanosatellites, collecting residue samples, and installing handrails and struts. The satellites have purposes including testing 3-D printed materials in orbit and commemorating Sputnik 1 and Konstantin Tsiolkovsky. It will be the 202nd ISS assembly and maintenance spacewalk.

Stenabolic (SR9009) is described as an oral synthetic Rev-ErbA ligand developed by the Scripps Research Institute under Thomas Burris. The passage claims it activates Rev-Erb proteins, influencing circadian rhythms, metabolism, fat storage, and macrophages. It says SR9009 may increase mitochondria in muscles, improve endurance and strength, raise resting energy expenditure, reduce fat storage, and lower several blood markers including cholesterol, glucose, insulin, and inflammatory cytokine IL-6.

The Pocatello-Chubbuck School District will use three focus groups to provide input on proposed high school boundary changes. Meetings will be public, with timelines posted online. Trustees delayed a decision last month to gather more feedback after ending two decades of open high school choice due to enrollment and socioeconomic disparities.

Steven Gittens, proceeding pro se, sued Garlock Sealing Technologies alleging disability discrimination under the ADA. Garlock moved for summary judgment, and despite court orders and warnings that failure to respond could lead to dismissal, Gittens filed no opposition, requested no extension, and made no contact with the court or defense counsel.

The court granted Garlock’s motion and dismissed the complaint with prejudice under Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 41(b), 16(f), and 56. It found dismissal warranted because Gittens failed to prosecute the case, disobeyed court scheduling orders, and failed to identify any genuine issue of material fact.

On the ADA claim, the court held that Gittens failed to establish he was disabled within the meaning of the statute. His alleged impairment was a lower spine injury resulting in a 25–30 pound lifting restriction. The court found this did not substantially limit a major life activity or employment generally, especially because inability to perform a single job does not constitute a disability under the ADA and Gittens had worked in other positions. The court also found Garlock had offered legitimate, nondiscriminatory reasons for reassigning him, with no evidence of pretext or discriminatory motive.

The passage argues for swift justice under law rather than mob lynching, warning that inflammatory speech can provoke mobs, intensify racial hatred, and encourage further crime. It emphasizes public education, including industrial training at schools such as Hampton and Tuskegee, as beneficial to Black citizens, white neighbors, and social relations. It also criticizes demagogues who inflame class hatred against the wealthy, saying they harm genuine reform, foster corruption and disorder, and provoke reaction. The passage calls for firm, sane reform that rejects both agitators who exploit popular passions and wealthy individuals who exploit others for profit.

Linux Foundation news highlights included Jim Zemlin citing Linux’s use in high-performance computing, stock exchanges, and mobile devices; Hart joining as a Gold member; a free open source software basics publication; and Cloud Native Computing Foundation announcing 11 new members.

The passage includes a U.S. passport application and oath template requiring allegiance to the United States, applicant description, and supporting affidavits. It then presents a 1902 U.S. legation report from Buenos Aires transmitting extracts from Argentine President Julio A. Roca’s message to Congress. The report notes public disappointment that the message was not explicit on international relations or finances, especially negotiations mediated by Britain for limiting armaments between Argentina and Chile. It describes heavy military and naval spending, debt, deficits, taxation burdens, and economic strain in both countries, concluding that both recognized the need to halt costly expenditures.

The author argues against owning Snap stock short term, citing competition from Facebook’s Instagram and Microsoft’s Skype, falling app downloads, low marketer adoption, and weak quarterly results. Snap reported $150 million in revenue, a $2.31 per-share loss, and 166 million daily active users, all below expectations. The upcoming IPO lock-up expiration could make 1.2 billion additional shares available, potentially pressuring the stock. The author expects volatility, views shorting as risky due to high short interest and expensive puts, and makes no trade recommendation.

The United States Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Indiana considered confirmation of Jeffery and Paulette Smith’s amended Chapter 13 plan after the standing trustee objected. The trustee argued that the plan unfairly favored Chrysler Financial over NBD Bank, lacked good faith, and failed to devote all disposable income to creditor payments.

The debtors proposed to pay Chrysler’s full $20,800 claim on a recently purchased 1997 Dodge Stratus, while paying NBD Bank only the replacement value of another vehicle and providing up to a 10% dividend to unsecured creditors. The court found the different treatment permissible because the debtors bought the Stratus shortly before filing bankruptcy, had made no payments to Chrysler, and proposed full payment to avoid unfairness to Chrysler. However, the court reduced Chrysler’s interest rate from the proposed 8% to the 3.9% contract rate.

The court found the amended plan was proposed in good faith. It accepted the debtors’ explanations regarding their income projections, omission and later correction of insurance cash values, and Mrs. Smith’s decision to defer profit-sharing benefits into a qualified plan rather than take a taxable cash distribution.

On disposable income, the court required additional protections for creditors. The debtors must provide paycheck stubs and year-to-date earnings every six months, increase plan payments by any net overtime income above projections, and raise monthly plan payments by $75, from $1,733.33 to $1,808.33. The court held that Mrs. Smith’s ERISA-qualified profit-sharing benefits are not disposable income unless received as cash, but any net cash distribution during the plan must be paid to creditors. Voluntary retirement or 401(k) contributions from the debtors’ income must cease during the plan.

The trustee’s objection was granted in part and denied in part, and the amended Chapter 13 plan was confirmed as modified.

Safety endpoints at 24 and 48 weeks were similar between groups. Before Week 24, adverse events occurred in 51.2% of Primary SOC and 52.0% of Additional Educational Program subjects; serious adverse events occurred in 12.4% and 14.7%, respectively. Between Weeks 24 and 48, adverse events occurred in 33.8% of Primary SOC, 40.8% of Secondary SOC, and 38.6% of Continued Additional Educational Program subjects. Overall, 24 deaths were reported, with no pregnancies or clinically concerning hepatic or renal laboratory signals. The educational program did not improve adherence or persistence.

The passage describes using the “Single/Double” offense to attack a Triangle & Two defense by freeing shooters with screens against strong pass-denial chasers. The offense relies on shooter communication, single and double screen options, base screens, side screens, post seals, rolls, kick-out passes, and counters to defensive overplays or help rotations. Successful implementation requires coordinated execution, defensive recognition, timing, non-verbal communication, strong post play, and practice through breakdown drills and scrimmaging. Game strategy includes scouting defensive tendencies, recognizing adjustments, varying alignments and entries, and attacking weak defenders. The Triangle & Two defense is defined as three players in a triangle zone with two chasers aggressively denying specific opponents the ball.
Microstructures may explain why dandelion seeds resist dislodging until better breezes.

The study examines Greek primary teachers’ views on STEM education and the conditions needed for its effective implementation. STEM education is presented as an interdisciplinary, inquiry-based approach connected to real-life problem solving, scientific practices, collaboration, critical thinking, and active learning. The literature review highlights generally positive student and teacher attitudes toward STEM internationally, while also identifying common barriers such as insufficient teacher preparation, limited time, lack of resources, and inadequate infrastructure.

The research involved 114 primary teachers in public schools in Attica, Greece, using a questionnaire and 27 structured interviews. Most teachers considered the development of students’ scientific thinking very or extremely important, mainly because it supports everyday problem solving, inquiry, critical thinking, cooperation, and knowledge acquisition. Teachers valued STEM practices such as problem solving, group work, experimentation, measurement, data interpretation, explanation, and communication of results, but reported that students rarely have opportunities to practice them in class.

Teachers reported greater confidence in teaching mathematics than science, while expressing insecurity about STEM implementation, especially due to lack of equipment, training, and guidance. They identified STEM’s main advantages as experiential and interdisciplinary learning, connection with daily life, use of scientific methodology and technology, teamwork, inquiry, creativity, active participation, and critical thinking. They also viewed STEM as potentially reducing educational inequalities by engaging students with different abilities and backgrounds.

The main weaknesses identified were lack of teacher training and educational material, insufficient infrastructure and equipment, limited teaching time, and unclear placement of STEM in the curriculum. Teachers requested practical training, teaching materials, sample lessons, ongoing support, better school infrastructure, more time, and collaboration with colleagues. The study concludes that Greek teachers are generally willing to implement STEM education but need systematic support, resources, training, and curricular adjustments for effective implementation.

A Korea Institute for Health and Social Affairs report said South Korea’s fertility rate fell sharply in the mid-1980s as married women’s education levels rose. The rate dropped from 2.1 in 1984 to 1.6 in 1987. The report linked women’s marriage and birth patterns to education, noting increased labor force participation and a 2015 fertility rate of 1.24.

Amsterdam archaeologists uncovered about 700,000 discarded objects while excavating the Amstel riverbed for the “Below the Surface” project, part of construction of a nearly 5-mile subway line. The finds, ranging from Neolithic stone axes to cellphones, document centuries of urban life and waste disposal along the river. Items include pots, coins, combs, utensils, keys, dolls, pipes, weapons, dentures, cameras and documents, with many preserved in mud and silt. A selection of 10,000 objects will be displayed at Rokin station, while about 30,000 are available in an online interactive database. The project also produced a catalog, “Stuff,” distributed to Amsterdam schools, and cost 6 million euros.

The goalie described making a key save after an initial breakaway stop and scramble, calling it a big play. He said playoff runs are emotional and require staying even keel, and noted the last two games were important for both the team and his confidence. He reflected on facing different scoring chances, including one he wished he handled differently. He also praised Nashville as his longtime home, highlighting the city’s hockey growth, passionate fans, and the special atmosphere during the finals. Timely saves, he said, boost confidence and help the game feel slower.

Concomitant medications and current diabetes treatments will be coded using WHODrug Global March 2018, mapped to ATC classes and preferred names, listed as recorded, and summarized by treatment using ATC level 2 and preferred name. Prior medications stop before first IMP administration; concomitant medications are ongoing at, stop on, or start after first study drug intake. Unclear cases are considered concomitant.

Primary efficacy analysis uses the FAS, with supportive PPS sensitivity analyses. The primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery, defined as the first plasma glucose increase of ≥20 mg/dL from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose. Secondary endpoints include glucose recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes, and glucose changes from baseline at those time points or rescue. Baseline is the last non-missing pre-dose value. Primary models adjust for age group and injection site. Missing data are not imputed, and no interim analyses are planned.

Dasiglucagon 0.6 mg will be compared with placebo using a hierarchical testing procedure at a two-sided 0.05 level. GlucaGen comparisons support study validity but are not part of the hierarchy. Time to recovery will be summarized using Kaplan-Meier methods and compared with a stratified log-rank test; rescue IV glucose before recovery is handled as not recovered and censored at 45 minutes in the primary analysis. Sensitivity analyses examine alternative censoring approaches. Supportive analyses include stratified Wilcoxon tests, Cox proportional hazards models, homogeneity models, histograms, and linear interpolation of recovery time.

Secondary recovery rates will be analyzed using Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests stratified by age group and injection site, with Fisher tests if needed. Glucose changes from baseline will be analyzed using ANOVA with treatment, age group, and injection site.

Pharmacokinetic analyses will describe dasiglucagon and glucagon concentrations and calculate PK metrics using Phoenix WinNonlin. Plasma samples are collected pre-dose and up to 300 minutes post-dose. Concentration handling rules define treatment of pre-dose, post-dose, LLOQ, and missing values. Pharmacodynamic plasma glucose is collected pre-dose and up to 45 or 60 minutes; AUE0-30min is the PD endpoint.

Safety analyses use the safety set. Exposure summaries include insulin use, hypoglycemia induction, trial medication administration, and rescue glucose infusion. Local tolerability is assessed at 30, 120, and 300 minutes and follow-up. Adverse events are coded with MedDRA and summarized mainly as TEAEs by treatment group, including AESIs, injection site reactions, study drug-related events, SAEs, deaths, causality, and severity. Laboratory data, vital signs, ECGs, pregnancy tests, alcohol breath tests, physical exams, and immunogenicity are summarized or listed as specified.

The SAP adds sensitivity and supportive analyses for the primary endpoint and changes some secondary efficacy terminology. Appendices specify table, figure, listing formatting, missing date handling, calculation formulas, SAS programming QC requirements, and planned outputs.

The ScottishPower Foundation has donated £95,220 to Sussex Wildlife Trust’s education programme during Woods Mill’s 50-year celebrations. The funding will enable 1,300 more people to attend events, support ten wildlife identification courses, train 250 wildlife champions, create a young naturalists club, improve habitats and paths, and install a kestrel nest box camera. Foundation trustees visited Woods Mill, which opened to the public in 1968, and observed activities with local schoolchildren.

The lecture continues the proof strategy for Freiman’s theorem. From Ruzsa’s modeling lemma, a large subset of a small-doubling set can be Freiman 8-isomorphic to a subset of a small cyclic group. The next goal is to extract additive structure from dense subsets of such groups.

In the finite field model \( \mathbb{F}_2^n \), a dense set \(A\) need not have \(A+A\) containing a bounded-codimension subspace; Hamming ball examples show this can fail. Bogolyubov’s lemma resolves this after more additions: if \(A\subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n\) has density \(\alpha\), then \(2A-2A\) contains a subspace of codimension less than \(1/\alpha^2\). The proof uses convolution, Fourier inversion, Parseval’s identity, and the fact that large Fourier coefficients are few.

The cyclic group version replaces subspaces with Bohr sets. For \(A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}\) of density \(\alpha\), \(2A-2A\) contains a Bohr set of width \(1/4\) and dimension less than \(1/\alpha^2\). The proof parallels the finite field argument using the Fourier transform on \(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}\).

The lecture then introduces geometry of numbers to show that Bohr sets contain large generalized arithmetic progressions. It defines lattices, determinants, centrally symmetric convex bodies, successive minima, and states Minkowski’s second theorem. Applying this theorem to a lattice associated with a Bohr set shows that every Bohr set of dimension \(d\) and width \(\epsilon\) in \(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}\) contains a proper generalized arithmetic progression of dimension at most \(d\) and size at least \((\epsilon/d)^d n\). These ingredients will be used next to complete Freiman’s theorem, with Ruzsa’s covering lemma handling the passage from a large subset back to the whole set.

Japanese universities lagged behind in ICT use before COVID-19 due to traditional views of face-to-face education, few adult undergraduates, and limits on distance-learning credits. The pandemic forced a rapid shift to online classes, prompting MEXT to temporarily relax credit limits, support digitalization projects, and later encourage a return to face-to-face teaching while preserving some remote-learning provisions.

Before the pandemic, faculty use of ICT was limited mainly to tools such as PowerPoint, while LMS and file-sharing tools were less used. During the pandemic, hybrid, high-flex, and online classes expanded rapidly, but challenges included weak communication, difficulty teaching practical skills, limited student support, group-work problems, and faculty computer-literacy gaps. Some universities shared online examples of good distance-learning practices.

For students, digitalization highlighted Japan’s longstanding issue of “substantiation of the credit system,” in which required study hours outside class are often not met. Online classes using LMS and assignments increased out-of-class learning time, but also increased student workload. Further improvement requires attention to course loads, curriculum management, teaching practices, and educational culture.

Lifelong learning in Japanese higher education remains weakly institutionalized. University distance learning has served many adult learners and had some digitalization before the pandemic, but it remained marginal to mainstream commuter programs. Non-degree programs such as public lectures are rarely digitalized, while newer vocational and certificate programs are more likely to use online formats.

The passage concludes that COVID-19 accelerated university digitalization in Japan and created opportunities for education reform and adult learning, but unresolved issues include educational culture, institutional structures, lifelong-learning capacity, and protection of student personal information as government and private-sector use of educational data expands.

The study developed and tested an online version of the SInQUE social inclusion assessment tool for use in mental health supported accommodation services. The tool is designed for staff and service users to complete collaboratively during care planning, generating scores and priority areas for improving social inclusion.

The study had two stages in one inner London borough: lab-testing with six staff members using think-aloud interviews, followed by five months of field-testing with interviews involving 12 staff and 12 service users. The tool was also made available in two other areas without an implementation strategy. Minor changes were made after testing, including clearer wording, added guidance, improved score summaries, and informational materials.

Staff and service users generally found the online SInQUE acceptable, user-friendly, relevant, quick to complete, and useful for prompting conversations, identifying priorities, supporting care planning, and monitoring change over time. Some staff worried that certain questions might feel intrusive, but service users generally did not share this concern. Uptake was highest in supported housing and lower in residential care and floating outreach services.

Use of the tool occurred mainly where an implementation strategy was provided. In the participating borough, 27 staff registered, 17 staff used the tool with at least one service user, and 30 completed assessments were recorded for 28 service users, representing just over 10% of supported accommodation service users in the borough. In areas without implementation support, no assessments were completed.

The authors concluded that the online SInQUE is a potentially useful and acceptable tool for supported accommodation settings, especially supported housing, but active leadership and implementation support are needed to promote use. Further research is needed to assess longer-term uptake, outcomes, use in other service types, and barriers among staff and service users who did not use the tool.

The passage describes NVIDIA A100 GPU architecture improvements over V100, focusing on Tensor Core efficiency, memory hierarchy, multi-tenancy, interconnects, CUDA features, and DGX A100 systems.

A100’s third-generation Tensor Cores improve data sharing across all 32 warp threads, reduce register file bandwidth and redundant shared-memory loads, increase matrix multiply instruction dimensions, issue fewer instructions, and reduce register accesses. The architecture adds asynchronous global-to-shared memory copy, asynchronous barriers, larger shared memory per SM, a 40 MB L2 cache, improved cache residency controls, and Compute Data Compression. A100 also provides higher HBM2 memory bandwidth, greater L2 read bandwidth, and improved data reuse for workloads such as deep learning training, inference, LSTMs, and producer-consumer chains.

The Multi-Instance GPU feature can partition one A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute and memory resources, enabling predictable throughput, latency, quality of service, and fault isolation for VMs, containers, processes, and multi-tenant cloud environments. MIG includes GPU slices, Sys Pipes, GPU Memory slices, and Compute Instances, and supports Volta-style MPS within Compute Instances. MIG also enables migration of vGPUs between GPU Instances or GPUs for load balancing, consolidation, servicing, and reduced fragmentation.

A100 includes third-generation NVLink with twelve links, 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, improved error handling, and support for NVSwitch-based systems such as DGX A100. It supports PCIe Gen 4 with 31.5 GB/sec per direction for x16 connections and SR-IOV virtualization. The architecture also improves error and fault detection, attribution, isolation, and containment, especially for MIG and NVLink-connected clusters.

Additional A100 features include hardware JPEG decode through NVJPG, an Optical Flow Accelerator, higher atomic operation throughput, and five NVDEC video decode units. CUDA 11 supports Ampere features including Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 residency controls, and Cooperative Groups enhancements. CUDA Graphs reduce repeated CPU submission overhead and improve launch and dependency execution latency. L2 residency controls allow persistent data regions to remain in cache, with examples showing speedups for histogram workloads.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs connected by third-generation NVLink and NVSwitch, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS in a 6U system, up to 56 isolated GPU Instances through MIG, and support for large-scale AI infrastructure using Mellanox networking, Magnum IO, NGC containers, CUDA, and Kubernetes or Slurm environments. The appendix explains sparse neural networks, pruning, fine-grained and coarse-grained sparsity, and A100’s fine-grained structured sparsity, which aims to improve compute efficiency while maintaining balanced workloads and minimal accuracy loss in evaluated networks.

Steven Kean forwarded Jeffrey McMahon a set of July 13, 2001 “Enron Mentions,” noting the last attached story and congratulating him for “shaking things up.”

The items include: Wisconsin Gas agreeing to buy a nine-mile high-pressure pipeline from Enron subsidiary Northern Natural Gas for $5 million, subject to regulatory approval; Dow Jones reports that LME copper prices fell amid rising warehouse stocks, with unconfirmed market talk linking Enron to much of the stock increase, which Enron declined to comment on; a Reuters report noting Enron sold its 40-million-share stake in Paladin Resources through HSBC; and a Bloomberg report on the debut of a Nymex low-sulfur coal futures contract, which Enron and Duke Energy had said they would trade.

The final Modern Metals article examines Enron’s push into steel markets under Jeff McMahon and Enron Industrial Markets. It says Enron is offering forward contracts and hedging products for steel, arguing that a transparent market could reduce price volatility and improve investment decisions. Industry reaction is mixed: some service center executives see possible benefits in hedging and enforceable contracts, while others criticize Enron as an intermediary seeking profit. Mill executives question whether Enron’s pricing would help the industry, and several sources raise concerns about inventory control, delivery, product specifications, and whether Enron could become a physical supplier or competitor.

The speaker bids farewell to Cabinet members, White House staff, and friends, asking them to serve the next President with the same devotion shown to him and previous Presidents. He praises the White House as “the best house” because of the people who serve there, expresses pride in his Administration, and says that while mistakes were made, no one profited at public expense. He emphasizes government service as a cause greater than money, tied to national strength, peace, and leadership. Reflecting on his parents and Theodore Roosevelt’s resilience after personal loss, he urges perseverance through defeat, sadness, and disappointment. He thanks those who served, encourages them to remain proud and dedicated, and says they will remain in his heart and prayers.

Dalhousie researcher Nancy McLean says native bees on P.E.I. blueberry fields may provide enough pollination without imported honey bees. Her Environment Canada-funded research found native bees make up over half the bees on blueberry flowers, are more efficient, suited to the climate, and can buzz pollinate. She encourages farmers to support native bees by planting preferred plants near fields, noting honey bees are costly, scarce, and may carry parasites.

Siddharth Agrawal manages Silkasia, a family garment and home textile export business with operations across India. He is also involved in native cow breed research, satellite dairy farms, urban rooftop farming, start-up investment and mentoring. He co-created Mayori and holds roles in EO Jaipur, YPO Rajasthan, RAIN and TIE Rajasthan.

Michael Dell said the AI infrastructure boom is still strong, driven by customers’ heavy demand for computing power and immediate deployment of data-center equipment. He said power availability, not lack of demand, is limiting some customers. Dell Technologies’ server-networking business grew 58% last year, and the company raised its revenue and earnings growth forecasts. Its stock has risen sharply alongside other AI infrastructure companies such as Oracle and AMD. While some market observers, including the Bank of England’s Financial Policy Committee, warn that AI-related equity valuations may be stretched, Dell said he sees no signs yet of too many data centers being built.

Vladimir Putin was declared winner of Russia’s presidential election with more than three-quarters of the vote, securing a fourth six-year term. Critics called the vote staged and predetermined. NPR’s Lucian Kim reported that turnout was encouraged through patriotic messaging tied to the anniversary of Crimea’s annexation. Putin’s campaign narrative emphasized Russia’s resilience under Western sanctions and portrayed accusations over the poisoning of a former Russian spy and election meddling as part of an anti-Russian campaign. Opposition figures reported pressure on voters, harassment of monitors, ballot stuffing, and some violence, but remained divided. Putin said he had no current plans to change the constitution.

An Enron media summary from Nov. 17–18, 2001, compiles articles on Enron’s financial collapse, accounting issues, falling stock price, SEC investigation, pension fund concerns, executive stock sales, and planned acquisition by Dynegy. Reports note Kenneth Lay declined a $60.6 million severance package, Enron restated four years of earnings by $586 million, and investors awaited a third-quarter SEC filing for details on liabilities, partnerships, debt, job cuts, and the Dynegy deal.

Several items discuss Dynegy’s proposed acquisition, related financing, and risks, including Enron’s $550 million loan secured by pipeline assets, Dynegy’s rights to acquire Northern Natural Gas if the merger fails, and energy traders limiting exposure in case Dynegy withdraws. Other reports cover possible sales of Enron assets such as Wessex Water and stakes in UK energy assets, with WestLB and other potential buyers mentioned.

The compilation also includes broader market and investing articles on stock rallies, bond declines, energy stock outlooks, diversification, executive compensation, and market irrationality, frequently citing Enron as an example of accounting opacity, concentrated investment risk, and corporate governance concerns.

The Dark Cloud Cover is a bearish reversal candlestick pattern that appears after an upswing. It consists of a bullish candle followed by a bearish candle that opens above the previous close and closes below the previous candle’s midpoint, suggesting a possible shift from bullish to bearish sentiment. Traders may use it to short sell or close long positions, especially during rallies in bearish markets, but it is not a guaranteed reversal signal. Confirmation may come from later price action, resistance levels, Moving Averages, MACD, RSI, market news, or fundamental analysis. The strategy can be applied across asset markets and timeframes, though shorter timeframes may create more false signals and longer ones may miss opportunities. Backtesting, clear rules, stop-losses, and risk management are recommended.

The document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) so guest operating systems can interoperate with hypervisors supporting SEV-ES or SEV-SNP. It defines required Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs), minimum guest state exposed through the GHCB, and special guest actions such as NMI handling and SMP booting.

The GHCB is a 4 KB decrypted page used for guest-hypervisor communication. Its layout mirrors parts of the SEV-ES VMCB save state area, but only required fields are exposed to limit guest state visibility. SEV-SNP introduces GHCB protocol version 2, which adds hypervisor feature advertisement, initial SEV-SNP support, XSS MSR reporting for CPUID 0xd, restricted APIC emulation support, and requirements for shared areas referenced by SW_SCRATCH. Later revisions add sequence number changes, new VMGEXIT error handling, VLEK GUID support, APIC ID list retrieval, multi-VMPL support, SEV-ES page state changes, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, and clarified unsupported protocol behavior.

Version 2 introduces a FEATURES bitmap, limited to 52 bits for GHCB MSR protocol return, allowing the hypervisor to advertise optional capabilities such as base SEV-SNP support, AP VMSA creation, restricted injection, APIC ID listing, multi-VMPL operation, SEV-ES page state change, trusted I/O, and GHCB unregister support. GHCB addresses are guest-selected, page-aligned, saved in the VMCB, and accessible through MSR 0xc001_0130, which the hypervisor must not intercept.

The GHCB MSR protocol uses the low 12 bits of the GHCB MSR for guest requests and hypervisor responses, including SEV information, CPUID requests, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration and unregistration, page state changes, VMPL switching, hypervisor feature requests, and guest termination. SEV-SNP guests must register a GHCB GPA before first use; registration replaces any prior registration, and unregistration may be requested if supported.

The document gives example GHCB negotiation flows for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests, including protocol version negotiation, encryption bit discovery, GHCB allocation, page sharing, and GHCB GPA registration. It also describes standard VMGEXIT handling: the guest populates GHCB fields and VALID_BITMAP entries, issues VMGEXIT, and the hypervisor processes SW_EXITCODE and returns state or errors through SW_EXITINFO fields.

NAE handling requires guests to handle #VC exceptions for supported events and hypervisors to handle VMGEXIT requests for listed events. Standard processing includes copying required state to the GHCB, setting valid bits, issuing VMGEXIT, and processing returned state or error requests. Special handling is described for I/O, MSR accesses, VMMCALL, MMIO, page state changes, SNP guest requests, extended guest requests, AP creation, restricted injection doorbell pages, IPIs, timers, APIC ID lists, VMPL switching, SNP TIO guest requests, Secure AVIC backing pages, termination requests, and unsupported exits.

The specification also defines SEV-SNP secrets page guest-reserved fields, an EFI Confidential Computing Blob protocol for communicating the SEV-SNP secrets and CPUID pages, requirements for guest identification of SEV-ES support through CPUID, SMP booting limitations and alternatives, AP creation under SEV-SNP, NMI completion signaling, hardware debug register virtualization behavior, and unsupported SMM and nested virtualization.

For restricted injection, the document defines a shared #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. It specifies host and guest behavior for interrupt presentation, acknowledgement, EOI optimization, non-maskable events, HLT handling, and validation of delivered vectors.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2016. Net sales were $78.4 billion, up 3% from $75.9 billion a year earlier, while net income was $17.9 billion, down from $18.4 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $3.36, up from $3.28, and cash dividends declared per share were $0.57.

Gross margin was $30.2 billion, or 38.5% of net sales, compared with 40.1% a year earlier. Operating income was $23.4 billion, down from $24.2 billion. Research and development expense rose to $2.9 billion, and selling, general and administrative expense rose to $3.9 billion. Other income, net, increased to $821 million.

By product, iPhone net sales rose 5% to $54.4 billion, iPad net sales fell 22% to $5.5 billion, Mac net sales rose 7% to $7.2 billion, Services net sales rose 18% to $7.2 billion, and Other Products net sales fell 8% to $4.0 billion. By segment, net sales increased in the Americas, Europe, Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific, but declined 12% in Greater China.

As of December 31, 2016, Apple had total assets of $331.1 billion, total liabilities of $198.8 billion and shareholders’ equity of $132.4 billion. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $246.1 billion, including $230.2 billion held by foreign subsidiaries. Total term debt was $77.1 billion, and commercial paper outstanding was $10.5 billion.

Operating activities generated $27.1 billion in cash during the quarter. Investing activities used $19.1 billion, mainly for marketable securities and property, plant and equipment. Financing activities used $12.0 billion, mainly for share repurchases and dividends.

Apple repurchased $10.9 billion of common stock during the quarter and paid $3.1 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents. As of December 31, 2016, $144 billion of its $175 billion share repurchase authorization had been used. The company expected to complete its capital return program by the end of March 2018.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2015. As of October 29, 2015, it had 130,951,319 common shares outstanding. Tesla designs, develops, manufactures and sells fully electric vehicles, powertrain components and Tesla Energy products, with subsidiaries in North America, Europe and Asia.

For the quarter ended September 30, 2015, Tesla reported total revenue of $936.8 million, up from $851.8 million a year earlier, driven primarily by growth in Model S deliveries. Gross profit was $231.5 million, and gross margin fell to 24.7% from 29.6%. Net loss was $229.9 million, compared with $74.7 million in the prior-year quarter. For the nine months ended September 30, 2015, revenue was $2.83 billion and net loss was $568.3 million.

As of September 30, 2015, Tesla had $7.55 billion in total assets, $6.19 billion in total liabilities and $1.31 billion in stockholders’ equity. Cash and cash equivalents were $1.43 billion, down from $1.91 billion at December 31, 2014. Inventory increased to $1.29 billion, and property, plant and equipment rose to $3.10 billion. Customer deposits totaled $269.5 million.

Tesla completed an August 2015 common stock offering, selling 3,099,173 shares for about $738.3 million in net proceeds. For the first nine months of 2015, operating activities used $494.7 million in cash, investing activities used $1.26 billion, and financing activities provided $1.30 billion.

Tesla began customer deliveries of Model X in September 2015 and was ramping production. It had delivered almost 90,000 vehicles through September 30, 2015. The company planned to unveil Model 3 in the first quarter of 2016, with first deliveries planned for late 2017. Tesla also began production and deliveries of Tesla Energy products in the third quarter of 2015 and transitioned production to the Gigafactory during the fourth quarter. Tesla projected 50,000 to 52,000 vehicle deliveries for 2015 and expected 2015 capital expenditures of about $1.7 billion.
Alabama voters decide a special Senate race between Democrat Doug Jones and Republican Roy Moore, who denies sexual misconduct allegations involving teenage girls and has largely avoided campaigning.

The passage introduces an analysis of AGN variability in Fairall 9 using ∼1000 days of Swift monitoring data, focusing on the connection between the UV-emitting disc and X-ray corona. Standard thin-disc reverberation models struggle to explain AGN variability because observed optical/UV changes occur too quickly, lags are often longer than predicted, and X-ray/UV correlations are weak.

The authors divide Fairall 9’s light curves into segments and model time-averaged SEDs with a warm Comptonising disc, hot X-ray corona, and reflection component. They find a clear SED evolution: the optical/UV disc brightens substantially between the first and later segments, consistent with an increased mass-accretion rate, while the integrated X-ray power remains roughly constant but softens, likely due to increased disc seed photons cooling the corona.

Using Gaussian Process regression, they generate evenly sampled UVW2 and hard X-ray light curves and compute Fourier-resolved power spectra, phase lags, and coherence. The UV variability is dominated by low frequencies, while the X-rays show flatter power spectra. The UV–X-ray lag behaviour changes across the campaign: including a sharp UV rise produces a coherent low-frequency UV lead, while later segments show weaker or absent coherence and different lag behaviour.

The authors develop a simplified analytic model in which observed UV and X-ray variability arise from intrinsic disc and corona fluctuations, disc reverberation, wind/BLR reprocessing, and disc seed photons entering the corona. They argue that later segments can be consistent with the same underlying model, with low coherence caused by interference between intrinsic disc and coronal variability. The sharp rising phase likely reflects a structural change in the accretion flow associated with increased mass accretion.

The passage concludes that Fairall 9’s variability is more complex than standard reverberation predicts, that its inner accretion structure may evolve on observable timescales, and that future timing analyses should account for possible SED and structural evolution when interpreting AGN variability.

Manny has remained around the team during his injury, contributing leadership on and off the ice, and his possible return would be an emotional boost. The speaker also says teammates can tell him and his brother apart, though coaches may struggle.

Thousands of Armenian-Americans marched in Los Angeles to commemorate the estimated 1.5 million Armenians who died under the Ottoman Empire starting in 1915 and to demand Turkey recognize the deaths as genocide. Turkey disputes that characterization. The demonstrations occurred hours after Armenian Prime Minister Serzh Sargsyan resigned following anti-government protests. Marchers carried flags and signs, shared family connections to the killings, and emphasized remembrance and recognition. Kim Kardashian West praised global Armenian demonstrations.
The speaker says joking keeps players relaxed, even after missed shots, but emphasizes they must win one game at a time.

The Jonathan Hunt Chapter of the Daughters of the American Revolution honored Good Citizens scholarship participants from eight high schools, recognizing their citizenship qualities, essays, and achievements at a tea in Elkin.

The passage is a STAT webpage excerpt for D.C. Diagnosis, a twice-weekly newsletter by Washington correspondent John Wilkerson on health care politics and policy, with subscription prompts and headlines on federal health policy, biotech, drug regulation, women’s health, ACA subsidies, and government shutdown negotiations.

The passage examines polar metals, focusing on distortive polar metals (DPMs), where polarity and metallic conductivity coexist after a centrosymmetry-lifting structural transition. It studies Mn5Al8 as a metallic DPM and reports that off-stoichiometric Mn51Al49 undergoes a first-order cubic γ-brass to rhombohedral γ2 transition near 880°C. X-ray diffraction confirms the low-temperature polar R3m structure, while resistivity measurements and density-functional-theory calculations confirm metallic behavior.

The γ → γ2 martensitic transformation produces rank-2 laminate twin microstructures, including a herringbone morphology with four crystallographic polar variants. Electron backscatter diffraction and high-resolution STEM characterize domain boundaries, while 4D-STEM differential phase contrast qualitatively maps geometric polarity and identifies head-to-head and tail-to-tail “charged” domain boundaries arranged in an interlocking Y pattern.

Surface-sensitive measurements suggest that these domain boundary types affect local electronic behavior. Low-voltage SEM, electrostatic force microscopy, copper deposition during metallographic preparation, and variable oxide formation show contrast or reactivity patterns consistent with the interlocking Y morphology. The authors suggest electron enrichment at head-to-head boundaries and depletion at tail-to-tail boundaries, linked to local variations in density of states or work function, despite screening in the metallic state.

A chemical sorting of polar compounds in the Inorganic Crystal Structure Database identifies at least 134 metallic polar compounds, with about 20% classified as DPMs. The passage argues that metallic DPMs and their domain boundaries are underexplored and may provide a broader chemical and functional space than previously emphasized polar metallic oxides.

The paper analyzes South Australia’s 2018 “World Class” public education policy using Bacchi’s “What’s the Problem Represented to be?” framework and publicly available and FOI-obtained documents. It situates the policy within the Global Education Reform Movement, PISA-linked accountability, and McKinsey and Company’s “Universal Scale” for comparing school systems.

The authors argue that the Department for Education represented system improvement as a problem of insufficient central control, unclear priorities, and underperforming schools, with McKinsey’s roadmap and standardized test data presented as the solution. The policy aimed for South Australia to reach “World Class” status by 2028, measured through NAPLAN, PISA, TIMSS, PIRLS, and SACE-related data.

The analysis finds that the policy centralized authority, increased surveillance of schools and principals, ranked schools through “differentiation,” and positioned departmental data as a “single source of truth.” The authors state that this reduced professional trust, narrowed educational purposes, intensified accountability, and placed greater scrutiny on disadvantaged schools. They argue that equity, local context, student wellbeing, and broader democratic purposes of education were marginalized.

The paper concludes by proposing a “Beyond World Class” framework based on professional trust, democratic policy development, equity, inclusion, and system-wide support informed by educators, schools, and the Alice Springs (Mparntwe) Education Declaration.

Jane Goodall, pioneering chimpanzee researcher and conservationist, died in her sleep of natural causes while on tour in California at age 91, the Jane Goodall Institute said. Goodall began observing chimpanzees in Gombe in 1960 and discovered they make and use tools, have personalities, conduct warfare, and engage in cannibalism. She earned a PhD from Cambridge in 1965 without a bachelor’s degree. Goodall founded the Jane Goodall Institute in 1977 and later created the Roots & Shoots youth program. She advocated for improved treatment of chimpanzees in research and became a prominent global conservation voice, receiving honors including UN Messenger of Peace and Dame of the British Empire.

Argentine defender Federico Allende of lower-division Sport Pacifico admitted in a radio interview that he used a needle to hurt Estudiantes strikers during Pacifico’s 3-2 cup upset. He said players must “play dirty” and be clever to beat bigger clubs. Pacifico president Hector Moncada said he would expel Allende, while Colombian striker Juan Otero called him “a nasty man.”

In 1889, Robert W. Wilcox and Robert Boyd led an insurrection in Hawaii that was quickly defeated, with U.S. sailors and marines briefly landed by permission to protect life and property. A constitutional dispute between King Kalakaua and the cabinet was decided against the King, affirming cabinet control over public documents and government administration. Hawaii was invited to the International American Conference in 1890, but its delegate arrived after adjournment. Kalakaua visited the United States in December 1890 and died in San Francisco in January 1891; Liliuokalani was then proclaimed Queen. U.S. Minister Stevens reported concerns that she might try to replace the ministry, though a later court ruling ended the prior cabinet and a new one was appointed. In 1891, Stevens reported the death of the Queen’s husband and discussions on revising the U.S.-Hawaii reciprocity treaty after sugar tariff changes. A special envoy was appointed, and a pro-treaty legislature was elected in 1892.

Stock trading strategies are rule-based methods for buying and selling stocks or ETFs, typically focused on short-term price movements rather than long-term holding. The passage describes strategies including day trading, swing trading, momentum trading, scalping, trend following, arbitrage, high-frequency trading, event-driven trading, sector rotation, pair trading, market-neutral trading, statistical arbitrage, technical analysis, seasonality, long-short equity, S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 trading, overnight trading, mean reversion, and oscillator trading.

The passage emphasizes quantified rules, backtesting, discipline, risk management, diversification, and accounting for costs such as commissions and slippage. It states that technical indicators such as moving averages, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and stochastic oscillators are commonly used, and that strategies can be automated with algorithms to execute trades faster and reduce human error. Volatility, timing, unexpected news, market conditions, emotions, and research all affect trading outcomes.

Stock trading differs from long-term investing because trading targets short-term movements over days, minutes, or seconds, while investing focuses on growth over years or decades. The passage warns that day trading, scalping, and institutional strategies such as arbitrage, high-frequency trading, and statistical arbitrage are difficult, and that many traders lose money.

The passage also discusses single-stock trading, where a trader focuses on one stock. It says this may allow deeper knowledge of a company’s fundamentals and price patterns, but it is risky because any company can suffer major losses or become insolvent. It recommends diversification across stocks, strategies, timeframes, and assets, especially for retail traders.

This randomized controlled trial compared Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) with MBSR plus group psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy (MBSR+PAP) in 25 physicians and nurses with COVID-19-related depression and burnout. Participants received an 8-week MBSR course; the MBSR+PAP group also received preparatory sessions, a 25 mg psilocybin group dosing session, and integration sessions.

The intervention was feasible, with high attendance in the MBSR+PAP arm, and no serious adverse events, emergent suicidality, or self-injurious behaviors occurred. All study-related adverse events were mild or moderate.

At 2 weeks post-intervention, MBSR+PAP produced significantly greater reductions in depressive symptoms than MBSR alone, with QIDS-SR-16 scores decreasing by 7.26 points versus 2.66 points. MBSR+PAP also showed greater improvements in depersonalization, demoralization, and connectedness at 2 weeks, and greater reduction in emotional exhaustion at 6 months. Expectancy was higher in the MBSR+PAP arm but was not associated with depression improvement in that group. Mystical experience and nondual awareness scores correlated with improvements in several outcomes.

Limitations included small sample size, limited demographic diversity, lack of blinding, unequal intervention experiences between groups, and inclusion of participants with prior psychedelic use. The authors conclude that MBSR combined with group psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy appears safe, feasible, and potentially effective for depression and burnout in frontline healthcare workers, warranting larger placebo-controlled studies.

Churchill High School senior Deanthony Gordley earned his diploma after facing homelessness and the deaths of both parents. After Hurricane Katrina, he moved to San Antonio with his father, who was later shot and killed. He then lived with his biological mother until she died after a heart attack. With no support, Gordley slept outside for about seven months before receiving temporary help from a stranger. NEISD connected him with the McKinney Vento Homeless Project, which helped him succeed in school. Gordley credits the program, families, and his school for supporting him, and hopes his story encourages others. He also shares his experiences through music sold on iTunes.
Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi won the 2025 chemistry Nobel for metal-organic frameworks.

Jalen Carey’s commitment strengthens Syracuse basketball’s 2018 recruiting class, joining Darius Bazley as Top 50 recruits with Buddy Boeheim as a complementary piece. The passage introduces a historical ranking of Syracuse recruiting classes based on arrival-time recruiting evaluations from multiple sources.

Stripe is launching Open Issuance, a product from its Bridge acquisition that lets businesses create and manage stablecoins and capture yield from reserves. Stripe says the offering could improve global money movement and encourage adoption, supported by new U.S. stablecoin regulation. The initial users are crypto firms Phantom, Hyperliquid, and MetaMask, while broader non-crypto adoption remains uncertain.

The 3-2 zone defense, a variation of the 1-2-2, drops the point defender to the free throw line so wing defenders can deny wing passes and protect the high post. It can disrupt zone offenses that start with wing entry passes but may allow open shots to the point guard; against strong shooters it can shift to a 1-2-2 or 1-3-1. A taller, athletic wing can interchange with the point to improve high-post denial and rebounding positioning. Like the 1-2-2, it supports fast breaks because defenders are already aligned in lanes. The passage details player rotations for ball positions in the middle, wings, and corners, including a point-wing interchange option.

The passage compiles news articles from May 12–13, 2001 mentioning Enron. Topics include California universities preparing for possible rolling blackouts during exams amid a dispute with Enron Energy Services; articles referencing Enron in Houston technology and civic planning discussions; and extensive coverage of Enron’s Dabhol Power Company in India, including MSEB’s refusal to take additional equity, tariff renegotiation talks, payment disputes, possible third-party power sales, and broader power-sector reform concerns. Other items report Enron’s possible withdrawal from the Dolphin Energy gas pipeline project, Oregon Congressman Peter DeFazio’s proposal that the state buy Enron-owned Portland General Electric, and business stories that mention Enron as a customer or financial reference point.

Cierra Dillard scored 22 points as 11th-seeded Buffalo defeated No. 3 Florida State 86-65 to reach the women’s NCAA Tournament Sweet 16 for the first time. Buffalo shot 47.4% and held Florida State to 33.8%. The Bulls will face defending champion South Carolina in Albany. Stephanie Reid added 18 points, and Shakayla Thomas led Florida State with 25.

Investing.com’s market outlook says markets shifted risk-off after a week of earnings, GDP data, an FOMC meeting, weak jobs data, tariff-policy uncertainty, and political developments. Q2 S&P 500 earnings and revenue beats were above historical averages, while GDP rose 3% versus 2.5% expected but was distorted by import volatility and weak personal spending. Payrolls rose 73,000 versus 100,000 expected, with large downward revisions, while unemployment edged to 4.2%. The Fed signaled patience, though markets priced high odds of rate cuts. Major indexes formed a bearish engulfing pattern, internals weakened, most sectors fell, and the article said tactical risk management may be warranted.

West Midlands house prices ended the year about £12,000 higher, with the average at £181,000 after 7.1% growth. UK prices rose 7.2% to December, strongest in England at 7.7% and weakest in Scotland at 3.5%. Shetland saw the largest rise, 26.1%, while Aberdeen fell 9.8%. Within the West Midlands, Wyre Forest and Kidderminster had the biggest increase at 10.4%, and South Staffordshire the lowest at 3.1%. PwC expected slower growth in 2017.

The global organic pigments market is forecast by MRFR to grow at about 4.5% through 2022, driven by increased use in paint and coatings, plastics, textiles, printing inks, and related applications. Growth factors include cost effectiveness, consistent and unique shades, solvent stability, and non-toxic properties. Asia-Pacific is expected to be the largest and fastest-growing region, with China creating opportunities for local and global players, followed by competition between North America and Europe. The report analyzes market segments by type, source, application, and region, covering pricing, supply chain, Porter’s Five Forces, revenue forecasts, country-level trends, competitive developments, and key players including BASF, Dow Chemical, Huntsman, Cabot, Clariant, Sensient Technologies, Evonik Degussa, DuPont, and DIC Corporation.

The passage describes a patent application for a storage system using stacked containers within a grid framework, accessed from above by robotic load handling devices. The invention adds service means within the framework, particularly through uprights and grid structures, to provide power, fluids, data communication, lighting, sensing, monitoring, and control.

The system includes rails forming a grid, uprights defining a framework, containers arranged in stacks, and load handling devices that move laterally above the stacks to lift containers. Services routed through the framework may support condition monitoring, structural monitoring, fire detection, temperature control, lighting, heating, cooling, fluid delivery, and communication with containers or central systems.

Sensors may detect smoke, fire, heat, gas, structural alignment issues, or container identity, and data may be logged locally or transmitted wirelessly or through cabling. Fluids such as water, carbon dioxide, or nitrogen may be routed through the framework for sprinklers, crop watering, greenhouse applications, or fire suppression. Containers may connect to the framework by contact or non-contact means, including conductive pads, brushes, magnetic induction, RF induction, or releasable connectors.

The framework may also support partitions to isolate sections for temperature control, fire containment, gas environments, or incident management. The described system aims to enable monitoring and control within dense automated storage systems while reducing downtime, damage, and operational cost.

Nahant’s April 29 Town Meeting will consider 41 articles, including Fire Chief Michael Feinberg’s request for an Ambulance Enterprise Fund funded by ambulance fees. The Finance Committee opposes it, citing questionable resident benefit and concerns about funding outside Proposition 2½ protections. Selectmen are divided, with Richard Lombard opposed and Enzo Barile and Chesley Taylor Jr. supportive. Members will also consider rescinding a 2008 decision on Coast Guard Housing and authorizing selectmen to sell the property, though the Finance Committee recommends postponement. The committee supports funding drainage repairs, DPW pickup trucks, and pumping station improvements.
