The ADS9803 is a 20-bit, eight-channel data acquisition system with simultaneous-sampling SAR ADCs, configurable single-ended or differential inputs, programmable gain amplifiers, low-pass filter bandwidth options, and up to 2MSPS per channel. It operates from 5V and 1.8V analog supplies, supports true bipolar inputs, includes a 4.096V internal reference, and provides 1MΩ input impedance independent of sampling frequency or input range.

Each analog input includes clamp protection tolerating up to ±18V, with input current above the clamp threshold limited to ±10mA. The device supports common-mode rejection up to ±12V, programmable input ranges, low- and wide-bandwidth modes, and 20-bit output data in straight-binary or two’s-complement format. It can use differential or single-ended sampling clocks, synchronize multiple devices with SMPL_SYNC, and operate with either the internal reference or an external reference on REFIO.

The ADS9803 supports 2-lane or 4-lane SDR and DDR data interfaces, source-synchronous output clocks, data randomization, simple and moving averaging for SNR improvement, and test patterns including fixed, ramp, and alternating outputs. It also provides a speed-boost mode up to 8MSPS for a selected analog input channel pair. Configuration uses SPI registers organized in banks, with support for daisy-chain operation across multiple devices.

Application information describes use in ATE systems, calibration for total unadjusted error, multiplexed PMU measurements, power-supply decoupling, layout guidance, and TI support, documentation, ESD, packaging, and disclaimer information.

Mineral companies owe more than $42 million in delinquent taxes to 12 Wyoming counties, largely because bankruptcies leave counties low priority for repayment. A Powder River Basin Resource Council report found Campbell County has over $26 million unpaid, while Sheridan County has about $7.46 million, mostly from Storm Cat Energy Operating Corporation and Summit Gas Resources. Officials cite Wyoming’s roughly 18-month county tax payment delay as a key factor, compared with faster state severance tax deadlines. Unpaid mineral taxes affect school districts and public services, with several Sheridan County educational entities owed significant amounts. The report recommends monthly ad valorem tax collection, continual liens, a state bankruptcy assistance fund and checks on tax debt before asset transfers. Similar legislative efforts have failed in recent years, though another bill is planned.

The passage argues that Western mainstream media has distorted peaceful opposition to Donald Trump and contributed to hostility against him, comparing this to Saudi Arabia’s alleged role in promoting extremist interpretations of Islam. It discusses the 2017 shooting at a Republican baseball practice, where James Hodgkinson shot five people, including Rep. Steve Scalise, before dying after police intervention. The passage describes Hodgkinson as a Bernie Sanders supporter with anti-Republican views, social media threats against Trump, and interest in anti-Trump media. It also links the attack to broader anti-Trump rhetoric, including Kathy Griffin’s photo depicting a mock beheading of Trump, and suggests media figures may bear responsibility if such rhetoric helped radicalize Hodgkinson.
UNMC College of Dentistry’s Children’s Dental Day provided free dental care and oral health education to Nebraska children. Since 2001, the program has delivered more than $3 million in dental work.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K dated February 8, 2018, reporting that it issued a press release and CFO commentary on results for the quarter and fiscal year ended January 28, 2018. The exhibits include the press release, “NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2018,” and CFO commentary by CFO Colette M. Kress.

Defenders must box out on all free throws to prevent offensive rebounds, which can decide games. Players should step up the lane with feet together, hands high, communicate assignments, and ensure the shooter is boxed out. If an offensive rebound occurs, defensive intensity must increase to get a stop. Against strong rebounders, defenders may pinch with a double box out. Teams should practice free throw responsibilities, including early push situations after made or missed shots.

A Cherokee County community will honor school leader Maleka Johnson, who was killed when a tour boat caught fire in the Bahamas during a vacation celebrating her 15th wedding anniversary. Her husband, Tiran, was critically injured. Their 12-year-old son Cameron was in Tennessee with family, who are now supporting him.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2021. Net sales increased to $108.5 billion from $75.5 billion in Q1 2020, while net income rose to $8.1 billion from $2.5 billion. Operating income increased to $8.9 billion from $4.0 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $15.79, compared with $5.01.

By segment, North America net sales were $64.4 billion with operating income of $3.5 billion; International net sales were $30.6 billion with operating income of $1.3 billion; and AWS net sales were $13.5 billion with operating income of $4.2 billion. Sales growth reflected increased unit sales, third-party seller activity, customer usage of AWS, and advertising sales, partially offset by fulfillment network capacity and supply chain constraints.

Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash were $34.2 billion at March 31, 2021, down from $42.4 billion at the beginning of the period. Operating activities provided $4.2 billion in cash, investing activities used $8.7 billion, and financing activities used $3.5 billion. Total assets were $323.1 billion, total liabilities were $219.8 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $103.3 billion.

Amazon reported approximately $2.0 billion in COVID-19 related costs in Q1 2021 and expected related effects on fulfillment costs, cost of sales, capacity, and supply chain constraints to continue into all or portions of Q2 2021. The company issued Q2 2021 guidance for net sales of $110.0 billion to $116.0 billion and operating income of $4.5 billion to $8.0 billion.

Vote counting is underway for by-elections to four Lok Sabha and 10 Assembly seats across several states. Key contests include Kairana, where the BJP faces an RLD candidate backed by BSP, SP and Congress, and Maharashtra’s Palghar and Bhandara-Gondia, contested by BJP, Shiv Sena, NCP and Congress. Kairana and Palghar fell vacant after BJP MPs died.

US-listed stock options generally expire on the Friday before the third Saturday of each month, with Thursday expirations when Friday is a holiday. The article tests the options expiration week effect mainly on the S&P 500 using SPY. A simple strategy buys at the open of options expiration week and exits at the close of expiration day, staying in cash otherwise. Backtests since SPY’s inception show a 2% CAGR, an average gain of 0.2% per week, and time in the market of about 18%, suggesting an options expiration week effect, though it has weakened in recent years and is not considered tradable on its own without additional parameters.

Results vary by month: April is described as the best month during options expiration week, while January and July show negative returns. Entering at the close of the prior Friday increases the S&P 500 average gain to 0.3% per trade. QQQ averages 0.25% per trade.

Options expiration day alone performs poorly in backtests. Holding SPY from the prior close to the OPEX day close produced negative average returns, including when filtered by whether SPY was above its 50-day moving average.

The week after options expiration is weaker than a random week, with a 1.5% CAGR and about 22% time in the market. Monthly results vary: August is historically positive, while September is the worst, with an average loss of 0.94% and a 25% win rate. February, June, and September are particularly negative.

The passage also notes that OPEX can create imbalances and volatility due to pin risk, hedging, and changes in open interest. Calendar-based trading strategies use specific dates or seasonal periods, such as options expiration, holidays, earnings, tax events, or economic releases, to exploit recurring market patterns.

The speaker takes the constitutional oath as President, expresses gratitude for the public’s confidence, and acknowledges the responsibilities of the office. He pledges to be guided by the Constitution, judicial interpretation, and the practices of earlier Presidents, especially Washington. He outlines presidential duties, including command of the military, treaty-making, appointments, informing Congress, and faithful execution of the laws.

He declares that his administration will serve the whole country rather than sectional interests and will uphold republican principles. He promises attention to the efficiency of the Army and Navy and support for military and naval schools. In foreign affairs, he favors sympathy for liberty, avoidance of entangling alliances, strict neutrality in disputes, peaceful relations, and diplomacy before war. For appointments, he identifies honesty, capacity, and fidelity as essential qualifications.

He intends to recommend constitutional measures to support agriculture, commerce, manufactures, river and harbor improvements, debt reduction, government accountability, and economy in public spending, while recognizing Congress’s legislative authority. He urges measures of conciliation to preserve the Union and concludes by noting national prosperity and calling for prudence, moderation, just principles, and broad patriotism.
Figures show multiple views and an exploded perspective of an under-sink organizer with a sliding storage basket; broken lines depict unclaimed portions.

The speaker says their team’s physical start made the opponent look overwhelmed, though the opponent played well early and is expected to respond with its best effort. They emphasize staying disciplined, physical, and ready from the start in the next game, noting that many shots went in during the previous win, which is unusual in the playoffs against a goalie like Belfour. The speaker says being in the Stanley Cup Final should be motivation, but the series resets each game. They praise Jason’s growing leadership and comfort in New Jersey, discuss the opponent’s goalie likely rebounding, and credit their own team for going hard to the net rather than benefiting from mistakes. They also highlight the scoring line’s chemistry and competitiveness, mention using medication when sick to focus on playing, and stress that winning Game 2 is important to keep home-ice advantage.

The lecture explains corporate carbon footprinting using a WidgetCo case study. WidgetCo manufactures office chairs in Michigan and through a 50-50 joint venture in Shanghai, operates U.S. distribution centers, uses owned and third-party transportation, and faces pressure after competitor FerretCo reports lower emissions and carbon-neutral plans.

Carbon footprint calculations generally use activity data multiplied by emissions factors, such as electricity use or fuel consumption. Fuel-based transportation data is preferred when available, while ton-mile estimates are used for shared transport. Aggregated shipment data can cause major errors if total weights and total distances are multiplied directly.

The lecture defines scope 1 as direct emissions from owned or controlled facilities and vehicles, scope 2 as indirect emissions from purchased electricity, and scope 3 as other indirect emissions. Organizational boundaries may be based on equity share or operational/financial control, affecting whether WidgetCo includes 0%, 50%, or 100% of the Shanghai plant’s emissions. Scope 3 inclusion is often optional and discretionary.

Student estimates of WidgetCo’s footprint varied, mainly due to boundary choices and calculation methods. Including all listed supply chain emissions gives about 580,000 tons CO2e, while including only directly owned operations gives just over 200,000 tons. Manufacturing drives most emissions.

The lecture notes that many companies disclose emissions through the Carbon Disclosure Project, often because of investor or business-customer pressure. Disclosure decisions depend on transparency, comparison risks, and readiness to explain reduction strategies. Corporate footprints are useful for tracking year-to-year performance, but comparing companies can be misleading when ownership and outsourcing differ.

The lecture concludes that corporate footprints often omit large supply chain impacts, prompting broader value-chain and product-level standards. The next class will address life cycle assessment for product-level emissions, using a hand-drying systems report as an example.

Eliud Kipchoge visited Tottenham Hotspur’s Hotspur Way after winning his third London Marathon title, meeting Victor Wanyama, Mauricio Pochettino and players with coach Patrick Sang. Wanyama congratulated Kipchoge, who was also crowned World Marathon Majors Champion and is expected to attempt Dennis Kimetto’s world record in Berlin.

A retrospective study analyzed 1,383 noma patients managed at Noma Children’s Hospital in Sokoto, Nigeria, from 1999 to 2024 to estimate noma incidence and clinical presentation in northern Nigeria. Patients ranged from 8 months to 80 years, with a median age of 6 years; 54.2% were male. Most cases came from Sokoto, Zamfara, Kebbi, and Kano states, and over half were recorded between 2021 and 2024.

Acute noma accounted for 67.3% of cases, while arrested noma accounted for 32.7%. Gangrene was the most common stage, representing 59.7% of all cases, followed by scarring, oedema, sequelae, and acute necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis. Acute disease was more common in children under five, while arrested noma was more common in older patients. The cheeks were the most frequently affected sites.

Using the WHO incidence estimation method, the study estimated 62,067 new noma cases in northern Nigeria during the study period, with an overall incidence of 114.5 cases per 100,000 population. Incidence was slightly higher among males than females. Annual incidence ranged from 0.2 to 21.3 cases per 100,000, with increases from 2020 to 2024. Sokoto had the highest state-level incidence and Adamawa the lowest. Incidence was highest among children under ten, while Kebbi had the highest incidence among young and middle-aged adults. The findings emphasize the need for awareness, screening, and early detection programs.

Noe Martinez Paredes appealed his guilty-plea conviction and 57-month sentence for drug conspiracy. His counsel filed an Anders brief and moved to withdraw, stating no grounds for relief. After independent review, the Ninth Circuit found no arguable appeal issues, granted counsel’s withdrawal motion, and affirmed.

This study investigated barriers to distance education in university mathematics education after Turkey’s 2023 earthquake shifted higher education online. Using Q methodology, data were collected from 13 mathematics education faculty members in Turkish universities through 50 ranked statements and follow-up interviews.

The analysis identified three main barrier types: student-related, technology-related, and pedagogical barriers. Student-related barriers were the strongest common perspective, including low engagement, reluctance to participate, distraction, and limited responsibility for learning. Technology-related barriers included insufficient access to digital resources and issues affecting participation. Pedagogical barriers were specific to mathematics education, including concerns about online assessment reliability, limited usefulness of tools such as graphic tablets compared with blackboards, and difficulties representing mathematical concepts online.

Participants generally reported having distance education experience, largely from the COVID-19 period, and did not identify teacher-related barriers as a distinct factor. Overall, curriculum and pedagogy barriers had the highest average effect, followed by teacher, technology, and student barriers. Faculty members generally viewed distance education alone as insufficient for mathematics education and favored blended, hybrid, or HyFlex models for the future.

The Senate approved on final reading the Philippine Identification System Act of 2018, creating a single official ID for citizens and foreign residents. The PSA would manage the registry and assign PhilSys Numbers. Senator Panfilo Lacson said it could aid law enforcement while protecting privacy. A 2019 rollout is expected with P2 billion allotted.

The passage describes a patent disclosure for secure, zero-knowledge sharing of encrypted data, particularly medical information, between users such as healthcare providers and patients. It addresses risks in storing and sharing sensitive information through cloud systems where providers may otherwise control or access encryption keys.

Some embodiments use layered encryption and a key hierarchy structure. User credentials, such as passwords or answers to security questions, derive keys that decrypt a master encryption key, which decrypts data encryption keys used for user data. Keys and credentials are generally kept client-side, while encrypted data may be stored on a server or cloud provider without giving the provider access to plaintext data or decryption keys.

The system may support patient-provider messaging, alerts, instructions, checklists, and shared medical data through client devices, web applications, mobile apps, or peer-to-peer communication. Public key encryption may be used to securely share data with individual recipients. For group sharing, a shared data key hierarchy structure may store encrypted shared data encryption keys for authorized users. Recipients can decrypt shared data with their private keys, and edits may require approval by the data owner before being incorporated.

The disclosure also describes registration, login, password recovery through security questions, generation and storage of encrypted private keys, key expiration, obfuscated key hierarchy entries, encrypted server storage, and optional secure sharing initiated through a printer driver. The enumerated embodiments cover methods, systems, and machine-readable media for deriving keys, decrypting layered encrypted data, and securely sharing encrypted data without server-side access to plaintext content.

Researchers found two grape-leaf bacterial strains that can degrade guaiacol, a key smoke-taint compound responsible for ashy flavors in wine after wildfire exposure. In lab tests, both strains made guaiacol barely detectable after 96 hours, and researchers identified a gene needed for the process. The bacteria did not break down similar smoky compounds, indicating other microbes may be needed. The approach could offer a more targeted alternative to current treatments like activated charcoal, which can remove desirable wine qualities. More research is needed on grape microbiomes and other smoke-taint compounds.

Barbeque Nation Hospitality filed a DRHP with Sebi for an IPO comprising a Rs 200 crore fresh issue and an offer for sale of 61.79 lakh shares. Proceeds will fund new restaurants, loan repayment and corporate purposes. The company operates 81 restaurants in India and one in Dubai.

Telstra CEO Andy Penn faces pressure ahead of investor day after a share price decline, a disguised earnings downgrade, and an S&P Global ratings cut. Analysts expect possible dividend cuts in 2019, though recent commentary from UBS and Morgan Stanley has become somewhat more positive.

Six months after Abby Williams and Libby German were killed near Delphi’s Monon High Bridge, no arrests have been made, but Indiana State Police say the case is not cold. Investigators have received over 24,000 tips, including 3,000 after releasing a suspect sketch, and continue reviewing leads, evidence, and DNA from the scene.

Ajay Bodke of Prabhudas Lilladher says retail investors need not worry about the 10% LTCG tax because equities remain the only asset class offering inflation-beating post-tax returns. He views Indian equities positively, citing expected revival in corporate earnings, disruptions from GST and demonetization being over, reasonable macro indicators, range-bound crude oil prices, and estimated GDP growth of 7.5% in FY18-19. He expects the RBI may struggle to maintain a neutral monetary stance amid global tightening and domestic fiscal concerns. Bodke notes strong domestic institutional inflows, rising SIP investments of Rs 5,000-6,000 crore per month, and increasing financialization of savings. He says equities have delivered the best CAGR returns compared with other assets, while gold has given inferior returns. He identifies insurance and retail-focused private BFSI players as attractive medium- to long-term sectors.

Montclair State University’s mascot, Rocky the Red Hawk, celebrated his 16th birthday by giving out free bagels, candy, cupcakes and other gifts around campus. Residence Life provided 500 bagels, while campus organizations offered items such as CDs, lip balm and cupcakes at a party in the Student Center Ballrooms. Students took photos, used GIF booths, won prizes and donated to a local food pantry. The celebration included remarks from President Susan Cole, a birthday song, cake and raffles for sweatshirts, a bookstore gift card and parking passes. Students said Rocky brings joy and helps unite the campus.

AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 specification update lists unresolved or documented silicon issues, their implications, and workarounds. Reported problems include PIT, PIC, DMA, UART, LPC, USB, IDE/ATAPI/UDMA, ACPI, PMC, GPIO, SMBus, RTC CMOS, KEL, GLIU, and PCI behavior deviations. Many issues have limited or no operational impact, while others may cause hangs, missed interrupts, failed accesses, corrupted register writes, unreliable DMA or UDMA operation, broken wake events, or clock-gating failures. Recommended resolutions commonly include avoiding affected modes or sequences, disabling clock gating, using DWORD-aligned PRDs, avoiding byte accesses to certain ACPI registers, using single-transfer DMA instead of block or demand modes, applying software traps or workarounds, and configuring delay counters appropriately. AMD disclaims warranties, reserves the right to change products, and states the products are not intended for life-support or similar critical applications.

Police bodycam footage shows 20-year-old Emily Weinman being arrested on a New Jersey beach during Memorial Day weekend after officers stopped her to check for underage drinking. She passed a breathalyser test but questioned why police were writing her up because the alcohol was unopened and refused to give her last name. The situation escalated, and an officer said she tried kicking them before saying he “slammed her on the ground” and hit her while cuffing her. Weinman was heard accusing police of choking and hitting her. A viral video sparked online debate over police brutality and her conduct. The officers were reassigned to desk duty pending an investigation. Weinman was charged with aggravated assault on police, spitting bodily fluids, disorderly conduct, resisting arrest, obstruction and minor in possession of alcohol.

The paper compares interdisciplinarity in impactful and less impactful medical journals using PubMed articles from 1999, 2010, and 2022. Impactful journals are defined as the top 10% of SCImago Journal Rank in medicine. The study represents medical knowledge structures as correlation networks of second-level MeSH disease terms, comparing impactful journals with size-adjusted less impactful journal samples.

The analysis finds that less impactful journals show higher average node strength, higher edge density, and slightly shorter average shortest path lengths, indicating greater interdisciplinarity and compactness than impactful journals. Impactful journal networks have higher modularity, suggesting more compartmentalised research. Both network types show similar clustering coefficients and moderately negative node strength assortativity.

Core analysis identifies stable, strongly connected medical concepts across years and journal types, including sexually transmitted diseases, communicable diseases, immunologic deficiency syndromes, genital diseases, and urogenital neoplasms. Neoplasms by site consistently ranks highest in node strength and betweenness, while central nervous system diseases serve an important bridging role. At broader MeSH levels, infections, nervous system diseases, and neoplasms are consistently prominent; infections dominate intra-community connections, while nervous system diseases and neoplasms contribute strongly to inter-community links.

Difference networks between impactful and less impactful journals show weak co-location of stronger differences and significant clustering around topic areas. These areas of relative prominence vary over time, unlike the stable core structure shared by both journal types.

The study concludes that highly impactful medical journals tend to publish less interdisciplinary research than less impactful journals, while cancer-related research is a major driver of interdisciplinarity in medicine. It suggests that evaluation systems, peer review, clinical guideline processes, and reporting standards may structurally disadvantage interdisciplinary research.

Archaeologists have linked a mass grave beside St. Wystan’s church in Repton, Derbyshire, to the Viking Great Heathen Army, which invaded Britain in the late 9th century. A new Antiquity study re-evaluated earlier carbon dating that had suggested the remains were too old to be Viking. Researchers found the dates had been skewed by the “marine reservoir effect” from seafood-heavy diets; after correction, the bones matched the winter of 874. The grave contained more than 250 people, including women, and evidence of traumatic injuries and unusual burial practices, such as a double grave with weapons and a Thor’s hammer pendant, and possible child sacrifices. The study supports the identification of the Repton remains as members of the Viking Great Army.

The Legislative Analyst’s Office says Gov. Jerry Brown’s tentative one-year contract with the California Correctional Peace Officers Association has a “weak justification,” arguing there is no evidence of recruitment or retention problems to support a 5 percent raise for 27,000 correctional employees. The Legislature and union members must approve the deal. The analyst found correctional officer staffing appears stable, entry-level hiring has increased, mid-career staffing has held steady, outside job prospects are limited, and wages have outpaced inflation since 2001. The Brown administration estimates the contract will cost $338 million over two years, but the analyst warns costs could be higher due to overtime and pension contributions.

Police searched nationwide for Steve Stephens, accused of posting Facebook video of himself fatally shooting 74-year-old Robert Godwin Sr. in Cleveland. Authorities said Godwin appeared randomly targeted and offered a $50,000 reward. Stephens blamed a former girlfriend in videos, but police said they did not know his motive. His phone was last detected in Erie, Pennsylvania, and possible sightings prompted investigations. Facebook removed the killing video after about three hours. Investigators said Godwin was the only confirmed victim despite Stephens’ claims of more killings.

The lecture covers plasma spectroscopy equilibria, modeling workflows, X-ray spectroscopy, filtering, imaging, and detectors. Complete thermodynamic equilibrium has Boltzmann state occupations, common electron/ion/radiation temperature, and balanced forward and reverse processes, but is rare. Local thermodynamic equilibrium assumes optically thin plasma where collisional processes dominate level populations and leads to Saha equilibrium for ionization states. Coronal, or collisional-radiative, equilibrium applies to low-density optically thin plasmas where collisions excite states and spontaneous emission de-excites them. Non-LTE modeling requires solving the relevant population-balance processes, though some processes may be neglected depending on the plasma.

Spectroscopic modeling starts with assumed density and temperature, selecting an equilibrium model, calculating ionization and excitation populations, computing line strengths, predicting spectra, accounting for opacity, reflections, and detector response, then comparing with experiment and iterating. Line ratios from strong, isolated, identified transitions can estimate ionization-state ratios and infer temperature, especially in optically thin cases.

X-ray spectroscopy is important for high-temperature plasmas and uses strong characteristic lines from low-level transitions in highly ionized atoms. K-shell transitions go to n=1, with K-alpha from n=2 to n=1 usually strongest; L-shell transitions go to n=2. These lines identify impurities and plasma conditions. X-ray filters use absorption edges from atomic transitions in materials, with edge positions depending on the element, to select spectral regions.

X-ray imaging lacks conventional lenses because refractive indices are near 1. Pinhole imaging uses geometric optics but is limited by geometric blur and diffraction blur, creating a trade-off in pinhole size. Bent crystals can provide monochromatic imaging by diffracting and focusing selected X-ray wavelengths but are expensive. Detectors include time-integrating film, reusable image plates with laser readout, time-gated cameras, and streak cameras that record one spatial dimension versus time.

Play action is a pass play designed to look like a run, with the quarterback faking a handoff to deceive the defense before looking downfield. It is most effective when an offense has established the run, causing defenders such as linebackers and safeties to move toward the line of scrimmage and leave space behind them. Successful play action requires the entire offense to sell the run, including the quarterback, running back, receivers, and offensive line, which initially shows run blocking before switching to pass protection.

Play action is often called in situations where defenses expect a run, such as short yardage, goal line, and red zone plays. Some professional offenses use play action on 30–40% of pass plays. Common concepts include the Double Post, which attacks deep coverage with two post routes, and Bubble Y Over, which uses short routes to draw defenders down while deeper routes attack open space.

Play action differs from a run pass option because play action is always intended as a pass, while an RPO can become either a run or pass depending on the defense after the snap.

Resolute Marine Energy (RME), founded by CEO Bill Staby, was developing Wave O™, a wave-powered desalination system intended to provide cheaper drinking water to coastal communities with weak or absent electric grids. In Ugu, South Africa, potable water cost $1.00/m³ after subsidy, partly because desalination depended on expensive diesel-generated electricity. RME believed its system could produce water for $1.00–$2.00/m³, compared with $3.00–$8.00/m³ in off-grid communities using diesel-powered desalination.

By 2012, after years of discussions, RME had signed non-binding agreements with Ugu and South Africa’s Council for Scientific and Industrial Research for a pilot project. The Development Bank of South Africa expressed interest in funding the South African side of the pilot, including site testing and permitting. RME needed $6 million to complete a second ocean trial and an integrated pilot in South Africa, and expected impact investors to be more suitable than traditional venture capital because of the project’s social and environmental mission.

RME was choosing among three commercialization strategies. The first was to build a wave energy converter that produced electricity to power a desalination plant, an easier and grant-supported route but with lower margins, brine-disposal issues, efficiency losses, stronger competition, and dependence on South Africa’s national electricity provider. The second was to use hydraulic power directly for desalination, RME’s business-plan approach, offering cleaner operation, lower production costs, and higher water-based margins, but requiring private funding and a desalination partner for an untested system. The third was a vertically integrated “black box” system combining wave conversion and desalination, potentially producing both water and electricity and capturing more value, but requiring more capital, technical expertise, time, and possibly sacrificing local partnership advantages.

RME had an experienced management and technical team and an intellectual property portfolio that included provisional patents and Patent Cooperation Treaty filings. The company also considered an Alaska opportunity to supply wave-generated electricity to remote diesel-dependent communities, though this raised questions about whether pursuing both water and electricity markets would confuse investors.

RME’s core strategic question was whether it should define itself as an energy company, a water company, or a more complex hybrid, while selecting the approach most likely to serve Ugu, attract investors, and support a future exit.

The Federal Circuit affirmed the Court of Federal Claims’ judgment awarding Public Safety Officers’ Benefits Act death benefits to the estate of Christine H. Roberts, mother of Sheriff Harold Ray Presley, who was killed in the line of duty. Roberts survived Presley and filed a claim but died before payment. The Bureau of Justice Assistance denied benefits, concluding her estate could not receive payment and that benefits were intended only for living beneficiaries.

The court held that eligibility for PSOBA death benefits is determined at the time of the public safety officer’s death. A beneficiary who survives the officer’s death becomes entitled to payment, and the government may not add a requirement that the beneficiary remain alive until the agency finishes processing the claim or issues payment. The court rejected the government’s statutory and regulatory interpretations, finding them inconsistent with the statute’s clear survival requirement.

Judge Prost dissented, arguing that the statute is silent or ambiguous on whether estates may receive PSOBA benefits and that the court should defer to the Bureau’s regulation limiting payment to living payees.

Apixaban compliance was high and comparable across groups, exceeding 95% through Week 24 and 94% at Week 48. The passage reports a study of CoSn₂ single crystals, a structurally simple three-dimensional intermetallic compound, focusing on low-temperature symmetry breaking. Resistivity shows metallic behavior with a slope change below 25 K, while specific heat and magnetic susceptibility show no anomaly or magnetic transition. Synchrotron single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals weak commensurate superlattice reflections below 22 K, indicating a symmetry reduction from high-temperature tetragonal I4/mcm to acentric monoclinic C2 with minimal lattice distortion. Angle-dependent magnetoresistance corroborates this transition, changing from nearly four-fold symmetry at higher temperatures to clear two-fold symmetry below 20–25 K.

First-principles calculations show dynamically stable phonons without imaginary modes, suggesting the distortion is not driven by lattice instability. Electronic structure calculations identify Fermi surface features with possible nesting, and susceptibility calculations indicate an electronically driven instability capable of breaking rotational symmetry. ARPES measurements reveal Fermi surface features broadly consistent with DFT and polarization-dependent anisotropy suggestive of orbital-selective electronic nematicity. Additional ARPES analysis identifies Dirac-like band crossings and a nodal loop near the Fermi level.

The study concludes that CoSn₂ exhibits low-temperature rotational symmetry breaking without magnetic order or strong structural distortion, positioning it as a nonmagnetic nodal-line semimetal platform for studying electronically driven nematic behavior.

The paper presents a causal Bayesian Network (BN) intended as a complementary clinical decision-support tool for Alzheimer’s disease (AD) diagnosis. AD is described as a neurodegenerative disease marked by amyloid beta plaques and tau tangles, with phases including preclinical AD, mild cognitive impairment due to AD, and dementia due to AD. The authors note diagnostic challenges, including clinician discomfort with AD diagnosis, symptom overlap with other conditions, and estimated misdiagnosis rates of 12% to 23%.

The proposed BN estimates both the probability that an individual has suspected AD and the probability they will receive a formal AD diagnosis, explicitly distinguishing disease status from diagnosis. Its structure follows medical reasoning “idioms” and includes risk factors, signs or symptoms, medical tests, comorbidities, complications, treatments, and other causes of cognitive impairment. Variables are based on validated diagnostic criteria, including NIA-AA guidance, and include cognitive symptoms, functional independence, cognitive tests, biomarker tests, age, family history, traumatic brain injury, and causative mutations in APP, PSEN1, or PSEN2.

Parameters were specified using a combination of data from the National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center Uniform Data Set, literature-derived estimates, and knowledge-based judgment. The model was internally validated by checking that prior probabilities matched estimated real-world prevalence, and externally assessed through clinical scenarios showing probability updates as symptoms, risk factors, alternative diagnoses, and biomarker results are entered.

The authors argue that the BN improves interpretability compared with black-box AI models, can update predictions with incomplete information, supports “what if” analysis, and applies to both early- and late-onset AD. Limitations include simplified modelling of non-AD causes of cognitive impairment, reliance on diagnosed AD cases in the dataset, manual parameter setting, uneven data across probability table cells, and missing causal relationships. Future work includes modelling other dementia causes separately, improving diagnosis validation with autopsy data, expanding early-onset AD modelling, supporting AD management decisions, and developing a research-focused BN that includes preclinical AD.

In Vansickle et al. v. Brown, Susan Ann Vansickle sued Brown for malicious prosecution after he caused her arrest for obstructing a public highway. The court held that evidence of the arresting officer’s insulting conduct was inadmissible absent proof Brown instigated it; a later trespass judgment against Brown was inadmissible on probable cause; county court proceedings that did not vacate the old road were irrelevant; and verbal directions from the county court were admissible only to show Brown’s good faith and lack of malice. Brown could testify to his good faith and lack of ill feeling. The court defined probable cause as the prosecutor’s reasonable belief in guilt, reaffirmed that malice and lack of probable cause must both be shown, and held that waiver of preliminary examination and recognizance were evidence of probable cause. The circuit court’s judgment for Brown was affirmed, with dissents noted on specific points.

AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine provides optional extensions to SEV and SNP to offload page migration between system physical addresses while preserving guest physical addresses. It supports migration of pages targeted by DMA through IOMMU coordination and migration of SNP guest pages inaccessible to the HV/OS. TMPM availability is indicated by the ENGINE_READY bit, and IOMMU enablement is required.

TMPM uses a separate page migration ring buffer managed by a driver through mailbox registers. Commands include PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, and PM_NOOP. Commands can process lists of up to 128 page migration entries, with per-command and per-page status reporting. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates hypervisor/default pages and can update IOMMU host PTEs for DMA-active pages; PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages between Guest-Valid/Guest-Invalid and Pre-Migration states.

The guide defines initialization, shutdown, pause/resume, interrupt handling, SPA encoding, firmware reload, debugging, and error handling procedures. TMPM performs best with larger batches, especially 128-page commands, and the ring buffer should be kept populated. Some structures cannot be migrated, including IOMMU structures, vIOMMU private mappings, pinned backing buffers, the ring buffer, and argument pages. All migrated SPAs must be 4KB aligned, with special alignment rules for host page table entries and 2MB pages.

Errors are reported through command status, migration entry status, PM_STATUS register bits, and sometimes MCA. Some failures allow retry, such as inability to gain exclusive RMP access, while hardware errors during a batch may make affected pages unrecoverable. Firmware reload requires no operations in flight, ring buffer teardown, version compatibility, and checking ENGINE_READY before use.

The article examines pedagogical approaches for teaching education for sustainable development within South Africa’s Technology Education curriculum, particularly the CAPS curriculum. It argues that although sustainable development is recognised globally and appears in policy documents, its integration into school-level Technology Education remains limited and inconsistently implemented.

The study used Kolb’s experiential learning theory as its framework, linking sustainability education to learner experience, reflection, practical activity, and real-world contexts. A qualitative descriptive case study was conducted with eight Senior Phase Technology teachers from the Ehlanzeni District in Mpumalanga, South Africa. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations and analysed using inductive content analysis.

Findings showed that teachers understood education for sustainable development as involving resource preservation, reduced environmental harm, renewable energy, responsible technology use, societal well-being, and indigenous or traditional sustainable practices. Teachers also identified opportunities in the Technology curriculum to teach sustainability through processing, recycling, design, renewable energy, environmental conservation, and investigation of technology’s social and environmental impacts. However, classroom observations showed that sustainability was rarely explicitly taught, and links to environmental, social, and economic dimensions were often absent.

Teachers identified collaborative learning as a useful pedagogical approach for sustainability education because it supports knowledge sharing, group problem-solving, creativity, cross-cultural learning, environmental stewardship, and practical solutions. Despite this, observed lessons relied mainly on demonstration and lecture methods rather than collaborative learning.

The article concludes that Technology Education has potential to support education for sustainable development, especially through practical design tasks, recycling, responsible resource use, indigenous knowledge, and collaborative learning. It recommends integrating sustainability holistically across the curriculum, encouraging value transformation, using practical sustainability-related projects, and promoting critical thinking about technology’s effects on society and the environment. Further research using both qualitative and quantitative approaches is recommended.

Soccer position numbering began in England in the 1920s, assigning numbers from back to front and right to left in a 2-3-5 formation, with 1 as goalkeeper and 9 as center forward. The 1950s “W-M” formation shifted inside forwards deeper and the center halfback into defense, helping create modern references such as “Number 9” for a central striker and “Number 10” for a scorer, playmaker, or set-back striker. From the 1960s, experimentation, “Total Football,” and freer jersey-number selection weakened the link between numbers and positions. In 2012, U.S. Soccer introduced a standardized numbering system based on a 4-3-3 formation, with defined position names and profiles tied to technical, tactical, physical, and mental attributes. The passage also notes terms such as “False 9” and “Double-9s.”

This passage describes a planned prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 4 trial in Thailand evaluating Thai cannabis oil in 90 women aged 18–70 with metastatic breast cancer receiving chemotherapy and ESAS scores ≥3. Participants at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital will be randomized 1:1:1 to Ganja Oil, Metta Osot, or placebo once daily before bedtime for 90 days. The study aims to assess quality of life, chemotherapy-related symptoms, adverse effects, microbiome changes, cytokines, bacterial metabolites, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacogenetic profiles. Blood, saliva, stool, and skin samples will be collected at baseline and day 90, with follow-up visits on days 30 and 90 and post-trial monitoring for withdrawal symptoms. The study is funded by Thailand’s Department of Thai Traditional and Alternative Medicine and was approved by the Chulalongkorn University ethics board.

The position differs from kicking on field goals, extra points, and kickoffs. Typical punters are slim, around 5’10”–6’2” and 180–210 pounds, with flexibility, coordination, creativity, and lower-body power. Notable punters include Shane Lechler, who holds the NFL record for highest average yards per punt, and Ray Guy, a first-round pick and three-time Super Bowl winner. Punters are important because field position affects scoring chances and defensive confidence.

Studies show millennials are saving for retirement at strong rates, with 71% of millennial workers saving and many starting earlier than Generation X. Transamerica found 39% save more than 10% of salary, Fidelity says they are on track to replace 78% of estimated retirement expenses, and Bank of America found about one in six have saved at least $100,000.

However, several surveys show millennials invest more conservatively than older generations, holding more cash and stable investments and expressing greater fear of the stock market. The passage says this may threaten long-term retirement security, noting that stock market returns from 2007 to 2017 outpaced money market account returns despite the financial crisis. Experts quoted argue that risk is unavoidable and should be viewed in context, and suggest millennials consider manageable ways to invest, including simple retirement portfolios or robo-advisors.

The passage describes a microservices architecture for cloud computing and data centers that abstracts hardware and software accelerators behind a common microservices API. The system allows applications to request functions without knowing whether they will be performed by local software, CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, ASICs, hardware accelerators, resource pools, virtual appliances, or remote services.

Microservice instances register with a service discovery function, which maintains a catalog of available services, capabilities, access methods, configuration data, load information, and mappings from standardized API calls to native service invocations. The catalog may include information for provisioning new instances, such as FPGA gate configurations. A microservices driver queries the service discovery function to select an available or best-fit implementation based on factors such as capability, bandwidth, latency, load, priority, and resource availability.

The architecture supports dynamic provisioning, uniform addressing, and unified access methods including REST APIs, URIs, PCIe, RDMA, shared memory, MMIO, system calls, libraries, or fabric-based communication. It also supports service chaining, where multiple microservices are linked so that outputs from one service pass directly to the next without repeatedly returning to the host application. Message forwarders configure and route these flows using path identifiers, next-hop information, tokens, buffers, and optional completion tracking.

The disclosure also describes data center environments, orchestration, workload clusters, virtual machines, hypervisors, switching fabrics, resource pools, telemetry collection, and load balancing. A load-balancing engine may route messages among service instances or trigger new instance creation using telemetry, service quality objectives, and policies such as round-robin, weighted fair queuing, prioritization, hot-potato routing, or deadline-based routing.

Example implementations include a computing apparatus or non-transitory computer-readable medium configured to receive microservice accelerator registrations, store them in a microservice registration database, publish registrations, map universal API calls to native invocations, support service chains, spawn new instances, program accelerators such as FPGAs, and track loading on existing instances.

Micro E-mini S&P 500 Index futures are CME contracts launched in 2019 that track the S&P 500 and are 1/10 the size of E-mini contracts. They trade electronically on CME Globex, are cash-settled, and have a contract value of $5 times the index, with a 0.25-point minimum fluctuation worth $1.25. They are aimed at retail traders with smaller accounts for speculation, diversification, or hedging.

A trading strategy may use technical and fundamental analysis, entry and exit rules, position sizing, and risk management. The passage references a paywalled mean-reversion strategy backtested on E-mini contracts using CME data, daily bars, and no risk-management parameters. Historically, S&P 500 futures have performed better in winter and spring than in summer.

Contracts are listed quarterly for March, June, September, and December over five consecutive quarters. Trading runs Sunday to Friday with a daily maintenance break. The MES symbol is used. The contract’s all-time high was 4808.25 in January 2022, and its lowest Micro E-mini level was 2174.00 in March 2020. Major risks include adverse price movement and leverage-related losses.

A user reports confirming an in-store Meijer PS4 Pro deal using mPerks coupon stacking. A new mPerks account gives 5% off, and an electronics/toys coupon gives $50 off a PS4 Pro. The console rings up at $349.99, reducing to $332.50 after 5% and $282.50 after the coupon. The deal is in-store only and requires a nearby Meijer.

The passage compiles May 18, 2001 news mentions of Enron and U.S. energy policy. The Wall Street Journal reports that Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay met with Vice President Dick Cheney and promoted an agenda reflected in parts of President Bush’s energy plan, including opposition to wholesale electricity price controls, broader access to transmission systems, and fewer barriers to new plants and power lines. The article details Enron’s political contributions, ties to Bush administration officials, lobbying around FERC appointments, and efforts to shape deregulated electricity markets.

The Los Angeles Times reports that Bush’s energy plan would mainly benefit oil, gas, coal, utility, construction, and labor interests, while offering less to renewable energy firms, consumers, environmentalists, and mass transit advocates. Bloomberg reports that Japanese utility leaders opposed Enron’s proposal to separate power generation, transmission, and distribution in Japan, citing concerns about responsibility for supply and California-style failures.

Other items note Enron leasing office space in Mumbai, plans to withdraw from the Dolphin gas project in the UAE, and criticism from watchdog groups that energy companies with close Bush administration ties could benefit from the new policy. Reuters reports mixed reactions to the Bush plan, with praise from some power suppliers, criticism from California Gov. Gray Davis and Democrats, and protests from environmental groups.

The speaker praises an experienced playoff player and says the team benefits from his past minutes. They feel confident in overtime by focusing on playing their game and trying to win. The speaker says the team has responded all year, needed to stop giving opponents too much respect, and enjoys tight, exciting games.

Janata Congress Chhattisgarh chief Ajit Jogi announced 11 candidates for next year’s Chhattisgarh assembly elections, saying more names, including six sitting MLAs and core committee members, would be revealed later. Google laid off more than 100 employees in design-related roles within its cloud unit, including quantitative user experience research and platform and service experience teams. Some cloud design teams were halved, with many affected roles based in the U.S.; some employees have until early December to find another internal role. The cuts come as Google reduces headcount and prioritizes AI investment, including buyouts across multiple U.S.-based divisions and reductions in some management roles.

China’s official manufacturing PMI rose to 49.8 in September, beating expectations of 49.6 but remaining in contraction and marking its strongest reading since March. RatingDog’s manufacturing PMI reached 51.2, above forecasts and its highest since May. Non-manufacturing PMI edged down to 52.9, while RatingDog’s services PMI eased to 50. Beijing’s October Politburo meeting may signal policy responses to third-quarter slowing.

A July 17, 2001 IEP news digest compiles articles on California’s energy crisis. The Wall Street Journal reports that Gov. Gray Davis has expanded state control over electricity purchasing, grid governance, transmission policy and power authority planning, committing $45 billion to $50 billion in power contracts and pursuing a $13 billion bond issue, while critics raise concerns about oversight, consumer costs, public disclosure and limits on customer choice. NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated November 15, 2018, reporting that it issued a press release announcing results for the quarter ended October 28, 2018. The filing includes Exhibit 99.1, the press release, and Exhibit 99.2, CFO commentary by Colette M. Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, which would be posted on NVIDIA’s investor website. The materials are furnished and not deemed filed under specified securities laws.

The passage explains the MOVE Index, a measure of U.S. interest rate volatility based on 1-month OTC options and often called the “VIX of the bond market.” It rose sharply amid Federal Reserve rate hikes and banking concerns, reaching 199 in March after starting the year at 120, compared with a long-term average near 85 and an all-time high of 264 in October 2008.

The article examines whether the MOVE Index can help trade long-term bonds using TLT. It notes that, unlike high VIX readings for stocks, high MOVE readings generally do not indicate a good time to buy bonds and generate few signals. A backtested strategy held TLT when the MOVE Index was below its historical mean and sold when it was above. The strategy reduced drawdowns, especially in 2022, but was not highly profitable and sometimes hurt returns, such as in 2008. The conclusion is that MOVE is useful for measuring bond volatility but not clearly effective as a bond trading indicator.

Vision in soccer is the ability to see, understand, and respond to positioning and movement on the field, enabling better passing, defending, and decision-making. Coaches emphasize constant scanning, knowing teammate and opponent locations, getting the head up after controlling the ball, using peripheral vision, anticipating options, and identifying runs. Communication from players with wider field views, especially goalkeepers, defenders, midfielders, and central attackers, helps the team. Training tips include receiving passes with the opposite foot, playing the first touch away from the body, and using drills that require players to scan before passing.

NatWest’s digital safety report, produced with The Future Laboratory, identified eight emerging financial scams, including smartphone malware, fake discounted FIFA World Cup ticket sites, social media-personalised fraud, Brexit-proof investment claims, money mules, fake wedding services, dating app catfishing and solicitor impersonation. The report says scammers exploit online shopping, mobile banking and social media, and advises verifying requests for personal information, updating security software and avoiding unknown links or files.

A Citizen experiment found that submitting fake research to predatory publishers led to repeated solicitations from other questionable journals, suggesting names, contact details, and even unpublished submissions are shared among scammers. OMICS International accepted absurd papers on ocean-bottom birds and flying pigs for conference presentation fees. Later, other journals requested full articles based on these fake submissions, including one never published, indicating academics who engage once may be targeted long-term.

Gianluca Vialli said Juventus must prevent the Camp Nou atmosphere from igniting in their second leg against Barcelona, recalling Chelsea’s 2000 collapse there after winning the first leg. Hucknall and Linby Dolphins finished fifth in an eight-team novice gala for nine to 11-year-olds at Arc Centre Matlock. Katie Hill earned three runner-up spots, several swimmers placed second or third, and the boys U10 relay team won.

DAWN-PLASMA was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 multicenter trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of convalescent plasma plus standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. The study followed Declaration of Helsinki, ICH-GCP, and IEC/IRB approval requirements, with informed consent required before enrollment.

The primary objective was to assess clinical efficacy and safety, with the primary endpoint defined as the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary endpoints included clinical status, mechanical ventilation or death through Days 30 and 90, thromboembolism, transfusion-related effects, antibody-titer correlations, safety, quality of life, laboratory data, vital signs, and severe adverse events or serious adverse events.

Eligible participants were adults with confirmed or clinically supported SARS-CoV-2 infection and evidence of respiratory illness. Exclusions included invasive or non-invasive mechanical ventilation at or before randomization, unacceptable safety risk, severe prior plasma allergy, treatment restrictions excluding ventilation or intubation, and recent anti-CD20 therapy.

Participants were randomized 2:1 to convalescent plasma plus standard of care or standard of care alone. Plasma recipients were intended to receive 800–1000 mL in four units, beginning within 12 hours of randomization. Plasma with neutralizing antibody titers below 1/160 was not allowed.

Between May 2, 2020, and January 26, 2021, 499 patients were assessed and 489 randomized: 326 to plasma and 163 to control. The Day 15 visit occurred in 434 patients and Day 30 in 423. Six randomized patients were excluded from the Full Analysis Set. In the plasma group, median time to first transfusion was 5 hours, median administered volume was 884 mL, and 91.9% received all four units.

Diversification reduces portfolio risk by combining investments that respond differently to market conditions, but it must consider risk factors, financial goals and investment horizon. Common mistakes include excluding investments such as provident fund balances or stock options when assessing asset allocation; holding too many investments, which can dilute benefits, raise costs and make monitoring difficult; investing in products without understanding them or, conversely, limiting choices too narrowly; failing to align asset allocation and liquidity with financial goals; and treating diversification as a one-time exercise instead of periodically rebalancing. Diversification can also be applied within asset classes, such as across equity sectors or debt credit profiles and tenors.

AOL Instant Messenger (AIM) will be discontinued on December 15. The company cited changes in communication habits, while users shared nostalgia on social media using #AIMmemories.

The passage presents UZEP, a cloud-based distance education platform developed for higher education institutions during the Covid-19 pandemic using an Education as a Service model. The study aimed to create a scalable, easy-to-use system that integrates with university management systems, supports data protection, and can be deployed quickly in emergencies. UZEP includes learning management, virtual classroom, online exam, homework-project, digital material sharing, announcement, survey, and reporting modules.

The platform was tested by 12 Turkish universities during the Fall 2020 semester, serving 78,732 users, 13,180 courses, 2,522 instructors, 11,314 exams, and 358,657 exam sessions. Evaluation was conducted through expert, pilot, administrator, lecturer, and student feedback. Experts found UZEP easy to use, suitable for emergency distance education, and strong in integration, virtual classrooms, assessment, and reporting, but noted weaknesses in communication, social tools, learning analytics, and some assessment features. Administrators rated ease of use and development potential positively but identified shortcomings in attractiveness, user attitudes, and responsiveness to change. Lecturers rated the virtual classroom highest, followed by assessment and LMS features. Students reported moderately positive satisfaction but requested better communication tools and improvements in assessment.

The study concludes that UZEP can help universities rapidly transition to distance education without requiring their own infrastructure. Compared with Moodle, edX, and Google Suite, UZEP’s integrated, scalable structure is presented as an advantage for emergency higher education use, while its limitations include weaker collaboration, social networking, and some assessment functions. Future work is planned for artificial intelligence-supported exam security and assessment, plus improved communication and interactive learning tools.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on December 29, 2020, its Board appointed Monica Lozano as a director, effective January 4, 2021. She will serve on the Audit and Finance Committee. As a non-employee director, Lozano will receive a $100,000 annual retainer, participate in Apple’s Non-Employee Director Stock Plan, and received an initial grant of 281 restricted stock units. Apple will enter into its standard director indemnification agreement with her, and no reportable transactions exist between Apple and Lozano under Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K.

The disclosure describes apparatus and methods for assessing tissue viability and damage around burns and other wounds by measuring electrical characteristics, including capacitance, and deriving sub-epidermal moisture (SEM) values. It addresses limitations of visual and tactile burn assessment, noting that burn wounds are dynamic and depth estimation is difficult.

The disclosed systems use electrodes on substrates to form capacitive, bioimpedance, or SEM sensors. Electrode arrays may create virtual sensors, including virtual center and ring electrodes, to measure capacitance over regions of tissue. Measured capacitance may be converted to SEM values or compared with stored capacitance-depth or SEM-depth data to determine burn depth.

SEM patterns are used to identify tissue zones around wounds. Tissue near a wound may show reduced SEM and lower viability, while surrounding tissue may show increased SEM associated with edema. For a third-degree burn, the disclosure describes a necrotic zone, a zone of stasis, and a zone of hyperaemia. Thresholds, peak SEM values, reference SEM values, and changes over time may be used to mark boundaries between tissue types, including viable and non-viable tissue.

Several embodiments are described: flexible substrates with SEM sensors and visual indicators; perforated substrates allowing clinicians to mark tissue; systems with LEDs indicating tissue zones; and systems using a camera, fiducial, SEM sensor, and projector to project boundary indicators onto tissue. Measurements may also be printed, stored, repeated over time, or used to monitor healing progress and therapy effectiveness after wound closure.

Wound Care Advantage, with Dr. David G. Armstrong, SALSA and Gen1 Research, launched Advanced Discovery, an investigative research alliance focused on evidence-based wound care. The alliance will provide access to an international network of wound and hyperbaric treatment centers and evaluate diagnostic and treatment approaches with manufacturers and research facilitators to improve wound healing outcomes and reduce treatment costs. Gen1 will provide administrative support and infrastructure. Advanced Discovery will use de-identified clinical data from more than 42,000 patients and 880,000 wound assessments, along with SALSA’s global academic affiliations. The announcement highlights the growing burden of chronic wounds, diabetes and diabetic foot ulcers in the U.S. Wound Care Advantage manages outpatient wound and hyperbaric centers, while Gen1 supports research execution through coordinators, analytics and research management software.

The passage describes systems and methods for reducing latency in wireless systems such as 5G flexible radio access technology by enabling a WTRU to determine transmission parameters before receiving a transmission grant. A WTRU may monitor and decode downlink control information, determine decoding parameters such as CRC length, aggregation level, DCI format, resource subset, or robustness level, and use them to derive transmission or reception parameters including QoS level, spectrum operating mode, MCS, resource blocks, power, timing, TTI duration, and HARQ feedback timing.

The disclosure covers 5G air interface features including flexible spectrum allocation, variable bandwidths, multiple waveforms, TDD/FDD operation, different spectrum operation modes, ultra-low latency, ultra-reliable transmission, machine-type communications, and multiple scheduling modes. It also describes WTRU and network architectures, logical channels, transport channels, and QoS-based handling of data.

To reduce grant-to-transmission delay, a WTRU may receive or determine PHY parameters such as MCS, resource ranges, coding, modulation, HARQ parameters, and transport block size before a grant. It may create, segment, assemble, multiplex, and encode fixed-size data blocks or MAC PDUs incrementally before the grant. Upon receiving a grant, the WTRU may select prepared data blocks based on flow, logical channel, QoS, TTL, grant restrictions, or transport block size efficiency, then complete transport block creation and any remaining PHY processing.

The passage also describes signaling of data block size, transport block size, and selected PHY parameters; implicit signaling using CRC values; ACK/NACK handling for data blocks and transport blocks; and aggregated data block status reports to support fast retransmissions for low-latency communication.

Plaintiffs, several Plumbers Local Union No. 93 boards and funds, sued Waterworks, Inc. under ERISA to compel an audit, claiming Waterworks was bound by a collective bargaining agreement. Waterworks disputed this, asserting it had only agreed orally to pay union rates and benefits for specific employees while not being bound by the CBA. The parties disagreed about a fall 2004 meeting and the significance of Waterworks’ later contribution reports and payments. The court found genuine issues of material fact regarding whether an agreement was formed and whether Waterworks’ conduct showed intent to be bound by the CBA. Both parties’ motions for summary judgment were denied.

CompareCards presents credit card offers with long 0% introductory APR periods, saying they may benefit consumers carrying high-interest balances or planning large purchases, especially those who pay balances in full and on time. The page lists partner cards with introductory APRs ranging from 12 to 21 months and highlights rewards such as cash back, travel points, sign-up bonuses, no annual fees, balance transfer offers, and category-based rewards from issuers including Discover, Bank of America, Citi, Wells Fargo, and Capital One. It notes that the site receives compensation from listed companies but says this does not influence ratings or reviews.

NVIDIA’s fiscal 2022 Form 10-K covers the year ended January 30, 2022. The company is headquartered in Santa Clara, California, trades on Nasdaq under NVDA, and had about 2.51 billion shares outstanding as of March 11, 2022. Sungi Cho, a former Army Black Hawk pilot with a mechanical engineering background, founded P6 Gear after developing 3D-printed solutions to improve military gear organization. His first product, the Warbelt Hanger, allowed soldiers to hang belts and loadouts for easier access and storage, and later gained customers in law enforcement.

Cho then developed the MOLLE Backer, a universal base mount for hard and soft MOLLE systems, priced at $10.99 for a two-pack. Demand stabilized at about 1,800 units per month. After leaving the Army to pursue an MBA at MIT Sloan, Cho moved his 15 printers to Cambridge, rented space, and hired two undergraduate engineering students at $20 per hour to assist with production and fulfillment.

Cho considered switching the MOLLE Backer from 3D printing to outsourced injection molding. 3D printing used 10 printers producing 180 units each per month, while injection molding could produce 200 units per hour. Injection molding offered lower PETG and scrap costs but required a third-party production price of $0.75 per unit and an $11,487 mold, compared with $1,716 per printer. Cho needed to evaluate the financial and non-financial implications of changing manufacturing methods.

The passage provides Sansa Fuze troubleshooting, support, warranty, and software license information.
