Options trading in EEM can provide market exposure and potential profits in rising or falling markets, but it is complex and carries risks including market losses, time decay, liquidity issues, volatility, leverage-related losses, and margin calls. Common strategies include long calls, long puts, covered calls, covered puts, straddles, strangles, collars, and butterfly spreads. Traders can evaluate trades using profit/loss calculations, fees, commissions, option delta, the Black-Scholes model, technical analysis, and backtesting. Costs, minimum deposits, margin requirements, liquidity, bid-ask spreads, and expiration dates vary by broker and contract type. Risk management practices include position sizing, stop losses, hedging, selecting suitable contracts, and using reputable brokers. Tax treatment depends on the trader’s country, and profits or losses are generally reported as capital gains or losses.

Eastern New England is forecast to receive more snow, with Maine, New Hampshire and Vermont expected to get close to a foot or more, especially in the mountains. Connecticut will mostly miss the storm, likely receiving only a dusting over the next 48 hours.

South Korea restored 46 public services after a fire at the National Information Resources Service data centre in Daejeon disrupted hundreds of government platforms. Authorities have restarted 551 of 647 affected systems, while passport, welfare and administrative services still await full restoration. President Lee Jae Myung called for stronger safeguards, backup plans and disaster preparedness.

The ADS868xW device provides programmable high and low analog input alarms with independent thresholds and common hysteresis, plus fixed AVDD alarms that assert above 5.3 V typical or below 4.7 V. It uses a multiSPI digital interface with configurable read and write protocols, supporting standard SPI, dual SDO, source-synchronous output, and daisy-chain topologies for multiple devices. In daisy-chain mode, devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK, use a single SDO-0 chain, and require 32 × N SCLK capture edges for N devices.

The device has RESET, ACQ, and CONV states controlled by RST and CONVST/CS. RESET can be configured as an application reset or power-on reset. ACQ acquires the analog input, and CONV performs conversion after a rising CONVST/CS edge. RVS indicates timing status, including conversion completion.

Programming uses nine configuration registers and supports data write and data read operations. A data transfer frame starts on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and ends on the next rising edge. Frames with 32 SCLKs are optimal; shorter frames invalidate writes but can read MSBs, while longer frames use the last 32 received bits as the command. Output data can include conversion results, register data, fixed patterns, device address, range flags, AVDD and input alarm flags, and parity bits.

Registers configure device ID, reset and power control, SDI and SDO protocols, output data format, input range, alarms, and alarm thresholds. The device supports NAP and power-down modes for reduced power consumption. Application guidance describes using the ADS868xW with an external multiplexer in industrial analog input modules, including programmable voltage and current ranges, alarm hysteresis use with thermistor sensing, power-supply decoupling, and PCB layout practices separating analog and digital sections.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that Rosalind G. Brewer informed the company on January 26, 2021, that she is resigning from its Board of Directors effective February 16, 2021. The report was signed by Senior Vice President David A. Zapolsky.

This retrospective study evaluated whether diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps can predict TERT promoter mutation status in glioblastoma using a ResNet deep learning model. The cohort included 266 adult patients with primary GBM, including 147 with DWI data. Conventional MRI sequences, DWI, ADC maps, clinical features, and different tumor regions of interest were analyzed.

Conventional structural MRI showed limited predictive value, with test accuracies around 50–52% and AUCs of 0.527–0.571. DWI alone achieved 54.58% accuracy, ADC maps achieved 78.63% accuracy, and combined DWI plus ADC achieved the best performance, with 85.20% slice-level accuracy and AUC 0.934; patient-level accuracy was 86.6%. Using the entire tumor as the region of interest performed best, followed by enhanced tumor and tumor core. Age, necrosis volume, and tumor location differed between mutation groups, but adding clinical characteristics did not improve model performance.

The study concludes that DWI combined with ADC maps outperformed conventional MRI for predicting TERT promoter mutation status in GBM, with the whole-tumor ROI providing the strongest predictive performance.

The Colorado Court of Appeals affirmed summary judgment for Shelter Mutual Insurance Company, holding that Shelter owed no additional uninsured/underinsured motorist payments to Samuel and Mary Breit. Breit had been injured in an accident, received $100,000 from the third party’s insurer, and sought $100,000 under each of two Shelter policies, though both contained $100,000 limits.

The court held that the policies’ anti-stacking provisions unambiguously limited Shelter’s total liability to the highest applicable limit under any one Shelter policy. It rejected the Breits’ arguments that the “Other Insurance” provision created ambiguity or conflicted with the “Other Insurance in the Company” clause, distinguishing Compton and relying on Thompson. The court also found the reasonable expectations doctrine inapplicable because the policy language was not ambiguous, conflicting, or contrary to legislative policy. Shelter’s request for appellate fees was denied because the appeal was not frivolous.

The ANC in the Free State has not yet started its delayed provincial congress in Parys, where new leadership is expected to be elected. Secretary William Bulwane said a court interdict attempt failed and that 28 of 29 required branch meetings had been rerun, with the last underway. Ace Magashule is expected to seek re-election.

This protocol describes a scoping review on antipsychotic-induced metabolic syndrome in community-dwelling adults. Antipsychotics improve psychiatric outcomes but are associated with metabolic syndrome, including weight gain, glucose dysregulation and dyslipidaemia, which increases risks of cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes and premature mortality. Reported non-modifiable determinants include gender, ethnicity, age and family history, while modifiable determinants include diet, physical activity and related behavioural changes. The relative importance of these factors and how they inform intervention targeting remain unclear.

The review aims to map evidence on non-modifiable and modifiable determinants, non-pharmacological interventions to prevent or treat antipsychotic-induced metabolic syndrome, and preferred contexts for intervention delivery. It will follow Joanna Briggs Institute guidance, Arksey and O’Malley’s framework, Levac et al.’s refinements and the PRISMA-ScR checklist. Quantitative, qualitative, mixed-method studies and evidence syntheses will be considered, excluding reviews, editorials, protocols and non-research letters. Searches will cover multiple bibliographic databases, Google Scholar, grey literature sources, reference lists and forward citations.

Records will be screened against inclusion criteria focused on adults prescribed antipsychotics in outpatient or community settings, metabolic syndrome, relevant determinants and non-pharmacological interventions. Data will be charted on study characteristics, populations, interventions, comparisons, outcomes, designs and key findings. Results will be narratively synthesised and mapped, without formal quality assessment, though evidence levels will be categorised using Joanna Briggs Institute ratings. Stakeholder consultation with patients and carers will inform interpretation. Findings will identify knowledge gaps and be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and conferences.

MetSoc of CIM announced its 2018 awards recipients, recognizing achievements and contributions in metallurgy and related fields. The recipients will be honored at the 57th Annual Conference of Metallurgists on October 15, 2018, in Columbus, Ohio. Awardees include Sam Marcuson, Priti Wanjara, Jun Song, Dr. Afshin Sadri and Hatch NDT, Xinjin Cao, Georgios Kolliopoulos, and Shauna Litke.

The Trump administration shifted day-to-day control of career and technical education from the Education Department to the Labor Department, saying the move will align programs with workforce needs, reduce state administrative burdens, and increase labor force participation. Supporters argue it could improve accountability, connect students to valuable credentials and apprenticeships, and better coordinate education and workforce systems, citing Alabama’s efforts as a model. Critics, including CTE advocates and Democrats, say the transfer may be illegal, unnecessary, understaffed, and part of dismantling the Education Department. They worry it could narrow CTE into short-term job training, revive stigma, reduce support for states and students with disabilities, and steer students toward low-wage jobs rather than long-term educational and career pathways.

A Phase I pilot clinical trial in Kisumu, Kenya, assessed acceptability of self-administered intravaginal 5-Fluorouracil (5FU) as adjuvant treatment after ablation or excision for CIN2/3 among 12 women living with HIV. Participants used 5FU at home every other week for eight doses and completed surveys and in-depth interviews. All participants completed treatment, strongly agreed the cream was safe, felt confident using it correctly, and said they would prefer it over prior ablation or excision if available as primary precancer treatment. Qualitative findings showed participants valued reduced pain, less fear, privacy, convenience, and home administration, though some reported challenges with measuring doses, tampon use, privacy at home, side effects, condom use, and partner support. Education from study staff increased confidence and comfort. The study found high acceptability but noted its small, single-site design and called for larger trials to evaluate efficacy and implementation in low- and middle-income countries.

Iranian President Hassan Rouhani warned that Iran could abandon the 2015 nuclear deal within hours if the United States continues imposing sanctions. He criticized President Donald Trump, saying Washington had broken promises, ignored global agreements, and shown itself to be an unreliable partner.

The Ministry of Education will fund a replacement for Walnut Park Elementary in Smithers, a more than 50-year-old school on unstable land where upgrades would cost more than rebuilding. The $28.5-million project will create a two-storey, LEED Gold-standard school for 440 students, with space for StrongStart and a neighbourhood learning centre. The province will contribute up to $27.6 million and SD54 will add $900,000. Construction is expected to begin next spring, with students moving in for the 2020-21 school year before the old school is demolished. Officials said the new facility will support modern learning, address safety and overcrowding concerns, and benefit the rural community.

CompareCards presents partner credit cards with 0% intro APR offers, generally ranging from 12 to 21 months, aimed at consumers carrying balances or planning large purchases. Featured cards include Discover, Bank of America, Citi, Capital One, and Wells Fargo products with cash back, travel rewards, sign-up bonuses, no annual fee options, and balance transfer terms. The passage explains that low or 0% interest credit cards can reduce costs on balance transfers and carried purchases, especially for consumers with good to excellent credit, but rates typically revert to variable APRs after promotional periods. It also notes that CompareCards receives compensation from listed companies but says this does not influence ratings or reviews.

The Indiana Supreme Court considered whether David Shaner’s wrongful death claim for survivor damages after his wife Laura’s death abated when David died intestate with no known heirs. The trial court and Court of Appeals had granted partial summary judgment for the defendants, concluding survivor damages would be punitive and that Laura’s estate representatives lacked standing. The Supreme Court held that Indiana’s wrongful death and survival statutes allow a properly accrued survivor-damages claim to continue regardless of whether an heir exists, and Bemenderfer did not impose an heir requirement. However, the Court found it unclear whether Laura’s estate representatives were the proper parties to pursue David’s claim. It reversed partial summary judgment and remanded for the trial court to determine whether a proper party exists to continue the claim, potentially through David’s estate.

A withdrawn medRxiv preprint evaluated six machine learning models for pancreatic cancer diagnosis using a synthetic dataset containing demographic factors, clinical risk factors, and symptoms. The models compared were Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Neural Network, Decision Tree, and SuperLearner. Data were split into 80% training and 20% testing, with preprocessing for missing values, feature scaling, and categorical encoding; no resampling was applied.

All models achieved similar accuracy, ranging from 76.05% to 76.35%, but sensitivity was very low across the board. Random Forest and Decision Tree identified no true positive cases. SVM had the highest sensitivity at 1.90%, while Logistic Regression and Neural Network each reached 1.47%. SuperLearner had the highest precision at 66.67% but sensitivity of only 0.42%. The study concluded that accuracy alone was misleading in this imbalanced diagnostic setting.

The authors identified class imbalance, limited sensitivity, and model interpretability as major barriers to clinical use. They suggested resampling methods, cost-sensitive learning, threshold tuning, feature engineering, explainable AI tools, real-world clinical datasets, and collaboration between data scientists and clinicians as possible directions for improving future models.

Pupils from Richardson Dees Primary School have transformed an unused rooftop space at The Forum shopping centre in Wallsend into a garden, growing flowers, fruit, vegetables and herbs. The project, initiated by centre manager Nick Lambert, aims to strengthen community links and gives children hands-on gardening experience, promoting healthy eating, responsibility, confidence and decision-making.

Kim Jong Un’s planned summit with Donald Trump remains uncertain as the US assesses what he would require to give up North Korea’s nuclear arsenal. The passage says Kim appears to want sanctions relief and economic development but is unlikely to abandon nuclear weapons unless he feels his regime is secure. Analysts describe him as anxious about his survival and political stability. Recent meetings with Xi Jinping and Moon Jae-in have portrayed him as a skilled diplomat seeking improved ties, legitimacy and economic benefits. Moon said Kim was concerned about whether the US would guarantee his regime’s security after denuclearisation. References by US officials to Libya heightened North Korean concerns, contributing to Trump’s temporary cancellation of the summit before talks appeared possible again. Kim has expressed openness to “complete denuclearisation,” but its meaning remains unclear.

Investing.com reports that market momentum remains intact but early warning signs are appearing. The S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July and 7.8% year to date, though it slipped at the start of August. Volatility and credit spreads are rising seasonally, portfolios are increasingly weighted toward tech, and U.S. electricity demand reached a new high. Short-term technicals look weaker, while medium- and long-term trends remain healthy.

The device provides an active-high alarm output on the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin when configured via SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] = 01b. It supports input and AVDD alarms, enabled by default when alarm functionality is on and selectively disabled using IN_AL_DIS and VDD_AL_DIS. Input alarms compare ADC input voltage against programmable thresholds; AVDD alarms compare supply voltage against 4.7V and 5.3V thresholds. Each alarm has active and tripped flags in ALARM_REG. Flags update at each conversion, with active flags clearing after the conversion and tripped flags clearing after ALARM_REG is read. Alarm status can be read from the ALARM pin, ALARM_REG, or appended data output.

Will Ma contrasts poker tournaments with cash games, explaining that tournaments have fixed buy-ins, rising blinds, elimination, survival-oriented strategy, less metagame, wider stack-size situations, and lower casino take, while cash games allow players to join, leave, rebuy, select tables, and target weaker opponents. He says the class focuses on tournaments because they are exciting, analytically simpler, and relevant to MIT Poker Club events, though strong fundamentals transfer between formats.

The lecture then covers preflop play, including typical equity categories: bigger pairs over smaller pairs, pairs versus overcards, dominated hands, two overcards versus pairs, and hands with all different cards. Ma emphasizes that suitedness matters more when behind and for implied odds. He encourages not fearing preflop all-ins in tournaments, especially with short stacks, and explains push/fold strategy, small blind versus big blind all-ins, exploitative reasoning, and Nash equilibrium ranges. He shows that if big blinds call too tightly, small blinds can profitably shove very wide, while optimal play balances shoving and calling frequencies.

Ma discusses how stack size, position, antes, and hand type affect all-in ranges, noting that position often matters more than stack depth. He explains calling all-ins with sufficient pot odds, especially from the big blind or after opening with shallow effective stacks. He also covers re-raising all-in, avoiding small raises when committed, using appropriate re-raise sizing, calling raises in position with deep stacks, adjusting raises against limpers, and avoiding plays that give opponents profitable extra options. The lecture ends with examples of straightforward all-in decisions and a plan to review tournament hand histories later.

The passage explains the S&P MidCap 400 index and E-mini S&P MidCap 400 futures. The S&P MidCap 400, formed in 1991, tracks 400 mid-sized U.S. companies with market capitalizations between $3.6 billion and $13.1 billion. It is market-cap weighted, rebalanced quarterly, and has ticker MID. The E-mini futures contract, ticker EMD, trades on CME Globex and represents $100 times the index value. It is used for hedging, speculation, arbitrage, and spread trading.

The contract trades Sunday to Friday from 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET, with daily breaks. It is financially settled, has quarterly contracts listed for five consecutive quarters, and trading ends at 9:30 a.m. ET on the third Friday of the contract month. Minimum price fluctuation is 0.10 index points, or $10 per contract, for outright Globex trading. The tick size is $10 for outright trading and $5 for BTIC and calendar spreads. The BTIC block minimum is 50 contracts.

The passage notes that S&P MidCap 400 seasonality tends to be stronger in winter and spring than in summer and fall. It mentions ETFs tracking the index, including IJH, SPMD, and EWMC. Backtested strategies described include a poor-performing volatility strategy and an overnight strategy with 362 trades, 0.31% average gain, 5% CAGR, 60% win rate, and 1.63 profit factor, though results were better on SPY and QQQ.

E-mini S&P MidCap 400 futures prices are affected by component stocks, interest rates, economic news, and the U.S. dollar. The all-time high cited for the futures is 2924.2 in November 2021; the index high is 2925.93 in November 2021, and the index low is 119.43 in June 1991. The main trading risk is adverse price movement because futures are leveraged.

Tyreek Hill returned to the Dolphins’ facility and spoke to teammates three days after season-ending surgery on a dislocated left knee. Coach Mike McDaniel said Hill encouraged the team to stay motivated. Miami will rely more on Jaylen Waddle, Malik Washington and tight end Darren Waller, though McDaniel said replacing Hill will require group execution rather than one player.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on November 9, 2021, its Board appointed Alex Gorsky as a director and member of the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. As a non-employee director, he will receive a $100,000 annual retainer, participate in the Non-Employee Director Stock Plan, and received an initial grant of 486 restricted stock units. Apple will enter into its standard director indemnification agreement with him, and no reportable transactions exist between Apple and Gorsky. The Board also amended Apple’s bylaws effective November 9, 2021, increasing the Board size from eight to nine members.

A Russell 2000 Death Cross occurs when the index’s 50-day moving average falls below its 200-day moving average and is often viewed as bearish. Rob Hanna’s study of 25 Russell Death Crosses since 1988 found that the S&P 500 rose in 21 cases, or 84%, over the following year, with the largest gain occurring in 2020 at over 60%. However, drawdowns were often sizable, so the signal is not considered perfect. The most recent Death Cross occurred in 2022, after which the S&P 500 fell. The passage notes the signal may be less reliable for the S&P 500 than for the Russell 2000 because small-cap stocks are generally more volatile.

The passage compiles July 17, 2001 news items mentioning Enron. Reports say James Fallon will lead Enron Broadband Services as it moves into Enron Wholesale Services, amid restructuring and a $102 million second-quarter loss. Another article discusses declining bandwidth markets, planned cutbacks, and Enron’s continued focus on intermediation, network services, and content. Rep. Henry Waxman urged a Justice Department review of Karl Rove’s contacts with companies including Enron while holding related stock; the White House denied wrongdoing. Other items cover Calpine’s approved Mississippi power plant permit plans near an Enron facility, EnronOnline’s trading volume growth and strategy, donations including Enron’s to Red Cross flood relief, and legal and political complications surrounding India’s Dabhol power project inquiry and Maharashtra’s prior support for Dabhol Phase II.

John Mellencamp knelt and raised his fist after performing “Easy Target” on “Late Show With Stephen Colbert,” supporting Black Lives Matter. The song addresses racial inequality. Mellencamp said taking a knee began as a protest against racial and social injustice but was politicized by the current administration.

The Ichimoku trading strategy is a technical analysis system that identifies support and resistance, trend direction, and momentum using multiple plotted averages that form a cloud. Its components are Tenkan-Sen, Kijun-Sen, Senkou Span A, Senkou Span B, and Chikou Span. Price above the cloud indicates an uptrend, while price below it indicates a downtrend; cloud thickness can indicate volatility. Tenkan/Kijun crossovers, Chikou Span signals, and Senkou Span support/resistance can be used alone or combined in systematic strategies.

The passage emphasizes that Ichimoku strategies should be backtested and forward-tested before use. Backtests on several assets suggested the strategy can reduce market exposure and drawdowns but often underperforms risk-adjusted buy-and-hold returns. Its main risk is unreliable or inaccurate signals, while its benefits include combining trend, support/resistance, and momentum analysis in one indicator.

The lecture covers supply-side modeling in static demand estimation, emphasizing how demand estimates, observed prices, ownership structure, and conduct assumptions can be used to recover marginal costs through firms’ first-order conditions. Because flexible marginal costs can rationalize many conduct models, additional assumptions or functional forms for costs are needed for testing. Joint estimation of demand and supply can improve precision and provide overidentifying restrictions for testing conduct models.

The lecture reviews BLP’s automobile demand results, highlighting the value of random coefficients for producing realistic substitution patterns. BLP’s model captures heterogeneous preferences and more plausible diversion to the outside option than simple logit models, especially across low- and high-end cars. The lecture also notes limitations of BLP, including its treatment of cars as non-durable goods, reliance on list prices, omission of dealerships, negotiated prices, and financing.

Nevo’s cereal market paper is discussed as an application of random coefficients demand and conduct testing. The cereal industry has many products but few major firms, making multiproduct pricing important. Nevo estimates demand, recovers markups under alternative conduct assumptions, and compares them with accounting-based margins. He rejects full collusion but not separate-brand or current-ownership pricing models. The lecture notes that demographic interactions explain much of the preference heterogeneity and that results differ substantially from simple logit estimates.

The final topic is the common ownership hypothesis, which argues that diversified institutional investors holding stakes in competing firms may soften competition. The lecture explains the theory through shareholder profit weights and connects it to multiproduct pricing incentives. Backus, Conlon, and Sinkinson document rising common ownership incentives, but their structural cereal-market test rejects common ownership, perfect competition, and monopoly in favor of own-profit maximization. The lecture concludes that common ownership remains debated, with skepticism partly due to uncertainty about the mechanism by which investors would influence firm conduct.

The passage previews Super Bowl 52 after the Denver Broncos’ disappointing 2017 season and notes local dislike for both the Patriots and Eagles. It encourages watching at local bars, casinos, lounges, and eateries, then presents predictions from TMJ staff, residents, business owners, and officials. Most pick New England to beat Philadelphia, often citing Tom Brady, Bill Belichick, and the Patriots’ experience, while several predict an Eagles upset behind Nick Foles and Philadelphia’s offense.

Microsoft filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2022. Revenue was $50.1 billion, up 11% from $45.3 billion in the prior-year quarter. Net income was $17.6 billion, down 14% from $20.5 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $2.35, down from $2.71. Operating income rose 6% to $21.5 billion.

Revenue by segment was $16.5 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $20.3 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $13.3 billion for More Personal Computing. Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 24% to $25.7 billion. Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 35%, Office 365 Commercial revenue grew 11%, LinkedIn revenue grew 17%, and Dynamics 365 revenue grew 24%. Windows OEM revenue declined 15%, and Xbox content and services revenue declined 3%.

Total assets were $359.8 billion as of September 30, 2022, compared with $364.8 billion as of June 30, 2022. Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $107.3 billion. Total liabilities were $186.2 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $173.6 billion. Net cash from operations was $23.2 billion.

Microsoft completed its acquisition of Nuance Communications on March 4, 2022, for $18.8 billion and reported Nuance within Intelligent Cloud. Microsoft also had an agreement to acquire Activision Blizzard for $68.7 billion, expected to close in fiscal year 2023 subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions. As of September 30, 2022, $36.1 billion remained under Microsoft’s $60.0 billion share repurchase program.

The passage presents a case on Bloomin’ Brands amid renewed investor interest in casual dining stocks in 2016, following the restaurant industry’s struggles during and after the Great Recession. In 2016, U.S. restaurant sales were projected near $800 billion, representing 4% of GDP and employing nearly 1 in 10 Americans. Casual dining offered a middle ground between fast food and fine dining, while fast casual emphasized higher quality than fast food with counter service.

Bloomin’ Brands began with the first Outback Steakhouse in Tampa, Florida, in 1988 and went public in 2012. By June 2016, it owned 1,335 restaurants and franchised 166 across Outback, Fleming’s, Bonefish Grill, and Carrabba’s; about 85% were in the U.S., and nearly two-thirds were Outback locations.

The passage lists 13 publicly traded restaurant companies as potential comparables, including Brinker, Buffalo Wild Wings, Cheesecake Factory, Chipotle, Cracker Barrel, Darden, DineEquity, McDonald’s, Panera, Shake Shack, Sonic, Texas Roadhouse, and Zoë’s Kitchen. Exhibits provide valuation multiples, income statement data, and balance sheet data. As of August 15, 2016, Bloomin’ had a $2.2 billion market capitalization, 40.2 trailing PE multiple, 12.6 forward PE multiple, 20.6% five-year average EPS growth, and 12.1% long-term EPS growth forecast.

The passage explains the 60/40 portfolio strategy, which allocates 60% to equities and 40% to bonds, often implemented through low-cost ETFs such as S&P 500 and Treasury or bond funds. It argues that the strategy works through diversification and the historical tendency of stocks and bonds to have low or negative correlation during market stress, though this failed in 2022 as both declined amid rising inflation.

The article cites Vanguard’s historical annual return of 8.8% since 1926 and notes that as of September 17, 2022, the portfolio had returned -17.77% year-to-date but 9.11% annualized over the prior 10 years. It also reports a 1.89% dividend yield, a -0.76 Sharpe ratio, 7.07% volatility, and a maximum drawdown of 21.85% since January 2010, recorded in March 2020.

Despite poor 2022 performance, the passage concludes the 60/40 portfolio is not dead, noting that past double-digit declines have often been followed by recoveries. It says investors may improve diversification by considering alternatives or additions such as the 80/20 portfolio, Ray Dalio’s All-Weather Portfolio, trend-following strategies, gold, crypto, international equities, tail risk strategies, and Thomas Carlson’s “Defense First” strategy.

The Rhode Island Supreme Court affirmed Andrew A. Bucci’s Superior Court conviction for furnishing legal advice to Robert Oliva while suspended from practicing law. The court held that recorded conversations provided ample evidence that Bucci advised Oliva on criminal litigation matters, including procedure, searches, venue, witnesses, and restitution. It rejected Bucci’s argument that the state had to prove pecuniary benefit, finding no such requirement in the statute. The court also declined to review his challenge to the six-month sentence because he had not first sought relief in Superior Court under Rule 35.

University of Liverpool researchers found that higher musical aptitude in 38 healthy adults was linked to lower hallucination proneness and greater corpus callosum integrity. Hallucination proneness was associated with reduced integrity in fibres connecting the brain hemispheres, suggesting corpus callosum microstructure mediates the relationship between musical aptitude and hallucination likelihood.

Global Agriculture Innovation & Solutions Ltd. (GAIS), a nonprofit working with 200 farmers in Gbudue state, urged South Sudan’s government to restrict international seed imports and support local suppliers. GAIS director Mike Gaga said FAO imported 100 metric tons of seed despite GAIS applying for a tender and producing about 150 metric tons of maize seed. Gbudue agriculture official Mariano Erneo said he was unaware FAO had brought in foreign seed and would seek details. FAO said it supports vulnerable farmers through seed distribution and seed fairs, follows transparent international procurement rules, and prioritizes local seed where possible. FAO’s South Sudan representative said GAIS has received prior support, and that imports were allowed under a government waiver due to low production and displacement. FAO plans to distribute 5,000 metric tons of seed this year.

Assam AHSEC Class 12 results 2018 will be released on May 31 at 9:30 am at ahsec.nic.in and resultsassam.nic.in, with examresults.net as an alternative. Exams were held from February 23 to March 22. Students need 20 marks in each subject to pass, while 70% or above qualifies for distinction. Results can be checked online, via SMS for different telecom users, or through apps after pre-registering the roll number.

Asian shares edged higher for a fourth session amid optimism on global growth and strong Chinese credit data, while Wall Street gained on technology and energy stocks. Markets largely ignored a New York commuter hub explosion. Investors awaited Federal Reserve and European Central Bank meetings, with JPMorgan expecting stronger Fed growth forecasts and possible higher 2018 rate projections, while the ECB was expected to maintain a low-rate stance. Despite wider U.S.-German yield spreads, the euro remained up 12% against the dollar this year. Forex trading was thin, bitcoin hit a record on Bitstamp, gold stayed weak after a sharp weekly fall, and oil firmed after a North Sea pipeline shutdown.

Coach Quenneville said playoff energy can be unpredictable and demanding, crediting players for their preparation and competitiveness. He discussed uncertainty around a player’s availability, confidence in top players despite scoring droughts, heavy defensive minutes, and line changes aimed at balance and production. He praised the penalty kill but emphasized staying out of the box against a strong power play. He also noted seeking advice from others, praised the team captain’s leadership in big moments, and described the series as tight and challenging after both teams came off seven-game series.

The study examined whether group-based brain parcellations bias estimates of functional connectivity differences between early psychosis patients and healthy controls. Using Human Connectome Project–Early Psychosis data, the authors compared standard Schaefer cortical atlases with individualized parcellations generated by the Group Prior Individualized Parcellation algorithm.

Individualized parcellation reassigned over 40% of cortical vertices relative to the group atlas, indicating substantial individual variability in functional organization. It produced slightly higher within-parcel functional homogeneity than the group-based approach in both controls and patients. Controls showed higher homogeneity than patients across both parcellation types.

Both parcellation methods identified widespread lower functional connectivity in patients compared with controls. However, group-based parcellations produced larger case-control differences and identified more dysconnected edges. Network Based Statistic analysis found one significant connected component for each method, comprising 2,712 edges with the group-based parcellation and 2,461 edges with the individualized parcellation, meaning the group-based method implicated about 9% more edges. The specific affected edges and regions differed notably between methods, including variation in medial frontal and insula regions, while network-level findings were more consistent. The control network was most affected in raw edge counts, especially connections between control and somatomotor networks.

The authors conclude that group-based parcellations may inflate functional connectivity differences in psychosis, while individualized parcellations provide more conservative and refined maps of brain dysconnectivity. Limitations included use of a low-resolution surface mesh, medicated patients, and clinical heterogeneity within the patient sample.

Stress after a spouse’s death can harm health, weaken immunity, and may contribute to heart attacks, broken heart syndrome, or higher mortality, though timing is often coincidental and underlying illness may be the main factor. George H.W. Bush, 93, was hospitalized with sepsis after Barbara Bush’s funeral and was recovering; doctors said stress may worsen infection risk or lead people to ignore symptoms, but Bush also had Parkinson’s disease and prior infections. Experts note grieving spouses need support because depression, poor eating, ignored symptoms, stress, and lack of rest can increase danger. The passage also cautions against overattributing deaths to “broken hearts,” citing Johnny Cash and Debbie Reynolds, whose deaths followed loved ones’ deaths but involved serious medical conditions.

The Japanese mobile game Tabikaeru has become popular in Taiwan, with psychologists saying it reflects users’ desire for companionship and a simpler life. Players care for a traveling frog without controlling it, creating an altruistic relationship. Its simplicity helps users relax. Despite being in Japanese, related searches in Taiwan rose sharply, and sales of frog-themed items increased.

Jacob Rees-Mogg was filmed trying to defuse scuffles after protesters disrupted a talk he was due to give at the University of the West of England in Bristol. Witnesses said a small group of masked protesters entered the hall shouting accusations including “fascist” and “racist,” prompting arguments with attendees. Rees-Mogg said they wanted to shut down the meeting but failed, and that he was not injured or physically threatened. He changed his topic to free speech and later continued the event. Witnesses said security arrived after several minutes and escorted the protesters out. UWE Bristol condemned the disruption, said police were called, and stated the protesters were not believed to be students or ticket holders.

The lecture reviews numerical methods covered so far: solving linear systems with MATLAB backslash, issues of ill conditioning, Newton-Raphson and dogleg methods for nonlinear equations, minimization links through fsolve and fmincon, and computational scaling. Implicit ODE methods require solving nonlinear systems at each time step, making cost depend on time steps, nonlinear iterations, and problem size, with Jacobian construction often important.

The professor introduces functionals as operations that take functions as inputs, such as fsolve, derivatives, gradients, Jacobians, and density functional theory applications.

The lecture then connects numerical integration, interpolation, and basis functions. Quadrature rules approximate a function using selected values, fit an interpolating or approximating function, and integrate that instead of the true function. Rectangle, midpoint, trapezoid, and Simpson’s rules can give misleading agreement or poor estimates depending on the function. Approximation quality depends on basis choice, number of parameters, and whether data points are exact or noisy.

Interpolation with basis functions leads to linear systems requiring nonsingular, preferably orthogonal, bases. Polynomial bases are common because they are easy to integrate and evaluate, but high-order polynomial interpolation can behave poorly. Monomials often produce ill-conditioned systems, while Lagrange and Newton polynomial bases have useful computational properties.

Gaussian quadrature chooses weights and points so integrals are exact for polynomials up to order \(2n-1\), often outperforming Simpson’s rule. Gauss-Kronrod-style comparisons can provide error estimates.

For multidimensional integrals, nested quadrature causes function evaluations to grow exponentially with dimension, illustrating the curse of dimensionality and motivating later methods with better scaling.

The study investigates software engineering challenges in integrating open-source and commercial large language models into financial report analysis workflows. It addresses two research questions: the main challenges in using LLMs for domain-specific report analysis, and how open-source and commercial LLMs compare in complexity, performance, and maintainability.

Using Design Science Research in collaboration with Getinge AB’s finance department, the study explored financial reporting tasks and developed two prototype solutions. Initial exploration identified financial commentary generation as a suitable use case, particularly summarizing changes in order intake and net sales. A third use case involving income statements was not pursued due to varied data formats and confidentiality constraints.

The first prototype used locally hosted open-source models through Ollama in a multi-agent workflow. It aimed to preserve data privacy and reduce external dependency. Smaller models struggled with hallucinations, instruction following, and inappropriate code generation. Larger local models improved output quality but remained limited by hardware constraints, instability, and error propagation across chained agents.

The second prototype used GPT-4o via API. It required less setup and produced more concise, professional summaries closer to financial reporting style. However, it sometimes omitted key drivers, mixed positive and negative trends, followed examples too rigidly, and struggled with strict formatting and conditional instructions. A later prompt-chained refinement improved analysis structure but did not fully resolve inconsistencies in final summaries.

Expert evaluation by business controllers found that both approaches could support early-stage drafting but required manual review before use in formal reporting. GPT-4o was preferred for external-style reporting, while the local solution showed potential for internal analysis. Common issues included redundancy, missed trends, unclear prioritization, incorrect regional attribution, lack of numerical context, and limited transparency.

The study identifies three main engineering challenges: task-specific prompt and system design, data preparation across heterogeneous financial sources, and constraints from sensitive financial data. It concludes that LLMs show promise for partially automating financial reporting workflows, but full end-to-end automation remains difficult due to reliability, formatting, traceability, and compliance requirements. Future work should explore rule-aware prompt templates, prompt versioning, stronger multi-agent coordination, fault isolation, and hybrid deployment strategies.

Hong Liu answers questions about the Hawking-Page transition, explaining that thermal AdS is AdS coupled to a thermal bath, dominated by a graviton or massless-particle gas. The transition is first-order: below a critical temperature, the thermal AdS phase is dominated by states with energy scaling as \(N^0\), while above it the black-hole phase is dominated by high-energy states of order \(N^2\) with larger entropy. The analogy to confinement/deconfinement is heuristic and based on free-energy scaling.

The lecture then introduces entanglement entropy. For a quantum system split into subsystems A and B, the Hilbert space factorizes as \(H_A \otimes H_B\). A state is entangled if it cannot be written as a single product state. The reduced density matrix \(\rho_A\) is obtained by tracing out B, and the entanglement entropy is the von Neumann entropy of \(\rho_A\). For pure states, \(S_A=S_B\), and zero entanglement entropy indicates an unentangled product state. For mixed states, entanglement entropy also includes classical statistical correlations.

A two-spin example illustrates entanglement entropy and maximally entangled states. Liu also states subadditivity and strong subadditivity inequalities for entropy, noting that they are intuitive classically but nontrivial quantum mechanically.

For quantum many-body systems, Liu explains that local Hamiltonians couple subsystems mainly near their shared boundary. In ground states of local Hamiltonians, entanglement entropy generally obeys an area law: the leading term is proportional to the area of the boundary of region A divided by a short-distance cutoff. This reflects dominance of short-range entanglement near the boundary, while subleading terms can encode long-range entanglement. Examples include topological entanglement entropy in \(2+1\)-dimensional gapped systems and the use of entanglement entropy to characterize degrees of freedom in conformal field theories, such as the central charge in \(1+1\)-dimensional CFTs.

The lecture then presents holographic entanglement entropy. For a CFT with a gravity dual, the Ryu-Takayanagi proposal states that the entanglement entropy of a boundary region A equals the area of the minimal bulk surface ending on \(\partial A\), divided by \(4G_N\). Liu notes that this formula is motivated by the black-hole entropy formula and is supported by checks such as satisfying strong subadditivity and reproducing known CFT results.

As an example, for a \(1+1\)-dimensional CFT dual to \(AdS_3\), the minimal curve for an interval is a semicircle in hyperbolic space, giving \(S_A=\frac{c}{3}\log(L/\epsilon)\), matching the known CFT result. At finite temperature, when the boundary region becomes the whole space, the holographic entanglement entropy reduces to the black-hole entropy. Liu concludes that the Ryu-Takayanagi formula suggests a deep relation between spacetime geometry and quantum information, connecting quantum information, many-body physics, quantum field theory, black holes, string theory, and gravity.

The passage outlines four key challenges for QED and quantum optics in attoscience: generating large-photon-number quantum states of light; producing entangled quantum states of light and matter in complex materials; developing ultrafast methods to characterize and exploit these states; and simulating strong-field dynamics with quantum platforms such as cold atoms and trapped ions. It emphasizes the need for quantum field-theoretical treatments of strong-field physics.

Recent progress includes fully quantized and hybrid theoretical models, attosecond metrology for photon statistics and quantum-state probing, structured and squeezed light sources, advanced material platforms such as 2D, correlated, and topological systems, quantum simulators, and ultrafast quantum-optical measurement tools. These advances aim to enable reproducible and scalable generation of high-photon-number quantum states.

The passage concludes that strong-field interactions are becoming a route to engineer non-classical light and matter states, with future developments depending on more complex materials, light fields, and measurement techniques. Potential outcomes include scalable quantum light sources, quantum simulation platforms, and ultrafast quantum processors.

The DAWN-plasma study was a randomized, open-label, multicenter phase 2 trial evaluating standard of care plus convalescent plasma versus standard of care alone in hospitalized adult COVID-19 patients. Participants were randomized 2:1; 320 received plasma plus standard care and 163 received standard care. Plasma patients were intended to receive four units totaling 800–1000 mL, with most units having high neutralizing antibody titers.

The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive and free of mechanical ventilation on Day 15. Results showed no difference between groups: 83.7% in the plasma group versus 84.1% in the control group. No statistically significant differences were found for secondary endpoints, including mortality, Day 30 outcomes, clinical status, laboratory markers, or vital signs. Adverse events, serious adverse events, and fatal adverse events were similar between groups. Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 19 of 320 plasma patients, with no TRALI cases reported. The study concluded that early high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not change the course of hospitalized COVID-19.

A hockey player discusses facing elimination, emphasizing the need to stay physical, disciplined, and focused on winning the next game before thinking ahead. Yankees shortstop Anthony Volpe played most of the season with a partially torn shoulder labrum suffered in early May and may need offseason action. After struggling statistically in 2025 and the postseason, Volpe said no decision has been made on surgery and that he will reassess with the team.

This proof-of-principle prospective longitudinal study evaluated whether next-generation sequencing of liquid biopsies could detect cancer-related DNA mutations before clinical diagnosis of oral potentially malignant lesions (OPMLs) or oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) in Fanconi anemia (FA) patients, who have high HNSCC risk and limited treatment tolerance.

Sixteen Spanish FA patients without prior solid or blood malignancies were enrolled between 2018 and 2021. Saliva and/or plasma were collected at 50 time points, and DNA was analyzed using the Oncomine Pan-Cancer Cell-Free Assay. Sequencing performance was generally better in saliva than plasma, with lower limits of detection. No copy-number variants were detected, but non-synonymous small variants were found in 15 samples from 9 patients, most frequently in TP53.

Among 14 patients with follow-up after liquid biopsy collection, 7 developed oral lesions or carcinomas and 7 did not. Mutations were detected before clinical diagnosis in 6 of 7 patients who later developed lesions or tumors, with lead times of 23 to 630 days. No mutations were found in samples from 5 lesion-free patients. Mutation presence was associated with significantly different oral lesion/tumor-free survival, with reported diagnostic accuracy of 92%, sensitivity of 86%, and specificity of 100%.

The study concludes that deep sequencing of saliva and plasma may help stratify FA patients by risk of developing OPMLs or OSCC and could support closer surveillance, particularly in patients without visible lesions. Larger longitudinal studies with longer follow-up are needed to assess earlier diagnosis potential.

The passage explains common football offensive line blocks and their purposes. Mental health experts in B.C. are urging suicide barriers on major Lower Mainland bridges, citing research that barriers prevent deaths and reduce attempts elsewhere. The crisis centre said half of jumping suicides from 1991 to 2007 occurred on five bridges. Crisis phones on Burrard Bridge have also connected at-risk people to 24/7 support.

This January 2025 ebook is Volume IV of Foreign Relations of the United States, 1981–1988, covering the Soviet Union from January 1983 to March 1985. The Office of the Historian created the ebook to provide the full content of FRUS volumes in a portable, searchable format usable offline, while preserving fidelity to printed editions. The FRUS series is the official documentary record of major U.S. foreign policy decisions and diplomatic activity. Its preparation is governed by standards of objectivity, accuracy, transparency about deletions, comprehensive documentation, and publication within 30 years of the events recorded. The volume’s sources were mainly from the Department of State and the National Archives.

This illustrated atlas links research and practice in periodontal plastic surgery and cosmetic dentistry, covering evidence-based decision making, treatment planning, recession defects, soft tissue substitutes, crown lengthening, peri-implant surgery, case studies, systematic review summaries, multidisciplinary decisions, and soft tissue augmentation decision trees for dental clinicians.

Participants were in the study for up to 26 months, and the full study took about 33 months, ending in February 2023. In Phase 2/3, two 30 µg doses of BNT162b2 were 95% effective at preventing COVID-19 from 7 days after Dose 2 through 03 December 2020, with similar results regardless of past COVID-19 infection. BNT162b2 and BNT162b2SA produced immune responses against the original virus strain and Beta variant that researchers judged unlikely due to chance.

Safety findings showed that injection site reactions and systemic events were generally well tolerated, short-lived, and mostly mild or moderate; pain, tiredness, and headache were common. Some Phase 1 participants had temporary lymphocyte decreases after Dose 1 that generally returned to normal. BNT162b2 30 µg was selected for Phase 2/3, while BNT162b1 100 µg was stopped after Dose 1 due to reactions or systemic events. Serious medical problems were uncommon, and researchers generally did not consider them related to study vaccines, though a few temporary serious problems in participants aged 16 years and older were considered possibly related. No deaths occurred in Phase 1; deaths in Phase 2/3 had different causes and were not believed to be caused by BNT162b2.

FDA drug regulator George Tidmarsh raised safety concerns on LinkedIn about voclosporin, a lupus nephritis drug approved in 2021, saying it has “significant toxicity” and lacks demonstrated direct clinical benefit. Scientists found that pollen collected by honeybees contains beneficial actinobacteria, especially Streptomyces, that produce antimicrobial compounds against bee and plant pathogens. Researchers sampled pollen from native plants and a nearby hive, identifying related bacterial strains in both. Many inhibited the mold causing stonebrood and showed activity against some honeybee bacterial pathogens. Genome evidence indicated the bacteria were plant endophytes. The findings suggest diverse plant landscapes may support bee health and that beneficial bacteria could help develop ecofriendly treatments for hives and crops.

The passage compares value and growth investing. Value investing buys undervalued stocks with strong fundamentals, often for stability, dividends, and long-term appreciation. Growth investing buys companies with strong future growth potential regardless of valuation, offering higher potential returns but higher volatility and risk. Backtesting can assess past performance and help determine an optimal mix of value and growth stocks.

Recent ETF backtests showed growth outperforming value, including small-cap growth outperforming small-cap value. However, longer historical data cited since 1926 showed value outperforming growth. The passage states that growth’s recent outperformance is unusual and that value has experienced a long drawdown since about 2007.

Risk is described mainly as volatility, with volatile small-cap stocks identified as especially risky. The passage argues that low-volatility, lower-market-value “boring” stocks may be preferable. It also presents a value-growth rotation strategy using momentum, a ratio, and moving averages, stating that the model outperformed holding either factor alone while reducing volatility and drawdown.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPU architecture, focusing on GA102 and GA104 GPUs used in products such as GeForce RTX 3090, RTX 3080, RTX 3070, NVIDIA RTX A6000, and NVIDIA A40. GA10x builds on Turing and is described as delivering up to 1.7x faster traditional raster graphics and up to 2x faster ray tracing. GA102 is fabricated on Samsung’s 8nm 8N NVIDIA Custom Process, includes 28.3 billion transistors, and a full configuration has 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores.

Key architectural changes include doubled FP32 processing in the GA10x SM, second-generation RT Cores with doubled ray/triangle intersection throughput and motion blur acceleration, and third-generation Tensor Cores supporting new data types such as TF32 and BF16 plus structured sparsity. The architecture also increases L1/shared memory capacity and bandwidth, moves ROPs into the GPC, supports PCIe Gen 4, and offers third-generation NVLink on GA102 products.

The GeForce RTX 3090 is positioned for 8K HDR gaming with 24GB of GDDR6X memory and DLSS 8K support. The RTX 3080 is described as offering up to 2x the performance of the RTX 2080, while the RTX 3070 rivals the prior GeForce RTX 2080 Ti. The RTX A6000 and A40 include 48GB of GDDR6 memory, support NVLink scaling to 96GB, and target professional visualization, rendering, AI, compute, and data center workloads.

GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory, developed with Micron, using PAM4 signaling to reach up to 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/sec of peak bandwidth. NVIDIA RTX IO is presented as a technology suite for GPU-based loading and decompression of game and creative assets, working with Microsoft DirectStorage to reduce CPU workload and improve I/O throughput.

The passage also covers display and media features, including DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, HDCP support, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode up to 8K60 HDR, and seventh-generation NVENC for hardware video encoding. Appendices provide additional GPU specifications, Error Detection and Replay technology for GDDR6X memory overclocking, RTX A6000 performance comparisons, and NVIDIA legal notices.

U.S. Navy-trained dolphins and handlers arrived in Mexico to help locate the few remaining critically endangered vaquita porpoises in the Gulf of California. Beginning Oct. 12, Mexican authorities and international experts plan to capture vaquitas and place them in a nearly completed sanctuary, though experts say the effort is risky because vaquitas have never been held or bred in captivity. Fewer than 30 are estimated to remain, largely due to illegal nets set for totoaba fish. Mexico has banned gillnet fishing in the northern Gulf. Conservationists support the rescue attempt but warn it should not allow continued fishing in vaquita habitat. Mexico also announced a fishing ban around the Revillagigedo Islands, creating what officials called North America’s largest unfished marine park.

Authorities said they had found no clear motive for Stephen Paddock’s Las Vegas shooting, which killed 58 and injured hundreds. Police reported no credible link to the Islamic State group despite its claim of responsibility and pledged to continue investigating.

Manuel and Esther Kitrosser sued CIT Group/Factoring after CIT liquidated collateral they had pledged to secure guarantees of debts owed by Top Form Mills and Top Blush, corporations connected to Mr. Kay. CIT had provided factoring and lending services to the corporations, which filed for bankruptcy in 1988 and were later dissolved. The Kays claimed CIT wrongfully retained and liquidated their collateral, including by charging postpetition interest and settling with the EDA for less than the guaranteed portion of a term loan.

The court held that postpetition interest on Top Form’s debts continued to accrue because the bankruptcy proceedings were dismissed without discharge, leaving the debts enforceable. Since the Kays’ guarantees were unconditional and covered Top Form’s indebtedness and obligations, CIT could apply their collateral to the debt, including postpetition interest. The court also held that CIT’s settlement with the EDA did not reduce Mr. Kay’s liability under his guarantee, which allowed CIT to compromise with other guarantors without affecting his obligations.

The court further held that the Kays’ amended claims, based on CIT’s reduction of Top Blush’s advance rate, did not relate back to the original complaint and were time-barred. CIT’s summary judgment motion was granted in part, and the amended complaint’s fifth and sixth causes of action were dismissed with prejudice.

The passage presents an AI-based computer science laboratory management system designed to improve practical skill development, reduce cheating, and provide richer assessment. The system generates unique lab questions for each student using faculty-provided keywords and difficulty levels, supports proctored and non-proctored modes, and includes gamified quizzes, coding tasks, and an AI-based viva to evaluate conceptual understanding and reasoning.

The system has faculty and student dashboards. Faculty can create labs, assign them to classes, set topic keywords, difficulty, viva duration, mode, descriptions, and instructions, view analytics, manage allocations, and override AI-generated scores. Students receive unique lab questions, submit code, complete AI-proctored viva sessions, view feedback reports, and may publish selected work to GitHub or Hugging Face.

A synthetic dataset of 10,000 ML and AI programming questions was constructed using Python scripts, ChatGPT, and Perplexity AI, with manual review. Each record includes an ID, question, Python answer, difficulty category, AI score, and faculty score. The question generator uses a fine-tuned CodeLlama model, while evaluation uses Sentence-BERT embeddings with XGBoost regression.

Experiments assessed dataset quality, question diversity, AI-faculty grading agreement, and fine-tuned evaluator performance. Generated questions showed diversity and faculty-rated appropriateness of 4.7/5. AI and faculty grading showed strong agreement, with Pearson correlation 0.914, Spearman correlation 0.892, and Cohen’s κ = 0.69. The evaluator achieved RMSE = 3.37 and R² = 0.861, with most prediction errors within ±5 marks. Largest deviations occurred in sequence-heavy labs such as LSTM, GRU, Transformer, and reinforcement learning tasks.

Berkshire Hills Bancorp reported Q1 2018 core EPS of $0.65, up 12% from Q4 and 18% year over year, with GAAP EPS of $0.55. Core ROA was 1.04%, core return on tangible equity was about 13.4%–13.5%, and the efficiency ratio remained below 60%. Management expects Q2 core EPS around $0.70 and GAAP EPS around $0.65, with full-year core EPS growth of 17% to 20%, core ROA above 1%, and efficiency below 60%. Q2 noninterest income is expected to rise about 10%, supported by seasonal strength in mortgage and SBA activity, while expenses are expected to increase in the low single digits.

Boston-area deposits exceed $400 million, and Greater Boston-related loans are approaching $2 billion. Commercial pipelines exceed $200 million, and the mortgage pipeline is $344 million. Management expects mid- to high-single-digit loan growth, with high-single-digit commercial loan growth, and said M&A is not a current priority compared with improving profitability and integrating recent growth. The passage presents a DFT+DMFT-based study of local and non-local self-energy effects on the electronic spectra of strongly correlated itinerant magnets in the paramagnetic phase. The approach uses a tight-binding multi-orbital Hubbard model with density-density Coulomb interactions, DMFT local self-energy, and non-local self-energy corrections from charge and spin fluctuations.

Numerical calculations are performed for α-iron, CrO₂, CrTe₂, and altermagnet CrSb using Quantum Espresso, Wannier90, CT-QMC, and analytic continuation. For iron and CrO₂, non-local magnetic correlations near the Curie temperature produce pronounced band shifts and splittings, making the spectra qualitatively similar to ferromagnetic DFT band structures. For CrTe₂ and CrSb, whose d-state fillings are closer to half filling, strong band splitting already appears from local spin correlations, while non-local corrections are weaker or enhance the splitting.

The study concludes that local and non-local magnetic correlations can generate split dispersive bands near van Hove singularities above magnetic transition temperatures. These bands lack definite spin polarization but carry partial spectral weight, resembling Hubbard subbands while remaining dispersive. The effects may influence transport and could be sensitive to weak magnetic fields. The density-density approximation overestimates magnetic transition temperatures, motivating future work with SU(2)-symmetric Hund interaction and studies of other observables.

The passage argues that large interstate corporations and trusts should not be destroyed but regulated to prevent misconduct and protect the public good. Congress is urged to pass reasonable and effective legislation, and if existing constitutional authority proves inadequate, to amend the Constitution to secure the needed power.

The passage compiles June 1, 2001 news items mentioning Enron. California lawmakers also considered plans to rescue Southern California Edison, including shifting costs to large business customers, while Enron lobbied for direct-access contracts with major commercial users.

Several items address Enron’s Dabhol Power Company in India. Officials said a new package was being developed to resolve Dabhol’s dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board over power costs and unpaid bills, while commentary urged allowing Dabhol to sell power to other buyers and renegotiating terms to reduce tariffs. Fitch placed India’s rating outlook on negative, citing fiscal concerns and noting Enron’s invocation of a central government guarantee.

Other reports note foreign companies buying Indian affiliates, ExxonMobil and Shell being favored for Saudi gas project leadership roles alongside other participants including Enron, Thomas E. White becoming Secretary of the Army after serving as vice chairman of Enron Energy Services, and construction beginning on a Cogentrix power plant in Mississippi with an Enron subsidiary as engineering and construction contractor.

The passage introduces GEM, a cryo-EM reconstruction framework that uses 3D Gaussian Splatting to model protein density explicitly in real space. Cryo-EM reconstructs 3D macromolecular density from many noisy 2D particle projections, often using Fourier-space methods based on the Fourier slice theorem. These methods are efficient but can incur information loss. Recent NeRF-based real-space approaches improve resolution but are slow and memory-intensive because they require dense volume sampling, full-image CTF application, and gradients over large 3D representations.

GEM represents protein density as a sparse set of 3D Gaussians placed in nonzero-density regions. Each Gaussian contributes to multiple pixels through parallel rasterization, and gradients are computed only for Gaussians affecting each pixel, reducing memory and computation compared with NeRF-based methods. The framework projects 3D Gaussians into 2D using closed-form integration, applies the CTF, and optimizes the representation against measured cryo-EM images.

Experiments on four widely used cryo-EM datasets show that GEM uses less memory, trains faster, and achieves better reconstruction quality than CryoDRGN and CryoNeRF. The passage reports GSFSC resolutions below 3 Å across datasets and up to 48× faster training than existing methods.

The paper presents new results on boundedness of Bergman-type projections in tubular domains over symmetric cones and products of such domains, with applications to analytic function spaces in several complex variables. It defines tube domains, weighted mixed-norm Bergman spaces, Bergman projections, reproducing kernels, and related notation. The paper also states a sharp decomposition theorem for Bergman \(A^1_\alpha\) spaces in tube domains, discusses related open problems for harmonic function spaces, and notes possible extensions to other domains. It reviews basic definitions of symmetric cones, including convex, self-dual, homogeneous, symmetric, and irreducible cones, as well as preliminary facts on Euclidean Jordan algebras and determinant functions.

The study investigates C–C bond formation from two methylene units to ethylene on gold surfaces using DFT with 2D periodic models. Because full dendritic gold structures are computationally infeasible, the work compares a gold monolayer with a three-layer gold surface to assess thickness effects on adsorption, reaction pathways, and energetics.

Calculations used PBE-D3 with Becke-Johnson damping in Turbomole, fixed gold atoms, and constrained optimizations along reaction paths with 14 structures for each surface. Adsorption energies were corrected for basis set superposition error.

Both surfaces show an initial diffusion stage followed by bond formation and a steep energy decrease. The monolayer gives stronger adsorption for reactants and products, a more exothermic reaction energy (−432.06 kJ mol−1 versus −335.50 kJ mol−1), and a much lower activation energy (4.78 kJ mol−1 versus 52.10 kJ mol−1). Products are weakly bound on both surfaces, especially on three gold layers.

Reaction behavior differs by thickness. On the monolayer, methylene fragments translate toward each other, associate through a shared proton, and then form the C=C bond as the proton shifts toward the gold layer. On three layers, rotational motion is more pronounced, intermediate association occurs at larger separation, and bond formation follows after further rotation. The authors conclude that gold layer thickness strongly affects adsorption, reaction pathways, and energetics, likely due to differences in availability of gold valence electrons. Further studies are suggested for other surface structures, defects, additional layers, and curvature.

Reagan argued that the United States needed a long-range diplomatic strategy, real friends, and renewed national strength. AMD testing identifies TMPM performance guidelines: use commands with at least 16 pages, with maximum performance at 128 pages; keep the command ring buffer filled; avoid interrupts on every command; and use low-water mark interrupts to refill the queue. System activity involving the data fabric, DMA, or IOMMU can reduce performance.

Several structures do not support migration, including SPA-accessed IOMMU memory structures, vIOMMU private address space page tables, pinned vIOMMU backing storage, the ring buffer, and argument pages. HV/OS software must avoid issuing migration commands for them. For PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, source pages must be DMA-mapped through one IOMMU host page table, and TMPM may non-atomically modify host page table entries, so software must avoid concurrent hPTE changes.

TMPM firmware can be reloaded only when no operations are in flight. HV/OS must pause operations, tear down the ring buffer, and issue the reload through the BIOS-to-PSP mailbox protocol. Reload fails if the ring buffer remains initialized, if the firmware version is older, or if other reload issues occur. Drivers should check ENGINE_READY before communicating with firmware. EPYC reload handling is selected using PM_GET_CAPABILITIES and FW_VER_Major.

TMPM moves data only between 4 KB-aligned pages, except host page table entry physical addresses, which are 8-byte aligned. Commands are submitted through a page migration ring buffer separate from SEV/SNP. Each command references a 4 KB parameter page containing 1–128 migration entries. Ring buffer pages must be DEFAULT or HV_FIXED, while argument pages may also be HV pages.

The TMPM interface uses mailbox registers and a ring buffer supporting parallel execution, so command execution order is not guaranteed. Firmware controls the read pointer, software controls the write pointer, and the ring buffer configuration cannot be changed during operation. Device initialization requires checking ENGINE_READY, setting ring buffer address and configuration, setting PM_WritePtr to zero, optionally configuring interrupts and pause mode, and waiting for DRIVER_INIT_COMPLETE. Shutdown requires pausing or draining the queue, clearing DRIVER_INITIALIZED, and cleanup.

TMPM interrupts include ring buffer write pointer errors, ring buffer memory errors, queue empty, low threshold, command error, and command completion. Some interrupt sources are configurable, while RBWritePtr_Err and RBMem_Err are not. Software may clear interrupt status only when the queue is empty or paused.

PM_GET_CAPABILITIES reports firmware capabilities and versions. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates hypervisor-owned or non-SNP pages and can update IOMMU host PTEs, but does not directly support 2 MB page migration. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages, requires RMP_ENFORCE, disallows DMA to migrating pages, and requires appropriate source, destination, and guest context states. NOP can mark the end of command sequences and request interrupt on completion.

TMPM reports command and migration-entry errors through status and sub-status fields, while ring buffer errors appear in PM_STATUS. Hardware-related failures may also be reported through MCA. If a TMPM operation times out or hardware errors occur, software should log errors and decide whether to save state, terminate VMs, stop issuing TMPM commands, or reboot.

Coach Sutter said both teams played well and that his team had good opportunities but needed to finish more chances against the New York Rangers. He said preparation is planned around travel and schedule, not judged by morning skate. He discussed lineup decisions, player roles, and the importance of consistency, praising a player for scoring big goals and understanding his role. Investing.com reports that market momentum remains intact but charts show early warnings. The S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July and 7.8% year-to-date, though it fell 1.6% on the first day of August. Volatility and credit spreads are rising seasonally, portfolios are increasingly weighted toward tech, and U.S. electricity demand reached a new high. The passage also includes market headlines, advertising, and risk disclosures about trading financial instruments and cryptocurrencies.

Ray Whitney said the team remains in a good position despite a tough loss and must move on to the next game. He defended the goaltender, citing his strong playoff performance, noted injuries are part of the playoffs, and said others must fill in if needed. He also pointed to penalties and a bad start as factors but rejected distractions as an excuse.
