The North Carolina Aquarium at Pine Knoll Shores held “Suds for Sharks” to raise funds for sand tiger shark research and a diver-supported cataloging system to help track and protect the species.

ICRA said the Union Budget 2018-19’s 20.8% increase in infrastructure outlay to Rs. 5.97 lakh crore would boost the rural economy through rural roads, housing, sanitation, irrigation and water supply. It noted higher allocations for rural and urban housing, irrigation projects and roads, while stressing the need for deeper bond markets and alternative funding routes for infrastructure financing.

Ghana marked the African Union Day of the African Child, focusing on child protection, empowerment and equal opportunity under the 2030 Agenda. Officials highlighted government initiatives including school feeding, capitation grants and free education, as well as child welfare and justice policies. The Gender Ministry said efforts were underway to address children loitering on streets, while UNICEF emphasized protecting children from violence, abuse and exploitation.

The On-Balance Volume (OBV) Trading Strategy is a volume-based technical indicator used to assess buying and selling pressure by adding volume on days when price closes higher and subtracting volume on days when price closes lower. OBV generally rises with uptrends and falls with downtrends, confirming whether volume supports price movement. Divergences can suggest weakening trends, while advanced breakouts or breakdowns may indicate trend continuation, though these patterns are difficult to backtest.

OBV was first published in 1963 by Joseph Granville in *New Key to Stock Market Profits*. He viewed volume as a key force behind major market moves and linked OBV to institutional “smart money” activity. The formula depends on whether today’s close is higher, lower, or equal to the previous close.

The passage backtests OBV on SPY using RSI applied to the OBV indicator. One tested setup, using a 5-day RSI and a buy threshold of 30, produced 337 trades, an average gain of 0.55% per trade, a 73% win rate, 24% maximum drawdown, and a 2.09 profit factor. The author concludes that volume has limited value overall and that OBV alone may not be an optimal trading parameter.

Former headteacher Christine Wright, featured on Channel 4’s The Great British Skinny Dip, denied reports that she was forced out, sacked or disciplined after being “outed” as a naturist. She said someone contacted her employers to hurt her, leading to prejudice that affected her health, and she was later granted early retirement on ill-health grounds. Wright said naturists can face misconceptions, including suspicion from those who wrongly link naturism with paedophilia. She now works for British Naturists as manager of legal and campaigns groups, helping challenge prejudice and recruit members. The documentary followed British Naturism’s efforts to attract people to public skinny dips and address misconceptions.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 1, 2017 reported third-quarter net sales of $45.4 billion, up from $42.4 billion a year earlier, and net income of $8.7 billion, up from $7.8 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.67, compared with $1.42. For the first nine months of fiscal 2017, net sales were $176.7 billion and net income was $37.6 billion.

Total assets were $345.2 billion as of July 1, 2017, including $18.6 billion in cash and cash equivalents, $58.2 billion in short-term marketable securities, and $184.8 billion in long-term marketable securities. Total liabilities were $212.7 billion, including $12.0 billion in commercial paper and $96.6 billion in aggregate principal amount of term debt. Shareholders’ equity was $132.4 billion.

Third-quarter sales increased in all geographic segments except Greater China. Americas net sales rose 13% to $20.4 billion, Europe rose 11% to $10.7 billion, Japan rose 3% to $3.6 billion, and Rest of Asia Pacific rose 15% to $2.7 billion. Greater China sales fell 10% to $8.0 billion. Product sales included $24.8 billion from iPhone, $5.6 billion from Mac, $5.0 billion from iPad, $7.3 billion from Services, and $2.7 billion from Other Products. Services sales increased 22%.

Gross margin was $17.5 billion, or 38.5% of net sales. Operating expenses were $6.7 billion, including $2.9 billion for research and development and $3.8 billion for selling, general and administrative expenses. Apple used $7.5 billion to repurchase shares and paid $3.4 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents during the quarter.

Apple stated that it had appealed the European Commission’s State Aid Decision regarding Ireland, which announced a recovery amount of up to €13 billion plus interest. The company also disclosed ongoing proceedings in Apple Inc. v. Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd., with no further amounts recognized because the case remained subject to further proceedings.

A first-year student describes trying to delete social media from their phone to focus on revision and real-life interaction, after realizing they spent significant time switching between apps and following people they barely knew. The passage argues that social media encourages comparison, escapism, procrastination, and validation-seeking, and cites studies linking higher use to depression and Instagram to poorer mental health among young people. The student found quitting difficult and isolating, partly because friends still used social media, and eventually returned to checking Twitter and Facebook in limited ways. They conclude that social media can drain mental energy and waste time unless used productively, while suggesting phone-monitoring apps and creative habits as ways to reduce dependence during exams.

The lecture transitions from linear algebra to solving systems of nonlinear equations and later optimization. It reviews singular value decomposition, condition numbers for any matrix via singular values, and iterative methods. For iterative solutions, convergence can be judged using function norm criteria, based on residual size, and step norm criteria, based on changes between iterations with absolute and relative tolerances; both can fail and are often used together. Numerical results should be validated through multiple methods, experiments, or analytical limits.

Systems of nonlinear equations are defined as finding roots of vector-valued functions \(f(x)=0\). Unlike linear systems, nonlinear systems may have no solutions, one or more locally unique solutions, or infinitely many solutions. Chemical engineering examples include equations of state, energy balances, and nonlinear reaction balances. A Van der Waals phase-equilibrium example leads to nonlinear equations for saturation pressure and gas and liquid molar volumes.

The lecture introduces locally unique solutions and the inverse function theorem: if \(f(x^*)=0\) and the Jacobian determinant at \(x^*\) is nonzero, then \(x^*\) is locally unique. The Jacobian contains partial derivatives of function components with respect to variables and supports local linearization. Linearization approximates nonlinear functions near a point with an error typically of order \(\Delta x^2\).

Newton-Raphson methods solve nonlinear systems by linearizing around the current guess and solving a linear system involving the Jacobian to choose the next step. The method can converge quadratically near locally unique roots but may fail or slow down with poor initial guesses, singular or ill-conditioned Jacobians, or non-locally unique solutions. An example using intersecting circles illustrates convergence regions, dependence on initial guesses, and problems near where the Jacobian determinant is zero.

In Bost v. Illinois State Board of Elections, the Supreme Court will consider whether Rep. Michael Bost has standing to challenge Illinois’ rule counting mail ballots received up to 14 days after Election Day if postmarked by then. Bost argues the rule is preempted by federal election law.

Lower courts dismissed the case for lack of standing. The 7th Circuit rejected Bost’s vote-dilution claim as a generalized grievance and found his claimed added costs for observers self-imposed and speculative. Before the Supreme Court, Bost focuses on those costs as pocketbook injury and argues the rule harms his electoral prospects, including fundraising, campaign spending, and future challenges tied to his margin of victory.

Bost also urges a broader rule that candidates have standing to challenge rules governing their elections, even when the rules do not directly regulate candidates. He argues this would simplify standing doctrine and prevent candidates, especially in noncompetitive or minor-party races, from being unable to challenge alleged election illegalities. The United States supports Bost’s narrower standing argument but opposes a blanket candidate-standing rule.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated October 2, 2017, furnishing a press release as Exhibit 99.1 under Items 2.02 and 7.01. The report was signed by CFO Deepak Ahuja and states the information is not deemed filed under Section 18 except by specific reference.

The study evaluated the Happy Ring, a finger-worn sleep-tracking device measuring electrodermal activity, accelerometry, photoplethysmography-derived heart rate, and skin temperature. It compared two scoring approaches, Happy Generalized and Happy Personalized, against laboratory polysomnography, at-home Dreem headband recordings, and other wearables including Oura, Whoop, Fitbit, and Actiwatch.

Data were analyzed from 36 healthy adults across 77 nights. Participants completed one laboratory night and two home nights. The study assessed sleep-wake detection, sleep staging, total sleep time, and wake after sleep onset.

In the laboratory, Happy Personalized and Happy Generalized achieved sleep-wake detection accuracies of 0.92 and 0.91, respectively, compared with 0.88 for Oura, 0.86 for Whoop, 0.84 for Fitbit, and 0.85 for Actiwatch. Happy Personalized showed significantly higher accuracy and specificity than the other devices. At home, Happy Personalized and Happy Generalized achieved accuracies of 0.92 and 0.91, while Oura, Whoop, Fitbit, and Actiwatch ranged from 0.89 to 0.92.

For sleep staging, the Happy Ring showed moderate agreement with laboratory and home polysomnography for light, deep, and REM sleep, similar to other devices. The personalized algorithm performed better than the generalized approach and other devices for sleep stage classification.

The study concludes that the Happy Ring performed well for sleep-wake detection and comparably for sleep staging, with the personalized algorithm improving specificity and overall performance. Limitations included a small, generally healthy sample, use of Dreem for home polysomnography, and undisclosed scoring algorithms.

The Winston County Library is hosting summer reading programs for children ages 3-5, first through fifth graders, and teens entering sixth through twelfth grades. Activities include storytime, magic shows, workshops, guest speakers, awards days, games, and Wet ’N Wild events. Featured guests include Dorian LaChance, The Snakeman, Todd Smith, Tommy Terrific, Andy Children, Mayor Will Hill, Susan Clark, and Johnny Lowe. Grand prizes include $50 Wal-Mart gift cards. Librarian Beth Edwards said local business sponsors and the Louisville Banker’s Association make the educational and entertaining programs possible.

The Hanover Insurance Group will release its second quarter financial results after market close on August 1, 2018, and webcast a discussion on August 2 at 8:00 a.m. ET via its website. The company is a property and casualty insurance holding company distributing products through independent agents and brokers.

Oil prices were flat Monday after early declines on concerns about Chinese demand were offset by possible supply reductions in Libya. Libya’s NOC opened an investigation into security violations at the Sharara field, while workers at the Zueitina terminal threatened to block a tanker over pay demands. Brent crude traded at $51.73 a barrel, down 37 cents, and U.S. WTI was at $48.62, down 20 cents. Potential Libyan cutbacks could improve OPEC compliance with output limits, though Libya’s recent production recovery has contributed to global supply growth. Prices had earlier fallen after China’s July refinery runs dropped more than expected.

The author says he accepts the scientific consensus on climate change despite not being able to evaluate the science himself. He questions whether warming and CO2 causation could be partly two-way, while acknowledging that science says CO2 causes warming and may become harmful. He argues laypeople cannot reliably “do their own research” because they lack expert context. He believes climate scientists are probably right but are less persuasive than skeptics, relying on facts, models, and criticism of opponents in ways he says may reduce credibility.

The post also notes a California law banning handheld phone use while driving and promotes the author’s WhenHub app as a way to reduce texting while meeting people by sharing temporary location approaches.

A woman died after being struck by an Uber self-driving vehicle in Tempe, Arizona. Uber suspended its autonomous vehicle tests across the United States and Canada and said it was cooperating with authorities.

Gladstone Investment Corporation (GAIN) is a business development company with an 8.4% dividend yield and monthly dividend payments. It invests debt and equity in privately held lower-middle-market companies, targeting a 75% debt and 25% equity portfolio mix. As of March 31, its portfolio included investments in 35 companies across 17 states and 18 industries.

GAIN earns money through capital gains, interest, and dividend income. From 2013 to 2017, its portfolio value grew at a double-digit annualized rate. In fiscal 2017, net investment income rose 8.2%, total investments increased 2.9% to $501.6 million, and net asset value rose 8% to $9.95. Investment sales also produced realized gains and other income.

The company’s debt portfolio was 93% variable-rate with a floor, which may help protect interest income if rates rise. GAIN qualifies as a regulated investment company and generally avoids income taxes if it distributes taxable income to shareholders. It pays a $0.064 monthly dividend, or $0.77 annually, and has made more than 140 consecutive monthly payments. Dividends grew 25% over five years, and the company also plans supplemental dividends when supported by undistributed earnings.

GAIN had leverage below 50% of total assets, assets valued at more than triple liabilities, and a fiscal 2017 distribution coverage ratio of 132%. The article concludes that GAIN’s distributions appear secure due to investment income and capital gains.

The passage lists AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 issues, including PIT, DMA, UART, LPC, ACPI, PMC, USB, IDE/UDMA, SMB, GPIO, and wake-event problems. One detailed issue describes a PIT deviation: a read-back command does not cancel an uncompleted counter latch command, so the PIT supplies the counter value first. The impact is negligible because it occurs only with a questionable programming sequence; the resolution is not to issue a read-back command before completing the current command.

Suncor will release fourth quarter 2018 financial results on Feb. 7, followed by a webcast on Feb. 8 hosted by Steve Douglas with management remarks and Q&A. The release also provides webcast access, analyst/media dial-in numbers, company background, stock listings, and media and investor contact information.

Congress MP Jyotiraditya Scindia will lead a 72-hour satyagraha at Dussehra Maidan in Bhopal, with around 2,000 farmers and Congress leaders participating to protest farmers’ killings and the state government’s alleged anti-farmer stance.

The Supreme Court appeared likely to rule against Colorado’s ban on licensed mental health practitioners providing therapy intended to change minors’ sexual orientation or gender identity. Challenger Kaley Chiles argues the law violates free speech, while Colorado says conversion therapy is medical treatment that harms young LGBTQ+ people and requires regulation. Conservative justices and federal attorneys questioned the strength and authority of medical consensus, raising broader implications for how states regulate medicine. The Court could uphold the law, send it back for stricter review, or find it unconstitutional, potentially affecting similar bans in other states.

Democratic Senator Ron Wyden asked Senate Intelligence Committee leaders to include a thorough review of financial ties between Russia and President Donald Trump and his associates in the investigation of Russian election meddling. Wyden cited the opacity of Trump’s and associates’ finances, including Trump’s refusal to release tax returns. The request followed disclosures of meetings and business links involving Jared Kushner, Paul Manafort, and wealthy Russians. Trump has denied improper Russia ties and said he has no business deals in Russia. Reuters reported Russian elites bought at least $98.4 million in property in Trump-branded Florida towers. Wyden has previously sought more public information on Russia investigations, while U.S. intelligence concluded Russia sought to help Trump and discredit Hillary Clinton; Russia denied the allegations.

The EU is preparing formal action against Italy over its use of “golden power” laws in banking mergers, arguing that broad government intervention may distort competition, deter foreign investment, and undermine the single market. Italy says the powers protect economic sovereignty and strategic assets, while Brussels seeks clearer limits, transparency, and proportionality in national security justifications.

Former BBC weatherman Bill Giles criticised the BBC’s new weather maps, calling them a “severe disappointment” and saying the old maps were clearer and more fit for purpose. He argued the UK appears smaller on screen, making local detail harder to see, while some broadcasts show only capital city forecasts. Giles said forecast accuracy was not the issue because much still comes from the Met Office, but clarity was. He recommended Channel 5’s graphics, though said its forecast was too short. The BBC said the new design is more realistic.

The passage presents iCVS, a mechanistic cardiovascular model designed to infer hidden physiological states of critically ill patients in real time using routinely available ICU signals, specifically arterial and venous blood pressure waveforms plus age and weight. The model uses mean arterial pressure, mean venous pressure, heart rate, peripheral resistance, and pulse pressure to estimate 15 hidden parameters related to cardiovascular function, autonomic regulation, intravascular volume change, vascular resistance modulation, and cardiac contractility.

iCVS incorporates baroreflex and independent autonomic components, as well as non-autonomic systemic vascular resistance modulation, allowing it to represent hypovolemic, distributive, cardiogenic, and combined shock states. It extracts both slow and fast timescale features from high-frequency pressure waveforms and performs inference over clinically relevant time windows of minutes.

The authors demonstrate iCVS using data from 10 critically ill children in a pediatric intensive care unit. The model identified patterns consistent with documented bleeding, distributive shock, cardiac dysfunction, combined shock, and stable control cases. Across the sample, patients with postoperative bleeding had more negative estimated intravascular volume change, while patients clinically labeled with distributive shock had lower estimated non-autonomic vascular resistance modulation. The authors state that larger prospective studies are needed for validation, threshold definition, and assessment in noisy real-world recordings.

The ADS9803 has three power supplies: AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD, with no required power-up sequence; IOVDD powers digital interfaces, and VDD_1V8 and IOVDD share a 1.8V supply. Each power pin requires separate nearby 0.1μF ceramic bypass capacitors, with vias avoided between pins and capacitors. Layout guidance includes avoiding digital lines crossing analog paths, keeping analog input and reference signals away from noise, placing reference decoupling capacitors close to REFIO and REFM, and connecting GND and REFM to a ground plane with short connections. TI provides development tools, documentation update notifications, E2E support forums, trademark information, ESD handling cautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information. The passage also includes notes on part status, materials, RoHS, lead finish, MSL ratings, markings, packaging dimensions, disclaimers, customer responsibilities, warranty limitations, and TI terms of use and sale.

China’s debt has grown rapidly, with estimates as high as 328% of GDP, driven by post-financial-crisis stimulus, loose credit through state banks, shadow banking, and uncertain official data. Although crisis has been avoided due to economic growth targets, reassurances, and a closed capital account, the debt may burden the economy and require major policy intervention.

The passage also argues that China faces external debt risks as a major creditor funding infrastructure and supporting governments abroad. Loans to Venezuela, Argentina, Belt and Road countries, Kenya, Laos, Sri Lanka, and Pakistan may be difficult to repay and could become politically contentious as governments change.

It compares this situation to the 1980s Latin American debt crisis, where abundant capital enabled unsustainable lending and misallocated investment. The passage suggests China’s large reserves and overseas lending may similarly create unserviceable debts, leading to pressure for write-offs if projects fail to generate returns.

The speaker defends signing the Payne tariff bill as a substantial, though incomplete, downward revision consistent with Republican protectionist principles. He argues that the goal was not free trade or injury to domestic industries, but reducing excessive duties while preserving protection equal to the difference between foreign and domestic production costs plus reasonable profit.

He says the Payne law changed 874 of 2,024 dutiable items from the Dingley law: 654 decreases, 220 increases, and 1,150 unchanged. He cites data showing duty reductions applied to nearly $5 billion in national consumption, mostly necessities, while non-luxury increases applied to about $299 million; many increases affected luxuries such as perfumes, wines, liquors, and silks.

The speaker acknowledges criticisms, especially that the wool schedule was not reduced, calling it the bill’s one important defect. He also discusses cotton, crockery, paper, hides, shoes, leather, coal, oil products, and lumber, arguing that Congress acted on available evidence and often compromised. He rejects claims that the tariff caused recent increases in the cost of living, attributing those increases mainly to worldwide conditions and food costs.

He justifies signing the bill and supports Republicans who voted for it, including Mr. Tawney, arguing that defeating or vetoing it would have demoralized the party, prolonged uncertainty, delayed prosperity, and blocked other legislation. He also emphasizes other provisions: a maximum-and-minimum tariff clause for dealing with discriminatory foreign tariffs, a corporate excise tax, freer trade with the Philippines under limits, and funding for a tariff board to gather impartial data for future revisions.

The speaker concludes that the Payne bill should be given time to operate, that another immediate tariff revision would disturb business, and that future revision should rely on more complete and impartial evidence.

Ascension Health and Providence St. Joseph Health are discussing a merger that would create the largest U.S. hospital chain, with 191 hospitals in 27 states and $44.8 billion in annual revenue, the Wall Street Journal reported. No agreement has been reached. The talks come amid major healthcare industry deals and policy and pricing pressures.

Dietitians advise planning ahead for Diwali by setting realistic goals, controlling portions, eating mindfully, and making healthier swaps while still enjoying festive foods. Suggested choices include high-fibre foods such as lentils, wholegrains, chickpeas, vegetables and fruit; lean proteins like grilled chicken, fish or tofu; and using vegetable, olive or sunflower oil instead of ghee, butter or coconut oil. They recommend baking instead of deep-frying, reducing salt with spices, limiting sweets, using fruit or dried fruit for sweetness, choosing low-fat milk, and using whole wheat flour. People with diabetes should monitor blood sugar, pair simple carbs with protein, healthy fats and fibre, avoid skipping meals, and watch for high-sugar drinks and alcohol. Staying hydrated, limiting alcohol, keeping active, and seeking family support can also help make Diwali healthier.

A pragmatic two-stage adaptive open-label randomized clinical trial evaluated auricular acupuncture, peripheral acupuncture, and usual care for acute musculoskeletal pain in an urban U.S. emergency department. Adults with acute new or exacerbated chronic musculoskeletal pain were enrolled from February 2020 to May 2021; 236 were randomized. Both acupuncture approaches were feasible, acceptable, and safe, with high satisfaction and no serious adverse events. At 1 hour, pain reductions were greater with auricular acupuncture plus usual care and peripheral acupuncture plus usual care than with usual care alone, while the two acupuncture styles did not differ significantly. Opioid use was lower in acupuncture groups, but not significantly. Limitations included a single-site setting, English-only enrollment, treatment by licensed acupuncturists, and inability to blind patients. The study concludes that both auricular and peripheral acupuncture may be effective ED options for acute musculoskeletal pain and warrant further study.

The lecture discusses thermal properties of foams, especially closed-cell foams used for insulation. Their low thermal conductivity mainly comes from their high gas volume fraction, low solid fraction, and small cell size, which reduce conduction, convection, and radiation. Aerogels have even lower thermal conductivity but are very weak and brittle.

Heat transfer is reviewed through Fourier’s law for steady-state conduction and a diffusivity equation for non-steady conduction. Thermal diffusivity depends on thermal conductivity, density, and specific heat; materials with high diffusivity adjust quickly to surrounding temperatures.

Foam thermal conductivity is described as the sum of contributions from conduction through the solid, conduction through the gas, convection within cells, and radiation. Gas conduction usually dominates, so low-conductivity gases can reduce foam conductivity, though aging occurs as these gases diffuse out and air diffuses in. Convection is generally negligible in typical foams because it becomes important only for relatively large cells, around 20 millimeters in the example discussed.

Radiative heat transfer is described using Stefan’s law and Beer's law. Radiation increases as relative density decreases and as cell size increases, while solid conduction increases with relative density, creating a tradeoff that can produce a minimum overall thermal conductivity. Aerogels reduce conductivity through very small pore sizes comparable to the mean free path of air.

The lecture also states that a foam’s specific heat and thermal expansion coefficient are the same as those of its solid material. Foams have good thermal shock resistance because their lower modulus reduces thermally induced stresses, allowing a larger critical temperature change before cracking or spalling compared with the solid.

El artículo analiza la expresión lingüística de las emociones en cuentas corporativas de Twitter de Acciona e Iberdrola. El corpus incluye 798 tuits publicados entre abril y junio de 2016. Mediante análisis del discurso, los tuits se clasifican como neutros o emocionales, y estos últimos como descriptivos o evocativos. También se identifican categorías semánticas de emoción y metáforas.

Los resultados muestran una alta presencia de tuits emocionales: 66,5% en Acciona y 73,62% en Iberdrola. Predominan las emociones de valencia positiva, especialmente orgullo, alegría, felicidad, optimismo, interés y confianza. Las emociones negativas —miedo, preocupación, tristeza e ira— aparecen con baja frecuencia.

El orgullo es la emoción más frecuente en ambas cuentas. En Acciona se vincula con innovación, sostenibilidad y logros empresariales; en Iberdrola, con el color verde, el equipo humano y el compromiso ambiental. La alegría, felicidad y optimismo se asocian en Iberdrola con metáforas de luz, energía, sol, calor y vida. En Acciona, la confianza se relaciona con la sostenibilidad, especialmente mediante el hashtag #RecuerdoSOStenible.

El estudio concluye que el microblog corporativo es un corpus válido para estudiar emociones en el entorno organizacional. Las metáforas detectadas están ligadas a la misión, visión y valores de las empresas y contribuyen a reforzar su identidad corporativa. También se propone incorporar el análisis de emociones y metáforas en la enseñanza del español de negocios.

This two-center retrospective study developed a fully automatic machine learning tool to predict 1-year overall survival in pediatric diffuse midline glioma using multisequence MRI. The tool performs deep learning-based tumor core and whole tumor segmentation, radiomic feature extraction, feature selection, and support vector machine survival prediction. It was trained and validated on 53 Children’s National Hospital patients and tested on 16 Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia patients. Automatic segmentation showed strong performance, especially for whole tumor volumes, with similar internal and external results. Survival prediction achieved 77–85% accuracy. Homogeneous whole tumor intensity on baseline T2 FLAIR and larger post-radiation tumor core/whole tumor volume ratio were associated with worse prognosis. The authors conclude the automated approach may support standardized tumor evaluation, risk stratification, treatment monitoring, and clinical trial use.

“Pound Cake” is an offense for attacking a Box & One defense by isolating the star player against the chaser in the post, where defensive help is limited by the 2-1-2 alignment. If no shot is available, the star can use base screens, curl, fade, back cut, roll, or pop out for a 1-on-1 isolation. Ball reversal, post flashes, screener pops, guard basket cuts, and double mid-screen “Horns” variations provide additional options.

Successful execution requires on-ball and off-ball screening, double screens, offensive rebounding, post-ups, timing, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, and coordinated team play. Teams should scout opponents, teach expected defensive reads and counters, adjust during games, vary alignments, and attack weak defenders. The Box & One defense uses four zone defenders in a box and one chaser whose role is to deny the targeted player the ball.

The Supreme Court will consider whether a trial court may bar a criminal defense lawyer from discussing a client’s ongoing testimony during an overnight recess. The case involves David Villarreal, convicted of murder and sentenced to 60 years after a judge told him and his lawyers to act as though he remained on the stand overnight and avoid conferring about his testimony. Villarreal argues the order violated his Sixth Amendment right to effective assistance of counsel.

Prior Supreme Court decisions allowed a ban on attorney-client contact during a brief recess but found unconstitutional a ban on overnight consultation “about anything.” State and federal courts have split on whether overnight discussions about testimony may be restricted. Villarreal argues such limits are unworkable because testimony is often tied to trial strategy, plea advice, witness decisions, and avoiding perjury. Texas argues the order was limited, workable, and properly distinguished testimony from other topics. The United States supports Texas, saying such orders can protect the trial’s truth-finding function. The Court’s decision may clarify how lawyers may confer with testifying clients during trial recesses.

The study used a single-group posttest experimental design to examine an eight-week activity-based amateur guitar lesson plan for five beginner volunteer students aged 18–33 with no prior guitar instruction. Three field experts reviewed the course outline and evaluated student performance using a 100-point scale based on pitch and duration accuracy, tempo, technique, and musicality. Online one-on-one lessons were held for 50 minutes over eight weeks, totaling 16 instructional hours. Final scores combined theoretical knowledge at 40% and performance at 60%.

The theoretical test average was 92. Individual chapter achievement scores were 91, 89.2, 95.5, 93.6, and 98.8, giving a class average of 93.6. All students completed the chapter with a “very good” grade. The study concluded that the activity-based lesson plan produced successful outcomes in amateur guitar education during the Covid-19 pandemic and supported student engagement, learning, and achievement.

The passage discusses Digital Business Ecosystems (DBEs), defined as the co-evolution of Business Ecosystems and Digital Ecosystems. It reviews related approaches for modeling electronic marketplaces, including Electronic Institutions, Contractual Agent Societies, Virtual Enterprises, and B2B e-commerce platforms. A DBE lifecycle consists of formation, evolution, and dissipation. The formation phase is emphasized as crucial because entities search for opportunities, partners, services, and resources, and negotiation supports contract establishment.

The paper focuses on negotiation during DBE formation, especially the Contract Net Protocol (CNP), a high-level communication protocol for cooperative task execution in distributed environments. CNP structures negotiation through task identification, announcement, announcement processing, bidding, bid processing, contract awarding, contract processing, and termination. FIPA extended CNP with interaction protocol modifications, and other extensions are also noted.

The authors propose Contract Net with Quality Protocol (CNQP), also called Q-Contract Net, extending FIPA CNP by adding quality evaluation steps. Participants evaluate the announcer’s quality during announcement processing, and announcers evaluate participants’ quality during bid processing. Quality includes reliability, trust, and reputation. The added quality checks increase negotiation time, but the authors argue they can reduce risk, improve confidence, and support better contract execution in DBEs. Future work will apply the proposed protocol to negotiation on service-level parameters between business entities.

Offensive tackles are key offensive linemen positioned on the outer edges of the line, responsible for run and pass blocking against defensive linemen, linebackers, and top pass rushers. They often work one-on-one with limited help, making their ability to protect the quarterback and create running lanes essential. The position requires football IQ, blocking technique, footwork, hand placement, coordination, agility, functional strength, size, and athleticism. NFL offensive tackles are generally 6’3” to 6’8”, weigh 300–340 pounds, and are tall, thick, and laterally mobile.

The name “offensive tackle” comes from early football, when offenses often ran outside and edge defenders tackled ball carriers; the terminology remained on both sides of the ball. Offensive tackle is abbreviated as OT or T, and linemen are sometimes nicknamed hogs, bruisers, bulldozers, or big uglies. Notable offensive tackles include Jonathan Ogden, Anthony Munoz, and Joe Thomas. The left tackle is especially important because he protects the quarterback’s blind side.

Researchers from the University of Exeter say they have refined James Lovelock’s 1970s Gaia hypothesis, which proposed that Earth functions as a self-regulating system where life and inorganic processes help maintain conditions for life. They identify “sequential selection” as a mechanism in which destabilizing life-environment interactions are short-lived, while stable states persist and can gain further stabilizing traits through “selection by survival alone.” Professor Tim Lenton said this helps explain how Earth accumulated stabilizing mechanisms over 3.5 billion years. The work, involving researchers from Exeter, Lincoln and Southampton, may help assess the likelihood of complex life elsewhere and understand Earth’s response to human-driven climate change and extinction events. The paper was published in Trends in Ecology and Evolution.

The passage describes container and distributed system patterns, beginning with ambassadors for traffic splitting, where IP hashing keeps users consistently assigned and weights can direct most traffic to the main application and a smaller portion to an experiment. It then explains the adapter pattern, in which a separate container modifies an application container’s interface to match expected conventions for monitoring, logging, or health checks. Examples include using Prometheus exporters for Redis metrics, fluentd plugins to normalize Redis and Apache Storm logs, and a separate MySQL health-check adapter that runs workload-specific queries without modifying the MySQL image.

The passage then introduces multi-node patterns and microservices. Microservices divide functionality into separate processes communicating through APIs, improving team independence, release agility, and scaling, but making debugging and architecture more complex. Replicated load-balanced services are presented as a basic distributed pattern for stateless services, using multiple identical replicas behind a load balancer for availability and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes indicate when replicas are prepared to serve traffic. Session-tracked services route a user’s requests to the same replica, often through IP hashing or cookies.

Application-layer replicated services can add caching and SSL termination. A Varnish cache layer can improve performance, but should often be scaled separately from web servers. Caching layers can also support rate limiting and denial-of-service defense. SSL termination can be handled by a replicated nginx layer in front of the cache.

The passage contrasts replicated services with sharded services, where each shard handles only part of the request space and a routing layer directs requests. Sharding is useful when state is too large for one machine. A sharded cache improves memory utilization compared with fully replicated caches, but shard failures can reduce cache hit rate and performance. Replicated sharded caches improve resilience and allow scaling individual hot shards. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform, and the shard key must match request characteristics. Consistent hashing reduces remapping during resharding.

The scatter/gather pattern distributes a request to multiple leaf nodes in parallel, gathers partial results, and combines them at the root. It can reduce processing time for parallelizable tasks such as document search, and can be combined with sharding when data does not fit on one machine. However, excessive parallelism adds overhead and worsens latency and availability due to stragglers. Replicating each shard improves reliability, upgrades, and scale.

Finally, the passage discusses function-as-a-service and event-driven processing. FaaS simplifies deployment, scaling, and recovery for stateless functions, but strong decoupling can complicate monitoring, debugging, state management, background processing, and workloads requiring large in-memory data. It is well suited to request or response decorators, such as adding defaults to API requests, and event handlers, such as asynchronous two-factor authentication workflows.

Former President George H.W. Bush was admitted to Houston Methodist Hospital after an infection spread to his blood following Barbara Bush’s burial. His spokesperson said he is “responding and recovering” and updates will be issued if anything changes. First Lady Melania Trump sent prayers and wishes for his recovery.

Short selling requires borrowing shares before selling them; selling without a locate is prohibited as naked short selling. Hard-to-borrow stocks are difficult to obtain for short selling due to limited supply, high demand, regulatory restrictions, higher loan fees, and locate requirements. Borrowing costs vary by stock characteristics: large, stable, liquid stocks usually have lower fees, while smaller, volatile, illiquid stocks can be more expensive, with fees ranging from about 1% to as high as 50%.

Verdad Research classified nearly 30,000 stocks from 2005 to 2023 by borrowability and found that in the US, hard-to-borrow stocks typically had negative returns over 3-, 6-, and 12-month horizons, while general collateral stocks tended to have positive returns. The same systematic underperformance was not observed in Japan and Europe. The passage suggests this may not be enough for a robust short-selling strategy because traders may be unable to obtain a short locate.

Short-borrow fees can change sharply with market conditions, as shown by GameStop, whose fee rose from about 1% in January 2019 to 34% in January 2021 during a short squeeze. Short selling is described as risky because potential losses are unlimited.

The passage argues that daily bars are the best starting time frame for trading because they are simple to backtest and may still reveal market inefficiencies. It recommends remaining flexible and using multiple time frames as a diversification tool. A trading time frame includes both the expected trade duration and the type of bars used, such as tick, minute, daily, weekly, or monthly bars. Traders can combine time frames, such as using weekly bars for trend direction and daily bars for entries.

Different participants use different horizons: investors typically hold for years or decades and rely on fundamental analysis, while traders may focus on intraday, overnight, swing, or trend-following strategies. The passage recommends daily bars for swing trading and even as inputs for day trading systems, while warning that intraday bars can contain more randomness and noise.

Trading across many time frames and asset classes can improve capital use, reduce correlations, and potentially offset losses in one strategy with gains in another. Drawdowns are described as inevitable, but diversification across time frames may help reduce their impact.

The passage condemns lynching as lawless mob violence that expands beyond accusations of rape, often killing innocent people and undermining civilization and orderly government. It cites officials and clergy warning that mobs endanger both Black and white people, inflame racial tensions, and morally degrade communities. It argues that justice must be applied equally to individuals regardless of race or status, rewarding or punishing people on their own merits rather than treating an entire race as guilty. The passage also says law-abiding Black citizens should help authorities pursue criminals, especially rapists, while white citizens should reject lynching. It supports severe legal punishment for rape and related assaults through proper courts, while protecting victims from unnecessary shame and publicity.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2021. The company designs, manufactures and sells electric vehicles, solar energy generation and energy storage products, and reports two segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. Total revenue was $10.39 billion, up from $5.99 billion in the prior-year quarter, with net income attributable to common stockholders of $438 million compared with $16 million. Total assets were $52.97 billion, cash and cash equivalents were $17.14 billion, and total liabilities were $28.51 billion as of March 31, 2021. Tesla recorded $27 million of bitcoin impairment losses and $128 million of realized gains from sales. The filing notes ongoing COVID-19-related logistics, supply chain and microchip supply challenges. Tesla reported material compliance with debt covenants, settlement of its 2021 convertible notes, and ongoing legal proceedings related to the SolarCity acquisition, executive compensation, director compensation and a potential going-private transaction.

The federal judiciary will use funding such as court fee balances to continue paid operations during the government shutdown, expecting to pay staff through Oct. 17. Most proceedings and deadlines will continue, though some cases involving unavailable executive-branch attorneys may be delayed. The Supreme Court will also rely on non-annual funds. Gillespie reported increased Tamiflu use and advised seeing a doctor for prolonged illness or fever above 102°F. He recommended a flu kit with hand sanitizer, masks, decongestants, pain relievers and water, and noted flu shots remain available at pharmacies.

The passage lists repeated global finance and business headlines, then focuses on U.S. soybean farmers facing severe pressure after China halted purchases from the current autumn crop amid trade tensions and tariffs. China is buying cheaper soybeans from Brazil and Argentina, leaving U.S. farmers with unsold stock and lower prices. Washington plans relief measures, while officials seek alternative buyers in Asia and Africa, though these markets are too small to replace China’s demand.

Scientists at Washington University School of Medicine found in mice that peroxisomes in brown fat can act as an alternative heat source when mitochondrial heat production slows. The pathway involves ACOX2, which helps metabolize certain fatty acids and generate heat. Mice lacking ACOX2 had poorer cold tolerance, lower body temperature, reduced insulin sensitivity, and gained more weight on high-fat diets, while mice with elevated ACOX2 showed improved heat production, cold tolerance, insulin sensitivity, and weight control. Researchers are exploring dietary and drug approaches to activate this pathway, though human benefits remain unproven.

The passage compares the rapid rebuilds of the Chicago Blackhawks and Philadelphia Flyers, noting Chicago’s draft-based approach and Philadelphia’s core players and strong blue line built through trades and free agency. It says Chicago appears positioned for repeated future success, while Philadelphia may feel more urgency to win now. Flyers fan interest is described as rising after dramatic playoff wins and renewed attention to team history. The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU based on the Ampere architecture for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads. A100 introduces third-generation Tensor Cores supporting TF32, BF16, FP64, FP16, INT8, INT4, binary formats, and fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity for up to doubled Tensor Core throughput. It provides 40 GB HBM2 memory, 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, larger L1/shared memory, compute data compression, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, and CUDA 11 support.

A100 includes Multi-Instance GPU capability, allowing one GPU to be partitioned into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory bandwidth, QoS, and fault isolation for multi-tenant and smaller workloads. It also supports Compute Instances, simultaneous context execution, MIG migration, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, and improved error detection and containment.

The passage also covers third-generation NVLink, which increases total A100 GPU bandwidth to 600 GB/sec, plus NVSwitch, Mellanox interconnects, Magnum IO, NVJPG decode, optical flow acceleration, improved atomics, and five NVDEC units. CUDA advances include task graphs, reduced launch latency, asynchronous memory operations, cooperative groups, and warp-wide reductions.

The DGX A100 system uses eight A100 GPUs connected through NVLink and NVSwitch, delivers up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, supports up to 56 GPU Instances through MIG, and is positioned as a scalable platform for enterprise AI infrastructure.

The author, who holds a long position in DineEquity, argues that concerns over the company are overstated despite its falling stock price. They conclude that goodwill impairment for Applebee’s franchise unit is unlikely, comparing 2016 franchise profit and debt costs favorably with 2009, when no impairment occurred. They also argue DineEquity’s debt is serviceable, noting its 4.277% interest rate, 2044 legal maturity, 2021 anticipated repayment date, and covenant metrics well above trigger levels.

The author believes DineEquity can maintain its dividend using operating cash flow, cash balances, and available liquidity, and suggests management reconsider share repurchases. The lecture continues discussion of numerical optimization, focusing on steepest descent, conjugate gradient, Newton-Raphson, and trust-region methods. Steepest descent follows directions perpendicular to contours and always moves downhill, but it can converge slowly, take very small steps in flat regions, or run away if no minimum exists. Step sizes can be improved using a quadratic Taylor approximation.

Linear systems \(Ax=b\) can be formulated as minimization of a quadratic objective when \(A\) is symmetric positive definite. Conjugate gradient improves on steepest descent by choosing conjugate directions that preserve prior minimization, can solve an \(n\)-variable system in at most \(n\) iterations, and only requires products of \(A\) with vectors. It applies directly to symmetric positive definite matrices, while related Krylov subspace methods handle broader cases.

Newton-Raphson solves \(\nabla f=0\) using the Hessian as the Jacobian and converges quadratically near a critical point. It is exact in one step for quadratic functions, but may seek saddle points or maxima, fail near singular Hessians, and requires solving linear systems.

Trust-region methods combine Newton-Raphson and steepest descent. They choose Newton-Raphson steps when the quadratic approximation appears reliable within a chosen radius and otherwise use steepest descent or boundary steps. The trust-region radius is adjusted based on how well the quadratic approximation predicts actual function values. Matlab’s solvers use related heuristic dogleg trust-region strategies.

A Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health study of 501 couples trying to conceive found that higher seafood intake was associated with more sexual activity and higher fecundity. Couples eating fish and shellfish at least twice weekly had a 92 percent pregnancy rate within a year, and those eating seafood eight or more times monthly had 22 percent more sexual activity than average. Researchers said the cause was unclear and did not link the findings directly to zinc. Other cited studies and surveys connected food with sex-related attitudes or outcomes, including millennials valuing food similarly to sex, guacamole mentions increasing dating-message replies, apples being associated with improved female sexual function, and men and women thinking about sex more often than food.

Emily Andrea has partnered with monkey monkey for a children’s eyewear summer awareness campaign promoting UV eye protection. She said learning that most lifetime UV exposure occurs before age 18 highlighted the importance of sunglasses for children, including her own.

AQTWM, Inc. (Aqua Terra) filed a preliminary long form prospectus with securities commissions in all Canadian provinces except Québec for an initial public offering of common shares. The speaker says he always believed he could reach this level, though the season’s success was unexpected. A sample of October 25, 2001 articles reports that Enron replaced CFO Andrew Fastow with Jeff McMahon to restore investor confidence amid an SEC inquiry into Fastow-related partnerships, including LJM. Enron’s stock had fallen sharply after third-quarter losses, a $1.2 billion shareholder equity reduction, and concerns over off-balance-sheet financing, disclosure, conflicts of interest, credit ratings, and potential dilution. Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated April 26, 2018, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2018. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration and Chief Accounting Officer.

Williams %R is an oscillating mean-reversion indicator ranging from 0 to -100, measuring the close relative to the highest high over a lookback period. The passage explains its formula, compares it to WilliamsVixFix, RSI, and Stochastics, and presents backtests on SPY and QQQ. The author concludes Williams %R works well in tested long strategies, especially with short lookback periods, but does not work for shorts. In SPY, a two-day lookback produced an 11.9% CAGR, 22% market exposure, 598 trades, 17% max drawdown, and a 2.2 profit factor. A comparable RSI strategy had a lower CAGR of 7.3%. Another Williams %R-based QQQ strategy had a 13.4% CAGR, 14% market exposure, 78% winners, 3.2 profit factor, 20.5% max drawdown, and 2.9 Sharpe Ratio. The passage states Williams %R performed better than RSI and Stochastics in the tested strategies.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 26, 2016, reporting that it issued a press release and related data sheet on financial results for its second fiscal quarter ended March 26, 2016. The filing includes Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2 and was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Information Services Group held its 92nd consecutive ISG Index call for Q3 2025. The ISG Index tracks technology industry health and growth through annual contract value, viewed as bookings and a leading revenue indicator. Speakers said enterprises continue shifting to cloud-first platforms, with as-a-service ACV up nearly 30% year-to-date, led by infrastructure deals.

This study investigated the relationship between hypertension, blood pressure, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) leakage in humans using a sensitive 7 Tesla dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI protocol. Participants included 23 patients with essential hypertension and 20 normotensive healthy controls, matched on age and sex; final analyses included 22 hypertensive patients and 19 controls after excluding two outliers.

BBB leakage rates did not significantly differ between hypertensive patients and controls when hypertension was treated as a dichotomous status. However, higher systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and mean arterial pressure were associated with stronger BBB leakage in grey matter, especially cortical grey matter, but not in white matter. These associations remained largely independent of cardiovascular risk factors, medication intake, and cerebral small vessel disease imaging markers. Blood plasma volume fraction was higher in hypertensive patients in grey matter regions, but was not significantly related to current blood pressure measures.

Post-hoc subgroup analysis suggested lower BBB leakage in medically well-treated hypertensive patients with normal blood pressure compared with patients who had current hypertension, indicating a possible protective effect of effective antihypertensive treatment. The study concludes that current blood pressure, rather than hypertension status alone, is associated with BBB leakage in grey matter, and recommends larger or longitudinal studies to further examine medication effects.

A valid device write requires at least 32 SCLKs per data transfer frame. Read protocols include legacy SPI-compatible single or dual SDO-x and source-synchronous modes. After power-up or asynchronous reset, the device uses SPI-00-S for reads and writes. Other SPI protocols are selected via SDI_MODE[1:0], with SDO_MODE[1:0] set to 00b for SPI reads. RVS stays low during SPI-compatible transfers.

Plans seek to extend Chichester Free School’s use of the former Bartons County Infant School for another academic year to September 31, 2019, increase pupils from 390 to 420, and address possible highways-related delays to relocation.

Andrew Lo reviews modern portfolio theory, explaining that combining imperfectly correlated securities creates a bullet-shaped risk-return opportunity set, whose upper branch is the efficient frontier. Rational investors prefer portfolios on this frontier because they offer higher expected return for the same risk or lower risk for the same expected return. With three stocks—General Motors, IBM, and Motorola—the efficient frontier shows that holding 100% of any single stock is generally inefficient.

Adding more securities cannot make investors worse off because they can assign zero weight to unwanted assets; it can improve the risk-return trade-off through diversification. Correlations arise from macroeconomic conditions and psychological market behavior. Negative correlations with positive expected returns are difficult to find and may disappear as investors buy such assets.

Introducing a risk-free asset such as T-Bills creates straight-line combinations with risky portfolios. The best such line is tangent to the efficient frontier, defining the tangency portfolio. All mean-variance investors, regardless of risk tolerance, prefer some combination of T-Bills and this tangency portfolio. The slope of this line is the Sharpe ratio, measuring expected excess return per unit of risk.

Lo explains that managers add value only if they deliver performance above this benchmark line, known as alpha. Warren Buffett is discussed as an example of a manager who historically achieved a higher Sharpe ratio, though identifying such managers in advance is difficult.

In equilibrium, if all investors hold combinations of T-Bills and the tangency portfolio, the tangency portfolio must be the market portfolio: all assets held in proportion to market capitalization. This leads to a relationship between expected return and risk for efficient portfolios. Sharpe’s further result extends this to any asset using beta, defined as the covariance of the asset’s return with the market return divided by the market return variance. Beta determines the appropriate risk premium and cost of capital in the capital asset pricing framework.

The President transmits to the Senate a convention between the United States and Great Britain, negotiated by John M. Clayton and Sir Henry Lytton Bulwer, for advice on ratification. The treaty aims to protect a proposed ship canal through Nicaragua connecting the Atlantic and Pacific, as well as possible routes through Tehuantepec, Panama, and other interoceanic communications. It requires no public Treasury funds, gives no route preference, and is intended to protect private capital and ensure equal access for all nations. The President states that the treaty seeks to secure transit across the Isthmus, preserve the independence of Central American republics, and prevent foreign aggression, while rejecting annexationist aims. He says the treaty follows prior U.S. policy, including actions and views of Presidents Jackson and Polk regarding neutral and protected interoceanic routes. He also submits related correspondence and notes that the United States deserves credit for first proposing such an arrangement. If both this treaty and the Nicaragua treaty are ratified, amendments may be needed to align them. He believes France and Russia are ready to accede and expects other maritime states to join.

Belarus’s out-of-school education system developed through three stages: early 20th-century literacy programs for poor and uneducated populations, a Soviet period that built a system focused on labor education, outdoor practice, career choice, and talent identification, and a post-Soviet period combining Soviet practices with EU educational ideas. The system is legally defined in the 2011 Education Code as part of lifelong learning and is supported by regulations covering institutions, training, methodology, access, funding, and protection of educational resources.

By the end of 2021, Belarus had 318 out-of-school educational institutions: 3 national and 315 regional, including 185 comprehensive and 133 specialized institutions. Specialized institutions include regional study tour, ecosystem protection, physical training, science and technology, professional training, and art training centers. About one-third of Belarusian children and adolescents participate in public out-of-school education. Public institutions are popular because of lower fees, state support, qualified staff, and links to academic competitions that can support university admission.

The system emphasizes patriotism, national identity, physical fitness, ecological awareness, scientific literacy, creativity, and personality development. Its main training objectives are four abilities: mastering information technology, developing social personality, surviving in a multicultural world, and sustaining lifelong study. Examples include Minsk State Children’s Palace for IT-related courses, the Belarusian Youth League for social activities and volunteering, international cultural exchange activities for multicultural education, and the Young Public Rescuers–Firefighters’ Association for safety, ecological awareness, and career-related learning.

The passage also notes shortcomings, including funding shortages, outdated equipment, unequal access to paid programs, limited advertising, occasional neglect of small-scale interpersonal skill development, and cultural activities that are often short-term. It concludes that Belarus’s experience may offer reference value for China’s public out-of-school education policy.

The passage describes four overnight S&P 500 trading strategies that buy at the close and sell at the next open or close, using short holding periods to reduce drawdowns. The first strategy buys new n-day lows with added criteria, including the close above the 200-day moving average, and reports an 8.43% profit with a 29% win rate. The second also buys new n-day lows, earns 12.69%, has a 14% win rate, and a 2.6 profit factor. Strategy three has a profit factor of about 3.8. Strategy four benefits from short-term oversold conditions and may improve by holding to the close when SPY opens lower than -0.1%.

The Dodge Challenger SRT Demon is a drag-focused coupe tested at Atco Dragway in New Jersey. It has a 6.2-liter supercharged V8 producing 808 hp, or 840 hp with the Demon Crate’s race-gas engine control module, and 770 lb-ft of torque. Based on the Hellcat engine, it includes extensive component upgrades, a reinforced 8-speed automatic transmission, and a TransBrake drag-racing system. Dodge reduced weight by 232 pounds, including removing passenger and rear seats, though they can be added back. Drag Mode adjusts the suspension for launch traction, helping the car run a quarter mile in 9.96 seconds on premium fuel or 9.65 seconds on race gas in ideal conditions. The author ran 10.2 seconds at 134 mph using launch control but struggled to improve with the TransBrake. Dodge says durability testing included over 500 quarter-mile runs on one axle and more than 900 on one transmission. The Demon starts at about $86,000, with 3,300 allocated for the U.S. and Canada.

The passage examines dropout tendencies in Turkish higher education, framing dropout as a multifaceted issue shaped by individual, institutional, social, academic, psychological, and economic factors. Grounded in Tinto’s Theoretical Dropout Model, the study used a descriptive correlational design with 1,061 undergraduate and preparatory students at Turkish public universities during 2023–2024.

Using the School Dropout Scale in Higher Education, the study found that students had a moderate dropout tendency overall. Health and wellbeing and institutional factors had the highest subdimension scores. No significant difference was found by gender, but dropout tendency was higher among students in later years, those studying outside metropolitan cities, those working while studying, and those with close friends who had dropped out. Dropout tendency was negatively correlated with school attendance, parental education, GPA, and family income, and positively correlated with number of siblings. All scale subdimensions were positively correlated with overall dropout tendency.

The study concludes that dropout risk in Turkish higher education is linked to demographic, academic, socioeconomic, and environmental factors. It recommends retention strategies such as academic mentoring, financial support, mental health services, attendance monitoring, and early identification of at-risk students, especially in non-metropolitan institutions.
The Louisiana Supreme Court denied Joshua W. Curran’s writ application.

On a “Jeopardy!” episode before the Super Bowl, contestants avoided the “Football” category until the end and failed to answer any questions, prompting host Alex Trebek to joke about their lack of football knowledge. The passage also notes reports that several Philadelphia Eagles players were affected by the flu before the Super Bowl.

A Princeton-led study published in Nature found that ISWI ATP-dependent chromatin remodelers use the nucleosome’s negatively charged “acidic patch” to remodel chromatin. The acidic patch is formed by histone proteins H2A and H2B and had not previously been implicated in chromatin remodeling. Using high-throughput screening, researchers showed that some non-ISWI remodeling enzymes also use this feature, suggesting it may be broadly required for chromatin remodeling. They also found that chemical modifications near the acidic patch can enhance or inhibit ISWI activity, with different chromatin-interacting proteins showing distinct responses. The study generated data for future research on ISWI regulation and may inform investigations into cancer-related mutations in the acidic patch.

ZnSe-WSe2 and ZnSe-MoSe2 core-shell nanowires were fabricated by depositing WO3 or MoO3 precursor layers on ZnSe nanowires via DC magnetron sputtering, followed by selenization in a three-zone furnace. Characterization by TEM, XRD, XPS, Raman spectroscopy, and photoluminescence confirmed successful conversion of oxide precursors into WSe2 and MoSe2 shells while preserving the ZnSe core. TEM showed conformal layered shells for ZnSe-WSe2 at 700°C and ZnSe-MoSe2 at 600°C, while higher selenization temperatures produced discontinuous shells with protruding TMD crystals. XRD detected wurtzite ZnSe and the corresponding TMD phases without precursor oxide peaks. The study indicates that selenization temperature controls shell morphology, with lower temperatures favoring smoother solid-state conversion and higher temperatures promoting evaporation, gas-phase reaction, and island growth. These trends may apply to other semiconductor nanowire/TMD core-shell heterostructures for optoelectronic, photocatalytic, and related nanoscale applications.

Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon said stock markets are likely to see a drawdown within 12 to 24 months as AI enthusiasm drives investors further out on the risk curve. Speaking at Italian Tech Week, he compared the current AI boom to past technology cycles, warning that some deployed capital will fail to deliver returns. He avoided calling it a bubble but said a reset is likely. Solomon also said AI remains powerful and exciting, with major potential for enterprises.

Scientists from the University of Oxford detected hydrogen sulphide, the gas responsible for rotten egg smell, in Uranus’ cloud tops using infrared data from the Gemini North telescope. The finding confirms earlier theories and contrasts with Jupiter and Saturn, whose clouds contain ammonia instead. Researchers said these differences may offer insights into how the planets formed.

The passage describes diplomatic exchanges in Seoul in June 1894 regarding Japanese and Chinese troops in Korea. John M. B. Sill portrays Japan as seeking Korea’s independence from Chinese suzerainty and supporting reforms. Foreign representatives propose simultaneous troop withdrawal. Japanese minister K. Otori says he will relay the request to his government and supports preserving peace. Yuan Shi-Kai reports China sent troops at Korea’s request to suppress rebels and will not withdraw unless Japan also withdraws under the Tien-Tsin agreement. Japan states its troops were sent to protect its legation and subjects and assist Korea.

Cameroon plans to restore 12 million hectares of deforested land by 2030 as part of the Bonn Challenge, with support from local councils, NGOs and businesses. The government says the effort will aid sustainable development, climate resilience and mitigation while also conserving indigenous forests. Cameroon lost 777,000 hectares of forest from 2001 to 2015, half since 2012. Funding will go to local councils and vulnerable chiefdoms for planting. Environmental experts welcome restoration but stress that protecting existing forests is more important for carbon storage, biodiversity, climate regulation and economic services such as water supply and hydropower.

The killing of Kim Jong Nam at a Malaysian airport has renewed attention on poison as a weapon of assassination. South Korean intelligence officials said female agents from North Korea administered a lethal dose, possibly sprayed in his face, while an autopsy was underway. The passage outlines common poisons including ricin, thallium, arsenic, strychnine, cyanide and potassium, noting their effects and forensic signs. It also reviews poison’s role in history, literature and alleged political murders, citing cases involving Georgy Markov, Alexander Litvinenko, the Tokyo sarin attack and Indonesian activist Munir Said Thalib.

The paper introduces EduVidQA, a dataset and benchmark for long-form question answering over educational lecture videos. A preliminary survey of 52 STEM students found that many use online lecture videos regularly and often want to ask content-related questions, but few do so in comments, motivating expert-level automated support.

EduVidQA contains 5,252 QA pairs from lecture videos: 270 real-world YouTube student questions manually answered or verified by domain experts, and 4,982 synthetic QA pairs generated from NPTEL course transcripts and refined through filtering, adversarial checks, Bloom’s taxonomy tagging, and quality validation. The dataset focuses on open-ended lecture-based questions requiring higher-level reasoning than prior educational video QA datasets.

The authors conduct a student preference study to identify desirable answer qualities. Clarity is the most preferred quality, while encouraging critical thinking and using pedagogical techniques are also considered useful. These findings inform qualitative evaluation metrics based on Likert-scale scoring with GPT-4o, validated against human annotations.

The benchmark evaluates open-source video and vision-language models, closed models, and finetuned variants using text-based metrics such as BLEU, ROUGE-L, METEOR, entailment, and FactQA, along with the proposed qualitative metrics. Results show that finetuning smaller open-source models on synthetic data improves performance and can make them comparable to, or sometimes better than, larger closed models on some quantitative and qualitative measures. However, all models still leave room for improvement.

The paper notes limitations including restricted demographics in human studies, limited real-world dataset size and domain coverage, dependence on LLM-based evaluation, and compute constraints affecting model selection.

CompositesWorld’s 2017 Carbon Fiber conference will be held Nov. 28-30 at Belmond Charleston Place in Charleston, South Carolina, with registration open. The event includes a Boeing 787 Dreamliner final assembly line tour, a pre-conference tutorial by Chris Red, and a keynote by Boeing’s Daniel P. Mooney on the 787 and Boeing South Carolina. The agenda features a carbon fiber recycling panel and presentations on CFRP processing, automated composites manufacturing, additive manufacturing, wind energy, automotive applications, renewable acrylonitrile, and CFRP adoption challenges.
