The speaker calls for joint executive and legislative action to “whip inflation,” saying Americans want leadership and action. He presents a 10-part program focused on food, energy, restrictive practices, capital, unemployment relief, housing, thrift institutions, international economic cooperation, taxes, and federal spending.

He urges increased food production, removal of remaining acreage limits on rice, peanuts, and cotton, fuel and fertilizer allocation for farmers, review of regulations affecting food prices, monitoring of grain exports, and changes to Public Law 480. On energy, he announces a national energy board led by the Secretary of the Interior, seeks to cut foreign oil imports by 1 million barrels per day by the end of 1975, and calls for greater use of coal, domestic oil, nuclear fuel, and cleaner energy sources.

He proposes stronger antitrust enforcement, higher penalties for violations, regulatory reform, inflation impact statements, and monitoring of wages and prices without compulsory controls. To expand capital, he recommends a 10 percent investment tax credit, deductible preferred-stock dividends, and capital gains tax changes. For those hurt by inflation, he proposes special unemployment benefits, a Community Improvement Corps, and tax relief through pending reform legislation.

He seeks support for housing through federal mortgage purchases, attention to thrift institutions, passage of a trade reform bill, a temporary 5 percent tax surcharge on corporations and upper-income individuals, and a $300 billion federal spending target. He also calls on citizens to save food and energy, drive less, share more, and join a voluntary anti-inflation effort called WIN.

Chicago Mercantile Exchange lean hog futures fell about three per cent Friday as abundant supplies pressured cash markets. October hogs closed at 59.175 cents/lb. and December at 60.925 cents. Live cattle futures rose to a two-week high, supported by technical and investment fund buying, while speculative investors increased net long positions in livestock futures and options.

Peter Blackmore’s August report says Compaq has solid momentum and morale across regions despite supply challenges. Latin America saw growth in direct business and e-business alliances with Diveo, Artikos, Terra and Patagon.com, while Canada reported an 88% profit increase over Q2 1999, direct-sales expansion, awards and several major customer wins.

Major wins included a more than $200 million U.S. Department of Energy/NNSA contract to build the “Q” supercomputer, plus large contracts with Alcatel, BMC Software, the U.K. Cabinet Office, EDF, Korea Telecom, KPMG, the National Science Foundation and Verizon. IDC data cited Compaq’s strength in PC servers, portables and regional market positions. The report also highlighted wins in global accounts, service provider/.com business, Compaq Financial Services, storage, business-critical servers, consumer products, CPCG profitability, ISSG products, Commerce One portals and North America e-business initiatives.

The remainder of the report lists numerous customer, professional services and product wins across Asia Pacific, EMEA, Greater China, Japan, Latin America and North America, and closes by noting upcoming European visits and subscription instructions for the Blackmore Report.

The passage proposes a hybrid memory system for long-running Low-Code/No-Code agents to address memory inflation and contextual degradation caused by finite LLM context windows. The system combines working memory, episodic memory in a vector database, and semantic memory for distilled knowledge. Its “Intelligent Decay” mechanism assigns each memory a utility score based on recency, relevance, and user-assigned importance, then retains, deletes, or consolidates memories accordingly. A user-facing timeline interface lets non-technical users pin, forget, or consolidate memories through Human-in-the-Loop feedback.

The paper compares the system against a sliding-window baseline and a basic RAG baseline in a simulated 500-turn project-planning task. The hybrid system achieved the highest task completion rate, consistency score, and lowest contradiction rate, while reducing token cost compared with basic RAG. The authors identify limitations including hyperparameter tuning and dependence on user feedback, and suggest future work on autonomous calibration, multimodal memory, procedural memory, pruning, and integration with stateful agent frameworks.

At the time of seizure, the Cape Horn Pigeon was managed by Joseph Wing and William R. Wing of New Bedford, operating as J. & W. R. Wing. Ownership was divided among listed Massachusetts owners, all stated to be native American citizens and U.S. citizens when the claim originated. The bark’s officers and 30 crew members were shipped under articles providing compensation from net voyage proceeds, with some crew claims assigned to the owners after advances. Built in Dartmouth, Massachusetts, in 1854 for whaling, the vessel had always been used for that business. It was fitted out at San Francisco in December 1891 for a year’s whaling voyage in the Japan and Okhotsk seas, fully equipped for whaling and not for sealing or assisting sealing.

The author thanks family, mentors, and parents. Modern applications require high availability, reliability, and rapid scalability, making many systems distributed. Building distributed systems is difficult, but containers and orchestrators enable reusable components and patterns that simplify their development.
The court affirmed the judgment of sentence on President Judge Griffith’s opinion and directed the appellant to appear below and be committed until complying with any unperformed sentence.

The passage specifies SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guest-hypervisor communication mechanisms using GHCB Non-Automatic Exit events. It describes SEV-SNP AP Creation, which lets a guest create, update, or remove AP vCPU state at a VMPL level using VMSA pages marked with RMPADJUST; VMPL selection is valid only when Multi-VMPL support is advertised, and errors leave the vCPU unrunnable until a VMSA is reassigned.

It defines #HV doorbell page registration for Restricted Injection, including actions to get a preferred GPA, set, query, and clear a per-vCPU doorbell page. The doorbell page is shared, host-owned memory used to report pending interrupts and non-maskable events through PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. Host and guest behavior for interrupt presentation, acknowledgement, end-of-interrupt handling, non-maskable events, HLT interaction, and validation of vectors is specified.

Additional NAE events include #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer using APIC timer semantics, APIC ID List retrieval through shared guest pages, SNP Run VMPL to switch a vCPU to another VMPL with a unique VMSA, SNP TIO Guest Request for trusted device binding and related measurements, Secure AVIC backing-page registration, termination requests, and handling unsupported NAE events.

The passage also covers SEV-ES guest identification through CPUID properties, AP boot challenges caused by measured and encrypted register state, AP Reset Hold and AP jump table behavior, and SEV-SNP AP Creation as an alternative that can support vCPU hotplug. It states that SMM and nested virtualization are not supported. It also describes NMI completion signaling, debug register virtualization behavior depending on DebugVirtualization support, and Restricted Injection requirements for isolated SNP guests.

Carroll County’s school board is asking commissioners to reconsider moving Carroll County Public Schools’ Central Office from Westminster to the former North Carroll High School in Hampstead, despite county budget approval for the move. Superintendent Stephen Guthrie said the main concern is the noncentral location, not the building’s adaptability. Staff estimates the move would increase travel to schools by about 50% in miles and 30% in time, raising operating costs. The board plans to send commissioners another letter detailing concerns and projected added annual costs. Commissioners previously approved $6 million in FY18 for moving the Central Office and part of the Sheriff’s Office to North Carroll, and $6 million in FY19 to expand other offices into the Winchester Building.

The speaker says winning again was as satisfying as the previous year, especially with key defensemen absent and Vladimir Konstantinov present. He says the team followed Konstantinov’s and Sergei’s recoveries closely but did not use the accident as motivation; instead, it brought the already close team closer. Giving Konstantinov the Stanley Cup on the ice was described as appropriate and significant.

He says he is having the most fun of his career and is not considering retirement, though the season was exhausting because of the Olympic schedule and nonstop games. He expects the team to remain competitive because much of its core is relatively young and should stay together. He is proud to have the Yzerman name on a major hockey trophy.

He says the sweep was deceptive because the Capitals series was difficult, while the Dallas series was probably the toughest physically. He credits the team’s success to strong defense, four effective lines, size, speed, and depth. He hopes coach Scotty Bowman returns, saying Bowman drives the team, keeps players motivated, and prevents overconfidence.

Formula 1’s 2019 season showed commercial momentum, with 4.2 million Grand Prix attendees, a 1.9 billion cumulative TV audience, 1.1 billion F1.com page views, and more than 25 million social media followers. However, the sport faced concerns about limited on-track competition, as aerodynamic wake made overtaking difficult and Mercedes, Ferrari, and Red Bull Racing dominated the Constructors’ Championship due in part to much larger budgets.

Since Liberty Media acquired Formula 1 in 2016, CEO Chase Carey, CCO Sean Bratches, and Managing Director of Motorsport Ross Brawn worked to modernize an organization previously run under Bernie Ecclestone’s centralized control. They aimed to turn F1 from a motorsport business into a global entertainment brand by improving competition, upgrading events, expanding digital engagement, broadening the brand through initiatives such as Esports and fantasy leagues, and growing in China and the United States.

F1 is the highest class of single-seater, open-cockpit auto racing, with teams building cars each season under evolving technical rules. The sport combines athletic performance, advanced engineering, and data analysis. Cars use hybrid engines, sophisticated electronics, telemetry, aerodynamic wings, and extensive sensors, producing large amounts of race-weekend data used by teams to guide strategy. F1 has also served as a testing ground for automotive innovation and announced a goal to become carbon neutral by 2030.

The sport’s main stakeholders are the teams, the FIA, and Formula 1. Teams receive funding from sponsors, prize money, and owners, with annual budgets ranging widely. The FIA regulates motorsport safety and compliance. Formula 1 manages the commercial side, including promotion, broadcasting, sponsorship, hospitality, and team payments under the Concorde Agreement.

Formula 1’s new leadership created formal business functions, including marketing, research, sponsorship, digital, and strategy. A global brand study found that fans valued drivers and wanted more access, but also viewed the sport as elitist and inaccessible. The organization began investing in fan engagement, digital content, social media, live experiences, research, and more personalized offerings.

By 2019, Formula 1’s main revenue units were promotion, broadcast, advertising and sponsorship, and other revenue such as the Paddock Club and F1TV Pro. Promotion fees came from race hosts, broadcasting was the largest revenue source, and sponsorship involved global partners such as Heineken, DHL, Rolex, Pirelli, Emirates, and AWS. The research team began collecting data on audiences, fan behavior, race engagement, and venue movement to support commercial and sporting decisions.

The 2019 season ended with Lewis Hamilton winning the Drivers’ Championship and Mercedes winning the Constructors’ Championship. Despite early title decisions, later races delivered notable drama and strong attendance. Formula 1, the FIA, and teams neared agreement on 2021 changes, including a $175 million team budget cap and redesigned cars intended to promote closer racing.

Formula 1 expanded fan experiences through exhibitions, Hot Laps, auctions, fan festivals, apps, podcasts, Esports, fantasy leagues, and Netflix’s Drive to Survive. The organization saw progress in audience growth and engagement but identified on-track competition as a continuing challenge. Its broader task was to balance commercial growth, fan entertainment, team and driver demands, technological leadership, and relevance amid climate change and changes in the automotive industry.

WIRED highlights discounted tech gadgets during Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days, including phones, tablets, Kindles, chargers, cameras, smart home devices, TVs, laptops, monitors, keyboards, mice, storage, and power stations. Featured deals include products from Google, OnePlus, Apple, Amazon, GoPro, TCL, Anker, Logitech, and others, with notes on key features, pricing drops, and suitability for different uses.

This study examined structural and policy barriers to medical oxygen access in Peru using political economy analysis, key informant interviews, and reviews of academic, grey, and policy literature. Peru’s fragmented and decentralized health system, political instability, and lack of a national oxygen strategy contributed to poor coordination before and during COVID-19.

Before the pandemic, Peru required medical oxygen purity above 99%, despite WHO-recognized lower-purity options. This limited competition, concentrated government contracts among a few suppliers, and restricted smaller providers. During COVID-19, demand surged, but production and distribution capacity were insufficient, especially outside Lima and coastal areas. Regulatory delays, weak procurement coordination, lack of reliable data, and fragmented responsibilities worsened shortages. Informal markets emerged, with high prices and unsafe cylinder use.

Civil society, religious groups, NGOs, and private actors helped fund and donate oxygen plants and supplies, but many donations lacked maintenance plans, legal formalization, trained personnel, or integration into health infrastructure. By the post-pandemic period, many oxygen plants were unused, broken, or abandoned, while health facilities increasingly returned to purchasing oxygen from established suppliers.

Interviewees emphasized that Peru remains inadequately prepared for future emergencies. The study concludes that Peru needs a coordinated National Oxygen System covering demand forecasting, supply management, quality control, maintenance, trained personnel, infrastructure, and equitable distribution to improve resilience and prevent future oxygen access crises.

Cash-in-transit heists in South Africa have exceeded 159 in 2018, with SABRIC reporting an increase from 2017 and vehicle losses of R1.1m to R1.4m. Apple Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended March 28, 2020. For the quarter, total net sales were $58.3 billion, compared with $58.0 billion a year earlier, and net income was $11.2 billion, compared with $11.6 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $2.55. Six-month net sales were $150.1 billion, net income was $33.5 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $7.56.

Quarterly product sales declined for iPhone, Mac, and iPad, while Wearables, Home and Accessories rose 23% and Services rose 17%. Apple reported total assets of $320.4 billion, total liabilities of $242.0 billion, and shareholders’ equity of $78.4 billion as of March 28, 2020. Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash totaled $43.0 billion at period end.

Apple stated that COVID-19 disrupted manufacturing, supply chain, logistics, retail operations, and demand, particularly affecting iPhone supply and sales in China and later outside China. The company repurchased $18.5 billion of common stock and paid $3.4 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents during the quarter. It also disclosed ongoing legal matters, including VirnetX litigation, iOS performance management cases, and a €1.1 billion fine from the French Competition Authority that Apple plans to appeal.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture improves video encoding quality over Pascal GPUs and software encoders, enabling lower CPU utilization and making 4K streaming possible. It adds USB Type-C and VirtualLink support to simplify VR headset connectivity by carrying power, display, and data through one connector. Turing also replaces prior SLI interfaces with second-generation NVLink on TU102 and TU104 GPUs, increasing GPU-to-GPU bandwidth and enabling new display topologies, while supporting two-way SLI but not 3-way or 4-way SLI.

Turing introduces real-time ray tracing through RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs combined with NVIDIA RTX software. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, offloading shader multiprocessors and enabling much faster ray tracing than Pascal. NVIDIA describes hybrid rendering as the preferred approach for many applications, combining rasterization with ray tracing for effects such as reflections, refractions, shadows, and ambient occlusion. Denoising reduces the number of rays needed per pixel while maintaining image quality.

The architecture includes NGX, a deep learning-based graphics stack using Turing Tensor Cores. NGX supports features such as DLSS, DLSS 2X, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS is trained using high-quality 64x supersampled images and aims to provide image quality similar to TAA with improved performance. NGX requires Turing GPUs and is managed through GeForce Experience or Quadro Experience.

Turing adds new graphics features including Mesh Shading, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering. Mesh Shading introduces Task and Mesh Shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and process large numbers of objects efficiently. Variable Rate Shading lets developers vary shading rates across 16x16 pixel regions and supports content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility sampling from appearance shading and enables reuse of shaded texels. Multi-View Rendering supports multiple views in one pass, improving VR and other multi-view workloads.

For VR, Turing combines VirtualLink, Multi-View Rendering, Variable Rate Shading, foveated rendering, and RT Core-accelerated VRWorks Audio to improve headset connectivity, rendering efficiency, immersion, and audio simulation.

The TU104 GPU includes up to 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and one x8 NVLink link. It is used in products including GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. Tesla T4 uses a TU104 configuration with 2560 CUDA cores and 320 Tensor Cores for inferencing. TU106, used in GeForce RTX 2070, includes 2304 CUDA cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but does not support NVLink or SLI.

NVIDIA defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering, combining weighted Tensor, FP32, RT Core, and INT32 operations. The passage also explains ray tracing mechanics, BVH acceleration, denoising, and examples of ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections. It concludes that hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH algorithms, and RT Cores together enable real-time ray tracing with Turing.

Researchers including Carl Lipo used 3D modeling and field experiments to support the hypothesis that Rapa Nui’s moai statues were moved upright by rocking them in a zig-zag motion with ropes. Models identified features such as forward lean and wide D-shaped bases, and a 4.35-ton replica was moved 100 meters by 18 people in 40 minutes. Concave roads on the island also supported this transport method. The study argues the method fits available evidence and highlights the engineering skill of the Rapa Nui people.

This scoping review examined methods used to measure socioeconomic status (SES) in health-related studies in sub-Saharan Africa. Searches were conducted in PubMed/Medline, CINAHL, EMBASE, Web of Science, and African Index Medicus for English-language publications from January 2012 to June 2024. After screening 19,669 records, 65 articles were included.

The studies covered 22 countries, most often South Africa, Kenya, and Ghana. Most were research articles, with cross-sectional and cohort designs predominating. The most common fields were SES assessment and maternal, child, youth, family health and wellbeing.

The review identified 41 SES measures grouped into 11 categories. Asset-based wealth indices were the most frequently used, accounting for 61.9% of measures, with the Wealth Index and its variants being the most common. Other categories included indices based on education, health, and living standards; occupation, income, and education; perceived wealth; income; and material affluence. Common indicators included durable goods, housing quality, utilities, land and livestock ownership, financial services, transportation assets, education, employment, health, and living standards.

Principal Component Analysis was the most common method for calculating asset-based wealth indices, used alone in 57.7% of cases and with other methods in 9.6%. The review found substantial variation in SES measurement approaches, limiting comparability across studies. It recommends moving toward standardized SES measurement methods in Africa while allowing adaptation to local contexts.

The speaker argues that the nation’s political success depends on the religious convictions of its people. Modern life has become more complex and interdependent, creating new opportunities for wrongdoing, crime, selfish misuse of government, and social disorder. War has contributed to crime and weakened restraints, while some people show disrespect for law, authority, property, and social discipline.

The speaker says government cannot fully solve these moral problems. Its proper role is to maintain order, protect persons and property, and administer justice, but it cannot create the public will to obey the law or provide the spiritual foundations needed for social reform. Law can deter wrongdoing only when supported by strong public sentiment, which the speaker attributes to religion. Education is also valuable, but intellectual development without moral growth can increase the capacity for evil as well as good.

The speaker maintains that American government rests on religious foundations, even though church and state are separated. Principles such as freedom, equality, self-government, and the authority of law are described as rooted in belief in the brotherhood of man and the fatherhood of God. Historical religious leaders are cited as contributors to education and government because their spiritual convictions led them to support enlightened society.

Because government reflects the character of the people, it cannot rise above their moral condition. Punishment may restrain crime but cannot reform character or make society virtuous. The speaker concludes that preserving and improving American institutions requires more religion, renewed faith, sacrifice, and continued moral teaching, especially by clergy and through the home. Without religious faith, enlightened civilization cannot endure.

Sudan, the world’s last male northern white rhinoceros, died in Kenya at age 45 after his health declined from a severe leg infection. He had been moved from a Czech zoo to Kenya’s Ol Pejeta Conservancy in 2009 with two female northern white rhinos, Najin and Fatu, in hopes they would breed, but they never reproduced. Northern white rhinos once lived across parts of central and eastern Africa, but war and poaching drove them extinct in the wild. Scientists collected sperm from Sudan and other males, but the two remaining females cannot carry a calf. Researchers hope to collect eggs, fertilize them, and implant embryos in southern white rhinos, though egg collection from rhinos has never been done and carries risks.

The study developed and tested a Maternal Vulnerability Segmentation Tool (MVST) to identify pregnant women in Oromia, Ethiopia, who are at higher risk of underusing antenatal care and health facility delivery. Using baseline data from a community-based quasi-experiment, researchers assessed 1,189 pregnant women and analyzed a baseline sample of 470. The tool was derived from predictors such as literacy, distance to health facilities, household assets, mobile phone ownership, food shortage, decision-making, and health worker visits.

Factor analyses identified four key vulnerability items for combined urban-rural settings and six for rural settings, with acceptable reliability and model fit. Higher vulnerability scores were associated with lower antenatal care use and lower likelihood of health facility delivery. Mediation analysis showed that vulnerability affected health facility delivery partly through antenatal care use. The authors conclude that the MVST may help frontline health workers segment pregnant women by vulnerability and support targeted maternal health interventions, while noting the need for further validation across contexts and health outcomes.

Traci Barker-Ball retires after 35 years at Poway High, where she served as student services coordinator, coached and advised student groups, and was PUSD Teacher of the Year in 1991. Don Jones retires after 34 years, most recently teaching health science and coaching track and field at Rancho Bernardo High, after prior work at Poway High. Melinda Watson retires after 34 years at Mt. Carmel High, where she taught math and previously taught swimming, physical education and health while coaching water polo and swimming.

Patsy Malta retires after 33 years, mostly teaching physical education at Mt. Carmel High, where she coached boys volleyball for 31 years and won multiple coaching honors. Lori “Brick” Brickley retires after 32 years, most recently teaching AP biology at Rancho Bernardo High, where she was a founding faculty member and sponsored several student organizations.
