Robert Saxton retires after 31 years at Abraxas High, where he taught art and sustainable agriculture and coordinated the community garden.

The retirees reflected on inspirations for teaching, changes in technology and student needs, memorable student moments, and plans including volunteering, coaching, travel, family time, gardening, art, surfing and staying active. Other retiring high school teachers recognized served between 10 and 29 years in subjects including Spanish, math, business, social science, special education, English, auto courses, adult education, computer science, world languages, library services, health and physical education.

Castle Gardens in Invergordon provides dementia, nursing, residential and end of life care. Facilities include en suite wheelchair-friendly rooms, GP service, activities, minibus trips, gardens, greenhouse and potting shed. Information is supplied by the care home.

Changing lifestyles, hectic schedules, shifting food preferences, and westernization are increasing global demand for convenient snacks, including cheese snacks. Persistence Market Research forecasts the global cheese snacks market to grow at a CAGR of 5.2% from 2017 to 2025. Savory products such as extruded snacks and salted chips are frequently consumed, while frozen and processed cheese are gaining popularity for convenience, affordability, taste, and hunger satisfaction. Demand for baked cheese snacks is rising as health-conscious consumers seek alternatives to fried foods. Growing awareness of cheese’s nutrient profile is also supporting consumption. Companies are focusing on improving taste and quality, with key players including Sargento Foods, PepsiCo, McCain Foods, TINE, UTZ Quality Foods, ITC, and General Mills.

Soumya Swaminathan, pediatrician, tuberculosis researcher and Director General of ICMR, will become WHO Deputy Director General (programmes) in Geneva in late November, the first Indian in the role. She said her priorities will align with WHO Director General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus’s agenda, including universal health coverage, epidemic response, non-communicable diseases, and access to diagnostics and drugs. She described universal health coverage as the biggest challenge, with WHO playing a stewardship and support role. For India, she highlighted regional health disparities and the importance of preventive and promotive healthcare through health and wellness centres. Her father, M.S. Swaminathan, said international exposure offers valuable perspective, and she hopes to continue contributing to India after her WHO stint.

The share of young Americans without college degrees who are working or looking for work has declined, with disconnected youth—those not in school, working, or seeking work—trending upward. Experts cited economic, cultural, and psychological factors, including dissatisfaction with available jobs, fewer family-sustaining roles for non-degree holders, stigma against blue-collar work, mental health challenges, substance issues, isolation, family financial support, and possible undercounting of gig workers. Suggested responses include education models with internships or apprenticeships and efforts to reduce stigma around non-degree career paths, though experts said helping older disconnected young adults may be difficult.

The passage describes a statistical analysis plan for a clinical trial comparing dasiglucagon, GlucaGen, and placebo. Analyses will use tables, listings, and figures following ICH conventions, with two-sided tests at the 0.05 significance level unless otherwise stated. Continuous and categorical variables will be summarized descriptively, and analyses will be performed using SAS, with PK/PD analyses using Phoenix WinNonlin.

Analysis populations include the safety analysis set, full analysis set (FAS), and per protocol set (PPS). The primary efficacy analysis will use the FAS, with supportive PPS analyses; safety analyses will use the safety set. The primary endpoint is time to plasma glucose recovery, defined as a ≥20 mg/dL increase from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue IV glucose. Secondary endpoints include glucose recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes and glucose changes from baseline at those time points.

Primary comparisons focus on dasiglucagon versus placebo using a stratified log-rank test adjusted for age group and injection site, with hierarchical testing to control multiplicity. Kaplan-Meier methods, sensitivity analyses, Wilcoxon tests, Cox proportional hazards models, and interpolation-based supportive analyses are also planned. Secondary recovery endpoints will use Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests, and glucose changes will use ANOVA.

The plan also covers demographic, baseline, concomitant medication, pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, safety, laboratory, vital sign, ECG, local tolerability, adverse event, and immunogenicity analyses. Missing data will not be imputed, and no interim analyses are planned. Appendices specify programming, formatting, quality control, derivation rules, and planned tables, figures, and listings.

The SPREAD offense is a 3-2 no-post motion offense requiring all players to pass, handle, cut, and read defensive overplays. Its continuity uses basket cuts, middle replacements, corner clears, and triple-threat decisions. Overplayed players should immediately back cut rather than fight pressure. Ball handlers may drive when defenders overplay passing lanes, then kick out if help defense appears. A back door option allows a corner player to break middle and feed an overplayed wing cutting to the basket.

Research from Ben-Gurion University found that using smiley emojis in formal work emails can reduce perceptions of the sender’s competence without increasing perceived warmth. In experiments with 549 participants from 29 countries, emails containing smileys led to less detailed responses and less information sharing. Unlike real smiles or smiling photos, which improved perceptions of competence and friendliness, smileys in work emails made senders seem less competent while not affecting friendliness. Participants were also more likely to assume an unknown sender using a smiley was female. Researchers advised avoiding smileys in initial workplace interactions.

Deepa Das Acevedo, a legal anthropologist and Emory law professor, argues that tenure protections are being weakened through state legislation, university policies and recent rapid disciplinary actions against faculty over social media speech. In an interview about her book The War on Tenure, she says attacks on tenure are intentional and tied to broader pressures on higher education, including defunding, classroom restrictions and retaliation for extramural speech.

Acevedo says the core justifications for tenure remain employment security and academic freedom. She rejects claims that tenure makes professors unproductive, saying available empirical data does not support that stereotype. She also argues tenure does not prevent universities from firing faculty for just cause, including serious misconduct or academic integrity violations; institutions may fail to act because of their own willingness or circumstances, not because tenure makes discipline impossible.

Recent dismissals after comments about Charlie Kirk, she says, show that universities increasingly disregard tenure’s expected processes, such as notice, due process and faculty input, sometimes terminating faculty within hours or days over social media posts.

U.S. Border Patrol agent Larry O’Neal, 44, of Houlton, was indicted Feb. 15 on a federal felony charge of possessing child pornography and pleaded not guilty Feb. 22 in U.S. District Court in Bangor. Investigators traced a suspected file to his home IP address, searched his home and vehicle on Jan. 19, and found child and adult pornography on a computer and external drive. Documents say O’Neal admitted downloading pornography using search terms including “young,” “rape,” and “teen hardcore.” No evidence showed use of government property. If convicted, he faces up to 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine.

A qualitative component of a quality improvement project examined perceptions of regional teaching for Stage 1 anaesthetic trainees in one UK deanery following the 2021 anaesthetic curriculum change. The deanery had around 50 core or ACCS anaesthetic trainees across five hospital trusts and previously had no Stage 1 regional teaching programme, with low GMC survey scores for regional teaching in some trusts.

Researchers conducted semi-structured Microsoft Teams focus groups with six trainees and eight trainers, including all college tutors and relevant school board members. Thematic analysis identified three overarching areas: Stage 1 training is complicated, implementation would not be easy, and a regional programme was worth trying.

Participants described uncertainty caused by the new curriculum, high demands on trainees, the importance and difficulty of the primary FRCA examination, and varied trainee learning needs. They reported major differences between hospitals in teaching quality, exam support, trainee numbers, resources, and consultant compensation for teaching, creating perceived unfairness and siloed working.

Concerns about a regional programme included location, travel, teaching format, room availability, group size, rota coordination, funding, and maintaining teaching quality. However, trainers and trainees identified potential benefits, including fairer access to teaching, better exam-focused support, broader educational content, development of educators, easier organisation for smaller hospitals, and improved networking.

The study concluded that both trainers and trainees supported developing a regional Stage 1 anaesthetic teaching programme, while recognising that success would require engagement, investment, quality control, and ongoing evaluation. Limitations included the small number of trainee participants and possible interviewer-related bias.

Neonatal jaundice affects many newborns and can lead to serious outcomes in severe cases. This study performed a genome-wide association study of neonatal jaundice using nearly 30,000 Norwegian parent-offspring trios, with replication in Danish cohorts. Two neonatal loci reached genome-wide significance: the UGT1A* region and a locus near CHRDL1 on chromosome X. A missense variant in UGT1A4, rs6755571, was associated with a substantially lower risk of neonatal jaundice and replicated in Danish data. Analyses suggested the effect was driven by the neonate’s inherited allele and may relate to regulation of UGT1A1 expression in the intestine rather than direct UGT1A4 bilirubin activity.

A maternal GWAS identified loci including ABO, where associations were consistent with maternal-fetal ABO blood group incompatibility, a known contributor to jaundice risk. The protective UGT1A4-associated variant remained protective despite ABO incompatibility and showed stronger effects in full-term and post-term newborns.

Comparison with adult bilirubin genetics showed important differences. Adult bilirubin-associated variants at UGT1A* and SLCO1B1 were not strongly associated with neonatal jaundice, and an adult bilirubin polygenic score was associated with neonatal jaundice mainly due to chromosome 2, which contains UGT1A*. The authors conclude that neonatal jaundice has context-specific genetic mechanisms that differ from adult bilirubin regulation.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 26, 2016, reporting that it issued a press release, data sheet, and supplemental materials regarding financial results for its first fiscal quarter ended December 26, 2015. The filing lists Exhibits 99.1, 99.2, and 99.3 for those materials. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The passage describes a hard-sided, collapsible portable shelter or camper designed to provide rigid, weather-tight, lockable protection while remaining compact and transportable. It can transition between an expanded configuration for sleeping, standing, or living use and a collapsed configuration forming a low-profile case. The shelter may include rigid insulated wall panels, roof, and floor; folding or bi-fold side, front, and rear panels; weather stripping or gaskets; doors, windows, locks, latches, and mechanical or powered opening systems.

The camper may be transported on vehicle roof racks, in pickup beds, on trailers, or by bicycles, motorcycles, cars, or people, and may remain attached to a vehicle without permanent modification. Embodiments may include solar panels, batteries, lighting, climate control, electronics, plumbing, kitchens, bathrooms, seating, and movable bed systems. Larger versions may use multiple folding wall sections and a mid-section connector to provide standing height, while a bed platform can be raised or lowered to allow different interior configurations. The passage also describes construction materials, dimensions, storage arrangements, sealing methods, fixtures, and methods for opening, closing, transporting, and using the shelter.

Germany’s RWE Supply & Trading may double or triple its LNG derivatives trades this year from 1.5 million tonnes in 2017, driven by price-risk management and Asia’s move toward spot and short-term trading. Its physical LNG trading rose to 6 million tonnes last year from 4.5 million in 2016. Executive Javier Moret cited fragmented Asian demand, new buyers, and uncertainty in power markets as factors boosting spot and derivatives activity. RWE is active in Platts’ JKM derivatives market and has already traded 7 to 10 JKM-indexed physical cargoes this year.

The passage explains pivot point trading strategies, which use support and resistance levels derived from previous market data, mainly the prior day’s high, low, and close. The author backtested six simple pivot point strategies on 1-minute futures data from 2010 onward for ES, NQ, RTY, and USD/CHF. None were found consistently tradeable, though some day-trading ideas might merit further research. One NQ strategy produced 172 trades with an average gain of 0.16% and a 62% win rate, but results were erratic. Other strategies performed poorly or had negative average gains. Lewis Borsellino reportedly used pivot points daily but did not explain his method. The passage states pivot points were invented by floor traders, are easy, objective, quantifiable, and versatile, but lag price and had low win ratios in the tests.

Lawton High School unveiled the second panel of a 22-foot Wolverine mural in its cafeteria. Created by art teacher Kenneth Hobbs and funded by the class of 2014, the new panel depicts the school, the “Hanta Yo!” sign, a Wolverine, and the 1993 National Wrestling Champions.

The lecture reviews the number four-vector and covariant number conservation, then introduces the stress-energy tensor as the central object describing energy density, energy flux, momentum density, and momentum flux. For dust, it is written as \(T^{\alpha\beta}=\rho_0 u^\alpha u^\beta\), and its components show that energy density is not a scalar or four-vector component but part of a tensor. The tensor is symmetric; a physical argument using torques on a small cube motivates why nonsymmetric spatial stresses would imply unphysical behavior.

A perfect fluid is defined as having no energy flow in its rest frame and no lateral stresses, leaving only energy density and isotropic pressure. Its stress-energy tensor is diagonal in the rest frame and can be written covariantly using the metric, four-velocity, energy density, and pressure. The lecture emphasizes that in relativistic gravity the whole stress-energy tensor, not just mass or energy density, must act as the source of gravity.

Stress-energy conservation is expressed covariantly as \(\partial_\alpha T^{\alpha\beta}=0\), combining conservation of energy and momentum, which separate only after choosing a reference frame. Additional examples include the stress-energy tensor of a point particle using Dirac delta functions and that of electromagnetic fields using the Faraday tensor, with components corresponding to field energy density, the Poynting vector, and electromagnetic stresses.

The lecture then begins transitioning toward curvature by introducing flat spacetime in curvilinear coordinates. Polar coordinates are used to show that coordinate basis vectors need not be normalized or constant, leading to transformation matrices with dimensionally different entries and, later, a metric with nontrivial coordinate dependence.

The passage discusses an article on minority representation in U.S. special education. It notes that federal policy has addressed concerns that racial, ethnic, and language-minority children are overrepresented in special education. However, the cited study found no evidence of disproportionate overrepresentation. After adjusting for factors such as socioeconomic status, academic achievement, and behavior, racial, ethnic, and language-minority children were less likely than comparable White, English-speaking children to be identified as disabled. The author argues that policies aimed at reducing minority special education placement may conflict with findings that minority children are comparatively underrepresented based on need.

The speaker says limiting opponents’ puck time, especially in their defensive zone and down low, is key. They note Mike’s speed and puck handling make him difficult to stop, and say giving players like him and Joe Nieuwendyk less room and time would help.

South Korea’s spy agency suspects two female North Korean agents assassinated Kim Jong Nam, the estranged half-brother of Kim Jong Un, in Malaysia. U.S. sources also said they believed he was killed by North Korean assassins. South Korean lawmakers said intelligence officials believed Kim was poisoned and that Kim Jong Un had issued a standing order for his killing, with a failed attempt in 2012. Malaysian police said the victim held a passport under the name Kim Chol and died after falling ill at Kuala Lumpur International Airport while preparing to travel to Macau. An autopsy was being conducted, and police said CCTV indicated a woman was involved. South Korean media reported he was poisoned with a needle by two women who fled by taxi, though Reuters could not confirm that. South Korea condemned the suspected killing and urged defectors to be cautious.

Minnesota public schools receive student mental health support from school staff, outside practitioners and nonprofits offering specialized care. Know the Truth provides substance-use prevention and peer recovery support, using staff with personal recovery experience to help students dealing with their own or family members’ addiction. Youth peer specialist Tiffany White works in schools and community settings, emphasizing harm reduction, trust-building and nonjudgmental support.

Restoration for All supports African immigrant and refugee youth through culturally specific mental health services, staff workshops, screenings, therapy, suicide monitoring and African mind-body practices. Founder Tolulope Ola said schools often misunderstand students’ cultural backgrounds and trauma histories, and the organization works to bridge gaps between school and home approaches to mental health. Both nonprofits rely on grants and contracts, with funding cuts affecting some services.

A Salvadoran woman who fled after two of her children disappeared amid gang violence was detained shortly after crossing into Texas and deported with about 100 other migrants under the Trump administration’s zero-tolerance policy. The article says many migrants from El Salvador, Honduras and Guatemala are fleeing gangs, not joining them; U.S. statistics show gang members made up 0.09% of 2017 Border Patrol detentions. It describes how MS-13 and Barrio 18 control neighborhoods, extort residents, threaten young people and restrict movement, while security forces also contribute to violence. Internal relocation is often ineffective in El Salvador, and advocates say many deportees try to migrate again soon after return.

Thames Centre councillor Kelly Elliot is urging the Thames Valley District School Board to adopt a defibrillator policy and install AEDs in schools. West Nissouri Public School fundraised for a device after a local child died during soccer, but the board declined installation and has not commented.
Division Two affirmed the Kitsap County Superior Court judgment.

Adrienne Motley moved to No. 7 on Miami’s all-time scoring list, passing Octavia Blue’s 1,724 points, as the No. 16 Hurricanes defeated Clemson 81-57. Miami also held its annual Play4Kay game and celebrated women’s athletics. Jessica Thomas reached 1,200 career points and led Miami with 18 points, while Motley scored 15 and Laura Cornelius added 14. Miami led for more than 36 minutes, shot efficiently early, and took a 48-30 halftime lead before outscoring Clemson 17-4 in the third quarter. The Hurricanes also led bench scoring 28-13. Miami next travels to face No. 14 Duke.

Eric Bass forwarded an Oct. 12, 2000 Dallas Morning News “Inside UT Football” newsletter by Chip Brown. The newsletter discusses Texas football after its loss to Oklahoma and ahead of its game at Colorado. Major Applewhite was named starter for the Colorado game, with Chris Simms to be used only if needed, while B.J. Johnson and Roy Williams were promoted to starting receiver roles. Brown addresses fan questions about the quarterback rotation, offensive struggles, coaching criticism, leadership issues, Kenny Hayter’s expected increased carries, Shaun Rogers’ anticipated return, recruiting, and Texas’ Big 12 South outlook. Brown says the Colorado game is crucial for Texas’ conference title hopes and that a win could put the Longhorns back in strong position.

U.S. stocks rebounded Wednesday as banks, energy companies and smaller companies rose, driven by hopes Italy could avoid new elections. The S&P 500, Dow, Nasdaq and Russell 2000 all posted gains for the day.

Several Long Island commercial real estate transactions were completed, including office leases in Melville by the Law Office of Peter D. Baron, Hartford Fire Insurance and Hollander Legal Group; retail leases in Carle Place by Jersey Mike’s Subs, Hand and Stone Massage and Fortunoff Bedding; an industrial lease in Ronkonkoma by SCH Sheet Metal; and an $850,000 Miller Place property sale to Marbai Profit Sharing.

A petition opposing the proposed closure of Alyn Family Doctors’ Gresford Health Centre branch has gained more than 600 signatures. The practice says it lacks the manpower to run three sites and has asked Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board to consider moving services to its Llay and Rossett surgeries. Patients fear longer travel, appointment pressures, and added strain from proposed housing developments. BCUHB said it is aware of the challenges and is supporting the practice in gathering patient feedback.

Travis Phippen of Valencia, who was wounded in the Las Vegas mass shooting that killed his father, John Phippen, filed a civil lawsuit against gunman Stephen Paddock’s estate in Clark County, Nevada. The suit seeks control and preservation of Paddock’s assets, including bank funds, safe deposit boxes, property and other estate holdings. At least 59 people were killed and 527 wounded in the Route 91 Harvest shooting. John Phippen died after being shot in the back, while Travis was shot in the arm. Several other Santa Clarita Valley residents remained hospitalized and recovering.

Scale AI cofounder Alexandr Wang says young people should spend thousands of hours “vibe-coding” with AI tools, comparing the opportunity to Bill Gates and Mark Zuckerberg gaining an early advantage with personal computers. He argues deep practice with AI coding assistants could become a major career advantage as automation reshapes tech jobs. Wang, who became a billionaire at 25, now leads Meta’s AI superintelligence team as chief AI officer.

A gaming machine, control method, and program are disclosed for synchronizing in-game event display timing with the beat of background music. The machine includes displays, speakers, storage, and a controller. The storage holds BGM sound data and tempo data containing beat information. The controller outputs the BGM, determines event display timing based on the tempo data, dynamically configures animation data so the event appears at that timing, and displays it.

Embodiments include synchronizing events triggered by player operations, random bonus events, event sounds, illumination, and multiple sequential events using rhythm pattern data. In a slot game example, the controller determines reel stop positions, identifies beat-aligned frame counts, generates reel spin and stop animations, and stops reels in synchronization with the BGM beat. Bonus-game animations can also be timed to BGM beats. The disclosed technique aims to reduce timing mismatch between sound and visual events and provide rhythmic game progression.

During an in-game penalty kick, the ball becomes live once kicked forward, so defenders must be positioned legally and ready to react to saves, blocks, or rebounds. Under Law 14, all players except the kicker and goalkeeper must be at least 10 yards from the mark, behind it, inside the field, and outside the penalty area. Defenders should take positions quickly, avoid illegal jostling, and move only after the ball is kicked and clearly moves forward.

Defenders must follow up every penalty kick, beat attackers to rebounds, clear danger, and transition quickly to attack if the goalkeeper secures or the team clears the ball. They must also know that the kicker may not touch the ball again until another player has touched it, except after a goalkeeper block. Early defender encroachment results in a goal if scored or a retake if not.

The passage also notes the rare “tap” penalty, where the kicker touches the ball forward for a teammate to shoot. Coaches are advised to practice defensive positioning, rebound reactions, outlet passes, and scenarios including goalkeeper blocks, secured balls, goalpost rebounds, and tap penalties. The article applies to penalty kicks during play, not shoot-outs, where no follow-up is allowed.

Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi won the 2025 Nobel Prize in chemistry for work on metal-organic frameworks, porous molecular structures that can store gases and chemicals. Potential uses include collecting water from air, capturing carbon dioxide and extracting PFAS. Robson created an early hole-filled crystalline structure in the late 1980s; Kitagawa developed MOFs that absorb gases; and Yaghi created a highly porous, stable framework with enormous surface area.

The speaker expresses gratitude for citizens’ confidence and acknowledges anxiety over the responsibilities of the chief executive office. He reviews the United States’ progress under self-government and the Constitution, citing regulated commerce, admission of new states, territorial expansion, protection of rights, prosperity, and successful endurance of war as evidence of effective institutions.

He emphasizes preserving the Union, crediting the people and their representatives for national success, and argues that liberty depends on an intelligent and virtuous citizenry. He warns that ignorance and corruption could enable usurpation, and urges constitutional efforts to promote public intelligence.

The speaker also identifies foreign dangers, including possible war, threats to commerce, navigation, fisheries, and national independence. He calls for fortified coasts and frontiers, a moderate but adequate Army and Navy, and especially a well-organized militia prepared in peace for emergencies.

He supports internal improvements such as roads and canals with constitutional sanction, saying they would strengthen interstate connection and the Union. He advocates government encouragement of manufacturing to reduce dependence on foreign supplies, support domestic capital, and provide markets for raw materials. He calls for friendly, liberal relations with Indian tribes and efforts to extend to them the advantages of civilization.

He notes strong revenue, a flourishing Treasury, and public lands as resources sufficient for emergencies and early repayment of the national debt. He stresses economy, accountability, and legislative oversight in public spending. He welcomes peace and pledges to preserve it on just terms with all nations. He also celebrates increasing harmony in the Union and commits to advancing republican principles and national interests, while honoring his predecessors and seeking divine protection.

This qualitative study explored infectious disease diagnostics stakeholders’ views on the utility and implementation of metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) for routine clinical use. mNGS can detect pathogens, antimicrobial resistance, functional genes and virulence genes from a single sample, but adoption in clinical laboratories has been limited despite its potential to overcome constraints of culture-based diagnostics.

Using an interpretive phenomenological approach, ten UK participants from clinical and academic roles were interviewed via Microsoft Teams between July and November 2021. Thematic analysis identified five themes: diagnostic choice, infrastructure, open data sharing, COVID-19 and communication.

Participants viewed mNGS as a valuable addition to diagnostic toolkits, but not a universal replacement for existing tests. Cost, funding disparities, and the need to demonstrate cost-effectiveness were major barriers. Speed was also critical, as results must be available within clinically actionable timeframes. Infrastructure challenges included limited laboratory and digital capacity, insufficient bioinformatics training, workforce constraints, accreditation difficulties, standardisation issues and inadequate data storage systems. Participants highlighted tensions between open genomic data sharing and patient privacy, while also noting that shared data could improve surveillance. COVID-19 was described as proof of concept for sequencing’s public health value and as a driver of capacity, visibility and manufacturing improvements. Communication within hospitals, between hospitals, and among healthcare, academia, industry and funders was considered essential for implementation.

The study found that barriers to routine mNGS include cost, speed, infrastructure, training, accreditation, standardisation, data systems and fragmented communication. Participants were generally positive about mNGS, especially following COVID-19, and emphasized that future diagnostic development must address clinical usability, equitable access and integration into existing workflows.

NHS staff recreated a 1927 photograph found in a broom cupboard to mark the health service’s 70th anniversary. The original image, taken at Sandwell Hospital in West Bromwich when it was Hallam Hospital, showed a matron, assistant and nurses. Fourteen staff from Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust recreated it in the same spot. The recovered images will be displayed during an NHS70 tea party at Sandwell Hospital.

VentureWire’s Nov. 7, 2000 issue reports Broadcom’s acquisition of SiByte for up to $2 billion in stock, Alta Partners’ new $275 million to $325 million fund, Furniture.com’s shutdown and layoffs, and eStellarNet’s $30 million first institutional round. The issue also covers numerous venture financings across IT, wireless, software, e-commerce, real estate, music, communications, and financial services; layoffs at Divine interVentures; Foodoo.com’s closure; product launches and company renamings; several acquisitions including Sonus buying telecom technologies and InfoSpace acquiring Locus Dialogue; board and executive appointments; new and expanding venture funds; VC personnel moves; and a correction regarding Tantivy’s location.

At Puerto Cortés in northern Honduras, Sergio Romero visits the Avontuur, a 97-year-old schooner that reached Honduras from Europe using wind power. Unlike typical cargo ships, it carries small cargo with sails rather than bunker fuel.

Andrew Lo discusses an auction exercise showing how lack of information affects valuation: an iPod sold for $45, while an autographed book retailing at $45 sold for $60. He connects this to current events, explaining the federal government’s takeover of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, government-sponsored entities that bought mortgages to support secondary lending markets. He says uncertainty about their obligations made their securities difficult to value, and the Treasury stepped in to guarantee their claims to prevent broader market disruption. Shareholders were expected to lose most of their investment, while counterparties holding issued paper were protected by government backing.

Lo then introduces the lecture topic: present value relations. He defines assets as sequences of current and future cashflows, excluding past cashflows, and notes that cashflows may be positive, negative, or zero. He emphasizes that assets must be considered at a specific point in time because their future cashflows can change. Examples include businesses, property, patents, reputation, and trade secrets, with discussion of patents as legally protected monopolies granted in exchange for disclosure.

He defines valuation as applying a value operator to a sequence of cashflows, with market prices serving as one example of such a valuation. To value assets, he stresses drawing timelines to identify when cashflows occur. Under perfect certainty, cashflows at different dates should be treated like different currencies: they cannot be added directly without conversion. Present value converts all future cashflows into today’s dollars using market-derived exchange rates or discount factors.

Lo explains net present value as the sum of current and future cashflows converted into present dollars, assuming known cashflows, known exchange rates, and no transaction frictions. He introduces the interest rate or opportunity cost of capital as a way to express exchange rates across time, where future cashflows are discounted by factors such as 1/(1+r). He concludes that, under simplifying assumptions, any certain cashflow sequence can be valued using present value methods, and the next lecture will apply this to annuities and perpetuities.
The speaker said effort is present but the team did not play together well, must act on its goals, and may need others to step up amid key injuries.

CUPA-HR’s report examines Title IX staffing in higher education amid changing federal regulations. Title IX offices most commonly reside in Human Resources (29%) or Student Affairs/Dean of Students/Student Services (28%), with smaller shares in compliance, DEI, legal affairs, presidents’ offices, academic affairs, or operations.

Dedicated Title IX staffing has increased: institutions with at least one full-time Title IX position rose from one-third in 2019-20 to 43% in 2023-24, while total reported Title IX staff increased 38%. However, 56% of institutions still lack a dedicated full-time Title IX position. Heads of institutional Title IX compliance are the most common role, followed by Title IX investigators and deputy heads. Doctoral institutions are most likely to have dedicated and multiple Title IX staff.

Women hold 77% of Title IX positions, and Black women are represented at more than double their share of the overall professional higher education workforce. Median salaries are $96,714 for heads, $84,931 for deputy heads, and $75,000 for investigators, all above the overall professional median of $66,000. Women and people of color in Title IX roles are paid equitably compared to White men, with several groups having higher median pay ratios.

The report recommends that institutions reassess Title IX responsibilities, increase staffing where needed, and monitor legal and regulatory developments to maintain compliance.

Berkshire Hathaway sold its 10.6 million-share stake in General Electric in the second quarter, according to a regulatory filing. The shares stemmed largely from Warren Buffett’s roughly $3 billion crisis-era investment in GE in 2008, which generated more than $1 billion in profit including dividends. The sale came as GE changed CEOs, with Jeff Immelt handing the role to John Flannery, and as GE shares fell nearly 20% for the year.

Berkshire also bought shares of Synchrony Financial and added to Bank of New York Mellon and Apple positions. Other filings showed Appaloosa Management sold its SPDR S&P 500 ETF stake, Soros bought more than $1 billion of PowerShares QQQ Trust, and Viking Global Investors purchased 12.3 million Wells Fargo shares worth about $680 million. Wells Fargo continued facing fallout from sales-practice and consumer-lending issues.

Gary Allen Darnell, 45, a convicted sex offender from Cottage Hills, was arrested in Grafton for allegedly loitering within 500 feet of a park after approaching children near the river and offering fishing poles. Jersey County State’s Attorney Ben Goetten said prosecutors will seek maximum penalties if he is convicted.

A Spring ISD middle school teacher is on administrative leave and under investigation after allegedly calling African American students “cotton pickers” at Dueitt Middle School. A parent reported the incident, other students confirmed hearing the slur, and the district removed the teacher from the classroom while the investigation continues.

His Majesty seeks formal acknowledgment by the United States of his Kingdom as a sovereign and independent state, arguing that foreign consuls, agents, and naval commanders have already treated it as such. The request cites major changes over the past twenty-three years: creation of a written language, widespread schools and literacy, publication of books, organization of a limited representative monarchy, enactment of civil and criminal laws, annual legislative sessions, courts, and jury trials. Foreigners and officials have relied on and demanded protection from these institutions, which His Majesty says has been provided. He also argues that continued independence serves commercial nations because the islands are central to whale fisheries, lie on key routes between America and Asia, and provide important repairs and supplies for vessels in the Pacific.

This study examines kindergarten teachers’ views and experiences regarding the role, teaching, challenges, and opportunities of visual arts in early childhood education, especially in multicultural pre-school settings. The literature review presents visual arts as supporting children’s expression, creativity, communication, emotional development, socialization, cooperation, problem-solving, observation, and inclusion, while noting that teachers often face limited training, resources, time, and confidence in teaching them.

The research used a mixed-type questionnaire with 16 closed and five open questions, administered electronically to 65 kindergarten teachers working in public or private kindergartens in the Municipality of Piraeus. Most participants were women, aged 23–42, held a four-year degree, had 1–5 years of experience, and had no specific visual arts training. Data were analyzed using SPSS and thematic analysis of open responses.

Findings show that most teachers considered visual arts crucial in early childhood education and believed they support imagination, creativity, intellectual development, emotional expression, social interaction, and social skills. Many reported that toddlers respond well to art activities and that children show high interest and participation. Teachers viewed positive feedback as important and described preferred strategies such as free approaches, group teaching, guided approaches, experimentation with materials, and use of tools such as theatre, brushes, recyclable materials, and messy play.

The main challenges identified were child management, concentration difficulties, tool-handling difficulties, lack of time, limited materials, school-related constraints, and parental ignorance. Suggested responses included patience, individual guidance, online demonstrations, rewards, role assignment, games, varied materials, cooperation, flexibility, continuous feedback, and support for imagination and self-expression. The study concludes that teachers hold positive views of visual arts, but effective integration requires targeted support, resources, training, and collaborative initiatives. Limitations include reliance on electronic questionnaire administration and limited depth compared with qualitative interviews.

The German Ambassador, recently returned from Berlin, stated that Germany was willing to confidentially present peace terms, including giving up Belgium while retaining travel rights on the Meuse, maintaining neutral buffer states, preserving French coastal territory, restoring Russian territory, properly treating Serbia and Roumania, and indemnifying Belgium. He claimed Britain hesitated to state peace terms because its maximum terms with allies were infeasible and minimum terms risked disputes, but might do so if pressured by America.

The Greek Chargé conveyed Greece’s response to the U.S. peace proposal, expressing strong appreciation for President Wilson’s initiative. Greece emphasized its suffering as a neutral state, citing violations of neutrality, loss of its fleet, disarmament, foreign occupation, blockade, and hardship among civilians. Greece said it remained committed to neutrality, supported peace efforts, regretted limitations on communication with belligerents, and stood ready to join future action securing stable peace, sovereignty, and independence for all states.

The passage outlines SOS defensive responses to side screen/roll action. When the screen occurs below the free throw line extended, defenders trap the ballhandler near the base or corner checkpoint before the screen is set, rotate into high/low Helpside “I” positions, deny return passes, front or snuggle post players, and close out according to passes out of the trap. If the ball enters the post, the nearest post defenders double team and others maintain Helpside “I” or denial positions, with all rotations occurring as the ball leaves the passer’s hands.

Above the free throw line, defenders use an aggressive contact switch to prevent quick jump shots and middle penetration. The screener is bumped and hedged, the ballhandler is forced toward the sideline or corner checkpoint, and defenders move into smother, snuggle denial, fronting, and weakside “I” responsibilities.

The “All Out” SOS disruption attacks before the screen or pass develops by trapping the point guard, forcing the offense out of planned routes. Defenders rotate by near-player principles, deny return passes, cover rolls to the basket, and apply basic SOS rules once matched up. Secondary traps occur on post entries or base rolls, with rotations and closeouts determined by the next pass or drive.

Whitman Howard raised Produce Investments Ltd’s target price from GBX 210 to GBX 240 and maintained a buy rating. Shore Capital and Numis Securities also reiterated buy ratings, with Numis setting a GBX 286 target. Shares traded at GBX 187 on Thursday, with a 12-month range of GBX 143 to GBX 220 and market capitalization of GBX 50.52 million. The company declared a GBX 5.03 dividend payable December 5. Produce Investments grows, sources, packs and markets potatoes, daffodil bulbs and flowers.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on November 18, 2022, it entered into a 364-day unsecured revolving credit agreement with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent and other lenders. The facility provides up to $10.0 billion in borrowing capacity, may be extended for an additional 364 days, and initially bears interest at SOFR plus 0.45%, with a 0.05% commitment fee on undrawn amounts. Borrowings will be used for general corporate purposes, including backing notes under Amazon’s commercial paper program. The agreement includes customary representations, covenants, and default provisions, but no financial covenants.

Marines with Task Force Southwest practiced flying InstantEye drones at Camp Lejeune ahead of a spring deployment to Afghanistan. Also at Camp Lejeune, 2nd Law Enforcement Battalion completed grenade-assault training for an upcoming exercise. The Marine Corps awarded a Purple Heart to 91-year-old Lee Anderson for injuries from Iwo Jima 72 years earlier.

Three University of Dayton students reported a naked man entered their bedrooms early Wednesday near campus. Incidents occurred on Woodland Ave., Frericks Way, and College Park, with entry through windows or an unsecured door. The suspect was described as a white male in his mid-20s. University police are investigating.

Hampton and Newport News police apprehended a 15-year-old suspect after a January 31 robbery at a Tinee Giant in Hampton. Police said the robber brandished a gun and left in a Ford SUV. Newport News police later found the SUV, and an officer found the teen nearby with a handgun and outstanding juvenile petitions. He faces firearm, concealed weapon, and tobacco charges, but no robbery charge.

The speaker discusses Corey Perry’s major junior success, playoff learning experience, and effectiveness with the puck. He says extra players are kept with the group for team building and education rather than separated. An injured player with a hand issue remains doubtful pending medical clearance. The speaker emphasizes the importance of strong starts, staying even-keeled through success and adversity, avoiding distractions, and preparing immediately for the next game. He says the team is committed to its system, leadership, sacrifice, and collective play, while recognizing the Stanley Cup opportunity may not come again.

The speaker reports that the United States is prosperous, with strong agriculture, manufactures, commerce, navigation, public credit, and confidence in government, shown partly by rapid subscriptions to the Bank of the United States. Measures from the previous session have been executed, including frontier defense. Treaties and peace efforts with Native tribes have continued, while military operations against hostile groups have been undertaken when peace efforts failed. The speaker urges policies ensuring justice, regulated land alienation, fair commerce, civilization efforts, peace incentives, and penalties for treaty violations.

The distilled spirits duties law has been implemented, though compensation provisions may need revision and some public discontent has arisen from novelty or misunderstanding. The permanent seat of government has been fixed on the Potomac, including Alexandria and Georgetown, and a city plan prepared. The census indicates the population borders on four million. Loans in Holland have been completed or initiated. Treaties with the Cherokees and Six Nations will be submitted to the Senate.

The debt subscription program has largely succeeded, and current revenues appear sufficient without new burdens unless unforeseen needs arise. The House is asked to provide for the next year’s service and immediate Treasury demands. Congress is also urged to address the militia, arsenals, fortifications, the post office and post roads, the mint, uniform weights and measures, and the sale of vacant public lands pledged toward the public debt.

The passage argues that while higher education has long leaned politically left, “viewpoint diversity” is inconsistently defined and may be used to advance political agendas. It says the Trump administration is pressuring universities through grant incentives and policy demands tied to federal priorities. The author warns that making funding contingent on compliance could undermine genuine intellectual diversity on campuses.

Michael Bennett, 39, and Trisha Steffes, 36, of Sarasota were arrested after accepting an internationally shipped package containing carfentanil, a synthetic opioid the DEA says is far more potent than morphine and fentanyl. A search of their home found over 7 grams of fentanyl, other drugs and paraphernalia. Both face drug-related charges and were released on bond.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting a temporary suspension of trading under its 401(k) plan. On November 15, 2019, the company notified plan participants that Fidelity Investments was selected as the new recordkeeper. During the expected blackout period from January 2, 2020, to the week of January 12, 2020, participants cannot make exchanges or allocation changes, take loans, or request withdrawals or distributions. On November 19, 2019, Amazon notified Section 16 officers and directors that trading restrictions would apply to certain company equity securities during the blackout period.

Alexander Zverev reached the French Open third round after a five-set win over Dusan Lajovic, continuing his pursuit of a first grand slam quarterfinal despite past struggles at majors. Grigor Dimitrov and Kei Nishikori also rallied from 2-1 set deficits, while Dominic Thiem’s match with Stefanos Tsitsipas was suspended due to darkness. Simona Halep overcame a slow start to beat Alison Riske, and Petra Kvitova and Elina Svitolina advanced in straight sets. Novak Djokovic defeated Jaume Munar in straight sets, while Marco Trungelliti lost to Marco Cecchinato.

The passage describes display device embodiments with a display panel including a display area with pixels, a peripheral area, a pad area, a circuit area, crack or defect sensing lines, test data lines, switching elements, and static electricity discharge elements. The crack sensing lines extend around the display area or bending area and connect to input pads and a crack sensing circuit used to detect defects such as cracks, lifting, or protrusions based on resistance changes.

The crack sensing circuit may include switching elements connected to data lines and test gate lines, matching resistors, and static electricity discharge elements connected to ends of the crack sensing lines. The static electricity discharge elements may include capacitors, transistors, or diodes, and may be positioned in a center area of the circuit area where switching elements are not disposed. Capacitors may connect between test data lines or between a test data line and a connection wire, and may include multiple sub-capacitors connected to sub-wires.

During testing, a test voltage is applied through the pad area and crack sensing lines. If no defect exists, pixels connected through the switching elements display a predetermined gray. If a crack or other defect increases resistance or disconnects a sensing line, affected pixel columns may show white lines, indicating a defect. The static electricity discharge elements store or discharge static electricity from the crack sensing lines, helping prevent leakage current, circuit damage, and erroneous defect detection.

The passage also describes possible bending-area configurations, layer structures, conductive and insulating layers, touch sensor layers, encapsulation, and variations in circuit placement and sensing-line arrangement.

Editors of the Foreign Relations series access State Department, Reagan Library, and other agency records, many pending declassification and transfer to the National Archives. The passage describes research sources, RAC scanning limitations, and editorial methods, including chronological presentation, preservation of original text features, bracketed corrections or omissions, classification notes, and source footnotes.

The passage argues that children often give brief answers or hesitate to ask questions, which can limit curiosity and learning. It recommends that parents and caregivers ask specific open-ended questions, engage seriously with children’s “why” questions, model curiosity, admit when they do not know something and show how to find answers, listen actively, avoid multitasking, and ask follow-up questions to encourage deeper conversation.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for indicating wireless channel status in digital communications, particularly for 5G NR high-frequency systems using beamforming. It addresses beam failure recovery and the sharing of quasi co-located (QCL) or spatial QCL information between user equipment (UE) and access nodes for decoding control and data channels such as PDCCH and PDSCH.

Example embodiments provide UE operations after beam failure recovery. A UE may receive a frame on a channel associated with a new beam identified during recovery, assume a QCL relationship between the channel and that beam, and decode the frame using a reference signal and the spatial receive filter used for the beam. After receiving updated QCL or transmission configuration indication (TCI) information, the UE may use the updated relationship for later frames.

Other embodiments describe decoding PDSCH data by assuming a QCL relationship with a PDCCH control channel, handling cases where TCI fields are present or absent in downlink control information, updating TCI tables and mappings after recovery, or temporarily assuming no QCL relationship until updated configuration is received. The disclosure also describes supporting communication systems, UE and base station architectures, and computing components for implementing the methods.

This cross-sectional study examined self-esteem and physical activity among 10th and 11th grade students at Capa Science High School in Istanbul during the 2022–2023 school year. Data were collected from 225 of 278 students using sociodemographic questions, the International Physical Activity Questionnaire Short Form, the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale, and self-reported height, weight, and school success.

Among participants, 71.6% were male and 27.6% were female. Males had higher Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale scores than females. Students who reported regular exercise had higher self-esteem scores than those who did not. Self-esteem was positively correlated with physical activity MET scores, height, and self-reported school success. BMI categories were not significantly associated with self-esteem. According to IPAQ-SF, 23% of participants were inactive, 61.7% minimally active, and 15.3% HEPA active; males had higher MET scores than females.

The study concluded that higher physical activity was correlated with higher self-esteem in this specific science high school population. The authors noted that the sample was highly specific and that height, weight, and school success were self-reported.

Canadian researchers analyzing blood samples from more than 2,800 people in Toronto found results consistent with other countries: celiac disease affects about one per cent of the population, and about 90 per cent of possible cases are undiagnosed. Celiac disease is an autoimmune condition triggered by gluten that can damage the small intestine and cause symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea, anemia and weight loss. Researchers and clinicians said diagnosis can be difficult because symptoms overlap with other conditions and testing should occur while patients are still consuming gluten to avoid false negatives. A biopsy remains the gold standard for confirmation. Experts said the findings are important for health care planning and awareness, though further studies in other provinces are needed to determine whether the results represent Canada as a whole.

U.S. stocks were mixed after the Federal Reserve raised the fed-funds rate by a quarter point to 1%-1.25% and said it expects to begin gradually reducing its $4.5 trillion balance sheet this year. The S&P 500 fell 0.4%, the Dow was nearly flat after hitting an intraday record, and the Nasdaq dropped 0.9%. Energy and materials shares led declines as oil fell 3.7% to $44.73 after data showed smaller-than-expected crude supply declines and rising gasoline supplies and production. May consumer prices fell 0.1%, and weak retail sales contributed to lower Treasury yields and a weaker dollar, while gold rose. Fed Chair Janet Yellen said inflation is still expected to reach 2% next year. Individual movers included gains for Tesla, H&R Block and Alexion, while oil-related stocks and UPS declined. European stocks slipped and Asian markets closed mixed.

The passage describes systems, devices, and methods for using automated insulin delivery records and closed-loop glucose control outcomes to adjust open-loop basal insulin parameters for diabetes management. A processor determines total insulin delivered over a time period, separates basal and bolus amounts, calculates the basal proportion, compares it with a threshold, and, if exceeded, generates instructions for a wearable drug delivery pump to deliver a modified basal dosage during a later period. Examples include limiting basal recommendations based on basal-bolus distribution thresholds, omitting insulin delivered near bolus events, segmenting time periods, applying clustering algorithms to create time-dependent basal profiles, and adjusting recommendations based on hypoglycemia data. The described system may include a wearable drug delivery device, glucose sensor, personal diabetes management device, smart device, artificial pancreas application or automated insulin delivery algorithm, wireless communication, memory, processors, and optional cloud services.

Schneider Electric introduced an Edge Module for mobile edge applications, aimed at helping telco customers deploy flexible, scalable and autonomous edge computing at distributed sites such as cell towers. The prefabricated module integrates power, cooling, software and IT components, supports single- or three-phase power, configurable racks, N+1 cooling and up to 48 KW power capacity. Using Schneider Electric’s EcoStruxure platform, it can be metered, remotely monitored and controlled, with optional security features including locks, cameras, exterior lights and card-key access.

Plaintiffs, alien enemies during World War I, sought in 1931 to recover property seized by the Alien Property Custodian under the Trading with the Enemy Act. The District Court dismissed the bill, finding recovery barred by Public Resolution No. 53, which postponed deliveries of property while Germany remained in arrears on specified obligations. The Court of Appeals held the case was governed by Cummings v. Deutsche Bank, where the Supreme Court ruled that Congress could suspend alien enemies’ rights to recover seized property. The court rejected plaintiffs’ attempt to distinguish their claim as involving illegal seizure, finding no meaningful difference from an alleged unlawful withholding. The dismissal was affirmed.

Boot pins are multiplexed between ARM Cortex-A8 boot mode and GPMC functions, sampled at reset for XIP, EMAC PHY, reserved, or ARM boot mode configuration, and after reset function as GPMC multiplexed data/address pins. OpenAI unveiled a preview Apps SDK that lets developers embed third-party apps directly inside ChatGPT, with early examples from Spotify, Canva, and Zillow responding to chat commands. CEO Sam Altman said the apps are meant to be adaptive, interactive, and personalized, and that OpenAI plans future monetization options, including an “agentic commerce protocol” with instant checkout inside ChatGPT. The company did not share revenue-share details with highlighted partners.

The announcement reflects OpenAI’s push to keep users within ChatGPT and turn it into a broader platform or chat-driven operating system. OpenAI also introduced tools for building AI agents, including AgentKit, and made Codex generally available with new Slack, SDK, and analytics tools. The company is competing with Google, Anthropic, Amazon, Meta, and DeepSeek for developers while also expanding open source models, APIs, coding tools, and data center capacity.

U.S. stocks fell sharply Friday as concerns over rising wages, inflation and bond yields drove investors out of equities. The Dow dropped 665.75 points, its biggest daily point decline since December 2008, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq also posted steep losses. All three major indexes recorded their worst weekly declines in two years after reaching record highs the prior week. A stronger-than-expected January jobs report and the largest wage gain in more than 8-1/2 years raised expectations of more aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield to its highest level since January 2014. All 11 S&P 500 sectors declined, led by technology. Volatility rose to its highest level since November 2016, while Exxon Mobil, Chevron, Alphabet and Apple fell on earnings or outlook concerns. Amazon gained after strong earnings.

Tail risk, or “fat tails,” refers to rare but severe market events occurring more often than a normal distribution suggests, especially left-tail losses. The passage discusses reasons to hedge tail risk, including limiting losses, surviving market crises, and avoiding behavioral mistakes during drawdowns. Suggested hedging approaches include put options, foreign assets, cash, Cambria’s TAIL ETF, Ray Dalio’s All Weather Portfolio, and trend-following strategies. These methods can reduce drawdowns or perform well during crises, but often lower long-term returns because protection is costly. Cambria’s TAIL ETF has helped during selloffs but has had negative returns since inception. The passage concludes that tail risk strategies involve trade-offs and can be difficult to follow psychologically.

Jordan L. Couch explains that AI, especially generative and agentic AI, is increasingly transforming legal practice. Generative AI creates content such as documents, arguments and marketing materials, while agentic AI analyzes data to support decisions and recommendations. He says lawyers should use AI when it is the best tool, including for document review, legal research, client communication, brainstorming and rough drafting, while leaving nuanced judgment to humans. He highlights tools such as Vincent AI, Copilot, ChatGPT, built-in legal software AI features and custom firm tools. A later column will address effective AI integration and future expectations.

The thesis analyzes web services in event management and proposes a mobile application to improve event attendance through features such as service booking, sensor use, and drone-camera viewing. It explains e-business, digital business, e-commerce, security concerns, cloud computing, Web 2.0, the Internet of Things, and mobile technologies as relevant to digital transformation.

The research analyzed 200 event management websites from Croatia and selected foreign countries between August and September 2017. Websites were evaluated using 103 criteria across website content, social networks and Web 2.0, public relations and support, multimedia and mobile technologies, and user experience and technical specifications.

Results show that foreign event management websites generally perform better than Croatian ones, especially in user experience, social media presence, privacy and terms information, newsletters, blogs, and technical performance. All analyzed foreign websites used photos, logos, HTML, Java, blogs, and email support. Many used Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, newsletters, animations, and fast-loading pages, while fewer used HTTPS, video content, mobile applications, or corporate social responsibility information.

The conclusion states that online presence, social media, mobile adaptation, multimedia content, and improved website performance are increasingly important for event management organizations. Croatian organizations have significant room for improvement, particularly in user experience, social media use, and mobile applications. Future research should examine customer perspectives and links between marketing activities and event management strategies.

Real Madrid drew Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League last 16 as they pursue a third straight European title. Other ties include Barcelona vs Chelsea, Manchester City vs Basel, Bayern Munich vs Besiktas, Juventus vs Tottenham, Manchester United vs Sevilla, Liverpool vs Porto, and Shakhtar Donetsk vs Roma. The 10-week courses let young musicians, and some adults, learn songs as a band before performing for friends and family. Founder and guitar tutor Ricky Comiskey said the school builds confidence, with many pupils forming bands. Mark’s son Tom was among the students who later formed Fading Sunlight, which has played across Yorkshire. Ricky praised Mark’s photos for chronicling pupils’ development.

The deal begins next season and follows prolonged negotiations. Kaprizov had 25 goals and 31 assists in 41 regular-season games in 2024-25 despite injury, plus nine playoff points. He holds several Wild franchise records and won the Calder Trophy in 2020-21.

This qualitative study examined anticipated challenges and training needs of pre-service physical education and health teachers in Quebec regarding student motivation. Four focus groups were conducted with 18 participants from francophone universities. Participants identified classroom management and students’ lack of motivation as their main anticipated challenges. Specific motivational challenges included student heterogeneity, designing motivating learning activities, student engagement, managing disengaged students, and gender differences. Participants said teacher education programs should better prepare them by integrating motivation into planning and evaluation courses, providing concrete strategies for implementation, and offering more practical teaching opportunities. The study concludes that pre-service teachers do not feel current Quebec programs fully meet their needs in preparing them to support student motivation.

A Tom Thomson painting once given as a gag gift sold for $481,250 at Heffel Fine Art Auction House in Toronto after being authenticated. The auction raised $14.1 million from 118 works, led by Paul-Emile Borduas’s “Figures schematiques,” which sold for $3.6 million. Other strong sales included works by Lawren Harris, A.J. Casson, Jack Bush, and Jean Paul Lemieux.

The lecture develops the AdS/CFT operator-field mapping, focusing on how a boundary operator’s scaling dimension relates to the mass of the dual bulk field. In semiclassical gravity, bulk fields are canonically normalized so nonlinear interactions are suppressed by powers of the gravitational coupling, allowing leading-order analysis with quadratic free-field actions.

For a massive scalar field in AdS, solving the near-boundary equation gives two asymptotic behaviors: \(A(x) z^{d-\Delta}\) and \(B(x) z^\Delta\), with \(\Delta = d/2 + \sqrt{d^2/4 + m^2R^2}\). Real exponents require the Breitenlohner-Freedman bound; violating it leads to instability. Normalizable modes define states in the Hilbert space, while non-normalizable modes define boundary conditions and correspond to deformations of the boundary theory.

In standard quantization, \(A(x)\) is the non-normalizable mode and acts as the source for the boundary operator \(O\), while \(B(x)\) corresponds to the expectation value of \(O\). In alternative quantization, possible for a certain mass range, the roles of \(A\) and \(B\) are exchanged. A scaling argument shows that \(\Delta\) is the scaling dimension of the operator dual to the scalar field, producing the mass-dimension relation \(m^2R^2=\Delta(\Delta-d)\).

The lecture also notes that massless scalar fields correspond to marginal operators, negative mass squared above the BF bound to relevant operators, and positive mass squared to irrelevant operators. Similar near-boundary analyses show that bulk gauge fields correspond to conserved currents of dimension \(d-1\), and metric perturbations correspond to the stress tensor of dimension \(d\).

Finally, correlation functions in the boundary theory are related to the bulk gravity partition function with specified boundary values. In the semiclassical limit, this partition function is evaluated by the on-shell Euclidean action of the classical gravity solution satisfying those boundary conditions.

Southwest Airlines apologized after UC Berkeley women’s basketball coach Lindsay Gottlieb said an employee asked her to prove her biracial 1-year-old son was hers while flying from Denver to Oakland. Gottlieb said she offered his passport but was asked for a birth certificate and then a Facebook post, and she suspected the questioning was related to her son’s skin color rather than his different last name. Southwest said its policy is to verify lap children are under 2 using a birth certificate or government-issued ID, but domestic travel does not require matching last names. The airline said it would review the matter with the employee. Some criticized the incident, while others defended such checks as child-trafficking precautions.

UAE Energy Minister Suhail al-Mazroui said OPEC and non-OPEC producers plan to announce an exit strategy from global supply cuts at their June meeting, but this does not mean the pact will end then. He said details are premature and depend on collective agreement. Kuwait’s oil minister said producers would study an exit strategy before June. Revenue rose 20% year over year, billings topped estimates, and paying customers reached 85,000. The company issued better-than-expected second-quarter guidance, but shares fell 4.6% after hours.

In John Q. A. Simmonds v. Nicholas T. P. Simmonds, appellee sued to recover 117½ acres in Bell County and obtained judgment for the land and rents. Appellee claimed title through a duplicate headright certificate issued to Willard Chamberlain, a patent, a transfer from Chamberlain by agent Louis C. Clemons to Joseph P. Sneed, and a deed from Sneed to appellee. Appellant relied on appellee’s alleged failure to prove title and on limitations.

The court held the transfer was admissible as an ancient instrument because it came from proper custody, was over thirty years old, was found genuine, and had been relied on for title. It sufficiently identified the certificate, and Clemons’s authority as agent was conclusively presumed. The court also upheld exclusion of a Land Office affidavit by W. R. Baker claiming ownership and an augmentation certificate offered to challenge identification. Evidence of appellant’s reputation for truth was properly excluded because conflicting testimony alone did not impeach him. Finding no error and sufficient evidence, the judgment was affirmed.

The paper addresses exact Nash equilibrium computation in multiplayer imperfect-information games, where existing iterative methods lack convergence guarantees and many Gambit methods are inapplicable or require exponential conversion to strategic form. The authors formulate the problem as a nonlinear complementarity problem using a multiplayer extension of the sequence-form representation, then model it as a quadratically constrained feasibility program solvable with nonconvex quadratic optimization.

The approach is tested mainly on reduced three-player Kuhn poker after removing dominated actions. Using Gurobi, it computes an essentially exact Nash equilibrium in 2.47 seconds, with no player able to gain more than \(1.4 \times 10^{-17}\) by deviating. It cannot solve the full game within 24 hours, showing limited scalability. Among applicable Gambit methods, only logit quantal response equilibrium tracing solves the reduced game, taking over 40 seconds and producing an approximate equilibrium with deviation gain up to \(1.667 \times 10^{-5}\). Logit tracing also solves the full game in several minutes.

Experiments on random strategic-form games show the nonlinear complementarity approach is faster than a prior mixed-integer bilinear formulation, though newer bilinear methods remain stronger for that setting. The authors conclude their method is promising for exact equilibrium computation in small multiplayer imperfect-information games, while logit QRE tracing appears more suitable for moderate-sized games requiring global convergence.

The passage contains certified documents concerning the American bark Cape Horn Pigeon. Thomas Scullun agreed with J. and W. R. Wing to serve as master for a whaling voyage from San Francisco in 1891, with compensation of a one-twelfth lay in net proceeds. The vessel cleared San Francisco on December 7, 1891, for a whaling voyage, with Thomas Scullun as master, 201 tons burden, and 44 men. Its outward foreign manifest and Scullun’s sworn statement certified the cargo was fully and accurately reported and intended for whaling. A later diplomatic reply states that in August/September 1892 Lieutenant von Cube detained the Cape Horn Pigeon in the Sea of Okhotsk after suspecting it had entered prohibited Russian waters near Aniva and Patience bays. A commission found the vessel had navigated within Russian territorial waters but ordered no confiscation, treating the arrest as a misunderstanding and returning the vessel to its owners.

Carol Moore and others blamed Burlington College’s closure on a 2010 land purchase championed by Jane Sanders. Federal authorities are examining related donation claims. Moore also criticized a college agreement with Driscoll’s Vermont Woodworking School.

Qualcomm accidentally published and removed a blog post about the Asus Zenfone AR, expected to be unveiled at CES. NVIDIA A100, based on the Ampere architecture and built on TSMC 7nm, is designed for AI, HPC, data analytics, and data center workloads. It includes 108 SMs, 6912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, 40 GB HBM2 memory, 40 MB L2 cache, and support for Compute Capability 8.0. Compared with Tesla V100, A100 increases Tensor Core performance, memory bandwidth, L2 capacity, and cache bandwidth.

A100 third-generation Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary formats. TF32 enables acceleration of FP32-based AI workloads with no user code changes, while FP16 and BF16 mixed precision provide higher training throughput. FP64 Tensor Core operations accelerate HPC workloads, and mixed-precision iterative refinement with cuSOLVER can improve solver performance.

A100 introduces fine-grained structured sparsity using a 2:4 pattern, allowing Tensor Cores to skip zero values and double compute throughput for supported sparse neural network operations. NVIDIA describes a workflow of dense training, structured pruning, and fine-tuning that results in virtually no inference accuracy loss across tested networks.

The architecture adds a larger combined L1/shared memory subsystem, asynchronous copy from global to shared memory, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, compute data compression, improved atomics, hardware JPEG decode, optical flow acceleration, and enhanced video decode. CUDA 11 supports these features through APIs for Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, asynchronous copy, barriers, MIG, and cache controls.

CUDA Task Graphs improve repeated GPU workflow submission by defining operations and dependencies once and launching them repeatedly. A100 adds hardware acceleration for graph launch and dependency handling, reducing CPU launch overhead and grid-to-grid latency, especially for short kernels and complex workflows.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) allows one A100 to be partitioned into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory bandwidth, and fault isolation. MIG supports multi-tenant, single-user, and multi-user scenarios, enabling better utilization and quality of service while preserving the CUDA programming model.

A100 includes third-generation NVLink with twelve links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, and improved error detection, isolation, containment, and recovery. DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with NVLink, NVSwitch, Mellanox networking, and NVIDIA software to deliver up to 5 PFLOPS and support scalable AI infrastructure.

IMF mission chief Ron van Rooden said Ukraine’s pension system is unsustainable, supports about 30 percent of the population, and operates at a loss. The IMF has urged Ukraine to reform the system as part of broader economic changes tied to Western lending. Ukraine has resisted raising the pension age due to public and parliamentary opposition. Van Rooden suggested reducing early retirements and increasing pension tax collection from companies. Ukraine hopes to secure another $4.5 billion from the IMF.

The passage explains the 20-day exponential moving average trading strategy, which uses the 20 EMA to identify short-term price swings and generate buy signals when price rises above the EMA and sell signals when it falls below. A backtest on SPY showed low CAGR, high market exposure, and significant drawdown, making the standalone strategy weak. Adding another technical indicator as a filter improved the equity curve and performance, nearly matching buy-and-hold CAGR on a risk-adjusted basis, though drawdown stayed the same. The strategy performed better on Bitcoin from 2014 onward, attributed to Bitcoin’s momentum.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2019. Net sales increased to $59.7 billion from $51.0 billion in Q1 2018, operating income rose to $4.4 billion from $1.9 billion, and net income increased to $3.6 billion from $1.6 billion. North America net sales were $35.8 billion with operating income of $2.3 billion; International net sales were $16.2 billion with an operating loss of $90 million; and AWS net sales were $7.7 billion with operating income of $2.2 billion. Net sales by category included $29.5 billion from online stores, $4.3 billion from physical stores, $11.1 billion from third-party seller services, $4.3 billion from subscription services, $7.7 billion from AWS, and $2.7 billion from other services.
