Total assets were $178.1 billion, total stockholders’ equity was $48.4 billion, and long-term debt was $23.3 billion as of March 31, 2019.

Amazon adopted new lease accounting guidance on January 1, 2019, recognizing approximately $21 billion of operating lease assets and liabilities. The company reported total lease cost of $3.5 billion for Q1 2019 and total contractual commitments of $131.3 billion as of March 31, 2019.

The filing discusses ongoing tax matters, including IRS transfer pricing proceedings and a European Commission state aid decision involving Luxembourg, as well as legal proceedings involving patent infringement claims. Amazon states that it disputes the allegations and intends to defend itself vigorously in the described matters.

Iron sulfate heptahydrate, also known as ferrous sulfate heptahydrate, copperas, or green vitriol, is a water- and acid-soluble sulfate compound produced during titanium dioxide manufacture from ilmenite or by crystallizing hot sulfate solution. It contains 18–20 wt% iron and up to 3 wt% free acid, with moisture and acidic liquid that may cause dustiness and container corrosion. It is used medically to treat iron deficiency and is listed by WHO as an essential medicine. Industrial and agricultural uses include textile dye fixing, leather blackening, ink production, treating iron chlorosis, water purification, phosphate removal from sewage, preventing eutrophication, reducing Cr6+ in cement, and supplying iron in agriculture.

The lecture explains the asymptotic equipartition property for discrete memoryless sources, defining typical sequences through sample averages of log probability mass functions. As block length grows, typical sequences have probability approaching 1, each has probability about \(2^{-nH(X)}\), and their number is about \(2^{nH(X)}\), making entropy central to source coding. Fixed-length coding can approach \(H(X)\) bits per symbol with rare failures, but rates below entropy lead to asymptotic failure.

The lecture then introduces Markov sources as models with memory, using finite-state Markov chains whose transitions produce source outputs. It focuses on ergodic Markov chains, where states are mutually accessible, aperiodic, and have unique steady-state probabilities approached from any initial state. For Markov source coding, single-symbol prefix-free codes may be ineffective, especially for binary alphabets, so block coding is used. The relevant limit is the conditional entropy \(H(X|S)\), which accounts for memory and determines achievable compression.

Finally, the lecture describes the Lempel-Ziv universal compression algorithm, especially LZ77. It requires no prior probability model, finds repeated strings in a sliding window, and encodes matches by length and location. Unary-binary coding is used for match lengths, and fixed-length coding for window positions. Asymptotically, for Markov sources, Lempel-Ziv achieves the same bits per symbol as the best model-based code, \(H(X|S)\). Practical considerations include window size, search speed, adaptation to changing statistics, and initialization.

The speaker thanks West Point leaders, guests, and cadets, then reflects on leadership, military service, and U.S. responsibilities after the Cold War. He says the end of the Cold War offers great promise, including more democratic governments and reduced nuclear danger through agreements such as START II, but warns that violence, dictatorships, weapons of mass destruction, terrorism, and human rights abuses remain threats.

He argues that the United States must remain engaged in world affairs and lead efforts toward a “new world order” based on democracy, tolerance, economic freedom, and peaceful dispute resolution. He says U.S. leadership should not mean acting as the world’s policeman, nor should it require unilateral action in every crisis, but the United States has a unique responsibility as the remaining superpower.

The speaker discusses the selective use of military force, citing Kuwait, Iraq, Somalia, Panama, and the Philippines, while explaining why force had not yet been used in the former Yugoslavia. He says military intervention requires judgment, clear and achievable missions, realistic plans, withdrawal criteria, and consideration of costs, risks, effectiveness, and international support.

He emphasizes the need for strong, modern, flexible armed forces and praises the All Volunteer Force, highlighting its professionalism, training, merit-based culture, discipline, diversity, and compassion. He tells cadets that military service is an honorable calling rooted in duty, sacrifice, and public service. Reflecting on his own enlistment in the Navy during World War II, he salutes the cadets’ choice and wishes them success as they enter a new world of challenge and opportunity.

The passage argues that treaty language referring to “the great ocean commonly called the Pacific Ocean” includes both the Bering and Okhotsk Seas as branches of that ocean. It cites the Paris arbitration decision that Russia limited its Bering Sea jurisdiction to cannon-shot range and did not exercise exclusive seal-fishery rights beyond territorial waters. The passage contends that exclusive jurisdiction over large gulfs such as the Okhotsk Sea conflicts with accepted international law, citing authorities who affirm freedom of connected seas and reject national control over large open waters.

Coach Quenneville discussed lineup adjustments, saying matchups, merit, and game situations influence changes, especially in playoffs when decisions must be made quickly. He praised “Johnny” for his all-zone play, speed, puck possession, special-teams work, defensive responsibility, and value beyond scoring. He called “Dunks” highly conditioned and capable of handling major ice time. He said “Bolly” has grown into more responsibility, offering defensive predictability and offensive skill.

Quenneville said the team values balanced production and consistency, and he emphasized that all four lines can be trusted in different matchups. He praised Chicago as a special sports city and said he feels fortunate to be part of the Blackhawks organization. Reflecting on the season, he noted the team’s strong start, high playoff expectations, adversity against Detroit, and continued improvement. He said the extra day off helped after a taxing game.

He commended the players for a consistent season, improved defense, and goaltending that won the Jennings. He praised Shaw’s competitiveness, Corey’s consistency and demeanor, and the goaltending tandem with Ray Emery. He also addressed too-many-men penalties, saying the team was fortunate to avoid damage in key overtime moments.

Damian Lillard scored 32 points and became the fastest Trail Blazers player to reach 10,000 career points, but Portland’s four-game winning streak ended with a 130-105 loss to Toronto. DeMar DeRozan led the Raptors with 35 points, matching his career high with six 3-pointers, while Jonas Valanciunas added 18. Toronto made a season-high 19 3-pointers and improved to an NBA-best 20-4 at home. CJ McCollum scored 21 and Jusuf Nurkic 20 for Portland, which has lost five of seven road games. The Raptors led 74-52 at halftime and beat Portland for the sixth straight time.

Harvey Weinstein has been indicted by a Manhattan grand jury on charges of rape and criminal sexual act involving two women. Manhattan District Attorney Cyrus Vance Jr. said the indictment brings Weinstein closer to accountability. Weinstein declined to testify before the grand jury, citing insufficient preparation time and late disclosure of the accusers’ identities.

PAM4 signaling in GDDR6X sends two bits per clock edge using four voltage levels, improving on GDDR6 NRZ signaling. NVIDIA and Micron developed MTA encoding, new training, adaptation, equalization, and careful package/PCB design to address PAM4 SNR challenges. On GA10x GPUs, GDDR6X supports up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/s peak bandwidth, over 52% higher than TU102.

NVIDIA RTX IO, used with Microsoft DirectStorage, enables GPU-based loading and lossless decompression of game and creative assets, reducing CPU workload and improving I/O performance compared with hard drives and traditional storage APIs. It supports faster loading, asset streaming, reduced stutter, and professional workflows involving large datasets.

The GA10x Ampere architecture provides up to 2x improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. It includes second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores with sparsity, GDDR6X support, and RTX IO. Ampere GPUs support DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 8K60 and 4K120 displays, HDCP 2.3, fifth-generation NVDEC decoding, AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-generation NVENC encoding.

The NVIDIA A40 is a GA10x-based data center GPU for visual computing, offering up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 5x AI/data science throughput versus Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink. It supports vGPU, Quadro Sync, PCIe Gen4, and NVIDIA EGX. The RTX A6000 workstation GPU includes 48GB GDDR6, NVLink support, and professional rendering, AI, HPC, and visualization capabilities.

GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 24GB GDDR6X, while RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6. GDDR6X Error Detection and Replay detects memory transmission errors and replays failed transactions, helping overclockers identify memory limits when performance plateaus.

An October 2001 Enron email forwards a Texas Monthly article, “How Enron Blew It,” about Enron’s rise and troubles. The article describes Enron’s transformation from a pipeline company into a major energy trading firm under Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling, driven by deregulation, the Gas Bank model, aggressive recruiting, rapid expansion, and a high-pressure culture focused on profits, risk-taking, and performance rankings.

It says Enron’s stock fell sharply in 2001 amid criticism over California’s energy crisis, costly international projects, failed telecommunications and broadband ventures, questions about accounting practices, and negative press. The article also details Skilling’s abrupt resignation after six months as CEO, Lay’s return to the role, and internal concerns that Enron’s culture had become harsh, disloyal, and better suited to good times than bad.

The passage presents a quantum learning study on whether \(k\)-replica joint measurements are necessary to efficiently estimate nonlinear functions such as \(\mathrm{tr}(\rho^{k+1}O)\). The authors prove that for broad classes of observables, any \(k\)-replica protocol requires exponentially many samples, while \((k+1)\)-replica measurements achieve constant or efficient sample complexity. This establishes a fine-grained hierarchy of quantum replica advantage for integer \(k\).

A central technical contribution is an indistinguishability principle for Haar-assembled ensembles, which are ensembles built from Haar-random states using tensor products, mixtures, and fixed unitaries. The principle shows that such ensembles are hard to distinguish from their averages using 1-replica protocols, and it is used to prove lower bounds for nonlinear property estimation, spectrum testing, and rank testing.

The authors also prove upper bounds showing that \(\lceil (k+1)/2\rceil\)-replica protocols can match the \(\sqrt d\) dependence of the lower bound for estimating \(\mathrm{tr}(\rho^{k+1}O)\). Additional applications include lower bounds for distinguishing spectra that agree on moments up to degree \(k\), rank testing under bounded-replica protocols, and estimating non-integer trace powers related to Tsallis entropy.

The passage outlines the proof strategy: construct hard ensembles with matching low-degree moments but differing \((k+1)\)-degree moments, use Haar-assembled indistinguishability to show bounded-replica protocols cannot distinguish them, and reduce successful nonlinear estimation to distinguishing these ensembles. It also lists future directions, including improving error dependence, closing the error-regime gap, extending spectrum testing results, and considering protocols with state resetting or limited working qubits.

Vertex Resource Group Ltd. acquired a private hydro-vac services business in Edmonton, Alberta, for $4.3 million, adding 11 hydro-vac units and doubling its hydro-vac fleet. The acquisition expands Vertex’s hydro-vac services into the Edmonton market, supports industry diversification, and is expected to add about $5 million in annual revenue based on historical financial information. The transaction closed June 30, 2018, and the acquired company began operating as Vertex. Vertex, headquartered in Sherwood Park, Alberta, provides environmental services across western Canada and select U.S. locations.

Flash memory endurance varies by address space, with the lower 32kB supporting higher erase/program cycles. The passage defines erase operations, write limits per word line, program time, and sector program time.

The speaker addresses the Foreign Service Institute, emphasizing that the central task of diplomacy is peace. He argues that postwar Europe’s recovery and stability resulted from common action, interdependent institutions, and collective security, especially through NATO. While NATO should adapt to changing circumstances, reform should occur through consultation among members, not isolation. The speaker presents NATO as an alliance to keep peace, stating that its integrated military strength and political unity have deterred war and reinforced stability. He warns that division and independent action could weaken security, while unity remains essential. The United States is committed to preserving and strengthening NATO’s deterrent power and hopes withdrawn allies will return to common obligations. He concludes that Atlantic unity, shared values, and human solidarity offer hope for Europe and the wider world.

The passage reviews the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card, highlighting its 0% intro APR for 21 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a variable APR of 16.99%, 23.49%, or 28.74%. It has no annual fee, offers up to $600 in cellphone protection with a $25 deductible, and provides access to My Wells Fargo Deals. Drawbacks include no ongoing rewards after the intro period, a 5% balance transfer fee with a $5 minimum, and a 3% foreign transaction fee. The card is presented as a strong option for paying down debt or financing large purchases, but less suitable for those seeking long-term rewards or travel benefits.

A penalty-kick tiebreaker, or shoot-out, is used when a tied soccer match requires a winner, often in single-elimination tournaments. Governed by IFAB Law 10, with kicks conducted under Law 14, the shoot-out begins with eligible players from each team taking five alternating kicks from the penalty mark. If one team has an insurmountable lead or scores more after five kicks, it wins; if tied, sudden death continues until one team scores and the other misses.

Only players on the field at the end of play are eligible, and all eligible players must kick before anyone takes a second kick. If one team has fewer players, the other must reduce its eligible players to match. The referee manages coin tosses for the goal and kicking order, enforces procedures, and records results. Goalkeepers may be changed by eligible players, and injured goalkeepers may be replaced if substitutes remain.

Coaches should prepare teams in advance by reviewing applicable rules and tournament modifications, identifying and ranking penalty takers, practicing full shoot-out scenarios, analyzing opponents, and supporting goalkeepers. During matches, coaches should avoid a late letdown, ensure preferred kickers are on the field, confirm kicking order, and keep players calm. Afterward, teams should maintain morale and review performance. Shoot-out goals are recorded in the match result but do not count toward individual statistics.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2019 identifies the company as a Washington-incorporated technology company headquartered in Redmond, Washington. Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and organization to achieve more. As of July 29, 2019, it had 7,635,409,400 common shares outstanding, and as of December 31, 2018, the market value of common stock held by non-affiliates was $769.6 billion.

Microsoft develops and supports software, services, devices, and solutions, including cloud services, operating systems, productivity applications, business applications, developer tools, video games, devices, consulting, support, and online advertising. Its research and development focus is organized around three ambitions: reinvent productivity and business processes, build the intelligent cloud and intelligent edge platform, and create more personal computing.

The company reports three operating segments: Productivity and Business Processes, including Office, LinkedIn, and Dynamics; Intelligent Cloud, including server products, Azure, GitHub, and enterprise services; and More Personal Computing, including Windows, Surface and other devices, gaming, and search. Microsoft completed its acquisition of GitHub on October 25, 2018, and LinkedIn acquired Glint on November 16, 2018.

Microsoft markets and distributes products and services through OEMs, direct sales, distributors, resellers, digital marketplaces, online stores, and retail stores. It operates regional operations centers, datacenters across multiple regions, and research and development facilities in the U.S. and internationally. As of June 30, 2019, Microsoft employed approximately 144,000 full-time employees, including 85,000 in the U.S. and 59,000 internationally.

The filing describes risks including intense competition, execution risks in cloud services, uncertain returns on investments, acquisition integration risks, goodwill or intangible asset impairment, cybersecurity threats, misuse or disclosure of personal data, platform abuse, IoT and AI risks, infrastructure outages, product quality or supply problems, intellectual property challenges, litigation, regulatory scrutiny, and anti-corruption and competition law compliance risks.

Sony confirmed the Xperia XZ Premium will receive Android Oreo later in 2017, adding features from the Xperia XZ1 and XZ1 Compact. Updates include the 3D Creator app, improved predictive capture that detects smiles, and enhanced burst mode with autofocus tracking at 10 photos per second.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K reporting that on June 24, 2020, it entered into a 90-day Indemnification Agreement with CEO Elon Musk. During this period, Tesla will evaluate options for directors’ and officers’ indemnity coverage and seek a binding market quote for a $100 million liability insurance policy. Musk will provide up to $100 million of indemnity coverage from personal funds where coverage is not indemnifiable by Tesla. Tesla will pay Musk a one-time fee of $972,361 and may pay an additional amount if a prorated, discounted market premium is higher.

The court affirmed dismissal of Patrick Sutherland’s CPLR article 78 petition challenging the Board of Parole’s denial of release. It held that Sutherland was precluded from contesting information in his presentence report because he had not timely challenged it, and found that the Board considered the required statutory factors and acted rationally.

AGNC Investment is presented as a bullish mortgage REIT benefiting from recent and expected Fed rate cuts, which may lower financing costs and improve mortgage-backed securities valuations. The passage cites AGNC’s improving spreads, third consecutive quarter of positive NII in Q2’25, premium to book value, and attractive monthly dividend. The author discloses long positions in AGNC and NLY and notes the article reflects personal opinions, not investment advice.

Andrea Conti’s agent Mario Giuffredi said the Atalanta wing-back only wants to join Milan and believes Gian Piero Gasperini should not block the move. Giuffredi said Conti is grateful to Atalanta but wants a collaborative solution allowing him to pursue his dream.

The speaker calls for a “new American experience” in the 1970s focused on peace, government reform, economic stability, law enforcement, environmental protection, and improved quality of life. He identifies ending the Vietnam War and pursuing peace as the top priority, while advocating reduced U.S. involvement abroad, greater responsibility by allies, and negotiation with the Soviet Union and Communist China.

Domestically, he urges welfare reform, a “New Federalism” returning power to states and people, expanded equal opportunity, balanced budgets to fight inflation, and stronger action against crime. He criticizes pending congressional inaction on crime legislation and supports increased federal spending for local law enforcement.

The speaker emphasizes environmental restoration as a major concern of the 1970s, proposing a comprehensive pollution-control program, including a $10 billion clean waters initiative, preservation of open spaces, stricter automobile pollution controls, and personal responsibility for cleaner surroundings. He also calls for a national growth policy to address urban decay, rural decline, and population shifts.

He concludes by envisioning, by the 1976 bicentennial, an America with reduced hunger, minimum income support, improved housing, transportation, health and education, controlled inflation, progress against crime and pollution, and peace with all nations, while stressing moral and spiritual leadership as essential to national purpose.

A remote-controlled swimming robot, nicknamed “mini manbo,” will inspect Fukushima Dai-Ichi’s Unit 3 primary containment vessel in July to assess damage and locate melted fuel submerged in radioactive water. Developed by Toshiba and Japan’s nuclear decommissioning institute, it uses lights, cameras, propellers and a radiation detector. Earlier robots became stuck or failed due to radiation and damage. Japan needs precise fuel-location and structural data to plan safe removal after the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.

Nassim Nicholas Taleb is a statistician, trader, investor, and author known for work on randomness, uncertainty, probability, tail risk, antifragility, and “skin in the game.” The passage discusses his books, background, options-based trading, and barbell strategy, which combines low-risk assets with high-risk, high-reward positions to benefit from extreme events. It also summarizes his views on Black Swans, randomness, cognitive biases, fragile systems, and incentives tied to personal risk.

Coach Vigneault said the team was disappointed after a hard-fought Stanley Cup Final loss, noting all three games at the venue went to overtime and both goaltenders played well. He said he was proud of the group’s effort and would reflect before discussing next steps. He also said the team needed to play better, maintain puck possession, attack quickly, and trust its power play despite missed chances.

Malawi Health Equity Network has urged government to deploy internal auditors to all 28 district councils, saying research in Ntcheu found their absence was affecting fund management and accountability. Executive Director George Jobe also cited poor coordination between councils, NGOs and CSOs, and said rural communities were not involved in budget preparation. Yohanne Nyanja of the Local Government Finance Committee said government plans to deploy auditors were advanced and urged councils to support them. The Mamaye-supported research cost K7 million and included training council members on budget tracking and transparency.

Donald Trump said the U.S.-Canada trade relationship would only be “tweaked,” but the passage notes Canada is far more dependent on U.S. trade than the reverse. Despite an encouraging White House meeting with Justin Trudeau, concerns remain over beef imports, agricultural supply management, softwood lumber, and U.S. deregulation and tax policy. Rona Ambrose said Trudeau was right not to confront Trump. The passage praises Trudeau’s diplomatic restraint and contrasts him with Pierre Trudeau’s more provocative style. Trump was described as gracious, calling Canada a great friend and ally. The meeting produced a joint communique supporting trade, energy, border security, alliances, the fight against ISIS, and a new council for women entrepreneurs and business leaders.

Coach DeBoer said home ice, rest, and focus are important as the team looks to improve and avoid a 0-3 series deficit. He emphasized better support across the ice, more puck possession, stronger attacking, and limiting distractions from being at home. Lineup decisions will be made on game day, with one player held out for maintenance. DeBoer said the series is not over until a team wins four games, citing past experience. He noted Pittsburgh’s speed and depth, including Crosby, Kessel, and Malkin on separate lines, create matchup problems, and said momentum will shift throughout the series.

Initial coin offerings (ICOs) are described as a way for startups or projects to raise money by selling crypto tokens, often before the underlying network or product is functional. The lecture traces the idea to JR Willett and notes Ethereum’s $18 million token sale as an early example. ICO activity grew sharply from mid-2017 to mid-2018, raising roughly $25 billion in 12 months, compared with global venture capital of about $125–$170 billion annually. Major offerings included EOS at $4.2 billion and Telegram at $1.7 billion.

ICOs typically fund network development, involve centralized early development even when open source is promised, and allow promoters to retain some tokens. Tokens are often transferable and may be sold before functionality exists, sometimes through arrangements such as Simple Agreements for Future Tokens. Many offerings include a monetary policy or supply mechanism, though not all do. Purchasers commonly expect appreciation or profit.

The lecture emphasizes evaluating ICOs by assessing whether a token use case is viable, reading the white paper, reviewing source code when available, examining the team, checking venture capital involvement, assessing community interest, understanding monetary policy, and reviewing token distribution. It also highlights questions about how ICO proceeds are accounted for, often as current or deferred revenue, and notes that regulation varies by jurisdiction, with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission treating many as securities offerings.

Statistics cited from ICO Rating show that in the third quarter of 2018, ICO funding fell sharply from the prior quarter, most offerings were on Ethereum, many raised little or no money, 76% were only ideas, and very few had working code or fully ready products. The lecture concludes that most ICOs have already failed or are likely to fail, though native tokens may still have some potential use in jumpstarting and motivating networks.

Carlos Palacios, Santa Cruz County’s assistant county administrative officer and former Watsonville city manager, will replace retiring County Administrative Officer Susan Mauriello. Palacios, 55, will be the county’s first Latino in the top administrative role and will earn a base salary of $263,057. Mauriello, 62, retires July 7 after 27 years. Palacios will oversee 2,400 staff and a roughly $720 million annual budget.

The President transmits a preliminary report by James Bronson Reynolds and Commissioner Charles P. Neill on conditions in Chicago stockyards, stating that it shows an urgent need for immediate federal legislation requiring thorough inspection of stockyards, packing houses, and meat products entering interstate or foreign commerce. He describes the conditions as revolting, unclean, and dangerous to health, and says existing law does not allow satisfactory inspection or enforcement, especially for prepared meat products shipped in interstate commerce. He notes that current law covers foreign shipments but leaves interstate commerce open to uninspected, diseased, or spoiled meats. He urges inspection and supervision “from the hoof to the can,” funded by a fee on each animal slaughtered, with inspection costs not exceeding 8 cents per head. The investigation remains unfinished, including allegations about harmful chemicals, dyes, and tainted meat. He warns that without legislation abuses could recur and recommends enactment of the Beveridge amendment to allow the Department of Agriculture to inspect meat products, supervise preparation methods, and prescribe sanitary conditions.

Armed police detained a 26-year-old man at Shackleton Court in Newton Heath after reports he threatened two people with a firearm. Police were called around 4:30pm Monday, searched the tower block, and arrested him after several hours. Witnesses reported numerous armed officers and police vans surrounding the complex.

Ashley Hollis, an A&O Shearman associate, won “Big Brother” after concealing her legal profession and posing as a social media marketing manager. She said she used attorney skills to craft her final speech, drew inspiration from Elle Woods, and plans to give much of her $750,000 prize to her parents while considering buying a home.

The passage introduces L-separability for logics L and L+, relating it to definability and Craig interpolation. It studies ML-definability and ML-separability of modal µ-calculus formulae over all models, words, binary trees, and d-ary trees. Main results include ExpTime-completeness over all models and binary trees, PSpace-completeness over words, and 2-ExpTime-completeness for separability over d-ary trees with d ≥ 3. Separator constructions have single, double, or triple exponential size depending on the model class. ML has Craig interpolation over all models, words, and binary trees, but not over d-ary trees for d ≥ 3; interpolant existence there is coNExpTime-complete. The passage also defines the relevant modal logics, Kripke structures, bisimulations, automata, and joint-consistency characterizations used to prove these results, and discusses graded-modal extensions where ML-separability becomes 2-ExpTime-complete.

The DAWN-PLASMA study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label phase 2 proof-of-concept trial evaluating standard of care plus convalescent plasma versus standard of care alone in hospitalized adult patients with COVID-19. The study was approved by independent ethics committees and conducted according to the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH-GCP guidelines. Eligible participants were adults with confirmed or clinically supported SARS-CoV-2 infection and respiratory illness; key exclusions included mechanical ventilation before or at randomization, unacceptable safety risk, severe prior plasma allergy, treatment restrictions excluding ventilation or intubation, and recent anti-CD20 therapy.

Between May 2, 2020 and January 26, 2021, 499 patients were assessed, and 489 were randomized 2:1 to convalescent plasma plus standard of care or standard of care alone. The Full Analysis Set excluded six randomized patients, leaving 320 in the plasma group and 163 in the control group. Patients in the plasma group were intended to receive 800–1000 mL of plasma in four units; 294 patients received all four units. The median time from randomization to first transfusion was 5 hours, and the median administered volume was 884 mL. Most administered plasma units had neutralizing antibody titers of at least 1/320.

The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive and free of mechanical ventilation at Day 15. This did not differ between groups: 83.7% in the convalescent plasma group versus 84.1% in the control group. No statistically significant differences were found for secondary endpoints, including mortality, Day 30 outcomes, clinical status, oxygenation, ventilation, hospitalization, or laboratory and vital sign trends. A prespecified subgroup analysis showed a significant interaction with age for the primary endpoint.

Safety outcomes were similar between groups. Adverse events occurred in 28.13% of plasma patients and 30.06% of control patients; fatal adverse events occurred in 10.31% and 9.82%, respectively; serious adverse events occurred in 20.62% and 20.68%, respectively. Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 12 plasma-group patients, and treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 7. Transfusion-related side effects were reported in 19 of 320 plasma patients, and no TRALI cases were reported.

The study concluded that early administration of high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not change the clinical course of hospitalized COVID-19 patients compared with standard of care alone.

This bibliometric study examines research on STEAM education with gamification from 2017 to 2023 using Scopus data. The search identified 34 English-language documents, analyzed quantitatively by publication trends, citations, authors, countries, keywords, collaborations, and factorial analysis. Publications increased notably from 2020 to 2023, peaking in 2022 with eight documents, indicating growing interest in the field.

The dataset contained 34 research documents and 155 citations. The most cited article was by Wannapiroon and Pimdee on Thai undergraduate STEAM creative thinking and innovation skill development, with 30 citations. CEUR Workshop Proceedings had the highest number of publications among sources. Leading authors included Nilsook, Wannapiroon, Kummanee, Lee, and Piriyasurawong, each with three publications. Thailand led in publications and citations, followed by countries including Bulgaria, Italy, and Malaysia. Computer science accounted for 37.7% of publications, and social sciences for 20.5%.

The most frequent keywords were gamification, STEAM, STEAM education, and computational thinking. Country collaboration analysis highlighted Germany, Latvia, Norway, and France. Factorial analysis identified clusters related to educational methodologies and tools, student-centered learning environments, and educational technologies such as augmented reality, e-learning, virtual reality, engagement, and instructional design. The study concludes that bibliometric analysis helps map the development, contributors, themes, and research directions of STEAM education with gamification.

Tharisa plc presented its phased transition from 15 years of open cast mining to underground mining as open pit resources are depleted, beginning with the west mine. CEO Phoevos Pouroulis said the shift has been planned for years and offers an opportunity to redefine resources and innovate. He was joined by CFO Michael Jones, Tharisa Minerals Managing Director Vulela Makuni and Operations Executive Roy Murley. The company aims to unlock long-term value through an integrated mining complex producing platinum group metals and chrome concentrate.
Libyan National Army forces in Benghazi lost four men and had 10 wounded in December amid clashes in Khreibish, months after Khalifa Haftar declared victory in the city.

The passage presents a study on adapting a Freirean dialogic educational activity to emergency remote education during the COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil. Using Cultural Historical Activity Theory, the authors analyze an activity in a physics teacher education course on non-formal education, focused on scientific dissemination and the debate over reopening schools during the pandemic.

The activity used Discord to support text and voice interaction, group work, student autonomy, and collaborative production. Students researched arguments for and against reopening schools, discussed scientific communication, and produced an infographic for social media. The authors conclude that Discord, combined with a Freirean dialogic approach, supported student voice, agency, self-organization, and connections between personal educational challenges and broader socio-political issues.

The passage describes an electronic gaming system and methods for a stop-based bonus game, such as a wheel, reel, dice, or grid construct. A bonus game may be triggered from a primary wagering game and may include stop positions associated with higher-value first awards, such as jackpots, and lower-value second awards, such as credit prizes or other non-jackpot awards. When a selected stop position is associated with a second award, the player may receive that award, and the stop position may then be changed to a first award for future bonus play, increasing later opportunities to win a jackpot. These changed associations may persist across base game play and, in some implementations, across player sessions, but may also reset or be reduced after a first award is won. The system may include displays, player input interfaces, credit input mechanisms, processors, memory, and stored instructions for controlling wagering games, bonus wheels, secondary jackpot wheels, awards, graphical updates, and trigger events.

Abercrombie & Fitch CEO Fran Horowitz said the retailer is not trying to be “cool” but aims to become a long-lasting lifestyle brand. Since taking over in 2017, she shifted management style, improved clothing quality, and avoided chasing trends. Under her leadership, Abercrombie & Fitch and Hollister sales have grown, with combined sales expected to exceed $5 billion for the first time. To sustain growth, the company is pursuing partnerships, including Abercrombie Kids selling at Macy’s and an NFL fashion partnership focused partly on better serving female fans with more sophisticated merchandise.

The passage presents a study on using generative AI in undergraduate physics labs by having students prompt, validate, and refine simulations of electric potential and equipotential lines. Conducted in a spring 2025 introductory physics for life sciences course at a large R1 public university, the study compared three lab formats: traditional physical equipment, a pre-built AI-designed simulation, and student-developed AI-generated simulations.

Students in all groups worked toward common learning objectives involving electric potential, equipotential lines, and charge configurations. Conceptual understanding was assessed immediately after the lab, with later midterm and final exam performance also analyzed. Student attitudes toward the lab formats were measured using Likert-scale survey questions.

Results showed that students using either the pre-built simulation or AI-generated simulation performed significantly better on immediate conceptual questions than students using physical equipment, while there was no significant difference between the two simulation groups. No significant differences appeared on later midterm or final exam performance. Student attitude responses were more positive for both simulation-based approaches than for the physical lab, with the pre-built simulation rated slightly more favorably than AI generation on one comparison item.

The authors conclude that AI-guided simulation development can support conceptual learning as effectively as pre-built simulations while also offering opportunities to develop skills in AI use, validation, and modeling. They argue that AI-based tools can complement, rather than replace, traditional physical labs, with different approaches serving different learning goals.

Muskogee veteran Rodney Orton, who relies on a mobility scooter because of breathing problems, could not get a replacement after his 15-year-old scooter stopped working. The VA initially told him he needed an evaluation with the next appointment six weeks away. After Problem Solver Travis Guillory contacted the VA, staff found a suitable scooter in local inventory and delivered it to Orton’s hospital room the next morning.
Toy-obsessed dogs may offer clues to behaviors resembling human behavioral addictions.

A Stanford psychology study found that college students chose and served themselves more vegetables when dishes had indulgent, taste-focused labels rather than basic or health-focused labels, despite identical preparation. The passage notes that taste strongly influences food choices and suggests using appetizing descriptions at home to encourage vegetable intake, alongside examples such as carrot fries, kale chips, corn salad, beet chips, cauliflower fried rice, and dressed green beans.

AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 specification update lists numerous unresolved or documented issues affecting PIT, PIC, DMA, GLIU, UART, LPC, IDE/ATAC, ACPI/PMC, KEL, PCI, USB, RTC, SMBus, GPIO, and sleep/wake behavior. Reported problems include incorrect PIT latch/read-back and mode 3 behavior, debug port hangs, DMA rotating priority errors, UART and LPC access failures during legacy DMA, illegal I/O address handling, PIC missed interrupts with clock gating, UDMA CRC and PRD alignment issues, unreliable SSMI behavior, ACPI byte-access hangs, PMC register corruption on BYTE/WORD writes, KEL status inaccuracies, PCI timing deviations, USB clock-gating failures, S3 wake input failures, RTC CMOS read errors, SMB controller NEGACK behavior, GPIO high-bank write corruption after suspend, missing LOWBAT_FLAG, and Sleep_X/Sleep_Y deassertion failures.

The lecture explains electroweak unification as a way to combine weak and electromagnetic interactions despite differences in interaction strength and coupling structure. The vector-axial weak coupling can be rewritten using left- and right-handed spinor projections, allowing weak currents to appear as vector currents. Electrons and neutrinos are organized into left-handed doublets, with charged weak currents rotating one into the other. A third weak isospin component resembles a neutral current, but hypercharge must be introduced to include right-handed particles. Generalizing these currents leads to weak isospin triplet fields and a hypercharge singlet. The W⁺ and W⁻ bosons arise from combinations of W1 and W2, while the photon and Z boson arise from mixing W3 with the singlet field through the weak mixing angle. This provides a consistent framework containing W⁺, W⁻, the photon, and the Z boson.

This cross-sectional study analyzed Alzheimer disease plasma biomarkers in 1,067 Amish participants from Ohio and Indiana enrolled in CAAMP. Researchers measured Aβ40, Aβ42, Aβ42/Aβ40, total tau, p-tau181, Aβ42/t-tau, and Aβ42/p-tau181 and examined associations with cognitive status, Alzheimer disease, and cognitive preservation.

Compared with cognitively unimpaired individuals, participants with Alzheimer disease had significantly higher plasma p-tau181 and lower Aβ42/p-tau181. In multivariate analyses, p-tau181 was significantly associated with Alzheimer disease among APOE ε4 carriers, while p-tau181 and Aβ42/p-tau181 were associated with cognitive preservation in sensitivity analyses. Models using all biomarkers or Aβ42/p-tau181 showed the strongest performance for distinguishing Alzheimer disease from cognitively unimpaired status.

Clustering based on Aβ42/Aβ40 and p-tau181 identified Amish subgroups with differing biomarker risk profiles. Higher-risk clusters showed lower Aβ42/Aβ40, lower Aβ42, higher p-tau181, more APOE ε4 carriers, and more Alzheimer disease cases. The authors conclude that plasma p-tau181, Aβ42/Aβ40, and Aβ42/p-tau181 are promising non-invasive biomarkers in the Amish, but longitudinal studies are needed for validation.

The passage describes an automated cryogenic storage system for storing, tracking, retrieving, and transferring biological or chemical samples while maintaining them below cryogenic temperature thresholds, such as −134°C or −150°C. The system includes one or more insulated storage vaults, a sample handling module, robotic sample transfer mechanisms, external ports for removable cryogenic storage devices, refrigeration and humidity controls, and a controller with a database for sample location tracking and barcode-based identification.

Storage vaults contain rotating interleaved shelves, trays holding multiple sample vials, vertical shuttle assemblies for raising trays to access openings, and refrigeration coils using cryogen such as liquid nitrogen. A sample handling module can transfer individual samples or trays between vaults or between a vault and a portable cryogenic workstation, often through a non-cryogenic environment, while limiting exposure time to prevent warming above the glass transition temperature. The system also includes seals, covers, grippers with insulating sleeves, docking interfaces, and mechanisms for maintaining low humidity using dry gas flow or cryotrap-based drying.

The passage further describes methods for sample transfer, vault access, refrigeration operation, portable workstation docking, tray retrieval, maintenance access, disaster recovery for jammed trays, cryogenic camera modules, alternative rack designs, and disassembly or replacement procedures for cryogenic storage vaults.

The passage also describes immediate-release, sustained-release, delayed-release, depot, injectable, and osmotic-controlled oral delivery formulations. Depot formulations may use biodegradable polymeric matrices such as PLGA to release compounds over periods such as 14 to 180 days.

Examples provide synthetic procedures for several deuterated compounds and comparative pharmacokinetic studies. He recommends expanding public building programs, increasing waterways and flood control appropriations, continuing highway development, addressing the Post Office deficit, revising air mail rates, and expanding South American postal services.

Commercial aviation has grown rapidly with federal support, while railroads are financially and physically strong but need consolidation legislation. The merchant marine is shifting toward private enterprise, with additional mail routes and new vessel construction proposed. Congress is asked to clarify shipping contract rules.

Conservation priorities include oil and gas resources, overgrazing on public lands, reclamation policy, and possible state transfers of some lands, with a commission appointed for study. The conclusion states that decisions should be judged by whether they advance self-government, justice, liberty, opportunity, prosperity, education, knowledge, religious spirit, tolerance, home life, and peace.

This institution-based cross-sectional study assessed awareness, attitudes, and factors influencing pregnant women’s decisions about labor epidural analgesia (LEA) at Hemen Medical Center in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, from June 3 to August 30, 2024. Of 267 recruited third-trimester women, 230 were analyzed. Most participants were aged 25–34 years, educated to degree level or higher, employed, and about half were nulliparous.

Overall, 78% had heard of LEA, mainly from previous users, family and friends, and the internet; only 6.5% cited healthcare providers as their primary source, and 34% had received explanations during antenatal care. Although 47% believed LEA effectively relieves labor pain, only 14.3% were willing to consider it during delivery. Common concerns included maternal side effects, fetal safety, interference with natural labor, and cost.

Multivariable analysis showed that education level, monthly family income, perceived fetal risks, and perceived pain-relief effectiveness were significantly associated with willingness to use LEA. The study concludes that despite relatively high awareness, willingness to use LEA was low, highlighting the need for antenatal education and counseling to address misconceptions and support informed decision-making.

The passage reviews ChatGPT’s development, educational uses, benefits, risks, and response accuracy. It describes ChatGPT’s evolution from GPT-1 in 2018 to GPT-4 in 2023 and notes its rapid uptake in education. Prior studies report potential benefits such as personalized learning, feedback, assessment support, engagement, accessibility, and support for language learning, while also raising concerns about plagiarism, cheating, bias, unreliable answers, limited reasoning, and effects on higher-order thinking.

The study aimed to assess the accuracy and validity of ChatGPT responses in education through a PRISMA-based systematic review. Searches were conducted in Google Scholar, Web of Science, and EBSCO using “ChatGPT + Education.” Peer-reviewed empirical studies in English were included, while unrelated, duplicate, or inaccessible studies were excluded. Eighteen studies were analyzed using thematic analysis.

Two main themes emerged: ChatGPT’s writing quality and its performance as a learner. Reviewed studies found that ChatGPT can produce coherent, structured, concise, and often high-quality writing, including essays, academic advising responses, and case-study answers. However, responses sometimes lacked argumentation, depth, related content, judgment, or reasoning. Its outputs could be difficult to distinguish from student writing.

As a learner, ChatGPT could pass several undergraduate and professional assessments and performed well in writing-heavy tasks, business assignments, some medical exams, coding tasks, and basic finance problems. However, it struggled with complex scientific problems, advanced finance questions, chemistry, calculation-based prompts, nuanced prompts, and some medical subject areas. Studies also reported hallucinations, confident false answers, inconsistency when given the same prompt, and limited deep understanding.

The passage concludes that ChatGPT has potential educational value but its responses require validation, especially in scientific and complex problem-solving contexts. It recommends careful prompt design, redesigned assessments, authentic assessment using ChatGPT, institutional guidelines and policies, and student training in constructive use. It also notes limitations of the review, including database scope, access limits, and inclusion criteria, and calls for further research on customized ChatGPT use, student learning, and innovative evaluation frameworks.

The “Four Down” offense is a spread alignment mainly used for the last shot of a period but also effective with a talented ballhandler. Four non-ballhandlers line the baseline, with shooters in the corners, creating space for one-on-one isolation. The ballhandler can drive, shoot, pass to posts when baseline help comes, or kick out to shooters when wing defenders sag. If pressured, corner players pop out for relief passes and may take over the isolation role. Special options include a mid screen for the ballhandler, a triple baseline screen for shooters, and a misdirection double screen involving a dribble handoff and weakside screening action.

The 2-3 zone is a common defense that protects the basket, limits dribble penetration, and works well against poor outside shooting teams, but it is vulnerable to strong outside shooters. It is often used by teams lacking quickness, athleticism, or skill, though quick players can make it an aggressive trapping defense. The alignment places two guards above the free throw line, a post defender in front of the basket, and two baseline defenders near the blocks. Defenders shift based on ball location, with guards covering wings and elbows, baseline players covering corners and rebounding positions, and the post staying between the ball and basket.

The defense includes wing adjustment options, such as denying corner return passes or dropping to help against the post. Reversal passes require baseline defenders to temporarily guard the ball until a guard recovers. A 1-1-3 variation can use tandem outside defenders to pressure the point guard and influence direction away from strong shooters. Trap options include corner traps, point traps, and automatic wing traps against outstanding shooters. Against a dominant low post player, the 2-3 zone uses pressure, 3/4 denial, backside support, and double or triple teams depending on ball location.

The UC1825B-SP sense resistor monitors transformer ripple current and shuts down switching if converter peak current exceeds the set limit, with the CS pin threshold around 1 V. The New York Court of Appeals considered whether Manhattan Community Board 7 had capacity to bring a CPLR article 78 proceeding challenging the New York City Department of City Planning’s denial of its FOIL request for documents related to the proposed Trump City development. Although the underlying project and FOIL request had become moot, the Court reviewed the issue because it was likely to recur, typically evade review, and was substantial.

The Court distinguished standing from capacity, explaining that standing concerns a party’s stake in a justiciable dispute, while capacity concerns the legal power to sue. Government entities created by statute have no inherent or common-law right to sue; their capacity must come from express statutory authority or necessary implication from their powers and responsibilities, absent contrary legislative intent.

The Court held that Community Board 7 lacked capacity to sue. Neither New York City Charter § 2800 nor the ULURP provisions expressly authorized community boards to bring lawsuits. The Charter and ULURP specify what documents boards are entitled to receive, give boards no subpoena power or authority to retain independent counsel, and assign them an advisory role in land use review. Legislative history showed that proposals to give community boards power to sue were not adopted. FOIL’s broad standing provision did not supply the separate requirement of capacity.

The Court reversed the Appellate Division and dismissed the petition.

The ADS9803 can be powered down through the PWDN pin or the PD_CH field in register bank 1. After power-up or reset, it requires an initialization sequence with a free-running sampling clock, after which registers return to default values and user configuration can set analog input range, bandwidth, common-mode range, and data interface lanes.

The device supports speed-boost mode, allowing up to 8MSPS on one selected analog input channel pair while the other six channels remain idle. Register operations enable or disable this mode.

Configuration registers are 16-bit, organized into three banks, and accessed with 8-bit addresses. Register writes require selecting the bank through register 0x03, then writing the target register. Register reads require enabling SPI read mode, issuing the register address, reading the returned value, and disabling read mode afterward.

Multiple ADS9803 devices can be configured in an SPI daisy-chain using shared CS and SCLK lines, with SDO connected to the next device’s SDI. Daisy-chain length is configured through DAISY_CHAIN_LEN, and register access requires N × 24 SCLKs for N devices.

The register descriptions include controls for SPI mode, daisy-chain length, register bank selection, data format, averaging, XOR operation, digital test patterns, speed-boost mode, gain correction, analog input bandwidth, power-down control, reference settings, output lane mode, common-mode range, and initialization-related settings.

Application information describes the ADS9803 as an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS DAQ system for ATE use, with post-calibration TUE of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C for a ±5V range. It supports direct PMU connections or multiplexed PMU outputs, with wide-bandwidth mode settling to 99.95% full scale in 7.5µs. The device uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies with no required power-up sequence. Layout guidance recommends close bypass and reference capacitors, short ground connections, and separation of analog paths from digital lines and noise sources.

The ADS868xW supports an external 4.096V reference by setting INTREF_DIS in RANGE_SEL_REG, using REFIO as an input and the internal buffer to drive REFCAP. REFCAP requires at least 10µF to REFGND plus a nearby 1µF decoupling capacitor, and the buffer must not drive external loads. The reference buffer is stable from –40°C to +125°C, with typical drift of 0.5ppm/°C and maximum drift of 2ppm/°C.

The ADC supports single-ended and differential inputs with bipolar and unipolar ranges, using straight-binary output. LSB size equals FSR / 2^16. Alarm features include input and AVDD alarms on the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin when configured. Input alarm thresholds and hysteresis are programmable; AVDD alarm thresholds are fixed at 4.7V and 5.3V. Alarm flags can be read through the pin, ALARM_REG, or appended to output data.

The device uses a multiSPI interface with configurable host-to-device topologies, including single-device SPI and multi-device daisy-chain operation. Functional states are RESET, ACQ, and CONV, controlled by RST and CONVST/CS. RESET can be application reset or power-on reset. ACQ acquires the analog input, and CONV performs conversion using an internal clock.

Programming uses nine configuration registers and supports data write and read operations. Data frames begin on CONVST/CS falling edge and end on the rising edge. A 32-clock frame is optimal; shorter frames invalidate writes but can read MSBs, while longer frames use the last 32 input bits as the command. Output data can include conversion results, register data, fixed patterns, device address, range flags, alarm flags, and parity.

Data transfer protocols include standard SPI modes, dual-SDO operation, and source-synchronous modes using RVS as an output clock. Registers configure device ID, reset and power control, SDI and SDO protocols, output data, input ranges and reference selection, and alarm thresholds and flags.

Application guidance describes the ADS868xW as a 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated AFE, reference, ADC driver, programmable gain, overvoltage protection, and alarms. An example industrial analog input module combines ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 for voltage, current, or temperature sensing. The device uses AVDD and DVDD supplies, requires supply and reference decoupling, and offers NAP and power-down modes for reduced power. Layout guidance recommends separating analog and digital sections, using close decoupling capacitors, and properly bypassing REFCAP and REFIO.

Europe’s ageing population creates pressure on health and social care systems, especially as the share of older citizens grows. The passage argues for a proactive prevention strategy focused on “young elderly” people aged 60–75, aiming to keep them healthy, active and independent before they reach the 75+ age group.

The proposed approach is digital wellness services delivered through smart mobile phones and omnivore platforms, supported by cloud services and analytics. These services would track and support daily wellness routines without relying on regulated health or social care data. Wellness is treated as multidimensional, including physical, intellectual, social and emotional aspects, which may compensate for or support each other.

The Finnish BeWell research program, running from 2014–2016, studies how such services can be designed, implemented and sustained. It involves Tieto Group, other companies, research partners and elderly associations. The program uses the Wellmo platform, which connects to many devices and applications, and the Tieto cloud platform for scalable analytics and reporting.

The passage emphasizes that services should be designed with young elderly users, not merely for them, using action design research and co-creation. It argues that commercially viable ecosystems are needed because research projects alone cannot sustain long-term services.

An empirical study in the Åland Islands surveyed 101 young elderly respondents. Most respondents used smartphones and mobile apps, and many considered mobile apps useful in daily life. They also rated wellness issues, especially intellectual challenges and physical health, as important. Statistical analyses suggested differences related to education, age, work status, income and app use, offering guidance for selecting user groups in future design and testing.

The authors conclude that young elderly people are a relevant user group for digital wellness services, that they consider wellness important, and that mobile platforms can support wellness routines if services are user-designed, scalable and embedded in sustainable digital business ecosystems.

The study analyzed the spatiotemporal evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Alpha and Delta variants in Vietnam in 2021 using genomic surveillance from samples processed at major hospitals in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. Vietnam recorded limited COVID-19 transmission in early 2021, but infections and deaths rose sharply from May to December. Of 1,303 genomes obtained, 93.8% were Delta and 5.7% Alpha; 99.2% of Delta sequences belonged to lineage AY.57. Alpha appeared in multiple sporadic clusters between January and May but did not sustain widespread transmission. Delta AY.57 was first detected in April, likely introduced in early 2021, and drove the nationwide outbreak. Phylogeographic analysis suggested early spread from northern regions, later reseeding from the southeast, with distinct localized clusters and limited dispersal between localities during travel restrictions. AY.57 genetic diversity increased sharply from April to August, then stabilized. The authors conclude that rigorous public health measures contained Alpha, while Delta AY.57 caused a major outbreak in a largely susceptible population, underscoring the value of genomic surveillance for pandemic response.
