Other institutional investors including UBS, PNC, Retirement Systems of Alabama and KBC Group increased positions, while M&T Bank acquired a new stake. DeVry shares traded at $31.20, with a 12-month range of $15.36 to $32.85 and a market cap of $1.95 billion. The company reported quarterly EPS of $0.39, missing estimates by $0.02, while revenue rose 1.9% year over year to $449.9 million. Analysts expect fiscal-year EPS of $2.55. DeVry paid a semiannual dividend of $0.18 per share. Analyst ratings include one sell, seven hold and four buy, with a consensus “Hold” rating and $26.11 average target price. Major shareholder Value Advisers International sold 3,272 shares. DeVry provides educational services through healthcare, international and professional education, and business, technology and management segments.

Chinese textile firms are increasingly using North Korean factories and workers to reduce costs, with garments often labelled “Made in China” and exported globally, traders and businesses in Dandong told Reuters. U.N. sanctions targeting North Korea’s weapons programs do not ban textile exports, and textiles were North Korea’s second-largest export in 2016 at $752 million. Chinese suppliers send materials to North Korea for assembly, while some North Korean workers are employed in Chinese factories. Traders said production in North Korea can cut costs significantly, and factories are fully booked. North Korean workers are paid far less than Chinese workers, with portions of wages going to the North Korean state. New U.N. sanctions restrict increases in North Korean laborers abroad.

Glenner Town Square, an 8,500-square-foot 1950s-style indoor downtown in Chula Vista, offers interactive experiences designed to spark long-term memories for Alzheimer’s and dementia patients. Opened in April 2018, it includes storefronts such as a cinema, diner, library, boutique, auto shop, pet store, hospital and nursery. Glenner also operates adult day-care centers in Hillcrest and Encinitas, planned for future Town Square transitions. The passage also lists other licensed adult day programs for cognitively impaired adults in San Diego County, including centers in Clairemont, College Area, Mira Mesa, Mission Valley, Logan Heights, Bankers Hill, Rancho Bernardo, San Marcos and Fallbrook, with services such as meals, transportation, nursing, therapies, therapeutic activities, caregiver support and dementia-focused programming.

This systematic review examined evidence on marijuana, cannabinoids, and microbiome changes in humans. The review was registered in PROSPERO and followed PRISMA guidelines. Searches of PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane up to July 20, 2022 identified 4,022 records; 9 studies were included after screening. These comprised 1 case-control study, 6 cohort studies, and 2 clinical trials, with 2,526 participants from the USA, Iran, Israel, and the UK.

Included studies assessed cannabis or endocannabinoid-related interventions in conditions including HIV infection, inflammation, obesity, cognitive deficits, musculoskeletal pain, oral disease, and systemic aspergillosis. Reported microbiome-related findings included associations between marijuana use and changes in Fusobacterium, Anaerotruncus, Dorea, Prevotella:Bacteroides ratio, oral bacteria such as Streptococcus mutans and Lactobacilli, and taxa linked to oral sites. Endocannabinoid changes were associated with short-chain fatty acids and inflammatory markers. Oleoylethanolamide supplementation in obesity was linked to reduced energy and macronutrient intake and increased Akkermansia muciniphila.

Adverse events reported with marijuana cigarettes included coughing, wheezing, drowsiness, night sweats, systemic aspergillosis, and coughing bouts, which resolved after stopping smoking. Risk-of-bias concerns were present in several observational studies and one randomized trial. Because available studies involved varied conditions and designs, meta-analysis was not conducted. The review concluded that limited evidence suggests marijuana use or endocannabinoid supplements and gastrointestinal microbiota may be related to pain and other clinical manifestations, but further research is needed.

A hockey player says reaching the finals for the third time with three different teams is unique, but he wants a better finish and to win the trophy. He praises the team’s hard work, the sold-out games, and the city’s enthusiastic fans. He expects a tight series against the Flyers, who he says have played well and have experience.

Ben Rice was born and raised in Cohasset, Massachusetts, near Boston, but grew up a Yankees fan with Derek Jeter as his favorite player. He attended Noble and Greenough School in Dedham and later played college baseball at Dartmouth, though his playing time was limited by the COVID-19 pandemic. The Yankees drafted him in the 12th round in 2021 after a strong summer league showing. Rice became a key Yankees player in 2025, hitting 26 home runs over 138 games while playing first base, catcher and designated hitter. He is 26 and is not set to become a free agent until after 2030.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate to 1–1.25 percent, citing strong job growth and moderate economic growth despite weakening inflation. Officials lowered their 2017 inflation forecast to 1.6 percent but maintained a 2 percent forecast for next year, while some predicted unemployment could fall below 4 percent.

The speaker reports that the state of the Union has improved, citing renewed optimism, lower inflation, tax reductions, deregulation, job growth, and economic recovery. He argues that government had grown too large and that deficits should be reduced mainly through spending restraint, budget reforms, a line-item veto, a balanced budget amendment, closing tax loopholes, and simplifying the tax code rather than raising taxes.

He outlines four goals: steady economic growth, developing America’s next frontier, strengthening traditional values, and building a meaningful peace. He directs NASA to develop a permanently manned space station within a decade, promotes private space investment, and calls for environmental efforts including Chesapeake Bay cleanup, hazardous waste funding, acid rain research, and conservation land acquisition.

He emphasizes family, faith, education, school discipline, merit for teachers, tuition tax credits, school prayer, abortion restrictions, crime reduction, victims’ rights, fair housing, women’s rights, child care, child support enforcement, and enterprise zones. On foreign policy, he stresses military strength, alliances, arms reductions, freer trade, support for democracy, peace efforts in Lebanon, Central America, the Middle East, and southern Africa, and action against terrorism. Addressing the Soviet people, he says nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, and calls for peace and eventual elimination of nuclear weapons.

He praises military personnel, volunteers, and citizens who serve others, concluding that America’s best days lie ahead if it keeps faith, freedom, and courage.

Tom Brady’s agent Don Yee said Brady intends to return to the Patriots in 2018 and play beyond his current contract, possibly into his mid-40s. Brady has two seasons left on his deal. Yee said Brady remains focused on preparation despite retirement speculation. Patriots owner Robert Kraft said there is no issue with Brady’s contract.

MultiChoice’s DStv Premium subscribers declined despite overall subscriber growth, reducing average revenue per customer. CEO Calvo Mawela said Netflix has an “unfair advantage” and that customers who move to streaming do not return to broadcast TV. MultiChoice is pursuing a standalone DStv streaming package, has secured streaming rights for all channels, and warned ICASA that over-regulation could hurt the business and jobs.

The study developed a simplified mathematical model and computer simulations to evaluate whether screening-isolation can control infectious disease spread in a semi-isolated community when vaccines and medications are unavailable. The model extends SIR-style dynamics by including infection influx from outside, screening efficiency, recovery/death rate, and isolation time lag.

Theoretical analysis showed that successful control depends strongly on short screening-to-isolation delays; large time lags make control difficult. Improving screening efficiency alone contributed only weakly to robustness when delays were significant.

Simulations found that daily screening-isolation with efficiency 0.9 controlled disease when R0 was 3.0, keeping infection waves small, and still worked at R0 6.0, though with more infections. At R0 8.0, screening-isolation alone failed, suggesting additional measures such as social distancing and mask use may be needed. For R0 3.0, screening every 3 days controlled transmission at efficiencies 0.7 and 0.9, but weekly screening performed much worse, especially at efficiency 0.7. Screening every two weeks failed regardless of efficiency. Higher external influx increased cumulative infections proportionally under frequent screening, supporting the need for strict border control.

The authors conclude that regular periodic screening can help control epidemics in semi-isolated communities without vaccines or medications, with outcomes affected by screening frequency, screening efficiency, migration rate, and isolation delay.

CoreWeave has rebounded amid strong AI sentiment and major deals with OpenAI and Meta, reducing but not eliminating Microsoft revenue concentration risk. However, its debt-funded growth, aggressive capex, high valuation, and rising competition raise sustainability concerns, suggesting shares may cool off.

Joppatowne High School held its 45th commencement Wednesday at Harford Community College, where more than 130 seniors received diplomas. Principal Pamela Zeigler said about 95 percent of the 138-member class plans to attend college, technical school, join the military or enter law enforcement. Graduate Amya Hill, supported by family in purple shirts, plans to study nursing at Albany State University and encouraged younger students to keep pushing through academic struggles. Graduate Zachary Wagmun plans to attend Harford Community College for an electrician’s apprenticeship.

Valedictorian Kacey Lebrun and class president Breea Stevenson addressed the class. Stevenson urged classmates to try new things, separate from negative influences and focus on the present while pursuing goals. Other speakers included local and state officials, with Sen. Robert Cassilly citing examples of public service and sacrifice.

A letter attributed to fired assistant U.S. attorney Michael Ben’Ary said a false social media post apparently led to his termination during a terrorism prosecution related to the 2021 Afghanistan airport bombing. The letter criticized DOJ leadership, saying it prioritized punishing President Trump’s perceived enemies over national security.

The speaker declines to analyze the previous game publicly, saying the team will review it internally. They say Tampa feels good, has no pressure, and is focused only on extending the series, while Calgary faces pressure to win at home with the Cup in the building and Canada watching. The speaker emphasizes that playoff success depends heavily on battles and big plays, praises a Calgary top player, and says Tampa’s travel plan is to stay overnight for rest. They suggest Tampa may have struggled mentally by anticipating winning the Cup, and Calgary could face a similar challenge in an elimination game at home.

OptumCare offers “Brainsaver” classes in the Valley as part of a 12-week course promoting brain health through physical exercise, stress reduction, cognitive exercises, education, socialization, and nutrition. The program is aimed at helping reduce Alzheimer’s risk and serves adults from their mid-50s to late 80s at locations in Deer Valley, Goodyear, and Chandler.

The manuscript identifies an intervalley superconducting phase in half-filled second moiré bands of approximately 2° twisted bilayer MoTe2 at hole filling νh = 3. Using exact diagonalization of a continuum model with both valleys and screened Coulomb interactions, the authors find a phase sequence as screening length d increases: ferromagnetic Chern insulator, superconducting intermediate phase, and non-Abelian fractional spin Hall insulator.

The intermediate phase is characterized by a singly degenerate paramagnetic ground state, 2π-periodic spectral flow, negative binding energy, a dominant eigenvalue in the pair density matrix, finite superfluid stiffness, and intervalley entanglement. Its pairing is time-reversal symmetric extended nodal s-wave, involving opposite valleys and momenta. The transition from the superconducting phase to the fractional spin Hall insulator appears continuous, and the authors formulate a field theory describing simultaneous changes in topology and symmetry.

The study also finds that replacing the moiré bands with ideal first Landau levels weakens superconductivity, while introducing non-uniform quantum geometry restores key superconducting features. The authors suggest that higher moiré bands in twisted bilayer MoTe2 may provide a platform for studying the interplay of superconductivity, strong correlations, topology, and quantum geometry.

OTC trading involves direct, decentralized transactions between two parties without a centralized exchange, often through electronic dealer or market-maker networks. OTC markets trade stocks, bonds, commodities, derivatives, ADRs, and some crypto deals, offering flexibility and access to capital for companies that cannot or do not list on major exchanges. However, OTC markets are generally less transparent, less liquid, less regulated, and carry higher counterparty, fraud, manipulation, and valuation risks. OTC stocks, especially penny stocks, are described as high-risk, often speculative, prone to pump-and-dump schemes, and historically associated with poor returns. The passage argues that both long-term investing and short-term trading in OTC stocks are generally unfavorable due to low liquidity, slippage, scams, and high failure rates.

A federal government shutdown appeared more likely after President Donald Trump met with congressional leaders. Vice President JD Vance blamed Democrats, while Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said both sides remain far apart and blamed Republicans. Republicans seek a clean stopgap funding bill through late November, while Democrats want health care provisions, including extended enhanced Obamacare tax credits. Previous short-term funding bills failed in the Senate.

Moina Shaiq started “Meet a Muslim” in Fremont, California, after realizing people were afraid to ask about Islam. Her first event drew about 100 people, and she now speaks at libraries, coffee shops, churches, service clubs and homes, addressing stereotypes and questions about Muslim beliefs, women, hijab, sects and American Muslim life. Similar “Ask a Muslim” efforts have reemerged amid rising anti-Muslim incidents. Shaiq has faced threats, while Muslim advocates say such programs can counter fear and xenophobia through personal interaction. Some critics argue the efforts repeat old conversations and should focus instead on policy change. Shaiq says her goal is to educate Americans and share a message of love, compassion and peace.

The disclosure concerns wireless communication methods and devices for transmitting and receiving sounding reference signals (SRS), particularly configuring guard periods for SRS antenna switching when adjacent to uplink transmissions such as PUSCH or PUCCH. A UE receives SRS configuration information from a base station, including SRS resources and usage information, and transmits SRS using those resources. When a guard period overlaps a configured uplink channel, its priority is set the same as the priority between the SRS and that uplink channel.

The disclosure describes configuring guard periods based on numerology, subcarrier spacing, SRS resource sets, and higher-layer signaling, including guard period start position, number of symbols, and whether it applies before or after adjacent uplink transmission. It also addresses collisions between guard periods, PUCCH, PUSCH, and SRS resource sets through priority rules, dropping rules, puncturing, rate matching, shifting transmissions, or reconfiguring SRS groups. The proposed methods aim to enable efficient uplink transmission and prevent distortion caused by collisions during SRS antenna switching.
Turing Tensor Cores accelerate deep learning matrix operations, add INT8 and INT4 modes for inferencing, and enable DLSS, which uses neural networks to improve rendered images with fewer samples.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on January 3, 2016 it issued a press release, attached as Exhibit 99.1, furnished under Items 2.02 and 7.01. The report was signed by General Counsel Todd A. Maron on January 4, 2016.

Zsolt Lakatos, 31, was arrested after eight days on the run following his conviction for wounding with intent over catastrophic injuries to his four-month-old son. He had failed to return to Liverpool Crown Court after being sent home during his trial and was sentenced in his absence to 13 years in prison. Lakatos admitted breaching bail, saying he “panicked” over the prospect of jail, and received an additional 10 days. The child, now 22 months old and in foster care, suffered brain bleeding, fractured ribs, a fractured shin and retinal haemorrhaging after being shaken on two occasions. The judge said the child would need lifelong care and medication.

Coach Quenneville discussed the Blackhawks’ consistent approach, emphasizing accountability, communication, leadership, and players’ commitment to improving and supporting teammates. He praised the team’s top players for setting the tone, noted strong goaltending from Corey Crawford and Scott Darling, and described roster decisions as based on performance and opportunity rather than “benching.” He highlighted improvements from several players, including stronger faceoffs, timely goals, defensive trust, versatility, and growth in bigger games. Quenneville said the team must avoid overconfidence, play each game as a must-win, adjust to opponents’ speed, and rely on quickness and finding ways to win.

Cover 0 is a man-to-man defensive coverage with no deep safety help. It is used to bring maximum blitz pressure, often adding six defenders near the line of scrimmage while ensuring eligible receivers are covered. Its strengths include clear assignments, easy adjustment to motion, strong run support, effectiveness against RPOs, screens, short routes, and pressure on long-developing plays. Its weaknesses are high risk: beaten defenders have no help, deep routes can create big plays, and draw plays, quarterback scrambles, and pick routes can exploit coverage. Variations include Cover 0 “Rat,” which rushes five and leaves one defender to cut off crossing routes or contain the quarterback, and schemes that drop hybrid defensive linemen into coverage.

Astronomers report that Oumuamua, the first confirmed interstellar object detected in our solar system, likely came from a binary star system and was ejected as planets formed. Discovered in October by a Hawaiian observatory, the red, cigar-shaped asteroid may be 400 meters long and is moving away at over 26 km per second. Researchers say it is tumbling through space, possibly after a collision, and may continue doing so for billions of years. Scientists now agree it is an asteroid, not a comet, and suggest close binary systems may produce many interstellar objects.

Soybean May futures rose as physical supplies declined and crushing demand stayed strong due to soy meal exports. Prices are expected to trade higher, though adequate supplies and cheap imports may pressure edible oil prices.

A University of Maryland study of 1,099 college students found that young adults who regularly consumed highly caffeinated energy drinks over time were more likely at age 25 to use cocaine, non-medically use prescription stimulants, and be at risk for alcohol use disorder. The study controlled for demographics, sensation-seeking, other caffeine use, and prior substance use. It was published in Drug and Alcohol Dependence.

The study examines holistic education in Indian higher education, drawing on Indian sages-thinkers and modern policy frameworks. It contrasts contemporary materialist education with traditions emphasizing integrated development of mind, body, society, and spirit. Tagore, Osho, Vivekananda, and Sri Aurobindo are presented as advocates of multidimensional education that combines inner growth, ethical formation, creativity, spirituality, and practical knowledge. The study links these ideas to India’s NEP 2020, UN SDG 4.7, and the ISEE emphasis on human flourishing.

Using a comprehensive literature review and a PRISMA-guided systematic literature review of Scopus and Semantic Scholar articles published before 2021, the authors identified and validated dimensions of holistic education. From 472 records, eight original articles were selected for thematic analysis using MAXQDA. The review found that Social-Emotional Learning provides a practical bridge between academic learning and broader human development. Among SEL models, the Indian LIBRE/EMC² framework was identified as contextually appropriate because it integrates whole-brain learning through empathy, mindfulness, compassion, and critical inquiry.

The systematic review supported these four dimensions. Empathy was associated with interpersonal sensitivity, cultural awareness, communication, collaboration, relationship-building, and global citizenship. Critical inquiry included analytical thinking, problem-solving, information management, intellectual curiosity, interdisciplinary synthesis, and reflective practice. Mindfulness involved self-actualization, spiritual awareness, self-knowledge, emotional resilience, moral awareness, and holistic integration. Compassion was linked to care, supportive action, stewardship, and integrity.

The study concludes that the LIBRE/EMC² dimensions align with Indian educational philosophy, NEP 2020, SDG 4.7, and holistic education literature. It argues that these dimensions can guide curriculum design, assessment, and policy implementation in Indian higher education. The authors note limitations, including reliance on two databases and exclusion of non-indexed sources such as Holistic Education Review, and recommend future research to expand source coverage, develop culturally sensitive assessment tools, and examine implementation across educational settings.

Consumer advocates reported glitches in the final days of Affordable Care Act enrollment, including incorrect HealthCare.gov messages in Illinois and other states saying no plans were available, though every county has at least one insurer. The Trump administration said the issue was resolved and affected consumers would be contacted, but advocates said the problem persisted. Enrollment through HealthCare.gov for 39 states ends Dec. 15 at midnight Pacific time, with Thursday and Friday expected to be the busiest days, possibly causing website slowdowns and call center delays. Hurricane-affected residents can request an extension to Dec. 31. Despite a shortened enrollment period and reduced advertising, consumer interest remained strong. Subsidies may lower 2018 premiums for many eligible consumers, with some bronze plans available at no monthly premium. It remains unclear whether the administration will grant deadline extensions for incomplete applications. States running their own exchanges generally have later deadlines, including Jan. 31 in California and New York.

President Woodrow Wilson proclaimed that a state of war existed between the United States and the Imperial German Government following Congress’s joint resolution. Citing statutory authority, he directed U.S. officers to act with vigilance, called on citizens to support the war effort, and defined unnaturalized German males aged fourteen and older in the United States as “alien enemies.” He stated that law-abiding alien enemies would be allowed to live and work peacefully, while those violating the law or regulations could be restrained, required to provide security, removed, or detained. Regulations barred alien enemies from possessing weapons, explosives, aircraft, wireless or signaling devices, ciphers, and related materials; approaching military or munitions sites; publishing attacks or threats against U.S. authorities or personnel; aiding enemies; entering prohibited areas; departing or entering the United States without permission; and avoiding registration if required. Suspected violators or dangers to public safety could be arrested and confined. The proclamation applied throughout U.S. jurisdiction.

Tesla announced lower-cost Standard versions of its Model 3 and Model Y. The Model 3 Standard starts at $36,990, while the Model Y Standard costs $39,990 and has an estimated 321-mile range. Both include fewer features than pricier variants, such as no FM/AM radio, and the Model Y Standard lacks Autosteer, an LED lightbar, and adaptive high beams. Buyers save $5,500 versus the Model 3 Premium rear-wheel drive and $5,000 versus the Model Y Premium rear-wheel drive. Tesla stock fell after the announcement. Availability is listed for November to December for the Model Y Standard and December to January for the Model 3 Standard.

The Nationals’ competition for the fifth starter spot may continue past opening day after signing veteran Jeremy Hellickson to a minor league deal. He joins A.J. Cole and Erick Fedde as candidates, though Washington may let Hellickson build arm strength in minor league camp rather than rush him. General manager Mike Rizzo said the move adds depth and noted the team learned from past mistakes in handling late-spring roster decisions. Cole, who is out of options, is expected to make the team, possibly in the bullpen. Manager Dave Martinez named Max Scherzer the opening day starter, followed by Stephen Strasburg, Gio Gonzalez and Tanner Roark. Fedde is likely headed to the minors. Hellickson is trying to rebound after struggling with Baltimore last season. Shortstop Trea Turner left camp to address an ingrown toenail but could return quickly.

VentureWire’s November 14, 2000 issue reports venture financing, layoffs, acquisitions, executive changes, and fund news. Top stories include Apax merging its European and Israeli units and pledging $600 million for Israeli investments; New Edge Networks cutting 135 jobs; KSolutions raising a $50 million first round; and Cisco acquiring wireless chip firm Radiata for $295 million in stock. The issue also covers numerous funding rounds across energy, wireless, optical networking, storage, e-learning, software, and marketplace companies; closures and layoffs at eSociety, iExplore, and Buzz MSP; company name changes and product launches; several acquisitions; new board appointments and CEOs; Murphree Venture Partners’ new fund; and personnel additions at Horizon Ventures and St. Paul Venture Capital.

The defendant appealed a conviction for simple assault after being charged with assault with a deadly weapon. He had followed his wife, saw her meet Albert Donaso, sought police help to remove Donaso from his home, then entered through a broken window and found his wife, her aunt, and Donaso in the kitchen. During a struggle, Donaso was repeatedly cut with a pocketknife.

The appellate court rejected claims of trial error. It found no prejudicial issue regarding questions about where Mrs. Ortiz met Donaso or why her aunt fled. It held that the prosecutor properly asked the defendant on cross-examination to demonstrate how he drew and opened the knife, because he claimed he did so in self-defense after Donaso rushed at him with a knife. The court also held that evidence about alleged threatening letters was collateral, since the main issue was whether the admitted cutting was in self-defense. The judgment was affirmed.

Devanna Cornitcher, 25, was found stabbed to death in a Chester, Pennsylvania apartment. Police arrested her boyfriend, Alonzo Carter, who allegedly confessed but claimed self-defense. Her two children were present, and Carter was denied bail.

NVIDIA describes Blackwell as designed to advance neural shaders and AI-based rendering. Ray Reconstruction uses AI to generate higher-quality pixels for ray-traced scenes and reduce denoiser artifacts, while DLAA applies AI anti-aliasing at native resolution for improved temporal stability and motion detail. Blackwell introduces developer-created neural shaders, supported by Cooperative Vectors API for DX12 and Vulkan, enabling Tensor Core access through graphics shaders and supporting techniques such as neural texture compression, RTX Neural Materials, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces.

The passage outlines shader evolution from fixed-function pipelines through vertex, pixel, geometry, tessellation, compute, mesh, ray tracing, and Blackwell neural shaders. Neural shaders train networks to approximate complex rendering tasks, including light-surface interaction, compressed texture decompression, indirect lighting prediction, and subsurface scattering. RTX Neural Materials approximates complex layered materials for real-time rendering; RTX Neural Texture Compression reduces memory use; Neural Radiance Cache infers multi-bounce indirect lighting from limited path-traced rays; RTX Skin brings ray-traced subsurface scattering to games; and RTX Neural Faces uses generative AI to infer more natural faces from rasterized input and pose data.

The Blackwell GPU family includes GB202, GB203, and GB205. GB202 is the flagship GPU with 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, and 768 Tensor Cores, used for GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 targets high-end graphics with 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, and 336 Tensor Cores, used for RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 targets the performance segment with 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA Cores, 50 RT Cores, and 200 Tensor Cores, used for RTX 5070. The document ends with NVIDIA legal disclaimers, warranty limitations, trademark notices, and copyright information.

Juan Archibeque sued Jose Maria Miera before a justice of the peace for damage allegedly caused to his wheat field by Miera’s cattle. The justice entered judgment for Archibeque for forty almudes of wheat, and Miera appealed to the district court, where the case was tried de novo and the jury found for Miera. Archibeque sought a new trial, which was denied, and appealed.

The court held that, under the organic act, only the supreme court has appellate jurisdiction; district courts cannot be given strictly appellate or revisory powers. Appeals from justices of the peace to district courts are tried de novo as matters of original jurisdiction. The justice’s transcript is used only to show that the case originated and was tried before the justice, that judgment was rendered, and that an appeal was properly taken. Therefore, the district court did not err in refusing to dismiss the case for alleged transcript errors or in allowing Archibeque to file his account.

On the merits, the court found that conflicting testimony about the number of cattle, timing, tracks, and possible damage by other animals was for the jury to weigh. Because the evidence did not clearly preponderate against the verdict, the refusal to grant a new trial was within the court’s discretion. The judgment for Miera was affirmed.

Chapter I covers January 1–March 8, 1945, including U.S. consultations with the United Kingdom, Soviet Union, China, and France on unresolved Dumbarton Oaks issues, Yalta decisions, consideration of views from governments, Congress, and the public, and invitations to 39 United Nations. A January 2 circular telegram notes a December 29 meeting where American Republic mission heads discussed memoranda from nine governments on Dumbarton Oaks proposals and preparations for a conference to coordinate views on international organization.

The speaker says both teams faced a tough early situation, praised the crowd and penalty killing, acknowledged frustration with recent effort, and said the team expects to improve at home by holding the puck longer against a talented opponent.

The passage argues that the Carter administration suffered strategic setbacks in Iran and Nicaragua by helping replace friendly moderate autocrats with less friendly extremist regimes. It says similar situations elsewhere require a realistic policy toward non-democratic governments threatened by Soviet-sponsored subversion. Kirkpatrick criticizes Carter officials for favoring leftist challenges to rightist autocracies despite risks, and argues that traditional authoritarian governments are generally less repressive, more open to liberalization, and more compatible with U.S. interests than revolutionary autocracies. She contrasts traditional autocrats, who preserve existing social patterns and inequalities, with revolutionary regimes, which she says create greater repression and disruption.

The Base Cross Offense is a basketball set designed to exploit post-ups and size mismatches, often using a smaller player to set a baseline screen for a bigger post player. It begins with entries such as pass, dribble clear, UCLA, or Hawk action, leading to a baseline screen for the post to receive a shot or strong post position. Success depends on precise execution of screens, post reads, ball reversal, and counters to defensive tactics such as trailing, fronting, switching, showing and recovering, or denying reversal passes. If the initial post option is unavailable, the offense can flow into weakside down screens, mid screens, side screens, back cuts, or post isolation. Teaching the offense requires strong fundamentals, defensive recognition, timing, communication, and practice through drills and scrimmage situations. Game strategy includes scouting opponents, anticipating defensive reads, varying alignments and entries, and attacking weak defenders.

The study used machine learning to predict depressive symptom severity from sleep quality, anxiety, and brain measures across three cohorts: HCP-Young, HCP-Aging, and eNKI, including a small longitudinal eNKI sample. Prior research linked sleep disturbance, anxiety, and depression, but often relied on single-cohort group comparisons with limited generalizability.

In HCP-Young, poor sleep quality predicted depressive symptom severity, and adding anxiety substantially improved prediction. Similar results were found in independent HCP-Aging and eNKI datasets, supporting model generalizability. In the longitudinal eNKI sample, baseline sleep quality and anxiety predicted future depressive symptoms, while prediction was not successful among participants who received neurofeedback therapy between visits.

Brain gray matter volume and resting-state functional measures did not improve prediction and did not mediate the sleep–depression association. Anxiety mediated much of the association between sleep quality and depressive symptoms. Complementary analyses showed findings were robust after excluding participants with lifetime depression history, removing sleep-related depression questionnaire items, testing sleep-quality components, and assessing reverse prediction. Predicting sleep quality from depressive symptoms was less robust than predicting depressive symptoms from sleep quality.

The authors conclude that poor sleep quality and anxiety are important contributors to depressive symptoms at the individual level, while the examined brain measures did not play an important predictive or mediating role.

A motorist led police on a two-hour chase from Kansas into Missouri after officers tried to stop him on felony warrants. Police arrested him after his vehicle crashed and found drugs and loaded weapons.

Markets shifted risk-off after a week of earnings, economic data, Fed signals, and policy uncertainty. Q2 earnings were generally stronger than expected, with most S&P 500 companies beating EPS and revenue estimates, but investors sold into good news. GDP beat expectations at 3%, though tariff-related import volatility clouded the data and personal spending showed softness. Payrolls missed expectations, prior months were sharply revised down, and unemployment rose slightly to 4.2%. The Fed held a data-dependent stance despite two dissents, while markets priced in high odds of a September rate cut and further cuts by January. Major indexes formed a bearish engulfing pattern, internals weakened, most sectors fell, and the risk gauge moved fully risk-off.

Des Moines Public Schools Superintendent Ian Roberts resigned effective immediately after being detained by ICE during a targeted enforcement operation. ICE said Roberts, born in Guyana, was in the U.S. unlawfully, had a final removal order from May 2024, and allegedly evaded arrest; agents reported finding a handgun, hunting knife, and $3,000 in his vehicle. His Iowa educator license was revoked, and the school board had requested documentation of his citizenship status.

Attorney Alfredo Parrish said Roberts believed his immigration case had been successfully closed based on a prior attorney’s letter and that his firm is seeking to reopen the case and filed a stay request in federal immigration court. Roberts is being held at the Woodbury County Jail.

Questions have emerged about the district’s hiring vetting process. District officials said Roberts completed I-9 verification, while a background-check firm said its criminal check did not verify legal work authorization. U.S. Rep. Zach Nunn said federal officials confirmed Roberts was subject to a final removal order.

A study found that treatments perceived as more expensive can produce stronger nocebo effects. Volunteers given an expensive-looking fake cream reported more heat-related pain than those given a generic-looking cream, after being told it could increase pain sensitivity. The expensive-looking cream increased reported pain by nearly 30 percent, compared with about 3 percent for the generic version. Brain imaging showed related activity changes in pain pathway regions. Researchers say the findings may help clinicians reduce nocebo effects when discussing medications.

The Patient Charter, based on the NHS Constitution, sets out patients’ legal rights, NHS pledges and patient responsibilities. It confirms access to NHS care based on need, generally free at the point of use, with exceptions such as prescriptions in England, dentistry and eye care. Patients have rights to equal access, safe and clean care, qualified staff, appropriate treatment, privacy, valid consent, clear information, choice of GP practice, involvement in decisions, and openness if something goes wrong.

The Charter also covers waiting time standards, access to NICE-recommended treatments where clinically suitable, fair local decisions on other treatments, vaccinations, complaints processes, escalation to the Ombudsman, judicial review and compensation for negligence. It emphasises fairness, transparency, accountability and continuous improvement in NHS services.

Patients are also expected to use the NHS responsibly by looking after their health where possible, respecting staff and other patients, following or discussing treatment plans, attending appointments, and participating in screening and vaccination programmes. The Charter presents the NHS as a partnership based on rights, responsibilities, trust and shared respect.

“Goal side” positioning in soccer means defenders place themselves between their own goal and the opponent, keeping opponents in front of them. Youth players should be taught to “get in the way” legally by recognizing their position relative to the goal, moving up to meet opponents, or sprinting past them and turning if caught behind. Practice should cover right, center, and left positions, movement with opponents, glancing back at the goal, and gradually increasing speed with and without the ball. Coaches should provide one-on-one instruction and remind players not to block or use their arms.

James F. Robertson III petitioned for a writ of mandamus ordering the Escambia Circuit Court to enter a default judgment in his divorce action against Cynthia D. Robertson. The trial court had denied his default-judgment motion for failure to comply with Rule 4.3, Ala. R. Civ. P., because the court file lacked proof of service by publication. The Court of Civil Appeals of Alabama denied the petition, holding that Robertson had not shown a clear legal right to relief because he failed to establish that the required publisher’s affidavit under Rule 4.3(d)(5) had been filed.

In United States v. Frank P. Dow Co. Inc., the Government appealed reappraisement of imported fishing equipment. The importer conceded outside packing charges were dutiable. The court found no evidence that a 26.557 yen invoice deduction was improper and set values at appraised values less specified charges and that deduction.

The Sensex rose 270 points to 29,683.87, ending a two-day losing streak, while the Nifty surpassed 9,200. Metal, energy, FMCG and banking stocks gained, though TCS was flat. Asian markets were mixed amid North Korea tensions, and the rupee traded slightly higher at 64.40 per dollar.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its FY2018 Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 28, 2018. The company is headquartered in Santa Clara, California, incorporated in Delaware, and its common stock trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the symbol NVDA. As of February 26, 2018, it had 605 million shares outstanding.

NVIDIA describes itself as a company that began with PC graphics, invented the GPU, and expanded into artificial intelligence, high performance computing, virtual reality, gaming, professional visualization, datacenter, and automotive applications. Its two reportable segments are GPU and Tegra Processor. GPU product brands include GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, GRID, DGX, and cryptocurrency-specific GPUs. Tegra products support DRIVE, SHIELD, and Jetson platforms.

The company serves four main markets: Gaming, Professional Visualization, Datacenter, and Automotive. Gaming products include GeForce GTX GPUs, SHIELD devices, GeForce NOW, and developer tools such as GameWorks and VRWorks. Professional Visualization products include Quadro GPUs and Holodeck. Datacenter offerings include Tesla GPUs, CUDA, cuDNN, TensorRT, NVLink, DGX systems, NVIDIA GPU Cloud, and GRID. Automotive offerings include DRIVE platforms for infotainment, driver assistance, and autonomous vehicles, with more than 320 companies and organizations working with NVIDIA’s DRIVE platform.

NVIDIA’s strategy includes advancing GPU computing, extending leadership in AI and visual computing, advancing autonomous vehicle platforms, and leveraging intellectual property. The company uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on suppliers and subcontractors for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging. Key suppliers include Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, Samsung Electronics, Advanced Semiconductor Engineering, BYD, Hon Hai, King Yuan Electronics, and others.

As of January 28, 2018, NVIDIA had 11,528 employees, including 8,191 in research and development. R&D expenses were $1.80 billion in fiscal 2018, compared with $1.46 billion in fiscal 2017 and $1.33 billion in fiscal 2016. The company reported $7.11 billion in cash and marketable securities at fiscal year-end 2018.

The filing lists risks including rapid technological change, competition, cybersecurity threats, product defects, reliance on third-party manufacturers, demand forecasting errors, international operations, employee retention, acquisitions, intellectual property disputes, litigation, tax changes, privacy regulation, and anti-takeover provisions.

NVIDIA’s headquarters complex includes leased and owned facilities in Santa Clara, California, with additional leased and owned facilities in the United States and internationally. In fiscal 2018, the company paid $341 million in cash dividends and had authorization to repurchase up to $1.82 billion of common stock through December 2020.

WMCC’s modern cabinetry and construction vocational class built cabinets and countertops for Kidder United Methodist Church’s kitchen, which is being upgraded to serve as a disaster relief center through a partnership with the church, Kidder and Caldwell County Emergency Management. The church paid material costs while the prison provided labor. Officials said the project gave offenders real-world experience, supported future employment skills and benefited the community.

Conrad Lapp acquired all stock of Joslyn Fruit Company before marrying Laura Lapp in Colorado. In 1977, Joslyn owed Pacific Gamble Robinson Company $34,710.70, and Lapp signed a promissory note in Colorado individually and for Joslyn; Mrs. Lapp did not sign. After default, the Lapps moved to Washington, where Pacific sued Joslyn, Lapp individually, and the marital community.

The trial court entered judgment against Lapp individually but dismissed the marital community, and the Court of Appeals affirmed. The Washington Supreme Court reversed. Applying the “most significant relationship” choice-of-law test, the court held Colorado law governed because the transaction, parties’ domicile at execution, corporation, and expected performance were all connected to Colorado, while Washington’s connection arose only after default. Under Colorado law, property subject to Mr. Lapp’s debt, including his wages and acquisitions but excluding Mrs. Lapp’s separate property and earnings, remained reachable in Washington despite Washington community property classifications.

The dissent argued Washington law should determine what property may satisfy a judgment in Washington and that Washington community property should not be liable for Mr. Lapp’s noncommunity debt.

The passage outlines cryptocurrency trading concepts, strategies, risks, and market influences. It describes trading as buying and selling digital assets like Bitcoin and Ethereum for profit, using strategies such as day trading, whale watching, swing trading, dark pool trading, trend following, range trading, fork trading, breakout trading, mean reversion, arbitrage, grid trading, sentiment analysis, technical analysis, staking, quantum trading, Ichimoku cloud trading, and NFT trading. It notes that crypto markets are volatile, trend-following has historically worked better than mean reversion in its studies, and backtesting is recommended before committing money. It discusses factors affecting prices, including demand, sentiment, regulation, technology, macroeconomic events, DeFi, hard forks, halving events, and Tether. It also highlights risks such as volatility, scams, cybercrime, exchange insolvency, private key loss, and limited regulation.

The St. Louis Court of Appeals affirmed the circuit court’s judgment in Century Realty Company v. Travelers Insurance Company, relying on the same facts, principles, and reasoning as in Century Realty Co. v. Frankfort Marine, Accident and Plate Glass Insurance Company.

An MIT course session featured a financing sources panel with Axel Bichara, Julianne Zimmerman, and Amir Nashat. The professor recapped prior classes on business planning, pitching, customer discovery, business models, and upcoming financial projections, then introduced financing options including venture capital, angels, friends and family, customers, grants, crowdfunding, credit cards, and competitions.

Panelists described backgrounds in startups, venture capital, accelerators, and seed investing. They emphasized matching financing sources to company stage, goals, market potential, and team; choosing investors carefully; aligning interests; and understanding that venture capital is not appropriate for most startups. Discussion covered incubators and accelerators, convertible notes versus equity, strategic investors, deal sizes, investor introductions, university technology commercialization, social-impact investing, and risks from mismatched or poorly structured investor groups. Key advice included working with good people, checking investor references, using mentors, targeting suitable investors, retiring major risks early, and ensuring partners and investors share a clear definition of success.

The passage introduces Flow Matching for Corrected Posterior Estimation (FMCPE), a method for addressing model misspecification in simulation-based inference. Standard neural posterior estimation can fail when simulator-generated data differ from real observations, producing biased or overconfident posteriors. FMCPE uses abundant low-fidelity simulations, a pretrained simulation-based posterior estimator, and a small calibration set of high-fidelity parameter–observation pairs.

The method applies two flow-matching steps: one learns a transport from real observations to simulator-domain samples, and the other transports samples from a simulation-informed proposal posterior toward the corrected posterior. The approach does not require knowing the form of misspecification or relying on conditional independence assumptions. The two flows are trained jointly using calibration data and simulator outputs.

Experiments on Gaussian, Pendulum, WindTunnel, and LightTunnel tasks compare FMCPE with NPE and MFNPE using joint classifier two-sample test, Wasserstein distance, and mean squared error. Results show that FMCPE generally outperforms both baselines, especially with small calibration sets, producing more accurate and better-calibrated posterior estimates. The method is computationally efficient, amortized, and usable as post-processing for existing SBI models.

The passage lists South Carolina news items on the 2018 governor’s race, Joe Wilson’s office move, constitution restoration funding, Ports Authority office sale, Medicare cardiac care testing, Tecklenburg’s first year, and new state laws.

Apple announced a free battery replacement program for eligible 13-inch MacBook Pro models without Touch Bar built between October 2016 and October 2017 due to potential battery swelling, which Apple says is not a safety issue.

The passage describes SD Memory Card Physical Layer Specification Version 6.00 features, interfaces, modes, commands, and card behavior. It covers Mc-EX transfer definitions, SD/SDIO relationships, card capacity classes (SDSC up to 2GB, SDHC over 2GB to 32GB, SDXC over 32GB to 2TB), voltage ranges, read/write and ROM card types, protected and user areas, speed classes, bus speed modes, form factors, registers, reset behavior, and communication protocols.

SD bus communication is host-controlled through commands, responses, and data tokens on CMD and DAT lines, with CRC protection. Data transfers use single or multiple blocks, with support for 1-bit and 4-bit buses. The passage defines command and response formats, data packet formats, SPI and UHS-II references, pad assignments, UHS-II interface handling, and ROM card restrictions.

It details UHS-I and UHS-II operation. UHS-I supports 1.8V signaling, SDR/DDR modes, up to 104MB/s, and requires voltage switching and 4-bit mode except for CMD42. UHS-II supports legacy SD and UHS-II interfaces, initialization stages, device enumeration, SD-TRAN command emulation, and modes up to FD624 at 624MB/s. It also describes application performance classes, cache, self-maintenance, command queueing, low-voltage initialization, and UHS-III terminology.

Card initialization uses CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, and CMD3 to reset, verify voltage, initialize, identify, and assign RCA. Data transfer mode uses CMD7 for card selection, CMD9 for CSD reading, CMD12 to stop transfers, and block read/write, erase, discard, and FULE command sequences. Write protection includes mechanical switch, internal protection, password locking, and Card Ownership Protection with PWD and FEP handling through CMD42.

A study by scientists at the Children's Hospital Oakland Research Institute found that 173 women aged 25 to 50 who usually drank less than a litre of water daily lost weight after adding half a litre of water to breakfast. The passage also states that other studies linked drinking half a litre of water to burning extra calories, and that high-protein diets may support weight loss.

Arthur James Balfour argues that the Central powers used calculated brutality in Belgium and submarine warfare to crush enemies and intimidate neutrals, and that a peace based on their success would undermine treaties, international law, and prospects for durable peace. He states that lasting peace requires reducing causes of unrest, discrediting the Central powers’ aggressive aims and methods among their peoples, and creating international sanctions to deter aggression. Britain’s sacrifices are presented as necessary for Allied success, peaceful civilization, and future international reforms. A separate dispatch from Greece reports acceptance of Entente ultimatum conditions without reservation, including liberation of political prisoners and internal control. Another note records Persia’s endorsement of President Wilson’s December 18, 1916 note and its request for U.S. assistance in maintaining Persia’s integrity and rights at a future peace conference.

DS-STAR is a data science agent that generates Python solutions through iterative planning and verification. It addresses limitations of prior agents that focus mainly on structured data and often treat successful code execution as sufficient evidence of correctness. DS-STAR first analyzes heterogeneous input files, such as CSV, JSON, Markdown, and unstructured text, by generating scripts that extract concise descriptions of file structure and content. It then builds solutions sequentially through a loop of planning, coding, execution, verification, and refinement.

The framework uses multiple LLM-based agents: an analyzer for file descriptions, a planner for solution steps, a coder for Python implementation, a verifier that judges whether the current plan is sufficient to answer the query, a router that decides whether to add a step or remove erroneous steps, and a debugger for execution errors. A retrieval module selects relevant files when many files are present.

Experiments on DABStep, KramaBench, and DA-Code show that DS-STAR outperforms prior methods. Compared with the best alternative, it improves accuracy from 41.0% to 45.2% on DABStep, 39.8% to 44.7% on KramaBench, and 37.0% to 38.5% on DA-Code. Ablation studies show that both the analyzer and router agents improve performance. Harder tasks require more refinement rounds, and higher iteration limits improve accuracy, especially on hard tasks. The paper identifies human-in-the-loop extension as future work.

The Yankees and Red Sox will meet in the 2025 AL Wild Card series in New York starting Tuesday, Sept. 30. Boston enters as the No. 5 seed after trading Rafael Devers, while New York is the No. 4 seed despite the AL’s second-best record. The best-of-three series airs on ESPN, with radio coverage on SiriusXM. This is their sixth postseason matchup, with Boston leading previous series 3-2.

“Sell the rip” is a trading strategy of selling an asset, either by closing a long position or opening a short position, when its price is considered overvalued or overbought. It is based on mean reversion and the idea that overpriced assets may correct or crash. The strategy is mainly used by short-term traders and may suit weak stocks inflated by sentiment, but it is not recommended for strong long-term growth assets. Indicators such as RSI, Stochastic, Williams %R, IBS, Bollinger Bands, and moving averages can help identify overbought conditions. A backtest on SPY using RSI showed promise but initially had large drawdowns; adjusted exit rules improved results by reducing holding time and increasing trade frequency. The passage notes that the strategy has worked better in the S&P 500 since the 1990s than in trend-following markets such as commodities.

At the Scripps National Spelling Bee, longtime associate pronouncer Rev. Brian Sietsema took over some duties from Jacques Bailly as the competition nearly doubled in size due to a wild-card program. Sietsema, a Greek Orthodox priest, former linguistics professor and former Merriam-Webster pronunciation editor, pronounced for about 180 spellers. More than 500 spellers competed in preliminary rounds, with 41 semifinalists chosen through written spelling and vocabulary test results. Stories included Rebekah Zeigler, a busy multisport athlete competing in her fourth bee; Reagan Remmers, reinstated after her spelling matched a Ukrainian city homonym; and Daniel Doudna of Alaska, who spells slowly to avoid mistakes.

The article argues that AI’s promise of personalized learning requires major changes to schooling, especially increased student autonomy. It identifies the prescribed curriculum as the central barrier because it structures school time, teaching, assessment, policy, and student outcomes. Despite reforms, technology adoption, and new pedagogical ideas, schools largely retain traditional structures in which students have little control over what, how, where, or with whom they learn.

Using panarchy theory, the article describes education as a complex, multi-layered system with resilience, adaptability, and limited transformability. It proposes a balanced curriculum that preserves some mandated content while giving students dedicated time for self-directed learning. Rather than transforming whole systems at once, it recommends creating autonomous subsystems within schools where students personalize learning, use AI extensively, and teachers act as coaches and facilitators.

Examples include Innovation, Creativity, and Entrepreneurship Education at Hongfan Middle School in China, related programs in Australia, and school-within-school models such as the Studio School and ScotsX. The article concludes that transformative education ideas need opportunities to survive, be experienced, and potentially spread through the broader system.

The passage lists major 1945 public statements on American foreign policy, including addresses, messages, reports, proclamations, letters, and statements by Presidents Roosevelt and Truman, Secretaries of State Stettinius and Byrnes, Under Secretary Grew, and Cordell Hull. Topics include the State of the Union, Yalta and Potsdam Conferences, United Nations Charter and San Francisco Conference, Germany’s and Japan’s unconditional surrender, atomic energy and Hiroshima, postwar world cooperation, the Council of Foreign Ministers, defense aid, and U.S. policy in China. Citations are primarily to the Department of State Bulletin and Truman’s public papers.

The speaker says the team’s defense has played well all year, crediting both the top four defenders and Yannick Weber and Matt Irwin for handling difficult matchups against teams with strong centers. He discusses learning from Shea Weber, past and present players, and coaches, emphasizing that playoff hockey requires constant learning. He reflects on changing his approach over time, including using off days for team meetings and resetting after games. He describes the environment as businesslike but enjoyable, noting the staff and players’ daily work and appreciation for playing hockey in June. He says both teams are hungry to win the Cup, and the next game will decide who succeeds.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on August 28, 2017, it completed its acquisition of Whole Foods Market, Inc. under a June 15, 2017 merger agreement. Walnut Merger Sub merged into Whole Foods Market, which became a wholly owned Amazon subsidiary. Whole Foods shareholders received $42.00 per share in cash, with equity awards converted or canceled according to the merger terms.
