Yunnan Lucky Air, founded in 2004, grew into a US$104.3 million low-cost airline by 2007, carrying 1.2 million passengers and serving mainly domestic routes from Kunming, Yunnan. It modeled its operations on Southwest Airlines, using one aircraft type, coach-only seating, simple pricing, short-haul point-to-point routes, and secondary cities. However, Chinese regulation limited cost advantages to about 5% below industry average, with fuel, landing fees, aircraft leasing, and taxes heavily controlled by government policy.

China’s airline market was expanding rapidly, with 387 million passengers in 2007 and projected 15% annual air traffic growth through 2020. Competition was also intensifying: 25 airlines operated in China by 2007, including 11 low-cost carriers, while major national airlines held 83.7% of the domestic market. Lucky Air sought new competitive advantages as pricing flexibility and operational savings were constrained.

E-commerce was a major option. China’s Internet population was growing quickly, but online travel remained small, payment systems were underdeveloped, credit card use was low, and Yunnan’s Internet penetration was only 6.8%. Offline agents dominated ticket distribution. Lucky Air sold about 80% of tickets through agents and only 1% directly to consumers through luckyair.net, though its website offered online booking, refunds, ticket validation, travel information, community features, and discounts of 5% to 20%.

Lucky Air’s IT support came from parent Hainan Airlines, and its website was considered advanced, with fully online transactions and credit card verification. The company studied U.S. and European airline e-commerce practices, including customer relationship management, Web 2.0 features, customer reviews, self-service, online payment tools such as PayPal, and targeted offerings for corporate travelers, students, and loyalty program members.

Lucky Air’s executives had to decide whether and how to invest in e-commerce, tourism bundling, customer self-service, or other strategies amid rapid market growth, tight regulation, limited funds, and increasing low-cost competition.

Lattice Semiconductor shows early revenue rebound signs, supported by data center strength but offset by weak automotive and industrial markets. Management cites opportunities in high-end data center chips and emerging robotics, vision, and security markets. Inventories are normalizing, cash generation is strong, debt is absent, and Q3 guidance implies growth. The target price was raised to $70, but the rating remains HOLD due to valuation concerns and limited margin of safety.

Researchers from the University of Washington, Texas A&M University and the Western Australian Museum discovered and named a new genus and species of clingfish, the duckbilled clingfish (Nettorhamphos radula), from specimens preserved in museum jars since the 1970s. Found off Southern Australia in 1977, the finger-sized fish differs from known clingfishes through its broad, flat snout, wider and longer upper jaw, and an estimated 1,800 to 2,300 backward-pointing conical teeth. Because only two specimens are known, researchers avoided dissection and used CT scanning and 3-D printing to study its skeletal and jaw structures noninvasively. The findings were published April 14 in Copeia and highlight the value of museum collections and digital imaging in identifying new species.

President Nixon announced an accelerated withdrawal of U.S. troops from Vietnam, stating that 100,000 more would be brought home between May 1 and December 1, raising total withdrawals to 365,000, over two-thirds of the force present when he took office. He said Vietnamization had succeeded, citing reduced U.S. and South Vietnamese casualties, South Vietnamese military performance, and operations in Cambodia and Laos that he said weakened North Vietnamese capabilities. Nixon reaffirmed the goal of total U.S. withdrawal, preferably through negotiations, and called on Hanoi to agree to a cease-fire, release prisoners of war, and pursue a political settlement. He rejected setting a fixed withdrawal date, arguing it would weaken bargaining power, endanger remaining troops, and reduce incentives for negotiation. He defended the conduct and sacrifices of American service members, said U.S. involvement was ending, and framed his policy as ending the war while preserving South Vietnam’s chance to determine its future and maintaining American credibility.

During finals from Dec. 12 to Dec. 20, Lehigh students face crowded libraries and limited study space. Some students say overcrowding in Fairchild-Martindale and Linderman libraries adds stress and distractions, despite changes to FML’s sixth floor adding tables and open space. Students use alternatives such as academic buildings, cafes, the bookstore, Williams Hall, Rauch Business Center and STEPS. Grant Cummings prefers academic buildings like Maginnes Hall for quieter, private rooms with boards. Rachael Grobman studies early in FML but finds seat-saving frustrating when spaces are left unused. Lehigh extends building hours during finals, with FML open 24 hours from Dec. 11 to Dec. 20, and Packard Lab, the University Center, Rauch and Williams open later than usual. Students can also reserve study rooms through the Center for Career and Professional Development, an option Allie Gleich says reduces stress and includes coffee and snacks.

The passage outlines statistical analysis and reporting specifications for a clinical trial SAP. ECG analyses will tabulate investigator assessments, summarize ECG parameters by visit and treatment, and provide categorical QTcF summaries for thresholds >450, >480, and >500 ms, plus postbaseline changes >30 and >60 ms. Immunogenicity will be analyzed descriptively by treatment group without statistical tests, with ADA incidence based on treatment-induced and treatment-boosted ADA among evaluable patients.

Changes from the protocol include rewording the primary efficacy analysis, adding sensitivity and supportive analyses, and revising secondary efficacy terminology from “within” to “at” specified time points. Appendices define table, figure, and listing formatting rules; handling of missing or incomplete dates using conservative assumptions; derivation formulas for durations, unit conversions, BMI, and change from baseline; and SAS programming QC requirements covering program review, log review, output review, dataset validation, data verification, figures, listings, and documentation.

The planned tables, figures, and listings include patient disposition, demographics, diabetes and medical history, concomitant medications, efficacy analyses for time to plasma glucose recovery and plasma glucose recovery at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes, adverse event summaries, insulin and hypoglycemia procedures, trial medication, rescue glucose infusion, ECG, laboratory tests, vital signs, local tolerability, immunogenicity, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic summaries, and related listings. Tables and figures may be reorganized during programming, and outputs will include source, data cutoff, and run date information.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2015. The company designs, develops, manufactures and sells fully electric vehicles and energy storage products, operating as one reportable segment. Its principal vehicles were the Model S sedan and Model X SUV, with more than 107,000 Model S vehicles delivered worldwide by year-end 2015 and Model X deliveries begun in the third quarter of 2015. Tesla planned to unveil the lower-priced Model 3 in March 2016 and begin production and deliveries in late 2017.

Tesla sells vehicles through company-owned stores, galleries, Service Plus locations and service centers, and operated 208 sales and service-related locations and 118 service locations worldwide as of December 31, 2015. It also operated 584 Supercharger stations and had more than 3,100 Tesla wall connectors installed at over 1,800 destination charging locations. The company manufactures primarily in Fremont and Lathrop, California; Tilburg, Netherlands; and at the Gigafactory near Reno, Nevada, where it began assembling Tesla Energy products in late 2015.

Tesla Energy products include Powerwall for residential and small commercial use and Powerpack for commercial, industrial and utility applications. Tesla’s technology focuses on battery packs, power electronics, dual motor powertrains, vehicle control and infotainment software, autopilot systems, and vehicle engineering.

The filing describes risks including production delays, challenges ramping Model X and developing Model 3, Gigafactory execution risks, supplier dependence, market acceptance of electric vehicles, international expansion, manufacturing costs, lithium-ion battery safety, currency fluctuations, resale value and leasing risks, competition, service requirements, regulatory issues, and reliance on key employees. As of December 31, 2015, Tesla had 13,058 full-time employees.

The Trump administration announced a 2018 Nuclear Posture Review policy to modernise the US nuclear arsenal, including smaller low-yield nuclear options, command and control systems, the nuclear triad, dual-capable aircraft and infrastructure. President Trump said the strategy aims to deter strategic attacks, support allies and maintain commitments to arms control, non-proliferation, the nuclear testing moratorium and countering nuclear terrorism.

Defence Secretary Jim Mattis said Russia and China are developing new nuclear capabilities and modernising conventional forces, challenging US military superiority. The report also cites threats from North Korea and Iran, but does not mention Pakistan. The US plans to modify some submarine-launched ballistic missile warheads for low-yield use and pursue a nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile, partly in response to Russia’s behaviour and treaty non-compliance.

The report says the US will not use or threaten nuclear weapons against compliant non-nuclear NPT states. Nikki Haley and Tom Shannon said the policy addresses current threats, strengthens extended deterrence for US allies, and reaffirms US commitments to allied security.

The federal government agreed to give provinces and territories 75% of tax revenues from legalized marijuana sales for two years, with Ottawa keeping 25% up to $100 million annually and any excess going to provinces and territories. Finance Minister Bill Morneau said the arrangement will help provinces manage costs and work with municipalities, which have sought revenue for policing and administrative expenses. Ottawa expects marijuana taxes to generate up to $400 million in the first two years and will reassess the framework in December 2018. The original federal proposal was a 50-50 split, which provinces rejected. Provinces may also apply markups outside the taxation model. Ministers also discussed equalization payments, the Canada Pension Plan review, the global economy, and improving corporate ownership information sharing to combat tax evasion, money laundering, and terrorist financing.

Scientists increasingly argue that ultraprocessed foods can have addictive properties similar to alcohol, nicotine or opioids, producing cravings, loss of control, withdrawal and tolerance. These products are often engineered from concentrated sugars, fats and salts with additives that enhance flavor, texture and appeal, while containing little whole food. In the United States, they account for more than half of average calorie intake.

Researchers use systems such as NOVA to classify foods by processing level, while related work examines “hyperpalatable” foods designed to be especially appealing. Studies suggest ultraprocessed foods can alter reward-related brain systems involving dopamine, serotonin and opioids. Research has also found stronger neural reactions to food cues after daily consumption of a high-fat, high-sugar dessert, and preliminary findings suggest young adults may eat more ultraprocessed food even without hunger.

The idea of food addiction has gained acceptance since nutrition and addiction researchers began formally discussing it in 2007. Using the Yale Food Addiction Scale, studies estimate that about 14 percent of adults and 12 percent of children meet criteria for food addiction. Researchers say some people show substance-use-disorder-like symptoms around ultraprocessed foods.

Policy responses are emerging, including federal scrutiny, proposed school restrictions, labeling efforts and discussion of regulation. Some researchers argue that focusing only on individual choice ignores how these foods are designed and marketed, while others point to taxes, warning labels and marketing limits, such as those used in Chile, as possible approaches.

ANU and the Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris studied alumino-silicate glass used in mobile screens, finding that atoms such as sodium and potassium form clusters or channels rather than distributing randomly. Researchers say these microscopic structures, along with calcium and magnesium, affect glass flexibility and fracture resistance, potentially helping manufacturers develop more shatter-resistant phone screens.

Moody’s is expected to keep South Africa’s last major investment-grade rating this week after Cyril Ramaphosa replaced Jacob Zuma, according to all 15 Bloomberg survey respondents. The rand and business confidence have improved, but risks remain from possible budget slippage, weak growth and the ANC’s push for land expropriation without compensation. Moody’s placed South Africa on review for downgrade in November and rates it one step above junk, while S&P and Fitch already rate its debt as junk. A Moody’s downgrade could remove South Africa from major bond indexes, trigger large outflows and raise borrowing costs. Analysts said Ramaphosa’s presidency has boosted confidence, but policy execution and land reform could affect future ratings.

The passage presents AMR-EnsembleNet, a framework for antimicrobial resistance prediction from whole-genome SNP data. It addresses limitations of culture-based diagnostics, gene-hunting approaches, and standard machine learning models that ignore SNP sequence context. The method combines a lightweight sequence-aware 1D CNN, designed to learn local SNP motifs, with XGBoost, which captures non-local feature interactions, using soft voting.

The study used the public GieSSen dataset of 809 E. coli isolates with 60,936 ordered SNP features and binary resistance labels for Ciprofloxacin, Cefotaxime, Ceftazidime, and Gentamicin. Models were evaluated on held-out test sets using accuracy, MCC, macro F1, and resistant-class precision, recall, and F1-score, with class weighting for imbalanced tasks.

Results showed strong performance for all models on Ciprofloxacin, with AMR-EnsembleNet matching the best accuracy and slightly improving MCC. For Cefotaxime, the ensemble achieved the best overall metrics and highest resistant-class recall. For Ceftazidime, Random Forest performed best, while the ensemble provided a balanced second-best result. For highly imbalanced Gentamicin, the 1D CNN achieved high recall, and AMR-EnsembleNet produced the best MCC and macro F1 by balancing recall and precision.

SHAP analysis of XGBoost identified influential SNPs mapped to known AMR-associated genes, including gyrB, marR, rpsL, parC, ampC, acrD, and ftsI, supporting the biological relevance of the predictions. The authors conclude that combining sequence-aware CNN features with XGBoost improves robustness for genomic AMR prediction and may support rapid diagnostics and surveillance. The dataset and code are publicly available.

The dollar rose broadly as traders reduced bearish positions following easing rhetoric over North Korea and weak inflation concerns. Analysts said the lack of further U.S.-North Korea tensions and Xi Jinping’s call for a peaceful resolution supported the currency. The dollar index gained 0.3 percent, and the dollar rose against the yen and Swiss franc. Gains in U.S. and global stocks also helped sentiment. Investors awaited U.S. retail sales data for further indications on inflation.

The speaker outlines the responsibilities of the presidency and the main priorities of the incoming administration. He pledges to maintain and enforce reforms begun by his predecessor against abuses by large railroad and industrial combinations, while seeking clearer laws that protect legitimate business and improve enforcement through departmental reorganization.

He identifies tariff revision as urgent and plans to call Congress into a special session to revise the Dingley Act, aiming for adequate revenue, protection for domestic labor and industry, and possible maximum tariffs against countries with unfair trade policies. Because revenues have fallen after the 1907 financial panic, he warns against continued deficits and recommends a graduated inheritance tax if import duties are insufficient.

The address supports necessary government spending for agriculture, business regulation, conservation, waterways, the Panama Canal, the army, navy, and coast defenses, while also calling for economy where possible. It argues that military preparedness supports peace, protects American interests, and strengthens foreign policy, including in the Orient and under the Monroe Doctrine.

The speaker calls for protection of American citizens abroad and federal authority to enforce treaty rights of aliens in the United States. He supports monetary and banking reform, a postal savings bank, expanded foreign trade, steamship lines to South America, and trade benefits from the Panama Canal. He reports satisfactory canal progress and pledges to continue construction under the adopted lock-canal plan.

He discusses Porto Rico and the Philippines, expecting improved Philippine business conditions through free trade with the United States. He expresses hope for better relations between the South and other regions, addresses the status of Black Americans under the constitutional amendments, supports fair voting qualifications consistent with the Fifteenth Amendment, and urges sympathy, aid, education, and careful recognition through appointments.

On labor, he supports laws improving liability, compensation, child labor protections, arbitration, and railway safety. He favors further safety legislation but opposes removing courts’ power to issue injunctions in labor disputes or legalizing secondary boycotts, while supporting statutory limits to prevent abuse of temporary restraining orders. He closes by asking for public support and divine aid in carrying out his duties.

Saskatoon city staff recommend a $1.2-million, two-year plan to remove and replace about 1,000 black ash trees damaged by cottony ash psyllids, a European lice species. Insecticide treatments have only delayed removals and did not slow tree decline this spring. The pest, first seen in 2006 and reappearing in 2015, has already led to removals in several city districts. Saskatoon has more than 105,000 inventoried trees, 27 per cent ash species. Funding is identified for the first year, but not the second.

This study investigates liquid-assisted capillary densification of electrospun polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofiber yarns using water or ethanol rolling, followed by drying and, in some cases, thermal annealing at 110 °C. The goal was to improve yarn mechanics by increasing fiber compaction, alignment, and inter-fiber adhesion.

Tensile testing showed that treated yarns had higher modulus, strength, and peak load than as-spun yarns, but reduced ductility. Water-treated yarns generally outperformed ethanol-treated yarns, attributed to stronger capillary compaction and slower evaporation. Heat treatment further increased stiffness and strength but promoted brittle fracture and reduced failure strain. Smaller-diameter yarns showed markedly higher modulus and peak stress, with yarns below 10 µm approaching reported single PAN nanofiber performance.

SEM-based image analysis showed that treatment improved fiber alignment and packing density. Peak load correlated strongly with both coherency-based alignment and in-plane packing density, and a combined regression model explained more variance than either descriptor alone. A stochastic mean-field constitutive model incorporating fiber recruitment, failure, orientation averaging, load-transfer efficiency, and post-failure load retention reproduced the observed stress–strain behavior and linked fitted parameters to SEM-derived structure metrics.

The study concludes that simple water-assisted capillary densification, with optional thermal annealing, provides a scalable route to strengthen electrospun PAN yarns by improving alignment, packing density, and inter-fiber load transfer.

Physicists developed a method to generate and self-organize immiscible liquid droplets into defined layered patterns, as reported in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Using mixtures of oil, water, and alcohol in confined geometries, the team found that de-mixing begins at the edge and moves inward, forming stripes or nested layers dependent on de-mixing speed rather than droplet size. Tunable experimental parameters allow control of emulsion structure and step-wise release of inner droplets, with potential applications in pharmaceuticals and consumer products.

The Fifth Circuit affirmed Jose Verastegui’s guilty-plea convictions and concurrent 120-month sentences for being a felon in possession of a firearm and unlawful reentry of a deported alien. The court held that Verastegui failed to show the district court abused its discretion in departing upward from the 63-to-78-month advisory guideline range or that the non-Guideline sentence was unreasonable. It also found his challenges to a guideline adjustment, the constitutionality of 18 U.S.C. § 922(g), and the constitutionality of 8 U.S.C. § 1326(b) were foreclosed by binding precedent, though raised to preserve further review.

OnePlus has officially released Android Nougat updates for the OnePlus 3 and 3T, rolling out globally with wider availability expected soon. The OxygenOS 4.0 update includes redesigned notifications and settings, multi-window support, direct replies, Doze on the Go, and other tweaks. Users can manually check for the update in Settings.

Gary Gensler begins by commenting on student papers, emphasizing critical reasoning tied to the relevant class topic rather than summaries of earlier readings or answers to study questions. He previews upcoming guest sessions, including one involving Jeff Sprecher of Intercontinental Exchange and Kelly Loeffler of Bakkt on payment systems.

The lecture focuses on finance, financial institutions, regulation, technology, credit, risk, crises, and blockchain opportunities. Gensler describes finance as allocating, pricing, and moving money and risk, with intermediaries positioned at the “neck of the hourglass.” Key financial functions include investment, credit, payments, liquidity, and risk transformation. Major sectors include commercial banks, investment banks and brokers, insurance, asset management, collective investment vehicles, exchanges, and clearinghouses.

Discussion of readings covers financial consolidation, income disparities, economic rents, regulation and deregulation, Citigroup, and Sheila Bair’s view that Citi might have been restructured to reduce moral hazard. Gensler notes that finance has long been regulated, citing historical examples such as interest-rate rules, debtor prisons, bankruptcy law, and modern reforms like Dodd-Frank. He frames financial regulation around financial stability, consumer and investor protection, and prevention of illicit activity.

Gensler highlights that ledgers are central to finance and blockchain. Payment systems transfer value by authorizing, clearing, recording, and finally settling changes to ledgers. Blockchain may matter because it can provide faster final settlement.

He argues finance has always had a close relationship with technology, from coinage and paper money to telegraphs, IBM systems, cryptography, cloud computing, AI, machine learning, open APIs, biometrics, robotic process automation, chatbots, and blockchain. He notes that legacy systems in incumbent financial firms may create opportunities for disruptors.

On credit, Gensler defines it as borrowing something of value with an agreement to return it later. He presents U.S. debt as about 350% of GDP, with credit spread across government, commercial, financial, and household sectors. He notes the large U.S. bond and equity markets, household mortgage debt, student debt, credit cards, auto loans, and home equity debt.

Risk management topics include market risk, credit risk, underwriting risk, liquidity risk, funding risk, settlement risk, model and correlation risk, operational and cyber risk, legal and compliance risk, and reputational risk. Gensler says liquidity, funding, settlement, and correlation risks often contribute to crises.

He summarizes the 2008 financial crisis as involving weak mortgage underwriting, predatory lending, a housing bubble, easy credit, derivatives, leverage, poor risk management, and asymmetric incentives. He says the financial system is stronger in some ways than ten years earlier, especially through higher bank capital, but also more concentrated and still vulnerable.

He concludes that blockchain opportunities in finance may arise where systems are data-intensive, legacy-based, rent-heavy, risk-concentrated, or costly, while cautioning that not all blockchain ideas are sound.

Enjifit, a New York City-based workout partner app founded by Nicole Garcia, launched for iOS on July 3, 2018. The app connects users with nearby workout partners or personal trainers based on goals, interests and location. Features include profiles, user filtering, in-app messaging, workout reminders, accomplishment tracking and posting workout sessions for others to join. It is free to download, with a PRO subscription for trainers and nutritionists to feature services. Enjifit held a July 1 launch event in New York City and plans to release an Android version soon.

The lecture explains that the nuclear force binds nuclei and is a residual interaction between quarks in different hadrons, making it difficult to fully describe because many quarks, protons, and neutrons are involved. Experimental understanding comes from nucleon-nucleon scattering, nuclear binding energies and mass measurements, and nuclear structure data such as energy levels, spin, parity, and moments.

Experiments show that the nuclear force depends on distance, spin, and angular momentum, with spin-orbit and tensor components. It is short range, vanishing beyond about 2 femtometers, and strongly repulsive below about 0.5 femtometers. Constant binding energy per nucleon suggests nucleons mainly interact with immediate neighbors, and nuclear densities indicate dense packing.

The force appears charge independent, meaning it does not depend on whether nucleons are protons or neutrons once electromagnetic effects are removed. This can be tested by comparing proton-proton, proton-neutron, and neutron-neutron scattering, and by studying mirror nuclei such as helium-3 and tritium. Mirror nuclei show similar binding energies after Coulomb corrections and comparable excitation energy levels.

Independent developer Milky Tea announced HyperBrawl Tournament will launch on Steam Early Access in June 2017. The game is a combat sports arena title combining no-rules, high-speed handball with PvP combat. Players choose from 10 warriors and 10 weapons, battle across six arenas, complete eight mini games, unlock content, and play 1v1 or 2v2 locally or online with up to four players.

Pepsi Nigeria’s No Shakin’ Carry Go campaign will send 10 fans on an all-expense-paid 3-day VVIP trip to the One Africa Music Fest in Dubai, including opportunities to meet Pepsi stars Wizkid, Tiwa Savage, Davido and Tekno.

An Accenture study found investors across ages and wealth levels prefer hybrid wealth management combining robo advisers with human expertise. Respondents favored hybrid firms for low-cost digital tools and human help in complex situations. The findings come as firms expand data-driven investing while some robo advisers add access to human advice.

Tech megacaps lost $770 billion in market value Friday after President Trump threatened major tariff increases on Chinese imports, later announcing a planned 100% tariff and Nov. 1 export controls on critical software. Nvidia, Amazon and Tesla fell about 5%, pushing the Nasdaq down 3.6% and the S&P 500 down 2.7%, their worst days since April. Nvidia’s market cap dropped nearly $229 billion, Microsoft’s by $85 billion, Amazon’s by $121 billion and Tesla’s by $71 billion.

The disclosure describes training and using a machine-learned depth estimation model that generates a depth map from a single color input image. The model may be trained using monocular video, stereoscopic image pairs, or both, without relying on detection-and-ranging ground truth. Training involves extracting depth maps and poses from images, generating synthetic frames by projecting images using depth and pose information, and refining model parameters based on photometric reconstruction error.

The training system uses an input-scale occlusion and motion-aware loss function. The loss may use the minimum photometric reconstruction error from adjacent monocular frames or paired stereoscopic images to reduce artifacts from occlusions and image borders. It may also use upsampled depth features to avoid depth upsampling artifacts and apply masks to discount static features that could distort depth estimates. A depth-pose hybrid model may share parameters between depth and pose estimation to reduce computation.

The trained depth estimation model can run on a client device, receive an image or video frame of a real-world scene, and output a depth map. In a location-based parallel reality game, the depth map may be used to generate and display augmented virtual content that interacts with the scene, such as appearing behind real objects or changing size with apparent distance. The system may include client devices, cameras, positioning modules, game servers, databases, and networked modules for game content, events, data collection, and depth model training.

Kennesaw State won the 2017 ASUN Championship at The Legends at Chateau Elan with a 1-under 863, defeating Lipscomb by one shot after entering the final round with a 10-shot lead. The Owls secured their seventh straight NCAA Regional berth, led by Jake Fendt and Pablo Rodriguez-Tabernero, who tied for second at 2 under. Lipscomb’s Dawson Armstrong won the individual title at 6-under 210, becoming the program’s first ASUN individual men’s conference champion. Armstrong, the ASUN Player of the Year, earned his sixth college win and third of the 2016-17 season. Jacksonville finished third and North Florida fourth, with both likely to receive regional bids.

Episode four of UFC 216 Embedded follows fighters preparing for UFC 216, including Demetrious Johnson shopping, Ray Borg training, Derrick Lewis doing a mock weigh-in, Tony Ferguson and Kevin Lee activities, and media day faceoffs.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on April 13, 2022, it closed the sale of seven series of notes totaling $12.75 billion in principal, with maturities from 2024 to 2062 and interest rates from 2.730% to 4.100%. The aggregate public offering price was $12.719 billion, with estimated net proceeds of about $12.692 billion before offering expenses. The notes were issued under a 2012 indenture, supplemented on April 13, 2022, with Computershare Trust Company as successor trustee. The filing also lists related underwriting, indenture, note form, legal opinion, and consent exhibits.

North Wales Police are seeking witnesses after an attempted kidnapping of a woman in her 30s on Sisson Street, Rhyl, at 8.25am. She escaped unharmed after a man in his 40s, described as of oriental appearance, tried to get her into a car before leaving in a silver vehicle. Police said no child was involved, correcting earlier council alerts to schools and parents. Anyone with information is asked to contact police or Crimestoppers quoting reference V151756.

Pupils appealed to President Mnangagwa to suspend the 2018 November public examinations, citing inadequate preparation caused by election-related disruptions and teachers’ absence on ZEC duties. Permanent Secretary Dr Sylvia Utete-Masango said the appeal was made during the President’s meeting with Child Parliamentarians, but did not disclose his response. She said schools should arrange holiday lessons through district and provincial offices, as the second term will close early for elections and the third term will open a week early to recover lost learning time.

NASA’s New Horizons, after its 2015 Pluto flyby, was extended to study Kuiper Belt Objects and is set to encounter 2014 MU69 on Jan. 1, 2019. The object, about 1.6 billion km beyond Pluto, will be the farthest object ever visited by a spacecraft and may be an elongated body or a close/contact binary. NASA and the New Horizons team held a public naming campaign hosted by the SETI Institute, drawing 115,000 participants and 34,000 nominations. The nickname “Ultima Thule,” meaning beyond the known world, was selected as a fitting working name. A formal name will be submitted to the International Astronomical Union after the flyby, depending on MU69’s nature.

Attacking runs in soccer are off-the-ball movements by offensive players into open space among, between, or behind defenders to receive passes and support attacks. Players must recognize or create open space, choose suitable runs, separate from defenders, time movement to avoid offside, receive appropriate passes, and communicate with the ball carrier. Common runs include bending, checking, diagonal, hooking, inside, lateral, onside, outlet, sideline, straight, through, and wide runs. Effective runs depend on both the runner completing the movement and the passer recognizing and rewarding it with a timely, accurate pass. Communication may be verbal, visual, or through eye contact. Coaching progression can begin with cone demonstrations, then add passes, defenders, supporting attackers, and full movement. Good attacking play requires players to keep moving, support the ball carrier, and avoid simply watching the ball.

A moderator interviews NHL draft prospects James van Riemsdyk, Kyle Turris, Patrick Kane, Sam Gagner, Keaton Ellerby, and Karl Alzner. Topics include their hometowns, college plans, family influences, favorite teams, playing styles, coaches, international tournaments, potential NHL draft outcomes, and connections to current or former NHL players. The players are congratulated and wished luck in Columbus, with family introductions and media interviews mentioned.

The passage explains how to attack a Diamond & One defense using the “Clock” 1-3-1 offense by placing the star player in the middle to create open shots, layups, offensive putbacks, and one-on-one post opportunities. It outlines rotations involving corner passes, basket cuts, ball reversals, post feeds, post rolls, and dribble clears, with continuity continuing whenever the ball goes to the corner. High-post triangle action begins when the star receives the ball, creating drive, drop-pass, kick-out, and post-flash options. The offense also emphasizes offensive rebounding through inside triangle positioning and possible back screens. Successful implementation requires execution, coordination, defensive recognition, communication, timing, experience, scouting, and varying alignments to attack weak defenders. The Diamond & One defense is described as four defenders in a diamond zone with one defender denying the opponent’s top scorer.

This study used exome sequencing data from 454,803 UK Biobank participants and 173,585 Geisinger MyCode participants to identify clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) and investigate its germline genetic causes and clinical consequences. The authors identified 27,331 CHIP carriers in UK Biobank and 12,877 in Geisinger, with DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, PPM1D, and TP53 as the most commonly mutated genes. CHIP prevalence rose with age, reaching about 15% by age 75, and was associated with older age and heavy smoking.

Genome-wide association analysis in UK Biobank identified 27 common-variant loci associated with CHIP, 24 of them novel, with replication support in Geisinger. Rare variant and gene burden analyses identified CHIP associations involving loci and genes including ATM, CHEK2, CTC1, CLPTM1L, and KDELC2, with evidence suggesting germline origins. CHIP gene-specific analyses found shared, distinct, and opposing genetic effects across CHIP subtypes. DNMT3A-CHIP had the most associated loci, including protective associations at PARP1 and LY75. The TCL1A locus showed opposing effects, increasing DNMT3A-CHIP risk while decreasing risk for TET2-CHIP, ASXL1-CHIP, and other subtypes.

Comparisons with other clonal hematopoiesis phenotypes showed CHIP was largely distinct from mosaic chromosomal alterations but enriched among their carriers. CHIP shared genetic risk factors with mosaic loss of Y and X chromosomes. Exome-wide analyses of non-CHIP phenotypes identified rare variant and gene burden associations involving genes such as KNTC1, TIE1, PTPRF, TM2D3, GIGYF1, RC3H1, PRR14L, DCLRE1B, PARN, and CTC1.

Phenome-wide analyses linked CHIP subtypes to hematologic, cardiovascular, neoplastic, infectious, renal, smoking-related, endocrine, ophthalmologic, and body-mass traits. DNMT3A-CHIP and TET2-CHIP often showed opposing associations with blood cell measures and adiposity-related traits. High variant allele fraction CHIP was associated with COVID-19 hospitalization and severe COVID-19.

Longitudinal analyses found high variant allele fraction CHIP carriers had elevated risks of cardiovascular disease, blood cancers, myeloid cancers, lung cancer, prostate cancer, and all-cause mortality. Cardiovascular risk was driven mainly by TET2-CHIP. Blood cancer risk was highest for TET2 mutation carriers, while DNMT3A mutations showed more modest risk unless accompanied by additional CHIP mutations. CHIP-associated lung cancer risk was observed in both smokers and non-smokers. A DNMT3A-CHIP polygenic risk score was associated with myeloid cancer, lung cancer, prostate cancer, and multiple CHIP subtypes, but not cardiovascular disease or all-cause mortality.

The authors conclude that CHIP is a heterogeneous group of somatic mutation-driven subtypes with shared and distinct germline genetic causes and clinical risk profiles.

The authors argue that education reforms, tools and policies often stall because leaders invest heavily in program design but little in shaping the public narrative around them. Without a clear story, communities interpret new initiatives through familiar concerns such as top-down control, data risks and technology replacing teachers. Examples include backlash to accountability policies, data platforms and AI tools.

They propose treating narrative development like research and development: frame the core story, test it with audiences, iterate based on feedback and scale it through toolkits, visuals, language and training. For standards, testing or AI pilots, leaders should map local mindsets, use shared values, provide concrete examples, explain how the change works, center teachers and students, and address risks such as privacy, bias and misuse. The authors say trust depends on involving communities, acknowledging past harms and building narratives that make innovations understandable, trustworthy and adoptable.

Output capacitance is determined by the greater of calculations for worst-case load transient voltage deviation and output voltage ripple, using targets of 2.5% and 2% of output voltage. At least 1.3 mF is required, with derating for aging, temperature, and DC bias. Space-grade designs may need more capacitance for radiation-induced SET mitigation; the example uses about 2.3 mF. An optional output filter with added inductance and ceramic capacitance can reduce ripple, with resonance set above crossover frequency and below switching frequency and the bulk capacitance ESR zero. Damping may be added if high-frequency peaking occurs. The converter’s cycle-by-cycle current limit begins near 35 A, giving about 45% margin over the 24.25 A peak inductor current at maximum load.

Quantum-correlated pairs are important for quantum information, including computation, communication, and metrology. Phonons are promising solid-state quantum resources because they can coherently interact with varied quantum systems, but optically generating nonclassical phonon pairs remains difficult due to weak single-photon optomechanical coupling and limited high-order nonlinearities. The passage presents a protocol using an optomechanical crystal nanobeam cavity and effective high-order optomechanical nonlinearity, where simultaneous Stokes and anti-Stokes interactions in one pulse generate degenerate correlated phonon pairs through an optomechanical spontaneous four-wave mixing process. A second red-detuned pulse retrieves the pairs, and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality verifies their quantum correlations.

The TPS7H500x-SP series uses fixed-frequency, peak current mode control for space-grade DC-DC converter designs. The controller regulates converter peak current and duty cycle by comparing sensed external switch current against a stepped-down COMP voltage and turning off the power switch when the threshold is reached.

The devices are radiation-hardness-assured current-mode PWM controllers intended for use with external gate drivers and support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz. They can be used in topologies such as buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge converters. A design example describes a synchronous push-pull converter using GaN devices with the TPS7H5001-SP, including component selections for switching frequency, feedback resistors, dead time, leading-edge blanking, soft start, transformer design, switching and synchronous rectifier FETs, RCD clamp, output inductor, output capacitance and filtering, current sensing, hiccup timing, compensation, and slope compensation.

The example design uses a 500-kHz switching frequency, 5-V output, approximately 25-ns dead time, 50-ns initial leading-edge blanking, a 33-nF soft-start capacitor, 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance, 0.47-µH output inductor, about 2.3 mF output capacitance, 7.5-Ω current sense resistor, 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation, and a 102-kΩ slope compensation resistor.

The controllers operate from a 4-V to 14-V input supply and require proper bypassing, including at least 0.1 µF from VIN to AVSS. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switch-node area and high-current loops, routing sensitive signals away from noisy traces, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, filtering current sense signals if needed, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS with multiple vias. The document also lists related documentation, revision history, mechanical and packaging information, ESD cautions, and TI warranty and resource disclaimers.

This work investigates improving electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) patterns captured with a 256×256 pixel Timepix-based direct electron detector using a sub-pixel shift-and-add reconstruction method. EBSD patterns were collected from single-crystal silicon using a high energy threshold, and multiple spatially offset patterns were registered, warped, and summed to create a super-resolution pattern. Pattern quality was evaluated using Fourier-based signal-to-noise analysis and compared with longer single-frame exposures, frame integration, camera retraction data, and simulations.

The method increased the signal-to-noise ratio from about 30 to 70 at an effective exposure time of around 1 second and produced patterns with finer angular information than equivalent-dose single exposures. The reconstructed pattern showed features comparable to camera-retracted data and BWKD simulations, including HOLZ rings and fine band structures. The authors conclude that sub-pixel shift-and-add reconstruction can more than double EBSD pattern signal-to-noise without hardware modification and may support improved pattern analysis, indexing, and high-angular-resolution applications.

Red Same, Red Opposite, and Red Rover are SOS half-court disruptions used briefly to change tempo, create easy baskets, disrupt set offenses, or remove the ball from a penetrating point guard. They differ by which defender initiates the trap. The ballhandler is trapped near the front-court sideline hash mark, while non-trapping defenders form Triangle “I” positions. When the ball is passed out, rotations occur as it leaves the passer’s hands, ending in coach-designated Base Go Red or Base Go I.

In Red Mid Same, X1 and X3 trap O1. In Red Opposite, X1 and X2 trap. In Red Rover 4, X4 is designated to trap with X1. In Red Rover 5, X5 traps with X1. After passes to O2, defenders rotate to the nearest offensive players, deny returns, protect lob and post options, and apply SNUGGLE, SMOTHER, Helpside “I,” or post-fronting positions. If O2 penetrates to the free-throw-line extended, Base Go I or Base Go Red is initiated; if O2 feeds the low post, Post Front trap rotations occur where specified.

The report reviews newcomer education in California using state data, district interviews, and literature, and recommends actions to improve outcomes. “Newcomers” are recently arrived students in U.S. schools, often with limited English proficiency, socioeconomic disadvantage, trauma, interrupted schooling, or unmet social-service needs. They are commonly treated as English learners, but their needs differ from those of typical English learners, and they lack safeguards comparable to those for foster youth or special education students.

California schools often lack the expertise, resources, systems, community partnerships, and funding needed to serve newcomers consistently. In 2020–21, California had 151,996 Title III Immigrant Students, or 2.5 percent of K–12 enrollment. Fifty-eight percent were enrolled in five counties: Los Angeles, Orange, San Diego, Alameda, and Santa Clara. Sixty-seven percent were socioeconomically disadvantaged. Less than half had Spanish as a home language, and the group showed significant language diversity. About 19 percent were in high school. Statewide data on students with interrupted formal education are unavailable.

Federal law requires districts to provide English learners and immigrant students meaningful access to public education, but the report states many districts may not meet the Castañeda standard for adequate English learner instruction for newcomers. Lawsuits are uncommon due to family concerns, district resource constraints, and political considerations.

Funding sources include California’s Local Control Funding Formula, the CalNEW program, the Opportunities for Youth pilot, Title III funds, the Title III Immigrant Student Program, and refugee-related federal programs. The report notes that Title III Immigrant Student Program funding is limited and uneven, with most newcomer students unsupported by that grant in 2022–23. California’s overall education funding and state-level instructional capacity are described as constrained.

The report identifies effective newcomer supports, including specialized instruction, newcomer high schools or programs, modified schedules, extended learning time, integrated language and content instruction, translanguaging, collaboration, oral language development, appropriate curricula, educator training, planning time, welcoming school environments, cultural orientation, social activities, robust intake, transcript articulation, and more nuanced assessment. It also emphasizes social services, family engagement, nonprofit and government partnerships, legal services, material supports, and mental health services.

Recommendations include building state leadership capacity, institutionalizing collaboration between the California Department of Education and Department of Social Services, collaborating nationally, adding newcomers and students with interrupted formal education to state data systems, continuing Opportunities for Youth, adjusting funding for late-arriving newcomers, addressing newcomers in instructional frameworks, investing in open curriculum and instructional resources, supporting research, and advocating for federal action on data systems and Title III funding rules.

Security chief Pierre-Yves Thouault said 23,000 police, 6,000 firemen and private agents would manage crowds, with special attention to mountain finishes such as Alpe d’Huez. Froome, cleared after an abnormal Salbutamol test from the Tour of Spain, is seeking a fifth Tour title and a Giro-Tour double.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated February 17, 2020, reporting that it issued an update to its quarterly guidance for the second quarter ending March 28, 2020. The update is attached as Exhibit 99.1, with Inline XBRL cover page data as Exhibit 104. The report was signed by CFO Luca Maestri.

An Enron email forwards a class action complaint filed in San Diego County by Pamela R. Gordon against Reliant, Southern, NRG, Dynegy, AES, Williams, Duke Energy, and others. The World Long Drive Association will hold the inaugural Atlantic City Boardwalk Bash, in partnership with the New Jersey CRDA, June 4-5 at Atlantic City Country Club, with live Golf Channel coverage from 6-8 p.m. ET on June 5. The event is the third WLDA competition in six weeks televised live on Golf Channel. Bald eagles have returned in large numbers to the La Crosse area along the Mississippi River, becoming a sign of spring and a conservation success. After DDT decimated populations, the pesticide was banned in 1972 and protections helped them recover from one nesting pair to over 300. The river refuge provides ideal fish-rich habitat, and younger eagles are often mistaken for other birds.

A car bomb and gunmen attacked a ministry compound in Kabul. Officials said 10 militants were involved, at least one policeman was killed and five were wounded. Attackers failed to breach key buildings, and Afghan forces quickly subdued the assault. Daesh claimed responsibility.

The Trump administration is considering selling parts of the $1.6 trillion federal student loan portfolio while pursuing plans to shut down the Education Department and move loans to another agency. Such sales are legally allowed only if they do not cost taxpayers money. Borrower advocates criticized the discussions, citing concerns about reduced protections.

Residents of Oshiyie, led by Abusuapayin Paul Ameni Annoh of the Nii Afadi Annoh Royal Family faction, petitioned the Inspector General of Police over unrest linked to an 18-year chieftaincy dispute with the Kofi Akrashie faction, currently before the Ngleshie Alata Traditional Council. The second annual Addiction & Recovery Awareness MusicFest will be held July 7 from noon to 10 p.m. at Buck Miller Arena in Westminster, offering a sober entertainment option for people in addiction recovery. The event features local music acts, food vendors, and speakers including Brandon Novak and Tim Ryan. Tickets cost $20 for general admission and $50 for VIP. Proceeds will benefit Rising Above Addiction, the Push HOPE Project, and the Up and Out Foundation. Founder Jesse Tomlin said the festival aims to raise money, provide fellowship, and show that recovery can include sober fun. Last year’s event raised more than $6,000 and drew nearly 600 attendees.

Backtesting simulates trading strategies on historical market data to assess potential profitability, risk, and robustness before using real capital. Reliable results depend on accurate, comprehensive, and relevant data, including delisted or failed assets to reduce survivorship bias. Traders use backtesting to define strategy parameters, evaluate drawdowns and volatility, incorporate market conditions, and refine risk management.

Effective backtesting should account for transaction costs, slippage, leverage, execution delays, and changing market dynamics. Common safeguards include diverse datasets, out-of-sample testing, sensitivity analysis, forward testing, paper trading, and scenario analysis to reduce overfitting and other biases. Key metrics include net profit, percent profitability, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, and other risk-adjusted performance measures.

Backtesting tools should be user-friendly, customizable, integrate accurate historical data, and support performance analysis. The passage discusses applications across equities, derivatives, options, futures, CFDs, cryptocurrency, and forex, each with specific challenges such as volatility, leverage, data quality, implied volatility, trading expenses, and psychological pressures absent from simulations. Backtesting is useful for strategy development and confidence, but positive results do not guarantee future success because market conditions change.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired by email while observing Rosh Hashanah after conservatives publicized alleged past blog posts criticizing President Donald Trump. The Miami Herald reported he is among several federal prosecutors fired by Trump’s Justice Department who were viewed as at odds with Trump or his agenda. The DOJ has also fired three Southern District of Florida prosecutors who worked with former special counsel Jack Smith. Smith recently criticized dismissals of career public servants and attacks on the rule of law.

The Missouri Court of Appeals considered a creditor’s motion to execute against stockholder Gerard B. Allen for unpaid stock of the Illinois and St. Louis Bridge Company. The court held that corporate creditors are preferred over stockholders, and stockholders may not retain personal profits from corporate transactions that diminish assets or increase liabilities before creditors are paid. Allen was liable for unpaid stock represented by a forty percent credit on bonus shares and for the amount he realized from second-mortgage bonds issued to stockholders without valuable consideration. However, the court held that liability under the statute is measured by the shares owned when the creditor’s motion is filed after notice, not when execution against the corporation is returned nulla bona. Because the lower court used the earlier date, the judgment was reversed and remanded.

The coach praised a young player’s conscientious approach, talent, and improved productivity after reduced minutes helped him regain energy and confidence. He emphasized playing the right way, limiting risk, winning puck battles, and trusting instincts. He said Sidney Crosby helps young players feel comfortable and confident. The team values lineup balance, depth, and flexibility, with players moved to create advantageous matchups. The coach highlighted resilience, sacrifice on the penalty kill, daily practice, video preparation, efficient breakouts, and in-game adjustments. He described Phil Kessel and Evgeni Malkin as dynamic elite players who are most effective when strong away from the puck. He also noted one player’s energy, skating, forechecking, physicality, and versatility across the lineup.

The 3-3-5 defense uses three defensive linemen, three linebackers, and five defensive backs, emphasizing pressure, speed, athleticism, and coverage disguise. It is used both as a sub package and, by some coordinators, as a base defense. The scheme favors smaller, faster players, with some coordinators moving larger linebackers to the line and bigger defensive backs to linebacker to maximize movement, stunts, and blitzing.

Its strengths include flexibility, multiple coverages from the same pre-snap shell, varied pressure sources, easy adjustment to formations, and the ability to create different fronts through slants and blitzes. Its weaknesses include vulnerability on the edges, especially against plays such as buck sweep and outside zone, where offenses can gain numbers advantages and force defenders to beat blocks in space.

Offenses commonly attack the 3-3-5 through seams in the passing game and off the edge in the run game. Four verticals can challenge cover 3, and trips formations can reduce box defenders and stress the boundary side. Common blitzes include the Sam blitz and SAW blitz, which use slanting or pinching defensive linemen with stack backers or overhangs as rushers. Common coverages include cover 1 and cover 3, both using a one-high safety look.

Joe Lee Dunn is credited as the inventor of the 3-3-5. Coaches and teams associated with it include Matt Campbell at Iowa State, Tony Gibson at North Carolina State, and Tim Racki at the prep level.

The passage describes dry electrode films for energy storage devices that include microparticulate non-fibrillizable binders, particularly particles about 0.5–40 μm, combined with active materials and fibrillizable binders. The films may be free-standing, self-supporting, solvent-free, and suitable for devices such as lithium ion batteries. Example binders include cellulose derivatives such as carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and fibrillizable polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE). The disclosed films may reduce defects such as holes, cracks, and surface pits, and may improve tensile strength, processability, cohesion, adhesion, and specific capacity.

Methods include jet milling a dry non-fibrillizable binder to reduce particle size, combining it with a fibrillizable binder and active material, and calendering the mixture into a free-standing dry electrode film. Another method uses parallel processing of bulk active material with non-fibrillizable binder and structural binder mixtures, followed by nondestructive mixing and film formation.

In Example 1, dry graphite anode films contained 96 wt.% graphite and 4 wt.% binder, including 2% PTFE, 1% CMC, and 1% PVDF. As-received CMC had a median particle size of about 70 μm, while jet-milled CMC had about 10 μm. Films made with milled CMC showed slightly higher first-cycle efficiency, fewer defects, and greater tensile strength. Tensile strength increased from 0.936 N for as-received CMC to 1.74 N for jet-milled CMC.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s RTX Blackwell Neural Rendering Architecture and GeForce RTX 50 Series features. GDDR7 memory supports Enhanced CRC, built-in always-enabled ECC with single-bit error correction, and Error Detection and Replay. Blackwell Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, INT8, FP8, plus new FP4 and FP6 operations; FP4 reduces AI model memory needs and can improve performance, enabling larger models such as FLUX.dev to run on more GPUs.

Blackwell’s fourth-generation RT Cores improve ray tracing with doubled ray-triangle intersection throughput, Mega Geometry, Triangle Cluster Intersection, Linear Swept Spheres, and Opacity Micromap support. Mega Geometry enables ray tracing of high-detail geometry, cluster-based level-of-detail updates, Cluster-level Acceleration Structures, and Partitioned Top-Level Acceleration Structures to reduce BVH rebuild cost and CPU overhead. It is supported across NVIDIA ray tracing APIs and RTX GPUs starting with Turing. Linear Swept Spheres accelerate strand-like geometry such as hair, offering faster rendering and lower VRAM use than DOTS in common cases.

Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 improves workload coherence and reduces reordering overhead. The AI Management Processor uses a dedicated RISC-V scheduler to manage GPU contexts with lower latency, reducing CPU dependence and improving multitasking and workload scheduling.

Blackwell adds hardware encode and decode support for 4:2:2 chroma video. Ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality, adds 4:2:2 H.264/HEVC encoding, and introduces AV1 Ultra High Quality mode. RTX 5090 supports up to three encoders and two decoders. Sixth-generation NVDEC improves H.264 decoding and adds 4:2:2 H.264/HEVC decode support. DisplayPort 2.1b supports up to 80 Gbps with UHBR 20.

Max-Q improvements include advanced power gating, separate power rails, faster power-state transitions, accelerated frequency switching, and low-latency sleep, improving power efficiency and battery use. DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three additional frames per rendered frame, plus transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA to improve stability, motion detail, lighting, and anti-aliasing.

Blackwell introduces developer-created neural shaders through Cooperative Vectors APIs for DX12 and Vulkan, enabling Tensor Core access from graphics shaders. Related technologies include RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces.

The passage also outlines Blackwell GPU configurations. GB202 targets the flagship segment with 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, and 768 Tensor Cores, powering RTX 5090. GB203 targets high-end GPUs with 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, and 10,752 CUDA cores, powering RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 targets performance GPUs with 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, and 6,400 CUDA cores, powering RTX 5070. The document closes with NVIDIA’s standard legal, warranty, liability, trademark, and copyright notices.

Tesla’s 2019 Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended December 31, 2019. Tesla, Inc., headquartered in Palo Alto, California, is a Delaware corporation listed on Nasdaq under TSLA and classified as a large accelerated filer. As of June 30, 2019, its non-affiliate voting stock market value was $31.54 billion, and as of February 7, 2020, it had 181,341,586 common shares outstanding.

Tesla designs, develops, manufactures, sells and leases fully electric vehicles and energy generation and storage systems, and provides related services. It operates two reportable segments: automotive, including vehicle sales, leasing, services, used vehicles, insurance and regulatory credits; and energy generation and storage, including solar and energy storage products and related services.

Its vehicle products include Model 3, Model Y, Model S, Model X, Cybertruck, Tesla Semi and the new Tesla Roadster. Energy products include Powerwall, Powerpack, Megapack, retrofit solar systems and Solar Roof. Tesla sells primarily through its website and company-owned stores, supports vehicles through service centers and Mobile Service technicians, and operates Supercharger and Destination Charging networks.

Tesla manufactures mainly at the Fremont Factory and nearby California facilities, Gigafactory Nevada, Gigafactory New York and Gigafactory Shanghai, and has selected a site near Berlin for Gigafactory Berlin. Gigafactory Shanghai began Model 3 production in December 2019 and has installed annual capacity for 150,000 Model 3 vehicles.

Tesla reported 48,016 full-time employees as of December 31, 2019. The filing also describes risks including production ramp delays, global sales and service expansion challenges, dependence on electric vehicle adoption, reliance on suppliers, and risks related to Gigafactory Nevada operations.

New York early intervention providers, including therapists and special education teachers serving children from birth to age 3 with developmental delays and disabilities, have not received a substantive pay increase in about 30 years. Reimbursement rates for many services are lower than when the program began in the 1990s, while inflation, reporting requirements, travel, unpaid preparation, and other job demands have increased. Advocates say rates would need to rise sharply to match their original spending power.

Low pay and reimbursement problems have driven many providers to leave for better-paid jobs, contributing to delays and shortages in services, especially in rural areas. A 2024 state-approved 5% increase for in-person services has not been fully implemented pending federal approval, while Medicaid cuts and telehealth rate reductions have added uncertainty. Families report missed services and regression in children, and advocates warn that delays in early intervention can worsen developmental challenges before children enter school.

A survey of 2,000 British adults by Tweak Mattress found the average Brit wakes three times a night, while one in 10 wakes 7 to 10 times. Common causes include needing the toilet (47%), snoring partners (41%), being pushed to the bed edge (25%), discomfort (19%), nightmares (11%), tossing and turning (10.5%), sleep talking or noises (10%), phone use (10%), anxiety (6%), and partners watching TV or reading (4.6%). Psychologist Robert Stewart said sleep quality depends on sleep hygiene and sleep cycles, noting that routines, avoiding screens, and a comfortable, quiet environment can help reduce disturbances.

Enron and creditors would receive 33% of pretax profits for at least two years, with later options reducing payments. Evidence suggests protein sources differ in quality, challenging dietary guidelines that treat equal amounts of protein from foods such as meat, eggs, beans, peanut butter and nuts as equivalent. Protein quality depends on essential amino acid content and digestibility; animal foods such as meat, dairy and eggs generally provide more bioavailable essential amino acids than many plant foods. Although U.S. adults often consume more protein than recommended, some may not get the right mix, especially older adults, who are at risk of muscle loss, weakness, falls and sarcopenia.

Researchers argue guidelines should account for essential amino acids rather than total protein alone. Tools such as the EAA-9 score show that foods like peanut butter or kidney beans may require larger servings than current guidelines suggest to match the protein benefits of an egg. Studies cited found animal-based meals or foods produced greater muscle protein synthesis than plant-based options, particularly in older adults.

Experts do not recommend simply eating more meat. They emphasize improving plant-based protein quality through larger portions, food combinations such as beans and rice, substitutions like sorghum or millet, and preparation methods such as soaking, sprouting and fermentation. Some groups, including older adults, pregnant or breastfeeding individuals and athletes, may need more protein than current recommendations. Younger adults in developed nations may be able to replace some animal protein with plant protein while meeting nutritional needs. Plant-forward diets may also support health and reduce environmental impacts, but consumers need clearer, demographic-specific guidance.

The author argues that Apple’s current valuation does not align with its growth rates and that its share price appears near the upper boundary of a long-term ascending channel. The strongest relationship is found between EV/FCF and FCF growth, leading the author to conclude that Apple’s capitalization is overvalued and that buying the shares at the current price is a poor investment decision.

A planned Fourth of July drone light show at Travis Air Force Base in northern California was postponed to July 5 due to high winds. Anthropologist Donald Blakeslee identified limestone boulders in Tami and Greg Norwood’s backyard as ancient Wichita Nation sacred shrines. Carvings with basins and channels carried poured water, reflecting beliefs in three worlds—sky, earth and underground—and water moving between them. Nearby stones with small depressions were used by women who filled them with water and prayed for successful pregnancies. Blakeslee believes the shrines can help record lost Wichita mythology. Gary McAdams of the Wichita and Affiliated Tribes said water was transformational in Wichita traditions, used in birth rites, prayers, preparation for major events and cleansing after death.

The passage describes three unusual animal relationships. Pearlfish live inside sea cucumber anuses for protection, emerging at night to hunt, though some parasitise their hosts by eating their gonads. Pistol shrimp and gobies form a mutually beneficial partnership: gobies guard the burrow while shrimp dig, maintain it, and clean the fish; some species even share similar colouring. The arid bronze azure butterfly survives by deceiving bearded sugar ants: its larvae emit chemicals that make ants treat them like queens, bring them into nurseries, and then the larvae feed on ant babies.

The article surveys selected results connecting logic, automata, circuit complexity, and transformer expressivity, focusing on formal-language perspectives. Transformers are modeled as sequence-to-sequence transformations using piecewise linear functions and attention layers, with variants based on softmax attention, unique hard attention (UHAT), and average hard attention (AHAT), as well as positional embeddings and masking.

For UHAT, languages recognized with positional embeddings are strictly contained in AC0, so languages such as PARITY and MAJ are not expressible. FO[Mon] is expressible by UHAT with positional embeddings, masked NoPE-UHAT coincides with first-order logic and star-free languages, and UHAT with positional embeddings can express all regular languages in AC0 and Palindrome. Verification of masked UHAT without positional embeddings is decidable and EXPSPACE-complete.

For AHAT, recognized languages are contained in TC0, and AHAT can express MAJ. Counting LTL with unary numerical predicates is expressible by AHAT with positional embeddings, while its fragment Kt[#] is expressible by masked NoPE-AHAT and can express languages such as MAJ and Dyck-1 but not PARITY. NoPE-AHAT exactly recognizes permutation-invariant languages with semi-algebraic Parikh images, making nonemptiness undecidable.

The article also discusses limitations of hard-attention models as approximations of practical softmax transformers. Softmax transformers can express PARITY and are not subsumed by UHAT, while AHAT[U], using uniform attention, is recognizable by softmax transformers. Finally, it distinguishes expressibility from trainability: PARITY is expressible by softmax transformers but difficult to train, while MAJ appears efficiently trainable. The article concludes by noting open challenges in the growing FLaNN research area.
