The passage describes a monthly momentum/rotation strategy that switches between SPY and TLT based on which ETF performed best in the prior month. It explains that momentum strategies have historically worked best over 1–12 month timeframes but can suffer from large drawdowns and survivorship bias. Sector rotation is defined as tactically selling one asset and buying another, often using momentum rules. The SPY/TLT strategy may work because Treasury bonds often act as a safe haven when stocks are weak, though the passage notes TLT did not hedge tail risk in 2022 when both SPY and TLT fell sharply. A backtest from 2003 showed a 9.2% CAGR with dividends reinvested, but maximum drawdown rose from 22% before 2022 to 41% during the bond decline. Entries and exits occur at each month’s close, excluding slippage and commissions.

The ADS868xW moves from ACQ to CONV state on the rising edge of CONVST/CS, ignores further CONVST/CS transitions during conversion, and returns to ACQ when conversion ends. The host can monitor RVS for a low-to-high transition or wait tconv_max before starting another operation.

The device has nine configuration registers and supports data write and data read operations. A data transfer frame starts on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and ends on the next rising edge, which starts conversion. During a frame, SCLK shifts input data through SDI and output data through SDO-x. A 32-SCLK frame is optimal and treats the 32-bit input as a valid command; fewer than 32 clocks create a short read-only frame with write treated as NOP; more than 32 clocks use the last 32 bits as the command.

Input commands configure registers and include byte and half-word operations. HWORD commands ignore the LSB of the 9-bit address. Register-read output appears in the following frame. Otherwise, the output word contains the latest 16-bit conversion result unless DATA_VAL selects fixed patterns. Optional output flags include device address, input range, AVDD alarms, input alarms, and parity.

The multiSPI interface supports legacy SPI-compatible protocols for writing and reading, single or dual SDO-x output, and source-synchronous read protocols using RVS as the output clock. On power-up or after asynchronous reset, SPI-00-S is used until configuration changes the protocol. Dual SDO mode uses SDO-0 and SDO-1 and reduces the number of clock cycles required to output data.

The register map includes DEVICE_ID_REG, RST_PWRCTL_REG, SDI_CTL_REG, SDO_CTL_REG, DATAOUT_CTL_REG, RANGE_SEL_REG, ALARM_REG, ALARM_H_TH_REG, and ALARM_L_TH_REG. These registers configure device ID, reset and power control, serial protocols, output formatting, input range and reference, alarms, and alarm thresholds.

The ADS868xW is a fully integrated, fully differential 16-bit SAR ADC-based data acquisition device with an analog front end, programmable gain, ADC driver, precision reference, overvoltage protection, input alarm, and AVDD alarm. An example design combines ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 differential multiplexer for industrial voltage and current inputs. The input alarm supports programmable high and low thresholds and hysteresis.

The device uses AVDD and DVDD supplies and recommends decoupling capacitors close to supply and reference pins. It supports NAP and power-down modes to reduce power consumption. Layout guidance includes separating analog and digital sections, clean bypassed supplies, short ground paths, and close placement of reference capacitors. The document also lists related resources, update notifications, support forums, ESD caution, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

Lecture 18 of 14.13 examines gender discrimination, identity, and labor market outcomes. It begins by motivating the study of gender differences through fairness, efficiency, and the formation of preferences and personality. The lecture describes persistent gender wage gaps: although women have made substantial labor market gains over the last half century, women still earn significantly less than men even conditional on work time and education.

The lecture reviews explanations for progress, including reduced education gaps, technological innovations, labor demand shifts toward services, and lower discrimination. Goldin and Rouse’s study of blind orchestra auditions is presented as evidence that anonymized evaluations increased impartiality and helped raise women’s representation, though results are complicated by multi-stage auditions and selection effects. The lecture also notes low female representation in economics, especially at senior levels and in recent assistant professor trends.

It then discusses discrimination in applications, including Bertrand and Mullainathan’s finding that resumes with white-sounding names received 50% more callbacks than identical resumes with African-American-sounding names. The lecture distinguishes taste-based discrimination from statistical discrimination.

Sarsons’ study of physicians’ referrals to surgeons shows that after bad outcomes, female surgeons receive larger referral declines than male surgeons, and other female surgeons are also penalized. After good outcomes, male surgeons receive larger referral increases than female surgeons. These asymmetric belief updates may affect promotion, retention, skill accumulation, and measured wage gaps. The lecture notes that algorithms may reproduce biased human decisions but may also be adjusted if fairness concerns are built into their objectives.

The lecture then turns to gender identity norms, especially the norm that husbands should earn more than wives. Bertrand et al. find a missing mass of couples just above the point where wives earn more than half of household income, suggesting such couples may be less likely to form, more likely to divorce, or adjust labor supply so wives earn less. Women may also do more unpaid household and childcare work, especially when earning more than their husbands.

Kleven et al.’s evidence shows a long-run earnings penalty for women after the first child, with smaller effects on hours and additional wage effects. Gender-neutral tenure-clock policies are discussed; Antecol et al. find such policies reduced female tenure rates while increasing male tenure rates in economics departments. Bursztyn et al. find that single female MBA students report lower career ambition when responses may be observed by single male peers.

Finally, the lecture discusses non-promotable tasks. Vesterlund et al. find women are more likely to volunteer for such tasks and, in experiments, more likely to invest in public-good tasks in mixed-gender groups. Gender differences disappear in single-sex groups, and women are more likely to be asked because they are more likely to comply. The lecture concludes that biased beliefs, identity norms, and task allocation can help explain persistent gender gaps.

Moldova’s economy grew 1.1% year-on-year in Q2 2025 after a 1.2% contraction in Q1, driven by construction, energy, and ICT. The EBRD forecasts 1.5% GDP growth in 2025 and 3.8% in 2026, dependent on reforms and international support. The central bank cut rates to 6% to support lending, while inflation, fiscal constraints, currency volatility, and regional uncertainty remain risks.

This study examined barriers and stigma faced by people with probable Long Covid who had not received a formal clinical diagnosis. It formed part of the NIHR STIMULATE-ICP study and used a co-produced community-based active case-finding approach developed with a Community Advisory Board including health professionals, people with Long Covid, carers, voluntary organisations, and public health stakeholders.

Study leaflets were distributed through community organisations, local authorities, and social prescribing teams in Camden, Merton, and Derbyshire. Twenty-three semi-structured interviews were conducted between August 2022 and May 2023 with participants reporting symptoms consistent with Long Covid but no known diagnosis. Thematic analysis identified four themes: uncertainty and Long Covid awareness, barriers to healthcare engagement, stigma and discrimination, and sources of support.

Participants reported limited awareness of Long Covid, uncertainty about whether symptoms were related to it, and self-doubt reinforced in some cases by healthcare interactions. Barriers to seeking care included reluctance to burden the NHS, fear of further investigations, concerns about judgement, difficulties accessing primary care, and the fluctuating, multi-system nature of symptoms. Some symptoms were attributed to menopause, mental health, ageing, stress, or pre-existing conditions.

Participants described perceived discrimination in healthcare, workplaces, and social settings, including dismissal of symptoms, ageism, gender discrimination, lack of understanding, and anticipated stigma. Internalised stigma included embarrassment, shame, and feeling less capable than before illness.

Some participants sought support outside the NHS, including alternative therapies, supplements, private healthcare, family or friends with health expertise, social media groups, and behavioural changes. Desired support included better awareness, longer and more accessible appointments, dedicated Long Covid services, social prescribing, peer support, employment support, and financial support.

The appeal was dismissed by stipulation of counsel, with mandate ordered forthwith.

New York City’s Department of Education spends $25,087 per student, up 40 percent since 2008-09, and had the highest per-pupil spending among the 100 largest U.S. school systems in fiscal 2015. The passage describes NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture, focusing on memory, display, video, VR, ray tracing, AI, shading, and GPU product features. Turing introduces GDDR6 memory with 14 Gbps signaling and 20% better power efficiency than Pascal’s GDDR5X, along with improved package and board design, larger L2 caches, and enhanced lossless memory compression. These changes provide about 50% higher effective bandwidth on TU102-based RTX 2080 Ti compared with Pascal GP102-based GTX 1080 Ti.

Turing’s display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, VESA DSC 1.2, HDR processing, and tone mapping based on ITU-R BT.2100. Its NVENC encoder supports H.265 8K encode at 30 fps and offers bitrate savings for HEVC and H.264, while NVDEC adds support for HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. Turing also supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink, enabling power, display, and data for VR headsets through one USB-C connector.

For multi-GPU configurations, TU102 and TU104 replace earlier SLI MIO and PCIe transfers with second-generation NVLink. TU102 includes two x8 NVLink links and TU104 includes one, with each link providing 25 GB/sec per direction. Two-way SLI is supported on Turing GPUs with NVLink, but 3-way and 4-way SLI are not.

Turing introduces RT Cores for hardware-accelerated ray tracing, enabling real-time hybrid rendering that combines rasterization and ray tracing. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, offloading work from SMs. The passage states Turing can perform ray tracing about 10 times faster than Pascal in certain workloads. Ray tracing is used for reflections, refractions, shadows, ambient occlusion, and indirect lighting, often combined with denoising to reduce required rays per pixel.

NVIDIA NGX uses Turing Tensor Cores and deep neural networks for AI-based graphics features. These include DLSS, which renders with fewer samples and infers higher-quality output; DLSS 2X, which approaches 64x supersampling quality; InPainting; AI Slow-Mo; and AI Super Rez.

Turing adds Mesh Shading with Task and Mesh Shaders, Variable Rate Shading for per-region shading-rate control, Texture Space Shading for decoupling visibility and appearance sampling, and Multi-View Rendering for rendering multiple viewpoints in one pass. These features target improved performance, VR rendering, complex geometry, foveated rendering, and reduced shading work.

The passage also describes TU104, TU106, Tesla T4, GeForce RTX 2080, Quadro RTX 5000, and GeForce RTX 2070 configurations, including SM counts, CUDA Cores, Tensor Cores, RT Cores, memory interfaces, and NVLink support. It defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric combining weighted Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations for hybrid rendering workloads.

The 3 Days Down Overnight Trading Strategy monitors SPY/S&P 500 for three consecutive lower closes, enters at the third day’s close, and exits the next day’s open. A backtest from 1993 produced 661 trades, a 0.13% average gain, 65% win rate, and 8% maximum drawdown, excluding slippage and commissions. Exiting at the next day’s close raised average gain to 0.24% and CAGR to 5% while reducing win rate to 61% and increasing drawdown to 17%. A March 2022 modified version reduced market exposure and drawdowns, with reported 0.35% average gain, 60% win ratio, and 10% maximum drawdown. In the 2022 bear market, it made 35 trades averaging 0.3%.

The double-down trading strategy involves adding the same position size to a losing trade to lower the average entry price and recover losses sooner if the price reverses. It differs from scaling in because it is often unplanned, from Martingale because it does not increase position size after each loss, and from repair strategies because it does not use options. Backtests suggest doubling down can improve results in mean-reverting assets such as SPY but worsens outcomes in trending assets such as HYG. The strategy carries significant risk if prices keep falling and is often described as a trading bias rather than a rational trading plan.

NVIDIA GA10x Ampere GPUs introduce third-generation NVLink, PCIe Gen 4, second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, GDDR6X memory, RTX IO, updated display support, AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-generation NVENC. Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection throughput over Turing and add hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur through an Interpolate Triangle Position unit. DLSS is enhanced with Ampere Tensor Core performance and a 9x Super Resolution scaling factor for 8K gaming.

GDDR6X, developed with Micron, uses PAM4 signaling and supports up to 19.5 Gbps data rates and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth on GA10x GPUs. RTX IO enables GPU-based loading and lossless decompression of assets with Microsoft DirectStorage, reducing CPU workload and improving I/O performance.

The passage highlights GeForce RTX 30-series, RTX 3090, RTX 3080, RTX 3070, RTX A6000, and NVIDIA A40 products. A low-side current sensing circuit uses an amplifier to amplify the shunt resistor voltage drop and a high-speed comparator that changes output state when the amplifier output reaches the over-current threshold. The design requires a logic-high alert when amplifier output exceeds 1.1 V. Proper supply bypassing with a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor close to each device is critical to avoid ringing, false triggers, and oscillations. The device supports split or single supplies, with inputs kept within the recommended range. Layout guidance includes minimizing output-to-input coupling, using solid grounding, placing input series resistors near the device, and adding small output series resistance or controlled-impedance routing for long traces. The lecture introduces nuclear binding energies as a basis for understanding nuclear stability and elemental abundances in the solar system. Binding energy is defined from the masses of protons, neutrons, electrons, and the nucleus, with the neutron slightly heavier than the proton and the electron much lighter.

The average binding energy per nucleon is mostly between 7.5 and 9 MeV, with a maximum near iron. Moving toward more tightly bound nuclei releases energy through fusion for lighter nuclei and fission for heavier nuclei.

The binding energy curve can be described by the semi-empirical Weizsager formula, also called the semi-empirical mass formula or liquid-drop model. It includes five terms: a dominant volume term proportional to mass number, indicating a short-range nuclear force; a surface term reducing binding for nucleons at the surface; a Coulomb term reducing binding due to proton repulsion; an asymmetry term related to neutron-proton imbalance and the Pauli exclusion principle; and a pairing term favoring even numbers of protons or neutrons. The combined terms reproduce the observed binding-energy maximum near iron.

The passage examines how IoT is reshaping ICT firms, business models, and productivity measurement. It argues that Internet-driven ICT advancement creates a new productivity paradox because investments may not translate into measured GDP gains, partly due to “uncaptured GDP” from free services, consumer surplus, online intermediaries, disruptive innovations, and other non-monetized value.

Using empirical analysis of 500 global ICT firms from 2005–2016, the paper finds that high R&D-intensive firms face declining marginal productivity of ICT, attributed to ICT’s two-faced nature: new functionality raises value while freebies, easy copying, and standardization reduce technology prices. Leading firms respond by developing sophisticated digital business strategies and activating self-propagating functionality through soft innovation resources such as supra-functionality, trust, sleeping resources, past experiences, memory, dreams, untapped resources, and vision.

The study identifies major shifts in global ICT leadership toward IoT after 2010, with market value moving toward firms such as Apple, Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Facebook, Tencent, Alibaba, Samsung, and Oracle. It highlights transformations from mechatronics to software, software to networks, networks to physical-digital integration, and commodities to culture.

Case reviews of Samsung, Intel, Google, Microsoft, Huawei, Apple, and Amazon show movement toward IoT-oriented disruptive business models. The paper concludes that ICT firms should recognize uncaptured GDP, shift from traditional ICT strategy to digital business strategy, build trust-based disruptive business models, and use soft innovation resources to sustain functionality development in an IoT-based society.

Researchers and medical professionals warn that drinking more than one glass of wine nightly may indicate risky alcohol use. U.S. imports from China have been large, and exports to China were growing, with 1841 direct exports valued at $715,000 in domestic products and $485,000 in foreign merchandise. An overlap in soccer sends an unmarked player from the back into attack, usually a wing fullback sprinting along the sideline past a midfielder. It creates space by forcing defenders to choose between marking the runner or leaving another attacker open. The overlapping player often receives the ball and crosses near the end-line; if covered, the ball may go to the midfielder. Overlaps are usually near sidelines because they require space and a clear lane, though they can occur centrally. An underlap is similar, but the fullback runs inside the midfielder, often to receive the ball and shoot. In both plays, the defender returns to their original position after the attack changes. Coaches are advised to vary overlaps and underlaps but not use them if they disrupt the team’s attack.

The Washington Supreme Court affirmed judgment for Peter John after sustaining a demurrer to Ross Nelson’s complaint seeking specific performance of a 1892 contract by Puyallup Indian allottees John and Chekudakai Salerhand to convey land. The court held that restrictions on alienation in the patent issued under the 1854 treaty were valid, not repugnant to the grant, and consistent with federal policy treating Indians as wards of the government. It further held that the Bland Act did not impliedly repeal those restrictions, and that the Washington statute removing restrictions required congressional consent. Congress’s 1893 act did not validate the prior conveyance and barred alienation of unselected allotted lands for ten years. Contracts made before valid removal of restrictions were void.

The passage introduces an article analyzing an SEIR-like model for SARS-CoV-2 with a time-dependent transmission parameter. The model includes nine compartments: susceptible, exposed, vaccinated, asymptomatic infectious, mildly infectious, severely infectious, critically infectious, recovered, and deceased. Transmission rates are parameterized by the rate for mildly infectious individuals, while other parameters include vaccination, recovery, hospitalization, ICU admission, and death rates.

The article establishes well-posedness of the model, proving existence, uniqueness, non-negativity of solutions, and conservation of total population. It defines a parameter-to-solution map from the transmission parameter to model solutions, proves properties such as injectivity, continuity, weak sequential closedness, and differentiability, and formulates the derivative through a related linear ODE system. The work aims to support rigorous estimation of time-dependent transmission rates from reported daily infections using Tikhonov-type regularization.

RTX Neural Texture Compression uses neural shaders to compress and decompress material textures more efficiently than traditional methods, reducing memory use in a demo from 1110 MB to 333 MB while improving visual quality. Stochastic Texture Filtering reduces artifacts such as aliasing and moiré patterns and can provide higher-order filtering with a single point sample.

Neural Radiance Cache uses neural shaders and real-time trained neural networks to estimate indirect illumination from path-traced rays after one bounce, improving performance and indirect lighting quality by avoiding full multi-bounce ray tracing. RTX Skin brings subsurface scattering into real-time path tracing for translucent materials such as skin. RTX Neural Faces uses a real-time generative AI model, trained from offline images or generated variants, to infer more natural faces from rasterized face and pose data.

Scientists at Washington University School of Medicine found that brown fat in mice has an alternative heat-producing pathway involving peroxisomes and the protein ACOX2. When ACOX2 was absent, mice had poorer cold tolerance, lower body temperature, reduced insulin sensitivity and greater weight gain on high-fat diets. Mice with elevated ACOX2 showed increased heat production, better insulin sensitivity and improved weight control. Researchers suggest the pathway may be relevant to humans and could inform future dietary or drug-based approaches for obesity and metabolic disease, though the findings are currently based on mouse studies.

An immigration judge in Baltimore rejected Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia’s request to seek asylum, leaving his 2019 removal order in place. The Trump administration cannot deport him again until a separate Maryland federal case is resolved. Abrego Garcia was mistakenly deported to El Salvador despite a prior bar on sending him there, then returned to face immigrant smuggling charges in Nashville. The S&P 500 Equal Weight Index, created in 2003 by Standard & Poor’s, contains the same 500 companies as the traditional S&P 500 but assigns each stock an equal 0.2% weight at each quarterly rebalance, rather than weighting by market capitalization. This means large companies such as Apple have the same index weight as the smallest companies in the index, and sector weights depend on the number of companies in each sector.

The traditional S&P 500 is heavily influenced by the largest mega-cap stocks, while the equal-weight version gives smaller companies more influence. ETFs tracking these indexes include Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP) and State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY). RSP requires rebalancing to maintain equal weights and may offer more protection when large technology stocks decline.

Historically, the equal-weight index has outperformed the market-weighted S&P 500, though not in the last decade. The passage attributes this to the small-cap effect, where smaller companies tend to grow faster than larger ones. From 2004 to 18 years later, a $10,000 investment grew to $60,000 in RSP versus $55,000 in SPY, despite RSP’s higher expense ratio.

The passage discusses choked gamma-ray burst jets in Blue and Red Supergiant progenitors as potential high-energy neutrino sources. In hydrogen-rich stellar envelopes, relativistic jets may fail to escape, suppressing gamma-ray emission while producing cocoon-driven shocks, shock breakout signatures, and TeV–PeV neutrinos through hadronic interactions.

The study uses relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations with the PLUTO code to model jet propagation, shock formation, and cocoon dynamics in extended progenitors. Density profiles are specified for BSG and RSG stars, and analytic and numerical estimates are used to determine jet breakout and choking times. A shock-finding method identifies strong shocks using converging flows, pressure jumps, aligned temperature-density gradients, and relativistic Mach numbers above one.

A detailed simulation is presented for a BSG with radius 50 solar radii and mass 15 solar masses. The injected jet has luminosity 10^51 erg s−1, initial Lorentz factor 7, magnetization 10−2, and engine duration 5 seconds. At 5 seconds, the jet head reaches about 0.03 stellar radii and forms a high-pressure cocoon with external, termination, and collimation shocks. After engine shutdown, the collimation shock fades, while cocoon-driven and residual termination shocks remain. By 30 seconds, these shocks dominate energy dissipation and may enable particle acceleration.

The results indicate that this jet chokes about a minute after launch. The study concludes that evolving shock structures in choked jets can provide sites for particle acceleration, with later neutrino or electromagnetic signatures likely originating mainly from forward-propagating shocks. Future work will extend the parameter study to BSG and RSG progenitors with varied luminosities, Lorentz factors, and viewing angles.

CEZ will buy back nearly all its 2017 convertible bonds linked to MOL shares and sell most of its 7.5% stake in MOL, raising 141.4 billion forints ($490 million) to pay bondholders. It will retain about 0.1% of MOL. CEZ received 463.1 million euros of the 470.2 million euro bond by deadline. Settlement of the share placing and bond repurchase is expected around April 4.

Ken Research’s “Thailand Frozen Foods Market Outlook to 2022” projects Thailand’s frozen foods market to grow at a CAGR of 5.9% during 2017–2022. Growth is expected from strong export demand for frozen seafood and meat, rising demand from hotels, restaurants, offices, hospitals and quick service outlets, increased production capacity, online retailing and canned food usage. Demand is also supported by healthier frozen snacks for children, frozen vegetarian ready meals, processed fruits and vegetables, and lower-sugar frozen desserts using alternative sweeteners. Government fishery improvement initiatives and Thailand’s partnership with Sustainable Fisheries Partnership are expected to support frozen seafood growth. The report covers frozen seafood and meat, ice cream and desserts, ready-to-eat meals, and processed fruits and vegetables, along with distribution channels and major companies in each segment.

The lecture reviews decoding rules and probability-of-error bounds, emphasizing the union bound estimate. It introduces effective coding gain in power-limited and bandwidth-limited regimes, distinguishing it from nominal coding gain and showing how nearest-neighbor counts affect performance. Examples include 2-PAM, 4-QAM, a reduced 4-QAM subset, and a 3D four-point constellation with about 1 dB effective coding gain.

Orthogonal signal sets are analyzed: their nominal coding gain grows with dimension, but nearest-neighbor counts also grow; they asymptotically approach the Shannon limit but have sharply decreasing spectral efficiency and high decoding complexity. Simplex and bi-orthogonal signal sets are briefly described as related constructions with similar theoretical interest and practical drawbacks.

For the bandwidth-limited regime, analogous expressions for nominal and effective coding gain are developed using probability of error per two dimensions. The lecture then previews binary block codes, where K input bits are encoded into N binary symbols and mapped to binary signaling. This separates coding and modulation, which is suitable for binary signaling but not optimal for non-binary signaling. The binary signaling constraint causes at most about 0.2 dB loss in the power-limited regime, motivating the study of binary linear block codes and finite field theory.

The lecture continues the discussion of the massive Sudakov form factor in SCET2, where rapidity divergences require an additional regulator beyond dimensional regularization. This introduces eta poles and dependence on a rapidity scale nu, alongside the usual mu scale. Collinear modes require nu of order the hard scale and mu of order the mass scale, while soft modes require both nu and mu of order the mass scale.

The factorization theorem contains hard, collinear, anti-collinear, and soft functions, all depending on renormalization scales. Because both mu and nu appear, renormalization group evolution occurs in a two-dimensional scale space. Physical observables are independent of the arbitrary final point and of the path taken in this space, leading to consistency relations between mu and nu anomalous dimensions. Counterterms remove epsilon and eta poles, and the resulting anomalous dimensions generate evolution kernels that resum large logarithms.

The same rapidity-renormalization structure appears in Higgs transverse-momentum production, where measuring small Higgs transverse momentum allows both collinear and soft radiation with comparable transverse momentum. The factorization theorem involves a hard function, transverse-momentum-dependent gluon PDFs, and a soft function, all requiring mu and nu evolution. Jet broadening in e+e− dijet production is mentioned as another SCET2 example.

The lecture then discusses Drell-Yan production. Key variables include the hadronic center-of-mass energy, the lepton-pair invariant mass, tau, rapidity, Bjorken-like variables, and parton momentum fractions. Several kinematic regimes lead to different factorization theorems: inclusive Drell-Yan permits hard radiation and involves ordinary PDFs; the threshold limit forces most energy into the lepton pair and leaves only soft radiation; and isolated Drell-Yan constrains hemisphere momenta, producing initial-state collinear jets plus ultrasoft radiation.

For isolated Drell-Yan, the factorization theorem includes hard, soft, and beam functions. Beam functions describe initial-state radiation and are matrix elements related to PDFs and jet functions. They can be matched onto standard PDFs with perturbative coefficients when separating the perturbative jet scale from the nonperturbative proton scale.

This study examined predictors of intention to comply with COVID-19 preventive measures among adults in Spain during the first pandemic wave. Using PSY-COVID online survey data from 15,131 residents, the study analyzed sociodemographic, behavioral, cognitive, social, affective, personality, and regional factors. The strongest predictors of post-confinement preventive behavior intention were self-efficacy, outcome expectations, general adherence to preventive behaviors, information level, prior preventive behavior, perceived vulnerability, trust in scientists, and social norms. Perceived severity moderated the effects of adherence to avoid infection and perceived vulnerability of others. Regional residence had a small but significant influence, with the Canary Islands showing the highest intention and Aragón and the Balearic Islands the lowest. The study concludes that socio-cognitive factors, especially self-efficacy and outcome expectations, are central to promoting compliance, and highlights the importance of clear communication, trust, and addressing regional disparities.

The paper proposes an optimized weighted expectation-maximization algorithm for estimating transition probability matrices in Markov cohort-state-transition models when data have unequal observation intervals or missing transitions. Unlike the uniform weighting approach of Craig and Sendi, the method assigns weights to estimated one-step count matrices to reduce output variance, using grid search and bootstrap-based uncertainty estimation. A fictitious three-state cost-effectiveness example comparing SuperDrug with placebo found a 15.2% reduction in ICER variance and a 3-percentage point increase in the probability of cost-effectiveness at £20,000/QALY, with similar ICER means. The authors caution that the method may be appropriate only when transition count matrices come from the same or similar studies, recommend comparing weighted and unweighted methods, and call for validation using clinical trial or real-world data.

NVIDIA Turing GPUs improve memory performance with optimized 14 Gbps GDDR6 signaling, larger and faster L2 caches, and enhanced lossless memory compression. TU102 includes 6 MB of L2 cache, twice GP102’s 3 MB, and the RTX 2080 Ti delivers about 50% higher effective bandwidth than the Pascal-based GTX 1080 Ti.

Turing adds a new display and video engine supporting DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, VESA DSC 1.2, HDR processing, BT.2100 tone mapping, HEVC 8K encode at 30 fps, improved NVENC bitrate efficiency, and updated NVDEC decoding. USB-C and VirtualLink support allow VR headsets to use one connector for power, display, and data. TU102 and TU104 use NVLink for SLI data transfers, with TU102 offering two x8 links and TU104 one x8 link; only two-way SLI is supported.

Turing introduces RT Cores in each SM to accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time ray tracing with NVIDIA RTX, DXR, OptiX, and future Vulkan ray tracing support. Hybrid rendering combines rasterization with ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, and ambient occlusion. Turing can deliver over 10 Giga Rays/sec using RT Cores, compared with Pascal’s software-based ray tracing at about 1.1 Giga Rays/sec.

NVIDIA NGX uses Turing Tensor Cores for AI-based graphics features such as DLSS, DLSS 2X, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS is trained using 64x supersampled reference images and can improve performance while maintaining image quality comparable to TAA.

Turing also adds Mesh Shading, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering. These features reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks, dynamically adjust shading rates, reuse shading results across frames or views, and render multiple viewpoints in one pass. They support use cases including VR, foveated rendering, motion-adaptive shading, stereo rendering, shadow maps, and complex object scenes.

TU104 includes 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 13.6 billion transistors, and second-generation NVLink. Tesla T4 uses a TU104 variant with 2560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, and 320 GB/s memory bandwidth. TU106, used in GeForce RTX 2070, includes 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, and no NVLink or SLI support.

The passage defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric combining Tensor, FP32, RT Core, and INT32 operations based on representative hybrid-rendering usage. It also explains ray tracing mechanics, BVH acceleration, denoising, ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, and states that hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH algorithms, and RT Cores together enable real-time ray tracing on Turing.

Cat tail movements can signal mood, but body language is also important. A tapping tail may show relaxed attention or dreaming, while whipping can indicate nervousness or aggression. Tail position may suggest friendliness, relaxation, or defensiveness. Sudden running, or “zoomies,” may result from arousal, frustration, fear, or pent-up energy.

The guide describes AMD Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM), optional extensions to SEV and SNP for offloading page migration. TMPM supports moving page contents between system physical addresses while maintaining the same GPA, requires IOMMU enablement, and can be detected through the ENGINE_READY bit in the PM_Status register.

TMPM enables migration of pages involved in concurrent DMA by pausing DMA while copying data and updating IOMMU mappings, and it can migrate SNP-protected guest pages inaccessible to the HV/OS. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates DMA-targeted pages and hypervisor-state pages, requiring the relevant IOMMU hPTE. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages from Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid source states to Pre-Migration destinations; after migration, sources become Pre-Migration and destinations take the original source state.

A new Pre-Migration RMP state uses PS_ASID_VAL and cannot be validated by a guest. Multi-page commands can migrate up to 128 pages using Page Migration Lists, with per-page status reporting. PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires checking individual entries; retry may be possible for PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE.

Performance improves with commands of 16 or more pages and is highest at 128 pages. Keeping the ring buffer supplied and limiting interrupts can improve throughput. Non-migratable structures include IOMMU SPA-accessed structures, vIOMMU private address space page tables, pinned backing buffers, the ring buffer, and argument pages. For PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, source pages must be DMA-mapped through one IOMMU host page table, and host software must avoid concurrent hPTE modifications during TMPM operations.

Blackwell was designed to improve performance and efficiency for neural shaders, which are presented as the future of game shader technology. The passage outlines shader evolution from fixed-function GPU pipelines to programmable vertex, pixel, geometry, compute, and ray tracing shaders. With Blackwell, developer-created neural shaders are introduced, some compatible with prior GPU generations.

The passage presents a multi-criteria integer programming model for ambulance station location planning. The model maximizes population coverage within two response-time thresholds while ensuring all demand points are covered within a legally allowed maximum time. It was applied in a real-world study in Southwest Germany, where locations for outdated ambulance stations were optimized using road-segment demand, population weights, OpenStreetMap data, and ambulance-specific travel-time estimates.

In the case study, optimizing for 5-minute coverage favored station locations in urban areas, while optimizing for 10-minute coverage led to more evenly distributed stations, including rural locations. Sixteen Pareto-optimal solutions showed trade-offs between these objectives. The results were used as decision-support input and further evaluated with emergency service experts and simulation. The authors conclude that the model supports real-world planning but leaves ethical choices between urban and rural prioritization to decision-makers. Future extensions may include investment costs, multiple coverage, and simultaneous optimization of locations and vehicle provision.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 25, 2016. For the quarter, net sales were $42.4 billion, down from $49.6 billion a year earlier, and net income was $7.8 billion, down from $10.7 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.42 versus $1.85. For the first nine months of fiscal 2016, net sales were $168.8 billion and net income was $36.7 billion, compared with $182.2 billion and $42.3 billion in the prior-year period.

The sales decline was primarily driven by lower iPhone unit sales and lower iPhone average selling prices. Quarterly iPhone net sales fell 23% to $24.0 billion, iPad net sales rose 7% to $4.9 billion, Mac net sales fell 13% to $5.2 billion, Services rose 19% to $6.0 billion, and Other Products fell 16% to $2.2 billion. By region, quarterly net sales decreased in the Americas, Europe, Greater China, and Rest of Asia Pacific, while Japan increased 23%.

Gross margin was 38.0% for the quarter, compared with 39.7% a year earlier. Operating income was $10.1 billion, down from $14.1 billion. Research and development expense increased to $2.6 billion, while selling, general and administrative expense decreased to $3.4 billion. Apple generated $49.7 billion in operating cash flow during the first nine months of fiscal 2016.

As of June 25, 2016, Apple had $305.6 billion in total assets, $231.5 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, $179.1 billion in total liabilities, and $126.5 billion in shareholders’ equity. The company had $12.5 billion of commercial paper outstanding and $71.6 billion aggregate principal amount of long-term notes. During the quarter, Apple repurchased $10.0 billion of common stock, paid $3.2 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents, and issued U.S. dollar- and Australian dollar-denominated long-term debt.

Police said a semi-automatic handgun apparently fired one round from inside a backpack at Sal Castro Middle School in Los Angeles, striking two 15-year-old students in the head and wrist. Doctors said both are expected to recover. A 12-year-old girl was arrested, held without bail at juvenile hall, and faces felony charges for firearm possession and having a weapon on school grounds. Detectives are investigating how she got the gun; her father reportedly said it did not belong to the family and apologized.

A short squeeze occurs when a heavily shorted stock rises instead of falling, forcing short sellers to buy back shares at higher prices to cover positions, which can push the price even higher. Losses for short sellers can be large because stock price increases have no theoretical limit. Short squeezes are described as rare, difficult to predict, and practically impossible to backtest into a reliable trading strategy.

Examples mentioned include GameStop in 2021 and Volkswagen, with GameStop rising sharply within a month. Short squeezes typically last 2–4 weeks, often less than a month, depending on short interest, trading volume, and broker actions. High short interest alone is not presented as a viable long strategy, and high short-interest stocks are said to underperform compared with low short-interest stocks.

Short selling is difficult because gains are capped at 100% while losses can be unlimited, and asset prices generally rise over time. Short squeezes may be illegal if caused by manipulation of stock price or availability; naked short selling is illegal. An exit strategy involves monitoring price momentum and short interest, using stop-loss or trailing stop orders, and exiting before a sharp reversal.

The passage outlines statistical analysis procedures for a clinical trial. Plasma glucose is sampled pre-dose and up to 45 or 60 minutes post-dose, with AUE0-30min as the pharmacodynamic endpoint calculated in SAS. Glucose concentrations, changes from pre-dose, pharmacodynamic metrics, and mean and individual time-concentration curves will be summarized by treatment group.

Safety analyses use the safety set and include exposure, insulin use before hypoglycemia induction, hypoglycemia induction details, trial medication administration, rescue glucose infusion, local tolerability, adverse events, laboratory tests, vital signs, physical examination, ECG, and immunogenicity. TEAEs are defined as events after dosing or worsened pre-existing events; missing causality is treated as related if unresolved. AE summaries use MedDRA terms and include special-interest events, injection site reactions, related events, serious events, deaths, causality, and severity.

Laboratory, vital sign, ECG, pregnancy, alcohol breath test, and ADA data will be summarized descriptively or listed as specified. The SAP notes changes from the protocol, including revised primary efficacy analysis wording and added sensitivity/supportive analyses. Appendices provide table, figure, listing, formatting, derivation, missing-date handling, SAS programming QC, validation, and planned output requirements.

Several June 25, 2001 articles mention Enron amid energy-sector developments. This study investigated whether brief resting-state SEEG data can identify seizure onset zones (SOZ) and predict seizure outcomes in 43 drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients. Ten-minute interictal resting-state SEEG epochs were analyzed using within-frequency directed transfer function, cross-frequency directionality, 1/f power slope estimation, and balanced random forest classification.

Results showed dominant information flow from non-SOZ to SOZ regions across multiple frequencies during resting state. SOZ regions had more negative 1/f power slopes than non-SOZ regions, suggesting lower excitability in SOZ and higher excitability in non-SOZ. Larger asymmetry in within-frequency information flow between SOZ and non-SOZ was associated with favorable seizure outcomes. A random forest classifier using broadband within-frequency information flow predicted SOZ with 0.85 accuracy and 0.94 AUC. Seizure outcome prediction achieved 0.77 accuracy and 0.78 AUC when clinician-defined SOZ was used, and 0.72 accuracy and 0.75 AUC when model-estimated SOZ was used.

The authors conclude that resting-state SEEG connectivity combined with machine learning may help localize SOZ and predict seizure outcomes without prolonged ictal recordings, potentially supplementing traditional SEEG interpretation and improving epilepsy treatment planning.

The study evaluated clinical efficacy and safety of convalescent plasma plus best supportive care versus standard care. Endpoints included WHO clinical status, mechanical ventilation or death by Day 30, sustained clinical improvement, ventilation, and ICU use. Analyses used intent-to-treat methods, multiple imputation, and regression models adjusted for period and site.

Business Insider analyzes 25 Taylor Swift songs with literary references, emphasizing her storytelling and poetic lyricism. The article identifies links to Robert Frost in “The Outside,” Shakespeare in “Love Story” and “The Fate of Ophelia,” Pablo Neruda in “All Too Well,” Lewis Carroll in “Wonderland,” Nathaniel Hawthorne in “New Romantics,” and Elizabeth Taylor/Richard Burton’s biography “Furious Love” in “…Ready For It?” It also connects several songs to F. Scott Fitzgerald, including “Don’t Blame Me,” “Delicate,” “This Is Why We Can’t Have Nice Things,” and “Happiness.”

Other cited influences include Kurt Vonnegut’s “Slaughterhouse-Five” in “So It Goes…,” Charles Dickens’ “A Tale of Two Cities” in “Getaway Car,” J.M. Barrie’s Peter Pan in “Cardigan” and “Peter,” Sylvia Plath in “Mirrorball” and possibly “Who’s Afraid of Little Old Me?,” Charlotte Brontë’s “Jane Eyre” in “Invisible String,” “Evermore,” and “Dear Reader,” Jean Rhys’ “Wide Sargasso Sea” in “Mad Woman,” William Wordsworth and Romantic poetry in “The Lakes,” Daphne du Maurier’s “Rebecca” in “Tolerate It,” Emily Dickinson and Sue Gilbert in “Ivy” and “Evermore,” and Samuel Coleridge’s “The Rime of the Ancient Mariner” in “The Albatross.” The article concludes that Swift often adapts literary figures and symbols to explore love, isolation, reputation, betrayal, survival, and self-definition.

RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection, enabling faster ray tracing for reflections, shadows, ambient occlusion, and other effects when paired with denoising and RTX-compatible APIs.

The passage also presents NVIDIA NGX, which uses Turing Tensor Cores for AI-based graphics features including DLSS, DLSS 2X, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. The lecture explains why Lebesgue integration is useful for communication theory, Fourier analysis, and random processes, especially when dealing with “weird” functions that may not be Riemann integrable. Riemann integration partitions the time axis, while Lebesgue integration partitions function values and uses measure to quantify where a function falls within intervals. When a Riemann integral exists, the Lebesgue integral gives the same value, but Lebesgue integration also handles broader cases.

Measure is introduced for intervals, countable unions of disjoint intervals, and sets of measure zero. Examples include the rationals in \((0,1)\), which are countable and have measure zero, and a Cantor-like uncountable set that also has measure zero. A function is measurable if the set of times for which it falls in any interval is measurable. For nonnegative measurable functions, the Lebesgue integral always exists as either finite or infinite.

The lecture defines \(L^1\) functions as measurable functions with finite integral of magnitude, and \(L^2\) functions as measurable functions with finite integral of squared magnitude. For finite-duration functions, \(L^2\) implies \(L^1\). This supports Fourier series results: finite Fourier coefficients exist for finite-duration \(L^2\) functions, and Fourier series converge in mean-square energy rather than necessarily pointwise. This convergence is denoted as limit in the mean.

The lecture then describes segmenting an arbitrary \(L^2\) function into finite time intervals and expanding each segment into a Fourier series, producing a double orthogonal expansion. This is connected to voice compression, where signals are divided into short time intervals and approximated by Fourier components. The lecture closes by introducing Fourier transform relationships between time and frequency and noting they will be discussed further next time.

Ric Flair is resting after undergoing unspecified surgery Monday, his representatives said. He had been hospitalized in intensive care over the weekend and placed in a medically induced coma before surgery. Reports said he was hospitalized near Atlanta for heart-related issues. His representatives asked fans for prayers and support.

Rockford High School students in Kris DeYoung’s television production class were named 2018 Station of the Year by the Michigan Association of Broadcasting at the Great Lakes Media Show. The team also earned recognition in 11 of 12 programming categories, including eight first-place awards. DeYoung credited the students’ dedication and highlighted senior leaders Jackson Carey and Megan Lindeboom. The program involves about 150 new students yearly and includes multiple skill levels. The team was later recognized by the Rockford Board of Education.

The passage presents variadic nominal anti-unification, a technique for computing least general generalizations of terms that include both variable binding and variadic arity. It motivates the approach through program analysis and code clone detection, where existing anti-unification methods struggle with insertions, deletions, and bound variable renaming. The proposed framework distinguishes atoms from variables, supports individual and hedge variables, uses freshness constraints and nominal equivalence, and computes both generalizations and difference information needed to reconstruct original terms. A rule-based VNAU algorithm is defined with decomposition, abstraction, solving, merging, and narrowing rules. The passage states termination, soundness, and completeness results, illustrates the algorithm on code clone examples, and notes limitations caused by nondeterminism and inefficient exhaustive search.

Sonali Bendre announced she has been diagnosed with high-grade cancer after tests for a persistent pain. She is undergoing treatment in New York and said she remains optimistic, supported by family and friends. She and other parents said costly trips exclude lower-income families, with some parents using credit cards or feeling pressured to pay when children are embarrassed or upset.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 24, 2015, reporting under Regulation FD that its 2014 Letter to Shareholders, accompanying the Annual Report for the year ended December 31, 2014, is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by David A. Zapolsky, Senior Vice President.

Google updated the Drive API to support Team Drives, allowing developers to add Team Drives functionality to apps without learning a new API. A G Suite Dev Show video covers creating Team Drives, adding members, creating folders, and uploading files. Features are available in Drive API v2 and v3.

This guide describes AMD Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM), an optional extension to SEV and SNP that offloads page migration by copying page contents and updating virtual-to-physical mappings. TMPM supports migration across memory tiers, concurrent DMA-safe migration through IOMMU coordination, and migration of SNP-protected guest pages that HV/OS cannot directly access. TMPM availability is checked via the ENGINE_READY bit and requires IOMMU enablement.

Key commands include PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO for DMA-targeted and hypervisor-state pages, and PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST for SNP guest pages using a Pre-Migration RMP state. Multi-page commands can migrate up to 128 pages, with per-page status reporting and retry support for conflicts such as PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE. Best performance is achieved with larger batches, especially 128-page commands, and by keeping the ring buffer filled while limiting interrupts.

Certain structures are non-migratable, including IOMMU SPA-accessed structures, vIOMMU private mappings, pinned buffers, the ring buffer, and argument pages. Host software must avoid concurrent hPTE modifications during TMPM operations. TMPM firmware can be reloaded only after operations are paused and the ring buffer is torn down; software should check ENGINE_READY before use. EPYC reload handling depends on PM_GET_CAPABILITIES and FW_VER_Major.

Marshall University Joan C. Edwards School of Medicine, Marshall Health and Cabell Huntington Hospital welcomed four new specialists. Pavithra Indramohan, a board-certified geriatrician and internal medicine physician, joins as an assistant professor and sees patients at Marshall Health’s Hanshaw Geriatric Center. Peimei He and Elie Khalil, both board-certified infectious disease specialists, join as assistant professors specializing in chronic and atypical infections and immunocompromised patients. Yara Tovar Marmolejo, a board-certified endocrinologist, joins as an assistant professor specializing in endocrine disorders such as diabetes and hyperthyroidism. He, Khalil and Tovar Marmolejo are accepting patients at Marshall Internal Medicine in Huntington.
The speaker says the team should shoot more, skate quicker, avoid sitting back, and create rebounds, noting opponents have played well and conditions are getting hotter late in the season.

The speaker urges fair treatment for Japanese residents and recommends allowing naturalization for Japanese intending to become American citizens. He argues that federal laws are inadequate to protect aliens’ treaty rights and asks Congress to strengthen criminal and civil statutes so the national government can enforce international obligations and prevent local violence that could provoke conflict with foreign nations. He also describes U.S. intervention in Cuba after an insurrection, the Cuban government’s collapse, and the risk of European intervention. U.S. ships, officials, and troops were sent; a provisional government was proclaimed under the Platt amendment; insurgents disarmed; and the island is being administered until elections can restore a new government.

The passage examines artificial intelligence in education, focusing on Hungarian education participants’ knowledge, attitudes, and the effectiveness of AI tools in programming education. AI is described as increasingly present in learning and teaching, with potential benefits such as assignment generation, grading support, immediate answers, accessibility, and equal opportunities, alongside risks including incorrect answers, reduced critical thinking, cheating, overreliance, legal issues, and unequal access.

The research used interviews with high school teachers and university lecturers (N=14) and questionnaires completed by university students (N=53). Participants were familiar with a range of AI tools, especially ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, DALL-E, Midjourney, and Bard/Gemini. They used AI for debugging, explaining steps, searching information, accelerating development, generating code and practice tasks, and summarizing material. Responses on AI’s educational usefulness were mixed, but 91% expressed a positive attitude toward AI integration in programming education.

A second study tested Gemini, ChatGPT, and Microsoft Copilot on beginner and complex programming tasks. None achieved full accuracy. ChatGPT performed best overall, scoring 46/50, compared with Copilot’s 37/50 and Gemini’s 32/50. In complex tasks, all three solved HTML, JavaScript, and JS/PHP tasks after some prompting, but only ChatGPT completed the C programming task. The study concludes that AI tools can support education when users have enough prior knowledge and critical thinking to identify errors, but they may mislead learners lacking sufficient subject knowledge.

The ADS8681W/ADS8685W/ADS8689W support synchronous register read/write operations using SCLK. Commands can access one byte or two bytes; half-word commands ignore the LSB of the 9-bit address. Supported functions include register read, half-word read, write, half-word write, bit set, and bit clear. All input commands used to configure internal registers are 32 bits and execute on the rising edge of CONVST/CS.

Output data is shifted through SDO-x pins and depends on the previous frame command and DATA_VAL settings. The next frame can output fixed patterns, 8-bit register data, 16-bit register data, or the latest 16-bit conversion result. DATAOUT_CTL_REG can append device address, input range flags, AVDD alarm flags, input alarm flags, parity bits, and zero padding.

The multiSPI interface supports write configuration through four SPI-compatible protocols: SPI-00-S, SPI-01-S, SPI-10-S, and SPI-11-S. After power-up or asynchronous reset, the device defaults to SPI-00-S. Read operations can use single SDO, dual SDO, or source-synchronous protocols. Dual SDO mode uses SDO-0 and SDO-1 to output two bits per clock. Source-synchronous mode uses RVS as an output clock synchronized to data, with internal or external clock options.

The device includes nine configuration registers: DEVICE_ID_REG, RST_PWRCTL_REG, SDI_CTL_REG, SDO_CTL_REG, DATAOUT_CTL_REG, RANGE_SEL_REG, ALARM_REG, ALARM_H_TH_REG, and ALARM_L_TH_REG. These control identification, reset and power-down, serial protocols, output formatting, input range, alarm flags, and alarm thresholds.

The ADS868xW is a fully integrated, fully differential 16-bit SAR ADC with integrated analog front end, programmable gain, ADC driver, reference, input alarm, AVDD alarm, and overvoltage protection. An example application combines ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 for industrial analog input modules supporting voltage and current inputs. The device uses AVDD and DVDD supplies, requires decoupling capacitors, and supports NAP and power-down modes for reduced power. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and digital sections and placing supply and reference capacitors close to device pins.

Warrensburg Central School District will hold a March 20 informational session on upcoming grades 3-8 ELA and Math testing. Grades 7-8 will pilot online exams, while grades 3-4 remain paper-based. Exams are reduced from three days to two, and teachers will share sample questions and answer questions.

He was also charged with drink driving, recording .142. He received an 18-month wholly suspended prison sentence, and the pair have lost contact.

Investing.com page highlights market headlines and an analysis arguing that gold’s rally, weak mining stock response, a potential USD Index rally, and bearish stock signals resemble conditions from 2008. The article says GDXJ failed to rally meaningfully, the USD Index is verifying a bullish inverse head-and-shoulders breakout, and stocks may decline after breaking support.
