The study examines conversational information-seeking with ChatGPT, focusing on how users adopt prompting strategies, how ChatGPT’s communication styles adapt to prompts and issue controversy, and how those styles affect AI perceptions and issue-specific attitudes. It frames prompting as a behavioral signal of AI literacy and a second-level digital divide, noting that ordinary users’ real-world prompting strategies remain understudied.

Researchers conducted a 3 × 2 between-subject experiment with 937 U.S. adults across health, science, and policy topics, comparing controversial and non-controversial issues. Participants interacted with ChatGPT for issue-specific information, and 747 valid conversations were analyzed. Communication styles were measured as self-revealing, information-seeking, fact-oriented, action-seeking, and cognitive complexity, alongside citation and structural features. Prompting strategies were annotated using ChatGPT and validated by human coders.

The study found that 19.1% of users used at least one prompting strategy, with use predicted by education level and party affiliation. Issue controversy influenced ChatGPT’s communication styles and citation counts, while user prompt styles stayed consistent across controversy levels. More cognitively complex ChatGPT responses were perceived less favorably but were associated with more positive issue-relevant attitude changes.

The TPS7H500x-SP FAULT pin enables external protection functions such as input overcurrent, overvoltage, or stricter thermal protection. A fault shutdown occurs if FAULT exceeds 0.6 V typical for the minimum pulse width of 0.4 µs to 1.4 µs. During a fault, SS discharges and controller outputs stop switching until FAULT falls below 0.5 V typical, after which a switching-frequency-dependent delay of about 15 cycles plus internal delay occurs before soft-start restarts.

The device uses peak current mode control and requires slope compensation to prevent subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle. Recommended slope compensation is equal to the inductor falling current slope and is set with a resistor from RSC to AVSS. Type 2A or Type 2B compensation can be used with the transconductance error amplifier; Type 2A adds a high-frequency noise attenuation capacitor.

Thermal shutdown stops switching when junction temperature exceeds 175°C typical and restarts power-up when it falls below 160°C typical. The controllers regulate peak current and duty cycle using an internal oscillator, external current sensing, and comparison against the stepped-down COMP voltage.

The TPS7H500x-SP family consists of radiation-hardness-assured current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters and supports topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. A design example describes a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull converter using GaN devices, including selection of timing resistors, feedback divider, dead time, leading-edge blanking, soft-start capacitor, transformer parameters, FET ratings, RCD clamp, output inductor, output capacitance, current sense resistor, hiccup capacitor, compensation network, and slope compensation resistor.

The controllers operate from a 4-V to 14-V input supply and require at least a 0.1-µF bypass capacitor from VIN to AVSS, with ceramic capacitors placed close to the device. Layout guidance emphasizes minimizing noisy switching loops and switch-node copper, separating analog and power grounds with a single connection point, keeping bypass and compensation components close, routing sensitive traces away from high dv/dt signals, filtering the CS_ILIM input if needed, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS with multiple vias.

The passage also lists related documentation, support resources, revision history, mechanical and orderable information, ESD cautions, and TI disclaimers regarding use of design resources and product information.

The passage presents a proposal that the United States join other nations in guaranteeing lasting peace through principles described as consistent with American tradition: non-extension of one nation’s polity over another, self-determination, avoidance of entangling alliances, common protection through a concert of power, government by consent, freedom of the seas, and moderation of armaments.

Subsequent diplomatic reports describe reactions abroad. In Italy, the Foreign Minister considered the Senate address idealistic and difficult to implement but not unfavorably received, and expected it to cause a stir; he also asked what specific plan was proposed for a peace preservation league. The Swiss Minister praised the address highly. In Spain, the Minister of State said Spain’s reply to the peace note would have differed had Spain been consulted first, but expressed willingness to cooperate with the United States on peace efforts and said the Senate address made an excellent impression. In Austria-Hungary, Count Tisza said Hungary welcomed peace efforts and was willing to continue exchanges with the United States, but argued that opponents’ conditions threatened the Austro-Hungarian and Ottoman Empires and conflicted with the President’s standpoint.

Three-year-old Liam Radcliffe left Barassie early years nursery in Ayrshire unnoticed and walked about half a mile home along busy roads. His mother, Sarra Reid, found him crying at the door and returned him to the nursery, where staff had not realised he was missing. Liam is believed to have passed through two sets of doors and an unlocked gate. After a meeting with nursery officials, Reid said she was told the main door would be alarmed, the gate padlocked and staffing increased. South Ayrshire Council confirmed additional security measures had been introduced.

The passage argues that judges and judicial decisions should be open to fair, public criticism, citing Lord Chancellor Parker and Judge W. H. Taft. Taft maintained that criticism helps judges deliberate carefully and serves as an important check, especially for judges with life tenure, though unjust attacks should be answered to preserve confidence in courts. The passage warns that refusing all criticism of judges may leave the field to intemperate agitators and foster dangerous hostility toward the judiciary. It then turns to delays in law enforcement, crime, corruption, and lynching, urging public conscience and faster, more certain legal processes. It condemns lynching and mob violence, noting that while many white men are lynched, the crime is especially frequent against black men, often following accusations of rape, and says mobs degrade themselves by torturing offenders.

The passage describes systems, methods, and computer-readable media for orthodontic treatment planning that automatically apply user or user-group clinical preferences when generating treatment plans. A treatment planning engine receives patient dentition information and user instructions, accesses or builds a database linking users, textual key preferences, and corresponding clinical behaviors, and incorporates matching behaviors into automatically generated dental treatment plans.

The database may be created from historical treatment data by identifying reference preference text, matching it to user-specific instructions within a probability range, and linking the matched text to clinical behaviors. Matching may use machine learning, similarity searching such as Damerau-Levenshtein distance, or both. The system may also use statistical preference analysis to detect consistent clinical behaviors over time and associate them with key preference text. Preferences may be manually verified before inclusion.

The disclosed workflow can update preferences based on user modifications to generated plans and may include monitoring tools that evaluate whether automatically applied preferences remain consistent with accepted treatment plans. The passage also describes systems with processors and memory configured to perform these methods, along with examples of workflows, reports, text classification, similarity matching, and statistical clustering used to identify and maintain user preferences.

Investing.com reports mixed market signals: the S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July and 7.8% year-to-date, with medium- and long-term trend indicators still healthy. However, August began weakly, volatility and credit spreads are rising seasonally, tech stock concentration is increasing, and short-term technical indicators show early warning signs.

BG Group agreed to buy Enron’s offshore oil and gas assets in India for $388 million, including stakes in the Tapti, Panna/Mukta, and CB-OS/1 fields, though the deal required government approval and agreement on operatorship. Reports described the price as favorable for BG and part of Enron’s retreat from physical assets in India, where it was also trying to exit the troubled Dabhol Power Project. Dabhol faced payment disputes, shutdowns, and a reported $24 million interest-payment default. Other Enron mentions included a stock rally, Edison debt-settlement issues involving Enron as a creditor, and former Enron executive Thomas White being named the Pentagon’s homeland security liaison.

Archive log listing Enron discussion-thread items in Steven Kean’s folder, mostly from September 2000 to July 2001, concerning California energy issues. Topics include CPUC and FERC proceedings, Governor Davis, CAISO/PX matters, PG&E and SCE finances, legislation, direct access, price caps, gas and power prices, hearings, media materials, Enron talking points, and PG&E’s bankruptcy.

A vehicle code stop in Chino led to the arrest of 36-year-old Mark William Ellis of Chino and the discovery of more than $200,000 in stolen property stored in six Montclair storage units, San Bernardino County sheriff’s officials said. Ellis, on probation at the time, was arrested Feb. 4 on suspicion of grand theft and vehicle theft and is being held without bail. Authorities said the thefts date back at least 12 years and involved vehicles, homes, businesses and schools in multiple cities. Items included firearms, electronics, tools, cellphones and gym equipment. Investigators have returned about $63,000 in property to victims and confirmed more than 50 vehicle burglaries involving 40 victims. Ellis pleaded not guilty and is due back in court March 21.

Centana Growth Partners raised $250 million for its first fund to invest in financial services startups, targeting $5 million to $30 million per company. Founded in 2015 by Eric Byunn, Steven Swain and Ben Cukier, it has invested in four companies, including One and Jumio.

Hong Liu introduces course logistics for a holographic duality class: there is no textbook, no recitation, office hours are Monday 3:30–4:30, materials will be posted online, grading is based on five problem sets worth 75% and a final 8–10 page project worth 25%. The course outline is flexible and ambitious, likely covering only part of the listed material, with emphasis on outside reading and student questions.

The lecture begins by contrasting gravity with other interactions. Electromagnetism, weak, and strong interactions are described by gauge theories on fixed spacetime, while quantum gravity lacks a precise formulation and raises unresolved questions about spacetime, black holes, and the universe’s beginning. Liu presents holographic duality as an equivalence between quantum gravity and field theories on fixed spacetime, describing the two sides as different descriptions of the same quantum system.

He discusses the idea that gravity may emerge from non-gravitational systems, citing Sakharov and analogies with hydrodynamics. He then introduces the Weinberg-Witten theorem, which restricts massless particles of high spin in theories with Lorentz-covariant conserved currents or stress tensors. The theorem rules out emergent gravitons in ordinary quantum field theories on the same spacetime but does not invalidate holographic duality because gravity lives in a different, higher-dimensional spacetime. Liu outlines a proof using Lorentz symmetry, helicity states, conserved currents, stress tensors, and rotation eigenvalues.

Obamacare affected many parts of the U.S. health care system, including Medicare, employer-sponsored insurance, the individual market, Medicaid and the uninsured. Republicans planned to repeal spending and revenue provisions such as subsidies, Medicaid expansion, taxes and mandates, with a broader repeal possible except for potentially keeping coverage for children under 26.

Repeal would likely raise Medicare premiums, deductibles and cost-sharing, restore the prescription drug “donut hole,” and end free preventive benefits, though higher-income beneficiaries could pay less in surcharges. Employer mandates would end, possibly affecting some workers near part-time thresholds, and requirements for free contraceptives, preventive screenings, dependent coverage to age 26, benefit limits and small-group protections could be reversed.

The individual market would lose major Obamacare protections and subsidies, including rules on pre-existing conditions, benefit caps, out-of-pocket limits, required benefits, gender pricing and limits on premiums for older people. Medicaid expansion repeal would leave millions of low-income adults without coverage. The individual mandate penalty would also be eliminated.

The passage describes NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture and related CUDA and DGX A100 features. GEMM operations are central to neural network workloads, and A100’s redesigned third-generation Tensor Cores deliver higher mixed-precision throughput than V100. An A100 SM has four Tensor Cores delivering 1024 FP16 FMA operations per clock, while the full GPU has 108 SMs and 432 Tensor Cores, reaching up to 312 TFLOPS dense mixed-precision FP16/FP32 performance.

A100 Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, INT4, binary, TF32, BF16, and FP64. TF32 enables Tensor Core acceleration for FP32 AI training inputs by default, while FP16 and BF16 mixed precision provide higher training throughput. A100 also accelerates HPC workloads with FP64 Tensor Core support, delivering up to 19.5 TFLOPS peak FP64 throughput and 2.5x the FP64 performance of Tesla V100. Mixed-precision iterative refinement using cuSOLVER showed TF32 as the fastest and most robust Tensor Core mode among tested formats.

A100 introduces fine-grained structured sparsity using a 2:4 pattern, allowing Sparse MMA instructions to skip zero values and double Tensor Core throughput. NVIDIA describes a pruning and fine-tuning method for inference that results in virtually no loss in accuracy across evaluated network types.

The architecture includes a combined L1 data cache and shared memory subsystem with 192 KB/SM, separate FP32 and INT32 cores for simultaneous execution, 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, SECDED ECC protection, and a 40 MB L2 cache with 2.3x V100 L2 bandwidth. A100 also adds L2 cache residency controls and Compute Data Compression.

For scaling and utilization, A100 supports Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), partitioning one GPU into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory resources. MIG supports QoS, fault isolation, multi-tenant use cases, VM deployment, and migration of vGPUs between compatible GPU Instances.

A100 includes third-generation NVLink with twelve links and 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, improved error and fault handling, NVJPG hardware JPEG decode, an Optical Flow Accelerator, improved atomics, and five NVDEC units.

CUDA 11 supports A100 features including Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 residency controls, and Cooperative Groups enhancements. DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with NVLink, NVSwitch, Mellanox networking, MIG, and an optimized software stack to support AI, HPC, analytics, and large-scale clustered workloads.

BioRecall is a cross-sectional pilot biobank-recall study designed to collect lifestyle and environmental exposure data and combine it with genotype, biological sample, and clinical outcome data from the Central Finland Biobank. The pilot will invite 1,386 previously genotyped adult biobank donors diagnosed with type 2 diabetes who have consented to recontact. Participants will complete an electronic questionnaire through MyBiobank, with consent collected via REDCap.

The questionnaire covers physical activity, diet, alcohol use, anthropometrics, weight loss history, smoking and substance use, medical history, women’s health, work characteristics, emotional states, sleep, residential environment, and socioeconomic background. Postal code data will be used to link participants to open-source environmental and socioeconomic datasets. Respondents will receive automated feedback on physical activity, diet, waist circumference, work stress, and sleep in relation to recommendations.

Data collection is planned to begin in February 2025. Collected data may be returned to the Central Finland Biobank with participant consent and made available for future approved research through Fingenious®. The study has received favourable ethics review from the University of Jyväskylä and approval from the Central Finland Biobank. If successful, the protocol may be expanded to other donors and Finnish biobanks. Strengths include fully electronic data collection, scalability, broad exposure assessment, and automated feedback; limitations include the pilot’s limited sample size, inclusion of one biobank, and lack of wearable data.

The column reviews Supreme Court relists from the term’s second week. The court denied several petitions, including cases involving ineffective appellate counsel, Seventh Amendment incorporation, school policies on transgender students, Section 230 immunity, FDA cell-processing rules, and California unclaimed-property law, with some denials accompanied by separate opinions.

Nine new relists fall into three groups. Four involve challenges to 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(3), which bars firearm possession by unlawful users of or people addicted to controlled substances. The government seeks review after lower courts found the law unconstitutional as applied in some circumstances.

Another relist, Keathley v. Buddy Ayers Construction, concerns whether judicial estoppel can bar a personal injury suit because the plaintiff failed to disclose the claim in bankruptcy filings. The petition argues the 5th Circuit’s strict approach conflicts with more intent-based approaches in other circuits.

Four additional relists are pro se prisoner petitions, many raising procedural claims. The column notes uncertainty about why some attracted the court’s interest and says remaining relists will return to conference.

Sony prepared to launch the PlayStation 3 in November 2006 amid intense competition from Microsoft’s Xbox 360, which had a one-year head start, and Nintendo’s lower-priced Wii, which targeted a broader audience. The PS3 also served as Sony’s vehicle for promoting Blu-Ray in a standards battle against Toshiba and Microsoft’s HD-DVD, though Sony had previously struggled to establish proprietary formats such as Betamax and UMD.

The case traces the video game industry’s evolution from Atari’s early dominance and collapse, to Nintendo’s rise through quality control and licensing, to Sony’s success with the PlayStation and PS2. Sony gained market share by emphasizing 3D gaming, CD-based software, broad third-party support, and DVD playback in the PS2. By early 2006, the PS2 held 55% of the console market.

Console makers often sold hardware at a loss and earned revenue from software royalties. Game development had become more expensive, blockbuster-driven, and consolidated as publishers acquired studios. Online connectivity became central with Xbox Live, Nintendo’s Virtual Console, and Sony’s PlayStation Network Platform. Sony and Microsoft targeted core gamers, while Nintendo sought to expand the market through simpler, intuitive gameplay.

The industry also faced criticism over violent content, leading to ratings systems, lawsuits, proposed legislation, and scrutiny of the ESRB. Analysts were divided but some projected PS3 leadership through 2010, while Microsoft’s early Xbox 360 sales and Nintendo’s Wii posed significant challenges.

Anthony Rizzo homered and drove in late runs as the Chicago Cubs beat the Pittsburgh Pirates 7-0, but his hard slide into catcher Elias Diaz in the eighth inning drew controversy. The slide, ruled legal after review, led to two runs and Pirates manager Clint Hurdle’s ejection. Diaz stayed in the game and said Rizzo apologized, though he believed the slide was unsafe.

Mike Montgomery, starting in place of injured Yu Darvish, allowed two singles over 5 2/3 scoreless innings. Addison Russell added a pinch-hit two-run homer, while Pittsburgh dropped to 2-8 in its last 10 games. The Cubs recalled Luke Farrell, Pittsburgh released George Kontos, and Pirates closer Felipe Vazquez was held out with forearm discomfort.

DNA origami uses base-pairing between DNA strands to self-assemble nanometer-scale structures. Researchers led by Ralf Jungmann developed a super-resolution microscopy approach using DNA-PAINT to visualize individual strands within DNA origami structures. In their study, a long scaffold strand and shorter staple strands formed flat rectangular nanostructures. DNA-PAINT uses dye-linked imager strands that transiently bind target sequences, producing blinking signals that enable precise localization. The method showed that assembly is generally robust across varying physical conditions, but incorporation efficiency depends on the target position in the structure. Adding staple strands in excess can improve efficiency, though not all sites are occupied in every final structure. The researchers say DNA-PAINT can help optimize DNA nanostructure construction and may support quantitative structural biology measurements.

The passage describes MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 device modules, peripherals, support resources, and packaging information. The PMU generates regulated core supplies, supervises VDD with brown-out reset thresholds, supports multiple power modes, and includes a bandgap reference. The clock module provides internal and external low- and high-frequency oscillators and distributes clocks including MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, MFCLK, LFCLK, ADCCLK, CLK_OUT, HFCLK, and HSCLK.

DMA_B supports two full-feature channels, one basic channel, peripheral triggers, multiple transfer sizes, up to 64k transfers, cascading, stride, gather, early interrupts, and channel interruption. The event manager routes static, DMA, and generic events between peripherals, DMA, and CPU. Flash memory supports in-circuit program/erase, 1KB sectors, and up to 100,000 cycles on selected sectors. SRAM provides zero-wait access, retention through RUN, SLEEP, STOP, and STANDBY, and 1KB-resolution write protection.

GPIO supports up to 45 pins, wake features, input filtering, and multi-bit set/clear/toggle. IOMUX configures pad behavior and pin multiplexing. The ADC supports 12-bit conversions up to 1.6 Msps, internal and external references, internal channels, and RUN, SLEEP, STOP, and STANDBY triggers. Other analog features include a calibrated temperature sensor, VREF with 1.4V and 2.5V internal references or external reference, and a comparator with blanking, wake, fault-handling, input selection, and DAC output support.

Security features include flexible firewalls and CRC-16. Communications peripherals include UART with LIN, FIFOs, DMA, loopback, and programmable baud; I2C with 7/10-bit addressing, multiple modes, up to 1Mbps, SMBus 3.0, wake, and glitch filters; and SPI with controller/peripheral modes, configurable chip select, 4–16 or 7–16 bit frames, FIFOs, DMA, and TI, Motorola, and National Microwire formats.

Watchdogs include an LFSS-based independent watchdog and a windowed watchdog. RTC_B provides calendar counters, alarms, periodic wakeups, calibration, compensation, and clock output. The paper studies modal extensions of lattice semantics, replacing classical Boolean valuations with lattices such as Łukasiewicz, Belnap, finite Boolean algebras, and twist algebras. It focuses mainly on interpreting necessity as the greatest lower bound of values in accessible worlds and examines when modal validity imposes algebraic constraints on the underlying lattice.

After defining lattice semantics, designated values, matrices, modal extensions, and normal modal valuations, the paper proves that for a complete lattice, the normal modal extension is regular exactly when the designated values form a filter and their meet is designated. For finite lattices, regularity is equivalent to the designated values forming a filter.

The paper then characterizes modal formulas in terms of lattice properties. It shows that the validity of \((\Box\varphi \vee \Box\psi) \to \Box(\varphi \vee \psi)\) over all frames is equivalent to the designated values being implicative. For axiom K, \(\Box(\varphi \to \psi) \to (\Box\varphi \to \Box\psi)\), the results depend on the implication used: with strictly deductive implication, validity over all frames is equivalent to the lattice being linear outside the filter; with implication defined as \(-x+y\), validity is tied to implicativity together with anti-monotone, involutive, and down-distributive properties.

An example using twist algebras from Boolean algebras shows how these results apply to paraconsistent semantics. The paper concludes that lattice-based modal structures provide a natural order-theoretic basis for necessity and may support communication between worlds governed by different logics, with future work directed toward finite-model properties.

The passage introduces work on modeling noisy, high-dimensional, nonlinear dynamical systems using transfer operator theory and RKHS methods. It describes dynamic mode decomposition as a Koopman-operator approximation based on linear regression and spectral analysis, useful for nonlinear, stochastic, and high-dimensional systems. It then presents Gaussian process regression as a kernel-based, non-parametric framework with probabilistic predictions and model selection. The paper’s contribution is a Bayesian interpretation of the embedded Perron–Frobenius operator to extend kernel-based DMD with uncertainty estimates, hyperparameter tuning, sparsity, and noisy-data handling. The method is related to EDMD and aims to reduce computational costs through variational free energy techniques while treating lifted operators probabilistically.

The lecture emphasizes that entrepreneurship depends on dynamic planning, creating and capturing value, and answering why the opportunity matters, why now, why the team, and why it might fail. Bob Jones argues that the key requirement for a successful business is customers, not technology, charm, or funding.

Jones describes a failed nutrition bar launch for dialysis patients, where clinicians liked the product but patients did not want or could not afford it, and retail pharmacies resisted carrying it. He attributes the failure to misidentifying the customer. He contrasts this with NiteBite, a product for people with diabetes at risk of nocturnal hypoglycemia. By talking directly with patients, parents, educators, retailers, and wholesalers, the company identified emotional demand, positioned the product as peace of mind, built customer demand, avoided slotting fees, and sold the business successfully.

Jones advises entrepreneurs to identify who will pay, who influences them, what problem they have, how they solve it now, and what benefits they value. He recommends focusing on specific customer segments, testing minimum viable products, making cold calls, and building evidence that customers will pay. Successful products must be unique and important to a defined group.

The American Indian College Fund announced a two-year study, funded by a $600,000 Strada Education Network grant, on the economic and social impact of five North Dakota tribal colleges and universities. The study develops an Atomic Cluster Expansion machine-learning potential for YBa2Cu3O7−x, trained on DFT data including defect-free structures, vacancies, interstitials, oxygen Frenkel pairs, transition-state geometries, expanded lattices, and amorphous-like configurations. The dataset contains 1368 configurations and 545267 atoms. The potential achieves energy and force RMSEs of about 10 meV/atom and 70 meV/Å and outperforms a Buckingham+Coulomb potential in reproducing lattice-parameter behavior, defect energetics, and oxygen migration barriers.

NPT molecular dynamics simulations using the ACE potential reproduce the orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition near 800 K, compared with an experimental value of about 1000 K. The transition is identified as an order-disorder process in the oxygen sublattice: oxygen atoms migrate mainly from CuO-chain O1 sites, and partly from apical O4 sites, to O5 positions between chains, making the a and b directions equivalent. The simulations show increasing O1/O5 occupancy and decreasing O4 occupancy with temperature.

The transition is attributed to entropic disordering, facilitated by reduced oxygen Frenkel-pair formation energies at thermally expanded lattice parameters. Differences from experiment are linked to the simulations conserving oxygen content, while experimental heating involves oxygen loss. The authors conclude that the potential enables accurate simulations of oxygen diffusion and defect processes in YBCO and may support studies of radiation damage recovery and annealing strategies in high-temperature superconducting tapes.

The lecture compares ion traps with neutral atom systems, emphasizing that ions are easier to confine because Coulomb forces allow much deeper traps than magnetic or optical traps for neutral atoms. Both ions and neutral atoms are used for clocks, quantum information, and quantum simulation.

Ions generally require dynamic trapping because static electric fields cannot confine them in all directions. Penning traps use electrostatic axial confinement and magnetic-field-induced cyclotron motion for radial confinement; MIT used them for highly precise ion mass measurements. RF or Paul traps, widely used in ion quantum information, alternate rapidly between confining and anti-confining potentials. The resulting micromotion produces an effective restoring force and trapping potential.

The lecture then explains ion-based quantum computation, focusing on the Cirac-Zoller gate. Single-qubit operations are Rabi oscillations on the Bloch sphere, while two-qubit operations require one ion’s state to affect another’s. The Cirac-Zoller scheme uses the ions’ shared center-of-mass motion as a data bus: information from one ion is swapped into the vibrational state, a controlled phase operation is applied to another ion, and the information is swapped back. This enables two-qubit gates in an ion chain. The scheme is pedagogically important but requires ground-state cooling and is limited by the slow center-of-mass motion; other gates avoid some of these limitations.

The passage reviews the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on inclusive education. It states that AI is increasingly used in education to support teaching, learning, instructional design, research, feedback, personalization, and accessibility. However, desirable outcomes do not result from technology use alone; effective implementation requires understanding its effects, educator involvement, and attention to student needs.

Inclusive education is described as a process that provides equal opportunities for all students regardless of disability, race, ethnicity, location, or background. It requires acceptance, accessibility, assessment reform, curriculum adaptation, supportive environments, and removal of barriers. Challenges include inadequate teacher training, inaccessible digital materials, poor infrastructure, overcrowded classrooms, insufficient resources, limited stakeholder support, labeling, and exclusion of students with special needs.

The passage identifies several benefits of AI for inclusion, including assistive tools such as text-to-speech, speech-to-text, spelling and grammar checkers, word prediction, chatbots, virtual assistants, adaptive learning, automated feedback, student performance monitoring, personalized instruction, and administrative support. AI can help educators identify student weaknesses, improve engagement, support self-directed learning, and provide resources across geographic or economic barriers. It may also support diversity, equity, and inclusion training.

The limitations of AI include biased outputs from biased data, possible reduction in demand for human educators, loss of human interaction, high implementation and maintenance costs, over-reliance on technology, privacy and data security concerns, and physical effects from some technologies. AI cannot fully reproduce human intelligence, creativity, emotion, or understanding of complex human experiences.

The study is non-empirical and based on literature reviewed from September 2023 to March 2024 using PRISMA guidelines and databases including Web of Science, Science Direct, and IEEE Xplore. Its limitations include lack of fieldwork, first-hand experimentation, empirical data, and detailed focus on minority or marginalized groups.

The passage recommends incorporating AI into teaching and learning, making education child-centered and inclusive, promoting active student participation, providing professional development for educators, ensuring safe learning environments, and increasing societal and policy awareness of inclusion.

Cadillac sold 35,020 vehicles globally in September 2017, marking 16 consecutive months of growth and a 16.5% year-over-year increase. Year-to-date sales reached 256,613, up 20.9% from 2016. This study examined racial differences in the relationship between blood pressure and longitudinal cognitive performance in older Black and White adults. Data came from three harmonized aging and dementia cohorts: MARS, MAP, and Black Clinical Core. Participants were at least 55 years old, self-identified as Black or White, and had at least two cognitive assessments and two blood pressure readings. The sample included 2,284 participants categorized by race and blood pressure status: normal, high, or variable systolic blood pressure.

Cognition was assessed annually across global cognition and five domains: episodic memory, visuospatial ability, processing speed, semantic memory, and working memory. Linear mixed effects models adjusted for age, sex, education, and baseline diagnosis.

Across all groups, greater time from baseline and older baseline age were associated with cognitive decline. Among participants with normal blood pressure, rates of cognitive decline generally did not differ between Black and White adults. White adults with high blood pressure showed faster decline than Black adults with high blood pressure in global cognition, processing speed, semantic memory, and working memory. White adults with variable blood pressure showed faster decline than Black adults with variable blood pressure across global cognition and all five cognitive domains.

Exploratory analyses indicated that the lower rate of decline observed in older Black adults was not explained by lower baseline cognitive scores. The authors note limitations including lack of medication adherence data and incomplete assessment of medication use. The study concludes that elevated and variable blood pressure were associated with greater cognitive decline in older White adults compared with older Black adults, highlighting racial differences in the relationship between blood pressure and cognitive aging.

In Wiechmann v Wiechmann, the Michigan Court of Appeals affirmed a divorce judgment awarding shared legal custody, physical custody of the two older children to the plaintiff father, and physical custody of the younger twin boys to the defendant mother. Although a custody specialist recommended that the mother receive custody of all four children, the trial court reviewed the statutory best-interest factors and found the parties largely equal, with one factor slightly favoring the father. The Court of Appeals held that courts should consider the effect of separating siblings, and that siblings should usually remain together, but the best interests of each individual child control when keeping them together would be contrary to those interests. Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) is an AMD firmware feature for secure, non-persistent runtime updates to selected AMD-provided binary firmware components and settings without BIOS reflash or system reset. It targets high-priority runtime issues, can reduce downtime, and does not patch x86 BIOS code such as SMM, AGESA, UEFI, or run-once boot code. SFS updates are interim steps between BIOS releases and must be reapplied after reboot.

Customers are responsible for testing patches and operating an SFS Deployment Agent that communicates with the AMD Security Processor (ASP). SFS packages apply only to specified firmware and patch levels, are AMD-signed, and may optionally be customer co-signed. BIOS support must be enabled through configuration flags, and customer signing keys must be provided during early boot if co-signing is required.

SFS tracks update state using the SFS Patch Level (SFSPL), firmware component versions and Security Patch Levels (SPL), and a System Patch Level (SYSPL) for run-once changes. Packages validate existing versions before applying updates and should not apply if any portion cannot complete. Patchable items include registers, firmware images, and portions of firmware packages.

SFS commands use a 2MB-aligned TEE extended command buffer and ASP mailbox registers. The ASP protects the DRAM region, verifies customer and AMD signatures, loads and runs the executable patch, updates patch level information, and returns status. Commands also allow software to retrieve firmware version and patch level information.

SFS package names align to AGESA releases and use monotonically increasing numbers. Updates are designed to run alongside x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact, though some operations, such as SEV firmware updates, may require affected virtual machines to stop and restart.

Marco Gonzales pitched 6 2/3 innings without allowing an earned run as the Seattle Mariners beat the Texas Rangers 2-1 for their ninth win in 10 games. Seattle improved to 13 games above .500 and leads the majors with 16 one-run wins. The passage examines distance education and artificial intelligence in education, especially in contexts such as the Covid-19 pandemic, which forced many countries to interrupt face-to-face schooling and adopt online alternatives. Using a literature review method, it discusses artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, algorithms, artificial neural networks, and examples such as IBM Watson, AlphaGo, BabyX, and Google Car.

The text describes artificial intelligence in education as applicable to personalized teaching, student support, assessment, data management, games, and intelligent education systems. These systems may adapt instruction to learners through domain, pedagogy, and learner models. The passage proposes three forms of AI-related education: AI-supported face-to-face education, face-to-face education conducted by AI, and simulation-based education with AI. It also distinguishes supervised systems designed by humans from unsupervised deep-learning systems in which AI may determine educational content and methods.

Possible learning environments include classroom-based AI instruction and virtual or simulation-based education, including augmented reality and future computer–human neural integration. The discussion identifies potential benefits such as efficiency, reduced cost and risk, individualized learning, improved motivation, and support for decision-making. It also notes risks including privacy problems, cyberattacks, social isolation, unemployment among educators, manipulation, psychological effects, and difficulty distinguishing virtual from real environments.

The conclusion states that although face-to-face education remains important, alternative systems are needed for disruptions such as pandemics and disasters. Artificial intelligence-based education requires further research and serious discussion, particularly because technological development may make computers increasingly central to education.

FCA data from its 2017 Financial Lives Survey shows up to 70% of adults planning to access defined contribution pensions within two years had not been asked by providers about their plans. Two thirds had not received advice from a pension provider adviser. Among those not taking advice, 40% felt able to decide alone and 10% cited fees. Respondents expected main retirement income from the state pension (33%), DC pots (21%) or final salary pensions (15%).

Taxify will launch in Sydney from Tuesday, its first entry into the Australian market, offering half-priced fares for one month. The company has more than 4000 registered drivers in Sydney and charges drivers 15 per cent commission, lower than Uber. Founder Markus Villig says its model is based on fairness and transparency. Taxify operates in 20 countries and is backed by Didi Chuxing.

State officials held a groundbreaking for the Mauka Concourse at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport. The $220 million project will add gates, larger aircraft capacity, passenger areas, restrooms, agricultural screening, and 260,000 square feet of environmentally friendly space. Completion is expected by late 2020 as part of a $1.3 billion modernization.

Research cited in the passage suggests that improving school air quality with portable air cleaners and ventilation upgrades can raise test scores, reduce absenteeism and improve health. Evidence includes the Aliso Canyon case, where schools receiving air purifiers saw math and English gains at far lower cost than class-size reduction, and studies linking air cleaners to lower absenteeism and illness. The passage argues that cleaner air supports cognition, health, attendance and equity, especially for low-income students in older or more polluted schools. It recommends reconnecting existing devices, installing filters, piloting broader programs, monitoring outcomes, and supporting research, funding and standards for school indoor air quality.

Index Markets Research’s Global Plastic Granules Market report analyzes industry definitions, applications, manufacturing technology, market size, trends, segmentation, volume, revenue, costs, production capacity, and regional demand. El texto analiza el neuromarketing aplicado al sector audiovisual, definido como el uso de técnicas neurocientíficas para comprender la conducta humana en mercados. Su interés aumenta por los cambios en el consumo audiovisual, la competencia mediática y la búsqueda de mayor eficacia y retorno de inversión. Empresas internacionales ya lo aplican en contenidos, promoción, publicidad, videojuegos y cine.

El estudio se centra en España y plantea que emerge una figura profesional vinculada al neuromarketing audiovisual. Se realizaron 18 entrevistas en profundidad a consultoras, representantes del sector audiovisual, neurocientíficos y académicos. También se identificaron cinco consultoras españolas activas en neuromarketing.

Los resultados indican que el estudio neurocientífico del consumidor audiovisual es viable, aunque presenta límites éticos, metodológicos y de interpretación. La investigación requiere equipos multidisciplinares con perfiles de neurociencia, marketing, comunicación y, en algunos casos, ingeniería biomédica. No se considera adecuado hablar de un experto integral único.

En España, el neuromarketing audiovisual es incipiente y se concentra principalmente en Atresmedia y Mediaset España. Las consultoras ofrecen servicios de análisis de contenidos y mejora de bloques publicitarios. Mediaset lo aplica sobre todo a ficción en prime time y Atresmedia a publicidad, tras abandonar una línea de análisis de contenidos. TVE habría usado estas técnicas, pero las dejó por motivos económicos.

Las productoras de cine y televisión muestran interés, especialmente para medir engagement y reducir sesgos de métodos tradicionales, pero no suelen invertir por falta de recursos y cultura investigadora. La evolución futura se considera positiva, condicionada por avances tecnológicos, mejor interpretación de datos, estandarización, abaratamiento y demostración de eficacia en términos de retorno de inversión.

Research published in Nature Climate Change describes recent sudden ecosystem shifts across Australia caused by gradual climate change combined with extreme weather events. Despite many ecosystems being adapted to climate variability and remaining relatively undisturbed, rising temperatures, more intense heatwaves, longer fire seasons, rainfall changes and unusual droughts are overwhelming their resilience. Case studies include kelp forests shifting after a marine heatwave, wildfire damage to Gondwanan refugia, Murray River floodplain forest dieback, alpine forest conversion to shrubland, arid-zone boom-and-bust events, and mangrove dieback in the Gulf of Carpentaria. Most had little prior human disturbance, showing pristine systems are not necessarily resilient. The passage says ecosystem collapse is difficult to predict, interventions may be costly and uncertain, and many apparently healthy ecosystems may be near tipping points.

This retrospective cohort study used All of Us Research Program data to predict healthy aging among adults aged 50 and older using social determinants of health and EHR data. Healthy aging was defined by absence of comorbidities, mild cognitive impairment, and assisted living status among older age thresholds. Three models were tested: logistic regression, multilayer perceptron, and XGBoost. In the primary cohort of about 99,936 participants, 44% met the healthy aging definition. XGBoost with oversampling performed best, with AUROC about 0.795 in the primary cohort and 0.862 in the secondary cohort, outperforming logistic regression and MLP. Fairness assessment showed similar predictive values across race and gender groups. SHAP analysis identified health insurance type as the strongest predictor, followed by employment status, substance use, and health insurance coverage. The study concluded that machine learning models using SDOH can predict healthy aging and that health insurance is a key factor associated with healthy aging, while noting limitations including definitions of healthy aging, potential selection bias, and unmeasured confounders.
