On Oct. 22, 2001, multiple news reports covered Enron after the SEC requested information on related-party transactions involving limited partnerships run by CFO Andrew Fastow and other executives. Enron said it would cooperate and stated that auditors, attorneys, and its board had reviewed and approved the arrangements, which it said were disclosed in SEC filings. Enron shares fell about 21%, reaching multiyear lows, amid concerns over the partnerships, a recent $618 million quarterly loss, $1.01 billion in charges and writedowns, and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity tied to repurchasing 55 million shares.

Shareholder lawsuits alleged Enron’s board breached fiduciary duties and that the company and officers concealed or misrepresented facts about the partnerships, which allegedly created conflicts of interest and caused losses. Analysts cited concerns about Enron’s credibility, debt ratings, and possible costs of unwinding affiliated entities. Separately, broader U.S. stocks closed higher on better-than-expected earnings despite anthrax concerns, while UniPrime announced a letter of intent involving a wind park lease owned by Enron Wind Development.

IES Holdings’ stock has nearly doubled year to date and outperformed infrastructure and Russell 2000 peers. Despite challenges in its residential division, data center projects are supporting growth in its next two largest divisions. Backlog has exceeded $2 billion and is growing over 20% year over year, with stronger cash flow and record cash balances. However, the article says the stock appears overextended, with a weak free cash flow yield and increased insider sales.

Institute boss Kevin Deery expressed frustration after a third consecutive draw, against Larne, saying his side deserved to win but lacked luck and missed chances. He cited two recent own-goal scorers, poor decision-making in both boxes, and near misses from Ciaron Harkin, Gareth Brown and Dean Curry, while noting Institute remain in the top six with 13 games left.

The study simulates replacing ICE vehicles with BEVs using one year of telematics data from 10,441 private car users in Asti, Italy, covering over 10 million cleaned trips and 98.9 million km. Trips are replicated without changing schedules or routes across four BEV models and four charging policies: workplace AC charging, low-SoC AC charging, overnight AC charging, and low-SoC DC fast charging.

Users typically make fewer than five trips per active day, drive a median of 40 km, and use cars less than two hours on over 90% of active days. Results show that BEV suitability depends strongly on vehicle range and charging behavior. Workplace-only charging performs worst, while DC fast charging at low SoC performs best. With the Audi A6 e-tron under the best policy, 95% of users can complete at least 99% of trips, and 72% can complete all trips. Overnight charging with the Fiat 500e is suitable for 35% of users.

Charging frequency also varies: for the Audi A6 e-tron, low-SoC charging policies require fewer monthly sessions than overnight charging. Scenario 3 provides the highest post-trip SoC levels, averaging above 70%. The study concludes that many users could already adopt BEVs, but current technology and charging assumptions do not satisfy all users. Limitations include simplified consumption and charging assumptions, presumed charger availability, no cost analysis, and lack of validation in other regions.

The ACC Tournament concluded a two-year run at Barclays Center with Virginia defeating North Carolina 71-63 for the championship. The passage highlights Virginia’s title, North Carolina’s win over Duke, Duke-North Carolina’s Brooklyn matchup, Marvin Bagley III’s performance, Clemson’s strong season, and interest in bringing the tournament back to Barclays Center.

The Maui News reported that former Maui County Councilmember and 2018 mayoral candidate Mike Victorino was involved in an April 13 collision on West Papa Avenue that injured two teenage males. Police and Joycelyn Victorino said alcohol and speeding were not factors, and the injuries were nonlife-threatening. Victorino stopped and waited for authorities. Police said the pedestrians were not in a crosswalk, while the mother of the older teen said her son reported they were in one.

The passage is an Enron media roundup from Feb. 6, 2002, covering widening investigations into Enron’s collapse. Reports say Jeffrey Skilling was expected to testify before Congress and not invoke the Fifth Amendment, while Andrew Fastow was scheduled to appear and Kenneth Lay faced subpoenas after canceling voluntary testimony. William Powers told congressional panels that Enron’s partnerships hid losses, inflated earnings, enriched executives, and raised concerns known to senior leadership. Lawmakers also examined employee retirement losses, executive bonuses, Arthur Andersen’s role, document shredding, and calls for stronger retirement protections.

Other articles report Enron’s debtor-in-possession financing shrinking, Enron Broadband owing back taxes, Enron fighting the Houston Astros’ attempt to reclaim stadium naming rights, and Spain’s energy regulator investigating Enron’s Spanish distribution operations. Additional commentary discusses broader investor distrust, corporate accounting concerns, bond-market “Enronization,” whistleblower Sherron Watkins, and satirical reactions to Enron’s collapse.

Linebackers need toughness, athleticism, and intelligence because they play a central role in defensive alignment, run defense, and pass defense. Positioned behind the defensive line and in front of the safeties, they often relay sideline calls and are considered the “quarterback of the defense.” The name comes from their alignment behind the defensive line and their original role as run-support backing.

Common linebacker terms include LB, backer, Sam, Mike, Will, and Jack. Key skills include vision, agility, change of direction, block shedding, explosiveness, tackling, strength, violent hands, and high motor. Typical body estimates range from 5’10” to 6’5” and 215–255 pounds with a lean-muscular build.

Notable linebackers mentioned are Ray Lewis, Chuck Bednarik, and Lawrence Taylor, all Pro Football Hall of Fame inductees with major awards and championships. In the NFL, inside linebacker value has declined with more spread and passing offenses, but versatile linebackers who can rush, cover, and stop the run remain valuable because they create defensive flexibility and matchup problems.

The Canadian dollar rose to nearly 75.50 U.S. cents Wednesday, up about 2% from last week, as markets reacted to signs of economic strength despite the Bank of Canada’s apparent preference for a weaker currency to support exports. The loonie has fluctuated this year, hitting a low of 72.73 U.S. cents on May 4. CIBC economist Andrew Grantham said the currency lacks clear direction amid mixed signals. Oil prices and the Canada-U.S. interest rate gap have pressured the loonie, but strong economic data, including 3.7% annualized first-quarter growth, has raised expectations of a Bank of Canada rate hike. CIBC now expects a rate increase in the fourth quarter rather than 2018.

Great Southern Storm named an initial 45-player colts squad under new coach Glynn Verbruggen for next month’s Great Southern Colts Carnival in Kulin. Verbruggen replaces Phil Gilbert, who coached seven of the past eight years and moved to Perth. The squad includes league regulars, State 16 players Heath Spinks and Jacob Blight, and several State Country colts representatives. North Albany has 12 players, Railways eight, and Albany and Royals seven each. The squad will train at Railways on June 4 and 11 before the final travelling team is selected.

The study examined whether role-taking and literacy-based interventions could reduce the influence of demographic and appearance-based cues on trust and risk-taking in social engineering contexts. Participants were Arab or Middle Eastern adults recruited through Prolific and assigned to persuader, persuadee, literacy, or control groups. They evaluated hotspot-sharing scenarios involving personas differing by age, gender, ethnicity, and attire before and one week after the intervention.

Repeated-measures ANOVAs showed no significant intervention effects on trust or risk-taking across persona factors, with Bayes Factors generally supporting the null hypothesis. Word-of-mouth measures also showed no significant change. Issue involvement changed significantly, though not driven by a specific group. Participant feedback suggested the intervention was engaging and encouraged reflection, but the findings indicate that short-term role-taking and literacy methods may be insufficient to alter deeply ingrained demographic and appearance-based biases. Future research should explore longer-term, more immersive interventions.

CSU’s Board of Governors heard feedback on the first two on-campus gamedays. ASCSU President Josh Silva said students lacked awareness of the tailgating lot and often used it only for parking; ASCSU plans rebranding and pre-game programming to increase use. Athletics Director Joe Parker reported attendance of 37,583 for the first game and 27,038 for the second. Queuing and concession congestion improved by the second game. Parker said transportation planning worked well, with student re-parking largely successful despite 50 vehicles towed each weekend from campus gameday lots. Similar towing occurred in nearby permit neighborhoods. Transit use exceeded expectations, with 7,000 attendees using gameday transit for the first game, and post-game traffic was not overwhelmed.

District and Sessions Judge Nasir Khan Yousafzai sentenced four convicts in separate murder cases in Zhob. Shehzado received the death penalty and a Rs. 200,000 fine, while Ajab Khan, Fateh Khan, and Dilbar Khan received 25-year prison terms and fines.

Allen Iverson discussed his memoir “Misunderstood” on ESPN’s “First Take,” saying his lowest point was his divorce from Tawanna Turner, which became final in 2013 as his NBA career ended. Iverson said the experience prompted self-reevaluation, helped him recognize alcohol as a problem, and contributed to rebuilding his marriage. He also reflected on his influence on younger NBA players.

Texas educators, parents and experts worry a new law replacing STAAR with three shorter tests may increase student stress and testing time rather than reduce it. The system, starting in 2027-28, includes beginning-, middle- and end-of-year exams, bans some practice tests, and requires faster score reporting. Critics say school accountability ratings will still heavily depend on the end-of-year test, while broader measures like extracurriculars and workforce training will not count. Supporters say the changes will monitor growth and reduce over-testing. Some educators want relaxed testing protocols, more teacher input, and use of existing assessments like MAP, which they say are less stressful.

The passage frames the “Berlin-Bagdad” problem as Germany’s potential organization of Central Europe and the Middle East under its political and military influence, especially through control over Poles, Czechs, South Slavs, and Bulgaria. It argues that the United States should not oppose economic or cultural unification in Central Europe, but should oppose imperialistic control by Berlin, Vienna, and Budapest using the region’s resources for aggressive foreign policy.

The current system is described as resting on shared interests among ruling powers in Berlin, Vienna, Budapest, Sofia, and Constantinople, including the subjection of national groups, German control over Austria-Hungary’s external affairs and resources, preservation of German-Magyar dominance, Bulgaria’s grievances from the Treaty of Bucharest, Turkey’s reliance on Germany, and wartime debts to Germany.

The passage identifies two major assets for disestablishing a Prussian-dominated Middle Europe: economic pressure and conditions within Austria-Hungary. Control over raw materials, markets, and communications could threaten Germany with postwar industrial hardship while offering hope of world cooperation, creating bargaining power. In Austria-Hungary, nationalist discontent among Czechs and South Slavs, combined with the monarchy’s desire to preserve its territory, support disarmament, and join a league of nations, could be used to reduce dependence on Berlin without fully dismembering the empire.

The passage introduces LAPIS, an MLIR-based compiler framework designed to improve performance, portability, and productivity for computational science and AI/ML applications. Traditional CSE codes often use C++ frameworks such as Kokkos, while AI/ML codes commonly use Python frameworks such as PyTorch and TensorFlow, making integration difficult and requiring boilerplate. LAPIS addresses this by compiling Python-based ML functions into Kokkos-based C++ source code that can be integrated into scientific applications.

LAPIS provides an automatic lowering pipeline from high-level MLIR to portable parallel Kokkos C++ and introduces a custom Kokkos dialect representing Kokkos constructs, Kokkos Kernels operations, hierarchical parallelism, synchronization, and memory behavior. It supports inputs from torch-mlir and MPACT using linalg-on-tensors dialects. Its contributions include Kokkos-inspired MLIR operations, mappings for sparse and dense linear algebra, lowering passes for accelerators, a portable memory model including DualView-like behavior, and a C++ emitter.

The framework lowers operations such as dense matrix multiplication, matrix-vector multiplication, and sparse linear algebra to Kokkos or Kokkos Kernels. It maps MLIR parallel loops to Kokkos execution policies, estimates parallelism for performance heuristics, and inserts synchronization where needed. The work demonstrates LAPIS on sparse and dense linear algebra kernels and on coupling CSE with AI/ML use cases, showing performance on AMD MI300A, NVIDIA H100 GPUs, and Intel Granite Rapids CPUs.

Chipotle released queso dip on Sept. 12, but customers criticized its price and taste on Twitter. Chips and queso cost $3.95 small or $6.25 large. Spokesman Chris Arnold said test markets responded positively and there are no plans to lower the price because it uses real, whole ingredients.

The passage introduces a paper on constructing strong pseudorandom unitaries in the quantum Haar random oracle model (QHROM). It reviews prior work on pseudorandom unitaries, pseudorandom states, idealized quantum models, and earlier results in inverseless QHROM. The paper’s main theorem states that strong pseudorandom unitaries exist in QHROM.

The construction uses a Haar random oracle \(U\) and defines \(G^U(1^\lambda,k)=X_{k_3}UX_{k_2}UX_{k_1}\), with a key split into three \(\lambda\)-bit strings. The proof replaces Haar-random unitaries with path-recording isometries, compares real and ideal experiments, and introduces an approximate isometry \(S\) that merges independent query databases while simulating keys. Security is shown through a query-by-query progress analysis and a sequence of hybrids moving from the real construction to two independent Haar-random unitaries. The passage also defines notation, strong pseudorandom unitaries, adversarial oracle access, and elements of the path-recording framework.

The State Bar of Michigan e-Journal for May 23, 2001 lists case summaries in bankruptcy, civil rights, constitutional law, criminal law, employment and labor, family law, insurance, litigation, municipal law, negligence and intentional tort, and real property. It notes one Sixth Circuit Bankruptcy Appellate Panel opinion, In re Hood, holding that the Tennessee Student Assistance Corporation was not immune from a bankruptcy dischargeability action. Other summarized decisions address racial discrimination claims, criminal jury instructions and discovery sanctions, termination of parental rights, insurance loss payable clauses, supplemental witness lists, zoning variances, premises liability, defamation, and negligence claims. The issue also includes classified advertisements, fields of practice listings, bar events, archived e-Journal links, and contact information.

Peggy Mahoney forwarded an Energy Central Deregulation Public Forum email dated August 25, 2000. The new forum question asks whether policy should encourage natural gas exploration and production on federal lands and the continental shelf to meet future electricity demand. The previous question addressed San Diego Gas & Electric bill increases and whether generators manipulated wholesale markets or price caps were needed. Responses varied: many attributed price spikes to supply-demand imbalance, flawed deregulation, weather, fuel costs, and lack of generation or transmission; many opposed price caps as harmful to investment and conservation, while some alleged manipulation or collusion and supported caps or cost-based pricing.

Paul Clement is set to become Swansea manager after Bayern Munich allowed him to speak to the club. Swansea chose Carlo Ancelotti’s assistant to replace Bob Bradley and hope to finalize a deal until 2019, with a £30m transfer budget planned. The club sit 19th in the Premier League after heavy defeats and 44 goals conceded in 19 games. Clement previously worked with Ancelotti at PSG, Real Madrid and Bayern, and had a short spell managing Derby.

CEMEX grew from a Mexican cement company into a global building materials leader through acquisitions and a disciplined integration model called the CEMEX Way. Under CEO Lorenzo Zambrano, the company prepared for globalization by divesting non-core assets, improving communications and information systems, and strengthening operational capabilities. Its international expansion began with Spain in 1992, followed by acquisitions in Latin America, Asia, the United States, Europe, and Australia.

CEMEX used acquisitions not only for growth but also to standardize processes, transfer best practices, and learn from acquired firms. The CEMEX Way emphasized global knowledge management, benchmarking, standardized processes, information technology, and innovation while allowing local flexibility. Post-merger integration teams helped reduce integration times and identify practices worth adopting across the company.

Major deals included Southdown in 2000, RMC in 2005, and Rinker in 2007. The RMC acquisition expanded CEMEX into ready-mix concrete and broader developed markets, while the Rinker deal made it one of the world’s largest building materials suppliers. By 2007, CEMEX had 65,000 employees, operations in 50 countries, and $21.7 billion in annual revenue, though its share price fell in 2008 amid the global downturn, credit crisis, and leverage from the Rinker acquisition.

A federal judge dismissed Drake’s defamation lawsuit over Kendrick Lamar’s “Not Like Us,” ruling that the “certified pedophile” lyric was nonactionable opinion and hyperbole in a heated rap battle. The judge granted Universal Music Group’s motion to dismiss claims including defamation, harassment and deceptive acts. Drake plans to appeal.

The Hungarian revolt of 1956 was a nationwide uprising whose Soviet repression became a turning point for the Soviet Union and NATO. After Hungary came under Soviet control, Communists led by Mátyás Rákosi eliminated opponents and imposed collectivization and rapid industrialization. Discontent grew after Stalin’s death, Khrushchev’s de-Stalinization, economic failure, repression, and events in Poland suggesting national Communism might be tolerated. A student rally in Budapest on 22 October issued demands for a similar system, and violence erupted the next day after state security police fired on crowds. Revolutionary councils called for nationalism, neutrality, and Soviet troop withdrawal. Imre Nagy was reappointed prime minister, and Soviet representatives briefly appeared to accept Hungarian sovereignty, but Soviet forces were preparing invasion. With world attention diverted by the Suez crisis, Soviet troops surrounded Budapest and attacked on 3/4 November. Hungarian resistance was defeated by 30 November, with about 25,000 Hungarians and 7,000 Soviet soldiers killed.

Springfield, Massachusetts, police officer Conrad Lariviere faces disciplinary action after commenting “Hahahaha love this” on Facebook about the Charlottesville car attack that killed counter-protester Heather Heyer and injured 19 others. Lariviere later apologized, calling it a “stupid comment,” and denied being racist. Police Commissioner John Barbieri opened an internal investigation, and Mayor Domenic Sarno condemned the remarks. The driver, James Alex Fields Jr., was arrested and charged with second-degree murder.

Williams & Connolly confirmed hackers accessed a small number of attorney email accounts through a zero-day attack but said there is no evidence confidential client data was taken from other IT systems. The firm said the hackers are believed to be linked to a nation-state actor involved in recent attacks on law firms and companies, and that it has blocked the threat with no evidence of ongoing unauthorized network traffic.

The DAWN-PLASMA study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 multicenter trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of convalescent plasma plus standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. It was conducted under IEC approval, informed consent requirements, Declaration of Helsinki principles, and ICH GCP guidelines. The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15; secondary endpoints included clinical status, ventilation or death, thromboembolism, transfusion reactions, safety, quality of life, adverse events, laboratory data, and vital signs. Eligible participants were adults with confirmed or clinically supported SARS-CoV-2 infection and respiratory illness criteria; key exclusions included mechanical ventilation at randomization, unacceptable safety risk, severe plasma allergy, treatment restrictions excluding ventilation/intubation, or recent anti-CD20 therapy. Participants were randomized 2:1 to standard of care with convalescent plasma or standard of care alone. Plasma recipients received 800–1000 mL in four doses, with the first dose within 12 hours of randomization. Five patients withdrew before intervention and one was a screen failure; all six were substituted, and no patients were lost to follow-up after intervention.

The passage describes digital video output terminal functions: signals carry 8 MSBs of G/Y/YC, B/CB/C, and R/CR video data depending on RGB, YUV444, Y/C, or BT.656 modes. It also defines pin notation, internal pull states after reset, and I/O supply voltage specification references.

Coppin State University in Maryland says its Expand Eagle Nation program, which offers in-state tuition to students from 41 states and territories without an HBCU and the District of Columbia, has helped more than quadruple out-of-state enrollment over two years. Qualifying students increased from 81 to 195 in 2024, then to 416 in this fall’s incoming class of 1,000. Overall enrollment is up 26 percent, including in-state growth, which officials attribute partly to increased attention from the program.

Coppin has expanded recruitment through high school visits, advertising, transfer partnerships, and outreach to regional college-access organizations. Officials say the program has increased the university’s name recognition and brought more geographic diversity to a student body that historically came mostly from within 50 miles. The growth comes as many colleges seek new student populations ahead of a projected national decline in high school graduates, while HBCUs are also seeing increased interest.

Coppin says it prepared for the growth by coordinating course and faculty capacity, building a new dorm, and using off-campus apartments with resident assistants and shuttles. Admissions officials said one challenge has been convincing families that the tuition offer is real.

A Democratic change in government is presented as a national call for reform rather than mere party victory. The passage praises the nation’s wealth, enterprise, moral energy, and system of government, but argues that these have been accompanied by waste, exploitation, neglected natural resources, human suffering in industry, and government used for private interests. It calls for restoration: reforming tariffs, banking and currency, industry, agriculture, conservation, public health, food safety, and labor conditions while preserving property and individual rights. The speaker emphasizes justice, careful action, and humane government, declaring the moment a day of dedication to the needs, hopes, and lives of the people.

Indianapolis Public Schools is inviting parents and community members to discuss a proposal to close three high schools by the 2018-2019 school year. A taskforce report cites a long decline in enrollment, with all seven high schools under capacity. Public meetings will continue through April and May. The administration is expected to recommend specific closures by June, and the board will vote in September.

The passage introduces LG-CD, a language-guided remote sensing change detection model that integrates visual and textual information. It uses a pre-trained SAM2 encoder with multi-level adapters to extract and fine-tune multi-scale bi-temporal image features, and CLIP to encode natural language prompts. A text fusion attention module aligns word-level and global text embeddings with visual features, guiding attention to relevant change regions. A visual-semantic fusion decoder then combines semantic and visual information to produce change detection masks. The method aims to improve accuracy, robustness, generalization, and multi-scale semantic understanding compared with unimodal visual approaches.

The White House said it was not defending Roseanne Barr’s racist tweet, but President Trump and Sarah Sanders argued ABC owed Trump an apology for derogatory comments aired about him. Trump tweeted that Disney CEO Bob Iger called Valerie Jarrett after Barr’s comments but had not apologized to him. Sanders said Trump was highlighting media hypocrisy and cited comments by Jemele Hill, Joy Behar and Keith Olbermann. She called Barr’s remarks inappropriate while saying Trump was focused on media bias and other issues, including a “right to try” bill.

The passage describes TPS7H500x-SP radiation-hardness-assured current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. The EN pin can enable the device through VLDO, an external signal, a PGOOD signal, or a VIN resistor divider for programmable UVLO. UVLO resistor values should be optimized for startup, with the UVLO value about 75% or less of input voltage.

Each device uses an internal 1.23-V reference on REFCAP, divided to 0.613 V for the error amplifier, and requires a 470-nF REFCAP capacitor. The controllers use a transconductance error amplifier, resistor-divider output voltage programming, and soft start controlled by a capacitor on SS. Switching frequency can be set by internal oscillator, external synchronization, or primary-secondary mode. Internal oscillator mode uses an RT resistor for 100 kHz to 2 MHz switching; external synchronization requires RT floating and a SYNC clock at twice the desired switching frequency. Primary-secondary mode synchronizes two controllers through SYNC and can support independent synchronized converters or interleaved parallel operation.

The TPS7H500x-SP family provides configurable primary switching outputs, synchronous rectifier outputs, dead time, leading-edge blanking, duty-cycle limits, current sensing, hiccup-mode overcurrent protection, external fault protection, slope compensation, and frequency compensation. OUTA/OUTB and SRA/SRB have about 150-mA peak capability, so external gate drivers are recommended. Synchronous rectifier outputs remain off during soft start until SS exceeds 1 V. Some devices support programmable dead time and leading-edge blanking; pulse skipping helps address minimum on-time limits. Duty-cycle limits are configured with DCL, with supported options varying by device.

The CS_ILIM pin senses current for PWM operation and overcurrent protection. When CS_ILIM exceeds 1.05 V, cycle-by-cycle limiting begins and hiccup timing is controlled by a capacitor on HICC. The FAULT pin allows external protections; exceeding its threshold stops switching until the fault clears and a delay expires. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C typical and restarts below 160°C typical.

The application section presents a TPS7H5001-SP synchronous push-pull converter design using GaN devices at 500 kHz, including component selection for RT, feedback resistors, dead time, leading-edge blanking, soft start, transformer, FETs, RCD clamp, output inductor, output capacitance and filtering, current sense, hiccup capacitor, compensation, and slope compensation. Power supply guidance specifies a 4-V to 14-V input range, bypass capacitance, and ceramic capacitors near the controller. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing high-current and switching loops, routing sensitive traces away from noisy nodes, placing bypass and compensation parts close to the device, filtering CS_ILIM if needed, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS. The passage also lists related documentation, update notification resources, support forums, ESD cautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable-information disclaimers.

Kyle Shanahan said minicamp practice was competitive, with both offense and defense showing positives and areas to clean up. He said his father, Mike Shanahan, observes film, offers ideas, and provides trusted input but is not part of the staff. Shanahan described balancing head-coaching and offensive duties as fast-paced and said he plans to take time away with family before training camp. He emphasized play-action as important to his offense because it pressures defenses, supports the run game, helps the offensive line and quarterbacks, creates explosive plays, and keeps defenses honest.

An Enron email compiles July 17–18, 2001 news articles on California energy issues, including competing legislative plans to prevent Southern California Edison’s bankruptcy, PG&E’s lawsuit seeking compensation for state-seized power contracts, criticism of utility rescue plans, state power purchases and surplus sales at losses, energy conservation efforts, consumer inflation tied partly to electricity prices, and Duke Energy’s higher earnings from trading and wholesale power.

A federal judge ruled that Nirvana’s 1991 album cover showing Spencer Elden as a naked baby underwater was not child pornography and dismissed his lawsuit. Judge Fernando Olguin found the image was not lascivious, comparing it to a family photo of a nude child bathing.

Prof. Cyril Dim describes cervical cancer as a malignant disease of the cervix, the neck of the womb. He says almost all cases are caused by sexually transmitted human papillomavirus, especially high-risk types such as HPV 16 and 18, which are included in vaccines. Precancerous cervical changes usually have no symptoms but can be detected through Pap smears and treated to prevent invasive cancer.

Early cervical cancer may also have no symptoms, but later signs include bleeding after sex, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, abnormal bleeding, pelvic pain, weight loss, weakness, anaemia, and loss of bladder or bowel control if it spreads. Diagnosis requires examination and confirmation through tissue biopsy and histology. Pap smears are recommended regularly for women of reproductive age.

Dim says early-stage cervical cancer can be cured with radical surgery or radiotherapy, while late-stage disease is managed mainly with radiotherapy and sometimes chemotherapy to prolong life. Survival depends on the stage at presentation; many patients in Nigeria present late. He notes that cervical cancer is common in developing countries because structured screening programmes are lacking. In Nigeria, it is a major cancer among women, with an estimated 15,000 new cases and about 10,000 deaths yearly.

The passage also lists risk factors including HPV infection, many sexual partners, smoking, birth control pills, and early sexual contact, and notes that HPV vaccination can help prevent infection with common cancer-associated types.

The lecture focuses on post-flop poker strategy, especially continuation betting, calling, raising, implied odds, and bluffing. The instructor explains that players often check to the preflop aggressor because that player’s range is stronger and can include hands like aces or kings. Bet sizing should generally be a meaningful fraction of the pot, often increasing from flop to turn to river, while very small bets are discouraged because they give opponents opportunities to check-raise cheaply.

A central concept presented is that post-flop bets should usually be either value bets with strong hands or bluffs with weak hands that can make better hands fold. Medium-strength hands are often better checked or called because betting may fold out worse hands while keeping in better ones. Examples compare hands like ace-queen, king-queen, pocket queens, and pocket sevens on the same flop to show when betting, checking, or folding is preferable.

The lecture also discusses when to call post-flop bets. Players should fold many weak hands to half-pot bets, especially with no pair, weak draws, or vulnerable holdings on coordinated boards. Calling is more reasonable with hands such as overcards on paired boards, bottom pair on safe boards, second pair, or strong but not raise-worthy top-pair hands. Raising generally requires a much stronger hand when stacks are deep, often two pair or better, though stack size changes the threshold: with shorter stacks, top pair may be strong enough to go all in.

The instructor explains advanced “leading” into the preflop aggressor when the flop favors the caller’s range more than the raiser’s, but notes that it is difficult to balance and unnecessary for beginners. Implied odds and reverse implied odds are introduced through examples involving short-stack calls, weak offsuit hands, suited connectors, and set mining. Hands that play well post-flop, such as suited connectors or small pairs in deep-stacked situations, can justify calls because they may win large pots when they improve.

Bluffing is described as most effective when done with draws or hands that have outs against calling ranges. The instructor emphasizes that before the river, the strength of a bluffing hand matters less than how many outs it has if called. A second bluffing principle is to consider what strong hands the bluff plausibly represents; if the board card favors the opponent’s range, giving up may be correct. The lecture ends by stressing that learning to bluff well is important so opponents will also pay off value bets.
Precise estimation of polynomial functionals of quantum states supports Rényi entropies, entanglement, coherence, and randomness certification in quantum information and physics.

A player said he was surprised and grateful that Pat put him back in the lineup after two weeks, and he focused on doing his part to help the team win. He was nervous during the final minute and planned to discuss his future with his family, saying it would be a sweet way to go out. He praised the team’s three Cups in nine years, its resilience during a difficult season, key additions, and Pat’s demanding, focused coaching.

Ottawa’s coach says the team has played below its ability in the first two games against Anaheim and must prove it is better, especially at home. He emphasizes improving puck possession, faceoffs, positioning, forechecking, speed, and avoiding risky stretch passes and turnovers. He says Anaheim has been disciplined, strong on matchups, effective on the forecheck, and especially successful through Pahlsson’s line and players like Rob Niedermayer. He praises Ottawa’s goaltender for giving the team a chance to win but says they have not tested Giguere enough. Chris Neil was given the day off because his wife was having a baby. The coach expects an emotional home crowd, plans to use the fourth line more, and says several forwards must return to their previous playoff form.

The passage discusses the growing role of artificial intelligence in higher education, noting its potential to transform teaching-learning processes, research, institutional management, and external relations. AI can support personalized learning, intelligent tutoring, automated grading, data analysis, translation, plagiarism detection, predictive analytics, student support, administrative efficiency, and research tasks such as literature review and data analysis. The paper is based on document collection and analysis from B-ON and SCILIT, combined with the authors’ reflective experience as university teachers.

The passage contrasts traditional higher education with AI-oriented models, highlighting differences in technological adaptation, governance based on big data, personalized training, and networked research. It also identifies challenges, including equity of access, disability inclusion, bias, privacy, data ethics, teacher training, student readiness, financial costs, organizational resistance, policy issues, and AI’s limits regarding creativity, feelings, and emotions.

The authors argue that AI integration should be participatory, supported by AI literacy beyond digital literacy, and accompanied by changes in teachers’ roles and competencies. They conclude that higher education cannot ignore AI but must critically examine how to use it while preserving academic freedom.

U.S. stock index futures rose Thursday as earnings season started strongly and oil prices rebounded, though North Korea-U.S. tensions and France’s presidential election kept investors cautious. Thomson Reuters data showed 75.4% of 57 S&P 500 companies reporting earnings beat expectations, while overall S&P 500 profits were estimated to rise 10.8%. Visa and Mattel were due to report. Qualcomm gained after beating estimates, while eBay fell on a weak profit forecast. Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures were all higher.

An analysis by Notre Dame law professor Derek Muller found that lawyers and staff at top BigLaw and larger plaintiffs-side firms gave 92.45% of 2023-2024 campaign contributions to Democrats, about $52 million versus $4 million to Republicans. The Democratic-to-Republican ratio rose to roughly 12-1 from 6-1 in a prior 2017-2020 analysis. Among top-grossing firms, Cleary Gottlieb, Fried Frank, and Mintz had the highest Democratic contribution percentages, while Nelson Mullins, Lewis Brisbois, and Ogletree Deakins had the lowest.

Quantbot Technologies LP increased its Zoe’s Kitchen stake by 114.5% in the second quarter to 17,056 shares worth $203,000. Other institutional investors also adjusted holdings. Director A Alexander Taylor II bought 3,100 shares at $12.87 each. Analysts give the stock a consensus “Hold” rating and $17.55 target. Zoe’s Kitchen opened at $12.39, with a $242.04 million market cap. Its latest quarterly EPS was $0.06, above estimates, while revenue rose 12.1% to $74.30 million.

The lecture reviews discrete symmetries in quantum field theory: parity, time reversal, and charge conjugation. Time reversal in quantum mechanics must be represented by an anti-linear, anti-unitary operator so that the Schrödinger equation transforms correctly under \(t \to -t\). For complex scalar fields, parity, time reversal, and charge conjugation are implemented by unitary operators with possible phases; parity squared constrains its phase to \(\pm 1\), distinguishing scalars and pseudoscalars. Charge conjugation exchanges particles and antiparticles.

For Dirac fields, discrete transformations require matrices acting on spinor space. Parity invariance leads to a matrix proportional to \(\gamma^0\). Charge conjugation uses a matrix \(C\) satisfying a relation between \(\gamma^\mu\) and \(-(\gamma^\mu)^T\), whose existence follows from equivalence of gamma-matrix representations. Time reversal is treated similarly, with its matrix related to \(C^{-1}\gamma^5\).

The lecture then introduces fermionic path integrals. Since fermion fields obey anti-commutation relations, their path-integral variables are Grassmann variables, which anticommute and square to zero. Functions of Grassmann variables truncate after finite terms. Derivatives and integrals are defined with special rules: integration is linear, total derivatives vanish, \(\int d\theta=0\), and \(\int d\theta\,\theta=1\), making single-variable Grassmann integration equivalent to differentiation.

The passage describes systems, devices, and methods for synchronizing sensor data from a rotating LIDAR sensor and one or more cameras. The LIDAR emits light pulses while rotating about an axis and detects reflections to scan an environment. The cameras detect external light and include rows of sensing elements aligned with the LIDAR rotation axis.

A controller operates the cameras, including in rolling shutter configurations, to obtain sequences of image pixel rows in an order and timing related to the LIDAR’s emitted beams, pointing direction, rotation rate, and rotation direction. Exposure timing, row readout order, and delays between rows may be adjusted to improve temporal and spatial alignment between image pixels and LIDAR data.

The passage also describes camera ring arrangements around the LIDAR, including multiple cameras with adjacent or overlapping fields of view and curved image sensor configurations. Synchronized LIDAR and camera data may be associated or mapped to generate representations of the environment, such as images, depth information, or colored 3D point clouds.

The Appellate Division affirmed Bradford Washington’s convictions under both indictments. It held that his challenges to detective testimony and a consciousness-of-guilt jury charge were unpreserved and meritless, that the prosecutor did not change the prosecution’s theory during summation, and that no independent claim affected the guilty-plea conviction.

Darren Osborne, 48, was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum term of 43 years for driving a van into worshippers outside mosques in Finsbury Park, north London, killing Makram Ali and injuring nine others. He was found guilty of murder and attempted murder. Osborne reportedly shouted anti-Muslim remarks after the attack and claimed during trial he had wanted to kill Sadiq Khan and Jeremy Corbyn. Ali’s family welcomed the verdict and described him as peaceful and innocent. Police said Osborne planned the attack in Wales before driving to London, while a counterterrorism commander praised the community response after the attack.

Facebook is adding a “Trending News” section to its iOS and Android apps, aggregating stories from multiple sources and ranking them by publication shares. Users can access it in Explore to view headlines, videos, photos, and related Facebook posts.

Several major hedge funds reduced healthcare holdings in the second quarter as the sector outperformed the broader S&P 500 amid fading Republican efforts to repeal the Affordable Care Act. Jana Partners exited stakes in nine healthcare companies, while Third Point cut positions in Humana and Baxter. Hedge funds gained 1 percent overall, trailing the first quarter. Managers also sold energy stocks as oil declines pushed the sector down 7 percent, with Third Point, Jana Partners and Omega Advisors exiting multiple energy positions.

The passage describes an electronic smoking device using a coil-less atomizer with one or more woven fiber tubes that function as both heating element and wick. The tubes may be electrically conductive, hollow, and shaped such as U-, C-, or L-shaped, with ends contacting a liquid supply. Liquid is transported to a heating section by capillary action through the tube interior and porous fiber walls, then vaporized when electrical current passes through a higher-resistance heating section. The device may use leads or surface electrical contacts, and tube sections can be coated or modified to control electrical resistance, conductivity, wicking, strength, and surface properties. Multiple tubes of equal or varied diameters may improve liquid flow or staged aerosol delivery. The passage also describes e-cigarette configurations, liquid supply designs, materials, manufacturing steps, and possible variations such as rechargeable or disposable devices.

The U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Massachusetts addressed remaining damages issues in litigation between Access Cardiosystems, its investors, and Randall Fincke. The court denied Fincke’s motion to reconsider its prior ruling that he violated Massachusetts securities law by falsely stating in an October 2002 Business Plan that Access had been advised by patent counsel that its product did not infringe known patents.

The court found the investors’ testimony that all later investments relied on that statement not credible. It concluded that only Joseph Zimmel’s October and November 2002 stock purchases, totaling $1.5 million, were made “by means of” the misstatement. Later investments were tied to other documents, negotiations, changed circumstances, or were not securities purchases.

Judgment was ordered against Fincke in favor of Zimmel for $1.5 million plus statutory interest and costs. The court also entered judgment for Access against Fincke for $281,534.62, plus interest and costs, based on Fincke’s waived objection to liability for breaching fiduciary duties by causing Access to repay his personal loans.

The passage describes the BIRDS workshop, which aims to connect digital library and GLAM domain experts with computational researchers to foster collaborations on practical digital library challenges. It notes that practitioners often know collections, metadata, and user needs but may lack technical resources, while computer science researchers have computational expertise but may not know real-world library problems.

The workshop’s goals include starting a collaboration-focused workshop series, identifying common digital library challenges, discussing early ideas and ongoing work at TPDL, producing a SIGIR Forum report, and continuing the series at future digital library conferences. It is planned as a full-day, in-person, interactive event with introductions, a keynote, scientific speed-dating, a panel discussion, breakout groups, and closing summaries. Discussion topics may include LLM use, OCR, interface evaluation, and effective access paths.

The intended audience includes practitioners, researchers, students, and library representatives interested in building research systems for digital libraries, with about 25 participants expected. The organisers are Christin Katharina Kreutz and Hermann Kroll, whose work spans digital libraries, information access, GLAM institutions, and related workshops and conferences.

The Ohio Supreme Court affirmed the constitutionality of R.C. 3105.03’s one-year residency requirement for filing divorce or annulment actions in Ohio. The appellant had not met the requirement when filing and challenged it under equal protection and the constitutional right to travel, relying on Shapiro v. Thompson and Dunn v. Blumstein. The court held that the requirement does not penalize interstate travel because divorce is not a basic necessity or fundamental right like welfare assistance or voting. It further held that Ohio has a compelling interest in regulating marriage and divorce for its residents and in ensuring its divorce laws are not applied to nonresidents. The court concluded that the one-year requirement is the least restrictive means of confirming domicile and protecting the state’s interest in marital status. Judgment was affirmed.

Apple filed a Form 8-K reporting that on August 17, 2022, its Compensation Committee approved the Apple Inc. Executive Cash Incentive Plan for eligible executive team members, with cash awards based on performance goals set and evaluated by the Committee. Apple’s Board also adopted amended and restated bylaws effective the same day, including changes to Board meeting notice, shareholder nomination and proposal procedures, special meeting and written consent requirements, proxy card color rules, meeting conduct authority, and emergency operating provisions. Exhibits include the amended bylaws and the Executive Cash Incentive Plan.

Oliver Stone’s Wall Street opened shortly after the 1987 Black Monday crash and remains a dominant film about finance. The passage argues its lasting appeal comes from combining a rags-to-riches story, the Hero’s Journey, and a fairy tale, as Bud Fox rises from low-level broker to wealth through Gordon Gekko. It also highlights the film’s vivid depiction of 1980s excess, from fashion and technology to yuppie lifestyle markers. The passage identifies Michael Douglas’s Oscar-winning performance as Gekko as the film’s strongest asset, portraying him as a charismatic symbol of greed and success who continues to influence people in finance. Phrases like “Greed is good” have helped make the film a memorable time capsule of its era.

A modified Google Camera app enables HDR+ on Android phones with Snapdragon 820, 821 or 835 processors, potentially improving photos. Amazon is offering refunds for faulty solar-eclipse glasses. HBO refuses to pay hackers despite new leaks, including Curb Your Enthusiasm episodes. Waymo patented technology to soften car body panels before pedestrian collisions, though it is only a patent.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its 2016 Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2016. The company is incorporated in Delaware, headquartered in Seattle, and its common stock trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under “AMZN.” As of January 25, 2017, it had 477,170,618 common shares outstanding.

Amazon operates through three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services. It serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators through retail websites, seller programs, AWS cloud services, Kindle Direct Publishing, advertising services, and co-branded credit card agreements. Amazon employed approximately 341,400 full-time and part-time employees as of December 31, 2016.

For 2016, Amazon reported net sales of $135.987 billion, operating income of $4.186 billion, net income of $2.371 billion, and diluted earnings per share of $4.90. Net sales were $79.785 billion in North America, $43.983 billion internationally, and $12.219 billion from AWS. Operating income was $2.361 billion in North America, a $1.283 billion loss internationally, and $3.108 billion from AWS.

The filing identifies major risks including intense competition, rapid expansion, international operations, fulfillment and data center operations, seasonality, acquisitions and investments, foreign exchange exposure, security breaches, system interruptions, inventory risks, intellectual property claims, evolving regulation, tax liabilities, supplier dependence, government contracts, product liability, payments-related risks, and seller fraud or unlawful activity.

As of December 31, 2016, Amazon had $83.402 billion in total assets, $20.301 billion in total long-term obligations, and $26.0 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. Net cash provided by operating activities was $16.443 billion in 2016, while investing activities used $9.876 billion and financing activities used $2.911 billion.

SCOTUSblog previews retired Justice Anthony Kennedy’s memoir, highlighting his views on judicial humility, constitutional interpretation, and rejection of strict originalism or pragmatism. Kennedy discusses major cases including Citizens United, same-sex marriage, Bush v. Gore, flag burning, and abortion, emphasizing legal duty over personal views. He also reflects on tensions and reconciliation with Justice Scalia, opposition to courtroom cameras, a meeting with Vladimir Putin, a possible retaliation against his family, and his views on his children’s music.

The paper examines diurnal temperature-induced phase drift in the room-temperature RF transmission lines of the Simons Observatory Large Aperture Telescope (LAT) SMuRF readout system. The LAT uses 18 SMuRF systems mounted on the receiver to read out 18 universal focal-plane modules containing nearly 31,000 TES detectors. Because the receiver cabin is kept isothermal with the telescope structure, the electronics and unregulated coaxial cables experience daily ambient temperature swings, potentially causing phase drifts that could mimic detector signals.

The study measures this effect using off-resonance SMuRF tones, which pass through the RF chain without interacting with microwave resonators. Data from 290 off-resonance tones over 22.6 hours show time-delay variations correlated with ambient temperature, clustered by RF transmission-line circuit, with magnitudes of only a few picoseconds over one day-night cycle. The authors convert this phase drift into an inferred TES noise-equivalent current using measured resonator calibration offsets and SQUID response curves from a LAT focal-plane module.

The resulting phase-drift noise contribution during a 40-minute constant-elevation scan is compared with representative on-sky detector noise and open-SQUID readout noise. The phase-drift contribution is found to be small, within the readout noise budget, and not expected to affect the LAT mapping speed.

Evelyn Montiel grew up helping run her family’s ice cream truck and frozen fruit stand in East Oakland while excelling in high school. Students Rising Above supported her goal of becoming the first in her family to attend college. After leaving an East Coast college due to depression, SRA helped her transfer to USC and secure internships. After graduating during the recession, she struggled to find work and returned to the family business, but SRA connected her to a finance job. She now works as a broker at a Silicon Valley startup and credits SRA with helping her succeed.

Tesla, Inc. filed its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022. The company designs, develops, manufactures, sells and leases fully electric vehicles and energy generation and storage systems, operating through automotive and energy generation and storage segments. Its automotive products include Model 3, Model Y, Model S, Model X, Tesla Semi, and planned vehicles such as Cybertruck and the new Tesla Roadster. Energy products include Powerwall, Megapack, retrofit solar systems and Solar Roof.

Tesla sells primarily through its website and company-owned stores, supports customers through service centers, Mobile Service, Superchargers and Destination Chargers, and offers financing, leasing, insurance and selected energy financing options. It manufactures in California, Nevada, New York, Texas, China and Germany, and sources parts and raw materials globally.

The report discusses government incentives and regulations affecting electric vehicles, energy storage and solar energy, including the Inflation Reduction Act. It also describes competitive markets for vehicles, energy storage and solar systems; Tesla’s intellectual property practices; ESG priorities; and human capital programs. As of December 31, 2022, Tesla and its subsidiaries had 127,855 full-time employees.

Risk factors include COVID-19-related impacts, supply chain constraints, production ramp delays, battery cell availability, competition, international operations, product defects, financing risks, obligations tied to Gigafactory New York, reliance on key personnel including Elon Musk, and cybersecurity threats.

VentureWire’s September 26, 2000 issue reports major venture financings, partnerships, closures, product launches, acquisitions, board appointments, executive moves, and fund news. Top stories include Chiaro Networks raising over $100 million, Bertelsmann and iSyndicate forming iSyndicate Europe, Novalux raising $109 million, Miadora shutting down, Sun Microsystems launching a $50 million Asia Pacific investment program, and Mayfield Fund naming Jennifer Jones marketing partner. Other reported financings include rounds for eHealth Direct, Palmchip, Nexsi, Netigy, Epylon, Hart InterCivic, Predictive Networks, Nonstop Solutions, Artesia Technology, Telecruz, and others. Product news includes launches or partnerships from SmartPipes, PocketPass.com, Fujitsu-ICL/Foursan, and w-Technologies. M&A items include Autodaq buying Market Wise, Burley House Weddings merging with Confetti Network, and DeepBridge acquiring Online Communications. The issue also covers new directors, CEO appointments, venture fund developments, and corrections involving Sharing Technologies and epipeline.com.

The passage discusses challenges in applying standard quantum chemistry methods to molecules in optical cavities described by the Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian. It highlights the non-local electron–photon coupling term and the need for accurate basis sets. The sinc basis is presented as orthonormal, systematically improvable, and suitable for extended interactions, though direct implementation has O(N⁴) cost for two-electron integrals, which may be reduced using sparse or low-rank approximations.

NVIDIA Corporation filed its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 29, 2017. The company is headquartered in Santa Clara, California, trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the symbol NVDA, and had 589 million common shares outstanding as of February 24, 2017. Its aggregate market value held by non-affiliates was approximately $28.98 billion as of July 29, 2016.

NVIDIA describes its business as focused on visual computing and accelerated computing, built around GPU and Tegra Processor reportable segments. Its platforms serve four main markets: Gaming, Professional Visualization, Datacenter, and Automotive. GPU brands include GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, DGX, GRID, and GeForce NOW. Tegra-based platforms include DRIVE PX and SHIELD. The company emphasizes artificial intelligence, deep learning, GPU computing, cloud gaming, virtualized graphics, and self-driving vehicle computing.

NVIDIA’s strategies include extending leadership in AI and visual computing, using GPU parallel processing for accelerated computing, expanding into mobile and cloud platforms, licensing intellectual property, and focusing on gaming, professional visualization, datacenter, and automotive markets. Sales are conducted through end customers and a partner network that includes OEMs, ODMs, system builders, add-in board manufacturers, retailers, distributors, and other industry participants. ASUSTeK Computer Inc. accounted for 12% of fiscal 2017 revenue.

The company uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on third parties for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, packaging, and some product manufacturing. Suppliers include Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, Samsung Electronics, Advanced Semiconductor Engineering, BYD Auto, Hon Hai Precision Industry, JSI Logistics, King Yuan Electronics, Siliconware Precision Industries, and others. NVIDIA reported cash and marketable securities of $6.80 billion at the end of fiscal 2017, up 35% from fiscal 2016.

NVIDIA had 10,299 employees as of January 29, 2017, including 7,282 in research and development. Research and development expenses were $1.46 billion in fiscal 2017, $1.33 billion in fiscal 2016, and $1.36 billion in fiscal 2015. The company competes in markets characterized by rapid technological change, citing competitors including AMD, ARM, Imagination Technologies, Intel, Xilinx, Ambarella, Apple, Broadcom, Mobileye, Qualcomm, Renesas, Samsung, and Texas Instruments.

Key risk factors include failure to meet market needs, manufacturing yield problems, cybersecurity breaches, product defects, loss of Intel licensing revenue, reliance on third-party manufacturers and software tools, failure to achieve design wins, business disruptions, customer concentration, gross margin fluctuations, demand forecasting errors, international operating risks, acquisition integration challenges, intellectual property disputes, operating result volatility, privacy concerns, headquarters construction risks, indebtedness, warrant dilution, and anti-takeover provisions.

NVIDIA’s headquarters complex in Santa Clara includes leased and owned facilities, and the company was constructing a new headquarters building targeted for completion in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2018. It also leases or owns facilities in the United States, India, Asia, and Europe.

In November 2016, NVIDIA increased its quarterly dividend to $0.14 per share. It paid $261 million in dividends in fiscal 2017 and $213 million in fiscal 2016. Its board authorized an additional $2.00 billion for share repurchases through December 2020, and the company had repurchased 245 million shares for $4.59 billion through January 29, 2017.

On Nov. 27, 2001, reports said Enron was struggling to maintain trading activity as many counterparties limited or stopped selling near-term gas and power to the company amid credit concerns. Some sources estimated Enron’s over-the-counter trading volume had fallen to about 25% of its level a month earlier, though Enron said the reduction was only slight.

Dynegy confirmed it was in talks with Enron and other parties about restructuring their proposed acquisition. Reports said the original all-stock deal, valued around $9 billion, could be cut by more than 40% to about $5 billion, with a lower exchange ratio of less than 0.15 Dynegy share per Enron share. Discussions also involved additional funding for Enron and restructuring or extending debt maturities.

Enron was seeking cash to address a liquidity crisis, including efforts to raise up to $2 billion, but investors including Prince Alwaleed, Carlyle and Blackstone declined to invest. Moody’s said Enron’s rating would remain Baa3 for the day, its lowest investment-grade rating.

Analysts and traders remained wary, citing deterioration in Enron’s core trading business, debt obligations, possible bankruptcy if the Dynegy deal failed, and uncertainty from accounting disclosures. Enron shares traded near $4, far below prior levels, while bonds rebounded from distressed prices. Reports also noted closure of Enron’s equity trading unit, employee lawsuits over 401(k) losses, and concerns that litigation or adverse developments could affect Dynegy’s ability to complete the deal.

The DAWN-plasma study was a randomized, multicenter, open-label phase 2 proof-of-concept trial evaluating standard of care plus convalescent plasma versus standard of care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive and free of mechanical ventilation on Day 15; secondary endpoints included clinical status, mortality, ventilation outcomes, safety, laboratory measures, and quality of life.

Between May 2, 2020, and January 26, 2021, 489 patients were randomized: 326 to convalescent plasma and 163 to control. In the full analysis set, 320 patients received plasma plus standard of care and 163 received standard of care. Plasma patients received 800–1000 mL in four doses, with most plasma units having neutralizing antibody titers of at least 1/320.

The primary endpoint did not differ between groups: 83.7% of plasma patients and 84.1% of control patients were alive and free of mechanical ventilation at Day 15. No statistically significant differences were found in secondary endpoints, including mortality or Day 30 outcomes. Serious, severe, fatal, and overall adverse events were similar between groups. Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 19 of 320 plasma patients, and no TRALI cases were reported. The study concluded that early high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not change the clinical course of hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
A study finds online image age gaps may shape AI chatbots to perceive women workers as younger and less experienced.

This nationally representative study used 2009–2020 NHANES data from 32,498 US adults over age 20 to identify empirical dietary patterns and examine their associations with cardiovascular disease (CVD), social risk factors, and SNAP participation. Principal components analysis identified four dietary patterns: American, Prudent, Legume, and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy. The American pattern, characterized by higher refined grains, meats, cured meats, milk, cheese, oils, solid fats, and added sugars, was most common and had the lowest HEI-2020 score. The Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy pattern had the highest HEI-2020 score.

Prevalent CVD was present in 8.3% of adults. Adults with CVD were more likely to align with the American pattern than those without CVD. Higher social determinants of health risk scores were associated with greater alignment with the American and Legume patterns and lower alignment with the Prudent and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy patterns. SNAP participants and income-eligible nonparticipants were more likely than SNAP-ineligible adults to align with the American pattern and less likely to align with the Prudent pattern. The Legume pattern was more common among socioeconomically vulnerable adults.

Associations varied by race and ethnicity for social risk factors and SNAP status, but not for CVD. Sensitivity analyses were generally similar. The authors conclude that naturally occurring dietary patterns differ by cardiovascular health and socioeconomic vulnerability, and nutrition interventions should account for these subgroup differences.

The Wham play is a complementary football run concept similar to Trap, but a tight end or fullback pulls to kick out a defensive lineman instead of a guard. Its main strength is creating quick, unexpected favorable running angles, especially when defenses have not practiced against it often. Its main weaknesses are that it is complex and time-consuming to install, requires linemen and the fullback to correctly identify fronts and assignments, and needs a powerful enough blocker to handle large defensive linemen. Teams often use specific formations to create predictable fronts. The passage outlines Wham assignments against 3-4 Odd and 4-3 Even fronts and describes variations including Gun H-Back Wham RPO, where the fullback blocks the nose tackle and the quarterback can throw based on the flat defender or box count, and Shotgun Influence Wham, which uses defensive reaction to pulling action to widen the running lane.

A player’s stable personality, skill, size, and strength have helped him perform under playoff pressure. The team focused on getting pucks in and punishing the defense, believing it would pay off as the series continued. Despite historical odds, they view themselves as mature and focused on one game at a time. Defensive adjustments and a loose, inspired effort built confidence, and they aim to repeat that performance.
