Microsoft filed a Form 8-K on March 13, 2020, reporting that Bill Gates, co-founder and Board member, resigned from Microsoft’s Board of Directors effective that date. The filing also lists registered securities and includes a related press release as Exhibit 99.1.

This study examined household transmission of hepatitis C virus (HCV) among household members of HCV-positive patients attending CUSP in Huye district, Rwanda. Using a descriptive cross-sectional design, 148 participants from 30 families were tested with HCV antibody rapid tests and ELISA confirmation, and questionnaires assessed risk factors and awareness. HCV prevalence among participants was 10.8%: 16 tested positive and 132 tested negative. Significant associations were found between HCV positivity and HBV history, HIV history, and unprotected sex, while blood transfusion was not significant. Awareness of HCV transmission was very low, with 93.9% giving incorrect answers, but awareness was not significantly associated with test results. The study concluded that household members of HCV-positive patients had high HCV prevalence, with unprotected sex identified as the main contributing risk factor among participants. It recommended early screening, follow-up of HCV-positive patients, education of household members, and broader future studies beyond Huye district.

Santa Barbara County sheriff’s detectives are investigating a robbery at the Summerland Antique Collective, where a man threatened and duct-taped two female employees before stealing cash and merchandise. The victims were found about 20 minutes later and did not appear seriously injured. Detectives are seeking information about the suspect.

President Donald Trump nominated Travis Hill, a former senior adviser at the Treasury Department, to chair the FDIC, pending Senate confirmation. The agency insures bank deposits and supports banking system stability. Hill’s nomination comes as U.S. banks face tighter credit, high interest rates, and concerns about smaller lenders. He is expected to support a pragmatic, lighter regulatory approach aligned with Trump’s deregulatory stance. If confirmed, he would oversee deposit insurance, bank assessments, and sector failures, influencing debates on insurance limits, risk management, and crisis intervention. The nomination is expected to face congressional scrutiny.

Iqaluit-Tasiluk MLA George Hickes says Nunavut public servants should not be discouraged or threatened by senior Government of Nunavut managers for speaking with MLAs. Hickes said some employees have been directed not to contact assembly members and that a culture of discomfort persists. He asked Public Service Act Minister David Akeeagok whether the law prohibits such communication or whether he knew of directives against it; Akeeagok said no and affirmed employees have the right to provide information to MLAs. Hickes said MLAs need constituent feedback to address complaints and improve government, especially when formal processes break down.

The Mining Expo & Conference will be held on April 25 and 26 at the Windhoek Show Grounds under the theme “Maximising the multiplier effect from Namibia’s mining sector.” Nedbank Namibia CIB’s Mining and Resources Finance team will showcase its mining finance capabilities, share insights on attracting foreign investment, and provide a networking lounge. Dominic Shikola said Nedbank CIB is committed to helping the sector access capital through funding solutions including sourcing, structuring and negotiating transactions. He said the mining sector contributes about 11 percent to Namibia’s GDP and remains important for foreign exchange, employment and tax revenue. The expo will support networking and information sharing on mining trends.

The speaker declined to discuss penalties and said the physical play and fights were part of playoff hockey. He identified the turning point as an offensive-zone faceoff win that became a turnover, penalty, and opponent power-play goal, after his team missed chances to score first. He emphasized the need to respond, win the next game, and maintain momentum in a playoff series. He said the team was fine after travel and a quick skate, and defended using seven defensemen for chemistry and flexibility. He also stressed the importance of faceoffs, puck possession, player self-evaluation, and taking opportunities.

Commissioner.COM sent a Football Commissioner 2001 fantasy football e-report on Oct. 18, 2001, containing SportsLine promotions and extensive NFL player updates. The report lists injury statuses, expected availability, and fantasy recommendations for numerous players, including Todd Heap, Jeff Garcia, Drew Bledsoe, Tyrone Wheatley, Chris Weinke, Brian Griese, Randy Moss, Marshall Faulk, Michael Bennett, and others. It also includes a “Luccis Losers” roster section with updates on players such as Charlie Garner, Duce Staley, Steve McNair, Cameron Cleeland, Kurt Warner, and Marty Booker.

The passage introduces Construction Defining Functionality (CDF), a framework for analyzing computational problems through three structural layers: syntactic space, semantic space, and logical space. These are connected by mappings from syntax to semantics, semantics to logic, and syntax directly to logic. CDF distinguishes intensional internal construction from extensional observable behavior and uses this distinction to study computational tractability.

CDF defines a function’s structural space as syntactic patterns, semantic input-output relations, and logical proof or computation structures. Stability occurs when mappings grow polynomially with input size; explosiveness occurs when growth exceeds polynomial bounds. A CDF diagram is compositionally coherent when the direct syntax-to-logic mapping equals the composition of syntax-to-semantics and semantics-to-logic. Based on this, CDF classifies structures as ComCDF, ExpCDF, or Semi-ExpCDF.

The passage argues that semantic explosion arises when syntactic structures generate exponentially large semantic spaces, especially in recursive or non-local systems. Examples include a linear function and the factorial function, illustrating stable structures for fixed inputs and growing complexity under input variability.

The framework is applied to 2SAT and 3SAT. 2SAT clauses can be converted into binary implications, enabling local, compositional reasoning through implication graphs and polynomial-time solvability. 3SAT clauses involve non-local ternary interactions that cannot be reduced to binary implications, causing exponential semantic growth and unstable logical mappings. The passage concludes that, in CDF, 3SAT’s intractability arises from its syntactic non-locality and the inherently explosive syntax-to-semantics mapping.

Expired 3D printing patents have enabled broad access to lower-cost machines, while companies like Stratasys and 3D Systems still sell high-end industrial systems for demanding applications. Industrial printers differ greatly from desktop models in price, materials, size, throughput, and uses. They can process plastics, metals, ceramics, and casting sand, producing parts for aerospace, automotive, dental, jewelry, and other industries. Large systems such as BAAM and high-throughput machines like HP Jet Fusion support short-run production without molds. Companies including NASA and GE use additive manufacturing for propulsion components and engine parts, achieving weight, cost, durability, and part-count improvements. The Wohlers Report is presented as a key annual resource on professional additive manufacturing.

China has become a global leader in the clean energy transition amid stalled climate action from the US, EU, India, and others. At the UN Climate Summit, Xi Jinping reaffirmed China’s climate commitments, including reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 7 to 10 percent by 2035, reaching 3,600 GW of wind and solar capacity, making renewables more than 30 percent of its energy mix, expanding electric vehicle adoption, broadening carbon trading, and increasing forests. China invested $625 billion in clean energy last year, nearly a third of the global total, and its renewable technology research, production, and domestic adoption have helped lower prices and reshape global green technology markets.

European shares rose Wednesday, with the STOXX 600 up 0.4 percent to its highest close in nearly 16 months, showing little reaction to Britain formally starting Brexit proceedings. Germany’s DAX also rose 0.4 percent, helped by Daimler’s record first-quarter sales outlook and gains in auto stocks. LSE and Deutsche Boerse shares rose after EU regulators blocked their merger as expected. Banks underperformed after reports ECB policymakers were wary of changing their policy message. Deutsche Bank gained amid optimism over its cash call. Engie and 3I Group rose following broker upgrades, while Scout24 fell after weak results and outlook. Aurelius plunged more than 35 percent as investors remained unconvinced by its response to a short-seller report.

Paulo Dybala said he has resumed training and expects to play against Barcelona. He also said renewing with Juventus until 2022 was his choice, adding he is happy at the club after his strong first-leg performance.

Sebi allowed debt issuers to request reviews of ratings by credit rating agencies, with review committees having a majority of independent members, to improve transparency, fairness, governance and accountability. It also mandated disclosure of non-accepted ratings on CRA websites for 12 months and half-yearly rating action summaries, with separate disclosures for securities and other financial instruments.

An open-label randomised controlled trial in Kampong Speu province, Cambodia, compared 14-day primaquine regimens of 3.5 mg/kg and 7.0 mg/kg for preventing Plasmodium vivax recurrence in G6PD-normal patients, with a no-primaquine comparator arm that included G6PD-deficient patients. All participants received artesunate for 7 days and were relocated to a non-transmission area for 90 days to reduce reinfection during follow-up.

Between November 2021 and February 2024, 160 patients were enrolled and 156 allocated: 49 to low-dose primaquine, 46 to high-dose primaquine, and 61 to no primaquine. Within 90 days, recurrence occurred in 81.4% of the no-primaquine arm, 24.4% of the low-dose arm, and 4.7% of the high-dose arm. High-dose primaquine had a significantly lower recurrence risk than low-dose primaquine, with a hazard ratio of 0.17. By 180 days, recurrence risk remained lower in the high-dose arm.

Both primaquine regimens were well tolerated in G6PD-normal patients, with comparable safety. Methaemoglobin increases were more frequent with high-dose primaquine but were clinically silent and resolved after treatment. No serious adverse events were reported. The study concludes that 7.0 mg/kg primaquine over 14 days was more effective than 3.5 mg/kg for preventing P. vivax recurrences in Cambodia and should be endorsed in Cambodia and likely other Southeast Asian countries.

Melinda Rosetti-Spence was sentenced to 10 years in prison for embezzling about $266,600 from Pink Hearts Fund, a Mississippi cancer charity where she volunteered as treasurer. A judge ordered repayment of about $181,000, with her family paying the balance. Prosecutors said she wrote 132 checks to herself in 2016. She pleaded guilty and said she had a gambling problem.

English local authorities are owed refunds after the Ministry of Justice found council tax summons fees had been overcharged by £2.50 per application since 2013-14 due to an administrative error. Councils overpaid about £9m annually and will be fully compensated, with refund details to follow. The MoJ said it will urgently reduce fees to the correct level. Councils issued about 3.5 million summons for council tax arrears last year, amid rising recovery action and concerns over penalties, bailiffs and imprisonment.

LG will release webOS TVs later this month with Sky EPG compatibility from launch. Users can view and control Sky content through the webOS interface using LG’s remote. WebOS also integrates viewing options from apps, online platforms, and live TV, enabling seamless input switching and program selection.

The U.S. government froze about $18 billion in federal funding for New York City infrastructure projects, including the Second Avenue Subway extension and Hudson River Tunnel, over concerns that contracts may have used unconstitutional DEI criteria. The DOT suspended a $300 million payment pending review. Local officials warn of delays, job impacts and cost overruns, while analysts say uncertainty could affect contractor and investor confidence. Funds may resume if the city is cleared, but violations could require renegotiation or risk major funding losses.

STAT’s “Up and down the ladder” highlights personnel changes in the pharmaceutical industry. This edition notes that enGene hired Hussein Sweiti as chief medical officer; he previously worked at Johnson & Johnson as global medical head of oncology clinical development. The full article is available to STAT+ subscribers.

The Council of Regional Accrediting Commissions is encouraging colleges to use AI to improve transfer credit evaluation and reduce credit loss, while emphasizing that doing so does not conflict with accreditation standards. CRAC says current transfer processes are often slow, inconsistent and harmful to students, sometimes requiring them to retake courses or abandon degrees.

A 2024 Public Agenda survey found that 58 percent of adults who tried to transfer credit lost some credit, 20 percent repeated a course, 13 percent ran out of financial aid after repeating coursework, and 16 percent gave up on a degree or credential. The survey also found racial disparities in credit acceptance.

Experts cited in the passage say AI can analyze course descriptions, enrollment data and learning outcomes to identify course equivalencies and support faculty decision-making. A 59-institution pilot is using an AI platform to find new or expanded course matches. CRAC urges institutions to default toward applying credits to program completion unless evidence shows learning outcomes are not met, while keeping humans involved in evaluation.

A 2,100-year-old chalk bowl fragment found in Jerusalem bears the Hebrew name “Hyrcanus,” but researchers cannot determine whether it belonged to a Hasmonean ruler or a commoner, since the name was common at the time. Discovered in 2015 under the Givati parking lot in the City of David, beneath foundations of a mikvah complex and near remains of the Akra fortress, the artifact is one of the earliest examples of chalk vessels in Jerusalem, which Jews used because they were considered unable to become ritually unclean.

Cryotherapy, a wellness trend involving brief exposure to temperatures as low as 180 degrees below zero, is gaining popularity in West Michigan with the opening of Polar Brrr Cryo. Enthusiasts claim it helps muscle recovery, inflammation, joint pain, circulation, mood, immunity, anxiety, depression, and calorie burning, though scientific support is limited. The FDA has not approved cryotherapy and warns of frostbite, burns, and eye injuries. Polar Brrr says clients are supervised during three-minute sessions and advises people with heart problems or hypertension to consult a doctor. Sessions normally cost $55, with introductory rates available.

Bollinger Bands are a technical analysis tool created by John Bollinger to measure volatility and identify potential overbought or oversold conditions. They typically use a 20-period simple moving average with upper and lower bands set two standard deviations away, though settings can be adjusted by timeframe, moving average type, lookback period, and standard deviation.

The bands widen during higher volatility and contract during lower volatility, with contractions or “squeezes” often used to anticipate possible breakouts. Common strategies include Bollinger Band Squeeze, Breakouts, %B, Band Walks, Basic Bounce, Double Bollinger Bands, Band Width, RSI Divergence, Pinch Play, Reversal, Volatility Contraction, and Triple Strategy. Breaks above the upper band may signal bullish momentum or overbought conditions, while breaks below the lower band may signal bearish momentum or oversold conditions.

The passage says Bollinger Bands show some profitability in mean-reverting stock strategies and promise as a breakout indicator in gold, but not useful results for stock indices. It emphasizes that Bollinger Bands should not be used alone, as they can produce delayed or false signals, especially during strong trends or short timeframes. Traders are advised to confirm signals with tools such as RSI, MACD, stochastic indicators, trend analysis, stop-loss orders, position sizing, and diversification.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting results from its March 1, 2019 Annual Meeting of Shareholders. Shareholders elected eight directors, ratified Ernst & Young LLP as independent registered public accounting firm for 2019, and approved an advisory resolution on executive compensation. Shareholder proposals on “Shareholder Proxy Access Amendments” and “True Diversity Board Policy” were not approved. The report was signed March 4, 2019, by Katherine Adams, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary.

The passage discusses the holiday effect in the stock market, defined as seasonal return patterns around non-weekend market holidays. It analyzes S&P 500 performance around several U.S. holidays using SPY and historical index data. The article suggests possible causes include lower liquidity, holiday optimism, reduced macro news, and pre-holiday risk reduction.

Backtests found little or no effect around Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Presidents’ Day, Memorial Day, and Labor Day. The strongest tradeable effects identified were around Independence Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas. The 4th of July and Thanksgiving strategies showed positive average gains, while the Christmas/Santa Claus rally produced strong results from late December to the first trading day of the new year.

The passage also examines post-holiday effects using SPY from 1993 onward. Some tests found better returns on the second day after holidays, and one unrevealed strategy reportedly produced high win rates with limited market exposure. The conclusion states that holiday effects are real but generally small and should be considered additions to broader trading strategies rather than guaranteed profit sources.

The passage highlights news about Amazon Alexa, including work on an AI chip, a popular Super Bowl YouTube ad, CES-related Alexa gains, speaker price competition with Google, Echo Dot holiday sales, a rogue Alexa incident, and plans to integrate Alexa into Big Mouth Billy Bass. It also mentions CES tech reveals and Apple’s delayed home speaker.

Scottish councils are setting budgets and can raise the basic council tax rate by up to 3% after the end of the long-running freeze. Some councils plan the maximum rise, while others may keep rates frozen. Separately, households in bands E to H will see bills rise regardless of council decisions due to higher multipliers approved by MSPs, expected to raise £100m annually. Average increases range from about £2 per week for band E to £10 for band H, on top of any local rise.

About 700,000 of Scotland’s nearly 2.6m homes, or 26%, are in bands E to H, with impacts varying by area. East Renfrewshire has 56% of homes in the top four bands, while East Ayrshire has 18%; Edinburgh has 37%, Dundee 14%, Glasgow 16%, and Aberdeen 27%.

Council tax bands are based on 1991 property values. A 2014 analysis suggested 57% of properties would change band under revaluation, but the government says revaluation would be costly, lengthy, and could cause major bill changes.

Councils rely heavily on Scottish government funding. Derek Mackay’s budget plans and a later deal with the Greens added £160m in direct local authority funding, though parties disagree over whether council budgets still face cuts.

A report by Lucas Chancel and Thomas Piketty says income inequality in India has risen rapidly since the 1980s, with the top 1% now receiving 22% of national income, the highest since income tax began in 1922. Inequality declined from the 1950s to 1970s under strong regulation and progressive taxation, when lower and middle incomes grew faster. The trend reversed in the mid-1980s with pro-business policies, liberalisation and deregulation. The report says “Shining India” mainly benefited the top 10%, while the middle 40% gained more during 1951-1980.

Multiple Oct. 29, 2001 news reports focused on Enron’s worsening credit and market position. Moody’s downgraded Enron’s senior unsecured debt to Baa2 and placed long-term debt and commercial paper ratings under review, citing reduced valuations, write-downs, weakened financial flexibility, and loss of investor confidence. Enron shares fell to near seven-year lows after a reported third-quarter loss, equity write-downs tied to partnerships run by former CFO Andrew Fastow, and an SEC inquiry. The company drew down about $3 billion in credit lines, repaid commercial paper, and sought an additional $1 billion to $2 billion in bank credit. U.S. trading partners generally said dealings continued normally, while some European energy firms reportedly froze or restricted trading with Enron over credit concerns. Other articles discussed broader corporate credit deterioration, Enron bond weakness, possible harsher lending terms, takeover speculation, utility insider buying excluding Enron, market confidence concerns, and a Houston Chronicle commentary praising Enron’s contributions to Houston.

Russia is increasingly targeting Ukrainian drone pilots with missiles, bombs, and other weapons because of their major battlefield impact in reconnaissance, targeting, and strikes. Ukrainian personnel said pilot casualties have risen sharply as drones cause many battlefield losses. Both Russia and Ukraine view enemy drone operators as high-value targets. Ukrainian pilots are responding with stronger shelters, deeper underground positions, and frequent rotation.

AMD’s SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block specification defines legal terms for using the AMD specification and standardizes guest-hypervisor communication for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests. AMD permits review only for product planning, interface design, and feedback; retains all rights; provides the specification “AS IS”; disclaims warranties and liability; restricts certain life-critical uses; may use submitted feedback freely; requires export-law compliance; and applies California law with disputes in Santa Clara County.

The specification describes SEV-ES and SEV-SNP protections that encrypt guest register state during world switches, preventing direct hypervisor access. Non-Automatic Exits allow the guest OS to selectively expose required state through the GHCB, while Automatic Exits do not require exposing guest register state. The GHCB is a 4 KB decrypted page shared between guest and hypervisor, based partly on the SEV-ES VMCB save state format, with only necessary fields exposed.

Version 2 adds SEV-SNP support, hypervisor feature advertisement, CPUID-related enhancements, shared-buffer requirements, restricted APIC emulation, and later revisions covering updated secrets-page sequence numbers, VLEK GUIDs, APIC ID list retrieval, multi-VMPL support, SEV-ES page state change, EFI confidential computing blob protocol, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, GHCB unregistering, and unsupported MSR protocol behavior.

The document defines GHCB establishment using MSR 0xc001_0130, GHCB protocol negotiation, GHCB GPA registration for SEV-SNP, feature-support bitmaps, CPUID request/response before a GHCB page is available, termination requests, and examples for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP negotiation. It specifies GHCB/VMGEXIT processing, VALID_BITMAP handling, error reporting through SW_EXITINFO fields, and requirements for supported Non-Automatic Exit events.

Defined NAE handling includes standard VMGEXIT, IOIO_PROT, MSR_PROT, VMMCALL, MMIO access, page state changes, SNP guest requests, extended guest requests returning certificates, SNP AP creation, #HV doorbell pages, #HV IPI and timer support, APIC ID list retrieval, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO guest requests, Secure AVIC backing-page registration, termination requests, and unsupported exits.

The specification also covers SEV-SNP secrets pages, EFI configuration tables for secrets and CPUID pages, SMP booting constraints, AP reset hold, AP jump tables, AP creation, NMI handling, debug-register support, lack of SMM support, lack of nested virtualization support, and SNP Restricted Injection using #HV doorbell data for host notifications.

The passage says adults should drink about 6–8 glasses, or 1.2 liters, of water daily, with some intake coming from food. Drinking too much can cause rare water intoxication, diluting blood salt and causing lethargy, light-headedness, or death in extreme cases. Research suggests drinking according to thirst rather than a strict schedule. A 2010 study found that people aged 55–75 who drank two cups of water before meals lost more weight on average than those who did not, and water is recommended over sugary, high-calorie drinks.

The passage presents Doublethink, a Bayesian model averaging method for identifying direct non-genetic risk factors in biobank-scale data while controlling Bayesian false discovery rate and frequentist familywise error rate. Applied to 1,912 UK Biobank variables and 1,917 COVID-19 hospitalization cases, it identified significant individual and grouped direct risk factors, including age, sex, deprivation, obesity-related measures, education, dementia, respiratory infection, falls, carer support indicators, and markers of comorbidity. Post-hoc grouping of correlated variables improved signal detection and interpretation. Compared with 127 published UK Biobank COVID-19 studies, the method supported some common risk factor categories but found no significant direct effects for others such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and hypertension, while highlighting less commonly studied factors. The authors emphasize that the approach estimates direct, not total, effects and is limited by mediation, measured variables, data curation choices, prior specification, large-sample assumptions, and high computational cost.

Teams should prepare for defensive, even, and offensive jump ball situations. Defensive jump balls occur when the opponent has a clear advantage, requiring early movement, rotations, pass denial, boxing out, and protection against easy shots. Alignments such as box, diamond, and “Y” use predetermined rotations and back defenders to reduce offensive chances and attempt long tips to teammates.

Even jump balls require boxing out, inside position, anticipation, aggressiveness, and coordinated clockwise or counter-clockwise rotations based on signals. Players should watch the jumper’s eyes and hands, as jumpers often indicate tip direction.

Offensive jump balls can be used when a team has a significant height advantage. Teams may run set plays while maintaining defensive balance and transitioning into offense if no good shot develops. Plays include ball possession, double tap, post split, jumper fly, forward fly, spread, tandem, and loop, all designed to control the tip, create cuts to the basket, or generate passing and driving opportunities.

A U.S. official told Mr. Toivola that a reported Finnish Legation statement blaming Soviet-Finnish peace rumors on “Anglo-American machinations” would be mistaken if true. The Finnish Minister sought clarification on travel restrictions affecting Finnish diplomatic and consular personnel, especially American citizens connected to Finnish offices. The British Embassy reported that the Soviet Minister in Stockholm had discreetly signaled willingness to contact Finland about possible peace terms. A State Department memorandum noted British views that a firm British-American stance toward Finnish policy could encourage Finland to make peace with the Soviet Union.

The passage traces how reusable patterns have shaped software development, from Knuth’s general-purpose algorithms to object-oriented design patterns and open source components. It argues that patterns help distributed systems development by capturing prior experience, creating shared vocabulary, and enabling reusable components.

It defines distributed system patterns as general blueprints independent of specific technologies. Containers are presented as foundational building blocks, including single-node groups of tightly coupled containers that may share filesystems, networks, and other resources. Splitting applications into multiple containers supports resource isolation, team ownership, reuse, separation of concerns, easier testing, and safer deployment.

Three single-node container patterns are described. The sidecar pattern uses an auxiliary container to augment an application container, such as adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service, synchronizing configuration, providing process introspection, or building a simple Git-based PaaS. Effective sidecars should be parameterized, expose stable APIs, and be documented through Dockerfile directives and labels. The ambassador pattern uses a container to broker communication between an application and external systems, including sharded storage, service discovery across environments, and request splitting for experiments. The adapter pattern modifies an application’s interface to match expected conventions, such as standardized monitoring, logging, or health checks, using examples with Prometheus, fluentd, Redis, Storm, and MySQL.

The passage then introduces multi-node distributed patterns and microservices. Microservices break systems into separate components communicating through defined APIs, improving agility, team independence, and scaling, but making debugging and architecture more difficult. Distributed patterns are presented as a way to simplify design and troubleshooting.

Replicated load-balanced services are described for stateless systems, where identical replicas sit behind a load balancer for availability and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes indicate when instances can serve traffic. Variations include session-tracked services, caching layers using reverse proxies, rate limiting, denial-of-service defense, and SSL termination with nginx.

Finally, sharded services are contrasted with replicated services. In sharded systems, each shard serves only part of the request space, usually to scale stateful data beyond one machine. The passage explains sharded caching, cache hit rates, effects on throughput and latency, risks during failures or upgrades, and the option of replicated shards to improve resilience and capacity.

The speaker reflects on winning the Stanley Cup, crediting Fleury’s saves, Geno’s Conn Smythe performance, team sacrifices, and leadership from Sidney Crosby. He says the team wanted to win for an injured Crosby and praises Crosby as the heart and soul of the Penguins. He also highlights Fleury as a winning goaltender, describes his own belief in big-game moments, and notes Mario Lemieux’s role in keeping the team in Pittsburgh.

Merck CEO Ken Frazier resigned from President Trump’s American Manufacturing Council, saying he was taking a stand against intolerance and extremism after the Charlottesville rally. Trump responded by criticizing Frazier on Twitter over drug prices, while the passage notes other executives had previously left Trump advisory councils.

ResearchAndMarkets.com added the “Global Industrial Hybrid Stepper Motors Market 2018-2022” report, which forecasts the market will generate over $1,000 million by 2022. The report cites demand for automated industrial equipment as a key driver, miniaturized stepper motors as a trend, and competition from servo and conventional stepper motors as a challenge. Key vendors include AMETEK, MinebeaMitsumi, Moons’, Nidec, and Schneider Electric.

Family members and survivors of the Grenfell Tower fire gave emotional tributes during the first phase of a public inquiry into the June 14 disaster, which killed 72 people. Ahmed Elgwahry described staying on the phone as his mother, Eslah, and sister, Mariem, died in the burning tower. Inquiry chair Martin Moore-Bick said the hearings should begin with the victims’ voices before examining fire materials, regulations and causes.

Relatives emphasized the human toll and raised concerns about safety failures. Karim Mussilhy described seeing blackened walls and fingerprints in the tower’s staircase after visiting the apartment where his uncle died. Criticism focused on local authorities, building management, government officials and fire guidance telling residents to stay inside. Paulos Tekle said his family was repeatedly told to remain in their 18th-floor apartment before his 5-year-old son Isaac died during their escape. Marcio Gomes described the death of his premature son Logan after the fire left his wife in a coma.

The passage examines two stocks with forecast dividend yields of 7.1%. Taylor Wimpey’s dividend is described as affordable and sustainable for now, supported by strong cash flow, surplus cash generation, and housing demand exceeding supply, though special dividends may not last indefinitely. Connect Group also generates strong cash flow and its dividend appears covered, but concerns include high debt, negative tangible asset value, and potential vulnerability to weaker trading or tighter lending. The author concludes Connect’s risks outweigh its potential rewards.

A 2017 Regina Police Service survey of 462 participants found the public was generally satisfied with police performance. Seventy-nine per cent rated service quality as very good to excellent, and over 80 per cent viewed RPS as honest and having integrity. Nearly 25 per cent felt RPS was not sensitive to their ethnic group, especially Indigenous people; Chief Evan Bray said reconciliation training is underway.

Baseline out-of-bounds situations give the defense a 5-on-4 advantage, but they require different defensive adjustments than standard half-court defense because the ball is behind the defense and cutters often move directly toward the basket. The passage presents four defensive approaches: Jam, Jump Switch, Trap, and Combination Defense. Jam emphasizes sagging to protect the basket, then aggressively denying cuts and screens without switching while smothering the inbounder. Jump Switch attacks screens and passing lanes through aggressive switches, especially with little time left. Trap double-teams the receiver after the inbound pass and rotates into help positions. Combination defenses such as Box-and-One, Diamond-and-One, and Triangle-and-Two use chasers to deny key players while the remaining defenders form zone alignments and adjust after the ball is inbounded.

The passage introduces diffusion models and flow matching as special cases of learning stochastic dynamics between distributions, framed through the Schrödinger bridge problem. Existing iterative proportional fitting (IPF) methods solve Schrödinger bridges when samples from both marginals are available but cannot handle marginals specified only by unnormalised densities. The authors propose extending IPF to data-to-energy and energy-to-energy settings, using reinforcement learning losses and stabilisation techniques to train bridges when one or both marginals are energy functions with unknown normalisation. They claim this is the first general method for such Schrödinger bridges. Their contributions include demonstrating low-cost bridges comparable to data-to-data IPF with oracle samples, improving data-to-data IPF by learning diffusion coefficients as well as drift, and applying data-to-energy IPF to translate priors to posteriors in generative model latent spaces for data-free image-to-image translation.

The passage compiles news mentions of Enron from May 26–27, 2001. Major topics include Kenneth Lay’s private Beverly Hills meeting with prominent Californians to promote Enron’s deregulation-based solution to California’s energy crisis, criticism of Enron’s influence over federal energy regulators, and Senator Dianne Feinstein’s call for hearings into possible improper ties between FERC and energy companies. Several articles cover California’s conservation efforts, possible Senate action on Western power price restraints, and political criticism surrounding the crisis. Other reports focus on Enron’s Dabhol Power dispute in India, including rejected payments, termination notices, contract challenges, lender meetings, and tariff disputes. Additional items mention Enron’s role in Saudi gas projects, high compensation for Houston energy executives, and Enron’s staffing changes in India.

This study examined local molecular signatures of neuropathic pain using Morton’s neuroma as a human peripheral nerve injury model. Researchers collected affected plantar digital nerves from 22 patients undergoing neuroma excision and control nerve samples from 11 participants undergoing other surgeries. Patients were clinically phenotyped for neuropathic pain, and samples were analyzed using RNA sequencing, gene ontology, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, deconvolution, and immunofluorescence.

Differential gene expression analysis identified 3,349 genes differing between Morton’s neuroma and control nerves, including 1,461 upregulated and 1,888 downregulated genes. Upregulated genes were enriched for immune and inflammatory responses, while downregulated genes were enriched for nervous system development processes such as axon guidance and myelination. Co-expression analysis identified modules related to immune response, neurogenesis, collagen metabolism, and other processes. A defence response module correlated positively with paroxysmal pain, while a neurogenesis module correlated negatively.

Deconvolution showed higher proportions of macrophages and memory B cells in Morton’s neuroma samples, with macrophage proportions correlating with paroxysmal pain severity. A gene signature involving MARCO, CD163, and STAB1, associated with M(GC) macrophages, was upregulated; MARCO expression correlated with paroxysmal pain. Immunofluorescence confirmed demyelination, increased intraneural T cells, and increased CD163+ and CD163+MARCO+ macrophages in Morton’s neuroma. CD68+ macrophage density correlated with burning pain.

The authors conclude that Morton’s neuroma is associated with intraneural inflammation and altered nervous system development signatures, implicating neuroinflammation in chronic human neuropathic pain linked to focal nerve injury.

The speaker described a one-goal hockey game decided by an early penalty-related goal, saying the team created chances in the second period but missed key opportunities. He emphasized the need to finish chances against teams that allow few, while defending the team’s effort and ability to move on from losses. He said they would not change their style, stressing that their speed—not physical play—has been central throughout the playoffs, though the current opponent is the fastest they have faced. He discussed using last change at home, adjusting matchups against opposing lines, and relying on players who meet the needed standard. He also commented on relationships with opposing management and coaches, praised players’ recent contributions, noted the demands of media and locker-room logistics during the finals, and said roster decisions are governed by available financial limits.

Overnight trading involves buying at the close and selling at the next day’s open or close, aiming to exploit short-term stock market edges. The passage describes several S&P 500/SPY overnight strategy examples, including Turnaround Tuesday, holiday seasonality, end-of-month effects, weekday effects, mean reversion, options expiration effects, and mixed strategies. Backtests since 1993 show positive average gains and win rates for these approaches, though backtests are described as approximations requiring judgment and logical structure.

The passage emphasizes building a portfolio of many uncorrelated, sub-optimal strategies rather than relying on one “perfect” strategy. It recommends diversifying across asset classes, time frames, and strategy types to reduce overlap and drawdowns. Avoiding large drawdowns is presented as important for compounding. The main drawback noted is the need to buy and sell at the close, often requiring automated or mechanical execution.

SpaceX will launch an unmanned Dragon cargo spacecraft to the ISS from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center at 12:31 pm ET, with live coverage available. The mission carries about 6,400 pounds of supplies, mainly scientific equipment, plus ice cream. It is NASA’s last new Dragon cargo craft, with future missions using flight-proven hardware.

The speaker says the team’s strength comes from shared support, defensive depth, and players learning from veterans like Ray Bourque. They emphasize respecting opponents’ power forwards, using positioning and containment rather than chasing big hits, and keeping the game simple. They say reaching the finals reflects the league’s competitiveness, the need for health, confidence, emotion, and experience, and that returning after a long wait feels special despite pressure and expectations.

Small sided games in soccer use teams with fewer than 11 players on reduced fields, in practice or competition, to increase individual touches on the ball. In practice, they range from 3v3 to 9v9, focus on tactical themes such as attack, defense, possession, passing, movement, shooting, transitions, and goalkeeping, and are adapted by age using fewer players and simpler spaces for younger groups.

For youth competition, U.S. Soccer’s 2017 Player Development Initiatives set national small-sided standards for U6 through U12. These games use fewer players, smaller fields, goals and balls, shorter game times, and modified rules to support development. From U9, build-out lines encourage playing out from the back and affect offside calls. The standards also ban headers, punts, and drop kicks, and include guidance on markings, substitutions, footwear, referees, restarts, and other rules.

The Syrian opposition’s High Negotiations Committee wants direct Geneva talks with the government focused on political transition and says President Bashar al-Assad cannot have a role. Spokesman Salim al-Muslit said the HNC has not received an agenda and wants discussion based on the 2012 Geneva communique on a transitional governing body with full executive powers.

A Northern California jury convicted 20-year-old Gonzalo Curiel of murdering two children in 2015 and torturing their older sister. The children’s relative, Tami Huntsman, had already pleaded guilty to two murder counts. The surviving sister testified about abuse by Huntsman and Curiel. Both were scheduled for sentencing the following week.

Dr. Pasvolsky explained that “peace-loving states” was chosen as a membership criterion to emphasize the organization’s peace purpose, with admission of new states to be recommended by the Security Council and decided by the Assembly. Mexico’s Ambassador said permanent peace through cooperation of all states should guide Chapter III, while acknowledging admission was complicated.

On Chapter IV, Mexico and Venezuela’s comments noted provision for subsidiary bodies. Pasvolsky said the chapter identified principal organs and emphasized the Security Council’s peace and security functions, the General Assembly’s role in creating conditions conducive to peace, and the International Court of Justice’s legal role; the Economic and Social Council’s status could be changed later.

On Chapter V, Ambassador Castillo Nájera discussed limiting Assembly delegations to three but noted support for no limit. Pasvolsky addressed criticism of the Assembly’s limited powers, saying responsibilities were divided for effectiveness. The Assembly could discuss and recommend on peace and security questions, but the Security Council held primary responsibility for action, especially because it would be continuously available. He stressed that the organization’s success depended on broad support by nations and that the Assembly’s handling of international relations would be crucial.

The disclosure concerns metal-assisted delayed fluorescent (MADF) emitters employing benzo-imidazo-phenanthridine and analogues for full-color displays and lighting. It claims priority to earlier U.S. applications and notes government support from the Department of Energy. The emitters include cyclic platinum(II), palladium(II), and octahedral iridium(III) complexes represented by General Formulas I–XVII, with variable metals, linking atoms, ligands, substituents, and aryl or heteroaryl groups.

The described Pt(II) and Pd(II) MADF complexes can use singlet and triplet excitons, enabling unity internal quantum efficiency and short lifetimes. Their design allows small singlet-triplet energy gaps so excitons can emit through thermally assisted delayed fluorescence while remaining triplet excitons emit through phosphorescence. The disclosure includes OLEDs, lighting devices, photovoltaic devices, and luminescent displays incorporating the compounds or compositions.

The passage defines numerous chemical terms and permissible substituents, describes OLED layer structures and possible materials, and provides examples of synthetic procedures for ligands and metal complexes, including reported yields and emission spectra for selected examples.

Ann Schmidt circulated media mentions involving Enron from Nov. 1–2, 2000. Articles covered growth in weather risk management, including Enron’s expansion of European weather-risk trading sites; Houston arena referendum debate; shareholder lawsuits challenging Enron’s proposed $275 million financing for Azurix to buy back shares at $7; C.I. The passage describes analyte monitoring systems for in vivo monitoring, including sensor applicators, sensor control devices, sensors, sharps, electronics housings, reader devices, and communication links. The lecture introduces the construction of SNARGs using two ingredients: BARGs and somewhere extractable, also called somewhere statistically binding, hash functions.

A BARG proves that many instances belong to an NP language with a proof whose size grows polylogarithmically in the number of instances and polynomially in one witness size. Its semi-adaptive soundness allows a cheating prover to choose instances after seeing the CRS, but the index of the false instance must be fixed beforehand. Fully adaptive soundness is harder because changing the CRS in the proof may change where the prover cheats, and membership in the language may be hard to determine.

A somewhere extractable hash includes key generation, evaluation, opening, verification, and extraction algorithms. It allows local openings of bits of a hashed string, hides the binding index, and is statistically binding at that index. Index hiding implies computational binding at other indices for polynomial-size adversaries. Repeating the construction gives binding on multiple locations, while unrevealed indices remain hidden even if some trapdoors are revealed.

The lecture also explains that BARG verifiers can be efficient for index languages: if the batched instances have a succinct description, verification time depends on that description and logarithmically on the number of instances, rather than linearly on all instances. BARG extractability can be obtained by combining a BARG with a somewhere extractable hash.

The somewhere extractable hash construction is sketched using fully homomorphic encryption. A simple Merkle-style construction that homomorphically selects encrypted bits is insufficient for binding because malicious ciphertexts may be malformed. The corrected construction uses different public keys per layer and encrypts secret keys so that each step decrypts child ciphertexts and re-encrypts selected values, ensuring well-formed ciphertexts along an opening path.

The SNARG construction hashes all wire values of a verification circuit using the somewhere extractable hash, then uses a BARG to prove that every circuit gate is satisfied and that the output wire is 1. The CRS contains the hash key and the BARG CRS. The prover outputs the hash value and the BARG proof. The verifier accepts exactly when the BARG verifies. Efficiency relies on the BARG being applied to an index language, so the verifier need not process all circuit gates explicitly.

The work theoretically studies optical cavity coupling to quantum critical magnetic systems, focusing on a transverse-field Ising model and related spin models. It shows that when a cavity photon mode couples directly and bilinearly to the matter degree of freedom with quantum critical fluctuations, the critical coupling needed for a superradiant phase transition vanishes at the matter quantum critical point. Thus, superradiance can occur at arbitrarily weak light-matter coupling near the critical regime.

For the cavity-coupled transverse-field Ising model, large-S analysis and one-dimensional DMRG calculations show a continuous superradiant transition whose phase boundary terminates at the Ising quantum critical point. The superradiant order parameter exhibits different scaling regimes depending on whether the matter sector is ordered, critical, or disordered. The coherent mixing of critical spin modes and cavity photons also produces enhanced intrinsic two-mode squeezing and increased quantum Fisher information, indicating stronger light-matter entanglement than in the standard Dicke model.

When the cavity couples to a non-critical spin component, ferromagnetism and superradiance compete rather than cooperate. This produces a more complex phase diagram with discontinuous and continuous superradiant transitions and a tricritical point with anomalous scaling. Analysis of a ferromagnetic XY model supports the robustness of quantum-critical facilitation of superradiance, with the critical coupling minimized near the relevant quantum critical point.

The authors propose that materials such as CoNb₂O₆, LiHoF₄, and CrI₃ coupled to cavity modes could test these effects, and suggest the framework may extend to driven-dissipative cavity quantum systems.

The passage describes a Reconfigurable Power Station (RPS) for unmanned aerial vehicles and other unmanned systems. The RPS is intended to extend UAV range by autonomously exchanging depleted universal Swap Cartridges (SCs), such as batteries, fuel cells, fossil fuel cartridges, or payloads, for energized ones. A UAV communicates with the RPS through a Universal Integrated Swap System (UIS), which includes a Universal Swap Processor (USP), Swap Cartridge Receptacles (SCRs), SCs, sensors, communication components, and identification markers.

The RPS includes a configurable landing zone, dynamic terminal landing system (DTL), modular power bays (MPBs), cartridge swapping mechanism, central processor, sensors, power systems, and communication systems. The DTL uses visible or non-visible markers or emitters to generate scalable composite images that help guide autonomous landing. After landing, the station may mechanically and electrically retain the UAV, power its systems, locate the UIS, remove depleted SCs, store or replenish them in MPBs, retrieve compatible energized SCs, install them into the UAV, and clear the UAV for takeoff.

The MPBs can store multiple SC types and sizes and may be configured in different arrangements. The RPS central processor manages cartridge exchange, environmental monitoring, data storage, safety systems, power management, communication, and readiness checks. The system may operate with internal or external power sources and may communicate with UAVs, operators, or remote systems. The passage also describes methods for landing approval, queueing UAVs, downloading data, swapping cartridges, recharging depleted cartridges, and assessing environmental conditions before launch.

The Jammu and Kashmir Assembly saw noisy scenes after opposition members raised alleged attacks on Kashmiri students in Haryana and other states, accusing the government of failing to prevent such incidents and staging a walkout during zero hour. Recent orbitronics experiments report orbital angular momentum generation through effects such as the orbital Hall effect and orbital Rashba-Edelstein effect. Common experimental approaches include measuring orbital torques in magnetic heterostructures, magnetoresistance, orbital pumping and THz emission, direct imaging of orbital accumulation using dichroism-based methods, and orbital Hanle magnetoresistance. Torque measurements often require conversion of orbital angular momentum to spin angular momentum via spin-orbit coupling, either in the ferromagnet or in an added conversion layer such as Pt or 4f transition metals. Material dependence, especially among ferromagnets, is used as evidence of orbital effects, but quantitative analysis remains difficult because generation, transport, interface transmission, spin conversion, and torque transfer are hard to disentangle.

Experiments have identified CuOx as a strong source of orbital angular momentum, producing enhanced torques in heterostructures, including a sixteen-fold torque increase in TmIG/Pt/CuOx. Orbital Rashba-Edelstein effects have also been reported in Ni-Fe/CuOx. Long orbital transport lengths in ferromagnets, reciprocal orbital pumping, and direct imaging of orbital accumulation have been reported. Two-dimensional van der Waals systems, especially transition metal dichalcogenides, are also being studied, with recent work distinguishing orbital Hall effects from valley Hall effects and exploring possible topological orbital Hall insulators.

Theoretically, orbital Hall effects are described as arising from momentum-space orbital texture and are expected to occur broadly in conducting solids. The interfacial orbital Rashba-Edelstein effect can also generate orbital angular momentum currents without spin-orbit coupling. Key open questions concern the magnitude of orbital torque and orbital angular momentum relaxation. Although strong crystal-field-driven orbital-lattice coupling can generate large orbital currents, it should also dissipate them efficiently, making experimentally reported long orbital relaxation lengths difficult to reconcile with theory. Conflicting calculations predict either long-range orbital torques in ferromagnets or very short orbital diffusion lengths in normal metals.

For applications, orbital torque may be useful in MRAM, oscillators, random number generators, logic devices, and THz emitters. In MRAM, it could offer alternatives to spin-orbit torque by using light metals such as Ti, V, and Cr, which have lower resistivity than W and may be integration-compatible. Challenges include increasing torque efficiency, achieving large orbital torque in high-tunneling-magnetoresistance-compatible systems such as CoFeB/MgO, and reducing layer thicknesses by shortening orbital angular momentum diffusion length. Reported developments include orbital-torque switching with reduced switching power compared to Pt spin-orbit torque devices and comparisons between W/CoFeB/MgO and Cr/CoFeB/MgO systems.

The field remains promising because orbital textures can exist without spin-orbit coupling, enabling potentially cheaper, lighter, and less hazardous materials. However, key processes—generation, long-distance and interfacial transport, orbital-to-spin conversion, and enhanced torques in two-dimensional materials—remain insufficiently understood. Orbital effects may be tunable through crystal and interface engineering and could connect with photonics, phononics, and other quasiparticle-based fields.
Application for a writ of habeas corpus was denied in People ex rel. Harry H. Boddie v. Ronald R. Emery.

Ryan Dempster said Kyle Hendricks’ success with the Cubs feels personal and gratifying because Hendricks was acquired when Dempster was traded to Texas in 2012. Hendricks later became a rotation fixture, won an ERA title, beat Clayton Kershaw in the 2016 NLCS clincher, started Game 7 of the Cubs’ World Series win and was set to start Game 1 of the NLDS against the Nationals. Dempster, now a Cubs front-office assistant, said seeing Hendricks succeed was meaningful because he had always wanted to win a World Series with Chicago. Dempster noted he had full no-trade rights, rejected a deal to Atlanta, and eventually accepted the Rangers trade that brought Hendricks and Christian Villanueva to the Cubs.

American detainee Christian Beasley escaped Bali’s overcrowded Kerobokan prison by sawing through a ceiling and jumping a wall. Another American inmate was caught attempting to flee. Authorities are investigating possible guard involvement amid severe understaffing. The prison, built for 300, holds nearly 1,600 inmates. It was the second escape there since June, reflecting broader jailbreak problems in Indonesia’s overcrowded prisons.

Jason Ku guest lectures on origami art and design, focusing on representational origami and the tree method. He compares origami to music, distinguishing design from performance, and surveys artistic styles from traditional crisp, geometric folding to nontraditional shaping and wet-folding. He discusses influential artists including Akira Yoshizawa, Hideo Komatsu, David Brill, Michael LaFosse, Eric Joisel, Robert Lang, Brian Chan, and Satoshi Kamiya, emphasizing their approaches to elegance, realism, texture, complexity, and single-sheet folding.

Ku explains origami design through tree theory, where a subject is abstracted into a stick figure, converted into a base, and then shaped into a final model. He reviews uniaxial bases, flaps, rivers, circle/river packings, active paths, and how crease patterns correspond to trees. Examples include crabs, insects, animals, dragons, and complex textured works. He demonstrates how TreeMaker can help generate crease patterns from a tree and briefly presents his own crab design process. He concludes by recommending Robert Lang’s *Origami Design Secrets*, the documentary *Between the Folds*, an online origami forum, and MIT’s origami club, OrigaMIT.

HHH defended excluding women from The Greatest Royal Rumble, saying cultures differ and WWE cannot force change by staying away. He cited WWE’s first women’s match in Abu Dhabi as cultural progress and said WWE hopes women can compete in Saudi Arabia within the next few years.

The coach said the team has managed emotions well, quickly refocusing after setbacks despite not getting desired results. He emphasized keeping to the game plan and avoiding distractions such as referees or bounces. He said Detroit has been better at net-front battles, loose pucks, scrambles, and timely goals, which has been the main difference. Pittsburgh has generated chances and outshot or outchanced Detroit, but must drive the net harder, create second chances, protect its crease better, and maintain composure, especially with emotional players like Geno. He also said Sidney Crosby has battled through matchups, Pascal Dupuis added speed and puck pursuit, and the team remains focused on improving at home.

He said the team would briefly enjoy the win before preparing to face New Jersey on the road. He attributed his overtime success to both luck and a strong desire to make a difference, praised “Jiggy” for leadership, and recounted the play that led to the goal. WHO said Yemen’s outbreak has caused 503,484 suspected cases and 1,975 deaths since late April, though its spread has slowed since early July. War-damaged infrastructure, poor sanitation, lack of clean water, unpaid health workers, and limited healthcare access have worsened the crisis. WHO urged support for health services and a political solution.

President Rutherford B. Hayes warned that unauthorized persons preparing to occupy or settle Indian Territory west of Arkansas were violating U.S. laws. He ordered that such persons be removed by Indian Department agents and stated that military force could be used if necessary to enforce the law.

Cosmetic tooth bleaching is a growing global industry with many over-the-counter options, though products do not require FDA approval because they are considered cosmetic. The ADA seal indicates independent review for safety and effectiveness, but only one over-the-counter bleaching product currently carries it. Whitening options include drugstore products, dentist-made trays, and faster in-office bleaching, which uses stronger hydrogen peroxide and can be more dramatic but is costly and usually not covered by insurance. Bleaching may cause temporary tooth sensitivity or gum irritation if products leak.

Dentists recommend an exam before whitening because discoloration can result from cavities or oral problems. Surface stains from coffee, tea, red wine, turmeric, cigarettes, and nicotine may be reduced by brushing, flossing, and professional cleaning. Deeper stains from aging, enamel cracks, grinding, or hard brushing may respond to bleaching, but discoloration from trauma, tetracycline, or excess fluoride is permanent and may require crowns or veneers. All bleaching is temporary, and the ADA says there is no evidence that “natural” remedies such as charcoal, baking soda, or lemon juice whiten teeth.

NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture increases memory, compute, and scalability for HPC, AI, analytics, and data center workloads. It includes 40 GB HBM2 memory across five active stacks, delivering 1555 GB/s bandwidth, with SECDED ECC protecting HBM2, L2 cache, L1 caches, and register files. A100 has a 40 MB L2 cache, 6.7x larger than V100, with 2.3x higher L2 bandwidth, residency controls, and Compute Data Compression that can improve DRAM and L2 bandwidth and effective L2 capacity.

A100 uses third-generation Tensor Cores, more SMs than V100, improved data sharing, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, larger shared memory, higher HBM2 and L2 bandwidth, and cache controls to improve deep learning strong scaling. It supports CUDA Compute Capability 8.0, CUDA 11 features including task graph acceleration, asynchronous copy APIs, L2 cache residency controls, Cooperative Groups enhancements, and support for Tensor Cores, sparsity, and Multi-Instance GPU.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can partition an A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory resources, supporting predictable QoS, fault isolation, multi-tenant use, VM and container workloads, and improved utilization. MIG uses GPU slices, Sys Pipes, GPU Memory slices, GPU Instances, and Compute Instances, with support for Volta-style MPS and vGPU migration.

A100 adds third-generation NVLink with twelve links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 with 31.5 GB/s per direction for x16 connections, SR-IOV, enhanced error detection and fault isolation, NVJPG JPEG decode, an Optical Flow Accelerator, improved atomic throughput, and five NVDEC units. DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with NVLink, NVSwitch, Mellanox networking, MIG, and optimized NVIDIA software to support scalable AI infrastructure. The passage also describes sparse neural networks, pruning, and A100’s fine-grained structured sparsity for improving compute, memory bandwidth, and latency while maintaining balanced workloads.

The Second Circuit reviewed consolidated admiralty actions arising after the oil-laden Barge New London, pushed by the Tug Ocean Prince, struck a charted rock outside the Hudson River channel, causing damage and an oil spill. The district court had denied exoneration but allowed Red Star, owner/charterer of the tug, to limit liability to the tug’s value, dismissed claims against the United States, found Pittston not responsible for the spill, and limited Red Star’s cleanup liability to $100 per gross ton.

The court accepted most factual findings but held the district court erred in allowing limitation. Red Star knew or should have known the voyage’s winter nighttime hazards, including ice, buoy unreliability, and the need for Hudson River experience. It failed to appoint a captain, failed to tell Kiernan that Reimer lacked Hudson River experience, and sent the tug out improperly manned. These acts made the vessel unseaworthy and occurred within Red Star’s privity and knowledge.

The court also held Red Star’s failure to require a proper lookout was negligent, violated a statutory duty, and could have contributed to the grounding because a lookout could have seen Con Hook Light in time to avoid the rock. This independently supported denial of limitation.

The court affirmed dismissal of claims against the United States, finding no proximate causation from any alleged inadequacy in navigational aids.

For pollution cleanup costs, the court held Red Star’s combined omissions amounted to willful misconduct within its privity and knowledge under 33 U.S.C. § 1321, so statutory limitation was unavailable. The judgment was reversed in part, affirmed in part, and remanded for entry of judgment for Pittston and the United States for their damages.

The Single/Double Offense is a basketball set used to free a strong shooter through double baseline and single down screens while attacking both sides of the defense. The shooter can curl, fade, back cut, or reverse depending on defensive positioning, while other players create opposite-side options, post mismatches, screen-and-roll actions, slips, lobs, and offensive rebounding opportunities. The offense requires precise execution of double screens, down screens, strong post-ups, defensive reads, timing, and non-verbal coordination. If initial options fail, it can continue into motion, side screen, or drive-and-kick actions. Coaches are advised to drill fundamentals, scout defensive tendencies, vary alignments, move players, and use side screens late in the clock.

CBD drug Epidiolex, made by GW Pharmaceuticals, is being considered for FDA approval to treat seizures caused by Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and Dravet syndrome in patients aged 2 and older. Unlike widely sold CBD products with unsubstantiated claims, Epidiolex is a purified, pharmaceutical-grade oral medicine made under manufacturing standards. FDA briefing documents said studies provide substantial evidence of effectiveness and acceptable risks for these rare, severe childhood-onset epilepsy syndromes. Physicians and parents described significant seizure reductions in some children. The drug contains CBD derived from cannabis but not THC, and its recommended use would be limited despite doctors’ ability to prescribe FDA-approved products as they see fit.

The passage argues that Google’s Pixel 2 and Pixel 2 XL differ more physically than Google’s marketing suggests. While last year’s Pixel models had a consistent design, the Pixel 2 and Pixel 2 XL feel like products from different manufacturers, with the smaller HTC-made Pixel 2 retaining large bezels, sharper chamfered edges, and weaker design refinement, while the LG-made Pixel 2 XL has rounded display corners, curved glass edges, and a more premium build. The author says the phones are similar in specifications and experience, but not in design quality, making Google’s claim that it does not reserve better features for the larger model technically true yet misleading in practice. The passage also criticizes broader inconsistency in Google’s design language, including the Pixelbook, and concludes that the Pixel 2 represents a step back toward Nexus-era inconsistency despite Google’s “Made by Google” branding.

After a birthday sleepover near Milwaukee, 12-year-old Payton Leutner crawled from the woods with 19 stab wounds while her friends Morgan Geyser and Anissa Weier were missing. Anissa’s mother found goodbye notes on her daughter’s phone and alerted detectives. Doctors said one wound narrowly missed a major artery near Payton’s heart and could have killed her quickly.

Nearly five hours later, Morgan and Anissa were found walking near Interstate 94, and police recovered a 5-inch knife from one girl’s bag. In separate police interviews, they said they had planned for months to kill Payton, whom they called Bella. Morgan said the attack felt “necessary” because of Slender Man, a fictional online horror character. The girls said they believed in Slender Man and wanted to become his “proxies” by killing someone to prove themselves worthy. In the hospital, Payton initially communicated in writing and asked whether police had caught them.

Spanish stocks in focus include OHL and Acciona on dividend announcements, Gas Natural after abandoning an Italian LNG project, NH Hotels on a reported Minor bid for HNA’s stake, Dogi on a proposed name change, and Parques Reunidos after reporting a smaller first-half net loss.

The passage introduces a proposed planar two-frequency Paul trap for simultaneously confining Ca ions and electrons to enable laser-accessible manipulation of quasi-free electron motional and spin states. It motivates the work by noting that trapped-ion qubits have high coherence and fidelity but relatively slow entangling gates, while electrons could enable much faster gates due to their smaller mass. Existing electron-based approaches face challenges including cryogenic requirements, readout limitations, and lack of integrated multi-electron spin and collective-state control.

The authors propose coupling trapped electrons to laser-cooled ions by storing both in the same space, avoiding magnetic-field-based complications and separated trap minima. Their concept uses a Ca²⁺ ion and an electron in a two-frequency Paul trap, with one radio-frequency component primarily trapping ions and the other electrons. The electron states fall into three regimes: low bound Ca⁺ states, transitional Rydberg-like states, and trap-induced states above the Ca⁺ ionization threshold. Photoionization of Doppler-cooled Ca⁺ is proposed to generate the system, followed by optical and radio-frequency control of transitions.

The paper focuses on a planar ring-trap design intended to maintain symmetric trapping fields for Ca⁺ ions and electrons about 1 mm from electrodes, reducing heating while supporting scalable fabrication and integration with photonic and electronic layers. The main goal is demonstrating simultaneous trapping of laser-cooled ions and detached electrons as a foundation for future quantum-information and signal-conversion applications.

The passage describes ultrasonic fingerprint sensor systems incorporated under displays, particularly OLED or flexible OLED displays. The systems transmit and receive ultrasonic waves through a display and platen to image fingerprints based on reflected signals from ridges and valleys. The disclosed apparatuses may include an ultrasonic sensor beneath a display, with layers in the acoustic path such as light-blocking layers, electrical shielding layers, adhesive layers, mechanical stress isolation layers, multi-functional films, high or low acoustic impedance layers, and foam or air backing layers.

The disclosure addresses integration challenges including optical blocking, electrical interference, acoustic transmission, mechanical stress, heat dissipation, reworkability, and display distortion. Light-blocking and electrical shielding layers may be substantially non-porous to permit ultrasonic transmission, while adhesive layers may allow sensor separation for replacement or refurbishment. Mechanical stress isolation layers may reduce stresses from bonding or sealing. Flexible substrates and piezoelectric materials such as PVDF, PVDF-TrFE, PZT, or AlN may be used.

The systems may be implemented in mobile devices and other electronic devices, including configurations where the fingerprint sensor is under the active display area rather than in a separate button. Methods of manufacturing include bonding shielding, blocking, stress isolation, and adhesive layers to a display and bonding the ultrasonic sensor beneath them. Various receiver-up and receiver-down sensor orientations, backing structures, housings, edge seals, and acoustic impedance configurations are described to improve fingerprint imaging and sensor reliability.

Zacks Investment Research downgraded Time Warner from buy to hold, citing strong performance, digital initiatives, international presence and earnings beats, but noting advertising weakness, currency headwinds and the pending $85.4 billion AT&T acquisition, which led to suspension of share repurchases. Other analysts issued mixed ratings, with an overall average of Hold and a $97.87 consensus target. Time Warner shares traded at $96.26 Monday, with a $74.31 billion market cap. The company reported fourth-quarter EPS of $1.25 on $7.90 billion revenue, beating estimates. It also declared a quarterly dividend of $0.4025 per share. Institutional investors own 79.34% of the stock.

E-Book Derivative Litigation. The court approved the settlement notice and set a July 20, 2018 hearing to consider the settlement, attorneys’ fees and expenses, service awards, and related matters. Shalah Dawn Nelson pleaded guilty in Salmon Arm Provincial Court to causing an animal to remain in distress after tying an elastic hair band around a neighbour’s dog’s testicles in December 2016. Criminal Code charges were stayed. Nelson was fined $1,000, placed on 12 months’ probation with no contact with the dog’s owner, and ordered to pay $850 restitution.

AMP improves scheduling and quality of service by reducing time to first response for LLMs and prioritizing game-engine work to prevent stuttering. NVIDIA’s RTX Blackwell architecture adds video, display, power-efficiency, DLSS, neural rendering, and GPU product updates.

Blackwell adds hardware encode and decode support for 4:2:2 chroma-sampled H.264 and H.265 video, balancing file size and color information between 4:4:4 and 4:2:0. Its ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality, adds 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC encoding, and introduces AV1 Ultra High Quality mode. RTX 5090 supports up to three encoders and two decoders, improving export speeds. Blackwell also includes a sixth-generation NVDEC with faster H.264 decoding and 4:2:2 H.264/HEVC decode support. DisplayPort 2.1b support provides up to 80 Gbps bandwidth for high-resolution, high-refresh displays.

Blackwell Max-Q improves power efficiency through advanced power gating, new clock gating, separate voltage rails for GPU cores and memory, accelerated frequency switching, and faster low-power sleep states. These changes allow finer workload-based power control, faster clock adjustments, and up to 50% power savings in an example small language model inference workload.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame, with a faster AI model using less VRAM. Enhanced Flip Metering moves frame pacing to the display engine. DLSS 4 also shifts Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA to transformer-based models, improving temporal stability, lighting detail, motion detail, anti-aliasing, and reducing artifacts compared with CNN models.

Blackwell is designed for neural shaders, allowing Tensor Cores to be accessed through graphics shaders via Cooperative Vectors APIs for DX12 and Vulkan. Neural shader technologies include RTX Neural Materials, RTX Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. These use AI to approximate complex material rendering, compress textures, infer lighting, simulate subsurface scattering, and generate more natural-looking faces in real time.

The Blackwell GPU family includes GB202 for ultra-enthusiast graphics, GB203 for high-end graphics, and GB205 for performance GPUs. The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS DAQ ADC that outputs conversion data in straight-binary or two’s-complement format. It requires a free-running sampling clock for valid output data, data clock, and frame clock, and supports differential or single-ended clock input. The SMPL_SYNC signal synchronizes channel sampling across multiple devices.

The device includes an internal low-drift voltage reference, with optional external reference connection at REFIO. It supports 2-lane or 4-lane SDR/DDR data interfaces, outputs 20-bit results MSB-first in 24-bit packets, and provides source-synchronous DCLKOUT and FCLKOUT. Features include output data randomization, simple and moving data averaging, digital test patterns, reset and power-down controls, and speed-boost mode up to 8MSPS for a selected channel pair.

Configuration uses 16-bit registers in three banks accessed through SPI, including support for daisy-chain topology across multiple ADCs. Register fields configure data format, averaging, test patterns, randomization, speed-boost mode, power-down, bandwidth, common-mode range, reference selection, lane mode, and gain correction. The device requires initialization register writes after power-up or reset.

For ATE applications, the ADS9803 provides a built-in analog front end, supports calibration for offset and gain errors, and offers low-noise and wide-bandwidth modes. Layout guidance recommends keeping analog and reference signals away from digital noise, using close bypass capacitors, and properly decoupling REFIO and supply pins.

The study developed a natural language processing classifier to identify documented goals-of-care discussions in electronic health record clinical notes for seriously ill hospital patients. The authors framed the task as binary classification of utterances and notes, using 776 inpatient notes from the University of Pennsylvania Health System: 400 Advance Care Planning notes and 376 general notes. Annotators labeled utterances as part of a goals-of-care conversation or not, with specialist adjudication.

Because goals-of-care discussions were much rarer in general notes than in Advance Care Planning notes, the dataset was highly imbalanced. The authors compared passive learning with active learning and used an ensemble of five classifiers: regular expressions, logistic regression, BERT-base, BioClinical BERT, and RoBERTa. Active learning selected difficult examples from general notes for annotation and retraining.

The best model, an actively trained weighted-average ensemble, achieved F1 scores of 0.557 for utterance classification and 0.629 for note classification. It retrieved 13 of 18 test notes containing goals-of-care discussions and incorrectly flagged 13 notes without such discussions. Active learning improved precision and reduced annotation effort, requiring annotation of 3,200 utterances, or 30% of the unlabeled general-note pool.

The authors conclude that detecting goals-of-care discussions in general clinical notes remains challenging but that their classifier may be usable in production to support clinician review and research data extraction. Limitations include moderate performance, lack of paragraph-level context, and a restricted unlabeled pool for active learning.
