The lecture discusses matching, running, and power corrections in Heavy Quark Effective Theory (HQET). It begins with heavy-quark wave function renormalization, showing that HQET loop integrals differ from QCD because of the heavy-quark propagator and require different renormalization factors. Heavy-to-light currents acquire a nonzero anomalous dimension in HQET, unlike the corresponding partially conserved current in full QCD, and this anomalous dimension is independent of the spin structure.

For heavy-to-heavy currents with different velocities, the anomalous dimension depends on \(w = v \cdot v'\), producing a nontrivial function \(r(w)\). This dependence arises because \(v^2 = v'^2 = 1\), while \(v \cdot v'\) varies with external kinematics, such as in \(B \to D^* \ell \nu\). Renormalization group evolution separates logarithms involving heavy-quark masses into Wilson coefficients and HQET matrix elements, with matrix elements evaluated at perturbative low scales such as 1–1.5 GeV.

The lecture also explains matching between QCD and HQET, including residue factors and vertex corrections. In heavy-to-light vector currents, HQET permits two current structures because \(v^\mu\) is available as an additional vector. A computational shortcut uses dimensional regularization for both UV and IR divergences: HQET on-shell diagrams become scaleless, leaving only IR poles that cancel against the full theory, so matching can be obtained from the renormalized full-theory result.

Power corrections are introduced by integrating out the small component field in the QCD Lagrangian, yielding the HQET Lagrangian through order \(1/M_Q\). The subleading terms are a kinetic-energy operator, which breaks flavor symmetry, and a magnetic-moment operator, which breaks both flavor and spin symmetry. A bottom-up construction must respect power counting, gauge symmetry, discrete symmetries, and Lorentz symmetry. Lorentz boosts are realized through reparameterization invariance, reflecting the freedom to shift momentum between \(M_Q v\) and residual momentum \(k\). This symmetry constrains the kinetic operator coefficient to be 1 to all orders, while the magnetic operator coefficient is unconstrained and has an anomalous dimension.

The Diamond & One is a Box & One derivative in which four defenders play zone and one chaser denies the opponent’s scoring ace. It is best used against odd or one-guard fronts, takes away the middle, but can give up the corner; if the corner becomes a problem, switch to Box & One. X5 stays low between ball and basket, X3 and X4 cover wing-to-corner areas, and X1 defends the high post. Against odd fronts, defenders push the ball toward sidelines or baseline while the chaser maintains denial. The defense can also double-team a strong post, with X4 and X5 trapping if the post receives the ball while outside defenders cut passing lanes.

The professor discusses midterm results, grading philosophy, and the course transition from block coding for AWGN capacity toward structured codes with lower-complexity decoding. Shannon showed random block codes can achieve capacity, and random linear codes make encoding polynomial, but maximum-likelihood decoding remains exponential; algebraic decoding is polynomial but cannot reach capacity.

The lecture introduces convolutional codes as linear time-invariant finite-state systems with dynamical structure suited to efficient decoding, especially by the Viterbi algorithm. A rate 1/2, constraint length 2 encoder is analyzed, producing two output bits from current and past input bits. The professor defines D transforms, Laurent sequences as semi-infinite binary sequences with a definite starting time, and explains why they form a field and support well-defined convolution and inverses. Rational sequences are described as eventually periodic.

A convolutional code is defined as all output sequences generated by Laurent input sequences through an encoder impulse response. General finite-state encoders may have rational causal impulse responses and can be represented with polynomial numerators and a common denominator. Equivalent encoders generate the same code and may differ by multiplication by a rational causal sequence; a canonical polynomial encoder is preferred.

For the example encoder, the code is linear, so minimum distance equals minimum nonzero codeword weight. Using impulse response and the state transition diagram, the free distance is shown to be 5. The next lecture will cover trellis diagrams, catastrophicity, canonical generators, and the Viterbi algorithm.

In Ward v. Yorba, the plaintiff sought to reform and specifically enforce a land sale contract. Both parties claimed title through a common source, and the defendant agreed to buy the plaintiff’s interest for $4,750. The written contract mistakenly required the plaintiff to convey good title, though evidence showed the actual agreement was to convey only the plaintiff’s interest. The court held that the mistake justified reformation, the defendant was not entitled to rescind because he knew the relevant title facts and acted with counsel’s advice, and the contract had sufficient consideration despite the defendant later claiming superior title. The judgment reforming and enforcing the contract was affirmed.

The study examines the integration of AI across all phases of a university-level Digital Photography in Nature course, focusing on instructor and student experiences. It addresses a literature gap concerning holistic AI use in applied, hands-on creative disciplines such as digital photography. The study is framed by TPACK and constructivist learning theory and uses the MRK instructional design process to support AI-enhanced course design.

A qualitative case study design was employed. Participants included 38 associate degree students at a public university in eastern Turkey and the course instructor. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews conducted online with students and face-to-face with the instructor. Content analysis was used, supported by manual coding and MAXQDA, with trustworthiness addressed through credibility, transferability, dependability, and confirmability procedures.

Findings showed that the instructor integrated AI to address limitations of traditional teacher-centered instruction, students’ limited access to photography equipment, and the technical demands of the course. AI tools supported learner analysis, instructional goals, flipped classroom practices, project-based collaborative learning, and assessment. The instructor used tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Flikia AI, Krea AI, Gamma App, and Data Analysis Report AI for feedback, content preparation, photo analysis, presentation design, and evaluation. AI contributed to academic language development, personalized learning, technical feedback, and more systematic assessment.

Students reported that AI improved their technical knowledge, helped them understand photography concepts, provided quick and detailed feedback, increased awareness of AI tools, and saved time. Some viewed AI as a teacher, assistant, or guide, while others emphasized that it could not replace human instructors due to inaccuracies.

The study also identified disadvantages and risks. Infrastructure limitations, unequal access to paid tools, AI hallucinations, misinformation, contradictory outputs, student passivity, over-reliance, and reduced originality were reported. Some students accepted AI feedback without sufficient verification, highlighting the need for critical evaluation and AI literacy.

The study concludes that AI-supported education can enhance personalized learning, feedback, academic language, assessment, engagement, and technical skill development when integrated within a clear pedagogical framework. However, it requires infrastructure support, ethical use, human oversight, critical thinking, reflection-based tasks, and balanced implementation to avoid dependency and preserve creativity. Limitations include the focus on one course at one university, reliance on one instructor’s experience, qualitative methods, and the absence of a control group.

Scientists led by the MRC Laboratory of Medical Sciences, Imperial College London, and the University of Cologne found that tumor-associated bacteria can produce 2-methylisocitrate (2-MiCit), a molecule that enhances the chemotherapy drug 5-fluorouracil against colorectal cancer. Screening in microscopic worms identified E. coli as a producer of 2-MiCit, and computer modeling suggested patient tumor microbiomes could also produce it. Tests in human cancer cells and a fly model showed anti-cancer effects and extended fly survival. The molecule inhibits a mitochondrial enzyme, disrupts cancer cell metabolism, causes DNA damage, and works synergistically with chemotherapy. Researchers also created a more potent synthetic version, suggesting potential for new treatments based on microbial products.

The North Carolina Court of Appeals vacated a preliminary injunction that barred Paul Alton Vaughn from operating a used car lot allegedly in violation of Knightdale’s zoning ordinance. The passage introduces Orochi, a versatile foundational model for low-level biomedical image processing. It argues that specialist models for restoration, super-resolution, fusion, and registration are inefficient in practical workflows because tasks are often sequential, degradations are related, and biomedical images are large and high-throughput. Orochi is designed to unify diverse tasks, learn robust cross-task features, and reduce redundant training and inference costs.

Orochi uses unlabeled raw data from over 100 public studies, covering 2D–5D modalities and over 100 TB of data, with Random Multi-scale Sampling for patch and volume generation. Its self-supervised Task-related Joint-embedding Pre-training applies multiple task-specific degradations and learns their relationships. The model uses Mamba blocks with a hierarchical structure inspired by Swin-Transformer for efficient long-range modeling. A three-tier fine-tuning framework supports full, normal, and lightweight parameter-efficient tuning, with the light version using depth-wise separable convolution.

The related work section reviews self-supervised learning methods, biomedical restoration, super-resolution, registration, and fusion models, including CNN-, Transformer-, Mamba-, diffusion-, GAN-, and unsupervised approaches.

The swinging gate formation is an unconventional football special teams alignment, usually used on two-point conversion attempts, where the offense can run a trick play or shift into a field goal/extra point formation. It typically uses kicking-team personnel, with the kicker as an eligible receiver, a long snapper, a detached offensive line to one side, and at least one player behind the snapper.

The formation aims to force the defense to react quickly to an unusual look, creating opportunities for a quick run or pass. If the defense aligns well, the offense can shift back into a kicking formation. Common plays include a side snap to a runner behind the offensive line and a quick pass or screen to the opposite side.

The swinging gate is uncommon in the NFL after touchdowns because extra points are snapped from the 15-yard line, removing the practical threat of shifting into a kick. It is more relevant in high school and college, where two-point attempts are closer to the goal line.

Defending it requires matching personnel, not just numbers, protecting the heavy side, covering eligible receivers, and assigning athletic players to defend alley spaces near the snapper. Coach John Grayson’s examples emphasize using box players against blockers, safeties in alley support, and corners with pass-first responsibilities.

Margin debt, a measured form of stock-market leverage, reached a record $665.7 billion in January before falling to $645.1 billion in February and ticking up to $645.2 billion in March, according to FINRA. The passage describes statistical analysis plans for safety, laboratory, vital signs, ECG, immunogenicity, programming, QC, and reporting outputs. Adverse events will be assessed for causality and severity, summarized by treatment group, MedDRA system organ class and preferred term, and categorized as TEAEs, AESIs, injection site reactions, study drug-related events, SAEs, deaths, and special search categories. Missing AE causality will be queried and, if unresolved, treated as related; missing severity will remain missing.

Laboratory data, vital signs, ECG parameters, pregnancy tests, alcohol breath tests, physical examinations, and ADA immunogenicity results will be summarized or listed using descriptive statistics, counts, percentages, and predefined categorical thresholds. ADA incidence will include treatment-induced and treatment-boosted ADA-positive patients among evaluable patients.

The SAP adds sensitivity and supportive analyses for the primary efficacy parameter and revises terminology for secondary efficacy variables. Appendices define table, figure, and listing formatting rules, handling of missing dates, derivation formulas, SAS programming QC requirements, validation procedures, documentation requirements, and planned tables, figures, and listings for efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and patient data outputs.

Secondary efficacy endpoints assess plasma glucose recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes after injection, defined as a ≥20 mg/dL increase from baseline. Patients receiving IV glucose before recovery are counted as not recovered. Recovery rates for dasiglucagon and placebo will be compared using stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests, with confidence intervals and ANOVA analyses for glucose changes.

Finance Minister Arun Jaitley told a pre-budget consultation with economists that India’s growth remained strong despite subdued global conditions, averaging 7.5% from 2014-15 to 2016-17, and that second-quarter 2017-18 growth reversed a recent declining trend. The passage explains common, old-school, backfield, spread, and gadget football offensive formations, noting that terminology varies by coach and team. Basic formations include the I Formation, which supports inside running with a fullback lead blocker while still allowing passing threats; Split Backs, which places backs on either side of the quarterback for running or passing variations; and Twins, which puts two receivers on one side and a tight end or tight ends on the other to balance run and pass options.

Spread offense formations include Ace, a balanced and versatile set with eligible receivers on both sides; Trips, with three eligible receivers to one side and one backside receiver; Empty, with five eligible receivers and no running backs in the backfield; Quads, an empty variation with four receivers to one side; and Bunch, a three-receiver cluster designed to create defensive confusion and route advantages.

Backfield formations include Shotgun, where the quarterback lines up several yards behind center; Pistol, a shotgun variation with the running back directly behind the quarterback; and Single Back, usually referring to one back behind an under-center quarterback.

Older formations include the Wishbone, Flexbone, Double Wing, T Formation, Wing-T, Power I, and Single Wing, many of which emphasize misdirection, option runs, leverage, and multiple backfield threats, and are more common at lower levels than in modern NFL or college play.

Gadget formations include the Wildcat, with a non-quarterback taking the snap and often an unbalanced line; Emory and Henry, which spreads players into unusual pods across the field; Swinging Gate, often used after touchdowns for two-point attempts; and Unbalanced formations, which place extra ineligible players on one side to stress defenses, especially in goal-line situations.

The speaker says the team must get pucks and players to the net, control emotions after a long layoff, and focus on preparation and execution. He discusses line matchups, playing top players often, and respecting the opponent’s hard play and goaltending. NVIDIA’s Turing architecture introduces a hybrid rendering model combining rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation. Rasterization remains efficient for visibility and many rendering tasks, while ray tracing is used for reflections, refractions, shadows, ambient occlusion, and other effects where rasterization produces artifacts. Turing RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, enabling ray tracing performance far beyond software-based approaches on prior GPUs, especially when paired with denoising.

Turing also includes Tensor Cores and NVIDIA NGX, a deep learning-based technology stack for graphics features such as DLSS, DLSS 2X, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS uses trained neural networks to produce high-quality images with improved performance compared with traditional TAA, while DLSS 2X targets image quality close to 64x supersampling.

The architecture adds Mesh Shading, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering. Mesh Shading improves handling of large numbers of objects and geometry manipulation. VRS lets developers vary shading rates across screen regions for content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. TSS decouples visibility and shading by storing shading values in texture space for reuse. MVR allows multiple views or instances to be rendered efficiently in a single pass.

Turing improves VR through VirtualLink support, Multi-View Rendering, Variable Rate Shading, foveated rendering, and RT Core acceleration for VRWorks Audio. The passage also describes TU104, TU106, and Tesla T4 configurations, including CUDA Cores, Tensor Cores, RT Cores, memory interfaces, and product examples such as GeForce RTX 2080, Quadro RTX 5000, Tesla T4, and GeForce RTX 2070.

Ray tracing is explained as casting rays from the camera through pixels into a scene to determine intersections, reflections, refractions, shadows, and lighting. BVH acceleration structures reduce intersection testing, and denoising reduces the number of rays needed. Turing combines hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH algorithms, and RT Cores to make real-time ray tracing practical for games and professional graphics applications.

The passage describes SEV-related guest–hypervisor mechanisms. SEV-TIO lets SNP guests bind to trusted devices, discover support through PCIe capabilities, issue SNP TIO guest requests, use shared contiguous data pages for measurements, certificates, TDISP reports, and optional nonces, and requires hypervisor validation of returned data storage. Secure AVIC uses guest-owned APIC backing pages per vCPU, with register and unregister actions. Termination requests allow guests to request shutdown with reason codes and unsupported feature masks, while unsupported negotiated exits use an “Unsupported Event” exit code.

SEV-ES guests identify support through hypervisor-provided CPUID properties. SMP booting under SEV-ES and some SEV-SNP cases requires AP startup methods that avoid hypervisor register updates after measurement, including reset-vector approaches, AP reset hold handling, AP jump tables, and restrictions on vCPU hotplug. SEV-SNP AP creation lets guests provide VMSA pages through VMGEXIT to create or update AP state and supports vCPU hotplug.

The passage also specifies NMI handling, debug register virtualization behavior, and states that SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported. It defines Restricted Injection host notification through a shared #HV doorbell page with PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields, including setup, host behavior, guest acknowledgement, interrupt and non-maskable event handling, EOI optimization, and expected behavior for non-cooperative guests or hosts.

The passage describes a patent application for a phase-stable colloidal polysaccharide suspension containing at least partly α(1→3)-glucan. The suspension is prepared from biotechnologically produced, never-dried α(1→3)-glucan press cake with 4–80% solids, preferably 15–45%, diluted to a polysaccharide concentration of 0.01–50%, preferably 1–20%, and mechanically comminuted using a dispersing unit such as an Ultraturrax or colloid mill.

The method avoids chemical or enzymatic pretreatment, dissolving and precipitating steps, high pressures, and high shear rates, reducing energy use compared with cellulose gels. The suspensions form non-fibrillar, three-dimensional networks, show shear-diluting behavior, can bind water, and may include other polysaccharides or additives.

The suspensions can be used for films, coatings, molded bodies, binders, viscosity modification, dried powders, hybrid particles, aerogels, and reinforced structures such as flushable wipes. Examples show that never-dried glucan forms stable gels, while dried glucans produce unstable suspensions with phase separation; colloid milling can produce homogeneous glucan gels at pilot scale and at concentrations up to 10%.

The passage specifies mechanical, material, visual, and electrical requirements for the Socket 940 and its mating 940-pin ceramic µPGA package. Socket 940 supports lidded and lidless package configurations, with lidless package thickness of at least 2.20 mm. The socket cover must support the package substrate without damaging pins, maintain seating-plane flatness under 0.25 mm, and position the seating plane 4.00 ± 0.20 mm from the mounting surface after PCB mounting. The base and cover are LCP rated UL 94 V-0; the cover thickness must not exceed 1.17 mm.

Required markings include “SOCKET 940,” locked/unlocked indicators, pin A01 orientation, UL symbol, and lot traceability. Contacts use high-strength copper alloy, nickel plating, and gold on mating areas. SMT solder balls are 63/37 ± 5% tin-lead, 0.76 mm diameter, with 0.20 mm co-planarity, and contacts must prevent solder wicking.

The stainless steel actuation lever enables tool-less operation. Package insertion/extraction force with the lever open must not exceed 2 kgf; closed-position pin extraction force must be at least 0.013 kgf per pin; lever actuation force must be under 3.6 kgf; pin displacement must be under 1.0 mm. The socket must remain functional after 50 actuation cycles.

Visual requirements prohibit missing, damaged, malformed, or misaligned solder balls, contacts, cover/base features, latch, or lever. Electrical requirements include 1.5 A per contact with under 30°C rise, LLCR not exceeding 25 mΩ per contact initially and finally, inductance limits near 3–4 nH, capacitance under 1 pF, differential impedance of 100 Ω ± 10%, propagation delay skew under 10 ps plus measurement error, dielectric withstand of at least 650 Vac, and insulation resistance of at least 1000 MΩ.

The parents had a 2003 custody agreement giving the father sole custody of their two daughters and visitation for the mother subject to the children’s wishes, while requiring the father to encourage and preserve the mother’s relationship with them. After the father moved to Florida with the daughters without notifying the mother, Family Court found he had intentionally violated the custody order by obstructing the mother’s communication and visitation, but did not change custody.

The mother later sought return of the children and temporary custody. Evidence showed the father and his wife repeatedly interfered with the mother’s efforts to contact the daughters, including violating a court-ordered phone schedule. The mother withdrew her custody request as to the older daughter but continued seeking custody or visitation regarding the younger daughter. Family Court found the father had alienated the children from their mother and caused harm, but denied a custody change, continued visitation subject to the children’s wishes, and allowed the mother unrestricted phone, e-mail, and correspondence access. It also suspended the mother’s child support payments.

On appeal, the court upheld the denial of a custody change, finding the limited record did not support transferring custody. However, it ruled that visitation with the younger daughter should not have been left to the child’s wishes because she was under undue influence and the record supported that visitation with the mother was in her best interests. The matter was remitted to Family Court for immediate consideration of court-ordered visitation after updated proceedings if necessary. The suspension of the mother’s child support payments was affirmed.

In a personal injury action, the plaintiff appealed the denial of his motion to set aside a jury verdict for the defendant and the judgment dismissing the complaint. The appellate court dismissed the appeal from the order, affirmed the judgment, awarded costs to the defendant, and held that the jury’s finding that the defendant was not negligent was based on a fair interpretation of the evidence.

The Passing Game offense is a team-oriented, unstructured basketball offense based on ball movement, player movement, off-ball screens, spacing, cuts, and purposeful actions rather than set plays. It involves all five players, can be run from multiple alignments, and can be effective against both zone and person-to-person defenses. Its strengths include continuous motion, creativity, tempo control, difficulty to scout, and effectiveness against varied defenses. Weaknesses include selfish play, poor offensive rebounding, lack of patience, poor defensive reading, and players unwilling to work without the ball.

Success requires unselfishness, patience, shot discipline, sharp passing, proper 12–18 foot spacing, purposeful movement, strong screening, limited dribbling, post play, offensive rebounding, and the ability to read defensive reactions. Basic rules emphasize moving with purpose, passing accurately, meeting passes, using screens correctly, back cutting against overplay, attacking from triple threat, taking good shots, posting mismatches, and pursuing rebounds aggressively.

Variations include three-player Hi/Lo action, four-out passing with single or rotating post play, and five-player motion designed for smaller, quicker teams. Zone adjustments include quicker ball movement, fewer screens, skip passes, attacking weak sides and gaps, flash cuts, early passing, offensive rebounding, and maintaining defensive balance. Coaches must commit to teaching fundamentals and accepting player freedom, with benefits including pressure on defenses, exploiting weak defenders, fatigue from constant motion, increased opponent mistakes, and stable team play based on patience and teamwork.

The author argues against a major effort to improve U.S.-Soviet relations until Soviet intentions and flexibility are tested through existing channels, especially Shultz-Gromyko exchanges. They support addressing human rights, Soviet internal behavior, and arms control as tests of Soviet seriousness, particularly on INF, reductions, equality, verification, and compliance.

This systematic literature review examines digital leadership in education, focusing on its definition, effects, and influencing factors. Following PRISMA guidelines, the study searched Scopus, Web of Science, and EBSCO, then used citation searching, resulting in 39 empirical articles.

The review found that definitions of digital leadership vary and often omit key elements such as interaction, leader competence, followers, goals, organizational context, or environment. The study suggests viewing digital leadership through a technology-organization-environment framework as a dynamic, adaptive practice that integrates technology, shapes organizational culture, and supports digital innovation.

Digital leadership’s effects were mainly studied at the teacher level, especially technology integration, ICT competence, reflective practice, work engagement, and job satisfaction. Fewer studies addressed school-level outcomes such as administrative effectiveness, teaching quality, digital transformation, and digital learning culture. Only one study focused on student academic performance.

Influencing factors were grouped into internal factors, including individual characteristics, professional experience, and digital literacy, and external factors, including infrastructure, school culture, training, technical supervision, policy, and the COVID-19 pandemic. The review concludes that future research should further explore influencing factors, lifelong learning, digital security, follower involvement, organizational culture, and digital leadership in multicultural teams.

Keith Chegwin has died aged 60 after a long battle with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, a progressive lung condition. His family said he died peacefully at home on 11 December with his wife Maria and children Rose and Ted by his side. The passage also explains that IPF scars the lungs, worsens breathing, usually progresses over time, and commonly affects older people, especially men. Symptoms include breathlessness, persistent cough, tiredness and clubbing of fingers or toes.

College football targeting is defined by the NCAA as taking aim at an opponent with forcible contact beyond a legal tackle, block or play on the ball. Defenseless players are especially protected, and when in question, a player is considered defenseless. Targeting carries a 15-yard penalty and automatic disqualification. If it occurs in the second half, the player is suspended for the first half of the next game; repeat offenders receive additional suspensions. The NCAA adopted targeting in 2008, added automatic disqualification in 2013 and required video review confirmation in 2019. Unlike the NCAA, the NFL addresses similar hits under unnecessary roughness against defenseless players and does not require automatic disqualification unless the act is deemed flagrant. The passage cites controversial targeting-related plays involving Texas-Arizona State in 2024-25 and Clemson-Ohio State in 2019.

Fitch Ratings assigned expected 'BB(EXP)' ratings to Telenet International Finance S.a.r.L.'s Term Loan AH and Telenet Financing USD LLC's Term Loan AI, subject to final documentation. Term Loan AI will be at least USD1 billion with an 8.25-year tenor, while Term Loan AH will be at least EUR750 million with a nine-year tenor.

Fitch cites Telenet’s strong operating position in Flanders and parts of Brussels, stable free cash flow, continued network investment, and manageable impact from Belgian cable wholesale regulation. Will Ma announces prize logistics and that Bill Chen will guest lecture the final class. He then analyzes a deep-stacked cash-game hand with eight-seven suited on the button, covering continuation-bet sizing, reasons to call or raise on flop and turn, river bluff sizing, polarized ranges, and the value of position. He performs an exploitative combinatorial range analysis of the opponent’s preflop raise, flop and turn bets, and river check, concluding that a river bluff is profitable because the opponent folds often enough and combinatorial weighting matters.

After a break, Ma discusses broader poker topics. He explains the Moneymaker effect, why poker attracted money, and factors such as overconfidence, gambling self-control, rapid strategic evolution, and avoiding results-oriented thinking. He recommends online resources including CardRunners, Two Plus Two, and Twitch streams, plus several poker books. In Q&A, he discusses ways to keep playing through MIT Poker Club, handling downswings by taking breaks, estimated edges in low-stakes games, casino strategy, avoiding overconfidence through honest feedback, and motivation for playing when online poker for money is unavailable in Massachusetts.

The speaker said they are ready when called by the coach, felt the team played well despite tough calls, and expected a fast, skilled opponent. They emphasized focusing on each shift and game, preparing for the next one, and continuing to fight back and find ways to win.

Facebook shares fell 6.8% Monday, on pace for their biggest percentage decline since 2014, after U.S. and U.K. regulators criticized the company over Cambridge Analytica’s access to user data without express permission. The drop erased nearly $40 billion in market value. Analysts said the episode creates public relations and regulatory risks, though opinions differed on Facebook’s resilience. Wells Fargo and GBH Insights maintained positive ratings, while Pivotal saw systemic issues but limited near-term business impact, and Stifel warned needed trust and security changes could hurt engagement and monetization. The controversy also weighed on broader technology stocks, including Twitter, Snap, Alphabet, and the Nasdaq.

Adm. Harry Harris, commander of U.S. forces in the Pacific, will be nominated as U.S. ambassador to South Korea instead of Australia, Australian Foreign Minister Julie Bishop said after being informed by Acting Secretary of State John Sullivan. Bishop said the U.S. faces significant challenges on the Korean peninsula and that appointing a new ambassador to Australia would be a priority. The Rams traded multiple 2016 and 2017 draft picks to the Titans in 2016 to move up to No. 1 overall and select quarterback Jared Goff. The Rams ultimately received Goff, Pharoh Cooper, Temarrick Hemingway and Mike Thomas through the deal and related pick swaps. Goff struggled as a rookie but made the Pro Bowl in 2017, while Cooper also became a Pro Bowl return specialist.

The Titans used the Rams’ picks and subsequent trades to acquire Corey Davis, Jack Conklin, Austin Johnson, Derrick Henry, Jonnu Smith, LeShaun Sims and Kalan Reed. Conklin became an All-Pro rookie starter, Henry was positioned to become the lead running back, and Davis, Smith and others contributed with varying levels of impact.

The passage concludes there is no clear winner, framing the trade as quality versus quantity. The Rams gained a potential franchise quarterback and two Pro Bowlers, while the Titans gained several starters. It gives the Rams a slight edge but says the debate may continue.

The author describes founding a successful supplement company as a teenager in the 1990s, then later noticing Amazon’s emerging role in supplement sales while marketing the nootropic product Excelerol. After listing Excelerol on Amazon and requesting reviews from subscribers, the product quickly gained reviews and sales. Amazon initially increased revenue and attracted customers, but policy changes and seller restrictions revealed risks, including loss of customer ownership, account suspensions, and dependence on Amazon’s systems. The author says learning to manage Amazon’s marketplace took over five years and led to consulting companies on Amazon strategy.

The study examines coarsening of phase-separating DNA nanostar droplets embedded in a 3D self-stirring active fluid made of extensile microtubule bundles, PEG depletant, and kinesin motor clusters. ATP-driven motor activity generates chaotic flows that advect droplets. After DNA-rich phase volume fraction stabilizes, droplet growth occurs mainly through collision-driven coalescence rather than Ostwald ripening.

Experiments show that active coarsening is faster than passive coarsening, and active droplet size distributions are not self-similar: many small droplets coexist with a few exceptionally large ones, with asymmetry increasing over time. Despite this, the mean droplet radius follows a power law with an exponent similar to passive Brownian coarsening, βR≈0.33, while the total droplet number decays faster in active fluids, with γN≈-1.65 compared with γN≈-0.89 in passive fluids. These active exponents are robust to changes in ATP concentration and confinement.

Droplet tracking shows that active droplets move ballistically at short times and diffusively at longer times, with effective diffusivity independent of droplet size. This contrasts with passive droplets, which follow the Stokes–Einstein–Sutherland relation. The active diffusivity is set by the product of active-flow speed and velocity correlation length.

Simulations of hydrodynamic active flows reproduce the experimental results, including accelerated coarsening, loss of self-similarity, and similar exponents. Simulations of self-propelled particles and anomalously diffusing droplets show that coarsening exponents depend on droplet motility and collision dynamics rather than the specific transport mechanism. Collision-kernel analysis identifies a unifying control parameter: the kernel exponent k. Positive k favors collisions between large droplets, causing non-self-similar coarsening and a nonlinear relationship between βR and γN. The study finds k=3-(m+2)/α for anomalously diffusing droplets with diffusivity scaling D~R-m and MSD~tα.

A probabilistic calculation confirms that the collision-kernel exponent controls the relationship between the radius and droplet-number coarsening exponents. The authors conclude that active flows and anomalous passive mechanics can produce similar coarsening laws through shared collision-kernel scaling. They discuss implications for molecular condensates, including nuclear condensates, pathological preferential attachment, and broader volume-conserving coarsening processes in flow environments.

The speaker describes winning the championship as unreal and credits teamwork, focus, and guidance from veterans like Ray Bourque, Rob Blake, Joe Sakic, Adam Foote, and Patrick Roy. They say winning for Bourque was especially meaningful and praise the entire organization, including ownership, management, scouting, coaches, and players. The speaker also reflects on living with Roy’s family, celebrating with family and friends, seeing and holding the Cup for the first time, and staying focused during the game.

The passage describes NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture features for AI and HPC workloads. A100 uses SECDED ECC for HBM2, L2, L1 caches, and register files. It includes a 40 MB L2 cache, 6.7x larger than V100, with 2.3x higher L2 bandwidth, cache residency controls, and Compute Data Compression that can improve DRAM bandwidth, L2 bandwidth, and L2 capacity.

A100 has more SMs than V100 and third-generation Tensor Cores that support larger tensor operations, higher mixed-precision performance, improved data sharing, fewer instructions, fewer register accesses, asynchronous global-to-shared memory copy, asynchronous barriers, and larger shared memory. It supports CUDA 11 features including task graph acceleration, asynchronous copy APIs, L2 residency controls, Cooperative Groups enhancements, MIG support, sparsity, and Tensor Core updates.

The Multi-Instance GPU feature can partition one A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory bandwidth, and fault isolation. MIG supports multi-tenant, single-user, and multi-user use cases, VM partitioning, QoS, and migration of vGPUs between compatible GPU Instances.

A100 also includes third-generation NVLink with twelve links and 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, improved error and fault detection, NVJPG hardware JPEG decode, an Optical Flow Accelerator, improved atomic operation throughput, and five NVDEC units. DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs with NVLink, NVSwitch, InfiniBand, MIG, and NVIDIA software to support scalable AI infrastructure. The passage also explains sparse neural networks and A100’s fine-grained structured sparsity support.

The Vintage Optical Shop, an online retailer of authentic vintage eyeglasses and sunglasses, is offering new email subscribers a one-time $20 coupon for their next purchase. Subscribers will also receive updates on new arrivals, sales, specials and coupons. The offer applies to products including cat eyeglasses and sunglasses, Pince Nez glasses, Windsor glasses, safety goggles and John Lennon glasses. The shop sells unused, handcrafted vintage eyewear sourced from the 1850s to the 1980s.

Trump claimed “Big Homebuilders” are sitting on 2 million empty lots and urged Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to help spur construction. Economist Bryan Caplan rejected the comparison to OPEC, arguing that housing shortages stem from zoning, permitting delays, and local regulation rather than builder collusion. NAHB data cited in the passage shows many builders report shortages of buildable lots. Chanse Alexander describes studying abroad in Buenos Aires as a Pepperdine sophomore and finding the experience welcoming despite concerns shaped by racism and discrimination in the U.S. He recalls police officers and strangers helping him when he was lost, making Argentine friends through nightlife, and feeling appreciated rather than singled out for his race. He notes that people of African descent seemed uncommon in the city, but he felt an immediate bond when meeting others of African descent. Living abroad for six months changed his outlook, and he encourages African American students not to let fear stop them from traveling.

Emma Stone signed a two-year Louis Vuitton deal worth between $6 million and $10 million after nearly a year of pursuit by LVMH. Ryan Gosling reportedly declined endorsement offers. Stone also discussed training for “Battle of the Sexes,” saying weightlifting and protein shakes helped her build strength and enjoy exercise.

The study evaluated whether transcriptome-wide splicing outlier patterns can aid rare disease diagnosis, focusing on mechanisms that affect splicing globally rather than single-gene cis effects. Whole-blood RNA-seq from 390 UDN and GREGoR samples was analyzed with FRASER and FRASER2 to detect splicing outliers, including intron retention in minor intron containing genes (MIGs).

Splicing outlier genes were enriched for OMIM disease genes and developmental delay/intellectual disability genes, and depleted for CRISPR non-essential genes; FRASER2 outliers were also enriched for haploinsufficient genes. Forty individuals, or 10.3% of the cohort, had excess splicing outliers by at least one metric. Batch effects significantly influenced some FRASER outlier measures, while FRASER2 measures showed no significant covariate associations.

Analysis of significant intron retention outliers in MIGs identified five individuals with excess events. Four had rare biallelic RNU4ATAC variants and phenotypes consistent with RNU4atac-opathy, supporting diagnoses and variant interpretation. The fifth individual had rare compound heterozygous RNU6ATAC variants, shared most MIG intron-retention outlier genes with the RNU4atac-opathy cases, and had overlapping clinical features, making RNU6ATAC a putative novel gene-disease candidate.

Increasing sample size increased the number and z-score of significant MIG intron-retention outliers detected in one RNU4atac-opathy case. FRASER2’s Jaccard index also identified the minor spliceopathy cases, though with less specificity. The authors conclude that biologically coherent transcriptome-wide splicing outlier patterns can support rare disease diagnosis, variant curation, and gene-disease discovery.

Sprint and The Sprint Foundation will provide free devices and wireless service to 180,000 low-income high school students this school year through the 1Million Project, a five-year effort to connect 1 million students without home internet access. Participants in more than 1,300 schools across 32 states will receive a smartphone, tablet, or hotspot plus 3GB of LTE data monthly for up to four years. Sprint said the program follows a January pilot with 3,750 students and will involve about $2.16 billion in donated service, support, and staffing.

Vijay Mallya appeared before Westminster Magistrates’ Court in London for his extradition case related to alleged loan defaults of nearly Rs 9,000 crore involving Kingfisher Airlines. He denied all allegations, said he had enough evidence to prove his case, and rejected claims that loans were diverted, including to Royal Challengers Bangalore. Chief Magistrate Emma Louise Arbuthnot extended his bail until December 4, tentatively set as the final hearing date, with the next case management hearing on July 6, which Mallya was excused from attending due to media crowding concerns.

Britain’s Crown Prosecution Service, representing Indian authorities, sought a December hearing, while Mallya’s defence requested March or April 2018, citing pending evidence and an expected second extradition request believed to relate to an Enforcement Directorate case. The judge said the December date would be reviewed in July. Mallya, arrested in April by Scotland Yard and released on conditional bail, has been in the UK since March 2016. The case may involve appeals even if extradition is ordered.

BiondVax Pharmaceuticals announced a $2.83 million investment from Angels High Tech Investments in exchange for 33.8 million ordinary shares, giving Angels 19.99% of the company. Angels is owned by Check Point co-founder and chairman Marius Nacht. BiondVax said the investment supports development and commercialization of its universal flu vaccine candidate.

The Enforcement Directorate told the Delhi High Court that Nirav Modi is using Firestar Diamonds to indirectly challenge the money laundering case and hinder the investigation. It opposed the firm’s plea to stay proceedings, calling it premature and misconceived, and said Modi has not joined investigations by the ED or CBI.

The passage describes AMD Generic Encapsulated Software Architecture (AGESA™), a BIOS procedure library intended to help AMD customers integrate AMD technology into products. The document defines user-level procedure interfaces for host environment wrapper implementers, recommends wrapper implementation practices, lists related AMD and industry specifications, and defines terminology such as wrapper, socket, processor, die, core, BSP, AP, and MP.

AGESA uses a three-level code version scheme X.Y.Z, while the interface specification uses X.Y. Major versions indicate major feature changes, minor versions indicate interface changes, and code update numbers indicate bug-fix releases without interface changes. Release packages include binaries, build control files, wrapper examples, specialized tools, and source files organized with descriptive long file names and standard headers.

The interface is designed to remain stable across processor generations by minimizing entry points and aligning them with boot-time phases rather than specific technical functions. AGESA automatically determines many configuration parameters, while required and optional host-supplied parameters are defined in call structures. Calls use initializer functions that allocate and pre-fill interface data structures with defaults, after which the host fills required fields, calls the main function, checks status, and releases the structure.

Build configuration is controlled mainly through a platform-specific `<Plat>Options.c` file, which describes target platform options and is used to generate defaults tables. AGESA supports binary module builds and full source integration. Binary images include headers identifying the image, module headers, dispatcher offsets, relocation information, image size, and checksums. Host environments locate the binary image, calculate dispatcher addresses, and call AGESA through a bridge routine. Execution expects 32-bit protected flat addressing, identity-mapped paging if enabled, and a valid stack.

Error reporting uses return codes and an event log. Status codes include success, unsupported, bounds check, alert, warning, error, critical, and fatal. The event log retains the 16 most recent events and can be read through `AmdReadEventLog`.

The passage also covers UEFI integration, including SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases, required tools, build files, environment variables, and PEIM/DXE responsibilities. UEFI support includes stack setup, processor initialization, memory initialization, reset coordination, late initialization, table generation, protocols, PPIs, and a VGA control driver for processor GPU decoding.

Porting guidance states that 16-bit real mode support is deprecated, while binary modules remain usable in 32-bit protected mode. The host BIOS must implement bridge and call-out router mechanisms, create and fill standard headers, provide stack setup, avoid modifying cache controls during Cache-As-RAM operation, and use provided stack procedures. AGESA provides service procedures for creating and releasing structures, reading event logs, querying processor, PCI, APIC, memory, MMIO, execution cache, and data eye information.

Published boot-time entry points include minimal reset initialization, early processor and platform initialization, and memory initialization. The passage warns that only published interface functions should be called, and internal functions may change or be removed.

Milford are favored to beat St. Naul’s in the 2017 Intermediate final at O’Donnell Park, Letterkenny. Milford, managed by Danny O’Donnell, have competed well in Division One, are on course to retain top-flight status, and reached the final by defeating Cloughaneely and Aodh Ruadh. Their only previous Intermediate title came in 1992, and O’Donnell says their target is to win and move into senior championship. The returns of Cathal McGettigan and Gary Merritt have strengthened their panel.

St. Naul’s have a painful history in the competition, reaching eight finals in 30 years but winning only once, in 2011. Under John McNulty, they have had a strong season, contending for promotion and winning an All-Ireland Gaeltacht crown, while reaching the final after a replay win over Gaeil Fhánada. Stephen Griffin’s return from injury and Peadar Mogan’s talent boost their chances, but the passage presents Milford as stronger overall and difficult to upset.

Enron-related news on Nov. 1, 2001 centered on the SEC elevating its inquiry into partnerships tied to former CFO Andrew Fastow into a formal investigation, raising analyst concerns that the probe could expand beyond the partnerships into Enron’s core trading business. Enron said it was cooperating and believed the probe remained limited to the partnerships.

Standard & Poor’s cut Enron’s long-term rating to BBB and short-term rating to A-3, warning of possible further downgrades. Moody’s had also recently downgraded Enron. Enron shares fell about 14% to $11.99 and had lost roughly two-thirds of their value in two weeks.

Enron secured a $1 billion credit line from J.P. Morgan Chase and Salomon Smith Barney, backed by Northern Natural Gas and Transwestern Pipeline assets, to support liquidity, refinance obligations, and maintain investment-grade status. Analysts described the financing as both positive and concerning because it was secured by assets.

Major North American gas and power trading partners generally said they continued doing business with Enron, though some firms were monitoring exposure, reviewing longer-term deals more closely, or requiring stricter credit terms. EnronOnline volumes were reported as strong, but competing exchanges such as IntercontinentalExchange and NYMEX were seen as potential limited beneficiaries of Enron’s credit concerns.

CBSMarketWatch reported Enron hired former SEC enforcement chief William McLucas as counsel and formed a special committee to address the SEC investigation.

The passage argues that state higher education funding remains deeply inequitable, reflecting a history of racism, sexism, classism, and exclusion. It cites examples such as Ole Miss receiving twice as much state funding per student as Jackson State, and UConn’s growing funding advantage over Southern Connecticut State University despite SCSU serving more marginalized and low-income students.

The author says most states perpetuate disparities through “base plus” budgeting, which relies on prior appropriations rather than formulas based on institutional or student need. Flagship universities receive substantially more state funding, private support, and tuition revenue while serving fewer marginalized students, even though most public university students, including most Black, Hispanic, Native American, and Pell-eligible students, attend non-flagship or open-access institutions.

The passage distinguishes equity from adequacy: equity means distributing available funds according to relative need, while adequacy means providing enough total funding for institutions to fulfill their missions. It argues that increasing total funding without first fixing inequitable distribution widens existing gaps.

The proposed solution is to rebuild higher education finance with equity as the foundation, drawing from K–12 funding reforms. States should fund institutions based on student and institutional need, account for outside revenue sources such as endowments and tuition, and separate education funding from research, health care, or agricultural missions. The passage concludes that higher education funding must be systemically reformed so resources align with today’s students and institutions.

The passage argues that climate education, especially within Comparative and International Education, often emphasizes scientific knowledge, sustainability, green technology, and policy solutions while neglecting colonial histories, Black and Indigenous knowledge systems, and ongoing ecological injustices. It critiques education for sustainable development and UN development frameworks for relying on modernization, resilience, and growth-based logics that can reproduce colonial inequalities.

The authors introduce “climate coloniality” to describe how colonial power structures, racial capitalism, extractivism, and unequal global relations shape climate impacts and solutions. They argue that communities in the Global South and marginalized groups bear disproportionate climate harms despite contributing least to emissions, while proposed solutions such as lithium mining, carbon offsets, and renewable technologies can continue patterns of extraction, displacement, and dispossession.

Using Said’s contrapuntal reading, the passage proposes examining climate education by identifying which voices are amplified or silenced. It advances “decolonial educational ecologies” as an approach that centers historically marginalized knowledge systems, Black and Indigenous perspectives, more-than-human relations, reparative justice, and context-specific alternatives to Western anthropocentric and capitalist frameworks. The authors reject climate solutionism and call for climate education that critically examines colonialism, modernity, extractivism, epistemic violence, and the political-economic systems underlying ecological crisis.

The passage argues that the human brain does not work like a computer and does not store memories, words, images, rules, algorithms, or representations. It says humans are born with senses, reflexes, and learning mechanisms, while computers literally encode, store, copy, retrieve, and process symbolic data using algorithms.

The author describes the “information processing” metaphor as one of many historical metaphors used to explain intelligence, following spiritual, hydraulic, mechanical, electrical, chemical, and telegraph-based models. He argues that this metaphor became dominant after the rise of computers and cognitive science but remains only a metaphor, not established knowledge.

Using a classroom exercise involving drawings of a dollar bill from memory and from sight, the author argues that recall is not retrieval of a stored image but a less accurate re-experiencing enabled by changes in the brain. He states that learning changes the brain in orderly ways, allowing people to perform tasks such as singing a song or reciting a poem without stored copies being retrieved.

The passage cites alternative approaches that reject mental representations, including an explanation of catching a fly ball through maintaining a visual relationship rather than computing a trajectory. It also criticizes predictions about downloading minds to computers, arguing that brains are living, unique systems shaped by individual histories. The author concludes that the information processing metaphor has distorted neuroscience and should be abandoned in favor of studying humans as organisms, not computers.

Revolution Lighting Technologies will report first-quarter 2017 financial results before market open on May 2, 2017, and host a conference call and live webcast at 11 a.m. ET. Replay access will be available until May 16, with an archived webcast on the company website. The company designs, manufactures, markets, and sells LED lighting solutions for industrial, commercial, and government markets.

Mike Francesa is expected to return to WFAN afternoons after approaching Entercom management and accepting a significant pay cut from his prior roughly $3 million salary, according to sources. The decision reportedly came above WFAN vice president Mark Chernoff, who did not support bringing him back. Francesa had retired Dec. 15 but sought a return after other options, including SiriusXM talks brokered by Chris Russo, did not meet his interests or desired pay.

Francesa’s new show is expected to air weekdays from 3 to 6:30 p.m. Chris Carlin, Maggie Gray and Bart Scott will move to 1-3 p.m., while Evan Roberts and Joe Benigno will shift to 10 a.m.-1 p.m. WFAN acknowledged talks but gave no details; Francesa did not comment directly beyond confirming to Newsday he was returning.

The move has created tension at WFAN. Russo criticized Francesa’s return, and Boomer Esiason called him “classless” after comments Francesa and Russo made about the station. Carlin addressed the situation by saying the trio would remain part of WFAN and that bringing back someone successful for 30 years made business sense. Sources said Entercom saw Francesa’s discounted return as financially attractive, with total salary costs still below the previous arrangement.

The passage reports an electrically driven polariton laser based on a solution-grown CsPbBr3 perovskite microplate embedded in an optical microcavity. The device uses chemically inert single-walled carbon nanotube electrodes and a two-stage cooling protocol to form and freeze a p-i-n rectifying diode structure from an initial metal-semiconductor-metal Schottky diode.

The authors fabricate CsPbBr3 microplates by anti-solvent vapor diffusion, transfer them onto patterned SWCNT electrodes on a distributed Bragg reflector, and complete the optical cavity with a top reflector. Under cryogenic conditions, carrier injection is enhanced by ion and vacancy redistribution in the perovskite, which thins interfacial barriers and enables rectifying behavior. Cooling under a constant current of 0.5 µA to 8 K stabilizes this structure.

Angle- and polarization-resolved electroluminescence measurements show strong coupling, with lower, middle, and upper polariton branches derived from a coupled-oscillator model. The device exhibits spatially localized polariton electroluminescence and a transition to polariton lasing at a threshold current of 60 µA, corresponding to about 2.8 kA cm−2, under continuous electrical injection. The transition is marked by increased emission intensity, linewidth narrowing, and energy blueshift. Further current increase leads to saturation and suppression attributed to self-heating. Temperature-dependent measurements support the role of Joule heating in post-threshold blueshifts.

The work presents a strategy for solution-processed electrically pumped semiconductor lasers using perovskite polariton devices.

Simon Paul Pearson, 28, of Twerton, was sentenced at Bristol Crown Court for stealing £759 of garden furniture from the Locksbrook Inn in Bath. He also admitted trespassing at three other Bath businesses with intent to steal. He received a 20-week jail sentence, suspended for 18 months.

The study examines whether scientific papers that create “knowledge gaps” in concept networks are more generative than other recombinations. Using 34,363,623 journal articles and conference proceedings from Microsoft Academic Graph from 1900 to 2020, the authors model knowledge as evolving networks of level-3 research concepts and use persistent homology to identify papers that create topological gaps.

Papers are classified as gap openers, non-gap openers with novel concept pairs, or non-gap openers without novel pairs. Gap openers make up only 0.84% of articles, vary by discipline, and decline over time after early growth. They tend to connect newer, less established concepts, cite fewer prior works, show higher recombinational novelty, and use title verbs associated with creation and innovation.

Gap-opening papers show stronger long-term generative capacity than the other paper types. They are more likely to become highly cited, score higher on disruption, show suggestive positive association with Nobel Prize-winning work, and receive substantially more citations over 20 years despite receiving fewer citations in the first five years. Their recognition tends to emerge after about eight years and is reflected in higher Sleeping Beauty Index scores.

Gap openers also differ in team characteristics. They are associated with smaller, younger, fresher, and more geographically proximate teams. The authors argue that topological significance, rather than novelty alone, helps explain which conceptual recombinations stimulate future research and redirect scientific inquiry.

The passage describes devices, systems, and methods for real-time measurement of working tool torque, power, energy, force, and penetration depth while drilling, cutting, or driving implants into materials such as animal tissue. It addresses limitations of conventional torque estimation, bone strength assessment, bore depth measurement, depth gauges, and fluoroscopy during orthopedic and related procedures.

The disclosed system includes an instrument with a working tool, sensors, a controller, and a display or graphical user interface. Sensors generate real-time torque and force signals, which the controller processes into values representative of torque, energy, power, accumulated energy, material strength, depth, or related measurements. Energy data may be used to determine regional material strength, bone density, and correlations with screw pullout strength. Power or torque changes may be used to help prevent inadvertent plunge and detect cortical or joint penetration.

The instrument may include rotational and axial drive motors, a floating motor sub-assembly with a torque sensor, a guide harp with rods and a distal guide element, axial force sensors for the guide harp and working tool, removable tool guides, irrigation, power systems, and interchangeable working tools such as drill bits, saws, burrs, reamers, screwdrivers, or self-drilling implants. The guide harp can provide real-time depth control and measurement by moving relative to the working tool.

The electronics module can include a controller, memory, communication port, sensors, and user interface. Data may be displayed on the instrument or an external computing device through wired or wireless communication. Alerts and graphical outputs can provide real-time information about axial force, torque, power, energy, depth, tool status, and penetration behavior to support user decisions during procedures.

A study published in Thorax examined whether cured meat consumption affects asthma symptoms using data from 971 adults in the French EGEA study. Participants averaged 2.5 servings of cured meat weekly and were grouped by low, medium, or high intake. During follow-up, asthma worsened in 20 percent, improved in 27 percent, and was unchanged in 53 percent. Worsening symptoms occurred in 14 percent of low consumers, 20 percent of medium consumers, and 22 percent of high consumers. After controlling for factors such as smoking, activity, age, sex, and education, high consumers were 76 percent more likely to report worsening asthma than low consumers. BMI accounted for 14 percent of worsening symptoms, suggesting an effect beyond weight. The observational study cannot prove cause and effect and relied on participants’ memories.

The speaker says the team must treat the game as its only chance to win, avoid extra games and injury risks, and focus on finding a way to win. They emphasize confidence, continued effort, matching the opponent’s intensity, and using past experience to stay relaxed and focused despite the crowd.

Julie Armstrong forwarded a Nov. 20, 2001 “Enron Mentions” news roundup and noted “See article #3 on Andersen.” The articles report that Enron widened its third-quarter loss, warned it might need to repay or collateralize a $690 million obligation after a credit downgrade, and said further downgrades could trigger $3.9 billion in additional repayments. Enron also warned of possible fourth-quarter charges, including a $700 million pretax hit tied to partnership assets, and said Arthur Andersen had not completed its review of the filing. Although the People conceded his appeal waiver was ineffective, his ineffective assistance claim regarding Grand Jury proceedings was unsupported and had been withdrawn with his motions. His challenge to restitution was also rejected because he consented to the court’s procedure. Remaining claims were found meritless.

The speaker says Belfour was ill, had breathing and energy issues, and was affected during the game, though he is expected to be ready. Dustin Johnson arrived at Erin Hills to defend his US Open title shortly after the birth of his second son, River, and said fatherhood has given him a new perspective, making family more important than golf. The world number one, favored for the Wisconsin tournament, said his family’s health made it an “awesome couple of days.” Johnson, who won his first major at Oakmont last year after near-misses, said he is still disappointed by the back injury that forced him out of the Masters. After missing the cut at Memorial, he practiced at Erin Hills and said the course suits him, though every part of his game must work to win.

LLMs can support social science by synthesizing research data, simulating demographic preferences and behaviors, assisting tasks such as stance detection and sentiment analysis, and helping generate hypotheses or theories. However, concerns include accuracy, bias, stereotyping, misinformation, ethical misuse, and the need for human oversight. The passage argues that AI governance must balance innovation with risk mitigation, address misinformation, deepfakes, bias, and regulatory gaps, and involve governments, industry, academia, developers, users, and communities through both top-down and bottom-up mechanisms. It calls for forward-looking, transparent, human-centered AI regulation and timely reporting, investigation, and updating of rules.

It urges repeal or revision of those laws, the Tenure of Office Act, and provisions limiting presidential military authority and state militias.

It emphasizes the need for retrenchment, citing large postwar expenditures, declining revenues, heavy military costs, and a public debt exceeding $2.5 billion. It recommends a definite plan to reduce the debt, lower interest burdens, and avoid permanent national indebtedness. It also calls for restoring specie payments, making currency uniform in value, and reducing reliance on depreciated paper money.

Department reports cover public land sales, pensions, patents, Indian treaties and reservations, Pacific railroad construction, Army and Navy reductions, and postal deficits caused partly by restored and expanded service. The message also reviews foreign relations, including mediation efforts in South America, issues involving Paraguay, treaties and negotiations with Mexico, Nicaragua, Venezuela, Denmark, Hawaii, Russia, Italy, Germany, Britain, China, Japan, and Spain, and possible future action regarding Caribbean republics.

The message renews recommendations for constitutional amendments providing direct popular election of the President, Vice President, and Senators; barring presidential reelection; clarifying succession if both the President and Vice President are unavailable; and limiting federal judicial terms. Aspire Music Group sued Cash Money Records over alleged unpaid profits and copyright royalties from Drake’s first six solo albums. Aspire claims a 2008 agreement entitled it to one-third of net profits and master recording copyrights, but Cash Money paid only modest advances and later signed Drake directly. Aspire seeks a court-supervised accounting, with the claim reportedly worth tens of millions.

The passage distinguishes biological sex from gender identity, stating that biological sex is guided by genes involved in sexual differentiation, including SRY on the Y chromosome, which is important for testis formation. Studies cited found SRY-related differences in XX anatomically male individuals and an SRY mutation in an XY anatomically female individual, and showed that inserting SRY into female mouse embryos caused male development. The author says gender identity is poorly understood but likely has biological influences, possibly involving genes on sex chromosomes, while cautioning against using biological variables as arbiters of gender identity.

Prime Minister Andrew Holness said Jamaica will intensify efforts to address crime, including splitting police operations in western parishes into two areas and increasing the Jamaica Defence Force presence to a battalion in Montego Bay. He said serious crimes, especially murders, have affected parts of the country and that Jamaicans want firm action against criminals. Holness said poverty and lack of opportunity do not excuse crime and argued that criminal activity harms livelihoods and communities. He announced plans to create a legislative framework for special long-term operations in high-crime areas, including searches for guns, contraband and criminals. He also said the Government has invested in maritime border control and is seeking international technical and strategic support, while stressing that Jamaica must solve its own crime problem.

The passage describes container-based patterns for distributed systems. The ambassador pattern separates application logic from communication logic by routing local requests to sharded storage, brokering service discovery across environments, or splitting traffic for experiments using tools such as twemproxy and nginx. The adapter pattern modifies an application container’s interface to meet expected conventions for monitoring, logging, or health checks, with examples using Prometheus exporters, fluentd, and MySQL health-check adapters.

It then contrasts microservices with monolithic systems, noting that microservices improve team autonomy, API-based decoupling, and independent scaling, while making debugging and architecture more complex. Several multi-node patterns are presented: replicated load-balanced stateless services for redundancy and scaling; session-tracked services for routing a user consistently to the same replica; caching layers for performance; rate limiting for denial-of-service defense; and nginx-based SSL termination.

The passage also explains sharded services, where each shard handles only part of the data. Sharded caches improve memory utilization, but failures or upgrades can reduce capacity and increase cache misses. Replicated sharded caches improve resilience and allow individual hot shards to scale. It discusses sharding functions, key selection, and consistent hashing to reduce remapping during resharding.

The scatter/gather pattern distributes a request to multiple leaf nodes, gathers partial results, and combines them at the root, enabling parallel processing. Examples include document search with replicated or sharded leaves. The passage notes limits from request overhead, stragglers, and availability risks, and recommends replicated shards for reliability and scale.

Finally, the passage introduces function-as-a-service and event-driven processing. FaaS simplifies deployment and automatic scaling but complicates system visibility, dependency tracking, background processing, memory-heavy workloads, and sustained request cost. It identifies request or response transformation as a suitable FaaS decorator pattern.

The passage argues that personal financial planning is complex and influenced by beliefs, attitudes, biases, and decisions. It outlines four areas for self-assessment: whether financial beliefs are grounded in objective information, whether one acknowledges limits in knowledge and seeks help, how often one reviews financial matters, and how well one manages change. It emphasizes moving away from bias, using objectivity, and understanding one’s own knowledge and behavior to support better financial decisions and family well-being.

Vice Admiral Kevin M Donegan met Admiral M Zakaullah at Naval Headquarters to discuss bilateral naval collaboration and Indian Ocean security, praised Exercise AMAN-17, Pakistan Navy professionalism, and its role in regional maritime security.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on July 31, 2019, its Leadership Development and Compensation Committee approved a one-year leave of absence for Jeffrey M. Blackburn, Senior Vice President, Business Development, beginning in the first quarter of 2020, and suspended forfeiture of his restricted stock unit awards during the leave.

Ali Allouche, a 17-year-old Virginia teen undergoing bone cancer treatment, has begun a food-focused trip across the U.S. with his mother, Jennifer Danko, inspired by Anthony Bourdain’s “Parts Unknown.” The trips are planned around his chemotherapy and surgery schedule and have helped give him and his mother something to look forward to. They recently ate at The Inn at Little Washington and hope to visit restaurants and food destinations in Chicago, Boston, Los Angeles and possibly Tokyo. Danko created a GoFundMe for travel and meals, raising $31,400 of a $35,000 goal. The U.S. Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to withhold $4 billion in foreign aid funds while Congress considers a rescission request under the Impoundment Control Act. The court said the government had made a sufficient preliminary showing and that alleged foreign-affairs harms outweighed potential harms to plaintiffs, while noting it was not deciding the merits. The ABA is among the plaintiffs, saying tens of millions in funding for foreign rule-of-law and human-rights programs were frozen. Justice Elena Kagan dissented, joined by Justices Sonia Sotomayor and Ketanji Brown Jackson, arguing the emergency application involved high-stakes, uncharted issues.

The White House said talks at the Korean demilitarized zone between a U.S. delegation led by Ambassador Sung Kim and North Korean officials were positive and would continue, with the Trump-Kim summit still expected to take place on June 12.

The passage reports pre-deployment laboratory characterization of 25 Ultra-High-Frequency detector modules for the Simons Observatory, which observes the cosmic microwave background from Chile. Each module contains 1720 antenna-coupled transition-edge sensor bolometers plus 36 dark devices, read out with microwave SQUID multiplexing. Across more than 36,000 tested TESs, average operable yield was 83%, meeting the baseline yield target, while resonator channel yield averaged 86%. Median detector properties were similar for the 220 and 280 GHz bands, with critical temperatures near 163 mK, saturation powers of 24 and 26 pW, dark noise-equivalent powers of 39 and 42 aW/√Hz, and optical efficiencies of 0.62 and 0.63. Most detectors met requirements for saturation power, noise, and optical efficiency, though two modules were rejected for saturation/noise concerns and one for low optical efficiency linked to re-annealing. Nineteen best-performing modules will be installed in Simons Observatory instruments; thirteen have already been deployed, with six more planned for the LAT upgrade.

Erik Demaine presents a cell-probe lower bound for dynamic connectivity: insertions, deletions, and connectivity queries require Ω(log n) time per operation, even when connected components are paths, with extensions to amortized and randomized settings.

The proof reduces dynamic connectivity to bulk operations on a √n by √n grid whose consecutive columns are connected by perfect matchings representing permutations. Updates replace one permutation using √n edge operations, and verify-sum queries check whether a prefix composition of permutations equals a given permutation using √n connectivity queries.

A bad access sequence is built using the bit-reversal order. A balanced binary tree over time is used to analyze communication from updates in a node’s left subtree to queries in its right subtree. For each node with l leaves, the proof shows that Ω(l√n) relevant cell probes are needed in expectation, and summing over the tree yields the Ω(n log n) total lower bound for bulk operations.

The argument uses information theory: random update permutations require Ω(l√n log n) bits to encode. If too few cells written in the left subtree are read in the right subtree, those permutations could be encoded too compactly, giving a contradiction. A warm-up proves this for prefix-sum queries; the final verify-sum proof uses simulation over all possible query permutations plus separator sets to handle incorrect queries. The result implies optimality of logarithmic-time dynamic tree structures such as link/cut trees.

Vernon Clausing appealed convictions for delivery and possession with intent to deliver legend drugs after his osteopathic medical license was revoked. He argued that jury instructions misstated RCW 69.41, the charging document was defective, certain testimony was improperly admitted, and prosecutorial misconduct denied him a fair trial.

The court held that the challenged instructions correctly stated that legend drugs must be dispensed by a licensed practitioner pursuant to a valid order or prescription, or delivered by a practitioner acting within the scope of a license. It rejected Clausing’s claim that any unlicensed person could lawfully deliver legend drugs to someone with a valid prescription without lawful dispensing. The court also found the charging document sufficient when liberally construed, held that instructions on valid prescriptions, labeling, and dispensing did not lessen the State’s burden, and concluded that admission of the Board of Pharmacy director’s opinion was harmless. The prosecutor’s closing remarks were not misconduct. The convictions were affirmed.

Enron’s Dabhol Power Co. issued a political force majeure notice to Maharashtra amid unpaid bills and disputes with the state electricity board, while India’s government said it would seek conciliation. Reports note Dabhol is owed payments, faces penalty claims, and may pursue arbitration in London.
