In Sparkman v. Brown, the court held that a cash sale does not pass title without payment. Because the defendant bought the property for cash and never paid or tendered payment, and no waiver was shown, the directed verdict for the plaintiff was proper. The dismissal of certiorari was affirmed.

This study investigated thalamic local field potentials (LFPs) as potential biomarkers for closed-loop VIM deep brain stimulation (DBS) for tremor. In 34 patients with essential tremor, multiple sclerosis, or Parkinson’s disease undergoing DBS-related surgery, thalamic LFPs and hand accelerometry were recorded. Tremor showed a moderate correlation with low-frequency LFP spectral power in alpha and theta bands and a strong correlation with peak LFP–acceleration coherence. Postural tremor was decoded from LFPs with an AUC of about 0.7, including during high-frequency DBS. High-frequency DBS reduced low-frequency spectral power compared with baseline. Computational modeling suggested that LFP spectral power varies with electrode location, tremor-cell distribution, and the proportion of tremor cells, potentially explaining participant variability.

In 2015, Dan Schulman became CEO of PayPal and set a mission to democratize financial services and promote financial health. PayPal grew within the expanding digital payments industry through partnerships, acquisitions, and new products, including digital wallets, remittances, lending, cryptocurrency payments, and its SuperApp.

In 2019, PayPal discovered that many of its own hourly and entry-level employees were financially insecure. Surveys and analysis showed that half of global customer service employees had only 4% to 6% of pay left after basic expenses, nearly two-thirds ran out or nearly ran out of money between paychecks, and nearly one-third could not cover a reasonable unexpected expense. PayPal concluded that market-based wages did not reflect local costs of living.

PayPal created an Employee Financial Wellness Initiative for hourly and entry-level employees. The plan included wage increases where appropriate, a 60% reduction in U.S. health care premiums for eligible employees, company-funded health reimbursement accounts, stock grants for employees who had not previously received equity, and financial coaching and tools. The initiative cost tens of millions of dollars in its first year and was supported by PayPal’s leadership and board as aligned with the company’s mission and business interests.

During the Covid-19 pandemic, PayPal moved employees to remote work, avoided pandemic-related layoffs, provided equipment and stipends, and introduced crisis leave. PayPal’s business also grew as digital payments and e-commerce adoption accelerated.

By 2021, PayPal reported indicators of improvement: customer service turnover fell from 19.4% in 2019 to 7.3% in 2020, engagement scores rose, more employees reported improved financial wellness, and 76% of surveyed respondents said they intended to stay at PayPal for at least five years. PayPal continued adding employee financial supports, including on-demand pay tools and additional equity grants.

PayPal also promoted stakeholder capitalism and employee financial wellness beyond the company, partnering with organizations including Financial Health Network, Good Jobs Institute, and Just Capital. By the end of 2021, 11 companies had joined the Worker Financial Wellness Initiative.

Industrial enterprises increasingly rely on complex simulations, modeling, and data analysis, but limited or outdated IT infrastructure forces trade-offs between speed, cost, and accuracy. IDC reports that 42% of respondents use outdated or inaccurate simulations, while half say calculations take too long. Demand for high-performance calculations is expected to rise sharply, from 8% currently reporting high demand to almost half within two years.

High-performance computing (HPC) is presented as a major enabler for product and process innovation in manufacturing. It supports complex calculations, improves simulation quality and speed, enables more iterations, unlocks new usage scenarios, and increases agility. Four out of five surveyed decision makers view HPC as a game changer, rising to 96% among enterprises already using it. More than a quarter already use professional HPC infrastructure, while 39% are planning or piloting deployment.

Most HPC users prefer external infrastructure: 87% use or plan external HPC from providers such as cloud providers, and 74% operate or plan their own HPC infrastructure in colocation datacenters. Only 6% currently use on-premises HPC, while 28% plan to do so. Key challenges include security concerns, cited by 72% of respondents, high investment and operating costs, licensing costs, energy consumption and sustainability concerns, computing power limitations, availability, scalability, complexity, and lack of expertise.

Cloud-based HPC and HPC as a Service are expected to become increasingly important because they can improve scalability, flexibility, performance, cost management, collaboration, and access to modern technologies. Public cloud is expected to be the most important HPC architecture for surveyed manufacturing enterprises using or planning HPC, followed by hybrid cloud. HPCaaS is viewed as useful for outsourcing infrastructure, avoiding in-house setup, supporting occasional users, enabling global collaboration, and creating HPC-based business models.

IDC concludes that HPC, simulations, modeling, and data analytics are becoming vital to industrial digital transformation, enabling faster development, supply chain and sustainability optimization, and new digital products, services, and business models. It recommends building virtual product and manufacturing development, creating a holistic data strategy and single source of truth, selecting suitable HPC operating models, prioritizing scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and using external expertise where needed.

The passage studies matching markets under ordinal preferences in three settings: house allocation, marriage, and roommates. It focuses on “popular” matchings, where a matching is at least as popular as any alternative if the total weight of agents who strictly prefer it is at least the total weight of agents who prefer the alternative. Because popular matchings may not exist, the paper introduces the “popular dimension”: the minimum size of a set of matchings that is collectively at least as popular as any single matching.

The paper evaluates the popular dimension for strict or weak preferences, and for unweighted or weighted agents. For house allocation, the popular dimension is exactly 2 in all four cases, and a polynomial-time algorithm is provided to find a popular winning set of size 2. For the marriage problem, the dimension is 1 for unweighted agents with strict preferences, since stable matchings exist and are popular. With weighted agents or ties, the dimension is at least 2 and at most 3. For the roommates problem, the dimension is exactly 2 for unweighted agents with strict preferences; with weights or ties, it is at least 2 and at most 3.

The paper also relates popular dimension to Condorcet dimension, noting that every popular winning set is a Condorcet winning set, so the popular dimension upper bounds imply corresponding Condorcet dimension bounds for these matching problems. The remaining open problem is to close the gap between 2 and 3 for marriage and roommates instances with weights or ties; the authors conjecture that the marriage problem has popular dimension exactly 2 even in the general case.

President Muhammadu Buhari said Nigerians were reporting improved power supply and cited national generation figures, but his hometown, Daura, was experiencing a 10-day blackout after a windstorm destroyed a newly erected power tower and 16 KEDCO poles. KEDCO said repairs were underway and power would be restored within 48 hours. Similar infrastructure-related outages have affected other areas, including parts of Lagos and Ondo states.

This study examines how climate change affects K–12 internally displaced learners in low- and middle-income countries, focusing on educational access, quality, learning environments, well-being, and gender disparities. It uses a framework combining a Human Rights-Based Approach to education with Education in Emergencies research, and is based on a literature review of 73 academic and grey-literature sources.

The findings show that climate change disrupts education through rapid-onset disasters, slow-onset environmental changes, economic hardship, damaged infrastructure, displacement, and health impacts. In learners’ homelands, school access and performance are affected by destroyed schools, damaged transport, reduced household income, food insecurity, child labor, migration, malnutrition, trauma, and temperature and rainfall changes. After displacement, students face additional barriers including school costs, documentation and enrollment requirements, curriculum differences, discrimination, social exclusion, limited representation in school decision-making, and inadequate distance-learning options.

Climate-related displacement also harms learners’ well-being through trauma, disrupted social connections, poor health, food and water scarcity, disease, stress, and developmental impacts. Girls face heightened risks because climate shocks intensify existing gender inequalities, increasing household responsibilities, reducing school attendance, encouraging families to prioritize boys’ education, and raising risks of early marriage or work migration.

The study argues that climate-displaced learners need scalable financial assistance, simplified administrative systems, academic and mental health support, stronger data collection, and gender-sensitive education policies. It identifies research gaps in climate-related displacement within Education in Emergencies, long-term educational outcomes, and proactive policy responses. It frames climate displacement as an educational emergency requiring long-term, rights-based, climate-specific education policies.

The study presents two all-optical thermometry methods using ~1 µm diamonds containing silicon-vacancy (SiV) centers. Temperature is estimated from temperature-dependent SiV photoluminescence and diamond Raman features, including intensity, peak position, and linewidth. The methods use multi-feature regression (MFR) with explicit feature selection and two-stage multi-feature regression (2SMFR) using PLS, Lasso regression, and spline correction.

Experiments measured eight diamonds from 25 °C to 85 °C in 10 °C increments. Models were trained on subsets of diamonds and temperature set points, then tested on unseen diamonds to evaluate generalized accuracy, resolution, and sensitivity. The best MFR model used SiV ZPL wavelength, SiV linewidth, and Raman linewidth, achieving 1.7 K accuracy and 1.2 K·Hz⁻¹/² resolution with limited calibration data, about 26% better accuracy than the best single-feature model. The 2SMFR model required larger calibration sets but achieved the best performance with seven diamonds and seven temperature points: 0.7 K accuracy, 0.6 K·Hz⁻¹/² resolution, and 0.04 K⁻¹ sensitivity. This represented improvements of ~59% over MFR and ~70% over the best single-feature model in accuracy, ~50% in resolution, and about sevenfold in sensitivity.

The results show that multi-feature regression improves optical diamond thermometry while allowing flexible calibration requirements. The authors caution that linear feature-temperature assumptions apply to the studied 25–85 °C range and that extrapolation beyond the training range may be unreliable.

Dabhol Power Company’s board authorised its management, including Neil McGregor and K Wade Cline, to issue a termination notice for its power purchase agreement with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board, after a London meeting where MSEB was barred from voting as an interested party and IDBI opposed the move. The decision followed disputes over unpaid bills, penalties, tariffs, and MSEB’s protest payments, including Rs 134 crore toward the March bill.

International and domestic lenders were divided: some foreign lenders supported termination or halted further disbursements, while Indian lenders led by IDBI urged renegotiation, citing risks to their loans. Maharashtra and central government officials said they preferred renegotiation and an amicable settlement, with Maharashtra planning a committee to renegotiate the deal. Reports said termination could create major liabilities for the Centre, including one year’s power bill and a $300 million termination fee.

In Mock v. Watson, the widow of John Mock sought to have her statutory interest in his real estate admeasured and set apart. The heirs objected, arguing the estate had large debts and no assets other than the land, so the widow’s share should not be assigned until debts were paid. The court held that the widow’s interest in her deceased husband’s real estate is not subject to payment of his debts and may be set apart without regard to them. Her interest attaches when the husband’s seizin and the wife’s coverture concur, and upon his death becomes a vested interest. Code provisions allowing sale of real estate for estate debts apply only to the estate’s interest in the land, not the widow’s share. The order setting apart the widow’s interest was affirmed.

Following the Sept. 11 attacks, U.S. energy companies heightened security, evacuated offices, and suspended or reduced trading, while maintaining normal electricity, gas, refinery, and pipeline operations. Enron, Dynegy, El Paso, Reliant and others sent workers home; NYMEX closed, disrupting linked markets and online platforms. Energy prices rose amid fears of supply disruption and possible Middle East tensions. Enron planned to resume North American gas and power trading by phone and EnronOnline on Sept. 12, saying markets should remain stable. Separate reports noted security reviews for South Asian energy operations and Enron’s ongoing Dabhol project payment dispute in India.

A self-driving Uber vehicle struck and killed pedestrian Elaine Herzberg, 49, in Tempe, Arizona, while in autonomous mode with a human operator behind the wheel. Uber suspended self-driving tests in the Phoenix area, Pittsburgh, San Francisco and Toronto and said it is cooperating with police. The incident may affect autonomous vehicle development and comes amid state-level regulatory activity and public concern.

The passage describes the quarterback as football’s most important offensive position because the quarterback touches the ball on nearly every play, leads the offense, communicates play calls, reads defenses, calls audibles, and helps determine whether the offense succeeds. Quarterbacks must study playbooks, scouting reports, and film, and their main duties include taking snaps, passing, occasionally running, protecting the football, and finding open receivers.

The term “quarterback” comes from early formations in which the player lined up a “quarter back” from the running back. Other names include signal caller, field general, gunslinger, and QB. The position has evolved from favoring tall, strong players to including smaller, more athletic quarterbacks.

Key quarterback skills include football IQ, decision-making, accuracy, leadership, footwork, athleticism, and arm strength. The passage lists Otto Graham, Peyton Manning, Dan Marino, Joe Montana, and Tom Brady among the best quarterbacks ever. It concludes that the quarterback is crucial because he is central to nearly everything an offense does.

HDFC Mutual Fund will wind up HDFC FMP 378D March 2014 (1) after unit holder approval. The scheme’s maturity was extended twice, but after the second rollover its net assets fell below Rs 10 crore, making it unviable to manage. Its corpus is invested in cash and cash equivalents.

Thai Prime Minister Prayuth Chan-ocha said Thailand has no trade or commerce with North Korea and has complied with U.N. resolutions, ahead of a visit by U.S. envoy Joseph Yun to discuss pressure over North Korea’s weapons programs. The U.S. has urged Southeast Asian countries, including Thailand, to cut North Korean funding streams. Thailand previously said trade with North Korea had fallen by up to 94 percent.

Carol Christ, 73, became UC Berkeley’s first female chancellor as the campus faced sexual assault scandals, budget problems, free speech controversies, housing shortages and scrutiny from state lawmakers. A former Berkeley professor, department chair, provost and Smith College president, Christ said she returned because she believed she could help. She plans to prioritize African American student representation, campus sexual assault response, free speech programming, student housing, homelessness concerns, budget cuts and rebuilding campus community. Berkeley must halve a $110 million deficit this year, and Christ has proposed increasing philanthropy and cutting administration. She also wants campuses to play a larger role in Sacramento amid criticism of UC’s financial transparency. Christ said she loves Berkeley and wants to give back.

The Surrogate’s Court affirmed a transfer tax order on the estate of Josephine Slosson, except for one modification. Slosson held a power of appointment over a trust fund created by her father’s will and validly exercised it through her own will by making bequests, directing payment of debts, and leaving the balance to her surviving issue. Because she effectively disposed of the trust fund, her children could not elect to take under their grandfather’s will, whose alternative provision applied only if she failed to exercise the power. The beneficiaries’ interests and debts paid from the trust fund were taxable. However, $682.04 paid to Alice Slosson for claims she had advanced funds to settle was not taxable as her bequest and was deducted.

The UC1825B-SP is a high-frequency PWM controller for switched mode power supplies, supporting current- or voltage-mode operation with input voltage feed-forward. It includes protection features, latched jitter-free logic, undervoltage lockout, and totem-pole outputs for capacitive loads.

Options expiry is when an options contract becomes void and can no longer be exercised. In the US, options expire on the third Saturday of the expiration month, while the last trading day is usually the preceding Friday, or Thursday if Friday is a public holiday. Expiration week is typically the third week of the month, and large-cap stocks with active options often show higher returns, volume, and volatility during this period. Quad witching occurs four times yearly, when stock options, stock index futures, and stock index options expire on the same day.

The passage discusses developing strategies through research, model creation, backtesting over at least 15 years or different market cycles, and forward-testing. It presents stock-based expiry strategy backtests rather than options strategies, citing complexity and data limitations. Backtests include SPY during expiration week with an average 0.3% weekly gain, an XLV strategy averaging about 0.7% per trade, an SPY overnight strategy averaging 0.46%, and an SPY expiry-day short day-trading strategy with 306 trades averaging 0.18% per trade. Expiry days showed slightly higher volatility than normal trading days, especially quad expiration days.

A penalty kick is a one-on-one restart awarded for certain defender fouls inside the penalty area, taken from the penalty mark 12 yards from goal. Law 14 requires the ball to be stationary, the kicker identified, the goalkeeper on the goal line until the kick, and all other players outside the penalty area and arc. The ball must move forward and is in play once kicked.

Effective penalty kick takers need technique, confidence, practice, and a consistent routine. Coaches should teach the rules, identify primary and alternate kickers before matches, and ensure the rest of the team understands positioning and follow-up responsibilities. Kickers should focus only on setting up and scoring, not organizing teammates.

Training should begin with proper equipment, confirmed penalty-mark placement, targets, and experimentation with kick type, run-up, target location, and body position. Common kick types are the inside-of-the-foot kick, instep drive, and instep-face kick. Accuracy is emphasized over full power, with lower corners often recommended because they reduce the risk of shooting over the goal, while upper corners are harder for goalkeepers to stop but easier to miss.

Mental preparation is central. Kickers should practice staying calm, blocking distractions, breathing, visualizing success, and maintaining confidence. They should ignore goalkeeper movements or distractions and avoid changing their planned shot at the last second. Feinting is allowed during the run-up but not after the run-up is completed.

After the kick, players must follow play: the kicker may shoot again if the goalkeeper saves it into the field, but not if it rebounds from the post or crossbar before another player touches it. Regular practice, repetition, fatigue-based drills, scrimmage simulations, goalkeeper feedback, and distraction training help build consistency. At higher levels, kickers may scout goalkeepers, keep records of tendencies, develop multiple kick options, use legal kicker changes, modify approaches, or attempt rare “tap” penalty kicks.

Coaches should select kickers based on demonstrated success and confidence, never as a last-second decision. Players should be allowed to decline if not confident, and teammates should not criticize missed penalties.

Chenai Mathabire, a Zimbabwean nurse and epidemiologist with Doctors Without Borders, received an International AIDS Society prize for research showing that a rapid tuberculosis test can be implemented at health centers in Malawi and Mozambique. Her work focused on HIV-positive patients, who are highly vulnerable to TB, a leading cause of death in the region. Mathabire’s team found that the urine-based test gives results in under an hour, can be administered after a few hours of staff training and is easy for health workers to interpret. Unlike standard cough tests or chest X-rays, which can take days or longer and require follow-up visits many patients cannot afford, the rapid test allows same-day treatment. The findings have led some Doctors Without Borders-supported health centers to adopt rapid TB testing and may encourage broader use. Mathabire continues to work with Doctors Without Borders and is considering further HIV and TB research.

The passage features hockey players discussing a playoff game and season. They say the opponent started strongly, but their team improved, scored late, limited shots despite penalties, and still had time to respond. Google’s Project Fi added three compatible phones: the $199 moto G6, $740 LG G7 ThinQ and $899 LG V35 ThinQ. Horgan rejected the claim, saying a nine-cent overnight increase was due to gouging, profits, and supply issues rather than taxation, and said he had raised the matter with the federal government.

May 23, 2001 news reports focused on the Enron-promoted Dabhol Power Company dispute in Maharashtra. Madhav Godbole resigned as head of the state-appointed renegotiation panel after Sharad Pawar criticized the panel’s “negative approach,” but Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh refused to accept the resignation and asked him to continue. The scheduled renegotiation meeting with DPC was cancelled.

Reports said Maharashtra was considering issuing a preliminary termination notice to DPC after DPC served one on MSEB over unpaid bills. North Tyneside Mayor Norma Redfearn said councils south of the Tyne could join the North of Tyne devolution deal later, though not at the current stage. North Tyneside Council’s cabinet unanimously approved moving forward with the deal, involving Newcastle, Northumberland and North Tyneside. Blackwell can provide up to 50% power savings in small language model inference through shorter active periods, lower-power transitional states, voltage and power gating, and faster entry into deep sleep.

Its new frame generation model is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and runs once per rendered frame. Blackwell also uses enhanced Flip Metering in the display engine for more precise frame pacing.

DLSS 4 replaces CNN-based models with transformer-based models that use self-attention, larger pixel windows, and 2x more parameters, improving temporal stability, lighting detail, motion detail, anti-aliasing, and reducing ghosting and denoising artifacts. Super Resolution constructs higher-resolution frames from lower-resolution inputs, Ray Reconstruction improves ray-traced scenes, and DLAA improves native-resolution image quality.

The dispute has strained party fundraising negotiations and may push lawmakers back into partisan divisions over climate policy. It also reflects a broader tension for California Republicans between working with Democrats to remain relevant and adhering to conservative doctrine.

The passage describes design guidance for a TPS7H500x-SP push-pull converter using GaN FETs. Because GaN FET reverse conduction can produce a large source-drain voltage, dead time was set to about 25 ns, with 20.5-kΩ resistors selected for RPS and RSP. Leading edge blank time was initially set near 50 ns using a 49.9-kΩ RLEB, with possible optimization needed for ringing, PCB parasitics, and gate-driver delay. A 33-nF soft-start capacitor gives an approximately 7.5-ms soft-start time.

Transformer design targets a 35% maximum duty cycle for margin below the 50% controller limit, uses an estimated 0.5-V synchronous rectifier voltage, selects a 2.5 turns ratio, and uses 40 µH primary inductance despite a calculated 33 µH value. Primary GaN FETs should be rated for voltage stress and transients; 170-V devices were selected for a 36-V maximum input. Synchronous rectifier GaN FETs see about 20 V maximum expected stress, but 80-V devices were selected, with optional parallel Schottky diodes to reduce soft-start and dead-time losses.

The design includes guidance for an RCD clamp, a 0.47-µH output inductor targeting 40% ripple current, and output capacitance based on ripple, load transient, and radiation-induced SET considerations. Although calculations required at least 1.3 mF, about 2.3 mF was used. A secondary output filter may reduce ripple, with damping added if peaking occurs. Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins near 35 A using a 7.5-Ω sense resistor and a 1:100 current sense transformer. A 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor is used. Type 2A compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover, with selected values of 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF; slope compensation uses a 102-kΩ resistor.

Power supply recommendations specify a 4-V to 14-V controller input, proper regulation, and at least 0.1 µF VIN bypass capacitance. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing high-current and switching loops, routing sensitive traces away from noisy nodes, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, filtering CS_ILIM if needed, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS with vias. The passage also lists related documentation, update notification, support resources, trademarks, ESD caution, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information disclaimers.

The 2025 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine was awarded to Shimon Sakaguchi, Mary Brunkow and Fred Ramsdell for work on regulatory T cells, which restrain immune responses and help prevent autoimmune disease. Sakaguchi identified T-regs in 1995, while Brunkow and Ramsdell studied a mutation causing fatal autoimmune disease in male mouse pups and reported related mutations in people in 2001.

Defendant Arthur Heine moved to dismiss a bigamy indictment, arguing his second marriage was void because it was performed by a justice of the peace when he was 19. Grand Jury minutes showed his first marriage to Aud Irene Kvamli Heine remained valid when he married Marie Licciardi in 1955, and he admitted both marriages and knowing he committed bigamy.

The court examined section 11 of the Domestic Relations Law, particularly subdivision 5, which limits who may solemnize marriages when either party is under 21. The issue was whether a marriage performed by a justice of the peace in such circumstances is merely prohibited but valid, or void. The court reviewed conflicting lower-court decisions: Caplan and De Martino held such marriages invalid, while Andrews and Graves held the prohibition applied only to the officer and did not invalidate the marriage. The court adopted the reasoning of Caplan and De Martino, held the second marriage invalid, and granted the motion to dismiss the indictment.

The Federal Reserve raised short-term interest rates by a quarter point, its third hike since December, bringing the key rate to 1%–1.25%. Volkswagen’s U.S. unit asked a Virginia judge to delay consumer fraud trials over diesel emissions for at least six months, arguing that comments by owners’ lawyer Michael Melkersen in a Netflix documentary could prejudice jurors. James Madison returned without signature a bill pledging funds for roads, canals, and waterway improvements, arguing that Congress lacks constitutional authority for such internal improvements. NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg said the alliance’s 2017 annual report showed increased deterrence, defense, burden-sharing and cooperation. NATO deployed four multinational battle groups to the Baltic states and Poland, increased its Black Sea presence, strengthened cyber defenses, joined the coalition against ISIS, expanded cooperation with the EU and welcomed Montenegro as its 29th member. Becton, Dickinson and Company has paid dividends since 1962 and has delivered double-digit dividend growth in 12 of the past 13 years, averaging 16.3% growth since 2004. The 2015 CareFusion merger increased share count and temporarily reduced profitability through acquisition, restructuring, and interest costs, but the passage states these costs are declining and margins are improving. The dividend payout ratio fell from 2015 to 2016 and is estimated at 37% for 2017. Risks cited include manufacturing issues, higher interest rates, and competing products. The author concludes Becton’s dividend is safe, with continued growth potential.

The study uses density functional theory to predict and analyze three previously unstudied o-MAX phases, Mo₂A₂AlC₃ (A = Zr, Nb, Ta), focusing on their structural, electronic, mechanical, thermal, and optical properties for potential thermal barrier coating applications. Calculations were performed with CASTEP using GGA-PBE and GGA-PBEsol functionals.

The compounds crystallize in a hexagonal P6₃/mmc structure with 16 atoms per unit cell. Negative formation energies, absence of imaginary phonon modes, and satisfaction of Born mechanical stability criteria confirm their chemical, dynamical, and mechanical stability. Electronic band structures and density of states show metallic behavior, with major contributions from Mo-4d states. Charge density and Mulliken analyses indicate mixed ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding, with strong M–C interactions.

Elastic calculations show that the compounds are mechanically stable, anisotropic, and brittle according to Pugh’s ratio, Poisson’s ratio, and Cauchy pressure. Mo₂Nb₂AlC₃ has the highest stiffness and fracture toughness, while Mo₂Zr₂AlC₃ shows higher damage tolerance. Vickers hardness values fall within the typical MAX-phase range, indicating moderate hardness and machinability.

Thermal analysis shows favorable Debye temperatures, melting temperatures, thermal expansion coefficients, and low minimum thermal conductivities. Mo₂Ta₂AlC₃ has the lowest minimum thermal conductivity, while Mo₂Zr₂AlC₃ has the highest Debye temperature. These properties support the potential of all three phases as thermal barrier coating materials. Optical calculations show high reflectivity, exceeding 44% across infrared, visible, and mid-ultraviolet ranges, suggesting possible use in solar heat-shielding coatings.

Celtic’s win at Ibrox showed their superiority over Rangers, with Brendan Rodgers’s side described as financially and competitively far ahead. Celtic’s Champions League income, strong signings such as Moussa Dembele and Scott Sinclair, and potential transfer funds are presented as an opportunity to strengthen further, compete better in Europe, and move permanently beyond Rangers domestically.

The passage argues that generative AI is fundamentally different from prior educational technologies and raises unresolved ethical and practical questions for online, blended, and in-person learning. It proposes using philosophy to guide AI’s educational use in humanizing and ethical ways.

The authors draw on Günther Anders to emphasize how technologies reshape human life and create a “Promethean discrepancy” between what humans can produce and what they can understand or emotionally grasp. They use Michel Foucault’s concept of “regimes of truth” to analyze AI as a system of power, noting risks from corporate-controlled AI, hallucinations, bias, inconsistent outputs, and unclear decision-making processes. They then use Paulo Freire’s ideas of conscientization and humanizing education to argue that educational technology is ethical only when it supports critical dialogue, agency, and transformation of the world.

The passage also examines Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy, noting that AI can perform tasks across cognitive levels but that this framework alone does not address ethical purposes. Hannah Arendt’s hierarchy of labor, work, and action is used to supplement Bloom by prioritizing education that moves beyond labor and consumption toward meaningful human action in public life.

The authors propose a framework for ethical AI use in education, ranging from consumptive labor to humanizing action. Ethical AI use should help students critically engage with AI, connect learning to their own perspectives, and act meaningfully in the world. Examples include using AI to support community-based political action and individualized research through Socratic dialogue.

The conclusion states that AI will remain part of education, requiring educators to continually rethink pedagogy, assessment, and AI use so that learning promotes human agency, critical reflection, and humanizing action.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K reporting that Jerome Guillen, President of Tesla Heavy Trucking, departed the company as of June 3, 2021. The report was signed on June 7, 2021, by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

Cowen Group shares rose 19% after CEFC China agreed to buy about a 20% stake for $100 million and provide $175 million in debt financing. CEFC will appoint three directors and pay $18 per Class A share, with the deal expected to close by Q3 2017.

Apple benefited from holiday demand for new iPhones, while Samsung was hurt by the Galaxy Note7 recall and brand damage. Gartner’s Anshul Gupta said Samsung could regain the lead with a new flagship phone due in March, while Apple may wait until September for its next iPhones. Samsung still led full-year sales with 20.5% share, ahead of Apple’s 14.4%. Huawei, Oppo, and BBK ranked third to fifth, reflecting Chinese vendors’ growth in China, South Asia, and potentially developed markets.

An 80-year-old patient was treated on the floor at Gujranwala DHQ Hospital due to a bed shortage, prompting family complaints. Separately, PML-N workers in Gujranwala celebrated Yaum-e-Takbeer and praised Nawaz Sharif.

The passage describes a patent disclosure for implementing fundamental computational primitives on a device using a matrix multiplication accelerator (MMA) coupled to a processor. The device includes memory, a processor with streaming engines, and an MMA with multiplier, multiplicand, and result buffers. Control software configures the streaming engines to stream data from memory, configures MMA formatting and operations, and executes primitives through Load, Store, and Execute instructions that can load data, store results, and perform matrix multiplication in a single cycle.

The MMA supports configurable input and output formatting, row offsets for loading data into multiplicand buffers, ping-pong buffering, result buffering, and an optional ReLU nonlinearity. Streaming engines generate ordered data streams from memory using programmable multi-level nested addressing and can support formatting such as zero padding, value copying, known matrix creation, even/odd vector generation, linked operations, seam removal, stride removal, and matrix transpose.

The disclosure explains how the MMA can implement primitives including small and large matrix multiplication, pointwise matrix multiplication, matrix addition, vector-matrix multiplication, vector summation, affine transformation, two-dimensional convolution for convolutional neural networks, row and column permutation, fast Fourier transforms, discrete cosine transforms, one-dimensional convolution and correlation, matrix assignment, and matrix transpose. Many primitives are mapped to matrix multiplication by arranging data in buffers, using identity or permutation matrices, loading repeated or tiled matrices, applying row offsets, and using streaming engine address patterns.

For two-dimensional convolution, feature maps and filters are arranged as matrix multiplication problems using tiled filtering matrices, with different handling for large and small feature map tiles, stride, seam removal, and optional zero padding. FFTs and DCTs are implemented through matrix-vector or matrix-matrix multiplication, with large FFTs using column FFTs, twiddle-factor multiplication, row FFTs, and transpose. Large one-dimensional convolution is performed by decomposing filters into smaller fragments and combining results.

The passage also notes that examples use a DSP and 1×32 or 32×32 MMA buffers, but other processors and buffer sizes may be used.

NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere GA100 architecture, is designed for cloud and data center AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads. It adds Third-Generation Tensor Cores with support for TF32, FP64, BF16, FP16, INT8, INT4, and binary operations, plus fine-grained structured sparsity that can double Tensor Core throughput. Compared with V100, it offers higher performance, 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, and faster cache bandwidth.

A100 introduces Multi-Instance GPU, allowing one GPU to be partitioned into up to seven isolated GPU instances with predictable throughput, latency, QoS, and fault isolation. It supports third-generation NVLink with 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, Magnum IO, and Mellanox interconnect solutions for scalable multi-GPU and multi-node systems. CUDA 11 features include asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, task graph acceleration, and improved programmability. The passage also highlights enhanced error detection, fault containment, and support for NVIDIA DGX, HGX, and EGX systems.

Unidentified gunmen attacked U.N. peacekeeping sites in Timbuktu and Douentza, Mali, killing nine people in total and injuring others. Mission chief Mahamat Saleh Annadif called both incidents terrorist attacks and urged justice. MINUSMA said its forces killed six assailants in Timbuktu and two in Douentza. U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the attacks, warning that targeting peacekeepers may constitute war crimes. The U.N. is investigating whether the attacks were connected.

Arizona ammunition dealer Douglas Haig was charged with manufacturing armor-piercing bullets without a license after unfired rounds found in the Las Vegas shooter’s hotel room contained his fingerprints. Haig said he sold Stephen Paddock 720 rounds of tracer ammunition weeks before the Oct. 1 attack that killed 58 people, but noticed nothing suspicious and denied contributing to the shooting. His name surfaced after a box with his name and address was found in Paddock’s hotel suite. Haig said Paddock claimed he planned to shoot the ammunition in the desert with friends. Haig has closed his ammunition business and said he has received media attention and death threats.

The Treasury Department recommended rolling back parts of Obama-era Wall Street regulations, including Dodd-Frank disclosure rules on CEO-worker pay gaps, easing IPO requirements, expanding crowdfunding limits, and revising derivatives oversight. Supporters said the changes could spur growth, while critics warned they would weaken post-crisis safeguards and increase risks.

The National Institute of Standards and Technology revised its password guidelines, moving away from requirements for special characters, mixed case and regular changes. Paul Grassi of NIST says passwords should be simple, long and memorable, using phrases, lowercase letters and common words. He argues longer passwords are harder to break and easier for users to remember. Password managers remain useful but are not necessary. Grassi says frequent password changes often lead users to make only minor alterations, which attackers anticipate.

The passage argues that LLMs show promise as synthetic agents in social science but should not be treated as Bayesian inference engines or as sources of calibrated population samples. Their outputs reflect pattern matching from training data and prompting rather than posterior beliefs or draws from human distributions. Studies show LLMs can replicate or predict some survey, experimental, and behavioral results, but they also exhibit distortions, subgroup failures, order sensitivity, variance collapse, and non-Bayesian drift such as “introspective hallucination.”

The author emphasizes that LLM success often comes from scale, training data, fine-tuning, and behavioral alignment, not statistical correction or generalizable understanding. Fine-tuned agents may perform well in narrow domains while failing outside them, so a universal “homo silicus” is unlikely. Instead, synthetic agents should be domain-specific, transparently conditioned, and evaluated as high-capacity predictors.

Recommended practices include validating against human data, measuring subgroup calibration and variance, using synthetic data to augment rather than replace human data, anchoring agents in individual- or task-level data, avoiding in-prompt self-conditioning, testing order invariance, stress-testing out-of-domain performance, reporting failures, and fully disclosing prompts, models, parameters, seeds, and aggregation methods. The conclusion is that LLM agents can be valuable for near-term prediction, research design, and difficult-to-study scenarios, but only if their black-box uncertainty and statistical limitations are openly recognized.

The final 2000 “Friday Burrito” reviews recent California electricity market turmoil, including FERC orders, emergency filings, rate stabilization proceedings, subpoenas, credit concerns, and high price spikes. The author argues the industry needs clearer public messaging focused on consumer bill impacts and says WPTF’s message should emphasize adding generation, expanding provider choice, and ensuring a provider of last resort.

The newsletter criticizes Senator Steve Peace’s letter to FERC, discusses SCE CEO John Bryson’s call to re-regulate California’s electric system, and explains credit risks affecting Pacific Northwest power sales into California. It notes the CPUC reopened PG&E and Edison rate stabilization applications after earlier suspension and quotes CPUC President Lynch’s comments on supply, plant availability, market design, and volatility.

Federal issues include Energy Secretary Bill Richardson’s order requiring out-of-state generators and marketers to sell into California and directing BPA and WAPA to send power, with concerns about BPA reserves and salmon impacts. WPTF supported the PX’s emergency FERC filing to remove the ISO’s hard cap on adjustment bids. The newsletter also includes member mail on public relations, details for WPTF’s February meeting in Scottsdale, election-themed humor, and a personal holiday reflection.

The paper examines early childhood education in rural Mewat, Haryana, focusing on 71 Anganwadi Centres in 25 villages of Nuh Block. Using checklists, observations, photographs, and interviews with Anganwadi workers, the study assessed infrastructure, learning environments, health and hygiene, administration, and worker competencies.

Findings showed major gaps: only 23 centres had safe building structures, 14 had leveled floors, three had clean drinking water, functional toilets, safe kitchens, lights, and fans, and none had mats, desks, chairs, or timetables for preschool education. Learning materials and play equipment were largely absent. Many Anganwadi workers lacked required qualifications, had limited knowledge of child development and curriculum domains, and often relied on repetition and memorization rather than activity-based learning. Parent involvement and child progress records were minimal.

The study concludes that early childhood education in rural Anganwadi Centres faces challenges related to infrastructure, resources, trained educators, socioeconomic conditions, cultural and language barriers, parental engagement, and monitoring. It recommends standardized basic infrastructure, provision of learning resources, worker training in child development and pedagogy, stronger parent awareness, and coordinated support from governments, communities, NGOs, and corporate social responsibility initiatives to improve equity in preschool education.

The passage discusses challenges in evaluating advanced AI systems on unforeseen tasks, including data contamination, overfitting, static benchmarks, safety concerns, and complex internal mechanisms. It proposes future LLM benchmarks with dynamic sample generation, configurable difficulty levels, and multi-faceted ability analysis, while noting the need to adapt psychometric principles for AI. It also highlights broader evaluation goals such as cultural respect, ethnic values, and human-defined safety principles. DyVal is presented as an early framework that dynamically generates low-duplicate evaluation samples with controlled uncertainty, varying complexity levels, and guaranteed ground truth using directed acyclic graphs for tasks such as mathematical and logical reasoning.

The passage is an AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 specification update listing unresolved or documented silicon issues. It includes errata involving PIT behavior, GLIU debug features, PIC interrupt handling, DMA priority rotation, thermal alarm recovery, PMC sleep clock configuration, UART access during DMA, LPC software DMA diagnostics, illegal PCI I/O addresses, USB over-voltage protection, LBAR address limits, automatic clock gating effects on PIC interrupts, ATAC and ACC PRD prefetch hazards, UDMA CRC corruption after device termination, and ATAC SSMI behavior during DMA.

Several issues are described as having negligible or no operational impact, especially those limited to debug features, diagnostic modes, illegal software sequences, or unsupported address values. Recommended resolutions include avoiding affected features or sequences, not using the debug port, waiting for DMA completion before UART access, avoiding PCI I/O cycles or LBAR values at 10000h or higher, using external USB over-voltage protection, disabling automatic clock gating in affected PIC use cases, ensuring PRD tables are properly prepared, and using ATAC UDMA I/O blocking to prevent host terminations.
Stack procedures are provided as macro-included native assembly code for host environments to establish or destroy a stack, requiring the host to define the execution environment.

Raja Jackson, son of retired MMA fighter Quinton “Rampage” Jackson, will face felony battery causing serious bodily injury and misdemeanor battery charges over an August assault at a KnokX professional wrestling event in Los Angeles. Jackson allegedly slammed wrestler Stuart Smith, known as Syko Stu, and continued striking him after he appeared unconscious. Smith reported jaw injuries, a serious head injury, a lip laceration and lost teeth. Jackson was arrested in September. His father has condemned his actions. Jackson faces up to four years in state prison, with prosecutors expected to seek a sentencing enhancement.

Micro E-mini Nasdaq 100 futures are electronically traded CME contracts based on the Nasdaq 100 Index and sized at one-tenth of E-mini Nasdaq 100 futures. They are cash-settled, expire quarterly, trade under symbol MNQ, and have a contract value of the index price multiplied by $2. The minimum fluctuation is 0.25 index points, or $0.50 per contract. Trading occurs mainly on CME Globex from Sunday evening to Friday afternoon, with daily maintenance breaks. Strategies may use technical and fundamental analysis, risk management, and position sizing. Prices are affected by component stocks, macroeconomic reports, interest rates, economic conditions, and sociopolitical events. The passage cites an all-time high of 16,676.50 in November 2021 and a low of 6,628.75 in March 2020.

Toll challenged probate proceedings involving title to a Denver property and sought to enjoin foreclosure of a trust deed held by Casey. McKenzie had bought the property with money borrowed from Casey, but his deed was unrecorded. After McKenzie’s death, Casey arranged for a new deed to Mrs. McKenzie, eliminating the minors’ ownership interest from the record. Mrs. McKenzie then sold the property to Toll, who later learned the minors owned an undivided half interest.

Mrs. McKenzie and Casey agreed to perfect Toll’s title through probate and guardianship proceedings at their expense. The court found that, although the original conduct involved constructive fraud and the agreement was not literally followed, the probate court ultimately had all material facts and the proceedings effectively gave Toll merchantable title. The probate judgment was affirmed as modified, with certain costs assigned to Mrs. McKenzie. The foreclosure judgment was also affirmed as modified: Toll was ordered to pay Casey the remaining debt with interest, less Casey’s obligations under the agreement, after which Casey must release the trust deed. Rehearing was denied except for remand to effectuate the modified judgment.

Muhammad Iqbal Khan recounts the life and death of his son, Mashal Khan, describing him as a gifted student who loved learning. Before his killing at Abdul Wali Khan University, Mashal had spoken to a local news channel about university issues, including the absence of a vice chancellor, high fees, and teachers holding multiple posts. On April 13, Iqbal was informed that Mashal had been hurt, then learned he had been murdered after being chased by students and shot. Police later arrested several young men. Iqbal calls for justice, says no one should fear going to school, and notes that public awareness and protests have grown, though no government representative had visited him.

The passage describes hydrogen peroxide as a common household disinfectant with oxidizing properties and lists 13 suggested uses. These include diluting it for bad breath, gradually lightening hair, treating ear infections, cleaning produce, whitening teeth with baking soda, disinfecting toilet bowls, removing caked-on food, sanitizing cutting boards, cleaning children’s toys, soaking feet, treating stains, soaking plant seeds to simulate rainwater, and disinfecting reusable shopping bags.

Orthopaedic surgeon Dr Sushrut Babhulkar and MAFSU veterinary doctors plan to fit a prosthetic limb on Sahebrao, an eight-year-old male tiger at Gorewada Rescue Centre whose front paw was amputated after a 2012 poachers’ trap injury near Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve. Babhulkar, who adopted the tiger, said such procedures have been done for dogs and elephants but not tigers. He plans to procure a silicon prosthesis from Germany’s AO Foundation after first evaluating and treating Sahebrao’s painful neuroma, using clinical tests and portable X-rays to minimize stress.

The 6-quart Instant Pot Ultra, the newest Instant Pot pressure cooker, is on sale for $120 at Amazon and Sur La Table, down from its usual $150. It adds an “Ultra” setting for custom temperature, pressure, and time controls, along with nine presets also found on the DUO Plus. Unlike DUO models, it displays cooking status details and includes a quick release button.

Former Trump aide Sebastian Gorka endorsed John McCann in New Jersey’s 5th district Republican congressional primary, citing McCann’s support for Trump’s “America First” agenda. McCann faces Steve Lonegan, a former Trump critic who backed Ted Cruz in 2016, with the winner challenging Democratic Rep. Josh Gottheimer. McCann praised Gorka’s endorsement.

The passage profiles Indian entrepreneurs behind major startups: Sachin and Binny Bansal of Flipkart, valued at USD 15 billion; Vijay Shekhar Sharma of Paytm, valued at USD 9.4 billion; Kunal Behl and Rohit Bansal of Snapdeal, valued at USD 6.5 billion; Bhavish Aggarwal of Ola, valued at USD 5 billion in 2015; Deepinder Goyal and Pankaj Chaddah of Zomato, valued at USD 1 billion in 2016; Ritesh Aggarwal of OYO Rooms, valued at USD 250 million; and Shashank ND of Practo, valued at USD 650 million. It highlights their app-based, user-friendly services and their role in shaping India’s startup ecosystem.

Leveraged ETF trading is a short-term strategy using ETFs that employ derivatives and debt to amplify daily returns of an underlying index, commonly at 2:1 or 3:1 ratios, or inversely. These products can magnify gains in favorable markets but also magnify losses, making them unsuitable for long-term holding due to costs, daily rebalancing, and volatility decay.

The passage states that the most effective approach is day trading or swing trading, especially for short-term momentum or index speculation. Risk management may include stop-loss orders, diversification across markets and ETFs, and using both directional and inverse leveraged ETFs. Performance and risk can be assessed with metrics such as the Sharpe ratio, Jensen’s alpha, and appraisal ratio.

Leveraged ETF profits are taxed like stock-trading profits, with short-term gains taxed as ordinary income rates and long-term gains taxed at long-term capital gains rates, depending on domicile.

Backtests comparing QQQ and the 2x leveraged QLD showed higher annual returns for QLD but not double the unleveraged results, likely due to time decay. The leveraged strategy also produced much larger drawdowns, including losses over 35% during 2008/09 and over 55% in a less robust RSI strategy. The passage emphasizes that leverage can be psychologically difficult and potentially lethal to trading strategies.

UnitedHealth Group named Duke Health chief data scientist Michael Pencina as its chief AI scientist. At Duke, Pencina advocated greater oversight of health care AI, including a registry tracking AI use and disclosures on training, development, and performance, and co-founded the Coalition for Health AI.

Accern rated media coverage of Celyad SA as somewhat positive, giving it a sentiment score of 0.19 and an impact score of 45.69, suggesting recent coverage is somewhat unlikely to affect the share price soon. Analysts recently issued mixed views: Piper Jaffray reaffirmed a buy rating with a $49 target, BidaskClub lowered it to hold, and ValuEngine raised it to hold. On Friday, Celyad shares fell 5.15% to $60.70, with a $578.19 million market capitalization. Celyad is a Belgium-based drug developer focused on stem cell-based cardiovascular therapies.

Bayern Munich players Robert Lewandowski, Arjen Robben, Arturo Vidal and Joshua Kimmich selected a FIFA 18 Ultimate Team Squad Battle lineup featuring 99-rated versions of themselves, alongside players including Lionel Messi, Ronaldo, Patrick Vieira, Lothar Matthaus, Paolo Maldini, David Alaba and Manuel Neuer.

The passage compiles June 4, 2001 media mentions of Enron. Reports include Karl Rove’s stock holdings in Enron and other major firms while advising President Bush; Saudi Arabia’s $25 billion-plus energy agreements with nine oil companies, including Enron; commentary on California’s energy crisis; and multiple articles on Enron’s disputes in India over the Dabhol Power project. Indian lenders planned to meet in Singapore to support the troubled $2.9 billion project, while foreign lenders considered withdrawal amid conflict with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board over unpaid bills, contract termination, and power costs. Rating agencies cited concerns about India’s reform climate and foreign investment. Other items cover a UK gas-electricity “spark spread” trade between Powergen and Enron, Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo criticizing Enron’s performance on a Lagos power project, and Enron Japan’s comments on Japanese power deregulation.

The TLV322x has an open-drain, sinking-only output that can be pulled up to 0V–5.5V independently of supply voltage, supporting wired-OR logic and level translation. TI recommends 100µA–1mA pull-up current; large resistors increase rise time, and output shorts require current limiting. Unused open-drain outputs may float or connect to V−.

TLV321x/TLV322x devices include ESD protection to V+ and V−; input voltages are limited to 0.2V beyond rails, and input clamp current should be limited to 10mA or less. TLV321x devices include a power-on reset that holds the output low for up to 32µs after crossing 1.65V, after which the output reflects the differential input.

Comparator output depends on VIN versus VREF, with propagation delay affected by overdrive voltage. Slow or noisy threshold crossings can cause chatter; external hysteresis using resistor feedback can reduce sensitivity to noise in inverting or non-inverting configurations. A typical low-side current-sensing application uses an amplifier and comparator to signal when amplifier output exceeds 1.1V.

Design guidance emphasizes local 0.1µF low-ESR bypass capacitors, stable low-noise supplies, careful grounding, minimizing input-output coupling, placing input resistors near the device, and adding small series output resistance or controlled-impedance routing for long traces. The document also provides support resources, ESD handling cautions, revision history, mechanical and packaging information, and TI warranty and liability notices.

Zachary Steele, 21, was arrested in Kanawha County after allegedly assaulting his father, stealing a vehicle, fleeing deputies, and threatening self-harm. He faces domestic battery and fleeing charges.

Injection site reactions and systemic events within 7 days after BNT162b1 or BNT162b2 were generally well tolerated, short-lived, and mostly mild or moderate; injection-site pain was the most common local reaction, while tiredness and headache were the most common systemic events. Phase 2 results were similar to overall Phase 2/3 results. In Phase 1, BNT162b1 and BNT162b2 doses of 10, 20, and 30 µg were well tolerated, but BNT162b1 100 µg was stopped after Dose 1 due to injection site reactions or systemic events; 30 µg BNT162b2 was selected for Phase 2/3. Few participants left Phase 2/3 because of medical problems, and most events were mild or moderate. Serious medical problems were uncommon across Phase 1, Phase 2/3, and booster groups; researchers generally did not consider them related to the study vaccine, though some temporary serious problems in participants aged 16 and older were considered possibly related. No participants died in Phase 1. In Phase 2/3, deaths occurred in BNT162b2 and placebo groups from different causes, and researchers did not believe they were caused by BNT162b2. No participants died in Phase 3 among those receiving BNT162b2SA without prior BNT162b2.

JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon, long critical of Bitcoin, said “blockchain is real” and sees use cases for stablecoins and JPMorgan’s deposit token. He said JPMorgan’s private blockchain addresses permission and rule-setting challenges and could replace some slow systems, but he warned blockchain is limited and “won’t replace everything.” He declined to comment on Bitcoin.

The Ohio Court of Appeals reversed a judgment holding Technology Education Corporation liable for $5,225 to each plaintiff for breach of educational-services contracts. The plaintiffs had contracted with Paraprofessional Institutes of Ohio, whose school assets were later sold to Educational Leadership Corporation and then to TEC after plaintiffs graduated and filed suit. Default judgments were entered against PIO and ELC; TEC appealed its liability as a successor corporation.

The court held that TEC was not liable merely as a successor. The asset purchase terms incorporated into TEC’s assignment expressly excluded liability for claims arising before the purchase, except for listed liabilities that did not include student contracts. TEC also did not impliedly assume liability simply because it may have known of pending litigation, and the parties were free to allocate liabilities by contract. The court further found no evidence that TEC was a mere continuation of ELC, since continuation requires more than carrying on the same business services and there was no evidence of common directors, stockholders, or corporate identity.

The court also noted that even if successor liability applied, plaintiffs still had to prove their contract claims, and the record contained little beyond allegations. TEC’s assignments of error were sustained, and the case was reversed and remanded for further proceedings.

Namibia’s defence ministry said national security and sovereignty remain protected despite budget cuts and soldiers being sent on furlough to save costs. Defence minister Penda ya Ndakolo said temporary measures target savings on utilities and feeding to fund priorities like training and transport. Leave mainly affects older troops nearing retirement and those with social issues, while 70% remain available and others can be recalled.

Pauline Hanson’s One Nation has announced conditional support for the Federal Government’s media ownership reforms, potentially ending a political deadlock opposed by Labor and the Greens. The changes would scrap rules limiting media ownership across TV, newspapers and radio, and preventing one TV broadcaster from reaching more than 75 per cent of the population. One Nation said it secured Government commitments to investigate ABC balance and regional coverage, require more transparency on ABC staff earning over $200,000, and provide an extra $12 million for community radio. The legislation is expected before Parliament this week.

The passage describes patent embodiments for preventing ransomware from encrypting files on a target machine. The approach uses an endpoint agent, such as a lightweight security agent, to monitor file system activity and detect unauthorized actions involving honeypot files or folders. These honeypots may be virtual entries injected into protected directory query results by a mini filter driver, positioned to increase the likelihood that ransomware targets them before real user files.

The endpoint agent monitors events such as file opens, file information changes, writes, deletes, renames, and directory enumeration. When a process accesses or modifies a honeypot file or folder in a dangerous way, the system can deny access, terminate the process, generate alerts, notify users, or log activity based on configured anti-ransomware policies. Protected directories, file types, exceptions, and response actions can be configured through policies and user interfaces.

The described implementation reduces storage overhead by mapping many virtual honeypot entries to a small set of real files, avoids leaving residue files across mounted disks, supports protected directory path patterns, and can hide honeypot files from ordinary users to reduce false positives. The techniques are described for multiple operating system environments and may be implemented as processes, systems, apparatuses, or computer program products.

The Chande Momentum Oscillator (CMO), introduced by Tushar Chande in 1994, is a momentum indicator that ranges from -100 to +100 and compares higher and lower closes over a chosen period. Values above zero suggest strength, below zero suggest weakness, while readings above +50 or below -50 may indicate overbought or oversold conditions depending on trend context. It can also signal potential reversals through divergences and may be paired with a moving average signal line. The CMO is not a trend-identification tool and is best combined with trend indicators such as moving averages or trendlines. Its settings, timeframes, and asset suitability should be determined through backtesting. A Python backtest on SPY using a 9-day CMO and a 5-day maximum holding period reportedly produced strong risk-adjusted returns and lower drawdown than buy-and-hold, though longer holding periods reduced returns.

The Nasdaq Composite hit an all-time high and the Dow headed for its best day in over a month after ADP reported U.S. private employers added 263,000 jobs in March, well above expectations. All 11 S&P 500 sectors rose, led by financials and technology. Investors were also awaiting Federal Reserve minutes and a meeting between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Amazon reached a record high, while Panera Bread surged after JAB Holdings agreed to buy it for $7.16 billion.

Germany, France, Britain, Spain and Italy warned Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin that proposed U.S. tax changes may violate international obligations and distort trade. Their finance ministers objected to measures taxing payments to foreign affiliates, cross-border financial transfers, and provisions they say could advantage U.S. companies, including exporters, as Congress works to reconcile House and Senate tax bills.

Students at Ron Clark Academy in Atlanta went viral after celebrating news they would see “Black Panther.” Teachers Wade King and Susan Barnes tied the film to curriculum, using comics and the movie to teach imperial history, African art, math, science and gym. King said students reacted with excitement and joy.

Research Report Insights predicts the global corrugated packaging market will grow at a 4% CAGR from 2014 to 2020, reaching US$173.6 million. Growth is driven by e-commerce, rising shipments, increasing population and income, and demand from end-user industries including medicine, rubber, food, consumer durables, and petroleum. Corrugated packaging is favored for low cost, easy handling, sustainability, and shipment suitability. Applications include liner board, container board, sheets, and boxes, with flute types A, B, C, E, and F. Market restraints include low durability and slower growth in some end-user industries. Major companies include Nine Dragons Paper, Smurfit Kappa, Georgia-Pacific, Mondi, DS Smith, International Paper, Rock-Tenn, Lee & Man, Oji Holdings, and American Packaging. Key producing regions include Japan, India, China, the U.S., major European countries, Brazil, and Turkey.

This bibliometric study maps research on primary science education, addressing a gap in prior analyses that focused on broader areas such as STEM, scientific literacy, and critical thinking. Using Web of Science data, the authors analyzed 2,295 English-language journal articles published from 1997 to December 31, 2024, with VOSviewer. The study applied bibliographic coupling and co-word analysis to identify intellectual structures, thematic clusters, influential publications, and emerging trends.

The dataset received 31,582 citations excluding self-citations, averaged 13.76 citations per paper, and had an H-index of 77. Publication activity began in 1997, increased notably after 2003, rose sharply from 2006 to 2019, and remained relatively stagnant from 2020 to 2023.

Bibliographic coupling identified five clusters: augmented reality, virtual reality, and ICT integration; equity, engagement, and teacher competence; cognitive and metacognitive supports; dialogic teaching, integration, and teacher beliefs; and artificial intelligence, computer science, and computational thinking. Co-word analysis identified four clusters: dialogic argumentation, discourse, and scientific literacy; teacher beliefs, pedagogical knowledge, and professional development; achievement, engagement, and conceptual change; and computational thinking and technology integration in STEM.

Findings indicate a shift in primary science education research toward inquiry-based, student-centered, digitally supported, and equity-oriented pedagogies. The study highlights remaining gaps, including culturally responsive computational thinking, teacher identity in reform contexts, inclusive digital integration, and broader global representation. The authors propose the DIG-EDU-QUEST framework, emphasizing culturally responsive inquiry, pedagogical practices, technological affordances, and sociocultural equity. Future research should expand beyond Web of Science and English-language publications and include qualitative approaches to examine classroom implementation across diverse settings.

Sterling traded in a tight range on Tuesday, rising 0.2 percent against the dollar and euro ahead of Prime Minister Theresa May’s formal Article 50 notification to start Brexit talks. Analysts said the trigger was largely symbolic for investors, with sterling more dependent on the EU response and UK economic outlook. Strong inflation data and signs the Bank of England may move toward raising rates supported the pound, though uncertainty over Brexit terms continued to weigh on it. Investors remained concerned about a hard Brexit, difficult negotiations, and the possibility of another Scottish independence referendum.

Research on the microbiota has shifted from viewing human-associated microbes as freeloaders to recognizing their roles in digestion, metabolism, immune responses and inflammation. Studies show gut microbiota composition and activity vary across the day, suggesting links between circadian rhythms, modern behaviors such as nighttime eating or light exposure, and health. In mice, gut microbes released molecules that changed daily gene expression in the liver, affected metabolism, and altered responses to acetaminophen toxicity depending on time of day. Antibiotics and changed feeding times also disrupted these patterns. Advances in DNA technology have enabled microbiome research, showing microbial communities function as interconnected systems. These findings may be relevant to people taking long-term antibiotics or shift workers eating at unusual times, potentially affecting metabolism and risks such as obesity and metabolic syndrome.

Under GST, e-way bills are required for transporting goods consignments valued above Rs50,000 to curb tax evasion, but the GST Council approved exemptions for 153 items. Exempt goods include LPG for households, PDS kerosene, currency, jewellery, postal baggage, used personal effects, animals, fruits, vegetables, milk, cereals, khadi, earthen lamps, puja items, hearing aids, condoms and contraceptives. E-way bills are also not needed for non-motorised transport or certain port-to-port movements. The system will start after government notification once NIC software is ready, likely by October. Bills will include transport, origin, destination, supplier, recipient and transporter details.

The passage introduces multi-organ imaging genetics as a growing area for studying aging and disease, strengthened by large multi-omics datasets, open GWAS resources, and computational genomics methods. It describes prior work deriving 2024 multi-organ AI endophenotypes from UK Biobank data and making their GWAS summary statistics public. The study uses public UKBB, FinnGen, and PGC GWAS resources, including 525 disease endpoints, to examine the genetic architecture of these endophenotypes and benchmark statistical methods in multi-organ analyses.

Center for Diagnostic Imaging Miami offers diagnostic medical imaging and preventive screening services using advanced technologies under board-certified radiologists, physicians and technicians. Services include X-ray, PET scan, PET CT, CTA, MRI, ultrasound, open MRI, 3D mammogram and nuclear medicine. Its Total Body Scan includes CT scans of the head, neck, chest, abdomen and pelvis, cardiac calcium scoring, and a physician consultation within 24–48 hours. The scan screens for conditions including cancer, diabetes, heart disease, vascular abnormalities, thyroid disease and organ abnormalities. CDI Miami also provides breast, ovarian and prostate cancer screenings and nuclear medicine tests such as thallium stress, bone and thyroid scans.

Police managed crowds while negotiators dealt with a distressed man on the Cambridge Mill roof. He spent hours near a chimney, discarded items, became agitated, explored possible escape routes, then walked toward negotiators and surrendered. He was taken to Cambridge Memorial Hospital for a mental health assessment, with charges pending. Restaurant staff later assessed damage, possible theft, and how he entered.

Energy Central Professional Dispatch for Jan. 30, 2002 lists electric power and gas industry news, with extensive coverage of Enron’s collapse, investigations, market impact, and related political scrutiny. The passage describes SD Memory Card physical-layer requirements for UHS-II, ROM, UHS-I, UHS-II/UHS-III, initialization, data transfer, erase, write protection, lock/unlock, and selected commands. UHS-II cards add interface contacts, require unused SD interface lines not be driven by the card and be held at defined host levels, and support modes including FD156, optional HD312, FD312, and FD624. UHS-I supports DS, HS, SDR104, and DDR50 modes, uses 1.8V signaling for higher speeds, requires voltage switching through ACMD41/CMD11, and uses CMD6 for driver strength, bus speed, and power/current limits.

ROM cards are read-only, treat write/erase-related commands as unsupported, may optionally support CMD42 and security commands, and full-size ROM cards do not have a write-protect switch. Application Performance Class defines minimum random and sequential performance, while cache, self-maintenance, command queue, and low-voltage interface features are introduced with references to later sections.

The host controls all communication using broadcast or addressed commands. Card identification mode uses CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, and CMD3 to reset, verify voltage, initialize, identify cards, and assign RCA. Data transfer mode uses CMD7 to select one card, CMD9 to read CSD, optional CMD4 for driver stages, and addressed commands for reads, writes, erase, and status. CMD19 provides tuning blocks in 1.8V transfer state when allowed.

Read and write operations are block-oriented, use CRC, and can be stopped with CMD12. Multiple-block writes are preferred for speed, ACMD23 may pre-erase blocks, and ACMD22 reports successfully written blocks. Erase uses CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38; DISCARD and FULE are CMD38 variants for SDHC/SDXC cards and are not supported through SPI.

The passage defines mechanical, internal, and password-based write protection. CMD42 manages card lock/unlock, password setting, clearing, force erase, and Card Ownership Protection. COP adds Force Erase Password handling, COP Unlock, FEP Force Erase, and restrictions when FEP is set. Locked cards accept only specified basic, initialization, status, and lock-related commands; other commands are treated as illegal. CMD55 marks the following command as application-specific, and CMD6 switches card functions including access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit.

After Hawaii ratified the reciprocity treaty, the King sought a commercial treaty with Japan, opposed by the U.S. minister at Honolulu. In 2015, MaryAnn Camacho became Executive Director of Quest Diagnostics’ National Customer Service organization, overseeing call centers in Lenexa, Kansas, Tampa, Florida, and remote representatives. Quest had consolidated 20 regional customer service centers into two in 2013, but the transition caused major operational problems: high labor costs, 60% first-year representative turnover, long phone wait times, inconsistent answers, poor first-call resolution, and customer losses.

Quest, the largest U.S. diagnostic-testing company by 2014 revenue, had grown through acquisitions that left labs and systems operating autonomously. Under CEO Steve Rusckowski, the company pursued operational excellence through standardization, productivity, and improved service. Executive Jim Davis identified turnover as a major obstacle, costing Quest $7,000–$10,000 per departing employee and weakening customer service.

The National Customer Service centers handled about 55,000 calls daily, mostly requests for test results. Representatives needed technical knowledge, but training was inconsistent, systems varied by region, and understaffing often prevented hands-on coaching. Supervisors spent much of their time handling escalations, absenteeism, staffing gaps, and unclear policies.

Before Camacho arrived, leaders identified four urgent priorities: step-based pay, career paths, supervisor development, and workforce planning. Camacho began by observing operations and speaking with frontline employees, while considering whether to focus first on operations, staffing, representative issues, or several problems at once.

Food scientist Paul Dawson tested double-dipping after watching a “Seinfeld” episode. His experiments found that double-dipped chips transferred far more bacteria than single-dipped chips, including 1,000 more bacteria per milliliter in water. Single-dipped dips showed no bacteria, while double-dipped salsa had more bacteria than chocolate syrup or cheese dip, likely due to its lower viscosity. After two hours, salsa’s bacteria count decreased, possibly because of acidity. Double-dipping can spread mouth bacteria and diseases.

The Money Flow Index (MFI) is a momentum indicator that combines price and volume to measure money flow into and out of a security over a set period. It ranges from 0 to 100 and is used to identify overbought, oversold, and divergence signals that may indicate reversals. Common thresholds are 80 for overbought and 20 for oversold, though settings vary by market and strategy. The default lookback period is 14 days, but shorter periods produced better stock backtest results in the passage. A strategy using MFI signals with bullish or bearish engulfing patterns performed well on PEP and SPY, with returns above buy-and-hold while invested less than half the time, but performed poorly on gold. The passage concludes that MFI can be useful when properly applied and backtested.

The Nanocrystal Glass Market Report analyzes current and future market challenges, production costs, policies, news, manufacturing processes, capacity, R&D status, raw material and technology sources.
