The passage describes patent embodiments for automated recognition of objects in video or image content. A media device or server receives visual content, selects frames according to a frame selection rate, partitions frames into image blocks, and uses machine-learning algorithms to identify regions likely to contain objects. Likelihood metrics, influenced by factors such as frame selection rate and recognition error, determine whether an object is accurately recognized. The system may refine recognition iteratively, adjust frame selection and partitioning, use product, merchant, audio, and feedback data, and update parameters based on recognition performance.

Recognized products may be displayed to viewers with related information such as name, price, brand, availability, merchants, recommendations, and advertisements. Products can populate a digital shopping cart or list, support purchasing directly or through merchant links, and be personalized using viewer data such as purchase history, browsing history, social media data, and preferences. The system includes components such as media devices, content, product and merchant databases, media servers, recognition engines, frame selection, partition, analysis, accuracy, display, communication, data, and shopping cart modules.

This study conducted a descriptive bibliometric content analysis of 273 full-text studies on modern physics education in Turkey published between 2000 and 2023. Data were collected from databases including Tübitak Ulakbim, YOK National Thesis Centre, ERIC, Scopus, Science Direct, Google Scholar, SpringerLink, Taylor & Francis, DOAJ, Sobiad, and TEI, using the Modern Physics Education Publication Classification Form.

Most studies were articles, written in Turkish, and published in Tübitak Ulakbim. Research activity was concentrated between 2010 and 2020, peaking in 2019, and declined in recent years. The most frequently studied topics were atoms, the photoelectric effect, the theory of relativity, nuclear energy, the Compton effect, and the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.

The studies most often aimed to examine instructional method and technique effectiveness, identify current situations, and assess cognitive or affective characteristics. Quantitative designs, especially quasi-experimental and descriptive survey models, were common, while qualitative case studies were also frequently used. Purposive sampling was widely preferred, though many studies did not report sampling methods. Samples most often consisted of education faculty undergraduates, high school students, and middle school students, typically with 31–100 participants.

Intervention durations were often unreported; when reported, they commonly ranged from 0 to 4 weeks. Interviews, tests, questionnaires, and scales were the most used data collection tools. Frequency, percentage, t-tests, item analysis, content analysis, and descriptive analysis were common analysis methods. Validity and reliability information was often limited, although expert review, detailed process descriptions, inter-coder consistency, and direct quotations were used in some studies.

Findings from the reviewed studies showed both positive and negative outcomes in modern physics education. Positive outcomes included increased academic achievement, concretization of knowledge, improved problem-solving skills, higher-order thinking, and positive attitudes. Negative outcomes included persistent misconceptions, reliance on classical physics thinking, difficulties with mathematical operations, and negative perceptions. The authors recommend using more diverse analytical methods, larger samples, richer methods and interventions, improved validity and reliability reporting, updated curricula, stronger links to modern physics philosophy, and more comprehensive future research.

The passage presents a first-principles study of higher-order atomic magnetic multipoles in altermagnets using group theory and density functional theory. It shows that MnF₂ and CrSb host real-space multipoles beyond dipoles, including octupoles and dotriacontapoles, constrained by magnetic site symmetries and visible in spin-density components. In MnF₂, in-phase octupolar and 32-polar components support d-wave altermagnetism, while in CrSb the lowest uncompensated collinear multipole is a 32-pole, consistent with g-wave altermagnetism.

The study emphasizes noncollinear spin density, which is symmetry-allowed even in collinear magnets but vanishes without spin-orbit coupling. With finite spin-orbit coupling, noncollinear octupoles and 32-poles appear linearly, while collinear multipoles change only weakly and quadratically. In KMnF₃, fluorine octahedral rotations break anti-translation symmetry and tune the system from antiferromagnetism to altermagnetism, inducing an in-phase 32-pole proportional to the rotation angle. The passage also connects these multipoles to macroscopic response tensors such as piezomagnetism and second-order magnetoelectric effects.

The study examines research hotspots and trends in the relationship between open education and vocational education in China and other countries from 2012 to 2023 using CiteSpace 6.2.R2 visual analysis. Open education and vocational education are presented as key parts of lifelong learning and learning society construction, supported in China by national policies promoting vocational education, flexible learning, resource sharing, and recognition of learning outcomes.

The study used 515 valid Chinese documents from CNKI and 329 foreign documents from Web of Science. It analyzed keyword networks, research hotspot timelines, and keywords with strong citation bursts.

In China, major research hotspots included open education, vocational education, higher vocational education, open universities, distance education, integrated development, collaborative integration, adult vocational education, practical teaching, and information technology. Integrated development showed particular importance. Timeline analysis found that before 2016, research mainly addressed the separate development of open and vocational education, while after 2016 it increasingly focused on their coordination and integration, including teaching models, curriculum systems, and online education. Since 2018, keywords such as integration and development, integrated development, and coordinated development showed strong citation bursts.

In other countries, research focused more on adult education, vocational training, online learning, vocational education and training, adult learning, higher education employees, and lifelong learning, with fewer studies directly addressing open education. Since 2013, attention increased on adult vocational education and vocational skills, and since 2018 research on online learning for vocational education learners grew. From 2020 to 2023, strong citation bursts included online learning, vocational education and training, adult learning, blended learning, young adults, technology, and personality.

The study concludes that Chinese research emphasizes integration between open and vocational education, while research in other countries focuses mainly on adult skills development and online learning.

The 1-3-1 zone is a versatile defense suited to matching up, overplaying passing lanes, and trapping. The passage outlines basic ball-location shifts, wing, baseline, point, and middle defender responsibilities, adjustments for skip passes and penetration, the “Three in a Line” variation, corner and top trapping actions, trap fundamentals, and extensions into quarter-court, half-court, and full-court pressure.

The passage describes a patent application for a system and method for multiple-factor verification of computer-vision-based interactions, especially in retail environments such as checkout-free or expedited checkout shopping. The invention uses two or more complementary monitoring systems—such as computer vision, RFID or RF tags, smart shelves or scales, user applications, smart carts, POS systems, profile prediction systems, and security tag barriers—to independently evaluate user activity or selected items. A verification system compares the outputs to determine monitoring alignment, identify discrepancies, assess confidence, update checkout lists, and trigger actions.

In retail use cases, the system may generate or validate a customer’s virtual cart, enable or block automatic checkout, direct manual inspection, alert workers, update customer profiles, recommend operational changes, train monitoring systems, or trigger security responses. The approach is intended to improve checkout reliability, reduce adversarial attacks, support user coaching, mitigate shoplifting, and allow lower-accuracy monitoring systems to operate more robustly through complementary verification. This study assessed cardiovascular disease risk among HIV/AIDS patients receiving antiretroviral therapy at the University Teaching Hospital of Butare (CHUB), focusing on lipid profiles and their association with ART regimens. It defined lipid-related markers including total cholesterol, HDL-C, LDL-C, and triglycerides, and described ART as a combination of drugs used to suppress HIV viral replication.

The study used a cross-sectional design from January to February 2021. Blood samples were collected and analyzed in the CHUB clinical chemistry laboratory using spectrophotometry. A total of 150 HIV/AIDS patients on ART were included, along with 49 HIV-negative controls. Among ART participants, 51 were male and 99 were female, with ages ranging from 29 to 75 years and a mean age of 49.4 years. Most participants, 108 (72%), were on first-line ART, 39 (26%) on second-line ART, and 3 (2%) on third-line ART.

Among ART participants, 48 (32%) had hypertriglyceridemia, 12 (8%) had high LDL-C, 29 (19.3%) had low HDL-C/high-risk HDL levels, and 23 (15.3%) had high total cholesterol. Compared with controls, ART participants had significantly higher abnormal lipid profile findings for triglycerides, LDL-C, HDL-C, and total cholesterol, with reported p-values below 0.05.

The study concluded that HIV/AIDS patients receiving ART at CHUB showed significant lipid profile changes associated with cardiovascular disease risk, particularly among those on first-line medication. It recommended adding lipid profile testing to routine biological assessments for people living with HIV and suggested further studies in other health institutions, including additional cardiovascular tests such as troponin, creatine kinase-MB, CRP, and electrolytes.

Embodiments describe a screen display method, apparatus, electronic device, storage medium, and program product for managing multiple application interfaces. When an electronic device displays multiple interfaces, such as a full-screen interface with one or more floating windows or two side-by-side interfaces, an operation on one interface may automatically minimize another interface and display it as a floating ball, application icon, contact avatar, or video pop-up window. If an edit box gains focus, other interfaces may be minimized to facilitate input; when focus is lost, they may be restored. A minimized interface may be displayed away from the cursor. Operations on a floating window may make it full screen while minimizing other interfaces. The disclosure also describes supporting hardware and software structures of an electronic device implementing these functions.

Missouri legislation approved by the House and Senate would allow K-12 public school students to take free online courses as early as next summer if signed by Gov. Eric Greitens. This cross-sectional study evaluated urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) in patients with urinary tract infections (UTIs) and its association with kidney damage. Conducted at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bangalore, it recruited 80 adults with confirmed UTIs and suspected proteinuria; after exclusions for low creatinine or absent proteinuria, 46 participants were analyzed. Participants were categorized by proteinuria stage: Stage I <15 mg/mM creatinine, Stage II 15–50 mg/mM, and Stage III >50 mg/mM.

Among the 46 participants, 67% were female and the mean age was 38.11 ± 7.3 years. Twelve participants had normal/mild proteinuria, 16 had moderate proteinuria, and 18 had severe proteinuria. Urinary creatinine excretion was significantly reduced across all stages compared with the reference interval, while urinary microprotein was significantly elevated in Stage III. The P/C ratio increased across stages, with Stage III showing the highest mean value. The study concluded that proteinuria is significantly associated with UTIs and that the P/C ratio is a reliable urinary marker for assessing UTI-associated renal impairment and disease progression.

Options trading in TSLA involves buying or selling derivatives that give the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell TSLA shares at a set price by a set date. It can generate profits, manage risk, leverage capital, hedge portfolios, and speculate on price movements, but it is complex and carries risks, including large or total losses.

Common strategies include long calls, long puts, covered calls, and spreads. Strategy selection depends on risk tolerance, investment goals, and market outlook. Potential returns depend on the option’s strike price, the underlying asset’s price at expiration, and price direction.

The passage emphasizes understanding risks, using quantified analysis and backtesting, monitoring performance through a clear plan, and applying risk management such as stop losses and taking profits when appropriate. It warns against overtrading, trading without understanding risks and returns, and relying on discretionary judgments. Fees vary by broker and may include commissions, platform, regulatory, and margin fees. Tax implications depend on trades and country, and consulting a tax professional is advised.

The passage describes container patterns and distributed system architectures. For sharded services, request-routing logic can be placed either inside the sharded service with a stateless load balancer or in a client-side ambassador that presents a single localhost backend while routing requests to shards. Examples include sharded Redis and memcached on Kubernetes using StatefulSets, Services, ConfigMaps, and twemproxy. Ambassadors can also support service brokering across environments and request splitting for experiments, such as using nginx to send 90% of traffic to production and 10% to an experimental service while preserving user consistency with IP hashing.

The adapter pattern modifies an application container’s interface to match expected operational conventions without changing the application itself. It is useful for monitoring, logging, and health checks. Examples include adding a Prometheus Redis exporter, using fluentd to normalize logs or collect Redis SLOWLOG and Apache Storm data, and adding a MySQL health-check adapter that runs diagnostic queries and exposes an HTTP health interface. The pattern promotes modularity, reuse, separation of concerns, and independent resource allocation.

The passage then introduces microservices as multi-node systems composed of separate components communicating through defined APIs, contrasted with monolithic systems. Microservices can improve reliability, agility, team independence, API stability, and independent scaling, but make debugging, design, and coordination more difficult. Distributed patterns help address these challenges.

Replicated load-balanced services use identical replicas behind a load balancer to provide redundancy, scalability, and high availability. Stateless services should include readiness probes so traffic is routed only to initialized instances. Kubernetes examples deploy a NodeJS dictionary service with Deployments and Services. Session-tracked services route a user’s requests to the same replica, often using IP hashing or cookies, and consistent hashing reduces remapping during scaling. Application-layer replicated services can add caching with Varnish, rate limiting, denial-of-service defense, and SSL termination with nginx.

Sharded services split state so each shard serves only part of the request space, with a root or router directing requests. Sharding is useful when data is too large for one machine. Sharded caches improve memory utilization compared with replicated caches but can reduce performance or capacity when shards fail or are upgraded. Replicated sharded caches add resilience and support scaling hot shards. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform, often using a hash and modulo, but key selection is crucial. Consistent hashing reduces remapping during resharding. Examples include HTTP sharding with nginx and hot sharding where heavily loaded shards are replicated.

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing across multiple leaf nodes. A root sends work to leaves, receives partial results, and combines them. It can reduce latency for independent computations such as document search. In replicated scatter/gather, homogeneous leaves share computation; in sharded scatter/gather, each leaf processes the request against its own data shard and the root merges results. Excessive parallelism can be limited by per-request overhead and the straggler problem, where the slowest leaf determines total latency. Replicating each shard improves reliability, upgrade safety, and scale.

The passage also discusses function-as-a-service and event-driven processing. FaaS simplifies deployment from source code, automatically scales and restarts functions, and encourages stateless, modular design. Its challenges include strong decoupling, difficulty understanding dependencies, operational complexity, monitoring needs, limited support for long-running background processing, problems with large in-memory datasets, and cost concerns for sustained high request volume.

United Airlines reported Q1 2017 earnings above analyst estimates and maintained Q2 guidance despite a recent passenger removal scandal. The company guided for up to 3% PRASM growth and pre-tax margins of 10% to 12%, despite higher costs. The article says cost trends are improving, the stock trades at about 8.7 times forward EPS, and United has $4.4 billion in operating loss carryforwards. The author is long UAL and views further scandal-related dips as a buying opportunity.

Ernesto Guevara, youngest son of Che Guevara, runs La Poderosa Tours, a Cuba motorbike tour company using Harley-Davidsons. A former lawyer, he operates the business with his wife and leads six- or nine-day tours priced around US$3,000 to US$6,000. The tours attract international riders, including more Americans, and are named after the motorcycle Che rode through South America.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on September 7, 2016, its Board elected Daniel P. Huttenlocher as a director and appointed him to the Leadership Development and Compensation Committee. Huttenlocher has been Dean and Vice Provost of Cornell Tech at Cornell University since 2012, has worked at Cornell since 1988, and has served as a Corning Incorporated director since February 2015. He received a restricted stock unit award for 1,131 Amazon shares vesting over three years and entered into the company’s standard director indemnification agreement.

Hajdu’s department prepared speaking points and media lines on Canada Summer Jobs eligibility changes between 2017 and 2018. Documents referenced prior funding to the Canadian Centre for Bio-Ethical Reform, a new declaration tied to human rights, and guidance defining sexual and reproductive rights as including access to safe and legal abortions. Officials said religious organizations were not ineligible or treated differently and that applicants’ beliefs were not assessed. Religious groups later met Hajdu and expressed disappointment that wording they found problematic would not be changed. In April 2018, Hajdu announced funded jobs, noting applications were on par with 2017 and hundreds of faith-based groups received funding.

The author explains his objections to a bill funding repairs, preservation, and completion of public works, focusing on the constitutional limits of federal authority over internal improvements. He argues that the Constitution grants no general power to Congress to establish a broad system of roads, canals, railroads, river improvements, harbors, or similar works. Such authority, if implied, would greatly expand federal power, spending, patronage, and influence beyond the enumerated powers reserved to the federal government.

He maintains that internal improvements may be constitutional only when necessary and incidental to specific federal powers, such as defense, the navy, armies, commerce, post roads, or management of federal property. He reviews earlier federal practice on lighthouses, beacons, buoys, piers, and navigation aids, noting long-standing acceptance of some works to make navigation safe, but distinguishing these from broader river and harbor improvements. He also discusses federal jurisdiction over navigable waters and the difficulty of defining the boundary between national and local authority.

The author concludes that Congress should exercise great caution in appropriations for rivers and harbors, limit federal spending to works necessary for clearly granted powers, require cession of land and jurisdiction for permanent public works, consider each project in a separate bill, and leave other improvements to private enterprise or the states, including through tonnage duties approved by Congress.

Justice Hyeladzira Ajiya Nganjiwa failed to secure a stay of proceedings in his trial over alleged corrupt enrichment and false information to EFCC officials. He was arraigned on a 14-count charge involving alleged $260,000 fraud and N8.6 million enrichment, pleaded not guilty, and was granted bail. His lawyer sought a stay pending appeal, citing constitutional grounds.

The disclosure describes autonomous vehicle systems and methods using a machine-learned yield model. The model receives feature data about perceived objects and the surrounding environment and outputs yield decisions, such as whether to yield to vehicles, traffic signals, gaps in traffic, or intersections to avoid gridlock. The autonomous vehicle may use sensors, map data, perception, prediction, and motion planning systems to identify objects, predict future locations, evaluate gaps, and generate motion plans that execute the yield behavior.

Feature data may include object location, speed, acceleration, heading, class, required deceleration or acceleration, traffic signal timing, stop line and exit locations, and gap information for predicted traffic openings. A yield controller may use the model to select a traffic gap or decide to stop, while an optimization planner generates trajectories using cost functions and penalties. The model may also support intersection decisions that prevent blocking or gridlock.

The machine-learned yield model may include decision tree-based models, random forests, neural networks, or other models. It can be trained using labeled driving logs from autonomous or human-operated vehicles, simulated scenarios, human labels, or automatic scoring functions. The disclosure states that this approach can reduce reliance on hand-crafted rules and improve scalability, adaptability, memory efficiency, and autonomous vehicle motion control.

Researchers found that grape-derived compounds may help treat depression by targeting inflammation and synaptic changes linked to the disorder. The Nature Communications study reported that a grape polyphenol preparation promoted resilience against stress-induced depression in mice. Two compounds, dihydrocaffeic acid and malvidin-3′-O-glucoside, were found to affect inflammation and synaptic plasticity, respectively. Researchers said combined treatment may help address depression mechanisms not targeted by current antidepressants.

The Henry James Review will move to Creighton University next year, with Greg Zacharias as editor. The journal, published by Johns Hopkins University Press, supports Creighton’s Center for Henry James Studies and will offer student learning and research opportunities. Founded in 1979 at Louisiana State University, it later moved to the University of Louisville before its transfer to Creighton.

Japan’s Financial Services Agency conducted surprise checks at Coincheck after hackers stole $530 million in digital currency, saying it had previously asked the exchange to fix security flaws. The inspection focused on customer compensation, finances, system management and consumer protection. Coincheck stored coins in a less secure “hot wallet” and lacked a multi-signature security system. The FSA ordered all Japanese cryptocurrency exchanges to report on system risk management and is investigating security gaps across the sector. Coincheck has promised to repay about 46.3 billion yen, though regulators have not confirmed it has sufficient funds. Police and authorities in several countries are investigating the NEM cryptocurrency heist. The theft has renewed scrutiny of Japan’s cryptocurrency regulation and broader concerns about risks in digital asset trading.

U.S. District Judge Barbara Lynn questioned the validity of some federal charges against Dallas County Commissioner John Wiley Price, indicating she was “99 percent sure” she would dismiss mail fraud counts even if the jury found him guilty. Prosecutors allege political consultant Kathy Nealy used car payments and cash to bribe Price on behalf of clients, but defense attorneys argued the payments were not part of any bribery conspiracy. Dismissal of mail fraud charges would significantly reduce Price’s potential sentence. Lynn also questioned whether prosecutors proved a quid pro quo between Price and Nealy, noting Price sometimes voted against Nealy’s clients. Closing arguments were set to begin Tuesday.

A rain delay for Mariners-Tigers ALDS Game 3 changed the broadcast from FS1 to MLB Network and FS2, with streaming still on the Fox One app and Fubo. The series is tied 1-1. Logan Gilbert starts for Seattle against Jack Flaherty for Detroit, which has Kerry Carpenter batting leadoff.

The passage compiles May 20, 2001 energy-related news mentioning Enron. Reports cover President Bush’s energy plan, which emphasizes increased natural gas use, transmission modernization, possible nuclear expansion, and investment in energy infrastructure amid projected electricity demand growth. A Washington Post article says turning the plan into legislation will spur conflicts among utilities, regions, environmental groups, cooperatives, and companies such as Enron and Southern Co. over deregulation, emissions rules, transmission control, and utility consolidation.

Texas articles report low residential participation in a pilot program ahead of electricity deregulation, though commercial interest is stronger. Officials cite consumer confusion, California’s power crisis, and an upcoming mandated rate cut as reasons for slow sign-ups. Enron-linked NewPower is among companies competing for customers.

Qatar’s energy minister says talks are progressing on gas exports to Kuwait and Bahrain, OPEC is unlikely to change output in June, and Qatar has not received confirmation that Enron will leave the Dolphin gas project.

In India, Enron-sponsored Dabhol Power Company served a preliminary termination notice to the Maharashtra State Electricity Board over its power purchase agreement. Reports say India’s central government may distance itself from the project, while Maharashtra leaders discussed options and called the notice improper.
Foothills Audubon Club’s first 2017 program is Jan. 9 at Berthoud Community Center, featuring PLANET EARTH: Saving Species on global conservation. Free, public, all ages welcome.

Former NFL quarterback and Fox Sports broadcaster Mark Sanchez was arrested in Indianapolis after an incident in which he was stabbed and hospitalized. Police said he faces possible misdemeanor charges of battery with injury, unlawful entry of a motor vehicle and public intoxication, with prosecutors to decide final charges. Sanchez is stable but will not work Sunday’s Colts game broadcast.

Devon and Cornwall Police has been charged under the Health and Safety Act over the 2012 death of Thomas Orchard, a 32-year-old church caretaker with paranoid schizophrenia who died in hospital seven days after being arrested in Exeter. During detention, he was restrained, handcuffed and had an Emergency Response Belt placed across his face before being left in a cell, where he was later found unresponsive. A pathologist found he died from severe hypoxic-ischemic brain damage after a prolonged cardio-respiratory arrest following a struggle and restraint.

The CPS said the force is charged with exposing Mr Orchard, a custody detainee, to a risk to his health or safety. The IOPC referred evidence concerning the force’s corporate decision-making on use of the belt. Three police staff were acquitted of gross negligence manslaughter in 2017, and misconduct hearings have been announced for six officers and staff. Mr Orchard’s family welcomed the prosecution and called for changes in police treatment of people with mental health vulnerabilities. The force will appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on May 24.

Recent studies suggest that children’s time outdoors has a protective effect against developing myopia, or nearsightedness, while near work such as reading, computer use, television and smartphone use is not considered an important factor. Myopia begins often in elementary school, occurs when the eye grows too long for distant light to focus on the retina, and usually requires lifelong refractive correction. It is increasing worldwide and can lead to serious eye diseases later in life. Genetic risk is important: children with two myopic parents have about a 60 percent chance of needing glasses if outdoor time is low, but about 14 hours per week outdoors can reduce that risk to about 20 percent. However, time outdoors has little to no effect on prescription changes in children who are already nearsighted. Theories for the protective effect include exercise, vitamin D, and especially brighter outdoor light stimulating retinal dopamine, which may slow abnormal eye growth. Children should still use sunscreen and sunglasses outdoors.

At a White House ceremony, the speaker thanks members of Congress, administration officials, disability advocates, organizations, and Americans with disabilities for helping make the Americans with Disabilities Act law. He describes the ADA as a landmark civil rights act and the world’s first comprehensive declaration of equality for people with disabilities, intended to advance independence, freedom, and inclusion.

The act prohibits covered employers from discriminating against qualified individuals with disabilities, ensures access to public accommodations, expands transportation access, and provides equivalent telephone services for people with speech or hearing impediments. The speaker says the law addresses segregation and discrimination, removes barriers, and benefits both people with disabilities and the nation. He also reassures businesses that the act was designed with flexibility and cost concerns in mind, while encouraging them to employ people with disabilities. The speech concludes by framing the ADA as ending a “wall of exclusion” and rejecting discrimination in America.

The paper investigates how early-stage startups develop Internet-of-Things systems from a software engineering perspective. It focuses on startups because traditional product development methods may not fit their limited resources, uncertainty, and changing requirements.

Using a multiple-case exploratory study, the authors examined eight IoT startups through twelve semi-structured interviews with CEOs, CTOs, and hardware developers, supplemented by public information and some internal documents. The startups worked on products including fish farm monitoring, connected cameras, underwater drones, shipment tracking, muscle measurement, smart home systems, and smart wheelchairs. The analysis used thematic analysis and the SEMAT Essence framework, focusing on team, system, work, and way of working.

The study found that IoT startups often lack all required competencies internally and depend on external consultants, component providers, service providers, and manufacturers. Their systems may start from either the application layer or perception layer and may be Internet-centric, thing-centric, or both. The authors identified three types of MVPs: looks-like MVPs that simulate the product experience, functional works-like MVPs that demonstrate core functions, and quality works-like MVPs that focus on quality attributes and integration.

Common development practices included in-house design, outsourced implementation and manufacturing, rapid prototyping, reuse of ready-made components, and iterative or Agile-inspired development. Startups prioritized speed, experimentation, and fast time-to-market, but hardware development introduced longer cycles, integration challenges, dependencies, and higher costs than software-only development. The paper concludes that IoT startup development resembles software startup MVP development in its iterative and opportunistic nature, but requires methodological adjustments for hardware-related constraints and dependencies.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 18, 2018, reporting under Regulation FD that its 2017 Letter to Shareholders, accompanying the Annual Report for the year ended December 31, 2017, is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Senior Vice President David A. Zapolsky.

The lecture introduces link-cut trees for maintaining dynamic forests of rooted unordered trees with edge insertions, deletions, and queries in logarithmic amortized time. Supported operations include make tree, link, cut, find root, and path aggregation such as min, max, or sum along a root-to-node path. The data structure represents unbalanced “represented trees” using auxiliary splay trees built from preferred paths, keyed by node depth, with path-parent pointers connecting auxiliary trees.

A central helper operation, access(v), makes the root-to-v path preferred and makes v the root of its auxiliary tree structure. This simplifies find root, path aggregation, link, and cut operations. The analysis first gives an O(log² n) amortized bound using preferred-child changes and heavy-light decomposition, then improves it to O(log n) amortized using the splay tree access lemma and a potential function based on subtree sizes in the tree of auxiliary trees. A worst-case logarithmic version exists using heavy-light decomposition directly, but with more complex operations.

Cpl. Marcus Hirschfield was seriously injured on Feb. 14, 2013, when a pickup hit his cruiser near Spruce Grove in icy conditions. He was trapped for 90 minutes, airlifted by STARS Air Ambulance, spent three months in hospital and continues physiotherapy. Now back with the RCMP, he shared his story to stress STARS’ importance. STARS receives one-third of its funding from the Alberta government, with the rest from donations and its lottery, which in 2017 risked not selling out for the first time in 23 years.
The passage lists multiple views of a centrifugal pump embodiment and notes that broken lines indicate unclaimed portions.

CompareCards says many issuers offer long 0% intro APR credit card deals, often 12 to 21 months, which may benefit consumers carrying balances or planning large purchases. The page lists partner cards with cash back, travel rewards, sign-up bonuses, balance transfer offers, no annual fee options, and variable APRs after promotional periods. It explains that low- or zero-interest cards can reduce borrowing costs, especially for those with good credit, but rates may change after intro periods and can be fixed or variable. CompareCards states compensation does not influence its ratings or reviews and that its editors use a data-driven ranking system.

Lawrence Timmons returned from suspension and immediately played every snap for the Dolphins against the Saints. He said he was not at his best but felt good and expects to improve, having stayed in shape during his week away by running, lifting and doing football-related workouts.

Postpartum bleeding occurs after both vaginal and C-section deliveries and is a natural part of recovery. Dr. Adrienne Zertuche explains it comes from the placental site in the uterus, which continues to bleed lightly and shed tissue called lochia as it returns to its pre-pregnancy state. After a C-section, bleeding may resemble a heavy period for several days and may include small clots, but it should become lighter each day and usually resolves within four weeks. A doctor should be contacted if bleeding lasts longer than six to eight weeks, soaks a pad every hour for two hours, includes large clots, or is accompanied by symptoms such as racing heart, shortness of breath, dizziness, lightheadedness, or fever. Recovery guidance includes limiting activity, avoiding heavy lifting, staying hydrated, eating well, and avoiding tampons, douching, baths, pools, hot tubs, exercise, sex, and repeated stair use.

An investigation found around a third of Scotland’s roads need repair, with 30% of A-roads and 35% of B-roads classed as requiring inspection or work between 2015 and 2017. This compared with much lower figures in England, though data is collected differently. Scotland spent more per head on local and national roads than the UK average. Areas with the highest proportions needing repairs included Argyll and Bute and Eilean Siar. Experts cited Scotland’s colder, wetter weather as a factor. Politicians blamed reduced council maintenance budgets, while the Scottish Government said it was committed to major road investment and had increased trunk road maintenance funding.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K with the SEC on April 30, 2019, reporting that it issued a press release about its financial results for the second fiscal quarter ended March 30, 2019. The press release is included as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K dated September 19, 2019, reporting that directors Charles H. Noski and Helmut Panke, both serving since 2003, will retire from the Microsoft Board of Directors and not seek re-election at the December 4, 2019 annual shareholders meeting. Their retirements will be effective on that date.

Research published by the American Psychological Association found that people may be happier when they experience the emotions they desire, even when those emotions are unpleasant, such as anger or hatred. The cross-cultural study surveyed 2,324 university students in the United States, Brazil, China, Germany, Ghana, Israel, Poland and Singapore. Participants reported desired and actual emotions, life satisfaction and depressive symptoms. Across cultures, those who experienced more of the emotions they wanted reported greater life satisfaction and fewer depressive symptoms, regardless of whether the emotions were pleasant or unpleasant. Most participants wanted more pleasant and fewer unpleasant emotions, but some wanted fewer transcendent emotions like love and empathy or more unpleasant emotions. Lead researcher Maya Tamir said further research is needed to determine whether desired emotions influence happiness or are only associated with it.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting results of its November 30, 2016 annual shareholders meeting. Of 7,779,736,996 eligible shares, 6,894,716,318 were voted. Shareholders re-elected all 11 director nominees, approved advisory executive compensation, ratified Deloitte & Touche LLP as fiscal 2017 independent auditor, approved an amendment to the Articles of Incorporation, and approved the French Sub Plan under the 2001 Stock Plan. A shareholder proposal to amend the proxy access bylaw was rejected. The filing included Microsoft’s amended and restated Articles of Incorporation as Exhibit 3.1.

The CCI (Commodity Channel Index) is a momentum oscillator that measures a security’s current price relative to its average price over a period, helping identify overbought and oversold conditions. Originally created by Donald R. Lambert in 1980 for commodities, it is now used on stocks, ETFs, and other markets. The indicator oscillates around zero, with readings above +100 generally considered overbought and below -100 oversold, though thresholds vary by asset.

The passage explains the CCI formula, notes that trading software usually calculates it, and says the indicator can also show bullish or bearish divergences. It states that CCI works best on stocks and partially bonds, especially for mean-reversion strategies, and that daily bars with short lookback periods, such as 5 to 9 days, work well. Its advantages include quantifying overbought and oversold conditions; its limitations include lagging price, weak trend detection, and poor timing precision.

Backtests on SPY found that a 9-day CCI with a buy threshold of -90 and selling when the close exceeds the prior high produced a profit factor of about 1.8, an average gain of 0.55% per trade, and a 23% maximum drawdown. The passage concludes that the best CCI strategy uses oversold levels with short lookback periods in the stock market, though it suggests other indicators may perform better.

The Second Circuit reversed a preliminary injunction issued by the District of Vermont in favor of Jackson Dairy, Inc., exclusive distributor of H. P. Hood’s “Schedule 3B” products in parts of Vermont and New Hampshire. Jackson alleged Hood breached their distributorship agreement by supplying Grand Union and Finast warehouses outside Jackson’s territory, enabling those chains to transship products to stores within the exclusive territory and bypass Jackson.

The court held Jackson had not shown irreparable harm, a required element for preliminary injunctive relief. Any loss from Grand Union, Finast, or other customers could be compensated by money damages if Hood breached the contract. Jackson’s claim that delivery routes might become unprofitable and customer relationships disrupted was also viewed as compensable in damages. The court therefore vacated the injunction without reaching Hood’s other arguments or deciding whether permanent injunctive relief might be available after trial.

Judge Mansfield concurred, agreeing reversal was proper but preferring to base it on Jackson’s failure to show likely success or serious merits questions. He stated the contract did not require Hood to police customers outside Jackson’s territory or prevent their transshipments, and the record did not show Hood controlled or encouraged the chains’ actions.

Apple Inc.’s 2016 Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended September 24, 2016. Apple, a California corporation established in 1977 and headquartered in Cupertino, designs, manufactures and markets mobile communication and media devices, personal computers, portable digital music players, and related software, services, accessories, networking solutions, and third-party digital content and applications. Its products and services include iPhone, iPad, Mac, iPod, Apple Watch, Apple TV, iOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, iCloud, Apple Pay, AppleCare, Apple Music, and various app and content stores.

Apple’s strategy focuses on integrating hardware, software and services, expanding digital content and application platforms, supporting third-party developers, investing in retail and online stores, and continuing R&D, marketing and advertising. The company manages operations by geographic segments: Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific. In 2016, direct and indirect distribution channels accounted for 25% and 75% of total net sales, respectively, and domestic and international net sales accounted for 35% and 65%.

The filing describes Apple’s competitive markets as highly competitive, with rapid technological change, frequent product introductions, aggressive pricing, and pressure on gross margins. It notes supply risks from single or limited-source components, reliance on outsourcing partners primarily in Asia, and potential effects from shortages, pricing fluctuations, or manufacturing disruptions. R&D expense was $10.0 billion in 2016, $8.1 billion in 2015, and $6.0 billion in 2014. Apple had approximately 116,000 full-time equivalent employees as of September 24, 2016.

Risk factors include global and regional economic conditions, competition, product transitions, reliance on distributors and carriers, inventory and purchase commitment risks, component supply constraints, outsourcing risks, product quality issues, access to third-party content and software, intellectual property matters, legal proceedings, regulatory compliance, international operations, retail store risks, acquisitions, IT system failures, data security and privacy, dependence on key personnel, business interruptions, quarterly fluctuations, stock price volatility, currency risk, investment and credit risk, and tax matters.

As of September 24, 2016, Apple owned 7.1 million square feet and leased 22.3 million square feet of building space, primarily in the U.S., and owned 2,583 acres of land primarily in the U.S. The company stated that legal proceedings and claims in the ordinary course of business were not expected by management to result in a material loss, though outcomes remain uncertain. Apple’s common stock trades on NASDAQ under AAPL; it paid $12.0 billion in dividends in 2016 and had used $133 billion of its $175 billion share repurchase authorization by September 24, 2016.

Personal trainer Liz Letchford says eccentric exercises—slow, controlled movements where muscles stay contracted while lengthening—can cause soreness but help build strength. Examples include slowly lowering from a pull-up, releasing a bicep curl slowly, or doing a slow “negative” push-up. She says stronger muscles increase the body’s energy needs and metabolism, helping fuel muscles rather than store energy as fat. Letchford also says “long, lean muscles” and easy bulking are myths; muscle growth depends on training demand, and a lean look comes from strength training and a healthy diet rather than hypertrophy-focused training.

CompareCards highlights credit cards with 0% introductory APR offers ranging from 12 to 21 months, aimed at consumers carrying balances or planning large purchases. She urged chairman-elect Wu Den-yih to take office soon, make appointments and complete the transition, citing urgent party asset-related issues and lawsuits. Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 31, 2019, reporting the announcement of its fourth quarter 2018 and year ended December 31, 2018 financial results. The filing incorporates Exhibit 99.1, the related press release, and Exhibit 99.2, information on non-GAAP financial measures. The report was signed by CFO Brian T. Olsavsky.

Pneumococcal disease causes substantial global morbidity and mortality, especially among young children, older adults, and susceptible populations. Streptococcus pneumoniae colonizes the upper respiratory tract and can cause invasive and noninvasive diseases. At least 100 serotypes exist, with vaccine-covered serotypes causing most invasive disease; in China, six serotypes are commonly implicated. China has PCV13 for young children and PPV23 for high-risk people aged 2 years and older, but neither is in the national immunization program, and uptake remains low. Sinovac developed a preservative-free PPV23 approved in China in 2020. Pre- and post-marketing data indicated acceptable safety. A phase 4 trial was conducted to compare Sinovac PPV23 with Pneumovax® in children, adults, and older adults in China, assessing immunogenicity, tolerability, and safety.

IDC says HPCaaS can support scalable HPC-based business models, such as offering algorithms, simulations, or insights as services. Among respondents already using HPC, 81% intend to implement HPC-based business models. HPCaaS can reduce upfront investment, support outsourcing, and provide access to modern hardware and methods, though trained IT and HPC professionals remain necessary.

IDC views simulations, modeling, and data analytics as key enablers for manufacturing enterprises facing disruption, helping improve product development, supply chains, sustainability, and digital products and services. HPC is described as increasingly necessary for modern simulations and complex performance requirements, with public cloud and HPCaaS offering agility, scalability, or alternatives to in-house infrastructure.

IDC recommends that enterprises develop virtual product and manufacturing processes, create holistic data strategies and a single source of truth, evaluate suitable HPC operating models, consider scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and use external expertise where needed. The findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 decision makers from industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

The speaker says the team is focused on tonight’s playoff game after a very tough previous one, emphasizing skating, competing, managing the puck, and preparing properly. He discusses connections from McGill and says the opposing leader’s reputation is earned through long-term competitiveness, leadership, and franchise success rather than mystique.

The message transmits to the Senate a treaty with Nicaragua for ratification, providing for construction of an interoceanic canal through Nicaraguan territory. It argues that such a canal is necessary for U.S. political, commercial, and defense interests because maritime travel between the Atlantic and Pacific coasts is slow and difficult, while rail transit is insufficient.

The treaty recognizes Nicaraguan sovereignty, disclaims U.S. territorial acquisition or political control, and provides for joint cooperation: Nicaragua supplies the territory and the United States supplies funding. The canal would be open for peaceful use by all nations on equal terms, with certain toll privileges reserved for the coasting trade of the two countries. It also allows construction of related railway and telegraph lines and includes protections for Nicaragua and the canal.

The passage emphasizes expected benefits: closer ties between U.S. coasts, cheaper transportation, reduced dependence on rail corporations, expanded trade with Pacific South America and Asia, restoration of U.S. maritime commerce, and major time savings for sailing vessels. It describes the Nicaragua route’s physical features, including Lake Nicaragua, required locks, canal excavation distances, and advantages over the Panama route for travel from New York to San Francisco.

The author states that although financial return is secondary to national benefit, the canal is expected to be remunerative and economically prudent. The treaty also includes a $4 million loan to Nicaragua for internal improvements supporting canal business. The message urges congressional approval, prompt legislation after ratification, recognition of citizens who aided preliminary work, and suggests the canal could be built most effectively by the Army Engineer Corps.

Inflation is a gradual decline in purchasing power caused by broad price increases. The passage identifies major causes as money supply growth, excess demand, rising production costs, and expectations of future inflation. It states that high inflation tends to make stocks more volatile and harms stocks in the short term, partly because consumers spend less, companies face higher costs, and central banks may raise interest rates. Value stocks may perform better than growth stocks, while dividend stocks can become less attractive if dividends fail to keep pace with inflation. The passage says inflation can benefit borrowers and asset owners, and lists diversified index funds, stocks, bonds, commodities, gold, real estate, REITs, and TIPS as possible inflation-related investments. A backtest on the S&P 500 is described as showing poor historical performance during high inflation.

The speaker says the team has played consistently despite being “under the radar.” Mike Commodore and Cory Stillman are described as well-liked, experienced additions and major contributors, with Commodore anchoring the defense and Stillman producing offensively. The coach expresses pride in being U.S.-born and credits his parents, family, and several coaches as influences. Lackawanna County Prison counselor Kimberly A. Rupp, 49, was charged with misdemeanor retail theft after police said she failed to pay for $206.77 in merchandise at a Dickson City Walmart self-checkout. She had been arrested Nov. 7 for allegedly trying to steal $3,194 in merchandise from Kohl’s, a felony charge. Rupp, a nearly 24-year county jail employee, was released on $10,000 unsecured bail.

Sentencing arguments for the Lake Louise ski resort, which pleaded guilty to charges under the Species At Risk Act and Canada National Parks Act after employees cut down endangered whitebark pine in Banff National Park, have been delayed until July. Judge Heather Lamoureux expressed frustration with the delay, citing court scheduling and clerk shortages. The Crown alleges at least 39 endangered trees were felled. Sentencing will consider the number of trees cut and environmental impact, with expert evidence expected. Bibliotherapy uses books to help readers address problems and has educational and clinical applications. Developmental bibliotherapy supports student growth, while therapeutic bibliotherapy targets mental health concerns. This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence on bibliotherapy practices and outcomes in educational settings.

Following PRISMA-P and PICO principles, the review searched ERIC, Elsevier, ResearchGate, Google Scholar, and article references for peer-reviewed English-language studies from 2006 to 2021. Thirty-five quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies were included; a meta-analysis was not conducted due to methodological variation.

Findings showed varied awareness and use of bibliotherapy among practitioners, with consistent concerns about limited training, time, resources, book selection, and student reluctance or boredom. Reported benefits included improvements in socio-emotional outcomes, such as reduced aggression and social anxiety, increased appropriate social behaviors, and improved emotional awareness. Academic benefits included gains in reading comprehension, vocabulary, articulation, writing, and English language and mathematics outcomes. Studies also reported improvements in self-esteem, hope, and resilience, as well as reductions in anxiety, depression, and, in some cases, stress. One study suggested bibliotherapy could help students discuss traumatic experiences.

The review concluded that bibliotherapy may support socio-emotional, academic, and psychological outcomes in education, but noted limitations including small samples, limited institutional scope, inconsistent methodological detail, and variation across geographic contexts.

The passage presents VN-HGCN, a virtual node-based heterogeneous graph convolutional network for learning node embeddings without predefined meta-paths. Existing heterogeneous graph neural networks often rely on expert-defined meta-paths, struggle with missing key semantic paths, or require many stacked layers to capture long-range information, which can cause over-smoothing and increased computational complexity.

VN-HGCN adds type-level virtual nodes for each node type and a central virtual node connecting them, shortening the distance between any node pair to a path of length 4. Type-level virtual nodes are initialized using the mean features of connected nodes, while the central node uses an all-ones vector. The model then applies transformation, node-level aggregation, and type-level attention-based aggregation to update node embeddings. Its time complexity is stated as linear in the number of layers, node types, nodes, and edges.

The authors also describe virtual nodes as a general framework that can be integrated into other heterogeneous graph models such as HGT, HetSANN, SimpleHGN, and ie-HGCN. Experiments on ACM, DBLP, and IMDB node classification tasks compare VN-HGCN with several baselines, including HAN, MAGNN, HGT, HetSANN, SimpleHGN, ie-HGCN, and ie-HGCN with virtual nodes. Results show VN-HGCN achieves the best performance in most training settings, particularly on ACM and DBLP. Parameter sensitivity analysis on IMDB indicates robustness across hidden dimensions, layer numbers, and numbers of virtual nodes, with performance improving up to 4 layers before declining. The paper concludes that virtual nodes improve long-range information aggregation and model performance while reducing reliance on meta-paths.

The passage introduces SimulRAG, a simulator-based retrieval-augmented generation framework for long-form scientific question answering. It addresses limitations of existing RAG methods, including difficulty connecting textual questions with numerical simulator inputs and outputs, and insufficient fine-grained control when updating long-form answers.

SimulRAG uses a simulator retrieval interface that prompts an LLM with a question and simulator handbook to extract parameter settings, runs the simulator, and converts outputs into textual context. Its generator decomposes long-form answers into atomic claims, verifies and updates selected claims using simulation outputs, and integrates high-confidence claims into a final response. To improve efficiency, it combines uncertainty estimation with simulator boundary assessment (UE+SBA), selecting claims that are both uncertain and compatible with the simulator.

The authors construct a benchmark for long-form scientific QA in climate modeling and epidemiology, using simulator-generated evidence and human verification. Experiments with GPT-4o and Claude-3.5 compare SimulRAG against adapted input-layer and output-layer RAG baselines. Results show SimulRAG improves informativeness by 30.4% and factuality by 16.3% over the best baseline. UE+SBA consistently outperforms random selection, verbalized uncertainty, and uncertainty-only methods across F1, AUPR, and AUROC metrics. Ablation studies show that selective claim verification can approach all-RAG performance while reducing computational overhead. The passage notes a limitation: SimulRAG assumes questions are related to available simulators.

Cardiac surgery commonly causes postoperative hyperglycemia, which is associated with infections, acute kidney injury, arrhythmias, longer hospital stay, and mortality. Existing insulin protocols often fail to account for rapidly changing postoperative conditions and individual variability, increasing risks of both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia.

The study developed GLUCOSE, a distributional offline reinforcement learning model designed to recommend personalized hourly regular insulin dosing during the first day after cardiac surgery. The model was trained and internally tested using MIMIC-IV data and externally validated using eICU-CRD data. The study included 6,148 patients in the development dataset and 649 in the external validation dataset.

GLUCOSE showed higher estimated performance returns than clinician dosing in both internal testing and external validation. Time in glucose range was highest when clinician-administered insulin doses matched GLUCOSE recommendations, and decreased as dosing differences increased. Feature importance analysis showed that current glucose, recent glucose values, weight, mechanical ventilation, and acuity-related features were important to the model.

Human evaluations compared GLUCOSE with recommendations from endocrinologists, cardiac intensivists, and nurse practitioners. GLUCOSE’s insulin dosing more closely matched endocrinologist recommendations than observed clinician dosing and performed comparably to or better than human policies in blinded ratings of safety, effectiveness, and acceptability.

The authors note limitations including the retrospective design, validation only during the first postoperative day, lack of dietary data, and exclusions related to ambiguous medication records. They conclude that GLUCOSE was externally validated and showed clinical robustness, with future randomized controlled trials needed to assess effectiveness and safety in diverse settings.

The passage describes a simple “Chase” offense for attacking a Box & One defense by countering pass denial and freeing the star player. Successful execution requires players to use on-ball and off-ball screens, double screens, offensive rebounding, post-ups, timing, communication, and defensive recognition. Implementation should include breakdown drills, shell drills, scrimmaging, scouting opponents, teaching expected defensive reads and counters, adjusting during games, varying alignments and entries, and attacking weaker defenders. The lecture explains taint tracking using TaintDroid, a system for detecting sensitive data exfiltration on Android phones. Android apps may access sensitive information such as contacts, phone numbers, email, GPS location, IMEI, and sensor data, then send it over the network. Traditional Android permissions are insufficient because they control access to devices or resources, not how specific data flows after access is granted. Blocking all apps that both read sensitive data and use the network would break legitimate apps and would not stop side channels or app collusion.

TaintDroid tracks sensitive data from information sources, such as GPS, accelerometers, contacts, IMEI, and other phone-linked data, and checks whether tainted data reaches a sink, primarily the network. It represents taint with a 32-bit bitvector, allowing up to 32 taint sources. Taint propagates through Dalvik VM instructions: assignments copy taint from source to destination, binary operations combine taints using a union, and arrays, IPC messages, and files use single conservative taint tags that overestimate taint to avoid leaks.

Native methods are difficult because they execute outside the Dalvik interpreter, often in C or C++. TaintDroid handles them through manual analysis of known native methods and automated policies for some signatures. Java state requiring taint includes local variables, method arguments, instance fields, static fields, and arrays. Taint tags are stored near associated variables to improve cache behavior. At network interfaces, TaintDroid checks outgoing data and can block, alert, or modify tainted transmissions depending on policy.

The paper’s evaluation found Android apps attempting to send user data such as location and phone numbers to remote servers without clearly exposing this behavior to users. TaintDroid has moderate overhead, reported as about 3% to 5% extra RAM and roughly 3% to 29% CPU overhead.

The lecture also discusses limitations. TaintDroid does not handle implicit flows, where sensitive data affects control flow rather than being directly assigned. PC tainting can address some implicit flows but may be overly conservative. Lower-level taint tracking at x86 or ARM instruction level can cover more code, including native code, but is expensive, complex, and prone to false positives or taint explosion. Scanning network output for sensitive-looking data is only a heuristic and can be evaded.

The lecture briefly contrasts TaintDroid with systems that let programmers define richer labels and policies, enabling some static checking of information-flow bugs. It also describes TightLip, which tracks possible leaks in legacy programs by running a doppelganger process on scrubbed sensitive files and comparing system calls with the original process. This can work without modifying applications but depends on correct file-type scrubbers.

Dietitian Samantha Rigoli says fruit is healthy, nutrient-dense, and valuable despite trends warning against it for carbs and natural sugars. She advises considering glycemic index for weight loss but emphasizes food quality over calories and recommends eating fruit every day.

The Patient Charter, based on the NHS Constitution, sets out patients’ legal rights, NHS pledges, and patient responsibilities. It affirms care free at the point of use, with exceptions, equal access, treatment based on need, waiting time standards, and alternatives when standards are not met. It includes rights to safe, clean, regulated care from qualified staff, nutritious hospital food, and continual improvement in care quality.

Patients have access to NICE-recommended treatments when clinically appropriate, fair local decisions on other treatments, and routine vaccinations. They also have rights to accept or refuse treatment, give valid consent, receive clear information, and have personal information kept private. The Charter supports patient choice, involvement in treatment decisions, openness when things go wrong, and formal complaints processes, including escalation, judicial review, and compensation for negligence.

Patients are responsible for looking after their health where possible, respecting staff and other patients, following treatment plans or discussing difficulties, attending appointments, and participating in vaccination and screening. The Charter presents the NHS as a partnership based on rights, fairness, trust, and shared responsibility.

This case-control study examined epidemiological data and risk factors for long COVID among healthcare workers in Brazil. It included adults at Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein with RT-PCR-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 from March 1, 2020, to July 15, 2022, followed for 180 days by the Employee Health Clinic. Long COVID cases were defined as symptoms developing during or after confirmed infection, lasting more than four weeks, and not explained by another diagnosis; controls recovered within four weeks. Symptoms included general, respiratory, cardiac, neurological, digestive, joint, and muscle symptoms. The study occurred in a setting where symptomatic healthcare workers had access to free RT-PCR testing and several COVID-19 vaccines were available.

California’s recreational cannabis market rollout has been hampered by complex regulations, slow licensing, local bans, high taxes, and continued black-market activity. Experts estimated that 85 to 90 percent of the prior industry remained unlicensed, with licensing bottlenecks largely at the municipal level and 85 percent of cities and counties banning recreational retailers. Limited legal access, product availability issues, and taxes that may reach nearly 80 percent for some dispensaries were cited as incentives for consumers to use illegal alternatives. Some experts noted Colorado also initially missed revenue projections before later exceeding them.

On Nov. 22, 2001, multiple reports described Enron’s deepening financial crisis. Enron shares fell to $5.01, down 28% for the day and about 94% for the year, despite lenders extending a $690 million debt payment to mid-December and providing access to a $1 billion credit line. Analysts and rating agencies warned that a credit downgrade, loss of lender support, or collapse of Dynegy’s planned $8.9 billion acquisition could push Enron toward bankruptcy. Dynegy said it was encouraged by Enron’s financing steps but continued due diligence, while some reports said Dynegy officials were weighing whether to renegotiate the merger.

The New York Times reported that Enron employees’ 401(k) retirement savings were badly damaged because the plan was heavily invested in Enron stock and was frozen during part of the stock’s collapse due to an administrative change. Employees at Portland General Electric reported large losses, and a lawsuit filed in federal court accused Enron of breaching fiduciary duties by promoting company stock as a retirement investment while allegedly knowing it was overvalued.

Other reports said Enron was reviewing or seeking to sell assets and operations, including its Japan subsidiary, its Wessex Water unit in the U.K., and its stake in India’s Dabhol Power project. Japanese market participants expressed concern about Enron yen-denominated bonds held by investors and money market funds. Bloomberg reported that major financial institutions had held Enron partnership bonds, which had fallen sharply amid concerns over Enron’s off-balance-sheet partnerships, debt obligations, and the uncertainty of the Dynegy deal.

Broader market reports noted that U.S. stocks declined before the Thanksgiving holiday as investors took profits and reacted to weak technology news, while Enron remained one of the most actively traded and closely watched stocks.

A 10-year-old Government Primary School student at PGI alleged youths in a black car tried to abduct her near a Vekra Booth. Police lodged a precautionary DDR, though locals reported seeing nothing. The incident followed another alleged kidnapping attempt days earlier.

The Cahokia Creek Watershed Planning project aims to address storm water, flooding and water quality issues in two Cahokia Creek watersheds in western Madison County, including areas around Glen Carbon and Edwardsville. Soccer coaches should prepare players for varied field, weather, equipment, referee, perimeter, lighting, ball, and marking conditions, and should inspect fields before matches to identify hazards or determine whether play is unsafe.

Field surfaces affect play: artificial turf speeds the ball and can become hot; crowned, sloped, wet, hard, soft, tall-grass, or uneven fields change ball movement and footing. Standing water, ice, protruding sprinkler heads, split seams, unsecured goals, dangerous rocks, pitching mounds, and major obstructions may make a field unplayable. Players should adjust passes, shots, movement, cleats, and goalkeeper technique to surface conditions.

Field size also requires tactical adjustment. Long or wide fields require more weight on passes and greater fitness; short or narrow fields favor earlier, lighter passes and shorter combination play.

Weather can cancel or alter matches. Severe storms, lightning, extreme heat, cold, rain, snow, wind, dew, fog, frost, and humidity require safety precautions, appropriate clothing, hydration, tactical adjustments, or abandonment of play. Lightning requires immediate evacuation and at least a 30-minute delay after thunder.

Referees and assistant referees can affect play through rebounds, interpretations, and offside decisions. Players should remain disciplined, adapt, and play to the whistle.

Perimeter hazards include boards, fences, drainage ditches, tracks, sidewalks, spectators, crowd noise, thrown objects, and overhanging branches. Players should be aware of surroundings and avoid unsafe contact.

Lighting conditions such as sun, glare, shadows, floodlights, and darkness can affect visibility. Games should not proceed if goals are not visible from the center mark.

Equipment issues include combination goals, missing or unsafe corner flags, absent or damaged nets, unstable goals, and different goal-frame shapes. Balls should be legal, consistent, properly inflated, and replaced if defective, waterlogged, wrong-sized, or unsafe.

Players should understand field markings and adapt when lines are missing, unclear, multiple, wavy, or non-parallel. Coaches should know local rules, maintain pre-game inspection routines, use practice conditions for instruction, ensure proper clothing and hydration, and treat practice safety concerns like match safety concerns.

This study compared REM sleep microstructure in 20 patients with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD), 20 patients with Parkinson’s disease and RBD (PD+RBD), and 20 controls using polysomnography. Patients with iRBD had a higher phasic REM sleep ratio and higher REM sleep arousal index than controls and PD+RBD patients. Patients with PD+RBD had reduced REM sleep duration and proportion, longer REM latency, shorter REM bouts, and lower sawtooth wave density and duration. Both patient groups showed altered sawtooth wave spectral characteristics, with a shift toward higher frequencies compared with controls. NREM/REM transition durations increased across groups, being shortest in controls, longer in iRBD, and longest in PD+RBD. The findings indicate that REM sleep abnormalities in RBD extend beyond loss of atonia and dream enactment to broader microstructural changes.

China’s first-quarter 2017 GDP rose 6.9%, above expectations and the government’s 6.5% target, but the passage questions the reliability and significance of China’s GDP and industrial production data. Industrial production rose 7.6% in March 2017, its highest rate since January 2015, after a long period of unusually stable growth around 6%–6.3%. The passage links this rise to improved exports, which turned positive in Q1 2017, but suggests the improvement may be temporary, as similar export and industrial production increases in March 2016 did not last.

Retail sales rose 10.9% in March after weaker January-February growth, but this was described as roughly average since the 2014 slowdown. State-owned enterprise fixed asset investment continued growing at double-digit rates, while private and total fixed asset investment remained subdued compared with earlier years. The passage argues that China may have stabilized after pressure from the “rising dollar,” but says this does not necessarily indicate renewed durable growth. It concludes that industrial production growth of 7.6% would only be meaningful if it began a sustained acceleration, which the broader data do not yet support.

The Delaware Supreme Court reversed the Superior Court’s judgment affirming the Industrial Accident Board’s denial of workers’ compensation benefits to Cheryl Tickles. Tickles, a PNC Bank employee, was injured after using an employee-only ATM in Building 103 of PNC’s Bellevue Complex before her shift in Building 400. She slipped on ice in the Building 103 parking lot and later became totally disabled for about twelve weeks after shoulder surgery. The Board and Superior Court found the injury noncompensable because her workday had not begun and she was on a personal errand. The Supreme Court held that Tickles was injured on her employer’s premises and during the course of employment, because using the ATM before work was an incidental preparatory act of personal convenience. The case was remanded for further proceedings.
Moody’s said Saudi Arabia’s fiscal position remains strong but oil dependency is a key credit challenge, forecasting 2017 GDP contraction and large deficits.

The lecture continues modeling honeycomb mechanical behavior. It derives brittle crushing for in-plane compression by equating applied bending moment in a cell wall to the fracture moment, yielding a plateau stress proportional to the cell wall modulus of rupture and \((t/l)^2\), with a value of \(4/9\,\sigma_{fs}(t/l)^2\) for regular hexagons.

For tensile behavior, elastic moduli are the same as in compression. There is no elastic buckling in tension, plastic plateau stress is approximately the same as in compression, and brittle honeycombs can undergo fast fracture. A fracture toughness expression is derived for cracks large relative to cell size, assuming bending-dominated deformation and constant cell wall modulus of rupture; the result depends on cell size.

The lecture then compares triangular honeycombs with hexagonal ones. Triangular honeycombs behave like trusses with mainly axial forces, giving a modulus proportional to \(E_s(t/l)\), unlike hexagonal honeycombs, whose bending-dominated in-plane modulus scales as \(E_s(t/l)^3\). This makes triangulated structures much stiffer.

Out-of-plane honeycomb behavior is introduced because it is important for sandwich panels and energy absorption. Out-of-plane Young’s modulus scales with relative density, \(E_3^*=E_s(t/l)\) times a geometric factor, producing strong anisotropy relative to in-plane moduli. Poisson’s ratios for loading in the 3-direction equal the solid’s Poisson’s ratio, while reciprocal Poisson’s ratios involving in-plane loading are small for small \(t/l\). Out-of-plane shear moduli also scale linearly with \(t/l\).

Out-of-plane compressive failure modes are modeled: elastic buckling is estimated using plate buckling and scales as \(E_s(t/l)^3\); plastic collapse is estimated through a folding/plastic-hinge work calculation and scales approximately as \(\sigma_{ys}(t/l)^2\), while a more exact result for regular hexagons scales as \(\sigma_{ys}(t/l)^{5/3}\). Out-of-plane brittle fracture and crushing are also described as proportional to relative density. The lecture concludes by noting that these honeycomb models will support later foam modeling, and introduces future discussion of natural honeycomb materials such as wood and cork.

The passage argues that forex trading should be avoided because it is highly leveraged, volatile, difficult to predict, and operates as a zero-sum market without long-term wealth-building tailwinds. It says small price movements can wipe out traders, risk management may be ineffective, and 24-hour markets encourage overtrading. It also cites counterparty risk, scams, weak regulation, gamblers entering the market, unreliable unbacktested strategies, and high failure rates for systematic forex strategies. The passage concludes that traders should be very cautious before entering forex markets.

The Michigan Supreme Court affirmed a directed verdict for the city of Marquette in a personal injury case brought by Robert A. Maclam, who claimed he was injured after tripping over poultry crates obstructing a sidewalk. The court held that subdivision 16, section 1, chapter 7 of Marquette’s charter exempted the city from liability for damages caused by a person’s neglect to keep sidewalks clear of snow, ice, dirt, wood, or other obstructions. The court found that this charter provision controlled despite the general state law imposing municipal liability, was not repealed by later local legislation, and was not invalid as class legislation. The court agreed that any remedy would be against the owner or occupant responsible for keeping the sidewalk clear.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces a unified SM memory design for shared memory, L1, and texture caching, increasing L1 hit bandwidth versus Pascal and improving delivered performance per CUDA core by 50%. It adds larger L2 caches, GDDR6 memory with 14 Gbps signaling and improved power efficiency, and enhanced compression that provides about 50% higher effective bandwidth compared with Pascal.

Turing includes enhanced Tensor Cores supporting FP16, INT8, and INT4 precision for deep learning training, inference, and neural graphics. These cores power NVIDIA NGX features such as DLSS, AI InPainting, AI Super Rez, and AI Slow-Mo. Tesla T4, the first Turing-based data center inference GPU, includes 2,560 CUDA cores and 320 Tensor Cores, delivering up to 130 TOPS INT8 and 260 TOPS INT4 performance, with higher inference performance and energy efficiency than CPU-based systems.

Turing adds RT Cores for hardware-accelerated ray tracing, including BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing.
