Combined with NVIDIA RTX software, denoising, and hybrid rendering, Turing enables real-time ray-traced reflections, shadows, ambient occlusion, and other effects on a single GPU. The architecture supports APIs and technologies including Microsoft DXR, NVIDIA OptiX, RTX libraries, and future Vulkan ray tracing support.

The architecture also introduces new graphics features including Mesh Shading, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering. These features reduce CPU and shading bottlenecks, support more flexible geometry processing, enable adaptive shading rates, reuse shading computations, and improve VR and multi-view rendering efficiency.

Turing improves display, video, and connectivity features with DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz support, HDR processing, improved NVENC and NVDEC video engines, USB-C, and VirtualLink for single-cable VR headset connectivity. TU102 and TU104 GPUs use second-generation NVLink for higher-bandwidth two-way SLI, while TU106 does not support NVLink or SLI.

The passage describes TU104 and TU106 GPUs, including CUDA cores, Tensor Cores, RT Cores, cache, memory interfaces, and product uses such as GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, Quadro RTX 5000, and GeForce RTX 2070. It also defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric combining Tensor, FP32, RT Core, and INT32 operation contributions for hybrid rendering workloads.

Lake Havasu City is Arizona’s hottest place, reaching a state-record 128 degrees on June 29, 1994, second in the U.S. only to Death Valley’s 134 degrees. Many of Arizona’s highest temperatures occur along the Colorado River, including Bullhead City, Parker, Willow Beach and Yuma. State Climatologist Nancy Selover said Lake Havasu itself has little effect on the city’s weather. Western Arizona’s extreme heat is driven by isolation, rocky desert terrain, lack of monsoon moisture and clouds, very dry air, hot west winds, and little nearby irrigated agriculture to provide cooling.

The speaker says the team must ignore past events and prepare for the next game as its own challenge, focusing from the first shift onward. He describes entering coaching after retirement at Jacques Lemaire’s invitation, eventually enjoying it because of the satisfaction of helping players succeed. He says coaching involves both good and bad days, teaching, developing players’ abilities, and helping them handle adversity. He confirms an unnamed player is fine despite some stiffness. He emphasizes that hockey is not about retribution, says any discipline is up to the league, and stresses the need to avoid needless penalties against a strong power-play team.

Brazil is Latin America’s largest economy and a major South American financial hub, with trading centered on BM&F and BOVESPA under regulation by the Brazilian Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM). The passage discusses day trading and swing trading in Brazil, including assets such as stocks, REITs, mutual funds, ETFs, commodities, derivatives, currencies, and bonds. It notes risks including volatility, political and economic instability, currency fluctuations, regulation, taxes, transparency issues, liquidity limits, and company-specific risks. Trading may be subject to capital gains tax, dividend income tax, VAT on brokerage fees, IOF on foreign currency transactions, and other taxes.

It lists trading approaches such as value investing, momentum trading, trend following, technical analysis, options trading, contrarian trading, and algorithmic trading, and mentions technical and fundamental analysis tools. It says investment timing should consider economic indicators, politics, market and sector performance, and global conditions. A referenced Brazilian swing trading backtest produced 250 trades, a 0.75% average gain per trade, a 67% win rate, 19% maximum drawdown, and a 2.1 profit factor.

Wall Street indexes had their worst week in two years as rising bond yields and inflation fears pressured stocks, with the S&P 500 falling 3.9 percent. Despite the selloff, corporate earnings forecasts are rising sharply, largely due to the U.S. tax overhaul cutting the corporate tax rate to 21 percent from 35 percent. S&P 500 first-quarter profit growth is estimated at 17.7 percent, up from 11.7 percent on Dec. 20, while 2018 growth is forecast at 18.2 percent, up from 11.5 percent. Analysts also cited global growth and a weaker dollar as earnings supports. Upcoming earnings reports are expected to influence whether the market downturn continues.

US officials told CNN that Trump advisers and business associates had frequent communications during the campaign with Russians known to US intelligence, raising concerns due to their frequency and proximity to Trump. Trump and Obama were briefed on the contacts, which were intercepted through routine intelligence collection. Investigators had not determined intent and were examining whether associates coordinated with Russian operatives on releasing damaging information about Hillary Clinton’s campaign.

The speaker says the team sought to improve offensively while goaltending and defense remained strengths, citing the Neal trade and later contributions from P.K. Subban. He emphasizes honest player evaluation, the difficulty of trading longtime players like Shea Weber, and credits staff and scouts for enabling major trades while keeping the defense strong. He highlights Milwaukee’s role in player development, saying injuries made organizational depth essential and that players like Pekka Rinne, Roman Josi, Ryan Suter, and Weber benefited from time there. He says Subban’s fit depended on communication about hockey goals and off-ice ventures, with both sides aligned on winning the Stanley Cup. He also praises Nashville’s atmosphere, fan support, Bridgestone Arena, and the city’s hockey excitement.

Pfizer’s agreement with the Trump administration to lower drug prices has prompted other major pharmaceutical companies to seek similar deals. Several firms that received letters from President Trump demanding price cuts are trying to show progress, with some hoping to announce agreements with the White House as soon as this week, according to anonymous Washington representatives and lobbyists.

A Nairaland post shares photos of Folake, a Nigerian woman living with HIV/AIDS, whose treatment through PEPFAR at a CDC/IHVN-supported site in Lagos reportedly saved her life. The U.S. Embassy in Nigeria shared the photos for World AIDS Day to show that HIV/AIDS is not a death sentence. Forum comments reacted to her transformation, antiretroviral treatment, HIV stigma, testing, and mortality.

In Brennen v. Livingston Circuit Judge, the Michigan Supreme Court granted mandamus requiring the Livingston circuit court to dismiss an action at law. A chancery suit had been filed in Livingston County against J. D. Brennen and Belle E. Brennen, who lived in Washtenaw County and were served there. The circuit court found the matter had an adequate remedy at law and transferred it to the law side under 3 Comp. Laws 1915, § 12351. After a declaration was filed, the defendants specially appeared and moved to dismiss because they had not been served with process in Livingston County as required for transitory actions at law under § 12430.

The court held that transferring a case from chancery to law did not confer personal jurisdiction over defendants not properly served for an action at law. It also held that the defendants’ appearance and answer in chancery, and counsel’s remarks about possible transfer and pleading deadlines, did not waive their right to object to personal jurisdiction after the declaration was filed. The writ was granted.

SUDEP is a leading cause of death in people with epilepsy, especially those with uncontrolled generalized tonic-clonic seizures, nocturnal convulsions, and prone postictal positioning. The passage describes development of Korus, an autonomous body-repositioning mattress intended to reduce SUDEP risk by detecting body position and repositioning patients after seizures.

Korus is a twin XL mattress with inflatable cells, embedded pressure sensors, networking hardware, and machine-learning body position detection for prone, supine, left, and right positions. An app supports visualization, training, and cell control. In testing with normative controls, cells inflated to 14 inches within 7 seconds and repositioned 10 subjects from prone to recovery position with 100% success in an average of 21.75 seconds. Prone-position detection accuracy was 96.8%, overall position accuracy was 92.4%, and long-term sleep recording showed correct position detection 97.3% of the time. The authors state that further development is needed for a fully autonomous SUDEP prevention system.

Yael Kalai introduces an advanced cryptography course focused on the evolution of proofs in computer science rather than cryptography itself. The course will cover interactive proofs, doubly efficient interactive proofs, the GKR protocol, applications to PCPs and multiprover interactive proofs, Shamir’s IP = PSPACE theorem, and cryptographic methods for making proofs succinct and non-interactive, including Fiat-Shamir and SNARGs. Course requirements include scribe notes, one problem set, and recommended readings.

The lecture explains that classical proofs are verified line by line, while zero-knowledge proofs motivated new randomized and interactive proof models in the mid-1980s. Interactive proofs involve a possibly all-powerful prover and a polynomial-time randomized verifier. Completeness means true statements are accepted with high probability; soundness means false statements are accepted only with low probability, even against cheating provers. Repetition can amplify the gap between completeness and soundness.

Kalai discusses NP as languages with polynomial-time verifiable witnesses, then contrasts it with randomized non-interactive proofs, known as MA. As an example of the usefulness of randomness, she presents a randomized test for verifying whether \(C = AB\) for matrices by checking \(Cx = ABx\) for a random vector of powers of a field element, reducing verification to matrix-vector products.

The main technical example is the sum-check protocol. Given a multivariate polynomial \(f\), a subset \(H\) of a finite field, and a claimed value \(\beta\), the prover convinces the verifier that the sum of \(f\) over \(H^m\) equals \(\beta\). In each round, the prover sends a univariate polynomial obtained by summing over all but one remaining variable, and the verifier checks its degree and consistency with the previous claim before choosing a random field element. After \(m\) rounds, the verifier checks the final value against oracle access to \(f\).

The protocol has \(m\) rounds, communication proportional to \(md\) field elements, and verifier time depending on \(m\), \(d\), \(|H|\), and field operations. Completeness is 1 for an honest prover. Soundness follows because a cheating prover must at some round move from a false polynomial claim to a true one, which succeeds with probability at most \(d/|F|\) per round, giving total soundness at most \(md/|F|\). The field can be enlarged using extension fields to reduce this error.

NVIDIA’s Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended January 31, 2021. The company is headquartered in Santa Clara, California, trades on Nasdaq under NVDA, and had 620 million common shares outstanding as of February 19, 2021. NVIDIA describes itself as a pioneer in accelerated computing, expanding from PC graphics into AI, data science, autonomous vehicles, robotics, AR/VR, HPC, and other compute-intensive fields.

NVIDIA reports two business segments: Graphics and Compute & Networking. Its key markets are Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive. Products and platforms include GeForce, NVIDIA RTX, Quadro/NVIDIA RTX, vGPU software, DGX, HGX, EGX, Jetson, DRIVE, and Mellanox networking and interconnect solutions. NVIDIA completed its Mellanox acquisition in fiscal 2021 and announced a planned $40 billion acquisition of Arm Limited, expected to close in the first quarter of calendar 2022 subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions.

The company uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on suppliers and subcontractors for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, packaging, cards, systems, cables, substrates, and memory. NVIDIA identifies intense competition from GPU, SoC, interconnect, switch, and cloud or internal chip-development providers. It relies on patents, trademarks, trade secrets, nondisclosure agreements, and licensing arrangements to protect intellectual property.

As of January 31, 2021, NVIDIA had 18,975 employees across 29 countries, including 13,532 in research and development. The filing discusses recruitment, employee development, compensation, diversity and inclusion, and COVID-19 safety measures. It also lists executive officers including CEO Jen-Hsun Huang and CFO Colette Kress.

Risk factors include failure to meet evolving market needs, competition, dependence on third-party manufacturing and supply chains, product defects, inaccurate demand estimates, cybersecurity breaches, business disruptions, COVID-19 impacts, and risks related to acquisitions and integration.

Harvey Weinstein was indicted by a New York grand jury on rape and criminal sex-act charges after being charged with felonies days earlier. Manhattan District Attorney Cyrus Vance said the indictment moved Weinstein closer to accountability and that the grand jury investigation remains active. Defense attorney Ben Brafman said the indictment repeated existing charges, called the allegations unsupported, and said Weinstein would plead not guilty and seek dismissal. Brafman also said Weinstein would not testify before the grand jury because his attorneys lacked sufficient time and access to information to prepare. Weinstein surrendered to police, was released on $1 million bail, and has denied having non-consensual sex with anyone.

The passage describes a rotorcraft landing device for enabling drones without image capturing functions to land at a destination, addressing privacy concerns from aerial cameras. The device includes a landing portion, position recognition using cameras on the landing portion, and remote control that guides an approved drone to land. It may include distance measurement to control descent speed, identification verification before remote control, movable plates to guide and secure packages, and an opening/closing mechanism that protects components when not in use.

In an embodiment, a delivery drone carries a package from a warehouse to a user house using GPS or beacons, then switches to remote control by the house landing device near the destination. After landing, the drone releases the package, which is moved toward the center of the landing portion and conveyed by an ascending/descending mechanism to the user’s residential space. The landing device may be installed above the residential area to reduce risks involving people, animals, theft, obstacles, or debris.

A management system coordinates delivery requests, drone routes, drone and battery data, weather information, user notifications, and completion notices. The passage also describes modifications including simplified landing devices for non-snowy areas, integration with ventilation or smoke exhaust systems, weather observation functions, emergency landing use, portable disaster-relief landing devices, fall warnings, approach warnings for camera-equipped drones, battery monitoring, black box recording, takeoff procedures, route rules, beacon base stations, and countermeasures against illegal drones used for terrorism.

The PGA848 output-stage difference amplifier provides DA_IN– and DA_IN+ pins for adding external capacitors in parallel with internal 6.67kΩ feedback resistors to implement noise filtering, noise shaping, or customized attenuating gains. Designers must account for the 0.01% resistor network accuracy, ±15% absolute resistance variation, possible CMRR degradation from leakage, and avoid sourcing or sinking current through these pins.

The PGA848 operates in a single functional mode when the input-stage supply exceeds ±4.5V and the output-stage supply exceeds ±2.25V. It is a high-voltage, high-bandwidth programmable gain instrumentation amplifier with eight binary gain settings from 0.5V/V to 100V/V, intended for applications including factory automation, analog input modules, data acquisition, test and measurement, and semiconductor test.

A typical application drives an ADS8860 16-bit, 1MSPS SAR ADC using ±15V input-stage supplies, a 5.3V output-stage supply, a REF6250 5V reference, and an OPA192 buffer to set the PGA848 REF pin to 2.5V. The design uses input EMI/RFI filtering, feedback filtering with CFB, and an ADC input charge-reservoir filter. With CFB = 75pF, the nominal cutoff is 318kHz, changing to 277kHz with resistor tolerance.

Power supply voltages above 40V permanently damage the device. Layout guidance emphasizes matched input paths, close low-ESR bypass capacitors, separation of input traces from supply and output traces, minimizing leakage and parasitic capacitance at DA_IN pins, reducing thermal junctions, and maintaining distance from heat sources. TI also provides simulation tools, documentation, support resources, ESD cautions, packaging information, and standard disclaimers.

Harav Aaron Brafman, longtime Menahel of Yeshiva Derech Ayson–Yeshiva of Far Rockaway, died on Erev Shabbos, 19 Av, at age 73. Born in 1944, he studied and taught at Yeshivah Torah Vodaath and was close to several leading Rebbeim. In 1970 he became Menahel in Far Rockaway, where he guided generations of talmidim, gave shiurim, supported community needs, and maintained a tzedakah fund. His levayah was held at the yeshiva, followed by burial in Beit Shemesh. He is survived by his wife, siblings, children, and many grandchildren.

Using Gaia’s initial data release combined with RAVE survey data, University of Toronto astrophysicists calculated the Sun’s orbital speed around the Milky Way at 240 km/s and refined the estimated distance from the Sun to the galactic center to 7.6–8.2 kiloparsecs, or about 24,788–26,745 light years. The team analyzed over 200,000 stars observed by both Gaia and RAVE, using their relative velocities and proper motion calculations for Sagittarius A* to triangulate the distance. The study improved on earlier work using far fewer stars and suggested future Gaia data releases could further increase measurement precision.

Alan Comnes forwarded a Washington Post column arguing that California Gov. Gray Davis’s political outlook had improved after a summer without blackouts, aided by mild weather and reduced electricity use. The column notes remaining risks, including Southern California Edison’s bailout bill, delayed bond sales tied to PG&E litigation, budget pressures, drought concerns, weak polling for Davis, and vulnerabilities among potential Republican challengers William Simon Jr., Bill Jones, and Richard Riordan.

The email also includes a prior California energy issues roundup covering reports that conservation, weather, new power plants, and federal market controls helped avert blackouts; debate over an Edison rescue plan versus bankruptcy; Williams’s $591 million claim in PG&E’s bankruptcy; criticism of Davis’s extensive executive orders during the energy crisis; consumer opposition to the Edison bailout; California’s $5.7 billion revenue anticipation notes; concerns over infrastructure funding; and questions about whether the state’s long-term power contracts may remain above market prices through 2010.

Motley Fool Money reviews the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card, highlighting its unlimited 2% cash rewards, $200 bonus after $500 in purchases in the first 3 months, $0 annual fee, 12-month 0% intro APR on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, and up to $600 cell phone protection. The passage notes approval is most likely for applicants with good credit and includes disclosures about advertising partnerships, compensation, and editorial independence.

Enrique Marquez Jr. of Riverside, Calif., agreed to plead guilty to federal charges related to buying the assault rifles used by Syed Rizwan Farook and Tashfeen Malik in the 2015 San Bernardino attack, which killed 14 and injured 22. Marquez admitted Farook paid him for the rifles and that he was a straw buyer. He also admitted conspiring with Farook in 2011 and 2012 to plan attacks on Riverside City College and freeway traffic, though those plans were not carried out. Prosecutors said there is no evidence Marquez participated in or had advance knowledge of the San Bernardino attack. He faces up to 25 years in federal prison.

Bitcoin fell below $8,000 after Indian Finance Minister Arun Jaitley said India would take measures to stop crypto assets from being used for illegitimate financing or as payment. India has warned citizens about cryptocurrencies for months, comparing them to Ponzi schemes and saying they lack official backing. Reports of Indian banks suspending accounts of exchanges added to market anxiety, though responses varied. Analysts said India’s crypto market is small, accounting for 2% to 3% of global trade, but has growth potential. Traders and industry figures are concerned about regulation, though some believe the government will wait for a committee report and may use blockchain technology in digital payments.

Lawyers for Venezuelan TPS holders asked the Supreme Court to keep in place a federal judge’s order temporarily blocking the Trump administration from ending their protected status. TPS allows eligible citizens of designated countries to remain and work in the U.S. when return is unsafe due to conditions such as disaster or conflict. Venezuela was designated in 2021, redesignated in 2023, and extended through October 2026 before DHS Secretary Kristi Noem ended the designation and extension.

The National TPS Alliance and Venezuelan TPS holders challenged the termination, arguing it violated administrative law and was partly motivated by racial animus. U.S. District Judge Edward Chen blocked the termination in March, but the Supreme Court paused that order in May. Chen later issued a final ruling finding Noem acted unlawfully, and the appeals court declined to pause it.

Solicitor General D. John Sauer returned to the Supreme Court, arguing lower courts defied its prior stay. The challengers responded that the earlier stay did not prevent final judgment, that Chen relied on different authority, and that the record is now more developed.

The speaker said the team had an outstanding, unexpected season despite the disappointment of losing the Stanley Cup Final to a better team that deserved to win. He praised the players’ effort, resilience, belief, and competitiveness, as well as the work of the coaching staff and management. He also highlighted the fans’ strong support, the team’s remarkable run, and the fun they had throughout the year, while noting the loss would hurt for a while.

Costamare (CMRE) is presented as an attractive investment opportunity as its share price rebounds amid improving global economic and shipping industry conditions. The stock fell sharply from 2014 to 2016 due to weak global trade, but the author says sentiment and fundamentals are improving. CMRE owns and charters 71 containerships with about 466,000 TEU capacity and has recently chartered 16 ships with none laid up. Management cited tightening supply-demand dynamics, higher charter rates, a low idle fleet of 1.8%, and an order book below 13%. The company has $1.2 billion in contracted revenues, about three years of remaining charter duration, and major charterers including Evergreen, MSC, Maersk, Cosco, and Hapag Lloyd. CMRE has also reduced net debt from $1.7 billion in 2013 to $1 billion and holds about $219 million in cash. The author believes improved fundamentals and balance sheet strength could support future share price gains and discloses a long position in CMRE.

Tesla, Inc.’s 2020 Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended December 31, 2020. Tesla is a Delaware company headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with common stock listed on Nasdaq under TSLA. As of June 30, 2020, the aggregate market value of voting stock held by non-affiliates was $160.57 billion, and as of February 1, 2021, 959,853,504 common shares were outstanding.

Tesla designs, develops, manufactures, sells and leases fully electric vehicles and energy generation and storage systems, and provides related services. It operates in two reportable segments: automotive, including electric vehicles, leasing, regulatory credits, services, used vehicles, merchandise and insurance; and energy generation and storage, including solar and energy storage products and related services.

Its vehicles include Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X, with planned products including Cybertruck, Tesla Semi, the new Tesla Roadster and a lower-cost vehicle. Energy products include Powerwall, Powerpack, Megapack, Solar Roof and retrofit solar systems. Tesla sells primarily through its website, company-owned stores and galleries, and supports customers through service centers, Mobile Service, Superchargers and Destination Chargers.

Tesla manufactures at facilities in California, Gigafactory Nevada, Gigafactory New York and Gigafactory Shanghai, and is building Gigafactory Berlin and Gigafactory Texas. The company relies on global suppliers, including for battery cells, while developing its own battery cell technology. It is subject to government incentives, regulatory credit programs, vehicle safety rules, self-driving regulations, dealer laws, battery regulations and solar energy policies.

The filing identifies risks including COVID-19 impacts, production and ramp delays, growth and logistics challenges, electric vehicle demand uncertainty, supplier constraints, battery cell supply needs, competition, international operations, product defects, product liability, public confidence, and risks related to financing and leasing programs.

John Ternus, Apple’s 50-year-old senior vice president of hardware engineering, is increasingly viewed as a likely successor to CEO Tim Cook, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. The speculation grew after COO Jeff Williams stepped back from operations and plans to leave Apple. Ternus joined Apple in 2001, helped oversee major products including iPad, iPhone, AirPods, Macs, Apple Silicon, and Vision Pro-related hardware, and has gained visibility at keynotes and product launches. Apple’s PR teams have reportedly put more spotlight on him as he takes on broader product strategy responsibilities. A University of Pennsylvania mechanical engineering graduate and former competitive swimmer, Ternus previously worked at Virtual Research Systems. His potential rise comes amid broader Apple executive turnover and questions about Cook’s eventual transition.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022. Amazon is incorporated in Delaware, headquartered in Seattle, trades on Nasdaq under AMZN, and had 10,247,259,757 common shares outstanding as of January 25, 2023. Its aggregate market value of voting stock held by non-affiliates was $944.7 billion as of June 30, 2022.

Amazon states its goal is to be “Earth’s most customer-centric company” and operates through three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services. It serves consumers through online and physical stores, devices, media content, and subscriptions such as Amazon Prime; sellers through programs enabling sales and fulfillment; developers and enterprises through AWS; content creators through publishing and content programs; and advertisers through sponsored ads, display, and video advertising.

The company faces broad competition across retail, media, e-commerce services, logistics, cloud computing, consumer electronics, grocery, and advertising. It identifies selection, price, convenience, fulfillment speed and reliability, service quality, and customer willingness to change business practices as key competitive factors. Amazon relies on intellectual property protections and notes that its business is seasonal, historically producing higher sales volume in the fourth quarter.

As of December 31, 2022, Amazon employed approximately 1,541,000 full-time and part-time employees and also used independent contractors and temporary personnel. It reported focus areas including investment and innovation, inclusion and diversity, safety, engagement, training, and employee development.

The filing lists risks including intense competition, expansion into new products and regions, international regulatory and operational challenges, demand variability, seller fraud, intellectual property disputes, foreign exchange exposure, operational complexity, system interruptions, data security, inventory risk, supplier risk, payments-related risk, litigation, product liability, tax obligations, and government contract requirements.

Amazon operated leased and owned facilities for offices, physical stores, fulfillment, data centers, and other uses across North America and international locations. Its common stock is traded on the Nasdaq Global Select Market, and it reported no recent sales of unregistered securities or issuer purchases of equity securities.

Amazon’s revenue comes primarily from sales of products and services. Its financial focus is long-term sustainable free cash flow through operating income growth and management of receivables, inventory, payables, and capital expenditures. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $96.0 billion at the end of 2021 and $70.0 billion at the end of 2022. Operating cash flow was $46.3 billion in 2021 and $46.8 billion in 2022.

The passage examines inclusive education for children with disabilities in Myanmar, focusing on visually impaired students in Yangon. Inclusive education is framed through international agreements such as the Salamanca Declaration and CRPD, while Myanmar’s legal framework includes the 2015 Law on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and amendments to the National Education Law.

The study used qualitative case study methods in two special schools for visually impaired students and two connected regular schools in Yangon. Students receive primary education in special schools, then attend lower secondary education in regular schools while continuing to receive support from special schools. The author describes this as “limited inclusive education in phase.”

Findings show that special schools provide Braille education, life skills, supplementary study, computer training, emotional security, and support from visually impaired teachers and peers. Regular schools help students with visual impairment develop social and communication skills and may increase disability awareness among students without disabilities. However, challenges include limited cooperation between special and regular school teachers, regular school teachers’ dependence on special school expertise, bullying and teasing, limited friendships between students with and without disabilities, and low public awareness of educational opportunities for children with disabilities.

The passage concludes that Myanmar’s phased model uses existing special and regular school resources and may offer lessons for inclusive education, but it requires stronger collaboration, teacher training, student inclusion programs, and attention to the broader needs of both disabled and non-disabled students.

The ADS9803 uses SMPL_SYNC with a free-running shared SMPL_CLK to synchronize channel selection and FCLKOUT across multiple ADCs after power-up, clock restart, or reset. It includes an internal low-drift reference filtered with a 10µF capacitor at REFIO, or an external reference with the internal reference disabled through SPI or SDI/EXTREF.

The device supports 2-lane and 4-lane SDR or DDR data interfaces, outputs 20-bit conversion results MSB first in 24-bit packets, and provides DCLKOUT and FCLKOUT. It includes data randomization using XOR with a PRBS bit or LSB, simple and moving averaging, and test patterns including fixed, ramp, and alternating patterns.

Reset and power-down can be controlled by pins or registers, with registers returning to defaults and requiring an initialization sequence using a free-running sampling clock. Speed-boost mode supports up to 8MSPS for a selected analog input channel pair while other channels remain idle.

Configuration registers are organized into three banks accessed by SPI, with procedures for register read/write and daisy-chain operation across multiple ADCs. Register fields configure interface modes, averaging, test patterns, speed-boost, gain correction, reference selection, lane count, analog bandwidth, power-down, and common-mode range.

Application guidance describes the ADS9803 as an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS DAQ system for ATE applications, with built-in analog front-end, post-calibration TUE of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C for ±5V range, low-noise and wide-bandwidth modes, and 7.5µs settling to 99.95% FS in wide-bandwidth mode. Layout guidance recommends close bypass and reference capacitors, avoiding vias between pins and capacitors, and keeping analog and reference signals away from digital noise sources.

The speaker says time off helped the team focus and prepare. They are focused on the next game, not looking ahead, and expect to review video and make adjustments against a strong shot-blocking opponent.

The passage describes a patent disclosure for systems and methods that create a neural bridge by decoding a user’s neural activity to determine intended movements and delivering electrical stimulation or control signals to a target such as a limb, prosthetic, wheelchair, cursor, exoskeleton, remote device, or robotic arm. The system measures neural signals, removes artifacts, extracts features such as amplitude, wavelet power, or firing rate, and uses trained decoders to identify desired movement and movement effort. A body state observer and sensor feedback may be used to dynamically adjust stimulation patterns in real time.

The disclosed system can deliver high-definition, multiplexed stimulation containing interleaved signals to produce compound or simultaneous movements without interference. It may account for electrode movement, joint position, user activation profiles, and changing neural activity during movement. Training can use visual cues, graphical body-part feedback, stimulation feedback, and machine learning methods such as support vector machines.

The disclosure includes examples showing accurate tracking of hand and finger positions using a stimulation sleeve and sensors, and an experiment with a quadriplegic participant. In that experiment, cortical signals were decoded to control discrete thumb flexion, discrete thumb extension, and rhythmic thumb wiggle using a virtual central pattern generator and neuromuscular electrical stimulation. The participant initiated, sustained, and completed these movements through thought alone, achieving reported individual movement accuracies above 84% and overall accuracy of 77.4% across rest and movement states.

The passage outlines sections of Foreign Relations papers on World War I, covering peace efforts before U.S. entry, Allied and Central Powers responses to peace proposals, U.S. initiatives involving Austria-Hungary, Mexico, Greece, and Germany’s constitutional struggle. It also lists topics on neutral rights, German unrestricted submarine warfare, severance of U.S.-German relations, the Zimmermann telegram, armed merchant ships, attacks on American vessels, the U.S. declaration of war on Germany, captured seamen, and Latin American reactions, including severed relations, declarations of war, neutrality changes, and proposed conferences.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that on August 1, 2016, it entered into an underwriting agreement for the issuance and sale of senior unsecured notes totaling $19.75 billion, with maturities from 2019 to 2056 and interest rates ranging from 1.100% to 3.950%. The notes will be issued under its May 18, 2009 indenture, as supplemented by an Eleventh Supplemental Indenture dated August 8, 2016, with U.S. Bank National Association as trustee. Interest is payable semiannually on February 8 and August 8 beginning February 8, 2017. The filing also lists related exhibits, including the underwriting agreement, supplemental indenture, note forms, and legal opinions.

The 3-4 defense uses 3 down linemen, 4 linebackers, and 4 defensive backs, with outside linebackers creating matchup problems through rushing or coverage. It typically requires bigger defensive linemen using a two-gap approach, hybrid outside linebackers, two inside linebackers, two corners, and two safeties.

Its strengths include versatility, disguised pressure, and the ability to blitz from multiple positions while changing coverage looks after the snap. Common blitzes include an outside linebacker edge blitz and the “Crossfire” blitz with both inside linebackers crossing toward the quarterback. Common coverages include Cover 4 and Cover 2 Man.

Weaknesses appear against modern spread offenses, especially when outside linebackers must cover receivers, leaving a lighter box vulnerable to the run. Trips formations can also create coverage problems.

The passage links the 3-4 defense to coaches Bill Parcells, Bill Belichick, Nick Saban, and Kirby Smart, noting major championships won by coaches from this coaching tree.

The study estimates SARS-CoV-2-attributable mortality in India during 2020–2021 using WHO-compliant verbal autopsy surveys linked to the Consumer Pyramids Household Survey. Researchers attempted verbal autopsies for 30,447 deaths reported in CPHS from 2018–2021, completed 22,178, and analyzed 20,453 after excluding deaths that occurred before 2018. Cause of death was assigned using ICD-10 codes by trained physicians, and statistical adjustments addressed verbal autopsy non-response, delayed death reporting, and population representativeness.

The study finds that India’s all-cause annual death rate in 2020–2021 was 81.19% higher than in 2018–2019. SARS-CoV-2 accounted for 17.93% of all deaths during the pandemic and 33.15% of excess deaths. Cardiovascular disease accounted for 27.18% of all deaths and 23.15% of excess deaths, while respiratory deaths declined by an amount equal to 1.52% of excess deaths. SARS-CoV-2 deaths spiked at the end of the national lockdown and during the second COVID wave, with the second wave showing a more distinct SARS-CoV-2 mortality spike relative to other causes.

SARS-CoV-2 death rates increased with age and were highest among those over 80, though most SARS-CoV-2 deaths occurred among ages 61–80. Rates were higher among urban residents, but total deaths were greater in rural areas because of the larger rural population. Differences by sex and income were not statistically significant. State-level SARS-CoV-2 excess death rates were lower in parts of the Gangetic plain and highest in Goa, Meghalaya, and Tripura.

The authors note limitations including possible misclassification of U07 and U08 deaths, imperfect statistical corrections for delayed reporting and survey non-response, and uncertainty in adapting verbal autopsy coding for SARS-CoV-2.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture improves rendering performance through 2x FP32 throughput, L1 cache advancements, second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, GDDR6X memory, and new concurrency features. In a Wolfenstein: Youngblood frame example, shader-only rendering takes 51 ms, adding RT Cores reduces it to 20 ms, DLSS reduces it to 12 ms, and the RTX 3080 renders it in 6.7 ms.

GA10x RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection testing over Turing and add an Interpolate Triangle Position unit to accelerate ray-traced motion blur. This enables more accurate motion blur for moving or deforming geometry, with rendering up to eight times faster than Turing in some cases and up to five times faster in a Blender Cycles 2.90 demo on RTX 3080 versus RTX 2080 Super.

Third-generation Tensor Cores support more data types, including TF32 and BF16, and add structured sparsity for up to 2x matrix multiplication throughput. RTX 3080 delivers higher Tensor Core throughput than RTX 2080 Super, including 119 peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS and 238 with sparsity. DLSS uses Tensor Cores to improve performance and image quality, and Ampere adds a 9x Super Resolution scaling factor for 8K gaming.

GA10x GPUs introduce GDDR6X memory developed with Micron, using PAM4 signaling to increase bandwidth. GDDR6X supports up to 19.5 Gbps data rates and up to 936 GB/sec peak memory bandwidth, with new encoding and signal methods to manage SNR challenges.

NVIDIA RTX IO enables GPU-based loading and decompression of game and creative assets, working with Microsoft DirectStorage to reduce CPU workload and improve I/O performance. It is intended to support faster loading, reduced stutter, asset streaming, and large open-world games.

The NVIDIA A40 is positioned for data center visual computing, offering higher FP32, ray tracing, and AI throughput than Quadro RTX 6000, PCIe Gen4 support, 48GB memory expandable to 96GB through NVLink, vGPU support, and EGX platform compatibility. Ampere GPUs also support DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, HDCP 2.3, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-generation NVENC encoding.

The passage also describes GeForce RTX 3090 and RTX 3070 specifications, Error Detection and Replay for GDDR6X memory overclocking, and RTX A6000 workstation capabilities, including 48GB GDDR6 memory, NVLink expansion, ray tracing, motion blur acceleration, and AI denoising.

Iran’s parliament gave initial approval to a bill increasing spending on its missile program and Revolutionary Guards in response to new US sanctions. The measure allocates over $260 million each to the ballistic missile program and Quds Force, supports those affected by sanctions, and requires further votes before becoming law.

The lecture reviews quiz results and then focuses on full factorial design of experiments. It explains 2-level factorial designs, contrasts, coded factor levels, main effects, interaction effects, and how these extend from 2-factor to k-factor experiments. The professor shows how contrast tables are used to estimate effects and how the same information forms the design matrix for regression models with interaction terms.

The lecture then discusses using ANOVA to test whether main effects and interactions are significant, comparing effect variation to residual or replicate error. A brake-forming example with punch depth and material type illustrates fitting a linear model with interaction, using replicates to estimate noise, examining residuals, and testing model terms. The lecture also covers lack-of-fit testing by adding center points or additional experimental points to check for curvature, especially when some factors are continuous and others are discrete.

The final portion introduces nuisance factors, blocking, randomization, and confounding. The professor explains that nuisance effects should be held constant when possible, randomized when uncontrollable, or blocked when known. A 2-by-2 example shows how blocking choices can avoid confounding nuisance factors with main effects, instead confounding them with less important interaction effects. This leads into the next topic: fractional factorial designs.

The Neofoot study assessed whether newborn foot length can identify low birth weight (LBW) and preterm birth (PTB) in Papua New Guinea, where many births occur outside health facilities and access to weighing and gestational age assessment is limited. The prospective diagnostic accuracy study enrolled 342 stable newborns assessed within 72 hours of birth in Madang Province. Birth weight was measured using electronic scales, gestational age was estimated from last menstrual period or ultrasound, and right foot length was measured twice using a plastic ruler fixed to a cardboard box. Trained volunteers also measured foot length for 123 babies.

Among enrolled newborns, 21.1% were LBW and 7.3% were preterm. Mean foot length was 7.8 cm. The optimal foot length cut-off for both LBW and PTB was <7.7 cm. For LBW, sensitivity was 84.7% and specificity 69.6%; for PTB, sensitivity was 88.0% and specificity 61.8%. Negative predictive values were high for LBW (94.5%) and PTB (98.5%), while positive predictive value was lower, especially for PTB (15.4%). Agreement between researcher and volunteer measurements showed a mean difference of 0.07 cm, with 7.3% of paired measurements outside the 95% limits of agreement.

The study found newborn foot length measurement to be a simple, feasible method for identifying LBW and PTB babies in this setting, though further implementation research is needed.

Blackwell adds fast clock gating, including for the entire memory clock tree via GDDR7, to reduce dynamic power. Separate GPU core and memory power rails enable workload-based voltage control and shutdown of unused chip portions to reduce leakage and idle power.

A Berliner Testament lets spouses appoint each other as sole heirs and usually their children as final heirs, providing financial security for the surviving spouse. However, it has a strong binding effect and generally cannot be changed unilaterally, even after major life changes or a spouse’s death. Clauses can reduce this rigidity. Tax allowances and inheritance tax consequences should also be considered, and legal advice is recommended.

Delta executives said premium cabin revenue could overtake standard coach sales for at least a quarter or two next year. Last quarter, premium ticket revenue rose 9% to nearly $5.8 billion, while main-cabin revenue fell 4% to just over $6 billion. CEO Ed Bastian said premium-travel demand shows no sign of slowing.

MSPM0G MCUs support five operating modes—RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN—with configurable policies for balancing performance and power. The devices use two power domains: PD1 for CPU, memories, and high-performance peripherals, and PD0 for low-speed, low-power peripherals. SHUTDOWN disables both domains and allows wake only through NRST, SWD, or certain IO logic matches.

The PMU provides regulated core supplies, VDD supervision, brown-out reset monitoring, and trim protection. The clock module includes LFOSC, SYSOSC, external clock/crystal inputs, and SYSPLL, distributing clocks such as MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, LFCLK, ADC clocks, and CAN clocks. DMA supports multiple transfer channels, configurable triggers, interrupt features, cascading, and stride mode. The event manager routes peripheral events to the CPU, DMA, or other peripherals.

Memory and peripheral features include up to dual-bank flash plus 16kB data flash with ECC, in-circuit programming, 1kB sectors, endurance options, and bank address swap; up to 128kB SRAM split into two banks with configurable protection and retention behavior; GPIO support for up to 93 pins; and IOMUX configuration for pad settings and pin multiplexing. Analog features include two 12-bit ADCs, a temperature sensor, configurable VREF, comparators, and a 12-bit buffered DAC.

Security and acceleration features include AES-128/256 acceleration, secure key storage for up to four keys, CRC-16/CRC-32, TRNG, and a math accelerator. Communication peripherals include UART, I2C, SPI, CAN-FD, RTC, watchdog timers, and general-purpose and advanced timers. The document also describes analog connections, IO diagrams, SWD debugging, boot strap loader operation over UART or I2C, factory constants, application layout recommendations, development tools, documentation support, revision history, and packaging/orderable information.

People have long used substances like caffeine and nicotine to improve focus, and science now better understands how they work. Current efforts to “hack” the mind include Tim Tully’s work on a possible memorization pill, including studying people with exceptional memory and engineering fruit flies with photographic memories through CREB activators. Other researchers are seeking genes linked to intelligence, though the task is difficult and controversial. Deep brain stimulation is also being developed to both monitor brain activity and respond to abnormal patterns linked to panic, depression, or psychosis by using electrical pulses to restore normal function.

The study compares models for forecasting fatal opioid-related overdoses at the census-tract level to support geographically targeted public health interventions. Using data from Cook County, Illinois (2015–2022) and Massachusetts (2001–2021), the authors evaluated simple baselines, statistical models, spatial models, tree-based models, and a neural network model. Inputs included prior overdose counts, location, time, and optional Social Vulnerability Index covariates.

The authors introduced “best possible reach” (%BPR), an intervention-focused metric measuring how well a model identifies the highest-burden tracts under a fixed intervention budget, and compared it with RMSE and MAE. Results showed that model rankings differed by metric: %BPR sometimes favored models that would identify more fatal overdoses than models preferred by error-based metrics. In Massachusetts, BST with SVI and NBSpLag with SVI achieved the highest %BPR; in Cook County, BST achieved the highest %BPR.

Simple historical average models performed competitively with more complex models in both locations, often within uncertainty intervals of top models. The authors recommend including tuned historical-average baselines in future overdose forecasting studies and using intervention-aware metrics when forecasts are intended to guide public health action. Limitations include evaluation in only two jurisdictions, use of K=100 tracts for %BPR, possible variation with other intervention budgets, and reliance on a limited covariate set.

The passage explains how the Relative Strength Index (RSI) can be used in CFD trading. RSI is a momentum indicator, introduced by J. Welles Wilder in 1978, that measures gains and losses over a period and ranges from 0 to 100. It is used to identify overbought and oversold conditions, potential reversals, corrective pullbacks, and buy or sell signals.

A Contract for Difference (CFD) is a financial contract based on the price difference of an underlying asset between opening and closing. CFDs allow traders to speculate on assets such as stocks, commodities, currencies, and indices without owning them. CFD trading is described as a zero-sum game.

The passage discusses RSI strategies including mean reversion, day trading thresholds, RSI momentum, and divergence signals. Typical RSI thresholds are 30 for oversold and 70 for overbought, while day trading may use more extreme levels such as 15 and 85 on shorter time frames. Shorter time frames may be more responsive but more erratic, while longer time frames may be smoother.

Backtesting is emphasized as essential for validating RSI strategies. Examples using SPY showed one strategy returning 0.86% per trade with significant drawdowns, while an enhanced two-day RSI strategy increased trades but reduced average gain to 0.67% with smoother drawdowns. The passage also recommends combining RSI with other indicators, adapting settings to asset class and market conditions, watching RSI divergences, and prioritizing risk management, especially because CFD leverage can be high.

Former Langley City mayor and Liberal MLA Peter Fassbender is considering running for Langley City mayor and expects to decide by early August. He previously served as mayor before being elected MLA for Surrey-Fleetwood in 2013, later holding several ministerial roles. Two incumbent councillors have already declared mayoral runs.

The speaker expresses gratitude and solemn responsibility upon being called to national office during a difficult global and domestic period. He says the United States had prospered through republican institutions, peace, commerce, agriculture, manufacturing, public revenue, debt reduction, and public improvements, and that current distress is not due to unjust American policy but to the actions of warring powers. He pledges to pursue peace, neutrality, constitutional union, states’ and individual rights, religious liberty, press freedom, fiscal economy, debt reduction, limited military force, public improvements, science, and efforts concerning aboriginal neighbors. He places confidence in prior examples, fellow citizens, public representatives, and divine guidance.

The Supreme Court agreed to hear the case of Hunter, a Texas man who pleaded guilty to aiding and abetting wire fraud and waived his appeal rights in a plea agreement. After sentencing, he challenged a mandatory mental-health medication condition, but the 5th Circuit dismissed the appeal based on the waiver. Hunter argues other circuits would allow such challenges, especially because the trial judge said he had a right to appeal. Arguments are expected early next year, with a decision by summer.

The passage describes host BIOS environment requirements for using the AGESA software interface, including establishing a valid stack, creating standard headers, locating binary image entry points, and routing calls through AMD dispatchers and host bridge procedures. The host environment must implement required call-out routing, allocate buffers, manage configuration blocks, and use published entry points rather than internal procedure names.

It outlines UEFI integration across SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases, including required tools, libraries, build targets, environment variables, and platform option files. UEFI-specific behavior includes StdHeader redefinition, PEI services handling, use of environment-specific libraries, and required integration of AGESA control files into the host build system.

The passage details stack-related procedures such as AMD_RESET_ENABLEMENT, AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK, and stack teardown routines. These establish Cache-As-RAM stack regions before main memory is available and must be used by the host environment, with restrictions on modifying stack registers, cache controls, MTRRs, or related settings during pre-memory execution.

It describes AGESA service and entry procedures, including AmdCreateStruct, AmdReleaseStruct, event log reading, APIC and PCI address queries, MMIO mapping, memory FRU identification, and data eye retrieval. Major initialization entry points include AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, graphics configuration, AmdInitLate, ready-to-boot handling, and S3 resume routines.

The passage also lists PEIM and DXE driver responsibilities, including processor initialization, memory initialization, reset coordination, publication of PPIs and HOBs, generation of ACPI/DMI tables, VGA resource control for iGPU, and suspend/resume context handling. Required host call-outs include buffer allocation and deallocation, which must cooperate with AGESA memory and runtime requirements.

Yankees rookie Cam Schlittler pitched eight scoreless innings in Game 3 of the AL Wild Card series, striking out 12 and allowing five hits. Scout Matt Hyde praised the performance as “unbelievable.” Schlittler, drafted in 2022, became the first MLB pitcher with eight scoreless innings, 12 strikeouts, and no walks.

The Colorado Supreme Court affirmed a directed verdict awarding real estate brokers a commission from George W. and Della B. Thuro. The brokers had procured Mrs. Charles Tallman as a purchaser, and her liability under the purchase contract was not disputed. The court held that George Thuro could not avoid the commission based on his refusal or inability to be bound by the contract, and issues concerning his or Charles Tallman’s ratification were immaterial. Any variance between the pleadings and proof was not prejudicial, and the refusal of requested instructions and denial of motions to strike were harmless.

Montecito Union School District in Santa Barbara County settled a sexual abuse lawsuit for $7.5 million with two brothers, now 65 and 68, who alleged that former superintendent and principal Stanford Kerr molested them in the 1970s. The district admitted no liability and said it settled to avoid the financial risk of a trial. The brothers had sought $35 million; a third plaintiff previously settled for $1 million.

The settlement equals about 40% of the 350-student district’s 2025-26 budget. Superintendent Anthony Ranii said the district lacks insurance coverage for the period in question and will manage costs through a hiring freeze, staff reductions through attrition, and redirected capital repair funds, while avoiding layoffs.

The case follows California’s Assembly Bill 218, which removed the statute of limitations for some childhood sexual abuse claims against public agencies. School districts statewide face potentially large costs from decades-old abuse claims, while efforts to restore a statute of limitations stalled in the Legislature.

The passage argues that common market labels based on percentage moves, such as a 20% decline for a bear market or a 20% rise for a bull market, lack rational or data-based support and do not help investors manage risk or allocate capital. The author says such definitions can be misleading across indexes and market periods. He proposes defining secular bull and bear markets by longer-term economic trends, investor psychology, volatility, and changes in valuation multiples. In a secular bull market, broad economic shifts support rising revenues and earnings, volatility tends to fall, and investors pay more for each dollar of earnings. In a secular bear market, volatility rises, rallies and retreats are frequent, economic conditions are challenging, and investors pay less for earnings. The author emphasizes that multiple expansion or contraction, rather than earnings growth alone, often drives market returns, citing the 1982–2000 bull market as an example.

Pharma tariffs President Trump had said would start Wednesday did not take effect, and no new timeline was provided. A White House official said the administration would prepare tariffs on companies that do not build in the U.S. or reach drug pricing agreements. Pharmaceutical executives are receiving near-daily calls from White House and agency officials as the administration seeks deals with drug companies and other industries ahead of the 2026 midterms.

This study compared Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) with an explainable machine learning approach for detecting outliers in plantar pressure data and evaluated how experts perceived their explanations. Multi-center static and dynamic plantar pressure data were collected using two pressure measurement systems, preprocessed to standardized 64×64 grids, and normalized. Expert annotation produced 1,031 samples, including 798 valid and 233 outlier samples across four categories: General Acquisition Error, Double Foot Capture, Inverted Orientation, and Incorrect Side Annotation. Synthetic augmentation expanded the dataset to 2,798 samples.

The SPM approach used affine registration, pixel-wise non-parametric testing against a normative dataset, and cluster-based correction. The machine learning approach used a convolutional neural network with foot-side metadata and SHAP explanations. Both methods were evaluated with nested stratified cross-validation.

The machine learning approach outperformed SPM, achieving an F1-score of 0.99 ± 0.00 and MCC of 0.96 ± 0.01, compared with SPM’s F1-score of 0.93 ± 0.01 and MCC of 0.78 ± 0.02. SPM false positives often involved valid but pathological feet, while many false negatives involved incorrect side annotations. The machine learning model had its lowest class accuracy for General Acquisition Error.

Sixteen experts evaluated explanations using a semantic differential survey. Both approaches were rated positively for clarity, correctness, usefulness, relevance, understandability, trustworthiness, and completeness. SPM was descriptively rated as simpler, but no statistically significant differences were found. Experts most often preferred the machine learning approach with SHAP explanations, followed by SPM.

The study concludes that both SPM and explainable machine learning are promising for automated detection of technical and procedural anomalies in plantar pressure data, with machine learning showing higher predictive performance and both approaches producing explanations perceived as useful by experts.

The passage explains defensive approaches against the High Post Split Offense, which uses a high post split followed by down screens to free shooters and create mismatches. Defenders must guard the high post, disrupt guard splits, handle down screens, and defend the low post.

A basic NBA “show and recover” strategy has defenders sag in front of the high post to force cutters wide, with the post defender protecting the basket and pressuring the high post toward the weak-hand corner. On down screens, defenders show to force shooters wide, then recover to deny passes and protect post matchups, avoiding switches that could create low-post mismatches.

The SOS disruption strategy applies early ball pressure, pushes the ballhandler to the sideline, denies the high post, switches on splits and down screens, and traps wing or low-post passes. It includes rotations for wing traps, pass-outs, and post traps, with defenders rotating into denial, fronting, and help positions according to ball movement and offensive actions.

Deutsche Bank is looking to sell its 8.8 percent stake in Dubai-based Abraaj, sources said, with urgency increasing amid Abraaj’s dispute with investors over alleged misuse of funds and Deutsche’s own restructuring. Deutsche considers the holding non-core and had sought a valuation about two years ago, though it was weaker than expected. Abraaj is under investigation by investors including the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and IFC over a $1 billion healthcare fund, allegations it denies. The firm has considered selling its investment business and other assets to ease cashflow pressures, while cutting jobs, reshuffling management, suspending new investments, and releasing some capital commitments. Two senior Abraaj executives have also resigned.

The passage describes attacking a Box & One defense using post flashes into the middle, backdoor cuts, and high/low action to exploit defensive vulnerabilities. If no shot is available, the offense can flow into single/double screen continuity. Variations include baseline screens for the star player and point backdoor entries. Successful implementation requires coordinated execution, screen and post-up skills, defensive recognition, communication, timing, scouting, and adjusting alignments to attack weak defenders.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated February 11, 2015, reporting that it issued a press release announcing results for the quarter and fiscal year ended January 25, 2015. The filing includes Exhibit 99.1, the press release titled “NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2015,” and Exhibit 99.2, CFO Commentary by Colette M. Kress. The materials are furnished, not filed, and are not incorporated by reference into SEC filings.

The passage examines the educational potential of the metaverse, describing it as an immersive virtual environment that can support collaboration, simulation, personalized learning, and safe practice in fields such as science, medicine, engineering, and special education. It also notes limitations, including monitoring difficulties, increased cognitive effort, uncertain learning gains, infrastructure needs, device access, teacher training, cost, health concerns, data security, and inequality of opportunity.

The study surveyed 333 teachers in Türkiye using a 28-question online questionnaire. Teachers reported moderate knowledge of the metaverse and limited direct experience, often related to virtual reality or three-dimensional virtual worlds. They generally held positive attitudes toward educational use, citing advantages such as student interest, real-world-like practice, learning by doing, exposure to new technologies, and reduced educational limitations. However, they also expressed concerns about technical problems, addiction, unequal access, data security, teacher readiness, preparation difficulty, physical discomfort, and classroom management.

Teachers were willing to use the metaverse and highly willing to receive training. They viewed information technology, physics, biology, chemistry, and mathematics as the most suitable subjects. They considered the education system, teachers, parents, and schools largely unready, while students were seen as relatively more ready. Most expected widespread effective use within one to five years. The passage concludes that the metaverse has transformative educational potential but requires infrastructure, content development, teacher preparation, health safeguards, and systematic planning.

The speaker describes the emotional birth of his baby, then discusses a teammate’s head injury, saying the team played harder in response. He also comments on a Drury hit, prior incidents, and possible league review.

H. B. Fuller VP Traci L. Jensen sold 5,397 shares on October 2 at an average price of $58.40, totaling $315,184.80. Shares opened at $56.81 Friday, with a $2.87 billion market cap, 25.96 PE ratio, and 52-week range of $41.52 to $58.74. The company reported quarterly EPS of $0.65, below the $0.67 consensus, on revenue of $562.87 million. A quarterly dividend of $0.15 will be paid November 2 to shareholders of record October 19. Analysts give H. B. Fuller an average “Hold” rating and $57.40 consensus price target. Institutional investors own 92.37% of shares. The company makes adhesives, sealants, and specialty chemical products across several global segments.

The Supreme Court will hear on August 17 Lt Col Prasad Shrikant Purohit’s bail plea in the 2008 Malegaon blast case and a plea challenging bail granted to co-accused Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur. The Bombay High Court had granted Thakur bail but rejected Purohit’s application.

The speaker says his MCL has healed, feels strong, and is not painful, though another torn issue will need surgery after the series and a brace will help. After quick rehab, he feels ready and anxious to return, and hopes Brett heals quickly too.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K reporting that on May 7, 2015 it issued a press release and CFO commentary on results for the quarter ended April 26, 2015. It also reported that its board approved winding down Icera modem operations in Q2 fiscal 2016 while remaining open to a sale. If unsold, NVIDIA estimates restructuring charges of $100 million to $125 million, primarily in fiscal 2016.

The passage introduces LUKB Disease Trajectory (LUKB DT), a web tool integrated into the LUKB platform for identifying disease trajectories from electronic medical records. The tool uses four main steps: inputting EMR data and parameters, filtering diseases associated with an exposure using Cox regression with time-varying covariates, detecting temporally ordered disease pairs using binomial tests, and validating disease-pair directionality using conditional logistic regression. Confirmed disease pairs are concatenated to construct trajectories.

A case study used UK Biobank ICD-10 diagnosis data to examine trajectories following COVID-19 diagnosis. The dataset included 6,166,668 medical records from 446,995 individuals. For analysis, 183,386 individuals were included, including 8,411 with COVID-19, and 274 diseases were assessed. Cox regression identified 90 diseases associated with COVID-19. These formed 8,010 disease pairs, of which 2,410 showed temporal association, 527 passed directionality testing, and all 527 were confirmed by conditional logistic regression. The resulting trajectories mainly linked COVID-19 to SARS-CoV-2-related conditions, viral pneumonia, respiratory failure, and other medical care. Immune-related diseases reported in other COVID-19 studies were not identified, possibly reflecting limitations of UK Biobank ICD-10 diagnosis data.

Benchmarking showed the case study took 55 minutes using 8 computational cores. The authors note limitations, including reliance on processed medical records and the fact that constructed trajectories may not fully represent real patient trajectories. They recommend using comprehensive representative datasets and treating LUKB DT primarily as a tool for investigating disease risk factors and mechanisms.

David Ellison, whose Paramount Skydance owns CBS News, praised the network while saying he wants to restore trust in media and make CBS News a trusted destination. He avoided specifying needed improvements and denied plans to make it aligned with Trumpworld. His appointment of Bari Weiss as CBS News editor in chief after acquiring The Free Press has raised questions about the network’s direction.

Children with language vulnerabilities may need tailored support for language development. Speech-language therapists often ask educators to reinforce linguistic structures, but producing consistent, varied examples in real time is demanding. Existing game-based language interventions can target morphology, but implementation is challenging, especially outside therapy contexts.

The authors propose using large language models in Robot-Assisted Language Learning to improve adaptability. Their TalBot application combines ChatGPT with the Furhat conversational robot to play an Alias-style word retrieval game with preschool children. In early co-designed tests with 13 children and 7 educators, TalBot managed turn-taking, gave clues and feedback, redirected dialogue, and showed potential in handling mispronunciations and speech recognition errors.

The authors argue that LLM-based robots can address limitations of rule-based RALL systems by generating flexible responses, interpreting varied input, supporting turn-taking, and producing customized linguistic material. They identify morphology learning as a promising application because robots can provide structured, repetitive exposure to target grammatical forms and model language for educators.

Future work will expand TalBot to grammar and morphology interventions through lab studies, preschool field studies, and a feasibility study with children with clinically significant language vulnerabilities. The project will evaluate linguistic output, educator use, child interaction, and user perceptions. Key considerations include data protection, EU AI Act requirements, ethical impacts on children, implementation challenges, cost, and possible resistance in educational settings.

Officials from the Grand Erie District School Board and Brant-Haldimand-Norfolk Catholic District School Board met with coaches and physical education teachers to discuss combining high school sports in Brantford, Haldimand and Norfolk into one league, potentially by 2019-20. Currently, most teams play only within their own county, aside from limited crossover in football. Grand Erie spokesperson Kimberly Newhouse said the goal is to create consistent rules, equitable opportunities and similar numbers of games across public and Catholic schools. No decision or timeline has been confirmed, and future talks are planned. Travel costs and distances, especially for Norfolk teams, are expected to be part of the discussion.

The passage advises young people choosing college options that it is normal not to know their lifelong career path and that choices can change. It emphasizes that technological advances will reshape many industries, citing petrol and diesel engines, electric cars, and fax machines as examples. The author argues that workers should focus on making their skills valuable to employers or customers, using burger sellers and surgeons as contrasting examples. It warns that employers may seek maximum work for minimum reward, so individuals should ensure their contribution is not cheap. It also notes that jobs will not always be enjoyable and that life outside work matters most.

The passage describes AGESA host-environment requirements, UEFI integration, build setup, stack handling, and service procedures. The host must establish a stack before calling stack-dependent procedures and, for binary image builds, implement a call-out router through a single interface portal. The router maps function identifiers to host call-out procedures and uses configuration data containing the standard header.

AGESA UEFI support spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases across 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit execution modes. The SEC phase establishes a C environment, enters 32-bit mode, and sets up a stack using AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK. PEI modules handle processor initialization, memory initialization, and reset coordination, publishing PPIs and HOBs such as AmdInitEarlyPPI, AmdInitPostPPI, Memory Init PPI, and memory information HOBs. The DXE driver performs late initialization, generates tables through AmdInitLate, and publishes AgesaDxeProtocol. The AmdGpuVgaControlDxe driver controls VGA decoding for the processor GPU through PciIo requests.

The build environment uses platform option files, UEFI control files, and environment variables including AGESA_ROOT, AGESA_OptsDir, and the AMD platform solution name. AGESA supports binary module and source integration build methods, with platform-specific customization through <plat>Options.c.

The passage also defines early stack and Cache-As-RAM procedures, including AMD_RESET_ENABLEMENT, AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK, and stack removal routines. These are stackless assembly routines used before main memory is available and must be invoked by the host environment.

Several AGESA service procedures are described, including AmdCreateStruct, AmdReleaseStruct, data eye retrieval, APIC and PCI address lookup, execution cache size query, current core identification, memory address-to-FRU mapping, MMIO range allocation, and event log reading. These procedures generally require a valid stack and may depend on coherent HyperTransport links or other initialization state.

The passage describes design details and documentation information for TPS7H500x-SP controllers. Type 2A frequency compensation was used with a 10-kHz target crossover frequency and 16.2-A/V power stage transconductance; selected compensation components were RCOMP = 40.2 kΩ, CCOMP = 15 nF, and CHF = 47 pF. Output capacitance used seven 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors with equivalent ESR of 0.86 mΩ. Slope compensation is set through the RSC pin, with a 102-kΩ resistor connected to AVSS. The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require at least a 0.1-µF VIN bypass capacitor, with ceramic capacitors placed close to the device. Layout guidance emphasizes separating noisy power paths from sensitive signals, minimizing switch-node and high-current loop areas, separating analog and power grounds, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, routing high-dv/dt traces away from sensitive pins, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS with multiple vias. The passage also lists related TI documentation, update notification guidance, support resources, trademark and ESD cautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, orderable, and disclaimer information.

Scotland will abolish local authority burial and cremation fees for anyone under 18, with the Scottish government providing £500,000 to cover costs. The agreement with Cosla aligns Scotland with England and addresses inconsistent council policies. The Church of Scotland welcomed the move, saying it would reduce financial pressure on bereaved families.

NVIDIA Corporation filed a Form 8-K reporting that Stephen C. Neal was appointed to its Board of Directors on March 30, 2019. In connection with the appointment, he received 1,419 restricted stock units vesting semi-annually over three years, 139 restricted stock units vesting on May 15, 2019, and a prorated annual cash retainer of $10,890. NVIDIA also entered into an indemnity agreement with Mr. Neal.

Cover 2 is a zone coverage with two deep safeties and five underneath defenders in a 4-3 defense: two corners and three linebackers. It is designed to cover short routes while protecting against deep throws, allowing defenders to read receivers and keep eyes on the quarterback. Its strengths include defending quick throws, hitches, slants, screens, outside runs, and perimeter plays because of hard corners near the line of scrimmage. Its weaknesses include multiple deep routes, especially four verticals, trips formations, and certain run looks that leave too few defenders or weak-side support in the box. Standard Cover 2 assigns corners to flat zones, safeties to deep halves, linebackers to hook/curl and middle hole zones. Variations include Cover 2 “Switch” and Cover 2 from a one-high shell.

Emirates Airlines reversed its decision to discontinue the Hindu meal option after negative customer feedback, saying it would continue offering it to help Hindu passengers identify and request the meal.

US non-farm payrolls rose by 200,000 in January, beating forecasts, while average hourly earnings increased 2.9% year-on-year, the fastest pace since 2009. Unemployment stayed at 4.1%. The data strengthened expectations for a March Federal Reserve rate rise and possibly more tightening. Treasury yields climbed after the report, with analysts citing wage growth, tax cuts and planned infrastructure spending as factors that could increase inflation pressure.

The study conducts a co-occurrence analysis of author-supplied keywords from 1,076 Information Systems Education Journal articles published from 2003 to 2024. Using VOSviewer, the authors grouped publications into eras and created term maps based on keyword frequency, link strength, and clusters.

The analysis identifies shifting topics across eras: 2003–2007 focused on IS education, curriculum, assessment, accreditation, ethics, and pedagogy; 2008–2012 emphasized pedagogy and student issues such as mentoring, retention, scholarships, women, and minorities; 2013–2017 highlighted cybersecurity, big data, analytics, pedagogy, programming, and online learning; 2018–2022 reflected COVID-19 impacts, with attention to online learning, attendance, attentiveness, analytics, capstone courses, and cybersecurity; and 2023–2024 centered on artificial intelligence, analytics, and pedagogy. Across the full network, pedagogy and curriculum remained central themes.

The authors note that the study is limited by reliance on author-supplied keywords and possible effects of special issues. Future research may include titles and abstracts and allow the data to define topical eras organically.

The speaker said the team does not need significant changes but must learn from the previous game, improve execution, avoid careless turnovers, and play its own style. They emphasized staying positive, reviewing video, strengthening the forecheck, limiting the goaltender’s involvement, and using physical play to create momentum and energize the crowd.

Leicester City manager Craig Shakespeare said the 4-2 defeat at Everton, his first loss since replacing Claudio Ranieri, would not affect the squad before their Champions League quarter-final against Atletico Madrid. He said Leicester remain resilient and explained his five team changes were due to fixture congestion and squad rotation.
