Shakespeare was more concerned about poor defending from set plays, which led to Everton’s decisive goals. He also confirmed captain Wes Morgan would miss the Madrid match with a back injury.

Dr. Harris L. Rittenberg’s Jacksonville family dental practice has served children and adults for over 50 years. The practice emphasizes personal care, advanced dentistry, continuing education, and quality treatment. Dr. Rittenberg participates in the AACD “Give Back a Smile” program and has welcomed Dr. Brittany Jones.

FERC approved NYISO’s extension of its Automated Mitigation Procedures through April 30, 2002, rather than the requested October 31, 2002, and granted waiver for a November 1, 2001 effective date. NYISO must file a comprehensive mitigation proposal by March 1, 2002, effective May 1, addressing FERC’s concerns about AMP and how NYISO’s mitigation measures work together.

FERC acknowledged NYISO’s planned fixes to limit mitigation to zones and hours failing the impact test and to exempt bids under 50 MW unless market power concerns are shown. FERC also directed NYISO to work with market participants on whether AMP creates barriers for new generation, whether energy-limited resources should be exempted or accommodated, how AMP coordinates with other mitigation measures, and whether must-run mitigation should align with ISO-NE and PJM. FERC encouraged NYISO to collaborate with PJM and ISO-NE toward one Northeast mitigation plan in the RTO process.

Laredo Petroleum Holdings Inc. (NYSE:LPI) shares rose 0.72% in the latest session and last closed at $9.80. Analysts surveyed by Thomson Reuters’ First Call have a 12-month average price target of $13.54, with targets ranging from $9.50 to $17, based on 24 opinions. The stock has an average brokerage recommendation of 2.47 from 15 recommendations. Analyst ratings include 5 Buy, 5 Outperform, 12 Hold, 2 Underperform, and 0 Sell. The company’s ATR-14 is 0.45, weekly volatility is 3.91%, monthly volatility is 3.97%, and RSI is 39.08. Laredo Petroleum has a market capitalization of $2.35 billion, 240.08 million shares outstanding, and recent trading volume of 3.32 million shares versus an average of 2.93 million.

The 5-day low overnight trading strategy trades the S&P 500 when it opens at a 5-day low and closes above its open, entering at the close and exiting at the next day’s open. Overnight S&P 500 trading has historically averaged 0.04% from close to next open, supporting mean reversion strategies. Since 2005, the strategy averaged 0.26% per trade, or 0.17% excluding its largest winner.

Lowe’s will leave NASCAR after 18 seasons, ending its longtime sponsorship of Jimmie Johnson’s No. 48 Hendrick Motorsports team. Johnson said a new sponsor has a “golden opportunity” to close out his Cup career with him. He said he has “a handful of years” left in Cup but plans to keep racing, with possible interests including Le Mans, the Rolex 24 at Daytona and possibly the Indianapolis 500 if IndyCar adopts halos.

Text messaging is widely used for fast communication, but alternative messaging apps offer expanded features. Music Messenger lets users send songs to express moods or messages. WhatsApp provides free smartphone messaging with videos, photos, sound clips, emoticons, personalized backgrounds, and automatic contact integration. Facebook Messenger offers media sharing, HD video chats, sound bites, group chats, no advertising, and customizable emojis and text colors.

New York’s Excelsior Scholarship offers tuition-free SUNY or CUNY attendance to qualifying residents, making cost a major factor for students such as Gianna Ruffle. The program has pushed more students to consider public colleges and created challenges for smaller private colleges. Private institutions are responding with tuition reductions, scholarships, graduation guarantees, internships and other initiatives to emphasize value, though some administrators say expanding existing aid programs would have been fairer. Several private colleges report strong enrollment or continued confidence in their missions, while families continue weighing affordability, fit, programs and potential debt.

The passage describes an image processing method, apparatus, electronic device, and computer-readable storage medium for placing a target model, such as a three-dimensional advertisement, into a video. The method obtains a video with multiple image frames, places a target three-dimensional model on a target plane in a first frame, determines feature-point coordinates on the model surface in both world and pixel coordinate systems, and calculates the pose of the first frame’s camera coordinate system relative to the world coordinate system.

For subsequent frames, the method tracks the target plane, determines homography matrices, calculates corresponding feature-point pixel coordinates, and uses camera intrinsic parameters and feature-point coordinates to determine camera poses for each frame. The target three-dimensional model is then replaced with a target model and projected into each frame according to the calculated camera poses, producing a target video containing the inserted model.

The disclosure also describes using neural network models to identify planes in the first frame, manual or automatic adjustment of the three-dimensional model pose, and examples using a cube as the placement model and a cola can as the advertisement. The stated advantages include reduced calculation, faster processing, convenient operation, high accuracy, no reliance on image feature-point calculation, no requirement for large video parallax, and applicability to more videos.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 27, 2017, announcing its first quarter 2017 financial results. The filing includes Exhibit 99.1, the related press release, and Exhibit 99.2, information regarding non-GAAP financial measures. The report was signed by CFO Brian T. Olsavsky.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated July 26, 2016, reporting that it issued a press release and related data sheet on its financial results for the third fiscal quarter ended June 25, 2016. The filing includes Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2 and was signed by CFO Luca Maestri.

Lotte Group plans to list Malaysian unit Lotte Chemical Titan Holding on Bursa Malaysia in Q3 2017. Sources said the IPO could raise $1 billion to $1.5 billion, potentially one of Malaysia’s biggest in years. Proceeds will fund petrochemical projects in Indonesia and Malaysia. The IPO was previously shelved amid South Korean investigations into alleged fraud at Lotte Group.

The Federal Reserve proposed easing the Volcker Rule, a Dodd-Frank regulation that restricts banks from making risky proprietary trades with depositors’ money. Officials said the changes would apply the strictest requirements to banks with the most trading activity and reduce uncertainty. The move follows broader efforts under President Trump to loosen financial regulations, including a recent law rolling back parts of Dodd-Frank and changes at the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau under Mick Mulvaney. Supporters of the Volcker Rule say weakening it could revive pre-crisis risk-taking, while some banking experts say proprietary trading desks are unlikely to return. Fed leaders Jerome Powell and Randal Quarles have supported improving or overhauling post-crisis rules without fully scrapping them.

The offside trap is a defensive soccer tactic in which all back defenders move upfield together just before a forward pass, attempting to leave attackers in an offside position and win an indirect free kick. It is risky because any defender who fails to move in unison can keep attackers onside, leaving the goalkeeper exposed. Changes to offside interpretation and increased use of short passing have made the tactic less reliable.

Coaches should assess whether their players understand the offside law, can coordinate timing and communication, and whether the benefits outweigh the risks. The trap is more effective against teams using through balls and less effective against quick short-passing teams. A flat-back-four formation supports execution better than a stopper-sweeper system.

Successful use requires a straight defensive line, constant communication, awareness of attackers and passing cues, and one designated defender to call the trap using a clear verbal or non-verbal signal. All defenders must react instantly, sprinting forward together to create clear separation. The tactic must be practiced repeatedly and used carefully, since opponents may recognize, scout, or beat it.

A North Korean missile launched near Sinpo failed almost immediately, with US officials describing it only as medium-range. Weapons expert John Schilling said the failure suggested an early test of a new or underdeveloped missile system, possibly one shown at a Pyongyang parade. Some reports identified it as a KN-17 Scud variant, while officials said details remained unclear. Speculation about US cyber sabotage followed, but Schilling said such claims were likely overstated. Separately, Pentagon chief Jim Mattis ordered a review of the US nuclear deterrent.

In December 2006, SunPower CEO Tom Werner faced questions about the growth of the solar power industry, the durability of SunPower’s advantage in high-efficiency photovoltaic cells, and competition from larger firms and emerging technology companies.

Interest in solar power was driven by energy independence and environmental concerns, especially rising greenhouse gas emissions and CO₂ levels. International policies such as the Kyoto Protocol, carbon trading, renewable portfolio standards, subsidies, rebates, and feed-in tariffs supported demand. In 2006, renewables supplied 13% of global energy needs, while photovoltaic systems supplied only 0.04% of global electricity.

The solar industry was growing rapidly despite electricity from solar power costing more than conventional power. Photovoltaic power grew 41% annually from 2003 to 2006 and was expected to grow 40% annually through 2011. Japan led PV shipments, Europe had overtaken the United States, and China became the third-largest PV cell producer in 2006. Demand was strongest in Europe, especially Germany, and Japan.

The solar value chain included silicon production, ingot and wafer manufacturing, cell manufacturing, module manufacturing, and installation. A silicon shortage raised prices sharply, but new capacity was expected to ease shortages around 2008. Installation costs and subsidies varied widely by region, affecting consumer economics.

Founded in 1987 by Richard Swanson, SunPower shifted from solar concentrator technology to high-efficiency solar cells. A partnership with Cypress Semiconductor in 2001 helped it begin commercial production in 2004, and it went public in 2005. Production rose from about 20 MW in 2005 to an expected 65 MW in 2006, while revenues increased from $6 million in 2004 to a projected $220 million-plus in 2006.

SunPower’s key advantage was producing the highest-efficiency commercial solar cells in 2006, using a back-contact design that improved efficiency and aesthetics. Its process required more steps and higher capital expenditure, but its cells used less silicon per watt and reduced installation costs by producing more power in limited space. SunPower pursued vertical integration through silicon supply agreements, wafer and ingot ventures, module manufacturing, and the acquisition of installer PowerLight.

Competitors included Sharp Solar, Q-Cells, REC Group, First Solar, SunTech, and Citizenre. SunPower’s strategic challenge was whether to focus on module pricing, process improvements, or a combination to sustain its competitive position in a fast-growing and evolving industry.
The speaker grew up with Brick Hockey Club, admired Jim Dowd’s work ethic, described an exciting game, aims to reach the NHL, and chose New Hampshire over Michigan, partly to stay close to home.

Gary Gensler introduces three lectures on the technical foundations of blockchain through Bitcoin, emphasizing that understanding the technology’s inner workings helps evaluate its uses. The session focuses on Bitcoin’s design features: cryptographic hash functions, timestamped append-only logs, block headers, Merkle trees, asymmetric cryptography, digital signatures, Bitcoin addresses, and transaction structure.

He reviews concepts from the previous class: money as a social and economic consensus mechanism, fiat currency instability, ledgers as records of transactions or balances, and Bitcoin’s goal of peer-to-peer money without a central authority. Bitcoin is described as a timestamped append-only database made of blocks, secured by hash functions and digital signatures, with consensus determining who may add data.

Key blockchain components discussed include proof of work, miners, nodes, nonces, peer-to-peer networking, native currency incentives, and transaction inputs and outputs. Bitcoin has about 10,000 nodes globally, a finite supply limit of 21 million bitcoins, about 17 million existing at the time, and mining rewards then at 12.5 bitcoins per block.

Gensler explains hash functions as deterministic, efficient mappings from inputs of any size to fixed-size outputs, used as data fingerprints. Cryptographic hash functions are described as one-way, collision resistant, avalanche-like, and puzzle friendly, though not impossible to break. Bitcoin uses SHA-256 in block headers and Merkle trees, while Bitcoin addresses use additional hashing.

Block headers contain the version, previous block hash, Merkle Root, timestamp, difficulty target, and nonce. Merkle trees compress many transactions into a single root hash while allowing later verification. Timestamps are used, though block ordering and previous block hashes are especially important.

The lecture also covers asymmetric cryptography: public and private key pairs, digital signatures, and verification. A private key signs a message, and a public key verifies it; secure random number generation is important for key creation. Bitcoin addresses are derived from public keys through hashing and encoding, making them related to but distinct from public keys.

Gensler concludes that blockchain technology can be understood through three main areas: cryptography, consensus mechanisms, and transactions. Upcoming lectures will address proof-of-work consensus, nodes, native currency, and transaction scripting.

Andrew Lo introduces equity as ownership in a corporation that provides value through dividends and capital gains. He contrasts equities with bonds, emphasizing that equity holders are residual claimants with unlimited upside but limited liability, which supports entrepreneurship, innovation, public capital formation, and investor participation through voting rights and public markets. He also explains that short selling improves market efficiency by allowing negative information to enter prices.

Lo distinguishes primary markets, where securities are first issued, from secondary markets, where existing securities trade. He notes that IPO activity is cyclical and tied to business and credit cycles, while secondary-market trading volume has grown significantly due to technologies such as internet trading, electronic communications networks, electronic order routing, and electronic trading.

The lecture then develops the dividend discount model, valuing stock as the present value of expected future dividends discounted at risk-adjusted rates. Lo stresses that both dividends and discount rates are uncertain, and that discount rates should reflect the risk of the specific cash flows and market conditions. He explains that the market determines appropriate rates of return, not the company itself.

Simplified cases include a constant-dividend perpetuity, where price equals dividends divided by the discount rate, and the Gordon growth model, where price equals dividends divided by the discount rate minus growth. Lo uses this to show how growth expectations can strongly affect stock prices and how the required return can be viewed as dividend yield plus expected growth. He notes that dividends are often stable because firms avoid cutting them, though temporary suspensions or extraordinary dividends can occur under special circumstances.

This protocol describes a systematic review of how Rapid Response Team (RRT) services are implemented or redesigned, why changes occur, the time frames involved, and how success is measured. The review will include prospective and retrospective observational cohort studies of healthcare systems introducing or modifying RRT services, with no restrictions on publication status, language, or year, except studies that cannot be translated into English.

Searches will be conducted in Medline, CINAHL, Embase, The Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, reference lists, conference abstracts, and through expert contact. Study selection and data extraction will be performed independently and in duplicate using COVIDENCE and a designed spreadsheet. Extracted data will cover study characteristics, team characteristics, implementation methods, and outcome assessments. Risk of bias will be assessed using the JBI critical appraisal checklist.

The primary outcome is to describe methods of RRT implementation or redesign. Secondary outcomes include reasons for change, implementation time frames, and outcome measures. Analysis will be mainly narrative, with simple statistics on implementation methods. No ethical approval is required because only published studies will be reviewed. Results are intended for presentation at scientific meetings and publication in a peer-reviewed journal. The review has no external funding.

Asia-Pacific equities rose in April on improved risk appetite, supported by French election results, easing North Korea concerns and strong Asian earnings. MSCI’s ex-Japan index neared a two-year high. Indian stocks led 2017 gains, while China lagged; New Zealand and India had the highest valuations.

The ADS868xW devices have ≥1MΩ resistive analog input impedance independent of sampling or input frequency, allowing direct connection of many sensors without low-impedance drivers. Matching source impedance between AIN_P and AIN_M helps maintain dc accuracy. Each analog input includes internal overvoltage protection; with AVDD = 5V, the circuit withstands up to ±20V, and with AVDD floating, protection is limited to ±15V. External protection is still required for surge, ESD, and EFT events.

The analog front end includes a programmable gain amplifier, second-order antialiasing low-pass filter with a typical 500kHz cutoff, and integrated ADC driver. The PGA supports multiple bipolar and unipolar input ranges selected through RANGE_SEL bits and uses trimmed resistor networks to reduce gain error. The device supports internal or external 4.096V references through the REFIO pin and internal buffer, with specified decoupling requirements for REFIO and REFCAP.

The ADC outputs straight-binary data for single-ended and differential inputs. Alarm features include programmable input high and low alarms with hysteresis, and fixed AVDD alarms at typical thresholds of 4.7V and 5.3V. Alarm flags can be read through the ALARM pin, internal registers, or appended to output data.

The device uses a multiSPI interface supporting standard SPI, dual-SDO, source-synchronous, and daisy-chain configurations. It has RESET, ACQ, and CONV functional states controlled by RST and CONVST/CS. Data frames begin on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and end on the rising edge, with 32-bit command and output shift-register operation. Nine configuration registers control device ID, reset and power modes, serial protocols, output data, input range and reference selection, and alarm thresholds.

Application guidance describes using ADS868xW in industrial analog input modules with a multiplexer for voltage, current, or temperature sensing. The device supports NAP and power-down modes for reduced power consumption. Power-supply and PCB layout recommendations include separate AVDD and DVDD decoupling, close placement of reference capacitors, partitioning analog and digital sections, and keeping analog and reference signals away from digital noise.

Enron replaced CFO Andrew Fastow with Jeff McMahon, head of its industrial markets group and former treasurer, after investor concerns over Fastow’s role in LJM partnerships that conducted transactions with Enron. Chairman and CEO Kenneth Lay said the move was needed to restore investor confidence, though he had defended Fastow a day earlier. Fastow took a leave of absence.

The Securities and Exchange Commission had begun an informal inquiry into the Fastow-related partnership transactions. Enron said it had done nothing wrong and that business operations were normal, but analysts criticized the company’s lack of transparency, complex financial structure, off-balance-sheet vehicles, and limited disclosure during a conference call.

Enron’s shares fell sharply, closing at $16.41 on Oct. 24, down 17% for the day and roughly half from Oct. 16, after a third-quarter report included major charges and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity tied to unwinding partnership-related arrangements. Several analysts downgraded the stock, including Prudential’s Carol Coale, who issued a “sell” recommendation. Concerns also affected other energy-trading and utility stocks.

Multiple reports noted that McMahon had previously raised concerns about Fastow’s partnership role. Shareholder lawsuits alleged Enron misled investors about overvalued assets, off-balance-sheet deals, and related-party transactions.

Air cargo containerization transports goods by air without unloading and reloading between locations, using custom containers and ground handling equipment. Passenger aircraft carry containers on lower decks, while cargo aircraft use both lower and upper decks. Market growth is driven by demand for faster global goods transport and lightweight containers that meet IATA load requirements and withstand rough handling. Constraints include global economic slowdown and rising aviation fuel costs, which reduce cargo aircraft flying hours. Future opportunities are linked to increasing commercial cargo aircraft and rising defense demand for rapid military equipment transport. The market is segmented by container type, end user, aircraft type, and geography. Key vendors include Nordisk Aviation Products, Zodiac Aerospace, VRR Aviation, Satco, Cargo Composites, Granger Aerospace, Chicago Metal Fabricators, PalNet GmbH Air Cargo Products, ACL Airshop, and DoKaSch Temperature Solutions.

The passage argues that Chinese family education has overemphasized grades, discipline, and examination success while neglecting children’s moral development, independence, emotional health, interests, and ability to function in society. It criticizes overindulgence under the one-child policy and cites problems such as poor life skills, emotional disorders, weak adaptability, and extreme responses to adversity.

It proposes improving family education by liberating children’s individuality, guiding them to find personal interests, teaching them to give and contribute to society, encouraging contact with nature, and prioritizing moral behavior over academic achievement. The passage highlights traditional Chinese moral education, parent-child communication through shared activities, manual labor and sports, religious or faith-based values, and the role of mothers and parents as children’s first educators. It concludes that modern China should combine moral and humanity education with traditional moral resources to improve family education.

Microsoft’s Cortana, introduced as a Siri-like voice assistant, has expanded from Windows Phone to Windows 10 desktops, laptops, and tablets. It works with the Edge browser, helps search files on hard drives and in the cloud, and can be activated by dedicated buttons on some devices. Cortana is also becoming available on Android and iOS, though less efficiently than on Windows. It includes voice recognition, humor features, and location-based reminders.

A geoarchaeological study of Karnak Temple near Luxor analyzed 61 sediment cores and tens of thousands of ceramic fragments to reconstruct the site’s landscape over 3,000 years. Researchers found the area was likely unsuitable for permanent occupation before about 2520 BCE due to Nile flooding, placing earliest occupation in the Old Kingdom. Karnak began on an island formed by Nile channels, which later silted and diverged, allowing expansion. The study suggests the temple’s location may have reflected Egyptian creation myths of high ground emerging from surrounding waters.

The speaker praised the team’s mental toughness, composure, and discipline in a difficult game, noting they generated more around the net and scored on a rebound. He highlighted a player’s strong overtime effort while playing extended minutes due to lineup changes. He said Tony Lydman chose to play after consulting trainers, another player has a charley horse, and one remains in protocol. The speaker emphasized taking the series game by game, said special teams have been strong, and stressed the need to improve five-on-five play. He declined to revisit prior comments, saying it was game day.

The passage reviews the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card, highlighting its 0% intro APR for 21 months from account opening on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a variable APR of 16.99%, 23.49%, or 28.74%. It has no annual fee and offers up to $600 in cellphone protection for theft or damage when the monthly bill is paid with the card, subject to a $25 deductible. The card is recommended for people looking to pay down debt or finance a large purchase without interest. Drawbacks include no ongoing rewards after the intro period, a 5% balance transfer fee with a $5 minimum, and a 3% foreign transaction fee. Applicants are advised that a good to excellent credit score is recommended, but approval is not guaranteed.

Former Ford CEO Mark Fields said US automakers overestimated EV demand and expanded capacity without enough focus on what would persuade consumers to buy. He said the EV market has not developed as expected, turning some automakers’ broad EV lineups into a burden. GM cited slower EV adoption after federal incentives ended and took a $1.6 billion charge to realign EV capacity. Industry leaders differ on the impact of subsidy rollbacks, with Ford CEO Jim Farley predicting a smaller market while former Tesla president Jon McNeill said EV sales can keep growing without subsidies.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K reporting that on March 26, 2020, it entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC to issue $5.0 billion of unsecured senior notes: $1.5 billion of 2.850% notes due 2030, $1.0 billion of 3.500% notes due 2040, $2.0 billion of 3.500% notes due 2050, and $0.5 billion of 3.700% notes due 2060. Net proceeds were approximately $4.97 billion, intended for general corporate purposes, including possible debt repayment. The notes are governed by a 2016 indenture with Wells Fargo Bank, supplemented by a March 31, 2020 Officers’ Certificate, with interest payable April 1 and October 1 beginning October 1, 2020. The filing also describes redemption terms, covenants, default provisions, change-of-control repurchase obligations, and related exhibits.

The speaker says he had many scoring chances, including two early opportunities, but failed to capitalize and must move on. He notes playoff hockey can limit chances, requiring discipline, hard work, and different players stepping up. He says the opponent worked hard, was fast, surrounded the puck well, and benefited from a bounce. He feels his game is improving after uneven playoff performances. He praises Dave as an experienced goal scorer, defensive contributor, leader, and hard worker. He emphasizes making defensemen work by playing below the circles and cycling the puck more effectively.

The article tests trend following and momentum strategies on BTC-USD using Yahoo Finance data from 2015 to April 2021, excluding commissions, slippage, and taxes. It finds that simple moving average strategies can outperform buy-and-hold while reducing drawdowns. A 100-day/250-day moving average strategy produced three trades, a 115% CAGR, and a 65% max drawdown. A 25-day momentum strategy also beat buy-and-hold with lower drawdown. The article concludes that Bitcoin’s volatility makes trend following and momentum strategies potentially effective, though future performance is not guaranteed.

The passage describes programming and application guidance for TPS7H500x-SP radiation-hardness-assured peak current mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. Output voltage is set with a VOUT-to-VSENSE resistor divider referenced to 0.613 V, and soft start is controlled by a capacitor on SS. Switching frequency can be set by an RT resistor, external synchronization through SYNC, or primary-secondary synchronization between two controllers. Internal oscillator operation supports 100 kHz to 2 MHz switching, while SYNC operates at twice the switching frequency.

The controllers provide primary outputs OUTA/OUTB and optional synchronous rectifier outputs SRA/SRB, with external gate drivers recommended due to roughly 150-mA peak output capability. Dead time, leading-edge blanking, duty-cycle limits, current sensing, hiccup-mode overcurrent response, FAULT shutdown, slope compensation, and Type 2A/2B frequency compensation are described. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C typical and restarts below 160°C typical.

Application guidance covers a TPS7H5001-SP synchronous push-pull GaN converter example, including selection of RT, feedback resistors, dead time, blanking time, soft-start capacitor, transformer, FETs, clamp, output inductor and capacitance, current sense resistor, hiccup capacitor, compensation, and slope compensation. Power supply and layout recommendations emphasize regulated 4-V to 14-V input, close bypassing, minimized high-current and high-dv/dt loops, separated analog and power grounds, careful routing of noise-sensitive signals, and package-specific layout considerations. The passage also lists related documentation, revision history, mechanical and orderable information, and TI disclaimers.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting results of its December 13, 2022 Annual Shareholders Meeting. Of 7,456,502,484 shares entitled to vote, 6,407,164,715 were voted in person or by proxy. Shareholders re-elected all 12 director nominees, approved advisory executive compensation, and ratified Deloitte & Touche LLP as independent auditor for fiscal 2023. Six shareholder proposals—covering diversity and inclusion analysis, hiring of persons with arrest or incarceration records, retirement fund investments related to climate change, government use of Microsoft technology, military product development, and tax transparency—were not approved.

UC San Diego engineers developed proof-of-concept ultrasound-powered nanorobots that swim through blood to remove bacteria and toxins. The robots are gold nanowires coated with hybrid platelet and red blood cell membranes: platelets bind pathogens such as MRSA, while red blood cells absorb and neutralize bacterial toxins. Ultrasound propulsion lets them move without chemical fuel and mix efficiently with targets. The membrane coating also helps prevent biofouling. In tests on MRSA-contaminated blood samples, five minutes of treatment left three times less bacteria and toxins than untreated samples. The work, published in Science Robotics, is at an early stage, with future plans including live animal tests and biodegradable materials.

The Minnesota Timberwolves host the NBA-best Houston Rockets on Sunday, with both teams playing the second night of back-to-backs. Minnesota is sixth in the Western Conference at 40-30, narrowly ahead of New Orleans, Denver and the Clippers, and is 4-4 since Jimmy Butler’s knee surgery. Karl-Anthony Towns has averaged 25.5 points over his last six games, while Andrew Wiggins has averaged 20.1.

Houston is 55-14 and leads Golden State by 2 1/2 games for the West’s top seed. The Rockets have beaten Minnesota three times this season, each by 18 points, and have won five straight and 17 of the last 19 meetings overall. Houston is 28-3 since Jan. 6 and 21-1 in its last 22 games after beating New Orleans 107-101 behind James Harden’s 32 points.

The speaker says the team had a strong game despite early penalties but is only halfway done and expects Jersey to respond hard. They emphasize limiting top scorers, taking away space, and using strong back pressure from forwards to help defenders stand up at the blue line.

Stifel downgraded GrubHub from Buy to Hold while raising its price target to $110, citing a balanced risk-reward profile after the stock’s more than 200% yearly gain. Analyst John Egbert noted benefits from the Yum! Brands partnership and expansion, but said valuation is elevated. Shares fell 1.6% Monday morning.

In Oxley et al. v. Oldden, the court discharged a rule to show cause seeking to strike off a reference because the referees had already examined the evidence, agreed on their report, and faced no allegations of misconduct, partiality, or improper refusal to hear testimony.

Brett Veach will lead his first NFL draft as Kansas City Chiefs general manager after taking over last summer. The Chiefs lack a first-round pick but have one second-round and two third-round selections, with needs especially on defense. Veach has already made several trades involving picks, including deals for Reggie Ragland, Cam Erving and Kendall Fuller, and trading away Alex Smith and Marcus Peters. He said he tends to be aggressive, though staff may temper that approach. Kansas City is expected to target pass rushers or cornerbacks early, while also considering offensive help for new starting quarterback Patrick Mahomes II. Local prospects Dorance Armstrong and D.J. Reed could fit. Recent Chiefs drafts produced Pro Bowlers Marcus Peters, Tyreek Hill and Kareem Hunt, along with Mahomes and Chris Jones, but also defensive misses such as KeiVarae Russell and Tanoh Kpassagnon.

Kickers are specialized football players responsible for extra points, field goals, kickoffs, and situational kicks such as onside kicks. Their role is pressure-filled because missed kicks can affect close games, while successful kicks can decide outcomes. NFL kickers are expected to make about 80% of field goals and 90% of extra points. They also help special teams through touchbacks, directional kickoffs, and recoverable onside kicks. Kickers are typically smaller, slim athletes with accuracy, lower-body power, consistent technique, and flexibility. Notable kickers include Justin Tucker, Morten Andersen, and Adam Vinatieri. A reliable kicker influences coaching decisions, reduces pressure on the offense and defense, and can be crucial in winning tight games.

The Nobel Prizes, first awarded in 1901 from Alfred Nobel’s fortune, have become the most recognized scientific honors, celebrating discoveries in physiology or medicine, chemistry and physics. Katalin Karikó’s 2023 physiology or medicine prize for mRNA work highlighted both the prestige of the awards and their limitations. The prizes recognize discoveries rather than people, are chosen through a nearly yearlong nomination and review process, and can be shared by no more than three individuals, leaving many contributors unrecognized.

Many scientists and fields fall outside Nobel recognition. Areas such as ecology, ocean science, climate, weather and geology do not fit easily into the existing categories. Winners have historically been mostly white men from wealthy regions such as the United States and Western Europe, where science has long been well funded. Women and people of color face barriers that can limit access to the types of research settings associated with Nobel-winning work.

Despite these limits, scientists quoted in the passage say the prizes remain important because they draw public attention to scientific discovery and its effects on society.

The passage describes patent priority and incorporated references for technology using deep learning to classify splice sites and detect aberrant splicing in genomic sequences. It covers machine learning, neural networks, convolutional neural networks, dilated/atrous convolutions, residual and skip connections, batch normalization, pooling, global average pooling, training methods, and genomics applications.

The disclosed technology trains atrous convolutional neural networks (ACNNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to identify donor splice sites, acceptor splice sites, and non-splicing sites in nucleotide sequences. Training examples include donor splice sites, acceptor splice sites, and non-splicing sites, with target nucleotides flanked by contextual nucleotides. Inputs may be one-hot encoded, and outputs are triplet scores indicating the likelihood of each nucleotide belonging to one of the three classes. Scores may be normalized and used for classification.

The ACNN implementations use dilated convolutions to capture long-range sequence context with fewer parameters. Architectures include groups of residual blocks, skip connections, batch normalization, ReLU layers, and atrous convolution layers. Example models include SpliceNet80, SpliceNet400, SpliceNet2000, and SpliceNet10000, which differ in context length, number of residual block groups, convolution window sizes, and atrous convolution rates.

The passage also describes systems and methods for detecting aberrant splicing by processing reference and variant sequences through a trained ACNN or CNN. The system compares splice site scores between aligned reference and variant target sequences, position by position or row by row, and classifies variants as causing aberrant splicing and therefore pathogenic when score differences exceed a threshold. Thresholds may be selected using benign common variants and pathogenic rare variants. The technology may be implemented on training servers and production servers using processors, memory, and non-transitory computer-readable storage media.

VentureWire’s May 31, 2001 newsletter reported major venture funding and private equity news, including Insight Capital Partners closing a $740 million fourth fund, Rho Ventures closing a $435 million fourth fund, MMC Capital closing a $250 million technology fund, and Quake Technologies raising a $30 million second round. Whitney & Co. planned to spin off its Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London offices after closing its fifth fund below target.

New financing included rounds for Arexis, SpeedGreetings, Tools for Health, Remedyne, Fractus, OmniSonics Medical Technologies, Xtime, Neurotech, Atherotech, Spirian Technologies, and E Ink. PaperExchange closed its European operations. Reported deals included Softbank and Scientia Health Group forming Scientia Japan, Eqvitec Partners and IT Provider forming an alliance, and Incyte collaborating with Iconix on a chemogenomic product.

M&A activity included Bertelsmann acquiring MyPlay, TMP Worldwide acquiring FlipDog.com, UsherPro merging with Season Ticket Networks, BuildOnline acquiring iScraper Germany, Metavante acquiring CyberBills, Outtask acquiring Upright Software, CableNet acquiring wireConnect assets, and Catenas acquiring a minority stake in Endero. The newsletter also covered new board appointments and executive hires at several companies, including Enanta, Polexis, and Ardent Pharmaceuticals.

North Carolina regulators are considering whether to test backyard garden vegetables near Chemours’ Fayetteville plant for GenX and related chemicals after Dutch researchers found such compounds in some vegetables near a Chemours factory in the Netherlands. State officials said discussions are ongoing and were prompted by residents’ concerns about health risks from plants, fish and venison. Fish test results from waterways near both plants are expected within months. GenX, used since 2009 as a replacement for PFOA, has shown toxic effects in animals, but its effects in humans are unknown and there are no federal health standards. GenX has also been detected in drinking water downstream in Wilmington.

Backtests of the higher highs and higher lows pattern across SPY, GLD, and TLT found weak short-term returns after two consecutive daily bars with the pattern. SPY and GLD showed poor gains versus random periods, while TLT had negative short-term returns. Increasing to three or four consecutive days did not improve results. The pattern appears to be a short-term reversal signal but is not strong enough alone for long or short trading strategies.

The study develops a machine-learning framework to predict ionic dielectric tensors in oxides by separately modeling Born effective charge tensors with an equivariant graph neural network and phonon properties with a pretrained machine-learning potential, then analytically combining them. The approach improves prediction accuracy over direct dielectric-tensor models, achieving an average R² of 0.843 for ionic dielectric tensors versus 0.418 for the direct model.

Using this framework, the authors screened 8,717 nonmetallic, nonmagnetic oxides from the Materials Project database. After stability checks, dielectric prediction, band-gap filtering, and first-principles validation, they identified 38 previously unknown high-κ oxide candidates with high figures of merit. Twelve exceeded the best-performing training-set oxide, KTaO₃. Ten identified oxides have reported experimental synthesis, and five have reported high experimental dielectric constants consistent with predictions.

The analysis shows that high dielectric response in the candidates is dominated by ionic contributions, typically exceeding 90% of the total dielectric constant. Most candidates contain transition metals with empty d orbitals and oxygen octahedral networks, including perovskite-related, pyrochlore, ReO₃, and Aurivillius-derived structures. The authors conclude that factorizing complex properties into fundamental components can improve machine-learning prediction and virtual screening of high-κ materials.

The speaker says the team is focused on its own preparation rather than the opponent’s injured players and is ready for the next game after gaining elimination-game experience. Practice was light after a long flight, meant only to loosen up. The team wanted injured teammate Nathan Horton included on the trip and honored him by bringing his equipment and hanging his sweater in his stall. The speaker emphasizes balancing relaxation with focus, saying this approach has helped the group handle pressure. He praises veteran leadership, especially from the captain and assistants, and says the team has created a positive dressing-room atmosphere. He adds that the team has discussed what it must change from its previous road games and is prepared to adjust its play.

“Dancing with the Stars” Season 34 entered Episode 3, “TikTok Night,” with 12 celebrity contestants remaining after a Week 2 double elimination sent home Corey Feldman with Jenna Johnson and Baron Davis with Britt Stewart. Jordan Chiles is the only athlete still competing. The passage also explains that judges Derek Hough, Carrie Ann Inaba and Bruno Tonioli score couples out of 30, with judges’ scores and public votes converted into percentages and combined equally. Viewers can vote during the live ET/CT broadcast online, through Disney+, or by text, with up to 10 votes per couple per method.

University of Edinburgh researchers identified 287 independent genetic signals linked to male pattern baldness in DNA from more than 52,000 mostly middle-aged men in the UK BioBank study. Forty of the signals were on the X chromosome, inherited from mothers, while the rest were spread across the genome. The team developed a genetic formula that was somewhat predictive of hair loss risk, but said it is still far from accurately predicting an individual’s hair loss pattern or enabling a blood test. The findings may help identify men at higher risk and potential genetic targets for intervention.

The passage describes the NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the NVIDIA Ampere architecture, as a data center and cloud GPU designed for AI, HPC, and data analytics. It introduces third-generation Tensor Cores supporting TF32, FP64, BF16, FP16, INT8, INT4, and binary formats, with sparsity features that can double Tensor Core throughput. Compared with Tesla V100, A100 offers higher performance, 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, improved cache controls, compute data compression, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, and CUDA 11 support.

A100 includes Multi-Instance GPU technology, allowing one GPU to be partitioned into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory resources for predictable performance, QoS, and fault isolation. It also supports third-generation NVLink with 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, NVIDIA Magnum IO, and Mellanox InfiniBand and Ethernet solutions for scaling multi-GPU and multi-node systems.

The passage also covers A100 architecture details, including GA100 GPU organization, improved error and fault detection, NVJPG decode, optical flow acceleration, NVDEC improvements, and atomic operation enhancements. CUDA advances include task graph acceleration, L2 cache residency control, cooperative groups, and warp-wide reductions. The NVIDIA DGX A100 system uses eight A100 GPUs, delivers up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, supports up to 56 GPU Instances through MIG, and is positioned as a scalable platform for enterprise AI infrastructure.

Sanergy, founded by MIT Sloan students David Auerbach, Lindsay Stradley, and Ani Vallabhaneni, provides sanitation solutions in Nairobi slums through Fresh Life toilets and converts collected waste into products such as Evergrow fertilizer under Farm Star. In 2015, communications manager Medora Brown was tasked with creating a social media strategy despite limited resources, diverse audiences, and executive questions about ROI.

Nairobi slums faced severe sanitation problems, including limited plumbing, unsafe public toilets, poor latrines, and “flying toilets.” Sanergy’s model covered the sanitation value chain: franchised hygienic toilets, daily waste collection, and processing waste into fertilizer. By 2015, Fresh Life had 615 toilets serving about 32,000 people, with ambitious growth goals for 2016 and 2020. Farm Star sold 118 tons of fertilizer in 2015 and aimed for major expansion.

Kenya’s internet, mobile phone, and social media use were growing, but usage varied by audience. Farmers were increasingly active on Facebook and WhatsApp, while slum dwellers and Fresh Life franchisees used social media less often. Fresh Life relied mainly on personal contact, events, SMS, and local trust-building. Farm Star began using Facebook and WhatsApp to generate leads and support consultative selling. Sanergy corporate used blogs, email, and speaking engagements to reach funders, though leaders questioned whether social media could attract major donors.

Brown needed to decide which platforms to prioritize, how to adapt content across brands, and how to measure whether social media could support sales, engagement, fundraising, and business goals in Kenya’s trust-based culture.

U.S. mortgage applications fell 0.8% to 403.6 in the week ended March 24, declining for a second week despite lower borrowing costs, MBA data showed. The average 30-year fixed conforming mortgage rate dropped to 4.33% from 4.46%. Refinance applications fell 2.9%, and their share declined to 44.0%, the lowest since October 2008. Purchase applications rose 1.2%. Treasury yields and mortgage rates fell amid doubts over U.S. tax cuts and infrastructure spending after the healthcare bill was shelved.

Mercy University’s School of Education has strengthened educator preparation through several grants supporting diversity, mentoring, curriculum innovation, STEM education, and preparation for diverse learners. The five-year $2.8 million GRAD-PRO grant supports Hispanic and other underserved graduate students through academic and career alignment, scholarships, faculty mentoring, and programs in health sciences, education, business, and mentoring. The BranchED grant supports teacher preparation at Mercy as a Minority Serving Institution through district partnerships, curriculum review, coaching, professional learning, and collaboration with PK-12 partners. The NSF-funded MISTI program prepares math and science teachers for high-need middle and high schools through coursework, school observations, social justice seminars, student teaching, mentoring, certification support, and early-career support. The NSF STEM Master Teaching Fellowship supported 14 PK-12 STEM teachers in high-need districts through graduate coursework, leadership projects, professional development, and community-based STEM initiatives. The NYSED-funded CR-ITI/ESOL program prepares teachers for ESOL certification in response to shortages in New York City, combining clinical practice, mentoring, coursework, professional development, and school partnerships. Together, these grants advance program improvement, educator readiness, mentoring, collaboration, and support for diverse PK-12 students.

The speaker credits teammates for strong defensive play and says their focus helped secure two successful games. They emphasize not getting caught up in individual achievements, staying focused in tight games, and recognizing that one shot or save can affect the series. The team has momentum but expects a major challenge in Anaheim, where opponents will be excited to respond in their first Stanley Cup Finals home game.

A CORAF report on the SRI-WAAPP project found that the System of Rice Intensification increased rice yields and farmer incomes across West Africa. The three-year project involved more than 50,000 farmers, over 1,000 sites, and 13 countries, and was coordinated by Mali’s National Center of Specialization on Rice with Cornell University through WAAPP. SRI reduces input needs while raising yields and can be adapted to local farming conditions. The report estimated that SRI produced over 20,000 additional tons of milled rice in 2015–2016, worth about US$10 million, and that full adoption in 2017 could have eliminated rice imports. Independent evaluation found yield increases of 54 percent, 65 percent, and 153 percent across irrigated, rainfed lowland, and rainfed upland systems, with farmer incomes rising 41 percent on average. The report recommends scaling SRI while adapting it locally, noting concerns about labor demands, especially for women. The project also encouraged regional collaboration and innovation sharing.

Retired civil litigator Marcel Strigberger describes decluttering his home by discarding law school books he bought more than 50 years ago at McGill. He recalls memorable cases and concepts from books on contracts, property and shipping law, but decides they are no longer useful after decades of practice. He recycles the books, though later notes one property law volume may have had resale value. He keeps one thick book because it works well as a reading stand.

Education Minister Mailis Reps signed a directive to create state-run upper secondary schools in Viimsi and Rapla, opening Sept. 1 next year, and began hiring leaders as building projects enter detailed design.

Investigators said they still had no clear motive five days after Stephen Paddock killed 58 people and wounded hundreds at a Las Vegas music festival before taking his own life. Authorities reviewed many leads, including his politics, finances, social behavior, possible radicalization, mental health, medications, recent contacts with prostitutes, cruises abroad and a cryptic note found in his hotel room. The FBI planned billboards seeking public tips. Officials said casino video suggests Paddock had no accomplice, but they want to know whether anyone knew of his plans. Investigators said he meticulously planned the attack, stockpiling guns and ammunition, modifying some weapons, setting up cameras and booking rooms overlooking other music festivals. His girlfriend, Marilou Danley, said she had no knowledge of his plans and noticed no signs he might become violent.

System Management Arts moved under Rule 54(b) to revise a prior decision denying partial summary judgment against Avesta and David Zager, citing newly discovered evidence allegedly showing that witness Igor Klener could not corroborate Avesta’s claims that Morgan Stanley’s “Delphi” software was prior art. The court held the motion was procedurally proper but denied it on the merits. It found that alleged bias from Klener’s Avesta stock investment opportunity and relationships with Avesta executives did not make his declaration insufficient as corroborating evidence as a matter of law. Credibility, bias, and the weight of his testimony were issues for the jury, and the new evidence did not eliminate genuine factual disputes over the prior art defense.

The passage presents a systematic literature review on robotic coding in science education, focusing on studies published between 2015 and 2022. It frames robotic coding as a STEM-related educational approach connected to 21st-century skills, including problem-solving, communication, computational thinking, scientific creativity, and technology literacy.

The study used Web of Science and Scopus databases, applying inclusion criteria such as English-language, peer-reviewed, empirical articles related to robotic coding in science education and published after 2015. From 74 initially identified studies, 15 articles were included after screening and quality appraisal. Data were analyzed through content analysis, with support from a measurement and evaluation specialist and a robotic coding field expert.

The reviewed studies mainly focused on cognitive skills, especially 21st-century skills and computational thinking skills. Other studies examined robotic coding applications, particularly integration into science and engineering and the use of tools such as Arduino and tablets. A smaller group addressed affective variables, including interest, motivation, and opinions.

The recommendations in the reviewed studies mostly concerned classroom applications and future research. Common suggestions included integrating robotic coding into STEM fields, subjects, educational environments, and teacher training; using robotic coding at different learning levels; conducting larger-scale and deeper studies; using different data collection tools; examining gender; and exploring different robotic coding programs.

The passage concludes that future research should address broader 21st-century skills, additional STEM-related skills, different coding tools, affective and psychomotor characteristics, curriculum development, and teacher in-service training. The review is limited to 15 full-text articles from Web of Science and Scopus published between 2015 and 2022.

The author contrasts machine translation’s practical usefulness with its lack of focus on understanding, citing Warren Weaver’s 1947 “decoding” view and introducing experiments to examine whether high-quality translation requires attention to meaning.

1515 Broadway Associates and Equitable moved to dismiss appeals by New York City and New York State from an order confirming 1515 Broadway’s Chapter 11 reorganization plan, arguing the appeals were moot because the plan had been consummated and no stay was obtained. The court held that failure to obtain a stay does not automatically moot all bankruptcy appeals; each claim must be assessed based on whether effective relief remains possible without disrupting the reorganization.

The court found moot the City’s challenge to the restructuring of 1515 Broadway’s partnership interests because that restructuring was central to the confirmed plan and could not be altered without affecting the reorganization. However, the City’s challenge regarding possible future foreclosure or sale of the building was not moot because no such transaction had yet occurred. The State’s appeal concerning possible New York Gains Tax liability was also not moot, particularly in light of intervening Second Circuit authority holding that the Gains Tax is not exempt as a stamp or similar tax under 11 U.S.C. § 1146(c). The motion to dismiss was therefore granted in part and denied in part.

The passage discusses software engineering, requirements engineering, and the distinction between functional and non-functional requirements. It reviews document classification methods including K-NN, Naïve Bayes, decision trees, and SVM, and summarizes related work on non-functional requirements generation, prioritization, estimation, analysis, and reuse. The proposed methodology identifies potential non-functional requirements using clustering, semantic similarity measures, Normalized Google Distance, average linkage, and a decision tree classifier. The implementation classifies null and non-null functions from an IVR dataset using an NFR matrix combined with a decision tree. Results report higher accuracy and lower execution time than the existing method using only an NFR matrix.

The Charlottesville protests highlighted how people online can participate by identifying demonstrators through social media. The Twitter account @YesYoureRacist gained 271,000 followers over the weekend while working to identify participants in the torch-lit rally associated with racist, Nazi, KKK, and other hate-group messages. The account helped identify several attendees, including Cole White, who was fired from Top Dog in Berkeley after his photo was posted. It also identified Peter Cvjetanovic, who defended promoting “white European culture” but later objected to being labeled “angry torch guy,” and James Allsup, a Washington State University student whose social media posts encouraged others to attend. The account was credited on Good Morning America for identifying men in widely circulated photos and for finding an image of the man who drove into protesters.

PML-N leader Dr Rana Muhammad Tariq Khan addressed a prize distribution ceremony at Government Girls High School, Liaquatabad, emphasizing support for government school students. He announced a water pump and furniture for the school. Education official Muhammad Aslam Qaisrani highlighted Punjab government provisions including qualified teachers, infrastructure, free education, curriculum, and stipends.

Smoky River FCSS is seeking parents with babies aged 2–4 months in October to participate in the 2017–2018 Roots of Empathy program, which uses classroom baby visits to help children develop empathy, positive social behavior, and reduce aggression. Interested families can contact Crystal.

NVIDIA expects Turing GPUs to be used for hybrid rasterization and ray tracing to achieve high frame rates and image quality, while some professional applications may use ray tracing for entire rendering workloads. Turing introduces a new rendering pipeline combining rasterization and ray tracing, supported by RT Cores, advanced BVH acceleration structures, denoising, RTX-compatible APIs, Microsoft DXR, NVIDIA OptiX, and future Vulkan ray tracing support. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, offloading work from SMs and enabling ray tracing performance around 10 times faster than Pascal in cited workloads.

Real-time ray tracing on Turing typically uses far fewer than hundreds of rays per pixel, with NVIDIA Real-Time Ray Tracing Denoiser modules reducing ray requirements while maintaining quality. Ray tracing can improve reflections, area light shadows, ambient occlusion, physics, collision detection, particle simulation, audio simulation, AI visibility queries, and in-engine path tracing. Ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections address limitations of shadow maps, SSAO, screen-space reflections, cubemap probes, and planar reflections.

NVIDIA NGX is a Turing-only deep learning graphics stack using Tensor Cores and pretrained DNN models. NGX supports features such as DLSS, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS uses training from 64x supersampled reference images to produce output similar to TAA with less shading work, while DLSS 2X targets image quality close to 64x supersampling. InPainting synthesizes replacement image content, AI Slow-Mo interpolates video frames, and AI Super Rez increases image or video resolution.

Turing adds Mesh Shading with Task Shaders and Mesh Shaders to reduce CPU draw call bottlenecks and enable more flexible geometry processing, including object list processing, level-of-detail selection, tessellation control, and dynamic CAD cutaways. Variable Rate Shading lets developers vary shading rates per 16x16 screen region or per primitive, enabling content adaptive shading, motion adaptive shading, foveated rendering, and increased shading rates with MSAA. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility sampling from appearance shading by storing shading results in texture space for reuse across frames, views, or requests.

Multi-View Rendering lets developers render multiple viewpoints or instances in one pass, with Turing supporting up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 at the API level. It expands Pascal’s SMP and supports VR use cases such as canted wide-FOV displays, calibrated stereo rendering, shadow rendering, and cascaded shadow maps. Turing also supports VirtualLink over USB Type-C and uses RT Cores to accelerate VRWorks Audio ray tracing.

The passage describes TU104, TU106, and Tesla T4 configurations. TU104 includes up to 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 13.6 billion transistors, and second-generation NVLink, and is used in products including GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. Tesla T4 uses a TU104 variant with 40 SMs, 2560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, a 256-bit memory interface, and 320 GB/s bandwidth. TU106, used in GeForce RTX 2070, includes 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, and 10.8 billion transistors, but does not support NVLink or SLI.

The passage defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering, combining Tensor, FP32, RT Core, and INT32 operations with usage weights based on observed frame workloads. It also explains ray tracing fundamentals, including casting rays from the camera into a scene, intersection testing, BVH acceleration, BVH building and refitting, and denoising. The document concludes that hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH algorithms, and RT Cores together enable real-time ray tracing on Turing GPUs.

Investing.com’s market outlook says markets may face a tactical pullback after a week of earnings, economic data, Fed policy signals, tariff developments, and political events. Earnings were generally strong, with 82% of reporting S&P 500 companies beating EPS estimates and 79% beating revenue estimates, while earnings revisions improved globally and in the U.S. GDP grew 3% versus 2.5% expected, but the report was described as distorted by tariff-related import volatility, with personal spending showing softness. Nonfarm payrolls rose by 73,000 versus 100,000 expected, with large downward revisions to prior months, while unemployment rose to 4.2%. The FOMC meeting included two dissents, and Powell emphasized patience and data dependency amid tariff and labor-force uncertainty; markets priced in high odds of a September rate cut and three cuts by January. Technical indicators turned risk-off, with major indexes posting a bearish engulfing pattern, weakening volume, negative internals, and broad sector declines except utilities. Bond ETFs showed signs of higher prices and lower rates, while commodities, foreign equities, bitcoin, regional banks, transports, and volatility indicators reflected mixed or negative signals.

The study addresses limitations in sex-specific Mendelian randomization caused by smaller sex-stratified GWAS sample sizes, particularly the low proportion of female participants in the Million Veteran Program. The authors performed sex-specific GWASs of sleep phenotypes, developed a semi-empirical Bayesian shrinkage approach to improve sex-specific variant-exposure effect estimates by borrowing information across sex groups, and integrated these estimates into two-sample MR analyses.

The proposed adaptive posterior mean estimator uses male-specific and sex-combined information while accounting for observed sex differences in genetic effects. Fixed-effects meta-analysis is shown to be a special case of the framework. Simulations based on MVP-like sample structures showed that adaptive shrinkage estimates improved causal effect estimation for the smaller female population, especially under weak instrument conditions, and were less sensitive to sex differences than fixed-effects meta-analysis. MR-RAPS performed at least as well as other MR methods in simulations and was used as the primary method.

Using MVP sleep GWAS data and All of Us cardiovascular outcome data, the study estimated causal effects of obstructive sleep apnea, insomnia, short sleep, long sleep, and daytime sleepiness on atrial fibrillation, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, heart failure, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes. With raw instrument selection, significant associations included insomnia with increased chronic kidney disease risk in females, long sleep with increased hypertension risk in females, and short sleep with increased coronary artery disease risk in males. With adaptive posterior mean instrument selection, additional associations were identified, including obstructive sleep apnea with type 2 diabetes and hypertension in females, and obstructive sleep apnea with chronic kidney disease and heart failure in males.

Sex-difference tests found a significant difference in the causal effect of obstructive sleep apnea on chronic kidney disease, with a stronger effect in males. Long sleep showed sex-different causal patterns for several cardiovascular-related outcomes, with higher risks in females and protective associations in males in selected analyses. Secondary analyses showed broadly similar results between MR-RAPS and MR-PRESSO.

The authors note limitations including sensitivity to instrumental variable selection, challenges testing sex differences when shrinkage estimates induce correlation, and restriction to European ancestry individuals. The method may be applicable to sex-specific analyses of other complex traits.

A University of Copenhagen study found that excessive social media use can harm emotional well-being, especially passive “lurking” on Facebook, which may lead to envy and worsened mood through unrealistic social comparisons. A 2015 study also linked teens’ heavy social media use to higher mental illness risk, though platforms may help provide mental health services. Researchers suggest limiting social media time or using it actively to connect with others.

The passage introduces a dynamically controllable dark-fringe x-ray Mössbauer interferometer designed to overcome limitations of traditional crystal-based x-ray interferometers and inline multi-target Mössbauer setups. The proposed and experimentally demonstrated system uses two 57Fe-enriched α-iron targets inside a high-purity polarimetry setup, with magnetizations arranged so that only two co-propagating polarization-dependent pathways contribute to the detected signal while radiative multi-target couplings cancel. In the ideal empty dark-fringe condition, transmitted intensity vanishes. Mechanical displacement of one target via a piezoelectric transducer introduces a controllable relative phase between the two pathways. The setup enables nanosecond-scale control of transmitted x-ray intensity and measurement of relative target displacements on x-ray wavelength and nanosecond time scales, including observation of mechanical wave propagation and reflection over more than 10 µs.

The passage argues that benchmark reliability is underexamined despite its importance in language model evaluation. It introduces HARMONY, an entropy-based metric for measuring how uniformly model performance is distributed across semantic subdomains within a benchmark. The method partitions benchmark data into clusters, measures per-cluster performance, and computes uniformity; high HARMONY suggests aggregate accuracy reflects broad competence, while low HARMONY may hide strengths and weaknesses. The authors recommend reporting HARMONY alongside accuracy and state that they map 19 MCQA benchmarks across five model families to assess benchmark reliability.

The speaker calls for cooperation with Congress to build prosperity, maintain peace, and address national priorities while cutting the federal deficit without raising taxes. He proposes modest spending increases focused on urgent needs and future investment, meeting Gramm-Rudman-Hollings targets, forming a leadership group for budget negotiations, adopting two-year budgets, expanding rescission authority, granting a line-item veto, and passing a balanced budget amendment.

He outlines priorities including economic growth, low taxes, family choice, anti-discrimination efforts, education reform, science and technology investment, competitiveness, NASA funding, a permanent research and development tax credit, lower capital gains taxes, and urban enterprise zones. Education proposals include merit school rewards, teacher awards, National Science Scholars, magnet schools, and alternative teacher certification.

The address calls for expanded action against illegal drugs, including nearly $1 billion more for treatment, prevention, interdiction, prosecution, prisons, and education, along with $1.6 billion for AIDS prevention and research. Environmental proposals include a stronger Clean Air Act, acid rain reductions, clean coal funding, park acquisitions, ocean dumping penalties, postponed lease sales pending environmental review, and tougher toxic-waste enforcement.

The speaker proposes expanded Medicaid for pregnant women near poverty, a child care tax credit for low-income families, adoption tax deductions, full Social Security funding, and increased homelessness assistance. He supports a Puerto Rico referendum, savings system reform within 45 days, and greater cleanup of nuclear weapons plants.

On defense and foreign policy, he supports a one-year military budget freeze tied to deficit reduction and future investment, followed by increases above inflation, plus reviews of national security policy and defense procurement. He emphasizes strength, cautious engagement with the Soviet Union, pursuit of the Strategic Defense Initiative, bans on chemical weapons, nuclear nonproliferation, democracy in Central America, stronger alliances, and consultations with NATO and Pacific partners.

He closes by urging service, responsibility, education involvement, support for disabled Americans, open markets for farmers, and bipartisan problem-solving for future generations.

Patient advocacy groups asked the U.K. antitrust regulator to investigate major drugmakers and their lobbying organization over suspected coordinated efforts to raise medicine prices. The complaint follows disputes over mandatory NHS rebates, which rose from 10% to 23%, and after AstraZeneca, Merck, and Eli Lilly halted or scrapped U.K. expansion plans worth $2.6 billion.

This passage introduces the 2018 ebook edition of Foreign Relations of the United States, 1919, Volume I, on the Paris Peace Conference. The Office of the Historian explains that the ebook preserves the printed edition’s content while adding portability, search, bookmarking, note-taking, and offline access, and recommends citing document numbers rather than page numbers. The preface states that, during World War II, studying the 1919 Paris settlement was necessary to help plan a just and stable postwar peace and avoid earlier mistakes. It presents the volume as part of the State Department’s effort to publish official American records of the 1919 conference, noting that no government had yet released a substantially complete record, though many unofficial memoirs, document collections, histories, and bibliographies already existed.

Systems development evolved from purpose-built machines to general-purpose computers, time-sharing systems, networked client-server architectures, and then large-scale distributed systems driven by the internet and datacenters. Distributed systems use multiple applications or replicas across machines to implement complex services. They can improve reliability and scalability, including organizational scalability, but are harder to design, build, and debug than single-machine applications. As demand for reliable distributed systems grows, containers, container images, and orchestrators provide foundations for reusable patterns and components.

The lecture continues the construction of the weak Hamiltonian for \(b \to c\bar{u}d\), focusing on renormalization group equations for Wilson coefficients and operators. Since the Hamiltonian is \(\mu\)-independent, the scale dependence of Wilson coefficients cancels that of operators, allowing anomalous dimension equations for coefficients to be derived from those for operators.

In the plus-minus basis, the leading-order equations decouple and can be solved using the beta function by changing variables from \(\mu\) to \(\alpha_s\). This yields Wilson coefficients at a low scale in terms of boundary conditions at a high scale \(\mu_W \sim M_W\), multiplied by a renormalization group evolution factor involving ratios of \(\alpha_s\). This sums leading logarithms of \(M_W/M_b\), which are treated as order one when multiplied by \(\alpha_s\).

The physical picture is that high-scale physics near \(M_W\) is integrated out into Wilson coefficients, which are then evolved down to a low scale \(\mu_b \sim M_b\), where matrix elements of operators are evaluated without large logarithms. This organization is useful for processes such as \(B \to D\pi\), where using coefficients and operators at the low scale separates the \(M_W\) dependence from hadronic matrix elements.

The lecture then discusses higher-order renormalization group improved perturbation theory. Leading-log accuracy requires tree-level matching and one-loop anomalous dimensions; next-to-leading-log accuracy requires one-loop matching and two-loop anomalous dimensions. At leading log, a Wilson coefficient that is zero at tree level can become nonzero through running.

One-loop matching is obtained by comparing renormalized full-theory and effective-theory amplitudes. The full theory is UV finite aside from coupling renormalization but contains infrared logarithms regulated by off-shell momenta. The effective theory reproduces the same infrared structure, confirming that it has the correct degrees of freedom, while differences in high-scale logarithms and constants determine Wilson coefficients.

At next-to-leading-log order, scheme dependence becomes important. Matching coefficients, anomalous dimensions, Wilson coefficients, and operator matrix elements can each depend on the renormalization scheme, but physical products such as \(C(\mu)O(\mu)\) are scheme independent. Consistency requires using the same scheme for matching, running, and matrix elements. The lecture closes by noting subtleties in full calculations, including treatment of \(\gamma_5\) in dimensional regularization and evanescent operators.

Penn Medicine researchers found that a single dose of psilocybin reduced chronic pain and pain-related anxiety and depression-like behaviors in mice for nearly two weeks. The effects were linked to serotonin receptor activity in the anterior cingulate cortex, a brain region involved in pain and emotion, rather than the injury site or spinal cord. Researchers say the findings could support development of non-opioid, non-addictive therapies, but more research is needed on dosing, long-term effects, safety, and use in clinical settings.

Baltimore County schools are increasingly using television studios for student broadcasts and media projects. At Lansdowne High School, students produce daily streamed announcements and other programs, gaining hands-on experience in video production, teamwork, communication and public speaking. About 100 of the county’s 161 schools have studios, and about half are digital. Funding remains a barrier, with basic livestream setups costing about $400 and full digital studios costing $15,000 to $18,000. Staff advisers are now eligible for extra-duty compensation. Educators and media experts said studio work supports critical thinking, creativity and technical skills as video becomes more important online. Schools such as Hillcrest Elementary and Arbutus Middle are also developing studios to support announcements and classroom projects.

The eighth annual Regional Theatrical Youth Camp runs June 19–30, 2017, with public productions of “Bye, Bye Birdie, Jr.” and an added show July 2. It offers programs for ages 5–8 and 9–18, directed by Cindy and Kenny Brown, sponsored by Oliver Companies. Registration information is available by phone.

The passage describes a study using DIA-based urinary proteomics and PRM validation to identify noninvasive biomarkers for hereditary angioedema (HAE). HAE causes recurrent swelling and can be life-threatening, with diagnosis often delayed. The study recruited HAE patients and healthy controls from Peking Union Medical College Hospital, collected first morning urine, and analyzed urinary proteins. Distinct urinary proteomic profiles were found among type 1 HAE, type 2 HAE, and controls. Enriched processes included complement and coagulation cascades, immune response, proteolysis, cell adhesion molecules, and bradykinin catabolism. A biomarker panel of C1-INH, KNG1, and EGF was identified as a promising diagnostic tool.

Researchers at Columbia University created a silicon photonics chip that turns a single powerful laser into a frequency comb, producing dozens of clean, high-power light channels. The discovery began during work on brighter LiDAR chips, when increased power generated the comb effect. The team used a locking mechanism to purify the noisy output of a multimode laser diode, achieving stable, coherent light before the chip’s nonlinear properties split it into evenly spaced wavelengths. The device could replace many individual lasers in data centers, reducing cost and space while improving speed and energy efficiency through parallel data streams in fiber. Potential applications also include sensing, quantum devices, optical clocks, portable spectrometers, and advanced LiDAR.

The passage describes a cryogenic experiment using a hard ferromagnetic microsphere levitated in a type I superconducting trap and detected with a dc SQUID. Meissner repulsion confines translation, while residual fields and anisotropy affect rotational modes. Synchronous feedback driving is used to spin the magnet and control its rotational speed.

Spin-down measurements are modeled with viscous gas damping, where the exponential decay rate gives the local gas pressure. Experiments show damping roughly linear with pressure and consistent with theoretical gas damping for helium at 4.2 K. At the lowest pressure, the rotor showed a damping rate of 4.75 × 10⁻⁷ s⁻¹, corresponding to an effective pressure of 4 × 10⁻⁸ mbar and a quality factor of 1.33 × 10¹³.
