The passage explains individual soccer defending against a dribbler, focusing on controlling, jockeying, containing, and delaying. A defender should first get goal-side, use a proper stance, and assess whether teammates are organized. If support is in place, the defender may use aggressive defending, such as cutting off the ball, tackling as the opponent receives it, interposing between player and ball, or preventing the opponent from turning. If the defense is not organized, the defender should stall the attack to allow teammates to recover.

Key 1v1 tactics include staying goal-side, maintaining a balanced stance, avoiding overreaction to fakes, blocking passes or shots, slowly giving ground, restricting the dribbler’s vision, jockeying, shepherding toward the sideline, and stealing the ball when control is lost. A defender can only retreat so far, often depending on field position, and must eventually stand ground or tackle.

Teammate communication is critical because the on-ball defender is focused on the dribbler. Calls such as “contain,” “delay,” “jockey,” and “stand him up” instruct the defender to stall, while “challenge,” “tackle,” “take him,” and “take him on” signal that support has arrived and the defender may attempt to win the ball. If beaten, the defender should chase immediately and switch roles if a teammate takes over.

Coaches should teach stance, positioning, movement, defensive techniques, use of field references, and communication terms through progressive practice with and without the ball.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K dated June 26, 2020, reporting that it issued a press release announcing a strategic change in its retail operations, including closing Microsoft Store physical locations. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer.

This study examined associations between rheumatoid arthritis (RA), depression, obesity, and hypertriglyceridemia (HTG), with attention to inflammation measured by C-reactive protein (CRP). Using 2007–2010 NHANES data, 4,136 eligible adults were analyzed, including 305 with self-reported RA. RA subjects were more often older, female, lower income, and had higher prevalence of hypertension, stroke, HTG, depression, diabetes, and obesity. RA was associated with higher PHQ-9 scores, BMI, triglyceride levels, and CRP levels. CRP was also higher among subjects with depression, obesity, or HTG. RA prevalence increased across low, medium, and high CRP categories. Depression and obesity each showed increased RA prevalence, while HTG alone did not. RA prevalence was especially higher when depression coexisted with obesity across CRP levels or with HTG at medium CRP levels. The study concludes that depression’s association with RA is strengthened by obesity or HTG and varies by inflammatory state. Limitations include cross-sectional design, self-reported RA, and CRP’s limited specificity.

The disclosure describes controlling uplink data transmission by a wireless device in an enhanced coverage state to reduce power consumption. Enhanced coverage can involve repeated transmissions in LTE, NB-IoT, or EC-GSM-IoT systems, which may increase battery use, especially for devices such as long-life asset trackers.

A device may determine it is in enhanced coverage based on coverage enhancement mode or level, coverage class, signal strength or quality, or a repetition count. Two approaches are described. In the first, an application obtains radio coverage information from a modem, such as through AT commands, and decides whether to send or refrain from sending uplink data. In the second, the application instructs the modem to transmit data only under specified conditions, and the modem applies the restrictions.

Transmission restrictions may depend on enhanced coverage status, repetition thresholds, signal strength or quality, data type, QoS, priority, timers, counters, device movement, location, battery level, or whether the device is connected to a power supply. Data not sent may be discarded or retained for later transmission. Exceptions may allow transmission for emergency data, critical information, stationary-device location updates, low battery conditions, or when the device is powered externally.

The disclosure also describes using AT commands, APIs, NAS messages, RRC messages, protocol configuration options, USIM application toolkit, or OMA device management to query coverage status, configure restrictions, and convey parameters. Network nodes may configure whether restrictions are allowed and under what conditions, including affected traffic classes, delay limits, battery thresholds, coverage levels, and maximum restriction durations. Similar principles may apply to mobile-terminated messages, where an application server or services capability server uses network-provided coverage information to decide whether to forward messages to a device.

The speaker says age is not important in today’s game and values knowledgeable veteran players who make team-first plays. He is proud to be part of the group and says winning matters more than individual goals. He notes he had only minor soreness and could play. He also explains he expected to re-sign with Dallas, but delays and budget issues left him without a team until he pushed for Detroit, which became a strong fit.

A True Potential survey found the average person’s debt rose by £560 in the first quarter of 2017, with single parents taking on about £10 per day. Around 15% of people, and 20% of single parents, borrowed to cover household necessities. Average debt was £1,797, highest among 45 to 54-year-olds and in North East England. True Potential’s David Harrison warned that easy access to poorly understood debt and borrowing “just to get by” point to a need for better financial education.

The speaker discusses a leg injury caused by another player falling on it, saying it feels sore but improved after treatment and he hopes to play tomorrow night. He says the team is tired but rested, understands the importance of the Stanley Cup Finals game, and must control its energy, stay disciplined, and play its best. He notes the series has had momentum swings, Tampa is a strong team, and the winner will be the team that pushes hardest from the start. He also praises Calgary’s fans and says he spends most of his time at home with his newborn.

The paper argues that Information Systems research has shifted from positivist, technology-focused approaches toward human and social perspectives, including mixed methods. It proposes that complexity theory and User Experience (UX) offer useful ways to understand information systems as dynamic, adaptive, irreversible, and shaped by human use. Complexity theory distinguishes complicated systems from complex ones, emphasizing self-organization, emergence, openness, nonlinearity, history, and far-from-equilibrium conditions. The paper applies these ideas to IS, arguing that adding human use makes systems complex rather than merely complicated.

The author contrasts traditional usability, focused on measurable task performance, with UX, which addresses subjective factors such as satisfaction, motivation, expectation, and experience. The paper also reviews prior IS work on complexity, critiques approaches that separate human and technical components, and argues that information systems must be understood as integrated, evolving systems. It introduces a research project with a UK UX SME to study irreversible user experiences and their implications for design, usability, complexity, and success.

The passage introduces ontology alignment as the task of identifying semantic correspondences between entities in different ontologies. It argues that while large language models are widely used for ontology alignment, knowledge graph embeddings remain underexplored despite their ability to encode structural and semantic graph information.

The work proposes a systematic framework that formulates ontology alignment as a link prediction task over merged source and target ontology triples. Triples from both ontologies are combined into a unified “triple factory,” enabling KGE models to learn shared latent representations. The approach is integrated into OntoAligner, a modular Python library for ontology alignment.

The methodology follows three stages: a parser extracts RDF-style metadata and class membership information; an encoder converts source and target ontologies into unified natural-language triples; and an aligner trains KGE models using PyKEEN, then computes cosine similarity between source and target entity embeddings. Post-processing enforces one-to-one alignments and filters matches by confidence threshold.

The passage also reviews related work using KGE models for ontology and entity alignment, including TransE, TransR, DistMult, ComplEx, RDF2Vec, OWL2Vec, and others. It then presents a collection of 17 KGE models supported in OntoAligner, including frequently used ontology alignment models and additional models effective in broader knowledge graph tasks.

The passage explains match-up zone defense, which combines person-to-person and zone principles through specific defensive rules. It can prevent offensive overloads, avoid splitting defenders, confuse opponents, and influence offensive alignments, but requires knowledgeable players and communication. Basic assignments define how defenders X1–X5 match up against 2-3, 1-3-1, 1-2-2, and 1-4 offensive alignments. The defense handles cutters, flashes, rolls, and baseline cuts through switching or interchanging roles, depending on the alignment and personnel. Match-up rules can also extend into half-court or full-court trapping, especially in corner trap zones or late-game situations.

The DAWN-PLASMA study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 multicenter trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of convalescent plasma plus standard of care versus standard of care alone in hospitalized adult COVID-19 patients. The study followed Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines, with ethics committee approval and informed consent required. Its primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15; secondary endpoints included clinical status, ventilation or death through Days 30 and 90, adverse events, laboratory data, vital signs, quality of life, and antibody-related outcomes.

Eligible participants were adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection or compatible symptoms and CT findings, plus evidence of respiratory illness. Exclusions included invasive or non-invasive mechanical ventilation at randomization, unacceptable safety risk, severe allergic reaction to plasma, treatment restrictions excluding ventilation or intubation, and recent anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody therapy.

Participants were randomized 2:1 to convalescent plasma plus standard of care or standard of care alone. Plasma recipients were to receive 800–1000 mL in four doses, beginning within 12 hours of randomization. Plasma with neutralizing antibody titers below 1/160 was not allowed.

Between May 2, 2020 and January 26, 2021, 499 patients were assessed, and 489 were randomized: 326 to convalescent plasma and 163 to control. Six randomized patients were excluded from the Full Analysis Set. Baseline characteristics and concomitant COVID-19 therapies were similar between groups. In the plasma group, median time to first transfusion was 5 hours, median plasma volume was 884 mL, and 91.9% received all four units.

At Day 15, survival without mechanical ventilation did not differ between groups in the Full Analysis Set: 83.7% with convalescent plasma versus 84.1% with control, with an odds ratio of 0.99 and p=0.976.

The passage reports that July economic data showed weakness, including 73,000 jobs added and downward revisions to May and June, while earnings remained strong, with most large-cap companies beating expectations and S&P 500 Q2 earnings growth rising to 11.2%. July was seasonally strong for stocks, but August through October are described as weaker periods. The S&P 500 reached its average annual return mark of 9.1%, while valuations remain high and the economy is slowing, though not necessarily heading into recession. The passage suggests possible market weakness in coming months and notes that AI-related stocks have driven much of the market’s strength.

DomeShelter Australia offers the Container Mounted DomeShelter™, a relocatable, weather-resistant shelter designed for industrial and other uses. Engineered for Australian Wind Regions Class A to D, it fits onto containers by welding, bolting or Twistlock and supports shipping logistics. It benefits sectors including oil and gas, agriculture, events and tourism by providing rain, UV, heat and moisture protection.

The passage explains container-based design patterns for distributed systems, beginning with single-node patterns in which tightly coupled containers are co-scheduled on one machine and may share filesystems, networking, and other resources. Splitting single-node applications into multiple containers supports resource isolation, team ownership, separation of concerns, reuse, independent deployment, and more reliable rollouts.

The sidecar pattern pairs an application container with a sidecar container that augments it, often without modifying the application. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service with an nginx sidecar, synchronizing configuration from an API to a local file, providing process introspection through a shared PID namespace, and building a simple PaaS where a Git synchronization sidecar updates files used by a Node.js server. Effective sidecars should be modular and reusable through clear parameterization, stable APIs, and documentation using Dockerfile directives and labels.

The ambassador pattern uses a companion container to broker communication between an application container and external services. It can hide sharding logic from applications by exposing a local endpoint that routes requests to the correct backend shard. It can also act as a service broker for environment-specific services such as MySQL, or support request splitting for experiments by proxying traffic to production and experimental services while returning production responses.

The adapter pattern modifies an application container’s interface to conform to common expectations. It can normalize monitoring, logging, and health-checking interfaces across heterogeneous applications. Examples include adapting Redis metrics for Prometheus, using fluentd to normalize logs from Redis or Apache Storm, and adding richer MySQL health checks without modifying the MySQL container.

The passage then introduces multi-node distributed patterns and microservices. Microservices divide systems into smaller components communicating through defined APIs, improving team independence, scaling, and agility, but making debugging and architecture more difficult. Distributed patterns help regularize these designs.

A replicated load-balanced service consists of interchangeable stateless replicas behind a load balancer. Replication improves availability, supports rolling upgrades, and enables horizontal scaling. Readiness probes distinguish live containers from those ready to serve traffic. Variants include session-tracked services, where requests from the same user are routed to the same replica, and application-layer replicated services with caching layers, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination.

Sharded services differ from replicated services because each shard serves only part of the request space. Sharding is used mainly for stateful services when data is too large for one machine. A sharded cache improves memory utilization by distributing cached keys across shards, but shard failure can reduce cache hit rates and affect latency or capacity. Replicated sharded caches increase resilience and allow individual shards to scale. Sharding functions map requests to shards, requiring deterministic and uniform hashing, careful key selection, and sometimes consistent hashing to reduce remapping during resharding.

The passage describes a smart plumbing fluid flow measuring and control device installed at a single location common to fluid-consuming appliances. The device includes a main flow channel, a parallel bypass channel with a flowmeter, a shut-off valve such as a solenoid valve, upstream and downstream pressure sensors, and a transceiver connected to a computer or remote server. The bypass flowmeter estimates overall flow while reducing resistance in the main channel, and may use a rotating wheel with two sensors to detect flow direction and calculate net flow including backflow.

The system collects flow, pressure, and optionally temperature data, stores appliance-specific fluid usage signatures, and compares actual measurements to those signatures to identify appliance use, abnormal consumption, leaks, pipe breaks, and changes in appliance behavior. If abnormal use or leakage is detected, the computer can close the valve, compare pressure readings, maintain closure or reopen the valve depending on pressure drop, and send notifications to a user device through a remote server. Methods are also described for training and labeling usage signatures, recognizing patterns with machine learning or pattern matching, detecting baseline and additional leakage, and shutting off flow during abnormal use.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for providing user interfaces that prompt users to confirm whether to proceed with or review actions associated with untrusted emails or domains. The system is intended to support phishing awareness training by pausing potentially risky actions, such as opening URLs, attachments, macros, scripts, or links from suspected phishing emails, and giving users a “second chance” to reconsider.

A device driver monitors process creation and termination. When a relevant application process is detected, a monitor library may be injected into the process to detect user actions involving untrusted domains or email-related content. The monitor library pauses the request and communicates with a user console, which resolves URLs, queries a server to determine whether a URL is trusted, untrusted, or unknown, and displays a notification if needed. The user may choose to continue or revert to review the action, and the response may be recorded on a remote server.

Notifications are configurable by a company administrator through an administrative console. Configurable elements include message titles, text fields, button labels, help links, checkbox visibility, colors, and other interface elements. The server maintains notification settings and hashes, while the client stores local settings and a client settings hash. When the client queries the server, hashes are compared; if they differ, updated settings and the server hash are sent to the client. An alternative update method uses timestamps.

The system may support standalone email clients, browser-based email clients, browser extensions, plugins, and injected monitoring code. It can monitor applications such as browsers, Microsoft Office programs, and PDF readers. The disclosure also describes network, cloud, and computing environments for implementing the system, including client devices, servers, APIs, shared memory communication, client services, and watchdog services.

The passage argues that elementary schools should provide consistently strong outcomes in both reading and math. Reviewing prior district analyses, the author found 140 districts that were strong across subjects and grade levels, while only 14 excelled in one subject and underperformed in another, mostly strong in math but weak in reading. Mississippi 2025 school data showed a strong correlation between reading and math scores, with reading and math proficiency correlated at 0.87. Growth data also showed that schools with strong reading gains generally had strong math gains: among the 50 schools with the greatest reading gains, none were below the statewide average in math growth. Similar subject-area correlations appeared in Florida. The author concludes that schools strong in one subject tend to be strong in others, though measuring school performance remains complex.

Crystal morphology strongly affects the sensitivity and performance of energetic materials, but common Wulff-based prediction models have limitations, including sensitivity to chosen planes, inability to capture edge and corner effects, and lack of growth dynamics. The work introduces a kinetic Monte Carlo simulation technique using intermolecular interaction parameters, implemented in the open-source Python package cgkmc, and applies it to PETN with agreement to attachment energy predictions and experiments. The model represents lattice sites as a colored graph with occupation states and interaction weights, computes interaction energy, identifies adsorption and evaporation candidates from coordination numbers, assigns adsorption and evaporation rates, dynamically updates the rate prefactor to reach a target crystal size, and evolves the system using the residence-time algorithm.

Teams need a practiced corner kick defense that players execute immediately. Key principles include avoiding unnecessary corners, assigning every player a clear role, letting the goalkeeper direct play, attacking the ball first, clearing high and wide, preparing an outlet or counterattack, communicating, and moving up after clearances.

The passage describes three defensive approaches: zone, man-to-man, and mixed. Zone defense assigns players to areas and is easy to teach, but can be overloaded or cause hesitation. Man-to-man marking assigns defenders to attackers and prevents flooded zones, but defenders may lose focus or be forced toward goal. A mixed system combines zonal positions near the goal with man marking elsewhere and may reduce goals conceded.

Drills should train quick positioning, clearances, communication, handling different corner types, and transition to attack. Coaches should scout opponents, adjust plans, keep the goalkeeper in charge, position the goalkeeper centrally, prepare for quick corners, and practice until reactions become automatic.

NVIDIA’s combined L1 data cache and shared memory architecture improves performance, simplifies programming, and reduces tuning. A100 increases combined capacity to 192 KB/SM from V100’s 128 KB/SM, providing low-latency, high-bandwidth access and improved performance for applications using L1 cache with device memory.

The Mid Screen offense is widely used in NBA and WNBA play because it occurs in the center of the floor, limits helpside support, and creates quick options from an on-ball high post screen. The point guard drives off the screen and may attack the basket, take a pull-up jumper, pass to the rolling or popping screener, or kick out to shooters on the wings.

The offense depends on reading defensive responses and applying counters. These include driving when defenders chase over the screen, kicking out when help defenders sag, dropping passes to posts, driving opposite when defenders cheat early, using lobs when the screener’s defender overplays, shooting when defenders go under, rolling or popping against show-and-recover coverage, exploiting mismatches after switches, slipping the screen against anticipated switches, and moving the ball quickly against traps.

If the initial action does not produce a shot, Mid Screen action can flow into continuities such as motion, single/double screens, flex, inside triangle, side screen, or post isolation. Common variations include screen-and-pop, Horns double screens, 1-4 low alignment, high post isolation, and a two-player passing game.

Successful implementation requires coordinated execution between ballhandler and screener, defensive recognition, timing, non-verbal communication, and practice through breakdown drills and scrimmaging. Game strategy includes scouting opponent screen defenses, watching for defensive adjustments, varying alignments and entries, and attacking weak defenders. The passage also emphasizes that teams must be prepared to defend Mid Screens because of their widespread use.

Casey Mittelstadt could join Rochester on an AHL or amateur tryout contract, including playoffs, but may seek an NHL entry-level deal instead. Buffalo’s preferred option is an amateur tryout now and entry-level contract for 2018-19. Signing any contract would forfeit his remaining NCAA eligibility.

The speaker describes a play where he waited for teammates to clear the zone, found space behind Zubov, went wide, and got a shot off. He says the Devils want to end the series on Thursday and avoid giving Dallas a chance to come back. He chose to sign with the Devils because he believed they could go far, and his experience in Finnish finals helped him handle pressure. He feels more comfortable against Dallas as the series continues, noting their speed, cycling, support, and ability to create space. He says the team has improved communication and discipline on line changes during the playoffs, and praises a veteran player for preparing well and stepping up in the postseason.

BMW explains the SAE’s five levels of self-driving capability. Current production cars have reached Levels 1 and 2, which require full driver attention. BMW expects Level 3, allowing limited hands-off and eyes-off driving with quick driver takeover, on its iNext in 2021, though some firms may skip it. Level 4 allows longer takeover times and safe stopping if the driver does not respond; BMW expects regulations and infrastructure to be ready mid-next decade. Waymo already has limited Level 4 cars and plans a Phoenix taxi service. Level 5, fully driverless operation, is expected by BMW near the end of next decade.

The passage presents a TPS7H500x-SP synchronous push-pull converter design example using GaN power devices at 500 kHz. Key selected values include a 205-kΩ RT resistor, 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ feedback divider for 5 V output, 25-ns dead time using 20.5-kΩ RPS and RSP, 49.9-kΩ RLEB for about 50-ns leading-edge blanking, and a 33-nF soft-start capacitor for about 7.5 ms soft start. The transformer uses a 2.5 turns ratio and 40-µH primary inductance. Primary GaN FETs are rated 170 V, synchronous rectifier GaN FETs 80 V, and Schottky diodes may be paralleled to reduce soft-start and dead-time losses. The output inductor is 0.47 µH, and about 2.3 mF output capacitance is used, including margin for single-event transient mitigation. Current limiting targets about 35 A output current with a 7.5-Ω sense resistor and 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor. Type 2A compensation uses 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF, with a 102-kΩ slope compensation resistor.

The TPS7H500x-SP controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require well-regulated, bypassed input power. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switch-node area and high-current loops, keeping sensitive traces away from noisy signals, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, filtering sensed current if needed, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS with vias. The passage also lists related TI documentation, update notification and support resources, trademark and ESD cautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information disclaimers.

The passage describes systems, methods, and computer-readable media for detecting abnormal cardiac activity using machine learning. The approach receives cardiac data, such as ECG or PPG, and motion data, such as accelerometer data, divides the data into time windows, determines signal quality indices, extracts cardiovascular features, and applies tensor transformations. A trained deep learning architecture, including a convolutional neural network, bidirectional recurrent neural network, and attention network, classifies windows or periods as normal, abnormal, or noisy and can identify windows likely containing abnormalities. Subject contextual information, including medical history and demographics, may also be used. The system may operate with wearable sensor devices, such as smart watches, and generate reports describing cardiac activity classifications, abnormal activity type, timing, or burden.

This retrospective cohort study examined incident hypertension after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) among patients aged 13–54 who delivered at two southeastern U.S. academic health systems from 2014–2017. Among 2,514 included patients with a 15–90 day postpartum blood pressure (BP) measurement and no prior hypertension, 13% were diagnosed with incident hypertension after that visit. Higher systolic BP at 15–90 days postpartum, older maternal age, and severe preeclampsia/eclampsia were associated with higher hypertension risk; longer time to postpartum BP measurement was associated with lower risk. About 40% of eligible patients with HDP lacked a documented 15–90 day postpartum BP check, and only 20% had a BP check within 14 days postpartum. The authors conclude that postpartum BP monitoring after HDP was inconsistently performed and that early identification and management of hypertension and cardiovascular risk factors are important after HDP.

JPMorgan Chase is expanding AI across its operations, deploying a proprietary generative AI platform to 200,000 employees and investing about $18 billion in technology, including AI, machine learning and cloud infrastructure. AI is being used in retail banking, wealth and asset management, credit assessments, onboarding, fraud detection and risk management. The bank reports productivity gains but faces challenges around compliance, transparency, model risk, security, legacy systems and adoption costs.

Wandera analyzed 50,000 moderately to heavily used iPhones and iPads and found that iOS 11 drained batteries more than twice as quickly as iOS 10. A device at 100% battery lasted an estimated 240 minutes on iOS 10, compared with 96 minutes on iOS 11. Some users reverted to iOS 10.3.3, though Wandera advised against it for security reasons. Older iPhones may experience worse battery drain than newer models. Apple released updates after iOS 11, with iOS 11.0.1 improving battery drain time to 159 minutes, a 65% improvement over iOS 11. Wandera said new operating systems often have bugs that affect battery life. Users can save battery by limiting background app refresh, location access, or using low power mode.

Connaught Public School in Hintonburg attempted to break the tunnel ball world record, with over 250 students playing at once compared to the previous record of 120. The attempt awaits Guinness verification. The event also raised $10,000 for school yard renewal, including plans for playground, basketball court, field, and tree improvements.

On Oct. 29, 2001, multiple news reports said Enron’s shares fell to multi-year lows after Moody’s downgraded its senior unsecured debt to Baa2, two notches above junk, and warned of possible further downgrades. Enron said it was seeking additional bank credit after drawing about $3 billion to $3.3 billion in existing lines, while analysts said lenders might demand higher rates, collateral, or stricter terms. The company’s stock had lost more than half its value amid disclosures of partnership transactions tied to former CFO Andrew Fastow, SEC scrutiny, write-downs, and equity charges. Reports also noted European energy firms reducing or restricting trades with Enron, concerns about its asset-light trading model and disclosure practices, and several shareholder lawsuits related to the partnerships and broadband-related transactions.

The passage lists AMD Geode CS5535 companion device errata 106–116, including issues with AuxOutputFull clearing on Port 60h reads, tACK not affecting UDMA timing, ATAC hangs with WORD-aligned PRDs, LPC aborts after turn-around, incorrect SMB NEGACK behavior, GLPCI retry counting, GPIO High Bank register writes after suspend, short SMBus hold time, missing LOWBAT_FLAG after abnormal standby, and Sleep_X/Sleep_Y not deasserting when delays exceed PM_SED. Recommended workarounds include using interrupts for PS/2 emulation, DWORD-aligning ATAC PRDs, applying LPC logic workarounds, double-writing SMB_STS, adjusting or disabling retry limits, using read-modify-write after suspend, and programming sleep delay counters below PM_SED.

The passage describes several billionaire founders and CEOs who reject or redefine work-life balance. Jeff Bezos prefers “work-life harmony,” saying work and home life reinforce each other rather than compete. Other leaders, including Andrew Feldman, Lucy Guo, Eric Yuan, Reid Hoffman, and Jack Ma, argue that building major companies often requires extreme work hours, though some acknowledge personal priorities such as family or close relationships.

U.S. consumer confidence rose in April to 128.7 from 127.0 in March, nearing February’s 18-year high of 130.0, the Conference Board said. The increase reflected favorable views of business and labor conditions, a strong job market, tax cuts, reduced market volatility and eased trade-war concerns, though some analysts cautioned spending growth may lag.

Seattle’s housing market has seen fast-rising prices and rents, fueling concerns about a bubble. A ValueInsured survey found 71 percent of Washington homeowners worried, though its sample was small. King County’s median home price rose 18.6 percent year over year to $658,000, while inventory fell. Real estate experts cited strong credit, higher down payments and homeowner equity as reasons a 2008-style collapse is unlikely, though some market correction and leveling of prices and inventory may occur.

NEC established the NEC Satellite Operation Center, scheduled for full operation in April, to operate ASNARO-2 using its GroundNEXTAR system and a secure data center. The center can manage multiple satellites, supports visualization and image distribution, and NEC plans to market ASNARO-2 images with JEOSS from September.

Software must manage ring buffer halting carefully, placing halt commands last and using one command at a time for precise error halting. Interrupt status bits can be cleared only when the ring buffer is empty or processing is paused.

SPA encoding includes encryption information when SMEE or SME-MK is enabled; SPAs must be well-formed and in valid address ranges. TMPM reports command and sub-status results through ring buffer entries and migration/update lists.

PM_GET_CAPABILITIES queries firmware capabilities. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates 1–128 Hypervisor-owned pages, updates IOMMU host PTEs, requires CPU access prevention, and does not directly support 2M page migration. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages, requires RMP_ENFORCE, disallows DMA during migration, and updates source and destination RMP states.

Errors may arise from command formatting, migration entries, ring buffer management, hardware failures, or timeouts. Some errors can cause partial success or unrecoverable page state, after which software may attempt recovery actions before rebooting.

McEachern, ranked SN NEXT No. 1, is visiting Harrison in Kennesaw, Georgia, with kickoff at 8 p.m. EST. Both teams are 5-0 after bye weeks. McEachern seeks to strengthen its case for The Sporting News High School Football Top 25, while Harrison aims to boost its profile with an upset.

The TPS7H500x-SP series supports Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation using its OTA error amplifier; Type 2A adds CHF for high-frequency noise attenuation. Compensation component selection depends mainly on crossover frequency and power stage transconductance, which varies by topology. The devices include thermal shutdown, stopping switching above 175°C typical and restarting below 160°C typical.

The controllers use fixed-frequency peak current-mode control for radiation-hardness-assured space-grade DC-DC converters and require external gate drivers. They support topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge, with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz.

A synchronous push-pull GaN design example uses 500 kHz switching, 5 V output, approximately 25 ns dead time, 50 ns leading-edge blanking, a 33 nF soft-start capacitor for about 7.5 ms soft start, a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, and a 40 µH primary inductance. Selected components include 170 V primary GaN FETs, 80 V synchronous rectifier GaN FETs, a 0.47 µH output inductor, about 2.3 mF output capacitance, a 7.5 Ω current-sense resistor, 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation with 40.2 kΩ RCOMP, 15 nF CCOMP, and 47 pF CHF, and a 102 kΩ slope compensation resistor.

Power supply recommendations specify a 4 V to 14 V input range, at least 0.1 µF VIN bypass capacitance, ceramic bypass capacitors placed close to the controller, and bulk capacitance if the supply is distant. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing high-current and switching loops, keeping sensitive traces away from noisy nodes, placing bypass and compensation components close to the device, filtering sensed current if needed, and properly connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS. The passage also lists related TI documentation, support resources, ESD cautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.

Astronomers discovered RAD J131346.9+500320, the most distant and powerful known odd radio circle, using RAD@home citizen scientists and LOFAR. The source lies at redshift ~0.94 and has two intersecting radio rings, only the second known example with this feature. The study suggests ORCs may be linked to superwind outflows from spiral host radio galaxies rather than shockwaves from merging supermassive black holes or galaxies. RAD@home also identified two other large radio-ring structures in galaxy clusters, where jets likely interact with hot surrounding plasma. Researchers say these findings indicate ORCs and radio rings may be part of a broader class of plasma structures shaped by black hole jets, winds, and their environments. Future facilities and surveys may uncover more ORCs and clarify how they form and evolve.

Peter Marks, former top FDA vaccine regulator ousted by RFK Jr., has joined Eli Lilly Research Laboratories to oversee molecule discovery and infectious diseases. He confirmed the role to STAT, saying he hopes to advance infectious disease products for public health. The move drew criticism over the revolving door between regulators and industry.

The State of Louisiana sued the Banking Department of the Citizens’ Bank to recover a license tax for conducting banking business. The president of the Citizens’ Bank excepted, arguing he lacked authority to represent the alleged department, that no such separate corporation existed, and that no proper citation had been served. The district court sustained the exception and dismissed the suit.

On appeal, the court held that the Citizens’ Bank was chartered as the corporation authorized to sue and be sued, and neither Act No. 246 of 1853 nor the cited compact created a separate “Banking Department” corporation with authority to stand in judgment. Because the state intentionally sued the Banking Department rather than the Citizens’ Bank, the defect was not merely a misnomer. Questions concerning corporate status, estoppel, and liability had to be determined contradictorily with the Citizens’ Bank, which was not made a party. The judgment was reversed, but the suit was dismissed as in case of nonsuit for want of citation. Justice Monroe dissented.

The passage presents a budget pacing approach for real-time online advertising auctions. It describes pacing as a control problem in which a bid modifier, λ, rescales final bids to align actual spending with a desired spending plan under budget constraints. The work proposes a Bucketized Hysteresis Controller that combines hysteresis control with proportional feedback to improve stability and reduce reliance on empirical tuning. It compares this method with a production variable-step multiplicative pacing controller, provides an analytical framework for parameter selection, and validates the approach through real-world auction experiments. The baseline controller adapts its update scale using recent λ×bid trajectories and a fluctuation factor to detect stable or oscillatory behavior. The proposed controller discretizes normalized pacing error into multiple bands and applies predefined multiplicative adjustment steps, using larger steps for large errors and smaller steps for minor errors to balance convergence speed and stability.

Running low on fuel, Dawn is expected to remain in orbit around Ceres to avoid contamination.

The Horns Offense uses high post screening similar to the MidScreen offense and can create layups or open shots if defenders are caught on screens. Defenses should influence the ballhandler toward the weaker offensive screener, weak hand, or away from the best post-up threat. NBA teams often avoid switching because it can create a post mismatch.

Defensive responses include Basic NBA Show & Recover, where the on-ball defender pushes the ballhandler wide, the screener’s defender shows, helpers cover the roll, and players recover to ball pressure, post defense, and pass denial positions. Subsequent rotations follow near-player concepts, with defenders closing out, denying passes, helping, fronting the post, and applying SOS principles. The passage explains the Internal Bar Strength (IBS) indicator, calculated as (Close-Low)/(High-Low), which measures where the close falls within the day’s range. Low IBS values are presented as bullish and high values as bearish in mean-reverting markets. The article says IBS has worked well for over two decades, especially on stocks and broad stock indices such as SPY and QQQ, but less well on other asset classes, commodity-related stocks, and markets such as Norway and Australia. Backtests cited show strong historical results, particularly for Nasdaq, and improved performance during volatile or bear markets. Adding filters such as VIX or the 200-day moving average may improve results, though the passage warns about optimization and curve fitting. A key weakness is execution, because trades need to be entered near the close; delaying entry to the next open significantly reduces returns. The author concludes IBS remains useful, especially when combined with other indicators, but should not be expected to work universally.

A guest lecture discussed experimentation and robust design of engineering systems, focusing on adaptive experimentation versus factorial and fractional factorial designs. The lecturer reviewed the history of experimental design, contrasting Edward John Russell’s preference for simple experiments with R.A. Fisher’s development of complex factorial designs, randomization, blocking, and fractional factorial experiments. Fisher showed factorial designs could improve efficiency, but full factorial designs scale poorly as factors increase, leading to fractional factorials that trade smaller experiment size for risks such as confounding main effects with interactions.

The lecture connected these methods to robust parameter design, where control factors are chosen to reduce sensitivity to noise factors. Taguchi’s crossed-array approach and later orthogonal-array methods were described as influential in industry and Six Sigma programs, though the lecturer argued that these methods can be burdensome and sometimes fail in practice. Observations from an agricultural equipment manufacturer showed many planned robust design experiments were never completed, motivating interest in adaptive one-factor-at-a-time experimentation.

Empirical and theoretical studies compared adaptive one-factor-at-a-time experiments with fractional factorial designs across many systems. Results suggested adaptive methods can perform as well or better when experimental error is moderate and interactions are not small, especially when the goal is improvement rather than precise effect estimation. The lecturer explained that adaptive experiments can exploit main effects and interactions without explicitly estimating interactions, and that informed starting points improve outcomes. Adaptive methods crossed with factorial noise designs were applied to robustness problems, including sheet metal spinning and paper airplane experiments, where adaptive approaches often outperformed Taguchi-style crossed arrays.

The lecturer also discussed ensemble adaptive experiments, where multiple one-factor-at-a-time runs can outperform larger fractional factorial designs and provide robustness to experimental error. Practical limitations were noted, including cases requiring parallel experimentation, delayed measurements, time trends, or archival learning needs, where factorial designs may be preferable. The lecture concluded that adaptive experimentation can provide substantial improvement efficiently, especially when applied broadly and with practical engineering judgment.

A later question-and-answer session addressed course logistics, problem set solutions, quiz preparation, regression confidence intervals, noise factors, lack-of-fit calculations, and requests for smaller examples of fitting models to factorial experiments.

The 2-1-2 zone is a compact variation of the 2-3 zone that protects the middle and positions big players near the basket for rebounding. It is vulnerable to strong outside shooting, so it is mainly used against poor outside shooters or high post offenses such as a 1-3-1 alignment. The middle defender actively covers the high post when the ball is out front and fronts the low post when the ball is on the wing or in the corner. The outside defenders shift together sideline to sideline and are usually the quickest players. The post defender stays between the ball and basket and guards the low post. Baseline defenders work opposite each other, with one often taking the ball or moving toward the corner while the other assumes weakside rebounding position.

The passage introduces a study of classical Heisenberg spins with bilinear-biquadratic exchange on a partially anisotropic triangular lattice made of isosceles triangles. It emphasizes teaching players how to attack breakaways, 2-on-1, 3-on-1, 3-on-2, and 3-on-3 situations, with goals such as layups, open jump shots, putbacks, and creating numerical advantages.

The passage stresses passing ahead, limiting dribbles, avoiding charges, finishing layups, rebounding missed shots, and using pressure opportunities after scores. In 3-on-2 and 3-on-3 situations, it describes options such as wing-to-wing passes, return passes, give-and-go cuts, down screens, dribble clears, base screens, splitting defenders, and turn-out actions.

If the initial push does not produce a shot, the offense should flow directly into early offensive actions without backing the ball out, preventing the defense from setting up. These early flow sets can also function as half-court offenses. The final phase, continuity, maintains offensive rhythm, spacing, rebounding position, and late-clock organization. The passage describes several continuity offenses, including Flex, Passing Game, Mid Screen, Side Screen, and Inside Triangle, each using screens, cuts, ball movement, and specific options to create shots.

The passage examines links between architectural design education and STEM education, focusing on how architectural studio methods may inform STEM practices. It reviews STEM/STEAM education, project-based learning, design, architectural studio education, technical drawing, and related literature on robotics, engineering, studio models, and multidisciplinary learning.

The study aims to identify prominent elements of first-year architectural design education at BUU Faculty of Architecture and use them to generate insights for STEM education through analogical inference. An ethnographic qualitative method was used. The first author observed first-year architectural design studio classes for four weeks, taking notes on student presentations and instructor critiques. Eight volunteer students were also interviewed. Data were analyzed through content analysis, with validity supported by instructor review, interview comparison, theoretical triangulation, and literature comparison.

Findings from observations produced four main themes: confronting open-ended problems, deepening understanding of the problem situation, gaining experience in presentation techniques, and meeting the culture of criticism. Students worked on real design problems, conducted field research, developed sketches, models, plans, storyboards, and portfolios, and received repeated critiques from instructors. Critiques addressed spatial errors, missing design logic, professional knowledge, user needs, safety, cost, feasibility, and the strength of design arguments. Interviews showed that students viewed the course as developing abstract and conceptual thinking, while difficulties included model making, time limits, hand drawing, presentations, and the invention process.

The discussion argues that architectural education resembles STEM education through real-life problems, learning by doing, open-ended inquiry, and iterative critique. Six conclusions are proposed for STEM education: students should solve open-ended problems independently from beginning to end; STEM projects should receive stronger motivational and curricular weight, especially at high school and undergraduate levels; STEM problems should be authentic and connected to real-life value; younger students should engage physically with materials and tools even without producing final products; technical drawing and graphic skills should be strengthened; and undergraduate STEM project courses should adopt stronger studio-like critique, jury evaluation, and reflection-in-action practices.
