The lecture examines when the Fiat-Shamir paradigm is sound in the random oracle model. Applying Fiat-Shamir to a zero-knowledge Hamiltonian cycle protocol with soundness 1/2 is not sound, because a cheating prover can repeatedly query the random oracle until it returns the desired challenge. Sequential repetition to make soundness negligible still fails, since the prover can preserve successful partial transcripts and extend them one round at a time.

A theorem is stated: Fiat-Shamir is sound in the random oracle model for public-coin protocols with negligible soundness and a constant number of rounds. The proof shows that if a polynomial-time prover can cheat in the Fiat-Shamir version with probability epsilon, then one can construct a prover that cheats in the original interactive protocol with probability about epsilon divided by the number of oracle queries, contradicting negligible soundness. For more verifier messages, the loss becomes roughly a power of the query bound, so the round count matters. Protocols with round-by-round soundness, such as GKR, can also support Fiat-Shamir despite having many rounds.

The Kilian-Micali protocol has constant rounds and negligible error, so Fiat-Shamir is sound for it in the random oracle model. However, the random oracle model is described as only a sanity check, not a standard-model proof; there are contrived hash functions for which a protocol secure in the random oracle model is insecure with any explicit hash family.

The lecture also discusses parallel repetition of the Hamiltonian zero-knowledge protocol. Sequential repetition remains zero knowledge, but parallel repetition is not known by the same simulation method because a malicious verifier may choose all challenges as a function of all commitments. A later result showed that for this specific protocol, parallel repetition is not zero knowledge, by proving Fiat-Shamir soundness for it under certain cryptographic assumptions. If Fiat-Shamir soundness holds for an interactive proof, then it cannot also be zero knowledge, since a simulator would produce accepting Fiat-Shamir transcripts even for some false statement, contradicting soundness.

The North Dakota Supreme Court reversed a district court order suppressing evidence against Denise Hahne in a DUI case. Hahne had been stopped after failing to stop at a temporary sobriety checkpoint, and testing showed alcohol levels above the legal limit. The district court suppressed the evidence because it found there was no safe or legal way for motorists to avoid the checkpoint.

The Supreme Court held that law enforcement is not required, as a matter of law, to provide motorists an opportunity to avoid sobriety checkpoints. It explained that checkpoint constitutionality depends on reasonableness under the balancing test from Brown v. Texas and Michigan Department of State Police v. Sitz, including public interest, effectiveness, and intrusion on individual liberty. The ability to avoid a checkpoint may be considered as one factor in evaluating intrusion, but it is not conclusive. The case was remanded for the district court to apply the correct legal standard and determine whether the checkpoint was constitutionally reasonable.

The OECD warned that threatened trade barriers and rising oil prices could weaken global growth by hurting confidence, investment, jobs, inflation and household incomes. It slightly lowered its 2018 global growth forecast to 3.8 percent and expects 3.9 percent in 2019.

New Jersey ranked 25th in the Commonwealth Fund’s 2018 healthcare scorecard, down two spots and behind other Northeast states. It scored well on access, children’s coverage, employee-based insurance costs, healthy lives, and infant mortality, but needs improvement in prevention, readmissions, and costs.

The 13/48 trading strategy uses the crossover of the 13-period EMA and 48-period EMA to identify trading signals. A 13 EMA cross above the 48 EMA is considered bullish, while a cross below is considered bearish. The strategy is momentum-based and is said to work better in trending markets, but it can be risky in sideways or choppy markets because EMA signals may be unreliable. Backtesting across markets found it worked best on stocks. For the S&P 500 cash index from 1960 to today, the strategy was invested 66% of the time and returned 5.1% annually versus 7.2% for buy and hold, with slightly better risk-adjusted return. The passage concludes it is a lagging strategy prone to whipsaws and not a guaranteed path to profits.

Alan Brister sued for a refund after the IRS applied his 1989–1992 tax overpayments to liabilities created by reversing withholding credits claimed on his 1985 and 1986 returns. The IRS conceded the 1993 adjustments were outside the normal three-year limit but argued the limitation did not apply because Brister filed false returns with intent to evade tax.

Brister had claimed large withholding amounts from Solar Roofing, supported by W-2 forms he prepared, though those amounts had not been paid to the IRS. The court found Brister knew Solar Roofing had not paid and was unlikely to pay the claimed withholdings, and that he used the returns to recover debts he believed the company owed him. It held that the 1985 and 1986 returns were knowingly false and filed with intent to deceive the Government. Therefore, the fraud exception allowed the IRS adjustments, and judgment was entered for the United States.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K dated August 3, 2017, announcing early adoption, effective July 1, 2017, of new FASB standards for revenue recognition and leases. Prior periods will be adjusted beginning with the quarter ending September 30, 2017. Revenue recognition adoption materially affects consolidated income statements and balance sheets, mainly software license revenue, but not cash flows. Lease standard adoption materially affects balance sheets through recognition of right-of-use assets and lease liabilities, with no material income statement impact and no cash flow impact. Exhibit 99.1 provides restated financial information for fiscal years 2017 and 2016.

The study examines the effects of distance education on equality and inequality of opportunity in education, based on opinions from faculty members and students. It defines distance education as a flexible learning model using communication technologies to connect teachers and learners in different locations, with synchronous and asynchronous forms. The passage notes that distance education can reduce costs, support lifelong learning, allow self-paced learning, expand access to information, and reduce time and place limitations, but it can also create problems related to socialization, practical training, learner readiness, technology access, internet infrastructure, and digital gaps.

The research used a qualitative case study design with semi-structured interviews. Participants were 21 faculty members and 26 students who had experienced distance education. Data were analyzed through content analysis.

Faculty members identified positive effects of distance education on equality of opportunity, including learning at a personal pace and easy access to information. They identified negative effects including problems accessing technology, internet connection issues, disregard of learner competencies, lack of suitable learning environments, and increased differences among students.

Students stated that distance education supports equality through freedom from time limitations, free education, and access to various sources. They identified financial limitations and internet problems as causes of inequality.

Suggested improvements included determining learner characteristics, improving access to technology, developing digital literacy skills, resolving internet infrastructure problems, providing state budgeting for technology access, and offering consultancy services to students. The study concludes that distance education has both equalizing and unequalizing effects, and that reducing inequality requires attention to infrastructure, access, learner support, and digital competencies.

The lecture discusses entangled photons and clarifies that entanglement requires non-factorizable states of physically distinct, separately addressable subsystems. It distinguishes true entangled states from single-photon mode superpositions and inseparable systems such as electrons in helium. Photon polarization and dual-rail qubit examples are used to illustrate entanglement, including Bell states and EPR-like states.

Entangled states are described as non-local and fragile against decoherence. The lecture introduces entanglement purification, where multiple weakly entangled pure states can probabilistically produce maximally entangled Bell states using controlled-NOT operations and measurements. Entanglement is then quantified through the entropy of the reduced density matrix after tracing out one subsystem; Bell states have entropy one.

The lecture also discusses creating entangled atoms. One proposed method is photodissociating a suitable molecule, though practical requirements make this difficult. Another probabilistic method uses photons emitted by two atoms: measurements on the photons can project the atoms into an entangled state. This relies on beam splitters, Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, and polarization manipulation to erase information about which atom emitted which photon.

Commissioner.COM sent a Nov. 25, 2001 fantasy football report for “Get Bad with Yourself,” including promotional offers, NFL player injury and lineup updates, fantasy start/sit recommendations for Week 11, and a schedule breakdown for Luccis Losers at Team Chick with all listed players at 0.0 points before play.

The passage introduces uncertainty quantification for computational oncology, focusing on quasi-Monte Carlo methods to estimate expectations of quantities of interest from semi-linear parabolic reaction-diffusion PDE tumor growth models with uncertain diffusion and proliferation coefficients. The work extends QMC analysis to a nonlinear parabolic PDE, proves well-posedness for general random fields, derives parametric regularity and QMC error estimates for uniform random fields, and supports the theory with numerical experiments, including log-normal random fields on a complex domain. The tumor model includes diffusion-driven invasion, logistic proliferation, treatment effects from radiotherapy and chemotherapy, homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, and bounded admissible coefficients.

In May 2007, Deputy Mayor for Education Victor Reinoso had to recommend a chancellor to lead Washington, DC Public Schools as Mayor Adrian Fenty prepared to assume control of the system. DCPS served 55,000 students in 150 schools, faced poor academic performance, high administrative spending, patronage, leadership turnover, underused facilities, and low public confidence.

Reinoso, a former consultant, school board member, and Federal City Council executive, viewed DCPS reform as a turnaround challenge. His school board experience convinced him that consensus-driven governance slowed difficult decisions, including school closures. After Fenty’s 2006 election on a platform of education reform, Reinoso became deputy mayor, built a flat internal consulting-style team, gathered data from the Parthenon Group, and helped draft legislation placing DCPS under mayoral control. The DC Public Education Reform Act made DCPS subordinate to the mayor, created a chancellor role, reduced the school board’s authority, shifted facilities management outside DCPS, and emphasized interagency coordination.

Reinoso sought a chancellor able to rethink public education, prioritize teaching and learning, improve student achievement, reject incremental reform, and set high expectations despite systemic challenges. Candidates included Rudy Crew, an experienced superintendent known for aggressive reforms; Michelle Rhee, founder of The New Teacher Project and advocate for teacher quality and staffing reform; and incumbent superintendent Clifford Janey, who had developed broad reform plans but was seen as cautious. Shortly before making his recommendation, Reinoso faced criticism for using unattributed material from another district’s education plan, but remained focused on choosing a leader who could “rock the boat” without capsizing it.

Mesh is a short-to-intermediate passing concept associated with the Air Raid but used across many offenses because it works against multiple coverages. It creates natural picks and movement against man coverage and lets receivers settle in open voids against zone. The concept is effective versus man and base zone coverages, with options such as drag, flare, arrow, and corner routes, but can struggle against zone blitzes or simulated pressures that challenge protection and timing.

Receivers adjust routes by coverage: drag runners stay on the move versus man and sit in zone voids versus zone, while backs release to flare or arrow routes. The quarterback must anticipate pressure, get the ball out quickly, and usually progresses from flare to shallow drag, deep drag, and fullback arrow, with the corner route often decided pre-snap.

Common variations include mesh rail, which makes the running back on a rail route the primary option, and designs using a sit route over the ball as a zone answer. The passage also notes mesh can be adapted to different systems, including the single wing.

Chris Lattner, creator of Apple’s Swift programming language, announced he is joining Google Brain to work on artificial intelligence. He previously left Apple for Tesla, where he led the Autopilot program before departing after about six months. Google is investing heavily in AI to support its cloud computing ambitions against Amazon Web Services.

Culp reported fiscal Q4 2017 net sales of $77.4 million, roughly flat year over year, with pretax income of $7 million, including about $250,000 in plant relocation expenses. Net income was $6.2 million, or $0.49 per diluted share, versus $3.6 million, or $0.29, a year earlier. For fiscal 2017, net sales were $309.5 million, down 1.1%, while pretax income reached a company record $29.7 million. Net income was $22.3 million, or $1.78 per diluted share, and adjusted EBITDA rose 7% to $40.1 million.

The mattress fabrics segment reported record annual sales of $190.8 million, up 2.4%, and record operating income of $29.4 million, up 11%. The company cited benefits from capital investments, lower input costs, and continued product innovation, despite industry disruption and production facility changes. Expansion projects in North Carolina and Canada were substantially completed, and a Haiti joint venture facility was expected to begin operations in the second quarter of fiscal 2018.

Upholstery fabrics sales were $118.7 million for the year, down 6%, reflecting softness in residential furniture retail, while operating income was $11.1 million, slightly below the prior year. The company reported stronger margins from hospitality and performance fabrics, favorable currency effects in China, and continued interest in hospitality-related acquisitions.

Culp ended the year with $54.2 million in cash and investments, no outstanding line-of-credit balances, operating cash flow of $33 million, and free cash flow of $18 million. The board approved a special dividend of $0.21 per share.

For fiscal Q1 2018, Culp expected overall sales comparable to the prior year, slightly lower mattress fabrics sales and operating income, and slightly higher upholstery fabrics sales and operating income. Pretax income was projected at $7.8 million to $8.4 million, including about $300,000 in plant relocation expenses.
Scotty will decide how much time he wants to devote to hockey and family, but the speaker expects him to return next year, citing his passion, energy, constant hockey watching, and success.

Channel 4 chief executive Alex Mahon said the broadcaster’s 28.6% gender pay gap is unacceptable and pledged to improve it. She aims for a 50:50 gender split among the top 100 highest-paid roles by 2023, where only 34 are currently held by women, despite women making up 59% of the workforce. The gap exceeds the national average of 17.4% and is higher than ITN’s 19.6% and the BBC’s 10.7%. Mahon attributed the gap partly to women being concentrated in lower-paid roles. The issue follows wider scrutiny of broadcaster pay, including at the BBC.

The passage outlines a specification for the SEV-ES and SEV-SNP Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB), which standardizes how encrypted guests communicate selected state to a hypervisor during Non-Automatic Exits. The GHCB is a 4 KB decrypted shared page, with protocol negotiation, feature advertisement, GHCB GPA registration, and MSR-based requests used before or alongside the GHCB page.

Version 2 adds SEV-SNP support, hypervisor feature advertisement, CPUID request support, restricted APIC emulation, SNP guest requests, page state changes, AP creation, multi-VMPL operation, trusted I/O, Secure AVIC, and GHCB unregister support. Revisions add expanded sequence numbers, new error reporting, APIC ID retrieval, multiple VMPL support, VLEK certificate GUIDs, SEV-TIO guest requests, and updated debug behavior.

The specification describes supported NAE events and guest/hypervisor responsibilities for VMGEXIT processing, including IO, MSR, VMMCALL, MMIO, page state changes, SNP guest and extended guest requests, AP creation, #HV doorbell pages, IPIs, timers, APIC ID lists, Run VMPL, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, termination requests, and unsupported exits. It also defines error handling through SW_EXITINFO fields and VALID_BITMAP usage.

Additional sections cover SEV-ES guest identification, SMP booting challenges, AP reset hold, AP jump tables, SNP AP creation, NMI handling, debug register support, lack of SMM and nested virtualization support, and SNP Restricted Injection. Restricted Injection uses a shared #HV doorbell page with PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields to communicate interrupts and non-maskable events while preserving guest isolation.

The passage describes technology for sealing high-pressure fluid flow devices used in harsh oil and gas environments, such as plug valves and hydraulic fracturing fluid ends. Existing designs often mount seals on removable components so they seal against bores in the main body, causing corrosion and abrasion damage to the body and making repairs costly and disruptive.

The disclosed technology mounts seals in grooves or recesses formed in the device body instead. These seals extend from the body to seal against mating components such as valve inserts, retaining nuts, discharge plugs, suction plugs, valve seats, stuffing box sleeves, discharge flanges, or suction manifolds. This transfers erosion wear from the main body to less complex and less expensive components that can be repaired, resurfaced, coated, or replaced more easily.

The invention includes fluid end assemblies with housings, internal chambers, intersecting conduits, endless grooves or recessed corner sections formed around conduit walls, and seals positioned in those grooves. It also includes methods for manufacturing such assemblies. Various seal types may be used, including radial, axial, crush, elastomeric, metal, or spring seals. The technology is illustrated with plug valves and fluid ends but is described as applicable to other high-pressure flow devices.

The passage introduces CTPNet, a framework for multivariate long-term time series forecasting. It addresses limitations of prior downsampling-based methods that mainly model intra-subsequence dependencies while neglecting inter-subsequence and inter-channel dependencies. CTPNet learns three dependency types: inter-channel dependencies through Channel-wise Representation Learning using temporal query-based multi-head attention; intra-subsequence trend dependencies through Trend-wise Representation Learning with efficient Transformer attention; and inter-subsequence periodic dependencies through Periodic-wise Representation Learning. The model includes downsampling, encoding, decoding, and inverse downsampling steps to process periodic subsequences and generate forecasts. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets compare CTPNet with recent models, and the reported results show CTPNet achieving the highest first-place count across MSE and MAE metrics.

A 34-year-old Mission man was arrested after a black pickup truck was reported driving recklessly at a Maple Ridge strip mall, hitting a vehicle, barricades, a drive-thru curb and a bus stop. A female pedestrian and her son suffered non-life-threatening injuries. The man faces impaired driving, hit and run and dangerous driving causing bodily harm charges.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated February 26, 2020, reporting that it issued a press release updating revenue guidance for its More Personal Computing segment for the quarter ending March 30, 2020. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The report lists Microsoft’s registered common stock and notes on NASDAQ and was signed by Frank H. Brod, Corporate Vice President, Finance and Administration, and Chief Accounting Officer.

The speaker was disappointed not to score right away but felt they were playing well overall. They stayed positive, kept working, and prioritized winning over personal scoring, believing goals would come with time.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver said there is “no contemplation” of moving the 2026 All-Star Game from the Clippers’ Intuit Dome despite an ongoing investigation into whether the team circumvented salary cap rules involving Kawhi Leonard and Aspiration Fund Adviser. The league is reviewing a reported $28 million endorsement deal, while All-Star planning continues independently. The game is expected to air on NBC on Feb. 15 with a new format.

The Louisiana Supreme Court affirmed Ray Jones, Jr.’s conviction and life sentence for the first degree murder of his infant son. Jones challenged admission of three inculpatory statements, arguing they were not voluntary and violated Miranda. The court found two hospital statements were spontaneous, voluntary, and not the result of police interrogation, so Miranda warnings were unnecessary. It also held the police-station statement was not obtained through interrogation after Jones requested counsel, and even if improperly admitted, any error was harmless given the other evidence. The court also rejected Jones’s claim that the trial judge improperly limited cross-examination of a psychiatrist, finding the excluded question irrelevant and within the judge’s discretion.

From April 1, Scotland will criminalize disclosing or threatening to disclose intimate photos or videos under the Abusive Behaviour and Sexual Harm Act, with a maximum penalty of five years in prison. The law targets private images shared without consent, addressing harms linked to online sharing, abuse, harassment, and technological change.

The passage examines how generative AI can be integrated into higher education assessment while addressing academic integrity, authenticity, feedback, and AI literacy. It argues that AI is increasingly relevant to employability and that universities should train students in its technological and ethical use. Traditional assessments such as essays, MCQs, SAQs, and online exams are described as vulnerable to AI-generated responses and often limited in authenticity, inclusivity, and ability to assess higher-order skills.

The passage highlights concerns that AI-generated text can be difficult to distinguish from student work and that detection tools may be unreliable, biased, and quickly outpaced by newer AI models. It also notes that ChatGPT and later models can perform well on MCQs and written assessments across several disciplines, creating challenges for conventional assessment design. Suggested responses include invigilated exams, more authentic assessments, higher-order MCQs, and assessments requiring students to evaluate AI outputs.

The paper proposes two broad assessment approaches: mitigating AI use through formats such as vivas, presentations, clinical assessments, practical exams, and invigilated exams; or integrating AI through tasks such as AI case studies, critique of AI output, debate with AI, draft generation, data visualization, question generation, and comparative analysis. Generative AI is also presented as a tool for feedback, idea generation, rubric creation, practice questions, peer review simulation, and progress evaluation, though limitations include inaccuracies, bias, lack of context, misalignment with curricula, and over-reliance.

A case study at a UK university redesigned a postgraduate immunology coursework essay to include ChatGPT 3.5 as an auxiliary tool. Students received training on AI policy, academic integrity, ChatGPT use, and prompt engineering; generated AI-assisted essay outlines; evaluated outputs with peers; and then completed final essays without further AI assistance. A survey of 20 students found that 57.9% had previously used generative AI, mainly ChatGPT, but only 5% felt very confident using it. Students saw AI as useful for planning, drafting, summarizing, revision, proofreading, idea generation, and research, while identifying limitations such as inaccuracy, outdated information, lack of references, superficiality, and weak critical thinking. Only 26% agreed that using generative AI in assessments was plagiarism, while 37% disagreed and 37% were unsure.

Students considered ChatGPT useful for producing a basic essay outline and learning about AI capabilities and limitations, but found outputs generic, superficial, similar across the cohort, and sometimes questionable in accuracy. The passage concludes that integrating AI into assessment can support more authentic, diverse, and higher-order assessment practices if accompanied by clear guidance, training, ethical use, and attention to academic integrity. It recommends that institutions rethink assessment policies, improve AI literacy for students and educators, and adopt innovative assessment approaches suited to an AI-driven society.

The passage describes a system and method for active ground terrain mapping to control a mobile agricultural machine. A pose detection sensor identifies the machine’s geographic position and orientation along a route. Using the sensor signals, machine dimensions, and configurable point cloud parameters, the system defines a virtual point cloud estimated to correspond to the ground surface around the machine and generates elevation values for points in the cloud.

The point cloud can be configured by resolution, width, length, and offset, and may be used to create a georeferenced elevation map made of discrete cells. Elevation values and confidence or weight values are aggregated as the machine travels, with weights based on distance from the pose detection sensor. Map layers may include elevation, confidence, number of accumulated points, and elevation variance.

The elevation map or predictive elevation values can be used to control machine subsystems, such as harvester header height, sprayer boom height, propulsion, steering, crop volume estimation, operator interfaces, and communications. The system may operate on the machine, with remote servers, or with mobile and general computing devices.

Matthew Shashy, 29, of Montgomery, was sentenced to four years of probation after a federal jury found him guilty of impeding, intimidating, and interfering with Air Force personnel at Maxwell Air Force Base. Prosecutors said Shashy spray-painted anti-government graffiti at several locations, then fired a shotgun three times near the base’s Day Street entrance on January 3, 2017, before fleeing. He later surrendered after barricading himself inside his residence, where authorities found firearms, ammunition, anti-government literature, and related evidence.

Micro-credentials certify specific knowledge and skills gained through targeted learning experiences and are viewed as a response to gaps between traditional higher education and workplace skill needs. This study examined education and industry leaders’ familiarity with micro-credentials in Mauritius, their potential integration into higher education credit systems, and their perceived professional value.

Using semi-structured interviews with 10 education leaders and four industry leaders in Mauritius, the study found general awareness and willingness to consider micro-credentials, though definitions varied. Respondents associated them with short, competency-based learning, assessment, professional development, badges, and possible pathways toward larger qualifications. Understanding of badges was less consistent.

Most respondents supported a flexible or hybrid model that could connect micro-credentials with existing academic credit systems while responding quickly to industry needs. They saw potential benefits for lifelong learning, employability, skills validation, and personalised learning pathways. However, they also identified challenges, including unclear recognition, limited regulatory structures, quality assurance, assessment reliability, credit mapping, and the rigidity of current systems.

The study concludes that micro-credentials in Mauritius require a phased approach, alignment with the National Qualifications Framework, reliable competency-based assessment, university credit mapping, and collaboration between education providers, regulators, and industry. While not fully understood, micro-credentials were broadly seen as important for future education and professional development.

Brookfield Infrastructure Partners has delivered strong historical returns, with 20% annualized returns since 2008 and Adjusted AFFO rising from $352M in 2012 to $926M. It currently offers a 4% distribution yield and 5.84% AFFO yield, retaining cash for growth while also issuing units. Brookfield targets 6–9% annual distribution growth, though the author views this as aggressive given currency and inflation factors. Same-store EBITDA growth has averaged 5% on a constant-currency basis. The lower current yield versus prior levels reflects a higher unit price, which benefits existing unitholders when new units fund higher-yielding investments, but creates risk if unit prices fall. The author expects future returns near 10%, below past levels, with a safe and growing dividend.

A Phase 2 NIAID-funded trial found that adding 16 weeks of omalizumab to oral immunotherapy improved outcomes for children allergic to multiple foods. Stanford researchers enrolled 48 children aged 4 to 15; all began daily OIT at week eight and were tested at week 36. Among children receiving omalizumab, 83% could consume at least two grams of two or more allergenic foods, compared with 33% receiving placebo. Omalizumab recipients also had fewer adverse events during early OIT. Larger studies are needed to confirm the findings.

Credit bureaus began by tracking consumers’ debt reliability for businesses. Today, companies like Equifax collect extensive financial data without consumer opt-in, making it difficult to avoid. The passage introduces a show about why bureaus know so much and why regulation has challenged lawmakers for decades.

Archaeologists searching a narrow gap at Dublin’s City Hall for Willie Halpin’s Easter Rising rifle found no gun but recovered other artefacts, including roof fragments, one with a bullet hole, 1930s milk bottles, pottery, and a teapot lid. Family history says Halpin threw the rifle from the roof rather than surrender it to British soldiers. Consultant archaeologist Franc Myles said the rifle was likely thrown into the gap but may have been removed soon after the Rising, possibly during later military inspections. The search was backed by Halpin’s family and Lord Mayor Nial Ring, who said it was worth investigating.

Former Western University professor John Knight left $5.25 million to LHSC’s translational ovarian cancer research team in tribute to his wife, Mary, who died of the disease in 2008. The donation will support hiring researchers, buying equipment and global collaborations. Victoria Hospital named its A-block lobby the Mary and John Knight atrium in recognition. Researchers said ovarian cancer is difficult to detect early and their work focuses on understanding metastasis.

ETF Channel calculated a weighted average analyst target price of $145.80 for the Vanguard Mid-Cap Growth ETF based on its holdings, implying 9.77% upside from its recent $132.83 price. Notable holdings with upside to analyst targets include Sensata Technologies at 11.37%, Global Payments at 10.34%, and Markel at 10.26%. The passage notes that high targets may reflect optimism or outdated assumptions requiring further investor research.

Former Facebook executives Chamath Palihapitiya, Sean Parker, and Antonio Garcia-Martinez expressed concerns about Facebook’s societal impact. Palihapitiya said he feels guilt and believes social media tools harm civil discourse and social fabric globally, though Facebook also does good. Parker warned it changes relationships and may affect children, while Garcia-Martinez criticized Facebook’s claims about user influence.

Tanzania has launched the Tanzania Business Clinic to improve the business climate by identifying solutions to challenges facing companies and sectors. Industry, Trade and Investment minister Charles Mwijage said the platform will include business experts and public officials who will advise on business practices, policies and regulations. It will operate from Dar es Salaam with branches in Sido offices nationwide. The initiative follows Cabinet approval of a regulatory reform blueprint intended to amend laws affecting areas such as VAT, imports, immigration, labour, social security and environmental management. The reforms aim to attract private investment in key sectors and address Tanzania’s poor World Bank Doing Business 2018 ranking, where it placed 137th out of 190 economies.
OpenAI’s GPT-5 launch faced glitches and criticism, with users saying the model was less friendly and fell short of high expectations despite being positioned as a major advance.

Voters in Julia Banks’ electorate of Chisholm were largely unaware of questions over whether she held dual Greek Australian citizenship, but several locals said they would continue to support her or the Liberal Party if a byelection were held. Banks won the previously Labor-held Melbourne seat in 2016 with a 2.84 per cent swing, defeating Labor’s Stefanie Perri by 2154 votes. The electorate includes multicultural suburbs such as Oakleigh, Box Hill, Clayton, Mount Waverley and Chadstone. Monash University politics lecturer Zareh Ghazarian said a byelection would likely favour Labor in the marginal seat, which the government held by just over 1 per cent, and could attract many candidates, increasing vote volatility. Labor figures expressed confidence they could regain Chisholm, with housing affordability, mortgage stress and renters’ security likely campaign issues.

The passage lists soccer on-field non-verbal communication methods, mainly hand signals, used by teammates during matches. Signals can indicate starts of set pieces, corner kicks, free kicks, throw-ins, substitutions, defensive wall positioning, passing preferences, player runs, through balls, marking assignments, goalkeeper instructions, and team movement. Other signals include head nods, ball taps, raising the ball, running over the ball, bouncing the ball a set number of times, and agreed-upon signals such as for an offside trap. It notes that coaches and players may need developed non-verbal systems when crowd noise prevents oral communication.

President Ulysses S. Grant warns against illegal military expeditions organized in the United States against Canada, urges all persons not to aid or join them, states participants will lose government protection, and orders U.S. officers to prevent such acts and bring offenders to justice.

11-year-old Damian Sunderland faces months of surgery after a relative’s dog attacked him at home. Doctors have performed skin grafts to reconstruct parts of his face, including his cheeks, jaw, nose and lips.

The passage describes SD Memory Card bus modes, initialization, command behavior, data transfer, erase, write protection, locking, and function switching.

UHS-I operates only in SD mode, not SPI, and uses 1.8V signaling for higher-speed modes. Cards start at 3.3V after power cycle; ACMD41 negotiates 1.8V support, CMD11 performs voltage switching, and CMD6 selects driver strength, bus speed mode, and power/current limits. UHS-I requires 4-bit bus mode except for CMD42 unlock operations, and CMD19 provides tuning in 1.8V transfer state when the card is unlocked.

UHS-II supports both legacy SD bus and UHS-II interfaces. Hosts detect UHS-II availability after power-up using lane signaling; otherwise they initialize through SD bus mode. UHS-II initialization includes PHY initialization, device initialization, enumeration, configuration, and SD-TRAN initialization. FD156, HD312, FD312, and FD624 modes are defined, with FD624 introduced as a higher-speed UHS-II/UHS-III mode.

Card initialization uses CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, and CMD3 to reset cards, validate voltage, determine capacity support, retrieve CID, and assign RCA. CMD8 is mandatory before ACMD41 for SDHC and SDXC initialization. ACMD41 reports readiness, capacity status, 1.8V switching acceptance, and related operating conditions.

Data transfer mode begins after RCA assignment. CMD7 selects one card for transfer, CMD9 reads CSD, CMD4 optionally sets driver strength, and ACMD6 selects 4-bit bus width. Read and write commands transfer block data with CRC, may be stopped by CMD12, and have defined behavior for misalignment, partial blocks, busy signaling, and programming states.

Erase operations use CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38. DISCARD and Full User Area Logical Erase are supported for SDHC and SDXC cards, not SPI, and require support bits in SD_STATUS. Cards signal erase or discard progress by holding DAT0 low.

Write protection includes a mechanical switch, optional internal protection, and password-based lock/unlock. CMD42 manages passwords, locking, unlocking, force erase, and Card Ownership Protection. COP adds Force Erase Password handling and COP unlock behavior. Locked cards accept only specified basic and lock-related commands, and ACMD6 is rejected while locked.

APP_CMD (CMD55) marks the following command as application-specific. CMD6 switches or checks card functions, including access speed mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. CMD6 is mandatory for Version 1.10 and later cards and is valid in transfer state.

The passage describes NVIDIA Blackwell GPU architecture features, including the AI Management Processor, a dedicated RISC-V-based GPU context scheduler that reduces CPU scheduling dependency, improves latency, and coordinates AI and graphics workloads. Blackwell adds 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC hardware encode/decode, ninth-generation NVENC with improved AV1/HEVC quality, AV1 Ultra High Quality mode, faster export speeds, improved NVDEC, and DisplayPort 2.1b with up to 80 Gbps bandwidth.

Blackwell Max-Q improvements include advanced power gating, separate voltage rails, accelerated frequency switching, and faster low-latency sleep, enabling higher efficiency and reported power savings in small language model inference. DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improved frame pacing through enhanced Flip Metering, and support from fifth-generation Tensor Cores.

The passage also covers neural shaders enabled through Cooperative Vectors APIs for DX12 and Vulkan, supporting technologies such as RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. It provides specifications for Blackwell GPUs including GB202, GB203, and GB205, and associated GeForce RTX 50 Series products such as RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, and 5070. NVIDIA includes standard disclaimers about accuracy, product changes, suitability, liability, licensing, trademarks, and copyright.

VentureWire’s May 22, 2001 issue reported that Kodiak Venture Partners closed its second fund at $290 million, Mercury Interactive acquired Freshwater Software for $147 million, Celetron raised a $48 million first round, and TVM held a first close of EUR 70 million for a new life sciences fund. The issue also covered numerous financings, including rounds for CGtime, Lawson Software, NetContinuum, Danger, FlightTime, NuVasive, MiFund, ViAir, SeeCommerce, Zinio Systems, Antrim Design Systems, and NewMarkets. Reported setbacks included staff cuts at AgWeb and Ironmax and Rx.com ceasing day-to-day prescription operations. Other items included AuctioNet.com renaming itself Realm Connect, Nextira Federal launching, several acquisitions by Blink.com, everstream, Primus, and MindArrow Systems, board and executive appointments, a University of Pittsburgh–Redleaf technology funding program, 3i’s planned chair transition to Baroness Sarah Hogg, and corrections regarding Broadview and Porivo Technologies.

A Phase 2/3 observer-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study evaluated SII-NVX-CoV2373 in Indian children and adolescents aged 2–17 years. A total of 920 participants were enrolled, with 460 aged 12–17 years and 460 aged 2–11 years, randomized 3:1 to receive two doses of vaccine or placebo on days 1 and 22 and followed to day 180.

The study found SII-NVX-CoV2373 to be safe and well tolerated. No adverse events of special interest were reported, and no serious adverse events were considered vaccine-related. Most adverse events were mild and resolved without sequelae; common solicited events included injection-site pain, tenderness, headache, fatigue, and fever.

The vaccine produced strong immune responses in both pediatric age groups. Anti-spike IgG and neutralizing antibody responses after the second dose were non-inferior to those previously observed in Indian adults receiving SII-NVX-CoV2373, with higher titers in children than adults. Seroconversion exceeded 98% after the second dose and remained above 90% at day 180. The vaccine also generated immune responses against Delta, Omicron BA.1, and Omicron BA.5 variants.

The authors conclude that SII-NVX-CoV2373 was safe, well tolerated, and highly immunogenic in children aged 2–17 years and may support pediatric COVID-19 vaccination. The study was funded by Serum Institute of India Pvt. Ltd.

The study examined education students’ and lecturers’ experiences of the effectiveness of Physical Education teacher training in distance mode at North-West University in South Africa. It used a qualitative design with open-ended questionnaires from 17 third-year B.Ed. distance students majoring in Life Orientation and semi-structured interviews with four lecturers.

Findings produced five themes: interaction between students and lecturers; competence, passion and enthusiasm to teach Physical Education; obstacles in distance learning; experiences of practical training; and the influence of the program on perceptions of Physical Education. Students reported that lecturers were accessible, professional and responsive, though the lack of physical contact limited interaction. Students’ confidence and subject knowledge increased, while lecturers expressed strong passion for Physical Education.

Key obstacles included students’ limited background knowledge, technological challenges, restricted internet access and assignment administration problems. Videos were viewed as useful for practical skills training, though delayed feedback on practical assignments was a concern. Many students found the course content interesting and reported a more positive view of Physical Education’s value in schools.

The study recommends more face-to-face contact opportunities, additional technological training, improved use of videos and media, increased student interaction through learning management systems, and stronger administrative systems.

Mud Bay is a Pacific Northwest pet store chain founded in 1988 by Elsa Wulff and later led by her children, co-CEOs Lars and Marisa Wulff. The company focused on healthy dog and cat products, extensive employee training, consultative selling, low everyday prices, and a customer experience centered on helping pet owners.

By 2014, Mud Bay had 27 stores, $38.4 million in revenue, $1.05 million in profit, and 261 employees. Although sales were strong, leadership believed the company was falling short as a workplace: turnover was 48%, wages were modest, and medical insurance participation was limited. In response, Mud Bay launched a “Good Jobs Vision” through an employee-involved planning process. Its five strategies were to invest in staff, offer fewer products at everyday low prices, standardize processes while empowering staff through continuous improvement, improve efficiency through cross-training and slack, and partner with animal welfare organizations.

From 2014 to 2017, Mud Bay raised wages, expanded eligibility for medical insurance, launched an Employee Stock Ownership Plan, improved training, reduced SKUs, lowered prices, created category expert teams, standardized some operations, expanded animal welfare partnerships, and introduced new roles and scheduling practices. Average hourly wages rose from $12.12 to $15.06, the share of employees working at least 30 hours rose from 69% to 82%, turnover fell from 48% to 31%, and employees came to own 4.8% of the company.

Financially, total sales grew 70% from 2014 to 2017, same-store sales growth averaged above 9%, and sales per labor hour increased. However, lower prices, higher wages and benefits, ESOP contributions, home office growth, and new stores reduced profitability. Net profit margins fell from 2.18% in 2014 to 1.99% in 2017.

By 2018, Mud Bay’s Good Jobs journey remained incomplete. Leaders noted gaps in execution capacity, standardization, continuous improvement, staffing systems, and delayed initiatives such as budgeting software, home delivery, and improved point-of-sale systems. As the 2018 planning team struggled to improve margins, COO Tracy Yamane proposed closing stores one hour earlier Monday through Saturday to reduce labor costs and improve employee quality of life. Marisa supported the idea, while Lars opposed it because of concerns about customer convenience and lost sales, prompting an analysis of sales by time of day before a decision was made.

A city court reserved its order for tomorrow on Shashi Tharoor’s anticipatory bail plea in the Sunanda Pushkar death case. Delhi Police opposed bail, arguing he might flee, influence witnesses, or harm the investigation. Tharoor’s lawyers said police had earlier stated he cooperated and was not arrested because custodial interrogation was unnecessary. Tharoor has been summoned as an accused on July 7 and charged under IPC sections 498A and 306. Police named him the only accused in its chargesheet.

Rieva Lesonsky explains that document management affects businesses of all sizes, with poor practices causing lost time, higher costs, customer service problems, security risks and inefficient use of office space and supplies. A Xerox survey found 40% of business processes remain document driven, and many small and midsize businesses are improving document management to support growth and productivity. Suggested steps include tracking print costs, scanning paper documents to cloud services, using Xerox ConnectKey and related apps to streamline scanning, sharing and workflows, enabling mobile document handling, requiring PINs for printing, restricting colour printing, and setting toner alerts.

U.S. passports may be issued only to citizens and generally to law-abiding applicants who meet prescribed rules, but issuance is not obligatory and denial does not itself deny citizenship. Applicants must satisfactorily establish citizenship, U.S. domicile, and intent to return and perform duties of citizenship. Expatriated persons, or those permanently resident and domiciled abroad, cannot receive passports. Expatriation depends on circumstances, including abandonment of allegiance, permanent foreign residence, political domicile abroad, and intent not to return. Factors weighing against issuance include severed U.S. ties, no family or property in the United States, foreign marriage and home, foreign business or profession, and plans unlikely to include U.S. domicile. Favorable factors include maintaining U.S. family and property ties, inability to return for health or financial reasons, and residence abroad for legitimate American enterprises. Special rules apply in semibarbarous countries or places with U.S. extraterritorial jurisdiction, where prolonged residence may not bar passport protection if pursuits are legitimate and not harmful to U.S. relations.

Matt Barbet is launching the Home Roads podcast on iTunes and Acast on June 8, featuring bike-ride conversations with professional cyclists and other cycling figures about their routes, careers and personal lives. Initial episodes include Alex Dowsett, Sarah Storey, Nicolas Roche and David Millar, with future guests including Ben Saunders, Simon Warren, Simon Mottram and Philippa York.

The passage explains the 200-day moving average as a technical indicator that averages closing prices over 200 trading days to identify long-term trends. It describes the basic rule: prices above the 200-day moving average suggest an uptrend, while prices below suggest a downtrend. The article says the strategy is simple, trend-following, and useful for reducing exposure during bear markets, but it can underperform buy-and-hold strategies during long rising markets because of whipsaws, transaction costs, and missed opportunities.

The passage cites Paul Tudor Jones as using the 200-day moving average for defensive investing and discusses examples from the S&P 500 and oil markets. Backtests suggest the strategy can reduce drawdowns but may produce many losing trades and false signals. Jeremy Siegel’s variation, using 1% thresholds around the 200-day average, is described as slightly improving results. The passage also compares SMA and EMA, notes that daily bars are commonly used, and says backtesting is needed to determine whether specific variations work.

NVIDIA A100 improves memory performance over V100 with 1555 GB/sec HBM2 bandwidth, 2.3x L2 cache read bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, cache residency controls, and Compute Data Compression. These features improve data reuse, reduce DRAM traffic, and support workloads such as deep learning training, inference, LSTM networks, and producer-consumer chains.

A100 introduces Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), allowing one GPU to be partitioned into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory bandwidth, and fault isolation. MIG supports multi-tenant, single-user, multi-user, VM, and container use cases while maintaining CUDA compatibility. Compute Instances further subdivide GPU Instances and support Volta-style MPS.

The architecture includes third-generation NVLink with twelve links and 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, improved fault detection and containment, NVJPG hardware JPEG decode, an Optical Flow Accelerator, improved atomics, and five NVDEC units. CUDA 11 adds support for A100 features including task graph acceleration, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 residency controls, Cooperative Groups enhancements, MIG, Tensor Cores, and sparsity.

DGX A100 uses eight A100 GPUs connected through third-generation NVLink and NVSwitch, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and supporting scaling through Mellanox networking, Magnum IO, NGC containers, and DGX software. MIG can provide up to 56 isolated GPU accelerators in one DGX A100 system.

The passage also describes sparse neural networks, pruning, and fine-grained structured sparsity. A100 supports 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity, intended to improve compute throughput, reduce memory bandwidth use, and maintain balanced workloads with minimal accuracy loss based on evaluated networks.

Researchers found that New Caledonian crows and kea parrots were better at solving tool-use tasks after previously exploring the relevant objects. The study suggests playful exploration helps animals incidentally learn object properties, similar to how human infants learn through play. Birds tested with blocks, ropes, balls and sticks could select appropriate tools after exploration, though they did not appear to deliberately seek information or change interactions after learning the objects’ uses. A separate report noted that wildlife selfies on Instagram have increased sharply since 2014 and may fuel cruel treatment of Amazon species.

Lecture 14 covered slender adorned chains, fatter linkages, and hinged dissections, with discussion focused on hinged dissections. There is no general software for hinged dissections, though some animated examples exist, and building such tools or implementing slender adorned chain refinements are suggested project ideas.

Greg Frederickson’s work and books are highlighted as major sources on dissections, including hinged and twist-hinged forms. The lecture sketches a construction showing that polyominoes, polyiamonds, and related polyforms can be hinge-dissected universally by cutting basic cells into pieces with hinges visible on every edge and using an induction on a spanning tree of the shape. Similar ideas extend to some 3D polyforms, such as tetrahedral constructions.

The lecture also discusses physical realizations, including salt-actuated mesoscale hinged dissections, DNA origami, ball-and-socket chains that can fold into voxelized shapes, and reconfigurable robots. Connected chain robots are contrasted with modular robots that attach and detach, with the connected approach preserving wiring and power links.

Several dissection techniques are reviewed, including the Montucla rectangle-to-rectangle dissection, piece-lie methods, Dudeney’s square-to-equilateral-triangle dissection, and furniture or architectural applications inspired by hinged dissections. The lecture explains that some hinge-refinement steps can cause at least exponential growth in pieces, but a pseudopolynomial bound is possible for polygons with vertices on an integer grid by carefully triangulating, chaining triangles, preserving hinges, and using gadgets such as hinge-moving constructions and pseudocuts.

Finally, the lecture surveys higher-dimensional dissections. In 3D, equal volume is not sufficient for two polyhedra to be dissectable; they must also have matching Dehn invariants. Dehn proved this invariant condition was necessary, and Sidler later proved that equal volume and equal Dehn invariant are sufficient in 3D. Similar results are known in 4D, while dimensions five and higher remain unresolved.

Joan Jordan, a 45-year-old Irish software engineer, struggled to find work after being diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2010, following paralysis on one side of her body. The passage describes techniques for address obfuscation in memory devices to improve endurance and reduce vulnerability to malicious attacks such as row hammer. Logical addresses received from a host are mapped to physical memory addresses using selectable and variable mapping functions, which may differ by device, die, array, bank, tile, or over time. These mappings can work with wear-leveling procedures that move data among memory cells to distribute wear.

A memory device may include selection, mapping, receiving, determination, access, and routing components. The selection component chooses a mapping function from supported functions, and mapping subcomponents apply logic operations to logical address bits to determine physical address bits. Supported operations may include inversion, pass-through, XOR, XNOR, address swap, and other logic functions. Mapping functions may be selected using random numbers, unique identifiers, schedules, trigger events such as boot, reboot, access-count thresholds, or detected attacks, or may be configured during manufacture using fuses, anti-fuses, trim parameters, or fuseload procedures.

The disclosure explains that varying the logical-to-physical address mapping can make it harder to reverse-engineer wear-leveling movement patterns. Even if a wear-leveling pattern is learned from one memory entity, different or changed mapping functions may make that information ineffective for other entities or later use. A security key may allow selection of a direct-addressing mapping function for manufacturer testing or debugging, such as passing logical address bits through without inversion.

Non-Automatic Exit (NAE) events are exit events that are not Automatic Exit (AE) events. In an SEV-ES guest, hardware throws a #VC exception for NAE events, with the #VC error code equal to the event’s VMEXIT code. The guest inspects the error code, copies required register state to the GHCB, executes VMGEXIT, and later resumes after VMGEXIT to process hypervisor results. The #VC handler exits with IRET, so IRET generally should not be intercepted.

The GHCB protocol defines required guest and hypervisor support for NAE events, including required state passed to and from the hypervisor. Guests must handle #VC exceptions for all listed NAE events, and hypervisors must handle VMGEXITs for those events even if the related instruction was not intercepted. GHCB fields used by the guest or hypervisor must be marked in VALID_BITMAP. At minimum, guests set validity for SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1, and SW_EXITINFO2; hypervisors set validity for SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2. Both sides should clear VALID_BITMAP before setting event-specific bits. Unless specified otherwise, SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2 are zero.

Software should disable interrupts and preemption while updating the GHCB, setting the GHCB MSR, and accessing GHCB contents after VMGEXIT. For NMI contexts, a separate GHCB or save/restore of active GHCB state is recommended. Hypervisors report VMGEXIT errors through SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2; nonzero SW_EXITINFO1[31:0] indicates an error or requested action, such as exception injection or malformed input reporting.

Specific NAE handling includes IOIO_PROT instruction decoding or paravirtualization, with decrypted buffers for string I/O; MSR_PROT decoding for RDMSR or WRMSR; hypervisor-specific VMMCALL register handling; and #NPF/MMIO access using decrypted buffers and SW_SCRATCH. Page State Change lets SEV-ES or SEV-SNP guests request private/shared page changes and related hints, with progress tracked in shared structures and reason codes used for incomplete or failed processing. SNP Guest Request and SNP Extended Guest Request allow SEV-SNP guests to make firmware requests through the hypervisor, using shared request, response, and optional data pages; extended requests can return certificate data identified by GUIDs.

Additional NAE events include AP Creation, #HV doorbell page registration, #HV Send IPI, #HV Timer, APIC ID List, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC backing page registration, and Termination Request. AP Creation lets an SEV-SNP guest create, update, or remove AP vCPU state using VMSA pages. #HV doorbell pages support Restricted Injection by allowing the hypervisor to notify guests of pending events. #HV Send IPI and #HV Timer provide IPI and timer functions when Restricted Injection is enabled. APIC ID List lets guests request assigned APIC IDs. SNP Run VMPL lets a guest request execution at another VMPL if a VMSA exists. SNP TIO Guest Request supports SEV-TIO trusted device requests with shared data pages for measurements, certificates, and reports. Secure AVIC uses guest-owned APIC backing pages per vCPU. Termination Request lets a guest request termination with reason codes.

Guests identify SEV-ES support through hypervisor-provided CPUID properties, including hypervisor presence, SEV support, encryption bit position, and physical address reduction. SMP booting under SEV-ES and some SEV-SNP configurations cannot rely on hypervisor register updates after measurement and encryption, so AP startup uses initial measured register state, AP Reset Hold, AP jump tables, or the SEV-SNP AP Creation feature. vCPU hotplug is not supported under the measured-register approach, but AP Creation can support vCPU hotplug by allowing guests to supply VMSA pages.

For NMIs, the hypervisor must not intercept IRET and must intercept #DB, using the guest’s “NMI Complete” VMGEXIT message before injecting another NMI. Hardware debug registers are virtualized when DebugVirtualization is supported; otherwise DR7 read/write intercepts are required, with guest-side caching. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

Restricted Injection uses #HV doorbell pages shared with the host. The doorbell page contains PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields aligned with APIC behavior. PendingEvent carries interrupt vectors, NMI, virtual #MC, and NoFurtherSignal state. Guests acknowledge pending events with atomic exchanges and validate vectors. Hosts emulate APIC interrupt presentation, acknowledgement, in-service, and EOI semantics, using NoEoiRequired to optimize EOI handling. Guests should execute HLT with interrupts disabled and inspect interrupt state after resuming. Non-cooperative host or guest behavior may cause denial of service or lost notifications but should not affect host integrity.
Camel engravings at Jebel Misma suggest early humans entered a once-verdant Nefud 12,000 years ago.

The passage is a SanDisk Sansa Fuze user manual excerpt covering safety, operation, media transfer, playback, settings, troubleshooting, support, warranty, and software license terms. It supports music, audiobooks, podcasts, photos, videos, voice recording, FM presets and recording, playlists, Go Lists, bookmarks, shuffle, repeat, EQ, ratings, slideshows, and deletion of content. The passage argues that K-12 education has overemphasized broad “skills” such as critical thinking, collaboration, metacognition and digital literacy while devaluing factual knowledge. It says such skills require background knowledge to be meaningful, citing examples from physics and cricket-related reading comprehension. The author criticizes “portrait of the graduate” frameworks, reduced graduation testing, grade inflation and disconnected curricula, while supporting high-quality instructional materials that build sequential knowledge. The passage also warns that AI may weaken strong curricula and links declining knowledge acquisition to widening educational gaps, especially for poorer students.

This study analyzed 2021 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Survey data to assess insecticide-treated net (ITN) ownership and use among children under 5 and pregnant women. Overall, 56% of households owned at least one ITN, but only 25% had enough for all members. Ownership was higher in rural areas, the North West and North East, and lower wealth quintiles. Among children under 5, 41.2% slept under an ITN, with higher use among younger children, rural residents, children in the North West and North East, and those from poorer households. Among pregnant women, 49.6% slept under an ITN, with higher use in the North East and North West, among less educated women, and among lower wealth groups. The study concludes that ITN use remains below Nigeria’s 80% target and that regional and socioeconomic disparities should be addressed through expanded distribution, healthcare access, and health education.

Mario Batali is taking a leave from his businesses after Eater reported sexual misconduct allegations from four women. Batali apologized, said some described behavior matched his past actions, and took responsibility. He was also removed from ABC’s “The Chew.”

NVIDIA filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended May 1, 2022. Revenue was $8.29 billion, up from $5.66 billion a year earlier, while net income fell to $1.62 billion from $1.91 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $0.64, compared with $0.76. Gross profit was $5.43 billion, and operating income was $1.87 billion.

The company recorded a $1.35 billion acquisition termination cost after NVIDIA and SoftBank terminated the agreement for NVIDIA to acquire Arm due to regulatory challenges. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $20.34 billion as of May 1, 2022. Total assets were $45.21 billion, total liabilities were $18.89 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $26.32 billion.

Gaming revenue was $3.62 billion, Data Center revenue was $3.75 billion, Professional Visualization revenue was $622 million, Automotive revenue was $138 million, and OEM and Other revenue was $158 million. Revenue by segment was $4.62 billion for Graphics and $3.67 billion for Compute & Networking.

NVIDIA repurchased $2.00 billion of common stock and paid $100 million in dividends during the quarter. Its board later increased and extended the share repurchase program to up to $15 billion through December 2023.

The filing discusses risks including demand uncertainty, cryptocurrency mining effects, supply constraints, COVID-19 disruptions, China lockdowns, the war in Ukraine, inflation, long manufacturing lead times, and potential inventory mismatches. NVIDIA also disclosed litigation related to prior cryptocurrency-related statements and a May 2022 SEC settlement involving a $5.5 million civil penalty without admitting or denying the SEC’s findings.

HMD Global has not released the Nokia 8 kernel source code 136 days after promising to share its modifications. The passage says this violates GPLv2 and has drawn criticism from developers, despite the company keeping devices updated and offering an Android 8.1 beta.

University of Queensland researchers found that venoms from the Black Mamba, Western Green Mamba and Jamesons Mamba can cause both limp paralysis and, after antivenom treatment, painful spastic paralysis. The study suggests current antivenoms may neutralize one effect while revealing another, helping explain treatment failures. Researchers also found venom differences by geography, especially in Black Mambas from Kenya and South Africa, and called for more specialized antivenoms.

Researchers analyzed 39 Newfoundland fossils once thought to be pseudofossils and propose they are spongelike animals from about 560 million years ago. The fossils had pores and fingerlike tubes suggesting filter feeding, and may be related to modern sponges. The creature was named in reference to punk rocker John Lydon and a local spiky fruit.
The speaker says the team appreciated support before Detroit, aims to gain ground, and focuses on reacting to players’ tendencies rather than categorizing them.

The speaker described an intense physical game, contributing to two goals, and focusing on helping the team win and prepare for the next home game. He said having his parents and brother at the Stanley Cup Finals was special, and praised Cory as an underrated playmaker and valuable teammate.

This systematic review examines the use of artificial intelligence in higher education assessment, grading, and feedback. It focuses on AI’s effectiveness in automating and standardizing assessment processes, the accuracy and fairness of AI-driven grading compared with traditional methods, and the benefits of personalized feedback. The review is framed by the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge framework, which emphasizes the integration of technology, pedagogy, and content knowledge.

The passage describes AI tools, including machine learning and natural language processing, as capable of improving efficiency, consistency, scalability, and personalization in educational assessment. AI can support formative assessment, automate grading, analyze student performance data, provide real-time feedback, and help educators tailor instruction. It may reduce educator workload and improve feedback timeliness, though concerns remain about assessing complex skills such as creativity, critical thinking, and qualitative responses.

The review identifies key challenges, including data privacy, algorithmic transparency, ethical concerns, bias, infrastructure limitations, and educator and student acceptance. These issues are discussed globally and in African and Zambian higher education contexts, where AI adoption is described as emerging and potentially useful for addressing large class sizes, limited resources, and inconsistent assessment practices.

The methodology involved a systematic review of literature from databases including PubMed, Google Scholar, IEEE Xplore, ERIC, and Scopus. Studies published between 2010 and 2023 in peer-reviewed journals were included if they addressed AI in higher education assessment, grading, or feedback. Twenty studies were included and summarized using a PRISMA-based process.

The findings indicate that AI shows promise in improving efficiency, scalability, personalized feedback, and adaptive learning. Students generally respond positively to timely and personalized AI-generated feedback. However, the review emphasizes that AI should complement rather than replace human educators, especially in interpreting assessment outcomes and supporting meaningful learning. The conclusion states that AI has transformative potential in higher education but requires ethical implementation, transparent policies, diverse training data, and interdisciplinary collaboration to ensure fair and effective use.

The passage lists Birmingham City’s top ten away days from the previous decade, highlighting memorable wins, survival escapes, promotion moments and strong travelling support. Featured matches include the 1-0 win at Bristol City in 2017 that secured Championship survival, the 2-1 derby win at Wolves, a 5-2 victory at Fulham, promotion clinched with a 2-1 win at Reading in 2009, and a 3-0 win at Derby.
