Ray Lewis, Brian Urlacher, Randy Moss, Terrell Owens, Brian Dawkins, Bobby Beathard, Jerry Kramer and Robert Brazile were selected for the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

Best Buy’s Techtober sale offers the Acer Swift 16 AI for $800, $450 off. It includes 16 GB RAM, 1 TB storage, a 16-inch 2,880 x 1,800 OLED 120-Hz display, and an Intel Core Ultra 7 256V CPU. WIRED testing found 13 hours of YouTube playback. The article notes it is chunkier than some alternatives, including the Lenovo Yoga Slim 7i Aura Edition for $900.

The passage examines BP and the 2010 Deepwater Horizon disaster. On April 20, 2010, explosions forced workers to abandon the Transocean-owned rig leased by BP for the Macondo well; 11 people died and 17 were injured. The rig burned for 36 hours and sank on April 22. By the time the well was capped on July 15, nearly five million barrels of oil had spilled into the Gulf of Mexico, making it the largest marine oil spill in U.S. waters at the time.

The case reviews BP’s history, growth through mergers, cost cutting, rebranding as “Beyond Petroleum,” and organizational shift toward decentralized asset management. It also describes prior BP safety failures, including the 2005 Texas City refinery explosion and the 2006 Prudhoe Bay spill, and reports criticizing BP’s maintenance, process safety, and communication of safety priorities.

At Macondo, BP held operational authority while Transocean operated the rig, and several contractors were involved. The project was behind schedule and over budget. The Deepwater Horizon had known maintenance issues, including disabled alarms and recurring equipment problems.

The passage focuses on three disputed decisions before the blowout: using long string casing rather than a liner/tieback design, proceeding with fewer centralizers than Halliburton’s model recommended, and not running a cement bond log after cementing. It also discusses limited mud circulation and broader concerns that decisions favored cost and time savings over caution.

The spill caused environmental damage across Gulf states, affected wildlife and wetlands, disrupted tourism and fishing, reduced drilling activity under a federal moratorium, and created major financial and legal exposure for BP. BP established a $20 billion Gulf Coast Claims Facility to compensate affected individuals, businesses, and governments. As of early 2011, investigations continued, with responsibility disputed among the parties involved.

The speaker calls for national candor, courage, and action amid severe economic distress, asserting that “the only thing we have to fear is fear itself.” He describes collapsed values, rising taxes, frozen trade, unemployment, lost savings, and hardship for farmers and families, while arguing that the crisis is material rather than a failure of national substance. He condemns failed financial leadership, speculation, and the pursuit of profit over social values, calling for honesty, responsibility, and immediate action.

The primary task is to put people to work through government recruitment and public projects, improve land use, raise agricultural values, prevent foreclosures, reduce government costs, unify relief, and plan transportation, communications, and utilities. He calls for strict supervision of banking, credit, and investments, along with sound currency. Domestic recovery is presented as the first priority, though he also supports restoring world trade and pursuing a “good neighbor” policy abroad.

He emphasizes interdependence, discipline, sacrifice, and unified leadership, pledging to act within the constitutional system while seeking swift congressional cooperation. If Congress fails to act and the emergency remains critical, he says he will request broad executive power to wage war against the emergency. He closes by expressing faith in democracy, national unity, moral duty, and divine guidance.

The lecture shifts from preferences to how people use information, focusing on limited attention before later topics on beliefs and learning. It reviews evidence from change blindness, the gorilla test, and dichotic listening experiments showing that people can direct attention but miss unattended information, especially when distracted. Attention may be affected by environment, worries, sleep, noise, temptations, practice, and poverty-related factors.

The lecture argues that inattention can occur even in high-stakes settings. In the EntreMed stock example, positive cancer-cure news appeared in Nature and the New York Times in 1997 but produced a large stock price reaction only when the same story appeared on the New York Times front page months later. A similar confusion occurred when investors bought shares of a different company named Zoom during the rise of the video-conferencing firm.

Chetty et al.’s study on tax salience is used to measure inattention. Sales taxes are usually added at the register and may be less salient than posted prices. In a California grocery experiment, researchers added tags showing after-tax prices for selected goods. Demand for treated goods fell by about 8.8%, implying consumers had previously paid limited attention to sales taxes. Using beer tax variation, the study also found stronger responses to salient excise taxes than to less salient sales taxes, suggesting substantial inattention to non-transparent taxes.

The lecture discusses why tax salience matters. Governments may prefer low salience for revenue-raising taxes because reduced consumer reaction lowers distortions, while taxes on goods such as alcohol or tobacco may be made salient to change behavior because of externalities or internalities. Heterogeneity in attention can complicate welfare effects.

The final section explains how inattention can persist when people lack the right model of what matters. Examples include headaches potentially linked to food and historical failures to identify germs as the cause of childbed fever. A seaweed farming study in Indonesia showed experienced farmers knew many production details but neglected pod size. Trial participation alone had little effect, but presenting summarized trial results changed farming behavior, indicating that farmers failed to learn from available information until attention was directed to the relevant variable.

Uhl informed Sill that the Department disapproved of Allen asking the U.S. consul-general at Shanghai to help have Kim Ok-kiun’s Korean murderer surrendered to Korea, since U.S. consular authority there extended only to U.S. citizens.

Sill reported that Korean rebels defeated Government forces near Yun-won/Yung-won, captured their guns, and took Chon-ju after it was left unprotected. He told Admiral Skerrett that the rebellion in southern Korea was expanding, the Korean Government lacked adequate means to restore order, and Seoul could become dangerous for the 70 to 80 Americans residing there. Skerrett said most of his squadron was assigned to Bering Sea but would send a vessel to Chemulpo when possible. Sill noted that British, French, Chinese, and Japanese vessels had already gone to Chemulpo and said he would request U.S. naval aid only if urgently necessary.

Denby reported that, at Korea’s request, China sent troops to assist against insurgents: 1,500 men departed Tien-tsin, with the force to rise to 2,225, and three Chinese warships were ordered to Chemulpo. Li Hung-chang assured Japan and Russia the troops would withdraw after hostilities ended and told Japan it could send gunboats to protect its subjects.

The passage lists @ThingsExpo blog posts from Jan. 1–2, 2017, covering IoT, M2M, WebRTC, data platforms, blockchain, Microsoft, Scrum, mobile transformation, and technology predictions. Several posts report @ThingsExpo’s recognition by Onalytica as a leading IoT and M2M brand based on Twitter analysis. Other entries discuss connected home devices, WebRTC identity management, IoT software and data challenges, data monetization, election data science, blockchain investment and hype, and upcoming @ThingsExpo events in New York.

Ann Schmidt circulated Jan. 19, 2001 news mentions covering California’s power crisis, utility defaults, federal and state emergency responses, and Enron-related items. Reports said PG&E and Southern California Edison faced over $11.5 billion in power-related debt, defaults, possible bankruptcy, and supplier reluctance amid high wholesale power and natural gas prices under capped retail rates. California approved $400 million for power purchases, considered multiyear contracts, and avoided further blackouts while maintaining alerts. Energy Secretary Bill Richardson ordered natural gas suppliers to continue selling to California.

Other items included analysis that deregulation had changed utility investing, Ken Lay’s opposition to Western wholesale power price caps, Pennsylvania regulators rejecting comparisons to California, EOTT Energy Partners declaring a quarterly distribution, growth in bandwidth market price listings, and Enron Energy Services signing a 10-year energy management agreement with Owens-Illinois covering 53 facilities and projected purchases above $2 billion.

The MACD and RSI strategy combines two momentum indicators to analyze markets and develop trading rules. MACD is a moving average-based momentum oscillator mainly used for trends, while RSI measures price momentum and is commonly used to identify overbought or oversold conditions. The passage describes using MACD and RSI together, sometimes with a mean reversion filter, and emphasizes defining clear rules and backtesting. One backtest on SMH from 2001 produced 235 trades, an average gain of 0.88% per trade, and a 73% win rate. The passage notes that MACD and RSI can confirm each other, but some analysts view combining them as redundant because both are momentum indicators. Effectiveness depends on the asset, settings, rules, and backtesting results.

President Trump has made several policy reversals, most recently declining to label China a currency manipulator. Analyst Sean King said Trump could also reconsider withdrawing from the Trans-Pacific Partnership, which Japan supported and is trying to revive with other members. King noted the treaty remains valid until February 2018 and members might offer concessions.

The Nifty50 ended Tuesday with a modest gain of 29.65 points, aided by short covering amid rollover activity. Wednesday is expected to open tepid, with rollovers dominating and resistance near 10,650. Key resistance levels are 10,650 and 10,695, with support at 10,585 and 10,510. RSI and MACD remain bullish, but Nifty has not broken out of its broad range. Low India VIX and elevated put-call ratio may cap upside and increase profit-taking risk. Traders are advised to remain cautious and protect profits.

Jeff Carter and Drew Doughty discussed an overtime playoff win that gave their team a two-game series lead. Carter called his first playoff overtime goal a special moment and credited traffic in front of Martin Brodeur. Doughty said the team must reset for the games in Los Angeles, treat the series as new, improve its play, and expect the Devils to respond desperately. Both noted excitement about returning home and playing in front of louder fans.

The flexbone offense is a run-heavy system that evolved from the wishbone and uses option plays, misdirection, and spacing. It moves two backs, called A-backs, closer to the line of scrimmage to create more passing threat and is often associated with the triple option.

Key personnel include a decisive running quarterback who can make option reads and complete play-action passes, a strong and athletic fullback or B-back for inside runs and blocking, versatile A-backs who can run, block, and catch, strong-blocking wide receivers who can threaten deep, and athletic offensive linemen skilled in cut and combo blocks.

Its strengths include being uncommon in modern football, making it difficult for defenses to prepare for, and its ability to control the ball, extend time of possession, create assignment confusion, and wear down poor-tackling defenses. Its weaknesses include limited high-volume passing, difficulty overcoming late deficits or operating quickly in two-minute situations, high practice demands for option execution, and vulnerability in bad weather due to timing and ball-security requirements.

Common formations include the double slot, trips, and receivers over. Common runs include the triple option, midline option, and rocket toss. Common passes include play-action wheel, toss boot, and four verticals.

Navy, Army, and Air Force have traditionally used versions of the flexbone. Paul Johnson ran it at Georgia Southern, Navy, and Georgia Tech, including Georgia Tech’s 2009 ACC Championship team. It is also used at lower college levels and remains common in high school football, especially at smaller schools.

Mississippi State (8-0) will face Cincinnati (7-2) on Tuesday at BB&T Arena in Newport, Kentucky, its first road game and toughest non-conference matchup. Cincinnati, ranked No. 25 in the AP poll, has struggled with turnovers, while MSU forces 17 per game. Rebounding, especially Cincinnati’s offensive rebounding, is another key factor. Depth may also matter, as Cincinnati has used a seven-man rotation recently, while MSU could have eight or nine contributors and a full roster with Eli Wright returning from suspension.

Germany’s Protestant church is marking 500 years since the Reformation while seeking new ways to reach people as church attendance declines. At the Walloon Reformed Church of St. Augustine in Magdeburg, Pastor Ralf Peter Reimann holds a Twitter service where worshippers tweet about the liturgy and share prayers online, with messages displayed in real time. Reimann says social media can include people who live online and allow Christians to communicate with one another. The passage compares this to Luther’s use of printed pamphlets, which scholars describe as a form of early social media that spread Reformation ideas widely. Reactions to the Twitter service are mixed: some users share prayers and encouragement, while others find it too hectic. Older worshippers such as Ingeborg Brunner prefer traditional services with hymns, though she supports efforts to reach digitally minded believers.

Warren Buffett has said Berkshire Hathaway should repurchase shares when they trade below intrinsic value. In 2011, Berkshire set a buyback limit of 110% of book value, buying only $67 million, then raised it to 120% in 2012 and repurchased about $1.3 billion. No repurchases occurred from 2013 to 2016, though the stock approached the threshold several times. The author argues that 120% of book value has become more conservative because Berkshire’s intrinsic value has increasingly exceeded book value, and says repurchases should be considered if price-to-book returns to the low-to-mid 120% range.

The passage describes the Larry Swedroe Portfolio as an evidence-based, diversified investment approach allocating 30% to stocks and 70% to bonds to pursue long-term growth while reducing risk. Its typical allocation includes 15% small-cap value, 7.5% international small-cap value, 7.5% emerging markets, and 70% intermediate bonds. Swedroe emphasizes low-cost index funds or ETFs, diversification across assets and geographies, value investing, bottom-up analysis, long-term holding, avoiding market timing, and periodic rebalancing. The passage notes that small-cap value investing may offer higher returns but carries higher volatility and risk. A backtest using VIOV from 2012 showed a 3.71% annual return, lower than historical returns, with the large bond allocation expected to trail stocks over the long term.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture and related CUDA and DGX A100 features. A100 uses TF32 Tensor Cores by default for deep learning training, offering up to 8x throughput over FP32 on A100 and up to 10x over FP32 on V100, while FP16 or BF16 mixed precision can provide up to 2x more throughput than TF32. For HPC, A100 Tensor Cores support IEEE-compliant FP64, delivering 19.5 TFLOPS peak FP64 throughput and up to 2.5x Tesla V100 FP64 performance.

A100 supports mixed-precision HPC solvers through cuSOLVER and TCAIRS. In tests on 37 SuiteSparse matrices, TF32 was the fastest and most robust Tensor Core mode, with a 2.0x geomean speedup over the FP64 solver and up to 4x speedup on large complex matrices.

A100 introduces fine-grained structured sparsity using a 2:4 nonzero pattern, enabling compressed weights, reduced memory footprint and bandwidth, and up to 2x Tensor Core throughput by skipping zero values. NVIDIA describes a pruning and fine-tuning workflow for inference that yields virtually no accuracy loss across evaluated networks.

The architecture includes a 192 KB per-SM combined L1/shared memory subsystem, simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/s bandwidth, SECDED ECC protection, and a 40 MB L2 cache that is 6.7x larger than V100’s. A100 adds L2 residency controls and Compute Data Compression, which can improve DRAM and L2 bandwidth and effective L2 capacity.

A100’s third-generation Tensor Cores improve data sharing, reduce instruction and register accesses, and support stronger scaling for deep learning. New asynchronous copy instructions move data directly from global memory to shared memory, supported by asynchronous barriers and larger shared memory allocation.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can partition one A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory bandwidth, and fault isolation. MIG supports multi-tenant, single-user, and multi-user use cases, works with Linux and virtualization/container environments, and allows vGPU migration for load balancing and servicing.

A100 also includes third-generation NVLink with twelve links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, improved error handling, NVJPG hardware JPEG decode, optical flow acceleration, faster atomics, and five NVDEC units. CUDA 11 supports A100 features including Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 residency controls, and Cooperative Groups enhancements.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs connected through NVLink and NVSwitch, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance in a 6U system, up to 6x DGX-1 training performance, and up to 56 isolated accelerators through MIG. Its software stack includes CUDA, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC containers, and support for deep learning, inference, data analytics, and HPC workloads.

European shares headed for their biggest weekly loss since November 2016, pressured by rising bond yields, a stronger euro and weak bank earnings. Deutsche Bank fell after a larger-than-expected 2017 loss, while Caixabank and Sabadell declined on mixed results. Analysts noted risks from higher funding costs for leveraged investors and a possible technical correction. Germany’s DAX reversed sharply after earlier gains, hurt by euro strength and bond-yield pressure. Investors awaited U.S. payrolls data, with concern that strong figures could raise expectations for more U.S. rate hikes.

The Florida Second District Court of Appeal reversed summary judgment for The Personal Service Insurance Company and George Johnson, Jr. Danny Langston was injured in Florida while riding in a vehicle owned by George Johnson and driven by Fred Johnson. Langston alleged Fred drove negligently with George’s consent. The court held that Florida tort law applies to owner liability because the accident occurred in Florida, and under Florida’s dangerous instrumentality doctrine, George could be personally liable if he entrusted the vehicle to Fred.

The court then applied Ohio law to the surety bond issued in Ohio by Personal Service. The bond was issued under Ohio’s Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act and covered final judgments against the principal for damages resulting from ownership, maintenance, or use of a motor vehicle. The court distinguished cited Ohio cases and concluded that if Langston obtains a judgment against George, Personal Service would be liable under the bond. The case was remanded for further proceedings.

The paper examines how an Australian university addressed limited primary pre-service teachers’ arts education competencies by developing an Arts Specialism. Using education policy sociology theory and critical discourse analysis, it analyses policy influences, curriculum text production and implementation.

The literature identifies persistent problems in arts teacher education, including limited curriculum time, insufficient preparation, and gaps between arts education policy and practice. In response, the university developed four Arts Specialism courses following a compulsory foundation arts course, covering dance, drama, media arts, music and visual arts. The curriculum was shaped by national policy requirements, stakeholder support, professional arts organisations and standards emphasising expert content knowledge, pedagogical knowledge and effective teaching.

Implementation began in 2019 and was affected by COVID-19, requiring online adaptations. Courses included experiential learning, school-based projects, partnerships with arts organisations, and attention to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander content. Pre-service teacher feedback indicated increased confidence, deeper arts knowledge and stronger understanding of arts pedagogy.

The paper concludes that the Arts Specialism offers a model for improving generalist primary teachers’ arts education competencies, though challenges remain around curriculum time, staffing, resources and institutional support. It identifies future opportunities for broader implementation, policy support, arts industry collaboration and longitudinal research into graduates and school-based arts curriculum enactment.

A free five-week chronic pain self-management course will start in Montrose in May, delivered by Pain Association Scotland for Angus Health and Social Care Partnership. Open to Angus residents aged 18 or over, it aims to improve understanding of pain and teach skills such as stress management, pacing, relaxation, managing flare-ups and understanding medication. Sessions are informal and interactive, bringing together people with similar experiences. To book, contact the Primary Care Team by phone or email.

The passage discusses historical accounts and legends of children allegedly raised in the wild by animals. It notes that many such stories are hoaxes or apocryphal, but some continue to intrigue. Examples include Jean de Liège, who reportedly lived in Belgian woods for about sixteen years and later learned to speak; an Irish “sheep-boy” described by Nicholas Tulp as bleating and eating grass; and a Texas “Wolf Girl” legend involving a child allegedly living with wolves near Devil’s River. The passage questions claims such as becoming overgrown with hair, suggesting possible distortion or conditions like hypertrichosis, while leaving open the controversial possibility of such cases.

The passage argues that iPhones trade some Android flexibility and innovation for stronger security through Apple’s closed platform. It highlights iOS 10.3.1 security features including data encryption via password, PIN, or thumbprint; prompts for two-factor authentication; automatic data erasure after ten failed login attempts; and iCloud backups. It states iOS is not immune to malware but has built-in anti-malware layers, frequent updates, and an exclusive App Store that reduce risk. Find My Phone allows users to locate, lock, or erase a stolen device through iCloud. The passage also describes Apple’s app permission controls as more secure than Android’s and notes that Apple’s control over both hardware and software makes security patching easier, while Android fragmentation across manufacturers complicates updates and security.

U.S. homebuilder sentiment fell in April, with the NAHB/Wells Fargo index dropping to 68 from 71 in March, below analysts’ expected 70 but still indicating favorable conditions. Measures of current sales, future sales expectations, and buyer traffic also declined. New-home sales remain strong, supported by low mortgage rates and a solid job market, with February sales up nearly 13% from a year earlier.

The passage specifies SEV-ES/SNP guest-hypervisor communication requirements. For NMI injection, the hypervisor must not intercept IRET, must intercept #DB, and must rely on the guest’s “NMI Complete” message before injecting another NMI. Guests may determine their own safe point for sending this message.

Hardware debug register virtualization is supported when “DebugVirtualization” is enabled in SEV_FEATURES, with debug register state saved and restored in the VMSA and hypervisor intercepts cleared. Without support, the hypervisor must intercept DR7 reads and writes; the #VC handler caches DR7 writes and returns the cached value on reads. SMM and nested virtualization are not supported.

For SNP-protected guests using RestrictInjection, host notification is delivered through a #HV doorbell page. The page includes PendingEvent, which records non-maskable events and interrupt vectors, and NoEoiRequired, which optimizes end-of-interrupt handling. The doorbell page must be host-owned and accessed by the guest with C=0. Guests configure it using VMGEXIT operations such as preferred-address request, SET, and QUERY.

Guests should execute HLT with interrupts disabled and check interrupt state after resuming as if #HV was received. The host must emulate APIC interrupt lifecycle semantics, write pending vectors and non-maskable event bits into PendingEvent, manage NoFurtherSignal and NoEoiRequired, and recognize guest acknowledgement and EOI actions. Guests must atomically exchange PendingEvent to acknowledge interrupts, validate vectors, handle EOIs through NoEoiRequired or VMGEXIT, and process non-maskable events even when EFLAGS.IF=0. Non-cooperative host behavior may cause denial of service, while non-cooperative guest behavior may lose notifications but does not affect host integrity.

Korean War veteran John Bishop, who fought at Kapyong 66 years ago, doubts Canada could now influence rising tensions on the Korean Peninsula. Former ambassador Marius Grinius said Canada lost influence after adopting a “controlled engagement” policy that cut diplomatic ties with North Korea. Amid recent North Korean missile and nuclear tests, U.S. Vice-President Mike Pence warned that “strategic patience is over,” while North Korea accused the U.S. of creating conditions for thermonuclear war. Veteran Doug Finney said Canada must act because of humanitarian suffering in North Korea and the legacy of Canadians who served and died in the Korean War. Tina Park said Canada has humanitarian obligations under the responsibility to protect doctrine.

Last shot situations require preparation, poise, simple execution, and getting the ball to the team’s best player while avoiding having that player inbound. Teams should read the defense, send non-shooters to the offensive boards, and practice varied end-of-period scenarios with the game clock. Holding for the last shot is recommended with under 30 seconds when leading or trailing by fewer than eight points because the final shot of one period and first shot of the next can create a major scoring swing.

Basic timing calls for players to be positioned at 10 seconds, initiating at 8 seconds, shooting with 3–5 seconds left, and crashing the boards. Players should practice long passes, skip passes, baseball or semi-hook passes, half-court shots, tips, offensive rebounding, and intentional missed free throws. Conditioning is also emphasized late in close games.

Strategies include saving at least two timeouts, communicating timeout status, taking a timeout with 1–3 seconds left, advancing the ball to half court before calling timeout when possible, using quick counter breaks after opponent scores, shooting in line with the basket, having the bench count down, ensuring clock operation is correct, practicing from both sides, developing passing skills, and designating a reliable inbound passer.

Guidelines vary by time and situation, including out-of-bounds plays, quick breaks, rebounds followed by timeouts, intentional missed free throws, and jump balls. With 3 seconds, use one dribble; with 5 seconds, three dribbles; and with 7 seconds, five dribbles.

October features a supermoon on October 6, appearing up to 30% brighter and 14% larger than a typical full moon. The Draconid meteor shower peaks around October 8 and may produce up to 10 meteors per hour. The Orionid meteor shower, caused by Halley’s Comet debris, peaks October 21 with about 20 meteors per hour under a moonless sky.

The lecture begins with a correction to a homework typo and a brief review of reordering systems of equations using permutation matrices. Permutation matrices swap rows when multiplied from the left and columns when multiplied from the right; they are unitary because their transpose is their inverse. Reordering is described as a form of preconditioning used to reduce numerical error through pivoting or to minimize fill-in for sparse systems.

The instructor reviews sparse matrices through a Plinko-based diffusion model, where probability spreads 50/50 to neighboring cells at each level. Repeated multiplication by a sparse matrix produces spreading distributions, and certain distributions remain unchanged under transformation, introducing the idea of eigenvectors.

Eigenvectors are defined as vectors that, when multiplied by a matrix, remain in the same direction but are stretched by an eigenvalue. Eigenvalues are found by solving the characteristic equation det(A − λI) = 0. Examples show that diagonal and triangular matrices have eigenvalues equal to their diagonal entries. Eigenvalues may have algebraic multiplicity, and their eigenvectors may have geometric multiplicity, the dimension of the null space of A − λI.

The lecture applies eigenvalues to a chemical reaction rate matrix, where a zero eigenvalue corresponds to steady state and other eigenvalues represent rate processes. Eigenvectors can be found by Gaussian elimination, though they are not unique in magnitude.

Matrices with a complete set of eigenvectors can be diagonalized as A = WΛW⁻¹, enabling simpler solutions of linear systems and decoupling of linear ordinary differential equations. For symmetric matrices with normalized eigenvectors, W⁻¹ = Wᵀ. If a complete eigenvector set is unavailable, other decompositions such as Jordan normal form, Schur decomposition, or singular value decomposition may be needed.

Taylor Swift has broken numerous records across awards, charts, streaming, touring, and wealth. She became the youngest artist to write and perform a No. 1 Hot Country Songs hit with “Our Song,” the youngest CMA entertainer of the year, and, at the time, the youngest Grammy album of the year winner with “Fearless.” She later became the first woman to win album of the year twice and three times, then the first artist to win it four times with “Midnights.”

Swift holds the record for most American Music Awards, most No. 1 hits on Billboard’s US Digital Song Sales chart, and the most Grammy song of the year nominations. She surpassed Shania Twain for most weeks at No. 1 on Billboard’s Top Country Albums chart, and “All Too Well (10 Minute Version)” became the longest song to reach No. 1.

She is the only artist to occupy all top 10 spots on the Billboard Hot 100 in one week, doing so with “Midnights” and again with “The Tortured Poets Department.” Her albums have repeatedly broken Spotify single-day streaming records, including “The Life of a Showgirl,” while “The Fate of Ophelia” became Spotify’s most-streamed song in a single day. Her latest releases also set Apple Music and Amazon Music records.

Swift’s Eras Tour became the highest-grossing music tour ever at $2 billion, and her reported net worth reached $1.6 billion, making her the world’s richest female musician.

The passage describes SD Memory Card physical-layer behavior for write, erase, discard, lock/unlock, command handling, switching functions, timing, CRC, and capacity-dependent operations.

Block write transfers append CRC bits to each block, and the card checks CRC before writing. Erroneous data is discarded. Write commands may be rejected for block length, address, misalignment, or write-protection errors. Multiple block write is preferred for speed, and ACMD23 can predefine blocks to be pre-erased before CMD25. ACMD22 reports the number of well-written blocks after errors in multiple block writes.

Erase operations use CMD32 to set the start block, CMD33 to set the end block, and CMD38 to execute. Out-of-sequence erase commands set error bits and reset the sequence. Write-protected sectors are not erased. DISCARD and Full User Area Logical Erase (FULE) are CMD38 variants supported only for SDHC and SDXC cards, not SPI. DISCARD treats contents as “don’t care,” while FULE logically erases the full user area. Both use DAT0 low to indicate busy.

Three write-protect methods are described: a mechanical switch handled by the host, optional internal card protection, and password-based lock operation. CMD42 manages password lock/unlock using nonvolatile PWD and PWD_LEN registers. Locked cards allow only basic commands, ACMD41, CMD16, and lock-related commands; data access is blocked. Force Erase can erase card contents and clear PWD when the card is locked.

Card Ownership Protection (COP) adds Force Erase Password (FEP) registers. When FEP is set, standard Force Erase and clearing PWD are disabled; COP Unlock is required after reset to access COP functions. FEP Force Erase erases user contents and PWD only when the correct FEP is supplied, while FEP itself remains unchanged.

APP_CMD (CMD55) marks the next command as application-specific. Defined legal ACMDs return APP_CMD status; undefined or illegal handling depends on command definition and state. CMD6 switches or checks card functions, including bus speed, command system, driver strength, and power limit. Mode 0 checks support and current or power consumption; Mode 1 switches functions. Function status is returned as a 512-bit data block.

High-Speed mode raises interface speed to 25 MB/sec using a 50 MHz clock and is enabled by CMD6 on Version 1.10 or later cards if supported. CMD8 checks host voltage compatibility during initialization for Version 2.00 or later cards.

SDSC cards use byte addressing and CMD16-defined block length, while SDHC and SDXC cards use 512-byte block addressing with fixed 512-byte memory access blocks and do not support partial or misaligned memory access. SDHC and SDXC also do not support write-protected groups.

The host may slow or stop the SD bus clock with restrictions, including required clocks after transactions and special ACMD41 handling. CRC7 protects commands and most responses; CRC16 protects data blocks. Commands with CRC errors or illegal commands are not executed and set status error bits.

Read, write, and erase timeout behavior is defined by card type and operation. SDHC writes have a maximum busy length of 250 ms, while SDXC may indicate up to 500 ms in specified cases. UHS-II uses Data Bursts with busy indication after each burst.

Commands use a fixed 48-bit format with start bit, transmission bit, command index, 32-bit argument, CRC, and end bit. Command classes define supported functionality, with several classes mandatory and others optional. Commands and application-specific commands are listed by class, with some reserved for security, command-system expansion, manufacturer use, or future specifications.

The passage explains exponential moving averages (EMA), a moving average indicator that gives more weight to recent prices than a simple moving average (SMA), making it more responsive but still lagging. EMA is used to smooth price data, identify trends, support and resistance, and trading signals, often alongside other indicators.

Backtests on SPY suggest EMA strategies can work differently depending on the time period. Short-term EMA mean-reversion strategies performed best when buying after the close crossed below a short EMA and selling after it crossed above; the best cited result used a 5-day EMA with a 7.41% CAGR and 30.54% maximum drawdown. Long-term trend-following strategies performed better with longer EMAs, buying when the close crossed above the EMA and selling when it crossed below; the 200-day EMA returned 7.84% with a 25.94% maximum drawdown. Other tests using fixed holding periods found the best result from buying below the 50-day EMA and selling after 200 days, producing 10.17% per trade.

The passage concludes that EMA strategies work best with either very short or very long moving average periods: mean reversion for short periods and trend following for long periods. It also notes that EMA can create false signals and is often best used as one part of a broader trading strategy.

The study conducted a systematic literature review of leading Information Systems journals from 2000 to 2017 using the terms “digital business strategy,” “digital transformation,” and “business digitalization.” From an initial 292 articles, 54 were selected based on titles, abstracts, and keywords, and 28 were retained after full-text review. The analysis followed Bandara’s and Wolifswinkel’s guidelines, using coding to identify dimensions and attributes of digital transformation, digital business strategy, and organizational capabilities.

Publication activity increased from 2009 and rose considerably in 2016. Research focused mainly on automotive, banking, telecommunications, healthcare, oil and gas, and manufacturing sectors, with many studies based in the US and European countries and fewer in Asia, the Middle East, Latin America, and Africa.

The review identified twelve dimensions of digital transformation, six of digital business strategy, and ten of organizational capabilities. Shared dimensions include collaborative digital platform ecosystems across all three concepts; technology use and structural changes between digital transformation and digital business strategy; digital leadership, agile and scalable operations, digitally enabled customer service, and digital artefacts between digital transformation and organizational capabilities; and dynamic capabilities between digital business strategy and organizational capabilities.

The study proposes that digital transformation is digital business strategy in action, supported by organizational capabilities. It presents conceptual frameworks showing how organizational capabilities and digital business strategy relate to digital transformation. The findings aim to support researchers and organizational leaders in understanding and deploying capabilities needed for digital transformation in electronic commerce.

April the giraffe’s livestream became YouTube’s second-most-watched live channel, with over 232 million views. Viewership peaked during her calf’s birth Saturday, when 1.2 million watched simultaneously and 14 million tuned in that day.

Editors of the Foreign Relations series have access to retired State Department records, including central files, lot files, Executive Secretariat files, and overseas post files. Records from 1981–1989 will be transferred to the National Archives and made available after declassification and processing. Research also uses restricted documents from the Reagan Library and other agencies; some published material comes from still-classified documents, and some source documents may not yet be fully available. Reagan Library collections include foreign affairs records from White House offices, State, NSC, CIA, Defense, and the Joint Chiefs. Some records were scanned through the Remote Archives Capture project, though attachments could not always be verified.

Documents are arranged chronologically by Washington time, with memoranda of conversation dated by the conversation. Texts are reproduced closely, preserving original spelling and formatting except for silent correction of obvious typographical errors. Brackets indicate editorial corrections, additions, omissions, or still-classified material.

The paper studies multi-period resource allocation under stochastic demands, aiming to maximize revenue subject to a finite resource constraint. It first formulates a static open-loop allocation problem, shows it is convex, and solves it efficiently via bisection on a dual variable using marginal demand quantile functions. The authors note that this static approach ignores temporal correlations and sequentially revealed demand information.

To address this, they propose a shrinking horizon sequential policy similar to model predictive control. At each time step, the policy allocates resources only for the current period, then re-solves the remaining problem after observing demand and conditioning the future demand distribution on past observations. The method is a heuristic and requires conditional quantile functions. When demands are independent, the sequential policy reduces to the static solution.

Simulations use jointly log-normal synthetic demand data with varying horizons. For independent demands, static and sequential allocations match. For correlated demands, the sequential policy achieves higher revenue than the static and roll-forward baselines and performs close to an oracle allocation that knows realized demands in advance. The paper concludes that the adaptive method improves revenue by exploiting temporal demand correlations and observed information.

Research links technological maturity with stronger business performance and finds that digitally mature companies have distinct data cultures. Digital leaders adopt a growth mindset, encourage experimentation and long-term skill development, use data to create shared context and transparency, empower teams to measure progress, and align the organization through common data-driven goals. They combine clear metrics with flexibility, allowing teams autonomy in how they achieve objectives.

Digital laggards often rely on legacy systems, short-term priorities, risk aversion, narrow training, siloed data, restricted access, qualitative measures, and poorly connected goals. Their decision-making may depend more on hierarchy, expertise, or process adherence than shared data and objective metrics.

The passage argues that successful digital transformation requires cultural change as well as technology. Strong data cultures align organizations vertically through shared objectives and horizontally through transparent data access. Organizations may begin as data novices, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant, depending on their cultural and technical maturity.

The article examines how anti-CRT legislation in Idaho, Utah, and Arizona affects Native content instruction in teacher education at predominantly white institutions. Using Tribal Critical Race Theory, the authors argue that CRT bans reinforce colonial unknowing by silencing Native perspectives, perpetuating Native invisibility in public education, and discouraging culturally sustaining pedagogies. They describe state anti-CRT measures, the predominantly white teacher workforce, limited preparation in Native-centered teaching, and uneven implementation of Native inclusion standards. Drawing on stories, interviews, and observations from their research and teaching, they show how Native histories, sovereignty, and contemporary presence are often excluded or resisted in K-12 and teacher education. The authors conclude that critical democratic education must include Native nationhood, sovereignty, histories, and knowledge to support democratic citizenship and defend tribal sovereignty.

Five-year-old Lyla Carreyn is home after receiving a kidney from her 4K teacher, Beth Battista. She was hospitalized since February 21 and had post-surgery complications, including an infection. Lyla still needs over 15 daily medications, labs three times weekly, and possible readmission if infection or rejection appears.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on September 4, 2020, it completed the sale of $5.0 billion, before commissions, of common stock through its previously disclosed at-the-market offering program. Final settlement of the shares was expected by September 9, 2020.

Sven Henrich agrees with Alan Greenspan’s view that both stocks and bonds are in bubbles. The study estimates U.S. county-month face mask-wearing from September 2020 to May 2021 using 8.3 million valid responses from the COVID-19 Trends and Impact Survey. Researchers used Bayesian binomial regression, raking by age, sex, and education, and bias correction based on discrepancies between self-reported and ground-truth vaccination data. Masking behavior showed strong spatial heterogeneity, varied substantially within states, and was higher in urban than rural counties. Masking peaked in January 2021 and declined sharply in May 2021, coinciding with increasing vaccination, declining cases, reduced worry about severe illness, and changing CDC guidance and mask mandates. Community-reported masking closely approximated bias-corrected self-reported masking. The authors conclude that fine-scale behavioral data are important for targeted public health strategies and infectious disease modeling, while noting limitations from survey bias, sample size, and assumptions used in debiasing.

Russ Tedrake introduces walking robots as a major unsolved robotics control problem, arguing that control rather than actuator power is the fundamental challenge. He identifies two key technical issues for applying previous optimal control tools to walking: limit cycles and impacts, or hybrid dynamics.

Using the Van der Pol oscillator, he explains stable limit cycles as periodic motions that nearby trajectories approach without synchronizing in time. He discusses why ordinary asymptotic trajectory convergence and standard Lyapunov approaches are insufficient, then introduces Poincaré sections and maps as a way to convert limit cycle stability into fixed-point stability in discrete time. Local stability is characterized by eigenvalues of the Poincaré map gradient having magnitude less than one.

Tedrake then reviews walking research, including Muybridge’s photographic gait studies, McMahon’s ballistic walker model, and Tad McGeer’s passive dynamic walkers, which walked down ramps without motors or controllers. He presents the rimless wheel as a simple model capturing essential passive walking dynamics: gravity adds energy downhill, inelastic foot impacts dissipate energy, and their balance creates a stable rolling limit cycle. The rimless wheel’s return map can be analyzed analytically, including rolling and standing fixed points and basins of attraction.

He explains that impact losses dominate walking dynamics and notes that push-off before collision can improve efficiency. Extending the rimless wheel by adding a hip pin joint yields the compass gait model, which can passively walk down a slope but has a smaller basin of attraction. Adding knees introduces another collision while preserving similar limit cycle behavior. The lecture concludes by previewing methods for applying optimization and gradient computations to hybrid walking dynamics.

This study evaluated the Disk Potentiation Test for detecting KPC and MBL carbapenemases among 147 imipenem-resistant gram-negative clinical isolates collected from Evercare Hospital, Dhaka, from January to June 2020. All isolates were resistant to imipenem, with resistance most common among patients over 60 years old and more frequent in males. The ICU had the highest prevalence of resistant isolates. KPC was detected in 39 isolates (26.53%), MBL in 66 isolates (44.89%), and both enzymes in 36 isolates (24.49%). Acinetobacter baumannii was the predominant organism carrying both enzymes, followed by Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Escherichia coli. KPC- and MBL-positive isolates were most common in ICU patients, and co-producing isolates were most frequently found in tracheal aspirates. The findings highlight the need for antimicrobial stewardship, infection control, and monitoring of carbapenemase-producing organisms in healthcare settings.

The passage describes AGESA host environment procedures for stack setup/removal and related services. The stack initialization routine is stackless assembler using register passing, creates a pre-memory stack region across processor cores, maps it globally, sets x86-64 MTRRs, creates a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instance, and must run on all cores. It handles protected mode and real mode differently and returns success, warning for stack reentry, or fatal error for unknown processor family. A stack removal routine disables Cache-as-RAM after memory is available, flushes cache lines, preserves EBX, must be run on all cores, and should be invoked only by the BSP.

The passage also describes AmdCreateStruct, which allocates and initializes AGESA parameter structures using PreMemHeap, PostMemDram, or host-provided storage, requiring a stack and proper release via AmdReleaseStruct. The passage examines curriculum literacy as an expanded form of literacy involving understanding, evaluating, adapting, and implementing educational programs. It emphasizes its importance for teachers, administrators, and students, particularly in relation to digital transformation, educational quality, equity, and effective teaching.

The study aimed to investigate the role, importance, themes, and development of curriculum literacy through thematic content analysis. Data were collected from English and Turkish peer-reviewed articles indexed in Scopus using the keyword “curriculum literacy.” After exclusions, 29 studies were analyzed by year, keyword, discipline, country, method, sample, and theme.

Findings show that research on curriculum literacy was limited before 2000, increased gradually between 2000 and 2020, and rose sharply between 2020 and 2025. Early studies emphasized social studies education and basic curriculum literacy; later studies focused on activity theory, culture, digital tools, dyslexia, diagnosis, empowerment, artificial intelligence, and interdisciplinary integration. Most studies were in social sciences, with fewer in psychology, arts and humanities, computer science, engineering, environmental science, mathematics, and biological sciences. Australia and the United States had the most studies, followed by Türkiye.

The reviewed studies indicate that curriculum literacy supports teachers’ pedagogical skills, use of instructional materials, digital technology integration, critical evaluation of curricula, and responsiveness to students’ individual and social needs. A weak but positive relationship was found between digital literacy and curriculum literacy. The passage concludes that curriculum literacy should be strengthened through teacher education, digital resources, interdisciplinary approaches, inclusive educational policies, and support for innovative teaching methods.

The paper examines digitalization in Vietnamese higher education and offers recommendations. Vietnam’s higher education system includes 237 universities, with governance shared among MOET, other ministries, local authorities, foreign organizations, and the Prime Minister’s Office for the two national universities. Before COVID-19, digitalization was uneven: some institutions had learning management systems and digital initiatives, but many lacked infrastructure, funding, skills, online teaching capacity, and coordinated governance.

Government policy has strongly shaped digital transformation, especially the 2020 National Digital Transformation Program and the 2022–2025 education digital transformation project. These policies prioritize online learning platforms, digital materials, shared resource databases, online assessment, recognition of online learning, and digital management systems.

COVID-19 accelerated digitalization. MOET amended regulations to allow portions of full-time and graduate programs to be delivered online, and many institutions expanded learning management systems, blended learning, paperless student services, and digital administration. National systems such as education databases, HEMIS, e-learning repositories, and Vietnamese Knowledge Systems have also developed. However, progress varies across institutions, and challenges remain in funding, infrastructure, system integration, copyright, quality control, and digital skills.

The paper recommends clearer policy guidance and dissemination, increased government funding and partnerships, training for institutional leaders, lecturer support in digital skills, online pedagogy, intellectual property, personalized learning, and mentoring, plus student training and expanded online administrative services.

A bear trap is a bullish trading pattern in an uptrend where a sharp price drop breaks support and tricks traders into shorting or selling before price reverses upward. It can affect retail traders through losses, triggered stop-loss orders, and FOMO-driven decisions. Traders may spot potential bear traps using support breaks, divergences in indicators like MACD or RSI, volume, moving averages, fundamentals, and backtesting. To avoid them, traders should not rely only on price, should consider broader market and company factors, remain disciplined, avoid crowd behavior, and backtest strategies. NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture improves effective memory bandwidth through enhanced lossless compression, delivering about 50% effective bandwidth improvement over Pascal in TU102-based RTX 2080 Ti versus GP102-based GTX 1080 Ti. Turing adds a new display engine supporting DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, HDR processing, tone mapping, and VESA DSC 1.2, plus enhanced NVENC and NVDEC video blocks for higher-quality encoding and broader decoding support.

Turing supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink to simplify VR headset connectivity by carrying power, display, and data through one USB-C connector. For SLI, TU102 and TU104 replace MIO and PCIe transfers with second-generation NVLink, supporting two-way SLI and higher-bandwidth display topologies, but not 3-way or 4-way SLI.

A major feature of Turing is real-time ray tracing using dedicated RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs with NVIDIA RTX software. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, offloading work from SMs and enabling hybrid rendering that combines rasterization and ray tracing. Turing ray tracing is described as up to 10 times faster than Pascal software ray tracing and supports reflections, refractions, shadows, ambient occlusion, physics, audio simulation, AI visibility queries, and path tracing workflows. Denoising and BVH acceleration reduce the number of rays needed for usable real-time results.

Turing also introduces NVIDIA NGX, a deep learning graphics stack using Tensor Cores. NGX supports features such as DLSS, DLSS 2X, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS uses trained neural networks to produce image quality comparable to TAA with less shading work, while DLSS 2X aims for image quality close to 64x supersampling.

The architecture adds Mesh Shading with Task and Mesh Shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and enable more flexible geometry processing. Variable Rate Shading lets developers vary shading rates across 16x16 screen regions or per primitive, supporting content adaptive shading, motion adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and appearance sampling by storing shading results in texture space for reuse across pixels, frames, or stereo views.

Turing expands Multi-View Rendering to support up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 views at the API level, improving VR, wide-FOV headsets, shadow rendering, and instancing. It also supports bindless Constant Buffer Views and Unordered Access Views under DX12 Tier 3 resource binding and Tier 2 resource heaps.

For VR, Turing combines VirtualLink, Multi-View Rendering, Variable Rate Shading, foveated rendering, and RT Core acceleration for VRWorks Audio. The TU104 GPU includes up to 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and one x8 NVLink link, and is used in products including GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. Tesla T4 uses a TU104 configuration aimed at inferencing. TU106, used in GeForce RTX 2070, includes 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but lacks NVLink and SLI support.

The passage defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering, weighting Tensor, FP32, RT Core, and INT32 operations by representative frame usage. It also explains ray tracing basics, including reverse ray casting from the camera, BVH acceleration, BVH building and refitting, denoising, and applications such as ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections. It concludes that hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH algorithms, and RT Cores together make real-time ray tracing possible on Turing GPUs.

The lecture reviews prior results on sequences: convergence can be characterized by absolute differences tending to 0, and the squeeze theorem shows that a sequence trapped between two sequences with the same limit converges to that limit. Using the binomial theorem and elementary inequalities, it proves special limits: \(1/n^p \to 0\) for \(p>0\), \(p^{1/n}\to 1\) for \(p>0\), and \(n^{1/n}\to 1\).

The lecture then introduces limsup and liminf for bounded sequences. For a bounded sequence \((x_n)\), define \(a_n=\sup\{x_k:k\ge n\}\) and \(b_n=\inf\{x_k:k\ge n\}\). The limsup is \(\lim a_n\), and the liminf is \(\lim b_n\). It is proved that \(a_n\) is monotone decreasing and bounded, while \(b_n\) is monotone increasing and bounded, so both limits exist. Also, \(\liminf x_n\le \limsup x_n\).

Examples show that for \(x_n=(-1)^n\), the limsup is 1 and the liminf is -1, while for \(x_n=1/n\), both are 0. The lecture notes that the sequences used to define limsup and liminf are not necessarily subsequences of the original sequence.

A theorem is proved stating that every bounded sequence has subsequences converging to its limsup and liminf. This yields the Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem: every bounded sequence has a convergent subsequence. Finally, it is shown that a bounded sequence converges if and only if its limsup equals its liminf, and in that case both equal the ordinary limit.

This retrospective single-center study in China compared tenecteplase with alteplase for intravenous thrombolysis in acute ischemic stroke. It included 120 patients treated with tenecteplase and 144 treated with alteplase within 4.5 hours of symptom onset. Baseline characteristics were largely comparable, though hyperlipidemia and atrial fibrillation differed between groups.

Tenecteplase was associated with shorter onset-to-treatment time, door-to-needle time, and door-to-puncture time. More patients receiving tenecteplase met target times for door-to-needle time ≤45 minutes and door-to-puncture time ≤120 minutes. Logistic regression identified tenecteplase as an independent predictor of achieving these workflow targets.

Clinically, the tenecteplase group had a higher rate of 24-hour NIHSS improvement and shorter hospital stays. Rates of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and any intracranial hemorrhage did not significantly differ between groups. Tenecteplase was an independent predictor of 24-hour NIHSS improvement, while baseline NIHSS and atrial fibrillation were associated with hemorrhage outcomes.

The authors concluded that tenecteplase may improve early clinical outcomes and treatment workflow efficiency in acute ischemic stroke, with safety comparable to alteplase, but noted limitations including single-center design, nonrandomized treatment assignment, early outcome assessment, and predominance of mild to moderate stroke cases.

The study examines digitalization in education, particularly in private-sector education departments, and aims to contribute to related literature. It notes that technological development, the digital economy, COVID-19, remote work, and distance education have accelerated digitalization in working life and education. The literature review defines digital education as the use of digital technologies, e-learning, or technology-enhanced learning, and discusses concepts such as Education 4.0, hybrid learning, gamification, augmented reality, virtual reality, personalized learning, and digital literacy. It also highlights risks including cybersecurity, cybercrime, inequality of opportunity, and the digital skills gap.

The research used a qualitative method with a semi-structured interview form. Participants were 20 expert-managers working in private-sector education. Due to the pandemic, forms were sent by email, and five participants were interviewed via Zoom. Data were analyzed through content analysis.

Most participants worked in national companies, had over 15 years of experience, and were employed in companies with 300 or more employees. Reported challenges in digitalizing education included technological problems, financial resources, unsuitable content, limited participation, lack of digital materials, reduced educational efficiency, participant fear or resistance, lack of digital literacy, distraction, and inequality of opportunity.

To adapt to digitalization, participants reported using online and hybrid training, digital education systems, online academies, training videos, workshops, projects, digital platforms, and technological tools. Positive effects included time- and location-independent access, time and cost savings, equality of opportunity, reaching larger audiences, adapting to personal learning pace, increased accessibility, and expanded e-learning content. Negative effects included participant indifference, concentration problems, lack of trained workforce, cognitive and physical difficulties, reduced interaction, lower efficiency in activities, difficulty with practice-oriented activities, cyberbullying, measurement problems, and cheating tendencies.

Participants defined digitalization in education mainly through technological opportunities and easy access, including online platforms, digital training materials, virtual reality, augmented reality, artificial intelligence, automation of training processes, and access to education regardless of time or place.

The study concludes that digitalization in education is an undeniable reality, but participants do not expect face-to-face education to disappear completely. It recommends adapting educational content through technological tools, virtual reality, and gamification, and suggests that practices in the private sector may inform digitalization in national and higher education.

The study presents an enhanced DiffCSP guided diffusion framework for inverse design of superconductors. The model was pretrained on over two million crystal structures from the Alexandria Database to learn structural priors, then fine-tuned on 7,183 labeled conventional superconductors to condition generation on critical temperature (Tc). Using classifier-free guidance, the authors generated 200,000 crystal structures and screened them through machine-learning relaxation, deduplication, metallicity checks, thermodynamic stability filters, phonon stability calculations, BEE-NET Tc prediction, and DFT electron-phonon calculations.

Validation showed that guidance could shift generated Tc distributions toward in-domain targets such as 10 K, while an out-of-distribution target of 110 K did not produce high-Tc structures, indicating that the model remained constrained by learned structural priors. From 34,027 unique novel generated structures, the workflow identified 773 candidates with DFT-calculated Tc > 5 K and energy above hull below 200 meV/atom. This corresponded to a 2.3% hit rate, compared with 0.017% for an element-substitution baseline and 0.83% in a prior generative study.

The final candidates were mostly multicomponent compounds, especially ternaries. Eighteen candidates were selected for arc-melting synthesis and characterization after filtering for composition, radioactivity, meltability, structural diversity, and stability. Nine showed superconductivity above 4.2 K, but measured Tc values were generally lower than predicted. X-ray diffraction indicated that the predicted ordered structures generally did not form; samples were mostly disordered BCC solid solutions or multiphase mixtures.

The authors conclude that generative AI can improve superconducting candidate discovery rates but emphasize limitations in synthesizability prediction, incomplete convex hull data in underexplored chemistries, and the need for experimental feedback, disorder-aware screening, and active-learning workflows.

SynDoc is a hybrid framework for domain-specific visually rich document understanding and key information extraction in zero-shot settings. It combines a discriminative vision-language pretrained “warmer” with a generative multimodal large language model. SynDoc uses OCR or PDF parsing, MLLM-driven semantic and spatial question generation, and quality verification to create synthetic training data. The warmer is adaptively tuned for structural and semantic understanding, then its retrieved entities guide the MLLM through recursive inference.

Experiments on FormNLU, CORD, Ephoie, and FUNSD show that incorporating warmer outputs generally improves MLLM performance, especially on domain-specific datasets. Gemini-based SynDoc outperforms vanilla Gemini on most domain-specific benchmarks, while cross-domain FUNSD shows possible noise effects. Structural adaptation, meaningfulness verification, prior MLLM outputs, top-K retrieved candidates, and iterative inference generally improve performance, though benefits vary by dataset and model. The study concludes that SynDoc improves domain-specific document key information extraction, but further work is needed for stronger cross-domain robustness.

The lecture begins constructing spacetime for compact spherical bodies: finite sources with vacuum exteriors. For a static, spherically symmetric body, the metric is written in Schwarzschild coordinates using an areal radius, with comparison to isotropic coordinates and the weak-field form.

The exterior vacuum region has zero stress-energy, so the Ricci tensor is set to zero. Solving the equations gives the Schwarzschild metric, with the integration constant fixed by matching the Newtonian weak-field limit. Birkhoff’s theorem is introduced: the exterior vacuum of any spherically symmetric body is described by the Schwarzschild metric, even if the source varies in time while preserving spherical symmetry. A brief proof shows that time dependence can be removed or absorbed into the time coordinate.

For the interior, the body is modeled as a static perfect fluid with pressure and density depending only on radius, both vanishing outside the stellar surface. The Einstein equations yield a mass function defined by integrating the density, though this gravitational mass differs from the proper-volume baryonic mass because of gravitational binding energy. The rr equation gives an equation for the metric function involving mass and pressure. Combining this with local stress-energy conservation gives the relativistic hydrostatic equilibrium equation.

The resulting coupled equations for pressure, mass, and metric potential form the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, used to build static spherically symmetric fluid bodies in general relativity given a central density and an equation of state.

Turing adds hardware support for USB Type-C and VirtualLink, enabling VR headsets to receive power, display, and data through a single USB-C connector. Turing TU102 and TU104 use second-generation NVLink for SLI data transfers, supporting two-way SLI and higher-bandwidth display topologies, while 3-way and 4-way SLI are not supported.

The architecture enables real-time ray tracing through RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs combined with NVIDIA RTX software. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, offloading shader multiprocessors and enabling hybrid rendering that combines rasterization with ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, ambient occlusion, and other effects. NVIDIA describes Turing ray tracing as significantly faster than Pascal, with RT Cores enabling around 10x faster ray tracing in cited workloads.

Turing also introduces NVIDIA NGX, a deep learning-based graphics stack using Tensor Cores for AI features such as DLSS, DLSS 2X, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS is trained from high-quality supersampled images to produce output similar to TAA with less shading work, while DLSS 2X aims to approach 64x supersampled quality.

New graphics features include Mesh Shading with Task and Mesh Shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and improve geometry processing; Variable Rate Shading to adjust shading rates per 16×16-pixel region for content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, and foveated rendering; Texture Space Shading to decouple visibility and shading and reuse shaded texels; and Multi-View Rendering to render multiple views or instances in a single pass.

For VR, Turing combines VirtualLink, Multi-View Rendering, foveated rendering through VRS, and RT Core acceleration for VRWorks Audio. Turing also expands resource management with bindless Constant Buffer Views and Unordered Access Views and Tier 2 resource heaps.

The TU104 GPU includes up to 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and one x8 NVLink link, and is used in products including GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. The Tesla T4 uses a TU104 configuration with 40 SMs, 2560 CUDA Cores, and 320 Tensor Cores. The TU106 GPU used in GeForce RTX 2070 includes 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but lacks NVLink and SLI support.

The passage explains RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric combining Tensor, FP32, RT Core, and INT32 operations according to estimated hybrid-rendering workload usage. It also outlines ray tracing fundamentals, including ray casting, BVH acceleration structures, denoising, ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, and concludes that hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH algorithms, and RT Cores together enable real-time ray tracing on Turing GPUs.

The main topic is proving soundness of the Fiat-Shamir transform in the standard model for a specific parallel-repeated zero-knowledge protocol for Hamiltonicity. The class recalls that Fiat-Shamir removes interaction by replacing verifier challenges with a hash function. Security was previously shown in the random oracle model, but the goal is to prove security for an explicit hash function.

The Hamiltonicity protocol is reviewed: the prover commits to a randomly permuted graph and responds to a verifier bit by either opening a Hamiltonian cycle or opening the nonedges with the permutation. One repetition has soundness 1/2, so the protocol is repeated in parallel with fresh permutations to obtain negligible soundness. The lecture emphasizes that the parallel-repeated version is the protocol under discussion.

The result presented is from Canetti, Lombardi, and Wichs (2019). The key idea is that for every first prover message α, there is only a small set, and in this case essentially one, “bad” challenge β that allows cheating. If a hash function could avoid this bad β for every α, Fiat-Shamir soundness would follow. However, computing the bad β is hard because it requires opening commitments.

To address this, the commitment is instantiated using public-key encryption: the prover encrypts the committed bits, and later opens them by revealing encryption randomness. A trusted common reference string supplies the public key so the prover cannot maliciously choose a bad key. The corresponding secret key acts as a trapdoor that can open commitments in the analysis and determine the bad challenge.

Since the trapdoor cannot be public, the construction uses fully homomorphic encryption (FHE). FHE allows computation on encrypted data: given encryptions of input bits and a circuit, it produces an encryption of the circuit output. The Fiat-Shamir hash key contains an FHE public key and an encryption of a circuit. Evaluation homomorphically computes the circuit on α.

In the real scheme the encrypted circuit may be a dummy all-zero circuit. In the proof, semantic security allows replacing it with a special circuit g* that uses the trapdoor to compute the bad β for α, decrypts it using the FHE secret key, and flips a bit so the output cannot equal the bad challenge. This shows that a cheating prover would contradict the construction. Because g* contains the FHE secret key, the proof assumes circular-secure FHE, meaning encryptions of the secret key are indistinguishable from encryptions of zeros. The lecture notes that later work removes this circular-security assumption using lattice-specific techniques.

A randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated SA58 nasal spray, a broad-spectrum anti-COVID-19 monoclonal antibody, as post-exposure prophylaxis in healthy adult workers in Beijing who had contact with SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals within 72 hours. The study ran from Nov 26 to Dec 9, 2022, during Omicron BF.7 outbreaks at 21 construction sites. Of 1,634 randomized participants, 1,222 entered the full analysis set; after excluding baseline RT-PCR-positive participants, 824 received SA58 and 299 received placebo for efficacy analysis.

Laboratory-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 occurred in 7 SA58 recipients and 14 placebo recipients, corresponding to an estimated treatment efficacy of 80.82% (95% CI 52.41%–92.27%). SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR positivity occurred in 32 participants in each group, with estimated efficacy against infection of 61.83% (95% CI 37.50%–76.69%). Sequenced positive samples were all Omicron BF.7. No severe COVID-19 cases or deaths occurred.

Adverse events were reported by 25% of SA58 recipients and 22% of placebo recipients; all were grade 1. Common events included nasal mucosal dryness, runny nose, fever, nasal congestion, headache, cough, and throat dryness. No serious adverse events or adverse events of special interest were reported.

The authors concluded that SA58 showed satisfactory efficacy and safety in healthy adults with early SARS-CoV-2 exposure and should be further evaluated in high-risk populations.

Tuberculosis remains a major global cause of mortality, with high risk among people living with HIV. Zambia is among the top 30 high-burden TB countries, and Kitwe Teaching Hospital previously reported TB as a leading cause of adult medical inpatient mortality.

This retrospective audit reviewed 74 TB-related mortality files at Kitwe Teaching Hospital from June 2018 to June 2019. Data included demographics, symptoms, HIV status, hospital stay, diagnoses, comorbidities, radiology, and laboratory findings. Thirty files were excluded because deaths occurred within 24 hours of admission or lacked clear TB confirmation.

Most deaths occurred among males (67.6%), patients younger than 50 years, HIV-positive patients (81.1%), and residents of high-density areas (83.8%). Common presenting symptoms were cough (41.9%), fever (40.5%), diarrhea (29.7%), productive cough (27.0%), headache (21.6%), and shortness of breath (16.2%). Vital signs showed elevated mean pulse rate on admission and unstable hemodynamic patterns before death.

Laboratory findings included anemia in 39.2%, microcytosis in 21.6%, hypoalbuminemia in 12.2%, elevated creatinine in 10.8%, and elevated liver enzymes. Radiological findings included miliary patterns, cavities, consolidation, and opacities. The audit concluded that TB mortality among inpatients was associated with male sex, age under 50, HIV positivity, residence in high-density areas, and clinical instability. The authors recommended a prospective study to identify mortality predictors and assess whether malignancy contributes to deaths among admitted TB/HIV co-infected patients.

PPP’s Taj Haider said Bilawal Bhutto Zardari would begin an aggressive election campaign in Punjab next week, starting in South Punjab, and urged authorities to ensure free, fair and transparent polls.

Dell Technologies expanded its strategic partnership with Salesforce, standardizing on Salesforce’s cloud-based CRM, sales, and marketing apps for nearly 40,000 global sales employees. The deal gives Dell contact centers access to Service Cloud Einstein, Salesforce’s AI customer service platform, and includes use of Dell Boomi for cloud data sharing.
