The agreement follows Dell’s merger with EMC and a prior multi-year deal for Salesforce to use Dell EMC infrastructure and Dell laptops.

A European Commission Joint Research Centre study found that the Amazon’s 2024 fire season was its worst in over two decades, releasing an estimated 791 million tons of carbon dioxide, roughly equal to Germany’s annual emissions and seven times the average of the previous two years. Fires affected 3.3 million hectares, with fire-driven forest degradation overtaking deforestation as the main source of carbon emissions for the first time in the 2022–2024 analysis. Researchers linked the surge to drought stress worsened by climate change, forest fragmentation, and land-use mismanagement. Using satellite data and Monte Carlo simulations, they documented severe impacts in Brazil and Bolivia, including fires affecting over 9% of Bolivia’s remaining intact forest cover. The study calls for action to reduce fire use, strengthen forest protection, support local and Indigenous stewardship, and address forest degradation in climate finance mechanisms.
SpaceX launched NASA’s TESS on a Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral on April 18 to search nearby stars for planets suitable for follow-up observations by powerful telescopes.

Canada’s S&P/TSX composite index hit a record high Wednesday morning, rising 97.66 points to 16,414.19 amid broad gains in energy, financial, technology and health care stocks. The Canadian dollar fell to 75.22 cents US amid U.S. rate and trade concerns. U.S. markets were mixed, while oil and natural gas rose and gold and copper declined.

The passage describes a high-voltage nanosecond pulsed electric field (nsPEF) generator for electrotherapy, particularly tumor treatment. NsPEF pulses can induce apoptosis in tumor cells and may stimulate immune responses. The disclosed system includes a controller, power supply, pulse generator, electrodes, interface, and sensors. A feedback control system adjusts pulse characteristics such as supply voltage, amplitude, pulse width, frequency, duty cycle, pulse count, energy, power, and tissue temperature based on measured parameters including voltage, current, impedance, and temperature.

The pulse generator uses a Marx-switch stack hybrid architecture with MOSFET switch stacks, allowing high-voltage, short-duration pulses with fewer stages, lower impedance, improved efficiency, and variable pulse duration. Multiple generator circuits may be connected in parallel for higher current or in series for higher voltage. Driver circuits use transformers to control switch timing and provide isolation, with pulse duration generally corresponding to input pulse duration.

The system may use suction or needle electrodes to deliver pulses to tumors, with sensors and analog-to-digital converters providing feedback from the pulse generator, electrodes, or treated tissue. Methods are described for controlling pulse amplitude, pulse width, tissue temperature, pulse generator charge voltage, delivered energy, and average power by comparing measured values with desired values and modifying control signals accordingly.

The orthopedic surgical system may include virtual planning, planning support, manufacturing and delivery, intraoperative guidance, medical education, monitoring, predictive analytics, and communication subsystems. Mixed reality systems may allow surgeons and other users to view and manipulate surgical plans, patient-specific bone models, implant models, cutting planes, drilling axes, entry points, tool guidance, workflow steps, and educational content. The Uzbek sum rose about 9% against the dollar on the black market over seven days as full exchange rate liberalisation appeared imminent. Uzbekistan recently ended mandatory foreign currency revenue sales by exporters and may move toward full convertibility, rate alignment, and lifting restrictions. Currency controls have been cited as a major obstacle to foreign investment.

The speaker said the team struggled defensively early, fell behind, and could not complete the comeback despite strong pressure and many chances late. They felt the third period was their best of the game or series, with offense not the issue but defensive mistakes being costly. They credited the opponent’s depth, size, speed, and home wins, while expressing confidence in returning home, using home-ice advantage, and responding well to adversity in the next game.

The passage discusses passive investing, Vanguard’s popularity, and eight Vanguard funds for retirement: Vanguard Target Retirement 2060, 2050, 2040, and Income Funds, plus Vanguard LifeStrategy Growth, Moderate Growth, Conservative Growth, and Income Funds. It states that passive investing has grown since the 2008/09 financial crisis due to low time commitment, cost-effectiveness, and satisfactory retirement returns. Vanguard, founded by John Bogle, manages over $6 trillion in assets and is popular for low costs, simple strategies, and broad fund choices.

A backtested Vanguard Retirement Portfolio using five retirement funds, buy-and-hold, and annual rebalancing from 2007 to 2023 grew from $10,000 to $23,317. Its returns were lower than the S&P 500 due to bond allocations.

The LifeStrategy funds use target allocations across four Vanguard funds with varying stock and bond exposure based on risk tolerance. The Target Retirement funds are designed for specific retirement periods and gradually become more conservative, eventually resembling the Target Retirement Income Fund. The passage advises investors to read each fund’s prospectus to determine suitability.

The passage describes a “Back Cut” offense for attacking a Diamond & One defense, which is identified as weak in the corners and middle. The offense aims to create open shots, layups, putbacks, and free the Star player through weakside back screens and single/double baseline screens. Its sequences include post entries, wing and baseline back cuts, corner cuts, dribble penetration, base cross action, and fake cross options if defenders cheat over screens. Success depends on coordinated execution, defensive recognition, non-verbal communication, timing, and experience. Suggested preparation includes breakdown drills, scrimmaging, scouting opponents, teaching expected defensive reads and counters, varying alignments and entries, and attacking weak defenders. The Diamond & One is described as a combination defense with four zone defenders and one defender denying the opponent’s scoring ace.

The speaker dedicates himself to the presidency, noting national progress after the Great War while warning of dangers to self-government. He identifies rising crime and weakened respect for law as urgent problems, calls for reform of the federal justice system, and urges enforcement of the eighteenth amendment with citizen support. He proposes a national commission to investigate federal jurisprudence and enforcement.

He supports regulation of private enterprise rather than government ownership, cooperation between government and civic or business groups, stronger education, and expanded public health efforts. In foreign policy, he emphasizes peace, opposition to imperialism, arms limitation, peaceful settlement of disputes, support for useful international institutions, and avoidance of commitments such as League of Nations membership.

He says political parties should carry out electoral mandates without partisan animosity, announces a special congressional session on agricultural relief and tariff changes, and lists priorities including constitutional integrity, law enforcement, economy, business regulation, federal reorganization, public works, education, the home, equality of opportunity, integrity, religious tolerance, and peace. He closes with confidence in the nation’s future and asks for citizens’ cooperation and God’s help.

Plex is launching podcast support in beta on iOS, Android, Roku, and Plex Web. Podcasts are free, do not require Plex Pass or a Plex Media Server, and include home screen access, recommendations, variable speeds, and skip controls. Plex also updated its mobile app with customizable home screens, tabs, and default locations across multiple servers.

The Boring Company sold out 20,000 $500 novelty “flamethrowers,” but Elon Musk said some customs agencies objected to the name. He proposed renaming it “Not a Flamethrower” or “Temperature Enhancement Device.” The device shoots flames under 10 feet and includes a fire extinguisher and serial number.

Confindustria cut Italy’s 2025 growth forecast from 0.6%, citing external pressures including U.S.–EU tariffs of up to 15% and a strong euro weakening exporters. It expects export growth to stagnate in 2025 and 2026, making investment the main growth driver. The Italian government is expected to revise its forecasts accordingly.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated November 1, 2017, reporting that it released financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2017 through its Third Quarter 2017 Shareholder Letter posted on its website. The shareholder letter is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by CFO Deepak Ahuja.

Scientists reported the first modern observed case of “river piracy,” attributing it to global warming. In May 2016, meltwater from Yukon’s Kaskawulsh glacier abruptly shifted from the Slims River to the Alsek River, redirecting flow from the Arctic’s Bering Sea toward the Pacific Ocean. The Slims became shallow and still, while the Alsek grew deeper and faster. Researchers said a 30-metre canyon formed at the glacier’s end, rerouting the water in about one day. They ruled out rainfall changes because the river is mainly glacier-fed and the Alsek gained water similar to what the Slims lost. Their modelling found only a one in 200 chance the glacier retreat and river piracy occurred naturally without man-made global warming. Outside scientists called the study significant.

Senator Leila de Lima rejected defeated senatorial candidate Francis Tolentino’s fraud accusations over the 2016 elections, saying recounts in his chosen precincts showed no irregularities or vote recovery. Tolentino, who placed 13th while De Lima won the final Senate seat, has pursued an electoral protest and sought to summon former elections chief Andres Bautista. De Lima called the protest baseless and dilatory, contrasted it with Aquilino Pimentel III’s successful protest against Juan Miguel Zubiri, and urged Tolentino to accept his loss.

Authorities are investigating a fire that destroyed South Carolina Circuit Judge Diane Goodstein’s Edisto Island beachfront home and injured at least three family members. Officials said there is no evidence so far that the fire was intentionally set or that a prefire explosion occurred. Occupants escaped by jumping from the elevated first floor and were rescued by kayak. Goodstein’s husband, Arnold Goodstein, was airlifted to a Charleston hospital. Goodstein recently temporarily blocked South Carolina from providing voter registration information to the federal government, but the state Supreme Court reversed her order.

Care Compliance Expert, founded to improve elder care, promotes higher standards in dementia care and health and safety in care homes. The company provides professional advice in these areas and is consulted by governmental organizations on regulatory changes. It states that improved care quality can enhance residents’ mood, quality of life, and overall standards in elder care.

France reached the World Cup quarter-finals after a 4-3 win over Argentina, driven by Kylian Mbappé’s two goals and penalty win, with support from teammates including Antoine Griezmann, Olivier Giroud and Paul Pogba. Benjamin Pavard also stood out with a long-range goal. France next face Uruguay, described by Didier Deschamps as “solid and aggressive,” with Luis Suarez leading the attack and a strong defence anchored by Diego Godin and Jose Maria Giminez. Edinson Cavani’s likely injury absence is a setback for Uruguay, though Blaise Matuidi said their style would not change much. Despite Uruguay conceding only one goal in four matches, France are considered favourites to reach the semi-finals.

SpaceX plans to launch its first recycled Falcon 9 rocket for NASA, carrying a previously flown Dragon capsule with nearly 5,000 pounds of supplies to the International Space Station. NASA said the risk is comparable to a new rocket but not zero. SpaceX has previously reused rockets for commercial launches and aims to reduce costs through reusability. The launch will mark the return of Launch Complex 40 after a $50 million rebuild following a 2016 explosion.

Lexington County authorities are searching for a woman suspected of making more than 60 fake 911 calls between March 25 and April 14, mostly from the Saint Andrews area. Officials say the calls endanger deputies and the public by prompting emergency responses and potentially delaying real emergencies. Investigators released one call seeking voice identification and ask tips be sent to Crimestoppers.

Fort Bend ISD maintenance crews worked overnight to repair air conditioning problems at Quail Valley Elementary School and Marshall High School after a three-day weekend and high temperatures. The elementary school’s AC was restored, and Marshall students said Tuesday was unusually hot, with some areas using fans and students gathering in the cooler cafeteria. The passage defines night or overnight trading as holding positions from the market close to the next open, distinct from after-hours trading. It states that since 1993, S&P 500 gains have come from owning the index overnight, with an average close-to-open gain of 0.04%, while open-to-close returns produced no gains. Similar overnight tendencies are reported in gold and gold miners. The passage attributes the bias partly to inflation, earnings growth, and compensation for overnight risk. It notes that slippage and commissions make simple overnight exposure insufficient, but says specific backtested strategies, including 24-hour variants, have performed well. The authors argue overnight stock trading strategies may offer useful risk and reward for traders.

Dengue is a mosquito-borne flavivirus disease with no direct-acting antivirals and limited vaccine protection across serotypes. AT-752 is an oral guanosine nucleotide prodrug inhibitor of dengue virus polymerase, metabolized to active triphosphate AT-9010, with AT-273 used as a plasma surrogate marker.

A first-in-human Phase 1 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study evaluated safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of single ascending doses and multiple ascending doses of AT-752 in healthy adults, including assessments of food effect and ethnic sensitivity. Sixty-five subjects were enrolled: 41 in single-dose cohorts and 24 in multiple-dose cohorts.

AT-752 was well tolerated as single doses up to 1500 mg and multiple doses up to 750 mg three times daily. No serious adverse events or adverse-event-related discontinuations occurred. Treatment-emergent adverse events were mild or moderate and resolved by study end; headache, nausea, and vomiting were most frequent.

After single dosing, AT-281 was rapidly eliminated, while AT-273 appeared more gradually and had a longer half-life, indicating sustained exposure to active metabolite. Pharmacokinetics were similar between Asian and mostly Caucasian cohorts, suggesting no ethnic sensitivity. Food reduced peak levels of some analytes but had limited or no effect on total exposure, supporting dosing with or without food. In multiple-dose cohorts, AT-752 750 mg three times daily rapidly increased AT-273 trough levels above the in vitro EC90 for dengue virus replication and maintained them during treatment. The results support further clinical study of AT-752 for dengue treatment.

Two studies published September 16 and 17 report that two oral GLP-1 drugs helped people with obesity lose weight. A 25-milligram oral semaglutide trial followed more than 300 participants for up to 64 weeks and found an average body weight drop of nearly 14 percent. An orforglipron trial followed more than 3,000 participants for up to 72 weeks, with people on the highest dose losing about 11 percent on average. Experts said pills could be easier to manufacture, distribute and take than injectable GLP-1 drugs, which often require refrigeration and needles, though both pills are taken daily. Side effects included nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and constipation, generally fading over time, and researchers did not observe liver toxicity. Longer-term studies are still needed, and availability could depend on FDA approval.

On March 11, 2011, a major earthquake, tsunami, and nuclear emergency struck Japan, causing severe human and economic damage and disrupting the automotive industry. Japanese auto production fell sharply, affecting both domestic plants and overseas factories dependent on Japanese components.

Nissan suffered damage to six production facilities and disruption among about 50 critical suppliers, but its prior risk management, flexible supply chain philosophy, and emergency-response planning helped it recover. The company had established disaster response principles focused on human life, preventing secondary disasters, rapid recovery, business continuity, and community support. After the disaster, Nissan quickly convened its Global Disaster Control Headquarters and created a Recovery Committee to coordinate global actions.

Nissan’s response emphasized information sharing across regions, allocation of constrained parts to higher-margin products, targeted production adjustments, use of in-transit inventory and air freight, and rapid decision-making through temporary changes to authority rules. Its decentralized but coordinated supply chain structure, simplified product line, and localization strategy also supported recovery.

Afterward, Nissan announced plans to increase localized production in the Americas, reduce reliance on Japanese-made components, and improve visibility into second- and third-tier supplier risks. The company identified the need for a stronger business continuity plan covering the broader supply chain.

This study investigates improving n-type Bi2Te3−xSex (BTS) thermoelectric materials, whose performance lags behind p-type Bi2−xSbxTe3 due to stronger anisotropy and intrinsic defects. The authors used a melting–hot pressing route followed by annealing to decouple carrier and phonon transport in Se-alloyed Bi2Te3. Bi2Te2.6Se0.4 was identified as the optimal composition, with Se substitution reducing lattice thermal conductivity through lattice distortion and suppressed bipolar conduction.

Annealing at 723 K tuned carrier density and mobility through Te(Se) volatilization and cation vacancy formation. After 100 h, Bi2Te2.6Se0.4 showed reduced carrier density, enhanced carrier mobility of 295.97 cm² V−1 s−1, and improved power factor. Annealing also introduced atomic-scale defects that increased phonon scattering and reduced lattice thermal conductivity to 0.48 W m−1 K−1 at room temperature. The optimized sample achieved a peak ZT of 1.06 at 373 K, a room-temperature ZT of 0.78, and an average ZT of 0.99 from 300 to 423 K. The work presents annealing as a practical post-synthesis strategy for improving n-type BTS thermoelectric performance for cooling and thermal management applications.

The passage presents a study on evaluating software accessibility, focusing on users with visual impairments. It notes that ISO 25023 defines accessibility metrics such as “Accessibility for users with disabilities” and “Supported languages adequacy” but does not provide methods for determining some parameters or weighting coefficients. The study aims to develop a classification, mathematical model, and evaluation methods for software accessibility.

The proposed model divides accessibility into perceptiveness, operability, understandability, and localization. It introduces quality attributes including alternative text, color contrast, subtitles and audio descriptions, keyboard navigation, structured navigation, clear instructions, input assistance, correct input support, and language support. Formulas and weighting coefficients are used to calculate subproperties, quality properties, and an overall accessibility indicator.

The methodology was tested on the Vasyl Stefanyk Precarpathian National University website using automated tools such as Image Alt Checker and WCAG Contrast Checker, along with expert weighting. The overall accessibility score was approximately 0.68, classified as “excellent” on the study’s quality scale. Weak areas included subtitles and audio descriptions, input assistance, alternative text, and structured navigation. The study concludes that the proposed model enables more precise accessibility evaluation and helps identify improvements for compliance with ISO 25023 and WCAG.

This protocol describes a systematic review of implementation determinants, implementation strategies, and adjunctive interventions for structural interventions supporting HIV evidence-based interventions in the U.S. The review addresses disparities shaped by social and structural determinants of health, including racism, stigma, housing instability, transportation barriers, and healthcare access.

Searches conducted from May to July 2024 across multiple databases and CDC sources identified 8,098 articles before deduplication. Eligibility criteria include U.S.-based HIV/AIDS behavioral or social science implementation research with original data, implementation outcomes, and interventions targeting factors external to individuals or social determinants of health. Natural language processing was used for preliminary screening, followed by manual title/abstract and full-text review in COVIDENCE.

Data extraction will include study setting, populations, intervention type, implementation outcomes, study design, and structural intervention category. Determinants will be coded using CFIR 2.0, and strategies will be coded using ERIC; adjunctive interventions will be coded using TDF and COM-B. Analyses will tabulate and stratify findings by population, setting, intervention type, HIV EBI, and outcomes, with NLP-assisted thematic analysis.

Results will be disseminated through manuscripts, conferences, and an online dashboard. The review aims to identify literature gaps and inform future research, policy, and programs to improve equitable implementation of HIV structural interventions.

This study examined relationships between mentalization, attachment, and personality pathology within the DSM-5 Alternative Model of Personality Disorders, focusing on Criterion A personality functioning and Criterion B maladaptive traits. It distinguished self-oriented mentalizing from other-oriented mentalizing and tested whether mentalizing moderated links between insecure attachment and personality pathology.

The sample included 109 participants from psychiatric inpatient services, universities, and the local community. Measures assessed DSM-5 personality disorders, other-mentalizing, self-mentalizing deficits, personality functioning, maladaptive traits, and attachment anxiety and avoidance. Analyses included correlations, multiple regressions, and moderation models.

Self-mentalizing deficits were strongly associated with impairments in both self and interpersonal functioning and with all five maladaptive trait domains. In regression analyses, self-mentalizing deficits were the strongest predictor across outcomes, especially self-functioning difficulties and Negative Affectivity. Correct other-mentalizing predicted fewer interpersonal functioning difficulties but was not significantly related to Criterion B traits when considered with self-mentalizing. Other-mentalizing showed more specific associations, particularly with interpersonal functioning and Detachment.

Attachment anxiety and avoidance predicted Criterion A impairments. For Criterion B, attachment anxiety was generally significant across traits, while avoidance mainly predicted Detachment. Mentalizing moderated several attachment-pathology relationships: correct other-mentalizing weakened, and hypermentalizing strengthened, the relationship between attachment anxiety and interpersonal functioning impairments. Self-mentalizing moderated links between attachment anxiety and both Negative Affectivity and Detachment. Correct other-mentalizing weakened the relationship between attachment avoidance and Detachment, while undermentalizing and nonmentalizing strengthened it.

The authors conclude that self-mentalizing has a broad role in personality pathology, whereas other-mentalizing is more specifically tied to interpersonal impairment and Detachment. They suggest that distinguishing self- and other-focused mentalization may help clarify mechanisms of personality disorders and inform targeted therapeutic interventions. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, small and heterogeneous sample, lack of assessment of symptomatic comorbidity, and possible method effects.

The passage describes thermal characterization of the Mod-Cam receiver, the single-module precursor and testbed for Prime-Cam on the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope. Mod-Cam uses kinetic inductance detectors operated near 100 mK, where thermal stability is critical because temperature fluctuations can shift detector resonant frequencies and add noise.

Measurements were performed mainly in a cold-load configuration to isolate intrinsic thermal behavior, with additional cryogenic performance measured in an optically open configuration. The system includes 40 K, 4 K, 1 K, and 100 mK stages coupled to a dilution refrigerator, with upgrades improving 40 K thermal stability. The detector stage was servo-controlled at 100 mK and monitored over eight hours.

The RMS temperature fluctuation at the 100 mK detector stage was 3.2 × 10⁻⁵ K. Thermal responsivity was measured for 2409 aluminum detectors and 1886 titanium-nitride detectors on the 280 GHz array. Median responsivities were 1.995 × 10⁻⁴ K⁻¹ for aluminum and −6.081 × 10⁻⁴ K⁻¹ for titanium nitride. These values were used to calculate equivalent optical power noise from thermal instability.

For a 5 pW optical load, the thermally induced equivalent power noise was 0.20 fW for aluminum detectors and 0.11 fW for titanium-nitride detectors, corresponding to fractional contributions of 0.0040% and 0.0023%, respectively. The study concludes that Mod-Cam’s cryogenic design and thermal control provide sufficient stability, and thermal fluctuations make a negligible contribution to detector noise.

The Missouri Supreme Court will hear two cases on whether the Missouri Human Rights Act covers discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, though those terms are not in the law. In R.M.A. v. Blue Springs R-IV School District, a transgender student sued after being denied access to boys’ restrooms and locker rooms, arguing gender identity is a sex-related trait protected by the Act. Missouri Commission on Human Rights, a gay state employee alleged sex discrimination based on gender stereotyping, and a coworker alleged retaliation. The Human Rights Commission rejected the claims as sexual-orientation based, but an appeals court disagreed. The state argues courts cannot add sexual orientation to the Act.

An experiment found that 6-year-olds doing repetitive tasks worked harder and stayed more focused when pretending to be characters like Batman or Dora the Explorer, while those focused on themselves took more breaks.

Erik Demaine introduces MIT 6.851 Advanced Data Structures, covering topics such as temporal data structures, geometry, dynamic optimality, memory hierarchy, hashing, integer data structures, dynamic graphs, strings, and succinct data structures. Administrative details include lectures, weekly problem sets, lecture scribing, and optional open problem sessions.

The lecture focuses on temporal data structures, beginning with the pointer machine model: memory consists of nodes with a constant number of fields containing pointers, nulls, or data, accessed through a root. The goal is to transform pointer-machine data structures into persistent ones that preserve previous versions.

Persistence is presented in four forms. Partial persistence allows queries on all versions but updates only the latest version, so versions form a line. Full persistence allows updates to any version, producing a version tree. Confluent persistence allows combining two versions, producing a version DAG. Functional data structures never modify existing nodes and therefore preserve all prior versions naturally, though they may impose performance constraints.

For partial persistence, Demaine describes the Driscoll-Sarnak-Sleator-Tarjan method for pointer-machine structures with constant in-degree. Each node stores back pointers and a bounded number of modification records containing a version, field, and value. Reads check applicable modifications; writes either add a modification or, if the node is full, create a new node, apply modifications, and recursively update pointers. A potential-function amortized analysis gives constant amortized overhead and constant space per change.

Full persistence uses similar ideas but must maintain versions as a tree. An order-maintenance data structure linearizes tree traversal intervals to test ancestor relationships in constant time. Full persistence also stores back pointers for all versions and splits full nodes into roughly balanced sets of modifications, updating pointers recursively. This also yields constant amortized overhead under the same bounded-degree assumptions. Worst-case constant slowdown is known for partial persistence, while deamortizing full persistence remains open.

Confluent persistence is harder because versions form a DAG and operations can cause exponential-size logical structures, such as repeatedly concatenating a structure with itself. Fiat and Kaplan provide a general method with overhead depending on the logarithm of updates and effective depth, but constant overhead remains open if queries are charged for space. A newer result gives logarithmic overhead in a disjoint case where combined versions share no nodes.

The lecture briefly notes functional techniques such as path copying for balanced search trees, functional deques with concatenation, tries, and open problems involving split and concatenate operations.

Denmark’s Systemic Risk Council urged tighter mortgage rules for highly indebted households in Copenhagen and Aarhus, targeting interest-only or variable-rate loans when debt exceeds 400% of pretax income. The government has three months to accept or publicly explain any refusal.

Investing.com highlights market news including Tesla’s record Q3 deliveries, higher Citi crypto forecasts, chip stock gains, and Bitcoin near $120,000. It notes potential further declines in yields and the dollar, technical signals in TLT, bullish implications for commodities, and widening divergence between growth and value. The work proposes an active learning queue prioritization algorithm for generative AI scientific discovery workflows. The method uses a surrogate model and acquisition functions to reorder candidates generated by a GenAI model, prioritizing those likely to score well while reducing evaluation of unreasonable candidates and mitigating model decay during iterative retraining.

The approach is demonstrated on metal-organic framework (MOF) discovery for carbon capture. A DiffLinker generative model proposes MOF linkers, while molecular dynamics simulations evaluate internal strain. Active learning prioritizes candidates using stability predictions, uncertainty, synthesizability scores, and similarity to known HMOF linkers. Experiments show that active learning improves queue ordering, supports multi-objective prioritization, and can balance exploration and exploitation.

Across 1000 generated candidates, the workflow without active learning produced an average of 281 high-performing candidates, while the active learning prioritization produced an average of 604. The added computational overhead was estimated below 1% of total workflow costs.

The speaker says his status for tonight is doubtful despite daily improvement from an injury suffered against Ottawa. He is preparing mentally and physically in case he must play but hopes he does not have to, as the team is doing well. He feels included by teammates and will know on the ice if he can play.

Jim Cramer has become more cautious on Snap nearly two months after comparing it to early Facebook. He cited Snapchat’s unpopular redesign, concerns about declining user engagement, advertiser risk, and negative celebrity reactions as key issues. Snap shares lost gains made after strong fourth-quarter results, and Cramer said the stock is currently too expensive and risky, though he may consider buying at a lower price. Researchers led by Dr. Shinichi Furuya of the NeuroPiano Institute and Sony Computer Science Laboratories scientifically confirmed that pianists can alter piano timbre through touch. Using the Hackkey sensor system, which measures all 88 keys at 1,000 fps and 0.01 mm resolution, the team recorded 20 internationally renowned pianists producing intended timbres such as bright/dark and light/heavy. In listening tests with 40 participants, including pianists and non-musicians, listeners consistently perceived the intended timbres, even when volume and tempo were controlled. Data analysis identified specific key-movement features, such as acceleration during escapement and hand synchronization deviations, as contributors to timbral differences, and experiments supported a causal link between movement and timbre. The findings, published in PNAS, may support evidence-based music education, skill training, neuroscience, rehabilitation, skill transfer, and human interface design.

Professor Noelle Selin discusses mercury as a global environmental and regulatory issue, focusing on the Minamata Convention, signed in 2013 as the first major new global environmental treaty in over a decade and a life-cycle approach to mercury regulation. Mercury is a global concern because atmospheric emissions travel widely, deposit into ecosystems, convert to toxic methylmercury, and accumulate in food chains, causing neurological and possible cardiovascular impacts. Major sources include coal combustion, artisanal and small-scale gold mining, industrial processes, products, waste, and cremation.

Selin explains that international action developed slowly after a 2002 scientific assessment, influenced by shifting positions among the US, EU, China, Latin America, and others. The treaty addresses emissions, mercury in products and processes, trade, waste, and artisanal gold mining, though many provisions rely on phase-outs, exemptions, capacity building, and voluntary implementation rather than strict enforcement. Products discussed include thermometers, batteries, fluorescent lamps, dental amalgam, cosmetics, vaccines, and industrial uses. Artisanal gold mining is highlighted as a major mercury source linked to informal trade, local health risks, and the gold supply chain.

The lecture also covers how domestic and regional regulations, especially from the US and EU, shape global standards, and how international negotiations involve scientific assessments, political compromise, industry observation, limited developing-country capacity, and slow consensus-building. Selin concludes that the treaty may mainly prevent future mercury increases and send a strong political signal, while stronger environmental results would require later technical tightening and implementation.

The passage describes KaviKrishna’s community-based participatory research approach to tuberculosis control in rural Northeast India, integrating Indigenous Knowledge System methods with modern clinical, molecular, stem cell, and genomic techniques. It argues that generalized, centrally controlled TB programs inadequately address regional strain diversity, MDR evolution, dormant TB reactivation, host-pathogen interactions, and community participation.

KaviKrishna developed a TB screening, monitoring, and research network through KaviKrishna Telemedicine Care, KaviKrishna Laboratory, and the KaviKrishna Centre of Indian Knowledge System. Its Indigenous Kamarupa Information Network uses temple-centered community networks, volunteers, focused group discussions, patient follow-up, nutrition support, and telemedicine to trace TB patients and contacts in the Sualkuchi-Hajo region. Since 2010, it screened 300 pulmonary TB cases among 500 suspected cases and maintains follow-up data for 210 patients.

The work includes longitudinal collection of sputum, blood, and bone marrow samples; culture and molecular identification of Mycobacterium tuberculosis; drug susceptibility testing; PCR methods to distinguish MTB from non-tuberculous mycobacteria; and evaluation of MDR-related mutations. The researchers also study TB dormancy and reactivation, reporting that dormant MTB may reside in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells and circulatory progenitor cells. Mouse model studies suggested dormant MTB in MSCs can retain viability and reactivate under stress conditions.

The laboratory established sputum processing, MTB culture, DNA extraction, drug susceptibility testing, MIC and antibiotic tolerance assays, viable-but-non-culturable MTB detection, and bacterial live/dead assays. Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics are used to identify circulating MTB lineages, mutation profiles, and possible compensatory mutations related to MDR evolution; sample WGS data have been deposited in NCBI.

The authors conclude that CBPR and IKS-based TB care may support patient tracing, stigma reduction, treatment monitoring, regional strain mapping, and research on TB dormancy, reactivation, and MDR evolution. The clinical study and related in-vivo and stem cell research received institutional approvals, with informed consent obtained from participants.

The passage describes container-based design patterns for distributed systems. The ambassador pattern can broker service discovery and configuration so applications connect to localhost while an ambassador locates the correct external service, and it can support experimentation or request splitting by routing portions of traffic to experimental services while returning production responses.

The adapter pattern modifies an application container’s interface to match expected conventions without changing the application. It can normalize monitoring interfaces, export Redis metrics for Prometheus, redirect or transform logs with tools such as fluentd, and add rich health checks to databases like MySQL through a separate container. This modularity supports reuse, independent updates, and separation of concerns.

The passage contrasts single-node patterns with multi-node distributed patterns and introduces microservices as systems composed of separate components communicating through APIs. Microservices can improve reliability, agility, independent scaling, and team autonomy, but make debugging and architecture more difficult.

Replicated load-balanced services use identical replicas behind a load balancer for redundancy, availability, and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes indicate when replicas can serve traffic. Session-tracked services route a user consistently to the same replica. Additional layers such as Varnish caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and nginx SSL termination can be added as replicated tiers.

Sharded services divide requests or data across shards, usually for stateful systems too large for one machine. Sharded caches improve memory utilization compared with replicated caches but require attention to cache hit rate, failures, rollouts, and latency. Replicated shards increase resilience and allow scaling hot shards. Sharding functions should be deterministic, uniform, and based on appropriate keys; consistent hashing reduces remapping during resharding.

The scatter/gather pattern distributes one request to multiple leaves, gathers partial results, and combines them at the root to reduce processing time. It can support document search and sharded search systems, but excessive parallelism adds overhead and creates straggler and reliability problems. Replicating each shard improves availability and upgrade safety.

The passage also discusses function-as-a-service and event-driven processing. FaaS simplifies deployment and automatic scaling, but strong decoupling complicates monitoring, debugging, background processing, memory-heavy workloads, and sustained high-volume request costs. One FaaS pattern is the decorator, which transforms requests or responses, such as adding default values to REST API requests before forwarding them.

Gary Gensler’s lecture focused on digital identity, identity and access management, and possible blockchain applications. The class first revisited supply chain transparency, with discussion of blockchain’s potential to verify supplier claims about sustainability, labor, and sourcing.

The identity discussion distinguished between identity as a person’s unique existence and practical identifiers such as birth certificates, biometrics, credentials, claims, and attestations. Students debated whether identity is inherent, contextual, socially constructed, or an aggregation of attributes. Biometrics and hashing were discussed as possible ways to create unique identifiers, though concerns included replication, theft, and the limits of biometric systems.

Gensler outlined identity management functions such as authentication and authorization, and described the roles of users, service providers, identity providers, attribute authorities, and certificate authorities. Certificate authorities were explained as central to internet security because they verify public keys for websites, helping users avoid fake sites and man-in-the-middle attacks.

The lecture identified pain points in identity systems, including privacy, security, identity theft, forged credentials, personal data updates, and large data breaches. Examples included major breaches affecting companies such as Yahoo, Equifax, Facebook, Marriott, and India’s Aadhaar system. Gensler also discussed credit card fraud, merchant data breaches, and debates over cybersecurity responsibility.

State identity projects discussed included Estonia’s e-identity system and India’s Aadhaar, neither of which was described as a blockchain project. Aadhaar was presented as promoting inclusion and government benefit delivery, but also raising concerns about hacks, errors, exclusion, and public debate over costs and benefits.

Self-sovereign identity was defined as a concept where people or entities have more control over identity attributes, direct access, portability, and interoperability. Gensler noted it does not require blockchain, but blockchain could potentially reduce verification costs, improve provenance, address censorship, and support privacy. Challenges include storing personal information on distributed ledgers, immutability, updating attributes, right-to-be-forgotten rules, and private-key loss.

Several blockchain or related identity efforts were mentioned, including Civic, ExistenceID, Sovrin, Bitnation, the Distributed Identity Foundation, Rebooting Web-of-Trust, W3C work, decentralized public key infrastructure, and MIT’s blockchain-backed diplomas. The lecture concluded by framing digital identity as closely linked to finance, banking, tax systems, and know-your-customer requirements.

Antonio Vasquez and Hector Perez were charged with possession of burglar’s tools, attempted petit larceny, and resisting arrest after allegedly trying to steal a chained bicycle with bolt cutters, then abandoning the attempt after speaking with a third person. OSCAR is introduced as a one-shot multi-label causal discovery method for high-dimensional event sequences. It uses two Transformer-based autoregressive density estimators to identify each label’s Markov Boundary through conditional mutual information and produce interpretable causal indicators between events and labels. The method assumes temporal precedence, bounded lagged effects, causal sufficiency, and accurate density estimation. Unlike classical local structure learning methods whose complexity depends on event and label cardinality, OSCAR parallelizes computations for scalability.

The approach was evaluated on a vehicular dataset with 300,000 sequences, 29,100 diagnostic trouble code event types, and 474 error-pattern labels. In comparisons using 50,000 samples, classical algorithms did not return Markov Boundaries within a three-day timeout, while OSCAR achieved 55.26% precision, 31.37% recall, and 40.02% F1 in 11.7 minutes. The authors conclude that OSCAR enables practical, sequence-specific causal reasoning and explainability for large-scale sequential data.

The ADS868xW device uses a multiSPI digital interface for host communication, supporting standard SPI-compatible and source-synchronous data transfer protocols. The interface includes input and output shift registers, configuration registers, and a protocol unit; the host views the device as a 32-bit input-output shift register during data frames.

Supported connection topologies include a single device using all multiSPI options, a single device with a standard SPI interface, and multiple devices in a daisy-chain topology. In daisy-chain mode, devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK, pass data through SDI and SDO-0, require identical configuration values, and use 32 × N SCLK capture edges for N devices.

The device has three functional states: RESET, ACQ, and CONV. RESET is entered with the active-low RST pin and can perform either an application reset or power-on reset. ACQ is used to acquire the analog input signal and supports NAP low-power mode. CONV begins on the rising edge of CONVST/CS, uses an internal clock, and returns to ACQ after conversion.

Programming uses nine configuration registers and supports data write and data read operations. Data frames begin on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and end on the following rising edge. A 32-clock frame is optimal; shorter frames invalidate writes but can read MSBs, while longer frames use the last 32 input bits as the command. Output data can include conversion results, register data, fixed patterns, and optional flags such as device address, range, alarm, and parity.

The device supports SPI-compatible read/write protocols, single or dual SDO output, and source-synchronous read protocols using RVS as the output clock. Registers configure reset and power control, SDI and SDO modes, output data content, input range, alarms, and alarm thresholds.

Application information describes use in industrial analog input modules with an ADS8681W ADC and MUX36D08 multiplexer for voltage, current, or temperature sensing. The device includes an internal programmable gain amplifier, ADC driver, reference, overvoltage protection, input alarm, and AVDD alarm. Power recommendations include AVDD and DVDD decoupling, NAP mode, power-down mode, and PCB layout practices separating analog and digital sections.

The lecture introduces iterative methods for solving large sparse linear systems, where direct elimination is too costly but matrix-vector multiplication is fast. It focuses on solving \(Ax=b\) using iterations based on a preconditioner \(P\), chosen to resemble \(A\) while being easier to solve. Examples include Jacobi’s method using the diagonal of \(A\), Gauss-Seidel using the lower triangular part including the diagonal, successive overrelaxation, and incomplete LU, which approximates LU factors while limiting fill-in.

The iteration is analyzed through the error equation, where the error is repeatedly multiplied by the iteration matrix \(M=I-P^{-1}A\). Convergence depends on the eigenvalues of \(M\): all must have magnitude below 1, and the spectral radius determines the convergence rate. For the standard tridiagonal matrix with diagonal 2 and off-diagonal -1, Jacobi has eigenvalues related to cosines and converges slowly because the largest magnitude eigenvalues are close to 1, especially for low-frequency modes. Weighted Jacobi can improve high-frequency convergence but leaves low frequencies slow, motivating multigrid. Gauss-Seidel uses updated values immediately, reduces storage, and effectively squares Jacobi eigenvalues, making each step comparable to two Jacobi steps, but it still requires order \(n^2\) iterations.

Çalışma, öğretmen adaylarının uzaktan eğitimle yürütülen özel eğitim dersine ilişkin görüşlerini, yaşadıkları sorunları ve çözüm önerilerini incelemiştir. Nitel fenomenoloji desenindeki araştırmaya, 2022-2023 yılında özel bir üniversitede öğrenim gören ve özel eğitim dersini ilk kez alan 45 öğretmen adayı gönüllü olarak katılmıştır. Veriler, araştırmacı tarafından hazırlanan yarı yapılandırılmış görüşme formuyla toplanmıştır.

Katılımcıların çoğu uzaktan eğitimle özel eğitim dersi almaktan memnun olduğunu belirtse de önemli bir bölümü yüz yüze eğitimin daha etkili, anlaşılır ve nitelikli olduğunu ifade etmiştir. Uzaktan eğitimde internet bağlantısı, teknik aksaklıklar, materyal eksikliği ve dikkat dağınıklığı temel sorunlar olarak öne çıkmıştır. Katılımcılar derse katılımın başarı ve öğrenme açısından önemli olduğunu vurgulamış, ancak bazıları dijital araç eksikliği ve video kayıtlarından öğrenme imkânı nedeniyle katılım zorunluluğuna karşı çıkmıştır. Çoğunluk uzaktan eğitimi etkili, ekonomik ve ev ortamı açısından rahat bulurken, bazıları özellikle uygulamalı derslerde verimsiz olduğunu belirtmiştir. Çalışmada sistemin, internet altyapısının, teknik desteğin ve dijital materyal olanaklarının geliştirilmesi önerilmiştir.

A Reversal Day occurs when a stock or market index changes direction after an extended trend, often with high trading volume. A Bullish Reversal Day follows a downtrend, makes a lower low than the previous day, then closes above the previous day’s high. A Bearish Reversal Day follows an uptrend, makes a higher high, then closes below the previous day’s low.

Stock reversals can be caused by changes in market sentiment, economic conditions, company-specific news, or technical factors. Traders may identify potential reversals by analyzing trend changes, volume, moving averages, RSI, Bollinger Bands, support and resistance, divergences, and broader market cycles.

Markets prone to reversals include stocks, currencies, commodities, and bonds, each influenced by factors such as sentiment, economic data, political events, supply and demand, inflation, and interest rates.

The article backtests bullish and bearish Reversal Day strategies in gold (GLD) using Amibroker with exits from 1 to 25 trading days. The bullish strategy showed generally good profit factors but few trades, with the highest average gain after 24 trading days. The bearish strategy produced losses, partly attributed to gold’s upward overnight drift, and had lower average gains than the bullish strategy. The article concludes that Reversal Day patterns have merit but should be evaluated with defined trading rules and market context.

Cocoa futures are standardized contracts to buy or sell 10 metric tons of cocoa at a future date and agreed price. They trade on ICE Futures US under symbol CC and on CME Globex/NYMEX under symbol CJ. CME contracts are financially settled, while ICE contracts are physically deliverable. Contract months are March, May, July, September, and December, with a minimum price fluctuation of $1 per metric ton, equal to $10 per contract.

A cocoa futures trading strategy may use fundamental and technical analysis, position sizing, and risk management to speculate or hedge cocoa prices. The passage states commodities, including cocoa, are difficult to trade. A referenced backtest had 96 trades, a 2.3 profit factor, and a 74% win rate. Cocoa futures have tended to perform better in summer and worse in spring and fall.

Cocoa prices are affected by supply and demand factors. Major risks include adverse price movement due to leverage and liquidity risk, since cocoa is less liquid than markets like gold or crude oil. Cocoa CFDs differ from futures because they are broker agreements to exchange price differences and do not involve exchange-traded futures settlement or delivery.

As of November 25, 2022, cocoa futures traded at $2,484 per metric ton. The all-time high cited was $5,379 in July 1977, while TradingView data since 1979 shows a low of $707 in December 2000 and a high of $3,775 in March 2011. An ETF/ETN option mentioned is iPath Bloomberg Cocoa Subindex Total Return ETN (NIB).

NVIDIA Turing GPUs add native HDR display pipeline support with tone mapping based on ITU-R BT.2100, enhanced NVENC encoding with H.265 8K at 30 fps and bitrate savings for HEVC and H.264, and updated NVDEC decoding for HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. Turing’s encoder improves streaming quality over Pascal and fast x264 software encoding while reducing CPU utilization, enabling 4K streaming.

Turing supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink to simplify VR headset connectivity by carrying power, display, and data through one USB-C connector. It also replaces prior SLI MIO/PCIe transfers with second-generation NVLink on TU102 and TU104, increasing GPU-to-GPU bandwidth and enabling new two-way SLI display topologies; 3-way and 4-way SLI are not supported.

The architecture introduces RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs for real-time ray tracing with NVIDIA RTX technology. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection testing, offloading shader multiprocessors and enabling hybrid rendering that combines rasterization and ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. NVIDIA states Turing can run ray tracing about 10 times faster than Pascal using RT Cores. Denoising, BVH acceleration, hybrid rendering, and RT Cores are presented as key technologies enabling real-time ray tracing.

NVIDIA NGX is a Turing-only deep learning-based technology stack using Tensor Cores for AI features in games and applications. It includes DLSS, which uses trained neural networks to produce image quality similar to TAA with lower shading work, and DLSS 2X, which targets image quality close to 64x supersampling. Other NGX features include InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez.

Turing adds Mesh Shading with Task Shaders and Mesh Shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and allow more flexible geometry processing. It also introduces Variable Rate Shading, allowing developers to vary shading rate per 16x16-pixel region for content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, foveated rendering, and MSAA-related rate increases. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility sampling from appearance shading by storing shading results as texels for reuse across pixels, frames, or stereo views.

Multi-View Rendering extends Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi-Projection by supporting up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 API-level views, improving VR stereo rendering, canted display support, shadow maps, and multi-instance rendering. Turing also expands DX12 resource support with bindless Constant Buffer Views and Unordered Access Views and supports Tier 2 resource heaps.

The passage describes Turing’s VR improvements, including VirtualLink, Multi-View Rendering, foveated rendering through VRS, and VRWorks Audio acceleration using RT Cores. It also details TU104 and TU106 GPU configurations, including CUDA Cores, Tensor Cores, RT Cores, memory interfaces, and product examples such as GeForce RTX 2080, Quadro RTX 5000, Tesla T4, and GeForce RTX 2070. RTX-OPS is introduced as a workload-based metric combining Tensor, FP32, RT Core, and INT32 operations according to representative hybrid rendering usage.

The passage also explains ray tracing fundamentals, including reverse ray casting from the camera, BVH acceleration, BVH building and refitting, denoising, and the use of ray tracing for shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections. It concludes with NVIDIA legal notices, warranty disclaimers, trademark statements, and copyright information.

MLPs had mixed performance in the final four days of the year but outperformed the S&P 500, while oil and natural gas ended the year with large gains. The AMZE total return was 22.5%, above the traditional Alerian MLP Index, partly reflecting gains in smaller MLPs and Enterprise Products Partners’ unusual underperformance. In December, the MLP Index returned 4.4%, contributing to three positive quarters and two positive months. For 2016, MLPs rose 18.3%, beating the S&P 500 for the first time since 2011 amid distribution adjustments and commodity volatility. SunCoke Energy Partners was the top-performing distributing MLP for the year, and Ferrellgas Partners was the biggest loser. General partners and midstream corporations underperformed MLPs again. Health savings accounts (HSAs), a Republican-backed idea receiving renewed attention as lawmakers consider replacing the Affordable Care Act, let eligible people with high-deductible health plans save and invest money tax-free for certain medical expenses. Participation is growing but remains limited, with about 20 million of 176 million insured people enrolled in 2015. Barriers include lack of upfront money and psychological resistance to saving. Experts say stress, short-term spending impulses, and avoidance of future health needs make saving difficult. Behavioral economist Mitesh Patel notes that people are often motivated by fear of losing money, and automatic enrollment could increase HSA participation. Studies suggest people with HSAs use less health care, but health outcomes are unclear; prescription drug costs fell while emergency room visits rose, especially among lower-income families. Estimating needed health savings is also difficult because medical prices are hard to determine. Financial therapist Alycia DeGraff says HSAs can help only those with enough income to cover daily expenses and save extra.

The passage argues that Morgan Tsvangirai was once vital to Zimbabwe’s opposition, notably helping form the MDC and challenging Robert Mugabe in 2008, but later electoral defeat, party splits, and illness have made him a liability. It says he should allow leadership renewal while supporting the opposition alliance in an advisory role.
