The SD Card Association releases the Simplified Specification/Addendum as a non-confidential subset provided “AS-IS,” with no warranties, liability, licenses, or obligation to disclose further technical information.

The passage criticizes Stanford’s Program in Writing and Rhetoric as lacking rigor, overly broad in course topics, politically biased, and ineffective at teaching academic writing. It argues that PWR encourages vague writing rather than source-based analysis, gives inflated grades, and functions as a requirement rather than meaningful skill development. The authors propose placement options for proficient writers, oppose a potential PWR minor, and suggest replacing current courses with a more standardized, rigorous, source-based writing class designed by experienced humanities professors.

This descriptive cross-sectional study examined burnout, associated factors, and coping strategies among prison officers at Nsawam Medium Security Prison in Ghana. Of 266 recruited officers, 243 questionnaires were analyzed. Data were collected using adapted tools including the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey, Work Environment Scale, and Coping Methods Checklist.

Participants were mostly male, single, junior-ranked officers, and many had worked for less than five years. Burnout prevalence was 9%. High emotional exhaustion was found in 42.0% of officers, high depersonalization in 32.5%, and low personal accomplishment in 68.7%. Irregular shifts, heavy workload, and lack of training and development opportunities were the main perceived causes of burnout.

Shift allocation was significantly associated with emotional exhaustion, and rank was significantly associated with depersonalization, with junior officers more affected. Sex and education were significantly associated with burnout: male officers and officers with diploma/certificate qualifications had lower odds of burnout than female officers and those with postgraduate degrees.

Officers reported mixed views of the work environment, including limited recognition, feedback, trust in superiors, and rewards, but many felt part of a team, valued by colleagues, in control of their work, and proud of their workplace. The main coping strategies were talking to colleagues, looking forward to off-duty periods, and talking to family. The study concludes that irregular shifts, heavy workload, and limited training opportunities require attention to reduce burnout among prison officers.

Montecito Fire Protection District will teach fire safety to about 800 elementary and preschool children during Fire Prevention Week, with lessons including “Stop Drop and Roll,” “Crawl Low in Smoke,” home fire hazards, 9-1-1 calls, and safe evacuation. Activities scheduled for Oct. 3-6 were canceled due to predicted inclement weather and will be rescheduled; other events remain scheduled.

BMW M has not revealed M8 specifications, but the passage suggests it will use a CLAR platform, a 4.4-liter twin-turbo V8 from the F90 M5, and all-wheel drive. The prototype shows downgraded lights, brakes, and wheels. The original M8 never reached production, though its V12 powered the McLaren F1.

Ottawa police say a man was robbed and assaulted after stopping to help a woman who claimed her car had broken down near Innes and O’Toole roads. Police allege the woman and two accomplices stole his wallet and fled with cash. The victim was treated in hospital. Police released suspect and vehicle descriptions and asked for information.

At the Code Conference, Aileen Lee, Megan Smith and Sukhinder Singh Cassidy discussed diversity and inclusion in tech. Lee criticized biases that favor men described as “good guys” while women and people of color face stricter qualification questions. She called for re-engineering business processes to reduce bias and emphasized board-level diversity. The panel also addressed backlash, including men avoiding one-on-one meetings with women. Smith said women of color are the most excluded.

StockX has added BAPE and PALACE to its streetwear marketplace, expanding a category that launched in October 2017 with Supreme merchandise. The company says it will offer over 4,000 authenticated BAPE products dating back to 2010 and more than 3,000 PALACE products. Scotty Newman leads BAPE as general manager, while Kenny Locklier manages PALACE curation. StockX, founded in 2016 by Josh Luber, Greg Schwartz and Dan Gilbert, enables anonymous, transparent buying and selling of sneakers, watches, handbags and streetwear, with all products physically inspected and authenticated.

Glen Campbell’s family shared that he is in the final stages of Alzheimer’s disease, but music remains a comforting part of his life. His daughter Ashley said he sometimes smiles and sings along. Fans are also hearing his final album, “Adios,” recorded in 2012 and released June 9.

Vertigo, an iOS app, now integrates with both Spotify Premium and Apple Music, enabling users to share music across subscriptions. Users can import playlists, find music, share songs, and host live listening sessions with video, photos, chat, or audio commentary. Sessions can be shared with individuals, friend groups, or the app community. Vertigo supports legal sharing by requiring paid subscriptions and paying royalties to rights holders, with royalties increasing as more subscribers listen. The app may help Apple Music users gain social features that Spotify emphasizes and Apple Music has reduced.

Brazilian stocks rose Thursday, led by Vale after record first-quarter iron ore output for the period and analyst support. Usiminas also gained after returning to profit. The real remained volatile amid geopolitical concerns and European election uncertainty, though French polls eased some worries.

The study evaluated a streamlined workflow for optical genome mapping (OGM) analysis and reporting in hematologic malignancies using Bionano Access and VIA software. Ten retrospective myeloid malignancy cases, including nine AML and one MDS, were reviewed multiple times by independent technologist-director teams to assess efficiency and reproducibility.

OGM via VIA detected all variants identified by standard-of-care testing and found additional reportable variants in five of six positive cases. Tier 1A variants, including BCR::ABL1, CBFB::MYH11, RUNX1::RUNX1T1, and KMT2A::MLLT10 fusions, were consistently identified and classified. Non–Tier 1A variants showed more variability in reporting and classification.

Technologist review averaged 25.2 minutes for negative cases, 28.5 minutes for simple cases, and 47.3 minutes for complex cases. Compared with prior Bionano Access-only review, VIA reduced analysis time and added features such as customizable reporting and variant database support. The authors conclude that OGM with VIA provides an efficient, single-assay approach for cytogenomic variant interpretation and reporting in hematologic disorders.

The reporter used a Eurail pass in October 2022 to take eight train rides across Germany, Austria, Italy, and Switzerland over seven days. The pass cost $477, with upgrades and overnight train fees bringing total train costs to $560. They preferred trains to flying because boarding was easier, seats and sleeper options were more comfortable, views were better, and train travel avoided issues like ear-popping and dehydration. They also valued trains as a more sustainable way to travel in Europe.

The Rio Blanco 4-H senior livestock judging team concluded its 2018 season at the 73rd annual Colorado 4-H June conference at Colorado State University. Macy Collins placed third high individual overall, and Marryn Shults placed seventh. Shults was fourth in beef, fifth in sheep/goats and seventh in individual placings; Collins was fifth in beef, third in swine, fourth in sheep/goats, eighth in individual placings and third in oral reasons. Jilly Bumguardner and Tatumn Kennedy gained experience for future contests. Collins made the Colorado State 4-H Livestock All State team, will be recognized at the Colorado State Fair, and will attend Hutchinson Junior College on a full academic and judging scholarship.

Trump warned Iran against restarting its nuclear program as he met Macron in Washington to discuss the 2015 nuclear deal. Trump criticized the accord as flawed for not addressing ballistic missiles or Iran’s regional role, while Macron urged preserving it as part of broader regional security efforts. Iran has threatened to expand its program if the deal collapses. The leaders also discussed steel tariffs, Syria, U.S. troops, and their countries’ cooperation in recent airstrikes.

A football holder catches the snap on field goals and extra points, quickly places the ball in the kicker’s preferred spot and angle, and turns the laces away. The role requires soft hands, consistency, quick mechanics, and precision under pressure, as mistakes can lead to missed scoring chances. Holders often work closely with long snappers and kickers to maintain rhythm and confidence. They may also be involved in fake field goals by passing, flipping, or running the ball. The position has no specific body type; NFL teams often use punters, while lower levels may use backup quarterbacks, receivers, or others. Holders receive little attention and have no NFL statistics, but they are important because their execution can affect extra points, field goals, and game outcomes.

The Daily Examiner is shifting from a metered digital subscription model to a premium model with some subscriber-only stories marked by a PLUS symbol. Public safety information and some local stories will remain accessible. Existing subscribers keep unlimited access, including other News Corp sites. Subscriptions may include the Saturday paper, digital access, the app, newsletters and alerts. Sign-ups are available online or by phone.

Thailand reported 390 road deaths during the seven days of Songkran, an 11% decrease from the previous year, following junta campaigns against drink driving. Measures included harsher penalties, vehicle seizures and mortuary visits for offenders, but Prayut Chan-O-Cha said the toll remained unacceptable. Drunk driving caused 28% of accidents, while authorities seized 5,600 motorbikes and 1,800 cars. Myanmar reported 285 road deaths during the same period.

The EU is preparing a proposal urging multilateral development banks to align financing more closely with the Paris Agreement, shift lending away from fossil fuels, and increase investment in green energy, climate resilience, and sustainability projects. Led by Germany and France, the plan will be discussed at World Bank and IMF meetings but faces U.S. opposition over concerns it could distract from poverty reduction and economic growth.

The Supreme Court of Canada ruled 7-0 that records detailing abuse of former residential school students may be destroyed after 15 years. The court upheld a lower court decision, saying the settlement’s independent assessment process was intended to be confidential and private. The records include sensitive information from more than 37,000 compensation claims involving accounts of physical, sexual and emotional abuse.

Eric Thames hit a two-run homer in the fifth inning to lift the Milwaukee Brewers over the Minnesota Twins 2-0. Junior Guerra pitched five shutout innings, while Josh Hader threw three hitless innings and Corey Knebel earned his ninth save. Jake Odorizzi allowed two runs over five innings for Minnesota, which fell to 1-7 on its road trip. Christian Yelich and Lorenzo Cain remained limited by injuries, and Chase Anderson is scheduled to start the series finale against Jose Berrios.

Steven Kean forwarded to Enron colleagues a McKinsey update from Suzanne Nimocks on international electric power sector privatization and restructuring for June–November 2000. The report says governments facing rising power demand and limited funds are broadly opening generation markets to foreign investors, unbundling state utilities, and introducing wholesale and retail competition. It reviews developments across Europe, Central and Eastern Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and the Middle East/Africa, noting EU-driven liberalization in Europe, renewed restructuring in recovering Asian economies, slower restarted privatizations in Latin America after currency problems, and increasing foreign investment and IPP activity in Africa and the Middle East. It also highlights trends including utility mergers, trading platforms, transmission concessions and regional grid links, while noting obstacles such as regulation gaps, drought, currency fluctuations, nonpayment, political opposition, and concerns over IPP contracts.

The passage argues that each U.S. inauguration renews national dedication, with the present task being to protect the nation and its institutions from external disruption. It rejects claims that democracy is failing, citing recent crisis survival, constitutional functioning, preserved rights, and free elections. It describes America’s spirit as rooted in freedom, democratic aspiration, founding documents, and generations seeking a new life. The passage states that national security, opportunity, and knowledge matter, but the nation’s spirit is greatest. It concludes that preserving democracy and the faith of America justifies sacrifice for national defense and requires moving forward rather than retreating.

Former CIA case officer Kevin Mallory is on trial in Alexandria, Virginia, accused of giving a Chinese spy top-secret information, including details about human assets, for $25,000. Prosecutors said his actions were exposed after customs agents found $16,500 in undeclared cash when he returned from Shanghai in 2017, and later found messages and classified documents. The defence said Mallory was a loyal American who contacted CIA associates because he suspected a Chinese think-tank offer and intended to feed false information. Witnesses testified he contacted CIA-linked individuals before the Shanghai trip. Mallory faces up to life in prison.

Olean’s Common Council unanimously authorized Mayor Bill Aiello to apply for a $10 million state Downtown Revitalization Initiative grant. The proposal area runs from Olean General Hospital to the Allegheny River and from Franchot Park to about Seventh Street. Proposed projects include redeveloping the former Manufacturers Hanover building, supporting business incubators, expanding downtown theater options, improving pedestrian access to Lincoln Park and creating a park near Olean General Hospital. Aiello said the city may also qualify for more than $2 million through the Buffalo Billion initiative. Jamestown Community College’s John Sayegh supported the application and said JCC could work with the city to improve the Cutco Theater.

Uber launched a nationwide in-app panic button allowing riders to call 911 from the home screen. The app shows riders’ real-time location, and in select pilot cities it automatically sends location and vehicle details to emergency dispatchers. CEO Dana Khosrowshahi said the feature aims to help users in emergencies.

IDC’s white paper examines the use of IT-based simulation, modeling, data analytics, and high-performance computing in manufacturing enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, based on a December 2021 survey of 200 decision makers. Industrial firms face pressures including geopolitical uncertainty, energy costs, supply disruptions, labor shortages, and sustainability demands, while digitalization is reshaping value creation.

Simulation, modeling, and analytics are widely linked to innovation, faster product development, cost reduction, quality improvement, and better decision making. Many firms already use them in product development, production planning, process planning, and quality management, with broader deployment expected. IDC highlights the need for integrated data sources and a single source of truth to avoid data silos and support collaboration across departments, partners, and ecosystems.

The paper identifies digital twins, virtual prototyping, design optimization, high-performance data analytics, visualization, AR/VR, and engineering workstations as a service as important technologies. HPC is presented as increasingly necessary for complex calculations, faster iterations, higher-quality simulations, and new use cases. While 81% of respondents view HPC as a game changer, firms face challenges including security concerns, high costs, energy consumption, technical complexity, availability, scalability, and shortages of expertise.

Most HPC users prefer or plan external infrastructures, cloud providers, colocation, or hybrid models rather than on-premises systems. IDC says public cloud, hybrid cloud, and HPC as a Service can improve scalability, flexibility, cost management, access to modern technologies, collaboration, and potential HPC-based business models. The paper recommends developing virtual product and manufacturing processes, creating a holistic data strategy, selecting suitable HPC operating models, prioritizing scalability, security and energy efficiency, and using external expertise where needed.

The passage lists AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Revision A3 specification issues and workarounds. Reported problems include missed PIC interrupts with automatic clock gating, PRD prefetch hazards in ATAC and ACC, UDMA CRC errors after device termination, IDE SSMI not blocking I/O, GLIU ASMI loss with clock gating, ACPI PM1 byte access hangs, PMC register corruption on WORD/BYTE writes, KEL emulation and snoop-mode register issues, PCI back-to-back read simulation failure, unsupported PIC polling, UART CEIR failure with clock gating, PCI tVAL timing shortfall, unreliable CS5535 SSMIs, IDE/ATAPI failures with improper bus-master sequencing or device interrupts, S3 wake limitations, RTC CMOS read/write anomalies, LPC DMA and LPC sync abort issues, USB controller clock-gating failures, SMB NEGACK and hold-time problems, GPIO high-bank write corruption after suspend, missing LOWBAT_FLAG, and sleep-exit delay counter issues. Recommended mitigations include disabling affected clock gating, using aligned and predefined PRD tables, avoiding unsupported features or byte accesses, trapping accesses in SMI, using normal IDE/UDMA procedures, using single-transfer DMA, using processor SSMI capabilities, using PWRBTN# for S3 wake, applying driver alignment requirements, and programming delay counters appropriately.

The speaker said their team struggled to generate chances, especially on the power play, and gave Detroit an early two-goal lead after a brief letdown. They felt the game was mostly even after the first ten minutes but acknowledged Detroit’s defensive strength and said their team must play better and contribute more.

The study examines the effects of digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth on sustainable supply chain performance through brand image and supply chain image, focusing on Indonesian ICT companies. It argues that digitalization and e-commerce influence customer experience, brand image, and supply chain activities, while ICT firms face challenges from rapid digital technology changes and limited infrastructure.

Data were collected from employees involved in product distribution in ICT companies. Indonesia was divided into 15 clusters, 10 were randomly selected, and respondents were randomly chosen. Of 568 distributed questionnaires, 315 valid responses were analyzed using PLS-SEM.

The measurement model showed acceptable factor loadings, reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity. Hypothesis testing supported all seven hypotheses. Digital customer experience positively affected brand image, and electronic word of mouth also positively affected brand image. Brand image positively affected supply chain image, and supply chain image positively affected sustainable supply chain performance. Brand image mediated the relationships between digital customer experience and supply chain image, and between electronic word of mouth and supply chain image. Supply chain image mediated the relationship between brand image and sustainable supply chain performance.

The model explained 82.3% of the variance in sustainable supply chain performance. The study concludes that Indonesian ICT companies should enhance brand image through digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth by implementing e-commerce practices, as this can improve supply chain image and sustainable supply chain performance.

The passage describes a NASA-supported patent application for operating a hybrid gas turbine electric propulsion system during descent. The engine includes compressor and turbine sections, shafts, a fan, geared architecture, and an electric motor/generator connected to a shaft. The engine may be undersized for takeoff or climb because the motor can supplement power. During descent or other low-power modes, the engine core may be turned off or maintained at a minimum temperature to avoid thermal cycling, reducing fuel burn and emissions. Aircraft systems can switch from engine bleed or engine power to electric operation using stored energy or electricity generated by fan windmilling. The motor/generator may also power the low spool to produce enough thrust to match descent requirements or overcome engine drag.

Apple filed a Form 8-K reporting that on February 8, 2021 it completed the issuance and sale of senior unsecured notes totaling $14.0 billion across six series maturing from 2026 to 2061. The notes were issued under a February 1, 2021 underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, J.P. Morgan Securities LLC and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, pursuant to Apple’s 2018 indenture and Form S-3 registration statement. Interest is payable semiannually on February 8 and August 8 beginning August 8, 2021. The filing includes related underwriting, officer certificate, note form, legal opinion and consent exhibits.

In spring 1953, the central question for the free world is the possibility of a just peace. The passage contrasts the hopes of 1945 with the fear and division that followed, arguing that the United States and other free nations pursued cooperation, self-determination, reduced armaments, and peace, while Soviet leaders sought security through force, domination, and military superiority.

The text states that Soviet power led free nations to arm themselves, unify, and remain ready for war, while still remaining open to genuine evidence of peaceful intent. It warns that continued militarization risks atomic war or, at best, a world burdened by fear, tension, and wasted resources. It emphasizes the human cost of armaments by comparing weapons spending to schools, hospitals, homes, food, power plants, and roads.

Following Stalin’s death, the passage says the new Soviet leadership has an opportunity to change course. It calls for deeds rather than rhetoric, citing possible signs such as an Austrian treaty and the release of World War II prisoners. It identifies an honorable armistice in Korea, free elections in a united Korea, and an end to attacks on Indochina and Malaya as first steps toward wider settlements.

The United States declares readiness to support Austrian independence, Western European unity, a free and united Germany, East European independence, and negotiated disarmament. Proposed measures include limits on military forces and strategic materials, international control of atomic energy, restrictions on destructive weapons, and enforcement through United Nations inspection.

The passage argues that savings from disarmament should support global aid, reconstruction, development, trade, and productive freedom. It concludes that peace depends on whether the Soviet Union will act concretely to support peace in Asia, allow nations free political choice, and join enforceable disarmament efforts.

Cloud-based HPCaaS offers manufacturing enterprises fast, flexible access to advanced analysis and simulation methods, modern hardware, scalability, and potential cost and agility benefits. IDC views HPC, simulations, modeling, and data analytics as key enablers of digital transformation, supporting faster product development, optimized supply chains, sustainability, and new digital products, services, and business models. IDC recommends adopting virtual product and manufacturing development, creating a holistic data strategy and single source of truth, evaluating the best HPC operating model, prioritizing scalability, security, and energy efficiency, and using external expertise where needed. The findings are based on a December 2021 IDC telephone survey of 200 decision makers from industrial enterprises in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

A federal judge ruled that Nirvana’s 1991 album cover showing Spencer Elden as a nude baby underwater was not child pornography and dismissed his 2021 lawsuit. Judge Fernando Olguin said the image was not lascivious and was most comparable to a family photo of a nude child bathing.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced to life in prison plus 30 years for conspiracy and solicitation in the 2014 murder of Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, her former son-in-law. Adelson denied involvement, calling herself innocent and claiming there was no evidence against her. Judge Stephen Everett warned he could consider her “utter lack of remorse.” Prosecutors said the murder-for-hire plot was motivated by the Adelson family’s desire to move Markel’s ex-wife, Wendi Adelson, and their children to South Florida. Donna’s son Charlie Adelson, Katherine Magbanua and one hit man were convicted of murder; another hit man pleaded guilty. Harvey Adelson also claimed his wife was innocent.

NVIDIA filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 30, 2022. Revenue was $5.93 billion for the quarter, down from $7.10 billion a year earlier, while net income was $680 million, down from $2.46 billion. For the first nine months of fiscal 2023, revenue was $20.92 billion, up from $19.27 billion, and net income was $2.95 billion, down from $6.75 billion.

Quarterly gross margin declined to 53.6% from 65.2%, primarily due to a $702 million inventory charge, partly offset by a $70 million warranty-related benefit. Operating expenses rose to $2.58 billion from $1.96 billion. NVIDIA recorded a $1.35 billion acquisition termination cost in the first quarter of fiscal 2023 after terminating its planned Arm acquisition due to regulatory challenges.

Data Center revenue was $3.83 billion in the quarter, up 31% year over year, while Gaming revenue fell 51% to $1.57 billion. Professional Visualization revenue fell 65% to $200 million, Automotive revenue rose 86% to $251 million, and OEM and Other revenue fell 69% to $73 million.

As of October 30, 2022, NVIDIA had $13.14 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. The company repurchased $8.99 billion of shares and paid $300 million in dividends during the first nine months of fiscal 2023. Common shares outstanding as of November 11, 2022 were 2.46 billion.

Myrna LaPlante, whose aunt Emily Osmond went missing in 2006, supports the current National Inquiry into Murdered and Missing Indigenous Women and Girls and opposes resetting it under new leadership, saying she would request her family’s story be removed from the public record. She said families were not consulted before the Assembly of First Nations voted to call for chief commissioner Marion Buller’s resignation, though she supports extending the inquiry by two years. LaPlante said the inquiry needs more time, staffing, and community partnerships. Other Saskatchewan families support Buller’s resignation, citing poor communication, late hearing changes, travel uncertainty, and lack of support. Lillian Ewenin said Saskatoon hearings reinforced concerns, while Danielle Ewenin criticized the commission’s handling of community trauma.

Scott Sheldon outlines ways to improve mortgage borrowing power as rates approach 5 percent for average 30-year fixed mortgages. He says paying off debt can lower debt-to-income ratios because lenders focus on minimum monthly payments, not interest rates. Adding a co-signer may help when income is insufficient, but the co-signer shares full responsibility until refinancing or sale. Changing loan programs, such as switching between Freddie Mac, Fannie Mae, conventional, or FHA loans, may affect approval chances. Putting more money down can help but may be less effective than paying off debt. Changing jobs may also help if the new position is in the same or a similar field, but it requires careful review by a loan officer.

IEP News for July 31, 2001 compiled articles on California’s energy crisis. Topics included criticism of Gov. Gray Davis’ $43 billion long-term power contracts, an SEC preliminary inquiry into whether Davis energy consultants used inside information to trade power company stocks, and scrutiny of spokesman Steve Maviglio’s Calpine and Enron holdings. Other reports covered efforts to bail out Southern California Edison, consultants Chris Lehane and Mark Fabiani agreeing to forgo state payments, San Francisco ballot measures to create public power agencies, limited federal electricity refunds for California, Texas beginning a deregulation pilot program, and concerns over utility restructuring in Maryland.

Sony released a firmware update for the A7Riii to fix the “Set File Name” issue and improve camera stability. Some Mac users cannot install it because macOS High Sierra 10.13 is not supported. The update is compatible with Mac OS X 10.10–10.11 and macOS 10.12; users can use an earlier macOS version or Windows as a workaround.

Singapore’s special education system has evolved within the country’s broader development as a highly successful, education-focused city-state. Before 2004, students with disabilities were largely served outside mainstream education through special schools run by voluntary welfare organizations, now social service agencies, while mainstream schools focused on integration rather than inclusion and could decide whether to admit students with disabilities.

The year 2004 marked a turning point after Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong called for a more inclusive society and better support for students with disabilities in mainstream schools. Subsequent developments included Enabling Masterplans, Singapore’s signing and ratification of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, and the recognition of special schools as part of a continuum within one national education system. The Compulsory Education Act of 2019 requires students with special educational needs to attend either mainstream primary schools or government-funded special schools.

The number of students with disabilities in mainstream schools rose from 2,500 in 2005 to 35,500, with about 80% of students with special needs now served in mainstream schools. Teacher and personnel preparation expanded through programs at the National Institute of Education, including training for Special Educational Needs Officers, the Certificate in Special Needs Support for mainstream teachers, compulsory pre-service coursework on diverse learners, and diploma, advanced diploma, master’s, and doctoral pathways in special education.

Policy implementation has been shaped by Singapore’s centralized education system, tripartite relationships among the Ministry of Education, the National Institute of Education, and schools, and continuity under long-term government leadership. Current issues include the status of special schools under social service agencies rather than the Ministry of Education, lower salaries for special education teachers compared with mainstream teachers, limited mainstream-based options for students with higher support needs, and the need to strengthen special education teacher preparation and career pathways. Singapore’s broader shift toward holistic, lifelong learning is expected to expand the role of special education in both mainstream and special schools.

The lecture reviews PDE modeling for a drug patch diffusion problem with flow, emphasizing sharp concentration gradients, small characteristic length scales, high Peclet number, mesh refinement, convergence checks, and skepticism toward numerical outputs. Students are instructed to solve the problem using COMSOL and their own finite volume code. Finite volume methods are explained through control volumes, flux balances, boundary conditions, ghost cells, sparse linear systems, and solver choices such as MATLAB backslash and BiCGSTAB. The lecture also introduces the CFL number for time-dependent PDEs and explains why large time steps relative to spatial discretization can produce unphysical results.

The second part introduces probability as essential because measurements and physical systems fluctuate. It discusses measurement uncertainty, averages, error bars, intrinsic fluctuations, and probability distributions. Basic probability concepts include event probabilities, joint probabilities, conditional probabilities, OR versus AND cases, Bayes’ theorem, and continuous probability densities. The lecture distinguishes probability density functions from cumulative probability distributions and notes that densities require integration over a range to yield probabilities.

Michael Lewis’ The Undoing Project recounts Lew Goldberg’s 1968 study in which doctors judged the probability of cancer in 96 stomach ulcers shown via x-rays, with duplicate cases mixed in. Doctors disagreed with one another and each contradicted themselves at least once. Researchers then asked doctors how they made diagnoses and built a simple computer algorithm from their answers; it performed better than the best doctor. The passage notes uncertainties about how disagreements were handled and how x-ray data was coded for computers, while raising broader questions about experts, algorithms, artificial intelligence, and diagnosis.

The New York Times reported U.S. agencies intercepted calls last year between Russian intelligence officials and Trump campaign members, including Paul Manafort, though officials said they found no evidence the campaign worked with Russia to influence the election. The FBI interviewed former national security adviser Michael Flynn about contacts with Russia’s ambassador after Trump’s inauguration; Flynn resigned amid concerns he misled officials. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called for an independent investigation and for Attorney General Jeff Sessions to recuse himself.

Several Republican senators withheld support for labor secretary nominee Andrew Puzder ahead of his hearing, citing questions about his employment of an unauthorized housekeeper and delayed tax payments. Linda McMahon was sworn in to lead the Small Business Administration after an 81-19 Senate confirmation vote. David Shulkin was sworn in as Veterans Affairs secretary after unanimous Senate confirmation.
United Way of Northwest Illinois will launch Imagination Library in Carroll County on March 28, 2018, providing books to children ages 0-5 with support from partners including the Morse Group.

Which? research suggests lenders were slow to pass the November base rate rise to savers but quicker to increase mortgage costs. It found 48% of 327 instant access savings accounts and ISAs saw no rate change within five weeks, while 21% passed on the full 0.25 percentage point rise. Among 95 providers, 10% applied the full rise to all such accounts. For mortgages, 53% of standard variable rate providers had raised rates for existing borrowers by the end of 2017, and average fixed-rate deals also increased. UK Finance said rates depend on various factors and customers can compare and switch products.

Rare wave-like Asperitas clouds were seen over Bristol, Thornbury, Filton and Monmouthshire on Monday morning. The Met Office said Asperitas was recently added to the International Cloud Atlas, though how the clouds form remains uncertain.

The lecture discusses D-branes as dynamical objects whose fluctuations arise from open-string massless modes, including gauge fields and scalar fields. The mass of a Dp-brane is defined as its ground-state energy, or the vacuum energy of open strings living on it, and its tension scales as \(1/g_s\) at weak string coupling. This follows from summing open-string vacuum diagrams with boundaries, where the disk contribution dominates.

An alternative way to determine D-brane tension is through the interaction between two D-branes. At large separation, their leading interaction is mediated by massless closed-string modes such as gravitons. The same cylinder diagram can be viewed either as tree-level closed-string exchange or as a one-loop open-string diagram, illustrating open-closed channel duality and hinting at the relation between gauge theory and gravity.

The low-energy effective action on a D-brane contains the brane tension, Maxwell terms for gauge fields, and kinetic terms for scalar fields describing transverse brane motion. For constant field strengths and small derivatives, higher-order corrections combine into the Dirac-Born-Infeld action. With no gauge field, this reduces to the volume action for a relativistically moving p-dimensional object. The scalar modes are massless because they are Goldstone bosons associated with broken translation symmetry.

Open-string interaction strength \(g_o\) is related to closed-string coupling by \(g_s \propto g_o^2\). When multiple coincident D-branes are present, open strings can begin and end on different branes, giving fields matrix indices. For \(N\) coincident branes, open-string modes become \(N \times N\) matrices, and the world-volume theory has \(U(N)\) gauge symmetry with Yang-Mills dynamics at low energies.

Separating branes changes the boundary conditions for strings stretched between them. Strings with both ends on the same brane remain massless, while strings stretched between different branes acquire mass proportional to their length times the string tension. In field-theory terms, separating branes corresponds to a Higgs mechanism breaking \(U(N)\) into products such as \(U(n_1)\times U(n_2)\times\cdots\), depending on how the branes are grouped.

Belleville-area residents are being advised to be aware of Hickory Tussock Moth caterpillars, which are white and fluffy with black markings and long black hairs connected to poison glands. Found mainly from July to September in trees such as hickory, walnut and oak, they can cause rashes, burning, swelling, pain, headaches, nausea or allergic reactions if touched. Public health officials recommend washing affected skin, using calamine lotion or cortisone for itching, and seeking medical attention for stronger reactions. Experts say the caterpillars are not a major health hazard and should simply be observed without touching.

The passage describes MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 device peripherals, support resources, application guidance, revision history, and packaging information. The LFSS includes a real-time clock with prescaler and timestamp captures plus an asynchronous independent watchdog, using a low-frequency clock typically at 32 kHz. VREF provides selectable 1.4 V and 2.5 V internal references, ADC support up to 515 ksps, and external reference pins. Investors can trade calls and puts on META and other assets through brokers, with different strikes and expirations. The passage states a $100 minimum deposit, one-contract minimum trade size, leverage up to 1:100 depending on broker, and margin requirements generally similar to other single-stock options. Brokers may provide order entry, options chains, watch lists, charts, analytics, research, education, demo accounts, and risk management tools such as stop losses and trailing stops. Fees may include broker commissions, financing charges, slippage, and inactivity fees. Strategies include calls, puts, covered or naked writing, straddles, strangles, and spreads. The Nuclear Medicine market report provides competitive analysis, company profiles, product specifications, technology, production, revenue, cost, gross margin, and regional data. Eric Hirsch, founding CEO of EdReports, will step down at the end of the school year as the board searches for a successor. Hirsch has led the nonprofit since 2014, when it began independently reviewing instructional materials. Despite early criticism from publishers, EdReports has completed more than 1,100 reviews and is widely used by states and districts in curriculum decisions.

His departure comes as EdReports revises its scoring process, expands into pre-K materials and faces criticism over how it evaluates reading programs and standards alignment. The organization has updated its criteria to emphasize phonics, fluency and phonemic awareness while continuing to consider standards where useful.

Observers said Hirsch maintained a strong focus on the connection between curriculum and standards, helping educators demand higher-quality materials. Looking ahead, EdReports may need leadership attentive to artificial intelligence, teacher guidance, tutoring and intervention supports. Hirsch noted that adopting strong curriculum alone is insufficient, citing research showing mismatches among curriculum, teacher training and assessment.

The Gann Fan is a technical analysis tool created by W.D. Gann that uses angled lines drawn from significant highs or lows to identify potential support and resistance levels, breakouts, reversals, entries, exits, and price targets. Its main 45-degree 1:1 line represents equal movement in price and time, with other angles including 2:1, 3:1, 4:1, 8:1, 1:8, 1:4, 1:3, and 1:2. The strategy assumes price moves follow geometric patterns, though the passage notes it is subjective and not always accurate. Traders are advised to use it with other tools, multiple timeframes, clear trading rules, and risk management. The passage says meaningful backtesting is difficult because the pattern lacks objective rules, and past performance does not guarantee future results.

Cover 1 is man-to-man coverage with a free safety in a deep middle zone and sometimes a low-hole defender for short-intermediate middle routes. It lets defenses simplify assignments, support the run, blitz, bracket receivers, and force difficult throws. Offenses attack Cover 1 by targeting the outside away from safety help, using perimeter matchups, pick plays, double moves, and routes that let receivers catch on the move. Examples include slot fades, bubble-go concepts, out-and-up double moves, goal-line motion to the flat, and red-zone scissors or snag-wheel combinations.

The passage traces how “unskilled” work in the United States has been classified, performed, valued, and regulated from the 19th century through the Covid-19 pandemic. Early occupational classifications distinguished “mental force” work from manual work, applying “skilled,” “semi-skilled,” and “unskilled” mainly to labor involving physical effort. “Unskilled” work was defined as requiring little training, judgment, or dexterity, but the passage shows that worker identity—especially race, gender, age, and immigration status—also shaped classification.

In 1930, about 14 million people, or 28% of the workforce, were in “unskilled” occupations such as farm labor, servant work, factory labor, and other labor. African Americans were disproportionately represented. By the 21st century, terms such as “low-skill” and “unskilled” remained common, often tied to education requirements or job content. In 2018, more than half of the U.S. labor force worked in jobs requiring a high school degree or less, with a median annual wage of $33,473.

The passage examines major categories of historically “unskilled” labor. Farm labor relied heavily on enslaved African labor, later sharecropping, convict leasing, and immigrant labor. Although agricultural employment declined sharply, many crops were still harvested by hand in 2019 by workers often facing low wages, part-time work, dangerous conditions, and limited protections. Factory labor expanded with industrialization, child labor, immigrant labor, and assembly-line production, then declined with automation, offshoring, and changes in production systems. Some remaining low-wage manufacturing work included prison labor and garment sweatshops.

Servant occupations shifted into modern service work as household technology and consumer habits changed. Domestic work, Pullman porter jobs, retail, fast food, home health care, childcare, and gig work are described as often low-paid, repetitive, physically demanding, unstable, or closely monitored, while frequently performed by women, people of color, immigrants, and non-college-educated workers. “Other labor” included construction, mining, warehousing, digital micro-tasking, and content moderation, with examples of dangerous or poorly paid work.

The passage reviews efforts to improve job quality. Education levels rose, but education alone did not improve conditions for low-wage workers. Government actions such as the Fair Labor Standards Act and National Labor Relations Act created labor protections, though agriculture, domestic work, tipped work, and independent contracting were excluded from key protections. Labor organizing, strikes, unions, and worker advocacy groups won wage increases, union recognition, and legal protections in several industries, though union membership declined after its mid-20th-century peak. Some employers improved wages, job design, training, scheduling, and career paths, including examples linked to Ford, Toyota, and companies using the “Good Jobs Strategy.”

During the Covid-19 pandemic, many workers in historically “unskilled” jobs were classified as “essential,” especially in healthcare, agriculture, transportation, warehousing, and services. These workers often could not work remotely, sometimes lacked adequate protection, and faced serious health risks while earning low wages.

The passage concludes that future-of-work debates have often emphasized automation and job loss, while recent commissions identified job quality as the central issue. It asks how work, workers, and pay should be understood when jobs historically categorized as “unskilled” are also essential to the economy.

Christine Milligan was surprised when asked whether to revoke her daughter Cassidey Ouellete’s organ donation consent after Ouellete died in a car accident near Peterborough, since Ouellete had signed her donor card at 16. Ontario’s Trillium Gift of Life Network says families can prevent donation if a loved one had expressed regret, though overrides are uncommon and fell from 21 per cent in 2015 to about 10 per cent in 2016. CEO Ronnie Gavsie said families may be exhausted when life support decisions are made and that donation can prolong the process. Trillium urges people to discuss their wishes with family. Milligan wants revived legislation that would let only donors revoke consent and would create presumed consent with opt-out provisions, but Gavsie said polls and agency research do not support presumed consent.

S&P Global Platts will launch low-sulphur marine gasoil and diesel price assessments at several Asian bunkering ports from June 1, 2017, reflecting fuels with maximum 0.1 percent sulphur. The move follows rising demand, including strong growth in Singapore sales, and expected tighter global sulphur limits. Prices will cover Singapore, Fujairah, Hong Kong, Shanghai, South Korea, Tokyo Bay and West Japan.

Motley Fool Money reviews the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card, highlighting unlimited 2% cash rewards on purchases, a $200 bonus after $500 spent in the first 3 months, 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, no annual fee, and up to $600 cell phone protection. The card is presented as suited for applicants with good/excellent credit and for users seeking simple flat-rate cash rewards. The passage also lists offers for the Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card and Citi Double Cash® Card, along with disclosures about advertising partnerships, compensation, and editorial independence.

The speaker praises a teammate’s reliable play and discusses enjoying life in Carolina, citing a family atmosphere, supportive neighborhood, and growing fan interest. He says winning helps build recognition and support, including for hockey in southern markets. He believes the game is more exciting with more scoring and comebacks, and wants to help attract more children to hockey. He notes Carolina’s appeal as a place to live and raise a family, says he hopes to finish his career there, and explains he joined because he saw depth and potential in the team despite its lack of big-name stars.

The passage argues that South American misunderstandings of the United States’ Monroe Doctrine—especially fears of superiority or protectorate claims—had hindered relations, trade, and investment. Secretary Root’s mission sought to dispel this view, and his Rio address emphasized peace, sovereignty, equal rights among American republics, mutual prosperity, opposition to colonization, and cooperation to prevent conflict. The speaker approves Root’s words and says they reflect American sentiment. The passage also cites Doctor Drago’s view that U.S. policy opposed European oppression without seeking dominance, praises honors given to U.S. figures in Argentina and Brazil, and thanks the governments and peoples visited by Root.

Steve Mitchell, a fifth-generation farmer at Boglily Farm near Kirkcaldy, says innovation and social media have helped grow The Buffalo Farm. The business uses social networking to promote products, share farm life and build brand awareness, including marketing buffalo meat to health-focused customers. Its buffalo fillet steak won the 2016 Scotland Food & Drink Excellence Awards Meat category, which Mitchell says boosted credibility and opened doors with larger clients. Entries are now open for the 2018 awards.

Edmonton officials called a road salting pilot successful after saving $4.2 million and reducing sand use by 68 per cent, but chemical engineer Arthur Potts warned council it is too early to continue. He said liquid calcium chloride may cause significant damage to vehicles, concrete, driveways and bridges, and argued testing done outside Edmonton may be irrelevant because corrosion depends on local conditions. Residents have reported increased rust on vehicles and bikes. Officials said they want to continue the program, potentially buying specialized equipment and pre-wetting traditional salt, though costs are unknown. Environmental monitoring results are expected in October, while collision comparison data is not yet available.

An AI tool called Waldo scanned more than 430,000 Reddit posts about cannabis use and flagged over 28,000 as potentially describing unexpected or harmful side effects. Researchers verified 250 flagged posts and found 86 percent described problematic cannabis experiences. Waldo was trained on hand-reviewed Reddit posts and outperformed ChatGPT by producing fewer false positives, though it did not outperform human reviewers. Researchers say such tools could help public health workers detect consumer harms from social media, especially where official reporting is limited, but caution that the tool may not work equally well for other products and would require ethical use and privacy protections.

Witnesses described a white van mounting the sidewalk on Yonge Street near Finch and striking pedestrians as it drove south, with several saying the driver appeared to hit people deliberately. Police said the van and driver were in custody, but the motive and cause were unknown. Officers shut down a large stretch of the area, sought witness information, and created a portal for photos and videos. Multiple witnesses reported bodies, severe injuries, damaged bus shelters, and emergency responders performing CPR. Sunnybrook hospital received 10 patients, including two pronounced dead, five in critical condition, and three in serious condition; North York General Hospital received four patients. Three injured people were Seneca College English Language Institute students. Public Safety Minister Ralph Goodale said available information did not indicate a change in public risk or a national security connection. The TTC temporarily shut subway service between Finch and Sheppard, and the city opened an emergency support site.

King Edward VI Grammar School in Louth placed second in the national schools University Challenge finals at the University of Lincoln. The team, Rowan Roddick, Jack Leeming, Fraser Whittock and Ben Jeffrey, scored 280, behind Southend High School for Boys with 315, after defeating St Ivo and Nottingham High School.

Indian Railways has adopted a “no bill, food is free” policy to prevent overcharging by train caterers. Railway Minister Piyush Goyal directed that trains serving paid food display the message by March 31, while IRCTC is publicising it online and deploying inspectors to ensure proper billing. Officials said many servers refuse bills using excuses. Overcharging is the largest catering complaint, with over 7,000 complaints between April and October last year, followed by quality issues. Railways has terminated two caterer contracts, fined vendors about 5,000 times, and warned of licence cancellations. The CAG had also recommended a system to stop overcharging.

The U.S. withdrew from U.N. discussions on the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration, saying the process could undermine U.S. sovereignty and immigration law. The U.S. bishops expressed disappointment and urged reconsideration, arguing participation would allow the U.S. to help shape international cooperation while protecting migrants’ rights. Pope Francis supported the negotiations and called for migrants and refugees to be welcomed, protected, promoted and integrated.

Supporters of the withdrawal, including the Center for Immigration Studies, said the compact risked interfering with U.S. laws on unauthorized employment and border detention. U.N. officials and others argued the framework would remain subject to national sovereignty and that U.S. absence could reduce its influence. Catholic leaders and scholars emphasized that nations have a right to control borders but also obligations to protect vulnerable migrants and cooperate internationally on migration.

The U.S. government shutdown has worsened air traffic controller shortages, with unpaid controllers calling out sick and staffing down by 50% in some areas, causing delays and safety concerns. The shortage predates the shutdown, driven by lengthy and costly training, high washout rates, retirements, and age limits. Controllers earn an average of $144,580 annually, but applicants must meet strict requirements, complete FAA training, and gain years of experience. The field is projected to grow 3% from 2023 to 2033.

Hascall Steel Company is a US steel service center offering steel processing and a diverse inventory for industrial and commercial applications. Its products include cold reduced, blanked, slit, flat-rolled, hot rolled black, cold rolled aluminized, and coated steel. The company works with local and foreign suppliers, evaluates customer specifications, conducts quality testing in an in-house laboratory, and aims to reduce lead times and supply chain costs. It has served customers for over 45 years.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K reporting a February 28, 2019 blog post announcing availability of the $35,000 standard Model 3 with 220 miles of range, 130 mph top speed, and 0–60 mph in 5.6 seconds. Tesla also introduced the $37,000 Model 3 Standard Range Plus with 240 miles of range, 140 mph top speed, 0–60 mph in 5.3 seconds, and most premium interior features. To support lower prices, Tesla said it would shift worldwide sales to online only, reduce vehicle prices by about 6% on average, wind down many stores while keeping some as galleries and information centers, and offer a 7-day or 1,000-mile return policy. Tesla also announced increased investment in service, firmware upgrades for Model 3 range, speed, and power, and stated it did not expect profitability in Q1 2019 but expected Q2 profitability was likely.

The passage describes NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture features for HPC, AI, and data center workloads. Mixed-precision Tensor Cores accelerate iterative refinement solvers through cuSOLVER’s TCAIRS, with TF32 providing the most robust results among tested Tensor Core modes and a 2.0x geomean speedup over FP64 on 37 SuiteSparse tests.

A100 introduces fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity, enabling compressed weights, reduced bandwidth, and doubled Tensor Core throughput for supported sparse matrix operations. The architecture also improves memory and compute systems with 40 GB HBM2 at 1555 GB/s, a 40 MB L2 cache, 192 KB/SM combined L1/shared memory, SECDED ECC protection, compute data compression, and simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution.

A100’s third-generation Tensor Cores improve deep learning performance through expanded data sharing, fewer instructions and register accesses, asynchronous global-to-shared memory copy, asynchronous barriers, larger shared memory allocation, L2 cache residency controls, and CUDA 11 support for Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, and other features.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can partition one A100 into up to seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory bandwidth, and fault isolation for multi-tenant and multi-user workloads. The passage also covers Compute Instances, migration of vGPUs, and continued support for MPS.

A100 includes third-generation NVLink with 600 GB/s total bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4 with SR-IOV, improved error handling, hardware JPEG decode, an optical flow accelerator, faster atomics, and five NVDEC units. DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs, NVSwitch, NVLink, Mellanox HDR InfiniBand, and NVIDIA software to support scalable AI, HPC, analytics, training, and inference workloads.
Judgment was reversed and a new trial granted because no decision supported it, and the plaintiff’s proof for an accounting was unduly restricted.

Researchers created tiny resealable synthetic packets that release contents when exposed to specific light wavelengths. The nanometer-scale packets use two linked polymers: a water-soluble outer layer and a rigid glassy inner layer that softens under light, allowing release, then reseals when light is removed. Potential uses include targeted medicine delivery, fertilizer release, and soil cleanup chemicals. The materials are biocompatible and already used in medical or consumer products. Researchers are also exploring molecules that respond to triggers such as pressure or chemical cues. The study appears in Nature Chemistry and was funded by the US Army Research Office.

The S&P 500 traded near record highs around 6,715, with valuations above pre-2000 levels raising bubble concerns. Tech weakness, Fed policy, and government shutdown headlines added caution, while the index held above 6,620 support. T-Tamer is a theoretical framework for managing bi-objective trade-offs in cascaded inference, such as accuracy–latency or accuracy–cost. It models routing and stopping across sub-models as a costly exploration problem over directed acyclic graphs, where nodes represent sub-models and edges encode precedence, costs, and dependencies. The framework uses a weighted loss formulation controlled by a parameter λ and learns model-agnostic routing and termination policies from sub-model outputs.

The work shows that no-recall strategies, including confidence-threshold early-exit methods, cannot achieve any constant-factor approximation to the offline optimum, even in a two-node bounded setting. For with-recall strategies, it develops a dynamic indexing policy that is online optimal for directed lines and extends this policy to directed trees and transitive closures of directed lines with polynomial preprocessing and O(n) inference time per input.

Experiments on vision and NLP early-exit workloads using VGG, BERT-base, and GPT-2 show favorable accuracy–latency trade-offs, including substantial latency reductions with limited accuracy degradation.

The passage describes an intervention research project in Palghar district, Maharashtra, to develop sustainable local master trainers for maternal and newborn health in-service training using a Training of Trainers model. The project scaled up a prior Pune pilot and used eight Pune core trainers to support 32 Palghar master trainers selected through screening and assessment.

A six-step approach was implemented: pre-TOT screening, training with pre- and post-assessment, staggered induction of trainers, continuous support from Pune core trainers, virtual quality assessment by UK experts, and virtual refresher training. The training used adult-learner-centric, simulation-based, and case-based methods.

Palghar master trainers trained 505 health providers over 18 months. Among 463 providers with complete assessment data, post-training scores improved significantly in clinical knowledge, abdominal palpation, newborn resuscitation, and eclampsia management. Qualitative findings indicated that Palghar trainers reported increased clinical competency, confidence as trainers, application of protocols, recognition from colleagues and seniors, and motivation for continued training roles.

The study concludes that a structured, supported, and hybrid TOT approach can build local training capacity within the public health system, though long-term evaluation of retention, application in care, and costing is needed.

At a February 13, 2017 town hall in Charlestown, Nevis, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Aviation Mark Brantley said the Team Unity Government created unprecedented cooperation between the Federal Government and the Nevis Island Administration. He reviewed the coalition’s launch in 2013, its 2015 election victory, and Dr. Timothy Harris’ swearing-in as Prime Minister. Brantley argued that Team Unity had delivered a “fair share” for Nevis, citing $62.2 million from the SIDF for projects including a pier, sporting facilities, geothermal work, an athletic track, airport upgrades, hospital funding, port equipment, a generator, Treasury rebuilding, and water projects. He also said Nevis received $51.16 million in federal budgetary support in less than two years, compared with $17.3 million from 2006 to 2015, totaling $113.36 million under Team Unity.

The passage describes an older Russian hockey player as hardworking, intelligent, helpful, and elite, noting his role in a famous line, strong performances internationally, and influence on a generation of Russian players.

H. White, and Kate and Anna. The Cape Horn Pigeon, an American whaling bark from New Bedford, was seized in the Sea of Okhotsk on September 10, 1892, taken to Vladivostok, detained until the end of the whaling season, and released without trial.

Investing.com’s passage discusses technical outlooks for USD/JPY, GBP/USD, and BTC/USD amid weak US jobs data, Fed uncertainty, UK economic pressure, and market caution. USD/JPY fell 2.25% after an NFP miss, with key support and resistance levels noted. Markets expect the BoE to cut rates despite inflation above target, while GBP/USD remains pressured by weak UK data. BTC/USD declined with equities, holding near support around its 50-day SMA, with further direction tied to Fed signals and resistance levels.

Evidence for dark matter comes from galaxy clusters, rotation curves, the CMB, x-ray cluster gas, cosmic shear, and gravitational lensing. Cold dark matter explains many large-scale observations but faces unresolved simulation-related issues such as the core-cusp, missing satellites, too many satellites, and too-big-to-fail problems. Particle physics searches have not detected WIMPs, motivating consideration of alternatives including axion-like particles, primordial black holes, warm dark matter, self-interacting dark matter, and modified gravity.

The passage reviews efforts to improve coordination, reproducibility, and open science in dark matter research. It highlights European initiatives such as EuCAPT, iDMEu, EOSC, OSCARS, ESCAPE, and the Dark Matter Data Centre. ESCAPE’s Dark Matter Test Science Project (TSP) uses EOSC services to provide FAIR access to software, data, workflows, and analysis tools across particle, astroparticle, and astronomy communities.

The Dark Matter TSP currently focuses mainly on particle and astroparticle experiments, including ATLAS collider searches, DarkSide direct detection, and indirect detection with Fermi LAT, KM3NeT, and CTA. It supports workflows for producing dark matter summary plots, reinterpreting collider results, generating exclusion curves, analysing gamma-ray and neutrino signals, and using shared tools such as the VRE, OSSR, ESCAPE Data Lake, and the Baler data-compression prototype.

The passage also describes astrophysical constraints that could be incorporated into the TSP. Gravitational lensing can probe dark matter substructure, warm dark matter particle masses, and self-interacting dark matter cross-sections. Dwarf spheroidal galaxies are promising indirect-detection targets because of their high dark matter content and low astrophysical gamma-ray backgrounds, though uncertainties in their dark matter density distributions affect inferred constraints.

Several software tools are identified as relevant for connecting astrophysical and particle-physics constraints, including pyHalo for lensing substructure simulations, GAMBIT for global fits of beyond-Standard-Model theories, AxionLimits for ultralight boson summary plots, and the Dark Matter Limit Plotter for comparing experimental limits.

The review aims to introduce astronomers to the ESCAPE Dark Matter TSP and encourage integration of astronomical dark matter searches into its services, enabling open, reproducible, and collaborative comparison of complementary constraints from astronomy and particle physics.

The speaker said their team lost by one goal after Buffalo capitalized on more scoring chances. They felt nervous early but settled down, played well, pressured late, and had chances to tie, though the puck did not go in.

The Delhi High Court sought responses from the Centre and Jammu and Kashmir on whether J&K High Court judges take an oath owing allegiance to the Constitution of India. The issue arose in a PIL challenging the Constitution Order 1954, which requires Presidential orders under Article 370 for constitutional amendments to apply to J&K. The petitioner argues the order unlawfully encroaches on Parliament’s amending powers under Article 368.

Hundreds of progressive advocates protested Wells Fargo’s annual shareholders meeting in Des Moines, calling for the bank’s CEO and board to resign over alleged abusive, discriminatory, and harmful business practices. Organized by People’s Action, activists criticized the bank’s ties to private prisons, guns, foreclosures, Indigenous land projects, and fossil fuels. The protest followed a $1 billion CFPB fine for mortgage practices. Advocates also cited Wells Fargo’s multibillion-dollar investments in extreme fossil fuel projects.

Knee injuries can be debilitating, especially as wear and tear increases with age, but healthy habits may reduce risk. Maintaining a healthy weight, staying active, strengthening muscles around the knees, improving flexibility, and doing low-impact cardio such as cycling or swimming can support knee health. Physiotherapy can help diagnose knee problems, improve strength and range of motion, support recovery, and may delay or avoid surgery. If surgery is needed, it can improve quality of life but carries risks, and physiotherapy after surgery can aid recovery and protect the knee.

The Government has launched a six-week consultation on proposals to update Package Travel Regulations, aiming to protect up to 10 million UK online package holidays. The changes would ensure online bookers receive clearer refund rights and protection if travel firms fail, with package providers responsible for the whole holiday. Consumer groups support closing gaps in protection.

The passage describes an absorbent core for hygiene articles such as diapers, incontinence products, sanitary napkins, and panty liners. The core includes front, back, and crotch portions and one or more substantially interconnected channels extending through at least part of the crotch portion along the core length and across its width. The channels may form U-shaped, funnel-shaped, semi-hourglass, V-shaped, or pie-shaped profiles and are designed to distribute fluid faster than surrounding absorbent structures, improving liquid distribution, reducing localized saturation, and maintaining visible channel patterns before and after use.

The core may include nonwoven webs, three-dimensional absorbent material, and superabsorbent polymer, with the channels preferably substantially free of absorbent material. Channel bonding may use adhesive zones of different strength so parts can separate upon wetting while other parts maintain channel integrity. The disclosure also describes combining the core with an acquisition and distribution layer, where positioning the layer so certain channel extremities remain uncovered may improve fluid inflow and outflow.

A manufacturing process is disclosed using a mold with a 3D insert shaped as the inverse of the desired channels. A vacuum draws absorbent material around the insert while nonwoven webs and absorbent material are layered and optionally bonded, forming channels substantially free of three-dimensional absorbent material.

Japan’s GDP grew at an annualised 4 percent in the second quarter, exceeding economists’ expectations, with the economy expanding for 18 months. The data can be volatile and revised, and markets showed little reaction. The growth suggests greater resilience under Shinzo Abe’s reforms, helped by global conditions and Bank of Japan policies. Household consumption rose 3.7 percent, supported by durable goods purchases, lower unemployment and higher base pay. However, wage growth and inflation remain weak, and the BOJ has delayed its 2 percent inflation target again.

The passage describes ADS8681W/ADS8685W/ADS8689W interface, operating modes, programming, registers, application guidance, power, layout, and support information. A single device can use a standard SPI interface with CONVST/CS, SCLK, SDI, and SDO-0; RST is tied to DVDD, RVS can be monitored for timing, and ALARM/SDO-1/GPO should not have an external connection in the minimum configuration.

Multiple devices can be connected in a daisy-chain topology with shared CONVST/CS and SCLK. Device outputs and inputs are chained through SDO-0 and SDI, and the host receives data from device N through device 1 in MSB-first order. Configuration registers should be programmed identically, SDO_CTL_REG bits 7-0 should be 00h, and an optimal frame uses 32 × N SCLK capture edges. System throughput decreases proportionally with the number of daisy-chained devices.

The device has RESET, ACQ, and CONV states controlled by RST and CONVST/CS. RESET is entered by pulling RST low and can be configured as application reset or power-on reset. ACQ acquires the analog input and is entered after power-up, reset, or conversion completion. CONV begins on a rising CONVST/CS edge and ignores further CONVST/CS transitions until conversion completes. RVS can be monitored or the host can wait for the maximum conversion time.

Programming uses nine configuration registers and supports data write and data read operations. A data transfer frame begins on the falling edge of CONVST/CS and ends on the next rising edge. A 32-clock frame is optimal; shorter frames invalidate writes but can read MSB output bits, while longer frames use the last 32 input bits as the command. Commands include register read, half-word read, byte or half-word write, set, clear, and NOP. Output data may contain conversion results, register data, fixed patterns, and optional flags such as device address, range, AVDD alarm, input alarm, and parity.

The multiSPI interface supports legacy SPI-compatible protocols for configuration and readback, single or dual SDO outputs, and source-synchronous read protocols using RVS as an output clock. The default after power-up or reset is SPI-00-S. Dual SDO mode uses SDO-0 and SDO-1 and requires half as many clock cycles to output the same data.

The register map includes DEVICE_ID_REG, RST_PWRCTL_REG, SDI_CTL_REG, SDO_CTL_REG, DATAOUT_CTL_REG, RANGE_SEL_REG, ALARM_REG, ALARM_H_TH_REG, and ALARM_L_TH_REG. These registers configure identification, reset and power modes, input and output protocols, output data format, input ranges and reference, alarm flags, thresholds, and hysteresis.

The application section describes the ADS868xW as a fully integrated, fully differential input, 16-bit SAR ADC data acquisition device with integrated analog front end, precision reference, and buffer. An example industrial analog input module combines ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 multiplexer to measure standard voltage and current inputs. The device supports alarms for input and AVDD conditions, including programmable input thresholds and hysteresis.

Power guidance covers separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, decoupling recommendations, NAP mode, and power-down mode. Layout guidance recommends separating analog and digital sections, placing bypass capacitors close to pins, grounding with low-impedance paths, and decoupling REFCAP and REFIO. The passage also lists related TI documentation, documentation update notifications, support resources, trademarks, ESD caution, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and ordering disclaimers.

The author argues that U.S. immigration debates are dominated by flawed proposals and dishonesty across the political spectrum. Sector trading involves buying and selling securities within specific economic sectors and may carry more risk than broad market investing. The 22nd District Agricultural Association board unanimously rejected two construction bids and will re-evaluate plans to remodel Surfside Race Place at the Del Mar Fairgrounds into a multipurpose entertainment venue after costs exceeded expectations, leaving a $4 million funding gap. AMD Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) enables runtime updates to AMD firmware. The AMD Security Processor (ASP) verifies AMD signatures before applying SFS packages and acts as AMD’s root of trust for detection. OEM/ODM system designers remain responsible for firmware root of trust for update, and may require co-signing so SFS packages must be signed by both AMD and the customer. Customer co-signing keys are provided to the ASP during early boot and cannot be updated after that stage; key maintenance is the customer’s responsibility.

SFS is opt-in through BIOS configuration flags and is disabled by default. SFS packages are applied only at runtime, do not persist across reboot, and must be reapplied after reset. In multi-socket systems, the first socket’s ASP receives the patch and the package determines how to apply it locally and to other sockets. Multiple updates must be applied sequentially.

Each patch checks existing system patch level and firmware versions before applying. Packages may patch registers or values, replace complete firmware images, or update portions of firmware. SEV updates are automatically committed to prevent rollback, and reverting an SFS-updated SEV firmware image requires reboot. SNP-enabled systems require update package pages to be HV-FIXED.

Applying SFS commands requires specific memory alignment and use of a customer-provided deployment agent. The ASP checks memory protection, verifies customer and AMD signatures as required, loads and runs the patch, updates patch level information, and returns status. SFS also provides commands to retrieve firmware and patch version information.

SFS packages are binary objects maintained by customers and aligned to AGESA releases, with names such as `fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg`. Packages apply only to specific firmware and patch-level combinations. Updates run in parallel with x86 and DMA traffic and are designed to minimize performance impact; some operations, such as SEV firmware updates, may require SEV or SEV/ES virtual machines to stop and restart, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating.

The Trump administration faces a Friday, Dec. 15 deadline for ACA enrollment through HealthCare.gov in 39 states, with heavy last-minute traffic expected after the sign-up period was shortened to 45 days. Analysts warn the website and call center could face volume problems. Most consumers must enroll or change plans by the deadline, though hurricane-affected residents may request an extension to Dec. 31. The passage introduces the empirical Stochastic Inverse Problem (eSIP), which seeks a probability distribution over unobserved physical parameters using observed quantities of interest produced by a model. Because the observation map is generally not one-to-one, multiple parameter values can yield the same data, requiring conditional probability and disintegration of measures.

The paper defines an abstract Stochastic Inverse Problem (SIP) and develops a Bayesian solution conditioned on a prior distribution. Under general assumptions, it proves existence and uniqueness of a posterior solution with an explicit density formula, establishes almost-everywhere continuity of the posterior density, and shows that the solution using a uniform prior has maximum entropy. For the empirical setting, it proposes a numerical estimator based on importance sampling that is asymptotically unbiased and strongly consistent, with variance and error estimates.

Examples illustrate the framework using an exponential decay model and a discrete inverse problem. The solution is a posterior probability distribution over parameter space, useful for estimating event probabilities, excluding low-probability parameter regions, and forecasting distributions of new quantities of interest. The passage also distinguishes eSIP from noisy-data inverse problems, Bayesian computer model calibration, and data assimilation methods, and outlines the paper’s sections on theory, numerical methods, examples, and proofs.

Colorado State defeated Wyoming 78-73 in Laramie in the 226th Border War, taking sole possession of first place in the Mountain West after Boise State lost to New Mexico.
