The passage describes AMD AGESA published entry functions, required host environment call-outs, initialization phases, resume/suspend handling, and platform customization controls. It warns that only published entry functions are stable and that enabling instruction cache outside the specified interface can cause data corruption.

AGESA routines cover reset, early initialization, memory initialization, environment setup, display configuration, late boot table generation, ready-to-boot suspend preparation, and S3 resume restoration. These routines require a stack, often require host-managed buffers, and distinguish responsibilities between BSP and AP cores. Reset and early initialization configure processor basics, cache regions, HyperTransport links, power management, PCIe/GNB, FCH, and platform settings. Memory initialization brings DRAM online, handles memory training and features such as ECC, interleaving, UMA, AMP, refresh control, and memory restore. Later stages move artifact data, configure graphics/display hardware, generate ACPI/DMI/WHEA/CRAT/CDIT/IVRS tables, and prepare the system for OS boot.

The host environment must implement required call-outs for allocating, locating, and freeing buffers; initiating cold or warm resets; reading SPD data; and dispatching functions to APs. Optional call-outs support IDS non-volatile data, heap rebasing, memory timing and voltage hooks, self-refresh handling, video BIOS repost, FCH customization, MBIST voltage adjustment, and platform-specific device controls.

The passage also defines many build options and configuration elements supplied through `<plat>Options.c`. These can remove unused support code, such as DIMM types, ECC, interleaving, ACPI tables, WHEA, DMI, processor families, socket types, Connected Standby, or S3 support. Configuration elements describe platform limits and features such as VRM capabilities, CPU frequency limits, PCI MMIO settings, IO APIC count, ACPI table fields, P-State and C-State behavior, Connected Standby, Core Performance Boost, Hybrid Boost, and core leveling.

The article examines reducing energy consumption in HF-band RFID/NFC systems by dynamically scaling the reader’s magnetic field strength. NFC in mobile devices increases battery drain because the reader often transmits at maximum power regardless of distance or transponder requirements, causing oversupply. Measurements show a smartphone consumes 50% more power with NFC active and no transponder in range, and up to 107% more while reading a transponder.

The authors identify three areas for magnetic field strength scaling: during card detection, during communication as distance and operations change, and in systems with multiple transponders. The main detailed method, called the PTF-Determinator, determines the power transfer function between reader and transponder during card detection. It gathers reader and transponder parameters, approximates the physical relation factor using field-strength steps and transponder responses, integrates this into the RFID communication flow, and exposes the result through a reader-side library for power management.

A case study applies the method to reading digital business cards and includes a maximum transmission distance feature that cuts off power transfer beyond a defined limit. Simulation with improved hardware shows up to 80% less transmission energy at close range and about 93% savings when the maximum distance is exceeded. Measurements on existing hardware show 26% lower transmission energy when within range and 75% lower when power is cut off beyond the maximum distance. Combined with smartphone measurements, the authors estimate up to 13% less battery drain for normal use and 39% less when avoiding out-of-range transactions. Future work will improve approximation of the physical relation factor and evaluate dynamic scaling during communication and with multiple transponders.

The 4-2-5 defense combines elements of the 4-3 and 3-3-5, using four down linemen, two linebackers, and five defensive backs. It aims to keep six defenders in the box while remaining sound against the pass, relying on pressure and athletic personnel. A key position is the Sam/Rover, a hybrid safety-linebacker who must cover, blitz, and handle run responsibilities.

Its strengths include versatility against spread formations, multiple coverage options, and strong blitz potential. Weaknesses include being unbalanced, especially away from the Sam, and sometimes struggling against bigger offensive lines and backs. Offenses often attack the weak side with runs such as outside zone or buck sweep.

Common blitzes include six-man Cover 0 pressures, sometimes expanding to seven rushers. Common coverages include Cover 4 and Cover 3 Sky from a two-high shell. Gary Patterson at TCU is highlighted as a prominent 4-2-5 coach, with Greg Etter also noted for using it successfully at smaller college programs.

Sleep problems are common and are associated with poorer mood, quality of life, productivity, cognitive functioning, chronic disease risk, and health disparities, particularly among older adults, minoritized groups, low-income populations, and people with low health literacy. This study evaluated a mobile app module providing tailored sleep psychoeducation to adults aged 40 and older with chronic health conditions and low health literacy.

The app was developed using existing chronic disease self-management resources, qualitative input from older adults, and guidance from a multidisciplinary team. Content was offered at different reading levels and included text, images, diagrams, narrated animations, self-check questions, and tailored information. The sleep module assessed insomnia symptoms and provided information on sleep stages, depression and stress effects, chronic conditions, sleep hygiene, sleep logs, and sleep restriction.

Participants were recruited in Fort Lauderdale and Atlanta. Eligibility included being at least 40 years old, having a chronic health condition under treatment, less than a college education, and low health literacy. Assessments occurred at baseline, post-intervention, and three-month follow-up. Analyses examined socioeconomic status, health literacy, health conditions, intervention effects, and treatment group.

Of 286 participants completing baseline assessments and the sleep module, 195 had insomnia scores meeting the study criterion and were analyzed. Most identified as BIPOC, and most reported annual income below $10,000. Sleep disturbance was related to hypercholesterolemia, depression, another nervous condition, and bipolar disorder, while associations with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and angina approached statistical significance.

Mixed-effects models showed that socioeconomic status, health literacy, and total health conditions were significantly associated with sleep quality over time. Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores decreased significantly during the study, with a small-to-medium intervention effect. The authors note that the brief, tailored, online intervention may be useful as an initial step in a stepped-care approach, though effects were modest. Limitations included the broader chronic disease focus of the intervention, possible influence of other app modules, reliance on self-reported sleep, limited generalizability, and the likelihood that more intensive interventions could produce larger improvements.

The lecture discusses pleat folding in origami, focusing on alternating mountain and valley folds that create 3D forms. A central example is the “hyperbolic paraboloid,” made from concentric square creases and diagonals, which appears to self-fold into a saddle-like shape. Similar pleated forms can be made with concentric circles, though their exact geometry is uncertain.

The professor explains paper’s elastic and plastic behavior: uncreased paper tends to flatten, while creased paper retains a bend. Simulations using spring-like force models reproduced physical pleated models, enabling “origami skeleton” sculptures made from 3D-printed joints and rods. Other sculptural applications include joining multiple hyperbolic paraboloids into “hyperhedra,” curved-crease sculptures, and glassblown forms containing folded paper-like structures.

The lecture then presents a key mathematical result: the standard concentric-square hyperbolic paraboloid crease pattern cannot properly fold into a non-flat 3D shape if its faces remain untriangulated. Real folded models likely involve additional hidden creases or bending. By adding diagonal triangulations to the trapezoidal faces, proper 3D foldings can be constructed and verified computationally using sphere intersections and interval arithmetic. Different triangulations behave differently, and the resulting shape closely but not exactly matches a true hyperbolic paraboloid.

The professor introduces differential-geometry tools to explain how paper folds between creases. Folded paper remains intrinsically flat, with zero Gaussian curvature, so smooth regions are ruled surfaces. Straight creases in a proper folding remain straight, and polygonal crease boundaries force interior faces to stay planar. These facts show why untriangulated concentric-square and similar pleated polygon patterns cannot properly fold.

The lecture briefly discusses open problems such as maximizing the volume of inflated shapes like pillows, tea bags, and Mylar balloons. It ends with curved-crease origami, especially David Huffman’s work, including efforts to reconstruct and analyze his models using computational diagrams and fabrication tools.

Micro E-mini futures are CME Group contracts launched in 2019 that are one-tenth the size of E-mini futures and trade on the CME Globex platform. They were created to make futures trading more accessible to retail traders with smaller capital, lower margin requirements, and greater flexibility for risk management. Initially offered for major indexes such as the S&P 500, Dow, Nasdaq 100, and Russell 2000, they now cover assets including bitcoin, copper, crude oil, Treasury yields, and FX futures.

A Micro E-mini futures strategy is a method for trading these contracts using entry and exit signals, position sizing, and risk management, often for speculation, diversification, or hedging. The passage recommends backtesting trading ideas and provides an example using the Nasdaq 100 E-mini contract due to Micro E-mini’s shorter history.

Micro E-mini contracts are generally financially settled, with cash settlement based on special opening quotes of the underlying asset. Trading specifications, tick size, seasonality, price drivers, and contract terms depend on the underlying asset. For Micro E-mini S&P 500 futures, one contract equals $5 times the index value, has a minimum fluctuation of 0.25 index points for outright trading, and trades Sunday to Friday with daily breaks.

The biggest risk is adverse price movement, especially with leverage, since losses are based on the full contract value rather than deposited margin. CFDs may track Micro E-mini futures, but unlike futures, CFDs do not have fixed expiration dates.

Napheesa Collier criticized WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert and league leadership, calling them negligent and accusing them of failing to address officiating, player compensation and product concerns. Collier alleged Engelbert dismissed officiating complaints, said young stars should be grateful for the WNBA’s platform, and suggested players should thank her for the media rights deal. Engelbert responded that she respects Collier but was disheartened by her characterization. Collier’s remarks come amid collective bargaining tensions, concerns about possible 2026 work stoppage, and scrutiny of her roles with the WNBPA and Unrivaled.

Stochastic Texture Filtering introduces randomness into texture sampling to reduce aliasing and moiré when traditional filtering is impractical, and can provide higher-order filtering with a single point sample, running faster on Blackwell GPUs due to improved point-sampled filtering rates.

Neural Radiance Cache uses a neural shader to cache and approximate radiance, training tiny networks on live game data to infer multi-bounce indirect lighting from rays traced after one bounce. This improves performance, indirect lighting quality, adaptability, and scalability.

RTX Skin brings subsurface scattering into real-time path tracing for translucent materials, improving skin and similar materials by modeling light penetration, scattering, and emission. RTX Neural Faces uses a real-time generative AI model, trained from offline images, to infer more natural faces from rasterized face and 3D pose inputs.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell GPU architecture targets multiple graphics segments. GB202 is the flagship GPU with 92.2 billion transistors, 12 GPCs, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores, and a 512-bit memory interface; it powers the GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 targets the high-end segment with 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, and a 256-bit interface; it powers the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 targets the performance segment with 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, and a 192-bit interface; it powers the RTX 5070.

The passage also states NVIDIA’s specifications are provided without warranties, may change, and products are subject to NVIDIA terms, usage restrictions, and intellectual property notices.

British expatriate Daniel Jones, 31, received a one-year suspended prison sentence in Cambodia for using “pornographic” photos to promote a Siem Reap pool party. He denied sex or nudity occurred and apologized, but prosecutors said images encouraging sexual activity violated Cambodian culture and decency laws. Jones had already served nearly two months on remand, with the remainder suspended. His lawyer may appeal. Cambodia has previously enforced strict rules protecting local traditions, especially around Angkor Wat.

Kay Frazier, 50, from Wigan, died after developing a large blood clot blocking blood to her brain. An inquest heard she underwent a risky thrombectomy at Salford Royal Hospital but suffered a ruptured artery during surgery and died two days later. Frazier had married jailed American killer Gary Frazier after exchanging thousands of letters and regularly visited him in Nebraska. The cause of the clot is unknown, and the coroner has not yet returned a verdict.

Retired civil litigator Marcel Strigberger recounts decluttering his home by recycling decades-old McGill law schoolbooks. He reflects humorously on memorable contract, property and maritime law cases and concepts, decides most are no longer useful, regrets one potentially valuable discard, and keeps one thick volume as a reading stand.

President Van Buren transmitted to the House further correspondence between Secretary of State Forsyth and British minister Fox regarding Alexander McLeod’s imprisonment in New York over the destruction of the steamboat Caroline. Fox regretted the President’s refusal to release McLeod, warned of serious consequences if further harm came to him, and said he had forwarded the correspondence to Her Majesty’s Government. He defended the Caroline’s destruction as necessary self-defense against a hostile vessel engaged in piratical war and protested describing the action as outrage or murder. Forsyth replied that evidence of the incident had been presented to the British Government with a demand for redress, making further discussion improper, and stated that Fox’s opinion likely rested on incomplete knowledge of the collected testimony.

The teams were closely matched with similar styles, leading to an emotional game. One speaker said their team corrected errors and improved effort rather than dwelling on mistakes. They emphasized staying poised, avoiding a defensive shell, creating chances, winning battles, getting pucks to the net, and building on their strong play in the final seven minutes.

The speaker says opponents were deliberately falling on him and pushing his teammates into him, which he considers dangerous, and believes referees should penalize it. He does not want retaliation but thinks his teammates should be more aggressive in front of Eddie while still playing smart. He expects similar tactics in upcoming games and plans to keep aggressively playing the puck, especially at home in Buffalo, where he feels more comfortable. He notes differences in ice and board bounces between Buffalo and Dallas that affect puck handling. He says he felt tired after the game but has no problems, and his groin is okay.

An international team from Leiden, Tsinghua, and Zhejiang universities used Bell’s test to verify quantum behavior in large systems. They tested Bell correlations in up to 73 superconducting qubits by measuring low-energy states beyond classical limits, with a 48-standard-deviation result. They also certified genuine multipartite Bell correlations up to 24 qubits. The findings show large quantum computers can display verifiable quantum behavior and may support advances in communication, cryptography, and quantum algorithms.

The speaker assumes the presidency amid business depression, industrial disturbance, unemployment, and financial strain. He calls for revision of the financial system, preservation of government credit, currency stability, and possible creation of a commission to review coinage, banking, and currency laws. He supports pursuing international bimetallism while maintaining silver at parity with gold.

He urges strict economy in government spending, adequate revenue, avoidance of debt in peacetime, and renewed protective tariff legislation to stop deficits, strengthen credit, support American labor and industry, and revive business. He also advocates reciprocity to expand foreign markets for American agricultural and manufactured products.

The address emphasizes relief for farmers, laborers, miners, and manufacturers through renewed industry and prudent legislation. It calls for preservation of constitutional rights, public order, lawful justice, opposition to lynching, enforcement of laws against trusts and oppressive trade practices, improved naturalization and immigration laws, expanded education, continued civil service reform, and restoration of the American merchant marine.

In foreign policy, the speaker supports peace, non-interference, avoidance of territorial aggression, protection of American rights, and arbitration, urging Senate action on an arbitration treaty with Great Britain. Because of the Treasury’s condition and need for revenue legislation, he announces that Congress will be convened in extraordinary session on March 15, 1897.

He concludes by praising national unity after the election, especially the diminishing of sectional divisions, and pledges to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution while seeking the support of the people.

The passage describes advanced attacking runs in soccer as movements designed to create opportunities several passes or significant time ahead. It categorizes them as individual, planned, and supporting runs. Individual runs include blind-side runs, drawing defenders out, inverted runs, overlaps or underlaps, third-man runs, late runs, and deep-lying runs. Planned runs include designed set-play routes, runs to receive specific passes such as crosses, and fast breaks following turnovers. Key considerations include avoiding offside, timing runs properly, showing patience, and remaining unpredictable. Supporting runs help maintain possession through back-pass options, square-pass options, and switching fields. Effective attacking runs require completed passes, full team participation despite only one runner receiving the ball, and scouting of defenders’ strengths, weaknesses, and tendencies.

Honor launched the Honor 9i in India on October 5, marking its third anniversary in the country. The phone is a rebranded Huawei Maimang 6/Nova 2i and features a 5.99-inch FullView full HD+ display, metal unibody design, and four cameras: 13MP+2MP front and 16MP+2MP rear, both supporting portrait mode. It runs on a Kirin 659 octa-core processor with Android Nougat-based EMUI, 4GB RAM, 64GB storage, and a 3,340mAh battery. Initial impressions noted good design, fast app and camera response, and promising camera performance under indoor lighting. It is priced at Rs. 17,999.

A research paper in Climate Change argues that the Eldgjá eruption, dated to spring 939 CE through at least autumn 940 CE, may have helped encourage Iceland’s conversion to Christianity. Researchers cite the 10th-century Völuspá, which describes volcanic and meteorological imagery and the doom of Norse gods, suggesting it drew on memories of the eruption to promote Christianisation. The eruption caused major lava flooding, ash-darkened skies, falling temperatures, and agricultural difficulties for Iceland’s early settlers. The paper links these events to Iceland’s gradual conversion in the latter half of the 10th century, officially dated to 999/1000 CE, and notes that later traditions such as Kristni saga also associated conversion debates with volcanic events.

Student mistreatment remains common in medical education and is associated with anxiety, depression, post-traumatic stress, hostility, burnout, reduced empathy, and career regret. Although 38.12% of graduating medical students reported mistreatment in the 2023 AAMC Graduation Questionnaire, only 26.9% of those students reported it, citing low perceived importance, belief that nothing would be done, and fear of reprisal.

This single-site qualitative study at a large urban academic institution in the southern United States used peer-to-peer semi-structured interviews with 21 medical students who had experienced mistreatment. Participants described 34 incidents, 12 of which were reported and 22 were not. Analysis identified four groups of factors influencing reporting decisions: personal, situational, structural, and climate.

Personal factors included fear of repercussions, concern about grades or career advancement, lack of personal motivation, and a sense of justice or duty to protect future students. Situational factors included the perceived severity and type of mistreatment, uncertainty about whether an incident qualified as mistreatment, input from confidants, bystander inaction, and perceptions of the perpetrator. Structural factors included uncertainty about reporting processes, lack of feedback, prior poor reporting experiences, and belief that no meaningful action would result. Climate factors centered on the perceived hierarchy and culture of medicine, in which mistreatment was often viewed as expected and reporting as powerless or futile.

The study concludes that few factors motivate students to report mistreatment. A sense of justice and support from confidants may promote reporting, while fear of retaliation, unclear systems, bystander inaction, and institutional culture discourage it. The authors recommend improving reporting systems, increasing transparency, protecting against retaliation, training bystanders, and addressing institutional culture to support safer learning environments.

The passage argues that remaining coal lands should remain publicly owned, withdrawn from sale or entry except in special cases, and worked by private individuals under a royalty system with government oversight of prices and carrier rates. It compares this policy to forest land withdrawal and says coal should benefit the public as a whole.

It also states that Congress has advanced national supervision of interstate corporations through railway rate, pure food, and beef-packing measures. The author suggests waiting to assess these laws but favors labeling dates and charging inspection costs to packers. The interstate commerce law is described as already producing reduced freight and fare tariffs while railroads increased earnings.

The passage calls for further expansion of national control over interstate corporations, including stronger Interstate Commerce Commission powers, prevention of excessive overcapitalization, and disclosure of corporate ownership and business structures. It argues that adequate regulation can prevent abuses, reduce calls for government ownership or socialism, and preserve individual initiative while limiting harmful unregulated competition.

Haas Alumni’s 10/19/00 weekly jobs email lists openings submitted by employers seeking Haas alumni candidates and invites companies to submit postings. Opportunities include roles at Kaiser Permanente, University of Michigan, United Nations Foundation, Micron Technology, Informatica, PG&E Corporation, Blue Shield of California, ePocrates, an online comparison shopping service, iVenturi, Extensity, Fremont Group, and Research Dog. Positions span business analysis, finance, development, communications, corporate development, product marketing, risk/accounting, health data reporting, business development, strategy, telesales, economics research, and market research/business intelligence. The email provides expanded descriptions, qualifications, contacts, and application instructions, plus alumni notes, event/survey links, subscription instructions, and a notice that listed companies and search firms have not been researched by Haas.

Delta reported record adjusted revenue of $15.2 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.71, beating forecasts, driven by premium and corporate travel demand. Premium revenue rose 9% to nearly $5.8 billion, while main cabin sales fell 4% to about $6 billion. Delta now expects premium seat sales to overtake main cabin in 2026, earlier than previously expected. CEO Ed Bastian projected full-year adjusted EPS of about $6. Shares rose as much as 6% after the results. Executives cited wealthier travelers, strategic route management, investments in coastal markets, and premium airport experiences as drivers of future growth.

Energy Central Daily News for Jan. 24, 2002 highlighted electric power and gas industry stories, with major focus on Enron-related investigations, Arthur Andersen subpoenas, document destruction concerns, bankruptcy issues, political fallout, creditor actions, and market impacts. Other topics included Long Island opening its power market to competition, Florida Power rate pressure, NRC nuclear waste site standards, BG acquiring Enron India fields, utility rates, power projects, renewables, international energy market developments, and company financial results.

The speaker says Darren protected Nick respectfully, discusses how enthusiastic fans can make places like Hartford, Dallas, and potentially the current city strong hockey towns, and emphasizes the importance of a physical, defensive line that can also score.

Michelle Bishop’s article presents research from D’harawal Country in south-west Sydney on what education grounded in Indigenous knowledges could look and feel like. The study responds to harms caused by colonial schooling systems for many Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students and prioritises Indigenous education sovereignty rather than school reform.

Bishop positions herself as a Gamilaroi woman raised on D’harawal Country and describes using Indigenous, decolonising and relational methodologies, including Indigenous futurities, envisioning, yarning and storying. The research involved 35 anonymous survey respondents and face-to-face yarns with more than 15 Indigenous participants connected to an Aboriginal community on D’harawal Country. Participant anonymity was protected through refusal to disclose some details and through an amalgamated story format.

The article argues that envisioning creates space to imagine education beyond colonial systems, informed by ancestors, Country, community and future generations. “Layering the vision” is used to represent multiple participant perspectives as part of a collective community vision. Story is used to present findings in an accessible, relational and culturally grounded way.

The story “Our Education, Our Way” depicts community members discussing an education system controlled and directed by Aboriginal people, centred on Country, culture, Elders, storytelling, language, identity, belonging and strong community relationships. Participants imagine education that supports literacy and numeracy without compromising Indigenous identity, and that helps future generations feel proud, connected and empowered.

Meb Faber’s S&P 500 trend-following strategy uses the 200-day moving average: buy when price crosses above it and sell when it crosses below. The approach focuses only on price, ignoring news, valuations, sentiment, and other factors. Paul Tudor Jones also cites the 200-day moving average as useful for avoiding major losses. Backtests from 1960 show the strategy helped avoid much of the 2008/09 financial crisis and reduced exposure during COVID-19 volatility. Using monthly data with a ten-month moving average, $100,000 invested in 1960 grew to $4.7 million excluding dividends, with a 6.3% CAGR versus 7% for buy and hold and a maximum drawdown of 26%. The passage concludes that while not the best indicator, the 200-day moving average is a simple tool that can reduce drawdowns while keeping returns reasonably close to long-term market performance.

The passage argues that Congress should fund stronger antitrust enforcement through the Department of Justice rather than use tariff reduction to address trusts. It says tariff changes would not effectively regulate large corporations, could harm weaker domestic competitors, and should remain separate from trust regulation. The passage supports the protective-tariff principle, economic stability, and avoiding radical changes that could disrupt business or lower American wage standards. It favors careful tariff readjustment through reciprocity treaties, direct legislation when needed, and expert investigation, potentially by a commission, to recommend schedule changes based on business conditions and national prosperity.

Printed Circuit Broker Elmatica is establishing a temporary department in South Africa after increased business, including 245 percent sales growth compared to 2016, and demand for closer technical support.

Crystal Palace came from two goals down to draw 2-2 at home with Leicester City. Robert Huth and Jamie Vardy gave Leicester a 2-0 lead, but Yohan Cabaye quickly pulled one back before Christian Benteke headed in a 70th-minute equalizer. Palace moved to 35 points from 32 games, two behind Leicester. Sam Allardyce praised Palace’s fightback, while Vardy said Leicester were disappointed before facing Atletico Madrid.

Construction crews on the $1.8 billion Las Vegas stadium project have exceeded minority hiring and subcontracting goals. Mortenson Construction reported that 54 percent of work hours were completed by minorities, women and military veterans, above the 38 percent goal, and 18 percent of subcontracts went to qualified small-business enterprises, surpassing the 15 percent goal. The project remains on schedule for summer 2020 completion.

The passage describes AGESA binary image and UEFI integration requirements for a host environment. In the binary build model, AGESA call-outs are routed through a single call port, requiring the host to implement a call-out router that maps function numbers to host procedures and loads its address in the standard header.

AGESA UEFI execution spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases across 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit modes. The build uses platform option files, UEFI control files, environment variables such as AGESA_ROOT and AGESA_OptsDir, and toolchains including MASM, Microsoft Macro Assembler, and Microsoft C/C++ compilers. No additional UEFI-specific user options are listed.

The host environment must establish early execution support, including Cache-As-RAM and stack setup, using provided macros such as AMD_RESET_ENABLEMENT and AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK. It must not modify stack registers or cache controls during the Cache-As-RAM period. AARCH64 APUs with PSP do not use these early stack macros because PSP initializes DRAM.

The passage outlines UEFI PEIM and DXE components for processor, memory, reset coordination, late initialization, table generation, and VGA decoding control. PEIMs publish PPIs after reset, early CPU initialization, memory initialization, and post initialization. DXE drivers generate and expose AMD-related tables through protocols.

Several AGESA service procedures are described, including structure creation and release, event log reading, MMIO range updates, APIC and PCI address discovery, execution cache size retrieval, data eye result retrieval, and memory FRU identification. These generally require a stack and, in some cases, operational coherent HyperTransport links.

The AGESA initialization sequence includes AmdInitReset, AmdInitEarly, AmdInitPost, AmdInitEnv, graphics configuration, AmdInitLate, AmdInitRtb, and resume-related procedures. These initialize processors, memory, platform configuration, GNB/FCH settings, ACPI and DMI tables, S3 save state, and resume restoration. BSP and AP cores perform different tasks at several stages.

Required host call-outs include buffer allocation, buffer deallocation, and system reset. Buffer allocation must provide main-memory storage after memory initialization and may need runtime persistence depending on heap status. Reset call-outs must initiate cold or warm resets as requested.

The paper examines border-crossing in language teacher education across English as a Second Language, Bilingual Education, and World Language Education. It argues that these fields share goals related to language learning but developed separately in distinct U.S. sociopolitical contexts, shaped by settler colonialism, English-only schooling, immigration, national security priorities, and differing assumptions about learners. The authors emphasize that language education should be understood not only as a question of which language is taught, but for whom.

Using Valdés’ framework of language curricularization, the paper analyzes how theories, ideologies, policies, contexts, and program elements shape language teacher education. It highlights tensions such as monolingual native-speaker ideals, deficit views of minoritized bilingual learners, and the need to align curriculum with multilingual and equity-oriented understandings of language learning.

The authors describe curricular innovation at their Chicago institution, where ESL/Bilingual Education and World Language programs are housed separately but overlap through coursework. In Phase 1, they redesigned an ESL methods course around translanguaging, culturally and linguistically responsive pedagogy, and flexible use of multiple languages. In Phase 2, they created an ESL and World Languages methods course focused on Chinese language teaching, supporting candidates who may teach learners with varied linguistic profiles across program models. In Phase 3, still in development, they plan to redesign a Bilingual Education methods course to connect World Language and Bilingual Education through critical consciousness, linguistic autobiographies, drama-based pedagogy, and case-based curricular analysis.

The paper concludes that bridging language teacher education fields can help candidates historicize ESL, Bilingual Education, and World Language Education; critically examine language ideologies; and design instruction responsive to learners’ diverse linguistic repertoires. The authors do not propose a single unified curriculum, but advocate for collaboration, historical awareness, pedagogical flexibility, and a language equity lens across programs.

Microsoft Corporation filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2015. For the three months ended March 31, 2015, revenue was $21.7 billion, up from $20.4 billion a year earlier, while net income decreased to $5.0 billion from $5.7 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $0.61, compared with $0.68. For the nine months ended March 31, 2015, revenue was $71.4 billion, up from $63.5 billion, and net income was $15.4 billion, down from $17.5 billion.

As of March 31, 2015, Microsoft reported total assets of $176.7 billion, total liabilities of $86.6 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $90.1 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $95.4 billion. Long-term debt, including the current portion, was $30.1 billion. Net cash from operations was $22.3 billion for the nine-month period.

Microsoft reported revenue across Devices and Consumer and Commercial segments. Devices and Consumer revenue was $9.0 billion for the quarter, while Commercial revenue was $12.8 billion. Operating income was $6.6 billion for the quarter, compared with $7.0 billion a year earlier.

During the period, Microsoft continued integrating Nokia’s Devices and Services business and completed the acquisition of Mojang for $2.5 billion in cash, net of cash acquired. The company also recorded restructuring charges related to a plan to eliminate up to 18,000 positions, with actions expected to be completed by June 30, 2015.

Microsoft repurchased $9.0 billion of common stock during the nine months ended March 31, 2015, and had $26.1 billion remaining under its $40.0 billion repurchase authorization. The company declared quarterly dividends of $0.31 per share during fiscal 2015.

The filing also describes accounting policies, investments, derivatives, fair value measurements, income taxes, legal contingencies, and segment information. Deloitte & Touche LLP reviewed the interim financial statements and stated it was not aware of material modifications needed for conformity with U.S. GAAP.

The passage compares dollar-cost averaging (DCA) with lump-sum investing, focusing on sequence of return risk. DCA invests money gradually over time, while lump-sum investing deploys capital at the earliest opportunity. The article states that studies show lump-sum investing usually outperforms DCA, including Morningstar findings that DCA beat lump-sum investing 27.8% of the time over 10-month periods and 10% over 10-year periods.

The passage argues DCA can reduce fear, behavioral mistakes, and exposure to short-term volatility, but may underperform depending on market return order. Using S&P 500 data from 2000 to 2019, a $60,000 lump-sum investment grew to $193,157 with a 6.02% CAGR. A DCA strategy over the same period produced a 5.5% CAGR. When returns were reshuffled so strong returns came first and weaker returns later, lump-sum results were similar, but DCA fell to $87,396 with a 1.9% CAGR. The article concludes that lump-sum investing is generally preferable and that DCA results are strongly affected by randomness and return sequence.

The lecture introduces 6.451 as a coding-focused course in a communications context, centered on approaching capacity on the additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel. The class will be videotaped for OpenCourseWare, uses course notes rather than a textbook, and has weekly problem sets, a midterm scheduled for March 16, and a final exam. The prerequisite 6.450 is enforced mainly to ensure mathematical readiness.

The course covers major coding methods and decoding algorithms, including algebraic block codes, convolutional codes, tail-biting codes, capacity-approaching codes, low-density parity-check codes, lattice codes, and trellis-coded modulation. This year the instructor plans to omit less essential topics to spend more time on recent capacity-approaching codes and possibly codes for band-limited channels.

The main engineering problem is designing modems that transmit as much digital information as possible over given channels. Examples include deep-space links, telephone lines, and wireless channels. The AWGN model is described by output \(Y(t)=X(t)+N(t)\), signal power \(P\), noise spectral density \(N_0\), bandwidth \(W\), and signal-to-noise ratio \(P/(N_0W)\). Shannon’s capacity formula for an AWGN channel is \(C=W\log_2(1+\text{SNR})\), giving an upper limit on reliable transmission rates, though Shannon’s proof is nonconstructive.

Coding is presented as introducing constraints over long sequences to increase distance between valid transmitted sequences and reduce error probability. The course traces how practical coding methods developed over decades to approach Shannon capacity.

The lecture also reviews decibels as a logarithmic way to express multiplicative factors, previews the first homework, and explains how a continuous-time AWGN channel can be converted to a discrete-time AWGN channel using orthonormal pulse amplitude modulation and sampled matched filtering. This preserves signal-to-noise ratio and relates bandwidth \(W\) to \(2W\) real symbols per second. Spectral efficiency is defined as \(R/W\) bits per second per Hertz, or bits per two dimensions in discrete time.

Motley Fool Money reviews the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card as a no-annual-fee cash back card offering unlimited 2% cash rewards on purchases, a $200 bonus after $500 in purchases in the first 3 months, and 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a variable APR of 18.99%, 23.99%, or 28.99%. The card also includes no reward categories to track, rewards that do not expire while the account remains open, Visa Signature® Concierge access, and up to $600 in cell phone protection with a $25 deductible. Approval is most likely for applicants with good credit, typically 670 or higher. The passage also lists offers for Capital One Quicksilver and Citi Double Cash, and includes compensation and advertising disclosures.

The passage reviews nine Vanguard ETFs for diversification: VTI, VT, VXUS, VNQ, VNQI, VTC, BND, BNDX, and BNDW. It explains that Vanguard, founded by John Bogle, is associated with passive investing and low-cost long-term strategies. The article backtests individual ETFs and a diversified portfolio from 2007 to 2023 using buy-and-hold with annual rebalancing; $10,000 grew to $19,318, with returns lower than the S&P 500 partly due to bond allocations. The ETFs provide broad exposure to U.S. and global stocks, real estate, corporate bonds, U.S. bonds, international bonds, and global bonds. The passage advises investors to read each prospectus to assess fit with their goals.

Weber State University canceled its Unity Conference, themed “Redacted: Navigating the Complexities of Censorship,” after presenters were told days before the event to remove terms such as “DEI,” “diversity,” “equity” and “inclusion” from their slides. Faculty, including Sarah Herrmann, withdrew rather than censor research, and organizers canceled the event on Oct. 1.

University officials said the conference was sponsored by Student Access and Success, making it subject to Utah’s HB 261, unlike academically sponsored events, which are exempt. Vice President Jessica Oyler told presenters that non-academic programming could not include certain language about identity, power structures or legislation. Faculty said the sponsorship and restrictions were unclear.

The incident occurred amid broader pressure from Utah lawmakers on public universities, including budget cuts and scrutiny of programs such as queer studies, ethnic studies and women’s and gender studies. Weber State said it is considering placing future Unity Conferences under Academic Affairs or a college to avoid HB 261 restrictions.

Eilish McCready, 25, from Glasgow, founded Fearless theatre school after graduating from an acting and performance course. The inclusive drama classes aim to build children’s confidence, social skills and personal development without the pressure of end-of-year performances. Classes are kept small and welcome confident children, shy children and those with additional needs, including autism.

Parents say the classes have helped their children. Lizanne Conway, whose sons have autism, said Fearless has improved Rudy and Carl’s confidence, communication, social interaction and self-esteem in a safe, inclusive environment. Lisa Byrne said her shy daughter Rua has become more confident, now sings in front of people and has started a YouTube channel.

Fearless classes are held at Studio 93 in Glasgow.

The address reviews the United States’ internal and external affairs, noting continued prosperity and implementation of recent acts of Congress. Measures were adopted to maintain peace with Native nations, protect frontier settlements, uphold treaty rights, and establish trading houses and military posts, including a new treaty with the Creeks.

The United States took possession of several posts evacuated by Britain under the Jay Treaty, while commissions proceeded on the St. Croix boundary and claims related to captured vessels. Under the treaty with Spain, steps began to run the Florida boundary and occupy posts vacated by Spanish troops, though no Spanish commissioner had yet been appointed for American claims. Agents were appointed to aid American seamen, and arrangements with Algiers had led to the liberation of American prisoners, with treaties being pursued with Tunis and Tripoli.

The address argues that commerce, especially in the Mediterranean, requires naval protection and recommends gradually creating a navy. It also urges continued encouragement of manufactures, possible public production of essential military supplies, support for agriculture through boards of information and premiums, and renewed consideration of a national university and military academy.

It calls for revising compensation for federal officers, reports injuries to American trade in the West Indies by French cruisers and agents, and expresses a continued desire for friendship with France while reserving a fuller message. The address notes improving revenues, urges further measures to reduce public debt, recalls the need for an efficient militia and secure harbors, and concludes by reflecting on the success of the government and praying for the preservation of the nation’s liberty, virtue, and happiness.

The passage compiles April 23, 2001 news items mentioning Enron. Reports include Dabhol Power Company, 65% owned by Enron, meeting lenders in London amid payment defaults by Maharashtra State Electricity Board and possible steps toward terminating its power purchase agreement for the $2.9–$3 billion Maharashtra project. Related India articles discuss concerns over Dabhol’s impact on other power projects, ONGC disputing Enron’s claims about gas reserves at the Tapti Moon Prospect, and Karnataka power pricing questions involving Enron comparisons.

Other items include Bloomberg’s account of PG&E’s bankruptcy after California wholesale power price spikes and failed expansion into businesses competing with Enron; a proposed 1,200-MW coal plant in Colorado near an Enron wind project; Saudi-U.S. energy talks involving possible roles for Enron/Oxy in Saudi gas developments; and Spain’s planned electricity market reforms sought by firms including Enron. The Wall Street Journal’s international brief also notes Dabhol shareholders may review the Maharashtra project’s future.

Evercore will release its second quarter 2018 financial results on July 25, 2018, and host a conference call at 8:00 a.m. ET with Ralph L. Schlosstein, John S. Weinberg, and Robert B. Walsh. The call will include a review and Q&A, with telephone replay available for one week and webcast archive available for 30 days.

Winter fishing will target offshore sailfish, dolphin, wahoo, and kingfish, with live bait and kite fishing recommended. Inshore, the inlet, beaches, and ICW should hold jacks, tarpon, and spawning sheepshead, with shrimp or clams as effective bait.

The passage compiles Oct. 23–24, 2001 media mentions of Enron. Reports focus on Enron’s efforts to reassure investors after its stock fell sharply, the SEC began inquiries into transactions involving CFO Andrew Fastow’s LJM partnerships, and analysts questioned the company’s disclosure and financing structures. Enron said it had sufficient liquidity, including credit lines, and might repay about $3.3 billion in notes from investment vehicles through asset sales, though Treasurer Ben Glisan said up to $1 billion in stock could be issued if needed. Other items mention Enron seeking a $750 million loan, possible shareholder litigation notices, Enron-related tax refunds in a House stimulus bill, and international asset and energy-sector developments involving Enron.

A study found that online images, videos and text portray women workers as younger than men, especially in prestigious roles, shaping both human perceptions and AI outputs. Researchers analyzed about 1.4 million online images and videos, online text, and an experiment with over 450 people. Participants exposed to occupational images estimated female workers as younger and male workers as older. ChatGPT, prompted to generate resumes for male and female names across 54 occupations, produced younger, less experienced female candidates and scored them lower than male candidates, reflecting overlapping age and gender bias not supported by U.S. workforce age data.

Michael Gayed’s SPY and XLU rotation strategy, described in a widely downloaded SSRN paper, rotates weekly between the S&P 500 ETF and utilities ETF based on past performance. Rotation systems aim to outperform buy-and-hold by switching among assets that perform better at different times. Utilities are emphasized because of their risk-aversion, low beta, and sensitivity to interest rates, often outperforming during falling-rate or volatile periods and underperforming when rate expectations rise.

Gayed’s long-term backtest showed strong outperformance since 1929, with 13.1% annual compounding. However, a backtest from XLU’s 1999 inception showed weaker results versus the market, though similar after volatility adjustment. From 1999 to March 2014, the strategy returned 6.7% annually versus 4.6% for buy-and-hold, but after publication it lagged SPY significantly, returning 5.1% annually versus 10.4%. The passage concludes the strategy has underperformed since publication, though it may be too soon to say it stopped working.

Researchers are exploring grape pomace, a major wine industry waste product, as a renewable source of antioxidants, oils and dietary fibers for health products, foods, pharmaceuticals and cosmetics. Pomace can pollute water, acidify soil and attract pests, while the wine industry produces about 14 million tons annually. Changmou Xu’s team is developing methods to extract useful nutrients while removing pesticides. They are studying pomace polyphenols for effects on foodborne pathogens, piglet health and natural food preservation. The researchers found phenolic compounds from pomace inhibited lipid oxidation in fatty foods such as mayonnaise and ranch dressing, extending shelf life, and previously reduced acrylamide formation in potato chips by 60 percent. Xu says grape pomace could help replace artificial antioxidants like EDTA with natural, label-friendly ingredients.

Game is selling an Xbox One S 500GB bundle for £249.99, including Forza Horizon 3, Tekken 7, Halo 5, and Gears of War 4. The items cost £297.10 separately on Amazon UK, making the bundle a £47.11 saving. The Xbox One S received a 4/5 review for its smaller design, 4K upscaling, UHD Blu-ray playback, and value. The included games were also reviewed positively: Forza Horizon 3 scored 5/5, Tekken 7 and Halo 5 scored 4/5, and Gears of War 4 scored 4.5/5.

NASA’s Cassini spacecraft completed the first of five close flybys of Saturn before its planned final plunge on September 15, ending its 20-year mission. The flybys make Cassini the first Saturn atmospheric probe and may include a maneuver bringing it closer to the cloud tops to gather data on the atmosphere, temperature, auroras, vortexes, chemical composition, and day length. Cassini spent 13 years at Saturn and made 127 close flybys of Titan, experience that helped prepare for these atmospheric passes. Because the spacecraft is low on fuel, the mission team chose to end it in Saturn to avoid a possible crash into Titan or Enceladus, both considered promising candidates for microbial life. Cassini’s final Titan encounter on September 11 will set up its descent.

The passage describes a patent application related to smart energy device infrastructure in surgical environments and incorporates numerous related patent applications by reference. It discloses methods for ultrasonic surgical devices that apply power to an ultrasonic transducer, measure impedance, compare it to stored reference values, classify the impedance, characterize the end effector state, function, or contacted tissue, and adjust power accordingly. It also describes interactive surgical systems with surgical hubs, cloud connectivity, visualization systems, robotic systems, intelligent instruments, modular generator, smoke evacuation, suction/irrigation, imaging, communication, processor, and storage modules. The system supports coordinated data, power, fluid management, real-time device communication, surgical imaging, cloud-based analytics, and adaptive control of ultrasonic and electrosurgical instruments.

The study tested BNT162b1, BNT162b2, BNT162b2SA, placebo, and booster doses in healthy participants aged 12 years and older without prior COVID-19 infection or vaccination. It ran at 153 locations in 6 countries from 29 April 2020 to 10 February 2023. Phase 1 included 195 participants; Phase 2/3 included 46,406 participants; and a Phase 3 group included 333 participants assigned to BNT162b2SA.

The first two doses were initially observer-blinded, later becoming open-label for original assignments. Some booster assignments remained observer-blinded. Participants stayed in the study for up to 26 months.

In Phase 2/3, BNT162b2 was 95% effective against COVID-19 from 7 days after Dose 2 through 03 December 2020 in participants aged 16 years and older, regardless of past COVID-19 infection. BNT162b2 and BNT162b2SA produced antibody responses judged not likely due to chance.

Safety findings showed temporary lymphocyte decreases in some Phase 1 participants after Dose 1, generally resolving within days. Injection-site reactions and systemic events were generally mild or moderate, short-lived, and well tolerated; injection-site pain, tiredness, and headache were common. BNT162b2 30 µg was selected for Phase 2/3, while BNT162b1 100 µg was stopped after Dose 1 due to reactions or systemic events.

Serious medical problems were uncommon. Most were not considered related to study vaccine, though a few temporary serious events in Phase 2/3 were considered possibly related. No deaths occurred in Phase 1. In Phase 2/3, deaths occurred in BNT162b2 and placebo/BNT162b2 groups from different causes, and researchers did not believe they were caused by BNT162b2. No deaths occurred in the BNT162b2SA Phase 3 group.

The Rams are seeking permission to interview Jaguars interim coach Doug Marrone for their head coaching vacancy. Marrone went 1-1 after replacing Gus Bradley and previously coached the Bills to a 9-7 record in 2014. The Jaguars may also consider making him their permanent head coach.

Plasma diagnostics infer plasma properties indirectly through physical effects, since quantities like density, temperature, velocity, and magnetic fields cannot be measured directly. The course assumes prior plasma physics knowledge and focuses on diagnostic principles rather than changing practical implementations.

Diagnostics are essential because plasma experiments are not useful without measurements. Historical examples include ZETA, where insufficient diagnostics led to mistaken fusion claims, later motivating Thomson scattering, and the National Ignition Facility, whose early lack of diagnostics limited understanding until improved measurements supported progress.

Experimenters need diagnostics to understand plasmas and measurement uncertainty; computational researchers use them to validate simulations and create comparable outputs; theorists need them to assess experimental claims and make testable predictions.

Desired plasma information includes particle distributions, moments such as density and average velocity, and magnetic fields from internal or external currents. In practice, diagnostics are limited: they may be sparse in space and time, line-integrated, filtered by instrument response, or dependent on uncertain physics such as atomic data in spectroscopy.

The lecture also surveys students’ plasma regimes and diagnostics across tokamaks, inertial confinement fusion, pulsed-power experiments, non-equilibrium plasmas, thrusters, helicon plasmas, and simulations, mentioning methods such as Langmuir probes, B-dot/Mirnov coils, spectroscopy, bolometers, neutron spectrometry, Thomson scattering, soft and hard X-ray detectors, interferometry, Faraday rotation imaging, electron cyclotron emission, flux loops, and laser shadowgraphy.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2015. Net sales were $22.7 billion, up from $19.7 billion in Q1 2014, while the company reported a net loss of $57 million, compared with net income of $108 million a year earlier. Operating income rose to $255 million from $146 million. North America net sales increased to $13.4 billion, International net sales decreased to $7.7 billion, and AWS net sales increased to $1.6 billion. AWS segment operating income was $265 million.

Operating cash flow was negative $1.5 billion for Q1 2015, compared with negative $2.5 billion in Q1 2014. For the trailing twelve months, operating cash flow was $7.8 billion and free cash flow was $3.2 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $13.8 billion at March 31, 2015, down from $17.4 billion at December 31, 2014. Total assets were $50.1 billion, total liabilities were $39.2 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $10.9 billion.

The company changed its reportable segments to North America, International, and AWS. It acquired certain companies during the quarter for an aggregate purchase price of $341 million, primarily to obtain technologies and know-how. Long-term debt had a face value of $8.4 billion, with no borrowings outstanding under its $2.0 billion revolving credit facility. Amazon reported $31.7 billion in principal contractual commitments and continued to face various legal and tax proceedings, including transfer pricing disputes and patent-related claims.

Tesla faced serious financial pressure in 2017–2018 while ramping production of the Model 3, with high cash burn and investor concerns about whether it would need additional capital. Founded in 2003, Tesla grew from the Roadster to the Model S, Model X, and Model 3, went public in 2010, expanded into batteries and solar energy, and acquired SolarCity in 2016. Despite a rising market value and strong product reception, Tesla struggled to generate profits or positive operating cash flow, repeatedly raising equity and debt after its IPO. By 2017, its shares outstanding had nearly doubled since the IPO and long-term debt exceeded $10 billion. Model 3 production delays intensified concerns, as reaching 5,000 cars per week was viewed as critical to becoming cash flow positive. Musk said in 2018 that Tesla would not need an equity or debt raise that year, but analysts questioned whether the company would require substantial external capital by 2020.

Hurricane Harvey may have damaged or destroyed up to a dozen critical wildlife habitats along the Texas Gulf Coast, including marshes, coastlines, and nesting sites for threatened and endangered species. Agencies are beginning assessments. Aransas National Wildlife Refuge and Attwater Prairie Chicken National Wildlife Refuge were affected, with only about 10 of 60 endangered prairie chickens believed to have survived. Some marine species, such as shrimp and crabs, appear to have survived, while oyster beds suffered losses and marine mammals may have been harmed by freshwater inflows.

The passage proposes an ascending-descending method to identify public transit mode hierarchies from passenger travel patterns using smart card data, without assuming spatial homogeneity. Transfers before and after half of a trip’s total distance are classified as ascending and descending phases, and transfer rate matrices are used to compute hierarchical distances and normalized hierarchy values for each mode. The method can also analyze interzonal and intrazonal hierarchies separately.

A Seoul Metropolitan Area case study used T-money data from November 12, 2019, covering 10,264,700 trip chains across Seoul, Gyeonggi Province, and Incheon. Modes included walking, community bus, urban bus, intercity bus, light rail, and metro. For trips within Seoul, hierarchy was consistent across ascending and descending phases: walking, community bus, urban bus, light rail, and metro. For interzonal trips between Seoul and Gyeonggi/Incheon, the hierarchy was community bus, urban bus, light rail, metro, and intercity bus, with intercity bus highest. Results showed that hierarchy values vary by included modes and by region, with differences observed for metro, intercity bus, and urban bus between Seoul and Gyeonggi/Incheon.

The Louisiana Second Circuit Court of Appeal reviewed a judgment against the Morehouse Parish Police Jury after 16-year-old Bradd Rudolph drove through a rural “T” intersection into Bayou Bartholomew, causing the drowning deaths of two back-seat passengers, including 15-year-old Michael Hill. The intersection had only a stop sign, though parish road supervisors testified that double-arrow warning signs had previously been placed there, were repeatedly knocked down or stolen, and had not been replaced for about three months. The trial court found the police jury knew of the intersection’s danger and failed to provide adequate warnings, allocating fault 20% to the police jury and 80% to Rudolph.

The appellate court affirmed the finding that the police jury breached its duty and that the absence of a double-arrow sign contributed to the accident. It amended the fault allocation to 35% for the police jury and 65% for Rudolph. The court upheld the $150,000 general damages award and special damages, finding no abuse of discretion. The judgment was amended and, as amended, affirmed; rehearing was denied.

This study assessed whether self-archiving could increase open access to clinical trial results publications from German university medical centers. Using the IntoValue cohort, Unpaywall, and Shareyourpaper, it examined 1,897 trial publications from 2010–2020 with DOIs. Overall, 54% were openly accessible through journals or repositories, while 46% were closed access. Open access increased from 50% in 2010 to 73% in 2020, mainly through gold and hybrid models.

Among 871 closed-access publications, Shareyourpaper provided sufficient information to determine self-archiving permissions for 736. All 736 could be archived as accepted or published versions in institutional repositories, often after a 12-month embargo. Including 143 publications already available only through repositories, realized green open access was estimated at 16% of otherwise closed-access publications with self-archiving permission.

The study concludes that many closed-access clinical trial results could be made openly available through existing publisher or journal self-archiving policies, supporting WHO guidance that clinical trial results publications should be open access where possible. It also presents an automated approach using open tools to identify actionable self-archiving opportunities at scale.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces GDDR6 memory, redesigned memory interfaces, improved clock gating, larger L2 caches, and enhanced lossless compression. Turing delivers 14 Gbps signaling, a 20% power efficiency improvement over GDDR5X, reduced signal crosstalk, and about 50% higher effective bandwidth versus Pascal in TU102-based RTX 2080 Ti compared with GP102-based 1080 Ti.

Turing includes a new display engine supporting DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, VESA DSC 1.2, HDR processing, tone mapping, and 8K output over USB-C. Its NVENC encoder supports H.265 8K at 30 fps and improves bitrate efficiency, while NVDEC adds support for HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit streams and VP9 10/12-bit HDR. Turing also supports USB Type-C and VirtualLink to deliver VR display, data, and power through one connector.

For multi-GPU configurations, Turing TU102 and TU104 use second-generation NVLink instead of MIO and PCIe for SLI data transfers. TU102 provides two x8 NVLink links, while TU104 provides one. Two-way SLI is supported on Turing GPUs with NVLink, but 3-way and 4-way SLI are not.

Turing enables real-time ray tracing through RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs combined with NVIDIA RTX software. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, offloading the SM and enabling hybrid rendering that combines rasterization and ray tracing. NVIDIA describes this as suitable for reflections, refractions, shadows, ambient occlusion, audio simulation, physics, AI visibility queries, and professional rendering. Turing can achieve over 10 Giga Rays/sec using RT Cores, compared with Pascal performing ray tracing in software.

Turing adds NVIDIA NGX, a deep learning-based technology stack using Tensor Cores for AI-enhanced graphics features. NGX supports DLSS, DLSS 2X, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS is trained using high-quality 64x supersampled reference images and can improve performance while producing image quality similar to TAA; DLSS 2X targets quality close to 64x supersampling.

The architecture introduces Mesh Shading with Task Shaders and Mesh Shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and support more flexible geometry processing. Variable Rate Shading lets developers vary shading rate per 16x16-pixel region or per primitive, supporting content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, foveated rendering, and higher shading rates with MSAA. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and shading, allowing shaded texels to be reused across pixels, frames, views, or applications such as VR stereo rendering.

Turing expands Multi-View Rendering, supporting up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 API-level views. It generalizes Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi-Projection and supports VR, canted-display headsets, cascaded shadow maps, and multiple character instances. Turing also extends DX12 resource support with bindless Constant Buffer Views and Unordered Access Views and supports Tier 2 resource heaps.

The TU104 GPU includes up to six GPCs, 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 13.6 billion transistors, and second-generation NVLink. It is used in products such as GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. Tesla T4 uses a TU104 configuration with 40 SMs, 2560 CUDA Cores, 320 Tensor Cores, a 256-bit memory interface, and 320 GB/s bandwidth. TU106, used in GeForce RTX 2070, includes 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, and does not support NVLink or SLI.

The passage presents RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering, combining weighted Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations. It also explains ray tracing fundamentals, BVH acceleration, denoising, and examples of ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections in games. It concludes that hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH algorithms, and RT Cores together enable real-time ray tracing on Turing GPUs.

Natural gas settled at $3.27/MMBtu, constrained by a descending wedge as strong U.S. LNG export demand is offset by North American oversupply, seasonal softness, and Canadian supply shocks. The passage also describes Traders Union as a financial portal offering broker reviews and market content.

U.S. markets fell sharply Tuesday as the 10-year Treasury yield reached three per cent and investors worried about interest rates and company results, including Alphabet. Canada’s S&P/TSX also declined but was supported by materials and gold stocks, including Barrick Gold. The Canadian dollar, gold and copper prices rose slightly.

The passage criticizes Ontario Premier Kathleen Wynne for remarks at Humber College suggesting that if young people and minorities do not vote, older white people will. It argues the comment is ageist and racist, claims it unfairly portrays demographic groups as having opposing interests, and cites Ali Taghva accusing Wynne of identity politics. Labour lawyer Sunira Chaudhri is quoted saying similar workplace comments could prompt Human Rights Tribunal complaints. The passage acknowledges that voter participation rises with age and that visible minorities may vote at lower rates, but argues voter turnout should be encouraged without demonizing other groups.

Global stock markets mostly rose after Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen said interest rates could increase as soon as next month, citing a stronger job market and modestly higher inflation. European indexes gained, Wall Street futures were little changed, and most Asian markets closed higher, though Shanghai and India declined. Analysts said Yellen’s comments surprised markets with a more hawkish tone, lifting bond yields, bank shares, the U.S. dollar and equities. Chinese inflation rose, raising concerns about possible tightening, though analysts saw no major policy shift. The dollar strengthened against the yen, the euro slipped, and U.S. and Brent crude prices fell.

Recent studies have renewed interest in psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy. MDMA-assisted therapy has shown significant and sustained reductions in PTSD symptoms, with Phase II pooled results showing 54% no longer met PTSD criteria. The FDA designated it a breakthrough therapy, and Phase 3 results confirmed safety and efficacy in severe PTSD.

Gary Gensler introduces MIT course 15.S12, “Blockchain and Money,” focused on blockchain’s intersection with finance and money. He explains that the course will examine what blockchain is, whether it may catalyze change in finance, and how to distinguish real opportunities from hype. The class will include cold calls, readings, individual write-ups, class participation, and a team project proposing a blockchain-related financial use case.

Gensler frames blockchain in relation to the internet, cryptography, digital payments, and earlier failed digital currencies. He describes cryptography as communication in the presence of adversaries and notes its importance to the internet and blockchain. He discusses Bitcoin as Satoshi Nakamoto’s peer-to-peer electronic cash system without a trusted third party, and defines blockchain as time-stamped append-only logs secured by cryptography, hash functions, digital signatures, and consensus protocols.

He emphasizes that blockchain technology verifiably moves data on decentralized networks and addresses the cost of trust, though it involves trade-offs. In finance, he says blockchain may affect systems for moving, allocating, and pricing money and risk. He identifies opportunities in payments, central banking, clearing and settlement, financial inclusion, and reducing economic rents, while noting challenges including scalability, performance, privacy, security, interoperability, governance, commercial use cases, and public policy concerns.

The lecture contrasts permissioned blockchains, often favored by financial institutions, with permissionless systems such as Bitcoin. Gensler gives examples including the Australian Stock Exchange and Depository Trust Corporation exploring controlled blockchain systems. He also discusses the scale of crypto finance compared with global equity, bond, debt, and gold markets, and outlines regulatory concerns such as illicit activity, financial stability, capital controls, and investor protection.

The course structure will cover blockchain fundamentals, economics, and financial-sector use cases such as payments, central bank digital currency, trading, venture capital, and initial coin offerings. Gensler says the class will consider minimalist and maximalist views, including critiques from prominent skeptics, and will analyze technology, markets, law, and social norms. He concludes that blockchain may provide a peer-to-peer alternative that addresses trust costs, but the course will critically assess whether and where it can improve finance.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated January 28, 2016, reporting its fourth quarter 2015 and year ended December 31, 2015 financial results. The filing incorporates a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and information on non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. The report was signed by CFO Brian T. Olsavsky.

Digital laggards often restrict data access, store data in silos, and rely on business judgment or leadership expertise over data-driven decisions. Data may be used mainly to justify decisions already made, reinforcing power dynamics and limiting shared understanding. By contrast, digital leaders provide more transparent data access, use standardized APIs more often, and encourage measurement to support learning, goal-setting, and progress tracking.

Digital leaders ground objectives in meaningful metrics, combine structured goals with flexibility in execution, and use data-driven objectives to align teams with company strategy. This can encourage experimentation, autonomy, and cross-functional collaboration, though some leaders still struggle with over-analysis. A retail company case showed how real-time sales reporting enabled faster data-driven decisions across inventory, marketing, and supply chain.

Digital laggards often set aspirational goals not grounded in data, leading employees to avoid measurement and focus on qualitative effort or adherence to process. This can stifle innovation and create misalignment between team actions and company strategy.

Strong data culture aligns organizations vertically and horizontally through shared metrics, transparent access, and common data models. Digital leaders make data culture central by connecting beliefs, values, and daily behaviors. Laggards may recognize the importance of data culture but face barriers such as entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient leadership focus. Organizations may fall into patterns such as data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant, each requiring targeted actions to strengthen data culture.

Ireland is highly exposed to exchange rate movements, affecting tourism, trade, industries, SMEs, and holidaymakers. A weak euro against the dollar has boosted US tourism, while weak sterling against the euro discourages UK visitors. Sterling has fallen from 76p to about 91p against the euro since the Brexit referendum, while the euro has risen from $1.05 to $1.18 amid expectations of ending quantitative easing and higher eurozone rates. The outlook remains uncertain due to ECB decisions and Brexit. Tourism firms have limited ability to hedge currency exposure. Importers from the UK benefit from cheap sterling and should hedge to lock in gains, while exporters to the UK and the car industry face difficulties from weak sterling and cheap UK second-hand cars.

Browns coach Kevin Stefanski said he has not decided whether rookie Shedeur Sanders will be Cleveland’s backup quarterback after Joe Flacco was traded to the Bengals. The trade left Sanders and Dillon Gabriel as the only quarterbacks on the active roster, though Stefanski may still consider roster moves involving Zappe. Stefanski emphasized player development in making the decision. Sanders has been inactive as the No. 3 emergency quarterback through five games but was listed as No. 2 on the unofficial depth chart. Flacco was benched for Gabriel, who made his first start in a 21-17 loss in London.

A University of Michigan study of more than 2,000 older Americans found that ultra-processed food addiction is more common among adults in their 50s and early 60s than among those aged 65 to 80, especially women. Using the modified Yale Food Addiction Scale 2.0, researchers found addiction rates of 21% for women and 10% for men in the younger group, compared with 12% and 4% in the older group. Researchers linked higher risk to self-reported overweight, fair or poor mental or physical health, and social isolation. They suggest 1980s marketing of diet-focused ultra-processed foods to women may have contributed and warn that today’s children could face higher future risks.

The Bank of England will keep the £5 polymer note and issue the £10 note as planned despite tallow concerns, citing costs and anti-counterfeit issues. It will consult on plant-based alternatives for future £20, £5 and £10 notes, with a decision due by summer 2017.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that Bob Iger resigned from its Board of Directors on September 10, 2019. The report was signed on September 13, 2019, by Katherine Adams, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary.

The study examines career transitions of civil servant lecturers and education personnel in Indonesian higher education institutions, focusing on adaptation and impacts. Using a qualitative grounded theory approach, data were collected through semi-structured interviews with informants selected by snowball sampling and analyzed with NVIVO using open, axial, and selective coding.

Findings show that Schlossberg’s 4S factors—situation, self, support, and strategies—explain adaptation, with reciprocal relationships among them. The study identifies additional dimensions: new tasks, personal strengths and weaknesses, and organizational support. Career transitions lead to changes in behavior, roles, learning, and perceptions. Lecturers and education staff often face dual roles, reduced performance in primary duties, and the need to balance organizational responsibilities with individual career demands. Unlike Schein’s career anchor theory, the study finds that informants use both competence and managerial anchors during transition.

The study suggests that organizations and government should better prepare and support career transitions, especially when assigning functional roles. Limitations include its qualitative design, focus on transitions within institutions, limited demographic consideration, and possible researcher bias.

Qarlinngua, meaning “like pants” in Inuktitut, is a large pants-shaped sea arch in salt water on the Brodeur Peninsula, about 80 to 90 kilometres southwest of Arctic Bay, Nunavut. A photo submitted to CBC North by local hunter Max Kalluk was initially suspected by some readers and tourism staff to be fake, but local sources confirmed the formation exists. It is reachable only by boat during a short summer window when sea ice breaks up.

Kalluk says he first saw Qarlinngua as a child while seal hunting and sees it yearly en route to narwhal hunting. He estimates it is more than 50 metres tall. Geologists who reviewed photos said it is a natural sea arch formed by erosion of sedimentary rock, likely sandstone, with more erosion-resistant quartz helping part of it remain standing. They said similar formations are uncommon in the Arctic, where summer sea ice has historically slowed erosion. Estimates for its collapse range from decades to thousands of years, though nearby cliffs may form new arches.

Arctic Bay Adventures says it is the only tour company taking visitors there, though access is limited to days or weeks each year. Nunavut tourism officials, previously unaware of Qarlinngua, said they hope to promote it to high-income travellers.
Judgment for New York City was affirmed with costs.
