The article examines leaders of education-related undergraduate programmes delivered in further education colleges in England, using Hodgson and Spours’s lifelong learning ecology model. It outlines how such provision developed through widening participation, foundation degrees, HE–FE partnerships and local workforce needs. The study draws on a British Education Studies Association-funded project using questionnaires from 70 programme leaders and 11 follow-up interviews, with particular focus on 14 further education-based respondents.

Findings show that FE programme leaders often enter roles through informal or internal routes, usually hold master’s degrees, and manage small teams with broad responsibilities. Their work includes administration, liaison with validating or franchising universities, recruitment, quality assurance, teaching, student academic support and pastoral care. They often support diverse, non-traditional learners, including mature students and those progressing towards teaching careers.

The article characterises FE undergraduate programme leaders as a “keystone species” within local learning ecologies because they anchor provision and support students’ development. However, they face tensions between institutional demands, higher education expectations, limited scholarly opportunities, unclear role definitions and commitments to student success. The authors argue that programme leaders need better “sightlines” beyond their institutions through research, scholarly activity, academic networks and partnerships to strengthen provision and support professional development.

The disclosure describes methods and systems for creating virtual game environments from real-world scenes. A user selects and arranges physical objects, such as everyday items or toy construction models, to form a physical model of a game scene. A capturing device, preferably a 3D or depth-sensitive camera, scans the scene to produce a digital three-dimensional representation containing information such as shape, dimensions, color, texture, or transparency. This representation is converted into a virtual toy construction model made of virtual construction elements, and game-controlling elements are defined based on detected physical properties and conversion rules.

Conversion rules may map object properties to virtual features depending on game context or theme, such as red objects becoming lava elements or green objects becoming jungle elements. Rules may be static or adaptive and may depend on recognized objects, user selections, scene properties, location, time, or user profile. Recognized objects can trigger themes, game rules, virtual objects, attributes, or functional behaviors. Known objects may be identified through image processing, visible markers, RFID, Bluetooth, or similar technologies, and may be matched with stored library data.

The virtual environment may be created as a modified version of the scanned scene, including removal or replacement of recognized objects, interpolation of surrounding geometry, or insertion of more accurate digital models with associated functions. Virtual objects may become player characters, non-player characters, vehicles, or interactive elements.

The disclosure also describes voxelization methods for converting surface representations, such as meshes, into voxel-based representations. Surface elements are sampled using points distributed across them, and each point is mapped to a voxel. Voxel attributes, including color, may be derived from surface attributes. A color-matching method identifies the closest color from a predetermined palette by limiting the search area in color space to improve efficiency.

An interactive game system may include a capturing device, display, storage, and processor, optionally integrated in a mobile device. The system may show augmented reality overlays to assist targeting and scanning. Game play may be cyclic: a virtual environment is created from scanned physical objects, game segments are played, outcomes unlock rewards or new features, and a new cycle begins. Physical playable characters made from toy construction elements may correspond to virtual playable characters, with physical tools unlocking matching virtual tools, skills, or powers.

U.S. District Judge Paul W. Grimm sentenced Gbenga “Benson” Ogundele of Laurel, Maryland, to 234 months in federal prison and his wife, Moji Popoola, to 18 months, each followed by three years of supervised release, for conspiracies to commit wire fraud and money laundering in an online dating fraud scheme. Ogundele was also convicted of aggravated identity theft and ordered to forfeit $2,195,103.36; Popoola was ordered to forfeit about $165,000 and pay $34,100 restitution. The scheme, active from January 2011 to May 2015, used online dating sites, false romantic relationships, and fake financial emergencies to obtain money from victims, with payments ranging from $1,720 to $50,000. Babatunde Popoola received 12 years in prison, Victor Oloyede received 234 months, and other co-conspirators pleaded guilty to money laundering-related charges.

Maria Saliagas, who has multiple sclerosis, says Delta employees tied her to a regular wheelchair with a blanket in Amsterdam because they lacked a wheelchair with straps, causing bruises and distress. Delta said it regrets the customers’ perception and contacted the family to address concerns. The family rejected 20,000 SkyMiles as insufficient and wants policy changes for passengers with disabilities.

The passage describes a patent application for novel compounds represented by Chemical Formula 1 and organic light emitting devices (OLEDs) including them. The compounds include defined aryl, heterocyclic, triazine-linked, and related substituent structures and may be used in one or more OLED organic layers, including light emitting, hole injection/transport, electron injection/transport, electron blocking, or hole blocking layers. The stated effects are reduced driving voltage, improved light efficiency, and enhanced lifetime characteristics due to thermal stability.

The OLED may include a first electrode, a second electrode facing it, and one or more organic material layers between them. Manufacturing methods include vacuum deposition and solution application methods, using known electrode and organic layer materials. Preparation examples describe synthesis of multiple compounds, and device examples use selected compounds as electron transport materials. Compared with comparative electron transport compounds, Examples 1–15 showed lower driving voltage, higher current efficiency, and longer lifetime.

Martyn Waghorn returns to Sunderland with Ipswich Town, his seventh club since leaving in 2010. He said former youth coach Kevin Ball helped revive his career when he nearly got released at 15, teaching him football fundamentals and encouraging him to focus. Waghorn, now 28, credits Ball and Sunderland for giving him a chance. Since leaving, he has scored 87 career goals, including 44 for Rangers, and is in double figures this season.

This unfunded protocol describes a register-based cohort study of Danish adults undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty from 1995 to 2022. Using Danish Hip Arthroplasty Register data, the study will examine trends in revision surgery for periprosthetic joint infection, categorized as DAIR, one-stage exchange, or two-stage exchange, and report second-revision risk after each approach. Analyses will include timing after primary surgery and use R with Cox models adjusted for calendar time, age, and sex. Strengths include nationwide data and long follow-up; limitations include incomplete private clinic reporting and surgeon-reported infection diagnoses.

Truck traffic through Ponca, Arkansas, has increased sharply, with residents linking the rise to GPS routes that send drivers onto steep, winding Arkansas 43. In the past 2½ years, seven trucks have wrecked on a 2-mile stretch north of town, where the road drops 1,300 feet from Arkansas 103 and includes difficult curves. Local business owners say drivers often burn up brakes, crash, or endanger motorists and pedestrians near the Buffalo National River tourist area. Some wrecks involved heavy loads headed toward Clarksville, including one Nov. 9 crash that totaled a truck carrying beverages. The Arkansas Highway and Transportation Department plans warning signs near Arkansas 103 reading, “Crooked and steep next 3 miles. Drive with care,” and is reassessing the issue after another Dec. 22 crash. Officials said similar GPS-related truck problems occur on other steep Newton County roads.

The passage describes a floor cleaner with a vacuum source, supply tank, distribution nozzle, suction inlet, recovery tank, rechargeable battery, steerable body, brushroll, removable brushroll cover, squeegees, lights, and fluid spray system. The recovery tank includes features such as a removable cover, strainer, inlet duct, baffle, shutoff float, filter with pull tab, and retention structures. The cleaner is designed with component placement for balance, a pivoting and steering connection between body and base, a hydrophobic brushroll with different fiber sets, removable access to the brushroll chamber, illuminated spray visibility, and squeegee/nozzle arrangements for fluid pickup and cleaning performance.

The passage criticizes the Philippine national basketball team, Gilas, for its role in a brawl during a FIBA World Cup qualifier against Australia in Bocaue, Bulacan. It notes that before the fight, Australia was decisively outplaying the Philippines, leading 79-48 late in the third quarter and eventually winning by default, 89-53. Australia dominated through strong defense, ball movement, three-point shooting, and efficient offense, while Gilas struggled with turnovers and poor shooting.

The article argues that the Philippine team’s violent reaction, including punches, thrown chairs, and involvement from the bench and crowd, was inexcusable despite alleged provocation by Australian player Daniel Kickert. It says Australia also bore responsibility, particularly for Kickert’s hit on RR Pogoy, and notes that both Australia and the Samahang Basketbol ng Pilipinas apologized. However, it emphasizes that the Philippines was more at fault for the escalation and that the incident damaged the team’s image on the global stage.

The passage calls for accountability beyond apology, including possible sanctions, greater restraint, and changes in how the national team responds to future conflicts.

Leam Richardson dismissed the tunnel incident after Wigan Athletic’s match against Fleetwood as minor, saying Ivan Toney and Nathan Pond briefly pushed and shoved but later laughed about it. He said it was not comparable to the Manchester derby “Milkgate” incident. Toney could start against AFC Fylde as Wigan seek an FA Cup third-round tie at Bournemouth. Richardson said Wigan must first overcome a tough test against Fylde.

The “Give & Go” isolation offense uses a 2-1-2 spread alignment to keep control with the two best ball handlers. The ballhandler passes to a wing, cuts hard to the basket, and receives a pass if open; if not, the receiver dribbles out and repeats the action. Options include wing back cuts against overplay, dribble penetration against soft defense, post pressure-release passes, and weakside help with return passes or initiating action. Weakside players may exchange positions or set down/back screens to occupy sagging defenders, while avoiding moving screen fouls.

Progressive reported February 2018 results with an 87.8% combined ratio, improved from February 2017, while net income fell 4% to $129 million. Net earned premiums rose 19% to $2.2 billion in February and 18% year to date to $4.9 billion, with all business lines growing at least 16%. The company priced debt and preferred share offerings with net proceeds of $1.08 billion for general corporate purposes and expanded commercial auto coverage for an Uber subsidiary in three additional states, adding $70 million in net premiums. The author estimates Progressive’s intrinsic value at about $48 per share based on current metrics and $50–$54 using expected 2018 metrics, but considers the stock slightly overvalued. The author expects higher 2018 earnings than 2017, book value growth above 10%, and a 2018 dividend of $0.76 to $1.85 per share.

An electronic device may include enclosure walls made of transparent and opaque materials, with display layers under transparent portions and touch sensor layers under both transparent and opaque portions. Touch and display layers may extend across front, rear, side, curved, or folded surfaces, enabling touch input on areas that may not display images. The device may use various display and touch technologies, including capacitive touch electrodes and pixel arrays.

Embodiments include devices with flat or curved sidewalls, rear touch sensors, wraparound displays, and foldable structures with flexible transparent wall portions joining planar walls. Foldable devices may use flexible layers, accordion structures, or pivot hinges, and may include multiple bend axes. Fabrication methods include laminating flexible touch or display layers to enclosure walls, depositing and patterning layers as coatings, molding walls, and applying hard coatings. Stress-tolerant features may help prevent damage in flexible regions.

Dual momentum, associated with Gary Antonacci, is an investing strategy that selects assets with both positive absolute momentum and stronger relative momentum than peers. Absolute momentum measures an asset’s own price change over a period, while relative momentum compares that performance with other assets. The strategy seeks to buy the strongest assets in rising markets and, where shorting is practical, sell the weakest assets in falling markets.

The concept builds on relative momentum research by Jagadeesh and Titman and adds absolute momentum to reduce volatility. It can be applied to individual assets, futures, sector rotation, and especially ETFs. Antonacci’s Global Equities Momentum model rotates among U.S. stocks, non-U.S. stocks, and bonds based on momentum signals. Backtests cited in the passage show lower drawdowns than benchmarks, though results are hypothetical and not indicative of future performance. The strategy may underperform in strong bull markets or sharp rebounds but is presented as useful for managing bear-market risk.

The study examines teachers’ opinions on culturally responsive education in the Turkish Education System. It uses Q methodology to identify similarities and differences in teachers’ perceptions. Thirty Q statements were developed from the literature, and 21 public school teachers from Denizli, Mardin, Erzurum, and Şanlıurfa ranked them through an online Q-sort process. Participants varied by age, gender, seniority, branch, city, and ethnic identity.

Analysis produced three factors: “Unification,” “Student Support,” and “Teacher Support.” The unification factor emphasized bringing cultures together, human values, and global culture. The student support factor focused on supporting students’ cultural competence, psychosocial needs, and awareness of inequality. The teacher support factor focused on teachers’ development, use of cultural differences in teaching, and curriculum-related practices.

Teachers generally viewed the Turkish education system as accepting cultural diversity and not denying different cultures, but also identified inequalities between cultures. They saw diversity as richness, yet considered the system insufficiently developed to fully address this diversity. Consensus was strongest on increasing students’ cultural competence, presenting life practices for general culture, and supporting students’ academic and social development with local culture, though these were mostly neutral positions. Disagreement centered on whether measures are taken against discrimination, whether different cultures are seen as a threat, and whether classrooms reflect society’s cultural diversity.

Participants declined to explain their strongest agreements or disagreements, which the study interprets as indicating sensitivity around multiculturalism and cultural responsiveness. The study concludes that initial steps toward culturally responsive education have been taken in Turkey, but further work is needed, especially in curriculum, teaching programs, student support, and teacher training. It recommends culturally responsive education workshops, stronger teacher professional development, classroom practices that allow students to express themselves and their cultures freely, broader academic research, and dissemination of knowledge about different cultures. The study notes limitations including participants’ hesitation to express views and the regional concentration of participants.

The Break, a longtime Five Points South restaurant and billiards hall in Birmingham, will be demolished for high-rise apartments. Some residents welcome the change, hoping it revives the area’s nightlife, while others worry new luxury apartments will worsen rising rents and want more affordable housing. No closure date has been set.

Neiman Gracie criticized Dillon Danis’ trash talking, saying Danis should fight professionally before speaking. Gracie accepted a Bellator 180 bout with Danis, but Danis declined; Gracie will instead face Dave Marfone.

US researchers found that higher temperatures are linked to lower exam scores, with a half-degree annual temperature rise associated with a 1% drop. Air conditioning may reduce the effect, but many UK schools lack it, and exams often take place in June when temperatures can exceed the threshold where negative effects begin. Moving exams or changing the academic year is complicated because schools, universities, employers, courts and Westminster follow similar schedules. UK exam grading also adjusts yearly based on average scores, reducing long-term disadvantage from unusually hot summers.

The advance/decline indicator, or AD line, is a market breadth indicator that cumulatively tracks the difference between advancing and declining stocks in a stock index, usually on a daily basis. It reflects market sentiment and can confirm trends or signal possible reversals when it diverges from the index. Advancing issues trade above the previous close, while declining issues trade below it. Advance/decline distribution and volume measure the number and volume of rising and falling stocks. The NYSE advance-decline line applies this calculation to stocks listed on the New York Stock Exchange. A backtest using SPY found weak and inconsistent results, with 229 trades, an average gain of 0.6%, and a profit factor of 1.55. The article concludes that the advance-decline indicator was not successful as a trading strategy in the tested versions.

Dive operators disagree on whether the ex-HMAS Tobruk landing on its side during scuttling will affect tourism. Dive Hervey Bay owner Glenn Bowman said the position could reduce income by 50% because the starboard side is largely inaccessible to general divers. Hervey Bay Dive Centre owner Ed Gibson said the wreck remains accessible and tourism should thrive with adjusted tours. Both agreed the dive would be spectacular. Hinkler MP Keith Pitt’s office declined to comment, saying control passed to the Queensland Government in 2016. Queensland Parks and Wildlife said the wreck is in the correct location, inspections are underway, and the government is consulting operators on dive opportunities.

IEP News for July 11, 2001 compiles energy-related articles, chiefly on California’s failed settlement talks with power suppliers over alleged electricity overcharges. Gov. Gray Davis said California would pursue its $8.9 billion refund demand in court if needed, while FERC administrative law judge Curtis Wagner indicated refunds may be closer to $1 billion and limited to sales after October 2000. Other items cover Calpine’s purchase of natural gas reserves, Edison International’s financial stabilization efforts, risks to California’s overloaded transmission grid, Texas officials contrasting their electricity market with California’s, federal energy legislation, and labor conditions for California shepherds.

The passage profiles wealthy celebrities and heiresses who launched businesses, many of which struggled financially. Millie Mackintosh’s fashion company collapsed with major debts, while Ella Mills closed two of her three Mae Deli sites after heavy losses, though her main Deliciously Ella business remained profitable. Trinny Woodall’s make-up brand reported mixed results but gained significant investor backing. Petra and Tamara Ecclestone’s handbag and haircare ventures accumulated large losses, with Petra winding up her firm and Tamara’s renamed company still losing money. Alexa Chung’s fashion label also posted losses but received investment from wealthy backers. Kate Rothschild’s record label closed after financial difficulties, and Sadie Frost’s lingerie label Frost French was eventually dissolved despite early success.

The speaker says their team needs to be more aggressive offensively and get to the net, while Detroit’s defense has adjusted well and limited shooting lanes. Both goaltenders and team defenses have been strong, creating tough battles in front of the net. The speaker praises the home fans as the NHL’s loudest and most energizing.

Generative AI and LLMs are transforming sectors such as finance, healthcare, and education while creating legal and ethical risks, including misinformation, deepfakes, bias, discrimination, and regulatory uncertainty. Existing and proposed AI policies aim to protect rights, inclusiveness, safety, transparency, and accountability, with governments such as the EU, United States, and China and companies such as Microsoft taking governance actions.

Key challenges include poor communication between industry and governments, lack of international consensus, inconsistent national regulations, higher compliance burdens, and difficulty identifying LLM risks during testing. The passage calls for AI governance that is human-centered, safe, secure, and trustworthy. It recommends stronger partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers, forward-looking regulation, and combined top-down and bottom-up governance. Developers, users, and communities should report risks throughout the AI lifecycle, while governments and companies should create channels to collect incidents, investigate risks, and update regulations transparently and promptly. Social computing techniques may help monitor regulatory needs in specific communities.

Global Ferronickel unit PGMC renewed a contract to supply 1.5 million WMT of medium-grade nickel ore to Guangdong Century Tsingshan Nickel for the 2018 mining season at market prices. Global Ferronickel reported 2017 income of P779.7 million and revenues of P5.8 billion.

This passage introduces the 2018 ebook edition of Foreign Relations of the United States: Diplomatic Papers, 1942, Volume II, Europe, produced by the Office of the Historian, U.S. Department of State. It explains the ebook initiative, its portability, search and offline access, and recommends citing document numbers rather than page numbers. The preface states that Foreign Relations is the official documentary record of U.S. foreign policy and is edited under principles of historical objectivity, with no unmarked deletions or omissions intended to conceal policy defects. It also identifies the Historical Office, Foreign Relations staff, compilers, and Division of Publishing Services personnel responsible for preparing and editing the volume.

The passage covers recent Supreme Court-related news, including Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson’s 2022 investiture, potential effects of a government shutdown on federal courts, and Chief Justice John Roberts’ 20 years leading the court. It notes upcoming major issues for the Roberts court, state attorneys general seeking to challenge limits on the death penalty for child rape, former Michigan athletes appealing an NIL lawsuit dismissal, Venezuelans asking the court to preserve protected status, and the court’s upcoming term and cert decisions. It also discusses historical Nixon-era communications with Chief Justice Warren Burger and the Trump administration’s request for the court to address birthright citizenship.

Salem residents are seeking bottled water, with local stores reporting shortages after the city announced low levels of cyanotoxins in the drinking water from an algae bloom in Detroit Lake. Officials said children under 6, pregnant or nursing mothers, people with compromised immune systems, dialysis patients, those with liver conditions, pets and other sensitive groups should not drink tap water. The city and Oregon Office of Emergency Management do not plan water distribution points and are directing residents to contact retailers. Major stores expect shipments but lack firm timing. Fresh test results are expected Thursday, and several nearby communities are also affected.

Eurozone stock markets fell Friday as the euro pressured the US dollar and traders awaited US jobs data. Germany’s DAX, France’s CAC 40 and the STOXX 600 declined, while London’s FTSE 100 fell less sharply. Deutsche Bank shares dropped after tax reforms pushed it into a loss. Analysts cited a global equity sell-off.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K dated February 9, 2017, reporting that it issued a press release announcing results for the quarter and fiscal year ended January 29, 2017. The filing includes Exhibit 99.1, the press release, and Exhibit 99.2, CFO commentary by Colette M. Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. The materials are furnished, not filed, and are not incorporated by reference into SEC filings.

End a job interview confidently and without lingering. Candidates should avoid seeming desperate, focus on the conversation and opportunity, ask necessary questions, and leave with a brief handshake and thanks. They should not ask when they will hear back, because employers often cannot accurately predict their decision timeline.

The passage explains offensive football positions and their roles. The offense aims to advance the ball, score touchdowns, or kick field goals. The quarterback leads the offense, handles the ball every play, makes passing and handoff decisions, and may call audibles before the snap. Running backs primarily carry the ball but may also catch passes and block. Tight ends combine receiving and blocking duties, with attached tight ends and sniffer/H-back types used in different alignments and roles.

The offensive line includes tackles, guards, and a center, who block for runs and passes. Tackles protect the edges, with the left tackle often protecting a right-handed quarterback’s blind side. Guards play between the center and tackles and may double-team or pull on run plays. The center snaps the ball and helps organize the line. Wide receivers catch passes, run routes, create space, and may block; types include X receivers, Z receivers, and slot receivers.

The paper studies learning Linear Temporal Logic on finite traces (LTLf): given positive and negative traces, find a minimal-size LTLf formula satisfied by all positives and no negatives. It situates LTLf learning in software specification mining, control and robotics, and AI, noting existing tools such as Scarlet and a GPU-accelerated VFB algorithm. Current methods face scaling limits, with Scarlet reportedly unable to reliably learn formulas larger than size 15.

The paper’s key idea is to separate Boolean operators from temporal operators. It first enumerates LTLf formulas up to a fixed size using a bounded VFB-style algorithm with characteristic tables and observational equivalence. If no solution is found, it treats the generated formulas as atoms and searches for larger Boolean combinations using conjunction and disjunction. This subproblem is called Boolean Set Cover.

Boolean Set Cover is defined over positive and negative elements and a weighted family of subsets. The goal is to construct a minimum-weight positive Boolean formula whose interpretation is exactly the positive set. The paper gives a polynomial criterion for whether any solution exists, shows the problem is NP-complete, and introduces domination, a pruning relation stronger than observational equivalence. Because full domination checks are costly, it proposes a fast approximate domination heuristic. It also uses a divide-and-conquer procedure that can find a valid solution when one exists, though without minimality guarantees.

The proposed Boolean Set Cover solver uses beam search: it enumerates formulas by weight while retaining only a fixed number of high-scoring candidates per weight, where score is based on the number of correctly classified elements. The full LTLf learning framework is implemented in a new Rust tool called Bolt.

The authors also provide a benchmark suite of more than 15,000 LTLf learning tasks across ten families, including fixed formulas, Hamming, ordered sequence, subword, subset, SYNTCOMP-derived counter and Nim tasks, and randomized formula families.

Experiments compare Bolt with Scarlet and the GPU algorithm. Against Scarlet, Bolt solves 14,374 of 15,595 tasks versus Scarlet’s 11,468, with lower average runtime and smaller average size ratio overall. Bolt is reported to be faster on most benchmark families, except some cases such as Subset and Nim. Against the GPU algorithm, Bolt solves fewer tasks on the comparable subset but remains competitive in runtime and formula size ratio. An ablation study shows that removing Boolean Set Cover causes fewer tasks to be solved, while the raw VFB algorithm usually either finds a minimal formula or times out.

The paper concludes that combining LTLf learning with Boolean Set Cover improves CPU-based state-of-the-art performance and argues that Boolean Set Cover may be useful beyond LTLf learning, including for other logics or specification languages with conjunctions and disjunctions.

Karnataka’s primary and secondary education department may cancel this year’s government school summer camps due to lack of funds, teacher duties in SSLC evaluation and election work. The camps, started in 2017-18 under “Swalpa odu, swalpa moju,” previously offered academic and extracurricular activities, mid-day meals, and targeted students in drought-hit taluks to improve learning outcomes.

A Cornell study by Adam Anderson, published in Psychological Science, found that people interpret emotions by analyzing eye expressions. Participants consistently linked narrowed eyes with discrimination-related states such as disgust and suspicion, and open eyes with sensitivity-related states such as fear, awe and curiosity. Using models of six facial expressions and 50 mental-state words, participants accurately identified basic emotions from eyes alone across 600 trials. Anderson found that eye openness was most closely tied to reading mental states, while other eye-region features helped signal whether states were positive or negative. Further studies showed the eyes conveyed emotions more robustly than other facial areas. The research builds on Anderson’s earlier work and supports Darwin’s theory that facial expressions originated from sensory functions before becoming tools for social communication.

Brendon Naidoo, DJ Zinhle’s boyfriend, faces multiple fraud charges linked to an alleged foreign-exchange trading scheme. He was granted R50,000 bail by the Alexandra Magistrate Court and must report to Sandton Police Station twice weekly. He is due back in court on May 5.

A town-commissioned study says relocating Vegreville’s federal immigration processing centre to Edmonton would hurt the community through population loss, lower property values, higher unemployment and fewer students. The centre employs 236 people. Officials and the workers’ union argue the closure is unnecessary and harmful to rural Vegreville.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics for experiments demonstrating macroscopic quantum mechanical tunnelling and energy quantisation in superconducting electric circuits. They will share nearly $1.2 million.

The study examined antimicrobial-resistant Enterobacteriaceae in untreated wastewater from metropolitan and non-metropolitan cities in Western Uttar Pradesh, India, during the COVID-19 pandemic. From 150 isolates collected between 2020 and 2021, 62% were E. coli, 24% K. pneumoniae, 8% other Enterobacteriaceae, and 6% unidentified mixed populations. Overall, 74% of isolates resisted one or more antibiotics, 79.3% of resistant isolates were ESBL producers, and approximately 80% were multidrug-resistant. MDR was detected mainly in E. coli and K. pneumoniae, with K. pneumoniae showing significantly higher MDR prevalence. Zone 1 had the highest overall MDR percentage, while Zone 3 had the highest MDR E. coli population. Resistance included carbapenems, cephalosporins, quinolones, aminoglycosides, sulfonamides, nitrofuran, and colistin, with colistin resistance observed in some non-E. coli isolates. The authors conclude that wastewater in India may serve as a reservoir for AMR and recommend periodic monitoring and molecular characterization of resistance genes.

Job interviews vary widely, from banal to elaborate or deliberately “zany.” Self-described disruptors avoid traditional questions, asking odd hypotheticals or riddles, and the passage advises responding assertively when they ask if you have questions.

Construction began on Fort Buford near the Missouri and Yellowstone rivers in 1866. The fort served as a military post until 1881, when Sitting Bull surrendered there. Soldiers faced poor food, scurvy, frozen supply lines, boredom, alcohol problems, and mental illness. A 1876 report described harsh conditions but also noted the Post Library’s books, newspapers, and magazines. Fort Buford was later abandoned, and a museum opened in the old headquarters building in 1963, with other parts restored afterward.

Anthony Davis and Eric Simmons appealed their Indiana convictions for Class A felony conspiracy to deal in cocaine in excess of three grams; Davis also appealed his forty-year enhanced sentence. The evidence showed that Simmons traveled from Detroit to Marion with others, helped package crack cocaine, went to a sparsely furnished apartment where Davis obtained cocaine, and participated in transactions involving confidential informant Euthan Lampkin. Lampkin made two purchases at the apartment, each under three grams, but the purchases totaled more than three grams.

The Court of Appeals held that, under the specific facts and charging allegations, sufficient evidence supported an agreement to deal more than three grams of cocaine, even though no single sale exceeded three grams. The court distinguished a prior case where there was no evidence connecting the defendant to multiple buys. It also rejected the claim that the verdicts were inconsistent, noting Davis had only one charge before the jury and that Simmons’s acquittal on dealing did not conflict with his conspiracy conviction because the State alleged multiple overt acts beyond the actual sale.

The court further held that Davis’s enhanced sentence was proper. Although some aggravators raised Blakely concerns, his criminal history alone supported the enhancement. The convictions and Davis’s sentence were affirmed.

The passage provides Texas Instruments device design guidance and specifications for power, reset, clocking, interrupts, and peripheral interfaces.

PLL and analog supplies should use ferrite beads and capacitors for noise filtering, with filters placed close to device pins. Decoupling capacitors are recommended as 0.1 µF in small packages, preferably no larger than 0402, with at least one capacitor per two power pins and one bulk capacitor of 10 µF or larger per roughly ten power pins. Excess capacitance should not slow power sequencing, and reset should remain low until all supplies are stable.

The device supports multiple reset types, including Power-on Reset, external warm reset, emulation warm reset, watchdog reset, software global cold and warm resets, test reset, local resets, and reset isolation for PCIe and EMAC Switch. POR resets the entire chip and requires stable supplies and clocks before deassertion. Warm reset excludes Test and Emulation logic and may optionally exclude the EMAC Switch. RSTOUT_WD_OUT indicates reset status and is affected by BTMODE[11] and watchdog reset behavior. Most resets place I/O pins in Hi-Z, with exceptions for emulation pins, EMAC isolation, RSTOUT_WD_OUT, and DDR behavior.

Clocking is based on reference clocks feeding PLLs and dividers. DEV and AUX clocks can come from external crystals with internal oscillators or from 1.8-V LVCMOS clock inputs. The DEV clock is typically 20 MHz and may range from 20–30 MHz under specified conditions; AUX is optional and supports 20–30 MHz. The PCIe PHY requires a high-quality low-jitter differential SERDES clock with AC coupling. The device includes multiple PLLs that start in bypass mode and must be configured within frequency limits. SYSCLK and module clock maximum frequencies are specified in tables.

The passage also describes interrupt handling. The ARM Cortex-A8 interrupt controller supports up to 128 requests with programmable priorities, while the C674x DSP interrupt controller combines up to 128 events into 12 prioritized CPU interrupts, with multiplexed event options.

Peripheral sections summarize features and timing references for DCAN, EDMA, advanced debug and trace, JTAG, EMAC Switch, MDIO, GPIO, GPMC/ELM, HDMI, HDVPSS, video DAC, and I2C. EMAC provides a three-port gigabit switch supporting MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII with MDIO PHY management. GPIO provides up to 128 configurable 1.8-V/3.3-V pins. GPMC supports NOR, NAND, SRAM, pseudo-SRAM, asynchronous and synchronous interfaces, and NAND error support through ELM. HDMI includes an HDMI 1.3a transmitter with TMDS, DDC, CEC, ESD, and PCB routing guidance. HDVPSS provides video input/output, processing, scaling, compositing, and display support. The I2C modules support standard and fast modes, 7- and 10-bit addressing, multimaster modes, filtering, and 32-byte FIFOs.

Flippy, a burger-flipping robot developed by Miso Robotics, has begun working as a grill cook at Caliburger’s Pasadena restaurant. The robot can reportedly grill 150 burgers per hour and is designed to operate in existing commercial kitchens alongside staff. It uses sensors, cameras, AI, and interchangeable tools to receive orders, cook burgers, and improve over time, though humans still place patties, add cheese, toppings, and wrap sandwiches. Caliburger has six months of exclusive use before other vendors can buy it. Flippy currently costs about $60,000, with possible price increases as it becomes more versatile. Caliburger plans U.S. expansion after a trial, while reports note fast food is highly vulnerable to automation.

Deutsche Telekom, Nokia and the Hamburg Port Authority will test 5G applications across an 8,000-hectare area of the Port of Hamburg. The trial will use an antenna on the Hamburg television tower and examine use cases including traffic light management, real-time environmental data processing from mobile sensors, and virtual reality monitoring of infrastructure. It will also test multiple network slices under live industrial conditions in Germany.

The passage describes reset, clocking, interrupt, peripheral, and timing information for a TMS320DM814x device. PCIe supports reset isolation, allowing the PCIe subsystem to reset independently, with different software handling for Root Complex and Endpoint modes. EMAC Switch reset isolation can preserve switch operation and traffic during most resets except POR when configured through RESET_ISO. Reset behavior is detailed for RSTOUT_WD_OUT, emulation logic, power domains, I/O pins, DDR pins, PINCNTL registers, and Boot ROM pin configuration effects.

The device uses DEV and AUX clock inputs, internal oscillators or 1.8-V LVCMOS clock inputs, SERDES differential clocking for PCIe, optional audio and 32.768-kHz clocks, selectable CLKOUT outputs, and multiple PLLs that start in bypass mode after reset. SYSCLK and module clock limits must be observed. Interrupt support includes ARM Cortex-A8 AINTC handling up to 128 requests and C674x DSP interrupt/event mapping with multiplexed events.

Peripheral sections describe DCAN, EDMA, AET, trace, JTAG, EMAC Switch, MDIO, GPIO, GPMC/ELM, HDMI, HDVPSS, video DAC, I2C, Imaging Subsystem, and DDR2/DDR3 memory controller functions, registers, electrical timing, and PCB/layout requirements. The passage also provides board-routing guidance, timing measurement assumptions, HDMI TMDS impedance and ESD guidance, video DAC routing recommendations, and DDR2/DDR3 routing requirements.

John Essey’s Pittsburgh-area home uses Internet-of-things devices to unlock doors, adjust lights and thermostats, and detect leaks. Carnegie Mellon Ph.D. student Gierad Laput says smart homes are often built either with costly connected appliances that may not work together or with many obtrusive sensors. His team developed a small wall-plug sensor that wirelessly detects environmental signals such as vibration, sound, and light to identify activities like a blender running or a light turning on. Laput sees domestic and commercial uses, such as detecting a stove left on or low paper towels. Critics, including IBM cybersecurity executive Bruce Schneier, warn that such devices raise surveillance and security concerns, arguing companies may use collected data for profit and that Internet-of-things makers are not prioritizing security.

The speaker says the team’s playoff success comes from focusing on one game at a time rather than the bigger picture, especially with two wins remaining. They praise a teammate’s hard play, leadership, and ability to avoid mistakes. The speaker discusses challenges playing the puck due to poor ice and glass conditions, reflects on sharing the Stanley Cup with meaningful causes, and says the team must watch a talented opponent closely. They compare past and current playoff runs, noting stronger offense now but emphasizing defense and key saves. They expect the next game to be difficult against an experienced team that responds well after losses.

Prosecutors dismissed the most serious charges against 18-year-old Jack Sawyer, accused of plotting a shooting at Fair Haven Union High School, after the Vermont Supreme Court ruled that preparation alone did not prove attempted aggravated murder. Sawyer still faces lesser charges of criminal threatening and carrying a dangerous weapon and has pleaded not guilty. Prosecutors say he kept a detailed shooting diary and bought a shotgun and ammunition, while his defense argued he took no concrete steps toward an attack. The case influenced Vermont Gov. Phil Scott to sign new gun restrictions, though they will not apply retroactively to Sawyer.

Apple filed its Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended June 26, 2021. Third-quarter net sales were $81.4 billion, up from $59.7 billion a year earlier, with net income of $21.7 billion and diluted earnings per share of $1.30. For the first nine months of fiscal 2021, net sales were $282.5 billion, net income was $74.1 billion and diluted earnings per share was $4.38.

Revenue increased across all product and service categories and all geographic segments. Third-quarter sales included $39.6 billion from iPhone, $8.2 billion from Mac, $7.4 billion from iPad, $8.8 billion from Wearables, Home and Accessories, and $17.5 billion from Services. Gross margin was $35.3 billion for the quarter.

As of June 26, 2021, Apple reported total assets of $329.8 billion, total liabilities of $265.6 billion and shareholders’ equity of $64.3 billion. Cash generated by operating activities for the first nine months was $83.8 billion. The company repurchased $22.5 billion of common stock and paid $3.8 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents during the quarter.

Apple said COVID-19 continued to affect aspects of its business, including store operations and remote work, though substantially all offices and retail stores had reopened subject to restrictions. The study examines the relationship between science education and citizenship education in Turkey through analysis of the Turkish science curriculum and interviews with eight science teachers. It argues that citizenship education has expanded beyond national identity formation to include democratic, global, environmental, and scientific competencies. Science education is presented as closely connected to citizenship through scientific literacy, socio-scientific issues, environmental awareness, sustainability, critical thinking, and responsible participation in society.

In Turkey, citizenship education historically focused on national identity and was mainly associated with social science courses. Since the 2000s, reforms introduced democratic, human rights, environmental, and multidisciplinary aims, but citizenship education later became more limited as a standalone or social studies responsibility. The science curriculum, especially after reforms influenced by the Science-Technology-Society-Environment approach, includes themes relevant to citizenship, such as scientific literacy, technology, society, environment, values, and skills, although it does not explicitly connect them to citizenship education.

The study used qualitative thematic analysis of curriculum documents and semi-structured interviews. Findings show that the strongest links between science and citizenship are scientific literacy, society, and especially the environment. Teachers viewed scientific literacy as essential for modern and active citizens, supporting problem-solving, inquiry, research, and critical thinking. Environmental topics such as climate change, pollution, recycling, biodiversity, renewable energy, and sustainability were frequently identified as central to citizenship. Teachers also linked science education to daily life, health, safety, socio-scientific issues, and values such as responsibility, respect, compassion, patriotism, and scientific integrity.

Teachers stated that science education can support citizenship skills, but practical barriers limit this potential. Reported problems included overcrowded classrooms, inadequate laboratories and materials, insufficient activities, exam-oriented education, curriculum limitations, student readiness, parent cooperation, and difficulties communicating with refugee students.

The study concludes that science education in Turkey has significant potential to contribute to citizenship education, but this relationship remains weak and insufficiently defined in practice. It recommends explicitly emphasizing citizenship skills in the science curriculum, promoting socio-scientific and environmental education, supporting democratic participation and inquiry in science classes, and providing teachers with training to integrate citizenship competencies into science education.

The passage discusses AI literacy and educational robotics as important parts of digital competence in preschool and primary education. It emphasizes that AI and robots can support personalized learning, feedback, engagement, algorithmic thinking, inclusion, social-emotional development, STE(A)M learning, and language learning. Serbia’s preschool curriculum framework and broader European and national strategies recognize digital competence as a key educational goal.

The study aimed to examine how future preschool and primary school teachers perceive robots and their pedagogical implications. Using a mixed-method approach and a Draw-And-Answer-Test, researchers analyzed drawings and written responses from 121 fourth-year students at the Faculty of Education, University of Belgrade: 75 future preschool teachers and 46 future primary school teachers. Two evaluators coded the data with very high agreement.

Most respondents correctly identified robots, while 22 showed misconceptions, most commonly depicting robots as ordinary electronic appliances. Future preschool teachers had more real-life experience with robots than future primary school teachers, largely connected to faculty coursework involving educational technologies.

The most common robot depictions were animal-shaped robots, especially Bee Bot and Mouse Bot, followed by typical robust-looking robots and mechanical objects. Most robots were shown without emotions, though many animal-like robots were depicted positively. Respondents most often associated robots with educational functions, followed by assistive functions. Preschool teacher students emphasized educational uses more strongly, while primary school teacher students gave similar importance to educational and assistive roles.

Most respondents gained robot experience at the Faculty of Education. Their reasons for depicting specific robots were most often linked to cognitive factors, such as practicality and educational usefulness, followed by affective interest and behavioral experience.

The study concludes that future teachers generally have accurate conceptions of robots, though some misconceptions remain. It recommends more frequent and purposeful integration of educational robots into teacher education, curriculum development based on a holistic approach, and continued development of digital and algorithmic competencies. It also stresses that successful robot use depends on teacher competence, robot quality, pedagogical strategies, inclusion, child safety, privacy protection, and equal access for all children.

Out-of-bounds situations are important and teams should practice inbounding from the baseline, sideline, and full court. The main goal is to inbound successfully, get the ball to top players, and create high-percentage shots. Plays should be simple, practiced, and based on vision, communication, timing, and reading defensive coverage. Players should know automatic options, such as cutting when defenders turn away, using give-and-go when the inbounder is unguarded, or lobbing when defenders face away from the passer. Teams should scout opponents’ out-of-bounds defenses and prepare counters. Players must also know key throw-in rules, including the five-second count, movement limits, baseline privileges after made baskets, backcourt passing rules, timeout timing, and violations involving defenders crossing the out-of-bounds plane.

The passage discusses Education 4.0 in the context of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, emphasizing the need to shift from rote learning to personalized, skill-based, and competency-based education. It highlights digital games and gamification as pedagogical tools recommended by India’s NEP 2020, noting their potential to support cognitive and non-cognitive skill development, motivation, engagement, problem solving, decision making, and higher-order thinking.

Digital Game-Based Learning can use commercial or customized games, with customized games better aligned to learning outcomes and assessment needs. Digital games can create multimodal learning environments and support learner-centered assessment through gameplay data.

The passage focuses on stealth assessment, an automated assessment approach embedded in digital games that collects learners’ digital traces during gameplay. Using AI, machine learning, and evidence-centered design, stealth assessment can assess competencies in real time, provide feedback, reduce test anxiety, and support tailored learning systems. Its development requires a multidisciplinary approach involving education, psychology, technology, programming, and statistics.

Challenges include limited teacher adoption, difficulty developing customized games, concerns about cognitive load, questions about brain effects, the need for appropriate difficulty levels, and the still-developing evidence base for the validity and reliability of digital game-based learning and assessment.

The lecture reviews experimental studies of neutrino oscillations and neutrino sources, including supernovae, Big Bang relics, cosmic ray showers, the sun, accelerator beamlines, and nuclear reactors. Different experiments probe oscillations using baseline length, neutrino energy, and sensitivity to mass-squared differences.

Solar neutrinos are produced in the sun with MeV-scale energies. Early experiments, including Homestake, observed fewer electron neutrinos than expected. The SNO experiment measured the total neutrino flux using neutral-current interactions and found agreement with theory, showing that solar neutrinos change flavor rather than disappear.

Atmospheric neutrinos arise from pion and kaon decays produced by cosmic rays in Earth’s atmosphere. Measurements showed deviations from the expected muon-to-electron neutrino ratio and clear disappearance of muon-like neutrinos, consistent with oscillations.

Accelerator experiments at facilities such as Fermilab, CERN, and in Japan use near and far detectors to measure flux and oscillation effects through appearance or disappearance. Reactor experiments study anti-electron-neutrino disappearance using inverse beta decay, with many experiments near reactors in countries including France, Japan, and China. These programs, especially since the 2000s, have provided extensive evidence and measurements of neutrino oscillations.

The paper argues that increasing AI regulation in the US and EU makes AI policy knowledge important for AI developers, but such topics remain largely absent from computer science curricula. It reviews the fragmented and politically volatile US AI policy landscape, including Biden’s rescinded EO 14110 and Trump’s EO 14179, and contrasts it with the EU AI Act’s risk-based regulatory framework and transparency requirements for general-purpose AI. The authors identify three key implications: rapid policy change, the challenge of translating abstract policy goals into technical requirements, and cross-border regulatory effects such as the potential influence of EU rules on US companies. They propose a framework for integrating AI policy into computing courses, organized by socio-political, translational, and technical perspectives, and by the dimensions of scope, power, and agency. The framework uses guiding questions to help students examine policy requirements, affected groups, technical implementation, responsibility, and opportunities for influence. Future work includes developing curricular activities and applying requirements engineering to translate AI policy principles into technical specifications.

A penalty kick during play is a restart, and the ball is live once kicked forward. Attacking players other than the kicker must be outside the penalty area, behind the mark, inside the field, and at least 10 yards from the mark until the kick is taken. They should position quickly, hold legal spots, and follow up rebounds or saves immediately. The kicker may play the ball again only after another player touches it, not after a rebound off the goal frame. If the goalkeeper secures the ball, attackers must transition to defense. Procedure violations by the kicker or teammates can lead to a retake or an indirect free kick.

The ADS868xW includes a programmable gain amplifier that converts single-ended or differential inputs for the SAR ADC, adjusts common-mode level, and supports selectable input ranges through RANGE_SEL bits. A second-order low-pass antialiasing filter at the PGA output typically has a 500kHz cutoff. An integrated ADC driver supports maximum sampling performance.

The device can use an internal or external 4.096V reference selected by INTREF_DIS. The internal reference requires REFIO decoupling and can shift with solder reflow or thermal stress; the external reference is applied at REFIO and buffered internally, with REFCAP decoupling required. The ADC supports single-ended and differential bipolar or unipolar inputs and outputs straight-binary conversion data.

Alarm functions include input and AVDD alarms on the multifunction ALARM pin when enabled. Input alarm thresholds and hysteresis are programmable, while AVDD alarm thresholds are fixed at 4.7V and 5.3V. Alarm flags can be read from ALARM_REG, output on the alarm pin, or appended to output data.

The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI, dual-SDO, source-synchronous read protocols, and daisy-chain operation for multiple devices. The device has RESET, ACQ, and CONV states controlled by RST and CONVST/CS. Data transfer frames begin on CONVST/CS falling edge and end on the rising edge, with 32-bit command and output shift-register operation. Short frames allow partial reads, and long frames use the last 32 input bits as the command.

Nine configuration registers control device ID, reset and power, SDI/SDO protocol, output data format, input range and reference, alarms, and alarm thresholds. Application guidance describes use in industrial analog input modules with an external multiplexer, programmable current or voltage channels, alarm hysteresis for thermistor sensing, AVDD and DVDD decoupling, NAP and power-down modes, and PCB layout practices separating analog and digital sections.

The study develops and experimentally validates a unified multiscale framework to predict GaN and III-nitride epitaxy growth kinetics from solid-melt interface energetics. Molecular dynamics simulations using machine-learning interatomic potentials show that liquid Ga forms ordered layers at GaN-Ga interfaces, with ordering and charge redistribution depending on polarity. Metadynamics simulations quantify free-energy landscapes for N adatom adsorption and migration, revealing that interfacial liquid Ga lowers N migration barriers compared with clean GaN surfaces, a mechanism described as “Ga lubrication.”

Calculated migration barriers are lower at liquid-covered interfaces than on clean surfaces, and step-edge simulations identify Ehrlich-Schwoebel barriers that can affect morphology. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations using these atomistic barriers show that high N flux produces rough joint-island growth, while lower flux produces diffusion-controlled layer-by-layer growth. Under typical MBE conditions, the authors predict diffusion-limited step-flow growth.

A diffusion-controlled growth model based on modified Fick’s law incorporates free-energy profiles, N diffusivity, and N solubility in liquid Ga to predict facet-dependent growth rates without fitted parameters. MBE experiments on partially nitridated Ga/GaN particles, analyzed by HAADF-STEM and HRTEM, confirm slow GaN growth and facet-dependent rates. Predicted rates of about 0.01–0.04 nm/s agree with experimental trends.

The work concludes that, for systems with low solubility of key elements such as N in liquid Ga, interfacial adsorption and migration free-energy profiles govern crystal growth kinetics and morphology. The framework is presented as transferable to other III-V/catalyst systems, while limitations include neglected impurities, machine-learning potential transferability, simplified transport assumptions, and experimental averaging over multiple facets.

The second defender provides support in defense after the first defender controls the opponent with the ball. They position behind and inside the first defender, stay goalside, maintain proper distance, avoid overrunning the play, and adjust as the attacker and first defender move. Their positioning helps force the dribbler outside toward the sideline. The support defender uses the same stance as the first defender and must communicate arrival with calls such as “support” or “you have help.” Once ready to cover if the first defender is beaten, they may tell the first defender to challenge or tackle. Practice should teach positioning, movement, stance, and communication, progressing from stationary setups to half-speed and full-speed play. Key communication includes calls to support, jockey, delay, contain, challenge, or tackle. If the first defender is beaten, the support defender may take over, possibly through a defensive switch.

The study compared air- and bone-conduction auditory brainstem response (ABR) and auditory steady-state response (ASSR) thresholds in infants aged 0–6 months with normal hearing or conductive hearing loss (CHL), using ABR as the gold standard. Sixty-four infants were recruited through a newborn hearing screening program; 50 completed testing. Thresholds were assessed mainly at 500 Hz and 2000 Hz, though no CHL was observed at 2000 Hz.

At 500 Hz, infants with CHL had significantly higher air-conduction ABR and ASSR thresholds than infants with normal hearing, while bone-conduction thresholds did not differ significantly between groups. ABR and ASSR thresholds were poorly correlated. Air-bone gaps were significantly larger in the CHL group than in the normal-hearing group for both ABR and ASSR, but ASSR showed more overlap between groups and greater variability. Minimum normal ASSR intensity levels were 40 dB HL for 500 Hz air conduction, 30 dB HL for 500 Hz bone conduction, and 40 dB HL for 2000 Hz air and bone conduction.

The study found that ABR better identified mild low-frequency CHL than ASSR under the tested conditions. ASSR thresholds and air-bone gaps were too variable to reliably separate normal hearing from mild CHL. The authors conclude that ABR should remain the primary diagnostic tool for infant hearing assessment in early hearing detection and intervention programs, and that more research is needed before ASSR can be considered for this role.
