The passage examines inclusive education and the role of legal frameworks and educational leaders’ awareness in implementing it in Addis Ababa inclusive education resource centers. Inclusive education is defined as providing equitable, meaningful, and flexible education for all learners, including students with disabilities. The study addresses a literature gap: prior Ethiopian research has focused mainly on barriers such as infrastructure, teacher preparedness, and resources, with less attention to legal frameworks and leaders’ awareness.

Using a qualitative case study design, the researchers purposively selected three inclusive education resource centers in Addis Ababa and interviewed 15 participants, including school principals, itinerant teachers, teachers, and Ministry of Education inclusion experts. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and document reviews, then analyzed thematically.

The study identified global frameworks such as the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Convention on the Rights of the Child, Salamanca Statement, Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, Marrakesh Treaty, and Sustainable Development Goals. Regional African frameworks included the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights, African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child, and African Disability Protocol. Ethiopian frameworks included the Constitution, Proclamation No. 1263/2021, Education and Training Policy 2023, Education Sector Development Plan VI, Special Needs/Inclusive Education Strategy, and National Children’s Policy.

Findings showed uneven awareness among educational leaders. Ministry of Education experts and itinerant teachers had relatively better knowledge of global, regional, and national frameworks, often due to training or special needs education backgrounds. School principals and classroom teachers showed limited awareness, despite recognizing the importance of including students with disabilities. Some teachers viewed inclusion mainly as compassion and fairness rather than as a rights-based practice guided by legal frameworks.

The study concludes that Ethiopia has a favorable legal and policy environment for inclusive education, but implementation depends on leaders’ awareness and capacity. It recommends regular professional development, integration of inclusive education policies into teacher training curricula, stronger alignment of local practice with international and regional standards, and Ministry of Education monitoring of policy awareness among school-level practitioners.

Microsoft Corporation filed a Form 8-K dated October 24, 2018, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2018. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Exchange Act unless specifically incorporated by reference.

NVIDIA Turing GPUs introduce a hybrid rendering model combining rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation. Dedicated RT Cores in each SM accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, offloading work from shaders and enabling real-time ray tracing on a single GPU when combined with denoising, BVH acceleration structures, and RTX-compatible APIs such as DXR, OptiX, NVIDIA RTX libraries, and Vulkan ray tracing. Turing ray tracing is described as up to 10 times faster than Pascal software ray tracing, with over 10 Giga Rays/sec using RT Cores.

Real-time ray tracing in Turing is used for shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections. Ray-traced shadows can provide hard edges and physically correct contact hardening, ray-traced ambient occlusion offers more realistic grounding than SSAO, and ray-traced reflections avoid limitations of screen-space reflections, cubemaps, and planar reflections. Denoising reduces the rays required per pixel while maintaining visual quality.

NVIDIA NGX is a Turing-only deep learning graphics stack using Tensor Cores and pretrained neural networks. Its features include DLSS, DLSS 2X, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS renders with fewer input samples and infers a target-resolution image similar in quality to TAA with roughly half the shading work, while DLSS 2X aims to approach 64x supersampling quality. AI Super Rez can upscale images or video by 2x, 4x, or 8x.

Turing adds Mesh Shading with Task Shaders and Mesh Shaders, enabling cooperative-thread geometry processing, reduced CPU draw-call bottlenecks, level-of-detail selection, and dynamic geometry manipulation. Variable Rate Shading lets developers vary shading rate per 16x16 pixel region or primitive, supporting content adaptive shading, motion adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility sampling from appearance shading by computing and reusing shading values in texture space.

Multi-View Rendering allows multiple viewpoints or instances to be rendered in a single pass, with Turing supporting up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 API-level views. It extends Pascal’s SMP and supports VR stereo rendering, canted displays, cascaded shadow maps, and multi-instance rendering. Turing also supports VirtualLink over USB-C, improved VR rendering features, and RT Core acceleration for VRWorks Audio.

The TU104 GPU includes up to six GPCs, 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and second-generation NVLink, and is used in products such as GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. Tesla T4 uses a TU104 configuration for inferencing with 2560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores. TU106, used in GeForce RTX 2070, includes 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but does not support NVLink or SLI.

The passage defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering that weights Tensor, FP32, RT Core, and INT32 operations according to estimated frame-time usage. It also explains ray tracing basics, including reverse ray casting from the camera, BVH acceleration, BVH building and refitting, and denoising as a way to improve performance and image quality.

Surmodics VP Charles W. Olson sold 1,201 shares at $26.00 each for $31,226 and now owns 27,386 shares. The company recently traded at $25.40, with a market cap of $335.46 million. Surmodics reported quarterly EPS of $0.26 on revenue of $18.20 million, above analyst expectations. Institutional investors own 87.45% of shares, and analysts have issued mixed ratings, including downgrades by Sidoti, Barrington Research, and TheStreet, and an upgrade by Zacks. Surmodics provides surface modification and in vitro diagnostic technologies to the healthcare industry.

Oprah Winfrey told Vogue she experienced six weeks of depression after the 1998 film Beloved underperformed at the box office. She said gratitude helped her cope and taught her not to place all expectations on box office results. She will appear in A Wrinkle in Time.

Xiaomi launched the Mi Band 3 at its annual product event in Shenzhen, China. The fitness tracker succeeds the Mi Band 2 and features a 0.78-inch OLED capacitive display, app and call notifications, motion tracking, health management, waterproofing up to 50m, and up to 20 days of battery life. It is priced at Yuan 169, around Rs 1,780. The device launched alongside products including the Mi 8, MIUI 10, Mi TV 4 75-inch, and Mi VR Standalone.

WIRED lists leftover deals still available after Amazon’s fall Prime Day sale, updated October 9, 2025, after removing inactive offers. The roundup highlights discounted tech and home products tested or approved by WIRED reviewers, including tablets, laptops, storage, smart speakers, chargers, power stations, cameras, monitors, phones, security cameras, smart locks, pet tech, scooters, TVs, soundbars, speakers, headphones, fitness trackers, kitchen appliances, vacuums, air purifiers, bedding, grooming tools, gaming gear, board games, and baby monitors. Featured deals include Apple iPads, GoPro cameras, Microsoft Surface laptops, MacBooks, Google Pixel devices, Samsung phones, JBL speakers, Bose headphones, Fitbit trackers, Ninja and Breville appliances, Dyson and Coway home products, and the Nanit Pro baby monitor. The passage also explains that Prime Day is a members-only Amazon sale, that the fall event ran from October 7 through October 8, and that WIRED is selecting deals by checking discounts on products it has tested and approved.

Yoga and fitness have become increasingly connected, with many options now available for fitness enthusiasts, recreational athletes and professionals. Yoga can support breathing, meditation, concentration, flexibility, balance, injury prevention, rehabilitation, strength, stability and stress reduction. Choosing a class depends on personal goals, training needs and intention.

Hatha yoga is an umbrella term for physical yoga styles common in the West. Popular styles include Ashtanga Vinyasa, a rigorous set sequence emphasizing strength, flexibility and stamina; Vinyasa or Flow, which links movement and breath in varied sequences; Iyengar, which emphasizes alignment and uses props therapeutically; Bikram and Hot Yoga, practised in hot, humid rooms; Yin Yoga, which holds poses to release connective tissue tension; Restorative Yoga, which uses props for slower passive stretching; and Kripalu, a gentle style focused on meditation and the mind-body connection.

Specialty yoga classes for runners, cyclists, golfers and other athletes address activity-specific stresses, muscle imbalances and injury prevention. The passage advises choosing gentler therapeutic styles when training hard and complementary styles to balance other activities. Heavens Fitness and Yoga Studio is hosting a free Outdoor Yoga Picnic on June 21 for International Yoga Day, with donations accepted for Brown Bagging for Calgary Kids.

Dundee & Angus College hairdressing and beauty therapy students won seven golds at the Scottish finals of the AHT Competition, along with eight runner-up places and six third-place finishes. Darcie Westland won Student of the Year in her first competition. Students from Arbroath, Kingsway and other local areas placed across categories including beauty care, bridal, hair styling, barbering, nail art, fantasy look and team presentation.

The President submits extracts on Texas’s condition and explains why the Executive has not recognized its independence. He argues that recognizing a new state is delicate, especially when it has separated from a country still claiming it, and that U.S. policy has been to avoid interference and recognize governments only when their independence is clearly established. Although Texas has expelled Mexican authority and formed a government, Mexico is preparing another invasion, leaving Texas’s independence uncertain. Because Texas has close ties to the United States and seeks annexation after recognition, early acknowledgment could appear self-interested. The President recommends continued caution until events prove Texas can maintain sovereignty, while leaving the final judgment to Congress.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 28, 2016, announcing its first quarter 2016 financial results. The filing incorporates a press release, non-GAAP financial measure information, and segment financial information as exhibits. Amazon began allocating stock-based compensation and other operating expense/income to segment results in Q1 2016, with historical 2015 and 2014 segment results provided. Consolidated net sales, operating income/loss, and net income/loss were not affected.

The government shutdown prevented release of the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ monthly jobs report and weekly jobless claims data. Nongovernment indicators suggest the September labor market remained stable but weak, with expected payroll growth of 51,000 and unemployment around 4.3%. Hiring is uneven: health care remains strong while other fields, including software development, lag. Job postings are down from a year ago, and job seekers are taking longer to find work. ADP reported job losses in September and August, while Goldman Sachs estimated initial jobless claims at 224,000. Spending data from Bank of America and Fiserv remained solid, though small business hiring indicators showed weakness.

The passage introduces a stochastic differential equation approach for modeling nanoscale light-matter interactions in quantum photonics, aiming to bridge quantum emitter dynamics with classical Maxwell electromagnetic solvers. Existing exact quantum methods become computationally prohibitive for complex systems, while semiclassical methods cannot fully capture quantum correlations and photon statistics. The proposed stochastic Bloch-vector method avoids wave-function unraveling, phase-space representations, and operator-valued noise, and is validated using the Mollow spectrum of a strongly driven two-level system. The work also addresses limitations of conventional SDE derivations by allowing complex, non-symmetric diffusion matrices to represent asymmetric noise correlations from non-commuting quantum operators.

News affecting Czech markets included a jump in Czech crown volatility hedging amid speculation the central bank may remove its currency cap, a 14.2% rise in first-quarter new car registrations, progress toward a Prague extradition hearing for a Russian accused of hacking LinkedIn, and RWE considering selling Hungarian power assets. Press reports said Mero seeks more oil exports via the TAL pipeline, the Czech cabinet backed Prisko’s 80 million crown bid for insolvent miner OKD despite a higher Alcentra offer, and Prague Airport plans 27 billion crowns in capacity investments.

Chefs’ Warehouse is presented as a premium-growth stock trading at 33.3x forward P/E, with a FY2027 target price of $79.3 implying 36% upside. EPS is forecast to grow at a 16.7% CAGR through 2028, supported by 8.4% revenue growth, margin expansion, pricing power, and exposure to luxury restaurants and hotels. The author discloses no position in the stock and no compensation beyond Seeking Alpha.

The speaker says the team accepts Chris Pronger’s one-game suspension for a hit to Dean McAmmond’s head, though he describes it as a reaction play. He argues Chris Neil’s hit on Andy McDonald was more dangerous, deliberate, and deserving of a hearing despite McDonald not being injured. He says the team is physical, not dirty, does not blame officials for missed calls, and believes the league can still impose supplemental discipline. He emphasizes the need to address head shots while preserving body contact in North American hockey.

Saudi Arabia approved the University of New Haven to open a branch campus in Riyadh, which the university expects to launch next fall and grow to 13,000 students within a decade. President Jens Frederiksen said the move reflects Saudi Arabia’s shift toward bringing international institutions into the country and supports Vision 2030 economic goals. Other universities are also pursuing Saudi branch campuses, while some institutions have built research, consulting and financial ties there.

New Haven has longstanding Saudi ties, including private education for the royal family and a controversial partnership with King Fahd Security College, which continued after Jamal Khashoggi’s killing. The Riyadh campus plans to teach in English, offer preparatory and ESL programs, and include colleges focused on business, engineering and applied sciences. University officials said it will be coeducational and they do not foresee academic freedom restrictions. The university still needs approval from its accreditor.

The President transmits departmental reports responding to a Senate resolution and explains that he left the existing military commandant in California exercising civil authority because Congress had not established a territorial government. He sent Thomas Butler King and other officers to California and New Mexico with instructions, encouraged the people to form state constitutions for congressional consideration, but denied authorizing executive interference in their domestic institutions or conventions. He lacks information on California laws or censuses. He favored early state applications to reduce national agitation over territorial slavery, arguing that domestic institutions should be settled by states themselves. He recommends admitting California if its proposed constitution meets constitutional requirements. He notes Texas’s claim to part of New Mexico and urges Congress to devise an adjustment, while questioning the expediency of creating a territorial government before resolving the boundary. He opposes imposing conditions on California’s admission affecting its domestic institutions and urges avoiding unnecessary controversy to preserve harmony and the Union.

The speaker says their team spent too much time in its own end, struggled to forecheck with speed, and failed to gain momentum after a bad first period, while praising the opponent’s strong backchecking.

NASA Glenn Research Center in Cleveland is using the Glenn Extreme Environments Rig, or GEER, to replicate Venus’ surface conditions for research. The chamber can recreate the planet’s extreme heat, pressure and carbon dioxide atmosphere. In an 80-day test, rock and mineral samples from Case Western Reserve University were chemically altered, helping researchers study how materials survive on Venus. NASA engineers are also testing electronics, including a durable computer chip that operated for 21 days in the simulator, a major step toward longer Venus missions. Scientists say Venus’ harsh surface, acidic clouds and runaway greenhouse history make it difficult to explore, but studying it may help researchers understand Earth’s climate and investigate possible life in its upper atmosphere.

Work has begun on a £252 million resource recovery centre at Avonmouth, built by Viridor with the Somerset Waste Partnership. Due to be fully operational in 2020, it will convert Somerset’s non-recyclable household waste into electricity for the National Grid, enough to power 44,000 West Country homes, while reducing landfill use. The launch will coincide with expanded kerbside recycling collections. Viridor says the process is controlled, emissions will meet European standards, and the Environment Agency will continually regulate compliance.

SEV-ES and SEV-SNP encrypt guest register state during world switches, preventing direct hypervisor access. The document standardizes the 4 KB decrypted Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB), Non-Automatic Exit handling, required guest state exposure, and special behaviors such as NMI handling and SMP booting.

Version 2 adds SEV-SNP support, hypervisor feature advertisement, GHCB protocol enhancements, restricted APIC emulation, and revised handling for CPUID, shared buffers, and feature negotiation. Later revisions add 64-bit guest request sequence numbers, VLEK GUID support, APIC ID list retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, Page State Change support for SEV-ES, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, updated debug behavior, and GHCB unregister support.

The GHCB MSR protocol supports protocol negotiation, encryption-bit discovery, CPUID requests, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration and unregistration, Page State Change requests, Run VMPL requests, feature bitmap retrieval, and guest termination requests. SEV-SNP guests must register a GHCB GPA before first use.

NAE handling requires guests to populate GHCB fields and VALID_BITMAP entries before VMGEXIT, while hypervisors return results and errors through SW_EXITINFO fields. Supported events include IO, MSR, VMMCALL, MMIO, Page State Change, SNP Guest Request, SNP Extended Guest Request, AP Creation, #HV doorbell page, #HV IPI, #HV timer, APIC ID list, SNP Run VMPL, SNP TIO Guest Request, Secure AVIC, and termination request.

The document also defines SEV-SNP secrets page guest-reserved fields, an EFI Confidential Computing Blob table for secrets and CPUID pages, certificate return formats for extended requests, trusted I/O request data handling, Secure AVIC backing page registration, SMP booting methods, AP Creation for SEV-SNP, NMI completion behavior, debug register virtualization rules, and states that SMM and nested virtualization are not supported. Restricted Injection uses a shared #HV doorbell page with pending-event and EOI-assist fields to deliver interrupts and non-maskable events.

The passage argues that the OxyChem deal has a greater impact on Occidental Petroleum than on Berkshire Hathaway. Jed Lowrie and Matt Olson added RBI doubles, while Santiago Casilla earned his first save. Adrian Beltre drove in both Texas runs but injured his left hamstring.

Victims described a culture of fear, intimidation, violence and sexual abuse. Cooper was denied bail despite health issues and remanded in custody pending sentencing.

Maya Kodes, a holographic virtual pop star created by Montreal’s Neweb Labs, has released a dance-pop song, performed 30 concerts and gained 5,500 Facebook followers. She will livestream a June 13 VIP performance to launch her EP, with a Toronto performance expected before year’s end.

Mike Modano’s ligament issue cannot worsen, but his ability to shoot, pass, take faceoffs, and handle key defensive situations will determine whether he plays. Ed Belfour’s past physical and mental struggles, including a serious back injury, improved after treatment and daily maintenance. A study found that women preferred the body odor of men who ate more fruits and vegetables, while men who ate more carbohydrates had less appealing odor. Researchers assessed young men’s diets using skin carotenoid measurements and food questionnaires, then had women rate sweat from T-shirts worn during exercise. Meat intake did not make odor more or less attractive but tended to make it more intense. Other research has also linked diet and body odor, though experts note the relationship is indirect: sweat itself is not smelly until bacteria on the skin metabolize compounds from sweat glands.

The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act.

A Mac Otakara rumor claims Apple’s upcoming iPhone 8, possibly called “iPhone Edition,” may feature an Apple Watch-inspired polished stainless steel frame between glass panels, an under-display Touch ID sensor, and vertically positioned dual cameras potentially for VR or augmented reality. The report is based on alleged design verification documents and remains unconfirmed.

This study evaluates strategies for developing machine learning potentials for material surfaces using a MACE universal interatomic potential as the foundation model. It compares training from scratch, zero-shot prediction, fine-tuning, and multi-head fine-tuning across unary Au, binary RuO₂, and ternary BiVO₄ surface systems.

Fine-tuned models consistently outperformed models trained from scratch at the same training-data sizes and often achieved comparable or better accuracy with far fewer data. For Au surfaces, fine-tuning with only 40 configurations substantially reduced energy and force errors relative to zero-shot prediction, and models trained from scratch showed less reliable diatomic potential behavior. For RuO₂, fine-tuning also reduced errors, though force prediction was more difficult due to the greater complexity of the binary oxide system. For BiVO₄, fine-tuning produced the lowest force errors and reduced high-force outliers compared with zero-shot and from-scratch models.

Diatomic potential analyses showed that models trained from scratch often produced unphysical short-range or long-range behavior, while fine-tuned models generally gave more physically reasonable curves. The study also found that conventional fine-tuning can reduce generalizability to other systems, as a model fine-tuned only on Au surfaces performed worse on Ag, Cu, Pt, and Ir surfaces than the original foundation model.

Multi-head fine-tuning, which trains on both original bulk data and surface data, mitigated catastrophic forgetting and improved out-of-domain surface-energy predictions for other unary metal surfaces. However, it increased computational cost and slightly reduced accuracy on the specific Au surface dataset compared with standard fine-tuning.

The authors conclude that fine-tuning efficiently improves surface-property predictions using limited data, while multi-head fine-tuning is useful when preserving foundation-model performance and improving specialized-domain accuracy are both required.

The article examines trauma-informed human rights education (TIHRE) in higher education, arguing that human rights teaching often remains legally focused and insufficiently prepared to address contemporary threats, politically sensitive histories, and the risk of retraumatising students with lived or intergenerational trauma. It defines trauma-informed HRE as teaching grounded in dignity, respect, equality, inclusion, safety, trust, collaboration, empowerment, and awareness of cultural, historical, and gendered contexts.

Using a structured review of interdisciplinary literature, the article identifies three main priorities. First, educators should develop a rights-respecting teaching persona through values clarification, self-awareness, and recognition of bias, privilege, and personal motivations. Second, course design should embed trauma-sensitive principles through student co-creation, project-based learning, skills development, reflective practice, and careful handling of potentially distressing material. Third, dialogic teaching should create respectful, participatory spaces where students engage with peers, practitioners, and survivors.

The article concludes that trauma-informed human rights teaching can reduce risks of retraumatisation, support wellbeing, and move learners from avoidance or apathy toward agency, advocacy, and action for human rights.

IDC’s white paper examines how high-performance computing (HPC), simulation, modeling, and data analysis support innovation in manufacturing. Industrial enterprises face geopolitical uncertainty, rising energy costs, raw material shortages, supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, and sustainability demands while digitalization reshapes value creation.

Simulation, modeling, and analytics are used to accelerate product development, improve quality, reduce costs, support decisions, and optimize production. Three-quarters of surveyed decision makers see innovation as a key objective, while 57% view these tools as important for improving product and service quality. Around half already use them in product development, production planning, and quality management, with deployment expected to rise significantly within two years. However, data silos and inconsistent information bases limit their effectiveness, making integrated data sources and a “single source of truth” important.

The paper highlights technologies such as CAD, CAM, CAE, 3D displays, virtual prototyping, digital twins, high-performance data analytics, AR/VR, and engineering workstations as a service. These enable virtual testing, design optimization, digital validation, feedback loops using IoT and sensor data, and potential new digital products, services, and business models.

Complex simulations require significant computing power, and many enterprises face trade-offs between calculation speed and accuracy. Half of respondents say iterations and calculations take too long, while 42% use simulations that are outdated or inaccurate. Demand for high-performance calculations is expected to increase sharply.

HPC enables complex calculations, improves simulation quality and speed, supports more iterations, unlocks new use cases, and increases innovation and agility. Four out of five respondents see HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation. More than a quarter already use professional HPC infrastructures, while 39% are planning or piloting deployment.

Current HPC use faces challenges including infrastructure choice, security, cost, energy consumption, and sustainability. Most HPC users prefer external infrastructures such as cloud providers, many use or plan colocation datacenters, and fewer operate on-premises HPC systems. Security concerns are cited by 72% of respondents, while 58% identify high energy use and sustainability as key issues.

The paper studies whether textual “soft” information in earnings press releases predicts stock returns on earnings announcement days. Using 138,676 press-release observations from 2005–2023, with a main analysis sample of 134,354 releases from 2006–2023, the authors combine earnings surprises from IBES, returns from CRSP and TAQ, and press releases from SEC EDGAR.

The study compares NLP methods including BKMX topic modeling, online LDA, BERT, MPNET, and FinBERT. It uses rolling-window training to avoid look-ahead bias and evaluates predictive power with regressions and SHAP values. Earnings surprise alone explains 3.3% of announcement-day return variation. Adding press-release text raises explanatory power up to 4.4%, with FinBERT providing the strongest soft-information signal. SHAP analysis shows FinBERT-based soft information can be as important as, or more important than, earnings surprise.

Topic analysis finds that financial performance, financial metrics, sector-specific news, and market/economic factors are important textual themes. The authors report evidence consistent with self-serving bias: companies discuss internal financial performance more positively when results are favorable and external or sector factors more negatively when results are unfavorable.

A trading test finds that strategies using public press-release signals after market open do not generate profits and mainly incur transaction costs, supporting market efficiency. However, if earnings surprises and press-release content are available before release, combining hard and soft information improves identification of top and bottom performing stocks. Precision@10 rises from roughly 0.25–0.36 using either signal separately to about 0.44–0.52 when the signals agree.

The paper concludes that earnings press releases contain economically meaningful soft information comparable to earnings surprises, that FinBERT is the strongest predictive model, and that topic models improve interpretability.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark short-term interest rate by a quarter point to 1 percent to 1.25 percent, its fourth hike in 18 months, and signaled one more increase this year if the economy remains solid. The move typically raises rates on credit card debt, home equity lines and some adjustable-rate mortgages, increasing costs for borrowers. Bankrate.com estimates that four hikes since December 2015 add about $700 in payments over the life of a $5,000 credit card balance paid at the monthly minimum.

Fixed mortgage rates and auto loans have changed little because long-term mortgages generally track the 10-year Treasury yield rather than the Fed’s rate. Mortgage rates remain low by historical standards. Higher U.S. rates can attract overseas investment, strengthen the dollar, make U.S. exports costlier and draw capital from developing countries.

Consumers with weaker credit may pay more, especially on used-car financing. Savers may see slightly higher returns at some smaller banks, though average CD rates remain low. Retirees invested in bonds are advised by Doug Amis to stay balanced between short- and long-term bonds rather than shift strategies.

A UCLA study by Gregory Okin estimated that meat-based food for America’s 163 million dogs and cats, along with their waste, produces the equivalent of about 64 million tons of carbon dioxide annually, comparable to 13.6 million cars. The study says pets account for 25 to 30 percent of the environmental impact of U.S. meat consumption. Okin said he is not urging vegetarian diets for pets but wants owners to consider climate impacts, especially with high-protein premium foods. UC Davis professor Frank Mitloehner noted pet food mostly uses rendered livestock byproducts that might otherwise be wasted. The passage also discusses debate over vegan pet diets, with some advocates citing healthy dogs, while many veterinarians warn against plant-based diets, particularly for cats needing taurine.

The Vegas Golden Knights will build their first roster through the NHL expansion draft, selecting one unprotected player from each of 30 teams. Teams must submit protected lists by Saturday, with selections announced June 21. The passage invites readers to create a protected list for the Calgary Flames and predict Vegas’s choice.

U.S. government bond prices fell Friday, pushing yields higher, after a jobs report showed stronger wage growth despite the first monthly job losses since 2010. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 2.370%, while the two-year yield climbed to 1.511%, with both rising for a fourth straight week. The economy lost 33,000 jobs, unemployment fell to 4.2%, and average hourly earnings rose 2.9%. Traders viewed wage gains as potentially inflationary and largely attributed payroll declines to hurricanes. Fed-funds futures showed an 88% chance of a December rate increase. Yields were also influenced by geopolitical concerns and upcoming Treasury debt auctions.

Steven Kean forwarded an “Enron Mentions” email containing several news articles. The Wall Street Journal reported on three small bidders for Strategic Petroleum Reserve oil; Renard Euell sought Enron as a partner, but Enron said no deal existed, while Ronald Peek transferred his interest to Hess. The Washington Post noted Enron Broadband Services invested in Artesia Technologies’ $26 million funding round. Houston Chronicle articles discussed Houston’s proposed downtown basketball arena, citing Enron Field’s development impact and Ken Lay’s support as co-chairman of the pro-arena campaign, while analyzing public costs, taxpayer benefits, and comparisons with other NBA arena deals.

The University of Notre Dame received two gifts totaling $205 million. Matthew and Joyce Walsh donated $150 million to the School of Architecture, which will be renamed for them. Francis and Kathleen Rooney made a gift to endow the Notre Dame Democracy Initiative, which promotes scholarship and dialogue on American democracy.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting results from its February 13, 2018 Annual Meeting of Shareholders. Shareholders elected James Bell, Tim Cook, Al Gore, Bob Iger, Andrea Jung, Art Levinson, Ron Sugar, and Sue Wagner as directors. They approved ratification of Ernst & Young LLP as independent registered public accounting firm for 2018, approved executive compensation on an advisory basis, and approved the amended and restated Apple Inc. Non-Employee Director Stock Plan. Shareholder proposals titled “Shareholder Proxy Access Amendments” and “Human Rights Committee” were not approved. The amended stock plan was filed as Exhibit 10.1.

North Park Elementary School in San Bernardino reopened a week after Cedric Anderson killed his estranged wife, teacher Karen Smith, and 8-year-old Jonathan Martinez before fatally shooting himself. A wounded 9-year-old student had been released from the hospital. Students returned to supportive signs, prayers, counselors and tightened security. Superintendent Dale Marsden said reopening was the first step toward healing.

The passage argues that Apple should let users teach Siri new words, pronunciations, nicknames, meanings, and command analogues. It says this could improve Siri’s handling of individual speech, vernacular, contacts, reminders, and photo searches, while allowing repeated user input to inform broader machine learning. The author criticizes Siri’s current nickname and language limitations and urges Apple to make Siri more capable of learning.

Amsterdam’s Buiksloterham docklands are being regenerated through an experimental, sustainable approach centered on De Ceuvel, a temporary co-working hub made from renovated houseboats on a polluted former shipyard. The site uses phytoremedial plants to clean soil, composting toilets, waste reuse, aquaponics, renewable energy, and a solar-based local currency called Jouliettes to encourage efficient power use. After ten years, De Ceuvel is intended to be dismantled, leaving cleaner land for future use. The wider area promotes eco-homes and aims to become highly sustainable. The project responds to costly conventional docklands regeneration, which often requires expensive soil removal and leads to luxury developments that price out local communities. De Ceuvel offers a lower-cost, circular, and more inclusive alternative.

Kilauea’s eruption, ongoing for 27 days, has sent lava through southeastern Hawaii communities and volcanic haze as far as Guam, where residents with respiratory issues were advised to stay indoors. On Hawaii’s Big Island, fast-moving lava from Fissure 8 threatened Leilani Estates, Lanipuna Gardens and Kapoho, with fountains reaching over 200 feet and flows moving about 600 yards per hour. Officials warned of volcanic glass fibers, high sulfur dioxide emissions, vog, poor air quality and possible isolation from lava. Since May 3, about 22 fissures have opened, at least 40 homes have been destroyed, more than 2,000 acres covered by lava, and about 200 people are in shelters.

Peel Regional Police say they have credible information that three men filmed assaulting a 29-year-old autistic man at Square One in Mississauga may be originally from British Columbia’s Lower Mainland and recently travelled to the GTA. Investigators are asking people in Vancouver-area communities to view the surveillance video and help identify them. The victim remains shaken, and police continue to seek tips through Peel police, local police, or Crime Stoppers.

The passage evaluates whether the RSI indicator works for Bitcoin and cryptocurrency trading. RSI measures the speed and magnitude of price movements on a 0–100 scale. Backtests from January 2015 to September 2021 found that RSI mean reversion strategies, such as buying low RSI readings and selling high readings, performed weakly on Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Dogecoin. However, RSI used as a momentum indicator produced much better results. One Bitcoin example using RSI(5) crossing above and below 50 showed higher CAGR than buy and hold and lower drawdowns. The passage concludes that RSI does not work well for crypto mean reversion, but appears useful as a momentum indicator.

Arkansas inmate Don Davis had his last meal while courts considered stays affecting planned executions. The state attorney general asked the US Supreme Court to overturn an Arkansas Supreme Court stay, while the 8th Circuit reversed a federal ruling that had halted all eight executions.

The passage introduces SpinGPT, an LLM-based agent for Spin & Go poker tournaments. Poker’s incomplete information, flexible bet sizes, and tournament dynamics make exhaustive search and chip EV maximization inadequate. Prior AI progress relied heavily on CFR-based methods, achieving strong results in heads-up and multiplayer poker, while earlier LLM poker efforts were limited by weak training data.

SpinGPT uses Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and a two-stage training pipeline. First, it is supervised fine-tuned on 320,000 professional decisions from 8,800 high-stakes Spin & Go games played on PartyPoker.fr between 2018 and 2020. Hand histories are anonymized, parsed into structured prompts, and trained with LoRA. Second, it is refined with offline reinforcement learning using ORPO on 270,000 InstaGTO solver-generated hands plus 50,000 human hands to align decisions toward game-theoretic play.

On a professional test set, SpinGPT-SFT achieved 80% exact accuracy, 84% tolerant accuracy, and 86% macro F1. After reinforcement learning, SpinGPT scored 79% exact accuracy, 83% tolerant accuracy, and 84% macro F1 on professional data, while improving bet-size MAE from 0.61 BB to 0.30 BB. On solver data, SpinGPT reached 72% exact accuracy, 78% tolerant accuracy, and 77% macro F1.

In gameplay, SpinGPT-SFT, with a simple all-in heuristic patch, achieved 13.4 ± 12.9 BB/100 over 30,000 hands against Slumbot. In a 10,000-hand duplicate match at 25 BB, SpinGPT beat SpinGPT-SFT by 13.2 ± 7.24 BB/100, indicating improvement from reinforcement learning. Limitations include mismatched benchmarking, lack of Slumbot evaluation for the final model, and LLM numerical errors. Future work includes stronger models, better data, retrieval of GTO charts, chain-of-thought prompting, opponent adaptation, explainability, and coupling LLMs with solvers.

A global learning crisis, worsened by school closures, climate change, conflict and economic slowdown, costs an estimated US$129 billion annually. Youth face high unemployment, with 20 percent not in employment, education or training in 2023, two-thirds of them young women. Employers report skills shortages, and educational mismatch affects many young workers in lower-income countries.

The Global Partnership for Education supports partner countries through policy dialogue, advocacy, financing and partnerships to build inclusive education systems that strengthen foundational learning and 21st century skills such as creativity, problem solving, collaboration, analytical thinking, resilience and adaptability. GPE promotes public-private partnerships to align curricula with labor market needs.

Examples include funding and education sector collaboration in Lesotho, a planned $40 million foundational learning investment in Ghana, a competency-based curriculum in Kenya, socio-emotional skills training in El Salvador, and assessment tools developed through GPE initiatives.

The manuscript argues for the value of quantitative criticalism in education research and aims to guide scholars using quantitative methods and critical perspectives. It emphasizes that quantitative research is not objective, since researchers’ identities, assumptions, and positionalities shape their work. The authors provide their own positionalities to show how lived experiences inform their approaches to studying queer and trans students, Asian American data disaggregation, institutional research, equity, and social justice.

Quantitative criticalism combines quantitative methods with critical epistemologies, rejecting the idea that numbers are neutral and focusing on systemic oppression rather than individual deficits. The manuscript states that justice-driven quantitative research should inform all stages of a project, including research questions, positionality, measurement, sampling, data collection, analysis, interpretation, and implications. It also stresses community partnership, data sovereignty, transparency in collaborations, and solidarity among scholars.

The manuscript identifies tensions in quantitative criticalism, including the historical ties between statistics and white supremacy, unclear thresholds for what counts as “critical,” and methodological difficulties in measuring identity, intersectionality, and systems of oppression. It notes challenges with essentialist demographic variables, small or underrepresented samples, generalizability, deficit-based comparisons, and the limitations of traditional statistical assumptions.

The authors review examples using critical race theory, queer theory, and intersectionality. These studies illustrate how critical frameworks can shape quantitative research questions, scale development, identity categorization, within-group analysis, interaction effects, and latent class analysis, while also revealing limits related to categorization, generalizability, sample composition, and instrument design.

The manuscript’s implications urge researchers and instructors to integrate epistemology with methods, reflect on intentions and positionalities, avoid simple judgments about criticality, and consider how quantitative criticalism can advance equity and justice. It closes by calling for critical reflection, coalition building, and the use of quantitative methods to challenge oppression and support collective liberation.

The MACD-histogram trading strategy is a mean-reversion system used to identify momentum changes and potential reversal points. The MACD Histogram shows the difference between the MACD line and signal line; bars above zero indicate bullish momentum, while bars below zero indicate bearish momentum. The tested strategy enters on the close and exits on the first day the close is higher than the previous close, with the short setup reversed. Long positions performed better than short positions. Across 77 liquid ETFs, the strategy generated 6,669 trades and was in cash most of the time. A Nasdaq 100 test using the 2x leveraged QLD ETF from 2007 produced 85 trades, a 2.2% average gain, 10.4% annual returns, 5% market exposure, and a 19% max drawdown.

The passage lists weight-loss habits it says may be harmful or counterproductive, including drinking from plastic bottles, cutting out sweets completely, being overly self-critical, emotional eating, consuming store-bought protein bars and energy drinks, eating sweets outside pre-workout periods, and surrounding oneself with unsupportive people. It advises against relying only on scales, meal-replacement supplements, eliminating carbs, eating only fat-free products, sleeping too little, eating too little while exercising more, repeating the same workout routine for weeks, drinking calories instead of eating meals, restricting the diet too quickly, and copying someone else’s weight-loss plan. It recommends moderation, whole foods, healthy fats and carbs, sufficient sleep, varied workouts, gradual dietary changes, and routines suited to one’s own body.

Nokia’s updated 3310 announcement generated interest in feature phones, which are used as secondary devices or to reduce smartphone use. The passage lists options including Nokia 216 (Rs 2,536) with camera, MP3 player, torch, internet and long battery life; Samsung Metro 350 (Rs 2,780) with 2MP camera and 1200 mAh battery; Nokia 230 (Rs 4,799) as a premium non-smartphone; Intex Yaari (Rs 799) for basic calls; Nokia 3310, expected around Rs 4,000; Micromax X408 with dual SIM under Rs 1,000; Samsung Guru E1200 (Rs 1,200) with flashlight; and Nokia 105 (Rs 1,310) for basic calling.

Onesmo Rupil, 23, began using drugs at 17 and was discontinued from the University of Dodoma in 2013 due to poor performance linked to substance abuse. Now recovered, he manages Philimisana Foundation Sober House in Mwanza, which rehabilitates about 30 young people, mostly marijuana users. He says marijuana is widely used locally, though harmful to the brain.

Rupil says his drug use began in secondary school and attributes part of his vulnerability to growing up in boarding schools with limited parental care. He later moved from marijuana to heroin, spent large sums on it, and stole laptops at Udom to fund his addiction. He was arrested in 2015, charged with stealing over 200 laptops, and detained at Isanga Prison, where his recovery began. He later received rehabilitation in Dar es Salaam.

Dr Kassian Nyandindi of Muhimbili National Hospital says 2014 research found 550,000 people affected by drug abuse in Tanzania, with about 25,000 addicts and only 3,500 receiving methadone treatment in Dar es Salaam. He says marijuana can damage the brain and that many youths in rehabilitation develop mental disorders after abusing it.

The study developed and evaluated an automated guideline adherence monitoring system for intensive care that uses FHIR-encoded computer-interpretable clinical recommendations and OMOP CDM-formatted patient data. Six guideline recommendations, mainly related to COVID-19 and ARDS care, were selected from intensive care guidelines, encoded in FHIR, and applied to data transformed from five university hospitals covering 82,015 intensive care episodes from January 2020 to May 2023.

Validation in three hospitals compared system outputs with physician reviews and expert-established ground truth. The system achieved 97.0% accuracy, exceeding human reviewers’ 86.6% accuracy, and processed more than 2,000 patient days per second compared with about 30 seconds per patient-day-recommendation for manual review. Most discrepancies were due to human reviewer errors; system errors were mainly caused by relevant information stored as unstructured free text not transferred into OMOP CDM.

Automated adherence analysis showed variation by recommendation and hospital, with many adherence rates between 10% and 60%. The authors identified incomplete documentation, evolving COVID-19 recommendations, and imprecise guideline wording as factors affecting adherence measurement. The study concludes that combining FHIR-encoded guidelines with OMOP-formatted data enables scalable, accurate, and efficient guideline adherence monitoring across healthcare institutions.

NVIDIA Turing GPUs introduce a new display engine supporting higher resolutions, faster refresh rates, HDR, DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, VESA DSC 1.2, tone mapping based on ITU-R BT.2100, and 8K output over USB-C. Updated NVENC supports H.265 8K encoding at 30 fps with bitrate savings for HEVC and H.264, while NVDEC supports HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit and VP9 10/12-bit HDR decoding.

Turing adds USB Type-C and VirtualLink hardware support to simplify VR headset connectivity by carrying power, display, and data through one USB-C connector. TU102 and TU104 replace older SLI interfaces with second-generation NVLink, enabling higher GPU-to-GPU bandwidth for two-way SLI, while 3-way and 4-way SLI are not supported.

A major Turing feature is real-time ray tracing using RT Cores in TU102, TU104, and TU106 GPUs with NVIDIA RTX software. RT Cores accelerate BVH traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, offloading shader multiprocessors and enabling hybrid rendering that combines rasterization with ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, and other effects. NVIDIA states Turing can reach 10+ Giga Rays/sec and run ray tracing about 10 times faster than Pascal. Denoising, BVH acceleration, and hybrid rendering reduce the ray count needed for real-time results.

Turing also introduces NVIDIA NGX, a deep learning-based graphics stack using Tensor Cores. NGX features include DLSS, DLSS 2X, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS is trained on high-quality supersampled images to produce output comparable to TAA with improved performance, while DLSS 2X targets image quality close to 64x supersampling.

New graphics pipeline features include Mesh Shading with Task and Mesh Shaders for more flexible geometry processing, reduced CPU draw-call bottlenecks, level-of-detail selection, and dynamic geometry manipulation. Variable Rate Shading lets developers vary shading rates per 16x16 screen region for content adaptive shading, motion adaptive shading, foveated rendering, and MSAA-related increases in shading rate. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility and appearance sampling by storing shading values in texture space for reuse across pixels, frames, or stereo views. Multi-View Rendering expands Pascal’s SMP, supporting up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 views at the API level.

Turing supports bindless Constant Buffer Views and Unordered Access Views under DX12 Tier 3 resource binding and Tier 2 resource heaps. For VR, Turing combines VirtualLink, Multi-View Rendering, Variable Rate Shading, foveated rendering, and RT Core acceleration for VRWorks Audio.

The TU104 GPU includes up to six GPCs, 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 13.6 billion transistors, and one x8 NVLink link. It is used in products such as GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. Tesla T4 uses a TU104 configuration with 2560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores. TU106, used in GeForce RTX 2070, includes 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, and 10.8 billion transistors, but does not support NVLink or SLI.

The passage defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric for hybrid rendering that weights Tensor, FP32 CUDA, RT Core, and INT32 operations according to observed usage. It also explains ray tracing basics, BVH acceleration, denoising, and examples of ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections in games such as Battlefield V and Shadow of the Tomb Raider.

The speaker says the Colorado series was tough, but fatigue is no excuse against New Jersey in the Stanley Cup finals. They describe the series as tight, low-scoring, and physically demanding, with both teams battling for space. New Jersey is praised for defensive play, confidence, quick transition, and a line with strong chemistry that must be contained. Matchups will be decided by Hitch and the coaching staff. A Journal of Climate paper by Nicholas Lewis and Judith Curry estimates climate sensitivity using observed temperature changes and radiative forcing data from the mid/late 19th century to 2016, incorporating updated greenhouse gas, ozone, and aerosol forcing estimates. It concludes that high future warming estimates from many CMIP5 climate models are inconsistent with observed historical warming and implies future warming under given emissions scenarios would be about 30–45% lower than central IPCC model projections.

Using globally complete temperature data, the paper estimates equilibrium climate sensitivity at 1.66°C and transient climate response at 1.33°C, compared with CMIP5 model estimates of 3.1°C and 1.9°C. The abstract reports slightly lower estimates using a 1869–1882 base period and 2007–2016 final period. The authors examine possible biases from time-varying feedbacks, forcing efficacy, temperature estimation, and sea-surface warming patterns, concluding these effects are minor when globally complete data are used.

Former Fed Chair Janet Yellen said interest rates should rise gradually to prevent the U.S. economy from overheating while allowing inflation to reach 2 percent. She said February’s 313,000 job gains exceeded a sustainable pace of 90,000 to 120,000. Yellen warned tightening too slowly risks overheating, while moving too quickly could keep inflation below target. Jerome Powell is expected to continue her gradual rate-hike policy.

The passage outlines planned statistical analyses and reporting for a clinical trial SAP. Plasma glucose concentrations, changes from pre-dose, and pharmacodynamic metrics will be summarized by treatment group, with mean and individual glucose concentration plots over nominal time. Safety analyses will use the safety set and include exposure, insulin use before hypoglycemia induction, hypoglycemia induction procedures, trial medication administration, rescue glucose infusion, local tolerability, adverse events, laboratory tests, vital signs, physical exams, ECGs, and immunogenicity.

Treatment-emergent adverse events are defined as events occurring or worsening after dosing, mapped using MedDRA, summarized by treatment group, causality, severity, seriousness, special interest status, injection site reaction status, and system organ class/preferred term. Missing AE causality is treated as related if unresolved. Laboratory, ECG, vital sign, ADA, and tolerability results will be summarized descriptively, with listings provided where applicable.

The SAP notes changes from the protocol for the primary efficacy analysis and secondary efficacy terminology. Appendices specify table, figure, and listing formatting, missing-date handling, derivation formulas, SAS programming QC requirements, validation procedures, documentation expectations, and planned tables, figures, and listings for efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and patient data.

Arizona’s school choice system includes open enrollment, charter schools, private school tax credits, and Empowerment Scholarship Account vouchers, which became universal in 2022 after voters rejected a capped expansion in 2018. The Grand Canyon Institute argues that Arizona provides more than $1 billion annually in private education subsidies with limited accountability and transparency.

GCI estimates that while a growing share of universal ESA participants come from charter or district schools, nearly three-quarters of total universal participants did not or would not have attended them. About 90% of new universal entrants in FY2025 had attended district or charter schools. ESA participation remains higher in wealthier zip codes, though income differences have declined since 2023.

ESA enrollment grew from 144 students in FY2012 to 87,602 by FY2025 Q2, with 64,133 in the universal category. GCI estimates FY2023 ESA allocations at about $415 million or more, with $304 million spent overall. Of $173 million spent on private schools, 51% went to religious schools and 44% to schools serving special needs students. No more than 40% of ESA students used allocations for private school tuition in FY2023, indicating substantial use for homeschooling or extracurricular purposes.

Unspent ESA funds accumulated significantly. About 60,000 accounts held $175 million at the end of FY2023, and GCI estimates balances reached $360 million by the end of FY2024.

GCI concludes universal ESA vouchers are a net cost to Arizona’s general fund because many recipients were not previously in public schools. It estimates net costs of at least $332 million in FY2024 and about $350 million in FY2025, including administrative costs. Charter-to-ESA transfers generate modest savings, district-to-ESA transfers create net costs, and students who would not have attended public schools represent the full voucher amount as new state costs.

The study examines pre-service teachers’ opinions on the Physical Education and Sports Curriculum for grades 5–8, focusing on outcomes, content, learning-teaching processes, and assessment-evaluation practices. Using a quantitative survey model, data were collected from 100 students at Bayburt University Faculty of Sports Sciences, with 25 participants from each department.

Findings show generally positive views about curriculum outcomes, especially their suitability to student levels, placement under correct learning areas, and clarity. However, many participants were undecided about possible scientific errors in outcome statements. Regarding content, most agreed it was meaningfully ordered, but many were undecided about scientific accuracy, age suitability, and compatibility with programs in other countries. For learning-teaching processes, many stated that activities and concrete materials were used, but most disagreed that different methods and techniques were included. Many were undecided about developmental suitability and interdisciplinary links. In assessment and evaluation, participants reported the use of different forms, while views on different or alternative evaluation methods were mixed or undecided.

The study concludes that pre-service teachers’ evaluations of curriculum objectives are generally positive, but their knowledge of content, scientific accuracy, international compatibility, and some teaching and evaluation dimensions appears limited. It recommends more studies, informative seminars or congresses, and curriculum review courses in teacher education programs.

The passage describes NVIDIA RTX Blackwell neural rendering technologies and related GPU features. Mega Geometry is an RTX technology that increases geometric detail in ray-traced applications by enabling full-fidelity ray tracing for modern LOD systems such as Unreal Engine 5 Nanite. It introduces cluster-level acceleration structures (CLAS), GPU-driven batched BVH management, and partitioned top-level acceleration structures (PTLAS) to reduce BVH build overhead for changing LODs and high object counts. It also supports real-time ray tracing of animated displaced subdivision surfaces. Mega Geometry is supported through NVIDIA ray tracing APIs including DXR via NVAPI, Vulkan extensions, and OptiX 9.0, and works on RTX GPUs starting with Turing, with Blackwell RT Cores adding hardware optimizations.

Blackwell adds hardware ray intersection support for Linear Swept Spheres (LSS), targeting strand-like objects such as hair, fur, and grass. LSS is described as about 2x faster than Disjoint Orthogonal Triangle Strips for common hair rendering use cases while using about 5x less VRAM. Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 improves GPU thread reordering for ray tracing, path tracing, and neural shading, with more efficient reorder logic and application-controlled APIs.

The AI Management Processor is a programmable GPU context scheduler implemented with a dedicated RISC-V processor. It offloads GPU task scheduling from the CPU, improves workload coordination for graphics and AI tasks, reduces latency, and can improve frame consistency and multitasking.

Blackwell video and display features include hardware encode and decode support for 4:2:2 chroma-sampled video, ninth-generation NVENC with improved AV1 and HEVC quality, AV1 Ultra High Quality mode, improved export speeds on GeForce RTX 5090, sixth-generation NVDEC with faster H.264 decoding, and DisplayPort 2.1b with up to 80 Gbps bandwidth.

Blackwell Max-Q improvements focus on power efficiency through advanced power gating, separate voltage rails, accelerated frequency switching, and low-latency sleep. These features allow faster transitions between power states, finer control of chip power, and up to 50% power savings in a small language model inference example.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame, using faster AI models with lower VRAM usage and enhanced Flip Metering for frame pacing. DLSS 4 also moves Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA to transformer-based models, improving temporal stability, lighting detail, motion detail, and reducing artifacts.

The passage also describes neural shaders enabled by Cooperative Vectors APIs for DX12 and Vulkan, giving graphics shaders access to Tensor Cores. Related technologies include RTX Neural Materials, RTX Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. These use neural networks to approximate complex materials, compress textures, infer indirect lighting, render subsurface scattering, and improve real-time face rendering.

Finally, the passage outlines Blackwell GPU products. GB202 targets the ultra-enthusiast segment and powers the GeForce RTX 5090, while GB203 targets the high-end segment for products including GeForce RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 targets the performance segment for GeForce RTX 5070. The document ends with NVIDIA warranty, liability, licensing, trademark, and copyright notices.

The passage describes methods for forming 3-dimensional vertical NOR-type memory string arrays. One embodiment uses damascene local vertical bit lines and forms local word lines through a two-step etching process to reduce aspect ratio, improve structural stability, and avoid ribboning. The method includes forming multilayer memory stacks over global interconnect lines, creating trenches, replacing sacrificial layers with metal word line strips, forming vias with tunneling dielectric, charge storage, blocking dielectric, channel, liner, and sacrificial dielectric layers, and adding source and drain semiconductor regions connected to global interconnect lines.

The invention addresses alignment variability in two-step etching and describes possible design accommodations. It also provides staircase structures for contacting local word lines and alternative arrangements for connecting source and drain regions to top or bottom global interconnect lines. Additional embodiments include using dielectric pillars to support high-aspect-ratio word line stacks and using stacked masks to form word line strips. The passage also summarizes related patent applications and references drawings illustrating fabrication steps and structural features.

Second-quarter S&P 500 earnings grew 11%, marking the fastest two-quarter growth since 2011, and more than half of companies beat forecasts. InnerDancer Performing Arts hosts monthly dances for teens and adults with developmental disabilities at the Gloria McClellan Adult Activity & Resource Center in Vista. Program manager Donna Meester said the events offer a safe, affordable recreational opportunity, with two hours of dancing, socializing and snacks for $12.

The passage proposes Digital Ecosystems as software systems inspired by biological ecosystems to address complex, dynamic computing problems through scalability, self-organisation, and automated composition. It argues that existing uses of “digital ecosystem” often lack ecological properties, while the intended model should exploit features of biological ecosystems, including evolving agents, dynamic fitness landscapes, distributed environments, migration, diversity, and adaptive self-organisation.

Digital Ecosystems are contrasted with traditional genetic algorithms by emphasizing changing user needs, complex dynamic fitness functions, and spatially distributed agent populations. Agents should reproduce, vary, interact, move, and die. Spatial dynamics, network connectivity, and migration are presented as important for maintaining diversity and avoiding premature convergence. The passage also frames Digital Ecosystems as Complex Adaptive Systems, noting both benefits such as scalable organisation and adaptation, and risks such as unpredictable dynamics, mass extinctions, and undesirable state changes.

The proposed architecture uses a decentralised peer-to-peer network of habitats, where agents migrate between nodes and local evolutionary algorithms combine agents to satisfy user requests. Agents include executable components and ontological descriptions. Network topology adapts using successful and unsuccessful agent migration, producing connectivity aligned with the user base. Unlike island-model distributed evolutionary computing, multiple populations evolve in response to similar requests, sharing useful solutions across habitats.

Users submit semantic descriptions of desired applications to local habitats. These requests define fitness measures for evolving agent sequences. Evolution is accelerated by localised agent pools, reuse of previously evolved sequences, and migration of relevant sequences from other users. The passage then describes a simulation using a business ecosystem of small and medium-sized enterprises, with 100 users, randomly connected habitats, deployed agents, generated service requests, and evolving populations used to find optimal agent sequences.
Coral Davenport reports on Russell Vought’s plans to bypass Congress’s budget powers for Trump’s agenda.

President Trump said the government shutdown gives him an “unprecedented opportunity” to cut federal agencies and Democratic-backed projects. His administration froze about $18 billion for New York infrastructure and canceled $8 billion for climate projects in Democratic-leaning states. Officials said federal layoffs could begin soon and may number in the thousands. The shutdown began after Congress failed to pass funding legislation, with Democrats seeking an extension of enhanced Obamacare tax credits and Republicans backing a short-term funding bill.

The lecture discusses effective field theory with fine tuning in two-nucleon nonrelativistic scattering. A naive dimensional power counting can classify contact operators as irrelevant, but calculations show that some must be promoted to relevant because the theory is expanded around an interacting fixed point rather than the trivial free fixed point.

For short-range interactions, elastic scattering in a partial wave is described by a phase shift, with the amplitude written in terms of \(P\cot\delta\). The effective range expansion states that \(P^{2L+1}\cot\delta\) has a Taylor expansion in momentum. In the EFT, nucleons interact through contact operators with increasing numbers of derivatives. Loop diagrams are bubble diagrams and can be summed exactly, yielding the effective range expansion without specifying a potential.

The kinetic energy term must be kept at leading order because energy scales as \(P^2/2M\); omitting it creates a pinch singularity. Dimensional analysis gives coefficients \(C_{2M}\sim 1/(M\Lambda^{2M+1})\), but experimental scattering lengths in the \(^{1}S_0\) and \(^{3}S_1\) channels are much larger than natural expectations, while effective ranges are natural. This indicates a fine tuning in the leading contact interaction \(C_0\).

Using off-shell momentum subtraction or power divergence subtraction tracks power-law divergences missed by MS-bar. The resulting renormalization group flow promotes \(C_0\) to scale as \(1/(M\mu)\), making it relevant when \(\mu\sim P\). The beta function has fixed points at zero and infinite scattering length; the physical systems lie near interacting fixed points. A pole in the amplitude corresponds to the deuteron bound state.

The fine tuning modifies the power counting of higher operators such as \(C_2\), whose scaling is enhanced relative to naive dimensional analysis. Renormalization group equations propagate the effect of the fine tuning through the EFT. The resulting expansion sums all powers of \(aP\) while treating effective range corrections perturbatively, producing scale-independent amplitudes order by order.

The D.C. Circuit reviewed Shieldalloy Metallurgical Corporation’s challenge to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission’s transfer of regulatory authority over certain nuclear materials to New Jersey under § 274 of the Atomic Energy Act. Shieldalloy, which had long pursued NRC approval for on-site decommissioning of its Newfield facility, argued that New Jersey’s program was incompatible with the federal regime and that the transfer would disrupt its pending decommissioning process.

The court held that the NRC failed to adequately explain its response to Shieldalloy’s concerns under criterion 25, which requires arrangements to prevent interference with existing licenses or pending applications during a transfer. The NRC also failed to sufficiently address whether it could retain jurisdiction over Shieldalloy’s site or a discrete category of materials, despite relevant prior NRC practice involving Oklahoma. Because the NRC did not provide a rational explanation connecting the facts to its decision, the court found the transfer arbitrary and capricious.

The court granted Shieldalloy’s petition, vacated the NRC’s transfer of authority to New Jersey, and remanded for further proceedings.

European shares headed for their biggest weekly loss since November 2016, pressured by rising bond yields, a stronger euro and weak banking results. The STOXX 600 fell for a fifth session, while Germany’s DAX reversed sharply after a strong start to 2018. Deutsche Bank dropped after a larger-than-expected 2017 loss, and Caixabank and Sabadell also fell after mixed results.
