The paper explores whether large language models can autoformalize physical systems, especially cyber-physical systems with continuous dynamics and discrete transitions, into differential game logic. It introduces 20 undergraduate kinematics benchmarks and an automated pipeline using LLM-generated formalizations, KeYmaera X parser feedback, and semantic checking through symbolic execution, Z3, and Mathematica.

The checker evaluates whether a generated model recovers the expected symbolic solution and whether enough variables are mutated to avoid trivial stasis models. A running example on average velocity shows that formalization can expose subtle modeling errors and unstated assumptions, such as nonzero distance and positive velocities.

The system queries an LLM to propose a dGL model, optionally using few-shot examples, then allows up to three syntax-repair attempts based on parser feedback. If parsing succeeds, the semantic checker tests equivalence to the expected solution and checks variable writes.

Experiments compare GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, and OpenAI o3 under zero-shot and few-shot prompting. GPT-4o fails all benchmarks without few-shot prompting, while few-shot prompting improves all models. With few-shot prompting, o3 achieves a 70% top-5 success rate, compared with 45% for GPT-4.1 and 20% for GPT-4o.

Six benchmarks remain unsolved by all models, mainly due to optimization structure, non-polynomial continuous dynamics, or complicated dynamics that exceed checker capabilities. The authors suggest improvements through stronger solvers, invariant generation, better modeling abstractions, and LLM guidance. The work concludes that LLM-based CPS autoformalization is promising and may support future applications involving autonomous systems formalizing unfamiliar situations from multimodal input.

The passage describes AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine, an optional extension to SEV and SNP that offloads page migration between physical memory tiers while preserving guest physical addresses. TMPM supports migration of pages targeted by concurrent DMA and pages protected by SNP that HV/OS cannot directly access. Availability is checked through the ENGINE_READY bit, and IOMMU enablement is required.

TMPM uses a separate page migration ring buffer, mailbox registers, and commands such as PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO, PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST, and PM_NOOP. Commands can process 1–128 migration entries, with per-command and per-page status reporting. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates hypervisor/default pages and can coordinate with IOMMU host page table entries to handle DMA. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages, requiring source pages in Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid state and destination pages in Pre-Migration state. After migration, guest destination pages inherit the source state, while source pages become Pre-Migration.

The Pre-Migration RMP state uses a platform-specific ASID value reported by the TMPM driver and cannot be PVALIDATEd by a guest. TMPM supports only 4 KB-aligned page moves, with special alignment rules for host page table entries and 2 MB pages. Certain structures must not be migrated, including IOMMU memory structures, vIOMMU private address space page tables, pinned vIOMMU backing storage, the ring buffer, and argument pages.

The driver initializes TMPM by checking ENGINE_READY, configuring ring buffer address and size, enabling queue behavior, setting DRIVER_INITIALIZED, and retrieving PS_ASID_VAL. It can pause, resume, shut down, or reinitialize the ring buffer. Interrupts report queue-empty, low-water mark, completion, error, write-pointer errors, and ring-buffer memory errors.

Firmware reload is supported only when no operations are in flight and the ring buffer is torn down. Reload capability is determined with PM_GET_CAPABILITIES, and EPYC Family 19h is identified by FW_VER_Major value 71. Reloaded firmware must be the same or a greater version.

Performance guidance recommends batching at least 16 pages per command, with maximum performance at 128 pages, keeping the ring buffer populated, and using interrupts sparingly. Error handling includes command and migration-entry status codes, ring-buffer status reporting, and possible MCA reporting for hardware errors; severe errors may leave memory state unrecoverable.

Mark Valladares writes from snowy Creeting St Peter, criticizing government ministers’ comments about potentially reneging on Theresa May’s EU deal and citing Simon Coveney’s reminder of the Ireland/Northern Ireland commitments. He previews House of Lords business with a focus on Liberal Democrat contributions, mentions Paul Walter’s pieces on a youth activist award scheme and the Samaritans, and invites readers to suggest “goodbye”-themed music or submit articles.

Theo Walcott scored in the 51st minute to give Everton a 1-0 Premier League win over Newcastle at Goodison Park. It was his third goal for Everton since joining in January. Everton next visits Huddersfield, while Newcastle hosts West Bromwich Albion on Saturday.

The study addresses depression and anxiety diagnosis using digital phenotyping and large language models. Researchers collected over 15,000 minutes of psychiatric interview recordings from 1,160 outpatients at Shanghai Mental Health Center, covering 25 diagnoses, mainly depression and anxiety. They developed clinical indicators from EMRs, diagnostic criteria, mental status evaluations, and assessment scales, then used and fine-tuned an LLM with psychiatrist annotations to identify symptoms and rate scale components. Linguistic and acoustic features were also extracted. These multimodal features were combined in an ensemble machine-learning pipeline to predict diagnostic groups and major symptoms, with the goal of improving objective biomarkers, clinical interpretability, and psychiatric assessment efficiency.

Cover Zero is an all-out pressure defense that blitzes every player not assigned to man coverage, forcing quick quarterback decisions but leaving defenders isolated. Offenses can attack it with quick man-beating routes, perimeter mismatches, slants, shallow crossers, and pick or rub concepts, especially because the middle of the field is often open. The passage highlights examples including double slants, a running back seam gadget, bunch jerk routes, slant-rub designs, and Jerry Rice motion slant-flat concepts used to create separation and quick throws against Cover Zero.

Former Aberdeen manager Steve Paterson said Pittodrie should host the funeral of Neale “Tattie” Cooper, arguing no church would be large enough for mourners. Cooper, 54, part of Aberdeen’s 1983 European Cup Winners’ Cup team, died after falling down stairs. Tributes came from fans, Alex McLeish, Willie Miller and chairman Stewart Milne.

FlowMotion ONE, a smartphone stabilizer, exceeded its $30,000 Kickstarter goal, raising over $600,000 from more than 2,700 backers after being funded in one hour. The device uses sensors and motors to reduce shaking and vibrations, enabling smooth smartphone video. Its 3inONE design allows use as a wearable mount, handheld stabilizer with joystick, or with an extension pole. Founded in 2015 by Lars Flesland, Julie Bauge, Eirik Dyrseth and Didrik Dimmen, FlowMotion developed the product after experiencing shaky footage during outdoor adventures. The company has offices in Palo Alto and Trondheim and has won awards in Norway, Finland, Germany and the United States.

An Oklahoma veterinarian removed 21 pacifiers from a dog named Dovey after the dog vomited one and an x-ray suggested several more. Dovey had been eating slowly and vomiting phlegm but otherwise seemed fine. The veterinarian said Dovey was recovering well.

This study used 2017–2018 Demographic and Health Survey data from Benin and Cameroon to assess awareness of cervical cancer and cervical screening among women aged 15–49 years and its association with demographic characteristics and media use. A total of 21,322 women were surveyed on cervical cancer awareness, including 7,706 in Benin and 13,616 in Cameroon; 7,010 were also asked about cervical screening awareness.

Awareness of cervical cancer was low, especially in Benin: 9.5% of women in Benin and 46.1% in Cameroon had heard of cervical cancer. Among women aware of cervical cancer, 51.4% in Benin and 59.7% in Cameroon were aware of cervical screening. Awareness was generally higher among older women, those with higher education, wealthier women, professional women, urban residents, and women using media, particularly the internet.

Multivariate analysis showed that older age, higher education, and recent internet use were significantly associated with increased cervical cancer awareness in both countries; wealth was also clearly associated in Cameroon. Awareness of cervical screening was associated with older age, higher education, radio use in Benin, and frequent internet use in Cameroon.

The study concludes that awareness of cervical cancer and screening in Benin and Cameroon is very low and recommends strengthening awareness programmes through stakeholder engagement, public enlightenment, media use, and implementation of cervical cancer control strategies.

COVID-19 is caused by SARS-CoV-2, which is shed in feces and can be detected in wastewater, making wastewater surveillance useful for monitoring outbreaks. Standard concentration methods often require larger sample volumes and centrifuges, limiting use in low-resource settings. Nanotrap particles can capture, concentrate, separate, and protect analytes, including viruses, in complex samples and have been used to detect SARS-CoV-2 and other respiratory viruses in wastewater. The study evaluated how factors such as pH, temperature, incubation time, sample volume, RNA extraction, and concentration method affect SARS-CoV-2 RNA detection, and compared Nanotrap-based methods with membrane filtration and skim milk methods using wastewater samples collected in Atlanta from June to August 2021.

A randomized, open-label clinical trial studied 1112 subjects treated with apixaban for NVAF over 48 weeks. Participants were assigned to standard care information or an Additional Education Program; after 24 weeks, the education group was rerandomized to continue or stop the program. Adherence was measured electronically and defined by 24-hour dosing windows, with rules for missed doses, withheld treatment, and permanent discontinuation after more than 30 consecutive days.

Ben Baby’s mailbag discusses Texas A&M’s game against No. 1 Alabama and Kevin Sumlin’s status, saying Florida is not necessarily a must-win even if A&M is blown out, but the Aggies need to play well late in the season. Other topics include A&M’s field tribute to Gene Stallings and the 1967 team, fall weddings, music requests, North Texas promotions, the “Go Mean Green” phrase, Arsene Wenger, and Chipotle.

Kratom, derived from Mitragyna speciosa, has stimulant-like effects at low doses and opioid-like sedative effects at higher doses. Although illegal statewide in Wisconsin, kratom use occurs there. Researchers analyzed Wisconsin Poison Center kratom-associated exposure calls from January 1, 2010, to September 1, 2022.

The center received 59 kratom exposure calls. Most exposed persons were male, and the mean age among those with age data was 35.3 years. Calls increased from 1 in 2011 to a peak of 15 in 2020. About half involved kratom alone, while polysubstance exposures commonly involved alcohol or benzodiazepines. The most reported symptoms were agitation, tachycardia, confusion, and central nervous system depression.

Among calls with known outcomes, 19 involved moderate or major medical outcomes, and one death was reported. Seven people required critical care; five had marked agitation, and three required mechanical ventilation. Three exposures occurred in infants under age 2 and were unintentional.

The authors conclude that kratom-associated exposure calls in Wisconsin have increased, often involve polysubstance exposure, and sometimes require intensive care. They recommend clinician awareness, improved documentation of kratom exposure, and education for adults who use kratom, especially with other substances or around children.

A Dec. 12, 2000 Enron media roundup includes articles on utility stocks, Enron’s Dabhol project in India, natural gas prices, digital media company Activate, retail energy certification, and online energy trading.

The Los Angeles Times reported utility stocks had risen strongly in 2000 due to power demand, falling bond yields, and defensive investors, but analysts said gains could slow if technology stocks recovered. Enron was cited as a major wholesale power marketer and energy trader.

Reuters reported Dabhol Power Company, 65% owned by Enron, said four Indian lenders agreed to cut loan rates by 450 basis points to 16.5%, which could help reduce power tariffs in Maharashtra.

The Dallas Morning News reported record natural gas prices led Terra Industries, Mississippi Chemical, and Seneca Resources to sell gas rather than use it in production. Enron spokesman Mark Palmer said volatility was good for Enron.

Business Wire reported Activate’s 2000 growth in Webcasting and digital media services, noting coordination with content distribution networks including Enron.

The Times of India published critical articles on Enron’s Maharashtra power project, alleging lack of transparency, high tariffs, and public-interest concerns. Retired judge Hosbet Suresh said the Maharashtra State Electricity Board’s agreement with Dabhol Power Company could be nullified.

Dow Jones reported Green Mountain applied to become a Texas retail electric provider; Enron units and The New Power Company had also applied. PR Newswire reported The New Power Company, formed by Enron, was certified as a retail natural gas marketer in Georgia.

Reuters and Bloomberg reported that EnronOnline, ICE, and Dynegydirect were leading online energy trading platforms, with EnronOnline trading about $2.4 billion per day.

Investing.com reports market momentum remains intact but charts show early warnings. The S&P 500 rose 2.2% in July and 7.8% year to date, though it slipped at the start of August. Volatility and credit spreads are rising seasonally, portfolios are increasingly weighted toward tech, and U.S. electricity demand reached a new high. Short-term technicals appear weaker, while medium- and long-term trend indicators remain healthy. The passage also includes market headlines, promotional content, and trading risk disclosures.

A watchdog rejected claims that Switzerland’s Office of the Attorney General was involved in alleged spying by a Swiss suspect arrested in Germany or exposed his identity in prosecution files. The former policeman, also investigated in Switzerland over stolen banking data, allegedly drew scrutiny after records reached German prosecutors. The case caused outrage in Germany, especially North Rhine-Westphalia, which bought stolen bank data that helped recover nearly €7 billion in taxes. It remains unclear whether the suspect worked for the Federal Intelligence Service. The Swiss government has stayed mostly silent, while parliamentary bodies review the case.

A 2-year-old girl, Laylah Washington, died after being shot in the head while riding in a car in Memphis. Police said the car was followed after a parking lot dispute, and shots were fired. No arrests have been made; police seek a black Chevrolet Impala.

Dustin Brown and Anze Kopitar attributed their team’s resilience to years of playing together, trust, comfort in difficult situations, and strong off-ice chemistry. They said the team dislikes falling behind but has repeatedly shown character in coming back, while better starts would provide needed relief. Brown said big-city matchups like New York versus Los Angeles increase excitement and visibility for hockey. Both players emphasized staying focused on the next game rather than reflecting during the playoffs. Brown praised Drew Doughty’s growth as a player and leader, described the team’s playoff style as difficult to beat, and said the Kings value Stanley Cup banners over regular-season success. Kopitar and Brown said Marian Gaborik fit in quickly because the room is close and has no cliques. Brown also described Justin as laid back, focused, and a big-game player.

HMP Northward, over its 212-inmate capacity with more than 220 men, will transfer some low-risk, risk-assessed inmates to a cordoned-off section of the Immigration Detention Centre at Fairbanks to ease overcrowding. Prison Director Steven Barrett said the move could free about 22 spaces and is the most viable short-term option, as overcrowding is creating security concerns and affecting rehabilitation programmes. Officials said the transfer and prison reconfiguration will not compromise safety or statutory obligations, and IDC operations will be coordinated around current migrants and asylum seekers. The centre is also facing pressure, including a hunger strike by nine asylum-seeking detainees.

A special weather statement was issued for Edmonton and nearby areas due to conditions favourable for funnel clouds Wednesday afternoon. Environment Canada said weak rotation could rarely intensify into a weak landspout tornado, which can cause damage. Reported funnel clouds were seen near Edmonton, including by Sturgeon Composite High School, where students were kept inside. Officials advised people to stay aware and prepare to shelter if funnel clouds develop nearby.

Microsoft’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2020 reported total revenue of $37.2 billion, up from $33.1 billion a year earlier, with net income of $13.9 billion and diluted EPS of $1.82. Operating income rose to $15.9 billion. Revenue grew across all segments: Productivity and Business Processes to $12.3 billion, Intelligent Cloud to $13.0 billion, and More Personal Computing to $11.8 billion. Commercial cloud revenue increased 31% to $15.2 billion, driven by growth in Office 365 Commercial, Azure, LinkedIn, Dynamics 365, Gaming, and Surface, while search advertising declined.

Microsoft reported total assets of $301.0 billion, total liabilities of $177.6 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $123.4 billion as of September 30, 2020. Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $138.0 billion. Net cash from operations was $19.3 billion. The company repurchased $5.3 billion of common stock and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.56 per share. Microsoft also entered into an agreement to acquire ZeniMax Media Inc. for $7.5 billion in cash, expected to close in the second half of fiscal year 2021.

The passage describes embodiments of a wireless communication processing method and apparatus for managing data transmission in a duplication mode, where PDCP data on a radio bearer is transmitted through one RLC entity and duplicated through another RLC entity on different paths.

One method allows a terminal device to trigger and send a data volume report for one selected path in a duplicated radio bearer, reducing signaling overhead compared with reporting all paths. The reported path may be indicated by the radio access network or selected by the terminal based on priority or data volume, and the report may be sent through a corresponding or alternative cell or cell group.

Another method manages activation or deactivation of duplication mode through an indication message from the radio access network. The message may use different field structures to identify the radio bearer, path activation status, and whether duplication mode is enabled. When duplication mode is activated, the terminal may duplicate data across RLC entities, report relevant buffered data volumes, and notify numbering information so the network can identify duplicated data. When duplication mode is deactivated, duplicated data may be stopped, discarded, or handled according to specified rules, while non-duplicated data may still be transmitted.

The passage also describes related communications apparatuses, computer storage media, and hardware implementations, including terminal devices, processors, receivers, transmitters, chips, and protocol-stack architectures involving CU/DU, carrier aggregation, and dual connectivity scenarios.

Britain’s FTSE 100 fell 0.2% on Friday, heading for its worst week since August 2017, as disappointing updates from BT and AstraZeneca weighed on shares. BT dropped over 5% to a five-year low amid concerns over stagnant divisions and its pension scheme, while AstraZeneca fell 1.7% after a weak profit outlook. Commodity and oil stocks gained, supported by firmer copper and oil prices. Capita rose more than 5% after Morgan Stanley upgraded it to “equal-weight,” despite recent profit warnings and a dividend suspension.

Treasury minister Mel Stride assured MPs that Britain’s fish fingers would be “safe” during Brexit talks after Labour’s Mel Onn urged continued sensible customs arrangements to protect Great Grimsby’s time-sensitive fish processing sector and 5,000 jobs.

The passage describes a data intake and query system for collecting, indexing, storing, and searching large volumes of machine-generated data from IT environments. Machine data from sources such as servers, applications, routers, sensors, mobile devices, and logs is parsed into timestamped events and stored with metadata such as host, source, and source type. The system preserves minimally processed or raw machine data and uses a flexible, late-binding schema that applies field extraction rules at search time, allowing users to define or refine fields after ingestion.

The system architecture includes forwarders, indexers, search heads, data stores, client devices, host devices, and optional monitoring components in client applications. Forwarders receive data, annotate it, and send it to indexers, which parse data into events, assign timestamps, apply transformations, generate keyword or field-value indexes, and store events in time-based buckets. Search heads coordinate queries across indexers, which can process data in parallel and return results for aggregation.

The passage also describes on-premises and cloud-based deployments, where system components may be managed locally or provided as a service. It further explains searching external data systems through External Result Provider processes, which translate search requests for external stores such as Hadoop, NoSQL, SQL, or other systems and return results in streaming, reporting, or mixed modes.

The indexing discussion covers inverted indexes that map tokens or field-value pairs to event references, enabling efficient filtering, categorization, and grouping of search results by criteria such as partition, time range, host, source, source type, keyword, or field values.

The U.S. District Court for the Middle District of North Carolina considered Melissa Jennings’ claims against UNC, women’s soccer coach Anson Dorrance, assistant coach William Palladino, and other UNC officials. Jennings, a former UNC women’s soccer team member dismissed in 1998, alleged that Dorrance and Palladino made sexually inappropriate comments and that Dorrance improperly questioned her personal life. She brought Title IX, § 1983, and state invasion-of-privacy claims.

The court denied Jennings’ motion to strike defendants’ amended answer and enter default judgment, finding no bad faith or clear inconsistency in Dorrance’s deposition testimony. It also denied her motion to strike exhibits attached to Dorrance’s affidavit, finding them authenticated and admissible as records of regularly conducted activity.

The court granted defendants’ motion for summary judgment. It held that the alleged conduct, while inappropriate or offensive in some respects, was not severe, pervasive, and objectively offensive enough to deprive Jennings of educational opportunities under Title IX. The court also rejected her § 1983 privacy claim, finding that Dorrance’s inquiries did not force disclosure of personal information or affect her decision-making rights. Her § 1983 sexual harassment claim failed for the same reasons as the Title IX claim, and supervisory liability claims failed because no constitutional violation was established. The court further held that Dorrance’s conduct did not meet North Carolina’s standard for common law invasion of privacy.

The passage reviews the integration of information technology into language education in Indonesia within Education 4.0. It highlights online learning platforms, mobile learning, blended learning, asynchronous learning, broadcasts, new assessments, parental involvement, and flexible policies as alternatives to face-to-face instruction. The study used qualitative descriptive analysis, comparative analysis, literature review, observation, and framework development, identifying 151 strongly relevant Scopus papers from 1,010 manuscripts.

Findings show that IT can improve language learning through tools such as automatic speech recognition, task-based learning, game-based learning, learning management systems, AI, VR, AR, and mobile platforms. Key challenges include teachers’ limited technological skills, reduced student engagement, unequal access to devices and internet, limited online teaching resources, difficulties in remote assessment, and reduced social interaction. Suggested management strategies include teacher training, digital platforms, language support tools, virtual exchange, cloud infrastructure, mobile learning, data-driven decisions, and inclusive IT policies. The passage concludes that IT can enhance language education if implemented with attention to pedagogy, management, access, and student needs.

This Agreement is the complete understanding regarding Software use. Invalid provisions do not affect the remainder. It is governed by California and U.S. federal law, excludes the U.N. sales convention, requires disputes in Santa Clara County courts, mandates export law compliance, and allows amendments or waivers only in signed writing.

A federal judge in Illinois dismissed a lawsuit accusing the College Board and 40 selective private institutions of conspiring to inflate tuition by requiring financial information from noncustodial parents in aid calculations. Judge Sara Ellis found the plaintiffs had not plausibly alleged an agreement or evidence that institutions shared aid processes or used the same formula.

At a human trafficking training session in Oshakati, Prosecutor-General Martha Imalwa said human trafficking is the third largest international crime, generating $32 billion annually, with millions living in slavery worldwide. She noted Namibia faces suspected trafficking cases, including vulnerable Angolan children working or selling goods. The training, supported by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, aims to help officials detect, investigate, assist victims of, and prosecute trafficking cases. Police Inspector-General Sebastian Ndeitunga said Namibia recorded 25 trafficking cases from 2010 to 2017, with six pending trial and 14 under investigation.

A randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated SA58 nasal spray, a broad-spectrum anti-COVID-19 monoclonal antibody, as post-exposure prophylaxis in healthy adult workers in Beijing within 72 hours of contact with SARS-CoV-2-infected individuals during an Omicron BF.7 outbreak. The study ran from Nov 26 to Dec 9, 2022, at 21 construction sites but ended early after COVID-19 restrictions were lifted. Of 1,634 randomized participants, 1,222 entered the full analysis set: 901 received SA58 and 321 placebo. Baseline characteristics were similar between groups.

After excluding participants who were SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR positive at baseline, 1,123 participants were included in the efficacy analysis. Laboratory-confirmed symptomatic COVID-19 occurred in 7 of 824 SA58 recipients versus 14 of 299 placebo recipients, corresponding to an estimated treatment efficacy of 80.82% (95% CI 52.41%–92.27%). SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR positivity occurred in 32 SA58 recipients and 32 placebo recipients, giving an estimated infection-lowering efficacy of 61.83% (95% CI 37.50%–76.69%). Sequenced positive samples were all Omicron BF.7. No severe COVID-19 or deaths occurred.

Adverse events were reported by 25% of SA58 recipients and 22% of placebo recipients; all were grade 1. No serious adverse events or adverse events of special interest were reported. Common events included nasal mucosal dryness, runny nose, fever, nasal congestion, headache, cough, and throat dryness.

The authors conclude that SA58 showed satisfactory efficacy and safety in reducing symptomatic COVID-19 and SARS-CoV-2 infection in healthy adults after early exposure, but further evaluation is needed in high-risk populations and larger studies.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed SB 53, a landmark AI safety law requiring major AI companies to publicly disclose risk mitigation plans, report critical safety incidents, protect whistleblowers, and support development of CalCompute for public AI research. Authored by State Sen. Scott Wiener, the law emphasizes transparency over liability and applies to large developers. Supporters including Anthropic and Encode AI praised its balance of safety and innovation, while critics warned it could burden startups and create fragmented state regulation. The law includes civil penalties, though some experts called them weak and urged stronger transparency and evaluations.

The passage describes a medical airway management system for assisting rescuers during intubation, including rapid sequence intubation. The system uses airflow, capnography, impedance, acoustic, pulse oximetry, ECG, blood pressure, motion, positioning, video, and other sensors to obtain intubation parameters such as oxygen concentration, CO2 concentration, gas flow, ETCO2, transthoracic impedance, oxygen saturation, ECG, acoustic information, and patient position.

A patient monitoring device, which may include a defibrillator, receives sensor data, determines the presence of airflow, detects procedural steps, initiates timers, and provides context-sensitive feedback through a user interface. The system can guide rescuers through intubation steps, display relevant physiological information, generate alarms, calculate drug dosage information, store event markers, and adjust feedback when it detects a transition between procedure steps. Displays may be touchscreen interfaces, and portable devices such as tablets, smartphones, laptops, wrist-worn devices, or heads-up displays may communicate with the system.

The system also verifies endotracheal tube placement and continued proper placement. It may confirm that airflow in the airway corresponds to physiological evidence that ventilation has reached the lungs, using ETCO2, transthoracic impedance, acoustic signals, or other data. Verification may occur within a predefined or user-defined timer interval, including default intervals between 5 and 15 seconds. Tube placement may be assessed using thresholds, trends, desired ranges, moving averages, initial baselines, dynamic baselines, prior baselines, and percentage deviations from physiological baselines.

The passage further describes integrated or separate airway sensors for use with a bag-valve mask, ventilator, or endotracheal tube. The system may monitor inspiratory and expiratory gases, calculate respiratory measures, detect inadequate ventilation, identify risks such as hypoxemia or hypercarbia, and alert rescuers with visual, audible, or haptic feedback. It includes examples of user interfaces, flow charts, and system components for preoxygenation, preparation, paralysis, positioning, tube placement, verification, post-intubation management, and post-case debriefing.

Kevin Love entered his fourth straight NBA Finals with Cleveland while recovering from a concussion that could keep him out of Game 1. His season included injuries, criticism, trade rumors, and public disclosure of longtime anxiety and panic attacks. After explaining his struggles to teammates and writing about them, Love received widespread support and said the experience made him more empathetic. Despite an uneven postseason and uncertain status, he said his time in Cleveland has been worthwhile, highlighted by winning a championship and hoping for more.

Tropical Storm Nate was expected to move across the northwestern Caribbean, reach the eastern Yucatan Peninsula, enter the Gulf of Mexico and approach the northern Gulf Coast by Saturday evening, potentially strengthening into a hurricane. The forecast cone included Pensacola, with impacts possible in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties, including heavy rain, tropical storm-force winds, storm surge, tornadoes and 3 to 5 inches of rainfall.

A tropical storm watch was issued for much of the Northwest Florida Gulf Coast. Local closures and cancellations included the University of West Florida, Gulf Islands National Seashore, BaseFEST, Pensacola ComposerFest and other events. Santa Rosa County made sand available at several locations.

Gov. Rick Scott declared a state of emergency for Escambia, Santa Rosa and 27 other Florida counties. State officials prepared the National Guard, sheltering operations, transportation support, utility coordination and fuel monitoring, while urging residents to prepare and follow local updates.

Researchers at UC Irvine and other institutions introduced a satellite-based drought severity index using NASA GRACE mission data. The GRACE-DSI incorporates terrestrial water storage, including groundwater, to supplement precipitation-based drought tools and provide globally consistent monitoring, especially where ground data are limited. Covering 2002 to 2014 and planned for extension through ongoing and follow-on GRACE missions, the index has shown agreement with established drought and vegetation indicators. Researchers say it improves assessment of hydrological drought, water management, and drought impacts on vegetation, food production, and water resources.
Tony Iommi attended a Q&A at BIMM Birmingham to announce his scholarship and discussed perseverance in his music career with prospective students.

The passage argues that the summer box office was dominated by three successful comic book superhero films: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2, Wonder Woman, and Spider-Man: Homecoming. Outside that category, most genres had only one clear success, such as Despicable Me 3, Girls Trip, Annabelle: Creation, Dunkirk, Baby Driver, 47 Meters Down, and The Big Sick. Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales performed adequately worldwide, but many other big-budget releases, including King Arthur, Valerian, The Mummy, Transformers: The Last Knight, and War for the Planet of the Apes, disappointed or bombed relative to costs and expectations. Comedies, animated films, horror releases, and female-led action films also largely underperformed, with a few exceptions. The author concludes that the season showed limited multiplex diversity, with superhero films consistently succeeding while most other categories produced only a single notable hit.

Ryan, the six-year-old star of Ryan ToysReview, ranked among Forbes’ top 10 highest-paid YouTube stars after his channel reportedly earned $11 million in 2017. Started in 2015, the toy review channel has over 10 million subscribers and billions of views. His family keeps their identity private and says the videos will continue only while Ryan enjoys making them.

Long-short equity is an investment strategy that takes long positions in stocks expected to rise and short positions in stocks expected to fall. It seeks to reduce risk through hedging while profiting from both undervalued and overvalued securities. The strategy is commonly used by hedge funds and institutional investors, often with leverage, derivatives, and a long bias such as a 130/30 structure. It requires research, portfolio construction, and multiple pairs to manage risk, and may be unsuitable for retail investors due to complexity and capital needs. The passage also discusses Edward Thorp’s role in quantitative investing and presents a simple Coca-Cola/Pepsi backtest with modest returns and mild drawdown.

A May 24, 2001 Enron mentions email compiles news articles on energy and political issues. Topics include California officials accusing power generators of price manipulation, criticism of Attorney General Bill Lockyer’s remarks about Kenneth Lay, possible industry effects of Sen. James Jeffords’ expected party switch, Brazil’s electricity rationing plan, Bill Simon Jr.’s energy investments, India’s efforts to resolve the Dabhol Power dispute involving Enron, Central European gas market changes, Endesa’s planned Electra de Viesgo sale, and Dynegy’s interest in acquisitions.

A New York Times survey found many responding federal judges dissatisfied with the U.S. Supreme Court’s emergency docket decisions in Trump-related cases. Of 65 judges, 12 said the court used the docket appropriately and 12 said lower courts received sufficient guidance; 47 and 48 disagreed, respectively. Of 54 judges, 42 said the docket harmed public perception of the judiciary, 10 saw no effect, and two saw improvement. Some judges criticized the orders as unclear or demoralizing, while one Trump appointee defended them. The survey included 28 Republican-appointed and 37 Democratic-appointed judges, but the Times noted respondents may not represent the judiciary. A Volokh Conspiracy critique said unhappy judges may have been more likely to respond and that districts handling Trump challenges may skew the sample.

The passage describes using the PGA848 to drive an ADS8860 16-bit, 1MSPS single-ended input SAR ADC. The circuit supports single-ended or differential inputs, uses ±15V input-stage supplies, a 5.3V output-stage/ADC supply to prevent ADC input overload during overdrive, and a REF6250 5V precision reference. The PGA848 REF pin is set to 2.5V ADC midscale through a precision 10kΩ/10kΩ divider buffered by an OPA192.

Three filters are used: an input EMI/RFI filter, a feedback filter using CFB with the PGA feedback resistors, and an ADC input charge-reservoir RC filter for sample-and-hold settling and THD performance. With CFB = 75pF, nominal bandwidth is 318kHz, changing to 277kHz at the high resistor tolerance limit, while maintaining –0.1dB flatness to 41kHz. C0G capacitors are used in the signal path.

The OPA192 REF buffer uses dual feedback with RISO = 20Ω, RF = 2kΩ, CF = 2nF, and a 22nF bypass capacitor, providing 86° phase margin. Changes to REF capacitance require stability recalculation and simulation.

Power guidance notes nominal PGA848 performance with ±15V supplies and warns that supplies above 40V permanently damage the device. The study presents an AI-assisted inverse design workflow for discovering Dion-Jacobson 2D hybrid perovskites with targeted energy level alignments. It uses an invertible 12-digit molecular fingerprint to represent conjugated diammonium organic spacers, linking spacer structure to electronic properties. Starting from 21 reported spacers, the authors generated about 4.9 million hypothetical spacers through molecular morphing and used high-throughput DFT calculations on selected candidates to train machine learning models predicting organic HOMO and LUMO levels.

The workflow combines chemical space generation, DFT calculations, interpretable machine learning, synthesis feasibility screening, and DFT validation. A LASSO regression model was selected for interpretability and identified key structural factors affecting frontier energy levels, including aromatic ring count, ammonium group structure, conjugation, and heteroatom substitution. Synthetic feasibility was assessed using PubChem availability and a formability score based on molecular descriptors relevant to DJ perovskite formation.

Screening generations G0–G6 identified DFT-validated type IIa and IIb candidates but no feasible type Ib candidates. An inverse design strategy then targeted constrained fingerprint regions beyond exhaustive enumeration, identifying two type Ib spacers, 12 type IIa candidates, and 42 type IIb candidates. Type Ib spacers required highly conjugated acene backbones, type IIa candidates were associated with extended conjugation, and type IIb spacers commonly involved nitrogen-substituted aromatic systems.

The authors conclude that the fingerprint-based workflow enables efficient and interpretable inverse design of DJ perovskites from limited data and may be adapted to other hybrid material systems and target properties. They also note limitations in representing complex molecular motifs, assessing synthesis feasibility, and the need for experimental validation.

In 2002, DEA agents destroyed Diane Monson’s medical marijuana plants despite their legality under California law, prompting Monson and Angel Raich to challenge federal authority over locally grown and used medical cannabis. Justice O’Connor and Justice Thomas dissented, warning that the ruling erased meaningful limits on Congress’ commerce power and undermined state authority. The decision was viewed as a major setback for efforts to limit federal power under the commerce clause, though later challenges, including to Obamacare’s insurance mandate, revived some limits. Thomas has continued to criticize broad commerce clause interpretations, particularly in relation to federal marijuana regulation.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for improving occlusion rendering in head-mounted device passthrough visualizations. Passthrough displays camera-captured views of a user’s physical surroundings, re-rendered from the user’s eye viewpoints using a 3D model generated from depth measurements. Because the 3D model may be inaccurate, especially near object edges, virtual objects and passthrough objects can be incorrectly occluded.

The disclosed approach uses instance segmentation masks to identify objects in captured images, such as people or pets, and assigns representative depth values to those masked objects based on the 3D model. Padded borders around masks may be assigned farther depth values to create stronger depth contrast at object edges. During rendering, the system uses mask-associated depth values, rather than only the 3D model’s measured depths, to determine whether passthrough or virtual objects should appear in front. The disclosure also describes depth estimation using stereo images, optical flow or video encoder motion vectors, 3D mesh generation, passthrough rendering, and example computing and network environments.

This study assessed molecular markers of antimalarial drug resistance in a low-transmission area of Choma District, southern Zambia, using dried blood spot samples collected through health-center and community surveillance from 2018 to 2023. The WHO-candidate Pfk13 P441L artemisinin partial resistance marker was detected in 6% of samples overall, increasing from 0% in 2018 to 7.2% in 2023, with a peak of 9.3% in 2022. P441L was found at all four health centers and in all years except 2018. Pfk13 A578S was detected in three samples from 2023. MDR1 Y184F prevalence was 41% without change over time, MDR1 N86 was present in all samples, and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance markers were common. The authors conclude that P441L is present and likely increasing in southern Zambia, exceeding the WHO 5% concern threshold, and recommend therapeutic efficacy studies, ex-vivo studies, whole-genome sequencing, and expanded molecular surveillance for emerging drug resistance.

A proper 1v1 soccer defensive stance helps a defender react quickly, stay balanced, slow or direct the attacker, avoid being beaten, and prepare to tackle. The stance typically uses one foot forward and one back, often with the dominant leg as the trail foot, feet angled and shoulder-width apart, knees bent, weight on the balls of the feet, and arms slightly out with elbows bent. Stance changes by field position: on the right side, the left foot usually leads; on the left side, the right foot leads; in the center, either foot may lead depending on play. Coaches should teach stance for right, center, and left positions, practice movement with and without the ball, and emphasize maintaining goal-side positioning without blocking or using arms to impede opponents.

The study reviews leadership models in education, including administrative/managerial, instructional, transformational, distributed, transactional, ethical, contingent, and participative leadership. It argues that no single model can fully address changing social and educational conditions, and proposes a synthetic approach that combines strengths from multiple models.

Administrative leadership provides structure, hierarchy, and clear responsibilities but may be rigid and limit innovation. Instructional leadership focuses on teaching, learning, school goals, and academic climate, but can be overly top-down and may neglect wider aspects of school life. Transformational leadership promotes vision, trust, innovation, collaboration, and professional growth, but may risk authoritarian tendencies if poorly applied. Distributed leadership encourages shared responsibility, participation, trust, and improved learning outcomes, though it can face communication problems, conflict, and reluctance among teachers to assume leadership roles.

Transactional leadership uses authority, incentives, and rewards to shape behavior and support organizational performance, but may limit innovation and long-term development. Ethical leadership emphasizes justice, respect, equality, democracy, honesty, and ethical decision-making, though conflicts may arise if ethical expectations differ within the school community. Contingent leadership stresses adaptation to specific circumstances and crises rather than fixed practices. Participative leadership involves school community members in decision-making, increasing satisfaction, morale, creativity, and ownership, but may slow decisions and create conflict or confidentiality risks.

The study concludes that educational leaders should combine models to create flexible, adaptive, ethical, and collaborative leadership suited to contemporary school challenges.

The passage describes methods and apparatus for improving user experience with electronically generated binaural or 3D sound. A key problem is that listeners may have difficulty localizing binaural sounds when the intended sound source is close to them, especially in the near-field range of less than about one meter. Near-field HRTFs can be unreliable, unavailable, or computationally intensive, while far-field HRTFs are generally less variable and easier to use.

The described embodiments process sound so that it is convolved to a location different from the visible or known sound source, often behind the sound source or along a line-of-sight from the listener to the sound source. Although the sound is processed to a farther coordinate location, the listener perceives it as originating from the visible source, such as an image on a smartphone, tablet, laptop, display, AR/VR object, or other electronic device. Volume may also be adjusted to correspond to the apparent distance of the sound source rather than the actual convolved location.

Examples include telephone or video calls in which a caller’s voice is processed with far-field HRTFs to a point behind a near-field display, while the listener perceives the voice as coming from the displayed image. Multiple sound sources may be displayed in different regions of a screen, with each voice processed to different behind-screen locations so the listener associates each voice with the correct image.

The passage also describes switching sound between binaural and mono or stereo in response to detected actions or device states. Triggers include rotating or moving a portable device, detecting or losing facial recognition, changes in gaze or head orientation, covering a camera or sensor, placing a device on a surface, changing audio output devices, or detecting low battery. These actions can change whether sound externally localizes as binaural sound or localizes internally as mono or stereo sound.

The passage investigates exchange bias in RuO2/ferromagnet heterostructures amid debate over whether rutile RuO2 intrinsically hosts altermagnetism. RuO2 thin films and TiO2/RuO2/FM/Ru heterostructures with Fe or Ni ferromagnetic layers were grown by sputtering and characterized using XRD, SQUID magnetometry, neutron diffraction, polarized neutron reflectometry, atom probe tomography, HRTEM, and EELS.

XRD confirmed epitaxial RuO2 film growth. SQUID measurements showed exchange-bias hysteresis loop shifts in RuO2/Fe/Ru heterostructures after field cooling, but polarized neutron diffraction found no detectable antiferromagnetic ordering or compensated sublattice moments in sputtered RuO2 films. Polarized neutron reflectometry showed uncompensated, field-history-dependent canted moments at the RuO2/Fe interface. APT, HRTEM, FFT analysis, and EELS indicated chemical intermixing at this interface, mainly involving iron oxide with detectable magnetite and Fe diffusion into RuO2.

Control RuO2/Ni/Ru heterostructures did not show exchange bias, while TiO2/Fe/Ru bilayers without RuO2 showed weaker exchange bias attributed to oxidation through the Ru cap. The study concludes that exchange bias in incoherent RuO2/Fe-based heterostructures arises from a magnetically active interfacial reaction layer, not intrinsic antiferromagnetic or altermagnetic ordering in RuO2.

The lecture finishes discussion of orthonormal expansions in infinite-dimensional inner product spaces. Projection onto an orthonormal set converges to the component of a vector in the span of that set, with the remaining difference orthogonal to every basis vector. This addresses issues from Fourier series, including whether the leftover term goes to zero and why inner products remain finite for arbitrary L2 functions. Truncated sinusoids and sinc-weighted sinusoids are said to span L2, and prolate spheroidal functions are introduced as an orthonormal expansion that maximizes energy concentration within given time and bandwidth limits.

The lecture then shifts to communication systems. A source is converted to binary data, then encoded into symbols, mapped to signals, and modulated into waveforms for transmission. Separating source coding, discrete encoding, and modulation is described as a layering principle that reduces system complexity, though modern systems may combine coding and modulation. The course will focus mainly on modulation rather than discrete coding.

Symbols are distinguished from signals: symbols are alphabet elements without numerical meaning, while signals are numerical values or vectors with distances. Modulation maps signal sequences to waveforms, often first at baseband and then to passband. A simple binary example maps 0 and 1 to +1 and −1, then forms a waveform using shifted sinc functions. The sinc pulse is theoretically useful but impractical because it is noncausal, starts at negative infinity, decays slowly, and would require excessive delay.

Delay and attenuation are treated as separate issues. Timing recovery lets the receiver align its clock with transmitter timing plus propagation delay, so delay is often ignored. Attenuation is handled through link budgets and signal-to-noise ratio, with decibels used because logarithms simplify multiplication of losses.

Pulse amplitude modulation (PAM) is introduced. PAM uses one-dimensional real signal constellations, typically equally spaced and symmetric around zero. For M equiprobable PAM signals, signal energy is given as d²(M²−1)/12. Larger alphabets allow more bits per signal but require energy that grows rapidly with M². Noise is not yet analyzed in detail, but signal points must be separated enough to avoid likely detection errors.

The modulation problem becomes choosing a pulse p(t) to replace the sinc pulse while controlling delay and bandwidth. A receiver may filter the received waveform with q(t), producing an equivalent composite filter g(t), the convolution of p(t) and q(t). Nyquist’s criterion says that g(t) avoids intersymbol interference if g(kT)=δk: it is 1 at zero and 0 at all other integer multiples of the symbol period. This condition is necessary and sufficient for sample-based linear reception without intersymbol interference.

Using aliasing, the ideal Nyquist condition is expressed in the frequency domain. The sinc pulse gives minimum bandwidth 1/(2T), called the Nyquist bandwidth, but has poor delay properties. Better delay requires spilling into higher frequencies. Band-edge symmetry allows filters wider than the minimum bandwidth to satisfy the Nyquist criterion. Raised cosine filters are presented as practical examples: they are flat over most of the band, taper with a raised cosine near the band edge, and are zero outside, with a rolloff parameter often around 15%.

The paper explores how a Bayesian approach can be applied to relevance-theoretic pragmatics, focusing on implicature comprehension. It contrasts explicatures, which are developed from an utterance’s logical form through contextual enrichment and reference resolution, with implicatures, which are implicit premises and conclusions supplied from context.

Using an example in which Mary answers Peter’s offer of coffee by saying she does not want energizing drinks at that time of day, the paper explains how Peter derives the explicature that Mary does not want energizing drinks at 6 pm and the implicature that she does not want coffee because coffee is an energizing drink. It also distinguishes strong implicatures, such as Mary not wanting coffee, from weaker implicatures involving other energizing drinks.

The paper reviews relevance theory’s account of communication as ostensive intention attribution. It discusses informative and communicative intentions, manifestness, relevance, and the communicative principle of relevance, according to which overt communication carries a presumption of optimal relevance. It presents the relevance-theoretic comprehension heuristic: audiences access interpretive hypotheses in order of accessibility, test them against relevance expectations, and accept the first satisfactory interpretation.

The authors compare relevance theory with Gricean pragmatics and Rational Speech Act theory. They argue that relevance theory treats comprehension as a psychologically grounded heuristic process rather than as reasoning involving literal speakers and listeners. They also emphasize that explicatures, implicatures, and contextual assumptions are adjusted in parallel during online comprehension.

The paper proposes modelling implicature comprehension probabilistically. It represents encyclopaedic knowledge as probabilistic graphs, links words such as “energizing drink” to concepts through inference rules, and models the parallel adjustment of explicatures and implicatures as a Bayesian network. Relevance expectations are represented as queries in ProbLog.

Several interpretive hypotheses are compared using Kullback-Leibler divergence between prior and posterior probability distributions over propositions, along with the size of the Herbrand base as a proxy for processing effort when KL divergence is equal. The proposed optimization model eliminates hypotheses that fail relevance expectations, prefers smaller Herbrand bases when KL values match, and otherwise selects the hypothesis with the highest KL measure.

The paper concludes that its ProbLog implementation provides an as-if optimization model of relevance-theoretic implicature comprehension. It focuses on hypothesis evaluation rather than hypothesis generation and on the audience’s comprehension process rather than the speaker’s production process, while identifying future extensions involving speaker reasoning, higher-level explicatures, and metarepresentational utterance use.

BioSafe Systems announced five strategic hires: Carleton Birk as Operations Manager in East Hartford, CT, and Tenaya Becker, Ester Mastronardi, Patrick Clark, and Kyle Pickles as Technical Sales Representatives covering regions in the USA and Canada. The new hires bring experience in operations, horticultural sales, agricultural product sales, agronomy, nursery management, water treatment, and technical support. BioSafe provided direct email contacts for each new team member and company contact information.

Georgia Institute of Technology researchers developed simulated ransomware that could control a water treatment plant by shutting valves, increasing chlorine, and showing false readings. The work highlights vulnerabilities in industrial control systems, which often have weak password and security policies and may be connected despite operators believing they are isolated. No real ransomware attacks on such control components have been reported, but researchers warn attackers may target them as other targets become harder and recommend stronger passwords, limited connections, and intrusion monitoring.

Mary Meeker’s annual Internet trends survey reported global internet usage growth slowing to 7%, with 3.6 billion users and smartphone sales stalling. Voice computing, e-commerce, subscription services, ride-hailing, and Airbnb showed growth. E-commerce reached 13% of retail sales, while unemployment was 3.9% and job openings hit 7 million.

The speaker says the team’s big win is still only one win and they remain behind in the series, though scoring multiple goals on Luongo may help confidence. He says the team was motivated by concern for Horton, who was hospitalized after what he describes as a late blindside hit, possibly with the hitter leaving his feet, and he will let the league address it. He criticizes unsportsmanlike behavior by his own players and says it is unacceptable, despite high emotions in a physical game. He praises the penalty kill, shot blocking, and defensive lanes, while noting the power play has improved by entering the zone and moving the puck better. The speaker says the team remains even-keeled, is in good spirits, values being at home, and must give fans a reason to cheer. He expects a tough response from the opponent, says both teams are physical, and notes the importance of rest and travel preparation.

The passage is a Sansa c200 manual excerpt covering recording, file transfer, media conversion, playback, settings, troubleshooting, support, warranty, licensing, and disposal. This study developed deep learning classifiers for hyper-scale medical imaging modality classification. Using 102 datasets, the authors created a multimodal dataset of millions of images covering CT, MRI, PET, and X-ray across multiple body locations. ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and VGG16 models were trained on dataset-level train/validation/test splits to avoid data leakage, with 3D scans treated as 2D slices and images resized to 224×224.

The best model, ResNet-18, achieved 96.00% test accuracy and 86.17% balanced accuracy, outperforming ResNet-50 and VGG16. Performance was high for CT, MRI, and PET, while X-ray accuracy was lower for bone X-ray datasets, suggesting the need for broader X-ray data coverage. The authors conclude that CNNs can classify hyper-scale multimodal medical image repositories with high accuracy and propose future work extending classification to 3D scans.

Chinese troops were sent to Korea after the Korean Government requested aid amid a southern rebellion, but Korean forces suppressed the rebellion before Chinese troops acted. Japan also sent troops, citing protection of Japanese subjects and its legation. Both Chinese and Japanese forces refused to withdraw first, alarming the Korean Government and foreign residents. Japanese troops occupied areas near Chemulpo, prompting protests from foreign representatives. U.S. officials, including Admiral Skerrett and Minister Sill, sought to support peaceful conditions. Sill reported that Korea’s integrity was threatened, China favored simultaneous withdrawal, Japan resisted, and the King was appealing to Japan.

The passage explains DAX trading strategies and vehicles. The DAX, or Deutscher Aktienindex, is Germany’s main equity index and includes the 40 largest or most liquid blue-chip stocks on Deutsche Börse Xetra, expanded from 30 stocks in September 2021. It is described as highly liquid, globally popular, and useful for diversification because it trades during different hours and moves differently from US markets.

DAX can be traded through futures, CFDs, and ETFs, with futures presented as the main vehicle. DAX futures trade electronically on Eurex, with full, Mini, and Micro contracts available. The passage highlights risks of futures leverage, including margin calls, while noting the market’s liquidity and low transaction costs.

The passage states that mean reversion, breakout, gap, momentum, and overnight strategies can work on DAX. It describes two overnight DAX strategies from November 2021 and November 2022, both entering at 17:30 German time and exiting at 09:00, with reported average gains of 0.22% and 0.23% per trade.

The passage argues for “educational pacifism,” the view that educational practices are just only if they do not harm innocent students. It claims mass formal schooling systems cause significant but often unnoticed harm because education is generally assumed to be beneficial. Harm is defined as negatively affecting important interests, and the passage distinguishes personal harm from more pervasive systemic harm.

Systemic educational harm is divided into structural, objective, and symbolic forms. Structural harm arises from authoritarian, hierarchical schooling practices that promote obedience, conformity, and social control. Objective harm is linked to schooling’s role in preparing students for unequal capitalist economic systems. Symbolic harm occurs through curricula, pedagogy, testing, ranking, surveillance, rewards, punishments, and institutional communication that normalize subordination and suppress autonomy, creativity, critical thinking, privacy, and self-realization.

The passage argues that such harm is morally unjust because students are generally innocent in the relevant sense: they are not harming or threatening others and therefore should not be treated merely as means to educational, social, or economic ends. It also states that mass formal schooling cannot be justified as a last resort because peaceful alternatives exist, including Montessori education and peace education.

The passage presents Montessori’s educational philosophy as broadly aligned with educational pacifism. Montessori is described as viewing education as the primary means to positive peace and as criticizing coercive, authoritarian schooling for suppressing children’s freedom, development, and natural drive to learn. Her approach emphasizes freedom, harmony, respect, prepared environments, and the development of peaceful individuals and societies.

The passage concludes that contemporary Montessorians should reject educational harm in pedagogy, curricula, and practice. It warns that some Montessori schools may reproduce harmful practices such as testing, timetabling, coercion, hierarchy, and segregation, and argues that Montessori education should provide a nonharmful alternative to mass formal schooling by prioritizing peace, liberty, justice, and respect for students.

Russ Tedrake introduces MIT’s Underactuated Robotics course, noting prerequisites in differential equations, linear algebra, and MATLAB, with no assumed prior robotics background. He motivates the topic by contrasting conservative, high-energy robots like ASIMO with passive dynamic walkers and agile biological systems such as birds, bats, albatrosses, trout, and fish using fluid dynamics. He argues many important robotics problems involve systems that cannot command accelerations in all directions.

The lecture defines fully actuated systems as those whose control input matrix has full rank equal to the dimension of the configuration variables, allowing feedback linearization. Underactuated systems have lower rank, so controls cannot directly accelerate every direction. Examples include walking robots, jumping robots, flying machines, and manipulation before force closure.

Tedrake reviews Lagrangian mechanics using a two-link robotic arm, deriving equations of motion and manipulator equations involving inertia, Coriolis, gravity, and control-input terms. Removing one motor creates an underactuated system, such as the Acrobot, requiring more sophisticated control.

He previews the course topics: nonlinear dynamics, pendulums, cart-pole and Acrobot systems, walking robots, impacts, limit cycles, higher-dimensional systems, uncertainty, unknown models, optimal control, dynamic programming, policy search, motion planning, reinforcement learning, and machine learning approaches.

The Blue Jays and Yankees will meet in a best-of-five 2025 ALDS after tying for the American League’s best record, with Toronto earning the No. 1 seed via tiebreaker. Toronto won the season series 8-5 and had a bye, while New York advanced by defeating Boston. The series starts Oct. 4, with Games 1, 2 and 5 in Toronto and Games 3 and 4 in the Bronx. Games 1 and 2 air on Fox and FS1.

Months after deep cuts to federal education research, researchers see cautious optimism as the Education Department plans to reinstate some contracts, temporarily revive regional education labs, seek input on modernizing IES, and hire for NAEP-related roles. Amber Northern’s advisory role has also encouraged some researchers. However, severe staff shortages, reduced NCES capacity, possible cuts to NAEP reporting, new data-collection demands, and ongoing uncertainty continue to raise concerns about research quality and federal education data.

Nick Mathewson introduces Tor as a volunteer-run anonymity network with about 6,000 nodes, serving hundreds of thousands to millions of users and carrying large traffic volumes. He explains that anonymity helps citizens, researchers, companies, law enforcement, and others protect privacy, though criminals also use such systems. Tor was created to support usable, low-latency anonymous web browsing rather than to solve every anonymity research problem first.

Mathewson defines anonymity as preventing an observer from linking a participant to an action, distinguishing it from unlinkability and unobservability. He describes Tor’s design: users route traffic through multiple relays, with layered encryption and symmetric keys established over circuits, so no single relay should know both source and destination. Tor does not fully protect against attackers who can observe both ends and correlate timing and volume.

He discusses design choices including relaying TCP stream contents rather than IP packets, using directory authorities to agree on available relays, and relying on large shared use because “anonymity loves company.” He notes legal and operational risks for relay operators, especially exit nodes.

The lecture covers abuse concerns, including site blocking, illegal activity, and limits of exit policies, as well as possible alternatives to IP-based blocking. Hidden services are explained as a harder responder-anonymity problem involving introduction points, directories, public keys, and planned defenses against enumeration.

Mathewson also reviews attacks such as hostile exit nodes observing unencrypted traffic, traffic tagging, denial-of-service, and cryptographic implementation errors. He briefly discusses censorship resistance through bridges and pluggable transports, related anonymity systems, and future work including improved hidden services, stronger cryptography, better path selection, congestion control, scalability, and traffic-analysis defenses.

Shares of cement and real estate-related companies traded firm in a weak market after Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced incentives to boost rural and urban housing post demonetization. Several stocks, including UltraTech Cement, Ambuja Cements, ACC, DLF, HDIL, NBCC and Godrej Properties, rose 2%-5% on the BSE, while the Sensex was down 0.39% at 26,523.

Saving penalty kicks is difficult for goalkeepers, with saves generally under 15%, while about 80% are scored and 5% missed. Goalkeepers must understand IFAB Law 14: they must face the kicker, remain between the posts, and have at least part of one foot on, in line with, or behind the goal line when the ball is kicked. Violations can lead to retakes, warnings, or cautions.

Coaches should prepare goalkeepers through regular and dedicated training, support them publicly, and avoid blaming them for missed saves. Modern guidance emphasizes “read and react” over guessing, especially because many penalties are scored up the middle. Training should include observation, repetition, equipment preparation, and study of opponents’ tendencies.

Goalkeepers should develop psychological readiness, including determination, composure, focus, and the ability to move on immediately after the kick. Mental preparation can include visualization, positive self-talk, routines, controlled breathing, and staying present. Physical preparation includes agility, diving, reaction work, footwork, and practicing how to cover reachable areas of the goal.

Goalkeepers are advised to study cues such as ball placement, the kicker’s gaze, approach angle, run-up, plant foot, hips, body lean, dominant foot, and kneecap position, while focusing only on cues that work for them. During the kick, they should stay calm, take a ready position, avoid diving early, read cues, react to the strike, and try to catch or deflect the ball safely.

After the kick, goalkeepers must respond appropriately: retrieve the ball after a goal, reset for goal or corner kicks, prepare for rebounds, start a fast break after a clean save, or retain possession. Coaches should also train teammates to follow up, cover, provide outlets, and avoid mobbing the goalkeeper after a save.

Jeff Davis Parish began the school year after summer preparations, including campus improvements, streamlined processes, staff orientations, teaching evaluations, and bus driver training. Educators focused on student success while meeting state requirements. The parish’s graduation rate is 92.5%, ranking fourth in Louisiana.

The speaker discusses a strong team performance, noting the importance of scoring first on the power play and gaining confidence after a poor previous game.
