He also explains the need to adjust defensive-zone breakouts because opponents pinch effectively along the boards. Finally, he credits Darryl with making players accountable, preventing long slumps, building mental toughness, and strengthening the team through key acquisitions.

The passage introduces metagenomic binning, the task of clustering DNA fragments from mixed microbial samples so each cluster corresponds to a genome. Existing approaches often use k-mer profiles or large language models to create deterministic embeddings, but deterministic mappings cannot resolve ambiguity when sequences appear in multiple genomes or when distinct sequences have highly similar k-mer profiles.

The authors propose UNCERTAINGEN, a probabilistic embedding framework for DNA sequences that maps each fragment to a distribution rather than a fixed point, capturing uncertainty from inter-species DNA sharing and similar representations. Their contrastive-learning formulation derives non-Euclidean distances from probability distributions and provides closed-form expected pairwise likelihoods for scalable optimization. The work claims theoretical guarantees on distinguishability, expanded latent space capacity, and empirical improvements over deterministic k-mer and LLM-based embeddings on real metagenomic datasets.

The related work section reviews k-mer methods, genome foundation models such as DNABERT variants and HYENADNA, lightweight metagenomic methods like SEMIBIN2, and probabilistic embeddings in contrastive learning. The proposed model aims to learn embeddings where sequences from the same cluster are close and different clusters are separated, building on lightweight k-mer-based contrastive binning methods that create positive pairs from halves of the same sequence and negative pairs from different sequences.

This scoping review examined barriers and facilitators to belonging in graduate health professions education and implications for occupational therapy education. From 202 identified studies, 9 articles met inclusion criteria across occupational therapy, physical therapy, and medical education. Qualitative content analysis found three main factors affecting belonging: environment, relationships, and personal traits. Physical spaces, institutional culture, faculty and peer relationships, mentorship, bias, microaggressions, students’ identities, and perceived academic ability could either support or undermine belonging. The authors conclude that occupational therapy programs should intentionally create inclusive spaces, strengthen mentorship and peer relationships, address bias, and conduct further research on belonging, especially for students from historically minoritized identities.

Actress Allison Mack was released on a $5 million bail bond to await trial on sex trafficking and conspiracy charges tied to alleged recruitment of women into a secret society within Keith Raniere’s Nxivm organization. She pleaded not guilty and will live under house arrest with her parents, whose home is collateral. Prosecutors said plea negotiations are underway. Mack is barred from contact with Raniere, Nxivm or associates. Raniere, also charged with sex trafficking, is held without bail and denies wrongdoing.

This study proposed a world model framework for autonomous endovascular navigation in mechanical thrombectomy (MT), aiming to train a single reinforcement learning agent to perform multiple navigation tasks across multiple patient vasculatures. The first MT phase was divided into five tasks from the common iliac artery to the internal carotid arteries. Simulations used the stEVE framework with industry-standard guide catheter and guidewire models, ten patient-specific aortic arch and cerebral vessel anatomies, and augmented vessel meshes.

Two reinforcement learning approaches were compared: SAC, a model-free method used as the current state-of-the-art baseline, and TD-MPC2, a model-based world model using learned dynamics and planning. Five SAC agents were first trained on individual tasks to generate replay data, then SAC and TD-MPC2 world models were trained and evaluated across all tasks and vasculatures.

Single-task SAC training achieved high success rates, including 100% for A1 and A2R and 82–92% for the remaining tasks. In multi-task world model training, TD-MPC2 achieved a significantly higher mean success rate than SAC across tasks, 65% versus 37%, and a higher mean path ratio, 73% versus 47%. TD-MPC2 significantly improved performance on A2R, A3L, and A3R, though it also increased procedure time across all tasks. Results suggest TD-MPC2 offers better multi-task generalization than SAC but remains insufficient for clinical deployment. Future work should improve generalization, expand datasets, refine planning efficiency, and incorporate more detailed simulation methods.

The Supreme Court declined to hear several cases from its Oct. 10 private conference, including Alex Jones’ appeal in a Connecticut defamation and emotional distress case brought by Sandy Hook families, and a challenge by Colorado parents alleging a school district excluded them from discussions of their children’s gender identity. Justice Alito, joined by Justices Thomas and Gorsuch, agreed with denying review in the Colorado case but expressed concern about unresolved constitutional questions involving parental rights.

The court also denied review in a case against Grindr involving Section 230 immunity, a Georgia death penalty case involving alleged juror misconduct, and a California property owners’ challenge over lack of jury trials for county code fines. Justice Sotomayor, joined by Justices Kagan and Jackson, dissented in the death penalty case. Justice Gorsuch wrote separately in the California case, saying a precedent limiting Seventh Amendment jury-trial rights against states may warrant reconsideration.

The justices requested the solicitor general’s views in two cases involving New Mexico insurance regulation and bankruptcy protections for nondebtors, and will meet again on Oct. 17.
Los Angeles County will pay nearly $12 million to the family of cyclist Milton Olin Jr., killed by a sheriff’s deputy allegedly texting and using a patrol car computer before the crash.

The passage describes a 2013–2023 global market report on household sewing machines, covering market size, forecasts, manufacturers, types, applications, costs, profits, marketing status, growth drivers, and challenges. It segments the market by region, type, and application, including mechanical and electronic sewing machines for home and light commercial use. Regions covered include North America, Europe, China, Japan, Rest APAC, and Latin America. Manufacturers analyzed include Brother, Singer, Janome, Necchi Macchina, Bernina International, Union Special, Merrow, AMF Reece, CR Consew, YAMATA, Elna International, SVP Worldwide, and Henderson Sewing. The table of contents outlines chapters on market status, regional production and demand, type and downstream industry forecasts, driving factors, competition, and manufacturer profiles.

The bankruptcy court considered summary judgment motions by Wells Fargo Bank and Dynamic Management against SCS General Contractors in Barnhill’s Buffets’ chapter 11-related adversary proceeding. SCS claimed unpaid construction balances for work on three Mississippi restaurant properties and sought equitable liens against leasehold and fee interests, as well as liability against Dynamic under an alter ego theory.

The court held that any equitable lien SCS may have had against Barnhill’s leaseholds was extinguished when Barnhill’s filed bankruptcy and became a debtor-in-possession with bona fide purchaser status. It also held SCS was not a party or third-party beneficiary to the leases and could not enforce lease obligations. As to the fee interests, the court found no lien could attach under Mississippi law because the landlords had not given written consent.

The court granted Wells Fargo’s motion for summary judgment in full and ordered the escrowed funds released to Wells, leaving SCS with an unsecured claim in the bankruptcy case. The court also granted Dynamic’s motion for summary judgment, finding SCS failed to provide sufficient evidence supporting its alter ego claim. SCS’s request for a continuance for further discovery was denied, and Spirit’s unopposed motion to dismiss was granted.

Many Westerners are reluctant to eat insects despite their nutritional value and ecological sustainability. The UN estimates about two billion people regularly eat bugs, with at least 1,900 edible species. Research on primate genomes found genes that help digest chitin in insect exoskeletons, and a Rutgers researcher noted cooking makes insects easier to chew and digest. In the U.S., cooked insects are appearing on menus; in 2017, the Seattle Mariners sold unexpectedly large quantities of roasted grasshoppers from Poquitos.

The author argues that the U.S. Department of Education should protect and strengthen the Institute of Education Sciences as it reviews the agency’s future. Recommendations from Knowledge Alliance include prioritizing research tied to urgent state and local needs, improving coordination and infrastructure, and helping districts apply evidence effectively. Suggested steps include creating learning agendas, faster research tracks, streamlined approvals, expanded rapid-cycle data tools, modernized data reporting, restarting Regional Education Laboratories and Comprehensive Centers, and requiring practitioner-facing resources for IES-funded studies. The author says these changes would make federal education research more responsive, efficient, and useful for improving student outcomes.

LG unveiled the G7 ThinQ smartphone in South Africa, positioning it as a competitive flagship against dominant brands. The device features Gorilla Glass 5, slim bezels, a bright screen, Snapdragon 845 processor, 4GB RAM, 64GB expandable storage, AI camera modes, Google Assistant and Google Lens shortcuts, dual 16MP rear cameras and an 8MP front camera. It is expected in shops in early June, starting at about R13,999.

Navy veteran Gerard Ah-Fook, whose specialized handcycle was stolen from his northwest-side home, received a replacement from stranger Randy Sooter after Sooter saw the Tucson News Now story. Ah-Fook, a competitive paracyclist, said he appreciated the generosity. Police are still searching for the stolen white “Top End Force RX” recumbent three-wheel bike.

The passage proposes a diplomatic offensive to weaken the German alliance and strengthen Allied unity. It recommends recognizing Bulgaria’s claims, Serbia’s independence and sea access, and Italy’s defensive and national frontier claims while addressing Italian economic needs. For Austria-Hungary, it advises highlighting nationality issues, German domination, and war debts, while assuring no intended dismemberment and engaging on disarmament concerns. Toward Germany, it urges linking democratization to postwar international intercourse while avoiding dictation of its government form. For Russia, it recommends stating war aims, promoting a league of nations, and showing diplomacy alongside force. It also suggests supporting French morale through attention to Alsace-Lorraine and strengthening western Allies through economic unity and liberal U.S. leadership.

Suggested peace terms include German evacuation and restoration of Belgium and northern France, leaving Luxemburg to negotiation, and undoing Germany’s 1871 seizure of Alsace-Lorraine.

Entrepreneur contributors share strategies for improving focus and reducing distractions. Lewis Howes recommends acting with urgency, clarifying goals, overcoming fear, and tracking daily progress. Mark Divine advises working one to two days a week in a distraction-free location, using breathing, visualization, 45-minute work blocks, movement, and yoga. Chris Harder suggests accepting only “heck-yes” opportunities and using a small advisory board to help decline distractions. Kenny Rueter recommends removing unnecessary tasks, choosing one top priority, and completing it before moving on. Nafisé Nina Hodjat says focus comes naturally when work becomes an obsession. Nik Halik outlines a five-step approach: use stress productively, develop a morning routine, work in 90-minute blocks, create recharge rituals, and optimize sleep. Tom Shieh recommends scheduling areas of focus to avoid divided attention. Peter Hernandez emphasizes building an organizational culture where each person has clear purpose, measurable goals, and filters new opportunities through that purpose.

Devro shares have risen nearly 25% since January. First-half sales increased 11% to just over £125m, supported by demand in Russia, south-east Asia and China, where a new plant is expected to reach full capacity by year-end.

The passage describes a patent disclosure for an AI-assisted activity training system, method, and computer program product. The system presents activity categories and activities to a user through a rendering device such as a smart mirror or display. The user provides voice-based input in a source language to select activities and attributes such as repetitions, sets, intervals, difficulty, pace, and sequence. An NLP model configured in a single intermediate language processes the input and extracts the training plan.

The system presents multimedia guidance, including steps performed by a virtual assistant or instructor. An AI model processes the video and data in real time to extract performance parameters, compare them with target parameters, and generate feedback. The disclosure includes embodiments using smart mirrors, display devices, gymnasium camera systems, central servers, live or recorded training broadcasts, social sharing, activity circuits, playlists, custom activity creation, multilingual interaction, and multimedia editing. Graphical interfaces may display activity categories, selected exercises, performance metrics, goals, dashboards, calendar schedules, device connections, themes, and language options. The system may also support prioritization of feedback messages, initial pose detection, camera focus changes, infrared mode, side-by-side performance comparison, and sharing of recorded or augmented activity content.

More than 3,400 students are expected to receive degrees during the University of North Texas fall 2017 commencement ceremonies Dec. 15-16 in Denton at the UNT Coliseum and Murchison Performing Arts Center. Eligible fall graduates include 2,731 undergraduates, 615 master’s students and 72 doctoral students, with some summer graduates also attending. Bachelor’s ceremonies run Dec. 15-16 by college, and the master’s and doctoral ceremony is 7 p.m. Dec. 15 at the Coliseum. Live streams will be available. UNT will also hold a special commencement ceremony in New Orleans at 6:15 p.m. Dec. 15 for graduates attending the New Orleans Bowl; students must RSVP. A reception for master’s and doctoral candidates follows Dec. 15 at the Gateway Center.

Strength training can build muscle mass, strength and endurance, but poor technique, inadequate warm-up or cool-down, excessive intensity, and inappropriate weights can cause injuries. Common injuries include rotator cuff injuries, hamstring strains or tears, herniated discs, tendonitis, and tennis or golfer’s elbow. Prevention includes good posture, proper form, stretching, warming up, cooling down, limiting repetitive forceful movements, working within personal limits, increasing intensity gradually, and allowing recovery time. Persistent pain, discomfort, or suspected injury should be assessed by a doctor, and beginners may benefit from guidance from a qualified fitness instructor. Rest, hydration, good diet, ice, compression, elevation, medicines, physiotherapy, injections, or surgery may be used depending on the injury and severity.

VentureWire’s October 31, 2000 issue reports that Trinity Ventures closed Trinity VIII, a $540 million early-stage fund focused on software, communications and online business infrastructure. Sun Microsystems plans to invest an additional $100 million in wireless companies over the next year. Online textbook retailer BigWords.com ceased operations on October 20 after previously raising $30 million. The Supreme Court appointed senior counsel Amarendra Sharan as amicus curiae to examine material submitted by petitioner Pankaj Kumud Chandra Phadnis seeking a fresh inquiry into the alleged larger conspiracy behind Mahatma Gandhi’s assassination. Phadnis challenged a Bombay High Court order rejecting his plea, alleging British Secret Service Force 136 involvement and calling the original investigation a cover-up.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its 2017 Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2017. The company is incorporated in Delaware, headquartered in Seattle, Washington, and its common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under “AMZN.” As of June 30, 2017, voting stock held by non-affiliates had an aggregate market value of $387.3 billion, and 484.1 million common shares were outstanding as of January 24, 2018.

Amazon operates through three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services. It serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators, and also provides advertising services and co-branded credit card agreements. Consumer offerings include retail websites, physical stores, electronic devices, media content, and Amazon Prime. AWS provides compute, storage, database, and other services. Whole Foods Market results were included from the August 28, 2017 acquisition date.

The company describes its market as rapidly evolving and intensely competitive, with competitors across retail, media, search, e-commerce services, logistics, cloud services, and consumer electronics. Key risk factors include intense competition, expansion challenges, international operating risks, fulfillment and data center risks, seasonality, acquisitions and investments, foreign exchange exposure, data breaches, system interruptions, inventory risk, intellectual property disputes, regulatory changes, tax liabilities, supplier risks, government contracts, product liability, payments-related risks, and seller fraud or unlawful activity.

Amazon employed approximately 566,000 full-time and part-time employees as of December 31, 2017. It operated approximately 240.0 million leased square feet and 14.0 million owned square feet of facilities, including offices, physical stores, fulfillment centers, data centers, and other facilities. Whole Foods Market had 465 North America and 7 International open stores at year-end.

For 2017, Amazon reported net sales of $177.9 billion, operating income of $4.1 billion, net income of $3.0 billion, basic earnings per share of $6.32, diluted earnings per share of $6.15, operating cash flow of $18.4 billion, total assets of $131.3 billion, and total long-term obligations of $45.7 billion. Net sales increased from $135.99 billion in 2016 and $107.01 billion in 2015. The company has never declared or paid cash dividends and reported no recent sales of unregistered securities or issuer purchases of equity securities.

The lecture introduces graph limits as analytic objects that represent limiting behavior of graph sequences, motivated by analogy with completing rational numbers to real numbers. A graphon is defined as a symmetric measurable function from \([0,1]^2\) to \([0,1]\), serving as a limit object for graphs.

Graphs can be represented as graphons by converting their adjacency matrices into pixelated functions on the unit square. Examples include half graphs converging to a triangular region, quasirandom graphs of edge density \(p\) converging to the constant graphon \(p\), and checkerboard patterns illustrating the need to account for vertex rearrangements.

The lecture defines graph homomorphisms, homomorphism counts, and homomorphism densities \(t(H,G)\), interpreted as the probability that a random vertex map from \(H\) to \(G\) preserves edges. For graphons, homomorphism densities are defined by integrals over products corresponding to the edges of \(H\), agreeing with graph densities when a graph is converted to its associated graphon.

A sequence of graphs or graphons is called convergent if \(t(H,G_n)\) converges for every fixed graph \(H\). To connect this with a metric notion of convergence, the lecture introduces the cut norm and cut distance. The cut norm maximizes the absolute integral of a function over measurable rectangles \(S \times T\). The cut distance between graphons minimizes the cut norm difference over measure-preserving transformations, accounting for vertex relabeling and more general rearrangements.

Three main theorems are stated: convergence of homomorphism densities is equivalent to being Cauchy in cut distance; every convergent graph or graphon sequence has a limit graphon; and the space of graphons, modulo distance zero, is compact. This compactness is related to Szemerédi’s Regularity Lemma and to quasirandomness, where constant graphons represent quasirandom graph limits.

An Enron email forwarded several media mentions from Oct. 15–16, 2000. A Wall Street Journal article described three small entrepreneurs who won Strategic Petroleum Reserve oil bids; Renard Euell sought Enron backing for a $93 million letter of credit, but Enron said no deal existed and his award lapsed. Five-year-old Angel, born in a Pakistani slum, has rare CLOVES syndrome, causing her feet to swell severely and leaving her in constant pain. Brought to Australia 18 months ago by humanitarian Moira Kelly, she arrived malnourished and too weak for surgery. After being bullied, refused school entry, and told by Pakistani doctors she could not be treated, Angel is now set to undergo a free double amputation in Melbourne by paediatric plastic and reconstructive surgeon Professor Tony Pennington. Kelly says Angel understands she will lose both feet and parts of her legs but is happy because she wants to wear shoes and dance.

Tesla Motors reported voting results from its May 31, 2016 Annual Meeting of Stockholders. Brad W. Buss and Ira Ehrenpreis were elected as Class III directors for three-year terms. Stockholders approved ratification of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as the company’s independent registered public accounting firm for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2016. The Centre has empowered CGST officers to verify all transitional credit claims under GST, regardless of whether taxpayers are administratively assigned to the Centre or states. CBEC said only authorities with jurisdiction under earlier laws and taxpayer records can conduct verification. Taxpayers have claimed Rs 1.6 lakh crore in transitional credits, though preliminary enquiries found only 5-7% invalid. Experts warned the move could cause Centre-state litigation. CBEC also indicated the CGST Act would be amended to exclude credit for cesses paid under the previous regime.

Attorney General Patrick Morrisey renewed a contract with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission allowing West Virginia investigators to check stores for recalled non-food products and proper recall notices. Since 2015, investigators have conducted more than 40 compliance checks and expect 25 additional searches between February and September.

The passage describes AGESA software integration requirements for host environments, including stack setup, call-out routing, UEFI build organization, boot-phase drivers, configuration files, environment variables, and initialization entry points. The host environment must establish stack support, implement a call-out router and required call-outs, preserve AGESA data across boot phases, and avoid modifying cache controls or core communication settings during specified initialization periods.

AGESA UEFI support spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases, with separate libraries and build targets for 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit execution. Platform options are configured through files such as `<Plat>Options.c`, with required variables including `AGESA_ROOT`, `AGESA_OptsDir`, and the platform solution name.

The passage details PEIM and DXE responsibilities, including processor initialization, memory initialization, reset coordination, late initialization, table generation, and VGA control for processor GPU resources. It also describes reference files, build control files, and recommended integration steps such as enabling Cache-as-RAM before `AmdInitReset`.

Core AGESA procedures include stack enable/disable macros, structure allocation and release, event log reading, MMIO range updates, processor and memory identification helpers, and cache-size queries. Published initialization entry points include `AmdInitReset`, `AmdInitEarly`, `AmdInitPost`, `AmdInitEnv`, graphics-related initialization, `AmdInitLate`, `AmdInitRtb`, and resume-path procedures. These routines initialize processors, memory, graphics, chipset interfaces, ACPI/DMI data tables, suspend state, and resume state.

Required host call-outs include buffer allocation, buffer deallocation, and system reset. These must provide memory services after main memory is available, manage persistent runtime buffers when required, and initiate cold or warm resets as requested.

The CCAT Collaboration is constructing the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope in Chile, with observations planned for 2026. Its Mod-Cam testbed and Prime-Cam science instrument will conduct broadband polarimetric and spectroscopic observations using large KID detector arrays. The paper characterizes flexible stripline circuits used to connect cryogenic detectors to readout electronics.

Measurements of Mod-Cam stripline copper traces found an RRR of about 120 and thermal conductivity consistent with literature values for OFHC copper. Thermal-loading estimates indicate that redesigned Prime-Cam striplines should reduce 4 K loading despite supporting more readout lines. Crosstalk testing showed that the stripline itself met requirements, while elevated crosstalk originated in SMP-SMA transition PCBs. Redesigned PCBs using buried signal traces are simulated to improve isolation and meet project requirements. The results support flexible stripline circuits as a scalable readout solution for large KID arrays.

Tesla Motors, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated October 2, 2015, reporting that it published a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1. The information was furnished under Items 2.02 and 7.01 and was not deemed filed under the Exchange Act unless specifically incorporated by reference.

The passage presents options-based strategies for investors seeking exposure to potential upside in AMD ahead of its Q1 2018 earnings announcement without immediately buying shares outright. The author notes AMD had traded in a range of about $9.30 to $15.13 and was near $10, which they viewed as a supported level.

The first strategy is buying a May 4, 2018 $10 call option for about $0.60, risking $60 per contract instead of spending $1,000 for 100 shares. The second is a $10/$12 call spread, buying the $10 call and selling the $12 call to reduce net cost to $0.50, with gains capped above $12. The third is selling a cash-covered $10 put for about $0.56, which could either generate premium if AMD stays above $10 or result in assignment of 100 shares with a $9.44 cost basis if AMD falls below $10.

The author also describes combining the put sale with the call spread, creating a net $0.06 credit but adding assignment risk if AMD closes below $10. The author says they are long AMD, INTC, and NVDA and believes AMD may benefit from earnings, product improvements, processor demand, market share opportunities, and a large short position.

Police arrested 37-year-old Jason A. Clifford after witnesses said he tried to break into southeast Portland apartments while threatening to kill people and carrying a slungshot. He was booked on burglary, weapon, menacing, coercion and theft charges. Two others in the apartment were arrested on outstanding warrants but were not believed involved.

President Donald Trump will direct U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer to decide whether to investigate Chinese trade practices that allegedly force U.S. firms to transfer intellectual property. Officials said the possible Section 301 probe is unrelated to U.S. efforts to secure China’s help on North Korea, though Trump has linked his trade stance toward Beijing to its cooperation on Pyongyang. Any investigation could take up to a year and might lead to tariffs or other restrictions, though officials said outcomes remain undecided and could include a negotiated agreement. The European Union, Japan, Germany and Canada have also expressed concern about Chinese intellectual property theft.

WIRED reviews white-noise and sound machines for sleep, noting that many devices also play pink noise, brown noise, fan sounds, nature sounds, and lullabies. For children, the passage advises keeping sound machines no louder than 50 decibels and more than 200 centimeters from where a baby sleeps.

The LectroFan Classic is described as a compact favorite with fan sounds, multiple colored-noise options, a 60-minute timer, and volume up to 85 decibels. The Snooz uses a real fan to generate white noise and is designed for simple use and central room placement. Hatch models combine sound machines with lights, clocks, app controls, and optional subscriptions; the Hatch Rest adds child-focused time-to-rest and time-to-rise features. The Babelio mini sound machine is presented as useful for pets, with timers and multiple noise options. Yogasleep’s Dohm is a simple fan-based machine with two settings, suitable for masking sound.

Portable options include Momcozy’s sound machine with night-light, Bluetooth, timers, and multiple sounds; ErgoPouch’s rechargeable device with a soft night-light; and smaller travel machines with varied sound and timer options. The passage also notes that Google and Alexa speakers can play ambient sleep sounds. Some tested models are described as less preferred due to price, audio quality, controls, or reliability. WIRED says its recommendations are selected independently, and tested products are donated after review.

The passage describes the Inverted Hammer candlestick pattern as a single-candle formation with a small body near the lower end, little or no lower shadow, and a long upper shadow. It commonly appears during a downward price swing and is often treated as a potential bullish reversal signal, especially near support levels or during pullbacks in an uptrend. The pattern suggests buyers may be gaining momentum against sellers, but the passage stresses that it should be confirmed with tools such as trendlines, support levels, moving averages, momentum oscillators, volume, and RSI.

The passage recommends backtesting candlestick strategies and using defined trading rules rather than relying on anecdotal evidence. It says the pattern can be used in swing trading, mean reversion strategies, and long entries after confirmation. Suggested risk controls include stop-loss orders below the pullback low, position sizing, diversification, and profit targets near resistance or based on a 2:1 reward/risk ratio.

Backtests cited in the passage report 132 Inverted Hammer occurrences in SPY/S&P 500 since 1993, a win ratio of 53% to 65% over 1–10 trading days, a 70% win rate in another ranking, and an average gain of 0.36% per trade. The passage also states the pattern occurs more often in overbought conditions than oversold ones and may be bearish when appearing after recent market strength, while tending to be more bullish during downturns. It distinguishes the Inverted Hammer from the Shooting Star, which appears after price has risen and may signal decline.

Violet Brown of Duanvale, Jamaica, celebrated her 117th birthday and is believed to have become the world’s oldest living person after the death of Italy’s Emma Morano. The Gerontology Research Group says Brown, born March 10, 1900, has credible birth documentation, though Guinness World Records has not yet confirmed a new title holder. Brown, a former sugarcane farmer, lives with her 97-year-old son, has two caregivers, and credits hard work and her Christian faith for her long life.

A UC Davis study of 50,921 firearm deaths in California from 2000 to 2015 found gun deaths declined, largely due to reduced gang violence and fewer black homicide victims. Firearm homicides fell from 4.19 per 100,000 people in 2000 to 3.13 in 2014, then rose slightly in 2015. Black male gun homicides dropped 32% from 2005 to 2015, while Hispanic male homicides declined 38%. Researchers hope the study informs further research, as California and private foundations have recently increased funding for gun violence studies.

Digital laggards often set aspirational goals that are not grounded in data and are viewed by employees as unrealistic, leading teams to avoid measurement and rely on qualitative “best effort” approaches. This focus on process over objective metrics can discourage deviation and stifle innovation.

Digital leaders use structured, data-driven goals and transparent metrics to align teams with company strategy, while allowing flexibility in process. Their objectives often connect individual and team work to broader organizational goals, creating shared purpose. However, excessive reliance on data can slow simple decisions and reduce the role of human judgment.

Data culture supports both vertical alignment, by linking individuals and groups to company goals, and horizontal alignment, by enabling collaboration through shared data models and transparent access. Digital leaders emphasize learning, transparency, measurement, and alignment as central to culture, while laggards often recognize the importance of data culture but struggle due to entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient leadership focus.

The passage identifies four patterns in data transformation: data novices, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant. Each reflects different strengths and gaps in culture, technology, or decision-making, and organizations can use these patterns to target improvements toward a stronger data culture.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture, as an 8th-generation data center GPU designed for AI, HPC, and data analytics. It builds on Volta V100 and Turing GPUs with third-generation Tensor Cores, new data type support, structured sparsity, Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitioning, faster NVLink, PCIe Gen 4, larger caches, higher memory bandwidth, and CUDA 11 software features.

A100 is fabricated on TSMC’s 7nm process and includes 54.2 billion transistors. It provides 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, and 108 SMs with 432 third-generation Tensor Cores. It supports TF32, FP16, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary operations. Compared with V100, A100 delivers major speedups, including 10x faster TF32 versus V100 FP32, 2.5x faster FP16/FP32 mixed precision, 2.5x faster FP64, and up to 20x faster sparse INT8.

MIG allows a single A100 to be divided into as many as seven isolated GPU instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory bandwidth, and fault isolation, improving utilization for cloud, enterprise, and multi-tenant environments. Third-generation NVLink doubles total GPU bandwidth versus V100 to 600 GB/sec, while PCIe Gen 4 doubles PCIe bandwidth over PCIe 3.0. A100 also improves error detection, isolation, and containment.

CUDA 11 adds support for A100 features including Tensor Cores, sparsity, MIG, task graph acceleration, asynchronous copy, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, and Cooperative Groups improvements. A100 also includes NVJPG JPEG decode, improved NVDEC video decoding, optical flow acceleration, and faster atomic operations.

The passage also describes DGX A100, a system with eight A100 GPUs interconnected by NVLink and NVSwitch, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and supporting up to 56 isolated GPU instances through MIG. DGX A100 is positioned for scalable AI infrastructure using NVIDIA software, NGC containers, CUDA, Magnum IO, Mellanox InfiniBand, and Kubernetes or Slurm clusters.

This study evaluates a handheld ISFET Lab-on-Chip device using RT-pHLAMP to detect circulating prostate cancer nucleic acid biomarkers from blood plasma. It focuses on YAP1 nucleic acid and AR-FL and AR-V7 mRNA as potential prognostic markers, aiming to support faster, minimally invasive point-of-care testing compared with PSA, biopsy, RT-qPCR, and ddPCR approaches.

TRIzol LS extraction enabled detection of spiked and patient-derived RNA, while direct plasma testing did not amplify patient samples. Benchtop RT-pHLAMP detected YAP1 nucleic acid in 62% of tested patient samples and showed strong concordance with RT-qPCR, except one low-concentration sample. AR-FL RT-pHLAMP showed 100% concordance with a large-fragment AR-FL RT-qPCR assay, and YAP1 detection was concordant in 12 of 13 samples with RT-qPCR assays.

The ISFET Lab-on-Chip device simultaneously detected YAP1 nucleic acid and AR-FL mRNA, with 100% concordance to benchtop RT-pHLAMP results. YAP1 positivity was associated with higher cancer staging and higher initial PSA. AR-FL mRNA was detected in high-risk or metastatic patients, and AR-V7 mRNA was detected in one metastatic patient. The authors conclude that the device can rapidly detect circulating prostate cancer nucleic acid markers after RNA extraction and may support point-of-care prognostic testing, though larger cohorts and point-of-care-compatible extraction methods are needed.

Mark Schroeder says the EU summary is useful for a quick overview but notes errors and omissions: Spain’s pool is not mandatory for generators that can bypass it, Denmark has more than two generators due to municipal ownership, Dutch transitional anti-competitive arrangements are not addressed, and Poland is omitted despite being described as the most progressive former Communist country.

It says governments are increasingly opening generation markets to foreign investors, unbundling state-owned utilities, and introducing wholesale and retail competition. Europe’s restructuring is driven by the EU Directive, with mergers and trading activity increasing. Central and Eastern European countries seeking EU membership are restructuring and privatizing, though progress varies. Asian governments are resuming reform after the economic crisis, while IPPs face PPA and guarantee issues. Latin American privatizations have restarted more slowly amid currency, inflation, drought, and ownership-limit concerns. African and Middle Eastern countries are opening mainly to IPPs, with regional transmission links emerging as a notable trend.

European shares rebounded Monday after their worst weekly losses of the year amid U.S.-North Korea tensions. The STOXX 600 rose 0.7%, led by banks. RWE, Danone, Standard Life Aberdeen and Fiat Chrysler gained, while Ladbrokes Coral fell. Energy and basic materials led earnings, while consumer cyclical and industrial firms lagged.

A study by Rand Corporation, Harvard Medical School, and UCLA found that many American workers experience demanding, unhealthy, or hostile workplaces. One in five reported a hostile or threatening social environment, women cited unwanted sexual attention, and young men reported verbal abuse. Still, most workers found their jobs meaningful, and over half described their boss as supportive.

Compass Minerals International prepared for its IPO on December 12, 2003, after Apollo Management acquired the business from IMC Global in 2001. CEO Michael Ducey considered investor expectations, future strategy, and how to sustain performance as a public company.

Salt was widely used in highway deicing and in chemical, food-processing, water-treatment, and agricultural industries. Production methods included rock salt mining, mechanical evaporation, and solar evaporation, with costs and purity varying by method. U.S. salt demand had grown over the 20th century, driven partly by chemicals and especially by highway deicing, though deicing demand fluctuated with winter severity.

The U.S. salt industry had consolidated significantly over time, from many producers in earlier decades to 29 firms operating 66 dry-salt establishments by the early 2000s. Production was capital intensive, transportation costs were high relative to product value, and plant location strongly affected markets, particularly for deicing salt. Highway deicing salt was generally sold through bids to public agencies and contractors.

Road salt created growing environmental concerns because dissolved sodium and chloride accumulated in soils and waterways, harming plants and freshwater ecosystems. Researchers found rising chloride concentrations in northeastern U.S. streams, especially where paved surfaces increased. Road salt was not regulated as a freshwater pollutant in the United States, but possible regulation posed a future threat.

Compass Minerals’ North American Salt was the third-largest U.S. salt producer. Its business included general trade salt, highway deicing, chemicals, and sulphate of potash. In 2002, general trade salt produced just over half of North American Salt’s revenue, while highway deicing accounted for about 40% of salt sales. The company operated mines and plants in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom, with major capacity at Goderich, Ontario; Cote Blanche, Louisiana; Ogden, Utah; and Winsford, Cheshire. Ducey emphasized safety, workforce development, operational execution, and core values while facing both regulatory risks and potential new uses for salt mines.

In his sixth and final State of the Union assessment, the President described ongoing national challenges including urban unrest, poverty, welfare pressures, education, crime, Vietnam, the Middle East, nuclear dangers, and relations with Communist powers. He emphasized national strengths such as the economy, democracy, exploration, public judgment, and a commitment to justice.

He reviewed achievements of the past five years, including Medicare, voting rights, federal education aid, Head Start, college assistance, conservation, job training for five million Americans, low unemployment, and job growth. He urged Congress to continue funding commitments in housing, model cities, an urban development bank, Social Security increases, maternal and child health care, protection from catastrophic illness, antipoverty efforts, job training, civil rights enforcement, voting rights extension, crime reduction funds, firearms licensing and registration, postal reorganization, congressional salary changes, and draft reform.

He reported projected budget surpluses, supported temporarily extending the surtax, and stressed resisting inflation while maintaining prosperity. On foreign policy, he called for ratification of the nonproliferation treaty, renewed missile talks with the Soviet Union, adequate economic assistance, support for European unity, liberal trade, monetary stability, and continued pursuit of peace in Vietnam and the Middle East.

He closed by reflecting on his years in public service, thanking congressional leaders and former Presidents, urging cooperation with President-elect Nixon, and expressing hope that their work made the country more just and protected liberty for future generations.

The passage studies optimal pricing for a monopolist selling a single expiring item, such as an event ticket, to strategic buyers who arrive stochastically. The item becomes worthless at expiration, making the seller time-sensitive, while buyers are modeled as time-neutral and may delay purchases to seek lower prices while risking stockout from competing buyers.

The model is formulated as a Stackelberg game: the seller commits to a continuous non-increasing pricing schedule over a finite horizon, and buyers observe it upon arrival and choose target purchase times based on private valuations and arrival times. Buyer arrivals follow a Poisson process, and valuations are uniformly distributed.

The paper’s first contribution is a tractable equilibrium framework using Value-Based Threshold strategies, which map buyer valuations to target purchase times. It derives necessary and sufficient conditions for equilibrium existence and uniqueness in a continuous valuation setting.

The second contribution is deriving near-optimal pricing schedules for thin and thick markets. In thin markets with little buyer competition, the optimal policy is a constant price that removes incentives to wait. In thick markets with intense competition, buyers act myopically, and the optimal policy is a linear discounting schedule. Numerical simulations validate these policies and show that pricing shifts from end-loaded to flat to front-loaded as seller time sensitivity increases.

The passage also contrasts the paper with prior dynamic pricing literature by assigning time-dependent disutility only to the seller, reflecting expiring-item markets where seller-side time pressure dominates.

The toss play is an outside run in which the quarterback tosses the ball to a running back aiming for the edge of the defense. It is widely used because it is simple to teach, quick to execute, and effective with fast tailbacks and athletic offensive linemen who can block in space. Its main weaknesses are reliance on the right personnel and vulnerability to edge blitzes or overload pressure. The passage outlines blocking responsibilities for toss from the I Formation against 3-4 and 4-3 fronts, emphasizing reach blocks, combination blocks, a fullback leading to the nearest unblocked defender, and receivers handling safeties or cornerbacks. Variations include Flexbone or “Rocket Toss,” which uses motion to get the ball outside quickly, and Single Back Toss G Pull, which uses the playside guard as the lead blocker instead of a fullback.

The speaker says the opponent’s neutral-zone play and backchecking have limited space. Their team plans adjustments, including on the power play, and hopes to improve, recover previous form, and tie the series.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting results from its December 4, 2019 Annual Shareholders Meeting. Of 7,632,138,696 shares entitled to vote, 6,610,123,128 were voted in person or by proxy. Shareholders elected all 13 director nominees, approved named executive officer compensation on an advisory basis, and ratified Deloitte & Touche LLP as independent registered public accounting firm for fiscal year 2020. Shareholders rejected proposals requesting reports on employee representation on the Board of Directors and on the gender pay gap. The report was signed December 5, 2019 by Assistant Secretary Keith R. Dolliver.

The speaker discusses playoff discipline, improved penalty killing, and staying focused game by game within the team’s system. They emphasize wearing opponents down, limiting access to the net, improving defensively, creating more traffic in front of the opposing goalie, and maintaining confidence from a previous series comeback. They also comment on fan reactions and joke about whether the winning team is allowed to keep the puck.

Diane David appealed the dissolution judgment ending her marriage to Joseph David, challenging the award of the marital farm to Joseph, the property division, and the failure to consider tax consequences if she liquidated retirement assets awarded to her. The parties had agreed to joint legal custody, Diane’s primary physical custody, Joseph’s visitation, and $710 monthly child support.

The Court of Appeals held that awarding the marital residence and farm to Joseph, though he was the noncustodial parent, was not an abuse of discretion because the trial court could weigh all statutory factors and evidence, including Joseph’s ability to farm the tillable acreage. The court also found no binding stipulation requiring an equal property division and held that the trial court could consider Diane’s separate teacher retirement account, while distinguishing precedent limiting the impact of such consideration. The court rejected Diane’s tax-consequence argument because it was raised for the first time on appeal.

However, the appellate court found a mathematical error: the trial court calculated Diane’s awarded assets as $62,781, but the appellate calculation using the trial court’s values was $59,182. Because this affected the property distribution, the judgment was vacated and remanded for reconsideration of the property division.

The Red Cross Society of Ghana is appealing for ambulances to support healthcare delivery, saying it has personnel to operate them. Its only ambulance, donated by the Chinese Red Cross Society, has broken down due to engine problems. Ghana has 55 functioning ambulances for 29 million people, while the government has begun processes to procure 275 more.

A player discusses excitement for the Stanley Cup Finals, emphasizing discipline, staying out of penalties, improving the power play, and playing hard every night. He says the opponent is highly skilled, talented, and the NHL’s best team, requiring smart, patient play with few turnovers. He praises his linemates Krejci and Lucic and says scoring against a top goaltender will require traffic in front of the net.

The passage is an excerpt from a Texas Instruments TMS320DM8127 DaVinci Digital Media Processor data manual. It describes the C674x floating-point DSP core, which is code-compatible with earlier C64x and C67x DSP generations and includes 32KB L1 program memory, 32KB L1 data memory, and 256KB L2 RAM with ECC. L1 memory can be configured as cache or noncacheable no-wait-state memory, and C674x L3 and off-chip memory accesses route through a system MMU.

The device includes an ARM Cortex-A8 subsystem for configuration and control of subsystems, peripherals, and external memories. It supports ARMv7 ISA features, debug and trace support, caches, NEON, VFPv3, an interrupt controller, and PLL-based clocking. The DSP subsystem includes a C674x CPU with eight functional units, two register files, two data paths, compact instructions, exception handling, privilege modes, and a time-stamp counter.

The manual excerpt covers device overview, memory maps, boot modes, pin multiplexing, operating conditions, power/reset/clocking/interrupts, peripherals, and mechanical information. It lists peripherals including DDR2/DDR3 controllers, EMAC, GPIO, GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP, McBSP, MMC/SD/SDIO, PCIe, SPI, timers, UART, USB, video input/output, HDVPSS, ISS, EDMA, and DCAN. It also describes modules such as HDVICP2 video acceleration, face detection, spinlocks, and mailbox communication.

The revision history notes updates from revisions A through C, including OPP combination support, RXACTIVE pin-control functionality, latch-up ratings, System MMU terminology, DDR3-1066 support, power sequencing changes, clock timing updates, EDMA register descriptions, DDR interface updates, and pin multiplexing corrections.

Tesla’s 2016 Form 10-K identifies Tesla, Inc. as a Delaware corporation headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with common stock listed on NASDAQ. For the year ended December 31, 2016, Tesla operated two reportable segments: automotive, and energy generation and storage. As of January 31, 2017, it had 161,670,428 common shares outstanding.

Tesla designs, develops, manufactures and sells fully electric vehicles, energy storage systems, and solar and energy storage products. In 2016, it produced and sold the Model S sedan and Model X SUV, and planned volume production and deliveries of the lower-priced Model 3 in the second half of 2017. Tesla also planned additional consumer and commercial electric vehicles. Its vehicle benefits include long range, charging flexibility, performance, over-the-air software updates, energy efficiency, and expected lower maintenance costs.

Tesla sells vehicles through company-owned stores, galleries, Service Plus locations and service centers, with 265 locations worldwide as of December 31, 2016. It also operated 790 Supercharger stations and had more than 7,110 wall connectors at over 4,140 destination charging locations. Vehicle service was provided through company-owned service centers, Service Plus sites and mobile Tesla Rangers; Tesla owned and operated 135 service locations at year-end 2016.

Tesla’s energy storage products include Powerwall 2 and Powerpack 2, produced at Gigafactory 1 beginning in the fourth quarter of 2016. These products support residential, commercial, industrial and utility applications. Through the November 21, 2016 acquisition of SolarCity, Tesla also sells renewable energy systems and services. SolarCity had installed solar energy systems for more than 325,000 customers since 2006. Tesla announced a solar roof in October 2016 and expected production at Gigafactory 2 in Buffalo, New York, in summer 2017, with installations later in 2017.

Tesla’s technology includes battery packs, power electronics, dual motor powertrains, vehicle control and infotainment software, and autopilot systems. In October 2016, Tesla began equipping vehicles with hardware intended for full self-driving capability, while stating drivers remain responsible for vehicle control.

Tesla manufactures vehicles and components at facilities in Fremont and Lathrop, California, and Tilburg, Netherlands. Gigafactory 1 near Reno, Nevada, is intended to integrate battery material, cell, module and pack production, support Model 3 and energy storage products, and reach full production capacity by 2020. Tesla also manufactures solar products in Fremont and at Gigafactory 2. Its supply chain uses hundreds of global suppliers, though many components come from single sources.

The filing describes government incentives, regulatory credits, vehicle safety and battery transport regulations, dealer licensing issues, energy storage policy developments, solar tax credits, net metering, and renewable portfolio standards. Tesla competes with established automakers, alternative fuel vehicle manufacturers, energy storage companies, utilities, and solar companies. It seeks to protect intellectual property but has pledged not to sue parties infringing its patents through electric-vehicle-related activity if acting in good faith.

Key risks include delays or complications in launching and ramping production of vehicles, energy storage products and the solar roof; uncertainty around Model 3 production timelines, costs and volumes; supplier dependence and single-source components; consumer adoption of electric vehicles; Gigafactory 1 expansion and operation; product defects; international expansion; manufacturing cost control; reliance on a limited vehicle lineup; lithium-ion battery safety; raw material costs and availability; product liability; and intense competition.

VentureWire’s May 22, 2001 issue reports venture funding, acquisitions, layoffs, executive changes, and fund news. Top stories include Kodiak Venture Partners closing a $290 million second fund, Mercury Interactive acquiring Freshwater Software for $147 million, Celetron raising a $48 million first round, and TVM’s first close of a new life sciences fund at EUR 70 million. Funding news includes rounds for CGtime, Lawson Software, NetContinuum, Danger, FlightTime, NuVasive, MiFund, ViAir, SeeCommerce, Zinio Systems, Antrim Design Systems, and others. Bad news includes staff cuts at AgWeb and Ironmax and Rx.com ceasing prescription fulfillment. The issue also covers product launches, M&A deals, board appointments, executive hires, a University of Pittsburgh-Redleaf startup funding program, VC personnel changes, and corrections from prior coverage.

Three George Washington University Alpha Phi sorority members will be removed from the chapter after a racist Snapchat image circulated online. The chapter apologized, acknowledged issues with privilege and diversity, and said membership termination is underway. University officials are investigating, while student leaders and the Black Student Union condemned the incident.

An Enron email chain forwards a class action complaint filed in San Diego Superior Court by Pamela R. Gordon against Reliant, Southern, NRG, Dynegy, AES, Williams, Duke Energy, and others. The complaint alleges that, beginning around May 22, 2000, defendants manipulated California wholesale electricity markets by using confidential real-time data, withholding capacity, exporting or parking power, coordinating outages, and exploiting market rules, causing artificially inflated prices. It cites FERC, CPUC, CAISO, media reports, and market analyses stating that summer 2000 prices were unjust, unreasonable, and linked to market power, with alleged overcharges of about $4 billion. The suit asserts antitrust, unfair business practices, consumer protection, and unconscionability claims, seeking class certification, damages, restitution, disgorgement, injunctive relief, interest, fees, and costs.

Vladimir Putin’s fourth presidential term is expected to further consolidate his power, sustain an assertive foreign policy and deepen tensions with the West. The passage argues that a key goal is developing a post-Soviet Russian ideology centered on Putin’s leadership, offering a mission statement and alternative to Western liberal democracy amid economic stagnation and weakening promises of prosperity. It says the Kremlin may seek to codify this worldview for domestic legitimacy and global influence. The West, it argues, should challenge the ideology’s claims and maintain a stronger positive vision.

Create Sheffield - Adventures in Cultural Education is a new partnership bringing together education, arts, culture and voluntary organisations to increase arts and cultural opportunities for Sheffield children and young people up to age 25. The partnership aims to improve attainment, employability and access to creative careers, amid concerns that arts subjects are being reduced in schools due to performance pressures. Its proposals include creating a list of cultural experiences, developing learning resources and supporting young makers. It will also help families access the arts and support schools seeking Artsmark accreditation. Membership begins in September, with annual fees from £125 to £5,000 depending on organisation size and turnover.

Oregon has one of the nation’s lowest high school graduation rates, with one in four students not graduating in four years, and also has fewer instructional days than most states. While other states average about 180 instructional days, Oregon averages about 165, based on required instructional hours. State school board member Kim Sordyl and some parents argue the reduced classroom time may contribute to low graduation rates and want lawmakers to add school days. Others, including State Representative Diego Hernandez, say the legislature has not studied a correlation and that issues such as class size, absenteeism, poverty, budget deficits and student supports must also be considered. At Tualatin High School, which has high graduation rates, Principal Darin Barnard emphasizes attendance and says limited instructional time makes every school day important.

Tropical Storm Nate could erode 70 percent of sandy beaches from the Florida Panhandle to southeast Louisiana and destroy about half the protective dunes, according to a USGS study. More than 90 percent of Louisiana beaches may erode, with the Chandeleur Islands especially vulnerable to overwash.

The speaker says Anaheim has not played its successful playoff style against New Jersey, citing poor puck management, neutral-zone turnovers, limited sustained offensive pressure, and few shots or scoring chances. They credit the Devils as a strong defensive team with a great goaltender and effective trap. Returning home to Anaheim may help through crowd energy, line matchups, and last change. The team respects New Jersey, rejects suggestions of arrogance or needing fights, and is focused on executing better, generating chances, capitalizing, limiting New Jersey’s opportunities, and handling the puck more effectively.

NVIDIA’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 31, 2016 reported revenue of $1.43 billion, up from $1.15 billion a year earlier, and net income of $253 million, up from $26 million. Diluted earnings per share were $0.40, compared with $0.05. For the first six months of fiscal 2017, revenue was $2.73 billion and net income was $449 million.

Gross margin for the quarter was 57.9%, compared with 55.0% a year earlier. Operating expenses were $509 million, down from $558 million, reflecting the absence of most prior-year restructuring charges related to the wind-down of Icera operations. Income from operations rose to $317 million from $76 million.

GPU segment revenue was $1.20 billion for the quarter, up 25% year over year, driven by gaming, datacenter, and professional visualization products. Tegra Processor revenue was $166 million, up 30%, driven by automotive systems. Revenue by market included $781 million from Gaming, $214 million from Professional Visualization, $151 million from Datacenter, $119 million from Automotive, and $163 million from OEM & IP.

As of July 31, 2016, NVIDIA had $4.88 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, compared with $5.04 billion at January 31, 2016. Operating activities provided $493 million in cash during the first six months, while financing activities used $570 million, including $509 million for share repurchases and $124 million for dividends.

The company reported settlement of intellectual property disputes with Samsung and Qualcomm, and resolution of litigation with Advanced Silicon Technologies. NVIDIA also continued construction of a new Santa Clara headquarters under an operating lease financing arrangement.

Copper is often considered a leading indicator for stocks because it is widely used across the economy, and rising or falling demand may reflect economic growth or slowdown. The passage tests this idea with a copper vs. stocks strategy: if copper’s four-week return is positive, buy SPY for the next week; otherwise, hold cash. A backtest since 2000 showed decent performance and smaller drawdowns than buy-and-hold, but the strategy had a long weak period from 2008 to 2016. Copper and SPY four-week returns were not strongly correlated, especially from 2011 to 2016. The passage concludes there is no concrete evidence that copper is a reliable leading indicator for stocks, and the strategy’s performance may be due to luck, though copper may help indicate business cycles.

EON Resources held a special conference call to discuss $45.5 million in funding and a related Farmout Agreement. Participants included CEO Dante Caravaggio, CFO Mitchell Trotter, VP of Operations Jesse Allen, and General Counsel David Smith. The call began with a standard forward-looking statements disclaimer before Caravaggio started the company overview.

The passage reports serious medical problems after BNT162b2, BNT162b2SA, or placebo in Phase 1, Phase 2/3, and Phase 3. Serious problems were generally few, with no single serious medical problem occurring in at least 1% of participants in described groups. In Phase 1, 2 participants had serious medical problems, not believed related to vaccination. In Phase 2/3 and Phase 3 booster analyses, few participants had serious medical problems; most were not considered related, though some in participants aged 16 years and older were considered possibly related.

Coach Quenneville said the team had a strong start but lost pace and momentum, stopped doing what made it successful, and played too much in front of the opponent instead of getting the puck behind them. He praised the goalie for keeping the team in the game and said some lines generated threats but were limited in overtime. He said Johnny had a strong year offensively and defensively, with elite conditioning and awareness. Quenneville emphasized playoff toughness, momentum, home ice, and the need to improve each game. He noted Boston’s effectiveness, expected a low-scoring series, and said line rotations and ice time would depend on each game.

Since 1950, the S&P 500 has reached 1,526 all-time highs, averaging nearly 21 per year, or 8.3% of trading days, while trading below all-time highs 91.7% of the time. Over that period, it compounded at 7.67% annually excluding dividends. All-time highs are associated with strong business activity, earnings, momentum, and bullish sentiment, though inflation can distort highs in some markets. A tested strategy buys the S&P 500 when it is within 5% of its all-time high and sells when it falls more than 5% below it. Backtesting showed a 3.20% CAGR, 43.2% market exposure, 7.40% risk-adjusted return, and 33.75% maximum drawdown. The passage emphasizes that profitability depends on how cash is used when the index is not near its all-time high.

The President submits documents to Congress concerning armed tensions in the disputed Aroostook territory claimed by Maine and Great Britain. He reports that unauthorized trespassers, mainly from British provinces, cut large quantities of timber, prompting Maine to send its land agent and an armed posse to stop the depredations. The land agent and others were seized and taken to New Brunswick.

British officials demanded Maine withdraw its force, asserting an agreement gave Great Britain exclusive jurisdiction pending boundary settlement. The President rejects that claim, stating prior correspondence shows no such agreement and that both sides have instead sought to avoid conflict while negotiations continue. He says Maine had the right to protect disputed property from trespassers, but distinguishes this from military occupation to enforce its boundary claim.

The President favors continued amicable settlement through negotiation, arbitration, or commission, and will not support force by Maine to settle the boundary. However, if New Brunswick militarily occupies the disputed territory, he would treat it as a constitutional case for federal aid to repel invasion. He expects detained agents on both sides to be released, recommends Maine disband any militia, warns that armed conflict would endanger peace, and asks Congress to consider measures needed before adjournment.

The Federal Government plans to release N750 billion this week to MDAs for 2017 capital projects, bringing total capital releases this year to N1.2 trillion. Finance Minister Kemi Adeosun announced this while receiving 30 French firms interested in investing in Nigeria’s banking, infrastructure, renewable energy, agriculture, services and youth empowerment sectors.

The passage describes respiratory mask systems for delivering therapies such as CPAP and NIV. The systems include a mask interface with a seal, frame, gas inlet, outlet vent, diffuser, and headgear assembly. The frame may have an angled, substantially elliptical gas inlet, a vent positioned near the inlet, and seal flanges or clip assemblies for attaching a seal. Some configurations include a recessed yoke channel across the frame with attachment features such as apertures, magnets, tabs, latches, bumps, grooves, recesses, or snap-fit structures.

The headgear may include a yoke configured to attach to the frame and to headgear straps. The yoke can have a narrowed middle portion, wider side portions, locating members, textile covering, magnets, hooks, tabs, or stretchable regions. In self-adjusting headgear embodiments, the yoke may serve as a collector for filaments and include washer housings, end caps with filament entry holes, and internal upper and lower line tracks divided by a line track divider.

The passage also describes nasal seal configurations with nasal prongs, a bridge portion, specified dimensional limits, wall thicknesses, sealing areas, a generally D-shaped inlet, and optional clip assemblies with vents and diffusers. Numerous figures are listed showing mask assemblies, frames, seals, yokes, headgear, attachment systems, diffuser arrangements, and seal comparisons.

Witting said Finland’s failed 1940 effort to form a common defense agreement with Sweden, Soviet objections, and Soviet military buildup contributed to Finland accepting the September 1940 German transit agreement. He said German awareness of Soviet preparations confirmed Finnish fears of renewed Soviet attack. Asked whether Finland had achieved its strategic aims, Witting said military aims could not be precisely defined in a democracy, but Finnish front activity had long been driven by Soviet offensives. He argued Finland could not control German actions affecting Allied supplies to Russia because Finland depended on German goodwill for essential imports. Schoenfeld concluded Finland would not voluntarily worsen relations with anti-Axis powers but expected military necessity or events beyond its control to prevent peace with the USSR. A Swedish colleague also said Finnish peace moves were unlikely, that pro-peace opinion lacked leadership, and that Sweden could not influence Finland without risking German displeasure.

The passage describes systems for optically switchable windows, including electrochromic windows, integrated with high-speed building communication networks. The disclosed networks may use serially coupled trunk line segments, coaxial cables, twisted pairs, passive circuits such as bias T circuits or directional couplers, and daisy chain topologies to transmit data, power, TCP/IP, wireless, 5G, or other signals at rates above 1 Gbps. These networks may connect windows, controllers, IoT devices, sensors, antennas, repeaters, microphones, speakers, microprocessors, and other building devices, and may be installed during building construction.

The disclosure also describes high-bandwidth control panels, network backbones, enhanced window controllers, digital architectural elements, and digital wall interfaces. Digital architectural elements may be installed on structural building components such as mullions, walls, doors, beams, or façades and may include sensors, processors, network interfaces, cameras, microphones, speakers, antennas, displays, Wi-Fi access points, air quality sensors, occupancy sensors, and power storage or harvesting components.

The systems may support window control and non-window functions, including internet connectivity, occupant communication, environmental sensing, security, HVAC and lighting control, media delivery, collaboration, acoustic control, personalization, and biometric recognition. Sensor data from distributed digital elements may be analyzed, including through machine learning, to adjust building operation parameters such as window tint, airflow, lighting, temperature, security alarms, door or window locks, and maintenance notifications. The passage also describes use cases involving air quality monitoring, occupancy-based HVAC changes, glare and tint control, sound detection, emergency response, and distinctive window tinting to identify security-related locations.

Patanjali’s “Kimbho” messaging app, launched by Ramdev as a challenge to WhatsApp, became unavailable on Google Play Store a day after launch, though it remained on the iOS App Store and accessible to existing users. Users reported its absence online. Analyst Faisal Kawoosa said it would be difficult for Kimbho to compete with WhatsApp solely on being “swadeshi,” noting about 5,000 installations and reviews citing issues. The app was described as offering messaging, groups, broadcast lists, celebrity following, doodles, calls, media sharing, stickers, location, GIFs and more. Its launch followed Patanjali’s Swadeshi Samriddhi SIM cards with BSNL.

A Nature Astronomy study found strong evidence of hydrogen sulfide in Uranus’s cloud tops, using light captured by the Gemini North telescope. Scientists said the gas, associated with rotten eggs, sewage, and flatulence, would create foul conditions, though Uranus’s extreme cold and atmosphere would be deadlier. The discovery may help explain Uranus’s formation.

The speaker said the team was excited for Manny’s return and contributions, emphasized staying focused after a playoff win before going to Boston, noted personal success against the Bruins, and described being prepared for a practice-like scoring attempt involving Hank.

The passage presents three free mean reversion trading strategies involving XLP, FXI, and the S&P 500, with references to historical backtesting and equity curves. It defines mean reversion as prices moving above and below an average, with abnormal rises tending to fall back and abnormal declines tending to reverse. The passage contrasts mean reversion with trend following, stating that mean reversion typically has a high win rate with many small winners and occasional large losers, while trend following relies more on rare large winners.

The passage argues that mean reversion works best in stocks, less so in markets such as commodities, and has become more effective since the 1990s. It attributes this to futures trading, arbitrage, volatility, and the interaction between buyers, sellers, and short sellers. It also states that mean reversion strategies often perform best in bear markets because higher volatility and sharp rallies create short-term trading opportunities. Data from 2008–2009 is cited to show large daily moves during the market decline. The article concludes that simple mean reversion strategies can produce useful trading results.

The study examined associations between unintended pregnancy and children’s psychosocial problems up to adolescence, including possible indirect effects through maternal mental health and bonding. It used data from 7,784 participants in the Amsterdam Born Children and their Development cohort, with measurements during pregnancy, preschool age, early adolescence, and middle adolescence.

Unintended pregnancy was measured through mistiming, unwantedness, and unhappiness. Children’s psychosocial problems were assessed using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire. Analyses controlled for maternal age, education, antepartum mental health, substance use, child sex, living situation, and adverse childhood experiences.

Pregnancy mistiming and unwantedness were associated with small increases in maternal-reported internalizing problems at preschool age, and mistiming was also associated with externalizing problems. No dimensions of unintended pregnancy were significantly associated with internalizing or externalizing problems in early or middle adolescence after controlling for co-occurring risks. Child-reported adolescent outcomes showed the same absence of associations.

Maternal bonding problems mediated associations between unintended pregnancy dimensions and preschool children’s internalizing and externalizing problems. Maternal psychosocial distress mediated the association between pregnancy mistiming and preschool children’s problems. The authors conclude that maternal mental health and bonding are more relevant targets for reducing young children’s psychosocial problems than unintended pregnancy itself.

The passage describes patent embodiments for a display device with a through hole in a substrate, surrounded by pixels in a display area. Scan lines and data lines provide signals to pixels; data lines adjacent to the through hole may curve along its perimeter and be arranged in different layers without overlapping to reduce the surrounding non-display area. The device may include thin film encapsulation with inorganic and organic layers, a dam near the through hole, and contact portions between inorganic layers to improve moisture sealing. Various embodiments modify the data line layers, passivation structures, and overlap arrangements. The display device may be used in mobile phones, smart watches, or vehicle dashboards.

The Bengals acquired quarterback Joe Flacco and a sixth-round pick from the Browns for a fifth-round pick amid struggles at quarterback after Joe Burrow’s toe surgery. Jake Browning has thrown eight interceptions over parts of four games, and Cincinnati has lost three straight while being outscored 113-37. Coach Zac Taylor praised Flacco’s experience and fit. Flacco, 40, had 815 yards, two touchdowns and six interceptions in four games with Cleveland this season. His departure could move Shedeur Sanders to the Browns’ No. 2 quarterback role behind Dillon Gabriel.

The speaker addresses the University of Michigan graduating class about building the “Great Society,” defined as a society of abundance, liberty, an end to poverty and racial injustice, enriched education, meaningful leisure, strong communities, natural beauty, and goals beyond material wealth. He identifies three key areas for action: cities, where rapid urban growth requires rebuilding and renewed community; the countryside, where pollution and loss of natural beauty threaten America; and classrooms, where millions lack adequate education and schools need more access, better teachers, and improved methods. He proposes White House conferences and cooperative federalism to develop solutions. He calls on the graduates to help advance equality, reduce poverty, promote peace, and use national progress to enrich the life of the mind and spirit.
