The “Box and One” is a combination defense with four players in a box zone and one chaser denying a targeted opponent the ball and rebounds. Baseline defenders shift like a 1-2-2 zone, while outside defenders shift like a 2-3 zone. Against even or odd fronts, defenders push the ball away from the chaser’s side, rotate to cover corners, wings, elbows, blocks, and low post areas, and return to starting positions on skip passes. The chaser’s denial aims to keep the opponent’s star scorer from receiving the ball and disrupt offensive plays.

The speaker said his team played well for two periods and early in the third but became conservative while protecting the lead, allowing Buffalo to gain momentum. He credited Buffalo for staying competitive, winning key puck battles late, and using skill throughout its lineup, while noting Hasek kept them in the game. He said his team needs more second and third scoring chances, better control of critical areas for the full game, and continued power-play puck movement. He described the series as close and competitive, said lineup changes may be considered, and emphasized the team’s unity, resilience, and need to improve.

The passage explains how to backtest a simple trading strategy in Python using pandas, yfinance, and matplotlib. It describes downloading SPY historical data from Yahoo Finance, calculating simple and exponential moving averages, generating trading signals when the close is above both averages, and calculating returns only when the strategy is invested. The strategy’s accumulated return is 804.82%, compared with 1505.31% for buy and hold, so it underperforms.

The passage describes AMD Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) requirements and processes. Customers provide an RSA public key for SFS package verification during early boot and cannot update it after that stage. Customers may co-sign AMD update packages using 2048-bit or 4096-bit RSA-PSS signatures. SFS packages can patch registers or values, replace firmware images, or update firmware components, and each package must validate applicable firmware and patch levels before applying updates.

SFS updates are non-persistent across reboots, so customers must apply patches during OS boot, after boot, or during operation. Commands require specific memory alignment, including a 2MB-aligned TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER, and update packages are sent through the ASP TEE mailbox interface. The ASP protects the memory region, verifies customer and AMD signatures, runs the executable patch, updates patch level information, and returns status.

GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO reports firmware and patch level information. UPDATE_FW loads, verifies, and executes an SFS package only after validation succeeds. Package names follow the format `fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg`. Updates must match the system’s firmware and patch levels. Most updates are intended to have minimal performance impact, though SEV firmware updates may require SEV or SEV/ES virtual machines to stop and restart.

Dane Gudauskas described paddling into a huge left during an XXL Cloudbreak swell in Fiji, calling it the most intense surf experience he has had. Conditions were stormy, windy, dark and difficult, with many surfers waiting on boats and some towing. He said the ocean had more energy than during his 2016 Cloudbreak wave, and he wiped out, broke his 8’6” board, and later felt sore from the adrenaline-filled experience. He credited water safety crews from Tavarua, Namotu and the mainland, and said he planned to unwind by enjoying simpler surfing.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2022. As of October 19, 2022, it had 10,201,654,176 common shares outstanding. In Q3 2022, net sales were $127.1 billion, up from $110.8 billion in Q3 2021. Net income was $2.9 billion, compared with $3.2 billion a year earlier, and diluted earnings per share were $0.28 versus $0.31.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2022, net sales were $364.8 billion, compared with $332.4 billion in 2021. The company reported a net loss of $3.0 billion, compared with net income of $19.0 billion in 2021, largely reflecting $13.4 billion in other expense. Operating income declined to $9.5 billion from $21.4 billion.

By segment for Q3 2022, North America sales were $78.8 billion with an operating loss of $412 million; International sales were $27.7 billion with an operating loss of $2.5 billion; and AWS sales were $20.5 billion with operating income of $5.4 billion. AWS sales rose 27% year over year.

Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash totaled $35.2 billion at September 30, 2022. Total assets were $428.4 billion, total liabilities were $290.9 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $137.5 billion. Amazon completed a 20-for-1 stock split on May 27, 2022, repurchased $6.0 billion of common stock during the first nine months of 2022, and acquired MGM for approximately $6.1 billion net of cash acquired.

Mr. Heard reported that Seoul remained quiet after April 20 and that investigations in the southern provinces found no evidence of significant Tong Hâk activity, though public discontent over official exactions could cause further rumors. Later, reports said many Tong Hâk had gathered at Po-eun, were increasing in number, drilling, and displaying anti-Japanese and anti-foreign banners. Korean alarm grew, some families left Seoul, and the Government sent troops with Gatling guns to block the route. The Crude Oil Friday seasonality strategy is based on the tendency for oil prices to rise on Fridays, with trades entered at Thursday’s close. Historical data from April 2006 to the present showed a 56.96% profit/loss, 98 trades, 60 winners, and an average profit of 0.58% per trade. The strategy performs better when Thursday is a down day, especially when USO falls at least 0.75 times the 25-day average high-low range. Buying on any Thursday’s close is not recommended; market conditions affect effectiveness.
Virtual machines use a shared #HV doorbell page aligned with APIC behavior, defining PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. The backing page must be host-owned, and guest accesses require C=0.

Biocon India Group, founded in 1978 by Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw in Bangalore, grew from enzyme manufacturing into generic pharmaceuticals and contract research through an “earn as you learn” approach. By early 2003 it had 800 employees and annual revenues of US$75 million. Its capabilities in fermentation led to generic statins, while its subsidiary Syngene, founded in 1994, became an Indian contract research organization serving mainly international pharmaceutical and biotech firms.

India’s pharmaceutical industry expanded rapidly after independence, shaped by policies including the 1970 India Patent Act and Drug Price Control Order. By 2001 the industry had strong domestic and export growth and more than 20,000 companies. Global pharmaceutical firms increasingly outsourced R&D, clinical trials, and manufacturing to reduce costs and speed development. India offered English-speaking scientific talent, low labor costs, genetic diversity, and government support for biotechnology, making clinical research an attractive growth area.

Biocon’s culture emphasized openness, trust, collaboration, limited hierarchy, meritocracy, and scientific talent with business orientation. These values supported its growth and were seen as central to its success.

In 2000 Biocon launched Clinigene to fill a missing capability in clinical trials and move toward becoming a fully integrated drug discovery and development company. Clinigene initially focused on clinical lab services, bio-equivalence and bio-availability studies, and hospital partnerships. It offered growth potential in India’s expanding CRO market, but also raised concerns. Biocon had limited direct experience in clinical trials, and Clinigene’s success could divert resources, grow larger than the parent company, strain Biocon’s collaborative culture, and require new structures. Clinical trials also carried financial, ethical, reputational, and political risks, especially because they involved human subjects in India.

Mazumdar-Shaw faced a strategic choice: aggressively grow Clinigene, limit it to safer lower-value services until Biocon’s own molecules needed testing, or acquire a clinical services CRO while preserving Biocon’s culture. The case centers on whether Clinigene would be a springboard, pitfall, or detour for Biocon’s future expansion.

Redding police reported several incidents: Dylan Kennedy, 19, was ticketed for speeding and possession of less than half an ounce of marijuana and charged with drug paraphernalia possession. Caton Preston, 18, was charged with minor alcohol possession and third-degree forgery after allegedly producing a fake driver’s license. Police collected 75 pounds of unused prescription drugs for destruction. Three children received trespassing warrants at Falls Hole restaurant. A Topstone Road resident reported a smashed mailbox. Police logged 204 total calls, including animal control, EMS assists, alarms, accidents, and suspicious person or vehicle reports.

The ADS868xW family comprises single-channel, 16-bit SAR ADC data acquisition devices with integrated analog front-end circuitry, supporting true bipolar differential and single-ended input swings up to ±12.288V from a single 5V analog supply. The devices include high input impedance, a programmable gain amplifier with nine input ranges, a second-order antialiasing low-pass filter, an ADC driver, ±20V powered input overvoltage protection, an internal 4.096V reference with buffer, and a multiSPI interface with daisy-chain and alarm features.

The devices support internal or external 4.096V references, straight-binary output, programmable input ranges, and active-high alarm functions for analog input thresholds and AVDD limits. The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI, dual-SDO, source-synchronous modes, daisy-chain operation, and 32-bit data frames for register read/write and conversion data output. Functional states include RESET, ACQ, and CONV, with NAP and power-down modes for reduced power consumption.

Configuration is handled through nine registers controlling device ID, reset and power, SDI/SDO protocols, output data formatting, input range and reference selection, and alarm thresholds/status. Application guidance covers industrial analog input modules, input alarm hysteresis, power-supply decoupling, low-power operation, and PCB layout practices. The document also includes support resources, revision history, packaging information, and TI disclaimers.

Mali’s gold exports and production are under pressure as legacy mines decline or close. The Sadiola mine, a joint venture between IAMGOLD, AngloGold Ashanti and Mali’s government, needs a $380 million investment to process hard-rock reserves and extend operations by 10 years, but negotiations appear stalled. Sadiola has 3.4 million ounces of proven and probable reserves and has been central to Mali’s rise as a major African gold producer. With Morila winding down and Yatela closed, failure to expand Sadiola could hurt state revenues, employment and investor confidence ahead of Mali’s 2018 elections. The expansion would use existing infrastructure, add new facilities, connect the mine to the power grid and potentially support local villages.

RTX IO improves game loading, frame rates, streaming, and storage efficiency by using Microsoft DirectStorage and GPU-based lossless decompression to move compressed data from SSDs to RTX GPUs, reducing CPU load and improving I/O performance. It also benefits professional workloads involving large datasets, rendering, CAD, visualization, and VR.

NVIDIA GA10x Ampere GPUs deliver up to 2x improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI, with second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, GDDR6X support, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4a, AV1 hardware decode, fifth-generation NVDEC, and seventh-generation NVENC. These features support high-resolution gaming, video decoding and encoding, ray tracing, DLSS, and 8K workflows.

The NVIDIA A40 is a GA10x-based data center GPU for visual computing, AI, data science, virtualization, and rendering, offering up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 5x AI/data science throughput compared with Quadro RTX 6000, plus 48GB memory scalable to 96GB via NVLink. The RTX A6000 is a professional workstation GPU with 48GB GDDR6, NVLink support, ray tracing, AI denoising, and large-scene rendering capabilities.

Appendices describe GeForce RTX 3090 and RTX 3070 specifications, GDDR6X Error Detection and Replay for memory overclocking, RTX A6000 performance comparisons, and NVIDIA’s legal and warranty disclaimers.

The address reports that the United States is experiencing rapid growth, prosperity, expanding population, flourishing agriculture, commerce, manufactures, navigation, adequate revenue, advancing fortifications, and naval growth. Foreign relations are generally friendly, though some disputes remain unresolved. Commercial reciprocity is emphasized, with agreements or arrangements involving France, Britain, Sweden, Russia, the Netherlands, Prussia, Hanseatic cities, Oldenburg, Sardinia, Colombia, and others. Outstanding issues include French indemnity claims, British colonial trade, some boundaries with Britain, suppression of the slave trade, and neutral rights in maritime war.

The Treasury is described as strong, with receipts exceeding expenditures, debt reduction continuing, and hopes that the public debt may be discharged within ten years if no unexpected events occur. The Army, Military Academy, fortifications, and engineering works are reported as effective, with recommendations to strengthen engineering corps for roads, canals, and surveys. Relations with most Indian tribes are friendly, though some tribes along the Missouri, Upper Mississippi, and Upper Lakes remain hostile; schools and civilization efforts are described, and a plan is proposed for voluntary relocation westward with civil governments and education.

The Navy is protecting commerce in the Mediterranean, Gulf of Mexico, African coast, and Pacific, though piracy near Cuba remains a serious problem requiring further consideration. The Post Office revenue has increased. Lafayette’s visit is described as receiving widespread gratitude, and Congress is asked to consider provision for his services and sacrifices.

The address discusses Greece, Spain, and the new South American states, affirming U.S. support for independence and noninterference while opposing European interference in neighboring states. It recommends judicial reorganization due to national expansion, consideration of a military post near the Columbia River, improvements in Washington, continued coastal defense, naval protection, internal improvements, adherence to constitutional limits, harmony between state and national governments, and vigilance against foreign and domestic dangers. The address closes with gratitude for public confidence and prayers for the preservation of national blessings.

The passage describes systems and methods for supporting vertical takeoff aerial vehicles using portable ground stations. Each ground station may include a protective casing, an extendable landing pad, a charging mechanism, and optionally a base platform with an elevator mechanism. The landing pad can transition between a closed configuration contained within the casing and an open configuration large enough for landing. A landed aerial vehicle may be retracted into the casing and charged.

The ground station may include centering mechanisms, homing aids, windbreakers, locking mechanisms, and communication units. Charging may use conducting terminals embedded in the base platform, flaps, casing, or top closing, with power supplied by batteries, fuel cells, photovoltaic panels, wind turbines, or other sources. The casing may be transparent to satellite navigation signals.

Examples include rectangular landing pads with folding side flaps and bridging lobes, telescoping extensions, sliding top doors, and triangular configurations. Homing aids may include visual patterns, beacons, or contrasting physical properties to guide aerial vehicles from high or low altitude. Multiple ground stations may be deployed to extend aerial vehicle range and support one or more vehicles, coordinated by a control server. Additional modules may provide weather sensing, transport, mounting, suspension, communication, radar, night vision, battery capacity, or carrying functions.

The Sri Lankan rupee fell for a third straight session, ending at 158.60/75 per dollar as importer dollar demand exceeded remittance inflows. Dealers cited pressure from Fed rate hikes, U.S.-China trade tensions and higher oil prices. Moody’s warned a stronger dollar raises credit risks and may reduce reserves. Sri Lanka also saw foreign outflows from government securities.

An Uzbek court convicted Uzbek-born U.S. citizen Zokir Aliyev of links to militant Islam, publicly calling for the government’s overthrow and participating in an extremist group, but fined him only $67 for alleged offenses from 1999. Aliyev, detained June 16 and freed after six days, denied involvement with the Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, saying he attended opposition meetings in Turkey. The U.S. embassy declined comment, citing privacy concerns.

This study investigates near-infrared spectra of cryogenic particulate mixtures relevant to Europa’s surface, focusing on water ice, epsomite, and halite. The work supports future interpretation of data from Europa Clipper and JUICE by providing laboratory spectra and assessing spectral mixture models.

The authors developed the CRONOS facility, a nitrogen-purged cryogenic glove-box setup, to prepare and measure samples while minimizing frost contamination. Water ice, epsomite, and halite were ground, wet-sieved with liquid nitrogen, and separated into four grain-size bins: fine, small, medium, and large. Samples included pure materials and 50%/50% volume mixtures of different grain sizes or materials, measured mostly near 100–120 K.

Laboratory spectra showed characteristic water ice absorption features at 1.25, 1.5, 1.65, and 2.0 µm, with reflectance decreasing and absorption features saturating as grain size increased. Cryogenic epsomite displayed many absorption features absent in ambient spectra, while halite showed a feature near 1.95 µm attributed to adsorbed water. In mixtures, water ice strongly dominated spectra; halite-water mixtures were nearly indistinguishable from pure water ice, and epsomite-water mixtures were difficult to distinguish for some grain sizes.

The study compared laboratory spectra with Hapke-based linear and intimate mixture models using optical constants for crystalline water ice and epsomite. Water ice models generally matched laboratory spectra within about 5–10% at many wavelengths, though discrepancies remained in continua and absorption bands. Linear and intimate models performed similarly for water ice. Epsomite modeling was less successful, likely due to issues with published cryogenic epsomite optical constants, which may resemble ambient-condition data.

The authors conclude that quantitative spectral mixture analysis is needed to determine material abundances and grain sizes on Europa, since mixed spectra do not simply fall midway between pure component spectra. Smaller grains can disproportionately affect spectral features, potentially creating observational bias. The study presents the first near-infrared spectra of cryogenic particulate mixtures of water ice, epsomite, and halite, and recommends caution when using existing epsomite optical constants until corrected data are available.

The President responds to a Senate request about alleged forcible resistance to U.S. law in Boston, citing a deputy marshal’s affidavit and noting that official information remains incomplete. He condemns the incident, argues it does not reflect Boston or Massachusetts generally, and reviews federal and Massachusetts laws affecting detention of federal prisoners and fugitive slaves. He states that Massachusetts law withdrew state assistance and jail use, but federal marshals remain required to secure detention facilities. He transmits related proclamations, instructions, and dispatches, and suggests Congress clarify the President’s authority to use militia, the Army, and Navy to execute laws without requiring prior proclamation in some cases.

He reaffirms his duty to enforce the laws and suppress opposition. In a separate proclamation, he warns against a planned U.S.-based military expedition to invade Cuba, a Spanish colony at peace with the United States, declares such actions illegal, and orders officials to arrest and prosecute offenders.

The passage explains that NVDA options trading may offer leveraged profit opportunities with losses for long options limited to the premium paid, but it involves significant complexity and risks. Common strategies include calls, puts, covered calls, spreads, straddles, strangles, collars, protective puts, stop-loss orders, hedging, diversification, and position sizing. Option prices are affected by the underlying stock price, time to expiration, implied volatility, market sentiment, dividends, liquidity, and market conditions. Implied volatility and pricing models such as Black-Scholes are emphasized as important tools. The passage also notes risks including adverse stock movement, time decay, volatility, liquidity, margin requirements, costs, and tax implications, and advises investors to understand option pricing and gain practical experience before trading.

The speaker says being in Quebec feels like home and is glad family can attend the game. They credit success to hard work, preparation, toughness, and creating luck through effort. They expect a tough road challenge, emphasizing intensity, energy, sticking to the game plan, and quieting the crowd early.

The passage examines the 2018-19 Union Budget’s implications for women, noting the absence of a separate women-focused allocation unlike previous years. Economists quoted argue that the Budget largely views women within existing social roles rather than addressing structural barriers to work or changing development patterns.

Some experts see positives, especially the National Health Protection Scheme, which proposes Rs 5 lakh annual insurance coverage per vulnerable family for about 50 crore beneficiaries. Supporters say it could improve women’s access to healthcare, while critics question its effectiveness, lack of clear funding, and limited rise in overall health allocations. The passage notes health spending rose only 2.7 percent, while the health ministry’s share of the total Budget fell, and National Health Mission allocation declined.

The Budget’s MSME support and reduced corporate tax for smaller firms are seen as potentially beneficial for women employed in small industries and self-help groups. Sanitation investments are also described as important for women’s health. However, maternity entitlement funding is criticized as inadequate, and the expansion of the Ujjwala LPG scheme is questioned because many women cannot afford refills.

Overall, the passage presents mixed views: some provisions may benefit women, but critics argue the Budget continues existing schemes and assumptions without significantly rethinking women’s economic or social roles.

USB-C and USB-A describe connector shapes, not speed or features. USB-C is smaller, reversible, more capable, and increasingly replacing USB-A, while older types like USB-B and Micro-USB still appear on some accessories. USB performance depends on the USB specification and the slowest device, port, or cable in the chain.

USB4 uses USB-C exclusively, originally supporting 20 to 40 Gbps, while USB4 Version 2 can reach up to 120 Gbps but is not widely adopted. USB 3.x naming is confusing, so speed ratings are more useful: USB-A tops out at 20 Gbps, while 10 Gbps and 5 Gbps ports may appear under several labels. USB 2.0 supports up to 480 Mbps.

USB Power Delivery allows USB-C ports to charge devices, with USB-PD 3.1 supporting up to 240 watts. Users should check whether chargers, hubs, and cables provide enough wattage for their devices. USB-C also supports DisplayPort Alternate Mode, which can carry audio and video to monitors over one cable. USB4 requires DP Alt Mode and uses DisplayPort 2.0 for higher display capabilities.

Thunderbolt uses USB-C but has stricter certification requirements. Thunderbolt 4, built on USB4, supports up to 40 Gbps, up to 100 watts, DisplayPort 2.0 Alt Mode, and more consistent display and cable-length capabilities than USB4, though implementations can vary. Thunderbolt remains compatible with USB-C devices but defaults to the slowest link.

Thunderbolt 5 is beginning to appear in high-end laptops and accessories. It supports up to 80 Gbps bidirectional bandwidth, up to 120 Gbps unidirectional bandwidth, expanded display support, and up to 240 watts of power delivery. To achieve rated speeds and power, cables must also support the required specifications; using included cables or checking listed speeds and wattage is recommended.

The Tenth Circuit affirmed Henry J. Adams III’s 140-month sentence for armed bank robbery. Adams pleaded guilty after serving as lookout, recruiting a driver, helping with transportation, and expecting a share of the proceeds. He argued that he should have received a two-level reduction as a minor participant and that the district court abused its discretion by imposing an above-guidelines sentence.

The court held that Adams was not entitled to a minor-participant reduction because he knowingly joined the robbery plan, acted as lookout, helped facilitate escape, and expected compensation. His role was not substantially less culpable than the other participants.

The court also upheld the above-guidelines sentence as an upward variance, not a departure. The district court relied on 18 U.S.C. § 3553(a) factors, especially Adams’s extensive criminal history, repeated reoffending, seriousness of the offense, need for deterrence, protection of the public, and rehabilitation. The appellate court found the sentence substantively reasonable and rejected Adams’s comparison to a codefendant’s sentence.

Lincoln argues that efforts begun five years earlier to end slavery agitation have instead intensified it, and that the United States cannot permanently remain half slave and half free. He says the Nebraska doctrine and Dred Scott decision form a legal “machinery” advancing slavery: repealing congressional prohibition in the territories, securing political endorsement through Buchanan’s election, and establishing that Black people cannot be citizens, Congress and territorial legislatures cannot exclude slavery from territories, and questions about slavery in free states remain unresolved. He warns that another Supreme Court decision could make it unconstitutional for states to exclude slavery, making slavery lawful everywhere.

Lincoln contends that Senator Douglas’s “care not” policy on whether slavery is voted up or down helps shape public opinion to tolerate slavery’s expansion. He rejects relying on Douglas to oppose slavery’s advance, saying Douglas is not with Republicans and has not promised to join them. Lincoln concludes that the cause must be carried by those who genuinely oppose slavery’s spread, urging Republicans to stand firm and predicting eventual victory.

Chelsea and Real Madrid are reportedly trying to rival Tottenham for Ajax defender Davinson Sanchez, valued at £40m. Tottenham are expected to offer £28m, while Ajax want to keep him. Sanchez reportedly wants to leave for Premier League and Champions League football.

Shares of Walgreens, CVS Health and Rite Aid fell after reports that Amazon may enter online prescription drug sales. Leerink said Amazon is assessing the market, while CNBC reported a decision could come before Thanksgiving.

The stick concept is a quick-game passing concept designed for fast quarterback decisions and short throws, with the stick route often serving as the primary option, especially for tight ends who can adjust to coverage. It works well against man, Cover 3, and Cover 4 by reading flat defenders or using backside options, but is less favorable against Cover 2 because the cornerback can undercut the arrow route, though the sideline “hole shot” may be available.

Routes vary by coverage: against man, the tight end releases vertically then runs away on a speed-out path; against zone, he settles in a void. Arrow routes stretch the flat, the X runs a slant, and the Z runs a go route to pull coverage or attack Cover 2. The quarterback identifies the flat defender pre-snap and reads his post-snap movement to choose between the arrow and stick routes, with backside slant/arrow options available against blitz or favorable matchups.

Variations include a 2x2 condensed version using arrow and stick routes with a running back checkdown, and “Trips Flex Sticko,” a double-move counter where the tight end sells stick before working downfield, supported by a delayed slant and backside sluggo.

The study examines the value loads conveyed by words in 2nd, 3rd, and 4th grade Turkish textbooks used by Turkey’s Ministry of National Education. Prose reading texts were digitized, cleaned, tokenized, and lemmatized, producing a database of 3,637 unique words. Three applied linguistics experts classified words as carrying positive, negative, or neutral value loads.

Overall, 172 words (4.72%) carried positive value transfer, 159 (4.37%) carried negative value transfer, and 3,306 (91.43%) were neutral. By grade level, 2nd grade texts contained 64 positive, 60 negative, and 1,104 neutral words; 3rd grade texts contained 78 positive, 69 negative, and 1,382 neutral words; and 4th grade texts contained 119 positive, 109 negative, and 2,199 neutral words.

The study concludes that there is no observable relationship between grade level and value transfer in the textbooks, and that positive and negative value-transfer words appear at similarly low rates. It suggests classifying textbook words by the values they convey and using corpus-based methods in textbook preparation.

The lecture introduces a course connecting extremal graph theory and additive combinatorics. Zhao explains Schur’s theorem, its infinitary and finitary forms, and how it shows that reducing Fermat’s equation modulo primes cannot prove Fermat’s Last Theorem. He proves Ramsey’s theorem for monochromatic triangles by induction and uses it to prove Schur’s theorem by converting a coloring of integers into an edge-coloring of a complete graph.

The lecture then surveys additive combinatorics, including Van der Waerden’s theorem, the Erdős–Turán conjecture, Roth’s theorem, Szemerédi’s theorem, and later approaches using ergodic theory, higher-order Fourier analysis, hypergraph regularity, and polymath collaborations. Zhao discusses themes such as structure versus randomness, multidimensional and polynomial generalizations of Szemerédi’s theorem, and the Green–Tao theorem on arithmetic progressions in primes.

The lecture closes by returning to Roth’s theorem in finitary form and previewing its graph-theoretic connections, including triangle-free graphs, Mantel’s theorem, and graphs where every edge lies in exactly one triangle. Upcoming lectures will focus on extremal graph theory and forbidden subgraph problems.

The speaker describes the United States as facing significant domestic and international challenges and calls for action with resolve. He cites recent accomplishments including education reform, creation of the Department of Homeland Security, tax relief, and corporate accountability measures.

He proposes accelerating and making permanent income-tax reductions, reducing the marriage penalty, increasing the child tax credit, ending double taxation of dividends, limiting spending growth, and offering younger workers retirement accounts they control. He calls for Medicare reform with prescription drug coverage, $400 billion over ten years for Medicare, and medical liability reform.

He urges passage of an energy plan, Clear Skies legislation, the Healthy Forests Initiative, and $1.2 billion for hydrogen-powered automobile research. He also calls for faith-based and service initiatives, $450 million for mentoring disadvantaged youth and children of prisoners, $600 million for drug treatment, a ban on partial-birth abortion, and a law against human cloning.

Abroad, he discusses continued support for Afghanistan, efforts toward peace between Israel and a democratic Palestine, U.S. food aid, and a proposed $15 billion Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief focused on Africa and the Caribbean.

On terrorism, he says the United States and partners have arrested or dealt with many Al Qaeda leaders, disrupted plots, strengthened homeland security, and will pursue Project BioShield with nearly $6 billion for vaccines and treatments. He announces plans for a Terrorist Threat Integration Center.

He identifies outlaw regimes seeking weapons of mass destruction as the gravest danger, discusses Iran and North Korea, and focuses heavily on Iraq. He says Saddam Hussein has violated disarmament obligations, concealed biological, chemical, and nuclear weapons programs, obstructed inspections, aided terrorists, and abused Iraqis. He states the United States will ask the U.N. Security Council to review evidence and will lead a coalition to disarm Iraq if Saddam Hussein does not fully disarm. He closes by addressing U.S. forces, saying the nation seeks peace but will fight if necessary, and expressing confidence in America’s strength, freedom, and faith.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired after conservatives highlighted alleged past blog posts criticizing President Donald Trump. The Miami Herald reported he is among several federal prosecutors dismissed by Trump’s Justice Department. The DOJ also fired three Southern District of Florida prosecutors who had worked with former special counsel Jack Smith.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed summary judgment for AMCO Insurance Company against George Morello. The court found no genuine issue of material fact that AMCO breached the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing, conducted an unreasonable investigation, or unreasonably withheld benefits. AMCO reasonably relied on expert medical opinions, and Morello’s expert reports were conclusory and rebutted by the record. Because Morello’s related claims for intentional infliction of emotional distress, unfair business practices, and Unruh Act violations were based on the same grounds, summary judgment was also proper on those claims. The court also affirmed denial of Morello’s motion for reconsideration, finding no clear error or intervening change in controlling law.

NVIDIA’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended May 2, 2021 reported revenue of $5.66 billion, up from $3.08 billion a year earlier, and net income of $1.91 billion, up from $917 million. Diluted net income per share was $3.03, compared with $1.47. Gross profit was $3.63 billion, and operating income was $1.96 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $12.67 billion.

Revenue grew in both reportable segments: Graphics revenue was $3.45 billion, and Compute & Networking revenue was $2.21 billion. By market platform, Gaming revenue was $2.76 billion, Data Center was $2.05 billion, Professional Visualization was $372 million, Automotive was $154 million, and OEM and Other was $327 million.

NVIDIA continued pursuing its pending acquisition of Arm Limited, a transaction valued at $40 billion, with expected closing likely in the first quarter of calendar 2022, subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions. The company also reported the completed April 2020 acquisition of Mellanox Technologies.

The company paid $99 million in dividends during the quarter and had authorization to repurchase up to $7.24 billion of common stock through December 2022. On May 21, 2021, NVIDIA’s board declared a four-for-one stock split, subject to stockholder approval to increase authorized common shares from 2 billion to 4 billion.

A weekly trading strategy focuses on weekly price action and can be used for position trading, swing trading, trend following, range trading, or broader market analysis for trades on lower timeframes. Weekly charts are often used to identify long-term trends, range-bound markets, and key support and resistance levels.

Common weekly strategies include range trading on the weekly chart, long-term trend following, and trading weekly highs and lows on lower timeframes such as H4. Range trading is described as common among position traders holding trades for 6–12 months. Weekly highs and lows can act as support and resistance on intraday charts and may be traded using breakout or reversal setups.

Weekly charts are not inherently better than daily charts; suitability depends on trading style and strategy. Position traders may prefer weekly charts, while daily charts may be more useful for other strategies. Backtesting across timeframes is recommended to determine which works best.

Stocks can be traded weekly by day traders or swing traders. Pattern day trading rules may require a $25,000 account if four or more day trades are made within five business days under specified conditions, while swing traders are not affected in the same way.

The passage presents a backtested weekly sector rotation strategy using ETFs. It reports 728 trades, 15.1% annual returns, a 43% maximum drawdown in 2008, and an average gain of 0.4% per trade before slippage and commissions. A monthly version had 166 trades, 12.1% annual returns, and a 21% maximum drawdown.

Under GST, e-way bills are required for transporting consignments worth over Rs 50,000 to curb tax evasion, but the GST Council approved exemptions for 153 items. Exempted items include LPG for households, PDS kerosene, currency, jewellery, postal baggage, used personal effects, animals, fruits, vegetables, milk, cereals, khadi, puja items, hearing aids, condoms and contraceptives. E-way bills are also not needed for non-motorised transport, certain customs movements, or conveyance details for intra-state transport under 10 km. The system will begin after NIC prepares the software, likely by October.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO processes 1–128 migration entries to move one or more pages in SNP-enabled or non-SNP systems. In SNP systems it applies only to Hypervisor-owned pages, with unencrypted or hypervisor-key encrypted memory; SEV systems may target unencrypted or host/hypervisor encrypted memory. It can migrate pages active with DMA by updating IOMMU host PTEs, but CPUs must be prevented from accessing the pages. ATS-related invalidation steps may be required before use. SNP-initialized systems require source and destination pages to be in Hypervisor state, and 2M pages must be split into 4K pages.

Firmware validates addresses, hPTE mappings, page states, page sizes, RMP exclusivity when enforced, performs CPU and IOMMU TLB invalidations and synchronization, marks migration state, flushes DMA, copies data with proper encryption, updates hPTEs, releases RMP access, and clears migration markers.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST processes 1–128 entries to move SNP guest pages and can replace SNP PAGE_MOVE. It requires RMP_ENFORCE, no concurrent DMA, CPU access prevention, valid guest context, matching page sizes, source pages in Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid state, and destination pages in Pre-Migration state. Destination pages inherit the source state, while source pages return to Pre-Migration.

A separate command marks the end of page migration command strings and may interrupt on completion. Errors may occur in command formatting, migration entries, ring buffer management, or hardware operation. Status is reported through command, entry, PM_STATUS, or MCA mechanisms. Hardware errors during a batch may make all pages in that command unrecoverable, though software may attempt to save state before reboot.

School districts are increasingly adding technology to school buses, including GPS tracking, live cameras, navigation tablets, student check-in systems, maintenance monitoring and parent apps. Kansas City Public Schools contracted with Zum for a high-tech fleet, while districts in Arkansas, Oregon and Florida use vendors such as Transportant and Transfinder to improve safety, routing, communication and driver support. Officials say the tools help parents track buses and students, reduce calls to dispatchers, improve efficiency and address driver shortages. Privacy advocates warn that expanded collection of GPS, video and student data creates security risks. Districts and vendors say they use safeguards such as encryption, separate storage, retention policies and routine deletion.

Infiniti’s Q Inspiration concept will influence a new electrified vehicle platform with up to five models planned over five years. The vehicles will be built in China, likely for global markets, and feature design elements from the four-door coupe concept.

Fiat Chrysler reportedly rejected a merger offer from an unidentified Chinese automaker because it considered the financial terms insufficient. FCA had previously sought mergers with companies such as General Motors and Volkswagen, but CEO Sergio Marchionne later said he was focusing on improving the company’s finances and was reluctant to sell. Several Chinese automakers, including joint venture partner Guangzhou, have reportedly shown interest, with meetings involving FCA executives in China and Chinese automakers visiting FCA’s Michigan headquarters. Automotive News said Chinese interest may be driven by government pressure to expand abroad, FCA’s distribution network, product line, history, debt-reduction plans, and Chinese automakers’ desire to enter the U.S. market through an established company.

The passage explains SOS pressure defense, emphasizing that effective man-to-man defense requires repeated drills, commitment, enthusiasm, and positive coaching feedback. SOS on-ball pressure consists of Set, On, and Smother actions. Set positions the defender to force the ballhandler to dribble rather than pass or shoot. On guides the dribbler toward sideline or baseline checkpoints while maintaining defensive position, including sprint-and-recover if beaten. Smother applies maximum pressure once the dribble stops to disrupt shots or passes.

SOS off-ball pressure uses Snuggle, Off, and Strike actions. Snuggle denies passes to an opponent one pass away through close positioning, active hands, and shadowing movement, including post-front technique in the low post. Off denies give-and-go cuts by jumping toward the ball and maintaining pass denial. Strike is a weakside help position used to impede cuts into the lane, cover lob passes, help beaten teammates, block layups, box out, rebound, and close out on crosscourt passes by transitioning into Set position.

Xiaomi is preparing for a major 2018 launch event, but a Digit report says the Xiaomi Mi A2 will not launch in India. A spokesperson said no phone exists by that name, while confirming more Android One phones are planned. The Xiaomi Mi 6X may still launch in India under a different name. Xiaomi is also preparing the Redmi S2/Y2 launch as an affordable dual-camera phone.

North American markets ended a volatile week with sharp losses. The Dow fell 666 points, or 2.5%, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq also posted their worst weekly losses since early 2016. Strong U.S. jobs and wage growth raised concerns about inflation and interest rate hikes, while rising bond yields and weak earnings from major companies, including Exxon Mobil, Chevron, Alphabet and Apple, weighed on markets. The Canadian dollar fell to 80.78 US cents. In Canada, the S&P/TSX Composite dropped 255 points, or 1.6%, for its worst decline in nearly five months, hurt by falling oil and gold prices and continued weakness in marijuana stocks. Canopy Growth fell 12.5%.

A railroad brakeman sued the Missouri-Kansas-Texas Railroad Company of Texas under the Federal Boiler Inspection Act and the Federal Employers’ Liability Act after suffering frostbite while flagging behind a disabled passenger train in zero weather. The train’s locomotive broke down when driving wheel tires slipped or came off, leaving it unable to proceed. A jury found the breakdown proximately caused the plaintiff’s injuries and assessed damages at $12,000, but also found the locomotive was safe to operate and that the accident was unavoidable. The district court entered judgment for the railroad.

The Fifth Circuit held that the trial court erred by failing to properly instruct the jury on the Boiler Inspection Act and by refusing judgment for the plaintiff. The court concluded that the locomotive’s breakdown and failure of its driving wheels while in use established a violation of the Act as a matter of law, regardless of negligence, and that the jury had found proximate cause and damages. The judgment was reversed with instructions to enter judgment for the plaintiff for $12,000.

The FBI arrested 23-year-old Jerry Drake Varnell of Sayre, Oklahoma, for allegedly attempting to detonate what he believed was an explosives-laden van outside an Oklahoma City bank. Authorities say an undercover agent assisted after learning Varnell wanted to bomb a building, initially the Federal Reserve in Washington, D.C.

The study examines how AI ethics is represented in computing curricula at top Indian engineering institutions. Motivated by growing ethical concerns around AI and gaps between ethical frameworks and practice, the authors analyzed 3,395 publicly available syllabi from the top 100 NIRF-ranked engineering institutions.

Only 75 courses, or 2.21%, included AI ethics content. Most covered it briefly: 60% in one session, 20% in two sessions, 13% over one week, and 7% as a full course. Courses were mainly undergraduate-level, and most had no prerequisites. AI ethics appeared either as standalone courses or as modules within broader AI, machine learning, data science, robotics, NLP, generative AI, and human-centered AI courses.

Common topics included privacy, legal issues, and data governance; accountability and policy; ethical frameworks and moral reasoning; human-AI interaction; algorithmic bias and fairness; AI safety and robustness; generative AI concerns; and social impact and justice. Most syllabi used standard AI or machine learning textbooks, with few ethics-specific resources. Learning objectives addressed privacy risks, fairness, explainability, ethical dilemmas, governance, and ethical reasoning. No syllabus documented assessments explicitly dedicated to AI ethics.

The authors conclude that AI ethics remains marginal, inconsistent, and often superficial in Indian computing education. They identify gaps in coverage of generative AI, sustainability, justice, labor ethics, instructional resources, assessment practices, and public curriculum transparency. They call for clearer learning goals, open teaching materials, India-specific case studies, assessment frameworks, and faculty development to integrate AI ethics more systematically. Limitations include reliance on publicly available syllabi, possible collection omissions, and a focus only on top-ranked engineering institutions.

Mazabuka, Zambia, grew rapidly around the sugar industry, attracting mobile male workers, truckers and a sex trade that helped fuel a severe AIDS epidemic. At its peak in 2003, Zambia recorded about 70,000 AIDS deaths a year, with hospitals and graveyards overwhelmed. HIV prevalence was especially high along transport routes.

The situation has improved through expanded testing, public education and access to drugs that control HIV and prevent AIDS. UNAIDS estimates Zambia still has 250 new infections daily, but infections have fallen 27 percent since 2010 and AIDS-related deaths 11 percent. A local NGO, DAPP, runs a military-style “Total Control of the Epidemic” campaign, using door-to-door outreach, rapid testing, condom distribution, former sex workers, trucker education and public testing by chiefs to reduce stigma. The programme has reached more than 1.5 million Zambians and has been implemented in Mazabuka and Sinazongwe, where officials say it has reached communities government services could not.

A federal judge ordered the Trump administration to reverse layoff notices for nearly all remaining Voice of America employees, including 532 journalists and support staff. Judge Royce C. Lamberth said officials, including Kari Lake, violated his April order requiring the news organization to continue operating as a reliable news source. He criticized reduced programming and staffing, warned officials they risk contempt, and noted Voice of America had dropped from around-the-clock broadcasting to about an hour per day.

Heart attacks and strokes in the UK have fallen by 30% over two decades, helped by cholesterol- and blood-pressure-lowering medicines, but they remain a major health risk. Statins are widely prescribed and effective, with many reported side effects linked to the nocebo effect. Other lipid-lowering treatments include newer medicines targeting PCSK9, usually for very high-risk patients. Lifestyle measures can also improve cholesterol and heart health, including maintaining a healthy weight, quitting smoking, exercising regularly, eating soluble fibre, using omega-3 sources, cooking from scratch, reducing sodium, and consuming plant sterol- or soya-based foods.

The passage is a guide to American football, covering its origins, terminology, rules, scoring, field dimensions, player roles, and notable players. It credits Walter Camp as the key figure in developing American football from rugby, introducing elements such as downs, 11-player teams, the line of scrimmage, the quarterback position, and scoring rules. It explains that American football descended from soccer and rugby, is not currently an Olympic sport, and remains dominated by American players, though flag football may appear at the 2028 Olympics.

American football uses 11 players per team on the field, while Canadian football uses 12. Professional and college games last 60 minutes, divided into four 15-minute quarters; high school games last 48 minutes. A football field is 100 yards between goal lines, with 10-yard end zones and a width of 160 feet.

Scoring includes touchdowns worth 6 points, extra points worth 1, two-point conversions, field goals worth 3, and safeties worth 2. The passage lists Tom Brady, Jerry Rice, Jim Brown, and Lawrence Taylor among the greatest players, noting their major achievements.

It also explains common rules and penalties, including offsides, encroachment, false start, pass interference, holding, defensive holding, personal fouls, roughing the passer, and illegal formation. Other concepts covered include catches, turnovers, interceptions, fumbles, turnover on downs, the line of scrimmage, the neutral zone, special teams, audibles, downs, and the red zone.

CBS’s legal drama “Doubt” premieres Wednesday, Feb. 15 at 10 p.m. Katherine Heigl stars as Sadie Ellis, a defense attorney who falls for client Billy Brennan, a pediatric surgeon accused of murdering his girlfriend 24 years earlier. The firm, led by Isaiah Roth, includes lawyers played by Dulé Hill and Laverne Cox, the first transgender actor to play a transgender regular on broadcast TV. The series combines Billy’s ongoing case with weekly legal stories and Sadie’s backstory. The review calls the show formulaic but competent, with a likable cast and some evenhanded treatment of real issues.

Police seized and are forensically examining a white Holden Commodore possibly linked to Aaron Marks’ murder in Ballina. Investigators are seeking the car’s passengers and checking for fingerprints, DNA, blood and other evidence. The driver is assisting police, who thanked the public and media.

Callum Knott, 21, of Worksop, admitted taking his aunt’s car without consent and driving without a licence or insurance. Mansfield Magistrates Court heard he took it out of boredom and abandoned it when the battery died. He received a 12-month community order, 80 hours’ unpaid work, a four-month ban, and £170 costs.
The East Demerara Football Association held its AGM with six clubs present. Alfred King was re-elected president, and a new executive committee was chosen under GFF observation.

Curaleaf Holdings and the cannabis sector gained on renewed hopes for U.S. cannabis rescheduling after Trump referenced CBD benefits. Curaleaf reported in-line Q2 2025 results, expanded international operations into Turkey, and the author maintained a Hold rating on CURLF due to sector uncertainty.

Cover 2 is a 5-under, 2-deep defense designed to stop quick passes while using safeties to limit deep throws. Its cornerbacks defend the flats, making them vulnerable to high-low route combinations such as smash and fade-out. Offenses also attack Cover 2 with three-receiver surfaces that stress the middle linebacker, vertical concepts like four verticals that strain the safeties, and routes targeting the open middle of the field. The passage gives examples from Ohio State, Oregon, Michigan, Ole Miss, and TCU showing concepts that widen safeties, exploit flat defenders, or create openings over linebacker level and downfield.

Andrew Dawes, CEO of Intels Nigeria Limited, said the company is partnering with the Federal Government and the Nigerian Ports Authority to boost port infrastructure investment. He denied monopoly allegations, stating that Intels invests heavily in concessioned terminals and pays significant fees to government. Dawes said falling oil and gas prices have reduced cargo volumes by 70 percent, slowing investment pace, but the company remains committed to long-term infrastructure development. He highlighted the Phase 4B project at Onne as ready to receive a full FPSO and noted progress on the Badagry deep seaport, planned as Africa’s largest port. Intels, established 30 years ago, provides integrated logistics, terminal operations, manpower, equipment, housing and office services for Nigeria’s oil and gas industry.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2020. The company reported total assets of $38.135 billion, total liabilities of $26.754 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $9.855 billion. For Q2 2020, revenues were $6.036 billion, gross profit was $1.267 billion, income from operations was $327 million, and net income attributable to common stockholders was $104 million, or $0.56 basic and $0.50 diluted per share.

For the six months ended June 30, 2020, revenues were $12.021 billion and net income attributable to common stockholders was $120 million. Operating cash flow was $524 million, investing cash outflow was $1.046 billion, and financing cash inflow was $2.831 billion. Tesla stated that COVID-19 temporarily suspended operations at its manufacturing facilities during the first half of 2020, but operations had resumed at all manufacturing facilities by the end of Q2.

The passage presents a methodology for studying digital business ecosystems (DBEs), defined as closed or semi-closed systems of SMEs interacting through buyer–seller relationships. Because company interactions are asymmetric, the authors argue that Markov random fields are unsuitable and instead propose a neural-network-inspired model using coupled nonlinear differential equations to represent company “fitness.”

The authors describe constructing a simulated DBE with companies, products, SELL and WANT lists, trust and mistrust relationships, and product attributes based on statistical properties of an observed DBE. Trust, indifference, and mistrust are converted into numerical weights using the Weber-Fechner law. Company fitness is modeled through decay, self-excitation, excitatory signals from potential trading partners, inhibitory signals from competitors, external inputs, and background economic input.

Preliminary experiments use a simulated DBE of 100 companies and 20 products to examine survival over iterations under different parameter values, including cases where a monopoly emerges. The authors conclude that simulated DBEs can support quantitative study of systems lacking complete real data, but further work is needed to connect model parameters with measurable quantities from real ecosystems and to refine aspects such as competition for limited supply and random entry of new companies.

The Camarilla pivot point, introduced in 1989 by Nick Scott, extends classical pivot points and provides day traders with four support and four resistance levels. It is used to identify intraday price levels, entries, exits, trend changes, and risk management points. Camarilla pivots use the previous day’s closing prices, while Fibonacci pivots use retracements and extensions. The passage encourages traders to backtest Camarilla strategies, noting prior ordinary pivot backtests showed no “super profits.”

The MOSAIC study evaluated a blood-based multi-omics approach for lung cancer detection using plasma samples from 2,513 subjects enrolled across 77 U.S. clinical sites. The study aimed to address limitations of low-dose CT screening, including low adherence and false-positive concerns, by developing a peripheral blood biomarker classifier for early-stage lung cancer.

After quality control and eligibility review, 2,094 subjects were clinically eligible, including 816 with lung cancer and 1,278 non-cancer controls. Proteomics, RNA-seq, metabolomics, and targeted immunoassay data were collected. The study detected 113,671 peptides, 219,729 mRNA transcripts, 71,756 introns, and 1,801 metabolites in at least one subject. Differential analysis found thousands of analytes differing between lung cancer and non-cancer cohorts, with substantial molecular heterogeneity.

Subjects with complete molecular data were divided into a training set of 1,225 and a validation set of 398. A baseline classifier using age, sex, and smoking status achieved an all-stage lung cancer AUC of 0.78. A classifier using untargeted proteomics achieved an AUC of 0.91. A multi-omics classifier using proteomics, metabolomics, RNA-seq, and four immunoassayed proteins achieved an all-stage AUC of 0.96 and stage I AUC of 0.93 in training.

In the held-out validation set, using a threshold fixed at 87.5% sensitivity in training, the multi-omics model achieved 89% specificity and 89% sensitivity across all lung cancer stages. Sensitivity was 80% for stage I, 88% for stage II, and 99% for stage III–IV lung cancer.

The final model included 682 analyte features: 211 peptide features mapping to 149 proteins, 354 transcript features mapping to 346 genes, and 117 metabolite features from 77 pathways. No single omics type dominated the most important features. Of the 682 features, 412 were significantly associated with cancer stage.

The authors conclude that this untargeted multi-omics biomarker discovery approach showed high performance for detecting all-stage and early-stage lung cancer and may support development of a blood-based early detection assay. They note that prospective validation in the intended high-risk screening population is needed.

The Trump administration is using long-standing criticisms of academic publishing—such as research fraud, paper mills, peer-review shortages, high costs and “publish or perish” incentives—to justify attacks on scientific institutions and journals. HHS secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and NIH director Jayanta Bhattacharya have criticized medical journals, pharmaceutical industry influence, bias, misinformation and limited access, while proposing changes including possible publication restrictions, a government journal, open-access requirements and caps on article processing charges.

Researchers and publishing experts acknowledge real problems in scientific publishing but question whether the administration’s proposals will improve them. Some warn the administration is exploiting legitimate concerns to advance ideological goals, especially while cutting NIH grants and budgets. Critics say a government journal could raise credibility concerns, open access alone will not restore public trust, and APC caps may shift costs elsewhere. Experts argue deeper reform must address research incentives, NIH peer review and how academic institutions evaluate scientists.

The coach said certain players have earned attention by delivering quality minutes, especially defensively, while contributing offensively in the playoffs. He emphasized puck possession, faceoffs, a familiar system, hard work, and directing pucks at the net as important factors, while noting the team was fortunate in a close Stanley Cup Finals win. He discussed tactical adjustments, including the opponent breaking up its top line, and credited Sammy Pahlsson’s shot. He said league competitiveness was tighter due partly to the salary cap. An injured player with pins in his hands was unlikely to return without medical clearance. He described optional skates and playoff routines involving hotel check-ins, meals, and naps. He minimized comments about Getzlaf, saying he does not publicly criticize players. He praised a veteran defenseman’s size, net-front play, and contribution. He said health affected fourth-line usage and that young players’ minutes must be managed. He also said the team aimed to move beyond mediocrity after losing to Edmonton, with Chris Pronger’s acquisition signaling a push toward becoming elite.

Lookout researchers reported that over a thousand Google Play apps contain SonicSpy spyware, which can record audio, take photos, make calls, send texts, retrieve data, and respond to more than 73 remote commands. A recent example, Soniac, posed as a messaging app using a customized Telegram version while hiding itself and connecting to command-and-control infrastructure. The iraqwebservice account behind Soniac had previously posted two other SonicSpy samples. Lookout warned that such apps are especially concerning for enterprises because they imitate trusted messaging tools and can compromise sensitive information on employee devices.

The Supreme Court again allowed the Trump administration to end Temporary Protected Status for hundreds of thousands of Venezuelan nationals, pausing a ruling by U.S. District Judge Edward Chen that had found Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem acted unlawfully. The court said its May decision pausing Chen’s earlier order applied because the parties’ legal arguments and harms had generally not changed. Justices Sonia Sotomayor, Elena Kagan, and Ketanji Brown Jackson would have denied the administration’s request. Jackson dissented, calling the order a misuse of the emergency docket and arguing the government had not shown a time-sensitive need for Supreme Court intervention.

Manjot Kalra, Player of the Match in the 2018 ICC Under-19 World Cup final, struggled to express himself in the post-match presentation but impressed on the field with an unbeaten century that helped India win its fourth U19 World Cup title. He built key partnerships with Prithvi Shaw and Shubman Gill, then adjusted his approach to guide the chase with Harvik Desai. The article notes Kalra’s sudden rise into the spotlight after being overshadowed by teammates and bought at base price in the IPL auction. It cautions against early comparisons with senior Indian stars, citing past U19 World Cup final centurions and players like Unmukt Chand who did not progress to senior international cricket. Rahul Dravid said the win should be a cherished memory but not one that defines the players, emphasizing that their careers are just beginning.
Seeking Alpha prompts users to enable JavaScript and cookies, and to disable ad-blockers if they are blocked from proceeding.

Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts is offering voluntary buyouts to about 750 employees aged 55 and older with at least 10 years at the company, as it seeks to reduce its workforce amid rising health care costs and financial losses. The buyouts are its first since the late 1980s.

Max Hayes High School Auto Collision Repair students refurbished a Cleveland police cruiser damaged during the 2016 Cavs championship celebrations. Teacher Greg Boykin proposed the project after seeing the damage on the news. Students rebuilt and repainted the vehicle with donated materials, saving the city about $10,000. The cruiser, once considered a total loss, will return to service as a zone car.

The passage describes a patent for dynamic graphics rendering based on saccade detection. The invention renders a computer simulated scene, detects the onset of a user’s saccade that causes saccadic masking, and reduces computing resources used to render frames during at least part of the saccade. The system may include an eye movement sensor, display, processor, memory, and optionally a GPU, and may be used in VR, AR, head-mounted displays, wearable devices, computers, game consoles, and similar systems.

Saccades may be detected using sensors such as cameras, optical sensors, infrared sensors, EMG sensors, Doppler sensors, range sensors, microphones, or optical reflector sensors. During detected saccades, the system may skip frames, repeat frames, reduce rendering resolution or detail, lower frame rate, or use less demanding rendering techniques. Saved computing resources may reduce power consumption or be reallocated to tasks such as complex lighting calculations.

The system may predict saccade duration using eye movement models, onset magnitude, acceleration, speed, EMG signals, or peak movement data. It may also measure saccade endings to calibrate predictions for individual users. Confidence levels in detection may determine how much rendering reduction is applied. The technique can be combined with foveated rendering and implemented through software stored on non-transitory computer-readable media.

UOB FX strategists say GBP/USD is unlikely to pull back to 1.2900 near term. They see scope for a slow rise toward 1.3040/45, with 1.3060 needed to end the bearish phase. Support is at 1.2975 and 1.2939.

The passage explains how to build and backtest an RSI-based trading strategy in TradingView using Pine Script. The example uses DOT on a 5-minute timeframe with a 14-period RSI, 65/35 overbought and oversold levels, long entries when RSI exits oversold, short entries when RSI exits overbought, and exits at RSI 50. It describes adding RSI to a chart, modifying settings, creating a strategy script, defining RSI conditions, using `strategy.entry` and `strategy.close`, and adding user inputs for configurable parameters. TradingView provides results such as equity curve, net profit, drawdown, win rate, performance metrics, and trade lists. Deep backtesting is available for Pro or higher accounts and uses available historical data. The passage notes that RSI alone may not perform consistently and is best used with other indicators or criteria.

Police arrested 40-year-old Nannette Perkins at her Taylorsville home after a tip, believing she was the pajama-wearing robber in at least six Salt Lake City-area bank robberies. She was held pending court.

Microsoft filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2017. For the quarter, revenue was $28.9 billion, up from $25.8 billion a year earlier, with operating income of $8.7 billion. The company reported a net loss of $6.3 billion, or $0.82 per share, compared with net income of $6.3 billion, or $0.80 diluted EPS, in the prior-year quarter, primarily reflecting a $13.8 billion estimated net charge related to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act.

For the six months ended December 31, 2017, revenue was $53.5 billion, operating income was $16.4 billion, and net income was $274 million. Total assets were $256.0 billion, total liabilities were $177.6 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $78.4 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $142.8 billion.

Net cash from operations was $20.3 billion for the six-month period. Microsoft had $12.5 billion of commercial paper outstanding and $76.8 billion in long-term debt, including the current portion. Unearned revenue totaled $23.8 billion, and contracted revenue not yet recognized was $61 billion.

Microsoft completed its LinkedIn acquisition on December 8, 2016 for $27.0 billion. Goodwill was $35.4 billion, and intangible assets were $9.0 billion. The company repurchased $3.4 billion of common stock during fiscal 2018 through December 31 and declared quarterly dividends of $0.42 per share. Legal liabilities accrued were $370 million, with additional reasonably possible adverse outcomes estimated at approximately $1.3 billion beyond recorded amounts.

The passage argues that student newsrooms are vital to campus communities, comparable to local news in small towns. It warns that removing them would limit students’ access to information about campus issues, events, and broader social debates. It connects student journalism to concerns about news deserts, media consolidation, and the public’s ability to make informed decisions. The author emphasizes that students need diverse, challenging information to become informed citizens and future workers.

American Mint offers the 24k gold-layered Band of Brothers Men’s Ring in sizes 8–14 for $129.90 while supplies last. The company sells collectibles and memorabilia and has served over a million customers from its Mechanicsburg facility.

The study developed strategies for managing vocational education toward excellence for institutions under Thailand’s Office of the Vocational Education Commission. It used a research and development approach in two phases: investigating current and desired conditions and needs, then developing and evaluating a strategic framework. Data were collected through document analysis, questionnaires from 206 respondents, interviews with exemplary institutions, SWOT analysis, and expert focus groups.

Findings showed that current vocational education management conditions were at a high level, while desired conditions were at the highest level. The overall priority needs index was 0.179. The highest need was curriculum development, followed by cooperation networks, personnel, teaching management, graduate quality, and management.

The resulting strategy framework consisted of vision, mission, objectives, strategies, and indicators. Six strategies were identified: enhancing professional management effectiveness; developing competency-based curricula to international standards; improving teaching and learning toward vocational education excellence; developing teachers and staff toward specialized professional expertise; building comprehensive networks for workforce development; and improving graduate quality for a high-competency workforce. Expert evaluation found the strategies’ suitability and feasibility to be at the highest level.

The study recommends that institutions prioritize competency-based curriculum development, adapt strategies to their specific contexts, and integrate them with existing plans and activities. Future research should focus on curriculum development models aligned with professional competencies and qualification systems, and on improving personnel capacity to produce digital content and meet international competency standards.
Cancer cells transfer mitochondria to fibroblasts, altering gene activity and promoting growth.

A QQQ mean reversion trading strategy has reportedly performed well since January 2000, with high profit factor, lower drawdown than buy and hold, and about 12.34% CAGR. Exits occur when the close exceeds yesterday’s high or close, but future performance is uncertain.

David Dickinson describes the anticipation surrounding the August 21 total solar eclipse crossing the United States from Oregon to South Carolina, bringing up to two minutes and 40 seconds of totality along a 70-mile-wide path. He explains the dedication of eclipse chasers, or umbraphiles, who travel globally to witness totality, which they distinguish sharply from partial eclipses. Dickinson recounts missing past total eclipses and planning to see his first at the Pisgah Astronomical Research Institute in North Carolina, while noting weather risks and other observers’ plans to adjust locations based on forecasts.

He emphasizes safe viewing, warning that looking at the sun during partial phases can damage eyes and recommending approved solar glasses, solar filters, or pinhole projection. He also advises first-time viewers to enjoy totality rather than focus on photography. Dickinson notes that total eclipses are possible because the sun and moon appear similar in size from Earth, but the moon’s gradual recession will eventually end total solar eclipses. He suggests the event may renew interest in science and notes another U.S. eclipse will occur on April 8, 2024.

The passage explains the London breakout strategy, a forex day trading approach that trades breakouts above or below the Asian session range during the London session, usually within its first three hours. Traders go long on upside breakouts and short on downside breakouts. The strategy is based on the London session’s high liquidity and volatility and can define the Asian range using either high-low prices or open-close candle bodies.

The passage describes the London breakout indicator as a custom forex tool that provides entry, stop loss, and take profit levels, often based on the Tokyo/Asian range, and can be automated. A backtest on EUR/USD found poor results for upside breakouts and near-zero average gains when fading downside breakouts, leading the authors to state the strategy needs more parameters or risk management and to express skepticism about forex trading edges. The passage also lists typical forex session times for London, Asian, and New York sessions and promotes a package of backtestable trading rules that includes the London breakout strategy code.

The study evaluates the maturity of recent AI in healthcare publications using a semi-automated approach combining a BERT-based maturity classifier with manual annotation. Prior literature offered limited assessment of publication maturity and key characteristics such as data type, model type, geography, and specialty.

The authors analyzed PubMed-indexed English-language human-subject publications from 2019–2021, selected from prior in-house AI in healthcare reviews and classified into medical specialties. After exclusions, the cohort included 1647 publications from 2019, 3232 from 2020, and 2182 from 2021. A BERT PubMed classifier assessed maturity from titles and abstracts, and mature articles were manually annotated for data type, model type, and disease type.

Only 5% of publications were classified as mature. Mature publications numbered 99 in 2019, 250 in 2020, and 36 in 2021 after excluding systematic reviews. Radiology had the highest number of mature models across the three years, followed by Pathology in 2019, Ophthalmology in 2020, and Gastroenterology in 2021. Gastroenterology, Oncology, and Ophthalmology showed steady increases. COVID-19 publications were numerous, but only 4% in 2020 and 1.6% in 2021 were mature.

Mature publications were geographically concentrated, with the United States and China leading most years; regions including South America, Eastern Europe, and Africa were underrepresented. Image data dominated mature publications, appearing in about 88–89% each year, while tabular data declined and text data increased. Deep learning was the most common model type, used in 66% of mature publications in 2019, 71% in 2020, and 62% in 2021.

The authors conclude that mature AI healthcare publications remain limited, especially outside radiology, and that broader use of diverse data types, models, and global resources could increase mature AI research across healthcare.

The study investigates MnBi₂Te₄/(Bi₂Te₃)ₙ crystals grown by the Inverted Vertical Bridgman Method, focusing on how melt flow, MnTe precipitation, and Mn distribution control stacking sequences and magnetic behavior. Four samples from different ingot positions showed distinct structures despite the same starting composition. Sample A contained pure MnBi₂Te₄ and MnBi₂Te₄/Bi₂Te₃ regions with high Mn content and antiferromagnetic transitions at 26 K and 13.5 K. Sample B was dominated by MnBi₂Te₄/Bi₂Te₃ and MnBi₂Te₄/(Bi₂Te₃)₂ phases, with a 13.5 K antiferromagnetic transition. Sample C showed grouped septuple layers separated by 7 ± 2 quintuple layers and ferromagnetic behavior near 11 K. Sample D showed more disorder, septuple-layer spacing of 4–5 quintuple layers, Mn-depleted septuple layers, and ferromagnetic behavior near 9 K.

TEM, EDX, SQUID magnetometry, and magnetic resonance measurements showed that magnetic ordering depends strongly on septuple-layer spacing and Mn content. Closely spaced, Mn-complete septuple layers produced antiferromagnetic phases, while larger separations and Mn depletion were associated with ferromagnetic-like behavior and reduced anisotropy.

The authors identify four growth regimes: turbulent flow enabling pure MnBi₂Te₄ formation, rapid MnTe precipitation reducing Mn concentration, stationary flow promoting ordered quintuple/septuple layering, and final flow cessation causing enhanced diffusion, structural disorder, Mn depletion, and stacking defects. They propose that septuple-layer spacing is inversely related to MnTe supersaturation due to diffusion-limited competition between MnBi₂Te₄ growth fronts. The results emphasize that controlling melt composition and flow dynamics is critical for tuning structure and magnetism in bulk-grown magnetic topological insulators.

A Nigerian bank support staff warned about an ATM fraud in which scammers ask people to receive transfers and withdraw cash for them, claiming they have exceeded withdrawal limits. The transfers are allegedly made from stolen phones or hacked accounts, causing recipients’ accounts to be frozen, their BVN flagged, and possible police action. The banker cited two cases: an 18-year-old forced at gunpoint to withdraw ₦40,000 and an adult who helped withdraw ₦50,000 and now faces arrest. The warning advises people not to accept transfer-for-withdrawal requests at ATMs.

The passage introduces a study of antiferromagnetic domain wall dynamics under spin-orbit torque. It notes growing interest due to improved observation, imaging, and manipulation of antiferromagnetic order, and highlights advantages over ferromagnets such as absence of stray fields and potentially faster domain wall motion.

The authors study precessional, propagating, and oscillatory domain wall dynamics, emphasizing effects beyond the idealized nonlinear σ-model, including damping-induced breaking of Lorentz invariance. They also discuss magnetic moments carried by antiferromagnetic textures, including additional moment contributions from time-dependent Néel order.

The model considers a spin chain with antiferromagnetic exchange, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, perpendicular anisotropy, damping, and spin torque from polarized electrons. A continuum approximation is derived using tetramers for a two-dimensional square spin lattice, yielding an extended nonlinear σ-model for the Néel vector. Magnetization is expressed in terms of the time dependence of the Néel vector. Numerical simulations are performed on a discrete spin lattice.
