For spin current polarization along the perpendicular axis and no Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, simulations show that an initially static Néel-type domain wall evolves into a steady state in which all spins precess around the axis with constant angular frequency. The theoretical treatment uses spherical parametrization of the Néel vector and derives equations describing stable precession.

California’s Department of Fish and Wildlife certified additional environmental analysis and re-approved Newhall Ranch after developers revised plans addressing greenhouse gas emissions and protections for the endangered unarmored three spine stickleback. The review followed a 2015 California Supreme Court order requiring closer examination of emissions impacts and fish-protection measures. Newhall Land, owned by FivePoint, created a Net Zero Newhall plan with 13 greenhouse gas reduction measures, and the California Air Resources Board found an adequate basis to conclude the project would not add net greenhouse gas emissions. The developer also changed bridge and bank stabilization construction plans to avoid water contact, eliminating the need for prior fish relocation measures. The project could include 12,000 homes and 11.5 million square feet of commercial and industrial space.

Young African entrepreneurs are using technology to make agriculture more resilient to climate change while creating jobs. In Rwanda, Jean Bosco Nzeyimana’s Habona Ltd employs 25 young people to turn organic waste into fuel briquettes and fertiliser, reducing open-fire waste burning and producing 50 tonnes of fuel monthly. In Malawi, Pilirani Khoza’s Bunda Female Students Organisation funds disadvantaged women science students, who train rural women farmers in climate-resilient methods such as water conservation, tree planting and growing drought- and flood-tolerant crops; the project has reached 360 farmers. In Kenya, Brian Bosire’s UjuziKilimo uses handheld soil sensors and mobile advice to help farmers choose crops and inputs, with plans to reach 200,000 farmers. Speakers at the Young Africa Works Summit said youth are central to transforming agriculture amid worsening climate pressures. Richard Munang of the U.N. Environment Programme said agriculture is key to reducing poverty in Africa and can create jobs through value chains involving technology, logistics and clean energy.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on February 13, 2020, it entered into an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC and Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC to issue and sell 2,650,000 shares of common stock in a public offering. Tesla granted underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to 397,500 additional shares, which was exercised in full on February 18, 2020. The offering closed on February 19, 2020, generating approximately $2.31 billion in net proceeds after discounts, commissions, and estimated expenses. Tesla also reported waivers of certain registration rights related to the offering and filed related exhibits, including the underwriting agreement, waiver, legal opinion, consent, and press release.

Bar Harbor Bankshares reported 2016 net income of $14.9 million, including $2.7 million in acquisition and system conversion charges. Assets rose to $1.8 billion, loans increased 14 percent, and non-interest income rose 38 percent, aided by securities gains.

Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN) is a hereditary cancer syndrome involving tumors in two or more endocrine glands, with MEN1, MEN2, and MEN4 linked to MEN1, RET, and CDKN1B variants respectively. This study classified MEN-linked variants in RET, MEN1, and CDKN1B from IndiGen, ClinVar, and Mastermind using ACMG/AMP guidelines to assess MEN genetic epidemiology in India and create the MAPVar database.

The analysis identified 1,324 unique variants for classification and estimated that about 1 in 341 individuals in India is a likely carrier of MEN-linked pathogenic RET mutations. Two likely pathogenic RET variants were found in IndiGen, one in an individual from Jammu and Kashmir and another in two individuals from Odisha. Comparison with 18 global datasets showed one variant was absent elsewhere, while the other appeared at low frequencies in selected populations and was significantly more frequent in IndiGen.

MAPVar contains 3,280 ACMG-classified MEN-linked variants: 1,094 pathogenic/likely pathogenic, 1,591 benign/likely benign, and 595 variants of uncertain significance. It provides searchable variant annotations, population frequencies, computational predictions, ACMG attributes, and classifications. Querying GUaRDIAN endocrine cohort data identified seven patient cases with MEN-linked pathogenic variants. The study also developed a multiplex primer panel covering coding regions of RET, MEN1, and CDKN1B across 38 amplicons, and used it in 72 endocrine disorder patients, resolving three cases with pathogenic MEN1 mutations. The authors conclude that MEN is understudied in India and that MAPVar and the NGS panel can support genetic testing, diagnosis, and variant interpretation.

The Supreme Court heard arguments on whether the U.S. Postal Service and federal government can be sued for intentional failure to deliver mail under the Federal Tort Claims Act’s postal exception. The case involves Lebene Konan, a Texas landlady who alleged postal workers intentionally withheld mail as racial harassment. The government argued the exception covers such claims, while Konan argued it applies only to loss, miscarriage, or negligent transmission, not intentional acts. Justices debated the meanings of “loss” and “miscarriage,” concerns about increased lawsuits, and whether barring claims could shield serious intentional misconduct. A decision is expected by early July.

The passage compiles Nov. 19–20, 2001 news on Enron’s worsening financial condition. Enron restated its third-quarter loss to 87 cents a share, or $664 million, and warned that credit concerns, asset declines and reduced trading could hurt fourth-quarter earnings, including a possible $700 million pretax loss tied to Whitewing LLP. A credit downgrade triggered a $690 million obligation due unless Enron posted collateral or renegotiated terms; failure could allow liquidation of partnership assets, including Brazilian gas assets. A further downgrade could trigger $3.9 billion in additional repayments. Reports also noted concerns that Dynegy might abandon its proposed acquisition under material adverse change provisions, while shareholder lawsuits and accounting investigations posed risks. Arthur Andersen had not completed its review of Enron’s filings, and Rep. John Dingell requested an investigation into Andersen’s audits of Enron and Waste Management.

At Silverbluff Audubon Center in Aiken County, staff are rooting for the Philadelphia Eagles in the Super Bowl because bald eagles live there, including a nesting pair present since 1994. VOT broadcasts to Tibet on shortwave at 11.510, 9.510, and 15.565 MHz at listed Tibet, India, and Nepal times, with frequent retuning advised. VOT satellite radio is on ASIASAT 7 at 105.5°E, 4146 MHz, horizontal polarization, SR 5317, FEC 5/6, listed as “MOMO,” broadcasting 24/7 in alternating 30-minute Mandarin and Tibetan segments.

Radford University named two finalists for Vice President for Student Affairs after Dr. Irvin Clark’s departure and Susan Trageser’s interim service. Forums were held Sept. 11–12, 2017. Dr. Thomas C. Segar, Vice President for Student Affairs at Shepherd University, emphasized student success, belonging, social justice, experiential learning, student services, institutional pride, and proactive advising. Dr. Ann Marie Klotz, Dean of Campus Life at New York Institute of Technology, highlighted mentorship, student-centered adaptability, community building, and using social media to share Radford’s story. Both finalists were described as experienced and interested in joining Radford.

Christa Goldblatt of Crossborder Energy emailed the Rebuttal Testimony of R. Thomas Beach on behalf of the Indicated Electric Generators in CPUC proceeding I.99-07-003, supporting the Comprehensive Settlement Agreement.

Beach’s testimony responds to SCGC and TURN’s Post-Interim Settlement Agreement, which he says fails to unbundle intrastate transmission on the SoCalGas system. He recommends that the Commission adopt the Comprehensive Settlement Agreement, arguing it advances the Commission’s identified restructuring options and has broad stakeholder support.

The testimony argues that SCGC and TURN overstate differences between PG&E and SoCalGas, and that SoCalGas’ backbone system can be unbundled similarly to PG&E’s Gas Accord. Beach states that the Gas Accord’s city-gate market has benefited electric generators through lower transportation-related costs without requiring customers to hold capacity or pay demand charges.

Beach also argues that SCGC and TURN’s cost-benefit analysis ignores benefits and exaggerates costs. He says the Comprehensive Settlement would reduce electric generator rates, improve rate certainty, shift backbone cost-recovery risk to SoCalGas shareholders, reduce storage revenue risk, and create new opportunities through unbundled transmission, storage, and balancing services.

The testimony disputes SCGC and TURN’s concerns about demand charges, asserting that generators can mitigate or avoid them through optional rates, interruptible service, secondary capacity markets, and city-gate gas purchases. Beach concludes that claims of plant closures, job losses, and reliability problems are unsupported or overstated.
All four analysts predict Beneil Dariush to beat Evan Dunham at UFC 216, citing Dariush’s superior all-around skills and ground game despite Dunham’s toughness and recent momentum.
Jacob Allen sued for withheld inheritance from Hope Allen’s estate; the jury awarded him his proportional share under the will and court costs.

Nick Kyrgios defeated Jan-Lennard Struff 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 to level Australia’s 2018 Davis Cup tie with Germany in Brisbane. Earlier, Alexander Zverev beat Alex de Minaur in five sets after the Australian teenager led two sets to one. Global markets sold off amid fears of potential conflict, with volatility expected to continue. A UCLA-led mouse study suggests black tea may support health and weight loss by altering gut bacteria, increasing microbes linked to lean body mass and decreasing those linked to obesity. Black tea acts in the gut, while green tea affects both gut and liver.

The article addresses the gap between U.S. higher education institutions’ global citizenship goals and low study abroad participation, citing financial, administrative, and logistical barriers. It argues for sustainable, scalable education abroad models that align curricular objectives, operational logistics, and financial structures.

The authors present a framework for designing faculty-led education abroad programs, emphasizing learning outcomes, credit structure, assessment, location, program duration, partnerships, risk management, leadership, travel timing, lodging, transportation, communication, meals, emergency planning, student preparation, and student wellbeing. Financial planning includes faculty and staff costs, external partner expenses, project and coordination costs, tuition, student fees, scholarships, grants, corporate sponsorships, and internal budget distribution.

The article identifies business model types based on external party-led, faculty-led, and student-led programs. External party models reduce faculty workload but increase student costs. Faculty-led models may rely on student payments, revenue generation, corporate donations, or grants. Student-led models often operate through clubs, donations, and student activity fees. The article concludes that sustainable global learning programs require careful alignment of academic goals, logistics, funding, institutional support, and delegation of responsibilities.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K dated July 8, 2021, announcing it will redeem all outstanding 2.125% Notes due December 6, 2021, with €1.75 billion principal, on September 6, 2021. The redemption price will equal the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the redemption date. The filing includes a July 8, 2021 press release as Exhibit 99.1.

Parker Hogan, 19, pleaded not guilty to charges related to allegedly helping plan roommate Michael Buskey’s suicide in New Hampshire. The speaker discussed adjusting to a large screen on the power play, improving puck visibility, and relying on fundamentals after a long layoff. Officials marked the completion of the 179-megawatt Switch Station 1 and 2 solar projects at Apex Industrial Park near Las Vegas. The arrays will power Switch data centers in Reno and Las Vegas and can generate electricity equivalent to the needs of 46,000 Nevada homes.

Hartman assesses that Andropov’s foreign policy shows no major experimentation or flexibility and largely continues Brezhnev’s line, including on Afghanistan, Poland, and Southern Africa. He argues the regime will be difficult to deal with, though U.S.-Soviet relations remain a Soviet priority. He says U.S. policy must focus first on security and reducing the danger of nuclear war, while avoiding past overreliance on arms control. Hartman recommends giving arms control higher priority because it is the main available catalyst for improving relations and is perceived publicly, especially in Western Europe, as a weak point in U.S. policy. He argues the U.S. INF “zero-zero” position has nearly outlived its usefulness and should change. He says Soviet strategy aims to block U.S. deployment in Europe without reducing Soviet forces, using negotiations and propaganda to influence European public opinion. Hartman warns that unless the U.S. anticipates further Soviet moves after the German election, the INF deployment schedule may be endangered. He recalls that the NATO INF deployment decision was chiefly political, meant to reassure Europeans that the U.S. would defend them against nuclear attack.

The study examines how advanced technologies may affect the digital transformation and management of higher education institutions offering open and distance education. It focuses on artificial intelligence, blockchain, metaverse, virtual and augmented reality, brain-computer interfaces, and brain chips.

Using a qualitative case study design, the researchers conducted semi-structured interviews with four Anadolu University academics who had at least 20 years of experience in open and distance education and practical experience in distance education management. Interview data were analyzed through content analysis using Nvivo.

Participants stated that advanced technologies could transform educational environments, administrative processes, services, content production, assessment, and learner support. Artificial intelligence was associated with adaptive learning, synthetic content, personal teaching assistants, managerial decision-making, supervision, evaluation, anomaly detection, and possible AI-based managers. Blockchain was linked to centralized control, recognition of prior learning, certification, and educational records. Metaverse, virtual reality, augmented reality, and brain-computer interfaces were discussed in relation to practice-based learning, virtual selves, brain chips, and new learning environments.

In management, participants emphasized the need for careful planning, cost-benefit analysis, investment decisions, and organizational adaptation. They predicted flatter structures, reduced hierarchy, increased automation, new employment areas, demand for technologically skilled knowledge workers, and possible reductions in some white-collar jobs.

Regarding economic effects, participants noted both potential savings and new infrastructure costs. They associated advanced technologies with increased productivity, reduced error rates, profit growth, automation concerns, unemployment risks, and the need for new human resources to manage technology.

Regarding socio-cultural effects, participants predicted changes in lifestyles, communication, cultural structures, and virtual communities. Concerns included increased screen use, laziness, dependency, reduced physical communication, virtual addiction, and psychological or sociological problems. The study concludes that institutions should prepare for these transformations by developing AI assistants and managers, blockchain-based certification systems, adaptive synthetic content, metaverse learning structures, and further research on brain-computer interfaces and brain chips.

Analyst Ming-chi Kuo expects Apple Watch Series 3 to include LTE-only cellular and non-cellular models in 38mm and 42mm sizes, with 17.5–18 million sales forecast next year and 2.8–3.6 million LTE units.

A Senate committee criticized the Supreme Court of Canada’s Jordan ruling, warning its trial deadlines could lead to many criminal charges being dismissed. The committee issued 50 recommendations to speed trials, arguing the justice system needs broad reform rather than rigid timelines.

John Bryant, a pro se Sing Sing inmate, sued DOCS, Sing Sing, and Officer Hernandez under Section 1983, alleging constitutional violations from a 20-day “Code Blue” lockdown based on Hernandez’s false ammunition report. Bryant claimed inmates were confined, searched, denied services, and inadequately compensated for prison work. DOCS moved to dismiss on Eleventh Amendment grounds. The court adopted Judge Maas’s recommendation, holding that DOCS and Sing Sing are state agencies immune from suit and not “persons” under Section 1983. The claims against DOCS and Sing Sing were dismissed, while Bryant’s claim against Officer Hernandez could proceed if service was proper.

The Government is consulting on reforms to tackle irresponsible company directors after failures such as Carillion and BHS. Proposals include reversing asset stripping to recover money for workers, disqualifying directors who sell struggling firms, and strengthening the Insolvency Service. Greg Clark said regulators need tougher powers, while Frank Field welcomed greater accountability. Rebecca Long-Bailey criticised the Government for acting too late.

The passage describes systems, devices, and methods for neural modulation, particularly spinal cord stimulation. A neuromodulation system includes electrodes on one or more leads, a modulation generator, and a programming system that determines electrode fractionalizations based on a target multipole. The target multipole uses progressively stacked target anodes and cathodes to produce a linear electric field over neural tissue, with options for directional electrodes, flanking electrodes, automatic movement within an electrode array, and search heuristics to optimize field strength, pole spacing, orientation, focus, and spread.

The programming system may include user interfaces for adjusting field angle, length, width, therapy strength, anatomical target regions, and patient-identified pain areas. Methods include programming modulation parameters, delivering energy through selected electrodes, and automatically determining or optimizing target multipoles.

The passage also describes neuromodulation system components, including implantable pulse generators, leads, electrodes, external programmers, remote controls, trial modulators, telemetry links, and waveform generators. It discusses spinal cord anatomy and explains that field shaping can preferentially modulate dorsal horn or dorsal root tissue while reducing dorsal column activation, potentially providing sub-perception therapy. Various figures illustrate spinal anatomy, system architecture, electrode configurations, target multipoles, field gradients, paddle and percutaneous lead implementations, and interface controls.

A $1.8-million Grand River Conservation Authority project will use LiDAR technology over five years to create detailed digital 3D floodplain maps for the Grand River and most of the Speed and Conestogo rivers. The maps will replace many hard-copy maps over 40 years old and support new flood forecasting software to provide near real-time predictions of downstream flooding and at-risk areas. The technology can model land and riverbeds, helping identify where water may spill over. Spokesperson Cam Linwood said updated maps are needed because rivers change over time and can improve emergency notifications during sudden floods.

Engineers reported a rapid optical technique for screening structural properties of natural and synthetic protein sequences, including inside living bacteria, using femto- and pico-second lasers in flow cytometry. The method, time-domain thermo-transmission, assesses crystallinity in milliseconds without heating samples enough to alter structure or kill cells. It can sort proteins with desired properties, including squid ring teeth-derived proteins produced by bacteria. The proof-of-concept worked, and Demirel received Defense University Research Instrumentation Program funding to develop larger-scale equipment.

A hockey player says children enjoy being on the ice when players are not skating. He describes the next game as very important but says the team must focus on execution rather than consequences. He says everyone wants to win the Cup, calling it a once-in-a-lifetime chance. The team plans to review tape, make defensive adjustments, reduce shots allowed, and improve along the boards against Detroit’s strong lines.

The paper addresses risk analysis in digital business ecosystems, where a trusting agent must decide whether to interact with a probable trusted agent. It defines risk as involving both the probability of failure and the consequences of failure, and focuses on determining the probability of failure beforehand.

The authors use the concepts of FailureLevel and a failure scale to express how likely a trusted agent is to fail to meet the trusting agent’s criteria. They propose dividing the relevant time space into non-overlapping time slots and assessing FailureLevel dynamically over time. In the pre-interaction phase, FailureLevel is determined from the trusting agent’s past interactions or from recommendations, considering recommendation trustworthiness, timing, and relevance to the interaction criteria. In the post-interaction phase, future FailureLevel is predicted using previously determined FailureLevels and Gaussian distribution to estimate the probability of each failure level.

An example compares two logistics agents for transporting goods, calculating their predicted failure probabilities across failure levels. The paper concludes that this methodology helps a trusting agent estimate the probability of failure before interaction; assessing consequences of failure is left as future work.

No. 14 Iowa State suffered its first loss of the season, falling 38-30 to Cincinnati after trailing 31-7 at halftime. The defeat ended the Cyclones’ unbeaten start and opened up the Big 12 championship race. The passage compares the result to last season’s Big 12 chaos, when unexpected teams rose while expected contenders struggled, suggesting the conference could again be unpredictable in 2025.

Kazakhstan’s education programs emphasize developing inclusive education and improving access for disabled students. The study aimed to evaluate disabled education in the distance education process according to inclusive education quality, based on special education teachers’ opinions.

Using a qualitative case study design, researchers interviewed 10 special education teachers in Kazakhstan who taught students with hearing and speech impairments, visual impairments, or mild intellectual disabilities. Data were collected through semi-structured online interviews and analyzed thematically.

Teachers reported using online lessons, video sharing, homework checks, online activities, and mobile applications during distance education. Most preferred formal education over distance education. Six teachers found distance education insufficient for meeting students’ individual learning needs. Teachers identified family anxiety, lack of technological resources, communication problems, and insufficient online family education as barriers to family participation. They also described teacher–student and peer interaction as weak, limited by time, unqualified, or disorganized.

The study recommends diversifying technology-based learning methods, creating content based on disabled students’ individual needs, organizing online seminars for families, and supporting regular social activities to improve teacher, student, and peer interaction.

A memorial match for Kirkcaldy footballer and Raith fan Aidan Sutherland, who died from diabetes complications shortly after his 20th birthday, will be held at Stark’s Park on Sunday. Organised by his friend Ben Graham, the event aims to raise diabetes awareness and funds for the Diabetes Research and Wellness Foundation. Friends, former teammates and ex-professionals including Colin Cameron and Darren Dods will play, with other activities including a pipe band, stalls, face painting and a sweetie bar. This study examined the relationship between Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and epilepsy-causing genes using transcriptomic data from multiple AD cohorts and brain regions. Prior evidence indicates a bidirectional association between AD and epilepsy, with seizures and epileptiform activity linked to earlier cognitive decline, faster progression, amyloid-β deposition, and tau hyperphosphorylation.

The authors analyzed RNA-seq data from the Knight ADRC, MSBB, and ROSMAP cohorts, focusing on a synaptic plasticity dysfunction (SPD) subtype of AD associated with worse cognitive and neuropathological outcomes. Among 105 selected epilepsy-associated genes, 45 were dysregulated in Knight ADRC, 67 in MSBB, and 41 in ROSMAP. Sixteen epilepsy-associated genes were dysregulated across all three cohorts; 15 were consistently downregulated and one, CERS1, was upregulated. Several shared genes, including ARHGEF9, GABRA1, GABRB3, GABRG2, GRIN2A, HCN1, NECAP1, SCN1A, and SCN8A, were synaptic genes highly expressed in neurons.

Pathway analyses showed enrichment of epilepsy-related pathways in the SPD profile, including glutamatergic, dopaminergic, and GABAergic synapse pathways, as well as ion channel, synaptic transmission, and receptor complex pathways. Dysregulation of epilepsy-causing genes was observed in both early and late AD, with stronger effects in later stages. The study concludes that epilepsy-causing genes and shared synaptic, neurotransmission, and ion channel pathways may contribute to the overlap between epilepsy and AD progression, though the order in which the conditions arise remains unclear.

The Tax Court considered whether noncharitable gifts made by checks delivered in December 1980 but paid in January 1981 were complete upon delivery for federal gift and estate tax purposes. Petitioner argued that payment related back to delivery, making the gifts complete in 1980 and eligible for annual exclusions. Respondent argued the gifts were incomplete until payment because the decedent retained control, including the ability to stop payment.

The court declined to extend the relation back doctrine to these facts, noting petitioner failed to prove unconditional delivery of the checks. Applying Oklahoma law, the court concluded that delivery of a donor’s personal check does not itself assign bank funds and that the donor retains dominion and control until the drawee bank pays or accepts the check. The court held the gifts were completed in 1981 when the checks were paid.

The speaker announces his farewell after half a century of public service and wishes the incoming President peace and prosperity. He expresses gratitude for cooperation between the Presidency and Congress, saying they often worked together for the national good.

He reflects that, despite major wars, America has become the world’s strongest and most productive nation, but its leadership depends on using power for peace and human betterment. He identifies America’s purposes as preserving peace, advancing human achievement, and promoting liberty, dignity, and integrity. He warns that a hostile global ideology requires a prolonged, steady struggle and urges balance in national programs, costs, duties, and future welfare.

He emphasizes the need for a strong, ready military but warns that the new combination of a vast defense establishment and arms industry—the military-industrial complex—could gain unwarranted influence and threaten liberty and democratic processes. He also warns that government-funded scientific research could dominate scholars, while public policy could become captive to a scientific-technological elite.

He urges Americans not to consume the resources of future generations and says democracy must endure. He calls for mutual trust among nations, disarmament with honor and confidence, and the resolution of differences through intellect and decent purpose rather than arms. Though disappointed that lasting peace is not yet in sight, he notes that war has been avoided and progress made. He closes by thanking citizens, urging strength, humility, devotion to principle, and praying for freedom, opportunity, charity, the end of poverty, disease, and ignorance, and peace based on mutual respect and love.

WIRED highlights discounted toys during Amazon Prime Day, including Squishmallows plushes, Magna-Tiles, a retired Lego dried flower centerpiece, Play-Doh, Halloween Lego, blind boxes, Melissa & Doug’s ice cream counter, Crayola’s Color Wonder station, and a National Geographic rock tumbler kit. The article frames the deals as options for children, gifts, holiday shopping, or adults buying for themselves.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture introduces performance and feature improvements for gaming, professional visualization, and data center workloads. Third-generation Tensor Cores support fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity, reducing weight storage and bandwidth while increasing sparse math throughput with minimal reported inference accuracy loss after pruning and fine-tuning. DLSS uses Tensor Cores to reconstruct high-quality images from multiple frames and, on Ampere, enables 8K gaming at 60 fps in many titles with the GeForce RTX 3090.

GA10x GPUs use GDDR6X memory developed with Micron, using PAM4 signaling and MTA encoding to deliver up to 19.5 Gbps data rates and 936 GB/sec peak bandwidth. NVIDIA RTX IO, used with Microsoft DirectStorage, enables GPU-based loading and decompression of game assets, reducing CPU workload and improving I/O performance.

The NVIDIA A40 targets data center visual computing with up to 2x FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 5x AI throughput versus Quadro RTX 6000, with 48GB memory expandable to 96GB via NVLink. Ampere GPUs support DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 8K displays, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-generation NVENC encoding. The RTX A6000 provides 48GB GDDR6, professional ray tracing, AI denoising, and NVLink memory expansion. The GeForce RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 24GB GDDR6X, while the RTX 3070 uses GA104 with GDDR6. GDDR6X Error Detection and Replay helps identify memory overclocking limits by retrying failed transmissions and causing performance to plateau before crashes.

The study developed and implemented a teacher education course integrating collaborative inquiry with panoramic cameras to improve teacher education students’ ability to diagnose young students’ learning problems and design instructional activities. The course included preparation, teaching practice, classroom observation, video-supported evidence collection, and post-lesson discussion across four cycles. Twenty-two teacher education students participated in five groups paired with junior high classrooms. Observation reports and questionnaires measured diagnostic ability and perceived instructional design capability. Results showed improvement in diagnostic scores across cycles and statistically significant gains in perceived abilities related to lesson preparation, linking student learning with teaching practice, and adjusting lesson plans. The study concludes that the course framework is feasible for teacher education, though further work is needed to assess the effectiveness of instructional strategies proposed after diagnosing student learning issues.

The passage presents a finite element model for methane gas bubble growth in shallow muddy aquatic sediments. Methane bubbles form from microbial decomposition, grow beyond pore scale by deforming sediment, and are treated as Mode I gas-filled cracks governed by Linear Elastic Fracture Mechanics (LEFM). The model couples dissolved methane diffusion, gas accumulation, sediment elasticity, and fracture propagation. Bubble pressure is calculated from methane concentration using Henry’s law and the ideal gas law, while fracture growth occurs when the stress intensity factor exceeds sediment fracture toughness. Crack increments vary along the bubble front, with maximum growth at the bubble head.

The model is implemented in COMSOL Multiphysics using coupled solute transport and force equilibrium equations, adaptive meshing, and symmetry conditions. Simulations begin with a 4 mm penny-shaped seed bubble and continue until a mature inverted tear-drop bubble with a closed tail forms. Input parameters are based on Eckernförde Bay sediment conditions. Validation against analytical solutions for mature bubble height and crack opening displacement shows good agreement across different fracture toughness values. The model applies to individual bubbles and is intended as a basis for future upscaling to predict gassy mud properties, sediment destabilization, geohazards, acoustic behavior, and methane flux uncertainty.

This preprint study investigated genetic and inflammatory biomarkers associated with symptomatic and aggressive cerebral cavernous malformation (CCM). In a single-site prospective observational cohort, 103 CCM patients were enrolled, including 44 with multifocal/familial CCM and 70 with symptomatic disease; 48 had symptomatic hemorrhage and 22 had seizures without MRI evidence of bleeding. Blood samples were analyzed for selected SNPs in PTPN2, VDR, and FCGR2A genes and for plasma cytokines.

PTPN2rs72872125 CT and VDRrs7975232 CC genotypes were more frequent in asymptomatic patients after adjustment. PTPN2rs72872125 CT was associated with higher IL-10 and lower IL-18 and IFN-γ levels, while VDRrs7975232 C allele carriers had lower IL-27 and IL-23 levels. A diagnostic biomarker combining PTPN2rs72872125 CC genotype and GM-CSF plasma levels showed association with symptomatic phenotype, with 85.7% specificity and 41.3% sensitivity, and performed better in familial CCM and infratentorial lesions.

Among 42 patients followed for 4 years, four developed symptomatic events. FCGR2Ars1801274 GG genotype was independently associated with symptomatic events during follow-up and showed high predictive accuracy in subgroup analyses. In silico analysis indicated this SNP substitutes histidine with arginine at position 131. VDRrs731236 AA was associated with later symptom presentation, while VDRrs11568820 CC was associated with earlier symptoms.

The authors conclude that PTPN2, VDR, and FCGR2A variants, along with inflammatory markers, may help characterize diagnostic and prognostic profiles in CCM and suggest a possible inflammatory contribution to aggressive CCM behavior.

Amazon received a patent for “directed fragmentation” of delivery drones, allowing a malfunctioning UAV to release components in a controlled sequence rather than fall intact. The system would update based on flight path, weather, malfunctions, and terrain data to direct parts toward safer locations such as water, forests, or open fields, while avoiding buildings, roads, schools, and other developed areas. Causes could include severe weather, battery failure, rotor issues, or sensor and computer malfunctions. Components could be released using latches, springs, compressed gas, or small explosive charges, with the sequence considering cost, weight, drag, and function. The patent does not guarantee use but shows Amazon is considering catastrophic drone failure risks.

Social media platforms are strengthening moderation policies, staffing, and algorithms in response to criticism over harmful content. A.I. can identify offensive language, certain images, slurs, extremist terms, nudity, and symbols, but it struggles with context, evolving language, and intent. Examples include Google Photos mislabeling dark-skinned people, Twitter mistakenly limiting searches for LGBT-related terms, and Facebook removing posts or images because algorithms misread swastikas, nudity, or historic content.

The passage emphasizes that A.I. can be biased because it is trained on human-labeled data, and those biases can spread when datasets are shared. A.I. is useful as an initial screening tool that helps prioritize content for human review, such as Facebook’s use of A.I. to detect suicidal tendencies. However, human moderators remain necessary, and Facebook planned to expand its review team to 20,000. Experts cited argue that A.I. improves efficiency but is not close to fully automated moderation, while ethical considerations lag behind the pace of technological development.

Connecticut municipal lobbyists asked Gov. Dannel P. Malloy for relief from costly state mandates and administrative burdens amid the state budget stalemate and deficit. COST and CCM seek changes to municipal retirement rules, collective bargaining arbitration, prevailing wage thresholds, service-sharing barriers, and retention of more land-transfer fees. Malloy called the meeting productive and said easing regulations could help towns and cities deliver services with fewer resources. CCM’s Joe DeLong said municipalities are not asking to be held harmless from aid cuts, but Senate President Martin Looney disputed that claim. Betsy Gara said small towns need tools to reduce costs, including mandate relief and making municipal pension contributions subject to collective bargaining.

The President reports that the United States is stable, at peace with other nations, and committed to neutrality amid foreign conflicts. Relations with Great Britain are friendly, diplomatic issues with France have ended, and neutrality was enforced regarding a German war steamer and a planned expedition against Cuba. He recalls the minister to Frankfort because no German Empire has been definitively formed, notes sympathy but no intervention in Hungary, and says unresolved claims against Portugal will be addressed separately.

Relations with Mexico are described as friendly under the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, though additional funds are needed for boundary surveys and claims work. Issues involving New Granada mail transit, Venezuelan grievances, Brazil claims, Central American treaties, and Pacific relations are discussed. He urges stronger laws against abuse of the U.S. flag in the African slave trade and supports protected interoceanic transit routes through Nicaragua, Tehuantepec, and Panama without monopoly by any great power. He also expresses interest in the independence of the Sandwich Islands.

Treasury receipts and expenditures are reported, along with projected deficits caused by the Mexican War and treaty. He recommends borrowing authority, strict economy, tariff revision to increase revenue and encourage domestic industry, and possible modification of the subtreasury system. He also recommends creating an agricultural bureau.

For California and New Mexico, he recommends favorable consideration if they seek admission as states with republican constitutions, while urging avoidance of sectional controversy. He discusses customs collection in California, coastal surveys, Indian agencies, a California branch mint, land-title commissions, surveyor-general offices, mineral surveys, and liberal land policies. He recommends studying possible railroad routes from the Atlantic or Gulf to the Pacific.

He calls for continued river and harbor improvements, an increased Army presence on the western frontier, reforms concerning rank, retirement, and care for disabled soldiers, and Navy reorganization with a retired list. He also asks for improved postal laws for California and Oregon, a possible reduction of single-letter postage to 5 cents, and notes implementation of a postal treaty with Great Britain.

Congress is urged to enact legislation for the Seventh Census and to attend to the District of Columbia. The President closes by emphasizing constitutional limits on executive power, restraint in using the veto, independence among the branches of government, respect for the Union, and his commitment to preserving it.

SanDisk warranty service requires contacting SanDisk, returning the product in tamper-resistant packaging with prepaid freight, and obtaining tracking confirmation. SanDisk may repair, replace, or refund the product, but is not responsible for lost data and limits liability to the purchase amount. Products are not warranted to operate without failure or for life-support use.

The software license applies upon downloading, installing, or using the software; otherwise, users must not proceed and may need to return the hardware/software package for a refund. SanDisk grants a limited personal-use license with a SanDisk product on one device. Users may not modify, reverse engineer, distribute components, or disclose proprietary information. The software is provided “as is,” with no warranties, and SanDisk limits liability for damages. Transfers are allowed only with the SanDisk product and agreement. The agreement may terminate upon breach, and the software is not intended for high-risk activities. The agreement is governed by California and U.S. federal law.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2018. The company designs, develops, manufactures and sells fully electric vehicles, solar energy generation products and energy storage products, and reports two segments: automotive and energy generation and storage.

As of September 30, 2018, Tesla had total assets of $29.26 billion, total liabilities of $23.41 billion, and total stockholders’ equity of $4.51 billion. Cash and cash equivalents were $2.97 billion, compared with $3.37 billion at December 31, 2017. Inventory was $3.31 billion, up from $2.26 billion at year-end 2017.

For the three months ended September 30, 2018, total revenue was $6.82 billion, up from $2.98 billion in the prior-year period. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $311.5 million, compared with a net loss of $619.4 million a year earlier. Basic earnings per share were $1.82 and diluted earnings per share were $1.75.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2018, revenue was $14.24 billion, up from $8.47 billion in the prior-year period. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $1.12 billion, compared with $1.29 billion in 2017. Tesla adopted the new revenue recognition standard ASC 606 on January 1, 2018, resulting in a $623.2 million decrease to beginning accumulated deficit. This study evaluated COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) in patients with hematological malignancies and COVID-19 in France. A cohort of 112 patients received CCP through a monitored access program between May 2020 and April 2021; 83 had B-lymphoid neoplasms, 10 myeloid neoplasms, and 19 multiple myeloma. Most patients had prior anti-CD20 or anti-CD19 therapy and negative SARS-CoV-2 serology at transfusion. CCP was generally well tolerated, with few reported adverse events.

After CCP transfusion, temperature and inflammatory markers decreased, while PCR cycle threshold values increased by day 7. The 90-day overall survival was 64.9% overall, 77.5% in patients with B-lymphoid neoplasm, 20% in myeloid neoplasm, and 36.8% in plasma-cell neoplasm. In multivariable analysis, age over 70, high blood pressure, and severe COVID-19 were associated with lower survival, while prior anti-CD20/CD19 therapy was associated with better survival among CCP-treated patients.

A propensity score analysis compared CCP-treated patients with B-cell neoplasms to similar untreated patients. In the main analysis of anti-CD20 pre-exposed patients alive 16 days after hospitalization, CCP exposure was associated with a 63% reduction in risk of death. Sensitivity analyses showed risk reductions ranging from 40% to 63%.

The authors conclude that CCP may be beneficial for COVID-19 patients with hematological malignancies, especially those with B-cell lymphoid malignancies previously treated with anti-CD20 antibodies, but state that confirmation in randomized prospective trials is needed.

The passage describes a continuation patent application for methods and systems for digitally planning orthodontic treatment and manufacturing orthodontic appliances. The disclosed method measures a patient’s tooth positions, receives tooth movement constraints, diagnoses malocclusion elements, generates multiple treatment plans, computes interim and final tooth positions, selects a treatment plan, creates appliance models for treatment stages, and outputs fabrication instructions. Appliances may then be fabricated for one or more stages.

The system can branch treatment plans based on malocclusion findings and treatment options, including whether to treat or maintain openbite, molar relationship problems, posterior crossbite, canine relationship problems, overjet, bi-protrusion, and anterior issues. Branches may include options such as bicuspid extraction, lower incisor extraction, interproximal reduction, correction of upper anterior spaces, or maintaining existing conditions. Plans may be discarded if interim final positions are clinically unacceptable, and selected plans may be presented to a dental professional.

The orthodontic appliances include tooth-repositioning aligners with tooth-receiving cavities, which may fit all or some teeth and may reposition teeth incrementally through a series of appliances. Appliances may include or work with auxiliary components such as elastics, wires, springs, expanders, bite ramps, hooks, brackets, and other features. Treatment may include overcorrection to address relapse, speed movement, or compensate for inaccuracies.

Appliances may be fabricated directly using additive or subtractive manufacturing methods, including stereolithography, selective laser sintering, fused deposition modeling, material jetting, continuous direct fabrication, or multi-material fabrication. They may also be fabricated indirectly by thermoforming over positive or negative molds, or by combining direct and indirect methods. Materials may vary by appliance region to provide different stiffness, elasticity, thickness, or force delivery.

The passage also describes computer-based treatment planning, including scanning or otherwise measuring teeth and oral tissues, generating digital models, determining movement paths, calculating force systems, designing appliance geometry and material composition, and producing fabrication instructions. A data processing system with processors, storage, user interfaces, scanners, network interfaces, and fabrication systems may carry out these functions locally or remotely.

Diana Containerships reported a quarterly loss of $0.66 per share, beating the consensus estimate of a $0.77 loss, while revenue of $5.40 million missed the $7.50 million estimate and fell 63.8% year over year. The company had negative return on equity and net margin, opened at $2.71, and had a $24.82 million market cap. Renaissance Technologies increased its stake by 94.4% to 231,485 shares, and Zacks upgraded the stock from “sell” to “hold.”

Apple Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on September 12, 2017 it completed the sale of $5 billion in senior unsecured notes: $1 billion of 1.500% notes due 2019, $1 billion of 2.100% notes due 2022, $2 billion of 2.900% notes due 2027, and $1 billion of 3.750% notes due 2047. The passage lists errata for AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3, including issues with PMC sleep clock control, GLIU errors, UART access during DMA, LPC/DMA failures, I/O hangs, PIC behavior, UDMA/IDE problems, ACPI access hangs, USB clock gating, SMB and GPIO issues, and wake/suspend problems. Detailed items describe PIT deviations from standard latch/read-back behavior and mode 3 count loading, a GLIU debug port that hangs and should not be used, XPIC auto-end-of-interrupt behavior that can send duplicate interrupts, DMA rotating priority that may not rotate correctly, thermal alarm recovery limitations in standby, and PMC sleep-clock option dependencies. Suggested resolutions include avoiding certain programming sequences, not using the debug port, avoiding reliance on affected PIT behavior, and enabling Sleep Clock in PMC registers when related options are used.

Roanoke’s Bittle tree, planted by first President Dr. David Bittle, stood for over 100 years before being removed after storm damage made it hazardous. Its wood was used to create the Bittle Tree of Life Cross for Antrim Chapel during Roanoke’s 175th anniversary year. Reverend Chris Bowen and George Arthur designed the cross to symbolize the College’s roots and future.

May Baxter-Thornton from Newport and Emma Lewis from Swansea have been appointed to the victims and survivors panel of the Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse. Both are survivors of child sexual abuse and will advise on reaching and listening to Welsh victims. Inquiry chair Professor Alexis Jay said their Welsh perspective is vital. The inquiry has operated in Wales since November 2016, meeting victims, survivors and experts across several locations.

The passage is an Enron news digest from March 27–28, 2001. It includes reports that Viacom dropped plans to split off Blockbuster after improved performance, while noting Blockbuster’s video-on-demand effort with Enron had ended. President Bush nominated Patrick Wood and Nora Brownell to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, with Wood described as supportive of markets but open to measures ensuring they function properly.

Several articles focus on Enron: Chairman Kenneth Lay received a $7 million bonus for 2000, up from $3.9 million, plus restricted stock and options. Enron’s Japanese venture submitted plans for a large LNG-fired power plant in Aomori, targeting construction in 2004 and operation in 2007. Enron also held a stake in the Dolphin gas project supplying Qatar gas to the UAE, exited bidding for India’s Vijayanagar power project, and sought approval to form an Indian wind-power subsidiary.

Other items cover California electricity rate hikes, Texas electricity deregulation, Enron CEO Jeffrey Skilling’s comments supporting the Texas market design and California rate increases, and his forecast of Enron 2001 revenue of $160 billion to $170 billion. The digest also notes UK electricity trading reforms and U.S. companies, including Enron, urging expanded export financing through private lenders.
The Louisiana Supreme Court granted review and ordered the Court of Appeal to send the case record.

Steve Yzerman said Tampa Bay did not set a timeline for its rebuild, focusing instead on drafting well, using free agency selectively, retaining picks, and allowing young players to develop. He emphasized that sustained success depends on homegrown talent, especially under the salary cap, and credited the scouting and development staffs for identifying and nurturing players such as Nikita Kucherov, Ondrej Palat, and Tyler Johnson, while noting the team was fortunate to already have Steven Stamkos and Victor Hedman.

Yzerman praised staff members for their roles in player development and said building a strong program is essential to attracting players, along with opportunity, competitiveness, and organizational standards. He cited Anton Stralman as a player who fit a major roster need.

Coach Jon Cooper said the team’s resilience grew through past adversity, including Stamkos’ injury, a first-round sweep, and difficult playoff series. He described the players as repeatedly responding to pressure and credited their character, leadership, and belief. Cooper also discussed his history coaching many of the young players in the minors, saying their shared development helped their transition to the NHL.

Both Yzerman and Cooper highlighted Stamkos’ growth as captain, describing him as a leader who accepts different roles, supports teammates, and prioritizes winning. They also discussed the skill and impact of players like Johnson, Kucherov, and Palat, and Yzerman said his current role during the playoffs is mainly to support the team.

Electric Resistance Welding (ERW) is used for transporting vapor and liquids such as petroleum and gas under high and low pressure. ERW steel pipes use hot-rolled coils, have efficient low-cost production, and are widely used in industries including energy, electricity, automobiles, and light industry. Their weld quality, burr removal, wall thickness control, and end processing follow standards such as API or GB/T9711.1, and they are widely used in urban gas pipe networks.

The disclosure describes methods, systems, devices, and computer-readable media for identifying audio content using a playback device. A playback device receives digital data representing audio content, sends at least part of that data to an audio identification system, receives information associated with the content, sends that information to a control device, and plays the audio through connected speakers. The control device may command the playback device to retrieve the information, receive it, and display metadata or related information retrieved from a metadata curating device.

The disclosure also describes example media playback environments with playback devices, control devices, playback zones, zone groups, queues, audio sources, and controller interfaces. Playback devices may include processors, memory, audio processing components, amplifiers, speakers, microphones, and wired or wireless network interfaces. Control devices may manage playback, zones, queues, volume, and metadata display.

Additional examples include identifying content after detecting discontinuities in digital data, sending portions of data periodically, using decoded or sample-rate-converted data, selecting data from different points in an audio processing pipeline, and sending frequency-segregated portions of data to an identification system. The described implementations may be embodied in hardware, software, firmware, or combinations thereof.

Two letters express opinions on public issues. Beth Utton argues that Rep. Ken Buck’s view of health care as a commodity supports a profit-driven system that endangers lives, and advocates Medicare for all as a rights-based alternative. Bonnie New criticizes a Tribune headline about Denver paying nearly $1 million to the family of a teen killed by police, arguing it should have noted the teen was allegedly committing crimes and that police deserve respect and support.

A Deloitte study found consumer confidence in autonomous vehicles has increased, with 49% now believing self-driving cars will not be safe, down from 73% last year. Trust in brands developing the technology is a key factor, with 53% more confident because of the companies involved and 51% trusting traditional car manufacturers over technology companies. Respondents still largely prefer engine-powered vehicles, while concerns about electric cars include range, price and charging infrastructure. Customer service also remains important in car buying. The UK government is launching an inquiry into autonomous vehicle safety.

The passage explains the Presidential Election Cycle theory, which links U.S. presidential terms to stock market performance based on historical patterns. Yale Hirsch and the Stock Trader’s Almanac are credited with quantifying the effect, noting that pre-election years tend to be strongest, election years second best, and midterm years often weakest until the fourth quarter, when performance improves. The Almanac reports that since 1952 the S&P 500 averaged higher returns in election years with an incumbent running than in open-field elections.

The passage says election-related uncertainty can increase volatility, especially in sectors affected by policy, such as healthcare, energy, and trade-sensitive industries. Analysts cited note that congressional control and legislation can be as important as the presidency. The passage concludes that investors should monitor policy impacts, remain invested, and rebalance portfolios, while recognizing that election-cycle trends may offer context but do not always predict market performance.

New Jersey Governor Chris Christie signed legislation strengthening protections for people with developmental disabilities and giving families more involvement in care. Prompted by Stephen Komninos’s 2007 death in a group home, the law allows twice-yearly unannounced inspections, authorizes additional Department of Human Services staff, requires injury notifications to parents or guardians within two to eight hours, and mandates family meetings at least twice annually.

The disclosure concerns illumination systems for 2D, 3D, autostereoscopic, privacy, multi-user, and directional displays. It describes display devices using directional backlights with waveguides, arrays of light sources, spatial light modulators, polarisers, and retarders to direct light into viewing windows and reduce off-axis visibility.

Spatially multiplexed autostereoscopic displays can suffer from reduced spatial resolution, non-uniform viewing windows, flicker during lateral observer movement, image crosstalk, visual strain, and brightness or electronics compromises. Time multiplexed autostereoscopic displays can improve resolution by directing all pixels to different viewing windows in different time slots, enabling observer tracking with lower flicker and crosstalk.

The disclosed directional backlight may use a waveguide with opposed guide surfaces, an input end with multiple light sources, reflective ends, and light extraction features. Light may propagate through the guide, reflect, and be extracted through tilted or curved facets into optical windows whose output directions depend on the light source positions. The waveguide may image light sources laterally to form viewing windows. Curved extraction features or reflective ends may provide optical power; linear extraction features may simplify manufacture.

Privacy display embodiments include an input polariser, output polariser, at least one additional polariser, and one or more retarders placed between the additional polariser and a display polariser. Retarder options include crossed A-plates, C-plates, O-plates, correcting passive retarders, and switchable liquid crystal retarders. These arrangements may reduce luminance to off-axis viewers while maintaining luminance for a primary user. Switchable liquid crystal retarders may enable switching between privacy and wide-angle modes, with voltage control used to adjust attenuation regions and viewing profiles.

The disclosure also describes reflective polarisers, rear reflectors with corner facets, patterned addressing electrodes, camouflage privacy patterns, multiple switchable retarder layers, and control systems that synchronize light sources, spatial light modulators, and retarder voltages. Control systems may provide narrow or wide viewing windows, temporally multiplex primary and secondary images, obscure images for snoopers, or adjust privacy based on snooper location.

Applications include autostereoscopic displays, observer-tracked 2D and 3D displays, privacy displays, multi-user displays, power-saving displays, high-luminance displays, vehicle displays, projectors, optical systems, computer systems, visual systems, and audiovisual systems. Directional backlights can provide controlled illumination from substantially the entire output surface using independently modulated light sources at a waveguide input, enabling security viewing, electrical efficiency, time-sequential stereoscopic viewing, and low-cost operation.

The Browns reportedly have not ruled out selecting Oklahoma quarterback Baker Mayfield with the No. 1 pick in the NFL draft. General manager John Dorsey said Cleveland remains open to options, while coach Hue Jackson said Sam Darnold, Josh Allen, Mayfield and Josh Rosen are all still in play.

Intel’s Management Engine is a small, always-on subsystem in many Intel CPUs that connects to peripherals such as storage and network interfaces. Researchers Mark Ermolov and Maxim Goryachy presented a Black Hat Europe exploit allowing arbitrary code execution on Intel ME, though it requires physical access. The passage says ME runs Minix and has been difficult for researchers to assess because Intel kept it closed-source.

Mitigation options include firmware updates from System76, some Dell systems sold with ME disabled, Intel’s tool to detect ME, OEM-specific disabling methods, and the me_cleaner tool, which can stop ME from functioning while allowing the computer to run. There is no universal way to disable ME, and invalid ME firmware can cause shutdown after thirty minutes. The current exploit is described as limited, but the passage argues that a future network-based ME exploit would be far more serious and emphasizes the risks of unauditable closed code.

Jefferies raised Ferguson Plc’s price target from GBX 5,170 to GBX 5,240 and kept a hold rating. The passage examines Mortimer J. Adler’s perennialist philosophy in relation to Christian education, global education management, and posthumanist challenges. It presents Adler’s emphasis on enduring values, rational inquiry, docility, democracy, and holistic learner development, contrasting instant achievement with sustained intellectual and moral formation. The study uses a qualitative literature review based on Adler’s works and recent scholarship on philosophy, Christian education, posthumanism, and education management.

The discussion connects posthumanism with questions about human identity, technology, agency, ecology, and the limits of anthropocentrism. It also reviews studies on Christian family education, spirituality and illness, moral education across Christian schools, character education, disaster response, business ethics, and cross-cultural education management. The authors argue that education management should extend beyond administration to include reflection, justice, identity, ethics, resilience, and learner formation.

The conclusion states that Adler’s view of docility is not natural slavery but a reflective, intellectually grounded obedience involving conscience and skepticism. The passage argues that teachers, parents, and governments share responsibility for educational failure and should not scapegoat children. It concludes that education management should prioritize perennial values, deeper learner development, and sustained intellectual formation over instant achievement.

Nicola Sturgeon said Theresa May’s snap general election call was a major U-turn and political miscalculation aimed at exploiting Labour divisions, increasing a Conservative majority, forcing through a hard Brexit, and imposing deeper cuts. She argued the election would be about standing up for Scotland and rejecting the Conservatives’ agenda, while reinforcing the mandate for Scots to choose their future. The announcement comes amid disputes between May and the SNP over a second Scottish independence referendum, which the Scottish Government wants between autumn 2018 and spring 2019. Angus Robertson framed the election as a choice between the SNP and Tories in Scotland, while Ruth Davidson said Conservatives would campaign for strong Brexit leadership and against another referendum.

Lawyers for Venezuelan TPS holders asked the Supreme Court to leave in place Judge Edward Chen’s order temporarily blocking the Trump administration from ending their protected status. The TPS program allows eligible nationals to remain and work in the U.S. when conditions in their home country prevent return. Venezuela was designated in 2021, redesignated in 2023, and extended through October 2026 before DHS Secretary Kristi Noem ended the designation and extension. Challengers argue DHS lacked authority and acted partly from racial animus. Chen ruled Noem acted unlawfully, and the 9th Circuit declined to pause his decision. Solicitor General D. John Sauer asked the Supreme Court to intervene, arguing lower courts defied the Court’s earlier stay. Challengers responded that the prior stay concerned only preliminary relief and did not bar final judgment.

Ed Sachse, 56, president of property services for Kennedy Wilson, oversees brokers and 21 million square feet of properties nationwide. He began working in real estate-related services as a teenager in Detroit, buying a window-washing business with a friend. After studying accounting at Michigan State and working for Arthur Andersen, he moved to Los Angeles, joined Douglas Emmett, and later became a broker at Coldwell Banker. His first major sale was an empty school purchased by the Simon Wiesenthal Center. Sachse started his own property management and brokerage company in 1993 after improving a client’s struggling strip mall. He continued running the business while battling stage 4 non-Hodgkin lymphoma for six years. During the Great Recession, he sought new business from contacts, including Kennedy Wilson, which ultimately acquired his company in 2009. He now lives in Pacific Palisades with his wife, Julie, and has two grown children.

President Rutherford B. Hayes proclaimed that domestic violence and obstruction of laws existed in West Virginia along the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad. He warned citizens not to aid unlawful actions and ordered those involved to disperse peacefully by noon on July 19, 1877.

The passage describes MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 device subsystems, peripherals, documentation, application guidance, revision history, and packaging information. The CPU subsystem includes an Arm Cortex-M0+ up to 32MHz, instruction pre-fetch/cache, SysTick, and NVIC with four priority levels. The devices support RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN power modes, using PD1 for CPU, memories, and high-performance peripherals and PD0 for low-speed, low-power peripherals.

The PMU provides regulated core supplies, VDD supervision, BOR monitoring, and trim protection. The clock module supplies internal and external oscillators and distributes clocks including MCLK, CPUCLK, ULPCLK, MFCLK, LFCLK, ADCCLK, CLK_OUT, HFCLK, and HSCLK. The event manager routes peripheral events to the CPU, DMA, or other peripherals.

Memory features include flash with 1KB sectors and up to 100,000 program/erase cycles on selected sectors, plus SRAM retained in RUN, SLEEP, STOP, and STANDBY but lost in SHUTDOWN. GPIO supports up to 45 pins, wake features, filtering, and bit set/clear/toggle. IOMUX configures IO pads, pin muxing, and digital data flow. Security features include firewalls and CRC-16; the CRC module supports CRC16-CCITT and bit reversal.

Debug support is provided through a two-wire Arm SWD interface and DEBUGSS, including configurable peripheral debug behavior, mailbox communication, SWD lockout, and password authenticated debugging. Factory constants provide device capability and trim data. Application guidance recommends VDD decoupling capacitors, NRST pullup and pulldown capacitor, crystal bypass capacitors where applicable, and pullups for 5V-tolerant open-drain IOs. The passage also lists TI development resources, documentation support, trademarks, ESD caution, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and orderable information.
