The passage describes an invention for improving optical waveguide displays by increasing field of view and reducing wavelength-dependent limitations in total internal reflection. Prior waveguide displays using Bragg gratings can lose red or blue light at field-of-view extremes because different wavelengths diffract at different angles, causing some light to escape rather than propagate by total internal reflection.

The invention coats external waveguide surfaces involved in internal reflection with a material, preferably a meta-material, having a refractive index substantially equal to or less than 1.0 at optical wavelengths. This lowers the critical angle for total internal reflection, allowing light from wider input angles or different wavelengths to remain guided in the waveguide and later be output for viewing.

The apparatus includes an input diffractive part, such as a Bragg grating, to inject display light into the waveguide, and an output diffractive part to release guided light. The diffractive parts may be conjugated to reduce geometric distortion and chromatic dispersion. The coating may also protect exposed waveguide and grating surfaces from damage or contamination.

The meta-material may use periodic fish-net or mesh nanophotonic unit cells, including conductive meshes and magnetic resonators, with structural parameters selected to produce refractive index values between 0 and 1. Multi-layer slab waveguides may use such coatings between layers to support multi-colour displays, protect surfaces, prevent contamination, and enhance total internal reflection.

Sheffield Lord Mayor Magid Magid declared Donald Trump a “wasteman” and said he was banned from the city ahead of Trump’s July 13 visit. Magid posted a photo wearing a sombrero in solidarity with Mexico and declared July 13 “Mexico Solidarity Day.” He said the move was intended to send a message and show support for Sheffield’s Mexican community. Magid, Sheffield’s youngest Lord Mayor and its first from the Green Party, criticized Trump over the Muslim ban, withdrawal from the Paris climate agreement, moving the US embassy to Jerusalem, child detention at borders, and defending white supremacists. He also criticized Theresa May for not banning Trump from the UK.

The author developed sepsis after scratching a hand on a nail and survived after a three-month coma and year-long recovery. Sepsis affects over 30 million people worldwide annually, killing about 6 million, including nearly 2 million children; 40% of survivors develop post-sepsis syndrome. It begins with an infection but becomes dangerous when the body’s immune response spirals out of control, causing organ failure. Symptoms can include mottled skin, severe breathlessness, shivering or muscle pain, no urination, nausea, or vomiting, requiring immediate emergency help. There is no specific cure, though antibiotics may treat the original infection and research into metformin and gene therapy is promising. Awareness remains low globally, and improved public and medical recognition, including use of protocols such as Sepsis6, is presented as the strongest current defence.

The passage presents a face anonymization system for intelligent scientific experiment education, where videos must protect student privacy while preserving visibility of instruments and operational techniques. Existing methods such as blurring, pixelation, clustering, and GAN-based anonymization are not well suited to experimental scenes because instruments, hands, transparent objects, and fine structures may occlude faces and must remain visible for assessment.

The proposed system uses an enhanced YOLOv8 model, MSFF-YOLOv8, for face detection and segmentation, BOTSort for tracking, and Gaussian blurring for anonymization. It distinguishes primary and non-primary operators, applying detailed segmentation to the primary operator and bounding-box blurring to others. The method includes Contour-Adaptive Occlusion Refinement (CAOR), a training-data preprocessing technique that dilates occlusion boundaries toward the face to reduce misblurring of instruments and hands. Two evaluation metrics are introduced: SOBA for blur accuracy and OBR for over-blurring of occluded objects.

The authors created a dataset from 51 scientific experiment videos, including face detection, segmentation, instrument, and tracking annotations. Experiments compared YOLOv8, MSFF-YOLOv8, SAM, and Edge-SAM. MSFF-YOLOv8 with CAOR achieved the best results, reaching 96.02% accuracy, 22.67 fps on 1080p video, and low over-blurring rates. The system maintained face anonymization while preserving important experimental details, though further work is needed for more precise real-time edge classification.

The lecture reviews renewal theory as preparation for countable-state Markov chains. It contrasts the strong law for renewals, the elementary renewal theorem, and Blackwell’s theorem, emphasizing that expected values alone may not describe sample-path behavior. For arithmetic renewal processes with span λ, Blackwell’s theorem implies that the probability of a renewal at a large time approaches λ divided by the mean inter-renewal time.

The lecture then analyzes age and duration at a fixed time for an arithmetic renewal process. It derives the joint probability of age and duration using the probability of an arrival at a prior time and the inter-renewal interval distribution. As time grows, Blackwell’s theorem makes this joint distribution depend only on the duration, not the age. The limiting duration distribution is proportional to k times the inter-renewal probability mass function, giving expected duration equal to E[X²]/E[X]. The expected age differs by a factor related to observing only integer times versus averaging over continuous time.

The lecture next introduces countable-state Markov chains, where recurrence requires more care than in finite chains. A random walk model of a Bernoulli process illustrates that probabilities of individual states can go to zero, so steady-state probabilities may not exist. Birth-death chains are discussed: for p < 1/2 states remain near zero, for p > 1/2 the chain drifts away, and p = 1/2 is a special case with eventual return but no steady-state probability.

First passage probabilities are defined as the probability of reaching a state for the first time at a given step. Their cumulative limits determine whether a state is reached eventually. A state is recurrent if return to it occurs with probability 1; then return times form a renewal process. Recurrent states may be positive recurrent if expected return time is finite, or null recurrent if it is infinite. States in the same communicating class are either all recurrent or all transient.

La-Z-Boy is presented as more favorable than Stanley Furniture, beating it on 12 of 14 compared factors. Analysts rate La-Z-Boy with a $30.33 consensus target price and 11.31% potential upside, while Stanley has no listed ratings. La-Z-Boy has higher institutional ownership, revenue, earnings, profitability, and pays a $0.44 annual dividend with a 1.6% yield. Stanley has higher insider ownership, a lower price-to-earnings ratio, and lower share-price volatility. Stanley markets residential wood furniture under brands including Stanley Furniture, Coastal Living, and Stone & Leigh, sourcing mainly from Vietnam. La-Z-Boy manufactures, distributes, and retails upholstery, accessories, and casegoods furniture through multiple segments, brands, and store networks.

Sam Altman said intellectual property rights holders react differently to AI-generated video than still images because video feels more real and emotionally resonant. Speaking with Ben Thompson, he said many rights holders are excited about OpenAI’s Sora but want more restrictions and granular control over character generation. Viral Sora videos have featured characters like SpongeBob and Pikachu, though some prompts are blocked by guardrails. Altman said OpenAI will adjust based on feedback and predicted companies may eventually seek more inclusion of their content in AI videos.

Scientists are making progress in understanding and potentially manipulating human memories. Research involving face cells, CREB, neuron activation, and memory reconsolidation suggests memories may be located, influenced, implanted, or altered. MIT researchers led by Dr. Susumu Tonegawa linked a harmless situation to fear, then later reversed a negative association into a positive one.

A trade deficit reduces domestic demand and can raise unemployment unless offset by budget deficits or asset bubbles. The passage argues that the dollar’s reserve currency role does not require large trade deficits, since other reserve-currency countries do not all run deficits. It says countries such as China and South Korea hold excess reserves to keep their currencies competitive. It also disputes criticism of China’s technology-transfer policies, arguing that U.S. companies chose to invest in China despite those conditions and were better positioned to protect their interests than typical workers.

The speaker says the team is unconcerned with outside perceptions and is excited to have earned a Stanley Cup opportunity after beating three strong teams. He praises Mike Peca as hockey’s best all-around player, emphasizing his value. He attributes the team’s success to a physical style and big forwards who skate well and forecheck hard. He says the long layoff allowed players to relax before refocusing in Dallas. He adds that recent playoff adversity has given the team enough experience and that they do not expect to be more nervous than in previous series.

The passage describes an RSI(2) mean-reversion trading strategy for QQQ/Nasdaq. It says the strategy buys when RSI(2) is below 10 and exits when the close is higher than the previous day’s high. From QQQ’s inception, it reportedly returned 10.01% versus 6.39% for buy and hold and performed well during several bear markets. Using RSI below 5 increased average gain but reduced total return. Adding a second indicator improved results, with a reported CAGR of about 12.7%, 14% market exposure, 232 trades, 75% winners, profit factor around 3, max drawdown of 19.5%, and Sharpe Ratio of 2.85.

SD Memory Cards are designed for secure, high-capacity, high-performance use in audio and video consumer devices, with content protection, mutual authentication, and optional standards-based security support. SDIO Cards extend SD cards with I/O functionality, optional memory, SD compatibility, low-power high-speed operation, and safe behavior in non-SDIO hosts. Communication uses a 9-pin interface up to 208 MHz.

JD Wetherspoon plans a new 1,600sq metre Dublin city centre gastropub using two Lower Abbey Street buildings, linked by glazed connections, after receiving a full drinks and restaurant licence subject to planning permission. The company operates several Irish pubs and plans another on Camden Street. Known for cheap food and drink, Wetherspoon’s has increased prices in recent years.
In HS mode, ADS7828 reads codes individually, stretches the clock until conversion completes, and remains in HS mode with repeated START instead of STOP.

An Alberta Education survey of nearly 10,000 people, about half teachers, found respondents want more practical skills and basics like reading, writing and math in the future K-12 curriculum. Feedback on social studies drew especially strong views, including debate over First Nations, Métis and Inuit content, civic literacy, global history, current events and concerns about promoting particular world views. Most respondents said the draft plans supported literacy, numeracy, critical thinking and student success. Alberta Teachers’ Association president Greg Jeffery said curriculum writers are on track but teacher preparation and pacing will be crucial. Education Minister David Eggen’s overhaul aims to have the K-4 curriculum written by December, with higher grades rolling out through 2022.

The BGF China Flexible Equity Fund provides access to both onshore China A-shares and offshore Chinese equities through one strategy. Managed by Helen Zhu and supported by China-focused analysts in Hong Kong and Shanghai, the long-only, fundamentals-driven fund invests in 20 to 50 companies from a broad universe. It uses flexible allocation across markets, sectors, factors and market capitalisations to capture valuation differences, market-cycle factors and sector opportunities in Chinese equities.

This ebook edition of Foreign Relations, 1981–1988, Volume I: Foundations of Foreign Policy was generated by the U.S. Department of State’s Office of the Historian in September 2022. The FRUS ebook program provides portable, searchable versions of the series while maintaining fidelity to printed editions and recommending citation by document number. The Foreign Relations series is the official documentary record of major U.S. foreign policy decisions and diplomatic activity. Its preparation is governed by standards first codified in 1925 and by Public Law 102–138, which requires thorough, accurate, reliable documentation, historical objectivity, transparency about deletions, and publication within 30 years. The statute also requires relevant U.S. Government entities to provide full access to pertinent records. Most sources for this volume have been declassified and are available at the National Archives.

The study examines Turkish tour guiding students’ perceptions and experiences of emergency distance education (EDE) during the Covid-19 pandemic. Using a qualitative phenomenological design, data were collected from 81 students in face-to-face tour guiding departments at Istanbul universities through semi-structured online questionnaires and analyzed with thematic content analysis.

Findings show that students generally considered EDE insufficient for tour guiding education because of inadequate vocational and practical training, limited communication, motivation problems, technical issues, and low course attendance. They viewed face-to-face education as more efficient for socialization, concentration, self-expression, interaction, and developing professional communication skills. However, students also identified advantages of EDE, including effective time management, access to recorded courses, location independence, cost savings, and easier access to materials.

Most students reported understanding distance courses, yet they still preferred face-to-face education, especially because tour guiding requires field practice, speaking skills, and interaction. The study concludes that students experienced a dilemma: they recognized the benefits of distance education but considered face-to-face education more appropriate for tour guiding. It suggests that hybrid approaches and stronger practical and communication-focused designs may better support tour guiding education.

The lecture covers auction theory, focusing on independent private values, revenue equivalence, reserve prices, common values, and an empirical study of oil lease auctions.

Auctions are important in government procurement, Treasury bill sales, online advertising, and spectrum allocation. In the independent private values model, bidders observe independent signals that determine only their own values, are risk neutral, and know only their own signals.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, each bidder submits a bid, the highest bidder wins, and pays the second-highest bid. Bidding one’s true value is a weakly dominant strategy, and with continuous distributions it is the unique symmetric equilibrium. Seller revenue equals the expected second-highest value. For uniform values, expected revenue is \((n-1)/(n+1)\).

An oral ascending auction can be modeled as a button auction, where bidders drop out when the price reaches their value. This yields the same outcome as a second-price auction. In practice, bidders may overbid in second-price sealed-bid auctions, and auctioneers may avoid them because they reveal the winner’s surplus and can create embarrassment when the top bid greatly exceeds the second bid.

In a first-price sealed-bid auction, the highest bidder wins and pays their own bid. Bidders shade bids below their values, trading off higher surplus if they win against a lower probability of winning. In symmetric equilibrium, bids can be derived using first-order conditions. For uniform values, the bid is \((n-1)/n\) times the value. The equilibrium bid equals the expected second-highest value conditional on having the highest value.

First- and second-price auctions yield the same expected seller revenue in the symmetric independent private values model. This is a case of the revenue equivalence theorem: any mechanism that allocates the object to the highest-value bidder and gives the lowest type zero surplus yields the same expected revenue and the same expected utility by type. The theorem can also solve other auctions, such as all-pay auctions, where all bidders pay their bids but only the highest bidder wins.

The lecture emphasizes limitations of revenue equivalence. It assumes risk neutrality, independent private values, and mechanisms that always allocate the good to the highest-value bidder. With risk-averse bidders, first-price auctions raise more revenue than second-price auctions. With positively correlated values, second-price auctions raise more expected revenue than first-price auctions.

Reserve prices address the limitation that revenue equivalence excludes nonallocation. In a second-price auction, the optimal reserve price is the monopoly price, regardless of the number of bidders. Reserve prices can increase revenue but reduce welfare when all bidders’ values are below the reserve. Entry costs and commitment problems can make reserve prices less attractive.

Common value auctions arise when bidders’ values depend on others’ signals. In pure common value settings, all bidders value the object equally but receive noisy signals. Winning reveals that one’s signal was relatively optimistic, creating the winner’s curse. Rational bidders account for this by shading bids based on expected value conditional on winning.

The lecture concludes with Hendricks and Porter’s study of U.S. offshore oil lease auctions. Wildcat tracts are riskier and less often productive, while drainage tracts near producing wells are more likely to contain oil and have higher average value. Despite this, drainage tracts attract fewer bidders and generate higher profits for winners. Hendricks and Porter explain this using asymmetric information: incumbents drilling nearby know more about the tract, so uninformed bidders fear the winner’s curse. Their model predicts bidding and profit patterns, including more frequent incumbent bidding, incumbent wins at least half the time, zero expected profits for uninformed bidders, positive incumbent profits, and incumbent bids increasing with true value and public signals. The data broadly support these predictions.

A data-driven culture can align organizations vertically through metrics tied to company goals and horizontally through common data models and transparent access that support collaboration. Digital leaders emphasize learning mindsets, transparent data access, clear metrics, and cultural alignment between leadership beliefs, company values, and employee behavior. Digital laggards often recognize the importance of data culture but struggle due to entrenched habits, skills gaps, and limited top-down focus. Changing mindsets and behaviors is described as a major challenge in digital transformation.

Technologically mature firms differ in their data culture by valuing learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement in daily practices. Organizations commonly fall into four patterns: data novices, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant. Each can build on strengths and target actions to develop a stronger data culture.

Brad Vis has been chosen as the Conservative candidate for Mission-Matsqui-Fraser Canyon in next year’s federal election after narrowly losing to Liberal Jati Sidhu in 2015. Conservative leader Andrew Scheer praised Vis, while riding officials said the party will conduct outreach across the large riding. Vis criticized Liberal spending and highlighted concerns of seniors and young families.

The speaker said they felt good and saw the puck well, but the opposing team played better, especially in the second period. They credited the Devils’ speed, intensity, experience, and strong goaltending, noting their own team did not play its game, use speed effectively, shoot enough, or create traffic. They described specific goals as good moves and said there was little they could do on one rebound. The speaker emphasized that the loss was one game, not due to time off, and that the next game is the biggest of the year. They said the team must learn from the adversity, match the opponent’s intensity, bounce back, and show up with no excuses.

The study examines the relationship between multilingualism and cultural awareness among Indonesian higher education students. Using an embedded mixed methods design, it surveyed 388 students from six Indonesian universities and used qualitative responses from 60 participants. Variables included multilingual competence, learning processes, psychological factors, social interaction, cultural knowledge, cultural practices, sociocultural context, and attitudes toward cultural learning.

Participants represented diverse ethnic and linguistic backgrounds. Indonesian was the dominant mother tongue, while Javanese, Bugis, and Makassarese were prominent regional languages. English was the most studied foreign language, followed by Korean, Arabic, Japanese, and German. Formal education was commonly used for Indonesian and foreign language learning, while local languages were often learned independently.

Results showed significant positive correlations among multilingual learning variables, among cultural awareness variables, and between multilingual learning and cultural awareness. Multilingual competence was strongly related to sociocultural context and cultural learning attitudes. The study identifies strategies such as inclusive content development, educator training, technology support, intercultural collaboration, community engagement, self-directed learning, and cultural integration. It concludes that integrating multilingual approaches with cultural awareness can support inclusive higher education and help students participate in diverse sociocultural and global contexts.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2015. The company is incorporated in Delaware, headquartered in Seattle, and its common stock trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under “AMZN.” As of January 20, 2016, it had 470,842,035 shares outstanding.

Amazon seeks to be “Earth’s most customer-centric company” and serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators. Beginning in 2015, it reported three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). Its consumer offerings include retail websites, mobile apps, electronic devices such as Kindle, Fire tablets, Fire TV, and Echo, and Amazon Prime. Seller programs allow third parties to sell through Amazon websites and fulfillment services. AWS provides compute, storage, database, and other services. Content offerings include Kindle Direct Publishing and other publishing programs.

Amazon described its markets as rapidly evolving and intensely competitive, with competitors across retail, media, search, e-commerce services, logistics, IT services, cloud infrastructure, and consumer electronics. Key competitive factors include selection, price, convenience, service quality, speed, and reliability.

For 2015, Amazon reported net sales of $107.0 billion, income from operations of $2.2 billion, net income of $596 million, diluted earnings per share of $1.25, and operating cash flow of $11.9 billion. Total assets were $65.4 billion and total long-term obligations were $18.2 billion at year-end. Net sales grew 20% from 2014, or 26% excluding foreign exchange effects. North America sales were $63.7 billion, International sales were $35.4 billion, and AWS sales were $7.9 billion.

Amazon identified major risks including intense competition, rapid expansion, international operations, fulfillment and data center execution, seasonality, acquisitions, foreign exchange exposure, loss of key personnel, data breaches, system interruptions, inventory risk, intellectual property claims, stock volatility, regulation, tax liabilities, supplier issues, government contracts, product liability, payments risks, and potential seller fraud.

As of December 31, 2015, Amazon employed approximately 230,800 full-time and part-time employees. It operated leased and owned office, fulfillment, data center, customer service, and other facilities primarily in North America, Europe, and Asia. The company has never declared or paid cash dividends on its common stock.

Suzanne Nimocks forwarded a McKinsey memorandum dated December 6, 2000, titled “Power sector restructuring: international activity, June–November 2000.” The update reports that global power privatization and restructuring continued, driven by rising demand, limited government funding, market liberalization, unbundling of state utilities, and increasing wholesale and retail competition.

In Europe, the EU Directive was spurring competition, with mergers, alliances, asset sales, trading offices, and online platforms shaping the market. Countries varied widely: the UK, NordPool countries, and others had advanced retail access, while France, Italy, Germany, Greece, and others were still addressing legislation, grid access, unbundling, regulation, or privatization.

In Central and Eastern Europe, privatization and restructuring were progressing, often linked to IMF pressure or EU accession goals. Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Romania, Slovakia, Turkey, Ukraine, Russia, and Moldova were pursuing varying degrees of unbundling, privatization, market opening, or regulatory reform.

In Asia-Pacific, economic recovery was reviving restructuring plans, though IPPs faced issues with PPAs, guarantees, and incumbent utilities. Australia, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, Malaysia, New Zealand, Thailand, Taiwan, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, the Philippines, China, and Vietnam were at different stages of deregulation, privatization, IPP development, or regulatory reform.

In Latin America, currency volatility, drought, hydro dependence, ownership limits, and political issues slowed some privatizations, though reforms and transmission opportunities continued. Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Venezuela, Peru, Nicaragua, Panama, and others were pursuing asset sales, market opening, regulation, or grid development with mixed progress.

In Africa and the Middle East, governments increasingly allowed foreign investment, mainly through IPPs, while some considered broader privatization. Regional transmission projects were notable, including links in West Africa, Southern Africa, and the Middle East. Countries such as Algeria, Ghana, Nigeria, South Africa, Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Tunisia, Morocco, and the UAE were pursuing reforms, IPPs, concessions, or restructuring.

Jeong-Suk Cha, 77, provides round-the-clock care for her 48-year-old son Alex, who has cerebral palsy and spinal cord damage, with help from family, a friend and personal support workers. Alex is on a long wait list for residential care at London’s Participation House, where 40 spaces exist and 60 to 90 people are waiting. Advocates describe such waits for severely physically disabled adults as potentially decades long.

A $100-million class-action lawsuit alleges Ontario denies services to developmentally disabled adults through inconsistent and unreasonable wait lists. The South West LHIN says it lacks complete data on referrals, client needs and wait lists for medically complex or developmentally delayed adults seeking residential care. Ontario’s ombudsman previously reported 9,700 people waiting for residential care provincewide.

Alex’s sister Jin Cha has intensified advocacy as their mother ages, saying long-term care with seniors is not appropriate for Alex. Alex wrote that he would rather die than go to long-term care and needs help.

This 2018 ebook edition of the 1917 FRUS Supplement 1 provides the full content of the printed volume with search and offline access, while preserving fidelity to the original. The preface explains that the documents mainly cover the period of U.S. neutrality in World War I, with some topics extending beyond April 6, 1917, including Latin America, China, Siam, and Liberia. It also describes editorial conventions for brackets, parentheses, corrections, omissions, garbled telegrams, and revised translations.

The paper proposes a methodology for a trusting agent in a digital business ecosystem to determine beforehand the probability that it will not achieve the full benefit of resources invested in an interaction with a probable trusted agent. Risk is treated as central to deciding whether to interact and is defined through the probability and consequences of failure. The methodology uses the trusted agent’s FailureLevel, representing the extent to which desired outcomes may not be achieved, assessed according to the interaction context and criteria.

The trusting agent analyzes FailureLevel across time slots in pre-interaction and post-interaction phases, using past interaction history or recommendations for pre-interaction slots and prediction for post-interaction slots. For post-interaction risk analysis, it determines the probability of occurrence of each failure level rather than a single crisp value.

The paper also defines an Amount Invested Curve, which represents the probability of a net amount of financial resources being at stake throughout a time slot, accounting for progressive or immediate investment. It then defines a Factual Amount Invested Curve by convolving the Amount Invested Curve with the trusted agent’s FailureLevel, showing the required probability of investment when possible failure is considered.

Finally, the Loss of Resource Benefit index is calculated from the Factual Amount Invested Curve at the end of the Amount Invested Curve. This index represents the probability that the trusting agent will not obtain the full benefit of its invested resources. The methodology is intended to help the trusting agent make a more informed choice among probable trusted agents.

The Shuffle offense is a motion-based basketball offense, originating with Bruce Drake at Oklahoma, that uses all five players in a rotating pattern to create high-percentage shots, reduce defensive help, and pull bigger defenders away from the basket. It is suited for teams lacking height and relies on passing, spacing, screening, receiving, rebounding, ball possession, and limited dribbling.

Its continuity includes reversal passes, rub cuts off post screens, flash cuts to the middle, weakside rebounding, and screens that restart action on the opposite side. The rub cut is central, with counters based on defensive reactions: cutting over or under screens, attacking switches, bumping back off double screens, or using the post popping out when help defenders show and recover.

Flash cut options involve the corner player rebounding, flashing to the middle, back cutting against denial, or continuing into a screening role. The offense also includes counters to defensive overplay, such as wing back cuts, dribble clears, point back doors, and post lobs against fronting or high-side denial.

GA10x Ampere GPUs feature PCIe 4.0, up to 64 GB/sec on x16 slots, improving CPU-GPU transfers and DMA workflows. GA102 contains seven GPCs, 42 TPCs, 84 SMs, twelve 32-bit memory controllers, and 6144 KB of L2 cache. Each GA10x SM includes 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation RT Core, texture units, register files, and 128 KB of configurable L1/shared memory.

GA10x moves ROPs into the GPC, increasing the full GA102 to 112 ROPs and improving raster operations. Its SM design doubles FP32 throughput versus Turing by enabling FP32 processing on both datapaths, while retaining concurrent FP32/INT32 execution. GA10x also increases L1 cache capacity and doubles shared memory bandwidth compared with Turing. Ampere GPUs are described as up to 1.9x more power efficient than Turing at the same performance level.

GA10x includes second-generation RT Cores that double ray/triangle intersection testing versus Turing and add hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur through an Interpolate Triangle Position unit. It also supports concurrent RT Core work with graphics or compute workloads. Third-generation Tensor Cores support additional data types including TF32 and BF16, add structured sparsity for up to 2x matrix throughput, and improve AI features such as DLSS.

The architecture introduces GDDR6X memory developed with Micron, using PAM4 signaling to reach up to 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/sec of bandwidth. NVIDIA RTX IO uses Microsoft DirectStorage to enable GPU-based loading and decompression, reducing CPU workload and improving asset streaming. GA10x also supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, HDCP, fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 hardware decode, and seventh-generation NVENC encoding.

The passage also describes NVIDIA A40 and RTX A6000 professional GPUs based on GA10x, targeting data center, workstation, rendering, AI, and visualization workloads. It lists GeForce RTX 3090 and RTX 3070 specifications and features, including RTX 3090’s 24 GB memory and RTX 3070’s GA104 GPU. An Error Detection and Replay feature for GDDR6X memory helps detect and replay failed memory transmissions during overclocking.

The Brunswick school board took the first step toward placing a 10-year, $4.67 million emergency levy renewal on the May ballot, with no tax increase. It also approved notes up to $10 million for a new middle school and other facility improvements, revised fiscal 2018 appropriations to reflect increased grant funds, and acknowledged several recent donations. The board recognized outgoing member Lisa Durichko for 12 years of service. An executive session was held with no action afterward. The organizational meeting is set for Jan. 8, with the regular meeting Jan. 22.
The speaker praises the arena’s atmosphere as an advantage for Philadelphia and describes their goalie as calm, resilient, and consistently important to the team’s success.

The AEGEAN study evaluated adherence to apixaban in subjects with atrial fibrillation using electronic monitoring, comparing standard of care with an additional educational program. A total of 1162 subjects were randomized for the 24-week analysis, and 524 were later assigned to Secondary SOC or Continued Additional Educational Program groups for assessment through 48 weeks. Baseline characteristics were comparable across groups.

Mean adherence at 24 weeks was 91.64% in Primary SOC and 91.88% in the Additional Educational Program group, with no significant difference. Adherence was also comparable at Weeks 4 and 12. From Weeks 24 to 48, adherence was 87.59% in Primary SOC, 87.51% in Secondary SOC, and 88.41% in Continued Additional Educational Program, with no significant differences. Persistence was also similar between groups at 24 and 48 weeks. Adherence declined significantly over time within groups.

Safety outcomes were similar across groups. Adverse events, serious adverse events, discontinuations, and bleeding events occurred at comparable rates. Overall, 24 deaths were reported, no pregnancies occurred, and laboratory review showed no clinically concerning hepatic or renal signal. The study concluded that adherence and persistence with apixaban were high through 24 weeks and sustained to 48 weeks, and the educational program did not provide additional benefit.

SD Memory Cards contain a User Area and a Protected Area, with total capacity classified as SDSC up to 2 GB, SDHC over 2 GB up to 32 GB, and SDXC over 32 GB up to 2 TB. Hosts supporting higher-capacity cards must also support lower-capacity cards. Speed Classes define minimum performance from unspecified Class 0 to Class 10 at 10 MB/s.

Communication is host-controlled using commands, responses, and block-based data transfers over SD, SPI, UHS-I, or UHS-II interfaces. Commands may be broadcast or addressed, and cards operate in card identification mode after reset and data transfer mode after RCA assignment. Initialization uses CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, and CMD3; SDHC/SDXC initialization requires CMD8 before ACMD41.

UHS-I supports modes up to 104 MB/s using 1.8V signaling in SD mode, while UHS-II adds a second-row interface with modes up to FD624 at 624 MB/s. Voltage switching, tuning, driver strength, bus width, and current limits are selected through defined command sequences.

The specification describes card registers, physical form factors, pad assignments, ROM card behavior, read/write/erase operations, discard and full user area logical erase, write protection methods, password-based lock/unlock, and Card Ownership Protection. It also defines Application Performance Classes, cache, self-maintenance, command queue features, low voltage initialization, and UHS-III as an enhanced UHS-II bus speed mode.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K reporting that on November 6, 2017, its wholly owned subsidiary NVIDIA Land Development exercised an option to terminate lease arrangements and purchase the company’s new Santa Clara campus property from Wachovia for approximately $350 million. Construction was substantially completed on October 31, 2017, and NVIDIA expected to complete the purchase in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2018. The filing also furnished NVIDIA’s November 9, 2017 press release and CFO commentary on third-quarter and first-nine-month fiscal 2018 results.

The speaker said he had many scoring chances in the finals and felt this was the right time to contribute. He stayed in Finland longer to gain professional experience before trying the NHL. He said the team should shoot more, maintain effort, and keep improving. He chose the Sharks because they showed interest and had strong leadership.

TDSAT passed an interim order giving Bharti Airtel and Idea Cellular temporary relief, barring penalties for non-compliance with Trai’s tariff reporting requirements until further orders, while allowing Trai to seek details of discounts or concessions used to retain customers. The tribunal stayed clauses on reporting requirements and significant market power after Trai issued Airtel a show-cause notice over unreported segmented tariffs. Trai’s February norms require operators to report new tariffs within seven working days, disclose retention offers, and treat discounts as new tariffs, with penalties for delays. Airtel and Idea challenged the order before TDSAT, while Vodafone approached the Madras high court. Operators object to rules on predatory pricing and significant market players.

Scientists from MIT and the University of Cambridge found that the Phoenix cluster’s central black hole may recycle hot gas into cold fuel for star formation. Jets of 10-million-degree gas from the black hole usually suppress star formation, but observations suggest they also create cold gas that falls back onto the galaxy and fuels starbursts. The Phoenix cluster, about 5.7 billion light years away and containing about 1,000 galaxies, has a central galaxy producing about 1,000 stars per year. Using ALMA data, researchers detected cold gas filaments extending 20,000 light years from the black hole. When compared with Chandra X-Ray Observatory maps, the cold gas aligned with bubbles of hot gas, offering insight into black holes’ influence on galaxy growth.

Patterns help distributed systems developers by providing a shared vocabulary for common concepts, reducing confusion and wasted discussion over different names for the same ideas. This enables faster knowledge sharing and focus on implementation. The sidecar container example shows how agreed terminology lets teams move directly to solving problems.

Five Gor Mahia players—Kenneth Muguna, Meddie Kagere, Musa Mohammed, Jacques Tuyisenge and George Odhiambo—were shortlisted for the 2017 Kenyan Premier League MVP award. Other MVP nominees include Massoud Juma, Patrick Matasi and Lawrence Juma. SJAK will hold its own awards on December 18 after KPL postponed its awards, with sponsorship including LG. The gala will feature eight categories: Golden Glove, Defender, Midfielder, Golden Boot, MVP, Young/New Player, Coach and the SJAK Award. Matasi leads the goalkeeper shortlist, while Musa Mohammed and Karim Nizigiyimana headline the defender nominees. Kariobangi Sharks, Nzoia Sugar and other clubs also have nominees across categories. Prize awards have not been announced.

This study examined whether placental biomarkers measured in early pregnancy are associated with retained placenta and/or postpartum hemorrhage requiring blood transfusion (RP/PPH), used as a proxy for greater postpartum blood loss, in the NuMoM2b dataset. The final sample included 2,192 nulliparous participants with singleton pregnancies and available first- and second-trimester biomarker data; 67 experienced RP/PPH.

Participants with RP/PPH did not differ demographically from those without RP/PPH, but were more likely to have preeclampsia, cesarean birth, and instrumental delivery. In the overall sample, second-trimester levels of sEng, β-hCG, INHA, PAPP-A, and sFlt-1 were significantly higher among participants who later experienced RP/PPH. First-trimester sFlt-1 and the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio were also higher in the RP/PPH group, while PlGF did not differ at either time point.

When stratified by preeclampsia, non-preeclamptic participants with RP/PPH had significantly higher second-trimester β-hCG, INHA, PAPP-A, and sFlt-1 than those without RP/PPH. Among preeclamptic participants, biomarker levels did not significantly differ by RP/PPH status. Changes from first to second trimester also varied by preeclampsia status: non-preeclamptic participants with RP/PPH had a greater increase in sFlt-1, while preeclamptic participants with RP/PPH had a greater increase in PAPP-A and decrease in sEng.

The authors conclude that biomarkers related to angiogenesis and placental function, particularly in the second trimester, warrant further study as potential predictors of postpartum hemorrhage risk. Limitations included the lack of direct blood-loss measurements or general PPH diagnosis, a small RP/PPH group, and overrepresentation of adverse pregnancy outcomes.

Retired Boynton Beach firefighter-paramedic Luis Garcia spent nearly $40,000 of his savings to buy 800 doses of Narcan, an opioid overdose-reversal drug, and distribute them for free. At a Stuart event hosted by the Treasure Coast Substance Awareness Coalition and Martin Health Systems, he trained residents and gave away about 50 doses. Garcia, who says he responded to about 3,000 overdoses during his career, now travels Florida training businesses, residents and law enforcement. He also carries Narcan himself and said he revived five of six overdose victims he assisted. Local agencies increasingly carry Narcan as opioid-related deaths have risen, while community organizers emphasized reducing stigma and spreading awareness.

National home prices rose 0.9% over the last quarter and 6.1% year over year, the highest annual growth since February 2015, despite a winter slowdown. Regional quarterly growth was 0.8% in the Midwest, 0.7% in the Northeast, and 1.0% in both the South and West. San Jose, CA, and Hartford, CT, each posted 0.3% quarterly price declines. Portland, OR, was the fastest-growing market, near 2% quarter over quarter, while 8 major metros grew at 1.5% or higher. Clear Capital reported that 16 of the top 50 metro housing markets have exceeded housing-bubble peak prices, with record-high major and micro markets representing about one-third of national housing stock. National annual price growth is projected to moderate to 2–3% in 2017.

The Steelers have won eight straight games, including a 39-38 win over the Ravens, but face the Patriots in Week 15 with possible AFC No. 1 seed implications. Shannon Sharpe said Tom Brady should be eager to face Pittsburgh’s defense, which has struggled recently and will be without injured linebacker Ryan Shazier.

London has seen a late surge in IPO activity after a weak start to 2025, raising hopes for a revival in its capital markets. Recent and potential listings include Beauty Tech Group, Princes Group, Shawbrook, and possibly Visma in 2026. Analysts say sustained momentum will depend on execution, investor demand, and post-listing performance.

Oversold stock markets or stocks are defined as having fallen significantly over a specified period, often measured with technical indicators such as the 3-day RSI. The passage argues that oversold markets tend to show short-term mean reversion, meaning prices often rebound after strong deviations, but this does not predict long-term returns.

A sample backtest buys the S&P 500 when the 3-day RSI is below 20 and sells when the close is higher than the previous day’s high. From 1985 to today, the strategy reportedly produced smooth returns, with an average gain of 0.64% per trade, a 75% win rate, about 7.6%–7.7% CAGR, 26% maximum drawdown, and a profit factor around 2.4–2.5. The passage notes the strategy worked less well before 1990 and that mean reversion may not persist indefinitely.

This study reviewed the first year of COVID-19 vaccination implementation in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), from April 2021 to March 2022, using secondary data from the Ministry of Health and WHO-African Region databases. The DRC launched its vaccination campaign in April 2021 after developing a deployment plan prioritizing healthcare workers, people with comorbidities, and adults aged 55 and older.

By the end of the first year, vaccination had started in 16 of 26 provinces. Coverage remained low: by March 2022, about 5.7% of the population had received at least one dose and 1.03% were fully vaccinated. Kasai Oriental recorded the highest full vaccination coverage, while Equateur, Tshuapa, and Kwilu had the lowest. Functional vaccination sites increased over time but were unevenly distributed, with Kinshasa consistently having the most sites.

Men were vaccinated more often than women in most provinces. Among high-risk groups, 8,302 healthcare workers and 46,495 older adults completed their primary series. Vaccinated people with comorbidities were most numerous in Haut-Katanga, Kasai Oriental, and Haut-Uele. The vaccines used included AstraZeneca, Johnson & Johnson/Janssen, Moderna, Pfizer, and Sinovac, with Janssen the most used and AstraZeneca the least requested.

Compared with neighboring Central African countries, the DRC had among the lowest vaccination indicators, including 2% of the population receiving at least one dose and 8% of received doses administered. Challenges included slow rollout, vaccine hesitancy linked to AstraZeneca safety concerns, competing public health emergencies, limited health workforce capacity, strikes, logistical barriers, vaccine expiry issues, and difficulty reaching priority groups.

The study concludes that the DRC made some progress during the first year of COVID-19 vaccination but faced major implementation challenges, underscoring the need for stronger health systems and improved strategies to increase vaccine uptake.

The passage discusses Robert S. Putnam’s role in popularizing the concept of social capital, especially through his work on Italian democracy and his book *Bowling Alone*. Putnam linked northern Italy’s stronger economic, social, and political performance to its history of civic engagement, contrasting it with southern Italy’s history of outside rule, mafia influence, secrecy, and corruption. His work helped spark academic and policy interest in social capital and made him a highly cited social scientist.

The passage identifies two major debates about social capital. One concerns its definition: Putnam emphasizes civic group participation, while others focus on generalized trust, which may improve economic performance by lowering transaction costs. A 1996 paper by Knack and Keefer found positive effects from generalized trust but not civic membership. The second debate distinguishes “bridging” social capital, which connects groups, from “bonding” social capital, which strengthens in-group ties against outsiders.

The passage also notes Putnam’s findings that ethnic diversity and fragmentation may not increase social capital, a conclusion the author says has been used by ethnocentrists and nationalists.

Tesla’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2019 reported total assets of $31.87 billion, total liabilities of $24.72 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $5.72 billion. Cash and cash equivalents were $4.95 billion, up from $3.69 billion at December 31, 2018. For Q2 2019, total revenue was $6.35 billion, gross profit was $921.0 million, loss from operations was $167.5 million, and net loss attributable to common stockholders was $408.3 million, or $2.31 per share.
