The speaker thanks Grand Forks Air Force Base for its national security work and support during recent flooding, then describes touring flood devastation and meeting with local, state, congressional, and federal officials. He says the federal government came to assess needs, offer support, and recognize the community’s courage and cooperation.

He announces FEMA will provide 100 percent of direct federal assistance for emergency work, expands disaster coverage to additional counties in Minnesota and South Dakota, and asks Congress for $200 million more in emergency funds, bringing requested disaster assistance for North Dakota, South Dakota, and Minnesota to $488 million. He acknowledges urgent needs such as housing, income, and sanitation, and says officials are working on short- and long-term solutions.

He urges residents to support one another emotionally in the difficult days ahead and says FEMA Director James Lee Witt will lead an interagency task force on long-term rebuilding. He praises local leaders, rescue workers, newspaper staff, volunteers, and residents offering housing, emphasizing the community’s resilience, shared values, and commitment to rebuilding stronger.

The First Circuit dismissed the government’s interlocutory appeal for lack of appellate jurisdiction. The government had sought review of district court orders denying a continuance and denying as moot a request to depose witness Anthony Spera abroad after immigration authorities deported him to Italy despite prior notice that he was important to the prosecution’s case against Philip Watson and Shane O’Hearn.

The court held that the Criminal Appeals Act, 18 U.S.C. § 3731, permits government appeals from pretrial orders suppressing or excluding evidence, but not from routine case-management orders such as the denial of a continuance. Although the denial could hinder or prevent the government from obtaining and using Spera’s testimony, the orders did not directly exclude evidence or rule on its admissibility. Their purpose was to prevent further delay in an already old case, particularly given possible Speedy Trial Act concerns and the government’s institutional responsibility for Spera’s deportation. Therefore, the orders fell outside § 3731, and the appeal was dismissed.

Micheal A. Gayed’s 2015 paper proposed using the lumber/gold ratio as a risk-on/risk-off indicator. Lumber is presented as a cyclical indicator tied to housing, construction, consumer spending, and economic turns, while gold is described as a diversifying store of value with low correlation to stocks, bonds, and macroeconomic variables. The strategy invests in stocks during “risk on” periods and long-term Treasuries during “risk off” periods. A modified backtest using WOOD as a lumber proxy and GLD for gold produced 11.4% annual returns since 2008 with an average gain of 2.2% per trade, but suffered a 35% drawdown during the 2022/23 bond market collapse. Replacing Treasuries with gold reduced performance to 8.7% annual returns.

VentureWire’s Nov. 28, 2000 issue reports venture funding, restructurings, acquisitions, product launches, executive moves, and VC fund news. Top stories include ReplayTV restructuring, cutting non-core staff, shifting to technology licensing, and replacing CEO Kim LeMasters with founder Anthony Wood; NetCom Technologies raising $75 million in Series A financing from Willis Stein & Partners; Access Point Telecommunications laying off about 35% of workers and refocusing as a switching reseller; and Rational Software acquiring Catapulse for $405 million.

Funding news includes rounds for C2C Fiber, Pacific Broadband Communications, PlanAnalytics, FinaPlex, Plastic Logic, 6Wind, ComSilica, AC&E, Verascape, MessageMachines, Currenex, MortgageRamp, VeriCenter, Zygon, Emageon, Hospit-hall.com, Chalk.com, Maxoptix, Dynaptics, Vector, MarketMile, Magnifi, Financial Technologies International, Medsite.com, Recourse Technologies, MindSHIFT, Moddo.com, NetSchools, Printlife, Infomarkets.com, and VisualFrenzy. VitaGO announced restructuring, discontinuing Italian operations, reviewing its U.K. business, and focusing on Germany.

New products and launches include Kasna, Cuantra’s Latin American ground transportation site, a Redpacket-Pocketpass wireless payments joint venture, and BuzzBack’s Web research product. M&A items include infoShark acquiring WebXi, Aptimus planning to acquire XMarksTheSpot, AutoMedia.com acquiring Automedia 2000, and iSuppli acquiring Stanford Resources.

The issue also covers board and executive appointments at several technology firms, WaldenVC closing a $275 million fund, Spinnaker Ventures launching a $53 million Latin America expansion fund, Austin Ventures promotions, and corrections on Walker Digital, Promptu, and SoftWatch.

This volume’s editorial notes provide context, source locations, related documents, event descriptions, and citations to public statements, supplemented when appropriate by memoirs and firsthand accounts. The Advisory Committee on Historical Diplomatic Documentation oversees and advises on the Foreign Relations series and declassification issues. The Department of State conducted declassification review under Executive Order 13526 from 2015 to 2019, withholding 1 document in full and making excisions in 33 documents.

The volume documents U.S. bilateral relations with the Soviet Union from January 1983 to March 1985 as part of the Reagan administration subseries. It focuses on implementation of NSDD 75’s four-part agenda: arms control, human rights, regional issues, and bilateral relations. It examines the roles of George Shultz, William Clark, Robert McFarlane, and Jack Matlock in developing and promoting policy through the NSC and State Department, including interactions with Anatoly Dobrynin and Andrei Gromyko.

The passage describes systems and methods for augmented reality and virtual reality, focusing on localization of position and orientation for users, head-mounted displays, handheld controllers, totems, haptic devices, and other objects. It explains challenges in AR/VR such as head-tracking accuracy, latency, stable placement of virtual objects, and interaction with real-world objects.

The disclosed systems include head-mounted AR displays, sensors, processors, local and cloud processing resources, stacked waveguides, cameras, QR-code-based content retrieval, wireless content access, and methods for sharing virtual content between users. A passable world model may store and update real-world mapping data using information captured by AR users.

The passage details electromagnetic tracking systems adapted for AR, including emitters, receiver coils, IMUs, sensor fusion, duty-cycle reduction, handheld-controller-based emitters, calibration methods, noise cancellation, multiplexing, ferrite cores, and distributed coil configurations. It also discusses vision-based localization using cameras, depth sensors, SLAM/PTAM techniques, feature tracking, map point creation, key frames, pose estimation, and mapping optimization. Various figures are listed showing AR hardware configurations, tracking systems, calibration, applications, and content presentation scenarios.

The passage outlines SOS defensive disruption schemes for baseline drives and side screen/roll actions. Defenders push wing ball handlers toward corner or baseline checkpoints to deny middle penetration, weakside reversals, and operating space. If the dribbler stops before the checkpoint, the on-ball defender smothers; if penetration occurs inside the checkpoint, “Base Go I” triggers an automatic baseline trap with rotations into Triangle I; “Base Go Red” is an early sideline trap used briefly to change tempo and disrupt half-court offense. All rotations occur as the pass leaves the passer’s hands. Side screen/roll coverage differs by location: above the free throw line uses aggressive switching, while below it uses hard traps near baseline or corner checkpoints, followed by near-player rotations, pass denials, post fronts, and Helpside I positioning.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture introduces RT Cores in each SM to accelerate BVH traversal and ray/triangle intersection tests, offloading shader work and enabling real-time ray tracing. RT Cores include units for bounding-box tests and ray-triangle tests, allowing Turing to achieve over 10 Giga Rays/sec and run ray tracing about 10 times faster than Pascal’s software-based approach.

Turing also introduces NVIDIA NGX, a deep learning-based technology stack using Turing Tensor Cores for AI graphics features. NGX supports pre-trained AI services for games and applications, managed through GeForce Experience or Quadro Experience, and does not work on pre-Turing GPUs. Its features include DLSS, which uses trained neural networks to produce image quality similar to TAA with reduced shading work; DLSS 2X, which approaches 64x supersampling quality; InPainting, which replaces removed image content with synthesized content; AI Slow-Mo, which inserts interpolated video frames; and AI Super Rez, which upscales images or video by creating new pixels.

Turing adds Mesh Shading through Task Shaders and Mesh Shaders, enabling more flexible geometry processing, reducing CPU draw-call bottlenecks, supporting level-of-detail selection, and enabling effects such as dynamic cutaways. Variable Rate Shading lets developers vary shading rates per 16x16 pixel region or per primitive, supporting content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, foveated rendering, and increased shading rates with MSAA. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility sampling from appearance shading by storing shading results in texture space for reuse across pixels, frames, views, or computations.

Multi-View Rendering allows scenes or instances to be rendered from multiple viewpoints in a single pass, with Turing supporting up to four hardware views per pass and up to 32 views at the API level. It expands Pascal’s Simultaneous Multi-Projection and supports VR use cases, canted displays, cascaded shadow maps, and multiple character instances. Turing also supports bindless Constant Buffer Views and Unordered Access Views under DX12 Tier 3, Tier 2 resource heaps, USB Type-C/VirtualLink for VR, and RT Core acceleration for VRWorks Audio.

The passage describes TU104, TU106, and Tesla T4 implementations. TU104 includes up to 48 SMs, 3072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and second-generation NVLink, and is used in products including GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. TU106, used in GeForce RTX 2070, includes 36 SMs, 2304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but lacks NVLink or SLI. Tesla T4 is a Turing-based inferencing GPU using TU104 with 2560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores.

Turing enables hybrid rendering, combining rasterization, ray tracing, AI, and simulation. The RTX-OPS metric weights Tensor, CUDA, RT Core, and INT32 operations by their representative use in hybrid workloads. The passage also explains ray tracing, BVH acceleration, denoising, and ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, concluding that hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH algorithms, and RT Cores together enable real-time ray tracing on Turing GPUs.

The passage discusses market commentary from Investing.com, arguing that gold’s recent rally remains below resistance and resembles its 2011–2013 pattern, while silver, platinum and mining stocks showed weak movement. It says junior gold miners failed to meaningfully rally, suggesting bearish implications, while the USD Index is verifying an inverse head-and-shoulders breakout and may rally further. Stocks are described as pausing after declines but showing bearish signals. The passage also includes promotional content, reader comments, market headlines, and trading risk disclosures.

The passage presents a local Boltzmann Generator architecture for equilibrium sampling of large crystalline materials. Generative models are framed as alternatives to molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo methods because they can generate independent equilibrium samples directly, but prior Boltzmann Generators have struggled to scale beyond small systems due to high training costs and low sampling efficiency.

The proposed method uses graph neural networks with augmented coupling flows to base transformations on local particle environments rather than full configurations. Auxiliary variables allow coupling-flow updates while preserving three-dimensional local structural information. The architecture scales linearly with system size, supports energy-based training without target samples, and can transfer models trained on small systems to much larger ones. It can also be conditioned on thermodynamic variables, box shape, or interaction-potential parameters.

Experiments cover Lennard-Jones crystals and Stillinger-Weber systems, including monatomic water, silicon, and related parameterizations. Models trained on small systems accurately generate structures and energy distributions for systems exceeding 1000 particles. Compared with global architectures, local Boltzmann Generators train faster and achieve higher effective sample sizes. They provide accurate Helmholtz and Gibbs free energies, including phase free-energy differences, with agreement against molecular-dynamics plus MBAR references.

Applications include size-transferable free-energy estimation for cubic and hexagonal monatomic-water ice, Gibbs free-energy differences between FCC and HCP Lennard-Jones crystals across cutoff radii, Stillinger-Weber phase stability as a function of three-body interaction strength, and a silicon diamond-cubic/β-tin phase diagram across temperature and pressure. The authors conclude that local, transferable Boltzmann Generators offer a scalable tool for equilibrium sampling and free-energy estimation in materials systems, with future work targeting liquids and broader chemical generalization.

Hola Publishing International has expanded its Spanish-language imprint in Mexico, offering authors and organizations publishing, printing, print-on-demand, and global distribution services. The company enables smaller book orders of 25 to 1,000 copies, reducing barriers tied to traditional large print runs and shipping costs. It provides paperback, hardcover, and e-book distribution while allowing authors to retain full rights. Hola says its Mexico-based production reduces turnaround time to 60 days and supports self-published authors, corporations, embassies, government, nonprofits, and universities.

The speaker addresses American University graduates and focuses on world peace, arguing that total war and nuclear conflict are irrational and devastating. He calls for a practical, attainable peace built through concrete actions, effective agreements, tolerance, and peaceful dispute resolution. He urges Americans to reexamine attitudes toward peace, the Soviet Union, and the cold war, emphasizing common interests, mutual dangers, and the need to avoid nuclear confrontations.

The speech supports strengthening the United Nations, pursuing arms control and disarmament, improving communication between Moscow and Washington, and preventing conflicts among allied and non-Communist nations. It announces forthcoming high-level talks in Moscow on a comprehensive nuclear test ban treaty and declares that the United States will not conduct atmospheric nuclear tests unless others do so. The speaker also links world peace to freedom and civil rights at home, stating that the United States seeks peace, will not start a war, and will work toward “a strategy of peace.”

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting results from its May 22, 2019 Annual Meeting of Shareholders. Ten director nominees were elected. Shareholders ratified Ernst & Young LLP as independent auditor for fiscal year ending December 31, 2019 and approved named executive officer compensation in an advisory vote. Shareholder proposals on food waste, special meeting thresholds, government use of technologies, product and employment reports, independent board chair policy, climate change, board ideology disclosure, gender pay reporting, executive compensation metrics, and vote-counting practices were not approved.

Just Patios offers durable, customisable carports designed for Australia’s harsh weather and to protect vehicles from rust and corrosion. Its galvanised or colourbond systems suit cars, boats, caravans, motorbikes and jet skis. Builders inspect homes to integrate installations with existing styles. Carport options include Flat/Skillion, Raised Flyover and Gable designs, with variants for different locations and vehicle needs. Just Patios serves Brisbane and the Sunshine Coast and provides products backed by 15-year warranties.

Mark Mobius told CNBC a 30 percent U.S. market correction is possible, citing ETF outflows and algorithm-driven selling as risks that could accelerate declines. He also warned emerging markets remain vulnerable, especially amid issues in Turkey, Argentina and Brazil, though selective opportunities exist. Paul Krugman also warned of a possible self-reinforcing emerging-market currency crisis.

The disclosure describes techniques for time-aware and time-sensitive networks, including low-latency scalable gate control, sharing a physical network link among multiple time-sensitive applications, and energy-efficient communication. It explains TSN, gPTP/PTP domains, grandmaster clock selection, time synchronization, PTP instance models, and scheduled traffic using traffic classes, queues, transmission gates, gate control lists, and gate operations.

Existing TSN NIC implementations store large gate control lists in NIC hardware, causing silicon area, power, and programming complexity issues. The proposed architecture moves the gate control list into host memory and uses smaller NIC registers and a prefetch buffer, with dedicated fetching of gate entries and data payloads to support lower latency, shorter cycle times, and finer timing resolution.

The passage also describes configuring complex end stations that host multiple talker applications. Such stations can be represented as a virtual bridge connected to multiple virtual end stations, enabling centralized network management to compute and apply TSN configurations while allowing multiple applications to share one physical network interface.

IUP President Dr. Michael Driscoll halted an Academic Integrity Board investigation and allowed senior Lake Ingle to return to a required religious studies class after Ingle was barred following comments during a transgender issues discussion. Driscoll said a faculty monitor will join the class to support a positive learning environment.
Figures show multiple views of a desk lamp design; dashed lines are not claimed.

The passage explains option trading in TQQQ, an ETF tracking the Nasdaq-100. It distinguishes options from stock trading, noting that calls give the right to buy and puts give the right to sell at a set price. TQQQ options include European and American styles with varying expirations and strike prices.

Common strategies include buying calls, buying puts, writing covered calls, and writing puts. Strategy choice depends on goals, risk tolerance, market conditions, time frame, liquidity, and the amount of money an investor is willing to risk. The passage repeatedly recommends backtesting and using risk management.

Options in TQQQ are leveraged and speculative, offering potential for higher returns but also greater losses. Suggested protections include stop-loss orders, cautious use of leverage, diversification, and avoiding investments beyond what one can afford to lose. Costs depend on the broker and may include commissions, contract fees, and slippage. Tax treatment generally involves capital gains tax but varies by jurisdiction. Fair value may be estimated with the Black-Scholes model, supplemented by other analysis.

The speaker declares that democracy has prevailed through a peaceful transfer of power after violence at the Capitol. He calls for national unity to address crises including the pandemic, job loss, racial injustice, climate change, political extremism, domestic terrorism, inequality, and threats to truth and democracy. He pledges to be a president for all Americans, defend the Constitution, restore alliances, engage with the world, and lead by example. He urges Americans to reject division, lies, and violence; honor those lost to the pandemic; and work together to build a future defined by hope, dignity, justice, healing, and public service.

University at Albany chemists synthesized manganese diboride, a boron-rich compound that is over 20% more energetic by weight and about 150% more energetic by volume than aluminum used in solid rocket boosters. It remains stable until ignited with an agent such as kerosene. Made with an arc melter at about 3,000°C and rapidly cooled, its strained, asymmetrical atomic structure stores high energy. Researchers say the compound could improve rocket fuel efficiency and that related boron structures may also aid catalytic converters and plastic breakdown.

Barry “The Hatchet” Vagnoni, a lifelong Philadelphia Eagles fan from Reading, Pennsylvania, hosts large game-day gatherings with his wife, Dawn, in a 2,000-square-foot Eagles-themed man cave. The space includes a bar, 16 televisions, memorabilia, and strict rules requiring Eagles gear and family-friendly behavior. For Super Bowl LII, when the Eagles face the New England Patriots, the Vagnonis expect more than 100 guests, along with food, entertainment, and performances. Vagnoni says the Eagles are his life’s passion and hopes for a Super Bowl victory with family and friends.

European football’s new season has opened with multiple discipline issues and transfer disputes. Cristiano Ronaldo received a five-match domestic ban for pushing a referee after being sent off in Real Madrid’s Spanish Super Cup win over Barcelona. Other incidents included Cesc Fabregas and Gary Cahill being sent off in Chelsea’s loss to Burnley, Jonjo Shelvey’s red card in Newcastle’s defeat to Tottenham, and Lille goalkeeper Mike Maignan’s dismissal in a 3-0 loss to Strasbourg. Juventus midfielder Miralem Pjanic avoided suspension after receiving only a yellow card for kicking Ciro Immobile.

Off the pitch, players including Virgil van Dijk, Philippe Coutinho, Danny Rose and Diego Costa have been involved in disputes or complaints linked to transfers, wages or club ambitions. The passage says these events show continuing petulance among European footballers and notes UEFA is preparing a new respect campaign.

Gap trading strategies involve trading price gaps between a prior close and the next open, most often on daily charts. Gaps can occur in any asset and time frame, commonly due to overnight news or imbalances. Types include common, exhaustion, runaway, and breakaway gaps. Small gaps are more likely to be filled, while larger gaps fill less often and may take longer.

The article states that gap trading in stocks and indices is less profitable than in the past because competition and computing power have reduced simple opportunities. Backtests on S&P 500 futures show fill rates decline as gap size increases: around 59–61% for 0.1% gaps, 42–43% for 0.5% gaps, and 28–33% for 1% gaps. Reliable data is emphasized as essential for backtesting.

Simple day-trading gap strategies tested in the article were mostly unprofitable or only marginally improved with filters. A swing trading example holding overnight showed an average gain of about 0.48% per trade and a profit factor of 1.8. The article concludes that gap trading can still work but is difficult, especially in popular stock indices, and often requires additional criteria, filters, or exploration of other markets.

A review of 10 trials involving 77,917 high-risk participants found omega-3 fatty acid supplements did not reduce deaths from heart disease, nonfatal heart attacks, strokes, or procedures to reopen clogged arteries. Researchers reported in JAMA Cardiology that outcomes were similar for supplement and placebo groups, offering no support for American Heart Association guidance recommending omega-3 supplements for patients with prior coronary heart disease. The study noted limitations including varied trial designs and lack of individual data on smoking and cancer history. Some experts not involved said supplements are inexpensive, safe, and may still be reasonable for some patients, while emphasizing fish consumption and broader healthy habits.

Boscov’s reported record-breaking sales in 2017, with its downtown Wilkes-Barre store seeing increased brick-and-mortar business despite broader department store struggles and nearby Bon-Ton and Sears closures. Customers and local officials credit the store’s success to loyal clientele, familiar staff, convenience, sales, and a hometown atmosphere. Officials say it supports other downtown businesses. Boscov’s plans to open a 47th store in Connecticut.

The passage argues that education requires comprehensive renewal because society and learners are changing rapidly. It emphasizes learner-centred education for the Net generation, including Millennials, Generation Z, and Generation Alpha, whose learning goals, motivations, and information processing differ from earlier generations. Technological change has created intertwined physical and cyber worlds, expanded intelligence beyond humans to AI and hybrid forms, and shifted education from face-to-face formal schooling toward blended and non-formal models.

The text outlines waves of technological-social change, from the steam engine and electricity to computing, the Internet, and the current sixth wave marked by generative AI and large language models. It states that generative AI is already affecting economies, politics, cultures, work, and education, raising questions about knowledge, educational content, assessment, and the teacher’s role. The passage concludes that education must move from digital pedagogy, where technology is a tool, to generative pedagogy, where generative AI becomes a partner. Teachers will no longer be the sole carriers of knowledge and will increasingly focus on relationships, values, and the affective domain.

Bayard received an “unmodified” audit grade from Fierro & Fierro, indicating good financial standing, despite two minimal findings: a $700 deficit in a new federal grant fund budget and $64 in mileage calculation errors. The Bayard City Council also unanimously approved a resolution supporting Santa Clara’s effort to manage Fort Bayard, despite concerns from Councilor Zeke Santa Maria about Santa Clara’s capacity. Chamber Director Scott Terry said Santa Clara seeks no funding from Bayard and has a plan to restore Fort Bayard, including leasing office space to the U.S. Forest Service. The council also heard an update on efforts to restore the historic Bayard train depot, complicated by railroad ownership of the land beneath it.

Horses4Heroes has opened registration for Saturdays at the Ranch Day Camps, Spring Break Camp and 10 weeks of Summer Camp for children ages 5 to 13 at its Equestrian Center in Floyd Lamb at Tule Springs, Las Vegas. Camps include horseback riding, Horse 101, hay rides, farm animals, outings and other activities. Reduced rates are available for veterans, military personnel, law enforcement officers, teachers and nurses. Teen volunteers ages 14 to 17 may serve as student counselors. Proceeds support animal care and scholarships for camps, lessons and workshops for veterans. Horses4Heroes also offers riding lessons, test rides, workshops and other programs for the community.

Smart beta ETFs have attracted significant assets, but many advisors lack familiarity. A 2018 FTSE Russell survey found 79% of U.S. advisors were aware of smart beta, while 35% were very familiar. Many cited insufficient knowledge, highlighting continued demand for education.

Ric Flair’s representative said the 68-year-old wrestling legend was hospitalized for routine monitoring and is dealing with “tough medical issues.” Melinda Morris Zanoni asked for prayers and positive energy, while Mick Foley and Eric Bischoff wished him well. Flair debuted in 1972 and entered WWE’s Hall of Fame in 2008.

The President returns without approval House bill No. 1471, which would double the pension of Andrew J. Hill. The Pension Bureau had recently rejected the claim, finding the existing pension commensurate with the disability. The President questions frequent congressional reversal of Bureau decisions through special pension legislation, arguing such intervention should be rare and that any flaws in the Bureau should be corrected directly. He notes that nearly 240 special pension bills were recently presented, many involving claims previously rejected or never reviewed by the Bureau, with estimated annual costs over $35,000. Many will become law without approval because there is insufficient time to issue objections. The specific bill is rejected because it names Andrew J. Hill, while records and the committee’s medical certificate show the intended beneficiary is Alfred J. Hill.

Xu Yan, wife of detained Chinese human rights lawyer Yu Wensheng, said police prevented her from leaving her Beijing neighbourhood without explanation. Yu was detained in January and charged with inciting subversion after calling for constitutional reforms. The passage links his case to China’s broader crackdown on independent legal activists and harassment of detainees’ families.

The Motley Fool Money review describes the Wells Fargo Reflect® Card as a strong option for people seeking to pay down debt or finance a large purchase with a long interest-free period. The card offers 0% intro APR for 21 months from account opening on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a variable APR of 16.99%, 23.49%, or 28.74%. It has no annual fee, up to $600 in cellphone protection for theft or damage when the monthly bill is paid with the card, and access to My Wells Fargo Deals.

The review notes drawbacks including no ongoing rewards after the intro APR period, a 5% balance transfer fee with a $5 minimum, and a 3% foreign transaction fee. It says the card may not suit users seeking cash back, travel rewards, or international spending benefits. Applicants are generally recommended to have good or excellent credit, though approval is not guaranteed.

Xiaomi’s Mi 8 models feature a Snapdragon 845 chipset, 6GB RAM, 6.21-inch AMOLED display, dual-frequency GPS, dual 12MP rear cameras, and a 20MP front camera with AI portrait features. Xiaomi also introduced the budget Mi 8 SE with Snapdragon 710, dual rear cameras, and a starting price of 1,799 yuan.

The passage discusses using ChatGPT for trading strategy development, including generating technical indicators, coding trading algorithms, analyzing sentiment from news and social media, and creating predictions based on historical data. It explains that traders should validate ChatGPT outputs with other sources, debug generated code, and backtest strategies before live use. The passage emphasizes that ChatGPT cannot identify the most profitable strategies or automate trading by itself, and it may produce incorrect or buggy results. An example Amibroker RSI mean-reversion strategy generated by ChatGPT produced logical rules but few trades and many coding errors. The passage concludes that ChatGPT can provide useful hints and support but should not be relied on for correct trading results without testing and validation.

The passage explains defensive approaches to mid screen basketball offense, where a big screens for a small to create dribble penetration or post-up opportunities. Because switching can create mismatches, NBA teams often prefer “show and recover,” in which the on-ball defender pushes the ballhandler wide while the screener’s defender shows, then recovers to the post as teammates deny passes and provide weakside help. Another strategy, “All Out SOS Disruption,” traps the point guard before the screen or pass develops, forcing the offense out of its planned action. Defenders then rotate using near-player concepts, deny return passes, close out on receivers, and apply SOS principles, including helpside positioning, post denial, and trap rotations when needed.

The volume documents Shultz’s bureaucratic struggle with the NSC, his eventual regular access to Reagan, and his efforts with Matlock and others to maintain dialogue with the Soviet Union despite opposition and crises in 1983. It covers Cold War flashpoints including SDI, the KAL 007 downing, Euromissile deployments, the Soviet “War Scare,” and Able Archer, showing how these affected U.S.-Soviet relations. After the Soviet walkout from INF talks, the administration focused in 1984 on restarting arms control negotiations, with SDI remaining a major point of contention. Shultz and Gromyko agreed in January 1985 to new Nuclear and Space Talks with START, INF, and Defense and Space tracks. The volume also acknowledges archival, declassification, editorial, and institutional assistance in preparing the documentation.

A report claims Nintendo may soon end production of the NES Classic Mini, with remaining shipments expected around April or May. A NeoGAF user claiming to work for a large Nordic retailer said Nintendo confirmed production had ended. It remains unclear whether the stock shortage applies only to Norway-based retailers or worldwide sellers.

Cell2Text is a multimodal generative framework that converts single-cell RNA-seq profiles into natural-language descriptions of cellular identity and function. It uses a frozen Geneformer encoder to produce gene-level embeddings, a lightweight adapter to align them with a language model’s embedding space, and instruction-tuned LLM decoders, including Llama-1B and Gemma-4B, to generate structured descriptions covering cell type, tissue, disease, developmental stage, and active pathways.

The authors build a 1 million-cell dataset from CELLxGENE with 7,331 donors, 783 cell types, 347 tissues, 128 disease conditions, ontology definitions, and pathway annotations from 34 MSigDB Hallmark pathways. Evaluation includes text-generation quality, classification labels parsed from generated text, ontology-aware PageRank similarity, and pathway classification.

Cell2Text achieves high semantic text quality, with BioBERT F1 scores above 93% for fully fine-tuned models. It outperforms Geneformer+Head and Geneformer+LGBM baselines on cell type, tissue, and disease prediction, with Gemma-4B reaching 77.83% cell type accuracy and 85.62% PageRank similarity. For pathway identification, Cell2Text performs competitively while not being specialized for the task. The study concludes that text-generation training yields interpretable and biologically meaningful cellular representations.

Haas School’s Nov. 9, 2000 alumni jobs bulletin lists openings across technology, finance, nonprofit, healthcare, education, and executive management. This study investigated whether oxytocin enhances responses to social touch targeting CT fibers through gentle stroking or non-CT pressure mechanoreceptors through medium pressure massage, and whether intranasal and oral administration differ. In a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled design, 171 healthy Chinese participants received 24 IU intranasal oxytocin, oral oxytocin, or placebo. Behavioral ratings, plasma oxytocin, physiological measures, and fNIRS responses in touch- and reward-related cortical regions were recorded.

Both intranasal and oral oxytocin increased plasma oxytocin concentrations and selectively increased pleasantness ratings for gentle stroking touch, but not medium pressure massage. Oxytocin also enhanced neural responses to gentle stroking touch in the medial and mediolateral orbitofrontal cortex and posterior superior temporal sulcus, with no significant effects for massage. Medium pressure massage was rated as more pleasant, intense, and arousing overall and produced greater somatosensory cortex responses. Post-treatment plasma oxytocin changes mediated oxytocin’s effects on pleasantness ratings. The findings suggest that exogenous oxytocin selectively facilitates behavioral and neural responses to CT-fiber-targeted social touch through peripheral-mediated routes.

Bandai Namco announced Super Robot Wars X for PS4 and PS Vita, launching March 29, 2018 in Japan and April 26 in Southeast Asia with English subtitles. Japan will receive a Premium Edition with 35 additional songs, while early purchases include two extra scenarios, an original theme, and early access to Cybuster and Masaki.

A Nature study led by University of Texas at Austin researchers warns that hundreds of built and proposed hydroelectric dams in the Amazon basin could harm ecosystems by trapping nutrient-rich sediments, altering river dynamics, increasing erosion and runoff pollution, and affecting regional climate. South American developers have proposed 428 dams, with 140 built or under construction. Researchers introduced the Dam Environmental Vulnerability Index to assess impacts. High-risk areas include the Marañon, Ucayali, Madeira and Tapajós rivers. The Madeira, which carries about half the Amazon system’s sediment from Bolivia and Peru, has already seen reduced sediment concentration after two large dams. Scientists say planned dams could threaten biodiversity, floodplains, mangroves, food supplies and sediment flows into the Atlantic, with possible climate effects beyond the region.

The passage describes a smart gateway platform for industrial Internet of Things analytics. The platform stores model templates associated with industrial business objectives, such as reducing downtime, improving product quality, increasing output, optimizing energy use, and reducing emissions. A user selects a model template, and maps its defined data inputs to data tags from industrial devices. The platform customizes the template into a model, collects relevant data, normalizes it, adds contextual and modeling metadata based on defined relationships between inputs, and sends the structured data to an artificial intelligence, machine learning, statistical, or other analytics system.

The approach is presented as an alternative to conventional big data analysis, which streams large volumes of unstructured industrial data to storage and applies analytics afterward. The described system uses domain expertise encoded in model templates to identify relevant data subsets and known correlations or causalities before analytics are performed, reducing data storage and processing requirements and helping analytics systems focus on useful business outcomes.

The smart gateway platform includes a device interface component, model configuration component, data modeling component, gateway analytics component, analytics interface component, user interface component, processors, and memory. It can collect data from industrial controllers, telemetry devices, motor drives, safety systems, historians, quality systems, and other sources. It can process both raw data and pre-contextualized smart data, including example smart tag types such as State, Rate, Odometer, and Event. The platform can add metadata, synchronize related data, calculate derived values, normalize formats from different devices, and model data according to enterprise or asset hierarchies.

Structured and contextualized data can be analyzed locally on the gateway, on edge devices, at device or system levels, at enterprise level, or on cloud platforms. Analytics may generate dashboards, notifications, recommendations, predictions, or control outputs that modify industrial device operation. The passage also describes scalable architectures in which analytics tasks may be performed at different levels of an industrial enterprise depending on relevance, time sensitivity, and available computing resources.

The passage describes a divisional Australian patent application for novel cationic lipids and lipid nanoparticle formulations used to deliver therapeutic nucleic acids, including mRNA, antisense oligonucleotides, plasmid DNA, miRNA inhibitors, and related agents. The passage presents a multi-hypothesis motion planning approach for robots operating in uncertain, partially observed off-road environments. Traditional single-hypothesis planning with the KEASL search space uses only the most recent cost map, which can cause inconsistent or oscillatory trajectories when successive maps differ due to sensor noise, occlusions, state estimation errors, or incomplete observations.

The authors propose computing edge costs using multiple temporally sampled environment maps, treating the newest map as the primary hypothesis that final plans must satisfy while using earlier maps to guide search. Four methods are explored: Valid in Every Hypothesis (VEH), which is conservative and requires all edges to be valid in every map; Per-Edge Hypothesis (PEH), which reroutes invalid edges but is computationally impractical; Goal-Edge Hypothesis (GEH), which reroutes after reaching the goal but concentrates expansions near the goal; and Goal-Edge Graph Revision Hypothesis (GEGRH), which adds graph revision to focus search at divergence points between hypotheses.

Experiments used 221 planning problems from UGV field data with two and three successive environment maps, using ARA* with a one-second planning limit. Compared with VEH, GEGRH reduced average planning time by 15.4% for two hypotheses and 29.27% for three hypotheses, and reduced path duration by 6.64% and 18.72%, respectively. Both multi-hypothesis methods had higher planning times and longer paths than single-hypothesis planning, reflecting added computation and more conservative behavior.

The results indicate that GEGRH can better balance caution and efficiency than planning through the union of all obstacles, though some cases show VEH producing lower-cost paths when GEGRH’s rerouting is constrained by time. Future work includes using more hypotheses, incorporating non-binary map information, testing alternative cost functions, and estimating hypothesis certainty.

Microsoft’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2019 reported second-quarter revenue of $36.9 billion, up 14% from $32.5 billion a year earlier. Net income was $11.6 billion, up 38%, and diluted EPS was $1.51, up 40%. For the six months ended December 31, 2019, revenue was $70.0 billion, net income was $22.3 billion, and diluted EPS was $2.90.

Revenue grew across all segments: Productivity and Business Processes rose 17% to $11.8 billion, Intelligent Cloud rose 27% to $11.9 billion, and More Personal Computing rose 2% to $13.2 billion. Commercial cloud revenue increased 39% to $12.5 billion. Growth drivers included Office 365 Commercial, LinkedIn, Azure, Windows OEM, and Windows Commercial, while Xbox content and services revenue declined.

As of December 31, 2019, Microsoft had total assets of $282.8 billion, total liabilities of $172.7 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $110.1 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $134.3 billion. Operating cash flow for the quarter was $10.7 billion. Microsoft repurchased $4.6 billion of common stock during the quarter and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.51 per share. Deloitte & Touche LLP reviewed the interim financial information and stated it was not aware of material modifications needed for GAAP conformity.

A 29-year-old Essex man, Christopher Koziana, faces impaired driving charges after allegedly crashing into a gas meter on Ridge Road. Police removed him from the vehicle due to a gas leak. He was not injured and is scheduled to appear in Windsor court on June 13.

The Yankees enter the offseason after a playoff loss to Toronto, with speculation about roster changes. A prediction has New York trading for Steven Kwan as its 2026 leadoff hitter and adding Josh Naylor at first base, potentially moving on from Trent Grisham and Paul Goldschmidt.

President Trump condemned white supremacists, neo-Nazis, the KKK and other hate groups as “repugnant” after violence in Charlottesville, Virginia, where a woman was killed. His statement followed criticism from Democrats and Republicans over his earlier claim that violence came from “many sides” and his nearly 48-hour silence. Gartner analyst Stephen Kleynhans argued that Windows 10 Pro is becoming unsuitable for enterprises as Microsoft reduces support and limits enterprise management features. He cited Microsoft’s decision to extend support for several Windows 10 releases from 18 to 24 months only for Enterprise and Education editions, excluding Pro. Paid supplemental servicing, which adds 12 more months of support, is also limited to Enterprise and Education. Kleynhans and Gartner colleague Michael Silver said Pro users should monitor Microsoft’s life cycle announcements and prepare to budget for Windows 10 Enterprise as Pro becomes more oriented toward prosumers and small businesses.

Ray Dalio said investors should consider allocating up to 15% of portfolios to gold, calling it a strong diversifier and hedge against monetary debasement and geopolitical uncertainty. He compared current conditions to the early 1970s, citing inflation, high debt and heavy government spending. Gold futures recently traded above $4,000 an ounce after rising more than 50% this year.

Federal prosecutors say Matthew Lane, a 19-year-old Massachusetts college student, pleaded guilty to hacking PowerSchool and stealing sensitive records of more than 60 million students and 10 million educators. Prosecutors allege he and at least one co-conspirator extorted nearly $3 million from the company, and they are seeking a seven-year prison sentence and more than $14 million in restitution.

A sentencing memo describes Lane’s activity as sophisticated and part of a broader cybercrime pattern dating to 2021, involving targets such as schools, companies and foreign governments. Cybersecurity firm Cyble linked several online aliases to Lane and said the PowerSchool attack appeared to be an escalation by an experienced cybercriminal, not an isolated act.

People who knew Lane described him as quiet, introverted, skilled with computers and interested in gaming. Prosecutors say he used anonymized tools, stolen credentials, foreign servers and encrypted communications to hide his identity and launder proceeds. PowerSchool said it notified customers and continues working with districts and law enforcement.
John Howendobler was jailed after calling dispatch to report he choked his wife around 1:30 a.m. Friday. His wife told officers he woke suddenly, as if from a bad dream, and began choking her.

Veeco Instruments published a slide deck for its Axcelis Technologies M&A call. The passage also includes Seeking Alpha transcript team information, related article headlines, and chart data ranging from Sept. 29 to Oct. 3, 2025.

Apple Inc. filed a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 29, 2018. Total net sales were $84.3 billion, down from $88.3 billion a year earlier, primarily due to lower iPhone sales, partly offset by higher Services and Wearables, Home and Accessories sales. Apple adopted new accounting standards related to revenue recognition, financial instruments, and income taxes. Apple reported $12.0 billion of commercial paper outstanding and $103.8 billion principal amount of term debt. Legal contingencies included matters involving VirnetX, Qualcomm, and iOS performance management cases. The company stated it had accrued its best estimates where applicable.

James Hodgkinson of Belleville, Illinois, was identified as the gunman who shot five people during a Republican charity baseball practice in Alexandria, Virginia, including Rep. The ADS7828 requires careful physical layout because SAR conversions are sensitive to glitches on power, reference, ground, and digital inputs. The passage describes patent-related cancer assay panels and methods for detecting cancer-associated DNA methylation patterns in cell-free DNA. It explains that whole-genome bisulfite sequencing is costly and inefficient for clinical assays because only a small portion of the genome is informative. The described approach uses targeted bait sets or probe panels to enrich converted cfDNA fragments from genomic regions with differential methylation between cancer and non-cancer samples, enabling deeper sequencing of selected regions.

The panels may include hundreds to tens of thousands of oligonucleotide probes or probe pairs, often tiled across target regions and designed to capture hypermethylated or hypomethylated cfDNA fragments while limiting off-target binding. Target regions are selected based on anomalous methylation patterns, CpG content, rarity in non-cancer samples, and occurrence in cancer versus non-cancer subjects. The methods include converting unmethylated cytosines to uracil, enriching target cfDNA by hybridization capture or amplification, sequencing, and evaluating methylation patterns.

The passage also describes classifiers trained on cancer and non-cancer cfDNA fragments to determine cancer presence, stage, type, or tissue of origin. Potential cancer types include head and neck, liver/bile duct, upper GI, pancreatic/gallbladder, colorectal, ovarian, lung, multiple myeloma, lymphoid neoplasms, melanoma, sarcoma, breast, and uterine cancers. It further provides methods for designing panels, identifying differentially methylated genomic regions, training models, treating identified cancer patients, figure descriptions, and definitions of methylation-related terms.

Henry Grivi sought a writ of mandate compelling the Los Angeles Superior Court to strike a “Report of Presiding Judge” from the McAdoo divorce case file. The report criticized Grivi for bypassing regular procedures by taking a same-day divorce case to a visiting judge, though it stated the irregularity did not affect the decree. The court held that mandamus cannot correct mere judicial error, but the issue was whether the presiding judge had jurisdiction to file the report in the divorce action. While the judge could investigate court-rule violations or pursue appropriate contempt or disciplinary proceedings, the report concerned the attorney’s conduct, not any issue in the divorce case, and was filed without proper jurisdiction or notice. The court ordered issuance of the peremptory writ striking the document.

Some embodiments describe a packet processing pipeline for reconfigurable hardware switches in SDN. The switch includes ingress and egress pipelines, each with a parser, match-action unit (MAU), and deparser. For each packet, the parser separates headers from payload and divides header fields into a primary packet header vector (PPHV) for fields that may be processed by the MAU and a secondary packet header vector (SPHV) for fields that will not be processed. The PPHV is sent through match-action stages, while the SPHV bypasses the MAU and is sent directly to the deparser with the payload.

The MAU matches selected header fields against exact and ternary match tables and applies actions such as modifying headers, assigning output ports or queues, sending packets to a controller, or dropping packets. The deparser reconstructs the packet using processed PPHV data, unprocessed SPHV data, and payload, then sends it to a queuing system in the ingress pipeline or out of the switch in the egress pipeline.

A compiler and configurator in the control plane generate and distribute configuration data for the parser and MAU. The parser uses this data, represented through parse graphs and flow graphs, to determine how to extract headers and whether fields belong in the PPHV or SPHV. Separating participating from non-participating fields reduces MAU resource use and allows the parser to reach deeper packet headers, including those in tunneling protocols, without increasing the amount of data sent to the MAU.

The lecture reviews Poisson processes, including IID exponential interarrival times, arrival epochs, counting processes, memorylessness, stationary and independent increments, and the Poisson PMF. It explains alternate definitions using Poisson counts or small-increment conditions. The professor discusses combining independent Poisson processes, showing their sum is Poisson with rate equal to the sum of rates, and splitting a Poisson process through independent Bernoulli routing, producing independent Poisson processes. Applications include last-come, first-served queues and non-homogeneous Poisson processes, where counts over intervals remain Poisson with parameter equal to the integrated rate. The lecture also analyzes arrival epochs conditioned on a fixed number of arrivals, showing they are distributed like ordered IID uniform random variables, and introduces the paradox that an arbitrary observation time tends to fall in longer interarrival intervals.

E-mini S&P 500 futures are CME Globex-traded derivatives tracking the S&P 500 index, introduced in 1997 at one-fifth the size of the standard S&P 500 futures. The contract trades Sunday to Friday, 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET, with a one-hour break. Fifth Third Bank announced a $10.9 billion all-stock acquisition of Comerica, expected to create the ninth-largest U.S. lender with about $288 billion in assets. The deal, pending regulatory approval and expected to close in early 2026, will expand Fifth Third’s presence in Sunbelt states and strengthen commercial payments and wealth management. Comerica shareholders will receive nearly 1.9 Fifth Third shares per share, and three Comerica board members will join Fifth Third’s leadership. Critics cite consolidation risks, while supporters argue stronger regional banks improve stability.

The passage describes frequency, timing, interface, interrupt, debug, memory, and PCB layout requirements for a Texas Instruments device. PLL REFCLK, CLKDCO, and CLKOUT values must remain within specified limits, with PLL_USB fixed at 960 MHz when USB is used. SYSCLK and module clock frequencies are constrained by device and module limits.

The ARM Cortex-A8 AINTC supports up to 128 programmable-priority interrupt requests, while the C674x DSP interrupt controller combines up to 128 device events into 12 prioritized CPU interrupts with selectable multiplexed sources. Timing sections define AC test conditions, 3.3-V reference levels, slew rates, board-routing considerations, and use of IBIS models.

Peripheral descriptions include DCAN, EDMA, GPIO, GPMC/ELM, HDMI, HDVPSS, I2C, ISS, EMAC/MDIO, DDR2/DDR3 memory controllers, JTAG, trace, and AET. The buy-and-hold strategy is a passive, long-term investing approach that involves buying stocks, ETFs, or funds and holding them for years or decades, regardless of short-term market fluctuations. It contrasts with active trading, which attempts to time market entries and exits. The strategy aims to benefit from long-term stock market growth and may offer advantages such as lower trading costs, tax deferral, reduced manager risk, less stress, and compatibility with dollar-cost averaging and index investing.

The passage states that studies show buy-and-hold investors often outperform active management over long horizons after fees, though critics argue they may miss optimal selling opportunities. It notes that stock selection is difficult because few stocks become major long-term winners, so diversified portfolios, ETFs, or passive index funds may be less risky. A backtest example of SPY from 1993 showed a 9.7% annual return, while a sample trading-strategy portfolio showed smoother results with lower drawdowns, though the passage emphasizes that investing and trading are different approaches. For most people, it presents passive buy and hold as a practical option for building wealth.

This multicenter cross-sectional study examined determinants of wasting, stunting, and undernutrition among 185 children aged 6–59 months attending Community Management of Acute Malnutrition centers in four villages of southern Punjab, Pakistan. Data were collected through parent interviews, medical and immunization records, and anthropometric assessments using WHO standards. Independent variables included sociodemographic, dietary, biological, and healthcare factors; analyses used t-tests and linear regression.

Participants had a mean age of 15.36 months; 56.2% were female, 69.2% had family income ≤15,000 PKR, 77.8% had at least two siblings, 54.1% had prior illness episodes, 80.5% had no exclusive breastfeeding, and 89.2% had poor complementary feeding practices. In multivariate analysis, wasting was significantly associated with family monthly income and complementary feeding practices. Stunting was significantly associated with tuberculosis contact history and exclusive breastfeeding practices. Undernutrition was significantly associated with monthly income and exclusive breastfeeding practices.

The study concluded that child malnutrition in southern Punjab was associated with breastfeeding and complementary feeding practices, household size, family income, and infection history. It recommended incorporating awareness of children’s dietary needs and growth-related factors into child nutrition programs.

A Death Cross occurs when a short-term moving average, usually the 50-day, crosses below a long-term moving average, usually the 200-day. It receives significant media attention and is often interpreted as a signal of potential market weakness, though it is a lagging indicator. Backtests on the S&P 500 using data from 1960 suggest the Death Cross signals weaker short-term returns, especially under 30 days, but longer-term returns tend to align with normal market averages. Selling on a Death Cross and reentering on a Golden Cross can reduce drawdowns and time in the market, but may also cause premature exits and missed gains. The article concludes that the Death Cross is mainly useful as a defensive short-term indicator rather than a strong long-term return predictor.

The passage explains how distributed system patterns help developers learn from prior experience, use a shared vocabulary, and build reusable components. Patterns support reliability, agility, and scalability, and reusable container-based components can be shared across languages and systems.

It introduces single-node container patterns built from tightly coupled containers scheduled together, such as Kubernetes pods. Splitting applications into multiple containers can provide resource isolation, clearer team ownership, reuse, separation of concerns, easier testing, and safer deployments.

The sidecar pattern uses an auxiliary container to augment an application container. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service with nginx, synchronizing configuration from an API to a filesystem, providing process introspection through a reusable topz container, and building a simple Git-based PaaS. Effective sidecars should be parameterized, expose stable APIs, and be documented through Dockerfile directives, labels, and comments.

The ambassador pattern uses a container to broker communication between an application and external services. It can route requests to sharded backends, broker service discovery across environments, or split traffic for experiments. Examples include using twemproxy for sharded Redis and nginx for 90/10 request splitting.

The adapter pattern modifies an application’s interface to match expected operational standards. It is useful for monitoring, logging, and health checks when applications expose heterogeneous interfaces. Examples include adapting Redis metrics for Prometheus, normalizing logs with fluentd plugins, and adding rich MySQL health checks without modifying the database container.

The passage then contrasts single-node patterns with multi-node distributed patterns and introduces microservices. Microservices divide applications into smaller services with defined APIs, improving team independence, release agility, reliability, and scaling flexibility, but making debugging and architecture more complex.

Replicated load-balanced services are described as a basic distributed pattern for stateless systems. Multiple identical replicas provide availability, redundancy, and horizontal scaling, with readiness probes used to determine when instances can receive traffic. Session-tracked services route a user consistently to the same replica, often using hashing or cookies.

The passage also describes application-layer replicated services with caching and SSL termination. A cache such as Varnish can improve performance, but may need to be deployed as a separate replicated tier rather than as a sidecar. Edge layers can also support rate limiting, denial-of-service defense, and SSL termination with nginx.

Finally, the passage explains sharded services, where each shard serves only part of the request space. Sharding is commonly used for stateful systems when data is too large for one machine. A sharded cache can improve memory utilization compared with replicated caches, but failures affect specific users or requests. Replicated sharded caches improve resilience and allow scaling of individual hot shards. The passage also discusses shard routing using ambassadors or shared router services and introduces sharding functions based on deterministic, uniform hashing.

The passage describes SD Memory Card physical-layer command behavior, timing, data transfer, erase, write protection, lock/unlock, switch functions, clock control, CRC, and timeout rules.

CMD19 tuning follows single-block read timing and must complete 40 consecutive executions within 150 ms, excluding host processing time. During card identification, the host remains at fOD; in data transfer mode it may use fPP. CMD9 reads CSD, CMD4 optionally sets DSR, and CMD7 selects or deselects cards. Only one card may be in Transfer State, and deselection may occur automatically with unmatched RCA on common CMD lines.

Read and write transfers can be stopped by CMD12. Write operations may enter Programming State, use DAT0 low as BUSY, and may continue if the card is deselected. Programming is terminated by CMD0 or CMD15, which may destroy data. Wide bus mode is selected by ACMD6, but locked cards reject ACMD6.

Read and write operations are block oriented, CRC protected, and may reject commands on block length or address errors. SDHC and SDXC use fixed 512-byte block length and block addressing, while SDSC uses byte addressing and CMD16-defined block length. Multiple block write is preferred for speed, and ACMD23 may predefine blocks to pre-erase.

Erase uses CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38. DISCARD and FULE are CMD38 variants supported only by SDHC and SDXC outside SPI mode, with support indicated in SD_STATUS. DISCARD treats contents as “don’t care,” while FULE logically erases the entire user area. DAT0 indicates busy during erase-related operations.

Three write protection methods are described: mechanical switch, optional internal protection, and password lock. CMD42 manages password-based lock/unlock using nonvolatile PWD and PWD_LEN registers. Card Ownership Protection adds FEP registers, COP Unlock, FEP management, Force Erase controls, and FEP Force Erase. Locked cards accept only specified commands; other commands are illegal. Force Erase clears user data and password state, except when blocked by FEP.

APP_CMD (CMD55) makes the next command application-specific. Undefined or illegal ACMD handling is defined, and ACMD41 has special APP_CMD status behavior. CMD6 switches or checks functions across groups including bus speed, command system, driver strength, and power limit. CMD6 returns a 512-bit status block and supports mode 0 checking and mode 1 switching. High-Speed mode is optional and enabled through CMD6.

CMD8 initializes Version 2.00 or later cards by checking host voltage and echoing a check pattern. The host may change or stop the bus clock under defined restrictions and must provide required post-transaction clocks. CRC7 protects commands, responses, CSD, and CID; CRC16 protects data blocks. Cards do not execute commands with CRC errors or illegal commands and set status error bits. Read, write, and erase timeout behavior is specified, including 100 ms read timeout guidance and write busy limits of 250 ms or, for some SDXC cases, 500 ms.

RFID-технологии, несмотря на трудности раннего внедрения в ритейле из-за стоимости меток, незрелости стандартов и интеграционных проблем, получили новые предпосылки для развития благодаря цифровизации, электронному документообороту, большим данным, онлайн-кассам, ИИ и другим технологиям. В современном ритейле RFID используется для идентификации товаров, инвентаризации в реальном времени, управления запасами, предотвращения потерь, автоматизации логистики, улучшения клиентского опыта и анализа поведения покупателей.

Современные RFID-системы обеспечивают точность инвентаризации около 98–99%, сокращают время учета, снижают уровень отсутствия товаров на полках или складе, помогают выявлять подозрительные перемещения товаров и автоматизируют приемку через RFID-ворота. Их архитектура включает метки, считыватели, корпоративные системы, middleware, базы данных и аналитические инструменты, а также может поддерживать обмен данными между участниками цепочки поставок через стандартизированные протоколы.

Исследования показывают, что RFID применяется в логистике, управлении цепями поставок, розничной торговле, управлении активами и производством. В ритейле RFID-данные позволяют анализировать перемещения покупателей, остановки в отделах, посещаемость зон, эффективность выкладки и связь поведения с POS-данными. Интеграция RFID с IoT расширяет возможности мониторинга и позиционирования в реальном времени.

Для оценки эффективности внедрения RFID предлагается система сбалансированных показателей, учитывающая финансовые, клиентские и операционные эффекты. Указаны такие возможные результаты, как ROI 20–30% за два года, сокращение потерь от краж до 75%, снижение логистических и инвентаризационных затрат на 30%, рост продаж на 5–10%, сокращение времени кассовых операций на 50% и повышение точности выполнения онлайн-заказов до 98%.

В работе описана архитектура сбора и обработки трекинговых данных клиентов на основе ETL-процессов, промежуточной и основной баз данных, хранилища, многомерного куба и инструментов визуализации. Harvard researcher Ian Wallace examined the knees of more than 2,000 skeletons from academic collections and found that knee osteoarthritis prevalence has doubled since the mid-20th century, from about 8 percent in earlier skeletons to 16 percent in recent ones. The increase remained even after adjusting for age and weight, suggesting factors beyond aging and obesity. Harvard professor Daniel Lieberman argues arthritis should not be viewed simply as age-related wear and tear and suggests physical inactivity may be a major factor, since people in the past tended to sit less and walk more. Co-author David Felson says joints need load and stress to remain resilient, and exercise can strengthen cartilage and supporting muscles, though it may not be appropriate to begin intense activity when disease is advanced. The researchers say the findings point to further study of lifestyle factors behind rising arthritis rates and how they might be changed.

The passage provides PCB layout guidance for the UC1825B-SP, emphasizing that feedback traces should be direct, somewhat thick, and kept away from inductors and noisy power traces, preferably separated by a ground plane. Input, output, feed-forward, and compensation capacitors should be placed close to the IC, with surface-mount parts recommended to reduce noise coupling and lead inductance. Power traces should be short, direct, and thick, with at least 15 mils per ampere, and power components should be placed close together to reduce EMI, ringing, resistive losses, and voltage errors. Grounds for key components should connect closely to a ground plane, with multilayer boards using planes and vias appropriately. Switching current loops should be arranged in the same direction to reduce radiated EMI.

For output drivers capable of 2-A peak currents, a ground plane is required, with a dedicated power-ground area for high di/dt currents connected to PGND. VCC and VREF require high-frequency bypass capacitors, with low ESR/ESL ceramic 1-mF capacitors recommended. The passage also includes documentation update instructions, TI E2E support information, trademark and ESD cautions, mechanical and packaging notes, orderable-information disclaimers, and TI’s general resource and warranty limitations.

The preprint investigates how human contact network structure affects respiratory disease spread, using COVID-19 as an example. It examines population-level risk tolerance, age and household-size distributions, and interaction types including households, classrooms, workplaces, and community background transmission. The abstract reports that vulnerable individuals changing behavior in isolation is insufficient to reduce their infection risk, population structure can have varied and counteracting effects, and co-worker interactions generally contribute more to spread than schoolchild interactions.

The study constructs synthetic contact networks of about 3,000 individuals based on U.S. demographic data, assigning age, household membership, vulnerability status, school classrooms, and workplaces. It compares networks modeled on Florida, with higher average age and smaller households, and Texas, with lower average age and larger households. Three behavioral scenarios are considered: all individuals fully participate in school and work interactions; vulnerable individuals avoid those interactions; and all members of households containing vulnerable individuals avoid them.

Disease spread is simulated with a modified SEIR chain-binomial model. Individuals may be susceptible, exposed, symptomatic infectious, asymptomatic infectious, recovered, or dead. Transmission depends on contact type, while progression, recovery, and mortality depend on disease parameters and vulnerability status. Parameters are based on literature values approximating the initial Wuhan strain of COVID-19.

This study used Mendelian randomization to identify genetically supported drug targets for prostate cancer. eQTLGen data, druggable gene lists, and GWAS data from UK Biobank and FinnGen were analyzed. In the discovery phase, 151 genes were causally associated with prostate cancer risk; replication identified 12 genes: HOXA9, MPHOSPH6, SLC45A3, PBX2, HLA-A, PPARGC1A, FLOT2, TKT, CARNS1, GPBAR1, CSF1R, and TRAV21. HOXA9, MPHOSPH6, SLC45A3, PBX2, and HLA-A were positively correlated with risk, while the others were negatively correlated. Enrichment analyses linked these genes to metabolic and cancer-related pathways, and PPI networks were constructed. DSigDB predicted five candidate drugs: tauroursodeoxycholic acid, Adehl, GDP366, decanoic acid, and GW612286X. Molecular docking showed binding affinities between these drugs and targets including PPARGC1A, GPBAR1, and CSF1R. The study suggests these genes and drugs may inform targeted therapy, but further experimental validation and clinical trials are needed.
