This study evaluated first-phase left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF-1) as an echocardiographic indicator of cardiac dysfunction in coronary heart disease (CHD). Patients undergoing first-time coronary angiography for chest pain were grouped by stenosis severity: mild, moderate, and severe. LVEF-1 was measured before angiography, and in PCI patients again on the fourth postoperative day.

Among 207 patients, LVEF did not differ significantly across stenosis groups, while LVEF-1 decreased as stenosis severity increased. LVEF-1 was negatively correlated with Gensini score and BNP and independently predicted coronary artery stenosis ≥50% and ≥70%. ROC analysis showed LVEF-1 had higher diagnostic value than GLS, E/e′, LVEF, and LVDd. After PCI, E/e′ decreased while GLS and LVEF-1 increased. Greater Gensini score and larger stent diameter independently influenced improvement in LVEF-1.

The study concludes that LVEF-1 is associated with CHD severity and may help assess cardiac dysfunction from coronary artery stenosis and early functional improvement after PCI.

The passage argues that the Modi government has taken steps toward an “ownership society,” a concept linked to Peter Drucker, David Howell, and later George W. Bush, emphasizing reduced state control and greater individual and private responsibility. It says India is still far from such a model due to pervasive government control, subsidies, and state-run companies. However, since 2014, reforms such as insolvency law, reduced political interference in banking, public sector bank consolidation, planned subsidy reductions for LPG and kerosene, and UDAY for state electricity boards are presented as efforts to reduce dependence on government handouts and shift responsibility to individuals, businesses, and states.

Researchers measured antibody responses 1 month after vaccination. BNT162b2 boosters produced immune responses against the original COVID-19 strain comparable to responses after Dose 2, and BNT162b2SA produced immune responses against the Beta variant comparable to BNT162b2 responses against the original strain. Researchers considered these results unlikely due to chance.

Safety monitoring found temporary lymphocyte decreases in some Phase 1 participants after Dose 1, which generally returned to normal within days. Injection site reactions and systemic events within 7 days were well tolerated, short-lived, and mostly mild or moderate; injection site pain, tiredness, and headache were common. BNT162b2 30 µg was selected for Phase 2/3, while BNT162b1 100 µg was stopped after Dose 1 because of reactions or systemic events.

Few participants left Phase 2/3 because of medical problems, and most reported problems were mild or moderate. Serious medical problems were uncommon across phases and booster groups; researchers generally did not consider them related to the study vaccine, though some temporary serious events in participants aged 16 and older were considered possibly related. No deaths occurred in Phase 1 or among BNT162b2SA recipients in Phase 3; deaths in Phase 2/3 occurred from different causes and were not believed to be caused by BNT162b2.

More than 500 flu cases were reported in Missouri in one week. Nurse Sandy Gibbons advised seeking treatment within 72 hours of symptoms, resting, drinking fluids, eating well, and avoiding returning to work too soon to prevent spreading illness.

The passage promotes an online custom term paper and essay writing service. It claims the service helps students obtain assignments conveniently, submit them on time, and improve grades. It advises comparing writing providers, reading reviews, checking prices, and contacting writers. The service advertises quality writing, fast delivery, experience, and commitment to customers.

A backtest examined whether a Santa Claus Rally exists in the NIFTY 50 using daily Yahoo Finance data from 2008 onward. The strategy went long at the close of the second Friday in December and exited on the first trading day of the new year. Results showed 1.2% average gain, 71% win ratio, profit factor of 6, and 7% maximum drawdown.

The Pittsburgh Steelers unveiled 1978 throwback jerseys at Heinz Field, modeled on uniforms from their Super Bowl XIII and XIV era. The jerseys will replace the “bumblebee” throwbacks for at least two seasons and be worn against the Cleveland Browns in Week 8. JuJu Smith-Schuster, Art Rooney II, Franco Harris and John Banaszak attended the unveiling.

Digital leaders promote transparent data access, shared context, and data-driven decision-making while applying governance controls to protect data and build trust. They discourage data hoarding, encourage measurement, and use clear metrics to support learning, experimentation, autonomy, and organizational alignment. Their goals often connect individual and team objectives to company strategy through transparent, data-grounded processes.

Digital laggards typically restrict data access, keep data in silos, and rely more on business judgment, hierarchy, or qualitative process adherence than on shared metrics. Their goals are often aspirational, poorly grounded in data, and weakly connected to strategy, which can reduce alignment and stifle innovation.

The passage argues that strong data culture aligns organizations vertically and horizontally through shared metrics, common data models, and transparent access. Successful digital transformation requires not only technology but also leadership sponsorship, cultural change, learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement. Organizations may fall into patterns such as data novice, insight ready, tech enabled, or data reliant, each requiring targeted actions to strengthen data culture.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on February 25, 2019, its Board elected Indra K. Nooyi as a director and appointed her to the Audit Committee. Nooyi previously served as PepsiCo’s CEO, chairman, president, CFO, and in other leadership roles, and has been a Schlumberger director since April 2015. She received a restricted stock unit award for 549 Amazon shares vesting in three equal annual installments beginning May 15, 2020, subject to continued director service, and entered into the company’s standard director indemnification agreement.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies such as buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge when paired with external gate drivers.

TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP allow programmable primary-to-synchronous and synchronous-to-primary dead times using resistors on PS and SP, while TPS7H5003-SP has a fixed 50-ns typical dead time. Leading-edge blanking is fixed at 50 ns typical for TPS7H5003-SP and programmable on other TPS7H500x-SP devices using the LEB pin. Pulse skipping is implemented to address minimum on-time issues, especially during high-frequency operation and startup.

TPS7H5001-SP, TPS7H5002-SP, and TPS7H5003-SP support configurable maximum duty cycle through DCL; TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50% maximum duty cycle. Current sensing through CS_ILIM supports PWM operation and overcurrent protection, entering hiccup behavior when the threshold is exceeded. The HICC pin capacitor sets delay and restart timing during overcurrent events. The FAULT pin enables external protection functions and shuts down switching when its threshold is exceeded for the required pulse width.

Slope compensation is programmed through RSC to mitigate subharmonic oscillation in peak current-mode designs. The devices use a transconductance error amplifier and support Type 2A or Type 2B compensation. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C typical and restarts after the junction temperature falls below 160°C typical.

An example synchronous push-pull converter design using TPS7H5001-SP and GaN devices is provided, covering switching frequency, feedback resistors, dead time, leading-edge blanking, soft start, transformer selection, FET ratings, RCD clamp, output inductor and capacitance, current sensing, hiccup capacitor, compensation, and slope compensation. Power supply guidance specifies a 4-V to 14-V input range, proper bypassing, and ceramic capacitors. Layout guidance emphasizes minimizing noisy switching loops, separating analog and power grounds, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, routing sensitive traces away from high dv/dt signals, and using appropriate grounding for CFP packages. Revision notes document updates including QMLP option releases and related documentation changes.

The passage compares stock and bond investment strategies. Stocks represent ownership in a company and can deliver high long-term returns, dividends, and increased ownership through buybacks, but they carry capital-loss risk and require diversification. Bonds are loans to companies or governments, usually with maturity dates and fixed interest payments; they are generally less risky than stocks because bondholders are paid before shareholders in bankruptcy. Historical evidence presented suggests stocks have outperformed bonds, but adding bonds to a portfolio can reduce volatility and drawdowns, especially near retirement or during market turmoil. A 60/40 stock-bond portfolio is described as having lower returns than an all-stock portfolio but less risk. The passage also discusses a “Sell in May and go away” winter-investing strategy, but its backtest did not perform as expected.

Motley Fool Money reviews the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card, highlighting unlimited 2% cash rewards on purchases, a $200 bonus after $500 in purchases in the first 3 months, no annual fee, 0% intro APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, and up to $600 in cell phone protection. Approval is most likely for applicants with good credit. The passage also lists alternative cash-back cards, including Capital One Quicksilver and Citi Double Cash, and includes advertising, compensation, and editorial disclosures.

The passage describes patent embodiments for muscle-targeting compositions, particularly engineered recombinant AAV vectors, capsids, particles, vector systems, cells, formulations, kits, and methods of use. The compositions include targeting moieties with n-mer motifs, including RGD or non-RGD motifs, that may be inserted into AAV capsid proteins to confer muscle-specific targeting. European stocks rose Monday in thin holiday trading, led by bank gains, while London and U.S. markets were closed. The Stoxx Europe 600 gained 0.5% after a 1.2% loss in 2016. Italian banks advanced following reports that Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena plans €15 billion in 2017 debt issuance. German banks also rose. Microsoft filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2020. For the quarter, revenue was $43.1 billion, up from $36.9 billion a year earlier; net income was $15.5 billion, up from $11.6 billion; diluted earnings per share were $2.03, up from $1.51. For the six months ended December 31, 2020, revenue was $80.2 billion and net income was $29.4 billion.

As of December 31, 2020, Microsoft had total assets of $304.1 billion, total liabilities of $173.9 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $130.2 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $132.0 billion. Net cash from operations was $31.9 billion for the six-month period.

Segment revenue for the quarter was $13.4 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $14.6 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $15.1 billion for More Personal Computing. Commercial cloud revenue increased 34% to $16.7 billion. Microsoft reported growth in Office 365 Commercial, LinkedIn, Dynamics 365, Azure, Xbox content and services, Surface, and Windows Commercial products and cloud services.

Microsoft entered into an agreement on September 19, 2020 to acquire ZeniMax Media Inc. for $7.5 billion in cash, expected to close in the second half of fiscal year 2021. The company also reported ongoing legal, tax, and regulatory matters, including IRS audits and litigation.

A Michigan family says their five-year-old son, Abdul Dannaoui, claimed two Highview Elementary educators repeatedly taped his mouth shut and threw out his lunch. His parents filed a police report and plan to sue. One substitute teaching assistant was removed, while the district disputed prior abuse claims and said it had no knowledge of earlier incidents. Police are investigating.

This study evaluated whether serum indole 3-acetate (3-IAA), previously associated with chemotherapy response in metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), was associated with treatment response or survival in borderline resectable or locally advanced PDAC. The cohort included 124 participants from the NORPACT2 study who provided blood before chemotherapy; 35 had a second sample after 2–4 months.

Median pre-treatment 3-IAA was 290 ng/mL and was positively correlated with age, but not tumor diameter or CA19-9. Pre-treatment 3-IAA did not differ significantly by CT response, CA19-9 decline, later surgical resection, or one-year survival. Among participants with paired samples, 3-IAA increased after chemotherapy, but not significantly. Median overall survival was 499 days. Survival did not differ significantly across 3-IAA quartiles, and Cox models showed no significant association between 3-IAA and overall survival, including after adjustment for age, ECOG performance status, CA19-9, and tumor classification.

The authors conclude that, in this non-metastatic PDAC cohort, serum 3-IAA was not associated with chemotherapy response or overall survival, and that prior findings in metastatic PDAC may not extend to borderline resectable or locally advanced disease.

The passage describes Reagan Library sources related to the 1980 Reagan transition, including foreign policy advisory materials, a Department of State transition report, and advisory committee membership. It also notes Reagan’s November 20, 1975 announcement challenging President Gerald Ford for the 1976 Republican nomination, emphasizing concerns about U.S. leadership, the economy, foreign energy dependence, military strength, détente, and the need for responsive government.

Builder Eric Woodward has begun creating a pop-up public park on his vacant Fort Langley lot at Glover Road and Mary Avenue after cancelling a mixed-use boutique hotel project due to a dispute with the Township. The park will include gathering spaces, play areas, picnic areas, outdoor ping pong, turfing, and adjusted fencing, with major work expected by early July.

Researchers at McGill University and the University of Toronto propose that gaslighting can be understood as a learning process based on prediction error minimization, rather than through older psychodynamic theories. Their model suggests gaslighters exploit trust in close relationships by repeatedly behaving in surprising ways and attributing the target’s confusion to a flawed grasp of reality. Over time, this can lead targets to internalize the belief that they are “epistemically incompetent.” Lead author Willis Klein says anyone could be vulnerable if they trust the wrong person, though future research may examine whether traits such as attachment style or trauma history affect susceptibility. The study was authored by Willis Klein, Suzanne Wood and Jennifer A. Bartz.

Sea of Thieves had the highest launch-month sales for a Rare-developed game since NPD tracking began in 1995. It was March’s second best-selling game and 2018’s eighth best-selling game year-to-date, excluding Game Pass downloads. The passage says it is Rare’s breakout hit for Microsoft.

Teuvo Teravainen said he plays best when calm, discussed his hockey-playing family, and described scoring against Tampa Bay as exciting for him and Finland. Antoine Vermette called the playoff opportunity exciting, emphasized bringing their best against competitive teams, and praised the team’s confidence through adversity. Both noted Tampa Bay’s fast start, while Vermette highlighted puck possession, pressure, skating, and Teravainen’s skill and smart play.

The passage examines transfer learning to address domain shift and data scarcity in neuroimaging, focusing on age and sex prediction from structural MRI. The authors use Simple Fully Convolutional Neural Networks pre-trained on UK Biobank data and fine-tuned on smaller OASIS, IXI, and ABIDE datasets. They describe the SFCN architecture, training losses, augmentation, preprocessing, dataset splits, and a transfer learning pipeline that reuses a pre-trained feature extractor and adapts the classifier and full model to target datasets.

Results show that models trained on UK Biobank perform worse when directly applied to other datasets, demonstrating domain shift, but still retain transferable information. Feature visualizations indicate that learned features are task-specific and more reusable when source and target tasks match. Fine-tuning generally improves performance, especially when pre-trained features are less aligned with the target data.

The proposed transfer learning method outperforms elastic net regression and usually outperforms training from scratch across age and sex prediction tasks. It improves reported results for OASIS and ABIDE age prediction, though comparisons are limited by differences in data splits and methods. The authors attribute performance gains to actual feature reuse rather than only favorable parameter scaling. Transfer learning also improves convergence speed, though in very small datasets fine-tuning only the final layer may be preferable to avoid overfitting. The discussion frames UK Biobank as a potentially useful pre-training resource for neuroimaging while noting challenges from scanner variability and task differences.

U.S. stocks fell Tuesday as 10-year Treasury yields reached 3 percent for the first time in four years, raising concerns about corporate borrowing costs and disappointing earnings outlooks. The S&P 500 and Dow posted their biggest declines in two-and-a-half weeks, with the Dow down for a fifth straight day. Technology and industrial shares, including Alphabet, Facebook, 3M and Caterpillar, pressured indexes. Apple and other FAANG stocks also declined. The agreement increased Amazon’s unsecured revolving credit facility from $3.0 billion to $7.0 billion and extended its term to April 27, 2021. Borrowings may be used for general corporate purposes, including backing notes issued under a commercial paper program. Amazon also established a commercial paper program allowing private placement issuance of unsecured notes up to $7.0 billion outstanding, with maturities not exceeding 397 days, for general corporate purposes. Kurt H. Zumwalt, Vice President and Treasurer, signed the report.

The study develops an AI approach for citation intent classification in Turkish academic texts, addressing the lack of large-scale Turkish resources and modern methods for this task. It introduces the first large-scale, publicly available Turkish citation intent dataset, containing 2,650 annotated citation sentences from 723 Computer Science research articles indexed in DergiPark and TR Dizin. Citation instances were extracted using the CEX module and annotated with a five-category Web of Science scheme: Background, Basis, Support, Differ, and Discuss.

The methodology combines human annotation with LLM-assisted support, using models such as GPT and Gemini to help resolve missing or ambiguous labels. Modeling experiments used In-Context Learning, automated prompt optimization with DSPy and MIPROv2, and ensemble learning. Manual prompting showed large performance variation, with revised prompts reaching 83.9% accuracy for Gemini-2.5-Flash and 85.0% for GPT-4o. DSPy optimization improved accuracy to 86.5%. Few-shot analysis showed that adding examples did not consistently improve performance.

For robust classification, ensemble methods were tested. Majority voting achieved 90.2% accuracy, logistic regression stacking reached 91.0%, and an XGBoost-based stacked ensemble achieved the best result at 91.3%. The study found major challenges from class imbalance, especially the dominance of the Background class, and difficulty distinguishing semantically close categories such as Support and Differ. It concludes that combining diverse LLM outputs through stacking provides a more reliable classifier and identifies future directions including hierarchical models, targeted or synthetic data augmentation, and broader contextual features.

A hockey player discusses preparing to close out a Stanley Cup Finals series, emphasizing focus, emotional control, and the difficulty of clinching against a team facing elimination. He says the team is aware of the stakes but must stay businesslike and concentrate on winning the game. He also addresses an injured teammate’s possible return and compares the pressures of winning at home versus on the road.

Ryan Malone signed a 25-game AHL tryout with the Iowa Wild to remain eligible for the 2018 U.S. Olympic men’s hockey team and confirmed he is pursuing a roster spot. Brian Gionta is also on USA Hockey’s radar and will attend a USOC countdown event. The 25-player Olympic roster will be named around Jan. 1.

Prof. Ross Levine and co-authors found that easier borrowing conditions lead businesses to invest more in pollution-reduction projects. Their NBER paper argues that increased credit supply makes environmental loans more available, while lower interest rates improve returns on green investments. The study used bank deposit windfalls from the fracking boom to isolate the effect of expanded lending, examining non-gas-producing counties served by banks that received shale-related deposits elsewhere. In counties with the largest credit gains, benzene levels fell 26 percent compared with average county changes, and other toxic pollutants also declined. The researchers also found that companies whose main lenders received shale-related deposit increases reduced toxic emissions more than comparable firms, received higher environmental ratings, and made stronger public statements on green issues. Levine emphasized that the study does not assess fracking’s environmental effects, but uses fracking-related bank liquidity to study how credit conditions affect environmental performance.

David Ellison, backed by his father Larry Ellison, recently acquired Paramount and is widely expected in the media industry to bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, though he has refused to discuss any plans. A deal would continue Hollywood consolidation and reduce the number of buyers for creators.

The equipment, worth an estimated $1,500 to $2,000, cost more than the car and is difficult for Sinfield, a single mother with multiple sclerosis on a fixed income, to replace. The speaker says each playoff series has become tougher and that the team must adjust to officiating, keep working, and stay disciplined. The passage introduces an edit distance for constructible \( \mathbb{R}^d \)-persistence modules and proves that it equals the interleaving distance. It situates the work within prior developments on edit distances, interleaving distances, Reeb graphs, and persistence modules, noting known links between edit-type and interleaving-type metrics.

The preliminaries review posets, lattices, Galois connections, grids, persistence modules, constructibility, finite presentations, and the relationship between \(d\)-graded modules and \( \mathbb{R}^d \)-persistence modules. Constructible \( \mathbb{R}^d \)-persistence modules are defined via left Kan extensions from finite subposets, and this notion is later shown to coincide with finite presentability.

Two categories of finite posets embedded in \( \mathbb{R}^d \) are defined: \(JS_d\), consisting of finite join-semilattices with morphisms admitting right adjoints, and \((1D)^d\), consisting of finite \(d\)-grids with grid morphisms admitting right adjoints. These categories are used to define categories of constructible persistence modules and corresponding edit distances based on sequences of morphisms weighted by distortion.

The main theorem states that for \(E \in \{JS_d,(1D)^d\}\), the edit distance \(d^E_{Ed}\) between constructible \( \mathbb{R}^d \)-persistence modules equals the interleaving distance \(d_I\). The proof establishes inequalities \(d_I \le d^{JS_d}_{Ed} \le d^{(1D)^d}_{Ed} \le d_I\), using Galois connections, free presentations, and an “easy-edit lemma” comparing presentations whose generators and relations are close.

Consequences include characterizations of interleaving-stable invariants in terms of edit-stable invariants, including that stability under a single edit suffices. The work also compares its theorem with earlier Galois-connection-based interleaving results, emphasizing that the new result handles constructible \( \mathbb{R}^d \)-persistence modules for any \(d\) and allows arbitrary edit sequences. Appendices compare constructibility notions and show that finitely presented modules are constructible.

The speaker said a mediocre second period with lapses cost the game despite strong play and chances in the third. They credited both goaltenders, said bounces favored the opponent, and emphasized working harder, playing consistently for 60 minutes, and building on recent strong home performances.

This week’s top posts cover DomTerm’s browser-based terminal emulator features, the history and meaning of open source software, container runtimes, Christine Peterson coining “open source software” in 1998, and an Ontario middle school program using Linux and open source software to keep over 200 old computers running.

Fourth-grader Lexi Bergeron in Grand Haven, Michigan, is selling handmade “stretchy straw fidgeters” to help pay classmates’ school lunch debts. A GoFundMe started by her mother surpassed its initial goal and aims to raise $2,200 for district lunch debts.

The passage describes TPS7H500x-SP current-mode PWM controller functions, protection features, design guidance, and application considerations. The CS_ILIM pin senses transformer primary-side current for PWM control and overcurrent protection; when it reaches the nominal 1.05 V threshold, the device enters cycle-by-cycle current limiting and can transition into hiccup mode. The HICC capacitor sets both the current-limit delay period and restart timing, with 3.3 nF recommended minimum. The FAULT pin enables external protections; a fault above 0.6 V for the required pulse width shuts down switching until the fault clears and a delay expires. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C typical and restarts below 160°C typical.

The device uses fixed-frequency peak current mode control and supports slope compensation through the RSC pin to mitigate subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle. Frequency compensation can use Type 2A or Type 2B networks connected to COMP. The TPS7H500x-SP family is intended for radiation-hardness-assured space-grade DC-DC converter designs and supports topologies such as buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge when paired with external gate drivers.

A synchronous push-pull GaN converter design example covers selecting switching frequency, feedback resistors, dead time, leading-edge blanking, soft-start capacitor, transformer parameters, primary and synchronous rectifier FET ratings, RCD clamp values, output inductor, output capacitance, current sense resistor, hiccup capacitor, compensation components, and slope compensation resistor. The example uses 500 kHz switching, 5 V output, 25 ns dead time, 50 ns leading-edge blanking, a 33 nF soft-start capacitor, 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 0.47 µH output inductor, about 2.3 mF output capacitance, 7.5 Ω current sense resistor, 3.3 nF hiccup capacitor, and 102 kΩ RSC resistor.

Power supply guidance specifies a 4 V to 14 V input range, at least 0.1 µF VIN bypass capacitance to AVSS, ceramic capacitors placed close to the controller, and bulk capacitance when the supply is distant. Layout guidance emphasizes minimizing noisy switching loops and switch-node area, separating analog and power grounds with a single connection point, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, routing sensitive feedback and control traces away from high dv/dt signals, filtering CS_ILIM when needed, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS with multiple vias. The passage also lists related TI documentation, update notification resources, support forums, ESD caution, revision history, mechanical and packaging information, and TI disclaimers.

The article argues for a sociocultural and ecological perspective on English language education policy and practice, focusing on state education systems in selected Asian countries. It examines why policy intentions often diverge from outcomes in contexts where English is compulsory and linked to economic development, and highlights inequalities in achievement shaped by socioeconomic, sociolinguistic and educational conditions.

Using Malaysia and Thailand as key examples, the article shows that mandated communicative approaches, CEFR-linked proficiency targets and English-medium expectations often do not align with classroom realities. Achievement tends to be higher among urban and higher socioeconomic groups, while rural and poorer learners face limited exposure to English, fewer resources and weaker support. National languages, such as Bahasa Malaysia and Thai, remain central to identity and daily communication, reducing opportunities and social incentives to use English.

The article also discusses concerns about teacher proficiency and criticizes reliance on standardized CEFR-related testing to define teacher competence without considering pedagogical skills or teachers’ own educational backgrounds. Classroom studies show that teachers often face large mixed-ability classes, exam pressures, low student proficiency, limited resources and curricula that do not reflect learners’ abilities. As a result, they may use students’ first language or teacher-centred methods despite policy mandates.

The article concludes that English education policies should be developed from an analysis of local social, linguistic and educational realities. Curriculum goals and proficiency targets need to align with system capacity and classroom conditions if English language programmes are to be effective.

P. vivax and P. ovale can relapse through dormant liver hypnozoites, but mechanisms of activation are poorly understood. This study evaluates a simple “exponential clock” model in which each hypnozoite activates independently at a constant rate, with no external triggers, while incorporating variation in infectious bites, sporozoite inoculum size, sporozoite fate, and age-related anti-disease immunity.

The model was fitted to detailed longitudinal data from the SPf66 falciparum vaccine trial on the Thailand-Myanmar border, where 1,344 children aged 2–15 were followed daily for 21 months. After excluding likely treatment failures, 2,504 symptomatic P. vivax infections, 1,164 P. falciparum infections, and 293 mixed infections were recorded. The model captured recurrent vivax infection patterns across childhood age groups, including up to 13 vivax episodes per child.

Estimated hypnozoite activation averaged once every 171 days, with a hypnozoite half-life of 118 days. The mean successful sporozoite inoculum was estimated at 6.9 per infective bite, with an average of 2.7 hypnozoites per bite. The estimated ratio of relapsing to primary P. vivax infections was 3.4, implying about 75% of observed symptomatic vivax infections were relapses. The study also found higher-than-expected vivax rates after falciparum monoinfections treated with artesunate monotherapy, compatible with external triggering, while mefloquine appeared to provide about one month of protection against emerging relapses.

Natural bacteria from grape plants may help reduce the ashy aftertaste in wildfire-tainted wine by degrading guaiacol, a key smoke-taint compound. Researchers sampled bacteria from chardonnay and cabernet sauvignon leaves and found two strains that grew on guaiacol and made it barely detectable after 96 hours. They also identified a gene needed for guaiacol degradation; deleting it stopped one strain from consuming the compound. The bacteria did not grow on related smoky compounds, suggesting other microbes may be needed to address additional smoke-taint chemicals. Researchers say the approach could be more targeted than current methods such as activated charcoal filtering, which can also remove desirable wine components, but more work is needed to study the grape microbiome’s broader potential.

The Department of Education will hold its first School Safety Conference at Okkodo High School to address concerns including drugs, violence, bullying, harassment, suicide, sexual identity, legal issues, crisis response and mental health. Officials cited rising safety issues, including 352 drug or alcohol cases in SY 2015-2016. DOE is focusing more on treatment and group therapy for drug offenses. About 400 support staff will attend the June 26 event.

Investors are speculating that the Czech National Bank may scrap its cap keeping the euro above 27 crowns, raising hedging costs to a nine-month high. Britain’s ONS is examining whether it can identify recessions sooner after past delays, despite current GDP data being produced quickly. Markets swung Wednesday as oil prices, strong U.S. jobs data, Fed minutes on stock valuations and balance sheet reduction, delays to U.S. tax reform, and caution before the Trump-Xi summit affected sentiment. Wall Street ended lower, Treasury yields and the dollar fell, Asian markets were mostly down, and European stocks were expected to open lower.

Jack Wilshere has held talks with West Ham manager Manuel Pellegrini over a possible move after leaving Arsenal. West Ham are reportedly leading interest, though Fenerbahce have offered a larger deal. Wilshere is considering his next move, with family in London and England prospects factors.

NVIDIA’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 27, 2019 reported third-quarter revenue of $3.014 billion, down from $3.181 billion a year earlier, and net income of $899 million, down from $1.230 billion. Diluted EPS was $1.45 versus $1.97. For the first nine months of fiscal 2020, revenue was $7.813 billion and net income was $1.845 billion, compared with $9.511 billion and $3.575 billion in the prior-year period. Gross margin rose to 63.6% in the quarter, while operating expenses increased to $989 million.

GPU revenue was $2.565 billion in the quarter, down 8% year over year, while Tegra Processor revenue was $449 million, up 10%. By market, Gaming revenue was $1.659 billion, Data Center was $726 million, Professional Visualization was $324 million, Automotive was $162 million, and OEM and Other was $143 million.

Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $9.769 billion as of October 27, 2019. NVIDIA had $1.990 billion in long-term debt and $11.214 billion in shareholders’ equity. The company paid $292 million in dividends during the first nine months of fiscal 2020 and did not expect to repurchase shares before closing its planned Mellanox acquisition. NVIDIA agreed to acquire Mellanox for $125 per share in cash, with closing expected likely in early calendar 2020, subject to regulatory approvals.

The Education Department continued negotiated rule-making talks on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act’s student loan changes despite the government shutdown. The first round ended without consensus and will resume Nov. 3–7. Key disputes centered on which postbaccalaureate programs qualify as “professional” and therefore for a $200,000 federal loan cap, versus $100,000 for graduate programs. The department initially proposed limiting professional programs to 10 listed in the Higher Education Act, then offered a one-year expansion for programs previously designated professional by institutions before July 4, 2025. Committee members raised concerns about legal standing, clarity, costs, workforce needs and whether the solution was only temporary.

The shutdown limited transparency because meeting materials were not being posted online, leaving committee members to share information with constituents. Repayment changes were also discussed, including the end of most income-driven repayment plans by July 1, 2026, except for a new Repayment Assistance plan and the remaining Income-Based Repayment option. Advocates warned that some borrowers, especially Parent PLUS borrowers, may face a complicated process to qualify for IBR before the deadline.

A UK Biobank study examined 451,355 participants stratified by ethnicity-specific BMI category and diabetes status to assess cardiovascular biomarkers, events, and mortality. Diabetes was present in 4.9% of participants; among them, 10.1% had normal weight, 34.4% were overweight, and 55.3% were obese. Participants with diabetes had more cardiometabolic comorbidities and adverse metabolic measures than those without diabetes within BMI categories.

In participants without diabetes, higher BMI was associated with increased carotid intima-media thickness, arterial stiffness, cardiac contractility index, and lower left ventricular ejection fraction. These BMI-related cardiovascular patterns were less clear among participants with diabetes, who showed cardiovascular abnormalities even at normal BMI. Within BMI categories, diabetes was associated with worse cardiovascular phenotype, especially among normal-weight participants.

Over a median 12 years of follow-up, all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and non-fatal ischaemic stroke increased with higher BMI, but rates were substantially higher in participants with diabetes. Normal-weight participants with diabetes had higher adjusted cardiovascular mortality risk than obese participants without diabetes. Metrics of adiposity correlated more strongly with cardiovascular biomarkers than diabetes-related measures, though correlations were weak.

The study concludes that obesity and diabetes are independently and additively associated with adverse cardiovascular biomarkers and outcomes, and that additional factors may contribute to the high cardiovascular risk seen in normal-weight diabetes.

The speaker says the team needs patience, simpler play, deeper puck placement, better shooting-lane execution, and more confrontation with defenders, while noting their goalie played well despite a long absence and frustration affected the team.

Defendant Yuk Bui Yee was charged in a 13-count indictment arising from six alleged extortion incidents at three Chinese restaurants. He moved to sever counts by incident, arguing joinder was discretionary under CPL 200.20(2)(c). The prosecution argued joinder was mandatory under CPL 200.20(2)(b), because proof of each incident would be admissible in trials of the others.

The court reviewed CPL 200.20, its legislative history, and the Molineux rule concerning admissibility of other-crime evidence. It grouped the charges by restaurant and found that repeated visits within Groups A and C could show common schemes within those groups, but not across all three groups. However, the court found the incidents shared distinctive features: the perpetrator spoke Mandarin, demanded money for his “brothers,” and claimed affiliation with the “Eagles,” supporting admissibility on identity. The court also found prior extortionate conduct relevant to intent in later incidents.

The court held all counts properly joinable under CPL 200.20(2)(b), leaving no authority to sever them. The motion to sever was denied.

Bear Grylls criticised schools for not doing enough to prepare children for adult life, saying they should empower young people rather than focus on league tables. He said success often comes from determination rather than exam results, adding that he was not brilliant at school but proved his persistence by passing SAS selection. Grylls praised Eton as progressive and said it gave him strong memories and close friends. He also discussed the possibility of Donald Trump joining him on Running Wild, saying Trump is tenacious but may be too busy and that surviving in the wild requires giving up the idea of being “king.”

This study examined cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between arterial stiffness, measured by brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV), and renal function, measured by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), in adults from central China. The cross-sectional analysis included 67,060 participants, and the longitudinal cohort included 12,324 participants. CKD was defined as eGFR <60 ml/min per 1.73 m² or microalbuminuria ≥30 mg/ml.

In cross-sectional analyses, eGFR was negatively associated with baPWV, and baPWV was negatively associated with eGFR after adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors. Longitudinally, higher baPWV predicted increased risk of incident CKD, while lower eGFR predicted increased risk of arterial stiffness. Cross-lagged path analysis showed that baseline eGFR had a stronger association with follow-up baPWV than baseline baPWV had with follow-up eGFR, suggesting kidney function decline preceded increased arterial stiffness.

The authors conclude that arterial stiffness is associated with CKD and that declining eGFR appears to precede increases in baPWV. Limitations included estimating eGFR using serum creatinine rather than the gold-standard 51Cr-EDTA technique and the study population being mainly from central China.

North Texas saw hail and four tornadoes amid a slow severe weather season. Oklahoma and Kansas have recorded zero tornadoes so far in 2018, unusually late for Oklahoma. However, tornado activity can increase sharply in May across Oklahoma and Texas.

This case study examined whether spinal cord stimulation (SCS) used to restore sensation in a missing limb modulates muscle activity during walking in one woman with unilateral transtibial amputation. Three percutaneous SCS leads were implanted near T12–L2 for 84 days. Stimulation was delivered during in-lab overground walking and triggered during prosthetic-limb stance using plantar pressure insoles. Electromyography and motion capture were used to compare muscle activation, co-contraction, and pelvic motion at early and later post-implant time points, with and without SCS.

Muscle activation profiles during walking with and without SCS at the later time point were highly similar. Over multiple weeks of in-lab SCS use, residual-limb tensor fasciae latae and vastus lateralis activation increased, while biceps femoris activity slightly decreased. Co-contraction between residual-limb knee antagonist muscles, vastus lateralis and biceps femoris, was significantly reduced at the later time point, both without and with stimulation. Increased tensor fasciae latae activity corresponded with increased pelvic obliquity range of motion and increased pelvic drop of the residual limb. Pelvic drop became more symmetrical with the intact limb and moved toward values reported for neurologically intact adults.

The authors conclude that SCS-mediated sensory feedback in this participant produced changes in residual-limb muscle activation associated with improved knee and hip motion during walking. They note that the persistence of some changes without stimulation suggests a possible rehabilitative effect, but additional participants are needed to support broader conclusions.

Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev said Russia’s economy is entering a growth stage, citing positive assessments, 1.3 percent industrial output growth, and 5 percent agricultural growth last year. He said agriculture has changed significantly, has strong export potential, and helped boost agricultural machinery production by 60 percent.

Exchange shopping privileges are limited to service members and families, but regulations allow anyone, including visitors, contractors and DoD civilians, to dine at Exchange restaurants or buy grab-and-go items from Express locations for on-installation consumption. Full-benefit eligibility questions should be directed to local Exchange managers.

This study introduced SCIseg, an open-source deep learning method for automatic segmentation of the spinal cord and T2-weighted hyperintense lesions in spinal cord injury MRI. The retrospective cohort included 191 patients and 231 scans from three sites, with varied scanner manufacturers, field strengths, image resolutions, orientations, treatment strategies, and traumatic or ischemic lesion etiologies. SCIseg was trained in three phases using nnUNet, active learning, and multi-site data, and evaluated against existing spinal cord segmentation tools and a 2D SCIseg variant.

SCIseg 3D achieved average spinal cord Dice score of 0.92 and lesion Dice score of 0.60 across test data, with better lesion performance on site 2 than site 1. It outperformed comparison methods for spinal cord segmentation and performed significantly better than SCIseg 2D for lesion segmentation. Active learning improved agreement between manual and automatic lesion biomarkers, particularly lesion volume. The model also showed qualitative generalization to degenerative cervical myelopathy.

MRI biomarkers derived from SCIseg-predicted lesion masks showed no statistically significant difference from manually derived biomarkers and correlated with selected discharge clinical scores. The authors conclude that SCIseg enables reproducible automatic segmentation of spinal cord and lesions in heterogeneous SCI MRI data and is available through open-source code and the Spinal Cord Toolbox.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated July 25, 2019, announcing its second quarter 2019 financial results. The filing incorporates a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and information on non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. The report was signed by Brian T. Olsavsky, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The speaker says the team is calm and focused ahead of Sunday, relying on the same game plan that has helped them wear opponents down. They emphasize mental toughness, experience in big games, and controlling what they can. The team wants a better start, expects both sides’ best effort, and praises strong goaltending and collective defensive work, including on the penalty kill. They also note the home atmosphere is special and say they have been aggressive in limiting the opponent’s skilled players.

Athletes Unlimited (AU), co-founded by Jon Patricof and Jonathan Soros, launched in 2020 as a new model for professional sports focused on women’s leagues, player empowerment, innovation, and social impact. Its first league was softball, developed with input from professional players, followed by volleyball, lacrosse, and basketball. AU’s model eliminates traditional team owners, uses short seasons in single locations, rotates teams through weekly drafts, ranks individual players on leaderboards, and gives athletes roles in governance through Player Executive Committees. Players also receive compensation, performance bonuses, and participation in a long-term profit-sharing plan.

The case describes the broader challenges facing women’s professional sports, including underinvestment, limited media exposure, low salaries, unstable leagues, and inadequate playing conditions. AU sought to address these issues by treating athletes as professionals, offering policies supporting pregnancy, parenting, and child care, and giving players influence over league operations and social initiatives.

AU organized as a public benefit corporation with a Mission Equity structure that caps investor returns and directs surplus toward athletes and mission-aligned programs. It built broadcast partnerships with ESPN, CBS Sports Network, Fox, Bally Sports, and others, while investing in storytelling and digital content to build fan awareness. By 2023, AU had more than 200 athletes, raised $30 million, and was named one of Fast Company’s most innovative sports companies. The case ends by raising questions about AU’s growth strategy, economic sustainability, expansion into additional sports, and how best to communicate its story.

Grupo Supervielle S.A. published a slide deck for its presentation at Latin Securities Argentina in London. Seeking Alpha’s transcripts team noted its role in producing and expanding transcript-related coverage.

The passage describes a patent disclosure for allocating wireless resource units in Wi-Fi networks with multiple BSSIDs. An access point may operate a multiple BSSID set with one transmitted BSSID and multiple non-transmitted BSSIDs, using management frames, TIM elements, BSSID indices, and AID mappings. Trigger frames can allocate dedicated or random resource units to stations, specific BSSIDs, groups of BSSIDs, all stations in the set, or unassociated stations. Random resource allocation may use AID values such as 0 for the transmitted or transmitting BSSID, a BSSID index for a selected non-transmitted BSSID, and 2045 for unassociated stations. The disclosure also describes station and access point architectures, virtual AP management, OFDMA resource units, trigger frame operation, and examples showing how targeted random RU allocation can improve medium utilization and fairness among BSSs with different traffic, device counts, priorities, or service requirements.

“Look Good … Feel Better” will offer a free May 8 event at Dignity Health Sierra Nevada Memorial Hospital, where beauty professionals help women in active cancer treatment manage appearance-related side effects.

The CAT offense attacks traps, double teams, and zone presses using a 2-1-2 spread alignment with sharp passing. The middle post is key and should be a skilled triple-threat player. When the ball enters the middle, baseline players back cut. When passed to a corner, the post rolls to the basket or back cuts if denied, then returns or interchanges with a corner. Under pressure, players should pass to the opposite corner. Dribble penetration should be used sparingly to escape trouble, drive and kick, keep the clock moving, and avoid fouls.

The speaker expresses gratitude for being at Amherst and praises the college’s tradition of graduates serving the public interest. He argues that privilege carries responsibility, citing unequal access to education, inherited poverty, unemployment among those without high school education, and income disparities. He urges educated men and women to help address national and global challenges, including jobs, international leadership, racial and religious harmony, freedom, and diversity.

The speech honors Robert Frost as both an artist and an American whose work strengthened national spirit and self-understanding. It emphasizes that artists question power, reveal truth, and defend individual perception against society and the state. The speaker says art is not propaganda but truth, and that democratic societies best serve themselves by allowing artists to remain faithful to their own visions.

He concludes by envisioning an America that balances strength with restraint, wealth with wisdom, and power with purpose; protects natural and historic beauty; builds better cities; rewards artistic achievement; expands cultural opportunity; and earns global respect for both strength and civilization.

Tight ends remain important in football because they combine receiving, blocking, size, and athleticism. They run short and medium routes, block defensive linemen and linebackers, help in pass protection and rushing attacks, and are valuable red-zone targets. The term comes from early football, when “ends” lined up on the line, with “tight ends” staying closer to the formation. Tight ends may also be called TEs or H-backs when aligned off the line. The position requires strong hands, athleticism, speed, blocking, route running, and physicality, with typical builds around 6’3”–6’8” and 240–270 pounds. Notable tight ends include Tony Gonzalez, Rob Gronkowski, Antonio Gates, and Shannon Sharpe. Their versatility allows offenses to use more schemes and create matchup problems for defenses.

CTC-Pak officials marked World No Tobacco Day by urging Pakistan to prioritize health over business and strengthen tobacco control. They said tobacco contributes significantly to non-communicable disease deaths, especially cardiovascular disease, and is linked to 108,800 deaths in Pakistan. Citing WHO, they noted tobacco’s impact on vulnerable populations and its global economic burden. Officials called for strict enforcement of tobacco laws, implementation of the delayed 85 percent pictorial health warning on cigarette packs, higher tobacco taxes, and stronger policies to reduce access, especially among children and youth. They said Pakistan, despite ratifying the WHO FCTC in 2004, still needs to fulfill its tobacco control obligations.

Guangdong Province is experiencing China’s largest recorded chikungunya outbreak, with over 4,000 confirmed cases since late July, mostly in Shunde District of Foshan. Cases have also appeared in Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, and Macao. The disease is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes and causes fever, severe joint pain, rash, headache, muscle aches, and joint swelling, but does not spread directly between people. Authorities are urging residents to remove standing water to reduce mosquito breeding. The outbreak is linked to conditions favoring mosquito-borne diseases, including climate change, urbanization, and international travel. WHO has issued clinical guidelines and strengthened its Global Arbovirus Initiative. The passage emphasizes genomic surveillance, community participation, and global collaboration, along with repellents, screens, protective clothing, and routine elimination of stagnant water to reduce infection risk.

The passage describes a method for estimating SNP-based heritability and genetic correlations using multivariate variance components linear mixed models with multiple phenotypes and variance components. Existing ML and REML approaches are computationally limited, so the authors implemented a minorization-maximization algorithm in Julia, citing its stability, convergence, and handling of positive semidefinite constraints. They applied the method to PsychENCODE isoform expression data, partitioning cis- and trans-SNP genetic variance and covariance. They report that local variants have sparse but large effects, distal variants have small but collectively large effects, cis-SNPs show substantial shared genetic influences, and isoform-level analyses identify more genetic signals than gene-level analyses, including signals associated with psychiatric disorder risk.

The paper introduces Solvent Data-Driven Embeddings (SoDaDE), a transformer-based solvent fingerprint designed to improve solvent representation for molecular modelling and solvent selection. It uses the Spange solvent property dataset, containing 191 solvents and up to 12 properties, augmented by shuffling property-value sequences and masking values during training. The model combines solvent type, ChemBERTa fingerprints, labels, and scalar property values, using causal and attention masks to predict masked solvent properties.

SoDaDE was evaluated on solvent property prediction and the Catechol Benchmark. On the solvent property test set, it achieved the lowest average MSE compared with averaged values, random forest, and Gaussian process models. On the Catechol Benchmark, SoDaDE outperformed prior representations including ACS, DRFPs, fragprints, Spange features, RXNFP, and ChemBERTa. It achieved MSEs of 0.0029 without fine-tuning and 0.0026 with fine-tuning on the full dataset, and 0.0044 on the single-solvent task in both settings. The authors conclude that SoDaDE provides an effective solvent fingerprint and that useful fingerprints can be created from small datasets.

True Orange’s Nov. 13, 2000 issue covers Texas Longhorn recruiting and sports updates. Texas football’s major recruiting weekend is Dec. 15-17, with 19 commitments expected and 10 remaining targets, including Tommie Harris, Derrick Johnson, Kaelen Jakes, James Moses, Jonathan Jackson, Jamie Hightower, William Winston, Dewayne Brandon, Quan Cosby and Paul Broussard. Bowl options after the Texas A&M game include the Cotton, Holiday or Alamo bowls if Texas wins.

Texas women’s basketball beat Tulane 71-47 to reach the Preseason WNIT semifinals, led by Tai Dillard’s 17 points, after opening with a 72-47 win over Wichita State. The issue also criticizes UT’s handling of football fans regarding early kickoffs and untelevised road games.

Texas baseball signed 12 recruits, while women’s basketball coach Jody Conradt signed four players: Kala Bowers, Heather Schreiber, Jody Bell and Colencia Reed. Football notes include Texas gaining 637 yards against Kansas and Hodges Mitchell setting a school and Big 12 all-purpose yardage record. Men’s basketball signed T.J. Ford and Chris Wright. Volleyball signed Bethany Howden and LaTonya Coates. Softball signed six players, led by pitcher Cat Osterman. Men’s golf signed Charlie Santaularia. The next issue is scheduled for Nov. 27.

The lecture introduces causality and stability for discrete-time systems, focusing on linear shift-invariant systems. Stability means every bounded input produces a bounded output; for linear shift-invariant systems, this is equivalent to the unit sample response being absolutely summable. Causality means the output at any time depends only on current or past inputs; for linear shift-invariant systems, this requires the unit sample response to be zero for negative time.

The lecture also introduces linear constant coefficient difference equations as descriptions of discrete-time systems. A zeroth-order equation directly gives the convolution sum, with the unit sample response equal to the input coefficients over a finite range. Higher-order equations require boundary or initial conditions; different choices can yield causal or non-causal systems and different stability properties. A first-order example shows a causal solution with unit sample response \(a^n u(n)\), stable when \(|a|<1\), and a non-causal solution with different stability behavior.

Finally, the lecture presents frequency response as an alternative representation of linear shift-invariant systems. Complex exponentials are eigenfunctions of such systems, so the output is the same exponential multiplied by \(H(e^{j\omega})\), the frequency response. This response determines the amplitude and phase changes of sinusoidal inputs. For a causal first-order system, the frequency response is derived as \(1/(1-ae^{-j\omega})\). The frequency response is a continuous function of \(\omega\) and is periodic with period \(2\pi\), leading into the next lecture on the Fourier transform.

GameStop says all 4,400-plus U.S. stores will receive at least five Nintendo Switch consoles by August 15, available no later than August 16, marking the first simultaneous nationwide in-store stock since launch. Units are in-store only at the normal $300 price; online sales remain limited to bundles shipping in September.

The lecture introduces plasma self-emission as a diagnostic tool, covering radiation across frequencies from radio waves to X-rays and gamma rays. Radiation can cool plasmas but also provides information about plasma conditions through its spectrum, location, and time variation.

Radiation transport is described as non-local energy transport involving emission, absorption, and re-emission. The radiation transport equation relates changes in spectral radiance along a path to emissivity and opacity. Optical depth is introduced to distinguish optically thin systems, where radiation passes through with little absorption, from optically thick systems, where radiation is strongly absorbed and approaches blackbody behavior. Kirchhoff’s law links emissivity and opacity, showing that strongly emitting regions also strongly absorb.

The lecture contrasts optical thickness with wave cutoffs: optical thickness involves gradual absorption, while cutoffs involve reflection and evanescent decay when the refractive index prevents propagation. It then begins discussing radiation from free charges, explaining qualitatively that stationary or uniformly moving charges do not radiate, while accelerating charges do. The full single-charge radiation expression includes near-field and far-field terms; only the far-field term represents propagating radiation. Applying this to plasmas requires solving particle motion and integrating over the velocity distribution, though those derivations are deferred.

The speaker said the team started well with strong transition play but made mistakes that led to goals and lost momentum. They aim to move past the last two games, improve offensive net presence and screens, and rely on home-ice energy in the remaining best-of-three Stanley Cup series. Boston was credited for smart defensive play, and Thomas was praised for strong goaltending. The speaker expressed confidence in Luongo, said officiating concerns involving scrums and Thomas’ contact were discussed with the NHL, and noted the ice conditions were the same for both teams.

MMFP-Tableau is a health data integration and visualization platform developed by the Mitochondrial Medicine Frontier Program at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia to support precision medicine and research in primary mitochondrial disease. It extracts, cleans, harmonizes, and integrates clinical and research data from EPIC/Clarity, REDCap, Excel files, surveys, laboratory specimen records, and other sources using Alteryx, then presents modeled data through secure Tableau dashboards.

The platform includes data from over 2,000 individuals evaluated clinically or enrolled in research. It supports role-based access to identifiable or de-identified data, real-time updates, customizable filters, cohort and patient-level views, and analysis of phenotypes, genotypes, laboratory results, medications, hospitalizations, patient-reported outcomes, and biospecimen information. Human Phenotype Ontology and diagnostic code mapping are used to standardize phenotypic data.

Reported use cases include clinical cohort characterization, clinical trial eligibility assessment, genotype-phenotype mapping, medication trend visualization, and risk factor analysis. The platform has reduced reliance on manual chart review, improved data accessibility, supported research recruitment and trial design, and influenced more structured clinical documentation.

Limitations include incomplete access to some non-discretized EMR data, certain imaging data, scanned PDFs, and externally sourced EMR data, as well as server performance issues from large live data volumes. The authors describe MMFP-Tableau as scalable and adaptable for other cohorts and disease areas.

The Trump administration has not implemented the 100% pharmaceutical tariffs threatened for Oct. 1. A White House official said it will “begin preparing” tariffs on companies that do not build in the U.S. or make a drug pricing agreement, with no new timeline provided.

House of Fraser reported pre-tax profits rising from £1.3 million to £3.4 million, with flat revenues of £1.3 billion and like-for-like sales up 0.9%. Online sales rose 16.1%. The retailer warned trading remains volatile, will discontinue five under-performing brands, and recently opened its first standalone shop in China.

The head and shoulders pattern is a technical chart formation used to identify potential price reversals. It consists of three swing highs, with the middle “head” higher than the two “shoulders,” and a neckline connecting the intervening lows. It is considered a bearish reversal pattern confirmed when price breaks below the neckline. The inverse head and shoulders has three swing lows, with the middle low deepest, and is considered a bullish reversal confirmed when price breaks above the neckline.

The passage states that the pattern is difficult to quantify and backtest objectively. It relies mainly on Thomas Bulkowski’s historical research, which found the head and shoulders pattern had a 93% success rate in a sample of 431 cases, with an average price decline of 23%. Bulkowski also found inverse head and shoulders formations had few false signals and notable profit potential. He concluded volume and neckline direction had limited significance, though inverse neckline breaks should occur on large volume.

The article urges caution because Bulkowski’s work used after-the-fact analysis, and the authors were unable to create a fully quantified head and shoulders trading strategy.

Blackwell introduces a ninth-generation NVENC encoder with 5% AV1 and HEVC quality improvements, 4:2:2 H.264/HEVC encoding, and AV1 Ultra High Quality mode. RTX 5090 supports up to three encoders and two decoders, while sixth-generation NVDEC adds faster H.264 decoding and 4:2:2 decode support. Blackwell also supports DisplayPort 2.1b UHBR 20.

Max-Q improvements include advanced power, clock, rail, and memory gating; accelerated frequency switching 1000x faster than previous architectures; and low-latency sleep that enters the deepest sleep state 10x faster than Ada. DLSS 4 adds Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three frames per rendered frame, with a faster, lower-memory AI model and enhanced frame pacing. It also introduces transformer models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA to improve stability, lighting detail, and motion detail.

Blackwell expands neural rendering through neural shaders, Cooperative Vectors for DX12 and Vulkan, and features such as RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Neural Texture Compression reduces memory use in one demo from 1110 MB to 333 MB.

The passage also describes Blackwell GPU products and chips, including GB202 for RTX 5090, GB203 for RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti, and GB205 for RTX 5070, along with legal disclaimers and trademark notices.

Around 125 people attended Newtongrange town centre masterplan sessions held by LDA on September 1 and 2. Feedback will inform design work by the masterplan team, Midlothian Council and Borders Railway Blueprint Partnership ahead of further community engagement later in the year.

Calvin Alexander, a seventh grader from Caddo Middle Magnet, won the Northwest Louisiana regional spelling bee for the second consecutive year with “nectarivorous.” The LSUS and KTBS-sponsored competition took place March 17 on the LSUS campus, included 22 spellers, and lasted 20 rounds. Alexander defeated Rosetta Schultz of Ruston Junior High after four final rounds and will advance to the 2018 Scripps National Spelling Bee near Washington, D.C., May 29-31. He also won an expenses-paid trip and prizes including a U.S. Mint Proof Set and online subscriptions from Britannica and Merriam-Webster.

The passage outlines defensive methods for countering the Base Cross offense, which is difficult to defend due to inside play, ball reversal, and down screens. Key fundamentals include defending dribble clears, low post play, and down screens. Two strategies are described: Basic NBA Show & Recover and All Out SOS Disruption. Show & Recover has the defender step out to force the post wide, allow recovery over the screen, and pack weakside defenders into help positions. SOS Disruption traps the ball handler before the post entry, uses a Hi-Lo Switch on base screens, rotates on passes out of traps, and applies team SOS principles with help, denial, and closeout responsibilities.

The OECD warned that signs of overheating are emerging in Ireland’s economy, citing sharp rises in new mortgage lending and loans to small firms, largely linked to construction. It said Central Bank lending restrictions may need to be extended to curb credit growth and warned of the risk of another property bubble if house prices continue rising at 13 percent annually. The warning followed data showing mortgage approvals rose 20 percent in April and a Central Bank study highlighting possible defaults among pre-crash mortgages during a financial shock. The OECD said Ireland’s economy should remain robust near term but urged stronger fiscal buffers against shocks, especially Brexit. Amid Italian political turmoil, NTMA chief Conor O’Kelly said stable Irish bond yields showed investors now view Ireland closer to the euro-zone core. European Commission officials also said housing supply shortages are driving Irish property price increases.

The DuBard School for Language Disorders at the University of Southern Mississippi was one of four U.S. schools recognized by IMSLEC for its use of multisensory structured language education. Its DuBard Association Method, accredited since 1998, is used daily and taught nationally through the school.

ExxonMobil launched a major marketing push in Dongying, China, to court independent “teapot” refiners, which have become significant crude buyers since receiving import licenses in 2015. The company sent traders, marketers and finance staff to a petrochemical trade exhibition, hosted events for potential customers and held private meetings. Exxon said the effort reflects the growing importance of China’s independent refiners, not politics, despite U.S.-China trade tensions and discussions about U.S. energy sales. China’s teapots buy about one-fifth of the country’s crude imports, with many based in Shandong. Exxon faces competition from earlier entrants including BP, Shell, Vitol, Trafigura and Mercuria, and local executives said Exxon is strong in global supply but less familiar with the local market.

The paper introduces automatic detection of “hype” language in biomedical research texts as an NLP task. Hype is defined as hyperbolic or subjective language used to promote, embellish, or exaggerate aspects of research. Prior work identified 140 potentially promotional adjectives in NIH grant abstracts, but context determines whether a term is hype.

The authors focus on 11 novelty-related adjectives from NIH grant application abstracts from 2016–2020 and create a dataset of 550 sampled sentences. They develop annotation guidelines based on value judgment, hyperbole, gratuitous use, amplification, coordination with other hype terms, and broader promotional context. Three researchers annotated the data; after discussion, 537 sentences remained, with 392 labeled Hype and 145 Not Hype. Hyperbolic adjectives such as groundbreaking, revolutionary, unparalleled, and unprecedented were always labeled hype.

The authors frame hype detection as text classification and test traditional classifiers, fine-tuned language models, and large language models. Fine-tuned BERT achieved the best reported performance, exceeding the human baseline, while traditional methods and frozen pretrained models performed worse. GPT-4O-MINI performed similarly to the human baseline, while LLAMA3.1-INSTRUCT performed poorly. The study concludes that formal annotation guidelines help humans annotate hype reliably and that trained NLP models show promise, while noting challenges related to subjectivity, domain knowledge, temporal context, limited dataset size, English-only biomedical focus, and computational constraints.

The passage discusses the difficulty of giving career advice to adult children, using an example of a father whose 28-year-old son reacted defensively to guidance about a job problem. Ruth Nemzoff advises parents to consider their own biases, understand each child’s communication style and circumstances, and account for changing workplace contexts before offering advice. She recommends asking whether the child wants advice or only to vent, beginning with curious questions, acknowledging the parent’s limited knowledge of the situation, and sharing personal career mistakes. Parents should help adult children identify next steps, suggest objective third-party guidance when useful, and avoid expecting their advice to be followed.

Sandvik beat first-quarter operating profit expectations, led by strong performance in its metal-cutting tools business, though weaker-than-expected mining gear results weighed on shares. Operating profit rose to 4.27 billion Swedish crowns, above forecasts, while order intake reached 25.4 billion crowns. CEO Bjorn Rosengren said mining profitability needed improvement.

Future Market Insights projects the global bioprocessing analytics equipment market to register a 4.5% CAGR from 2018 to 2028. The market is segmented by product type, application, end user, and region. Osmometers are expected to lead by product type, while industrial applications are projected to dominate with a 4.4% CAGR. Biopharmaceutical companies are the largest end users, with demand expected to grow at 3.9%. North America is estimated to dominate the market by revenue share in 2018, while Western Europe and APECJ together are expected to hold 39.2% share. APECJ revenue is projected to grow at 5.9%.

Nike’s Considered strategy aimed to integrate sustainability into product design and core business processes rather than treat corporate responsibility as a separate staff function. The Air Jordan XX3, launched in January 2008, was an early high-performance example, using recycled sneaker content and reduced solvents.

Nike’s sustainability concerns were shaped by its large global supply chain, dependence on oil and fossil fuels, waste, toxic materials, water use, and lessons from its 1990s labor crisis, when denial of responsibility for contract factory conditions damaged the company. Under Corporate Responsibility VP Hannah Jones and CEO Mark Parker, Nike reframed corporate responsibility around business value, collaboration, and “ROI2,” linking financial and social/environmental returns.

In 2005 Nike created the Considered Group to spread sustainable design practices across product teams. The group developed the Considered Index, introduced in 2007, to help footwear teams score products on environmentally preferred materials, solvent use, waste, and innovation. Products could earn Bronze, Silver, or Gold ratings, with Silver and Gold considered “Considered.” Nike committed that all footwear would meet a minimum Considered standard by Spring 2011.

Core Performance, Nike’s largest footwear category by volume, successfully embedded Considered into briefs, reviews, materials sourcing, and factory engagement. Its Spring 2009 line largely achieved Silver ratings, and the Dual D Hoop became a Gold-rated shoe by reducing tooling, solvents, and waste while staying on time and budget.

Implementation challenges included performance and aesthetic limits of some environmentally preferred materials, added design complexity, time pressures, margin impacts, uneven factory capabilities, supplier hesitation, retailer priorities, and uncertainty about consumer willingness to value or pay for sustainability. Some categories adopted Considered more effectively than others.

Nike had baseline data on waste, solvents, energy, greenhouse gases, and materials impacts, but in mid-2008 had limited data on Considered’s actual business and environmental results. Competitors including Timberland, Adidas, and Brooks were also pursuing greener products. The passage introduces a study on automated chest X-ray classification for pneumonia and tuberculosis, emphasizing their global health burden, risks of misdiagnosis, and need for reliable diagnostic tools. It reviews AI and deep learning methods, especially CNNs, for medical image analysis and notes their use in detecting lung diseases from chest radiographs. Existing studies report high performance for pneumonia, TB, and COVID-19 detection, but many are limited by binary classification, small or imbalanced datasets, dataset overlap, poor generalizability, computational complexity, overfitting risks, and failure to handle anomalous or non-X-ray inputs. The proposed study introduces a pretrained CNN-based multi-class framework classifying images as normal, pneumonia, tuberculosis, or non-X-ray to improve robustness in real-world clinical settings. The study uses anonymized, publicly available data, required no additional ethical approval, followed the Declaration of Helsinki, and received no funding.

Hounds of the Bay is a stock-picking strategy selecting the highest dividend-paying stocks in Canada’s S&P/TSX 60, named after Toronto’s Bay Street. Limited backtest data and academic research suggest it has historically worked, though its effect has diminished in recent decades.

The passage presents a theoretical study of chlorothalonil (CLT) adsorption on single-walled carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs) with (8,0), (10,0), and (12,0) chiralities. CLT is described as a toxic, persistent fungicide and pollutant, motivating research into nanotube-based removal and sensing.

The study used density functional theory, semi-empirical screening, periodic and non-periodic nanotube models, charge and electronic-structure analyses, and molecular dynamics simulations in water. The most stable adsorption geometry placed the CLT aromatic ring parallel to the nanotube surface, indicating physical adsorption rather than chemical bonding.

Adsorption became stronger as nanotube radius increased for both CNTs and BNNTs. CNTs showed stronger adsorption than BNNTs, especially for the (12,0) CNT, but increasing CNT radius also greatly increased recovery time, making larger CNTs less suitable for reversible sensing. BNNTs showed lower adsorption energies and shorter recovery times, supporting reusability.

CLT adsorption caused only small band-gap and work-function changes in CNTs, suggesting poor electronic sensing performance. In contrast, BNNTs showed large band-gap reductions, conductivity changes, and stronger electronic sensitivity due to new defect levels in the band gap. Work-function sensitivity in BNNTs decreased with increasing radius, indicating that BNNT diameter must be controlled for such applications.

Electronic analyses indicated charge transfer from nanotubes to CLT. CNT interactions were attributed to stronger π-π stacking due to greater polarizability and more distributed π-electron density, while BNNTs showed weaker adsorption but larger electronic perturbation. Molecular dynamics confirmed stable adsorption of CLT on both nanotubes in aqueous solution, with CLT remaining parallel to the tube surface.

The authors conclude that both CNTs and BNNTs can remove CLT, but BNNTs are more suitable for CLT detection and removal because they combine reversible adsorption with significant electronic response. The interaction is expected to remain physisorption even for larger nanotubes.
