The lecture discusses running dynamics using the spring-loaded inverted pendulum (SLIP) model, a point mass on a massless spring leg. The model has stance and flight phases, with polar coordinates during stance and Cartesian coordinates during flight. Under assumptions of a massless leg and toe, an ideal lossless spring, no drag, and instantaneous leg placement at a fixed touchdown angle, the system is conservative.

The lecturer argues that the SLIP model is biologically plausible through comparative biomechanics. Animals with very different sizes and gaits, including cockroaches, horses, crabs, humans, and kangaroos, show dynamic similarity when described with nondimensional quantities. Relative leg spring constants across species also appear similar, supporting the use of spring-based models for running. Tendons and other passive structures in animals can store and release energy, improving locomotion efficiency.

A key analysis goal is reducing the SLIP dynamics to a one-dimensional apex-to-apex return map. By choosing the apex of flight as the surface of section, horizontal position is ignored, vertical velocity is zero, and horizontal velocity can be determined from energy and apex height. The trajectory is mapped through apex, touchdown, stance, takeoff, and the next apex. The stance phase requires solving nonlinear dynamics; with small-angle and small-displacement approximations, a closed-form return map can be obtained. This map shows stable and unstable fixed points, demonstrating passive stability in a conservative, piecewise holonomic system.

The lecture also covers extensions with toe mass, where ground impact causes energy loss and added energy is needed through spring control. Raibert hopper robots are presented as examples of spring-based running machines capable of robust hopping, running, flips, stairs, and quadrupedal motion. Cockroach experiments show rapid recovery from perturbations, suggesting passive “preflex” responses from musculoskeletal compliance rather than neural control. The lecture ends by discussing SLIP walkers and transitions between walking and running, noting that humans naturally switch gait near the point where running becomes less costly than walking.

Nathan Johan Gallagher, 29, of Wrexham, gave police a false name after being stopped driving on Bellevue Road on August 8. Officers later found a bank card with his real name and discovered he had been disqualified since a 2004 dangerous driving offence and had not taken the required extended retest. He was found guilty of driving while disqualified and obstructing police, and admitted driving without a valid licence and insurance. Wrexham magistrates gave him a 12-week suspended sentence, a £50 fine, a 15-day rehabilitation requirement, a further 12-month driving ban, £250 costs and a £115 victim surcharge.

Political leaders honored the Rev. Billy Graham as he lay in honor in the U.S. Capitol Rotunda before his funeral in Charlotte, North Carolina. House Speaker Paul Ryan, President Donald Trump and Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell praised Graham’s decades of ministry to presidents, lawmakers and the public. Graham, who died at 99, had met every president since Harry Truman and counseled many of them, though he became wary of politics after Watergate. Former Presidents Bill Clinton and George W. Bush visited Graham’s home before the Washington tribute. Graham is the fourth private person to lie in honor in the Rotunda since 1998. Trump was scheduled to attend the funeral, while no former presidents were expected to attend.

State-owned oil marketing companies’ shares fell after reports that BPCL and IOC may each buy about 26% of the government’s stake in GAIL, requiring around Rs19,500 crore each. Investors are concerned about limited synergies, balance-sheet strain, and the deal mainly aiding government disinvestment. OMC stocks have already underperformed amid pressure on marketing margins, though margins have recently recovered to about Rs3.5 per litre. Future margins may depend on crude prices and election-related limits on fuel price increases. March-quarter earnings expectations are positive due to improved marketing and refining margins and possible inventory gains, but a GAIL stake purchase could hurt investor sentiment.

Infinium Global Research’s report analyzes the global aerosol valves market by application and region, covering trends, growth prospects, drivers, restraints, opportunities, forecasts, and competitive dynamics for 2017–2023. The market is expected to grow at a CAGR of 6% during the forecast period. Application segments include automotive and industrial, household, personal care, foods, paints, medical, and others. Regional coverage includes North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Rest of the World, with country-level analysis for major markets. The U.S. leads North America, while Asia-Pacific shows substantial growth potential due to India and China. The report profiles Aptar Group, Aroma Industries, Ehrensperger AG, EC Pack Industrial Ltd., Newman-Green Inc., Mitani Valve Co. Ltd, Lindal Group, Coster Group, DS Containers, and Precision Valve Corporation. It includes Porter’s five forces, DRO analysis, IGR-Growth Matrix, demand forecasts, market trends, and competitive market share analysis.

Budget Blinds Serving Bothell, based in Bothell, Washington, offers custom window covering services including blinds, shades, shutters, draperies, roller blinds, and roller shades. The company says its professionals help clients choose options suited to their windows, homes, needs, and budgets. It promotes fast, quality installation, low-cost products, and value for money. Contact details include an address on Bothell Everett Highway, a phone number, Yelp review URL, and website.

A child accidentally jabbed himself with a syringe while playing in a wooded area near Quentin Pool in Coventry. His family fears possible infection and is awaiting blood test results. His aunt urged the council to clear the area, where drug paraphernalia has been found.

This study estimated monthly SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence among pregnant women attending first antenatal care visits in four Zambian districts from September 2021 to September 2022, spanning the Omicron wave and early COVID-19 vaccine rollout. Repeated cross-sectional surveys enrolled 9,221 women; 8,304 valid antibody results were linked to questionnaires. Overall, 63.8% were SARS-CoV-2 seropositive. Seroprevalence was highest in Lusaka and lowest in Chadiza, rising to about 100% in Lusaka and near 100% in Chipata and Chongwe by August 2022, while Chadiza peaked at 77.2% in April 2022 and declined by July.

Most antibody responses appeared infection-induced rather than vaccine-induced. COVID-19 vaccination coverage among participants rose from 4.4% to 26.6%, and vaccination was associated with higher odds of seropositivity in all districts. Hybrid infection and vaccination responses produced higher receptor-binding domain signal ratios than infection or vaccination alone. Reported prior COVID-19 was uncommon, and estimated SARS-CoV-2 exposures greatly exceeded reported cases, with seroprevalence-to-cumulative-incidence ratios ranging from 29:1 to 92:1 across districts.

The authors conclude that SARS-CoV-2 exposure was widespread among first antenatal care attendees in Zambia, with geographic variation and mostly infection-induced antibodies. They note that antenatal care platforms can support serosurveillance and may be useful for monitoring population immunity and future epidemic responses.

The passage describes a rotation strategy that switches monthly between the S&P 500 and gold using the gold/S&P 500 ratio and its 20-month moving average. When the ratio is above the moving average, the strategy holds the S&P 500 for the next month; when below, it holds gold. Tested from 1985 to July 2020 using monthly spot gold and Yahoo Finance S&P 500 data, the strategy produced a 9.9% CAGR and a 22% maximum drawdown, compared with a 55% maximum drawdown for the S&P 500. It underperformed the S&P 500 until the 2008/09 financial crisis but benefited from lower drawdowns during that period and compounded from a higher base afterward. Gains from gold and the S&P 500 were described as roughly equal. The passage notes that dividends were not included, which underrates both S&P 500 buy-and-hold performance and the strategy’s results, and that only the 20-month moving average was tested.

The global activated alumina market serves industries including oil & gas, plastics, water treatment, and healthcare. Asia Pacific holds a major share and is expected to lead due to industrialization, population-driven demand for clean water, and oil & gas growth in India and China. North America is expected to retain dominance, supported by developed end-use industries and shale gas activity. Europe is projected to grow steadily, driven by healthcare uses such as bone and dental replacements. Market segments include catalysts, desiccants, fluoride adsorbents, bioceramics, and end-use industries. Prominent players include BASF, Honeywell, Sumitomo Chemical, Porocel, and Dynamic Adsorbents.

PointState Capital LP bought 6,057,459 shares of Peabody Energy Corporation in the second quarter, valued at about $148.1 million, making it 1.6% of its portfolio and its 23rd largest holding. Other hedge funds also initiated positions, and institutional investors own 97.98% of the company. Discovery Capital Management sold 12.8 million shares for $346.88 million. Analysts have given Peabody an average “Buy” rating with a $35 target price. Peabody shares traded at $29.59, with a market cap of $2.97 billion. The company reported a quarterly loss of $0.18 per share, missing estimates, while revenue rose 21% year over year to $1.26 billion.

Saks Fifth Avenue is marking the 10th anniversary of its 10022-SHOE salon, launched in 2007 at its New York flagship. Executives Tracy Margolies, Marc Metrick and Betty Wang said the concept made shoes a retail destination, emphasized exclusive assortments and helped spotlight emerging designers. Saks will celebrate with more than 75 exclusive styles from designers including Christian Louboutin, Sergio Rossi, Aquazzura and Nicholas Kirkwood, along with store installations, themed windows and made-to-order customization programs from brands such as Manolo Blahnik, Fendi and Jimmy Choo. Since its debut, 10022-SHOE has expanded to 25 locations, including a 14,000-square-foot stand-alone store in Greenwich, Connecticut. The New York flagship’s shoe floor spans about 30,000 square feet and can hold 200,000 pairs.

This study evaluated the clinical relevance of circulating tumor cell (CTC) genomic variation in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). Whole-exome sequencing was performed on CTC pools and matched PBMC controls from 29 mCRC patients, with downstream analyses restricted to 28 microsatellite-stable cases. The study measured multiple genomic diversity metrics, including mutational burden, proportion of aberrant genome, MATH score, CRC driver mutations, copy number alterations, and recurrent driver gene mutation status.

CTC pools showed substantial genomic variation across patients, including mutations in CRC driver genes and widespread copy number alterations. Higher binary MATH scores and non-silent BCL9L mutations were significantly associated with poorer overall survival in multivariate analysis. Patients with high bMATH had a median survival of 18.3 months versus 52.9 months for low bMATH, while patients with BCL9L mutations had a median survival of 14.5 months versus 34.2 months for those without mutations. A custom 55-gene panel produced MATH scores correlated with whole-exome sequencing and also predicted worse survival, while tested commercial panels did not. The authors conclude that CTC genomic diversity may serve as a prognostic tool in mCRC, though larger cohorts are needed for validation.

Kerala has directed state and affiliated universities to reserve two seats for transgender students in undergraduate and postgraduate Arts and Sciences courses, subject to qualifications, and prevent discrimination. The move aims to reduce dropouts caused by social pressure. Activists welcomed it. The state has also launched education and shelter initiatives for transgender persons, amid survey findings of high school dropout rates linked to harassment, bullying, accommodation denial and financial exclusion.

BerkeleyGW advances exascale quantum many-body materials simulations with performance portability across AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA GPU architectures. The work optimizes GW and GW perturbation theory calculations for quasiparticle excitations and correlated electron-phonon coupling, addressing computational bottlenecks in large heterogeneous quantum materials such as defects and moiré systems.

Key innovations include directive-based OpenACC/OpenMP portability, hardware-optimized HIP, SYCL, and CUDA kernels, a fast full-frequency GW method using static subspace approximation, a mixed stochastic-deterministic pseudobands approach to reduce scaling, and optimized diagonal and off-diagonal GPP self-energy kernels. The off-diagonal formulation recasts major computations into dense matrix multiplications for higher arithmetic intensity.

Benchmarks on Frontier, Aurora, and Perlmutter show strong and weak scaling to nearly full systems. BerkeleyGW achieved 1.069 ExaFLOP/s on Frontier and 707.52 PetaFLOP/s on Aurora for optimized off-diagonal GPP kernels, reaching 59.45% and 48.79% of theoretical or attainable peak performance, respectively. Applications include silicon divacancy systems up to 2,742 atoms, lithium hydride defects up to 17,574 atoms, BN moiré bilayers, and GWPT calculations for electron-phonon coupling.

Wall Street and global stock markets reached fresh highs as optimism over U.S. tax reform and global growth lifted investor sentiment. The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq posted record closes for a fourth straight day, while MSCI’s global equity index also hit a record. The dollar rose after data showed a smaller U.S. trade deficit and lower-than-expected jobless claims, reinforcing expectations of a Federal Reserve rate increase. Gold fell, and Philadelphia Fed President Patrick Harker said he expected one more rate hike in 2017 and three in 2018. Oil prices gained as expectations that Saudi Arabia and Russia would limit production outweighed record U.S. exports and renewed Libyan output.

ASP validates protected DRAM access, verifies customer and AMD signatures, loads and runs the patch, updates patch level information, and returns status. The ASP interface can report base firmware and patch levels using GET_SFS_VERSION_INFO with two 4096-byte pages. SFS update commands load, verify, and execute packages without applying updates until validation completes. Packages align to AGESA releases, use version-specific applicability, and follow names like fam_<family>-<AGESA-Release>-SFS-<n>.pkg. Updates run alongside x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact; some operations may require limited quiescing, such as stopping and restarting SEV or SEV/ES virtual machines for SEV firmware updates.

A federal judge ordered Alabama to release records about its lethal injection protocol after news organizations sought access following the aborted execution of Doyle Lee Hamm. The state may keep some security-related information secret, such as names of low-level prison employees. The judge said the records could help the public understand whether similar execution problems might recur or be avoided.

Mr. Otori sought a Korean council to consider Japanese proposals and demanded its appointment within three days. On John M. B. Sill’s advice, Korea allowed a council only to listen and report, then replied that although some proposals matched Korea’s reform policy, they could not be accepted under Japanese military occupation. The King appointed a separate reform council, which began abolishing needless taxes. Foreign representatives discussed neutrality for Chemulpo; China consented, while Japan’s conditions effectively prevented it. Russian representative Mr. Waeber returned, and U.S. vessels Monocacy and reportedly Baltimore arrived at Chemulpo. Chinese residents and merchants were leaving, and Ye Cha-yun was appointed to a senior foreign office post. Separately, Acting Consul-General C. T. Gardner reported that Japanese soldiers assaulted him, stopped his party, and pushed Mrs. Gardner’s chair into a ditch. Mr. Otori said he would investigate, then forwarded General Oshima’s report denying the alleged assault, obstruction, and mistreatment of any lady, stating instead that foreigners ignored a sentinel and entered a Japanese bivouac.

Toronto police say 26-year-old Nnamdi Ogba was fatally shot Friday night while walking to his car after visiting friends at a Toronto Community Housing complex. Det. Jason Shankaran said two men approached from behind, opened fire, and fled in a waiting SUV, believed to be a newer model Nissan Rogue. Police believe Ogba, an engaged electrical engineer with no criminal record or gang ties, did not know his attackers and was an innocent victim of a retaliatory attack intended to intimidate the Scarlettwood Court community. Investigators released security footage and urged residents to help identify the suspects.

A federal judge in Newark temporarily halted deportation proceedings against Indonesian Christians in the U.S. illegally who are seeking legal status, applying to those with removal orders before 2009. The order, issued in response to an ACLU lawsuit, affects about 50 people in New Jersey who had identified themselves to ICE in 2009 for work authorization and deportation stays. The lawsuit followed recent immigration enforcement actions targeting Indonesian Christians, including arrests after two men dropped children at school. Several men, including Harry Pangemanan, Arthur Jemmy and Yohanes Tasik, sought sanctuary at the Reformed Church of Highland Park. Pangemanan, who helped organize Superstorm Sandy rebuilding volunteers, said he and others fear returning to Indonesia because of past persecution of Christians. Judge Esther Salas ordered both sides to file briefs over the next month.

A coach said an injured player is fine and expected to be in the lineup. He said the team’s power play started well but lost focus and struggled with passing under the Devils’ pressure, while the penalty kill performed well. He said the team did not play well enough to win, despite doing some good things, and must refocus for the next game. He emphasized discipline, composure, avoiding retaliation penalties, and not using Forsberg’s absence as an excuse. He noted both teams defended well, limiting chances and space, and said momentum, mental mistakes, and discipline will be key. He also said officials missed high-stick incidents on both sides because the plays happened quickly. The team is approaching the road games positively.

The paper introduces ABXLAB, an open-source man-in-the-middle framework for studying how large language model agents make decisions in realistic web environments. ABXLAB intercepts and modifies web content in real time, enabling controlled manipulation of choice architecture without building custom environments.

The study evaluates LLM agents in an online shopping setting using binary product choices. Product pairs are constrained by category, price, and rating similarity, with additional matched-rating and matched-rating-and-price conditions. Interventions include authority cues, social proof, scarcity, negative framing, and incentives. The authors ran over 80,000 experiments across 17 state-of-the-art models, using more than 2.5 billion tokens and about 400,000 requests. Human baseline data were also collected for the original condition.

Results show that LLM agents exhibit strong systematic sensitivity to ratings, prices, order effects, and nudges, often far exceeding human responses. Higher ratings increased selection probability by 30–80 percentage points for most models. Cheaper prices also strongly influenced choices, especially when ratings were matched. Order effects were heterogeneous but sometimes near-deterministic. Nudges shifted choices by 10–60 percentage points on average when ratings and prices were matched, with Wirecutter-style authority cues, “Buy 1 Get 1 Free,” and “best seller” among the strongest. Humans showed much smaller effects across the same cues.

User profile experiments found that explicit preferences acted like categorical switches: declared priorities such as valuing ratings, price, or expert recommendations dominated agent decisions and suppressed competing attributes.

The authors conclude that current LLM agents are highly susceptible to superficial cues and brittle decision heuristics. They present ABXLAB as a foundation for reproducible behavioral science of AI agents, while noting limitations including the binary-choice setup, controlled textual nudges, focus on consumer behavior, and use of contemporary models.

First Solar, a photovoltaic manufacturer using proprietary thin-film cadmium telluride technology, had long been a low-cost industry leader and in 2009 became the first PV manufacturer to produce panels below $1.00 per watt. By 2011, however, it reported a $39 million net operating loss, slowing revenue growth, and a major fourth-quarter loss amid declining solar prices, reduced European subsidies, weaker project financing after the financial crisis, and rising competition from Chinese crystalline-silicon manufacturers.

The PV market included residential, commercial, and utility segments, with utilities expected to grow fastest. Customer priorities varied, but levelized cost of electricity, installation costs, watts per area, reliability, and vendor track record were important. First Solar initially sold mostly to European system integrators but later expanded into high-sunshine, less subsidy-dependent markets and vertically integrated into systems through acquisitions. Its systems business grew from 5% of sales in 2009 to 25% in 2011, while increasing SG&A expenses.

First Solar manufactured in Ohio, Germany, and Malaysia, with Malaysian plants having the lowest production costs. It operated below capacity in 2011 due to competition. Its manufacturing cost per watt remained lower than SunPower, Suntech, and Yingli, but falling silicon prices benefited crystalline-silicon rivals. Chinese producers, supported by government programs and lower costs, expanded rapidly to nearly 60% of global PV panel production by 2012, contributing to oversupply and price pressure. Several U.S. solar manufacturers, including Evergreen Solar, SpectraWatt, and Solyndra, filed for bankruptcy in 2011.

First Solar maintained a conservative financial strategy with less debt and more cash than competitors. Facing eroding cost advantages, oversupply, subsidy reductions, and Chinese competition, senior vice president Tymen deJong prepared to assess whether First Solar’s advantages remained sustainable and whether its systems business, market focus, and strategy should change.

The passage describes DAWn-plasma study procedures for viral qPCR nasopharyngeal swabs at screening and day +6. Routine analysis is performed locally, while remaining swab material should be stored at 4°C for up to 24 hours with minimal room-temperature exposure, then frozen at -80°C preferably or -20°C until batch transport to the central Leuven laboratory for later quantitative PCR analysis. It also lists related DAWn-plasma publications, a convalescent plasma meta-analysis, a treatment benefit index validation study, and contents including figures on mechanical ventilation, biomarkers, temperature, and neutralizing antibody titers, plus tables on protocol violations, exclusions, baseline characteristics, therapies, endpoints, adverse events, and transfusion-related side effects.

Alan Oppenheim demonstrates sampling, aliasing, and properties of discrete-time linear systems using a programmable digital filter. The system samples a continuous-time input, applies a digital filter, converts the result back to continuous time, and smooths it with a low-pass filter. With the digital filter set to identity, sampling produces periodic spectral replicas; if the input bandwidth is too high relative to the sampling frequency, aliasing occurs. A sinusoidal input shows output frequency increasing until half the sampling frequency, then decreasing due to aliasing, with beating near the transition because the smoothing filter is not ideal.

The lecture then inserts a linear-phase digital low-pass filter with cutoff frequency π/5, equal to one tenth of 2π. The equivalent continuous-time filter has the same response shape but with frequency scaled by the sampling period, making its cutoff one tenth of the sampling frequency. Demonstrations show the filter impulse response, DAC boxcar output smoothing, sinusoidal frequency sweeps, periodic digital frequency response, and how changing sampling rate changes effective analog cutoff. Audio examples illustrate the narrowing bandwidth as sampling frequency decreases.

The message reports an eventful year marked by national prosperity, a financial crisis, reduced political partisanship in agricultural regions, and the seizure of the U.S.-registered steamer Virginius by Spanish forces. Relations with most foreign powers remained friendly. The United States participated in the Vienna exposition, where American exhibitors received awards, and joined discussions on protecting inventions. The message notes diplomatic developments in China, limited progress against the Chinese cooly trade, and recommends further legislation on that subject.

The Geneva arbitration award was paid by Britain and placed in the Treasury, with a recommendation to create a commission to audit direct losses from Confederate cruisers. Boundary work with British possessions progressed, including the northwest water boundary and surveys west of the Lake of the Woods. A mixed U.S.-British claims commission awarded Britain $1,929,819 and dismissed most other claims; an appropriation is recommended. The message also addresses neutrality in the Netherlands-Acheen war, the Mexican claims commission, Texas border forays, Venezuelan obligations, proposed changes to consular judicial authority in Ottoman and Egyptian territories, Santo Domingo’s request for a protectorate, and recent treaties.

The President urges Congress to clarify expatriation, nationality, the status of American women marrying foreigners, and children born abroad to American parents. On Spain and Cuba, the message praises reforms in Porto Rico and Cuba but says slavery and reactionary forces in Cuba remain central problems. It details the seizure of the Virginius, the execution of 53 passengers and crew, U.S. demands for restoration, surrender of survivors, reparation, punishment, and indemnity, and Spain’s agreement to those terms. The Navy was put on a war footing during the crisis.

The message suggests constitutional amendments allowing the President to approve parts of bills while vetoing others and limiting legislation in extra sessions to subjects submitted by the Executive. Treasury receipts exceeded expenditures in the previous fiscal year, but declining revenue after the financial panic prompted calls for economy. The President discusses currency elasticity, specie payments, national banking reforms, clearing houses, limits on bank interest on deposits, and possible note issuance backed by bonds. He also recommends tariff codification, more mints, attention to shipbuilding, cheap transportation, canal and river improvements, and an Amazon exploration.

War Department recommendations include strengthening seacoast armament and reopening promotions in Army staff corps. The Navy had repaired and built vessels and was preparing all available force for possible service. Postal revenues rose but expenditures rose more; recommendations include expanded free delivery, revised postage rules, postal savings depositories, and renewed consideration of postal telegraphs.

The Justice Department section calls for legislation to restore jury trials in Utah, limit probate court jurisdiction there, and repeal involuntary bankruptcy provisions tied to suspended payment. It warns of accumulating and potentially fraudulent claims against the Government, especially from the rebellion, and recommends stricter procedures. The Interior section says Indian policy will continue, with Indians gathered on reservations and taught self-support, and recommends a territorial government for Indian Territory. It reports increased land disposal, surveys, pension rolls, anti-fraud pension efforts, educational progress, and support for a possible 1875 census.

The message praises improvements in Washington, D.C., recommends federal support for District expenses, and suggests donating land for a high-class university in the capital. It renews support for civil-service reform through enforceable rules approved by Congress and the Executive. It recommends admitting Colorado as a State, encouraging an irrigation canal from the Rocky Mountains toward the Missouri River, granting general amnesty to remaining persons disabled by the rebellion, and enacting legislation to better secure the civil rights of freed people.

Week 6 college football featured major upsets and missed upset chances that reshaped conference and playoff outlooks. UCLA, previously 0-4, stunned Penn State 42-37, marking the first win by a team 0-4 or worse over a top-10 opponent since UTEP beat BYU in 1985. UCLA’s offense, led by Nico Iamaleava and newly promoted playcaller Jerry Neuheisel, produced 430-plus yards against a Penn State defense rarely beaten that badly. The loss severely hurt Penn State’s playoff and Big Ten title hopes.

Florida beat Texas 29-21 as DJ Lagway outplayed Arch Manning, throwing for 298 yards and two touchdowns against a highly rated Texas defense. Texas fell to 0-2 against stronger opponents and dropped in SP+, with a projected most likely record of 7-5.

Alabama avoided an upset against Vanderbilt, benefiting from key Diego Pavia turnovers before pulling away late. Miami defeated Florida State after the Seminoles committed three turnovers and struggled offensively after a fast start, damaging FSU’s ACC title and playoff hopes.

In the Big 12, Texas Tech remained dominant, while Cincinnati beat previously unbeaten Iowa State to enter the conference title race. SP+ ratings rose notably for teams including Florida, UCLA and Northwestern, while Penn State had the week’s biggest decline.

The passage also highlights weekly Heisman-style points, led by Alabama’s Ty Simpson, and several dramatic lower-division finishes, including buzzer-beaters, overtime games and a record 46 consecutive completions by Western Carolina’s quarterback.

Sun Waa, a Chinese takeaway in Littleover, received a food hygiene rating of one from Derby City Council after inspectors found issues including fried rice left at room temperature for six hours, an obstructed wash basin, food debris buildup, cross-contamination risks, improper cleaning methods, insect webbing and a faulty probe thermometer. The business said it had worked to improve standards, and council officers later reported significant hygiene improvements. A re-score was expected in March.

Tarren Joseph Titus, 23, of Sarnia, received three months of house arrest with only a curfew, followed by one year’s probation, after pleading guilty to hydromorphone possession and two probation violations. Police found him in 2017 in a bedroom containing the painkiller and drug paraphernalia. Justice Deborah Austin praised his “outstanding” transformation away from drug abuse. Titus must continue counselling and avoid drugs. His lawyer said he had been exposed to drug culture from a young age, while Titus said daily sobriety meetings have been part of his recovery.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K reporting that CFO Deepak Ahuja intends to retire after a brief transition period and then serve as an advisor. Tesla plans to appoint Zachary Kirkhorn, then Vice President of Finance, Financial Planning and Business Operations, as CFO. Kirkhorn joined Tesla in 2010 and contributed to major programs including Gigafactory 1, Model X, and Model 3.

Sixteen-year-old Murad Rahimov, who immigrated from Uzbekistan to the U.S. in 2010 and recently became a U.S. citizen with his family, received a private tour of NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center after an NPR listener connected him with astrophysicist Jeremy Schnittman. Murad, long passionate about space and aspiring to become an astronaut and work for NASA, toured facilities including the clean room, cryo-vac chamber, acoustic chamber and laser lab. Schnittman discussed black holes, Einstein and time travel with him, and they agreed to stay in touch. Murad, now a high school junior taking advanced classes, hopes to attend Cal Tech and one day lead a Mars mission. He also looked forward to watching the total solar eclipse from Kansas City.

Michelle Munson of NYU and Sarah Narendorf of the University of Houston study “mental health narratives” among marginalized young adults, arguing that how young people understand the causes, meaning, and management of their mental health conditions strongly affects treatment engagement and self-care. Their work focuses on young adults facing challenges such as poverty, discrimination, disabilities, young parenthood, and reliance on safety-net systems. They emphasize that providers should ask about patients’ beliefs, fears, treatment expectations, and perceived consequences of not getting help.

The researchers distinguish mental health narratives from physical illness narratives because stigma, shame, and discrimination often shape responses to psychiatric diagnoses. Their studies use in-depth interviews to understand young adults’ experiences and are continuing through projects such as “Just Do You” in Brooklyn and the Bronx. They propose training providers and developing technology-based interventions to help young adults construct useful narratives. They argue that improving care requires cultural humility, collaboration between professionals and young adults, and serious attention to patients’ own interpretations of their conditions.

Players discussed staying focused ahead of a chance to win the Stanley Cup, saying location does not matter and outside excitement will not help them achieve their goal. Jonathan Toews described the playoffs as a fast, difficult journey built on adversity and togetherness, and said the team tends to improve as series progress. Brad Richards said prior championship experience helps players prepare and focus, while Kris Versteeg called the run tough and emphasized staying ready when given an opportunity. They praised Joel’s coaching, the team’s leadership and preparation, noted the importance of health and recovery, and expected another close game against a strong Tampa Bay team.

The NRA told members that YETI had cut ties with the organization, prompting boycott calls and videos of supporters destroying YETI products. YETI responded that it had only ended outdated discount programs for the NRA Foundation and other groups while offering an alternative customization program. The company called the NRA’s statement inaccurate and said it remains committed to the Constitution and the Second Amendment.

BBC Radio 4 presenter Anita Anand was temporarily removed from Any Answers less than 24 hours before broadcast because the programme was due to discuss the BBC gender pay dispute, which she had publicly supported on social media. Julian Worricker presented instead, though Anand is expected to return next week. Critics said the decision insulted women journalists by questioning their impartiality. The move follows similar action involving Woman’s Hour host Dame Jenni Murray, who stepped aside from a BBC pay discussion after signing a letter about the gender pay gap. The BBC said editors decide case by case whether publicly campaigning presenters can cover related topics to ensure impartiality.

The passage lists folate-rich foods and their nutritional contributions. Asparagus provides 33% of the daily folate value per boiled cup and contains vitamins K, C, A, and manganese. Broccoli, cauliflower, and beetroot each provide about 14% per cup. Citrus fruits, including oranges, along with papaya, grapefruit, grapes, bananas, and strawberries, contain folate. Legumes such as beans, peas, and lentils can supply much of daily folate needs. Avocado provides 110 mcg per cup, or 28%, plus fatty acids and fibre. Lady’s finger offers 103 mcg per cooked half cup. Nuts, seeds, carrots, and corn also contribute folate.

This study benchmarks 15 two-sample Mendelian randomization methods using GWAS summary statistics and real-world genetic datasets. The evaluation covers type I error control under population stratification, pleiotropy, and family-level confounding; accuracy of causal effect estimates; replicability; power; and sensitivity to instrumental variable selection.

Across negative control analyses, MR-APSS, Egger, and Weighted-mode generally showed better type I error control, while CAUSE often produced deflated p-values and failed under strong population stratification. Many other methods showed inflated p-values, especially with population stratification and looser instrumental variable thresholds. Family-based GWAS data improved type I error control for all methods in the family-level confounding scenario.

In accuracy analyses where exposure and outcome were the same trait, MR-APSS produced estimates closest to the known causal effect of one and maintained confidence interval coverage across thresholds. Weighted-mode performed comparably at stringent thresholds, while Egger overestimated effects with looser thresholds. Many methods were biased toward the null when weaker instruments were included.

In the LDL-C and CAD case study, CAUSE and MR-APSS showed the strongest replicability across datasets and thresholds, though CAUSE p-values were inconsistent with confidence intervals. Larger GWAS sample sizes improved consistency across methods. The study recommends using negative controls, multiple IV selection standards, and multiple independent data sources when applying summary-level MR methods.

The passage profiles four female winemakers discussing women’s changing role in winemaking. Zita Kovács says she initially faced prejudice but is now treated with respect as a winemaker. Zsófi Laposa notes the profession has become more open to women due to technological development. Krisztina Csetvei balances winemaking with motherhood and named a wine after her daughter. Andi Gere co-manages her family winery and says women add elegance and variety to Hungarian wines.

New deals suggest junior mining M&A, especially in gold, may be increasing after a slow period. Hecla Mining proposed a US$462 million cash-and-share acquisition of Klondex Mines, which would add three Nevada gold mines and raise Hecla’s annual gold output to about 370,000 ounces. Alio Gold proposed a $128 million cash acquisition of Rye Patch Gold, creating a producer with an estimated 165,000 ounces of annual gold production from mines in Mexico and Nevada. Anaconda Mining also proposed acquiring Maritime Resources. Analysts and executives cited diversification, balance-sheet strength, risk management and cost of capital as factors supporting further consolidation among junior miners.

The speaker describes Detroit as the strongest opponent faced, citing its offensive firepower and elite goaltending. He emphasizes the need to play tough but clean, avoid penalties, improve power-play decisions, win faceoffs against a puck-possession team, and rebound offensively after a penalty-filled game. He praises Detroit’s Draper line, several faceoff specialists, and a highly intelligent defenseman. He says the team must ignore distractions, focus on the next finals game, and expects an excited, loud home crowd.

MSPM0C1105/6 MCUs are ultra-low-power 32-bit Arm Cortex-M0+ devices operating up to 32MHz, with up to 64KB flash and 8KB SRAM. They support -40°C to 125°C operation, 1.62V to 3.6V supply, integrated analog and digital peripherals, and multiple communication protocols. TI supports them with development kits, SDK, examples, training, and forums.

Pusa, 63, a sitting AICC member and former Nagaland minister, died leaving his wife, two sons and a daughter. He served in the SC Jamir-led Congress government, was a two-term opposition MLA, and first won as an independent in 1993. His funeral was held at his residence and burial in Viswema. Several governors, chief ministers, MPs and ministers condoled his death or attended the funeral.

The disclosure describes articles that exhibit structural color using optical elements rather than relying solely on pigments or dyes. Structural color is produced through optical effects such as scattering, refraction, reflection, interference, and diffraction. The optical element may be used alone or with a textured surface, primer layer, protective layer, polymeric layer, or combinations of these to impart colors including single-hue, multihued, iridescent, limited-iridescent, matte, glossy, or metallic appearances.

The articles may include footwear, apparel, sporting equipment, containers, electronic equipment, and vision wear. In footwear, the optical element can be disposed on or incorporated into uppers, soles, cushioning elements, bladders, foam elements, or visible components. The optical element may include one or more optical layers, such as multilayer reflectors or multilayer filters, with layer materials, refractive indices, thicknesses, and numbers selected to produce desired structural colors.

The disclosure also describes methods for measuring and characterizing structural color using CIE 1976 L*a*b*, CIELCH, and Pantone systems at different observation or illumination angles. Textured surfaces may include nano- or microscale profile features, flat areas, gratings, or other structures that affect optical behavior. Primer layers may include paints, inks, degraded polymer layers, metal layers, oxide layers, coatings, pigments, dyes, or crosslinked polymer matrices. The optical and supporting layers can be formed or applied using techniques such as vapor deposition, sputtering, chemical vapor deposition, sol-gel deposition, printing, coating, molding, stamping, or etching.

India’s state-run banks recorded a combined loss of 853.7 billion rupees in the fiscal year ended March, their highest ever, as bad-loan provisions rose after stricter Reserve Bank of India rules. Fourth-quarter losses totaled 626.81 billion rupees, with only Indian Bank and Vijaya Bank profitable. Gross non-performing loans rose 15 percent to 8.96 trillion rupees. The losses come as New Delhi plans a 2.11 trillion-rupee recapitalization of state lenders.

A Zillow analysis found that U.S. homes with central air conditioning sold for 2.5% more than comparable homes without it, a premium of nearly $5,500 for the typical home. The highest sale premiums were in San Antonio (5.8%) and Cincinnati (5.7%), with 5% or higher premiums also in Detroit, Indianapolis and Las Vegas. Air conditioning was considered required by 62% of buyers, compared with 48% who deemed private outdoor space essential. Nationally, 66.1% of homes sold in the past year had air conditioning, rising to 99.1% in Las Vegas and 97.9% in Phoenix. Rentals with central air conditioning listed on Zillow rented for 2.8% more, or about $40 more per month, with the highest rent premiums in New York, Las Vegas and Phoenix.

IWM options trading involves buying and selling call and put contracts to speculate on price movements or hedge risk. Calls give the right to buy shares at an agreed price, while puts give the right to sell. Available order types include market, limit, stop, and trailing stop orders. Common strategies include buying calls or puts, covered calls, protective puts, spreads, and technical analysis. Risks include losing the entire investment, premium costs, margin risks, and potentially unlimited risk when short calls are used. Risk management may involve stop-loss orders, limiting capital per trade, diversification, and backtesting strategies. Requirements, fees, option types, and minimum balances depend on the broker, though a margin account and sufficient funds may be needed. Investors should research the underlying asset, option contracts, strategies, technical indicators, news, and economic data before trading.

Gov. Kay Ivey announced the voluntary Alabama Sentry Program, which will train approved administrators in schools without resource officers to keep secured firearms on campus for active shooter response. Participants need training and approval from local officials. Ivey, Alabama Secretary of Law Enforcement Hal Taylor, and Superintendent Eric Mackey said the program adds school security while broader plans for more resource officers are developed.

The passage lists global finance and business headlines, then focuses on a Bank of England warning that AI-related stock valuations may be unsustainable and resemble dot-com-era levels. The BoE said gains concentrated in major U.S. tech firms, infrastructure constraints, and excessive optimism could trigger a sharp correction with global spillovers, including to the UK.

The passage describes systems and methods for identifying risky blockchain transactions and tracing digital asset flows for regulatory compliance, anti-money laundering, counter-terrorism financing, cybersecurity forensics, investigation, and fraud detection. The system receives blockchain transaction data and off-blockchain information, applies intelligence labels and machine learning-based behavioral classifications to blockchain addresses, assigns risk scores, and uses rules-based policies to approve, block, freeze, or suspend transactions or accounts.

An auto-tracing system collects transaction data from blockchain ledgers and labels from blockchain ecosystem intelligence databases, then applies input trace parameters such as direction, time range, transaction volume, hop limits, and filters. It uses artificial intelligence graph search algorithms, including breadth-first search, Dijkstra, and heuristic-based methods, to determine asset paths between source, intermediate, and destination addresses. The system may generate reports, visual result graphs, journey boards, summary statistics, alerts, and suspicious address lists.

The disclosed machine learning components include AutoML pipelines, decision trees, regression models, neural networks, and behavior-based classification models. These models may classify entities such as exchanges, mixers, bots, hackers, terrorists, money laundering addresses, and bad actor clusters using statistical, topology, temporal, linkage, derived, and sequential features. Risk scores may range from safe to risky and may incorporate transaction history, external information, graph connectivity, and time decay.

The system may support multiple blockchains and may extend tracing between cryptocurrency and fiat banking systems using exchange KYC mappings. It also describes address clustering methods that group similar blockchain addresses into cluster identifiers based on transaction behavior, intelligence labels, and address similarity analysis.

Plum School District officials will begin preliminary 2018-19 budget discussions Tuesday, hoping to avoid a third consecutive tax increase. The district starts the year more than $4 million in debt after approving a $66 million budget with a tax hike and a $5.6 million bond. Officials also will discuss recruiting Chinese tuition students, elementary construction, consolidation, redistricting, and beginning the process to close Regency Park Elementary School. A special voting meeting before the workshop will address personnel moves and volunteer coaches.

A survey of 100 financial services professionals by Infosys Finacle found over 80% of global bankers expect commercial blockchain adoption by 2020. Average 2017 investment is expected near $1 million, with cross-border payments and identity among top use cases. Most banks prefer private blockchains, while 10% prefer public ones.

Pump and dump schemes involve promoters acquiring positions in stocks, often thinly traded penny stocks, then spreading false or misleading information to artificially raise prices before selling to latecomers. Prices often collapse after interest fades, leaving many later investors with losses. The passage describes these schemes as scams, immoral, and illegal on regulated exchanges.

Pump and dumps are most common in OTC penny stocks and unregulated crypto markets, especially low-volume coins on small exchanges. Social media, forums, chat rooms, and messaging services can help spread hype and trigger fear of missing out. Regulated exchanges are less vulnerable because of enforcement and larger stock sizes.

A cited study found that pump-and-dump participation was fairly common among sampled German online investors and produced average losses of 28%. The passage advises avoiding suspected schemes, being cautious in OTC markets, and focusing on legitimate, systematic, long-term investing or trading practices.

Orbital ATK reported Q2 2017 sales of $1.12 billion, up 3% year over year and slightly above analyst estimates, with adjusted earnings of $1.56 per share beating expectations. GAAP earnings fell 3% to $1.51 per share as operating margin declined to 12.2%, and free cash flow turned negative at $55.8 million versus positive $107.2 million a year earlier.

Management remained optimistic, citing strong bookings of $1.4 billion in new firm and option orders plus $220 million in option exercises, producing a book-to-bill ratio of about 1.45. Orbital raised full-year guidance to $4.6 billion–$4.65 billion in sales and $5.95–$6.25 in earnings per share, while keeping free cash flow guidance at $250 million–$300 million.

Argus Research upgraded Orbital ATK from hold to buy with a $120 price target, citing expected cash flow milestones and potential defense spending benefits. The author argues the stock is too expensive, noting its 44% rise over 12 months, valuation of 22 times trailing earnings, enterprise value-to-free-cash-flow above 40, and expected profit growth of no more than 10% annually.

The disclosure relates to wireless communication methods, apparatuses, systems, storage media, base stations, terminal devices, and computer program products for transmitting paging information in new-generation, beamforming-based wireless systems. High-frequency communication uses beamforming to improve coverage, but narrow beams make it difficult for a network to know which beam covers an idle UE. Repeated paging over beams and flexible beam scheduling complicate or prevent use of LTE-style DRX paging mechanisms.

The proposed methods calculate a time-domain position of a paging occasion (PO) for a second communication node and transmit or receive paging information within that PO. The paging information may include paging downlink control information and/or a paging message. The PO includes a group of paging resources for one or more preset beams or ports and may correspond to a synchronization signal burst set or preset sweeping resources.

The PO may be determined using parameters such as the second node’s DRX cycle, the first node’s paging transmission interval, the number of paging transmissions within a DRX cycle, the second node identifier, and a PO offset. The PO may involve calculating a starting radio frame number and, when applicable, a starting subframe position. Paging may be transmitted on all beams or ports within the paging transmission interval.

The disclosure also provides configuration or indication of quasi-co-location relationships between paging-related signals and other sweeping signals or channels, enabling the second node to determine resources, ports, or receive beams for paging reception. Corresponding apparatuses include calculation, transmitting, receiving, configuration, and determination devices for first and second communication nodes.
The appeal was docketed and dismissed on the appellee’s motion with the appellant’s consent.

Under director Jill Medvedow, Boston’s Institute of Contemporary Art transformed from a financially weak, marginal institution with few members, no permanent collection, and about 25,000 annual visitors into a prominent waterfront museum. After arriving in 1998, Medvedow focused on stabilizing and reinventing the ICA, broadening its audience, expanding education, exploring collecting, and seeking a new location.

The ICA won the right to build on Parcel J at Fan Pier in 1999 after presenting a plan for a waterfront museum and building political and community support. It launched a major fundraising campaign, recruited influential board members, and selected Diller + Scofidio to design the building through an unusually public architect-selection process. The project faced regulatory hurdles, the loss of the surrounding developer’s partnership, and construction delays, but the new $51 million building opened in December 2006.

The ICA exceeded its $62 million capital campaign goal, attracted more than 280,000 visitors in its first year, and maintained strong attendance in 2008 and 2009. Shepard Fairey’s 2009 exhibition drew 130,000 visitors despite his arrest outside the museum on opening night.

The study introduces “whole human pedagogy,” a decolonial framework for education abroad that centers embodiment, emotions, belonging, and becoming. Drawing on hooks, Thompson, experiential learning, decolonial theory, and alternative pedagogies, it addresses the exclusion of embodied, emotional, relational, and transformative knowledge in higher education.

Using purposive and snowball sampling, the qualitative study interviewed 17 education abroad practitioners in Fall 2023. Participants generally viewed whole-human approaches as central to education abroad. They described embodiment through physical, sensory, place-based, mindful, and identity-related learning; emotions through culture shock, discomfort, expectation-setting, and reflection; belonging through reciprocal relationships, learning communities, vulnerability, and trust; and becoming through transformation, self-knowledge, and students’ future direction.

The findings suggest whole human pedagogy is a useful framework for education abroad praxis, shaping educators’ philosophies, goals, and self-reflexivity while emphasizing collaboration, presence, mutuality, creativity, and wellbeing. The study argues that this approach challenges dominant Euro-U.S. epistemological values and supports holistic, liberatory education. It may be applied to program development, assessment, professional development, and future research on holistic education abroad.

Amazon announced new Echo devices with Alexa+ support, three Kindle Scribe tablets including a Colorsoft model, Fire TVs, a Fire TV Stick 4K Select running the new Vega operating system, and updated Ring and Blink cameras. Alexa+ is rolling out in the US in early access, is free for Prime members, and costs $20 monthly for others. New Echo devices feature faster chips, Omnisense sensors, improved audio, and preorder availability.

The new Kindle Scribe models are thinner, faster, support lower-latency writing, and add features such as Quick Notes, Kindle Workspace, cloud file import/export, AI notebook search, Story So Far, and Ask This Book. Amazon also introduced Fire TVs with faster performance, Dialogue Boost, and Omnisense, plus a $40 Fire TV Stick 4K Select with 4K and HDR10+ support.

Ring announced new 2K and 4K cameras using Retinal image processing, with features including Familiar Faces, Alexa+ Greetings, and Search Party for finding lost dogs. Blink introduced new 2K cameras and an Arc accessory that combines two cameras for 180-degree footage.

Sean “Diddy” Combs was sentenced to four years and two months in prison and fined $500,000 after being convicted of transporting people across state lines for prostitution-related sexual encounters. He has already served about a year in jail. Combs was acquitted of sex trafficking and racketeering charges. At trial, former girlfriends testified that he used violence, threats, drugs and coercion during years of sexual encounters involving male sex workers. Combs apologized in court and asked for leniency, while prosecutors said serious prison time was necessary. Several of his children also addressed the judge, asking for mercy.

Mr. Stevens reported in 1892 that revolutionary plans in Hawaii were restrained by a U.S. naval presence, hostility existed toward the heir, and sentiment for annexation was growing. He described dissatisfaction with the Queen’s influences, political deadlock, cabinet crises, and possible overthrow of the monarchy. He recommended annexation or a customs union with U.S. control of Pearl Harbor and an implied protectorate. Navy reports corroborated these accounts before news arrived of a peaceful revolution and the Queen’s dethronement. The report states that U.S. policy toward Hawaii from 1820 to 1893 emphasized friendship, protection, Hawaiian autonomy, preservation of American rights, distrust of foreign intervention, and occasional consideration of annexation. The appendix explains that it provides selected important correspondence and excludes private claims not requiring separate negotiation.

Months after major Trump administration cuts to the Education Department’s research operations, researchers see cautious signs of rebuilding. The department plans to reinstate some canceled contracts, temporarily restore regional education labs, seek input on modernizing the Institute of Education Sciences, and hire for National Center for Education Statistics assessment roles. Researchers welcomed the involvement of Amber Northern and said officials appear interested in reform rather than eliminating federal education research. Still, experts warned that severe staff shortages, reduced reporting functions, new data-collection demands, and uncertainty over funding and priorities continue to threaten research quality, NAEP usefulness, and education data systems.

Theratechnologies announced an agreement with underwriters led by RBC Capital Markets to issue US$50 million in convertible unsecured senior notes due June 30, 2023, with a possible US$7.5 million over-allotment option. The notes bear 5.75% annual interest and are convertible into common shares at US$14.85 per share. Proceeds will fund payments under the EMD Serono Termination Agreement, Trogarzo™ approval and commercialization in Europe and other jurisdictions, and general corporate purposes. Closing is expected around June 19, 2018, subject to regulatory approvals.

NGC 5949 is a nearby dwarf galaxy about 44 million light-years from Earth, imaged by Hubble. Though only about one-hundredth the Milky Way’s mass, it is relatively bulky for a dwarf and has barred spiral features. Its study relates to dark matter and missing satellite galaxy puzzles.

The passage describes container design patterns for building and operating applications.

The sidecar pattern adds functionality to an application container without changing the application. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service with an nginx sidecar, synchronizing configuration through a configuration-manager sidecar, providing process introspection with a topz sidecar, and building a simple Git-based PaaS using a Node.js application container and a Git synchronization sidecar. Effective sidecars should be modular and reusable, with parameterized containers, clearly defined APIs, and documentation through Dockerfile directives such as EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL.

The ambassador pattern brokers communication between an application container and external services. It can route requests to sharded backends, as shown with Redis and twemproxy, provide service discovery across environments such as public and private clouds, and support experimentation or request splitting by sending a portion of traffic to beta services while keeping production responses for users.

The adapter pattern modifies an application container’s interface to match expected operational standards. It can adapt monitoring output, such as using a Prometheus exporter for Redis, normalize logging through fluentd adapters, and provide richer health checks, such as running MySQL diagnostic queries from a separate adapter container.

The passage then introduces multi-node distributed patterns and microservices. Microservices split systems into smaller components with defined APIs, improving agility, team independence, and scaling, but making debugging and architecture more difficult. Distributed patterns help structure such systems.

Replicated load-balanced services use identical replicas behind a load balancer for reliability, redundancy, and horizontal scaling. Stateless services need multiple replicas for high availability, and readiness probes tell the load balancer when instances are ready. Session-tracked services route a user’s requests to the same replica, often using hashing or cookies. Additional replicated layers can provide caching with Varnish, rate limiting, denial-of-service defense, and SSL termination with nginx.

Sharded services split data across shards, with routing logic directing each request to the correct shard. Sharding is useful when state exceeds a single machine’s capacity. A sharded cache improves memory utilization compared with replicated caches, but shard failures can affect cache hit rate, latency, and backend load. Replicated sharded caches improve resilience and allow hot shards to scale independently. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform, use appropriate keys, and may use consistent hashing to reduce remapping during resharding.

The scatter/gather pattern uses replication to reduce request latency by distributing parts of a request to multiple replicas in parallel, gathering partial results, and combining them into a complete response.

The Supreme Court dismissed Varun Thakur’s plea to cancel interim bail for Ryan International School owners, the Pinto family, in his son Pradyuman’s murder case. The CBI cleared bus conductor Ashok and accused a Class 11 student.

Automation could displace many workers, including 3.5 million U.S. truck drivers, as autonomous vehicles and AI systems advance across industries. The passage explores augmentation as a possible response, highlighting neural lace concepts to improve brain-computer interfaces, exosuits that combine human decision-making with robotic strength, and skill development to help workers remain employable. Researchers and companies are developing injectable brain electronics, powered exoskeletons, and soft wearable robots for medical, military, and industrial uses. Tom Davenport argues workers must develop new skills and find roles alongside smart machines, though physical laborers may face especially difficult transitions. He notes that narrow AI already threatens some jobs, while artificial general intelligence would make outcomes uncertain.

The Ultimate Oscillator is a momentum indicator developed by Larry Williams in 1976 to measure price momentum across three timeframes, typically 7, 14, and 28 periods. It combines weighted averages of buying pressure and true range, giving the shortest timeframe the most weight, to reduce false overbought signals and bearish divergences common in single-timeframe oscillators. Values range from 0 to 100, with below 30 considered oversold and above 70 overbought.

Trading signals are based on divergences between price and the indicator. A buy signal requires bullish divergence from oversold territory and a rise above the divergence high, while sell signals use opposite bearish conditions. The passage presents backtests showing default settings performed poorly, but optimized settings produced strong results, including examples with profit factors above 2, 355 trades, 0.77% average gain per trade, 78% win rate, and 25% maximum drawdown. The author describes the Ultimate Oscillator as a consistent mean reversion indicator in backtests.
President Trump denied a New York Times report that he watches four to eight hours of television daily. The Times stood by its reporting, citing interviews with 60 sources.

Meb Faber’s Tactical Asset Allocation strategy is an active trend-following approach using market timing across stocks, bonds, REITs, and commodities, divided into U.S. stocks, foreign stocks, U.S. bonds, U.S. REITs, and world commodities. It can be implemented with five diversified index ETFs, allocating 20% to each asset and moving to cash when no signal exists. The passage says backtests over 16 years showed reduced drawdowns, with a maximum drawdown of -13.24%, compared with higher drawdowns for passive portfolios. The strategy is described as adaptable to other asset classes and ETFs.

A fast-moving lava flow from Hawaii’s Kilauea volcano crossed Highway 132, destroyed utility equipment, and cut power to coastal communities including Vacationland and Kapoho Beach Lots. Officials said 71 homes and additional structures have been destroyed, with the number expected to rise. Residents in the Kapoho area were urged to evacuate due to possible isolation from lava. The eruption has destroyed more than 400 utility poles, displaced thousands, and opened 24 fissures since May 3. Authorities warned residents to limit exposure to volcanic glass, gases, ash, and pollution. Lava also covered two monitored geothermal wells, though officials said no dangerous gases were released.

Richard Berg appealed a Minnesota trial court order increasing his child support after his net monthly income rose from $1,246 to $1,721 following the parties’ 1981 divorce. Nancy Berg, who had custody of the children, sought guideline-level support based on increased child-rearing expenses. The trial court raised support to $516 per month for two children, later reducing it to $430 under specified circumstances, and denied or dismissed requests for extended support for two children.

The Court of Appeals held that although the support amount was within the trial court’s discretion, the findings were inadequate under Moylan v. Moylan. The court remanded for complete and specific findings explaining the basis for the child support modification.

The Canadian dollar was little changed at C$1.2857 per U.S. dollar as investors awaited a Federal Reserve rate decision and a speech by Bank of Canada Governor Stephen Poloz. The currency fell 1.3% last week after the Bank of Canada held rates and sounded dovish. Speculators trimmed bullish bets. Oil prices edged higher, while Canadian government bond prices rose slightly across a flatter yield curve.

BidaskClub upgraded Rapid7 from “hold” to “buy.” Other analysts issued mixed actions, and the stock has an average “Buy” rating with a $20.19 consensus target. Rapid7 opened at $18.47 Friday, with a $796.26 million market cap and a 52-week range of $10.63 to $18.65. The company reported quarterly EPS of ($0.26), beating estimates, on revenue of $47.44 million, up 27.3% year over year. Insiders sold 93,770 shares worth $1.6 million over 90 days, while institutional investors own 71.01% of the stock. Rapid7 provides security and IT operations analytics.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2017. Net sales were $43.7 billion for Q3 2017, up from $32.7 billion in Q3 2016, and $117.4 billion for the first nine months of 2017, up from $92.2 billion. Net income was $256 million in Q3 2017 and $1.18 billion for the first nine months, compared with $252 million and $1.62 billion in the prior-year periods. Operating income declined to $347 million in Q3 2017 and $2.0 billion for the first nine months.

Segment results for Q3 2017 included North America net sales of $25.4 billion and operating income of $112 million, International net sales of $13.7 billion and an operating loss of $936 million, and AWS net sales of $4.6 billion and operating income of $1.17 billion. AWS sales increased 42% from Q3 2016.

As of September 30, 2017, Amazon had $12.8 billion in cash and cash equivalents, $24.3 billion in total cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, total assets of $115.3 billion, long-term debt of $24.7 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $24.7 billion. Operating cash flow for the trailing twelve months was $17.1 billion, while investing activities used $30.0 billion and financing activities provided $11.9 billion.

Amazon acquired Souq Group Ltd. for approximately $579 million, net of cash acquired, and Whole Foods Market for approximately $13.2 billion, net of cash acquired. Whole Foods Market contributed $1.3 billion in net sales and $21 million in operating income from the acquisition date through September 30, 2017.

The company issued $16.0 billion of unsecured senior notes in August 2017, primarily to fund the Whole Foods Market acquisition, repay 2017 notes, and support general corporate purposes. Amazon also disclosed ongoing tax matters involving the IRS, French Tax Administration, and European Commission, as well as legal proceedings involving patent and employment-related claims.

A senior Revolutionary Guards commander said the Guards were ready to prevent regional oil exports if U.S. actions banned Iranian oil sales, praising President Hassan Rouhani’s threat to disrupt neighboring countries’ shipments if Washington pushes countries to stop buying Iranian oil.

The University of Agriculture Faisalabad approved Rs3.28 billion non-development accounts for 2015-16 at its 44th Senate meeting. VC Dr Iqrar Ahmad said UAF launched 48 new degree programs, enrollment exceeded 25,000, financial assistance reached Rs700 million, and its competitive research portfolio crossed Rs2.5 billion. He urged greater investment in agricultural research, highlighted water scarcity, malnutrition affecting 40 percent of the population, and post-harvest losses, calling for modern farming, storage, processing, and value-addition techniques.

President Donald Trump said the U.S. will impose an additional 100% tariff on imports from China starting Nov. 1, on top of existing tariffs, and will add export controls on “any and all critical software.” The move follows China’s new export controls on rare earth minerals, which are vital to high-tech industries and largely supplied by China. Trump also suggested he may cancel an upcoming meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. China’s measures require licenses for certain rare earth-related exports beginning Dec. 1.

Richard Mosse’s project Heat Maps documents the refugee crisis across Europe, North Africa and the Middle East using a military-grade thermal camera that renders people as grey, indistinct figures. Mosse says the technology strips subjects of identity and reflects how Western governments regard refugees. The large-scale images combine surveillance, ambiguity and constructed photo-illustration, highlighting camp conditions while leaving individuals largely unidentifiable. Mosse also emphasizes the ethical discomfort of photographing from long range and repurposing technology designed for surveillance and targeting. The three-year project faced access, border and logistical challenges, including work in Tempelhof Airport and the Calais Jungle. Heat Maps is displayed at Jack Shainman Gallery in New York.

India demanded that the UN Secretariat disclose data on serious misconduct by UN personnel and cases where immunity was invoked or not waived to prevent prosecution. Yedla Umasankar, legal advisor at India’s UN Mission, criticized the UN for allegedly not pursuing serious allegations vigorously and said reluctance to waive immunity harms the organization’s credibility. He sought details on registered misconduct cases, host-country requests for waivers, UN prosecution requests, consultations with countries, and refusals to waive citizens’ immunity. The request excludes diplomats representing member states. Although the UN publishes some data on sexual misconduct in peacekeeping, it has not released a full roster of serious misconduct cases. Umasankar cited legal, jurisdictional, and national prosecution capacity issues, noting the UN cannot prosecute criminal cases itself.

Emperor penguins are classified as near-threatened, with a 2014 study projecting their population could fall 19 percent by 2100. A new monitoring system uses time-lapse photography and weather data to remotely track colony behavior. It has shown penguins huddling in warmer conditions, suggesting reduced body fat and possible food shortages linked to sea ice loss. One expert cited climate-related food impacts, while another suggested commercial fishing may be responsible. Researchers praised the system as cost-effective for studying Antarctica’s harsh environment.

A double bottom chart pattern is a bullish reversal price action formation with two swing lows around the same level and a swing high between them. The lows create support, while the swing high forms a resistance level called the neckline. The pattern is considered complete when price breaks above the neckline, often signaling a potential upward move.

Traders may enter long positions after a neckline breakout, estimate targets by projecting the pattern’s height upward, and place stop losses either within or below the pattern. Aggressive traders may act near the second low using reversal signals, while conservative traders wait for a confirmed breakout with increased volume.

The passage notes that coding and backtesting the pattern is difficult because it requires many rules and settings. It cites Thomas Bulkowski’s research on chart patterns, while cautioning that the study involved manual interpretation, a limited five-year period, and possible survivorship bias.

A preceding UDMA read with host termination can corrupt state, causing CRC errors during later UDMA writes when an IDE device terminates the transaction. The first CRC is correct, but subsequent CRC generation may continue incorrectly unless a rare host-initiated I/O restarts it. As a result, UDMA writes generally cannot be used; use the UDMA I/O blocking feature tied to bit 8 of the ATAC Error MSR.

The court sentenced Pomeroy to six $1,000 fines totaling $6,000, and the New York Central and Hudson River Railroad Company to six $18,000 fines totaling $108,000. The passage criticizes criminal law practices that overturn lower-court judgments on technicalities unrelated to justice and proposes barring new trials or reversals unless errors caused a miscarriage of justice. It also addresses injunctions, especially in labor cases, opposing their abolition while warning against abuse. Injunctions should restrain violence and intimidation but not prevent lawful labor action or serve corporate aggrandizement. The passage argues judges should use injunctions carefully, face public scrutiny, and be open to criticism when they act timidly, oppressively, or unjustly.

Mark Palmer forwarded to Enron colleagues a class action complaint filed in San Diego County Superior Court against Reliant, Southern Company, NRG, Dynegy, AES, Williams Energy, Duke Energy North America, and unnamed defendants. The suit, brought by Pamela R. Gordon on behalf of California electricity customers, alleges that generators and traders manipulated California wholesale electricity markets in 2000 by using confidential real-time market data, withholding capacity, exporting or parking power, coordinating outages, and creating transmission congestion to raise prices. The complaint cites FERC, CPUC, CAISO, media reports, and market analyses alleging unjust and unreasonable prices, market power, and more than $4 billion in overcharges. It asserts claims under California antitrust, unfair competition, consumer protection, and unconscionability laws, seeking class certification, damages, treble damages where applicable, restitution, disgorgement, injunctive relief, interest, costs, and attorneys’ fees.

The study presents interferometric second-harmonic generation (SHG) polarimetry as a scalable optical method for assessing crystalline quality in two-dimensional hBN. Conventional methods such as TEM, STM, LEED, and Raman spectroscopy either have limited sampling, cannot distinguish antiparallel domains, or lack direct sensitivity to orientational polarity. The authors show that coherent SHG is highly sensitive to antiparallel domains because their fields interfere destructively, reducing SHG intensity.

Across hBN samples grown by ten CVD methods and mechanically exfoliated references, SHG intensity varied by up to three orders of magnitude, far more than Raman intensity. Raman E2g intensity and linewidth provided indicators of crystallinity, but SHG intensity and orientational spread were more sensitive to structural disorder. Dual-polarization SHG imaging mapped crystallographic orientations and revealed distinct domain structures in samples grown on different catalysts. Interferometric SHG distinguished antiparallel domains by detecting phase shifts, showing that such domains and boundaries are common even in films that appear unidirectionally aligned.

A mixed-domain model showed that orientational spread alone cannot explain the large SHG suppression; destructive interference among antiparallel domains accounts for the observed intensity reductions. The study establishes correlations among SHG intensity, Raman intensity, Raman linewidth, and orientational disorder, providing quantitative optical metrics for hBN quality. The method offers wide-area, high-throughput structural imaging and is proposed as broadly applicable to other non-centrosymmetric 2D materials, including transition metal dichalcogenides.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed dismissal of an antitrust action brought by Innofood and Sea Breeze against Mitsubishi entities and ESSA. Plaintiffs alleged ESSA, a Mexican salt producer majority-owned and controlled by Mexico, unlawfully ended distribution arrangements and returned to selling Mexico’s sea salt exclusively through Mitsubishi.

The court held the claims were barred by the act of state doctrine because they challenged Mexico’s sovereign decision, through ESSA, about how to exploit and distribute its natural resources. Mexico’s constitution treats sea salt as a state-owned natural resource, and ESSA’s alleged conduct occurred in Mexico. Granting relief would require a U.S. court to judge and potentially invalidate Mexico’s chosen method of allocating and profiting from its salt production.

The court found the relevant prudential factors supported applying the doctrine: there was no shown international consensus against such exclusive resource arrangements, the case could affect foreign relations, and Mexico’s government continues to exist. The court declined to decide whether a commercial exception to the act of state doctrine exists, concluding any such exception would not apply because the challenged decisions were sovereign rather than purely commercial. It also rejected dismissal of Sea Breeze’s appeal based on a temporary suspension of corporate status because that status had been restored.
