This prospective multicenter study used untargeted metabolomics to examine plasma metabolites in cirrhotic patients undergoing transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) placement and assess associations with later hepatic encephalopathy (HE). HE is a complication of advanced liver disease, and TIPS can increase HE risk, but mechanisms and reliable biomarkers remain unclear.

Twenty-two participants underwent TIPS, with hepatic vein and peripheral vein blood collected before and after shunt placement and peripheral blood collected before discharge. Participants were followed for up to one year, and worst HE grade was recorded. LC-MS/MS metabolomics with molecular networking annotated 234 features.

Metabolomic changes were greater in peripheral vein samples than hepatic vein samples, with the largest changes occurring between post-TIPS peripheral samples and samples collected before discharge. Bile acids were major contributors to these shifts. Glycoursodeoxycholic acid decreased immediately after TIPS, and many bile acids differed between post-TIPS and discharge samples.

Participants who later developed HE showed greater pre- to post-TIPS dissimilarity in hepatic vein metabolomes, which the authors suggest may reflect less preexisting intrahepatic shunting. This pattern was not explained by changes in portal pressure. More severe HE was associated with larger post-shunt decreases in bile acids and glycerophosphocholine-related metabolites. Three conjugated hydroxylated bile acids in post-TIPS peripheral blood were inversely associated with HE grade. In two participants readmitted for HE, these bile acids decreased after TIPS and increased after HE treatment.

Chemical proportionality analysis identified notable pre- to post-TIPS fluctuations among glycerophosphocholine and bilirubin-related metabolites, including changes involving biliverdin. The authors conclude that bile acids, glycerophosphocholines, and bilirubin-related metabolites may be involved in post-TIPS HE and could inform future biomarker or therapeutic studies. Limitations include cohort size, incomplete metabolite coverage, reliance on putative annotations, and lack of microbiome association data.

AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 has multiple documented issues affecting DMA, UART, LPC, PCI, USB, PIC, ACPI, IDE/ATAC, KEL, SMBus, GPIO, and power management behavior.

Key issues include discarded UART writes and all-ones UART reads during 8237 block or demand DMA, failed LPC software DMA memory writes with no operational impact, illegal I/O or LBAR addresses at 10000h or higher, missing USB over-voltage protection requiring external circuitry, and PIC missed interrupts when automatic clock gating is enabled while edge-triggered sources remain high.

DMA and IDE-related issues include PRD prefetch hazards for ATAC and ACC when PRD tables are not 8-byte aligned, UDMA write CRC corruption after certain prior UDMA read host terminations, ATAC SSMI not blocking IDE I/O during DMA, PIO access failures when IDE bus mastering is enabled before command packets, ATAPI packet command failures after bus master enable in one CD-ROM case, ATAC hangs with non-DWORD-aligned PRDs, and fixed tACK timing that does not violate requirements.

Clock-gating problems affect GLIU ASMI delivery, CEIR UART operation, USB controller register reads, and PIC recovery. Recommended resolutions generally disable automatic clock gating for affected domains or avoid affected modes.

ACPI and PMC issues include byte accesses to PM1_EN and PM1_STS hanging, WORD and BYTE writes to PMC registers potentially corrupting other writes, wake event inputs GPIO[27:24] not working from ACPI S3, LOWBAT_FLAG not being set after abnormal standby, and Sleep_X/Sleep_Y not deasserting if certain delay counters exceed PM_SED.

KEL issues include inability to distinguish writes to ports 060h and 064h through HceStatus[3], Snoop mode incorrectly changing HCE register state, and AuxOutputFull being cleared by reads from Port 60h. Software workarounds include using ASMI trap information, saving and restoring HCE state, and using interrupts for USB keyboard and mouse PS/2 emulation.

Other issues include possible but non-real-world PCI back-to-back memory read failure, unsupported PIC polling mode, unreliable CS5535-generated SSMIs when IRQs occur simultaneously, RTC CMOS read inconsistency after extended RAM writes, LPC transaction aborts with LPC-to-ISA bridges, incorrect SMB NEGACK behavior, GLPCI retry counter counting unrelated retries, GPIO high-bank atomic writes clearing unselected bits after suspend, and SMBus hold time shorter than the SMB 2.0 requirement.

The passage explains several container and distributed-system design patterns.

The adapter pattern is used to make existing containers expose expected interfaces without modifying them. Examples include adding a Prometheus Redis exporter so Redis can be monitored, using fluentd adapters to normalize logs or collect Redis slow logs and Apache Storm logs, and adding an adapter container to run richer database health checks for MySQL. This approach supports modularity, reuse, independent updates, and sharing.

The passage then introduces multi-node distributed patterns and microservices. Microservices split systems into smaller services with defined APIs, improving team independence, agility, scaling, and reliability, but making debugging, architecture, and coordination more difficult. Distributed patterns help address these challenges.

Replicated load-balanced services are described as identical stateless replicas behind a load balancer. They improve availability, support rolling upgrades, and scale horizontally. Readiness probes tell load balancers when replicas are ready to receive traffic. Session-tracked services route a user’s requests to the same replica, often using IP-based or application-level tracking. Additional application-layer patterns include caching with Varnish, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination with nginx.

Sharded services divide requests or data across shards, with a root or router sending requests to the correct shard. Sharding is useful when state is too large for one machine. Sharded caches improve memory use because each shard stores different data, but failures or rollouts can reduce cache hit rates and performance. Replicating each shard improves reliability and allows hot shards to scale. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform, and the shard key must reflect what makes responses equivalent. Consistent hashing reduces remapping when shard counts change.

The scatter/gather pattern parallelizes request processing across many leaf nodes. A root sends work to leaves, collects partial results, and combines them. It can speed up independent computation, such as document search, and can also use sharded leaves for larger datasets. However, too much parallelism adds overhead and increases exposure to slow “straggler” nodes. Replicating shards improves reliability, upgrade safety, and scale.

The passage also discusses Function-as-a-Service and event-driven processing. FaaS simplifies deployment, scaling, and failure recovery, and works well for stateless functions, request or response decorators, asynchronous event handling, and event pipelines. Its challenges include operational visibility, debugging, hidden dependencies, limited suitability for long-running background work, poor fit for large in-memory datasets, and potentially unfavorable cost at sustained high request volume. Examples include request defaulting, two-factor authentication, and new-user signup workflows built from small functions.

Ari Guiragos Minassian, Orange County’s only Armenian school, held its 31st Annual Banquet in Santa Ana on April 1 with over 250 guests. James T. Hodgkinson, 66, shot Rep. Steve Scalise and several others during a Republican baseball practice in Alexandria, Virginia, before being fatally shot by police. Authorities believe he had been living in a van in northern Virginia since March and frequently visited a nearby YMCA, where witnesses described him as quiet and solitary. Investigators said they were still determining a motive, though Hodgkinson had posted grievances about President Donald Trump and Republicans.

Hodgkinson was armed with a handgun and rifle, and the FBI was tracing the weapons. Injured victims included a congressional aide, two Capitol Police officers and a former congressional aide. The FBI sought public help reconstructing Hodgkinson’s activities in Alexandria.

Hodgkinson had run a home-inspection business in Illinois, supported Bernie Sanders’ 2016 campaign, wrote letters about income inequality, and had prior arrests, including a dismissed 2006 battery case. Local police had also responded in March after he fired a rifle near homes; no charges were filed.

US Charge d'Affaires William Gill said at a July 4 event in Baku that US-Azerbaijan cooperation supports an independent, stable Azerbaijan and can build a better future for both countries and the world.

Perplexity AI announced its AI-powered Comet browser is now available worldwide for free. Comet, initially launched in July for $200-a-month Perplexity Max subscribers, can search the web, organize tabs, draft emails, shop and perform other assistant-like tasks. NCC Executive Vice Chairman Umar Danbatta said Nigeria’s internet users grew from 28 million in 2012 to 103 million in May 2018, highlighting the internet’s role in good governance. Internet growth continues despite challenges including cost, scalability, power outages and education barriers.

John LeClair said the team was flat, made bad decisions, failed to skate, and did not pursue loose pucks, allowing a quick opponent to control play. The President transmits to Congress a letter from the governor of Texas and the administration’s response concerning Texas’s attempt to extend civil jurisdiction over El Paso, Worth, Presidio, and Santa Fe. Texas claims these areas east of the Rio Grande as within its limits and has called its legislature to maintain that claim and establish jurisdiction, possibly by force. The President warns that if Texas militia or civil forces enter territory outside Texas to enforce Texas law and obstruct U.S. law or treaty obligations, the Constitution and federal statutes require him to use militia or federal military and naval forces if necessary to execute the laws.

The message argues that New Mexico is a Territory of the United States as possessed at the time of the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, and that the treaty’s protections for former Mexican residents are part of the supreme law of the land. Until a lawful boundary is established, the Executive must protect inhabitants of New Mexico in their liberty, property, and religion, but has no authority to create a civil or military government there; that power belongs to Congress.

The President states that the Executive cannot determine the disputed boundary between Texas and New Mexico. He urges Congress to settle the boundary promptly, preferably with Texas’s assent, to avoid delay, disturbance, and collision. He suggests Congress may offer Texas a fair indemnity for surrendering any claim it may have. He concludes that settling the boundary during the current session is essential to public interest, domestic tranquility, and renewed harmony.

James D. Rone sued Boncar Construction for injuries suffered at an Indiana sewer construction site when his hands were caught in a back hoe cable while he was descending from the gantry after lifting telephone wires. In the AEGEAN study, apixaban exposure, interruptions, dosing, and compliance were comparable across study groups. Mean adherence at 24 weeks was 91.64% in Primary SOC and 91.88% in the Additional Educational Program group, with no significant difference. Adherence remained comparable at 48 weeks across Primary SOC, Secondary SOC, and Continued Additional Educational Program groups, though adherence declined significantly over later treatment periods. Persistence was also similar at 24 and 48 weeks. Fully adherent subject rates were low and comparable between groups. Subgroup analyses showed no significant interaction at 24 or 48 weeks, with some interactions from Week 24 to Week 48 by atrial fibrillation type and sex. Safety outcomes, adverse events, serious adverse events, discontinuations, bleeding events, deaths, and laboratory findings were broadly similar across groups. The proactive educational program did not improve adherence or persistence.

Opening range breakout (ORB) strategies trade breakouts above or below a defined opening range, often using short intraday intervals such as the first five minutes. The article backtests ORB strategies mainly on S&P 500 futures and finds that simple versions perform poorly, with small average gains, low win rates, and negative results across additional futures including Nasdaq, gold, silver, and oil. The author argues ORB strategies are less effective than in the past due to false breakouts, overnight gains, computer-driven arbitrage, and the tendency for daily highs and lows to occur near the open or close. Adding daily or weekly filters based on trends, volume, reversals, or overbought/oversold conditions may improve results, but traders should avoid overfitting.

The Amoeba defense, developed by Jerry Tarkanian at UNLV, is an aggressive trapping match-up zone from a 1-1-3 alignment used to disrupt opponents. The ball defender applies heavy pressure while the other four defenders zone, requiring quick guards and aiming to create steals and transition baskets. Utah anti-police brutality groups criticized Salt Lake County District Attorney Sim Gill’s ruling that Officer Clinton Fox was legally justified in fatally shooting Patrick Harmon, a 50-year-old black man, in August. The passage explains momentum investing as buying stocks with strong historical performance, typically over 3–12 months, and periodically rebalancing into the highest-momentum stocks. It says this approach is based on the momentum hypothesis, which links medium-term past returns with future returns. Citing Eric Crittenden’s research, it notes that from 1989 to 2015 about 20% of stocks accounted for all market gains, while the rest produced zero returns overall.

The passage presents a simple monthly S&P 500 momentum strategy using a moving average crossover system. Backtested on the cash index from 1960 to February 2023, the strategy grew $100,000 to $5.575 million, with a 6.6% annual return versus 7% for buy and hold. However, it was invested only 69% of the time and had lower drawdowns, 26% versus 55%, with a stated risk-adjusted return of 9.5%. The average loss was under 5%, while the average winner was nearly 25%. The passage also mentions the S&P 500 Momentum Index, which tracks stocks showing relative strength.

This retrospective VHA study used an emulated trial design to compare suicide attempts and self-directed violence among Veterans with PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and matched uninfected comparators. The cohort included 198,938 infected Veterans and 992,036 comparators, followed for up to one year after the index date. Outcomes were identified using VHA-curated self-directed violence event data.

Within one year, 3,078 cohort members had a documented suicide attempt and 2,887 had documented self-directed violence. In Cox analyses, infected Veterans had higher risk of suicide attempt than comparators in the short term, long term, and one-year periods, with one-year HR=1.41. They also had higher risk of self-directed violence across all periods, with one-year HR=1.38. Risks were greatest during the first 30 days after infection. Stratified analyses showed increased risk particularly among those without prior suicide attempt or self-directed violence. Reported suicide deaths did not differ significantly between groups.

The study concludes that SARS-CoV-2 infection among Veterans was associated with increased risk of suicide attempts and self-directed violence, especially soon after infection, supporting early monitoring and prevention efforts after COVID-19 illness.

ADP reported a loss of 32,000 private nonfarm jobs in September, the largest since June 2020. The six-month moving average fell to 23,000. Education & Health Services gained 33,000 jobs, while Leisure & Hospitality lost 19,000.

Overbought stock markets have risen significantly over a defined period and may indicate weaker short-term returns, but not long-term weakness, as returns tend to revert toward historical averages. Overbought conditions can be measured with indicators such as RSI, with the example using a 2-day RSI above 95. Backtests suggest returns are lower than average in the first few days after overbought signals, though this does not necessarily create a tradable short-selling strategy. Media coverage may amplify overbought conditions through positive articles and FOMO, while negative coverage during downturns may increase panic.

Kiran Rana, a digital and social media editor at The Globe and Mail, reflects on her heavy use of social media for work and personal life. The TPS7H500x-SP controllers support internal oscillator, external synchronization, and primary-secondary oscillator modes. Internal oscillator mode uses an RT-to-AVSS resistor to set 100 kHz to 2 MHz switching; SYNC outputs a clock at twice the switching frequency. External synchronization leaves RT floating and applies a 200 kHz to 4 MHz clock at SYNC, twice the desired switching frequency, with 40% to 60% duty cycle. Primary-secondary mode uses one controller’s SYNC output to clock another controller with its RT pin floating, enabling synchronized independent converters or parallel interleaved operation.

The controllers provide one or two primary outputs and optional synchronous rectifier outputs, with roughly 150 mA peak capability, so external gate drivers are recommended. OUTB and SRB are active only in specified 50% duty-cycle configurations. Dead time, leading-edge blanking, duty-cycle limits, current sensing, hiccup protection, external fault handling, slope compensation, and frequency compensation are configurable through external components, with some features fixed on specific devices. Pulse skipping is implemented to address minimum on-time issues, especially during high-frequency operation.

The CS_ILIM pin supports peak current mode PWM and overcurrent protection. When CS_ILIM exceeds 1.05 V, cycle-by-cycle limiting occurs and the HICC capacitor controls delay and restart timing. The FAULT pin can implement external protections; when its threshold is exceeded, switching stops until the fault clears and a delay elapses. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C typical and restarts below 160°C typical.

The TPS7H500x-SP family is intended for radiation-hardness-assured, space-grade DC-DC converter designs including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. An example synchronous push-pull GaN converter design describes selection of RT, feedback resistors, dead time, leading-edge blanking, soft-start, transformer parameters, FET ratings, RCD clamp, output inductor, output capacitance, current sense resistor, hiccup capacitor, compensation, and slope compensation. The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require proper bypassing and PCB layout practices to reduce noise, EMI, and coupling.

William C. Smith, 42, of Trotwood, pleaded not guilty in Miami County Municipal Court to murdering Willard Higgins Jr., 40, after a Friday altercation in Troy. Bond was set at $500,000, an autopsy is underway, and a pre-trial hearing is set for Dec. 19.

Blackwell’s RT Core adds hardware ray intersection support for Linear Swept Spheres, improving hair rendering speed and reducing VRAM use versus DOTS. SER 2.0 improves GPU thread reordering efficiency and precision, benefiting path tracing and neural shading. The AI Management Processor is a programmable GPU context scheduler using a dedicated RISC-V processor to reduce CPU scheduling overhead, improve latency, and coordinate AI and graphics workloads.

Blackwell adds 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC encode/decode support, ninth-generation NVENC with improved AV1 and HEVC quality, AV1 Ultra High Quality mode, faster export speeds on RTX 5090, sixth-generation NVDEC with faster H.264 decode, and DisplayPort 2.1b UHBR 20. Max-Q improvements include advanced power gating, separate voltage rails, accelerated frequency switching, and faster low-latency sleep.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three additional frames per rendered frame, with faster and lower-memory AI models and enhanced Flip Metering. DLSS also moves to transformer models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving stability, detail, anti-aliasing, and lighting quality.

Blackwell supports neural shaders through Cooperative Vectors APIs for DX12 and Vulkan, enabling Tensor Core access from shaders. Described neural rendering features include RTX Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces.

The passage also outlines Blackwell GPU variants and GeForce RTX 50 series products: GB202 for RTX 5090, GB203 for RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti, and GB205 for RTX 5070, along with their chip-level resources and positioning. Blue Bird reported record Q3 sales, strong margins, solid bus volumes, higher pricing, and resilient demand despite tariff headwinds. Its 3,900-unit backlog supports expected growth into FY25, while facility investments, product innovation, and federal EV funding are cited as long-term growth drivers. The author maintains a Buy rating, noting valuation, demand, margin expansion, and short-term EV risks.

The passage states that Russia acknowledged the seizure of the bark Cape Horn Pigeon was unjustifiable and that indemnity was due, but rejected the main claim for loss of the vessel’s services during detention. The United States offered to settle for $42,000 without prejudicing the claimants’ rights if refused; Russia rejected this and again offered $2,500. The passage argues that the Okhotsk Sea was not subject to exclusive Russian control, citing its size, lack of occupation or prohibition, treaties with the United States and Great Britain, and evidence that foreign whalers commonly used it. It also cites the captain’s affidavit that the Russian commander claimed the sea was closed and ordered seizures of whaling vessels.

Stocks, bonds, and commodities fell sharply Friday, with major indices down about 2 percent and the Dow dropping over 600 points. The selloff followed wage growth data that raised inflation and interest-rate concerns. Analysts largely viewed it as an overdue correction toward more normal market volatility, not broader economic trouble.

The lecture reviews coherent or collective Thomson scattering, where the scattering vector wavelength \(2\pi/|k|\), with \(k=k_s-k_i\), is larger than the Debye length, so the laser samples collective plasma motion. Relevant plasma modes include ion acoustic waves and electron plasma waves, whose frequencies are much lower than the laser frequency and whose phase velocities are much less than the speed of light.

Scattering occurs from naturally present plasma fluctuations. A detector or spectrometer defines the scattered wave vector direction, while the scattering angle and incident wavelength determine \(|k|\). Real measurements collect a range of angles, which broadens the spectrum, along with thermal effects. Expected spectra contain low-frequency ion acoustic features and higher-frequency electron plasma wave features, broadened rather than delta functions.

The derivation proceeds in two steps: relating scattered power to electron density fluctuations, then calculating those fluctuations. Using the Klimontovich distribution and retaining particle positions allows interference between scattered fields, unlike the incoherent case. The scattered power spectrum is proportional to constants describing geometry, laser power, scattering volume, and the spectral density function \(S(k,\omega)\), which contains the spectrum’s shape and depends on the squared Fourier-transformed electron density fluctuations.

Density fluctuations are calculated with a test-particle treatment. Each electron and ion perturbs the plasma, producing shielding electron density. Electron test particles contribute directly plus their shielding response; ions contribute only through the electrons drawn into their shielding clouds, since ion scattering itself is neglected. This leads to a general expression for \(S(k,\omega)\) involving electron and ion distribution functions, susceptibilities, and the dielectric permittivity \(\epsilon=1+\chi_e+\sum_i\chi_i\). Peaks occur where \(\epsilon(k,\omega)\to 0\), corresponding to normal plasma modes.

To find susceptibilities, the lecture uses the collisionless Vlasov equation, justified because Thomson scattering wavelengths can be much shorter than the mean free path even in collisional plasmas. Linearizing the distribution function gives \(\chi\) in terms of an integral over the velocity distribution, evaluated with the Landau contour. For Maxwellian distributions, the susceptibility can be written using the Debye length, the coupling parameter, species charge, density, temperature, and a dimensionless phase-velocity-to-thermal-velocity parameter. The resulting function is related to the plasma dispersion function and complex error-function family and is commonly tabulated or implemented in numerical tools.

The passage describes the SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) specification, which standardizes communication between SEV-ES or SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors while limiting exposed guest register state. SEV-ES and SEV-SNP protect guest register state from direct hypervisor access, and Non-Automatic Exits allow guests to selectively share state through the GHCB.

The GHCB is a 4 KB decrypted page mapped by the guest for guest-hypervisor communication. Version 2 adds SEV-SNP support, hypervisor feature advertisement, CPUID-related enhancements, page state change support, restricted APIC emulation, APIC ID list retrieval, multi-VMPL support, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, and GHCB unregister support. Hypervisor feature support is exposed through a bitmap retrievable via the GHCB MSR protocol.

The passage defines GHCB MSR protocol usage, GHCB GPA registration and unregistration, protocol negotiation examples for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP, VMGEXIT handling, valid Non-Automatic Exit behavior, error reporting, and use of VALID_BITMAP. It also describes the SEV-SNP secrets page guest reserved area, EFI Confidential Computing Blob configuration table, page state change operations, SNP Guest Request, and SNP Extended Guest Request for returning certificate data such as VCEK and VLEK certificates.

The speaker says the team is excited, healthy aside from Dwayne’s injury, rested, confident, and focused on executing its game plan Saturday night. They praise a physical player’s contribution and believe playing well will give them the desired result.

Massachusetts General Hospital’s Pre-Admission Testing Area (PATA), responsible for pre-operative work-ups for surgical outpatients, had faced long wait times and inefficiencies for over two years by June 2009. Patients often spent more time waiting than with providers, with average appointments lasting about two-and-a-half hours and some exceeding four hours, despite only 80–90 minutes of provider face time. Complaints affected patients, staff, surgeons, and operating room operations.

PATA saw about 65% of surgical outpatients due to limited capacity, prioritizing complex cases, while others received work-ups on the day of surgery in the OR. Incomplete or missing work-ups contributed to delayed surgery starts, overtime, cancellations, lost productivity, and lower revenue. The OR director estimated OR delays caused 57,000 minutes of lost productivity annually.

The clinic used 12 exam rooms and manual processes. Each patient saw a lab technician, nurse, and anesthesiologist. Five lab technicians, five nurses, and eight anesthesiologists were scheduled daily, serving about 55 patients. The process included check-in, vitals and EKG, nurse assessment, anesthesiologist assessment and consent, blood work, and check-out. Bottlenecks arose from uneven patient flow, provider variability, lunch scheduling, manual tracking, unclear communication, missing records, and limited rooms.

Previous improvement attempts, including a proposed second clinic and broader perioperative projects, failed because of resource, funding, political, and cultural barriers. In 2008, Dr. Jeanine Wiener-Kronish formed a PATA Task Force led by Susan Moss. After data collection by an MBA intern confirmed extensive waiting and variability, the task force considered options such as longer hours, reduced volume, added resources, better triage, online education, electronic records, and process improvements using existing resources.

This study examined long-term effects of stimulant medication on brain development in males with ADHD using a 4-year naturalistic follow-up of the ePOD-methylphenidate randomized controlled trial. Participants were stimulant treatment-naive at baseline and included adolescents and adults. Resting cerebral blood flow (CBF) and CBF response to an acute methylphenidate challenge were assessed with pharmacological MRI at baseline and follow-up after a one-week stimulant washout.

Of the original 50 children and 49 adults, 32 adolescents and 24 adults were included in the final sample. The study found no evidence that stimulant medication use was associated with age-dependent changes over time in resting relative CBF or CBF response to methylphenidate. Initial treatment allocation to methylphenidate or placebo also showed no long-lasting effects. However, across visits, greater stimulant use was associated with lower thalamic resting relative CBF in adults, but not adolescents, and with lower medial prefrontal cortex CBF response in adolescents, but not adults. These associations were present before stimulant treatment and were not related to ADHD symptom severity. Whole-brain analysis found CBF response was associated with noradrenaline transporter distribution, but not dopamine transporter or receptor distributions.

The authors conclude that the study found no evidence for long-lasting stimulant treatment effects on dopamine system development, but identified age-dependent associations between pharmacological MRI measures and later stimulant medication use that may have predictive value for ADHD treatment patterns.

Linguistics researcher Martin O’Leary created Twitter charts showing how seemingly unrelated English words share ancient roots in Proto-Indo-European (PIE), a “mother tongue” spoken around 4,500 to 2,500 BC and thought to have originated north of the Caspian Sea. PIE gave rise to more than 440 modern languages, though no texts survive from it. Examples include “architect” and “dachshund” deriving from PIE “teks” (“to weave”), “science” and “sh*t” from “sek,” and “blue,” “phlegm” and “flamingo” from “bhel.” The charts drew thousands of retweets and fascinated responses from Twitter users.

This cross-sectional study examined associations between personal health literacy, school health literacy environment, and health outcomes among 7,264 teachers from 11 urban and rural schools in Zhengzhou, Henan Province, China. Teachers completed an online questionnaire covering sociodemographics, personal health literacy, school health literacy environment, health status, health-compromising behaviours, health service use, and healthcare costs.

Low health literacy was common: 43.1% of teachers had problematic health literacy and 13.8% had inadequate health literacy. Only 31.0% perceived their school health literacy environment as supportive. Poor health status was reported by 15.0%, at least one health-compromising behaviour by 75.2%, at least one health service use by 82.4%, and annual out-of-pocket healthcare costs of at least 1,000 RMB by 60.7%.

Personal health literacy and perceived school health literacy environment varied by sociodemographic and professional characteristics, including school type, age, marital status, teaching duration, subject taught, health awareness, chronic health conditions, and medical insurance type. After adjustment, inadequate personal health literacy was associated with higher odds of poor health status, health-compromising behaviours, health service use, and higher healthcare costs. Lower perceived supportiveness of the school health literacy environment was also associated with these outcomes.

The study concludes that both individual and organizational health literacy are important to teachers’ health outcomes, and that interventions should address personal health literacy and school environments while considering differences across teacher subgroups.

Webster Elementary dedicated two recycled-material “buddy benches” in honor of former music teacher Robert Pickell, who died in July after falling through his roof at home. More than 100 staff, students, friends, and family gathered for the ceremony, where students wrote goodbye messages and shared memories of his kindness and influence. Pickell’s wife said he valued recycling and would be proud of the benches. Staff said the benches reflect his spirit of friendship. A tree was also planted in his honor, with a plaque to be added later.

Vert Rotors has developed VERT.500, a scaled-up version of its patented small compressor, for industrial use. Created with the Advanced Manufacturing and Automation Centre, it aims to provide clean air with better energy efficiency and lower noise than standard oil-free compressors. Founder Olly Dmitriev said it could reduce noise-protection costs, electricity bills and CO2 emissions for hospitals and businesses relying on clean air.

The speaker values veteran leadership, communication, and trusting speed and effort despite uncertain outcomes. They emphasize learning from experienced teammates, playing with pace, and keeping a sidelined teammate involved because he remains an important part of the team.

Investing.com reports that the S&P 500 fell sharply last week, dropping more than 3% from Thursday’s record high before a likely Monday rebound. Investor sentiment improved slightly, but volatility rose and a deeper correction remains possible. Nasdaq also declined, while crude oil fell after stock weakness and OPEC+ production hike news. The outlook highlights earnings, macro risks, tariffs, jobs data, and demand concerns, suggesting investors may consider more defensive positioning.

The ADS7828 samples the selected analog input onto an internal capacitor, with input current dependent on conversion rate and capacitor charging. It can use an internal 2.5V reference or an external reference; lower reference voltages reduce LSB size but increase apparent offset, gain, and noise errors, which may be reduced by averaging.

The device operates as an I2C slave in standard, fast, and high-speed modes using SDA and SCL. Transfers begin with START and end with STOP or repeated START conditions, use byte-wise acknowledgements, and support slave receiver and slave transmitter modes. The address includes a factory-set 10010 code, A1/A0 device-select bits, and an R/W bit. Up to four devices with the same preset code can share a bus.

Conversions are initiated through a command byte, and 12-bit results are read as two bytes. In fast/standard mode, repeated START can support continuous conversions. In high-speed mode, the ADS7828 may stretch SCL low until conversion completes; repeated START keeps the device in high-speed mode.

When using the internal reference, PD1 must remain set, settling time must be allowed after turn-on, and the reference turns on only after a command with PD1 = 1 followed by STOP or repeated START. With an external reference, PD1 must be 0 and the reference must be settled.

For best performance, power, reference, ground, and digital input transients should be minimized. The supply should be clean and bypassed, external reference noise directly affects results, and ground layout should avoid noisy digital grounding points. The passage also includes TI ordering, material, packaging, reliability, and legal disclaimer information.

Intel may mark the 40th anniversary of the 8086 processor with the rumored Core i7-8086K, listed by retailers with six cores, 12 threads, 12MB L3 cache, and a 5GHz maximum clock speed. Its specifications resemble the Core i7-8700K but are 300MHz faster. As an overclockable K-series chip, it may be a speed-binned 8700K with greater overclocking potential, priced around $480.

The passage discusses female genital mutilation (FGM) in the context of Canadian values. It cites allegations against Detroit doctor Jumana Nagarwala, who denies charges of performing FGM on girls. The Ontario Human Rights Commission says reliable statistics are unavailable but there is evidence FGM occurs in Ontario and Canada, including cases where girls are sent abroad. The passage describes FGM as a cultural practice and child abuse, notes concerns about reinfibulation after childbirth, and quotes doctors opposing non-medically necessary genital mutilation. It concludes that FGM is not a Canadian value and supports screening would-be citizens on such values.

Interfacial mobility governs interface migration and microstructural evolution, but linking atomistic simulations to coarse-grained models remains difficult, especially with solute-drag effects. Conventional molecular dynamics methods assume memory-free Markovian motion, while real interfaces may exhibit memory from broad relaxation times, causing transient sub-diffusion and complicating mobility extraction. The study adapts memory-analysis methods from biochemistry to a simplified kinetic Monte Carlo model of solute-influenced interface migration, examines limitations of the capillary fluctuation method, proposes mobility extraction from mean boundary motion, and applies a time convolutionless propagator approach. The model uses a two-dimensional lattice interface with tunable stiffness, solute binding, and diffusion kinetics.

A memorandum on the Inquiry argues that the war will likely continue into peace discussions and that Germany is using increasingly moderate peace proposals to divide Allied nations and their domestic political groups. It describes Allied vulnerabilities, tensions within Central Europe, and two responses: coercive suppression of receptive opinion, and President Wilson’s broader appeal to widely shared war aims. It warns that public debate over territorial peace terms would weaken morale, reduce the war to nationalism, and split the coalition.
Experienced players must keep the team focused on the game plan, avoid distractions in Calgary, build on strong road play, and prepare for the next challenge.

Scientists studied 105 toy-loving pet dogs and found that 33 showed addictive-like behaviors toward toy play, such as fixating on inaccessible toys, ignoring food, and taking longer to calm down. Researcher Stefanie Riemer says the drive likely comes from the excitement of play rather than the toy itself, and cautions against equating dog behavior with human addiction. The traits were more common in terriers and shepherds and may be rare overall.

The passage presents a study using the Netherlands as a case to evaluate whether subnational COVID-19 interventions during the first wave could have reduced societal burden while maintaining epidemic control. The authors developed an agent-based, geographically and demographically stratified SEIR framework using data on demography, mobility, mixing, hospitalization, and seroprevalence. The model represents about 17 million residents with 170,721 agents across 380 municipalities and simulates hourly contact patterns based on mobile phone mobility data and mixing matrices.

The first Dutch COVID-19 wave was analyzed from February 27 to June 1, 2020, across four policy phases: unchecked transmission, minor interventions, strict national lockdown, and gradual lifting of measures. The model was calibrated to national hospital admissions and reproduced broad national and geographic epidemic patterns, including spread from the south to other regions. It found that mobility reductions contributed most to epidemic control; without them, hospital admissions would have approximately doubled. Behavioral changes also had a substantial effect, while school closures had little impact in the modeled first wave because they occurred relatively late.

The study tested municipality-level interventions triggered by local infection prevalence thresholds of 3%, 1%, 0.33%, and 0.1%. Higher thresholds reduced the number of municipalities under restrictions but increased hospital admissions. A 0.33% threshold produced 410 additional hospital admissions compared with national interventions while allowing 167 municipalities to delay interventions and generating 36 million additional person-days free from restrictions. At this threshold, about 6% of municipalities never underwent interventions. Municipalities remaining intervention-free were mainly in the north and east, which were more rural, isolated, and less densely populated.

The authors conclude that subnational interventions could have reduced societal burden with limited additional health impact if sufficiently detailed local infection monitoring had been available. They note limitations including omitted household-level structure, simplified mobility assumptions, lack of individual itineraries, and use of national rather than geographically stratified mobility reductions. The framework may be adaptable to other countries or policy questions if comparable local data are available.

In February 2013, leaders of MIT Sloan’s Sloan Women in Management club faced whether to cancel, modify, or proceed with their third annual conference, scheduled for the next day, as forecasts predicted a major snowstorm in Boston. The conference, themed “Dare to Fail: Taking Risks When it Matters Most,” had taken 11 months to plan and involved 500 sold-out tickets, 15 confirmed speakers, $38,000 in sponsorships, vendors, catering, and a VIP dinner.

Planning had been difficult, with tensions between co-presidents and conference directors, slow speaker recruitment, one director leaving MIT Sloan, a keynote cancellation two weeks before the event, lagging ticket sales, operational complications, and budget changes. By the week of the conference, however, speakers, sponsorship, marketing, and logistics had largely come together.

On February 7, weather forecasts worsened, attendees began asking about cancellation or refunds, and MIT had not yet decided whether to close. Vendors were scheduled to begin setup at 2:00 p.m., after which SWIM would incur significant costs, including potentially higher rental fees if MIT later closed. The leadership team, advised by Student Life Office staff, narrowed its options to cancel before setup, hold a half-day conference, or wait for more information, knowing the decision would affect attendees, speakers, sponsors, costs, safety, and SWIM’s reputation.

Baking powder and baking soda both help doughs rise but differ chemically. Baking soda reacts with acids, while baking powder contains baking soda and dry acid. They can be substituted with adjusted amounts. Baking powder expires faster, especially in humidity; both can be tested by bubbling reactions.

Federal Reserve minutes showed officials broadly supported September’s quarter-point rate cut due to labor market weakness, but were split on further easing. A 10-9 majority expected two more cuts by year-end, while Stephen Miran dissented in favor of a half-point cut. Officials still expected inflation to return to 2%, though concerns remained. A government shutdown could limit key economic data before the October meeting.

The paper introduces LLM-proposed Open Taxonomy (LOT), an inductive method for identifying and classifying reasoning differences between large reasoning models (LRMs) directly from their outputs. LOT uses an LLM to compare paired reasoning traces, propose distinguishing natural-language features, annotate new traces into feature vectors, and train a logistic classifier to predict the source model. When classification fails, LOT adds new features and retrains.

The authors apply LOT to 12 open-source LRMs across math, science, and code reasoning datasets. LOT achieves 80–100% classification accuracy when models differ substantially in scale, base family, or domain specialization, outperforming few-shot prompting, Verbalized Machine Learning, and a fixed human-defined taxonomy. It identifies interpretable differences, such as smaller Qwen3 models showing more circular reasoning or theory-switching, Qwen3-32B more reliably checking applicability and maintaining stepwise analysis, and a code-specialized model sometimes using Python-style reasoning on math problems.

Experiments show that models from the same base family are harder to distinguish, while frequency-based reasoning features improve classification on harder benchmarks. A case study links LOT-identified reasoning differences among Qwen3 models to GPQA-Diamond performance gaps. Test-time interventions that modify smaller Qwen models’ reasoning traces according to these differences improve accuracy by 3.3–5.7% in several cases.

The paper concludes that LOT can classify, interpret, and help explain reasoning differences among LRMs, while noting limitations including lack of controlled causal evidence for model attributes, possible variation in LLM-generated taxonomies, incomplete feature coverage, and unexplored effects of the annotator model.

Comcast Corporation has a consensus “Buy” rating from 23 brokerages, with an average 12-month target price of $79.31. Several analysts recently raised ratings or price targets, including Jefferies, Deutsche Bank, Instinet, Macquarie, and RBC Capital Markets. Company insiders sold 229,839 shares valued at $17.17 million in the last quarter, while insiders own 1.27% of the stock. Institutional investors own 82.03%.

Comcast opened at $75.71, with a market cap of $179.87 billion, a P/E ratio of 21.21, and a beta of 1.07. The stock has traded between $56.59 and $76.87 over 12 months. A 2-for-1 stock split was scheduled for February 20. Comcast reported quarterly EPS of $0.89, beating estimates by $0.02, with revenue of $21 billion, up 9.2% year over year. The company also raised its quarterly dividend to $0.1575 per share.

A new study suggests passengers who want to avoid catching a cold or flu on an airplane should choose a window seat and stay there, limiting contact with others. Researchers observed passenger movement and tested surfaces and air on 10 flights, but found no cold or flu viruses and observed only one coughing passenger. The Boeing-funded study used modeling to estimate that, on a 150-passenger flight, about one person would be infected by a hypothetical sick passenger in an aisle seat. Researchers not involved said the study was too small for broad conclusions but valuable because airplane virus transmission is little studied. The study found aisle-seat passengers moved more often than middle- or window-seat passengers, and the 11 people seated nearest an infectious passenger faced the highest risk.

Amazon updated Alexa to support Outlook.com calendars, allowing users to add or review events through connected Alexa devices. Outlook calendars can be added in the iOS Alexa app. Amazon also added hands-free Alexa support to Tap speakers, while maintaining about eight hours of battery life and adding echo spatial perception.

The lecture discusses policy with behavioral agents, focusing on paternalism, internalities, libertarian paternalism, market solutions, nudges, and sludges. Traditional neoclassical reasons for government intervention include externalities, public goods, redistribution, macroeconomic policy, competition policy, and innovation-related market failures. Behavioral policy adds “internalities,” where people fail to fully account for costs or benefits imposed on their future selves.

Paternalism is defined as influencing or controlling people’s conduct for their own good, rather than to address externalities. It may be warranted when people make mistakes due to self-control problems, limited attention, memory failures, incorrect beliefs, overoptimism, overconfidence, projection bias, attribution bias, or discrimination. It is less clearly warranted for preferences such as risk preferences, social preferences, reference dependence, or motivated beliefs, where people may derive utility from their beliefs.

The lecture distinguishes hard paternalism from soft paternalism. Hard paternalism changes prices substantially, mandates choices, bans products, or imposes taxes. Soft paternalism includes libertarian paternalism, which influences behavior while preserving freedom of choice, and asymmetric paternalism, which aims to help people who make mistakes while minimally affecting those already optimizing. Cigarette taxes illustrate the difficulty: they may help smokers who underestimate future harms but harm smokers who knowingly choose to smoke.

Arguments against paternalism include government error, lack of information about individual preferences, heterogeneity, regulatory capture, corruption, inefficient implementation, threats to freedom of choice, dislike of restrictions, and difficulty choosing the right policy. Arguments in favor include helping people make fewer mistakes, reducing costly decision-making burdens, screening out exploitative options, and using opt-out or low-cost interventions that do not substantially restrict choice.

Examples of popular paternalism include Social Security, Medicare, restrictions on 401(k) investment menus, consumer safety regulations, mandatory education, cigarette taxes, bans on prostitution or polygamy, mask mandates in some places, junk food restrictions in schools, calorie disclosure laws, and default 401(k) enrollment. Unpopular or contested examples include helmet and seatbelt mandates, junk food taxes, gambling and pornography laws, soda size bans, and some drug prohibitions. The lecture notes large variation across states in cigarette taxes, alcohol taxes, mask policies, and marijuana legalization.

Some nudges have large effects, such as automatic retirement enrollment and text reminders for court appearances. However, not all nudges work: the HeartStrong randomized trial using reminders, incentives, wireless pill bottles, and social support after heart attacks had no effect. Evidence from nudge units often shows smaller effects than published academic studies, possibly due to publication bias or implementation differences. Some people also dislike being nudged, as shown in energy-use comparison reports where some individuals were willing to pay not to receive them. This raises concerns for asymmetric paternalism and suggests opt-out options may be useful.

The Save More Tomorrow plan is presented as a successful example of libertarian paternalism. Employees could voluntarily commit future pay raises to increased retirement savings, with automatic contribution increases after raises and the option to opt out. The plan uses behavioral principles including present bias, loss aversion, reference dependence, and defaults, while preserving choice.

The lecture argues that markets do not necessarily solve behavioral problems. Firms may provide helpful products, but they may also exploit naive consumers through targeting, advertising, and complex financial products. Behavioral industrial organization studies how firms exploit behavioral consumers and how regulation, such as disclosure rules or interest-rate caps, might help.

Finally, the lecture discusses “sludges,” which use behavioral frictions to harm or exploit people, such as burdensome rebate forms or difficult voter registration procedures. Reducing sludges can improve welfare alongside implementing beneficial nudges. The course concludes that psychological factors are important in economic behavior, that individuals can benefit from understanding their own biases, and that policymakers, firms, and designers should account for behavioral considerations while being cautious about welfare effects.

SOS Pressure Defense presents a basketball defensive system intended to address increasingly skilled modern offenses. It emphasizes pressure defense as a growing alternative or reinforcement to containment defenses and offers techniques applicable to various defensive philosophies. The program focuses on developing fundamentals through a simple-to-complex progression, from one-on-one positioning and movement to full team pressure, with daily reinforcement. It uses consistent S-O-S key words to identify and trigger on-ball and off-ball defensive actions. Players are taught to pressure opponents toward designated “checkpoint” areas away from high-percentage shooting zones. The system supports switching on screens as a way to reduce confusion and disrupt offensive motion. It also stresses stopping transition offense by applying backcourt pressure immediately after rebounds and assigning clear roles to all defenders. Overall, SOS defense aims to create coordinated, intense team pressure that limits scoring options, forces turnovers, denies passing lanes, and helps teams compete more effectively.

The speaker says a player’s playoff impact comes less from numbers than from hard forechecking, grit, and commitment after a tough regular season. Facing elimination, the team is relying on internal energy, leadership, experience, discipline, and a desire to keep playing together. Researchers studied fossilized embryos of Protoceratops from Mongolia and Hypacrosaurus from Alberta to determine dinosaur egg incubation times. By counting daily growth lines in developing teeth, they found Protoceratops incubated for nearly three months and Hypacrosaurus for about six months. These periods are longer than expected and closer to reptiles than modern birds, suggesting birds evolved faster incubation after diverging from other dinosaurs. The findings indicate long incubation may have exposed dinosaur eggs and parents to prolonged risks and reduced their ability to reproduce quickly, possibly disadvantaging non-avian dinosaurs during the end-Cretaceous extinction. The Hypacrosaurus embryo came from Devil’s Coulee in southern Alberta, a rich nesting site. Researchers expect further embryo studies on other dinosaur species.

Trump asked the Supreme Court to review lower-court rulings against his executive order ending birthright citizenship. After Trump issued the order on Jan. 20, federal challenges led to nationwide injunctions blocking enforcement. In March, the administration asked the Supreme Court to limit universal injunctions, not to decide the citizenship issue. In June, the court ruled 6-3 that lower courts generally lack authority to issue nationwide injunctions, leaving narrower relief questions to lower courts.

Subsequent rulings again blocked the order. Judges certified classes of affected children or found nationwide relief necessary, and the 9th Circuit ruled the order invalid under the Fourteenth Amendment. The administration indicated in August that it would seek Supreme Court review, then filed petitions asking the justices to review the 9th Circuit ruling and a New Hampshire decision. It did not request fast-track review, so if the court grants review, arguments would likely occur in 2026 with a decision expected near the end of the term.

Andrew Anton Sabo appealed his Wisconsin convictions for possessing cocaine with intent to deliver as a repeat offense and being a felon in possession of firearms. He argued that evidence seized from his residence under a search warrant should have been suppressed because the warrant affidavit lacked probable cause, contained false statements warranting a Franks-Mann hearing, and relied on an informant whose identity should have been disclosed.

The affidavit stated that a citizen informant told Officer Rodolfo Ayala that Sabo, known as “Drew,” possessed a firearm despite being a felon and was packaging cocaine for distribution at a West Burnham Street residence. Ayala identified Sabo through police records, confirmed his felony status and probation, and observed him at the residence. A search found firearms, ammunition, suspected crack cocaine, drug paraphernalia, cash, surveillance cameras, and marijuana plants.

The trial court denied Sabo’s motions to suppress, compel disclosure of the informant, and hold a Franks-Mann hearing. It found the informant’s details sufficiently credible and independently corroborated, and found Sabo had not made a substantial preliminary showing that the affidavit contained deliberate or reckless falsehoods.

The Court of Appeals affirmed. It held that the affidavit supported probable cause, the trial court reasonably found the informant credible, Sabo failed to justify a Franks-Mann hearing, and the court properly declined to order disclosure of the informant’s identity.

The passage describes techniques for selecting an ingress edge region in an Internet-based overlay network used to transport traffic such as IPsec traffic for customer branch offices. Traditional WAN approaches such as MPLS are efficient and secure but costly, while Internet-based overlay networks can provide optimized routing, security, and reliability using CDN-style infrastructure.

The disclosed method uses an overlay network authoritative DNS service and edge regions called NEdges. A customer premises router first resolves a service hostname through a corporate DNS resolver, which may return an edge region suitable for the resolver’s location rather than the router’s location. The router then establishes an IKEv2 session and outer IPsec tunnel to that first edge. After tunnel establishment, the first edge performs a secondary DNS lookup based on the router IP address to determine whether it is the appropriate ingress region. If another edge is preferred, the first edge sends an IKEv2 redirect message directing the router to establish a new tunnel with the second edge.

The system may also perform later lookups to verify that the current edge remains appropriate. If the edge determines it is no longer valid, it may intentionally drop liveness probe responses sent over the tunnel, causing the router to treat the tunnel as failed and initiate selection of another edge region. The described functions may be implemented in software on standard server hardware within a CDN or overlay network infrastructure.

WORD and BYTE writes to PMC registers can corrupt current or future register writes because shadow registers update byte lanes but operational registers update at 32-bit granularity. Corruption may be local or cross-register. ACPI permits WORD/BYTE access to certain registers, causing this issue; proprietary non-ACPI registers require DWORD access. An SMI I/O trap can control ACPI register accesses.

The lecture discusses exact solutions for nonlinear PDEs, focusing on inviscid Burgers’ equation, viscous Burgers’ equation, Korteweg-de Vries (KDV), and related Hamilton-Jacobi equations. For inviscid Burgers’ equation with a delta-function initial condition, the solution is described as a fan followed by a shock. Conservation of mass gives the shock position as \(X=\sqrt{2t}\), and the solution satisfies the shock jump condition and entropy condition.

The professor then explains an exact formula for Burgers’ equation obtained by studying the viscous form and letting viscosity go to zero. A change of variables transforms viscous Burgers’ equation into the heat equation, whose known solution leads to a minimization formula in the inviscid limit. The limiting behavior is governed by the point where the exponent is minimized.

The lecture also briefly covers KDV, noting its role in water waves and its numerical discovery as a completely integrable nonlinear equation. Traveling wave solutions called solitons can interact and reemerge with unchanged shapes, suggesting hidden linearity. The professor mentions nonlinear Schrödinger equations as another integrable example, contrasts these with Navier-Stokes equations, and previews later topics including numerical methods, level set methods, financial mathematics PDEs, and large linear systems.

AfriForum appointed forensic scientist Dr David Klatzow to investigate the cause of the Knysna fires. The first phase involves gathering information, meeting role-players, assessing the disaster area by air, and inviting public submissions.

The passage is an Enron email compiling June 28–29, 2001 energy-related news articles. Major topics include a California Senate committee citing Enron and Mirant for contempt over subpoenaed documents in a power-pricing investigation, with a July 10 compliance deadline; Edison International obtaining $1.19 billion in financing; California regulators exempting oil refineries from rolling blackouts; Standard & Poor’s removing California from credit watch after bridge loans; and State Controller Kathleen Connell planning to release unedited long-term power contracts. Gray Davis’s energy-crisis handling, slow congressional action on President Bush’s energy proposals, restored conservation funding, forecasts of economic effects from the crisis, Southern California Gas price cuts, SMUD’s web-based demand reduction program, Alan Greenspan’s comments on energy markets and price caps, and federal approval of temporary wholesale power price controls for New York.

Toto Wolff said Mercedes may need stress, tension and disruption between Lewis Hamilton and Valtteri Bottas to maintain dominance. After a controversy-free season that delivered a fourth straight constructors’ title, Wolff suggested stronger rivalry could push both drivers to improve, despite past tensions between Hamilton and Nico Rosberg.

Reinaldo De Jesus Henao, 36, was arrested at Coachella on suspicion of stealing over 100 phones after attendees used Find My Phone. Police said phones were found in his backpack. He was charged with grand theft and receiving stolen property, then released on $10,000 bail.

Astronomers observed rogue planet Cha 1170-7626, about 600 light-years away, rapidly accreting gas and dust at 6 billion metric tons per second, the fastest growth recorded for any planet. VLT and James Webb data showed its accretion rate rose up to eightfold from earlier months, with hotter, brighter material and new water vapor signatures. The burst resembled rare growth spurts seen in young stars, suggesting a starlike origin, and researchers plan further observations.

Thruxton’s 50th anniversary meeting will feature historic races, high-speed demonstrations and the opening of the new £2million Thruxton Centre by Nigel Mansell and Murray Walker. Theresa May is reportedly set to ask Cabinet to support a “soft” Brexit plan at Chequers, including continued UK alignment with some EU rules on goods and agricultural standards, an end to freedom of movement with easier access for EU citizens than other migrants, and a customs arrangement where the UK collects tariffs on behalf of the EU. The paper presents NeuroAdapter, an end-to-end brain decoding framework that conditions a latent diffusion model directly on fMRI activity instead of mapping brain signals through intermediate foundation-model embedding spaces. The method uses parcel-wise fMRI embeddings, cross-attention modules in Stable Diffusion, fMRI token dropout, and min-SNR loss weighting, while keeping most diffusion-model parameters frozen. During evaluation, a brain encoder selects the best reconstruction among candidates by comparing predicted and measured fMRI responses.

The authors also introduce IBBI, an interpretability framework that analyzes cross-attention dynamics during diffusion. It provides a brain-directed view of parcel contributions over denoising steps and an image-directed view showing where specific brain ROIs attend in reconstructed images.

Experiments on NSD, NSD-Imagery, and Deeprecon show that NeuroAdapter achieves competitive reconstruction performance, especially on high-level semantic metrics, without relying on external embedding spaces. Results suggest it can generalize to mental imagery and recover category-level and some low-level visual properties. Interpretability analyses show how different cortical parcels and ROIs influence image generation, and perturbation experiments indicate that masking high-level ROIs substantially alters semantic content while masking low-level ROIs has less semantic impact.

The speaker says he has moved on from a league decision about a recent incident and is focused on the next Stanley Cup Finals game. He respects the league’s decision, wants to avoid goalie interference and penalties, credits several players for different strengths, and says time away from the rink is spent with family and managing a fantasy baseball team.

AOL Instant Messenger announced it will shut down permanently on December 15 after operating since 1997. Once a leading U.S. messaging service, AIM declined as cell phone messaging and social media platforms changed how people communicate.

The Colorado Supreme Court reviewed a discovery order in a personal injury case brought by Erin Bond and her family against YMCA of the Rockies after Erin was severely injured in a truck accident. YMCA sought notes and records from the petitioners’ mental health therapists concerning psychological evaluations and treatment. The petitioners provided an evaluation report but sought a protective order against disclosure of therapy notes and records. The district court denied the protective order and ordered production subject to confidentiality.

The court held that although the petitioners waived physician-patient and psychologist-patient privileges by seeking damages for mental suffering and psychiatric expenses, the district court abused its discretion by failing to balance the petitioners’ confidentiality and treatment-related interests against YMCA’s need for discovery. The court made the rule absolute and remanded for reconsideration under the proper balancing standard, noting that protective procedures such as in camera review and tailored protective orders may be used.

Earth experiences total solar eclipses because the moon, though about 400 times smaller than the sun, is about 400 times closer, making them appear similar in size. Other planets lack the right conditions. The moon is slowly moving away from Earth, so total eclipses like this are temporary; in about 600 million years, it will no longer fully cover the sun.

The goal is to improve resource efficiency while maintaining availability and reducing reconnection delays for users.

Responsible integration requires governance frameworks, data privacy, bias mitigation, human oversight, transparency, accessibility, equity, and continuous evaluation.

It recommends that higher education institutions adopt AI with clear vision, goals, guidelines, and safeguards, while cautioning against student use of AI in schooling and coursework where it may weaken analytical, critical thinking, and academic skills.

Ramu Damodaran highlights water as a universal need and a focus of United Nations action. The Put-Call ratio is a sentiment indicator that compares put options to call options using volume or open interest. It is often used as a contrarian signal: high readings may indicate fear or panic, while low readings may indicate complacency. Puts give the holder the right to sell shares at a set price within a time frame, while calls give the right to buy shares. The ratio is calculated by dividing traded put options by traded call options, though volume and open interest differ. There are different Put-Call ratios for indices and stocks, and no universal rule defines a good or bad reading. The passage states that backtests found the Put-Call ratio less effective than other sentiment indicators, such as the VIX, and that the authors do not use it in their trading strategies. The ratio is available on many trading websites, apps, exchanges, and platforms, though free downloadable sources may be difficult to find.

The 2018 Chevrolet Equinox offers an available 1.6L turbo-diesel engine with highway fuel efficiency of 6.0 L/100km on the FWD model, expected to lead its segment. Developed by General Motors with extensive testing, it includes a Diesel Exhaust Fluid system integrated by the Canadian Technical Centre in Oshawa. The all-new Equinox features updated design, increased cargo space, connectivity, available safety technologies, and turbocharged engine options. The LakeSmart Team is delivering its summer Dock Talk program to share information on maintaining healthy lake ecosystems around Lake of the Woods and nearby lakes. The passage describes apparatuses and methods for AI-based image encoding and decoding. An AI decoding apparatus decodes the image data into a second image, determines from AI data and DNN availability whether to perform AI up-scaling, and either outputs a third image generated by an up-scaling DNN or outputs the second image.

The AI data may include resolution differences, first-image information, codec or bitrate information, identifiers or settings for DNNs, and reference information such as pixel positions or encoding parameters. The up-scaling DNN may use convolution layers, activation layers, scaler components, and bypass scaling, with DNN settings selected according to AI data, image characteristics, display capability, stored settings, or user input. If the up-scaling DNN or its setting information is unavailable, the system may output the decoded second image, request display-side up-scaling, or perform legacy up-scaling. The first and second DNNs may be jointly trained so that down-scaling and up-scaling targets correspond, supporting lower bitrate encoding while reconstructing higher-resolution output.

The passage describes techniques for reducing power consumption in near-eye display systems by controlling luminance levels of individual light sources based on a user’s field of view or gaze direction. A maximum luminance location is determined, such as the center of the user’s field of view or the foveal region, using eye tracking. Light sources closer to this location are driven at higher luminance levels than light sources farther away, even when associated with the same input display value. Different display zones may use different relationships between input display values and luminance levels, with central zones having larger luminance ranges than peripheral zones.

The disclosed systems may include OLED, AMOLED, micro-LED, or other display panels, each light source being driven by a respective drive circuit. Eye-tracking subsystems may use illumination sources, cameras, pupil detection, corneal reflections, glints, calibration data, and gaze estimation to determine eye position and gaze direction. A controller or display driver may use this data to generate luminance maps for display zones and instruct display gate and source drivers accordingly.

The passage also describes artificial reality systems, including head-mounted displays, glasses-based displays, waveguide displays, image source assemblies, projectors, scanning mirrors, sensors, controllers, and consoles for VR, AR, and MR applications. The luminance-control techniques are intended to improve display power efficiency while maintaining user experience.

Harvey Weinstein was indicted in New York on rape and criminal sex act charges, advancing the first criminal case stemming from sexual misconduct allegations against him. Manhattan District Attorney Cyrus R. Vance Jr. said the indictment moved Weinstein closer to accountability. Weinstein’s lawyers said he declined to testify before the grand jury because he lacked time to prepare and claimed political pressure made indictment inevitable. Weinstein, freed on $1 million bail with electronic monitoring, denies all nonconsensual sex allegations. His lawyer disputed the rape allegation, while accuser Lucia Evans has publicly alleged Weinstein forced her to perform oral sex in 2004. Vance previously faced criticism for declining to prosecute Weinstein in a 2015 groping allegation, prompting a state review.

The lecture explains how the large-N expansion of gauge theories has the same mathematical structure as the genus expansion of string scattering amplitudes when the string coupling is identified with 1/N. Single-trace operators correspond to glueball or string states, and Feynman diagrams of fixed genus can be viewed as discrete triangulations of two-dimensional surfaces. Summing over such diagrams resembles summing over string worldsheets, but making this precise for field theories is difficult because Feynman diagram weights look unlike string actions and a continuum geometric picture is expected only at strong coupling.

The speaker notes that this philosophy can be made explicit in simpler systems such as matrix integrals and matrix quantum mechanics, where large-N expansions also organize diagrams by topology. Including fields in the fundamental representation leads to surfaces with boundaries, corresponding to open strings, while using real symmetric or antisymmetric matrices leads to non-orientable surfaces and non-orientable strings.

Attempts to describe large-N QCD directly as a string theory in 3+1-dimensional Minkowski spacetime fail because such string theories are inconsistent except in special dimensions, and compactifying higher-dimensional string theory would introduce a massless spin-2 particle absent in QCD. The lecture then motivates considering a string theory in one higher noncompact dimension, supported by holographic reasoning and string-theory consistency. If a large-N field theory is conformal, requiring scale symmetry fixes the five-dimensional metric to anti-de Sitter form, suggesting that a large-N CFT in d dimensions may correspond to string theory on AdS\(_{d+1}\), with 1/N related to the string coupling.

The lecture briefly reviews the history from early string theory, QCD, ’t Hooft’s large-N expansion, black hole thermodynamics, lattice QCD, matrix models, the holographic principle, D-branes, Maldacena’s 1997 examples, and Witten’s connection to holography. It then begins preparing for the derivation of the correspondence by introducing string theory basics: a string worldsheet embedded in spacetime, the induced metric, the Nambu-Goto action as worldsheet area, and the equivalent Polyakov action using an auxiliary worldsheet metric. Quantizing strings is described as quantizing two-dimensional gravity coupled to scalar fields.

Touch Football Australia and the NRL have launched the NRL Touch Premiership, beginning May 18 as a curtain raiser to NRL matches. Elite male and female touch players will represent teams aligned with six NRL clubs, with games broadcast nationally over seven rounds. Brigginshaw uses touch to maintain fitness but said her Jillaroos contract likely prevents her from joining the inaugural competition.

Instructions for replacing an HDD with a SanDisk SSD: shut down the computer, disconnect power, and remove the battery for notebooks. For desktops, open the case, disconnect SATA data and power cables from the HDD, remove it, install the SSD—using a 3.5-inch mounting adapter if needed—connect SATA cables, close the case, plug in, and power on. The old HDD may be kept as a backup.

The PGA848 linear input range extends within 3 V of either supply and maintains common-mode rejection across temperature. A typical application drives an ADS8860 16-bit, 1 MSPS SAR ADC using ±15 V input-stage supplies and a 5.3 V output/ADC supply to help protect ADC inputs during overdrive. A REF6250 5 V reference and resistor divider set the PGA848 REF pin to 2.5 V, buffered by an OPA192. Three filters address EMI/RFI, PGA feedback bandwidth, and ADC charge kickback; the nominal bandwidth is 318 kHz, changing to 277 kHz at high feedback-resistor tolerance, with –0.1 dB flatness to 41 kHz. Supply voltages above 40 V permanently damage the device. Layout guidance emphasizes matched input paths, close bypass capacitors, separation of input traces from noisy traces, reduced leakage and parasitic capacitance, and minimized thermal gradients. The passage also lists TI simulation tools, related documentation, support resources, trademarks, ESD precautions, revision history, packaging information, and legal disclaimers.

Leapfrog reported signs of improved hospital patient safety in its latest Safety Grades. Five hospitals earned an “A” for the first time after previously receiving an “F,” 46 hospitals earned their first “A” since the program began, and 89 hospitals with an “A” had once received a “D” or “F.” Rhode Island, Hawaii, Wisconsin and Idaho moved from near the bottom to the top ten in percentage of “A” hospitals. Maryland improved with three “A” hospitals and six hospitals rising to “B,” while Washington, D.C. received its first “A” hospital since 2013. Of about 2,500 hospitals graded, 30% earned “A,” 28% “B,” 35% “C,” 6% “D” and 1% “F.” The Leapfrog Hospital Safety Grade is updated twice yearly and is free to the public.

The Boathouse at City Point will open June 17 on Hopewell’s riverfront at 701 West Randolph Street. The 6,000-square-foot restaurant includes patio and event space and is the fourth Central Virginia Boathouse location. Officials describe it as part of Hopewell riverfront revitalization. It will serve lunch, dinner and Sunday brunch.

Madison Realty Capital provided JDS Development Group a $137 million construction loan for Monad Terrace, a 59-residence waterfront project in South Beach, Miami, designed by Jean Nouvel with Kobi Karp Architecture and Interior Design.
