Archaeologists used Lidar laser technology to uncover over 60,000 previously unknown Mayan structures in Guatemala’s Petén jungle, including house foundations, fortifications, causeways, and a seven-story pyramid. The technology detects hidden structures beneath dense vegetation and creates detailed 3D maps, saving researchers extensive fieldwork. Archaeologists said the discovery could significantly change understanding of Mayan civilization, suggesting it controlled large territories with millions of people, advanced food production, trade networks, and engineered water management. Researchers said population estimates may have been greatly underestimated, possibly reaching 10 to 15 million people, including in areas previously thought uninhabitable. A National Geographic special on the findings was scheduled for February 6.

TeraWulf is shifting from bitcoin mining to digital infrastructure, supported by AI hosting contracts, an expanded Fluidstack deal, and a $3.2 billion Google commitment. The passage says these could support $760 million in annual revenue, with plans to scale power capacity to 1,150 MW by 2030 and potentially reach $1.5 billion in annual revenue. It also includes promotional material, author disclosures, investment-risk disclaimers, related article titles, and chart range data.

Britain’s exam regulator Ofqual said OCR should be fined £175,000 after a 2017 exam question wrongly described Tybalt as hating the Capulet family instead of the Montagues. The error affected Romeo and Juliet candidates, with some grades based on other exam sections.

Steven Kean asks how important the Export-Import Bank funding fight is to Enron, forwarding media mentions. The main article says Boeing, Caterpillar, Enron, Halliburton and others are lobbying Congress against a proposed 25% cut to Ex-Im Bank’s $865 million operating budget, which the White House calls corporate welfare. Enron is listed as the ninth-largest Ex-Im recipient in fiscal 2000, with $135 million in financing.

Other forwarded mentions include Houston office development tied to Enron’s tower, Dutch gas market competition involving Enron Europe trading at emerging hubs, and California energy issues. Southern California Edison’s tentative $2.7 billion transmission-line sale to the state may take until 2002, while suppliers including Enron Wind have sued Edison over unpaid bills. Sierra Pacific’s CEO doubts SEC approval of its $3.1 billion acquisition of Enron’s Portland General Electric due to financial weakness. California’s announced long-term power contracts remain partly unsigned, with Enron saying terms are agreed except for credit details. U.S. natural gas prices fell as demand eased, and work on Enron’s Transwestern San Juan lateral was completed.

In a cross-sectional analysis of 45 patients aged 50–74 with CSF biomarker-confirmed mild Alzheimer disease, researchers evaluated whether BCHE-K carrier status affected age at diagnosis among APOE4 carriers. Among 33 APOE4 carriers, BCHE-K carriers were diagnosed 6.4 years earlier on average than BCHE-K noncarriers (60.6 vs 67.0 years; P < .001). A similar effect was not observed in 12 APOE4 noncarriers.

APOE4 carriers with BCHE-K also had a baseline age more than 6 years younger, with slightly higher amyloid and tau accumulation. APOE4 carriers showed greater amyloid pathology than noncarriers, and APOE4 homozygotes with BCHE-K exemplified an amyloid-predominant, limbic-amnestic phenotype with lower markers of glial activation.

Multiple regression linked amyloid accumulation with APOE4 carrier status, larger ventricular volume, less synaptic injury, and less tau, while tau pathophysiology was associated with neuroaxonal damage, synaptic injury, and glial activation. The authors conclude that BCHE-K may contribute to earlier Alzheimer disease diagnosis in APOE4 carriers under age 75 and that glial activation may help explain APOE4 and BCHE-K effects on early Alzheimer disease phenotype. The findings require confirmation in larger prospective longitudinal studies.

A 5m bronze sculpture, “The Last Three,” has gone on display in New York City to memorialize the last three Northern White Rhinos, now extinct in the wild. The work sparked debate after critic Jerry Saltz condemned it, while others praised its role in raising awareness about endangered rhinos.

Legal and public notices for the week of May 31, 2018 include vehicle possession notices for a 2000 Chevy Silverado and a 1999 Suzuki; probate land sales for the estates of Alfred Gene Stewart Jr. and Betty Rose Drake; creditor notices for the estates of Leon Dewayne Barnes, Nellie Belle Hunter, and Sarah Kaye Stallings; service by publication in an adoption and parental rights case involving Jason Rodgers; a Department of Children’s Services notice to Danny Lee Brown; trustee’s sales for properties at 217 College Avenue East and 9 Hills Dale Lane East in Carthage; and links to the Town of Gordonsville budget and South Side Utility District water reports.

The lecture focuses on structures for finite impulse response (FIR) systems. FIR systems have a finite number of nonzero impulse response samples, and their difference equation corresponds to the convolution sum, with coefficients equal to impulse response values. Direct form, transposed form, and cascade implementations can be applied to FIR systems, while the usual parallel form is not applicable because FIR systems have no poles.

For linear phase FIR systems, the impulse response satisfies a symmetry condition, allowing implementation with about half the number of multipliers compared with a general direct form structure. An example with impulse response length 8 uses seven delays but only four coefficients by adding symmetric delayed input samples before multiplication.

The lecture also introduces the frequency sampling structure, derived by expressing the FIR system through discrete Fourier transform coefficients, which are samples of the frequency response. This structure appears recursive and includes poles, but these poles are canceled by zeros from a preceding factor, leaving an overall FIR system. Its disadvantages include reliance on pole-zero cancellation, but its advantages include efficiency when many frequency samples are zero and usefulness in implementing filter banks with shared structure.

The lecture concludes by comparing digital filter structures using criteria such as number of delays, number of multiplications, modularity, and finite register length effects. Parameter quantization affects pole locations, with higher-order polynomial implementations being more sensitive. Cascade and parallel structures are less sensitive than direct form structures. Different second-order implementations, such as direct form and coupled form, lead to different sets of realizable pole locations under coefficient quantization.

Ultralight backpacking is defined here as carrying a base weight of 10 pounds or less, excluding worn items and consumables. The author traces the movement to Mark Jenkins’ 1994 Backpacker article and emphasizes that reducing weight begins with bringing fewer unnecessary items. Gear should be evaluated by whether it is needed to stay warm, comfortable, well-fed, and safe. The biggest weight reductions usually come from the backpack, sleep system, and shelter, but experimentation—such as trying tarps, cowboy camping, or quilts—helps determine real needs. The author presents ultralight backpacking as a philosophy focused on comfort, safety, and enjoyment with less burden, rather than simply hitting a weight target.

The study analyzed US death certificate data from 2014–2020 to examine the relationship between cancer mortality and COVID-19, accounting for underlying and multiple-cause death coding. Nationally, underlying-cause cancer deaths did not increase during 2020, while multiple-cause cancer deaths rose modestly by about 12,000 deaths, a 2% elevation over baseline. Hematological cancers showed the largest cancer-specific increase at 5%, while pancreatic and lung cancers showed little or no excess mortality. In contrast, diabetes and Alzheimer’s mortality rose substantially and tracked COVID-19 waves closely.

State-level analyses of New York, California, and Texas found no notable increases in underlying-cause cancer mortality and only modest multiple-cause increases, with the largest in New York during its spring 2020 wave. A demographic model suggested that differences in age, population size, and baseline mortality risk could explain much of the variation in excess mortality across chronic conditions. The authors conclude that cancer mortality increased at most modestly during the first pandemic year, likely reflecting competing mortality risks from cancer itself rather than protection from immunosuppression, while hematological cancers were more affected than other cancer types. Future research should examine hospitalization, Long COVID, screening changes, and longer-term cancer mortality patterns.

Researchers sequenced RSV genomes from 105 symptomatic patients at Massachusetts General Hospital and outpatient practices during the autumn 2022 U.S. RSV surge. They recovered 54 near-complete and 23 partial genomes and identified some respiratory co-infections. Genomic analysis showed the surge involved multiple pre-existing RSV lineages: 91% RSV-A and 9% RSV-B, with RSV-A genomes spanning at least 10 distinct lineages. Several lineages were shared between Massachusetts and Washington samples. Genetic divergence was consistent with expected RSV evolutionary rates, not accelerated evolution. The findings were inconsistent with a single highly transmissible RSV lineage causing the surge, and the authors suggested investigating non-viral factors, including altered RSV dynamics during the COVID-19 pandemic.

M. de Martens states that foreign ships generally cannot be searched or arrested on the high seas, except vessels suspected of piracy, and wrongful arrest entails damages. The Cape Horn Pigeon was seized 125 miles from Russian land and 84 miles from Japanese land while whaling on the high seas. Its captain protested, and the Russian officer said indemnity would be paid if the seizure was wrongful. Russia later stated that an inquiry found the vessel had navigated within Russian waters but gave no evidence and found no grounds for confiscation. The passage argues that innocent passage in territorial waters is established under international law and that the seizure violated treaty and international rights. Russia acknowledged the arrest resulted from a misunderstanding, returned the vessel, and offered inadequate indemnity. The owners, officers, and crew claimed $45,000 for loss of the vessel’s service, calculated from average prior whaling results minus the catch already made. The claim is presented as direct damages caused by the seizure, with precedents cited from the Betsey and Neptune cases.

Ben Affleck was seen smiling and looking upbeat at what is believed to be an outpatient treatment centre in LA, seven months after announcing he had completed treatment for alcohol addiction. In March, he publicly addressed his struggle, saying rehab was the first of many steps toward recovery. He said he wanted to live fully, be the best father possible, and show his children there is no shame in seeking help. He also credited support from family, friends, and co-parent Jennifer Garner.

The passage discusses environmental education as a key process for addressing environmental crises and supporting sustainable development. It describes global environmental concerns such as global warming, disasters, resource depletion, pollution, and environmental degradation, and notes international milestones including the 1972 Stockholm Conference, the 1992 Earth Summit, Agenda 21, and the 1975 Belgrade workshop by UNEP and UNESCO.

Environmental education is defined as an interdisciplinary, lifelong process that builds awareness, knowledge, attitudes, skills, participation, and evaluation ability to help individuals and communities prevent and solve environmental problems. Its guiding principles include considering natural and human-made environments, using interdisciplinary and participatory approaches, addressing local to global issues, and preparing for current and future environmental challenges.

The passage classifies the environment into natural and human-made categories and outlines environmental knowledge areas such as natural resources, social environment, environmental technology, waste, and pollution. It emphasizes that environmental education should occur in formal and non-formal settings, including outdoor learning, and can benefit students with special needs.

Sustainable development is presented as meeting present needs without compromising future generations’ ability to meet theirs. Sustainable environmental development requires environmental education to change behavior, raise awareness, reduce energy use, minimize waste, conserve natural resources, use clean technologies, and apply environmental management. Examples include community learning projects, the Huai Sai royal initiative, natural capital accounting in Thailand, and national ecosystem assessment efforts.

Anton Shekhovtsov’s book “Tango Noir: Russia and the Western Far Right” examines how Russia has cultivated Western far-right activists to promote narratives of Western chaos and Russia as an alternative power. The passage traces this strategy from Soviet-era operations, including KGB efforts to exploit fears of Nazism in West Germany, to a major shift after Russia’s 2008 invasion of Georgia, when the Kremlin expanded its information war against the West. It describes tactics such as using fringe activists, laundering narratives into mainstream discourse, and selective sourcing by outlets like RT. Far-right groups have also supported Russia’s annexation of Crimea through observer missions. Shekhovtsov argues that Putin’s system involves competing networks, including sympathetic foreigners, activists, think tanks, oligarchs, diplomats, and United Russia figures. While Russia has tried to influence politics in countries such as Austria, Italy, France, and Germany, the book concludes its results have been limited, with sanctions, poor global favorability, and weak relations with the United States persisting. The passage notes concern over Russian paramilitary assistance to European far-right groups.

Foreigners entered a bivouac despite warnings and were escorted out. K. Otori demanded C. T. Gardner contradict reports that Otori had asked Korea to dismiss naval instructor Mr. Collwell; Gardner replied that inquiries should follow usual channels. Japanese advice to Korea set deadlines for reforms. Mr. Gresham reported that Korea feared Japanese and Chinese troops, sought U.S. assistance, and wanted troop withdrawal and neutral mediation. The United States expressed sympathy but maintained impartial neutrality and refused joint intervention.

The passage argues that music education should be approached interdisciplinarily because it relates to mathematics, language development, cognitive skills, emotional intelligence, technology, psychology, and social development. It reviews literature suggesting that interdisciplinary music education supports memory, problem-solving, analytical thinking, language learning, STEAM learning, creativity, cultural awareness, collaboration, and empathy.

The study used a qualitative literature review and a single-participant case study with a semi-structured interview. The participant, a social studies teacher studying in a Fine Arts Faculty music department, stated that basic music education in primary and secondary education is insufficient and that music departments should include preparatory classes, differentiated curricula, practical teaching methods, creative drama, media literacy, material design, learning psychology, speech/diction, movement, and workshop-based courses.

Findings emphasize the need for practical and interdisciplinary training in music departments, including micro-teaching, presentation work, instrument accompaniment repertoires, rhythm instrument design, and exposure to methods such as Orff, Kodály, Suzuki, and Dalcroze. The passage concludes that interdisciplinary basic music education is necessary in modern education because it supports academic, cognitive, cultural, emotional, social, and artistic development, and recommends revising curricula and policies to strengthen connections between music and other disciplines.

The study explored the readiness, expertise, and needs of Faculty of Industrial Education students regarding educational multimedia creation. It focused on students in computer, mechanical, industrial, and technical education programs who were preparing for or undertaking teaching practice. Using a descriptive design, the researchers reviewed relevant literature, interviewed stakeholders, and surveyed 124 randomly selected students online.

The study identified multimedia elements including text, images, sound, animation, video, metaverse, AR/VR, and interactive features. It examined topics such as multimedia importance, development processes, colour use, resource downloading, presentation media, infographic design, video production, educational posters, metaverse creation, copyright, and classroom media application.

Results showed students had high readiness to create educational multimedia, with notebooks and smartphones the most commonly used devices. Students also showed generally high readiness and some expertise in multimedia design tools. Overall multimedia expertise was rated high (𝑥̅ = 3.51, S.D. = 0.97), while the need for multimedia learning materials was rated at the highest level (𝑥̅ = 4.62, S.D. = 0.58). Students reported lower expertise in areas such as copyright and educational metaverse creation and higher need for learning materials in those areas.

The study concludes that students need targeted learning materials in multimedia areas where they have less experience. It notes limitations including the small sample size and limited population diversity, suggesting future research with broader and more diverse student groups.

Nabors Industries divested Quail Tools for more than its purchase price and plans to use proceeds to reduce debt by 25%. The passage says Nabors’ key U.S. and Saudi markets appear near cyclical troughs, and its stock has risen 70% from recent lows while remaining below historical valuations.

Florida International University reopened Monday, four days after a pedestrian bridge collapsed onto a busy road, killing six people. President Mark B. Rosenberg expressed condolences and said the school is cooperating with investigators. Authorities continued examining the rubble and documents. Southwest Eighth Street remained closed indefinitely, and the student government planned a Wednesday vigil for the victims.

This stackless native assembler procedure initializes the processor and cache system to create a pre-memory stack region for all processor cores, maps it to global address space, sets MTRRs, and creates a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instance. It uses register passing, preserves protected-mode SS, sets SS:ESP appropriately for real mode, and destroys specified registers. Status codes report success, stack reentry warning, or unknown processor family fatal error. A related stackless procedure removes the pre-memory stack once main memory is available, preserves EBX, disables CAR mode without modifying MTRR settings, and must also run on all cores.

Jean Munoz circulated an IEP news digest dated May 24, 2001, compiling articles mainly on California’s energy crisis.

The items include a Houston Chronicle commentary criticizing California officials Bill Lockyer and Gov. Gray Davis over their treatment of Texas energy producers and Enron. Multiple reports describe Davis considering or preparing plans to use diesel backup generators to reduce blackout risks, despite objections from environmentalists and air-quality officials who cited high pollution and soot emissions. Business groups and some state advisers argued the generators could help relieve the grid during emergencies.

Other articles report that California Public Utilities Commission President Loretta Lynch said investigators found evidence that generators varied plant output to raise electricity prices, while energy companies said output changes had legitimate business reasons. El Paso Merchant Group President Ralph Eads denied allegations that his company manipulated California natural gas prices, saying hedging contracts caused it to miss potential profits despite earning $184 million.

Several stories focus on political responses: President Bush agreed to meet Davis during a California visit amid disputes over federal energy policy and wholesale price caps. A Los Angeles Times article says Sen. James Jeffords’ expected departure from the Republican Party could give Democrats Senate control and increase California’s influence on energy and environmental issues. Reliant Energy offered to cut emergency power prices if air pollution rules limiting plant operation were waived.

The digest also includes reports that Davis planned to require at least one hour’s notice before blackouts, with earlier alerts for law enforcement, and a Field Poll showing Californians rated private utilities, out-of-state providers, Bush, federal regulators, the Legislature and Davis poorly on handling the energy crisis.

Caroline Hope, a 37-year-old teacher, died at Queen Elizabeth University Hospital in Glasgow after contracting E.coli during surgery for advanced colon cancer in Turkey. Her family raised more than £31,000 through crowdfunding to bring her back to Scotland for care.

The passage lists 179 songs certified diamond by the RIAA, meaning they moved at least 10 million equivalent units through sales and streaming. The diamond award was officially introduced in 1999, though Elton John’s “Something About The Way You Look Tonight / Candle in the Wind” was recognized in 1997 as the first diamond song and remains the only diamond-certified physical single. The list is organized by certification date, ending with Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy),” certified on September 15, 2025. Drake holds the record with 10 diamond singles, followed by Post Malone with nine; Rihanna and The Weeknd each have seven, while Katy Perry and Bruno Mars each have six.

North Carolina DHHS set a 140 parts-per-trillion health goal for GenX in water, addressing non-cancer effects such as endocrine disruption, thyroid disease, and reproductive effects. Cancer associations remain uncertain. A GenX forum with Erin Brockovich and Robert Bowcock is scheduled at UNCW.

Christian Kirk, whom Alabama linebacker Shaun Dion Hamilton first noticed at The Opening in 2013, is viewed as a major challenge for Alabama against Texas A&M. Nick Saban called him one of the SEC’s best all-purpose players. Kirk has hurt Alabama as a receiver and returner, with 16 catches, 148 yards, a receiving touchdown, and a punt return touchdown in two games.

Hong Kong and Singapore have seen a sharp rise in ICO activity after China and South Korea banned token sales. Companies from China and South Korea are moving fundraising efforts there because ICOs remain loosely regulated and the regulatory environment is viewed as more favorable. Examples include Beijing-based Xender seeking US$10 million in Singapore and reports of South Korea’s Bithumb and Zikto preparing ICOs through Singapore.

The Trump administration’s cuts and policy changes affecting services for more than 5 million English language learners have led schools to cancel professional development, close newcomer centers, suspend English learner teacher hiring, and reduce translation, interpretation, tutoring, family engagement, supplies, materials, and adult ESL classes. Advocates warn the proposed 2026 budget would further reduce support, with Oklahoma projected to lose $6.4 million and Virginia $17.5 million.

Educators report that immigrant and newcomer students are increasingly afraid to answer questions about their backgrounds or accept services, fearing identification or deportation. Some districts have seen sharp declines in newcomer enrollment or participation. In one Texas district, newcomer centers in nine high schools were consolidated after enrollment dropped to fewer than 30 students, leading to teacher reassignments.

Advocates also cite concerns about the federal government’s reduced oversight role and the impact on schools’ ability to meet legal obligations. Educators in New Jersey, Indianapolis, and Texas described lost staffing pipelines, halted training, and uncertainty about retaining bilingual teachers and support programs. Harvard education professor Gabrielle Oliveira said cuts to programs and staff reduce the information and support available to immigrant families.

Apple Inc. filed its Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended December 28, 2019. Total net sales were $91.8 billion, up 9% from $84.3 billion a year earlier, driven mainly by higher iPhone and Wearables, Home and Accessories sales. Net income was $22.2 billion, compared with $20.0 billion, and diluted earnings per share were $4.99, compared with $4.18.

Products net sales were $79.1 billion and Services net sales were $12.7 billion. iPhone sales rose to $56.0 billion, Wearables, Home and Accessories rose to $10.0 billion, Services rose to $12.7 billion, while Mac and iPad sales declined. By region, net sales increased in the Americas, Europe, Greater China and Rest of Asia Pacific, but decreased in Japan.

Apple reported total assets of $340.6 billion, total liabilities of $251.1 billion and shareholders’ equity of $89.5 billion. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $207.1 billion, including $19.1 billion restricted from general use. Operating cash flow was $30.5 billion. During the quarter, Apple repurchased $20.0 billion of common stock and paid $3.5 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents.

A record-setting Russian spacewalk outside the International Space Station ended with a communications antenna positioned 180 degrees farther than expected, though NASA said it was still working. Commander Alexander Misurkin and Anton Shkaplerov replaced an obsolete electronics box to upgrade the antenna, but had difficulty extending it properly. The spacewalk lasted 8 hours and 13 minutes, the longest by Russians and fifth longest overall, exceeding its planned six hours. Russian officials were assessing whether further action was needed. The old electronics box was discarded safely away from the station and is expected to burn up on re-entry.

Bills running back James Cook has started the season strongly after signing a $48 million contract, totaling 401 rushing yards, five touchdowns, and three straight 100-yard games. Josh Allen said the contract may have helped Cook play more freely and praised him as an “all-time teammate.” The 4-0 Bills face the Patriots in Week 5 with a chance to move to 3-0 in the division.

The passage provides instructions for installing a SanDisk SSD. If the SSD is not recognized, disconnect other USB devices. Users should run cloning software, select the internal drive as the source and the SanDisk SSD as the destination, then complete the cloning process. After shutting down and disconnecting power, notebook users remove the battery, transfer any brackets or adapters from the old HDD to the SSD, install the SSD in the drive bay, replace the battery and power cable, and restart. Desktop users open the case, remove the old HDD, install the SSD—using a 3.5-inch mounting adapter if needed—connect SATA data and power cables, close the case, and power on. The old HDD may be kept as a backup.

New research from Yale’s Budget Lab and the Brookings Institution found no evidence that AI has caused discernible disruption to U.S. jobs since ChatGPT launched in 2022, though occupational shifts and entry-level hiring challenges continue. Researchers said current employment changes do not appear tied to AI exposure, automation, or augmentation, and warned their analysis is not predictive.

The passage also reports that Meta will use AI chatbot conversations to personalize ads and recommendations, Thinking Machines Lab launched Tinker for custom frontier AI models, OpenAI released Sora 2, Periodic Labs recruited top AI researchers, and AI-related risk disclosures among S&P 500 companies rose from 12% in 2023 to 72% in 2025.

The passage describes the Gold Overnight Trading Strategy, which involves buying gold futures, GLD, GDX, or GDXJ at the market close and selling at the next open to capture overnight price movements. Backtests cited show overnight gains in GDX averaging 0.12% versus a 0.09% average intraday loss, while GLD had 8.4% annual overnight returns compared with 8.2% buy-and-hold returns and near-zero intraday gains. The passage notes that these average gains may be too small to trade in some cases and that gold and commodities are difficult, volatile, and less robust than stock strategies. It also discusses risk management, psychology, trade execution, and developing trading plans, emphasizing discipline, emotional control, stop-losses, profit targets, and market analysis. Incubated long and short overnight strategies are mentioned, including one long strategy with 741 trades and 0.17% average gain, and one short GDX strategy with 205 trades and 0.7% average gain.

The passage describes the 2018 ebook edition of Foreign Relations of the United States, 1894, produced by the Office of the Historian, noting its portability, search features, offline access, and citation guidance. It includes contents from Senate Executive Documents concerning President Benjamin Harrison’s 1893 transmissions to the Senate of materials on an uncompleted 1854 treaty with Hawaii and correspondence on U.S.–Hawaiian relations from 1820 to 1893.

The passage outlines SOS defensive tactics for disrupting strong low-post offense. The primary method is aggressively fronting the post to reduce catches, touches, and shots, supported by Helpside I rotations and double teams on lob passes. Main disruption options include Post Front, Base Go, Go Top, Go Wing, Hold, and Yo-Yo.

Base Go is the primary low-post trap, using the low Helpside I defender to double team along the baseline when the post catches. Go Top is a secondary trap using the high Helpside I defender, effective when the post tends to turn middle. Go Wing sends the wing defender with the pass to double team, especially when the wing is a poor outside shooter. Hold keeps other defenders home in pass denial to prevent kick-out threes while the post defender plays one-on-one. Yo-Yo allows a defender guarding a non-shooting wing to sag in and out to help on the post while others deny kick-out passes.

Across all options, rotations occur as the ball leaves the passer’s hands, defenders close out to shooters, deny return passes, front low-post players, and assume Helpside I positions when matched up.

The American Stroke Association’s FAST acronym helps identify major stroke symptoms and stresses urgent action: face drooping, arm weakness, speech difficulty, and time to call 911. If any symptom appears, even briefly, emergency help should be called and the symptom start time noted. A similar mnemonic, STR, asks a suspected stroke victim to smile, talk, and raise both arms.

A Nov. 5, 2001 Enron news compilation reports scrutiny of Enron’s financial dealings, including a $35 million March purchase from Chewco Investments, an entity linked to former Enron officer Michael Kopper, and transactions involving JEDI, LJM2, Andrew Fastow, and off-balance-sheet debt. Enron said its actions were legal and properly disclosed and pledged cooperation with the SEC’s formal investigation. Wall Street Journal articles also described short seller James Chanos identifying red flags in Enron filings and raised questions about Arthur Andersen’s role in ensuring clear financial disclosure. Other reports said unions sought governance reforms, Enron might need to sell assets, and the company was pursuing or facing developments involving Dabhol Power in India, Indian oil and gas assets, and a possible sale of its 50% stake in a Korean gas venture.

The passage describes U.S. diplomatic policy toward Hawaii in the 1880s. Mr. Blaine stated in 1881 that Hawaii could not grant other powers privileges exclusively given to the United States under the 1875 treaty, and warned against undue foreign influence. He also described Hawaii as key to American Pacific interests and said the United States would seek an American solution if Hawaiian neutrality became impracticable. In 1883, Mr. Frelinghuysen declined to join Hawaii’s protest against British and French expansion in Polynesia. The U.S.-Hawaii reciprocity treaty was renewed by an 1884 convention, including exclusive U.S. rights to enter and develop Pearl River Harbor as a coaling and repair station, though ratification was delayed until 1887 amid opposition. Gen. Schofield had earlier recommended acquiring Pearl River Harbor. The passage also recounts cable proposals linking Hawaii with Australia and North America, related Hawaiian legislation, British objections to exclusive cable privileges, and an 1891–92 U.S. cable survey from California to Honolulu.

The author criticizes cryonics, describing skepticism from making a film about a Frenchman who froze his wife after death. The passage cites a London teenager cryopreserved in the US after her grandparents paid £37,000, and explains Robert Ettinger’s 1964 theory of freezing bodies for future revival. It notes that about 2,000 people have paid for cryopreservation, including some celebrities and pet owners. The author argues that scientists do not believe frozen brains or bodies can be revived and condemns cryonics firms as exploiting fear of death.

Children’s mobile phone ownership varies widely by country and culture. Sara Zaske said her daughter rarely wanted a phone while attending school in Berlin, where few classmates had one, but wanted one after moving to California, where she was the only student in her fourth-grade class without a smartphone. Studies cited show 51% of German children ages 6 to 13 have a mobile phone, while across parts of Europe about 46% of children ages 9 to 16 owned smartphones in 2013-14, with usage restrictions and cost concerns differing by country. In the United States, a Nielsen report found 45% of children ages 10 to 12 had their own smartphone service plan, and Common Sense Media found 42% of children 8 and younger had their own tablets. Other studies reported high smartphone ownership among South Korean children ages 11 to 12, rising phone use among Taiwanese children ages 11 to 15, varied parental views in Turkey, and lower but increasing ownership in Malawi, Ghana and South Africa. In Australia, a study found the median age for first owning or using a mobile phone was 8. The American Academy of Pediatrics says there is no “right” age for a child’s first phone but recommends limits and monitoring for children’s media use.

Since 1900, the best-performing stock markets have included Australia, the United States, South Africa, New Zealand, Denmark, Sweden, Canada, Finland, Switzerland, and the Netherlands, with the top five being Australia, the U.S., South Africa, New Zealand, and Denmark. Credit Suisse data identifies Australia as the strongest performer over about 120 years, with real annual returns above 6.5% in U.S. dollar terms. The U.S. market delivered about 6.5% real annualized returns, while South Africa returned 7.2% locally and 6.4% in U.S. dollars; New Zealand also returned about 6.4%. Denmark ranks fifth, though its market experienced long periods of weak performance before stronger real returns in recent decades.

The passage attributes long-term equity outperformance to economic rebuilding after crises, productivity growth, technological innovation, and lower interest rates. Stocks outperformed bonds and Treasury bills globally from 1900 to 2019. It also notes that dividends, natural resources, diversification, and institutional factors contributed to Australia’s strong performance. Stock investing offers potential returns, inflation protection, dividends, ownership, liquidity, diversification, and accessibility, but most individual stocks underperform Treasury bills, and past performance does not guarantee future results.

Beignet the Nutria, a permitted mascot for the South Louisiana Wetlands Discovery Center, marked World Wetlands Day by predicting hurricane season based on whether he saw his shadow. He did not, signaling a mild season with no hurricanes. Punxsutawney Phil predicted six more weeks of winter.

The passage supports France’s recovery of Alsace-Lorraine as desirable and important to ending German militarism, while avoiding a U.S. commitment beyond France’s own aims. It recognizes Italy’s right to boundary rectifications based on defensive and nationalist considerations, supports a commercially free Trieste with cultural autonomy, and rejects broader Adriatic ambitions. For the Balkans, it rejects the Treaty of Bucharest as unjust, calls for evacuation and restoration of occupied states, and argues that settlements should balance national and economic factors after impartial inquiry, without great-power intrigue or massacre. It lists tentative considerations on Dobrudja, Bulgaria’s borders, Serbia’s sea access, Macedonia, and Albania, emphasizing economic prosperity as key to lasting peace. For Poland, it calls for an independent democratic state with boundaries balancing national and economic needs and adequate sea access, while noting the difficulty of unifying Poles and the risks of economic dependence, exposure, and internal ethnic friction without democracy.

Montreal has been named the world’s best city for students in the QS Best Student Cities ranking, replacing Paris, which held first place for four years. The ranking assesses factors including university quality, affordability, desirability, employer access, international character, tolerance, pollution and safety. Canada performed strongly, with Vancouver 10th and Toronto joint 11th, and QS forecasts Canada will become a major player in attracting international students. London rose to third, helped by strong universities and improved affordability after the pound’s fall. Paris slipped to second due to cost and lower desirability, though QS rejected a direct link to terror attacks. Seoul rose to fourth, reflecting Asia’s growing appeal. Germany had Berlin and Munich in the top 10, helped by free tuition for overseas students. The passage notes that international students are economically important, with overseas students worth almost $36bn to the US economy.

In October 2000, four months after Zipcar’s launch, co-founder Robin Chase discovered that September revenue was about half of her estimate and that the company’s model could not break even as designed. Zipcar had launched in June 2000 to provide urban residents convenient car access, using Internet and wireless technology, and had gained positive press and 430 members by October.

Chase’s background included an international childhood, work in public health consulting, and an MIT Sloan MBA, where she strengthened her finance skills. She developed Zipcar after hearing from Antje Danielson about car sharing in Berlin, seeing it as a useful service for people like herself who needed occasional car access. Chase and Danielson agreed to 50-50 ownership.

Chase built Zipcar through extensive networking, learning from advisers, transportation experts, policymakers, car manufacturers, insurers, parking authorities, and Communauto founder Benoît Robert. She assembled a small team including Danielson, her husband Roy Russell, her brother Mark, Stephen Oakley, Larry Slotnick, and consultants. Early operations involved difficult work securing cars, parking, insurance, technology, and funding. Zipcar launched with four Volkswagens, rudimentary access technology, and a pricing model based on membership fees plus hourly, daily, and mileage charges.

By mid-October, Zipcar had 10 cars and over 400 members, but utilization was 22% rather than the projected 40%, and revenue per trip was about half of expectations. Chase determined that daily rentals, which made up more revenue than expected, were underpriced and would need a 20% increase for the company to break even. Team members worried this could be seen as a bait-and-switch and could hurt customers and fundraising, just as Zipcar was nearing a $1.3 million financing round.

South Korean prosecutors raided Korean Air Lines’ headquarters over suspected embezzlement and breach of trust by members of its owning family, Yonhap reported. The investigation includes possible tax evasion involving Chairman Cho Yang-ho and his family, suspicious money flows, and inherited overseas assets. The probe follows scrutiny of the Cho family after incidents involving Cho Hyun-min and Heather Cho.

David Clarkson said the team has played well despite unfavorable bounces and must create more traffic, finish chances, and stay focused shift by shift. He praised the group’s heart, belief, and resilience, acknowledged the opposing goalie’s strong play, and said they will keep pushing in the next game.

International Development Secretary Penny Mordaunt became the first minister to use sign language in Parliament, signing while answering a Commons question. She highlighted the upcoming Global Disability Summit in London, co-organised by the UK, Kenya and the International Disability Alliance, to promote disability inclusion in poorer countries.

The speaker says the team must take more initiative, improve its penalty kill, disrupt Carolina’s entries and offensive-zone setup, and focus on details like blocked shots, giveaways and takeaways. They emphasize players should stay within their own games rather than try to do too much in the Stanley Cup Finals. The speaker also reflects on what the moment means for players’ careers, highlights Rem’s perseverance, and notes efforts to limit opponents’ faceoff advantages.

Consilium Software announced that Consilium UniRSM™ is available worldwide on Cisco SolutionsPlus through Cisco Commerce as a replacement for the end-of-sale Cisco Remote Silent Monitoring product. Designed for Cisco Contact Center Enterprise environments, UniRSM enables remote phone-based silent monitoring and whisper coaching without requiring a network connection to the Cisco environment. Developed with Cisco product engineering input, it includes architectural, reliability and feature improvements for CCE release 11.6(x), including reduced audio streaming delays, coaching mode, multi-call monitoring, high availability, VVB support, web-based reporting, and Windows and Linux support. Consilium provides enterprise software for unified communications and contact centers, while Cisco SolutionsPlus allows approved third-party Cisco Compatible products to be ordered through Cisco sales teams and partners.

The TPS7H500x-SP controllers use fixed-frequency, peak current mode control with a transconductance error amplifier that compares VSENSE to the lower of SS or the 0.613-V reference. Output voltage is programmed with a resistor divider to VSENSE, and soft start is controlled by a capacitor on SS; synchronous rectifier outputs activate after SS exceeds 1 V.

Switching frequency can be set by an internal oscillator, external synchronization, or primary-secondary operation. Internal oscillator mode uses an RT resistor and supports 100 kHz to 2 MHz switching, with SYNC outputting twice the switching frequency. External synchronization requires RT floating and a SYNC clock from 200 kHz to 4 MHz at twice the desired switching frequency. Primary-secondary mode uses the primary controller’s SYNC output to drive a secondary controller, producing a 90° or 270° phase shift.

The device family supports different combinations of primary outputs OUTA/OUTB and synchronous rectifier outputs SRA/SRB. External gate drivers are recommended because each output has about 150-mA peak current capability. Dead time, leading-edge blanking, duty-cycle limits, current sensing, slope compensation, hiccup-mode overcurrent response, FAULT shutdown, and thermal shutdown are configurable or specified depending on device variant.

The passage also describes compensation options, including Type 2A and Type 2B networks connected to COMP, and provides design guidance for supported DC-DC topologies such as buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. A synchronous push-pull GaN design example for TPS7H5001-SP covers frequency setting, feedback resistors, dead time, blanking, soft start, transformer design, FET selection, clamp design, output filtering, current limiting, hiccup timing, compensation, and slope compensation.

Recommended power supply operation is 4 V to 14 V with proper bypassing. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing high-current and high-switching loops, routing sensitive traces away from noisy nodes and outputs, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, and using appropriate grounding and via practices for package options. The passage also lists related documentation, support resources, revision history, mechanical and packaging information, and TI disclaimers.

Lincolnshire County Council leader Martin Hill urged health bosses to reveal detailed future plans for county services after a CQC report rated ULHT as “requiring improvement” overall, despite 72% of inspected areas being rated “good.” Hill welcomed progress but raised concerns about children’s services at Boston, issues at Lincoln, and ongoing recruitment problems. He said clearer plans would improve public and staff confidence. The report rated Lincoln “requires improvement,” Boston “inadequate,” and Grantham and Louth “good.”

An informal survey of 13 CFD brokers found that 62% to 82% of retail CFD traders lose money, with Interactive Brokers having the lowest reported loss rate at 62%. The passage argues that most CFD traders lose due to factors including lack of a trading plan, limited knowledge and experience, leverage, hidden costs, bid-ask spreads, overnight fees, illiquidity, and CFDs being a zero-sum derivative product. It states that CFD trading is generally not profitable for most traders, though a minority may profit through discipline, risk management, lower costs, and proven strategies. The passage concludes that retail CFD traders face significant obstacles and that most short-term traders fail.

The passage describes a patent application for systems and methods enabling changed-block tracking (CBT) for differential and incremental backups in cloud or network computing environments that do not natively support CBT, such as some OpenStack-based architectures. The disclosed approach generates virtual machine disk images at different times, compares them to identify changed blocks, creates a map of changed block locations, loads a virtual machine disk copy at a virtual server agent, extracts the changed blocks using the map, and backs them up.

It also provides an overview of an information management system for protecting and managing enterprise data. The system may include client computing devices, primary and secondary storage devices, storage managers, data agents, and media agents. It supports operations such as backups, archives, snapshots, replication, deduplication, hierarchical storage management, restores, indexing, policy-based automation, and scalable distributed management across physical, virtual, and cloud environments.

U.S. investor sentiment has turned cautious as stock valuations reach multi-year highs, driven by AI and technology gains. The S&P 500 is up about 15% this year and the Nasdaq nearly 19%, with major firms including Nvidia, Microsoft and Oracle leading the rally. The IMF and JPMorgan warned of correction risks, while Goldman Sachs said earnings growth and productivity may support higher valuations. Options activity shows elevated call volumes, and upcoming earnings plus central bank commentary are expected to shape market direction.

The passage discusses international condemnation of Donald Trump’s decision to recognize Jerusalem as Israel’s capital. The interviewee argues the US was never neutral in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and suggests Trump sought support from Zionist elements in the American establishment while aligning with Saudi Arabia and Israel. The Arab League is described as weak and unlikely to take strong punitive action. The interviewee says Trump’s move exposed the Israeli-Palestinian peace process as a sham but had limited immediate effect on the ground. The passage also highlights the lack of citizenship rights for non-Jewish Jerusalem residents and references UN Resolution 478 declaring Israel’s annexation of East Jerusalem illegal. The interviewee concludes that the two-state solution is nearly dead and supports fighting for equal rights.

Investigating officer Sergeant Marlon Appollis testified in Jason Rohde’s murder trial that no suicide note or evidence indicating Susan Rohde had taken her own life was found in their Spier hotel room in July 2016. Susan was found hanging behind the bathroom door while the couple attended a conference. Appollis said he found no signs of forced entry, no object she could have stood on, no footprints on the bath edge, and no fingerprints on the basin or window. He found a note suggesting Jason was involved in an extramarital affair. After the autopsy indicated Susan died from manual strangulation rather than hanging, the case was changed to murder and Jason was treated as a possible suspect. The court also heard that tests were requested on the bathroom door hook to determine whether it could hold about 51kg. The trial was postponed to allow the defence to prepare for cross-examination.

Tarik Skubal tied a Tigers postseason record with 14 strikeouts, leading Detroit to a 2-1 win over Cleveland in Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series. Skubal allowed one run on three hits over 7 2/3 innings. Will Vest recorded the final four outs, including tagging out José Ramírez in the ninth. Detroit can advance with a win Wednesday.

The Ravens fell to 1-3 after a 37-20 loss to the Chiefs, raising concerns about their playoff hopes. CBS Sports’ John Breech gave Baltimore an “F,” citing a defense that failed to force a punt until the fourth quarter and Lamar Jackson’s two turnovers before leaving with a hamstring injury. With two games before the bye, Baltimore needs wins to reach 3-3 and stabilize its season.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K reporting that on June 23, 2020, it entered into an amended and restated credit agreement with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent and other lenders. The agreement extends the revolving credit facility term to June 23, 2023, and borrowings may be used for general corporate purposes, including backing notes under its commercial paper program.

A hockey player says an MRI at Duke indicated a third-degree MCL injury, possibly slightly less severe, that is expected to heal but not immediately. He recalls the injury occurred during a net-front collision when Mark Andre was defending his position; the player’s knee and elbow became wedged against the post, causing his knee to pop and leaving him without control when trying to go into a butterfly. He says the play likely was not a penalty and that Mark Andre should not be blamed. He is frustrated to be injured during a Stanley Cup run but says the team has handled adversity throughout the playoffs. Although he will not be on the ice, he hopes to help however he can, especially by supporting goalies Ty and Jussi without overwhelming them with information.

Tesla, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated October 23, 2019, reporting that it released financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2019 by posting its Third Quarter 2019 Update on its website. The update is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report was signed by CFO Zachary J. Kirkhorn.

This study sequenced and characterized SARS-CoV-2 genomes from Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, focusing on molecular evolution and selection in the structural E, M, and N proteins. Twelve respiratory samples from Esteio collected between April and June 2021 were sequenced; 10 belonged to lineage P.1 and 2 to P.1.17, both within the Gamma clade. The genomes showed 68 nucleotide substitutions, including 36 non-synonymous changes. Several mutations were reported for the first time in Rio Grande do Sul, including NSP3:D1208A, also first described in Brazil, and NSP12:I136V, not previously described in GISAID.

Analysis of 4,706 SARS-CoV-2 genomes from Rio Grande do Sul showed lineage shifts from B.1.1.33 in 2020 to Zeta, Gamma, Delta, and later Omicron. Gamma predominated from February to July 2021, Delta from August to late 2021, and Omicron exceeded 90% of sequenced genomes between January and April 2022. Phylogenomic analysis supported monophyletic groups for major variants and placed all 12 study genomes within the Gamma clade.

Selection analyses found no positively selected sites in the E protein, two positively selected sites in M, and 14 in N. Negative selection was detected at two sites in E, 12 in M, and 46 in N. Molecular stability predictions suggested most tested M mutations were stabilizing, while N mutations showed mixed effects, with several C-terminal substitutions predicted to destabilize the protein. The authors conclude that structural proteins, particularly M and N, show evolutionary patterns relevant to SARS-CoV-2 diversification and conservation in Rio Grande do Sul.

This study protocol describes a three-arm randomized controlled trial in Singapore testing the Digital-MindCAN programme, an eight-week real-time videotelephony mindfulness psychoeducation intervention tailored for cancer survivors. Adults aged 21–65 with stage 0–III cancer who completed curative treatment within two weeks to two years will be recruited from a tertiary hospital and randomized to Digital-MindCAN plus standard care, Palouse Mindfulness plus standard care, or a wait-list control group. The target sample is 150 participants. Primary outcomes are objective and subjective stress; secondary outcomes include psychological well-being, perceived relaxation, mindfulness, resilience, depression, and anxiety. Data will be collected through questionnaires, physiological measures, and focus group interviews, then analyzed using quantitative statistical methods and realist evaluation for qualitative findings. The trial aims to determine whether Digital-MindCAN is superior to wait-list control and non-inferior to Palouse Mindfulness, and whether it could inform future clinical practice for cancer survivors.

Stanford researchers developed “biofilm lithography,” a technique using blue light and genetically engineered E. coli to pattern bacterial biofilms into shapes such as dots, stripes and circuits overnight. The method achieves 25-micrometer resolution and is described as faster, simpler, higher-resolution and compatible with varied surfaces, including microfluidic devices, compared with other bacterial patterning methods. The researchers say it could help study biofilm growth, bacterial interactions, synthetic microbial communities, biomaterials and biofilm-based circuits. Testing also suggested that bacteria may repeatedly attach to and detach from surfaces rather than freely swim across culture dishes. The team is working to pattern multiple bacterial strains to study multi-species communities and antibiotic resistance sharing in biofilms.

The study examined preschool teachers’ views on sensory education and their classroom practices. Using a phenomenological qualitative design, researchers interviewed 20 preschool teachers selected through maximum diversity sampling. Data were collected with a 12-question semi-structured interview form and analyzed through content analysis, producing 81 codes under 9 categories and 3 themes: importance of sensory education, its relationship with the preschool education program, and difficulties and limitations.

Teachers stated that sensory education is important, should begin in early childhood, and supports children’s developmental areas. They reported using sensory activities in daily routines, including visual, auditory, music-rhythm, art, experiment, touch, drama, play, and balance activities. However, they said sensory education is not clearly or sufficiently addressed in the preschool education program, although it appears in outcomes, indicators, and concepts. Teachers evaluated sensory activities mainly through observation, question-answer, development forms, and family cooperation.

Participants reported insufficient materials, unfavorable physical classroom and school conditions, and limited competence regarding sensory integration problems. Most wanted training on sensory education. The study recommended in-service training, occupational therapist support, sensory materials for preschool settings, greater inclusion of sensory education in undergraduate programs, and sample activities prepared by occupational therapists and teachers.

Wisconsin’s frack sand industry has rebounded as domestic crude oil production grows, reviving idled mines and demand. New Texas mines are expected to add competition, but analysts say rising demand and differences in sand type should limit impact on Wisconsin’s northern white sand, whose price may rise 10 to 12 percent this year.

The speaker said the team focused on quicker defensive positioning, protecting the net, limiting rebounds, and improving puck movement after rushing plays previously. They felt stronger despite the Dallas heat and benefited from easier westward travel. A scoring play came from patience at the blue line and traffic to the net. The team planned to maintain a specific line matchup, especially in Dallas. After an embarrassing previous performance, players took personal responsibility and aimed to respond with more emotion, urgency, skating, and checking.

CMD42 requires a block length at least as large as its data structure; otherwise results are undefined and the card may lock unexpectedly. Reserved parameter bits are don’t care. Required passwords must be correct, and password length must be 1–128 bits or an error occurs. On CMD42 errors, LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED is set, while CARD_IS_LOCKED reflects the current card state after execution.

The author argues that Agilent Technologies’ shares, up about 22% in the past month, should be avoided or sold due to valuation and risk. While noting positives such as shareholder-friendly management, dividend growth, a shrinking share count, manageable debt, and recent six-month improvement, the author says revenue and net income growth have been uninspiring. A dividend-based forecast using 6% growth implies about a 6.7% annual return over four years, which the author views as insufficient given risks tied to variable customer spending and research budgets. The author also cites a bearish technical view if shares close below $58.50, with a possible decline to $53. The conclusion is that Agilent’s stock is priced too optimistically, trades at a premium to the market, and should be rated “avoid.”

The speaker said the team gained confidence from past comebacks but did not want to rely on late rallies after poor first and second periods. They emphasized needing better skating, puck movement, discipline, and fewer penalties. The goalie was praised as level-headed and outstanding. The speaker was unsure about the penalty-shot call after reviewing video. They described the team’s refusal to quit, its focus on pushing the pace when trailing, and the importance of preparing for Edmonton while ultimately concentrating on improving their own play. They noted Edmonton’s physicality, strong goaltending, defensive challenges, and special-teams matchups. The speaker also praised the team’s locker-room character, depth, power play options, deadline additions, and the home-game environment.

External Affairs Minister Sushma Swaraj sought a report from the Indian High Commission in Pakistan after Sikh leader Charnjit Singh, an outspoken Taliban critic and inter-faith activist, was shot dead in Peshawar. Sukhbir Singh Badal urged her to raise the issue with Pakistan over Sikh safety.

The speaker says the team approached the game as a single opportunity to win and gained confidence from the result. They emphasize staying within their straightforward system, keeping games close, using all four lines, getting strong back pressure from forwards, and relying on defense and goaltending. They expect Detroit to respond with its best effort and note Detroit’s speed, scoring ability, size, and talent. The speaker stresses focus, limiting distractions in Detroit, and not changing the team’s approach, aside from possibly taking shorter shifts. They describe Ron Francis as a classy, respected, mostly hands-off captain, and say the team plays for one another. They also note that young players’ inexperience may help them avoid pressure, while veterans understand the sacrifices required.

Washington Prime Group Inc. (NYSE: WPG) shares recently traded down 0.27%, closing at $7.51. Analysts project a 52-week mean target price of $6.77 based on three opinions, with a high target of $7.50 and a low of $6. The stock has an average brokerage recommendation of 4, based on two recommendations, and its industry ranks 173 of 265 by ABR. Analyst ratings include two Holds, one Underperform, no Buys, no Outperforms, and no Sells. WPG’s ATR-14 is 0.25, weekly volatility is 2.76%, monthly volatility is 3.38%, and RSI is 65.19. The company has a market capitalization of $1.41 billion, 187.31 million shares outstanding, and recent trading volume of 3.62 million shares versus an average of 3.47 million.

A Markov cohort model assessed whether a RATIONS-style nutritional intervention for HIV-negative household contacts of persons with tuberculosis in India would be cost-effective. The intervention provided household contacts with a food basket containing micronutrients, rice, and lentils for six months, and nutritional support for individuals who developed TB during treatment. Using RATIONS study effect sizes and costs, the model simulated 100,000 household contacts over their lifetimes from government and societal perspectives.

Compared with usual care, the intervention reduced projected lifetime TB incidence from 7,718 to 6,749 cases and TB deaths from 1,529 to 906 per 100,000 contacts. It averted 13,775 DALYs per 100,000 people, mainly through reduced TB mortality. Discounted costs were higher with the intervention, but the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was $229 per DALY averted from the healthcare perspective and $184 from the societal perspective, both below India’s $550 willingness-to-pay threshold.

Sensitivity analyses found results were most affected by supplementation cost and the intervention’s effect on TB incidence. The intervention remained cost-effective across broad assumptions and was favored in more than 99% of probabilistic simulations at the willingness-to-pay threshold. The study concludes that RATIONS-style nutritional support could be cost-effective for populations in India with high burdens of TB and undernutrition.

The passage examines higher education projects (HEPs) created or relocated abroad by Russian academics after the 2022 invasion of Ukraine and subsequent repression in Russian academia. It frames these initiatives as a form of education in emergencies operating outside the conflict zone and explores how they understand their relationship to Russia while in exile.

The study analyzes four HEPs with varying levels of institutionalization, from informal online courses to accredited degree programs. Using interviews and discourse analysis, it identifies three main narratives. First, HEPs present themselves as “safe havens” that support fleeing scholars and students, preserve academic identity, and provide spaces of intellectual freedom. Second, they aim to preserve and reconceptualize academic traditions, especially in social sciences and humanities, though the passage notes that this reconceptualization appears limited. Third, they practice “hope-making” by acting toward an imagined future for Russia despite uncertainty about return.

The passage concludes that these HEPs function as support structures, preserve displaced academic communities, and create hope through educational practice. It calls for further research on their internal biases, international influences, teaching practices, evolving self-concepts, and role in reshaping international higher education.

The speaker says the reviewed puck play was inconclusive and could have been called either way, but they trust Toronto and the referees. They defend Pekks despite poor single-game stats, saying he has been their best player in the playoffs and in many games. They also credit Milwaukee’s organization with helping players mature on and off the ice.

A premature newborn from an Oregon faith-healing church died after birth from complications of prematurity; the medical examiner said immediate care could have saved her. Her twin survived after treatment. Authorities are investigating because no one called 911, and no charges have been filed.

Martin Brodeur said he is enjoying the playoff run and the team is still fighting for the Cup. He emphasized creating more offense by driving players to the net, building on the last win, and taking things day to day. He said the pressure feels lower than earlier in his career, and off days help him relax and refocus.

Faviola Dadis said at a Los Angeles news conference that Steven Seagal sexually assaulted her during a 2002 late-night casting session in a Beverly Hills hotel room when she was a 17-year-old model and aspiring actress. She said she recently filed a police report, and Los Angeles prosecutors said the case is under review. Seagal’s attorney did not immediately comment. Dadis said she came forward after recent entertainment industry misconduct reports. She appeared with attorney Lisa Bloom and Regina Simons, who has also accused Seagal of assault. Other women, including Portia de Rossi and Jenny McCarthy, have accused Seagal of misconduct; Seagal has denied prior allegations. Bloom said no lawsuits are immediately planned.

The lecture introduces dynamic optimality for binary search trees (BSTs): whether one online BST algorithm can perform within a constant factor of the best offline BST algorithm for every access sequence. The BST model stores keys in a tree and allows pointer moves to left, right, or parent nodes, plus rotations; searches start at the root and are assumed successful, with no insertions or deletions.

Worst-case BST access requires Θ(log n), but some sequences can be faster. Discussed properties include sequential access, dynamic finger, entropy, working set, and unified bounds. Sequential access can be served in constant amortized time. Dynamic finger bounds access cost by the logarithm of key-distance from the previous access. Entropy reflects access frequency distribution and matches static optimality. Working set bounds cost by the logarithm of the number of distinct keys accessed since the last access to the same key and implies entropy. The unified property combines spatial closeness and temporal recency, but no BST is known to achieve it exactly; the best known BST result has an additive log log n term.

Dynamic optimality asks for an online BST whose total cost on any access sequence is within a constant factor of the offline optimal BST tailored to that sequence. This remains open. A log log n-competitive BST is known, while any balanced BST is trivially log n-competitive.

Splay trees are reviewed as a leading candidate for dynamic optimality. They move the accessed node to the root using zig-zig and zig-zag rotations. Splay trees are known to satisfy sequential access, working set, entropy, and dynamic finger properties, but it is unknown whether they satisfy the unified property or are dynamically optimal.

The lecture then presents a geometric view of BST executions. Searches are represented as points in a space-time grid, and a BST execution corresponds to all nodes touched during searches. A point set represents a valid BST execution iff every rectangle spanned by two points not sharing a row or column contains another point; this is called arboral satisfaction. Dynamic optimality can therefore be phrased as finding a minimum-size satisfied superset of the access points. It is unknown whether this problem is NP-hard or admits a constant-factor approximation; the best known approximation is log log n.

The equivalence is proved using least common ancestors for one direction and treaps for the reverse direction. Treaps are BSTs ordered by keys and heap-ordered by next touch time. The proof shows how a satisfied point set can be simulated by a BST through rotations while touching only prescribed nodes.

Finally, the greedy geometric algorithm is introduced: process accesses bottom-up in time and add only necessary points on the current row to satisfy rectangles with past points. This corresponds to an offline tree algorithm that rearranges the search path optimally for future accesses. In the geometric view it is online, and with split trees it can be implemented as an online BST. The next lecture will discuss lower bounds that come close to proving greedy optimal.

The lecture discusses finite-temperature CFTs on a sphere and their gravity duals in AdS. Unlike CFTs on flat space, where temperature is the only scale and physics is related by scaling, a CFT on a sphere has a dimensionless parameter \(RT\), making low- and high-temperature behavior distinct.

For a spherical boundary, thermal AdS is a valid Euclidean solution because the Euclidean time circle remains bounded from below and the metric is nonsingular. There are also AdS black hole solutions. Their temperature as a function of horizon radius has a maximum inverse temperature, implying a minimum temperature for black holes. Above this minimum temperature, two black hole solutions exist: a small black hole with negative specific heat and a big black hole with positive specific heat.

The gravity path integral is evaluated by saddle-point approximation, so thermal AdS, the small black hole, and the big black hole are possible saddle points. The dominant phase is the one with lowest free energy, equivalently the largest Euclidean action contribution in the large-\(N\) limit. The small black hole never dominates. Thermal AdS dominates below a critical temperature \(T_c\), while the big black hole dominates above \(T_c\). This first-order phase transition is the Hawking-Page transition. At \(T_c\), the black hole horizon radius equals the AdS radius, and the free energy changes from order \(N^0\) below \(T_c\) to order \(N^2\) above it.

The high-temperature or large-sphere limit corresponds to the flat-space CFT and is described by a large black hole whose spherical horizon locally resembles a planar horizon. The lecture then explains the field-theory interpretation using a toy model of matrix harmonic oscillators with an SU(\(N\)) singlet constraint. Low-energy states have order \(N^0\) degeneracy, while states of energy order \(N^2\) have exponentially large degeneracy. At high temperature, entropy overcomes thermal suppression, producing an order \(N^2\) free energy, matching the Hawking-Page transition.

Dale Capstick of Coxheath, Cape Breton, has reported nightly sightings of large, fast-moving spiders in her home since August, identifying them as Eratigena atrica, or giant house spiders. Her husband has killed about 30. Nearby resident Charles Andrews also captured one, later confirmed by Nova Scotia Museum biologist Calum Ewing as the European House Spider. Ewing said the spiders are harmless but startling, can have leg spans up to 10 centimetres, and have been in Nova Scotia since the mid-1990s. Often found in sinks or bathtubs, they are attracted by insect populations and may leave or die once prey is gone. Capstick hopes the spiders have vacated after several days without sightings.

Meizu’s Pro 7 and Pro 7 Plus have received a 600 Yuan price cut in China, bringing the Pro 7 series starting price to 1,999 Yuan from December 12. The phones feature secondary AMOLED displays, dual 12MP rear cameras, 16MP front cameras, Flyme OS 6 based on Android Nougat, and Helio processors. The Pro 7 has a 3,000mAh battery, while the Pro 7 Plus has 3,500mAh with faster mCharge 4.0.

The Bemidji Blue Ox won the Region 10C title after entering the tournament as the top seed and defeating Crookston in Saturday’s championship. Bemidji had already clinched a state tournament berth by reaching the final, while Crookston earned its berth earlier with an extra-inning win over Moorhead. Bemidji led 5-0 early and held on for the win, with Ben Thoma pitching seven innings, striking out seven and allowing one run. Cody Benson went 3-for-5. As region champion, Bemidji receives a first-round bye in the 48-team state tournament and will open Aug. 27 in Hamburg against Fort Ripley or Blue Earth.

Rushin Shah, Apple’s former head of Natural Language Understanding for Siri, has left after five years to join Facebook in Menlo Park, where he will work on natural language and dialogue understanding. At Apple, Shah helped develop Siri’s voice recognition, intent interpretation, and conversational features. He said on LinkedIn that he wanted “a new challenge” and was excited to work on Facebook products with large daily user bases. His departure comes as Siri faces growing competition from Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant, and as Apple expands Siri through iOS, Mac, and its newly announced HomePod smart speaker. It is not known who will replace Shah at Apple.

HPE introduced the Edgeline Services Platform and two related apps at Discover 2017 to help customers manage expanding IoT device inventories and integrate IT systems with Operational Technology functions. The platform runs IoT applications outside traditional data centers or the cloud, near equipment in locations such as factories, refineries, vehicles or cities. The Edgeline Data Aggregation App combines data from OT devices including PLCs and SCADA systems into a single collection. The Edgeline Address Translation App gathers network address translations from larger networks and delivers them to subset networks, with remote software-defined configuration. Analyst Mike Krell said HPE’s single-vendor approach can help customers navigate complex IoT technology choices in a competitive market.

The Canadian Couch Potato podcast episode examines balancing investment costs, complexity, simplicity and convenience. Guest John Robertson, author of the revised second edition of *The Value of Simple*, discusses indexing options, robo-advisors, his comparison tool AutoInvest.ca, and his online course Practical Index Investing for Canadians.

The episode also reviews Vanguard’s new asset allocation ETFs, which charge a 0.22% management fee and may appeal to some investors. However, investors using Tangerine or TD e-Series funds should consider trade-offs before switching. Factors include portfolio size, since fee savings are smaller on smaller balances; whether automatic regular contributions are important, as ETFs do not support the same automation; comfort with ETF trading; account complexity, especially taxable and multi-account portfolios; and whether the ETF’s asset mix matches the investor’s target allocation. The Vanguard ETFs are best suited to 60% or 80% equity allocations, while conservative investors may prefer adding GICs instead of holding 60% bonds.

Researchers led by UCL and Imperial College London showed how polymyxin B, a last-resort antibiotic for Gram-negative bacterial infections, disrupts bacterial outer “armor.” High-resolution imaging and biochemical experiments found that active bacteria exposed to the drug rapidly formed surface bulges, overproduced outer membrane material, and shed it, creating gaps that allowed the antibiotic to enter and kill the cell. Dormant bacteria, whose armor production is switched off, were not killed; when given sugar, they resumed activity and became vulnerable after a delay. The findings may help explain recurrent infections and suggest strategies such as waking dormant bacteria or promoting armor production during treatment.

ESA inaugurated New Norcia 3, a new 35-meter deep space antenna in Western Australia and the fourth in its Estrack deep space tracking network. Due to enter service in 2026, it will expand ESA’s ability to download data and communicate with missions including Juice, Solar Orbiter, BepiColombo, Mars Express, Hera, Plato, Envision, Ariel, Ramses, and Vigil. The antenna uses cryogenically cooled components, a 20 kW radio-frequency amplifier, and advanced timing and communication systems to detect weak signals and send commands across deep space. The project began in 2021, cost an estimated €62.3 million, and included a €3 million Australian Space Agency contribution. It was built by European contractors with Australian industry involvement and will also support cooperation with NASA, JAXA, ISRO, and commercial missions.

The West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals addressed certified questions arising from the termination of three at-will Holiday Inn employees who refused to take polygraph tests required by their employer, General Hugh Mercer Corporation. The employees had signed agreements permitting polygraph testing, later refused testing after the employer announced a testing program, and were fired.

The Court held that determining whether a substantial public policy exists is a question of law for the court, not a jury. It also held that firing employees for refusing to submit to a polygraph or similar test as a condition of employment violated West Virginia public policy, grounded in the state’s recognition of individual privacy rights. The Court affirmed the circuit court’s ruling and remanded for further proceedings.

Justice Miller dissented, joined by Justice Neely, arguing that no established public policy against such discharges existed when the employees were terminated because the relevant statute limiting employer polygraph use became effective afterward.
